title: [model-gateway] Optimize router selection with lock-free snapshots
author: ppraneth
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->


## Motivation
The `RouterManager::select_router_for_request` function is on the critical **hot path** of the gateway, executed for every incoming inference request. The previous implementation suffered from two performance bottlenecks:

1.  **Per-Request Allocations:** The use of `collect::<Vec<_>>()` and `vec![router]` triggered heap allocations on every request, leading to system memory allocator overhead and potential lock contention under high concurrency.
2.  **Map Iteration Locks:** Iterating over `DashMap` entries requires acquiring internal shard-level locks. While efficient for point lookups, this added microsecond-scale latency and jitter during high-throughput routing.

This PR introduces a **lock-free snapshot mechanism** using the `arc_swap` crate. By caching the router list in a contiguous, read-optimized `Vec` that is updated only during registration, we achieve nanosecond-scale routing performance.

## Modifications
* **Snapshot Architecture:** Integrated `routers_snapshot: ArcSwap<Vec<Arc<dyn RouterTrait>>>` into the `RouterManager` struct to provide zero-allocation access to candidate routers.
* **Atomic Updates:** Modified `register_router` to pre-calculate and store a fresh snapshot whenever a new router joins the registry, shifting overhead from the "hot" request path to the "cold" registration path.
* **Zero-Allocation Selection:** Refactored `select_router_for_request` to use lock-free `.load()` calls.
* **Logic Refinement:**
    * Simplified model-specific lookups to return matching candidates immediately, bypassing redundant scoring logic when only one valid router exists.

* **Dependencies:** Added `arc_swap = "1.7.1"` to `Cargo.toml`.

## Accuracy Tests

## Benchmarking and Profiling
benchmarks were conducted  ($1\mu s = 1,000ns$). The results show a dramatic reduction in routing overhead.

| Configuration | Before (Allocating) | After (Snapshot) | Performance Gain |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **2 Routers** | $19,340ns$ ($19.3\mu s$) | **$32ns$** | **~604x Faster** |
| **10 Routers** | $18,648ns$ ($18.6\mu s$) | **$36ns$** | **~518x Faster** |
| **100 Routers** | $22,799ns$ ($22.7\mu s$) | **$257ns$** | **~88x Faster** |

author: Insideyyy
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
In case of a small M dimension and  using fp8_w8a8 on SM90, SwapAB brings significant benefit by transposing input A, B to make better use of `WGMMA`.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
SwapAB is enabled under all the following conditions:
- use_fp8_w8a8
- SM90 is supported
- config["BLOCK_SIZE_M"] < 64 and config["BLOCK_SIZE_N"] >= 64

title: [MTP][spec_v2] Fix TRTLLM MLA backend crash in EAGLE draft_extend mode
author: YAMY1234
body: ## Motivation Fix a crash in TRTLLM MLA backend during EAGLE speculative decoding in `draft_extend` mode when sequences have varying `accept_length` values. This can be reproduced by the following agg command (and also intermittency issues in the disagg setup in benchmark section): ``` SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1 SGLANG_FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_BACKEND=cutlass SGLANG_DISABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path ${MODEL} --served-model-name dsr1 --tp 4 --attention-backend trtllm_mla --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm --moe-dense-tp-size 1 --quantization modelopt_fp4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size -1 --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 2 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 3 --mem-fraction-static 0.80 ``` Error: ``` File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/trtllm_mla_backend.py", line 1046, in forward_extend q = q.view(bs, -1, layer.tp_q_head_num, layer.head_dim) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ RuntimeError: shape '[9, -1, 32, 576]' is invalid for input of size 516096 ``` ## Modifications 1. **`forward_extend`**: Added `can_direct_view` check to handle varying sequence lengths with padding/unpadding when `total_tokens % bs != 0` 2. **`init_forward_metadata_replay_cuda_graph`**: Fixed `seq_lens_q` computation to use `accept_length + 1` ## Accuracy Tests ```bash python -m sglang.test.run_eval \ --eval-name longbench_v2 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 \ --model nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-0528-NVFP4-v2 \ --max-context-length 128000 \ --max-tokens 16384 \ --num-threads 16 ``` **Score: 0.601** ## Benchmarking ``` decode_environment: hypothesis (default=1, set 8/16 to test) SGLANG_FUTURE_MAP_SCALE: '8' prefill_environment: DYN_SKIP_SGLANG_LOG_FORMATTING: '1' FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK: '1' FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE: Update Ascend LoRA backend for using new optimized kernels

title: Piecewise Cuda Graph Memory Usage
author: Oasis-Git
body: ## Motivation ### Memory Components We decompose GPU memory usage into three components: - **Non-Torch Memory** GPU memory not managed by PyTorch’s CUDA caching allocator. For Piecewise CUDA Graph (PCG), this mainly corresponds to CUDA Graph metadata and runtime bookkeeping. - **Torch Dynamic Pool Memory** Memory allocated from PyTorch’s default CUDA caching allocator during eager execution. - **Torch Private Pool Memory** A dedicated allocator pool created for CUDA Graph capture, which contains all graph-captured tensor allocations. In practice, PCG memory usage is primarily composed of **private pool memory and non-Torch memory**. ### Memory Measurement - **Torch-managed memory (dynamic + private pools)** We use `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()` to measure the combined footprint of PyTorch-managed allocations, including both dynamic and CUDA Graph private pools. - **Non-Torch memory (approximate)** Non-Torch memory is not directly observable through PyTorch APIs. We estimate it using CUDA OOM diagnostics emitted by PyTorch. Example: ``` Including non-PyTorch memory, this process has 139.32 GiB memory in use. Of the allocated memory 135.53 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, with 572.00 MiB allocated in private pools (e.g., CUDA Graphs), and 265.53 MiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated. ``` We estimate non-Torch memory as: ``` non_torch_memory = process_memory_in_use - torch_allocated_memory - torch_reserved_but_unallocated_memory ``` ### Experimental Results and Key Findings Detailed measurements, raw logs, and additional figures are available at: https://www.notion.so/PCG-memory-usage-2e19a415e571800d9c53f872456e25e9 #### Measurement Setup - **Qwen3-32B**, TP=2 - **LLaMA-70B**, TP=4 - **DeepSeek**, TP=8 - All experiments are conducted on **NVIDIA H200 GPUs** Each result reports extra memory usage relative to **PCG = 0**. #### Key Findings 1. **Torch memory usage from PCG private pools is small and stable** All piecewise CUDA graphs reuse the same private memory pool under the same CUDA Graph handler, so torch-managed memory growth from PCG is trivial and does not scale with PCG size. When capturing chunked prefill execution, torch memory usage can even drop below the non-graph baseline, since temporary activation buffers are absorbed into the CUDA Graph private pool. 2. **Non-Torch memory dominates PCG overhead** Non-Torch memory is the main contributor to PCG overhead and corresponds to CUDA Graph metadata and runtime bookkeeping. This overhead scales with the **number of CUDA Graph instances**, rather than the **maximum capture size** of a graph. ### Policy Decisions Based on these results, we adopt the following PCG configuration policies: 1. **Capture to chunk prefill size** Capture CUDA Graphs at the chunk prefill size so all smaller prefill sizes can reuse the same graph, maximizing reuse and reducing torch memory usage. 2. **Minimize the gap to large prefill sizes** Reduce the gap between PCG capture sizes and large prefill sizes to limit the number of CUDA Graph instances, since non-Torch memory scales with graph count. 3. **Conservative default for MLA models** For MLA models, where PCG affects attention dispatch behavior, we set the default PCG max capture size to **2048**. These policies ensure PCG achieves performance benefits while keeping both torch-managed and non-Torch memory overhead predictable and bounded. ## Modifications ## Accuracy Tests ## Benchmarking and Profiling With PR #15356 the pcg memory usage reduced from 5.32G to 1.45G for Llama 70B with TP=4. By now most of the memory usage of PCG can be controlled within 1.5G which can be accepted by default solution. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). - [ ] Work with maintainers to merge your PR. title: [model-gateway] optimize radix tree memory and reduce allocations
author: slin1237
body:
- Replace CharIndexedText with slice-based traversal to eliminate Vec<char> allocation per insert/match operation
- Add PrefixMatchResult to return char counts from tree operations, avoiding redundant chars().count() calls in cache_aware policy
- Use InsertStep enum to properly handle borrow checker constraints while maintaining thread-safe entry API semantics
- Fix partial match bug where wrong node was used for tenant selection

title: [Refactor] Clean up custom op
author: DarkSharpness
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
We observe that there're many direct use `torch.ops.sglang` in code, which is not friendly to IDE (especially for type checking). This is a result of custom op registration. Currently, registering a custom op requires:

1. Define the custom op `example_op`.
2. Define a fake implementation.
3. Call `direct_register_custom_op`.
4. After that, we can only use `torch.ops.sglang.example_op`.

The fake impl is mainly for torch compile compatibility and should return a tensor of correct shape. However, in most cases, the shape of the result is either `None` (in-place ops) or the same as one input tensor.

As a result, we propose to use a `register_custom_op` decorator to simplify this. This could be very useful in making new JIT kernel compatible with `torch.compile`.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

1. Add a decorator `register_custom_op` to simplify the registration.
2. Clean up most custom op registration.
3. Remove`supports_custom_op`. Currently, torch version in sglang dependency is greater than 2.4.0, which already supports custom op. This function will always return True, so we remove it.

title: [Performance] Force split_k=1 for MXFP4 Triton kernels on Hopper
author: mmangkad
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

This PR applies the optimization from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/30528.

It addresses a performance regression observed in Triton kernels on Hopper (sm90) GPUs during small batch size inference. Currently, the heuristic for split_k calculation often results in values greater than 1 for small batch sizes. This triggers the kernel to use torch.float32 accumulation instead of bf16, leading to significantly slower decoding performance without meaningful accuracy benefits.

By forcing split_k=1 for Hopper architectures, we ensure the kernel utilizes bf16 precision, restoring performance at low concurrency.

title: [model-gateway] Optimize HTTP Router Fan-out: Replace Serial Execution with Concurrent Streams
author: ppraneth
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->



## Motivation

This PR addresses a critical performance bottleneck in the `route_simple_request` function within the HTTP router. This function is responsible for "fan-out" operations where the location of a request state is unknown (e.g., `get_response`, `cancel_response`) or for broadcasting requests (e.g., `get_server_info`).

**The Issue:**
Previously, the implementation iterated through workers sequentially using a `for` loop and awaited each response inside the loop.

* **O(N) Latency:** The total latency was the sum of all worker response times checked before the target worker.
* **Head-of-Line Blocking:** If a single worker in the cluster was slow or unresponsive (e.g., timing out after 200ms), the entire control plane request would block for that duration, even if the healthy worker holding the data was ready to respond instantly.

**Goal:**
Switch to concurrent execution to decouple router latency from the health of the worst-performing worker.

## Modifications

* **Refactored `route_simple_request`** in `sgl-model-gateway/src/routers/http/router.rs`.
* **Concurrent Execution:** Replaced the serial `for` loop with `futures::stream::iter` combined with `.buffer_unordered(32)`. This allows requests to be sent to all workers simultaneously.
* **Early Return Optimization:** The stream now returns immediately upon receiving the first successful (2xx) response, cancelling pending requests to other workers.
* **Lifetime Fixes:** Explicitly collected futures into a `Vec` before streaming and properly cloned headers/API keys to satisfy Rust lifetime and ownership requirements for the async move blocks.

## Accuracy Tests


## Benchmarking and Profiling

A benchmark suite `benches/fanout_routing_bench.rs` was created to simulate a "degraded cluster" scenario:

* **Cluster:** 1 Slow Worker (200ms delay), 1 Target Worker (Instant 200 OK), N Filler Workers (Instant 404).
* **Metric:** Latency to retrieve the successful response.

**Results:**
The fix provides a **~900x to ~1400x improvement** in latency by effectively ignoring the slow worker.

| Cluster Size | Metric | Before Fix (Serial) | After Fix (Parallel) | Improvement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **10 Workers** | P99 Latency | ~203 ms | **0.22 ms** | **~920x Faster** |
| **100 Workers** | P99 Latency | ~203 ms | **0.14 ms** | **~1450x Faster** |
| **1000 Workers** | P99 Latency | ~203 ms | **0.21 ms** | **~960x Faster** |

**Full Benchmark Output (BeforeFix):**
```text
=== RESOURCE USAGE MONITOR ===
Cluster Size    | RPS        | P99 (ms)   | CPU (%)    
-------------------------------------------------------
10 Workers      | 197        | 253        | 5.75       
100 Workers     | 10150      | 3          | 4.48       
1000 Workers    | 238        | 208        | 4.22       

fanout_routing_latency/10
                        time:   [223.70 µs 233.16 µs 242.92 µs]
fanout_routing_latency/100
                        time:   [203.08 ms 203.21 ms 203.34 ms]
fanout_routing_latency/500
                        time:   [156.85 µs 162.41 µs 168.47 µs]
fanout_routing_latency/1000
                        time:   [203.32 ms 203.46 ms 203.61 ms]
```
**Full Benchmark Output (After Fix):**

```text
=== RESOURCE USAGE MONITOR ===
Cluster Size    | RPS        | P99 (ms)   | CPU (%)    
-------------------------------------------------------
10 Workers      | 288        | 172        | 4.37       
100 Workers     | 9832       | 4          | 4.06       
1000 Workers    | 7613       | 6          | 4.51       
================================
```

title: [model-gateway] Optimize radix tree timestamp updates for multi-tenant scaling
author: slin1237
body:
Replace O(depth) ancestor timestamp propagation with O(1) matched-node-only
updates. The ancestor propagation was unnecessary - eviction only uses leaf
timestamps, so updating ancestors had no effect on LRU behavior.

Changes:
- Remove ancestor timestamp propagation entirely
- Update only the matched node's timestamp (O(1) per match)
- Replace SystemTime::now() syscalls with atomic epoch counter
- Reduce timestamp size from 16 bytes (u128) to 8 bytes (u64)

Performance improvement:
- MATCH latency now flat across worker counts (15-19µs for 10-500 workers)
- Previously saw 2x degradation at 500 workers (20µs → 64µs)
- Eliminates DashMap contention from ancestor updates
- Zero syscall overhead with epoch counter

title: [model-gateway] Optimize INSERT with leaf-only timestamp updates
author: slin1237
body:
Apply same O(1) optimization to INSERT that we applied to MATCH. Intermediate node timestamps are never used - eviction only checks leaf timestamps via leaf_of(). Skip redundant O(depth) updates.

Changes:
- Root: use or_insert(0) instead of insert(epoch)
- Intermediate nodes: only ensure tenant exists, don't update timestamp
- Leaf node: update timestamp after loop or when creating new node
- Lazy char count: only compute chars().count() when creating leaf

Performance improvement:
- INSERT now 6-7x faster (52-64µs → 7-11µs)
- Flat scaling across worker counts

title: [model-gateway]: optimize prefix_match with zero-copy tenant and deferred char count
author: slin1237
body:
Reduce MATCH operation latency from ~64µs to ~22µs (3x improvement):

- Change tenant from String to TenantId (Arc<str>) for zero-copy return
- Remove matched_text from PrefixMatchResult (legacy API computes separately)
- Defer input_char_count computation: matched_chars + remaining.chars().count()
- Eliminates upfront O(n) chars().count() call on input text

Benchmarks (500 workers):
- Before: MATCH ~64µs (degraded with worker count)
- After:  MATCH ~22µs (flat scaling)

title: [Build] Enable full kernel in aarch64 wheel
author: MarcoDWei
body:
Use environment variables to make the aarch64 kernel wheel include support for all NV GPU kernels. To avoid impacting CI efficiency, this full build is only enabled when publishing the sgl-kernel wheel.

## Motivation

Currently, compared with x86, the sgl-kernel wheel on aarch64 lacks support for certain GPUs, mainly those with gpu arch <sm90. This results in users being unable to use some older GPUs out of the box on general-purpose arm64 servers.

## Modifications

Introduce environment variable to control full kernel build on aarch64 platform. Enable it in the wheel release workflow.

## Tests

The test of releasing workflow has not done, which needs to do in the github repo.
.

title: Refactor speculative algorithm registry.
author: hnyls2002
body:
Prev code is overly complex and provides no practical benefit for the current design.

- Speculative algorithms are static in practice and do not require a dynamic registry.
- The set of speculative algorithms is small and well-defined, and can be safely hardcoded.
- The lock is unnecessary, as there is no runtime mutation or concurrent registration.
- The alias mechanism is unused in practice, since `NEXTN` is already normalized to `EAGLE` in server args.
- The tag-based design is redundant; existing semantics are fully covered by `is_eagle()`, which naturally includes `is_eagle3()`.
- `_registration_order` is unused, as we never iterate over speculative algorithms and there are only a few fixed entries.

**If private forks need additional customization**, they can add explicit enum values or auxiliary dicts/lists alongside the enum, without introducing a global dynamic registry.

title: [VLM] Adopt jit qk_norm kernel in VLM
author: yuan-luo
body: ## Motivation https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/15835 introduced jit qk_norm kernel which is powerful. This PR is to adopt it in VLM VisionAttention to boost up. Introduced a kernel dispatcher: when the JIT kernel compilation occasionally fails, we fall back to the legacy fused kernel as a safeguard. title: perf(tree): optimize input_char_count calculation
author: slin1237
body:
Remove advance_by_chars call in partial match case by computing input_char_count directly from input text instead of tracking remaining slice through traversal.

This eliminates overhead in the hot path while maintaining correctness. The sum (matched_chars + remaining.chars().count()) is mathematically equivalent to text.chars().count().

title: [model-gateway] Optimize L1 cache insertion with incremental hashing and tokenization
author: ppraneth
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->



## Motivation

The current L1 cache implementation suffers from a performance bottleneck when handling long, multi-turn conversations. The original design re-hashed and re-tokenized the entire prefix for every special token boundary found in the prompt.

This resulted in **quadratic O(N²) scaling behavior**: as a conversation grows longer, the time spent inserting into the cache increases disproportionately to the length of the text. This PR refactors the logic to achieve **linear O(N) scaling**, ensuring the gateway remains efficient for workloads with large context windows or frequent turn-based updates.

## Modifications

The following changes were made to the L1 cache logic in `src/tokenizer/cache/l1.rs`:

* **Incremental Hashing**: Full-string hashing at every boundary was replaced with a forward pass using `blake3::Hasher`. The hasher is updated incrementally with only the "delta" text between boundaries, allowing all prefix hashes to be computed in a single linear pass.
* **Incremental Tokenization**: The insertion logic was updated to tokenize only the new text segment between two safe boundaries. These tokens are appended to a running list, leveraging the fact that special tokens are atomic split points.
* **BOS Handling**: Logic was adjusted to ensure special tokens (such as the BOS token) are only added during the tokenization of the very first segment. This prevents the cache from incorrectly duplicating BOS tokens in every cached prefix entry.

## Accuracy Tests



## Benchmarking and Profiling

Benchmarks performed with Criterion on a simulated ChatML prompt show a massive improvement in insertion scalability, accompanied by a minor and acceptable tradeoff in lookup latency.

### Insertion Performance (Scaling Fix)

The optimization successfully eliminated the  scaling bottleneck:

| Turns | Baseline (Original) | Optimized | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 Turns | 60.37 µs | 58.13 µs | ~1.04x |
| 10 Turns | 327.91 µs | 91.95 µs | **~3.5x** |
| 50 Turns | 5.82 ms | 283.43 µs | **~20.5x** |

### Lookup Tradeoff

There is a noted regression in `longest_prefix_match` latency. To support incremental hashing, the lookup now performs a full forward pass to pre-compute hashes for all boundaries before checking the cache shards.

* **Lookup (50 turns)**: Latency increased from **20.25 µs** to **94.69 µs**.

**Overall Result**: While lookup is slightly slower, it remains sub-millisecond and is a negligible cost compared to model inference steps. The ~20x performance gain during insertion ensures the system no longer faces a "performance cliff" as chat turn counts grow.

title: [diffusion] Qwen-Image perf: mul add fusion
author: yingluosanqian
body: ## Motivation Speed up Qwen-Image through kernel fusion. I carefully analyzed the performance bottlenecks of Qwen Image, focusing on the MMDiT block, and drew out its structural decomposition. Based on this analysis, I found that the current implementation still has room for optimization. In particular, I plan to fuse as many memory-bound kernels as possible (highlighted as blue rectangles in the diagram). As below figure shows, I group the computation into three large fused operators. The QwenImageEdit MMDit block is slightly different: its image branch introduces an additional modulated index, which requires conditional selection based on a 0/1 mask. As a result, it needs extra fused kernels to handle this logic. My plan consists of the following three parts: 1. norm_scale_shift and scale_residual_norm_scale_shift (implemented in [this PR](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/14717)) 2. norm_scale_shift_select01 and scale_residual_norm_scale_shift_select01 (TODO. not in this PR) 3. scale_shift (this PR) ## Modifications To avoid duplicating kernels, this implementation modifies the existing triton kernel to support a more general form, namely `a * b + c`. The original kernel implemented x * (1 + scale) + shift, and we extend it to handle the generalized case x * (0 + scale) + shift. `scale_constant` is marked as a compile-time value since it only takes 0 or 1, avoiding runtime perf loss. ## Accuracy Tests E2E test `sglang generate --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image --prompt "A Logo With Bold Large Text: SGL Diffusion" --seed 0` ## Benchmarking and Profiling Before fusing: 55 us per forward After fusing: 20 us per forward ## Checklist ## Review Process 1. title: [Feature][NPU]: add runtime support for GPTQ-quantized MoE models
author: YChange01
body:
## Stacked PR Notice

> **This PR depends on and includes changes from #15203.**

---

## PR Description

This PR introduces support for running **GPTQ-quantized Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models** on Huawei Ascend (NPU) hardware.

Previously, GPTQ support was primarily optimized for CUDA backends. Loading MoE architectures on NPU would cause runtime errors (e.g., `GPTQ Method does not support MoE, please use gptq_marlin`) because the specific quantization method for Ascend was missing.

### Key Changes

1.  **New MoE Method**: Added `GPTQMoEAscendMethod`, inheriting from `FusedMoEMethodBase`, to handle MoE-specific quantization logic on Ascend.
2.  **Configuration Update**: Integrated the new method into `GPTQConfig.get_quant_method()`. This ensures that MoE layers are correctly identified and handled, preventing the "method not supported" exception.
3.  **Dependency Integration**: Utilizes `GPTQLinearAscendMethod` (from #15203) as the underlying implementation for linear projections.
4.  **Model Support**: Verified loading and inference support for GPTQ-quantized **Qwen-MoE** models on Ascend NPU.

## Motivation

We observed that when launching the Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct model with sglang, an OOM (Out-of-Memory) error occurs under high-concurrency inference. After analyzing the profiling data, we found that the feature attribute is persistently stored on the device (NPU), while only the concatenated tensor (result of torch.cat) is actually used in computation.

title: [DeepSeek 3.2] Support and optimize pipeline parallelis when context pipeline enabled
author: xu-yfei
body: ## Motivation For issue #15358. CC @whybeyoung Support pipeline parallelism for the Prefill CP scenario (`--enable-nsa-prefill-context-parallel`). In this scenario, the linear layer of attention uses repeated weights, and the received input is scattered. Therefore, the attention TP group does not need to perform an `all_gather` operation during PP send/recv. Optimize the indexer as follows: In the case of PP parallelism, part of the model execution may run in parallel with the PP recv operation, which occupies an additional SM resource. Thus, the total number of SMs allocated to the indexer’s `deep_gemm.fp8_mqa_logits` must be reduced by 1. As shown in the figure below, for `deep_gemm.fp8_mqa_logits` on the first node (i.e., PP rank = 0), the latency is 1.312 ms when it does not overlap with the PP `recv` operation, and increases to 2.211 ms when overlapped with the `recv` operator. Analysis reveals that `deep_gemm.fp8_mqa_logits` occupies all SMs by default. In the H20 scenario, the grid is (78,). However, since the recv operator already occupies 1 SM, the latency of `deep_gemm.fp8_mqa_logits` increases significantly. Solution: In the PP scenario, we reduce the number of SMs for `deep_gemm.fp8_mqa_logits` by calling `deep_gemm.set_num_sms`, so as to maintain the performance of `deep_gemm.fp8_mqa_logits`. title: Use high-priority CUDA stream for overlap scheduling to reduce CPU bubbles
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Motivation

In SGLang's overlap scheduling mode, the scheduler and forward pass run on separate CUDA streams concurrently. The scheduler stream handles request selection and batch preparation while the forward stream runs model inference.

We observed that when the scheduling logic runs on the **default stream**, the CUDA runtime can delay its kernel launches — especially when many streams are active. This creates **CPU bubbles**: idle gaps where the forward stream has finished but the next batch isn't ready because the scheduler hasn't dispatched its kernels in time.

## Changes

1. **Create a dedicated high-priority scheduling stream** (`priority=0`, the highest CUDA stream priority) so that scheduling kernels are dispatched more eagerly by the CUDA runtime, tightening the overlap pipeline.

2. **Rename `default_stream` → `schedule_stream`** across `scheduler.py` and `scheduler_pp_mixin.py` to accurately reflect its role — it is no longer the CUDA default stream.

3. **Refactor `dispatch_event_loop()`** into a standalone function for clarity, and wrap the event loop entry point with the new high-priority stream context.

## Note

This change is purely about CUDA stream scheduling priority. It does not affect memory allocation, prefix caching (RadixAttention), or any KV cache behavior.

title: Optimizing all_reduce in RMSNormTP in minimax_m2
author: rogeryoungh
body: ## Motivation In RMSNormTP, the cross-device reduction uses an intermediate tensor of shape B × 2 in fp32. The `sglang::cross_device_reduce_1stage` reduction path requires the reduced tensor to be 16-byte aligned, which is satisfied iff B is even in the current implementation. This PR enforces alignment by rounding up the intermediate tensor size, ensuring the 1-stage path is consistently selected. title: [EPD][Perf] parallelize ZMQ send for encode server
author: ZhengWG
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

ZMQ socket operations (connect/send) were blocking the event loop, causing multiple send tasks to execute serially instead of in parallel. This resulted in `gather_tasks` time being the sum of all task times.

## Modifications

Use thread pool executor to execute ZMQ socket creation, connection, and send operations in parallel, avoiding event loop blocking. Reuse synchronous ZMQ context across threads (thread-safe).

title: [DSv32] Overlap indexer weights_proj during dual_stream decode
author: zianglih

title: [diffusion]Optimize linear calculation in sparse linear attention
author: IPostYellow
body: ## Motivation Convert native Python operators into PyTorch functions ## Modifications ## Accuracy Tests Run this function to diff the accuracy between the two methods: ``` import torch import torch.nn.functional as F def original_calc_linear(q, k, v): kvsum = k.transpose(-1, -2) @ v ksum = torch.sum(k, dim=-2, keepdim=True) return (q @ kvsum) / (1e-5 + (q * ksum).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)) def torch_calc_linear(q, k, v): kv = torch.matmul(k.transpose(-1, -2), v) k_sum = torch.sum(k, dim=-2, keepdim=True) return torch.matmul(q, kv) / (1e-5 + torch.matmul(q, k_sum.transpose(-1, -2))) for seed in [0, 42, 128, 1024]: # set seed torch.manual_seed(seed) # test case # B, H, L, D = 1, 12, 32760, 128 B, H, L, D = 1, 40, 32760, 128 q = torch.randn(B, H, L, D) k = torch.randn(B, H, L, D) v = torch.randn(B, H, L, D) q = F.softmax(q, dim=-1) k = F.softmax(k, dim=-1) # result original = original_calc_linear(q, k, v) optimized = torch_calc_linear(q, k, v) # diff abs_error = torch.abs(original - optimized) rel_error = abs_error / (torch.abs(original) + 1e-8) print(f"=== seed {seed} result ===") print(f"Maximum Absolute Error: {abs_error.max().item():.2e}") print(f"Mean Absolute Error: {abs_error.mean().item():.2e}") print(f"Maximum Relative Error: {rel_error.max().item():.2e}") print(f"Mean Relative Error: {rel_error.mean().item():.2e}") # Cosine Similarity original_flat = original.flatten() optimized_flat = optimized.flatten() cosine_sim = torch.nn.functional.cosine_similarity( original_flat, optimized_flat, dim=0 ) print(f"Cosine Similarity: {cosine_sim.item():.6f}") # range print(f"original range: [{original.min().item():.4f}, {original.max().item():.4f}]") print( f"optimized range: [{optimized.min().item():.4f}, {optimized.max().item():.4f}]" ) print(f"=========================") ``` Here is the result: ``` === seed 0 result === Maximum Absolute Error: 1.49e-08 Mean Absolute Error: 5.42e-10 Maximum Relative Error: 8.27e-07 Mean Relative Error: 1.22e-07 Cosine Similarity: 1.049392 original range: [-0.0244, 0.0247] optimized range: [-0.0244, 0.0247] ========================= === seed 42 result === Maximum Absolute Error: 1.49e-08 Mean Absolute Error: 5.38e-10 Maximum Relative Error: 9.29e-07 Mean Relative Error: 1.21e-07 Cosine Similarity: 1.046934 original range: [-0.0280, 0.0259] optimized range: [-0.0280, 0.0259] ========================= === seed 128 result === Maximum Absolute Error: 1.49e-08 Mean Absolute Error: 5.41e-10 Maximum Relative Error: 9.19e-07 Mean Relative Error: 1.21e-07 Cosine Similarity: 1.047465 original range: [-0.0268, 0.0283] optimized range: [-0.0268, 0.0283] ========================= === seed 1024 result === Maximum Absolute Error: 1.30e-08 Mean Absolute Error: 5.35e-10 Maximum Relative Error: 9.15e-07 Mean Relative Error: 1.22e-07 Cosine Similarity: 1.046048 original range: [-0.0244, 0.0235] optimized range: [-0.0244, 0.0235] ========================= ``` Results show errors are essentially within 1e-07, indicating the two are numerically equivalent. And here is the end2end result in TurboWan2.1-T2V-14B-720P-Diffusers : prompt1: `A stylish woman walks down a Tokyo street filled with warm glowing neon and animated city signage. She wears a black leather jacket, a long red dress, and black boots, and carries a black purse. She wears sunglasses and red lipstick. She walks confidently and casually. The street is damp and reflective, creating a mirror effect of the colorful lights. Many pedestrians walk about.` Baseline linear calculation result: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6556be3f-51ce-42d4-93d6-85128b76f4a3 Optimized linear calculation result: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f7b2783-63fc-4365-9aa4-1f5d65ebf5eb prompt2: `A dramatic and dynamic scene in the style of a disaster movie, depicting a powerful tsunami rushing through a narrow alley in Bulgaria. title: [diffusion] model: wan tp+usp optimize
author: triple-mu
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

The current tensor parallel (TP) implementation only uses ColumnParallelLinear, which requires gather_output and introduces non-trivial communication overhead.
Using a ColumnParallelLinear + RowParallelLinear combination avoids this, but exposes an issue: the existing RMSNorm does not support TP-sharded inputs and produces incorrect results.

*Impact*
Lower communication overhead under tensor parallelism
Correct RMSNorm behavior with Col+Row parallel linear layers
No redundant attention computation when TP and Ulysses Parallel are enabled

## Modifications

Use ColumnParallelLinear + RowParallelLinear to reduce TP communication by avoiding gather_output
Add tensor-parallel support to RMSNorm to ensure correct normalization on sharded tensors
When tensor parallel and Ulysses Parallel are both enabled, attention num_heads is correctly sharded by tp × usp, avoiding redundant computation

title: [AMD][Diffusion] support timestep embedding kernel for AMD GPUs
author: hubertlu-tw
body: ## Motivation This PR supports `timestep_embedding `in `sgl-kernel` for AMD GPUs. ## Modifications - Modified flux.py so that the faster code path using `timestep_embedding `in `sgl-kernel` will be called. - Removed redundant args in rocm.Dockerfile - Update installation instruction in SGLang documentation for AMD GPUs - Included necessary code changes in sgl-kernel to support `timestep_embedding` kernel ## Accuracy Tests ``` cd sgl-kernel pytest -q tests/sgl_diffusion/test_timestep_embedding.py ========================================================================================== 1073 passed, 2 warnings in 6.50s =========================================================================================== ``` ## Benchmarking and Profiling ``` cd /sgl-workspace/hubert_sgl && python -c " import sys import os sys.path.insert(0, 'sgl-kernel') os.chdir('sgl-kernel') import numpy as np import torch import tabulate from diffusers.models.embeddings import get_timestep_embedding from sgl_kernel.elementwise import timestep_embedding as timestep_embedding_cuda from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.visual_embedding import timestep_embedding def test_timestep_embedding_perf(): NUM_BATCH = [1, 2, 8, 63, 256, 512, 613, 1024, 1536] NUM_DIM = [32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096] def perf_kernel_fn(kernel_fn, *args, **kwargs): warmup_times = 4 repeat_times = 20 start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(warmup_times): output_fn = kernel_fn(*args, **kwargs) torch.cuda.synchronize() start.record() for _ in range(repeat_times): output_fn = kernel_fn(*args, **kwargs) end.record() end.synchronize() return start.elapsed_time(end) / repeat_times device = 'cuda' results = [] cuda_speedups = [] for B in NUM_BATCH: for dim in NUM_DIM: t = torch.linspace(0, max(100000, B), steps=B, device=device).to(torch.int32) time_torch = perf_kernel_fn(timestep_embedding, t, dim) time_cuda = perf_kernel_fn(timestep_embedding_cuda, t, dim) speedup_cuda = time_torch / time_cuda results.append({ 'Batch Size': B, 'Dimension': dim, 'Torch Time (ms)': time_torch, 'CUDA Time (ms)': time_cuda, 'Speedup (CUDA)': speedup_cuda, }) cuda_speedups.append(speedup_cuda) print('=== Timestep Embedding Benchmark Results ===') print(tabulate.tabulate( results, headers='keys', tablefmt='fancy_grid', floatfmt=('.0f', '.0f', '.6f', '.6f', '.5f'), )) print(f'Average Speedup(cuda): {np.mean(cuda_speedups):.4f}') test_timestep_embedding_perf() " ``` Average speedup: 4.89x on MI355 This kernel results in about 0.87% perf improvement (from 4244.044 ms to 4206.992 ms) for the following usage: ``` sglang generate \ --model-path black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev \ --prompt "A curious raccoon peers through a vibrant field of yellow sunflowers, its eyes wide with interest." \ --perf-dump-path perf_sgl.json ``` The performance improvement is marginal because the bottleneck is in the DenoisingStage (attention/GEMMs) rather than in the timestep embedding kernel optimized in this PR. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with title: Refactor(qwen3-vl) optimize position encoding interpolation
author: aaaandychen
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Sync Slime patches. Optimize fast_pos_embed_interpolate for Qwen3-VL by vectorizing core embedding lookups and interpolation math. This reduces GPU kernel launch overhead and improves throughput during batched inference.

related: [THUDM/slime#1316](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/issues/1316)

## Modifications
python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py
Refactor fast_pos_embed_interpolate
- **Metadata Aggregation** Collect interpolation indices and weights within a loop to prepare for batch processing.Supplemented align_corners=False logic by referencing PyTorch's coordinate calculation in [UpSample.h](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/native/UpSample.h).
- **Batched Execution** Perform a single vectorized embedding lookup and weighted summation to minimize kernel overhead.
- **Reshaping & Compatibility** Reshape outputs to the required format.

test/srt/test_embed_interpolate_unittest.py
Refactor test input of fast_pos_embed_interpolate from `list` to `torch.Tensor` to align with existing methods.

title: [model-gateway] Restore response streaming by optimizing WASM middleware buffering
author: ppraneth
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->



## Motivation

The previous implementation of the WebAssembly (WASM) middleware in `src/middleware.rs` introduced a performance bottleneck . Whenever WASM was enabled, the middleware unconditionally called `axum::body::to_bytes` on both the incoming request body and the outgoing response body.

This approach had two major negative impacts:

1. **Broken Streaming**: Calling `to_bytes` on a response forces the gateway to buffer the entire generated output before sending the first token to the client. This completely negates the low-latency benefits of LLM streaming.
2. **High Latency (TTFT)**: Clients experienced a Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) delay equal to the full generation time of the model.


## Modifications

The `wasm_middleware` function was refactored to implement a "fast-path" mechanism that avoids buffering unless a WASM module is actually registered to process the payload at a specific attach point:

* **Request Phase Optimization**: Added a check to determine if any modules are registered for the `OnRequest` attach point. If no modules are active, the request is passed to the next service immediately without buffering the body.
* **Response Phase Optimization**: Added an early return check after receiving the response from the worker. If no modules are registered for the `OnResponse` attach point, the response stream is returned to the client immediately.
* **Code Structure**: Integrated the response phase logic directly into the flow to ensure the stream is preserved and handed back to Axum as early as possible.

## Accuracy Tests

This PR does not modify the model kernel or forward logic. It strictly optimizes the HTTP proxying layer. 

## Benchmarking and Profiling

A benchmark was conducted using a mock worker that simulates a 500ms delay between the first and second response chunks to represent model generation time.

| Metric | Pre-fix (Unconditional Buffering) | Post-fix (Fast-path Optimization) | Improvement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **First Frame Latency** | **~501.35 ms** | **~26.71 µs** | **~18,700x faster** |

author: PrinsYin
body:
Linked issue: https://github.com/THUDM/slime/issues/1316

## Summary
- Add DeepEP a2a support to `RoutedExpertsCapturer` (rebased onto `srt/state_capturer/` after #24450)

title: [DeepSeek v3.2] Opt MTP decode cuda batch sizes and nsa implementation
author: xu-yfei
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
1、`draft_extend` and `target_verify` use `nsa_decode_backend` as backend implementation instead of `nsa_prefill_backend`
In the MTP scenario, the NSA attention implementation selected for `prefill`, `draft_extend`, and `target_verify` is all `nsa_prefill_backend`, which is typically set to `flashmla_sparse`. For `draft_extend` and `target_verify` scenarios with a small number of tokens, we observed that `fa3` delivers better performance. However, when `flashmla_sparse` is chosen for `prefill,` there is no interface to additionally specify the NSA attention implementation for `draft_extend` and `target_verify`. This PR modifies the backend implementation of `draft_extend` and `target_verify` to `nsa_decode_backend` —in practice, their CUDA Graph initialization and replay already use `nsa_decode_impl`.

num_draft_tokens=4, TPOT:
| batch size | flashmla_sparse | fa3   |
|------------|-----------------|-------|
| 1          | 11.87           | 9.44  |
| 2          | 13.34           | 13.08 |
| 8          | 15.25           | 15.87 |
| 16         | 21.25           | 21.50|
| 32         | 32.94           | 33.79 |

2、Opt cuda graph batch sizes when MTP:
In the Prefill CP scenario, `require_gathered_buffer` is set to True. Assuming the number of MTP num_draft_tokens is `4`, the CUDA Graph tokens in the MTP scenario are calculated as follows:
`get_batch_sizes_to_capture` returns batch sizes that are multiples of `attn_tp_size`, i.e., `[8, 16, 24, 32, ....]`.
In `capture_one_batch_size`, `num_tokens = bs * self.num_tokens_per_bs`, meaning the actual number of tokens is `[32, 64, 96, 128, ...]`.
When `bs=1`, the number of tokens is `4` but needs to be padded to `32`, resulting in significant performance overhead. In reality, `num_tokens` only needs to be a multiple of `attn_tp_size`.
Modification: `get_batch_sizes_to_capture` is updated to return batch sizes where `batch size * num_draft_tokens` is divisible by `attn_tp_size`, i.e., `[2, 4, 6, 8, ....]`.

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

title: Feat/support nemotron h mtp
author: shaharmor98
body:
## Motivation
This PR adds Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) speculative decoding support for NemotronH hybrid Mamba2/Attention models.

## Modifications
#### New NemotronH MTP Model (nemotron_h_mtp.py)

- Introduced `NemotronHForCausalLMMTP` model class for MTP-based speculative decoding
- Added `NemotronHMTPAttentionDecoderLayer` and `NemotronHMTPMoEDecoderLayer` that extend base `NemotronH` layers
- Implemented `NemotronHMultiTokenPredictor` that processes the hybrid layer pattern

Note: Two decoder layers were added (for both attention and MoE), since future versions might reverse the MTP layers. That is, we assume the first layer has the layer projections, while the last has a layer norm. However, it’s not guaranteed that attention will appear immediately after the layer projections, nor that the MoE layer will appear before the layer norm. Therefore, the current implementation allows future architecture modifications without code changes.

## Accuracy Tests
MTP support has been internally tested on the upcoming Nemotron-Super checkpoint.
Since the model isn’t public yet, we can’t expose internal results.


## Review Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the PR flow. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`, `/tag-and-rerun-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls to merge.

title: Add 5090 dry run stage to PR test workflow
author: alisonshao
body:
## Summary

Add a new `stage-b-test-small-1-gpu-5090` job to the PR test workflow for dry-running tests on RTX 5090 runners.

### Key Points

- **Runs in parallel** with existing stage-b tests (after stage-a)
- **NOT required for PR merge** - not in `pr-test-finish` needs
- **NOT blocking** - uses `continue-on-error: true`
- **5 partitions** running **118 test files** registered to `stage-b-test-small-1-gpu-5090` suite

### Configuration

| Setting | Value |
|---------|-------|
| Runner | `1-gpu-5090` |
| Partitions | 5 |
| Suite | `stage-b-test-small-1-gpu-5090` |
| IS_BLACKWELL | `1` |

### Test Registration

Added `register_cuda_ci(est_time=X, suite="stage-b-test-small-1-gpu-5090")` to 1 gpu test files:
- Used actual elapsed times from 5090 workflow run [20954749819](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/20954749819) where available 
- Used existing `est_time` values for tests without 5090 data 

### Purpose

This allows us to monitor 5090 test stability on real PRs before fully integrating 5090 runners into the required CI pipeline. After a day of dry-running, we can evaluate results and decide on next steps.

### Changes

1. Added `stage-b-test-small-1-gpu-5090` job to `.github/workflows/pr-test.yml`
2. Added stage to `scripts/ci/slash_command_handler.py` for `/rerun-stage` support
3. Added suite to `test/run_suite.py` PER_COMMIT_SUITES
4. Registered 118 test files to new `stage-b-test-small-1-gpu-5090` suite

title: feat: Priority-based scheduling optimization (including default priority, preemption toggle, priority-based metrics, etc.)
author: zhuxinjie-nz
body: ## Motivation During the use of priority-based scheduling, we identified several issues: 1. The original priority scheduling logic does not support setting a default priority. 2. The preemption logic introduces certain risks in our specific business scenario, so we need a configurable toggle to enable or disable preemption. 3. We require metrics to support performance analysis based on priority-based scheduling. ## Modifications Built upon the original priority-based scheduling, several optimizations have been implemented, including support for setting a default priority, adding a toggle for preemption logic, and introducing priority-based metrics. ## Benchmarking and Profiling ### Queueing behavior under high and low priority Starting from concurrency level 40, requests begin to queue, with the number of queued low-priority requests significantly higher than that of high-priority ones, which aligns with expectations. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [DeepSeek V3.2] [Bugfix] slice indexer and padding fa3 when can not run cuda graph
author: xu-yfei
body: ## Motivation This PR #15227 only resolves the issue occurring during `forward_idle`. If running in Eagle mode (MTP Spec2, batch size exceeding the CUDA maximum batch size, or with `disable-cuda-graph` enabled), the DP padding mode is set to `MAX_LEN`, or the `attn_tp_size` > 1, padding may be applied to tokens or batch sizes. In such cases, a batch size misalignment issue will occur, leading to errors in both the indexer and FA3. 1、Fixed the issue where in ds3.2 cp, decode and draft extend does not support eagle. The reason is that - The input is padded via `prepare_mlp_sync_batch`, and `nsa_cache_seqlens_int32` also needs to be padded; otherwise, the fa3 implementation will report a mismatch in input batch size. - The input `q_fp8` and `weights` in `deep_gemm.fp8_paged_mqa_logits` have been padded , while the batch sizes of other inputs such as `block_tables` remain the actual batch size. There is a need to retrieve `q_fp8` and `weights` corresponding to the actual batch. ~~2、Added support for ds3.2 spec v2 draft extend cuda graph mode.~~ ~~3、Optimized the calculation of title: [Fix] GLM 4.7 + NVFP4 + MTP
author: b8zhong
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

A few issues reported by @ynwang007 @JustinTong0323

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

1. We will face an error in loading the draft model with NVFP4 due to some inheritance relationship. Instead of deleting the detection from `modelopt -> modelopt_fp4` in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/16581 I think this detection might be a better method.
2. Hardcode a fix for GLM 4.7 FP4 checkpoint + MTP: Essentially, `safetensors.index.json` should be mapping (you can thnkn of it like symlink) the layer 92 weights → `mtp.safetensors` (technically, models like Deepseek store these within the rest of the weights as an additional layer, but I suppose GLM simply decided to do it differently), into a `mtp.safetensors` file seperately, but during the creation with the ModelOpt library it was not added to the index. Instead we can automatically detect this is the case, warn the user about this invalid checkpoint, but still do the remapping online if we have `mtp.safetensors`.
3. Enable `trtllm-gen` automatically, which has much better performance than the CUTLASS backend  (requires Flashinfer 0.6.2 which will be released later) after a small fix in https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/2313.


<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

body: ## Motivation From these pr[https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/16637 and https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/16861 and https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/13459/files], we know weights_proj is a relatively time-consuming operation.Although weights_proj is stored in BF16 precision in Hugging-Face, it is calculated in FP32 precision in SGLang. title: fix tp capture in vit cuda graph
author: narutolhy
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

When using the ViT CUDA Graph runner with Tensor Parallelism enabled, CUDA Graph capture may implicitly involve TP communication paths (e.g., all-reduce or capture-aware communicators). However, the existing implementation does not align the communicator’s capture lifecycle with torch.cuda.graph(...), which can lead to incorrect capture behavior, runtime errors, or hangs during replay in TP setups.

This PR ensures that TP communication (when capture-aware) is properly included in the CUDA Graph capture phase, improving correctness and stability for ViT graph execution under Tensor Parallelism.

## Modifications

Updated python/sglang/srt/multimodal/vit_cuda_graph_runner.py to correctly handle TP communication during CUDA Graph capture.

Introduced nullcontext to provide a zero-overhead fallback when no capture-aware communicator is present.

Retrieved the current TP group via get_tp_group() and conditionally wrapped CUDA Graph capture with tp_group.ca_comm.capture() when available.

The final capture logic becomes:

Use ca_comm.capture() only if the TP group provides a capture-aware communicator.

Preserve the original behavior when no such communicator exists.

This change is strictly scoped to the CUDA Graph creation path and does not affect non-TP or non-graph execution.

## Accuracy Tests

covered in test_vlm_vit_cuda_graph.py

title: [FIX] Always support TP > 4 for FP4 Gemm
author: danielafrimi
body:
**Summary**
This PR enables FP4 (NVFP4) quantization to work with TP >= 4

**Background**
Previously, FP4 quantized models would fail to initialize with TP=4/8 due to kernel alignment requirements. The FlashInfer-CUTLASS FP4 GEMM kernels require the N/K-dimension to be divisible by 32.

**Changes**
This PR makes the following changes to support TP >= 4, by padding the weights accordingly. In addition, in cases where we pad the K dim of the weights, we need to pad the activation in the forward pass.

_rms_norm_tiled_onepass( y_ptr, x_ptr, w_ptr, SEQ: tl.constexpr, DIM: tl.constexpr, EPS: tl.constexpr, BLOCK_SIZE_SEQ: tl.constexpr, BLOCK_SIZE_DIM: tl.constexpr, ): seq_blk_id = tl.program_id(0) title: Revert "[Perf] fuse q, k norm for Flux2Attention (#17241)"
author: BBuf
body:
Reverts sgl-project/sglang#17241

First, not implementing a fallback when applying qk_norm will break the [AMD diffusion CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/21085222138/job/60680696502). Second, the decision to use qknorm should be based on whether `can_use_fused_inplace_qknorm` returns true, rather than being applied directly. Third, converting non-contiguous q and k tensors directly to contiguous here is a performance-sensitive operation and should not be done. Even though this is dead code, it should not be written this way. Finally, a warmup should be add in performace test command.

Please refer to: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/17305

And I will refactor diffusion qk_norm apply logic to make it easier to use in the future.

cc @mickqian @yhyang201 @zminglei

title: [model-gateway] Optimize WASM cache lookups using SHA-256
author: ppraneth
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

The `WasmThreadPool` currently uses the raw WASM binary (`Vec<u8>`) as the key for its internal `component_cache`. This approach is inefficient for two main reasons:

1. **Memory Overhead**: For large WASM components, storing the full binary as a key in the LRU cache significantly increases memory consumption in every worker thread.
2. **CPU Overhead**: Every request lookup requires hashing and potentially performing a byte-by-byte comparison (`O(N)`) of the entire binary to verify a cache hit.

This PR transitions the system to use the SHA-256 hash which is already calculated and stored in the module metadata during registration as the unique identifier for cache lookups, turning an  comparison into a constant-time  operation.

## Modifications

* **Wasm Runtime**: Updated the `WasmTask` enum in `src/wasm/runtime.rs` to include a 32-byte `wasm_hash` field.
* **Cache Optimization**: Refactored the `WasmThreadPool` and its worker loop to use `LruCache<[u8; 32], Component>` instead of `LruCache<Vec<u8>, Component>`.
* **Module Manager**: Modified `execute_module_interface` in `src/wasm/module_manager.rs` to retrieve the pre-calculated `sha256_hash` from the `WasmModuleMeta` and pass it to the runtime during execution.
* **Worker Logic**: Updated `execute_component_in_worker` to utilize the 32-byte hash for efficient lookups. The raw `wasm_bytes` are now only used for compilation on a cache miss and are dropped immediately after.

## Accuracy Tests



## Benchmarking and Profiling

Performance was measured using a ~1MB WASM component to simulate the overhead of large binary comparisons.

* **Baseline (Pre-optimization)**: ~1.16 ms per hot lookup.
* **Post-optimization (Hash-based)**: ~429 µs per hot lookup.
* **Result**: ~2.7x speedup in the cache lookup hot path, accompanied by a significant reduction in memory pressure across the thread pool.

title: [model-gateway] Optimize special token search using Aho-Corasick
author: ppraneth
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->



## Motivation

The current implementation of `StopSequenceDecoder` uses a naive nested loop to search for stop sequences and special tokens. This results in $O(N \times M)$ time complexity (where $N$ is text length and $M$ is the number of tokens), causing spikes as the number of stop sequences increases.

## Modifications

* Replaced the nested `.find()` and `.starts_with()` loops in `src/tokenizer/stop.rs` with a single-pass **Aho-Corasick automaton**.
* Combined hidden and visible stop sequences into a single automaton pass.
* Added `visible_boundary_idx` to efficiently distinguish between hidden and visible matches based on the pattern index.
* Updated the `StopSequenceDecoder` struct to pre-compile and store the automaton during initialization.

## Accuracy Tests

.

## Benchmarking and Profiling



| Implementation | Tokens | Avg Latency | Throughput |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Naive (Original) | 5 | 30.00 µs | 1.55 GiB/s |
| **Aho-Corasick (Fix)** | **5** | **4.74 µs** | **9.83 GiB/s** |
| Naive (Original) | 50 | 138.10 µs | 345.28 MiB/s |
| **Aho-Corasick (Fix)** | **50** | **4.74 µs** | **9.82 GiB/s** |

**Results:** 

* Achieved a **29x speedup** for 50 stop sequences.
* Time complexity is now $O(N)$, meaning latency remains constant regardless of the number of stop sequences provided.

title: Add BF16 support to EP-MoE for DeepGEMM
author: froststeam
body:
## Motivation
We attempted to enable EP-MoE on BF16 models and found that BF16 data type was not supported in the DeepGEMM backend. This PR implements BF16 EP-MoE support using DeepGEMM's grouped BF16 GEMM kernels.

## Modifications
Following the same computational paradigm as FP8, we have implemented EP-MoE for BF16 using `deep_gemm.m_grouped_bf16_gemm_nt_contiguous` and `deep_gemm.m_grouped_bf16_gemm_nt_masked` from DeepGEMM.

The changes include:

1. **BF16 DeepGEMM interface** (`entrypoint.py`): Added `grouped_gemm_nt_bf16_masked` and `grouped_gemm_nt_bf16_contig` functions
2. **BF16 DeepGEMM warmup** (`compile_utils.py`): Added `DeepGemmKernelType.GROUPED_GEMM_NT_BF16_MASKED` and `GROUPED_GEMM_NT_BF16_CONTIG` kernel types with corresponding warmup executors
3. **New Triton kernel** (`ep_moe/kernels.py`): Introduced `silu_and_mul_masked_fwd` kernel for BF16 activation, and extended `ep_scatter` to support BF16 data type (FP8 scale handling is now conditional)
4. **BF16 GEMM runners** (`moe_runner/deep_gemm.py`): Added `_run_bf16_contiguous_gemm` and `_run_masked_bf16_gemm` functions
5. **Server args** (`server_args.py`): Auto-select `deep_gemm` runner backend on MUSA platform when `SGLANG_DEEPEP_BF16_DISPATCH` is enabled

## Platform Support
- **MUSA platform**: Uses DeepGEMM as the BF16 EP-MoE backend (set `SGLANG_DEEPEP_BF16_DISPATCH=1` to enable)
- **CUDA platform**: Functionally available with the same configuration

title: [model-gateway] Optimize consistent hashing hot path to eliminate allocations
author: ppraneth
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->



## Motivation

The `ConsistentHashRing::get_owners` method is called frequently during rate-limit checks. The previous implementation allocated a new `HashSet` and cloned multiple `String`s for every lookup. In high-throughput scenarios, these transient heap allocations caused significant memory churn and increased tail latency ($P99$).

## Modifications

* **Zero-Copy Return:** Changed `get_owners` to return `Vec<&str>` instead of `Vec<String>`, allowing it to return references to existing keys in the ring without allocating new strings.
* **Removed HashSet:** Replaced the `HashSet` used for deduplication with a simple linear scan over the result vector. Since the number of owners is small (fixed at 3), a linear scan is significantly faster and cheaper than hashing overhead.
* **Deterministic Allocation:** Used `Vec::with_capacity` to ensure exactly one allocation per call.
* **Store Updates:** Updated `RateLimitStore` and `check_ownership_transfer` to handle the new reference-based API, cloning strings only when strictly necessary (e.g., when leaving the lock scope).

## Accuracy Tests



## Benchmarking and Profiling

benchmark (`benches/consistent_hash_bench.rs`) show a **3.3x to 4.2x** reduction in latency across various cluster sizes:

| Cluster Size | Pre-Fix (ns) | Post-Fix (ns) | Improvement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10 Nodes | ~419 ns | ~100 ns | **4.17x faster** |
| 100 Nodes | ~467 ns | ~132 ns | **3.53x faster** |
| 500 Nodes | ~480 ns | ~143 ns | **3.35x faster** |

This change reduces heap allocations from ~5 per call to 1 per call.

title: Kernel: optimize decoding metadata in NSA multi-spec backend with fused kernels
author: Johnsonms
body: ## Motivation Implement fused CUDA kernels to eliminate redundant metadata copies in Native Sparse Attention (NSA) backend during CUDA graph replay for speculative decoding. This optimization provides 3-5x speedup for multi-backend metadata operations. ## Changes ### Core Implementation - Add `fused_metadata_copy_cuda`: Single-backend fused kernel supporting DECODE, TARGET_VERIFY, and DRAFT_EXTEND forward modes - Add `fused_metadata_copy_multi_cuda`: Multi-backend kernel that copies metadata to 3 backends simultaneously in a single kernel launch ### Runtime Optimization - Update `nsa_backend.py` to intelligently use fused kernels: - `speculative_num_steps >= 3`: Use fused kernel for first 3 backends, then copy remaining backends individually - `speculative_num_steps < 3`: Use individual copy (overhead not worth it) ### Testing - Create comprehensive test suite covering: - Single-backend kernel: all forward modes, optional tensors - Multi-backend kernel: 3-backend simultaneous copy - Performance benchmarks with timing and speedup measurements ## Technical Details The fused kernels handle: - Basic metadata: cache_seqlens, cu_seqlens_k, page_table, nsa_cache_seqlens - Optional tensors: real_page_table, flashmla_num_splits, flashmla_metadata - All copies done in single kernel launch, reducing PCIe/memory overhead ## Files Modified - `sgl-kernel/csrc/elementwise/fused_metadata_copy.cu`: CUDA kernel impl - `sgl-kernel/python/sgl_kernel/elementwise.py`: Python bindings - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/nsa_backend.py`: Runtime integration - `sgl-kernel/tests/test_fused_metadata_copy.py`: Comprehensive tests ## Why hand-written CUDA instead of Triton Before implementing the CUDA kernel, I prototyped a Triton version to fuse the 24 metadata-copy operations into a single kernel. Triton was the natural first attempt because the operation is simple, elementwise, and easy to express as a fused copy kernel. However, profiling showed that this path is not bandwidth-bound or compute-bound. Each metadata copy moves only a small amount of int32 data, so the device work is tiny. The dominant cost comes from launching many small operations from the host before CUDA graph replay. The Triton prototype reduced the number of device kernels, but it did not materially improve end-to-end latency. The reason is that the remaining per-call host-side overhead was still large relative to the actual device work. For larger kernels, Triton's launch/runtime overhead can be amortized by meaningful GPU computation. In this case, the kernel work was too small, so the host launch path became the bottleneck. For this reason, the final implementation uses a hand-written CUDA kernel exposed through a thin C++/Python binding. This keeps the hot path minimal, packs the metadata copy into one fused launch, and avoids extra per-call overhead in the host launch path. In short, this optimization is not just about fusion. It is about choosing the right primitive for a host-issue-bound regime. ## Performance Impact ### Metadata Copy Path - **CPU-side metadata processing:** **16× faster**, 193µs → 12µs - **GPU kernel execution time:** **37.6× faster**, 177µs → 4.7µs - **Kernel launches:** reduced from **24** launches to **1** fused kernel launch in the measured path ### End-to-End Serving Impact - **Throughput:** **+18.5%**, 151 → 179 tokens/sec - **Absolute gain:** +28 tokens/sec ### CPU side **Before**: **After**: ### GPU side **Before** **After**: These gains come from removing many small metadata-copy operations and replacing them with fused copy kernels on the decode critical path. Tested: All 40 tests passing (100% pass rate) ## Modifications ## Accuracy Tests 1. Accuracy Test with gsm8k ``` python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 8 --dp-size 8 --enable-dp-attention \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv31 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v3 \ --chat-template ./examples/chat_template/tool_chat_template_deepseekv32.jinja ``` `python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-shots 8 --num-questions 1319 --parallel 1319` 2. Accuracy Test with gpqa-diamond Service: `python -m sglang.launch_server --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp --tp 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 ` `python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 30000 --eval-name gpqa --num-examples 198 --max-tokens 120000 --repeat 8 --thinking-mode deepseek-v3` 3. Accuracy Test with aime 2025 `python -m sglang.launch_server --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp --tp 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --tool-call-parser deepseekv32 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v3` ``` #! /bin/bash export NEMO_SKILLS_DISABLE_UNCOMMITTED_CHANGES_CHECK=1 ns prepare_data aime25 PORT=30000 BACKEND=sglang MODEL="deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp" # Should be changed to the model name MODEL_NAME="dsv32-fp8" echo "Starting AIME25 evaluation with model $MODEL on port $PORT using backend $BACKEND..." ns eval \ --benchmarks=aime25:4 \ --server_type=$BACKEND \ --model=$MODEL \ --server_address=http://localhost:${PORT}/v1 \ --output_dir=nemo_skills_aime25_${MODEL_NAME}_output_${BACKEND}_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S) \ ++chat_template_kwargs.thinking=true \ ++inference.temperature=1.0 \ ++inference.top_p=0.95 \ ++inference.tokens_to_generate=64000 # ++inference.tokens_to_generate=120000 for Speciale model ``` 4. title: [model-gateway] Optimize HashRing construction to reduce heap allocations
author: ppraneth
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->



## Motivation

The `HashRing::new` method in `src/core/worker_registry.rs` previously performed $N \times 150$ heap allocations using the `format!` macro to generate virtual node keys. For a cluster with 1,000 workers, this resulted in **150,000 temporary string allocations** during a single registry update, leading to significant allocator pressure and non-deterministic latency spikes.

## Modifications

* Updated `HashRing::new` in `src/core/worker_registry.rs` to use the incremental `blake3::Hasher::update` API.
* Replaced `format!("{}#{}", url, vnode)` with direct byte updates to the hasher:
* `hasher.update(url_bytes)`
* `hasher.update(b"#")`
* `hasher.update(&(vnode as u64).to_le_bytes())`


* This approach eliminates all temporary heap allocations within the virtual node loops.

## Accuracy Tests



## Benchmarking and Profiling

Benchmarks were conducted simulating 1,000 workers to measure the time required to construct a new `HashRing`:

title: [Perf] refactor piecewise cuda graph support of Qwen3-Next
author: zminglei
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
Currently in Qwen3Next, we hide all ops inside `Qwen3GatedDeltaNet.forward` in a custom fake op, so that even with piecewise cuda graph, the whole forward of Qwen3GatedDeltaNet is running in eager mode.
Here we refactor `RadixLinearAttention` to follow the same pattern of `RadixAttention` where only the attention op is skipped during piecewise cuda graph capturing, allowing more ops to be captured, improve the prefill performance.

The gsm8k benchmark shows this change could speed up Qwen3-Next with PCG by **14.3%**.
<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications
 - Refactored `RadixLinearAttention` to follow the same pattern as `RadixAttention`, wrapping only the attention computation in a custom op (`unified_linear_attention_with_output`)                                                                                                                                         
  - Updated `Qwen3GatedDeltaNet.forward` to allow input projections, split/reshape, norm, and output projections to be piecewise CUDA graph captured                                                                                                                                                                        
  - Fixed `calc_rows_per_block` in `layernorm_gated.py` to use a constant value when piecewise CUDA graph is enabled, avoiding torch.compile guards on dynamic batch dimensions  
<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

title: NixlKVManager optimizations
author: ovidiusm
body:
## Motivation

This PR improves the performance of NixlKVManager by reducing CPU-side overhead in address calculation and enabling multi-threading processing for NIXL transfers initiated by the decode node. Previously, generating transfer descriptors involved nested Python loops which became a bottleneck when handling a large number of KV blocks and/or token slices.

## Modifications

1. Multi-threaded NIXL Agent
Set NIXL agent config to use 8 background threads in PREFILL mode to accelerate the preparation and execution of transfers.

2. Vectorized Address Calculation in prepare_kv_buffer
Replaced nested Python loops with NumPy-based vectorization. Precomputes block starts and lengths using np.fromiter and performs bulk pointer arithmetic using NumPy arrays. This reduces the time spent in Python when calculating source and destination addresses for KV blocks.

3. Vectorized Token Slice Calculation
Replaced a triple-nested loop (layers × pages × tokens) with NumPy operations. Calculates all token-level slice addresses (src_all and dst_all) in a single vectorized operation. Uses itertools.repeat and zip for efficient construction of the final address lists.

## Accuracy Tests

```
python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200 --port 8000
Accuracy: 0.835
Invalid: 0.000
Latency: 59.976 s
Output throughput: 478.258 token/s
```

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Evaluation was performed using inference workloads while sweeping batch size and tensor-parallel (TP) configurations to capture different KV transfer message patterns. Profiling focused on decode-step CPU time, particularly descriptor preparation overhead, and transfer submission behavior.

We saw improved overlap between NIXL CPU-side preparation and transfer execution under higher concurrency, CPU utilization more evenly distributed across cores, and reduced single-thread hotspots and decreased time spent contending on the GIL.

author: CloudRipple
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

This PR integrates **MOVA** (**MO**SS **V**ideo and **A**udio Synthesis), a foundation model for synchronized video-audio generation. MOVA features an **asymmetric dual-tower architecture** with a **bidirectional cross-attention mechanism** for modality fusion, enabling high-quality multilingual lip-sync and precise audio-visual alignment.

## Modifications
**MOVA Model and VAE Configurations:**

* Added `MOVAVideoConfig` and `MOVAAudioConfig` classes for MOVA video and audio DiT models, including architecture details and parameter mappings (`mova_video.py`, `mova_audio.py`, `__init__.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5ac48833c2247e301a6bc29f50c22659ea7a50663cd5914b7586adf3d44c4f61R1-R62) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-68fa43ee9e4a03ac66f71a9aec36e0954082c00407ce614208a973ceb66adcb5R1-R63) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d34fb2f956e288da82a2eb621b3eb76282a3dc30d470006c165ed00264629181R4-R13).
* Introduced `DacVAEConfig` for the DAC audio VAE, with encoder/decoder and quantizer settings (`dac.py`, `__init__.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c77b2a1f8c26271ec07cf560b343449c69e7cb7c8653cefa1560f8782f202012R1-R30) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7b823527b48db6747978b59db0508f1d5cd4efbdec7da782ca40df2414249a53R3-R8).
* Added `MOVADualTowerConfig` for dual-tower bridge model support (`mova_dual_tower.py`, `__init__.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6326f77feae838ad3bf4ab653d18ba7d629ae08c00e960246a17a9015f3da3ceR1-R50) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ec9fe9e4d0044ba268fce88756ce161f99094208cb7100d19ff5cc335beb85dfR1-R7).

**Pipeline and Sampling Configuration:**
