title: [AMD] Fix EAGLE3 speculative decoding with aiter attention backend
author: hubertlu-tw
body:
## Motivation

EAGLE3 speculative decoding crashes on the aiter backend for non-MLA models
(e.g. Llama). Two root causes:

1. The `target_verify` CUDA graph capture/replay paths had separate,
   duplicated `qo_indptr`/`kv_indptr`/`kv_indices` setup for MLA vs non-MLA.
   The non-MLA branch used different tensor objects than the ones updated
   during replay, causing stale indices and garbled output.

2. Several `if _use_mla_ps_kernel:` guards in the replay path were missing
   the `self.use_mla` check, so non-MLA models hit
   `AttributeError: 'AiterAttnBackend' object has no attribute 'max_split_per_batch'`.

## Modifications

### `aiter_backend.py`

- **Capture `target_verify`** — Unified the `qo_indptr`/`kv_indptr`/`kv_indices`
setup so both MLA and non-MLA share the same tensor allocation (using
`kv_lens = seq_lens + self.num_draft_tokens`). The `ForwardMetadata` creation
is still split: MLA uses `work_metadata` + MLA PS kernel metadata, non-MLA
uses `custom_mask`/`mask_indptr`/`max_extend_len` for the triton extend kernel.

- **Replay `target_verify`** — Same restructuring as capture. The old code had
`if not self.use_mla:` updating `custom_mask` followed by an unguarded
`if _use_mla_ps_kernel:` that crashed for non-MLA. Now properly branches into
MLA vs non-MLA with separate `ForwardMetadata` construction.

- **Replay `draft_extend`** — Changed `if _use_mla_ps_kernel:` to
`if self.use_mla and _use_mla_ps_kernel:` to prevent accessing
`self.max_split_per_batch` on non-MLA models.

### `test_eagle3_basic.py`

- Register the test for AMD CI (`register_amd_ci`).
- Conditionally add `--attention-backend aiter` when running on HIP.
- Lower `avg_spec_accept_length` threshold from 2.26 to 2.24 to account for
  minor numerical variance across hardware.

## Accuracy test

- [x] `test_eagle3_basic.py` passes end-to-end on MI300X with aiter backend
  (MMLU score 0.75, accept length ~2.26)
  (The test will be included in AMD's CI under `stage-b-test-small-1-gpu`)

title: Fix NSA CP positions mismatch in eagle NextN model
author: alisonshao
body:
## Summary
- When context parallelism (CP) is enabled, the eagle NextN model (`deepseek_nextn.py`) splits `hidden_states` across CP ranks but does **not** split `positions`, causing a shape mismatch in the NSA indexer's rotary embedding
- The rotary embedding uses `positions.size(0)` as batch size to reshape `k_rope`, but `k_rope` has fewer elements because `hidden_states` was already CP-split
- Adds the missing `cp_split_and_rebuild_position` call, matching what the main model (`deepseek_v2.py:2707`) already does

## Error
```
RuntimeError: shape '[8, -1, 64]' is invalid for input of size 64
```
at `rotary_embedding/base.py:292` during eagle speculative decoding with `ATTN_CP4 TP4`.

Full trace: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/22376709996/job/64768484941

title: Fix parallel tool call test for speculative decoding variants
author: alisonshao
body:
## Summary

- Fix `_test_parallel` in `tool_call_test_runner.py` to reliably pass across all DeepSeek V3.2 variants (DP8, DP8+MTP, TP8, TP8+MTP)
- Use `tool_choice="auto"` with strict tools to get `structural_tag` constraint (DSML format), avoiding EAGLE+DP early JSON array termination with `tool_choice="required"`
- Use `temperature=0` for deterministic behavior and explicit prompt for reliable parallel tool call generation

## Root Cause

The parallel tool call test was failing for different variants depending on the constraint mode:

1. **`tool_choice="required"`** (original): Uses JSON schema `{"type": "array", "minItems": 1}`. EAGLE speculative decoding with DP attention would close the JSON array after 1 tool call since the grammar accepts `minItems=1`. Failed for DP8+MTP variant.

2. **`tool_choice="auto"` with non-strict tools** (first fix attempt): Produces **no grammar constraint at all**, leaving model behavior uncontrolled. Failed for TP8 variant due to non-deterministic generation at `temperature=0.1`.

The fix uses `tool_choice="auto"` with **strict tools** (`strict: true`), which activates the `structural_tag` constraint (DSML format). Combined with `temperature=0` and an explicit prompt, the test reliably produces 2+ parallel tool calls across all configurations.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes for all 4 DeepSeek V3.2 variants: DP8, DP8+MTP, TP8, TP8+MTP

title: [BUG]: fix prevent illegal memory access in Mamba SSM tracking during EAGLE speculative verification
author: ConnorLi96
body:
When using `--mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer` with EAGLE speculative decoding, mamba_track_mask and mamba_track_seqlens were never reset after prepare_for_extend(). This caused an illegal GPU memory access during the TARGET_VERIFY phase.

Root cause:
- `prepare_for_extend() `sets all three Mamba tracking fields with values sized for the full prefill sequence (e.g. 1000 tokens).
- `prepare_for_decode()` early-returns for speculative decoding, leaving all three fields untouched.
- ` prepare_for_verify()` correctly updates mamba_track_indices to the ping-pong slot indices, but left mamba_track_mask and `mamba_track_seqlens` stale.
- During TARGET_VERIFY, `_track_mamba_state_extend()` uses the stale `mamba_track_mask` to index into h, which only has `draft_token_num` rows (typically 5-7). The stale indices (e.g. 512, 576, ...) are far out of bounds, causing cudaErrorIllegalAddress and a segfault.

Fix:
Explicitly set `batch.mamba_track_mask = None` and `batch.mamba_track_seqlens = None` in `prepare_for_verify()`, _since TARGET_VERIFY does not need prefix-cache Mamba state tracking._



<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
Without this fix, we will get error like in high workload (not stable reproduce):


```python

title: [AMD] Use fused GEMM with FP8 cast for FP8 prefill
author: 1am9trash
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

cc @HaiShaw, @kkHuang-amd 

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

When using FP8 prefill, q, k, v tensors require a separate element-wise BF16 to FP8 cast before the prefill attention kernel, adding overhead.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Use the aiter Triton kernel `fused_gemm_afp4wfp4_split_cat()` to fuse the GEMM, split, and k_pe concatenation into a single kernel that outputs k and v directly in FP8, eliminating the standalone cast.
- Move `kv_indices` (torch.arange) creation from per-layer forward to `init_forward_metadata`, computed once per batch.

## Accuracy Tests

title: [Qwen3-Next] Support gdn fused_rms_norm_gated
author: yuan-luo
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
This PR is to refactor Qwen3-Next GDN fused_rms_norm_gate.

The ground is in attention / state-space style architectures, each layer and each step does a norm + gate, fusing them saves a lot of bandwidth. head_v_dim is often <= 256, which lands right in the fused-kernel sweet spot optimized for D <= 512.

The fused kernel's forward path is split into two variants:
- D <= 512: use layer_norm_gated_fwd_kernel. Each program handles a BT × BD tile (processes multiple rows per launch), it behaves like a throughput-oriented kernel.
- D > 512: use kernel1 (one row per program) to reduce register pressure and overall complexity.

```
BT: Block/Tilesize in T(or row) dimension
BD: Block/Tilesize in D dimension
      D dimension（feature）
     <-------- BD -------->
row  [ x x x x x x x x ... ]   ^
row  [ x x x x x x x x ... ]   |
row  [ x x x x x x x x ... ]   |  BT line
...  [ x x x x x x x x ... ]   v
``` 

It is good for the frequent Transformer-block pattern: (x + residual) → norm → gate. It also has fewer kernel launches and less memory traffic.

Moreover, this PR involves a refactor to move `layer_norm_gated_fwd_kernel` from KDA to FLA folder, as `layer_norm_gate` is a common kernel utilized by both KDA and GDN. It is more appropriate to put it there.

Performance wise, this fused kernel obtains 4% TTFT speedup and increases throughput in the same scale.

title: [Kernel Slimming] Migrate NVFP4 kernels to JIT
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation
#17865

This PR moves NVFP4 kernels from AOT `sgl-kernel` to JIT (`python/sglang/jit_kernel`).

_“Should we migrate this given its CUTLASS dependency and JIT compile overhead?”_

I think yes, because in almost all serving setups with FlashInfer always installed, these JIT CUTLASS kernels are not usually on the default path anymore.

Exact runtime behavior that can still use these even with FlashInfer available:
- On non-SM120, SGLang currently uses JIT `scaled_fp4_quant` because `flashinfer.fp4_quantize` is gated by `is_sm120_supported()`. But I verified this can already support SM100, so changing this to `is_sm100_supported() or is_sm120_supported()` should enable the FlashInfer path on SM100.
- NVFP4 MoE groupmm (`cutlass_fp4_group_mm`) is only used in non-FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE paths; for many defaults, `auto` selects `flashinfer_trtllm`, so this path is often not default. I think this can only use JIT now if `--moe-runner-backend cutlass` is explicitly set.

cc @BBuf 

## Modifications

- Added JIT NVFP4 implementation module:
  - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/nvfp4.py`
  - Includes JIT loaders for quant, scaled MM, expert quant, and blockwise MoE group MM.
- Added CUDA JIT sources:
  - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/gemm/nvfp4/nvfp4_quant.cuh`
  - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/gemm/nvfp4/nvfp4_quant_entry.cuh`
  - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/gemm/nvfp4/nvfp4_quant_kernels.cuh`
  - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/gemm/nvfp4/nvfp4_scaled_mm_entry.cuh`
  - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/gemm/nvfp4/nvfp4_scaled_mm_kernels.cuh`
  - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/gemm/nvfp4/nvfp4_expert_quant.cuh`
  - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/moe/nvfp4_blockwise_moe.cuh`
- Runtime wiring switched from `sgl_kernel` AOT NVFP4 ops to JIT imports in:
  - `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py`
  - `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/cutlass_moe.py`
  - `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py`
  - `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/standard.py`
- Added MoE argument plumbing for JIT grouped MM in:
  - `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/cutlass_moe_params.py`
- Slimmed AOT NVFP4 registration/build in `sgl-kernel`:
  - Removed NVFP4 AOT compilation/registration from:
    - `sgl-kernel/CMakeLists.txt`
    - `sgl-kernel/csrc/common_extension.cc`
    - `sgl-kernel/include/sgl_kernel_ops.h`
  - Kept compatibility APIs by forwarding Python helpers to JIT:
    - `sgl-kernel/python/sgl_kernel/gemm.py`
    - `sgl-kernel/python/sgl_kernel/moe.py`
- Added tests:
  - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_nvfp4_quant.py`
  - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_nvfp4_gemm.py`
  - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_nvfp4_blockwise_moe.py`
- Added benchmarks:
  - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/benchmark/bench_nvfp4_quant.py`
  - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/benchmark/bench_nvfp4_scaled_mm.py`
  - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/benchmark/bench_nvfp4_blockwise_moe.py`

## Tests

title: [CI] Skip flashinfer-cubin reinstall when version matches
author: alisonshao
body:
## Summary
- Skip uninstalling `flashinfer-cubin` (150+ MB) when the installed version already matches `pyproject.toml`, preserving both the pip package and extra cubins downloaded by `ci_download_flashinfer_cubin.sh`
- Add timeouts (60s for status check, 300s for download) to prevent CI hangs when GPUs are in error state
- Set `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=''` for the cubin status check since it only inspects local files

Followup to #18887

Example failure (20min timeout caused by `get_artifacts_status()` hanging on bad GPU): https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/22441992948/job/64987077421

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify CI passes with flashinfer-cubin already installed (common case — should see "already installed, keeping it" in logs)
- [ ] Verify CI handles version mismatch correctly (when flashinfer-cubin version is bumped)
- [ ] Verify timeout prevents hangs on runners with bad GPUs

## Motivation when i running with this cmd ```bash model_path=/pfs/pfs-OqLB2M/models/DeepSeek-R1-0528-NVFP4-v2 TP_SIZE=8 DP_SIZE=8 EP_SIZE=1 NNODES=1 NODE_RANK=0 export SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0 export NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 export NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 export SGLANG_USE_MESSAGE_QUEUE_BROADCASTER=0 export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=256 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --nnodes $NNODES --node-rank $NODE_RANK \ --model-path ${model_path} \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8000 \ --decode-log-interval 1 \ --max-running-requests 2048 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --disable-shared-experts-fusion \ --watchdog-timeout 1000000 \ --tp-size ${TP_SIZE} \ --enable-dp-lm-head \ --decode-log-interval 1 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \ --max-prefill-tokens 1048576 \ --trust-remote-code \ --disable-cuda-graph \ --enable-layerwise-nvtx-marker \ --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --tokenizer-worker-num 8 \ --quantization modelopt_fp4 \ --show-time-cost --enable-request-time-stats-logging --enable-metrics \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 ``` I found that the last shuffle_rows and reduce sum operations in the calculation of cutlass_moe_fp4 are extremely time-consuming, and their proportion increases with the increase of sequence length. To improve the performance of moe computation, this commen to use a fused kernel to implement these functions. ## Modifications Use the kernel apply_router_weight_on_input to replace the multiple elementwise operations shuffle_rows+view+mul+reduce sum ## Accuracy Tests ### Before test_moe_eval_accuracy_large.TestMoEEvalAccuracyLarge.test_mmlu Score: 0.750 test_moe_eval_accuracy_large.TestMoEEvalAccuracyLarge.test_mgsm_en Score: 0.768 test_moe_eval_accuracy_large.TestMoEEvalAccuracyLarge.test_human_eval Score: 0.491 ### After test_moe_eval_accuracy_large.TestMoEEvalAccuracyLarge.test_mmlu Score: 0.757 test_moe_eval_accuracy_large.TestMoEEvalAccuracyLarge.test_mgsm_en Score: test twice: first time is 0.752, second time is 0.792, so i think the accuracy is good test_moe_eval_accuracy_large.TestMoEEvalAccuracyLarge.test_human_eval Score: 0.463 ## Benchmarking and Profiling use bench_serving for testing, set --random-input-len in 8k,16k,32k,64k,128k ```bash python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang-oai-chat --dataset-name random --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --model /pfs/pfs-OqLB2M/models/DeepSeek-R1-0528-NVFP4-v2 --random-input-len 8192 --random-output -len 16 --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 8 ``` ### Benchmarking Before

title: KDA: fuse qkv conv and support stride for fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_kernel
author: strgrb
body: ## Motivation For KDA, qkv conv can be fused to 1 as implemented in GDN. But `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_kernel` kernel does not support stride, so some of inputs (q, k, v and b) should invoke extra element-wise kernels. And GDN can also benefit from this kernel modification. ## Modifications qkv conv is fused and stride is supported for `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_kernel`. ## Accuracy Tests before: ``` $python bench_sglang.py --port 8188 --data-path ./test.jsonl --num-questions -1 100%|████████████████████████████████| 1318/1318 [01:16<00:00, 17.31it/s] Accuracy: 0.894 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 76.215 s Output throughput: 1693.587 token/s ``` after: ``` $python bench_sglang.py --port 8189 --data-path ./test.jsonl --num-questions -1 100%|████████████████████████████████| 1318/1318 [01:12<00:00, 18.08it/s] Accuracy: 0.894 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 73.004 s Output throughput: 1750.681 token/s ``` ## Benchmarking and Profiling before: max concurrency | random input len | random output len | throughput | TTFT | TPOT ----|----|----|----|----|---- 8 | 4096 | 1536 | 0.93 | 461.19 | 5.30 32 | 4096 | 1536 | 1.84 | 1438.68 | 10.39 128 | 4096 | 1536 | 2.99 | 5481.30 | 24.27 after: max concurrency | random input len | random output len | throughput | TTFT | TPOT ----|----|----|----|----|---- 8 | 4096 | 1536 | 0.95 | 464.02 | 5.28 32 | 4096 | 1536 | 1.86 | 1434.09 | 10.27 128 | 4096 | 1536 | 3.12 | 5490.07 | 23.02 TPOT decreases by ~1%, and this is stable. body:

## Motivation

The previous PR [17511](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/17511)  added a condition ( forward_mode.is_extend() ) to avoid using fused Triton kernel (split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope) during prefill stage. However, when using speculative inference (such as eagle3)，the condition will become invalid because the decode stage will be TARGET_VERIFY, and forward_mode.is_extend() will always be true. title: feat(observability): add OpenTelemetry tracing for speculative decoding
author: RichardoMrMu
body:
## Motivation

This PR adds OpenTelemetry tracing support for the speculative decoding pipeline, as part of the tracing roadmap (#13511).

Currently, the speculative decoding phases (draft, verify, accept) are not instrumented, making it difficult to diagnose performance bottlenecks in the speculative decoding pipeline. This PR fills that gap.

## Changes

### EAGLE Worker (`eagle_worker.py`)
- **`spec_draft`** (level 2): trace span wrapping the `draft()` call
- **`spec_verify`** (level 2): trace span wrapping the `verify()` call  
- **`spec_accept`** (level 2 event): records `accepted_tokens` per request after verification
- **`spec_draft_extend`** (level 3): trace span wrapping `forward_draft_extend_after_decode()`

### NGRAM Worker (`ngram_worker.py`)
- **`spec_draft`** (level 2): trace span wrapping `_prepare_for_speculative_decoding()`
- **`spec_verify`** (level 2): trace span wrapping the target verify forward + `verify()`
- **`spec_accept`** (level 2 event): records `accepted_tokens` per request after verification

### Design Decisions
- All tracing is gated behind `get_global_tracing_enabled()` to avoid any overhead when tracing is disabled
- Uses the existing `TraceReqContext` / `TraceNullContext` pattern from `req_time_stats.py`
- Per-request tracing: iterates over `batch.reqs` to emit spans for each request individually
- Timestamps use `convert_time_to_realtime_ns(time.perf_counter())` consistent with existing tracing code

title: [AMD] Add AWQ AMD CI coverage and quantization platform compatibility docs
author: brucechanglongxu
body:
SGLang's AWQ quantization path on AMD GPUs goes through Triton-based
dequantization (awq_dequantize_triton in awq_triton.py) rather than the
Marlin kernels used on NVIDIA. This path has been functional but had no CI
coverage, meaning regressions could ship undetected. This PR registers
test_awq.py for the AMD CI suite so the Mixtral-8x7B AWQ-INT4 MoE eval
runs on MI300X/MI325X hardware.

The existing test file contains three test classes: TestAWQ (which exercises
the Triton dequant path used on HIP), and two AWQ Marlin variants that
explicitly pass --quantization awq_marlin. Since is_awq_marlin_compatible
returns False on HIP and the Marlin GEMM kernels are CUDA-only, the Marlin
classes are skipped in AMD CI via @unittest.skipIf(is_in_amd_ci(), ...).

Separately, there was no documentation anywhere that told AMD users which
quantization methods actually work on their hardware. I audited every method
registered in QUANTIZATION_METHODS (and the conditional mxfp4 entry), traced
the backend dispatch in each config class to determine HIP compatibility, and
added a platform compatibility table to quantization.md. The table covers all
18+ methods with their NVIDIA/AMD support status and notes on which backend
(Aiter, Triton, vLLM, etc.) is used on each platform.

The AMD GPU doc (amd_gpu.md) also had no mention of quantization at all, so
I added a section with practical notes on what works, the SGLANG_USE_AITER=1
setup, runnable examples, and the list of unsupported methods (awq_marlin,
gptq_marlin, gguf, modelopt_fp8, modelopt_fp4, petit_nvfp4).

## Test plan

- AWQ Triton path CI: test_awq.py::TestAWQ registered for
  stage-b-test-large-1-gpu-amd (est. 200s). Runs MMLU eval (64 examples)
  on hugging-quants/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-AWQ-INT4, threshold > 0.64.
- Marlin classes (TestAWQMarlinBfloat16, TestAWQMarlinFloat16) confirmed
  skipped on AMD CI via is_in_amd_ci() guard.
- Doc links verified: quantization.md#platform-compatibility anchor exists,
  cross-reference from amd_gpu.md resolves correctly.

title: [Feature] NVFP4 Marlin fallback for non-Blackwell GPUs (SM75+)
author: Godmook
body:
## Motivation
Related Issue: #19491
NVFP4-quantized models (e.g., `nvidia/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-NVFP4`, `nvidia/DeepSeek-V3-0324-FP4`, `mistralai/Minimax-M2.5-NVFP4`) crash immediately on non-Blackwell GPUs because `get_min_capability()` returned 100.
This forces users on A100/A40/H100/RTX 3090 to fall back to less accurate quantization (AWQ/GPTQ) or switch to vLLM, which already supports this via Marlin fallback. This PR brings equivalent functionality to SGLang.
 
**Key properties:**
- Weights remain compressed in FP4 (2 values per byte) — no VRAM explosion unlike naive BF16 dequantization
- FP4 dequantization happens in-flight inside the Marlin kernel via fast bitwise operations during tensor core matmul
- Fully automatic — no user-side flags needed; fallback is triggered based on GPU capability detection
- All kernel changes are gated by `w_type == kFE2M1f` (FP4 only) — **zero impact on existing INT4/INT8/FP8 quantization paths**
 
---
 
## Modifications
 
### Summary
 
| File | Type | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| `marlin_utils_fp4.py` | **New** | Core NVFP4 Marlin utilities (prepare, apply, scale conversion) |
| `test_nvfp4_marlin_fallback.py` | **New** | 6 unit tests covering full fallback stack |
| `marlin/marlin_template.h` (JIT) | **Kernel fix** | Fix FP4 scale stride/group mismatch — aligns with vLLM |
| `marlin/marlin_template.h` (sgl-kernel) | **Kernel fix** | Same fix as JIT — identical changes |
| `marlin_moe/marlin_template.h` | **Kernel fix** | Uncomment `dequant_fp8_scales()` for `kFE2M1f`; fix `global_scale` application |
| `marlin_moe/moe_wna16_marlin.cuh` | Modified | Guard FP4 kernel instantiation behind `SGL_MOE_MARLIN_FP4` macro |
| `moe_wna16_marlin.py` | Modified | Add separate FP4 JIT module to avoid compile-time regression for non-FP4 |
| `fused_marlin_moe.py` | Modified | Add `w1/w2_global_scale` params; detect FP4 Marlin mode |
| `moe_runner/marlin.py` | Modified | Add `w13/w2_global_scale` fields to `MarlinMoeQuantInfo` |
| `compressed_tensors_w4a4_nvfp4.py` | Modified | `get_min_capability` 100→75; Marlin fallback in linear path |
| `compressed_tensors_w4a4_nvfp4_moe.py` | Modified | `get_min_capability` 100→75; Marlin fallback in MoE path |
| `modelopt_quant.py` | Modified | `get_min_capability` 100→75; Marlin fallback in linear + MoE path |
| `weight_utils.py` | Modified | Explicit FP8/FP4 config routing for modelopt checkpoints |
| `environ.py` | Modified | Add `SGLANG_FORCE_NVFP4_MARLIN` env var |
| `environment_variables.md` | Modified | Document new env var |
 
---
 
## 1. New: `marlin_utils_fp4.py`
 
Core utility module. All Marlin-specific preparation and inference logic is isolated here.
 
| Function | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `is_fp4_marlin_supported()` | Returns `True` if SM ≥ 75 |
| `nvfp4_marlin_process_scales()` | Converts per-group FP8-S1E4M3 scales to FP8-S0E5M3 format required by Marlin dequant kernel |
| `nvfp4_marlin_process_global_scale()` | Pre-adjusts FP4↔BF16 exponent bias for `gptq_marlin_gemm` |
| `apply_fp4_marlin_linear()` | Runs linear inference via `gptq_marlin_gemm` with `float4_e2m1f` scalar type |
| `prepare_fp4_layer_for_marlin()` | Repacks linear weights (`gptq_marlin_repack`), permutes + converts scales, creates workspace |
| `prepare_moe_fp4_layer_for_marlin()` | Same as above, applied per-expert for MoE layers |
 
---
 
## 2. Kernel Bug Fixes
 
### 2a. Linear kernel: `marlin/marlin_template.h` (JIT + sgl-kernel)
 
**Root cause:** SGLang's Marlin kernel had incorrect FP4 scale stride calculations that diverged from vLLM's corrected implementation. The kernel assumed FP16-sized (2-byte) elements for scale strides, but NVFP4 uses FP8 scales (1 byte each). This caused the kernel to read every other scale row and misalign scale-to-weight-group mapping, producing garbage output on all non-Blackwell GPUs.
 
**6 changes, all gated by `w_type == kFE2M1f`** (zero impact on INT4/INT8/FP8 paths):
 
| Variable | Before (FP4 path) | After (FP4 path) | Impact on non-FP4 |
|----------|-------------------|-------------------|-------------------|
| `s_gl_stride` | `prob_n / 8` | `prob_n / 16` | None (ternary returns 8) |
| `s_sh_stride` | `16 * thread_n_blocks / 8` | `16 * thread_n_blocks / 16` | None (ternary returns 8) |
| `s_tb_groups` | `thread_k_blocks / group_blocks / 2` | `thread_k_blocks / group_blocks` | None (ternary returned `/1`) |
| `s_gl_rd` | `... / 2 + ...` | `... + ...` | None (ternary returned `/1`) |
| `s_sh_rd` | Special `*2 + warp_row%2` block | Shared logic with other types | None (deleted block was FP4-only) |
| `cur_group_id` | `k_blocks / (group_blocks * 2)` | `k_blocks / group_blocks` | None (ternary returned `*1`) |
 
These changes align SGLang's Marlin kernel with [vLLM's corrected implementation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/csrc/quantization/marlin/marlin_template.h).
 
### 2b. MoE kernel: `marlin_moe/marlin_template.h`
 
Same As Linear Kernel.
 
---
 
## 3. Fallback Integration — Both Quantization Formats
 
Both supported NVFP4 quantization formats now have full Marlin fallback:
 
| Format | Files Changed | `get_min_capability` | Linear | MoE |
|--------|--------------|----------------------|--------|-----|
| compressed-tensors W4A4 NVFP4 | `compressed_tensors_w4a4_nvfp4.py`, `.._moe.py` | 100 → 75 | ✅ | ✅ |
| ModelOpt NVFP4 | `modelopt_quant.py` | 100 → 75 | ✅ | ✅ |
 
**Fallback trigger flow (automatic, no user action needed):**
 
```
Model Load
└─ get_min_capability() = 75 → SM75+ GPU accepted
 
process_weights_after_loading()
└─ not is_blackwell_supported() AND is_fp4_marlin_supported()
   ├─ prepare_fp4_layer_for_marlin()      # linear layers
   ├─ prepare_moe_fp4_layer_for_marlin()  # MoE layers
   └─ layer.use_marlin_fallback = True
 
Inference (forward pass)
└─ if use_marlin_fallback:
   ├─ apply_fp4_marlin_linear()           # linear: gptq_marlin_gemm
   └─ runner.run(MarlinMoeQuantInfo)      # MoE: moe_wna16_marlin_gemm
```
 
**Blackwell (SM100+) is completely unaffected** — the fallback path is only taken when `is_blackwell_supported()` returns `False`. Native FP4 inference continues to use the existing Blackwell-optimized path. Users can force the Marlin fallback on Blackwell for testing via `SGLANG_FORCE_NVFP4_MARLIN=1`.
 
---
 
## 4. New: `test/registered/quant/test_nvfp4_marlin_fallback.py`
 
| Test | What it validates |
|------|-------------------|
| `test_is_fp4_marlin_supported` | SM capability detection (SM ≥ 75 → True) |
| `test_min_capability_changed` | `ModelOptFp4Config.get_min_capability()` == 75 |
| `test_nvfp4_marlin_process_scales` | FP8 scale conversion produces no NaN |
| `test_prepare_and_apply_fp4_marlin_linear` | Linear layer prepare + inference end-to-end |
| `test_fused_marlin_moe_fp4` | MoE Marlin GEMM end-to-end (previously NaN, now fixed) |
| `test_prepare_moe_fp4_layer_for_marlin` | MoE weight repacking shape correctness |
 
---
 
## Accuracy Tests
 
### Unit tests (A40, SM86)
 
All 6 unit tests pass:
 
```
$ python test/registered/quant/test_nvfp4_marlin_fallback.py
GPU: NVIDIA A40 (SM86)
SM86: Testing Marlin FP4 fallback (non-Blackwell GPU).
test_is_fp4_marlin_supported ... ok
test_min_capability_changed ... ok
test_nvfp4_marlin_process_scales ... ok
test_prepare_and_apply_fp4_marlin_linear ... ok
test_fused_marlin_moe_fp4 ... ok
test_prepare_moe_fp4_layer_for_marlin ... ok
 
Ran 6 tests in 8.191s
OK
```
 
---
 
## Benchmarking and Profiling
 
This PR is a correctness fix that unblocks a previously unsupported code path. Comparison against native Blackwell FP4 is not applicable since the target hardware is different.
 
- **Memory efficiency:** weights remain in FP4 format (same VRAM as native FP4), unlike naive BF16 dequantization which would 4× the weight memory
- **Throughput** on non-Blackwell GPUs will be lower than native Blackwell FP4 — this is expected and noted in the startup warning. End-to-end throughput benchmarks against AWQ/GPTQ alternatives on A100 are left for follow-up

title: [CPU] improve numa memory binding
author: blzheng
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
We observed that when `SGLANG_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND` is set to cross NUMA with SNC enabled, the memory is still bound only to the first NUMA node, which is not the expected behavior.

In this PR, we enhanced the NUMA memory binding logic to properly support cross-NUMA memory binding.

**Usage example:**
Assume a machine with 2 sockets (96 cores/socket) and SNC enabled. The NUMA nodes are shown below.
NUMA nodes 0-2 belong to socket 0, while nodes 3-5 belong to socket 1.
```
NUMA node0: 0-31
NUMA node1: 32-63
NUMA node2: 64-95
NUMA node3: 96-127
NUMA node4: 128-159
NUMA node5: 160-191
```

Taking `SGLANG_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND="0-95|96-191"` as an example:
- rank0 is expected to bind socket 0, which is equivalent to `numactl -C 0-95 -m 0-2`
- rank1 is expected to bind socket 1, which is equivalent to `numactl -C 96-191 -m 3-5`

However, before this PR, the bindings were:
- rank0: `numactl -C 0-95 -m 0` 
- rank1: `numactl -C 96-191 -m 3`

title: Add Lychee Doc Links Check to Local and CI
author: JiaxinD
body:
## Motivation

This PR improves documentation link reliability while keeping contributor workflow lightweight:

- **CI enforces full link checks** (offline references + online external links)
- **Local lychee is manual-only** to avoid blocking local commits by platform/network issues

This follows the direction from @zijiexia’s `main...zijiexia:sglang:fix/broken_link`.

## What Changed

### 1) Local lychee config (`.github/linters/lychee.toml`)
- `offline = true` for fast/stable local checks
- excludes generated docs artifacts (`docs/_build/`)
- keeps local/non-routable excludes

### 2) CI lychee config (`.github/linters/lychee-ci.toml`)
- `offline = false` for online validation
- checks `http/https`
- retry settings for transient failures
- excludes known non-actionable noisy endpoints
- fix regex for `example_image.png?raw=true` exclusion anchor

### 3) Pre-commit integration (`.pre-commit-config.yaml`)
- keep lychee hook available
- set lychee to **manual-only** (`stages: [manual]`)
- local commits are not blocked by lychee by default

### 4) Lint workflow (`.github/workflows/lint.yml`)
In the same `lint` job, run two lychee steps:
1. **offline references pass** using `.github/linters/lychee.toml`
2. **online external-links pass** using `.github/linters/lychee-ci.toml` (with `GITHUB_TOKEN`)

### 5) Contributor docs
Updated [`docs/developer_guide/contribution_guide.md`](docs/developer_guide/contribution_guide.md):
- CI is source of truth for link checks
- local manual command:
  - `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual lychee --all-files`
- CI-like local command:
  - `lychee --config .github/linters/lychee-ci.toml README.md docs/**/*.md docs/**/*.rst docs/**/*.ipynb`

### 6) Link fixes
This PR also includes broken/stale link fixes across docs/examples/notebooks (stale GitHub paths, invalid URL forms, wrong relative targets).

## Validation

- local manual lychee checks
- CI-like online lychee checks
- verified broken links and replacements

## Benchmarking / Profiling

Not applicable (docs/tooling/CI workflow changes only; no runtime/model path changes).

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit
- [ ] Add unit tests (N/A: docs + CI/tooling only)
- [x] Update documentation
- [ ] Accuracy/speed benchmarks (N/A: no runtime/model changes)
- [x] Follow SGLang code style guidance

- [ ] Trigger/monitor CI (`/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`, `/tag-and-rerun-ci`) as needed
- [ ] Merge after required approvals + green CI

title: [GDN][Qwen3-Next][Qwen3.5] Fuse fused_gdn_gating and fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_update in verify_target
author: yuan-luo
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

There are three key kernels in GDN. This PR is concerned with the last kernel.
- for extend
- for decode
- for verify_target

Currently in GDN, verify path uses fused_gdn_gating + fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_update. Our goal is to fuse them into one kernel, so as to improve performance. (reduce kernel launch time, reduce register usage)

Our first approach is to directly leverage `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update`. Then we encountered the obstacle that this kernel is a simple kernel designed for decode (single-step update) and does not have the state control (write-back prohibition), intermediate state caching, and tree attention support required by target verification. The cumulative effect of these three deficiencies has led to a collapse in accuracy from 0.83 to 0.35. (See the first commit of this PR)

Given the background, in this PR we introduced a new kernel `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_mtp` which does not write-back state, it has tree attention to support target verification and provides intermediate state caching.

[Update] After refactoring based on @kaixih 's comments, reused `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` and added new logic inside this kernel, so as in the future when KDA support MTP, it can also leverage this feature.

For seq-lens 8k input 1.5k output, TTFT improved 11%.

gsm8k has no drop.

title: Add compile-time 256-bit vector guard for pre-Blackwell
author: xingsy97
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up from #19770 review discussion. On pre-Blackwell GPUs (SM < 100), CUDA only supports 128-bit vector load/store. The 32-byte `AlignedVector` path compiles but should never run. This PR adds a compile-time guard so invalid 256-bit instantiations are caught at compile time rather than relying solely on runtime dispatch.

## Modifications

- **`utils.cuh`**: Add `SGL_ARCH_IS_HOPPER_PLUS` and `SGL_ARCH_IS_BLACKWELL_PLUS` macros. Refactor existing PDL `__CUDA_ARCH__` checks to use them.
- **`vec.cuh`**: Split `AlignedVector` `static_assert` by arch — 16 bytes max on pre-Blackwell, 32 bytes on Blackwell+.
- **`fused_add_rmsnorm.cuh`** / **`qknorm_across_heads.cuh`**: Add `if constexpr` early return in 32B kernel template on pre-Blackwell, preventing the body (which instantiates 32-byte `AlignedVector`) from being compiled.

## Accuracy Tests

No model output changes. This is a compile-time guard only — kernel logic is unchanged.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

No performance impact. The guard is resolved at compile time (`if constexpr` / `#if` preprocessor), producing identical codegen for all existing paths.

title: [Kernel] Dispatch exp/sin/cos through dtype_trait
author: xingsy97
body:
## Motivation

`exp`/`sin`/`cos` in `math.cuh` are hardcoded with `float` signatures, while all other math functions (`abs`, `sqrt`, `rsqrt`, `max`, `min`) dispatch through `dtype_trait<T>`. This inconsistency allows silent implicit conversion when half/bfloat16 values are passed.

Addresses review feedback from #19770.

## Modifications

- Register `exp`/`sin`/`cos` as unary functions in `dtype_trait<fp32_t>` (`type.cuh`).
- Convert `exp`/`sin`/`cos` in `math.cuh` from `float`-only to `template<typename T>` dispatching through `dtype_trait<T>`.

No behavioral change for existing callers (all pass `float`).

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — no change to model outputs. Only the function signature changed from `float` to `template<typename T>`; all existing callers already pass `float`.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

N/A — no change to inference speed. The generated PTX is identical for `float` callers.

title: Fix torch.compile/dynamo crash with Qwen3 QK-norm in piecewise CUDA g…
author: jasperjiaguo
body:
…raph

When using `--enable-piecewise-cuda-graph --piecewise-cuda-graph-compiler inductor` with Qwen3 models (which use QK-norm), the server crashes during CUDA graph warmup with `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported`.

Root cause: `can_use_fused_inplace_qknorm()` calls `logging.getLogger(__name__)` inside the function body. When torch.compile/dynamo traces this function, it cannot handle the `logging.getLogger()` call (string comparison with `LoggingLoggerVariable` fails). Additionally, the function performs filesystem I/O via `_jit_qknorm_module()` which dynamo also cannot trace.

Fix:
1. Move `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` to module level so dynamo never encounters it during tracing.
2. Add `@torch.compiler.assume_constant_result` decorator so dynamo evaluates the function eagerly in Python and inlines the boolean result, avoiding tracing into filesystem/JIT operations entirely.

Tested with Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B on H200 with piecewise CUDA graph + inductor.

title: [Triton] Use dynamic loop bound in `alloc_extend_kernel`
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary
- Use per-request `num_part2` (runtime value) as blocked loop bound instead of `max_num_extend_tokens` constexpr (fixes #19588, supersedes #19780)
- Remove `seen_max_num_extend_tokens_next_power_of_2` state and `TRITON_MAX_TENSOR_NUMEL` dispatch to `alloc_extend_naive` fallback

## Background
- Previous kernel used `max_num_extend_tokens: tl.constexpr` (historical max, power-of-2) as loop bound
- Every new power-of-2 value triggered Triton recompile (~15s), stalling EP ranks in collective ops
- #19780 replaced large `tl.arange` with blocked loop but kept the constexpr bound — loop was still statically unrolled

## Fix
- Use `num_part2` (already computed per-request in the kernel) as loop bound — `num_blocks` is no longer constexpr, so Triton emits a real dynamic loop
- One kernel compilation, right-sized per request, no fallback needed

title: Enable Piecewise CUDA Graph for NemotronH Hybrid (Mamba+Attention) Models
author: vedantjh2
body:
### Motivation

Piecewise CUDA graph (PCG) was previously disabled for NemotronH models because the layer detection logic required all layers to use standard GQA attention. NemotronH is a hybrid architecture (4 Attention + 24 Mamba + 24 MLP across 52 layers) where all sublayers use a `mixer` attribute instead of `self_attn`, causing the detection to fail with:

```
Disable piecewise CUDA graph because some layers do not apply Standard GQA
```

### Changes

**model_runner.py**

* Added `mixer` attribute detection for NemotronH-style hybrid models
* Every layer now gets an entry in `attention_layers` (`None` for non-attention layers), enabling PCG to handle sparse attention architectures
* Relaxed validation: PCG is only disabled when *no* attention layers are found, rather than when any layer lacks attention

**`nemotron_h.py`**

* Extracted `_forward_mamba()` method from `NemotronHMambaDecoderLayer.forward()`
* Added `nemotron_mamba2_with_output` split op (using `register_custom_op` + `register_split_op`) to enable graph breaks around Mamba layers during PCG capture
* Added token slicing in the split op to handle padded CUDA graph buffers (Mamba asserts on exact token counts)
* Changed `Layers` from union type (`A | B | C | D`) to tuple for `torch.compile` compatibility

### Benchmark Results

**Model:** NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 (H100, bfloat16)
**Benchmark:** GSM8K (200 samples)

| Configuration                          | Throughput (tok/s) | Latency (s) |  Accuracy |
| -------------------------------------- | -----------------: | ----------: | --------: |
| Baseline (no PCG)                      |               1521 |       15.74 |     88.0% |
| **With PCG (inductor)**                |           **1681** |   **14.29** | **89.0%** |
| **With PCG (eager)**                   |         **1542.8** |   **15.60** | **89.0%** |
| **Improvement vs baseline (inductor)** |         **+10.5%** |   **-9.2%** |         — |
| **Improvement vs baseline (eager)**    |          **+1.4%** |   **-0.9%** |         — |

**Notes**

* PCG provides the best gains when paired with the **inductor** compiler backend in this setup.
* PCG **eager** achieves essentially the same accuracy as PCG+inductor (89.0%), with smaller performance gains.

### Launch commands

```bash
# Baseline
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000

# With PCG (inductor)
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \
  --enable-piecewise-cuda-graph \
  --piecewise-cuda-graph-compiler inductor

# With PCG (eager)
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /shared/public/elr-models/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \
  --enable-piecewise-cuda-graph \
  --piecewise-cuda-graph-compiler eager
```

title: correct allreduce fusion and dummy_run alignment in SCATTERED MLP mode (moe_dense_tp_size=1)
author: weireweire
body:
## Problem

When `--moe-dense-tp-size 1` is set, dense MLP layers run in **SCATTERED mode** — hidden states are distributed across `attn_tp_size` ranks via reduce-scatter/all-gather instead of a standard TP all-reduce. Two bugs exist in this path.

---

### Bug 1 — Garbled output from spurious allreduce fusion (`communicator.py`)

`should_fuse_mlp_allreduce_with_next_layer()` returns `True` in SCATTERED mode, instructing the scheduler to fuse an all-reduce that does not exist. The actual gather communication is skipped, and all downstream layers receive wrong data → **garbage output from every inference request**.


**Fix:** return `False` early in `should_fuse_mlp_allreduce_with_next_layer()` when `mlp_mode == ScatterMode.SCATTERED`.

---

### Bug 2 — `_dummy_run` crash when `max_running_requests` not divisible by TP size (`model_runner.py`)

`_dummy_run()` passes `batch_size = max_running_requests` straight to the forward pass. In SCATTERED mode the reduce-scatter kernel requires `num_tokens % attn_tp_size == 0`. When this does not hold (e.g. `--max-running-requests 97` with `attn_tp_size = 8`, since `97 % 8 = 1`), the kernel raises:

```
ValueError: input tensor must be the same size as output size times world size
```

The server crashes during warmup before accepting any requests. The scheduler already performs this ceil-alignment at runtime; `_dummy_run` was the only call site that bypassed it.

**Fix:** ceil-align `num_tokens` to `attn_tp_size` inside `_dummy_run` when `moe_dense_tp_size == 1`.

---

## Reproduction

Tested on B200, 8×GPU, DeepSeek-R1 (FP8/FP4), sglang v0.5.8.post1.

**Bug 1 — garbled output (server starts, inference returns garbage):**

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <deepseek-r1-fp8> \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 8 --ep 8 --moe-dense-tp-size 1 \
  --enable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion \
  --attention-backend trtllm_mla \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --max-running-requests 96 \
  --port 30000

curl http://localhost:30000/v1/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1","prompt":"Hello","max_tokens":32}'
# Without fix: "@@#SeptemberCreative---##0LTHE" (random tokens)
# With fix:    "<think>\nOkay, the user just sent a simple..." (coherent)
```

**Bug 2 — crash during warmup:**

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <deepseek-r1-fp8> \
  --tp 8 --ep 8 --moe-dense-tp-size 1 \
  --max-running-requests 97 \
  --port 30000
# Without fix: ValueError: input tensor must be the same size as output size times world size
#              (raised from _dummy_run → reduce_scatter_tensor, server exits)
# With fix: server starts successfully
```

title: fix scheduler for non-cuda devices and disable piecewise cuda graph f…
author: jmunetong
body:
# Fix scheduler for non-CUDA devices and disable piecewise CUDA graph for XPU

## Motivation

SGLang’s scheduler and server args were not fully compatible with non-CUDA devices (e.g. Intel XPU):

1. **XPU and piecewise CUDA graph**: Piecewise CUDA graph is a CUDA-specific feature. When `device == "xpu"`, it should be disabled automatically and the user informed, so XPU runs without attempting unsupported CUDA graph capture.

This PR  adds XPU-specific handling to force-disable piecewise CUDA graph with a clear warning.

## Modifications

- **`python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`**

- **`python/sglang/srt/server_args.py`**
  - Imported `is_xpu` from `sglang.srt.utils.common`.
  - adds if statement check `is_xpu` under _handle_piecewise_cuda_graph to be able to disable this argument.
  - adds import of is_xpu check
## Accuracy Tests

This change does not alter model forward or kernel logic. It only:
- Switches the scheduler to a device-agnostic stream context.
- Ensures piecewise CUDA graph is off on XPU.

No accuracy test results are required; behavior on CUDA is unchanged, and on XPU piecewise CUDA graph is explicitly disabled.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not applicable. The change fixes correctness and compatibility for non-CUDA (e.g. XPU) and does not intentionally change inference speed. On XPU, piecewise CUDA graph was not supported before; it is now cleanly disabled.

title: fix: default FP4 GEMM backend to flashinfer_cudnn on SM120 (Blackwell)
author: voipmonitor
body:
## Summary

- Default `--fp4-gemm-backend` from `flashinfer_cutlass` to `auto`
- `auto` now selects `flashinfer_cudnn` on SM120 (Blackwell), `flashinfer_cutlass` on other architectures (no behavior change for non-Blackwell)

## Problem

The `flashinfer_cutlass` FP4 GEMM backend produces **NaN values in dense MLP layers** when processing heterogeneous batches on SM120 (Blackwell) GPUs. This causes `torch.multinomial` to crash with `probability tensor contains either inf, nan or element < 0` under concurrent request load.

Key findings from debugging:
- NaN originates in **layer 0 dense MLP** (not attention, not MoE)
- Only **3-5 rows out of ~2000** get full NaN (all hidden dims)
- **Batch-composition dependent** — same input replayed alone doesn't trigger NaN; requires heterogeneous batches
- Identical NaN pattern across all 8 TP ranks (not a NCCL issue)
- Crashes consistently within 1-4 rounds of 64 concurrent requests

## Fix

`flashinfer_cudnn` does not exhibit this issue. Stress-tested:
- **flashinfer_cutlass**: NaN crash within 1-4 rounds of 64 concurrent requests
- **flashinfer_cudnn**: 3,200 requests (50 rounds × 64 concurrent) — **zero NaN, zero crashes**

This PR changes the default to `auto` which auto-selects `flashinfer_cudnn` on SM120 and preserves `flashinfer_cutlass` on all other architectures.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified `flashinfer_cudnn` produces zero NaN on SM120 with 3,200 concurrent requests
- [x] Verified `--fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutlass` still works as explicit override
- [ ] Non-Blackwell GPUs: `auto` resolves to `flashinfer_cutlass` (existing behavior unchanged)

## Environment tested

- 8× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, 96GB)
- GLM-5-NVFP4-MTP with `--quantization modelopt_fp4`, TP=8
- SGLang built from `main`

Full investigation details: Fix #20043

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Bugfix] Fix load_audio: mono before resample + use torchaudio
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Summary
- Reorder `load_audio()` to convert to mono **before** resampling (reduces computation by ~50% for stereo)
- Replace `scipy.signal.resample` (FFT-based, ~40min for 2hr audio) with `torchaudio.functional.resample` (polyphase filtering, industry standard)
- Handle multi-channel audio dimension correctly: transpose `(time, channel)` to `(channel, time)` for torchaudio, transpose back after
- `torchaudio` was already a project dependency but unused in `load_audio()`

## Test plan
- [x] Test with short audio files (< 1 min)
- [x] Test with long stereo audio (~2 hours) to verify performance improvement
- [x] Test with multi-channel audio (stereo, mono=False) to verify correct output

title: Enable modelopt quantized FLUX deployment
author: Edwardf0t1
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Add support for deploying NVIDIA ModelOpt FP8-quantized diffusion models in SGLang, starting with FLUX. This enables running FP8 checkpoints produced by ModelOpt's post-training quantization (`quant_algo: "FP8", quant_method: "modelopt"`) directly through the existing sglang generate / sglang serve CLI with no special flags — the pipeline auto-detects the `quantization_config` in the transformer's `config.json`.
FP8 inference uses the same CUTLASS FP8 GEMM kernels (`sgl_kernel.fp8_scaled_mm`) already used by the LLM runtime, providing faster inference on GPUs with FP8 tensor core support (Ada/Hopper/Blackwell).

## Modifications

New file: `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/quantization/modelopt_fp8.py`

- ModelOptFp8Config: Quantization config that parses ModelOpt's checkpoint format (quant_algo: "FP8") and implements ignore-list matching for excluded layers (e.g., `context_embedder`, `norm_out*`, `proj_out`, `time_text_embed*`, `x_embedder`).
- ModelOptFp8LinearMethod: Linear method that creates FP8 weight + per-tensor scale parameters, processes weights after loading (transpose to column-major layout, convert scales to per-channel for CUTLASS), and calls `apply_fp8_linear` from the LLM runtime for inference.

Modified: `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/quantization/__init__.py`

- Registered `"modelopt"` -> `ModelOptFp8Config` in the quantization method registry so it is auto-detected when loading a ModelOpt checkpoint.

Modified: `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/fsdp_load.py`

- Added auto-dequantization in `load_model_from_full_model_state_dict:` when a checkpoint weight is `float8_e4m3fn` but the target model parameter is a higher-precision dtype (e.g., `bfloat16`), the loader automatically looks up the corresponding `weight_scale` and dequantizes (`float_value = fp8_value * weight_scale`). This handles modules like diffusers' `AdaLayerNormZero` that contain linear layers quantized in the ModelOpt checkpoint but are not FP8-aware in the model definition (they use standard `nn.Linear` rather than SGLang's quantization-aware `LinearBase`).

## Accuracy Tests

Example usage:
```
sglang generate   --model-path /home/omniml_data_3/zhiyuc/checkpoints/FLUX.1-dev-FP8   --prompt "A beautiful sunset over the mountains"   --save-output --output-path outputs
```

- [x] Verify ModelOptFp8Config correctly parses the quantization_config from a ModelOpt FP8 checkpoint
- [x] Verify ignore-list matching correctly identifies excluded layers vs quantized layers
- [x] Generate an image with the FP8 FLUX checkpoint and confirm visual quality

title: feat: [1/2] [DeepEP] Fuse shared expert into MoE dispatch under EP
author: xutizhou
body:
## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

In DeepSeek V3/R1 with expert parallelism (EP), each rank currently computes the shared expert **separately** from routed experts. This means shared expert is not part of the DeepEP dispatch/compute/combine pipeline — it runs as a standalone forward pass on every rank.

This PR fuses the shared expert into the MoE path by treating it as an additional routed expert (the "9th expert" per rank). Instead of computing shared expert separately, it is dispatched through DeepEP alongside routed experts, assigned to the source rank's local shared expert slot.

This is the **first half** of the waterfill feature split (requested by @ch-wan in #19290):
- **[1/2] This PR**: Fuse shared expert into DeepEP dispatch (fixed local assignment)
- **[2/2] Follow-up PR**: Add waterfill load balancing to dynamically assign shared expert to the least-loaded rank

coauthor: @AichenF

## Modifications

**New file: `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/deepep_shared_expert_fusion.py`** (65 lines)
- `LOCAL_SHARED_MARKER`: sentinel value for invalid expert ID (DeepEP ignores `expert_id < 0`)
- `expand_topk_with_shared_expert()`: expands topk output `[N, 8] → [N, 9]` with expert ID remapping and shared expert always assigned to source rank

**Modified files:**

- **`models/deepseek_v2.py`** (+138/−22):
  - Adjusts `num_experts` and `top_k` to account for extra shared expert slots (`+ep_size` experts, `+1` topk)
  - Skips standalone shared expert forward when fusion is enabled
  - Calls `expand_topk_with_shared_expert()` after TopK selection to append shared expert column
  - Allows shared expert fusion under EP when `--enable-deepep-waterfill` is set (bypasses existing EP disable checks)

- **`layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py`** (+40/−2):
  - Expert ID remapping in weight loading: maps checkpoint expert IDs to expanded layout (original routed experts + 1 shared expert slot per rank)
  - Adjusts shared expert detection threshold for the expanded expert ID space

- **`server_args.py`** (+29/−1):
  - Adds `--enable-deepep-waterfill` CLI flag with validation (requires `moe_a2a_backend='deepep'`)
  - Updates `--disable-shared-experts-fusion` help text

## Usage

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path <DeepSeek-V3-path> \
    --tp 16 --dp-size 16 --nnodes 2 --node-rank {0|1} \
    --dist-init-addr <addr>:<port> \
    --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode normal \
    --enable-dp-attention \
    --enable-deepep-waterfill
```

title: fix: add ModelScope cache lookup and speculative path support
author: alphabetc1
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
When `SGLANG_USE_MODELSCOPE=true`, sglang already supports downloading models from ModelScope. However, many popular models have different repo IDs on HuggingFace vs ModelScope (e.g. `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct` on HF → `LLM-Research/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct` on ModelScope).

The current code calls `snapshot_download` directly, which hits the ModelScope API to verify the repo exists before checking any local cache. So even if you symlink the model into the cache directory, it still fails with a 404 because the HF repo ID doesn't exist on ModelScope.

This PR checks the local cache first before falling back to `snapshot_download`. That way, if you create a symlink under the ModelScope cache dir, sglang picks it up immediately without any network call.

Also extends ModelScope support to `speculative_draft_model_path` and `load_token_map`, which were previously HF-only.

### usage
```
# Create a symlink in the ModelScope cache:
ln -s /path/to/local/model \
  ~/.cache/modelscope/hub/models/meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct
```
```
# Then launch as usual:
SGLANG_USE_MODELSCOPE=true SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-draft-model-path lmsys/sglang-EAGLE-LLaMA3-Instruct-8B \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.7 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 8 \
  --dtype float16
```

title: [JIT] Inject target architecture flag into JIT compilation
author: xingsy97
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up from #19794 (comment by @DarkSharpness): `__CUDA_ARCH__` is only available in the device pass, so arch macros can't be used for host-side dispatch. This PR injects `-DSGL_CUDA_ARCH=<value>` via `load_jit()` so that arch-dependent macros work in both host and device passes.

## Modifications

- **`utils.py`**: Inject `-DSGL_CUDA_ARCH={major*100+minor*10}` into JIT cuda cflags based on `torch.cuda.get_device_capability()`.
- **`utils.cuh`**: Add `SGL_TARGET_CUDA_ARCH` (prefers `__CUDA_ARCH__` in device pass, falls back to `SGL_CUDA_ARCH` in host pass). Define `SGL_ARCH_HOPPER_OR_GREATER` and `SGL_ARCH_BLACKWELL_OR_GREATER`. Refactor PDL guards to use them.

title: [env] Add SGLANG_SORT_WEIGHT_FILES env var for sequential I/O optimization
author: power-more
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

When loading large sharded models, the order in which weight files are accessed can impact I/O performance. `glob.glob()` returns files in an order determined by the underlying file system (typically inode order on ext4), which may not be sequential. On inference-engine-aware file systems with sequential prefetch, non-sequential access leads to suboptimal prefetch behavior and increased I/O latency.

This PR adds a lightweight environment variable `SGLANG_SORT_WEIGHT_FILES` that sorts weight files alphabetically before loading, ensuring a deterministic and sequential access pattern.

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

- **`python/sglang/srt/environ.py`**: Add `SGLANG_SORT_WEIGHT_FILES = EnvBool(False)` to the `Envs` class.
- **`python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py`**: Sort `hf_weights_files` in `DefaultModelLoader._prepare_weights()` when the env var is set. Applies to all weight formats (safetensors, bin, pt).
- **`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/component_loaders/text_encoder_loader.py`**: Sort `hf_weights_files` in `TextEncoderLoader._prepare_weights()` using the same env var, replacing the previous `self._server_args` approach with a cleaner direct env var read.

Key design points:
- **Zero invasion**: Guarded by a runtime switch (`default=False`). When disabled by default, no code path is touched.

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

## Accuracy Tests

No accuracy impact. The change only affects the *order* of file loading, not the content. Each tensor is loaded by name from the state dict, so the final model weights are identical regardless of file order.

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

## Benchmarking and Profiling

| Metric | Without Sort (avg) | With Sort (avg) |
|---|---|---|
| Weight-load phase | 1244 s | 1230 s |
| Tensor deserialization | 704 s | 666 s |
| Startup overhead | 107 s | 107 s |
| **Total end-to-end** | **2055 s** | **2003 s** |

**Key observations:**
- On inference-engine-aware file systems with sequential prefetch optimizations, the improvement is expected to be significantly larger.
- This switch-controlled feature serves as a prerequisite for follow-up I/O optimizations (e.g., concurrent prefetch).

title: perf: avoid unnecessary gpu-cpu sync in eagle_info
author: ehuaa
body: ## Motivation When stress testing Qwen3.5-397B with MTP enabled, the scheduler occasionally encounters the following scheduler watchdog error. Preliminary analysis suggests a potential deadlock arising from the interaction between GPU-CPU synchronization and collective communications (e.g., AllReduce). According to the log below, the GPU-CPU sync happens in eagle_info.py. This PR not only mitigates potential deadlock issues but also eliminates synchronization overhead, thereby improving overall inference performance. ``` [2026-03-10 02:09:02 TP2] Pyspy dump for PID 501830: Process 501830: sglang::scheduler_TP2 Python v3.12.3 (/usr/bin/python3.12) Thread 501830 (active): "MainThread" 0x7f9484041d1d (libcuda.so.575.57.08) 0x7f9483df9493 (libcuda.so.575.57.08) 0x7f9483e3a2eb (libcuda.so.575.57.08) 0x7f9484acc998 (libcuda.so.575.57.08) 0x7f9484accdc8 (libcuda.so.575.57.08) 0x7f9483e0542c (libcuda.so.575.57.08) 0x7f9483ec4d3a (libcuda.so.575.57.08) 0x7f9484a864e9 (libcuda.so.575.57.08) 0x7f9483f76e37 (libcuda.so.575.57.08) cuStreamSynchronize (libcuda.so.575.57.08) 0x7f95b1e128b3 (libcudart.so.12) cudaStreamSynchronize (libcudart.so.12) at::native::_local_scalar_dense_cuda(at::Tensor const&)::{lambda()#1}::operator() const (libtorch_cuda.so) at::native::_local_scalar_dense_cuda (libtorch_cuda.so) at::(anonymous namespace)::(anonymous namespace)::wrapper_CUDA___local_scalar_dense (libtorch_cuda.so) c10::impl::wrap_kernel_functor_unboxed_, c10::Scalar, c10::guts::typelist::typelist >, c10::Scalar(at::Tensor const&)>::call (libtorch_cuda.so) at::_ops::_local_scalar_dense::redispatch (libtorch_cpu.so) torch::autograd::VariableType::(anonymous namespace)::_local_scalar_dense (libtorch_cpu.so) c10::impl::wrap_kernel_functor_unboxed_, c10::Scalar, c10::guts::typelist::typelist >, c10::Scalar(c10::DispatchKeySet, at::Tensor const&)>::call (libtorch_cpu.so) at::_ops::_local_scalar_dense::call (libtorch_cpu.so) at::native::item (libtorch_cpu.so) c10::impl::wrap_kernel_functor_unboxed_, c10::Scalar, c10::guts::typelist::typelist >, c10::Scalar(at::Tensor const&)>::call (libtorch_cpu.so) at::_ops::item::call (libtorch_cpu.so) at::native::is_nonzero (libtorch_cpu.so) at::_ops::is_nonzero::call (libtorch_cpu.so) torch::autograd::THPVariable_is_nonzero (libtorch_python.so) verify (eagle_info.py:340) verify (eagle_worker.py:748) forward_batch_generation (eagle_worker.py:316) run_batch (scheduler.py:2368) event_loop_normal (scheduler.py:1123) ... ``` ## Modifications modify if-statement in eagle_info.py to use need_top_p_sampling instead of computing top_p sampling mask again. ## Accuracy Tests This pull requests does not affect model outputs. ## Benchmarking and Profiling Before After The comparison shows that we’ve shaved off serveral cuda kernel operations, for example, ten D2H operations (equivalent to the number of steps in the profile). title: [diffusion] doc: add diffusion-optimal-perf
author: mickqian
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->



### Motivation

There was no centralized reference for all performance-related CLI flags and their trade-offs in SGLang-Diffusion. Users (and AI coding assistants) had to piece together information from PRs, blog posts, and source code to figure out the fastest command for a given setup.

### Modifications

- Added `.claude/skills/diffusion-optimal-perf/SKILL.md` — a structured performance tuning guide with:
- Updated `.claude/CLAUDE.md` to reference the new skill under a `## Performance Tuning` section.

### Example (With Claude Code 2.1.72, Opus 4.6)



**Question:**


> I have 8x H100 80GB GPUs. I want to generate a 720p, 81-frame video using Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers with 40 inference steps and guidance_scale=5.0. What's the fastest `sglang generate` command I can use? Also, what should I change if I run into OOM?

**Answer:**

⏺ Fastest lossless command:

```
  sglang generate --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers \
    --num-gpus 8 --enable-cfg-parallel --ulysses-degree 4 \
    --enable-torch-compile --warmup \
    --text-encoder-cpu-offload true \
    --prompt "Your prompt here" \
    --num-inference-steps 40 --guidance-scale 5.0 \
    --height 720 --width 1280 --num-frames 81 \
    --save-output
  ```

  Why these flags:

  - --enable-cfg-parallel --ulysses-degree 4 — CFG parallel splits the 8 GPUs into 2 groups of 4 (conditional
   + unconditional branches run in parallel). This is faster than pure Ulysses-8 for CFG models.
  - --enable-torch-compile --warmup — Fuses ops in the DiT; warmup eliminates first-request compilation
  latency.
  - --dit-layerwise-offload — Enabled by default for Wan video models. Zero-cost because per-layer compute >>
   H2D transfer time for 81-frame video.
  - --text-encoder-cpu-offload true — Frees VRAM after text encoding is done.

  If you hit OOM, try these in order:

  1. --vae-cpu-offload true — Offloads VAE to CPU when not decoding. This is the biggest single win since the
   VAE is only used at the end.
  2. --dit-offload-prefetch-size 0 — Minimizes DiT VRAM to ~2 layers on GPU at a time (default prefetch is
  already conservative, but 0 is the floor).
  3. --dit-precision fp16 — Halves DiT memory vs BF16 (lossy, but usually acceptable).
  4. Reduce --ulysses-degree to 2 — Less SP communication overhead but more VRAM per GPU since fewer GPUs
  share the sequence.

  With 8x H100 80GB you should have plenty of headroom though — Wan A14B with layerwise offload uses ~11 GB per GPU for the DiT.

title: perf(qwen3_5): replace einops rearrange with torch.flatten in GatedDe…
author: vedantjh2
body: ## Motivation `einops.rearrange` performs Python-level string parsing and validation on **every call**. In `Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet.forward()`, the pattern `rearrange(x, "... h d -> ... (h d)")` is a simple flatten of the last two dimensions — equivalent to `torch.flatten(-2)`, which is a zero-copy view operation with no parsing overhead. This call runs on every forward pass through every GDN layer in the model, so the overhead accumulates significantly. ## Changes - Replace `rearrange(core_attn_out, "... h d -> ... (h d)")` with `core_attn_out.flatten(-2)` in `Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet.forward()` - Remove unused `from einops import rearrange` import ## Profiling Results Profiled on **Qwen3.5-9B**, H100 80GB, TP=1, CUDA graphs disabled, using `sglang.bench_serving` with torch profiler. Perfetto SQL queries filtered to only `GatedDeltaNet` ancestor slices. ### Baseline (einops) | name | call_count | avg_dur_us | total_dur_us | |---|---|---|---| | `einops/einops.py(561): rearrange` | 720 | 12.67 | 9125.43 | ### Optimized (torch.flatten) | name | call_count | avg_dur_us | total_dur_us | min_dur_us | max_dur_us | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `` | 720 | 4.74 | 3410.18 | 3.97 | 67.35 | | `aten::flatten` | 720 | 2.50 | 1797.94 | 2.09 | 65.37 | ### Summary - **Per-call: 2.67x faster** (12.67 us → 4.74 us) - **Total time: 63% reduction** (9125 us → 3410 us across 720 calls) - **5715 us saved** per profiled window ## Profiling Reproduction Commands ### 1. Launch server ```bash export SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR=/path/to/traces python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B \ --port 30000 --tp 1 --disable-cuda-graph ``` ### 2. Run profiling benchmark ```bash export PYTHONPATH=/path/to/sglang/python:$PYTHONPATH export SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR=/path/to/traces python -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang \ --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B \ --num-prompts 10 --random-input-len 256 --random-output-len 32 \ --dataset-name random --profile ``` ### 3. Perfetto SQL queries **Baseline** (einops rearrange in GatedDeltaNet): ```sql SELECT s.name, COUNT(*) AS call_count, AVG(s.dur)/1000.0 AS avg_dur_us, SUM(s.dur)/1000.0 AS total_dur_us FROM slice s WHERE s.name LIKE '%rearrange%' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ancestor_slice(s.id) a WHERE a.name LIKE '%GatedDeltaNet%') GROUP BY s.name; ``` **Optimized** (flatten in GatedDeltaNet): ```sql SELECT s.name, COUNT(*) AS call_count, AVG(s.dur)/1000.0 AS avg_dur_us, SUM(s.dur)/1000.0 AS total_dur_us, MIN(s.dur)/1000.0 AS min_dur_us, MAX(s.dur)/1000.0 AS max_dur_us FROM slice s WHERE s.name LIKE '%flatten%' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ancestor_slice(s.id) a WHERE a.name LIKE '%GatedDeltaNet%') GROUP BY s.name; ``` ## Correctness `flatten(-2)` is semantically identical to `rearrange("... h d -> ... (h d)")` — both merge the last two dimensions into one. No behavior change. Ran GSM8k to test performance and accuracy | Metric | Baseline (einops) | Optimized (native) | |---|---|---| | **Accuracy** | **0.905** | **0.900** | | Invalid | 0.000 | 0.000 | | Latency | 28.075s | 26.704s | | Output throughput | 789.6 tok/s | 828.1 tok/s | ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. title: Add offline auto-tuning for LoRA CSGMV kernel
author: satyamk7054
body:
## Motivation

Add offline auto-tuning script for LoRA csgmv shrink / expand kernels (similar to MoE auto-tuning)

On H200 with Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (rank=64), tuning yields **2-3x speedup on shrink kernels** and **1.1-1.5x on expand kernels**

## Modifications

- **Add `lora_tuning_config.py`**: Config loader with LRU cache – same MoE loader
- **Add `tune_lora_csgmv.py`**: Offline script to generate configs
- Update kernel invocations to use the loaded configs (with existing defaults); maxnregs helped with occupancy so added that as kwargs
- Unit test for loading logic
```
python -m unittest test.manual.lora.test_lora_tuning_config -v
```

### Fallback behavior
When no tuned config is found (no config file for the current GPU/model/Triton version), falls back to the original upstream defaults. 

### Usage
```bash
# Tune for a model (auto-derives all layer dims)
python benchmark/kernels/lora_csgmv/tune_lora_csgmv.py \
    --model Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B --rank 64

# Configs saved to python/sglang/srt/lora/triton_ops/csgmv_configs/<triton_version>/
# Server automatically picks them up with --lora-backend csgmv

title: perf(kimi_linear): replace einops rearrange with native torch ops in Kimi-Linear KDA path
author: vedantjh2
body: ## Motivation `einops.rearrange` adds Python-level overhead (pattern parsing, backend dispatch, shape validation) on every call. In the Kimi-Linear-48B model's KimiDeltaAttention hot path, this is called thousands of times per forward pass. This PR replaces all 8 `einops.rearrange` calls with equivalent native PyTorch operations (`unflatten`, `unsqueeze`, `squeeze`, `flatten`) across 2 files, removing the `einops` import entirely from both. ## Files Changed - **`kimi_linear.py`** — 2 rearrange calls replaced in `KimiDeltaAttention.forward()` - **`kda_backend.py`** — 6 rearrange calls replaced in `forward_decode()` and `forward_extend()` ## Profiling Results Profiled with **Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct** on **2x H100 80GB (TP=2)**, `--disable-cuda-graph`, 10 prompts (512 input / 128 output tokens). Results scoped to `nn.Module: KimiDeltaAttention_*` spans via Perfetto SQL. ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /shared/public/elr-models/moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct \ --port 30000 --tp 2 --disable-cuda-graph --trust-remote-code ``` ### Baseline (einops) ```sql SELECT name, COUNT(*) AS calls, ROUND(AVG(dur) / 1e3, 4) AS avg_ms, ROUND(SUM(dur) / 1e3, 2) AS total_ms FROM slice WHERE name = 'einops/einops.py(561): rearrange' AND id IN ( SELECT s.id FROM slice s JOIN ancestor_slice(s.id) a ON a.name GLOB 'nn.Module: KimiDeltaAttention_*' ) GROUP BY name;wwwww ``` | name | calls | avg (us) | total (ms) | |---|---|---|---| | `einops::rearrange` | 12,600 | 15.77 | 198.70 | ### Optimized (native torch) ```sql SELECT name, COUNT(*) AS calls, ROUND(AVG(dur) / 1e3, 4) AS avg_ms, ROUND(SUM(dur) / 1e3, 2) AS total_ms FROM slice WHERE name IN ('aten::unflatten', 'aten::flatten', 'aten::unsqueeze', 'aten::squeeze') AND id IN ( SELECT s.id FROM slice s JOIN ancestor_slice(s.id) a ON a.name GLOB 'nn.Module: KimiDeltaAttention_*' ) GROUP BY name; ``` | name | calls | avg (us) | total (ms) | |---|---|---|---| | `aten::unflatten` | 10,080 | 3.41 | 34.41 | | `aten::unsqueeze` | 12,604 | 2.62 | 33.06 | | `aten::squeeze` | 7,520 | 5.29 | 39.80 | | `aten::flatten` | 2,520 | 2.57 | 6.47 | | **Total** | | | **113.74** | **~1.75x reduction** in reshape-related CPU overhead (198.70ms -> 113.74ms). ## Correctness ``` python benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --data-path /shared/public/data/gsm8k/test.jsonl ``` | Metric | Baseline (einops) | Optimized (native torch) | |---|---|---| | **Accuracy** | 0.915 | 0.910 | | Invalid | 0.000 | 0.000 | | Latency | 41.6s | 40.0s | | Throughput | 471.9 tok/s | 490.7 tok/s | Ran the same test in `registered/models/test_kimi_linear_models.py` Locally launched SGLang server with the command: ``` python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /shared/public/elr-models/moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct --port 30000 --tp 2 --trust-remote-code ``` then launched the test with the following command and result: ``` python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-shots 5 --num-questions 200 --max-new-tokens 512 --parallel 128 --port 30000 --data-path /shared/public/data/gsm8k/test.jsonl 100%|██████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████| 200/200 [00:09<00:00, 21.65it/s] Accuracy: 0.900 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 9.288 s Output throughput: 2059.970 token/s ``` All replacements produce **bitwise identical** outputs to the original einops operations, verified with `torch.equal` across multiple tensor shapes, dtypes, and contiguity states.

title: [DP Attention] Optimize dp_padding_mode selection for dp_size=1 in extend mode
author: wangfakang
body:
CC @yizhang2077 @ShangmingCai @nvcastet @ch-wan @merrymercy @Fridge003 PTAL, thx. 

## Motivation

When dp_size=1, the `MAX_LEN` and `SUM_LEN` modes have identical communication overhead since max_len equals sum_len. Previously, extend mode(`get_dp_padding_mode`) unconditionally used `SUM_LEN`, which prevented symmetric memory from being used (via disabled=True).

Now with dp_size=1, we prefer `MAX_LEN` mode to enable symmetric memory optimizations needed for NSA CP and other features.


https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/abc672e7177b3ec366c2791845447e3f121fdfc9/python/sglang/srt/layers/dp_attention.py#L64-L68

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/abc672e7177b3ec366c2791845447e3f121fdfc9/python/sglang/srt/layers/dp_attention.py#L119-L125

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/abc672e7177b3ec366c2791845447e3f121fdfc9/python/sglang/srt/layers/dp_attention.py#L129-L135

## Modifications
Update the logic of  `get_dp_padding_mode` :

  - Only use `SUM_LEN` for extend mode when `dp_size > 1`.
  - Prefer MAX_LEN when communication cost is equal (`>=` instead of `>`).
  - This allows symmetric memory optimization for NSA CP and other use cases.

title: [AMD][AITER] Guard _use_mla_ps_kernel with self.use_mla in draft_extend_v2 paths
author: ChuanLi1101
body:
## Motivation

This PR fixes #16027 — non-MLA models (e.g. GLM-4.7) crash with `AttributeError: 'AiterAttnBackend' object has no attribute 'max_split_per_batch'` when using EAGLE speculative decoding with the AITER attention backend on ROCm.

The root cause: the global flag `_use_mla_ps_kernel` defaults to `True`, but `self.max_split_per_batch` is only initialized inside the `if self.use_mla:` block in `__init__`. Two code paths in `is_draft_extend_v2()` branches check `if _use_mla_ps_kernel:` without verifying `self.use_mla` first, causing the crash on non-MLA models.

A previous fix attempt (PR #16682) was closed without merge.

## Modifications

Added `self.use_mla and` guard to two bare `if _use_mla_ps_kernel:` checks in `aiter_backend.py`:

1. `init_forward_metadata_capture_cuda_graph` — `is_draft_extend_v2()` branch (line 1316)
