title: Fix failing `test_nvidia_nemotron_3_nano` by fixing `test_grouped_topk`
author: kpham-sgl
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Fix the Nemotron-3-Nano FP8 failure exposed after enabling the JIT grouped-topk path.

Nemotron now selects the JIT `grouped_topk` path because its router config matches the kernel constraints: one expert group, `topk_group=1`, 128 routed experts, `topk=6`, and correction bias. That exposed two separate issues.

First, the grouped-topk kernel did not order negative choice scores correctly. Nemotron's correction bias can make `sigmoid(score) + bias` negative, so the float packing used for max reduction must preserve ordering across the full float range, not just positive values.

Second, Nemotron's PCG Mamba split op receives buffers padded to the captured graph size, but Mamba only computes the actual token rows. Before this PR, the padded rows in the split-op output were left uninitialized. Once execution continued into the grouped-topk/FP8 MoE path under graph replay, downstream kernels could see those padded rows as garbage/non-finite hidden states. Zero-filling the padded tail makes that region deterministic and harmless.

## Modifications

- Fix `grouped_topk` float packing so `sigmoid(score) + correction_bias` is ordered correctly even when the result is negative.
- Zero-fill padded Nemotron Mamba outputs in piecewise CUDA graph mode.
- Add a regression test for Nemotron-like `E=128, topk=6` routing with negative choice scores.

## Accuracy Tests

`pytest python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_grouped_topk.py` and `pytest test/registered/models/test_nvidia_nemotron_3_nano.py ` all passed locally

## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: [Bug Fix] Reject incompatible combination of --disable-cuda-graph-padding and --enable-torch-compile
author: ppraneth
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Fixes #23865.

When a user passes both `--disable-cuda-graph-padding` and `--enable-torch-compile` together, the engine never finishes initializing. It silently hangs for many minutes (or indefinitely on larger models) with no indication that anything is wrong.

The root cause is a batch size explosion in the CUDA/CPU graph capture step. With padding enabled, the capture list is a small fixed set of bucket sizes like `[1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24]`. With padding disabled, `_generate_cuda_graph_batch_sizes` and `_generate_cpu_graph_batch_sizes` both expand this to every integer from 1 up to `cuda_graph_max_bs` (for example, 1 through 24 or up to 160 on small GPUs). Because `CPUGraphRunner` runs a full `torch.compile` and Triton AUTOTUNE cycle for each batch size, the number of kernel benchmarks grows from roughly 28 (7 buckets x 4 matmul shapes) to hundreds or thousands. In the reproduction on an RTX 4090, the process was killed after 3 minutes while still at batch size 11 out of 24.

The two flags are also semantically incompatible at runtime. `--disable-cuda-graph-padding` means the server will route exact incoming batch sizes without rounding up. If those exact sizes were not pre-compiled, `torch.compile` would trigger a new compilation on the fly during request serving, causing latency spikes for real traffic.

## Modifications

- Added a validation check in `ServerArgs.check_server_args()` in `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py` that raises an `AssertionError` immediately at engine startup when both `--disable-cuda-graph-padding` and `--enable-torch-compile` are passed together.
- The error message explains the cause (O(max_batch_size) autotune explosion) and tells the user which flag to remove, so there is no silent hang and no confusion about what went wrong.
- No behavior change for any other flag combination.

title: [Refactor] Cuda Graph Runner/Backend Refactor
author: Oasis-Git
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/23004 

## Modifications

### Runner ↔ CudaGraphBackend Interaction (cg-refactor)

Two layers are in scope:

- **Phase runner** — `PrefillCudaGraphRunner` / `DecodeCudaGraphRunner`
  - Both subclass `BaseCudaGraphRunner`
  - Exactly one runner per phase
  - Fixed implementation

- **CG backend** — `BaseCudaGraphBackend` and its subclasses:
  - `FullCudaGraphBackend`
  - `BreakableCudaGraphBackend`
  - `TcPiecewiseCudaGraphBackend`
  - Pluggable per phase
  - Selected at initialization by:
    - `resolve_prefill_backend(model_runner)`
    - `resolve_decode_backend(model_runner)`
  - Backend type comes from:
    - `cuda_graph_config[phase].backend`

---

### Phase Runner API (`BaseCudaGraphRunner`)

Exposed upward to `ModelRunner`.

Each method delegates strategy-specific behavior to `self.backend`.

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `can_run(forward_batch) -> bool` | Determine whether the current batch can use a captured graph. Performs runner-level filtering before consulting the backend. |
| `capture()` | One-time capture entrypoint. Enumerates all capture shapes and invokes `capture_one_shape()` for each. |
| `capture_one_shape(size, ...)` | Captures a single shape. Builds a dummy forward batch and delegates actual capture to `self.backend.capture_one(...)`. |
| `replay_prepare(forward_batch, **kwargs) -> ForwardBatch` | Pads or reshapes inputs to match a captured shape and returns the static batch used during replay. |
| `replay(forward_batch, ...) -> ModelOutput` | Executes the captured graph via `self.backend.replay(...)`. |

---

### CG Backend API (`BaseCudaGraphBackend`)

Exposed downward to the phase runner.

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `prepare(runner)` | One-time setup against the owning runner. Wires static buffers, patches the model module, and installs forward hooks. |
| `setup_prefill_state(runner)` *(prefill only)* | Additional one-time initialization for prefill-specific state. |
| `can_run(forward_batch) -> bool` | Strategy-specific runtime gate. Examples: BCG rejects sparse-DP batches; TcPiecewise checks `torch.compile` state. |
| `capture_session(stream)` *(context manager)* | Wraps the entire capture phase. Sets graph-pool ID, capture flags, allocator hints, etc. |
| `capture_one(num_tokens, ...)` | Captures a single shape. The runner provides the dummy batch; the backend performs warmup and recorded forward execution. |
| `has_shape(shape_key) -> bool` | Returns whether a recorded graph exists for the given shape. Used by `runner.can_run()`. |
| `runtime_session()` *(context manager)* | Wraps a replay execution. Sets replay flags, locks caches, and scopes graph resources. |
| `replay(shape_key, forward_batch) -> ModelOutput` | Executes the recorded graph corresponding to the shape key. |
| `populate_prefill_dummy_inputs(...)` *(prefill only)* | Fills capture-time placeholders so recorded graphs observe stable input addresses. |
| `commit_prefill_serving_inputs(forward_batch)` *(prefill only)* | Copies real serving inputs into static buffers immediately before replay. |
| `cleanup()` | Releases graph pools and removes any model patching. |

---

### Runner → Backend Interaction

#### Initialization

Once per runner:

    runner.init
    └─ self.backend = resolve_{prefill,decode}_backend(model_runner)
       ├─ self.backend.prepare(self)
       └─ prefill only:
          └─ self.backend.setup_prefill_state(self)

---

#### Capture

Once, across all capture shapes:

    runner.capture()
    └─ with backend.capture_session(stream):
       └─ for size in capture_shapes:
          └─ runner.capture_one_shape(size)
             ├─ build dummy forward_batch
             │  └─ runner-owned logic
             ├─ prefill only:
             │  └─ backend.populate_prefill_dummy_inputs(...)
             └─ backend.capture_one(num_tokens, ...)
                └─ warmup + recorded forward

---

#### Replay

Per forward, on the hot path:

    ModelRunner.forward(batch)
    ├─ if not runner.can_run(batch):
    │  └─ fall back to eager
    │
    │     runner.can_run() internally consults:
    │     - backend.has_shape(...)
    │     - backend.can_run(...)
    │
    ├─ static_batch = runner.replay_prepare(batch)
    │  └─ prefill only:
    │     └─ backend.commit_prefill_serving_inputs(batch)
    │
    └─ with backend.runtime_session():
       └─ output = backend.replay(shape_key, static_batch)

---

### Backend-Specific Overrides

| Backend | Capture mechanism | Distinct overrides |
|---|---|---|
| `FullCudaGraphBackend` | `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` over the entire model forward | `capture_session()`, `capture_one()`, `replay()` |
| `BreakableCudaGraphBackend` | Multiple `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` segments stitched at `eager_on_graph` breakpoints | `capture_one()`, `replay()`, plus per-segment metadata in `attn_metadata_buffers` |
| `TcPiecewiseCudaGraphBackend` | `torch.compile(mode="reduce-overhead")` with FX-level piecewise splits | `prepare()` installs compile hooks; `capture_one()` drives `torch.compile` warmup; no direct graph replay recording because `torch.compile` owns execution |

---

### Where the Seam Matters

The runner/backend boundary is the extensibility point.

Adding a new CUDA Graph strategy requires:

1. Creating a new `BaseCudaGraphBackend` subclass.
2. Registering it in the backend factory.

The phase runner code should remain unchanged.

This refactor replaces the previous design where each strategy required its own runner implementation.

The strict API contract is the runner call points listed above. If a new strategy requires additional coordination, the corresponding hook should be added to `BaseCudaGraphBackend` so that all runners can drive the strategy uniformly.

## Accuracy Tests

## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: jit_kernel/deepseek_v4: replace BF16->FP32 cuBLAS JIT with torch.mm
author: sihan-zzz
body:
## Motivation

Use the PyTorch-native `torch.mm(input, mat2, out_dtype=torch.float32)` API for the BF16-input / FP32-output GEMM, instead of the hand-written JIT `cublasGemmEx` kernel.

The JIT kernel was the right thing to ship before this `out_dtype` overload landed. PyTorch 2.9 (which `python/pyproject.toml` already pins via `"torch==2.9.1"`) lowers `torch.mm(bf16, bf16, out_dtype=torch.float32)` directly to the same cuBLAS `gemmEx` path, so the JIT no longer adds anything — it just costs ~74 s of `nvcc` compile on cold start, an inline-CUDA blob, and a `compile_aot()` entry.

## Change

`python/sglang/jit_kernel/deepseek_v4.py`:

- Replace the `algo == "cublas"` branch in `_dispatch_bf16_fp32_backend` with `torch.mm(x, y.t(), out_dtype=torch.float32)`.
- Delete `_jit_torch_cublas_bf16_fp32()` (the `@cache_once` `load_inline` block).
- Remove the corresponding `("cublas", _jit_torch_cublas_bf16_fp32)` entry from `compile_aot()`.

`deep_gemm` and the python-fallback branches are kept untouched. Net diff: **+4 / -62**.

## Verification

Built the same JIT kernel inline (verbatim source from this branch's parent commit) and compared head-to-head against `torch.mm(out_dtype=torch.float32)`. Tested on **B200** (`lmsysorg/sglang:deepseek-v4-blackwell` image, GCP a4 partition) and **H100** (`lmsysorg/sglang:deepseek-v4-hopper` image, single GPU). Both: `torch==2.9.1+cu129`, CUDA 12.9.

### 1. Accuracy — bit-exact on every shape, both GPUs

`torch.equal(jit_out, mm_out) == True`, max abs diff = `0.0` for all M ∈ {1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192,16384} (with N=1024 K=4096), and for the additional shapes (256/1024/4096/8192, 4096, 4096), (256/1024/4096, 8192, 4096). Both implementations also produce the same residual against an FP32 reference.

| (M, N, K)            | max abs diff (pair) | bit-exact (B200) | bit-exact (H100) |
| -------------------- | ------------------- | :--------------: | :--------------: |
| (1, 1024, 4096)      | 0.000e+00           |        ✓         |        ✓         |
| (256, 1024, 4096)    | 0.000e+00           |        ✓         |        ✓         |
| (4096, 1024, 4096)   | 0.000e+00           |        ✓         |        ✓         |
| (16384, 1024, 4096)  | 0.000e+00           |        ✓         |        ✓         |
| (4096, 4096, 4096)   | 0.000e+00           |        ✓         |        ✓         |
| (4096, 8192, 4096)   | 0.000e+00           |        ✓         |        ✓         |

This confirms `torch.mm(out_dtype=fp32)` dispatches into the **same** cuBLAS routine with the same algo selection as `cublasGemmEx(... CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F, CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP)`.

### 2. Performance — focus on **CUDA Graph** numbers (kernel-only, no Python overhead)

CUDA Graph capture replays 8 ops per graph × 2000 graphs = **16 000 timed kernel invocations per cell**, eliminating eager-mode Python dispatcher / driver-launch overhead so we measure the kernel itself.

**B200 — reference shape `[M, 4096] × [1024, 4096]ᵀ` → `[M, 1024]`**

|     M | JIT graph (µs) | mm graph (µs) | Δ (mm − JIT) |
| ----: | -------------: | ------------: | -----------: |
|     1 |       **7.42** |      **7.42** |    **+0.00** |
|    32 |       **7.42** |      **7.42** |    **+0.00** |
|    64 |       **7.43** |      **7.43** |    **+0.00** |
|   128 |       **7.69** |      **7.69** |    **+0.00** |
|   256 |           7.69 |          7.68 |        −0.01 |
|  1024 |          10.40 |         10.57 |        +0.17 |
|  4096 |          28.75 |         28.90 |        +0.15 |
|  8192 |          59.16 |         58.73 |        −0.43 |
| 16384 |         112.30 |        112.32 |        +0.02 |

**H100 — same shape**

|     M | JIT graph (µs) | mm graph (µs) | Δ (mm − JIT) |
| ----: | -------------: | ------------: | -----------: |
|     1 |       **6.05** |      **5.94** |    **−0.11** |
|     2 |       **5.95** |      **5.95** |    **+0.00** |
|     8 |       **6.01** |      **5.99** |    **−0.02** |
|    32 |       **6.20** |      **6.25** |    **+0.05** |
|   128 |       **7.77** |      **7.77** |    **+0.00** |
|   256 |           8.35 |          8.38 |        +0.03 |
|  1024 |          19.72 |         16.88 |        −2.84 |
|  4096 |          62.36 |         62.31 |        −0.05 |
|  8192 |         123.25 |        123.25 |    **+0.00** |
| 16384 |         247.74 |        248.39 |        +0.65 |

**Reading these.** Inside CUDA Graph, the two routes are statistically indistinguishable on both architectures — `|Δ|` ≤ ~0.7 µs everywhere, with many rows reading exactly equal to the µs. The single H100 outlier at M=1024 has `mm` *faster* than the JIT, suggesting the variance is from cuBLAS heuristic selection per graph capture rather than any systematic kernel difference.

Launch-bound floors (M ≤ 128): B200 ~7.4 µs, H100 ~6.0 µs — the cuBLAS minimum-tile + graph-launch cost. Neither implementation can go below that.

### 3. Eager-mode footnote

In eager mode at very small M (≤ 128), `torch.mm` is ~1 µs (8–10 %) slower than the JIT — but that gap is **purely Python dispatcher overhead** (extra ~1 µs from torch's dispatcher / autograd-key check vs the JIT's leaner pybind11 stub). It vanishes under any CUDA Graph capture, including `torch.compile(mode="reduce-overhead")`. Decoding loops in sglang already capture graphs, so this is invisible in practice.

For compute-bound shapes (M ≥ 256) eager-mode times also match within ±5 % run-to-run noise on both GPUs.

### Test commands

Build the JIT kernel inline (verbatim source from `_jit_torch_cublas_bf16_fp32`) and run:

```bash
# inside lmsysorg/sglang:deepseek-v4-{blackwell,hopper}
python bench_bf16_fp32_gemm.py \
    --warmup 30 --iters 300 \
    --batch-sizes 1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192,16384

python bench_overhead.py \
    --batch-sizes 1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192,16384
```

Bench scripts available on request.

### Summary

| Aspect           | Result                                                                                                         |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Accuracy         | **Bit-exact** on every shape, both B200 and H100 (`torch.equal == True`)                                       |
| Perf, M ≥ 256    | Same TFLOPS within ±5 % noise (both GPUs)                                                                      |
| Perf, M ≤ 128    | **Identical under CUDA Graph** (\|Δ\| ≤ 0.2 µs over 16 000 timed calls/cell)                                   |
| Eager-mode small-M | ~1 µs Python-dispatcher overhead in `torch.mm`; closed by any graph capture                                  |
| Cold-start cost  | -1 × `nvcc` JIT compile (~60–74 s) and -1 `compile_aot` entry                                                  |

Net: drops 62 lines of inline-CUDA + JIT machinery, with no perf or accuracy regression.

title: [AMD] Replace fp8 mla with fp8 mha kernel for diffusion model aiter backend
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation
Dependency: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/2911 (merged)
The original FP8 prefill path in the AITer backend temporarily used the MLA prefill ASM kernel to get FP8 attention running on MI350 series for Wan 2.2. Switching to the proper FP8 FMHA ASM kernel fmha_fwd_hd128_fp8_gfx950 removes extra padding, the head-divisibility constraint, and the whole metadata-building scaffolding. That FMHA path natively supports MHA with q/k/v head_dim == 128 and applies to Wan 2.2 as well as other diffusion models’ self- and cross-attention shapes.

| Aspect | Before — MLA prefill ASM (`mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd` + `mla_reduce_v1`) | After — FMHA FP8 ASM (`aiter.flash_attn_fp8_pertensor_func`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Q/K head dim | `qk_head_dim = 192` hard-coded in the binary; Wan's 128 had to be **zero-padded 128 → 192** on every call (extra memory + bandwidth) | `q_head_dim = k_head_dim = 128` natively; **no padding** |
| Head-tiling constraint | Tiles 8 heads at a time (`m32x8`); `num_heads` **must be divisible by 8**, so Ulysses SP degree=4 on 40 heads (→ 10/rank) crashed with OOB reads | No head-divisibility constraint; **Ulysses SP=4 on 40-head models works** |
| `torch.compile` compatibility | `@torch.compiler.disable` required on the wrapper (Python-side metadata construction breaks Dynamo) | Decorator removed; **path is Dynamo-friendly** |

## Modifications

`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/attention/backends/aiter.py`:

- **Removed** the MLA prefill code path:
  - `_can_use_mla_prefill(...)`
  - `_build_mla_prefill_metadata(...)` (persistent-scheduling metadata builder for `mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd`)
  - `_mla_prefill_ps_attention(...)` (varlen reshape + Q/K zero-pad-to-192 + `mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd` + `mla_reduce_v1`)
- **Added** the FMHA FP8 prefill code path:
  - `_FMHA_FP8_HEAD_DIM = 128` constant.
  - `_can_use_fmha_fp8_prefill(q_head_dim, k_head_dim, v_head_dim, num_heads, num_kv_heads)` — gates on `_use_aiter_gfx95`, full MHA (`num_kv_heads == num_heads`), and `q == k == v == 128`.
- **Restriction Update**:
   - Drops the `num_heads % 8 == 0` constraint, unblocking Ulysses SP degree=4 for 40-head models.
   - No more `F.pad` of Q/K on the hot path.
   - The `@torch.compiler.disable` decorator on `AITerImpl.forward` (no longer needed since the new path doesn't go through Python-side metadata construction that breaks Dynamo).

## Accuracy Tests
Kernel unit test pass

## Speed Tests and Profiling
Image: rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.10.post1-rocm700-mi35x-20260426
Wan 2.2 T2V, 1MI355

### Per-kernel
| Path | Kernel | Time (us) | Subtotal (us) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Before** (MLA prefill + reduce) | `aiter::mla_pfl_qh192_vh128_m32x8_n128x1_causal0` | 87,409.1 | |
|                                   | `_Z19kn_mla_reduce_v1_...` (`mla_reduce_v1`)      | 4.4      | **87,413.5** |
| **After** (this PR, FMHA FP8)     | `_ZN5aiter24fmha_fwd_hd128_fp8_gfx950E`           | 78,006.2 | **78,006.2** |


### End-to-end
Stage-level wallclock for one full Wan 2.2 T2V run, FP8 attention path:
| Path | Encoding (s) | Denoising (s) | Decoding (s) | Total (s) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Before** (FP8 MLA prefill, with 128→192 pad + `mla_reduce_v1`) | 4.34 | 96.90 | 11.80 | **113.04** |
| **After**  (this PR, FP8 FMHA `hd128` pertensor)                 | 4.41 | 81.28 | 11.79 | **97.48**  |
| **Δ**                                                            | +0.07 | **−15.62** | −0.01 | **−15.56 (−13.8 %, ~1.16× faster)** |

title: support asymmetric pd-mtp via mock spec hidden
author: hnyls2002
body:
Always size the PD MetadataBuffers hidden_states buffer to model_config.spec_hidden_size on both prefill and decode (instead of conditional on local --speculative-algorithm). This unblocks asymmetric P/D configs where prefill runs no spec module but decode runs EAGLE/MTP: prefill ships a zero-initialized buffer that decode consumes as mock conditioning for the first draft step. Verified spec decoding keeps the output token correct -- only the first decode iteration's accept length is affected (~ < 1% throughput hit on long generations).

Cost: when neither side runs spec, the buffer is allocated but unused (~few MB). The alternative is a wire-protocol size mismatch on asymmetric configs.

Test: test_dsv4_pd_disagg_nixl.py uses asymmetric config (prefill TP-only, decode TP+DP+EAGLE), no new server arg required. Follow-up to #23918.

title: Nixl async transfer
author: ovidiusm
body:
Taken over from https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20680

## Motivation

This PR improves the performance of NixlKVManager by making KV transfer asynchronous and multi-threaded on the prefill node. Previously, `add_transfer_request` performed each chunk transfer synchronously and the caller (NixlKVSender) had to track and poll all transfer handles. With many decode instances and chunked transfers, this caused the prefill scheduler to block on transfer completion and limited throughput. This change aligns NIXL with the queue-based, multi-worker transfer design.

## Performance

We ran **Qwen3-32B PD disaggregation** with NIXL and observed a clear improvement in transfer latency via NIXL telemetry:

- **Mean transfer time**: **162,225 μs → 41,225 μs** (about **4× lower**).
- **Distribution**: Before, transfer times had high variance with many samples in the 250k–1.2M μs range and a long tail; after the change, the vast majority of samples sit in the **34k–42k μs** band with much lower variance and no large outliers.

Async multi-worker transfer removes the synchronous bottleneck on the prefill path: chunks are processed in parallel by worker threads, and decode instances are sharded across queues for better overlap, which explains the lower mean and significantly improved tail (P95/P99) latency.


## Modifications

1. **Async transfer with queue + worker pool (PREFILL mode)**
   - Introduced multiple `FastQueue` instances (count controlled by `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_QUEUE_SIZE`) and a `ThreadPoolExecutor` per queue (total worker count from `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_THREAD_POOL_SIZE`).
   - Added a `TransferKVChunk` dataclass and daemon `transfer_worker` threads that consume chunks from the queues and execute `send_kvcache` / `send_kvcache_slice`, `maybe_send_extra`, and `send_aux` in the worker.
   - Default thread pool size: `min(max(4, (0.5 * cpu_count) // 8), 12)` when the env var is not set; queue size defaults to env (e.g. 4).

2. **Non-blocking `add_transfer_request`**
   - `add_transfer_request` no longer performs transfer inline; it enqueues a `TransferKVChunk` to `transfer_queues[bootstrap_room % len(transfer_queues)]` and returns `None`.
   - Workers update `request_status` (e.g. `Transferring`, `Success`, `Failed`), so the sender no longer needs to hold or poll transfer handles.

3. **NixlKVSender simplifications**
   - Removed `xfer_handles`; `poll()` now relies on `kv_mgr.check_status(bootstrap_room)` only.
   - Added `clear()` to remove `bootstrap_room` from `request_status` when appropriate.
   - Last-chunk path no longer deletes `request_status` in the sender; the worker clears `transfer_infos` and sets status to `Success` when the last chunk is done.

4. **Scheduler handling of Bootstrapping**
   - In `prefill.py`, requests in `KVPoll.Bootstrapping` are now treated as undone (together with `WaitingForInput` and `Transferring`) so the scheduler does not consider them complete before transfer progress.

## Testing

* `python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000`: Accuracy: 0.945 with Qwen/Qwen3-8B
* `TestDisaggregationAccuracy ` passes with NIXL  (score 0.76, throughput 3949 token/s)

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (Regression: ran `test_disaggregation_basic.py`; 7 tests passed.)

title: [Fix] FP8 Qwen3-Next quant error by removing fallback fused shards
author: Jiminator
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
- Fixes a regression introduced by #23467 that broke Qwen3-Next FP8 on B200 4-GPU at server initialization with: 
```ValueError: Weight output_partition_size = 8 is not divisible by weight quantization block_n = 128.```
- Root cause. #23467 added `in_proj_ba` and `in_proj_qkvz` to `_FALLBACK_FUSED_SHARDS` in `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/utils.py`, treating them as virtual fused names. However, they are real, unified tensors in the Qwen3-Next FP8 checkpoint, listed explicitly in modules_to_not_convert. The fallback unfused them into non-existent shard names (`in_proj_b/_a`, `in_proj_qkv/_z`), which never appear in `modules_to_not_convert`, so `is_layer_skipped` returned `False` for layers that should have been skipped. `Fp8LinearMethod.validate_block_quant_shapes` then ran on those layers and failed the `block_n = 128` divisibility check.
- The original motivation of #23467, preventing `mlp.gate` from substring-matching `mlp.gate_up_proj`, is preserved by `_module_path_match`, which is unchanged. Models that genuinely fuse these projections (Qwen3.5 on gfx95/NPU) declare them in their own packed_modules_mapping, which is_layer_skipped already prefers over the global fallback.

## Modifications
-  `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/utils.py`: removed the spurious `in_proj_ba` and `in_proj_qkvz` entries from `_FALLBACK_FUSED_SHARDS`
- `test/registered/quant/test_is_layer_skipped.py`: new CPU regression test (≈5s, stage-a-test-cpu) covering:
  -` in_proj_ba` and `in_proj_qkvz` are correctly skipped when listed in modules_to_not_convert (the bug)
  - `mlp.gate` does not match a sibling `mlp.gate_up_proj` (the preserved motivation of #23467)
 
<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->
No model forward, kernel, or quantization-math changes. The fix only affects which layers are skipped during FP8 quantization config resolution at startup — restoring the pre-#23467 behavior for in_proj_ba/in_proj_qkvz. Verified that Qwen3-Next-80B FP8 now loads on B200 4-GPU without the divisibility error.

title: [attention] Fallback to Triton merge_state when FlashInfer hits CUDA thread limit
author: brucechanglongxu
body:
## Motivation

FlashInfer's `MergeState` CUDA kernel launches with `blockDim = (head_dim/vec_size, num_heads)`. When `num_heads` is large (e.g. with DP attention where `attention_tp_size=1`, putting all KV heads on a single rank), the total threads per block can exceed CUDA's limit of 1024 and the launch fails with `invalid configuration argument`.

## Modifications

- Add a `_safe_merge_state` wrapper around the single FlashInfer `merge_state` call site in `FlashInferAttnBackend` (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_backend.py`).
- The wrapper mirrors flashinfer's `vec_size` selection (matching `include/flashinfer/attention/cascade.cuh`) and falls back to the in-tree `merge_state_triton` when `num_heads * (head_dim / vec_size)` would exceed the per-block thread limit of 1024.
- The Triton kernel uses `(num_tokens, num_heads)` as its launch grid (one block per `(token, head)`), so its block size is unaffected by `num_heads`.
- Small `num_heads` continues to use the existing FlashInfer CUDA kernel — behavior unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

`merge_state_triton` is the existing in-tree implementation already used elsewhere in SGLang (e.g. `xpu_backend`, `musa` backends) and shares the same numerical formulation as FlashInfer's `merge_state` (max-subtract softmax stabilization). No model-output behavior change for the small-`num_heads` case (FlashInfer kernel still used).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No perf change in the common case — the wrapper is a single integer comparison around the existing FlashInfer call. The fallback path only triggers in configurations that previously crashed, so any latency there is strictly an improvement over a broken launch.

- [ ] Update documentation — N/A, internal fallback.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — see above.

title: (1/n - prefill optimize)feat(lora): enable csgmv backend with virtual experts for MoE LoRA
author: yushengsu-thu
body:
## Summary

- Remove the assertion that restricted `--lora-use-virtual-experts` to triton-only. The virtual experts path uses its own triton kernel (`merged_experts_fused_moe_lora_add`) independent of the dense-LoRA backend, so csgmv is fully compatible.
- Fix CUDA graph crash when using `--lora-backend csgmv --lora-use-virtual-experts` by adding per-request segment info (`req_seg_indptr`, `req_weight_indices`) to `LoRABatchInfo`. The csgmv backend's chunked-segment semantics differ from what MoE virtual experts expect (per-request), causing garbage token-to-adapter mappings and device-side asserts.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `server_args.py` | Remove triton-only assertion for `--lora-use-virtual-experts` |
| `lora/utils.py` | Add `req_seg_indptr` and `req_weight_indices` fields to `LoRABatchInfo` |
| `lora/backend/chunked_backend.py` | csgmv backend computes and stores per-request segment info (incl. CUDA graph pre-allocation) |
| `lora/layers.py` | MoE LoRA `_get_lora_info` uses per-request fields when available |

## Benchmark Results (Qwen3-30B-A3B, TP=4, GB300, in=1024, out=2048)

| BS | triton (e2e tps) | csgmv (e2e tps) | csgmv vs triton |
|----|-----------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| 1 | 201.0/s | 205.5/s | **102.2%** |
| 128 | 2753.3/s | 2800.3/s | **101.7%** |
| 512 | 2758.7/s | 2807.6/s | **101.8%** |

csgmv matches triton throughput (~1.7-2.2% faster) since MoE LoRA uses the same virtual experts triton kernel regardless of the dense-LoRA backend.

## Accuracy

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| KL(sglang, trainer) | 0.00392 |
| KL(orig_sampler, trainer) | 0.00424 |
| KL(sglang, orig_sampler) | 0.00497 |

Accuracy verified — sglang csgmv+virtual_experts output closely matches the training reference (lower KL than the original sampler).

## Test plan

- [x] Perf benchmark: triton vs csgmv with virtual experts (BS=1,128,512)
- [x] Accuracy test: KL divergence against training logprobs
- [x] CUDA graph capture succeeds with csgmv + virtual experts

title: [diffusion] fix: improve LTX2.3 reference accuracy controls
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

Improve LTX-2.3 one-stage TI2V reference alignment controls and update the CI consistency threshold for the regenerated faithful V2A-enabled GT.

## Changes

- Process LTX2 text connector positive and negative CFG branches independently to match official behavior more closely.
- Fix LTX2.3 audio cross-attention RoPE scale factors.
- Add explicit `skip_v2a_cross_attn_for_video_gt` sampling flag for reproducing legacy GT behavior only when needed.
- Preserve `--disable-autocast` when applying config dict overrides, with unit coverage.
- Update `ltx_2.3_one_stage_ti2v` consistency threshold for the regenerated faithful V2A-enabled GT in `sglang-ci-data`.

## Accuracy Notes

The regenerated GT is now in `sglang-ci-data/main` commit `03cba05fc35219f5e7407d6d1ac33ecee3819191` and keeps V2A cross-attention enabled by default.

Current code-only branch, without transformer fp8-cast and without legacy V2A skip, measured against the regenerated GT:

- min_clip `0.8053`
- min_ssim `0.7934`
- min_psnr `20.8080`
- max_mean_abs_diff `10.3797`

Thresholds are set with CI margin:

- clip `0.78`
- ssim `0.78`
- psnr `20.0`
- mean_abs_diff `11.0`

Alignment percentage by min SSIM: `79.34%`.

For comparison, the separate transformer fp8-cast branch (#24024) measured `min_ssim=0.8291` against the same regenerated GT, but that compatibility mode is intentionally not kept in this PR.

## Validation

- `git diff --check origin/main` passed.
- Local targeted pytest command was attempted: `python -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_server_args.py -q`.
- Local pytest did not reach test assertions because the current shell environment imported another repo path and failed during collection on missing `triton.compiler`.

title: [VLM] Optimize Gemma4 VLM with PCG and fuse RMSNorm + residual add + scalar
author: yuan-luo
body: ## Motivation Optimize Gemma4 26B-A4B prefill performance through two complementary approaches: 1. Fused Triton kernels for Gemma4 decoder layers — Reduces kernel launch overhead by fusing multiple operations into single kernels. 2. Enable Piecewise CUDA Graph (PCG) for VLM models — Fixes PCG support for multimodal models that use self.language_model instead of self.model to reference their text backbone. Main: PR: ## Modifications ### Fused Triton Kernels (sglang/srt/layers/gemma4_fused_ops.py) - gemma_rmsnorm_residual_scalar: Fuses RMSNorm + residual add + scalar multiply into a single Triton kernel (replaces 3 separate ops). - gemma_dual_rmsnorm_residual_scalar: Fuses the full MoE post-processing pipeline — rmsnorm(rmsnorm(dense_out, w1) + rmsnorm(moe_out, w2), w3) + residual) * scalar — into a single kernel (replaces 5+ separate ops per MoE layer). ### Gemma4 Model Integration (sglang/srt/models/gemma4_causal.py) - Updated Gemma4DecoderLayer.forward() to use the fused kernels in the MoE block, eliminating redundant kernel launches. ### PCG VLM Compatibility (sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py) - resolve_language_model(): Added fallback to model.language_model when model.model is not present, supporting VLM architectures like Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration. - PCG gate check: Extended the guard condition to also check for language_model attribute, preventing false disabling of PCG for VLMs. - Layer resolution: Added flexible layer discovery that handles both language_model.model.layers (standard) and language_model.layers (Gemma4 VLM where TextModel is the language_model directly). ### PCG Runner Fix (sglang/srt/model_executor/piecewise_cuda_graph_runner.py) - Updated patch_model target resolution to handle models where the TextModel (with .layers) is the language_model itself, not nested under .model. ## Accuracy Tests MMMU match official 54.9%. | Tasks |Filter|n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |--------|------|-----:|--------|---|-----:|---|------| |mmmu_val|none | 0|mmmu_acc|↑ |0.5489|± |N/A | ## Speed Tests and Profiling PCG eliminates CPU dispatch overhead by capturing per-layer CUDA graphs for prefill. The benefit is most significant at small-to-medium token counts where kernel launch latency dominates compute time. | Tokens | Baseline | Fused + PCG | Improvement | |--------|----------|-------------|-------------| | 93 | 35.6ms | 16.5ms | -53.7% | | 189 | 35.4ms | 17.1ms | -51.7% | | 1453 | 36.3ms | 25.1ms | -30.9% | | 2893 | 40.6ms | 30.6ms | -24.6% | | 5773 | ~49ms | 41.6ms | -15.1% | | 11533 | ~70ms | 66.4ms | -5.1% | ## Compatibility - Non-VLM models: No change — existing model.model path is tried first. - VLM models with self.model (e.g., Qwen2.5-VL): No change — hasattr(model, "model") succeeds as before. - VLM models with self.language_model (e.g., Gemma4): Now correctly supported. - Verified correctness on both Gemma4 (text + image) and Qwen2.5-VL (text + image) with PCG enabled. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. title: [SPEC][5/N] feat: batchsize-aware support for adaptive speculative_num_steps
author: maodoudou168
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

PR #21599 introduced adaptive speculative decoding that dynamically adjusts `speculative_num_steps` based on EMA of accept lengths. 

This PR extends the adaptive controller to maintain **per-batch-size independent state**, where each BS range has its own EMA tracker, candidate steps, and hysteresis thresholds.

## Modifications

### Architecture

The `AdaptiveController` maintains a `bs_params` dict keyed by BS lower bounds, matched via `bisect_right - 1`, here's the default value:

```
AdaptiveController
├── bs_params: Dict[int, AdaptiveSpeculativeParams]
│   ├── BS [1, 64):   steps=[1,3,7], hysteresis=(up=0.0, dn=-0.25)
│   ├── BS [64, 128):  steps=[1,2,5], hysteresis=(up=0.0, dn=0.0)
│   └── BS [128, ∞):   steps=[1,2,6], hysteresis=(up=-0.1, dn=0.25)
└── _states: Dict[int, SpecRuntimeState]  (shared, indexed by step count)
```

Each BS range has its own:
- **EMA tracker** — observations from small bs don't pollute the large bs signal
- **current_step seperated for different bs** — small bs can run at step 7 while large bs runs at step 5
- **different bs can take different sets of candidate_params** — small bs candidates default to take [1,3,7] vs large bs candidates default to [1,2,6]
- **Hysteresis parameters** — can be tuned per BS range

`SpecRuntimeState` objects are shared across BS ranges (keyed by step count, not by BS), since CUDA graphs and attention backends depend only on step count.

### Per-BS Config File Format

Example:

```json
{
  "1":   {"steps": [1, 3, 7], "up_hysteresis": 0.0, "down_hysteresis": -0.25},
  "8":   {"steps": [1, 3, 7], "up_hysteresis": 0.0, "down_hysteresis": -0.25},
  "32":   {"steps": [1, 3, 7], "up_hysteresis": 0.0, "down_hysteresis": -0.25},
  "64":  {"steps": [1, 2, 5], "up_hysteresis": 0.0,  "down_hysteresis": 0.0},
  "128": {"steps": [1, 2, 6], "up_hysteresis": -0.1, "down_hysteresis": 0.25}
}
```

Config keys are **lower bounds** matched via `bisect_right - 1`. In the above example, BS=16 uses the `"8"` slot; BS=100 uses the `"64"` slot; BS=200 uses the `"128"` slot. This flat format is backward-compatible with the original adaptive config from PR #21599.

### Backward Compatibility

To get behavior identical to PR #21599 (disable bs-aware), use a config with a **single BS=1 entry**:

```json
{
  "1": {"steps": [1, 3, 7], "up_hysteresis": 0.0, "down_hysteresis": -0.25}
}
```

With a single BS=1 entry, all batch sizes map to the same slot, producing identical EMA tracking, step selection, and activation timing as the global EMA-only baseline.

Without `--speculative-adaptive-config`, the built-in defaults (per-BS steps and hysteresis) are used automatically.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Setup
- **Model**: GLM-4.7-FP8 on 8×GPU (TP=8), EAGLE speculative decoding with topk=1
- **Workload**: `transition` (alternating low/high acceptance phases: low_1 → high_1 → low_2 → high_2)
- **Benchmark tool**: `bench_adaptive_speculative.py`
- **Metrics**: 3-run average throughput (tok/s), per-phase throughput
- **CUDA graph BS**: `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128]`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.65`
- **Configs compared**: No-bs-aware (`ema_only_config.json`, single BS=1 slot with `[1,3,7]`) vs BS-aware (default config, with lower num_steps candidate when bs>=64)

### Comprehensive Results: SpecV1 and SpecV2

Both SpecV1 (synchronous scheduler) and SpecV2 (overlap scheduler) support bs-aware adaptive spec. The table below shows 3-run average output throughput across all batch sizes.

#### Output Throughput (tok/s, 3-run average)

| BS | Num Req | specv1 no-bs-aware | specv1 bs-aware | **Δ v1** | specv2 no-bs-aware | specv2 bs-aware | **Δ v2** |
|---|---|---:|---:|:---:|---:|---:|:---:|
| 1 | 16 | 117.6 | 122.4 | equal | 122.6 | 122.5 | equal |
| 8 | 64 | 549.4 | 565.4 | equal | 586.2 | 583.7 | equal |
| 64 | 128 | 2,336.4 | **2,462.9** | **+126.5(+5.4%)** | 2,557.8 | **2,630.9** | **+73.1(+2.9%)** |
| 128 | 256 | 3,361.8 | **3,489.2** | **+127.4(+3.8%)** | 3,508.9 | **3,659.9** | **+151(+4.3%)** |

BS-aware consistently outperforms EMA-only at large batch sizes (BS≥64) in both schedulers, where per-BS tuned step ladders avoid wasted draft compute.


## Usage

```bash
# Per-BS adaptive with built-in defaults
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/model \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-adaptive

# Per-BS adaptive with custom config file
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/model \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-adaptive \
  --speculative-adaptive-config /path/to/per_bs_config.json

# Fallback to EMA-only (identical to PR #21599)
# Use a config with a single BS=1 entry:
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/model \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-adaptive \
  --speculative-adaptive-config ema_only_config.json
```

Where `ema_only_config.json` contains:
```json
{
  "1": {"steps": [1, 3, 7], "up_hysteresis": 0.0, "down_hysteresis": -0.25}
}
```

- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [codex] Optimize Helios fused norm modulation
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

This PR switches Helios' FP32 LayerNorm + scale/shift modulation sites to the existing fused `LayerNormScaleShift` path, and keeps the residual norm on the custom `LayerNorm` wrapper.

The affected sites are:
- `HeliosTransformerBlock.norm1`
- `HeliosTransformerBlock.norm3`
- `HeliosOutputNorm.norm`
- `self_attn_residual_norm`

No benchmark videos are checked into the branch; they are attached below as GitHub user-attachments and embedded directly in this description.

## Benchmark

Environment:
- Host/container: `radixark03`, `sglang-diffusion-bbuf`

title: Add speculative decoding naming convention rule
author: hnyls2002
body:
Add `.claude/rules/speculative-naming.md` codifying naming conventions for speculative decoding identifiers.

## External-facing key audit

Audit of all externally consumed spec-decoding keys against the new rules. Items marked as violations / inconsistencies are candidates for follow-up deprecation.

### Prometheus gauges (`sglang:` prefix)

- `sglang:spec_accept_length` — τ (with bonus) — paper-aligned, OK
- `sglang:spec_accept_rate` — α (without bonus) — paper-aligned, OK

### `meta_info[*]` (per-request HTTP response)

- `spec_accept_rate` — α — OK
- `spec_accept_length` — τ — OK
- `spec_verify_ct` — verify forward count — OK (Rule 4 counter form)
- `spec_accept_histogram` — per-step accept-count histogram — OK (verb form)
- `spec_accepted_drafts` — correct drafts (no bonus) — **violates Rule 1 (-ed form) / Rule 3 (should be `correct_*`)**
- `spec_proposed_drafts` — total proposed drafts — acceptable
- `completion_tokens` — generic API field, not spec-specific

### IPC dataclass (`SpeculativeDecodingMetricsMixin`, `io_struct.py:85`)

- `spec_verify_ct` — OK
- `spec_accepted_drafts` — **violates Rule 1 (-ed form)**
- `spec_acceptance_histogram` — **inconsistent with `meta_info["spec_accept_histogram"]` (noun vs verb form)**

### `SpeculativeMetrics` dataclass → `internal_state` HTTP (`io_struct.py:1914`)

- `accept_length` — missing `spec_` prefix used by all other external surfaces
- `accept_rate` — same as above

title: fix(sgl-kernel): sm90 compile flashmla failed
author: imp2002
body: ## Motivation ### close https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24126 Fixes a FlashMLA build issue on Hopper GPUs such as H20 when buildingwith CUDA 12.8. In `sgl-kernel/cmake/flashmla.cmake`, the `sm100` Blackwell source files were always appended to `FlashMLA_SOURCES`, even when the build only targeted Hopper (`sm90a`). At the same time,`sm100` gencode was only added when `CUDA_VERSION > 12.8`. That mismatch meant a CUDA 12.8 Hopper build could still compile Blackwell-only FlashMLA source files unnecessarily, which can lead to compilation failures or toolchain incompatibilities on H20 / SM90 environments. ## Modifications - Add a local `FLASHMLA_ENABLE_SM100` switch in `sgl-kernel/cmake/flashmla.cmake`. - Enable that switch only when `CUDA_VERSION > 12.8`, the same condition used to add `-gencode=arch=compute_100a,code=sm_100a`. - Move all `sm100` FlashMLA source files behind `if(FLASHMLA_ENABLE_SM100)` so Hopper-only builds do not compile Blackwell sources. ## Accuracy Tests N/A. This change only affects build-time source and architecture selection in the FlashMLA CMake configuration. No kernel math or model runtime logic was changed. After fix, compile succeed. Install the `.whl` file and run DeepSeek V3.2. It works properly. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. This PR does not change runtime execution paths or kernel implementations. It only prevents unnecessary `sm100` FlashMLA compilation on Hopper builds. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). title: ci: run setup_ld_library_path before install_sglang_kernel
author: alisonshao
body:
## Summary

`nvidia-cusparselt-cu13` was bumped on PyPI from 0.9.0 → 0.9.1 on 2026-04-29 18:36 UTC. On the affected runners, uv's upgrade install partially failed: it wrote the new `0.9.1` dist-info (registering the package as installed) but did not extract the bundled `nvidia/cusparselt/lib/libcusparseLt.so.0`. Because the dist-info looks intact, every subsequent `uv pip install` skips it as "already satisfied," so the broken state is sticky and `import torch` fails with `libcusparseLt.so.0: cannot open shared object file`.

Fix: at the end of `install_sglang`, if the wheel metadata is present but the `.so` is missing on disk, force-reinstall the wheel.

Failure example: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/25158915002/job/73748785757

## Test plan
- [ ] Trigger PR Test on a 1-GPU runner (5090 or h100); verify install dependency completes without `libcusparseLt.so.0` ImportError
- [ ] Confirm the WARNING fires on a runner where the file is missing, and is silent on a runner where it's present

body:
Aiter backend can be used for DeepSeek 3.2 and models with similar model architecture like the GLM5 to run the models on AMD Instinct. There is some differences in the optimizations and code path used for the MI30X and MI35X GPUs. The accuracy is fine when running on MI300X GPUs. However, there is currently an issue with the model output and accuracy when running on MI35X series GPUs.

**Steps to reproduce the issue**

Use some recent container, for example:
`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.10.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260503`

Server launch command:
```
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 \
  --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --attention-backend aiter \
  --nsa-prefill-backend aiter \
  --nsa-decode-backend aiter \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --disable-radix-cache
```

Run Gsm8k benchmark command with lm-eval:

title: [LoRA][MOE] Fix EP correctness in MoE LoRA slicing and virtual-experts kernels
author: jybsuper
body:
## Motivation

Two correctness gaps in the LoRA MoE path under expert parallelism, plus small cleanups uncovered while tracing them:

1. **`tp_size > ep_size > 1` crashes during adapter load.** `LoRAMemoryPool.load_lora_weight_to_buffer` passes the outer `tp_rank` to `slice_moe_lora_{a,b}_weights`, but per-expert MoE weights are sharded along `moe_tp_size = tp/ep/dp`. On `tp=4 ep=2`, outer ranks 2,3 slice past `intermediate_size` and `load_lora_weight_tensor` asserts with `weight shape torch.Size([r, 0])`. Reproducible on `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct-FP8` + a per-expert LoRA.

2. **Virtual-experts kernels mishandle the post-EP `-1` sentinel `topk_ids`.** Non-local experts arrive as `-1` after EP dispatch. `_fused_virtual_topk_ids_kernel` mapped `-1` to `-1 + safe_lora * num_experts`, landing on a real virtual-expert slot belonging to another adapter. The `num_experts >= 1024` torch.compile fallback `_align_block_size_torch` then OOB-indexed `padded_offsets[sorted_expert_ids]` for both negative (Python wrap) and out-of-range ids.

**Related**: #23632 (still open) lands the same EP correctness fixes (items 1-2) plus Qwen3.5-specific layer wrappers. This PR is independent of #23632 and limits scope to the EP fixes + regression tests; the Qwen3.5 wrappers are unnecessary because #23594 (merged) already covers Qwen3.5 via a generalized n-slice path.

## Changes

- **`mem_pool.py`**:
  - Pass `self.moe_tp_rank` (not `self.tp_rank`) to `slice_moe_lora_{a,b}_weights` so MoE per-expert slicing matches `moe_tp_size` sharding.
  - Track `active_target_modules` per layer and skip the buffer-copy loop for keys with no wrapped module on that layer — avoids redundant GPU zero-fills on hybrid-arch models (Qwen3.5 linear-attn vs full-attn) where `temp_A/B_buffer` is seeded with the union of all target modules.
- **`triton_ops/virtual_experts.py`**:
  - `_fused_virtual_topk_ids_kernel`: `tl.where(base < 0, base, shifted)` preserves negative sentinels.
  - `_align_block_size_torch`: route invalid ids into a dedicated sentinel bucket (`bucket_count = num_experts + 1`); zero its block count so its blocks stay marked `-1` and the consumer kernel's existing `if off_expert == -1: return` skips them.
- **`lora_manager.py`**: add `if layer_id is None: continue` guard in the `FusedMoE` wrapping loop to avoid indexing `self.lora_modules` with `None`.

## Tests

New regression tests; each was verified to fail when its corresponding fix is reverted.

- **`test/registered/unit/lora/test_mem_pool_ep_unit.py`** (CPU-only, +1 case): `TestLoadBufferPassesMoeTpRankToSlice` exercises `load_lora_weight_to_buffer` at `tp=4 ep=2` (outer rank 3, `moe_tp_rank=1`) with a mocked `FusedMoEWithLoRA` whose slicer captures the rank then raises to short-circuit before the buffer-copy phase. Catches item 1.
- **`test/registered/lora/test_virtual_experts_kernels.py`** (new file, GPU, 8 cases):
  - `TestFusedVirtualTopkIdsPreservesSentinels`: negative-sentinel preservation, positive-id remap sanity, `lora_id=-1` no-shift behavior. Catches the kernel half of item 2.
  - `TestAlignBlockSizeTorchSentinelBucket`: all-valid baseline, `-1` ids excluded from real-expert assignment, OOR ids excluded, mixed invalid at the production-trigger size (`num_experts=1500`), empty input. Catches the torch.compile-fallback half of item 2.

## Compatibility / Perf

- `ep == tp`: `moe_tp_size == 1` → MoE slicing already skipped. No-op.
- `ep == 1`: `moe_tp_rank == tp_rank` by construction. No-op.
- Virtual-experts kernel: one extra in-register `tl.where` per element. The `_align_block_size_torch` path is gated on `virtual_num_experts >= 1024`; adds a handful of `@torch.compile`-fused elementwise ops + one extra padded block. <1% overhead either way.
- Adapter load: `active_target_modules` filter is a strict win (skips zero-fills) — no behavior change.

## Test plan

- [x] `tp=4 ep=2` adapter load on Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-FP8 with the per-expert LoRA — crashed before, runs to completion after.
- [x] `tp=4 ep=1` and `tp=4 ep=4` still load and serve (existing `test_lora_qwen3_vl_30b_a3b_instruct_logprob_diff`, `test_lora_qwen3_5_*_logprob_diff`).
- [x] New unit tests above; verified each fails under its reverted fix and passes after restoration. 38/38 pass on a single GPU in ~12s.

title: (2/n - prefill optimize)perf(lora): remove GPU-CPU sync barrier (.item()) in MoE LoRA path and remove duplicate code
author: yushengsu-thu
body:
## Summary

based on https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24007

- Remove `.item()` call in `_add_lora_gate_up_delta` that caused unnecessary GPU-CPU synchronization (`cudaStreamSynchronize`) on every MoE layer forward pass during eager execution
- Clean up duplicate code blocks (duplicate function definitions, dataclass fields, variable assignments)

### Root Cause

The original code used `.any().item()` on GPU tensors to check whether any LoRA adapter was active before running the LoRA kernel. This `.item()` call forced a **GPU→CPU synchronization barrier** on every MoE layer, creating pipeline bubbles where the GPU sat idle waiting for the CPU.

From profiling traces:
- **4,728 extra `bool .item()` calls** in the LoRA path, totaling ~2 seconds of synchronization overhead
- Average `.item()` latency: **291 μs** (vs 7 μs in no-LoRA baseline) due to pipeline flush

### Fix

Replace the GPU-side `has_active_lora` check (which required `.item()`) with CPU-side checks (`lora_info is None or lora_info.max_lora_rank == 0`) that don't trigger GPU-CPU sync. The CUDA graph path already handled this correctly via `get_capture_lora_variant()`.

## Benchmark Results

**Config:** csgmv backend, TP=4, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, input=1024, output=2048, 4x GB300

### Prefill Latency (TTFT - Time To First Token)

| BS | Before | After (this PR) | Change |
|----|--------|-----------------|--------|
| 1 | 151.38 ms | 141.97 ms | **-6.22%** |
| 128 | 313.15 ms | 293.24 ms | **-6.36%** |
| 512 | 303.70 ms | 278.66 ms | **-8.24%** |

### Decode Latency (TPOT - Time Per Output Token)

| BS | Before | After (this PR) | Change |
|----|--------|-----------------|--------|
| 1 | 7.19 ms | 7.17 ms | -0.29% |
| 128 | 8.67 ms | 8.67 ms | -0.03% |
| 512 | 8.66 ms | 8.66 ms | -0.06% |

### End-to-End Latency

| BS | Before | After (this PR) | Change |
|----|--------|-----------------|--------|
| 1 | 7741.37 ms | 7710.56 ms | -0.40% |
| 128 | 9305.59 ms | 9283.18 ms | -0.24% |
| 512 | 9288.87 ms | 9259.43 ms | -0.32% |

### Throughput

| BS | Before | After (this PR) | Speedup |
|----|--------|-----------------|---------|
| 1 | 205.1 tok/s | 205.9 tok/s | 1.004x |
| 128 | 2799.9 tok/s | 2804.3 tok/s | 1.002x |
| 512 | 2804.3 tok/s | 2810.0 tok/s | 1.002x |

### Analysis

- **Prefill is the primary beneficiary**: 6-8% TTFT reduction from eliminating GPU-CPU sync barriers
- **Decode is unaffected**: decode uses CUDA graph replay, which doesn't hit the `.item()` code path
- **E2E improvement is modest** (~0.3%) because decode dominates total latency (output_len=2048 >> input_len=1024)

## Test Plan

- [x] Benchmark with csgmv backend on Qwen3-30B-A3B (TP=4, GB300)
- [ ] Verify correctness with LoRA inference outputs

title: [core/loader] Add presharded load format
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

Initial weight loading + quantization processing for large MoE models (e.g., DeepSeek-V2 family with `--quantization fp8`, DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-V4-Pro with mxfp4) is expensive and re-runs every time the engine starts with the same parallelism + quantization config. This PR introduces a `presharded` load format that caches the post-`process_weights_after_loading` state on disk so subsequent runs skip the source-shard iteration, the model-specific `post_load_weights` conversion, and the quant-method `process_weights_after_loading` reshape on real data.

## Modifications

New `--load-format presharded` (`LoadFormat.PRESHARDED`). Behavior:

- **First run (dump)**: each rank loads weights normally, runs `post_load_weights`, runs `process_weights_after_loading` to materialize the inference-ready layout, then ranks coordinate to dump a per-rank deduplicated safetensors set under `<model_path>/presharded/<config subfolder>/`.
- **Subsequent runs (reload)** with the same config: each rank initializes the model, runs `process_weights_after_loading` once on uninitialized parameters purely to materialize post-process shapes, then multi-thread reads only the files it needs and `copy_`s dumped values in. Source ckpt is not iterated; `post_load_weights` is not re-run on real data.

Subfolder name is derived from a structural signature over TP/DP/EP/PP, quantization, dtype, EPLB, expert location, and related knobs (e.g. `TP-8-sig-…`).

### Algorithm (rank-coordinated dump)

1. Each rank hashes every tensor in its post-process state with **xxh3-128** over `(shape, dtype, raw little-endian bytes)` and writes a small JSON manifest. CUDA tensors use pinned streaming D2H so multi-GB weights never need a single contiguous host allocation. Hashing is multi-threaded (`hash_num_threads`, default 8); xxhash releases the GIL.
2. Rank 0 reads all manifests, deduplicates by content digest, groups by rank-list signature, and bin-packs into files of at most 20 GiB (balanced across writers). Rank 0 also computes a **per-rank aggregate checksum**: sum (mod 2^64) of per-tensor 64-bit folds of `xxh3(name + ":" + content_digest)`. The plan is published as `checksum.json`.
3. Each rank writes the files it owns (`model-…-common.safetensors` / `model-…-rank-….safetensors`).
4. After a final barrier, rank 0 writes a **`READY`** sentinel last so concurrent readers never observe a half-written dump.

### Reload path (efficiency)

- **Default `verify_on_load=false`**: pure multi-thread safetensors → device `copy_` (no content re-hash).
- **`verify_on_load=true`**: re-hash loaded tensors with xxh3 and compare the rank aggregate against `rank_checksums`.
- **Multi-thread I/O**: same knobs as the HF path — `enable_multithread_load` (default true) and `num_threads` (default 8). Workers only do disk→CPU reads; GPU apply stays on the main thread. Sliding window bounds host RAM to ~`num_threads` in-flight files.
- **No mid-load `empty_cache`**: params are filled with in-place `copy_`, so the caching allocator does not grow file-by-file. One sync + `empty_cache` at end of load matches `DefaultModelLoader`. Per-file `empty_cache` previously dominated large MoE reloads (hundreds of shards).

### Capture timing — why post-process

State is captured **after** both `model.load_weights` (so model-specific `post_load_weights` has run) **and** layer-level `quant_method.process_weights_after_loading` (so e.g. mxfp4 expert weights are already packed).

Reload reproduces the layout by running `process_weights_after_loading` on the initialized model *before* copying dumped values. The transform depends only on shape, not values. Non-`nn.Parameter` Tensor attributes installed by `post_load_weights` (`w_kc`, `w_vc`, `compressor.freqs_cis`, …) are persisted as extras and reinstalled via `setattr`. GemmaRMSNorm non-persistent `gemma_weight` and GDN Parameter aliases are refreshed/rebound after copy.

Post-process capture also avoids memory doubling on large quant models (e.g. DeepSeek-V4-Pro mxfp4: pre-process ~283 GB vs post-process ~223 GB per rank).

### Optional extra-config knobs (`--model-loader-extra-config`)

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `presharded_path` | under model path | Override dump/load directory |
| `max_file_bytes` | 20 GiB | Per-file cap |
| `hash_num_threads` | 8 | Parallel hash workers (dump / optional verify) |
| `verify_on_load` | **false** | Re-hash and check rank checksums |
| `enable_multithread_load` | true | Multi-thread file I/O on reload (and first-time HF load) |
| `num_threads` | 8 | Worker count for multi-thread load |

## Accuracy Tests

**DeepSeek-V4-Pro mxfp4, TP=4 EP=4 DP-attn, 4×GB300**: full param-hash diff between baseline (`--load-format auto`) and presharded reload with `verify_on_load=true`, hashing every `state_dict` entry **and** every non-`nn.Parameter` Tensor attr installed by `post_load_weights`. Result: **9288/9288 params bit-identical across all 4 ranks**.

Also verified on DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct across TP/quant configs and on Qwen3.5 (including GDN / GemmaRMSNorm rebind) with matching generation text after reload.

Plan corruption (flipping one byte of `rank_checksums["0"]`) is correctly detected when `verify_on_load=true`.

## Speed Tests

Method (unless noted): **weight-load only** — no warmup generate, `disable_cuda_graph=True`, `max_total_tokens=10000`. Metric: scheduler `Load weight end. elapsed=` (max across ranks). Hardware: 8×H200. Reload uses default `verify_on_load=false`. Dump is one-time (source load + hash + write).

Rank spread on reload: 15.0–16.0 s (tight). Earlier serial + per-file `empty_cache` path was ~160 s on the same dump — multi-thread I/O + dropping mid-load `empty_cache` recover the win.

title: (3/n - prefill optimize)[LoRA][MoE] Optimize virtual experts: remove CPU-GPU sync & multi-block CUDA JIT histogram
author: yushengsu-thu
body:
## Summary

based on https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24246

I add the jit but also keep the original in case our hardware can fall back to torch if fail on jit.

  ### Hidden side-benefit: ~68% drop in `AllReduce` kernel time on prefill-heavy LoRA workloads

  While cross-checking optimize-2 against pre-opt-2 traces (Qwen3-30B-A3B + LoRA, TP=4, GB300,
  input=65536 / output=32, 10 prompts, `--max-concurrency 4`), I noticed a much larger drop in
  `ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_bf16` than the PR's micro-benchmark numbers would suggest:

  | metric | pre-opt-2 (merged 4-TP) | post-opt-2 (TP-0 × 4 estimate) | Δ |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | `AllReduce` kernel total | 6,778 ms | ~2,192 ms | **−4,586 ms (−68%)** |

  #### Mechanism

  NCCL collectives are CUDA kernels that **spin-wait inside the kernel** until all ranks
  arrive. Pre-opt-2 had a recurring per-layer CPU stall on each TP rank coming from the PyTorch
   align fallback:

  | pre-opt-2 CPU stall source | time (ms) | removed by |
  |---|---:|---|
  | `Torch-Compiled Region: 4/0` (`_align_block_size_torch` + `torch.compile`) | 3,851 | **this
   PR** |
  | `aten::sort` (`torch.argsort` in the fallback) | 790 | **this PR** |
  | `aten::item` / `_local_scalar_dense` (`.any().item()` ×4,728 in `_add_lora_gate_up_delta`)
  | ~2,000 | #24246 |

  Whichever rank is currently stalled forces the other three ranks' AllReduce kernels to keep
  spinning until it catches up. After this PR (combined with #24246) no rank stalls, all four
  ranks reach AllReduce together, and the kernel duration collapses to roughly just the actual
  data transfer.

  #### Attribution to this PR

  The two stall sources that this PR removes (`Torch-Compiled Region` + `aten::sort`) sum to
  **~4,640 ms**, which closely matches the observed −4,586 ms AllReduce drop. #24246
  contributes another ~2 sec on a separate path (likely partially overlapping in the same
  stream).

  Long stalls hurt NCCL more than frequent short ones: the `.any().item()` calls in #24246 are
  4,728 × ~291 µs (often amortizable), whereas one `Torch-Compiled Region` call is hundreds of
  µs continuous, which the other ranks cannot work around.

  #### Caveats

  - No incremental traces were taken — only `pre-opt-2` vs `post-opt-2`. The per-PR attribution
   above is by stall-source matching, not direct per-PR measurement.
  - The post side uses **TP-0 × 4** as a rough proxy for merged 4-TP; a full merged 4-TP
  post-opt-2 trace would tighten the number.
  - The `4,640 + 2,000 = 6,640 ms` total estimated stall removal exceeds the observed `−4,586
  ms` AllReduce drop, which is consistent with overlap (the two PRs' stalls partially share the
   same GPU-stream window).

  **TL;DR:** the headline 8× speedup of `_align_block_size` is real, but on prefill-heavy
  multi-TP workloads the bigger end-to-end win is **NCCL un-stalling**, which only shows up
  when you diff `AllReduce` kernel time across pre-vs-post traces.

## Accuracy Tests

Verified on 3 models with LoRA adapters (TP=4, NVIDIA GB300):

| Model | KL(sglang, trainer) | KL(sglang, orig_sampler) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 | 0.00392 | 0.00497 | ✅ PASS |
| Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct | 0.00072 | 0.00162 | ✅ PASS |
| gpt-oss-20b | 0.00094 | 0.00110 | ✅ PASS |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

| Config | JIT (new) | PyTorch (old) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8E×128L, 64 tokens | 0.048ms | 0.384ms | **8.0×** |
| 8E×256L, 256 tokens | 0.038ms | 0.320ms | **8.5×** |
| 64E×64L, 256 tokens | 0.038ms | 0.322ms | **8.6×** |
| 8E×256L, 1 token (decode) | 0.037ms | 0.327ms | **8.8×** |

title: [KDA] Optimize prefill kernels with diagonal and recompute fuse
author: yuan-luo
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
Improve KDA prefill kernel performance for hybrid linear-attention models such as `Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct` on Hopper-class GPUs. Profiling shows KDA accounts for ~13 % of prefill GPU time on a 4-GPU TP setup; the two dominant KDA kernels (`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` and `chunk_kda_fwd_kernel_inter_solve_fused`) had restrictive autotune configs and were leaving SM utilization on the table: `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64`'s grid `(V/BV, B·H_per_rank)` produces only 16 CTAs at TP=8 H=4, far below Hopper's per-GPU SM count, so most SMs sit idle.

## Modifications

KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) is a chunked linear-attention variant. For each chunk t of size BT=64, the per-layer forward decomposes into four stages:

1. **`cumsum`** — chunk-local cumulative gate `gk`
2. **`chunk_kda_fwd_intra`** — three sub-kernels that compute, per chunk, the gated qk attention `Aqk`, the lower-triangular gated kk matrix `Akk`, its inverse via in-chunk forward substitution, and finally the delta-rule helpers `w =
β·k·Akk⁻¹`, `u = β·v·Akk⁻¹`, `kg = k·exp(gn − gk)`. Each step is parallelizable over `(chunk, head, batch)`.
3. **`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h`** — the recurrence: `h_{t+1} = h_t ⊙ exp(gk_last_t) + k_t.T @ (u_t − w_t @ h_t.T)`. **Serial across the NT chunk axis**; only parallelizable over `(head, batch, V-slice)`.
4. **`chunk_gla_fwd_o_gk`** — output `o = q·g·h.T + Aqk·v_new`. Parallel over `(chunk, head, V-slice)`.

This PR's improvement comes from the following perspectives:

### 1. h-recurrence kernel: SM under-utilization at small per-rank H
- **Expand the BV sweep to include 16 and num_warps to include 8** so triton can pick a wider grid (`V/BV = 8`) when small per-rank H starves SMs. The smaller per-CTA tile also reduces register pressure on the `b_h₁..b_h₄` accumulators (each `[BV, 64]` fp32), which raises occupancy per SM.
- **Add `NT_BUCKET` to the autotune key** (3 buckets: NT ≤ 32, ≤ 128, > 128). The optimal config genuinely differs by chunk count: short prefills favor larger BV (more work amortized over launch), long prefills favor smaller BV (more parallelism to fill SMs). Without bucketing, whichever shape autotunes first locks the choice for all subsequent shapes.
- **Add `restore_value=["h", "v_new", "initial_state"]`** to the autotune decorator. Triton's autotune benchmarks each config by repeatedly invoking the kernel; without this, the post-autotune output tensor reflects whichever config ran last in the benchmark sequence rather than the chosen config, which can produce transient precision drift on the first call. Save+restore makes the cold-cache output identical to the steady-state output.

### 2. chunk_intra: kernel-launch and HBM round-trip overhead

The intra stage was three separate kernels (`token_parallel` for diagonal Akk blocks, `inter_solve_fused` for off-diagonal blocks + lower-triangular solve, `recompute_w_u_fwd` for w/u/kg). Each boundary materializes an intermediate tensor in HBM:
- `Akkd` (diagonal blocks, fp32, ~T·H·16·4 bytes) between kernels 1 and 2
- `Akk_inv` (full triangular inverse, ~T·H·64·4 bytes) between kernels 2 and 3

The PR introduces two `tl.constexpr` modes inside `chunk_kda_fwd_kernel_inter_solve_fused`:
- **`FUSE_DIAGONAL`** — folds the diagonal Akk computation into the same kernel. Diagonal blocks live in registers and are consumed immediately by the forward-substitution; the Akkd round-trip is eliminated.
- **`FUSE_RECOMPUTE`** — additionally folds the w/u/kg recompute. The Akk_inv sub-blocks stay in registers after solve and are immediately used to construct `w = β·k·Akk_inv` etc.; the Akk_inv round-trip is eliminated.

### 3. Off-diagonal MMA in bf16

Off-diagonal `tl.dot` inputs were upcast to fp32 before the matmul; cast the per-block products `b_q·b_gqn`, `b_k·b_gqn`, and the transposed key tile to bf16 before MMA so the Hopper tensor cores run at bf16 rate (2× throughput vs the fp32 path). Accumulator stays fp32. Validated against `test_chunk_gated_delta_rule.py` (ATOL=2e-2).

### 4. Grid-aware fuse gate (kda.py dispatcher)

Compute `_small_grid = (B · NT_pr · H_per_rank ≤ 256)` and pass `fuse_diagonal=_small_grid, fuse_recompute=_small_grid` to `chunk_kda_fwd_intra`. Fusion saves launch overhead at small grid where the kernel is launch-bound; falls back to the
unfused path at large grid where the extra register footprint would spill.

For varlen (packed) tensors `NT_pr` uses `chunk_indices.shape[0]` to correctly count per-sequence chunks (chunks don't cross sequence boundaries, so `cdiv(total_tokens, chunk_size)` undercounts for typical short-sequence packs).

---

All the modified files are in `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/fla/`:

**`chunk_delta_h.py`** — thread `chunk_indices` through the wrapper for varlen, keep autotune at a single config.

**`chunk_intra.py`** — fuse diagonal-block compute and `recompute_w_u_fwd` into the inter+solve kernel (`FUSE_DIAGONAL`, `FUSE_RECOMPUTE`); cast off-diagonal MMA inputs to bf16; keep the autotune sweep narrow (`BK ∈ {32, 64} × num_warps ∈ {1, 2, 4}`) since wider sweeps caused triton 3.6 to pick suboptimal configs at large grids.

**`kda.py`** — grid-aware dispatcher (`_small_grid`) with varlen-correct `NT_pr`; `chunk_gla_fwd_kernel_o` autotune restricted to `BK=64, BV=64` (matches pre-PR hardcoded values; wider sweeps on triton 3.6+ either crash or pick suboptimal configs).

**`cumsum.py`** — minor: add `num_stages` to the existing autotune sweep so longer prefills can benefit from deeper pipelining.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct GSM8K accuracy: **90.0 %** (no drops vs main).

| Metric          | Value         |
| --------------- | ------------: |
| Accuracy        | **90.0 %**    |
| Invalid outputs | 0.0 %         |
| Output throughput | 356 tok/s   |

```
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct \
  --tp 4 --trust-remote-code \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.7 --attention-backend triton \
  --port 30000
python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-shots 8 --num-questions 200 --port 30000
```

Registered correctness tests:

| Test | Result |
| ---- | ------ |
| `test/registered/attention/test_chunk_gated_delta_rule.py` | **28/28 PASS** (ATOL=2e-2) |
| `test/registered/models/test_kimi_linear_models.py::TestKimiLinear::test_gsm8k` | **PASS** |

PyTorch reference verified independently against multiple equivalent formulations (direct serial, affine-form `h = h @ M + b`, block-parallel scan with various `SEG_LEN`); all match to fp32 epsilon.

| Test | Configs | Output max-diff vs PyTorch reference | Status |
| ---- | ------- | ----------------------------------: | ------ |
| `test_fuse_diagonal.py`  | B=1/T=4096, varlen B=8/T=4096, B=1/T=8192 | 6 × 10⁻⁵ – 3 × 10⁻³ | **PASS** |
| `test_fuse_recompute.py` | same 3                                    | 3 × 10⁻⁵ – 3 × 10⁻⁵ | **PASS** |
| `test_fused_ho.py`       | same 3                                    | 6 × 10⁻⁵ – 3 × 10⁻³ | **PASS** |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Prefill B=1 T=8192, attention-backend=triton.

title: [codex] Optimize LTX2.3 HQ denoising split passes
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- Optimize LTX2.3 HQ guided denoising by passing disable-attention options directly to the model when each forward contains only one expanded-batch item.
- Avoid an internal CUDA bool sync in the res2s SDE terminal path.
- Keep TI2V/non-HQ on `perturbation_configs`, which stores one disable-attention config per expanded-batch item; changing this path previously affected accuracy.

## Motivation

`pass_specs` defines the denoising results we need from the model: `cond`, `neg`, optional `perturbed`, and optional `modality`. The code builds an expanded batch of size `batch_size_local * len(pass_specs)`. Each expanded-batch item is one local batch element evaluated under one of those pass specs.

A perturbation config tells the transformer which attention paths to disable for one expanded-batch item: selected video/audio self-attention blocks and A2V/V2A cross-attention. The perturbed and modality results use those disabled attention paths for STG/modality guidance.

In the HQ path, `_split_ltx2_model_kwargs(..., [1] * expanded_batch_size)` makes one model call per expanded-batch item. Because that call has only one perturbation config, we can pass the disable-attention options directly as normal model arguments and avoid the per-item config list.

In TI2V/non-HQ, one model call may contain multiple expanded-batch items with different perturbation configs. That path must keep `perturbation_configs`, one config per item; otherwise the model would apply one setting to the whole call and change the output.

## Performance

Benchmark: H100 80GB, snapshot mode, `ltx_2_3_hq_pipeline`, parent `28238d5b1` vs optimized validation commit `aeea82a08f`.

| Metric | Parent | Optimized | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `LTX2AVDenoisingStage` | 10054.60 ms | 9737.69 ms | +3.15% |
| Avg denoise step | 601.32 ms | 582.47 ms | +3.13% |
| Median denoise step | 636.53 ms | 617.63 ms | +2.97% |
| E2E baseline dump | 15468.94 ms | 15192.81 ms | +1.78% |

## Validation

- `ltx_2_3_hq_pipeline` consistency passed: min clip `0.8043`, min SSIM `0.4844`, min PSNR `12.1561`, max mean abs diff `46.4682`.
- Full pytest still fails only the unrelated `LTX2AVDecodingStage` perf threshold (`actual 1474 ms`, threshold `1053 ms`); this PR does not touch decode.
- 2-GPU two-stage TI2V comparison: optimized and parent both fail consistency with identical metrics (`clip 0.8993`, `SSIM 0.5444`, `PSNR 16.8427`, `mean_abs_diff 21.9915`), so this is not a new regression from the patch.
