title: Profiling Enhancements [1/3]: cuda graph profile traces
author: mohbasit
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

# Profiling Enhancements [1/3]: CUDA-graph capture profile traces

## Summary

Adds opt-in profiling of the **CUDA-graph capture phase**. When enabled, each
captured decode batch size is recorded with a `torch.profiler` pass and exported
as its own Chrome trace, giving per-shape visibility (kernel identities, input
shapes, FLOPs, memory) into the graphs that are replayed at serving time.

## Motivation

During startup the runner captures one CUDA graph per batch size. At serving
time the graph matching the current batch size is replayed, so the shapes and
kernels seen during capture are exactly what runs in production. Capturing a
profiler trace per batch size lets us inspect those per-shape kernels offline
(e.g. `aiter fused_moe`, attention) without having to profile a live run.

## What this PR does

- **Per-bs capture traces.** During graph capture (`--enable-profile-cuda-graph`),
  a scheduled profiler (`wait=2, warmup=0, active=1, repeat=0`) skips the two
  warmup passes and records the single capture pass for each batch size. The
  `on_trace_ready` callback writes one Chrome trace per batch size.
- **Output location / naming.**
  `${SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR}/capture_traces/bs_<bs>_rank<tp_rank>.json.gz`
  (batch sizes follow the reversed capture order; files are namespaced by TP
  rank so ranks never collide).
- **Profiler knobs:** `record_shapes=True`, `with_stack=True`, `with_flops=True`,
  `profile_memory=True`.
- **Opt-in flag.** The per-bs trace export is gated by the environment variable
  `SGLANG_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH_CAPTURE_TRACE`. When it is unset, the profiler still
  runs (for the existing key-averages summary tables and the memory snapshot),
  but no per-bs trace files are written and `on_trace_ready` stays `None`.

## Configuration

| Setting | Type | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--enable-profile-cuda-graph` | server arg | Builds the capture profiler; emits the summary tables + memory snapshot. |
| `SGLANG_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH_CAPTURE_TRACE=1` | env var | Opt-in: persist one Chrome trace per batch size to `capture_traces/`. No-op unless `--enable-profile-cuda-graph` is also set. |
| `SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR` | env var | Base directory for trace output (default `traces`). |

### Example

```bash
export SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR=/path/to/profile
export SGLANG_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH_CAPTURE_TRACE=1
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-profile-cuda-graph \
  ...
```

Produces, e.g.:

```
/path/to/profile/capture_traces/
  bs_1_rank0.json.gz   ... bs_128_rank0.json.gz
  bs_1_rank1.json.gz   ... bs_128_rank1.json.gz
  ...                       (one set per TP rank)
```

## Scope / notes

- Only the decode CUDA-graph runner is affected. 

## Test plan

- **Unit tests** (`test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`,
  CPU-only, `base-a-test-cpu`):
  - creates the `capture_traces` dir under `SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR`;
  - primes reversed per-bs bookkeeping and zero index;
  - builds the profiler with the trace-export knobs and `wait=2/warmup=0/active=1/repeat=0` schedule;
  - `on_trace_ready` names each trace `bs_<bs>_rank<rank>.json.gz` and advances the index;
  - with the flag unset: `on_trace_ready` is `None`, no dir is created, no bookkeeping is primed.

## Performance Impact - None


### Setup

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Model | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3` (native fp8) |
| Hardware | MI355X (gfx950) |
| Parallelism | TP=4 |
| Attention backend | `aiter` |
| KV cache | `fp8_e4m3` |
| CUDA graph max bs | 32 (captured bs: 1,2,4,8,12,16,24,32) |
| Recipe | `InferenceX/benchmarks/single_node/fixed_seq_len/dsr1_fp8_mi355x.sh` |
| Workload | random ISL=1024, OSL=1024, `--random-range-ratio 0.8` |
| Load | 320 prompts @ max-concurrency 32, 64 warmups, `--request-rate inf` |

- **Baseline (`main`)** = commit `94743f934` — the exact `main` commit
  `feat/capture_graph` is built on, so config1→config2 isolates *only* the PR's
  code. The PR footprint vs this commit is the profiling files + tests + doc.
- **My code** = `feat/capture_graph` @ `e7b77c55d`.
- Steady-state serving is measured *after* the server is ready; the profiling
  flags only affect the one-time startup graph-capture phase.

---

### Configurations

| # | Dir | Branch | Server flag | Env |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `c1_main` | main | — | — |
| 2 | `c2` | feat/capture_graph | — | — |
| 3 | `c3_profile` | feat/capture_graph | `--enable-profile-cuda-graph` | — |
| 4 | `c4_profile_trace` | feat/capture_graph | `--enable-profile-cuda-graph` | `SGLANG_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH_CAPTURE_TRACE=1` |
| 5 | `c5_main_profile` | main | `--enable-profile-cuda-graph` | — |
| 6 | `c6_main_profile_trace` | main | `--enable-profile-cuda-graph` | `SGLANG_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH_CAPTURE_TRACE=1` |

---

### Results — steady-state serving (the runtime impact)

| # | Branch | Flags | Out tok/s | Req/s | Mean TTFT (ms) | Med TTFT (ms) | P99 TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Mean ITL (ms) | Mean E2E (ms) | OK |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 | main | none (baseline) | 1193.75 | 1.29 | 300.67 | 131.75 | 1635.43 | 25.94 | 25.95 | 24248 | 320/320 |
| 2 | feat/capture_graph | none | 1191.44 | 1.29 | 266.26 | 131.45 | 1371.98 | 26.04 | 26.05 | 24301 | 320/320 |
| 3 | feat/capture_graph | `--enable-profile-cuda-graph` | 1187.38 | 1.29 | 237.83 | 133.19 | 1075.19 | 26.15 | 26.17 | 24381 | 320/320 |
| 4 | feat/capture_graph | flag + `CAPTURE_TRACE=1` | 1188.21 | 1.29 | 238.24 | 132.74 | 1078.08 | 26.14 | 26.15 | 24364 | 320/320 |
| 5 | main | `--enable-profile-cuda-graph` | 1188.15 | 1.29 | 237.52 | 132.18 | — | 26.15 | 26.16 | — | 320/320 |
| 6 | main | flag + `CAPTURE_TRACE=1` | 1185.85 | 1.29 | 237.98 | 131.79 | — | 26.18 | 26.19 | — | 320/320 |

- Output-throughput spread across all six runs: **1185.85–1193.75 tok/s (0.66%)**.
- TPOT spread: **25.94–26.18 ms (0.9%)**. Request throughput: flat 1.29 req/s.


**Conclusion:**  The new code is a true no-op at serving time with flags off (config 2 ≈ config 1), and enabling the flags does not change serving throughput/latency on either branch.

---

### Results — one-time startup (CUDA-graph capture) 


| # | Branch | Flags | Decode capture elapsed | Trace output | 
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- | 
| 1 / 2 | both | none | ~8 s | none |
| 5 | main | flag | ~37 s | summary tables + `cuda_graph_runner_memory_usage.pickle` | 
| 3 | feat/capture_graph | flag | ~37 s | summary tables + memory pickle | 
| 6 | main | flag + trace | ~49 s | **1 combined trace per rank** (`graph_capture_profile/cuda_graph_capture-DecodeCudaGraphRunner-TP-{0-3}.json.gz`) | 
| 4 | feat/capture_graph | flag + trace | ~47 s | **1 trace per batch size per rank** (`capture_traces/bs_{bs}_rank{r}.json.gz`) | 



---
As evident the code takes the same amount of time in the CUDA graph capture as current main code

# [XPU] Enable NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 on Intel XPU

## Summary

Enable `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16` (hybrid Mamba + attention
MoE, squared-ReLU activation) on Intel XPU with the `intel_xpu` attention
backend at `tp=4` on 4× Intel Arc Pro B60. Before this PR the model crashes at
load on XPU: the `causal_conv1d` import gate only binds on CUDA/NPU, and the MoE
path rejects the `relu2` activation Nemotron-H uses.

No CUDA/NPU behavior changes — both edits are additive XPU-only branches.

**Key changes:**

- Bind `causal_conv1d_*` to the pure-Triton implementation on XPU
- Admit `relu2` MoE activation on XPU

---

| Filter | XPU tp=4 B60 | B200 BF16 (cookbook §5.2.1) | Δ |

title: [Fix] Reset positions tensor in CUDA graph runner when batch size differs from captured size
author: weizhoublue
body:
…fers from captured size

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

fix https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24361

## Modifications

### Trigger condition                                                                                                                                                       
  NGRAM speculative decoding + flashinfer attention + CUDA graph replay on Blackwell sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000). Occurs intermittently after 2–5 hours of sustained inference,  when the captured bs differs from the actual raw_bs, hitting the padding-reset path in populate_from_forward_batch.                                                                                                                                                       
  Scheduler process SIGABRTs with cudaErrorIllegalMemory access inside flashinfer.prefill.plan, triggered from cuda_graph_runner.replay_prepare on the target worker's  verify path.                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                        

### Expected behavior                                                                                                                                                       
  When bs != raw_bs, all input tensors in the padding region (beyond the real batch) should be reset to safe values so the attention backend never reads stale data from a
   prior replay.                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                        
###  Root cause                                                                                                                                                              
  In cuda_graph_runner.py:populate_from_forward_batch, the bs != raw_bs branch resets seq_lens, out_cache_loc, mamba_track_indices, and mamba_track_mask — but omits    
  resetting positions. Padding tokens' positions retain garbage from the previous replay, causing flashinfer to compute an invalid qo_indptr and access illegal memory. PR   #10892 fixed the identical bug in the EAGLE draft runners but missed the main runner (used by NGRAM verify).

title: [diffusion] Fuse LTX2 split rotary embedding
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary
- add a Triton kernel for the LTX2 split rotary embedding layout used by the DiT path
- route the CUDA BF16 3D contiguous LTX2 split-RoPE case through the fused kernel
- keep the existing PyTorch path for other dtypes, layouts, and shapes

## Background
Before this PR there was no LTX2-specific fused kernel for this split-RoPE layout. The existing path used PyTorch reshape/broadcast/elementwise ops:

```python
split_x = x.reshape(*x.shape[:-1], 2, r)
first_x = split_x[..., :1, :]
second_x = split_x[..., 1:, :]

cos_u = cos.unsqueeze(-2)
sin_u = sin.unsqueeze(-2)

out = split_x * cos_u
first_out = out[..., :1, :]
second_out = out[..., 1:, :]
first_out.addcmul_(-sin_u, second_x)
second_out.addcmul_(sin_u, first_x)
```

This PR only replaces the common LTX2 CUDA BF16 hot path where `x` is a contiguous 3D tensor and `cos/sin` are 4D tensors. Other cases continue to use the PyTorch implementation above.

## Accuracy
The kernel preserves the original PyTorch operation order for BF16: the `x * cos` term is rounded to BF16 before adding the sine product, matching the existing `addcmul_` behavior.

Remote kernel checks on the LTX2 target shapes showed bit-exact results:
- `(4, 1152, 32, 128)`: `max_abs=0.0`
- `(4, 25, 32, 64)`: `max_abs=0.0`

Precision alignment: 100% for the checked kernel shapes.

## Performance
E2E experiment on one H100 80GB, `Lightricks/LTX-2.3`, `LTX2TwoStageHQPipeline`, snapshot device mode, `1024x1024`, 24 frames, after warmup. Command shape:

```bash
SGLANG_GEN_BASELINE=1 SGLANG_SKIP_CONSISTENCY=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/python \
python -m pytest -s \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_1_gpu.py \
  -k ltx_2_3_hq_pipeline --tb=short
```

| Metric | Base `6279aee716` | This PR `5a7d6c6785` | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| E2E pixel generation | 28.50s | 28.19s | -1.1% |
| Stage 1 denoise total | 9.5370s | 9.4211s | -1.2% |
| Stage 1 denoise avg step | 585.7ms | 577.7ms | -1.4% |
| Stage 2 refinement total | 1.6825s | 1.6564s | -1.6% |
| Stage 2 refinement avg step | 496.8ms | 485.1ms | -2.4% |
| Peak memory | 74384 MB | 74384 MB | no change |

This is a small but measurable request-level win; the main value is removing repeated PyTorch reshape/broadcast/elementwise work from the LTX2 split-RoPE hot path without changing numerics.

title: [Gemma 4] Adding MTP support
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

Add Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) speculative decoding for Gemma 4. Each Gemma 4 target ships with a small "assistant" checkpoint trained for MTP. This PR introduces a new speculative algorithm — **`FROZEN_KV_MTP`** — that runs the assistant against the target's KV cache (the assistant has no KV of its own and a recurrent hidden state across draft steps, so it does not fit cleanly under EAGLE/EAGLE3 or NEXTN).

`NEXTN` and `EAGLE` are auto-promoted to `FROZEN_KV_MTP` when `--speculative-draft-model-path` resolves to a `Gemma4AssistantForCausalLM`. `EAGLE3` is rejected for this draft architecture.

**Supported Targets:**

| Target | Architecture | Parameters |
|-------|--------------|------------|
| [google/gemma-4-E2B-it](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-E2B-it) | Dense | ~2B |
| [google/gemma-4-E4B-it](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-E4B-it) | Dense | ~4B |
| [google/gemma-4-31B-it](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-31B-it) | Dense | 31B |
| [google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it) | MoE | 26B total / 4B active |

Both `Gemma4ForCausalLM` (text) and `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` (multimodal) targets are supported.

## Installation

```bash
# Install transformers with Gemma 4 support
pip install 'git+https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.git@2c7d385621c80fee70c1472f3a622fcba2c93fb9'
```

## Usage

### Launch Server

```bash
# E4B + matched assistant, topk=1
sglang serve --model-path google/gemma-4-E4B-it \
  --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \
  --speculative-draft-model-path google/gemma-4-E4B-it-mtp \
  --speculative-num-steps 5 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \

# Tree verify (topk=3)
  --speculative-eagle-topk 3 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 12

# Tree verify (topk=5)
  --speculative-eagle-topk 5 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 16
```

When `FROZEN_KV_MTP` is active, the overlap scheduler and mixed chunked prefill are force-disabled, and `--max-running-requests` defaults to 48 if unset.

## Accuracy Tests

MTP matches the target-only baseline across GPQA Diamond (CoT / generative) and GSM8K (CoT, 0-shot):

### Topk = 1

| Model | Config | GPQA-D CoT | GPQA-D gen | GSM8K CoT |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| E2B     | baseline | 0.3384 | 0.3838 | 0.7369 |
| E2B     | MTP      | 0.3586 | 0.3889 | 0.7369 |
| E4B     | baseline | 0.5505 | 0.3939 | 0.7582 |
| E4B     | MTP      | 0.5303 | 0.3990 | 0.7597 |
| 31B     | baseline | 0.7172 | 0.6111 | 0.8802 |
| 31B     | MTP      | 0.7121 | 0.6162 | 0.8817 |
| 26B-A4B | baseline | 0.7172 | 0.5455 | 0.8772 |
| 26B-A4B | MTP      | 0.7222 | 0.5758 | 0.8696 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Will follow up with `FROZEN_KV_MTP` speed benchmark and profiling later

## Modifications

*   New assistant model: `gemma4_mtp.py` (`Gemma4AssistantForCausalLM`) — target-embed + recurrent hidden via pre/post projection, owns its own `lm_head`, optional centroid-ordered logits head.
*   New speculative algorithm `FROZEN_KV_MTP` in `speculative/spec_info.py` (with `FROZEN_KV_MTP_DRAFT` / `FROZEN_KV_MTP_VERIFY` spec input types).
*   New worker + utilities: `frozen_kv_mtp_worker.py`, `frozen_kv_mtp_info.py`, `frozen_kv_mtp_utils.py`, `frozen_kv_mtp_cuda_graph_runner.py` (supports `topk=1` and tree verify for `topk>1`, with full CUDA graph capture).
*   Frozen-KV binding collapses HF Gemma 4's typed-last-layer + `kv_shared_layer_index` two-hop into a direct assistant-logical → target-physical layer map. Assistant KV writes are suppressed.
*   `server_args.py`: alias resolution promotes `NEXTN`/`EAGLE` → `FROZEN_KV_MTP` for Gemma 4 assistant drafts and rejects `EAGLE3`. Force-disables overlap scheduler and mixed chunked prefill.
*   `hf_transformers/config.py`: recognize `model_type == "gemma4_assistant"` for SWA attribute remap.
*   `gemma4_causal.py` / `gemma4_mm.py`: expose `get_embed_and_head()` so the assistant can rebind to the target's input embedding at load time.
*   Manual GSM8K validation harness in `test/manual/models/test_gemma4_mtp.py` (target-only baseline → `topk=1` MTP → `topk>1` MTP).

title: propagate pytest exit code from test __main__ entries
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Problem

`run_files` in `python/sglang/test/ci/ci_utils.py` decides whether a
test file passed by reading the wrapping python script's
`process.returncode`. Files using

    if __name__ == "__main__":
        pytest.main([__file__])

discard pytest's exit code, so the script returns 0 even when assertions
fail. The CI runner then logs the file as PASSED while pytest's stdout
reports the failure — silently masking real regressions.

(Discovered when `test_norm_tanh_mul_add_norm_scale.py` printed
`1 failed, 47 passed` but the CI suite stayed green.)

## Fix

Add a stage-a CPU guard `test/registered/unit/test_no_bare_pytest_main.py`
that AST-scans `python/` and `test/` for any `if __name__ == "__main__":`
block containing a bare `pytest.main(...)` expression statement. Any
future test file that forgets the `sys.exit(...)` wrapper fails this
check in stage-a.

## Removed tests (please re-add with `sys.exit(pytest.main(...))`)

The following tests used bare `pytest.main(...)` and several were
already silently broken (their failures were being swallowed). They are
dropped here so this PR stays focused on the guard. Original authors,
please re-add with the proper wrapper — the new guard will enforce it:

- `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/diffusion/test_norm_tanh_mul_add_norm_scale.py` — @qimcis (#18762). Heads up: bf16 `atol=5e-2` is on the edge; consider tightening seed or widening tolerance on re-add.
- `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_cast.py` — @Johnsonms (#19103)
- `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_flash_attention_3.py` — @FlamingoPg (#4902)
- `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_fused_qknorm_rope.py` — @Johnsonms (#19059)
- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_tracing.py` — @jh-nv (#21254)
- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/manual/test_patch_embed.py` — @AichenF (#21014)
- `test/registered/lora/test_lora_moe_runner.py` — @klshuster (#21858)
- `test/registered/lora/test_marlin_lora_correctness.py` — @klshuster (#21858). Heads up: `MockServerArgs` needs to also patch `fused_moe.get_global_server_args` (same fix as `d2b3247a` applied to `test_lora_moe_runner.py`).
- `test/registered/lora/test_sgemm_sorted_by_adapter.py` — @klshuster (#22386)

## Out of scope

The runner uses `python3 file.py -f` because `-f` is intentional for the
696 `unittest.main()`-based test files (`unittest --failfast`, added in
#21330). Switching the runner to `python -m pytest` globally would touch
all of those — left alone.

title: Port MXFP4 Marlin MoE support to JIT kernel path
author: yhyang201
body:
## Summary
- Port kernel-level and Python-level MXFP4 (E8M0) Marlin MoE changes from #23686 (AOT sgl-kernel) to the JIT kernel path on `dsv4-rebase`
- Enables DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 quantized inference via `--moe-runner-backend marlin` on Hopper GPUs

## Changes

### CUDA kernel (`marlin_template.h`)
- Add `is_8bit_scale` generalization (replaces hardcoded `kFE2M1f` checks)
- Optimize `read_moe_block_data` with `cp_async4_pred` + warp-level `__reduce_add_sync`
- Fix scale stride/fetch logic for 8-bit scale types (E4M3, E8M0)
- Enable `dequant_fp8_scales` with compile-time guards
- Unify scale/zp pipe fetch with `div_ceil` pattern

### Python
- **`fused_marlin_moe.py`**: MXFP4 detection (`float8_e8m0fnu` scales), `swiglu_limit_func`, `clamp_limit` parameter, conditional `moe_sum_reduce` vs `torch.sum`
- **`marlin.py` (runner)**: FP16→BF16 upcast for MXFP4, `clamp_limit` forwarding
- **`marlin_utils_fp4.py`** (new): Weight repack + scale permutation for MXFP4 Marlin
- **`mxfp4_marlin_moe.py`** (new): `Mxfp4MarlinMoEMethod` class (weight loading, runner creation, inference)
- **`fp8.py`**: Marlin MXFP4 routing in `get_quant_method()` + early return in FP4 weight processing

## Correctness Verification

### AIME25 (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MXFP4 Marlin, H200 × 8)

Server config: `--tp 8 --moe-runner-backend marlin --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.85`

Eval config: `sgl-eval run aime25 --n-repeats 16 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 1.0 --max-tokens 400000 --num-threads 8`

| Metric | Score | Threshold |
|--------|-------|-----------|
| **pass@1** | **96.25%** (462/480) | >= 95% |
| **cons@16** | **100%** (30/30) | — |

All 30 questions answered correctly by majority vote. Weakest: Q13, Q14 (13/16 = 81%), Q19 (12/16 = 75%) — all comfortably pass.

## Test plan
- [x] Test with DeepSeek-V4-Pro MXFP4 checkpoint using `--moe-runner-backend marlin` + EAGLE speculative decoding
- [x] AIME25 pass@1 = 96.25% (threshold: >= 95%)
- [ ] Verify no regression on existing GPTQ/AWQ Marlin models
- [ ] Compare Marlin MXFP4 outputs with FlashInfer MXFP4 path

title: LPLB: linear-programming load balancer for MoE expert parallelism
author: feliang-git
body:
## Summary

Adds LPLB (Linear Programming Load Balancer), a new MoE expert-dispatch algorithm that solves a per-layer LP to balance token routing across redundant expert replicas. Opt-in via `--ep-dispatch-algorithm=lp`; default behavior unchanged.

- New `lp` choice for `--ep-dispatch-algorithm` (complements `static`, `dynamic`, `fake`).
- 4 JIT-compiled CUDA kernels under `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/lplb/`: a single-block IPM (`ipm.cuh`) using cuBLASDx for GEMMs and a hand-written block Cholesky for POSV (no `-rdc=true` device linking required), plus three more (`lp_prep`, `lp_post`, `dispatch_probability`) that fuse 8/5/7 torch ops into single launches.
- Math-DX is the only new dependency. Resolved via `MATHDX_HOME` env var, the `nvidia-mathdx` PyPI package, or the bundled `python/sglang/jit_kernel/lplb/resources/download-mathdx.sh`.
- Strict failure semantics: the server raises at startup if the fused backend isn't available (no CUDA, SM < 9.0, missing Math-DX); no silent fallback to torch IPM or to dynamic dispatch.

## Performance

Measured on 2× H20 nodes, DeepSeek-R1, EP=16 with DP-attention, DeepEP backend, `--max-concurrency 2048`, 4096-prompt timed runs × 3 reps each, counterbalanced order:

| Dataset  | dynamic tput | lp tput | Δ% | TTFT p50 Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **GSM8K**   | 19,715 | **20,779** | **+5.40%** | -5.99% |
| MMLU     | 22,949 | 22,825 | -0.54% | -2.58% |
| ShareGPT | 2,114  | 2,104  | -0.48% | **-9.18%** |

GSM8K is the routing-skewed workload LPLB targets. MMLU and ShareGPT are nulls on throughput (LPLB doesn't regress on uniform-routing or prefill-bound workloads). ShareGPT's TTFT p50 is -9.2% — the median-user TTFT improvement, which is the load-balance signal on long-context chat workloads. n = 3 reps; all p > 0.05, but effects are directionally consistent across all metrics on GSM8K (5/5 favor LP).

## Reproducing the benchmark

### 0. One-time: install Math-DX

```bash
# Either via PyPI:
pip install nvidia-mathdx
# or via the bundled script (idempotent — safe to re-run):
bash python/sglang/jit_kernel/lplb/resources/download-mathdx.sh
```

### 1. Launch the server (run on both nodes; `--node-rank` differs)

```bash
# Required to keep the JIT path off the legacy default CUDA stream
# under DP-attention all-reduce.
export NVSHMEM_IB_GID_INDEX=3
export NVSHMEM_IBGDA_NIC_HANDLER=cpu
export NVSHMEM_BOOTSTRAP_UID_SOCK_IFNAME=bond0

python3 -u -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path /path/to/DeepSeek-R1 \
    --tokenizer-path /path/to/DeepSeek-R1 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \
    --tp-size 16 --dp-size 16 --ep-size 16 \
    --enable-dp-attention \
    --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode normal \
    --ep-num-redundant-experts 16 \
    --ep-dispatch-algorithm lp \
    --init-expert-location /path/to/expert_stats.pt \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
    --max-running-requests 1024 \
    --max-prefill-tokens 65536 \
    --chunked-prefill-size 65536 \
    --schedule-conservativeness 0.3 \
    --disable-radix-cache \
    --nnodes 2 --node-rank 0 \
    --dist-init-addr <head-node-ip>:29500
```

`expert_stats.pt` is a per-dataset routing-statistics file produced by a 1000-prompt run with `--ep-dispatch-algorithm=dynamic --expert-distribution-recorder-mode=stat` and dumped via `/dump_expert_distribution_record`. The file must exist on every node (the cluster /raid is non-shared in our setup).

### 2. Run the benchmark

```bash
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \
    --backend sglang-oai \
    --base-url http://localhost:30000 \
    --dataset-name custom \
    --dataset-path /path/to/dataset.jsonl \
    --num-prompts 4096 \
    --max-concurrency 2048 \
    --sharegpt-output-len 4 \
    --output-file lp.json
```

Re-run with `--ep-dispatch-algorithm=dynamic` for the baseline. We counterbalanced 3 reps × 2 algorithms with kill-and-relaunch between every rep to control for JIT-cache and NIC-heat drift.

## Scope

**DeepSeek-v2 only.** Other MoE forward paths (Qwen3, GLM4, SDAR-MoE, …) return `empty_topk_output` directly without participating in the EP all-reduce; with LP active they would deadlock under DP-attention. Out of scope for this PR; future work to enable.

LP additionally requires:
- `--enable-dp-attention`
- `--moe-a2a-backend=deepep`
- Hopper-class GPU (SM ≥ 9.0)
- Math-DX cuBLASDx headers reachable

`check_lplb_server_args` validates the first two at startup with clear errors. The model-arch check fires at `LPLBSolver.__init__`.

## Notes for reviewers

- Default behavior (no LP flags) is byte-identical to pre-PR upstream — LP code paths are inert imports.
- This PR also includes a small worker-node startup fix in `entrypoints/http_server.py` and `entrypoints/openai/serving_{base,chat}.py` (guard against `tokenizer_manager is None` for `node_rank >= 1` in multi-node serving). Happy to split into a separate PR if preferred — it's unrelated to LPLB but came up during multi-node bring-up.
- `download-mathdx.sh` is idempotent (skips if `mathdx/include` and `mathdx/lib` are present).
- No NCCL or NVSHMEM changes; LP runs over existing all-reduce primitives.

## Test plan

- [x] Multi-rank smoke test on 2× H20 with DeepSeek-R1: server boots, `/server_info` reports `ep_dispatch_algorithm=lp`, single + 8-parallel completions return valid text.
- [x] End-to-end 3-dataset benchmark sweep (3 datasets × 6 reps each, 18 timed runs): no errors, numbers match the table above.
- [x] Codex review + rescue passes against the diff (P0 clean; P1 findings addressed in the last two commits).
- [ ] CI: `pytest test/registered/eplb/test_lplb_distributed.py` under `torchrun --nproc-per-node 2` (to be triggered in CI).

title: [NPU] [Bugfix] Wan quantization fix
author: OrangeRedeng
body: ## Description Fix Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers-w8a8/w8a8/mxfp8 quant scheme recognition on NPU by threading `reverse_param_names_mapping` through the ModelSlim config stack. ## Motivation Fix of https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24518. After PR #23625 reshaped quantized‑diffusion prefixes, the Wan2.2‑W8A8 model stopped loading (`No modelslim compatible scheme`). The bug is that `_get_scheme_from_parts` uses the **model’s internal layer name** (e.g. `blocks.0.self_attn.to_q`) to look up the quant description, but the quant config file uses **architecture‑canonical names** (e.g. `blocks.0.attn1.to_q`). The WanVideo arch‑config already carries a `reverse_param_names_mapping` that translates internal names back to canonical names, but the ModelSlim initialisation path silently discarded this mapping. ## Modifications - **`modelslim.py`** – accept `reverse_param_names_mapping` in `__init__` and `from_config`, build a mapper via `get_param_names_mapping`, and use it in `_get_scheme_from_parts` before querying `quant_model_description.json`. - **`transformer_load_utils.py`** – read `reverse_param_names_mapping` from the arch config and pass it into `get_quant_config`. - **`quantization_utils.py`** – accept and forward `reverse_param_names_mapping`. - **`fsdp_load.py`** – add missing quant parameter suffixes (`input_offset`, `quant_bias`, `deq_scale`) to the sharding allow‑list; mark sharded tensors with `requires_grad=False` to avoid meta‑tensor copy errors. - **`npu/utils.py`** – update a performance warning to mention `--dit-cpu-offload false`. ## Accuracy Tests Command: ```SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_FN=2 SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_BN=1 SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_WARMUP=4 SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_RDT=0.4 SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_MC=4 SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TAYLORSEER=true SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TS_ORDER=2 SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true sglang generate --model-path ./weights/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers-w8a8/ --prompt "Two anthropomorphic cats in comfy boxing gear and bright gloves fight intensely on a spotlighted stage." --height 720 --width 1280 --tp-size 2 --sp-degree 2 --num-gpus 4 --num-frames 81 --num-inference-steps 40 --warmup true``` https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/678e4823-0c70-47f5-82f5-e1f0e0f52a51 ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. (align with cann 8.5, when qlen=1, pre&next tokens will be invalid for sparsemode4, fia squeezed mask to induct the true mask will fail as well ) (cann 9 may support this) refactor activation function for moe part. title: [AMD][aiter] Fix cuda_graph_kv_indices OOB under page_size>1
author: xiaobochen-amd
body:
## Motivation

The aiter attention backend crashes on ROCm with
`HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_APERTURE_VIOLATION` /
`HIP error: an illegal memory access was encountered` once the running
batch's `seq_lens_sum` grows past the cuda-graph KV-indices buffer.
The crash typically lands at a downstream `torch.cat` /
`synchronize()` so it looks unrelated, but the actual fault is an OOB
`tl.store` inside `create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton`.

Trigger conditions (must all hold):
- `--attention-backend aiter`, non-MLA model, `--page-size > 1`
- CUDA graph enabled (default)
- `seq_lens_sum` at decode time exceeds
  `cuda_graph_max_bs * ceil(max_context_len / page_size)` — easy to
  hit at moderate concurrency on long-context models, especially when
  `cuda_graph_max_bs` is small (e.g. clamped by
  `--max-running-requests`).

Root cause: `init_cuda_graph_state` allocates `cuda_graph_kv_indices`
at page granularity (`max_bs * ceil(max_context_len / page_size)`),
but every forward path that fills it (default decode, MLA decode,
target_verify, draft_extend{,_v2}) writes per token via
`create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton` with
`kv_indptr = cumsum(seq_lens)`. With `--page-size > 1` the buffer is
under-sized by `page_size`x and the kernel writes past its end.

Workaround for affected versions (no code change): pass `--page-size 1`.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py`,
  `init_cuda_graph_state`: allocate
  `max_bs * max_num_blocks_per_seq * page_size` instead of
  `max_bs * max_num_blocks_per_seq`.
  - `>= max_bs * max_context_len`, the worst-case per-token write.
  - Still divisible by `max_num_blocks_per_seq`, so the unified
    attention path's `view(-1, max_num_blocks_per_seq)` stays valid
    even when `max_context_len % page_size != 0`.
  - Identical to old behavior at `page_size = 1`.
- Inline TODO captures the proper page-mode root fix
  (`paged_attention_ragged` still runs with `view(-1, 1, ...)` and
  `block_size=1`, so `--page-size > 1` does not actually engage the
  attention kernel today; making it engage requires a per-page indices
  kernel + all metadata sites + the `paged_attention_ragged` call site
  + FP8 KV coordination, after which this allocation can revert).
- No other call sites or kernels are touched.

## Accuracy Tests

Reproducer (deterministic crash without this PR):

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path MiniMax-M2.7 \
  --tp-size 2 \
  --attention-backend aiter \
  --page-size 64 \
  --max-running-requests 64 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3

title: [diffusion] optimize: optimize frame returns path
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary
- materialize diffusion `return_frames` outputs to uint8 numpy frames inside the rank-0 GPU worker before returning them to the offline client
- spill large local numpy frame arrays to temporary file refs before scheduler/client ZMQ pickling, then materialize and unlink them on the client side
- widen `OutputBatch.output` typing and add CPU-only coverage for the array IPC helper

## Why
Wan2.2 TI2V profiling showed a large gap between worker execution time and offline `generate()` wall time. The dominant overhead was returning generated frame tensors through pickle/ZMQ rather than the model forward path.

## Validation
- Prior remote H200/no-cache Wan2.2 TI2V benchmark with this return path: README literal size `576x768` SGLD `2.059s` vs vLLM-Omni `2.505s`; Wan official auto-size `800x1088` SGLD `3.761s` vs vLLM-Omni `5.100s`. The earlier unoptimized SGLD profile showed `outer ~4.421s`, worker `~3.093s`, with about `1.305s` in the scheduler/client return path.

title: [Fix] Disable FlashInfer allreduce fusion under deterministic inference
author: Jiminator
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

PR #22664 (commit `c6a45fab64`) added `Qwen3NextForCausalLM` to the model-arch list in `ServerArgs._handle_model_specific_adjustments` that auto-enables `enable_flashinfer_allreduce_fusion` on SM90/SM100 with `tp_size > 1`. The fused FlashInfer/TRTLLM allreduce kernel chooses different reduction shapes/orderings depending on batch size, which breaks bit-exact determinism.

This violates the `--enable-deterministic-inference` contract, and has been failing the `nightly-test-general-4-gpu-h100 :: TestFlashInferDeterministic.test_prefix_with_logprobs` CI lane every dispatched run from 2026-04-19 through today (e.g. [run 24971499389](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24971499389/job/73115280649), [run 25469734855](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/25469734855)). The same auto-enable list also covers `DeepseekV3`, `GptOss`, `Glm4Moe`, `Qwen3MoE`, `KimiK2.5`, `Qwen3.5 MoE/non-MoE`, so any other deterministic-inference test on those arches with TP>1 on H100/H200/B200 is silently affected as well.

`_handle_deterministic_inference` currently force-disables only the **aiter** allredxruce fusion path; the FlashInfer counterpart is missing.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/server_args.py`:

1. In `_handle_deterministic_inference`, mirror the existing `enable_aiter_allreduce_fusion` handling — when `enable_deterministic_inference` is set, warn and clear `enable_flashinfer_allreduce_fusion`.
2. In `__post_init__`, set `enforce_disable_flashinfer_allreduce_fusion = True` **before** `_handle_model_specific_adjustments` runs, so the existing enforce check at the end of that handler (already present, line ~2378) is the single source of truth that drives the override. This addresses the concern that setting the enforce flag inside `_handle_deterministic_inference` would be redundant given `_handle_model_specific_adjustments` runs earlier in `__post_init__`.

No change to default (non-deterministic) behavior; `enable_flashinfer_allreduce_fusion` is still auto-enabled for the listed MoE arches when deterministic inference is **not** requested.

## Accuracy Tests

Local repro on 8× H100 80GB (driver 580.126.20), `--tp 4`, `Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct`, command identical to CI:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 SGLANG_IS_IN_CI=true \
python test/registered/core/test_qwen3_next_deterministic.py \
  TestFlashInferDeterministic.test_prefix_with_logprobs -v
```

| Commit | `enable_flashinfer_allreduce_fusion` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `4839cecbb0` (parent of #22664) | `False` | PASS — `Ran 1 test in 118.4s / OK / ✓✓✓ Logprobs are identical across all batch sizes! ✓✓✓` |
| `c6a45fab64` (#22664, introducing) | `True` | FAIL — `Ran 1 test in 102.6s / FAILED (errors=1) / ✗✗✗ Some logprobs differ across batch sizes! ✗✗✗`, 244 per-sample mismatches |
| HEAD (`5b589ed2e7`) | `True` | FAIL (same signature) |
| HEAD + this PR | `False` (forced via enforce flag) | PASS — `Ran 1 test in 94.6s / OK / ✓✓✓ Logprobs are identical across all batch sizes! ✓✓✓` |

Failing-vs-passing diffs reproduce the exact CI numerical fingerprint, e.g. `Logprob mismatch at position 0: -2.3552... vs -2.3723... (diff 0.017068...)`, the same value seen in the failing nightly logs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — change only fires when the user opts into `--enable-deterministic-inference`, where deterministic correctness already supersedes peak performance. No effect on the default (non-deterministic) path.

title: [Xeon] CPU CI enhancement for Intel Xeon platforms
author: MingxuZh
body:
## Summary

This PR improves Xeon CI reliability and coverage for CPU tests by fixing Hugging Face cache/token setup on self-hosted Xeon runners, expanding `base-b-test-cpu` registrations, and running the suite in 2 auto-partitioned shards to keep runtime manageable.

## Motivation

The previous Xeon workflow had a few practical issues:

1. It mounted a fixed Hugging Face cache path (`/home/sdp/.cache/huggingface`) that does not match current Xeon CI runner environments.
2. Some model-dependent tests require Hugging Face authentication, but `HF_TOKEN` was not injected into the container.
3. Xeon `base-b-test-cpu` coverage was narrower than desired for AMX/CPU-engine validation.
4. As more tests are included, a single-shard execution can become slow and unstable near timeout limits.

This PR addresses these gaps so Xeon CI can run a broader and more representative CPU test set with better stability.

## What Has Been Changed

### 1) Xeon workflow updates (`.github/workflows/pr-test-xeon.yml`)

- Added workspace cleanup before checkout for self-hosted runner hygiene.
- Set checkout `clean: false` to avoid workspace cleanup conflicts.
- Replaced fixed HF cache mount with runner-local cache mount:
  - from `${HF_HOME}` (`/home/sdp/.cache/huggingface`)
  - to `$HOME/.cache/huggingface`
- Injected Hugging Face token into container using:
  - `-e HF_TOKEN="$(cat ~/huggingface_token.txt)"`
- Switched `build-test` to a matrix with 2 partitions of the same suite:
  - `--auto-partition-id 0 --auto-partition-size 2`
  - `--auto-partition-id 1 --auto-partition-size 2`
- Kept Xeon execution on `base-b-test-cpu`, now split for better wall-clock behavior.

### 2) Xeon Docker image update (`docker/xeon.Dockerfile`)

- Installed `pytest` in the Xeon image to support newly covered tests and test runtime dependencies.

### 3) Test registration expansion (mostly under `test/registered/**`)

- Added many `register_cpu_ci(..., suite="base-b-test-cpu")` entries across unit/debug/lora/model-loading/function-call/observability and related test groups.
- Existing registrations (e.g. `base-a-test-cpu`, GPU/AMD nightly) are retained; this is additive coverage for Xeon.

### 4) Additional test tweak

- Updated `test/srt/cpu/test_cpu_graph.py` memory fraction from `0.05` to `0.5` for torch-compile CPU graph scenarios.

## Expected Impact

- Xeon CI can correctly reuse local HF cache and access gated models.
- Broader CPU test coverage now runs on Xeon AMX environment via `base-b-test-cpu`.
- 2-way partitioning helps reduce single-job bottlenecks and improves CI robustness.

title: [AMD] Add fused all-reduce RMSNorm per-group quant for Qwen3.5 FP8
author: hubertlu-tw
body:
Co-author: @mqhc2020, @yichiche  
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

This PR adds a fused aiter path for the Qwen3.5 FP8 attention/GDN input normalization path on AMD. The baseline path around `prepare_attn` runs all-reduce, RMSNorm, and per-group activation quant as separate work before the FP8 projection consumes `(fp8, scale)`.

The new path lets `LayerCommunicator.prepare_attn` request fused all-reduce + RMSNorm + per-group FP8 quant. Standard attention receives `(fp8, scale)` directly for `qkv_proj`. GDN receives `(bf16, fp8, scale)` so `in_proj_qkvz` can skip its internal activation quant while `in_proj_ba` still reads the bf16 activation it needs.

The fused-quant path is scoped to ROCm/aiter. The aiter single-kernel dispatch is gated to gfx95 / gfx950-class GPUs through `is_gfx95_supported()`, and plain `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` AR+RMSNorm behavior remains separate. If the fused-quant path is unavailable, callers fall back to fused AR+RMSNorm or the existing generic path.

## Modifications


- Added a tensor-parallel API for fused all-reduce + RMSNorm + per-group FP8
  quant:
  - `tensor_model_parallel_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_quant_per_group(...)`
  - `GroupCoordinator.fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_quant_per_group(...)`
- Added layernorm helpers that return tuple activations for FP8 consumers:
  - `((fp8, scale), residual)` for standard attention.
  - `((bf16, fp8, scale), residual)` for GDN, where bf16 is required by `in_proj_ba`.
- Wired `LayerCommunicator.prepare_attn` to prefer the fused-quant helper when `_sglang_needs_allreduce_fusion` is set and the layer opts in with `enable_fused_ar_quant=True`.
- Wired Qwen3.5 standard attention with `keep_bf16=False` and GDN with `keep_bf16=True`.
- Updated Qwen3.5 GDN input projection to consume the `(bf16, fp8, scale)` tuple without dequantizing fp8 back to bf16.
- Added `SGLANG_DISABLE_FUSED_AR_QUANT=1` as the operator opt-out for this quantized handoff while keeping the existing AR+RMSNorm fusion eligible.

Fallback order:

1. aiter single-kernel AR + RMSNorm + per-group FP8 quant, optionally with bf16 side-output.
2. aiter fused AR + RMSNorm plus separate aiter per-1x128 quant.
3. Generic caller fallback.

The single-kernel dispatch is intentionally limited to ROCm + aiter + gfx95.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K was run on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 with TP=8 and
`--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`.

| Config | GSM8K command | Accuracy |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Baseline | `python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 1319 --parallel 1319 --num-shots 5 --port 9000` | 0.946 |
| Fused AR+RMSNorm+per-group quant | `python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 1319 --parallel 1319 --num-shots 5 --port 9000` | 0.955 |

The fused path is above the 0.94 accuracy gate used for this model.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<details>
<summary>Server command</summary>

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true}' \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30001 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --attention-backend aiter --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --page-size 16 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --watchdog-timeout 1200 \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Serving benchmark command</summary>

```bash
for cc in 2 8 32; do
  python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30001 \
    --model /data2/Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
    --dataset-name random --random-input 8192 --random-output 1024 \
    --random-range-ratio 0.8 --max-concurrency $cc \
    --num-prompts $((cc*10)) --seed 0
done
```

</details>

Case A: baseline without `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` 
Case B: with `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`
| cc | Output tok/s A -> B | Delta | Mean TPOT A -> B | Delta | Mean TTFT A -> B |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 186.42 -> 197.21 | +5.8% | 10.46 ms -> 9.88 ms | +5.5% | 222.27 ms -> 225.39 ms |
| 8 | 598.54 -> 625.89 | +4.6% | 12.82 ms -> 12.23 ms | +4.6% | 292.07 ms -> 305.96 ms |
| 32 | 1332.17 -> 1328.84 | -0.2% | 22.81 ms -> 22.90 ms | -0.4% | 571.93 ms -> 560.36 ms |

Improvement formula:

- Throughput: `(candidate - baseline) / baseline * 100`.
- TPOT: `(baseline - candidate) / baseline * 100`.

Kernel-count profile, per decode pass on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 / TP=8 with 60
decoder layers:

| Kernel | Baseline | Fused path | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `cross_device_reduce_*stage` (plain AR) | 60 | 0 | -60 |
| `add_rmsnorm_quant_kernel` (RMSNorm+add) | 60 | 0 | -60 |
| `dynamic_per_group_scaled_quant_kernel` | 60 | 0 | -60 |
| `allreduce_fusion_kernel_1stage` (AR+RMSNorm) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `allreduce_fusion_kernel_1stage_per_group` | 0 | 60 | +60 |
| Comm-side separate quant for GDN keep-bf16 path | 45 | 0 | -45 |
| Total kernels saved on `prepare_attn` | | | -165 |

title: Optimize streaming detokenizer updates
author: inkcherry
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->
cc @ZhaiFeiyue  @Duyi-Wang 
## Motivation

`DetokenizerManager` is on the streaming output hot path. Under high-concurrency streaming workloads, it can spend noticeable CPU time on two avoidable operations:
1. Repeatedly concatenating `decoded_text += new_text` for every incremental text chunk.
2. Calling `tokenizer.batch_decode` on empty token spans, which decode to `""` but still pay tokenizer overhead.

## Modifications

- Add lazy chunk accumulation to `DecodeStatus`.
  - New text chunks are appended to a list and materialized only when the full decoded text is needed.
  - The common streaming path emits `new_text` directly when the sent offset is already aligned.
- Skip empty token spans in `_grouped_batch_decode`.
  - Empty spans return `""` directly.
  - Non-empty spans are decoded with the existing grouped `batch_decode` logic


<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

title: [diffusion] fix: further align ltx2.3 accuracy with tp
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Improve LTX-2 / LTX-2.3 diffusion accuracy against official-generated outputs, especially for multi-GPU CI cases and the LTX-2.3 HQ two-stage path.

The previous LTX-2.3 multi-GPU CI settings had weak consistency thresholds for some cases and could use parallelism modes that were either slower or less aligned with the official output. The HQ path also regressed on the PR #23366 SpongeBob repro.

Transformer fp8-cast is intentionally **not** included in this PR. It did not materially help this PR's target CI paths, and any future precision branch can keep or reintroduce it as a separate opt-in change.

## Modifications

- Tighten LTX consistency coverage:
  - switch selected LTX multi-GPU CI cases to the fastest verified TP/CFG-parallel settings instead of SP/Ulysses where those modes hurt accuracy or performance;
  - tighten thresholds for `ltx_2.3_one_stage_ti2v`, `ltx_2.3_two_stage_t2v_2gpus`, and `ltx_2_3_two_stage_ti2v_2gpus`.
- Improve LTX-2.3 HQ numerical alignment:
  - keep RoPE frequency generation on the target device to preserve the validated LTX-2.3 HQ rounding trajectory;
  - honor `frequencies_precision="float64"` from LTX/Diffusers configs;
  - restore the HQ res2s noise dtype boundary and stage-2 sigma-space res2s math.
- Fix two-stage / parallel runtime details:
  - let secondary components such as `transformer_2` inherit the base component attention backend unless explicitly overridden;
  - use the CFG process group's global source rank when broadcasting pipeline batches;
  - handle older FA3 varlen kernels that do not accept an `out=` keyword.
- Preserve explicit transformer quantization semantics:

title: [diffusion] fix FA3 varlen out argument handling
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

Fix FA3 varlen attention calls so wrappers do not pass `out=None` into kernels that do not expose an `out` keyword.

## Root Cause

`flash_attn_with_kvcache` already routes through `_call_fa3_kernel`, which omits `out` when it is `None` and retries without `out` for kernels that reject it. `flash_attn_varlen_func` bypassed that helper and always forwarded `out=out`, so kernels without an `out` parameter failed with:

```text
flash_attn_varlen_func() got an unexpected keyword argument 'out'
```

## Changes

- Extend `_call_fa3_kernel` to support keyword arguments.
- Route FA3 varlen attention through the same helper used by kvcache attention.

## Validation

- Remote H100, default FA3 backend, `--enable-torch-compile`, Flux.1-dev 1024x1024 1-step image request returned HTTP 200.
- No local tests were run.

title: [Gemma4] Optimize Gemm4 with fused Q/K/V RMSNorm + per-expert FP8 ckpt loader
author: yuan-luo
body:
## Motivation

The original motivation is to speedup Gemm4 model. Two unrelated issues on the Gemma4 FP8-MoE path:

1. **Attention RMSNorm is launch-bound.** Each Gemma4 attention layer issues three separate sgl-kernel `rmsnorm` launches (q/k/v). At small token counts the per-launch host overhead dominates — three back-to-back launches cost ~60μs regardless of M, even though the actual compute is trivial.

2. **compressed-tensors per-expert FP8 checkpoints fail silently.** Models like `RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-Dynamic` store one weight per expert (`experts.<id>.{gate,up,down}_proj.{weight,weight_scale}`). The existing loader only recognizes the stacked `experts.gate_up_proj` / `experts.down_proj` layout, so every routed expert is silently skipped → zero-init expert weights → server launches fine but generation collapses to all-`<pad>` and GSM8K = 0.0.

## Design

### 1. Fused Q/K/V RMSNorm (`gemma_qkv_rmsnorm`)

- One Triton kernel computes `x · rsqrt(mean(x²) + eps) · w` for all q/k/v heads in a single launch, in-place into the qkv buffer.
- Grid `(M,)`, `BLOCK = next_pow2(head_dim)`, with `tl.static_range` over heads.
- Operates on `qkv.split(...)` strided views via `stride_*_m` — no `.contiguous()` copy.
- V path skips the weight multiply (V uses `with_scale=False` → weight is identically 1).
- Conservative fallback in `Gemma4Attention.forward`: only takes the fused path when CUDA + `q_norm.scale_shift == 0 == k_norm.scale_shift` + `not v_norm.with_scale`. Non-standard configs and KV-shared layers retain the original three-norm
path.

### 2. Per-expert FP8 loader

- New regex branch in `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration.load_weights` for `^.*\.moe\.experts\.<id>\.(gate|up|down)_proj\.(weight|weight_scale)$`.
- Maps each per-expert key to the fused FusedMoE param + shard id + expert id, then dispatches via `param.weight_loader` (standard FusedMoE signature).
- If the regex matches but the fused param is absent (e.g. ckpt-format drift), emit `logger.warning` instead of silently skipping — this prevents reproducing the very failure mode the patch fixes.

### 3. Test

- `test/registered/models/test_gemma4_fp8_per_expert_loading.py` (CI: `stage-c-test-4-gpu-h100`, est 120s) launches the FP8 model with TP=4 and asserts: server health, non-`<pad>` chat output, and GSM8K-20 ≥ 0.80 (BF16 baseline ~0.95). All three checks fail pre-fix.

## Accuracy

MMLU 500 examples
BF16 （500 examples, TP=4）：0.878

RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-Dynamic
| Category | Score |
|---|---|
| Overall | 0.885 |
| STEM | 0.952 |
| Social sciences | 0.918 |
| Other | 0.872 |
| Humanities | 0.823 |

## Benchmark

H100 ×4, TP=4, `RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-Dynamic`, batch=1, in=2048, out=64.

**Microbench (single H100, bf16, Q=8h, KV=2h, head_dim=128):**

| M | unfused (μs) | fused (μs) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 44.4 | 19.8 | 2.25x |
| 8 | 59.4 | 20.3 | 2.93x |
| 64 | 59.4 | 20.4 | 2.91x |
| 256 | 59.7 | 20.1 | 2.96x |
| 1024 | 60.1 | 20.2 | 2.97x |
| 4096 | 58.4 | 18.6 | 3.14x |
| 8192 | 59.3 | 32.3 | 1.83x |
| 16384 | 108.0 | 75.0 | 1.44x |

Bit-exact vs unfused at M=1/8/128 (max abs diff = 0).

**End-to-end (4-GPU, RedHatAI FP8):**

| Metric | Unfused (baseline) | Fused (this PR) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prefill 2048 tok | 47.0 ms | 46.0 ms | **-2.1%** |
| Decode median | 5.47 ms/tok | 5.45 ms/tok | -0.4% |
| Total | 0.393 s | 0.390 s | -0.8% |

Decode benefit is muted because the SGLang decode path runs inside CUDA Graph, which amortizes the launch overhead the fused kernel saves. Prefill (no graph) realizes the full 2% win. Net change is neutral-to-positive across regimes; never negative within the tested M range.

The per-expert FP8 loader is a correctness fix: pre-fix GSM8K-20 = 0.00, post-fix ≈ 0.95 — gated at ≥ 0.80 in the new test.

## Test plan

- [x] Microbench: fused vs unfused bit-exact, 1.4–3.1x faster across M ∈ [1, 16384]
- [x] E2E prefill/decode latency comparison (above)
- [x] New CI test `test_gemma4_fp8_per_expert_loading.py` exercises the loader fix end-to-end on 4 GPUs
- [ ] Existing Gemma4 tests still pass (need full CI run)

title: ci: tag-gated nightly migration — foundation + 40 whole-file moves
author: alisonshao
body:
## Summary

PR2 of the CI pruning effort. Introduces a **conditional-CI** middle tier driven by PR labels + per-test tags, then applies it to 59 nightly migrations and assorted cleanup. Combined with PR1 (#24721, merged), the per-commit CUDA budget drops from 1232 min → 753 min (**−305 min in this PR alone, −38.9% combined, ~8h total**).

## New vocabulary

| Tier | When it runs | How it's defined |
|---|---|---|
| **baseline CI** | every PR commit, unconditional | `nightly=False` |
| **conditional CI** | when PR labels intersect a test's `tags` | `nightly=True, tags=(...)` |
| **full CI** | scheduled cron (3×/day) + nightly | union of everything |

`runs-on-PR = baseline ∪ conditional`. Scheduled cron passes `--include-tags=*` so it always exercises full CI.

## Mechanism

1. `.github/labeler.yml` auto-applies labels by file glob; users can also add labels manually.
2. `pr-test.yml` resolves labels into `INCLUDE_TAGS_FLAG` and threads it into every `run_suite.py` invocation.
3. `run_suite.py` pulls in any `nightly=True` test whose `tags ∩ pr_labels ≠ ∅`, restricted to nightly suites compatible with the per-commit suite per `PER_COMMIT_TO_NIGHTLY` (so a label-pulled test only lands on a runner the per-commit job is already invoking).

## Tags (8 new, 6 reused)

**New** — `attention-backend`, `moe`, `rl` (weight_sync only — `entrypoints/engine.py` deliberately excluded), `scoring`, `session`, `perf`, `scheduler`, `model-coverage`.

**Reused** — `Multi-modal`, `blackwell`, `deepseek`, `lora`, `piecewise-cuda-graph`, `quant`, `speculative-decoding`, `hicache`.

## Changes

### Foundation (no-op without test edits)
- `python/sglang/test/ci/ci_register.py` — add `tags: tuple = ()` to `CIRegistry`; AST validator accepts tuple/list literals of strings; runtime stubs gain a `tags` kwarg.
- `test/run_suite.py` — add `PER_COMMIT_TO_NIGHTLY` map, `--include-tags` CLI arg, `*` wildcard for "every nightly test in compatible-suite set", and `nightly-1-gpu-5090` registered in `NIGHTLY_SUITES`.
- `.github/workflows/pr-test.yml`:
  - `INCLUDE_TAGS_FLAG` resolved per event (`*` for schedule, joined labels for `pull_request`, gh-API lookup for `workflow_dispatch /rerun-stage`).
  - Threaded into all 15 `run_suite.py` invocations.
  - Stage-c → stage-b tier collapse: `wait-for-stage-b` deleted, all stage-c-* jobs now wait on `wait-for-stage-a`. Net pipeline: stage-a → stage-b (everything parallel) → done.
  - Dropped the dead `max-parallel:` matrix caps + the set-parallel scaffolding (cap was already = partition count = no throttle).
- `.github/labeler.yml` — 8 new tags with verified globs (corrected `scoring` and `session` paths; tightened `rl` to `weight_sync/**` only).

### Whole-file nightly moves (53)
Each test's `register_cuda_ci(...)` flips to `nightly=True`, suite remapped per `PER_COMMIT_TO_NIGHTLY`, `tags=(...)` added.

| Per-commit suite (was) | Nightly suite (now) | Tests |
|---|---|---:|
| `stage-b-test-1-gpu-large` | `nightly-1-gpu` | 18 |
| `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small` | `nightly-1-gpu-5090` | 13 |
| `stage-b-test-2-gpu-large` | `nightly-2-gpu` | 6 |
| `stage-c-test-4-gpu-b200` | `nightly-4-gpu-b200` | 7 |
| `stage-c-test-4-gpu-h100` | `nightly-4-gpu` | 3 |
| `stage-c-test-8-gpu-h200` (and `-deepep-`) | `nightly-8-gpu-h200` | 6 |

The 13 SM12.0/5090 tests depend on the `nightly-test-general-1-gpu-5090` workflow job in **#24731** (companion PR).

### Subset-move file splits (6)
Class-level partitions; sibling per-commit + nightly files using the `sys.path.insert` pattern from `test_streaming_session_swa.py`.

| File | What stays per-commit | What goes nightly | Tags (nightly) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_standalone_speculative_decoding.py` | V2 (Triton/Flashinfer/FA3) | non-V2 (Triton/Flashinfer/FA3) | `("speculative-decoding",)` |
| `test_ngram_speculative_decoding.py` | Paged | Triton + Flashinfer | `("speculative-decoding",)` (FA3 base archived to `test/manual/`) |
| `test_pcg_with_speculative_decoding.py` | EAGLE3 | MTP + STANDALONE + NGRAM | `("piecewise-cuda-graph", "speculative-decoding")` |
| `test_moe_ep.py` | TestEp | TestEpDeepGEMM | `("moe", "quant")` |
| `test_deepseek_v3_fp4_4gpu.py` | SymmetricMemory | CutlassMoE | `("blackwell", "deepseek", "moe", "quant")` (default-backend FP4 archived to `test/manual/`) |
| `test_streaming_session.py` | EagleV2RetractLargePage + AbortLeakRepro | base + 5 Retract*/Eagle* | `("session",)` |

### Cleanup (smaller, opportunistic)
- `test_tool_choice.py` → moved to `test/manual/openai_server/function_call/` (drops both CUDA + AMD per-commit registrations).
- `test_evs.py` → migrated GPU → CPU (`stage-a-test-cpu`); it's a pure unit test.
- `test_vision_openai_server_a.py` → removed 7 model classes overlapping with nightly (`Qwen2.5-VL`, `Qwen3-VL`, `InternVL2_5`, `MiniCPM-o-2_6`, `Kimi-VL`, `gemma-3-4b-it`, `GLM-4.1V`).
- `test_vlm_perf_5090.py` → `num_prompts=250 → 25` on `test_vlm_online_latency`; est_time scaled.

## Companion PRs

- **#24721** (merged) — PR1: 25 whole-file removals + 13 testcase archives.
- **#24731** (open) — adds the `nightly-test-general-1-gpu-5090` workflow job that the 13 SM12.0 tests depend on. Merge order: #24731 first, then this PR (otherwise SM12.0 tests silently skip until both land).

## Test plan

- [ ] Branch CI green on this PR.
- [ ] Verify a PR with the `quant` label pulls the `nightly-1-gpu` quant tests on `stage-b-test-1-gpu-large` (and not on `stage-b-test-2-gpu-large`) — sanity-check `PER_COMMIT_TO_NIGHTLY`.
- [ ] Verify a PR with no labels does not run any nightly tests.
- [ ] Verify the scheduled cron run picks up everything via `*` (full CI semantics preserved).
- [ ] Confirm stage-c jobs now run in parallel with stage-b jobs after stage-a passes (verify in workflow Gantt for a fresh PR).

title: fix(cuda_graph): zero out_cache_loc_swa on pad and use int32 (hybrid-SWA accuracy fix)
author: JoyFuture
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

  PR #23552 added a pre-computed `out_cache_loc_swa` buffer in `DecodeInputBuffers` so the captured decode graph can hit
  `set_kv_buffer`'s fast path on hybrid-SWA models (Gemma, MiMoV2, DeepSeek V4, …). On the main `CudaGraphRunner`, the main correctness issue is that `out_cache_loc_swa` is not cleared on padding, which can silently corrupt the SWA KV cache when decode cuda graphs are enabled. While touching this path, this patch also fixes a related dtype mismatch.                                                                                                                                                                 

  The user-visible symptom we hit is a measurable accuracy regression on **MiMoV2.5 Pro** (which is registered as hybrid SWA via `MIMO_V2_MODEL_ARCHS` in `model_config.py`). With the same checkpoint and identical eval workload:                                                                                                                                                                              

  | Benchmark      | Before | After   | Δ      |                                                                                                                                                            
  | -------------- | ------ | ------- | ------ |                                                                                                                                                            
  | aime24_25      | 80.3   | 90.3    | +10.0  |                                                                                                                                                            
  | cmmlu          | 87.6   | 90.1    | +2.5   |                                                                                                                                                            
  | minerva_math   | 89.4   | 93.6    | +4.2   |                                                                                                                                                            
  | mmlu-pro       | 82.6   | 85.1    | +2.5   |                                                                                                                                                            
  | mmlu_redux     | 93.1   | 94.97   | +1.87  |                                                                                                                                                            
  | supergpqa      | 59.1   | 62.4    | +3.3   |                                                                                                                                                            

  The regression is reproducible only when decode cuda graphs are enabled **and** the served batch size is small enough to be padded to a `capture_bs` bucket — which is exactly the common decode steady-state. 

## Root cause                                                                                                                                                                                             

  ### 1. Stale padding indices corrupt the SWA KV cache                                                                                                                                                     

  In `populate_from_forward_batch` (the main `CudaGraphRunner`), when `bs != raw_bs` only `out_cache_loc` is zeroed before the per-tensor copy. `out_cache_loc_swa` is not — and the subsequent copy only writes the first `raw_num_token` entries:                                                                                                                                                                        

  ```python                                                                                                                                                                                                 
  if bs != raw_bs:                                          
      self.seq_lens.fill_(seq_len_fill_value)                                                                                                                                                               
      self.out_cache_loc.zero_()                                                                                                                                                                            
      # out_cache_loc_swa is NOT zeroed                                                                                                                                                                     
      ...                                                                                                                                                                                                   

  if (                                                                                                                                                                                                      
      self.out_cache_loc_swa is not None                                                                                                                                                                    
      and forward_batch.out_cache_loc_swa is not None       
  ):                                                                                                                                                                                                        
      dsts.append(self.out_cache_loc_swa[:raw_num_token])
      srcs.append(forward_batch.out_cache_loc_swa[:raw_num_token])                                                                                                                                          
  ```

  The captured graph, however, runs set_kv_buffer over the full buffers.out_cache_loc_swa[:num_tokens] slice. The padded region [raw_num_token : num_tokens] keeps real SWA indices from the previous replay, so padded tokens write their junk KV into live SWA slots belonging to previously active requests. The pre-#23552 fallback path  (translate_loc_from_full_to_swa(out_cache_loc) per layer) didn't have this problem because out_cache_loc is zeroed on pad, so padded positions translate to the SWA sentinel.                                                                                                                                                                  

  The piecewise runner already does the right thing — it zeroes the buffer on pad in piecewise_cuda_graph_runner.py:654-655. The fix brings the main runner in line with that.                                                                                                                                                                 

  ### 2. Dtype mismatch with translate_loc_from_full_to_swa                                                                                                                                                     

  out_cache_loc_swa was allocated as torch.int64, but both SWAKVPool.translate_loc_from_full_to_swa (swa_memory_pool.py:170) and the DSV4 equivalent (deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:482) return torch.int32. The populate_from_forward_batch copy then implicitly  widens int32 → int64 and the captured graph hands an int64 index tensor to SWAKVPool.set_kv_buffer. This was flagged in the #23552 review and deferred; it's cheap to fix here alongside the correctness issue.

title: Optimize large add_constant tensors

body:
## Summary

- Add an architecture-aware vectorized path for large `add_constant` tensors: 16-byte vectors on pre-Blackwell / AMD, and 32-byte vectors on Blackwell when supported by the CUDA toolchain.
- Keep the scalar kernel for small tensors and for inputs/outputs that are not aligned to the selected vector type.
- Add an `add_constant` benchmark and extend correctness coverage for larger aligned and unaligned inputs.

## H200 Validation

title: Optimize MHC pipeline: DeepGemm, fused norm, fused hc_head
author: yhyang201
body:
## Summary
- Fold split-k stage-1 reduction into big_fuse (eliminates one kernel launch for num_tokens <= 2048)
- Use DeepGemm `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` for mhc_pre GEMM when `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM` is enabled
- Fuse RMSNorm into `mhc_pre_big_fuse` kernel (eliminates separate norm kernel launch + HBM round-trip)
- Add fused Triton kernel for `hc_head` (fuses RMSNorm + Linear + Sigmoid-gate + weighted-sum into one kernel)

Ported from:
- sgl-project/sglang@112f514 (fold reduction)
- sgl-project/sglang@2a3365d (DeepGemm)
- sgl-project/sglang@6b50c94 + sgl-project/sglang@c4554dc (fused norm)
- sgl-project/sglang@b427eba (fused hc_head)

## Microbench
