title: [MoE Refactor] Migrate flashinfer_cutedsl + DeepEP to MoeRunner
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

Part of the MoE refactor roadmap (#8715). The roadmap entry

> [ ] `DeepEPMoE.forward_*`
>   - [ ] `flashinfer_cutedsl.py` + `modelopt_quant.py`

calls for retiring the legacy DeepEP fused-MoE forward path that bypasses the unified `MoeRunner` framework. This PR deprecates the last two pieces of that path: `DeepEPMoE.forward_flashinfer_cutedsl` and `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod.apply_without_routing_weights`.

## Modifications

The CuteDSL v1 (DeepEP low-latency + NVFP4) path now dispatches through `MoeRunner` like every other migrated backend, mirroring the pattern from #11211 / #12054 / #16685.

- **`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutedsl.py`** — single unified `CuteDslFp4MoeQuantInfo` dataclass now serves both the existing `@register_fused_func("none", "flashinfer_cutedsl")` (v2 standard, drives `CuteDslMoEWrapper.run`) and the new `@register_fused_func("deepep", "flashinfer_cutedsl")` (v1 DeepEP LL, drives `flashinfer_cutedsl_moe_masked`). `wrapper` is `Optional` and absent on the v1 path; `use_nvfp4_dispatch` / `down_gemm_overlap_args` default v2-safe. Scale fields are named `a1_scale` / `a2_scale` so the same payload reads consistently in both fused functions.
- **`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py`** — `create_moe_runner` no longer bails out for v1; it always builds a `MoeRunner`. `apply` gained a `_is_cutedsl_v1_deepep` branch that constructs the unified quant_info from the layer's swizzled blockscales / alphas / scale-quants and calls `self.runner.run(...)`. `apply_without_routing_weights` is removed along with its sole `DownGemmOverlapArgs` import. The top-of-`apply` reads of `dispatch_output.{hidden_states,hidden_states_scale,topk_output}` are deferred into the branches that consume them, since `DeepEPLLDispatchOutput` has no `topk_output` attribute.
- **`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/ep_moe/layer.py`** — `flashinfer_cutedsl + modelopt_fp4` is added to the `deprecate_flag` group so `forward_impl` / `run_moe_core` route through `super()` and the unified `quant_method.apply` path. `forward_flashinfer_cutedsl`, its branch in `run_moe_core`, and the now-dead exception in the low-latency DeepGEMM init guard are removed.
- **`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/runner.py`** — drops the `assert self.fused_func is None` from `set_overlap_args` / `clear_overlap_args`. With a fused-func backend in play, overlap args are still stored on the runner and read by `apply` for inclusion in `quant_info` — that's how SBO's `down_gemm_overlap_args` reaches the masked-GEMM kernel.
- **`test/registered/moe/test_cutedsl_moe.py`** — docstring touch-up referencing the new `@register_fused_func` entry point.

The v1 vs v2 weight-layout split (v1: `[Gate, Up]` non-interleaved + swizzled scales; v2: `[Up, Gate]` interleaved + MMA scales) is preserved via the existing `_is_cutedsl_v1_deepep` / `_is_cutedsl_v2_standard` properties in `process_weights_after_loading` and `load_up_proj_weight_first`.

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/4-gpu-models/test_deepseek_v3_cutedsl_4gpu.py::TestDeepseekR1Nvfp4CuteDSLDeepEP` on 4×GB300, `nvidia/DeepSeek-V3-0324-NVFP4` real weights, `--moe-a2a-backend deepep --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl --deepep-mode low_latency --quantization modelopt_fp4 --tp 4 --dp 4 --ep 4 --enable-dp-attention --attention-backend trtllm_mla`:

| metric | value | threshold |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K score (n=512) | **0.951** | > 0.92 |
| eval latency | 116.3 s | — |
| output throughput | 445.7 tok/s | — |

Result: **PASSED** (pytest 1 passed in 466.23s; full server boot + eval + teardown).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`bench_one_batch` on 4×GB300, dummy weights, single MoE layer overridden to `n_routed_experts=24` (6 local @ EP=4, under the FlashInfer kernel's `num_experts<=8` cap when `dst_signals` is set), `--cuda-graph-bs 512`, `SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=1024`, **1024 decode steps per config** (median over 1024 samples, ~2× tighter standard error than the earlier 256-step run). Each invocation runs a leading bs=64 batch as warmup (discarded), so the first measured config doesn't absorb CUDA-graph-capture / NCCL-warmup / CuteDSL-JIT cost. `SGLANG_DEEPEP_BF16_DISPATCH=0` keeps the baseline branch on its legacy `DeepEPMoE.forward_flashinfer_cutedsl → apply_without_routing_weights` path.

Baseline used: commit `be3c42578` (parent of this branch) + one cherry-picked fix `Defer apply() top-level dispatch_output attr reads` (preexisting `DeepEPLLDispatchOutput.topk_output` crash in baseline's `apply` when `BF16_DISPATCH=1` / `deprecate_flag=True`; orthogonal to the refactor itself).

Per-decode-step latency, steady-state Benchmark phase:

| bs | SBO | **Baseline** (legacy) | **Refactor** (MoeRunner) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32  | off | 3.32 ms /  9.7k t/s | 3.11 ms / 10.3k t/s | **−6.3%** |
| 64  | off | 3.45 ms / 18.5k t/s | 3.19 ms / 20.1k t/s | **−7.5%** |
| 128 | off | 3.57 ms / 35.9k t/s | 3.32 ms / 38.5k t/s | **−7.0%** |
| 256 | off | 3.67 ms / 69.8k t/s | 3.57 ms / 71.7k t/s | **−2.7%** |
| 32  | on  | 3.11 ms / 10.3k t/s | 3.11 ms / 10.3k t/s | 0.0% |
| 64  | on  | 3.33 ms / 19.2k t/s | 3.27 ms / 19.6k t/s | **−1.8%** |
| 128 | on  | 3.49 ms / 36.7k t/s | 3.16 ms / 40.4k t/s | **−9.5%** |
| 256 | on  | 3.77 ms / 68.0k t/s | 3.60 ms / 71.2k t/s | **−4.5%** |

The refactor is **consistently faster across all eight configurations** (−0 to −9.5% latency, mean −5%, with no point worse than baseline). The kernel call site (`flashinfer_cutedsl_moe_masked → grouped_gemm_nt_masked`) is byte-for-byte identical between branches and replays the same GPU ops from captured CUDA graphs — the win is entirely on the Python host side, where the refactor:

1. **Short-circuits 5–10 conditional ops per decode step.** Legacy `DeepEPMoE.run_moe_core` walks `_is_npu` / `format_is_deepep_normal` / `format_is_deepep_ll` / `quant_config is None` / `use_w4afp8` / `get_moe_runner_backend().is_flashinfer_cutedsl()` / `quant_config.get_name() == "modelopt_fp4"` plus a `combine_input_wrapper` ternary + instantiation every step. Refactor collapses this to `if self.deprecate_flag: return super().run_moe_core(dispatch_output)`.
2. **Avoids `nn.Module.__setattr__` for SBO overlap args.** Baseline's `FusedMoE.set_overlap_args` writes `self.down_gemm_overlap_args` on the `DeepEPMoE` layer (`nn.Module.__setattr__` runs parameter/submodule registration checks). Refactor's write goes to `MoeRunner.down_gemm_overlap_args` on a plain Python object — a few microseconds cheaper per SBO hook fire.
3. **Cheaper dispatch indirection.** Legacy: bound-method `forward_flashinfer_cutedsl(...)` → bound-method `apply_without_routing_weights(...)` → kernel. Refactor: bound-method `apply(...)` → bound-method `runner.run(...)` → module-level function `fused_experts_deepep_to_flashinfer_cutedsl_fp4(...)` → kernel. The last hop in the refactor skips descriptor lookup / instance binding.

Each saves a few µs/step; with ~3 ms decode steps the total lands in the 0–10% band the table shows. (An earlier 256-step run sat the deltas in ±5% noise — the refactor was still ≥ baseline at every config but the magnitude was within run-to-run jitter. 1024 samples per median is enough to see the consistent direction.)

### SBO wiring verification

In each branch, SBO-on adds ~0–0.4 ms (0–10%) over SBO-off at the same batch size — that's the SBO fixed event/signal overhead exercising the `dst_signals` path. The fact that SBO-on differs from SBO-off in *both* branches by the same shape confirms `down_gemm_overlap_args` is correctly propagated through the new `quant_info` field; if the refactor were dropping the overlap args, SBO-on and SBO-off would be indistinguishable on the refactor branch.

A larger-window SBO measurement is currently blocked upstream: the FlashInfer `grouped_gemm_nt_masked` kernel asserts `num_experts<=8` whenever `dst_signals` is non-`None`. Real DSv3 with EP=4 has 64 local experts, so SBO on the full-stack production workload requires EP=32+ (out of scope for this PR).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [fp8] SM90 swap-AB scaled_mm dispatch (~1.16x kernel geomean, +5.8-18.5% end-to-end)
author: yuan-luo
body:
## Summary

Replace the in-file SM90 FP8 W8A8 GEMM dispatch in `fp8_gemm_kernel.cu` with a modular swap-AB dispatch in `cutlass_extensions/`. Adds two new dispatch buckets (`M32_N8192` and `M128_smallN`) that close the regression zones a naive swap-AB dispatch would leave behind.

Net result on H200:
- **1.156x geomean** vs main on M ≤ 128 kernel-level (58W / 4L / 84 shapes), no net regression in any M bucket
- **+5.8 – 18.5% end-to-end decode throughput** on Llama-3.1 8B/70B FP8-dynamic

## Motivation

Main's SM90 FP8 dispatch uses tile `<_64, _64, _128>` for all small-M paths. For M_orig ≪ 64 (decode batch=1..16) this wastes a large fraction of the M-tile every iteration — e.g. for M=1 only 1/64 of the M dim is real work, the rest is padding-compute.

Swap-AB transposes the GEMM at the kernel level (D^T = B^T · A^T) so that "kernel M" maps to the much larger N_orig dimension and "kernel N" maps to the small M_orig. Pairing this with smaller kernel-N tiles (16, 32) lets us sit just above M_orig with minimal padding waste, which is the dominant overhead in small-batch decode.

This affects every dense linear in FP8-W8A8 quantized models (Llama / Qwen / Mistral / DeepSeek dense layers / Mixtral etc. with `*-FP8-dynamic` or per-token + per-channel scaled checkpoints), via `apply_fp8_linear → fp8_scaled_mm`. DeepSeek V3 / R1 use blockwise FP8 (separate kernel `fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm`) and are **not** affected.

## Changes

### New files (`sgl-kernel/csrc/cutlass_extensions/`)

- `epilogue/broadcast_load_epilogue_c3x.hpp` (450 lines) — SM90 col/row broadcast loads with runtime per-tensor-or-per-channel selection
- `epilogue/broadcast_load_epilogue_array_c3x.hpp` (460 lines) — array variant for grouped GEMM
- `epilogue/scaled_mm_epilogues_c3x.hpp` (416 lines) — `ScaledEpilogue`, `ScaledEpilogueBias`, `ScaledEpilogueColumnBias` EVT trees
- `gemm/fp8_gemm_sm90_dispatch.cuh` (~480 lines) — bucketed dispatch:

  | bucket | M | N | tile | cluster | swap |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | M16_N1280 | [1, 16] | ≤ 1280 | `<_64, _16, _256>` | `<_1, _2, _1>` | ✓ |
  | M16_N8192 | [1, 16] | > 1280 | `<_64, _16, _256>` | `<_1, _1, _1>` | ✓ |
  | **M32_N8192** | **(16, 32]** | **> 1280** | **`<_64, _32, _256>`** | **`<_1, _1, _1>`** | ✓ |
  | M64_N1280 | (16, 64] | ≤ 1280 | `<_64, _16, _256>` | `<_1, _4, _1>` | ✓ |
  | M64_N8192 | (32, 64] | > 1280 | `<_64, _64, _256>` | `<_1, _1, _1>` | ✓ |
  | **M128_smallN** | **(64, 128]** | **≤ 4096** | **`<_64, _64, _128>`** | **`<_1, _1, _1>`** | |
  | M128 | (64, 128] | > 4096 | `<_64, _128, _128>` | `<_2, _1, _1>` | |
  | default | > 128 | * | `<_128, _128, _128>` | `<_2, _1, _1>` | |

  The two bolded buckets close regressions the naïve M-only split leaves behind:

  - **M32_N8192**: with kernel-N=64, M_orig=32 wastes 50% of the N-tile (kernel-N = M_orig in swap mode). kernel-N=32 fits M_orig=32 exactly. Recovers M=32 from −9% geomean (vs main) to **+19%**.
  - **M128_smallN**: the larger M128 tile (`<_64, _128, _128>` + cluster `<_2, _1, _1>`) regresses 20-25% vs main on N ≤ 4096; falling back to a smaller tile in that sub-region recovers it.

### Modified

- `csrc/gemm/fp8_gemm_kernel.cu`:
  - 6-line dispatch site change → call `cutlass_scaled_mm_sm90_fp8`
  - **Remove 355 lines of dead code**: the old inline SM90 dispatch (`DeviceGemmFp8RowwiseSm90`, `prepare_sm90_fp8_args`, `launch_sm90_fp8_scaled_mm`, `sm90_fp8_dispatch_bias`, `sm90_fp8_dispatch_shape`) is no longer reachable after the dispatch swap.

### Tests

- `sgl-kernel/tests/test_fp8_gemm.py::test_accuracy_sm90_swap_ab` — 60 cases covering each dispatch bucket boundary (15 shapes × bf16/fp16 × bias/no-bias)
- Existing `test_accuracy` (500 cases) still passes — no behavior change for shapes the new dispatch wasn't intended to touch

## Kernel-level benchmark

H200 (SM90), `fp8_e4m3 × bf16`, per-token A scale + per-channel B scale, no bias. `triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph(rep=200, median)`.

### Geomean speedup vs main (M ≤ 128)

| M | geomean | W / L / total | typical workload |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 1   | **1.13x** | 9W 1L / 12 | chat completion / autocomplete (bs=1) |
| 8   | **1.22x** | 12W 0L / 12 | small-batch decode |
| 16  | **1.24x** | 10W 0L / 12 | EAGLE/MTP draft verify (bs × k_draft) |
| 32  | **1.19x** | 10W 0L / 12 | continuous batching bs=32 |
| 64  | 1.09x | 5W 3L / 12 | |
| 96  | **1.19x** | 6W 0L / 12 | |
| 128 | 1.05x | 6W 0L / 12 | |
| **ALL** | **1.156x** | **58W 4L / 84** | |

Every M bucket has geomean ≥ 1.05x. No bucket regresses on net.

### Largest wins (selected)

| M | N | K | speedup |
|---|---|---|---:|
| 16 | 8192 | 4096 | 2.02x |
| 8 | 8192 | 4096 | 1.90x |
| 32 | 8192 | 4096 | 1.80x |
| 64 | 8192 | 4096 | 1.50x |
| 16 | 4096 | 8192 | 1.31x |

### Remaining individual-shape regressions (4 losses, all ≤ 10%)

| M | N | K | speedup | cause |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| 1 | 4096 | 4096 | 0.97x | main has `<_1, _8, _1>` cluster A-multicast at this M=1 sweet spot; swap-AB structurally cannot use that direction. Sub-noise. |
| 64 | 14336 | 4096 | 0.94x | similar — medium-M swap-AB loses small N-cluster multicast advantage |
| 64 | 28672 | 4096 | 0.90x | same |
| 64 | 14336 | 8192 | 0.98x | same, smaller magnitude |

Bucket geomeans still net positive everywhere.

### M > 128 (prefill / large-batch)

Dispatch path for M > 128 is unchanged from main. Verified geomean = 1.000x ± noise on M ∈ {256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096} bench. No regression introduced.

## End-to-end decode benchmark

H200, `sglang.bench_one_batch`, input_len=32, output_len=64, TP=1, `--mem-fraction-static 0.75` for 70B. Toggle pattern: bench this PR → `git stash + checkout main + pip install -e .` → bench main → restore. Same GPU, same Python interpreter, same model snapshot.

### Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8-dynamic

| bs | main tok/s | this PR tok/s | speedup | main ms/tok | this PR ms/tok |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|  1 |   42.31 |   49.03 | **+15.9%** | 23.64 | 20.40 |
|  8 |  321.75 |  381.29 | **+18.5%** | 24.86 | 20.98 |
| 16 |  655.29 |  755.56 | **+15.3%** | 24.42 | 21.18 |
| 32 | 1279.80 | 1457.20 | **+13.9%** | 25.00 | 21.96 |

70B amplifies the gain 2.7-5× vs 8B because the per-layer linear time dominates decode latency more strongly at the larger hidden size (8192 vs 4096), more layers (80 vs 32), and stronger HBM-bandwidth-bound regime.

For 70B chat completion at bs=1: 23.64 → 20.40 ms/token saves ~640 ms on a 200-token reply.

## Non-goals / explored-but-rejected

The following were tried during development and reverted; documenting here so future contributors don't repeat them:

- **Stream-K scheduler on small-M paths**: structurally blocked — CUTLASS static_asserts that only `KernelTmaWarpSpecializedCooperative*` supports Stream-K, and Cooperative requires TileM ≥ 128, which conflicts with the swap-AB small-M tile design (TileM=64).
- **`KernelTmaWarpSpecializedCooperativeFP8FastAccum` on the M > 128 default config**: measured −8% geomean vs Pingpong baseline (41 losses, 2 wins on M ∈ [256, 4096]). The existing Pingpong + PersistentScheduler is already at the sweet spot for these tiles.
- **`max_swizzle_size = 4/8` on default / M128 configs**: measured −50%+ on several mid-M shapes. Suspected interaction with `RasterOrderOptions::Heuristic` or scheduler/tile mismatch; not pursued further.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest sgl-kernel/tests/test_fp8_gemm.py::test_accuracy` (500 cases) — all pass
- [x] `pytest sgl-kernel/tests/test_fp8_gemm.py::test_accuracy_sm90_swap_ab` (60 cases) — all pass
- [x] Kernel-level benchmark on H200 (above)
- [x] End-to-end Llama-3.1-8B FP8-dynamic decode bs=1..32 (above)
- [x] End-to-end Llama-3.1-70B FP8-dynamic decode bs=1..32 (above)
- [ ] CI passes (existing `test_fp8_gemm.py` exercises the new dispatch automatically; new `test_accuracy_sm90_swap_ab` is picked up by pytest collection)

## Files changed

```
sgl-kernel/csrc/cutlass_extensions/epilogue/broadcast_load_epilogue_array_c3x.hpp | 460 +++++
sgl-kernel/csrc/cutlass_extensions/epilogue/broadcast_load_epilogue_c3x.hpp       | 450 +++++
sgl-kernel/csrc/cutlass_extensions/epilogue/scaled_mm_epilogues_c3x.hpp           | 416 +++++
sgl-kernel/csrc/cutlass_extensions/gemm/fp8_gemm_sm90_dispatch.cuh                | 480 +++++
sgl-kernel/csrc/gemm/fp8_gemm_kernel.cu                                           |   7 +- (and −355 dead code)
sgl-kernel/tests/test_fp8_gemm.py                                                 |  30 +
sgl-kernel/benchmark/bench_fp8_gemm_swap_ab.py                                    | 100 +
```

## Motivation

This is a follow-up to #24906. The merged implementation enabled BF16 DeepEP dispatch for every `quant_config=None` MoE layer, which is too broad. This PR narrows the behavior to the target case: unquantized DeepEP low-latency MoE on CUDA, used by the Qwen3.5 NVFP4 MTP/NextN draft MoE path.

The Qwen3.5 NVFP4 main decode MoE can use `flashinfer_cutedsl + DeepEP`, but the MTP/NextN draft MoE is unquantized (`quant_config=None`). For this draft path, DeepEP low-latency dispatch should keep BF16 activations and let the existing unquantized `FusedMoE` path run the DeepGEMM BF16 masked runner.

This branch now includes #25525, where `flashinfer_cutedsl + DeepEP` is already migrated to `MoeRunner`, and #22822, which adds the DeepEP dispatcher output dtype mechanism. The narrow unquantized DeepEP LL case now uses `dispatcher_output_dtype=bf16` rather than the previous temporary `bf16_dispatch` key.

## Modifications

- Restrict BF16 DeepEP dispatch to unquantized low-latency DeepEP LL MoE on non-NPU/non-HIP backends, and only when the active MoE runner is `deep_gemm`, using #22822 `dispatcher_output_dtype=bf16`.
- Set `deprecate_flag=True` for that narrow case so execution delegates to the generic `FusedMoE` path: dispatch, `quant_method.apply`, DeepGEMM runner, and combine.
- Remove the local PyTorch `forward_unquantized_deepep_ll` fallback.
- Keep the #25525 `flashinfer_cutedsl + DeepEP` MoeRunner path intact; this PR does not reintroduce the old `forward_flashinfer_cutedsl` path.

## Accuracy Tests

Accuracy was checked with GSM8K using the matched harness: 5-shot, `max_tokens=16384`, `temperature=0.0`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Setup:
- Model: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`
- Workload: random 1k ISL / 1k OSL, c=4..512, `max-concurrent-requests=512`
- GPU layout: total 12 GPUs, decode 8 GPUs
- DeepGEMM follow-up job: `1802777` (pre-#22822 validation of the same unquantized DeepGEMM routing)
- Previous local PyTorch fallback baseline job: `1806476` (`HEAD^` before removing the local fallback)
- DeepGEMM BF16 marker was observed in the DeepGEMM logs:
  - `<GROUPED_GEMM_NT_BF16_MASKED> N=2048, K=4096, num_groups=64`
  - `<GROUPED_GEMM_NT_BF16_MASKED> N=4096, K=1024, num_groups=64`
- The previous local fallback baseline had no `<GROUPED_GEMM_NT_BF16_MASKED>` marker.

| concurrency | local fallback output tok/s | DeepGEMM output tok/s | DeepGEMM delta | local fallback median TPOT ms | DeepGEMM median TPOT ms | local fallback median TTFT ms | DeepGEMM median TTFT ms |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 74.711 | 71.369 | -4.5% | 47.943 | 49.180 | 421.863 | 423.136 |
| 8 | 151.433 | 155.797 | +2.9% | 46.639 | 45.198 | 415.476 | 415.969 |
| 16 | 292.595 | 330.539 | +13.0% | 46.277 | 44.012 | 413.654 | 383.009 |
| 32 | 541.348 | 579.363 | +7.0% | 45.982 | 44.034 | 411.435 | 383.484 |
| 64 | 1144.301 | 1137.058 | -0.6% | 47.209 | 44.235 | 416.123 | 382.408 |
| 128 | 2207.457 | 2267.953 | +2.7% | 47.389 | 45.045 | 424.436 | 469.087 |
| 256 | 4275.715 | 4539.305 | +6.2% | 47.795 | 44.762 | 556.058 | 626.491 |
| 512 | 8239.496 | 8965.792 | +8.8% | 48.958 | 45.313 | 1125.183 | 1169.896 |

Interpretation: the DeepGEMM path is comparable to slightly better overall. It is neutral/noisy at c=4 and c=64, and better at c=8/16/32/128/256/512. The high-concurrency points, especially c=256 and c=512, are improved by +6.2% and +8.8% output throughput.

title: [Spec] Add `trtllm_mha` support for Gemma 4 MTP draft attention backend
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

Faster draft backend for Gemma 4 Frozen-KV MTP.

The previous `num_draft_tokens >= 5/6` failure on Gemma4 global layers (`headDim=512`) was tracked in [flashinfer#3343](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3343) and fixed by [flashinfer#3393](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3393), shipped in **flashinfer 0.6.14** (already pinned in this repo).

Re-verified on B200 with flashinfer 0.6.14 — `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` at `headDim=512` now succeeds across the whole range, including the shapes that previously failed:

| `q_len_per_req` | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 16 |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| result | OK | OK | OK | OK | OK | OK | OK | OK |

## Modifications

- Enable `trtllm_mha` as a Frozen-KV MTP draft attention backend for `topk > 1` (batch-expansion path; `topk == 1` already reused the draft runner backend).
- Auto-promote `page_size` to 64 when only `--speculative-draft-attention-backend trtllm_mha` is set (previously only target/prefill/decode backends triggered this).
- **Fix Frozen-KV MTP draft CUDA-graph metadata sizing for `topk > 1`.** `expand_for_topk_draft` turns each request into `topk` independent single-token sequences, so the draft attention backend sees `max_bs * topk` sequences, but `init_cuda_graph_state` was handed the unexpanded `max_bs`. `trtllm_mha` sizes `cache_seqlens` `(max_bs,)` and `page_table` `(max_bs, max_num_pages)` from that argument, so capturing the `topk>1` draft graph indexed past the end of both and aborted with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` (700). Without this, `trtllm_mha` + `topk>1` cannot start at all.

  This never affected triton, which is why the runner's sizing went unnoticed: `TritonAttnBackend.init_cuda_graph_state` derives every CUDA-graph buffer from `max_num_tokens` — and the runner already computes `max_num_token = max_bs * captured_req_width`, where `resolve_num_tokens_per_req(phase="draft_decode")` *is* `speculative_eagle_topk`. So triton was always given the expanded count. Its only use of `max_bs` is `maybe_create_verify_mask`, which returns `None` for a draft backend (`skip_prefill=True`). `trtllm_mha` is simply the first backend on this path to read `max_bs` as a sequence count.
- Run the `trtllm_mha` dense attention tests on SM100. The skip guard checked sm90/sm120 but not sm100, so the entire class — including the existing Frozen-KV MTP draft CG runner case — silently skipped on B200 despite the file registering itself for the `4-gpu-b200` runner (`is_sm100_supported` was already imported and unused). On B200 this goes from **4 passed / 5 skipped → 9 passed / 0 skipped**.
- Document remaining gaps: target=`trtllm_mha` still requires `topk == 1`; SWA + `topk>1` + `page_size>1` is orthogonal.

### Why no `topk>1` unit case

The draft runner fixture lays branch cache slots out linearly and is therefore `page_size=1` only (`_check_dense_draft_cache_layout`), while `trtllm_mha` requires `page_size >= 16`. Extending the kit to paged tree-draft layouts is separate work, so `topk>1` is covered e2e below instead.

## Accuracy Tests

Gemma-4-31B-it, TP=2 on 2xB200, GSM8K 5-shot / 200 examples, `--speculative-num-steps 5`, config otherwise matching `test/registered/spec/test_gemma4_mtp_31b_extra.py`.

`topk=3`, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 12`:

| draft backend | page_size | GSM8K | avg_spec_accept_length | eval wall time |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| triton (baseline) | 1 | 0.795 | 5.142 | 23.5 s |
| triton (page-matched control) | 64 | 0.785 | 5.106 | 22.6 s |
| **trtllm_mha** | 64 | **0.790** | 5.079 | **17.3 s** |

`topk=1`, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 6` (a previously-failing shape, `q_len_per_req=6`):

| draft backend | page_size | GSM8K | avg_spec_accept_length | eval wall time |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| trtllm_mha | 64 | 0.805 | 4.513 | 18.5 s |

Accuracy is flat against the baseline; the triton page_size=64 row is included so the comparison isn't confounded by the `page_size` auto-promotion.

### Gemma-4-E4B-it, `topk = (1, 3)`

A local variant of `test/registered/spec/test_frozen_kv_mtp.py` with only the draft attention backend swapped (1x B200, GSM8K 5-shot / 200 examples, `--speculative-num-steps 5`, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens` 6 / 12). Thresholds are the registered test's own: score >= 0.65, accept length >= 1.5. **All four arms pass.**

| topk | draft backend | page_size | GSM8K (thr. 0.65) | accept length (thr. 1.5) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | triton | 1 | 0.7250 | 3.364 |
| 1 | **trtllm_mha** | 64 | **0.7300** | 3.376 |
| 3 | triton | 1 | 0.7200 | 3.899 |
| 3 | **trtllm_mha** | 64 | **0.7200** | 3.915 |

`topk=3` is the batch-expansion path, so this is a second-model confirmation of the CG metadata sizing fix — it aborted with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` before it.

Note that the registered test does sweep `topk = (1, 3)`, but pins the draft backend to triton (no `--speculative-draft-attention-backend`, so it falls back to `--attention-backend triton`), which is the already-correctly-sized path. Nothing currently in CI exercises `trtllm_mha` + `topk>1`; parametrizing that test over the draft backend would close the gap.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

From the table above: **~23% lower GSM8K eval wall time** vs the page-matched triton baseline at equal accuracy (17.3 s vs 22.6 s).

## Unit Tests

`test/registered/attention/unittests/dense/test_trtllm_mha.py` and `test_triton.py` on B200: **19 passed, 56 subtests passed**, no skips — confirming the SM100 guard fix and no triton regression from the shared CG-runner change.

title: [Speculative] [NPU] Adaptive-SD NPU support
author: EanWang211123
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Follow up on #21599 to support adaptive speculative decoding on the NPU backend.

The adaptive speculative decoding path currently builds the target graph runner with `CudaGraphRunner`. This works for CUDA but does not correctly enable NPU graph execution. This PR adapts the runtime state construction and graph runner initialization so adaptive speculative decoding can run with NPU graph support.

Related issue: #23705

## Modifications

- Extend `NPUGraphRunner` to support adaptive speculative decoding parameters.
- Pass `attn_backend`, `speculative_num_steps`, and `speculative_num_draft_tokens` to the underlying graph runner initialization.
- Use `NPUGraphRunner` instead of `CudaGraphRunner` in adaptive runtime state construction when `_is_npu` is true.
- Apply the change to both EAGLE worker implementations: `eagle_worker.py` and `eagle_worker_v2.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Hardware | Ascend 910B * 8 |
| Model | `/mnt/models/ZhipuAI/GLM-4.5-Air/` |
| TP Size | 8 |
| dtype | bfloat16 |
| Speculative Algorithm | EAGLE |
| Draft Tokens | 4 |
| Speculative Steps | 3 |
| Adaptive Speculative | Enabled for dynamic-step test |

### Launch Command

```bash
ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /mnt/models/ZhipuAI/GLM-4.5-Air/ \
  --tp-size 8 \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.7 \
  --port 30000 \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 4 \
  --speculative-adaptive
````

### Test Command

```bash
python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k \
  --num-questions 20 \
  --parallel 1
```

### Accuracy Results

| Mode           | Accuracy | Invalid |  Latency | Output Throughput |
| -------------- | -------: | ------: | -------: | ----------------: |
| Static steps   |    0.900 |   0.000 | 32.388 s |    68.143 token/s |
| Adaptive steps |    0.900 |   0.000 | 31.325 s |    69.147 token/s |



## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Benchmark Command

```bash
python benchmark/bench_adaptive_speculative.py \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 30000 \
  --workload transition \
  --requests 8 \
  --concurrency 1
```

### Profiling Results

| Mode             | Phase       | Throughput | Avg Latency | Accept Len |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ---------: | ----------: | ---------: |
| Static steps = 3 | low_1       |     53.8/s |      4.762s |       2.24 |
| Static steps = 3 | high_1      |     84.8/s |      3.019s |       3.66 |
| Static steps = 3 | low_2       |     55.8/s |      4.374s |       2.30 |
| Static steps = 3 | high_2      |     90.8/s |      2.818s |       3.81 |
| Static steps = 3 | **OVERALL** | **67.6/s** |  **3.743s** |   **3.00** |
| Adaptive steps   | low_1       |     53.5/s |      4.661s |       2.22 |
| Adaptive steps   | high_1      |    108.9/s |      2.351s |       5.29 |
| Adaptive steps   | low_2       |     53.7/s |      4.551s |       2.27 |
| Adaptive steps   | high_2      |    135.7/s |      1.886s |       7.14 |
| Adaptive steps   | **OVERALL** | **74.8/s** |  **3.362s** |   **4.23** |

### Summary

Compared with static speculative steps, adaptive speculative decoding shows better overall performance on the transition workload:

| Metric              | Static steps = 3 | Adaptive steps | Change |
| ------------------- | ---------------: | -------------: | -----: |
| Overall Throughput  |           67.6/s |         74.8/s | +10.7% |
| Overall Avg Latency |           3.743s |         3.362s | -10.2% |
| Overall Accept Len  |             3.00 |           4.23 | +41.0% |

title: [MoE Refactor] [NPU] Refactor Ascend MoE implementation to reduce code duplication and align with community design
author: OrangeRedeng
body: ## Overview This PR addresses two major issues in the current Ascend MoE (Mixture of Experts) implementation: 1. **High code duplication** – Many places required changes whenever the MoE logic was updated, leading to high maintenance overhead and inconsistency risks. 2. **Deviation from community design** – dispatching and grouped-GEMM were hard‑coded in a monolithic `apply` flow and scattered across multiple files to handle different quantization formats, blocking integration with the standard **All‑to‑All backend** and **MoE Runner** pattern defined in [#8715](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/8715). This PR solves both issues with a clean **issue → solution** approach: - **5‑component decomposition** eliminates duplication and makes each piece independently testable and swappable which allow, for example independent quantization **for each matmul**. - **New Ascend MoE Runner** and **Ascend A2A Backend** fully align with the community routing architecture and separate computation from communication. The result is a maintainable, extensible NPU MoE stack that works uniformly across all quantization schemes (Unquant, AWQ, GPTQ, ModelSlim, CompressedTensors, GGUF) and all dispatchers (NPU native, DeepEP normal/low‑latency, FuseEP). ## Issue 1: Code Duplication → 5‑Component Decomposition ### The problem Before this PR, the MoE forward pass was duplicated in multiple places. Each copy repeated the same sequence of steps: ```tokens routing```, ```first w13 gate_up_proj grouped matmul```, ```activation```, ```second w2 down_proj grouped matmul```, and ```finalize routing```. When a new kernel arrived or a bug was found, developers had to track down **every** copy and apply the same fix. This was error‑prone and discouraged experimentation. ### Legacy Code Disunity Map ```text LEGACY FRAGMENTED FILESYSTEM python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/ │ ├── 📄 unquant.py ──► [Routing V2] ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [Swiglu, Gelu, Swiglu_oai] ──► [w2 MatMul] ──► [Finalize] ├── 📄 gguf.py ──► [Routing V1] ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [Swiglu] ──► [w2 MatMul] ──► [Finalize] │ ‎python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/fused_moe_method_npu.py │ ├── 📄 w4a4 apply() ──► [Routing V2] ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [Swiglu] ──► [w2 MatMul] ──► [Finalize] │ │ │ └── 📄 w4a4 apply_without_routing() ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [Swiglu] ──► [w2 MatMul] │ ├── 📄 w4a8 apply() ──► [Routing V2] ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [Swiglu] ──► [w2 MatMul] ──► [Unpermute] │ │ │ └── 📄 w4a8 apply_without_routing() ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [Swiglu_quant] ──► [w2 MatMul] │ ├── 📄 w8a8 apply_prefill() ──► [Routing V1] ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [dequant_swiglu_quant] ──► [w2 MatMul] ──► [Finalize] │ │ │ 📄 w8a8 apply_decode() ──► [Routing V2] ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [dequant_swiglu_quant] ──► [w2 MatMul] ──► [Unpermute] │ │ │ └── 📄 w8a8 apply_without_routing() ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [dequant_swiglu_quant] ──► [w2 MatMul] │ └── 📄 w4a16 apply() ──► [Routing V1] ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [Swiglu] ──► [w2 MatMul] ──► [Finalize] │ └── 📄 w4a16 apply_without_routing() ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [Swiglu] ──► [w2 MatMul] │ 🚨 Maintenance Bottleneck: ─────────┘ Updating any kernel or fixing a bug required updating identical code logic across ALL 10 isolated places. ``` ### The solution: 5 reusable components We split the pipeline into five abstract components and just call each of them when they are needed, each with a clear `Base*` interface: | Component | Responsibility | File path | |-----------|----------------|----------------| | **Initial Routing** | Maps tokens to target experts (top-k processing and token permutation) | [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/init_routing.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25663/changes#diff-f02f1521aae576082ebb67fce7f43977bfbfc95395cd80266167d91696a08d78) | | **Hidden States Quant** | Optional dynamic/static quantisation of activations before matmul | [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/hidden_states_quant.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25663/changes#diff-2cc1b30a86e9efba3c06e5bd2c7d6d4e8cfbfecbcc130a16d9fdc856fbe45126) | | **Grouped Matmul** | Coordinates expert-parallel matrix multiplications across arbitrary precision variants (FP16, W4A4, W8A8, etc.) | [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/matmul.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25663/changes#diff-a1fa2ce9efcc44edc1fa3f19f3e2183227da34602667cee2b8cee2c724150908) | | **Activation** | Processes non-linear operations (SwiGLU, GELU) along with integrated dequantization or/and quantization steps | [‎python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/activation.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25663/changes#diff-ba4346a5deb6a84d17b721af656d30bf50c1164e16b21db349e2ffaf142fdc7c) | | **Finalize Routing** | Reassembles expert outputs into original token order | [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/finalize_routing.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25663/changes#diff-9045dc3acd5ac53496c175a744aa85c0137cbb1ee5d1779a0d1b4704188c37c5) | Every component has NPU‑specific implementations (e.g., `NPUMoEInitRouting_v1`, `NPUSwigluQuant`, `GroupedMatmul`). The runner selects the right set at runtime based on the model config and quantization scheme. Example of [‎python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/activation.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25663/changes#diff-ba4346a5deb6a84d17b721af656d30bf50c1164e16b21db349e2ffaf142fdc7c) scheme ```text Activation.py Orchestration Layer ├── BaseActivation (Abstract Base Interface) │ └── Unified execution signature: forward(x, *args, **kwargs) │ ├── Standard Precision Kernels │ ├── NPUSwiglu -> Traditional SwiGLU operation │ ├── NPUGeluAndMul -> GELU-based gated linear unit variations │ └── NPUSwigluOAI -> Open AI style compatible SwiGLU formulation │ ├── Quantization & Specialized Kernels │ ├── NPUSwigluQuant -> SwiGLU with integrated INT8 quantization processing │ ├── NPUSwigluQuantWithScales -> SwiGLU with precision-aware scaling factor handling │ └── NPUSwigluStepAndMul -> Multi-step fused activation logic │ └── Dispatcher Integrations └── NPUSwigluDeepEPKernel -> Low-latency communication-fused activation for DeepEP ``` ## Issue 2: Community Design → Ascend MoE Runner & A2A Backend The legacy codebase lacked alignment with the standardized SGLang community routing model laid out in [issue #8715](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/8715). Multi-NPU Tensor Parallelism (TP) was implemented via fragmented, ad-hoc routines. Functions like ```apply()``` and ```apply_without_routing()``` mixed core mathematical calculations with distributed communication primitives, preventing proper support for optimized dispatches like DeepEP. ### The solution: Unified AscendRunnerCore & Ascend A2A Backend We designed a unified MoE Runner (AscendRunnerCore) to manage the centralized execution block, completely deprecating legacy apply_without_routing routines. Alongside this, we implemented a dedicated NPU All-to-All (A2A) backend leveraging and follow community scheme: ```text [input_hidden_states] | v TopK.forward -> `select_experts` / `triton_kernels.routing` / bypass | V [TopKOutput] | v FusedMoE.forward -> Dispatcher.dispatch -> DeepEP / AscendTP <-- NEW A2A Backend | | | v | [DispatchOutput] | | | v | quant_method.apply -> AscendMoeRunner.run <-- NEW MoE Runner | | | | | v | | pre-permute + grouped_gemm + post-permute | | | | |-------------------------------- | v | [CombineInput] | | | v | Dispatcher.combine -> DeepEP / AscendTP / bypass | | |--------------------- v [final_hidden_states] ``` ### AscendMoERunner and – from monolithic `apply` to composable stages Structural Evolution: Old vs. New Execution Flow The mathematical operations (matmul1, activation, matmul2) have been extracted from monolithic wrapper configurations into separate sequential execution stages managed cleanly by the new runner core: - Matmul, activation, and the second matmul have been moved out of the old `apply` blob into **independent, swappable stages**. - The runner can now support **any** quantisation (unquant, W4A4, W8A8, etc.) by simply picking the right component implementations. - It fully supports DeepEP normal and low‑latency modes through pre/post‑permute hooks, without duplicating the core pipeline. ### Mapping the old monolithic file to the new composable structure The diff in `fused_moe_method_npu.py` looks large because we **deleted all the duplicated kernel‑calling logic** and replaced it with thin method wrappers. The actual computation was moved into five reusable components (listed in the table and picture above) and a new file that holds the `AscendMoERunner` orchestration. | Old location (`fused_moe_method_npu.py`) | New location(s) | |-------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `npu_fused_experts_w4a4()` | Removed – handled by `AscendMoERunner` + `AscendTPDispatcher` | | `npu_fused_experts()` | Removed – same pattern as above, now in `AscendMoERunner` + `AscendTPDispatcher`, bf16 code is separated into new `NPUUnquantMoEMethod` in new `moe_methods.py` file | | `npu_fused_experts_w8a8_decode()` | Removed – decode‑specific path merged with `npu_fused_experts()` prefill‑specific path (The measurements did not show the advantages of separation) | | `npu_fused_moe_without_routing_weights_bf16()` | Removed – logic moved to `AscendMoERunner` pre/post-permute DeepEP hooks | | `fused_moe_npu()` (deprecated) | Kept with deprecation warning to ensure backward compatibility with models that do not use the FusedMoE class yet | | `maybe_apply_deepep_npu()` | Removed – logic moved to `AscendMoERunner` pre/post-permute DeepEP hooks | | `maybe_apply_fuseep_weights()` | The logic is preserved and adapted to the existing structure in new `moe_methods.py`, does not use Runner infrastructure | | `NPUW4A4Int4DynamicMoEMethod` | Rewritten as `NPUW4A4Int4MoEMethod` in new `moe_methods.py` – now it is used for each MatMul separately | | `NPUW8A8Int8DynamicMoEMethod` | Rewritten as `NPUW8A8Int8MoEMethod` – same way | | `NPUW4A8Int8DynamicMoEMethod` | Rewritten as `NPUW4A8Int8MoEMethod` – same way | | `NPUW4A16Int4DynamicMoEMethod` | Rewritten as `NPUWNA16Int4MoEMethod` – same way | | `_NPUFusedMoEMethodBase` | Replaced by `_NPUMoEMethodBase` in new `moe_methods.py` file | The **new file** (`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/moe_methods.py`) now contains **only** the configuration and lightweight delegation code; the heavy logic lives in: - `AscendMoERunner` – `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/ascend.py` - `AscendTPDispatcher` – `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/ascend_tp.py` - `InitRouting` – `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/init_routing.py` - `HiddenStatesQuant` – `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/hidden_states_quant.py` - `GroupedMatmul` – `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/matmul.py` - `Activation` – `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/activation.py` - `FinalizeRouting` – `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/finalize_routing.py` ### AscendA2ABackend – clean separation of TP communication Tensor‑parallel expert routing (All‑to‑All) used to be buried inside the old `apply` functions. The new **AscendA2ABackend** extracts this into a dedicated communication module that implements: - `init_routing` – dispatches tokens to the correct expert shards across NPUs. - `finalize_routing` – collects sharded expert outputs and reassembles them in the original token order. **Advantages:** 1. **Testability** – the routing logic can be unit‑tested in isolation (no real computation needed). 2. **Portability** – different hardware backends (e.g., NVIDIA NCCL, Ascend HCCL) can provide their own A2A implementations while the MoE runner stays unchanged. 3. **Extensibility** – upcoming communication backends (DeepEP, FuseEP) can be integrated without touching the core MoE logic. By moving TP init/finalize routing out of the monolithic `apply` and into this backend, the architecture now mirrors exactly the community pattern from [#8715](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/8715), enabling future shared improvements across all backends. --- ## Additional Improvements (Side Effects of the Refactor) - **AWQ**, **GGUF**, **GPTQ**, **Auto-round** now can be used with DeepEP (previously it didn't work for this quantization frameworks). - **AWQ** models compatibility were improved by implementing new unquant path for Linear to to circumvent ```torch_npu.npu_weight_quant_batchmatmul``` kernel limitations. - **AWQ** MoE now uses 2x times less memory after ```process_weights_after_loading``` redesign. - **Modelslim** now supports mix-bits quantized MoE models (with different w13/w2 quant schemes). - **GGUF** performance were improved by adding npu_format_cast to enable NZ weights format. - **GPTQ** performance and accuracy were improved by using new kernels versions. - **GPTQ** add scales expanded size does not match K_shard warning and support negative-scale correction skipping. - **W4A4 NZ format fix** – the NPU kernel now correctly uses the native NZ memory layout (instead of forced ND), giving up to **5-10% speedup**. - **Improved int4 packing** – support improved int4 packing using ```SGLANG_NPU_W4A4_NEW_PACKING=True``` env variable, two int4 values are now stored in one int8, halving the memory footprint during weight loading. - **def fused_moe_npu()** now deprecated and will be removed in future releases. Reverts https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29503 to avoid performance drops --- ## Accuracy Tests ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 4. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 5. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #29395737061](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29395737061) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #29395736920](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29395736920)

title: Add GB10 FP8 fused MoE Triton config
author: janbernloehr
body:
## Motivation

Add a tuned fused MoE Triton FP8 config for NVIDIA GB10 for the Qwen3 MoE shape `E=128, N=768`.

Without a GB10-specific config, SGLang falls back to the default MoE kernel config for this shape.

## Modifications

Added the Triton 3.6.0 config generated by the fused MoE tuner:

`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/configs/triton_3_6_0/E=128,N=768,device_name=NVIDIA_GB10,dtype=fp8_w8a8.json`

This PR intentionally only adds the tuned config. A separate issue/PR can track tuner behavior for checkpoints whose metadata reports `block_shape: [0, None]`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This PR only adds a fused MoE Triton tuning config and does not change model math or kernel code.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The config was generated on actual NVIDIA GB10 hardware with:

```bash
python3 benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton/tuning_fused_moe_triton.py \
  --model <Qwen3-30B-A3B FP8 ModelOpt checkpoint> \
  --tp-size 1 \
  --dtype fp8_w8a8 \
  --batch-size <batch_size> \
  --tune
```

Observed facts from the benchmark logs:

- GPU: `NVIDIA GB10`
- `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,compute_cap,memory.total`: `NVIDIA GB10, 12.1, [N/A]`
- PyTorch CUDA device name: `NVIDIA GB10`
- CUDA capability from PyTorch: `12.1`
- PyTorch-reported SM count: `48`
- PyTorch-reported total memory: `128495886336`
- `shared_memory_per_block`: `49152`
- `shared_memory_per_block_optin`: `101376`
- `shared_memory_per_multiprocessor`: `102400`
- PyTorch: `2.11.0+cu130`
- Triton: `3.6.0`
- SGLang version under test: `0.0.0.dev1+g688b679af`

The tuner observed this model/config shape:

```json
{
  "architecture": "Qwen3MoeForCausalLM",
  "block_shape": [0, null],
  "dtype": "torch.bfloat16",
  "hidden_size": 2048,
  "num_experts": 128,
  "shard_intermediate_size": 1536,
  "topk": 8
}
```

All default batch sizes completed successfully:

`1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 1536, 2048, 3072, 4096`

The longest tuning job was batch size `4096`; its log ended with:

```text
Tuning took 9659.23 seconds
Completed tuning for batch_size=4096
```

title: [EPD][Perf] Async image preprocessing and cross-request ViT batching for encode_server
author: ntgiang71096
body:
## Motivation

The EPD encoder server (`encode_server.py`) processes image preprocessing
(PIL resize + normalize via `image_processor()`) synchronously on the asyncio
event loop. Under N concurrent requests, all preprocessing is serialized —
each request waits for the previous one to finish. Additionally, after
preprocessing completes, each request triggers its own individual ViT forward
pass rather than batching across concurrent requests arriving at the same time.

## Modifications

### 1. Async image preprocessing (`preproc_executor`)

Moves `image_processor()` calls off the asyncio event loop into a dedicated
`ThreadPoolExecutor` via `run_in_executor`. N concurrent requests now
preprocess images in parallel without blocking request acceptance or each other.

A separate executor (`preproc_executor`) is used instead of the existing
`self.executor` (which handles ZMQ sends) to prevent contention under high
concurrency.

Configurable via `SGLANG_ENCODER_PREPROC_WORKERS` (default: 8).

### 2. Cross-request ViT batching (`_vit_batch_loop`)

Adds an asyncio queue (`_vit_queue`) and a background coroutine
(`_vit_batch_loop`) that collects concurrently preprocessed images and runs
them as a single batched ViT forward pass instead of N separate ones.

**Adaptive sleep:** when the queue already has items the loop yields
immediately (`asyncio.sleep(0)`); it only waits `SGLANG_ENCODER_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS`
(default: 20 ms) when the queue is empty, avoiding unnecessary latency for
staggered arrivals while still allowing batch accumulation.

Configurable via:
- `SGLANG_ENCODER_BATCH_SIZE` (default: 8) — max requests per ViT batch
- `SGLANG_ENCODER_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS` (default: 20) — batch accumulation window

Unit tests added in `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_encode_server_perf.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

No change to model outputs. Preprocessing and ViT inference are unchanged;
only the scheduling of when they execute changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Benchmarked with `sglang.bench_serving` on AMD MI355X, Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, EPD 1E1P.
`output_len=1` isolates the encoder path (preprocessing + ViT + ZMQ + PD prefill); no decode pressure — metric is end-to-end request latency.

```bash
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \
    --backend sglang \
    --host 127.0.0.1 \
    --port <pd_port> \
    --model Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \
    --dataset-name image \
    --image-count 8 \
    --image-resolution 720p \
    --num-prompts 100 \
    --random-input-len 128 \
    --random-output-len 1 \
    --max-concurrency 16
```

Encoder env (as measured): `SGLANG_ENCODER_BATCH_SIZE=16`. Note: `SGLANG_ENCODER_PREPROC_WORKERS` was at its then-default of 32, but `--max-concurrency 16` caps in-flight requests, so effective preproc parallelism is 16 — any value ≥16 reproduces these numbers. The default is now **8** (per @ShangmingCai review): for this workload that means ~2 preprocessing waves instead of 1, still well clear of stock's 16-wide event-loop serialization (the source of the gain). Tunable via the env var.

| Config | Median E2E Latency | Throughput | vs Stock |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Stock (no patch) | 5,820 ms | 2.59 req/s | — |
| This PR | 4,705 ms | 3.19 req/s | **−19% latency, +23% tput** |

Both changes are platform-agnostic (standard Python asyncio + `concurrent.futures`).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). — ran `pre-commit run --all-files`, all hooks passed.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — added 5 tests in `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_encode_server_perf.py` covering async preprocessing concurrency and ViT batch queue correctness.
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no existing docs page for `encode_server` configuration; the three new env vars (`SGLANG_ENCODER_BATCH_SIZE`, `SGLANG_ENCODER_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS`, `SGLANG_ENCODER_PREPROC_WORKERS`) are documented in the Modifications section above.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — accuracy unaffected (no change to model outputs); speed results provided in Speed Tests section.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). — covered by pre-commit (Black, Ruff, isort, codespell).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

cc @ShangmingCai @liusy58 @ZhengWG @gty111 @ByronHsu @hnyls2002 @mickqian

---

## Update 2026-05-26: Scope narrowed to async preprocessing only

Per reviewer feedback from @liusy58, this PR is narrowed to keep only the
async preprocessing change. Cross-request ViT batching is dropped because
PR #25964 covers it at a coarser layer (its `EncoderScheduler` +
`batch_encode` fuses the HF processor call too). The two changes compose:
async preprocessing keeps the event loop free so #25964's batch worker
actually sees concurrent requests, instead of seeing them arrive
one-at-a-time after each blocking processor call.

**Removed:** `_vit_queue` / `_vit_task` / `_vit_batch_loop` /
`_ensure_vit_batch_loop`, `SGLANG_ENCODER_BATCH_SIZE` and
`SGLANG_ENCODER_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS` env vars, `TestViTBatchQueue` test class
(4 tests).

**Kept:** `preproc_executor`, `SGLANG_ENCODER_PREPROC_WORKERS`
(now in `sglang.srt.environ`, default 8), `run_in_executor` wrapping for
image / video / audio preprocessing.

### Performance note

The narrowed scope does **not** lose measurable perf on this benchmark.
The "This PR" row was measured with ViT batching included. Re-measuring
the same workload with ViT batching removed (async preprocessing only)
gives −18% lat / +26% tput — essentially the same as the table row,
within run-to-run noise. The current benchmark setup doesn't exercise
the ViT-batching improvement enough to show a distinguishable delta.

### Inline review threads
- @ZhengWG: apply `run_in_executor` to video/audio paths — **kept** in this PR.

title: [MoE Refactor] deprecate forward_npu and NpuFuseEPMoE
author: ch-wan
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Continues the MoE refactor roadmap (#8715). Deprecates `DeepEPMoE.forward_npu` and the `NpuFuseEPMoE` class so the NPU paths fit the unified `FusedMoE.forward` → `dispatcher.dispatch` → `quant_method.apply` → `dispatcher.combine` pipeline. Tracks the roadmap items:

- [ ] `DeepEPMoE.forward_*` → `npu.py` + `fp8.py`
- [ ] `unquant.py` → `npu.py`

## Modifications

Follows the mega_moe pattern (free-function bypass + quant_method weight hook) rather than introducing a new dispatcher/format.

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/ep_moe/layer.py`
  - Set `deprecate_flag = True` for `_is_npu` in `DeepEPMoE.__init__` so NPU + DeepEP routes through `FusedMoE.forward_impl` / `quant_method.apply`.
  - Delete `DeepEPMoE.forward_npu` and the `NpuFuseEPMoE` class.
  - `get_moe_impl_class` returns `FusedMoE` for `ascend_fuseep`.
  - Drop the `FusedMoEMode` / `npu_format_cast` imports that only `NpuFuseEPMoE` used.

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py`
  - Fold `ascend_fuseep` into the `StandardDispatcher` branch of `create_moe_dispatcher` (alongside `is_none()` and `is_megamoe()`); the dispatcher is created but never invoked.
  - Cache `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_ascend_fuseep()` as `self._use_ascend_fuseep` in `FusedMoE.__init__`.
  - `FusedMoE.forward` early-returns to `forward_fuseep(self, hidden_states, topk_output)` when that flag is set. The early return happens before `forward_impl`, so the `use_symmetric_memory` context / slice / optional all-reduce are intentionally bypassed — matching the old `NpuFuseEPMoE.forward`.

- `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/fuseep.py` (new)
  - `forward_fuseep` — free function that drives the fused dispatch+GEMM+combine via `DeepEPBuffer.fused_deep_moe`. Mirrors the old `NpuFuseEPDispatcher.dispatch` call sequence (same group, `_PARAMS_BYTES = 2` for bf16, `DeepEPMode.LOW_LATENCY`, env reads, weight kwargs).
  - `process_fuseep_weights` — FuseEP-specific weight reshape/permute/int64-scale logic that used to live in `NpuFuseEPMoE._process_weights_after_loading`.

- `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/fused_moe_method_npu.py`
  - Module-level `maybe_apply_deepep_npu(quant_method, layer, dispatch_output)` absorbs the old `forward_npu` per-format dispatch logic and calls `quant_method.apply_without_routing_weights`.
  - Module-level `maybe_apply_fuseep_weights(layer)` delegates to `process_fuseep_weights` when `is_ascend_fuseep()`.
  - All four NPU MoE methods (`NPUW4A4Int4`, `NPUW8A8Int8`, `NPUW4A8Int8`, `NPUW4A16Int4`) call `_maybe_apply_deepep` at the top of `apply` so DeepEP dispatch outputs are intercepted.
  - **Only `NPUW8A8Int8DynamicMoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading` calls `_maybe_apply_fuseep_weights`.** The FUSED_DEEP_MOE kernel only supports W8A8 INT8 ([FUSED_DEEP_MOE_CN.md](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/blob/0ff3be0094b7dcebcd446042c48f72259bc70b27/python/deep_ep/doc/FUSED_DEEP_MOE_CN.md)) — restricting the gate to W8A8 prevents silent wrong-output if a user combines `ascend_fuseep` with an unsupported quant. Per NPU maintainer feedback ([#25678 (comment)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25678#discussion_r3264992853)).

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py`
  - `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod.forward_npu` adds a `_forward_npu_deepep` branch for the bf16-unquantized DeepEP case, calling `npu_fused_moe_without_routing_weights_bf16` (the same path the old `forward_npu`'s `w13_weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16` branch used). Annotates `dispatch_output` as `DispatchOutput` since both Standard and DeepEP formats are now valid.

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py`
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelslim/modelslim.py`
  - **Unchanged.** Wrapper-level hooks are not needed: `CompressedTensorsFusedMoEMethod.apply` → `scheme.apply_weights` → `kernel.apply` and `process_weights_after_loading` → `scheme.process_weights_after_loading` → `kernel.process_weights_after_loading` already fire the NPU kernel's gates (where `kernel` is one of the four NPU MoE methods above). Same for ModelSlim. An earlier revision added wrapper-level hooks; reverted in e8897eac0 per maintainer feedback ([#25678 (comment)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25678#discussion_r3265176447)).

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/{__init__.py, fuseep.py}`
  - Delete `NpuFuseEPDispatcher`, `FuseEPDispatchOutput`, `FuseEPCombineInput` and their re-exports; fuseep no longer goes through the dispatcher abstraction.

## Accuracy Tests

Not yet validated on NPU hardware — relying on NPU CI and reviewers with Ascend access.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not yet measured. NPU + DeepEP paths now route through `FusedMoE.forward_impl`, which (relative to the deleted `DeepEPMoE.forward_impl`) adds `use_symmetric_memory` context, slice-to-`origin_hidden_states_dim`, and optional `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce`. For typical DeepEP layers these are no-ops (`reduce_results=False`, symmetric memory disabled by default, no hidden-size padding), matching the deepgemm deprecation in #12054. The `ascend_fuseep` path early-returns from `FusedMoE.forward` before `forward_impl`, so none of those ops run on it.

title: [Quantization][Bugfix]: Join multi-arg RuntimeError in Quark _check_scheme_supported
author: spandantiwari
body:
## Motivation

`QuarkConfig._check_scheme_supported` raises a capability-mismatch error like this:

```python
raise RuntimeError(
    "Quantization scheme is not supported for ",
    f"the current GPU. Min capability: {min_capability}. ",
    f"Current capability: {capability}.",
)
```

That passes **three positional arguments** to `RuntimeError`. `Exception.__str__` formats `self.args` as a tuple repr when `len(args) != 1`, so the message the user actually sees today is the tuple-stringified mess on the left, not the intended sentence on the right:

| Today (buggy) | After this PR |
|---|---|
| `('Quantization scheme is not supported for ', 'the current GPU. Min capability: 200. ', 'Current capability: 70.')` | `Quantization scheme is not supported for the current GPU. Min capability: 200. Current capability: 70.` |

Parens, quoted fragments, and quote-comma joins all leak through — what looked like three message fragments meant to be concatenated were instead stored as three separate `args` entries.

## Modifications

**`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py:187-192`** — replace the three-argument call with a single message built via adjacent string-literal concatenation. The diff is a two-character semantic change (drop two commas) plus a short clarifying comment:

```python
raise RuntimeError(
    "Quantization scheme is not supported for "
    f"the current GPU. Min capability: {min_capability}. "
    f"Current capability: {capability}."
)
```

No other code paths in the function change.

**`test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_quark_config.py`** (new) — CPU-only regression test registered to `base-a-test-cpu` (`est_time=5`). Six cases:

| Test | Purpose | On unfixed code |
|---|---|---|
| `test_error_is_single_argument` | structural — asserts `len(err.args) == 1` | **fails** (gets 3 args) |
| `test_error_message_renders_as_sentence` | rejects leading `(` and quote-comma fragment joins | **fails** |
| `test_error_message_content` | substring sanity check on the rendered message | passes either way |
| `test_unsupported_returns_false_when_error_disabled` | guardrail for `error=False` branch | passes |
| `test_supported_returns_true` | guardrail for the `supported` path | passes |
| `test_no_device_returns_false` | guardrail for `get_device_capability() is None` | passes |

The test mocks `sglang.srt.layers.quantization.quark.quark.get_device_capability` and uses `QuarkConfig.__new__(QuarkConfig)` to skip `__init__` (the method under test reads no instance attributes).

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — this is an error-formatting fix. It does not touch quantization math, kernel selection, or any model-output code path. The exception is raised only on the unsupported-capability branch; values returned by `_check_scheme_supported` (`True` / `False`) are unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A — no kernel changes, no hot-path modifications. The change is to an exception-construction expression that only fires on a fatal-startup error.

title: Expose can-run-cuda-graph as a regular property on the embedding result
author: fzyzcjy
body:
``EmbeddingBatchResult`` did not declare a ``can_run_cuda_graph`` field,
so ``process_batch_result_prefill`` used ``getattr(result,
"can_run_cuda_graph", False)`` to read it across the
``Union[GenerationBatchResult, EmbeddingBatchResult]`` prefill result
type. Embedding forward never runs through a CUDA graph, so the
fallback always resolved to ``False`` -- make this explicit on the
type instead of leaving it implicit via ``getattr`` tolerance.

Expose ``can_run_cuda_graph`` as a ``@property`` on
``EmbeddingBatchResult`` that always returns ``False`` (no underlying
storage needed since the value is invariant for this type), and
rewrite the callsite to ``result.can_run_cuda_graph`` direct access.

title: [AMD] Bump amd/Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4 revision to align with shared-experts fusion
author: yctseng0211
body: ## Motivation After PR25390 enabled shared-experts fusion for Kimi-K2.5 (`n_routed_experts=384`) on the AMD path, `test_kimi_k25_mxfp4.py` started failing at weight load: ``` RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (3584) must match the size of tensor b (7168) at non-singleton dimension 1 File ".../layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 492, in _load_w13 expert_data.copy_(loaded_weight) ``` The root cause is that the currently pinned revision (`b071bc6f`, set in #22188) keeps the shared experts **unquantized**: ```json // config.json @ b071bc6f "exclude": [ "lm_head", "re:.*self_attn.*", "re:.*shared_experts.*", // shared_experts -> bf16 "re:.*mlp\\.(gate|up|gate_up|down)_proj.*", ... ] ``` When the fusion path renames `mlp.shared_experts.*` → `mlp.experts.384.*` and tries to copy the bf16 (unpacked hidden dim) shared-expert weight into the MXFP4 (uint8-packed hidden dim) routed-experts slot, the dim-1 sizes don't match (`3584 = hidden/2` vs `7168 = hidden`), and `_load_w13` crashes. The HF repo already shipped a fix on 2026-04-01 (commit `94d8c1bd` — *"quantize mlp.up_proj, mlp.down_proj, shared_experts"*) that quantizes the shared experts to MXFP4, but the test pin was never moved forward, so PR25390's fusion path always runs against a checkpoint it cannot load. ## Modifications - Bump `KIMI_K25_MXFP4_REVISION` from `b071bc6f8eb042e093e14f3b8bdbad71c18e09d3` → `419004c8716cf22c929aa15d39b85e09a8a2091a` (current HF `main` HEAD; identical safetensors to `94d8c1bd`, only README updates + `quark_profile.yaml` deletion in between). - Add an inline comment so future revision bumps don't accidentally regress below `94d8c1bd`. ### Why this revision is safe Verified directly against the HF `model.safetensors.index.json` at each revision — MXFP4 weight scales for shared experts only exist from `94d8c1bd` onward: | Revision | `shared_experts.*.weight_scale` entries | shared_experts dtype | |---|---|---| | `b071bc6f` (old pin) | 0 | bf16 | | `94d8c1bd` (HF fix) | 180 (60 MoE layers × {gate, up, down}) | MXFP4 (uint8) | | `419004c8` (new pin / main HEAD) | 180 | MXFP4 (uint8) | After the bump, both sides of the fusion `expert_data.copy_(loaded_weight)` have matching dtype/shape, so the new fusion path enabled in PR25390 loads cleanly. This is also the minimum-risk fix: the AMD CI keeps a single pinned rev ## Accuracy Tests https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26075873213 ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. title: loader: yield filtered MTP weights lazily to avoid OOM hang on multi-layer EAGLE
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Summary

`DefaultModelLoader._filter_mtp_weights` was materializing the entire filtered checkpoint into a `tuple` before returning, which defeated the bounded sliding-window in `buffered_multi_thread_safetensors_weights_iterator` (`buffer_size = max_workers + 1`).

With multi-layer EAGLE on large MoE checkpoints (e.g. MiMo-V2.5-Pro, ~963 GiB fp8), each TP rank instantiates `speculative_num_steps` draft runners (each with its own `draft_model_idx`), and every runner independently re-scans the full checkpoint. The eager `tuple(filtered_weights)` held the full prefix-renamed payload resident on CPU per runner — at TP=8 with 3 draft runners that's enough live tensors per host to push it into page reclaim. The visible symptom was:

- All scheduler threads stuck on `futex_do_wait`
- `/proc/<pid>/io read_bytes = 0`, no `rchar` growth
- No progress past `Found local HF snapshot ... skipping download.`
- Identical on virtiofs and local NVMe (rules out storage)

Switching to a generator preserves behavior (callers already iterate the result; sibling `_get_weights_iterator` paths already return generators) while letting the buffered upstream actually bound CPU memory.

## Test plan

Tested on 8× B200 with MiMo-V2.5-Pro (~963 GiB fp8) and the default `enable_multithread_load=True`:

| | before (default `enable_multithread_load=True`) | after (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Server ready | **hangs indefinitely** (all sched in `futex_do_wait`) | ~2.5 min |
| GSM8K (200, parallel=4) | n/a (hung) | score 0.97 |
| avg accept_rate | n/a | 0.755 (over 307 batches) |
| avg accept_length | n/a | 3.27 (max 4) |
| gen throughput | n/a | ~700 tok/s |

Behaviour with the previous `--model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load":false}'` workaround is unchanged: same accept_rate (0.753 → 0.755), same GSM8K score (0.975 → 0.97 — within noise), but server is now ~30 % faster to ready because the multi-thread loader is actually live.

Launch:
\`\`\`bash
export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
sglang serve --trust-remote-code --model-path XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5-Pro --tp 8 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm --attention-backend fa4 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --max-running-requests 128 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --enable-multi-layer-eagle \
  --reasoning-parser mimo --tool-call-parser mimo \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
\`\`\`
