title: [Kernel] Add SM90 Q8KV8 FP8 Sparse MLA Prefill JIT Kernel with Tests and Benchmark
author: JackChuang
body:
# Summary
This PR adds a Q8KV8 FP8 sparse MLA prefill JIT kernel for SM90, together with its Python wrapper, correctness/accuracy tests, and performance benchmark.

This PR is part of the roadmap tracked in #25746 (PR1 of 2).

# Takeaways
- **Performance**: Q8KV8 is **1.15x - 1.31x faster** than the Q16/BF16 FlashMLA sparse prefill baseline on representative long-context sparse MLA shapes.
- **Kernel correctness**: Q8KV8 matches the dequantized-FP8 FP32 reference with **~0.7% rel_mean error**, validating the intended FP8 computation path.
- **Precision tradeoff**: Compared with the Q16/KV16 sparse prefill path, Q8KV8 shows an expected **~2.8% accuracy drop**, mainly from BF16-to-FP8 Q/K/V quantization.


# Motivation
<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
Sparse MLA prefill becomes a major contributor to long-context latency. FlashMLA already lowers KV to FP8 for this kernel while keeping Q in BF16/FP16; promoting Q to FP8 (Q8KV8) closes the remaining precision gap, unlocking full FP8 tensor-core throughput and halving Q-side memory traffic at long context.

The kernel is kept under `sglang.jit_kernel` so it can be reviewed, tested, and benchmarked as a standalone kernel before any future runtime integration.

# Context
See the project roadmap and tracking issue: #25746. This PR delivers **PR1** of that roadmap — a standalone, independently reviewable kernel building block. PR2 will build on the merged kernel API to wire it into the NSA prefill backend and report end-to-end serving gains.

# Modifications
<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
Included in this PR:
- An SM90 Q8KV8 sparse MLA prefill CUDA C++ kernel using CUTLASS/CuTe primitives and native Hopper FP8 GMMA
- Python JIT wrapper under `sglang.jit_kernel`
- Accuracy & correctness tests under `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests`
- Performance benchmark under `python/sglang/jit_kernel/benchmark`

## Kernel Implementation
The kernel is a SM90 implementation of FP8 sparse MLA prefill, with an algorithm inspired by DeepSeek FlashMLA but rewritten for the Q8KV8 path.
- **Native FP8 attention on Hopper.** Both QK and PV are issued as native FP8 GMMA on SM90. There is no on-the-fly BF16 dequant on the inner loop, so the kernel benefits directly from Hopper's higher FP8 throughput and lower KV memory traffic.
- **Producer / consumer pipeline.** A producer stage streams FP8 KV from gmem into shared memory and prepares it for the PV GMMA, while consumer stages run QK, online softmax, and PV. This keeps memory movement and compute overlapped on the critical path.
- **Specialized for the sparse MLA prefill shape.** The kernel is built around `d_v = 512`, `h_kv = 1`, and the two query/key head dimensions used in practice (`d_qk = 512` and `d_qk = 576`, the latter matching the V3.2-style `nope + rope` layout). Sparse indexing is aligned to the kernel's tile granularity.
- **Compile-time specialization for optional features.** `d_qk`, `attn_sink`, and per-row `topk_length` are compile-time switches, so the common no-sink path stays branch-free while the full path still supports `attn_sink` and `topk_length` when callers need them.
- **BF16 output with FP32 softmax metadata.** The kernel returns the BF16 attention output together with per-row `max_logits` and `lse`, matching the sparse MLA prefill API and preserving the softmax metadata needed for correctness checks and numerically stable merging of partial attention results in downstream attention paths.
- **Python integration.** The kernel is exposed via a JIT-loaded wrapper under `sglang.jit_kernel`. The wrapper caches the resolved entry points and output buffers, and registers each dispatch path as a `custom_op` so calls integrate with `torch.library` / `torch.compile` and the existing kernel API logging.

# Experimental Results
## Performance Benchmark
<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->
The benchmark checks CI regressions and real NSA serving throughput gains. Cases are split into two groups. The CI-sized group provides a lightweight end-to-end smoke check that runs quickly in CI and confirms the kernel produces a measurable result without requiring a full-scale context. The long-context group targets the actual NSA prefill scenario — large batch size, long KV sequence, and substantial topk — where native FP8 GMMA throughput and reduced KV bandwidth are expected to have the largest impact. All cases `d_v = 512`, `h_kv = 1`, and both `d_qk` variants (`512` and `576`) are covered.

The baseline is the existing Q16/BF16 FlashMLA sparse prefill path (`sgl_kernel.flash_mla.flash_mla_sparse_fwd`), representing a production NSA deployment, and all speedup numbers reflect the direct like-for-like latency improvement from switching to the Q8KV8 path on the same hardware.

**Reproduction:**
```
PYTHONPATH=python python3 python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_sparse_mla_q8kv8_prefill_sm90.py
```

**CI-sized (regression smoke) results:**
CI-sized cases (`s_q = 2`) are small enough for fast regression smoke runs and verify the kernel produces a measurable result without the full context. 



Shape `(s_q, s_kv, h_q, d_qk, topk)` | Q16/BF16 FlashMLA | Q8KV8 FP8 JIT | Speedup
-- | -- | -- | --
`(2, 1024, 64, 512, 128)` | 16.576 us | 11.776 us | 1.407x
`(2, 1024, 64, 576, 128)` | 15.072 us | 12.000 us | 1.256x

**Representative long-context results:**
The larger long-context cases (`s_q = 4096`, `s_kv` up to 65536, `topk` up to 2048) represent the actual NSA prefill workload where reduced KV bandwidth and native FP8 execution are expected to matter most; these shapes cover both the `d_qk = 576` (V3.2-style nope+rope) and `d_qk = 512` head dimension variants.


Shape `(s_q, s_kv, h_q, d_qk, topk)` | Q16/BF16 FlashMLA | Q8KV8 FP8 JIT | Speedup
-- | -- | -- | --
`(4096, 8192, 128, 576, 2048)` | 3489.74 us | 3039.23 us | 1.148x
`(4096, 32768, 128, 576, 2048)` | 4138.08 us | 3162.14 us | 1.309x
`(4096, 65536, 128, 576, 2048)` | 4385.41 us | 3372.99 us | 1.300x
`(4096, 8192, 64, 512, 512)` | 602.82 us | 487.97 us | 1.235x
`(4096, 32768, 64, 512, 512)` | 602.46 us | 518.16 us | 1.163x

The Q8KV8 kernel is consistently faster across all tested configurations, with speedups ranging from **1.15x** to **1.41x**. The gains grow with sequence length and topk size, which is the expected pattern: at longer context the kernel spends more time in the inner loop where native FP8 GMMA throughput and reduced KV traffic have the largest impact. This aligns with the primary motivation for this kernel — improving sparse MLA prefill latency in long-context NSA workloads.

## Correctness and Accuracy Tests
<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->
The correctness and accuracy tests are designed to validate two things: first, that the CUDA kernel correctly implements the intended Q8KV8 sparse MLA computation; second, that the expected numerical tradeoff versus the existing Q16/KV16 path is understood and bounded.

For kernel correctness, the Q8KV8 output is compared against a PyTorch FP32 sparse-attention reference that dequantizes the same FP8 Q/K/V tensors. This isolates kernel implementation error from the BF16-to-FP8 quantization error.

All cases use `d_v = 512` and `h_kv = 1`, matching the sparse MLA layout targeted by this PR.


Group | Cases | What It Covers
-- | -- | --
Basic no-sink correctness | 2 | Both supported head dimensions, `d_qk = 512` and `d_qk = 576`, through the common no-sink path used as the current NSA E2E proxy
Sink / topk_length feature coverage | 4 | The full dispatch path with `attn_sink` and per-row `topk_length`, including minimal query count, multiple query rows, and larger topk/KV sizes
Cross-shape corner coverage | 2 | Non-trivial query counts and larger sparse shapes for both `d_qk = 512` and `d_qk = 576`, including non-small `s_q` cases that exercise more CTA scheduling patterns
Precision-focused no-sink coverage | 4 | Larger no-sink cases for both head dimensions, used to report aggregate precision metrics on the path closest to current NSA serving behavior

**Reproduction and results:**
```
$ PYTHONPATH=python python3 python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_sparse_mla_q8kv8_prefill_sm90.py
12 / 12 passed

max_diff   ≤ 1.80e-04
p99_diff   ≤ 8.14e-05
mean_diff  ~  2e-05
rel_mean   ~  0.71% - 0.73%
cos_diff   ~  2.7e-05
fail_rate  = 0%
```

**Q8KV8 kernel vs dequantized-FP8 FP32 reference results:**
The **~0.7% relative mean error** measures the kernel implementation error for the intended FP8 path: both the CUDA kernel and the PyTorch reference consume the same FP8 inputs, with the reference dequantizing them to FP32 before computing sparse attention. This shows the CUDA kernel closely matches the expected Q8KV8 computation.

### Accuracy Test: Q8KV8 vs. Q16/KV16 Sparse Prefill Precision Tradeoff
We compare the Q8KV8 path against the existing Q16/KV16 sparse prefill kernel to quantify the expected precision tradeoff when switching from the BF16/Q16 path to the FP8 Q8KV8 path. The observed accuracy drop is about **2.8%**, which is expected for an FP8 attention path.
This gap is mainly introduced by BF16-to-FP8 quantization of Q/K/V before attention, then amplified through QK softmax and PV accumulation. The Q8KV8 kernel therefore trades a small numerical drop for consistent latency gains on the sparse MLA prefill workloads targeted by this PR, and the result should be interpreted together with the latency gains reported in the benchmark section.

title: [Fix][NPU] Preserve existing packed_modules_mapping when merging model-level fused module mappings
author: litmei
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Commit abe2ec2af introduced a direct assignment in `DeepseekV2ForCausalLM.__init__` that overwrites `quant_config.packed_modules_mapping`. Before the overwrite, the dict (pre-populated by the weight loader for ModelSlim) has a nested structure:

```python
{
    "visual": {...},
    "vision_model": {...},
    "model": {"fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa": ["q_a_proj", "kv_a_proj_with_mqa"], ...},
}
```

After the overwrite, it is replaced with the model's flat dict:

```python
{"fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa": ["q_a_proj", "kv_a_proj_with_mqa"]}
```

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

Replace direct assignment ( = ) with `.update()` when using modelslim.

## Motivation

This is a rebase commit from the upstream branch.
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23724
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21741

We found that the DeepSeek-V4 mxfp4 version adopts quantization with a group size of 32, while Wint4A16 and Wint4AFP8 usually use a group size of 128 for quantization. After multiple tests, we confirmed that adopting either 128 or 32 for Wint4A16 brings no significant accuracy difference to the model. In contrast, Wint4AFP8 relies on Cutlass implementation and currently only supports the quantization configuration with a group size of 128.


coauther @guzekai01

title: perf(dsv4): add MHC token-count prewarm
author: YAMY1234
body: ## Motivation DeepSeek V4 MHC pre can hit a large one-time cold cost when a rare token-count bucket first enters the server process. In internal DSV4 profiling runs, the long 20-40s forward stalls aligned with first-seen MHC pre split buckets in sparse mixed/decode tail. This patch moves that first-hit cost into startup warmup so live traffic and benchmark measurement do not pay it at the tail. ## Changes - Add an optional model-level kernel warmup hook in `ModelRunner.kernel_warmup()`, before CUDA graph capture. - Implement the DeepSeek V4 MHC prewarm in the DeepSeek V4 model, keeping model-specific logic out of `ModelRunner`. - Gate the hook narrowly to DeepSeek V4 + hybrid SWA + `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=1` + `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=1`. - Infer the warmup range from the normalized `server_args.chunked_prefill_size`; if it is unset or invalid, fall back to `8192`. - Compute one representative token count per MHC pre split bucket under that range, instead of requiring users to manually provide token counts. - Run both attention and FFN `hc_pre` paths on one local DeepSeek V4 decoder layer for each representative token-count bucket. - Expose the MHC prewarm path through the DeepSeek V4 NextN wrapper so the inherited model hook can handle that runtime path as well. ## Notes for reviewers - There is no new user-facing environment variable in the final version. The prewarm range follows the same `chunked_prefill_size` budget used by serving. - With DP attention enabled, `ServerArgs` already normalizes `chunked_prefill_size` by `dp_size`, so `ModelRunner` sees the local per-DP-rank token budget and should not divide it again. - Warming one local decoder layer is enough for this purpose because the MHC pre kernel shape is determined by token count and hidden shape, not by layer-specific weights. ## Accuracy Full GSM8K validation on a B300 DeepSeek V4-Pro DP-attention mixed-chunk setup. The run did not set any `SGLANG_DSV4_MHC_PREWARM_*` env; the prewarm range was derived from `chunked_prefill_size`. Representative setup: ```bash export SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE=1 export SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=2048 export SGLANG_EXPERIMENTAL_ENABLE_PIECEWISE_CUDA_GRAPH_MOE_A2A=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_NORM=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_INDEXER_METADATA=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_V2=1 export SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0 export SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_FAST_WARMUP=1 python3 -m dynamo.sglang \ --model-path /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 6100 \ --trust-remote-code \ --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \ --max-prefill-tokens 16384 \ --enable-mixed-chunk \ --context-length 16384 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --data-parallel-size 8 \ --expert-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --moe-a2a-backend deepep \ --deepep-config '{"normal_dispatch":{"num_sms":96},"normal_combine":{"num_sms":96}}' \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 544 \ --max-running-requests 4352 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.835 \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.075 \ --stream-interval 30 \ --tokenizer-worker-num 1 \ --watchdog-timeout 86400 ``` With DP attention, the global `--chunked-prefill-size 16384` is normalized by DP size 8, so each local DP rank sees `max_num_tokens=2048` for this warmup. The worker log confirmed the local prewarm range and representative buckets: ```text Running DeepSeek V4 MHC prewarm for max_num_tokens=2048 DeepSeek V4 MHC prewarm max_num_tokens=2048 representative token counts: (2048, 1856, 1536, 1344, 1152, 1024, 896, 832, 768, 704, 640, 576, 512, 448, 384, 320, 256, 192, 128, 64) DeepSeek V4 MHC prewarm path=attn num_tokens=2048 completed in 28.551s DeepSeek V4 MHC prewarm path=attn num_tokens=64 completed in 28.014s Capture cuda graph end. Time elapsed: 247.96 s. ``` Full GSM8K benchmark output: ```text GSM8K Config: endpoint=http://localhost:8000; num_examples=1319; max_tokens=2048; num_threads=512; num_shots=8; temperature=default; top_p=default; top_k=default Running GSM8K evaluation... Total latency: 131.544 s Score: 0.969 Output throughput: 4405.387 token/s [METRIC] gsm8k_score=0.9687261632341724 labels={"model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro", "eval": "gsm8k"} [METRIC] gsm8k_latency=131.54371510795318 labels={"model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro", "eval": "gsm8k"} {'score:std': np.float64(0.17405684100250698), 'score': np.float64(0.9687261632341724), 'latency': 131.54371510795318, 'output_throughput': 4405.3872092971105} GSM8K evaluation complete ``` ## Benchmark Before: After: Total TPS/GPU from 9266.78 to 9644.40 under conc=2048 on B300 --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #26182953200](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26182953200) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #26182953180](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26182953180)

title: [Refactor] Encapsulate SWA loc translation inside SWAKVPool with per-batch cache invalidation
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

Removes the \`set_swa_loc\` side channel from \`SWAKVPool\` and makes the pool translate \`out_cache_loc\` to SWA pool indices internally, with a memoised per-batch cache.

**Before**: callers pre-set \`pool.swa_loc\` before each \`set_kv_buffer\`, and \`out_cache_loc_swa\` was a pre-computed field on \`ForwardBatch\` that needed to be sliced and threaded through every graph runner.

**After**: \`SWAKVPool.set_kv_buffer\` calls \`translate_loc_from_full_to_swa(loc)\` directly.

### Design

The translation follows a **prepare → fallback** pattern:

1. **Preparation** — \`invalidate_loc_cache()\` is called once per batch before the model forward (in \`_forward_raw()\` and at the top of every \`run_once()\`). This resets the cache so the upcoming forward sees a clean slate.

2. **Translation as fallback** — \`translate_loc_from_full_to_swa()\` fires lazily on the first SWA-layer access within the forward. It computes the gather, stores the result keyed on \`(data_ptr, numel)\`, and every subsequent SWA layer in the same pass gets an O(1) cache hit. The translation is never eagerly pre-computed — it only runs if a SWA layer is actually reached.

This means \`invalidate_loc_cache()\` is the **contract boundary**: callers that mutate \`full_to_swa_index_mapping\` (all seven allocator methods) call it immediately so the next translation sees the updated mapping.

### Cache-key choice

The key is \`(data_ptr(), numel)\` rather than \`untyped_storage().data_ptr()\`:  \`data_ptr()\` encodes the slice offset within the storage, so \`out_cache_loc[:real_n]\` (created each layer in piecewise / extend paths) correctly hits the cache from the first layer, while two views at different offsets that happen to have the same storage base are correctly treated as distinct inputs.

### CUDA graph safety

\`run_once()\` invalidates at its top before each warmup and capture invocation. Without this, warmup-1 would populate the Python-level cache and the capture run would get a cache hit — the gather kernel would never be recorded in the graph, and every replay would silently reuse the stale warmup-1 SWA indices.

This is especially important for \`eagle_draft_extend\` and \`multi_layer_eagle_draft_extend\`, which call \`model.forward()\` directly and bypass \`_forward_raw()\`, so they have no other invalidation point.

### Other changes

- **\`BaseSWAKVPool.invalidate_loc_cache()\`** is a no-op default — subclasses that don't cache (\`DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool\`) inherit it safely.
- **\`swa_out_cache_loc\` removed** from \`MultiLayerEagleDraftExtendInputBuffers\` — it was the pre-translated buffer fed via the now-removed \`ForwardBatch.out_cache_loc_swa\` field and had no consumer after this refactor.

## Modifications

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| \`mem_cache/base_swa_memory_pool.py\` | Add no-op \`invalidate_loc_cache()\`; remove abstract \`set_swa_loc\` |
| \`mem_cache/swa_memory_pool.py\` | Core: \`(data_ptr, numel)\` cache + invalidation in 7 allocator sites; remove \`set_swa_loc\` / \`swa_loc\` |
| \`mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py\` | Remove \`set_swa_loc\` no-op (base-class default covers it) |
| \`model_executor/forward_batch_info.py\` | Remove \`out_cache_loc_swa\` field |
| \`model_executor/model_runner.py\` | Call \`invalidate_loc_cache()\` once per forward; remove \`set_swa_loc\` |
| \`model_executor/cuda_graph_runner.py\` | \`run_once()\`: invalidate + remove \`out_cache_loc_swa\` buffers |
| \`model_executor/piecewise_cuda_graph_runner.py\` | Same |
| \`model_executor/breakable_cuda_graph_runner.py\` | Same |
| \`layers/radix_attention.py\` | Remove \`out_cache_loc_swa\` narrow/restore; remove \`set_swa_loc\` calls |
| \`layers/radix_linear_attention.py\` | Same |
| \`layers/attention/triton_backend.py\` | Remove \`swa_loc is not None\` fast-path; always use \`translate_loc_from_full_to_swa\` |
| \`layers/attention/trtllm_mha_backend.py\` | Remove \`out_cache_loc_swa\` fast path; call \`translate_loc_from_full_to_swa\` directly |
| \`speculative/eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py\` | Add \`invalidate_loc_cache()\` in \`run_once()\` |
| \`speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py\` | Same (bypasses \`_forward_raw()\`) |
| \`speculative/frozen_kv_mtp_cuda_graph_runner.py\` | Same |
| \`speculative/multi_layer_eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py\` | Same; remove dead \`swa_out_cache_loc\` buffer |
| \`test/manual/core/test_swa_loc_translation_cache.py\` | New: unit tests for cache-key correctness, allocator-mutation invalidation, and base-class no-op |

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — no computation change on the default path.

## Summary

- Route CUDA `concat_mla_k` / `concat_mla_absorb_q` runtime call sites through `sglang.jit_kernel.concat_mla`.
- Keep the MUSA `concat_mla_k` path on the existing `sgl_kernel` AOT implementation.
- Remove the unused JIT `downcast_fp8` wrapper, CUDA header, and JIT-only benchmark.
- Keep `mla_kv_pack_quantize_fp8` and MXFP8 JIT kernels untouched.

## Rationale

`concat_mla` already has a JIT implementation with JIT-vs-AOT coverage. The CUDA runtime paths can use that implementation directly, reducing active dependency on the duplicate AOT CUDA op while leaving the MUSA AOT path intact.

`downcast_fp8` has no SGLang runtime import or call site. A reference scan on `origin/main` only finds the JIT wrapper/header/benchmark themselves; current runtime FP8 KV-cache paths use other Triton/backend-specific implementations instead.

title: sgl-router: experimental Rust HTTP router for SGLang worker pools
author: Kangyan-Zhou
body:
## Summary

Draft PR for the experimental `sgl-router` project under `experimental/sgl-router/` — a slim, Rust-based HTTP router that fronts a pool of SGLang inference workers. Targets the same role as the model-gateway sidecar (SMG) but as a single self-contained Rust binary instead of a Python service.

This branch carries the full milestone arc (M0 scaffold → M6 observability + Docker/Helm) plus recent PD-on-K8s work. 141 commits, structured to be reviewable per-commit. Filed as **draft** for visibility and incremental review — not intended to merge as a single shot.

## What's included (by theme)

- **Scaffold + CI** (M0–M1): Cargo workspace, lib/main stubs, PR test workflow with tiered gates, tokenizer parity matrix.
- **Discovery + worker registry** (M2): static-file backend (TOML), K8s `EndpointSlice` backend via `kube-rs`, `WorkerManager` driving the registry from a unified `DiscoveryEvent` stream, circuit-breaker per worker with `NonZeroU32` thresholds.
- **KV-events + cache-aware routing** (M3–M4): ZMQ subscriber, hash-keyed radix tree, `cache_aware_zmq` policy combining tree-overlap score with per-worker active-load tracking via RAII guards + stale-request janitor. PD-disagg dispatch (Pattern B — spawn prefill, await decode) with bootstrap-room injection and decoder-affinity hint.
- **Completions parsers** (M5): chat completion handler, request-body parsing, header forwarding.
- **Observability + ops** (M6): Prometheus `/metrics`, JSON logs for k8s log aggregators, Docker image, graceful shutdown drain, benchmark harness for cache-aware tree + policy-select microbenches.
- **Recent post-review polish + PD-on-K8s** (this session's commits):
  - Test layout reorganization (`tests/{component,proxy,e2e}/` purpose-grouped subdirs), M4 milestone artifact cleanup, raise default request/stale timeouts to 300s/600s, HA convergence test pair (`kv_events_two_subscribers.rs` + `test_two_router_convergence.py`).
  - `/server_info`-derived disaggregation role: `WorkerIntrospector` now resolves `DisaggregationRole` from `disaggregation_mode` + `disaggregation_bootstrap_port` ServerArgs fields surfaced through `/server_info`. Manager applies the role to override the discovery backend's classification.
  - Enable PD on K8s discovery: drop `ConfigError::PdNotImplemented`; K8s + PD config now loads successfully and routes correctly because the manager fills `WorkerMode` and `bootstrap_port` from `/server_info` post-discovery.
  - K8s + PD pipeline integration test: synthesizes `EndpointSlice` events + per-pod fake `/server_info` listeners, drives them through `process_events` → DiscoveryEvent channel → manager, asserts registry settles to (2 Prefill + 2 Decode) with the right per-pod bootstrap_port.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests pass: 267 lib tests in `cargo test --lib`.
- [x] Integration test binaries pass: 42 component + 47 proxy + 3 other = 92 tests.
- [x] Real-SGLang e2e validation on a 4× H200 devbox (`kangyan-zhou-h200-4gpu`): spun up Qwen3-0.6B in prefill + decode modes, confirmed `/server_info` exposes the expected `disaggregation_mode` + `disaggregation_bootstrap_port`, ran the router with `mode = "plain"` in workers.toml, observed the override log line bring each worker to the correct PD role, sent a real chat completion via `curl /v1/chat/completions`, got HTTP 200 + `x-sgl-decode-url` header + real model output. KV transfer over mooncake bootstrap port 8998 worked end-to-end.
- [ ] K8s + PD e2e (kind cluster): not run; devbox is itself K8s-hosted and kind-in-kind was deemed not worth the friction. The Rust integration test (`k8s_pd_pipeline_registers_workers_with_per_pod_bootstrap_port`) covers the seams that would otherwise need a real cluster.
- [ ] SMG parity benchmarks: deferred to M7 (separate scope).

## Known limitations / follow-ups

- K8s + PD e2e in a real cluster: integration test covers the wiring; needs a follow-up e2e test in `tests/e2e/k8s_integration/` once a GPU-enabled kind cluster is in CI.
- `/server_info` fetch failure for a freshly-discovered prefill pod: today the manager falls back to the discovery backend's classification (Plain by default for K8s), so the pod is registered but won't enter the prefill pool until a re-discovery succeeds. Two options for hardening: introspector retry loop matching `kv_events::discovery::fetch_with_retry`, or a periodic refresher. Deferred.
- Mode flip after registration (worker rolls prefill → decode without restart): neither backend nor manager notices. Out of scope; document as known limitation.
- Static-file `bootstrap_port` TOML field is now functionally redundant with `/server_info`. Left in place (no breaking change); a v2 cleanup could deprecate it.
- Helm chart removed in this branch (intentional, replaced by a different deployment path). The Docker image and JSON logs remain.

## File layout

```
experimental/sgl-router/
├── Cargo.toml
├── src/
│   ├── main.rs              # binary entrypoint
│   ├── lib.rs               # library root
│   ├── config/              # Config + TOML/YAML schema
│   ├── discovery/           # static_file + k8s + worker_manager events
│   ├── policies/            # round_robin, random, power_of_two, cache_aware_zmq
│   ├── policies/active_load.rs   # per-worker counters + RAII guards + stale-request janitor
│   ├── policies/kv_events/  # ZMQ subscriber, hash tree, KvEventIndex
│   ├── proxy/               # reqwest-based upstream HTTP, SSE pump
│   ├── server/              # axum HTTP server, routes, metrics, app context
│   ├── workers/             # WorkerSpec, Worker, Registry, Introspector
│   └── health/              # circuit breaker
├── tests/
│   ├── component/{discovery,health,policies,tokenizer,workers}/
│   ├── proxy/{chat_routing,failover,pd_*,...}/
│   └── e2e/{chat_completions,k8s_integration,...}/
└── .github/workflows/pr-test-sgl-router.yml
```

## Review guidance

This PR is filed draft for visibility. Recommended approach: review per-commit rather than per-PR — the commit history is structured to be readable in topological order from M0 scaffold forward. A reviewer interested in a specific feature can jump to the matching commit (e.g., `git log --oneline upstream/main..HEAD | grep cache_aware`).

The last four commits (top of the log) are this session's work; the remainder is prior milestone work that has already had internal code reviews against earlier branches.

title: perf(jit_kernel/deepseek_v4): optimize paged_mqa_metadata
author: yangdian96
body:
## Motivation

`paged_mqa_metadata.cuh` (introduced in #23882) is currently a single-block
kernel whose Phase 3 has lane 0 of each warp serially advancing `q` across
the per-batch prefix array — `O(bs)` dependent smem loads on one SM with the
other 131 SMs idle. For `bs ≥ 1024` the kernel costs 60–2000 µs.

This PR rewrites it as a batch-size-adaptive 3-path dispatch (tiny / small /
multi-block), replacing Phase 3 with `num_sm + 1` parallel `upper_bound`s
(O(log bs) per thread) and fanning out Phase 1 across SMs for large `bs`.

**Result on H200 (sm_90, num_sm=132): GeoMean 45.3× over `bs ∈ [128, 32768]`,
peak 297× at `bs = 32768`, byte-equal correctness preserved.**

## Modifications

| op | path | LoC |
|---|---|---|
| rewrite | `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/deepseek_v4/paged_mqa_metadata.cuh` | 119 → 386 |
| new | `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/deepseek_v4/test_paged_mqa_metadata.py` | 199 |
| new | `python/sglang/jit_kernel/benchmark/bench_paged_mqa_metadata.py` | 78 |

Public API is unchanged: `IndexerMetadataKernel::run(TensorView, TensorView)`
signature is locked by `cuda_wrappers=[("run", ...)]` in `deepseek_v4.py:244`
and we preserve it byte-for-byte. The Python wrapper
`get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata` and all 8 in-tree callers in
`srt/layers/attention/{nsa_backend,nsa/nsa_indexer,dsv4/metadata}.py` need
no edits.

Key algorithm changes:
- `cub::BlockScan<u32, {256, 1024}, BLOCK_SCAN_WARP_SCANS>` replaces the
  hand-rolled 2-level warp reduce for the prefix sum.
- Phase 3 uses `num_sm + 1` threads doing parallel `upper_bound` over the
  prefix (O(log bs) per thread, ≤ 11 dependent loads), instead of lane-0
  serial advance (O(bs)).
- Multi-block dispatch for `bs > 2048`: phase 1 is fanned out across
  `⌈bs/4096⌉` blocks; phase 2 is a 256-thread scheduler with a per-device
  stream-cached scratch buffer (`cudaMalloc`, CUDA-Graph-safe).
- Per-target write loop uses a stride pattern
  `for (i = tx; i <= num_sm; i += blockDim.x)` so `num_sm > blockDim.x - 1`
  is fully covered (preserves the upstream `num_sm ≤ 1024` contract).

## Accuracy Tests

```
$ pytest python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/deepseek_v4/test_paged_mqa_metadata.py -v
...
127 passed, 4 skipped
```
(skipped: `test_matches_deep_gemm` at `bs ∈ {16384, 32768}` — deep_gemm
exceeds sm_90 smem cap there; the multi-block path is still gated against
the PyTorch ref oracle at those bs)

Output is `int32 [num_sm + 1, 2]` (deterministic partition), verified
byte-for-byte with `torch.equal` — no `atol`/`rtol`. Two oracles:

- **Primary**: `deep_gemm.get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata` (the production
  reference; sglang prod callers default to it, this PR optimizes the
  JIT fallback). Gated by `test_matches_deep_gemm` across the dispatch
  envelope; auto-skips at `bs ≥ 16384` where deep_gemm exceeds sm_90's
  per-block smem cap (see footnote in the Speed Tests section).
- **Secondary**: inlined pure-PyTorch algorithmic spec, gating the full
  envelope including the multi-block path beyond deep_gemm's cap.

Envelope covers `bs ∈ {1, 17, 32, 128, 129, 257, 512, 1024, 1025, 2048,
4096, 8192, 16384, 32768}` × `max_ctx ∈ {1, 255, 256, 257, 2048, 8192,
32768}`, hand-crafted `kSplitKV=256` boundary patterns, `bs ∈ {65536,
131072}` for the multi-block gmem path, and `num_sm ∈ {256, 257, 1024}`
across all dispatch paths. Registered via
`register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, suite="base-b-kernel-unit-1-gpu-large")` +
nightly.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Measurement**: `triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph` median µs (via
`sglang.jit_kernel.benchmark.utils.run_benchmark`).

### Primary target: H200 (sm_90, num_sm=132)

| bs | `max_ctx=2048` (µs) before → after | `max_ctx=32768` (µs) before → after | speedup |
|---:|:---|:---|---:|
| 1     | 2.03 → 1.26   | 2.17 → 1.36   | 1.6× |
| 32    | 3.96 → 1.57   | 3.95 → 1.57   | 2.5× |
| 128   | 9.65 → 1.75   | 9.63 → 1.75   | **5.5×** |
| 512   | 32.48 → 1.93  | 32.46 → 1.93  | **16.8×** |
| 1024  | 62.89 → 2.10  | 62.75 → 2.11  | **30.0×** |
| 2048  | 123.59 → 2.50 | 123.63 → 2.50 | **49.4×** |
| 4096  | 245.07 → 6.13 | 245.02 → 6.12 | **40.0×** |
| 8192  | 488.13 → 6.28 | 488.22 → 6.28 | **77.7×** |
| 16384 | 973.94 → 6.38 | 973.88 → 6.38 | **152.7×** |
| 32768 | 1945.81 → 6.55 | 1945.83 → 6.55 | **297.1×** |

GeoMean over `bs ∈ [128, 32768]` = **45.3×**. The two `max_ctx` columns agree
within 0.5% per row, as expected (compute is `O(bs)`, value-invariant).

### vs `deep_gemm.get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata` (production reference)

sglang production callers default to
`deep_gemm.get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata`; the sglang JIT path this PR
optimizes is the fallback. Running both with the same
`do_bench_cudagraph` harness on H200 (`max_ctx=8192`; value-invariant):

| bs | deep_gemm (µs) | this PR (µs) | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1     | 1.96  | 1.24 | 1.59× |
| 8     | 2.71  | 1.54 | 1.76× |
| 16    | 2.92  | 1.59 | 1.84× |
| 32    | 3.10  | 1.63 | 1.90× |
| 64    | 3.55  | 1.81 | 1.96× |
| 128   | 3.81  | 1.83 | 2.08× |
| 256   | 4.08  | 1.86 | 2.19× |
| 384   | 4.67  | 1.90 | 2.46× |
| 512   | 4.88  | 1.97 | 2.48× |
| 1024  | 5.69  | 2.12 | 2.68× |
| 2048  | 6.83  | 2.44 | 2.80× |
| 4096  | 9.15  | 6.04 | 1.51× |
| 8192  | 30.78 | 6.13 | **5.02×** |
| 16384 | _smem cap_ † | 6.31 | n/a |
| 32768 | _smem cap_ † | 6.45 | n/a |

GeoMean over the bs range where deep_gemm is benchmarkable on sm_90
(`bs ∈ [128, 8192]`): **2.51×**.

† deep_gemm fails on sm_90 at `bs ≥ 16384` with smem-capacity errors —
driver-level `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE` from `cudaFuncSetAttribute` at
`bs=16384`, internal `smem_size <= SM90ArchSpec::smem_capacity` assertion
at `bs=32768`. deep_gemm stages the prefix array in a single
`__shared__ uint32_t [kAlignedBatchSize]` buffer; sm_90's per-block
opt-in smem cap (228 KB) is exceeded once three such buffers — one each
for `varlen_atom_token_start`, `varlen_atom_context_len`, `prefix_sum`
— grow to ~192 KB / 384 KB at `bs=16384` / `bs=32768`. This PR's
multi-block path keeps per-block smem at ~8 KB regardless of
`batch_size`, so it scales past the limit (the 6.31 / 6.45 µs at
bs=16384 / 32768 above).

The bs=8192 5× spike is the same root cause: deep_gemm's template
instantiation at that bs starts requiring the smem opt-in
(96 KB), which adds one-time `cudaFuncSetAttribute` cost and changes
occupancy.

### Cross-architecture sanity: RTX 4090 (sm_89, num_sm=128)

Re-ran the same bench against a locally-patched sglang baseline\* on a 4090
to check the speedup isn't Hopper-specific.

| bs | upstream-equivalent (µs) | this PR (µs) | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1     | 1.82    | 1.23 | 1.5× |
| 128   | 7.46    | 1.50 | **5.0×** |
| 512   | 24.68   | 1.63 | **15.2×** |
| 1024  | 47.80   | 1.72 | **27.8×** |
| 2048  | 93.44   | 1.97 | **47.5×** |
| 4096  | 185.59  | 4.66 | **39.8×** |
| 8192  | 368.76  | 4.72 | **78.1×** |
| 16384 | 735.61  | 4.78 | **153.8×** |
| 32768 | 1731.89 | 4.87 | **355.3×** |

GeoMean over `bs ∈ [128, 32768]` = **44.8×** — within 1% of the H200 number.

\* sglang's current `cudaFuncSetAttribute(MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, 128 KB)`
fails on sm_89's 100 KB per-block cap; the 4090 baseline used here is a
local patch with `kMaxBatchSizeInSmem` lowered from 32768 to 24576. Not
asking sglang to support consumer GPUs (DSv4 has other sm_90+ dependencies);
the 4090 number is cross-architecture robustness evidence, not a portability
claim.

## Checklist

- [x] `pre-commit run` on touched files passed.
- [x] Unit test added (`tests/deepseek_v4/test_paged_mqa_metadata.py`), registered to `base-b-kernel-unit-1-gpu-large` + nightly.
- [x] Benchmark added (`benchmark/bench_paged_mqa_metadata.py`), registered to `base-b-kernel-benchmark-1-gpu-large`.
- [x] Byte-equal verified across the full bs envelope on H200 (115/115 PASS, no `atol`/`rtol` drift).
- [x] Public interface preserved; no caller edits needed.
- [ ] AMD / MUSA / SM100+ not tested (no hardware locally). Algorithm uses no SM-specific intrinsics; static smem ≤ 8 KB on the fast paths.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS).
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) (`/tag-and-rerun-ci`).
4. After green CI and required approvals, merge.

title: [codex] Reland Wan2.2 ModelOpt CI checkpoints
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- Reland #25483 to move Wan2.2 ModelOpt CI/docs from the old lmsys transformer overrides to NVIDIA full Diffusers FP8/NVFP4 checkpoints.
- Keep the change's per-case Wan2.2 NVFP4 FlashInfer TRTLLM override instead of changing the global diffusion NVFP4 default backend.
- Fix the B200-only diffusion NVFP4 JIT test by making its synthetic pre-swapped checkpoint explicitly request `swap_weight_nibbles=True`.

## Root Cause

#25483 intentionally changes the ModelOpt FP4 fallback default for `swap_weight_nibbles` to `False` so NVIDIA full-repo checkpoints without the field load in runtime order. The B200 JIT test builds a synthetic checkpoint by pre-swapping nibbles with `_swap_fp4_nibbles(weight_fp4)`, but did not pass the knob explicitly, so after the default flip its expected weight stayed one nibble-swap away from the processed layer weight.

## Tests

title: Address overlap future token map by request-pool index
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Why req-pool-indexed

The ring allocator slot id is a temporary counter — slot K denotes different requests at different times, driving sizing miscalculations (chunked-prefill blowup), wrap-around aliasing, slot-reuse staleness, and a cross-stream indices-tensor lifetime race. Indexing every future-map buffer by `req_pool_idx` instead binds each slot to a request's lifetime in the pool, so slot identity stops drifting.

## Consecutive prefill batches

Two prefill iters with disjoint requests (e.g. `[A, B]` then `[C, D]`) write to disjoint slots; a later mixed/decode batch gathers `token_ids_buf[[A.idx, B.idx, C.idx, D.idx]]` and reads each request's first output independently — no overwrite, no combining logic.

## Chunked prefill

The same request keeps its `req_pool_idx` across all chunks. Mid-chunk writes to `token_ids_buf[req_pool_idx]` are never read (the request is in extend mode, input loaded from CPU); the final chunk's write is the real first output, picked up by gather the first time the request enters decode.

## Sizing

Buffer size = `req_to_token.shape[0]` (i.e. `ReqToTokenPool._alloc_size = size + 1`), so slot 0 is the padding row shared with the KV cache pool — CUDA-graph padded batches (req_pool_idx == 0) read/write here harmlessly. Real `req_pool_idx >= 1` keeps `-req_pool_idx` strictly negative for the existing `resolve_future` placeholder encoding.

## Removed

Ring allocator state (`future_ct`, `future_limit`, `future_buffer_len`, `max_num_chunks`), `is_empty_slice` guard, `FutureIndices.interval`, and the per-iter `record_stream` on the indices tensor (slot is now `batch.req_pool_indices`, pinned by `record_batch_in_overlap`'s `attr_snapshot` for 2 iters; Python refcount stays > 0 across forward's read).

Disagg prebuilt's `alloc_future_indices` now returns the same req-indexed handle as the standard path.

title: fix: forward update_mamba_state_after_mtp_verify in HybridAttnBackend
author: 00fish0
body:
When a hybrid Mamba model runs speculative decoding (MTP) with HybridAttnBackend (different prefill/decode attention backends), the speculative workers call
`attn_backend.update_mamba_state_after_mtp_verify(...)` on the target worker's attention backend. HybridAttnBackend did not implement this method, which caused:

- AttributeError in eagle_worker / eagle_worker_v2 / multi_layer_eagle_worker, which call the method unconditionally;
- a silent no-op in dflash_worker, which guards the call with `hasattr` and therefore skipped committing the Mamba state after verify.

Add the method on HybridAttnBackend and forward it to the sub-backend that handled target_verify (decode_backend when speculative_attention_mode is "decode", otherwise prefill_backend), mirroring _select_backend's target_verify branch. title: Fix/dsv4 flash eagle dummy ima
author: mattteochen
body:
## Motivation

Closes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25767

`--load-format dummy` only initializes floating-point tensors, leaving `HashTopK.tid2eid` uninitialized because it is an integer lookup table. For DeepSeek-V4-Flash with `flashinfer_mxfp4`, this can produce invalid expert ids and trigger CUDA illegal memory accesses during hash top-k execution, including CUDA graph capture.

## Modifications

Initialize `HashTopK.tid2eid` with a deterministic valid default mapping when the layer is constructed. This keeps dummy-loaded models within valid expert-id bounds while preserving normal checkpoint behavior, since real weights still overwrite `tid2eid` during loading.

title: [diffusion] optimize: reuse cached dynamic lora weights
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

This avoids rebuilding dynamic LoRA weights when a previously applied adapter is only deactivated and then reactivated with the same single-adapter configuration.

The fast path only toggles the wrapped LoRA layers back on when the cached A/B tensors, path, and strength still match. Merged LoRA, previously merged layers, and layerwise-offloaded modules still use the existing weight-update context.

## Impact

- Reduces dynamic LoRA reactivation from a full per-layer LoRA state rebuild to metadata reactivation when the cached adapter still matches.
- Preserves the existing path for merged LoRA and offloaded components.
- Also handles the API case where `set_lora` passes only an already-loaded nickname and omits `lora_path`.
- Latest high-memory resident LTX2 two-stage mode keeps both DiTs resident and already reports near-zero `ltx2_lora_switch_stage2`, so this PR is primarily justified by dynamic/offload modes rather than that resident path.

## Validation

- `python3 -m pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_lora_pipeline.py`
  - `2 passed`
- Paired H200 run of `ltx_2_3_two_stage_ti2v_2gpus` on clean main and this PR:
  - clean main also fails the current perf/PSNR gates with identical PSNR values, so this run is not an accuracy regression from this PR
  - `ltx2_lora_switch_stage2`: 49.19 ms -> 5.19 ms
  - total E2E was noisy in this run, so this PR does not claim a stable end-to-end improvement by itself
- Latest-main H200 resident sanity check on `ltx_2.3_two_stage_t2v_2gpus` (`base=55ba03db6a`):
  - clean base already reports `ltx2_lora_switch_stage2=0.01ms`
  - stacked patch reports `ltx2_lora_switch_stage2=0.00ms`

author: kkHuang-amd
body:
Co-authored-by: @1am9trash @RolaoDenthu @yichiche @hubertlu-tw @sogalin @HaiShaw @yctseng0211 @bingxche @amd-danli103 @Raiden-Makoto ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4 (DSV4) on AMD MI300X/MI350X GPUs encounters multiple runtime failures when serving inference workloads: 1. **GPU fault (HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION)** — The core `CompressStatePool` is initialized without `swa_page_size`, defaulting to 0. This causes division-by-zero in `translate_from_swa_loc_to_state_loc()`, producing out-of-bounds `state_loc` indices (e.g., 525448 vs buffer size 470528) that trigger a hardware exception during `index_put_`. 2. **Model registration failure** — `fused_softmax_pool_triton` is imported at module level in `compress_hip.py` but doesn't exist in the current `deepseek_v4_rope.py`, blocking `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` class registration. 3. **JIT kernel incompatibilities** — Wave64 shuffle intrinsics, DLPack device type, FP8 conversion, and kernel launch APIs differ between CUDA and HIP. ## Modifications ### Commit 1: JIT kernel HIP/ROCm compatibility infrastructure Adds HIP compatibility to JIT kernel shared headers for wave64 architectures: - `warp.cuh`: Use `__shfl_xor`/`__shfl_up` (HIP-native) instead of `__shfl_xor_sync`/`__shfl_up_sync`; 64-bit `kFullMask` for wave64 - `tensor.h`: `kDLGPU` device type abstraction (DLPack) - `utils.cuh`: Skip Hopper/Blackwell arch asserts on ROCm; disable PDL/cluster launch attributes - `fp8_utils.cuh`: Software FP8 E4M3/E4M3FNUZ conversion for MI300X (gfx942 FNUZ) vs MI350X (gfx950 E4M3); `pack_fp8` as `uint16_t` - `c128_v2.cuh`, `c4_v2.cuh`: `kDLCUDA` → `kDLGPU` device type fix - `utils.py`: `is_hip_runtime()` helper ### Commit 2: Port HIP/ROCm runtime fixes from upstream - `jit_kernel/deepseek_v4.py`: Add `is_hip_runtime()` dispatch for `fused_q_indexer_rope_hadamard_quant`, `topk_transform_512`, `hash_topk`, and `fused_store_cache` to route to sgl-kernel ops or Triton fallbacks on HIP - `jit_kernel/triton/hash_topk.py`: New Triton implementation (CUDA JIT uses CUDA-only primitives) - `jit_kernel/triton_store_cache.py`: New Triton fused FP8 store cache for ROCm (FlashMLA + indexer paths with UE8M0 quantization) - `layers/attention/dsv4/compress_hip.py`: Graceful fallback for missing `fused_softmax_pool_triton` - `mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`: Add missing `swa_page_size` parameter to core `CompressStatePool` - `sgl-kernel/`: Add DSV4 norm+rope and topk AOT kernel sources (`.cu`/`.hip`), op declarations, registrations, Python wrappers, and build config ## AMD Accuracy Tests

title: [bugfix] Honor cast_x_before_out_mul in RMSNorm.forward_cuda residual path
author: charlotte12l
body:
## Bug

`RMSNorm.forward_cuda` silently drops the `cast_x_before_out_mul` flag when a residual is provided.

The non-residual path correctly dispatches to the HF JIT kernel (`rmsnorm_hf`) when the flag is set — and even falls back to `forward_native` when the JIT kernel's hidden-size / dtype constraints don't match (see lines 235-248). But the residual-present path falls through to `fused_add_rmsnorm` without any such fallback.

Reproducer (conceptually):
```python
norm = RMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=1e-5, cast_x_before_out_mul=True).cuda()
x = torch.randn(B, S, H, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device='cuda')

# Layer 0: residual is None → cast_x_before_out_mul honored
# (HF JIT kernel, or forward_native fallback if JIT not applicable)
out0 = norm(x)

# Layer 1+: residual provided → flag silently dropped, fused_add_rmsnorm used
out1, _ = norm(x, residual=x.clone())   # ← wrong math
```

For any transformer using the standard residual-stream pattern, every layer ≥ 1 silently produces the wrong math whenever `cast_x_before_out_mul=True`.

## Fix (2 commits)

### 1. Dispatch fallback (`299858c9d`)

Mirror the existing no-residual fallback: when `cast_x_before_out_mul=True` AND `residual is not None`, fall back to `forward_native` (which already implements cast-before-multiply correctly). Layer 0 behavior is unchanged. This is the minimum-surface correctness fix.

### 2. JIT kernel `fused_add_rmsnorm_hf` (`aaf7008d1`)

Eliminates the `forward_native` fallback cost from #1 by adding a fused CUDA kernel. Adapted from `rmsnorm_hf.cuh` as a template, with these adjustments:

- Param struct gains `residual` and (optional) `post_residual` pointers + strides.
- Pass 1 loads `x + residual (+ post_residual)` in fp32, writes the sum back to `residual` as the input dtype, and accumulates squares on the fp32 sum.
- Pass 2 unchanged (cast-before-multiply with weight).
- `kHasPostResidual` template bool — zero overhead when not used.

Dispatch in `forward_cuda` prefers the JIT kernel when shape/dtype constraints are satisfied; falls back to `forward_native` for shapes the JIT kernel can't handle.

**Bonus correctness improvement on the 3-way path:** the existing `fused_add_rmsnorm` path handles `post_residual_addition` by pre-summing `residual = residual + post_residual_addition` in narrow dtype (bf16), which is lossy — flagged by an existing TODO in `layernorm.py`. The new kernel does the 3-way add in fp32, matching `forward_native` exactly. Strict correctness improvement for models combining `cast_x_before_out_mul=True` with `post_residual_addition` (e.g. qwen3-vl with deepstack_embeds).

## Scope of the bug

Models in the current tree that set `cast_x_before_out_mul=True` and subsequently call the norm with a residual:

| File | Sites |
|---|---|
| `python/sglang/srt/models/sdar.py` | 2 |
| `python/sglang/srt/models/sdar_moe.py` | 2 |
| `python/sglang/srt/models/moss_vl.py` | 1 |
| `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2.py` | 1 |
| `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3.py` | 2 |
| `python/sglang/srt/models/transformers.py` | 1 |
| `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/vision.py` | 1 |

Outputs for those models will shift slightly toward the cast-before-multiply semantics they originally requested via the flag — closer to the reference implementations (e.g. HF transformers), not further. Cached golden snapshots / tight CI tolerances may need refreshing.

## Notes

This PR also includes a small rustfmt cleanup in `sgl-model-gateway/src/service_discovery.rs` to unblock the lint check — an unrelated pre-existing failure.

## Test plan

New `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_fused_add_rmsnorm_hf.py` mirrors `test_fused_add_rmsnorm.py` style:
- `test_..._correctness` — loose tolerance (`atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2`) over the full BS × hidden range, bf16.
- `test_..._bitwise_canonical[False/True]` — strict bitwise vs `forward_native` on one canonical setup `(bs=4, hidden=4096, bf16)` for both 2-way and 3-way paths. Single-shape because bitwise equivalence depends on fp32 reduction order ↔ bf16 rounding interaction (shape/arch sensitive), not kernel correctness.
- Validation tests (shape/dtype/dim/hidden_size mismatches).

Locally on sm100: all pass.

title: [Docs] DeepSeek-V4: switch H200 FP4 Pro to flashinfer_mxfp4, Flash Balanced too
author: zijiexia
body:
## Summary

The DeepSeek-V4 cookbook command generator's H200 (FP4) branch unconditionally emitted `--moe-runner-backend marlin` for every (variant, recipe). This PR picks the runner per (variant, recipe) based on **verified** behavior + benchmark:

- **Pro (all recipes)** → `flashinfer_mxfp4`. Marlin **fails to start the server** on Pro at TP=8 on a single H200 node, so the cookbook's Pro recipes were effectively unrunnable on H200 FP4. Flashinfer mxfp4 boots cleanly on the same hardware.
- **Flash Balanced** → `flashinfer_mxfp4`. **~1.25x faster output throughput** than Marlin in the balanced throughput benchmark.
- **Flash Low-Latency / Max-Throughput** → `marlin` (unchanged). Marlin still benchmarks faster on those recipes.

Both Pro startup and the Flash Balanced speedup were verified on 2026-05-20.

title: [perf] skip add_special_tokens=False kwarg on chat-template tokenize for slow tokenizers
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Summary

Sibling of #25265 for `/v1/chat/completions`. Some slow tokenizers (e.g. Kimi-K2.5's `TikTokenTokenizer`) treat **any** kwarg to `encode()` as a slow-path trigger — falling back to `PreTrainedTokenizer.encode()` which re-runs the tokenize work and round-trips every token through string conversion. The current chat-template path always passes `add_special_tokens=False`, hitting that slow path even on tokenizers where the kwarg is a no-op.

## Fix

At `OpenAIServingChat` init, probe `tokenizer.encode("")` once. If empty, the tokenizer doesn't auto-add specials → safe to drop the kwarg at the chat-template encode site. Otherwise keep `add_special_tokens=False` (correctness — avoids double BOS).

To make the kwarg controllable, `apply_chat_template(..., tokenize=True, ...)` is replaced with the explicit two-call form (`apply_chat_template(tokenize=False)` + `tokenizer.encode(rendered, **encode_kwargs)`). The Jinja `TemplateError` fallback path is updated identically.

```python
# in __init__
self._tokenizer_auto_adds_specials = (
    len(self.tokenizer_manager.tokenizer.encode("")) > 0
)

# in _apply_jinja_template
encode_kwargs = {"add_special_tokens": False} if self._tokenizer_auto_adds_specials else {}
rendered = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, ...)
prompt_ids = tokenizer.encode(rendered, **encode_kwargs)
```

## Micro-benchmark — Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 `TikTokenTokenizer` (`is_fast=False`, `encode("")=[]`)

Standalone tokenizer-only timing (no sglang server in the loop):

| input tokens | `encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)` *(current main)* | `encode(text)` *(this PR for Kimi)* | speedup | saving |
|-------------:|----------------------------------------------------------:|------------------------------------:|--------:|-------:|
|        1,001 |                                                   3.25 ms |                             0.28 ms |  11.8 × |  2.97 ms |
|       10,001 |                                                  32.07 ms |                             2.59 ms |  12.4 × | 29.48 ms |
|       80,001 |                                                 254.25 ms |                            20.66 ms |  12.3 × | 233.59 ms |

Token IDs are identical between the two paths at every size. **For an 80k prompt that's ~234 ms shaved off the chat-template tokenize step**, which lives entirely on the OpenAI handler thread before the scheduler sees the request.

## End-to-end context (from #25933's measurement)

The companion observability PR #25933 split the `chat_template` histogram into `chat_template_render` (0.18 ms) and `chat_template_encode` (309.93 ms) on the same 80k workload. This PR is the optimization that #25933's measurements identified. Expected impact on `chat_template_encode` for that bench: roughly the 234 ms saving above → from ~310 ms to ~80 ms, an ~ 33 % cut to TTFT for long-prompt high-cache-hit chat workloads on Kimi.

## Why only "Kimi-like" tokenizers benefit

- **Slow tokenizers** (`is_fast=False`) often have custom `encode()` implementations. The Kimi one falls back to `super().encode()` on any kwarg and re-runs everything.
- **Fast tokenizers** (`PreTrainedTokenizerFast`, Rust-backed) handle kwargs efficiently; this PR keeps the kwarg for them.
- The probe (`len(encode(""))`) cleanly separates the two cases: tokenizers that add BOS by default in `encode()` (e.g. LLaMA family) keep the kwarg; tokenizers that don't (e.g. Kimi) drop it.

## Risk

- Behavior is correctness-preserving by construction: the kwarg is dropped only when its semantics are a no-op.
- The shape of `_apply_jinja_template` changes (one HF call → two), but the two calls are bracketed by the same try/except so error handling is unchanged.
- Backward compat: tokenizers that auto-add BOS still get `add_special_tokens=False`; their behavior is identical to before.

## Test plan

- [ ] Diff `prompt_tokens` before/after on the same prompt for both Kimi (`is_fast=False`, probe empty) and a LLaMA-family slow tokenizer (`is_fast=False`, probe non-empty) — must be identical for both.
- [ ] `/v1/chat/completions` bench on Kimi-K2.5 with ISL=80k: TTFT should drop by ~230 ms relative to current main.
- [ ] No regression for fast tokenizers — `_tokenizer_auto_adds_specials` defaults to `True` on probe failure, so behavior is identical to before.
- [ ] Existing chat-template `TemplateError` fallback still triggers the second `apply_chat_template(tokenize=False)` call.

## Related

- #25265 (Qiaolin Yu) — same idea, applied to `tokenizer_manager._tokenize_texts` for the `/generate` text path.
- #25933 — observability PR that surfaces `chat_template_encode` as a histogram and provided the measurements above.

title: [Fix]: Restrict Kimi-K2.5 shared-experts fusion to Quark MXFP4 checkpoints
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

Fix nightly `TestKimiK25.test_kimi_k25` failure (gsm8k 0.000 on both TP8 and TP8+DP8 since 2026-05-19, runs [26069709241](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26069709241) and [26134864664](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26134864664)).

Bisection points at #25390 (`abe2ec2af`), which widened the `n_routed_experts` allow-list in `determine_num_fused_shared_experts` from `{256}` to `{256, 384}` for AMD MXFP4. That unconditionally enables shared-experts fusion for **any** Kimi-K2.5 load. The fused path requires the shared expert to be pre-fused into the routed-experts tensor on disk — true only for `amd/Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4` (Quark). The standard `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5` (compressed-tensors) checkpoint keeps the shared expert in `quantization_config.ignore` (different dtype/scale from the int4 routed experts) and the fused loader silently misses every `experts.wN_weight` (load log shows `not found in params_dict` for every MoE layer; weight mem 84.39 GB vs the safe 72.19 GB). Output is silent garbage.

## Modifications

Restrict the new `384` allow-list entry to `quant_config.get_name() == "quark"`. The `256` (DeepSeek-V3/R1) path is unchanged, and the AMD MXFP4 perf win from #25390 is preserved.

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/8-gpu-models/test_kimi_k25.py` on 8×H200, `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5` (compressed-tensors):

| parent of suspect | `e5589843a` | gsm8k 0.947 ✓ | gsm8k 0.946 ✓ | PASSED |
| **this PR** | `a0cc1af7` | **gsm8k 0.942 ✓** | **gsm8k 0.945 ✓** | **PASSED** |

`Load weight end. ... mem usage = 72.19 GB` matches the parent run's safe-path footprint; zero `experts.wN_weight not found in params_dict` warnings (suspect had one per MoE layer). Ran 1 test in 1712.355s.

N/A — correctness fix; behavior for `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5` matches the parent of #25390 (fusion off), and for `amd/Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4` and DeepSeek-V3/R1 is unchanged.

title: [DeepSeek-V4] Add mhc_fused_post_pre kernel
author: JoeLee314
body: # [DeepSeek-V4] Add fused mHC post/pre kernel ## Motivation This PR optimizes the DeepSeek-V4 mHC path by fusing the boundary between one mHC post step and the next mHC pre step. The approach is adapted from TRTLLM. The main idea is to avoid launching separate kernels for the latency-sensitive decode path: ```text mhc_post -> pre-norm GEMM -> mhc_pre finalization ``` The fused path keeps the existing numerically sensitive `mhc_pre_big_fuse(_with_norm)` finalization stage, but removes the separate post/pre scheduling boundary. For small token batches, a TileLang scalar-FMA kernel computes the following work in one launch: ```text previous hc_post + bf16 residual materialization + pre-norm GEMM partials + RMS square-sum partials ``` For larger token batches, the implementation keeps the existing high-throughput TileLang `mhc_post` + DeepGEMM decomposition. The optimization is guarded by a new env var: ```bash SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE=1 ``` It intentionally depends on the existing TileLang mHC switches: ```bash SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=1 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_POST=1 ``` because the fused implementation directly reuses the TileLang mHC tensor layouts and the `mhc_pre_big_fuse(_with_norm)` finalization kernels. ## Performance Test total_throughput increased by 3.35% ### Performance summary ## Accuracy / Correctness Tests GSM8K score: 0.975 ## Modifications ### `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` Add: ```python SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE = EnvBool(False) ``` ### `python/sglang/srt/layers/mhc.py` - Add `mhc_fused_post_pre_fma_tilelang`, a small-token fused TileLang kernel. - Add `mhc_fused_post_pre`, which dispatches: - small batches to the fused FMA kernel; - larger batches to the existing TileLang `mhc_post` + DeepGEMM path. - Preserve the existing `mhc_pre_big_fuse(_with_norm)` finalization stage. - Handle zero-token DP/EP ranks with correctly typed empty tensors. ### `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py` - Add fused mHC enable check cached in `__init__`. - Fuse: - cross-layer previous FFN `hc_post` + next attention `hc_pre`; - within-layer attention `hc_post` + FFN `hc_pre`. - Defer the final FFN `hc_post` and close it at model tail. - Cache bf16 RMSNorm weights for the fused path to avoid per-forward casts. ### `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_nextn.py` - Adapt NextN decoder usage to the decoder layer returning deferred fused state. ### `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py` - Add coverage for `mhc_fused_post_pre` vs the unfused reference sequence. ## Checklist - [x] Added fused mHC post/pre boundary optimization. - [x] Added env guard `SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE`. - [x] Kept the fused path dependent on TileLang mHC pre/post kernels. - [x] Added kernel unit test for fused vs unfused mHC. - [x] Verified operator-level precision. - [x] Verified short deterministic sanity prompts. - [x] Verified GSM8K-200 end-to-end accuracy. - [x] Verified `bench_serving` performance improvement on DeepSeek-V4-Flash. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #26549213709](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26549213709) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #26549213622](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26549213622)

title: amd/deepseek_v4 30/N Enable fused nosplitk attention dispatch for extend, from separate gather+attention to 1 fused kernel
author: yichiche
body:
Update amd/deepseek_v4 integration branch

Following PRs have large set of conflict, we use this PR and upstream amd/deepseek_v4 branch to integrate in parallel.
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23600
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23608

## Motivation

On MI355, the Triton MLA attention dispatch for DeepSeek V4 extend/prefill has two issues:

1. **c128 layers (L31-type, non-MoE)**: Fall through to the slow separate `gather_dequant + unified_sparse_decode` fallback path because `_should_use_fused_nosplitk()` rejects `total_topk < 200`. The fused dual-scope kernel already exists and works for c4 layers with larger topk. c128 layers with `total_topk=192` are blocked solely by this threshold, which was calibrated for decode workloads.

2. **TP>1 configurations (h_q <= 64)**: Both c128 and c4 layers are blocked by a `h_q <= 64: return False` guard, causing c4 layers to fall into a 3-chunk fallback (5 GB intermediate buffer exceeds 2 GB limit). The fused kernel avoids buffer allocation entirely, so this limit is irrelevant.

For extend with `total_tokens >= 1024`, the GPU grid already has thousands of blocks, so the fused kernel is strictly better: it eliminates the intermediate `gathered_kv` buffer (1.5-5 GB), removes 2x `_gather_dequant_dsv4_kernel` launches (~414 us), and avoids chunking overhead.

## Modifications

- **`triton_mla_kernels_decode_optimized.py`**: Add an early `return True` in `_should_use_fused_nosplitk()` when `total_tokens >= 1024`. This routes all extend workloads to the fused dual-scope kernel regardless of `h_q` or `total_topk`. Decode paths (`total_tokens < 1024`) are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

| Benchmark | Score | Threshold | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| GSM8K 5-shot (2000 questions) | 0.911 | 0.88 | PASS |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

### Kernel Change (L31 c128, extend il8k, TP=8)

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Kernel(s) | `_gather_dequant_dsv4` x2 + `_unified_sparse_decode` | `_fused_gather_attn_dsv4_dual_scope` |
| Kernel count | 3 | 1 |
| Attention time | ~2005 us | 1882 us |
| Intermediate buffer | 1.5 GB `gathered_kv` | None |

### Kernel Change (L32 c4, extend il8k, TP=8)

| | Before (TP=8) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Path | 3-chunk fallback (5 GB > 2 GB limit) | fused nosplitk |
| Kernel(s) | 3x chunked gather+attention | `_fused_gather_attn_dsv4_dual_scope` |
| Attention time | chunked (multiple launches) | 4459 us (single kernel) |

### E2E Benchmark (il8k_ol1k, concurrency=4, TP=8, 8xMI355)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total token throughput | 1584 tok/s |
| Output throughput | 176 tok/s |
| Median TTFT | 1532 ms |
| Median ITL | 20.56 ms |
| Median E2E | 23065 ms |

title: [codex] Centralize Triton utility kernels

## Summary
- move FlashInfer/FlashMLA KV index, KV split, FlashAttention metadata, cache, padding, RoPE/cache, and position Triton kernels into focused `attention/triton_ops/*` and `model_executor/triton_ops/*` modules

Several non-diffusion Triton kernels were embedded inline in large backend/helper files. This PR centralizes those kernels into domain-specific `triton_ops` modules as a pure relocation cleanup, without changing kernel behavior.
