title: Apply apply_group_norm_silu to LTX-2 latent upsampler
author: pengdurice
body:
## Motivation The LTX-2 spatial **`LatentUpsampler`** (`runtime/models/upsampler/latent_upsampler.py`) is auto-loaded as the `spatial_upsampler` component of every LTX-2 two-stage pipeline — Lightricks generates latents at lower spatial resolution and uses this module to upscale them by 2× before VAE decode, so it sits on the critical path of every LTX-2 generation. Its `LatentUpsampler` and `ResBlock` modules use `torch.nn.GroupNorm(32, ...) + torch.nn.SiLU()` at multiple sites, but the existing inline `silu(norm(x))` pattern bypasses the Triton-fused `apply_group_norm_silu` helper that HunyuanVAE already routes through. This PR plumbs the helper into the three eligible direct-`silu(norm(x))` sites in `latent_upsampler.py`, picking up a **6.5×–14× kernel speedup on H100** (vs eager `silu(group_norm(x))`) without changing model outputs. The speedup factors into a ~1.55× SiLU+GroupNorm fusion win (constant across shapes) and a 4×–9× parallelization win that scales with per-group size; see [Speed Tests and Profiling](#speed-tests-and-profiling) for the decomposition. This also addresses the "kernel fusion instead of compiler-driven fusion" line under Performance Improvements in [Roadmap] SGLang-Diffusion (26 Q2) (#23035). ## Modifications - **`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/upsampler/latent_upsampler.py`** — route three `silu(norm(x))` sites through `apply_group_norm_silu`: | Site | Class | Hit per `LatentUpsampler.forward` | |---|---|---| | `initial_norm` + `initial_activation` | `LatentUpsampler.forward` (both 2D and 3D paths) | 1 | | `norm1` + `activation` | `ResBlock.forward` (one per ResBlock) | `2 * num_blocks_per_stage` | At the default `num_blocks_per_stage=4` this is **9 fused sites per upsampler call** (1 initial + 4 pre-upsample ResBlocks + 4 post-upsample ResBlocks). The second norm site inside `ResBlock` (`silu(norm2(x) + residual)` at line 118) is deliberately left on the eager path with an inline comment — the current `apply_group_norm_silu` helper only covers `silu(norm(x))`, not the `silu(norm(x) + residual)` pattern. A follow-up `apply_group_norm_add_silu` kernel would catch those remaining 8 sites per generation (doubling fusion coverage on this module); it's out of scope here. - **`python/sglang/jit_kernel/benchmark/diffusion/bench_group_norm_silu.py`** — add three LTX-2 latent upsampler shape cases (`ltx2_upsampler_small`, `ltx2_upsampler_pre_720p`, `ltx2_upsampler_post_720p`) at `num_groups=32`, bracketing the production shape range that Lightricks ships in the LTX-2.3 spatial upscaler checkpoints. The `post_720p` case is ~471M bf16 elements (~940 MB), making the kernel asymptotically HBM-bandwidth-bound. This bench is registered with `disabled="standalone benchmark"`, so it never appears in the regular CI memory budget. - **`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_latent_upsampler_group_norm_silu.py`** (new file) — 19 unit tests (10 CPU-fp32 wiring + 9 CUDA bf16/fp16 production-path parity, the CUDA tests gated on `torch.cuda.is_available()`). ## Accuracy Tests Zero-tolerance parity vs the original eager `silu(norm(x))` chain on CPU plus CUDA-tolerance parity on the production fast path: ```bash $ PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_latent_upsampler_group_norm_silu.py -v ... ================ 19 passed, 16 warnings in 8.89s ================ ``` **Coverage:** | Test | Tier | What it pins | |---|---|---| | `test_resblock_forward_parity` (3 parametrized) | CPU fp32 | `ResBlock.forward` output bit-identical (`atol=0.0, rtol=0.0`) to an explicit `activation(norm(x))` reference. CPU helper fallback path. | | `test_latent_upsampler_forward_parity` (2 parametrized) | CPU fp32 | Same for `LatentUpsampler.forward` across 2D + 3D conv paths. | | `test_resblock_fuses_exactly_one_site` | CPU fp32 | Patches `apply_group_norm_silu` and asserts exactly 1 call per `ResBlock.forward` (the residual-add `norm2` site must stay eager). | | `test_latent_upsampler_fuses_expected_sites` (3 parametrized) | CPU fp32 | Asserts call count equals `1 + 2 * num_blocks_per_stage` (i.e., 5, 9 across configs). | | `test_latent_upsampler_module_wires_fused_helper` | CPU fp32 | Smoke test: module imports `apply_group_norm_silu` at top level. | | **`test_resblock_forward_parity_cuda`** (4 parametrized) | **CUDA bf16/fp16** | `ResBlock.forward` on CUDA actually fires `triton_group_norm_silu`; output matches eager reference within kernel-side tolerance (bf16: `atol=7e-2, rtol=2e-2`; fp16: `atol=3e-3, rtol=3e-3`). | | **`test_latent_upsampler_forward_parity_cuda`** (4 parametrized) | **CUDA bf16/fp16** | Full `LatentUpsampler.forward` end-to-end parity. fp16 tolerance is intentionally looser (`atol=2e-2, rtol=1e-1`) to absorb the multi-layer fp16 quantization drift through the 8+ downstream conv layers; bf16 stays at kernel-side tolerance because bf16 has fp32-equivalent exponent range. | | **`test_resblock_actually_uses_triton_kernel_cuda`** | **CUDA bf16** | Patches `triton_group_norm_silu` and asserts `call_count >= 1` — explicit proof the production path doesn't silently fall back to eager. | The Triton kernel itself is already covered by `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/diffusion/test_group_norm_silu.py` (parametrized over `(shape, num_groups, dtype)`, registered via `register_cuda_ci`). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Measured on H100 SXM5 (`p5.48xlarge`, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`) via the bench script added in this PR: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python \ python/sglang/jit_kernel/benchmark/diffusion/bench_group_norm_silu.py \ --cases ltx2_upsampler_small,ltx2_upsampler_pre_720p,ltx2_upsampler_post_720p \ --dtypes bf16,fp16 --rounds 3 --warmup 25 --rep 100 ``` | case | dtype | shape | native (µs) | fused (µs) | speedup | |---|---|---|---:|---:|---:| | `ltx2_upsampler_small` | bf16 | 1×512×8×45×80 | 452.00 | 70.05 | **6.45×** | | `ltx2_upsampler_small` | fp16 | 1×512×8×45×80 | 451.49 | 69.22 | 6.52× | | `ltx2_upsampler_pre_720p` | bf16 | 1×512×16×90×160 | 3 468.27 | 261.87 | **13.24×** | | `ltx2_upsampler_pre_720p` | fp16 | 1×512×16×90×160 | 3 468.50 | 260.26 | 13.33× | | `ltx2_upsampler_post_720p` | bf16 | 1×512×16×180×320 | 13 710.72 | 987.52 | **13.88×** | | `ltx2_upsampler_post_720p` | fp16 | 1×512×16×180×320 | 13 717.54 | 984.90 | 13.93× | Geomean kernel speedup on LTX-2 upsampler shapes: **~10.7×**. **Where the speedup comes from.** A 13.9× speedup deserves scrutiny, so I forced the kernel onto its non-chunked one-pass path (same parallelism as PyTorch's `native_group_norm` CUDA kernel — one block per `(batch, group)` pair) and re-measured. The headline decomposes cleanly into two roughly multiplicative factors: | case | fusion-only
`native / one-pass` | parallelization
`one-pass / chunked` | total
`native / chunked` | |---|---:|---:|---:| | `ltx2_upsampler_small` | 1.56× | 3.94× | 6.13× | | `ltx2_upsampler_pre_720p` | 1.56× | 8.57× | 13.34× | | `ltx2_upsampler_post_720p` | 1.55× | 8.96× | 13.91× | 1. **Fusion contributes a flat ~1.55×**, constant across shapes — exactly what's expected for collapsing `F.silu(...)` into the apply pass: one full-tensor read + write saved per call, theoretical ceiling 2×. 2. **Chunked Welford parallelization contributes 4× → 9×**, scaling with per-group size. PyTorch's `native_group_norm` CUDA kernel (and Triton's own one-pass fallback) both launch one block per `(batch, group)` pair → **32 blocks on a 132-SM H100, ~24% SM occupancy**, with per-block work serialized across the entire `group_size` (461 K → 14.7 M elements as shape grows). The production `_launch_chunked` path splits each group into 8 192-element chunks reduced in parallel → **~57 600 programs for `post_720p`**, achieving **~2.87 TB/s = 86% of H100 HBM peak**. PyTorch's path tops out at ~12% of HBM peak on the same workload — not a memory-traffic problem, a parallelism problem. To reproduce the decomposition, override the threshold at runtime: ```python from sglang.jit_kernel.diffusion.triton import group_norm_silu as gns gns._LARGE_GROUP_THRESHOLD = 10**10 # force one-pass path ``` **Where this generalizes.** Smaller DiT-side `group_norm` call sites will see only the fusion-only **~1.5×** factor; the 6×+ headline numbers are specific to **large VAE/upsampler-style shapes** where per-group size is large enough that PyTorch's per-group kernel is severely under-parallelized on Hopper. The existing HunyuanVAE wiring that this PR follows has similar (large per-group) shapes, which is why the same kernel pays off there too. **E2E translation.** Each `LatentUpsampler.forward` call fires the helper 9 times — 5 sites at the pre-upsample resolution (1 initial + 4 pre-upsample ResBlocks) and 4 sites at the post-upsample resolution (4 post-upsample ResBlocks). For a 720p clip, naive multi-site savings: | Sites | Per-call saved (bf16) | × count | Subtotal | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Pre-upsample (initial + 4 pre ResBlocks) | ~3.2 ms | × 5 | ~16 ms | | Post-upsample (4 post ResBlocks) | ~12.7 ms | × 4 | ~51 ms | **Total saved per generation: ~67 ms** of `LatentUpsampler.forward` wall time on H100. The latent upsampler is one bounded subsystem of a multi-second LTX-2 generation, so relative E2E gain is small in absolute terms — but it represents 20–45% of the upsampler's own runtime budget, and every LTX-2 generation pays it. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #26735497021](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26735497021) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #26735496918](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26735496918)

title: [docs] DeepSeek-V4 cookbook: split Quantization axis, add H100 SGLang FP8
author: zijiexia
body:
## Motivation

The DeepSeek-V4 cookbook currently encodes the FP4 / FP8 choice into the hardware radio label itself (`H200 (FP8)` vs `H200 (FP4)`, etc.). That conflates two orthogonal dimensions, hides the H100 SGLang-FP8 path entirely, and forces the user to mentally translate between "hardware I have" and "checkpoint I want to run."

This PR splits the two: hardware row is just the GPU (B200 / B300 / GB200 / GB300 / H200 / H100), and a new **Quantization** row picks `FP4` (default) or `SGLang FP8`. SGLang FP8 is greyed out everywhere except H100 and H200, and on H100 the Pro variant stays greyed (only Flash FP8 ships).

It also fills in the previously-`Pending update` benchmark cells from the upstream cookbook rerun.

## Modifications

**`docs_new/src/snippets/autoregressive/deepseek-v4-deployment.jsx`** — structural refactor; no command changes.

- Hardware radio: drop `(FP4)` / `(FP8)` suffixes, remove the `h200-fp4` entry.
- New `Quantization` axis: `FP4` (default) / `SGLang FP8` (subtitle "H100/H200 only").
- Internal `effHw(hardware, quantization)` translates the new (hw, quant) pair back into the existing spec keys (`h200-fp4`, `h200`, `h100`, `h100-fp8`), so `HW_SIZE_SPEC` / `PD_TP_SPEC` / `VERIFIED_RECIPES` keep working unchanged.
- Constraint plumbing:
  - FP8 disabled when hardware is not H100/H200.
  - Pro disabled when hardware=H100 AND quant=FP8 (only Flash ships).
  - cp / pd-disagg disabled on Marlin FP4 Hopper paths (existing) and on h100-fp8 (new TBD).
  - `handleRadioChange` auto-falls-back stale selections (FP8 → FP4 on non-Hopper, Pro → Flash on H100+FP8, cp/pd-disagg → low-latency on Marlin / h100-fp8).
- New `h100-fp8|small` spec entry + verified recipes (low-latency / balanced / max-throughput). Slug `sgl-project/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8`, TP=8 single-node. The general command branch is extended with `isHopperFp8(effHw)` so flashinfer-mxfp4 / chunked-prefill / Blackwell-only flags don't leak into the H100 FP8 path.

**`docs_new/cookbook/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V4.mdx`**

- Pro intro-table row reworded as `H200 8 GPU (FP4) or 16 GPU (SGLang FP8)`.
- Rewrote the Hopper note around the new Quantization axis; now covers H100 + the Flash-only constraint.
- §4.2 Reasoning Parser / Tool Calling examples wrapped in `<Accordion>` (code + example output as separate collapsible blocks).
- Filled real `bench_serving` / GSM8K / MMLU numbers (sglang 0.5.12).
- Reorganized §5 to match the source cookbook: §5.1 Accuracy (GSM8K, MMLU) first, §5.2 Speed unified with Hopper / Blackwell h4 sub-sections + shared `random`-dataset intro.
- Annotated B200 Max-Throughput card as `(MegaMoE W4A4)` with a hint to flip the MegaMoE toggle, since the default Max-Throughput recipe (`deepep`) does not reproduce the 4860 tok/s number.

## Accuracy Tests

No model code changed. The MDX includes the actual GSM8K / MMLU numbers from the upstream cookbook for DeepSeek-V4-Pro (FP4, low-latency):

- **GSM8K**: B300 0.965, H200 0.975.
- **MMLU** (weighted avg over 10 subjects, 1369 questions): B300 0.879, H200 0.893.

MMLU averages cross-checked against the per-subject × `#q` weighted sum.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No engine code changed; this PR only restructures the UI generator and the cookbook copy. Bench numbers shown in the cookbook were measured upstream on sglang 0.5.12:

- H200 (Flash FP4, TP=4) Low-Latency: mean E2E 1596.65 ms / mean TPOT 3.50 ms / accept length 2.96.
- H200 (Flash FP4, TP=4) Max-Throughput: 2574.64 output tok/s (= 644 tok/s/GPU).
- B200 (Flash FP4, TP=4) Low-Latency: mean E2E 1523.83 ms / mean TPOT 3.40 ms / accept length 2.73.
- B200 (Flash FP4, TP=4 · MegaMoE W4A4) Max-Throughput: 4860.54 output tok/s (= 1215 tok/s/GPU).

Internal-consistency checks pass on every block (Input + Output = Total throughput; Output throughput × duration = generated tokens; mean E2E × num-prompts ≈ benchmark duration).

## Command-Generator Compatibility Verification

Pinned `main` (`a24c374f8`) and the worktree's JSX through esbuild, then exercised `generateCommand` across the full reachable Cartesian product (7 hardware × 2 sizes × 5 recipes × 5 toggle combos − 40 UI-unreachable cells = **310 combos**). All 310 outputs are byte-for-byte identical between main and this branch under the translation:

| main `hardware` | this branch (`hardware`, `quantization`) |
| --- | --- |
| `h200` | `h200` + `fp8` |
| `h200-fp4` | `h200` + `fp4` |
| `h100` | `h100` + `fp4` |
| `b200` / `b300` / `gb200` / `gb300` | unchanged + `fp4` |

The only net-new combos are `h100 + fp8 + Flash` for the three core recipes. No existing combo is altered or removed.

- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). _N/A — docs-only._
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). _N/A — no engine change._

title: perf: eliminate CUDA syncs in VLM embed path
author: Jumiar
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
During VLM (Vision Language Model) inference with SGLang, the multimodal embedding path introduces unnecessary CUDA stream synchronizations that stall the GPU pipeline. Profiling identified three sync points in mm_utils.py:

 1. torch.where(mask) in embed_mm_inputs — torch.where must synchronize to determine the output tensor size on CPU before allocating the index tensor.
 2. mask.sum().item() in _adjust_embedding_length — .item() forces a device-to-host transfer and sync to read a scalar value.
 3. tensor_hash re-computation in hash_feature — When features are transferred via ShmPointerMMData (shared memory), the SHA256 hash is recomputed from scratch on the receiver side, even though the sender already computed it.

 These syncs serialize GPU execution and degrade throughput, especially for multi-image and video workloads.
<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

 1. Replace torch.where with masked_scatter_ (embed_mm_inputs)

 - Before: torch.where(mask.squeeze(-1))[0] extracts indices, then input_embeds[indices] = embedding scatters values.
 - After: input_embeds.masked_scatter_(mask.expand_as(input_embeds), embedding) performs the same scatter without materializing indices.
 - Why it works: masked_scatter_ fills True positions in row-major order, which is identical to the sorted-index assignment from torch.where. The mask shape [seq_len, 1] is expanded to [seq_len, hidden_dim], ensuring full-row fills match the old behavior. _adjust_embedding_length is called upstream to guarantee src has the correct element count.

 2. CPU-side multimodal token counting (_count_mm_tokens_from_offsets)

 - Before: mask.sum().item() counts True values in the multimodal mask, requiring a GPU→CPU sync.
 - After: New function _count_mm_tokens_from_offsets computes the same count purely from CPU-side offset metadata (items_offset_list, prefix_length, extend_length) using inclusive-range overlap arithmetic.
 - Fallback: When EVS (Efficient Variable-length Sequence) modifies input_ids — detected via Python object identity — the original offsets become stale and the code falls back to mask.sum().item(). EVS only triggers in the legacy (non-per-image) path.
 - Legacy path refactor: _get_chunked_prefill_embedding now returns a third value evs_modified: bool, early-returning to get_chunked_prefill_embedding_legacy for non-per-image items to cleanly separate the two code paths.

 3. Precomputed hash forwarding (ShmPointerMMData)

 - Before: hash_feature calls tensor_hash([f.tensor]) (SHA256) on every ShmPointerMMData access, even though the hash was already computed at image processing time.
 - After: ShmPointerMMData.__init__ accepts an optional precomputed_hash. wrap_shm_features forwards item.hash from the processing stage. hash_feature returns the cached hash directly, skipping SHA256.
 - Serialization: __getstate__/__setstate__ preserve the hash through shared memory transport. __setstate__ uses .get() for backward compatibility.
 - List features: Per-element precomputed hashes are intentionally not forwarded for list[ShmPointerMMData] — the joint hash must cover all elements, so individual hashes are not applicable.

 4. Bug fix: empty list guard in hash_feature

 Added len(f) > 0 checks before isinstance(f[0], ...) to prevent IndexError on empty feature lists.

 5. CI fix: Kimi-VL OOM workaround

 Added --mem-fraction-static=0.40 to the TestKimiVLServer test config. This addresses a pre-existing OOM in MoonViT's sdpa_attention that peaks ~40GB on 4-image requests — reproduced on main without this PR.
<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

title: Implement online nvfp4 quantization
author: zianglih
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
@humansand
Add online NVFP4 MoE weight quantization under the `--quantization nvfp4_online` interface.

After #22918, FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE can use runtime per-token activation scaling, so SGLang no longer needs a calibrated static activation FP32 scale for this path. The `nvfp4_online` interface is explicitly a load-time conversion mode: weights still use static NVFP4 block scales plus static per-tensor FP32 scales, while activations use runtime per-token FP32 scales. This makes it possible to load BF16/FP16 or FP8 checkpoints and quantize eligible MoE expert weights to NVFP4 during weight loading, instead of requiring a pre-quantized NVFP4 checkpoint.

The intended initial scope is narrow: Blackwell GPUs only, MoE only, no dense linear quantization, and only the FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE backends (`flashinfer_trtllm` and `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`).

## Modifications

- Add the `nvfp4_online` quantization method for online NVFP4 MoE expert weight quantization.
- Quantize eligible expert weights as they are loaded, avoiding a separate whole-checkpoint conversion step and keeping peak memory lower during startup.
- Use static per-tensor FP32 weight scales and runtime per-token activation scales; no activation-scale calibration is required.
- Support FP8 checkpoints by dequantizing eligible FP8 expert weights during load and requantizing them to NVFP4.
- Keep dense linear layers in their source precision or checkpoint quantization path; only MoE experts are converted to NVFP4.
- Add `SGLANG_FP4_IGNORED_LAYERS` so users can keep selected MoE layers or shared experts high precision.
- Default the MoE runner backend to `flashinfer_trtllm` when `--quantization nvfp4_online` is used without an explicit backend, and error out for unsupported backend, hardware, or MoE TP configurations.
- Thread per-token activation metadata through FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE quant info and add registered coverage with Qwen3-Next FP8 online NVFP4 per-token activation serving plus GSM8K accuracy.

title: GLM-4.7-Flash: standalone MLA impl and MLA NextN/MTP
author: zRzRzRzRzRzRzR
body:
## Motivation
  
  `glm4_moe_lite` (GLM-4.7-Flash, MLA) had a few issues when running with the
  native SGLang implementation:

  - It subclassed the `deepseek_v2.py` wrapper classes, so DSV4/DSA/CP changes
    there kept leaking in and breaking it.
  - The MoE gate computed routing logits in the model dtype (bf16), but GLM
    requires an FP32 gate projection — wrong-precision routing corrupts output.
  - With MTP/EAGLE speculative decoding, the draft (NextN) for this MLA model was
    mapped to the **GQA** `Glm4MoeForCausalLMNextN`, causing a KV-cache shape
    mismatch during draft CUDA graph capture:
    `value tensor of shape [bs, 5, 64] cannot be broadcast to [bs, 5, 256]`.

  ## Changes

  - **`glm4_moe_lite.py`**: rewritten as a standalone model that no longer
    inherits the `deepseek_v2.py` wrapper classes. It mirrors `glm4_moe.py`'s
    structure/style and only reuses the stable shared pieces — `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA`
    (composition) and `DeepseekV2WeightLoaderMixin`. Gate now does FP32 projection,
  - **`glm4_moe_lite_nextn.py`** (new): MLA-based NextN draft
    (`Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLMNextN`) built from `Glm4MoeLiteDecoderLayer`, passing
    the `zero_allocator` MLA requires (mirrors `deepseek_nextn.py`).
  - **`model_config.py`**: route the `Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM` draft to
    `Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLMNextN` (instead of the GQA NextN), and add the new
    NextN arch to the MLA detection list (draft arch is rewritten before MLA
    detection runs).

title: [refactor] unify cuda-graph capture/replay across attention backends
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

\`init_forward_metadata_capture_cuda_graph\` and \`init_forward_metadata_replay_cuda_graph\` share substantial logic across every attention backend but were maintained as independent copies. This caused real divergence: \`WaveAttnBackend\` silently skipped \`get_num_kv_splits\` during capture, \`CutlassMLABackend\` had a spurious \`assert seq_lens_cpu is not None\` (the parameter was never read), and \`FlashInferAttnBackend\` duplicated ~240 lines of per-mode dispatch between the two methods.

## Modifications

**WaveAttnBackend** (Pattern A — capture delegates to replay):
- Add \`_build_cuda_graph_forward_metadata\` to assemble \`ForwardMetadata\` from pre-allocated buffers.
- \`capture\` early-returns for the multi-step spec-decode path, then delegates all buffer writes to \`replay\` and calls \`_build_cuda_graph_forward_metadata\` to freeze the result.
- Fixes a latent bug: \`get_num_kv_splits\` was not called during capture but was called during replay, causing inconsistent state.

**CutlassMLABackend** (Pattern A):
- Same capture-delegates-to-replay pattern for the decode path.
- Removes spurious \`assert seq_lens_cpu is not None\` from replay (never used in the body).

**FlashInferAttnBackend** (Pattern B — prepare + replay):
- Extract \`_create_decode_wrappers\` / \`_create_prefill_wrappers\` factories that own the wrapper construction and buffer binding.
- Extract \`_prepare_cuda_graph_metadata\`: creates wrappers, stores \`[bs]\`, sets \`forward_metadata\`. \`fast_decode_plan\` is installed **after** \`replay()\` since it depends on \`_cached_module\` set by the initial full \`begin_forward\` call.
- \`capture\` collapses to \`_prepare_cuda_graph_metadata()\` + \`replay()\` with no branches.
- \`replay\`: merges \`is_target_verify\` and \`is_draft_extend\` branches (identical logic).

**FlashInferMLAAttnBackend**:
- Merges the \`is_target_verify\` / \`is_draft_extend\` branches in both capture and replay — they are byte-for-byte identical in both methods.

Backends using Pattern C (create metadata in capture, update in-place in replay): \`flashattention_backend\`, \`trtllm_mha_backend\`, \`trtllm_mla_backend\`, \`flashmla_backend\`, \`deepseek_v4_backend\`, \`aiter_backend\`, \`dsa_backend\` — deferred to a follow-up PR as they require a different approach.

## Accuracy Tests

Pure refactor — no changes to kernel dispatch, index computation, or model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel changes. The only behavioral difference is that \`WaveAttnBackend\` now correctly calls \`get_num_kv_splits\` during CUDA graph capture (matching what replay already did), which may improve decode accuracy for that backend.

## GB300 Validation (4×B200 NVL4)

Ran all nightly GB300 tests manually on \`cheng/refactor/unify-attn-backend-cuda-graph-capture-replay\` to validate \`CutlassMLABackend\` capture/replay on real B200 hardware:

| DeepSeek-V3.2 BF16 (TP4, TP4+DPA, TP4+DPA+MTP) | CutlassMLA | ✅ PASS | 49:05 |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 NVFP4 (TP4, TP4+DPA, TP4+DPA+MTP) | CutlassMLA | ✅ PASS | 1:15:36 |
| GLM5 FP8 (TP4, TP4+DPA, TP4+DPA+MTP) | CutlassMLA | ✅ PASS | 1:06:16 |
| GLM5 NVFP4 (TP4, TP4+DPA, TP4+DPA+MTP) | CutlassMLA | ✅ PASS | 1:37:55 |
| Kimi-K2.5 BF16 (TP4, TP4+DPA) | CutlassMLA | ✅ PASS | 1:29:00 |
| Kimi-K2.5 NVFP4 (TP4, TP4+DPA) | CutlassMLA | ✅ PASS | 1:32:38 |

title: [SRT] fix flashInfer allreduce fusion not used on blackwell
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- Detect FlashInfer allreduce-fusion API capabilities before passing version-specific kwargs.
- Keep subgroup rendezvous on newer FlashInfer while allowing older builds to use comm-backend-only workspace creation.

## Analysis

It fixes the TP8 runtime communication path used by the Qwen3.5 397B Blackwell benchmark.

In the tested B200 environment, SGLang was launched with `--enable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion`, but the installed FlashInfer build rejected newer kwargs such as `group` and `trigger_completion_at_end`. SGLang then logged the error and disabled FlashInfer allreduce fusion, so the benchmark was not actually exercising the requested fusion path.

This PR checks the installed FlashInfer signatures once and only passes supported kwargs. Newer FlashInfer keeps subgroup rendezvous; older builds keep using allreduce fusion instead of silently falling back.

Latency distribution after this change shows that the remaining OCRBench TTFT gap vs vLLM is mostly first-serving-batch/cold runtime, not the gRPC preprocessed-pixel path: SGLang OCRBench first 100 requests average about 6.36s TTFT, while later requests average about 1.66s. The same-env vLLM run is about 3.91s / 3.55s for the same split. Text-only is still a separate baseline gap where SGLang remains slower than vLLM.

## Benchmark Results

Qwen3.5 397B FP8, TP8, B200, SMG gRPC, cuda-ipc enabled, `limit=200`, `concurrency=100`, `max_tokens=5`. Baseline includes the gRPC preprocessed-input hash/dispatch PR (#26105); this PR is measured on top.

| Scenario | Baseline TTFT mean | This PR TTFT mean | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ocrbench-text | 1.037s | 0.690s | -33.5% |
| synthetic-text | 0.807s | 0.685s | -15.1% |
| ocrbench | 4.111s | 4.010s | -2.5% |

Same-env vLLM reference: OCRBench TTFT mean is 3.730s, E2E is 4.057s. With this PR SGLang is still slower on OCRBench TTFT at 4.010s, but close on E2E at 4.099s and faster on TPOT at 0.0165s vs vLLM 0.0773s.

## Tests

- `uvx ruff@0.15.1 check --select=F401,F821 --fix python/sglang/srt/layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py`
- `uvx black==26.1.0 --check python/sglang/srt/layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py`
- `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py`

title: [GDN] Support SM100 CuTeDSL GDN Prefill Kernel
author: yuan-luo
body: ## Summary - Port the SM100 (Blackwell) CuTeDSL chunkwise GDN prefill kernel from vLLM PR [#43273](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43273) into SGLang as a new option for `--linear-attn-prefill-backend cutedsl`. - Three CuTeDSL kernels (`kkt_inv_uw`, `h`, `o`) plus shared Blackwell helpers (`cute_utils/`: tcgen05 / tmem / TMA bulk-swizzle / PTX BF16 wrappers). - 1.7x geomean kernel speedup over Triton FLA baseline on Qwen3-Next prefill shapes (B200, bfloat16). - +12.7% total throughput and -17% mean TTFT on Qwen3.6-27B TP=1 end-to-end (input=4096, output=256, 64 concurrent prompts). - SM90 path is unchanged: when the user picks `cutedsl` on Hopper, the dispatcher transparently falls back to Triton for prefill (decode keeps the existing CuTeDSL fused recurrent kernel). ## Motivation vLLM PR [#43273](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43273) introduces a Blackwell-specific CuTeDSL GDN prefill kernel that beats both Triton FLA and FlashInfer's GDN Blackwell path in the multi-request / mixed-length / lower-head-count workloads that production serving actually sees. SGLang's existing `gdn_cutedsl.py` only wired the decode path; prefill on Blackwell was stuck on Triton. This PR closes that gap by porting the upstream kernel byte-for-byte under `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/kernels/gdn_blackwell/`, with the integration cost limited to a new `extend()` method on `CuteDSLGDNKernel` and an additional dispatch branch in `GDNKernelDispatcher`. The kernels follow the design of FLA: kkt_inv_uw_kernel: fusion of FLA's chunk_scaled_dot_kkt_fwd(), solve_tril(), and recompute_w_u_fwd() h_kernel: FLA's chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h() o_kernel: FLA's chunk_fwd_o() This kernel also provides native support for BF16 state (no extra BF16->FP32 casting) Kernel timeline (just to illustrate the pipeline, not drawn correct to relative latencies) **Note** The following diagrams are extracted from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43273. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/cute_utils/` — shared Blackwell helpers (3 files: tcgen05 / tmem / TMA-bulk-swizzle wrappers and PTX BF16 SIMD ops). Sourced from `vllm/cute_utils/` (Apache-2.0). - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/kernels/gdn_blackwell/` — 4 files: `kernel_kkt_inv_uw.py`, `kernel_h.py`, `kernel_o.py`, and the top-level `chunk_gated_delta_rule_cutedsl` + `prepare_metadata_cutedsl` entry. Sourced from `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/gdn_chunk_cutedsl/`. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/kernels/gdn_cutedsl.py` — `CuteDSLGDNKernel.extend()` added; `decode()` unchanged. Adapts to the existing SGLang contract: l2norm Q/K outside the kernel, gather initial state from the pool, build `chunk_indices` / `chunk_offsets` via `prepare_metadata_cutedsl`, scatter final state back. Lazy import keeps SM90 boxes able to construct the kernel for decode only. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py` — `GDNKernelDispatcher` learns to route prefill through the CuTeDSL kernel when `prefill_backend=cutedsl` and `cutedsl_kernel.supports_prefill` is True (SM>=10); else it logs a one-line warning and falls back to Triton. - `test/registered/attention/test_gdn_prefill_cutedsl.py` — correctness test (6 cases: `num_seqs in {1,5,257}` x `state_dtype in {bf16, fp32}`) against `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule` as ground truth. Registered for CI via `register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="base-b", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")` and module-level `pytest.skip` on SM<10. - `benchmark/bench_linear_attention/bench_gdn_prefill_cutedsl.py` — Triton-vs-CuteDSL correctness sweep (19 shapes) plus `do_bench_cudagraph` perf table. ## Benchmarks ### Kernel microbench NVIDIA B200, bfloat16, `do_bench_cudagraph`, Qwen3-Next preset (K=V=128, pool_size=256). | B | H | T/seq | T_tot | triton (ms) | TFLOPS | TB/s | cutedsl (ms) | TFLOPS | TB/s | speedup | |----:|----:|------:|-------:|------------:|-------:|-------:|-------------:|-------:|-------:|--------:| | 4 | 16 | 256 | 1024 | 0.656 | 1.64 | 0.04 | 0.367 | 2.92 | 0.07 | 1.79x | | 4 | 32 | 256 | 1024 | 1.267 | 1.70 | 0.04 | 0.696 | 3.08 | 0.07 | 1.82x | | 16 | 16 | 256 | 4096 | 0.750 | 5.72 | 0.13 | 0.427 | 10.07 | 0.24 | 1.76x | | 16 | 32 | 256 | 4096 | 1.472 | 5.84 | 0.14 | 0.831 | 10.34 | 0.24 | 1.77x | | 32 | 16 | 256 | 8192 | 0.888 | 9.67 | 0.23 | 0.516 | 16.63 | 0.39 | 1.72x | | 32 | 32 | 256 | 8192 | 1.742 | 9.86 | 0.23 | 1.000 | 17.18 | 0.40 | 1.74x | | 64 | 16 | 256 | 16384 | 1.155 | 14.87 | 0.35 | 0.683 | 25.17 | 0.59 | 1.69x | | 64 | 32 | 256 | 16384 | 2.283 | 15.05 | 0.35 | 1.335 | 25.74 | 0.61 | 1.71x | | 128 | 16 | 256 | 32768 | 1.693 | 20.29 | 0.48 | 1.012 | 33.94 | 0.80 | 1.67x | | 128 | 32 | 256 | 32768 | 3.371 | 20.39 | 0.48 | 2.002 | 34.33 | 0.81 | 1.68x | | 4 | 16 | 1024 | 4096 | 0.751 | 5.72 | 0.10 | 0.414 | 10.38 | 0.18 | 1.82x | | 4 | 32 | 1024 | 4096 | 1.482 | 5.80 | 0.10 | 0.791 | 10.86 | 0.19 | 1.87x | | 32 | 16 | 1024 | 32768 | 1.657 | 20.74 | 0.37 | 0.876 | 39.22 | 0.69 | 1.89x | | 32 | 32 | 1024 | 32768 | 3.301 | 20.82 | 0.37 | 1.719 | 39.97 | 0.71 | 1.92x | Geomean speedup across all 14 shapes: **~1.78x**. Range: 1.67x to 1.92x. No regression on any shape. ### End-to-end Qwen3.6-27B (`Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B`), B200 TP=1, `sglang.bench_serving --dataset-name random --num-prompts 64 --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1.0`. Both backends use `--linear-attn-decode-backend triton` (decode unchanged); only `--linear-attn-prefill-backend` differs. | Metric | Triton | CuteDSL | Delta | |------------------------------|--------:|--------:|---------:| | Bench duration (s) | 20.55 | 18.24 | -11.2% | | Total token throughput (t/s) | 13,557 | 15,273 | +12.7% | | Input throughput (t/s) | 12,759 | 14,375 | +12.7% | | Output throughput (t/s) | 797 | 898 | +12.7% | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 8,243 | 6,842 | -17.0% | | P99 TTFT (ms) | 14,890 | 12,681 | -14.8% | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 48.0 | 44.5 | -7.4% | | Mean E2E latency (ms) | 20,489 | 18,181 | -11.3% | Server log for the CuteDSL run confirms `Using CuTe DSL GDN prefill (Blackwell)`. ### Accuracy (GSM8K) `python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200 --port 30000` (5-shot, temperature=0, greedy decode, same prompts). | Backend | Accuracy | Invalid | Latency (s) | |------------------|---------:|--------:|------------:| | Triton (run 1) | 0.620 | 0.235 | 14.81 | | Triton (run 2) | 0.640 | 0.240 | 13.87 | | CuteDSL | 0.725 | 0.120 | 14.62 | No regression. The +9 pp accuracy delta on this 200-question subset is driven by a lower invalid (unparseable answer) rate from CuteDSL: with greedy decode at temperature=0, the chunked accumulation order differs between the two backends, which propagates into different reasoning trajectories. Both backends sit in the expected range for a 27B model on 5-shot GSM8K; treat the gap as run-to-run numerical variance rather than a quality claim. ## How to use ``` python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp 1 \ --linear-attn-prefill-backend cutedsl \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` The flag is also accepted on SM90 (Hopper); the dispatcher transparently falls back to Triton for prefill and prints one info-level line. This means users can pick `cutedsl` uniformly across hardware without per-host configuration. ## Requirements - CUDA runtime >= 13. - `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.5.0` — **the `[cu13]` extra matters**. The base `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.5.0` wheel does not pull in the matching `cuda-bindings 13.2.0` / `cuda-pathfinder` / `numpy 2.4.x` set, and the kernel fails to compile inside `cute.copy` (asserts in `_ods_common._get_value`) without them. Consider updating `requirements/cuda.txt` accordingly. - `quack-kernels>=0.3.3`. ## Limitations and future work - The ported kernel hard-codes `BT=64` and `K_dim=V_dim=128`. The wrapper asserts `head_k_dim==128` at first call; a clearer error path may be added later. - KDA (Kimi Delta Attention, used by Kimi-Linear) cannot reuse this kernel: GDN's forget gate is per-head scalar `[T, Hv]`, while KDA's is per-K-dim `[T, H, K]`. The kernel's `Gamma[i,j] = exp(g_cu[i] - g_cu[j])` is structurally per-head. A KDA-specific Blackwell kernel would need to add a K dim to `Gamma` and to the H/state-evolution and output kernels; this is left as follow-up. - Two reviewer flags from the upstream Gemini bot on the source PR are not yet addressed there (TMEM hardcoded base addresses; an H-kernel TMEM dealloc race). These carry over to this port; we should re-sync once upstream lands fixes. - Decode path is unchanged. Existing `cutedsl_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` continues to serve decode on SM90+ via the unmodified `CuteDSLGDNKernel.decode()`. ## Test plan - [x] Correctness: `pytest test/registered/attention/test_gdn_prefill_cutedsl.py -v` on B200 — 6/6 pass. - [x] Regression: `pytest test/registered/attention/test_kda_kernels.py -v` on B200 — 6/6 pass (KDA path unaffected). - [x] Standalone kernel sweep: `bench_gdn_prefill_cutedsl.py --mode correctness` — 19/19 PASS across varying B, T_per_seq, H, sparse vs sequential pool indices. - [x] SM90 fallback: `--linear-attn-prefill-backend cutedsl` on H200 logs the fallback and uses Triton for extend (decode keeps CuteDSL). - [x] End-to-end correctness: GSM8K 5-shot @ 200 questions on Qwen3.6-27B — no regression. - [x] End-to-end perf: Qwen3.6-27B TP=1 random workload — measured throughput / TTFT / TPOT. - [ ] Update `requirements/cuda.txt` to pin `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.5.0` (follow-up). - [ ] CLI flag plumbing: ensure `linear_attn_prefill_backend` is wired through any model-specific entry points (Qwen3-Next, Kimi-Linear) — verified for the dispatcher; spot-check other call sites in review. ## Credits The CuTeDSL kernel code under `gdn_blackwell/` and `cute_utils/` is a near-byte-identical port from [vllm-project/vllm#43273](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43273) by [@gau-nernst](https://github.com/gau-nernst), originally written in CUDA C++ by team CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN for the MLSys 2026 FlashInfer Kernel competition and rewritten in CuTeDSL by the vLLM PR author. The only changes here are import paths (`vllm.cute_utils` -> `sglang.srt.layers.attention.cute_utils`; `vllm.triton_utils` -> `triton`). License preserved as Apache-2.0. Many thanks to the upstream authors. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #26396897793](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26396897793) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #26396897621](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26396897621)

title: [GDN] Optimize prefill QKV split dispatch
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

This patch reduces Qwen3.6 GDN prefill QKV split overhead observed during profiling:

- add a Triton `fused_qkv_split_gdn_prefill_kernel` to split post-conv GDN Q/K/V into contiguous FLA prefill tensors in one launch;
- route CUDA GDN prefill tensors, including strided post-conv views, through that fused split path with a guarded fallback to the previous `torch.split(...).view(...)` path;
- add a focused `bench_gdn_qkv_split.py` benchmark for contiguous and strided inputs;
- tune the single safe `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` config to `BV=32`, `num_warps=4`, `num_stages=4`, while keeping env overrides for validation.

The chunk-h autotune remains single-config because this kernel updates the state pool in place; multi-config autotune can corrupt the state pool during benchmarking.

## Benchmark

Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8`  
Hardware: single NVIDIA B200, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1`  
Workload: default SOTA serving workload, 80 random prompts, `--disable-radix-cache` for the winning SGLang lane.

| Framework / candidate | Chat 1000/1000 out tok/s | Chat TTFT ms | Chat TPOT ms | Long 8000/1000 out tok/s | Long TTFT ms | Long TPOT ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SGLang baseline best | 7205.38 | 858.08 | 10.20 | 4243.72 | 4014.37 | 14.55 |
| vLLM latest best | 6480.19 | 1975.60 | 10.33 | 3993.22 | 4275.92 | 15.35 |
| SGLang patched GDN fused split + w4/s4 | 7396.73 | 709.25 | 10.07 | 4353.39 | 3820.19 | 14.28 |
| TensorRT-LLM latest | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A |

TensorRT-LLM latest could not serve this checkpoint because the bundled Transformers stack does not recognize `model_type=qwen3_5_moe`.

## Kernel Profile

| Row | Baseline SGLang | Patched SGLang |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` | 24.21 ms / 90 = 269.00 us | 19.69 ms / 90 = 218.78 us |
| FLA/GDN prep copy | 18.97 ms | removed; replaced by 3.33 ms fused split |
| `fused_qkv_split_gdn_prefill_kernel` | N/A | 3.33 ms / 90 = 37.00 us |

## QKV Split Microbenchmark

H200 smoke benchmark for the new split path, `seq_len=8192`, `qkv_dim=6144`, bf16:

| Layout | Baseline us | Fused us | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| contiguous | 124.54 | 52.41 | 2.38x |
| strided | 349.45 | 338.48 | 1.03x |

## Accuracy

Full-dataset regression runs used the same model and 1x B200 setup. The eval command used `--chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'`; MMLU used `--max-tokens 512`, and GSM8K used `--max-tokens 1024 --num-shots 5`.

| Variant | MMLU full | GSM8K full | Delta vs baseline |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline SGLang | 0.436761 | 0.954338 | - |
| SGLang patched GDN fused split + w4/s4 | 0.437687 | 0.955860 | +0.000926 MMLU / +0.001522 GSM8K |

## Validation

- `python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/jit_kernel/triton/gdn_fused_proj.py python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/fla/chunk_delta_h.py python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py`
- `python3 benchmark/bench_linear_attention/bench_gdn_qkv_split.py --seq-len 8192 --warmup 10 --iters 50` on `ion8-h200`, GPU 0.
- Real-model serving benchmark on `ion-b200`, single B200.
- Torch profiler comparison against the strongest vLLM latest-image candidate.
- Full MMLU and GSM8K regression runs for baseline and patched SGLang.

title: [perf][spec decoding] Skip full-vocab softmax in EAGLE draft when topk == 1
author: Qiaolin-Yu
body:
The greedy spec-decoding path (`--speculative-eagle-topk 1`) currently runs a full-vocab `torch.softmax` + `torch.max` for every draft step and again for `_draft_extend_for_decode` (both eager and inside the captured draft-extend cuda graph). With topk == 1 the draft tree is a single path, so `topk_p` does not feed back into any ranking decision (see `spec_utils._select_top_k_tokens_later` — the scores are multiplied along a degenerate single branch). `topk_index = argmax(logits)` is identical to `argmax(softmax(logits))`, so the softmax is purely wasted work.

Profile (Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 / TP=4 / 80K ctx / EAGLE3 3-step / bs=1): `cunn_SoftMaxForward` was ~43 µs/call. It fired 2× per DRAFT_DECODE (steps 0 and 1 of the loop), 1× per `_draft_extend_for_decode`, and 1× inside the captured DRAFT_EXTEND graph — ~175 µs/cycle total. After this change all three call sites use argmax with a constant `topk_p = ones`.

Patched sites:
- `eagle_worker_v2.py:draft_forward` — inner draft step loop, runs inside the captured DRAFT_DECODE cuda graph.
- `eagle_worker_v2.py:_draft_extend_for_decode` — post-graph reorganization after the draft-extend replay.
- `eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:capture_one_batch_size` — the softmax+topk burned into the DRAFT_EXTEND cuda graph itself.

All three are gated by `if self.topk == 1`; multi-path tree behavior (topk > 1) is unchanged.

Measured on the canonical workload (10 prompts, max-concurrency=1, no `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`):

  metric         baseline   patched   delta
  Mean TPOT      2.41 ms    2.36 ms   -0.05 ms
  Med  TPOT      2.37 ms    2.34 ms   -0.03 ms
  1000/Mean      414.9      423.7     +8.8 tok/s (+2.1%)
  1000/Med       421.9      427.4     +5.5 tok/s (+1.3%)
  accept_length  3.92       3.94      unchanged (within noise)

GPU-side `cunn_SoftMaxForward` count drops to 0 in both DRAFT_DECODE and DRAFT_EXTEND kernel breakdowns.

title: [dsv4] fix multi-step draft on non-cuda-graph path
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary
- Fix DSv4 EAGLE multi-step draft on the non-cuda-graph path (`init_forward_metadata`); the assert `req_pool_indices.shape[0] == seq_lens.shape[0] == out_cache_loc.shape[0]` in `init_forward_metadata_decode` previously fired with `out_cache_loc.shape=[bs * topk * num_steps]` vs `seq_lens.shape=[bs]`
- Introduce a shared per-step layout helper so `EagleWorkerV2.draft_forward` and `DeepseekV4AttnBackend` agree on the slice convention

## Background
- DSv4 backend bakes per-step KV write targets (`c4_out_loc` / `c128_out_loc`) into the attention metadata at `init_forward_metadata` time — unlike FlashMLA / FlashInfer / Triton, which consume `out_cache_loc` only in `forward_*`
- The default cuda-graph capture/replay route bypasses `init_forward_metadata`, so the bug was only reachable with `--disable-cuda-graph`. PR #23882 introduced the path; not exercised by CI

## Fix
- `per_step_draft_out_cache_loc` in `eagle_utils.py`: single source of truth for the `[bs, topk, num_steps] -> [num_steps, bs * topk]` view, with a shape assert
- `EagleWorkerV2.draft_forward`: call the helper instead of inline reshape
- `DeepseekV4AttnBackend.init_forward_metadata`: when running as a multi-step draft sub-backend (`topk > 0 and speculative_num_steps > 1`), select this step's slice via the helper before calling `init_forward_metadata_decode`

title: [perf][spec decoding] Skip common_template in TRTLLMMLAMultiStepDraftBackend init
author: Qiaolin-Yu
body:
`FlashInferMLAMultiStepDraftBackend.{init_forward_metadata, init_forward_metadata_replay_cuda_graph}` go through `common_template`, which launches the `generate_draft_decode_kv_indices` triton kernel and slices `spec_info.kv_indptr/kv_indices` for each draft step. title: [Spec] fix EAGLE v2 verify metadata init order on non-cuda-graph path
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary
- `EagleVerifyInput.prepare_for_v2_verify` called `init_forward_metadata` on the non-cuda-graph path **before** `_forward_raw -> prepare_mlp_sync_batch` padded the forward batch
- `eagle_worker_v2.verify` then passed `skip_attn_backend_init=True` unconditionally, so the eventual `forward_extend` skipped re-init
- Metadata reflected pre-pad shapes while the actual forward consumed post-pad `input_ids` / `out_cache_loc`; backends that bake those shapes into metadata (DSv4 indexer's c4/c128 write targets + symbolic-shape TVM kernel) crashed on shape mismatch

## Fix
- `eagle_info_v2.py`: drop the eager `init_forward_metadata` in the non-cuda-graph branch (cuda-graph branch still runs `replay_prepare` in `plan_stream`)
- `eagle_worker_v2.py`: pass `skip_attn_backend_init=can_run_cuda_graph` so the non-cuda-graph path inits in `forward_extend` after `prepare_mlp_sync_batch`. Same pattern as `model_runner.forward_idle:3104-3108`

## Impact
- cuda-graph path (default): unchanged
- non-cuda-graph path: correctness restored; minor perf cost (init moves off `plan_stream`). Manual reproducer (`test_disaggregation_dsv4.py` + `--disable-cuda-graph`) now passes GSM8K (score 0.965)

title: [observability] add Ray metric backend wrappers
author: nadongjun
body:
## Motivation

Implements item 2 of #24467.

PR #24610 (item 1) added class-level DI on the five `*MetricsCollector` classes (`_counter_cls`, `_gauge_cls`, `_histogram_cls`, `_summary_cls`) and a `ServerArgs.stat_loggers` role-to-subclass map, but shipped no concrete backend. Downstream platforms that want to surface SGLang metrics through Ray's `ray.util.metrics` agent, instead of a standalone `prometheus_client` scrape, still had to either fork SGLang or vendor their own wrapper layer.

This PR provides the missing backend.

With this change, an embedded SGLang engine running inside a Ray Serve replica can forward all engine metrics through Ray's metric agent and have them appear on Ray's Prometheus endpoint and dashboard alongside other Ray metrics, by passing a single `stat_loggers={...}` map.

The wrappers mirror `vllm/v1/metrics/ray_wrappers.py` so the integration pattern matches vLLM, with two SGLang-specific additions:

* `RaySummaryWrapper`: Ray has no `Summary` primitive. The wrapper falls back to a `Histogram` with conservative default boundaries; quantile queries can be approximated downstream via `histogram_quantile()`.
* Five collector subclasses, one per `*MetricsCollector`, overriding only the `_xxx_cls` attributes each parent actually consumes.

## Modifications

Adds `python/sglang/srt/observability/ray_wrappers.py` (~300 lines).

### Four wrapper classes

These implement the `prometheus_client` API surface that the existing collectors call.

| Wrapper | Backing Ray primitive | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `RayCounterWrapper` | `ray.util.metrics.Counter` | `inc(0)` is a no-op (parity with `prometheus_client`) |
| `RayGaugeWrapper` | `ray.util.metrics.Gauge` | Accepts and discards `multiprocess_mode` for API parity. Ray aggregates per `WorkerId` / `ReplicaId` at the metric agent, so prom multiproc modes are not meaningful |
| `RayHistogramWrapper` | `ray.util.metrics.Histogram` | Non-positive `boundaries` are silently filtered (see below) |
| `RaySummaryWrapper` | `ray.util.metrics.Histogram` (fallback) | Ray has no Summary primitive; emits as a Histogram with conservative defaults |

### Five collector subclasses

These wire the wrappers into PR #24610's DI hooks.

```python
class RaySchedulerMetricsCollector(SchedulerMetricsCollector):
    _counter_cls   = RayCounterWrapper
    _gauge_cls     = RayGaugeWrapper
    _histogram_cls = RayHistogramWrapper
    _summary_cls   = RaySummaryWrapper

class RayTokenizerMetricsCollector(TokenizerMetricsCollector):
    _counter_cls   = RayCounterWrapper
    _histogram_cls = RayHistogramWrapper

class RayStorageMetricsCollector(StorageMetricsCollector):
    _counter_cls   = RayCounterWrapper
    _histogram_cls = RayHistogramWrapper

class RayRadixCacheMetricsCollector(RadixCacheMetricsCollector):
    _counter_cls   = RayCounterWrapper
    _histogram_cls = RayHistogramWrapper

class RayExpertDispatchCollector(ExpertDispatchCollector):
    _histogram_cls = RayHistogramWrapper
```

Each subclass overrides only the `_xxx_cls` attributes its parent actually uses; PR #24610's `_StatLoggerDIMixin` defaults handle the rest.

### Production hardening

Mirrored from vLLM's wrapper evolution (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/84bd8a3c1eb7560a810ff4d99a476708a6f9f2f2/vllm/v1/metrics/ray_wrappers.py), with one SGLang-specific addition.

| Concern | Handling |
|---|---|
| OpenTelemetry name validation (`a-zA-Z0-9_` only) | `_get_sanitized_opentelemetry_name()` replaces `:` and other punctuation with `_`. SGLang's existing `sglang:foo` names stay valid without churn on the prom_client side. |
| Ray Serve replica identification on dashboards | `ReplicaId` tag is appended to every metric and populated at instantiation, then again on each `labels()` call from `serve.get_replica_context()`. |
| Concurrent-emit state leakage between callers | `labels()` returns a `copy.copy()` of the wrapper with its tags bound; the `_is_labeled` guard rejects a second `labels()` call. |
| Positional `labels(*args)` support | `_build_tags` fills the tag keys in parent order; the trailing `ReplicaId` slot is always populated by the wrapper, not the caller. |
| `Histogram.boundaries` must be strictly positive (SGLang has `0.0` lower buckets in `queue_time_seconds` and others) | `_coerce_positive_boundaries()` filters non-positive entries. Caught during GPU e2e (would otherwise crash engine startup). |
| Ray not installed (CPU / legacy deployments) | Top-level `try / except ImportError` sets module-level Ray refs to `None`; module imports cleanly, wrapper construction raises a clear `ImportError`. |

No changes outside the new file. The `_StatLoggerDIMixin` plumbing in PR #24610 means the 101 existing instrument call sites stay untouched. With `stat_loggers=None`, behavior is bit-for-bit identical to `main`.

## Accuracy Tests

### Unit tests

`test/registered/unit/observability/test_ray_wrappers.py`, 31 cases covering:

- OTel name sanitization (`:` and other punctuation become `_`)
- `ReplicaId` tag auto-injection from `serve.get_replica_context()`
- `inc` / `set` / `observe` forwarding for each wrapper type
- `inc(0)` no-op, `multiprocess_mode` accepted for API parity
- `labels()` copy semantics, positional / kwarg args, double-call guard, concurrent emit isolation
- DI wiring on the 5 collector subclasses (each overrides exactly the `_xxx_cls` attributes its parent uses)
- Non-positive Histogram boundary filtering (SGLang's `queue_time_seconds` starts at `0.0`; Ray rejects boundaries `<= 0`)
- Graceful module import when Ray is not installed

```
======================== 31 passed in 3.6s ========================
```

### Ray Serve replica e2e (GPU)

Real Ray cluster plus Serve deployment on my host. The replica instantiates each wrapper type with `SchedulerMetricsCollector`'s canonical label keys (`model_name`, `engine_type`, `tp_rank`, `pp_rank`, `moe_ep_rank`), drives `inc` / `set` / `observe` three times per type, then we scrape Ray's Prometheus exporter on port 18080.

#### Test script

```python
import ray
from ray import serve
from sglang.srt.observability.ray_wrappers import (
    RayCounterWrapper, RayGaugeWrapper, RayHistogramWrapper, RaySummaryWrapper,
)

ray.init(num_cpus=2, _metrics_export_port=18080)

@serve.deployment(num_replicas=1)
class SglangEmitter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.labels = {
            "model_name": "demo",
            "engine_type": "prefill_decode",
            "tp_rank": "0", "pp_rank": "0", "moe_ep_rank": "0",
        }
        keys = list(self.labels.keys())

        self.prompt_tokens_total = RayCounterWrapper(
            "sglang:prompt_tokens_total", "...", labelnames=keys)
        self.num_running_reqs = RayGaugeWrapper(
            "sglang:num_running_reqs", "...", labelnames=keys)
        # 0.0-prefixed bucket list, same as SGLang's queue_time_seconds
        self.queue_time = RayHistogramWrapper(
            "sglang:queue_time_seconds", "...", labelnames=keys,
            buckets=[0.0, 0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5,
                     1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60])
        self.e2e_latency = RayHistogramWrapper(
            "sglang:e2e_request_latency_seconds", "...", labelnames=keys,
            buckets=[0.3, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0, 10.0, 30.0, 60.0, 120.0])
        self.summary = RaySummaryWrapper(
            "sglang:summary_demo", "...", labelnames=keys)

    async def __call__(self, request):
        L = self.labels
        self.prompt_tokens_total.labels(**L).inc(50)
        self.num_running_reqs.labels(**L).set(3)
        self.queue_time.labels(**L).observe(0.42)
        self.e2e_latency.labels(**L).observe(1.5)
        self.summary.labels(**L).observe(0.05)
        return {}

serve.run(SglangEmitter.bind(), route_prefix="/")
# POST 3 times, wait 12s for the metric agent to flush, scrape :18080
```

Verified from the `/metrics` scrape:

- `sglang_*` metrics appear in Ray's Prometheus output (Ray prepends `ray_`).
- `ReplicaId` tag is attached to every line, populated from `serve.get_replica_context()`.
- OTel name sanitization applied (`sglang:prompt_tokens_total` exported as `ray_sglang_prompt_tokens_total`).
- Histogram with `0.0` lower bucket: lowest exported bucket is `le="0.001"` (non-positive entry silently dropped).
- Histogram with positive-only buckets: count = 3, sum = 4.5 (= 3 × 1.5).
- Summary → Histogram fallback emits `_count` / `_sum` / `_bucket` correctly.
- Canonical SGLang labels (`engine_type`, `model_name`, `moe_ep_rank`, `pp_rank`, `tp_rank`) preserved on every line.

Excerpt:

```
ray_sglang_prompt_tokens_total{ReplicaId="jx8woahf", ...} 150.0
ray_sglang_num_running_reqs{ReplicaId="jx8woahf", ...} 3.0
ray_sglang_queue_time_seconds_bucket{ReplicaId="jx8woahf", ..., le="0.001"} 0.0
ray_sglang_queue_time_seconds_count{ReplicaId="jx8woahf", ...} 3.0
ray_sglang_e2e_request_latency_seconds_count{ReplicaId="jx8woahf", ...} 3.0
ray_sglang_summary_demo_count{ReplicaId="jx8woahf", ...} 3.0
```

### Scope and impact

This PR only adds `python/sglang/srt/observability/ray_wrappers.py` and its unit tests. No existing collector, server, or engine code is touched. With the default `stat_loggers=None` (PR #24610 behavior), the new file is never imported and behavior is bit-for-bit identical to `main`. The wrappers only activate when a downstream platform (e.g., a Ray Serve based deployment) passes the Ray-backed collector subclasses via `stat_loggers={...}`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. Observability wrappers add a single function call per emit (the wrapper forwards to `ray.util.metrics`). 

No model-path code is touched with the default `stat_loggers=None`, behavior is bit-for-bit identical to `main` and this file is not even imported.

title: Lazy-load speculative-naming via skill instead of always-on rule
author: fzyzcjy
body:
## Motivation

`.claude/rules/speculative-naming.md` is a project-level rule, which Claude Code loads into every agent context whenever someone works in this repo — regardless of whether they're touching speculative decoding, LoRA, the router, attention backends, or anything else. The rule's own first line scopes it narrowly ("apply when adding, renaming, or reviewing identifiers in speculative decoding code"), so the loading scope (every sglang task) is much wider than the application scope (spec decoding only). Every unrelated task pays ~100 lines of context for instructions it will never use.

## Change

Move the full conventions (Rules 1–6 + the "Out of scope" table) into a new on-demand skill, and leave a one-line trigger in the rule:

- `.claude/skills/speculative-naming/SKILL.md` — full content, with frontmatter describing when to load.
- `.claude/rules/speculative-naming.md` — now a single sentence pointing at the skill.

Content is byte-identical aside from the frontmatter and the new pointer line; no rule wording changed.

## Effect

- Non-spec sglang work: ~100 lines saved per agent context.
- Spec decoding work: skill is auto-discovered via its description and loaded on demand; the slim rule also acts as an explicit "go read the skill" trigger.

title: amd/deepseek_v4 33/N remove BF16-to-FP32 elementwise cast from compressor GEMM on HIP
author: yichiche
body:
Update amd/deepseek_v4 integration branch

Merging to main is WIP, we use this PR and upstream amd/deepseek_v4 branch to integrate in parallel.

Original PRs at Day-0:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23600
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23608


## Motivation

On MI355/HIP, `Compressor.forward()` calls `linear_bf16_fp32()` which does:
```python
return tgemm.mm(x, y, otype=x.dtype).float()
```
The `.float()` triggers a separate `bfloat16tofloat32_copy_kernel_cuda` elementwise kernel (~4.2 us each). This fires once per compressor GEMM call:
- C-type layers (compress_ratio=4): 2 compressor GEMMs -> 2 cast kernels
- B-type layers (compress_ratio=128): 1 compressor GEMM -> 1 cast kernel
- A-type layers (compress_ratio=0): no compressor -> 0 cast kernels

Total: 30x2 + 30x1 = 90 cast kernels per iteration, ~384 us (~1.87% of ITL).

### Why B200 doesn't have this problem

`linear_bf16_fp32()` dispatches to different GEMM backends depending on the platform:

| Path | Method | FP32 output? |
|------|--------|-------------|
| B200 `deep_gemm` | `bf16_gemm_nt(x, y, z)` — output tensor `z` is pre-allocated as FP32, GEMM writes FP32 directly | Native, no extra kernel |
| B200 `cublas` | JIT CUDA module outputs FP32 directly | Native, no extra kernel |
| MI355 `aiter` | `tgemm.mm(x, y, otype=x.dtype)` — tuned flydsl configs only support BF16 output | Requires separate `.float()` cast |

B200's GEMM kernels natively support FP32 output in a single kernel launch. MI355's tuned flydsl kernels only support BF16 output, so the FP32 cast requires a separate elementwise kernel.

### Why removing the cast is safe on HIP

`linear_bf16_fp32()` has an FP32-output contract used by multiple paths (cublas, deep_gemm, torch fallback). Rather than breaking this contract, the compressor call site on HIP/aiter bypasses it and calls `tgemm.mm()` directly to get BF16 output.

This is safe because all downstream fused Triton compress kernels (`_c4_decode_kernel`, `_c128_decode_kernel`, `_compress_norm_rope_kernel`) already promote to FP32 internally via `.to(tl.float32)`. The GEMM itself uses FP32 accumulators internally -- the BF16 output simply avoids the unnecessary BF16->FP32->BF16->FP32 round-trip (GEMM accumulates in FP32, truncates to BF16 output, `.float()` casts back to FP32, then Triton loads and promotes to FP32 again).

The `CompressStatePool` buffer remains FP32 (`pool_configurator.py` sets `state_dtype=torch.float32`). Triton handles the mixed-dtype scenario (BF16 input stored into FP32 buffer) correctly via automatic type promotion.

## Modifications

- **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`**:
  - In `Compressor.forward()`, the aiter/HIP path now calls `_tgemm.mm()` directly (returns BF16), bypassing `linear_bf16_fp32()` and its `.float()` cast. The non-aiter path is unchanged.
  - Added `from aiter.tuned_gemm import tgemm as _tgemm` under the `if _use_aiter:` gate.

- **`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/compressed/fused_compress_triton.py`**:
  - Relaxed FP32-only assertions in `_check_common()` to accept BF16 input (`kv_score_input` and `out`), since BF16 `kv_score` now flows through `compress_dispatch()` into the fused Triton kernels. The `kv_score_buffer` assertion remains FP32-only (state pool is always FP32).

## Accuracy Tests

| Benchmark | Score | Threshold | Status |
|-----------|-------|-----------|--------|
| GSM8K (2000 questions, 5-shot, parallel=1000) | 0.908 | 0.88 | PASS |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

### Kernel Replacement (per C-type layer, decode)

| Before | Time (us) | After | Time (us) |
|--------|-----------|-------|-----------|
| `hgemm_bf16` (C4 GEMM) | 8.8 | `hgemm_bf16` (C4 GEMM) | 8.8 |
| `bfloat16tofloat32_copy` | 4.4 | *(eliminated)* | -- |
| `hgemm_bf16` (C128 GEMM) | 9.3 | `hgemm_bf16` (C128 GEMM) | 9.3 |
| `bfloat16tofloat32_copy` | 4.2 | *(eliminated)* | -- |
| **Total** | **26.7** | **Total** | **18.1** |

### Kernel-to-E2E Impact Analysis

| Layer Type | Layers/iter | Kernel Savings/Layer | Total Savings |
|------------|-------------|---------------------|---------------|
| C-type (MLA+Compressor+MoE) | 30 | 8.6 us | 258 us |
| B-type (MoE) | 30 | 4.2 us | 126 us |
| A-type (MLA+Dense) | 61 | 0 us | 0 us |
| **Total** | | | **384 us** |

Expected ITL improvement: 384 us / 20,590 us = **1.87%** (~0.38 ms).

TTFT impact: Negligible -- prefill is dominated by large GEMMs.

### End-to-End Benchmark (il8k_ol1k, concurrency=4, 32 prompts)

| Metric | Baseline | After | Delta |
|--------|----------|-------|-------|
| Total throughput (tok/s) | 1,558.2 | 1,591.2 | +2.1% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 173.1 | 176.8 | +2.1% |
| Median E2E Latency (ms) | 23,109.0 | 22,969.5 | -0.6% |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 1,546.1 | 1,535.9 | -0.7% |
| Median ITL (ms) | 20.59 | 20.46 | -0.6% |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 21.54 | 20.99 | -2.6% |

### Configuration

- Model: DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP=8, MI355
- Attention backend: compressed
- Page size: 256, chunked prefill: 8192

title: Zero `req_pool_indices` padding in cuda-graph populate
author: hnyls2002
body:
Pair `seq_lens.fill_(seq_len_fill_value)` with `req_pool_indices.zero_()` in cuda-graph populate. title: [MoE] Extend kimi_k2_moe_fused_gate to support 256 experts (MiMo V2 Flash)
author: mpdfdfl
body: ## Motivation `kimi_k2_moe_fused_gate` is currently hard-coded for 384-expert routing (Kimi K2). MiMo V2 Flash uses the same DeepSeek-style `noaux_tc` routing with `num_expert_group=1` but has 256 experts. This PR extends the fast-path kernel to cover both 256 and 384 expert configurations from a single code path, so MiMo V2 Flash can take the same optimized fused gate as Kimi K2 instead of falling back to the slower generic biased grouped topk. Alongside the templating, the kernel itself receives several micro-optimizations on the existing 384-expert path. ## Modifications ### `sgl-kernel/csrc/moe/kimi_k2_moe_fused_gate.cu` **Multi-config support** - Refactor kernel-side constants into `template struct GateConfig` so `VPT`, `WARPS_PER_TOKEN_SMALL`, `THREADS_PER_BLOCK_SMALL`, `VEC_PER_LANE`, etc. all derive from `NUM_EXPERTS = N` at compile time. - Templated `kimi_k2_moe_fused_gate_kernel_small_token` and `kimi_k2_moe_fused_gate_kernel` on `N`; the kernel body is identical for 256 and 384. - Host launcher dispatches via `switch (num_experts) { case 256 / case 384 / default }`. Unsupported sizes hit `TORCH_CHECK(false, ...)` with a clear message instead of silently returning uninitialized output. - Added `TORCH_CHECK(topk <= 8)` so the implicit `selected_experts[MAX_TOPK=8]` shared-memory bound is a hard contract instead of a silent overflow. - Internal kernel symbols and public API names stay as `kimi_k2_*`; no file rename, no API change. **Large-token kernel micro-optimizations** - **Bank-conflict-free shared-memory writes**: changed lane indexing from `vec_idx = lane_id * VEC_PER_LANE + i` (chunked-per-lane, multi-way conflicts on STS.128) to `vec_idx = lane_id + i * WARP_SIZE` (lane-strided). Each iteration's 32-lane STS.128 is now lane-contiguous — sm_70+ hardware path has no shared-memory bank conflicts. - **Vectorized shared-memory stores**: build the sigmoid and biased `float4` chunks in registers, then issue one STS.128 per chunk to `warp_scores_v4` / `warp_original_scores_v4`. Replaces the old per-element scalar writes (`warp_scores[expert] = ...`). - **Single-pass renorm**: `sum_for_renorm` is accumulated in lane 0 during the topk picking loop, and `top_indices[MAX_TOPK]` is buffered in registers. Writeback then folds `routed_scaling_factor` into `rcp` once and does a single global write per `(token, k)`. Eliminates the post-loop pass over `output_ptr[]`. **Small-token kernel micro-optimizations** - **Register-resident `biased_val`**: dropped the `__shared__ float shared_scores[NUM_EXPERTS]` mirror and the `selected_vals[8]` shared array. Each thread keeps its own biased score in a register and masks the winner in place via `if (tid == selected) biased_val = -FLT_MAX;`. Saves `NUM_EXPERTS + 8` floats of shared memory and a shared-mem read per topk iteration. - **Single-pass renorm**: same change as the large-token kernel — `sum_for_renorm` accumulated by lane 0 of warp 0 during topk, scaling folded into `rcp`, single-pass writeback. ### `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py` - `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` fast path now activates for `num_experts in (256, 384)` (was 384 only) and gates on `topk <= 8`, so requests outside the kernel's contract gracefully fall through to the next branch instead of tripping the kernel's `TORCH_CHECK`. - Cast `correction_bias` to `float32` at the call site. Some quant configs (e.g., `modelopt_fp4` + `flashinfer_trtllm`) initialize `correction_bias` as `bfloat16`; the kernel requires `float32` and would otherwise crash on the dtype check. This is a zero-copy no-op when the bias is already `float32` (the default in unquantized configs). ### `sgl-kernel/tests/test_kimi_k2_moe_fused_gate.py` - Parameterized over both `(384, 6, 2.872)` (Kimi K2) and `(256, 8, 1.0)` (MiMo V2 Flash) configurations across 22 sequence lengths and both `apply_routed_scaling_factor_on_output` values. ## Accuracy Tests `test_kimi_k2_moe_fused_gate.py` is extended to cover both 256 and 384 experts: - `test_kimi_k2_moe_fused_gate`: parameterized over `seq_length ∈ {1..9, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 65536}` × both expert configs × `apply_routed_scaling_factor_on_output ∈ {True, False}`. Output weights are matched against the Python reference `kimi_k2_biased_topk_impl` within `rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-3`. - `test_kimi_k2_specific_case`: shape / dtype / renormalization-sum sanity checks for both configs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The 384-expert path is now strictly faster than before due to the bank-conflict fix, vectorized stores, single-pass renorm, and warp-only barrier. The new 256-expert path replaces what was previously a fallback to the generic biased grouped topk. | seq_length | kimi orig (us) | new (us) | speedup | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 3.80 | 3.23 | **1.18×** | | 4 | 3.80 | 3.24 | **1.17×** | | 16 | 3.84 | 3.28 | **1.17×** | | 64 | 3.90 | 3.34 | **1.17×** | | 128 | 4.00 | 3.45 | **1.16×** | | 256 | 4.29 | 3.72 | **1.15×** | | 512 | 5.37 | 4.54 | **1.18×** | | 1024 | 5.98 | 4.72 | **1.27×** | | 4096 | 11.77 | 9.18 | **1.28×** | | 16384 | 31.11 | 25.03 | **1.24×** | | 65536 | 108.46 | 89.86 | **1.21×** | **main :** "pr :" ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code with pre-commit - [ ] Add unit tests — `test_kimi_k2_moe_fused_gate.py` extended for the 256-expert case - [ ] Update documentation — N/A (kernel API unchanged; supported expert counts not enumerated in user-facing docs) - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style guidance (kernel mirrors existing templated idioms) --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #26686303094](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26686303094) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #26686303059](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26686303059)

## Motivation

Add classic reject sampling (RS) in Eagle speculative decoding.

The current pipeline of Eagle speculative decoding employ greedy sampling in both predicting draft tokens and target verification.

Use classic reject sampling means to use actual draft prob distribution for sampling draft tokens and for acceptance criterion.

Experimental results show using classic rs can largely improve accept length across various tasks.

title: [diffusion][jit_kernel] perf: varlen FA fast path for USPAttention masked branch
author: mispa-ms
body:
## Motivation

When `attn_mask` is supplied to `USPAttention.forward` (joint self-attention with text + image streams of differing valid lengths, e.g. Qwen-Image), PyTorch SDPA cannot use FlashAttention with a non-None mask and falls back to the EFFICIENT (`fmha_cutlassF_*_sm80`) kernel. On Blackwell (B200, SM 10.0) this SM80 path is ~7× slower per call than the native FA4 (`flash_fwd_sm100`) path, dominating the denoise loop.

This PR replaces the SDPA-with-mask path with `flash_attn_varlen_func` after packing Q/K/V at valid positions via a fused Triton kernel pair, plus a per-request precompute hook so the cu_seqlens / indices metadata is built once and reused by every block.

## Approach

```
build_varlen_mask_meta(mask)            # once per request, in pipeline
  → joint_attention_kwargs["attn_mask_meta"]
    → USPAttention.forward
        if mask path eligible (bool/int 2D mask, matching Q/K/V):
            fused_pack_qkv(Q, K, V, indices)         # 1 Triton launch
            flash_attn_varlen_func(...)               # FA4 / FA3
            fused_scatter_to_padded(out, inv_idx)    # 1 Triton launch
        else (no meta or all-False mask):
            fall back to SDPA (unchanged)
```

Net host launches per attention call: 5 PyTorch ops (`index_select × 3 + zeros + index_copy_`) → 2 Triton kernels.

`SGLANG_VARLEN_FA=0` disables the fast path entirely (defaults on). Gating is strict: bool/int `[B, S]` mask only, matching Q/K/V shapes, cuda/bf16/fp16. Float additive masks and cross-attention shapes pass through to SDPA so their semantics are preserved.

## Perf (B200, Qwen-Image-2512, 50 steps, `--batching-max-size 24`, same-session A/B)

GPU active (busy-on-chip) vs E2E wall (client perspective):

| c | E2E base | E2E fused | E2E Δ% | Active base | Active fused | Active Δ% | Regime |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
|  1 |  3,430 |  3,375 | -1.6% |    835 |    837 |  +0.2% | B=1, mask not built |
|  2 |  4,250 |  4,035 | -5.1% |  1,692 |  1,406 | **-16.9%** | active win absorbed by idle |
|  4 |  4,287 |  4,143 | -3.4% |  2,798 |  2,291 | **-18.1%** | same pattern |
|  6 |  4,628 |  4,356 | -5.9% |  4,074 |  3,220 | **-21.0%** | same pattern |
|  8 |  5,938 |  5,092 | **-14.2%** |  5,403 |  4,553 | -15.7% | **saturated, active ≈ e2e** |
| 12 |  8,469 |  7,249 | **-14.4%** |  7,887 |  6,567 | -16.7% | saturated, active ≈ e2e |
| 16 | 11,275 |  9,513 | **-15.6%** | 10,515 |  8,720 | -17.1% | saturated, active ≈ e2e |
| 20 | 14,083 | 11,707 | **-16.9%** | 13,008 | 10,808 | -16.9% | **perfect 1:1**, biggest abs win |

Per-image throughput at fused: c=16 → 595 ms/img, c=20 → 585 ms/img (5.8× vs c=1, plateauing).

Kernel-level (full 35-batch trace): `fmha_cutlassF` 29,720 ms → 38 ms (-29,682 ms); net attention GPU time 33.3 s → 9.7 s (-23.6 s).

(c=24 measurements omitted — at batching-max-size=24 the server reaches the batch capacity limit, causing NVTX denoise-stage boundaries to overlap across concurrent batches. aiperf p50 still showed -10.2% but the per-batch trace decomposition is unreliable.)

## Safety

- **Env toggle**: `SGLANG_VARLEN_FA=0` returns to upstream SDPA path with bit-exact behavior (verified by A/B kernel-signature match).
- **All-False mask guard**: `indices.shape[0] == 0` → falls through to SDPA broadcast (FA varlen rejects zero-length input).
- **Shape gating**: bool/int `[B, S]` mask only, matching Q/K/V shapes. Float / cross-attention masks fall through unchanged.
- **Shape consistency assert**: `attn_mask_meta["inv_indices"].shape[0] == B*S` guards against caller mismatch.
- **Numerical tests**: 25 CI-registered cases (`base-b-kernel-unit-1-gpu-large` + `nightly-kernel-1-gpu`) check bit-exact equivalence against PyTorch references (`index_select` / `zeros+index_copy_`) across bf16/fp16, 7 production-like shapes (incl. zero-text-row edges), non-contiguous input, and empty-mask edge.

## Regression check on a non-mask model (FLUX.2-klein-4B)

Same-session A/B (`SGLANG_VARLEN_FA=0` vs `=1`) on `black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4B`, which does not pass `attn_mask` to USPAttention:

| c | base | fused | Δ% |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|  1 |  222 |  221 | -0.5% |
|  8 |  691 |  683 | -1.2% |
| 16 | 1,264 | 1,252 | -0.9% |
| 24 | 1,803 | 1,793 | -0.6% |

All deltas within measurement noise; kernel signatures identical between toggles (`flash_attn`: 14,360 in both, `_fused_pack_qkv`: 0 in both). The fast path is strictly opt-in.

## Industry validation

vllm-omni's diffusion attention backend (`vllm_omni/diffusion/attention/backends/flash_attn.py`) uses the same `_upad_input → flash_attn_varlen_func → _pad_input` pattern, implemented with PyTorch built-ins (`_index_first_axis × 3 + torch.zeros + index_copy_` = 5 host launches per attention call) and re-derives the mask metadata inside every block. This PR's Triton fusion (2 launches per call) and per-request precompute reduce dispatch overhead while keeping the architecture identical, so the change is consistent with established practice across major serving frameworks. Upstream FA still does not support dense masks ([Dao-AILab/flash-attention#409](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/issues/409), 2023-08; revisited in [#1990](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/issues/1990) 2025-11).

## Test plan

- [x] CI: `test_varlen_pack_pad.py` (25 cases bf16+fp16, registered to `base-b-kernel-unit-1-gpu-large` + `nightly-kernel-1-gpu`)
- [x] Manual: Qwen-Image-2512 E2E A/B on B200 (above table)
- [x] Manual: FLUX.2-klein-4B regression A/B (above table, zero impact confirmed)
- [x] Manual: `SGLANG_VARLEN_FA=0` returns to upstream SDPA path with identical wall-time on FLUX.2
