title: [Spec] Async-assert probes across EAGLE/MTP; zero `tgt_cache_loc`
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary
- Add `maybe_detect_nan/inf/oob` async-assert probes throughout EAGLE v1/v2, multi-layer EAGLE v2, frozen-KV MTP, and `MHATokenToKVPool.move_kv_cache`
- Switch `tgt_cache_loc` from `torch.empty_like` to `torch.zeros_like` in `get_src_tgt_cache_loc` so any uncovered tail lands on reserved padding slot 0 instead of caching-allocator garbage
- Consolidate `SGLANG_SPEC_NAN_DETECTION` + `SGLANG_SPEC_OOB_DETECTION` into a single `SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT` env (default off in prod, on in spec test fixtures)
- Move all probe helpers from `speculative/spec_utils.py` to neutral `utils/async_probe.py` (eliminates reverse `mem_cache → speculative` dependency)
- Remove deprecated `--enable-nan-detection` CLI flag and the sampler's CPU-sync NaN-replace-with-`-1e5` recovery path

## Background
- `test_eagle_infer_b::TestEAGLEServerAdditional` (page_size=256, topk=5, fa3, fp16) has been flaky for several days (~30 hits across recent runs)
- Three failure modes confirmed via cuda-gdb on coredumps:
  - **A** (5/7) NaN target logits caught by existing `maybe_detect_nan`
  - **B** (1/7) illegal address in `copy_all_layer_kv_cache_tiled` (`MHATokenToKVPool.move_kv_cache`) — `src_cache_loc` carrying out-of-range slot id
  - **C** (1/7) `vectorized_gather_kernel` WARP_ASSERT on `embed_tokens(input_ids)` — `input_ids` containing token id `>= vocab_size`
- All failures isolated to v1 path; v2 (`test_eagle_infer_beta`) has zero failures in the same window
- Root cause not pinned down. This PR is **defense-in-depth + instrumentation**: it does not claim to fix the bug, only narrows the illegal-addr exposure surface and ensures the next flaky trigger surfaces a precise async-assert with the offending tensor / value range instead of a delayed NaN cascade

## Changes
**Probes** (CI-only, gated on `SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT`)
- `eagle_info.py`: `input_ids` vs `vocab_size`; `accept_index` ∈ `[-1, bs*draft_token_num)`; `num_correct_drafts` upper bound; `accept_tokens` vs `vocab_size`; target_probs NaN after softmax / top_k_renorm / top_p_renorm
- `eagle_info_v2.py`: input_ids check at both `prepare_for_extend_to_fill_draft_kvcache` and `prepare_for_verify`; target_probs intermediate NaN checks
- `eagle_worker.py` / `eagle_worker_v2.py` / `multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py` / `frozen_kv_mtp_worker.py`: `maybe_detect_inf` paired with each existing `maybe_detect_nan` on logits / hidden_states
- `memory_pool.py`: `move_kv_cache` entry — `tgt_loc` / `src_loc` OOB vs `size + page_size`

**Behavior changes**
- Removed `--enable-nan-detection` CLI flag (long-deprecated); use `SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT=1` instead
- Sampler's CPU-sync NaN-replace-with-`-1e5` recovery path removed (was gated on the deprecated flag). Async assert is the new mechanism

**Refactor**
- `tgt_cache_loc = empty_like(...)` → `zeros_like(...)` in `get_src_tgt_cache_loc` (`spec_utils.py`)
- Probe helpers moved from `speculative/spec_utils.py` to new `utils/async_probe.py`; `mem_cache/memory_pool.py` no longer needs a function-body local import

## Test plan
- [x] Lint / pre-commit / isort / black
- [ ] base-b suite (`test_eagle_infer_b`, `test_eagle_infer_beta`, `test_eagle_constrained_decoding`, `test_eagle_dp_attention`, `test_deepseek_v3_fp4_mtp_small`, `test_dflash`, `test_constrained_decoding_spec_reasoning`)
- [ ] Optional `pr-test-extra` for broader sampler coverage (sampler.py touched)
- [ ] Post-merge: monitor flaky rate of `TestEAGLEServerAdditional`

title: Optimize get load calls (/v1/loads) using shared-memory load snapshots
author: merrymercy
body:
## Summary

- make the `get_loads` call 10x - 100x faster with shared memory and scheduler bypass. The old piggyback method will lead to bad latency when scheduler is blocked by a long chunked prefill and it does some extra zmq communications.
- Replace the zmq round-trip approach for `/v1/loads` and DP budget updates with a shared-memory (mmap) snapshot mechanism.
- Each scheduler publishes load metrics to `/dev/shm`; readers (tokenizer manager, DP controller) read directly from shared memory with no IPC overhead.
- For multi-node DP attention, a zmq PUSH/PULL transport relays snapshots to node 0's SHM file.
- Remove server-side aggregate and `dp_rank_count` from `/v1/loads` response (clients compute these).
- Add `--load-snapshot-publish-interval` flag and `SGLANG_LOAD_SNAPSHOT_USE_ZMQ` env var.

## Original commits

- `c8f8380a2`
- author: @cctry 
- https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25841

The combination of (a) the manual scout reproducing R108 on `a77449f86` with known-good aiter and (b) the revert-branch verify scoring 0.975 on rocm720 with default aiter proves the cause is on the sglang side, specifically #26235.

title: [core] WAR barrier for overlap schedule buffer writes, without fwd occupancy cost
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary
- Fix a data race in overlap scheduling: `schedule_stream` writes to shared GPU buffers (the SWA index mapping in particular) race the previous forward's reads -> flaky dsv4 disagg gsm8k.
- Add a general `schedule_stream.wait_stream(forward_stream)` WAR barrier at each overlap loop top, then keep it free of fwd occupancy regression by moving the host syncs it serializes off the schedule stream.
- Supersedes #26376 (bidirectional `wait_stream` — race-free but -4% fwd occupancy / ~20 tok/s).

## Background
- In overlap scheduling, `schedule_stream` writes shared GPU buffers (`req_to_token_pool` from alloc, `full_to_swa_index_mapping` from retract / free_swa) while the previous forward still reads them — a WAR hazard. On dsv4 disagg this surfaced as flaky gsm8k (e.g. `test_disaggregation_dsv4`, ~0.87). `seq_lens` itself does not race.
- A `wait_stream` barrier fixes it but pins `schedule_stream` to the prev forward's end, so any blocking host sync issued on that stream stalls the host a full forward, losing overlap with `draft_extend` (the -4%).

## Fix
- **Race fix (general):** `schedule_stream.wait_stream(forward_stream)` at each overlap event-loop top (normal + disagg decode/prefill) — all schedule writes to shared GPU buffers wait for the prev forward's reads. Not seq_lens-specific.
- **Occupancy:** the barrier serializes two blocking host syncs that sat on the schedule stream; move both off it (each is the bottleneck if the other is fixed alone):
  - **H2D** (`prepare_for_decode` kv_lens `.to()`): a known CPU value needs no wait -> `non_blocking=True` drops the stream sync.
  - **D2H** (`resolve_seq_lens_cpu` seq_lens): a forward-computed value needs a sync -> run it on a private stream gated only on the publish event (mid-forward), host-select `seq_lens_cpu` via `req_pool_indices_cpu`. Now overlaps `draft_extend`.

Builds on #26425 (`req_pool_indices_cpu` host mirror).

```text
1) PREV: no WAR barrier
forward_stream : draft|verify o====== draft_extend ======|next_fwd->
schedule_stream: alloc|write shared buf  (NO wait_stream)
                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ RACE with forward's reads
                 >> FAST (overlaps) but DATA RACE

2) WITH BARRIER: .cpu() on schedule stream
```

title: Enable Kimi-K2.5 piecewise CUDA graph
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

This PR enables piecewise CUDA graph for the Kimi-K2.5 multimodal wrapper.

Root cause: `KimiK25ForConditionalGeneration` wraps the language model as `language_model`, but the generic piecewise CUDA graph setup checks the common `.model` wrapper path. Without that alias, startup logs report `Disable piecewise CUDA graph because the model is not a language model`, and prefill runs without piecewise CUDA graph.

Changes:
- Add a `.model` property alias that returns `self.language_model`.
- Ignore writes to `.model` during ModelRunner piecewise CUDA graph setup so we do not register a duplicate `nn.Module` alias or perturb state dict / loading paths.
- Pass the runtime token count with a `2048` floor, `max_token_num=max(x.shape[0], 2048)`, to FlashInfer allreduce residual RMSNorm fusion.

## Retest on B200

Re-tested on `ion-b200` on 2026-05-26 with the same Kimi-K2.5 command and workload for both rows. The patched row was re-tested after the Gemini follow-up at head `625b07d03`.

Server shape:
- Model: `/tmp/models/Kimi-K2.5`
- GPUs: B200 `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7`, `--tp 4`
- Key flags: `--enable-multimodal --schedule-policy lpm --enable-mixed-chunk --enable-cache-report --keep-mm-feature-on-device --enforce-piecewise-cuda-graph --piecewise-cuda-graph-max-tokens 4096`
- Env: `SGLANG_MM_FEATURE_CACHE_MB=1024`, `SGLANG_USE_CUDA_IPC_TRANSPORT=1`

Probe shape:
- `synthetic-text`, `--synthetic-words 512`, `--limit 256`, `--concurrency 32`, `--max-tokens 20`, `--no-thinking`
- Metrics below use the second warm run after prefix cache is populated.

| Build | Piecewise CUDA graph evidence | TTFT mean | TTFT p50 | TTFT p90 | TTFT p99 | TPOT mean | E2E mean | Cache read tokens |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `origin/main` | disabled: `not a language model`; prefill `cuda graph: False` | 0.479s | 0.495s | 0.528s | 0.546s | 12.5ms | 0.722s | 131,072 |
| this PR | enabled: `Capture piecewise CUDA graph end`; prefill `cuda graph: True` | 0.147s | 0.133s | 0.216s | 0.243s | 17.7ms | 0.488s | 131,072 |

TTFT mean drops from `0.479s` to `0.147s` on this workload.

Relevant log evidence:

```text
# origin/main
Disable piecewise CUDA graph because the model is not a language model
Prefill batch ... cuda graph: False

# this PR
Capture piecewise CUDA graph end. Time elapsed: 87.16 s.
Prefill batch ... cuda graph: True
```

## Checks

- `git diff --check`
- `ruff check --select F401,F821 python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k25.py`
- `python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k25.py`
- Verified a dummy `@model.setter` on `nn.Module` still registers duplicate `model.*` state_dict keys for `Module` values, so `__setattr__` is intentional here.
- Remote B200 launch + latency probes above

title: [AMD][DSV4] DSV4 MTP graph + sparse triton attn optimizations
author: kkHuang-amd
body:
Co-authored-by: @1am9trash @RolaoDenthu @yichiche @hubertlu-tw @sogalin @HaiShaw @yctseng0211 @bingxche @amd-danli103 @Raiden-Makoto ## Motivation The long-standing draft #25552 collected 85 commits of AMD / DSV4 work over several rebases. Most of the optimization PRs it tracked (compressor opts, fused topk, sparse MLA kernels, fused compress, etc.) have already been merged into `main` through smaller follow-up PRs (e.g. #26208, #25251, #25878, #25977, #26014). What remains is a small but meaningful set of changes needed to: 1. Make DSV4 + EAGLE/MTP speculative decoding work correctly under CUDA-graph capture on ROCm. The current HIP radix backend mis-handles per-step draft `out_cache_loc` slicing and trips planner invariants inside `init_forward_metadata_target_verify` when `SGLANG_PREP_IN_CUDA_GRAPH` is on, leading to graph-capture failure / wrong KV slots being written during target verification. 2. Land the last round of ROCm performance wins for DSV4 decode/extend that did not make it into the previously merged sub-PRs: - Fused Triton `mhc_post_pre` for low concurrency (enabled behind `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TRITON_FUSED_MHC`). - `aiter.greedy_sample` fast path for all-greedy sampling on ROCm. - Enable `w_qkv` fusion on ROCm and tidy up the HIP multi-stream path. 3. Provide a clean, single-commit, conflict-free landing of the above so reviewers do not have to wade through 85 commits / merge commits. The diff against `main` is small (10 files, +656 / -65), self-contained to ROCm-specific code paths plus a single shared `deepseek_common/amd/` helper, and does not change CUDA behavior outside of `is_hip()` guarded branches. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` - Add `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TRITON_FUSED_MHC` (default `True`) to gate the new fused mHC post+pre helper. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py` - When `SGLANG_USE_AITER` is set on ROCm, replace the `torch.argmax` all-greedy fallback with `aiter.greedy_sample` writing into a preallocated `int32` buffer. Non-HIP / non-aiter paths are unchanged. - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/draft_utils.py` - In `DraftBackendFactory._create_dsv4_decode_backend` and `_create_dsv4_prefill_backend`, dispatch to `deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.DeepseekV4MultiStepBackend` / `DeepseekV4HipRadixBackend` on ROCm and fall back to the existing CUDA `deepseek_v4_backend` elsewhere. This is the actual bug-fix for "DSV4 MTP graph backend handling on HIP". - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py` - `init_forward_metadata_target_verify`: always build metadata eagerly via `init_forward_metadata_target_verify_old` for the HIP path. The previous `SGLANG_PREP_IN_CUDA_GRAPH` raw/lazy-upgrade branch hit DSV4+EAGLE planner invariants during graph capture. - `init_forward_metadata_target_verify_old`: normalize `extend_seq_lens` (allocate per-batch when missing, clamp to `seq_lens`, floor at 1) so target-verify works for all draft batch shapes. - `init_forward_metadata`: in decode/idle mode slice the shared multi-step `out_cache_loc` with `per_step_draft_out_cache_loc(... )[self.speculative_step_id]` before passing it into metadata, matching how DSV4 bakes the c4/c128 KV write target into metadata. Also forward `forward_batch.extend_seq_lens` into target-verify metadata. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/nsa/triton_decode/triton_mla_kernels_decode_fused.py`, `triton_mla_kernels_decode_optimized.py` - Wire the fused / optimized Triton sparse MLA decode kernels into the new "single fused gather + attention" prefill dispatch path used by HIP. These are the kernel-side updates for the prefill-fusion item. - `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/amd/__init__.py` (new) - `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/amd/deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py` (new, 158 lines) - New shared AMD helper `try_fused_hc_post_pre(...)` that performs the fused `hc_post + hc_pre` (matmul + scale/base + sinkhorn + RMSNorm) and reports back whether the post-attention layernorm was fused. Returns `None` to signal the caller to fall back to the unfused path. - `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py` - Add `_freqs_cis_to_cos_sin` cache so all layers sharing a `precompute_freqs_cis` result reuse the same `(cos, sin)` bf16 contiguous tables. - In `MQALayer`: enable `fuse_wqa_wkv` on ROCm (drop the `not _is_hip` gate) and pass `attn_backend` into the compressor call when fused. Guard the multi-stream alt-stream creation to avoid HIP cases where `self.compressor is None`. - In `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.forward`: try the fused `try_fused_hc_post_pre(...)` first; consume its `(residual, hidden_states, post, comb, norm_fused)` tuple and only run the unfused `hc_post` / `hc_pre` / `post_attention_layernorm` path when the helper returns `None`. This preserves the existing `norm_fused` return contract. - In `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM.load_weights`: also enable `fuse_wqa_wkv` weight bucketing on ROCm. - `test/registered/ops/test_aiter_greedy_sample_amd.py` (new, 289 lines) - Registered unit test covering the `aiter.greedy_sample` sampler integration on AMD, exercising small / large vocab, tied logits, and parity vs `torch.argmax` across dtypes and batch sizes. ## AMD Accuracy Tests

title: [Bug] Forward fixed_split_size in SWA / cross-attention paths of FlashInfer backend
author: charlotte12l
body:
## Bug

`--enable-deterministic-inference` sets `prefill_split_tile_size` — the FlashInfer knob that pins split-K reduction order so attention output is batch-invariant — and threads it through the `update()` chain as `fixed_split_size` (plus `disable_split_kv` on the decode side). But three of the four `update_*` leaf methods in `FlashInferIndicesUpdater{Decode,Prefill}` silently drop these values before calling `call_begin_forward()`:

- `FlashInferIndicesUpdaterDecode.update_sliding_window`
- `FlashInferIndicesUpdaterDecode.update_cross_attention`
- `FlashInferIndicesUpdaterPrefill.update_sliding_window`
- `FlashInferIndicesUpdaterPrefill.update_cross_attention`

Only `update_single_wrapper` (full-attention path) forwarded them correctly.

## Impact

Models with sliding-window attention or cross-attention take the SWA / cross-attn path on every layer, so `fixed_split_size` never reaches the FlashInfer kernel. FlashInfer then auto-picks split sizes, and the split-K reduction order depends on total batch tokens. Result: attention output (and downstream logp) drifts across batch shapes / batch composition, in spite of `--enable-deterministic-inference`.

Models without SWA/cross-attention (e.g. Qwen3-8B in the default deterministic-inference CI) take `update_single_wrapper` and are unaffected, which is why existing CI passes today. The bug only surfaces on SWA / cross-attention models.

Verified on an internal SWA model setup with `python -m sglang.test.test_deterministic --test-mode prefix --n-start 10 --n-trials 10` against a live server launched with `--attention-backend flashinfer --enable-deterministic-inference`:

- **Before:** prefix length 2048 → `Unique samples: 6` (text-level failure too), 22/43 logp mismatches; lengths 511 / 4097 also drift in logp.
- **After:** all 4 prefix lengths → `Unique samples: 1`, `✓✓✓ Logprobs are identical across all batch sizes! ✓✓✓`.

## Fix

Add `fixed_split_size=fixed_split_size` (and `disable_split_kv=disable_split_kv` on the decode side) to the `call_begin_forward()` invocation inside each of the four affected methods. Behavior with `--enable-deterministic-inference` off is unchanged — the value passed in is `None`.

title: [Perf][Spec Decoding] Skip cat/topk/sort/gather in draft_forward for topk=1
author: Qiaolin-Yu
body:
When speculative_eagle_topk == 1 the draft tree is a chain, so the post-loop machinery in draft_forward — concat(score_list).flatten → torch.topk(.., num_draft-1) → torch.sort → torch.gather over ss_token_list — is structurally an identity:

  parent_list      = [-1, 0, 1, ..., num_draft-2]   (chain parents)
  top_scores_index = [ 0, 1, 2, ..., num_draft-2]   (sorted picks)
  draft_tokens     = cat(token_list, dim=1)

Pre-allocate parent_list / top_scores_index once at worker __init__ sized to cuda_graph_max_bs and slice [:bs] inside the captured graph. The bitonicSortKVInPlace + sbtopk::gatherTopK kernels disappear from the DRAFT_DECODE phase.

topk > 1 path is unchanged.

Measured: tightens DRAFT_DECODE GPU work by ~25 us/cycle. Combined with other topk=1 fast-paths the net was +2 tok/s on Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 TP=4 80K ctx EAGLE3 topk=1 bs=1. gsm8k unchanged.

title: [MUSA] Fix startup with patched torchada
author: popsiclexu
body:
## Summary

- Bump MUSA torchada requirements to `>=0.1.57` so SGLang picks up MooreThreads/torchada#70.
- Skip CUDA PDL arch probing on MUSA runtime.

## Motivation

SGLang can fail during MUSA startup with:

`AttributeError: module 'triton.language.extra' has no attribute 'cuda'`

The torchada-side patch is available in https://github.com/MooreThreads/torchada/pull/70, so this updates the dependency and avoids the CUDA-specific PDL path on MUSA.

## Validation

### Test startup script

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --served-model-name "./DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat" \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \
  --disable-overlap-schedule \
  --host "$HOST" \
  --port "$PORT" \
  --attention-backend fa3 \
  --cuda-graph-bs $(seq 1 2 64) \
  --tp-size 1 \
  --chunked-prefill-size -1 \
  --max-prefill-tokens 8192 \
  --disable-piecewise-cuda-graph
```

title: [Bug Fix] Fix activation.cuh JIT compilation failure on CUDA 13 due to template type/value mismatch
author: 256256mjw
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

  Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25487

  On CUDA 13.0, the JIT compilation of `activation.cuh` fails during CUDA graph capture, crashing the server process. The root cause is a C++ template type/value mismatch in the `select_kernel` trailing return type:

  activation.cuh:95:52: error: type/value mismatch at argument 1 in template parameter list
    note: expected a type, got 'ActivationKind::kSiLU'

  CUDA 13's stricter `nvcc` cannot correctly parse `decltype(ActivationKernel::template activation_kernel<ActivationKind::kSiLU, kFilterExpert>)` in a dependent context (trailing return type with an outer template parameter `kFilterExpert`). It
   misinterprets the non-type enum value `ActivationKind::kSiLU` as a type argument. Older CUDA versions (11/12) silently accepted this.

  ## Modifications

  - Introduced an explicit `kernel_fn_t` type alias via `decltype(&act_and_mul_kernel<...>)` on the global function template (avoids the problematic variable template parsing path).
  - Replaced `auto` with `kernel_fn_t` for the `activation_kernel` variable template.
  - Removed the `decltype`-based trailing return type from `select_kernel`, using `kernel_fn_t` directly.
  - Removed unnecessary `ActivationKernel::template` qualification inside the class body.
  - Added `static_cast<uint32_t>()` for `hidden_size` to fix a signed-to-unsigned narrowing conversion warning.

  All changes are compile-time only — no runtime behavior or performance change. Compatible with CUDA 11, 12, 13, and ROCm/HIP.

  ## Accuracy Tests

  N/A — This is a compile-time fix only. No changes to kernel logic, numerical computation, or model output.

  ## Speed Tests and Profiling

  N/A — No runtime behavior change. The generated PTX/SASS is identical since the function pointer type and kernel code are unchanged.

Previously, FlashInfer AllReduce Fusion was disabled on H20 devices due to a known bug tracked in https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/2204. The workaround involved checking the device name and skipping the optimization if an H20 device was detected.

This device check is no longer needed as the underlying issue has been resolved:
- Performed a clean compilation without encountering any compilation issues
- Ran benchmark script on H20 with `--enable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion` flag - worked without any issues

Removing this restriction allows H20 users to benefit from the performance improvements of FlashInfer AllReduce Fusion.
Closes #25027

- Removed `get_device_name` from imports (no longer needed)
- Removed H20 device detection logic (`is_h20_device` check)

The changes affect `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py`:

- Lines 2507-2511: Removed H20 device check and comment

title: perf(gemma4): single-launch fused router (topk + softmax + scale)
author: pyc96
body:
## Motivation

`Gemma4MoE.routing_function` emits four per-layer GPU kernels for every MoE
forward pass (one decode step touches ~30 routed-MoE layers):

| Kernel | Decode share (Gemma-4-26B-A4B-IT + MTP, B200) |
|---|---|
| `at::native::sbtopk::gatherTopK<bf16,uint,2,false>` (torch.topk) | 2.4% |
| `at::native::bitonicSortKVInPlace<2,-1,16,16,bf16,...>` (torch.topk tie-break) | 2.0% |
| `at::native::index_elementwise_kernel<bf16>` (`per_expert_scale[topk_ids]`) | 1.4% |
| `MulFunctor<bf16>` + softmax + fp32 cast | folded |
| **total** | **~5.8%** |

vLLM's [`_gemma4_routing_kernel`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39083)
(apache-2.0) does the same logical work in a single Triton launch and brings
its share of decode GPU time to ~1.1%. This PR ports the same algorithm
to SGLang, rewritten from scratch in SGLang style.

## Modifications

* New file `python/sglang/srt/layers/gemma4_fused_ops.py`:
  - `_gemma4_routing_kernel` — one Triton program per token. Packs
    `(bijective(logit_bits), expert_id)` into int64; the bijection is
    anti-monotone on the float value and the `<<32` shift puts the int32
    key's high bit into the int64 sign position, so signed ascending
    `tl.sort` yields the original logits in descending float order in one
    pass. Softmaxes in fp32, multiplies by `per_expert_scale[topk_ids]`,
    writes `(fp32 weights, int32 ids)` matching the SGLang TopK output
    contract.
  - `num_warps=1` for Gemma4's `E = num_experts = 128` (fits in one warp).
  - Defensive `E <= 1024` assert.
* `python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_causal.py`:
  - `Gemma4MoE.routing_function` calls the fused kernel on CUDA fp16/bf16/
    fp32 router logits; falls back to the original torch path otherwise.

## Quantization compatibility

The router projection in `Gemma4Router` is constructed with
`quant_config=None`, so router logits are always emitted in the activation
dtype (bf16/fp16/fp32) regardless of expert quantization. The fast path's
dtype guard is therefore safe under any expert quantization that goes
through the standard topk dispatch.

| MoE runner backend | Gemma4 routing path | Fused kernel called? |
|---|---|---:|
| `triton` / `triton_kernel` (BF16, FP16) | `custom_routing_function` via `select_experts` | ✅ |
| FP8 (compressed-tensors, W8A8) | `custom_routing_function` via `select_experts` | ✅ |
| `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` (NVFP4 opt-in) | `custom_routing_function` via `select_experts` | ✅ |
| `flashinfer_trtllm` (NVFP4 default on SM100) | `BypassedTopKOutput` → trtllm does routing internally | ❌ (no-op) |
| `flashinfer_mxfp4` (`is_fp4_experts=False`) | `BypassedTopKOutput` → flashinfer mxfp4 kernel | ❌ (no-op) |

On the BYPASSED paths neither the fused kernel nor the previous torch
fallback runs, so this PR is a strict no-op there.

## Accuracy Tests

### Unit tests — `test/srt/layers/test_gemma4_fused_routing.py` (47 cases)

47 shape/dtype combinations against the previous torch routing function:
`E ∈ {64, 128, 256}`, `K ∈ {4, 8}`, `T ∈ {0, 1, 7, 64, 128, 1024}`,
`dtype ∈ {bf16, fp16, fp32}`. Tolerances set to the input dtype eps; the
fused kernel does softmax in fp32 throughout while the torch fallback does
softmax in input dtype, so the fused path is the more accurate one for
bf16/fp16.

```bash
$ python -m pytest test/srt/layers/test_gemma4_fused_routing.py
47 passed in 27.75s
```

### Equivalence probe (819,200 random tokens, E=128, K=8)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Top-K **set** disagreement (different K experts chosen) | **0.00%** |
| Top-K order disagreement (same K, different array order) | 20.4% |
| Max id-aligned weight diff when sets agree | **7.5e-3** (≤ bf16 eps) |

The fused kernel and torch fallback always pick the exact same K experts;
only the position of each `(id, weight)` pair within `topk_ids[t, :K]` may
differ. Order doesn't affect the downstream MoE sum.

### End-to-end MMLU (1× B200, BF16, 5-shot, temp=0)

Full MMLU: 57 subjects, **14,042 questions per variant**. A/B via local
env-toggle in `Gemma4MoE.routing_function` that forces the torch fallback.
Each variant run twice from a clean server start.

| Variant | Run 1 | Run 2 | Mean |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Fused router ON | **0.6329** | 0.6335 | **0.6332** |
| Torch fallback | 0.6288 | 0.6280 | 0.6284 |

Gap = +0.5pp (fused vs torch).

**McNemar's test on paired per-question outcomes** (Run 1 of each, N=14,042):

| | Count |
|---|---:|
| Fused-only correct | 826 |
| Torch-only correct | 769 |
| Both correct | 8,061 |
| Neither correct | 4,386 |
| **McNemar χ²** (continuity correction) | **1.97** |
| Critical χ² at p=0.05 (df=1) | 3.84 |

**Conclusion**: no statistically significant difference between fused and torch
at p=0.05.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

1× B200 (sm_100a), BF16, `Gemma-4-26B-A4B-IT` + Gemma4 MTP, triton
attention, `--speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4
--speculative-eagle-topk 1`. Both scenarios use
`python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang-oai-chat
--random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 80 --warmup-requests 2 --seed 1`.

| Workload | Baseline | This PR | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| chat random 1000/1000 output tok/s | 2729.30 | **2880.94** | **+5.6%** |
| chat median TPOT (ms) | 21.11 | 20.70 | -1.9% |
| chat accept length | 2.75 | 2.80 | +1.8% |
| summarization random 8000/1000 output tok/s | 1060.98 | **1108.42** | **+4.5%** |

torch.profiler share of the four pre-fusion kernels drops from ~5.8% to
~1.4% of decode GPU time, in line with vLLM's measured share.

## Provenance

* Algorithm reference: vllm-project/vllm#39083 (apache-2.0).
* Kernel and Python wrapper rewritten from scratch in SGLang style; no
  source copy.

title: Fix FlashInfer SWA EXTEND-with-prefix correctness in merge_state path
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

The FlashInfer SWA EXTEND path with nonzero prefix and `use_ragged=True` (the merge_state branch) returned incorrect outputs. Surfaced under module-level tests as ~0.2 max abs diff vs an HF-style PyTorch reference; under server-level SWA workloads with prefix caching, this produces silently-wrong tokens.

### Bug

When `extend_no_prefix=False` and `use_ragged=True`, `forward_extend` runs **two** FlashInfer wrappers and combines them with `merge_state`:
* a ragged wrapper over Q vs **extend K/V**
* a paged wrapper over Q vs **cached prefix K/V**

Two issues combined:

1. **`window_left` not passed to `forward_return_lse`**: both wrappers ran without per-query sliding-window masking. The `use_ragged=False` branch above already supplied `window_left` (with a multi-item-scoring guard); this branch did not.

2. **`update_sliding_window` reading uninitialized cache positions**: it set `paged_kernel_lens = min(seq_lens, window + extend_lens)`, but K for the extend tokens is written to the KV cache **after** the paged wrapper runs. Positions `[prefix_len, seq_len)` therefore hold stale/uninitialized data when the paged wrapper executes.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_backend.py`:

* Pass `window_left = layer.sliding_window_size` (with the same multi-item-scoring guard) to both `forward_return_lse` calls in the `use_ragged=True` branch of `forward_extend`.

* In `FlashInferIndicesUpdaterPrefill.update_sliding_window`, branch on `use_ragged`:
  - **`use_ragged=True`**: read prefix-only from offset 0 (`paged_kernel_lens = prefix_lens`, `kv_start_idx = 0`). Supply a per-(q, k) custom mask `k >= prefix_len + q - window_left` via `cross_attention_custom_mask` so each extend query gates to prefix keys inside its window.
  - **`use_ragged=False`**: existing behavior unchanged.

The custom mask is required because FlashInfer's built-in `window_left` anchors Q at the end of `kv_len` (i.e. `kv_len - qo_len + qo_idx`), which doesn't express the correct prefix-vs-extend offset when the paged wrapper sees prefix-only K.

## Accuracy Tests

| Fixture | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| FlashInfer SWA EXTEND `prefix=8, extend=8, window=12` (within-window) | ~0.2 max abs diff vs HF reference | ≤ atol |
| FlashInfer SWA EXTEND `prefix=16, extend=2` (cross-window) | ~0.2 max abs diff | ≤ atol |
| FlashInfer SWA DECODE within window | already correct | unchanged |
| Non-SWA `use_ragged=True` EXTEND | unchanged | unchanged |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The fix adds one `kv_start_idx` tensor zero-fill and an additional custom-mask build under SWA + prefix. Both are O(num_requests) and dominated by the existing FlashInfer wrapper launch cost. No measurable kernel-time change.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Tests are part of a follow-up consolidated PR that lifts the attention-backend unit-test matrix into `test/registered/attention/unittest/`.
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy benchmark results (above).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: fix: copy seq_lens in TRTLLM MHA draft decode cuda graph capture
author: libertyeagle
body:
## Motivation

`TRTLLMHAAttnBackend.init_forward_metadata_capture_cuda_graph` re-uses a
pre-allocated, zero-initialized `cache_seqlens` buffer for the draft-decode
branch but never copies the current `seq_lens` into it. As a result, the
captured kernel runs with `cache_seqlens == 0` (empty KV range), which
produces NaN at softmax normalization during CUDA graph warmup.

The normal-decode branch implicitly seeds the buffer via `seq_lens.to(int32)`
(which allocates a new tensor populated from `seq_lens`), and the replay path
explicitly does `metadata.cache_seqlens_int32.copy_(seq_lens + step + 1)`,
so this is a capture-only omission specific to the draft-decode branch.

## Symptom

Reproducible with EAGLE3 + `trtllm_mha` + `SGLANG_SPEC_NAN_DETECTION=1`:

```
Capturing batches (bs=30 ...): 4%|...
/pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/TensorCompare.cu:109: _assert_async_cuda_kernel:
  Assertion `NaN detected! draft_forward step 0` failed.
```

Inspection of the dumped `attn_out` of the draft model layer 0 shows the first
3 rows are entirely NaN while the remaining rows are exactly 0 — consistent
with some TRT-LLM MHA tiles short-circuiting empty-KV softmax to 0 and others
returning 0/0 = NaN.

## Fix

Mirror the replay-time copy in the draft-decode capture branch so the captured
graph sees `cache_seqlens > 0` during warmup.

## Verification

After the fix:
- `/health` returns 200, repeated HEALTH_CHECK requests succeed
- `/generate` returns identical output with spec decoding still active
  (accept rate / accept length / verify count unchanged)
- `SGLANG_SPEC_NAN_DETECTION=1` no longer triggers during CG capture

## Original commits

- `f00ec0825`

title: [CI] FA3: ascending cuda-graph capture to avoid varlen workspace IMA (#26532)
author: hnyls2002
body:
Workaround for #26532. Under `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI` + FA3 only; production capture order unchanged.

## Validation

Triggered `/rerun-test registered/spec/eagle/test_eagle_infer_b.py` on this PR ([run 26560654779](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26560654779), `conclusion=success`).

Confirmed the gate behaves correctly across test classes in the same run:

| Test class | `attention_backend` | `cuda_graph_max_bs` | Observed capture order | Gate decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TestEAGLEServerBasic` | (default, non-fa3) | 8 | `bs=8,7,6,5,4,3,2,1` | reversed (unchanged) |
| **`TestEAGLEServerAdditional`** (the originally-flaky config) | **`fa3`** | **5** | **`bs=1,2,3,4,5`** | **ascending (fix active)** |
| Later non-fa3 test class | (default) | 64 | `bs=64,60,...,1` | reversed (unchanged) |

Captured directly from the `Capturing batches (bs=... avail_mem=... GB)` per-bs print in `CudaGraphRunner._capture_one_stream`.

## Memory cost

For `TestEAGLEServerAdditional` (`fa3`, `cuda_graph_max_bs=5`), comparing first-bs vs last-bs `avail_mem` across the three capture phases:

| Capture phase | First-bs `avail_mem` | Last-bs `avail_mem` | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Target decode | 23.42 GB | 23.33 GB | 90 MB |
| Draft decode  | 20.80 GB | 20.73 GB | 70 MB |
| Draft extend  | 20.73 GB | 20.68 GB | 50 MB |

Sum ~0.21 GB for `max_bs=5`. The ascending order ends the per-call FA3 workspace slot sized for `max_bs` (rather than `min_bs`), which is the whole point of the fix; the only marginal cost is the output buffer slot sizing for `max_bs` vs the smaller bs initially, well under 1 % of the cuda-graph footprint.

## Scope

- Helper `_ci_use_ascending_capture_order(server_args)` lives in `cuda_graph_runner.py` (module-level, no test-utils dependency).
- Gate: `envs.SGLANG_IS_IN_CI.get()` AND `"fa3"` in `server_args.get_attention_backends()` (the canonical resolver, accounts for `attention_backend` / `prefill_attention_backend` / `decode_attention_backend` fallback) OR `server_args.speculative_draft_attention_backend == "fa3"`.
- Default (non-CI or non-FA3): reversed order preserved -- the original "better memory sharing across cuda graphs" optimization from #4195 is untouched.

Once the next scheduled CI cycle confirms `test_eagle_infer_b` flakiness drops, we can consider removing the CI gate and applying the change unconditionally (subject to a production memory check at higher `max_bs`).

title: Optimize Gemma4 H200 MoE and extend attention
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- Add H200 Triton fused MoE configs for Gemma4 `E=128,N=704` normal and down projections.
- Tune Hopper extend-attention block sizes for `Lq=129..256` to reduce TTFT/TPOT on Gemma4 prefill-heavy serving.
- Add a small-batch (M ≤ 256) per-head Triton kernel for Gemma4 QKV RMSNorm to lower MTP draft latency.
- ~~Add a Gemma4-specific Triton routing kernel that fuses top-k selection, top-k softmax, and per-expert scale into `gemma4_topk_softmax_scale`.~~ Reverted (commit `27cb94c45`) due to BF16 precision regression on MoE routing — see "Reverted optimizations" below.
- ~~Replace `Gemma4Router.norm(x) * fused_scale` with a single fused `rmsnorm(x, fused_scale, eps)` call on the CUDA fast path.~~ Reverted (commit `0d3c9c694`) for the same reason.
- Keep the optimization scoped to Gemma4/Hopper paths so existing model families keep their current behavior.

## Performance

Re-measured on `ion8-h200`, `sglang_bbuf`, single NVIDIA H200, TP=1, `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`, BF16, `--attention-backend triton`, random `1024/256`, request rate 8, max concurrency 64, 80 prompts. Baseline = latest `origin/main` (`376635c1e`); patched = PR head (`27cb94c45`, with c2/c3 reverted).

| Workload | Build | Output tok/s | p50 TTFT ms | p50 TPOT ms | Median E2E ms | Result |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Random `1024/256`, 80 prompts | SGLang baseline (`376635c1e`) | 1670.72 | 96.56 | 20.30 | 5295.91 | Baseline |
| Random `1024/256`, 80 prompts | SGLang patched (`27cb94c45`) | **1725.50** | **74.04** | **16.62** | **4338.60** | **+3.28% output tok/s, -23.3% TTFT, -18.2% TPOT, -18.1% E2E** |

Full benchmark details:

| Build | Completed | Duration s | Request throughput req/s | Total tok/s | Median E2E ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SGLang baseline (`376635c1e`) | 80 | 12.26 | 6.526 | 8353.59 | 5295.91 |
| SGLang patched (`27cb94c45`) | 80 | 11.87 | 6.740 | 8627.50 | 4338.60 |

The remaining speedup comes from the H200 MoE Triton configs + Hopper extend-attention block-size tuning + small-batch QKV RMSNorm; the heavier routing-fusion optimizations were dropped to keep accuracy on the MTP path.

## Accuracy

Validated on `ion8-h200` via the registered Gemma4 MTP CI test (`test_gemma4_mtp_26b_a4b_extra::test_gsm8k_mtp`, TP=2, `--enable-deterministic-inference`, NEXTN spec decode, 200 GSM8K examples, 5-shot). With the two reverted commits, GSM8K MTP score is back to baseline:

| Build (TP=2, deterministic) | GSM8K MTP topk=1 | avg accept length | Threshold 0.41 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| SGLang baseline (`376635c1e`, all reverts = main) | 0.445 | 4.494 | ✓ pass |
| SGLang patched (`27cb94c45`, c1+c4 kept, c2+c3 reverted) | 0.445 | 4.494 | ✓ pass |
| ~~PR head before revert (`10ab189e3`, all 4 commits)~~ | ~~0.360~~ | ~~4.475~~ | ✗ fail (-5pp) |

Standalone GSM8K (TP=1, no MTP, 8-shot, 200 questions, no deterministic mode) shows the typical run-to-run variance (~5pp swing) but no systematic regression — patched and baseline land within noise of each other (patched: 0.41 / 0.495 across two runs; baseline: 0.465 / 0.445).

## Reverted optimizations

Bisecting `test_gemma4_mtp_26b_a4b_extra` on `ion8-h200` (TP=2, deterministic):

| Configuration | GSM8K topk=1 | Δ vs PR head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| PR head (all 4 commits) | 0.360 | 0 |
| Revert only `fabb5b5ee` (QKV RMSNorm small batch) | 0.360 | 0 — innocuous |
| Revert only `d72d246a3` (Router RMSNorm fuse) | 0.395 | +0.035 |
| Revert only `03826cdd9` (MoE topk fuse) | 0.380 | +0.020 |
| Revert only `3398cb7af` (extend-attn + MoE configs) | 0.360 | 0 — innocuous |
| **Revert `d72d246a3` + `03826cdd9` together** | **0.445** | **+0.085 (pass)** |
| Revert all 4 (= origin/main) | 0.445 | identical to c2+c3 revert |

Both reverted commits modify the Gemma4 MoE routing path in `gemma4_causal.py`:
- `d72d246a3`: `rmsnorm(x, fused_scale, eps)` fast path in `Gemma4Router.forward`. The math is equivalent to `(self.norm(x) with weight=1) * fused_scale`, but BF16 accumulation order in the fused kernel diverges from the two-step path when `fused_scale ≈ hidden_size**-0.5 ≈ 0.022`.
- `03826cdd9`: `_gemma4_topk_softmax_scale_kernel` doing topk + stable-softmax + per-expert scale in one pass. Equivalent to `softmax(topk_logits) * scale[topk_ids]` for `topk ≤ 8`, but its FP32-internal `exp(top_logit - top1) / sum_top_exp` ordering doesn't match `torch.nn.functional.softmax` bit-for-bit.

Either alone causes a ~0.02-0.035 GSM8K drop; together the routing logits drift enough to flip enough expert selections that the MTP draft/target distribution gap widens (MTP `avg_accept_length` still looks healthy at 4.48, masking the underlying quality regression).

If you want to recover these speedups, the kernels need to be made bit-equivalent to the eager paths — e.g. accept `weight=ones` in the fused router RMSNorm and apply `fused_scale` as a separate elementwise op, and have `_gemma4_topk_softmax_scale_kernel` mirror PyTorch's exact softmax floating-point order (compute max, subtract, exp, sum, divide — all in fp32 with the same reduction tree).

## Validation

- Bisect, perf re-measurement, and Gemma4 MTP accuracy validation all completed on `ion8-h200`, container `sglang_bbuf`.
- Python syntax check passed for the changed Python files.
- New H200 Triton config JSON files (`E=128,N=704`) parse successfully.
- Extend-attention block-size sanity checked for `Lq=128,192,256,288`.
- Server benchmark + Gemma4 MTP CI test (TP=2, deterministic, 200-question GSM8K) confirm patched ≡ baseline accuracy (both 0.445).

title: Improve registration in cpu_graph_runner
author: CaoE
body:
## Motivation

During CPU graph compilation, these custom CPU ops are intended to run through Inductor fallback. When a custom op does not have an explicit lowering registered, Inductor can create an implicit fallback, but that path first builds diagnostic
messages for the missing lowering. For large CPU compile graphs, formatting those diagnostics may be extremely slow.

## Modifications

* Explicitly registers fallback lowerings with `make_fallback(op, warn=False)` for the CPU custom ops that already have fake implementations, so Inductor can take the fallback path directly.

title: [AMD] Enable HiSparse on ROCm
author: clintg6
body:
# Enable HiSparse for DSA models on ROCm

## Summary

This change enables HiSparse for DeepSeek-style DSA models on ROCm, validated on MI355X, while keeping CUDA behavior unchanged. ROCm uses TileLang as the default HiSparse DSA backend, supports FP8 and BF16 KV cache, and can also run with AITER when the user explicitly selects the AITER DSA backend.

The main work is in three areas: making the shared HiSparse swap-in kernel correct for AMD wavefront64, adding the ROCm-specific HiSparse allocator/coordinator paths, and wiring ROCm DSA backend policy so TileLang and AITER use the KV-cache layout their kernels expect.

## Why This Is Needed

HiSparse keeps a hot working set of KV cache on GPU and stores the rest in host memory. The existing implementation was built around CUDA assumptions: warp32 behavior, CUDA inline PTX copies, and allocator flows that did not cover ROCm’s `page_size == 1` path.

On ROCm these assumptions can break swap-in correctness and leak temporary device mappings during decode. For DSA models, ROCm also needs a backend choice that matches the KV-cache layout. TileLang is currently the fastest validated option, so it remains the default. AITER is supported as an explicit opt-in backend for comparison and debugging.

## Backend Behavior

With `--enable-hisparse` on ROCm, the default DSA backend is `tilelang` for both prefill and decode.

If the user explicitly selects:

```bash
--dsa-prefill-backend aiter --dsa-decode-backend aiter
```

AITER is accepted on ROCm. With BF16 KV cache, it uses the normal AITER sparse path. With FP8 KV cache, it automatically uses AITER’s BF16-Q/FP8-KV persistent sparse MLA metadata path. No extra environment flag is required.

Both TileLang and AITER keep ROCm HiSparse FP8 KV cache in the raw MLA layout:

```text
nope 512 fp8 + rope 64 fp8 = 576
```

This avoids the CUDA scaled FP8 layout, which is 656 bytes per token and is incompatible with the ROCm sparse MLA views used here.

## CUDA Impact

This PR is intended to be behaviorally unchanged on CUDA.

The wavefront64 kernel fixes are guarded with `USE_ROCM`, and the CUDA branch keeps the original assumptions: warp32 masks, CUDA inline PTX copy, and the prior LRU writeback loop. The coordinator cleanup for stale temporary HiSparse mappings is also ROCm-gated because CUDA’s swap-in path consumes only `top_k_device_locs`, where those stale mapping entries are harmless.

CUDA HiSparse backend selection remains dtype-specific:

```text
bfloat16 KV -> flashmla_sparse
fp8_e4m3 KV -> flashmla_kv
```

## Implementation

The swap-in JIT kernel now has ROCm-safe wavefront handling in `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/hisparse.cuh`. The code uses a platform-dependent `WARP_SIZE`, ballot mask type, full-warp mask, and popcount helper. ROCm gets a HIP byte-copy fallback instead of CUDA inline PTX. The inclusive-scan window and large LRU writeback path are fixed under `USE_ROCM` so wavefront64 lanes do not write outside the current iteration’s intended shared-memory window.

The HiSparse allocator now supports ROCm’s `page_size == 1` path. `HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator.alloc()` allocates both logical and HiSparse device indices and rolls back the logical allocation if the device allocation fails. `alloc_extend()` no longer asserts `page_size > 1`, allowing ROCm decode/extend flows to use the normal allocation path.

The HiSparse coordinator now frees stale temporary device mappings during ROCm decode remap before replacing them with the reserved device-buffer slot. Without this cleanup, temporary page-size-1 mappings can leak and later corrupt swap-in lookups.

The model-runner KV-cache sizing keeps ROCm TileLang and AITER in the raw 576-wide MLA layout for FP8 KV cache. This is required for both backends and prevents the AITER sparse MLA view failure caused by the CUDA scaled layout.

The AITER DSA path now handles FP8 KV cache without user environment flags. For explicit AITER + FP8 KV, both decode and extend build AITER persistent sparse MLA metadata and pass BF16 Q with FP8 KV into `mla_decode_fwd`.

## Tests And Validation

The packaged changes add focused unit and regression coverage:

- HiSparse JIT tests are registered in AMD CI.
- The swap-in JIT kernel has a multi-miss copy regression test.
- ROCm has a large LRU writeback regression test covering the wavefront64 scan-window fix.
- HiSparse manager unit tests are registered in AMD CI and cover the `page_size == 1` allocator path and decode-remap cleanup.
- Server-args tests cover CUDA/ROCm backend defaults, explicit AITER acceptance on ROCm, raw MLA KV-cache sizing for ROCm AITER FP8, invalid platform/backend combinations, and accepted/rejected HiSparse KV dtypes.
- The GLM-5 HiSparse E2E test is registered for AMD CI and uses TileLang on ROCm.

Local checks run on the packaged files:

```bash
python3 -m ruff check <modified python files>
python3 -m black --check <modified python files>
python3 -m isort --check-only <modified python files>
clang-format --style=file --dry-run python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/hisparse.cuh
```

All pass.

Runtime validation on MI355X showed:

```text
TileLang FP8 KV:
Accuracy 0.968, latency 531.376s, output throughput 80.642 token/s

AITER BF16-Q/FP8-KV persistent path:
Accuracy 0.968, latency 666.757s, output throughput 63.344 token/s
```

TileLang is therefore kept as the default ROCm HiSparse backend. AITER remains useful for explicit comparison and debugging, and it no longer requires a separate environment flag for FP8 KV cache.

## Recommended ROCm Starting Point

For MI300X-class GPUs, the validated GLM-5 HiSparse configuration starts from:

```bash
nohup python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/GLM-5.1/ \
  --tp 8 \
  --port 8000 \
  --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 8}' \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.65 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang \
  --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --max-running-requests 2 \
  --watchdog-timeout 1200 \
  --skip-server-warmup \
  --enable-hisparse \
  --hisparse-config '{"top_k": 2048, "device_buffer_size": 2048, "host_to_device_ratio": 1}' \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  &
```

These are test/serving recommendations, not forced runtime defaults.

## Notes

TileLang remains the recommended ROCm HiSparse backend because it is faster in current testing. AITER is accepted when explicitly selected and uses BF16-Q/FP8-KV persistent sparse MLA automatically for FP8 KV cache.

title: [core] Make overlap-schedule WAR barrier CUDA-only
author: bingxche
body:
Started as a revert of #26380; instead this keeps #26380's data-race fix on CUDA and reverts it on other platforms, where the barrier caused regressions.

## Summary
- Gate the overlap-schedule WAR barrier (`schedule_stream.wait_stream(forward_stream)`) and its D2H-stream occupancy compensation behind `is_cuda()`. CUDA keeps #26380; other platforms (HIP / NPU / CPU) fall back to pre-#26380 behavior.

## Background
- #26380 added a global WAR barrier to fix an overlap-scheduling data race. It is free on CUDA but regressed AMD/HIP:
  - `test_deepseek_r1_mxfp4_8gpu` (MTP): all 8 TP ranks hit the scheduler watchdog timeout (hang).
  - `test_priority_scheduling`: `test_priority_scheduling_request_ordering_validation` assertion failure.
  - DSv4 non-MTP: ~20% throughput drop.
- CUDA shows no measurable throughput change across Llama-3 + EAGLE3 (MTP), DSv4 MTP, and DSv4 non-MTP — data in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26380#issuecomment-4571064550.

## Changes
- `scheduler.py` / `disaggregation/decode.py` / `disaggregation/prefill.py`: guard the three `schedule_stream.wait_stream(forward_stream)` barriers with `self._war_barrier_enabled = is_cuda()`.
- `managers/overlap_utils.py`: narrow the `fwd_prepare_d2h_stream` + pinned-buffer compensation from `_is_cuda or _is_hip` to `_is_cuda`.

Reference #26380.

title: test: stabilize Gemma4 26B-A4B MTP GSM8K test with deterministic inference + tuned threshold
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Summary

`test/registered/spec/test_gemma4_mtp_26b_a4b_extra.py` fails on `main`. Two issues:

1. **Unreachable threshold.** `GSM8K_SCORE_THRESHOLD` (0.42) was derived from placeholder cookbook values (`OBSERVED_GSM8K_SCORES = {1: 0.45, 3: 0.45}`). Measured GSM8K (200 ex, 5-shot, greedy, triton, TP=2) centers around **0.36–0.39**, so the assertion never passes.
2. **High run-to-run variance.** Under the default (non-deterministic) path the `topk=3` config swings **~0.33–0.50** (std ≈ 0.06 over N=20) because batch-composition nondeterminism gets amplified through the speculative verify path. `topk=1` and baseline are more stable but still noisy (std ≈ 0.02).

This PR makes the test deterministic and recalibrates the threshold to the deterministic measurements.

### Changes
- Add `--enable-deterministic-inference` to the server args (batch-invariant kernels; triton is supported and keeps radix cache / CUDA graph).
- Recalibrate `OBSERVED_GSM8K_SCORES` to deterministic values `{1: 0.445, 3: 0.440}` → `GSM8K_SCORE_THRESHOLD = 0.440 - 0.03 = 0.41`.

### Evidence (N=20 each, 200 examples, 5-shot, greedy, triton, TP=2)

| config | non-deterministic mean ± std (range) | deterministic (std=0) |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (no MTP) | 0.378 ± 0.021 (0.335–0.435) | 0.470 |
| MTP topk=1 | 0.371 ± 0.017 (0.350–0.425) | **0.445** |
| MTP topk=3 | 0.409 ± 0.059 (0.335–0.500) | **0.440** |

With deterministic inference every one of the 20 runs/config produced an identical score (std = 0), and the `topk=3` bimodal swing disappears entirely — confirming it was nondeterminism, not a correctness bug. Acceptance lengths stay healthy (topk=1 ≈ 4.49, topk=3 ≈ 4.96; threshold 1.5).

## Test plan
- [ ] CI `extra-a` stage (`2-gpu-large`) runs `test_gsm8k_mtp` for topk ∈ {1, 3}; both should clear 0.41 with margin and std≈0.
- Note: deterministic mode is slightly slower per run (~40s vs ~35s here) and disables overlap scheduler / custom all-reduce.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)
The ~2.5–3 pt gap between baseline (0.470) and MTP (0.445/0.440) under greedy is small but nonzero; spec decoding should be near-lossless. Worth a separate investigation into the Frozen-KV MTP verify path. The non-deterministic topk=3 amplification is also worth understanding.

title: [refactor] unify cuda-graph capture/replay across attention backends
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

Reland of #26134 (reverted by #26166), extended to cover four additional backends. Single PR replacing the stacked split series — #26144 (round 2), #26159 (round 3), #26160 (round 4), #26162 (round 5) — which were chained off each other's branches and could not land independently without sequential rebases.

## Modifications

Unify `init_forward_metadata_{capture,replay}_cuda_graph` across attention backends. Capture either delegates to replay (Pattern A) or shares a common buffer-binding helper (Pattern B). Per-backend details are in the individual commit messages.

Backends covered:

- FlashAttention, FlashMLA, TRTLLM-MHA — from #26144
- AITER, DualChunk FlashAttention, Hybrid linear attn, TRTLLM-MLA — from #26159
- Ascend, Ascend-GDN, Lightning, TBO — from #26160
- DeepSeek V4 (+ HIP-radix), DSA, FlashInfer-MLA — from #26162
- **New in this PR**: CutlassMLA, FlashInfer, Triton, Wave

Also adds a TBO regression test in `test/registered/attention/unittests/dense/test_tbo.py` — the dropped round-4 TBO change had capture short-circuit to its own replay (skipping `primary.capture`), which left per-bs metadata dicts empty and raised `KeyError: bs` at replay time. The test wires `TboAttnBackend(primary=fa3, children=[fa3, fa3])`, prepares a TARGET_VERIFY chain batch with EAGLE spec_info, and calls `init_forward_metadata_capture_cuda_graph` directly; without the guard the call raises, with it capture completes cleanly.

The `triton_backend.py` conflict between this refactor and #26152's SWA fix is resolved by taking the state with both applied — so this PR includes the #26152 fix.

## Supersedes

- #26168 — first reland attempt, CI red, closed
- #26144 / #26159 / #26160 / #26162 — stacked split series, to be closed after this lands

title: test: add trtllm_mha EAGLE-draft CG runner coverage (chain)
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

PRs #26521 and #26655 both fixed bugs in `trtllm_mha_backend.py`'s draft-decode CG path. Both fixes shipped under green unittests because no test exercised that code path — the `trtllm_mha` EAGLE-draft runner cell in `dense/README.md` was marked `deferred: requires chain-only graph capture wiring`.

This PR closes that gap: adds a chain-only (topk=1) EAGLE-draft CG runner test that drives `init_forward_metadata_capture_cuda_graph:320-340` and `init_forward_metadata_replay_cuda_graph:460-476` — the exact code paths those PRs patched.

## Verification

With **PR #26521's capture-time `.copy_()` reverted**, the new test fails:
```
AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
Mismatched elements: 2 / 4 (50.0%)
```
Confirms the test catches the capture-time NaN bug (#26521).

With **PR #26655's replay-time rebind reverted** while #26521 is intact, the test still **passes** — PR #26655's bug requires multi-batch-size replay sequencing (e.g., capture at `[2, 4]`, replay at bs=2 after bs=4) which the current single-replay harness doesn't expose. A follow-up could extend the harness to alternate replays across captured batch sizes to close that gap.

## Why chain only

title: [AMD] Work around HIP TPOT regression from Event.wait() in MTP seq lens resolution

Use Event.synchronize() instead of Event.wait() for publish_ready on HIP,

title: Capture indexer top-k for rollout replay (DP-attention / cuda-graph safe)
author: yueming-yuan
body:
## What

Capture the NSA / DSV4 indexer's per-query top-k selection during rollout so RL training can **replay** it instead of recomputing, for GLM-5 / DeepSeek-V4 sparse (compressed) attention.

Three commits:

1. **Return indexer_topk num_layers in meta_info** — plumb the indexer top-k layer count through the response pipeline (mirrors the existing `routed_experts` return path).
2. **Capture sequence-relative indexer top-k for rollout replay** — record the unfused `fast_topk_v2` selection (request-local sequence positions) rather than the post-`topk_transform` paged/ragged KV-cache coordinates; the attention kernel still consumes the transformed indices. The dense-MHA prefill path also captures its select-all selection when a capturer is set.
3. **Make indexer top-k capture DP-attention / cuda-graph safe** — under DP attention the device buffer is a shared, rank-padded global buffer, but each DP rank only computes its own tokens' top-k. Write/read at the per-DP-rank offset (mirroring `RoutedExpertsCapturer`) instead of the buffer head, and handle the `global_num_tokens_cpu is None` cuda-graph-capture batch.

## Why

Training-side replay needs request-local sequence positions. The earlier capture recorded paged coordinates and, under DP attention, only DP rank 0 was correct (ranks 1+ clobbered/read the buffer head) — training then attended to out-of-window keys (`-inf` indexer logits) and produced NaN in the backward pass.

Validated end-to-end on the GLM-5 4-layer indexer-replay e2e test: replay mismatch = 0 and finite train grad-norm across training steps.

title: [bugfix]: size CuteDSL MoE allgather buffers for the worst-case forward
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

`--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl` on the standard (non-A2A) allgather path crashes at serving time:

```
ValueError: num_tokens (4073) exceeds max_num_tokens (2048)
```

Regression from #22669: `ensure_cutedsl_wrapper` sizes the `CuteDslMoEWrapper` CUDA-graph buffers from the **first forward's** token count (`max(num_tokens, 1)`) — a small startup capture batch. A larger real forward then trips FlashInfer's `run()` guard and kills the scheduler. Repros on `nvidia/DeepSeek-V3-0324-FP4` (`--tp 4 --ep 1 --attention-backend trtllm_mla --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl --quantization modelopt_fp4`, no DP attention); still on `main`. The buffer should instead cover the worst-case forward, which is known up front from the server config.

## Modifications

- Add `ServerArgs.cutedsl_moe_max_num_tokens()`: the single per-(DP-)rank bound `max(max_prefill_tokens, piecewise_cuda_graph_max_tokens, cuda_graph_max_bs * num_tokens_per_bs)` (`num_tokens_per_bs = speculative_num_draft_tokens` under spec decode).
- Allgather wrapper sizing uses `dp_size * cutedsl_moe_max_num_tokens()`; drop the unused `num_tokens` parameter.
- The FlashInfer A2A startup guard reuses the same helper (previously `max_prefill_tokens`-only), so both cutedsl paths share one bound.
- Unit tests for the bound (`TestCutedslMoeMaxNumTokens`).

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K (1319 q), `nvidia/DeepSeek-V3-0324-FP4`, 4xB200:

| State | Result |
|---|---|
| Parent of #22669 | PASS, 0.944 |
| #22669 / `main` | FAIL, `num_tokens (4073) exceeds max_num_tokens (2048)` |
| This PR | PASS, 0.945 |

A spec-decode stress config (small `--chunked-prefill-size` + NEXTN) confirmed each bound is load-bearing. A2A guard verified at startup level (valid config clears `__post_init__`; under-provisioned dispatch budget fails fast); full a2a serving wasn't run here (flashinfer alltoall needs MNNVL / `SYS_PTRACE`), but the a2a forward path is unchanged.

- [x] accuracy results

author: DarkSharpness
body:
(auto generated by claude)

## Motivation

Multi-GPU tests/benches under `python/sglang/jit_kernel/` each reimplement
torchrun dispatch and use `pytest.parametrize` to fan out across world
sizes. This PR centralizes that into one harness, migrates the custom-AR
and TP-QKNorm test/bench files onto it, and fixes the
`Exception ignored in: __del__` noise printed at exit.

## Modifications

- New `python/sglang/jit_kernel/mp.py`:
  - `multigpu_launch(...)` — outer process relaunches the script under
    `torchrun --nproc_per_node=N` once per N in `num_gpus`
    (`--num-gpu N,M,...` argv overrides, `--local-addr 127.0.0.1`).
    Optional `pre_launch_fn` runs once outer-side before any child, used
    here to parallel-precompile every `(dtype, world_size)` JIT variant
    so children hit a warm on-disk cache.
  - `register_comm_cleanup(comm)` — atexit-safe shutdown for
    `CustomAllReduceV2` / AOT `CustomAllreduce`: closes while modules
    are alive, then zeros the fields each `close()` rechecks
    (`disabled`, `obj`, `_ptr`) so the post-atexit `__del__`
    short-circuits.
- New `multigpu_pytest_main` (`tests/utils.py`) and `multigpu_bench_main`
  (`benchmark/utils.py`) on top of `multigpu_launch`. Legacy
  `multiprocess_test` / `multiprocess_main` removed (no callers).
- `benchmark/marker.py` `do_bench` gains `graph_context_fn` (wraps cuda
  graph capture, needed by `CustomAllReduceV2.capture()`) and
  `sync_multigpu_fn` (e.g. `dist.barrier(...)` before each timed
  replay). L2 flush is sized from `props.L2_cache_size`, and the

- `tests/test_custom_all_reduce.py`, `tests/test_tp_qknorm.py`,

title: amd/deepseek_v4 35/N refactor Triton sparse MLA decode dispatch kernel to always run in a fused kernel
author: amd-danli103
body: Update amd/deepseek_v4 integration branch Merging to main is WIP, we use this PR and upstream amd/deepseek_v4 branch to integrate in parallel. Original PRs at Day-0: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23600 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23608 Co-author: @yichiche, @Raiden-Makoto ## Motivation The Triton sparse MLA decode kernel dispatch logic previously had a fallback path to a 2-phase (separate gather + attention) implementation for decode batch sizes in [33, 255] from kernel-level benchmarking. But for real E2E test, this 2-phase path caused significant performance degradation at high concurrency (8k/1k, TP=8, cc=64/128) due to: - Extra intermediate buffer allocation (gathered_kv) - Additional kernel launch overhead - Inability to fuse gather and attention operations For example, at bs=64, `_unified_sparse_decode_kernel` alone takes ~65% of decode attention time, whereas at bs=4, the fused `_fused_gather_attn_dsv4_dual_scope_kernel `only takes ~29.6%. We should try forcing the fused kernel path even at high concurrency. ## Modifications - **Remove 2-phase implementation**: Delete 3 files containing the separate gather+attention path since won't be called anymore. (`triton_mla_kernels_decode_common.py`, `triton_mla_kernels_decode_dsv4.py`, `triton_mla_kernels_decode_splitk.py`) - **Simplify kernel dispatch**: All dual-scope cases now use fused kernels: - Small batches: fused split-K kernel (better GPU utilization) - Large batches / extend / prefill: fused no-splitk kernel - Previously 2-phase [33, 255] range: now uses fused no-splitk - **Code cleanup**: Inline `_bucket_total_tokens`, extract `_decide_splitk_dual_scope` as shared function, remove dead code ## Accuracy Tests gsm8k accuracy ~0.939/0.942 (2 rounds confirmation) ## Speed Tests and Profiling This opt should benefit those cases where the batch size locates in [33, 255] that will fall back to the 2phase implementation, and now they will be forced to run into the fused kernel. title: [refactor] Unify CUDA graph runner input buffers behind CudaGraphBufferRegistry
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

The CUDA graph runners — full-graph decode (`CudaGraphRunner`), piecewise
(`PiecewiseCudaGraphRunner`), and breakable (`BreakableCudaGraphRunner`) — each
keep their own set of graph-resident input buffers and a hand-written routine
that, on every replay, resets the padded regions and copies each `ForwardBatch`
field into those buffers one by one. This per-field logic is duplicated and
subtly divergent across runners (padding resets, dtype-grouped copies, computed
fields such as `num_token_non_padded` / `global_num_tokens_*`, and structured
fields such as `ngram_embedding_info` / `pp_proxy_tensors`), and is easy to get
wrong when adding a feature.

This PR introduces a single, declarative registry for the `ForwardBatch`-shared
graph-resident input buffers and routes the existing runners' capture and replay
through it. It is **behavior-preserving**: the registry writes the same buffers,
with the same padding semantics, that the per-field code did.

## Modifications

**New `cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py`:**
- `GraphSlot` — declares one mirrored buffer: shape / dtype / axis
  (`bs` / `tokens` / `none`), a `PaddingPolicy`, an optional `post_fill` hook
  (computed fields), an optional `slice_fn` (non-trivial layouts such as
  `mrope_positions` `[3, T]`), and an optional `source_fn` (fields sourced from a
  nested `ForwardBatch` attribute or an out-of-band input).
- `PaddingPolicy` — `KEEP_PAD` / `FILL_SENTINEL` / `ZERO` / `FOREACH_COPY` /
  `FILL_ONCE`, capturing the padding behaviors the previous code encoded inline.
- `CudaGraphBufferRegistry` — registers slots, allocates them (or adopts an
  existing tensor via `bind`), and exposes `fill_from(fb, ...)` (padding reset →
  dtype-grouped D2D copy → post-fill hooks) and `extract_buffer(...)`.
- `build_decode_registry(...)` (bs-axis) and `build_prefill_registry(...)`
  (token-axis) factories.

**Runners routed through the registry (behavior-preserving):**
- `CudaGraphRunner`: builds a registry that **adopts** the existing decode
  buffers' storage; `populate_from_forward_batch` becomes a thin call to
  `registry.fill_from`, and capture sources its input views from the registry.
  All `ForwardBatch`-shared decode fields are registry-owned.
- `PiecewiseCudaGraphRunner` / `BreakableCudaGraphRunner`: a token-axis registry
  backs `replay_prepare` and the capture sites (breakable reuses the piecewise
  path via delegation).

**Input-buffer pool:** `share_input_buffer` now keys the shared pool on
`(name, numel, dtype, device)` instead of name alone with a strictly-larger
reuse rule. Buffers that mirror the same field with the same size/dtype/device
share one allocation regardless of registration order; differently-sized
requests get their own buffer and never displace an existing one, so a buffer
that has already been captured is never repointed.

The registry **adopts** existing buffer storage rather than allocating a second
copy, so capture and replay observe identical `data_ptr`s. The eager forward
path is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

This is a behavior-preserving refactor — the registry reproduces the exact
padding resets and field copies the per-field code performed, writing the same
buffers. A new CPU-only unit suite,
`test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py`
(33 tests), covers slot registration, every padding policy, `fill_from` /
`extract_buffer`, `post_fill`, `source_fn`, both factories, and the pool sharing
semantics. End-to-end validation should run the existing CUDA-graph integration
suites (full-graph decode, piecewise, breakable) on GPU via CI.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change to the eager forward path. The capture/replay copy preserves the
existing dtype-grouped `_foreach_copy_` batching, so no throughput change is
expected.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [DeepSeek-V4] Fuse UE8M0 scale rounding into FP8 group quantization
author: JoeLee314
body: ## Motivation This PR optimizes the DeepSeek-V4 `wo_a` FP8 path by removing the separate `deep_gemm.ceil_to_ue8m0` call after activation quantization. The original path launches quantization first, then rounds the generated FP8 scales to UE8M0/power-of-two format: ```text sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8 -> deep_gemm.ceil_to_ue8m0 -> deep_gemm.fp8_einsum ``` The optimized path emits the rounded power-of-two scale directly from the per-token group quantization kernel: ```text sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8(scale_ue8m0=True) -> deep_gemm.fp8_einsum ``` ## Performance Test DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP=4, 32K input / 1K output, 128 requests, max concurrency 4. Output token throughput increased by 7.8%. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K score: 0.928 ## Update: precision fix on Blackwell (B300/B200) The initial fused kernel in this PR had a precision issue on Blackwell: in the `SCALE_UE8M0 && !IS_COLUMN_MAJOR` branch, activations were quantized with the exact FP32 scale while only the *output* scale was rounded to UE8M0 (power-of-2). Since quantization and dequantization then used mismatched scales, EAGLE speculative decoding accept_length dropped from 2.76 to 2.69 on B300/B200. Thanks to @yhyang201 for catching this and providing the fix. The special branch is removed and all UE8M0 paths now go through `calculate_fp8_scales`, which computes the rounded (power-of-2) scale first and quantizes with it — matching the official DeepSeek-V4 `kernel.py` `act_quant(scale_fmt="ue8m0")`. The row-major UE8M0 test now asserts the scales are exact powers of 2 and the fp8 codes match the `ceil_to_ue8m0` reference. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #27789934317](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27789934317) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #27791183010](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27791183010)

title: update quantization code owner and document quantization contributions
author: Alisehen
body:
# PR Title

Add Alisehen as quantization code owner and document quantization contributions

# PR Body

## Summary

This PR updates quantization ownership and adds a developer guide for future quantization contributions.

- Add `@Alisehen` as a code owner for `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization`.
- Add `@Alisehen` as a code owner for backend quantization kernels under GPU and NPU paths.
- Add a `docs_new` quantization contribution guide that documents the Config / Scheme / Backend Kernel split, recommended file layout, validation expectations, and PR checklist.
- Link the new guide from the Developer Guide navigation and overview page.

## Motivation

The quantization codebase has been moving toward the structure proposed in the roadmap issue:

- https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/15194

The goal is to keep quantization config, scheme-specific weight handling, and hardware backend kernel execution separate. This makes it easier to support new quantization formats, review platform-specific changes, and maintain CUDA/NPU backend implementations independently.

I have been contributing to this refactor through merged PRs:

- [[4/N] Quantization Refactor: AWQ schemes and Kernel call and weight init split #21126](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21126): refactored AWQ into scheme-based quantization and split GPU/NPU backend kernel calls.
- [[5/N] Quantization Refactor: GPTQ schemes and kernel split #26402](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26402): applied the same scheme/kernel split to GPTQ.
- [[GPTQ] Refactor CPU quantization schemes #26786](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26786): refactored GPTQ CPU quantization schemes as part of the same config/scheme/backend separation work.

These PRs are tracked in the roadmap under "Kernel call and weight init split".

## Why update CODEOWNERS

The changed ownership scope matches the areas covered by the recent AWQ and GPTQ refactors:

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization`: shared quantization configs, method selection, schemes, and layer wiring.
- `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/gpu/quantization`: GPU quantization backend kernels.
- `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization`: NPU quantization backend kernels.

Adding this ownership helps route future quantization PRs to reviewers familiar with the scheme/backend split and recent AWQ/GPTQ implementation details.

## Documentation

The new `docs_new/docs/developer_guide/quantization_contribution_guide.mdx` guide documents:

- the Config / Scheme / Backend Kernel architecture,
- recommended file layout for new quantization methods,
- how to split method logic from backend-specific kernels,
- tests and validation expected for quantization changes,
- PR checklist items for accuracy, benchmarking, and compatibility notes.

title: [JIT Kernel] DeepSeek-V4 DSA indexer: faster top-k + page-table transform (runtime k <= 2048)
author: DarkSharpness
body:
Note: after this PR, the v1 should be deprecated. v2 is now a superset of v1. (this line is written by human)
 
(auto-generated by claude)

## Motivation

The DeepSeek-V4 DSA indexer selects the top-k KV positions per query for sparse
attention and maps the selected indices through a page table. This fused top-k +
page-table transform sits on the decode critical path, especially for long context.
This PR provides an optimized JIT kernel for it.

## Feature

- **Runtime top-k — `k = 512`, `1024`, and `2048` are all supported** (`k` is a
  runtime argument, so a single module serves every `k`).
- Ragged per-batch sequence lengths.
- Arbitrary (power-of-two) page size.
- Optional raw (pre-transform) top-k index output.

## Performance

Benchmarked on B200 against flashinfer's `top_k_page_table_transform`
(apples-to-apples: both do top-k **and** the page-table transform), `k=512`:

- Faster in nearly all `(batch, seq)` configurations; up to ~1.5× at large batch /
  long context.
- Sustains ~3.0–3.6 TB/s (near HBM peak) for `batch ≥ 2048` at `seq ≥ 64K`.

Correctness is validated against `torch.topk` across all dispatch paths
(172 unit-test cases).

title: Fix the EAGLE chunked-prefill next-token chain (#26329)
author: fzyzcjy
body:
When EAGLE speculative decoding runs with chunked prefill, the draft input
rotation must use the next prompt token (not the verified next token) at the
tail of a non-final chunk, otherwise the draft chain diverges from the target.

Tracks the next prompt token of the chunked request on `ScheduleBatch`
(`chunked_req_next_prompt_token`, computed by
`_compute_chunked_req_next_prompt_token`), and consumes it in the EAGLE draft
workers via `_eagle_prefill_tail_tokens` so the per-seq tail token is correct
for the chunked request. Adds explanatory TODOs in the single- and
multi-layer EAGLE v2 draft workers referencing PR #26329.

title: Add a periodic full-radix-tree KV-canary sweep
author: fzyzcjy
body:
Introduce a periodic full-radix-tree re-verification mode for the KV
canary. Every N forward steps the canary walks all radix-tree-held KV
slots and verifies them, in addition to the per-forward HEAD/TAIL
verify. This catches silent corruption of cached KV that a given
forward step never touches.

Gating:
- Server arg `--kv-canary-sweep-interval` / `ServerArgs.kv_canary_sweep_interval`
  (0 disables; positive N runs every N-th forward step). Validated to
  require `--kv-canary` in {log, raise}.
- Threaded through as `CanaryConfig.sweep_interval` via
  `CanaryConfig.from_env`.

Runtime (python/sglang/srt/kv_canary/):
- `runner/sweep.py` (SweepOrchestrator): drives the cadence and launches.
- `sweep_plan_builder.py` (build_verify_plan_radix_sweep): builds a verify
  plan directly from the radix-cache walker output.
- `radix_cache_walker.py`: enumerates radix-tree-held KV slots.
- `runner/canary_manager.py`: constructs the orchestrator, calls
  `maybe_run_sweep()` in `_post_ops_outside_graph`, and exposes
  `attach_radix_cache()` (wired from `Scheduler` once the tree cache is
  built).
- `runner/kernel_launcher.py` (launch_endpoints_sweep) and `endpoint.py`
  (launch_sweep): launch the verify-only sweep kernels.

Kernel-tag taxonomy (jit_kernel):
- Add `SWEEP_K_FULL, SWEEP_V_FULL, SWEEP_K_SWA, SWEEP_V_SWA` to the
  `CanaryLaunchTag` enum so sweep launches stamp distinct kernel_kind
  values into violation rows.

Tests:
- `test_self_unit_runner_sweep.py`, `test_self_unit_sweep_plan_builder.py`,
  `test_self_unit_radix_walker.py`, plus sweep cases in
  `test_self_unit_endpoint.py`.
