title: Support EAGLE speculative decoding in the KV-canary
author: fzyzcjy
body:
Wire kv-canary into the EAGLE speculative-decoding draft/verify forward
paths so the canary write/verify runs during draft steps, in addition to
the existing non-EAGLE model-runner integration.

EAGLE issues multiple single-forward draft steps per outer step, so this
adds per-step single-forward-manager bracketing on top of the base canary
plumbing:

- `kv_canary/runner/canary_manager.py`: accept `speculative_num_steps` and
  allocate one `SingleForwardManager` per inner draft step
  (`num_sfms = max(1, speculative_num_steps - 1)`), so each draft step gets
  its own canary single-forward state. (The non-EAGLE path uses index 0.)
- `kv_canary/api.py`: thread `speculative_num_steps` into `CanaryManager`,
  and set `kv_token_id_vs_position_offset = 1` for draft workers (EAGLE
  draft pools rotate input_ids so slot `p` stores K/V for the token at
  position `p+1`; target pools have no such shift).
- `speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py`: swap the `canary_ctx` placeholders for
  the real `with_ops_outside_graph` / `with_active_single_forward_manager` /
  `context_tuple` hooks at the draft replay, per-step draft forward,
  draft-extend-for-prefill, and draft-extend forward sites, and call
  `mark_init_finished()` once draft cuda graphs are captured.
- `speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py`: swap the
  `canary_ctx` placeholder for the active single-forward-manager context.

The `with canary_ctx:` scaffolding was already inserted by the nullcontext
placeholder PR, so this is just swapping the placeholder for the real
context plus the import/mark_init_finished plumbing -- no re-indentation.

Every hook is dormant when canary is off
(`X if (c := <obj>.canary_manager) is not None else contextlib.nullcontext()`),
so there is no behavior change unless kv-canary is enabled.

Includes the mock-model spec-EAGLE end-to-end test.

title: Add real-data KV verification to the KV-canary
author: fzyzcjy
body:

(synthetic-only) canary: alongside the synthetic chain hash, hash the model's

actual cached K/V is caught (not just the synthetic stamps).

  chain hash (splitmix64_mix3) is unchanged; real_kv is a separate slot field.
- runtime: CanaryConfig.real_kv_hash_mode (from --kv-canary-real-data),
  CanaryBufferGroup.real_kv_sources_{k,v}, CanaryEndpoint real_kv plumbing,
  the pool-patcher real_kv source construction (buffer_alloc + adapters), and
  real_kv_hash_mode threading through kernel_launcher / single_forward_manager /
  sweep.
- server_args: the --kv-canary-real-data {none,partial,all} knob.
- tests/benches: real_kv coverage for the verify/write kernels and the runtime
  buffer-alloc / endpoint / pool-patcher units.

author: fzyzcjy
body:
Add two always-on KV-canary observability add-ons, both pure observers
of CanaryDeviceState counters and the sweep orchestrator (nothing
depends on their output):

- Periodic stats logging
  (python/sglang/srt/kv_canary/runner/stats_logger.py): a
  PeriodicCanaryStatsLogger that prints, every N forward steps, the
  number of protected tokens, sweep passes, cumulative violations and
  the count of active launch tags, driven once per outer step via a
  delayed D2H handler so the read never blocks the forward. Gated by
  CanaryConfig.stats_print_every_n_steps (env
  SGLANG_KV_CANARY_STATS_PRINT_EVERY_N_STEPS, 0 disables).

- Kernel-run-counter health check
  (python/sglang/srt/kv_canary/runner/health_checker.py): a
  KernelRunCounterHealthChecker that watches the per-tag kernel run
  counters and warns when a canary kernel stops advancing (e.g. a tag
  silently goes un-launched), catching wiring regressions that would
  otherwise pass silently. Unit test in
  test/registered/kv_canary/test_self_unit_runner_health.py.

Both are constructed alongside the other per-step runners in
CanaryManager and ticked once per outer step.

title: fix(moe): avoid unpacking None from masked deep_gemm without overlap when sbo enabled
author: whybeyoung
body:
# Summary
Under Single Batch Overlap (SBO), DeepGemmRunnerCore._run_masked_gemm can crash during CUDA graph capture with:

TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType object
  File ".../moe_runner/deep_gemm.py", line ..., in _run_masked_gemm
    block_m, threshold = deep_gemm_return_value

# Root cause
deep_gemm_wrapper.grouped_gemm_nt_f8f8bf16_masked only returns (block_m, threshold) when it is run with down-gemm overlap (i.e. overlap_args is passed); otherwise it returns None.

In _run_masked_gemm, the decision to unpack that return value was gated solely on the presence of meta_overlap_args:

meta_overlap_args = running_state.get("meta_overlap_args", None)
if meta_overlap_args is not None:
    block_m, threshold = deep_gemm_return_value  # crashes if None

But meta_overlap_args and down_gemm_overlap_args can become out of sync. In compute_overlap_args (single_batch_overlap.py):
- meta_overlap_args is populated whenever the SBO overlap path is taken, and
- down_gemm_overlap_args is only populated when SboFlags.enable_combine_down_gemm_two_stream_overlap() is true.

So whenever SBO is enabled but down-gemm overlap is not actually active, running_state ends up with a non-None meta_overlap_args while no overlap_args was passed to the kernel — the GEMM returns None, but the code still tries to unpack it.

This half-on state happens, for example, when:
- the effective runner is DeepGEMM via AUTO (--moe-runner-backend unset) while enable_combine_down_gemm_two_stream_overlap() checks the raw is_deep_gemm() enum and returns False, or
- the installed DeepGEMM build does not support the down-gemm overlap kernel (fp8_m_grouped_gemm_nt_masked → m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_masked() has no enable_overlap kwarg).

# Trigger conditions
- --enable-single-batch-overlap (SBO) enabled — this is required; without SBO meta_overlap_args is never set and the branch is never reached.
- DeepEP a2a + DeepGEMM masked-gemm path (forward_deepep → _run_masked_gemm).

CC @Fridge003 @BBuf 

## Reprodution

```
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /work/models/ --port 30000 --trust-remote --host 0.0.0.0 --served-model-name xdeepseekv3testbo --log-level debug --enable-single-batch-overlap --enable-cache-report --prefill-round-robin-balance --moe-a2a-backend deepep --crash-dump-folder /log --enable-dp-lm-head --page-size 64 --chunked-prefill-size 131072 --enable-dp-attention --tp-size 16 --dp-size 16 --deepep-mode low_latency --context-length 131072 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 --max-running-requests 512 --ep-num-redundant-experts 16 --moe-dense-tp-size 1 --disaggregation-ib-device mlx5_bond_0,mlx5_bond_1,mlx5_bond_2,mlx5_bond_3 --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --allow-auto-truncate --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --load-balance-method total_tokens --enable-metrics --tokenizer-worker-num 8 --disaggregation-mode decode --nnodes 2 --dist-init-addr test-glm5-deploy-decode-0.test-glm5-deploy-decode.aiservice:20102 --node-rank 0
```

title: [AMD]Reuse fused FP8 KV cache write on standard aiter prefill/decode
author: IzacharyI
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
The fused bf16→fp8 KV cache write kernel (launch_reshape_and_cache_flash) was only enabled on the unified-attention path (use_triton_unified_attention). On the standard aiter path (read via paged_attention_ragged), FP8 KV writes fell back to set_kv_buffer, which performs a separate divide + cast + store_kvcache — i.e. extra elementwise kernels and intermediate DRAM traffic per K/V per attention layer.

The KV write only produces the fp8 cache and is independent of the attention read path, so the fused kernel can be reused for the standard path as well. This PR broadens the fused write to the standard aiter prefill/decode FP8 path and fixes a latent scale-correctness gap.

## Modifications
python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py:

Decode (forward_decode): relax the fused-write gating from use_triton_unified_attention and kv_cache_dtype == fp8 to kv_cache_dtype == fp8 and not use_mla, so the standard (non-unified) aiter path also uses launch_reshape_and_cache_flash instead of set_kv_buffer.
Prefill (forward_extend): add the same fused write for the non-SWA, non-MLA FP8 case (previously this path used the naive set_kv_buffer).
Correctness: pass k_scale/v_scale to launch_reshape_and_cache_flash. The existing decode FP8 branch (#23620) omitted them, which is only correct when the KV descale is 1.0; passing them keeps non-unit descales correct.
MLA is explicitly excluded (not use_mla) and keeps its own KV write path.

## Accuracy Tests

### Kernel-level (fused write vs naive set_kv_buffer)
Compared the reused fused write against the naive set_kv_buffer path (per-tensor descale = amax/fp8_max), checking both the written cache slots and fp8 contents:

| Case                   | fused vs fp32-divide ref | fused vs naive-bf16 mismatch | mean abs err vs fp32 ref (fused / naive) |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| decode  [32, 1, 256]   | 0.0000% (bit-identical)  | ~1.7%                        | fused ≤ naive                            |
| prefill [8000, 1, 256] | 0.0000% (bit-identical)  | ~2.5%                        | fused ≤ naive (fused slightly closer)    |

### End-to-end (before vs after, standard aiter FP8 path)
To isolate "FP8 KV quantization itself" from "this change", I compared the pre-change naive `set_kv_buffer` write against the fused write on the same standard aiter path. The pre-change naive FP8 write is not directly runnable on ROCm (`set_kv_buffer` → `store_cache` raises `BufferError: float8 types are not supported by dlpack`), so for the baseline I bypassed `store_cache` to use the naive scatter write — identical numerics, only a different store mechanism.

GSM8K, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, TP8, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy:

KV / FP8 write | gsm8k (1319) | invalid
-- | -- | --
naive set_kv_buffer FP8 (before) | 93.1% | 3.4%
fused FP8 write (this PR)         | 92.9% | 3.7%
bf16 KV (full-precision ref)      | 94.2% | 2.1%

naive vs fused differ by 0.2pp, and fp8 vs full-precision bf16 by ~1.3pp
(decode is bit-identical at the kernel level). So the small gap comes from FP8 KV
quantization itself, not from this change.

### Kernel speed (fused write vs naive)
case | naive (before) | fused (after) | speedUp
-- | -- | -- | --
decode bs=1 nkv=1 | 39.75us | 37.51us | 1.06x
decode bs=16 nkv=1 | 39.40us | 37.49us | 1.05x
decode bs=32 nkv=1 | 37.90us | 36.49us | 1.04x
decode bs=32 nkv=4 | 37.37us | 35.30us | 1.06x
prefill q=8000 nkv=1 | 100.41us | 41.32us | 2.43x
prefill q=8000 nkv=4 | 271.33us | 42.38us | 6.40x

## Speed Tests and Profiling
e2e: fp8-KV (this PR) vs bf16-KV (reference) — Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, TP8, bs=1, out=128
```log
===== fp8-KV (this PR)   in=8000 out=128 bs=1 =====
Output token throughput (tok/s):         73.77
Mean TTFT (ms):                          528.10
Median TTFT (ms):                        400.18
Mean TPOT (ms):                          9.48
Median TPOT (ms):                        8.60
===== fp8-KV (this PR)   in=2000 out=128 bs=1 =====
Output token throughput (tok/s):         100.90
Mean TTFT (ms):                          176.18
Median TTFT (ms):                        175.58
Mean TPOT (ms):                          8.58
Median TPOT (ms):                        8.58

===== bf16-KV (reference) in=8000 out=128 bs=1 =====
Output token throughput (tok/s):         84.33
Mean TTFT (ms):                          410.65
Median TTFT (ms):                        408.34
Mean TPOT (ms):                          8.70
Median TPOT (ms):                        8.70
===== bf16-KV (reference) in=2000 out=128 bs=1 =====
Output token throughput (tok/s):         100.31
Mean TTFT (ms):                          171.43
Median TTFT (ms):                        170.57
Mean TPOT (ms):                          8.68
Median TPOT (ms):                        8.68
```


KV dtype | TTFT in=8000 | TTFT in=2000 | TPOT | gsm8k (1319q)
-- | -- | -- | -- | --
fp8 (this PR) | 400.2 ms | 175.6 ms | 8.60 ms | 92.9%
bf16 (ref)    | 408.3 ms | 170.6 ms | 8.70 ms | 94.2%

title: Refactor EAGLE infer tests: shared fixture + kits + overlap matrix
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary

Refactor the EAGLE/EAGLE3 speculative-decoding tests (`test_eagle_infer_{a,b,beta}.py`) into shared, reusable pieces split by **feature x runner**. The old `a/b/beta` files mixed engine-vs-server, models, and overlap modes arbitrarily and the names carried no meaning.

This is a behavior-preserving reorg: the set of server configurations exercised is a **superset** of `main` (it adds the EAGLE3 topk=1 v1+v2 matrix and explicit flashinfer/fa3 coverage).

## Structure

**Shared infra**
- `python/sglang/test/server_fixtures/spec_eagle_fixture.py` — `SpecEagleServerBase` launches a spec server entirely from class-attribute knobs (`spec_topk`, `page_size`, `attention_backend`, `disable_overlap`, `env_overrides`, ...). `Eagle3Base` / `EagleLlama2Base` are config presets.
- `python/sglang/test/kits/spec_server_kits.py` — per-concern test-method mixins: `SpecCorrectnessKit`, `SpecParityKit`, `SpecAccuracyKit`, `SpecLogprobKit`, `SpecPenaltyKit`, `SpecFeatureKit`, `SpecPerfKit`.

**Test files** — all `stage="base-b"` (run on every PR); cheap/expensive is decided only by `runner_config`. Backends are pinned so a future default-selection change can't silently alter what each file exercises.

| File | runner | backend | content |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_spec_eagle.py` | 5090 | flashinfer | core: overlap x no-overlap matrix + full sanity kits |
| `test_spec_eagle_topk.py` | 5090 | flashinfer | topk>1: EAGLE3 topk16, Llama-2 topk8, chunked-prefill=4, FR-Spec token map |
| `test_spec_eagle_page.py` | 5090 | flashinfer | page64 (EAGLE3), page4 x {topk1, topk8} (Llama-2) |
| `test_spec_eagle_triton.py` | 5090 | triton | EAGLE3 (v2) + Llama-2 |
| `test_spec_eagle_fa3.py` | H200 | fa3 | EAGLE3 (the real H200 default) + Llama-2 topk5 page256 |
| `test_spec_eagle_parity.py` | H200 | flashinfer | lossless output parity vs a non-spec reference |
| `test_spec_eagle_stress.py` | H200 | flashinfer | perf (throughput) + retract / abort / waiting-/running-timeout |

## Coverage (server-config set)

Covers everything the old `a/b/beta` did, plus more. Every `(config x test-method)` cell from `a/b/beta` maps to a landing spot here; the logprob-losslessness gate and the `first_token_finish` / `max_token_one` checks are preserved on their original configs.

**EAGLE3 (Llama-3.1-8B):** topk1 v2 / topk1 v1 (matrix) - topk16 v1 - triton (v2) - fa3 (v2) - page64 (v2) - perf - parity
**EAGLE (Llama-2-7B), all v1:** topk8 (full kits) - chunked-prefill=4 - triton - page4 x {topk1,topk8} - fa3+page256 (topk5) - retract - abort-all - waiting/running timeout
**EAGLE (Llama-3-8B):** FR-Spec token map (topk4)

Axes covered: backends `{flashinfer, triton, fa3}` - page sizes `{1, 4, 64, 256}` - topk `{1, 4, 5, 8, 16}` - spec v1 + v2 - busy-time pool check - retract / timeouts / abort / token-map.

## Differences from `main`

Strict superset except for two intentional deltas:
1. **FR-Spec token map** is now guarded only by its gsm8k acceptance-length threshold (`~2.57`), instead of the full engine method set. The accept-quality intent (catching token-map regressing toward accept~1) is preserved.
2. **EAGLE3 page64** backend changed `triton` -> `flashinfer` (logprob-losslessness on page64 is still asserted, just on flashinfer).

## Notes
- **Parity is sequential**, not concurrent: the reference (non-spec) server is launched and torn down *before* the spec server, so only one model is resident at a time (two 8B servers don't fit on one GPU).
- Acceptance-length thresholds are per-model (EAGLE3 topk16 gsm8k `~2.48`, FR-Spec token map `~2.57`); they catch spec regressing toward accept`~1`, not tuned to pass.

title: Fix EAGLE draft graph seq_lens_sum padding
author: Terry-Uv
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

`EAGLEDraftCudaGraphRunner.replay()` pads `batch_size`, `seq_lens`, `seq_lens_cpu`, `req_pool_indices`, and related graph inputs from `raw_bs` to the captured CUDA graph `bs`.

However, `forward_batch.seq_lens_sum` still described only the raw batch. Several in-tree multi-step draft decode backends read `forward_batch.seq_lens_sum` while slicing draft `kv_indices`, including FlashInfer, FlashInfer MLA, and Aiter. This can make replay metadata inconsistent with the padded `seq_lens`.

This aligns the EAGLE draft decode CUDA graph runner with the normal CUDA graph and draft-extend graph behavior: padded fake rows are reflected in `seq_lens_sum` while replay metadata and graph replay run.

## Modifications

- Temporarily set `forward_batch.seq_lens_sum` to the padded value during draft decode CUDA graph metadata replay and graph replay.
- Restore the raw value with `finally`, including error paths.
- Preserve `None` when `seq_lens_sum` is intentionally absent.

## Tests

Test Command:

```
PYTHONPATH=python python test/registered/unit/spec/test_eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py
```

In the repro, the raw batch has:

```
seq_lens = [10, 11]
seq_lens_sum = 21
```

CUDA graph replay pads `raw_bs=2` to captured `bs=4` with `seq_len_fill_value=1`, so replay metadata should observe:

```
seq_lens = [10, 11, 1, 1]
seq_lens_sum = 23
```

Before this fix, the new regression test fails because replay metadata observes the raw `seq_lens_sum` even though the batch has already been padded:

```
AssertionError: 21 != 23
```

After this fix:

```
[CI Test Method] TestEagleDraftCudaGraphRunner.test_pads_seq_lens_sum_during_metadata_and_replay
.[CI Test Method] TestEagleDraftCudaGraphRunner.test_restores_seq_lens_sum_when_replay_raises

OK

title: fix(mlx): set canary_manager and materialize overlap-loop inputs on Apple Silicon
author: LijuanTang94
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #26832.

This PR restores end-to-end inference on the MLX backend (Apple Silicon, `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1`), which crashes in two places on recent main:

1. **Startup `AttributeError`.** `ModelRunner` sets `canary_manager` via `install_canary()` inside `initialize()`. `MlxModelRunnerStub` overrides `initialize()` with a lightweight path that skips that step, so the attribute is never set. Consumers (scheduler, cuda graph runner, speculative workers) read `model_runner.canary_manager` guarded by `is not None`, so the missing attribute raises:
   ```
   AttributeError: 'MlxModelRunnerStub' object has no attribute 'canary_manager'
   ```
2. **Prefill crash in the MLX overlap loop.** With deferred input materialization, `get_next_batch_to_run` leaves `batch.input_ids` unset; the CUDA paths call `resolve_forward_inputs` to gather tokens from CPU staging / the `FutureMap` relay, but the MLX overlap loop (`event_loop_overlap_mlx`) did not, so `async_forward_batch_generation_mlx` dereferenced a `None`:
   ```
   AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'cpu'
   ```

## Modifications

- Set `canary_manager = None` as a **class attribute** on `MlxModelRunnerStub`. The MLX path installs no KV canary and every consumer already guards with `is not None`, so `None` is the correct default; a class attribute keeps the guard valid even before `initialize()` completes.
- Call `resolve_forward_inputs(batch, self.future_map)` in the MLX overlap loop's `_launch_fresh`, before the forward, so prefill/decode inputs are materialized. Because this backend keeps a real `FutureMap` for the decode relay, no change to `resolve_forward_inputs` (nullable `future_map`) is required.
- Keep the `FutureMap` relay for the normal (non-overlap) MLX scheduler path in `init_overlap`.
- Add a regression test (`test_overlap_loop_materializes_prefill_input_ids`) that drives one overlap-loop iteration and asserts `input_ids` is materialized before the forward; it fails without the fix.

## Relationship to #26952

#26952 fixes the same overlap-loop crash by making `future_map` nullable across `resolve_forward_inputs` plus doc updates. This PR instead keeps a real `FutureMap` on the MLX path, so it only needs to wire `resolve_forward_inputs` into the overlap loop, with no signature/guard changes and no doc churn. The `canary_manager` class attribute matches #26952 so the two do not conflict in `model_runner_stub.py`. Documentation updates from #26952 can land separately.

## Accuracy Tests

Verified end-to-end on Apple M4 Pro (`SGLANG_USE_MLX=1`) with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` (a pure-transformer model, so the overlap scheduler is active):

- Before: the server crashes during prefill with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'cpu'`.
- After: the server starts and generates correctly, e.g. `"The capital of France is"` -> `" Paris. It is the largest city in Europe..."`; `/v1/chat/completions` and multi-step decode also succeed, with no crashes.

Note: mamba/hybrid models such as Qwen3.5 force `disable_overlap_schedule=True`, which masks this crash, so a pure-transformer model is required to exercise the overlap path.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A — functional bug fix, no inference-speed impact.

## Checklist

- [x] Code formatted (4-space indent, line length < 100).
- [x] Unit tests added (`test_overlap_loop_materializes_prefill_input_ids`); full MLX unit suite passes (49 tests).
- [x] Verified end-to-end on Apple M4 Pro hardware.

title: [AMD] Fuse compress norm+rope+hadamard into single Triton kernel
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

In the DSV4 compressor decode path on MI355, the post-compression pipeline runs two separate kernels back-to-back on the same `kv_compressed` tensor `[num_tokens, 512]`:

1. `_compress_norm_rope_kernel` (RMSNorm + RoPE) -- ~4.0 us
2. `fast_hadamard_transform_kernel` (Hadamard rotation) -- ~4.1 us

Since both operate on the same data and the full head_dim (512) fits in registers, fusing them eliminates one kernel launch and one global memory round-trip.

This fusion fires for every C4 compressor call with `rotate=True` (C-type layers have 2 such calls, A-type layers have 1). The C128 compressor has `rotate=False` and is unaffected.

## Modifications

- **`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/compressed/fused_compress_triton.py`**:
  - Added `_compress_norm_rope_hadamard_kernel`: Triton kernel that performs RMSNorm + RoPE + Walsh-Hadamard butterfly transform (9 stages for dim=512) in a single kernel launch. The butterfly uses a store-reload pattern through L1 cache (2KB per row).
  - Added `hip_compress_fused_norm_rope_hadamard_inplace()`: Python wrapper that launches the fused kernel with the hadamard scale factor (`head_dim^-0.5`).

- **`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/compressed/compressor.py`**:
  - When `rotate=True` (C4 compressor), dispatch to the new fused `hip_compress_fused_norm_rope_hadamard_inplace()` instead of separate `hip_compress_fused_norm_rope_inplace()` + `rotate_activation()`.
  - When `rotate=False` (C128 compressor), unchanged -- still uses `hip_compress_fused_norm_rope_inplace()`.

## Accuracy Tests

| Benchmark | Score | Threshold | Status |
|-----------|-------|-----------|--------|
| GSM8K (2000 questions, 5-shot, parallel=1000) | 0.950 | 0.94 | PASS |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

### Kernel Replacement (C-type layer, decode)

| Before | Time (us) | After | Time (us) |
|--------|-----------|-------|-----------|
| `_compress_norm_rope_kernel` (×2) | 8.3 | `_compress_norm_rope_hadamard_kernel` (×1) | 4.1 |
| `fast_hadamard_transform_kernel` (×2) | 8.3 | *(eliminated)* | -- |
| **Total** | **16.6** | `_compress_norm_rope_kernel` (×1, C128 rotate=False) | 4.0 |
| | | **Total** | **8.1** |

### Kernel-to-E2E Impact Analysis

| Layer Type | Layers/iter | Kernel Savings/Layer | Total Savings |
|------------|-------------|---------------------|---------------|
| C-type (MLA+Compressor+MoE) | 30 | 6.3 us | 189 us |
| A-type (MLA+Dense) | 61 | 0 us | 0 us |
| B-type (MoE) | 30 | 0 us | 0 us |
| **Total** | | | **189 us** |

Expected ITL improvement: 189 us / 20,570 us = **0.92%** (~0.19 ms). This is within typical run-to-run benchmark noise (1-2%), so the improvement is real at the kernel level but not distinguishable in e2e benchmarks at this precision.

TTFT impact: Negligible — prefill is dominated by large GEMMs; compressor norm+rope+hadamard is a tiny fraction.

### End-to-End Benchmark (il8k_ol1k, concurrency=4, 32 prompts)

| Metric | Baseline | After | Delta |
|--------|----------|-------|-------|
| Total throughput (tok/s) | 1,560.0 | 1,583.5 | +1.5% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 173.3 | 175.9 | +1.5% |
| Median E2E Latency (ms) | 23,080.4 | 23,078.8 | -0.0% |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 1,542.7 | 1,542.0 | -0.0% |
| Median ITL (ms) | 20.57 | 20.56 | -0.0% |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 21.51 | 21.10 | -1.9% |

### Configuration

- Model: DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP=8, MI355
- Attention backend: compressed
- Page size: 256, chunked prefill: 8192

title: [4/N] Qwen3.5Opt: Overlap mamba verify update with draft extend
author: yhyang201
body:
## Motivation

Add fused Triton kernels for Qwen3.5 (397B-A17B) to reduce kernel launch overhead and memory allocations in the attention output gate and MoE shared expert paths.

Target model config: `hidden_size=4096, num_attention_heads=32, head_dim=256, attn_output_gate=true`

## Modifications

1. **`fused_sigmoid_mul`** — fused `attn_output * sigmoid(gate)` kernel in `layers/elementwise.py`
   - Supports inplace write-back, strided 3D gate (avoids `.contiguous()` copy from `torch.chunk`)
   - Used in every attention layer's output gate path
2. **`fused_gate_sigmoid_mul_add`** — fused `final += sigmoid(hidden @ gate_weight) * shared_output` kernel
   - Used in MoE shared expert gate path
3. **Overlap mamba verify update with draft extend** via side stream in `eagle_worker_v2.py`

## Unit Tests

All tests passed on B200:

- `test_fused_gate_sigmoid_mul_add`: **91 passed**
- `test_fused_sigmoid_mul`: **201 passed** (flat, 3D, strided gate, Qwen3.5 MoE target config)

## Speed Tests

Benchmarked on B200, bf16.

### `fused_gate_sigmoid_mul_add` (hidden_dim=4096)

```
   num_tokens  Triton fused (us)  PyTorch eager (us)
          1.0          12.5            87.9     (7.0x)
          8.0           7.1            76.0    (10.7x)
         16.0           7.1           107.0    (15.1x)
       1024.0          13.2            87.1     (6.6x)
       4096.0          27.0            95.6     (3.5x)
       8192.0          45.9           130.8     (2.8x)
```

### `fused_sigmoid_mul` (Qwen3.5 MoE target: 32 heads, head_dim=256)

- **auto**: `inplace=False`, allocates new output tensor
- **auto inplace**: `inplace=True`, writes result back to `attn_output`, saves one allocation

```

title: feat: SM120 (Blackwell Desktop) support for GLM-5.1 inference
author: yilin-void
body:
Related issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/26087

Reference vLLM implementation: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43477

Old version prebuilt image: [`void0110/sglang-sm120-glm51:main-deepgemm324-flashinfer3395-cu130-20260602`](https://hub.docker.com/r/void0110/sglang-sm120-glm51/tags?name=main-deepgemm324-flashinfer3395-cu130-20260602)

## Motivation

GLM-5.1 NVFP4 uses DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) with an FP8 KV cache.
Running this path on NVIDIA SM120/SM121 requires both the sparse-MLA attention
work merged in [FlashInfer #3395](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3395)
and the SM120 paged-MQA/indexer work merged in
[DeepGEMM #324](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/324).

SGLang currently pins `flashinfer_python[cu13]==0.6.12`,
`flashinfer_cubin==0.6.12`, and `sgl-deep-gemm==0.1.3`. Those released
dependencies do not provide the required SM120 API and kernel combination.
This PR migrates the attention integration to FlashInfer's merged public API,
preserves GLM's packed arbitrary-FP32-scale KV layout, corrects memory-pool
accounting for that layout, and provides opt-in source overlays for validation.

The existing `trtllm` backend remains the default for GLM DSA on SM120 with an
FP8 KV cache. `flashinfer_sparse_mla` is an explicit opt-in until compatible
FlashInfer and DeepGEMM releases can be adopted together.

## Changes

- Add `flashinfer_sparse_mla` as a DSA prefill and decode backend.
- Call the public
  `flashinfer.mla.trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` API from SGLang's
  prefill/extend and decode paths.
- Adapt SGLang's GLM tensors to the FlashInfer SM120 sparse-MLA contract:
  - BF16 query `[tokens, heads, 576] -> [tokens, 1, heads, 576]`
  - packed byte-addressable KV `[pages, 1, 64, 656]`
  - 656 bytes per token: 512 FP8 KV bytes, 16 bytes of FP32 scales, and
    128 bytes of BF16 RoPE data
  - int32 physical sparse indices `[tokens, topk] -> [tokens, 1, topk]`,
    preserving inactive `-1` entries
  - `backend="sparse"`, `kv_scale_format="arbitrary_fp32"`,
    `bmm1_scale=layer.scaling`, and `bmm2_scale=1.0`
- Fail early when the installed FlashInfer API predates the merged sparse-MLA
  arguments, and reject unsupported shapes, dtypes, layouts, and skip-softmax
  settings before dispatch.
- Restrict this backend to `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, NVIDIA compute capability
  major 12, FP8 E4M3 KV, page size 64, and identical prefill/decode backends.
  A single explicit backend selection is propagated to the unspecified side;
  mixed TRTLLM/FlashInfer KV layouts are rejected.
- Reuse a dedicated zero-initialized FlashInfer workspace across DSA backend
  instances in the process.
- Size the MLA memory pool through `ModelRunner.calculate_mla_kv_cache_dim()`.
  For this packed layout, the main KV cost is 656 rather than 576 bytes per
  token per layer; including the existing 132-byte indexer cache, the total is
  788 rather than 708 bytes.
- Enable FlashInfer autotuning when sparse MLA decode is selected. When the
  normal warmup exceeds the 64-token decode cutoff, also run a representative
  small decode shape. Include the DSA prefill/decode pair in the autotune cache
  key.
- Fix the FlashInfer release bump helper so it reads and updates dependencies
  with extras such as `flashinfer_python[cu13]` without dropping the extra.

The CUDA indexer continues to call DeepGEMM metadata and MQA-logits paths, so a
compatible SM120 DeepGEMM build is required.

## Dependency Integration

The normal Docker dependency path is unchanged. The two source overlays are
disabled unless their corresponding `*_SOURCE_REPO` build arguments are set,
and they can be enabled independently.

- DeepGEMM defaults to commit
  [`2073ddb2814892014c33ef4cd1c7d4c148baf1fe`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/commit/2073ddb2814892014c33ef4cd1c7d4c148baf1fe),
  the merge commit for DeepGEMM #324. The Docker overlay checks out and
  verifies the full SHA, then installs the upstream source with
  `DG_FORCE_BUILD=1`.
- FlashInfer defaults to revision
  [`5f2bdc41f9ffecef9d8ed590e688e7c0f108504f`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/5f2bdc41f9ffecef9d8ed590e688e7c0f108504f),
  which contains the merged #3395 implementation. The overlay installs the
  Python, cubin, and JIT-cache packages from that checkout; the JIT-cache AOT
  build targets `12.0f` by default.

These are Docker-only validation overlays; they do not change SGLang's normal
exact dependency pins. The DeepGEMM overlay installs the upstream distribution
without removing the installed `sgl-deep-gemm` dependency metadata. The
FlashInfer checkout reports a newer version than the pinned `0.6.12` metadata,
so this path should not be described as a release-aligned dependency update.

### Source build

For this GLM SM120 path, enable both overlays:

```bash
DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build \
  -f docker/Dockerfile \
  --target runtime \
  --build-arg BRANCH_TYPE=local \
  --build-arg CUDA_VERSION=13.0.1 \
  --build-arg DEEPGEMM_SOURCE_REPO=https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM.git \
  --build-arg DEEPGEMM_SOURCE_REF=2073ddb2814892014c33ef4cd1c7d4c148baf1fe \
  --build-arg FLASHINFER_SOURCE_REPO=https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer.git \
  --build-arg FLASHINFER_SOURCE_REF=5f2bdc41f9ffecef9d8ed590e688e7c0f108504f \
  --build-arg FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.0f \
  -t sglang-sm120-glm51:source .
```

### Launch

```bash
sglang serve \
  --model-path nvidia/GLM-5.1-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --pp-size 2 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --attention-backend dsa \
  --dsa-prefill-backend flashinfer_sparse_mla \
  --dsa-decode-backend flashinfer_sparse_mla \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
  --context-length 131072 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 8 \
  --disable-prefill-cuda-graph \
  --json-model-override-args '{"index_topk_pattern":"FFSFSSSFSSFFFSSSFFFSFSSSSSSFFSFFSFFSSFFFFFFSFFFFFSFFSSSSSSFSFFFSFSSSFSFFSFFSSS"}' \
  --trust-remote-code
```

The `index_topk_pattern` override is specific to the validation checkpoint. It
is a checkpoint compatibility and performance/quality choice, not a sparse-MLA
kernel requirement.

## Current-Head Accuracy and Performance

8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, TP4PP2,
`sglang@1ad864e0c`, `FlashInfer@5f2bdc4`, `DeepGEMM@2073ddb`, GLM-5.1 NVFP4,
FP8 E4M3 KV cache, and `flashinfer_sparse_mla` prefill/decode.

### Accuracy

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K, 5-shot | **1273/1314 (96.8798%)** | 3549.472 s total | 209.789 |

| Cold passkey, 65,528-65,529 input tokens, positions 10%/50%/90% | **3/3** | 8.872 s | - |

### No-cache E2E Performance

title: [Spec] Fix Gemma 4 MTP with `trtllm_mha` crash issue
author: kpham-sgl
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

`trtllm_mha` + FROZEN_KV MTP (NEXTN) on hybrid-SWA models (e.g. Gemma-4) crashes with a CUDA illegal memory access once the SWA pool fills past the SWA-vs-full layer ratio (issue [#26957](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/26957), prior attempt [#26531](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26531)). `TRTLLMHAAttnBackend` cached its SWA state at `__init__` from `model_runner.token_to_kv_pool`. On the draft worker that is the draft's own non-SWA pool, so `use_sliding_window_kv_pool` was `False` and the SWA→full page-index translation became dead code — SWA layers then got raw full-pool indices and read the smaller SWA k-cache out of bounds.

## Modifications

- Resolve the SWA pool from `model_runner.token_to_kv_pool_allocator` (`get_kvcache()`) instead of `token_to_kv_pool`. In FrozenKVMTP the draft's `token_to_kv_pool` is swapped to the target's `SWAKVPool` per forward call, but `token_to_kv_pool_allocator` is set once at init and is stable — the correct source of truth.
- Mirrors FlashInfer, which already gates SWA eligibility on the allocator (`isinstance(token_to_kv_pool_allocator, SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator)`, `flashinfer_backend.py:1027`).
- Not registering the Gemma-4 draft as hybrid-SWA: the draft owns no KV (frozen), so its own `SWAKVPool` would be keyed by draft layer ids while attention runs on remapped target layer ids (KeyError + wasted alloc); the allocator already points at the correct target pool.

## Accuracy Tests

Reproduced end-to-end on B200 (SM100) with [repro_26957_e2e.py](https://gist.github.com/kpham-sgl/d696a3b8c2fdc959c940f7a8afdd9c9b): crashes before the fix (CUDA illegal memory access), passes after.

title: [Spec] Add `move_kv_cache` to `MLATokenToKVPool` for EAGLE v2 verify
author: alisonshao
body:
Stacked on #26997 (reland of #26866, the spec v2 tree drafting feature). This PR adds the missing MLA KV-move that the EAGLE v2 verify path requires.

## Background
- EAGLE v2 verify unconditionally calls `move_kv_cache(...)` on the KV pool (`eagle_worker_v2.py`) to relocate accepted draft tokens into their canonical slots.
- `MHATokenToKVPool` and the SWA hybrid pool define it; **`MLATokenToKVPool` never did** — so MLA + EAGLE v2 spec decode crashed with `AttributeError: 'MLATokenToKVPool' object has no attribute 'move_kv_cache'`.
- This is why #26866 was reverted in #26981 — the spec v2 path it enabled hit this missing method on MLA models.

## Changes
- Add `MLATokenToKVPool.move_kv_cache` — moves the single combined `kv_buffer` (latent KV + rope) per layer, with the same OOB-detect guard as the MHA path.
- Override on `DSATokenToKVPool` to move `index_k_with_scale_buffer` in lockstep (otherwise the indexer's quantised key + scale point at stale slots after acceptance, producing wrong sparse-attention scores at decode).
- `MLATokenToKVPoolFP4` inherits the base impl unchanged.

title: jit_kernel tests: bump multiprocess_test timeout 90s -> 240s (cold JIT cache)
author: alisonshao
body:
## Symptom

`test_tp_qknorm[2]` keeps tripping the 90s `multiprocess_test` budget on `call-jit-kernel-tests / jit-kernel-multigpu-unit-test`, even on **main** (e.g. [run 26792861548, head `54143264bf`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26792861548/job/78982967504)).

## Smoking gun

In the **same** job, the slower-looking parametrisations PASS:

| Test | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|
| `test_tp_qknorm[2]` | ❌ timeout | >90s |
| `test_tp_qknorm[4]` | ✅ PASS | ~45s |
| `test_tp_qknorm[8]` | ✅ PASS | ~52s |

Fewer ranks taking *longer* only makes sense if the first invocation paid for triton + cutlass JIT compilation that the later parametrisations then reused from a warm cache. The captured worker stdout supports this — only torch's `Setting OMP_NUM_THREADS` warning appeared before the kill, nothing else from the actual test.

## Fix

One-line bump of the `multiprocess_test` default timeout in `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/utils.py` from **90s → 240s**, plus a short docstring note explaining the cold-cache reasoning. Both existing callers (`test_custom_all_reduce.py`, `test_tp_qknorm.py`) inherit the new default; neither needs to override it.

The right longer-term fix is to pin JIT cache directories to host-stable paths (so fresh installs hit the existing kernel cache), but that's a separate, larger change. This is the minimum to stop the flake bleeding.

title: [HiCache] Fix PP inconsistency with HiCache L3 (#22607)
author: stepinto
body:
## Motivation

When deploying HiCache and PP, multiple PP ranks go diverge and eventually cause sglang crash.  The detailed reason was discussed in issue #22607.

## Modifications

This patch introduces two kinds of synchronization mechanisms to fix the issue.  I will illustrate this idea with an example of pp_size=2 and tp_size=1.

1. **pp_sync** across scheduler threads.  pp_sync is a new name introduced by this patch.  PP0's scheduler thread determine the number of completion events in its local queues (ack_load_queue, ack_prefetch_queue, etc). Then, PP1 must consume the **exact** same number of events from its queues.  This prevents divergence.

2. **all_reduce** across prefetch threads.  Consider a case that PP0 and PP1 have different lengths on their L3 storage for a given sequence. They have to reach an agreement on the length, by perform all_reduce(MIN).  This behavior is consistent with TP.

This patch also changes how `check_prefetch_progress` works.  Before this patch, it simply does all_reduce(MIN) to determine the final tokens prefetchted.  However, this would not work on PP, as we cannot do that in the scheduler thread.  This patch adds a new background thread `prefetch_sync_thread`, which does the all_reduce work instead.

## Accuracy Tests

Added `test_unified_radix_cache_hicache_pp_kl.py`.

I have also tested SWE-bench verified with DSv4 flash model.

I ran two groups:

- Group A: The baseline, commit 5747ed3b, without this PR, TP=8, L3 enabled.  Resolved 356/500.
- Group B: This PR, PP=4, TP=2, L3 enabled.  Resolved 353/500.

I analyzed the difference, and found 351 cases successful in both group, 5 are successful only in group A, and 2 are successful only in group B.  The 7 cases that are successfuly in one group but failed in another, are due to container exits after a long time. 

Here are commands for anyone has interested in reproducing this test.  Hints to make L3 are in-use:
- Use large number of workers (128), leading to large number of running requests.
- Limit number of tokens in L1 and L2.

title: [BCG][GLM5] perf: BCG support and prefill enhancements
author: mattteochen
body: ## Motivation https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23351 introduced PCG for GLM5 (`nsa_indexer`). As the current implementation runs the full indexer path, which is not fully captured by a CUDA graph, we found that running the fast indexer in eager mode yields better performance. Moreover, the current PCG split creates a CUDA graph island with only 1 kernel, introducing unnecessary overhead during dispatch. After `2048` tokens, PCG is disabled; the full path is being run eagerly in any case. ## Modifications - BCG support for NSA models - Run the fast nsa idexer (only k) in eager mode, marking it as a split op (opt in with env variable) - Registered another custom op with `bmm` + `unified_attention_with_output` to avoid single cuda graph with only `bmm` (opt in with env variable) - Updated the breakable cuda graph handler to merge adjacent eager Modules (this optimisation was also implemented for PCG, but then removed to reduce this PR code changes, as PCG is planned to be deprecated) ## Accuracy Tests PCG: ```bash gpqa: ==================== Repeat: 6, mean: 0.863 Scores: ['0.833', '0.854', '0.884', '0.879', '0.869', '0.859'] Mean latency: 14037.766 s ==================== ``` BCG: ```bash ==================== Repeat: 6, mean: 0.854 Scores: ['0.848', '0.854', '0.869', '0.869', '0.838', '0.848'] Mean latency: 15453.834 s ==================== ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Tested on B200 and INTEL(R) XEON(R) PLATINUM 8570. ### 1k1k Pareto for 1k1k on B200 TP8: ~4% speedup over the PCG solution at max concurrency: Median TTFT for 1k1k sees 10% improvement at max conc (not in pareto). title: Add FP4 Indexer for DeepSeek V4 on SM120
author: liz-badada
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #26209, extends the FP4 Indexer to SM120 (depends on https://github.com/sgl-project/DeepGEMM/pull/56). 

## Accuracy

DeepSeek V4 Flash GSM8K
|                                 | Accuracy |
|-------------------|----------|
| Default FP8            |    95.5% |
| FP4 indexer            |    93.0% |

## Performance

Two sets of results are reported because they were collected on different SGLang software stacks. They use the same model, workload, and FP8-versus-FP4 indexer comparison, but different SM120 main-attention backends. Therefore, each table is a valid within-stack A/B comparison, while the absolute numbers across the two tables are not directly comparable as a regression test.

### Test configurations

| Setting | Original PR measurement | Latest validation |
|---|---|---|
| SGLang source | `5453e93c50` | Tested at `245a47444c`; tree identical to current squashed PR head `9f100e6e27` |
| DeepGEMM source | https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/324 | https://github.com/sgl-project/DeepGEMM/pull/55 |
| Hardware | 4x SM120 | 4x SM120 |
| FlashInfer | Not used for SM120 attention | 0.6.14 |
| SM120 attention backend | **Triton** | **FlashInfer** |
| Baseline indexer | **Torch FP8** | **Torch FP8** |
| Optimized indexer | **DeepGEMM FP4** | **DeepGEMM FP4** |
| Model | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | DeepSeek-V4-Flash |
| Tensor parallelism | TP4 | TP4 |
| Workload | 8 prompts, 8192 input tokens, 256 output tokens, concurrency 8, seed 3 | Same |
| MoE backend | Marlin | Marlin |
| Chunked prefill | 4096 | 4096 |
| Radix cache | Disabled | Disabled |
| CUDA Graph | Maximum decode batch size 16 | Maximum decode batch size 16 |

The latest validation explicitly selected the supported SM120 FlashInfer paged-attention path:

```bash
export SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=flashinfer
export SGLANG_OPT_DSV4_NONPAGED_INDEXER=0
export SGLANG_OPT_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PREFILL=0
```

`SGLANG_OPT_DSV4_NONPAGED_INDEXER=0` ensures that the paged indexer path covered by DeepGEMM PR #55 is exercised. Sparse prefill was disabled to isolate the supported FlashInfer paged path on SM120.


### Latest validation: FlashInfer attention

SGLang tested commit: `245a47444c`  
Current PR head: `9f100e6e27`  
Both commits have the same Git tree: `dce05ad8fc61e17e0062bbafa376fc54cd8f95ae`.

Both cases completed all 8 requests successfully.

| Metric | Default FP8 Indexer | FP4 Indexer | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Successful requests | 8/8 | 8/8 | - |
| Request throughput | 0.155116 req/s | 0.389084 req/s | +150.83% |
| Input throughput | 1270.710 tok/s | 3187.374 tok/s | +150.83% |
| Output throughput | 39.7097 tok/s | 99.6054 tok/s | +150.83% |
| Mean E2E latency | 51.447145 s | 20.533064 s | -60.09% |
| Mean TTFT | 12.946906 s | 9.395233 s | -27.43% |
| Mean TPOT | 150.981 ms | 43.678 ms | -71.07% |

The latest server command was:

```bash
export SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=flashinfer
export SGLANG_OPT_DSV4_NONPAGED_INDEXER=0
export SGLANG_OPT_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PREFILL=0

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 31720 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 4 \
  --moe-runner-backend marlin \
  --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.70 \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --skip-server-warmup \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16
```

For the FP4 case, the same command was used with:

```bash
--enable-deepseek-v4-fp4-indexer
```

The current benchmark entry point has moved from `sglang.bench_serving` to `sglang.benchmark.serving`:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
  --backend sglang \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 31720 \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --tokenizer /models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --dataset-name random-ids \
  --random-input-len 8192 \
  --random-output-len 256 \
  --random-range-ratio 1 \
  --num-prompts 8 \
  --max-concurrency 8 \
  --seed 3 \
  --output-file benchmark.jsonl
```

Although `--skip-server-warmup` was used in the latest run, the benchmark client performed its default warmup request before starting the timed region.

### Original measurement: Triton attention

SGLang commit: `5453e93c50`

At this revision, the SM120 attention implementation selected Triton by default through `SGLANG_SM120_TRITON_FLASHMLA=1`.

| Metric | Default FP8 Indexer | FP4 Indexer | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Input throughput | 148.52 tok/s | 159.58 tok/s | +7.45% |
| Output throughput | 4.641 tok/s | 4.987 tok/s | +7.45% |
| Mean E2E latency | 440.97 s | 410.49 s | -6.91% |
| Mean TTFT | 237.20 s | 233.58 s | -1.53% |
| Mean TPOT | 799.11 ms | 693.75 ms | -13.19% |

The original server command was:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 31720 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 4 \
  --moe-runner-backend marlin \
  --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.70 \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 16
```

For the FP4 case, the same command was used with:

```bash
--enable-deepseek-v4-fp4-indexer
```

The benchmark command was:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \
  --backend sglang \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 31720 \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --tokenizer /models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --dataset-name random-ids \
  --random-input-len 8192 \
  --random-output-len 256 \
  --random-range-ratio 1 \
  --num-prompts 8 \
  --max-concurrency 8 \
  --seed 3
```

## Why the percentage improvement changed

The two result sets are not contradictory. The following decomposition shows what changed:

| Stack | FP4 E2E | Additional time observed with the FP8 indexer (`FP8 - FP4`) | FP8 E2E | E2E reduction from FP4 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Original Triton stack | 410.49 s | +30.48 s | 440.97 s | 6.91% |
| Latest FlashInfer stack | 20.53 s | +30.91 s | 51.45 s | 60.09% |

The FP8 indexer adds approximately 31 seconds in both measurements. The major change is that the FP4 path, which represents the rest of the model plus the faster indexer, decreased from 410.49 seconds to 20.53 seconds on the newer stack.

On the original stack, the approximately 30.48-second saving was small relative to the 440.97-second total, so E2E latency improved by only 6.91%. On the latest stack, the surrounding model path became much faster while the FP8-indexer overhead remained approximately 31 seconds. Removing that overhead reduced E2E latency from 51.45 seconds to 20.53 seconds, or 60.09%.

For the fixed-concurrency workload, benchmark duration decreased from approximately 51.57 seconds to 20.56 seconds. Throughput is inversely proportional to duration for a fixed amount of work, so this is a `51.57 / 20.56 = 2.508x` throughput ratio, reported as a 150.83% increase.

Therefore, the larger percentage does not mean that the FP4 indexer itself suddenly became several times faster. Its absolute E2E benefit remained approximately 31 seconds. The newer SGLang stack made the surrounding SM120 attention and model-execution path much faster, exposing the FP8 indexer as the dominant remaining bottleneck.

The full cross-run speedup should not be attributed solely to FlashInfer because the SGLang revisions also differ by roughly six weeks of development. A backend-only experiment on one fixed SGLang revision would be required to isolate the exact contribution of the attention backend.

title: [AMD] Optimize gpt-oss-120B performance
author: kkHuang-amd
body:
## Motivation

Integrate Atom's `pa_decode_gluon` paged-attention decode kernel into
SGLang's AITER backend to accelerate gpt-oss-120b decode on ROCm
(MI300 / MI355).  The kernel requires a SHUFFLE 5D vectorized KV
cache layout that aiter's `mha_batch_prefill_func` also consumes
natively, so we add the layout as a new opt-in pool format
(`SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d`) and route the AITER backend
through it on both prefill and decode.

End result on gpt-oss-120b @ MI300, TP=1, page=64, c=128:

- **+14 % TPOT** and **+15 % output throughput** vs the NHD baseline
  on 8K/1K decode; pa_decode_gluon itself is ~46 % faster than the
  legacy `unified_attention` decode kernel.
- GSM8K (lm_eval, 3-shot, chat template) stays within seed noise of
  baseline for both bf16 and fp8 KV cache.

The layout is fully opt-in — when `SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT` is unset
(default `"nhd"`) every code path is bit-for-bit identical to current
`main`.

## Modifications

### New env var
- `SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT` (`environ.py`) selects the physical KV pool
  layout. `"nhd"` (default) keeps today's behaviour; `"vectorized_5d"`
  enables the SHUFFLE 5D layout.

### Memory pool (`mem_cache/`)
- `MHATokenToKVPool` allocates the 5D layout when the flag is set:
  - K: `(num_blocks, H_kv, head_dim/X, page_size, X)`
  - V: `(num_blocks, H_kv, page_size/X, head_dim, X)`,
    where `X = 16 / store_dtype.itemsize` (8 for bf16, 16 for fp8).
- `SWAKVPool` propagates the layout to both full-attn and SWA sub-pools
  so SWA decode can also go through `pa_decode_gluon`.
- `set_kv_buffer` already does per-tensor fp8 quant on the host before
  the writer kernel, so the kernel just byte-copies into the cache —
  no scale plumbing needed on the writer side.

### Writer kernel (`layers/attention/utils.py`)
- `reshape_and_cache_shuffle_5d` / `launch_reshape_and_cache_shuffle_5d`:
  Triton scatter from per-token `(num_tokens, num_heads, head_size)`
  K/V into the 5D SHUFFLE layout. Used by `MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer`
  when the fused QKV+RoPE+set_kv writer is unavailable.

### Reader kernel (`layers/attention/utils.py`)
- `gather_shuffle_5d_to_linear` / `launch_gather_shuffle_5d_to_linear`:
  bit-exact triton inverse of the writer. Materialises per-token
  `(T, num_heads, head_size)` K/V from a list of pool slot ids. Used
  by the chunked-prefill gather-and-linearize fallback (see below).

### AITER backend wiring (`layers/attention/aiter_backend.py` + new
`layers/attention/aiter_utils.py`)

Two 5D-specific entry points live in `aiter_utils.py` and are called
from `forward_extend` / `forward_decode` only when the active pool is
5D, keeping the backend file focused on dispatch and the legacy NHD
path:

- `forward_extend_vectorized_5d`
  - **Fresh-prompt shortcut**: when every request in the batch has
    `extend_prefix_lens == 0` (first prefill chunk, no prefix reuse)
    skip pool reads entirely and feed the raw `(k, v)` to
    `mha_batch_prefill_func` in 3D LINEAR mode (page_size=1) on bf16.
  - **Gather-and-linearize**: otherwise gather the full per-request
    K/V from the SHUFFLE 5D pool via `launch_gather_shuffle_5d_to_linear`
    into a contiguous `(T, H, D)` buffer in `store_dtype`, then run
    the same LINEAR prefill. fp8-store layers forward the raw fp8
    tensors with per-tensor descales — aiter's LINEAR-mode prefill
    supports fp8 K/V/Q natively, no host-side dequant needed.
  - Without this path aiter's paged `mha_batch_prefill_func` aborts
    with `"no matching kernel found"` for our
    `(page_size=64, bf16/fp8, SHUFFLE 5D)` configuration whenever the
    scheduler produces a non-first chunked-prefill batch.

- `forward_decode_vectorized_5d`
  - Routes BOTH full-attn and SWA layers through `pa_decode_gluon`
    (SWA sub-pool is also allocated 5D). Full layers pass
    `kv_indices` + `sliding_window=0`; SWA layers pass
    `swa_page_table` + `sliding_window=layer.sliding_window_size`.
    fp8 KV cache forwards `layer.k_scale` / `layer.v_scale` as
    `key_scale` / `value_scale` so the kernel dequantises correctly.

### Fused RoPE + KV write (`layers/rotary_embedding/base.py`, `models/utils.py`)
- The HIP fused `fused_qk_rope_reshape_and_cache` kernel already
  supports the 5D SHUFFLE layout (`flash_layout=False`). Re-enable
  `enable_fused_set_kv_buffer` for the 5D pool and have the arg
  builder pass the raw 5D buffer when `k_buffer.ndim == 5`. This
  collapses RoPE + KV write into a single launch per layer per step.

### UX
- `server_args._handle_page_size` defaults `page_size=64` when
  `SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d`, since that is the page size
  the 5D kernels are tuned for.

## Accuracy Tests

All numbers below are GSM8K (3-shot, chat template) on gpt-oss-120b @
MI300, **TP=1**, run with the following commands:

```bash
# Server (vary --kv-cache-dtype between auto / fp8_e4m3; drop the
# SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT env for the NHD baseline rows).
SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d \
SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=False \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/gpt-oss-120b/ \
  --tp 1 --trust-remote-code \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --prefill-attention-backend aiter --decode-attention-backend aiter \
  --chunked-prefill-size 131072 --max-running-requests 256 \
  --page-size 64 --disable-radix-cache --port 8000 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3   # or `auto` for bf16

# Client
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template \
  --model_args model=/path/to/gpt-oss-120b/,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=65,max_retries=3,max_gen_toks=2048,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 3
```

| Layout              | KV dtype  | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---------------------|-----------|-----------------:|-------------:|
| NHD (baseline)      | bf16      | 0.8855           | 0.3647       |
| NHD                 | fp8_e4m3  | 0.8893           | 0.3381       |
| **SHUFFLE 5D (this PR)** | bf16 | **0.8870**       | **0.3389**   |
| **SHUFFLE 5D (this PR)** | fp8_e4m3 | **0.8848** | **0.3374**   |

Specific path coverage:
- Chunked-prefill gather-and-linearize path (forced by the repro in
  the bugfix commit): bf16 → 0.8863 / 0.3442, fp8 → 0.8848 / 0.3374.
- fp8 with the fused write path disabled (forces the standalone 5D
  writer): 0.8848 / 0.3480 — confirms `set_kv_buffer`'s host-side
  per-tensor quant feeds the writer correctly.

> **TP > 1 caveat:** GSM8K at TP=2 / TP=4 fails on this branch *and*
> on pre-Plan-A `main` (the NHD baseline also drops to ~0.32 / 0.16 at
> TP=2). Suspected upstream MoE FlyDSL kernel dispatch bug at
> per-rank shapes. TP=1 and TP=8 are unaffected. Tracked in
> `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` (A1, local doc) — not introduced by this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

InferenceX-style sweep on 8K/1K decode (256 prompts, MI300, TP=1,
`--page-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype auto --disable-radix-cache`):

| Concurrency | Layout | Median TPOT (ms) | Output throughput (tok/s) |
|--:|---|--:|--:|
|  4 | NHD baseline       | ~4.75 |   780 |
|  4 | SHUFFLE 5D (this)  | **~4.17 (-12 %)** | **~920 (+18 %)** |
|  8 | NHD baseline       | ~6.06 | 1220  |
|  8 | SHUFFLE 5D (this)  | **~4.88 (-19 %)** | **~1530 (+26 %)** |
| 128 | NHD baseline      | ~7.05 | 2007  |
| 128 | SHUFFLE 5D (this) | **~6.06 (-14 %)** | **~2307 (+15 %)** |

For full-context fp8 + 8K c=64 we re-verified single-run noise: the
SHUFFLE 5D + `pa_decode_gluon` path matches ATOM throughput within
±6 % across the sweep and beats it by 18-26 % at low concurrency.

`pa_decode_gluon` itself is ~46 % faster than `unified_attention` on
the same `(bs, num_kv_heads, head_dim, ctx_len)` for our gpt-oss
shapes.

## Known issues / how to use

```bash
SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d \
SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=False \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/gpt-oss-120b/ \
  --tp 1 --trust-remote-code \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --prefill-attention-backend aiter --decode-attention-backend aiter \
  --page-size 64 --disable-radix-cache \
  --max-running-requests 256 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3
```

- `--max-running-requests 256` (or omit; auto-tuned default is
  >= 256) is **required** for full accuracy on gpt-oss-120b. With
  `--max-running-requests < 256` the AITER MoE dispatch in
  `aiter/fused_moe.py` selects a bf16-activation path (governed by
  `GPTOSS_SWIGLU_MXFP4_BF16_BOUND`, default 256) that produces
  measurably wrong logits on gpt-oss MXFP4 — independently of this
  PR. Workaround for smaller batches:
  `export GPTOSS_SWIGLU_MXFP4_BF16_BOUND=128` (don't set to 0 — that
  crashes the server at init since warmup hits tiny `M`).

## Checklist

* [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit.
* [ ] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests.
* [x] Update documentation according to Write documentations.
* [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to Test
      the accuracy and Benchmark the speed.
* [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [diffusion] perf: Shard text when using SP in FLUX.1/2
author: avjves
body: ## Motivation Currently, in SP, only the image is sharded and the text is replicated on all GPUs. While this saves some comms time by not needing to transmit the replicated text in the all2all calls, it also balloons the GEMMs. As the entire text is kept, each GPU runs the full text through all the operations even though they only need part of it. This extra compute dwarfs the gains from less comms. Sharding the text has its limits - if the text tensor shape is not divisable by the number of GPUs, one would need padding for it, which would not be numerically accurate and therefore unacceptable. Given the limit above, this PR adds the sharding support to FLUX1/2 only: - By default, the text encoder in FLUX produces output tensors with shape matching the `maximum_sequence_length`, which is hardcoded to 512. This means the shape is not prompt-dependant and is therefore always divisable (2, 4, 8 GPUs). - In the cases where it would not be divisable (6 GPUs used), the old sharding behavior is used, i.e. whole text is replicated. Other models (like Qwen) have variable length text encoder output, so this is less applicable there. This would only benefit it given the right combination of prompt + sp_degree. ## Modifications For both FLUXs: - Added RoPE + text sharding if the constraints are met - `num_replicated_prefix` is now passed as the proper value, so no need to infer it ## Accuracy Tests ### FLUX.1 **Before:** **After:** **Command:** ``` sglang generate --model-path black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev --height 1024 --width 1024 --ulysses-degree 8 --num-gpus 8 --num-inference-steps 25 --guidance-scale 0.0 --prompt "Add a cute hat to the cat" --dit-cpu-offload False --dit-layerwise-offload False --text-encoder-cpu-offload False --image-encoder-cpu-offload False --vae-cpu-offload False --warmup True --warmup-steps 2 --vae-precision bf16 --seed 42 --enable-torch-compile ``` ### FLUX.2 **Before:** **After:** **Command:** ``` sglang generate --model-path black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev --height 1024 --width 1024 --ulysses-degree 8 --num-gpus 8 --num-inference-steps 50 --guidance-scale 4.0 --prompt "Add a cute hat to the cat" --dit-cpu-offload False --dit-layerwise-offload False --text-encoder-cpu-offload False --image-encoder-cpu-offload False --vae-cpu-offload False --warmup True --warmup-steps 2 --vae-precision bf16 --seed 42 --image-path /app/data/flux_cat.png --enable-torch-compile ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling **FLUX.2:** #### 1. title: [Gemma4] Use hard GSM8K accuracy floor for 31B MTP test
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

The Gemma 4 31B MTP test (`test/registered/spec/test_gemma4_mtp_31b_extra.py`) derived its GSM8K pass/fail threshold from placeholder "observed" scores:

```python
GSM8K_SCORE_MARGIN = 0.03
OBSERVED_GSM8K_SCORES = {1: 0.805, 3: 0.805}
GSM8K_SCORE_THRESHOLD = min(OBSERVED_GSM8K_SCORES.values()) - GSM8K_SCORE_MARGIN  # = 0.775
```

As the original comment noted, those `0.805` values were *seeded from the cookbook* as placeholders, not measured from this test's actual MTP first-200-sample run (both top-k entries being identical is the tell). The derived floor of `0.775` is therefore not grounded in real calibration data.

## Modifications

Replace the seeded dict + margin with a direct hard accuracy floor:

```python
# Hard accuracy floor for the MTP first-200-sample GSM8K run.
GSM8K_SCORE_THRESHOLD = 0.75
```

This lowers the effective threshold from 0.775 to 0.75 and removes the misleading placeholder-derived computation. Downstream logging and the `assertGreaterEqual(mtp_score, GSM8K_SCORE_THRESHOLD)` assertion are unchanged.

## Calibration

Measured GSM8K scores (first 200 samples) across repeated MTP runs:

| topk | runs | min | max | mean | std | pass | min margin | accept len |
|------|------|-------|-------|--------|--------|-------|------------|------------|
| 1 | 20 | 0.765 | 0.790 | 0.7798 | 0.0062 | 20/20 | +0.000 | 4.45 |
| 3 | 20 | 0.765 | 0.795 | 0.7808 | 0.0064 | 20/20 | +0.000 | 5.03 |
| all | 40 | 0.765 | 0.795 | 0.7802 | 0.0063 | 40/40 | +0.000 | — |

The worst observed run scored 0.765 (mean ~0.780). The hard floor of 0.75 sits ~0.015 below the minimum observed score, giving headroom for run-to-run variance while still catching real regressions.

## Checklist

- [x] `python3 -m py_compile` passes on the modified file.
