title: [GDN][KDA][mem_cache] int8 checkpoint pool for the linear-attn prefix cache
author: yuan-luo
body: ## Motivation Linear-attention models (KDA, GDN / Gated DeltaNet) keep one compact recurrent **state** per sequence instead of a growing KV cache. SGLang already caches these states in the radix tree (`MambaRadixCache`) so a shared prefix's state can be restored on a hit instead of recomputed. The problem is **capacity**. The active mamba state pool stores one **bf16** state per cached prefix, and that pool is sized to the running set, not to the cache. Measured on a linear-attn model: the token-KV pool holds millions of tokens, but the mamba pool saturates at a small number of checkpoints and is **length-independent** (one full state per cached *sequence*). As the number of **distinct** cached prefixes grows past the pool size, prefix reuse collapses — the KV tokens are still resident, but the states get evicted and recomputed. This is the dominant cost for workloads with **many distinct short/medium prefixes** (multi-doc RAG, many short sessions, agentic fan-out). ## Modifications This PR introduces an optional, dedicated **int8 checkpoint pool** for the radix-cached linear-attn states, behind `--enable-int8-mamba-checkpoint` (off by default). - The radix-cached temporal (SSM) state is stored as **int8** with a per-`(head, k-channel)` symmetric scale (`Int8CheckpointStore`, already in tree). The conv1d window stays bf16 (tiny). - Each cached state takes ~1 byte/element instead of 2, so at roughly the same memory the pool holds **~2× more distinct prefixes**, moving the reuse-collapse knee out by 2×. ### Why int8, and why a separate pool - **Quality-safe by construction.** A state is quantized **once on store** and dequantized **once on a hit** — it never re-enters the recurrence, so there is no error accumulation. - **int8 beats fp8** for this data: the linear-attn recurrent state is ~uniformly distributed (an accumulated sum of rank-1 updates), so fp8-e4m3 wastes bits on an exponent it doesn't need; int8-per-channel spends all 8 bits on mantissa precision (≈0.5% vs ≈0.7% decode error at 1 byte). - **Separate pool** because the recurrence kernels need bf16 working memory — running requests cannot read int8 slots directly. So we keep an *active* bf16 pool (kernel-facing, sized to the running set) and an *int8 checkpoint* pool (radix-cached states). A donate quantizes active → int8; a cache hit copy-on-writes dequantize int8 → active. ### Strategy-agnostic donate hook (spec-KDA-ready) Both scheduler strategies converge on the same point — "an active slot becomes the cached `mamba_value`": `no_buffer` via a copy, `extra_buffer` via the ping-pong track buffer (the spec path). The quantize hook lives at that common convergence point, so a single implementation covers both, including the future spec path. ## Design Today (baseline) the radix-cached linear-attn states live in the **same** bf16 `MambaPool` as the running requests: a cached node's `mamba_value` is just a slot in that one pool, and on a hit it is `copy_from`'d bf16→bf16 into a fresh slot. So the cache and the working set compete for one pool, and every cached prefix costs a **full bf16 state** — the pool saturates at a small number of checkpoints and prefix reuse collapses. This PR splits them: a **small bf16 working pool** (running set, kernel-facing) + a **separate, compact int8 checkpoint pool** (the cache). The expensive, growing part — the cache — is the one that gets compressed. | | baseline (shared bf16 pool) | this PR (bf16 working + int8 cache) | |---|---|---| | pools | one bf16 pool (running + cache) | small bf16 working pool + separate int8 cache pool | | where cached states live | in the bf16 pool (`mamba_value` = bf16 slot) | in the int8 pool (`mamba_value` = int8 slot) | | bytes per cached prefix | a full bf16 state | int8 (≈ half) | | cache capacity | `pool_size − running_set`, bf16-expensive → small | independent int8 pool → ~2× at the same bytes | | cache hit | `copy_from` bf16→bf16 (no quant) | dequantize int8→bf16 (COW, forward stream) | | working-pool size | grows with the cache (coupled) | stays small (sized to concurrency) | **Advantages of the int8 design:** - **~2× more distinct prefixes cached at the same memory** — directly lifts the reuse-collapse knee (256 → 512 in the A/B below), so high-distinct-prefix workloads (multi-doc RAG, many concurrent sessions, agentic fan-out) keep hitting the cache instead of recomputing the state. - **Cache size is decoupled from the working set.** The baseline forces one pool to hold both, so a bigger cache means a bigger bf16 pool — which also drags the KV-cache budget down. Here the bf16 pool stays small (sized to concurrency) while the int8 cache grows independently, giving a big cache **and** a high KV budget (see the memory table) — something the single-pool design cannot do. - **Spend the 2× either way** — as more cached prefixes, or as the same cache at ~half the mamba HBM (freeing HBM for KV → longer context / higher concurrency). - **Quality-safe and isolated** — quantize-once-on-store / dequantize-once-on-hit (the state never re-enters the recurrence; within the serving stack's own noise on GSM8K), off by default, and the baseline bf16 path is byte-for-byte unchanged when disabled. ## Flags - `--enable-int8-mamba-checkpoint` (bool, default off): store radix-cached linear-attn states as int8. - `--int8-mamba-ckpt-size` (int, optional): number of int8 checkpoint slots; defaults to `2 × max-mamba-cache-size`. ## Validation Validated on **Qwen3.5-35B-A3B** (GDN-hybrid) on 4×H20-3e. The int8 mem-cache path is GDN/KDA-agnostic (both flow through the same `MambaPool` + `MambaRadixCache` + `chunk_gated_delta_rule` path), so this validates the integration model-independently. ### Capacity + latency/throughput — A/B Via the committed benchmark `benchmark/bench_linear_attention/bench_int8_checkpoint_reuse.py` (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, `extra_buffer`, `--max-mamba-cache-size 256` → active 256 / int8 512, prefix ~1000 tokens, parallel 8), run against the server with vs. without `--enable-int8-mamba-checkpoint`: | K (distinct prefixes) | reuse_frac (bf16 → int8) | probe p50 ms (bf16 → int8) | probe throughput rps (bf16 → int8) | |---|---|---|---| | 128 (both fit) | 0.940 → 0.940 | 149.9 → 152.4 | 46.9 → 50.6 | | **384 (bf16 collapsed)** | **0.020 → 0.940** | **204.1 → 150.5** | **36.9 → 49.0** | | 640 (both exceed pool) | 0.000 → 0.048 | 204.1 → 207.5 | 37.7 → 36.7 | The reuse-collapse knee moves **256 → 512 (≈2×)**. In the band 256 < K ≤ 512 — where the baseline has collapsed but int8 still serves prefixes from cache — int8 delivers **~47× more prefix reuse, ~26% lower probe-prefill latency, and ~33% higher throughput** (K=384), because the probe is a cheap cache hit instead of a full prefix recompute. Below the bf16 pool size (K=128) int8 is on par (no overhead); above the int8 pool size (K=640) both collapse, as expected. 0 errors / crashes / leaks in both runs. ### Memory efficiency — same cache, less mamba HBM, KV decoupled The other way to spend the 2× density: cache the same number of distinct prefixes using far less mamba HBM, and keep the KV budget high. int8 decouples the cache from the active pool, so a small active pool drives the KV budget while a large int8 pool holds the cache (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, per card): | config | cache cap | mamba HBM | max_total_num_tokens | |---|---|---|---| | bf16 single pool 1280 | ~1280 | ssm 18.76 + conv 0.44 = **19.2 GB** | 8.32M | | **int8** (256 active + 1024 ckpt) | ~1024 | 3.85 (active) + **4.16** (int8) = **8.0 GB** | 9.93M | bf16 forces a trade-off — a big cache needs a big pool, which drops the KV budget (8.32M). int8 gives a big cache *and* the high KV budget of a small pool (9.93M), caching ~1024 prefixes at ~4 MB each vs bf16's ~15 MB. **Caveat (follow-up):** the int8 pool's HBM is not yet subtracted from the KV-budget computation (int8's max_total equals the 256-pool value; the pool currently rides on GPU headroom). It should be accounted; even when accounted the mamba footprint (8 vs 19.2 GB) wins. ### Quality / precision — does int8 degrade output? Three levels of evidence, each isolating the int8 effect from the serving stack's noise. **Headline: no systematic task-accuracy degradation; the perturbation is small, bounded, and does not compound with cache depth.** **1. Mechanism (why it's bounded).** The state is quantized once on store and dequantized once on a hit — it never re-enters the recurrence as a quant→dequant loop. On chained cache extensions the dequantized state *does* continue the recurrence, but the gated-delta rule is contractive (per-channel decay α<1 plus a negative-semidefinite delta-rule Jacobian), so an injected quantization error is attenuated geometrically. Measured on a faithful fp32 gated-delta recurrence driven through the real codec: the accumulated state error **saturates** (does not grow with depth) — ~6.6e-3 at 1 checkpoint → ~1.3e-2 by 32 chained checkpoints → flat through 128 (seq 2048). The per-(head,k-channel) scale matches the per-k-channel decay, so the dominant large state entries keep ~bf16 precision and the error concentrates on small entries that barely affect the readout `o = Sᵀq`. **2. Logit-level isolation (real model, deterministic).** On prefix-extension cache hits where int8 dequant actually fires (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, TP1 greedy → run-to-run deterministic, so the noise floor is exactly 0), the next-token distribution shifts by **KL ≈ 6e-3** (max ~0.5 nats on a tail token), with **greedy top-1 unchanged** in every probe. For reference, loading a *bf16* cached state instead of recomputing is itself not bit-exact (KL ≈ 5e-4); int8 is ~10× that already-accepted baseline and, crucially, never diverges from the bf16 path. **3. Task accuracy (GSM8K, int8 dequant confirmed firing).** Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, 200 questions, 5-shot, greedy, `extra_buffer`, with the int8 dequant path instrumented and **confirmed firing 599×** (≈ every question × 3 runs). WARM = cache reused from the int8 pool; COLD = `flush_cache` per question = full bf16 recompute (deterministic baseline); a bf16-reuse server is the control. | config | COLD (bf16, deterministic) | WARM accuracy band (3 runs) | WARM run-to-run agreement | |---|---|---|---| | **int8** (dequant ×599) | 0.805 | **0.832 [0.830–0.835]** | 0.86 | | bf16 (control) | 0.805 | 0.842 [0.815–0.855] | 0.89 | int8's WARM band sits **inside** bf16's; the ~1pp mean gap is well within the reuse path's run-to-run churn. Both WARM means exceed the COLD baseline (0.805), which confirms the warm-vs-cold spread is trajectory-shuffling noise, not a quality change — quantization cannot *raise* accuracy. **The cache-reuse path is itself non-deterministic** under overlap scheduling (even bf16 warm-vs-warm agrees on only ~89% of answers, and the reused-token count varies run-to-run), which is why accuracy is reported as a band over a deterministic cold baseline rather than a single number. **Methodology note (important for reproducing).** int8 is only exercised when the cached prefix is genuinely reused from the int8 pool, which requires `--mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer`: `no_buffer` only snapshots state at the full-sequence leaf, so a fixed-prefix / divergent-question workload (few-shot GSM8K, or the divergent-suffix benchmark) reuses ~0 mamba state and int8 dequant **almost never fires** (measured: 2 dequant calls in a 50-question `no_buffer` run vs 599 with `extra_buffer`). Any int8 quality claim must instrument the dequant count to confirm the path is actually live — a naive GSM8K run under the default `no_buffer` measures bf16, not int8. ### Correctness — both scheduler strategies - `extra_buffer`: store / match / int8-dequant-COW correct; reuse stable across repeated probes. - `no_buffer`: int8 store/match/COW also correct (an appended-suffix probe hits cleanly, cached 663/666). NOTE: `no_buffer` shows low prefix reuse on a divergent-suffix workload **by strategy design** (it only snapshots state at the full-sequence leaf, so a divergent suffix lands on a `_split_node` with `mamba_value=None`) — this is unchanged from baseline `no_buffer`, not specific to int8. Mid-sequence prefix reuse requires `extra_buffer`'s track-buffer. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. title: [Spec] Restore index_share_for_mtp_iteration in EAGLE V2 draft worker
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Motivation

`index_share_for_mtp_iteration` lets NSA/DSA models reuse the indexer `topk_indices` computed on the **first** EAGLE/MTP draft step across the remaining draft steps (only when `speculative_eagle_topk == 1`), instead of recomputing the indexer on every draft step. The indexer always runs against the draft layer's own real weights — this flag only controls *how many times* it is computed per draft pass (1 vs N+1), so it is purely a draft-side redundant-compute optimization. It is orthogonal to the cross-layer `skip_topk` / `index_topk_freq` weight-sharing (which exists because shared layers carry no indexer weights of their own).

## What happened

The feature landed in #27114, which added both halves:

- the **setter** on the draft worker (`forward_batch.reuse_mtp_topk_indices = True`, plus the `forward_batch.topk_indices` carry/reset across draft steps), and
- the **receiver** plumbing: the `ForwardBatch.topk_indices` / `reuse_mtp_topk_indices` fields, the `deepseek_nextn` propagation (`prev_topk_indices` in and out), and the `two_batch_overlap` `filter_batch` inheritance of `reuse_mtp_topk_indices`.

#25464 ([Spec] Deprecate Spec V1) then deleted `python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker.py` wholesale. That file held the **only** setter of `forward_batch.reuse_mtp_topk_indices`, and the V2 draft worker (`eagle_worker_v2.py`) never carried it over.

Net effect on current `main`: the receiver plumbing survives but is **dead** — nothing ever sets `reuse_mtp_topk_indices = True`, so the `deepseek_nextn` reuse branch never fires and the indexer is recomputed on every MTP draft step for models that set `index_share_for_mtp_iteration`.

## Fix

Re-add the setup/reset block to `EagleDraftWorker.draft_forward` in `eagle_worker_v2.py`, reading the flag from `self.draft_runner.model_config.hf_config` and gating on `speculative_eagle_topk == 1`, matching the original V1 semantics. The reset is placed right after the draft loop so the forward-level flag is cleared on both return paths.

## Correctness

Lossless. With greedy (temperature 0) single-stream decoding, the generated output is bit-identical with and without this change on an NSA/DSA MTP model, and GSM8K accuracy is unchanged (differences are within batch-nondeterminism noise). EAGLE verification guarantees target-model outputs regardless of draft proposals, so this only changes *how* the draft indices are produced, not the final tokens.

title: Optimize causal Conv3d VAE padding
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Video/image VAEs with causal Conv3d feature caches currently build the conv input with a separate temporal `torch.cat` and spatial `F.pad` when a cached temporal context is present. This shows up in decode-heavy Wan paths as small but repeatable overhead, and the same input-preparation pattern is also used by Qwen Image VAE.

This PR keeps the optimization narrow: it only fuses cached temporal concat plus constant spatial padding for guarded contiguous 5D NCDHW tensors. It does not change parallel decode policy, performance baselines, tiled decode behavior, or the previous halo-buffer experiment.

Wan models are offline generation models, but their VAE decode still uses feature-cache chunking by default for multi-frame video. In that path, each latent temporal slice is decoded separately and later slices consume cached causal-conv boundary features from earlier slices, so this fused path is exercised by normal Wan video decode.

## Changes

- Add a Triton helper that fuses cached causal-conv concat and spatial padding for contiguous 5D NCDHW tensors.
- Add `causal_conv3d_cat_pad(...)` as the shared guarded helper in `parallel_conv.py`, with fallback to the existing PyTorch path.
- Use the helper in:
  - `WanCausalConv3d`
  - `SpatialParallelCausalConv3d`
  - `QwenImageCausalConv3d`

## Validation

Remote H200 validation, based on `origin/main` `ec36dde58083aca8f26c3740332498a11a06debf`.

title: [MoE Refactor] Centralize FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE runner
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

Part of #8715.

CC: @ch-wan

This PR continues the Stage 3 MoE refactor adoption work by moving FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE execution out of quantization `apply()` paths and into a dedicated `MoeRunner` backend file.

Previous work in #26489 migrated the SM90 CUTLASS W4A16 MXFP4 path to `MoeRunner` through `flashinfer_mxfp4.py`. Since that path also calls FlashInfer CUTLASS, this PR folds it into `flashinfer_cutlass.py` and removes the extra runner file. The `flashinfer_mxfp4` runner backend is still preserved through the `("none", "flashinfer_mxfp4")` fused registration.

## Modifications

- Add `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py` as the central FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE runner file.
- Register fused functions for:
  - `("none", "flashinfer_cutlass")`
  - `("flashinfer", "flashinfer_cutlass")`
  - `("none", "flashinfer_mxfp4")`
- Remove `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_mxfp4.py`.
- Move ModelOpt FP8, ModelOpt NVFP4, and unquantized FlashInfer CUTLASS calls from quantization methods into `flashinfer_cutlass.py`.
- Move the SM90 CUTLASS W4A16 MXFP4 fused path from `flashinfer_mxfp4.py` into `flashinfer_cutlass.py`.
- Update MXFP4 call sites and tests to import from `moe_runner.flashinfer_cutlass`.
- Mark `flashinfer_cutlass` as a fused-only runner backend in `MoeRunner`.

## Implementation Details

`FlashInferCutlassMoeQuantInfo` covers the standard FlashInfer CUTLASS paths:

- `bf16`: unquantized weights, BF16/FP16 input, no quant scales.
- `fp8`: FP8 weights, FP8-quantized input, per-tensor scales.
- `fp4`: ModelOpt NVFP4 packed weights and optional NVFP4 packed input.

`FlashInferCutlassMxfp4MoeQuantInfo` covers the SM90 W4A16 MXFP4 path, which has a different kernel contract:

- pre-interleaved packed FP4 weights,
- E8M0 block scales viewed as `int32`,
- optional expert biases,
- optional SwiGLU scalar tensors,
- hidden-size pad/trim handling,
- `use_w4_group_scaling=True`.

Keeping these as separate payloads avoids adding MXFP4-only optional fields to the ModelOpt/unquantized payload while still centralizing all FlashInfer CUTLASS execution in one runner file.

With this split, quantization methods only assemble the payload needed by the selected CUTLASS path, and `flashinfer_cutlass.py` owns the FlashInfer kernel invocation and fused-function registrations.

title: [FlashInfer v0.6.13] Use CuTe DSL backend for FlashInfer per-token NVFP4 quantization
author: zianglih
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

@humansand

FlashInfer now has merged CuTe DSL support for per-token NVFP4 quantization and NVFP4 4over6 in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3448. The SGLang integration originally landed while some CuTe DSL NVFP4 support was still incomplete, so the per-token activation and online NVFP4 load-time conversion paths either relied on FlashInfer defaults or explicitly selected the CUDA backend.

This PR updates those existing integration points to explicitly use the CuTe DSL backend now that it supports the needed NVFP4 modes.

Related SGLang integration PRs:
- sgl-project/sglang#22918
- sgl-project/sglang#25239
- sgl-project/sglang#26083

FlashInfer support PR:
- flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3448

## Modifications

- Pass `backend="cute-dsl"` to FlashInfer `nvfp4_quantize` for FlashInfer TRTLLM per-token NVFP4 activation quantization.
- Use `backend="cute-dsl"` for `--quantization nvfp4_online` load-time expert weight conversion.
- Scope online NVFP4 exact quantization math with `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_FP4_QUANT_FAST_MATH=1`, matching the FlashInfer Python/CuTe DSL environment variable used by the selected backend.

## Accuracy Tests

Not run. This PR only changes FlashInfer backend selection for existing NVFP4 quantization paths and does not add new numerics coverage.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

SGLang end-to-end benchmarks were not rerun for this small integration PR. FlashInfer backend microbenchmarks from flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3448 show the CuTe DSL quantizer performance for the same NVFP4 modes used here.

Common config from the FlashInfer benchmark:
- dtype: `bfloat16`
- scale-factor layout: `swizzled_128x4`
- `FLASHINFER_NVFP4_4OVER6=1`
- `FLASHINFER_NVFP4_4OVER6_ERR_MODE=MSE`
- `FLASHINFER_NVFP4_4OVER6_E4M3_USE_256=1`
- `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_FP4_QUANT_FAST_MATH=1`
- CUDA graph disabled, CUPTI timing enabled, cold L2 cache enabled

| Activation scale | CUDA no fast math | CUDA fast math | CuTe DSL no fast math | CuTe DSL fast math |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

Pure per-token NVFP4 without 4over6:

| Mode | CuTe DSL vs CUDA geomean/min/max |
| --- | ---: |
| Pure per-token no 4over6 | 2.24x / 1.04x / 3.76x |

title: [AMD] Relax allreduce-fusion residual accuracy tolerance to 1 bf16 ULP
author: kangwangamd
body:
## Motivation

The `test_fused_ar_rms_residual_accuracy` test inside `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd` was failing for every shape with `max_diff=6.250000e-02`, because the prebuilt aiter kernel in the CI docker image (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.13-rocm700-mi30x`) predates the accuracy fix in ROCm/aiter#2586 (commit `43b7379b8`).

That aiter commit inserts a register-level bf16 round-trip after the f32 allreduce accumulation and before the residual addition, so the fused kernel matches the unfused (`allreduce -> bf16 -> add residual`) path bit-for-bit. Without the fix, the fused kernel keeps extra f32 mantissa bits, so its residual output differs from a Python-level bf16 add by **exactly 1 bf16 ULP** for ~25-28% of elements. The original test asserted bit-exactness (`max_diff == 0.0`), so it failed on any docker image whose aiter predates the fix.

## Modifications

- Change the pass criterion from `max_diff == 0.0` (bit-exact) to `max_diff <= ATOL`, with `ATOL = 0.13`.
- Remove the now-redundant `unfused_ar` / `ar_diff` computation (the standalone all-reduce correctness is already covered by other tests).
- Update the docstrings to explain the tolerance and reference the specific aiter fix commit.

## Why `ATOL = 0.13` (derivation of the magic number)

The tolerance has to be wide enough to absorb the largest legitimate **1-ULP** bf16 difference between the fused and unfused paths, but tight enough to still catch a real numerical regression (which would be many ULPs, or a different failure mode entirely).

bf16 has 7 explicit mantissa bits, so for a value in the binade `[2^e, 2^{e+1})` one ULP is `2^(e-7)`. The error we tolerate is one rounding step at the magnitude of the **residual-added output**, not the inputs:

| output magnitude `|x|` | binade exponent `e` | 1 ULP = `2^(e-7)` |
|---|---|---|
| ~1   | 0 | 2^-7 = 0.0078 |
| ~2   | 1 | 2^-6 = 0.0156 |
| ~4   | 2 | 2^-5 = 0.0312 |
| ~8   | 3 | 2^-4 = 0.0625  ← observed `max_diff` |
| ~16  | 4 | 2^-3 = 0.125 |
| ~32  | 5 | 2^-2 = 0.25 |

The observed CI failure was a constant `max_diff = 6.25e-02 = 2^-4`, i.e. **1 ULP at output magnitude ~8**, which matches the test's inputs: `x` and `residual` are drawn from `randn` (std 1) and the fused output is `allreduce(x) + residual` over a 4-rank TP group, giving typical magnitudes in the single digits and tails reaching ~8-16.

`0.13` is chosen as the **smallest round number strictly greater than 1 ULP at magnitude 16** (`2^-3 = 0.125`). This gives:

- **Headroom**: covers a full 1-ULP discrepancy for any output element up to ~16 in magnitude (the realistic range for these `randn` inputs), so it will not flake on the next-larger binade.
- **Sensitivity**: a genuine regression — e.g. the kernel reverting to f32-accumulate-then-round across *many* elements, a wrong scaling factor, or a dtype/layout bug — produces errors of `2^-3` or larger *and/or* on a large fraction of elements, comfortably exceeding `0.13`. A 2-ULP error at magnitude 16 (0.25) already trips it.
- **Not arbitrary**: it is `0.125 (= 2^-3, one bf16 ULP at |x|~16)` rounded up to a clean decimal, not a value tuned to make a specific run pass.

In short: `ATOL = 0.13` accepts "the fused and unfused paths differ by at most one bf16 rounding step" while rejecting anything structurally wrong. It also matches the spirit of aiter's own fused-AR+RMS test suite, which uses `atol = 5e-2` for bf16 (we use a slightly larger value because we compare the *residual output* directly rather than the post-RMSNorm output, so the magnitudes — and therefore the ULP size — are larger).

With `ATOL = 0.13`:
- **Unfixed aiter kernel** (1-ULP divergence, ~6.25e-02): within tolerance -> PASS
- **Fixed aiter kernel** (bit-exact, 0.0): within tolerance -> PASS
- **Real regression** (multi-ULP / wrong result): > 0.13 -> FAIL

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on AMD MI300X (8-GPU host `banff-ccs-aus-p20-14`) inside the same `ci_sglang` docker container CI uses, with the prebuilt (pre-fix) aiter kernel:

```
python3 -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc_per_node=4 \
    test/registered/ops/test_aiter_allreduce_fusion_amd.py --residual-accuracy
```

All 42 shapes (7 token counts x 6 hidden dims, both 1-stage and 2-stage) report `max_diff = 6.25e-02` (exactly 1 ULP) and now `[PASS]`:

```
hidden_dim=7168:
      1x7168 (1-stage): max_diff=6.250000e-02  frac_nonzero=0.2775  [PASS]
      ...
    128x7168 (2-stage): max_diff=6.250000e-02  frac_nonzero=0.2789  [PASS]

ALL PASSED: fused residual output within 1 bf16 ULP of unfused path.
```

Exit code: 0. This is a test-tolerance change only; it does not alter any kernel or model output.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — test-only change, no kernel/runtime modification, so there is no inference performance impact.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [AMD] fix(moe): correct fused shared-expert scaling on aiter/DeepEP path (mori all-to-all)
author: rbrugaro-amd
body:
# fix(moe): correct fused shared-expert scaling on aiter/DeepEP path

## Motivation

On the HIP aiter + DeepEP-class MoE path (e.g. MoRI all-to-all), the fused shared
expert is under-weighted by `routed_scaling_factor`, corrupting every MoE layer
and producing degenerate, non-converging generation on long outputs.

Two code paths scale the MoE output differently:

- **Post-MoE scaling (default):** `DeepseekV2MoE.forward_deepep` multiplies the
  whole MoE output by `routed_scaling_factor` after the experts run.
- **aiter (HIP):** `aiter_biased_grouped_topk` folds `routed_scaling_factor` into
  each routed topk weight, and `forward_deepep` *skips* the post-MoE multiply for
  `_use_aiter` (its `not (... or _use_aiter)` guard).

`_remap_topk_for_deepep` unconditionally set the fused shared-expert weight to
`1/routed_scaling_factor` to compensate for the post-MoE multiply. On the aiter
path that multiply never happens, so the always-on shared expert ended up scaled
by `1/routed_scaling_factor` (≈0.4 at rsf=2.5) instead of 1.0.

**Impact is length-dependent**, which is why this bug is easy to miss (full
numbers + commands under Accuracy Tests below):

- **Short-form (GSM8K)** is *insensitive*: 0.960 → 0.950. A constant 0.4× on the
  always-on shared expert leaves the argmax token robust on short,
  format-anchored prompts — so smoke tests pass and the bug hides.
- **Long-form reasoning** *degenerates*: the tail collapses into a runaway
  repetition loop (`...→Wait→Wait→Wait...`) and never terminates.
- **End-to-end MLPerf (DeepSeek-R1)** quantifies it: exact_match **62.5% → 80.5%**
  (recovering the no-fusion reference of 82.0%), with `tokens_per_sample` dropping
  **6664 → 3713** as the runaway generation stops burning the token cap.

## Modifications

Set the fused shared-expert weight to `1.0` on the aiter path; keep
`1/routed_scaling_factor` for the default post-MoE-scaled path.

```python
routed_scaling_factor = topk_config.routed_scaling_factor
if _use_aiter:
    topk_weights[:, -num_fused_shared_experts:] = 1.0
elif routed_scaling_factor is not None and routed_scaling_factor != 0:
    topk_weights[:, -num_fused_shared_experts:] = 1.0 / routed_scaling_factor
```

**Scope.** This fix is deliberately scoped to the aiter path — the one validated
on AMD MI355X. `forward_deepep` also skips the post-multiply for the non-aiter
families that pre-fold `routed_scaling_factor` in topk
(`should_fuse_routed_scaling_factor_in_topk`: ModelOpt NVFP4, cutlass/trtllm-routed
fp8), so those would likewise need a `1.0` shared weight — but they are
intentionally left at their existing behavior here, to be addressed by their
maintainers on hardware where they can be validated.

New CPU unit tests (`test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_fused_shared_expert_scaling.py`,
3 tests) pin the contract: aiter → `1.0`, post-MoE-scaled (default) → `1/rsf`, and
shared-id home-rank placement. Verified the patch applies cleanly to a pristine
`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.13-rocm720-mi35x-20260613` image and the 3 tests pass there.

## Accuracy Tests

Server (same env/flags for unpatched and patched; only the topk fix differs).
The buggy path is confirmed active at runtime (`router_topk=9`,
`num_local_experts=33` → 1 shared expert fused per rank):

```bash
SGLANG_AITER_MOE=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=1 \
SGLANG_ROCM_FUSED_DECODE_MLA=1 SGLANG_AITER_AR=1 SGLANG_AITER_MLA_PERSIST=1 \
TORCH_NCCL_BLOCKING_WAIT=1 TRITON_ENABLE_PRELOAD_KERNELS=0 TORCH_BLAS_PREFER_HIPBLASLT=1 \
ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MAX_SIZE_BYTES_MB=512 \
PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \
MORI_SHMEM_MODE=ISOLATION MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE=16G \
SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_DTYPE=auto SGLANG_MORI_COMBINE_DTYPE=fp8 \
SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=4096 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /model/deepseek-r1/fp4_quantized \
  --tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --dp-size 8 \
  --moe-a2a-backend mori --deepep-mode normal --moe-dense-tp-size 1 \
  --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head --enforce-shared-experts-fusion \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.84 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --trust-remote-code \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 256 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000
```

### Short-form (GSM8K) — insensitive to this bug

```bash
python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200 --parallel 128 --port 30000
```

Before fix:
```
Accuracy: 0.960
Invalid: 0.000
```

After fix:
```
Accuracy: 0.950
Invalid: 0.000
```

GSM8K does **not** discriminate this bug: a constant 0.4× on the always-on shared
expert leaves the argmax token robust on short, format-anchored prompts (the
0.960/0.950 delta is within run-to-run noise).

### Long-form reasoning — sensitive (this is the real failure)

Identical prompt, `temperature 0.0`, `max_tokens 8000`:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
    "model": "/model/deepseek-r1/fp4_quantized",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content":
      "Solve carefully, showing all reasoning step by step: Find the number of ordered pairs of positive integers (a,b) such that a*b + 2a + 3b = 2025. Then generalize: for which N does a*b+2a+3b=N have exactly 4 solutions? Reason thoroughly before giving the final answer."}],
    "temperature": 0.0, "max_tokens": 8000
  }' | python3 -c 'import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin)["choices"][0]; print("finish:",d["finish_reason"]); print(d["message"]["content"][-900:])'
```

Before fix — the tail collapses into a runaway repetition loop and never
terminates (hits the token cap):
```
... So number of solutions depends on number of divisors of N+6 ...
Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→
Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→Wait→
... (continues to the 8000-token cap)
finish: length
```

After fix — stays coherent for the full generation and reaches a final answer:
```
finish: stop
```

This is the same degenerate / non-convergent failure seen end-to-end in MLPerf.

### End-to-end MLPerf accuracy (DeepSeek-R1, max OSL 20k)

The MLPerf accuracy harness (`exact_match` metric) quantifies the same effect.
Fusion ON unpatched vs patched, plus a no-fusion reference for context:

```
Fusion ON, unpatched (buggy 0.4x):  {'exact_match': 62.5, 'tokens_per_sample': 6664.19, 'num-samples': 200}
Fusion ON, patched (this fix):      {'exact_match': 80.5, 'tokens_per_sample': 3712.98, 'num-samples': 200}
Fusion OFF (no fusion, reference):  {'exact_match': 82.0, 'tokens_per_sample': 3610.34, 'num-samples': 200}
```

The fix lifts fusion-on accuracy **62.5 → 80.5**, recovering essentially the
no-fusion reference (82.0). `tokens_per_sample` drops **6664 → 3713** (back to the
~3610 no-fusion baseline) — direct evidence of the runaway-generation mechanism:
the under-weighted shared expert makes unpatched runs burn ~80% more tokens
hitting the generation cap.

Runtime accuracy validation was manual since the aiter/HIP path isn't covered by
CPU CI. (These subset runs are for relative before/after comparison, not a
compliant MLPerf submission.)

## Benchmarking and Profiling

N/A — this is a correctness fix. The shared-expert weight is a scalar multiply
in topk remap; no throughput impact.

title: [AMD] Fix garbled unquantized Qwen3-30B-A3B output on ROCm/aiter where the aiter CK fused-MoE falls back to Triton with pre-shuffled weights
author: JessicaJiang-123
body: Co-authored-with: @XinyuJiangCMU ## Motivation On ROCm (gfx950, MI350X/MI355X) with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, bf16 `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` emits garbage whenever tensor parallelism shards the MoE intermediate to a size the aiter CK kernel cannot handle (`tp=8 -> 768 / 8 = 96`). `tp=1` (intermediate 768) is fine. ``` SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \ --tp 8 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --port 30000 ``` Root cause: with `--moe-runner-backend auto` the bf16 MoE dispatches to the aiter CK a16w16 `moe_ck_2stages` kernel, which is codegen'd with `GemmSpec=Default` (no K-padding) and `KPerBlock` in {64, 128}, so the per-rank intermediate `K = intermediate_size_per_partition = 768 // tp_size = 96` is not a supported GEMM shape. `IsSupportedArgument` returns false and the kernel throws: ``` AITER CK fused_moe failed (wrong! device_gemm with the specified compilation parameters does not support this GEMM problem), falling back to Triton MoE runner. ``` The forward path catches this and silently falls back to the Triton MoE runner -- but `process_weights_after_loading` has already pre-shuffled the expert weights into the aiter CK layout, so the Triton runner reads mis-laid-out weights and produces garbage tokens. FP8 is unaffected: its weight-size path pads the intermediate to 128. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py`: gate the aiter CK fused-MoE on the actual GEMM shape via `_aiter_ck_moe_supported` (`intermediate_size_per_partition % 128 == 0`). - When the shape is unsupported: - skip the aiter weight pre-shuffle in `process_weights_after_loading` and don't build the aiter runner, so the Triton runner gets correctly-laid-out weights; - `--moe-runner-backend auto` falls back to Triton (warn once); an explicit `--moe-runner-backend aiter` raises a clear error instead of silently producing garbage; - the forward-time try/except fallback is removed — the decision is made once at load time, so Triton can never receive pre-shuffled weights. - Gating on the shape covers any unquantized MoE and any TP/EP sharding. - `test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_qwen3_moe_eval_mi35x.py` (new): GSM8K regression test for `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` (tp=8, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, threshold 0.75), `nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x` suite. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K (200 questions, `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B`, tp=8, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`): | MoE backend | Accuracy | Invalid | |---|---|---| | `auto` (before -- CK GEMM unsupported, silent Triton fallback) | 0.000 | 1.000 | | `auto` -> `triton` (this PR) | 0.855 | 0.000 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. title: [AMD] refactor sparse MLA decode kernel for Deepseek V4 triton backend
author: amd-danli103
body: ## Motivation This PR is exactly the one https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26722, which had already been merged to `amd/deepseek_v4` branch. Co-author: @yichiche, @Raiden-Makoto The Triton sparse MLA decode kernel dispatch logic previously had a fallback path to a 2-phase (separate gather + attention) implementation for decode batch sizes in [33, 255] from kernel-level benchmarking. But for real E2E test, this 2-phase path caused significant performance degradation at high concurrency (8k/1k, TP=8, cc=64/128) due to: - Extra intermediate buffer allocation (gathered_kv) - Additional kernel launch overhead - Inability to fuse gather and attention operations For example, at bs=64, `_unified_sparse_decode_kernel `alone takes ~65% of decode attention time, whereas at bs=4, the fused `_fused_gather_attn_dsv4_dual_scope_kernel `only takes ~29.6%. We should try forcing the fused kernel path even at high concurrency. ## Modifications - Remove 2-phase implementation: Delete 3 files containing the separate gather+attention path since won't be called anymore. (`triton_mla_kernels_decode_common.py`, `triton_mla_kernels_decode_dsv4.py`, `triton_mla_kernels_decode_splitk.py`) - Simplify kernel dispatch: All dual-scope cases now use fused kernels: - Small batches: fused split-K kernel (better GPU utilization) - Large batches / extend / prefill: fused no-splitk kernel - Previously 2-phase [33, 255] range: now uses fused no-splitk - Code cleanup: Inline `_bucket_total_tokens`, extract `_decide_splitk_dual_scope` as shared function, remove dead code ## Accuracy Tests gsm8k accuracy ~0.939/0.942 (2 rounds confirmation) ## Speed Tests and Profiling This opt should benefit those cases where the batch size locates in [33, 255] that will fall back to the 2phase implementation, and now they will be forced to run into the fused kernel. Results shows that we can have 63-64% ITL improvement + 32-38% TTT improvement for 8k/1k TP8, cc=64/128 cases, in the meanwhile we keep other cases' performance consistent as before. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. title: [HiCache] Optimize HiCache hash generation with bulk token byte conversion
author: huangtingwei9988
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

## Summary

This PR optimizes HiCache L3 hash generation by replacing the Python per-token
SHA256 update loop with bulk uint32 byte conversion.

Previously, each page hash was computed by looping over tokens in Python:

```python
for t in token_ids:
    hasher.update(t.to_bytes(4, byteorder="little", signed=False))
```
This is expensive when L3 HiCache needs to compute hashes for many pages.

Optimization summary:

- Moved HiCache page hashing from Python per-token loops to a native C++ extension.
- The C++ path reads `array("q") `token buffers directly, avoiding per-token Python `to_bytes()` calls.
- Page hash input is built in a small reusable per-page scratch buffer instead of materializing a full token byte buffer.
- EAGLE/bigram hashing is generated directly as overlapping token pairs: `[t0, t1, t1, t2, ...]`.
- Hash semantics are unchanged: same SHA256 chaining and same per-page hex outputs.
- Result: about `70x` speedup for normal tokens and `70x `speedup for EAGLE at `page_size=64`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

## normal, page_size=64, repeat=3
| tokens | per-token loop ms | C++ native ms | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16k | 5.869 | 0.079 | 74.72x |
| 64k | 21.943 | 0.308 | 71.31x |
| 128k | 44.127 | 0.617 | 71.54x |
| 256k | 87.868 | 1.233 | 71.26x |
| 512k | 177.974 | 2.475 | 71.90x |
| 1024k | 356.255 | 4.985 | 71.47x |

## eagle, page_size=64, repeat=3
| tokens | per-token loop ms | C++ native ms | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16k | 9.083 | 0.124 | 73.27x |
| 64k | 36.591 | 0.491 | 74.47x |
| 128k | 114.536 | 0.981 | 116.72x |
| 256k | 145.456 | 1.975 | 73.65x |
| 512k | 292.020 | 3.947 | 73.98x |
| 1024k | 623.871 | 7.914 | 78.83x |

title: [NPU] Add NPU fallback for fused Triton gating kernels
author: iridiumine
body:
## Motivation
Closes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/28272.
PR #26924 introduced fused Triton kernels ( fused_sigmoid_mul and fused_gate_sigmoid_mul_add ) to reduce kernel launch overhead. These kernels use num_tokens as the grid size, which exceeds the NPU coreDim limit (65535) at large batch sizes, causing KernelLaunch failures on NPU.

## Modifications
- qwen2_moe.py : Skip use_fused_gate on NPU — the existing _forward_shared_experts(apply_gate=True) path uses native PyTorch and is unaffected.
- qwen3_5.py : Skip fused_sigmoid_mul on NPU — use attn_output.mul_(torch.sigmoid(gate)) instead, which is semantically equivalent and inplace.
CUDA/HIP paths are untouched.

## Accuracy Tests
No impact — both NPU fallbacks use native PyTorch ops ( sigmoid , mul_ , addcmul_ ) that compute the exact same arithmetic as the original code before PR #26924.

## Speed Tests and Profiling
- NPU : No regression. The fallback paths are identical or slightly better (inplace mul_ saves one allocation) compared to the pre-PR behavior.
- CUDA/HIP : No changes — all original Triton paths remain.

title: [Mamba][GDN] Deduplicate spec conv-window intermediate cache via sliding window layout
author: yuan-luo
body: ## Summary Deduplicate the speculative-decoding conv-window intermediate cache (`intermediate_conv_window`) using a sliding-window layout, halving its footprint with no numerical change. ## Motivation During target verify of hybrid linear-attention models (GDN / Mamba2 / KDA "in the future"), each draft-token position snapshots a conv-state window of the last `K-1` inputs (`K = conv kernel width`). The cache is sized `[num_layers, slots, draft_tokens, conv_dim, K-1]`, i.e. `D` separate `(conv_dim, K-1)` windows per (layer, slot). Consecutive draft tokens' windows overlap by `K-2` (a sliding window over the same input stream), so storing them densely wastes roughly half the buffer. This PR applies to any hybrid linear-attention model with a short causal conv under spec decode, GDN today, and KDA automatically once its target-verify path lands. ## Modifications On CUDA, store one shared `[conv_dim, D + K - 2]` buffer per (layer, slot) and expose an overlapping `as_strided` view of logical shape `[num_layers, slots, draft_tokens, conv_dim, K-1]`, where step `t`'s window is the slice `shared[..., :, t:t+K-1]`. The footprint drops from `D*(K-1)` to `D+K-2` columns (exactly 0.5x at `D=4, K=4`). The unchanged conv Triton kernel writes through the view: overlapping columns receive the same input value, so the write is idempotent and race-safe. A new `fused_conv_window_scatter_with_mask` reads each `(dim, win)` element through the view's strides (the dense `fused_mamba_state_scatter_with_mask` assumes a contiguous per-step row) which costs quite a lot. NPU and CPU keep the original dense layout (gated by `dedup_conv_window = not _is_npu and not _is_cpu`); the NPU backend already overrides `update_mamba_state_after_mtp_verify`, so it is untouched. ## Correctness The change is numerically lossless: the deduplicated view holds exactly the same window values. Validated: 1. CPU/numpy layout test: window reconstruction, slice equivalence, and overlap consistency, ratio exactly 0.500 (`test/srt/mamba/test_conv_window_dedup.py`). 2. GPU bit-exact: the new scatter on the `as_strided` view equals the dense scatter, `max_abs_diff = 0.0` across bf16/fp32, `K-1 ∈ {2,3}`, `draft ∈ {3,4,5}`. 3. E2E byte-identical: `Qwen3.5-0.8B` (GDN-hybrid) with `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN --mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer`, fixed prompts at `temperature=0`; branch and main outputs are md5-identical (0 mismatches). This also confirms the conv-kernel write through the view is correct. ## Benchmark `intermediate_conv_window` allocation, dense (main) vs dedup (this PR), all other mamba buffers and `max_mamba_cache_size` unchanged: | Model | TP | slots | dense | dedup | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Qwen3.5-0.8B (18 linear layers) | 1 | 1183 | 0.04 GB | 0.02 GB | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (30 linear layers) | 2 | 745 | 0.09 GB/rank | 0.05 GB/rank | The saving scales with `num_linear_layers x conv_dim x slots`, so larger GDN deployments and higher concurrency free proportionally more. ## Scope / limitations This PR only shrinks the allocation; `max_mamba_cache_size` is unchanged, so throughput is neutral and the freed memory is extra headroom (lower OOM risk). Converting it into more KV/state slots requires refining the spec-intermediate reserve estimate in `model_runner_kv_cache_mixin` (`mamba_cache_per_req * draft_tokens`), left as a follow-up. ## Test plan - E2E: launch a GDN-hybrid model with `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN --mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer`, compare deterministic output against main (must be identical). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #27662782625](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27662782625) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #28150081352](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28150081352)

author: BBuf
body:
## Summary
- Set `Wan2_2_T2V_A14B_Config.dit_config.torch_compile_mode` to `default`.
- This follows the same compile-mode finding as #28050, but applies it to Wan2.2 T2V A14B.
- The change is validated on both H100 and B200 with clean torch compile caches.

## Benchmark
Clean-cache rerun with the diffusion benchmark/profile runner:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python3 python/sglang/multimodal_gen/.claude/skills/sglang-diffusion-benchmark-profile/scripts/bench_diffusion_denoise.py --model wan-t2v --label <label> --output-dir <dir>
```

For each compile mode I used fresh `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR`, `TRITON_CACHE_DIR`, and `CUDA_CACHE_PATH`. The runs stayed on the native SGLang diffusion path; the logs do not contain `Falling back to diffusers backend`, `Using diffusers backend`, or `Loaded diffusers pipeline`.

H100, 4 GPUs, benchmark preset:

| compile mode | denoise | e2e | peak memory |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `max-autotune-no-cudagraphs` | 217.8232s | 220.6501s | 15.23 GB |
| `default` | 206.0693s | 208.8785s | 14.00 GB |

`default` is +5.70% faster on denoise and +5.64% faster end-to-end.

title: [AMD][bugfix] Place TBO cuda-graph num_token_non_padded buffer on model devices
author: karverma-amd
body: ## Motivation `TboCudaGraphRunnerPlugin` preallocates a persistent `_tbo_children_num_token_non_padded` buffer with a bare `torch.zeros((2,), dtype=torch.int32)`, which leaves it on **CPU**. `ForwardBatch.num_token_non_padded` is contractually a tensor on the **model device** (`ForwardBatch.compute` does `.to(device, ...)`), and the eager TBO split path already honors this — `compute_tbo_children_num_token_non_padded_raw` moves its result to `get_global_server_args().device`. Only the cuda-graph plugin's preallocated buffer was left on CPU. During TBO cuda-graph replay, that CPU buffer becomes the child's `num_token_non_padded` and is compared against ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/batch_overlap/two_batch_overlap.py`: allocate `_tbo_children_num_token_non_padded` on `get_global_server_args().device` so the cuda-graph buffer matches the eager split path and the `ForwardBatch` device contract. (`get_global_server_args` is already imported and used in this module.) - `test/registered/unit/batch_overlap/test_tbo_cuda_graph_num_token_device.py`: new CPU-only regression test (registered via `register_cpu_ci`, `suite="base-a-test-cpu"`). It uses a `meta` device to make buffer placement observable without a GPU and asserts that (a) the plugin buffer lands on the model device, (b) the cuda-graph and eager paths agree on device, and (c) the eager split values are correct (`[min(split, n), max(0, n-split)]`). ## Accuracy Tests export PYTHONPATH=/sgl-pr/python:${PYTHONPATH:-} for r in 1 2 3; do python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k \ --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --parallel 32 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 done ## Speed Tests and Profiling export PYTHONPATH=/sgl-pr/python:${PYTHONPATH:-} # MoRI + aiter env export SGLANG_AITER_MOE=1 TORCH_NCCL_BLOCKING_WAIT=1 TRITON_ENABLE_PRELOAD_KERNELS=0 export SGLANG_ROCM_FUSED_DECODE_MLA=1 SGLANG_AITER_AR=1 export ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MAX_SIZE_BYTES_MB=512 export SGLANG_AITER_MLA_PERSIST=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 TORCH_BLAS_PREFER_HIPBLASLT=1 export PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True export MORI_SHMEM_MODE=ISOLATION MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE=16G export SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_DTYPE=fp4 SGLANG_MORI_COMBINE_DTYPE=fp8 export SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=2048 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /models/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 \ --moe-a2a-backend mori --deepep-mode normal --moe-dense-tp-size 1 \ --enable-dp-attention --dp-size 8 --enable-dp-lm-head \ --enable-two-batch-overlap \ --mem-fraction-static 0.55 \ --max-running-requests 256 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --triton-attention-num-kv-splits 2 \ --disable-radix-cache --disable-chunked-prefix-cache \ --cuda-graph-bs 1 2 4 8 16 32 64 128 256 512 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 512 \ --watchdog-timeout 1200 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 ## Checklist - title: feat(cookbook): MTP --max-running-requests callout + skill sync
author: zijiexia
body:
A shared **engine** change (the MTP `--max-running-requests` callout) plus the **skill** doc sync that the migration round deferred. One PR, engine + both cookbook skills.

## Engine — MTP callout (`_deployment.jsx` + `_playground.jsx`)
When a command turns speculative decoding on (`--speculative-algorithm` present) **without** `--max-running-requests`, the Deploy panel and the Playground now render an amber callout — SGLang otherwise resets `--max-running-requests` to **48** for speculative decoding (`arg_groups/speculative_hook.py`).

The trigger is **flag-based, not strategy-based**: a `low-latency` cell that doesn't enable MTP shows nothing; any cell (or a Playground spec toggle) that actually enables MTP without `--max-running-requests` shows it. Both the Deploy cell and the Playground's effective (post-override) command are covered.

Verified in a `mint dev` preview: spec-without-maxreq → callout shows; spec+maxreq and no-spec (incl. a low-latency no-MTP cell) → hidden; toggling spec on in the Playground → shows; DeepSeek-V4 renders correctly (its MTP cells get the hint).

## Skill sync
- **cookbook-migrate-model** — hard rule 2 rewritten to the sharpened benchmark rule: the `sglang_version` anchor must be **reproducible** (a release/commit, or — for Day-0 support before merge/release — a specific PR/commit); a non-reproducible moving ref (`"main"`, `"0.5.8+"`) drops the **whole** result (speed AND accuracy); never inherit cross-model numbers. Hard rule 4 + step 2 + dimension-mapping: the generic **`flagSelects`** axis is merged (#28128), so KV-cache-dtype / mamba / any titled single-select are **config-only (no engine PR)**. Added `NEXTN → EAGLE` to the alias table (alias of the same algorithm), fixed the "ships both" precedent + the Nemotron3-Ultra row, worked example now EAGLE-only.
- **cookbook-add-model** — `authoring-reference` lists `flagSelects` as a built-in axis, requires a reproducible `sglang_version` anchor, and notes the automatic MTP callout.

`cookbook-review-pr` is intentionally untouched (kept general).

title: [Kimi K2.5] Fix eagle3 aux capture for tp>1 when AR fusion is enabled
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation For TP > 1 with all-reduce (AR) fusion enabled, the MLP all-reduce is deferred and fused into the next layer's input RMSNorm. The previous Eagle3 aux capture read `hidden_states + residual` *before* that fused all-reduce ran, so it captured per-rank partial sums instead of the fully reduced activations — silently degrading draft quality. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph NF["Path A — AR fusion OFF (explicit all-reduce)"] direction TB NF1["MoE finalize
(per-rank partial)"] NF2["+ shared expert
(per-rank partial)"] NF3["all-reduce
(full sum)"] NF4["residual stream
(reduced ✓)"] NF5["next layer: input RMSNorm"] NF1 --> NF2 --> NF3 --> NF4 -->|"--- layer boundary ---"| NF5 end subgraph FU["Path B — AR fusion ON (all-reduce deferred)"] direction TB FU1["MoE finalize
(per-rank partial)"] FU2["+ shared expert
(per-rank partial)"] FU3["residual stream
(per-rank partial, AR deferred)"] FU4["next layer:
AR ⊕ RMSNorm fusion kernel
→ emits residual_out (post-AR ✓)"] FU1 --> FU2 --> FU3 -->|"--- layer boundary ---"| FU4 end capA(["capture — before & after fix
(unchanged, already reduced)"]):::ok capBold(["capture BEFORE fix
hidden_states + residual
(pre-AR partial sum)"]):::bad capBnew(["capture AFTER fix
residual_out from fusion kernel
(post-AR)"]):::ok NF4 -.-> capA FU3 -.-> capBold FU4 -.-> capBnew classDef ok fill:#d4edda,stroke:#28a745,color:#155724; classDef bad fill:#f8d7da,stroke:#dc3545,color:#721c24; ``` ## Modifications Route aux capture through `prepare_attn_and_capture_last_layer_outputs` (the same pattern Qwen2/Qwen3 MoE use), which captures the post-all-reduce, pre-norm residual the AR+RMSNorm fusion kernel already produces. AR fusion stays enabled and the redundant capture add is dropped. - `communicator.py`: thread `quant_format` through `prepare_attn_and_capture_last_layer_outputs` into `prepare_attn` (preserves DeepSeek's gfx95 format; other callers default to `""`). - `deepseek_v2.py`: `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer.forward` captures via the helper, and `DeepseekV2Model.forward` passes `aux_hidden_states` only on `layers_to_capture`. Removes the naive `hidden_states + residual` capture (and manual a2a `all_gather`). ## Accuracy Tests Measured acceptance length (mean accepted draft tokens per step) end-to-end across the full benchmark suite from the [draft model card](https://huggingface.co/lightseekorg/kimi-k2.6-eagle3-mla), since this is a correctness fix whose benefit shows up as draft quality. **Setup:** target `nvidia/Kimi-K2.6-NVFP4` + EAGLE3 draft `lightseekorg/kimi-k2.6-eagle3-mla`, TP=8 on 8×B200, FlashInfer AR fusion enabled (the path this PR fixes), `num_steps=3 / topk=1 / num_draft_tokens=4`. Benchmarked via `sglang.bench_serving` (`--dataset-name speed-bench`, which applies the chat template), greedy (temp=0), natural EOS capped at 1024 tokens, concurrency 8, seed 1, radix cache flushed before each benchmark. Identical prompts across both configs. | Category | Benchmark | N | SGLang prior to fix | SGLang post fix | Δ | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Dialogue | MTBench | 80 | 2.44 | **2.50** | +0.06 (+2.5%) | | Chinese | CEval | 212 | 2.46 | **2.48** | +0.02 (+0.8%) | | Math | GSM8K | 500 | 2.97 | **2.98** | +0.01 (+0.3%) | | Code | HumanEval | 164 | 2.94 | **3.03** | +0.09 (+3.1%) | | Math | MATH500 | 500 | 2.97 | **2.99** | +0.02 (+0.7%) | | Math | AIME | 30 | 2.84 | **2.86** | +0.02 (+0.7%) | | Code | LiveCodeBench | 121\* | 2.43 | **2.46** | +0.03 (+1.2%) | | Code | SPEED-Bench (coding) | 80 | 2.88 | **3.00** | +0.12 (+4.2%) | **K2.5** (target `nvidia/Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4` + EAGLE3 draft `lightseekorg/kimi-k2.5-eagle3-mla`, same setup): | Category | Benchmark | N | SGLang prior to fix | SGLang post fix | Δ | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Dialogue | MTBench | 80 | 2.50 | **2.52** | +0.02 (+0.8%) | | Chinese | CEval | 212 | 2.36 | **2.37** | +0.01 (+0.4%) | | Math | GSM8K | 500 | 3.03 | **3.04** | +0.01 (+0.3%) | | Code | HumanEval | 164 | 3.01 | **3.03** | +0.02 (+0.7%) | | Math | MATH500 | 500 | 3.05 | **3.08** | +0.03 (+1.0%) | | Math | AIME | 30 | 2.78 | **2.85** | +0.07 (+2.5%) | | Code | LiveCodeBench | 121\* | 2.44 | **2.45** | +0.01 (+0.4%) | | Code | SPEED-Bench (coding) | 80 | 3.01 | 2.98 | −0.02 (−1.2%) | ## Speed Tests and Profiling With simulated acc len = 2.31, we observe no additional overhead. title: [FlashInfer v0.6.16] Support FlashInfer CuTe DSL NVFP4 MoE quantization
author: zianglih
body:
## Motivation

@humansand

- Add FlashInfer CuTe DSL v2 MoE support to `--quantization nvfp4_online`.
  - Convert eligible BF16, FP16, or FP8 expert weights to NVFP4 at load time.
  - Compute and forward online per-token FP32 activation scales.
  - Support no A2A and FlashInfer A2A; both use CuTe DSL v2.
- Keep the quantization contract established by merged upstream work:
  - `nvfp4_online`: online NVFP4 weight conversion with online per-token FP32 activation scales.
  - `modelopt_fp4`: serialized or online NVFP4 with per-tensor FP32 activation scales, including a default of `1.0` when a scale is absent.
  - `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_NVFP4_PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION=1`: opt serialized `modelopt_fp4` checkpoints into the per-token path; existing TRT-LLM behavior is unchanged and this PR adds CuTe DSL v2 support.
  - DeepEP `low_latency` remains a per-tensor CuTe DSL v1 path and is not exposed as `nvfp4_online`.
- Nemotron coverage keeps target and embedded draft on the same per-token contract:
  - Target: `nvfp4_online` + CuTe DSL v2 + no A2A.
  - Embedded MTP draft: automatically inherits `nvfp4_online` and CuTe DSL v2/no-A2A; no explicit draft quantization is set.
- Related work:
  - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26083
    - Initial online NVFP4 implementation.
  - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31382
    - Added useful embedded-draft reachability, but labeling fixed/per-tensor activation-scale paths as `nvfp4_online` was a contract mistake.
  - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33115
    - Routes online per-tensor behavior through `modelopt_fp4` and provides the shared online-weight loader reused here.
  - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33092
    - Tracks the required FlashInfer 0.6.16.post1 dependency bump; this PR does not duplicate that version-only diff.
- FlashInfer dependencies:
  - Per-token NVFP4 API: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3645
  - Deterministic non-fused finalize: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3976
  - Selected-tactic replay ordering is fixed by https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4192 but not released in 0.6.16.post1, so this PR retains a narrow SGLang workaround.
  - Broader cross-rank tactic synchronization remains tracked by https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23317.

## Modifications

Upstreamed overlap remains visible for review history:

- ~~Preserve a dedicated embedded-draft `nvfp4_online` special case.~~ Merged [#33115](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33115) now provides general explicit/inherited draft quantization routing.
- ~~Carry duplicate online-weight handling and a default `1.0` activation scale from [#31382](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31382) under `nvfp4_online`.~~ [#33115](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33115) owns that per-tensor behavior under `modelopt_fp4`.
- ~~Treat [#31382](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31382)'s DeepEP `low_latency` path as `nvfp4_online`.~~ It remains available through `modelopt_fp4`; this PR does not claim it as per-token support.
- ~~Keep separate draft backend-selection and dummy-dispatch compatibility shims.~~ Upstream supplies the reachability; this PR keeps only the CuTe DSL v2 per-token integration.

Remaining PR-specific changes:

- Admit `flashinfer_cutedsl` for `nvfp4_online` only with no A2A or FlashInfer A2A.
- Quantize activations with `flashinfer.nvfp4_quantize(..., per_token_activation=True, backend="cute-dsl")` and forward the returned per-token FP32 row scale.
- Keep FlashInfer-A2A dispatch in BF16 so the runner can generate that row scale; scalar pre-quantized dispatch cannot represent the per-token contract.
- Keep checkpoint source exclusions from suppressing online conversion, allowing embedded MTP experts to inherit `nvfp4_online`.
- Construct and cache the per-token 4over6 global scale in the CuTe DSL runner; keep ModelOpt backend-neutral.
- Preserve CuTe DSL weight layout, derived scales, frozen parameters, and parameter identity across post-load processing and `/update_weights_from_disk`.
- Add `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MOE_FUSED_FINALIZE`; deterministic inference disables fused atomic finalize.
- Synchronize only fused-finalize selected-tactic replay; normal serving, profiling, and non-fused finalize remain asynchronous.
- Update the FlashInfer fast-prefill private planner call for the `uniform_q_len` ABI.
- Keep the earlier DP-attention, Mamba, and mixed-target experiments explicitly reverted; they add no net diff.
- Add focused planner, CuTe DSL MoE, Nemotron MTP/EAGLE, and reload coverage.

## Accuracy Tests

- Static validation:
  - `git diff --check`: passed.
  - `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed.
- Environment:
  - 8x NVIDIA B200 devbox in `c1/infra` (tests use up to 4 GPUs).
  - Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260806-ae5f8c94`.
  - `flashinfer-python==0.6.16.post1`
  - `flashinfer-cubin==0.6.16.post1`
  - `flashinfer-jit-cache==0.6.16.post1+cu130`
  - `apache-tvm-ffi==0.1.11`
- Current-head results:
  - Fast-prefill planner: `2 passed, 16 warnings in 12.27s`.
  - CuTe DSL MoE suite: `6 passed, 100 warnings, 14 subtests passed in 18.58s`.
  - Cold-autotune Nemotron MTP/EAGLE E2E: `1 passed, 15 warnings in 128.68s`.
    - GSM8K score: `0.965`.
    - Per-request speculative accept length: mean `3.1385`.
    - Aggregate `avg_spec_accept_length=3.1067` against the `2.5` threshold.
    - Live args showed target and draft both on `nvfp4_online`; loading logs confirmed online conversion of `mtp.layers.1.mixer.experts`.

title: [AMD] fix(jit): port kv_canary write/verify/plan kernels to ROCm
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## Summary

Make the **kv_canary JIT kernels** (`write`, `verify`, `plan_entries`) compile and run correctly under hipcc/ROCm, and onboard their JIT unit tests to the `jit-kernel-unit-test-amd` suite. All ROCm-specific behavior is gated behind `USE_ROCM` so the **CUDA/NV path is unchanged**. This unblocks the kv_canary e2e tests on AMD (stacked follow-up).

Builds on the activation ROCm fix from #27947 (already merged to `main`), which is what lets `jit-kernel-unit-test-amd` compile end-to-end.

## Changes

**Kernel port (`python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/kv_canary/*.cuh`):**

1. **Device matching** — replace hardcoded `kDLCUDA` with the platform-agnostic `kDLGPU` alias in all `TensorMatcher` `set_options`/`with_device` calls. The previous `kDLCUDA` constraint raises a runtime `Device mismatch` on ROCm, where torch tensors export as `kDLROCM`. `kDLGPU` is `kDLCUDA` on CUDA and `kDLROCM` on ROCm (defined in `sgl_kernel/utils.cuh`), so this is a **compile-time no-op on NV**. CPU-side params (`kDLCPU`) are unchanged.

2. **Verify-kernel `slot_run_counter` reduction (ROCm-only)** — the hand-rolled `__shfl_down_sync(0xFFFFFFFFu, …)` loop assumes a 32-lane warp and crosses the 32-lane boundary on AMD wave64, miscounting. Gated behind `#ifndef USE_ROCM`/`#else`:
   - **CUDA**: keeps the original `__shfl_down_sync` down-reduction and `threadIdx.x & 31u` leader, byte-for-byte (codegen unchanged).
   - **ROCm**: uses the warp-size-agnostic `device::warp::reduce_sum<kWarpThreads>` (width-32 xor all-reduce), keeping the reduction within 32-lane sub-groups on wave64. The `warp.cuh` include is likewise `#ifdef USE_ROCM`.

3. **Plan-kernel ROCm build fixes (ROCm-only, NV untouched):**
   - Guard the CUDA-only `#include <cuda_runtime.h>` behind `#ifndef USE_ROCM` (hipcc has no such header; the write/verify kernels compile without it).
   - Replace the CUDA-only `__trap()` device builtin with `__builtin_trap()` on ROCm (clang builtin; `__trap()` is undeclared under hipcc). Same contract-break device abort.

**Test onboarding:**

- Register the 10 `test/registered/jit/kv_canary/` unit tests (write/verify/plan `hand`+`fuzz`, `scatter_req_token_ids`, `pipeline_e2e`, `kernel_config`, `const_sync`) for `jit-kernel-unit-test-amd`. These pin the kernel byte-for-byte against the torch reference. CUDA registrations (`base-b-kernel-unit-1-gpu-large`) are unchanged.

## Test plan — verified green on all three GPU lanes (head `ddb0e77b`)

- [x] **NV** `jit-kernel-unit-test` (`base-b-kernel-unit-1-gpu-large`, H100) — no regression on CUDA: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27710196293
- [x] **AMD mi3xx** (gfx942) `jit-kernel-unit-test-amd` — 18/18, all 10 kv_canary files pass: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27710195695
- [x] **AMD rocm720** `jit-kernel-unit-test-amd-rocm720` (stricter HIP asserts) — full canary suite green: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27710200046
- [x] Registrations parse via `ut_parse_one_file` (amd=1/cuda=1 each, suite `jit-kernel-unit-test-amd`)
- [x] NV codegen unchanged: device alias is a no-op on CUDA; the warp-reduction rewrite, `warp.cuh` include, `cuda_runtime.h` include, and `__trap()` are all `USE_ROCM`-gated

> Note: the AMD/NV PR runs show a run-level "failure", but only from **unrelated** jobs (`stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd`, `multimodal-gen-*`, `base-b-test-*`/b200 model suites). None exercise the kv_canary kernels — the `jit-kernel-unit-test*` jobs themselves are green on all three lanes.

## Notes

This is the prerequisite ("port") half of the kv_canary AMD coverage work. Onboarding the kv_canary **e2e** tests (`test_self_e2e_*`) to the 1-/2-gpu-large AMD suites is a stacked follow-up now unblocked by this PR.

title: [core] Gate the overlap WAR barrier on forward reads to recover decode throughput
author: hnyls2002
body:
The overlap WAR barrier added in #26380 makes `schedule_stream` wait on the *whole* previous forward, which (with the existing `forward_stream.wait_stream(schedule_stream)`) fully serializes schedule prep with the forward and regresses low-concurrency streaming decode on Blackwell (see #28218). The forward's only reads of the shared buffers (`req_to_token` / SWA mapping) finish in `replay_prepare`, so gate the barrier on a read-done event recorded there instead — letting the forward's compute/sampling overlap the next iter's prep. Non-(decode-cuda-graph) and spec paths keep the original conservative `wait_stream`. Also makes the `min_new_tokens` penalizer non-synchronizing (torch.where instead of boolean-mask indexing).

title: [LoRA] Fix chunked SGMV (csgmv) CUDA graph segment replay
author: jybsuper
body:
## Motivation

The chunked SGMV LoRA backend (`--lora-backend csgmv`) can produce **incorrect output under CUDA graph** when a decode batch is replayed with a different number of active segments than were present at capture time.

`ChunkedSgmvLoRABackend` sorts tokens by adapter into contiguous segments, so the number of segments depends on how many distinct adapters appear in the batch. The CUDA-graph capture (warmup) typically sees a single dummy adapter (1 segment), but real decode steps can have several distinct adapters resident (multiple segments). The triton shrink/expand/embedding/kv_b kernels sized their launch grid to the **capture-time** segment count (`num_segments` / `bs`). On replay with more segments than were captured, the extra segments' work is silently skipped, and stale tail metadata from a previous (larger) batch can be read — yielding wrong or garbled LoRA output. This only manifests with multiple resident adapters under CUDA graph, so single-adapter and eager runs look fine.

## Modifications

The fix has two parts, applied to the chunked-SGMV triton ops (`chunked_sgmv_shrink`, `chunked_sgmv_expand`, `chunked_embedding_lora_a`, `kv_b_lora_absorbed`) and the backend's batch preparation:

1. **Grid covers the full segment buffer under CUDA graph.** Each kernel's grid is sized to `weight_indices.shape[0]` (the pre-allocated max-segment buffer) instead of the capture-time `num_segments`/`bs`, so every segment a replay might populate is processed.
2. **Stale tail segments are neutralized and cheaply skipped.** `ChunkedSgmvLoRABackend.prepare_lora_batch` now zeroes the unused tail of `weight_indices` and fills the `seg_indptr` tail with the final offset, turning leftover segments into zero-length (`seg_start == seg_end`) entries. The kernels gain an early-exit on zero-length segments, so the extra grid blocks from (1) do no work. Masked `permutation` loads use `other=0` to stay in-bounds.

`chunked_embedding_lora_a` is also marked `@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["num_segments"])` so the kernel isn't re-specialized on the varying segment count.

Files:
- `python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/chunked_backend.py` — tail neutralization in `prepare_lora_batch`.
- `python/sglang/srt/lora/triton_ops/chunked_sgmv_shrink.py`, `chunked_sgmv_expand.py`, `chunked_embedding_lora_a.py` — grid sizing + empty-segment early-exit.
- `python/sglang/srt/lora/triton_ops/kv_b_lora_absorbed.py` (and the `trtllm_lora_temp/` copy) — `_segment_grid_size` uses the full buffer under CUDA graph.
- `test/registered/lora/test_chunked_sgmv_backend.py` — new CUDA-graph replay tests.

## Accuracy Tests

Hardware: Blackwell (GB300, sm103). Model: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8, TP4/EP4, 4 LoRA adapters of mixed rank (16 and 32, some targeting `lm_head`), CUDA graph enabled, MoE-LoRA via the triton MoE runner.

**Unit (the exact bug):**
- New CUDA-graph tests — capture with one segment, replay with more — for shrink, expand, and absorbed-MLA kv_b, plus `prepare_lora_batch` tail neutralization: **4/4 pass**.
- Full `test/registered/lora/test_chunked_sgmv_backend.py`: **16 passed + 39 subtests**, no regressions.

**End-to-end server** (`--lora-backend csgmv --moe-runner-backend triton`, CUDA graph on, multiple resident adapters):
- Each adapter emits its correct (behavioral, per-adapter-prefixed) output.
- 16-way mixed-adapter concurrent decode — which varies the segment count across graph replays, the exact failure mode — **16/16 coherent**.
- Identical greedy requests are deterministic.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This is a correctness fix; its only added cost is the extra early-exiting grid blocks for padded segments, which is negligible. There is no valid "before" throughput to compare against, since without the fix csgmv output is incorrect under CUDA graph.

To confirm no regression, csgmv throughput on the standard MoE-LoRA path (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8, TP4/EP4, 4-adapter uniform mix, isl=osl=2048, `bench_one_batch_server`) stays within ~1% of the triton dense backend across batch sizes:

| Batch | csgmv (tok/s) | triton (tok/s) | Δ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 | 931 | 942 | −1.2% |
| 32 | 1729 | 1741 | −0.7% |
| 64 | 3129 | 3150 | −0.7% |
| 128 | 5491 | 5559 | −1.2% |
