title: [Perf] Avoid per-decode-step host sync in min_new_tokens penalty
author: hnyls2002
body:
`BatchedMinNewTokensPenalizer._apply` used boolean-mask indexing (`logits[mask]`), which is data-dependent and forces a device-to-host sync on every decode step whenever the penalty is active (any request with `min_tokens > 0`). Replace it with a `torch.where` elementwise select: no sync, numerically equivalent, and avoids `-inf * 0 = nan`.

This per-step host sync is part of the reason for the decode throughput regression reported in #28218 — it lands on the per-token critical path for `min_tokens` workloads. This PR addresses that one contributing factor and is not a full fix on its own.

title: [PD] Introduce runtime role switching between prefill and decode
author: inkcherry
body:
## [PD] Introduce runtime prefill<->decode role switching (mori backend)

### Motivation

SGLang's PD disaggregation currently **pins each instance's role (`prefill` / `decode`) at startup** with no way to change it at runtime — to re-balance the P:D ratio you must tear down and relaunch servers. This PR introduces **runtime P<->D role switching**: an operator/router can convert a prefill instance into a decode instance (or vice versa) live, without restarting the server or reloading weights. It lands as a first PoC on the **mori** transfer backend; the control plane is backend-agnostic.

### Design: in-place role flip

Key enabler: **the token KV pool is role-independent** — prefill and decode allocate the same KV memory structure. Only the *role-specific* disaggregation structures differ (prefill: bootstrap queue + KV sender; decode: receiver/poll threads, bootstrap registration, role-specific queues/metadata buffers).

A flip therefore does **not** reallocate the KV pool or touch model weights. It only tears down and rebuilds the small role-specific structures, then re-dispatches the scheduler event loop to the new role. Draining to idle before teardown is a correctness requirement (an in-flight decode request's KV is owned by an upstream prefill).

### API

```
POST /pd_role_switch
{"new_role": "prefill" | "decode", "decode_cuda_graph_bs": [..]?}
```

Gated by `--enable-pd-role-switch` (default **off**, zero impact on existing PD).

### What's in this PR

- **Control plane**: `--enable-pd-role-switch`; `PdRoleSwitchReqInput/Output`; `POST /pd_role_switch`; `handle_pd_role_switch` + teardown/rebuild in a dedicated `disaggregation/role_switch.py`; event-loop re-dispatch on flip. Hardened with an in-progress re-entrancy guard, a fail-fast "unhealthy" state on rebuild failure, and table-driven precondition checks.
- **Decode CUDA graph on flip**: enable and capture the decode graph on the flip to decode; the captured batch sizes are queryable via `/get_server_info` and can be passed as `decode_cuda_graph_bs` for a size-matched capture; idempotent.
- **Backend opt-in interface**: `BaseKVManager.supports_role_switch` + `teardown()`, so other transfer backends can support role switching (checked up-front in the reject path).
- **mori & mooncake backends**: teardown/rebuild hooks for KV-transfer managers (worker threads poll-based so they observe the stop flag; sockets, zmq context, RDMA registrations and the IOEngine / transfer engine released). mooncake: @LLLL114 (Mooncake team).
- **Radix / hicache compatibility**: release the prefix cache on flip; removes the previous `--disable-radix-cache` requirement (works with `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache`).
- **Plumbing / invariants**: `disagg_service.py` (bootstrap started on role-switch instances), `tokenizer_control_mixin.py`, `model_runner_kv_cache_mixin.py` (role-agnostic pre-alloc), `invariant_checker.py` (leak check keyed on the pool, not the role).
- **Unit tests** (CPU-only, mocked): `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_pd_role_switch.py`.

### Validation

**Unit tests** — `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_pd_role_switch.py`: **17 passed** (control-plane contract, all reject branches, same-role no-op, successful-flip orchestration, serialization, teardown thread-leak, radix-on prefix-cache release).

**E2E accuracy (original)** — DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4, 1P1D on 2×MI355X, mori KV transfer, TP8 (pure-TP MoE), concurrency 128, GSM8K (1319, lm_eval flexible/strict):

| stage | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|-------|------------------|--------------|
| baseline (P=node A, D=node B) | 0.9469 | 0.9462 |
| after flip (roles swapped via /pd_role_switch) | 0.9462 | 0.9454 |
| after flip back (reverted) | 0.9416 | 0.9447 |

**Accuracy + performance with radix cache ON (new)** — Qwen3-32B (dense, TP=8, pure-TP), mori, 1P1D on 2×MI300X; 8k1k = random 8192/1024, 320 prompts, concurrency 32, warmup 64:

| state | gsm8k | out tok/s | total tok/s | TTFT med | TPOT med |
|-------|-------|-----------|-------------|----------|----------|
| ① baseline  | 0.840 | 2680 | 24119 | 649 ms | 10.62 ms |
| ② flip      | 0.850 | 2655 | 23895 | 633 ms | 10.77 ms |
| ③ flip-back | 0.840 | 2641 | 23772 | 679 ms | 10.69 ms |


**Leak stress (new)** — 25 round-trip cycles = **100 role switches**, run once with the radix cache OFF and once ON, metrics recorded per cycle. `flip_fails=0`; weight / kvcache / graph / GPU-free / thread-count stay flat across cycles 2–25 in both configs ⇒ no resource leak.

| metric (radix OFF) | baseline | cycles 1–25 |
|--------------------|----------|-------------|
| kvcache / graph (GB) | 115.05 / 1.09 | constant |
| gpu_free (MB) | P=53567 D=53488 | constant |
| threads (lwp) | P=2127 D=2047 | constant |

| metric (radix ON) | baseline | cycles 1–25 |
|-------------------|----------|-------------|
| kvcache / graph (GB) | 115.05 / 1.07 | constant |
| gpu_free (MB) | P=50908 D=50748 | bit-for-bit constant |
| threads (lwp) | P=2519 D=2224 | ±16, non-monotonic |



### Limitations / follow-ups

- Only the **mori** backend's teardown/rebuild hooks are implemented; other backends opt in via `supports_role_switch` + `teardown()`.
- Validated with pure-TP MoE (`--tp-size 8`, no EP / DP-attention / MoE a2a). With `--moe-a2a-backend mori`, the a2a dispatch buffer is sized per-role at startup and is not yet rebuilt on flip — a follow-up.
- Flip is driven externally (operator/router); an automatic load-based flip policy is out of scope here.

### How to use

```bash
# launch both instances with the flag (add --disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache to run with radix on)
python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... --disaggregation-mode prefill --enable-pd-role-switch
python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... --disaggregation-mode decode  --enable-pd-role-switch

# (optional) query a decode server's captured decode-graph batch sizes
curl http://<decode>:8000/get_server_info      # -> internal_states[].decode_cuda_graph_bs

# after draining, flip (optionally pass decode_cuda_graph_bs for a size-matched capture)
curl http://<inst>:8000/pd_role_switch -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"new_role":"decode"}'
```

title: [Bugfix] Fix MTP acceptance regression on plan stream by moving int64 cast before plan stream context
author: iridiumine
body:
## Motivation
Closes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/28405, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/28406.
PR #28043 fixed a DeepSeek-V4 DP dtype mismatch hang by normalizing predict to torch.int64 inside prepare_for_draft_extend . However, when the overlap plan stream is enabled, this cast executes on the plan stream while predict is produced on the main stream, creating a cross-stream data race that silently corrupts draft token ids and drops MTP acceptance to nearly zero.

## Modifications
- eagle_worker_v2.py : Move the predict.to(torch.int64) cast from inside prepare_for_draft_extend to _draft_extend_for_decode , before entering the plan stream context. The cast now runs on the main stream with correct synchronization.
- base_spec_worker.py : Update the comment in prepare_for_draft_extend to explain why dtype normalization must NOT be done inside this function, and that the caller should cast before entering the plan stream.

## Accuracy Tests
No impact on model output — the int64 cast preserves all token id values. The fix only changes where the cast executes (main stream vs. plan stream).

```
export ASCEND_USE_FIA=1
export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1

MODEL_PATH=/home/weights/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
sglang serve \
        --model-path ${MODEL_PATH} \
        --attention-backend ascend \
        --device npu \
        --tp-size 2 --nnodes 1 --node-rank 0 \
        --chunked-prefill-size -1 \
        --trust-remote-code \
        --host 127.0.0.1 --max-running-requests 64 \
        --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
        --port 9903 \
        --mm-attention-backend ascend_attn \
        --dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
        --base-gpu-id 12 \
        --enable-multimodal \
        --disable-radix-cache \
        --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
        --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \
        --cuda-graph-bs 8 12 16 20 24 32 40 48 56 64 \
```

```
┌─────────────────┬───────────┬──────────┬──────────┬───────┬─────────┬─────────┐
│ Model           │ Dataset   │ Metric   │ Subset   │   Num │   Score │ Cat.0   │
├─────────────────┼───────────┼──────────┼──────────┼───────┼─────────┼─────────┤
│ Qwen3.6-35B-A3B │ gsm8k     │ mean_acc │ main     │   200 │    0.96 │ default │
└─────────────────┴───────────┴──────────┴──────────┴───────┴─────────┴─────────┘
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling
No impact on inference speed. The int64 cast is a lightweight element-wise operation on a small token-id tensor, not on hidden states, logits, or KV cache. The cast already existed in PR #28043; this PR only moves its execution point without adding extra overhead.

title: [GLM5][MoE] perf: Write FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE output directly
author: mattteochen
body: ## Motivation SGLang allocates the FlashInfer MoE result in symmetric memory, but older FlashInfer releases did not let the monolithic `trtllm_fp8_block_scale_moe` API write into that buffer. The result therefore required an additional `copy_`, and the first version of this PR used a dual-stream copy/add workaround to hide it. SGLang now pins FlashInfer 0.6.14. That release exposes an `output` tensor for both the [non-routed and routed FP8 block-scale MoE APIs](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.6.14/flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py), so both kernels can write directly into the symmetric output buffer without the scheduling workaround. ## Modifications - Added mutation-only SGLang custom-op wrappers for the routed and non-routed FlashInfer FP8 block-scale MoE `output` paths. Keeping these separate from the allocating wrappers avoids returning a tensor that aliases a mutated custom-op argument. - Passed `symm_output` directly to both FlashInfer kernels and removed the post-kernel `copy_`. - Removed the runtime-context and shared-expert dual-stream copy/add workaround. - Added real FlashInfer regression coverage for both output-buffer paths. ## FlashInfer 0.6.14 Validation Environment: NVIDIA B200, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.6.14. - The non-routed DeepSeekV3 grouped-routing API returned the supplied output storage and matched the allocating path exactly (`max_abs_diff=0`). - `pytest test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_flashinfer_trtllm_moe_output.py -q`: `2 passed`. title: [NPU] Enable piecewise CUDA graph support on NPU
author: hanwlax
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Piecewise CUDA Graph (PCG) was disabled on NPU, so NPU prefill could not use the
torch.compile-driven piecewise capture/replay path. Enabling it also requires the NPU
MoE, fused QKV/RMSNorm/RoPE, elementwise, and FLA layernorm-gated helpers to be visible
to Dynamo as traceable custom ops instead of unsupported Python or external-kernel code.

This PR enables NPU PCG behind the opt-in
`SGLANG_NPU_ENABLE_PIECEWISE_CUDA_GRAPH=1` environment variable and adds the
torch.compile compatibility needed by Qwen3/Qwen3-MoE/Qwen3.5 prefill.

## Modifications

Three commits:

**1. `[NPU] Make MoE helper ops torch.compile friendly.`**
- Register NPU weight-prefetch and CMO/shared-stream synchronization helpers as custom
  ops, separating list and single-tensor cache paths.
- Run the shared expert serially while compiling, avoiding Dynamo tracing of NPU stream
  management.
- Wrap the NPU MoE `l1_norm` helper as a custom op.
- Use a torch implementation of `fused_sigmoid_mul` during NPU compilation.
- Register the NPU fused split-QKV/RMSNorm/RoPE kernel, including its fake implementation,
  as a custom op for Qwen3 and Qwen3-MoE.
- Pass tensors through the registered stream-wait ops in Qwen2-MoE and Qwen3.

**2. `[NPU] Wrap FLA layernorm-gated op for torch.compile.`**
- Register the NPU `layer_norm_fwd` path as a custom op and declare `out` as the
  mutated argument.
- Preserve the existing `(y, mean, rstd)` return contract; the unused NPU mean/rstd
  values remain `None`.

**3. `[PCG] Enable NPU piecewise CUDA graph support.`**
- Add the `SGLANG_NPU_ENABLE_PIECEWISE_CUDA_GRAPH` opt-in and allow PCG on NPU only
  when it is enabled.
- During torch.compile warmup, execute the compiled general-shape graph directly; also
  use that path for pieces without symbolic shape inputs.
- Capture NPU graphs on the PCG capture stream with `auto_dispatch_capture=True`.
- Skip Qwen3.5 expert-distribution-recorder layer contexts only for TC-piecewise
  prefill.
- Add a registered NPU TP=2 PCG serving test for `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`. The test
  runs 128 requests with 4096 input tokens, concurrency 32, chunk size 2048, and
  requires all requests to complete with input throughput above 8500 tok/s.

## Accuracy Tests

The change adds the registered NPU test
`test_npu_piecewise_graph_prefill_tp2.py` for the PCG serving path. It checks request
completion, concurrency, and a minimum input-throughput threshold on
Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (NPU, TP=2, Ascend attention backend).

No model-quality/accuracy benchmark is included in `result_0803.md`; the file contains
serving performance results only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Prefill-heavy serving benchmark on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, NPU, TP=2, Ascend attention
backend.

Setup:
- Backend: sglang
- Requests: 200
- Warmup requests: 20
- Max request concurrency: 32
- Chunked prefill size: 2048
- Output length: 1 token per request
- Traffic request rate: inf

Input Length | Config | Duration (s) | Req throughput (req/s) | Input tok throughput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | P99 TTFT (ms)
-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --
1024 | PCG on | 23.89 | 8.37 | 8574.20 | 3497.49 | 3705.16 | 4148.41
1024 | PCG off (eager) | 25.85 | 7.74 | 7921.86 | 3780.05 | 4018.07 | 4487.11
2048 | PCG on | 45.14 | 4.43 | 9073.23 | 6579.56 | 7183.29 | 7460.18
2048 | PCG off (eager) | 49.01 | 4.08 | 8357.08 | 7141.70 | 7832.46 | 8093.45
4096 | PCG on | 89.86 | 2.23 | 9116.60 | 13216.90 | 14302.62 | 14561.43
4096 | PCG off (eager) | 97.01 | 2.06 | 8444.48 | 14263.16 | 15485.94 | 15799.91
8192 | PCG on | 185.38 | 1.08 | 8838.17 | 27013.84 | 29589.69 | 29880.22
8192 | PCG off (eager) | 197.99 | 1.01 | 8275.33 | 28860.96 | 31585.78 | 32001.35

Input Length | Input Throughput Improvement | Mean TTFT Reduction
-- | -- | --
1024 | +8.2% | -7.5%
2048 | +8.6% | -7.9%
4096 | +8.0% | -7.3%
8192 | +6.8% | -6.4%

Across the four tested input lengths, PCG improves input-token throughput by
6.8–8.6% and reduces mean TTFT by 6.4–7.9%. This workload is prefill-dominated
because each request generates one output token.

title: [XPU] Guard tvm_ffi import in dsv4 compress modules under TYPE_CHECKING
author: arathi-hlab
body:
## Summary

- PR #26471 (DeepSeek-V4 Online Compress support MTP) reintroduced an unconditional `from tvm_ffi.module import Module` in `python/sglang/jit_kernel/dsv4/compress.py` and added the same import in the new `python/sglang/jit_kernel/dsv4/online_c128_mtp.py`.
- The XPU CI image (`intel/sglang-dev:latest`) does not ship `tvm_ffi`, so importing `sglang.jit_kernel.dsv4` (which `__init__.py` does eagerly from `compress`) fails with `ModuleNotFoundError`. That breaks `test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_basic.py`, since the spawned `python -m sglang.bench_one_batch` aborts at import time and `run_bench_one_batch` raises `RuntimeError: Failed to parse benchmark output...`.
- Both files use `from __future__ import annotations` and reference `Module` only in return-type annotations, so the import is purely for typing. This PR moves it back under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`, matching PR #26118 (the original Intel GPU fix) and the pattern used by sibling jit_kernel modules (`nvfp4.py`, `moe_align.py`, `concat_mla.py`, etc.).

## Failure example

`stage-a-test-1-gpu-xpu` of run https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27611089958/job/81635454303:

```
File ".../sglang/jit_kernel/dsv4/compress.py", line 6, in <module>
    from tvm_ffi.module import Module
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tvm_ffi'
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Stage A XPU job (`stage-a-test-1-gpu-xpu`) passes — specifically `test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_basic.py::TestXPUBasic::test_basic_generation`.
- [ ] CUDA stages remain green (no behavior change on CUDA — only the import site moves).

title: [EPD] Optimize multimodal global cache with paged embedding pool
author: cccccya
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
The original multimodal global embedding cache stores all embeddings in one flat CPU pinned buffer and uses a first-fit contiguous allocator for variable-sized embedding blocks. This works when the pool has large contiguous free regions, but multimodal embeddings can have different token lengths, and repeated insert/evict cycles can split the free space into many small holes.

In that case, allocation can fail even when the total free cache memory is still large, because each new embedding requires one contiguous CPU block. Eviction does not fully solve this: evicted entries only merge with adjacent free blocks, and entries protected by in-flight RDMA transfers or active CPU views cannot be evicted. As a result, fragmentation can reduce the effective usable cache capacity and cause cache insert/prefetch skips.

This PR changes the embedding cache to use a paged host pool. Each embedding can be stored across one or more physical page runs, so the cache can reuse fragmented free pages instead of requiring a single contiguous allocation. Together with Mooncake multi-buffer scatter/gather APIs, the paged layout can be transferred without flattening into a temporary contiguous buffer. The goal is to improve cache memory utilization and robustness under fragmentation while keeping transfer and end-to-end performance comparable to the original path.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
- Replace contiguous embedding allocation with a paged host pool.
  - Add `RangePageAllocator` and `PageRun` to allocate embeddings across one or more page ranges.
  - Store cache metadata as page runs instead of a single `(offset, size)` CPU block.
  - Prefer contiguous page runs when available, but fall back to scattered page runs when the pool is fragmented.

- Split the embedding pool by modality.
  - Use a vision pool for image/video embeddings.
  - Use an audio pool for audio embeddings.
  - Maintain independent allocation and eviction state for each pool.

- Add explicit cache entry state and pinning.
  - Track entries as `FILLING` or `READY` so readers never consume partially written embeddings.
  - Pin entries during Mooncake transfer, host/device copy, or pool-view usage.
  - Only allow READY entries with no active pins to be evicted.

- Integrate Mooncake multi-buffer APIs.
  - Add wrappers for `batch_get_into_multi_buffers`.
  - Add wrappers for `batch_put_from_multi_buffers`.
  - Build one pointer/size list per embedding from its physical page runs.

- Update encoder assembly paths for paged embeddings.
  - Use async host-to-device copies for cached embeddings in the Mooncake path.
  - Keep newly computed miss/fallback embeddings usable while async D2H cache storage proceeds.
  - Push newly stored embeddings to Mooncake in the background when possible.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->
This PR does not change model forward computation or model outputs. It only changes multimodal embedding cache storage, transfer, and assembly.

Unit tests added/updated for cache-controller behavior:
```bash
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_embedding_cache_controller.py -v
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->
### Mooncake multi-buffer API benchmark

Environment:
- RDMA: RoCE v2
- Protocol: `rdma + P2PHANDSHAKE`
- Segment size: 32GB
- Memory allocator: `MooncakeHostMemAllocator`

The benchmark compares single-buffer `batch_get` / `batch_put` with multi-buffer `batch_get_into_multi_buffers` / `batch_put_from_multi_buffers`. Each multi-buffer embedding is split into independently allocated non-contiguous buffers to match the paged-pool cache path.

| API | Batch | Emb Size | Page Size | Pages/Emb | Latency (ms) | Throughput (GB/s) |
|-----|-------|----------|-----------|-----------|--------------|-------------------|
| PUT single | 1 | 64MB | - | 1 | 1.699 | 35.9 |
| PUT multi | 1 | 64MB | 128KB | 512 | 1.873 | 32.6 |
| GET single | 1 | 64MB | - | 1 | 1.758 | 34.7 |
| GET multi | 1 | 64MB | 128KB | 512 | 1.913 | 31.9 |
| PUT single | 2 | 64MB | - | 1 | 3.105 | 39.3 |
| PUT multi | 2 | 64MB | 128KB | 512 | 3.352 | 36.4 |
| GET single | 2 | 64MB | - | 1 | 3.250 | 37.6 |
| GET multi | 2 | 64MB | 128KB | 512 | 3.570 | 34.2 |
| PUT single | 1 | 128MB | - | 1 | 3.282 | 37.2 |
| PUT multi | 1 | 128MB | 256KB | 512 | 3.516 | 34.7 |
| GET single | 1 | 128MB | - | 1 | 3.434 | 35.6 |
| GET multi | 1 | 128MB | 256KB | 512 | 3.630 | 33.6 |
| PUT single | 2 | 128MB | - | 1 | 6.080 | 40.1 |
| PUT multi | 2 | 128MB | 256KB | 512 | 6.386 | 38.2 |
| GET single | 2 | 128MB | - | 1 | 6.445 | 37.9 |
| GET multi | 2 | 128MB | 256KB | 512 | 6.824 | 35.8 |
| PUT single | 1 | 256MB | - | 1 | 6.564 | 37.2 |
| PUT multi | 1 | 256MB | 512KB | 512 | 6.786 | 36.0 |
| GET single | 1 | 256MB | - | 1 | 6.785 | 36.0 |
| GET multi | 1 | 256MB | 512KB | 512 | 7.038 | 34.7 |
| PUT single | 2 | 256MB | - | 1 | 12.531 | 38.9 |
| PUT multi | 2 | 256MB | 512KB | 512 | 12.819 | 38.1 |
| GET single | 2 | 256MB | - | 1 | 13.402 | 36.4 |
| GET multi | 2 | 256MB | 512KB | 512 | 13.359 | 36.5 |
| PUT single | 4 | 256MB | - | 1 | 24.646 | 39.6 |
| PUT multi | 4 | 256MB | 1MB | 256 | 25.227 | 38.7 |
| GET single | 4 | 256MB | - | 1 | 26.032 | 37.5 |
| GET multi | 4 | 256MB | 1MB | 256 | 26.390 | 37.0 |

Conclusion: Mooncake multi-buffer scatter/gather throughput is close to the single-buffer API. The overhead is around 8-10% with 512 pages of 128KB buffers, drops below 4% with page sizes >= 512KB, and is close to zero with 1MB pages.

### End-to-end performance benchmark

Environment and setup:
- Model: `Qwen3.5-9B`
- Request size: 4 images of 2560x1440 per request
- Samples: 3 warmup runs + 10 measured runs per scenario
- TTFT: time from `/generate` streaming request start to the first valid chunk
- Embedding cache time: temporary `BENCH_EMBED_MS` markers from encoder logs
- Global cache path: image batching was temporarily disabled to force per-request global cache path for image requests

| Code | Interface | Type | N | Avg Embed (ms) | Avg TTFT (ms) |
|------|-----------|------|---:|---------------:|--------------:|
| new | `encode_with_global_cache_mooncake` | miss | 10 | 1876.8 | 3687.9 |
| new | `encode_with_global_cache_mooncake` | hit | 10 | 382.2 | 1221.6 |
| new | `encode_with_global_cache` | miss | 10 | 1886.9 | 3860.8 |
| new | `encode_with_global_cache` | hit | 10 | 466.4 | 1903.5 |
| old | `encode_with_global_cache_mooncake` | miss | 10 | 1889.2 | 3777.8 |
| old | `encode_with_global_cache_mooncake` | hit | 10 | 379.5 | 1212.8 |
| old | `encode_with_global_cache` | miss | 10 | 1952.2 | 3938.4 |
| old | `encode_with_global_cache` | hit | 10 | 454.7 | 1761.8 |

New vs old, positive means the new code is faster by average latency:

| Interface | Type | Embed | TTFT |
|-----------|------|------:|-----:|
| `encode_with_global_cache_mooncake` | miss | +0.7% | +2.4% |
| `encode_with_global_cache_mooncake` | hit | -0.7% | -0.7% |
| `encode_with_global_cache` | miss | +3.3% | +2.0% |
| `encode_with_global_cache` | hit | -2.6% | -8.0% |

Observations:
- The new code shows a small improvement on miss paths: `encode_with_global_cache_mooncake` TTFT is about 2.4% faster, and `encode_with_global_cache` TTFT is about 2.0% faster.
- Hit paths do not show a stable improvement in this run. Mooncake hit is roughly flat, while non-Mooncake hit regresses by about 8% on average TTFT.
- Encoder logs confirmed that hit scenarios reached the global cache hit path with `Misses (GPU Work): 0`.

title: docs(cookbook): tune GLM-5.2 MTP to 5-1-6 and simplify launch flags
author: JustinTong0323
body:
Follow-up to #28437 (GLM-5.2 deployment cookbook).

### What changed
- **MTP recipe 3-1-4 → 5-1-6** for low-latency. GLM-5.2's MTP head is strong — accept length is near-saturating (~6/6 measured on GB300), so a longer draft (`--speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6`) is a clear win at low concurrency. Updated the low-latency cells, the playground preset, and the config tip; balanced keeps `1-1-2`. Added accept-length tuning guidance so users can adapt the draft length to their own workload.
- **Drop `--trust-remote-code`.** GLM-5.2 (`glm_moe_dsa`) is natively integrated in `transformers` (5.8.1+) and the checkpoints ship no modeling `.py` files, so the flag is unnecessary.
- **Drop the `HF_TOKEN` docker env for GLM-5.2** (public/ungated weights). The shared deployment renderer now emits `--env "HF_TOKEN=..."` only when a config declares an `HF_TOKEN` placeholder, so gated models are unaffected.
- **Document the DSA KV-cache auto-default** (`fp8_e4m3` on Blackwell, routing DSA through the TensorRT-LLM backend; `bf16` on Hopper) — clarifies why no `--kv-cache-dtype` flag is shown.

### Benchmarks
- GB300 low-latency re-measured under 5-1-6 (v0.5.13.post1): conc=1 79 tok/s/gpu (TPOT 2.78 ms), conc=16 341 tok/s/gpu (TPOT 8.53 ms) — +34%/+24% throughput and −28%/−18% TPOT vs 3-1-4.
- H200 / B200 low-latency re-measurement under 5-1-6 is in progress; their cards will be updated in this PR before merge.

Docs-only change under `docs_new/`.

title: [AMD] Fuse shared-expert append + DeepEP remap into one Triton kernel
author: rbrugaro-amd
body: ## Motivation On the AMD aiter / DeepEP-class MoE path, every layer runs the shared-expert append (`fused_append_shared_experts`) immediately followed by the eager DeepEP interleaved remap (`_remap_topk_for_deepep`). The remap is a sequence of small, launch-latency-bound elementwise ops (floor-div, add, arange, fill, copy) that each cost a kernel launch. With one shared-expert append + remap per MoE layer across many layers, this launch overhead is pure dispatch cost on top of work the append kernel is already doing. This PR fuses the append and the remap into the **single Triton kernel** that already iterates over the topk rows, so the remap math runs on the rows already resident in registers instead of as extra eager launches. It also fuses the HIP padded-token masking into one Triton kernel. The change is **numerics-preserving by construction**: the fused kernel produces bit-identical `topk_ids` / `topk_weights` to the eager append+remap pair it replaces (proven by the unit test below). ## Modifications **`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py`** - Add `_fused_append_remap_shared_experts_deepep_kernel` and the `fused_append_remap_shared_experts_deepep` wrapper. In one pass it: - appends the shared experts, - applies the DeepEP interleaved routed-id remap (`e -> e + e // num_local_routed`), - assigns the per-rank shared-expert ids (`shared_id_base + s`), - writes the shared-expert weight as a host-computed scalar. Host code computes the scalar remap params so the kernel stays branch-free. **`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`** - Wire the fused path into `_post_process_topk_ids`: when shared experts are fused **and** the backend is DeepEP-class on aiter, call the new fused kernel instead of `fused_append_shared_experts()` + `_remap_topk_for_deepep()`. The aiter-only / deepep-only branches are preserved unchanged. - The shared-expert weight on this fused branch is `1.0`: on aiter, `aiter_biased_grouped_topk` folds `routed_scaling_factor` into the routed weights and `forward_deepep` skips the post-MoE multiply, so the always-on shared expert must contribute 1.0x. (This matches the aiter behavior of `_remap_topk_for_deepep` addressed in #28237.) - Add `_fill_padded_rows` / `_fill_padded_rows_kernel`: a single Triton launch that zeroes/fills the CUDA/HIP-graph padded rows (`row >= num_token_non_padded`, read from device memory), replacing the eager `arange + (>=) + index_put_` sequence. Used by `_mask_topk_ids_padded_region` and `_zero_topk_weights_padded_region` with an eager fallback for non-2D / non-contiguous tensors. - Remove the redundant first HIP weight-zeroing pass (the final pass already re-zeros after the shared-expert append/remap; zeroing is idempotent). - Add the `SGLANG_MORI_NO_PAD_MASK` env gate (default **off**) to optionally skip the HIP padded-mask pass entirely. This is numerics-affecting and must be validated with an accuracy run before being enabled, hence off by default. **`test/registered/moe/test_fused_append_remap_deepep.py`** (new, registered for both CUDA and AMD CI) - `test_matches_golden_reference` — kernel output vs a pure-torch reference of the documented remap/append math, across shapes and EP ranks. - `test_equivalence_with_eager_append_then_remap` — bit-identical to `fused_append_shared_experts()` + `_remap_topk_for_deepep()`. - `test_shared_weight_is_one_on_aiter_path`. - `test_no_shared_experts_is_noop`. > Note on overlap: the padded-token masking fusion (`_fill_padded_rows`, > `SGLANG_MORI_NO_PAD_MASK`, redundant-pass removal) overlaps with #28084. It is > kept here for now; if #28084 merges first this branch will be rebased to drop > the duplicated portion. ## Accuracy Tests **End-to-end (gsm8k):** standard sglang gsm8k eval against a MoRI-EP DeepSeek-R1 server with this change, including the `SGLANG_MORI_NO_PAD_MASK=1` mask-skip path active (8xMI355X, fp8 MoRI dispatch/combine, mem_fraction_static 0.96): | Test set | Accuracy | Invalid | |---|---|---| | gsm8k full (1319 q) | **0.950** | **0.000** | | gsm8k (200 q) | 0.965 | 0.000 | ```bash # --- 1. Server (MoRI-EP DeepSeek-R1) --- # env (selected; SGLANG_USE_AITER + moe_a2a_backend=mori activate the fused path, # SGLANG_MORI_NO_PAD_MASK=1 enables the mask-skip path under validation) export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_AITER_MOE=1 AITER_FUSE_STAGE1_QUANT=1 \ SGLANG_AITER_AR=1 SGLANG_AITER_MLA_PERSIST=1 SGLANG_ROCM_FUSED_DECODE_MLA=1 \ SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=1 TORCH_BLAS_PREFER_HIPBLASLT=1 TORCH_NCCL_BLOCKING_WAIT=1 \ TRITON_ENABLE_PRELOAD_KERNELS=0 PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \ ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MAX_SIZE_BYTES_MB=512 \ MORI_SHMEM_MODE=ISOLATION MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE=16G \ SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_DTYPE=auto SGLANG_MORI_COMBINE_DTYPE=fp8 \ SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=4096 SGLANG_MORI_NO_PAD_MASK=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /model/Deepseek-R1-MXFP4-MLPerf \ --tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --dp-size 8 \ --moe-a2a-backend mori --deepep-mode normal --moe-dense-tp-size 1 \ --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head --enforce-shared-experts-fusion \ --mem-fraction-static 0.96 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --max-running-requests 22400 --max-prefill-tokens 4500000 \ --schedule-conservativeness 3.35 --num-continuous-decode-steps 192 \ --triton-attention-num-kv-splits 2 \ --disable-radix-cache --disable-chunked-prefix-cache \ --trust-remote-code --watchdog-timeout 6000 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 # --- 2. Eval (standard sglang gsm8k) --- python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 \ --max-new-tokens 4096 --parallel 64 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 # (equivalently: python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k) ``` 95.0% / 0% invalid on the full test set confirms both the fused append+remap and the (default-off) `SGLANG_MORI_NO_PAD_MASK=1` path are accuracy-clean on DeepSeek-R1. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The fused kernel collapses the per-MoE-layer append + eager-remap sequence (~6 launch-bound elementwise kernels: floor-div / add / arange / fill / copy) into the one append kernel that already runs, removing those launches per layer. Before: After **End-to-end `bench_serving` A/B** (8xMI355X, DeepSeek-R1 MoRI-EP, fp8 MoRI dispatch/combine, `SGLANG_MORI_NO_PAD_MASK=1`; `--dataset-name random --num-prompts 1000 --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --request-rate inf --seed 42`). BEFORE = the pre-fix base image (eager `fused_append_shared_experts()` + `_remap_topk_for_deepep()`); AFTER = with the fused kernel. The padded-token mask fusion is present in **both** images, so this isolates the fused append+remap kernel. Mean of 3 runs each: | Metric | BEFORE (eager) | AFTER (fused) | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | Total token throughput | 25,890 tok/s | 26,934 tok/s | **+4.0%** | | Request throughput | 25.3 req/s | 26.3 req/s | +4.0% | | Mean TPOT | 54.9 ms | 53.3 ms | −3.0% | | Mean TTFT | 3,910 ms | 3,716 ms | −5.0% | Per-run total throughput — BEFORE: 25613 / 25877 / 26181 tok/s; AFTER: 26448 / 27175 / 27179 tok/s. The improvement is consistent across every metric and run. title: [GDN][KDA] ReplaySSM buffered output-only decode for Linear Attention
author: yuan-luo
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

To address https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/28511.

The GDN (Gated DeltaNet) decode kernel reads the full recurrent state `S [HV, V, K]` from HBM **and writes it back every decode step**. On the H20‑3e this packed decode is **70–79% memory-bandwidth-bound at batch ≥ 64** — the per-step state read+write traffic dominates.

ReplaySSM (Dao AI Lab, https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/) removes the per-step state write: keep a small per-slot ring buffer of the last `L` steps' `(d, k, g)`, read the output via the history route, and flush the full state only every `L` steps. Per-step state traffic drops from read+write ( ~`8dn` ) to read-only ( ~`4dn` ) → roughly halved.

This PR ports the ReplaySSM decode path into SGLang behind a flag, fully integrated with CUDA graph and the radix prefix cache. It covers **both** linear-attention gate granularities with **one** gate-type-parametrized kernel: **GDN** (per-head scalar gate, radix + CUDA graph) and **KDA** (Kimi Delta Attention, per-K-channel gate).

## Modifications

Adds `--enable-linear-replayssm` (with `--linear-replayssm-cache-len L`, default 16). When enabled, single-token linear-attention decode runs a buffered output-only kernel (`fused_recurrent_linear_replayssm_decode`, `IS_KDA` constexpr) instead of the packed decode — `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode` for GDN or `fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode` for KDA. The GDN math (per-head scalar gate $\alpha$):

$$
\begin{aligned}
\alpha &= \exp(g) && \text{per-head decay} \\
d_{\mathrm{cur}} &= \beta (v - \alpha (Sk)) && \text{GDN corrected delta-rule vector} \\
o &= \alpha (Sq) + d_{\mathrm{cur}} (k^{\top} q) && \text{output-only, } k^{\top} q \text{ factored first} \\
S_{\mathrm{new}} &= \alpha S + d_{\mathrm{cur}} k^{\top} && \text{persisted only on a flush (every } L \text{ steps)}
\end{aligned}
$$

where $S \in \mathbb{R}^{V \times K}$; $Sk$ and $Sq$ are matrix-vector contractions over the key dimension; and $q$ is already L2-normed (optional) and scaled.

The $[V, K]$ state is reconstructed from the checkpoint $S_0$ + ring in K-tiles and read with $q$ / $k$ immediately, so it is never materialized to HBM on a non-flush step. The reconstruction `tl.dot` runs on **tensor cores** (TF32 for fp32, bf16 tensor cores for bf16) — required so the $L$-deep reconstruction stays hidden under the reduced memory traffic.

## Design

This is a memory-traffic optimization for a memory-bound decode kernel, so several decisions trade extra (cheap, tensor-core) compute for less HBM traffic, and several more are about doing that safely under CUDA graph + the radix prefix cache. The non-obvious ones:

### 1. Output-only reconstruction, never materialize the state

On a non-flush step the buffered state before the current token is

$$S = A S_0 + \sum_{j} w_j d_j k_j^{\top}$$

with total decay $A = \prod_i \alpha_i$ and per-position replay decay $w_j = \prod_{i>j} \alpha_i$, both built from the cached per-step gates $g_j$ via a `cumsum` (no per-step state needed). $S$ is reconstructed **in K-tiles** and each tile is immediately contracted with $q$ and $k$ into the scalars $S q$ / $S k$, so the full $[V,K]$ tile never lands in HBM. At $L=1$ the ring is always empty and the kernel reduces *algebraically* to `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode` (used as the bit-exact correctness oracle).

### 2. Tensor cores are mandatory, not optional (the main perf trap)

The reconstruction is $O(L\cdot K\cdot V)$ compute — $L\times$ the baseline's rank-1 update. That only stays hidden under the (halved) memory traffic if the `tl.dot` runs on tensor cores. We hit this directly: forcing an IEEE fp32 dot (e.g. to pass an over-tight unit-test tolerance) drops tensor cores and makes the kernel **~10–20× slower** — turning a 1.5× win into a 15× regression. The fix is to keep the dot on tensor cores (TF32 for fp32 inputs, bf16 tensor cores for bf16) and set **tensor-core-realistic test tolerances** instead. TF32 (~4e-4) / bf16 (~1e-3) reconstruction error is benign end-to-end (GSM8K parity below); GDN's per-step decay $\alpha<1$ attenuates old reconstruction error so it does not accumulate across flushes over a long decode.

### 3. `write_pos` is a per-slot decode-position counter, not derived from `seq_len`

The ring cursor is tracked per **physical mamba slot** (in `MambaPool`), not computed from `seq_len`. Deriving it from `seq_len % L` would be wrong: `seq_len` includes the prefill length, so a slot's first decode step would read a non-empty ring of zeros. Instead:

- **Reset to 0 at slot allocation** — at that moment prefill has written the post-prefill state into `temporal[slot]`, which is exactly the correct checkpoint $S_0$ with an empty ring.
- **Advanced once per forward** (in the attention metadata build), *not* per layer — `write_pos` is the decode position, shared by all GDN layers in a step. Advance rule: `next = 0 if (write_pos == L-1 or force_flush) else write_pos + 1`.

The prefill path is untouched; it writes the full state to `temporal[slot]`, which becomes the decode checkpoint.

### 4. CUDA-graph safety

The decode forward is captured once and replayed, so `write_pos` cannot be a fresh tensor per step. It is a **static per-bs buffer** captured by the graph and refreshed in-place each replay from the persistent per-slot counter, mirroring how `mamba_cache_indices` is handled (`_replay_metadata`, outside the captured region). The per-slot advance also runs there, guarded by `not in_capture` so warmup/capture never mutates the persistent counter. The flush decision is a **device-side branch** (`is_flush = write_pos == L-1`), so a single captured graph handles every step regardless of where in the ring cycle each row is.

### 5. Radix coordination — flush exactly when the cache snapshots

The radix prefix cache snapshots the working `temporal[slot]` at `seq_lens % mamba_track_interval == 0` boundaries for prefix reuse. For ReplaySSM `temporal[slot]` is the checkpoint, which is stale between flushes. So the decode kernel must flush on **exactly** those steps. `force_flush` is computed from the **identical** condition and the **same** post-increment `seq_lens_cpu` the radix cache uses (`schedule_batch.py`), so there is no off-by-one — the ring is folded into `temporal[slot]` on the same step the snapshot reads it. The kernel ORs `force_flush` into `is_flush` while `cache_valid` still uses the true `write_pos` (only committed ring entries are read, even when flushing mid-buffer).

On a prefix **hit**, `MambaPool.copy_from` clones the (now always fully-flushed) snapshot into the request's private slot; we reset that slot's `write_pos` to 0 so the destination ring starts empty.

### 6. `flag-OFF` is byte-identical

When the flag is off no ring tensors are allocated, the metadata fields stay `None`, and the kernel dispatch falls through to the existing packed decode — zero change to the current path.

### 7. One kernel for GDN (scalar gate) and KDA (per-K gate)

GDN and KDA are the **same** delta-rule decode modulo gate granularity: GDN decays the whole state by a per-head **scalar** $\alpha=\exp(g)$; KDA decays it **per key channel**, $S' = S\,\mathrm{Diag}(a) + d\,k^{\top}$ with $a=\exp(g)\in\mathbb{R}^{K}$. A single `IS_KDA` constexpr selects the gate path (mirroring the baseline `fused_recurrent_*_packed_decode` split), and the **GDN path is bit-for-bit the original kernel** (no regression — see Validation).

The non-obvious part is that ReplaySSM *accumulates* the gate into the reconstruction, so per-K gating touches more than the one baseline line:

- ring `g_cache` becomes per-K: `[…, L]` (GDN) → `[…, L, K]` (KDA);
- total / replay decay become per-channel `cumsum` over the buffer ($A[c]=\exp(\sum_j g_j[c])$, $w_j[c]=\exp(\sum_{i>j} g_i[c])$);
- the replay decay folds onto the **cached keys** (per-K) instead of onto $d$ (scalar), and the current-token $\alpha$ folds into $q$/$k$ instead of a scalar post-multiply.

Everything else — the rank-1 reconstruction skeleton, output-only readout, K-tiling, ring / `write_pos` / flush, and the **entire runtime integration** (memory pool ring, CUDA graph, COW) — is gate-agnostic and shared. `MambaPool` sizes `g_cache` from `cache_params.is_kda` (Mamba2 → scalar, KimiLinear → per-K). KDA ships **without radix coordination for now** (`force_flush` left off for KDA; KimiLinear has the radix cache disabled upstream anyway), so the KDA ring flushes only at the natural `write_pos == L-1` wrap.

### Notes investigated

- **finish-donate**: `cache_finished_req` donates the working `temporal` at the request's full (non-`L`-aligned) length. We checked whether this exposes a stale ReplaySSM checkpoint on exact full-prefix reuse; in practice it is TF32-level only and GSM8K parity (below) shows no correctness impact.
- **Roofline**: on H20-3e the packed GDN decode is 70–79% HBM-bandwidth-bound at batch ≥ 64; ReplaySSM cuts state traffic to ~0.53×, for a ~1.7× kernel ceiling at high batch.

## Usage

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <Qwen3.5-GDN-model> \
  --linear-attn-decode-backend triton \
  --enable-linear-replayssm --linear-replayssm-cache-len 16
# works with the radix cache and CUDA graph both ON (defaults)
```

## Implementation

Landed as reviewable slices (one commit each):

| Slice | What |
|---|---|
| kernel | `fused_recurrent_linear_replayssm_decode` Triton kernel (`IS_KDA` constexpr) + wrapper + unit test (GDN + KDA) + microbench |
| 1a | `MambaPool` ring (`d/k/g` + per-slot `write_pos`); GDN backend decode dispatch behind the flag (eager) |
| 1b | CUDA-graph-safe `write_pos` (static per-bs buffer refreshed/advanced outside the captured region) |
| 2a | kernel `force_flush` input (`is_flush |= force_flush`) to allow a flush mid-buffer |
| 2b | radix integration: `force_flush` = the radix track mask (`seq_lens_cpu % mamba_track_interval == 0`, identical to `schedule_batch.py`), so the ring flushes on exactly the steps the radix cache snapshots `temporal[slot]`; `write_pos` reset on COW (`MambaPool.copy_from`) |
| KDA | generalize the kernel to a per-K gate (`IS_KDA` constexpr; GDN path byte-identical); `MambaPool` sizes per-K `g_cache` from `cache_params.is_kda`; KDA backend + `kda_triton` decode dispatch threading; flag generalized `--enable-gdn-replayssm` → `--enable-linear-replayssm` |

`write_pos` is a per-SLOT decode-position counter (reset to 0 at slot alloc and at COW), advanced once per forward; flag-OFF is byte-identical to the current path.

## Validation (H20-3e)

**GDN correctness — Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (GDN-hybrid)**
- Kernel unit test (`test_linear_replayssm_decode.py`): GDN fp32 **bit-exact at `L=1`**, tensor-core-realistic tolerances for `L>1`, forced-flush mid-buffer — all pass.
- **GSM8K (200 q): flag-on 0.880 vs baseline 0.860** — within noise, **no regression**, re-confirmed *after* the GDN+KDA kernel unification. (The earlier GDN-only integration slices validated at **0.900 vs 0.850 with radix + CUDA graph ON**.)
- Greedy decode is **byte-identical to baseline until the first near-tie token**, then differs only via benign TF32 word-flips (both continuations correct) — not corruption.

**KDA correctness — per-K gate**
- Kernel unit test: KDA passes against `fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode` at the same tensor-core tolerances (`L=1` and `L>1`), forced-flush included — confirms the per-K reconstruction math.
- e2e plumbing verified live: server starts with the flag, `MambaPool` allocates per-K `g_cache [.,L,K]` (`g≈k` in size, vs GDN's scalar `g≈k/128` — confirms `is_kda` routing), decode runs end-to-end without crash.

**Performance**
- Kernel microbench: **1.2–1.5× vs packed decode at batch ≥ 16** (L=8); slightly slower at batch 1 (overhead-bound, not an operating point).
- E2E (128 concurrency, 256/512 in/out): ~2.3% TPOT improvement. The end-to-end gain is **model-dependent** — small here because Qwen3.5-35B-A3B is MoE-heavy and the GDN linear layers are a diluted fraction of decode; a GDN-dense model would show more.

## Scope / follow-ups

- **GDN: fully integrated** (radix + CUDA graph, GSM8K parity). **KDA: kernel + decode dispatch wired and kernel-validated**; radix coordination for KDA is a follow-up (`force_flush` currently off for KDA — it flushes only at the natural `L-1` wrap).
- **KV-pool budgeting**: `mamba_cache_per_req` does not yet include the ReplaySSM ring bytes, so the KV pool can be over-sized when the rings are large (KDA / big `L`) → OOM at default `mem_fraction_static`. Workaround: lower `--mem-fraction-static`. Proper fix (count ring bytes in `mamba_cache_per_req`) is a follow-up.
- Requires `--linear-attn-decode-backend triton` and `mamba_scheduler_strategy=no_buffer` (the default). The `extra_buffer`/ping-pong donation path is not yet covered and is guarded out.
- Kernel is ported from vLLM `fused_recurrent_replayssm.py` (ReplaySSM); the `vllm::persistent`-style math is preserved for diff-friendly upstream sync.

## Credit

Algorithm: ReplaySSM, Dao AI Lab (2026).

title: [AMD] Fix DeepSeek-V4 fp8 KV path on gfx942 (e4m3fnuz)
author: Raiden-Makoto
body:
## Motivation
The DeepSeek-V4 `triton` flashmla fp8 path assumed CUDA / gfx950 (CDNA4) `e4m3fn`, but
gfx942 (MI300 / MI325, CDNA3) uses `e4m3fnuz`. The two formats differ in exponent bias,
max value, and bit patterns, so on gfx942 the fp8 KV path collapses GSM8K accuracy
(~0.00) and emits NaNs in the sampler.

These changes arch-gate the fp8 store / decode / quant paths for `fnuz` so the default
`triton` flashmla backend is correct on gfx942. gfx950 behavior is unchanged.

## Modifications

- **fp8 fnuz underflow → NaN** — `jit_kernel/include/sgl_kernel/deepseek_v4/fp8_utils.cuh`
  (`cvt_float_to_fp8_e4m3`): on `e4m3fnuz`, byte `0x80` is NaN (not `-0.0`). An
  underflowing negative returned `0x80`, poisoning the compressed KV cache. Flush
  underflow to `+0` under fnuz.
- **fp8 store / decode dtype match** — arch-gate the flashmla KV store to `float8e4b8`
  (fnuz / gfx942) vs `float8e4nv` (fn / gfx950) to match the decode bitcast; gate the
  decode KV dequant to `e4m3fnuz` on gfx942.
  (`fused_qk_norm_rope_store.py`, `nsa/triton_decode/triton_mla_kernels_decode_fused.py`)
- **arch-aware fp8 max** — `kFP8E4M3Max` (224 fnuz / 448 fn) for fp8 quant scale/clamp
  across the compute path; the compressed-KV and indexer / index-K fp8 stores use the
  arch-aware clip max for the UE8M0 scale divisor, fixing gfx942 under-scaling.
  (`math.cuh`, `fused_norm_rope_v2.cuh`, `store.cuh`, `dsa/fused_store_index_cache.cuh`)

  For reference, the platform-dependent `kFP8E4M3Max` is defined in
  `python/sglang/jit_kernel/include/sgl_kernel/type.cuh`:

  ```cpp
  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  // FP8 max clamp value — platform-dependent
  //   CUDA (e4m3fn):       448.0f
  //   AMD FNUZ (e4m3fnuz): 224.0f
  //   AMD E4M3 (e4m3fn):   448.0f
  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  #ifndef USE_ROCM
  constexpr float kFP8E4M3Max = 448.0f;
  #else  // USE_ROCM
  #if HIP_FP8_TYPE_FNUZ
  constexpr float kFP8E4M3Max = 224.0f;
  #else   // HIP_FP8_TYPE_E4M3
  constexpr float kFP8E4M3Max = 448.0f;
  #endif  // HIP_FP8_TYPE_FNUZ
  #endif  // USE_ROCM
  ```
- **zero-init `q_padded`** — `models/deepseek_v4.py`: uninitialized TP padding heads could
  inject NaN into attention; allocate with `new_zeros`.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K 5-shot, full 1319 questions, tp8, gfx942 (MI325), `triton` flashmla fp8:

| | accuracy | invalid |
|---|---|---|
| before | ~0.00 | — |
| after | 0.911 | 0.000 |

No NaN-in-sampler warnings after the fix.


## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

body:
## Summary

Extends the AMD `extra-a` opt-in CI tier (the ROCm mirror of CUDA `extra-a`)
beyond the existing 1-gpu-small mock-model / kv_canary unit suite, onboarding
the CUDA-`extra-a` model e2e tests **validated green on mi325**.

- `test/run_suite.py`: add `extra-a-test-1-gpu-large-amd` as an AMD per-commit
  suite (tagged per-commit; dispatched only on the `run-ci-extra` opt-in label).
- `.github/workflows/pr-test-amd-extra.yml`: add the matching 1-gpu-large job
  (1-gpu pool), mirroring the 1-gpu-small job's container bring-up, wired into
  the finish aggregator.
- Register `register_amd_ci` on the ROCm-green tests. For `spec_standalone`,
  guard the `fa3`/`flashinfer` subclasses with `@skipIf(is_hip())` (those
  backends aren't built in the ROCm sgl_kernel) so the `triton` subclass runs.

### Onboarded (green on mi325)

| Test | Suite | ROCm runtime |
|---|---|---|
| `quant/test_fp8kv_triton` | `extra-a-test-1-gpu-large-amd` | ~74s |
| `sessions/test_streaming_session_extra` (EAGLE3 streaming) | `extra-a-test-1-gpu-large-amd` | ~558s |
| `spec/test_spec_standalone_extra` (triton subclass; fa3/flashinfer skipped) | `extra-a-test-1-gpu-large-amd` | ~103s |

### Validated but left CUDA-only (ROCm gaps)

Three `continue_on_error` discovery dispatches on mi325 exercised the rest of
the `extra-a` candidates across `lora`/`spec`/`quant`/`sessions`/`chunked_prefill`/`models_e2e`/`cuda_graph`:

| Test | Failure on ROCm |
|---|---|
| `spec/test_spec_ngram_extra` | `sgl_kernel.reconstruct_indices_from_tree_mask` (NGRAM tree-mask op) missing in ROCm build |
| `lora/test_lora_qwen3_8b_logprob_diff` | hardcodes `fa4`/CUTE + flashinfer (`ImportError: flash_attn.cute`) |
| `lora/test_lora_qwen3_5_4b_logprob_diff` | KL(sglang,trainer)=2.25e-2 > 4e-3 (logprob numerics) |
| `lora/test_lora_moe_tp_logprob_diff` | TP=1 vs TP=2 parity failure |
| `spec/test_gemma4_mtp_31b_extra` | gsm8k topk=3 leg 0.72 < 0.75 floor |
| `quant/test_gptqmodel_dynamic` | gsm8k accuracy 0.0 (GPTQ-4bit kernel) |
| `quant/test_w8a8_quantization` | gsm8k accuracy 0.0 (w8a8 int8 kernel) |
| `sessions/test_session_latency` | `Unknown quantization method: mxfp4` (gpt-oss-20b) |
| `chunked_prefill/test_scripted_swa_1gpu` | gpt-oss-20b mxfp4 → ScriptedHttpServer connect timeout |
| `chunked_prefill/test_scripted_core_1gpu` | ScriptedHttpServer connect timeout |
| `models_e2e/test_ministral4_models` | scheduler abort exit -6 (Mistral-Small-4-119B tp2) |
| `cuda_graph/.../test_pcg_with_speculative_decoding_extra` | `Mamba extra_buffer` only on CUDA/MUSA/NPU (FLA backend) |

Excluded up front as NV-only / blocked: FA3-parity kernels, `*_sm120`, hybrid
attn (FA3+FlashInfer), `moe_ep` (deep_gemm), hicache file/mooncake
(`@skipIf(is_hip())`), the `kv_canary`/`mock_model` *e2e* suites (need the
canary JIT kernel ported to ROCm), and `gemma4_mtp_26b` (disabled on CUDA).

Opt-in only: no change to default PR or scheduled AMD CI cadence.

## Test plan

title: [RL] Fix FlashInfer TRTLLM MXFP8 dense weight layout
author: zianglih
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
@humansand

FlashInfer TRTLLM MXFP8 dense GEMM expects FlashInfer-shuffled B weights and 128x4-swizzled scaling factors. The non-multiple-of-128 dense output shape covered here comes from the fused MLA QKV projection, so checkpoint-shaped scaling factors can fail the FlashInfer `M % 128 == 0` scale-layout requirement.

FlashInfer's `shuffle_matrix_sf_a` applies the TRTLLM scale row shuffle and then `block_scale_interleave`, but it does not add row padding. SGLang therefore needs to pad dense MXFP8 scale rows before calling the helper.

This mirrors the existing `flashinfer_cutlass` MXFP8 structure from [sgl-project/sglang#22484](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22484): keep checkpoint-shaped tensors for loading and `/update_weights_from_disk`, and store the backend-ready swizzled/shuffled scale buffer separately because the FlashInfer scale transformation can pad or reshape scales.

## Modifications

- For the FlashInfer TRTLLM MXFP8 dense linear path, shuffle loaded weights with FlashInfer `shuffle_matrix_a`.
- Convert loaded MXFP8 weight scales to the linear uint8 scale matrix, pad only the scale rows to a multiple of 128 with `F.pad` when needed, then call `shuffle_matrix_sf_a(..., num_elts_per_sf=32)`.
- Keep canonical checkpoint-shaped `weight` and `weight_scale_inv` parameters for weight loading and `/update_weights_from_disk`, while storing the FlashInfer-ready scale buffer separately as `weight_scale_inv_shuffled`.
- Switch `TestFlashinferTrtllmRoutedMxfp8MixedBF16` to exercise `--fp8-gemm-backend flashinfer_trtllm`.
- Update the MXFP8 update-from-disk registered test to use `zianglih/JoyAI-LLM-Flash-MXFP8-last-6-BF16`, which is already used by the existing `TestFlashinferTrtllmRoutedMxfp8MixedBF16` registered test on `main`.
- Enable DP attention and `--trust-remote-code` for the MXFP8 update-from-disk test so it matches the checkpoint/runtime requirements.

## Accuracy Tests

Latest validation after the scale-padding cleanup:

- `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 python3 -m pytest -s test/registered/rl/test_update_weights_from_disk_blackwell.py::TestServerUpdateWeightsFromDiskMXFP8::test_parameterized_update_weights_from_disk`

Earlier branch validation:

  - Passed.

The mixed BF16 registered test reported GSM8K output throughput `3544.248 token/s`.

No additional profiling was run for the scale-padding cleanup.

title: [AMD] Fall back to layer_first layout for kernel write-back on ROCm
author: yctseng0211
body: ## Motivation After #21631 changed the default `hicache_mem_layout` from `layer_first` to `page_first`, AMD/ROCm HiCache CI started failing. On non-CUDA platforms the JIT staged write-back kernel is disabled, because it is gated by `can_use_jit = _is_cuda and ...` in `memory_pool_host.py`. With the new `page_first` default, the kernel write-back therefore falls into the non-JIT fallback path: - MHA: `transfer_kv_all_layer_lf_pf` - MLA: `transfer_kv_all_layer_mla_lf_pf` These fallback kernels require the index tensors to live on CUDA: ``` TORCH_CHECK(src_indices.is_cuda(), "Source indices must be a CUDA tensor"); TORCH_CHECK(dst_indices.is_cuda(), "Destination indices must be a CUDA tensor"); ``` but write-back passes `host_indices` (a CPU tensor), so the scheduler crashes: ``` RuntimeError: Destination indices must be a CUDA tensor ``` This manifests in two ways in CI: 1. `test_hicache_variants.py` (DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite, MLA): scheduler hits the exception, server exits with code -9 → `setUpClass` fails. 2. `test_hicache_storage.py` (Llama-3.1-8B, MHA): the server crashes on the first write-back, so the MMLU eval gets only connection errors and scores `0.0` → `AssertionError: 0.0 not greater than or equal to 0.65`. The `page_first` + non-JIT write-back path was effectively never supported (the load direction passes host indices to the same CUDA-only kernels too); it was simply never exercised before, since the old default was `layer_first` and CUDA always takes the JIT path. ## Modification In `ServerArgs._resolve_layout_io_compatibility()`, when `hicache_mem_layout == "page_first"` and `hicache_io_backend == "kernel"` on a non-CUDA platform, fall back to `layer_first` (the layout that AMD CI used before #21631). NVIDIA is unaffected and keeps `page_first` + JIT staged write-back. ## Accuracy Tests ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. title: [Perf] Make latest_output_ids H2D non-blocking in prepare_for_decode
author: hnyls2002
body:
`prepare_for_decode` builds `latest_output_ids` with a blocking `torch.tensor(..., device=...)`, unlike the other per-step H2D copies in this path which all use `non_blocking=True`. Under the overlap scheduler this forces a `cudaStreamSynchronize` every decode step that stalls the CPU behind the in-flight forward — most visible at small batch / low latency.

`forward_stream` already waits on `schedule_stream`, so the async copy stays ordered before the forward consumes it. For penalties that don't read the tensor (e.g. `min_new_tokens`, which only counts) it was pure overhead.

## Benchmark

`openai/gpt-oss-120b`, TP=4 (GB300), overlap scheduler. Workload is `aiperf` 1k-in / 1k-out at concurrency 1 (bs=1 decode), with `min_tokens` set so the penalizer path that builds `latest_output_ids` is active. `fwd occupancy` = median of `sglang:fwd_occupancy` from `/metrics` while the bench runs.

Launch:

```
SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model openai/gpt-oss-120b --tp 4 --enable-metrics \
  --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8
```

Bench:

```
aiperf profile \
  --model openai/gpt-oss-120b --url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \
  --endpoint-type chat --streaming \
  --isl 1024 --osl 1024 --concurrency 1 \
  --extra-inputs min_tokens:1024 --extra-inputs ignore_eos:true \
  --benchmark-duration 85
```

|                          | fwd occupancy | decode throughput | inter-token latency |
| ------------------------ | ------------- | ----------------- | ------------------- |
| before (blocking H2D)    | 71.4%         | 255 tok/s         | 3.91 ms             |
| after (non-blocking H2D) | 86.9%         | 330 tok/s         | 2.96 ms             |

When no penalizer is active the copy is skipped entirely, so that path is unchanged (~90% occupancy either way).

title: [LoRA] Fix chunked SGMV (csgmv) CUDA graph segment replay (#28371)
author: jybsuper
body:
Cherry-pick of #28371 (commit 093908d4c0df80453e89e873f721b9830c857742, already on `main`) onto `sglang-miles`.

## What it fixes
In CUDA-graph mode the chunked-SGMV (csgmv) LoRA kernels baked the grid size (`batch_info.bs`) and the `num_segments` scalar into the captured graph at capture time. On replay, the real batch's segment count differs, so the kernels processed the wrong number of segments — dropping the LoRA delta for some segments, or processing stale tail metadata covering live token rows. csgmv is the default LoRA backend, so any multi-adapter decode batch under CUDA graph was affected.

The fix makes the grid and `num_segments` a capture-invariant value (the statically-sized buffer `weight_indices.shape[0]`) and neutralizes the unused tail every step in `prepare_lora_batch` (`weight_indices[num_segments:].zero_()`, `seg_indptr[num_segments+1:].fill_(total_tokens)`), so padded segments are zero-length and skipped. The same baked-scalar fix is applied to the absorbed-MLA `kv_b` LoRA kernels.

## Cherry-pick notes
- `chunked_backend.py` 3-way merged cleanly; the padding-fix hunks are identical to the original commit. The only difference vs the upstream commit's tree is the unrelated `_add_moe_lora_info` line, which does not exist on `sglang-miles`.
- The original commit also touched `python/sglang/srt/lora/trtllm_lora_temp/triton_ops/kv_b_lora_absorbed.py`, which **does not exist on `sglang-miles`** (modify/delete conflict). That file was excluded from this cherry-pick; the in-tree `kv_b_lora_absorbed.py` fix applied unchanged.

6 files changed, +383/−22.

title: :recycle: [llm][npu][quant] Delegate MXFP8 dense scheme to kernel and use torch.ops.npu
author: TallMessiWu
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #22352 (W8A8 MXFP8 for Qwen3 Dense on Ascend NPU). It addresses two
review comments from @TamirBaydasov that were deferred to keep that already-approved
PR stable:

- https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22352#discussion_r3395802464 — a scheme
  should own only hardware-agnostic weight creation and delegate
  `process_weights_after_loading` / `apply` to a linear-method kernel (`self.kernel`),
  like the other ModelSlim schemes.
- https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22352#discussion_r3395718707 — NPU ops can
  be reached through `torch.ops.npu.*`, so the top-level `import torch_npu` is unnecessary.

## Modifications

- `ModelSlimMXFP8Scheme` now keeps only `create_weights` and delegates
  `process_weights_after_loading` / `apply_weights` to `NPUMXFP8LinearMethod`
  (`self.kernel`), matching `ModelSlimW8A8Int8`.
- `NPUMXFP8LinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading` branches on the weight dtype:
  pre-quantized `float8_e4m3fn` weights (offline ModelSlim) are only re-laid-out, while
  `float16`/`bfloat16` weights (online) are quantized to MXFP8 at load time. Both paths
  converge on `weight_scale_inv`, so `apply` is shared.
- MXFP8 ops now go through `torch.ops.npu.npu_dynamic_mx_quant` /
  `torch.ops.npu.npu_quant_matmul` with standard `torch.float8_*` dtypes, matching the
  int8/int4 methods in the same file. The top-level `import torch_npu` and the
  `current_platform.is_npu()` guard are dropped from both files, keeping them importable
  on non-NPU (CUDA/CPU/AMD/XPU) CI.

No functional change: the online (`--quantization mxfp8`) and offline
(`--quantization modelslim`, `W8A8_MXFP8`) paths keep the same weight/scale layout.

## Accuracy Test / Benchmark

- `pre-commit run --all-files` passes.
- Verified end-to-end on Ascend NPU: Qwen3 dense online (`--quantization mxfp8`) and
  offline (`--quantization modelslim`) both produce coherent output; the weight/scale
  layout is unchanged, so throughput is on par with the pre-refactor baseline.

title: [AMD] Fix deepseek-v4 mtp accept length issue
author: 1am9trash
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

Co-authored-by: @bingxche 
Waiting CI checking by Bingxche help: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27679583497/job/81863337423

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

On DeepSeek-V4 with MTP enabled, the `unified_kv_triton` attention backend reaches an average accept length of only ~2.17, while the `triton` backend reaches ~3.04. Accuracy is unaffected, but the lower accept length significantly hurts decode throughput.

Per-position acceptance rate shows the draft chain collapsing from token 2 onward on `unified_kv_triton`.
| backend                     | token 0 | token 1 | token 2 | token 3 | accept length |
| --------------------------- | ------- | ------- | ------- | ------- | ------------- |
| unified_kv_triton (before)  | 1.00    | 0.894   | 0.223   | 0.054   | 2.17          |
| triton                      | 1.00    | 0.999   | 0.710   | 0.333   | 3.04          |


## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py`
- The SWA ring **write target** (`swa_loc`) is precomputed once per forward. This path never accounted for multi-step draft decode: across draft steps the positions advance, but the cached `swa_loc` does not, so every draft step writes its KV to the *same* ring slot.  Later steps overwrite the KV that earlier draft tokens produced, breaking the draft chain at depth >= 2 and collapsing accept length.
- In `get_unified_swa_loc`, detect multi-step draft decode and recompute the ring slot from the live per-step positions. It only triggers on draft layers, so the overhead is negligible.

`test/registered/amd/test_deepseek_v4_pro_fp4_mtp.py`
- Also add a DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4 + MTP accuracy/accept-length CI test to the nightly MI355 ROCm 7.2 suite.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

Local run new CI task command:
```
SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton python test/registered/amd/test_deepseek_v4_pro_fp4_mtp.py
```

Both accept length and accuracy check passed.

title: [AMD] Enable JIT staged HiCache write-back and fix CPU-index crash
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
On ROCm, `page_first` + `kernel` HiCache write-back crashes on the first prefill with `RuntimeError: Destination indices must be a CUDA tensor`. This PR fixes the underlying cause so ROCm runs the **same** `page_first` + `kernel` JIT staged write-back path as CUDA, instead of the #28473 `layer_first` fallback.

## Root cause

`HiCacheController.start_writing()` keeps `host_indices` on the CPU for the `kernel` io-backend + `page_first` layout, assuming the staged JIT write-back kernel (which stages through device memory and accepts a CPU destination index) will consume them. That JIT path is gated behind `_is_cuda`, so on ROCm it is disabled and the code falls back to the plain `transfer_kv_all_layer_mla_lf_pf` C++ kernel, whose launcher asserts `dst_indices.is_cuda()`. CPU `host_indices` -> assert -> all TP scheduler ranks crash -> prefill dies.

## Why fix the cause instead of the #28473 `layer_first` fallback

#28473 works around the same crash by forcing `hicache_mem_layout = "layer_first"` on ROCm whenever `page_first` + `kernel` is requested. That keeps CI green, but it:

- **disables the JIT staged write-back path on AMD entirely** — ROCm permanently runs the older `layer_first` path and never benefits from the staged kernel that CUDA uses;
- **diverges ROCm from CUDA** at the config layer, so the two platforms exercise different layouts/kernels and have to be maintained separately;
- leaves the actual `page_first` + `kernel` ROCm path broken.

This PR fixes the underlying cause so ROCm keeps the *same* path as CUDA: platform parity, retained staged write-back bandwidth, vectorized non-temporal device transfers, and no second code path to maintain.

**Once this lands, #28473 should be reverted** — its ROCm `layer_first` fallback in `ServerArgs._resolve_layout_io_compatibility()` is no longer needed (and would otherwise keep short-circuiting ROCm away from the now-correct `page_first` + `kernel` JIT path).

## Modifications

- **`hicache.cuh`**: guard the NVIDIA-only PTX `ld/st.global.L1::no_allocate` helpers (`load_nc`/`store_nc`) behind `#ifndef USE_ROCM` and provide ROCm equivalents using non-temporal loads/stores, so the JIT HiCache module also builds with hipcc. The ROCm paths use a single `__builtin_nontemporal_{load,store}` over Clang `ext_vector_type(2/4)` (with `__builtin_bit_cast`) so the vectorized `global_{load,store}_dwordx{2,4}` non-temporal ops are deterministic instead of relying on the LoadStoreVectorizer.
- **`memory_pool_host.py`**: allow `can_use_jit` on HIP, not only CUDA, so ROCm uses the same staged write-back path as CUDA.
- **`cache_controller.py`**: only keep `host_indices` on CPU when the staged JIT kernel is actually available (`can_use_jit`); otherwise move them to the device. This makes the `kernel` io-backend correct on any backend where the JIT kernel is unavailable.
- **`staged_write_back.cuh` / `hicache.cuh` device matchers**: accept `kDLROCM` (device) / `kDLROCMHost` (pinned host) alongside `kDLCUDA`/`kDLCUDAHost`, mirroring the other JIT kernels (`clamp_position`, `kvcache`, `resolve_future_token_ids`).

## Reproduction

> **Note:** main currently contains #28473's ROCm `page_first` + `kernel` -> `layer_first` fallback in `ServerArgs._resolve_layout_io_compatibility()`. Revert it first; otherwise ROCm silently switches to `layer_first` and this path is never exercised.

2P1D ROCm deployment with `page_first` + `kernel` HiCache write-back (`--hicache-io-backend` defaults to `kernel`, the JIT staged write-back path this PR fixes). Core launch commands (TP=8, Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4):

### Prefill

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_AITER_MLA_PERSIST=1 AITER_MXFP4_MOE_SF=1 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/amd/Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4 \
  --served-model-name Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4 \
  --tool-call-parser kimi_k2 --reasoning-parser kimi_k2 \
  --chat-template /models/amd/Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4/chat_template.jinja \
  --tp-size 8 --page-size 64 \
  --context-length 262144 --kv-cache-dtype bf16 \
  --attention-backend aiter \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --max-running-requests 128 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
  --cuda-graph-bs $(seq 1 128) --cuda-graph-max-bs 128 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --disaggregation-mode prefill \
  --disaggregation-transfer-backend mori \
  --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 8998 \
  --disaggregation-ib-device ionic_0,ionic_1,ionic_2,ionic_3,ionic_4,ionic_5,ionic_6,ionic_7 \
  --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-size 192 \
  --hicache-mem-layout page_first --hicache-write-policy write_through \
  --enable-metrics --enable-cache-report \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30020
```

### Decode

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_AITER_MLA_PERSIST=1 AITER_MXFP4_MOE_SF=1 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/amd/Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4 \
  --served-model-name Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4 \
  --tool-call-parser kimi_k2 --reasoning-parser kimi_k2 \
  --chat-template /models/amd/Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4/chat_template.jinja \
  --tp-size 8 --page-size 64 \
  --context-length 262144 --kv-cache-dtype bf16 \
  --attention-backend aiter \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --max-running-requests 128 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --cuda-graph-bs $(seq 1 128) --cuda-graph-max-bs 128 \
  --num-continuous-decode-steps 4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --disaggregation-mode decode \
  --disaggregation-transfer-backend mori \
  --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 19100 \
  --disaggregation-ib-device ionic_0,ionic_1,ionic_2,ionic_3,ionic_4,ionic_5,ionic_6,ionic_7 \
  --enable-metrics --enable-cache-report \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30030
```

### Router (native PD-disaggregation router)

```bash
python3 -m sglang_router.launch_router \
  --pd-disaggregation \
  --prefill http://<PREFILL_IP>:30020 8998 \
  --decode  http://<DECODE_IP>:30030 \
  --prefill-policy cache_aware --decode-policy round_robin \
  --disable-circuit-breaker \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8100
```

Then send multi-turn / prefix-reusing traffic at the router (`:8100`). Before this PR, on ROCm the first prefill HiCache write-back crashes with `RuntimeError: Destination indices must be a CUDA tensor`, and the first prefix-cache hit crashes with `Tensor match failed ... device=rocm:N`. With this PR both paths run cleanly.

## Accuracy / functional tests

- JIT HiCache module compiles and loads with hipcc on gfx942 and gfx950 (ROCm 7.2).
- ISA check on gfx950: the ROCm `load_nc`/`store_nc` emit single `global_load_dwordx2/x4` and `global_store_dwordx2/x4` with the non-temporal (`nt`) flag.
- End-to-end on a 2P1D Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4 disaggregated deployment (TP=8, HiCache `page_first` + `kernel`, `write_through`) running the AgentX v0.3 agentic trace replay at concurrency 64: warmup + 900s profiling complete (328 requests, 0 errors) with no `Destination indices must be a CUDA tensor` and no `Tensor match failed ... device=rocm:N` crashes (both crashed pre-fix on the first write-back / first prefix-cache-hit load).

## Speed tests and profiling

To check that the staged write-back path is worth keeping on ROCm (rather than degrading to `layer_first` per #28473), I ran the equivalent of the #21631 write-back micro-benchmark on **AMD MI355X / gfx950, ROCm 7.2**, comparing the installed `sgl_kernel` LF->PF kernels against the JIT staged LF->PF kernels on the same host-destination write-back workload.

Setup mirrors #21631: `dtype=bf16`, `page_size=64`, `batch_pages=64`, `total_pages=128`, timing via `triton.testing.do_bench(warmup=5, rep=25)`. Each kernel is fed indices in the residency it requires (baseline `*_lf_pf`: device `dst_indices`; staged: pinned-host `dst_indices`); correctness is verified with `torch.testing.assert_close` for every row before timing. MHA bandwidth counts `K + V`; MLA counts a single buffer. `speedup = staged_jit / sgl_kernel_lf_pf`. title: [diffusion] Fix FP8 fused TP scale loading
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

Fix fused per-tensor FP8 scale loading for diffusion tensor-parallel linear layers.

## Root Cause

ModelOpt FP8 checkpoints can store fused linear per-tensor scales as scalar tensors with shape `[1]`. For fused `MergedColumnParallelLinear` / `QKVParallelLinear` parameters, the loader previously routed the scalar through the shard-0 path only. The remaining logical scale slots stayed uninitialized, and later quantization setup used `.max()` over the fused scale buffer, which could pick garbage values and corrupt FP8 TP outputs.

## Changes

- Broadcast scalar `PerTensorScaleParameter` checkpoint tensors into every logical fused scale slot.
- Copy full fused scale vectors directly when checkpoint and parameter shapes already match.
- Add CPU unit coverage for scalar and full-vector scale loading in `MergedColumnParallelLinear` and `QKVParallelLinear`.
- Move FLUX.2 ModelOpt FP8 e2e coverage from 1GPU to a 2GPU TP consistency case: `flux2_modelopt_fp8_tp2_t2i`.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/gpu_cases.py python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/linear.py python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_parallel_linear_weight_loading.py`
- 4x H200 FLUX.2 ModelOpt FP8 smoke generate with TP4/SP1 and TP2/SP2 produced normal images after the fix.
- 4x H200 warmup/no-save repeat after the fix:
  - TP4/SP1: ~114.4 ms/denoise step, peak reserved 20844 MB
  - TP2/SP2: ~110.0 ms/denoise step, peak reserved 39248 MB
- Triggered GT generation for new `flux2_modelopt_fp8_tp2_t2i` consistency case: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27730695244
