title: [Intel XPU] Enable fused_moe_triton tuning on XPU and add tuned DeepSeek-OCR-2 configs
author: rahulvijayaraghavan
body:
## Motivation

Enable `fused_moe_triton` tuning on Intel XPU and ship tuned DeepSeek-OCR-2 MoE
configs for Arc Pro B60.

The `_sep` tuner is CUDA-only: graph capture, events, seeding, and timing go
through `torch.cuda.*` directly, and its ray worker pins every actor to device 0.
This makes it device-agnostic, fixes tuner issues that a full sweep exposes, and
adds the resulting `E=64,N=896` configs under `configs/triton_3_8_0/`.

## Modifications

- Route synchronize / events / seeding / graph capture through `get_device_module`,
  and apply the device id ray assigns each worker. Both follow `tuning_fused_moe_triton.py`.
- Clear the B `TensorDescriptor` cache per config: the tuner allocates fresh weights
  each time, so stale entries pin dead ones and starve graph capture. Inert for
  serving, where weights live for the process lifetime.
- Resolve the `topk_ids` layer layout from the model config instead of DeepSeek-V3's
  hardcoded 61/3, and register `DeepseekOCRForCausalLM` in `common_utils.py`.
- Declare the `ray` extra in `pyproject_xpu.toml`, with `dpctl` that ray's Intel GPU
  detection is gated on; opt-in, not in `all`, so serving installs are unaffected.
- Add tuned `E=64,N=896` configs (full sweep, 18 batch sizes, both projections),
  keyed on shape so they also serve DeepSeek-OCR v1. CUDA serving paths untouched.

## Upstream Triton issues

Both raised from this work against `intel/intel-xpu-backend-for-triton`, both
resolved:

- [#7306](https://github.com/intel/intel-xpu-backend-for-triton/issues/7306) —
  Host-side tensor descriptors drop the 2D-block-I/O fast path on XPU (BMG/CRI).
- [#7691](https://github.com/intel/intel-xpu-backend-for-triton/issues/7691) —
  `TensorDescriptor` shape specialization causes one JIT compile per batch size.

## Kernel results

Time per MoE layer (up + down projection) in microseconds, lower is better.
`E=64, N=896, K=1280, topk=6`, bf16, single Arc Pro B60. Measured with the
tuner's own `--configs` mode, so routing and the serving stack are outside the
timed region.

| M | tuned up config | tuned down config | untuned | tuned, TMA off | tuned, TMA on | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `16 64 64 16 4 4` | `16 32 64 1 4 3` | 259.9 | 148.2 | 131.3 | **1.98x** |
| 32 | `16 64 64 1 4 2` | `16 32 64 64 8 2` | 1496.2 | 1146.9 | 1003.7 | **1.49x** |
| 64 | `16 64 64 16 4 4` | `16 64 64 1 8 2` | 1567.8 | 1090.4 | 1045.5 | **1.50x** |
| 96 | `16 64 64 64 4 2` | `16 64 128 1 8 2` | 1583.7 | 1093.4 | 1058.4 | **1.50x** |
| 128 | `32 128 64 16 8 3` | `32 32 64 64 8 3` | 1590.3 | 1137.1 | 1075.6 | **1.48x** |
| 256 | `32 64 64 16 4 5` | `32 32 64 1 4 3` | 1609.3 | 1307.3 | 1159.6 | **1.39x** |

Config order is `BLOCK_SIZE_M BLOCK_SIZE_N BLOCK_SIZE_K GROUP_SIZE_M num_warps
num_stages`. `untuned` is `get_default_config()` — `64/64/32`,
`GROUP_SIZE_M 8`, no down config and so no TMA. `speedup` compares untuned
against tuned with TMA on.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

Three tuner invocations per batch size, because `--configs` applies one config to
both projections: take `t0`/`t1` from the heuristic run for untuned up/down,
`t0` from the tuned-up run, and `t1`/`t1_tma` from the tuned-down run.

```bash
BENCH=$REPO/benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton
CFG="$REPO/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/configs/triton_3_8_0/E=64,N=896,device_name=Intel(R)_Arc(TM)_Pro_B60_Graphics"
export ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=3
HEUR="64 64 32 8 4 2"
cd "$BENCH"

for M in 1 32 64 96 128 256; do
  UP=$(python -c "import json;c=json.load(open(r'''$CFG.json'''))['$M'];print(*[c[k] for k in ('BLOCK_SIZE_M','BLOCK_SIZE_N','BLOCK_SIZE_K','GROUP_SIZE_M','num_warps','num_stages')])")
  DN=$(python -c "import json;c=json.load(open(r'''${CFG}_down.json'''))['$M'];print(*[c[k] for k in ('BLOCK_SIZE_M','BLOCK_SIZE_N','BLOCK_SIZE_K','GROUP_SIZE_M','num_warps','num_stages')])")
  for CFGS in "$HEUR" "$UP" "$DN"; do
    echo "M=$M configs=$CFGS"
    python tuning_fused_moe_triton_sep.py --model $MODEL --tp-size 1 \
      --topk-ids-dir $TOPK_IDS_DIR --batch-size "$M" --configs $CFGS 2>/dev/null | grep '^t0='
  done
done
```

</details>

## Workload results

Decode batch M = 96, 384 requests per run, median of 2 runs per arm.
`+` = tuned better (sign flipped for latency rows).

### Eager

| Metric | untuned | tuned | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 2080.0 | 2348.2 | **+12.9%** |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 39.06 | 33.74 | **+13.6%** |
| Median ITL (ms) | 30.43 | 26.51 | **+12.9%** |
| Median E2E latency (ms) | 35328 | 31160 | +11.8% |
| P99 E2E latency (ms) | 44609 | 39111 | +12.3% |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 4742 | 5313 | −12.0% |
| P99 TTFT (ms) | 12315 | 11532 | +6.4% |

### XPU graph

| Metric | untuned | tuned | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 2168.3 | 2449.4 | **+13.0%** |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 37.47 | 32.66 | **+12.8%** |
| Median ITL (ms) | 29.90 | 25.34 | **+15.3%** |
| Median E2E latency (ms) | 33501 | 29749 | +11.2% |
| P99 E2E latency (ms) | 40985 | 37326 | +8.9% |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 5132 | 4203 | +18.1% |
| P99 TTFT (ms) | 10606 | 10304 | +2.8% |

Both modes agree on ~+13% output throughput and ~+13% TPOT, and in each mode
every tuned run beats every untuned run on throughput and ITL.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

Server:

```bash
export ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=3
sglang serve --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR-2 --enable-multimodal \
  --dtype bfloat16 --tp-size 1 --trust-remote-code --disable-radix-cache \
  --attention-backend intel_xpu --mem-fraction-static 0.65 \
  --max-running-requests 96 --enable-mixed-chunk --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --moe-runner-backend triton --grammar-backend none --device xpu \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 21000 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled
```

`--moe-runner-backend triton` is required. Without it `moe_runner_backend`
resolves to `auto`, the fused_moe_triton config lookup is never reached, and both
arms measure the same code path (they came out within 2% of each other).

Client:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --base-url http://127.0.0.1:21000 \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR-2 --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR-2 \
  --dataset-name image --num-prompts 384 --max-concurrency 96 \
  --random-input-len 256 --random-output-len 768 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --image-count 1 --image-resolution 512x512 --seed 42
```

`untuned` is the same run with `SGLANG_MOE_CONFIG_DIR` pointed at a directory
whose `configs/` is empty, so every lookup misses and `get_default_config()`
supplies `BLOCK_SIZE_M/N/K = 64/64/32`, `GROUP_SIZE_M = 8`, and no down config.
Each server logs which source it resolved (`Using MoE kernel config from ...` vs
`Using default MoE kernel config`), so the two arms are verifiable.

The graph rows swap in `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable
--cuda-graph-backend-decode full --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 104`. Breakable
prefill on `DeepseekOCRForCausalLM` also needs a nested `layer_model` resolution
fix in `prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py` that is not part of this PR.

</details>

## Accuracy

olmOCR-bench (`benchmark/ocr/bench_sglang.py`), DeepSeek-OCR-2, all 7 splits.
No regression — the tuned and untuned arms land 0.2 points apart over ~7,000
tests, with per-split deltas in both directions, consistent with bf16 reduction
order changing under different `BLOCK_SIZE_M` / `BLOCK_SIZE_K`.

| Split | Tests | tuned | untuned |
|---|---|---|---|
| arxiv_math | 2927 | 99.2% | 99.2% |

| long_tiny_text | 442 | 50.2% | 50.0% |
| **TOTAL** | **6989 / 6965** | **85.6%** | **85.8%** |

The two totals are not over an identical test set: the harness derives tests from
returned output, and `old_scans` yielded 496 vs 472 scorable tests. Under 0.4% of
the total, so read this as "no regression within noise" rather than a precise

title: [AMD] Fix Load and Inference of MLA models with Quark PTPC FP8 attention on ROCm
author: ColinZ22
body:
## Motivation

Loading and running MLA models with quark-quantized MXFP4 weights + per-token-per-channel FP8 attention (like `amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`) on ROCm/gfx95 fails with multiple errors.

The root cause is that the aiter gfx95 `_gfx95_quant_format="fp8"` path fuses RMSNorm + FP8 quantization into a single kernel (`fused_rms_fp8_group_quant`), passing pre-quantized **tuples** instead of plain bf16 tensors downstream. This pattern was already handled for compressed_tensors attention quantization across three prior PRs:

- **#12181** added the `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear` routing in `compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.py` for pre-quantized tuple inputs
- **#21403** added the `isinstance(input, tuple)` branch in `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear` itself
- **#22258** added the 3-tuple `(fp8, scale, bf16)` passthrough from `fused_rms_fp8_group_quant` in `communicator.py`, and the corresponding unwrap in `dsa_indexer._project_and_scale_head_gates`

None of these extended to **quark** attention quantization, and this PR closes that gap.

## Modifications

**`fp8_utils.py`: `channel_quant_to_tensor_quant`**  
Reshape 1D per-channel scale `[N]` -> `[N, 1]` before multiplying against the 2D weight. Quark's `kv_b_proj` has a per-channel FP8 weight with a 1D scale vector that failed to broadcast correctly against the `[N, K]` weight.

**`fp8_utils.py`: `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear`**  
Unpack pre-quantized input tuple as `input[0], input[1]` instead of destructuring, to tolerate both 2-tuples and 3-tuples (the 3-tuple was introduced in #22258 but the unpack assumed exactly 2 elements).

**`quark_w8a8_fp8.py`: `apply_weights`**  
Mirror the handling that #12181 added to `compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.apply_weights`, extended for quark's weight layout and both tuple formats
Note: unlike compressed_tensors which stores `shuffle(w)`, quark stores `shuffle(w).t()`, making the weight layout incompatible with `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear`/`gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle`; So we dequantize to bf16 and use the existing `apply_fp8_linear` path without requiring weight storage changes.

**`dsa_indexer.py`: `_get_q_k_bf16` and `_get_k_bf16`**  
Mirror the unwrap added in #22258 for `_project_and_scale_head_gates`, applied to the two remaining methods that also receive `x` and call `self.wk`. 

## Validation

Accuracy is evaluated using [lm_eval](https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness) on MI355X.

Model: `amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`

| Task  | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K | 93.93% ± 0.66% | 93.71% ± 0.67% |

## Reproduction

### Launch server

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 sglang serve \
    --model-path amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 \
    --trust-remote-code --tp 8 \
    --json-model-override-args '{"qk_rope_head_dim": 64}' \
    --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
    --speculative-num-steps 5 \
    --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
    --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
    --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
    --watchdog-timeout 1200 \
    --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 8}' \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000
```

### Accuracy

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions \
    --model_args model=amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8,base_url=http://localhost:30000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=128,max_retries
  =10,max_gen_toks=2048,timeout=60000 \
    --batch_size auto --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 8
```

## Performance

Benchmarked on MI350X, tp=4, `sglang.bench_serving` random workload (1k input / 1k output, 128 prompts, concurrency 64), averaged across 5 runs.

| Checkpoint | Config | Output tput (tok/s) | Median TPOT (ms) | Median ITL (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 | EAGLE spec-decoding | 2524 | 15.74 | 14.02 |
| **amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8** (this PR enables) | EAGLE spec-decoding | 2721 (**+7.8%**) | 14.83 (**-5.8%**) | 13.47 (**-3.9%**) |
| amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 | No spec-decoding | 1941 | 32.63 | 32.48 |
| **amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8** (this PR enables) | No spec-decoding | 2187 (**+12.7%**) | 28.92 (**-11.4%**) | 28.76 (**-11.5%**) |

title: refactor(runner): move kernel warmup into the shared runner lifecycle (warmup())
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

Kernel warmup / flashinfer autotune belongs to the runner lifecycle and should run at init, not as a standalone `ModelRunner` step or in the forward path.

## Modifications

- `BaseRunner.warmup()` holds the orchestration (run-once guard, device guard, flashinfer allreduce pre-init, flashinfer autotune, PP-DeepGEMM warmup). The cuda-graph runners warm up from `capture()`; the `EagerRunner` warms up in its `__init__` (it has no capture step). The eager runner is built before the cuda-graph runners, so its autotune precedes their capture and warmup is fully init-time — never in the forward path.
- The autotune / dummy-run machinery moves onto `base_runner.py`: `_should_run_flashinfer_autotune`, `_flashinfer_autotune`, `_flashinfer_autotune_cache_path`, `_dummy_run`, `_pre_initialize_flashinfer_allreduce_workspace`, and the module-level `_allocate_decode_buffers`. `pp_parallel_deep_gemm_warmup` takes the runner.
- `init_backends` is restructured to one unified order: per-device attention-backend init → build `EagerRunner` (after the attention backend) → `init_prefill_cuda_graph` → `init_decode_cuda_graph`, with a `cg_supported` flag preserving the out-of-tree / unknown-device guards.
- `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py` recomputes `compile_bs` after `warmup()`, since warmup may disable torch.compile for a model whose `_can_torch_compile` is false.
- The attention test-kit mock runners set `_kernel_warmed_up = True` so the runner-mode unit tests don't re-run warmup.

Behavior-preserving — the moved methods read shared `ModelRunner` state through `self.model_runner`.
## Accuracy Tests

N/A — behavior-preserving refactor (no change to model outputs).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A — no inference-speed impact.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code with pre-commit.
- [x] Behavior-preserving; covered by the existing runner-mode attention unit tests (`test/registered/attention/unittests/dense`).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [diffusion] Optimize realtime causal attention fastpath
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- plumb `num_splits` through the diffusion FlashAttention backend and let realtime causal self-attention use FA3 auto split selection
- skip KV-cache update for direct-current causal attention when the cache window exactly matches the current chunk and has no sink tokens
- add unit coverage for the direct-current cache predicate

## Why

Realtime causal diffusion can hit configurations where the visible attention window is exactly the current chunk. In that case writing K/V into the cache and reading it back is redundant. FA3 also exposes `num_splits=0` heuristic selection, which is useful for realtime causal self-attention without changing global attention defaults.

## Validation

title: [codex] Optimize DMD Wan auto residency on high-memory GPUs
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- Keep default layerwise-offloaded auxiliary components resident for FastWan2.1 T2V 1.3B and TurboWan2.1 T2V 1.3B DMD pipelines when auto mode sees at least 60 GiB of available GPU memory.
- Add a TurboWan 1.3B-specific pipeline config so the untested TurboWan 14B registry entries keep the previous config and auto-offload behavior.
- Extend the deployment hint component type to include `vae`, and add unit coverage for high-memory and mid-memory auto policy behavior.

## Root Cause / Why

The DMD fast paths are not primarily denoise-bound on B200. In the baseline auto policy, both FastWan2.1 and TurboWan2.1 selected default layerwise offload for `text_encoder`, `image_encoder`, and `vae` even with ~178 GiB free on a B200. Full-stage profiling showed the largest copy bucket as `Memcpy HtoD (Pinned -> Device)`, ~399.9 ms / 505 copies for both models. Keeping the auxiliary components resident removes most of the text-encoder offload cost while still staying comfortably under 40 GiB peak VRAM on the tested 1.3B DMD workloads.

The 60 GiB threshold is intentionally conservative: the measured patched-auto peak was ~35-36 GiB, leaving substantial headroom while keeping 40/48 GiB GPUs on the existing memory-saving path.

## B200 Benchmark

Hardware: 1x NVIDIA B200. Code base: `origin/main` at `45d203fb08d1dcd00db69547468285d4268e8940` plus this patch. Command shape: `--backend=sglang`, `832x480`, `61` frames, `seed=42`, warmup enabled, same prompt for all runs.

| FastVideo/FastWan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers | patched auto | 1602.91 | 240.55 | 311.31 | 1048.48 | 35562 | `bb3ebcea25ee70301948f12b6cd33d8ec922eb520470425a2162d59a7a65aba0` |

title: [Spec] Support FlashInfer CUDA graph for EAGLE draft-extend
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary
- Run the EAGLE draft-extend forward as a captured CUDA graph for FlashInfer (add `FlashInferAttnBackend` to the draft-extend graph whitelist), replacing eager per-layer launches.
- ~10% online median E2E latency improvement (request-rate 8, Llama-2-7B EAGLE topk=4); accept length unchanged.

## Changes
- **Graph capture**: add `is_draft_extend_v2()` branches to `_prepare_cuda_graph_metadata` / `init_forward_metadata_out_graph` so the draft-extend forward replays as a causal paged-prefill graph.
- **Fixed qo layout**: `EagleDraftExtendInput.generate_attn_arg_prefill` uses a constant `num_draft_tokens` qo layout (required for graph capture/replay), matching the padded draft-extend input.
- **Drop a per-step D2H**: pass host-known `extend_prefix_lens_cpu` into `FlashInferIndicesUpdaterPrefill.update`, replacing `paged_kernel_lens.sum().item()` with a host-side sum.

## Notes
- FR-Spec (`speculative_token_map`) falls back to eager: the draft-extend graph buffers are sized to the full draft vocab and are incompatible with the reduced (hot) vocab head.

title: [B300] Enable FlashInfer allreduce for Qwen3-VL MoE
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

This PR enables FlashInfer allreduce fusion by default for Qwen3-VL MoE on the existing SM100 auto-enable path used by other supported MoE models:

- add `Qwen3VLMoeForConditionalGeneration` to the FlashInfer allreduce-fusion allowlist
- keep the existing guards unchanged: `flashinfer_allreduce_fusion_backend is None`, TP > 1, no DP attention, and `moe_a2a_backend == "none"`
- no FlashInfer JIT/AOT workaround is included in this PR

Qwen3-VL MoE reuses the Qwen3 MoE decoder/layer-communicator path, and the optimization already works when explicitly enabled with FlashInfer allreduce fusion. This PR makes that optimized path the default under the same safety conditions as the other supported MoE families.

## Environment Note

During B300 validation, the container had a FlashInfer package mismatch:

| Package | Version |

title: [AMD] Fix int32 offset overflow in Triton decode-attention kernels
author: yuankaichen-amd
body:
The decode-attention stage1/stage1-grouped/stage2 kernels index the flat `Mid_O`/`Mid_O_1` scratch buffers using `cur_batch * stride`, where `cur_batch = tl.program_id(0)` is int32. When `max_kv_splits` is large (e.g. ceil(context_len/256) ~ 792 for long-context MLA models) and CUDA graph captures large batch sizes, so `batch * num_head * max_kv_splits * head_dim` can exceed 2**31. The int32 offset then overflows and the kernel reads/writes out of bounds, crashing CUDA graph capture with "Memory access fault by GPU".

Widen the program id to int64 at each kernel entry so offset arithmetic is computed in int64.

title: Re-enable SM90 FlashInfer allreduce fusion with safe backend defaults
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

This follows up on PR #23402. I was working on a Hopper box and noticed FlashInfer allreduce fusion was not getting auto-enabled on SM90 anymore. Looking back at #23402, the last pre-merge change switched the model-specific auto-enable gate from SM90/SM10X to SM10X-only to get around Hopper CI failures that looked tied to the `mnnvl` multicast path.

That fixed the CI failure, but it also turned off the valid SM90 `trtllm` path by default. That is a perf regression for supported Hopper single-node runs. The issue was really the backend picked by `auto` (`mnnvl` on SM90), not SM90 FlashInfer allreduce fusion itself.

This PR makes the default safer while restoring SM90 auto-enable:

- SM90 single-node: `auto -> trtllm`
- SM90 multi-node: hard error
- SM100/SM103 single-node: `auto -> trtllm`
- SM100/SM103 multi-node: `auto -> mnnvl`
- outside SM90/SM10X, for example SM120: hard error
- explicit SM90/SM10X single-node `mnnvl` still works for users who know their fabric is healthy

Previously, `auto` also picked `mnnvl` on SM10X single-node. This changes that to `trtllm` too for the same reason. The CI failure happened on SM90, but there is no need to make fabric/multicast the default risk on single-node Blackwell either. The single-node perf gap between `trtllm` and `mnnvl` is not the main reason to use `mnnvl`. The place where `mnnvl` really matters is SM10X multi-node.

So SM90 gets the stable default path again, `mnnvl` is only auto-selected where it makes sense, and unsupported arch/topology combinations fail early instead of falling through to FlashInfer workspace or kernel failures.

title: [Fix][BCG][Spec] Restore EAGLE prefill plumbing dropped by #23906
author: Oasis-Git
body:
The cuda graph runner refactor (#23906) consolidated BCG and PCG into PrefillCudaGraphRunner but dropped four #25795 hooks needed for BCG+EAGLE end to end:

  * __init__: capture_hidden_mode for BCG+EAGLE — draft worker LAST, target worker FULL.
  * __init__: allocate static_draft_hidden_states buffer for BCG+draft+EAGLE (captured segments hold its address).
  * capture_prepare: pass spec_info=EagleDraftInput(hidden_states=...) aliasing the static buffer instead of spec_info=None.
  * load_batch: copy live forward_batch.spec_info.hidden_states into the static buffer before replay.

Also narrow the existing model_runner.py skip block to non-BCG so the restored target-FULL capture isn't short-circuited to eager_runner. tc_piecewise stays on the skip — it has no pre-#23906 logic to restore here, and its dead-graph capture corrupts FP4 / TRTLLM-MoE decode replay (see #28386).

Alternative to PR #28809, which only attempted the target-worker capture_hidden_mode flip, botched the tc_piecewise branch (codex P1), and dropped the skip block — reproducing the #28386 corruption end to end (gsm8k=0.0 on test_deepseek_v3_fp4_mtp_small in PR Test (Base)).

title: fix(nightly-precision): pin flashinfer allreduce-fusion backend for TP-partial capture contract
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Problem

The nightly precision regression test (`test_nightly_precision_regression`, suite `nightly-precision-8-gpu-h200`) has been failing on `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8` since 2026-06-17:

```
FAILED - tensor=non_intrusive__model.layers.8.inputs.1 rel_diff=0.7537
```

30/33 captured layers fail, all with `rel_diff` in `[0.7497, 0.7839]`. Only layer 0 passes.

## Root cause

Bisected to #23402 (`32685874f3`, "Reenable MNNVL backend for FlashInfer allreduce fusion"). That PR correctly dropped SM90 from the fusion auto-enable list (SM90 mnnvl needs an NVLink multicast fabric H200 nodes do not reliably have), changing the gate on H200 from `enable_flashinfer_allreduce_fusion` (auto True for GLM-family) to `flashinfer_allreduce_fusion_backend is not None` (None on H200).

The nightly serve flags pass no fusion flag, so fusion is now OFF where it used to be ON. This flips the dumper capture contract:

- fusion ON (#23402 before): the previous MLP layer skips `postprocess_layer` and tags the tensor for deferred allreduce, so the dumper pre-hook at the next layer entry captures a TP-partial sum (ranks differ).
- fusion OFF (#23402 after): the previous layer allreduces immediately, so the dumper captures an identical full sum on every rank.

The comparator compares with `--override-dims "...:bs h[tp:partial]"`, whose `tp:partial` is a ReduceSum (`torch.stack(ranks).sum(0)`). Summing 8 identical full-sum tensors yields 8x the baseline (partial-sum) magnitude — abs_mean 0.00556 -> 0.04443, exactly 8x — and `rel_diff = 1 - 16/65 = 0.7538`, matching the observed 0.7537.

Layer 0 passes because `inputs.1` of layer 0 is the embedding output, before any MLP allreduce.

## Fix

- Pin `--flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend=trtllm` in the nightly serve flags so the dumper captures TP-partial sums again (the comparator contract). Explicit `trtllm`, not `auto`, because `auto` resolves to `mnnvl` on SM90 single-node.
- Include the fusion backend in the capture signature so a future change to the fusion default re-establishes the baseline (first run) instead of silently mismatching partial vs full tensors.

This is a test-infra capture-contract fix, not a forward-precision change: the model forward is unchanged, only which tensor (partial vs full) the dumper records. The fused H200 GLM path is what the existing baselines and comparator dims were built for.

## Verification

E2E on an H200 devbox (8xH200, TP8, main worktree, GLM-5.1-FP8):

- Served with the nightly flags + `--flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend=trtllm`. Chat returned 200; dumper captured 1872 tensors (78 layers x 8 ranks x 3 steps).
- Ran the nightly comparator against the 2026-06-16 HF baseline (run-2dd449c, pre-#23402 partial-sum): **33/33 passed, max_rel_diff=0.000000** — bit-exact match. This confirms the fix restores the pre-#23402 capture contract (TP-partial), so the existing baseline is reusable.
- Causal chain confirmed: with the flag, `flashinfer_allreduce_fusion_backend` resolves to `trtllm` and `apply_flashinfer_allreduce_fusion(bs)` returns `True`; without it, the backend is `None` and it returns `False`.
- Historical HF baseline data corroborates the regression: 2026-06-16 (pre-#23402) baseline layer 8 abs_mean=0.00556 (partial); 2026-06-17/22 target abs_mean=0.04443 = 8x, rel_diff=0.7537.
- `pre-commit` (black/isort/ruff/clang-format) passes; `py_compile` passes.

## Related

- #28190 fixes `_select_latest_run` to not promote failed runs to the comparison baseline. That bug caused 2026-06-20/21 to pass falsely (the 06-19 failed full-sum run became the baseline). It is independent of this fix but should land together so failed runs can no longer mask this class of regression.

title: [diffusion] Add Qwen-Image ModelOpt NVFP4 support
author: BBuf
body: ## Summary The NVFP4 checkpoints used for this PR were produced locally on the B200 validation node from NVIDIA ModelOpt PR #1706, branch `qwen-image-svdquant-nvfp4-pr` (`31db2397`). I used ModelOpt's diffusers quantization entrypoint (`examples/diffusers/quantization/quantize.py`) with the `qwen-image` recipe, BF16 model loading, `--format fp4`, and the default `max` quantization algorithm. The calibration set was `/data/bbuf/qwen_image_nvfp4/prompts/qwen_calib_8.txt`, which produced 8 calibration batches in the export logs. The four hosted checkpoints uploaded for this PR are full Hugging Face-style pipeline directories under `lmsys/*`: - `lmsys/qwen-image-modelopt-nvfp4-sglang` from `Qwen/Qwen-Image` - `lmsys/qwen-image-2512-modelopt-nvfp4-sglang` from `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2512` - `lmsys/qwen-image-edit-modelopt-nvfp4-sglang` from `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit` - `lmsys/qwen-image-edit-2511-modelopt-nvfp4-sglang` from `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511` The local B200 export directories were kept under `/data/bbuf/qwen_image_nvfp4/ckpts/` before upload. `Qwen-Image-Edit-2509` was validated locally but is not part of the hosted checkpoint set for this PR. ModelOpt PR #1706 exposes Qwen Image through the `qwen-image` model type, so the edit variants were exported through the same recipe with the base model path overridden to the edit repos. The Qwen recipe quantized only `transformer_blocks`, excluded the first two and last two transformer blocks, used NVFP4 block size 16, disabled attention quantizers through the Qwen filter, fused QKV amax groups during export, and saved the resulting packed NVFP4 transformer plus the unquantized pipeline components into the local HF directories above. This PR adds Qwen-Image ModelOpt NVFP4 loading support for SGLang Diffusion, based on the draft support in #28557 and validated with public `lmsys/*` checkpoints exported from NVIDIA ModelOpt PR #1706. Changes: - Register the Qwen-Image NVFP4 full-model repo layout for native diffusion loading. - Canonicalize Qwen modulation tensor names such as `img_mod.1` / `txt_mod.1` when reconstructing ModelOpt NVFP4 exclude modules. - Add one B200 diffusion 50-step consistency case for `lmsys/qwen-image-2512-modelopt-nvfp4-sglang`, backed by a new `ci-data` GT image. - Document the hosted `lmsys/*` checkpoint workflow and B200 performance caveat in `docs` and `docs_new`, including Qwen-Image-2512 and Qwen-Image-Edit variant validation. The hosted `lmsys/*` checkpoints are now public and readable from CI. This PR enables one representative B200 NVFP4 50-step consistency test for `lmsys/qwen-image-2512-modelopt-nvfp4-sglang`; the other hosted Qwen Image NVFP4 repos are documented but not added to the B200 shard to keep runtime bounded. ## B200 validation Environment: - 8x NVIDIA B200 node, SGLang native diffusion backend. - Base models: `Qwen/Qwen-Image`, `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2512`, `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit`, `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2509`, and `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511`. - Quantized checkpoints: public `lmsys/*` ModelOpt PR #1706 exports using `--format fp4 --quant-algo max`; Edit variants were exported through a local wrapper because PR #1706 currently exposes only the `qwen-image` model type. - No diffusers fallback markers in representative NVFP4 logs. - Transformer memory reduced from roughly 38.05 GB BF16 to 13.69 GB NVFP4 at load. ### Image quality spot-check (BF16 vs NVFP4, model-config steps) The following samples were generated on B200 with the same prompt, seed, resolution, and each model config's default sampling steps. The commands did not pass `--num-inference-steps`. - `Qwen-Image`: BF16 `Qwen/Qwen-Image` vs `lmsys/qwen-image-modelopt-nvfp4-sglang`, `infer_steps=50` - `Qwen-Image-2512`: BF16 `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2512` vs `lmsys/qwen-image-2512-modelopt-nvfp4-sglang`, `infer_steps=50` - `Qwen-Image-Edit`: BF16 `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit` vs `lmsys/qwen-image-edit-modelopt-nvfp4-sglang`, `infer_steps=50` - `Qwen-Image-Edit-2511`: BF16 `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511` vs `lmsys/qwen-image-edit-2511-modelopt-nvfp4-sglang`, `infer_steps=40` ![qwen_image_bf16_vs_nvfp4_config_steps_contact_sheet.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e64b753-c2c5-4220-b856-f39f7304b921) ### B200 benchmark rerun with the diffusion benchmark/profile skill command (updated 2026-06-24) The Qwen-Image 1024x1024 rows below were rerun on B200 with the command shape used by `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/.claude/skills/sglang-diffusion-benchmark-profile`: native SGLang backend, seed 42, 1024x1024, `--save-output`, `--warmup`, and `--enable-torch-compile`. The commands do not pass `--num-inference-steps`, so Qwen-Image uses its model-config default `infer_steps=50`. Warmup is excluded by the perf dump, but the measured request can still include remaining torch.compile specialization in the first denoise steps; `Avg step (all 50)` is the end-to-end denoise average for the standardized command, while `Tail avg` excludes the first two compile-heavy denoise steps. The default NVFP4 FP4 GEMM path in this run is FlashInfer TRT-LLM (`trtllm_fp4_gemm_runner`). Commands: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH=python FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \ sglang generate \ --backend=sglang \ --model-path=Qwen/Qwen-Image \ --prompt="A futuristic cyberpunk city at night, neon lights reflecting on wet streets" \ --seed=42 \ --width=1024 \ --height=1024 \ --save-output \ --warmup \ --enable-torch-compile \ --perf-dump-path /home/sglang-omni/bbuf/qwen_nvfp4_pr28928_rebench_20260624_results/benchmarks/bf16_qwen_image_1024_compile.json CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH=python FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \ sglang generate \ --backend=sglang \ --model-path=lmsys/qwen-image-modelopt-nvfp4-sglang \ --prompt="A futuristic cyberpunk city at night, neon lights reflecting on wet streets" \ --seed=42 \ --width=1024 \ --height=1024 \ --save-output \ --warmup \ --enable-torch-compile \ --perf-dump-path /home/sglang-omni/bbuf/qwen_nvfp4_pr28928_rebench_20260624_results/benchmarks/nvfp4_qwen_image_1024_compile.json ``` | Model | Resolution / steps | Backend | Denoise | Avg step (all 50) | Median step | Tail avg (excl. first 2) | Peak reserved | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Qwen-Image | 1024x1024 / 50 | BF16 | 50.91 s | 1018.2 ms | 139.8 ms | 139.0 ms | 46.8 GB | | Qwen-Image | 1024x1024 / 50 | NVFP4 `flashinfer_trtllm` | 62.91 s | 1258.1 ms | 1111.2 ms | 1157.9 ms | 22.3 GB | Takeaway from the standardized 50-step, torch-compile-enabled 1024x1024 run: NVFP4 is about 23.6% slower than BF16 for Qwen-Image denoising on this B200 setup, while reducing peak reserved memory by about 52.4%. This supersedes the earlier short-step 1024x1024 timing rows, which used explicit 8-step smoke commands and are not comparable to the benchmark/profile skill command. The earlier 2048x2048 and edit-model measurements were bring-up spot checks under shorter commands and should be treated as directional validation only, not as the standardized benchmark table. Profiler traces for the same 1024x1024 setup were generated by adding `--profile` and `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR=...`; both traces passed gzip integrity checks on the B200 node. The trace files are large because SGLang diffusion profiling records CPU+CUDA events with shapes and stacks: BF16 is 2.2 GB compressed and NVFP4 is 396 MB compressed. ## Profiler - main: The red box means `nn.Linear` - pr: The green box means quant overhead. ## Test Plan On the B200 container: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python -m py_compile \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/registry.py \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/utils/quantization_utils.py \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/gpu_cases.py \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/testcase_configs.py ``` Model-backed validation on B200: - Exported `Qwen/Qwen-Image`, `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2512`, `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit`, `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2509`, and `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511` NVFP4 checkpoints with ModelOpt PR #1706. - Uploaded the four hosted checkpoints listed above to `lmsys/*` and verified each public repo has `README.md`, `model_index.json`, and safetensors files through `HfApi.model_info`. - Loaded the hosted `lmsys/qwen-image-2512-modelopt-nvfp4-sglang` checkpoint directly through `--model-path` using the native SGLang diffusion backend. - Confirmed representative NVFP4 logs contain `Built NVFP4 quant config` and native `Loaded transformer` markers without diffusers fallback markers. - Ran the consistency and perf runs listed above. - Re-ran the Qwen-Image 1024x1024 benchmark with the diffusion benchmark/profile skill command shape: 50 model-config steps, `--warmup`, and `--enable-torch-compile`; BF16 denoise was 50.91s and NVFP4 denoise was 62.91s. - Generated BF16 and NVFP4 torch profiler traces for the same 1024x1024 setup with `--profile`; both `.trace.json.gz` files passed gzip integrity checks on the B200 node. - Added the 1-GPU Qwen-Image-2512 NVFP4 GT image in `sgl-project/ci-data` PR #23 and pinned `SGL_TEST_FILES_CI_DATA_REVISION` to `187b8fdc5f49c63d965a1b80528a27ecca9067b2`. B200 CI consistency case added in this PR: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH=python pytest -q \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_b200.py \ -k qwen_image_2512_modelopt_nvfp4_t2i -s ``` Result: `1 passed, 4 deselected` in 114.91s. The hosted Qwen-Image-2512 NVFP4 case loaded from HF cache, generated a 768x768 image with 50 denoise steps, fetched the GT image through `sgl-project/ci-data@187b8fdc5f49c63d965a1b80528a27ecca9067b2` (ci-data PR #23), and passed consistency with `clip=1.0000`, `ssim=1.0000`, `psnr=inf`, and `mean_abs_diff=0.0000`. The same run reported `avg_denoise=326.79ms`, `median_denoise=326.39ms`. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #28167508009](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28167508009) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #28167507920](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28167507920)

title: [VLM] Qwen3-VL / Moss-VL ViT preprocessing optimizations
author: yuan-luo
body:
### Motivation

The ViT position-embedding bilinear interpolation (`fast_pos_embed_interpolate*`) loops in
Python over images, and on the ViT cuda-graph path (`SGLANG_VIT_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1`) it
additionally does a `grid_thw.cpu().numpy()` round-trip plus a numpy per-image loop. The cost
scales with the number of images — invisible for one image, a real bottleneck for many-image /
video / long multimodal prefills.

Two behavior-preserving optimizations that target the **same bottleneck class: multimodal
preprocessing cost that scales with the number of images per request**. Each is negligible for a
single image but becomes a real cost for many-image / video / long multimodal prefills — exactly
the regime that is growing. Both remove a *per-image serial* cost on the critical path:

1. **Vectorize ViT position-embedding interpolation** — replaces the per-image Python loop (and a
   numpy `grid_thw.cpu()` round-trip on the cuda-graph path) with a single batched op whose cost
   is independent of the number of images. (`qwen3_vl.py`, `moss_vl.py`, `environ.py`)
2. **Decode images in the io worker thread instead of lazily on the event loop** — moves the PIL
   decode of each image off the single main event-loop thread (where it ran serially for all
   images) into the io thread pool, so the per-image decode parallelizes across workers.
   (`base_processor.py`)

Both are gated/safe and verified bit-identical to the existing behavior. The two commits are
self-contained independently.

### Modifications
- `fast_pos_embed_interpolate_vectorized` on `Qwen3VLMoeVisionModel` and `MossVLVisionModel`:
  builds per-token `(image, row, col)` coordinates with `arange` + `repeat_interleave`, computes
  interpolation coordinates via a per-unique-size `linspace` lookup, does the 4-corner bilinear
  weighted sum in one batched op, and does the temporal-repeat + spatial-merge reorder with a
  single gather/scatter. Cost is independent of the number of images.
- New env flag `SGLANG_VIT_ENABLE_VECTORIZED_POS_EMBED` (`EnvBool`, default `True`).
- Both call sites wired: the default `forward` path and the cuda-graph `_prepare_graph_inputs` path.
- Image-count threshold `_VECTORIZED_POS_EMBED_MIN_IMAGES = 6`: below it the per-image loop is
  faster, so it falls back. Both paths are bit-exact, so the switch only trades speed for speed.

### Precision — bit-exact
The vectorized path reproduces the legacy arithmetic exactly (same `linspace` coords, same
bilinear-weight arithmetic, same 4-corner reduction, gather/scatter is a pure permutation):
`rtol=0, atol=0` across single / large-upsample / multi-mixed / video / video+image / many-image
grids, in bf16 and fp32, on CPU and CUDA.

### Performance
`fast_pos_embed_interpolate` micro-benchmark on H20-3e (Qwen3-VL config, bf16), vectorized vs loop:

| images | 1 | 8 | 64 | 256 | 552 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| speedup | 0.27x | 1.34x | 4.68x | 7.82x | 5.85x |

Crossover ~6 images (hence the threshold); single-image (common case) keeps the faster loop.

---

## 2. Decode images in the io worker thread instead of lazily on the event loop

### Motivation
`BaseMultimodalProcessor._load_single_item` runs in the multimodal `io_executor` thread pool and
is meant to do per-item decode off the main thread. But for **PNG / non-JPEG** inputs
`load_image` returns a `PIL.Image` from `Image.open(...)`, which **decodes lazily** — the pixel
data is materialized only on first access. That first access happens later, inside the HF fast
image processor's `pil_to_tensor` → `PIL.Image.tobytes()`, which runs on the **tokenizer
manager's main event-loop thread** (the processor call is `await`ed but executes synchronously in
the loop). So the decode is serialized on a single thread and blocks the event loop.

py-spy of the tokenizer-manager process under multi-image load shows this `tobytes()` decode as
the dominant main-thread cost (~69% of main-thread samples for 16×448px PNG).

### What changed
In `_load_single_item`, force the PIL decode in the io worker thread:

```python
if modality == Modality.IMAGE:
    img, _ = load_image(data, cls.gpu_image_decode)
    if not isinstance(img, torch.Tensor):
        if discard_alpha_channel and img.mode != "RGB":
            img = img.convert("RGB")   # convert() also forces the decode
        else:
            img.load()                 # force the otherwise-lazy decode here
    return img
```

The decode now runs in the `io_executor` worker (parallelized across workers, off the main
thread); the later `tobytes()` becomes a cheap memcpy. JPEG is unaffected — it already returns a
CUDA tensor via nvJPEG (`decode_jpeg(device="cuda")`) and skips this branch.

### Precision — behavior unchanged
Output is bit-identical: same mode (RGBA/P/L → RGB via the existing `convert("RGB")` when
`discard_alpha_channel`; RGB unchanged) and same pixels. Only *when/which thread* the decode runs
changes. `img.load()` is idempotent and safe.

### Performance
Qwen3-VL-4B, 16 images @448px, H20-3e, isolated requests, with `--keep-mm-feature-on-device`:

| metric | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `processor.__call__` (image processing) | ~95 ms | **~11 ms** |
| preprocess `total_time` | ~124 ms | **~38 ms** |
| py-spy main-thread `tobytes` share | ~69% | **~3%** |

This is a **preprocessing-latency / event-loop-occupancy** win, not a throughput win for
GPU-bound serving: for heavy multi-image requests the vision encoder on the base GPU is the
bottleneck (cold concurrent throughput is GPU-bound and unchanged by this patch). The benefit
shows up in single-request / TTFT latency, in workloads where the vision encoder is not the wall,
and in keeping the tokenizer manager's event loop responsive under load. PNG / non-JPEG only.

---

## Tests

- **Pos-embed**: `test/registered/models/test_vit_pos_embed_interpolate.py` — `torch.equal` between
  the vectorized and loop paths for Qwen3-VL and Moss-VL across single / large / multi-mixed /
  video / video+image / many-image grids, bf16 + fp32, CPU + CUDA.
- **Image decode**: `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_base_processor_image_decode.py`
  (`base-a-test-cpu`, no server/model) — asserts `_load_single_item` returns an already-decoded
  image (vs a bare lazy `Image.open`), preserves RGBA→RGB alpha-discard, and returns pixels
  bit-identical to the reference path. Verified as a genuine regression test: it **fails on the
  pre-fix code** (`test_load_single_item_forces_decode`) and passes with the fix.

```bash
python -m pytest test/registered/models/test_vit_pos_embed_interpolate.py -v
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_base_processor_image_decode.py -v
```

title: [CI] Optimize nixl dependency installation script
author: ShangmingCai
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
The CI dependency install script (`install_extra_deps()`) unconditionally runs `pip install nixl==... nixl-cuXX==...` on every CI run, even when the runner image already has the correct versions installed. Since nixl ships native binaries, repeated installs add unnecessary network I/O and `--force-reinstall` overhead.
The same script already uses a version-check-and-skip pattern for flashinfer in `uninstall_stale_flashinfer()` to avoid re-downloading large packages. This PR applies the same approach to nixl: skip reinstallation when both the meta package and the correct CUDA variant are already at the required version.
## Modifications
- Refactor nixl installation logic in `scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh` → `install_extra_deps()`:
  - Split nixl out of the main `pip install` line into a separate conditional install step
  - Before installing, check versions of the `nixl` meta package and the matching CUDA binary (`nixl-cu12` or `nixl-cu13`) via `pip show`
  - Skip installation when both match `NIXL_VERSION` (currently `1.3.0`) and log the skip
  - On version mismatch or missing packages, install with `--no-deps --force-reinstall`
  - Remove proactive uninstall of the wrong CUDA variant to avoid touching packages that may already exist on the runner image
- Simplify variables: replace `NIXL_PKG` / `NIXL_BIN_PKG` / `NIXL_STALE_BIN_PKG` with `NIXL_BIN_NAME`

title: [LoRA] BF16 support + EP cuda-graph crash fix for experimental_sgl_trtllm MoE-LoRA
author: jybsuper
body:
## Summary

Two changes on the `experimental_sgl_trtllm` MoE-LoRA fast path:

1. **BF16 support** for the path (previously FP8 / NVFP4 only), plus `experts_shared_outer` LoRA.
2. **Stability fixes** that make the path correct under expert parallelism (EP) + CUDA graph:
   - **NVFP4 (Kimi-K2.5):** fix an illegal-memory-access that crashed batched serving under CUDA graph with the two-stream overlap enabled.
   - **BF16:** two follow-up correctness fixes (routing arg parity + CUDA-graph allocation safety).


## Testing

Hardware: **2 nodes × 8× GB300 (TP8 / EP8, MNNVL)**, flashinfer 0.6.12.

### Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 — the crash fix
`--moe-runner-backend experimental_sgl_trtllm`, two-stream overlap **on**, CUDA graph **on**, rank-16 adapter.

- **Before:** batched `bench_one_batch_server` crashes with an illegal memory access (TMA descriptor init) during prefill.
- **After:** no crash; greedy generation coherent across diverse prompts (adapter behavior preserved). Validated bs1 prefill (the minimal repro) through bs128.
- **End-to-end overall throughput** at `input = output = 2048`, vs the no-LoRA `flashinfer_trtllm` baseline:

| batch | LoRA (tok/s) | base (tok/s) | % of base |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 | 2519 | 3244 | 78% |
| 32 | 4513 | 5294 | 85% |
| 64 | 7353 | 8266 | 89% |
| 128 | 11628 | 13076 | 89% |

(decode-only ratio rises 79% → 96% with batch as the two-stream overlap amortizes.)

### Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (BF16) — the BF16 path
Experimental path, CUDA graph + two-stream on:

- `--max-loras-per-batch` 2 and 4 with distinct adapters in a single batch: all outputs coherent, no cross-adapter contamination.

Add `register_amd_ci(suite="nightly-amd-kernel-1-gpu", nightly=True)` to **7** JIT-kernel correctness tests (previously CUDA-only) that are **validated to pass on both ROCm 7.0 and ROCm 7.2** (MI35x / gfx950).

## ✅ Verified on real MI35x via `run_suite` (per-file runtime)

`run_suite.py --hw amd --suite nightly-amd-kernel-1-gpu --nightly` — dedicated runs of the kernel suite on both stacks, **both jobs green (11/11 files passed)**:

| Test | ROCm 7.0 | ROCm 7.2 |

| `test_minimax_decode_topk` (118 cases) | ✅ 11s | ✅ 13s |

Latest dispatched runs (kernel job only):
- ROCm 7.0: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28066360661
- ROCm 7.2: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28066361479

## Placement

Mirrors NV's nightly tier (NV dual-registers each JIT kernel test to `base-b-kernel-unit-1-gpu-large` + `nightly-kernel-1-gpu`). AMD's `nightly-amd-kernel-1-gpu` suite is already wired in `nightly-test-amd.yml` / `nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`, so **no workflow changes** are needed.

## Approach — purely additive, AMD-only

- Each file keeps its existing `register_cuda_ci(...)`; we only add one `register_amd_ci(..., nightly=True)` line.
- No new files, no moves, no workflow changes. Legacy `sgl-kernel/tests/` and NV / MUSA jobs untouched.

## Scope note (why these and not the rest)

Candidates were trial-registered and run on both ROCm stacks; only the ones green on **both** are kept. The remainder were dropped — their failures are **environment / portability gaps, not registration issues** (confirmed from run logs):
- Missing dep on ROCm (`flashinfer`) → norm / rope family (`test_rmsnorm`, `test_qknorm`, `test_rope`, ...).
- JIT sources `#include` raw CUDA headers not hipified on ROCm (`cuda_runtime.h`, `cuda_fp16.h`, `cuda/ptx`, `cub/cub.cuh`, `cooperative_groups/reduce.h`) → `ninja` compile failures.
- AOT `sgl_kernel` ops not built on the ROCm images (e.g. `concat_mla_*`, `sgl_per_token_group_quant_8bit_v2`); `renorm` op not registered.
- wave64 portability: 32-bit `__shfl_sync` mask static-assert (`test_grouped_topk`).
- JIT runtime `Tensor match failed` on ROCm device (`test_add_constant`, `test_ngram_embedding`; incl. fp8 `e4m3fnuz` vs `e4m3fn`).
- `diffusers` dep (`test_timestep_embedding`).
- `test_moe_align_block_size`: 4392-case matrix all fail + 900s timeout.

These can be revisited once the ROCm jit-build / deps gaps are addressed (separate effort).

- `collect_tests(sanity_check=True)` passes; all 7 register to `nightly-amd-kernel-1-gpu` (each has a `__main__` entry).
- `ruff`, `isort`, `black` clean.

- [x] No change to NV / MUSA / per-commit AMD behavior (CUDA registrations untouched).

title: [Refactor] Share CUDA graph memory pool across prefill and decode
author: cctry
body:
## Motivation

Since the cuda graph runner/backend refactor (#23906), the prefill and decode graph backends each allocate their own `graph_pool_handle()`, so their captured graphs reserve memory independently. The `_global_graph_memory_pool` helper added in that refactor has been unused.

## Modifications

Route all three backends (`FullCudaGraphBackend`, `BreakableCudaGraphBackend`, `TcPiecewiseCudaGraphBackend`) through a new `get_or_create_global_graph_memory_pool()` in `runner_utils/pool.py`. The first phase to capture allocates the pool; the other reuses the same handle.

This is safe: the pool only holds scratch/activation memory allocated *during* capture (static I/O buffers live outside it), and prefill/decode never replay concurrently — so sharing reserves only the larger phase's footprint instead of the sum. Same pattern as the existing decode-target / EAGLE-draft pool sharing.

## Accuracy / Speed

No output change (memory-layout only). Functional + memory check pending on CI.

title: [weight checker] refactor: add precision branch; allow ULP quant err; used chunked compare
author: yueming-yuan
body:
## Motivation

The weight checker's `compare`/`checksum` actions require two block-quantized weights to be **bit-identical** after dequant. But two independent yet faithful quantizations of the same source weight — e.g. before vs. after a weight update that requantizes — can legitimately differ per element. Tolerating that with a hand-tuned mean-error threshold is both too loose (a mean lets per-element corruption hide in a large tensor) and arbitrary per model/precision.

This replaces it with a principled, per-element tolerance: each side of a block-quant pair is one faithful quantization of the same source weight, so each may deviate from it by up to 1 ULP of its own representation — i.e. the two may differ by at most `expect_ulp + actual_ulp` per element in dequantized space. Opt in via `allow_quant_error`; the default stays exact-equality (no behavior change).

## Modifications

- `CheckWeightsReqInput` gains `allow_quant_error: bool = False`, plumbed through scheduler / `model_runner.check_weights` into the weight checker.
- New `weight_checker_quant.py` holds the quantization-aware comparison behind a small `ReferenceWeight` seam (`Fp8BlockReference` today). Adding a precision is a new subclass.
- `select_quantization_method` dispatches on `module.quant_method` (not param names — robust to swizzled scales / per-format naming) and raises `NotImplementedError` for formats with no `ReferenceWeight`, so mxfp8 / nvfp4 / int4 fail loudly instead of being silently mis-compared.
- Comparison/dequant is chunked to bound GPU memory; NaN counts as exceeding tolerance (`~(diff <= tol)`); block size is inferred from weight/scale shapes (handles partial last blocks and non-128 block formats).

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/utils/test_weight_checker.py` (CUDA-gated):
- `TestQuantUlp` — `_quant_ulp` brute-force verified against the true spacing of all 256 bit patterns of `float8_e4m3fn` / `float8_e5m2` (exact match).
- `TestCompareQuantPair` — two quantizations within tolerance pass; bit-flip corruption and fp8 NaN exceed; chunked == unchunked; partial last block; 3D expert tensors; ue8m0-packed scales.
- `TestSelectQuantizationMethod` — unsupported quant method raises.

title: [AMD] [GLM5] Add opt-in Triton fp8 sparse-MLA prefill kernel for gfx950
author: Raiden-Makoto
body:
## Motivation

This affects HIP serving of DSA (DeepSeek Sparse Attention) models; it was found
and validated on **GLM-5.1-MXFP4** (which uses the DSA indexer) on MI350X.

On the HIP fp8 path, `tilelang_sparse_fwd` runs the *same* TileLang
partial+combine kernel for prefill as for decode. The sparse-MLA attention tile
is tiny — `M = 16` heads (one `16x16` MFMA) — so the 256-thread (4-warp)
TileLang block over-parallelizes it and spends most of its time on intra-block
coordination rather than the matmuls (profiling at the prefill config on gfx950
shows the kernel VALU-bound at ~42% with MFMA at ~12% and ~37% occupancy).

A per-query Triton flash kernel with a small `2-warp` / `BLOCK_N=32` tile fits
the problem shape and saturates the GPU on block count instead. It also reads
`q_nope`/`q_rope` directly, skipping the per-layer concat (the kernel splits q
into main/tail internally anyway, so combining them first is wasted work — and
the HIP path uses a plain `torch.cat`, not the fused CUDA concat). Decode is
left on TileLang.

## Modifications

- New `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/triton_sparse_mla.py`: a per-query
  Triton flash kernel over the indexer-selected topk KV. Autotuned over
  `BLOCK_N`/`num_warps`/`num_stages`; guards an all-masked query row against
  `NaN` (finite softmax shift when the row has no valid key). Reads `q_nope`
  (width `d_v`) and `q_rope` (width `dim-d_v`) as two separate tensors.
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa_backend.py`: in `forward_extend`, route
  the fp8 prefill path to the Triton kernel and pass `q_nope`/`q_rope` directly,
  skipping `concat_mla_absorb_q_general`.
  - **Opt-in, default off**: enable with `SGLANG_DSA_TRITON_PREFILL=1`.
  - Gated to gfx950 + the validated shape (`num_heads==16`, `d_v==512`,
    `tail==64`, `topk==2048`); other archs/shapes use TileLang.
  - Prefill only; decode stays on TileLang.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K 5-shot, full 1319 questions, GLM-5.1-MXFP4, MI350X (gfx950), tp4,
fp8_e4m3 KV:

| | accuracy |
|---|---|
| TileLang prefill (default) | 0.938 |
| Triton prefill (`SGLANG_DSA_TRITON_PREFILL=1`) | 0.941 |

No regression.

## Speed Benchmarks

E2E `sglang.bench_serving` (random, input 8192 / output 1024, median latencies),
GLM-5.1-MXFP4 / MI350X / tp4 / fp8_e4m3 KV.

Baseline (TileLang prefill):

| concurrency | total tok/s | TTFT (ms) | ITL (ms) | E2EL (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 944 | 920 | 17.74 | 19491 |
| 4 | 1717 | 1752 | 18.56 | 21436 |
| 8 | 2847 | 2887 | 20.66 | 25895 |
| 16 | 4343 | 5116 | 24.23 | 33946 |
| 32 | 6233 | 9588 | 28.68 | 47438 |
| 64 | 8158 | 18558 | 35.54 | 72308 |

This PR (`SGLANG_DSA_TRITON_PREFILL=1`):

| concurrency | total tok/s | TTFT (ms) | TTFT delta | ITL (ms) | E2EL (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 957 | 798 | -13.3% | 17.71 | 19228 |
| 4 | 1738 | 1511 | -13.8% | 18.58 | 21126 |
| 8 | 2922 | 2486 | -13.9% | 20.73 | 25217 |
| 16 | 4515 | 4410 | -13.8% | 24.22 | 32655 |
| 32 | 6574 | 8276 | -13.7% | 28.56 | 44814 |
| 64 | 8750 | 16051 | -13.5% | 35.36 | 67431 |

Median TTFT improves 13.3-13.9% across the sweep; median ITL is unchanged
(within +/-0.5%) and median E2EL is flat-to-better, confirming the change is
prefill-side with no decode regression.

title: perf(deepseek_v4): enable SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM on sm90 (Hopper)
author: guzekai01
body:
## Motivation

`SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM` runs the DeepSeek-V4 `wo_a` projection as an fp8
grouped matmul (`deep_gemm.fp8_einsum`). It was gated to Blackwell (sm100+)
because it assumed ue8m0-format scales. DeepGEMM's grouped fp8 GEMM also works
on Hopper (sm90) with fp32 scales, so this enables the path there. Opt-in;
sm100 behavior unchanged.

## Modifications

- `models/deepseek_v4.py`: pick scale format + recipe by `DEEPGEMM_SCALE_UE8M0`
  — sm100 ue8m0 `(1,1,128)`, sm90 fp32 `(1,128,128)` — in the `wo_a` forward,
  `_setup_fp8_wo_a_scales`, and layer init.
- `server_args.py`: keep the flag opt-in on sm90 (default off) instead of
  force-disabling below sm100; still force-off below sm90.
- `deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py`: skip the ue8m0 sanity check on the
  fp32-scale path.
- `test/manual/dsv4/wo_a_fp8_sm90_correctness.py`: correctness test (cosine vs
  the bf16 reference).

Validated on H20 (sm90), marlin MoE backend, A/B toggling only the flag:
DeepSeek-V4-**Flash** (TP8, single node) and DeepSeek-V4-**Pro** (TP8 + PP2,
2 nodes).

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, 1319 questions, parallel 100 (Invalid = 0.000 in all four runs):

| model | bf16 wo_a | fp8 wo_a |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Flash | 0.955 | 0.952 |
| Pro | 0.955 | 0.955 |

**Accuracy check — AIME2025**

Ran the AIME2025 regression on Hopper (sm90, H20) with the fp8 `wo_a` path enabled
(`SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=1`, i.e. the sm90 opt-in this PR adds), Think-Max reasoning,
temperature 1.0 / top-p 1.0, on DeepSeek-V4-Flash:

| SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM | AIME2025 (opencompass, 30 Q) |
|---|---|
| `1` (fp8 wo_a, sm90 path) | **96.67%** |

In line with the DeepSeek-V4-Flash reference (~95%, repeated runs 93.3–100%), so the
sm90 fp8 `wo_a` GEMM introduces no accuracy regression.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`bench_serving`. Δ = (fp8 − bf16)/bf16, negative = fp8 faster.

Prefill TTFT (ms, median; out=1, conc=1):

| ISL | Flash bf16 | Flash fp8 | Δ | Pro bf16 | Pro fp8 | Δ |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1k | 190.4 | 160.7 | −15.6% | 276.3 | 271.6 | −1.7% |
| 2k | 164.2 | 180.7 | +10.0% | 478.2 | 446.4 | −6.7% |
| 4k | 270.2 | 285.8 | +5.8% | 852.8 | 817.0 | −4.2% |
| 8k | 536.0 | 455.8 | −15.0% | 1474.2 | 1398.1 | −5.2% |
| 16k | 1092.3 | 984.0 | −9.9% | 2305.7 | 2242.5 | −2.7% |
| 32k | 2014.8 | 1886.7 | −6.4% | 4000.7 | 3858.7 | −3.5% |
| 64k | 3855.5 | 3821.0 | −0.9% | 7564.1 | 7275.4 | −3.8% |

title: Add SM90 FP8 MegaMoE support for DeepSeek-V4
author: qiushixiaoyu
body:
## Motivation
This PR adds SM90 DeepGEMM MegaMoE adaptation for DeepSeek-V4 FP8 serving. It enables the MegaMoE A2A path with the DeepGEMM MoE runner on SM90, including the pre-dispatch JIT kernel, FP8 expert weight preparation, and DeepSeek-V4 integration.

The goal is to improve long-context / large decode serving throughput for DeepSeek-V4-Flash/Pro-FP8 workloads while keeping the path guarded by environment variables.

## Modifications

- Add SM90 MegaMoE pre-dispatch JIT kernel for preparing activations, scales, top-k indices, and top-k weights.
- Add unit tests for the SM90 MegaMoE pre-dispatch kernel against a PyTorch reference implementation.
- Integrate the MegaMoE path into DeepSeek-V4 / FP8 MoE execution.
- Add FP8 MegaMoE expert weight preparation support.
- Wire DeepGEMM MegaMoE execution through the existing MoE backend selection.

Environment variables used to enable the path:
- `SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE=1` enables the DeepGEMM MegaMoE path.
- `SGLANG_OPT_FIX_MEGA_MOE_MEMORY=1` enables the fixed MegaMoE memory path.
- `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_EP_ACTIVATION=1` is required by the fixed MegaMoE memory path.
- `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=4096` configures the max token buffer size per rank used by the MegaMoE path. In PD colocated serving, it should be set to the same value as `--chunked-prefill-size`; in decode-only serving, it should be larger than the maximum number of tokens per rank. The experiment below used `4096`, matching `--chunked-prefill-size=4096`.

Serving command used in the experiment:

> export MODEL_PATH=/data00/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8
> export SERVER_PORT=30000
> export NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX=3
> export NCCL_IB_HCA=mlx5_1,mlx5_2,mlx5_3,mlx5_4,mlx5_5,mlx5_6,mlx5_7,mlx5_8
> export FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1
> export NVSHMEM_HCA_PE_MAPPING=mlx5_1:1:1,mlx5_2:1:1,mlx5_3:1:1,mlx5_4:1:1,mlx5_5:1:1,mlx5_6:1:1,mlx5_7:1:1,mlx5_8:1:1
> export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
> export SGLANG_ENABLE_THINKING=1
> export SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=0
> export SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0
> export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0
> export NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=24
> export NCCL_IB_QPS_PER_CONNECTION=8
> 
> export SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE=1
> export SGLANG_OPT_FIX_MEGA_MOE_MEMORY=1
> export SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_EP_ACTIVATION=1
> export SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=4096
> 
> python -m sglang.launch_server \
>   --trust-remote-code \
>   --model-path "${MODEL_PATH}" \
>   --tp 8 \
>   --ep-size 8 \
>   --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
>   --moe-a2a-backend deepep \
>   --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \
>   --deepep-mode auto \
>   --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \
>   --max-running-requests 32 \
>   --speculative-algo EAGLE \
>   --speculative-num-steps 3 \
>   --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
>   --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
>   --enable-metrics \
>   --host 0.0.0.0 \
>   --port "${SERVER_PORT}" \
>   --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \
>   --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \
>   --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4

## Accuracy Tests

sgl-eval run gpqa
--n-repeats 16 --max-tokens 200000
--temperature 1.0 --top-p 1.0 --thinking
--out-dir /sgl-workspace/logs
--base-url http://localhost:30000/v1

> == gpqa ==
> 198 examples x 16 repeats | 13017.8s | 2620 tok/s | 34.1M tokens
> 
> pass@1[avg-of-16] = 88.64% +/- 1.28% (SEM 0.32%)
> pass@16 = 96.46%
> majority@16 = 90.15%
> no_answer = 0.03%
> stop_rate = 100.00%
> truncated_rate = 0.00%
> error_rate = 0.00%

Benchmark | Result
-- | --
GSM8K | Accuracy 0.956, Invalid 0.000
GPQA | Score 0.90625, num_examples=32

Unit test:

> python -m pytest -q python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_mega_moe_pre_dispatch_sm90.py

Result:

> 10 passed, 20 warnings in 7.32s

## Speed Tests and Profiling
DeepGEMM dependency note:

The FP8 MegaMoE operator has already been merged into DeepGEMM in [sgl-project/DeepGEMM#36](https://github.com/sgl-project/DeepGEMM/pull/36). This benchmark additionally includes the small-batch performance optimization from [sgl-project/DeepGEMM#48](https://github.com/sgl-project/DeepGEMM/pull/48).

Benchmark script:
The serving benchmark was run with `sglang_auto_bench.py`, an internal helper script that wraps `python -m sglang.bench_serving` and automatically searches for the highest request rate / max concurrency for a given input-output length. It reports both:

- SLO-compliant throughput, constrained by the configured TTFT / TPOT targets.
- Max throughput, which may violate the SLO and is used only to understand the saturation point.

For the result below, the script was run with random prompts, input/output length `3500/1500`, and SLO targets `TTFT <= 2000 ms` and `TPOT <= 20 ms`.

Mode | SLO total throughput | SLO output throughput | TTFT | TPOT
-- | -- | -- | -- | --
MegaMoE ON | 7001.55 tok/s | 2100.46 tok/s | 683.94 ms | 13.83 ms
MegaMoE OFF | 5727.56 tok/s | 1718.27 tok/s | 825.53 ms | 17.05 ms

MegaMoE ON vs OFF:
SLO total throughput: +22.24%
SLO output throughput: +22.24%

title: build(sgl-kernel): bump FlashMLA pin + fix cccl include for CUDA 13
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Summary

Bumps the vendored FlashMLA pin in `sgl-kernel/cmake/flashmla.cmake` to pick up sm90 dense decode `HEAD_DIM_K=512` support, and adds the CUDA 13 `cccl` include-path fix that the pin bump requires.

Two changes, both in `sgl-kernel/cmake/flashmla.cmake`:

1. **FlashMLA pin bump** `df022eba` → `05e26647` — pulls in sgl-project/FlashMLA#9 (`sm90 dense decode: support HEAD_DIM_K=512 (zero RoPE tail)`, merged into the `rebase` branch), which parameterizes `HEAD_DIM_K` so models with a pure-latent 512-dim K head (no RoPE tail) can use the sm90 dense decode kernel.
2. **CUDA 13 `cccl` include-path fix** — in CUDA 13, `cuda/std/*` moved under `cccl/cuda/std/*`. The vendored cutlass routes `<cuda/std/...>` to `<cccl/cuda/std/...>` when `__CUDACC_VER_MAJOR__ >= 13`, so the host C++ translation unit (compiled by g++, where that macro is unset for the legacy path) needs the cccl root on the search path. Without this, building `flashmla_ops` on CUDA 13 fails with `fatal error: cuda/std/utility: No such file or directory`.

## Validation

Built `sgl-kernel` on an 8×H200 devbox (CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.11+cu130) using the formal GitHub-archive pin: full build passes (527/527 targets) — confirms the cccl fix resolves the `cuda/std/utility` failure. The `HEAD_DIM_K=512` instantiation is present in `flashmla_ops.so`. Numerical smoke test confirms the PR#9 bit-exact claim: `head_dim_k=512` output is bit-exact (`max abs diff 0.00000000`) with `head_dim_k=576` whose RoPE tail is zeroed.

All three originally-requested e2e tests passed on the 8×H200 devbox with the rebuilt `sgl-kernel`:

| Test | Model | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `test/registered/mla/test_flashmla.py` | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324` (MLA, head_dim_k=576) | **PASS** — gsm8k 0.965 (>0.60); `attention_backend=flashmla` drives the PR#9 sm90 dense decode kernel |
| `test/registered/models_e2e/test_dsa_glm5_tp_mtp.py` | `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8` | **PASS** — gsm8k 0.948 (≥0.94), avg_spec_accept_length 3.29 (≥2.7) |
| `test/registered/models_e2e/test_dsa_glm5_dp_mtp.py` | `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8` | **PASS** — gsm8k 0.958 (≥0.94), avg_spec_accept_length 3.26 (≥2.7) |

Notes on test substitutions (the upstream fixtures point at private/CI-only repos, so public equivalents were used):
- `test_flashmla.py` originally uses `lmsys/sglang-ci-dsv3-test` + `lmsys/sglang-ci-dsv3-test-NextN` (both HF 404, private CI models). Substituted public `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324` and dropped the MTP/EAGLE args (DSv3 has no public MTP draft checkpoint), keeping `--attention-backend flashmla` so it still exercises the PR#9 dense decode kernel on the 576 path.
- The two glm5 e2e tests originally use `zai-org/GLM-5-FP8` (HF 404 in our cache); substituted the public `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8` (same DSA family, head_dim_k=576). They use `attention_backend=dsa` (decode via `fa3`, prefill via `flashmla_sparse`), so they serve as regression coverage confirming the pin bump + cccl fix does not break GLM-5.1 DSA serving rather than exercising the 512 path directly.
- The new 512 path's correctness is covered by the bit-exact smoke test above.

title: fix(runner): autotune flashinfer MoE on a decode-shaped buffer
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

The warmup flashinfer-autotune dummy forward runs on the `EagerRunner`'s input registry, whose buffers are sized to the prefill token ceiling. flashinfer's trtllm MoE autotuner selects kernel tactics by on-device timing, so the buffer it tunes against must be representative of the live decode shape. Tuning on the prefill-sized buffer selects tactics that are suboptimal at decode — most visible on MoE models, where decode scatters tokens across experts and the hot path is the small-`m` grouped GEMM.

## Modifications

`EagerRunner._autotune_buffers` now allocates a decode/target-verify shaped dummy buffer via `_alloc_dummy_decode_buffers` rather than adapting the prefill-sized eager registry. `_allocate_decode_buffers` already populates every field `_dummy_run` consumes (`custom_mask`, `pp_proxy_tensors` incl. `topk_indices`, global token counts), so spec / pp>1 / dp paths stay covered. The buffer is one-shot at warmup and freed before graph capture, so the eager registry remains the canonical shared-pool buffer that the cuda-graph runners coalesce onto.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerical change — this only affects which kernel tactic flashinfer caches, not the MoE result.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, B300, TP4 / EP1, EAGLE MTP (steps 3 / topk 1 / draft 4), `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm`, conc 32, random isl/osl 1024/1024:

| | output throughput (tok/s) | mean TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| main | 1414 | 21.3 |
| this PR | 2353 | 12.5 |

title: [Perf] Overlap result D2H copy with the next forward step
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary
- Run the per-step result D2H (`next_token_ids`, logprobs, hidden states, spec `accept_lens`) on the dedicated `copy_stream` so it overlaps the next forward instead of serializing on `forward_stream`.
- Route every result-side device->host copy through a single `_async_d2h` primitive (pinned dst + `record_stream`), so the copy and its cross-stream lifetime safety live in one place.

## Background
- `copy_to_cpu` issued the D2H on `forward_stream` into pageable host memory. A D2H to pageable memory is synchronous on the host, so it blocked the scheduler thread and serialized ahead of the next forward.
- The sub-result copies (`TopkCaptureOutput`, `ExpertDistributionMetrics`) each hand-rolled their own `.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)`, duplicating the copy across modules.

## Changes
**Overlap**
- Issue the result D2H on `copy_stream` with `copy_stream.wait_stream(forward_stream)` for ordering. The copy is a leaf gated by `copy_done`, so nothing on `forward_stream` waits on it.
- `_async_d2h` writes into a pinned host buffer so the copy is genuinely async and no longer stalls the scheduler thread; `record_stream` keeps each GPU source alive until `copy_stream` drains.

**Single copy primitive**
- `_async_d2h(t)` is the only place a result-side D2H + `record_stream` happens.
- `TopkCaptureOutput` / `ExpertDistributionMetrics` now expose `map_device_tensors(fn)` (declare their device fields only); `GenerationBatchResult.copy_to_cpu` injects `_async_d2h`, so a new tensor holder cannot miss the safety step.
- `EmbeddingBatchResult.copy_to_cpu` routes through `_async_d2h` too.

**Observability**
- Annotate `copy_to_cpu` with `@torch.profiler.record_function` so the copy is identifiable in traces and projects onto the `copy_stream` GPU track.

## Notes
- CUDA-only; non-CUDA falls back to the previous plain `.to("cpu")` path.
- The next-iteration seq_lens relay D2H is intentionally left separate (different consumer, timing, and stream).

title: [NPU] perf: precompute mamba conv-state track indices once per batch
author: AndyLi429
body:
## Motivation

  In the Ascend GDN (Gated Delta Net) attention backend, the prefill/extend path  recomputed the mamba conv-state tracking indices **inside `forward_extend`,  once per linear-attention layer**. The index computation
  (`mamba_track_mask.nonzero()` plus a gather into `mamba_track_indices`) is  batch-level data — it does not change across layers — yet it was redone on  every layer. On NPU, `nonzero()` produces a data-dependent shape and forces a
  device→host sync, so repeating it per layer adds avoidable overhead on the  prefill critical path.
  This PR computes those indices **once per batch** and reuses them across all  layers, reducing time-to-first-token without changing any model output.
  ## Modifications

  - Add `_prepare_mamba_track_metadata()` to `AscendGDNAttnBackend`. When    `forward_metadata.has_mamba_track_mask` is set, it precomputes:
    - `mamba_track_mask_indices = mamba_track_mask.nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]`
    - `conv_states_mask_indices = mamba_track_indices[mamba_track_mask_indices]`
    and stores them on `ForwardMetadata`. It is invoked from both  `init_forward_metadata` and `init_forward_metadata_out_graph`, i.e. once per   batch.
  - In `forward_extend`, replace the per-layer inline computation (`nonzero()` +   gather) and the inline `mamba_track_mask is not None and .any()` guard with a    read of the precomputed `forward_metadata.conv_states_mask_indices`, gated by    `forward_metadata.has_mamba_track_mask`.
  - Net effect: for a hybrid model with K linear-attention layers, the   dynamic-shape `nonzero()` runs **once per batch** instead of **K times per    prefill**. The decode path is untouched.

  This is a behavior-preserving change: `has_mamba_track_mask` is defined as  `bool(mamba_track_mask is not None and mamba_track_mask.any())`, identical to  the guard it replaces, and `conv_states_mask_indices` equals the previous
  `mamba_track_indices[mask_indices]`. A fresh `ForwardMetadata` is built per  batch, so no stale indices can leak across batches.

 ## Accuracy Tests

  The change is behavior-preserving, so accuracy is expected to match the  pre-change build. Verified with GPQA-Diamond on `Qwen3.6-27B`:

  | Model | Dataset | Metric | Num | Score |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `Qwen3.6-27B` | gpqa_diamond | mean_acc | 198 | **0.8586** |
