title: [Kernel] Sweep decoupled scattered kernels into sglang.kernels.ops (RFC #29630)
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

Continues the RFC #29630 scattered-kernel sweep. This PR moves the kernels that are **genuinely decoupled** (no srt runtime-type dependency) into `sglang.kernels.ops.*`, byte-identically, following the Phase 2.5 recipe (move + `KernelSpec` registration + in-tree import rewrites only).

## Moved (byte-identical)
| from | to |
|---|---|
| `srt/speculative/ragged_verify_kernels.py` | `kernels/ops/speculative/` |
| `srt/speculative/reject_sampling.py` | `kernels/ops/speculative/` |
| `srt/layers/attention/dsv4/attn_metadata_kernels.py` | `kernels/ops/attention/dsv4_attn_metadata_kernels.py` |
| `srt/layers/attention/cute_utils/` (CuTe DSL) | `kernels/ops/attention/cute_utils/` |
| `srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/moe_fused_mul_sum.py` | `kernels/ops/moe/` |

Moving `cute_utils` also removes a `kernels → srt` **reverse import** that the kda/gdn blackwell kernels previously had.

## Verification
- Namespace import stays metadata-only (torch-free / no `sgl_kernel` / no `jit_kernel`) — the invariant `test_import_stays_metadata_only` guards.
- 182 ops registered; 68 CPU tests pass; lint clean.

## Deliberately NOT moved (would break the namespace or recreate reverse imports)
- **SB/RVL-bound** (depend on `ScheduleBatch` / `RaggedVerifyLayout`): `dspark_verify_window`, `dspark_accept`, `mem_cache/allocation`.
- **Would recreate a `kernels → srt` reverse import**: `batch_invariant_ops` (deep_gemm/npu config), `lora/trtllm_lora_temp/specialized_expand` (`lora_envs`), `dspark_schedule/draft_model/attn_metadata` (dspark `dispatch`).

Pure kernels embedded in large subsystem/model modules (`memory_pool`, `models/*`, `base_backend`, `staging_buffer`, …) are extractable and handled as a follow-up.

title: Revert "Fix mamba track-boundary seqlen under overlap scheduler (#31369)"
author: alisonshao
body:
## Problem

Reverts #31369, which introduced a **deterministic correctness regression** on `main`: the Qwen3-Next decode-cache-hit logprobs diverge from a cold recompute, failing the nightly `4-gpu-h100` test since 2026-07-17:

```
test/registered/models_e2e/test_qwen3_next_models.py::test_input_output_logprobs_match_decode_cache_hit_helper
AssertionError: avg_kl_div=0.006489 > threshold=0.002 for Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct
```

(identical kl_div on every retry → deterministic, not flaky).

## Bisect

Pinned to #31369 (`0675d3033f`):
- kl_div was ≤0.0005 (pass) at `dc0b3eb` and jumped to 0.0065 (fail) at `681c2235`; #31369 is **absent in the good run, present in the bad run**.
- It is the **only** commit in that window touching `_mamba_check_track_boundary` / `batch_result_processor.py` / the mamba track-boundary logic.
- It rewrites the exact function that records the mamba tracking boundary for cache-hit decode — which is precisely what the failing test validates.

## Why it regressed

#31369 changed the boundary seqlen from `req.kv_committed_len` to `len(req.origin_input_ids) + len(req.output_ids) - 1`. That new seqlen mislabels the mamba track boundary for the decode-cache-hit case, so a reused/donated tracked prefix extends from a state a cold prefill recompute would not produce — exactly the mismatch the test catches (and the symptom #31369's own description warns about).

## Scope

Reverting restores the previously-passing behavior. The original overlap-scheduler boundary issue #31369 aimed at should re-land through the open #29792 ("Fix Mamba track-boundary bookkeeping under overlap scheduling"), which targets the same code with the correct bookkeeping.

Hardware A/B confirmation (revert → kl_div back under threshold) on a 4×H100 devbox is in progress; will update this PR with the before/after numbers.

title: [Feature] Beam search support
author: hnyls2002
body:
Beam search as a per-request feature: `sampling_params.beam_width = k` runs a
k-wide beam and returns the top-`n` sequences, `n` defaulting to 1 as in HF and
the OpenAI API (`n <= k`; `n > 1` returns that many candidates instead of
parallel samples). No server flag; beam and ordinary requests share the same
batches and memory pools.

## Results

`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-Base`, 1x H200, `beam_width = 5000`. End-to-end latency (ms),
mean / p50 / p90:

| output tokens | sync | overlap |
|---|---|---|
| 3   | 244.6 / 158.0 / 469.0 | 259.1 / 176.6 / 470.4 |
| 16  | 927.7 / 1028.8 / 1120.6 | 903.9 / 957.6 / 1361.7 |
| 32  | 1690.7 / 1788.6 / 1827.3 | 1650.9 / 1716.8 / 2003.0 |
| 64  | 3511.0 / 3554.1 / 3697.7 | 3303.3 / 3277.3 / 3506.5 |
| 128 | 8087.3 / 8267.2 / 8655.6 | 7067.0 / 7164.5 / 7201.3 |

`sglang:fwd_occupancy` median under saturated load is 43.7-50.1%, at 67-87%
whole-device utilization.

## Repro

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-Base --port 30000 \
  --dtype bfloat16 --attention-backend flashinfer \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.4 --max-running-requests 20004 \
  --context-length 4096 --random-seed 0 \
  --disable-radix-cache --disable-chunked-prefix-cache
  # add --disable-overlap-schedule for the sync column
```

Drive concurrent `/generate` calls with `{"beam_width": 5000, "n": 5000}`,
sweeping `max_new_tokens`. Per row, `(max_new_tokens, num_requests, qps,
concurrency)`: `(3, 23, 0.8, 4)`, `(16, 10, 0.3, 2)`, `(32, 8, 0.25, 2)`,
`(64, 6, 0.2, 2)`, `(128, 4, 0.15, 2)`.

For the occupancy row, add `SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER=1`,
`--enable-metrics --decode-log-interval 2`, and take the median of
`sglang:fwd_occupancy`. `--decode-log-interval 1` reports `NaN`: the window
resets every batch and never reaches the branch that computes the ratio.

## Verification

- Unit tests (`beam_search`, managers, mem_cache): 2062 passed.
- HF parity (`test/manual/beam_search/test_beam_parity.py`): sequence-set
  overlap 8/10 at `k = 10`.
- Load (`test/manual/beam_search/test_beam_search_load.py`): mixed widths 2-100,
  100 requests at 10 QPS, p50/p90/p99 = 53/58/175 ms; 3200-wide fan-out passes.
- Beam mixed with ordinary penalized requests in the same batches: 36/36.
- Sync and overlap agree digest-for-digest, with
  `SGLANG_ENABLE_STRICT_MEM_CHECK_DURING_BUSY=1` silent throughout.
- Ordinary-path regression: `few_shot_gsm8k` 200q greedy 0.470 unchanged.

## Not supported yet

Rejected at admission with an explicit error: speculative decoding, PD
disaggregation, dp attention, pipeline parallelism, `page_size > 1`,
hierarchical cache, SWA/mamba hybrid caches, hisparse, encoder-decoder,
diffusion LLM, LoRA, sessions, constrained decoding, stop strings/regex,
`min_new_tokens`, `return_logprob`, `return_hidden_states`, and
sampling-mask/routed-experts returns. Beam requests are also excluded from
mixed-chunk prefill batches.

**Retraction.** A beam group cannot be retracted: its member rows alias the
leader's prompt KV, so rolling back part of the group corrupts it. Under KV
pressure ordinary requests are retracted first, and if that is not enough the
whole group is aborted with HTTP 500 instead of being requeued. Admission
reserves the group's `req_to_token` rows but still budgets decode KV at one
token per step, so a large `beam_width` can reach this path under load.

title: [NPU] FIX garbled characters illusion problems, in prefix cache mtp scenarios.
author: McZyWu
body: ## Motivation For NPU, when the input and output reach tens of thousands of tokens, enabling radix cache in MTP scenarios can occasionally cause the illusion of garbled characters. Opening images or using PlanStream will exacerbate this issue. When close radix cache, the above hallucination problem will not occur. ``` export GDN_ATTN_BACKEND_TRITON=1 export ASCEND_USE_FIA=1 export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32 export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=512 export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=3000 export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_ROUND=32 export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_PER_ROUND_TOKENS=3584 export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT=3600 export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1 export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /data/weights/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \ --stream-response-default-include-usage --attention-backend ascend --device npu --tp-size 2 \ --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 16384 --trust-remote-code --host 0.0.0.0 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --port 8898 \ --enable-prefill-delayer --prefill-delayer-max-delay-passes 30 \ --cuda-graph-bs 1 2 4 6 8 10 16 20 24 --max-running-request 24 --context-length 262144 \ --mm-attention-backend ascend_attn --max-mamba-cache-size 120 \ --enable-metrics --enable-multimodal \ --mm-attention-backend ascend_attn --dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ ``` Found some bugs. ## Modifications --CODE-- python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py This modification skips `move_intermediate_cache` when `accept_lens=1`. The principle is as follows: - When `accept_lens=1`, `last_steps=[0]`, and the SSM state at step=0 is the recurrent state that was just calculated. - The model forward has already written it to the correct position, so it doesn't need to be copied again. - The NPU's intermediate_ssm has bfloat16 rounding differences; each copy accumulates error → drift after a long sequence. The intermediate_ssm copy path is only used when `all_step0=False` (when `accept_lens>1`). --- --CODE-- ``` if cache_len is None or cache_len == 0: # Nothing to cache: free KV and mamba slots without inserting # a key_len=0 ghost node into the radix tree. Such empty nodes # poison subsequent match_prefix calls by serving as a stale # mamba COW source with best_value_len=0 (see cache_finished_req # of a short request with no track boundary). Only free the unprotected # part of kv_indices. self.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.free( kv_indices[req.cache_protected_len :] ) self.req_to_token_pool.free_mamba_cache(req) self.dec_lock_ref(req.last_node) return ``` Scenario: The warmup request only has 80 tokens, far less than `mamba_cache_chunk_size=256`, so during the extend phase, `mask=False` — no track checkpoint was ever created, and `mamba_last_track_seqlen` is always `None`. Original code: `cache_len=None` → set to 0 → inserting `key_len=0`, `value_len=0` into the radix tree, creating an empty ghost node. Subsequent requests will match this ghost node in `match_prefix`, with `best_value_len=0` and `mamba_value=yes`, triggering COW to copy a never-correctly-initialized Mamba slot → resulting in garbled characters. This fix: When `cache_len is None` or `cache_len == 0` is detected, directly free the KV and Mamba slot, skipping the radix insert and eliminating the ghost node. This is the correct protection logic. ---- --CODE-- ``` for i, req in enumerate(batch.reqs): if to_track[i] and req.mamba_next_track_idx is not None: req.mamba_next_track_idx = ( pool.get_mamba_ping_pong_other_idx( req.mamba_next_track_idx ) ) ``` In``prepare_mamba_track_for_verify`` , it calls``set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs(batch)`` which rebuilds mamba_track_indices from req objects. But if``req.mamba_next_track_idx`` never gets flipped, then``mamba_track_indices`` stays the same. In decode, the non-spec path flips it in``prepare_for_decode`` . For spec decode, the flip was missing The absence of this flip will cause the same track slot to be repeatedly overwritten. After a boundary crossing, the next verify will write to the same slot that was just committed. ---- ## Accuracy Tests aime qwen3.6-35b--prefix cache--0.9 The above hallucination problem didn't appear after repair. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ``` Serving Benchmark Result Backend: sglang Traffic request rate: inf Max request concurrency: 40 Successful requests: 40 Benchmark duration (s): 48.97 Total input tokens: 2806984 Total input text tokens: 2806984 Total generated tokens: 40960 Total generated tokens (retokenized): 35576 Request throughput (req/s): 0.82 Input token throughput (tok/s): 57316.79 Output token throughput (tok/s): 836.38 Peak output token throughput (tok/s): 1687.00 Peak concurrent requests: 40 Total token throughput (tok/s): 58153.17 Concurrency: 35.60 Accept length: 3.40 ----------------End-to-End Latency---------------- Mean E2E Latency (ms): 43580.33 Median E2E Latency (ms): 43964.78 P90 E2E Latency (ms): 46101.03 P95 E2E Latency (ms): 47670.80 P99 E2E Latency title: Add Inkling model support
author: ch-wan
body:
Supersedes #31358 — rebased on the latest `main`.

## Motivation

Add serving support for the **Inkling** model family — a hybrid-attention Mixture-of-Experts architecture that interleaves sliding-window and full softmax attention with Mamba2 linear-attention layers, an NVFP4-quantized MoE, optional vision/audio multimodal towers, and native multi-token-prediction (MTP) speculative decoding.

## Modifications

- **Model**: `InklingForConditionalGeneration` and its multimodal / MTP-draft variants, registered in the model and architecture maps.
- **Hybrid SWA + Mamba KV cache**: routes Inkling through the hybrid sliding-window / full-attention KV pool and the Mamba2 state cache, with per-layer window and cache sizing. Uses the unified radix tree and extra-buffer Mamba strategy, applied automatically via architecture defaults.
- **MoE**: NVFP4 MoE served through the FlashInfer TRT-LLM routed runner.
- **Multimodal**: optional vision and audio towers with dedicated Inkling image/audio processors; the towers are built only when `--enable-multimodal` is set.
- **Speculative decoding**: multi-layer EAGLE / MTP draft support (chain-style hidden-state propagation, draft-extend window widening).
- **Attention**: FA4 (Blackwell) / Triton backends, selected automatically for the architecture, with MXFP8 KV-cache support on the FA4 path.
- **Kernels**: JIT CUDA kernels for the model's fused paths.
- **Tokenizer / parsers**: tiktoken-based tokenizer wiring (including the turn-final stop token), plus `inkling` reasoning and tool-call parsers.

## Accuracy

Evaluated on the public `thinkingmachines/Inkling-NVFP4` checkpoint (TP8):

| Benchmark | pass@1 |
| --- | --- |
| AIME25 | 95.8% |
| AIME26 | 96.2% |

Multi-token-prediction speculative decoding preserves accuracy (spec-on is within noise of spec-off, at ~3.7-4.1 accepted tokens per verification step). Long-context needle-in-a-haystack retrieval passes to ~880K tokens, and multimodal understanding is validated on MMMU-Pro.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation as needed.

title: [DeepSeek-V4] Fix idle-rank dummy-extend sparse-prefill crash under DP breakable CUDA graph
author: alisonshao
body:
## Problem

`test_deepseek_v4_flash_fp4_b200.py` (base-c b200 deepep, BCG recipe: TP4/DP4/DeepEP, `--enable-mixed-chunk --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`) crashes deterministically on idle DP ranks:

```
_forward_prefill_sparse: assert core_attn_metadata.c4_sparse_raw_indices is not None
AssertionError: sparse-prefill c4 path requires c4_sparse_raw_indices
```

## Root cause

Latent defect from #30898, surfaced by #31487.

Under DP attention + breakable prefill CUDA graph (#30898), an idle rank is padded into a fabricated dummy EXTEND: `forward_batch_info` stashes the real mode in `_original_forward_mode` (IDLE) and sets `forward_mode = EXTEND`. `_get_logical_forward_mode` returns the stale IDLE, so metadata is built via the decode branch (no `c4_sparse_raw_indices`, gated on `is_prefill=True`), while the forward keys off `forward_mode = EXTEND` and runs `_forward_prefill_sparse` (default-on since #29775) → assertion.

Latent since 7-12; #31487 ("avoid excessive prefill CUDA graph padding") then made DP prefill land on the small capture buckets (4/16) where the dummy extend actually fires, flipping the job green→red (bisected: last green `0ad0ff2e9e`, first red `216b750c`).

## Fix

Build metadata for the mode the forward actually runs: when `forward_mode == EXTEND`, return it instead of the stale `_original_forward_mode`, so extend metadata is built and `c4_sparse_raw_indices` is allocated. The fabricated batch already carries valid extend fields. `TARGET_VERIFY` overwrites (MTP hybrid SSM) still prefer `_original_forward_mode`.

## Validation

Reproduced + fixed on a 4×B200 devbox at `216b750c` (exact BCG args, shipped code): before, crashes under load (idle ranks DP1/2/3); after, 204/204 requests OK, 0 assertions. Crash/liveness verified under synthetic load; gsm8k accuracy left to CI.

title: [AMD] Fix DeepSeek-V4 fused-RMS FP8 scale metadata on gfx950
author: hdt98
body:
> [!NOTE]
> Exact two-node TP8/DP8/EP8 MORI validation remains pending; the closest available TP4/DP4/EP4 results are below.

## Motivation

Fixes #31490. DeepSeek-V4-Flash FP8/FP4 on gfx950/ROCm 7.2 regressed from the ~0.925 GSM8K band to ~0.912 in the 1P1D DP-attention workload.

## Root Cause

DeepSeek-V4's separate fused-RMS FP8 producer calls AITER with `transpose_scale=True`. AITER writes CK-ready transposed scale storage but returns contiguous-looking `[M, G]` metadata. For logical scales `[[a,b,c],[d,e,f]]`, the storage is `[a,d,b,e,c,f]`; it needs stride `(1, M)`, while contiguous metadata reads it as `[[a,d,b],[e,c,f]]`.

The CK materializer added by #29275 trusted that metadata, associating valid scales with the wrong token/group cells when `M > 1`. Real-AITER A/B tests show bit-identical FP8 activations, an unchanged BF16 side output, and exact logical
scales after the zero-copy stride repair with the same storage pointer. `M = 1` remains exactly unchanged. This tuple is injected only into DeepSeek-V4 attention-side dense GEMMs.

My thought is this points toward batch dependence and excludes wholesale activation corruption, but it was my mistake in not covering this case: a scale permutation can still cause a large GEMM error. The ~1–2 GSM8K-point effect is the measured end-to-end result, not a bound.

The  #31490's `TP == DP` topology has attention TP size one. A matching TP4/DP4/EP4 trace that I was able to run saw zero attention gathers and CK in all 240 relevant GEMMs, excluding the initially suspected Triton/collective path from this issue.

## Modifications

- Restore truthful `[M, G]` strides at the DeepSeek-V4 AITER producer with a zero-copy view.
- Test exact values, strides, storage aliasing, and decode-like/batched shapes with CPU and real AITER.

The shared DeepSeekV2/GLM producers, generic CK materializer, communicator, and Triton path are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

DeepSeek-V4-Flash, two MI35x nodes, 1P1D TP4/DP4/EP4 per role, MORI, 8-shot GSM8K (1319 questions):

| Configuration | Stock | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| FP8, current CK | 0.919 | 0.921 / 0.927 |
| FP8, CK #8639 | 0.913 | 0.928 |
| FP4, current CK | 0.911 / 0.912 | 0.924 / 0.930 / 0.930 |

The stochastic runs show recovery and compatibility with current and future CK #8639.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Controlled candidate/stock; same model, topology, image, warm-ups, and 1024-token input/output workload:

| Concurrency | TPOT (lower is better) | Output throughput |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | +0.187% | -0.295% |
| 16 | -1.203% | +1.174% |
| 32 | -1.047% | +1.014% |

No TPOT or output-throughput regression was observed.

## Checklist

- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` passed.
- [x] CPU and registered real-operator tests added.
- [x] Accuracy and speed results included.
- [x] No user-facing API/configuration or documentation change.
- [x] Forward-path change is code-style-compliant and zero-copy.

Exact TP8/DP8/EP8 MORI remains the final integration validation gate before merge.

title: Fix stop boundaries for grammar-constrained speculative decoding
author: windscope
body:
## Summary

Run existing stop-string and stop-token checks before using grammar termination as the finish fallback. This preserves the earliest registered stop boundary when speculative decoding accepts multiple tokens.

## Root cause

Previously, Req.update_finish_state used this ordering:

    max length
    -> grammar terminated: use last token and return
    -> stop-string checks
    -> stop-token/EOS checks

The grammar return therefore skipped normal stop handling. This was effectively harmless for single-token decoding because the grammar terminal token was also the last accepted token.

Grammar-constrained speculative decoding exposes the incorrect assumption that the last accepted token is always the finish boundary.

    registered stop token: STOP
    newly accepted tokens: [STOP, EOS]
    grammar terminated: true

| Result | Old behavior | Correct behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| matched token | EOS (the last token) | STOP (the first registered stop) |
| finished_len | unset | immediately after STOP |
| emitted accepted suffix | [STOP, EOS] | [STOP] |

## Fix

Use this ordering instead:

    max length
    -> stop-string checks
    -> stop-token/EOS checks
    -> grammar termination fallback

The token checker scans newly accepted tokens from left to right, matches STOP before EOS, and sets finished_len at that boundary. output_ids_through_stop then excludes the trailing EOS. Grammar termination remains available when no normal stop condition matches.

The regression covers both request stop_token_ids and tokenizer additional_stop_token_ids.

## Tests

- pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/test_grammar_stop_speculative.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_stop_str_speculative.py (11 passed)
- pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_grammar_stop_speculative.py

title: [AMD] Enable mamba JIT transfer kernel on ROCm (fix transfer_kv_mamba NameError)
author: kangwangamd
body:
## Problem

The mamba KV-cache JIT transfer kernel (`transfer_kv_mamba_pf_lf` / `transfer_kv_mamba_lf_pf`) is gated to CUDA only, so on ROCm the symbols are never imported. The nightly AMD kernel job (`nightly-*-1-gpu-kernel`, `test/registered/jit/test_transfer_mamba.py`) has been red every run with `NameError: transfer_kv_mamba_lf_pf` (12 subtests) — first seen Jul-16, never-passed on AMD.

## Root cause (two parts)

1. **Import guard.** In `memory_pool_host.py` the mamba JIT import is under `if _is_cuda:` only, while the `sgl_kernel.kvcacheio` import one line above already uses `if _is_cuda or _is_hip:`. On ROCm the two symbols never bind → `NameError` when `MambaPoolHost` drives the `io_backend="kernel"` path.
2. **Runtime device check.** Widening the guard alone is **not** enough: `transfer_mamba.cuh` hardcodes `.with_device<kDLCUDA>()` in three `TensorMatcher`s, which rejects a `rocm:` tensor at runtime:
   ```
   RuntimeError: Tensor match failed ... Device value [rocm:0] not in allowed options: [cuda]
     at transfer_mamba.cuh:151
   ```
   The HIP-enabled sibling `hicache.cuh` avoids this by using the portable **`kDLGPU`** alias (`jit_kernel/include/sgl_kernel/utils.cuh` maps `kDLGPU = kDLCUDA` on CUDA and `kDLGPU = kDLROCM` on HIP).

## Fix

- `memory_pool_host.py`: `if _is_cuda:` → `if _is_cuda or _is_hip:` for the `transfer_mamba` import.
- `transfer_mamba.cuh` (×3): `with_device<kDLCUDA>` → `with_device<kDLGPU>`.

Both mirror patterns already used by the HIP-enabled `hicache.cuh`. This *enables* the kernel on ROCm rather than skipping the test.

## Offline validation — MI300X (gfx942), hipcc 7.2, torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2

Because the JIT kernel + device check are device-independent, I validated on a real MI300X:

| Step | Stock (CUDA-only) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `_jit_transfer_mamba_module()` build under hipcc | (symbols never imported on ROCm) | **BUILD_OK** — compiles + loads, both symbols bound |
| Runtime device match on a `rocm:0` tensor | `RuntimeError: Device value [rocm:0] not in allowed options: [cuda]` | accepted |
| Backup `lf→pf` (all layers) roundtrip | — | **bit-exact** |
| Load `pf→lf` (per layer) roundtrip | — | **bit-exact** |

Roundtrip config: 4 layers, 256-byte items, 8 pages, 3 indices; device layer-first buffers backed up to a page-first host buffer and loaded back, compared element-wise → `ALL_PASS`.

## Scope / safety

Guarded by `_is_hip` / the portable `kDLGPU` alias, so CUDA behavior is unchanged (`kDLGPU == kDLCUDA` on nvcc). No change to kernel math or launch logic. Fixes R270.

title: [NPU] Fix LLaDA2 MoE OOM after the FRACTAL_NZ cast, re-enabling the NZ speedup
author: wenxuewuhd
body: ## Motivation Loading LLaDA2 on NPU with the FRACTAL_NZ weight cast enabled roughly doubles MoE weight memory, and on a 64 GB 910B3 the server fails to start at all. `LLaDA2MoeModelLM.load_weights` ended by building `self.routed_experts_weights_of_layer` from `LLaDA2MoeSparseMoeBlock.get_moe_weights()`, which snapshots `x.data` — a separate Tensor object sharing the Parameter's storage — for every expert weight. That snapshot is taken *before* `process_weights_after_loading` runs, so when the NZ cast rebinds `weight.data` to the newly allocated NZ tensor, the map still holds a handle on the ND storage and its refcount never reaches zero. Every MoE weight then stays resident in both layouts. Verified by walking the referrer graph during a real model load: immediately after the cast, exactly one live tensor still shares the pre-cast storage — same shape, not a Parameter, reachable from the dict key `routed_experts_weights_of_layer`. For LLaDA2.0-mini (19 MoE layers, w13 1 GiB + w2 0.5 GiB each) that pins an extra 28.5 GiB. Measured on TP1 / 910B3 with the CI test's config (`--mem-fraction-static 0.9`, NZ cast on): | | weights | load time | result | |---|---|---|---| | before | 59.03 GB | 73.9 s | `ValueError: loaded weights leave no GPU memory for the KV cache` | | after | 30.45 GB | 38.4 s | KV cache 628736 tokens, server starts, GSM8K 0.93 | The LLaDA2-mini CI test has been masking the symptom with `SGLANG_NPU_DISABLE_ACL_FORMAT_WEIGHT=1`, which also gives up the NZ kernel's speedup. ## Modifications **1. Build the map lazily (`models/llada2.py`)** Wrapped `routed_experts_weights_of_layer` in `LazyValue`, deferring it until EPLB actually asks for it — which is after weight processing. This matches the existing pattern in `qwen3_moe.py` and `sdar_moe.py` (and `deepseek_v2.py`, which exposes it through a property). The dict comprehension and its filters are unchanged; only the evaluation point moves. This also fixes a latent correctness bug that is not NPU-specific: with the eager build, any backend whose `process_weights_after_loading` rebinds `weight.data` left the map pointing at storage the model no longer uses, so EPLB expert relocation would have written into dead tensors. Built lazily, the map aliases the live post-processing weights. **2. Drop the kill switch from the CI test (`test/registered/ascend/basic_function/dllm/test_npu_llada2_mini.py`)** With the OOM fixed, `SGLANG_NPU_DISABLE_ACL_FORMAT_WEIGHT=1` is unnecessary and the NZ cast is re-enabled. An aligned single-denoise-iteration profile on LLaDA2.1-mini (decode trajectories verified identical, 556 device kernels and 38 GroupedMatmul calls per side, identical input shapes) shows the cast is also a small win at the kernel level: | | ND | NZ | | |---|---|---|---| | MoE GroupedMatmul | 8305.9 us | 7697.8 us | 1.08x (38/38 calls faster) | | whole-step kernels | 13308.2 us | 12736.0 us | 1.045x | NZ dispatches to `aclnnGroupedMatmulWeightNz` instead of `aclnnGroupedMatmulV5`, and no `TransData` appears, so there is no runtime format-conversion penalty. The whole `env` override is removed rather than just the one key: it replaced `GSM8KAscendMixin.env` wholesale, so the test was also running without the mixin defaults (`PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF`, `HCCL_BUFFSIZE`, and the rest). That was *not* the cause of the OOM — both runs in the table above had `PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF` unset — just an unrelated papercut fixed in passing. ## Note `bailing_moe.py` and `sarvam_moe.py` still build this map eagerly and have the same latent issue. They are left alone here since I have no way to validate a change to them. ## Accuracy/Speed Tests and Profiling **Accuracy and Speed Test: LLaDA 2.1-mini GSM8K zero shot first 200** **Before** Total latency: 182.875 s Score: 0.890 Output throughput: 242.947 token/s [METRIC] gsm8k_score=0.89 labels={"model": "/workspace/models/LLaDA/LLaDA2.1-mini/", "eval": "gsm8k"} [METRIC] gsm8k_latency=182.87526191899087 labels={"model": "/workspace/models/LLaDA/LLaDA2.1-mini/", "eval": "gsm8k"} **After** Total latency: 169.541 s Score: 0.890 Output throughput: 262.055 token/s [METRIC] gsm8k_score=0.89 labels={"model": "/workspace/models/LLaDA/LLaDA2.1-mini/", "eval": "gsm8k"} [METRIC] gsm8k_latency=169.54097811097745 labels={"model": "/workspace/models/LLaDA/LLaDA2.1-mini/", "eval": "gsm8k"} **Profiling** **Before** **After** ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. title: [Fix][AMD] Qwen3.5 MoE: disable global-slot shared-expert fusion under per-rank EP backends (MoRI + dp-attention init crash)
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #31336.

Serving **Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8** (512 routed + 1 fused shared expert) with `--moe-a2a-backend mori --enable-dp-attention` on MI355X/ROCm crashes at model init. Every scheduler rank aborts in `FusedMoE.__init__`:

```
File ".../srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 227, ...
    assert (num_experts - num_shared_slots) % self.moe_ep_size == 0
AssertionError
```

With `--enable-dp-attention`, `moe_ep_size` is promoted to `tp_size` (8). `has_per_rank_fused_shared_slots()` is `True` for MoRI (deepep-class), so `num_shared_slots = 1 * 8 = 8`, and `(513 - 8) % 8 = 505 % 8 = 1 != 0`.

### Root cause (and why the layout matters)

MoRI's dispatcher (`token_dispatcher/moriep.py`) masks experts with a **contiguous per-rank block**: `expert_mask[ep_rank * num_local_experts : + num_local_experts] = 1`. This is valid only when the blocks tile the id space exactly, i.e. `num_experts == num_local_experts * ep_size`, which requires **per-rank** shared slots (one shared slot per EP rank). DeepSeek-V2 already builds `num_experts` this way for per-rank backends.

Qwen's shared-expert fusion, however, is a **global-slot** design: `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock` constructs its `TopK` **without** `num_fused_shared_experts` (so the per-rank remap in `topk.py` never fires) and instead appends the shared expert manually at a **single global id** (`_append_shared_to_topk_output`, base id `N == num_experts`) with a **per-token `shared_expert_gate`**. This global-slot-with-gate layout cannot be expressed in MoRI's per-rank contiguous tiling, and it can't reuse DeepSeek's (gate-less) per-rank remap machinery.

The alternative floated in the issue — treating MoRI as "global" (`num_shared_slots = 1`) — passes the `__init__` assertion but then breaks MoRI's contiguous dispatch mask (`num_local_experts * ep_size = 65 * 8 = 520 != 513`, so rank 7's block runs out of bounds) and silently misroutes experts.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2_moe.py`: when shared-expert fusion is enabled **and** a per-rank EP shared-slot backend is active (`uses_per_rank_fused_shared_slots()`) **and** `moe_ep_size > 1`, disable the fusion and fall back to the separate (correct) shared-expert MLP path. A one-time warning is logged. `moe_ep_size == 1` and non-per-rank backends are unaffected (fusion stays on).

This is the correct-by-construction fix: with fusion off, `num_experts = 512` tiles exactly (`64 * 8`), the shared expert is computed by the dense `shared_expert` MLP (with its gate) and added after the experts. The fully-fused per-rank shared expert with a per-token gate is a larger enablement task (needs a per-rank remap+append kernel that also applies the gate) and is left as follow-up.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K sweep on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 (MI355X), **with this PR applied** so the MoRI configs get past the #31336 init crash. Flags added one at a time. `Accuracy` = correct fraction, `Invalid` = unparseable/garbage fraction.

```
┌─────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────┬─────────┬───────────────┐
│ Run │                Added flag                 │ Accuracy │ Invalid │    Verdict    │
├─────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼─────────┼───────────────┤
│ R0  │ (baseline)                                │    0.925 │   0.005 │ ✓             │
├─────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼─────────┼───────────────┤
│ R1  │ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3                 │    0.915 │   0.010 │ clean         │
├─────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼─────────┼───────────────┤
│ R2  │ --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head │    0.935 │   0.000 │ clean         │
├─────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼─────────┼───────────────┤
│ R3  │ --moe-a2a-backend mori                    │    0.010 │   0.420 │ ← breaks      │
├─────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼─────────┼───────────────┤
│ R4  │ mori + fp8-KV                             │    0.010 │   0.455 │ breaks (mori) │
├─────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼─────────┼───────────────┤
│ R5  │ full (dp-attn + mori + fp8-KV)            │    0.000 │   0.415 │ breaks (mori) │
└─────┴───────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────┴─────────┴───────────────┘
```

Reading:
- **This PR's scope (init crash) is resolved:** the MoRI + dp-attention configs now load and run instead of aborting in `FusedMoE.__init__`.
- **No regression on the clean paths:** baseline (R0), fp8-KV (R1), and `--enable-dp-attention` alone (R2, **0.935**) are all healthy. R2 is the path this PR most directly enables and it is clean.
- **A separate MoRI issue remains:** every run that adds `--moe-a2a-backend mori` (R3/R4/R5) collapses to ~0.01 accuracy with a high invalid rate, **independent of dp-attention and of fp8-KV**. That is a MoRI all-to-all correctness problem, **out of scope for this init-crash fix** and tracked separately (likely part of the ROCm-MoRI enablement in #21886). This PR is a prerequisite that lets that issue be reached and debugged at all.

Assertion-level validation (mocked MoRI, `ep_size=8`): pre-fix `num_experts=513, num_shared_slots=8` → assertion fails; with fix, fusion disabled → `num_experts=512, num_shared_slots=0` → assertion passes and MoRI's contiguous mask tiles `[0, 512)` exactly. `ep_size==1` and non-per-rank backends keep fusion (no behavior change).

## Checklist

- [x] Format with `pre-commit run --all-files` (isort/ruff/black pass)
- [x] Linked the issue (#31336)
- [x] Added a clear explanation of the root cause and the tradeoff

title: [AMD][Fix] Qwen3.5: guard zero-grid launch in fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm(_with_gate) (HIP invalid configuration on idle DP rank)
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

Bringing up **Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8** with MoRI expert-parallel all-to-all (`--moe-a2a-backend mori`) and `--enable-dp-attention` on MI355X/ROCm surfaces three connected failures. This PR fixes the two that live in the model / idle-rank path (bug #2 and bug #3 below); bug #1 is the prerequisite init fix already handled in #31793.

**Bug #1 — Qwen shared-expert fusion vs. per-rank EP layout (prerequisite, fixed in #31793).** Qwen uses a single global shared-expert slot with a per-token gate, while MoRI / DeepEP-family backends use per-rank expert slots. The mismatch trips a model-init assertion / mis-maps the shared-expert id. #31793 disables the global-slot shared-expert fusion under per-rank EP backends. It must be applied for the model to load past init.

**Bug #2 — idle DP-attention ranks launch zero-sized grids (fixes #31350, #31594).** Under DP attention an active rank may hold e.g. 80 tokens while the other DP ranks hold 0. Many Triton/AITER kernels grid on the token count, so an empty rank launches with grid `(0, ...)`. CUDA tolerates a zero-sized grid as a no-op; **HIP rejects it with `invalid configuration argument`** (surfacing asynchronously later, e.g. during decode CUDA-graph capture / the Mamba allocator).

```
File ".../srt/models/utils.py", in fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_with_gate
    _fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_gate_kernel[(q_rows,)](...)   # grid == (0,)
torch.AcceleratorError: HIP error: invalid configuration argument
```

**Bug #3 — MoRI was misrouted through the plain TP-MoE path (root-cause collective fix).** `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock` only took the EP dispatch/combine path for `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep()`. MoRI uses EP dispatch/combine but is not `.is_deepep()`, so it fell into the ordinary TP path and ran a `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce()` **after** combine. Combine already returns each token to its source rank, so the trailing all-reduce mixed mismatched per-rank shapes — active rank `[80, 4096]` vs. idle rank `[0, 4096]` — a heterogeneous collective that crashes or deadlocks custom all-reduce.

## Modifications

**MoRI routed through the EP path — `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2_moe.py`** (three `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep()` → `is_deepep_class_backend()` swaps, kept together):
- Shared expert built with TP1 (`tp_rank=0, tp_size=1`) so each source rank computes its full shared-expert output locally, matching the DeepEP/MoRI dispatch/combine model.
- EP metadata (`ep_size`, full expert count, `top_k`) initialized for MoRI instead of plain TP-MoE metadata.
- `forward()` dispatches to `_forward_deepep()` for MoRI, so combine returns tokens to the source rank and the block no longer falls into `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce()` — eliminating the `[80,4096]` vs `[0,4096]` heterogeneous all-reduce.

**Idle-rank zero-grid guards** (all are rank-local computations with no cross-rank collective, so an early empty return is safe):
- `python/sglang/srt/models/utils.py` — `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm` and `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_with_gate` return the already-allocated, correctly-shaped empty outputs when `q_rows == 0` (fixes #31350).
- `python/sglang/jit_kernel/triton/gdn_fused_proj.py` — `fused_qkvzba_split_reshape_cat`, `..._contiguous`, and `fused_qkv_split_gdn_prefill` skip the kernel launch on empty batch, returning the pre-shaped empty tensors.
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py` — GatedDeltaNet decode/prefill return an empty `[1, 0, num_v_heads, head_v_dim]` before entering `causal_conv1d_fn` / `chunk_gated_delta_rule` on an empty batch (fixes #31594).
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py` — return an empty token-id tensor when `logits.shape[0] == 0` instead of launching greedy/softmax/sampling kernels on a 0-row batch.

Non-empty behavior on every path is unchanged (each guard is a single `== 0` check before the launch).

## Accuracy Tests

E2E on MI355X/ROCm with the full failing stack — Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, `--moe-a2a-backend mori`, `--enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head`, `--tp-size 4 --dp-size 4`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--attention-backend aiter` (repro: `repro_bug23_fp8.sh`):

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Server bring-up (CUDA-graph capture + warmup) | crash: HIP `invalid configuration argument` | completes, `/health` 200 |
| MoRI combine all-reduce | `[80,4096]` vs `[0,4096]` crash/deadlock | no heterogeneous all-reduce |
| **gsm8k accuracy** | — (server never served) | **0.94** |

Unit-level (fused QK-RMSNorm guard):
- **Non-empty (seq=5):** fixed outputs are bit-exact (`max_abs_diff == 0.0`) vs an eager GemmaRMSNorm reference for `q_out`/`k_out`, and the deinterleaved `gate_out` matches exactly.
- **Empty (seq=0):** both functions return the correct empty shapes (`(0, head_dim)`) without launching the kernel.

## Benchmarking

No perf-relevant change on the hot path: every guard is a single `== 0` check and non-empty launches are untouched; the MoRI change only selects the already-existing `_forward_deepep()` path instead of the TP path for MoRI.

## Checklist

- [x] Format with `pre-commit run --all-files` (isort/ruff/black/codespell pass)
- [x] Linked the issues (#31350, #31594); prerequisite init fix #31793
- [x] Guards applied to all sibling functions (QK-RMSNorm, GDN proj, GDN backend, sampler)
- [x] E2E verified: server serves and gsm8k = 0.94 with MoRI + DP-attention

title: [Quant] Support NVFP4_AWQ checkpoints in ModelOpt FP4 path
author: kfhfar
body:
Load and run ModelOpt NVFP4_AWQ checkpoints, which share the NVFP4 weight
  layout plus a per-input-channel pre_quant_scale that AWQ folds into the
  weights offline.

  - Accept NVFP4_AWQ in the quant_algo allowlist; set is_awq on the config.
  - Register a per-input-channel pre_quant_scale param for AWQ layers and apply it to activations before fp4_quantize (non-AWQ layers unaffected).
  - Default group_size to 16 on the flat config.json path, which ModelOpt's AWQ export omits (present only in nested hf_quant_config.json).
  - Add unit coverage for AWQ config parsing.

title: Support a same-size mixed q dtype in the fused RoPE kernels
author: pranjalssh
body:
## Motivation

Some fused QK-norm implementations emit q in a different (same-size) dtype than k — e.g. fp16 q while k stays bf16. The fused RoPE JIT kernels previously assumed a single dtype for q/k, and `RadixAttention` sized its extend output buffer off `q.dtype`, so a mixed-dtype q would change the dtype the attention backend writes.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/elementwise/rope.cuh`: factor the per-head rotation into `rope_rotate_head<T, ...>` and give `fused_rope_kernel` / `fused_rope_store_kernel` a separate `QDType` template parameter (same-size dtypes only, enforced with a `static_assert`). k/v and the KV caches keep `DType`. The k branch of the store kernel now passes the cache pointer into the shared helper instead of duplicating the rotation code.
- `python/sglang/jit_kernel/rope.py`: key the JIT module off both `k.dtype` and `q.dtype`.
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py`: size the extend attention output buffer off `v.dtype` (the model dtype) when v is present, so a mixed-dtype q does not change the backend output dtype. The existing fp8→bf16 clamp for mxfp8 KV-cache attention is preserved (now applied to the v-derived dtype as well).
- `test/registered/jit/test_rope.py`: bitwise tests that the mixed-dtype kernels (fp16 q + bf16 k) match the corresponding single-dtype kernels exactly — q vs the all-fp16 kernel, k/k_cache/v_cache vs the all-bf16 kernel, for both the in-place and the fused KV-store paths.

The all-same-dtype instantiations are unchanged (the q/k branches keep one instruction stream per instantiation; the helper is predicated on the cache pointer).

## Testing

- `test/registered/jit/test_rope.py` (including the new mixed-dtype tests) passed on an internal setup with the equivalent change; the registered CI suites cover it here.
- Formatting validated with the pinned pre-commit tool versions (black 26.1.0, isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1, clang-format 20.1.7).

title: fix(diffusion): keep fused qk-norm-rope out of dynamo tracing
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

With `torch.compile` enabled (e.g. `performance_mode=speed`), every qwen-image request fails with HTTP 500:

```
torch._dynamo.exc.AsPythonConstantNotImplementedError: SymNodeVariable() is not a constant
```

`can_use_fused_inplace_qknorm_rope` is decorated with `@torch.compiler.assume_constant_result`, but the qwen call sites pass `head_dim=img_query.shape[-1]` / `rope_dim=cos_sin_cache.size(-1)`, which become SymInts under dynamo tracing; `assume_constant_result` cannot fold SymInt arguments (wrapping in `int()` does not help — dynamo keeps them symbolic).

## Modifications

- Gate the fused inplace qk-norm-rope path with `not torch.compiler.is_compiling()`. Under compile, the unfused path is traced and inductor fuses it on its own; the handwritten fused kernel remains active for eager.
- Pass the static `self.head_dim` at the two qwen-image call sites instead of a runtime shape.

## Test

On 2×H100 (Qwen-Image-2512, 1024x1024, 50 steps, ulysses=2, torch.compile on): requests return 500 before this change and 200 after, with the compile path serving normally.

title: perf(diffusion): CUDA-IPC zero-staging all-to-all for 2-rank Ulysses
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

At ulysses degree 2 on one node, every transformer layer pays 4 NCCL all-to-alls (separate q/k/v input A2As + the output A2A). Each one costs a rendezvous plus multiple full-tensor staging copies (transpose/contiguous/cat on both sides). Profiling qwen-image showed the A2A data plane — not the transfer itself — dominating the communication cost.

## Modifications

The 2-rank Ulysses A2A family runs over a CUDA-IPC transport (new `device_communicators/ipc_a2a.py`), **opt-in via `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_IPC_A2A=1`**. The gate is narrow — 2 ranks, peer-to-peer access, a successful JIT build — and every failure falls back to NCCL, so no other topology is affected:

- **Local-context peer mapping**: each rank re-opens the peer's staging IPC handle in its *own* device context (vLLM custom-allreduce style), so all accesses are same-device semantics over NVLink.
- **GPU-side sync**: a sequence counter with a `bump_signal`/`spin_wait` kernel pair replaces the NCCL rendezvous; the transport is CUDA-graph capturable. Double-buffered slots alternate per call; slot reuse is ordered by the intervening wait.
- **One sync for q/k/v**: the three input A2As of an attention collapse into a single exchange.
- **Zero staging for qwen joint attention**: a segmented variant reads the (txt, img) projections directly in `join_seqs` layout, and the staging buffer *is* the gathered q/k/v — likewise for the output A2A's gathered result. The per-layer joint cats and all intermediate gather copies disappear: each byte moves exactly once, from projection output to the peer's consumption buffer.

**Coverage**: the `usp.py` hooks serve the whole USPAttention family (qwen, flux, flux_2, zimage, wan, mova, cosmos3, ernie, glm, helios, joy, ideogram, krea2, lingbot, ltx_2) with no per-model wiring; a second commit routes `AllToAll4D` through the same exchange, covering the stacked-qkv UlyssesAttention users (hunyuanvideo, wan-VSA, zimage's secondary attention). Fallback to the NCCL path on any init failure (no P2P access, >2 ranks, capture in progress) and for all other topologies.

Both paths are **2-rank only** (single-node ulysses=2 / tp=2), and the rank-scaling section below shows that is the right boundary rather than a stopgap: measured at 4 ranks, this scheme loses to NCCL.

## Benchmark

2×H100 ulysses=2, 50 steps, fixed seed, steady-state; FCG = #31852 enabled.

**Qwen-Image-2512 1024×1024** (per-feature ladder, experimental tree):

| config | ms/step | e2e |
|---|---|---|
| NCCL A2A | 81.3 | 4.41s |
| + IPC transport | 79.6 | 4.22s |
| + single-sync qkv | 77.5 | 4.15s |
| + zero-staging segmented (input+output) | **64.8** | **3.95s** |

**PR stack as-is on latest main (PR #31849 + #31852 + this)**: eager 4.505-4.565s → full stack **3.929-3.950s (64.5 ms/step)**; IPC alone (no CUDA graph) 4.074-4.092s. Output bitwise-identical to the NCCL path in every configuration (same b64 md5).

**FLUX.1-dev 1024×1024** (zero per-model wiring, generic hooks only): eager 4.858s → **4.447-4.463s (-8.4%)**, output bitwise-identical.

Microbench for the 38MB qkv shape: 360µs (NCCL, incl. staging) → 272µs in-graph.

## Rank scaling: why this stays 2-rank

A standalone microbenchmark, independent of the code here, so a positive result
would have doubled as a clean N-rank reference: each rank writes its chunk into
every peer's mapped staging buffer (`R-1` remote writes plus one local),
publishes a sequence number into every peer's flag, and spins until all peers
have published — the shipped 2-rank structure, generalised, with peer access
enabled for *every* peer. Baseline is `dist.all_to_all_single` on the same
buffers. 4×H100 single node NVLink; 10 warmup then 30 iterations of
`barrier(); synchronize(); t0; exchange(); synchronize()`, median reported; every
configuration's IPC result checked against the NCCL result with `torch.equal`
(all passed).

IPC latency relative to NCCL, higher is better for IPC:

| ranks | 1 MB | 4 MB | 16 MB |
|---|---|---|---|
| **R=2** | 1.00x | 1.05x | **1.19x** |
| **R=4** | **0.69x** | **0.75x** | **0.78x** |

At 4 ranks the scheme is **25-45% slower**. Its cost is linear in rank count on
two axes NCCL amortises: `R-1` separate `copy_` calls, each its own scheduling
and copy-engine event where NCCL fuses all peers into one kernel's channels, and
`R-1` flags polled serially in the wait kernel. At R=2 both collapse to a single
remote write and a single flag.

This also corrects the attribution of the numbers above: **the win is not faster
byte movement** — even at R=2 the raw transfer is only 1.00-1.19x. It comes from
what surrounds 120 exchanges per step (NCCL's per-op launch and protocol
overhead removed, three exchanges folded into one, the post-exchange gather copy
eliminated) and, above all, from being CUDA-graph capturable: a captured NCCL
collective bakes a per-op sequence number and deadlocks on replay, which is why
the full-forward graph in #31852 needs this transport to work at all on more
than one GPU.

Side result: the illegal memory access that broke an earlier N-rank attempt is
explained — `cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess(1 - dev, 0)` hardcodes the 2-rank peer,
so with R>2 a kernel dereferencing a third device's mapping faults. The generic
implementation above enables peer access for all peers and is correct at R=4. It
is not worth landing, since generalisation does not pay.

Method note: the first version of this benchmark timed 50 iterations with a
single sync at the end, which measures launch-queue throughput rather than
per-call latency and produced non-monotonic output (NCCL R=4: 1MB 0.018 → 4MB
0.116 → 16MB 0.066 ms). Spin-flag sync also passes trivially when the flag is
already at or above the target, so a broken protocol yields fast wrong numbers
instead of an error — hence the per-call sync and the correctness check.

## Robustness

Both were prerequisites for ever making this the default:

- **The spin is bounded.** `spin_wait` was an unbounded `while (*flag < t) {}`,
  so any rank-asymmetric call sequence parked the stream with no diagnostic —
  exactly how the full-graph deadlock presented (both ranks in
  `graph.replay()`, only `py-spy` showed where). It now spins against a
  `clock64` deadline, records a device-side flag on expiry and returns; the host
  reads that flag at each request boundary, outside any capture where a device
  read is legal, and falls back to NCCL for the rest of the process. A desync
  degrades instead of wedging the server. The deadline is converted with the max
  SM clock, so under a power cap the real budget only comes out longer, which is
  the safe direction for a watchdog.
- **Staging is bounded.** Buffers were keyed by `(n_local, n_peer, dtype)` and
  never freed, so a server handling several resolutions kept accumulating pairs
  (~38MB each for qwen 1024² at two slots). Now an `OrderedDict` with a cap and
  oldest-first eviction. Eviction drops a buffer the peer still maps, so it has
  to be the same key on both ranks — they insert and touch keys in the same
  order, and the code says so.

Tunable via `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_IPC_A2A_TIMEOUT_MS` (200) and
`SGLANG_DIFFUSION_IPC_A2A_MAX_BUFFERS` (16).

- **The path is covered by CI.** `test/single_test_file/test_ipc_a2a_2_gpu.py`
  (2-gpu suite) runs the A2A family twice per shape, once over NCCL and once
  over IPC, and requires identical bytes; it also walks a capped staging cache
  through eviction. It asserts the transport *engaged* (initialised, not failed,
  staging populated) rather than only that the two arms agreed — otherwise a
  silent double fallback would pass while testing nothing. Measured 30s on
  2xH100, `IPC_A2A_PARITY PASS (staged keys=6)`.

title: [NPU] FIX garbled characters illusion problems, in prefix cache mtp scenarios.
author: McZyWu
body: ## Motivation For NPU, when the input and output reach tens of thousands of tokens, enabling radix cache in MTP scenarios can occasionally cause the illusion of garbled characters. Opening images or using PlanStream will exacerbate this issue. When close radix cache, the above hallucination problem will not occur. ``` export GDN_ATTN_BACKEND_TRITON=1 export ASCEND_USE_FIA=1 export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32 export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=512 export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=3000 export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_ROUND=32 export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_PER_ROUND_TOKENS=3584 export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT=3600 export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1 export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /data/weights/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \ --stream-response-default-include-usage --attention-backend ascend --device npu --tp-size 2 \ --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 16384 --trust-remote-code --host 0.0.0.0 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --port 8898 \ --enable-prefill-delayer --prefill-delayer-max-delay-passes 30 \ --cuda-graph-bs 1 2 4 6 8 10 16 20 24 --max-running-request 24 --context-length 262144 \ --mm-attention-backend ascend_attn --max-mamba-cache-size 120 \ --enable-metrics --enable-multimodal \ --mm-attention-backend ascend_attn --dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ ``` Found some bugs. ## Modifications --CODE-- python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py This modification skips `move_intermediate_cache` when `accept_lens=1`. The principle is as follows: - When `accept_lens=1`, `last_steps=[0]`, and the SSM state at step=0 is the recurrent state that was just calculated. - The model forward has already written it to the correct position, so it doesn't need to be copied again. - The NPU's intermediate_ssm has bfloat16 rounding differences; each copy accumulates error → drift after a long sequence. The intermediate_ssm copy path is only used when `all_step0=False` (when `accept_lens>1`). --- --CODE-- ``` if cache_len is None or cache_len == 0: # Nothing to cache: free KV and mamba slots without inserting # a key_len=0 ghost node into the radix tree. Such empty nodes # poison subsequent match_prefix calls by serving as a stale # mamba COW source with best_value_len=0 (see cache_finished_req # of a short request with no track boundary). Only free the unprotected # part of kv_indices. self.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.free( kv_indices[req.cache_protected_len :] ) self.req_to_token_pool.free_mamba_cache(req) self.dec_lock_ref(req.last_node) return ``` Scenario: The warmup request only has 80 tokens, far less than `mamba_cache_chunk_size=256`, so during the extend phase, `mask=False` — no track checkpoint was ever created, and `mamba_last_track_seqlen` is always `None`. Original code: `cache_len=None` → set to 0 → inserting `key_len=0`, `value_len=0` into the radix tree, creating an empty ghost node. Subsequent requests will match this ghost node in `match_prefix`, with `best_value_len=0` and `mamba_value=yes`, triggering COW to copy a never-correctly-initialized Mamba slot → resulting in garbled characters. This fix: When `cache_len is None` or `cache_len == 0` is detected, directly free the KV and Mamba slot, skipping the radix insert and eliminating the ghost node. This is the correct protection logic. ---- --CODE-- ``` for i, req in enumerate(batch.reqs): if to_track[i] and req.mamba_next_track_idx is not None: req.mamba_next_track_idx = ( pool.get_mamba_ping_pong_other_idx( req.mamba_next_track_idx ) ) ``` In``prepare_mamba_track_for_verify`` , it calls``set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs(batch)`` which rebuilds mamba_track_indices from req objects. But if``req.mamba_next_track_idx`` never gets flipped, then``mamba_track_indices`` stays the same. In decode, the non-spec path flips it in``prepare_for_decode`` . For spec decode, the flip was missing The absence of this flip will cause the same track slot to be repeatedly overwritten. After a boundary crossing, the next verify will write to the same slot that was just committed. ---- ## Accuracy Tests aime qwen3.6-35b--prefix cache--0.9 The above hallucination problem didn't appear after repair. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ``` Serving Benchmark Result Backend: sglang Traffic request rate: inf Max request concurrency: 40 Successful requests: 40 Benchmark duration (s): 48.97 Total input tokens: 2806984 Total input text tokens: 2806984 Total generated tokens: 40960 Total generated tokens (retokenized): 35576 Request throughput (req/s): 0.82 Input token throughput (tok/s): 57316.79 Output token throughput (tok/s): 836.38 Peak output token throughput (tok/s): 1687.00 Peak concurrent requests: 40 Total token throughput (tok/s): 58153.17 Concurrency: 35.60 Accept length: title: [DSA] Q8KV8 FP8 Sparse Prefill on GLM-5.2 & DeepSeek-V3.2: Q8-Path & Shared-Path Optimizations
author: JackChuang
body:
> Part of the Q8KV8 FP8 sparse-attention roadmap #25746; follow-up to #25751 (kernel) and
> #30514 (DSA integration), both now in main. Throughout,
> **q8** = the Q8KV8 fp8 sparse-prefill backend and **q16** = the bf16-sparse FlashMLA
> baseline; both arms always run the fp8 KV cache. Scope: **GLM-5.2 + DeepSeek-V3.2** (shared
> levers measured on both; the q8-only levers apply to any DSA architecture using this backend).

## TL;DR

- **General DSA-pipeline optimizations (backend-agnostic — GLM-5.2 & DeepSeek-V3.2):**
  End-to-end on 8×H200 (TP8/EP8/DP8), the bf16 FlashMLA baseline itself gains +8.8–10.3%
  saturated throughput and +4.4–6.3% single-request TTFT (positive = faster) on GLM-5.2,
  and +4.3–6.7% saturated throughput on DeepSeek-V3.2 (DS TTFT ~flat at +0.3–0.9% — the DS
  pipeline gain lands almost entirely in throughput; see table), across 3.5k–160k context.
- **Q8KV8 vs the already-optimized bf16 FlashMLA baseline** (measured on this
  PR's head, both arms fp8 KV): GLM-5.2 single-request TTFT +9.6–13.6%, saturated throughput
  +3.4–6.8%; DeepSeek-V3.2 TTFT +8.1–20.9%, saturated +5.0–10.1% across 3.5k–160k context.
- **Net effect vs out-of-the-box bf16 baseline** (upstream defaults vs this PR's
  recommended config + code): GLM-5.2 saturated throughput **+13.1–17.5%**, TTFT
  **+14.4–20.0%**; DeepSeek-V3.2 saturated throughput **+9.5–17.4%**, TTFT **+8.4–21.3%**.
- **Accuracy q8 vs q16 (shipped lossless config):** gsm8k per-rung Δ +0.3 to −0.6% across the
  shipped-config and PR-head ladders (full 1319q/rung, σ ≈ 0.3–0.6% — parity); forced-sparse
  MMLU (N=14,042, every question through the sparse kernel) +0.26% (within 1 per-arm SE,
  ~0.33%); LongBench-v2 −0.8 to −1.0% (σ ≈ 0.8–1.5%; an earlier unoptimized-config
  measurement was −2.3%) — within 1σ. DeepSeek-V3.2 gsm8k −0.6% (≈1σ).

## Motivation

DeepSeek-V3.2's Q8KV8 fp8 sparse-MLA prefill path (#25751 kernel, #30514 DSA integration — both now in main) is
dispatch-gated only on backend/KV-dtype/SM90 — model-agnostic across DSA architectures. This
PR (a) validates it end-to-end on **GLM-5.2** (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`): zero new integration
code needed (64 q-heads = the kernel's native tile; kernel-facing shapes byte-identical to
V3.2); and (b) contributes **seven optimizations, two fixes, and a recommended-flags
config** (plus two experimental opt-in levers, below) found during this validation work —
each gated by bitwise/numeric tests plus a gsm8k probe; the assembled stack additionally
passed the c=512 stress suite and full DeepSeek-V3.2 cross-validation.

The performance contribution is **two independent stages, reported separately**
(protocol: 8×H200, TP8/EP8/DP8, both arms fp8 KV cache):

- **Stage 1 — general DSA-pipeline optimizations (every deployment benefits, q8 not
  required):** the bf16-sparse (upstream-default) arm itself gains **+8.8–10.3% saturated
  throughput and c=1 TTFT +4.4–6.3%** on GLM-5.2 from the shared levers
  (NVLS + GATHERV + JIT-DeepGEMM restore + fp8 DP-gather). Of this, +6.9–8.0% saturated
  comes from enabling existing upstream default-off flags (NVLS, GATHERV); the remainder
  comes from new code in this PR.
- **Stage 2 — Q8KV8 fp8 sparse prefill, measured against that already-optimized baseline,
  measured on this PR's head:** q8 wins all 14 rows — **saturated +3.4–6.8%,
  c=1 TTFT +9.6–13.6%** (3.5k single-request TTFT 361 ms).
  Both arms run the same optimized config, so this A/B is conservative: the baseline arm
  includes every shared optimization in this PR.
- **Net effect vs upstream out-of-the-box (Stage 1 × Stage 2): GLM-5.2 saturated
  +13.1–17.5%, c=1 TTFT +14.4–20.0%; DeepSeek-V3.2 saturated +9.5–17.4%, c=1 TTFT
  +8.4–21.3%.**
- **DeepSeek-V3.2 (same two-stage treatment, full lever stack, measured on the PR
  head): Δ saturated +5.0–10.1% / c=1 TTFT +8.1–20.9%**; the q8-only levers (born-fp8 is
  1.68× on DS) fully transfer.
- **Accuracy — near-lossless:** 9 of 10 levers bitwise-exact or numeric-neutral
  (test-asserted). LongBench-v2 (LBV2) official protocol on the final stack: q8-vs-q16
  **Δ −0.8 to −1.0% (≈1σ)**; an earlier unoptimized-config measurement was −2.3±0.8%
  (the difference between the two measurements is within ~1σ). The only lossy lever
  (fp8 DP-gather wire-quant) is gsm8k-neutral (full-1319q ladder Δ +0.001) with a measured
  LBV2 cost of ~1.8% on GLM — therefore the **recommended default is the lossless lever
  set** (the always-on code paths plus the envs/flags in §Usage); wire-quant stays opt-in
  for throughput-first deployments (labeled below).

## Modifications (levers, each a separate commit / env)

| lever | scope | default | numerics | measured effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| vectorized 16B KV-gather + fused pad-zero + cached buffer (`kernels/ops/attention/dsa/dequant_k_cache.py`) | q8-only | always-on | bit-exact | 7.2× (112→15.6 µs/call) |
| born-fp8 q: fused absorbed-bmm+concat+cast (`SGLANG_ENABLE_DSA_Q8KV8_BORN_FP8_Q`) | q8-only | opt-in | bit-exact | 1.31× GLM / 1.68× DS q-prep |
| per-row topk_length early-exit + backscan derivation (`SGLANG_ENABLE_DSA_Q8KV8_TOPK_LENGTH`) | q8-only | opt-in | bit-exact (bitwise-asserted) | raised the 3.5k tput delta from +2.1% to +6.5% at adoption (lat3.5k from +4.3% to ~+14%); kernel time −25.9% @ s_q=437 |
| persistent kernel-output buffers | q8-only | always-on | bit-exact | removes 3 allocs/layer-call |
| fused non-prefix KV prep (`SGLANG_ENABLE_DSA_Q8KV8_KV_CAT_FUSION`) | q8-only | opt-in | bit-exact (canary-verified) | 3 kernels+1 alloc → 1 kernel; c=1 +0.5–0.7% (individually sub-noise e2e; accepted on the kernel-level win) |
| fp8 DP-gather wire format (`SGLANG_ENABLE_DP_GATHER_FP8`) | shared (dp-attention) | opt-in | **lossy on the wire; gsm8k-neutral proven** (q16 on/off full ladder; measured LBV2 cost ~1.8% — see §Accuracy) | GLM sat +1.2–1.4% / **DS sat +4.9%** |
| DLPack stride shim (`jit_kernel/dsa/paged_mqa_logits.py`) | shared bugfix | always-on | n/a | fixes the bs=1 crash on upstream-default JIT-DeepGEMM; this shim is what makes the upstream-default JIT-DeepGEMM usable — "JIT-DeepGEMM restore" in Stage 1 refers to it |
| MAX_LEN pad-row MoE dispatch mask (`SGLANG_OPT_MASK_DP_PAD_MOE`) | shared | opt-in | lossless (the masked rows' outputs were already discarded) | efficiency fix — pad rows waste MoE compute; numerics unchanged, hence safe to keep opt-in pending the upstream issue |
| SM90 WGMMA q-prep kernel (`SGLANG_OPT_Q8KV8_QPREP_VARIANT=cuda`) | q8-only | opt-in | bit-exact (7 shape configs) | q-prep 1.25× GLM / 1.16× DS over the Triton optimum; e2e +0.2–1.1% (individually sub-noise; accepted on the kernel-level win) |
| recommended flags: `--enable-nccl-nvls`, `SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1` (upstream, default-off) | shared | opt-in | numeric-neutral | sat +6.9–8.0% combined |
| tests | — | — | — | kernel suites 21 → **42** (bitwise topk-length/backscan sweeps + WGMMA q-prep suite) |

Default policy: the bit-exact internal rewrites (KV-gather, persistent buffers) and the
DLPack bugfix are always-on; every behavior-selectable lever ships opt-in (default-off) to
keep this PR's diff conservative — we propose promoting the bitwise-verified levers to
default-on in a follow-up once CI covers them. (Env-var naming — `SGLANG_ENABLE_*` vs
`SGLANG_OPT_*` — will be aligned to project conventions during review.)

Archived negative results (in-tree, documented, not wired): grouped-GEMM q-prep variant
(+0.5% e2e, sub-noise — 173 µs = the Triton practical optimum; dropped because it was later
dominated by the shipped SM90 WGMMA kernel above, not on the e2e number alone);
dispatch-level split-topk (the wave-fill gain is real, but the LSE-merge traffic cost
cancels it); DeepGEMM masked-GEMM m-cap (`SGLANG_OPT_DG_MASKED_M_CAP`, blocked by an
upstream pad/dummy-routing issue — a detailed report will be filed as a separate upstream
issue). Two further opt-in, default-off experimental levers ship in-tree: MoE quantize-once
(`SGLANG_OPT_MOE_QUANT_ONCE`; bitwise-verified but e2e-negative on these models, kept for
future architectures) and q-prep/indexer overlap (`SGLANG_ENABLE_DSA_Q8KV8_QPREP_OVERLAP`;
no effect on GLM's shared-indexer schedule).

## Usage

```bash
# RECOMMENDED optimized config (lossless: bitwise / numeric-neutral levers only):
SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1 SGLANG_ENABLE_DSA_Q8KV8_BORN_FP8_Q=1 \
SGLANG_ENABLE_DSA_Q8KV8_TOPK_LENGTH=1 SGLANG_ENABLE_DSA_Q8KV8_KV_CAT_FUSION=1 \
SGLANG_OPT_Q8KV8_QPREP_VARIANT=cuda \
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse_q8 --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_kv \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --dp-size 8 \
  --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.84 --context-length 163840 --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --enable-nccl-nvls --trust-remote-code

# (SGLANG_OPT_MASK_DP_PAD_MOE is also lossless but stays opt-in pending the upstream
#  MoE pad-dispatch issue — see Known upstream issues.)
# OPTIONAL throughput-first variant — additionally prefix the same launch command with:
#   SGLANG_ENABLE_DP_GATHER_FP8=1
# (wire-quantizes the DP-gather to fp8; gsm8k-neutral, measured LBV2 cost ~1.8% on GLM —
#  see §Accuracy; +1.2–1.4% sat GLM / +4.9% sat DS)
```

The bf16 baseline is `--dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse` (the only change needed for an
A/B). Contexts ≤ `index_topk` (2048) take the dense path, where both backends are identical.
DeepSeek-V3.2 runs used identical flags (except the reasoning parser) with `--model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2` and
the same chunked-prefill/mem-fraction.

Note on configs: the q8-vs-q16 A/B tables were measured with the optional wire-quant
enabled **on both arms** (arm-symmetric, so those deltas are unaffected by it); in the
pipeline and net-effect tables it is part of the optimized config being measured. Running
the recommended lossless-only default lowers saturated absolutes by ~1.2–1.4%
(GLM) / ~4.9% (DS). The accuracy ladders were run on the recommended lossless config.

## Experimental Results

Notation: *il* = input length; *sat_c* = the saturating (knee) concurrency; *latN* =
single-request (c=1) TTFT at input length N; *tputN* = saturated throughput at il = N.
All Δ/gain columns in this document's tables are quoted so positive = faster: throughput
ratio − 1 for saturated rows, time-ratio (slower/faster) − 1 for TTFT.
All performance tables use `sglang.bench_serving`
(random dataset, range-ratio 1.0, cache flushed between runs), except the prefix-cached
control in §MTP, which deliberately uses generated shared prefixes with radix reuse.
Representative invocations — latN rows: `--dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 1.0
--random-input-len N --random-output-len 1 --max-concurrency 1 --flush-cache`; tputN rows:
`--random-input-len N --random-output-len 1 --num-prompts <per-knee count>
--max-concurrency <sat_c> --flush-cache`.

Scope and limitations: all measurements are on a single 8×H200 node (the q8 kernel dispatch
is SM90-gated), one parallelism topology (TP8/EP8/DP8), synthetic fixed-length workloads;
multi-node, PD disaggregation, and other hardware were not benchmarked.

Base/config map for the tables below:

| table | base | config | arms |
|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.2 headline A/B (sat + TTFT) | PR head | optimized (wire-quant on, both arms) | q8 vs q16 |
| GLM-5.2 pipeline (Stage 1) | development pin¹ | out-of-the-box → optimized | q16 only |
| GLM-5.2 net effect | development pin¹ | out-of-the-box → optimized q8 | q16 vs q8 |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 pipeline (Stage 1) | PR head | out-of-the-box → optimized | q16 only |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 net effect | PR head | out-of-the-box → optimized q8 | q16 vs q8 |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 full-stack A/B | PR head | optimized (wire-quant on, both arms) | q8 vs q16 |

¹ development pin = upstream main @ `bbc53703` (2026-07-07) + this PR's levers.

Knee note: the GLM 64k saturated row is quoted at its PR-head re-verified knee (c=24) in
the headline table and at c=16 (its development-pin knee) in the pipeline/net tables.

### GLM-5.2 headline: q8 vs bf16-sparse, both arms on the optimized config (measured on this PR's head; q8 wins 14/14)

**Reading order matters:** the q16 column below is the *already-optimized* baseline (all
shared levers on — matching the "opt" column of the pipeline table further down, which was
measured at the development pin; cross-base agreement is within ±1%). The deltas here are
therefore the q8 backend's genuine second-stage contribution, on top of a baseline this PR itself
made ~10% faster on saturated throughput (and ~5% on TTFT).

**Saturated throughput (tot tok/s; sat_c per il re-verified by 2× knee probes):**

| il (sat_c) | q8 | q16 | Δ |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 3.5k (c64) | 33,050 | 30,956 | **+6.8%** |
| 8k (c32) | 31,846 | 30,623 | +4.0% |
| 16k (c16) | 31,560 | 30,515 | +3.4% |
| 32k (c16) | 31,296 | 30,163 | +3.8% |
| 64k (c24) | 30,775 | 29,676 | +3.7% |
| 120k (c16) | 28,837 | 27,611 | +4.4% |
| 160k (c16) | 28,082 | 26,806 | +4.8% |

**c=1 single-request TTFT (ms):**

| il | q8 | q16 | Δ |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 3.5k | **361** | 410 | **+13.6%** |
| 8k | 795 | 884 | +11.2% |
| 16k | 1,618 | 1,782 | +10.1% |
| 32k | 3,303 | 3,621 | +9.6% |
| 64k | 6,868 | 7,534 | +9.7% |
| 120k | 13,780 | 15,142 | +9.9% |
| 160k | 19,413 | 21,383 | +10.1% |

### General DSA-pipeline optimizations (both backends benefit — measured on the bf16-sparse arm)

The shared levers (NVLS + GATHERV + JIT-DeepGEMM + fp8 DP-gather) speed up the **entire DSA
serving path regardless of prefill backend**. Measured on the q16 (bf16-sparse, upstream-SOTA)
arm itself — same protocol, out-of-the-box config vs optimized config
(measured at the development pin; the headline tables above were measured on the PR head —
cross-base agreement within ±1% throughout; the 64k saturated row is additionally quoted at
its re-verified knee c=24 on the PR head vs c=16 here). The out-of-the-box arm uses the
identical launch command and tuning (chunked-prefill 32768, mem-fraction 0.84, TP8/EP8/DP8)
with none of this PR's levers enabled and without `--enable-nccl-nvls`/GATHERV;
JIT-DeepGEMM runs disabled in the GLM baseline (at baseline-measurement time the
upstream-default JIT-DeepGEMM path was unusable here — it crashes at bs=1 without this
PR's DLPack fix — so the working out-of-the-box state ran without it; re-enabling it,
made possible by that fix, is the "JIT-DeepGEMM restore" lever counted in Stage 1). The
DeepSeek-V3.2 baseline runs JIT-DeepGEMM at its upstream default (on):

| il | q16 sat tot tok/s (oob → opt) | gain | q16 c=1 TTFT ms (oob → opt) | gain |
|---|---|--:|---|--:|
| 3.5k | 28,114 → 31,004 | **+10.3%** | 432 → 410 | +5.4% |
| 8k | 27,925 → 30,672 | +9.8% | 938 → 882 | +6.3% |
| 16k | 27,890 → 30,493 | +9.3% | 1,884 → 1,784 | +5.6% |
| 32k | 27,396 → 30,191 | +10.2% | 3,813 → 3,622 | +5.3% |
| 64k | 26,628 → 29,320 | +10.1% | 7,920 → 7,513 | +5.4% |
| 120k | 25,187 → 27,552 | +9.4% | 15,874 → 15,134 | +4.9% |
| 160k | 24,697 → 26,881 | +8.8% | 22,298 → 21,365 | +4.4% |

(The q8 arm gains +11.8–16.2% saturated / +8.5–16.1% TTFT over the same span = shared +
q8-only levers combined.) These shared-lever gains apply to every DSA deployment —
including bf16-sparse-only users who never enable the q8 backend.

Same measurement on **DeepSeek-V3.2** (bf16-sparse arm, out-of-the-box vs optimized config,
measured on this PR's head; note DS's out-of-the-box already includes JIT-DeepGEMM — the
upstream SM90 default — so the pipeline gain here comes from NVLS+GATHERV+wire-quant only,
and lands almost entirely in throughput):

| il | q16 sat tot tok/s (oob → opt) | gain | q16 c=1 TTFT ms (oob → opt) | gain |
|---|---|--:|---|--:|
| 3.5k | 27,409 → 29,237 | **+6.7%** | 486.5 → 485 | +0.3% |
| 8k | 26,731 → 28,413 | +6.3% | 1,115 → 1,105 | +0.9% |
| 16k | 25,956 → 27,555 | +6.2% | 2,298 → 2,278 | +0.9% |
| 32k | 24,977 → 26,534 | +6.2% | 4,880 → 4,837 | +0.9% |

### Net effect: optimized q8 vs upstream out-of-the-box bf16-sparse (Stage 1 × Stage 2)

development-pin measurements as the pipeline table above.)

**DeepSeek-V3.2** (both columns measured on this PR's head):

### DeepSeek-V3.2, full lever stack (measured on this PR's head; q8 wins 14/14)
