Reference points: the shared-levers-only config Δ was saturated +2.9–4.2% / c=1 +4.6–8.0%;
the #30514-shipped table (as originally reported) was +1.8–2.7% / +4.4–7.6% — and an
out-of-the-box q8-vs-q16 re-run on this PR's head reproduces it (+1.8–3.6% / +4.3–8.2%),
independently corroborating the shipped numbers on the current base; the full-stack deltas
above are 1.8–3.7× those shipped reference deltas. The q8-only levers transfer fully to
DeepSeek-V3.2 (its larger attention share — ~13.5% of GPU busy vs GLM's ~6% — amplifies
the same kernel-level wins).

### MTP / speculative decoding compatibility (GLM's recommended deploy mode)

Both backends were validated with EAGLE MTP enabled (`--speculative-algorithm EAGLE
--speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6`,
the cookbook low-latency recipe), on this PR's head: q8 gsm8k 0.940 with MTP on (q16-MTP
gsm8k not separately scored; decode path and KV dtype are identical between arms — so ITL
is unaffected — and prefill accuracy is covered by the ladders above); prefill advantages
persist — lat8k 891 vs 1,085 ms (+21.8%), lat64k 7,045 vs 7,733 ms (+9.8%); tput64k +3.9%.
A prefix-cached-traffic control experiment (30k-token shared prefixes, radix reuse,
256-token questions) showed parity — within ±0.5% TTFT / throughput mixed within
run-to-run noise — as designed: short cached-prefix extend batches take the dense path,
where both backends are identical.

### Correctness

- Kernel pytest **42/42** (bitwise topk-length-equality + backscan exact-match sweeps +
  the WGMMA q-prep suite); every accepted lever's probe carried a gsm8k gate (0.94–0.97).
- c=512 stress suite (512 concurrent long-generation requests), 3/3 passes clean on the
  PR branch (217 s/pass, zero hangs, zero crash markers).
- DeepSeek-V3.2 full-stack validation: gsm8k 0.960 (initial full-stack probe; see
  §Accuracy for the full-1319q @120-shot A/B), all benches clean.
- **Base robustness:** tables measured at a pinned base, then re-validated twice while
  rebasing forward: (i) on 2026-07-16 main (410 commits including the topk-v2 rewrite
  #30645) — 42/42 bit-exact, 4-row spot-check within ±0.25%; (ii) on the PR branch (main
  @ b8ec544946, i.e. with #30514 merged, + these commits) — full 28-row re-validation
  within ±0.7%; and finally the headline tables above were re-measured in full
  on the PR head itself. Cross-base agreement throughout development:
  every same-concurrency row within ±1%, deltas stable-to-wider. gsm8k ladder re-run on the
  PR head (shipped lossless config, full 1319q): q8 0.939/0.934/0.945 vs
  q16 0.939/0.939/0.951 — parity.

### Accuracy

Harnesses: gsm8k — train-split few-shot completion harness, temp 0, full 1319-question
test set; MMLU/MGSM — `sglang.test.run_eval`; LBV2 — official protocol, temp 1.0 /
top_p 0.95, thinking-ON.

- gsm8k uniform ladder (full 1319q/rung, train-split shots, temp 0): both models flat and
  healthy. **Final shipped config (lossless lever set), full 1319q per rung:**
  q8 0.942/0.945/0.953 vs q16 0.942/0.942/0.955 at 20/120/390-shot (~3.6k/20k/65k ctx) —
  parity within σ (max |Δ| 0.3%), zero invalid answers (re-run on the PR head: same
  parity, see §Correctness).
- **Forced-sparse MMLU (largest-N check of the quantized kernel path):** with
  `SGLANG_DSA_PREFILL_DENSE_ATTN_KV_LEN_THRESHOLD=64` every question is routed through the
  sparse prefill kernel (N=14,042, per-arm SE ~0.33%): **q8 0.8146 vs q16 0.8120 (+0.26%)** —
  statistically equivalent (note: at these context lengths top-k covers nearly the full
  context, so this stresses fp8 kernel numerics rather than selection sparsity). MGSM same
  setup: 0.898 vs 0.902 (parity).
- DeepSeek-V3.2 on the full lever stack, full-1319q gsm8k @120-shot: 0.951 vs 0.957 (≈1σ).
- **Wire-quant (the only lossy lever) isolation:** q16 arm with fp8 DP-gather on/off, full
  ladder — Δ 0.000/+0.009/−0.007 (pooled +0.001, σ ≈ 0.5–0.7%) = statistically zero.
- **LBV2 (official protocol, thinking-ON), final stack, all four configs:**

  | arm (pooled LBV2 score) | wire-quant ON | wire-quant OFF |
  |---|--:|--:|
  | q8 | 0.5791 | 0.5980 |
  | q16 | 0.5891 | 0.6060 |

  q8-vs-q16 on the final stack: **Δ −1.0% (wire-quant on) / −0.8% (off), ≈1σ**; an
  earlier unoptimized-config measurement was −2.3±0.8%, and the difference between the
  two measurements is within ~1σ (the bitwise q8-path levers do not add accuracy cost;
  the final stack's LBV2 gap is statistically marginal).
  Wire-quant's own cost is roughly arm-symmetric: −1.9% (q8) / −1.7% (q16) — real on
  LBV2 though invisible to gsm8k — hence its "optional, documented" positioning in §Usage.

## Known upstream issues (documented, not introduced here)

- Fused top-k v2 tie-overflow IMA (illegal memory access) — already fixed in main (#30512); GLM-5.2 trips the pre-fix bug at much shorter contexts (~16k) than V3.2 did (>131k), so the fix is load-bearing for GLM deployments on older releases.
- JIT-DeepGEMM bs=1 DLPack stride crash — fixed by this PR's shim.
- MoE dispatch of MAX_LEN pad rows / degenerate dummy-forward routing — masked (opt-in
  `SGLANG_OPT_MASK_DP_PAD_MOE`); a full write-up will be filed as a separate upstream issue.

title: Bump FlashInfer to 0.6.15.post1
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

- bump `flashinfer_python`, `flashinfer-cubin`, and the optional JIT cache from 0.6.14 to 0.6.15.post1
- reland the FlashInfer 0.6.15 API compatibility and regression cleanup from #31502
- restore the GLM-5.2 NVFP4 performance threshold after removing the obsolete correction-bias workaround

## Why

The original 0.6.15 bump was reverted in #31625 after host-side regressions reduced long-context serving throughput. FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1 includes both follow-up fixes needed to recover performance:

- flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3970 memoizes MLA decode `TuningConfig` objects for equivalent inputs. This prevents fresh, unequal initializer closures from growing a single `_find_nearest_profile` hash-collision chain, which made per-call host overhead O(n) and total overhead O(n²) in long-running MLA decode workloads. It also improves persisted autotuner-cache validation and healing.
- flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4045 caches constructor-derived fused-MoE runners per host thread and validates only the selected tactic pair. This removes roughly 0.4 ms of warmed host-dispatch overhead per invocation while leaving tactic selection and dispatched CUDA kernels unchanged; its end-to-end GB300 test recovered the approximately 6% gap observed against the compatibility baseline.

This release therefore addresses the issues that led to the revert while retaining the 0.6.15 compatibility changes.

## Validation

- repository pre-commit hooks (TOML, AST, isort, Ruff, codespell, registered-test validation)
- Python syntax compilation for all modified Python modules
- `python/pyproject.toml` TOML parsing
- PEP 440 ordering check for `0.6.15.post1 > 0.6.15`
- Docker, Python dependency, and runtime FlashInfer pin consistency check
- `git diff --check`

GPU model E2E tests were not run locally.

title: [NPU] Optimize DeepSeek-V4 performance
author: Talantan1102
body:
## Motivation

This PR improves DeepSeek-V4 serving performance on Ascend NPU by adding PD disaggregation and chunked prefill support, together with optimizations for the prefill and decode execution paths.

All hardware-specific behavior is gated to the NPU + DeepSeek-V4 path, leaving CUDA, ROCm, and other model architectures unchanged.

## Modifications

| Area | Changes |
| --- | --- |
| PD disaggregation | Represent the DSV4 SWA, C4, C128, indexer, and compression-state pools as independent Ascend PD components; add DSV4-specific decode allocation and request-to-token mappings; transfer each pool through positionally matched page indices on the Ascend/Mooncake path. |
| Chunked prefill | Make compressed-KV allocation prefix-aware, preserve partial compression states across chunks, and keep the C4, C128, and indexer page tables aligned with global sequence positions. |
| Performance optimizations | Optimize the fused NPU compressor and graph replay paths; enable DeepEP decode dual-stream execution; simplify interleaved RoPE handling; add NPU `MoEGatingTopK`; and fix NPU graph-update and runtime compatibility issues. |

## Launch Command

The following core configuration was used for full-model validation in an Ascend A3 environment. Replace the model and ZBAL bootstrap placeholders with the local deployment values.

```bash
# Core DSV4 NPU configuration
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export INF_NAN_MODE_FORCE_DISABLE=1
export IS_DEEPSEEK_V4=1
export USE_FUSED_HC_PRE_ASCENDC=1
export SGLANG_DSV4_NPU_FUSED_COMPRESSOR=1
export SGLANG_DSV4_NPU_FUSED_COMPRESSOR_PREFILL=0

# ModelSlim W8A8
export SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=0
export SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=False
export FORCE_DRAFT_MODEL_NON_QUANT=1

# DeepEP / ZBAL
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=8
export DEEP_NORMAL_MODE_USE_INT8_QUANT=1
export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=64
export SGLANG_ZBAL_LOCAL_MEM_SIZE=61000
export SGLANG_ZBAL_BOOTSTRAP_URL="tcp://<zbal-bootstrap-host>:<port>"
export ZBAL_ENABLE_GRAPH=1

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path "${MODEL_PATH}" \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --device npu \
    --attention-backend dsv4 \
    --quantization modelslim \
    --kv-cache-dtype auto \
    --page-size 128 \
    --tp-size 16 \
    --dp-size 16 \
    --enable-dp-attention \
    --enable-dp-lm-head \
    --moe-a2a-backend deepep \
    --deepep-mode auto \
    --prefill-max-requests 2 \
    --chunked-prefill-size 65536 \
    --max-running-requests 160 \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \
    --disable-overlap-schedule \
    --cuda-graph-bs 1 2 4 8 10 \
    --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
    --speculative-num-steps 1 \
    --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
    --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 30000
```

## Accuracy Tests

Evaluated the full DeepSeek-V4-Flash W8A8 ModelSlim model through the OpenAI-compatible API in a 16-device Ascend A3 environment.

| Benchmark | Mode | Configuration | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| GPQA-Diamond | Thinking enabled | `temperature=1`, `top_p=1`, `max_tokens=120000` | **86.87% (172/198)** |

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Targeted unit tests: 10 passed.
- Full-model GPQA-Diamond evaluation completed with 0 request errors.
- Server health check passed after evaluation.

title: [Fix] Reject online weight updates while the HPC-Ops router GEMM split cache is active
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #30247 (merged), addressing @VAthree's [review comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30247#discussion_r3619585198): the bf16xfp32 split cache (`w_high`/`w_low` derived from the fp32 router weight) went stale after SGLang's online weight-update APIs. The loaders write parameters in place via `param.data.copy_()`, which changes none of the fields the cache can observe (`data_ptr`/shape/stride/device/dtype, and `.data` writes do not bump `_version` either), so after `update_weights_from_disk/tensor/distributed/ipc` the HPC router kept computing logits from the old weights. Fixed-weight serving was unaffected.

## Modifications

This optimization targets fixed-weight serving, so rather than wiring the derived cache into the weight-update lifecycle, **online weight updates are rejected while the optimization is enabled**, and the enablement signal is **startup-determined and rank-uniform** (addressing the [DP-divergence review catch](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31943#discussion_r3635423390)):

- `kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/gemm.py`: `LongcatFlashRouter.__init__` declares the HPC router GEMM path via `mark_hpc_bf16xfp32_gemm_enabled()` (no-op when the kernel is unavailable); the generic env opt-in (`SGLANG_OPT_BF16_FP32_GEMM_ALGO=hpc`) is a startup constant already. `hpc_bf16xfp32_gemm_enabled()` therefore depends only on startup facts — installed packages, GPU arch, model config — and is **identical on every rank**. It is never set lazily from a forward pass: a lazily set flag would diverge across DP ranks (only ranks whose local batch clears `min_m` build a cache), letting a weight update be rejected on some workers while others proceed, or split a distributed collective. The split-cache path raises if a future call site forgets to declare itself at init.
- `model_runner_components/weight_updater.py`: the four online update entry points (`update_weights_from_disk`, `update_weights_from_tensor` incl. direct/custom/flattened-bucket formats, `update_weights_from_distributed` incl. bucketed, `update_weights_from_ipc`) fail fast with a clear error message — before touching any weight or entering any collective — when the optimization is enabled. Since the check is rank-uniform, an update is either rejected on all workers or proceeds on all workers.
- **CUDA-graph hazard fixed**: the cache key is layout-only (`_version` dropped). Captured graphs replay the split buffers by address, so the buffers are allocated once and can never be reallocated out from under a captured graph by an in-place write.
- Regression tests: (1) the weight updater rejects updates when the optimization is enabled; (2) split-buffer addresses stay stable across `param.data.copy_()` under CUDA-graph capture/replay, with eager and replay staying consistent.

## Validation (H200)

`test/registered/gemm/test_linear_bf16_fp32_hpc.py` — 5 tests / 6 subtests pass on H200 with HPC-Ops installed, plus the LongCat router dispatch unit test:

```
============== 5 passed, 21 warnings, 6 subtests passed in 12.13s ==============
```

In CI (no `hpc` package on runners) the GPU suite skips cleanly; the CPU dispatch test runs as before.

title: [perf] Compute input logprobs without materializing the full-vocab log-softmax
author: sshleifer
body:
## Motivation

Input (prefill) logprob processing runs an out-of-place `log_softmax` over `[rows, vocab]` before extracting per-token logprobs, top-k, and token-ids probes (`InputLogprobProcessor._forward_by_chunk`). Everything downstream needs only small gathers plus a per-row normalizer, so the full-vocab materialization is pure memory traffic — at 32k rows x 152k vocab it allocates 10–20 GB of transient auxiliary memory. This is what forces small `SGLANG_LOGPROB_CHUNK_SIZE` values (each chunk pays a separate lm_head pass) and OOMs large-batch prefill with logprobs enabled, e.g. RL teacher / distillation workloads that request prompt top-k logprobs at scale.

## Modifications

- Keep the raw logits and compute a per-row logsumexp normalizer instead: `logprob[i] = logit[i] - lse(row)`. Top-k runs directly on the logits (identical order — the shift is a per-row constant), then values are normalized by subtraction; token-ids probes and the target-token gather do the same.
- New `srt/layers/logsumexp.py`: single-pass online-logsumexp Triton kernel (one read of the logits, fp32 accumulation, inf-safe). It returns per-row `(max, logsumexp - max)` and consumers compute `(logit - max) - log_sum`, preserving log-softmax's shift invariance for rows with a large common offset. When top-k is requested with k<=8, a fused variant maintains the running top-k in registers during the same single read (packed value+index keys, value ties broken by the lowest index); k>8 falls back to torch.topk on the raw logits. Non-CUDA falls back to torch. No dependencies beyond triton.
- `get_top_logprobs_chunk` / `get_token_ids_logprobs_chunk` accept an optional `log_normalizer`; behavior is unchanged when it is not passed.
- Opt-out escape hatch: `SGLANG_ENABLE_FAST_INPUT_LOGPROBS=0` restores the previous path.

Results are mathematically identical; for bf16 logits they are strictly *closer* to the exact values than the old path, because normalization happens in fp32 instead of rounding through a bf16 log-softmax.

## Benchmark

GB300, vocab=151936, k=2, 20-iter mean (isolated microbench of the replaced region: log_softmax+topk+gather vs logsumexp+topk+gather):

| rows | k | dtype | baseline | fast (fused kernel) | peak aux mem |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8192 | 2 | bf16 | 9.55 ms / 2532 MB | **2.39 ms (4.0x)** | 43 MB (**58.6x smaller**) |
| 32768 | 2 | bf16 | 42.34 ms / 10.1 GB | **9.39 ms (4.5x)** | 173 MB (**58.6x smaller**) |
| 8192 | 2 | fp32 | 15.54 ms / 5.0 GB | **2.47 ms (6.3x)** | 43 MB (**116.1x smaller**) |
| 8192 | 8 | bf16 | 9.58 ms | **3.84 ms (2.5x)** | 43 MB |

The commit history shows the evolution: an intermediate version used flashinfer's `top_k` (3.2-5.7x, but implementation-defined tie order and a hard dependency); the final fused kernel is faster at production k, dependency-free, and tie-deterministic. Above k=8 the fused selection cost overtakes a separate top-k pass (measured crossover ~k=6; below plain torch.topk near k=32), so larger k uses `logsumexp kernel + torch.topk` (~1.1x, never below baseline).

## Numerics

- **Shift-invariant**: normalization computes `(logit - max) - log_sum`, the same order as log-softmax; regression-tested at a 1e8 common offset.
- **Deterministic**: fixed reduction order, no atomics; run-to-run bitwise reproducibility is asserted in tests.
- **Tie-stable**: top-k value ties break by lowest index. fp32 indices are tested exactly equal to torch.topk's; a crafted-duplicates test pins the tie rule.
- **vs the old path**: the normalizer is an online logsumexp (the FlashAttention-style running max/sum) rather than torch's two-pass log-softmax. The algebra is identical — exactly equal in exact arithmetic — but the floating-point reduction order differs, so values agree to ulp level rather than bitwise (tested at 1e-5 fp32 across chunk splits; neither result is more correct than the other). For bf16 the fast path is strictly *closer* to the exact answer than before, because the old path rounds through a bf16 log-softmax while the normalizer here accumulates in fp32 (tested against float64 ground truth).
- **dtype**: the fast path returns fp32 token/top-k logprobs regardless of logits dtype (the normalizer is fp32, so fp32 is the true precision of the result); the old path returned the logits dtype. Responses serialize to python floats either way.
- `SGLANG_ENABLE_FAST_INPUT_LOGPROBS=0` reproduces today's behavior exactly, including torch.topk tie order.

## Test

- `test/registered/unit/layers/test_logprob_fast_input.py` (registered CPU CI):
  - fp32 sweep: fast vs log-softmax reference across heterogeneous per-sequence top-k/probe params and chunk splits — identical indices, values to 1e-5.
  - bf16 sweep: fast path vs float64 ground truth to 1e-4 (tighter than bf16 resolution; the old path cannot be used as an order reference because bf16 log-softmax rounds near-ties together).
  - Kernels vs float64 `logsumexp` / torch.topk for k in 1..8, including rows=0, cols=0, -inf-dominated rows, non-contiguous inputs, crafted value ties, the fused pair bitwise-equal to the non-fused kernel, a shift-invariance regression at offset 1e8, run-to-run bitwise determinism, and an end-to-end CUDA pass through the chunked processor including the k>8 fallback (CUDA tests skipped on CPU CI).
- Existing `test_logprob_chunk_stitching.py` passes with the fast path enabled (default).

title: [Perf] Skip page-table columns past kv length in DSA draft-extend metadata kernel
author: hnyls2002
body:
The DSA draft-extend metadata kernel copies the page table over the full captured context width, but each request's real kv length is far smaller. Add a per-program early-exit: skip whole column blocks whose start is past the request's kv length (downstream attention and the indexer both bound their reads by `cache_seqlens`, so those columns are never read).

The kernel runs once per draft-extend step, so this is a per-step metadata-prep saving on the speculative-decoding hot path; the win grows with the gap between the captured graph's context bucket and the real sequence length. In a bs=1 draft-extend profile the prep drops from ~74.9us to ~40.9us.

title: [Perf] Fold dspark dense draft embedding into the draft graph via forward_embed
author: hnyls2002
body:
The dense DSpark draft model drops the shared embedding in `attach_shared_modules`, so the runner stages `input_embeds` eagerly before every draft graph replay. `deepseek_v4_dspark` already opts into the `forward_embed` mechanism that the cuda-graph runner and draft proposer support (keep `embed_tokens`, expose `forward_embed`). Wire the dense dspark model in the same way so the embedding lookup runs inside the draft graph and the eager staging copy is skipped. Same lookup, just moved into the graph; the `dflash` base keeps the raise for models without `forward_embed`.

title: [Perf] Stack dspark dense draft per-layer ctx KV projection into one GEMM
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary
- Stack every draft layer's ctx-KV projection into one GEMM + a batched per-head k-norm + one shared RoPE, replacing the per-layer loop in `write_target_hidden_kv`.
- Collapses N GEMMs + N k-norms + N RoPEs into one each on the speculative-decoding hot path.

## Why it is exact
- `write_target_hidden_kv` feeds the identical `ctx_hidden` (target hidden) through every layer's KV projection, so concatenating the per-layer weight columns is algebraically equivalent to N separate GEMMs.
- The batched k-norm reproduces per-head RMSNorm (fp32 variance/weight); one RoPE over all layers' heads matches the per-layer RoPE (shared rotary params + positions).
- Falls back to the per-layer loop when a layer's QKV weight cannot be sliced (quantized) or layers disagree on norm epsilon / bias presence.
- The stacked weight is cached on first use (assumes draft weights are frozen after load).

## Test plan
- New `test/registered/spec/dspark/test_dspark_stacked_ctx_kv_parity.py`: compares the stacked path against the per-layer path (`kv_proj_only` + `apply_k_norm` + `apply_k_rope`) on the same input, with distinct per-layer weights so a wrong slice / layer order / permute fails; fp16 (tight) + bf16 tolerances; plus the three fallbacks (quantized / eps mismatch / inconsistent bias).
- This ctx KV feeds only the draft; spec decoding keeps the final output correct regardless of draft-KV precision, so accuracy tests cannot catch a broken write -- this parity UT is the gate.

## Motivation

Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/31827

Similar to `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-NVFP4`, `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4` is a hybrid quantized model with only certain layers in NVFP4. This time the MoE routed experts are in NVFP4 and other layers in MXFP8. We didn't handle the MXFP8 layers properly.

```
sglang serve --model-path nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 --trust-remote-code --tp 8 --context-length 2048 --mem-fraction-static 0.79
```

* Support MXFP8 layers in "modelopt_mixed" mixed precision models
* Since the shared experts and routed experts use different precisions, disable shared expert fusion

title: [Model Loading] Overlap checkpoint staging with CUDA graph capture during startup
author: yh0903
body:
## Motivation The native/default model-loading path currently finishes loading and post-processing the real weights before CUDA graph capture begins. For large checkpoints, checkpoint I/O and CUDA graph capture are both material parts of engine startup, but they run serially. This PR introduces an opt-in startup path that stages safetensors checkpoint pages while the runtime initializes and CUDA graphs are captured. It then loads and post-processes the real weights in place, without changing the tensor storage referenced by the captured graphs. The existing behavior remains the default: ```text --startup-weight-load-mode serial # default ``` This PR does not enable overlap by default. ## Modifications ### Startup flow #### Existing serial startup ```mermaid flowchart LR S1["Load and post-process
real weights"] S2["Initialize runtime and
capture CUDA graphs"] S3["Ready to serve"] S1 --> S2 --> S3 ``` #### Opt-in overlap startup ```mermaid flowchart TB O1["Allocate final GPU storage
and resolve safetensors shards"] O2["Initialize capture-safe weights
and required post-processing"] O3["Explicitly start checkpoint prefetch"] O4["Storage-to-OS-page-cache staging"] O5["Initialize memory pools and attention backends
and capture CUDA graphs"] O6["Load and post-process real weights
in the existing storage"] O7["CUDA synchronize and verify storage identity,
stop/join prefetch, and run the TP barrier"] O8["Ready to serve"] O1 --> O2 --> O3 --> O5 --> O6 --> O7 --> O8 O3 --> O4 O4 -. "runs concurrently" .-> O5 O4 -. "warms pages consumed by" .-> O6 ``` The overlapped work is checkpoint staging from storage into the OS page cache. Real checkpoint iteration, GPU weight commit, and post-load processing still happen after CUDA graph capture. - Add `--startup-weight-load-mode {serial,overlap}`, defaulting to `serial`. - Split the exact `DefaultModelLoader` startup lifecycle into model/storage initialization, checkpoint resolution, capture-safe initialization, and post-capture in-place commit. - Reuse the existing coordinated checkpoint page-cache prefetcher through a cancellable lifecycle handle and reuse the resolved checkpoint source during commit. - Verify that graph-visible tensor object identity, data pointer, shape, stride, dtype, device, and storage offset remain unchanged after the real-weight commit. - Start background prefetch only after `ModelRunner`/TP-worker construction completes; scheduler startup and `sglang.benchmark.one_batch` explicitly own the active lifetime. - Propagate explicit start/finalize handling through `ModelRunner` and TP workers. - Match the existing process-terminal startup contract: prepare, graph-capture, commit, and barrier failures are not recovered, so no failure-only cancellation or cleanup path is added. On the successful path, finalize stops and joins checkpoint prefetch before the TP barrier and serving. - Keep `--weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints` as an independent serial-path control and avoid starting a second prefetch when overlap already owns staging. ### Scope and rollout plan This is PR 1 of a staged three-PR rollout. The overlap path is intentionally opt-in and explicitly gated here. Its initial supported scope is: - CUDA graph capture with the exact `DefaultModelLoader` - `auto`/`safetensors` loading with mmap enabled - Native dense Llama, Qwen2, and Qwen3 generation models - FP16/BF16, TP1/TP2, and a single primary checkpoint source Unsupported configurations raise an explicit error instead of silently changing startup behavior. The existing serial path remains unchanged. Planned follow-ups: - **PR 2 — generalize and harden:** broaden the validated support matrix, add startup-phase timing/diagnostics, and factor shared lifecycle pieces so the native/default-loader and checkpoint-engine paths can converge where their semantics match. The feature remains opt-in while this coverage expands. - **PR 3 — default rollout:** introduce an `auto` policy and make it the default after broader CI and benchmark burn-in. Validated configurations select overlap automatically; unsupported configurations retain the serial path, with an explicit serial escape hatch. ## Accuracy Tests - Added a registered 1-GPU end-to-end test comparing default serial and overlap output token IDs, generated text, and output logprobs (`1e-5` tolerance). - Added registered CPU unit coverage for compatibility selection, explicit rejection, successful lifecycle transitions, graph-visible storage invariants, checkpoint-source reuse, prefetch cancel/wait behavior, serial/overlap scheduler routing, server arguments, and MLX routing. - Manually validated the overlap safetensors Engine path and `sglang.benchmark.one_batch` overlap path on H100. A focused latest-code smoke produced identical serial/overlap input IDs, prefill logits, and decoded text through real decode CUDA graphs; this smoke is not used for performance claims. - Qwen3-32B benchmark runs produced matching output IDs, text, and logprobs across all three startup modes. - `scripts/ci/check_registered_tests.py`, Python compilation, formatting/lint, and `git diff --check` pass. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Configuration: Qwen3-32B BF16 on H100, Triton decode CUDA graphs through batch size 256, prefill CUDA graphs disabled, three timed samples per configuration with A/B/C scheduled in Latin-square order, and warmed compiler/graph caches. Reported values are mean ± sample standard deviation. Checkpoint files were present on the local NVMe filesystem before timing; before every run, `POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED` was applied and `mincore` verified zero resident checkpoint pages. Prefetch used four threads per rank unless otherwise noted. These results were collected against commit `0dbcd4199`. ### Primary result: incremental overlap benefit The primary comparison is **B → C**. Both configurations use the same coordinated page-cache prefetch mechanism; C changes the startup order so runtime initialization and CUDA graph capture occur before the real-weight commit. This is the closest measured control for the additional overlap benefit. | Storage | TP | B: Serial + prefetch | C: Overlap | Wall time saved | B → C reduction | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Local NVMe | 1 | 38.94 ± 0.56 s | 35.60 ± 0.83 s | 3.34 s | 8.6% | 1.09x | | Local NVMe | 2 | 51.12 ± 1.16 s | 45.16 ± 0.29 s | 5.96 s | 11.7% | 1.13x | Across the refreshed local-NVMe configurations, overlap reduced startup by **8.6–11.7%** relative to serial startup with coordinated prefetch. Each of the three paired B → C samples favored C for both TP1 and TP2. With three repeats per configuration, these results characterize the observed startup behavior but are not intended to establish tight statistical confidence. A latest-code TP2 NFS rerun passed output parity but was excluded from the performance table because shared-storage contention made the samples unsuitable for a stable mean comparison: default-serial startup ranged from 148.70 to 1093.41 s, and overlap ranged from 53.72 to 118.67 s. No NFS speed claim is made from that run. ### End-to-end context For context, the complete opt-in path also includes the existing coordinated-prefetch gain: | Storage | TP | A: Default serial | B: Serial + prefetch | C: Overlap | A → B reduction | A → C reduction | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Local NVMe | 1 | 84.83 ± 0.30 s | 38.94 ± 0.56 s | 35.60 ± 0.83 s | 54.1% | 58.0% (2.38x) | | Local NVMe | 2 | 78.60 ± 0.36 s | 51.12 ± 1.16 s | 45.16 ± 0.29 s | 35.0% | 42.5% (1.74x) | Most of the A → C reduction comes from coordinated checkpoint prefetching. A → C describes the end-to-end opt-in startup path; **B → C is the main result attributable to the new startup ordering**. The sequential percentage reductions are not additive because they use different baselines. These measurements do not establish monotonic scaling with TP size. TP1 and TP2 were measured in separate executions on different nodes. Matching eight aggregate prefetch threads on TP1 produced means of 43.25 s for B and 36.71 s for C, a **15.1% reduction (1.18x)**, compared with **11.7% (1.13x)** on TP2 using four threads per rank, also eight aggregate threads. Each TP rank captures its own CUDA graph concurrently, so capture time is not summed across ranks. The results demonstrate a benefit at TP1 and TP2, but do not imply increasing percentage savings as TP rank grows. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code according to the contribution guide. - [x] Add registered unit and end-to-end tests. - [x] Update user-facing argument help for the new control. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Preserve the existing serial startup behavior by default. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #31526564021](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31526564021) Latest PR Test (Extra): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32449179602](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32449179602) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.

title: [Scheduler] Enable decode retraction ordering under speculative decoding
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `retract_decode` disabled the retraction-order policy under speculative decoding, citing "filter_batch can only filter requests from the back" — so spec runs retract in arrival order instead of the configured `retraction_policy` (default: shortest-output first, which minimizes wasted rework)
- The constraint is stale: the scheduler-side `filter_batch` calls `spec_info.filter_batch(..., has_been_filtered=False)`, and every implementation (`eagle_info`, `dflash_info_v2`, `ngram_info`, including the overlap `future_indices` path) gathers with the arbitrary `new_indices` tensor on that path. The truncation-only branch (`has_been_filtered=True`) has no remaining callers at all — the verify-side pre-filtering it served left with the spec v1 paths (#27977); the scheduler is the only caller today and always passes `False`
- Ordering only changes which requests get retracted — each individual retraction is the same already-supported operation, and non-spec retraction has been shipping policy-sorted (non-ascending) keep sets through the same gathers
- Removes the dead family outright: the `has_been_filtered` parameter (all three spec_info implementations + the scheduler call site), the truncation branch, and the `SGLANG_SPEC_ENABLE_STRICT_FILTER_CHECK` env that only the dead branch read
- Adds a CPU unit test for `_get_decode_retraction_order` (length / priority policies, tie-breaks, `None` priority)

## Why the constraint existed, and when it expired

- Born in #3988 (spec v1): verify filtered finished requests itself (`unfinished_index`), so the scheduler-side `spec_info.filter_batch` only truncated (`[: len(new_indices)]`) — truncation can only drop a suffix, hence "retract from the back"
- #9252 added the real gather branch (`has_been_filtered=False`); #27977 removed the spec v1 scheduler paths, after which the scheduler always declares `has_been_filtered=False` — the truncation branch no longer has any caller
- The gate survived as a fossil and was carried verbatim into the new helper by #30573

title: feat(humming): support native W4AFP8 checkpoint schemas
author: guzekai01
body:
## Summary

no `--json-model-override-args` needed. Reuses `W4AFp8Config` metadata and maps

block-FP8 path. Stacked on #31429.

Server (1 node × 8 H20, GLM-5.2-W4AFP8 tp8):

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path GLM-5.2-W4AFP8 --trust-remote-code \
  --tp-size 8 \
  --quantization humming --moe-runner-backend humming \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 1 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --context-length 90000
```

(baseline arm: `--quantization w4afp8`, no Humming flags)

Accuracy client:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --api chat \
  --num-examples 1319 --num-shots 8 --num-threads 32 \
  --temperature 0 --max-tokens 1024 \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'
```

title: [Kernel] RFC #29630 finale: retire sglang.jit_kernel into sglang.kernels
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

Structural **finale** of the `sglang.jit_kernel` → `sglang.kernels` migration (RFC #29630). After batch-1/2/3 (#31666, #32015, #32045) moved every operator into `sglang.kernels.ops.<group>`, this PR removes the `sglang.jit_kernel` package **entirely**.

## What changed

- **Build infra moved** into `sglang/kernels/jit/`: `csrc/`, `include/`, `__main__.py`, `benchmark/`, `tests/`, `.clang-format` (git-tracked as renames).
- **`KERNEL_PATH` refactor** (`kernels/jit/utils/compile.py`): `find_spec("sglang.jit_kernel")` → `find_spec("sglang.kernels.jit")`. `csrc/`+`include/` now resolve under `kernels/jit/`.
- **Last 8 batch-1 shims deleted** (activation, norm, dsv3_fused_a_gemm, dsv3_router_gemm, set_mla_kv_buffer, per_tensor_quant_fp8, per_token_group_quant, per_token_group_quant_8bit_v2); all call sites rewritten to `sglang.kernels.ops.<group>._jit_<op>`.
- **Fixed batch-2/3 dangling refs** that used the package-relative (`from sglang.jit_kernel import X`) or top-level-tree import forms and were missed by the earlier dotted-only rewrites: `inkling_*`, `cutedsl_gdn`/`cutedsl_kda`, `dsa`, `rope`, `hicache`, the split `triton.*` submodules, `flash_attention` — across `benchmark/` and `sgl-kernel/`.
- **Packaging**: `[tool.setuptools.package-data]` glob `jit_kernel/**/*` → `kernels/**/*` (ships csrc, include, and moved data dirs like `trtllm_lora_temp/data`).
- **CI / ownership**: change-filters (`_pr-test-check-changes`, `pr-test-amd`, `pr-test-amd-rocm720`, `pr-test-npu`), `labeler.yml`, `CODEOWNERS`, `MAINTAINER.md` now point at `python/sglang/kernels/**`. The namespace-invariant test now guards `sglang.kernels.jit`.
- **`python/sglang/jit_kernel/` no longer exists.**

## Validation (local, torch 2.11)

- `import sglang.kernels.ops` stays metadata-only → **CLEAN** (no `sgl_kernel` / `sglang.kernels.jit`).
- `KERNEL_PATH` resolves to `kernels/jit` with `csrc/` + `include/` present.
- All 24 rewrite-target module paths importable via `find_spec`.
- 155 changed `.py` files compile; `pre-commit` clean.

Part of RFC #29630. This is the last migration PR — the `sglang.kernels` namespace is now the single home for all kernels.

title: [Perf] Skip blocks past per-request live length in full-width Triton kernels
author: hnyls2002
body:
Extend the per-request early-exit pattern from #31981 to the remaining kernels whose grid or inner loop spans the full captured width: DSA decode / target-verify metadata, FA3 decode metadata, TRTLLM MHA graph metadata, extend attention (regular and unified), the DSA indexer K+S gather, and the sparse prefill index transform.

<details>
<summary>Appendix: microbenchmark results (kernel x setting, main vs this PR, n=10)</summary>

Methodology: 10 interleaved A/B process pairs (main / PR alternating); each sample is one Triton `do_bench` (100ms warmup + 1000ms measurement); values are mean +- std over the 10 runs; verdicts use a paired t-test (n=10, two-sided 5%). `SKIP` = most blocks are past the per-request live length, the early exit fires; `NOSKIP` = every block is live, the exit never fires (worst case, pure guard overhead). "n.s." = not statistically significant.

### Metadata kernels (decode / verify graph replay)

| Kernel | Setting | main (us) | PR (us) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fused_dsa_decode_metadata` | SKIP bs=1, width=16384, seq=1024 | 5.87 +- 0.11 | 5.73 +- 0.09 | -2.4% |
| | SKIP bs=8 | 6.29 +- 0.11 | 6.04 +- 0.18 | -3.9% |
| | SKIP bs=64 | 10.71 +- 0.17 | 10.10 +- 0.15 | -5.6% |
| | half live: bs=8, seq=8192 | 6.28 +- 0.17 | 6.26 +- 0.21 | n.s. |
| | SKIP bs=8, width=65536, no wide table | 8.12 +- 0.17 | 7.66 +- 0.15 | -5.7% |
| | NOSKIP bs=8 | 6.27 +- 0.14 | 6.39 +- 0.15 | +2.0% n.s. (p~0.06) |
| | NOSKIP bs=64 | 10.69 +- 0.19 | 10.73 +- 0.07 | n.s. |
| `fused_dsa_target_verify_metadata` | SKIP bs=1 / 8 / 32, seq=1024 | 6.00 / 8.07 / 15.55 | 5.81 / 7.63 / 15.02 | -3.0% / -5.5% / -3.4% |
| | NOSKIP bs=8 / bs=32 | 8.04 / 15.50 | 8.04 / 15.54 | flat / n.s. |
| `normal_decode_set_metadata` (FA3) | SKIP bs=1, page=1 | 5.88 +- 0.17 | 5.84 +- 0.08 | n.s. |
| | SKIP bs=8, page=1 | 6.35 +- 0.14 | 6.22 +- 0.14 | -2.1% |
| | SKIP bs=64, page=1 | 11.95 +- 0.18 | 7.89 +- 0.18 | **-34.0%** |
| | NOSKIP bs=8, page=1 | 6.34 +- 0.18 | 6.44 +- 0.22 | +1.7% n.s. |
| | NOSKIP bs=64, page=1 | 11.94 +- 0.14 | 9.82 +- 0.16 | -17.7% |
| | SKIP bs=8 / bs=64, page=64 | 6.70 / 12.96 | 6.22 / 9.04 | -7.1% / **-30.3%** |
| | NOSKIP bs=64, page=64 | 12.92 +- 0.14 | 10.97 +- 0.11 | -15.1% |
| `update_trtllm_mha_graph_metadata` | SKIP bs=1 / 8 / 64, seq=1024 | 11.46 / 12.15 / 16.88 | 5.60 / 5.77 / 6.08 | **-51% / -53% / -64%** |
| | NOSKIP bs=8 / bs=64 | 12.18 / 16.88 | 12.00 / 16.78 | -1.4% / n.s. |

### Attention / gather kernels

| Kernel | Setting | main (us) | PR (us) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `extend_attention_fwd` | SKIP ragged extend 7x16 + 1x4096, prefix=1024 | 4207.6 +- 4.6 | 1272.9 +- 5.5 | **3.3x** |
| | SKIP same, prefix=8192 | 30262.8 +- 42.6 | 5154.2 +- 12.3 | **5.9x** |
| | NOSKIP uniform extend 8x64 | 139.44 +- 0.11 | 138.26 +- 0.13 | -0.85% |
| | NOSKIP uniform extend 4x4096 | 4709.2 +- 8.4 | 4727.9 +- 11.4 | +0.40% |
| `extend_attention_fwd_unified` | SKIP ragged extend 7x16 + 1x4096, prefix=1024 | 5681.5 +- 15.1 | 2262.9 +- 7.1 | **2.5x** |
| | SKIP same, prefix=8192 | 35138.8 +- 105.4 | 7133.4 +- 20.1 | **4.9x** |
| | NOSKIP uniform extend 8x64 | 153.32 +- 0.33 | 153.67 +- 0.18 | +0.23% |
| | NOSKIP uniform extend 4x4096 | 9615.1 +- 26.3 | 9627.0 +- 10.8 | n.s. |
| `_get_k_and_s_triton` | NOSKIP uniform seq=1024 / 8192; SKIP ragged | 7.38 / 10.28 / 7.90 | 7.46 / 10.34 / 7.91 | n.s. (all) |
| `transform_index_page_table_prefill` | SKIP ragged extend 7x16 + 1x4096 | 128.30 +- 0.42 | 73.09 +- 0.35 | **-43.0%** |
| | NOSKIP uniform extend=64 / 512 | 40.20 / 77.62 | 40.16 / 77.62 | flat |

Notes:
- Every SKIP-scenario gain above is statistically significant (paired t-test, p < 0.05; the PR side is faster in at least 7 of 10 paired runs, usually 10 of 10).
- No metadata-kernel NOSKIP config shows a significant regression. The closest is DSA decode NOSKIP bs=8 at +2.0% (p ~ 0.06, ~+0.12us); this worst case requires seq == the captured max-context width, which real serving essentially never reaches. On the live path the `kv_len` load is issued alongside the existing `req_idx` load, so no serialized latency is added.
- For the attention kernels the guard shifts NOSKIP shapes within +-0.9% with no consistent sign (-0.85% / +0.40% / +0.23% / n.s.), i.e. code-layout jitter from the added branch rather than a systematic cost; the ragged-batch upside is 2.5-5.9x.

### Where the gains are large in practice

- `update_trtllm_mha_graph_metadata` (**2.1-2.8x**): the page-table width is the static max-context bound while real seq lens are far smaller, so the skip applies on essentially every replay; the kernel runs ~4 times per decode step per TP rank and feeds the first all-reduce, making this a per-step latency win.
- `normal_decode_set_metadata` (**-30~-34% at bs=64**): FA3 decode replay also always passes the max-context width; gains grow with batch size.
- `extend_attention_fwd` / `_unified` (**2.5-5.9x** on ragged batches): mixed-length extend batches (continuous batching, mixed chunked prefill) skip whole attention compute blocks, not just metadata copies; uniform batches (e.g. spec verify) are unchanged.
- `transform_index_page_table_prefill` (**-43%** on ragged batches): sparse prefill index transform for mixed-length batches.
- DSA decode / target-verify metadata gains are real but small (launch-bound, -2~-6% per step), consistent with the draft-extend kernel from #31981.

</details>

title: Fix nightly CI: NVFP4 cuda-graph crash, NVILA batching, CuTe paged-KV zero-size, Kimi-VL OOM
author: b8zhong
body:
## Summary

Independent fixes for failures found triaging the Nightly Test (Nvidia) run, each reproduced with a full traceback and root-caused before fixing.

2. **`nvila.py`**: `test_vlms_mmmu_eval.py` crashed with `stack expects each tensor to be equal size` — `get_image_feature` used `torch.stack` on per-image vision-feature tensors whose patch count varies with image resolution, then immediately flattened the stacked dim away with a rearrange. Replaced with `torch.cat` directly (what the code actually wanted).

3. **`flash_attn/cute/interface.py`**: `test_disaggregation_dwdp_mimo.py` / `test_mimo_cp.py` crashed with `ValueError: Expected size in shape to be strictly positive, but got 0` in the CuTe FA4 paged-KV kernel. Root cause: the SM100 diff-headdim (`head_dim != head_dim_v`, e.g. 192/128) SMEM-saving optimization shrinks `n_block_size` to 64 under split-KV, but for `q_stage==1` (decode) with paged KV, the non-TMA load path uses 128 threads, so `page_entry_per_thread = n_block_size // num_threads` floors to 0. Skip the shrink for that specific combination. Reproduced standalone on real B300 hardware with MiMo-V2.5's actual config (`head_dim=192`, `head_dim_v=128`, default `page_size=1`, forced split-KV) — crashed before the fix, produced finite correct-shaped output after.

4. **`kimi_vl.py` / `kimi_vl_moonvit.py`**: `test_vlms_mmmu_eval.py` also crashed on Kimi-VL. MoonViT's vision tower forced HF's `sdpa` attention path (dense attention over all packed image tokens) instead of sglang's own flash-attn, causing an OOM; fixed by routing MoonViT's attention through sglang's `VisionAttention` wrapper (same pattern `kimi_k25.py`'s MoonViT-style vision tower already uses), which also required remapping the vision checkpoint's `wqkv`/`wo` weight names to the wrapper's `attn.qkv_proj`/`attn.proj` names in `load_weights`.

## Test plan

- [x] All changed files compile and pass `pre-commit` (isort/ruff/black).
- [x] CuTe paged-KV fix verified with a standalone repro script directly calling `flash_attn_varlen_func` with MiMo-V2.5's real head_dim/head_dim_v/page_size, both batch_size=1 and batch_size=8 — crashes on `main`, succeeds with finite output after the fix.
- [x] NVFP4 pinned-memory fix verified with a standalone repro directly capturing `nvfp4_quantize(..., backend="cute-dsl", per_token_activation=True)` in a real `torch.cuda.graph()` — crashes on unpatched flashinfer, succeeds after the upstream fix.
- [x] Kimi-VL weight-name remap verified by instantiating `MoonVitPretrainedModel` directly and confirming its real parameter names match the remap.
- [ ] `/rerun-test` on the originally-failing files (posting next).

title: [AMD][DI][CI] 8/N Add GLM-5.2 MXFP4 1P1D DI/CI recipes (base + MTP + DP8/EP8)
author: Lzy17
body:
## Motivation

Add AMD MI355X DI/CI nightly recipes for **GLM-5.2 (MXFP4)** 2-node 1P1D
disaggregation, so the nightly exercises the GLM MoE line the same way it already
covers DeepSeek-V4 and Kimi-K2.6. Scope is the **basic tier** (TP8 1P1D, base +
MTP + DP8/EP8); wide-EP16 is deferred to a follow-up.

GLM-5.2 uses `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` (DeepSeek Sparse Attention; sglang
auto-selects the DSA attention backend) with a **built-in NextN MTP head**
(`num_nextn_predict_layers=1`) — the same MTP mechanism as DeepSeek-V4, so no
external draft checkpoint is needed.

## What's new

4 new recipes under `scripts/ci/slurm/recipes/mi355x-fp4/glm52/1k1k/`:

| Recipe | Topology | MTP |
|---|---|---|
| `1p1d.yaml` | TP8 1P1D | no |
| `1p1d-mtp.yaml` | TP8 1P1D | NextN |
| `1p1d-dp8ep8.yaml` | DP-attn 8 + EP8 1P1D | no |
| `1p1d-dp8ep8-mtp.yaml` | DP-attn 8 + EP8 1P1D | NextN |

Plus 4 matching blocks in `scripts/ci/slurm/nightly-configs.yaml`
(`glm52-fp4-mi355x[-mtp|-dp8ep8|-dp8ep8-mtp]-sglang`).

Each recipe carries a `model:` block so the launcher takes the **generic**
command-build path (not the hardcoded DeepSeek-V4 branch): it sets the GLM
reasoning/tool parsers (`glm45`) and `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`
(GLM has `n_shared_experts=1`), and leaves `attention_backend` unset so the
server auto-selects DSA for `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`.

## Runtime image

Recipes reference **`lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.15.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260722`**.
This image includes **#30265** ("[AMD] Fix GLM-5.2 MTP Quark excludes"), which adds
the dedicated `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLMNextN` class + GLM-specific Quark excludes /
MTP layer-index remap. That fix is required for GLM NextN MTP accuracy — an
earlier image predating #30265 ran GLM MTP through the raw non-DSA V3 NextN and
dropped GSM8K to ~0.87.

## Validation (MI355X, 2-node 1P1D, GSM8K full 1319Q 8-shot, gate 0.91)

| Leg | Accuracy | Invalid | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `1p1d.yaml` (base) | **0.930** | 0.001 | ✅ PASS |
| `1p1d-mtp.yaml` (NextN) | **0.933** | 0.000 | ✅ PASS |
| `1p1d-dp8ep8.yaml` | **0.945** | 0.000 | ✅ PASS |
| `1p1d-dp8ep8-mtp.yaml` | — | — | ❌ CRASH (see below) |

Three of the four legs pass cleanly on 20260722. **`1p1d-dp8ep8-mtp` crashes at
runtime** — it is kept in this draft but must not be treated as passing.

### dp8ep8-mtp crash

`RuntimeError: Expected lengths.size(0) == B to be true, but got false` in the DSA
sparse-attention top-k indexer during the NextN draft forward, only when
DP-attention and MTP are combined:

```
deepseek_nextn.py:276 forward
  -> deepseek_v2.py:1860 forward -> forward_absorb_prepare (forward_mla.py:384)
    -> dsa_indexer.py:1998 forward_cuda -> _get_topk_paged (dsa_indexer.py:1038)
      -> dsa_backend.py:315 topk_transform -> dsa_topk_backend.py:130
        -> sgl_kernel/top_k.py:77 fast_topk_transform_fused  (assert lengths.size(0)==B)
```

Each ingredient works alone on this image (dp8ep8 without MTP = 0.945; MTP without
DP-attention = 0.933); only the dp8+MTP combination breaks the DSA topk `lengths`
tensor (per-batch seqlens not built for the DP-padded NextN draft-extend batch).
This is a source-level bug in DSA + NextN + DP-attention, not a recipe knob, and is
out of scope for this recipe PR — tracked separately.

## Non-regression

Adds only new files + new nightly blocks. No existing recipe, launcher line, or
nightly block is modified — existing legs stay byte-identical.

## Notes / caveats

- **Checkpoint on disk is `amd/GLM-5.1-MXFP4`** (the only GLM MXFP4 build currently
  mirrored on `/it-share`). The recipe/block naming tracks the GLM-5.2 model line;
  `model_path` points at the mirrored 5.1 MXFP4 checkpoint. Retarget `model_path`
  when the 5.2 checkpoint lands.

## Checklist
- [ ] Format with pre-commit
- [x] Validate base on MI355X (GSM8K 0.930 >= 0.91)
- [x] Validate MTP on MI355X (GSM8K 0.933 >= 0.91)
- [x] Validate DP8/EP8 on MI355X (GSM8K 0.945 >= 0.91)
- [ ] Fix dp8ep8-mtp DSA+NextN+DP-attn crash (source-level, tracked separately)

  - **Repo tooling**: `.claude/` skills + `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/.claude/` diffusion skills

Verified: no `docs_new` occurrences remain; touched Python parses; `docs/docs.json` is valid JSON.

## Guard against reintroducing `docs_new/`

Many open PRs still touch `docs_new/`. For PRs that only **modify** existing files, git's rename detection follows the edit to `docs/`. But PRs that **add new files** under `docs_new/` have no rename to follow, so on merge git silently re-adds them and resurrects the directory **without a conflict**.

To catch that, this PR adds a CI (Lint workflow) + pre-commit gate that fails if any tracked path under `docs_new/` reappears. Both use a tree-presence check (`git ls-files` / pre-commit `language: fail`) instead of a base-ref diff, avoiding the shallow-checkout / silent-diff pitfalls the earlier legacy-`docs/` gate (#26322) had to work around.

## Public URLs are unaffected

The `docs.json` navigation paths do not include the folder name, so hosted doc URLs do not change.

## ⚠️ Action required on merge (out of repo)

The **Mintlify hosting dashboard's content directory** currently points at `docs_new/`. It must be updated to `docs/` when this merges, or the hosted site build will fail. Please coordinate the merge with that dashboard change.

title: [Kernel] Reclassify kernel tests by ops group + move helpers out of the package (RFC #29630)
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to RFC #29630. Organizes **all** kernel tests + benchmarks to mirror `sglang.kernels.ops.<group>`, keeps **tests and benchmarks separate**, and gets the last test files out of the `sglang` package.

## Final layout

```
test/registered/kernels/
  ops/<group>/         # tests            (test_*.py)
  benchmark/<group>/   # benchmarks       (bench_*.py + data fixtures)
python/sglang/kernels/testing/   # shared test-support helpers (importable)
```

## What changed

- **Reclassify by ops group** — moved `test/registered/jit/` (102) + `test/registered/kernels/` (21) into `test/registered/kernels/ops/<group>/` (tests) and `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/<group>/` (benchmarks), classified by the operator each exercises, primarily by its `sglang.kernels.ops.<group>` imports. Tests and benchmarks are kept in **separate** trees.
- **Move test helpers out of the package** — the awkward `python/sglang/kernels/jit/tests/` folder → proper support package `python/sglang/kernels/testing/` (`utils.py`, `kv_canary/`, `deepseek_v4/`); rewrote all `sglang.kernels.jit.tests` → `sglang.kernels.testing` imports.
- **Register 6 previously-orphaned tests** — `minimax_m3_{mxfp8,rmsnorm}`, `sconv_{decode,extend}_metadata`, `moe_{preprocess,topk_sigmoid}` had test functions but no CI registration (never ran). Added `register_*_ci`: CUDA → `base-b-kernel-unit`; ROCm-only `minimax_m3` → `jit-kernel-unit` (amd).
- **Resolve a name collision** — two `test_sigmoid_gate_mul.py` (base vs broadcast); broadcast one renamed `test_sigmoid_gate_mul_broadcast.py`.
- **Move the nvfp4 bench data fixture** (`diffusion_nvfp4_shapes.json`) alongside its bench.
- **Repoint CI change-filters** — `test/registered/jit/**` → `test/registered/kernels/**` (covers ops/ tests + benchmark/ benches), diffusion bench filter → `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/diffusion/**`.

## Why it's safe

Benchmarks and tests are both CI-registered and stay under `test/registered/`. CI discovery is a recursive glob over `test/registered/**` keyed on each file's `register_*_ci(stage=...)` — **path-independent** — so nothing changes about which suite each test/benchmark runs in. (Registered files cannot live in the package: `run_suite.py` doesn't glob it, and the `check-no-registered-tests-in-package` hook forbids it.) `python/sglang/` now has **zero** CI-registered tests.

Validated: `validate registered test CI registries` + `reject CI-registered tests inside the sglang package` hooks pass, `sglang.kernels.testing` imports, `import sglang.kernels.ops` stays metadata-only, pre-commit clean. Almost entirely `git mv` renames.

body:
## Summary

Post-migration review follow-up on `python/sglang/kernels/` — tightens classification and naming consistency. Almost entirely `git mv` renames + import rewrites.

## Changes

- **Unify JIT-op naming** — drop the leftover `_jit_` prefix (a batch-1 shim-era artifact) from 8 modules so JIT-backed ops read consistently with the rest (`flash_attention.py`, `rope.py`, …): `activation/activation`, `layernorm/norm`, `gemm/dsv3_{fused_a,router}_gemm`, `kvcache/set_mla_kv_buffer`, `quantization/per_{tensor_quant_fp8,token_group_quant,token_group_quant_8bit_v2}`.

title: [diffusion] fix: per-shard FP8 scale shape for single-GPU fused linears
author: AgainstEntropy
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

On a single GPU, ckpts whose fused QKV is a `MergedColumnParallelLinear` (e.g. HunyuanVideo img_attn_qkv) fail to load the quantized transformer and fall back to a non-FP8 "native" model.

```
Error while loading customized transformer, falling back to native version
```

A fused checkpoint stacks its 3 per-projection scales into (3,), but the layer's weight_scale/input_scale are created as (1,), so the load asserts.

Root cause:

`MergedColumnParallelLinear.__init__` set `self.output_sizes` before `super().__init__()` only when tp_size > 1. `ColumnParallelLinear` derives per-shard output_partition_sizes via `hasattr(self, "output_sizes")`, and the FP8 method sizes per-tensor scales as `(len(output_partition_sizes),)`.
On a single GPU the attribute was unset at that point -> `output_partition_sizes = [sum(output_sizes)]` -> scales collapsed to (1,).

`QKVParallelLinear` already sets it unconditionally, so it was never affected.

title: [HiSparse] Support hisparse multi-step swap io kernel
author: huangtingwei9988
body: ## Motivation The existing HiSparse swap path processes speculative decoding steps sequentially. For a four-step MTP request, this requires four independent cache lookups, swap passes, and cache-state updates. It also cannot naturally deduplicate misses shared by multiple speculative steps. This PR adds a standalone multi-step HiSparse swap kernel. It treats all MTP top-k tensors as one working set and resolves their device locations in one gather/commit launch pair. The scope of this PR is intentionally limited to the swap kernel, its JIT wrapper, correctness tests, and benchmark. It does not include IO prefetching or coordinator integration. ## Design The implementation uses two kernels: 1. A gather kernel flattens `[batch, steps, top_k]`, resolves extra-page and hot-cache hits, deduplicates host misses across speculative steps, and copies each unique miss into a scratch device location exactly once. 2. A per-request commit kernel updates the CLOCK cache, rotates scratch and hot locations, updates the token-to-slot hash tables, and resolves direct overflow misses. The two-kernel structure provides the grid-wide synchronization required before the cache commit can consume the final miss count and scratch hash table. Programmatic Dependent Launch is enabled on supported Hopper GPUs. Current-call device locations remain exact. If the union of unique hits and misses exceeds the hot-cache capacity, only the cache admission policy becomes approximate: the kernel favors the most recent speculative step for future cache residency. This does not change the data returned for the current attention call. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["top_k_tokens [batch, steps, top_k]"] --> B["Gather kernel"] B --> C["Extra-page lookup"] B --> D["Hot-cache hash lookup"] B --> E["Cross-step miss deduplication"] E --> F["Unique host-to-device copies"] C --> G["Resolved device locations"] D --> G F --> G B --> H["Commit kernel"] H --> I["CLOCK victim selection"] H --> J["Cache/hash update"] H --> K["Overflow resolution"] I --> L["Persistent state for next decode"] J --> L ``` ## Performance The benchmark uses CUDA Graphs with four speculative steps, top-k 2048, a 4096-entry hot cache, 576-byte MLA cache items, and 782 unique misses per request. On an NVIDIA H20, MTP reduces batch-64 latency from 794.42 us for four sequential LRU passes to 411.85 us, a 48.2% reduction. The gather block size is set to 64 threads. It preserves the cross-step warp mapping while reducing host-I/O bursts compared with larger CTAs. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. title: [XPU] Use SYCL kernels for DeepSeek V4 MHC on XPU
author: cyxlily
body:
## Motivation
Enable XPU-specific optimized kernels for the DeepSeek V4 MHC (Multi-Head Compression) path on Intel XPU hardware. author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

Root-cause fixes for the H100 `deepep-4-gpu-h100` CI breakage (`TestTBOWithTPAttn`: `RuntimeError: The specified pointer resides on host memory and is not registered with any CUDA device` during CUDA graph capture, and `NaN detected! sampler: next_token_logits`) introduced by #30924.

There are **two independent bugs**. This PR fixes both at their root, keeps the unified JIT quant kernel everywhere, and supersedes #32051 (whose Hopper masked-path revert does not fix the test — its own `/rerun-test` failed 5x with the same NaN, because bug 2 lives in a path that revert keeps).

## Bug 1: use-after-free on the activation scale (the "host memory" crash)

In sgl-deep-gemm (<= 0.1.4.post1), `get_mn_major_tma_aligned_tensor` crosses TVM-FFI via a **non-owning** `torch::from_blob` view (`csrc/utils/torch_compat.hpp`), and the already-aligned fast path (`smxx_layout.hpp`) returns that alias directly. The caller rebinds the result over its only reference:

```python
down_input_scale = deep_gemm_wrapper.get_mn_major_tma_aligned_tensor(down_input_scale)
```

so the storage is freed to the caching allocator and reused **before the down GEMM (enqueued later) reads the scales**. #30924 triggered it because the unified kernel emits scales already MN-major/TMA-aligned — hitting the no-op alias path for the first time (the old row-major scales always took the owning copy path). TBO makes the reuse near-certain: the other micro-batch's layer (dozens of small allocations) is enqueued between the rebind and the GEMM. Blackwell is unaffected (`DEEPGEMM_NEED_TMA_ALIGNED_SCALES=False`).

**Fix:** the sglang wrapper returns the input tensor itself whenever deep_gemm returns an alias of it (`deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py`). Follow-up: fix ownership semantics in sgl-project/DeepGEMM itself.

**Evidence (H200):** production-path repro (JIT masked quant → transform rebind → 64 small allocs simulating the other TBO micro-batch → real DeepGEMM masked GEMM) yields **688 NaN rows** without the fix, **0** with it. With `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1` (free = real `cudaFree`) the unfixed path reproduces the CI error **byte-identically**; fixed path is clean.

## Bug 2: the unified kernel dropped non-finite input sanitization (the NaN at capture)

Every kernel the unified one replaced (AOT v1, JIT v2, Triton) clamps with IEEE `fminf/fmaxf` before converting to fp8 — and IEEE min/max return the **non-NaN operand**, so NaN/Inf inputs quantize to ±448. The new kernel relied on SATFINITE alone ("no need to clip"), but SATFINITE only saturates inf/out-of-range: **NaN converts to an fp8 NaN code**. (Also `amax=inf` → `__frcp_rn(inf)=0` → `inf*0=NaN`.)

CUDA-graph capture warmup runs the model over reused, uninitialized buffers. On CI runners GPU memory is dirty from back-to-back jobs, so warmup activations contain NaN bit patterns; the old kernels silently sanitized them, the new kernel forwards fp8 NaN codes into the downstream GEMM → `NaN detected! sampler: next_token_logits` during capture. This is why the failure needs CI-runner conditions to reproduce (fresh GPUs hand out zeroed pages), why it survives #32051's masked-path revert (the **flat** path — every block-fp8 linear input quant — still used the new kernel), and why it survives the bug-1 fix alone.

**Fix:** restore the clamp on both the fp32-scale and UE8M0 paths in `per_token_group_quant.cuh`. For finite inputs this is bit-identical to bare SATFINITE (UE8M0's pow-2 scale already bounds finite scaled values to ±448), so all bit-exactness guarantees hold.

**Evidence (H200):** NaN/Inf-poisoned inputs: unfixed kernel emits fp8 NaN codes, v2 emits none; fixed kernel matches v2 exactly. Full unit suite (92 original + 12 new sanitization + 1 ownership regression) passes: **105/105**.

## Validation

- H200: micro/production/deterministic repros for bug 1 (table above), poison probes for bug 2, 105/105 kernel unit tests.
- E2E (H200, Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8, `--tp 4 --moe-a2a-backend deepep --enable-two-batch-overlap`): GSM8K **0.96**, no NaN.
- `/rerun-test registered/ep/test_deepep_small.py` on this PR: pending below.

## Test-matrix consistency check

| Configuration | masked path | flat path | deepep H100 result |
|---|---|---|---|
| pre-#30924 | Triton (sanitizing) | v2 (sanitizing) | green |
| main (post-#30924) | JIT (alias + no sanitize) | JIT (no sanitize) | red (host-ptr / NaN) |
| #32051 (masked revert) | Triton | JIT (no sanitize) | red (NaN, 5x rerun) |
| this PR before bug-2 fix | JIT + ownership fix | JIT (no sanitize) | red (NaN) |
| **this PR** | JIT + ownership fix + sanitize | JIT + sanitize | expected green |

title: [PD] Keep EAGLE DP graph and token metadata consistent
author: weireweire
body:
Fixes #32182.

In PD decode, target and draft can use different MoE A2A backends. The scheduler kept target-local token counts for the draft worker, so DP ranks disagreed on draft padding and collective shapes. Missing GLM DSA seeds could also make only active ranks fall back to eager.

This change synchronizes graph eligibility across DP ranks and keeps draft-specific token counts without changing the target DeepEP path.

Validation:
- GLM-5.2-NVFP4 TP4/DP4 EAGLE GSM8K: 0.948 (474/500), with 500/500 requests completed and no DSA/CUDA errors or rank hangs.

title: [NPU] Fix MTP IndexShare warm-up for attention DP and prefill CP
author: stellaxcpeng
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Fix two MTP IndexShare issues on NPU PD disaggregation:

1. **Decode warm-up hang with attention DP**

   [PR #30839](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30839) (`78dc581518`) added a rank-local graph-to-eager fallback when the DSA top-k seed is missing.

   During decode warm-up, a non-idle rank may select eager while idle ranks continue graph replay. Since draft forward contains TP/EP collectives, inconsistent execution paths across ranks can cause a deadlock.

2. **Prefill CP top-k gather failure**

   The prefill CP IndexShare path introduced by [PR #30992](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30992) (`7e229e2a81`) assumes `topk_indices` is a tensor.

   On the NPU CP path it may be a tuple/list, causing:

   ```text
   AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'shape'
   ```
## Modifications

Override `EAGLEDraftNpuGraphRunner.can_run_graph()` for NPU attention DP:

- Keep the existing local graph eligibility checks.
- Include DSA seed readiness in the local decision.
- Synchronize the decision with a `MIN` all-reduce.
- Use graph replay only when every participating rank is eligible; otherwise, all ranks use eager execution.

This change only affects the NPU EAGLE draft graph runner. It does not modify the common EAGLE logic or GPU behavior.

 Normalize tuple/list DSA top-k results before CP all-gather:
  - Concatenate the tensors along the token dimension.
  - Remove the singleton head dimension.
  - Preserve the existing tensor input path.

## Accuracy Tests

Before the fix: decode worker hangs during warm-up.
After the fix: decode warm-up completes successfully.
