title: [MoE] Fuse swiglu moe up gemm epilogue
author: yuan-luo
body: ## Motivation **What the MoE activation costs today.** The triton fused-MoE path runs three steps per layer: an up-GEMM that writes `intermediate_cache1` at the full gate+up width `N`, a standalone `silu_and_mul` that reads that buffer and writes `intermediate_cache2` at width `N/2`, and a down-GEMM. The middle step is pure data movement dressed as compute — it round-trips the entire intermediate tensor through HBM to apply an elementwise function whose inputs the up-GEMM already had sitting in registers. **Why that is worth removing at small batch.** At batch 1 a MoE layer's GEMMs degenerate into `M=4..8` slivers, so the step is bound by weight bandwidth and by the intrinsic latency floor of several hundred tiny kernels rather than by arithmetic. In that regime an extra launch plus a full round trip of the intermediate buffer, paid once per MoE layer per decode step, is a visible fraction of the step. It is also a link in the dependency chain — `GEMM1 -> act -> GEMM2` — that no amount of overlap can shorten while the activation stands between the two GEMMs. **Why it cannot simply be folded in.** The activation needs `gate[i]` and `up[i]` together, but the checkpoint stores W13 as two contiguous halves, so those two values come out of output columns `i` and `i + N/2` — different tiles of the up-GEMM. A tile holding `gate[i]` does not hold `up[i]`, and vice versa. **The fix.** Permute the rows of W13 once at load so gate and up of the same intermediate channel become adjacent columns. Each GEMM output column is an independent dot product of the input with one row of W13, so reordering rows can only reorder columns — the permute is value-neutral. After it, every `(gate[i], up[i])` pair lands in the *same* output tile as an even/odd column pair, the epilogue applies `silu(gate) * up` in-register, and only the half-width result is stored. `intermediate_cache1` and the standalone activation launch disappear, and the chain shortens to `GEMM1 -> GEMM2`. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py`: `FUSE_SWIGLU` constexpr on `fused_moe_kernel`, plus the epilogue that splits the accumulator into even/odd column pairs, applies the activation, and stores the half-width result. `invoke_fused_moe_kernel` gains a `fuse_swiglu` argument and asserts the output flavors it is incompatible with. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py`: allocates the half-width buffer as the up-GEMM destination, skips the standalone activation, and threads the flag through `fused_experts` / `fused_experts_impl` / `_fused_moe_kernel_sequence`. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton.py`: `TritonMoeQuantInfo.fuse_swiglu_interleaved` carries the layout fact from the weight owner to both `fused_experts` entry points. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py`: `_maybe_interleave_w13_for_fused_swiglu` performs the load-time permute, per expert so the gather temporary stays at one expert's slice. - `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: `SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_SWIGLU_INTERLEAVED`, default off. ### Bit parity is instruction-level, not approximate The kernel being replaced is compiled with `-use_fast_math`, so matching it means matching the instructions it emits. The epilogue uses `tl.inline_asm_elementwise` to do exactly that: `mul + ex2.approx.ftz` for `__expf`, `div.approx.ftz` for the division, and `mul.ftz.f32` for the product, with a single final rounding to bf16. The accumulator is already `compute_type` at that point, which matches the reference's bf16 store to `intermediate_cache1` followed by a reload. One detail is easy to get wrong and invisible from the call site: the reference instantiates its activation functor at `float`, so silu never lands in bf16 before the multiply. An implementation that rounds silu to bf16 first double-rounds and diverges on a large fraction of inputs. The first version of this change did exactly that, and only an element-wise bit comparison caught it. ### Why this is opt-in The permuted layout is understood by the fused epilogue and by nothing else, so every consumer that reads W13 — or the pre-activation buffer — in the checkpoint's halves layout has to be excluded at load rather than trapped later. The gate requires CUDA, the plain triton runner, standard a2a, no bias, bf16, and gated silu without `alpha` / `clamp_limit` / `swiglu_limit`, and additionally excludes: - **LoRA.** `_add_lora_gate_up_delta` adds its delta into the full-width pre-activation buffer this path eliminates, and indexes gate/up as contiguous halves of it — both assumptions break. Excluding it at load matters more than asserting at run time: permuting first and asserting later would turn `--enable-lora` into a crash after warmup instead of a clean fallback. The virtual-experts LoRA path is unaffected, since it consumes `lora_a` / `lora_b` and never the base W13. - **EPLB**, which rearranges experts by copying checkpoint-layout weights into the parameter. - Runtime weight updates, for the same reason; this one is documented on the env var rather than detected. Two further guards fail loudly rather than silently: `_fused_moe_kernel_sequence` asserts the call carries no hooks and no quantization, and `invoke_fused_moe_kernel` asserts that none of `fuse_add_to_output` / `mask_output` / `fuse_sum_all_reduce` / `lora_preserve_base` are set — those address `C` at the full width `N` and would write past the row end of the half-width buffer. Filtered (`-1`) expert blocks skip the store entirely for the same reason. Under the unfused path those rows are zero-filled at full width; here the row is only `N/2` wide, so an `N`-wide zero store would run into the next token's data. The rows are never read, because the down-GEMM CTA for such a block early-exits before loading its input. ## Accuracy Tests New: `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_fused_swiglu_epilogue.py`, registered `base-b-kernel-unit` / `1-gpu-large`. Both cases assert **bitwise** equality; a tolerance would defeat their purpose, since the failure mode this change risks is a plausible-looking few-ULP drift that no `assert_close` would flag. - `test_fused_matches_unfused_bitwise` drives the real `fused_experts` entry point twice — halves layout with the standalone activation, then interleaved layout with the epilogue — and requires the final MoE output to be bit-identical. Shapes cover a bs=1 decode row and a ragged token count that forces the `BLOCK_SIZE_M` tail. It also covers the filtered-expert claim: if those unwritten rows were ever read, the comparison would fail immediately. - `test_epilogue_matches_silu_and_mul_bitwise` isolates the epilogue arithmetic against `silu_and_mul` over random values plus the saturating tails and signed zeros. This is the guard against a future "simplification" to `tl.sigmoid` or an early bf16 cast. All three pass on H20-3e (sm90). End-to-end on `Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct` (256 experts, `moe_intermediate_size` 1024, bf16, TP4, H20-3e): six greedy prompts at 128 new tokens each, served once with the flag off and once with it on. The two output sets are **byte-identical** (equal md5). The fused run logs `Interleaved w13 gate/up: ...` on all four TP ranks and the baseline run logs it zero times, so the comparison is not vacuously passing on an inactive fast path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Removed, per MoE layer per forward: | | before | after | |---|---|---| | kernel launches | up-GEMM, activation, down-GEMM | up-GEMM, down-GEMM | | intermediate traffic | `intermediate_cache1` written at width `N`, read back at width `N` | none | | dependency chain | `GEMM1 -> act -> GEMM2` | `GEMM1 -> GEMM2` | Measured on `Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct`, TP4 on H20-3e (sm90), `bench_serving --dataset-name random --num-prompts 24 --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 256 --max-concurrency 1`, four runs per configuration: | | mean TPOT (4 runs) | output throughput | |---|---|---| | baseline | 2.49 / 2.49 / 2.49 / 2.49 ms | 362.2 - 368.6 tok/s | | fused | **2.46 / 2.46 / 2.46 / 2.46 ms** | 364.5 - 372.4 tok/s | **-1.2% mean TPOT**, with the two sets fully separated — no overlap across four runs each. Throughput moves the same way but its run-to-run spread (~1.8%) is wider than the effect, so only the TPOT column supports a conclusion here. The win scales with how launch-bound the step is, so it is largest at small batch and shrinks toward zero once the GEMMs grow big enough to dominate. sm90 with a 27-layer model at 512/256 is a conservative setting for it; the shape this was originally built for is batch-1 decode on Blackwell with a deeper MoE stack, which is not measured here. That asymmetry is the other reason this ships opt-in rather than on by default. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #31776581047](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31776581047) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #31776580851](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31776580851)

title: [JIT] Drop redundant per-kernel arch overrides
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> Generated by Claude.

## Motivation

`get_jit_cuda_arch()` already resolves the local GPU to its arch-specific target (`_cuda_arch_suffix`: 9.x/10.x+ → `a`, 12.0 → `f`), so the three kernels that wrapped `load_jit` in `override_jit_cuda_arch` to force an `a` target were pinning what detection hands them anyway. Those overrides predate the default-suffix logic and are now noise.

Note this is *sglang's* JIT default, not nvcc's — plain `-arch=sm_90` still defines no `__CUDA_ARCH_FEAT_SM90_ALL`:

```
sm_90    (none)
sm_90a   -D__CUDA_ARCH_FEAT_SM90_ALL -D__CUDA_ARCH_SPECIFIC__=900 -D__CUDA_ARCH_FAMILY_SPECIFIC__=900
sm_120   (none)
sm_120a  -D__CUDA_ARCH_FEAT_SM120_ALL -D__CUDA_ARCH_SPECIFIC__=1200 -D__CUDA_ARCH_FAMILY_SPECIFIC__=1200
sm_120f  -D__CUDA_ARCH_FAMILY_SPECIFIC__=1200
```
<sub>(`nvcc --dryrun`, CUDA 13.2)</sub>

## Modifications

**Remove the overrides** from `qprep_bf16_fp8_sm90`, `sparse_mla_q8kv8_prefill_sm90` and `fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm`:

- Both SM90 kernels forced `9.0a`; `_cuda_arch_suffix(9, 0)` is unconditionally `"a"`, so the target is identical. They stay SM90-gated — `qprep` keeps its explicit capability check, and the q8kv8 prefill path is validated in `DeepseekSparseAttnBackend.__init__` and skipped via `is_sm90_supported()` in its tests.
- `fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm` forced `12.0a`; detection gives `12.0f`. Verified equivalent by disassembling both builds — identical SASS, only the ELF target/headerflags differ. `120f` additionally runs on SM121.

  | target | SASS instrs | LDSM | STSM | MMA | kernels |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `sm_120a` | 20400 | 344 | 144 | 840 | 8 |
  | `sm_120f` | 20400 | 344 | 144 | 840 | 8 |
  | `sm_120` | **192** | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 |

**Fix the pre-12.9 fallback** that removing the SM120 override exposes. It returned a plain `""` suffix, and as the table above shows, plain `sm_120` is not a usable target for this kernel: without `a`/`f` CUTLASS's SM120 atoms lose LDSM/STSM and the module compiles down to trap stubs, so it asserts at launch instead of failing the build. Fall back to `"a"` — available for SM120 since CUDA 12.8; only the family-specific `"f"` target needs 12.9.

**Gate that on the JIT compiler's version, not `torch.version.cuda`.** The suffix has to follow the compiler that runs the build: a cu129 wheel on a CUDA 12.8 toolkit would pick `sm_120f`, which nvcc 12.8 rejects. `_jit_cuda_version` resolves nvcc the way tvm-ffi's `load_inline` does — `CUDA_HOME` / `CUDA_PATH`, then `$PATH`, then `/usr/local/cuda` — parses `nvcc --version`, and falls back to `torch.version.cuda` only when nvcc can't be probed, matching the order in FlashInfer's `jit.cpp_ext.get_cuda_version`. Unlike FlashInfer it never raises: an unprobeable toolkit degrades to `"a"`, the target that builds on the widest range. The probe only fires for SM120, and is cached.

**Keep `override_jit_cuda_arch`** for compiling off-target arches. Its last in-tree caller, the clangd generator, now builds an explicit `ArchInfo` via `make_jit_cuda_arch` and passes it to `get_default_target_flags` rather than mutating the global. That also fixes `--cuda-target 9.0` emitting `--cuda-gpu-arch=sm_90` where auto-detection emits `sm_90a`. `suffix` now defaults to `None` → `_cuda_arch_suffix`, so the helper retained for off-target builds doesn't reintroduce the missing-`a`/`f` footgun fixed above (`override_jit_cuda_arch(9, 0)` targeted plain `9.0`); passing a suffix explicitly still forces it.

## Accuracy Tests

No behavior change on SM90 (identical target) and none on SM120 with CUDA >= 12.9 (identical SASS); the pre-12.9 path moves from trap stubs to a working `sm_120a` build. Arch-gated tests are unchanged and skip off-target:

```
test_qprep_bf16_fp8_sm90.py test_sparse_mla_q8kv8_prefill_sm90.py test_fp8_blockwise_gemm.py
  -> 482 skipped (SM100 host)
test_kernel_inventory.py -> 5 passed
test_clamp_position.py test_concat_mla.py -> 158 passed   # exercises the JIT compile path
```

The clangd generator was run through both branches (`--cuda-target 9.0` → `sm_90a`, `12.0` → `sm_120f`, `8.0` → `sm_80`, auto-detect → `sm_100a`).

All four nvcc-resolution paths were exercised on an SM100 host (nvcc 13.2, torch cu13.0 — the two already disagree there), plus `override_jit_cuda_arch` defaulting and explicit override:

| nvcc resolution | probed | SM120 target |
|---|---|---|
| `$PATH` (no `CUDA_HOME`) | `(13, 2)` | `12.0f` |
| `CUDA_HOME` → stub reporting 12.8 | `(12, 8)` | `12.0a` |
| `CUDA_HOME` nonexistent | `(13, 0)` via torch, warns | `12.0f` |
| no nvcc on `$PATH`, no `CUDA_HOME` | `(13, 2)` via `/usr/local/cuda` | `12.0f` |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not applicable — no kernel source or launch configuration changed.

title: [Fix] Restore online MXFP8 quantization for linear layers
author: b8zhong
body:
## Motivation

Any bf16 checkpoint launched with `--quantization mxfp8` fails at model init because AMD broke it again:

```
ValueError: MXFP8 requires fp8-serialized checkpoint for linear layers.
```

But that is exactly the online quantization path — the weights are meant to be created in bf16 and quantized in `process_weights_after_loading`.

The guard was unreachable when added in #17449 (nested inside `if is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized:`). The `create_fp8_weight_` refactor in #28291 hoisted it out to an `elif`, making it fire. Only linear layers are affected; the MoE path never had this guard.

## Modifications

Drop the `elif use_mxfp8: raise ValueError(...)` branch in `Fp8LinearMethod.create_fp8_weight_`.

title: [Kernel] cutedsl_bf16_gemm: trailing cluster barrier for 2-CTA TGV kernel exit (#32907)
author: QIN2DIM
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #32907
Fixes #32855 

The TGV CuTe DSL GEMM (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/cutedsl_bf16_gemm.py`) synchronizes the 2-CTA cluster only at kernel **entry** (`cluster_arrive_relaxed` / `cluster_wait`, L378/L438). With `use_2cta`, cross-CTA traffic persists until kernel end — peer-redirected mbarrier arrives (L546/L617), multicast `tcgen05.commit` (L747/L754), cluster-coherent TMEM dealloc (L763) — so one CTA can retire while its peer still has in-flight DSM operations targeting it. Under PDL + CUDA graph (successor kernel stealing SMs mid-graph) the two cluster CTAs get descheduled asymmetrically and the straggler faults on the vacated peer. Production signatures observed across three independent reports (`lmsysorg/sglang:kimi-k3` deployments, B300/SM103, DSPARK decode):

- `dmesg`: `NVRM: Xid 13, Graphics SM Cga Exception ... CTA Not Present`
- sglang: `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure` (async — surfaces at the next sync point, e.g. the overlap-scheduler grammar barrier)
- CUDA core dump: `CUDBG_EXCEPTION_CLUSTER_BLOCK_NOT_PRESENT` (block 0 exited while block 1 still emits DSM traffic toward it)

Root-cause analysis, the ~330 MB CUDA core dump, and the proposed fix are all by **@junliu-mde** in #32907. This PR upstreams that fix (3 lines of code + rationale comment).

## Modifications

One change in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/cutedsl_bf16_gemm.py`: a cluster-wide exit barrier at the end of the kernel body, gated to `use_2cta`:

```python
if cutlass.const_expr(self.use_2cta):
    cute.arch.cluster_arrive_relaxed()
    cute.arch.cluster_wait()
```

All 8 warps (256 threads) of both cluster CTAs reach this point after their warp dispatch branch returns, so neither CTA can retire before the peer's tail work (SMEM arrives / TMA / TMEM dealloc) has landed. 1-CTA tactics are unaffected — the barrier is compiled out under `const_expr`. Strictly additive synchronization: no new data flow, the only new risk was deadlock, excluded by the tests below.

## Accuracy Tests

The patch adds synchronization only; arithmetic and dataflow are untouched, so model-output bits are unchanged by construction. Numeric spot-check on the affected kernel (tactic 18, `M=8 N=7168 K=768`, bf16): patched output vs `xW.T` reference — `max|diff| = 0.031` (bf16 rounding floor), identical to the unpatched kernel against the same reference.

Production-path validation on B300 1×8, Kimi-K3 + DSPARK (`lmsysorg/sglang:kimi-k3` @ `c6ad1f26`, via bind-mounted source — sglang installs editable + this kernel is CuTe-DSL JIT, no AOT artifact):

| Case | Base image | With patch |
|---|---|---|
| Single-request decode crossing ~219k-token context (reported trigger) | Xid 13 crash (~219k bf16, ~303k fp8; 3 further crashes overnight) | Survived to **222,436 tokens**, 0 scheduler exceptions, 0 new Xid |
| 1×200k prefill + 3×20k sequential (concurrency 2, 8k out) | — | PASS, all 4 requests |
| 8×~100k concurrent prefills + 8k decode | — | **8/8 PASS** (728k prompt + 65,536 completion tokens) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

tactic-18 PDL CUDA-graph-chain repro from #32907, 100,000 graph replays (idle B300):

| | unpatched | patched |
|---|---|---|
| total wall (startup+compile+100k replays) | ~28-31 s | ~31.4 s |

i.e., the exit barrier (`cluster_arrive`+`cluster_wait`, one per CTA at kernel tail) is within measurement noise. Note: the synthetic repro **does not reproduce** the race on idle GPUs even unpatched (matches @junliu-mde's caveat of ~2.5e8 clean launches) — the race needs real PDL scheduling skew — so this repro validates "no deadlock, no perf regression", and correctness of the fix rests on the core-dump analysis in #32907 + the production A/B above.

Model e2e throughput in the soak: decode ~73 tok/s at 150k context, ~56 tok/s at 222k context — same band as the pre-patch logs in #32855.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). *(matches surrounding style; no line exceeds 88 cols)*
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). *(no unit test added: the race needs PDL scheduling skew that a synthetic test cannot reliably trigger — see #32907's caveat covering ~2.5e8 clean launches; happy to add a tactic-18 compile+numeric smoke if maintainers want one)*
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). *(inline rationale comment at the barrier; no public API/flag change)*
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). *(see sections above)*
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Related issues

- #32855 — same crash signature (DSPARK, long context, Xid 13 CTA Not Present)
- #32924 — same crash signature on the same image; reporter rolled back to the 07-27 image (`74968e5653`), which predates the fused MoE-front path (#32699) that drives this kernel
- #32907 — root-cause analysis + proposed fix by @junliu-mde

## Notes

Worth cherry-picking into the `kimi-k3` overlay branch behind the `lmsysorg/sglang:kimi-k3` images — all three reports come from that image line.

title: [Docs] Add a Conventions section to the add-jit-kernel skill
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> Generated by Claude.

## Motivation

The `add-jit-kernel` skill described every API but never stated the rules that apply across all of them, so each new kernel re-decided them. It also still pointed at the pre-`sglang.kernels` layout: it tells you to create the Python wrapper at `python/sglang/kernels/jit/scale.py` and the test at `test/registered/jit/test_scale.py`, and `test/registered/jit/` contains no test files at all today (all 131 live under `test/registered/kernels/`).

## Modifications

### New `Conventions` section

- **Check where the check is cheapest:** `static_assert` > C++ host check > cached Python > per-call Python. Tensor invariants belong in the C++ launcher; a check Python cannot delegate goes inside the `@cache_once` module factory, which keys on its arguments and therefore runs once per specialisation instead of once per forward. The tutorial's dtype guard moves there.
- **Fixed-width integer types** over `int` / `long` / `long long`, with the narrow exceptions named (unrolled loop counter over a `constexpr` bound, template `int` parameter) and the `int64_t` FFI boundary called out.
- **Doxygen comments in C++**, the way `include/sgl_kernel/` writes them. The Step 1 example is converted to match, since that is what gets copied.
- **ASCII only in C++ and CUDA sources.**
- **`const T* __restrict__` for read-only pointers** — the existing practice in 93 `csrc/` files.
- **Register budget** — keep memory-bound kernels near 64 registers, verify with `-Xptxas -v`.

### Newly documented

- **`ffi.h` gets its own section** — `host::alloc_workspace_tensor` for scratch, plus `ffi::empty` / `empty_like` / `from_blob`, and the fact that allocation goes through `TVMFFIEnvTensorAlloc` (PyTorch's caching allocator) rather than a raw `cudaMalloc`.
- **PDL's two halves are not symmetric.** `griddepcontrol.launch_dependents` only lets the next kernel *start* and orders nothing — matching its asm, which carries no `"memory"` clobber — while `griddepcontrol.wait` is the ordering point. Hence the wait belongs immediately before the first read of upstream data; a kernel that waits on its first line gains nothing.
- `host::is_type<T>` in the `tensor.h` list, and a `TensorMatcher` example mixing a `SymbolicSize` with a plain integer dimension.

### Corrections, each verified against the tree

| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| wrapper at `kernels/jit/scale.py` | `kernels/ops/elementwise/scale.py` (`kernels/jit/` holds only infra) |
| tests at `test/registered/jit/` | `test/registered/kernels/ops/<group>/` |
| benchmarks at `test/registered/jit/benchmark/` | `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/<group>/` |
| `cache_once`, `should_run_full_tests`, `get_ci_test_range` in `utils/compile.py` | `utils/common.py` |
| `const size_t n = N.unwrap()` | `const int64_t n` — `SymbolicSize::unwrap()` returns `int64_t` |
| "`graph_clone_args` covers every read tensor" | it defaults to `"all"`; narrowing it must still cover reads, and written tensors belong in it because they set the rotation count |
| `RuntimeDeviceCheck` listed above `CHECK_CUDA` with no guidance | framed as the function-style alternative, mirroring `RuntimeCheck` vs `CHECK_HOST` |

Also dropped the rule requiring a `// For ...` trailing comment on every `sgl_kernel` include: it contradicted the tutorial's own code block ("Comments for headers are not common in practice"), and only 88 of 492 such includes in `csrc/` follow it.

## Accuracy Tests

Documentation only — no runtime code touched. Verified mechanically:

- Every `python/sglang/...` and `test/registered/...` path in the file resolves on disk, except the four files the tutorial asks the reader to create.
- Every suite name (`base-b-kernel-unit-test-{1-gpu-large,4-gpu-b200,8-gpu-h200}`, `base-b-kernel-benchmark-test-1-gpu-large`, `nightly-kernel-1-gpu`) appears in `test/run_suite.py`; both referenced workflow files exist; `SGLANG_JIT_KERNEL_RUN_FULL_TESTS` resolves via `envs`.
- Every newly documented symbol was read in its header: `alloc_workspace_tensor` (`utils.cuh`), `ffi::empty` / `empty_like` / `from_blob` / `_dummy_deleter` (`ffi.h`), `is_type` and `SizeRef(int64_t)` (`tensor.h`), the two `griddepcontrol` asm statements (`utils.cuh`), `cache_once`'s per-argument keying (`utils/common.py`).
- All fenced code blocks are ASCII and the fences balance; `pre-commit run --files` is clean.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not applicable.

title: [unified-memory] Support MLA-hybrid-Mamba (Kimi-Linear) on the Triton backend
author: ch-wan
body:
## What this does

Extends `--enable-unified-memory` to **MLA-hybrid-Mamba** models (Kimi-Linear), on the Triton attention backend.

Unified memory replaces the two static pools — a full-KV pool and a Mamba/linear-attention state pool, split once at startup by `--mamba-full-memory-ratio` and never rebalanced — with a single shared buffer that two `MultiEndedAllocator`s grow into from opposite ends. The pain it removes is one side idling while the other retracts or OOMs. The MHA-hybrid version already landed upstream; this adds the MLA-hybrid case.

## Design: dense views

The MLA layers have uniform entries (`kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim` = 576 wide for Kimi-Linear), and the page-major envelope is already a legal dense paged pool — so no new physical layout is needed, only index renumbering:

- each layer gets a contiguous view into the envelope starting at byte `l · page_size · E` (`build_dense_mla_views`)
- dense loc `φ(t) = (t // ps) · (ps · L) + t % ps`, layer-independent
- three coordinate systems: **virtual** (what upper layers persist) → **physical** (internal to compaction) → **dense** (handed to the kernel per forward)

Because compaction only rewrites the virtual→physical table, references held above the pool never move. And because the per-layer view is contiguous, **the stock MLA kernels work unmodified**.

## Contents

- `MLASubPoolSpec` + `build_dense_mla_views` (`mem_cache/layout/page_major.py`)
- `UnifiedMLATokenToKVPool` with whole-page envelope `move_kv_cache`
- `translate_kv_loc_dense` in `multi_ended_allocator.py`, keeping `translate_kv_loc`'s physical semantics for compaction hazard tracking
- `UnifiedKVPool` gains `view_tail_pad_bytes` and a sink lower-bound fix (needed once `page_size > 1`)
- KV write path routed through `KVWriteLoc.full_loc` + the `_full_translate` hook
- drops the `not use_mla_backend` assertion in `kv_cache_configurator.py` and forwards `kv_lora_rank` / `qk_rope_head_dim`

### Upstream bug fixed along the way

`fla/chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` hardcodes the linear-attention state slot pitch as `H · V · K`, which mis-addresses any envelope-strided pool. Switched to `initial_state.stride(0)` with int64 indexing. This affects **all KDA × page-major** configurations, not just unified; behavior on contiguous pools is unchanged.

## Tests

New unit tests (`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/`): dense addressing, tail padding, whole-page move, dense translate including across compaction, write routing, the `full_loc` fast path, and a **GPU byte-parity** test.

`test_unified_mla_views.py`, `test_unified_mla_gpu_parity.py`, `test_full_loc_fast_path.py` — verified passing on B300 (single node, 8×B300 SXM6, CUDA 13.0, flashinfer 0.6.15.post1).

## Validation

End-to-end on Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (27 layers = 20 KDA + 7 MLA), single B300, TP1, GSM8K 200q:

| config | GSM8K |
|---|---|
| static two-pool, triton prefill+decode | 0.910 |
| **unified**, triton prefill+decode | **0.910** |

Exact parity with the static baseline on the same commit and GPU.

## Notes for reviewers

- Gating is unchanged and still conservative: unified ⇒ page-major ⇒ full-attention limited to Triton in this PR (the paged MLA kernels are the follow-up), linear/Mamba side Triton-only; spec decode / PD disagg / hicache / DCP remain gated off.
- Based on `9f5655340`; `main` has since advanced ~24 commits, so this wants a rebase before merge.

The follow-up PR stacked on this one opens the full-attention allowlist to the paged MLA backends (`trtllm_mla`, `flashinfer` prefill, `cutedsl_mla`, `tokenspeed_mla`).

title: [unified-memory] Let Kimi-Linear use the paged MLA attention backends
author: ch-wan
body:
> Stacked on #32971 (base is `feature/unified-memory-kimi-linear-triton`). Review that one first; this PR's diff is just the two commits on top.

Some refactor work is needed after Kimi K3 is merged to main.

## What this does

With the dense per-layer MLA views from #32971 in place, the **stock paged MLA kernels can read the unified pool directly** — only their `kv_indices` / block tables need remapping to dense ids. No change to the physical layout, the allocator, or compaction.

So this opens the page-major full-attention allowlist from `{triton}` to the paged MLA backends when `--enable-unified-memory` is set on an MLA model:

| backend | role | how |
|---|---|---|
| `trtllm_mla` | prefill + decode | block table via `create_flashmla_kv_indices_triton`, now fused with `v2p_ptr` + `PAGE_MULT` |
| `flashinfer` | prefill + decode | token-level `kv_indices` remapped to dense, written back **in place** (see below) |
| `cutedsl_mla` | decode | subclasses `TRTLLMMLABackend`, inherits the dense path with zero extra code |
| `tokenspeed_mla` | decode (fp8) | same inheritance |

`flashmla` / `cutlass_mla` share the `create_flashmla` block-table path and can be added the same way once exercised.

### Cuda-graph safety

`trtllm_mla` decode gets a capture-stable dense write-loc buffer (`cuda_graph_out_cache_loc_dense`) filled **out of graph**, so the in-graph `set_mla_kv_buffer` captures no translate. The replay prep zeroes the buffer's tail beyond the raw batch size — without that, pad rows retain stale dense locs from earlier larger replays and scatter garbage KV into live pages (a bug that only appears once a server has load history, and which bf16 can mask through batch saturation).

## Validation

Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (27 layers = 20 KDA + 7 MLA, `kv_lora_rank` 512 + `qk_rope_head_dim` 64), single node 8×B300 SXM6, TP1 per cell, GSM8K 200q. Every cell has a **same-commit, same-GPU static-pool twin**, so the unified column is a delta and not an absolute:

| prefill | decode | KV | static | **unified** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| triton | triton | bf16 | 0.910 | **0.910** |
| trtllm_mla | trtllm_mla | bf16 | 0.905 | **0.895** |
| trtllm_mla | cutedsl_mla | bf16 | 0.915 | **0.915** |
| trtllm_mla | tokenspeed_mla | fp8_e4m3, ps64 | 0.905 | **0.905** |
| flashinfer | flashinfer | bf16 | 0.910 | **0.925** (eager) |

The 0.895–0.925 band is noise: the static arms span the same 0.905–0.915, and each unified arm matches its own twin inside it.

Unit tests: `test_unified_mla_dense_block_table.py` (new) plus the #32971 suite and the allowlist test — 43 passed on B300.

## Correction: flashinfer decode is admitted, not excluded

> **This section replaced an earlier one titled "The allowlist is per role: flashinfer decode is excluded."** That described an interim version of the third commit that was superseded before merge; the description was not updated at the time. What follows is what actually merged. The diagnosis and the numbers below are unchanged and still accurate — only the remedy differs.

The second commit fixes a bug found while validating the first. Admitting `flashinfer` for **decode** under unified served silently wrong output:

| config | GSM8K |
|---|---|
| unified + flashinfer decode + **cuda graph** | **0.000** (Invalid 1.000, reproduced twice, no crash, no warning) |
| unified + flashinfer decode + eager | 0.925 |
| static + flashinfer decode + cuda graph | 0.910 |

Cause: `FlashInferMLAIndicesUpdaterDecode.call_begin_forward` did its virtual→dense remap as a per-forward gather returning a **fresh tensor**, rebinding a local. On replay, the capture-stable buffer the captured kernel actually reads kept the raw **virtual** ids — `fast_mla_decode_plan` ignores its `kv_indices` argument entirely, so the rebind was dead. `trtllm_mla` escaped this only because it was given the out-of-graph capture-stable buffer described above.

**The remedy that merged writes the translation back in place** rather than rejecting the backend:

```python
valid = kv_indices[:paged_kernel_lens_sum]
valid.copy_(self._translate_kv_loc_dense(valid))
```

bounded to the prefix the index kernel just filled, so the stale tail can never index the v2p table out of bounds. This is why a per-role split was not taken: `--attention-backend flashinfer` resolves to flashinfer for *both* roles, so a decode-only rejection would have rejected the only invocation anyone actually uses, leaving only a never-exercised `flashinfer` prefill + `triton` decode mix. `_handle_page_major_kv_layout` therefore keeps a single `allowed_full` set, with `flashinfer` admitted for both roles.

The in-place write is correct because of a flashinfer-side contract: under `use_cuda_graph`, `BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper` keeps the buffer passed at construction as `_kv_indices_buf` and `plan()` copies *into* it rather than rebinding, so the kernel reads exactly the buffer we wrote. No flashinfer patch is needed.

**Post-merge validation** (this was measured after merge; every flashinfer figure above was eager, so the captured path had not actually been run). Kimi-Linear-48B, 2×H200 TP2, `--attention-backend flashinfer`, cuda graph enabled and confirmed replaying (`cuda graph: True` on every decode batch line):

| examples | unified | static twin |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 200 | 0.905 | 0.925 |
| 400 | 0.917 | 0.902 |

Pooled over 600: 0.913 unified vs 0.910 static. The gap changes sign between the two sample sizes — noise, not a regression.

Fusing the remap into `create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton` (`v2p_ptr` + `PAGE_MULT`, as `create_flashmla_kv_indices_triton` already does) remains a worthwhile follow-up — it saves a launch and a temporary, and makes the remap impossible to skip — but it is an optimization, not a correctness prerequisite.

## Two pre-existing issues found, NOT introduced here

Both reproduce on the **static** pool at this commit, so they belong to `main`, not to this PR. Filing separately; noting them here because they shape what a reviewer can reproduce on Kimi-Linear:

1. **flashinfer prefill in a mixed pair crashes.** `ValueError: q.shape[0] (2586) does not match qo_indptr[-1] (664)` from the chunked-MHA path (`flashinfer_mla_backend.py` `mha_chunk_kv_cache.forward` ← `deepseek_common/.../forward_mha.py forward_normal_core` ← `hybrid_attn_backend.py`). Fires whenever flashinfer prefill is paired with a *different* decode backend; a uniform flashinfer pair never hits it.
2. **fp8 × flashinfer prefill materialises the whole KV pool as bf16.** `k_buf = self.token_to_kv_pool.get_key_buffer(layer_id).to(q.dtype)` → `OutOfMemoryError: Tried to allocate 270.37 GiB`. Routing `tokenspeed_mla` through a `trtllm_mla` prefill instead gives the 0.905 == 0.905 row above, so the fp8 decode backend itself is fine.

## Limitations

- **TP1 only.** TP1 is what made an 8-cell parallel sweep cheap (48B bf16 = 98 GB fits one 275 GB B300) and it exercises the same dense-view code, but it does not cover TP-sharded behavior. Worth a TP8 confirmation before this is called a platform result.
- Correctness only — no perf A/B, no retraction or long-context stress in this round.
- Based on `9f5655340`; wants a rebase (`main` is ~24 commits ahead).

title: [MLX] Upgrade to Torch 2.13/MLX 0.32+ and redesign the Torch-MLX tensor bridge
author: yeahdongcn
body:
## Motivation

MLX 0.32 can import Torch MPS allocations directly, while Torch 2.13 changes
the runtime and DLPack edge cases that the Apple Silicon integration must
support. The existing bridge stages MPS tensors through CPU memory, obscures
borrowed-versus-owned lifetimes, and pays payload-sized copies. Separately,
diffusion's `SGLANG_USE_MLX` norm override is not selected by normal MPS
`CustomOp` dispatch; forcing those norms through Torch-MLX crossings is slower
end to end.

This PR upgrades the `srt_mps` runtime, fails fast on unsupported Torch/MLX
pairs, separates owned copies from scoped zero-copy borrows, and removes the
unreachable diffusion-only MLX fallback. It does not replace the existing SRT
MLX runner; the stacked
[yeahdongcn/sglang#7](https://github.com/yeahdongcn/sglang/pull/7) consumes these
bridge primitives while redesigning that backend.

## Modifications

- Update `srt_mps` in `python/pyproject_other.toml` to Torch 2.13.0, MLX >=
  0.32.0, TorchVision 0.28.0, TorchAudio 2.11.0, and TorchCodec 0.15.0.
  The versions stay directly in `srt_mps`, matching the existing extra layout;
  `all_mps` inherits them through `srt_mps`. MLX keeps a 0.32.0 minimum but
  has no upper bound; startup accepts newer stable MLX releases. TorchAudio
  2.11 remains intentional and was validated with the tested Torch 2.13 MPS
  stack. CPU and standalone `diffusion_mps` dependency lists are unchanged.
- Move the SRT MLX version/device validation to the earliest model-independent
  `ServerArgs` bootstrap. With `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1`, SGLang requires stable
  Torch 2.13.x and stable MLX >= 0.32.0. Older MLX, Torch outside 2.13.x, and
  rc/dev builds fail before model path resolution/downloads and before the
  dummy-model short circuit. With the flag unset, importing SGLang still does
  not import MLX.
- Redesign `tensor_bridge.py` around explicit ownership and batching:
  - `torch_to_mlx` creates and materializes MLX-owned storage when the result
    must outlive its Torch source.
  - `MlxTensorView` and `borrow_torch_tensors` provide persistent and batched
    zero-copy MPS borrows while retaining every Torch storage owner.
  - `mlx_call` and `mlx_call_multi` validate the target before work, fence
    Torch producers once, keep all borrowed inputs alive through lazy
    evaluation, evaluate ordinary multi-output results at one shared `mx.eval`
    boundary, batch the additional materialization boundary required by
    negative-stride outputs, and export them through DLPack.
  - `mlx_to_torch` uses evaluated DLPack views for MPS and explicit CPU views.
    Positive-stride layouts, including CPU float64, remain zero-copy.
    Negative-stride MLX views are materialized because Torch 2.13's DLPack
    importer otherwise aborts the process instead of raising a Python
    exception; unsupported CPU dtypes fail instead of silently narrowing.
  This PR intentionally owns these shared Torch-MLX bridge primitives. The
  stacked MPS redesign in
  [yeahdongcn/sglang#7](https://github.com/yeahdongcn/sglang/pull/7) consumes
  them for Torch-owned model weights and provider outputs, while its
  provider-specific invalidation callbacks and phase timing stay in that PR.
- Remove `mps_fallback.py`, route diffusion MPS kernels to native Torch
  fallbacks, and use `F.layer_norm`/`F.rms_norm` instead of the old manual
  decomposition. The shared fallback remains compatible with both the
  default Torch 2.11 and CPU-backend Torch 2.12 stacks. RMSNorm preserves the
  optional-bias and input-dtype contracts even with fp32 parameters. The
  removed rotary and scale/shift entries were
  already aliases to Torch implementations; only the norm entries had
  MLX-specific implementations.
- Remove diffusion's `SGLANG_USE_MLX` runtime handling and clarify in the
  existing documentation that the variable applies only to SRT serving. SRT
  keeps its existing `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1` opt-in.
- Add Torch 2.13-compatible Triton import-stub symbols used by Inductor on
  MPS.
- Rebase the branch onto upstream `main` at `978244d67148`; update VAE and
  Transformer component loaders to the upstream unified residency API so MPS
  layerwise offload remains valid after the upstream loader refactor.

The diffusion MLX norm path is intentionally dropped after tracing and
measurement. `CustomOp.dispatch_forward()` routes MPS to `forward_native`, so
the legacy MLX override is unreachable in the normal production graph. Sana
instrumentation confirmed zero legacy entrypoint calls, and forcing all 58
norms per DiT forward through MLX was slower end to end. Isolated large fp32
LayerNorm microbenchmarks sometimes favored MLX by a few percent, but the result was not
robust across the common fp16/bf16 cases and did not justify repeated
framework crossings. A future fully MLX-resident diffusion path can be
evaluated separately.

## Accuracy Tests

- `PATH="$PWD/sglang-metal/bin:$PATH" SGLANG_USE_MLX=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 ./sglang-metal/bin/python test/run_suite.py --hw mlx --suite stage-a-unit-test-mlx`
  - **21/21 registered test files passed locally** on Apple M1 at PR head
    `c1f34a81d1`, including bridge, startup runtime gate, Triton-stub, and
    diffusion fallback coverage.
  - The focused bridge/runtime/diffusion-loader bundle passed **121 tests plus 36 subtests** after the rebase.
- All four new test files are registered in `stage-a-unit-test-mlx`.
  `test_diffusion_torch_fallback.py` is additionally registered in
  `base-a-test-cpu`, `base-b-test-cpu`, and `base-b-test-cpu-arm64`.
- The same six fallback UTs passed **6/6** in isolated Torch 2.11.0 and 2.12.0
  CPU environments, including fp16/bf16 inputs with fp32 parameters.
- Runtime tests verify Torch 2.12/2.14, MLX 0.31, and Torch/MLX rc/dev builds
  are rejected, while stable Torch 2.13 patch releases and stable MLX releases
  from 0.32.0 onward (including future minor versions) are accepted.
  Incompatible versions abort `ServerArgs` creation even for
  `model_path="dummy"`; missing MLX, unavailable PyTorch MPS, and unavailable
  MLX Metal each produce actionable startup errors. The disabled path
  constructs `ServerArgs` without importing MLX.
- Bridge ownership checks cover owned/scoped/persistent lifetimes, source
  mutation and deletion, single-fence batched borrows, shared-eval multi-output
  calls, bfloat16/non-contiguous views, CPU float64 and unsupported dtypes,
  autograd detachment, invalid-target fail-fast behavior, and negative-stride
  materialization in an abort-safe subprocess.
- SRT serving smoke with local `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`: both
  `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1` and the no-env Torch-MPS path returned **200** from
  `/health` and `/generate`. For prompt `The capital of France is` with
  greedy 8-token decoding, both paths returned identical output token IDs
  `[12095, 13, 576, 6722, 315, 9625, 374, 1083]` and text
  `Paris. The capital of France is also`.
- Sana 600M, prompt `A small red cube on a plain white background`, seed 42,
  256x256, 4 steps: native Torch output and the hypothetical all-MLX norm
  output remained visually consistent (PSNR 41.95 dB; max pixel delta 50).
  The final `mlx_call` image was byte-identical to the earlier explicit-
  keepalive MLX image.
  The ordinary Sana path recorded 58 Torch norm calls per DiT forward and zero
  legacy norm-fallback entrypoint calls. After the rebase, a native Torch-MPS
  Sana smoke with the same 256x256/4-step configuration produced a valid RGB
  PNG in 24.87s with 6.33GB peak memory.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Environment: Apple M1, macOS 26.5.2, Torch 2.13.0, MLX 0.32.0. All timings
include the required producer/consumer synchronization. The operation table
reports end-to-end norm-call timings, including bridge/export and
synchronization, rather than raw kernel-only timings. It is one representative
median-after-warmup run; an independent rerun preserved the common-Sana
ordering but flipped whether large-fp32 MLX was slightly ahead or behind.

| Case | Torch native | MLX owned copy | MLX scoped borrow |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Sana RMSNorm `(1,300,1152)` fp32 | 230 us | 676 us | 259 us |
| Sana LayerNorm `(1,256,1152)` bf16 | 254 us | 913 us | 324 us |
| Flux LayerNorm `(1,4096,3072)` fp32 | 2508 us | 4763 us | 2441 us |

Bridge A/B directly calls the final `mlx_call(lambda a: a, tensor)` API
against the pre-change CPU-staging implementation at the branch merge base
(Apple M1, Torch 2.13.0, MLX 0.32.0). The table reports the range of per-batch
p50 values across three independent batches; each batch used 5 warmups and 20
measured samples with producer/consumer synchronization:

| Logical tensor | dtype / payload | Old CPU-staging p50 range | Final `mlx_call` p50 range | Minimum paired speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `(4096,4096)` | fp32 / 64 MiB | 32.134-57.424 ms | 0.0410-0.0871 ms | 368.8x |
| `(4096,4096)` | bf16 / 32 MiB | 10.301-34.715 ms | 0.0293-0.0418 ms | 351.2x |
| `(4096,8192)` | bf16 / 64 MiB | 16.896-22.184 ms | 0.0407-0.0617 ms | 273.7x |

The old MPS round-trip staged payload through CPU/NumPy in both directions.
The final `mlx_call` path aliases the Metal allocation through DLPack,
removing the payload-sized copies; the synchronized wrapper/barrier cost was
29-87 us across these repeats. The same-shape bf16 case is 32 MiB because each
element uses two bytes; the final row adds a true 64 MiB bf16 payload.

This zero-copy result applies to the scoped-borrow API, not to an MLX array
that must own its storage after the call. For that ownership contract, the
64 MiB fp32 materialized copy is about 4.08 ms versus about 60 us for a scoped
borrow. This is why the API separates owned and borrowed semantics instead of
exposing an unchecked `copy=False` default.

Final-API Sana 4-step E2E forced-MLX experiment using `mlx_call` for all 58
norms per DiT forward (clean paired repeat):

| Metric | Torch native | MLX scoped borrow | MLX penalty |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Denoising step median | 720.18 ms | 1170.40 ms | +62.5% |
| DiT forward median | 375.06 ms | 581.92 ms | +55.2% |
| Steady DiT median (drop first 2) | 353.42 ms | 581.92 ms | +64.7% |

A second same-configuration measurement had higher Torch variance and a
smaller penalty (+20.6% step, +21.9% DiT), but MLX was slower in both runs.

## Checklist

- [x] Formatted with repository pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Added and ran registered unit tests.
- [x] Registered the shared diffusion fallback in CPU CI.
- [x] Updated Apple Metal and diffusion documentation.
- [x] Included accuracy and speed evidence above.
- [x] CPU dependency pins remain unchanged.

## Review and Merge Process

This is a draft for review of the ownership contract and the diffusion path
decision. Please review the Torch/MLX lifetime semantics first; CI should run
the MLX, CPU, JIT-kernel, and multimodal-generation change paths before
promotion. In particular, the draft-gated MLX, Xeon CPU, and ARM64 CPU jobs
must complete before this PR is marked ready.

title: feat(attention): add architecture-owned SM12x FA4 kernels
author: lucifer1004
body:
## Motivation

SGLang currently routes SM12x FA4 through an SM80-derived forward path. That
path uses the older mainloop and does not expose the SM12x TMA dataflow, paged
KV, SplitKV, or relative/shared-bias support.

This PR adds an architecture-owned SM12x implementation and keeps its kernel,
scheduler, and runtime policy under
`sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fa4_sm120`.

## Modifications

- Add TMA-based SM12x forward and paged-decode kernels with warp MMA.
- Add persistent scheduling and runtime-SM-count-aware tile selection instead
  of assuming a fixed GPU size.
- Support BF16/FP16, MHA/GQA/MQA, dense and variable-length attention, paged
  KV, SplitKV, global/local/noncausal masks, attention sinks, packed GQA, and
  relative/shared bias with shearing.
- Add SM12x-owned host policy, launch-plan caching, preallocated-output paths,
  CUDA Graph-safe decode plans, and TVM-FFI launch fast paths.
- Route SM12x through a narrow architecture dispatch bridge while leaving
  SM80/SM9x/SM10x kernel ownership unchanged.
- Replace the previous SM80-derived SM120 fallback and add comprehensive
  SM12x regression tests.

## Accuracy Tests

The focused SM12x test file passes in full:

```text
test_flash_attention_4_sm120.py: 53 passed
```

Coverage includes dense/varlen attention, BF16/FP16, MHA/GQA/MQA,
asymmetric Q/V dimensions, packed and unpacked GQA, paged KV, SplitKV,
attention sinks, relative/shared bias, preallocated output, CUDA Graph replay,
PDL, and specialization-cache ordering.

The 684 measured prefill SKU-case pairs all passed comparison against the
SGLang Triton baseline:

| GPU | Cases | Maximum absolute difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell | 228 | 0.0078125 |
| RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell | 228 | 0.0078125 |
| GB10 (SM121) | 228 | 0.015625 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Prefill

The common three-way matrix contains 228 matched cases per GPU: BF16/FP16,
MHA/GQA/MQA, head dimensions 32/64/96/128/192->128/256, sequence lengths
128/512/2048/6144, dense and ragged varlen inputs, and causal-global,
causal-local-with-sink, and noncausal-global modes.

Each case uses five warmups followed by three shuffled trials with 20 CUDA
event samples per trial. PR and SM80-fallback runs are each paired with the
same byte-identical Triton implementation. `PR / SM80` below is the ratio of
those paired speedups, which normalizes process-level clock drift.

| GPU | SMs | PR / Triton | Wins | SM80 fallback / Triton | Wins | PR / SM80 fallback | Wins |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell | 188 | 3.027x | 228/228 | 1.274x | 112/228 | 2.377x | 222/228 |
| RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell | 110 | 3.311x | 228/228 | 1.574x | 150/228 | 2.104x | 224/228 |
| GB10 (SM121) | 48 | 3.610x | 228/228 | 2.087x | 171/228 | 1.730x | 205/228 |

Across all 684 equally weighted SKU-case pairs, the PR is **3.308x over
Triton with 684/684 wins**, and **2.053x over the SM80-derived fallback with
651/684 wins**.

![SM12x FA4 three-way prefill speedup](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/lucifer1004/869b4fb5b4da6c46f09ed9a45ccff7bc/raw/f0353430a86c8b6b257f3a58eb8bd33ed4963a1a/fa4-sm12x-threeway-speedup.svg)

Representative absolute latency:

| GPU | Case | PR | Triton | SM80 fallback |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| RTX PRO 6000 | MHA, BF16, HD64, L128 | 22.66 us | 32.22 us | 60.85 us |
| RTX PRO 6000 | local+sink GQA, BF16, HD128, L2048 | 31.12 us | 161.34 us | 84.64 us |
| RTX PRO 6000 | MHA, BF16, HD256, L6144 | 456.29 us | 2588.77 us | 571.95 us |
| RTX PRO 5000 | MHA, BF16, HD64, L128 | 14.64 us | 21.10 us | 33.42 us |
| RTX PRO 5000 | local+sink GQA, BF16, HD128, L2048 | 30.37 us | 198.30 us | 91.81 us |
| RTX PRO 5000 | MHA, BF16, HD256, L6144 | 745.12 us | 3487.39 us | 827.04 us |
| GB10 (SM121) | MHA, BF16, HD64, L128 | 18.14 us | 24.93 us | 38.37 us |
| GB10 (SM121) | local+sink GQA, BF16, HD128, L2048 | 66.75 us | 437.20 us | 158.91 us |
| GB10 (SM121) | MHA, BF16, HD256, L6144 | 2108.42 us | 13977.18 us | 1823.94 us |

The few PR/fallback losses are concentrated in long ragged HD256 and dense
noncausal GQA, most visibly on the 48-SM device. Every measured PR case still
beats Triton.

Theoretical useful-compute SOL and logical-memory roofline ratios:

| GPU | Compute SOL median / max | Logical-memory ratio median / max |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell | 14.2% / 72.4% | 10.8% / 83.3% |
| RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell | 35.6% / 82.0% | 14.2% / 80.0% |
| GB10 (SM121) | 34.0% / 74.3% | 40.8% / 165.1% |

The logical-memory ratio uses one compulsory Q/K/V read and one output write
against peak DRAM bandwidth. Repeated resident tensors can be served from
cache, so values above 100% are not literal measured DRAM SOL.

### Paged decode

Paged decode covers 108 cases per GPU across MHA/GQA/MQA, head dimensions
64/128/256, batch sizes 1/8/32, KV lengths 128/512/2048/8192, and page size
64. CUDA Graph replay is the kernel-focused comparison; eager and synchronized
wall timings include host overhead.

| GPU | Graph PR / Triton | Graph wins | Eager PR / Triton | Wall PR / Triton |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell | 1.311x | 92/108 | 1.432x | 1.317x |
| RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell | 1.317x | 96/108 | 1.424x | 1.286x |
| GB10 (SM121) | 1.214x | 90/108 | 1.377x | 1.307x |

The SM80-derived fallback explicitly rejects paged KV and SplitKV, so it is
reported as unsupported rather than assigned a synthetic timing. The fallback
also does not support the relative/shared-bias path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format changed code with the repository `prek` hooks.
- [x] Add focused SM12x unit and regression tests.
- [x] No user-facing documentation update is required for this internal
  attention-kernel implementation.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance.

title: Add flashinfer rmsnorm + quant fusion support SM90, SM100, SM120
author: DevashishLal-CB
body:
## Motivation I had been working on the torch compile fusion approach for this for a while and am not sure what's gonna happen with it but the kernel gains are significant and can easily be done directly, this builds upon the norm quant kernels added to flashinfer which are faster than the kernels I tried writing for jit kernels (cuz they use clusters) **H100 Gains are in the range of 1.5%~2.5%** **B200 Gains are in the range of 4%~5%** references - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/10549 - https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/2243 To be merged in two parts due to AOT kernel changes - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33469 - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33471 ## B200 Gains
Metric BS4 BS8 BS16 BS32 BS64 BS128 BS256 Mean
Benchmark duration +5.03% +4.92% +3.48% +3.09% +2.25% +0.91% +1.37% +3.01%
Input token throughput +5.30% +5.15% +3.59% +3.18% +2.31% +0.92% +1.39% +3.12%
Output token throughput +5.29% +5.15% +3.59% +3.18% +2.31% +0.92% +1.39% +3.12%
Total token throughput +5.30% +5.15% +3.59% +3.18% +2.31% +0.92% +1.39% +3.12%
Mean E2E latency +5.04% +4.91% +3.54% +3.09% +2.27% +0.55% +1.19% +2.94%
Median E2E latency +4.64% +4.47% +3.57% +2.78% +2.07% +0.94% +1.00% +2.78%
Mean TTFT +24.47% +19.82% +0.59% +9.13% +6.76% -4.46% +5.92% +8.89%
Median TTFT -2.09% -2.86% +4.38% -3.61% +2.38% +5.67% +7.71% +1.65%
Mean TPOT +4.58% +4.70% +3.76% +2.81% +2.05% +0.80% +0.77% +2.78%
Median TPOT +4.58% +4.38% +3.75% +2.84% +1.90% +0.79% +0.64% +2.70%
Mean ITL +4.58% +4.70% +3.76% +2.81% +2.05% +0.80% +0.77% +2.78%
Median ITL +4.61% +4.73% +3.47% +3.11% +1.93% +0.76% +0.43% +2.72%
## Modifications Fuse RMSNorm with downstream static per-tensor FP8 activation quantization using FlashInfer's `rmsnorm_quant` and `fused_add_rmsnorm_quant` kernels. The norm can emit an already-quantized FP8 activation, allowing the following FP8 linear layer to skip its activation quantization. On SM90, channelwise CUTLASS FP8 GEMMs now consume the scalar activation scale directly instead of expanding it per token, eliminating the extra copy that reduced the fusion benefit. ### Changes - Add fused RMSNorm + static FP8 quantization, including residual paths and FP16/BF16 output dtype propagation. - Enable compatible FP8 linear layers to consume pre-quantized `(fp8, scale, original_dtype)` inputs. - Support both native FP8 and compressed-tensors W8A8 FP8 linear methods. - Pass downstream projections to Llama and Qwen2 norms so the fused path can be selected. - Add `--enable-flashinfer-rmsnorm-fp8-quant`, disabled by default. - Add native scalar-A/channelwise-B broadcasting to the SM90,SM100,SM120 CUTLASS FP8 GEMM while preserving dynamic per-token and non-SM90,SM100,SM120 behavior. **These changes give a small boost to without fusions also** - Add correctness, dispatch, dtype, scalar-broadcast, and benchmark coverage. title: fix(fa4): isolate sheared-bias workspaces by CUDA stream
author: lucifer1004
body:
## Motivation

FA4 uses a reusable staging buffer when converting relative bias into the
column-aligned sheared-bias layout consumed by the attention kernel. The
workspace is currently cached only by CUDA device.

Each relative-bias call launches a producer-consumer pair on its current
stream:

1. the shearing kernel writes the staging buffer;
2. the attention kernel reads that buffer.

CUDA preserves this ordering within one stream, but not between independent
streams. Two concurrent calls on the same device therefore reuse the same
buffer without cross-stream synchronization, allowing one shearing kernel to
overwrite data that another attention kernel has not consumed yet.

## Modifications

- Cache eager-mode sheared-bias workspaces by CUDA device and raw stream
  identity instead of device alone.
- Preserve the existing grow-only reuse policy independently for each stream.
- Query the raw current stream directly to avoid allocating a
  `torch.cuda.Stream` wrapper on the host hot path.
- Add `clear_shear_bias_workspace()` so callers can explicitly drop retained
  staging buffers.
- Keep the existing fake-tensor and CUDA Graph capture behavior unchanged;
  both paths continue to bypass the eager workspace cache.
- Add a deterministic two-stream regression test covering buffer isolation,
  same-stream reuse, event-ordered concurrent access, and cache clearing.

## Accuracy Tests

Run this script against upstream and this PR. CUDA events force stream B's
write between stream A's write and read, so the result does not depend on
scheduler timing:

```python
import torch

from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.flash_attn.cute.interface import (
    _shear_bias_empty,
    _shear_bias_workspace,
)

device = torch.device("cuda", torch.cuda.current_device())
stream_a, stream_b = torch.cuda.Stream(), torch.cuda.Stream()
_shear_bias_workspace.clear()

with torch.cuda.stream(stream_a):
    workspace_a = _shear_bias_empty((4096,), torch.uint8, device)
with torch.cuda.stream(stream_b):
    workspace_b = _shear_bias_empty((4096,), torch.uint8, device)

a_ready, b_done = torch.cuda.Event(), torch.cuda.Event()
observed_a = torch.empty_like(workspace_a)

with torch.cuda.stream(stream_a):
    workspace_a.fill_(1)
    a_ready.record()
with torch.cuda.stream(stream_b):
    stream_b.wait_event(a_ready)
    workspace_b.fill_(2)
    b_done.record()
with torch.cuda.stream(stream_a):
    stream_a.wait_event(b_done)
    observed_a.copy_(workspace_a)

torch.cuda.synchronize()
print(
    {
        "same_pointer": workspace_a.data_ptr() == workspace_b.data_ptr(),
        "cache_entries": len(_shear_bias_workspace),
        "observed_by_a": observed_a.unique().tolist(),
    }
)
assert torch.all(observed_a == 1)
```

Observed results:

| Implementation | Workspace pointers | Cache entries | Value observed by stream A |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Upstream device-only cache | Aliased | 1 | 2 |
| This PR | Distinct | 2 | 1 |

Focused test result:

```text
test_shear_bias_workspace_is_stream_local_and_clearable: 1 passed
```

The test also verifies that a smaller request on the same stream reuses the
existing allocation and that `clear_shear_bias_workspace()` empties the
workspace cache.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

A host-only cache-hit microbenchmark ran 50,000 workspace requests per sample
for seven samples:

| Implementation | Median host time per cache hit |
| --- | ---: |
| Upstream device-only cache | 4.34 us |
| This PR | 4.53 us |

The stream-safe lookup adds approximately 0.19 us per relative-bias call. This
uses the raw current-stream query; constructing a `torch.cuda.Stream` wrapper
on every call was measured separately and intentionally not used.

No attention-kernel instructions or launch configuration are changed by this
PR.

## Checklist

- [x] Format changed code with the repository `prek` hooks.
- [x] Add a deterministic multi-stream regression test.
- [x] No user-facing documentation update is required for this internal
  workspace-management fix.
- [x] Provide correctness reproduction and host-overhead measurements.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance.

title: fix(dsa): use FlashInfer fused top-k for packed PAGED rows
author: zianglih
body:
## Motivation

@humansand

- [sgl-project/sglang#32490](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32490) added an SGL-kernel fallback because FlashInfer previously used one `row_starts` tensor for both score and page-table windows.
- [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4169](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4169) adds `page_table_row_starts`, allowing independent score and page-table origins. It is available in [FlashInfer v0.6.17rc1](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/tag/v0.6.17rc1).
- The rebased PR is validated against the official FlashInfer v0.6.17rc1 CUDA 13 artifacts. It is waiting for final v0.6.17 and the aligned SGLang Python, Docker, and runtime pins.

## Modifications

- Remove the packed-PAGED FlashInfer-to-SGL-kernel fallback.
- Pass batch-global `row_starts` as the score-window origin and request-local `page_table_row_starts` as the page-table origin.
- Preserve `row_to_batch`, `dsa_graph_safe=True`, and the SGL-only top-k-v2 policy.
- Extend the fused backend-equivalence test to cover shifted packed-PAGED rows and verify both FlashInfer start tensors.

This PR intentionally does not change FlashInfer dependency pins. Upstream main currently pins `0.6.15.post1`.

## Accuracy Tests

Static validation at rebased head `e074a275de1290cc5f284ee16a90644d5119cd74`:

```text
python3 -m compileall -q python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_topk_backend.py test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsa_indexer.py
```

All passed.

- `flashinfer-python==0.6.17rc1`
- `flashinfer-cubin==0.6.17rc1`
- `flashinfer-jit-cache==0.6.17rc1+cu130`

SGLang was installed from the exact rebased PR head with `--no-deps`.

Focused DSA top-k coverage:

```bash

  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsa_indexer.py::TestDSAIndexer::test_topk_v2_respects_topk_backend
```

```text
3 passed, 15 warnings, 30 subtests passed in 14.34s
```

A CUDA graph smoke test captured and replayed the packed-PAGED FlashInfer path, then mutated the scores and shifted every global `row_starts` origin before replaying again:

No model-level accuracy benchmark was run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. This change selects the configured FlashInfer fused transform instead of the temporary SGL-kernel fallback; no performance claim is made.

title: [Fix] Clear stale FlashInfer BF16 MoE index cache
author: zianglih
body:
## Motivation

@humansand

Colocated RL weight updates pause and offload the rollout model before loading new weights. `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod` caches FlashInfer permutation-index tensors on the GPU, so those tensors can point to released memory after the model resumes. Reusing them during post-load processing can corrupt the shuffled BF16 expert weights.

[sgl-project/sglang#28676](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28676) fixed the equivalent MXFP8 cache, but mixed-precision checkpoints with BF16 experts use this separate cache in `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`.

ModelOpt NVFP4 quantized experts do not need the same clear: `prepare_static_weights_for_trtllm_fp4_moe()` creates its permutation-index dictionary locally for each post-load call. The BF16 experts in the first/last layers, plus the BF16 shared experts, use `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`, whose persistent instance cache is what this PR clears.

## Modifications

Clear the FlashInfer TRT-LLM BF16 permutation-index cache once at the start of each post-load processing cycle. The rebuilt indices are still reused across experts within that cycle.

## Accuracy Tests

- Targeted external regression test for two consecutive BF16 FlashInfer post-load cycles: `1 passed`.
- DeepSeek V3.2 5-layer MXFP8 Miles E2E on 8x B200 with 8-GPU training and 8-GPU colocated rollout:
  - dense FP8 GEMM backend: `flashinfer_cutlass`
  - MoE backend: `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`
  - 3/3 rollouts and 24/24 training steps completed
  - the one injected rollout-engine failure was detected and one engine was recovered
  - weight-checker lifecycle completed and the Ray job succeeded
- GLM-5.2 5-layer ModelOpt NVFP4 Miles E2E on 8x B200 with 8-GPU training and 8-GPU colocated rollout:
  - environment: FlashInfer `0.6.15.post1`; image-pinned SGLang commit `3fe50eddf881b4f33c60c1867af84eeb1626d91d` with only this PR's patch applied
  - rollout: four TP2/DP2/EP2 engines with `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`
  - 2/2 rollouts, 2/2 training steps, and 3/3 weight-update/resume cycles completed
  - Ray job succeeded without a crash or hang
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed.

No test file is included in this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The cache clear runs only during weight post-processing, not in the model forward path.

title: [AMD] Drop redundant FP8 bpreshuffle scale transpose via fused AR kernel
author: yichiche
body:
Dependent on https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4478, merged and aiter update on 08/21
## Motivation

On gfx95 (MI35x, ROCm >= 7.2) the gfx95 bpreshuffle FP8 block-scale GEMM consumes the per-group activation scale in a **column-major** layout, whereas the fused all-reduce + RMSNorm + per-group-FP8-quant kernel emits it **row-major**. To bridge the two, the fused-quant path in `layernorm.py` currently runs an explicit post-kernel transpose (`materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale`, i.e. `scale.t().contiguous().t()`) on every eligible layer. That `.contiguous()` launches an extra copy kernel per fused-quant call — pure overhead in the decode-latency-bound regime where the model is dominated by many small kernel launches.

aiter's fused kernel already has a compile-time `TRANSPOSE_SCALE` template (ROCm/aiter#3652) that can write the scale directly in the column-major layout the bpreshuffle GEMM wants, at zero extra cost (it only changes the store-index math). This PR plumbs that flag through so the fused kernel emits the transposed scale itself, and drops the redundant post-kernel transpose on the fused-success paths.

The emitted layout is byte-for-byte identical to what `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale` produced (column-major storage `(num_groups, M)` viewed as `(M, num_groups)`, stride `(1, M)`), so this is a numerics-preserving change.

This is FP8-only. The MXFP4 path uses a different kernel (`custom_fused_ar_rms_mxfp4_quant`) and is untouched.

**Dependency:** requires the paired aiter change that forwards `transpose_scale` through `custom_fused_ar_rms_per_group_quant` / `fused_ar_rms_per_group_quant` / the ops stub to the (already capable) C++ op, plus a bundled-aiter pin bump. Without it, the fused-kernel call falls back (the flag is ignored / raises and is caught), so this PR should land together with / after the aiter bump.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/distributed/communication_op.py`: add a `transpose_scale` kwarg to `tensor_model_parallel_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_quant_per_group` and forward it to the group coordinator.
- `python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py`: add `transpose_scale` to `GroupCoordinator.fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_quant_per_group` and forward it into the `ca_comm.custom_fused_ar_rms_per_group_quant` call.
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py`: pass `transpose_scale=use_bpreshuffle` to both fused per-group-quant calls (the `keep_bf16=False` attention path and the `keep_bf16=True` GDN emit_bf16 path), and remove the now-redundant `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale` on the two fused-success return paths.
- The two separate-per-group-quant **fallback** paths intentionally keep `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale`: `per_1x128_quant`'s own `transpose_scale` byte-shuffles the scale into a different physical arrangement, not the column-major layout this GEMM consumes.
- The FP8 linear consumer (`aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear`) is unchanged: the scale layout reaching it is identical, and its own `materialize` call becomes an idempotent no-op (`.contiguous()` short-circuits on an already-column-major tensor).

## Accuracy Tests

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4 (MI35x), `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`, gsm8k (1319 questions):

| Metric | Reference (with transpose) | This PR (fused transpose_scale) |
|---|---|---|
| Accuracy | 0.947 | **0.955** |
| Invalid | 0.008 | 0.008 |

Within run-to-run noise (marginally higher) — the change is numerics-preserving.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

**Kernel-level confirmation (conc4 profile, IL8192/OL1024, 8 steps):** the fused kernel template flipped `TRANSPOSE_SCALE` false→true (`allreduce_fusion_kernel_1stage_per_group<…Lb0ELb0E>` → `<…Lb0ELb1E>`, 354 calls; `local_device_load_rmsnorm_quant_per_group_naive` Lb0→Lb1, 59 calls). The removed transpose copy (`elementwise_kernel_manual_unroll<…nocast>`) dropped from **960 → 547 = −413**, exactly `354 + 59` (one `.contiguous()` per fused-quant call). Total GPU kernel launches: 11555 → 11142.

**End-to-end (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, IL8192/OL1024, num_prompts = concurrency × 10):**

| Concurrency | Output tok/s (before → after) | Δ throughput | Median TPOT ms (before → after) | Δ TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 438.8 → 443.1 | +0.98% | 8.44 → 8.41 | −0.37% |
| 8 | 744.7 → 754.0 | +1.25% | 9.67 → 9.54 | −1.30% |
| 16 | 1058.3 → 1071.4 | +1.24% | 13.53 → 13.30 | −1.67% |
| 32 | 1525.8 → 1536.3 | +0.69% | 18.05 → 17.97 | −0.42% |
| 64 | 1960.7 → 1973.7 | +0.66% | 27.27 → 27.09 | −0.65% |
| 128 | 2615.1 → 2621.7 | +0.25% | 38.42 → 38.38 | −0.09% |

Output-throughput geomean **+0.84%**; decode TPOT consistently lower across the sweep. A small but clean, zero-risk reduction — the benefit is the removal of ~per-layer kernel launches in the decode path.

- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Fix] Disable --enable-symm-mem under CUDA graphs on Kimi hybrid models
author: hnyls2002
body:
Symmetric-memory allocations are per-forward, so an address taken from that pool during graph capture is neither reserved for the graph's lifetime nor at the same offset on every rank. Under capture this corrupts DSPARK speculative decoding: accept collapses to 1.000, or (worse) the server silently emits garbage while reporting accept pinned at the ceiling, with no error. The flag is now forced off on Kimi hybrid archs unless every phase runs eager; the auto-probed K3 fused all-reduce is faster than the symm-mem path anyway.

title: [unified-memory] Support fa3, the default MLA backend on pre-Blackwell hosts
author: ch-wan
body:
Follow-up to #32971 / #32972. Those two made `--enable-unified-memory` work for Kimi-Linear, but the page-major full-attention allowlist still omitted `fa3` — which is exactly what an unspecified `--attention-backend` resolves to for an MLA model on Hopper. So on H100/H200 the feature **failed at startup under its own default configuration**, and you had to know to pass `--attention-backend triton`.

This is the pre-Blackwell counterpart of the same gap #32972 had for `flashinfer`, on the more common hardware.

## What this does

Adds `fa3` to the allowlist and remaps its page table to dense ids. **No fa3 kernel change is needed.** Its absorbed-MLA path reads the pool only through `page_table[b, i]` into `get_key_buffer(l)` reshaped to `(-1, page_size, heads, dim)`, and `build_dense_mla_views` hands out a *contiguous* per-layer view — so the last-dim slices and both reshapes behave exactly as they do on the static pool. The only thing missing was the table in DENSE id space instead of the virtual one `req_to_token` holds.

There is already a precedent for remapping at that site: the SWA pool threads `translate_loc_from_full_to_swa` through the same page-table build.

## Two paths, one site each

| path | where | why there |
|---|---|---|
| captured decode | folded into `normal_decode_set_metadata`'s fused gather (`v2p_ptr` / `PAGE_MULT`) | the capture-stable `page_table` is written **already translated** — no separate pass a caller can forget, and no temporary that must stay pointer-stable across replays |
| eager | one remap at the tail of `init_forward_metadata` | ~9 branches build `page_table` above it; funnelling means none can be missed |

Both default to the identity, so the statically-partitioned pool is byte-identical.

Two details that matter:

- In the general metadata kernel the remap derives from `page_table_val`, **not** `page_index` — the SWA branch below still needs the virtual value.
- The eager remap sits deliberately *before* the `// page_size` reduction, in token space. `dense(t) = phys_page * (ps * L) + t % ps`, so `dense(page_start) // ps == phys_page * L`, which is exactly the dense page id the kernel wants. That is what lets one site serve both page sizes, and it inherits `translate_kv_loc_dense`'s tombstone clamp so an unwritten `req_to_token` slot lands in the reserved page-0 sink rather than at a negative page id.

`unified_mla_hooks` moves out of `flashinfer_mla_backend` into `layers/attention/unified_mem_hooks.py`: three unrelated backend families consume it now, and fa3 should not have to import the flashinfer MLA module to get it.

## Validation

Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct, 2×H200 SXM TP2, `--enable-unified-memory`, GSM8K:

| attention backend | examples | score |
|---|---:|---:|
| **resolved default (`fa3`), no backend flags** | 400 | **0.917** |
| static pools, baseline | 400 | 0.915 |
| `fa3`, `--page-size 64` | 200 | 0.905 |

1σ is ~0.015 at n=400 and ~0.021 at n=200. The default run is the point of the change — it resolves to `fa3` (confirmed in the server log) and matches the static baseline. The `--page-size 64` run exercises the general metadata kernel; the default (page_size 1, since `fa3` imposes no page-size constraint) exercises the ps1/no-SWA fast path.

## The nightly test drops its backend pin

`test_kimi_linear_unified_memory.py` no longer passes `--attention-backend triton`, so it runs the configuration a user actually gets (`fa3` on the `nightly-4-gpu` H100 runner). This is deliberate: **both** defects found in review on #32972 were reachable only under a resolved default, which a pinned test hides by construction.

## Tests

- `test_unified_mla_dense_block_table.py` (+5 GPU cases): fa3's fused metadata kernels are byte-identical with the hooks absent; match the python reference on both the ps1 fast path and the general path; handle the single-full-attention-layer case (multiplier 1 with a real v2p); and agree page-for-page with the block table `create_flashmla_kv_indices_triton` builds for `trtllm_mla`.
- `test_page_major_backend_allowlist.py`: `fa3` moves from the rejected set to the dense-MLA set, keeping the MHA-path and no-unified-memory rejections intact.
- Pre-existing `test_normal_decode_set_metadata.py` passes unchanged (16 cases + 8 subtests), confirming the identity defaults.
- 54 unified-memory unit cases pass in total.

## One bug worth flagging

My first eager-funnel version passed the 2-D `page_table` straight to `translate_kv_loc_dense`, whose `page_size == 1` path goes through `index_select` — which requires a 1-D index. Caught before the verification run; it now flattens and reshapes. Note the failure mode: the `page_size > 1` path uses advanced indexing and *would* have accepted 2-D, so this would have crashed only on the default configuration. Same class of gap as the two review findings, which is the argument for the unpinned nightly test above.
