title: fix(xpu): enable compressed-tensors FP8 W8A8 on XPU (RedHatAI FP8-dynamic models)
author: vshekhawat-hlab
body:
## Motivation

compressed-tensors FP8 W8A8 quantized models (e.g. RedHatAI's `*-FP8-dynamic` family — `Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509-FP8-dynamic`, `Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct-2503-FP8-dynamic`, `granite-4.0-h-small-FP8-dynamic`, `NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2-FP8-dynamic`) currently fail to serve on XPU. The very first failure happens at layer-construction time, before any kernel dispatch:

```
AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled
```

Fixing that surfaces two further, distinct XPU-specific issues before the model actually serves and generates correctly.

## Modifications

- `compressed_tensors.py` (`CompressedTensorsConfig`): `_check_scheme_supported` unconditionally called `torch.cuda.get_device_capability()`, which is CUDA-only. Only `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8` has a real XPU-usable kernel path today (via the existing device-agnostic `_apply_fallback_scaled_mm` in `fp8_utils.py`, not a missing native kernel); every other capability-gated scheme (NVFP4/cutlass, Marlin-based W8A16Fp8, WNA16, ...) is explicitly rejected with a clean `RuntimeError` on XPU instead of crashing on the CUDA-only call.
- `fp8_kernel.py`: the non-CUDA/non-MUSA branch never imported `sgl_per_token_quant_fp8`/`sgl_per_tensor_quant_fp8` for XPU, even though sgl-kernel-xpu registers both natively — this caused a `NameError` on the first forward pass once the above crash was fixed.
- `fp8_utils.py` (`apply_fp8_linear`): the activation-quant padding decision (`num_token_padding=17`, meant to make `torch._scaled_mm` more performant on CUDA for small batches) was only skipped when `cutlass_fp8_supported` (CUDA-only). sgl-kernel-xpu's per-token quant kernel requires `output_q` to exactly match `input`'s shape and doesn't support padded output, raising a shape-mismatch `RuntimeError` whenever a forward pass had fewer than 17 rows (e.g. small prefill/decode steps).
-  fp8.py (Fp8MoEMethod.apply): the native sgl-kernel-xpu MoE fast path was taken unconditionally on XPU, before checking the explicitly-selected MoE runner backend.
  This made --moe-runner-backend triton a no-op on XPU for this quantization scheme — the native kernel path was still hit and raised "current MoE does not support
  use_fp8_w8a8" even when the Triton runner had been explicitly requested. Now skips the native XPU path when the runner backend is explicitly triton, falling through to
  the existing Triton dispatch below.
- internvl.py: InternVLChatConfig has no top-level num_experts — the MoE config lives on the nested llm_config (the text-backbone config). Fixes an AttributeError when
  loading MoE-based InternVL variants.
- runtime_context.py (get_stream): replaced a hardcoded torch.cuda.Stream() with torch.get_device_module(device).Stream(), so the named process-level side stream is 
  created on whichever device backend is active instead of always assuming CUDA.
- topk.py (biased_grouped_topk_gpu, XPU path): the topk_sigmoid kernel requires correction_bias to be float32. The CUDA branch a few lines above already casts it; the 
 XPU branch passed it through unchanged, raising RuntimeError: correction_bias must be float32 on the first generation request for some MoE models. Now cast to float32 
  before the call, matching the CUDA branch.

## Accuracy Tests

Verified locally end-to-end in a docker container (XPU backend, Intel Arc Pro/BMG) with the patched sglang installed in place of the image's baked-in copy:

- `RedHatAI/Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509-FP8-dynamic` (TP=1, `--attention-backend intel_xpu`) serves and evaluates gsm8k (5-shot) correctly:
  - `exact_match,flexible-extract = 0.5891 ± 0.0136`
  - `strict-match = 0.5390 ± 0.0137`
- Regression check that the shared code paths touched here don't affect other backends/schemes:
  - All three changes are gated behind `if _is_xpu:` / `elif _is_xpu:` branches that are new no-ops on every other platform; `cutlass_fp8_supported`-driven CUDA behavior is unchanged (verified by re-reading every other call site of the touched functions — `scaled_fp8_quant`'s other callers in `fp8_utils.py` are gated by `if _is_cuda:`/`if _is_hip:`, never reaching the changed XPU branch on other devices).
  - No currently-passing XPU model can regress from these changes: any compressed-tensors quantized model on XPU previously hit the `_check_scheme_supported` crash unconditionally at layer-construction time (before this PR), so none could have been passing beforehand.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — these are correctness/compatibility fixes for an existing fallback code path (`_apply_fallback_scaled_mm`), no new kernel or scheduling changes. The activation-quant padding skip on XPU has a minor performance implication (an extra kernel-launch on small batches that would otherwise reuse a padded buffer), but padding was never functional on XPU before this PR (it crashed), so there's no regression relative to current behavior.

- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [trtllm_mha] perf: Stop allocating per-layer scratch inside the decode CUDA graph
author: mattteochen
body: ## Motivation Two allocations in the TRTLLM-MHA decode path emit a fill kernel per attention layer per forward, and CUDA-graph capture bakes them into every replay: 1. FlashInfer allocates and zeroes a fresh multi-CTA KV counter buffer on every `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` call when the caller supplies none — even though its own docstring says the kernel self-resets the counters at the end of each launch and that callers should own the buffer. 2. `fused_fp8_qkv_kv_cache` builds `float32 [1]` scale tensors with `torch.ones()` when `layer.k_scale` / `v_scale` are `None`, which is every layer of any checkpoint without KV scales. Three launches per full-attention layer, moving 4, 4 and ~600 bytes. They also sit *between* two PDL-linked kernels, so `_fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate`'s `gdc_launch_dependents()` was signalling a `FillFunctor` instead of `fused_fp8_qkv_kv_cache`'s `PDLWaitPrimary`. ## Modifications `trtllm_mha_backend.py` only: - Lease one counter buffer per backend instance via the existing `make_persistent_multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer` (already used by `trtllm_mla_backend` and `dsa_backend`), sized for the widest batch the backend can see, and pass it to the decode call and all three target-verify calls. FlashInfer rejects an undersized buffer, never an oversized one. - Hold one `float32 [1]` ones tensor on the backend for layers with no checkpoint KV scale. Both are allocated at backend construction, outside graph capture. ## Correctness Semantically an identity: the same constant `1.0` scale reaches the kernel, and the counter buffer contract is FlashInfer's documented one. GSM8K 5-shot, full 1319 questions, `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --parallel 128`, temperature 0, `--max-new-tokens 4096`: | arm | GSM8K | |---|---:| | main | 0.822 | | this PR | **0.813** | Run-to-run spread on this harness is ~2pp, larger than the gap between arms. ## Performance Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, 4xB200, TP4, `trtllm_mha` + `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE, fp8 weights + fp8 KV cache, bs=1, input-len 8192. **-90us per decode step, 1.64% of a 5.490ms step.** 45 launches removed (3 per full-attention layer); the full-attention layer span drops 6.02us, x15 such layers. | | main | this PR | |---|---:|---:| | kernels per decode step | 1656 | 1611 | | full-attn layer span | 91.10us | 85.09us | | GDN layer span | 77.85us | 77.63us | main: PR: The prologue in execution order, medians over the 15 full-attention layers: ``` main this PR _fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate 2.82us _fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate 2.66us gap-after 0.35us gap-after -0.03us <- PDL restored FillFunctor 1.12us (removed) FillFunctor 1.05us (removed) fused_fp8_qkv_kv_cache 3.78us fused_fp8_qkv_kv_cache 3.62us gap-after 0.32us gap-after -0.70us <- PDL restored FillFunctor 1.18us (removed) fmhaSm100fKernel 10.98us fmhaSm100fKernel 10.98us ------------------------------------- ------------------------------------- window 22.24us window 16.48us ``` --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #30963620445](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30963620445) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #30963620279](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30963620279)

title: [Fix] Honor FlashMLA natural-log LSE in DCP reduction
author: CyberSecurityErial
body:
## Motivation

FlashMLA returns natural-log softmax LSE, while the MLA DCP merge paths currently treat all decode LSE as base-2. As a result, FlashMLA + DCP computes incorrect cross-rank softmax weights and attention output.

For partition functions `Z = [2, 8]` and a second-shard local output of `10`, the correct contribution is `8`. Interpreting `[ln(2), ln(8)]` with `exp2` produces `7.2330317` instead.

Fixes #33064.

## Modifications

- Make the AG/RS Triton correction kernel select `exp/log` or `exp2/log2` through a compile-time LSE-base flag.
- Propagate that flag through `cp_lse_ag_out_rs_mla`.
- Select natural-log LSE for the `flashmla` attention backend in both MLA DCP communication paths:
  - all-gather LSE + reduce-scatter output;
  - A2A/FlashInfer-A2A LSE reduction.
- Keep base-2 as the default, so FlashInfer MLA behavior is unchanged.
- Add a GPU regression for the exact natural-log weighting error and a routing test for backend selection.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested on one NVIDIA H20 GPU with the branch source based on `585a7d05e384c79ee17bf3185c7469fe8ce75946`:

```text
PYTHONPATH=/work/flashmla-lse/python python3 -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/kernels/test_dcp_lse_combine.py \
  -k "flashmla_natural_log_lse_correction or flashmla_selects_natural_log_lse"

2 passed, 21 deselected in 24.83s
```

The full related test file also passes:

```text
PYTHONPATH=/work/flashmla-lse/python python3 -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/kernels/test_dcp_lse_combine.py

23 passed in 25.88s
```

The warnings emitted by the container are unrelated environment/deprecation warnings; there were no test failures.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This fixes output correctness. The log-base branch is a Triton `tl.constexpr`, so it is specialized at compilation rather than selected per element at runtime.

- [x] Add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation (not needed: no public API or user-facing configuration change).
- [x] Provide accuracy test results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [Fix] Allow flashinfer_sparse_mla DSA backend for HiSparse on SM120 FP8 KV
author: gongwei1027
body:
## Motivation

`--enable-hisparse` cannot start at all on SM120/SM121 (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 5090) with FP8 KV cache, because two parts of the argument pipeline disagree about which DSA backend is legal.

The resolution pass already selects `flashinfer_sparse_mla` for GLM DSA models on SM120 with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` — it is the only DSA kernel available on that architecture (`_dsa_split_backend_resolution`, `is_glm_sm12_fp8` arm in `python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/overrides.py`). But the HiSparse validator in `hisparse_hook.py` still whitelisted only `flashmla_kv` for FP8 KV, so the server dies during argument validation:

```
ValueError: HiSparse supports DSA prefill backend(s) ['flashmla_kv'] on this
platform with --kv-cache-dtype=fp8_e4m3, but got
--dsa-prefill-backend=flashinfer_sparse_mla. Please use
--dsa-prefill-backend=flashmla_kv or omit it.
```

The suggestion in that message is also unsatisfiable on SM120: `flashmla_kv` is not available there, and omitting the flag re-derives `flashinfer_sparse_mla` and fails again.

The runtime path already supports this combination on current `main` — `flashinfer_sparse_mla` and its SM120 kernel path landed in #26928 — so only the startup-time allow-list was stale. The end-to-end run below confirms this.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/hisparse_hook.py`:
- Add `flashinfer_sparse_mla` to `HISPARSE_CUDA_DSA_BACKENDS_BY_DTYPE["fp8_e4m3"]` and to the unknown-dtype fallback set in `_hisparse_allowed_backends`.
- Fix the error message to list the full allowed set instead of suggesting a single default backend.

No supported configuration changes for other platforms or KV-cache dtypes:
- BF16 KV still allows only `flashmla_sparse`.
- ROCm still allows only `{tilelang, aiter}`.
- Arch/model/device narrowing for `flashinfer_sparse_mla` is unchanged and still enforced later by `flash_mla_sm120._validate_flashinfer_sparse_mla_backend`, which rejects it for anything other than GLM DSA + FP8 KV + SM120/SM121. This change only stops HiSparse from pre-emptively rejecting a backend the resolver itself chose.

`docs_new/docs/advanced_features/hisparse_guide.mdx`: document the SM120/SM121 GLM + FP8 case in the DSA backend note and Key Notes.

`test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py`: add `test_hisparse_accepts_flashinfer_sparse_mla_on_cuda_fp8` to `TestHiSparseDsaBackendPolicy`, asserting both prefill and decode validators accept `flashinfer_sparse_mla` under FP8 KV.

## Unit Tests

Run on real SM120 hardware in the nightly image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20260729-16a52bff` (`sglang.__version__ == 0.0.0.dev1+gcb12a1547` — the tag carries the pipeline trigger SHA, the built source is `cb12a1547`). That revision's `hisparse_hook.py` is byte-identical to this PR's base, so the baseline behavior it exhibits is the behavior this PR changes:

```
$ git diff cb12a1547 e3d4f48e55 -- python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/hisparse_hook.py
(empty)
```

```
$ pytest test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py -k HiSparse -q
# baseline (before this PR's test case)
12 passed, 106 deselected, 15 warnings in 8.73s

# with this PR's test case added
test_hisparse_accepts_flashinfer_sparse_mla_on_cuda_fp8 PASSED [ 30%]
13 passed, 106 deselected, 15 warnings in 7.39s
```

Allow-set assertions with the patched hook:

```
ALLOWSET_fp8  = ['flashinfer_sparse_mla', 'flashmla_kv']
ALLOWSET_bf16 = ['flashmla_sparse']
Set DSA backends for GLM FP8 KV Cache on SM120/SM121: prefill=flashinfer_sparse_mla, decode=flashinfer_sparse_mla.
Ran 4 tests in 0.827s
OK
```

Negative control — reverting only the fp8 allow-set entry, everything else unchanged, reproduces the original startup failure:

```
REVERTED allow-set: ['flashmla_kv']
ValueError: HiSparse supports DSA prefill backend(s) ['flashmla_kv'] on this platform
with --kv-cache-dtype=fp8_e4m3, but got --dsa-prefill-backend=flashinfer_sparse_mla.
```

CI coverage note: the upstream SM120 PR-test runners are 5090 (32 GB), which cannot host GLM-5.2, so no CI job exercises this configuration end-to-end. CI covers the allow-list policy through the CPU-only unit test above; the hardware validation below covers the rest.

## Accuracy Tests

Full PD-disaggregated GLM-5.2-NVFP4 deployment:

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| GPU | 2 nodes × 8 × RTX PRO 6000 (SM120, 96 GB), TP=8 per node |
| Model / quantization | GLM-5.2, `modelopt_fp4` |
| KV cache dtype | `fp8_e4m3` |
| Attention backend | `dsa`, prefill = decode = `flashinfer_sparse_mla` |
| HiSparse config | `{"top_k": 2048, "device_buffer_size": 4096, "host_to_device_ratio": 10}` |
| Topology | P (prefill, no HiSparse) → D (decode, `--enable-hisparse --disable-radix-cache`), mooncake transfer over `mlx5_0` |
| SGLang build | same image as the unit tests above (`nightly-dev-20260729-16a52bff`), with this PR's `hisparse_hook.py` applied |

Decode instance startup with the fix:

```
Set DSA backends for GLM FP8 KV Cache on SM120/SM121: prefill=flashinfer_sparse_mla, decode=flashinfer_sparse_mla.
The server is fired up and ready to roll!
```

Without the fix the decode instance never reaches this point — it aborts in argument validation with the `ValueError` quoted above.

Single-request correctness through the P→D path:

```
$ curl http://router:8000/generate -d '{"text":"What is 1+1?","sampling_params":{"max_new_tokens":20,"temperature":0,"ignore_eos":true}}'
{"text":" I will give brainliest.\n\nStep-by-step explanation:\n\n1+1=2\n\n(If this", ...
 "finish_reason":{"type":"length","length":20},"prompt_tokens":7,"completion_tokens":20,
 "e2e_latency":0.5475991275161505}
HTTP=200 TIME=0.549638
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This PR only changes a startup-time allow-list — no kernel, no forward path — so it cannot affect throughput on any platform. As a liveness check that the unblocked path is usable rather than merely startable, a sustained load through the PD router (54 in-flight requests, input 32k / output 4k, 660 s) held steady state at 54/54 running requests with 701.73 tok/s average gen throughput (354 decode batches) and zero retractions.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).

title: perf(hisparse): 128-bit non-temporal swap-in copy on ROCm
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
## Motivation

`transfer_item_warp` exists **twice** in the tree:

| file | used by | ROCm today |
|---|---|---|
| `python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/kvcacheio/transfer.cu` | HiCache L2→L1 gather (prefill/TTFT) | being widened in #30024 |
| `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/hisparse.cuh` | **HiSparse swap-in miss copy (decode)** | plain 64-bit scalar, no non-temporal hint |

#30024 widens the first. This PR does the equivalent for the second, which #30024 does not touch. Note that `hisparse.cuh`'s own **CUDA** branch (lines 53-79) already issues 128-bit paired `ld.global.nc.v2.b64`, so today the ROCm path is strictly narrower than the CUDA path *in the same file*.

The swap-in matters because it is on the decode critical path: `swap_in_selected_pages` runs once per C4 layer per decode step, on the main stream, between that layer's indexer and its attention, so it does not overlap compute. Each miss is one wavefront reading an item straight out of pinned host DRAM.

## Modifications

ROCm branch of `transfer_item_warp` only:

- 128-bit path using a `__vector_size__(16)` `uint32` vector, taken when both operands are 16B-aligned **and** `item_size_bytes >= WARP_SIZE * 16`.
- `__builtin_nontemporal_load` for the source (streamed in once, consumed by the attention kernel, no reuse to preserve). The **store is deliberately left cached** — its destination is the device buffer the next kernel reads.
- The pre-existing 64-bit loop is retained; it covers the sub-threshold and unaligned cases in full and serves as the remainder tail. No API, config, or template changes. No CUDA behavior change.

### The item-size gate is load-bearing — the ungated version was a regression

My first version widened unconditionally. Benchmarked with `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/kvcache/bench_hisparse.py` on MI355X (gfx950), it was **14-22% slower** at that benchmark's default `ITEM_SIZE_BYTES = 512`.

The cause is lane utilisation on wave64, not copy width. A 16B-per-lane step spans only `item_size_bytes/16` lanes, so at 512B the wide path engages **32 of 64 lanes** while the 8B path engages all 64 — for the *same* iteration count. An isolating run separates the two factors (median of 3 alternating reps, `miss_rate=0.2`, `hot=4096`, vs unmodified baseline):

| variant | 512B b1 | 512B b10 | 1024B b1 | 1024B b10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128-bit + non-temporal, **ungated** | +18.8% | +21.6% | -10.9% | -0.3% |
| 128-bit, cached load, ungated | +14.3% | +20.2% | -11.1% | -2.0% |
| 64-bit + non-temporal (width unchanged) | -0.1% | +2.1% | +0.4% | +1.4% |

So the non-temporal hint alone is neutral (a useful control: 81.1 vs 81.2 us), and the regression was entirely the width. Hence the `item_size_bytes >= WARP_SIZE * 16` gate.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

`bench_hisparse.py` on MI355X (gfx950), median of **3 alternating reps** of 5 timed rounds each, `miss_rate=0.2`, `hot_buffer_size=4096`:

| batch | 512B before → after | 1024B before → after |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 82.5 → 82.7 us (+0.2%) | 105.9 → **84.8 us (-19.9%)** |
| 10 | 88.7 → 88.6 us (-0.1%) | 116.2 → **101.3 us (-12.8%)** |
| 24 | 114.1 → 114.4 us (+0.3%) | 201.6 → 200.3 us (-0.6%) |
| 100 | 397.9 → 397.4 us (-0.1%) | 762.0 → 757.9 us (-0.5%) |

512B is neutral by construction (gate not taken). 1024B — the DeepSeek-V4 unified-KV C4 item size, and exactly `WARP_SIZE * 16` — gains at low and mid batch.

**Why the gain converges to ~0 at batch >= 24.** Converting misses x item size / time into achieved H2D bandwidth on the unmodified kernel at 1024B:

| batch | misses | achieved H2D |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 410 | 4.0 GB/s |
| 10 | 4,100 | 34.7 GB/s |
| 24 | 9,840 | 49.4 GB/s |
| 100 | 41,000 | 55.3 GB/s |

The kernel is latency-bound at low batch — which is where a wider load helps — and by batch ~24 it is already at ~90% of the ~55 GB/s host-fabric ceiling #30024 reports for this part, so copy width stops mattering. Anyone at high batch should not expect this change to show up end to end; the lever there is moving fewer bytes, not moving them wider.

**Incidental finding that may be worth acting on separately:** `bench_hisparse.py` only measures a *sequential* gather. `_make_top_k_tokens` builds misses as `hot_buffer_size + arange(num_misses)` and `host_cache_locs` is `arange(...)`, so every miss reads a contiguous host slot, whereas real HiSparse misses are scattered across the host pool. I re-ran with `host_cache_locs` randomised over an 8 GiB pinned pool and the difference is negligible (1.00-1.05x at batch 1/10/24/100), so the benchmark is not misleading for bandwidth here — but the sequential pattern is not obvious from reading it, and a random mode would make that explicit.

## Accuracy Tests

Adds `test_load_cache_to_device_buffer_miss_copy_is_byte_exact` to `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hisparse.py`.

Coverage gap it closes: every pre-existing case that runs on ROCm uses `ITEM_SIZE_BYTES = 8 * fp32 = 32`, an exact multiple of 16, and the only non-multiple-of-16 cases (the DSV4 paged ones, 576B value + 8B scale) are `@pytest.mark.skipif(is_hip(...))`. So the boundary between the wide copy and the narrower remainder loops had no coverage at all on ROCm. The new case sweeps 16/20/24/40B items at both 16B-aligned and unaligned sources, asserts the miss lands byte-exact, and asserts neighbouring slots are not corrupted by an over-copy.

Run on MI355X against both the unmodified and the patched kernel: the new cases pass on both (they are regression protection for the new seam, not a demonstration of an existing bug), and the rest of the suite is unchanged — same 13 passed / 2 skipped on both. Two cases in that file (`fast_path_overwrites_stale_output`, `batched_with_padding`) fail identically with and without this patch in my environment, so they are unrelated to it.

Also verified separately that the new helper is byte-exact against the previous one for item sizes {8, 12, 16, 17, 24, 64, 576, 1024, 1152} at aligned and unaligned offsets across all 64 lanes.

Related: #30024, #31341, #28874.

## Checklist

- [x] Format: `black` clean; C++ change confined to one ROCm `#ifdef` branch, <= 120 cols.
- [x] No public API / config / docs surface touched.
- [x] Unit test added for the new code path; full suite run before/after on MI355X.

## Motivation

Enable Inkling-small MoE kernels on DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121). The existing Triton configs and grouped-GEMM staging assumptions target larger GPUs; sm_121 has less shared-memory headroom, so default configs can fail or underperform without platform-specific tuning.

## Modifications

- Add `is_dgx_spark()` in `common.py` (CUDA + compute capability `(12, 1)`), cached via `lru_cache`.
- In `inkling_moe.grouped_gemm_triton`, reduce `num_stages` by 1 on DGX Spark to fit shared-memory limits.
- Add Helion autotune config `silu_and_mul_interleaved_sm_121.json` for the silu-and-mul interleaved MoE path on sm_121 (copied from sm_100).

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

N/A. Config and `num_stages` tuning for sm_121 only; no intentional change to numerics beyond kernel launch parameters. This is an enablement PR. Model outputs normal language after tested on DGX Spark.

title: [ModelOpt FP4] Support online MoE weight quantization
author: zianglih
body:
## Motivation

@humansand

- Add online ModelOpt FP4 quantization for eligible MoE expert weights from BF16, FP16, or FP8 checkpoints.
- Current contract:
  - `modelopt_fp4`:
    - Serialized NVFP4: load packed weights and checkpoint per-tensor FP32 activation scales; missing scales default to `1.0`, and loaded scales overwrite the fallback.
    - BF16/FP16 source: quantize eligible MoE expert weights to NVFP4 at load time; dense and excluded layers keep their source precision.
    - FP8 source: dequantize eligible MoE expert weights to BF16, then quantize them to NVFP4; other layers keep their source quantization.
    - Online conversion uses per-tensor FP32 activation scales. Existing serialized-checkpoint behavior under `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_NVFP4_PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION=1` is unchanged.
  - `nvfp4_online`:
    - Quantize eligible BF16/FP16/FP8 MoE expert weights at load time with online per-token FP32 activation scales.
    - Support only `flashinfer_trtllm` and `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`; per-tensor activation behavior belongs to `modelopt_fp4`.
  - Draft models:
    - For non-serialized sources, `--quantization modelopt_fp4` is inherited by the draft unless overridden; both target and draft use the generic online MoE conversion path.
    - For a serialized target checkpoint whose BF16 MTP experts are excluded, explicit `--speculative-draft-model-quantization modelopt_fp4` opts the draft into online conversion; inherited draft quantization remains checkpoint-driven.
    - Qwen3.5 MTP distinguishes serialized and online `modelopt_fp4`. Existing DeepSeek, GLM, Bailing, and Kimi NextN/EAGLE draft constructors still opt out and remain outside this generic draft path.
  - Scope: MoE expert weights only. Dense, shared, and excluded layers keep their source representation. MXFP8 source requantization is not supported.
- Related work:
  - Initial online NVFP4 implementation:
    - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26083
  - Corrects the activation contract introduced in:
    - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31382
    - ~~CuTe DSL with FlashInfer A2A or DeepEP used per-tensor activation scaling under `nvfp4_online`.~~ That behavior is now routed through `modelopt_fp4`.
  - Pending CuTe DSL integration for the `nvfp4_online` per-token activation contract:
    - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28354

## Modifications

- Reuse the `nvfp4_online` weight loader through a thin `modelopt_fp4` adapter instead of duplicating conversion logic.
- Use `DefaultModelLoader` for ordinary online `modelopt_fp4`; preserve explicit ModelOpt restore, save, and export workflows.
- Convert FP8 MoE weights through BF16 before NVFP4 quantization while preserving source quantization for other layers.
- Initialize missing per-tensor FP32 activation scales to `1.0`; checkpoint tensors overwrite the fallback.
- Scope exact FP4 quantization math to load-time conversion.
- Track explicit draft quantization separately from target-inherited defaults and route excluded Qwen3.5 MTP experts accordingly.
- Remove stale `nvfp4_online` backend claims inherited from the per-tensor design and document the two activation contracts.

## Accuracy Tests

- Focused B200 unit tests:
  - Environment: 8x NVIDIA B200, `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260801-e4c4faf8`, PyTorch `2.11.0+cu130`, CUDA `13.0`.
  - Result: `27 passed, 15 warnings, 15 subtests passed`.
  - Command:

    ```bash
    python3 -m pytest -q \
      test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_modelopt_nvfp4.py \
      test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_modelopt_loader.py
    ```

- Static checks: `pre-commit run --all-files` passed at the current head.
- Model-output accuracy: not run locally; no model-level result is claimed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- Not run; this PR adds load-time conversion and quantization routing, not a new kernel.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: perf(startup): skip unused PyTorch headers for KV VMM allocator stub
author: ajtulloch
body:
## Summary

`KvVmmArena` builds a small allocator stub for each KV arena. `load_inline` adds `torch/extension.h` by default.

The stub does not use PyTorch APIs. This change disables implicit headers and keeps the allocator ABI unchanged.

The standalone reproduction in the commit message produced these results:

| Mode | Time | Library size |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Implicit headers | 12.191s | 1246.5 KiB |
| No implicit headers | 0.232s | 69.9 KiB |

## Test plan

- `python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_vmm_backing.py`
- `uvx pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_vmm_backing.py`

title: Support DeepGEMM for standard MoE dispatch
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

The `deep_gemm` MoE runner can be selected with the standard token dispatcher, but the existing integration assumes the DeepEP weight and activation layouts. Standard MoE layers therefore do not consistently requantize both expert weights to UE8M0, and the standard dispatch path does not provide a compact local-expert layout for DeepGEMM.

This change completes the standard-dispatch integration while preserving the existing DeepEP path.

Co-authored-by: Sam Li (@samuellees)

## Modifications

- Requantize both gate/up and down expert weights when a standard MoE layer uses the DeepGEMM runner.
- Quantize Blackwell FP8 activations directly with their UE8M0 scales instead of rounding the scales after quantization.
- Use the masked DeepGEMM layout when expert parallelism keeps the local expert buffer small.
- Use a compact, graph-static layout for the remaining standard-dispatch cases, including tensor-parallel execution without expert parallelism.
- Ignore non-local expert assignments during scatter and post-permute while preserving CUDA Graph-compatible buffer shapes.
- Use an uninitialized BF16 compact input buffer because scatter writes every valid row before the grouped matrix multiplication consumes it.
- Mark every compact-layout padding row with expert index `-1`, so DeepGEMM skips padding without a separate initialization kernel.
- Extend the existing UE8M0 and MoE scatter tests to cover standard-layer weight processing and real masked-versus-compact DeepGEMM execution.
- Extend the existing end-to-end standard-dispatch kernel test to cover FP8 and BF16 expert weights and validate every padding index.

## Tests

The existing registered MoE kernel test file completed with **52 passed** on an NVIDIA GB300. The FP8 and BF16 cases both execute the standard-dispatch pre-permute, grouped matrix multiplications, activation, down projection, and post-permute path.

## Accuracy Tests

Model-level validation completed at [commit `02d9f2e642`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/02d9f2e642907ceadb60279165a9359a47d436b4) with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` on 16 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs. The server used PP2/TP8/EP1, the standard dispatcher with the DeepGEMM MoE runner, FP8 weights, BF16 KV and SSM caches, and full decode CUDA Graph through batch size 256. The configured breakable prefill graph was skipped by the existing runtime compatibility guard because some model layers do not apply Standard GQA.

```bash
python -m sglang.test.run_eval \
  --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --eval-name gsm8k \
  --num-examples 1319 \
  --num-shots 5 \
  --num-threads 256 \
  --max-tokens 16384 \
  --temperature 0
```

The evaluator completed every scored request without request-level errors: **1,288 correct and 26 incorrect, for 0.9802130898 accuracy (1,288/1,314)**. The 1,314 denominator is expected because the five-shot harness reserves five records from the 1,319-record GSM8K test file as fixed demonstrations and scores the remaining records.

## Speed Tests

The matched matrix ran at [commit `02d9f2e642`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/02d9f2e642907ceadb60279165a9359a47d436b4). The current head adds only [Black formatting](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/bc7a37ab3f); an AST comparison excluding source positions is identical before and after that formatting commit.

Both lanes used the same Qwen3.5 checkpoint, 16 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs, PP2/TP8/EP1, exact 8,192-token input and 1,024-token output lengths, and concurrency 1–128. Each lane was repeated three times. The only runtime difference was:

```text
moe-runner-backend: flashinfer_trtllm -> deep_gemm
```

Values are median total tokens/s/GPU across the three runs. Classification compares the full three-run ranges; every range below is non-overlapping.

| Concurrency | FlashInfer TRTLLM | DeepGEMM | Change | Classification |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|:---|
| 1 | 75.49 | 55.18 | -26.90% | DeepGEMM slower |
| 2 | 104.87 | 77.79 | -25.82% | DeepGEMM slower |
| 4 | 207.41 | 157.64 | -23.99% | DeepGEMM slower |
| 8 | 398.99 | 283.63 | -28.91% | DeepGEMM slower |
| 16 | 697.80 | 484.15 | -30.62% | DeepGEMM slower |
| 32 | 1,140.88 | 743.62 | -34.82% | DeepGEMM slower |
| 64 | 1,715.61 | 1,037.06 | -39.55% | DeepGEMM slower |
| 128 | 2,420.24 | 1,410.13 | -41.74% | DeepGEMM slower |

All 48 formal results completed their full request counts with exact input and output lengths and no request-level errors. Full decode CUDA Graph captured on all 16 ranks in all six runs. The requested breakable prefill graph was skipped by the same model compatibility guard in both lanes. Runtime logs also confirm that every candidate rank selected the DeepGEMM runner and exercised grouped-contiguous DeepGEMM JIT.

This standard-dispatch implementation is functionally correct for the tested Qwen3.5 PP2/TP8/EP1 configuration, but it is not a performance win over FlashInfer TRTLLM at concurrency 1–128. The measured regression ranges from 23.99% to 41.74%, and no crossover appears in this range.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [testing guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Kimi-K3] Fail fast when FlashInfer kernel prerequisites are missing
author: Fridge003
body:
## Summary

- Keep Kimi-K3's Blackwell default MoE runner on `flashinfer_mxfp4` when the TRTLLM Gen SiTU cubin pool is available.
- Raise an actionable error when `SGLANG_TRTLLM_GEN_MOE_CUBIN_POOL` is missing or invalid instead of silently falling back to Marlin. Explicit non-FlashInfer selections such as `--moe-runner-backend marlin` remain unchanged.
- For Kimi-K3 with `dcp_size > 1` and the default/explicit `cutedsl_mla` decode backend, verify that `flashinfer.decode.trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` exposes `enable_dcp`. If not, fail early with the Kimi-K3 Dockerfile patch instructions.

## Why

The previous Blackwell override silently changed the Kimi-K3 MoE implementation from FlashInfer MXFP4 to Marlin when the private TRTLLM Gen cubin pool was unavailable. This could make a launch appear valid while exercising a different kernel.

Similarly, an unpatched FlashInfer installation does not expose the DCP arguments required by Kimi-K3's CuTeDSL MLA path. Detecting this at argument resolution time gives users a deterministic and actionable failure instead of a later launch/runtime error.

## B300 validation

Hardware: 8x NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC  
Model: `/scratch/models/Kimi-K3`  
FlashInfer: `flashinfer-python==0.6.15.post1`, `flashinfer-cubin==0.6.15.post1`, `flashinfer-jit-cache==0.6.15.post1+cu130`  
TRTLLM Gen pool: `trtllm_gen_moe_cubin_pool_20260617_v0613rc1` (1,696 cubins)

The GPU validation was run at Kimi-K3 base commit `578edb240a6d6f6f2fa4c31497276955d7f73432` plus this change. The PR was subsequently rebased onto the latest `kimi-k3`; the intervening commits did not modify `overrides.py`.

### Expected failures before installing/applying prerequisites

| Launch | Result | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| Low latency, cubin pool unset | exit 1 | Error requires a valid `SGLANG_TRTLLM_GEN_MOE_CUBIN_POOL` and gives install commands; no Marlin fallback |
| Balanced, unpatched FlashInfer MLA | exit 1 | Error reports missing `enable_dcp` and links to the Kimi-K3 Dockerfile patch instructions |

### OCRBench after installing the cubin pool and applying the CuTeDSL MLA DCP patch

All runs used Kimi-Vendor-Verifier OCRBench with 1,000 samples, max thinking, streaming, 50 connections, `max_tokens=16384`, temperature 1.0, and top-p 0.95.

| Configuration | Verified kernel/backend | Accuracy | stderr | Total time | Benchmark errors |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Low latency | MoE: `flashinfer_mxfp4` + TRTLLM Gen SiTU cubin; MLA: `trtllm_mla`; DCP=1 | **0.890** | 0.010 | 5:10 | 0 |
| Balanced | MoE: `flashinfer_mxfp4` + TRTLLM Gen SiTU cubin; decode: `cutedsl_mla`; prefill: `trtllm_mla`; DCP=8 | **0.887** | 0.010 | 6:36 | 0 |
| MegaMoE | MoE: `deep_gemm` + `megamoe`; decode: `cutedsl_mla`; prefill: `trtllm_mla`; EP=8, DCP=8 | **0.909** | 0.009 | 13:42 | 1 max-token sample |

For Low latency and Balanced, server logs reported `moe_runner_backend=flashinfer_mxfp4 (trtllm-gen SiTU cubin pool found)`; neither log contained a Marlin MoE path. Balanced and MegaMoE logged `flashinfer.cute_dsl MLA decode using impl=monolithic` on all eight ranks.

The MegaMoE benchmark completed all 1,000 samples; one sample reached the configured 16,384 completion-token limit and was recorded by the verifier as `max_tokens`.

## Local checks

- `python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/overrides.py`
- `black --check python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/overrides.py`
- pre-commit hooks run by `git commit`
- `git diff --check`

No unit test is added in this PR.

title: [CP] Support breakable CUDA graphs for zigzag strategy
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

Split PR 2 of #32714. Enable breakable prefill CUDA graphs for the validated zigzag context-parallel path as an independent PR, then incorporate the requested review refactor.

## Modifications

- allow full zigzag prefill CP with TensorRT-LLM MHA to retain breakable prefill CUDA graphs, without an architecture restriction
- keep CP-specific BCG eligibility, static inputs, capture preparation, replay, gather, and eager logits-tail handling in `sglang.srt.layers.cp.bcg`
- capture only token buckets where zigzag CP is valid
- gate live batches at the prefill CUDA graph dispatch boundary so batches that cannot use CP-v2 fall back to eager execution
- extend `test_gpt_oss_4gpu_mxfp4_cp.py` with `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`
- remove the two standalone unit-test files requested in review

The final PR owns 5 files and has no changed-file overlap with the other split PRs.

title: [Quantization] Route per-tensor FP8 checkpoints to FlashInfer on SM90
author: adityakamat24
body:
Closes #32993

## Motivation

A per-tensor FP8 checkpoint carries one scalar weight scale and one scalar activation scale. Those layers go to the AOT CUTLASS rowwise GEMM, which only takes a per-token activation vector and a per-channel weight vector. So both scalars get broadcast: the weight scale at load time in `convert_to_channelwise`, and the activation scale on every forward in `static_quant_fp8(repeat_scale=True)`. The GEMM then runs a rowwise epilogue on a problem that is per-tensor.

The FlashInfer per-tensor path already exists as `apply_fp8_linear_bmm_flashinfer`. But the `flashinfer_bmm_fp8` custom op is defined inside the `is_blackwell_supported()` block at `fp8_utils.py:304`, so on Hopper the symbol does not exist at all. Flipping a caller flag would just raise `NameError`.

flashinfer's cuBLAS backend has always covered both arches. In 0.6.14 and 0.6.15.post1, `_cublas_bmm_fp8_requirement` is decorated `@supported_compute_capability([89, 90, 100, 103, 110, 120, 121])`. And `fp8_utils.py:176` already imports `flashinfer.bmm_fp8` on every CUDA arch with no gate, which DeepSeek MLA calls at `forward_mla.py:702`. So this adds no import surface and no new build dependency.

The issue asks for SM89 and SM90. I measured both. **SM90 gains, SM89 regresses**, so this routes SM90 and Blackwell only. The Ada data is below.

## Modifications

`fp8_utils.py`: add `flashinfer_per_tensor_fp8_supported()`, and move the `flashinfer_bmm_fp8` custom op out of the Blackwell-only block into its own guard. The rest of that block (`SfLayout`, `mm_mxfp8`, `mxfp8_quantize`, `gemm_fp8_nt_groupwise`) really is Blackwell-only and stays put.

`modelopt_quant.py`: the GEMM choice and the weight-scale layout become one per-layer decision, `layer.use_flashinfer_bmm`, taken in `process_weights_after_loading`. Before this, the load-time gate and the runtime gate were different conditions, and the runtime one had an extra `layer.input_scale is not None` term the load-time one did not. If that term ever went false, the layer kept a scalar scale, failed the `weight_scale.numel() == weight.shape[1]` check in `apply_fp8_linear`, and dropped to the unfused dequant path with no error.

The predicate also needs K and N aligned. cuBLAS FP8 raises `CUBLAS_STATUS` on unaligned shapes and `bmm_fp8` has no fallback, while `apply_fp8_linear` drops to `triton_scaled_mm`. I measured the limit on SM90 as K divisible by 4 and N even:

```
N=256   K=256   -> ok        N=256   K=242   -> RAISE
N=256   K=248   -> ok        N=256   K=130   -> RAISE
N=256   K=244   -> ok        N=256   K=129   -> RAISE
N=242   K=256   -> ok        N=129   K=256   -> RAISE
```

The bound I used is the same 16-element one `apply_fp8_linear` already applies to the CUTLASS kernel, which leaves room for per-arch differences. No real transformer shape is affected either way.

## Accuracy Tests

`nvidia/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8` with `--quantization modelopt_fp8`. GSM8K 5-shot, greedy, 1314 examples.

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path nvidia/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp8 --port 30000 --mem-fraction-static 0.85

python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 30000 --eval-name gsm8k \
  --num-examples 1319 --num-threads 200
```

| GPU | baseline `0d6bef6b6d` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H100 NVL | 0.809 | 0.807 |
| H100 80GB SXM | 0.800 | 0.805 |
| L40 (SM89, forced on) | 0.819 | 0.815 |

`test/registered/quant/test_modelopt_fp8.py` is registered to `1-gpu-large`, which is an H100, and serves the same checkpoint. It exercises this path in CI with no changes.

## Unit Tests

New file `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_fp8_per_tensor_flashinfer.py`, registered `stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-large"`. On the patched tree, H100 NVL:

```
12 passed, 2 warnings in 0.66s
```

It covers three things:

- The scale layout and the dispatch target together. `use_flashinfer_bmm` picks both, and if they drift apart nothing fails until a real forward on real hardware.
- Numeric agreement with the CUTLASS rowwise route it replaces, in bf16 and fp16. The model-level tests only ever run bf16.
- The arch window, by patching compute capability. There is no Ada runner in CI, so this is the only way to cover SM89.

On an L40 the same file gives `3 passed, 9 skipped`. The capability cases run, and the route cases skip, since that arch no longer has the route.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Shapes are the TP4 and TP8 shards of `nvidia/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-FP8`: hidden 8192, intermediate 28672, 64 heads, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, so qkv N is 8192 + 1024 + 1024 = 10240 before sharding.

Timing uses `flashinfer.testing.utils.bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(use_cuda_graph=True)`. It reads GPU kernel time from CUPTI and flushes L2 between iterations. I checked CUPTI was actually running before each sweep, because it quietly falls back to CUDA events when `cupti-python` is missing. Cold L2 matters here: an L40 has 96MB of L2, enough to hold a 31MB weight matrix, so a hot run reads much faster than reality.

```bash
pip install -U cupti-python
python python/sglang/kernels/aot/benchmark/bench_fp8_pertensor_gemm.py --tp 4
python python/sglang/kernels/aot/benchmark/bench_fp8_pertensor_gemm.py --tp 8
```

Numbers are `cutlass_rowwise / flashinfer_pertensor` for the whole linear, quantization included. Above 1.00 means the FlashInfer route is faster.

### SM90 (H100), no bias

TP4:

| shape | m=1 | 8 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 256 | 512 | 1024 | 2048 | 4096 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| qkv_proj N2560 K8192 | 0.88 | 0.90 | 0.88 | 1.09 | 1.05 | 1.32 | 1.24 | 1.32 | 1.18 | 1.09 |
| o_proj N8192 K2048 | 1.00 | 1.01 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.08 | 1.10 | 1.15 | 1.00 | 0.93 | 1.02 |
| gate_up_proj N14336 K8192 | 1.00 | 1.01 | 0.99 | 1.00 | 1.02 | 1.04 | 1.07 | 0.98 | 1.09 | 1.06 |
| down_proj N8192 K7168 | 0.99 | 1.00 | 0.99 | 0.99 | 1.03 | 1.04 | 1.08 | 1.09 | 1.03 | 1.06 |

TP8:

| shape | m=1 | 8 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 256 | 512 | 1024 | 2048 | 4096 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| qkv_proj N1280 K8192 | 0.88 | 0.91 | 0.89 | 0.87 | 1.13 | 1.79 | 1.43 | 1.23 | 1.35 | 1.20 |
| o_proj N8192 K1024 | 1.01 | 1.02 | 1.01 | 1.00 | 1.10 | 1.12 | 1.04 | 1.00 | 0.88 | 0.93 |
| gate_up_proj N7168 K8192 | 0.98 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.99 | 1.04 | 1.09 | 1.08 | 1.09 | 1.04 | 1.11 |
| down_proj N8192 K3584 | 0.99 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.06 | 1.08 | 1.11 | 1.03 | 1.03 | 1.08 |

The split is by M, not by shape.

Up to m=64, three of the four projections sit between 0.98 and 1.02, and only `qkv_proj` loses. Adding the TP4 times at m=1 across all four gives 112.26us against 114.31us, so decode is about 2% slower in total, not the 12% the `qkv_proj` cell suggests on its own.

From m=128 up it wins everywhere, 1.02x to 1.79x. The 1.79x is a CUTLASS tile cliff: TP8 `qkv_proj` goes from 14.59us at m=128 to 27.52us at m=256, so 1.9x the time for 2x the work, while cuBLAS scales smoothly through it.

### SM90 end to end

`nvidia/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8` on an H100 NVL, with `--disable-radix-cache`. `bench_serving` regenerates the same prompts each run, so with prefix caching on, a repeat run barely prefills and the numbers mean nothing. Each arm ran twice, same build, to show the noise.

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path nvidia/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp8 --port 30000 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --disable-radix-cache

python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 32 \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 32 --warmup-requests 3
```

Prefill-heavy, 4096 in / 32 out, concurrency 32:

| metric | baseline | baseline re-run | this PR | this PR re-run | delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| input tok/s | 34725.15 | 34645.24 | 40146.78 | 40019.58 | +15.6% |
| median TTFT (ms) | 1837.84 | 1843.85 | 1557.51 | 1564.76 | -15.2% |

The same-build spread is 0.23% on baseline and 0.32% on this PR, so both deltas are far outside the noise.

Decode-heavy, 1024 in / 512 out, cache also disabled. This matches the m=1 column above:

| concurrency | metric | baseline | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | output tok/s | 223.71 | 223.58 |
| 1 | median TPOT (ms) | 4.42 | 4.42 |
| 8 | output tok/s | 1513.62 | 1527.40 |
| 8 | median TPOT (ms) | 5.04 | 5.03 |

### SM89 (L40), no bias

TP4:

| shape | m=1 | 8 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 256 | 512 | 1024 | 2048 | 4096 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| qkv_proj N2560 K8192 | 0.91 | 0.98 | 0.93 | 0.90 | 0.99 | 0.84 | 1.17 | 1.32 | 1.14 | 1.04 |
| o_proj N8192 K2048 | 1.04 | 1.05 | 1.04 | 1.01 | 1.04 | 1.08 | 1.09 | 0.99 | 1.06 | 1.02 |
| gate_up_proj N14336 K8192 | 0.82 | 0.96 | 0.97 | 0.96 | 0.78 | 0.97 | 1.02 | 0.91 | 1.07 | 0.92 |
| down_proj N8192 K7168 | 1.02 | 1.02 | 1.02 | 0.96 | 0.96 | 0.94 | 1.17 | 1.07 | 1.06 | 0.93 |

TP8:

| shape | m=1 | 8 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 256 | 512 | 1024 | 2048 | 4096 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| qkv_proj N1280 K8192 | 0.86 | 1.25 | 0.87 | 0.90 | 1.61 | 1.80 | 1.69 | 1.08 | 1.26 | 1.12 |
| o_proj N8192 K1024 | 1.06 | 1.07 | 1.07 | 1.09 | 1.16 | 0.99 | 1.03 | 1.01 | 1.06 | 1.16 |
| gate_up_proj N7168 K8192 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.95 | 0.95 | 0.83 | 1.06 | 0.98 | 0.97 | 1.08 |
| down_proj N8192 K3584 | 1.04 | 1.04 | 1.03 | 0.97 | 0.99 | 1.04 | 1.10 | 1.09 | 1.05 | 1.02 |

I reran this on a second L40 from a different provider, with a different host CPU. All 80 no-bias points agree within 0.01 to 0.04:

| | m | L40 #1 | L40 #2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TP4 gate_up_proj | 4096 | 0.92 | 0.88 |
| TP4 down_proj | 4096 | 0.93 | 0.90 |
| TP4 gate_up_proj | 128 | 0.78 | 0.77 |
| TP8 qkv_proj | 256 | 1.80 | 1.81 |
| TP8 gate_up_proj | 256 | 0.83 | 0.83 |
| TP8 o_proj | 4096 | 1.16 | 1.17 |

### SM89 end to end

Same workload, same `--disable-radix-cache`, two runs per arm. Both arms use `--attention-backend triton`, since SM89 cannot use FA3 and the flashinfer attention backend wants a newer flashinfer than installs on CUDA 13 today. The enabled arm was produced by forcing the predicate true, because the code here excludes Ada.

| metric | baseline | baseline re-run | SM89 enabled | re-run | delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| input tok/s | 10987.39 | 10948.71 | 10432.43 | 10322.25 | -5.4% |
| median TTFT (ms) | 5752.31 | 5737.38 | 6025.41 | 6125.88 | +5.8% |

The same-build spread is 0.35% and 1.06%, so both deltas are outside it.

### Why the two arches disagree

The issue describes one "outdated GEMM", but `fp8_gemm_kernel.cu:1155-1168` sends each arch to a different kernel:

```cpp
if (sm_version >= 90) { cutlass_scaled_mm_sm90_fp8(...); }    // CUTLASS 3.x
if (sm_version == 89) { sm89_fp8_dispatch_shape<...>(...); }  // ArchTag = Sm89, CUTLASS 2.x
```

The Ada kernel comes from TensorRT-LLM and picks its tile shapes from a hand-written table: `if (m == 1) { if (n <= 8192) GemmShape<16,64,128> ... }`, then `m <= 16`, `m <= 64`, and so on. That makes it very uneven across M. I measured 27.4us at m=1, 39.1us at m=2, then 29.3us at m=32. flashinfer's 1.8x on TP8 `qkv_proj` comes from one of those weak buckets.

But prefill runs at `chunked_prefill_size`, so m=4096, and the hand-tuned buckets are good there. That is why `gate_up_proj` and `down_proj` both lose and the end-to-end number goes negative.

On Hopper the incumbent is generic CUTLASS 3.x and cuBLAS is the tuned side, so the comparison flips.

Two checks rule out the other explanations. `torch._scaled_mm` is a separate cuBLAS entry point with no batched wrapper, and it loses in the same Ada places, sometimes by more (TP4 `gate_up_proj` at m=4096 is 0.83x). And turning on flashinfer's cuBLAS algo autotuning never lifts a losing Ada shape above parity, 0.99x being the best I saw, so this is not just a bad default tactic.

<details>

title: [Kernel] Unify BaseFusedOp and MultiPlatformOp dispatch
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

RFC #29630 introduced `BaseFusedOp` as the per-operator multi-backend contract of the unified `sglang.kernels` namespace, while `sglang.srt.layers.utils.MultiPlatformOp` still owned multi-platform dispatch, OOT platform plugins, and the torch.compile enter/leave protocol. This PR completes the unification discussed in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29630#issuecomment-4920387930 and https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29630#issuecomment-5150881012 (HAL context: #26426): **`BaseFusedOp` is now the single operator abstraction**, and every in-repo `MultiPlatformOp` user is migrated.

## Architecture

`BaseFusedOp` (`python/sglang/kernels/fused_op.py`) is now a standard `torch.nn.Module` (`nn.Module + ABC`, cooperative `__init__`, calls go through `nn.Module.__call__` so forward hooks / module traversal work). It keeps **two dimensions strictly separate**:

- **Kernel backend (provenance, `KernelBackend`)**: `forward_native` (required pure-torch reference), `forward_torch_compile`, `forward_triton`, `forward_jit`, `forward_aot`, `forward_cute_dsl`, `forward_flashinfer`, `forward_deepgemm`, `forward_aiter`, `forward_torch_npu` (renamed from `forward_npu` in the ops group so the torch_npu *backend* method never collides with the NPU *platform* method). Device support stays per-`(op, backend)` metadata via `CapabilityRequirement` — CUDA/HIP are **not** kernel backends.
- **Platform / device**: `forward_cuda`, `forward_hip` (→ `forward_cuda`), `forward_musa`, `forward_npu`, `forward_xpu`, `forward_cpu` (AMX-gated), plus `forward_<key>` / `register_oot_forward()` for out-of-tree platform plugins. These are defined only when a subclass provides them; a missing platform path falls back to native instead of raising. Only HIP keeps the implicit CUDA-path fallback; **MUSA opts into the CUDA path explicitly** (review feedback — srt kernel imports are gated on `is_cuda()`, so an implicitly reached `forward_cuda` on MUSA can NameError instead of degrading). TopK and the Gemma norm family, the ops with demonstrated MUSA support, define explicit `forward_musa` so their dispatch is unchanged.

### Final dispatch priority (highest first)

1. Explicit `forward(..., backend=KernelBackend.X)`
2. Global forced backend (`SGLANG_FORCE_FUSED_OP_BACKEND` / `set_fused_op_backend`) — checked per call so tests/tools can flip it on live instances. **Best-effort**: an op that does not implement the forced backend (e.g. forcing `torch` on the device-only DSA `Indexer`) falls back to normal dispatch with a one-time warning, so the numerics-bisect switch now works on whole models (on main it only affected the `kernels/ops` instances). Explicit per-call `backend=` stays strict and raises.
3. OOT platform override: forward registered via `register_oot_forward` (exact-type lookup) > `forward_<dispatch_key>` method > native
4. Optimized kernel backends by class `priority`: a backend participates in auto-selection only when its method is overridden **and** it is declared in `capabilities` (declaring with an empty set = any device). Overriding `backend_eligible()` adds per-call shape/dtype gates and switches this step to per-call resolution.
5. Platform-specific forward (HIP → CUDA default chain only, CPU gated on AMX — same platform order as `MultiPlatformOp`; the old implicit MUSA → CUDA chain was dropped per review, with explicit `forward_musa` opt-ins where MUSA support exists)
6. `forward_native`

Steps 3–6 are static per process: resolved lazily on first call (so `import sglang.kernels` still never triggers platform detection or kernel-backend imports) and cached in `self._forward_method`; subclass `__init__` may pre-seed it (the existing env-gated aiter/native pins in `srt/layers` keep working unchanged).

### torch.compile

`enter_torch_compile(num_tokens)` / `leave_torch_compile()` moved into `BaseFusedOp` with identical semantics: idempotent (modules shared across layers), restores the original forward on leave, and switches to the compile-safe native path so an outer `torch.compile` never traces device kernels (no nested per-op compile is introduced; `forward_torch_compile` is never auto-selected). The old class-name string matching (`"FusedMoE" in cls.__name__` / `"TopK" in ...`) is replaced by an overridable `_torch_compile_forward(num_tokens)` hook: `TopK` returns `forward_native` only for `num_tokens == 1`, `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod` returns `fused_moe_forward_native` only for `num_tokens == 1` — inherited by their subclasses, same behavior as before. `enter_torch_compile` also warms the lazy env/platform resolution so compiled traces never graph-break on an import.

`torch_compile_decoration._to_torch` and tc_piecewise's `_toggle_fused_ops` (renamed from `_toggle_multi_platform_ops`) now flip `BaseFusedOp` submodules.

## Migrated users

Activation (`SiluAndMul`, `GeluAndMul`, `NewGELU`, `ReLU2`, `QuickGELU`, `XIELU`), layernorm (`RMSNorm`, `LayerNorm`, `GemmaRMSNorm`, `Gemma3RMSNorm`, `Gemma4RMSNorm`, `RMSNormWithoutScale`), `Conv2dLayer`/`Conv3dLayer`, `TopK`, `RotaryEmbedding` (+ all subclasses incl. mrope / DeepseekScaling) and `DualChunkRotaryEmbedding`, DSA `Indexer`, DSV4 `Compressor`, `Mixer2RMSNormGated`, `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod` (multi-inheritance `(FusedMoEMethodBase, BaseFusedOp)` kept, MRO/init order unchanged), plus `torch_compile_decoration`, `tc_piecewise_cuda_graph_backend`, and the platform-interface docs. Ops that override `forward()` directly or have no pure-torch path (`XIELU`, `DualChunkRotaryEmbedding`, `Indexer`) gained explicit `forward_native` definitions preserving the old semantics (`UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod` already had one via its pre-existing `forward_native = forward_cpu` alias).

`git grep MultiPlatformOp` now matches only the deprecated alias module, its re-export, and historical comments — no production code imports or inherits it.

## OOT plugin compatibility

- `sglang.srt.layers.utils(.multi_platform).MultiPlatformOp` remains importable as a **deprecated alias**: a `BaseFusedOp` subclass that emits a `DeprecationWarning` on subclassing and stays attribute-compatible with the old class — the lenient concrete `forward_native` and all the old per-platform default methods (`forward_hip`/`forward_musa` → `forward_cuda`, `forward_npu`/`forward_xpu`/`forward_hpu`/`forward_cpu` → `forward_native`, raising `forward_cuda`) are kept so plugin subclasses that call them directly (or rely on the raise-on-CUDA-without-override behavior) are bit-identical. No second dispatch implementation is maintained.
- `register_oot_forward(op_cls, fn, platform_key)` is unchanged and shared between the alias and `BaseFusedOp` (single registry); `SRTPlatform.get_dispatch_key_name()` keeps driving `forward_<key>` selection.
- No new ServerArgs; the existing `SGLANG_FORCE_FUSED_OP_BACKEND` env and programmatic `set_fused_op_backend` are preserved.

## Behavior notes (intentional deltas)

- **Failure-mode delta, scoped precisely**: on main, only `forward_cuda` raised when missing (with HIP/MUSA chaining into it) — the old `forward_npu` / `forward_xpu` / `forward_cpu` base defaults were already silent `forward_native` fallbacks. So the raise→native change applies to CUDA/HIP-without-override only, and the single in-repo op in that bucket is DSV4 `Compressor` (whose `__call__` path is dead on CUDA/HIP in-tree; only the Ascend backend calls it, hitting its defined `forward_npu`). No op loses a loud NPU error: `forward_torch_npu` (the torch_npu *backend* stub) still raises when explicitly selected.
- Auto-selection of optimized kernel backends now requires a `capabilities` declaration (all existing `kernels/ops` classes already declare theirs). Undeclared-but-overridden methods stay reachable via explicit `backend=` / forced selection. This is what keeps e.g. `RMSNorm.forward_aiter` (an env-gated instance pin, not an auto path) from being auto-picked.
- The unused, never-dispatched `forward_hpu` default was dropped from the base class (it survives on the deprecated alias).
- `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod` keeps its pre-existing `forward_native = forward_cpu` class-body alias (discovered during review — the old class already had a native path via this alias); only the compile hook was added.
- `NPUMXFP8OnlineMoEMethod` (subclass of `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod` whose name does **not** contain "FusedMoE") was missed by the old name-based compile special-case and got the generic native switch; it now inherits the FusedMoE hook (bs=1-only). This is a bugfix-grade divergence on a path (torch.compile on NPU) that is not exercised today.
- `sglang.kernels` now imports `torch` at package import (required by the `nn.Module` base). It still never imports `sgl_kernel` / `sglang.kernels.jit` / platform detection at import time — the metadata-only registry property is unchanged (covered by `test_import_stays_metadata_only`).

## Tests & benchmarks actually run

**H200 (ion9, CUDA 8×H200, torch 2.11, sgl-kernel 0.4.5):**
- `test/registered/kernels/test_fused_op_dispatch.py` (new, base-a-test-cpu): **58 passed** — nn.Module hooks/traversal, full priority ladder, platform chains, capability filtering, static-dispatch caching, per-call `backend_eligible` gating, forced-backend fallback semantics, compile enter/leave idempotency, TopK/FusedMoE hooks, tracing, deprecated alias (incl. legacy platform defaults), and a completeness check that every migrated op subclasses `BaseFusedOp` (not the alias).
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_fused_op_gpu_parity.py`: **26 passed** (every eligible backend vs native on real GPU).
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_fused_op.py`, `test_kernels_namespace.py`, `test_kernel_inventory.py`: pass (one pre-existing failure `test_import_stays_metadata_only` fails identically on upstream `main` on any box with sgl_kernel installed — `import sglang` itself pulls `sgl_kernel` via `hf_transformers_patches`; unrelated to this PR, passes on the CPU CI runner).
- `test/registered/unit/layers/test_conv_layer.py`: 35 passed. (`test/registered/rotary/test_rope_rocm.py` fails identically on upstream main on this CUDA box — pre-existing.)
- Real-model smokes on Qwen2.5: plain `bench_one_batch` ✓; `--enable-torch-compile` ✓ with decode median **212.66 tok/s vs 212.65 tok/s on upstream main** (same box/GPU); prefill `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill tc_piecewise` ✓; `--correctness-test` output coherent.

**Dispatch microbenchmark** (`test/manual/kernels/bench_fused_op_dispatch.py`, no-op op body = pure dispatch overhead):

| path | Linux/H200 host | macOS |
|---|---|---|
| plain bound method | 36 ns/call | 24 ns/call |
| `MultiPlatformOp` replica | 1086 ns/call | 481 ns/call |
| unified `BaseFusedOp` | 1124 ns/call | 518 ns/call |
| **delta** | **+38 ns/call** | **+37 ns/call** |

The added cost (forced-backend global read + cached-dispatch None check + trace flag) is ~3% of the `nn.Module.__call__` overhead both classes already pay, and noise relative to any real kernel.

## Not covered

No ROCm/HIP, Ascend NPU, XPU, MUSA, or OOT-platform hardware was available; those paths are covered by the mocked-platform unit tests and preserve the previous dispatch order by construction. AMD/NPU CI lanes should exercise them on this PR.

An adversarial differential review (old-vs-new dispatch for all 21 migrated classes and their transitive subclasses across all platforms, compile-protocol callers, OOT registry, import graph) was run on the final diff; the three actionable findings it produced (forced-backend crash scope, dead `forward_native` stub in unquant, alias attribute compatibility) are fixed in the last commit.

Refs: #29630, #26426

title: [MXFP8] Use FlashInfer CUTLASS for dense GEMM on SM120, delete Triton path
author: b8zhong
body:
MXFP8 dense GEMM picked its backend from the blockwise-FP8 setting, so on SM120 (`auto` -> `cutlass`) it fell through to Triton. This GEMM is created earlier this year and can't achieve good perf in most shapes.

Resolve the MXFP8 dense backend separately: SM120 keeps `cutlass` for blockwise FP8, MXFP8 goes to FlashInfer CUTLASS. Delete the Triton MXFP8 dense kernel; the DeepGEMM shape/dtype fallback now uses FlashInfer.

### Benchmark

Speedup of FlashInfer CUTLASS over the deleted Triton path, on `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8` dense linear shapes at TP=1 (assuming MXFP8 weights). 1x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm120).

title: [Feat] cp: Support FlashInfer prefill context parallelism
author: wirybeaver
body:
## Motivation

FlashInfer could not use the existing zigzag prefill CP path for dense MHA/GQA models. This PR adds that backend integration, addressing the FlashInfer coverage task in #21788.

## Modification

Keep queries zigzag-sharded, gather KV into the full paged cache, and execute FlashInfer prefill on each rank's logical queries. Restore physical padding at the strategy boundary.

```text
zigzag token shards
  |-- local K/V --> all-gather --> full paged KV --+
  |-- local Q -----------------------------------+--> FlashInfer prefill
                                                          |
                                                          v
                                                local output + padding
```

Supports eager dense causal MHA/GQA with direct NHD KV. Uses current runtime configuration without deprecated `enable_cp_v2` or model-file changes. CPU coverage checks routing/padding; the registered Qwen3-8B server test uses `GSM8KMixin`.

## Accuracy Result

Qwen3-8B BF16 on 2× H100. Parity compares TP2/CP2 with both cold cache and prefix reuse.

| Validation | Result | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Registered CP2 GSM8K, 200 examples | 191/200 = **95.5%**, above the 90% floor; zero errors/truncations | Pass |
| 2K cold/reuse parity | Identical output token IDs; max absolute logprob delta **1.19e-7 < 0.2** | Pass |
| 8K cold/reuse parity | Identical output token IDs; max absolute logprob delta **0.111686 < 0.2** | Pass |
| 16K cold/reuse parity | Identical output token IDs; max absolute logprob delta **0 < 0.2** | Pass |

The paired GSM8K experiment measured TP2 96.0% versus CP2 95.5% (-0.5 percentage points), so passing the floor does not establish identical accuracy.

## Benchmarking Result

Qwen3-8B BF16, 2× H100, concurrency 1, one output token, 75% prefix reuse, 8K chunked prefill. Ordered fresh-server visits: **TP2 -> CP2 -> CP2 -> TP2 -> TP2 -> CP2**, with 256 timed samples per workload per visit.

Per-visit processed-input throughput (tok/s):

| Visit | Arm | Cold 2K | Cold 8K | Cold 16K | Reuse 2K | Reuse 8K | Reuse 16K |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | TP2 | 47,496 | 56,379 | 47,447 | 11,437 | 41,293 | 35,001 |
| 2 | CP2 | 32,949 | 50,281 | 43,077 | 9,189 | 34,827 | 33,206 |
| 3 | CP2 | 31,313 | 50,758 | 43,330 | 9,245 | 36,546 | 33,400 |
| 4 | TP2 | 49,460 | 56,237 | 47,497 | 11,265 | 41,270 | 35,015 |
| 5 | TP2 | 49,139 | 56,747 | 47,363 | 11,884 | 41,436 | 35,120 |
| 6 | CP2 | 32,703 | 50,517 | 43,328 | 8,743 | 34,716 | 33,369 |

A = TP2; B = CP2. Throughput is actual processed input tokens divided by summed generation-request latency, in tok/s; cache reset/prime time is excluded. Changes use the unrounded per-visit throughputs: mean(B visits) / mean(A visits) - 1 and median(B visits) / median(A visits) - 1. Negative means lower CP2 throughput.

| Workload | Mean throughput change | Median throughput change |
|---|---:|---:|
| Cold 2K | -33.63% | -33.45% |
| Cold 8K | -10.51% | -10.40% |
| Cold 16K | -8.83% | -8.68% |
| Reuse 2K | -21.42% | -19.65% |
| Reuse 8K | -14.44% | -15.66% |
| Reuse 16K | -4.91% | -4.70% |

CP2 did not improve performance in these workloads. Output token parity and generated-token logprob tolerance passed the focused checks above; no bitwise-logit or unchanged-GSM8K claim is made.

[Accuracy and performance details](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33226#issuecomment-6101828491) · [Historical performance](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33226#issuecomment-5574927639)

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with repository tools.
- [x] Add CPU unit and registered two-GPU accuracy coverage.
- [x] Provide correctness and scoped performance measurements.
- [x] Follow repository coding-style guidance.

title: [FlashInfer V0.6.18] feat(dsv4): support --dsa-topk-backend flashinfer with fused top-k
author: zianglih
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

@humansand

**Scope: DeepSeek V4 FlashInfer top-k backend support.** This PR makes `--dsa-topk-backend flashinfer` usable for the DeepSeek V4 indexer. It uses FlashInfer's fused compact-page transform when `SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK=true` and preserves the existing unfused FlashInfer path when the flag is disabled.

The packed PAGED-row prerequisite was merged in [#33006](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33006). DeepSeek V4 adds a compact page table where one page-table entry represents 64 score positions. FlashInfer [#4315](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4315) added the required `page_size`, caller-owned output, raw-index output, and padded-stride support.

> **Dependency:** final [FlashInfer v0.6.18](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/tag/v0.6.18) contains the compact-page fused top-k API from [flashinfer#4315](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4315). SGLang `main` now pins v0.6.18 through merged [#36954](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36954). This PR extends the existing runtime check to target and speculative-draft DSA top-k selection.

## Modifications

- Add a fused DeepSeek V4 FlashInfer helper that calls `top_k_page_table_transform` with:
  - padded-stride score rows without a contiguous materialization;
  - the compact page table with `page_size=64`;
  - graph-safe deterministic and tie-break settings;
  - caller-owned translated and optional raw-index output buffers.
- Preserve the existing unfused `flashinfer.top_k` plus vectorized page translation path and resolve the fused/unfused transform once during backend initialization.
- Pass a required, already-resolved `should_use_topk_v2()` decision into indexer metadata; FlashInfer and Torch do not create or copy an unused SGL plan.
- Require `flashinfer-python>=0.6.18` when FlashInfer is selected for target or speculative-draft DSA top-k, while preserving the existing resolved attention-backend check.
- Update `bench_topk.py` to benchmark `page_size={1,64}` as a Cartesian axis with a preallocated output while keeping the focused CI value at `K=512`. The expanded performance grid below uses a source-unchanged runtime-axis wrapper. Page size 64 matches the compact CUDA DSA layout; page size 1 is the noncompact baseline.
- Extend existing CPU and CUDA-graph tests across fused/unfused routing, `K={512,1024}`, optional raw output, padded score strides, replayed inputs, short rows, and raw/translated alignment. Tests exercise non-contiguous page tables and assert FlashInfer 0.6.18's `-1` padding contract for every unused translated/raw suffix slot.

## Accuracy Tests

Post-merge validation used SGLang `abaeebc57eacb256a4e8013b59646c4d71cf0dc6` on one NVIDIA B300:

- **Merge parents:** PR head `d8750c398dccbea72bbc37bf37ddacae2defe801` and upstream `main` `881cbfe54c98356cfa1eaa134aa4d0be702fc90f`.
- **Image:** `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260831-bb5e6198` (amd64 image `sha256:3c75c6f7f8e6eaeebdcf92ef47caef818608134252ad5898f4c670b7911768a6`).
- **Hardware/runtime:** NVIDIA B300 (SM103), driver 590.48.01, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA 13.0.
- **FlashInfer:** `flashinfer-python==0.6.18`, `flashinfer-cubin==0.6.18`, and `flashinfer-jit-cache==0.6.18+cu130`, force-reinstalled directly from the final release assets because this nightly image predates #36954.

Install and focused test commands:

```bash
python3 -m pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps --no-cache-dir \
  https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/download/v0.6.18/flashinfer_python-0.6.18-py3-none-any.whl \
  https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/download/v0.6.18/flashinfer_cubin-0.6.18-py3-none-any.whl \
  'https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/download/v0.6.18/flashinfer_jit_cache-0.6.18%2Bcu130-cp39-abi3-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl'

cd /sgl-workspace/pr33237-merge-validation/sglang
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python"
export SGLANG_CACHE_DIR=/sgl-workspace/pr33237-merge-validation/cache
export FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE="$SGLANG_CACHE_DIR/flashinfer"
unset FLASHINFER_TOPK_ALGO SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK SGLANG_SKIP_SGL_KERNEL_VERSION_CHECK

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python3 -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/test_pre_publish_readers.py \
  test/registered/unit/test_platform_address_not_frozen.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/test_dsv4_nonpaged_indexer.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsa_indexer.py::TestDSAIndexer::test_dsv4_flashinfer_compact_topk_cuda_graph \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsa_indexer.py::TestDSAIndexer::test_topk_v2_respects_topk_backend
```

Raw results:

```text
engine FlashInfer gates and caller-derived XPU topk-v2 eligibility: PASS
17 passed, 15 warnings, 28 subtests passed in 35.17s
```

The suite covers upstream's pre-publish/platform guards, init-time fused/unfused routing, required resolved top-k-v2 metadata, a non-contiguous compact page table, `K={512,1024}`, optional raw output, padded score strides, `-1` suffix padding, replayed inputs, short rows, raw/translated alignment, and CUDA-graph replay. A direct mock smoke independently checked both target/speculative FlashInfer version gates and the caller-resolved XPU exclusion. Changed-file pre-commit passed and left the checkout clean. No DeepSeek V4 model-serving accuracy run or performance rerun was performed; the speed data below remains historical pre-merge evidence. Test log SHA-256: `341cb33a65a9e7f97a6c9985a6977a1d111074d66960040146776aaf3714ff10`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Historical single-GPU operator microbenchmark at SGLang `798019b5dcf815371b4986b84117ad56eff092ae`, using the pre-release FlashInfer 0.6.18 nightly recorded below:

- **Workload:** FP32 random score rows, full uniform lengths, identity page tables, and caller-owned int32 translated-output buffers. Exact Cartesian grid: `K={512,1024,2048} × seq_len={8192,65536,131072} × batch_size={4,8,16,32,64} × page_size={1,64}`. Providers: SGL JIT-v1, SGL JIT-v2, FlashInfer, and PyTorch. JIT-v1 is unavailable at `K=2048` by design.
- **Invocation:** the committed benchmark keeps its focused CI value `K=512`. A source-unchanged inline wrapper accepts the four requested axes as command-line arguments and replaces the benchmark's runtime configuration before calling `Benchmark.run()`; the provider list is asserted unchanged.
- **Page-table layouts:** page size 64 matches DeepSeek V4's compact C4 transform and the shared SGL JIT-v2 representation. Page size 1 matches the current generic DSA/GLM-5 FlashInfer path, which expands its underlying 64-token KV pages into one table entry per token.
- **Timing:** 50 warmups; CUDA-graph replay measured with CUDA events; read inputs rotated and L2 flushed between timed replays; 1,000 requested operator iterations; median microseconds reported. Compilation, JIT-v2 planning, output initialization/allocation, Python/host dispatch, and serving are excluded.
- **Repetition:** three independent complete sweeps on the same B200. All 330 timed cells per sweep had a cross-sweep max-minus-min span below 0.41% of their median.
- **Backend settings:** `FLASHINFER_TOPK_ALGO` unset (automatic); `SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK` unset. The benchmark directly calls the fused FlashInfer API, so this is not a fused-versus-unfused comparison. The tested FlashInfer nightly predates the open CUB TopK PR, so these are not CUB-backend results. Each process emitted the already-documented AOT-to-JIT fallback warning; compilation remained outside timing.

Command:

```bash
cd /hai-workspace/sglang-pr33237-benchmark
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python"
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
export SGLANG_KERNEL_DISABLE_LOG_BANDWIDTH=1
unset FLASHINFER_TOPK_ALGO SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK

for benchmark_repeat in 1 2 3; do
  SGLANG_IS_IN_CI=true \
    /hai-workspace/sglang-pr33237-bench-venv/bin/python - \
    --k 512 1024 2048 \
    --seq-len 8192 65536 131072 \
    --batch-size 4 8 16 32 64 \
    --page-size 1 64 <<'PY' 2>&1 \
    | tee "/hai-workspace/sglang-pr33237-results-full-grid-798019b5d/run-${benchmark_repeat}.log"
import argparse
import runpy

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--k", nargs="+", type=int, required=True)
parser.add_argument("--seq-len", nargs="+", type=int, required=True)
parser.add_argument("--batch-size", nargs="+", type=int, required=True)
parser.add_argument("--page-size", nargs="+", type=int, required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()

benchmark = runpy.run_path(
    "test/registered/kernels/benchmark/attention/bench_topk.py",
    run_name="bench_topk_module",
)["benchmark"]
overrides = {
    ("k",): args.k,
    ("seq_len",): args.seq_len,
    ("batch_size",): args.batch_size,
    ("page_size",): args.page_size,
}
if {names for names, _ in benchmark._configs} != set(overrides):
    raise RuntimeError(f"unexpected axes: {benchmark._configs}")
benchmark._configs[:] = [
    (names, [(value,) for value in overrides[names]])
    for names, _ in benchmark._configs
]
expected_providers = ["jit_v1", "jit_v2", "flashinfer", "torch"]
if benchmark._line_vals != expected_providers:
    raise RuntimeError(f"unexpected providers: {benchmark._line_vals}")
print("effective benchmark configs:", benchmark._configs, flush=True)
print("effective providers:", benchmark._line_vals, flush=True)
benchmark.run()
