title: [MoonEP] BF16 PoC integration for Kimi-K3
author: wirybeaver
body:
It is opened as a draft for partial task of #32607's Integrate MoonEP, not as a final production-ready merge request.

### What is included

- Distinct `moonep` MoE A2A backend recognition.
- MoonEP dispatch/combine data contracts and process-wide buffer facade.
- BF16 contiguous expert layout and correctness-first expert segment runner.
- Eager runtime path: dispatch -> weight prefetch -> BF16 compute -> combine.
- Distributed validation script: `scripts/moonep/validate_moonep_bf16_poc.py`.

### Validation
- 8x H100 SXM (`NV18`) passed BF16 validation on 8 ranks with `global_ok=true`, `max_abs_err=0.0`, `relative_err=0.0`.
- `docker-ncu-benchmark` preflight was run. Suitable Vast.ai H100 NVSwitch hosts were container instances without Docker/NVIDIA Container Toolkit; host NCU counters were restricted (`ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM`), so no NCU performance claims are made.

### Known limitations

- BF16/unquantized only.
- Eager-only; CUDA graph disabled.
- Correctness-first Python segment loop, not final grouped GEMM kernel.
- PoC global expert-row storage is memory-heavy; Kimi-K3 production needs sharded symmetric-memory expert ownership.
- Requires NVSwitch/multicast-capable hosts (8x H100/H200/B200 class).

### Notes

Local agent workflow files, scratch artifacts, and spec notes are intentionally omitted from this upstream PR diff.

Fork PoC PR: wirybeaver/sglang#17

title: Fix padded positions in breakable CUDA Graph attention
author: YAMY1234
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Breakable CUDA Graph pads token buffers to a captured bucket. The attention wrapper already narrows Q/K/V and cache locations to the real token count, but it still passes padded `positions` to the backend. Decode context parallelism (DCP) uses these positions to determine key-value (KV) ownership, so virtual padded tokens can compete with real tokens for the same physical KV slots and silently corrupt the cache.

## Modifications

- Narrow `forward_batch.positions` to the real query-token count together with `out_cache_loc` for the attention call.
- Restore both tensors on the shared `ForwardBatch` after the call.
- Extend the existing Breakable CUDA Graph test to verify the narrowed backend view and restored batch metadata.

## Accuracy Tests

The targeted GPU regression was run before and after the change:

- Before: the attention backend received five padded positions for three real cache locations, and the test failed.
- After: the backend received only the three real positions. The targeted test passed, and the full `TestBreakableCUDAGraphBasic` suite passed (`9 passed`).

An end-to-end matched A/B used Qwen3.5-397B-A17B FP8 with TP16/DCP4, FP8 KV cache, Breakable CUDA Graph prefill, full decode CUDA Graph, GSM8K-128, 8-shot prompting, temperature 0, and `max_tokens=16384`. The validation stack included #32795 and #32858; the only runtime-code difference between before and after was this PR's four-line positions fix.

| Version | Runs | GSM8K |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Before | 1 | 0.875 (112/128) |
| After | 3 | 0.984375 (126/128) in every run |

All four runs completed 128/128 requests with HTTP 200 and no non-200 responses.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked. This correctness fix does not change kernels or CUDA Graph configuration; it creates a tensor view and restores the original reference around the existing attention call.

## Problem

`base-a-test-cpu` fails on `main`: `test_model_overrides.py::TestGoldenModelOverrides::test_page_constraint_passes_at_callable_level` raises

```
AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'speculative_draft_attention_backend'
```

Seen in scheduled run [30723127006](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30723127006/job/91430085617); the partition was green in the four scheduled runs before it.

## Cause

#25545 added one line to `_mla_backend_page_constraints`:

```python
or view.speculative_draft_attention_backend == "trtllm_mha"
```

The `_view` helper in this test builds a `SimpleNamespace` with only four fields, and `ResolvedView.__getattr__` forwards to it — so the new read raises on a stub that the real `ServerArgs` would satisfy. #25545 touched four files, none of them this test.

## Fix

Add the field to the stub's defaults.

## Validation

Reproduced at the failing sha `131bd51b01` on an H100 devbox — the exact `AttributeError` — then with this line applied `test_model_overrides.py` runs **68 tests, OK**.

title: [Perf] Broadcast single-image DP vision embedding instead of pad-to-max all-gather
author: hnyls2002
body:
For a single-image request exactly one rank holds the embedding, so the symmetric all-gather moves `tp_size x max_len` rows of which `(tp_size-1)/tp_size` is padding, and every rank allocates a `tp_size`-times-larger buffer. Broadcast from the owner rank instead — bit-identical, one copy instead of `tp_size`.

Verified on 8x B300, 3 runs: all ranks bitwise-equal to both the all-gather result and ground truth; all-gather 0.69ms -> broadcast 0.09ms (7.6x) at `[5476, 4096]` bf16 (~45MB). Reproducer: `torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 test/manual/vlm/verify_single_image_gather.py`.

Multi-image and `tp_size == 1` paths are untouched.

title: [XPU] Use SYCL kernels for topk_transform on XPU
author: cyxlily
body:
## Motivation

Route `topk_transform` , `topk_transform_paged` and `topk_transform_ragged` to the native SYCL
kernels on XPU. The SYCL implementations are added in the `sgl-kernel-xpu` PR (https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/366, https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/452) and exposed as
`torch.ops.sgl_kernel.topk_transform`, `topk_transform_paged` and `topk_transform_ragged` . Without this dispatch, XPU
runs fall through to the JIT CUDA path and fail to load, or drop to a
significantly slower vectorized PyTorch fallback.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/topk.py`:
  - `topk_transform(...)`: added an `elif scores.device.type == "xpu"`
    branch that calls `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.topk_transform(...)`, before
    the existing generic JIT path.
  - `topk_transform_paged(...)`: added an early-return branch for
    `scores.device.type == "xpu"` that calls
    `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.topk_transform_paged(...)`. On XPU the
    `metadata` argument is accepted for API parity but ignored by the
    kernel.
  - `topk_transform_ragged(...)`: added an `elif scores.device.type == "xpu"`
    branch that calls `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.topk_transform_ragged(...)`, before
    the existing generic JIT path.
## Accuracy Tests

Correctness of the XPU dispatch is verified against the
vectorized PyTorch reference at the kernel level in the `sgl-kernel-xpu` PR (https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/366)

title: config: retire the last process-global config field reads
author: ch-wan
body:
> Part 5 of five, all based on `main` and meant to merge in order.
> Applies on top of parts 1–4. Until they land, this PR's diff includes them.
>
> Replaces #33244, which was closed unmerged: GitHub treated the previous
> chained-base series as a stack, which blocks both base retargeting and
> every merge path except the async endpoint. The review discussion and the
> triage of each round of comments is on #33244; the code here is identical to
> that PR's final revision.

## What

`get_server_args().<field>` reads the startup record of one process. Twenty-six of
those reads were left in `srt`; this removes every one that has somewhere better to
go, and pins the rest.

**Nine reads move to the namespace accessors** — the value they want is the resolved
one, including post-publish overrides: `attention_backend` ×5 →
`get_exec().kernel`, `skip_tokenizer_init` ×2 → `get_serving()`, the draft-aware
`load_format` → `get_model()`, and a PP size → `get_parallel()` (live topology, which
is what the DSA indexer wants).

**Two reads move to the instance instead of a namespace.** The multimodal processor
picked its fast-image-processor device from the process-global config, but
`base_gpu_id` differs per worker — the encode-server DP workers each specialise their
own copy — so no process-global value can stand in for it, and several `Engine`s can
share a tokenizer process. The decision moves into
`BaseMultimodalProcessor._fast_image_processor_device`, reading the instance the
processor was constructed with, like the ten other config reads in that class. Branch
order, the NPU preprocess patches and the case that leaves `device` unset are
unchanged.

**What stays is the derived API**: `mamba_cache_chunk_size` (`@property`),
`get_model_config()`, `enable_mamba_extra_buffer{,_lazy}()` — computed from several
fields plus the HF config, so they are not namespace leaves and `ServerArgs` is their
only home. Two config-intent reads of live-shadowed sizes also stay: `get_parallel()`
shadows `tp/pp/dcp/attn_cp/moe_dp_size` with the live topology, and both sites run
where no process group exists (`cuda_ipc_transport_utils` even guards for "not
published yet").

A new AST ratchet pins field reads at zero and exempts the above by name, with the
reasoning in its docstring.

## Test changes

`test_dllm_fdfo_kv_reuse` rebound `allocation.get_server_args` to a
`SimpleNamespace`. That kind of stand-in stops intercepting the moment a reader
migrates — which is exactly what happened here — so it publishes a real config now.
New `test_processor_device_selection.py` pins the per-instance device resolution
against a conflicting published config.

## Validation

Per-area unit suites (`mem_cache`, `multimodal`, `batch_overlap`,
`layers/attention`, `managers`) and all ratchets pass. Full registered CPU battery
(16 partitions) against `main`: seven branch-only failures, each re-run serially and
green — two were port collisions from the parallel run itself, the rest are the
box's standing environment failures. No new failures.

Not covered locally: the flipped reads sit in model and attention paths that need a
GPU to execute; the flips are value-preserving (the bags are projected from the same
published config), but the speculative and model CI suites are the real check.

title: [Perf] Speed up the Kimi-K2.5 vision path and match PIL bicubic in the GPU resize
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary

Speeds up the Kimi-K2.5/K2.7 vision and preprocessing path, and fixes the GPU image resize so it reproduces what the checkpoint's HF processor produces.

## Fix: GPU resize did not match `PIL.Image.resize(..., BICUBIC)`

`KimiGPUProcessorWrapper` bypasses the HF media processor and resizes on the GPU with `F.interpolate(mode="bicubic")`. Two mismatches against PIL:

- PIL's bicubic widens its kernel support by the scale factor, i.e. it always antialiases on downscale. `F.interpolate` needs `antialias=True` to do the same. Kimi's NaViT sizing only ever downscales, so every resized image took the aliased path.
- PIL returns `uint8`. The GPU path fed unquantized floats (including bicubic overshoot outside `[0, 255]`) straight into normalization.

Measured against real `PIL.Image.resize(..., BICUBIC)`, per 8-bit channel:

| content | before, mean / max abs err | after, mean / max abs err |
|---|---|---|
| photo-like (1024x1024 -> 476x476) | 3.79 / 34.5 | 0.15 / 2.0 |
| photo-like (2048x1536 -> 476x364) | 5.25 / 38.8 | 0.10 / 1.0 |
| uniform noise (512x512 -> 252x252) | 38.9 / 173.2 | 0.15 / 5.0 |

Against PIL's *float* path the two agree to ~5e-3, so the resampling kernel now matches exactly and the residual above is only PIL's fixed-point arithmetic for `uint8` images.

This changes model inputs on the K2.5 GPU preprocessing path — toward the reference processor, not away from it.

## Perf

- **Fused QK RoPE.** A fused interleaved-complex kernel replaces the `view_as_complex` round trip in every MoonViT encoder block.
- **Fused normalize + patchify.** `normalize_and_patchify` replaces the pad -> `/255` -> `(x - mean) * inv_std` -> reshape/permute chain, folding the constants into one affine (`scale = 1/(255*std)`, `bias = -mean/std`).
- **No redundant `max_seqlen` sync.** `prepare_vision_attention_metadata` grows an optional `max_seqlen`, so the caller's already-computed value is reused instead of forcing a second device-to-host sync per forward.
- **`grid_thws` stays on the host.** MoonViT3d only ever reads it as shape metadata (`.tolist()` in the pos-emb, RoPE and merger), so the non-DP path no longer copies it to CUDA — that copy cost one sync per read. This is the contract the encoder-DP path in `mm_utils` already relies on.
- **No throwaway tokenizer pass.** With `prefer_tokenized_input`, the wrapper was decoding to text, splicing thousands of repeated `<|media_pad|>` strings and re-tokenizing — only for `process_and_combine_mm_data` to discard that and re-expand the original IDs anyway (`SGLANG_MM_AVOID_RETOKENIZE` defaults on). Expand the incoming IDs directly with `np.repeat` and set `preserve_processor_input_ids` so the base class skips its now-identical rebuild.
- **Single-image concat elided.** `concat_or_single` moves into `mm_utils` and is shared by the four encoder-DP concat sites and the projector, so a one-image request no longer copies its embedding.

B300, K2.5 vision config (patch 14, 16 heads, 27 layers, hidden 1152):

| | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| QK RoPE, 27 layers, 5329 tokens | 2.107 ms | 0.310 ms | 6.8x |
| QK RoPE, 27 layers, 12544 tokens | 4.604 ms | 0.649 ms | 7.1x |
| normalize + patchify, 1x 1022x1022 | 0.082 ms | 0.015 ms | 5.4x |
| normalize + patchify, 8x 1022x1022 | 0.296 ms | 0.066 ms | 4.5x |
| attention metadata per forward | 61.4 us | 39.4 us | one sync removed |

About 1.9 ms per 1024x1024 image off the vision path, before counting the `grid_thws` syncs.

## Other changes

- **Concurrent processing.** `supports_mm_processor_concurrency` with 2 processor / 16 IO workers. This required building the GPU wrapper *before* `super().__init__`, since the base constructor clones `self._processor` for the worker pool — cloning the raw HF processor would have silently bypassed Kimi's GPU preprocessing.
- **The CPU fallback keeps the request's tokens too.** `preserve_processor_input_ids` disables the base rebuild on every path, so `_cpu_call` now expands the placeholders itself instead of letting the HF re-tokenization through.
- **One-to-one placeholder validation.** `count_image_placeholders` returns the token count or `None` for a text prompt; the caller decides between `fast_load_mm_data` and `load_mm_data` and raises on a mismatch. KimiVL gets the same check.
- **Raw `uint8` contract enforced.** `_ensure_chw_rgb` rejects non-`uint8` input: the resize rounds to integers and the normalization folds in a `1/255` scale, so an already-normalized float image would collapse to 0/1 and then be rescaled.
- **Fused RoPE gated on dtype.** The in-place kernel is a JIT template on the q/k dtype; only fp16/bf16 are covered by tests, so other dtypes stay on the portable path.
- `tpool_patch_merger` moves next to `patch_merger` in `kimi_vl_moonvit.py` and skips the temporal mean when `t == 1` (bit-identical: averaging one frame is a divide by 1). `mm_projection_auto` returns the packed 2D feature instead of splitting per image for the sole caller to concatenate right back.

## Test plan

- `test/registered/unit/models/test_kimi_k25.py` — 23 passed. New coverage for the PIL-bicubic match, placeholder counting and expansion, the CPU fallback preserving request tokens, the `uint8` guard, the `t == 1` pooling equivalence, the packed projection contract, and a guard that the non-DP path hands `grid_thws` to the tower on the host (a `meta` tower device makes a stray `.to()` visible without a GPU; verified to fail against the previous code).
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/test_kimi_k3_prerequisite_ops.py` — new `test_vision_rope_inplace` covers the in-place kernel this PR actually ships (the existing `test_vision_rope` covers the non-in-place variant) for bf16 and fp16, plus its `complex64` input check.
- `test/registered/vlm/test_token_id_retokenize_e2e.py` — passes, covering the `SGLANG_MM_AVOID_RETOKENIZE` path that the new `preserve_processor_input_ids` gate sits on.
- `test/manual/vlm/verify_k25_equivalence.py` (new, needs a GPU) proves the two rewrites match the code they replace:
  - `normalize_and_patchify` vs the old pad/normalize/patchify, max abs diff `4.8e-07`, including padded cells correctly carrying `-mean/std` rather than 0.
  - fused RoPE vs the `view_as_complex` reference: **bit-identical** (max abs diff `0.00e+00`) for bf16 and fp16 across `{1024, 4096, 37}` tokens x `{16, 8, 4}` heads x `{72, 128, 64}` head dims.

title: fix: always capture default prefill CUDA graph
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- remove the fixed 4 GiB runtime gate added by #31204
- always capture an automatically selected prefill CUDA graph instead of silently falling back to eager execution based on free memory
- remove the defensive `getattr` and replace the obsolete threshold tests with a regression test that verifies capture still proceeds with 3.99 GiB free

Existing explicit disable and model/backend compatibility guards are unchanged.

## Root cause

The memory gate used a model-agnostic fixed threshold after weights, KV cache, and eager buffers were allocated. That allowed default configurations to disable prefill CUDA graphs at runtime and introduced a silent performance regression for otherwise supported models.

Memory sizing should be handled by the configured cache/capture parameters. An automatically selected prefill graph should not be overridden by a hard-coded free-memory threshold.

## Validation

title: [Feat] speculative: Seed rejection-sampling draft proposals for deterministic inference
author: ajit283
body:
## Motivation

Classic EAGLE/NEXTN rejection sampling draws each draft proposal with `fast_sample()`. Although target sampling and verify-side rejection coins support request-local seeds, this proposal draw used the global PyTorch RNG (`exponential_()`), so `--enable-deterministic-inference` still changed outputs with batch shape and CUDA graph replay.

This is the draft-worker follow-up documented in #30822. Before this change, Qwen3.5-9B NEXTN rejection sampling produced 12 unique outputs in 12 changing-batch trials with a fixed sampling seed.

## Modifications

- Add an optional deterministic path to `fast_sample()` keyed by:
  - request sampling seed
  - absolute sequence position
  - draft step / MTP layer
  - vocabulary entry
- Domain-separate draft proposal randomness from target sampling and verify-side rejection coins.
- Convert MurmurHash32 output to open-interval uniforms with midpoint binning, then use exponential-race categorical sampling in float64.
- Preserve the existing RNG-backed fast path when deterministic inference is disabled.
- Plumb request seeds and positions through eager and CUDA-graph EAGLE/NEXTN workers.
- Support both ordinary and multi-layer EAGLE, including the single-CUDA-graph multi-layer draft-extend path.
- Keep deterministic rejection sampling guarded on non-CUDA-compatible devices because this implementation uses a Triton hash kernel.
- Add sampler tests for replay, batch permutation/splitting, seed/position/step separation, hash endpoints, CUDA graph updates, and categorical distribution sanity.
- Add dedicated deterministic E2E smoke tests without changing the existing unseeded rejection-sampling and chain-MTP test configurations.
- Add a reproducible seeded/unseeded sampling microbenchmark.

## Accuracy Tests

### Regular EAGLE/NEXTN

Qwen3.5-9B, TP2, NEXTN, rejection sampling, temperature 1.0, sampling seed 42:

| Version | Changing-batch trials | Unique outputs |
|---|---:|---:|
| Before | 12 | 12 |
| After | 12 | 1 |

The deterministic harness also passed changing batch sizes, prefix batching, bitwise logprob comparison, and radix-cache consistency.

Post-rebase validation on B200:

```text
7 passed, 16 warnings, 2 subtests passed
Total samples: 6, Unique samples: 1
OK
```

The unit suite includes 100,000 distinct seeded draws from `[0.1, 0.2, 0.7]` and verifies that observed frequencies are within 0.01 absolute tolerance.

### Multi-layer EAGLE

`stepfun-ai/Step-3.5-Flash`, TP8 on 8x B200, FA4, three MTP layers, single-CUDA-graph draft extend:

```text
Total samples: 6, Unique samples: 1
MULTI_LAYER_EAGLE_REJECTION_SAMPLING_IS_DETERMINISTIC
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B200, vocabulary size 163,840, CUDA-graph replay:

| Batch | Unseeded | Seeded | Slowdown |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 31.9 us | 47.2 us | 1.48x |
| 8 | 38.0 us | 63.5 us | 1.67x |
| 32 | 54.5 us | 131.9 us | 2.42x |
| 128 | 138.9 us | 544.1 us | 3.92x |

Peak allocated memory for batch 128 and vocabulary 163,840:

```text
Input probabilities:       80.00 MiB
Baseline allocated:        80.00 MiB
Peak allocated:           321.25 MiB
Incremental seeded peak:  241.25 MiB
```

The deterministic mode is opt-in. A fused hash/exponential/argmax kernel can be considered separately if end-to-end profiling shows that the materialized hash and score matrices materially affect serving throughput.

title: [jit_kernel] Move JIT kernels into namespace sglang
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> Generated by Claude.

## Motivation

Every JIT kernel used to sit in the global namespace (or an anonymous one), with a handful of files having already started on `namespace sglang` and reaching back out via `using namespace sglang;` / `sglang::`. This unifies that: all JIT C++ under `python/sglang/kernels/jit/` now lives in `namespace sglang`, and no `sglang::` qualification is needed anywhere inside it.

## Modifications

- **`namespace sglang` everywhere** — device kernels, traits and the host wrapper together, plus the shared `include/sgl_kernel/` headers, so `host::` / `device::` resolve unqualified. 166 C++ files.
- **`load_jit` emits the export inside the namespace** — `_make_sources` wraps `TVM_FFI_DLL_EXPORT_TYPED_FUNC` in `namespace sglang { ... }`, so the Python-side `kernel_name` is written without a prefix (`Add3Kernel<...>::launch`, not `sglang::Add3Kernel<...>::launch`).
- **Dropped the reach-arounds** — the 5 `using namespace sglang;` and every redundant `sglang::`. The `sglang_<kernel>` pseudo-namespaces under `csrc/diffusion/` become real nesting (`sglang::norm_scale_shift`, `sglang::usp_relayout`, ...), with the Python wrapper names updated to match.
- **Removed 102 top-level anonymous namespaces** — `namespace sglang` already scopes these names, symbols are not interposed across separately `dlopen`ed modules, and each header-only module compiles exactly one root source. One consequence needed handling: `gemm/per_token_group_quant.cuh`'s file-local `details` became ambiguous with `device::details` once the anonymous namespace stopped isolating it, so it is now `detail`.
- **Fixed `::arrive_barrier`** in `gemm/dsv3_fused_a_gemm.cuh` — it resolved to global scope while the function moved into `namespace sglang`. See the note below on why this one was easy to miss.
- Docs + `add-jit-kernel` skill note the namespace convention.

### Deliberately left at global scope

| Files | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `csrc/moe/tvm_ffi_utils.h` | near-verbatim FlashInfer port, no `sgl_kernel` dependency |
| `csrc/fast-hadamard-transform/*.h` | vendored from Tri Dao / sgl-project fork, ditto |
| `csrc/sparse_mla_q8kv8_prefill_sm90/*` (7 files) | `kernel.cuh` needs a global `using namespace cute;` *before* mid-file `#include`s of the `dense_fp8` headers, which cannot survive wrapping. Only its `entry.cuh` host wrapper moved in. |
| `csrc/attention/kda_prefill.cu` | builds via `torch.utils.cpp_extension`, not `load_jit` |
| `csrc/moe/expert_specialization/*` (4 files) | not reachable from any `load_jit` call — the live path is the AOT twin in `aot/csrc/expert_specialization/` |

## Accuracy Tests

All 137 kernel test files were run on 8x B200, one test per GPU across 7 cards.

**The sweep caught a real bug.** `::arrive_barrier` broke `test_dsv3_fused_a_gemm` (192 failed), and a header-include-only compile did *not* catch it: nvcc defers lookup of non-dependent names inside template bodies until instantiation. After the fix it is **192 passed**. I then scanned every `::identifier` in the tree — the rest are genuinely global (`cuda*`, `atomicAdd`, `min`/`max`/`abs`, `TVMFFI*`) or `decltype(...)::value` false hits.

Multi-GPU (via each file's own torchrun entry point, world sizes <= 6):

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `test_custom_all_reduce --num-gpu 2,4` | 180 passed each |
| `test_tp_qknorm --num-gpu 2,4` | 42 passed each |
| `test_symm_mem_all_gather --num-gpu 4,6` | 48 passed (4-GPU self-skips by design) |
| `kimi_k3/test_collectives --num-gpu 4` | 4 passed |
| `test_dcp_lse_combine` | 21 passed |

Remaining failures were each re-run against `HEAD` in a separate worktree and are pre-existing with identical failure sets: `test_per_token_group_quant_8bit_v2` (66, JIT-vs-AOT bit-exactness on B200), `test_qknorm_rope` (1/1249 bf16 rounding), `test_dsa_indexer` (`MockModelRunner` missing an attribute), `test_kernels_namespace` (`assert 'CLEAN' in 'DIRTY'`, local env), `test_varlen_uspattn_equivalence` (local `flash_attn` missing `flash_attn_varlen_func`), and the two CP parity tests (need multi-GPU).

### Two pre-existing test failures fixed along the way

Both are B200-only, because the JIT kernel CI runs on H100/H200 and never exercises the Blackwell branch of `kMaxVecBytes = SGL_ARCH_BLACKWELL_OR_GREATER ? 32 : 16`:

- **`test_activation`** — the `(7, 16)` / `(3, 5, 16)` shapes give `hidden=8`, which the kernel rejects outright when the fp16/bf16 vector is 16 elements wide. Dropped rather than made arch-conditional; every remaining shape is 16-aligned. 24 failed -> **451 passed** (97 in CI mode).
- **`test_fused_add_rmsnorm`** — bf16's 1 ulp is `2^-8 ~= 7.8e-3`, so `rtol=1e-2` expressed only 1.28 ulp while the fp32 reference (which rounds in a different order than the kernel) disagrees by up to 1.75 ulp. The fp32-reference path now uses `rtol=1.5e-2`, the tightest bound that clears the noise — it still catches a systematic 0.75% deviation, whereas `2e-2` would let 1% through. No cases removed: 2 failed / 558 passed -> **560 passed**.

## Checklist

- [x] `pre-commit run` clean on the diff (incl. pinned clang-format 20.1.7, CI-registry validation)
- [x] No non-ASCII introduced in C++ sources
- [x] Namespace braces verified programmatically to sit on the same `#if` branch in every file

title: Fix deterministic inference for Inkling
author: ispobock
body:
## Motivation

`--enable-deterministic-inference` does not hold for Inkling -- scoring the same context twice returns different logprobs. On the checkpoint the per-commit consistency test uses (bf16, tp=1, fa4) it reports **4380 mismatching observations out of 6072**, and on `Inkling-Small-NVFP4` at tp=8 **50302 out of 116k**. Three code paths pick an implementation from the batch shape:

- **fa4 derives its masked/unmasked KV-block split from `seqlen_q`** (`BlockInfo.get_n_block_min_causal_local_mask`), so a block lands on a differently-rounding path depending on query-tile alignment -- a prefill and a cache-hit extend covering the same row disagree. A model-free repro clusters the output by `qo_len <= seqlen_k % tile_n`, and page-aligned `seqlen_k` gives one cluster. The modulus is `tile_n`, not `page_size`: sweeping page_size 128 to 1 leaves the boundary unmoved. `num_splits=1` fixes the KV-side split but not this one. `batch_invariant` masks every block instead, which is identity below the diagonal.
- **`RelLogitsProj` picks its implementation from the token count**, so a row's kernel follows the batch composition. Custom kernels bypass the aten overrides `batch_invariant_ops` installs.
- **`should_torch_symm_mem_allreduce()` takes the symmetric-memory path only below a byte threshold**, so which reduce runs follows the token count. Deterministic inference already pins `NCCL_ALGO=allreduce:tree` and disables custom all-reduce for tp>1; symmetric memory was the one path that block did not cover, and at tp=8 it dominates -- every layer all-reduces.

flashinfer autotune also selects configs per problem shape and is skipped as well. All are gated on `enable_deterministic_inference`; the default path is unchanged.

## Accuracy

Ablation on the per-commit configuration (Inkling bf16, tp=1, fa4, 6072 observations):

| fa4 split | dispatch gates | mismatches |
|---|---|---|
| – | – | 4380 |
| ✓ | – | 1844 |
| – | ✓ | 4070 |
| ✓ | ✓ | **0** |

Both are required. On `Inkling-Small-NVFP4` at tp=8 with `--enable-torch-symm-mem`, over a 116k-observation workload (10 prefixes, 10 requests each, 2048-4096 token prefixes, 2048 new tokens), the symmetric-memory gate takes **50302 mismatches to 0**.

Max-abs distance to an fp32 reference is unchanged by the fa4 change (`7.040e-04` before and after at `seqlen_k=400`), so it moves rounding, not accuracy.

The 8-GPU variant of the consistency test follows in a separate PR: it passes on this branch (27 min, 116k observations, 0 mismatches) but is a nightly-suite addition worth reviewing on its own.

title: Reduce startup log noise and fix Dynamo / CUDA-graph edge cases
author: merrymercy
body:
## Summary

Server startup emits several redundant or misleading log lines, and two small
correctness issues were found alongside them.

**Log noise:**
- The eight per-backend `"<X> MoE is enabled. The expert parallel size is adjusted ..."` warnings in `server_args.py` all say the same thing and fire unconditionally, even when `ep_size` already equals `tp_size`. They are replaced by one `logger.info` inside the `_a2a_ep_size` post-process, which is the single place the adjustment actually happens, and which only logs when the value really changes.
- The `"DeepGemm is enabled but the scale_fmt of checkpoint is not ue8m0"` warning fires on every non-ue8m0 checkpoint and is not actionable. Removed along with the now-unused `use_scale_ue8m0` attribute (it had no other readers).
- A missing `generation_config.json` is normal for many checkpoints and HF surfaces it as a generic `OSError`, not `FileNotFoundError`, so the fallback path logged a `WARNING` on every such startup. Both exception types are now handled together at `DEBUG`.
- The TRTLLM MoE deferred-finalize line used `print_info_once`, which keys on the full message; because different MoE layers can resolve to different quant methods, it printed once per distinct quant method. A module-level flag makes it once per rank.

**Correctness:**
- `load_jit` is now `@torch.compiler.disable`d. JIT compilation is pure Python/filesystem plumbing (`.resolve()` calls `os.lstat`, etc.) that Dynamo cannot trace, so a lazily-loaded kernel first reached from inside a `@torch.compile`d region produced spurious `Dynamo does not know how to trace the builtin 'posix.lstat'` graph breaks. The load is memoized, so keeping it out of the graph costs nothing.
- `BreakableCudaGraphBackend` constructed `BreakableCUDAGraph()` with no argument, so despite mixing in `DedupedCudaGraphMixin` its segments were never registered with the dedup registry. It now passes `self.deduped_cuda_graph`.
- The VLM `mem_fraction_static` adjustment is skipped when `disaggregation_mode == "decode"`. The vision encoder only runs during prefill, so PD decode engines were reserving encoder headroom they never use, shrinking the KV pool. Prefill and non-PD engines are unaffected.

Behavior for non-PD and non-multimodal serving is unchanged apart from the log output.

## Test plan

- `uv run pre-commit run --files <the 7 changed files>` — all hooks pass.
- `python3 -m py_compile` on all 7 changed files — clean.
- Verified `use_scale_ue8m0` has no remaining readers anywhere in `python/` or `test/` before removing it.
- Verified no test asserts on any of the removed/reworded log strings.
- Verified `BreakableCUDAGraph.__init__` already accepts an optional `deduped_cuda_graph` and that `DedupedCudaGraphMixin` provides the `deduped_cuda_graph` attribute, so the new argument needs no signature change.
- Not run: GPU end-to-end serving, PD-disaggregated decode startup, and the `torch.compile` + JIT-kernel path. These need multi-GPU hardware not available in this environment; the change relies on CI for runtime coverage.

title: [Fix] Skip padded state slots in the chunked GDN kernel
author: Oasis-Git
body:
_forward_metadata poisons padded request rows with state index -1, and the decode kernel already skips them (fused_recurrent: `if idx >= 0`). The chunked extend kernel had no such guard, so -1 reached `initial_state + index * stride_init_state` for both the initial-state load and the in-place final-state store, addressing before the state pool. boundary_check does not help: it validates against the declared block shape, not the allocation.

Under breakable-CUDA-graph prefill with DP attention an idle DP rank replays an extend with an all-padded batch, so every row carries -1 and the kernel faults with cudaErrorIllegalAddress. Reproduced on Qwen3-Next-80B and Qwen3.5-397B on pristine main; a single request against --dp 4 is enough. No per-commit suite covers a linear-attn hybrid with DP attention, which is why this went unseen.

Add a regression test in the existing base-b (1-GPU, per-commit) kernel suite; it fails without the guard.

title: [NVIDIA] Use sm_100f instead of sm_100a for sgl-kernel and FlashMLA

## Motivation

CUDA 12.9+ supports `sm_100f` which is able to run on all sm_10x-family GPUs, whereas `sm_100a` can only run on `sm_100a` GPUs.

We can use this to reduce wheel size by removing redundant `sm_103` binaries while also being able to run on Rubin `sm_107` when it is available.

See https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-blackwell-and-nvidia-cuda-12-9-introduce-family-specific-architecture-features/ for more information.

## Modifications

Update arch build flags to use sm_100f for sgl-kernel and the FlashMLA submodule.

title: fix: support FA4 backend for GLM4.7-flash
author: zyzshishui
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Enable GLM-4.7-Flash to serve correctly with `--attention-backend fa4` on Blackwell using default non-deterministic decode and CUDA Graphs. SGLang's absorbed MLA presents 20 Q/QV heads over one latent KV head at TP1, but FA4's packed kernel requires the ratio to be compatible with its 128-row tile.

The current `pack_gqa=False` QV varlen decode path is incorrect for bs>1: queries after the first sequence can read another sequence's paged KV. Even if that upstream bug is fixed, unpacking would schedule Q heads separately instead of folding them into the M tile, repeating traversal of the shared latent KV and badly underutilizing 128-row decode tiles. Padding keeps the packed path; using one split also avoids unsupported automatic split-KV for QV MLA.

## Modifications

- Pad each Q/QV KV group to a tile-compatible power-of-two ratio (20 to 32 for GLM TP1), then crop output and LSE to the original heads.
- Use one split when a QV call requests automatic split selection.
- Materialize dense Q/K/V for the dedicated head-dimension-256 kernel.
- Add QV coverage to `test_flash_attn_varlen_output`. All runtime changes stay in the SGLang FA4 wrapper.

## Accuracy Tests

```bash
python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k \
  --num-questions 200 \
  --data-path gsm8k-test.jsonl \
  --port 30000
```

| FA4 | 0.830 | 166/200 | 0 | 11.215 s | 1668.941 |
| Triton | 0.820 | 164/200 | 0 | 8.889 s | 2075.046 |

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
The Kimi-K3 SiTU activation kernels cannot be JIT-compiled on ROCm.`situ_and_mul.cuh` includes `<cuda_fp8.h>` unconditionally, which is a CUDA-only header, so hipcc fails with:

   21 | #include <cuda_fp8.h>
      |          ^~~~~~~~~~~~
1 error generated when compiling for gfx950.
```

Guard the `<cuda_fp8.h>` include with `#ifndef USE_ROCM`

title: [diffusion] FLUX.2 VAE decoder fast path behind quality=high (H200: 1024^2 97.6->29.2 ms, 2048^2 437.2->168.5 ms)
author: BBuf
body: Branch: `pr-flux2-vae-fastpath`, single commit `eada083612` on `main` (7ba393dd15, post-#33453), standalone — no dependencies. 5 files, +920/−28. ## Motivation FLUX.2 image generation spends 97.6 ms (1024^2) / 437.2 ms (2048^2) per image in VAE decode on H200. Profiling the decoder (diffusers `Decoder`) shows two structural problems: - the `GroupNorm -> SiLU` chains upcast to fp32 under autocast and are ~46% of decode time — and they get *worse* if you naively switch to channels_last, because aten GroupNorm is ~2x slower on NHWC and the existing `triton_group_norm_silu` kernel forces a `.contiguous()` (NCHW) round-trip on channels_last inputs; - the decoder runs NCHW, so every cuDNN conv pays nchwToNhwc/nhwcToNchw transpose kernels, and the D512 mid-block runs a single-head attention whose diffusers `AttnProcessor2_0` forward is layout-unsafe (calls `.view` on the 4D activation). This PR adds (a) a layout-aware two-pass GroupNorm(+SiLU) Triton kernel and (b) a request-scoped, quality-gated FLUX.2 VAE decoder fast path built on it. All decoder rewrites are mathematically exact re-associations of the original operators (weight folding is done lazily in fp32 on first fast-path use). ## Modifications **1. Kernel** — new `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/triton/group_norm_silu_twopass.py` (+232): - Channels-last only. Pass 1: per-(batch, channel) partial sum / sum-of-squares reduction over (N, L, C) rows with C innermost (serves channels_last 4D via a free permute view). Finalize: per-(batch, group) fp32 mean/rstd with the affine transform folded into per-(batch, channel) scale/shift. Pass 2: fused elementwise apply + optional SiLU. - Public API `group_norm_silu_4d` / `group_norm_silu_rows` returns `None` for unsupported inputs (non-CUDA, grad enabled, non-pow2 C, C > 2048, not channels_last); callers must fall back. - Coexists with the existing general `group_norm_silu.py` (any channels-per-group, always-SiLU, NCHW via `.contiguous()`), which keeps serving the HunyuanVAE / latent-upsampler paths unchanged; on NCHW the two are a wash (63–219 us vs 81–210 us), so this kernel deliberately has no NCHW variant — gate-off decodes run the original aten path, never this kernel. Documented in the module docstring. **2. FLUX.2 fast paths + gate** — `runtime/models/vaes/flux2_vae_cuda_opt.py` (+421): - `CudaPlatform.optimize_vae` (existing platform hook called by the VAE loader, +22 in `platforms/cuda.py`) installs always-present fast-path wrappers on the FLUX.2 decoder; each wrapper's forward dispatches on a shared per-VAE `VaeFastPathGate` (a module-local bool holder published on the VAE as `_sgl_vae_fast_path_gate`). - Gate semantics: **`quality == "high"` (#33453 tier) runs the fast paths; the `"lossless"` default runs the original module path bit-for-bit** (verified byte-identical below), so golden-output CI is unaffected. - Install is all-or-nothing and fail-closed: without Triton, or with any attention block lacking the layout-safe rewrite, nothing is installed and every request runs the unmodified decoder. - **channels_last decoding**: parameter layout swapped at decode entry to match the gate (layout swaps are pure permutations), so lossless decodes always run the baseline NCHW kernels bit-for-bit. - **GroupNorm+SiLU fusion** via the new two-pass kernel (ResnetBlock2D norm1/norm2 + SiLU chains and the `conv_norm_out`/`conv_act` tail). - **Fused nearest-2x upsample + Conv2d(3x3, p1) == ConvTranspose2d(k4, s2, p1)** with a lazily-summed kernel (nearest upsampling is pure pixel replication, so the fusion only re-associates conv taps). - **Layout-safe single-head attention forward** with the output projection folded into V (softmax rows sum to 1, so `A @ (V W_v^T + b_v) W_o^T + b_o == A @ (V W'^T) + b'`). Attention stays on the stock SDPA backend here; the exact chunked D512 composition for >= 16k tokens is a follow-up PR (recovers 168.1 -> ~147 ms at 2048^2). **3. DecodingStage wiring** — `pipelines_core/stages/decoding.py` (+39/−27, mostly the try/finally re-indent): - `DecodingStage.forward` sets the gate for the duration of a decode iff the request's `quality` sampling param is `"high"` and always restores it in a `finally`; VAEs without installed wrappers have no gate attribute (no-op). Follow-up PRs: (1) chunked D512 attention composition; (2) Qwen-Image VAE fast paths. ## Speedup All numbers H200, bf16 decode. Three levels: **Kernel microbenchmark** (FLUX.2 VAE decoder norm shapes, G=32, us per call, mean of 50; before = aten fp32 GroupNorm+SiLU on channels_last, after = new kernel on channels_last): | shape | aten CL | existing kernel fed CL | new CL | speedup vs aten / vs existing | |---|---|---|---|---| | (1, 512, 128, 128) | 365.9 | 93.0 | **76.0** | 4.8x / 1.2x | | (1, 512, 256, 256) | 1394.6 | 284.0 | **121.0** | 11.5x / 2.3x | | (1, 512, 512, 512) | 5863.9 | 1430.5 | **311.1** | 18.9x / 4.6x | | (1, 256, 1024, 1024) | 16310.2 | 7544.4 | **913.8** | 17.8x / 8.3x | | (1, 128, 1024, 1024) | 7965.2 | 3698.7 | **307.9** | 25.9x / 12.0x | (HunyuanVAE-style 5D shapes are untouched — no call site of the existing kernel changes.) **Component harness** (frozen decode-input latents, steady-state mean of 5 decodes, this branch): | workload | lossless (= main) | quality=high (this PR) | speedup | |---|---|---|---| | flux2 1024^2 | 97.6 ms | **29.3 ms** | 3.33x | | flux2 2048^2 | 437.2 ms | **168.1 ms** | 2.60x | Lossless-path timing on this branch is unregressed (97.1 / 437.0 ms vs main baseline 97.6 / 437.2 ms); the minimized branch reproduces the fast path at 29.2 / 168.5 ms (run-to-run noise of the numbers above). **End-to-end latency** (`sglang generate`, FLUX.2-klein-4B, H200, prompt "A futuristic cyberpunk city at night, neon lights reflecting on wet streets", seed 42, `--dit-layerwise-offload false --warmup --save-output`). Metric = per-request wall-clock measured client-side around the full request round-trip ("Pixel data generated successfully in X seconds"), which includes the VAE decode GPU time, the final sync, and the PNG write. Per cell: one warmed process serving sequential identical requests, first request dropped (absorbs the post-warmup pickup gap), median of >= 5 clean steady-state requests (min–max); requests hit by neighbor-GPU interference on the shared box are excluded via a denoise-time stability filter (DenoisingStage is untouched by this PR, so its per-request time must be flat): | resolution | default (lossless) | `--quality high` | Δ per request | component-harness decode Δ | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1024^2 | 0.740 s (0.69–0.80) | **0.640 s** (0.64–0.66) | **−0.100 s** | −68 ms (97.6 → 29.3) | | 2048^2 | 2.705 s (2.64–2.90) | **2.430 s** (2.41–2.50) | **−0.275 s** | −269 ms (437.2 → 168.1) | The e2e deltas match the component-harness decode deltas within run-to-run noise (a 4-step klein request is denoise-dominated, so decode's share of the request bounds the relative win). The component harness table above stays the authoritative decode-time measurement. Cross-checks: (1) the pipeline stage-timer total (`total_duration_ms`, printed as "Warmed-up request processed in X") stops at decode kernel launch without a CUDA sync, so it is decode-blind by construction — and it is flat between the two modes (medians of 5 independent cold-process runs per cell: 0.41 / 0.41 s at 1024^2, 1.47 / 1.46 s at 2048^2; perf-dump totals 407 / 407 ms and 1454 / 1457 ms), which independently confirms the gate adds no overhead to TextEncoding/Denoising or host-side dispatch. (2) `--quality high` is accepted end-to-end by the generic sampling-param validation, and the log confirms the fast path engages only there — "FLUX.2 VAE: decoder switched to channels_last (NHWC) layout" appears once per process (lazy fold, not per request) and never in lossless runs. **End-to-end quality validation** (maintainer bar for `quality=high`: PSNR > 25 dB vs the lossless output, same seed and prompt, saved PNGs): | prompt | resolution | PSNR (dB) | SSIM | bar | PASS | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | cyberpunk city (main) | 1024^2 | 56.70 | 0.99949 | PSNR > 25 | yes | | cyberpunk city (main) | 2048^2 | 57.85 | 0.99930 | PSNR > 25 | yes | | mountain lake at sunrise | 1024^2 | 59.11 | 0.99900 | PSNR > 25 | yes | | elderly fisherman close-up portrait | 1024^2 | 58.06 | 0.99912 | PSNR > 25 | yes | All pairs sit 30+ dB above the bar (max per-pixel diff 4–6/255): the deviation is bf16 rounding-order level, not a visible quality change; the fp32 ground-truth check below confirms the fast path is not statistically further from an fp32 reference than the baseline bf16 decoder. ## Accuracy - **Lossless default is bit-exact end-to-end**: gate-off decodes of the frozen FLUX.2 latents on this branch produce byte-identical PNGs to the `origin/main` baseline (verified with `cmp` at 1024^2 and 2048^2), so golden-output CI is unaffected. - **fp32 ground-truth check** (frozen latents, 1024^2, full decoder): fast-path bf16 error vs an fp32 VAE ground truth is statistically identical to the baseline bf16 error — mean abs err 0.000828 vs 0.000824, p99 0.003051 vs 0.003027. - **e2e quality**: `--quality high` vs default output PSNR = 56.7–59.1 dB and SSIM >= 0.999 across 3 prompts / 2 resolutions (>= 55 dB internal bar; maintainer bar PSNR > 25 dB — see the e2e quality table above). - Unit tests: `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_flux2_vae_fastpath.py` (+206, one file, 7 cases: channels_last kernel numerics fp32/bf16 vs fp32 reference, rows variant as used by attention, unsupported-input `None` contract incl. NCHW; gate-off `torch.equal` + no eager folding + fast-path PSNR for GroupNorm+SiLU and fused upsample; attention V/proj fold exactness). 7 passed on H200. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. ## Sample outputs (lossless vs `--quality high`) FLUX.2-klein-4B, seed 42. Left: default (`lossless`, bit-exact reference path). Right: `--quality high` (fast path). Full-resolution originals; PSNR/SSIM per pair in the quality table above. | | lossless (default) | `--quality high` | |---|---|---| | cyberpunk city, 1024x1024 | | | | cyberpunk city, 2048x2048 | | | | mountain lake, 1024x1024 | | | | fisherman portrait, 1024x1024 | | | 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #30906077610](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30906077610) Latest PR Test (Extra): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #30906077382](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30906077382)

title: [Kimi-K3][NPU]  Support Kimi-K3 on NPU
author: McZyWu
body:
## Summary

Add Kimi-K3 support for Ascend NPU on top of upstream SGLang main and the GPU model integration from #32541.

This PR keeps shared/GPU behavior intact where possible and dispatches NPU-specific implementations through the Ascend backend. The extracted Ascend Triton kernels are proposed separately in sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu#658.

## Main changes

- Full 93-layer Kimi-K3 execution on Ascend with TP64/DP4.
- DeepEP and Ascend FuseEP integration.
- DSPARK / Speculative V2 with CUDA Graph decode batches 1/4/16.
- KDA prefill/verify and recurrent SSM/conv state commit/replay.
- MLA precision fallback using `torch_npu.npu_transpose_batchmatmul` instead of the numerically divergent `torch.ops.npu.batch_matmul_transpose` path.
- Kimi-K3 sigmoid routing and NPU grouped TopK renormalization.
- ModelSlim W4A8/MXFP loading and MoE weight-layout support.
- NPU top-k/top-p renormalization for DFlash verification.
- Four-node launch recipe under `scripts/playground/launch_kimi_k3_npu_4node.sh`.

## DSPARK graph behavior

For the validated greedy serving path the launch recipe now uses:

```bash
SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_PROPOSAL=1
SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_SAMPLING=0
```

This captures the shared-LM-head projection, Markov proposal head and greedy token selection as a draft-graph tail hook, matching the 0728 reference behavior. Stochastic sampling remains eager, avoiding its extra static logits/noise buffers and sampling kernels.

## Run
```bash
vi k3.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eo pipefail

NODE_RANK="$1"
source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh

export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1
export SGLANG_ONE_VISIBLE_DEVICE_PER_PROCESS=1
export SGLANG_NPU_USE_TRITON_PREFIX_KV_CACHE_STORE=1
export SGLANG_K3_SHARED_EXPERTS_ATTN_TP=1
export SGLANG_K3_DENSE_MLP_ATTN_TP=1
export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
export SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static
export SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_PROPOSAL=0
export SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_SAMPLING=0
export SGLANG_DSPARK_STACKED_CTX_KV=0
export SGLANG_DSPARK_EMBED_IN_GRAPH=0
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=enp194s0f0
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=enp194s0f0
export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32
export DEEP_NORMAL_MODE_USE_INT8_QUANT=1
export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=128
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=2000
export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_ROUND=64
export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_PER_ROUND_TOKENS=512
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV

unset ASCEND_CUSTOM_OPP_PATH
unset SGLANG_NPU_FUSED_MOE_MODE
unset ENABLE_PROFILING
unset SGLANG_K3_TRACE_STATE_FILE
unset SGLANG_K3_TRACE_HIDDEN_FILE

nohup python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true}' \
  --dist-init-addr <<first node>>:30143 \
  --nnodes 4 \
  --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --model-path /home/weights/Kimi-K3-W4A8 \
  --tokenizer-path /home/weights/Kimi-K3-W4A8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --attention-backend ascend \
  --device npu \
  --quantization modelslim \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tp-size 64 \
  --enable-dp-attention \
  --dp-size 4 \
  --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.72 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --cuda-graph-bs 1 4 16 \
  --max-running-requests 64 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30543 \
  --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
  --moe-a2a-backend deepep \
  --deepep-mode auto \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
  --speculative-draft-model-path /home/weights/Kimi-K3-DSpark \
  --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \
  --speculative-dspark-block-size 7 \
  --speculative-draft-attention-backend ascend \
  --linear-attn-verify-backend triton \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --watchdog-timeout 9000 \
  > 88.log 2>&1 &
```
```bash
bash k3.sh 0
bash k3.sh 1
bash k3.sh 2
bash k3.sh 3
```
## Performance follow-up

The corresponding attention-residual optimization is in sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu#658: score, softmax and residual mixing are fused into one persistent vector-core kernel, with token and block counts marked `do_not_specialize`.

Before extraction, three consecutive no-cache random 8K-input/1K-output, concurrency-1 runs measured:

| Run | TTFT (ms) | TPOT (ms) | Throughput (tok/s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 7358.21 | 14.67 | 45.2 |
| 2 | 7364.2 | 15.05 | 44.43 |
| 3 | 7603.79 | 15.24 | 43.61 |

Mean TPOT was 15.37 ms, with average accepted length about 7.32 and acceptance rate about 90%. These measurements document the validated source configuration; the extracted PR heads still require final hardware CI/performance confirmation.

## Precision validation

Validated on four Ascend nodes with full 93 layers, DeepEP, DSPARK/Spec V2 and graph decode batches 1/4/16:

- Fixed incremental generation for `The capital of France is`: max new tokens 1/2/3/8 and default length.
- Chat completion for `Who are you` completes coherently.
- GSM8K: 94.6% on 1,319 questions (96.5% on the 200-question smoke test).
- GPQA-Diamond: 94.44%.

## Static validation

- `git diff --check`
- conflict-marker scan
- Python `py_compile` for affected modules
- shell syntax check for the four-node launcher

## Compatibility

- GPU/shared paths are preserved where possible.
- NPU-specific kernels live in the Ascend backend or sgl-kernel-npu.
- Model weights and container images are not modified.

title: Select DeepGEMM standard layouts by memory budget
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation The standard DeepGEMM dispatcher currently selects the masked layout from expert parallelism alone. However, masked workspace grows with the local expert count and padded forward size, so a fixed expert-count threshold can miss safe performance opportunities and can still select shapes that exceed available memory. This follows the layout-selection discussion in [#33128](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33128#issuecomment-5162601075). ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_DEEPGEMM_STANDARD_LAYOUT={auto|masked|compact}`. - Add `SGLANG_DEEPGEMM_MASKED_MEMORY_BUDGET_FRACTION`, with a default of `0.25`. - Estimate masked peak workspace from the runtime token count, local expert count, model dimensions, activation dtype, and scale layout. - Cache a budget from the minimum free memory across ranks after eager buffers are allocated and before graph capture. Capture paths do not query free memory or synchronize. - Preserve explicit `masked` and `compact` overrides. ## Default Budget Calibration `Captured M` is the aggregate token dimension of a captured prefill bucket, not the ISL of one request. The masked layout allocates a padded M dimension for every local expert, so its workspace grows approximately linearly with both `Captured M` and the local expert count. The policy estimates the largest live stage as: ```text estimated_peak = local_experts * padded_M * max( input + input_scale + gateup_output, gateup_output + down_input + down_scale, down_input + down_scale + final_output, ) masked_budget = capture_start_free_memory * budget_fraction ``` The following matched Qwen3.5-397B serving measurements on GB300 GPUs were used for calibration. All memory values are per GPU. Values marked with `~` are estimated peak workspace; allocation values are taken from the CUDA OOM report. | Captured M | Local experts / topology | Masked memory | Serving result | | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | 8K | 512 / EP1 | ~34.2 GiB | Pass | | 8K | 256 / EP2 | ~17.1 GiB | Pass | | 8K | 128 / EP4 | ~8.5 GiB | Pass | | 8K | 64 / EP8 | ~4.2 GiB | Pass | | 16K | 512 / EP1 | ~67.3 GiB | CUDA Graph capture OOM | | 32K | 512 / EP1 | 129 GiB allocation | OOM | | 32K | 256 / EP2 | 64.5 GiB allocation | OOM | | 32K | 128 / EP4 | ~33 GiB | Pass | | 32K | 64 / EP8 | ~16 GiB | Pass | | 128K | 64 / EP8 | 64.1 GiB allocation | OOM | Immediately before CUDA Graph capture, the measured free memory was 170.48 GiB per GPU. The default follows from the observed boundaries: 1. The largest successful masked workspace was 34.2 GiB: `34.2 / 170.48 = 20.1%`. 2. The smallest masked workspace that failed was 64.1 GiB: `64.1 / 170.48 = 37.6%`. 3. A calibration value should therefore sit above 20.1% to retain every observed successful case and below 37.6% to reject every observed OOM case. 4. `0.25 * 170.48 = 42.62 GiB`, which is 8.42 GiB above the largest observed success and 21.48 GiB below the smallest observed OOM. It leaves 127.86 GiB, or 75% of capture-start free memory, for other graph pools, temporary activations, and allocator fragmentation. The default is intentionally conservative rather than a universal memory guarantee. `SGLANG_DEEPGEMM_MASKED_MEMORY_BUDGET_FRACTION` remains configurable because model dimensions, dtype, capture buckets, and allocator behavior can move these boundaries. ## Auto Policy E2E Verification The memory-aware policy was exercised end to end at this pull request head on 4 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs with Qwen3.5-397B FP8, breakable prefill CUDA Graph, and full decode CUDA Graph. Every formal request completed with zero request errors. | Captured M / topology | Estimated masked peak | Measured free / budget | Auto JIT layouts | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | | 8K / TP4-EP1 | 34.0 GiB | 175.64 / 43.91 GiB | masked only | 48/48, zero errors | | 16K / TP4-EP1 | 67.0 GiB | 170.48 / 42.62 GiB | masked + compact | 12/12, zero errors | | 32K / TP4-EP2 | 66.5 GiB | 174.58 / 43.65 GiB | masked + compact | 192/192, zero errors | | 32K / TP4-EP4 | 33.3 GiB | 175.15 / 43.79 GiB | masked only | 192/192, zero errors | The mixed JIT sets are expected: selection is evaluated from the runtime M, so large prefill buckets fall back to compact while smaller prefill/decode buckets can still use masked. Matched forced-layout controls completed with the same CUDA Graph configuration and zero errors. ## Accuracy Tests This pull request does not change the numerical implementation of either standard DeepGEMM layout. Quantization, scatter, grouped matrix multiplications, activation, down projection, and post-permute are unchanged. It only replaces the previous expert-count selector with the memory-budget gate described above. The underlying standard DeepGEMM path was already validated in [#33128](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33128) at [commit `02d9f2e642`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/02d9f2e642907ceadb60279165a9359a47d436b4). The model-level run used `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` on 16 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs with PP2/TP8/EP1, standard dispatch, the DeepGEMM MoE runner, FP8 weights, BF16 KV and SSM caches, and full decode CUDA Graph through batch size 256. ```bash python -m sglang.test.run_eval \ --base-url http://localhost:8000 \ --eval-name gsm8k \ --num-examples 1319 \ --num-shots 5 \ --num-threads 256 \ --max-tokens 16384 \ --temperature 0 ``` Every scored request completed without request-level errors: **1,288 correct and 26 incorrect, for 0.9802130898 accuracy (1,288/1,314)**. The five-shot harness reserves five records from the 1,319-record GSM8K test file as demonstrations and scores the remaining 1,314 records. The existing Blackwell kernel test also executes the masked and compact layouts explicitly for FP8 and BF16 expert weights and compares their end-to-end outputs. This pull request only adds the focused policy coverage for the new selection boundary. ## Speed Tests and Profiling We compared the standard DeepGEMM masked and compact layouts on NVIDIA GB300 GPUs using Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 shapes. Apart from the explicit layout override, every matched pair used the same topology, workload, backend, and CUDA Graph settings. Only completed, exact-token, zero-error pairs are included. `M` is the aggregate number of MoE input rows. Across all **50 valid matched comparisons**, masked was faster: - Isolated standard runner: **24/24**, with **+40.4% to +160.7%** equivalent throughput. - Full serving, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024: **12/12**, with **+14.34% to +41.39%** total TPS/GPU. - Prefill, OSL 1: **14/14**, with **+2.69% to +68.25%** total TPS/GPU. The detailed tables are collapsed by default.
Isolated standard runner: 24/24 wins (+40.4% to +160.7%) Masked was faster for every tested M and topology. Values are median eager-mode latency per invocation; lower latency is better, and gain is `compact_latency / masked_latency - 1`. | Topology | Local experts | M | Compact (ms) | Masked (ms) | Masked throughput gain | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | TP4/EP1 | 512 | 512 | 1.2703 | 0.6926 | +83.4% | | TP4/EP1 | 512 | 1,024 | 1.2953 | 0.6869 | +88.6% | | TP4/EP1 | 512 | 2,048 | 1.3436 | 0.6935 | +93.8% | | TP4/EP1 | 512 | 4,096 | 1.4598 | 0.7132 | +104.7% | | TP4/EP1 | 512 | 8,192 | 1.4467 | 1.0306 | +40.4% | | TP4/EP1 | 512 | 16,384 | 2.2249 | 1.4313 | +55.4% | | TP4/EP2 | 256 | 512 | 1.2750 | 0.6135 | +107.8% | | TP4/EP2 | 256 | 1,024 | 1.2719 | 0.6011 | +111.6% | | TP4/EP2 | 256 | 2,048 | 1.2780 | 0.5772 | +121.4% | | TP4/EP2 | 256 | 4,096 | 1.3359 | 0.5575 | +139.6% | | TP4/EP2 | 256 | 8,192 | 1.4396 | 0.6614 | +117.7% | | TP4/EP2 | 256 | 16,384 | 1.8592 | 0.8383 | +121.8% | | TP4/EP4 | 128 | 512 | 1.2648 | 0.6296 | +100.9% | | TP4/EP4 | 128 | 1,024 | 1.2755 | 0.6344 | +101.0% | | TP4/EP4 | 128 | 2,048 | 1.2120 | 0.6224 | +94.7% | | TP4/EP4 | 128 | 4,096 | 1.2498 | 0.6044 | +106.8% | | TP4/EP4 | 128 | 8,192 | 1.3141 | 0.5782 | +127.3% | | TP4/EP4 | 128 | 16,384 | 1.6254 | 0.6372 | +155.1% | | TP8/EP8 | 64 | 512 | 1.2008 | 0.6072 | +97.7% | | TP8/EP8 | 64 | 1,024 | 1.1865 | 0.6254 | +89.7% | | TP8/EP8 | 64 | 2,048 | 1.1970 | 0.6100 | +96.2% | | TP8/EP8 | 64 | 4,096 | 1.2048 | 0.6009 | +100.5% | | TP8/EP8 | 64 | 8,192 | 1.2642 | 0.5864 | +115.6% | | TP8/EP8 | 64 | 16,384 | 1.5085 | 0.5785 | +160.7% |
Full serving: 12/12 wins (+14.34% to +41.39%) Masked improved total TPS/GPU at every concurrency for ISL 8192 / OSL 1024 with FP8 KV cache, breakable prefill CUDA Graph, and full decode CUDA Graph. | Topology | Concurrency | Compact total TPS/GPU | Masked total TPS/GPU | Masked gain | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | TP4/EP1 | 64 | 3,116.39 | 4,228.26 | +35.68% | | TP4/EP1 | 256 | 7,053.88 | 8,194.68 | +16.17% | | TP4/EP1 | 512 | 9,094.61 | 10,398.62 | +14.34% | | TP4/EP2 | 64 | 3,608.80 | 5,102.49 | +41.39% | | TP4/EP2 | 256 | 7,600.70 | 9,530.51 | +25.39% | | TP4/EP2 | 512 | 9,477.80 | 11,310.73 | +19.34% | | TP4/EP4 | 64 | 3,872.37 | 5,427.89 | +40.17% | | TP4/EP4 | 256 | 7,648.09 | 10,206.96 | +33.46% | | TP4/EP4 | 512 | 9,304.69 | 12,013.25 | +29.11% | | TP8/EP8 | 64 | 2,608.40 | 3,647.59 | +39.84% | | TP8/EP8 | 256 | 4,726.60 | 6,656.01 | +40.82% | | TP8/EP8 | 512 | 5,215.81 | 6,844.06 | +31.22% |

title: Put the DSA cuda-graph page table in the pausable memory region
author: yueming-yuan
body:
Under RL training the engine is paused between rollouts to hand its GPU memory to the trainer. The DSA backend's wide `page_table` — `max_num_tokens x max_ctx_len` int32, the dominant static cuda-graph buffer once speculative decoding widens `max_num_tokens` — stayed resident across the pause because `init_cuda_graph_state` allocated it outside the memory saver's cuda-graph region.

`page_table` and `flashmla_metadata` are rewritten in full by the replay metadata path before every replay, so neither needs to survive a pause; both move inside the region. `cache_seqlens`, `cu_seqlens_q`, `cu_seqlens_k` and `real_page_table` are written once at init and would silently come back zeroed after a resume, so they stay outside.

The region comes from `TorchMemorySaverAdapter` with the `GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_CUDA_GRAPH` tag, matching how the graph runners tag their pools. Without `--enable-memory-saver` and `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH=1` the helper returns a `nullcontext`, so allocation is byte-for-byte unchanged on the default path.

Measured on GLM-5.2 744B (DSA + EAGLE) on GB300.

title: [AMD] Support prefill context parallel two batch overlap for DeepSeek V4
author: At1a8
body: ## Motivation DeepSeek V4 prefill context parallelism (CP) distributes long-context prefill across attention CP ranks, but introduces several per-layer CP collectives around attention and MoE. Previously, the DeepSeek V4 two-batch-overlap (TBO) path only supported non-CP DP/EP workflows: - `--enable-prefill-cp` with `--enable-two-batch-overlap` was rejected when DP attention was disabled. - CP batches were explicitly excluded by the runtime TBO gate. - Existing TBO operations only handled DP/EP communication and could not schedule CP all-gather/reduce-scatter operations. This PR enables TBO for the AMD/ROCm DeepSeek V4 DSA prefill CP path. Each eligible prefill batch is split into two sub-batches so that one sub-batch's CP MoE communication can overlap with the other sub-batch's attention and expert computation. Attention-side KV and `kv_score` all-gathers are also launched early and hidden behind projection, indexer, and compressor computation. The goal is to reduce TTFT and improve long-context prefill throughput while preserving CP-only accuracy and leaving existing CUDA and non-CP behavior unchanged. ## Modifications - Add a HIP-only CP-aware TBO forward path for DeepSeek V4: - Split each prefill batch into two independently managed sub-batches. - Rebuild CP metadata and round-robin split `hidden_states`, `positions`, and `input_ids` for each sub-batch. - Restore each sub-batch from CP layout and merge the outputs after overlapped execution. - Add a CP-specific TBO operation schedule: - Overlap one sub-batch's MoE all-gather with the other sub-batch's attention computation. - Overlap one sub-batch's reduce-scatter with the other sub-batch's MoE computation. - Use persistent buffers and stream events to safely manage asynchronous communication. - Add a duplicate `attn_cp_overlap` communicator over the same CP ranks. This allows collectives on the communication stream to execute concurrently with attention collectives on the compute stream without driving the same RCCL communicator from multiple streams, which can deadlock. - Add split-phase CP all-gather helpers: - Launch KV and `kv_score` all-gathers as soon as their inputs become available. - Delay synchronization until immediately before the gathered tensors are consumed. - Keep communication inputs alive until completion to prevent allocator reuse. - Update validation and fallback logic: - Enable CP+TBO only for HIP, DSA prefill CP with round-robin split, CP-v1, non-EP TP-MoE, single-stage PP, and valid sub-batches. - Fall back to the original eager path for unsupported or undersized batches. - Align TBO padding with both TP and CP requirements. - Preserve the existing behavior on NVIDIA/CUDA and non-CP paths. - Add an AMD 8-GPU DeepSeek V4 Pro FP4 nightly test covering CP+TBO startup, high-concurrency GSM8K accuracy, per-sub-batch CP metadata, and concurrent-communicator stability. CP+TBO overlap results ## Server command ``` #!/bin/bash set -uo pipefail ARM=${1:-cptbo} export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 export SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=max export SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=0 export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=${SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND:-unified_kv_triton} export SGLANG_OPT_USE_MULTI_STREAM_OVERLAP=false export SGLANG_ROCM_USE_MULTI_STREAM=false export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1 export SGLANG_DP_USE_REDUCE_SCATTER=1 export GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=5 MODEL=${MODEL:-/mnt/raid0/pretrained_model/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro} CHUNK=${CHUNK:-51200} PREFILL_TOKENS=${PREFILL_TOKENS:-${CHUNK}} COMMON=( --model-path "${MODEL}" --trust-remote-code --tp 8 --dp 1 --disable-radix-cache --attention-backend dsv4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --page-size 256 --mem-fraction-static "${MEM_FRAC:-0.9}" --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --disable-shared-experts-fusion --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 --chunked-prefill-size "${CHUNK}" --max-prefill-tokens "${PREFILL_TOKENS}" --max-running-requests 256 --cuda-graph-max-bs 256 ) case "${ARM}" in base | baseline) ARGS=() ;; cp) ARGS=(--enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave) ;; cptbo | cp_tbo) ARGS=(--enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave --enable-two-batch-overlap) ;; *) echo "unknown arm: ${ARM} (可选: base | cp | cptbo)" >&2 exit 2 ;; esac echo "[server] arm=${ARM} chunk=${CHUNK} max_prefill_tokens=${PREFILL_TOKENS} args=${ARGS[*]:-}" exec sglang serve "${COMMON[@]}" "${ARGS[@]}" ``` ## Accuracy Tests config | GSM8K 1319 accuracy | -- | -- cp | 0.944 cp+tbo | 0.936 ## Speed Tests and Profiling I/O = 8k/1k~256k/1k, conc=8, np=4*conc TBO's benefit scales with input length, moving from −3.6% throughput at 8k/1k to +7.2% at 256k/1k, with TTFT stabilizing at around −11% once the input reaches 64k. I/O | cp TPUT | cptbo TPUT | ΔTPUT | cp TTFT | cptbo TTFT | ΔTTFT | cp TPOT | cptbo TPOT | ΔTPOT -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 8k/1k | 3452 | 3327 | −3.6% | 1354 | 1477 | +9.1% | 19.51 | 20.18 | +3.4% 16k/1k | 6059 | 5961 | −1.6% | 2063 | 2055 | −0.4% | 20.39 | 20.77 | +1.9% 32k/1k | 10450 | 10513 | +0.6% | 3557 | 3296 | −7.3% | 21.71 | 21.83 | +0.6% 64k/1k | 16701 | 17198 | +3.0% | 6687 | 5962 | −10.9% | 24.46 | 24.28 | −0.7% 128k/1k | 23684 | 24899 | +5.1% | 13168 | 11624 | −11.7% | 30.42 | 29.83 | −1.9% 256k/1k | 29004 | 31102 | +7.2% | 27542 | 24383 | −11.5% | 43.37 | 41.74 | −3.8% I/O = 128k/1k, conc=2/4/8/16, np=4*conc At a fixed 128k input, TBO gains grow with concurrency (−1.2% → +4.6% throughput from conc 2 to 16), while TTFT improves consistently by 8–11% across all levels. conc | cp TPUT | tbo TPUT | ΔTPUT | cp TTFT | tbo TTFT | ΔTTFT | cp TPOT | tbo TPOT | ΔTPOT -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 2 | 9536 | 9424 | −1.2% | 4813 | 4417 | −8.2% | 22.25 | 22.97 | +3.2% 4 | 15534 | 15713 | +1.2% | 7663 | 7047 | −8.0% | 25.57 | 25.86 | +1.1% 8 | 22449 | 23349 | +4.0% | 13479 | 12258 | −9.1% | 32.51 | 31.96 | −1.7% 16 | 28333 | 29651 | +4.6% | 25237 | 22501 | −10.8% | 47.65 | 47.11 | −1.1% I/O = 50k/1, prefill only With decode removed, TBO reaches its full prefill-side benefit: 10–14% higher throughput and 8–12% lower TTFT at every concurrency level. conc | cp TPUT | tbo TPUT | ΔTPUT | cp TTFT | tbo TTFT | ΔTTFT -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 2 | 44133 | 49299 | +11.7% | 2141 | 1941 | −9.3% 4 | 45040 | 49594 | +10.1% | 4042 | 3711 | −8.2% 8 | 45410 | 50311 | +10.8% | 8003 | 7266 | −9.2% 16 | 45536 | 51859 | +13.9% | 15683 | 13823 | −11.9% ## Checklist - title: perf(hisparse): fuse the DSv4 value and scale swap-in copy on ROCm
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
## Motivation

A DeepSeek-V4 C4 token is 584 bytes, but it is **not one contiguous range**. A page row holds 64 values of 576B followed by 64 scales of 8B:

```
/// Paged C4 cache layout:
/// VALUE 0, VALUE 1, ..., VALUE 63,
/// SCALE 0, SCALE 1, ..., SCALE 63,
/// [Padding to align to 576 bytes]
```

So the ROCm swap-in copies a token with two `transfer_item_warp` calls, 576B then 8B. On wave64 that is three wavefront passes — 64 value words, 8 value words, then 1 scale word — and only the first keeps the whole wavefront busy.

The passes also do not overlap. `item_size_bytes` reaches `transfer_item_warp` as a runtime argument, so the compiler keeps the value copy as a rolled loop with the wait inside the body. Disassembling the gfx950 code object:

```
global_load_dwordx2 v[30:31], v[22:23]
s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)
global_store_dwordx2 v[24:25], v[30:31]
s_cbranch_execnz ...                       <- second value pass
...
global_load_dwordx2 v[22:23], v[22:23]     <- scale
s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)
global_store_dwordx2 v[24:25], v[22:23]
```

Three serialized host round trips per miss, on the decode critical path: `swap_in_selected_pages` runs once per C4 layer per decode step, on the main stream, between that layer's indexer and its attention.

The CUDA branch does not have this problem — `device::hisparse::transfer_item` already moves the value tail and the scale together. It is unusable on ROCm only because its warp logic is hardcoded to 32 lanes.

## Modifications

Adds `transfer_dsv4_item_warp`, used by the ROCm `IsDsv4Layout` miss copy in place of the two `transfer_item_warp` calls. It walks the token as one 73-word space so the value tail and the scale land in the same pass, and stages every load before any store. The pass count is a compile-time constant, so the copy unrolls and both loads issue before either store:

```
global_load_dwordx2 v[22:23], v[24:25]
global_load_dwordx2 v[20:21], v[18:19]
s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)
global_store_dwordx2 v[16:17], v[22:23]
s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)
global_store_dwordx2 v[14:15], v[20:21]
```

One exposed round trip instead of three. No API, config, or template change. CUDA behavior untouched; the generic (non-DSv4) path is untouched.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

MI355X (gfx950), DSv4 paged-layout swap-in, `miss_rate=0.2`, `hot_buffer_size=4096`, `top_k=2048`.

**Methodology.** Both variants are compiled into a single kernel and selected at runtime, with reps alternating between arms inside one process. This matters here: comparing two separate builds moves identical code paths by up to 14% on this kernel, which is more than the effect being measured. Medians of 15 reps × 5 timed rounds, two independent runs.

| batch | before | after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 102.4 / 105.7 us | **87.8 / 87.9 us** | -14.2% / -16.9% |
| 10 | 122.8 / 119.8 us | **97.2 / 96.2 us** | -20.9% / -19.8% |
| 24 | 136.9 / 136.1 us | 125.2 / 125.2 us | -8.5% / -8.0% |
| 100 | 468.6 / 467.5 us | 451.7 / 451.5 us | -3.6% / -3.4% |

The copy is worth optimizing: dropping `miss_rate` from 0.2 to 0.001 on the unmodified kernel takes batch 1 from 110.7 to 20.5 us, so **82% of the swap-in is the miss copy**. The gain fades at high batch because the kernel becomes bandwidth-bound rather than latency-bound, and round-trip count stops mattering there.

### A one-pass variant was tried and is worse

576B is exactly 36 × 16B, and both the page stride (37440) and the value stride (576) are multiples of 16, so the value is always 16B-aligned and the whole token fits in a single pass: lanes 0–35 move one 16B vector each, lane 36 moves the scale. Despite needing fewer passes it lost at every batch size, and was slower than the baseline at batch 1:

| batch | two-pass 64-bit | one-pass 128-bit |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | -14.2% / -16.9% | +3.6% / +1.0% |
| 10 | -20.9% / -19.8% | -4.9% / -4.3% |
| 24 | -8.5% / -8.0% | -4.7% / -4.3% |
| 100 | -3.6% / -3.4% | -1.1% / -1.0% |

The two-pass form engages all 64 lanes on its first pass; the one-pass form only 37. For these host reads, full wavefront occupancy at 64-bit beats partial occupancy at 128-bit even when the wider form needs fewer round trips. This is the same effect that gates the widening in #33085.

## Accuracy Tests

Adds `test_load_cache_to_device_buffer_dsv4_fused_copy_multi_miss`: several misses in one launch at varying source and destination page offsets, including the second page, so the value/scale seam does not always fall at the same address. It takes the destinations from the kernel output rather than assuming an eviction order, and checks that slots the kernel never wrote keep their fill.

Suppressing the scale half of the copy fails both the new test and the existing `dsv4_mla_miss_copy_layout` case, so the coverage has teeth.

Full file on MI355X: 10 passed, 2 skipped (the 2 skips are the CUDA-only DSv4 paged cases).

## Checklist

- [x] Format: `black` clean; C++ change confined to the ROCm `#ifdef` branch, <= 120 cols.
- [x] No public API / config / docs surface touched.
- [x] Unit test added for the new code path; full file run before/after on MI355X.

Related: #33085 (widens the generic path; disjoint branch, no overlap with this change).
