title: feat(kernels): generalize persistent CuTe JIT cache
author: chromecast56
body:
## Motivation

SGLang already has a persistent CuTe JIT cache for FlashAttention, but it lives under the FlashAttention package and only supports TVM-FFI exports. Kimi-K3 KDA also uses explicit `cute.compile` calls, but its cache is process-local.

## Modifications

- Move the existing cache to `sglang.kernels.jit.cute_aot_cache`.
- Generalize it over consumer source roots and CuTe ABI while keeping per-key file locking.
- Include the explicit `CUTE_DSL_ARCH` target, or the detected local CUDA architecture, in the source fingerprint. GPU probing remains lazy when persistence is disabled.
- Publish compiled objects through a temporary path and `os.replace`, so readers never observe a partially written final object and failed exports leave no temporary artifact.
- If an object fails to load, discard it while the per-key shared lock still excludes writers, then fall back to compilation.
- Keep routine cache activity at debug level so enabling persistence does not add normal INFO-level server noise.
- Keep FlashAttention as the TVM-FFI consumer. A small cache adapter preserves `FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_*` behavior and gives `SGLANG_CUTE_AOT_CACHE_DIR` precedence when both configurations are present.
- Add `SGLANG_CUTE_AOT_CACHE_DIR` as the shared opt-in cache root and document that it must be trusted.
- Make Kimi-K3 KDA MTP the second consumer using the native CuTe ABI.
- Normalize CUDA device ordinals only for disk keys so same-architecture ranks can share objects; KDA includes compute capability and indexing width in its compile key.

The default remains process-local. This does not introduce rank authority, compiler monkeypatching, or kernel math changes.

## Reviewability

Git detects the existing cache module as a 51%-similarity rename. The aggregate patch is 394 additions and 86 deletions across six files; 184 added lines are focused tests. The large add/delete presentation from the previous revision was caused by rename detection falling below GitHub's threshold and has been removed.

## Validation

### Focused unit and static validation

- Eleven focused cache cases cover new/legacy FlashAttention environment precedence, quiet routine logging, disabled behavior, lazy architecture detection, factory/source/architecture namespacing, CUDA device ordinal normalization, both native and TVM-FFI export/load paths, atomic publication, failed-export cleanup, and invalid-object eviction.
- SGLang's registered-test collector resolves the pytest file to `base-a-test-cpu`.
- Black, Ruff, isort (for applicable paths), codespell, Python syntax compilation, `scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py`, and `git diff --check` pass.

### Real GPU cache validation

Validated commit `e48384b39c` on one NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (SM103) with Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, NVIDIA CUTLASS DSL 4.6.2, and TVM-FFI 0.1.11. This was cache/kernel validation only; no model was loaded.

- **KDA native ABI:** `TestKimiK3ComputeKernels.test_mtp_replayssm_ring` cold-compiled and exported two objects. A fresh process with `cute.compile` replaced by an exception loaded both objects, passed the same output and recurrent-state checks, and left object hashes unchanged.
- **FlashAttention TVM-FFI ABI:** a BF16 `[1, 64, 4, 64]` causal forward cold-compiled and exported one object. A fresh process with `cute.compile` replaced by an exception loaded it and produced the identical output SHA-256 (`780881b74eb262e7831f1f2a710c53a5ec209f52f371ec4fe51c6b43b2ff9678`). Against an FP32 reference, relative L2 was `0.001861` and max absolute error was `0.007716`.
- **Corruption recovery:** the FlashAttention object was replaced with invalid bytes. The next process detected and removed it, recompiled with the same output SHA-256, and published a repaired object. A final fresh process with `cute.compile` blocked loaded the repaired object successfully. [Validation run](https://modal.com/apps/modal-flash/main/ap-3PyR14z34YcGgsm8zGdHgO)
- No object hashes changed and no `.tmp.o` artifacts remained after validation.

## Speed tests and profiling

No end-to-end speed benchmark is included. A warm process can load an existing FlashAttention or KDA object instead of compiling it again.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code according to the project configuration.
- [x] Add focused unit tests.
- [x] Document the new environment variable and trust boundary.
- [x] Validate native and TVM-FFI cold-to-warm round trips on a real GPU.
- [x] Validate invalid-object eviction, recompilation, and repaired warm loading.
- [x] Keep the cache move visible as a rename for review.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.
- [ ] Provide an end-to-end speed benchmark (out of scope for cache validation).

title: fix(dflash): account for DCP in draft KV pool sizing
author: milesial
body:
## Summary

- account for the DCP-replicated draft KV pool when using the exact DFLASH/DSPARK draft bytes-per-token budget added by #34234
- use the resolved runtime DCP size at the shared draft-budget accessor
- cover both DCP-disabled and DCP8 pool sizing with a valid TP8 topology

## Motivation

DFLASH-family draft pools span the allocator's widened virtual location space under DCP, so each target-pool token requires `dcp_size` draft-pool rows. The layer-count fallback already applies that factor, but the exact geometry/dtype path added by #34234 bypasses the fallback and previously added only one draft row's cost.

This keeps the exact and fallback paths consistent without duplicating the geometry or dtype resolution now present on `main`.

title: Fix Qwen3.5 GDN multi-item scoring
author: daii-0818
body:
## Motivation

Qwen3.5 hybrid models use recurrent GDN layers alongside full-attention layers. Multi-item scoring already gives the full-attention layers an item-branching mask, but the GDN prefill path previously processed the packed suffix as one continuous recurrent sequence. As a result, later items could inherit convolution and SSM state from earlier items.

Fixes #31969.

## Modifications

- Add a read-only final-state mode to the Triton chunk gated-delta-rule path while preserving in-place updates by default.
- Build GDN-specific MIS metadata once per forward for compact query and item segments.
- Run GDN MIS prefill in two phases: compute each request query once, then branch every item from the query-end convolution and SSM states.
- Keep item recurrence read-only against the request SSM pool and use unique cloned convolution slots per item.
- Reject unsupported combinations, including non-Triton GDN prefill, page-major layout, cached prefixes, non-prefill requests, and hybrid linear backends without MIS support.
- Add kernel, causal-convolution, backend, metadata, validation, and Qwen3.5 end-to-end coverage.

## Reproduction

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --enable-mis \
  --attention-backend flashinfer \
  --linear-attn-prefill-backend triton \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --disable-cuda-graph \
  --chunked-prefill-size -1 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000
```

## Accuracy Tests

Tested on one NVIDIA H20 with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` in BF16, FlashInfer full attention, and Triton linear-attention prefill.

- Qwen3.5 MIS end-to-end: 3 tests passed, covering empty queries, concurrent requests, varied item counts and lengths, and sibling modification/reordering.
- Focused recurrent, causal-convolution, GDN backend, metadata, and validation suite: 27 tests passed with 46 subtests.
- Full recurrent and causal-convolution test files: 275 tests passed.
- Multi-item scores match per-item MIS scoring with `atol=2e-2, rtol=2e-2`.
- Formatting, import checks, spelling, syntax compilation, CI registration validation, and whitespace checks passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Single H20, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`, query length 120, item length 180, 10 items per request, 10 warmup requests, followed by three 60-second runs. CUDA graph, radix cache, and chunked prefill were disabled in both modes.

| Mode | Items/s/GPU | P50 latency | P99 latency |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Independent pointwise scoring | 52.80 | 189.06 ms | 195.25 ms |
| Multi-item scoring | 62.75 | 158.74 ms | 167.21 ms |

This is an 18.84% throughput increase, with P50 latency reduced by 16.04% and P99 latency reduced by 14.36%.

- [x] Add unit and end-to-end tests.

title: [DCP] Support decode context parallelism on the trtllm_mla decode path
author: qtris123
body:
## Motivation

Draft for the unassigned `trtllm_mla` decode path item in the DCP roadmap #29736 (also relevant to #26432).

`trtllm_mla` has no DCP decode path. `forward_decode` builds its page table and `seq_lens` from the global sequence lengths and returns a bare tensor, while under DCP the model routes decode through `attn_mqa_for_dcp_decode` and expects a rank-local `(out, lse)` pair. The DCP code already in `trtllm_mla_backend.py` covers only speculative `target_verify`, and delegates to `_run_decode_kernel`, which the base rejected — only the `cutedsl_mla` / `tokenspeed_mla` subclasses served it.

This is reachable without asking for it: `arg_groups/overrides.py` auto-selects `trtllm_mla` on sm100 for `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM`, and `forward_mla.py` routes decode to `attn_mqa_for_dcp_decode` whenever `get_parallel().dcp_enabled` is set, regardless of backend.

### The approach, and its main assumption

flashinfer implements in-kernel DCP only for the CuTeDSL MLA kernel and rejects it elsewhere (`_validate_mla_dcp_args` in `flashinfer/mla/_core.py`), so spec-decode × DCP on `trtllm_mla` is blocked upstream and stays rejected here.

The assumption this draft rests on is that a `q_len == 1` decode does not need it: `cp_world` / `cp_rank` / `causal_seqlens_kv_global` exist so a kernel can resolve a per-query global causal bound, and that bound only varies across query rows when `q_len > 1`. With a single query token the cyclic owner rule should already select exactly the causally visible prefix, leaving the rank-local page table and `seq_lens` sufficient. `trtllm-gen` already supports `return_lse`.

## Modifications

- **Hoist the DCP metadata plumbing onto `TRTLLMMLABackend`.** The rank-local length and page-table helpers were duplicated between `cutedsl_mla_backend.py` and `tokenspeed_mla_backend.py`; both carried a TODO to collapse them into the base. They are kernel-agnostic, so the base now owns them and both subclasses define only their kernel call and decode forward. Every branch is a no-op when DCP is off.
- **`_run_decode_kernel`**: forwards `return_lse`, and narrows the blanket `cp_world > 1 or return_lse` refusal to `cp_world > 1 and causal_seqs is not None` — callers needing a global causal bound signal it by passing `causal_seqs`.
- **`forward_decode`**: new `_forward_decode_dcp` returns the rank-local `(out, lse)`, with `fixup_zero_kv_rows` neutralizing ranks owning no slice of a request.
- **LSE base**: resolved per backend in `__init__` from a `backend -> bool` mapping rather than a class attribute. `TRTLLMMLABackend` takes `backend` as a constructor argument and `CuteDslMLABackend` constructs the parent with `"cute-dsl"`, so one class drives either kernel and a class attribute cannot express both: `trtllm-gen` emits base-2 and needs no rebase, `cute-dsl` emits natural log and does.
- **Gate the fused bf16 KV-write off under DCP.** `set_mla_kv_concat_q` takes no `dcp_world_size` / `dcp_rank`, unlike its fp8 sibling `set_mla_kv_concat_q_fp8`, so under DCP it writes the KV row at the raw **virtual** `out_cache_loc` from every rank — while the reader `create_mla_kv_page_table_for_dcp` computes `virtual_locs // DCP_SIZE // PHYSICAL_PAGE_SIZE` and expects the **compacted** row `loc // dcp_size`, written only by the owning rank. The two disagree, so the fused write lands where no page table entry points. DCP runs now fall back to the pool's DCP-aware `set_mla_kv_buffer` plus `concat_mla_absorb_q_general`. `dcp_enabled` is `dcp_size > 1`, so this is a no-op at `dcp_size == 1` and the non-DCP fast path is untouched.
- **Tests**: a CPU test pinning the partition invariant the approach depends on. The tokenspeed metadata test is renamed and broadened across the three backends — it patched `get_parallel` in the tokenspeed module, which the hoist would otherwise have bypassed.

## Accuracy Tests

### Metadata regression check (B200)

The DCP metadata tests pass on hardware for all three backends — `TRTLLMMLABackend`, `TokenspeedMLABackend`, `CuteDslMLABackend` — and `test_dcp_layout_unit.py` passes identically on this branch and on its merge base. So the hoist does not change metadata behaviour for the two backends that already had working DCP, which was the main regression risk.

### The decode path, end to end (B200)

GSM8K via lm-eval, full 1319 problems, 5-shot, greedy. `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite` with `--tp-size 8` on 8×B200, `--attention-backend trtllm_mla`, CUDA graph **on**, servers identical apart from `--dcp-size`:

| n | arm | strict-match | flexible-extract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1319 (full) | `dcp_size=1` | 0.3806 ± 0.0134 | 0.3851 ± 0.0134 |
| 1319 (full) | `dcp_size=8` | 0.3851 ± 0.0134 | 0.3882 ± 0.0134 |

Both columns score the same generations with different answer extractors: **strict-match** requires the canonical `#### <number>` ending that the few-shot prompt demonstrates, while **flexible-extract** accepts the last number appearing anywhere in the output. The gap between the two reflects formatting compliance rather than reasoning.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

DeepSeek-V2-Lite on 8×B200, `--attention-backend trtllm_mla`, `--dcp-comm-backend ag_rs`, `--tp-size 8` in every arm with `--dcp-size` 1 / 4 / 8 — so all three arms use the same 8 GPUs and differ only in whether the KV cache is sharded across them. aiperf, synthetic, OSL 1024, concurrency 1–64, ISL 32K / 64K / 128K / 256K, `--disable-radix-cache`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.85`, CUDA graph on.

![Interactivity vs throughput, TP vs DCP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qtris123/sglang/bench-assets-dcp-trtllm-mla/bench/pareto.png)

Each point is one concurrency level, labelled on the marker; concurrency rises up and to the left. Left axis is per-GPU throughput, right axis the same curve as a total across the 8 GPUs.

DCP trades an all-gather plus reduce-scatter per decode layer for an N-way reduction in the KV bytes each rank reads per decode step. That trade is a loss at low concurrency, where the collective is pure overhead, and a win once there is enough KV traffic to amortize it — so the arms cross, and the crossing moves to lower concurrency as context grows: between concurrency 8 and 16 at 32K, 4 and 8 at 64K, 2 and 4 at 128K, and below 1 at 256K, where DCP leads at every level measured. At concurrency 64, `dcp_size=8` is +57% at 32K, +57% at 64K, +68% at 128K and +52% at 256K.

The other effect visible here is TP running out of KV capacity: at 128K and 256K the `dcp_size=1` curve turns horizontal at the left, meaning added concurrency buys latency cost with no throughput in return. Numerically it goes 648 → 681 → 673 output tok/s across concurrency 16/32/64 at 128K, and is flat at ~286 from concurrency 16 onward at 256K. Both DCP arms are still climbing at concurrency 64 in every panel, so these are a lower bound on the gap rather than a measured saturation point.

Raw per-point numbers are in the CSV behind this plot and can be posted on request.

### Control for the fused-KV gate

The gate added in Modifications removes the fused bf16 KV-write from DCP runs, so a plain DCP-vs-TP comparison would otherwise charge DCP for that change. Running `dcp_size=1` with the fused path forced off (isl 4096 / osl 256, `--tp-size 2` on 2×B200) shows it is worth nothing at this shape:

| concurrency | `dcp_size=1` | `dcp_size=1`, fused KV-write forced off |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 298.0 | 302.6 |
| 8 | 1539.9 | 1571.9 |
| 32 | 3624.9 | 3644.9 |
| 64 | 4932.8 | 5015.8 |

The control arm is marginally *faster* than stock, i.e. inside run-to-run noise. So the gate itself is free, and the DCP deltas above are DCP's own communication cost rather than an artifact of that code change.

### Caveats

- One model. `DeepSeek-V2-Lite` is the smallest MLA model available, which maximises KV pressure per unit of compute but also makes the decode step cheap, so the per-layer collective is a larger share of the step than it would be on a production-scale MLA model. If anything this understates DCP.
- `ag_rs` only; `a2a` is not covered.
- Concurrency stops at 64, below saturation for the DCP arms.

title: perf(vlm): materialize Qwen encoder-DP features on owner ranks
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- Keep Qwen3-VL/Qwen3.5 image and video GPU-transport proxies lazy until encoder-DP load balancing assigns each item.
- Reconstruct and pack only the images owned by the local attention-TP rank.
- Use the same path for bounded CUDA IPC and CUDA VMM transport; CPU transport and non-encoder-DP serving keep the eager path.
- Reuse the transport proxy's declared consumer set so CUDA VMM acknowledgements remain correct with DP attention.

At TP8 encoder DP, one owner rank copies each raw visual feature instead of all eight ranks. ViT execution and the existing post-encoder gather are unchanged.

## Server benchmark

Real `Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct`, NVIDIA H200 x8, TP8 encoder DP, `--mm-feature-transport cuda_ipc`, 1 GiB bounded pool, OpenAI Chat `bench_serving`. Base `e0c94d36c52a` (#33949) and head `083a58caffc1`; the later main-only merges do not change any files in this PR.

The general workload uses 48 requests per rate, 1-4 seeded random JPEG images/request, random 256-1024 px dimensions, 64 text input tokens, and 8 output tokens. All 288 A/B requests completed successfully.

| Request rate | Base req/s | Head req/s | Change | Base p50 TTFT | Head p50 TTFT |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2 | 1.948 | 1.947 | -0.0% | 71.2 ms | 71.2 ms |
| 8 | 9.249 | 9.251 | +0.0% | 85.9 ms | 85.9 ms |
| unlimited | 34.434 | 35.370 | +2.7% | 840.3 ms | 859.5 ms |

The transport-heavy workload fixes 4 images/request at random 512-1536 px dimensions (128 images and about 130k vision tokens per 32-request run). After excluding the first new-shape compilation sample, the table reports the median of two saturated runs.

| Request rate | Metric | Base | Head | Change |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| unlimited | Request throughput | 12.73 req/s | 14.63 req/s | +14.9% |
| unlimited | Mean TTFT | 1476.8 ms | 1358.1 ms | -8.0% |
| unlimited | P99 TTFT | 2395.1 ms | 2042.6 ms | -14.7% |
| 8 | Median TTFT | 171.9 ms | 149.6 ms | -13.0% |
| 8 | P99 TTFT | 321.0 ms | 287.3 ms | -10.5% |

This matches the intended scope: owner-only materialization is neutral on small/moderate features and becomes visible when large image payload copies are material.

## Validation

- Pre-commit passes on all changed files.
- Unit coverage checks both `cuda_ipc` and `cuda_vmm`, explicit CPU opt-out, image/video marking, audio exclusion, and owner-only materialization.
- Existing non-DP image/video feature packing coverage remains intact.
- Real-weight H200 server A/B completed with zero request failures; latest-head NVIDIA CI is running after the main merge.

## Dependency

Stacked on #33949, which is stacked on #33936. Retarget after the lower PRs merge.

title: [Diffusion] perf: build qwen's masked varlen metadata host-side
author: mickqian
body:
Split out of #31852 per its acceptance review — the whole-forward graph did not clear the bar, but this piece pays regardless of graphs.

qwen's masked branch rebuilds varlen metadata from the joint mask with a GPU `nonzero()`, which forces a device sync on **every denoising step**. `txt_seq_lens` already carries each row's valid text prefix (the mask is derived from it), so the metadata can be assembled host-side with the existing `build_varlen_mask_meta_from_ranges` helper — same `cu_seqlens`/`indices`/`inv_indices`, no GPU round-trip. The mask-based builder stays as the fallback for callers without usable lengths, and BCG's replay-local `DynamicVarlenMaskMeta` path is untouched.

Includes a unit test asserting the host-built metadata is element-for-element identical to the nonzero builder's output for prefix-text + full-image masks (including an all-padding row).

title: [unified memory] Support DSPARK speculative decoding + fix two NaN root causes (page hand-out zeroing, CuTe int32 slot-stride wrap)
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

`--enable-unified-memory` currently hard-blocks speculative decoding (`server_args.py`: `assert self.speculative_algorithm is None`). This PR wires chain DSPARK through the unified pool and fixes the two real NaN/corruption root causes found while validating it end to end on Kimi-K3 (TP8, 2x4 GB300) and Kimi-Linear-48B (TP1 x8 B300-class). Other speculative algorithms (EAGLE / tree / DFLASH / NGRAM) remain blocked pending their own virtual-vs-dense loc audits.

## Modifications

Five commits, reviewable independently:

1. **`unified-memory: wire DSPARK chain speculative decoding`**
   - `server_args.py`: relax the unified gate to `speculative_algorithm in (None, "DSPARK")`, chain only (`speculative_eagle_topk in (None, 1)`).
   - `trtllm_mla_backend.py`: extend the capture-stable DENSE write-loc fill from `is_decode_or_idle()` to `is_target_verify()`, and route the `forward_extend` KV write through it (`loc_is_dense=True`) when set — the verify graph must not capture a translate allocation (same class as the decode path that already exists).
   - `mamba_state_scatter_triton.py`: replace the blanket `dst.is_contiguous()` asserts with the kernels' true contract (arbitrary layer/slot strides — already consumed via real int64-promoted strides — with contiguous trailing entry dims), so the unified pool's envelope-strided conv/temporal views pass. CPU layout-contract tests + a CUDA envelope-dst end-to-end test added.
   - `hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py`: `update_mamba_state_after_mtp_verify` translates the ScheduleBatch-side (VIRTUAL) `mamba_track_indices` to physical at a single point (identity on static pools) — using them raw silently mis-addresses within bounds on the unified pool.
   - `kv_cache_configurator.py`: size the DSPARK draft pool by the shared unified allocator's virtual-id space (`size_full`, page-aligned up) instead of `max_total_num_tokens` — the draft pool is direct-indexed by virtual ids which range over the whole virtual space; keep the draft pool on the plain contiguous layout (page-major is a target-pool layout choice).

2. **`debug(unified): SGLANG_DEBUG_POISON_POOL`** — env-gated: fill the pool with bf16-NaN bit patterns at boot instead of zeros. Turns the "does freed GPU heap happen to contain NaN patterns" boot lottery into a deterministic switch; kept as the permanent regression harness for the class of bug below (zero default overhead).

3. **`fix(unified): zero page envelopes on allocator hand-out`** — root cause 1. The trtllm-gen MLA kernel reads whole pages and masks rows beyond `seq_len` arithmetically (NaN-unsafe); the unified pool zeroes its raw buffer only at boot, so page recycling re-exposes historical bytes and NaN in a request's last partial page tail leaks into the attention output. Speculative decoding amplifies exposure (every verify window lands on a fresh page at the sequence tail). Static pools are safe by construction (`torch.zeros` + only finite KV ever written); this gives the shared pool the same guarantee at the alloc boundary. Cost: one contiguous page-envelope memset per handed-out page on the schedule stream — benched at zero (below).

4. **`fix(kda_decode_mtp): promote slot ids to int64 before state-stride multiplies`** — root cause 2, and the reason this presented as a "weird" load-dependent heisenbug. The DSPARK KDA verify kernel (`nv_cutedsl` fast path) compiles with STATIC CuTe layouts: state-pool strides are compile-time constants. On the unified pool the envelope-strided KDA state views carry slot strides of ~14M (fp32 ssm) / ~28M (bf16 conv) elements; each constant individually fits int32, so it folds into 32-bit arithmetic and `slot * stride` silently wraps mod 2^32 once slot ids exceed ~153 (conv) / ~306 (ssm) — reads land inside other slots' bytes (silent state corruption on a CLEAN boot: GSM8K 0.120, fake accept-rate bursts) or fly off the allocation (illegal access). Static contiguous pools never reach the wrap point (slot stride ~197K elements); Kimi-Linear never engages this kernel (head dims fail the 128 contract → triton fallback); cold boots hand out low slot ids — which is exactly why it was unified-only, K3-only, and load-only. Proven with an offline replay sentinel (dump one real in-system call; rebuild states contiguous vs faithful strided replicas with zero/NaN gap fill; sweep slot magnitudes): before — slots ≤75 bit-exact, 100–150 illegal access, ≥155 silent divergence; after — bit-exact everywhere.

5. **`unified+spec: keep lazy compaction ON`** — reverts an over-conservative eager forcing from an earlier draft of commit 1 after verifying the actual ordering: the scheduler registers the in-flight write-set (`set_inflight_forward(forward_done, batch.out_cache_loc)`) AFTER `forward_batch_generation()` returns, and the DSPARK verify executor has by then rebound `ScheduleBatch.out_cache_loc` to the verify-window locs (never restored) — so lazy compaction's write-race classification covers verify writes exactly like decode writes, and the event-gated freed-page reuse orders the hand-out zeroing (commit 3) after the in-flight forward.

## Accuracy

GSM8K 200q (`sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`), Kimi-K3 TP8 2-node GB300, marlin MoE, trtllm_mla, verify graph captured:

| config | fixes | GSM8K | accept rate/len |
|---|---|---|---|
| unified, no spec (baseline) | pristine base | 0.985 | — |
| unified + DSPARK rand draft, POISONED pool | none | 0.005 / Invalid 0.985 | **1.00 / 8.00 (fake — argmax(NaN)=0 token chains)** |
| unified + DSPARK rand draft, POISONED pool | zeroing only | 0.125 / Invalid 0.745 | 0.00 (still corrupt via int32 wrap) |
| unified + DSPARK rand draft, **clean** pool | zeroing only | 0.120 / Invalid 0.715 | 0.52 (fake) — the int32 wrap needs no poison |
| unified + DSPARK rand draft, POISONED pool | **both** | **0.985 / Invalid 0.005** | 0.00 / 1.00 ✓ (correct full-reject semantics) |
| unified + DSPARK **real draft** ([RadixArk/Kimi-K3-DSpark](https://huggingface.co/RadixArk/Kimi-K3-DSpark)), clean | **both** | **0.990 / Invalid 0.005** | 0.53 / 4.74 (real multi-accept commit path) |
| unified + DSPARK real draft, `--disable-radix-cache`, 500q, lazy-compaction stats on | both | 0.976 / Invalid 0.002 | 0.49 / 4.45 |

Poison acceptance criterion: a poisoned boot must score identically to a clean boot — it does (0.985/0.990 both). Kimi-Linear-48B TP1: unified+DSPARK poisoned 0.910 = clean 0.905 = static twin 0.910.

## Performance (fix cost = zero)

`sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server`, isl 8192 / osl 1024, bs sweep, 2 reps per arm, K3 TP8:

- **Zeroing fix A/B** (unified no-spec, fix vs no-fix, only var = checkout): output tok/s deltas bs 1/8/16/24/32 = **−0.07% / −0.02% / +0.05% / +0.03% / +0.02%**; TTFT within ±0.34%. Rep-to-rep variance exceeds the fix delta at every point.
- **Unified vs static under DSPARK** (rand draft, both arms at tip): deltas −0.83%…+0.07% (bs=1 single-request noise); TTFT +0.31~0.37% = the pool's known pre-existing translate overhead, present without these fixes too.
- **int64 slot promotion micro-bench** (offline replay, 200 calls ×3): 416 vs 411 µs/call, run-to-run spread ±4% ≫ delta — one scalar 64-bit multiply against a memory-bound kernel.

## Limitations / follow-ups

- The branch base is an ancestor of current main (no divergence; merge-tree is conflict-free). Happy to rebase before merge — flagging that the accuracy/perf numbers above are bound to the base as validated.
- Compaction MOVE racing an in-flight verify write was not dynamically exercised (short GSM8K sequences free at the watermark frontier → `moves=0` in the stats run); its correctness rests on the verified write-set ordering (commit 5) plus poison acceptance. A fragmenting long-generation stress is a good follow-up before enabling this in latency-critical production lanes.
- fa3 / flashinfer as the target-verify backend under unified+spec are not exercised (K3 lane = trtllm_mla; flashinfer decode is already role-scope-blocked by the allowlist).
- The kernel-owner-side fix for the arithmetic (NaN-unsafe) masked-tail reads remains an upstream flashinfer/trtllm-gen item; commit 3 makes the pool safe regardless.

title: [AMD] Add K3 verified mla kernel for DSpark on triton backend
author: 1am9trash
body:
## Motivation Kimi-K3 DSpark throughput is slow, at high conc it is even slower than non-DSpark setting. Root cause: the target-verify attention runs through verify_splitkv, which is invoked on every MLA full-attention layer (~24 calls/step for K3). That kernel is designed for standard MHA, not MLA: it parallelizes one program per query head, so it re-reads the single shared MLA latent (h_kv=1) once per head (~12x redundant load at TP8). On this memory-bound verify shape that is very slow, and the cost grows with batch/conc. Kernel Code path: `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/verify_splitkv.py` ## Modifications Add a new MLA kernel `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/verify_mla.py`. Its two-stage architecture and API mirror verify_splitkv (drop-in `verify_mla_fwd`, same positional args, returns True/False so the caller can fall back). Key points: - Grid changed to `(bs, n_head_blocks, split)`: each program handles BLOCK_H query heads x all draft queries, so the shared latent tile is loaded once and reused across BLOCK_H heads. - GEMM split the single 576-wide QK dot into nope (kv_lora_rank=512) + pe (qk_rope=64), both powers of two (no wasted padding 576 -> 1024). - Split uses floor partitioning (`seqlen // active`) with the last split absorbing the remainder. Every active split is non-empty (no sentinel). - Partial outputs are stored in bf16 (lse fp32) to halve the scratch round-trip. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8k, 1319: ``` 100%|████████| 1319/1319 [02:07<00:00, 10.31it/s] Accuracy: 0.951 Invalid: 0.001 Latency: 127.998 s Output throughput: 1039.629 token/s ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: [diffusion] Enable breakable CUDA graph for SANA (H200 1024px e2e -26%, bit-exact)
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

SANA1.5-1.6B at 1024x1024 is the most launch/CPU-bound model in the diffusion tree: a
steady eager denoise step issues ~2,000 CUDA kernels and keeps the GPU only ~30% busy
(torch.profiler, H200; ~23.4 ms GPU busy inside a ~80 ms profiled step window). This is
exactly the workload breakable CUDA graph (BCG, #27436) was built for, and the same
situation LTX-2 was in before #33885. `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph` currently
silently no-ops for SANA.

Two gaps blocked BCG on SANA:

1. **Allowlist** (`server_args.py`): `SanaPipelineConfig` / the SANA1.5 model id were
   not on `BREAKABLE_CUDA_GRAPH_SUPPORTED_{PIPELINE_CONFIGS,MODEL_IDS}`, so the flag was
   silently dropped.
2. **Dead `mask_strategy` payload poisons the BCG signature path**
   (`denoising.py` / `denoising_dmd.py`): `predict_noise` builds
   `dict_to_3d_list(None, t_max=50, l_max=60, h_max=24)` — a 72,000-element nested list
   of `None` — on **every DiT forward** and passes it as a `mask_strategy` kwarg.
   No in-tree DiT consumes this kwarg (grep over `runtime/models/dits/` finds zero
   consumers; the sliding-tile attention backend loads its mask strategy from
   `mask_strategy_file_path` on its own). The 15 DiT classes whose `forward` takes
   `**kwargs` (SANA, Wan, HunyuanVideo, LTX-2, Z-Image, ERNIE, Krea2, Helios, ...)
   silently swallow it. Building the list costs ~1.1 ms CPU per call in eager mode, and
   under BCG the runner's signature/flatten pass walks all 72k leaves on every call,
   which made BCG replay *slower* than eager (denoise 2.63 s vs 0.67 s). This PR removes
   the payload.

With both fixed, warmup captures one graph per text bucket (5 buckets, **1 segment
each** — SANA's linear-attention forward is fully capturable, no attention break
points) and serving replays with zero signature misses.

## Benchmark

H200, `Efficient-Large-Model/SANA1.5_1.6B_1024px_diffusers`, 1024x1024, default 20
steps, seed 42, eager (`--enable-torch-compile=false`, production default), single GPU.
9 back-to-back requests in one warmed process, drop-first median (protocol of #33885):

| arm | wall / req | e2e (total_duration) | denoise |
|---|---|---|---|
| eager (main 5ca734fc3d) | 1.028 s | 0.821 s | 699.2 ms |
| eager + dead-payload removal | ~1.03 s (noise band) | — | 685.1 ms (-2.0%) |
| **eager + BCG (this PR)** | **0.781 s (-24.0%)** | **0.608 s (-25.9%)** | **408.1 ms (-41.6%)** |

Reproduce:

```bash
sglang generate --backend=sglang \
  --model-path=Efficient-Large-Model/SANA1.5_1.6B_1024px_diffusers \
  --prompt="A cup of coffee on a wooden table in a sunlit cafe" \
  --width=1024 --height=1024 --seed=42 --num-gpus=1 \
  --enable-torch-compile=false --warmup-mode request \
  --enable-breakable-cuda-graph --warmup-resolutions 1024x1024 --save-output
```

## Serving mode: prompt-length matrix (does a different prompt length re-capture?)

**No — capture happens only at warmup; serving never captures.** SANA encodes prompts
with Gemma2 at variable length (tokenizer cap 300); warmup captures **one graph per text
bucket** (default buckets 64/128/256/512/1024, `1 segment, 5 tensor inputs` each) and
serving pads each prompt up to the nearest bucket and replays. Since the tokenizer cap
(300) is below the largest default bucket (1024), the over-bucket fallback is unreachable
in the default config.

Real HTTP server (`serve` entrypoint, `POST /v1/images/generations`), H200 x1, 1024x1024,
20 steps, seed 42, 4 requests/tier, medians:

| prompt tier | eager denoise (s) | BCG denoise (s) | delta | capture evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| short (5 words, ~7 tok) | 0.663 | 0.395 | **-40.4%** | pads to bucket 64 -> replay |
| medium (33 words, ~45 tok) | 0.684 | 0.394 | **-42.3%** | pads to bucket 64 -> replay |
| long (126 words, 152 tok) | 0.657 | 0.404 | **-38.5%** | pads to bucket 256 -> replay |
| xlong (281 words, 300-tok cap) | 0.651 | 0.420 | **-35.5%** | pads to bucket 512 -> replay |

Server-log evidence: exactly 5 graphs captured, all before "The server is fired up";
serving-phase captures = **0** after 16 requests; misses/warnings = **0**; all 16 BCG
images **md5-identical** to the eager server's (same seed).

Fallback path exercised explicitly with `--bcg-text-buckets 64 128` (max bucket below the
152/300-token prompts): those prompts log
`[Diffusion BCG] text length 152 exceeds max bucket 128; not padding ... Raise --bcg-text-buckets.`
once per forward and run eager — still **0 serving captures** and still md5-identical
(the negative CFG branch, ~40 tok, keeps replaying bucket 64, so the tier lands between
full-replay and full-eager: 0.48 s vs 0.39/0.66 s).

Profiler comparison (5 profiled timesteps; eager span is inflated by profiler overhead —
steady-state numbers are in the table):

![sana serving profiler](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/assets-bcg-serving/sana_bcg_vs_eager_timeline.png)

eager: GPU busy 28.5%, 8,412 runtime launches; BCG: GPU busy 93.3%, 132 launches.

<details>
<summary>Serving commands</summary>

```bash
# server (eager arm; BCG arm adds --enable-breakable-cuda-graph;
# fallback demo adds --bcg-text-buckets 64 128)
python3 -m sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.entrypoints.cli.main serve \
  --model-path Efficient-Large-Model/SANA1.5_1.6B_1024px_diffusers \
  --num-gpus 1 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31100 --warmup-resolutions 1024x1024

# client: POST /v1/images/generations {"prompt", "size": "1024x1024", "seed": 42};
# 4 prompt tiers x 4 requests (5 / 33 / 126 / 281 words)
```
</details>

## Correctness

- **Bit-exact**: all 27 outputs (9 requests x 3 arms: main-eager / fixed-eager / BCG)
  share a single md5 (`0e0b6e045e0abdcf...`). BCG replays the captured eager kernel
  stream, and the payload removal deletes a value nothing reads.
- **No silent fallback**: 5 captured signatures, `[Diffusion BCG] ... MISSED` count = 0
  over all serving requests.
- **Unit tests**: `test_diffusion_bcg_padding.py` + `test_cfg_parallel_warmup.py`
  (55 passed).

## Profiler evidence

| | eager | BCG |
|---|---|---|
| GPU busy in steady step | ~26-33% | **~94%** |
| step wall (profiled) | ~80 ms | ~4.5 ms (replay-issue steps) |
| CUDA kernels / step | ~2,017 | same kernels, replayed as graphs |

(3-step torch.profiler windows per arm, same analysis pipeline as #33885.)

## Notes

- The dead-payload removal also shaves ~1.1 ms CPU per `predict_noise` call from every
  eager model that goes through the generic denoising stage (visible as denoise
  699.2 -> 685.1 ms on SANA; within noise on GPU-bound models), and shrinks the BCG
  signature key for every current and future BCG model.
- Only the validated SANA1.5-1.6B id is added to the model allowlist, mirroring how
  #33885 added only `Lightricks/LTX-2`.
- `mask_strategy` plumbing for the sliding-tile-attention backend is untouched: the
  backend reads `attention_backend_config.mask_strategy_file_path` itself
  (`sliding_tile_attn.py:123-132`).

## Benchmark configuration

All numbers are eager mode (`--enable-torch-compile=false`), the production default
path; BCG composes with eager (it captures the eager stream). Driver: 9 back-to-back
`DiffGenerator.generate` calls in one warmed process with per-request perf dumps,
same protocol as #33885 (reproduce command above).

title: [HiCache] Optimize LogicalHostPool free-list release
author: wangwenmingaa
body:
Motivation

This PR is a follow-up to #30658.

PR #30658 defers host-pool free-list concatenation for HostKVCache-based pools. However, LogicalHostPool is a standalone allocator and does not inherit from HostKVCache, so it is not covered by that optimization.

LogicalHostPool.free() still eagerly rebuilds the complete free-slot tensor on every release:

self.free_slots = torch.cat([self.free_slots, released_indices])

When HiCache uses a large logical host pool, free_slots can contain hundreds of thousands or millions of entries. Releasing a small number of slots therefore copies the entire existing free list. Repeated releases during cache eviction can introduce significant CPU stalls during HiCache cold fill and warm-up.

In an internal DSV4 HiCache workload, the allocator eviction-and-retry path showed representative average latencies of approximately 392.6–586.7 ms, with a maximum close to 592 ms. Profiling identified repeated large free-list concatenations as the dominant CPU-side overhead.

The issue was especially visible with a large logical cache capacity, but the underlying allocator problem is independent of any particular cache-sharding configuration.

Modifications

Apply the lazy free-slot release strategy from #30658 to LogicalHostPool:

  • Keep released slot tensors in release_slots instead of concatenating them immediately.

  • Track pending released slots with num_release_slots.

  • Include pending released slots in available_size().

  • Continue allocating from the primary free_slots tensor while it has sufficient capacity.

  • Merge pending released chunks only when an allocation cannot be satisfied by the primary free list.

  • Avoid recording empty releases.

  • Reset all pending-release state in clear().

  • Preserve the existing page-alignment validation and slot reuse order.

The patch does not add runtime logging, configuration flags, or model-specific behavior.

Unit tests cover:

  • deferred release without rebuilding the primary free list;

  • allocation from the primary free list before merging pending slots;

  • reuse of released slots after a deferred merge;

  • merging multiple released chunks;

  • empty releases;

  • state reset through clear();

  • preservation of LogicalHostPool page-alignment checks.

Accuracy Tests

This change only modifies CPU-side free-slot allocator metadata.

It does not modify:

  • model weights or model forward execution;

  • KV cache tensor contents;

  • cache keys or page-table mappings;

  • host-to-device or device-to-host data transfer;

  • attention, sampling, or CUDA kernels.

The unit test verifies that slot allocation and reuse order remain unchanged. Therefore, model output accuracy is not expected to change.

Local checks completed:

PASS: Python syntax compilation for the modified source and test files
PASS: scripts/ci/check_registered_tests.py
PASS: git diff --check

The PyTorch unit test is added to the existing registered CPU test suite and will be executed by GitHub CI:

python3 -m unittest \
  test.registered.unit.mem_cache.test_mem_pool_host.TestLazyHostPoolRelease.test_logical_pool_lazy_release

Speed Tests and Profiling

Before this change, every LogicalHostPool.free(K) may concatenate the released slots with an existing free list containing F entries:

Free-list maintenance cost: O(F + K)

After this change, free() only records the released tensor and updates a counter:

Free-list maintenance cost: O(1)

The larger concatenation is deferred until the primary free list cannot satisfy an allocation. Multiple releases can therefore be combined into one allocation-side merge instead of repeatedly copying the full free list.

Behavior | Before | After -- | -- | -- torch.cat during every free() | Yes | No Primary allocation fast path | Tensor slice | Tensor slice Released-slot accounting | Eager full-list rebuild | Append chunk and update counter Large merge | Once per release | Only when released slots are needed Page-alignment semantics | Preserved | Preserved Allocation/reuse order | Primary free list, then released slots | Unchanged

In the internal HiCache workload that exposed this issue:

  • the pre-change eviction-and-retry path reached approximately 392.6–586.7 ms average CPU latency;

  • the maximum observed latency was approximately 592 ms;

  • after applying lazy release, repeated eager concatenations were removed from the free() hot path;

  • the amount of traffic required for HiCache warm-up was substantially reduced, although other cache-population costs can still require a smaller warm-up period.

This matches the optimization strategy and performance rationale already validated for other host pools in #30658.

Checklist

  • Format the code with pre-commit. Pending local dependency setup or GitHub CI.

  • Add unit tests according to the unit-test guidance.

  • Documentation update is not required because this change does not introduce or modify a user-facing interface.

  • Provide accuracy and performance analysis.

  • Follow the SGLang code-style guidance.

Review and Merge Process

  2. Get approvals from CODEOWNERS and other reviewers.

  3. Trigger CI tests with the documented CI comments or contact an authorized user.

## Motivation This PR is a follow-up to [[#30658](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30658)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30658). PR #30658 defers host-pool free-list concatenation for `HostKVCache`-based pools. However, `LogicalHostPool` is a standalone allocator and does not inherit from `HostKVCache`, so it is not covered by that optimization. `LogicalHostPool.free()` still eagerly rebuilds the complete free-slot tensor on every release: ```python self.free_slots = torch.cat([self.free_slots, released_indices]) ``` When HiCache uses a large logical host pool, `free_slots` can contain hundreds of thousands or millions of entries. Releasing a small number of slots therefore copies the entire existing free list. Repeated releases during cache eviction can introduce significant CPU stalls during HiCache cold fill and warm-up. In an internal DSV4 HiCache workload, the allocator eviction-and-retry path showed representative average latencies of approximately `392.6–586.7 ms`, with a maximum close to `592 ms`. Profiling identified repeated large free-list concatenations as the dominant CPU-side overhead. The issue was especially visible with a large logical cache capacity, but the underlying allocator problem is independent of any particular cache-sharding configuration. ## Modifications Apply the lazy free-slot release strategy from #30658 to `LogicalHostPool`: - Keep released slot tensors in `release_slots` instead of concatenating them immediately. - Track pending released slots with `num_release_slots`. - Include pending released slots in `available_size()`. - Continue allocating from the primary `free_slots` tensor while it has sufficient capacity. - Merge pending released chunks only when an allocation cannot be satisfied by the primary free list. - Avoid recording empty releases. - Reset all pending-release state in `clear()`. - Preserve the existing page-alignment validation and slot reuse order. The patch does not add runtime logging, configuration flags, or model-specific behavior. Unit tests cover: - deferred release without rebuilding the primary free list; - allocation from the primary free list before merging pending slots; - reuse of released slots after a deferred merge; - merging multiple released chunks; - empty releases; - state reset through `clear()`; - preservation of `LogicalHostPool` page-alignment checks. ## Accuracy Tests This change only modifies CPU-side free-slot allocator metadata. It does not modify: - model weights or model forward execution; - KV cache tensor contents; - cache keys or page-table mappings; - host-to-device or device-to-host data transfer; - attention, sampling, or CUDA kernels. The unit test verifies that slot allocation and reuse order remain unchanged. Therefore, model output accuracy is not expected to change. Local checks completed: ```text PASS: Python syntax compilation for the modified source and test files PASS: scripts/ci/check_registered_tests.py PASS: git diff --check ``` The PyTorch unit test is added to the existing registered CPU test suite and will be executed by GitHub CI: ```bash python3 -m unittest \ test.registered.unit.mem_cache.test_mem_pool_host.TestLazyHostPoolRelease.test_logical_pool_lazy_release ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Before this change, every `LogicalHostPool.free(K)` may concatenate the released slots with an existing free list containing `F` entries: ```text Free-list maintenance cost: O(F + K) ``` After this change, `free()` only records the released tensor and updates a counter: ```text Free-list maintenance cost: O(1) ``` The larger concatenation is deferred until the primary free list cannot satisfy an allocation. Multiple releases can therefore be combined into one allocation-side merge instead of repeatedly copying the full free list. In the internal HiCache workload that exposed this issue: - the pre-change eviction-and-retry path reached approximately `392.6–586.7 ms` average CPU latency; - the maximum observed latency was approximately `592 ms`; - after applying lazy release, repeated eager concatenations were removed from the `free()` hot path; - the amount of traffic required for HiCache warm-up was substantially reduced, although other cache-population costs can still require a smaller warm-up period. This matches the optimization strategy and performance rationale already validated for other host pools in #30658. ## Checklist - [ ] Format the code with [[pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). Pending local dependency setup or GitHub CI. - [x] Add unit tests according to the [[unit-test guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Documentation update is not required because this change does not introduce or modify a user-facing interface. - [x] Provide accuracy and performance analysis. - [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance. ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [[PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [[CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with the documented CI comments or contact an authorized user. 4. title: [diffusion] FLUX.1 fused adaLN modulate (bit-exact) + RoPE cache hoist, LN-affine folding behind quality=high (H200 e2e -3.5% lossless / -6.9% high)
author: BBuf
body:
Branch: `k2-flux-modulate-rope`, three commits on `main` (d4be483efb), standalone — no dependencies. Third wave of the FLUX.1 elementwise cleanup after #33819 (residual-gate fast path + gated GELU epilogue): FLUX.1 runs at ~97.8% GPU busy, so the remaining eager elementwise chains (13.4% of step kernel time) convert directly into wall-clock.

| commit | scope | tier |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `7fd67406a6` | RoPE cos/sin cache hoisted to one build per step | lossless (same tensor reused) |
| `95675ae120` | new bit-exact fused adaLN modulate kernel, wired unconditionally | lossless (`torch.equal`) |
| `2eda4a7725` | modulate folded into the LN affine (one aten kernel per site) | `quality="high"` mount |

## Motivation

Per 50-step 1024x1024 FLUX.1-dev image, the diffusers-style adaLN plumbing runs:

- **Modulate chains**: `norm(x) * (1 + scale) + shift` at 114 sites/step (19 dual blocks x 4: norm1/norm1_context/norm2/norm2_context + 38 single blocks x 1) = three eager elementwise kernels each — a tiny `1 + scale` row op plus **two full HBM passes** over the `[1, L, 3072]` activation (mul 3.09 ms/step + add 3.14 ms/step + row ops 0.15 ms/step in the S1 trace).
- **RoPE cache rebuilds**: every attention call re-ran `torch.cat([cos.float(), sin.float()], -1)` on identical inputs — 57 launches/step (19 dual + 38 single), 2,850 per image, all but one producing the same tensor.

## Modifications

**Commit 1 — RoPE hoist (lossless by construction).** `FluxTransformer2DModel.forward` builds the concatenated fp32 cache once per step (separately for the single-block relayout when SP text sharding is active) and passes the tensor down; `FluxAttention` keeps accepting the raw `(cos, sin)` tuple for other callers. Every attention consumes the same tensor values as before.

**Commit 2 — bit-exact fused modulate (lossless, `torch.equal`).** New JIT CUDA kernel `modulate_scale_shift.cuh` (sibling of `residual_gate_add.cuh`, same vec-8 row-broadcast tile structure) computing `round(round(x * round(1+scale)) + shift)` — each intermediate rounded back to the storage dtype exactly like the eager chain's kernel boundaries, which also structurally blocks FMA contraction. Because every eager op in the chain is elementwise, matching the per-op rounding is sufficient for bit-exactness (no reduction-order risk). Wired unconditionally via local `FluxAdaLayerNormZero{,Single}` subclasses (same parameters/state-dict as the diffusers parents) and the dual-block norm2 sites; guarded inputs (non-half dtype, B>1 non-contiguous chunk views, misalignment) fall back to the eager expression, `torch.compiler.is_compiling()` escape hatch as in #33819. Nunchaku branches (`scale` without `1+`) untouched.

**Commit 3 — LN-affine folding behind `quality="high"`.** The remaining lossless-path pair per site is the affine-free LayerNorm kernel + the fused modulate (two HBM passes). For high requests the modulate folds into the LN's elementwise affine: `layer_norm(x, weight=1+scale, bias=shift)` — one aten kernel, one pass. `1 + scale` keeps the eager rounding of the `[1, D]` row; the remaining difference is that scale/shift apply in fp32 to the *unrounded* normalized value (bf16 rounding-order level, max abs diff ~0.05 on FLUX shapes) — close, but not bit-exact, hence mounted per batch by the DenoisingStage exactly like the fused linear+GELU epilogue (#33819): sites default off, lossless requests keep the bit-exact reference path (mount log: `Mounted fused LN+modulate (affine folding) for quality=high`). Per-call guard requires B == 1 (the folded affine is a `[D]` row).

### Why the LN reduction itself is not fused on the lossless path

#33819 already audited the shared norm+scale/shift fusions for FLUX and dropped them (`norm_scale_shift_native` is Blackwell-gated; the Triton `select01` layers are fp32 single-pass, not bit-exact). A T10-style (#33734 ERNIE) bit-exact replication was assessed against torch 2.11's `vectorized_layer_norm_kernel`: unlike the CuTe-DSL RMSNorm T10 replicated (documented ordered fadd chain + butterfly fold), aten's LayerNorm uses per-element Welford updates (`mean + delta * (1.f/new_count)`), count-weighted `cuWelfordCombine` merges, and the accurate multi-instruction `rsqrtf` — with the effective FMA-contraction choices baked into shipped libtorch SASS. Reproducing that bit-for-bit in Triton is a full task with real failure risk, so the LN fusion ships as the gated affine-folding instead (the fallback the plan anticipated), and the lossless tier keeps aten's LN kernel untouched.

## Speed Tests (H200)

FLUX.1-dev (sha256-verified `unsloth/FLUX.1-dev` mirror), 1024x1024, 50 steps, bf16, embedded guidance (single forward, B=1), fixed prompt, `seed=42`. One warmed process, 10 sequential generations, first dropped, median of 9 (#33451/#33536/#33819 protocol), single pinned H200.

| Arm | E2E wall (ms) | DenoisingStage (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| main @ d4be483efb, lossless | 7442.9 | 6809.5 |
| + commit 1 (RoPE hoist) | 7396.0 (-0.6%) | 6789.8 (-0.3%) |
| **this PR, lossless (default)** | **7181.9 (-3.5%)** | **6607.3 (-3.0%)** |
| main, quality=high (GELU epilogue) | 7218.7 | 6648.4 |
| **this PR, quality=high** | **6926.1** | **6405.5** |

- Gated tier vs its own baseline (both at quality=high): denoise **-3.7%**, wall **-4.1%**.
- Combined vs main lossless: denoise **-5.9%**, wall **-6.9%**.

Attribution closes against kernel microbenchmarks at the real shapes (bf16, 200 iters after warmup):

| Op | shape | eager | fused | speedup |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| modulate chain | (1, 4096, 3072), rows (1, 3072) | 68.5 us | 15.9 us | 4.32x |
| modulate chain | (1, 512, 3072) | 25.4 us | 13.2 us | 1.92x |
| modulate chain | (1, 4608, 3072) | 76.8 us | 17.8 us | 4.33x |
| LN + fused modulate vs folded LN | (1, 4096, 3072) | 38.3 us | 27.3 us | 1.40x |
| LN + fused modulate vs folded LN | (1, 512, 3072) | 23.3 us | 20.1 us | 1.16x |
| RoPE cos/sin cat | (4608, 128) fp32 x2 | 7.5 us/call | 1 call/step instead of 57 | — |

Summed over sites: RoPE 0.43 ms/step vs measured 0.39 ms/step commit-1 delta; modulate ~4.7 ms/step (micro) vs 3.65 ms/step measured; LN folding ~1.0 ms/step (micro) vs ~0.8 ms/step measured (high-arm delta net of the lossless wins). Microbenchmarks run standalone slightly above the in-graph deltas, as expected for launch-dense eager chains.

## Accuracy Tests

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| kernel unit tests (`test_modulate_scale_shift.py`, 12 cases: FLUX shapes, bf16/fp16, batched rows, adaLN chunk views) | `torch.equal` vs eager chain, all pass |
| module A/B: `FluxAdaLayerNormZero{,Single}` vs diffusers parents, L in {4096, 512, 4608} | bit-exact (`torch.equal`, all outputs) |
| e2e md5, lossless: main x10 / commit-1 x10 / this PR x10 / final HEAD x2 iter images | **all 32 images one identical md5** (`cad50fb5...`) |
| `test_fused_ln_modulate.py` (folded-LN closeness + mount protocol) | pass (max abs diff 0.047 at bf16, rounding-order level) |
| adjacent suites (`test_transformer_quant`, `test_fused_linear_gelu`, `test_residual_gate_add`) | 45 passed |
| pre-commit (pinned) on all changed files, per commit | clean |

quality=high image quality (vs the bit-exact lossless reference, same seed; #33819 table protocol):

| Prompt | PSNR | SSIM |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| cyberpunk city (bench prompt) | 35.48 dB | 0.9785 |
| mountain lake sunrise | 36.40 dB | 0.9873 |
| elderly craftsman portrait | 37.95 dB | 0.9916 |

Context: the already-merged GELU-epilogue high tier alone measures 34.67 dB / 0.9765 on the bench prompt against the same reference — the LN folding does not degrade the high tier's quality band (this PR high vs main high: 35.64 dB / 0.9786). Sample images: `/data/solmig/k2_runs/{main,mainhigh,k2high,mainref}/`.

## Benchmark configuration

- Machine: `ion8-h200` (H200, container `sglang-bbuf`), `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2`, torch 2.11.0+cu130.
- Model: `unsloth/FLUX.1-dev` from the shared HF cache (byte-identical mirror of the gated `black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev`).
- Driver: `/data/solmig/prA_work/pra_e2e.py` (the #33819 harness) — `DiffGenerator.from_pretrained(model_path, num_gpus=1, local_mode=True)`, `prompt="A futuristic cyberpunk city at night, neon lights reflecting on wet streets"`, `seed=42`, `width=height=1024`, `num_inference_steps=50`, `quality={lossless|high}`, 10 iterations, per-iter PNGs for md5/PSNR.
- Arms/worktrees: main `/data/solmig/k2_main_tree` (d4be483efb), commit-1 `/data/solmig/k2_rope_tree` (7fd67406a6), PR `/data/solmig/k2_tree` (HEAD). Raw logs and records JSON: `/data/solmig/k2_runs/{main,rope,k2,mainhigh,k2high,mainref,k2final}*`.
- DenoisingStage times parsed from the scheduler logs (`[DenoisingStage] finished in X seconds`), same drop-first/median-of-9 policy as wall.


Side-by-side sample (lossless left — md5-identical to main — vs quality=high right):

title: [diffusion] GLM-Image bit-exact fused aten LayerNorm+modulate / qk-LN (H200 30-step denoise -8.1%)
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

GLM-Image's transformer block (hidden 4096, 30 blocks, 32 heads x head_dim
128, 30 steps, true CFG = 2 forwards/step) still runs its adaLN chain in
eager pieces — 242 bare aten `layer_norm` launches per step plus a
hand-written modulate/gate chain around them:

- `GlmImageAdaLayerNormZero` runs bare `nn.LayerNorm` (no affine) plus a
  hand-written `norm * (1 + scale) + shift` for both the image and text
  streams — 4 aten kernels per stream per block;
- the qk-norm is `nn.LayerNorm(128)` per head on `(1, S, 32, 128)`: aten's
  `vectorized_layer_norm_kernel` spends a full 128-thread block per
  128-element row (warp 0 does 4 elements per lane, warps 1-3 idle), and
  the two launches cost 301 us per block at the real shape — **10.1% of
  denoise GPU time** in the profiler trace;
- the final `GlmImageAdaLayerNormContinuous` repeats the LN+modulate
  pattern once per forward;
- the ff gate `hidden + ff_out * gate` is another eager pair per stream.

This PR fuses each site into one Triton kernel that is **numerically
re-engineered to be rounding-faithful to the eager chain, step for step**,
so it is bit-exact (`torch.equal`, full-image md5-identical) and wired on
the default lossless path with no quality gate — the standard #33734 /
#33854 / #33886 used.

## What "rounding-faithful" means here

`nn.LayerNorm` on bf16 dispatches to aten's
`vectorized_layer_norm_kernel<BFloat16, float>`. The Triton kernels
replicate that kernel's exact arithmetic DAG, verified instruction by
instruction against the sm_90 SASS of torch 2.11's `libtorch_cuda.so`:

- the (32, 4) block's per-thread serial Welford accumulation over
  `aligned_vector<bf16, 4>` loads (thread t owns vectors `t, t+128, ...`),
  with both FMA contractions nvcc makes (`mean' = FFMA(delta, recip, mean)`,
  `sigma2' = FFMA(delta, val - mean', sigma2)`) and its guarded
  4-instruction reciprocal fast path (`MUFU.RCP; FFMA(x,r,-1);
  FADD.FTZ(-e,-0); FFMA(r,e,r)`) reproduced via inline PTX;
- the `SHFL.DOWN` 16/8/4/2/1 fold tree through `cuWelfordCombine`
  (count-weighted merge, zero-count branch included) expressed with
  order-exact `tl.reshape`/`tl.permute`/`tl.split` folds, then the
  (0,2)/(1,3)/(0,1) inter-warp combines;
- `sigma2 / float(N)` as an IEEE correctly-rounded `div.rn.f32`, and
  `rstd = rsqrtf(...)` as `rsqrt.approx.f32` with the 2^24/2^12 subnormal
  rescale branch;
- the output `cvt.rn.bf16(FMUL(rstd, FADD(x, -mean)))` (no FMA), then the
  aten modulate chain's per-op bf16 boundaries (`round(1+scale)`,
  `round(y*(1+scale))`, `round(+shift)`) via the bitcast RNE helper from
  #33854;
- the qk kernel replicates the same DAG for head_dim <= 128 rows, where
  only vectors `0..head_dim/4-1` of the 128 aten threads carry data (the
  remaining lanes and warps 1..3 enter the fold with count 0), and handles
  q and k in one launch, 64 rows per program.

Because bit-exactness is a property of *which LayerNorm implementation aten
dispatches to*, the model-side wrappers **verify `torch.equal` against the
eager chain once at runtime** on the first real input and permanently fall
back to eager on any mismatch. The fast path can never silently change
outputs.

The ff gate reuses `residual_gate_add_cuda` (bit-exact by construction,
#33734) behind the same one-time-disable wrapper.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/triton/layernorm_modulate.py`
  (new): the two Triton kernels + guards, registered as custom ops
  (torch.compile-safe fake impls).
- `glm_image.py`: `_glm_ln_modulate` / `_glm_qk_layernorm` /
  `_glm_residual_gate_add` wrappers (first-call self-verification, one-time
  disable on exception/mismatch, #33854 style) wired at
  `GlmImageAdaLayerNormZero` (both streams),
  `GlmImageAdaLayerNormContinuous`, the attention qk-norm, and both ff-gate
  sites.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_glm_image_ln_modulate.py`
  (new): bit-exactness at the real GLM-Image shapes plus an assertion that
  the fast paths were actually taken (not silently disabled).

## Speed Tests (H200)

`zai-org/GLM-Image`, 1024x1024, default 30-step preset (true CFG, 2
forwards/step), bf16, eager, fixed prompt, `seed=42`. One warmed process,
10 sequential requests, first dropped, median of 9, GPU 0.

| arm | DenoisingStage (s) | s/step | GlmImageAR (s) | e2e wall (s) | e2e minus AR (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main (d4be483efb), run 1 | 6.385 | 0.2127 | 32.09 | 38.785 | 6.70 |
| this PR | **5.870** | **0.1956** | 35.37 | 41.559 | **6.19** |
| main, run 2 (A/B/A) | 6.391 | 0.2129 | 33.24 | 39.952 | 6.71 |

DenoisingStage **-8.1%** (pooled main 6.388 -> 5.870 s), bit-exact
(md5-identical) output.

E2e caveat: ~83% of e2e is the `GlmImageAR` autoregressive prior-token
stage (a separate `GlmImageForConditionalGeneration` model this PR does not
touch), which drifted 32.1 -> 35.4 -> 33.2 s across the three arms with
host load (other tenants on the box) — the A/B/A bracket shows the drift is
environmental, not tree-dependent (main's own e2e moved +1.2 s between its
two runs while its denoise stayed within 6 ms). Net of the AR stage, e2e
drops 6.70/6.71 -> 6.19 s (**-7.7%**, i.e. -0.52 s/request, -1.3% of total
e2e).

Kernel microbenchmark at the real shapes (`triton.testing.do_bench`):

| Site | eager | fused | speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `LN + norm*(1+scale)+shift` (1, 4096, 4096) bf16 (aten LN + 3 aten elementwise) | 121.8 us | 38.5 us | 3.16x |
| qk `nn.LayerNorm(128)` (1, 4360, 32, 128) bf16, q and k (2 aten launches) | 301.2 us | 62 us | 4.86x |

Attribution (built-in `--profile`, same 5-step denoise window on both
trees, kernel self-time):

| kernel family | main | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| aten `vectorized_layer_norm_kernel` (norm1 x2, qk x2, norm_out) | 141.3 ms / 10.8% (n=1517) | 0 |
| aten modulate/gate elementwise (mul + adds) | 64.8 ms / 4.9% | 0 |
| `_qk_ln_head_kernel` (new) | - | 24.1 ms / 2.0% |
| `_ln_modulate_kernel` (new) | - | 17.6 ms / 1.5% |
| `residual_gate_add` (reused #33734 kernel) | - | 9.6 ms / 0.8% |
| whole window | 1313.4 ms | 1202.5 ms (**-8.4%**) |

Remaining window is GEMMs (72.8%) and FlashAttention (13.6%), consistent
with the -8.1% DenoisingStage wall-clock delta.

## Benchmark command

Both arms run the identical protocol (this PR is lossless-only; arms = main
tree @ d4be483efb vs PR tree), default eager configuration
(`performance_mode=auto`, `enable_torch_compile=false`):

```python
from sglang.multimodal_gen import DiffGenerator

gen = DiffGenerator.from_pretrained(
    model_path="zai-org/GLM-Image", num_gpus=1, local_mode=True
)
for i in range(10):
    gen.generate(sampling_params_kwargs=dict(
        prompt=PROMPT, seed=42, width=1024, height=1024,  # default 30-step preset
    ))
```

## Accuracy Tests

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Both kernels vs eager chain, `torch.equal`, real shapes (1,4096,4096) LN+mod, (1,4360,32,128) qk, plus text-stream/odd shapes | `True` (registered unit test, 6 passed) |
| Full 1024x1024 images, 2 prompts x 2 seeds, this PR vs main | **md5 identical in all 4 pairs** (`f86659da...`, `91882448...`, `7a2f3b00...`, `ac01683d...`) |
| Runtime self-verification | wired; first call per site verifies `torch.equal` vs eager and permanently disables the fast path on mismatch |
| Fallback warnings in the 14-request PR arm | none |

```
6 passed
```
