title: perf: add H200 Triton MoE configs for E256 N512
author: vedantjh2
body:
## Summary

- add Triton 3.7.1 BF16 fused-MoE configurations for `E=256`, `N=512` on NVIDIA H200
- tune the gate/up and down projections separately
- enable TMA for the down projection at the tuned `M=512` and `M=1024` tiers
- preserve the existing heuristic configuration at `M=256`

The target shape is used by LLaDA2.1-mini. Without these files, SGLang logs a missing-config warning and falls back to the generic Triton heuristic.

## Tuning methodology

These values were selected by measurement rather than copied or chosen manually.

- swept the existing heuristic plus 21 curated candidates at each `M=256`, `M=512`, and `M=1024` tier
- varied `BLOCK_SIZE_M/N/K`, `GROUP_SIZE_M`, warp count, and pipeline stages
- benchmarked gate/up and down projections independently while requiring the same `BLOCK_SIZE_M`
- measured both non-TMA and TMA down-projection paths
- used randomized top-k routing inputs, CUDA-graph warmup, and repeated kernel timing
- retested the selected pair through the complete fused-MoE runtime before serving tests

| Tier | Existing heuristic | Best swept pair | Latency change | Selected configuration |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `M=256` | 390.0 us | 386.9 us | -0.8% | Keep existing heuristic; the gain was too small |
| `M=512` | 545.5 us | 394.2 us | **-27.7%** | Up: `M32/N128/K128/G32/w8/s3`; down: `M32/N64/K128/G32/w4/s3 + TMA` |
| `M=1024` | 585.5 us | 409.6 us | **-30.0%** | Up: `M64/N64/K64/G1/w4/s3`; down: `M64/N128/K64/G1/w4/s3 + TMA` |

The complete runtime benchmark independently confirmed the `M=1024` selection at 650.1 us versus 448.3 us (**31.0% lower latency**).

This was a bounded denoise-focused sweep rather than an exhaustive search over every possible tile. No separate `M=8192` prefill sweep was performed; the 500-request 8K-prefill serving test below was neutral and confirmed that the nearest tuned profile did not regress that workload materially.

## Performance

Environment:

- one NVIDIA H200
- LLaDA2.1-mini, BF16, TP1/EP1
- JointThreshold + FDFO + vectorized decoding
- FlashInfer attention and Triton MoE
- concurrency 32, identical seeds and requests
- baseline first, server restarted between arms
- shape warmup and `/flush_cache` before every measurement

The full fused-MoE microbenchmark at `M=1024` improved from 650.1 us to 448.3 us (**31.0% lower latency**).

### 500-request serving tests

| Workload | Metric | Default | Tuned | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 input / 512 output | Output throughput | 1,650.96 tok/s | 1,766.32 tok/s | **+7.0%** |
|  | Mean TPOT | 17.09 ms | 15.95 ms | **-6.7%** |
|  | P95 TPOT | 27.89 ms | 25.85 ms | **-7.3%** |
| 128 input / 2,048 output | Output throughput | 4,155.39 tok/s | 4,687.85 tok/s | **+12.8%** |
|  | Mean TPOT | 6.94 ms | 6.14 ms | **-11.5%** |
|  | P95 TPOT | 21.53 ms | 19.36 ms | **-10.1%** |
| 8,192 input / 128 output | Output throughput | 100.06 tok/s | 100.31 tok/s | +0.3% |
|  | Mean TPOT | 222.92 ms | 223.52 ms | +0.3% |
|  | P95 TPOT | 354.69 ms | 354.62 ms | ~0% |

The decode-heavy workload benefits most. The long-prefill workload is neutral, as expected when MoE denoising is not the dominant cost.

All six 500-request arms completed successfully, produced every requested output token, and reported no request errors. Server logs confirmed that the default arms used the fallback heuristic and the tuned arms loaded both new configuration files.

## Testing

- validated both JSON files with `python3 -m json.tool`
- ran `git diff --check`
- ran matched 64-request smoke tests before the full tests
- ran three matched 500-request serving comparisons described above

title: [DSA] Fix top-k v2 dropping non-primary ranks' output on CUDA 13.1+ (root cause for #33835)
author: DarkSharpness
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 DSA decode can return a corrupt top-k from the fused small-batch
cluster kernel, which downstream sparse attention then dereferences as garbage KV
indices (the illegal memory access reported in #33835).

The trigger is the **CUDA toolkit version, not the GPU architecture**: identical
source and identical hardware (H200, sm_90a) are correct when built with nvcc
12.9/13.0 and wrong when built with 13.1/13.2/13.3.

## Root cause

`TopKCluster::forward` picked its phase-3 scatter destination up front:

```c
const auto cur_out = is_primary ? problem.out : smem->tmp_out;
...
cur_out[pos] = idx;
```

`problem.out` can be a `shared::cluster` (DSMEM) alias of the elected rank's
buffer, while `smem->tmp_out` is `shared::cta`. Merging both into one pointer
variable makes cicc 13.1+ mis-lower the block-local arm on sm_90a and **silently
drop every non-primary rank's staged output** — `tmp_out` stays zero, and phase
3.5 then faithfully copies zeros to perfectly correct DSMEM addresses.

Slot-diffing one row against a CUDA 12.9 build shows exactly one contiguous bad
run:

```
correct slots: 129/512      bad-slot runs: [(61, 443, 383)]
```

Slots 0–60 are the primary's own scatter and 444–511 are the `handle_tie` tail;
the 383 lost slots are exactly the seven peers' contributions. Read-back
instrumentation confirms the mechanism — `tmp_out[0] == 0` on all seven peers
under 13.3 versus valid indices (8161, 10064, 16264, …) under 12.9, while
`count_gt` reports 34–64 candidates found.

Verified *not* the cause (each tested and ruled out): `enable_smem_spilling`,
`__restrict__` on `TopKProblem::out`, the store's address space (forcing a
generic `st.u32` at the emit changes nothing), the load side (`volatile` loads),
and memory ordering (explicit `barrier.cluster.arrive.release` /
`wait.acquire`, `__threadfence()`). Pointer values, `start_write`/`num_write`,
and the store addresses were all dumped and are **correct in both toolchains** —
only the data was wrong.

## Changes

**1. Keep the two scatter destinations in separate code paths** so neither
pointer ever carries two address spaces, with a comment so nobody merges them
back. This is the actual fix.

**2. Drop the `peer_problem` copy from #32910**, stating the block-local pointer
at the read-back site instead. That `__builtin_assume` is load-bearing, not an
optimization: removing it reproduces the #32830 cicc segfault on 13.1/13.2/13.3.

**3. Make top-k v1 take a runtime `topk`** (second commit, separable). v1 baked
`topk` in via `-DSGL_TOPK`, building one module per k; since the macro fed a
`constexpr` rather than a template parameter, the modules exported identically
mangled symbols, and `setup_kernel_smem_once`'s function-local static is emitted
as `STB_GNU_UNIQUE` — merged across every loaded object regardless of
`RTLD_LOCAL`. The module used *second* therefore skipped its
`cudaFuncSetAttribute` opt-in and failed to launch with 64 KB of dynamic shared
memory (`CUDA error: invalid argument`). `bench_topk.py` hits this because it
sweeps k in {512, 1024} in one process; a server only ever uses one k.

## Scope correction vs #33835

#33835 attributes this to Hopper and to rows just above the 32K small-batch
floor. Measured here, **every** fused small-batch cluster shape is affected
(`batch <= 30` and `seq_len > cluster_floor`), including 65537 and 98304 which
that PR reports as fine — the floor only makes the path reachable at
`batch <= 15`. The persistent-pool path was never affected because it stages
output in global memory. With the root cause fixed, no arch gate is needed and
the fused path keeps working on Hopper.

The boundary regression test added by #33835 is still worth keeping; it covers a
real gap (`batch <= 15` with `seq_len` in (32768, 65536]).

## Validation

H200 (sm_90a), 157-row suite = the report's shapes + a boundary sweep +
register/streaming/persistent controls, k in {512, 1024, 2048}:

| nvcc | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 12.9 | 0 bad | 0 bad |
| 13.0 | 0 bad | 0 bad |
| 13.1 | **157 bad** | 0 bad |
| 13.2 | **157 bad** | 0 bad |
| 13.3 | **157 bad** | 0 bad |

Those are all five stable nvcc minors >= 12.9. Additionally: 1500-iteration
randomized stress and 500 CUDA-graph replays clean; builds for **sm_90a and
sm_100a** on every toolchain; v1's runtime-topk path passes 80 cases spanning
k in {1, 2, 7, 31, 64, 100, 255, 256, 257, 300, 511, 512, 513, 777, 1023, 1024}
against trivial / boundary / radix shapes.

**No performance regression** (CUDA 12.9, where both old and new are correct, so
the comparison is at equal correctness):

| case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| register 8x8192 | 3.882 | 3.884 |
| streaming 100x65536 | 14.276 | 14.261 |
| fused-cluster 8x33000 | 8.387 | **8.230** |
| fused-cluster 8x98304 | 9.431 | **9.309** |
| fused-cluster 30x131072 | 13.805 | **13.564** |
| 1 long + 7 short (report shape) | 9.740 | **9.575** |
| persistent 128x131072 | 42.010 | 42.025 |

Worst case +0.1% (noise); the fused cluster path gets 1.3–2.9% faster.

## Caveats

- **sm_100a is compile-verified only** — no Blackwell was available to run on.
  Runtime confirmation there would be welcome.
- CI builds cu130, which is a clean cell, so **CI cannot currently catch this
  class of bug**. Worth considering a toolkit-version guard or moving a build to
  13.1+.
- The remaining exported-weak-symbol hazard in v1 (the kernel host stub itself)
  is not addressed here. Compiling JIT modules with hidden visibility would be
  the general fix; it matters because that half fails *silently* rather than
  erroring.

## Checklist

- [x] Root cause identified and the disproven hypotheses documented
- [x] Verified across every stable nvcc minor >= 12.9, before and after
- [x] Performance measured at equal correctness; no regression
- [ ] Blackwell (sm_100a) runtime validation
- [ ] CI

title: [diffusion] LTX-2 quality=high fused RMSNorm+modulate + FFN GELU epilogue (H200 ltx23-one-stage denoise 45.85->43.24 s, ~matches torch.compile)
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Profiling `ltx23-one-stage` eager vs `torch.compile` on H200 (5-step denoise trace) shows LTX-2 video denoise is **compute-bound** — GPU-busy ≈ **89%** in eager — so a breakable CUDA graph recovers almost nothing. `torch.compile`'s advantage (~6% denoise) comes almost entirely from **fusing two elementwise chains**: the adaLN `RMSNorm(x) * (1 + scale) + shift` modulate at every transformer block, and the FFN `GELU`. Kernel-time attribution: compile cuts total GPU-op time 8.58 M → 7.37 M µs (−14%) purely by collapsing the aten `vectorized_layer_norm` + generic `elementwise` + `GELU` launches into fused Triton kernels; GEMMs and attention are untouched.

This PR reproduces those two fusions in **eager** behind `quality="high"`, so the high tier reaches near-parity with `torch.compile` **without** compile's ~minutes-long warmup or its cross-session nondeterminism. The `lossless` default is unchanged and runs the verbatim reference path.

## Changes

- **`kernels/ops/diffusion/ltx2_rmsnorm_modulate.py`** (new): a `QualityGatedFusion` wrapper that folds `rms_norm(x) * (1 + scale) + shift` into one launch by reusing the existing `fused_rmsnorm_scale_shift_bitexact` kernel. LTX-2 uses weightless `RMSNormNoWeight`, so a cached ones weight reproduces it. The fused kernel is not bit-exact vs aten `F.rms_norm` (`rsqrt.approx` vs aten's refined `rsqrtf`, ≤ 1 bf16 ULP), hence the `quality="high"` gate rather than a lossless self-check.
- **`models/dits/ltx_2.py`**: the six `LTX2TransformerBlock` adaLN sites route through `_ltx2_rms_norm_modulate` (fused when mounted, verbatim eager otherwise). `LTX2FeedForward`'s `proj_in`+GELU-tanh is marked as a `fused_linear_gelu` site (cublasLt GELU epilogue), reusing the existing handler.
- **`pipelines_core/stages/denoising.py`**: registers the new fusion in `_QUALITY_FUSION_HANDLERS`, so it mounts/unmounts at the batch boundary for `quality="high"` alongside the existing families. Models without marked sites are unaffected.

## Speed (H200)

`quality=high` vs the `lossless` default vs `torch.compile`, denoise / e2e seconds (one warmed process, warmup dropped):

| preset | lossless (default) | **quality=high** | torch.compile |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ltx23-one-stage (768×512×121f, 30 step) | 45.85 / 47.31 | **43.24 / 44.65 (−5.7% / −5.6%)** | 42.95 / 44.54 |
| ltx23-two-stage | 29.87 / 33.27 | 29.61 / 33.15 | 28.93 / 32.33 |

On `one-stage`, `quality=high` lands within **0.7%** of `torch.compile` on denoise and **0.25%** on e2e — i.e. eager parity without compile. On the two-stage / refinement variants the gain is small: the refinement stage is more attention/GEMM-bound, so the elementwise share (and thus the fusible surface) is smaller; the fusion is still applied and remains harmless.

## Accuracy

`quality=high` is numerically equivalent only at half-precision rounding level (each fold is ≤ 1 bf16 ULP), so it is gated per-batch and the `lossless` default is bit-exact.

- **PSNR(high vs lossless)** over the full 121-frame ltx23-one-stage output: **min 35.29 dB / mean 36.34 dB** (acceptance bar > 25 dB). No frame drops below the bar over the 30-step denoise.
- **Unit test** `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_ltx2_rms_norm_modulate.py` (registered CUDA CI): the unmounted (lossless) path is `torch.equal` to the eager reference; the mounted path routes through the fused kernel and stays within half-precision rounding of eager. Existing `fused_linear_gelu` / `rmsnorm_scale_shift` suites unchanged.

## Benchmark configuration

```
sglang.multimodal_gen.DiffGenerator, model=Lightricks/LTX-2.3, local_mode=True,
num_gpus=2, enable_torch_compile=false, seed=1234, 768x512, 121 frames,
num_inference_steps=30, quality={lossless|high}
```

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [diffusion] Clean up shared bitexact gates, helpers, and stale naming
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary
- Centralize bit-exact first-sight `torch.equal` verify/disable behind `BitExactFusionGate` for FLUX / GLM / Sana / Ernie fused-norm sites (stops another per-model `_DISABLED/_VERIFIED` copy after #34126).
- Deduplicate shared helpers: Flux/Flux2/Qwen `_get_qkv_projections`, transformer lazy-load for denoising/Hunyuan3D, and route Z-Image RMSNorm wrappers through `fused_gate_rmsnorm`.
- Drop unused package-level `get_kernel` wrappers; keep registry entries for namespace discovery (including `sparse_linear_attn_fwd`).
- Rename generic native NSS symbols off the Qwen-only prefix; move `PRECISION_TO_TYPE` to a leaf `precision_types` module; refresh skill docs for `native_bf16_rmsnorm` / `BitExactFusionGate`.

## Why
Post-#34085 / #34126 parallel fast-path work left duplicated verify scaffolding, model-local helpers, dead package wrappers, and stale Qwen/Z-Image naming in code and skills. This cleanup keeps one implementation for each shared concern without changing numerical contracts.

## Impact
- No intended model-output, accuracy, or precision change.
- Bit-exact paths still self-verify on first sight and permanently fall back on mismatch.
- Unsupported shapes/dtypes/devices/compile contexts continue to use reference paths.
- JIT module/symbol names for native NSS change (`norm_scale_shift_native` / `nss_bf16_row`); cold rebuild expected on first use.

## Validation
- `python3 -m py_compile` on all touched Python modules.
- `ruff check --select F401,F841,F821,F811` on touched Python files: clean.
- Local smoke of `BitExactFusionGate` once/per-signature/mismatch paths.
- CUDA kernel/integration tests not re-run in this environment (no usable GPU / broken local `transformers`); rely on registered CI: `test_bitexact_gate`, `test_flux_ln_modulate`, `test_glm_image_ln_modulate`, `test_sana_ln_modulate`, `test_ernie_norm_scale_shift`, `test_kernels_namespace`.

title: [DSV4] Fix silent KV corruption when speculative draft tokens > 4
author: hnyls2002
body:
Supersedes #33872.

## Motivation

The compress write plan decides which tokens' raw KV get persisted into the compress-state ring for a *future* compression window to read. A speculative verify batch plans from the optimistic `seq_len = prefix_len + num_draft_tokens` but rolls back to `prefix_len + accept_len`, so every committed token must stay resident whatever the accept length turns out to be.

`c_plan.cuh` capped that pad at a hard-coded 4:

```cpp
constexpr int32_t kMaxMTPDraftTokens = 4;
const auto mtp_pad = std::min(ring_size - compress_ratio, kMaxMTPDraftTokens);
```

With `--speculative-num-draft-tokens > 4` the plan under-writes the ring, and a later compression reads stale slots. This fails silently -- no illegal access, no NaN, no assertion, just wrong compressed state. The host planner path was additionally missing the pad term entirely, so the CPU and GPU planners disagreed.

## Modifications

**The pad is a property of the ring, not of the batch.** A write at `w` aliases onto `w - ring_size`, and the earliest position a future compression can still need is `prefix_len - window_size + 2` (the next batch commits at least one token, and `run_prefill` launches the compress kernel before the write kernel, so a batch's own compressions read the pre-write ring). So the ring's capacity is `ring_size - window_size + 2`, and the plan can simply always pad that far:

```cpp
const auto mtp_pad = ring_size > window_size ? ring_size - window_size + 2 : 0;
```

Padding past a batch's own extend range is harmless -- the planner loops only span `[prefix_len, seq_len)`. A non-speculative ring is exactly one window wide, so the pad is 0 there and the write set is unchanged.

All three planner paths (both `plan_compress_prefill_kernel0` branches and the C++ host loop) now share this value, fixing the CPU/GPU divergence.

**Capacity is validated at startup.** `DSV4PoolConfigurator` rejects a draft count the ring cannot serve, using `max_speculative_num_draft_tokens` since the ring is sized once and must serve the largest adaptive tier. The planner itself cannot do this -- it cannot tell an over-configured verify batch from an ordinary long prefill -- so an over-configured server now fails at startup instead of corrupting state at run time.

The current rings serve `num_draft_tokens <= 10` for c4 and `<= 130` for c128. Raising the c4 bound means growing the ring, which scales the c4 state pool; that tradeoff is left out of this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

`test_deepseek_v4_compress_plan_draft_pad.py` (kernel, ~8s in CI):

- `test_c4_ring_residency` / `test_c128_ring_residency` -- for every draft count the ring serves, crossed with residues of `seq_len % compress_ratio`, assert `plan_w` covers all of `[prefix_len, seq_len)`. This is the sufficient condition: if each step writes its whole extend range, the next compression window is resident by induction whatever the accept length. Reverting the pad turns these red for `D > 4`.
- `test_cpu_and_gpu_planner_agree` -- pins `plan_compress_prefill_kernel0` to the host-loop plan, so the fix has to hold on both paths.
- `test_plain_prefill_write_set` -- non-speculative rings produce the pre-existing write set for both ratios, i.e. no change for non-speculative serving.
- `test_over_capacity_under_writes` -- past the ring capacity the plan silently under-writes, which is why the bound is enforced at startup rather than in the planner.

`test_dsv4_compress_write_pad.py` (CPU unit, ~1s) covers the capacity helper: 0 without speculation, 10/130 for the speculative rings, and 0 for the online-c128 ring of 1.

### The kernel test fails on the pre-fix planner

A regression test that also passes on the buggy code proves nothing, so this was checked directly — running the test file above against the pre-fix planner gives **19 failures**:

| test | failing cases before the fix |
|---|---|
| `test_c4_ring_residency` | D = 5, 9, 10 (each across 4 residues of `seq_len % 4`) |
| `test_c128_ring_residency` | D = 129, 130 |
| `test_cpu_and_gpu_planner_agree` | compress_ratio=128, D=130 |

Two things worth calling out. c4 starts losing positions at **D=5**, exactly `D > kMaxMTPDraftTokens` — the boundary is sharp, which is why an `ndt` of 4 or 2 never sees it. And c128 only breaks near the ring's capacity: its `first_w_pos = min(last_c_pos, seq_len - pad)` usually takes `last_c_pos` (as `seq_len % 128` is typically much larger than the pad), which already reaches far enough back. The exposure is concentrated in the c4 layers.

The third row is a separate defect the pre-fix code also had: the C++ host loop carried no pad term at all, only the GPU kernel did, so the two planner paths emitted different write sets.

### End-to-end

DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSPARK at `--speculative-dspark-block-size 7` (D=8, past the old cap of 4), TP=4, `--moe-runner-backend marlin`; two servers launched identically apart from the checkout.

| | GSM8K (200) | GPQA diamond (198, 5 rounds) | latency | throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 0.990 | 0.7172 | 65.1s | 354.8 tok/s |
| after | 0.985 | 0.7374 | 64.7s | 352.7 tok/s |

Plus an opaque-id echo probe (200 requests, 4000-token prefix, greedy): 200/200 exact on both.

**These numbers show no regression; they are not evidence the fix works.** GPQA leans positive (4 of 5 rounds, +0.02 mean) but is not significant — paired t = 2.0 at df=4, p ~ 0.12. At `temperature=0` over a fixed question set the five rounds should have been identical yet spanned ~4.5pp, so concurrent-batch nondeterminism puts the noise floor above the effect size.

That the fix is not visible end-to-end is expected. The skipped positions are the head of the draft tail, and consecutive verify batches have heavily overlapping write sets, so the next step usually rewrites what the previous one skipped. Corruption needs a position to stay unwritten until a compression actually reads it, which depends on accept-length distribution, sequence length, and compression-point alignment lining up.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance impact expected. The change replaces a compile-time constant with an expression over values the planner already receives; no extra memory traffic, no new launches, no change to the compress kernels. A speculative verify batch writes more rows than before, which is the fix, bounded by the ring capacity.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). -- no user-facing flag or behavior change; the rationale lives in the `c_plan.cuh` comment and the test module docstring.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [PD] Skip speculative verify scratch on prefill servers (saves num_draft_tokens x mamba pool per rank)
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

On a PD-disaggregation **prefill** server, speculative decoding's TARGET_VERIFY never runs — `server_args` already rejects `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec` there with exactly this rationale ("the prefill server never runs spec verify"). However, with speculative decoding enabled on hybrid linear-attention models (GDN/KDA), the prefill server still pays for the full verify machinery:

1. **Pool**: it allocates the verify-only per-draft-token mamba state snapshots — `intermediate_ssm_state_cache` ≈ `num_draft_tokens × (whole mamba pool)`, plus `intermediate_conv_window_cache`. With a 256-slot pool (~6 GB ssm_state per rank) and `num_draft_tokens=4` (NEXTN, 3 steps), this is **~24 GB of dead weight per rank**.
2. **Graphs**: it captures target-verify CUDA graphs that are never replayed.
3. **Warmup**: its warmup dummy forward runs in TARGET_VERIFY mode.

(1) alone is enough to push deep-PP prefill layouts into OOM at prefill CUDA graph capture (the capture of a large prefill token bucket has a transient footprint well above the final graph size).

## Modifications

Gate all three on `disaggregation_mode == "prefill"` for the **target** worker, reusing the existing draft-head precedent (`speculative_num_draft_tokens=None` ⇒ pools skip the `SpeculativeState` buffers):

- `kv_cache_configurator.py::_build_hybrid_req_pool`: pass `speculative_num_draft_tokens=None` on a PD prefill server.
- `cuda_graph_setup.py::capture_decode_graph`: skip target-verify graph capture on a PD prefill server (with the scratch gone it could not be captured anyway, and it would never be replayed).
- `base_runner.py::_dummy_run`: don't promote the warmup dummy forward to TARGET_VERIFY on a PD prefill target worker — warm up in plain DECODE, identical to a non-speculative server.

Draft workers, decode servers, and aggregated (non-disagg) deployments are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K (200 examples, 8-shot, temperature 0) on **Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8**, PD-disaggregated 1P1D (TP4 prefill / TP4 decode, mooncake), **NEXTN speculative decoding on both sides** (`num_steps=3`, `eagle_topk=1`, `num_draft_tokens=4`). The two runs are field-for-field identical except that the prefill server runs with vs. without this change:

| | with this change | baseline (unpatched prefill) |
|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K accuracy | **0.99** | **0.98** |
| MTP accept length (weighted mean) | **3.474** | **3.481** |
| prefill `intermediate_ssm_state_cache` | **not allocated** | 4.31 GB |

Accuracy differs by one example out of 200 (within the sampling noise; reported std 0.099 / 0.140). Accept length is a request-weighted mean over the whole run (259 / 242 decode-batch samples, `#running-req`-weighted) and matches to 0.2% — a meaningful check here, since the acceptance rate depends directly on the state the prefill server hands to the decode server, and would collapse rather than hold if the skipped buffers were live.

Memory saved on the prefill server in that configuration: 4.31 GB/rank (mamba pool 1270 slots, `ssm_state` 27.93 GB, TP4). On a deeper-PP layout with a 256-slot pool the same term is ~24 GB/rank, which is what made prefill CUDA graph capture OOM before this change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed change expected on unaffected paths (decode/agg identical). Memory saving on PD prefill: `num_draft_tokens × mamba-pool bytes` per rank.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).

title: [AMD] Perf Kimi-K3 fuse ROCm KDA decode boundary
author: kkHuang-amd
body:
Defer the `f_b` projection into the gfx950 FlyDSL kernel so decode fuses convolution, recurrent state update, and gated RMSNorm while preserving the existing fail-closed fallback.

## Summary

- Vendor the Kimi-K3 KDA-only FlyDSL wrapper and gfx950 decode kernels in SGLang.
- Prefer the local implementation through the source selector while retaining the AITER module as a fail-closed fallback.
- Remove the dependency on the unreleased `aiter.ops.flydsl.kimi_k3_kda_decode` module; stock pinned AITER supplies only FlyDSL tensor/vector/JIT shims.
- Automatically select the validated cooperative `f_a`, wave-specialized front, fused norm reduction, BF16 `fdot2`, WPE3 schedule only for exact C2.
- Keep every other batch on the original kernel schedule.

## Modifications

- Add a trimmed KDA-only vendored FlyDSL package and source selector.
- Route the existing HIP fused KDA adapter through the SGLang module first.
- Make the exact-C2 winner an internal batch specialization with no per-knob environment configuration.
- Add focused recurrent/graph tests and an allocation-free graph benchmark.

## Runtime gate and fallback

The fused ROCm KDA boundary is opt-in:

```bash
export SGLANG_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND=aiter
```

This flag controls the entire PR path, not only the C2 tuning. During model initialization, Kimi-K3 prepares the deferred `f_b` weights and fused decode arguments only when the value is exactly `aiter` and the gfx950 FlyDSL implementation is available. During decode, `covered()` revalidates runtime shapes, dtypes, strides, state indices, and output buffers before dispatch.

Behavior by configuration:

- Flag unset or any value other than `aiter`: preserve the existing unfused KDA path.
- Flag set to `aiter`, supported gfx950 inputs: use the fused `f_b + convolution + recurrence + gated RMSNorm` boundary.
- Flag set but unsupported runtime inputs: fail closed to the existing KDA implementation.
- Exact C2: automatically select the validated WPE3/cooperative/front-specialized/fused-reduction/`fdot2` schedule.
- C1 and C4+: use the original fused-kernel build options; the C2 specialization does not apply.

`SGLANG_K3_FLYDSL_SOURCE` defaults to `auto`, which prefers the vendored SGLang kernel and falls back to the AITER module if needed. `SGLANG_K3_AITER_KDA_GROUP64` is a separate, optional input-preparation optimization and is not required by this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

- GSM8K 1319: `0.950`
- Invalid responses: `0.001`

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Automatic-profile micro A/B on the integration branch:

```text
batch  baseline us  auto-profile us  delta
1      12.2758      12.3008          +0.20%
2      12.7725      11.9959          -6.08%
4      12.8509      12.8770          +0.20%
8      13.4043      13.3785          -0.19%
16     14.0342      14.0324          -0.01%
```

Non-C2 changes are within the measurement noise floor; only C2 changes build options.

Prior production-like results:

- 69-layer graph: `9.20 -> 8.38 us/layer` (`-8.9%`).
- Matched C2 endpoint: `+0.19%` throughput, `-0.20%` TPOT.

## Validation

- [x] KDA FlyDSL focused tests on PR branch: 15 passed
- [x] KDA FlyDSL focused tests on integration branch: 15 passed
- [x] C1/C2/C4/C8/C16 graph micro A/B
- [x] GSM8K 1319
- [x] Fail-closed non-C2 fallback

## Checklist

- [x] Add focused unit tests
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results
- [x] Preserve fail-closed fallback

title: [RL, Spec] Introduce top-p mask capture for spec and add DFlash/DSpark impl
author: jvmncs
body:
## Relationship to existing work

#27408 introduced sampling-mask output support. #35205 restored the finite-`top_k` requirement and bounded support packing for sampling masks. #33459 added the DFlash SpecV2 logprob path.

This PR extends that machinery to the DFlash family, with worker-specific adapters for DFlash and DSpark, while preserving the finite-`top_k` contract from #35205.

## Motivation

Sampling masks let RL trainers reconstruct the inference policy more accurately and reduce rollout/training policy mismatch. This change makes that metadata available when using DFlash or DSpark speculative decoding, and introduces a contract that other spec implementations can implement for their own support.


## Modifications

- Add `speculative/spec_sampling_mask.py`, the speculative sampling-mask contract shared by DFlash and DSpark:
  - `validate_spec_sampling_mask_request` rejects configurations whose committed tokens are not exact samples from the captured target distribution: unsupported speculative methods, `min_p`, simulated acceptance, and for DFlash, acceptance thresholds other than 1.0 or missing sampling-verification support.
  - `SpeculativeSamplingMaskCapture.from_logits` rebuilds the target policy after acceptance from the final adjusted logits (grammar, penalties, logit bias, custom logit processors), only for batches with mask requests; greedy rows emit singleton masks with logprob 0.
- Keep speculative acceptance untouched; each worker calls the capture once after accept, including DSpark compact/ragged verification after logits are restored to strided layout.
- Align metadata with committed `out_tokens` / `commit_lens` via `SamplingMaskOutput.num_accept_tokens`; the result processor appends one support row per accepted token and trims at `finished_len`.
- Track per-row mask `top_k` on `SamplingBatchInfo` (`sampling_mask_top_ks`, maintained on filter/merge) to bound the packed support width; unbounded top-k stays rejected per #35205.
- Reject runtime acceptance-threshold updates while DFlash mask requests are active, including PD decode queues.
- Rename `build_dflash_verify_target_probs` to `build_speculative_verify_target_probs`, as it is shared by DFlash, DSpark, UNO and the capture.
- EAGLE, NGRAM and other speculative methods keep rejecting sampling-mask requests.

## Tests

- Add `SpecSamplingMaskKit` (mixed greedy/sampling batch, `selected` and `support` modes) and run it in the DFlash and DSpark basic sanity suites.
- Existing sampling-mask materialization unit tests now build real `SamplingMaskOutput` objects.

## Performance considerations

Capture remains opt-in: batches without mask requests do no extra work. Support is bounded by the largest finite mask `top_k` in the batch and packed before device-to-host transfer. For batches with mask requests, both DFlash and DSpark recompute the target policy once after verification.

## Accuracy Tests

Targeted final implementation:

- 4/4 DFlash sampling-mask unit tests passed in Modal:
    - tensor-backed deferred materialization;
    - filtered target probabilities and selected-token logprobs;
    - greedy singleton masks;
    - whole-request rejection on support overflow.

- Added `SpecSamplingMaskKit` coverage asserting:
    - seven generated tokens produce seven masks and seven logprobs;
    - every sampled token belongs to its corresponding support;
    - greedy rows return singleton masks with logprob 0.

- Full Qwen3.6 NVFP4+DFlash B200 run:
    - 98,304 measured output tokens;
    - 49,152 requested masks returned, with no missing masks;
    - maximum observed top-p support was 5,306; a repeat reached 7,476;
    - completed without generation or mask-alignment errors.

This feature only returns metadata and is not intended to change sampling decisions, so no downstream task-accuracy benchmark was run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

One B200 with:

- nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4;
- modal-labs/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash;
- DFlash block size 8, FA4 draft attention;
- 32 concurrent requests, 512 generated tokens each;
- warmup followed by six alternating mask/no-mask rounds.

Results:

- Without masks: 4,163.78 tok/s median
- With masks: 4,160.45 tok/s median
- Ratio: 0.9992, or approximately −0.08%

The difference was within run-to-run noise. A complete repeat also showed no slowdown.

These numbers were measured on an earlier revision in which DFlash reused the verification probabilities instead of recomputing them after accept; requests without masks are unaffected either way.

title: [AMD] Fix AITER custom reduce-scatter CUDA-graph capture crash under torch_memory_saver
author: JessicaJiang-123
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

When `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH=1`, TMS allocates the CUDA-graph pool with HIP VMM. AITER's registered custom-collective path tries to IPC-register the caller's tensor after capture, but HIP IPC does not support these VMM allocations. This causes CUDA-graph capture to abort with `invalid device pointer`. SGLang already uses the unregistered AITER path under TMS for custom all-reduce and all-gather. Reduce-scatter was the remaining gap: `_maybe_aiter_reduce_scatter()` still hardcoded `registered=True` during capture.

This PR uses the unregistered reduce-scatter path under TMS as well.

| collective | TMS handling |
|---|---|
| custom all-reduce | disables registered capture buffers (#19162 / #20155) |
| custom all-gather | uses the unregistered path (#30557) |
| **custom reduce-scatter** | **fixed in this PR** |

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

Use AITER's unregistered reduce-scatter path during CUDA-graph capture when `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH=1`. Default serving behavior is unchanged.

title: [misc] Pass FP8 scales in FlashInfer SWA prefill, autotune fp8 on SM120, and tighten `is_image_understandable_model`
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary

- Pass `k_scale`/`v_scale` in the FlashInfer SWA chunked-prefill paged read, the one paged call site that omits them
- Let SM120 satisfy the fp8 autotune condition in `should_run_flashinfer_autotune`
- Key `is_image_understandable_model` on a non-`None` `vision_config` rather than attribute presence
- Trim redundant comments across the MLX backend (no code changes)

## Fixes

**`k_scale`/`v_scale` missing in SWA chunked prefill**

`FlashInferAttnBackend` has three paged-KV wrapper calls. Two pass the KV dequant scales; the sliding-window `forward_return_lse` in `forward_extend` does not, so a model combining an FP8 KV cache with a sliding window reads the cache as if it were unscaled.

```
prefill_wrapper_paged.forward            k_scale/v_scale  (present)
prefill_wrapper_paged.forward_return_lse                  <- missing
decode_wrapper.forward                   k_scale/v_scale  (present)
```

All three carry the same comment about using the `_float` variants, so this reads as a copy-paste omission. The two ragged calls in the same function correctly omit the scales -- they read the current batch's k/v, not the paged cache.

No effect when the KV cache is not FP8: `k_scale_float`/`v_scale_float` default to `None`, exactly what the already-shipping `forward` call on the same wrapper object passes.

**SM120 excluded from fp8 autotune**

`should_run_flashinfer_autotune` gated the modelopt-fp8 arm on `is_sm100_supported()`. SM120 satisfies `is_blackwell_supported()`, so `resolve_mxfp8_dense_gemm_backend` sends it to the same tunable FlashInfer CUTLASS MXFP8 dense GEMM as SM100 -- without this the kernel always runs at `tactic=-1` there.

(The `mxfp8_gemm` half of this PR is dropped: #33962 cleared `FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_WORKAROUND_SKIPS` for every architecture, which supersedes it.)

**`is_image_understandable_model` keys on attribute presence**

`hasattr(hf_config, "vision_config")` asks whether the attribute exists; the intent is whether a vision tower exists. These diverge for a config declaring `vision_config` with a `None` default -- `deepseek_ocr`, `deepseekvl2`, `unlimited_ocr` and `janus_pro` all declare it that way as a class attribute. Such a config would be reported as image-capable and server warmup would probe it with an image.

No current model hits this: every config above assigns a real object in `__init__`. This is a correctness tightening of the predicate, not a fix for an observed failure.

## MLX comment cleanup

Drops restating and duplicated comments across `hardware_backend/mlx/` plus the MLX-related blocks in `arg_groups/overrides.py`, `constrained/xgrammar_backend.py` and `server_args.py`.

Comments only -- every touched file is AST-identical to `main` once docstrings and comments are stripped.

title: [Feature] Support NVFP4 token embedding in ModelOpt mixed-precision checkpoints
author: hnyls2002
body:
The MIXED_PRECISION format describes quantization as a per-prefix `quantized_layers` map, and the format itself does not restrict what a prefix points at. `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig.get_quant_method` dispatches on `LinearBase`/`ParallelLMHead`, `RadixAttention` and `FusedMoE`, but a `VocabParallelEmbedding` falls through to the closing `return None` -- so a checkpoint whose map marks the token embedding cannot be served at all.

This adds `ModelOptNvFp4EmbeddingMethod`, which keeps the table packed and unpacks rows to the activation dtype on gather. An embedding is a row gather rather than a GEMM, so there is no NVFP4 kernel to dispatch to and no compute win here -- the gain is purely footprint. On a large vocabulary that is not a rounding error: a 200k-token table over a few thousand channels runs to a billion-plus parameters, where the bf16-to-4-bit difference is on the order of a GiB, and on a single-GPU deployment that turns straight into KV cache.

## Behavior

Unchanged for every checkpoint that loads today. The new branch returns `None` unless the map resolves that prefix to `NVFP4`, and honors `exclude_modules` / `is_layer_excluded` first. Whether the embedding is quantized at all remains the checkpoint author's decision; this only makes the result servable.

The branch must stay after the `ParallelLMHead` one. `ParallelLMHead` subclasses `VocabParallelEmbedding`, and under `tie_word_embeddings` the lm_head *is* the embedding module, so it reaches this branch and gets a gather-only method; `apply()` raises with a message pointing at the recipe. A comment records the ordering requirement.

## Dequant

Follows the same NVFP4 decode as `kvfp4_tensor.batched_dequantize`: low nibble to even lanes, `0x8` sign, `0x7` magnitude into the E2M1 table. The scale step differs by format -- NVFP4 carries an e4m3 per-16 block scale plus an fp32 global scale, applied as a product, where the KV path uses a single E8M0 power-of-two.

## Tests

`test/registered/quant/test_nvfp4_embedding.py` checks the gather against a reference dequant written independently as a plain per-element Python loop, at `rtol=0, atol=0`, plus the group-size divisibility guard.

title: [AMD] Broadcast the EAGLE greedy verify decision across TP ranks on ROCm
author: JessicaJiang-123
body:
Co-author-with: @XinyuJiangCMU 

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

On ROCm with TP > 1, EAGLE speculative decoding can intermittently deadlock. Observed on 4x MI355X (gfx950), GLM-4.7-Flash, TP4, with **2 deadlocks in 5 runs**. Before the watchdog fires, TP ranks disagree on the running batch:

```text
TP0: batch_size()=24, first_req=86e5957d…
TP1: batch_size()=24, first_req=86e5957d…
TP2: batch_size()=25, first_req=f224663e…
TP3: batch_size()=25, first_req=f224663e…
```

On ROCm, _is_hip makes `eagle_sample()` always use the greedy verify path. This path can receive different draft candidates across ranks, while the sampling path already broadcasts its result from rank 0. With different draft candidates, TP ranks can therefore accept different numbers of drafts, and eventually diverge in `seq_lens` / batch composition and deadlock.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

On ROCm, broadcast `predict`, `accept_index`, and `num_correct_drafts` from TP rank 0 after the verify decision is finalized. A normal process-group broadcast is sufficient because `eagle_sample()` runs after the target forward CUDA graph replay.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

End-to-end on 4x MI355X, GLM-4.7-Flash, EAGLE + MTP. Deadlock rate:

| | runs | deadlocks |
|---|---:|---:|
| before | 5 | **2** |
| after | 6 | **0** |

All six post-fix runs completed without watchdog, memory access fault, or scheduler divergence.

title: [BCG][6/N] Allow prefill breakable CUDA graph for the Kimi archs
author: Oasis-Git
body:
Kimi configs always construct a vision_config (KimiK3Config defaults it to KimiK3VisionConfig() when absent), so ModelConfig.is_multimodal is True via the has_multimodal_subconfig sniff even when serving text only -- neither the arch name nor multimodal_model_archs is involved. The generic "multimodal model" rule in _disable_breakable_cudagraph_if_incompatible then forced prefill.backend to DISABLED on the default path.

This only ever showed up on the default path: _apply_cuda_graph_compatibility returns early when the prefill backend is explicitly locked, so validation runs using --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable bypassed the rule and looked fine. With #33661 making MLA fully supported under BCG (and dropping the per-arch MLA opt-in list), this multimodal rule was the last thing keeping Kimi off BCG.

Opt both Kimi archs into the breakable allowlist, and give the tc_piecewise upgrade an explicit precedence rule. That upgrade runs before the disable rules and consulted only the piecewise allowlist, so for any arch on both lists it silently won and breakable membership was dead -- K2.5 is on both. Preferring breakable there keeps K2.5 on the piecewise allowlist (it is still piecewise-validated, and is_piecewise_cuda_graph_disabled_model stays False) while actually resolving to breakable.

Capturing is safe for the same reason it is for the other allowlisted archs: can_replay_locally rejects any batch carrying input_embeds/replace_embeds, so image-carrying batches fall back to eager and only text-only prefill replays.

The tc_piecewise upgrade test builds its model_config as a SimpleNamespace; add the field the new condition reads.

title: perf(vla): graph Pi0.5 prefix encoding
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- add a bounded full CUDA graph runner for static, single-request Pi0.5 prefix encoding
- build the prefix attention mask directly on device and keep VLA graph utilities together
- preserve eager execution for grouped batches, prefix TP, CPU offload, global prefix-cache misses, and per-request graph opt-out
- copy mutable prefix-graph K/V into the action graph buffers so replayed requests cannot observe stale context

## Performance

Measured on one H200 with `lerobot/pi05_base`, ALOHA observations, 10 flow-matching steps, and the existing action-denoise graph enabled:

| Path | End-to-end p50 | Prefix p50 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Action graph only | 49.26 ms | 19.01 ms |
| Prefix + action graphs | 43.07 ms | 11.99 ms |

This is a `1.144x` end-to-end speedup in the post-rebase confirmation run. A prefix shape bucket adds about 48.5 MiB for the validated ALOHA shape. Residency is bounded to one bucket by default; grouped batch=4 showed no prefix-graph benefit and remains eager.

The native HTTP/msgpack action path was also exercised through `sglang serve`; it returned HTTP 200 with a raw-policy p50 of 47.71 ms in the earlier end-to-end run.

## Correctness

- graph enabled/disabled comparison is bit-exact for two different observations at both 5 and 10 denoise steps (`np.array_equal`, max absolute difference 0)
- 24 Pi0.5 runtime/action API/prefix-cache unit tests pass on GPU
- pre-commit passes for the full branch diff

## Configuration

- `enable_prefix_cuda_graph` controls prefix capture
- `prefix_cuda_graph_max_entries` bounds graph residency and defaults to 1
- request-level `runtime.cuda_graph=false` disables both prefix and action graph paths

title: [JIT Kernel] Migrate per-token FP8 quantization from AOT to JIT
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

Migrate CUDA per-token FP8 activation quantization from the prebuilt `sgl_kernel` path to SGLang's lightweight JIT kernel infrastructure. This reduces the CUDA runtime's dependency on the AOT wheel for this operation while preserving the existing output-buffer contract, numerical behavior, and public compatibility API.

## Modifications

- Add a JIT CUDA implementation of dynamic per-token FP8 E4M3 quantization with the existing CTA and warp dispatch strategies.
- Route SGLang CUDA serving through the JIT kernel registry and a `torch.compile`-compatible custom-op wrapper.
- Preserve the legacy CUDA `sgl_kernel.sgl_per_token_quant_fp8` entry point for external consumers, AOT/JIT differential testing, and performance comparisons. MUSA continues to use its AOT path.
- Preserve padded output support: output buffers may contain more rows than the input, and the kernel writes only the first `num_tokens` rows.
- Preserve the AOT dtype boundary and bit-level behavior, including the legacy dispatch-specific zero-row behavior.
- Move correctness coverage and benchmarking into the registered kernel test layout. The benchmark directly compares JIT and AOT implementations.
- Register differential correctness coverage on H100 and B200 so both the shuffle reduction and the SM100 `redux.sync.max.f32` path are checked.
- Remove the superseded AOT-only test and benchmark files.

## Accuracy Tests

- `pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_per_token_quant_fp8.py test/registered/kernels/test_kernel_inventory.py`
- On NVIDIA H200 (SM90): 32 tests passed, including bit-exact AOT-vs-JIT coverage of both CTA and warp dispatch paths.
- On NVIDIA B300 (SM103): 32 tests passed, including bit-exact AOT-vs-JIT coverage of the SM100-family reduction path.
- The differential suite checks raw-bit equality between AOT and JIT outputs and scales for:
  - FP16, BF16, and FP32 inputs.
  - CTA and warp dispatch paths.
  - Non-power-of-two hidden dimensions.
  - Zero rows and FP8 midpoint values.
- Regression coverage verifies padded serving outputs, untouched padded tails, and rejection of unsupported input dtypes.
- B200 execution is registered in `base-b-kernel-unit-test-4-gpu-b200` to validate bit-exactness on the SM100-specific reduction path.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- The registered AOT-vs-JIT benchmark matrix covers FP16/BF16, token counts `1..7807`, and hidden dimensions `512..4096`.
- On NVIDIA H200 (SM90), JIT was faster in 58 of 72 configurations, with a 1.095x geometric-mean speedup over AOT. The range was 0.885x to 3.254x: the slowest relative result was FP16 `(39, 4096)` at 2.925 us vs 2.588 us, and the fastest was FP16 `(7807, 1368)` at 10.965 us vs 35.684 us.
- On NVIDIA B300 (SM103), JIT was faster in 48 of 72 configurations, with a 1.061x geometric-mean speedup over AOT. The range was 0.864x to 2.453x: the slowest relative result was BF16 `(7807, 512)` at 4.852 us vs 4.194 us, and the fastest was FP16 `(7807, 1368)` at 8.743 us vs 21.442 us.

title: [kernel] Content-addressed JIT build cache, generated from our own ninja
author: DarkSharpness
body:
## Problem

`_local_jit_source_hash` decided whether a cached `.so` was still valid by hand-rolling a preprocessor out of two regexes. It follows `"..."` includes only when they sit next to their own file, and `<...>` only under `sgl_kernel/`. Measured on this tree:

| | |
|---|---|
| Files the walker reaches for a CUTLASS kernel | **8** |
| Files the compiler actually reads | **1112** |
| Quoted includes it cannot resolve (across 185 in-tree sources) | 30 (CUTLASS, found via `-I`) |
| Angle includes it skips | 648 (92× `<tvm/ffi/container/tensor.h>`, 59× dlpack, 21× `<cuda_bf16.h>`) |

Each miss also hides that header's entire subtree, so **upgrading flashinfer or editing a CUTLASS header reused a stale binary**. Compiler and package versions were absent from the key as well, and because `load_jit` always passed an explicit `build_directory`, tvm-ffi's own flag-aware hash never ran — `extra_cuda_cflags` reached the key only when a call site remembered to encode it in the module name by hand (`activation` vs `rounded_activation`).

## Approach

Two keys, because the full answer is not computable before the first build — and `build.ninja` is generated here rather than obtained from `tvm_ffi.cpp.load_inline`.

**`build_key`** — everything knowable before compiling. Owning the build file is what makes this exact rather than a hand-maintained list: the key is taken over the generated ninja text itself, plus the generated wrapper source (which carries the exports that never appear in the build file), the direct sources' contents, and a fingerprint of the target, both compilers, and the dependency package versions.

**`deps_key`** — the transitive closure, read back from the depfiles the build leaves behind. **Each leaf carries its own dependency list and is never modified after publication**, and counts as a hit only when re-hashing that list reproduces the leaf's own name. Recorded data is therefore verified rather than trusted: a truncated, tampered, or foreign list simply fails to reproduce the name, so no format-version field has to be believed and there is no shared mutable manifest for writers to merge into.

```
$SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR/<target>/<module_name>/build-<build_key>/
    deps-<deps_key>/          one leaf per transitive-content state
        sgl_deps.json         the dependency list of *this* build
        <module_name>.so
    .staging-<uuid>/          a build in progress
```

Paths are anchor-normalized (`<kernels>/csrc/...`, `<tvm_ffi>/include`), which is what lets a second clone at a different location reuse the first clone's builds.

## Results

| | CUDA (H100) | ROCm (MI350X / gfx950) |
|---|---|---|
| cold build | 5.26 s | 2.89 s |
| warm load | 0.02 s | 0.08 s |
| after `touch` of every header | 0.05 s (no rebuild) | 0.08 s (no rebuild) |
| after editing a transitive header | rebuild, naming the file | rebuild, naming the file |
| after reverting that edit | 0.06 s (earlier leaf reused) | 0.07 s |
| second clone, different path, fresh mtimes | 5.26 s → **0.05 s** | 2.66 s → **0.07 s** |

Numerical output verified against a `F.silu` reference on both platforms.

## Fixes found along the way

**ROCm carried no header dependencies at all.** tvm-ffi declares `depfile = $out.d` on a HIP command that never writes one. Verified on real MI350X hardware:

```
--generate-dependencies-with-compile   →  clang++: error: unknown argument   (nvcc-only flag)
no dependency flags (tvm-ffi's HIP branch) →  rc=0, depfile: NONE
-MD -MF (this PR)                      →  rc=0, depfile: 21307 bytes
```

**Every tensor-parallel rank compiled the same kernel.** They reach the same cold cache simultaneously; with 8 ranks all eight compiled. Builds are now serialized per module variant with a re-check after acquiring the lock — one compiles, seven take the cache. The lock only saves duplicated work: publication is made safe by an atomic directory rename, and readers on the fast path deliberately take no lock (taking it would serialize every warm load).

**The generated wrapper did not include the header defining the macro it uses.** It compiled only because every kernel in tree happens to drag `<tvm/ffi/function.h>` in transitively — which is not something a new kernel's author would know to preserve. Now included explicitly, matching what tvm-ffi's own `_decorate_with_tvm_ffi` prepended.

## Structure

`compile.py` becomes a package along the seams this created, in dependency order with no cycles:

```
paths      where the in-tree sources live, and the default flags
cpp_args   rendering Python values as C++ template arguments
spec       BuildSpec: one fully-resolved build
toolchain  compilers, tvm-ffi locations, platform base flags
ninja      generating and running build.ninja, reading its depfiles
cache      build_key / deps_key, cache layout, publication
loader     load_jit
```

`arch.py` is unchanged. What is still consumed from tvm-ffi: `tvm_ffi.libinfo` for header and library locations, `tvm_ffi.load_module` to load the result, and the `TVM_FFI_DLL_EXPORT_TYPED_FUNC` macro on the C++ side.

`load_jit` loses `external_cpp_files` / `external_cuda_files`; an absolute path in `cpp_files` / `cuda_files` now means the same thing.

## Environment variables

| | |
|---|---|
| `SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` | cache root (default `~/.cache/sglang/jit`); point it at a persistent mount to share builds across CI jobs |
| `SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DEBUG` | log, at INFO, which dependency changed whenever a module is rebuilt |
| `SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_KEEP` | builds kept per module variant; unset keeps all, which is what makes reverting an edit an instant hit |

## Tests

41 CPU-only cases in `test/registered/kernels/test_jit_cache.py` (`base-a-test-cpu`), covering anchor normalization, per-field key separation, leaf self-verification, the commit-side guards, ninja generation, and depfile parsing.

Two of them pin failure modes that are silent rather than loud, and both were confirmed to fail when the property is broken:

- **`test_no_unordered_container_reaches_the_key`** — a `set` or `dict` among the hashed parts would make the same tree key differently in two processes: no error, no wrong result, the cache simply never hits again. Verified end-to-end across four `PYTHONHASHSEED` values and two working directories.
- **`test_a_leaf_that_does_not_match_its_own_name_is_skipped`** — the recorded list is verified, not trusted.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code and pass the pre-commit hooks
- [x] Add unit tests
- [x] Verified on both CUDA (H100) and ROCm (MI350X)

title: [Diffusion] Fuse Cosmos3 QK norm, RoPE, and KV packing
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- let the fused QK-norm + RoPE CUDA path consume flattenable strided Q/K views
- fuse QK norm, RoPE, UND-prefix K/V copy, and GEN-suffix K/V packing into one JIT CUDA launch for Cosmos3 cross-attention
- retain the existing eager/SP/compiler fallbacks and cover packed GQA storage and multi-batch KV layout

## Why

Cosmos3-Nano policy generation runs 48 GEN layers per denoise step. Its Q/K tensors are views into one packed QKV projection, but the previous dispatch copied Q and K before the fused QK-norm + RoPE kernel. Cross-attention then launched two more `torch.cat` kernels per layer to assemble `[UND prefix | GEN suffix]` K/V.

The CUDA kernel already supports the packed QKV strides. This change uses those views directly and adds a KV-pack variant that writes normalized/rotated GEN K directly to its final attention buffer while copying prefix K and prefix/suffix V in the same launch. It does not use `torch.compile` or compiler fusion.

## Performance

H200, BF16, Cosmos3-Nano policy generation, 832x480, 30 denoise steps, action shape `[16, 10]`, 7 measured requests after warmup:

| Path | Median latency | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline | 1488.30 ms | - |
| Strided fused QK-norm + RoPE | 1473.17 ms | -15.13 ms (-1.02%) |
| + fused UND/GEN KV packing | 1456.85 ms | -31.45 ms (-2.11%) |

The KV-pack fusion contributes 16.32 ms (`1.11%`) beyond the strided Q/K path. Generated actions are bit-exact across all three paths (`array_equal=True`, `max_abs_diff=0`).

At the Cosmos3 layer shape (suffix 1966, prefix 107, 32 Q heads, 8 KV heads, head dim 128):

- removing Q/K copies changes QK-norm + RoPE from 0.0490 to 0.0313 ms/layer and removes about 19.8 MiB of transient allocation
- fusing QK-norm + RoPE with KV packing changes 0.0668 to 0.0528 ms/layer
- in a 3-step trace, K/V cat kernels drop from 288 calls / 4.58 ms to zero; total kernel count drops from 2516 to 2228
- total profiled GPU kernel time drops from 181.26 to 178.59 ms over 3 steps
- sampled process peak VRAM is unchanged within measurement noise: 37,454 MiB vs 37,456 MiB

## Compatibility

- CUDA, SP=1, matching FP16/BF16 activation/prefix/weight dtypes: fused KV-pack path
- SP>1, compiler capture, unsupported dtype/layout, or differing norm epsilon: existing QK-norm/attention path

title: [AMD] Use fast exponentials in C4 and C128 ROCm kernels
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
## Motivation

ROCm JIT compilation currently drops `-use_fast_math`, so ordinary `expf` in the DeepSeek V4 C4 and C128 compression kernels keeps full FP32 range reduction and overflow/underflow handling. These softmax exponentials are always max-shifted and therefore non-positive, making the ROCm fast device exponential appropriate without exposing positive-overflow behavior.

## Modifications

- Add small per-kernel exponential helpers in `c4_v2.cuh` and `c128_v2.cuh`.
- Use `__expf` only under `USE_ROCM`.
- Preserve the existing CUDA `expf` behavior.
- Replace one C4 and two C128 max-shifted softmax exponential call sites.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`) with ROCm 7.2:

- `test_deepseek_v4_compress_state_runtime_shapes.py`: 90/90 passed.
- `test_c128_v2.py` FP64-reference suite: 26/26 passed.
- C4 numerical stress: 540/540 finite across head dimensions 128/512, FP32/BF16 state, five seeds, score scales `1e-4` to `1e3`, and KV scales `1e-3` to `1e3`.
  - State writes were identical.
  - Maximum normalized candidate-vs-parent output difference: `1.81e-7`.
  - Maximum candidate excess normalized FP64-reference error: `1.19e-7`.
- C128 numerical stress: 270/270 finite across FP32/BF16 state and the same extreme score/KV scale families.
  - State writes were identical.
  - Worst normalized FP64-reference error remained `5.60e-5`, identical to the parent.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same-process HIP-graph ABBA measurements on MI355X, rebased to `main` at `77c90e7e5`. Each high-signal sample amortizes 100 kernel/workload groups per graph.

### C4 V2

| Workload | Geomean speedup | Case range |
|---|---:|---:|
| Boundary decode | 1.2967x | 1.2293x to 1.3772x |
| Complete 4-token decode cycle | 1.0948x | 1.0354x to 1.1211x |
| Prefill | 1.1618x | 1.1229x to 1.2170x |

For head_dim=512 BF16, disassembly shrank from 1,952 to 1,200 lines. `v_exp_f32` count stayed at 64, while `v_ldexp_f32` and `v_rndne_f32` each dropped from 64 to 0. Decode VGPR decreased from 82 to 81; neither version uses scratch.

### C128 V2

| State dtype | Mode | Geomean speedup | Case range |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| FP32 | Decode | 1.1572x | 1.0191x to 1.2137x |
| FP32 | Prefill | 1.2272x | 1.1796x to 1.2444x |
| BF16 | Decode | 1.2386x | 1.1743x to 1.3109x |
| BF16 | Prefill | 1.2143x | 1.1878x to 1.2257x |

The C128 fast path similarly lowers to `x * log2(e)` followed by native `v_exp_f32`, eliminating the ordinary `expf` range-reconstruction sequence.

title: [diffusion] weight-only FP8: dequantize linear weights once at first use (Ideogram-4 denoise -18.8% H200 / -7.8% H100, bit-exact)
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

The storage-only weight-only FP8 linears (`WeightOnlyFP8*Linear`, used by Ideogram-4-FP8) re-materialize the **full weight matrix on every forward**: `weight.to(bf16) * scale`, then `F.linear`. On the `ideogram4-fp8` preset (TP=2, 1024², 5-step trace) the dequant cast alone is ~13% of per-step GPU time (`direct_copy` 186k µs / 1.42M µs, 2639 calls = every linear × every call), plus the broadcast scale-multiply on top. This is also why `torch.compile` — which constant-folds the dequant — beat eager on H100 for this model.

## What this PR does

Dequantize the weight to the compute dtype **once, on the first device-resident forward**, replacing the FP8 parameter; every later forward runs a plain compute-dtype GEMM. Outputs are **bit-identical** because the same dequantized values feed the same GEMM.

The first-use (rather than load-time) hook is deliberate: the loader calls `post_load_weights` before the model reaches its final device on some paths, and CPU-offloaded modules only land on the device per layer. The decision is remembered per module, and the weight stays FP8-resident (per-forward dequant, exactly today's behavior) when:

- `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_FP8_WEIGHT_DEQUANT_CACHE=0` (kill switch, default on),
- the W8A8 GEMM path is enabled (it consumes FP8 weights directly),
- free device memory is below a 4 GiB reserve (checked per weight),
- a CUDA graph capture is in progress (never allocate inside capture; retried on the next eager call).

No model-file changes — the quantization layer self-manages, so any future weight-only-FP8 model inherits the fast path.

## Performance (ideogram4-fp8 preset, TP=2, 1024², seed 42, `--quality=lossless`)

| card | arm | denoise (s) | e2e (s) | output md5 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| H200 | eager (main) | 4.985 | 5.114 | `43c0463e…` |
| H200 | **eager (this PR)** | **4.050 (−18.8%)** | **4.174** | `43c0463e…` (**identical**) |
| H100 | eager (main) | 5.225 | 5.355 | `14f1d205…` |
| H100 | **eager (this PR)** | **4.818 (−7.8%)** | **4.942** | `14f1d205…` (**identical**) |

Memory: peak reserved per rank 20.2 → 40.0 GiB (the compute-dtype weight copy plus allocator retention of the freed FP8 blocks). The 4 GiB-reserve guard keeps memory-tight deployments on the FP8-resident path automatically.

For reference, the issue-#21 H100 compile baseline is 4.097 s denoise — this PR closes most of the eager-vs-compile gap losslessly (the remainder is inductor fusing the rope/SwiGLU elementwise, a separate follow-up).

## Correctness

- Output md5 identical to main on both cards (tables above).
- Unit tests (`test_weight_only_fp8_dequant_cache.py`): first-forward promotion is `torch.equal` with the per-call dequant reference; promotion dtype follows the input when `compute_dtype` is unset; env kill switch, low-memory guard, and CPU forwards keep the FP8 weight; 5/5 on H200.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Provide accuracy and repro results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [diffusion] ERNIE-Image: fuse rotate-half RoPE + GELU-mul and hoist rope cos/sin (denoise -16.2% H100 / -12.7% H200, bit-exact)
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

ERNIE-Image eager lags `torch.compile` on H100 (issue benchmark: denoise 15.458 s vs 13.665 s at 1024², seed 42), while on H200 compile is a regression. A 5-step trace explains both: the eager RoPE + GEGLU elementwise soup is ~413k µs of a 1.89M µs step window, inductor fuses the same surface down to ~97k µs — but inductor's GEMM selection is ~10% slower than eager's, which cancels the win on H200. Hand-fusing the eager path takes the elementwise win without the GEMM regression.

Three block-level hot spots, all pure elementwise, all reproduced **bit for bit**:

1. **RoPE cos/sin recomputed per layer per projection** — `torch.cos(freqs).to(dtype)` ran twice per q/k per layer although `freqs` is constant across the forward. Now computed once per forward.
2. **The rotate-half chain** (`chunk` + `neg` + `cat` + two muls + add + tail `cat`, ~7 kernels per projection) becomes one Triton kernel (`rope_rotate_half_bitexact.py`) that replicates every aten bf16 rounding boundary: `round(round(x1·cos1) + round(-x2·sin1))` per element, tail columns copied through.
3. **GEGLU** (`up * F.gelu(gate)`, two full passes over the FFN intermediate) uses the activation kernel's rounding variant, which rounds the erf-GELU to bf16 before the multiply exactly like the eager two-step (new thin wrapper `gelu_and_mul_with_activation_rounding`).

Because the math is elementwise (no reductions), exact-rounding replication is possible, so the fast paths mount **by default** behind ERNIE's existing `BitExactFusionGate` first-call self-verification (fused vs eager compared with `torch.equal` on the live tensors; permanent eager fallback on any mismatch or unsupported shape/dtype/platform).

## Performance (ernie-image-turbo preset, 1024², seed 42, `--quality=lossless`, single GPU)

| card | arm | denoise (s) | e2e (s) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| H100 | eager (main) | 15.789 | 23.157 |
| H100 | **eager (this PR)** | **13.226 (−16.2%)** | **18.245** |
| H100 | torch.compile (issue baseline) | 13.665 | 17.231 |
| H200 | eager (main) | 15.184 | 24.105 |
| H200 | **eager (this PR)** | **13.249 (−12.7%)** | **22.386** |
| H200 | torch.compile (issue baseline) | 25.677 | 32.126 |

Eager now beats compile on H100 for this model (and was already far ahead on H200). Gate log shows zero fallbacks.

## Correctness

- Unit tests (`test_ernie_rope_geglu_fusion.py`): fused RoPE `torch.equal` vs the pre-fusion per-layer chain across (B, S, H, D, rot) combos incl. `rot < head_dim` and non-power-of-two halves; fused GEGLU `torch.equal` vs `up * F.gelu(gate)`; CPU fallback paths return the eager result.
- Runtime: first-call self-verification gates compare fused vs eager on the real activations in-process (`torch.equal`), 0 fallbacks over the full run on both cards.
- End-to-end md5 is **not** a usable metric for this model: two consecutive eager runs of unmodified main differ (`cb961b8f…` vs `d74c6ac5…`, PSNR 8.54 dB — ERNIE has process-level nondeterminism independent of this PR). The fused arm sits at the same distance (PSNR 8.69 dB), i.e. indistinguishable from an independent eager run.

- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Provide accuracy and repro results.

title: [diffusion] Ideogram-4: fuse Qwen3-style RoPE and SwiGLU silu-mul (denoise -5.1% H100 / -4.7% H200, bit-exact)
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

After #34305 removes the per-forward FP8 weight dequant, Ideogram-4's remaining eager-vs-compile gap on H100 is its own elementwise soup (~15% of per-step GPU time in the TP=2 trace):

- the Qwen3-style rotate-half RoPE runs ~6 kernels per projection per layer (four muls, two add/subs, plus the sliced `empty_like` fills in `qwen3_apply_rotary_pos_emb`);
- the SwiGLU pair `F.silu(w1(x)) * w3(x)` makes two full passes over the FFN intermediate — the gate/up projections are separate GEMMs, so the concatenated-input `silu_and_mul` kernels would need an extra full-width `cat` pass that cancels the win.

## What this PR does

Both chains are pure elementwise, so their aten bf16 rounding boundaries can be reproduced exactly:

1. **RoPE** → one Triton kernel per projection (`rope_rotate_half_bitexact.py` — the same file #34306 adds for ERNIE; identical content, merges cleanly in either order). `round(round(q1·cos1) + round(−q2·sin1))` equals the eager `round(round(q1·cos1) − round(q2·sin1))` exactly under round-to-nearest.
2. **SwiGLU** → a new two-input `silu(a) * b` Triton kernel (`silu_mul_bitexact.py`); `tl.sigmoid` matches the aten silu bit-for-bit (verified on 1M random bf16 values), and the multiply rounds once like the eager pair.

Both mount **by default** behind first-call `BitExactFusionGate` self-verification (fused vs eager compared with `torch.equal` on the live tensors, permanent eager fallback on mismatch or unsupported shapes), mirroring the ERNIE mounts in #34306.

## Performance (ideogram4-fp8 preset, TP=2, 1024², seed 42, `--quality=lossless`)

| card | arm | denoise (s) | e2e (s) | output md5 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| H200 | eager (main) | 5.005 | 5.211 | `43c0463e…` |
| H200 | **eager (this PR)** | **4.769 (−4.7%)** | **4.898** | `43c0463e…` (**identical**) |
| H100 | eager (main) | 5.177 | 5.315 | `14f1d205…` |
| H100 | **eager (this PR)** | **4.911 (−5.1%)** | **5.041** | `14f1d205…` (**identical**) |

Gate log shows zero fallbacks. Composes with #34305 (orthogonal: weights vs activations); measured here against unmodified main to isolate this PR's effect.

## Correctness

- Output md5 identical to main on both cards.
- Unit tests (`test_ideogram_rope_swiglu_fusion.py`): fused RoPE `torch.equal` vs `qwen3_apply_rotary_pos_emb` across shape combos; fused SwiGLU `torch.equal` vs `F.silu(a) * b`; CPU fallbacks return the eager result.

title: [diffusion] LTX-2: mount the bit-exact fused modulate at the 8 bare adaLN sites (ltx23-one-stage denoise -2.8% H100 / -2.6% H200)
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

The LTX-2 block leaves eight `x * (1 + scale) + shift` adaLN chains unfused (three kernels each, two of them full passes over the video/audio streams): the four a2v/v2a cross-attention modulates, the two prompt modulates on the LTX-2.3 `cross_attention_adaln` branch, and the two output-layer modulates. The bit-exact fused CUDA modulate (`kernels/ops/diffusion/modulate_scale_shift.py`, already mounted by FLUX and MiniMax-H3) collapses each to one kernel — no quality gate needed by its numerics contract.

## What this PR does

Routes the eight sites through a small `_ltx2_modulate` helper:

- the adaLN rows here are strided `(B, 1, D)` views from `unbind`/`squeeze` of the combined tables, so the helper densifies them to the `(B, D)` layout the kernel expects (a bit-exact copy of tiny tensors);
- per-token modulation rows (`dim 1 > 1`, e.g. per-token timesteps) and unsupported platforms/dtypes keep the eager chain;
- on top of the kernel's own contract, the first fused call self-verifies `torch.equal` against the eager chain (`BitExactFusionGate`, same pattern as the ERNIE/Ideogram mounts) and falls back permanently on any mismatch.

## Performance (seed 42, `--quality=lossless`, 2 GPUs)

| card | preset | arm | denoise (s) | e2e (s) | output md5 |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| H200 | ltx2 (768×512×121f) | eager (main) | 8.012 | 9.098 | `2447032f…` |
| H200 | ltx2 | **this PR** | **7.962 (−0.6%)** | **9.043** | `2447032f…` (**identical**) |
| H200 | ltx23-one-stage | eager (main) | 45.855 / 45.839¹ | 47.214 | n/d¹ |
| H200 | ltx23-one-stage | **this PR** | **44.687 (−2.6%)** | **46.049** | n/d¹ |
| H100 | ltx2 | eager (main) | 6.560 | 7.963 | `984e6885…` |
| H100 | ltx2 | **this PR** | **6.582 (parity)** | **7.983** | `984e6885…` (**identical**) |
| H100 | ltx23-one-stage | eager (main) | 46.385 | 48.167 | n/d¹ |
| H100 | ltx23-one-stage | **this PR** | **45.092 (−2.8%)** | **46.845** | n/d¹ |

The gains concentrate on the LTX-2.3 `cross_attention_adaln` path (more sites engage, larger streams); the `ltx2` preset stays at parity while keeping bit-identical output — the mount is a strict no-regression.

¹ `ltx23-one-stage` is **process-nondeterministic on unmodified main**: two consecutive eager runs (same seed, same GPUs) produce different output md5s with denoise within 0.03% (45.855 vs 45.839 s). Output md5 is therefore not a usable correctness metric for this preset; correctness rests on the in-process first-call `torch.equal` gate (zero fallbacks over full runs on both cards), the md5-identical deterministic `ltx2` preset, and the unit tests.

title: [Kernel] Route large SM90 row/column-scaled FP8 GEMMs to Torch
author: RunFMe
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to [#33275](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33275), which added MiniMax-H3 and its online FP8 transformer path.

The current `sgl_kernel.fp8_scaled_mm` is slower than Torch `_scaled_mm` on the larger H3 dense shapes on SM90. This PR adds both implementations to `BaseFusedOp` and routes shapes using:

`(K >= 5376 and N >= 3584) or (K >= 3584 and M >= 8192)`

The AOT kernel remains the fallback for smaller shapes. The Torch path requires FP8 E4M3FN inputs, BF16 output, FP32 row/column scales, compatible layouts, and no bias.

## Kernel results

H100 80 GB, median of 10 measurements after 5 warmups:

| Operation | M × K × N | SGLang AOT | Torch | Reduction | Torch TFLOP/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Attention QKV, TP1 | 8320 × 5376 × 21504 | 2036.7 µs | 1351.1 µs | 33.66% | 1424 |
| MLP gate/up, TP2 | 8320 × 5376 × 14336 | 1321.9 µs | 896.4 µs | 32.19% | 1431 |
| MLP gate/up, TP1 | 23216 × 5376 × 28672 | 7823.2 µs | 5295.9 µs | 32.30% | 1351 |
| MLP gate/up, TP1 | 15760 × 5376 × 28672 | 4892.1 µs | 3570.9 µs | 27.01% | 1361 |
| MLP down, TP1 | 8320 × 14336 × 5376 | 990.0 µs | 843.9 µs | 14.76% | 1520 |

The sweep covered all 64 H3 dense shapes across TP1/2/4/8 and four production sequence lengths. Torch won 49 shapes, AOT won 15, and the heuristic selected the measured winner for all 64.

## Full MiniMax-H3 result

H100 ×8, TP2/Ulysses4, FP8, FlashAttention, 768×1120 FL2VA request with 49 denoising steps. Medians from three matched runs after two warmups:

| Metric | AOT only | Routed | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Inference | 30.213 s | 27.955 s | -7.47% |
| Wall time | 31.076 s | 29.068 s | -6.46% |
| Peak memory | 35,254 MB | 35,254 MB | unchanged |

The matched outputs were byte-identical. All eight profiler traces confirmed the routed path while retaining AOT for smaller shapes.

## Newer GPUs

I only have access to SM90 hardware, so the capability gate is intentionally limited to SM90. Help benchmarking and tuning these shapes on SM100/SM120 would be appreciated. Torch `_scaled_mm` may also win there

title: [Fix: RL] Snapshot async state-capture outputs before overlap
author: jvmncs
body:
## Motivation

MoE routing decisions are exposable via TopKCapture. This is required for implementing [R3, Rollout Routing Replay](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11370v1) on top of SGLang.

This PR exposes and patches a correctness bug for when when overlap scheduling is enabled and MoE routing indices are captured 

Required conditions:
 - Routed-expert or indexer TopK capture enabled.
 - Normal overlap scheduling enabled—the default.
 - CUDA result copies running on the dedicated copy stream.
 - A subsequent forward reusing the capture buffers before D2H completed.

With overlap scheduling enabled, state-capture results are copied to CPU asynchronously on the result-copy stream while the next model forward may begin. TopkCaptureOutput retained views into the reusable TopK device cache and out_cache_loc buffer. A subsequent forward could therefore mutate those tensors before the asynchronous D2H copy completed. `record_stream` prevents allocator reuse, but cannot prevent in-place mutation of persistent buffers.

## Modifications

Clone TopKCapture output cache + top-k buffers before yielding back to the host. Snapshotting these buffer tensors guarantees the copy stream observes immutable data.

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/unit/test_state_capturer.py` was added to flex the conditions above and demonstrate the issue. It demonstrates garbled TopK, failing on the last commit and passing after.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Benchmarked the added snapshots on an NVIDIA B200 with PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130.

Representative Qwen3.6 DFlash/R3 shape:

- 256 verify tokens (batch_size=32, block size 8)
- 40 MoE layers
- Top-8 routed experts
- 329,728 bytes copied per result
- 10 warmup iterations and 100 measured iterations

| Operation | Median | Mean | P95 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Added device snapshots | 0.01896 ms | 0.01928 ms | 0.02064 ms |
| Existing D2H export, for context | 0.07842 ms | 0.08013 ms | 0.09288 ms |

The patch adds approximately 19 µs per captured forward for this representative shape. It adds no work when state capture
is disabled, and the synchronous non-overlap path is unchanged.
