title: Store mamba prefix-cache checkpoints at the configured SSM state dtype
author: yhyang201
body:
The mamba radix track path snapshots the SSM state at the last chunk boundary of chunk-unaligned sequences so a later prefix-cache hit can restore it. That path read the per-chunk states `h`, which are always stored in the activation dtype (bf16) — so the checkpoint was pinned to bf16 regardless of `--mamba-ssm-dtype`. With the default fp32 pool (and likewise for fp16), a cache hit restored a lower-precision state than a cache miss keeps, making cached and uncached runs numerically diverge. The chunk-aligned path and the in-place final-state path already wrote at the pool dtype; only this intermediate-state path could not honor it.

This PR snapshots the in-kernel fp32 accumulator and casts it once to the pool dtype, so checkpoints on this path faithfully follow `--mamba-ssm-dtype` (float32 / bfloat16 / float16):

- Triton `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` gains `track_state`/`track_chunk_idx`: at the tracked chunk boundary it stores the fp32 accumulator into a per-sequence buffer, and `_track_mamba_state_extend` copies that buffer (instead of the rounded `h`) into the track slots, converting to `ssm_states.dtype` once.
- The Helion prefill kernel gets native support for the same snapshot (separate varlen kernel configs so the tuned non-track configs are untouched).
- New `LinearAttnKernelBase.supports_track_state_snapshot` capability flag; `KDAAttnBackend` asserts it before allocating the snapshot buffer, so a prefill kernel that cannot honor the snapshot fails loudly instead of silently caching unwritten state. FlashKDA's Triton fallback now forwards the track arguments (it previously dropped them), and PTX routes snapshot-carrying batches to its Triton fallback (the native kernel cannot write the buffer).
- The track-slot copy indexes the snapshot buffer by CPU-computed batch rows (`track_ssm_h_batch_src`) — a boolean mask would `nonzero()`-sync the stream once per layer.
- Tests: `test_kda_track_state.py` checks the snapshot matches an fp32 truncated-run reference and is strictly more precise than the bf16 `h` row (Triton and Helion, num_heads 2/16 covering both Helion track configs); `test_mamba_track_state_dtype.py` pins the single cast into each pool dtype (including fp16 not double-rounded through bf16); a CPU bookkeeping test pins every prefill kernel's declaration of the flag; `test_kda_ptx.py` pins the PTX routing.

## Accuracy

Cold vs warm teacher-forced logprob comparison across a prefix-cache resume, in the style of #34808, measured on this PR's head on a single GB300 (TP1, no DCP — this defect needs no page/chunk grid mismatch, only the default fp32 pool and a chunk-unaligned prompt):

```bash
SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct --trust-remote-code \
  --tp-size 1 --page-size 64 \
  --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer \
  --disable-overlap-schedule --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --port 30000
```

Cold scores the full sequence on an empty cache; warm flushes, prefills the prompt alone (both prompts are 34 mod 64, so the resume lands on the tracked intermediate checkpoint), then scores the full sequence again. One setup caveat: with `return_logprob` the prefix match is capped at `logprob_start_len` (`_compute_max_prefix_len`), so the compared window must start past the tracked checkpoint — a window starting below it resumes from an older, aligned checkpoint and does not exercise this path. The "before" row is the same head with the snapshot buffer disabled (`h_track_buf = None`), which reproduces the pre-PR bf16-`h` checkpoint exactly; "aligned" uses chunk-aligned prompts (8256 / 20480), which resume through the final-state path that never had this defect. Every row reproduced identically across 2 rounds.

```
before (bf16 h)  prompt=8226  cached=8192  n_cmp=999 max|dlp|=0.001942
this PR          prompt=8226  cached=8192  n_cmp=999 max|dlp|=0.001661
before (bf16 h)  prompt=20450 cached=20416 n_cmp=999 max|dlp|=0.003692
this PR          prompt=20450 cached=20416 n_cmp=999 max|dlp|=0.002872
aligned          prompt=8256  cached=8256  n_cmp=999 max|dlp|=0.00128
aligned          prompt=20480 cached=20480 n_cmp=999 max|dlp|=0.004311
```

The fixed path's residual equals the aligned path's, so the checkpoint is no longer a visible error source; the ~1e-3 floor itself is not mamba-related — on current main the whole-network resume is not bitwise-stable (the full-attention layers read cached KV pages instead of freshly computed ones). Comparing the before/after warm runs directly — same tree, same cached prefix, only the checkpoint dtype differs — isolates the bf16 checkpoint's own effect: max |Δlogprob| 0.0014 (8226) / 0.0023 (20450), mean ~1e-4. (On the bitwise-stable v0.5.17 branch with different prompts the same defect showed far more visibly: 0.007 → 0.0.) The precision guarantee itself is pinned at the kernel level: `test_kda_track_state.py` shows the snapshot equals an fp32 truncated-run reference while the bf16 `h` row is exactly its lossy rounding.

Prefill-kernel coverage (`--linear-attn-prefill-backend`, same setup, 2 rounds, all cached at the tracked checkpoint):

```
backend     prompt=8226 (cached=8192)   prompt=20450 (cached=20416)
triton      max|dlp|=0.001661           max|dlp|=0.002872
helion      max|dlp|=0.001407           max|dlp|=0.001583
ptx_kda     max|dlp|=0.001661           64/64 greedy tokens identical
nvidia_kda  max|dlp|=0.001661           max|dlp|=0.002872
```

ptx_kda and nvidia_kda match triton exactly on 8226, since their tracked batches route to Triton. ptx_kda's 20450 row uses greedy-token comparison because PTX-native prefill returns None input logprobs (pre-existing, unrelated to this PR). flashkda is not measured here (the `flash_kda` package is unavailable on this box), and `cutedsl` rejects `extra_buffer` loudly with a pre-existing `NotImplementedError`.

title: Skip oow slot freeing under eagle
author: ispobock
body:
## Motivation

#34653 flipped `SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS` to `True`. On a hybrid SWA model with EAGLE speculative decoding this trips the pool invariant checker and kills every TP rank:

```
pool memory leak detected!
[full] total=13510080, available=13509568, evictable=8192, protected=0
[swa]  total=10808064, available=10807552, evictable=1024, protected=0
```

Root cause: in the new-leaf path, `split_pos = swa_evicted_seqlen - result.prefix_len` mixes units. `swa_evicted_seqlen` is a raw-token length while `prefix_len` is in bigram key units under EAGLE, so `split_pos` goes negative (observed `-64` with `page_size 64`) and the leaf is neither tombstoned nor split, while its SWA slots were already returned to the allocator. The tree keeps counting them as evictable, so the accounted total exceeds the pool total.

Note the blast radius is wider than the flag suggests: `registry.py` routes every hybrid SWA model to `UnifiedRadixCache` unconditionally, without `SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE`.

This gates the new default off for the EAGLE family until the unit mismatch is fixed. DSpark, DFlash, non-speculative and hybrid SSM keep the optimization, since `tree_core.is_eagle` is `params.is_eagle and MAMBA not in components`.

## Repro

8xH200, gpt-oss-120b, `--page-size 64 --chunked-prefill-size 16384`, EAGLE3 draft `lmsys/EAGLE3-gpt-oss-120b-bf16`, `bench_one_batch_server --batch-size 1 8 --input-len 8192 --output-len 512`:

| config | result |
| --- | --- |
| EAGLE3, OOW=1 | 8/8 ranks crash, leak detected |
| EAGLE3, OOW=0 | pass |
| no spec, OOW=1 | pass |

`page_size 64` is required to reproduce. At `page_size 1` the page-alignment paths are skipped entirely and the mismatch does not surface.

Nightly hit the same signature on B200: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31710357501

title: [AMD] Add concat_and_cast_mha_k_pad_kernel to support 12-head and enable K3 aiter prefill kernel
author: 1am9trash
body:
With this PR, K3 can use the AITER prefill kernel, but must disable FP8 kernel, which does not support 12 heads. Two changes to the server cmd (full cmd in the description above) - `export SGLANG_AITER_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=0` - `--prefill-attention-backend aiter` ## Motivation The triton `extend_attention_fwd` is much slower than the aiter kernel for MLA prefill. - Triton kernel: `extend_attention_fwd()` in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/extend_attention.py` - AITER kernel: `_fmha_fwd_bf16_opus_fwd` in `aiter/ops/mha.py`, calling `gqa_d192_v128_kernel` kernel K3 at TP8 gives 12 heads per GPU, so the existing `concat_and_cast_mha_k_kernel` hits arange's range must be a power of 2. title: Revert "[Fix] Disable --enable-symm-mem under CUDA graphs on Kimi hybrid models"

title: [NPU] [Diffusion] Fix critical Ascend NPU Diffusion regression/bugs & restore 2-NPU CI testcase
author: OrangeRedeng
body:
## Motivation

Restore Ascend/NPU packed Ring Attention, 2-NPU diffusion CI suite, fix NPU correctness, runtime, and CI regressions exposed by recent Ring, SRT-CLIP, residency, and MOVA changes.

After [#35004](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35004), diffusion can import SRT CLIP code and execute SRT `init_npu_backend()`. Importing `torch_npu.contrib.transfer_to_npu` inside a native NPU diffusion process globally rewrites CUDA-facing APIs/device arguments and can alter runtime feature detection and kernel selection. `allow_internal_format=True` is also known to regress unquantized diffusion performance; the earlier Wan regression in [#20533](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/20533), fixed by [#20684](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20684), increased `DecodingStage` from **6.1889 s to 11.76 s (+90.0%, 1.90x slower)**.

The packed-attention implementation is extracted from the Ascend work in [#33569](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33569).

## Modifications

- **Packed varlen / Ring Attention.** [#33327](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33327) extended Qwen to tail-padded Ring and fixed `u=1, r>1` replicated-token semantics, exposing the shared packed `flash_attn_varlen_func` path on NPU. Add an Ascend implementation backed by `npu_fused_infer_attention_score` (`TND`) with independent Q/K packed lengths, boundary validation, empty/non-contiguous handling, LSE normalization, and `AscendFlashAttnImpl.forward_varlen`. Unsupported FlashAttention options fail explicitly.

- **Diffusion NPU runtime isolation.** Keep the SRT CUDA-compatibility layer out of diffusion: when `sglang.multimodal_gen` is loaded, do not import `torch_npu.contrib.transfer_to_npu` and do not enable `torch_npu.npu.config.allow_internal_format`. Preserve the existing `torch.cuda.is_available=False` re-mock on the SRT path after `transfer_to_npu`. `jit_compile=False` remains unchanged.

- **MOVA 2-NPU correctness.** [#31453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31453) left a contiguous-layout assumption after attention. Multi-NPU attention may return a non-contiguous tensor, so use `reshape()` instead of `view()`.

- **Host-memory accounting.** [#35641](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35641) introduced storage-based module sizing for host-memory budgeting. Skip tensors whose storage access raises `RuntimeError` instead of failing memory planning; add focused unit coverage.

- **NPU CI / GT.**
  - Restore the 2-NPU diffusion suite on `linux-aarch64-a3-800t-16`.
  - Split both 1-NPU and 2-NPU suites into two partitions.
  - Run GT generation on the A3-800T runner families.
  - Make GT jobs check out the requested `workflow_dispatch` ref.
  - Retry transient HTTP/image-decoding failures while downloading GT.
  - Update the NPU GT revision to `8e3d717e65fb87339c2974382a092a731669f884`.

- **NPU dependencies.** Pin `sgl-kernel-npu` to `2026.8.13` and install the packaged `attentions` wheel in NPU CI/Docker; update release Docker pins accordingly.

- **Performance baselines.** Refresh affected FLUX.2 text-encoding, ERNIE timestep-preparation, and LTX-2 connector/decoding baselines plus partition-duration estimates for the current A3-800T / auto-residency environment. Related residency policy: [#34615](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34615). These are CI baseline updates, not algorithmic speedups.

## Accuracy Tests

- NPU diffusion GT was regenerated successfully after the Ring semantic changes and A3-800T CI migration: [Generate Diffusion CI Ground Truth #32478548704](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32478548704).
- Qwen Ring keeps the corrected semantics from #33327; no consistency thresholds are relaxed.
- Runtime isolation changes backend initialization/dispatch only; #20684 reported no accuracy impact from disabling the problematic internal-format behavior.
- The restored 2-NPU suite exercises the packed Ring path.
- Invalid-storage host-memory handling has dedicated unit coverage.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The runtime fix prevents diffusion from inheriting SRT's global CUDA-compatibility monkey patches and `allow_internal_format=True`.

title: [Perf] Hoist DSv4 draft-extend SWA write locs; unify SWA graph buffer naming
author: hnyls2002
body:
Hoist the DSv4 draft-extend SWA write-loc translate out of the captured graph, and align the remaining backends on the shared buffer conventions.

## DSv4 draft-extend
- Previously the out-graph metadata init left `swa_out_cache_loc` unset, so every SWA layer's `store_cache` recorded a `full_to_swa_index_mapping[out_cache_loc]` translate inside the graph (one per layer per replay).
- `init_cuda_graph_state` now pre-allocates `cuda_graph_swa_out_cache_loc` (draft runner only); the metadata init refills it outside the graph (zeroed tail, `[:num_tokens]` view) and stamps it, so the captured `store_cache` takes the cached path -- one translate per step, off the replay.
- Eager miss (no graph state / oversized batch) stamps a fresh per-step translate instead of falling back to per-layer translation at store time; capture always fits the pre-sized buffer, so it never records a temporary tensor's address.

## Cross-backend alignment
- Rename `swa_out_cache_loc_buf` -> `cuda_graph_swa_out_cache_loc` in the flashattention and ascend backends; the SWA write-target graph buffer now has one name across triton / trtllm_mha / flashinfer / aiter / fa3 / ascend / dsv4.
- XPU: read `full_to_swa_index_mapping` live from the pool instead of caching the tensor ref at init; drop a redundant pool re-assignment.

title: [MoE] Gather the cutlass MoE activation and its scales in one launch
author: yuan-luo
body: ## Motivation The fp8 blockwise CUTLASS MoE quantizes its activation once and then replicates rows per routed expert, so the gather it performs walks a `dst2src` map of `m * topk` entries. Until now it walked that map twice: one `shuffle_rows` launch for the fp8 values and a second one for the fp32 group scales. The second walk moves a thirty-second of the bytes the first one does — `k // 128` fp32 against `k` fp8 — so as a launch of its own it is almost entirely latency. That is exactly the cost that matters where this path spends its time: at low concurrency the whole gather is a few tens of KB, and the launch is the work. Where the gather sits, between quantizing the activation once and the first grouped GEMM: ## Modifications A triton kernel that walks the map once and writes both tensors, registered as a TRITON `KernelSpec` (`op="moe.shuffle_rows_with_scales"`) per RFC #29630. The grid is `(dst_row, k_tile)`; the tile that owns column 0 also carries that row's scales, which are 1/32 the width and do not deserve a launch of their own. The non-mxfp8 path calls it instead of the two `shuffle_rows`. The SM100 mxfp8 ES branch gathers a bf16 activation through a different kernel and is untouched. The two blue arrows are the point: `token 0` is read twice because it routes to two experts, which is why the gather moves `topk` times the rows the quantizer ever saw. The narrow cell trailing each row is that row's scales, and it travels under the same `a_map` — that shared map is the whole reason one kernel can produce both. Rows are copied as bytes rather than as fp8 — the values are never decoded — so the kernel works for any 1-byte dtype and cannot perturb them. Row bases are computed in int64, matching the CUDA `shuffle_rows` it replaces, since `rows * k` overflows int32 well inside the shapes this path serves. The kernel also masks its tails. The CUDA `shuffle_rows` takes its element count as `num_cols / elems_per_thread` with no remainder handling, so it only moves a whole fp32 scale row when `(k // 128) % 4 == 0`; every `k` that is a multiple of 512 is unaffected either way, which covers the shapes this path serves today. **mxfp8 MoE is not affected by this PR.** It will be addressed in the next PR. ## Accuracy Tests The result is **bit-identical** to the pair of calls it replaces, by construction rather than by tolerance. `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_shuffle_rows_with_scales.py` (new) checks that three ways, on B200: against plain torch advanced indexing as the oracle, against the two `shuffle_rows` calls for drop-in equivalence, and on the zero-row short circuit. Comparisons are made on integer views of both tensors — a random fp8 byte pattern is a NaN often enough that `torch.equal` on the float view would report a difference where the bytes agree, and bytes are what the kernel promises. The shape list includes `k = 896` (7 scale groups), which the CUDA reference cannot express because of the remainder above, so that case is checked against the torch oracle only. Maps are drawn with `randint` and therefore contain duplicate source rows, which is the normal case here: a token is replicated once per expert it routes to. ``` 22 passed, 6 warnings in 16.02s ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/moe/bench_shuffle_rows_with_scales.py` (new) benchmarks the fused kernel against the two launches it replaces. On B200 (sm100, torch 2.11.0+cu130, triton 3.6.0), topk 8: | k | tokens | rows | two launches | fused | speedup | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 7168 | 1 | 8 | 3.06 us | 1.31 us | 2.33x | | 2048 | 1 | 8 | 2.47 us | 1.42 us | 1.74x | | 7168 | 8 | 64 | 3.25 us | 1.60 us | 2.03x | | 7168 | 64 | 512 | 4.30 us | 2.10 us | 2.05x | | 7168 | 1024 | 8192 | 23.78 us | 11.14 us | 2.14x | ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32585586997](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32585586997) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #32585586727](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32585586727) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :x: [Run #32585586801](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32585586801)

title: Fix DSpark CUDA graph replay with MegaMoE TP attention
author: BJWang-ant
body: ## Motivation DSpark speculative decoding does not work correctly with MegaMoE when attention tensor parallelism is enabled. The combination exposes several related issues: 1. DSpark next-token layers may call the MoE FFN path without `input_ids` or `input_ids_global`. 2. The TP-attention-to-A2A scatter path unconditionally splits these token ID tensors, causing: ```text AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'tensor_split' ``` 3.DSpark constructs its draft ForwardBatch manually, but CUDA graph eligibility and non-padded token metadata were only populated inside the DP-MoE synchronization branch. 4.Without DP attention, the function returns before filling this metadata: - Draft CUDA graphs are captured but rejected during replay. - After propagating graph eligibility, replay fails because num_token_non_padded is missing. 5.Creating a new CUDA scalar for num_token_non_padded on every decode step introduces an unexpected host-to-device copy and stream synchronization. ## Root Cause When MegaMoE is used with attention TP, hidden states are temporarily scattered along the token dimension before MoE execution: ```text Replicated attention-TP token batch -> local token scatter -> MegaMoE -> attention-TP all-gather -> replicated token batch ``` DSpark next-token layers are not hash-routed and intentionally do not carry token IDs. However, the scatter path assumed that both token ID tensors were always present. In addition, MegaMoE CUDA graph replay requires metadata that was previously treated as DP-MoE-only metadata: - can_run_dp_cuda_graph - num_token_non_padded - num_token_non_padded_cpu Although can_run_dp_cuda_graph is named after DP, it is also used by the gathered-buffer path required by MegaMoE attention-TP execution. ## Changes 1. Support missing token IDs in the TP-attention A2A scatter path Update _run_moe_ffn_dp_sync() to accept optional token ID tensors: ```python input_ids: Optional[torch.Tensor] input_ids_global: Optional[torch.Tensor] ``` Only split them when they are present: ```python if input_ids is not None: input_ids = input_ids.tensor_split(s)[r].contiguous() if input_ids_global is not None: input_ids_global = input_ids_global.tensor_split(s)[r].contiguous() ``` Hidden-state scattering remains unchanged. Regular target layers that provide token IDs preserve their existing behavior. 2. Propagate CUDA graph eligibility to the DSpark draft batch Copy the scheduler batch eligibility before the DP-MoE early return: ```python forward_batch.can_run_dp_cuda_graph = batch.can_run_dp_cuda_graph ``` This allows the already-captured DSpark draft CUDA graph to be replayed when MegaMoE requires the attention-TP gathered-buffer path. 3. Populate non-padded token metadata outside the DP-MoE branch Calculate the actual draft token count before returning from the non-DP path: ```python num_tokens = forward_batch.input_ids.numel() forward_batch.num_token_non_padded_cpu = num_tokens ``` The device-side value is also populated when required. This is necessary because CUDA graph buckets may contain padding. For example, with TP2, 17 requests and 5 draft tokens per request produce 85 real tokens, while replay may use a 90-token graph bucket. The graph runner needs the real token count to determine the valid token range on each rank. DP-specific global token metadata remains guarded by _dp_moe_sync; this change does not enable DP synchronization for non-DP configurations. 4. Reuse a persistent device scalar Allocate the device-side non-padded token counter once in DraftBlockProposer.__init__(): ```python self._num_token_non_padded = torch.empty( (1,), dtype=torch.int32, device=self.draft_model_runner.device, ) ``` Update it on each step with: ```python self._num_token_non_padded.fill_(num_tokens) ``` This avoids creating a new CUDA tensor and performing a host-to-device scalar copy on every decode iteration. The previous code did capture the cuda-graphs of both "draft" and "verify", but during the actual runtime, only the cuda-graph of "verify" could be replayed. This PR has fixed the aforementioned issue. It fetches two cuda-graphs and during the runtime phase, it can hit both of the cuda-graphs. ## performer： ### using no-megamoe: ### using meggamoe without this pr: ###this pr with megamoe: --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #34097986731](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34097986731) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #34097986464](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34097986464) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #34097986611](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34097986611)

title: Suppress expected FlashInfer TRT-LLM workspace warnings
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

FlashInfer TRT-LLM warns on every oversized all-reduce during prefill CUDA graph capture, even though SGLang safely falls back. One startup produced **28,032 repeated warnings / 56,064 warning lines** like this:

```text
Workspace is insufficient for problem size. Workspace validation failed:
  - token_num (8192) * hidden_dim (2880) exceeds workspace max_token_num (2048) * hidden_dim (2880). This may cause Illegal Memory Access.
```

This skips the noisy TRT-LLM validator only when cached workspace metadata already proves the request cannot fit. It preserves valid total-capacity reuse and FP32 Lamport compatibility, while leaving MNNVL's validator untouched.

Added focused regression coverage and confirmed on 4x H100 with TP4: full prefill graph capture through 8192 tokens completed without the warnings, while TRT-LLM fusion stayed enabled.

title: Apply latest DeepEP branch
author: Fridge003
body:
## Summary

- configure `NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH` before CUDA DeepEP low-latency buffer initialization
- enforce `max(existing value, 1024, 2 * (num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank + 1))`
- preserve larger user-provided values and leave NPU and normal DeepEP paths unchanged
- force reinstall `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.30.7` in CUDA 13 CI and the main CUDA 13 image; CUDA 12 remains unchanged
- bump the runtime dependency to `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1`

## Motivation

DeepEP v2 requires NCCL Gin from NCCL 2.30.7 and an NVSHMEM QP depth of at least twice the low-latency dispatch capacity plus two. For the DeepSeek V4 configuration with 1024 dispatch tokens per rank, the required QP depth is 2050, which is larger than NVSHMEM default of 1024.

## Validation

- SGLang pre-commit hooks passed for all changed files
- PyPI reports `sgl-deep-ep` 0.1.1 as the latest release with 8 wheel files
- CI dependency script passes shell syntax validation

title: [diffusion][kernel] Accelerate Sana BCG with bit-exact conv post-processing
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- fuse Sana GLUMB convolution bias + SiLU and bias + GLU post-processing into bit-exact Triton kernels during BCG capture/replay
- reuse the shared bit-exact residual-gate-add kernel at the attention and MLP residual sites
- materialize the patch-token layout once instead of making every downstream LayerNorm copy the same transposed view
- verify each fused convolution path on first sight and permanently fall back to eager if the platform is not bit-exact

## Why

The B300 profile showed that Sana BCG was launch-bound after the existing LayerNorm fusion. Repeated `add`, `copy`, `mul`, activation, and gating operations around the GLUMB convolutions accounted for most of the remaining gap to `torch.compile`.

The new kernels preserve the BF16 materialization boundaries used by eager PyTorch, so `quality=lossless` output remains bit-exact.

## B300 performance

Measured in the 2026-08-14 full sweep from #21 on one NVIDIA B300, Sana 1.5 1.6B at the preset's default 1024px workload:

| Mode | Denoise | E2E |
|---|---:|---:|
| eager | 0.350 s | 0.476 s |
| eager + BCG, before this optimization | ~0.333 s | — |
| eager + BCG, this change | **0.233 s** | **0.363 s** |
| `torch.compile` | 0.272 s | 0.388 s |

The optimized BCG denoise latency is about 14.2% lower than `torch.compile` and about 30% lower than the profiled pre-optimization BCG path.

## Validation

- added CUDA tests for BF16 channels-last bias-SiLU and bias-GLU; both require `torch.equal` against the eager chain
- full pre-commit and CI registry validation pass on the rebased branch
- Python syntax compilation passes
- original isolated B300 candidate: `099844c2c`; this PR is rebuilt on current `main`

title: [diffusion] Enable breakable CUDA graphs for LTX-2.3
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- register Lightricks/LTX-2.3 model IDs and `LTX23PipelineConfig` for breakable CUDA graphs
- keep RoPE coordinate creation outside graph capture for legacy one-stage and two-stage paths
- extract the existing coordinate preparation into a focused helper and add coverage for disabled, missing, and precomputed coordinates
- add an explicit BCG registration test for both LTX-2 and LTX-2.3

## Why

LTX-2.3 uses the same capturable DiT path as LTX-2, but the support gate still rejected its model IDs and pipeline config. Its legacy path can also create RoPE coordinates from host data inside the model forward; doing that during capture causes an illegal unpinned host-to-device copy. title: perf: overlap Qwen shared expert with DeepEP routed experts
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

For Qwen MoE models using CUDA and DeepEP, the shared expert currently runs on the default stream before the routed-expert path. This serializes two independent computations and leaves an available alternate stream unused.

This PR adds an opt-in path that overlaps the Qwen shared expert with routed-expert/DeepEP execution.

## Modifications

- Add `SGLANG_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP` (default: `false`).
- When enabled on CUDA, enqueue the shared expert on `alt_stream`, execute the routed-expert path on the current stream, and wait on an event immediately before accumulating the shared output.
- When breakable CUDA graph is active, skip this optimization and retain the existing serial shared-expert path; cross-segment overlap across the eager DeepEP break is out of scope.
- Document the new environment variable.

## Accuracy Tests

The accuracy evidence below was collected on predecessor `38f714d28e1fa01ae5b1ce38ce576373b8293722`, based on upstream main `0c072235f44fce4b89e594c2d3348e4f48e774b8`, with a clean source tree. Current head `76815b3766deb3a3c9aceef1cb346093f691d976` differs only by making breakable CUDA graph use the pre-existing serial fallback instead of an alternate-stream path with an immediate wait; the non-breakable overlap implementation measured below is unchanged.

Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 8x GB300, FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, TP8/DP8/EP8, NEXTN draft length 6, DeepEP low-latency mode, 200 GSM8K examples, 5 shots, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, and top-k 20. The run used natural NEXTN acceptance.

| Metric | Result | Gate |
|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K score | **0.990** (200/200) | >= 0.95 |
| Request-weighted mean accepted length | **4.6102** (1,379 decode-log rows; request weight 11,625) | > 3.3 |
| Evaluation latency | 95.646 s | -- |
| Evaluation output throughput | 5,621.1 token/s | -- |

All eight ranks completed target verify CUDA graph capture, followed by draft decode and draft extend graph capture. The job completed successfully with exit code 0. Breakable CUDA graph is now intentionally excluded from this optimization, and no performance gain is claimed for that fallback.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The performance A/B exercised the same overlap mechanism on the benchmark stack before this upstream-main port. The upstream-main commit listed in the accuracy section was validated separately through CUDA graph capture and GSM8K.

The end-to-end A/B comparison used the same configuration and differed only in the job name and `SGLANG_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP=true`.

Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 24x GB300 disaggregated serving (four TP4/DP4/EP4 prefill replicas and one TP8/DP8/EP8 decode replica), FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, NEXTN draft length 6, concurrency 896, fixed accepted length 4.8, and a 3,600-second AgentX replay.

| AIPerf metric | Disabled | Enabled | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total token throughput | 2,649,331.82 token/s | 2,705,912.48 token/s | **+2.14%** |
| Output token throughput | 25,466.20 token/s | 26,000.99 token/s | **+2.10%** |
| Request throughput | 27.980 request/s | 28.516 request/s | **+1.91%** |
| Mean inter-token latency | 18.220 ms | 17.623 ms | **-3.28%** |
| Theoretical prefix-cache hit | 95.433% | 95.452% | +0.020 pp |

These are end-to-end AIPerf results without profiler instrumentation.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). The GPU-only stream path is covered by the end-to-end graph-capture and accuracy tests above.

title: [Perf] Restore the 16-token router GEMM threshold on SM10X
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

#29470 dropped `max_router_gemm_tokens` from 16 to 4 on SM10X. That doesn't hold anymore: I re-ran its sweep and the JIT `dsv3_router_gemm` wins every `M` up to 12, ties 13-16.

Likely #29783, which swapped the fallback it was measured against (`F.linear` → `linear_bf16_fp32`). Unverified.

Speculative decoding never gets the fast path: the router sees `M = batch_size * num_draft_tokens`, so EAGLE 5/1/6 is at `M = 6` from concurrency 1. Plain decode keeps it to concurrency 4.

So put it back to the kernel's compiled `1..16` range, the same bound `linear_with_fused_a_gemm` already uses. Literal revert of #29470.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

4x GB300, `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`, TP4, `--quantization modelopt_fp4`.

### M sweep, current main

Not an exact replication of #29470's: all 16 points instead of 8, and 8192/1024 instead of 1K/1K. No MTP, so router `M == concurrency`. WITH = JIT forced on, WITHOUT = cuBLAS forced on.

| M | ITL WITH | ITL WITHOUT | ΔITL | tok/s WITH | tok/s WITHOUT | Δtok/s | winner |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|:---|
| 1 | 6.63 | 6.85 | −3.21% | 144.13 | 140.08 | +2.89% | JIT |
| 2 | 7.21 | 7.54 | −4.38% | 256.41 | 246.73 | +3.92% | JIT |
| 3 | 8.18 | 8.51 | −3.88% | 332.53 | 321.75 | +3.35% | JIT |
| 4 | 8.11 | 8.44 | −3.91% | 435.57 | 421.00 | +3.46% | JIT |
| 5 | 9.28 | 9.53 | −2.62% | 470.70 | 461.76 | +1.94% | JIT |
| 6 | 9.56 | 9.80 | −2.45% | 536.96 | 527.81 | +1.73% | JIT |
| 7 | 9.87 | 10.09 | −2.18% | 599.41 | 588.15 | +1.91% | JIT |
| 8 | 9.81 | 10.04 | −2.29% | 672.72 | 660.05 | +1.92% | JIT |
| 9 | 10.81 | 10.94 | −1.19% | 684.09 | 679.03 | +0.75% | JIT |
| 10 | 11.10 | 11.23 | −1.16% | 730.54 | 724.47 | +0.84% | JIT |
| 11 | 11.40 | 11.51 | −0.96% | 773.95 | 767.62 | +0.82% | JIT |
| 12 | 11.31 | 11.39 | −0.70% | 834.13 | 829.49 | +0.56% | JIT |
| 13 | 12.20 | 12.18 | +0.16% | 837.63 | 839.08 | −0.17% | tie |
| 14 | 12.47 | 12.42 | +0.40% | 872.36 | 875.12 | −0.32% | tie |
| 15 | 12.67 | 12.63 | +0.32% | 909.12 | 911.54 | −0.27% | tie |
| 16 | 12.57 | 12.55 | +0.16% | 960.27 | 961.61 | −0.14% | tie |

Against what #29470 reported:

| M | #29470, Jun 2026 | current main |
|---:|:---|:---|
| 1-4 | JIT +1.0 to 2.1% | JIT +2.9 to 3.9% |
| 5 | **cuBLAS +1.8%** | **JIT +1.9%** |
| 8 | **cuBLAS +1.7%** | **JIT +1.9%** |
| 12 | **cuBLAS +1.7%** | **JIT +0.6%** |
| 16 | **cuBLAS +3.4%** | tie |

Each column is JIT against the fallback of its day (`F.linear` then, `linear_bf16_fp32` now), so this isn't a controlled A/B against their baseline.

Every router call in a run sees the same `M`, so this grid derives any threshold `T`: `perf(T, M) = WITH(M) if M <= T else WITHOUT(M)`. `T = 16` wins or ties everywhere.

### E2E, speculative decoding

```
sglang serve \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --model-path nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 5 \

```

```
python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
  --backend sglang \
  --model nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 \
  --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --num-prompts 8 \
  --max-concurrency 1 \
  --warmup-requests 64 \
  --flush-cache
```

19 runs over 7 server launches (9 before / 10 after):

| metric | before (M=6 → cuBLAS) | after (M=6 → JIT) | Δ |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|
| Benchmark duration | 17.041 s | **16.681 s** | **−2.11%** |
| Output token throughput | 480.76 tok/s | **491.13 tok/s** | **+2.16%** |
| Mean E2E latency | 2127.7 ms | **2082.7 ms** | **−2.11%** |

title: [Quantization] Fix GPTQ scheme attachment broken by LinearBase.scheme default
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

#29328 added a class-level `scheme = None` to `LinearBase`, turning GPTQ's `if not hasattr(layer, "scheme")` guard into a no-op — the scheme never gets built and every GPTQ checkpoint dies on load with `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'create_weights'`. The probe becomes `layer.scheme is None`, which makes that default load-bearing, so it's declared on the other two bases a GPTQ method can be handed (`VocabParallelEmbedding` for a quantized `ParallelLMHead`, `FusedMoE` for gptq_marlin MoE) and `FusedMoE`'s two `hasattr` weight-loader reads flip with it — leaving those would set `method = None` for every unquantized and fp8 MoE layer on reload.

title: [MoE] Add FlashInfer SM90 MXFP4 W4A8 CUTLASS MoE
author: yuan-luo
body:
## Motivation

SGLang currently supports FlashInfer's SM90 MXFP4 W4A16 CUTLASS MoE path, which was introduced in SGLang #24816 on top of FlashInfer [#3084](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3084). FlashInfer [#3738](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738) adds a different Hopper path that dynamically quantizes activations to FP8 and runs MXFP4-weight x FP8-activation MoE GEMMs using Humming-style pre-MMA E8M0 scale fusion.

This PR wires that path into SGLang as an explicit opt-in:

```bash
--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8
```

The existing `default` and `bf16` behavior is unchanged.

Related work:

- SGLang https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24816
- FlashInfer https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738

### FlashInfer version requirement

This integration intentionally targets the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431, where the FC1 and FC2 residual scales are FP32 tensors in local-expert order with shape `[num_local_experts]`. FlashInfer reuses its internal expert permutation to map those scales to routed rows, including global-to-local expert mapping under EP.

The original #3738 ABI briefly shipped before being reverted from FlashInfer 0.6.17 by #4411. It required downstream runtimes to construct routed-row residual tensors during every forward. SGLang does not support that older ABI.

The new option therefore requires both:

- `flashinfer-python >= 0.6.18`
- `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming`

SGLang currently pins FlashInfer 0.6.17. This PR does not change that global pin. With 0.6.17, selecting `fp8` fails immediately with an actionable error, while all existing FlashInfer paths remain compatible. The dependency, cubin, and JIT-cache pins should be upgraded together in a follow-up change.

GPU validation for this PR used FlashInfer 0.6.18 built from commit `8044d94bf9acc5369857baf88d28906bb32bf264`, which contains the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431.

## Modifications

### Runtime selection and compatibility

- Add `fp8` to `--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision`.
- Select the new path only for `flashinfer_mxfp4` on SM90.
- Keep W4A16 as the default SM90 behavior.
- Reject the SM90-specific `fp8` option on SM100 and SM120 to avoid confusing it with their existing MXFP8 activation paths.
- Require the corrected FlashInfer 0.6.18+ API instead of accepting the older routed-row residual ABI.
- Pass `use_wfp4afp8_humming=True` only when the new path is selected. The keyword is omitted completely for FlashInfer 0.6.17 compatibility.

### Weight preprocessing

- Use `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming` for both FC1 and FC2 during post-load processing.
- Store the folded interleaved weight scales produced by FlashInfer.
- Store `residual * 64` as one FP32 value per local expert for FC1 and FC2.
- Preserve GPT-OSS gate/up layout conversion and its existing padding rules.
- Fill synthetic E8M0 scale padding from an existing scale in the same expert, preventing padding from changing that expert's min/max exponent range.
- Support both the GPT-OSS MXFP4 quantization path and the DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 expert path.

### Kernel invocation

Construct the five Humming quant-scale slots expected by the corrected FlashInfer API:

1. FC1 folded weight block scales
2. FC1 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation
3. Reserved scalar FC2 activation scale
4. FC2 folded weight block scales
5. FC2 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation

The existing TP/EP topology is forwarded to FlashInfer so it can map global expert IDs to the corresponding local residual scale.

### Tests and benchmark

- Extend the registered SM90 MXFP4 test suite with:
  - GPT-OSS preprocessing checks against the FlashInfer helper
  - five-scale kernel invocation and direct FlashInfer comparison
  - aligned and non-aligned hidden/intermediate dimensions
  - padding invariance for per-expert residual scales
  - EP rank with global expert IDs
  - DeepSeek-V4 preprocessing
  - fail-fast behavior on FlashInfer versions before 0.6.18
- Extend the manual SM90 benchmark to compare:
  - SGLang Marlin W4A16
  - FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A16
  - FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A8
- Update the server-argument documentation.

## Accuracy Tests

The registered SM90 MXFP4 suite passed:

```bash
python -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_mxfp4_sm90_cutlass.py -v
```

```text
18 passed, 1 skipped
```

The DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 checkpoint was launched with:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 4 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
  --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 \
  --enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000
```

DeepSeek-V4 accuracy was evaluated using the same 200-example GSM8K setup as SGLang #24816. Both runs used the same TP=4 configuration, dataset, sampling parameters, and server options; only `--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision` changed between `bf16` and `fp8`.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/sgl-workspace/sglang_dev/python \
python -m sglang.test.run_eval \
  --port 30000 \
  --eval-name gsm8k \
  --num-examples 200 \
  --api chat \
  --max-tokens 1024 \
  --num-threads 32 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --gsm8k-data-path /tmp/gsm8k-test.jsonl
```

| MoE precision | GSM8K score | Total latency | Output throughput |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| W4A16 (`bf16`) | 0.985 | 37.301 s | 611.809 token/s |
| W4A8 (`fp8`) | 0.985 | 32.952 s | 683.574 token/s |

W4A8 preserved the W4A16 GSM8K score while reducing evaluation latency by 11.7% and increasing output throughput by 11.7%. The score also matches the 0.985 W4A16 result reported in SGLang #24816. 

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The downstream benchmark uses the GPT-OSS-like shape from SGLang #24816: hidden size 4096, intermediate size 2048, 256 experts, and top-k 6. Each FlashInfer path was fully autotuned, followed by 5 warmup iterations and 30 timed iterations. The remaining token shapes were run in parallel with one independent shape per H20 GPU; each W4A16/W4A8 pair ran on the same GPU.

The benchmark can be reproduced with FlashInfer 0.6.18+:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python:/path/to/flashinfer \
FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \
python test/manual/layers/moe/bench_mxfp4_sm90_kernels.py
```

Results on NVIDIA H20-3e:

| Tokens | CUTLASS W4A16 median (min) | CUTLASS W4A8 median (min) | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | 0.275 ms (0.272 ms) | 0.164 ms (0.162 ms) | 1.68x |
| 16 | 0.842 ms (0.840 ms) | 0.463 ms (0.460 ms) | 1.82x |
| 64 | 1.894 ms (1.892 ms) | 1.037 ms (1.019 ms) | 1.83x |
| 256 | 2.410 ms (2.403 ms) | 1.478 ms (1.383 ms) | 1.63x |
| 1024 | 3.912 ms (3.906 ms) | 2.093 ms (1.999 ms) | 1.87x |
| 2048 | 6.973 ms (6.954 ms) | 3.394 ms (3.384 ms) | 2.05x |
| 4096 | 13.013 ms (12.971 ms) | 6.295 ms (6.210 ms) | 2.07x |
| 8192 | 25.624 ms (25.546 ms) | 12.308 ms (12.293 ms) | 2.08x |

FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A8 was faster at every measured token count, with speedups ranging from 1.63x to 2.08x. The gain reaches approximately 2.0x for token counts of 2048 and above. The GSM8K latency and throughput numbers above provide an end-to-end serving sanity check, but the kernel benchmark is the more controlled performance comparison because generated output lengths are not fixed.

## Scope and Limitations

- The implementation is SM90-only.
- It is opt-in and does not change the default W4A16 path.
- A coordinated FlashInfer 0.6.18 dependency update is required before production enablement.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the repository test conventions.
- [x] Update server-argument documentation.
- [x] Run the registered tests on an SM90 GPU with FlashInfer 0.6.18.
- [x] Add a DeepSeek-V4 end-to-end smoke-test result.
- [ ] Upgrade the FlashInfer Python, cubin, and JIT-cache pins together in a coordinated follow-up change.

title: [AMD] DSv4: fuse the qk-norm-rope pair on the MTP target-verify path
author: karverma-amd
body:
## Summary

On the DeepSeek-V4 unified-KV path, the fused qk-norm-rope kernel is wired to
decode only. MTP **target-verify** falls back to running the same work as two
separate launches per layer — `sglang::fused_q_norm_rope` for q and
`sglang::fused_norm_rope` for kv — which is 122 launches per verify step across
the 61 target layers.

This PR routes target-verify through the same fused kernel, **with the cache
store left off**.

The store half deliberately does not move. Decode is a 1-source consumer: the
ring holds everything, so writing it before attention is required. Target-verify
is **2-source** — attention reads history from the ring and takes the current
chunk as `k`/`v` so the draft tokens stay causally masked against one another.
Writing the current chunk into the ring ahead of attention makes those tokens
indistinguishable from history, and every draft position then attends to all of
them regardless of order. Fusing the store as well drops GSM8K from 0.950 to
0.027 while looking like a ~7% throughput win, because it skips exactly the work
correctness depends on. Only the norm+RoPE half is sound, and that is what this
PR fuses.

## Modifications

- **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`** (`MQALayer._forward_prepare`)
  - `do_fused_store` now also admits `is_target_verify()` when the new gate is
    on. The kernel is token-indexed (`q`, `kv` and `positions` are all length M),
    so a verify batch carrying several draft tokens per request is a shape it
    already handles.
  - On that path the kernel is called with `swa_cache`/`swa_loc` left as `None`,
    so it performs q-norm+RoPE and kv-norm+RoPE and stores nothing.
    `get_unified_swa_loc` is not called at all — it exists solely to address a
    store this path no longer performs.
  - `kv` is returned instead of being set to `None`, so the caller's existing
    contract drives the rest unchanged: `attn_k = kv` gives attention the real
    current-chunk source, and `save_kv_cache = kv is not None` makes the backend
    write the ring after attention, exactly as the unfused path did.
  - `kv` is materialised with `.contiguous()` first: it is a strided slice of
    `qkv_a`, and the ring store requires a contiguous buffer. The unfused path
    pays the identical copy inside `_compute_kv_bf16`, so this is parity, not
    added overhead.
- **`python/sglang/srt/environ.py`** — new `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY`
  (default on). Set to 0 to fall back to the unfused chain on the verify path.

Decode, prefill and the non-unified paths are untouched.

### Kernel-level evidence

Per target-verify forward, from graphs-off traces segmented by the 61
`DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` frames (TP8, 8k/1k, conc 16, rank 0). `fused_q_norm_rope`
and `fused_norm_rope` both go to zero and one `_fused_qk_norm_rope_store_kernel`
replaces them; no other kernel is added.

| layer type | launches/fwd (base → patched) | GPU us/fwd excl. collective |
|---|---|---|
| CSA (30 layers) | 1920.0 → 1800.0 | 15779 → 15488 (−1.8%) |
| HCA (31 layers) | 1526.8 → 1410.5 | 12385 → 12014 (−3.0%) |

"excl. collective" is the number to read: `cross_device_reduce` blocks until the
slowest rank arrives, so its duration tracks inter-rank skew rather than work
this change moves.

## Accuracy

Model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`, MI355X (gfx950), TP8. GSM8K, full 1319
questions, 5-shot, greedy.

| run | accuracy | invalid |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (gate 0) | 0.950 | 0.000 |
| patched (gate 1) | 0.949 | 0.000 |
| patched (gate 1, repeat) | 0.945 | 0.000 |

Note this is measured **without** `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`. The throughput
harness pins acceptance to the golden AL, which fabricates which draft tokens are
accepted — fine for speed, but it would bypass the accept/reject path this change
touches. Acceptance here is whatever the draft model earns.

```bash
export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton
export SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1
export SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1
export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0
export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=high

# flip this between 0 (baseline) and 1 (patched)
export SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY=1

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
    --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 31710 --trust-remote-code \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --attention-backend dsv4 \
    --page-size 256 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
    --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
    --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \
    --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
    --max-running-requests 32 --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \
    --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \
    --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4

python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \
    --backend srt --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 31710 \
    --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 \
    --max-new-tokens 1024 --temperature 0.0 --parallel 32
```

## Performance

Same model and hardware. 8k input / 1k output, TP8, steady state (10 waves
through a `--max-concurrency` gate). Each cell is the mean of 2 repeats run in
`off, on, on, off` order per concurrency, so a monotonic drift over the block
shifts both arms equally instead of being credited to the patch. Repeated
all-gates-off runs on this node put the noise floor at 0.25% (1σ).

| concurrency | output tok/s (base → patched) | uplift | mean TPOT ms | accept len |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4  | 332.43 → 341.07 | **+2.60%** | 11.37 → 11.06 | 2.499 → 2.498 |
| 8  | 543.73 → 555.57 | **+2.18%** | 13.75 → 13.46 | 2.499 → 2.469 |
| 16 | 839.00 → 857.32 | **+2.18%** | 17.98 → 17.57 | 2.499 → 2.507 |
| 32 | 1167.14 → 1186.66 | **+1.67%** | 25.79 → 25.34 | 2.482 → 2.508 |

Acceptance length is flat across arms, so the uplift is kernel time and not a
shift in speculation behaviour.

```bash
# same server launch as above, with SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY
# flipped 0/1 between arms, plus the throughput harness env:
export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=2.49
export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected
export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token

# CONC in {4, 8, 16, 32}; --max-running-requests/--cuda-graph-max-bs = 2*CONC
# capped at 32 on both arms (this image cannot capture a decode graph at bs 48).
CONC=16
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31710 --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
    --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
    --random-range-ratio 0.8 --num-prompts $((CONC * 10)) \
    --max-concurrency $CONC
```

`bench_serving` ignores EOS by default here (it only offers
`--disable-ignore-eos`), so every request runs to exactly 1024 output tokens and
neither arm can win by generating less.

title: [AMD] Add the Kimi-K3 MI35x perf benchmarks in nightly
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
Follow-up to #32568. Adds the Kimi-K3 MI35x performance benchmarks to the nightly, running immediately after the existing accuracy step in the same job so throughput is only measured once the model is known to produce correct tokens. ## Hardware result [Run 32074996819 summary](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32074996819/attempts/1#summary-95526175371) — both accuracy and performance steps passed on 8×MI355X with ROCm 7.2, on head `33d2793ae0`. **Accuracy** | Metric | Result | | --- | ---: | | GSM8K accuracy | **0.953** (threshold 0.92) | | Invalid responses | 0.1% | | Eval latency | 270.60 s | | Eval output throughput | 501.01 tok/s | **Performance sweep** | batch size | input len | latency (s) | input throughput (tok/s) | output throughput (tok/s) | ITL (ms) | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 4096 | 9.34 | 13,530.74 | 56.62 | 17.66 | | 8 | 4096 | 13.85 | 18,097.61 | 340.10 | 23.52 | | 16 | 4096 | 17.68 | 18,196.44 | 581.97 | 27.49 | | 64 | 4096 | 37.73 | 18,217.66 | 1,403.86 | 45.59 | **Runtime** | Phase | Runtime | | --- | ---: | | Container setup | 4m 23s | | Dependency install | 1m 59s | | Accuracy step (server load + eval) | 45m 57s | | └ GSM8K request phase | 4m 31s | | Performance step | 5m 51s | | **Full job** | **58m 17s** | The accuracy step dominates because it includes loading the 1.56 TB checkpoint and server warmup. Perf runs immediately afterward in the same job, reusing the node's on-disk model cache and avoiding another container setup. > The sweep above was measured with `batch_sizes = [1, 8, 16, 64]`, before the warmup change below. Its batch-1 row therefore includes first-request warmup; with the repeated leading `1` that row becomes a post-warmup measurement and should land above 56.62 tok/s. The other three rows are unaffected. The perf step should gain roughly one batch-1 iteration of wall time, about 9 s. ## Review follow-up Three notes from @bingxche, all addressed: - **Use the shared report helper.** `sglang.test.nightly_bench_utils` already exports `generate_simple_markdown_report`, and its `default_gpu_config` parameter covers the `"MI35x"` label that the local copy hardcoded. The shared version is otherwise line-for-line identical, and it guards the ITL division against a zero `output_throughput` where the copy did not, so this removes duplication and closes a latent `ZeroDivisionError`. `test_gpt_oss_perf_mi35x.py` already imports it this way. Dropping the copy left `typing.List` and `BenchmarkResult` unused, so both imports are gone. - **Make the warmup skip actually fire.** The helper detects a warmup run by a repeated leading batch size, so with `[1, 8, 16, 64]` that branch was dead and the batch-1 row absorbed first-request warmup. Now `[1, 1, 8, 16, 64]`. - **Fix the circular `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` comment.** It claimed the value was "matched to `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`" when `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` is what that flag is set from, so it explained nothing. It now states the constraint the accuracy test records — the ~53 GB per GPU left after the MXFP4 weights — and keeps only the non-circular half, that graphs are not captured for batches the server would never admit. ### Why a warmup batch, given perf runs right after accuracy Running after the eval does not leave the perf sweep warm, because what it inherits is only on-disk state: - `run_benchmark_for_model` calls `popen_launch_server(...)` and then `kill_process_tree(...)` in its `finally`. The accuracy test does the same, so its server is already gone when the perf step starts and the sweep measures a brand-new process. The step still finished in 5m51s against ~41 min of loading in the accuracy step, which is the on-disk checkpoint and page cache being reused — not process state. - The server's own startup warmup is on by default but sends `input_ids=[10, 11, 12]` with `max_new_tokens=8`. The first measured run is a 4096-token prefill with 512 output tokens, so shape-keyed Triton/AITER autotuning and allocator first-touch for those buffers still land on it. HIP graph capture does happen during init, so that cost is already outside the measurement, and `--disable-radix-cache` means there is no prefix reuse between runs. - `test_gpt_oss_perf_mi35x.py`, the one MI35x perf test that already repeats the leading batch size, runs in `nightly-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-rocm720` — an accuracy step followed by a perf step in the same job on the same runner class. So the precedent comes from exactly this arrangement. Worth knowing for review: it is a precedent of one. The other fourteen MI35x perf tests use `[1, 8, 16, 64]` and so fold warmup into their batch-1 row, which means K3's batch-1 number will not be directly comparable to theirs. The tradeoff is a cleaner regression signal for K3 over time against cross-model comparability, at a cost of about 9 s per nightly. Happy to drop it if the reviewer would rather K3 match the majority. ## Test plan Verified with a harness that loads the real `NightlyBenchmarkRunner` and the real `nightly_bench_utils` with only the torch-backed leaf imports stubbed, so the code under test is the tree's: - [x] `setUpClass()` runs to completion and creates `performance_results_kimi_k3_mi35x` - [x] Every `runner.*` attribute the test touches exists on `NightlyBenchmarkRunner` - [x] The `run_benchmark_for_model(...)` call binds against the real signature - [x] No local `generate_simple_markdown_report` remains; the call site resolves to the shared function by identity, and the only symbol imported from `nightly_bench_utils` is that function - [x] No unused imports remain (checked by AST, so the dropped `List` / `BenchmarkResult` cannot silently linger) - [x] Rendering a five-run sweep through the shared helper emits four rows, so the warmup row is genuinely dropped, and the `[MI35x]` label still appears via `default_gpu_config` - [x] Workflow YAML parses; job count, `job_select` options and `check-all-jobs` entries are unchanged from the base - [x] The K3 job runs `nightly-amd-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3` first, then directly invokes `registered/amd/perf/mi35x/test_kimi_k3_perf_mi35x.py` in the same job; `test/run_suite.py` is unchanged - [x] `codespell --config .codespellrc` clean repo-wide; `black --check` and `isort --check-only` clean - [x] Direct file invocation validated on hardware at head `33d2793ae0`; see **Hardware result** above - [ ] Re-run on hardware to capture the post-warmup batch-1 number. The review changes touch only the batch list and the report helper, not the server args, so accuracy is unaffected and the other three sweep rows should reproduce.

title: [diffusion] feat: load quantized H3 text encoder checkpoints
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- detect serialized quantization metadata from an overridden native text-encoder checkpoint
- opt MiniMax-H3's native Qwen3-VL language stack into checkpoint FP8 while keeping embeddings, normalization, and the vision tower in BF16
- use the generic component-path interface (`--component-paths.text_encoder`, with `--text-encoder-path` as an alias) and fail closed for encoder/format combinations that have not explicitly opted in
- document the checkpoint-first workflow without adding text-encoder-specific online quantization flags

## Why

MiniMax-H3 uses a large Qwen3-VL prompt encoder, and users commonly want to select a concrete pre-quantized checkpoint for that component. The native encoder loader previously did not resolve the checkpoint's quantization metadata, pass it into the language model, or run post-load processing for quantized linears.

The component path is generic, but quantization contracts are not: VAE, image-encoder, and text-encoder checkpoints can use different layer types, scale layouts, and kernels. This change therefore keeps support capability-based instead of claiming blanket quantization support for every component.

## Validation

- H100 serialized `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct-FP8` load through the normal `sglang serve` download path
- complete 5-second 1344×768 T2VA request with the serialized checkpoint and layerwise offload
- serialized FP8 TP1/TP2 load and forward comparison
- after rebasing onto current `main` and removing the online-only API: `23 passed` in the focused loader/admission suite
- changed-files pre-commit passed on the remote checkout

title: Support unified SWA page mapping in attention metadata
author: merrymercy
body:
## Motivation

Unified full-attention and sliding-window pools maintain independent virtual-to-physical page tables, while the decode metadata kernel currently assumes a legacy full-to-SWA slot mapping.

## Modifications

- Detect unified SWA pools and pass their independent virtual-to-physical page table to the general metadata kernel.
- Translate virtual page indices directly for both page-size-one and paged layouts.
- Preserve the existing mapping path for statically partitioned SWA pools.
- Preserve OSS formatter output; this accounts for the three-line stat difference from the source diff.

## Accuracy Tests

- `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib64/libnuma.so.1 with-proxy uv run --with pytest python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/attention/test_normal_decode_set_metadata.py` (16 passed, 8 subtests passed)
- CUDA smoke test with a minimal `UnifiedSWAKVPool` verified full page-table output `[[0, 1]]` and independent SWA output `[[2, 5]]`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run; the change reuses the existing fused metadata kernel and adds only a compile-time mapping-mode branch.

## Checklist

- [x] `with-proxy uv run pre-commit run --files python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/metadata.py`
- [x] `uv run python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/metadata.py`
- [x] No documentation update is required for this internal page-table mapping.

## Original commits

- `52d1a85cf`

title: spec: size the speculative buffers from the bags, not the startup record
author: ch-wan
body:
Adaptive speculative decoding switches the step config at runtime through
get_context().override, which moves the spec bag leaves and leaves the
ServerArgs record on its startup values. Six sizing paths read the record:

  - allocation_sizing: the per-decode KV reserve, recomputed every decode
    batch, kept reserving for the startup step count after a switch
  - spec_utils.resolve_num_tokens_per_req: draft-extend capture widths were
    sized for the startup draft-token count while a different candidate state
    was being captured
  - spec_info.create_dummy_verify_input: the autotune forward inside the
    capture window built its dummy verify input at the startup tree shape
  - eagle_disaggregation: the prebuilt-batch draft-input state count
  - managers.utils.compute_num_reserved_tokens: the token budget the rust
    ingress enforces

All of them read the spec bag now, and so do the two DSA seed predicates the
disagg path calls. The config parameter goes away where every caller was
handing over the process config anyway, which drops the disagg draft-input
hand-off chain down to what it uses; the tests that drove those paths with
stand-in objects publish a config. The exposure pins shrink by 16 (axis 1)
and 6 (axis 2) pairs.

title: [JIT Kernel] Migrate causal_conv1d_fwd and causal_conv1d_update from AOT to JIT
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

Move `causal_conv1d_fwd` / `causal_conv1d_update` off the prebuilt `sgl_kernel` wheel and onto the JIT kernel infra, keeping the in-place contract, the exported ops, and bit-level numerics. Both sit on the prefill/decode path of every short-conv hybrid model — LFM2 / LFM2-MoE, Mamba2, GDN.

## Modifications

- Device kernels move into `kernels/jit/csrc/mamba/causal_conv1d.cuh` unchanged; only the host launchers switch to the tvm-ffi `TensorView` API. Strides stay `uint32_t` elements, as in the AOT `ConvParamsBase`.
- The JIT build matches the wheel's arch split — `-use_fast_math` on SM 9.0, precise math elsewhere, per `load_utils.py`'s `compute_capability == 90` — so the SiLU epilogue emits the same bits. Math mode is part of the build key.
- CUDA serving goes through the JIT registry behind a `torch.compile`-compatible custom op; everything else keeps Triton. The AOT ops stay exported for external users and for the differential test.
- Only a JIT/CUDA spec is registered, since the AOT kernel was CUDA-only anyway — `csrc/mamba/causal_conv1d.cu` sits in the CUDA CMakeLists and nowhere else, and `common_extension_rocm.cc` never defined the ops. ROCm and MUSA were already landing on Triton through the old `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.causal_conv1d_update` probe; now they get there directly via `_HAS_CONV1D_KERNEL = is_cuda()`. Nothing changes on any device.
- The AOT `cudaFuncSetAttribute` branch goes away behind a `static_assert`: every instantiation sits near 4 KB of shared memory, nowhere near the 48 KB it existed to raise.
- `width` outside 2..4 now raises in prefill, where the AOT `if`/`else if` chain had no `else` and quietly did nothing.
- `has_initial_state` gets a dtype check. The kernel reads it as `const bool*`, and `kDLBool` has no C++ trait, so it lands as a `CHECK_HOST` on the dtype code rather than a matcher clause.
- Tests and benchmarks move to the registered kernel layout, and the superseded AOT-only test is gone.

## Accuracy Tests

`pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py`

| | H200 (SM90, fast-math) | GB300 (SM103, precise-math) |
|---|---|---|
| Total | 473 passed, 12 skipped | 473 passed, 12 skipped |
| Bit-exact vs AOT (72 cases) | pass | pass |
| Reference vs `F.conv1d` (393 cases) | pass | pass |

Two machines because the kernel picks its math mode by arch, so each one compiles a different build. The 12 skips are the same deliberate guard on both: the circular-buffer reference can't arbitrate when `seqlen > state_len`, where `scatter_` hits duplicate indices.

Behind those counts, the reference tests cover FP32/FP16/BF16 × widths 2–4 × seqlens 1–4096, varlen (per sequence) and non-varlen, both conv-state layouts, gathered slots. The differential is one config per dispatch path, narrowed from a ~900-config sweep that came back bit-identical to AOT throughout. On GB300 the SiLU epilogue — where a math-flag mismatch would show up — gives `max_abs_diff = 0.000e+00`.

Also checked: `pad_slot_id` slots untouched, bad dtype / width / non-bool mask rejected, `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` bit-identical to eager, and `LiquidAI/LFM2-350M` serving end to end (GSM8K 200q = 0.325, H200). B200 is registered in `base-b-kernel-unit-test-4-gpu-b200`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`test/registered/kernels/benchmark/mamba/bench_causal_conv1d.py` — FP16/BF16, `dim` 2048–8192, prefill seqlens 128–8192 (4-sequence varlen batch), decode batch 1–256 with gathered slots. 24 configs each.

| | prefill geomean | prefill range | prefill wins | decode geomean | decode range | decode wins |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H200 (SM90) | **1.063x** | 1.022x – 1.122x | 24/24 | 1.001x | 0.995x – 1.015x | 14/24 |
| GB300 (SM103) | **1.041x** | 1.015x – 1.062x | 24/24 | 1.000x | 0.987x – 1.013x | 10/24 (3 tied) |

- Prefill wins every config on both machines. GB300 extremes: BF16 `(512, 2048)` 22.09 vs 22.41 us, BF16 `(2048, 8192)` 84.90 vs 90.16 us.
- Decode is a wash, and those win counts are noise rather than a result: 23/24 configs on H200 and 20/24 on GB300 land within ±1% either way, three of them exact ties. The decode kernel is unchanged, so neither direction means anything.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing documentation change is required.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

title: [DSA] Trim top-k v2 output modes and tighten its PDL waits
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> Generated by Claude.

## Motivation

The DeepSeek-V4 (DSA indexer) top-k v2 kernel carried an optional `raw_indices`
output that no production caller ever requests: the c4 indexer routes to the v1
kernel whenever it needs raw indices, so the v2 argument was only ever exercised
by a unit test. Everyone else still paid for it with a per-element
`raw_out != nullptr` branch inside the page-table transform loop.

While removing it, two PDL (programmatic dependent launch) details in the same
kernel turned out to be leaving performance on the table or resting on a
condition the caller was not told about.

## Modifications

**Output modes.** `raw_indices` is gone; `page_tables` becomes optional instead.
`None` selects a `TopKMode::INDICES` template that emits the selected positions
straight into the output, so the transform pass -- and the 8 KB shared staging
buffer it needs -- is compiled out rather than skipped at runtime. Passing a page
table keeps the existing behaviour bit for bit.

**Output buffer is no longer prefilled with -1.** Every path already writes all
`topk` slots of every row: the collect pass fills `[0, above_count)`, `handle_tie`
fills `[above_count, topk)` (padding included), and the trivial path fills
everything. The per-layer fill kernel was dead work.

**Level-3 PDL wait narrowed to the cluster path.** Only rows whose raw indices
come from the persistent cluster kernel need that kernel to have retired. The
register / streaming / trivial rows were waiting on it too, holding an SM slot
until the long-running pool finished and serializing the short items behind it --
which is exactly the mix level 3 exists for. The wait now lives inside the
cluster branch (block-uniform, so the following `__syncthreads()` is unaffected).

**Small-batch kernel.** Dropped the redundant `PDLWaitPrimary` after `forward()`
(`forward()` already waits internally) and added the missing
`PDLTriggerSecondary` so dependents can be scheduled without waiting for the
whole grid to drain.

**PDL prefetch contract.** The kernel reads `seq_lens` and the plan metadata
*before* its `griddepcontrol.wait`, which is only legal while neither is produced
by the immediately preceding kernel in the stream (per CUDA: the launch trigger
"provides no memory visibility guarantee itself"). Production satisfies this --
both are built during per-forward metadata prep -- but two call sites could
quietly break it, so:

- the DSA backend now asserts `lengths.dtype == torch.int32` instead of calling
  `.to(torch.int32)`, which would place a cast kernel exactly there;
- the unit test no longer launches `plan_topk_v2` back to back with the
  transform.

Also renamed `TopKMode::INDICE` to `INDICES`.

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_topk_v2.py` -- 234/234 pass on B200.
The no-page-table mode is validated directly against `torch.topk` across every
dispatch template and boundary (`test_topk_v2_output_indices`), and the paged
mode is still validated by inverting the output through the page table
(`test_topk_v2`, `test_topk_v2_ragged`), so both modes keep full coverage.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

No kernel-algorithm change on the paged path, so throughput is unchanged for the
common shapes. The wins are structural: one fewer fill kernel per layer, one
fewer branch per output element in the transform loop, and short rows in a
mixed-length long-context batch no longer sit blocked on the persistent cluster
pool.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci).

title: [XPU] Fix decode graph runner is_current_stream_capturing on non-CUDA devices
author: arathi-hlab
body:
## Summary
- Fix XPU stage-b CI regression: `_record_in_graph_metadata_prep_done` in `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py` unconditionally calls `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()`, which is a dummy stub on `torch==2.12.0+xpu` and raises `RuntimeError: Tried to instantiate dummy base class _cuda_isCurrentStreamCapturing`.

Introduced by #34916 (`[misc] Rename the WAR read-done fastpath to shared-read-done`, 2026-08-15 22:02 UTC), which dropped the pre-refactor `war_read_done_event is not None` guard that used to short-circuit XPU before the CUDA-only call.

title: [XPU][Fix] Pack device-pointer tables as uint64 to avoid 64-bit address overflow
author: dayanandav
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #35047.

Several kernels pass base addresses to the device in a side table and bitcast each entry back to a pointer (`tl.load(meta_ptr + i).to(tl.pointer_type(...))`). Those tables were built with `dtype=torch.int64`, which cannot hold an address `>= 2**63`: `torch.tensor()` unpacks Python ints through `long long`, so the build raises

```
ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long
```

on the host, before any kernel is launched. Note this is device-independent — the unpacking happens while building the tensor, so even a `device="cpu"` table raises. Intel XPU (Level Zero / SYCL USM) device addresses have the top bit set, e.g. `0xffff85abd4e00000`, so every Mamba/GDN model hits this in conv-state scatter and `MambaPool` slot maintenance. CUDA/HIP VAs stay in the low canonical half, which is the only reason `int64` looks lossless there.

## Modifications

- New `sglang.kernels.ops.memory.ptr_table.make_ptr_table(rows, device)`: builds the table as `uint64` (the only dtype that accepts a full 64-bit address) and `view`s it back to `int64`. `view` moves no bits, so kernels keep their existing signed element type — no kernel-side change. Companion columns (strides, element counts, block offsets) are non-negative, so their bits are unchanged too.
- Route the two affected table builders through it: `_conv_multi_build_meta` (`mamba_state_scatter_triton.py`) and `build_conv_slot_descriptor` (`mem_cache/mamba_slot_fused.py`). Both build device-resident tables from `data_ptr()` values, so both overflow on XPU.
- `MambaPool`: replace three hardcoded `device="cuda"` allocations with the pool's own device.

## Tests

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/memory/test_ptr_table.py` (new): covers the full `[0, 2**64)` address range, and asserts both call sites' tables round-trip a spoofed top-bit-set `data_ptr()` while leaving companion columns identical to a real-address build. It spoofs the address because a backend whose VAs stay `< 2**47` can never catch this regression — the guard has to run on any runner.
- `test_mamba_slot_fused.py` and `test_mamba_state_scatter_triton.py` now select the accelerator via `get_device()` instead of hardcoding CUDA. Added coverage for `fused_conv_window_scatter_multi` (single-type, multi-type, and with the second/track index set), which had no test on any backend and is the kernel most exposed to the packing.
- Registered the touched tests on the XPU suites so these paths actually run there: `stage-b-test-1-gpu-xpu` for `test_ptr_table.py`, `test_mamba_state_scatter_triton.py`, `test_mamba_slot_fused.py` and `test_mamba_unittest.py`; `nightly-xpu-2-gpu` for `test_mamba2_mixer.py`, which asserts `NUM_GPUS` rather than skipping and so needs the 2-GPU pool.

Verified on Intel Arc Pro B60 (torch 2.13.0+xpu): the new cases fail with the reported `ValueError` when `make_ptr_table` is reverted to `int64`, and all 27 tests (+16 subtests) pass with the fix. `est_time` values are measured, not estimated. `pre-commit run --all-files` is clean.

title: [Spec] Point multi-layer eagle's last shared-read runner at the draft runner
author: hnyls2002
body:
`MultiLayerEagleWorkerV2` inherited `BaseSpecWorker.last_shared_read_runner`, which points at the target runner. Its step is draft-organize -> verify -> draft extend, and draft extend runs on the draft runner, so the target runner is not the one doing the step's last shared-buffer read.

No behavior change today: under this algorithm both runners' `shared_read_done_event` stay `None` (verify resolves to `UNKNOWN` because the algorithm's last reading phase is draft extend, and the draft-extend runners declare `UNKNOWN` for `DRAFT_EXTEND_V2`), so the scheduler takes the coarse WAR fence either way. This makes the ownership correct before anything starts relying on it.
