title: [Bug][Spec] fix startup crash and reduce CUDA graph memory usage for speculative adaptive
author: Deleter-D
body:
## Motivation

Three separate problems show up when `--speculative-adaptive` is enabled:
1. **Startup crash.** `ModelRunner.max_decode_logits_rows()` sizes the shared logits buffer from the *static* `decode_num_tokens_per_req()`, but adaptive speculative decoding replays runners built for larger draft-token widths. The buffer is too small and the server fails to start. (mentioned in #30549)
2. **IMA on the first replay.** `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture_one_shape` looked up `on_after_cuda_graph_warmup` on `self.model_runner.attn_backend` instead of on the backend this capture actually ran against (`attn_backend` from `capture_prepare`). For the runner the `ModelRunner` owns these are the same object, but adaptive speculative decoding builds extra runners bound to their own freshly created backend while `model_runner.attn_backend` still points at the active one. Hooking the wrong backend leaves this capture's warmup-upgraded metadata (raw→full, FlashMLA scheduler meta) frozen into the graph, which produces an illegal memory access on the first replay.
3. **Redundant CUDA graph memory.** Each capture pass opened `graph_capture()` without a stream, so every pass captured on a fresh stream. The caching allocator partitions the graph pool's segments **by stream**, so each pass re-reserved the pool's MoE / DeepEP scratch instead of reusing what an earlier pass left inactive. With adaptive speculative decoding that is one pass per candidate step × three runners — tens of GB of segments that all read back `inactive`.

## Modifications
1. `max_decode_logits_rows()` now derives `num_tokens_per_req` from `max_speculative_num_draft_tokens`, so the shared logits buffer is sized for the widest adaptive graph. (Same fix as #30554.)
2. `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:1226-1237` — resolve `post_warmup_hook` from the capture-local `attn_backend` rather than `model_runner.attn_backend`, with a comment recording why.
3. Added `get_or_create_global_graph_capture_stream()` in `runner_utils/pool.py` (a named stream lease in the `Resources` tier, alongside the existing process-wide graph memory pool) and used it as the `graph_capture(stream=...)` argument in both `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture` and `PrefillCudaGraphRunner.capture`. All capture passes therefore share one stream and reserve that scratch exactly once. Captures are strictly serial (`Scheduler.init_all_cuda_graphs` runs target and draft workers in turn; the adaptive controller builds one runtime state at a time), so a single shared stream is safe.

Also added a CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_graph_capture_resources.py` covering both the pool and the new capture-stream lease.

## Accuracy Tests

Server launched following the cookbook:

```bash
sglang serve \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
    --tp 4 \
    --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
    --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
    --speculative-num-steps 3 \
    --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
    --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
    --speculative-adaptive \
    --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
    --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 30000
```

Evaluated on the three datasets shown in the cookbook:

|          | GPQA Diamond | AIME25 | GSM8k |
| -------- | ------------ | ------ | ----- |
| cookbook | 88.1         | 95     | 96.13 |
| before   | 88.13        | 98.33  | 96.89 |
| after    | 88.04          | 97.29  | 96.97 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput change is expected; the win is memory. With the launch command above and the default adaptive speculative decoding parameters, CUDA graph memory drops from **14.4 GB → 10.13 GB**. With my own serving config and adaptive speculative decoding parameters, it drops from **44.3 GB → 16 GB**, which frees the corresponding capacity for the KV cache.

title: [Kimi-K3] Fix "wrong grids" crash in DP-sharded vision preprocessing
author: fullyz
body:
## Motivation

Regression introduced by #34404

On Kimi-K3 with cpu transport and DP-sharded vision, one batch with ≥2 images of different resolutions crashes the server with `ValueError: Kimi-K3 deferred GPU preprocessing produced wrong grids`.

Root cause: the deferred path reads `grid_thws_host` with shard-local positions instead of global image positions.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py`: index `grid_thws_host` by global image position at both deferred reads, mapping shard-local positions back via `image_indices`.
- `test/registered/unit/models/test_kimi_k3_vision.py`: `test_kimi_k3_preprocesses_only_dp_owner_images` now uses distinct per-image grids (identical ones mask the bug); fails on main, passes with this fix.

## Accuracy Tests

Verified on 4-node × 8 H100 (TP32/EP32, cpu transport): one request with three different-resolution images crashes on main, completes with this fix.

No impact

title: [diffusion] Allow per-role attention backend override
author: avjves
body: ## Motivation Currently one can choose a global attention backend or a specific backend per component. This PR adds support to choose attention backend per component for each role. That is, a different backend for self-attention and cross-attention. The motivation here is that when using quantized attention backends, there's a quantization overhead prior to running the lower precision kernel. This overhead is mostly worth it in self-attention, but cross-attention calls are often so light that the overhead can be enough for the entire call to be slower than the un-quantized counterpart. The backend can be chosen via the component backend selection: ``` --component-attention-backends.transformer.self=backend_1 -component-attention-backends.transformer.cross=backend_2 ``` The backend choice tree is as follows: 1. selected_attention_backend - explicit arg passed directly into `get_attn_backend()` 2. Global forced backend - `get_global_forced_attn_backend()`, set via `global_force_attn_backend()` (programmatic override) 3. Component + role override - `get_component_forced_attn_backend_for_role(attention_role)`, i.e. the config key transformer.cross / transformer.self 4. Component-wide override - `get_component_forced_attn_backend()`, i.e. the config key transformer (no role suffix) 5. CLI global - `--attention-backend` flag 6. `default_attention_backend` 7. Platform default - if everything above is None, platform picks This now only adds the choice via the `--component-attention-backends`. If desired, I can also add a `--cross-attention-backend` flag. ## Modifications - Enhances the component-attention-backend to support self/cross attn as well - Adds AttentionRole enum used to specify self/cross role (can support others, like joint, as well, if needed) - Stores role-qualified entries in a separate `component_attention_backend_roles` map rather than in `component_attention_backends`, so consumers that look a component up by name are unaffected by a role key ## Accuracy Tests Here the self was `aiter` and cross is `aiter_sage`. Both are used as expected. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3cfabbf1-b440-4aad-bf3b-637cfae01906 Output is good. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. title: Support deepseek v4 and kimi k3 on ssd
author: beyondHJM
body:
# [Feature] Add SSD-backed Expert Pack inference for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi-K3

## Summary

This PR adds an opt-in SSD-backed inference path for **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** and **Kimi-K3**. It allows these MoE models to run when their complete weights are larger than GPU VRAM and host RAM combined.

Routed expert weights are stored on SSD and loaded only when selected by the router. The implementation uses:

- an expert-major **Expert Pack** layout for efficient random access;
- direct I/O into aligned pinned host buffers;
- asynchronous host-to-device transfers; and
- a byte-budgeted LFU/LRU GPU cache for frequently used experts.

The runtime does not prune, merge, skip, replace, or re-quantize experts, and does not reduce Expert Top-K. The default `auto`, `safetensors`, and `gguf` loading paths remain unchanged; SSD execution is enabled only through the explicit `expert_pack` path.

## Supported Scope

`ExpertPackModelLoader` is selected only with `--load-format expert_pack`. Official checkpoints loaded through the standard `auto` or `safetensors` paths never enter this loader.

The currently validated DeepSeek input is the single-file MXFP4 GGUF used by `frob/deepseek-v4-flash-0731:latest`. Its routed expert matrices use `MXFP4`; the large non-routed matrices are mostly `Q8_0`, router input weights are `BF16`, and the inventory also contains `F32` and `I32` normalization or auxiliary tensors. The inspected GGUF contains 129 `MXFP4`, 512 `Q8_0`, 43 `BF16`, 641 `F32`, and 3 `I32` tensors. It contains no FP8 tensors.

The other validated input is the text-only 38-shard `KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-*.gguf`, whose routed experts use Q2_K for gate/up and Q3_K for down. The Kimi launcher extracts the official `text_config` into a flat `KimiLinearConfig`; the complete multimodal Kimi-K3 checkpoint is not supported by this loader. Other GGUF quantization variants have not been validated and are not currently claimed as supported.

## Usage

Install this branch from source before running the examples:

```bash
python3 -m pip install -e "python"
```

### DeepSeek-V4-Flash

The tested MXFP4 GGUF is available as [`frob/deepseek-v4-flash-0731:latest`](https://ollama.com/frob/deepseek-v4-flash-0731), which was imported from [`unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF`](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF). The benchmark used the immutable Ollama model blob with SHA-256 `947ac34c08c0e5c5752ac76398f934b3b6b4075cfe915ba43dd5ac754900a4cd`.

```bash
python3 examples/runtime/deepseek_v4/benchmark_deepseek_5090.py \
  --gguf /path/to/deepseek-v4-flash-0731-mxfp4.gguf \
  --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \
  --max-new-tokens 200
```

### Kimi-K3

Download all 38 Q2_K GGUF shards from [`Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED`](https://huggingface.co/Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED). Also place the tokenizer/config files from [`moonshotai/Kimi-K3`](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3) in a sibling directory named `kimi-k3-tokenizer`.

```bash
hf download Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED \
  --include "KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-*.gguf" \
  --local-dir /path/to/kimi-k3
```

```bash
python3 examples/runtime/kimi_k3/benchmark_kimi_k3_5090.py \
  --gguf /path/to/kimi-k3/KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-00001-of-00038.gguf \
  --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \
  --max-new-tokens 200
```

The first shard is only the entrypoint. The launcher automatically discovers and uses all 38 shards in the same directory. Both launchers derive the remaining paths automatically. If the Expert Pack is missing, it is built on the first launch and reused afterward.

| Model | First Expert Pack build | Approximate first-run readiness |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Estimated **5-10 minutes** on the benchmark NVMe SSD | **8-15 minutes** |
| Kimi-K3 | **29 minutes 42 seconds measured** | **35-45 minutes** |

The 38 Kimi-K3 source shards and generated Expert Pack occupy approximately 1.814 TiB in total, so a 4 TB SSD is recommended for practical headroom.

## Correctness

- DeepSeek-V4-Flash produced semantically equivalent answers to Ollama across travel planning, science, history, programming, and mathematics prompts.
- Kimi-K3 matched the 200-token SGLang reference output exactly. All 92 routed layers executed Top-16 experts with `fallback_count=0` and `io_errors=0`.

## Performance

The target platform is one RTX 5090 with 32 GB VRAM, 32 GB host RAM, and NVMe SSD storage. The retained measurements were collected on RTX 5090 hosts; host RAM and SSD capacity differed between the two model runs.

### DeepSeek-V4-Flash vs Ollama

Five prompts were measured with 200 generated tokens per prompt.

| Metric | SGLang | Ollama | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Prefill | 3.265 token/s | 1.457 token/s | **2.24x faster** |
| Decode | 2.020 token/s | 1.354 token/s | **1.49x faster** |

### Kimi-K3 vs llama.cpp

The SGLang run used a 91-token prompt and generated 200 tokens.

| Metric | SGLang | llama.cpp | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Prefill | 0.66412 token/s | 0.11289 token/s | **5.88x faster** |
| Decode | 0.44830 token/s | 0.1810 token/s | **2.48x faster** |

The llama.cpp decode baseline came from an earlier 50-token run, so the 2.48x decode figure is indicative rather than a strict equal-length comparison.

title: [Perf] PaddleOCR-VL: overlap page preprocessing, pack the ViT, enable prefill CUDA graph
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

PaddleOCR-VL served a 1080p page in **235 ms** and saturated at **6.7 req/s** on an H200 while the GPU sat idle. Profiling put almost none of that in the model's own compute:

| what | why it was slow |
|---|---|
| Image processor ran **single-threaded** | `QwenVLImageProcessor` grants concurrent workers only to an explicit `model_type` allowlist that `paddleocr_vl` is not on. An 87 ms/page preprocess caps throughput at ~11 req/s no matter how much GPU is left. |
| **Prefill CUDA graph was off** | Breakable CG is the CUDA default, but the generic "multimodal model" rule disables it for every multimodal arch. PaddleOCR-VL's config always carries a `vision_config`, so even *text-only* prefill lost the graph. |
| ViT recomputed and re-synchronized **per image** | A device-side `max()` for the rope table, one host sync per image to slice the encoder output, a bilinear position-embedding interpolation per image per forward (the LFU cache written for it was never called), and a full projector pass per image. |
| `quant_config` accepted and **dropped** | `--quantization` was a silent no-op for both the LM and the vision tower. |

## Modifications

- `multimodal/processors/paddleocr_vlm.py` — opt into concurrent preprocessing (4 workers, 16 IO threads). A document page is a far heavier preprocessing unit than a chat image.
- `configs/model_config.py` — allowlist the arch for breakable prefill CUDA graph, the way the Kimi archs are. Embed-carrying batches are still rejected at replay and run eager, so this is a text/mixed-traffic win.
- `models/paddleocr_vl.py` — run the vision tower packed: grids stay on the host, the encoder output stays concatenated, the 2x2 merge writes into one buffer, and the two projections run once for the batch instead of once per image. Wire up the position-embedding LFU cache that was already written but never called. Pass `quant_config` through. Take `Conv2dLayer`'s unfold+matmul path for the patch embedding (kernel == stride, zero padding).
- `models/ernie4.py` — give `Ernie4Model` a `get_input_embeddings`, replacing a `hasattr` + `types.MethodType` patch at the PaddleOCR-VL call site.
- Cookbook page for PaddleOCR-VL / 1.5 / 1.6 (identical `config.json`, so one recipe serves all three), plus the `supported-models` row.

## Accuracy

Every arm was gated on output equality before it was measured: five page geometries x two task prompts under greedy decoding, compared against the pre-change baseline.

- packed ViT: **10/10 byte-identical** (text and token counts)
- \+ four concurrent preprocessing workers: **10/10**
- \+ transformers-native image processor: **10/10**
- \+ the final scheduling recipe: **10/10**

CPU unit tests pin the packed vision math to a per-image reference implementation at fp64 (packed 2x2 merge, batch invariance, the position-embedding cache vs uncached interpolation, LFU eviction, conv-vs-matmul, packed 2D position ids), and a second file pins the two allowlist memberships, which are exactly the kind of setting a refactor drops silently.

## Benchmark

One H200, PaddleOCR-VL-0.9B, `bench_serving --dataset-name image`, 1080p JPEG pages (~2700 image tokens), 128 output tokens, prefix + multimodal caches disabled, **median** TTFT, arms interleaved within a single run, 2-3 reps.

| workload | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 1080p page, 1 stream (TTFT) | 235.1 ms | **119.6 ms** (1.97x) |
| 1080p page, 32 concurrent | 6.67 req/s | **12.26 req/s** (1.84x) |
| 2704-token text, 1 stream (TTFT) | 16.1 ms | **11.5 ms** (1.40x, from the prefill graph) |

Against vLLM 0.27.1 on the same box, same caches-off settings:

| workload | sglang | vLLM |
|---|---|---|
| 2704-tok text, 1 stream TTFT | **11.5 ms** | 15.9 ms |
| 2704-tok text, 32 concurrent | **95.4 req/s** | 81.8 req/s |
| 1080p page, 1 stream TTFT | **119.6 ms** | 137.5 ms |
| 1080p page, 32 concurrent | 12.26 req/s | **12.77 req/s** |

The one remaining loss is saturated page throughput, ~4% behind. It is GPU-bound in the vision tower (full attention over ~10.7k patches, `head_dim=72`); `fa4`, `triton_attn`, `cuda_ipc` feature transport, more processor workers, PD-multiplexing and every chunked-prefill size were all measured and none of them helped.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code and run lint locally
- [x] Add unit tests (`test/registered/unit/models/test_paddleocr_vl_vision.py`, `..._serving_defaults.py`) and an e2e server test (`test/registered/vlm/test_paddleocr_vl_server.py`)
- [x] Benchmark on real hardware with accuracy verified against the pre-change baseline
- [x] Update documentation (cookbook page + supported-models row)

title: [Kimi] Enable GB300 TP4 and GB200/GB300 TP16 SP collectives
author: ajit283
body:
## Summary

Enable tuned Kimi K3 sequence-parallel collectives for:

- GB300 DP4 x attention-TP4 / EP16, where attention TP is a derived node-local subgroup of full TP16.
- GB200 and GB300 attention-TP16 / EP16 across four nodes in one NVL72 segment.

## Relationship to upstream communicator work

#35061 provides generic SM100 world-size-16 CustomAllReduceV2 admission and configuration. #35735 subsequently split the communicator into push and pull planes and moved push-capacity validation into push binding.

This PR now contains only the remaining K3-specific functionality:

1. Derived attention-TP groups inherit the global custom-AR policy instead of unconditionally setting `use_custom_allreduce=False`. Capability selection still happens independently per group, and explicit `--disable-custom-all-reduce` remains respected.
2. K3 SP dispatch admits world size 16 on SM100 and SM103.
3. Correctness-checked, exact-device GB200 and GB300 `world=16,H=7168` RS/AG tables are added.
4. Pull/direct K3 strategies no longer require push-workspace capacity. Every selected push bucket fits the default 256 KiB world-16 workspace.

The superseded K3 `.cuh` capacity change was dropped during the rebase; #35735 now owns that check in the push plane. Ordinary TP16 all-reduce behavior remains owned by the generic SM100 heuristics.

## Changes

### Attention process group

- Let derived attention-TP groups inherit the global custom-all-reduce policy.
- Leave final communicator selection to per-group topology and allocator capability checks.
- Add focused CPU coverage for the derived-group option.

### K3 world-16 support

- Enable K3 SP on SM100/SM103 when an exact-device table is available.
- Add GB200 and GB300 `world=16,H=7168` reduce-scatter/all-gather tables.
- Keep untuned attention-residual fusion entries on the existing `separate` path.
- Check push workspace only after dispatch selects a push strategy; pull RS and direct AG use dedicated symmetric tensors.
- Add exact-device table lookup and default-workspace-envelope tests.
- Add one-time dispatch/fallback diagnostics.

## Post-rebase tuning and correctness

Both devices were freshly retuned after #35735 on four 4-GPU nodes in one NVL72 segment over global-token buckets 16 through 16384.

- Every measured push/pull/direct candidate was checked against NCCL before timing.
- BF16 comparison used `rtol=2e-2`, `atol=5e-2` for rank-16 reduction-order differences.
- Every selected custom bucket was faster than NCCL.
- Production selection excludes push candidates above the generic world-16 256 KiB per-rank workspace.
- Attention-residual fusion was not part of the sweep and remains `separate`.
- Independent production-table runs captured and replayed every RS+AG pair with the default workspace: all 11 buckets passed on each device.

### GB200 (SM100)

|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|

| All-gather | 512 | 93.383 us | 17.473 us | direct | 5.34x |

title: [XPU][CI] key persistent JIT kernel cache by image content ID
author: arathi-hlab
body:
## Summary

Nightly image rebuilds swap the runtime libs that cached JIT `.so` files link against (e.g. `libsycl.so.8` -> `libsycl.so.9`). Triton keys its cache on source hash only, so the previous gpu-mask-only cache path dlopens stale `.so`s from the prior image and every XPU CI job dies with `OSError: libsycl.so.N: cannot open shared object file`.

- Include the resolved `docker image inspect` ID in the cache path so a new image gets a fresh cache dir.
- Prune sibling caches for the same GPU but a different image ID via a rootful busybox helper (files are root-owned by the CI container, same pattern as the workspace-ownership reset).
- Explicit `XPU_KERNEL_CACHE_DIR` overrides are still honored verbatim; if `docker image inspect` fails we fall back to the legacy unversioned path with a warning.
- Over-cap reset switched from a runner-level `rm -rf` to the same busybox helper for the same root-owned reason.

## Test plan

- [ ] XPU CI passes on an image with a torch/SYCL bump (verify no `libsycl.so.*: cannot open shared object` failures).
- [ ] Sibling `kernel-cache-gpu*-<oldid>` dirs are pruned on first run after an image rebuild.
- [ ] `XPU_KERNEL_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/foo` override still lands at `/tmp/foo` with no pruning.
- [ ] Over-cap path (>`XPU_KERNEL_CACHE_MAX_MB`) resets cleanly.

title: [AMD][Fix] Qwen3.5: make empty-batch guard tuple-aware on fused AR+quant path
author: bingxche
body: ## Problem [#24651](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24651) made Qwen3.5's AMD fused AR+RMSNorm+per-group-quant path return quantized activations as tuples: - GDN layers: `(bf16, fp8, scale)` - full-attention layers: `(fp8, scale)` [#34474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34474) later added empty-batch guards that read `hidden_states.shape[0]`. On the fused path, those guards run before attention unpacks the tuple, so decode CUDA-graph capture fails: ```text AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'shape' ``` The scheduler failure then surfaces in the test as `Server process exited with code -9`. The `SGLANG_DISABLE_FUSED_AR_QUANT=1` control stays on the tensor path and is unaffected. ## Fix Use the tuple's first tensor for the row-count check at both Qwen3.5 decoder guards, while passing the original `hidden_states` to attention unchanged. Both sites are required: GDN receives the 3-tuple, while full attention receives the 2-tuple. Zero-token inputs are handled before fused quantization, so they remain tensors and the empty-batch behavior from #34474 is preserved. Supersedes #35250, which covered only the GDN guard. ## Verification - The target `test_qwen35_fp8_ar_fusion_mi35x.py` partition passed: [job 95989392541](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32227220289/job/95989392541). ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32946726011](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32946726011) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32946725868](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32946725868) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :x: [Run #32946725974](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32946725974)

title: Sync FlashInfer autotune tactic choice across TP ranks
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

FlashInfer's autotuner times every candidate tactic on the rank's own GPU and keeps whichever came out fastest. That works fine on one GPU. With TP > 1 each rank runs that search on its own, and the ranks don't come out the same.

Measured on `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, TP=4, 4x GB300 (sm103), flashinfer 0.6.17. The per-rank tactic caches sglang already writes (`rank_tp{0..3}_pp0_dp0.json`) show it directly:

| | Tuned shape buckets | Diverging across ranks |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 20 | **20 / 20** |
| After | 20 | **0 / 20** |

Every tuned `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` shape landed on a different tactic somewhere, and not just as a tie-break — at m=16 rank 0 took a tile-8 tactic while ranks 1–3 took tile-16. Same shape, different tile size.

Dumping the autotuner's per-tactic timings per rank explains it. Each rank recorded 12,188 measurements, the same count on all four, so the tuning loop is already walking in step; what differs is the numbers it walks away with:

| m | candidates | same-tactic spread across ranks | gap best → runner-up | tactics within noise of best |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 920 | 3.5% | 2.14% | 5 |
| 8 | 920 | 2.9% | 0.43% | 25 |
| 16 | 920 | 1.2% | 0.08% | 28 |
| 256 | 920 | 0.7% | 0.14% | 10 |
| 4096 | 50 | 0.7% | 0.14% | 6 |

The last two columns are the whole story. In all 20 buckets the gap between the winner and the runner-up is smaller than the noise on a single tactic's own measurement, and anywhere from 2 to 28 candidates sit inside that noise. `argmin` over a field like that is a coin flip, which is why divergence is 20/20 rather than occasional, and why it's worst at small `m` where the kernel runs ~20 µs and jitter dominates.

It costs something, too. Scored against the consensus best — the tactic that wins on the mean of all four ranks' timings — the worst rank was +2.45% off at m=1, and +0.63% off averaged across buckets. Once the timings are shared, every rank lands on the consensus best and that gap closes to zero.

## Modifications

- `_autotune_tactic_sync_group` hands FlashInfer the TP group's `cpu_group` through `set_autotune_process_group`. FlashInfer then all-reduces each tactic's measured time, so every rank minimizes over the same numbers instead of its own. TP is the right scope, since those ranks run the same dummy forward; a lone rank has nobody to agree with and tunes without a group.
- `_autotune_process_group` wraps the `autotune()` block and puts the previous group back on the way out, so a nested tuning pass can't leave a stale one behind.
- Sharing the timings only helps if the ranks start from the same cache, because a cache hit skips a profile and knocks them out of step. `_drop_diverged_autotune_cache` all-gathers a digest of what each rank would actually load — the cache file plus the environment stamp `load_configs` checks it against, since a stamp mismatch makes FlashInfer discard the file wholesale — and deletes the caches when those digests disagree.
- The extend pass used to swallow a rank-local OOM and carry on. Tuning is collective now, so carrying on would strand the other ranks inside the reduce; the OOM is re-raised whenever a sync group is active.
- `test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_flashinfer_autotune_sync.py` (CPU suite) covers the digest's load-decision semantics, plus the cache gate itself over a real 2-rank gloo group and real files: matching caches survive, diverged ones are dropped on every rank, and so are caches that differ only in their metadata stamp.

## Accuracy Tests

GPQA diamond on gpt-oss-120b TP=4, reasoning effort low, temperature 1.0. Each run grades 1,584 samples — 198 questions, eight shuffles each — and the whole run is repeated:

| | Runs | Mean |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 60.86 / 63.64 / 61.93 / 61.87 | **62.1** |
| After | 63.26 / 62.25 / 63.19 | **62.9** |

The sides overlap: 2.8 points of spread before, 1.0 after, 0.8 points between the means. Tactic selection picks among kernels FlashInfer treats as interchangeable for a given shape, and the scores agree.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`openai/gpt-oss-120b`, TP=4, 4x GB300, clean autotune cache for each configuration. "Before" is the same build without the cross-rank reduction.

Single stream, `python -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 8 --max-concurrency 1 --warmup-requests 8 --flush-cache`, three repetitions:

| | Output tok/s | Mean E2E (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 508.74 / 509.99 / 509.95 → **509.56 ± 0.72** | 2008.1 | 1.94–1.95 |
| After | 510.60 / 510.61 / 510.83 → **510.68 ± 0.13** | 2003.7 | 1.94 |

At concurrency 32 (1k in / 512 out, 128 prompts) total throughput went 22,956 → 23,130 tok/s.

Both deltas — +0.22% and +0.8% — are small enough that the honest claim is no regression rather than a speedup, though they point the same way the tactic-cost numbers above predict. The clearer effect is stability: run-to-run spread tightened about 5x (±0.13 vs ±0.72 tok/s), which is what you'd expect once all four ranks are running the same kernel.

Tuning wall-clock goes 79 s → 106 s from the extra per-tactic reduction. That's paid once — the result is cached, and a warm restart reuses it with no retune and no cache drop.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — nothing user-facing to document.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [mxfp8-kv] Skip writes to the reserved CUDA-graph padding slot
author: sshleifer
body:
## Motivation

Slot 0 of the KV pool is the reserved CUDA-graph padding sink: padded lanes write their dummy K/V there, and padded page-table entries read its page back. Padding lanes carry undefined activations (upstream model kernels legitimately leave rows past the real token count uninitialized), which the MXFP8 path quantizes into NaN fp8 payload and `0xFF` (e8m0 NaN) scale bytes.

The bf16 write path already guards this: the `store_cache` jit kernel skips writes targeting `reserved_skip_index` (slot 0), so the reserved page keeps its zeros. The MXFP8 pool had no equivalent guard on any of its write paths — the direct fancy-index stores, `store_sf_interleaved` (scales), and the fused `quant_store_kv_mxfp8` kernel all wrote to slot 0. A poisoned slot 0 is then read back by attention for padded/masked lanes, where a NaN V defeats probability masking (`0 * NaN = NaN` in the PV accumulator) and poisons real outputs. We root-caused a production NaN crash in MXFP8-KV serving (galileo-class hybrid model, prefill CUDA graphs) to exactly this write-side poison; the bf16 configuration was immune only because it has the `store_cache` guard.

## Modifications

Same skip-at-source design as the bf16 path, with the skip inside kernels that were already running (measured cost: run noise vs the unguarded baseline):

- The direct path (precomputed scales) now routes the fp8 payload through the `store_cache` jit kernel — a byte-width-agnostic row copier (fp8 row = `head_num * head_dim` bytes) that already skips `reserved_skip_index = 0` — and fuses the K+V scatters into one launch. Asserts replace the previous fancy-index writes and capture-mode alt-stream branch: this pool is CUDA-only (`float8_e8m0fnu` + triton + FA4) and `head_dim % 32 == 0` makes rows always `store_cache`-compatible, so those paths were unreachable.
- `_store_sf_interleaved_kernel` masks out `slots == 0` (one predicate).
- `_mxfp8_quant_store_qkv_kernel` (fused quant-store path) returns early when `myloc == 0`.

## Test

`test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_mxfp8_kv_reserved_slot.py` (next to `test_store_cache.py`, which covers the bf16 guard; SM100+): the direct and fused `set_kv_buffer` paths leave slot 0 at exactly zero payload/scale bytes under NaN padding-lane writes, and `set_kv_buffer` captures and replays inside a `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph`.

Negative control (verified on the equivalent internal tree): with the fix reverted, all tests fail with "reserved slot K payload written"; with the fix, all pass. The asserts require slot 0 to equal its init value rather than merely be NaN-free, so finite-garbage writes fail too.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code with pre-commit
- [x] Add unit tests

-Robot

title: [diffusion] make --vae-tiling honest, fix the decode OOM advice, gate NVFP4 on Blackwell
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary
Three failures that all present as something other than what they are. Found while auditing consumer-GPU support.

**`--vae-tiling` was a silent no-op on any VAE without `enable_tiling`.** The call sat under a bare `except Exception: pass`. MiniMax-H3's VAE is one of those, and it happens to tile anyway because `decoder_tiling` is set from its VAE config at construction — so the flag looked accepted while doing nothing, and the OOM message below told users to reach for it. `AutoencoderKL` now has `enable_tiling` (`decoder_tiling` is read per decode in `_adaptive_decode`, so setting it takes effect on the next call), and the caller's guard narrows to `AttributeError` and names the VAE class instead of discarding the request. Every `enable_tiling` implementation in the tree takes only optional arguments, so narrowing the guard cannot turn a previously swallowed error into a crash.

**The decode OOM handler recommended `--vae-cpu-offload`,** which moves VAE weights and does nothing for the activations that overflow. Decode runs after denoising, so the DiT and encoders are idle but may still hold VRAM — freeing them is the actual lever. The message now points at `--cpu-offload-components`, then tile size, then resolution.

**`ModelOptFp4Config.get_min_capability()` declared 100 but was never called.** The only real gate was whether flashinfer imports, so on a pre-Blackwell card with flashinfer installed the load succeeded and then failed inside the CUDA kernel with an opaque error. The FP4 linear method now enforces the declared minimum. A GPU whose capability cannot be read is left alone, so this only ever turns a crash into a message and never blocks a card that would have worked.

## Test plan
- [x] New unit test covers the gate's three branches: reject below the minimum (8.6 / 8.9 / 9.0), allow Blackwell (10.0 / 12.0), and leave an undetectable capability alone.
- [x] Real hardware, H200 (compute capability 9.0): the gate rejects with `NVFP4 checkpoints need compute capability 10.0 or newer (Blackwell); this GPU is 9.0.` instead of reaching the kernel.
- [x] Verified on the same box that `MiniMaxH3VideoVAE` now resolves `enable_tiling`, and that its `decoder_tiling` is already true at construction.
- [x] Audited all four `enable_tiling` implementations for required arguments before narrowing the guard.

**Not covered:** the allow path on live Blackwell silicon — no B200/B300/5090 capacity was free. It is exercised with a mocked capability, and the values match this repo's own detection (`is_blackwell()` is `major == 10`, `is_sm120()` is `major == 12`, both ≥ 100 via `DeviceCapability.to_int()`). The two OOM log branches are also not triggered end to end; they are message-only changes.

title: [diffusion] feat: load GGUF transformer checkpoints (MiniMax-H3)
author: zijiexia
body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-H3's transformer is 61.7 GiB in BF16, and the FL2VA partition is
135 GiB in total. Layerwise offload already lets the model run on a consumer
GPU, so the remaining barriers are the checkpoint download, host memory, and
bytes streamed per layer.

This adds a pre-quantized GGUF transformer path. The validated Q4_K_M DiT is
17.5 GiB instead of 61.7 GiB. It complements online `kitchen_int8`: GGUF avoids
first downloading and pinning the complete BF16 DiT, while `kitchen_int8`
remains the faster compute-oriented path.

## Interface

`--model-path` continues to provide the pipeline components and
`--transformer-weights-path` selects the GGUF DiT. The loader accepts a local
file, `owner/repo/path/file.gguf`, or `owner/repo:QUANT_TYPE` when that suffix
matches exactly one file. Repositories containing multiple variants require
the full file path.

```bash
sglang serve \
  --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \
  --model-variant fl2va \
  --transformer-weights-path \
    leejet/MiniMax-H3-GGUF/minimax_h3_fl2va-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --attention-backend fa \
  --performance-mode memory \
  --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \
  --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \
  --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0 \
  --enable-torch-compile false \
  --port 30010
```

`--quantization gguf` is intentionally rejected: quantization is encoded in
the checkpoint and the file path is the selector.

## Implementation

- Reuses SRT's GGUF file detection, Hub resolver, quantization type sets, and
  CUDA dequantization helper. Diffusion no longer carries duplicate download
  resolution, GGML support tables, or dequantization shape logic.
- Keeps a small diffusion-specific header reader because model construction
  needs each tensor's exact logical and packed shape before parameters exist.
  Packed tensors stay mmap-backed until the generic loader copies their TP
  shard, which avoids cloning the complete 17.5 GiB checkpoint during load.
- Uses dequantization followed by native GEMM for DiT linears. SRT's fused
  MMVQ/MMQ path is optimized for low-token LLM inference and regresses normal
  diffusion sequence lengths.
- Supports block-aligned tensor parallel row/column/merged linear slicing.
  Incompatible TP degrees fail during model construction.
- Supports both the original MiniMax-H3 timestep MLP and pruned community
  checkpoints containing an unquantized `adaln_t_table` curve.
- Fails before download for conflicting or unsupported configurations:
  non-CUDA, FSDP for the GGUF component, LoRA, another `--quantization`,
  SVDQuant, and the separate MiniMax-H3 AdaLN cache/online paths.
- Keeps `quality=high` fail-closed when replacement transformer weights are
  supplied.

F32/F16/BF16 tensors use the ordinary linear path. Quantized tensors must be
2D `.weight` matrices and have valid GGML block alignment; malformed, corrupt,
opposite-endian, or unsupported files fail at load.

## Validation

### Automated

- Changed-files pre-commit: passed.
- Focused remote NVIDIA suite: **163 passed, 2 subtests passed**.
- Coverage includes header corruption/endianness/BF16 handling, Hub
  resolution and ambiguity, type selection, CPU-offload loading, pre-download
  guards, quality admission, pruned curve interpolation, and TP
  row/column/merged slicing.

### Kernel selection

On H200 with the real H3 Q4_K QKV matrix `(21504, 5376)`, fused MMVQ is useful
only at one or two tokens. At 256 and 2048 tokens, SRT MMQ took 2.60 ms and
20.61 ms versus 0.37 ms and 0.91 ms for dequantize + GEMM. The final diffusion
adapter therefore keeps the native-GEMM path.

### End to end

1x H200, FL2VA Q4_K_M, layerwise-offloaded DiT/text encoder, fixed seed,
1344x768, 107 frames, 2 inference steps:

| Revision | Warmup | Generation | Peak GPU | Output |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Original PR dense-dequant path | 12.67 s | 10.11 s | 17,174 MB | H.264 + AAC |
| Refactored SRT-reuse path | 12.64 s | 10.13 s | 17,174 MB | H.264 + AAC |

The two MP4 files are byte-identical (same SHA-256; PSNR infinite, SSIM 1.0).
The refactored loader constructed the 17.49 GiB DiT in about 1 second versus
about 19 seconds in the original PR run because packed values are no longer
cloned wholesale during iteration.

The pruned `unsloth/MiniMax-H3-GGUF` FL2VA Q4_K checkpoint also completed
server warmup and a real 1344x768, 107-frame video + AAC request on H200; its
loaded DiT size was 10.72 GiB.

The original RTX 5090 measurements remain valid: 39.0 s denoise and 26.3 GiB
peak with `dit,text_encoder` offload; adding VAE offload lowered peak to
19.6 GiB and increased VAE decode from 9.5 s to 57.2 s.

Not yet validated end to end: `ref2va`, quantization types other than the
listed Q4 variants, and multi-GPU GGUF. TP packed slicing is unit-tested, but a
requested 2x H100 validation box remained in infrastructure provisioning and
is not reported as a successful run.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Update CLI, quantization, compatibility, and MiniMax-H3 documentation.
- [x] Run real checkpoint and end-to-end NVIDIA validation.

title: [Spec] DFlash2: local convolution + candidate selector
author: SubSir
body:
## Motivation

Two additions to the DFlash draft, both switched on by the checkpoint. A DFlash
checkpoint declares neither and takes the path it always took.

**Grouped dynamic depthwise convolution** inside each block, so a proposal
position can see the ones before it without another backbone pass.
`out[i,c] = Σ_t (base[t,c] + δ[i,t,g(c)]) · x[i−t,c]`, taps zero across the block
boundary. Wraps each sublayer in and out from one projection of its input.
On when `conv_kernel_size` and `conv_group_size` are set.

**Candidate selector.** Instead of an independent argmax per slot, keep the
target head's top-K per slot, score adjacent transitions
`edge(p→c) = ⟨A[p] ⊙ project(h), B[c]⟩ + unary[c]`, and walk the best path from
the verified anchor. At T>0 it walks by inverse CDF and returns q over the K
candidates for the lossless verify. On when `selector_rank` and
`selector_top_k` are set.

## Modifications

```
srt/models/dflash.py                 the convolution, the selector, the walk kernel
srt/speculative/dflash_utils.py      four config fields
srt/speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py  the proposal and the T>0 verify
```

The selector's decode is folded into the draft CUDA graph, greedy and sampled
alike. The walk is one Triton program per request: a slot's K scores stay in
registers, greedy rows take the argmax and emit a one-hot q, and the slot-to-slot
dependency is a loop inside the program rather than a kernel per slot. No new
server args, no new env vars, nothing outside DFlash touched.

## Accuracy Tests

```
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/spec/test_dflash_logits.py
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/model_executor/model_runner_components/test_spec_aux_hidden_state.py
```

`4 passed` and `5 passed`. `test_dflash_logits.py` covers the selector's sampled path end to end,
the mixed greedy/sampling batch — each row identical to running it alone, with
greedy rows asserted to carry a one-hot q — and the rejection of a quantized
target LM head.

Lossless decoding is the property that matters here and it is structural: greedy
walks emit the point mass at the token they take, and sampled walks return the
realized q over the K candidates, so the verify sees the proposal distribution it
actually drew from.

## Speed Tests and Profiling


Published evaluation for
[`z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`](https://huggingface.co/z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2)
on `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`: SGLang on one H200 with FlashAttention 3, block size 8
(seven draft tokens per verification step), Qwen3.8's recommended sampling
(temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20) at `xhigh` reasoning effort, 4096 max new
tokens, prompts formatted by [`z-lab/dflash`](https://github.com/z-lab/dflash).
Compared against the target's built-in MTP and a community DSpark drafter,
[`RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark`](https://huggingface.co/RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark),
both also proposing seven tokens per step.

### Acceptance length

Per-request mean of completion tokens over verification steps.

| Dataset | MTP | DSpark | DFlash 2 |
|---------|----:|-------:|---------:|
| GSM8K | 5.02 | 4.36 | **5.46** |
| MATH-500 | 4.72 | 3.92 | **5.28** |
| HumanEval | 3.91 | 3.30 | **4.39** |
| MBPP | 3.99 | 3.51 | **4.79** |
| MT-Bench | 3.74 | 3.01 | **4.10** |

### Throughput, GSM8K

Output tokens over end-to-end wall time, with speedup over autoregressive
decoding.

| conc | autoregressive | MTP | DSpark | DFlash 2 |
|------|---------------:|----:|-------:|---------:|
| 1 | 68.9 | 178.5 (2.59×) | 185.3 (2.69×) | **236.1 (3.43×)** |
| 8 | 467.2 | 1,022.1 (2.19×) | 1,040.8 (2.23×) | **1,328.7 (2.84×)** |
| 32 | 1,329.8 | 1,381.1 (1.04×) | 1,506.5 (1.13×) | **1,922.5 (1.45×)** |

Full tables for the other four datasets, and for
[`z-lab/Muse-Glimmer-30B-DFlash2`](https://huggingface.co/z-lab/Muse-Glimmer-30B-DFlash2)
against Meta's published DFlash assistant, are on the model cards.

### What it costs

The convolution and the selector are the whole difference between a DFlash draft
and a DFlash 2 draft, so their cost is what a step loses by having them. Measured
against Meta's published DFlash assistant on the same target,
[`meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B`](https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B),
block 16, GSM8K, four H200 shards. `cost` is `(1 + accept gain) / (1 + throughput
gain) - 1` — the throughput gain the extra acceptance would have produced had the
step stayed the same length, against the gain it actually produced.

| conc | acceptance | throughput | cost | | acceptance | throughput | cost |
|------|-----------:|-----------:|-----:|---|-----------:|-----------:|-----:|
| | **T=0** | | | | **T=1** | | |
| 1 | +13.6% | +11.7% | 1.7% | | +24.4% | +21.1% | 2.7% |
| 8 | +14.0% | +11.4% | 2.3% | | +24.5% | +21.5% | 2.5% |
| 32 | +14.1% | +11.9% | 2.0% | | +24.0% | +21.2% | 2.3% |
| 64 | +14.0% | +12.3% | 1.5% | | +24.3% | +22.2% | 1.7% |

So 1.5–2.7%, and it falls as the batch grows: the target verify grows with the
batch while the selector's work does not keep pace. It falls as the target grows
for the same reason.

Acceptance enters this table only as a ratio between the two drafts, both
measured the same way — as total accepted tokens over total verification steps,
where the model card reports a mean over per-request ratios. The two statistics
differ on absolute values but nearly cancel in the gain: +24.3% here at
concurrency 64 against the card's +21.0% for the same pair of checkpoints.

title: [Kernel] Support wider rows in mega_moe_pre_dispatch
body:
## Motivation

`mega_moe_pre_dispatch` assigns one thread to each 8-element input chunk, so a single CUDA block can only cover hidden dimensions up to 8192. Wider shapes are rejected before launch.

## Modifications

- Cap the block size at the CUDA 1024-thread limit and process wider rows in strided chunks.
- Recompute quantization-group indices for each chunk while preserving the UE8M0 scale layout.
- Keep a separate single-chunk kernel specialization so existing shapes retain the same instruction path.
- Reject wide shapes whose tail would split a warp-level reduction.

## Accuracy Tests

- Verified bitwise FP8 output and UE8M0 scale bytes against a reference implementation for hidden dimensions 3584, 5632, 8192, 12288, and 16384.
- Verified exact top-k copies and idle-slot padding.
- Verified that hidden dimension 8320 fails with the expected full-warp alignment error.
- JIT-compiled the ported CUDA header successfully.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- The single-chunk specialization produces the same SASS instruction stream as the previous kernel.
- CUDA-event microbenchmarks showed no measurable regression for shapes that already fit in one chunk.

title: [Kernel] Add H200 MoE configs for Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6
author: vedantjh2
body:
## Summary

Add NVIDIA H200 Triton 3.6 fused-MoE configs for:

- Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8: `E=256,N=512`, block FP8 `[128,128]`, TP1, with separate up/gate and down-projection tables
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8: the cached checkpoint requests the same lookup keys and shares the Qwen3.5 FP8 tables
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-BF16: `E=256,N=512`, TP1, with separate up/gate and decode-aware down-projection tables

The unsupported Qwen3.8 MoE entry has been removed. Qwen3.8-27B is a dense hybrid-attention model, so it cannot use these MoE tables. Its H200 packed-GDN and ReplaySSM verification candidates were tuned and validated separately; both were end-to-end neutral and are not included in this change.

## Full-model GSM8K validation

All primary comparisons used one H200, SGLang v0.5.17, the official `benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py`, five shots, temperature 0, a 20-question warmup, ten 200-question repetitions per A/B/A phase, and closed-loop parallelism 64 without a request-rate or TPOT throttle. Changes are against the mean of the A1 and A2 phase medians.

| Model | A1 latency / throughput | Tuned latency / throughput | A2 latency / throughput | Drift-adjusted change | Accuracy A1 / tuned / A2 | Invalid |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5 FP8 | 12.575 s / 3151.08 tok/s | 11.693 s / 3290.12 tok/s | 12.792 s / 3187.02 tok/s | **-7.81% latency, +3.82% throughput** | 0.775 / 0.768 / 0.768 | 0% |
| Qwen3.6 FP8 | 8.793 s / 2965.50 tok/s | 7.999 s / 3128.58 tok/s | 8.403 s / 2879.70 tok/s | **-6.96% latency, +7.05% throughput** | 0.415 / 0.425 / 0.413 | 0% |
| Qwen3.6 BF16 | 14.812 s / 2620.40 tok/s | 14.919 s / 2628.53 tok/s | 14.996 s / 2640.67 tok/s | +0.10% latency, -0.08% throughput | 0.518 / 0.518 / 0.525 | 0% |

Qwen3.6 BF16 was also tested at saturated parallelism 128 using all 1,319 GSM8K questions, with three repetitions per phase:

| Phase | Median latency | Median output throughput | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline A1 | 84.680 s | 2906.36 tok/s | 0.600 | 0% |
| Tuned | 85.558 s | 2980.93 tok/s | 0.534 | 0% |
| Baseline A2 | 85.536 s | 2934.67 tok/s | 0.527 | 0% |

The bracket estimate is **+2.07% throughput** and +0.53% latency. A1 had substantial output/accuracy drift; tuned closely matched A2, where it was +1.58% throughput with effectively unchanged latency. This is a saturation-throughput result, not a latency or quality claim.

## Isolated kernel results

### Qwen3.5 FP8 up/gate

| Routed tokens | Baseline | Tuned | Latency reduction |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 256 | 255.43 us | 220.90 us | 13.52% |
| 512 | 265.41 us | 242.75 us | 8.54% |
| 1024 | 284.93 us | 274.94 us | 3.50% |

### Qwen3.5 FP8 down projection

The dedicated down table improves on the previous up-table fallback at every tested serving size.

| Routed tokens | Up-table fallback | Tuned down | Incremental reduction |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 7.75 us | 7.34 us | 5.24% |
| 4 | 11.83 us | 11.26 us | 4.88% |
| 16 | 21.48 us | 20.30 us | 5.48% |
| 32 | 28.33 us | 26.83 us | 5.27% |
| 64 | 35.54 us | 33.43 us | 5.93% |
| 128 | 49.63 us | 46.91 us | 5.47% |
| 256 | 62.99 us | 57.25 us | 9.11% |
| 512 | 85.86 us | 74.59 us | 13.13% |
| 1024 | 107.87 us | 88.59 us | 17.87% |

### Qwen3.6 BF16

| Projection | Routed tokens | Baseline | Tuned | Latency reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Up/gate | 256 | 191.70 us | 181.01 us | 5.58% |
| Up/gate | 512 | 328.60 us | 217.48 us | 33.82% |
| Up/gate | 1024 | 374.91 us | 241.59 us | 35.56% |
| Down | 1 | 8.11 us | 6.96 us | 14.23% |
| Down | 4 | 17.21 us | 15.61 us | 9.25% |
| Down | 16 | 32.50 us | 30.57 us | 5.94% |
| Down | 32 | 42.31 us | 39.10 us | 7.60% |
| Down | 64 | 54.86 us | 51.03 us | 6.98% |
| Down | 128 | 79.94 us | 75.17 us | 5.97% |
| Down | 256 | 105.84 us | 94.32 us | 10.88% |
| Down | 512 | 143.77 us | 115.12 us | 19.92% |
| Down | 1024 | 166.01 us | 131.28 us | 20.92% |

## Qwen3.8-27B dense-kernel evaluation

The public Qwen3.8-27B BF16 checkpoint was tested on the same H200:

- Packed-GDN exact shape `(H,HV,K,V)=(16,48,128,128)`: `BV=16`, 4 stages, 1 warp reduced aggregate B4-B32 kernel time by 5.89% (6.26% gain), with exact output and state matches in 14/14 correctness cases. Full-model A/B/A was neutral: **+0.02% throughput, -0.17% latency**. Rejected.
- ReplaySSM MTP verification exact-shape candidate: 3 stages and `NK=4`, compared against stock ReplaySSM-spec with identical EAGLE 3/1/4 settings. Full-model A/B/A was neutral: **+0.20% throughput, -0.15% latency**. Rejected.
- Operationally, enabling non-speculative ReplaySSM with its required `no_buffer` and overlap-disabled settings raised request capacity from 41 to 69 and measured **+16.06% throughput / -13.72% latency** with unchanged GSM8K accuracy. This is a server-configuration result, not a code change in this PR.

## Reproduce the GSM8K results

Use two source trees built from the same SGLang revision:

- `BASE_SOURCE`: the baseline tree
- `TUNED_SOURCE`: the same tree with this PR's diff applied

Run the commands below three times in order: `BASE_SOURCE` (A1), `TUNED_SOURCE` (B), then `BASE_SOURCE` again (A2). Set `SOURCE` accordingly and use a separate `OUTPUT_DIR` for each phase. Set `MODEL` to one of:

```bash
Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8
Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8
Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
```

Start the server:

```bash
export SOURCE=/path/to/sglang-source
export MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8
export PORT=30000
export DATA=/tmp/gsm8k_test.jsonl
export OUTPUT_DIR=/tmp/gsm8k-qwen
mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"

export PYTHONPATH="$SOURCE/python"
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path "$MODEL" \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port "$PORT" \
  --tp-size 1 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --random-seed 0 \
  >"$OUTPUT_DIR/server.log" 2>&1 &
SERVER_PID=$!

until curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health_generate" >/dev/null; do
  sleep 2
done
```

Run the official SGLang GSM8K warmup and ten measured repetitions:

```bash
python "$SOURCE/benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py" \
  --backend srt \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port "$PORT" \
  --data-path "$DATA" \
  --num-questions 20 \
  --num-shots 5 \
  --parallel 64 \
  --max-new-tokens 512 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --top-p 1 \
  --result-file "$OUTPUT_DIR/warmup-result.jsonl" \
  --raw-result-file "$OUTPUT_DIR/warmup-raw.jsonl"

for repeat in $(seq -w 1 10); do
  python "$SOURCE/benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py" \
    --backend srt \
    --host 127.0.0.1 \
    --port "$PORT" \
    --data-path "$DATA" \
    --num-questions 200 \
    --num-shots 5 \
    --parallel 64 \
    --max-new-tokens 512 \
    --temperature 0 \
    --top-p 1 \
    --result-file "$OUTPUT_DIR/run-$repeat-result.jsonl" \
    --raw-result-file "$OUTPUT_DIR/run-$repeat-raw.jsonl"
done

kill "$SERVER_PID"
wait "$SERVER_PID" || true
```

For the saturated Qwen3.6 BF16 run, change `--parallel 64` to `--parallel 128`, `--num-questions 200` to `--num-questions 1319`, and run three measured repetitions.

For the Qwen3.8-27B operational ReplaySSM comparison, use `MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`. Keep the baseline server command unchanged and add these flags to the optimized server:

```bash
--mamba-radix-cache-strategy no_buffer \
--disable-overlap-schedule \
--enable-linear-replayssm
```

For the isolated ReplaySSM verification-kernel comparison, use the following flags on both baseline and tuned servers:

```bash
--speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
--speculative-num-steps 3 \
--speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
--enable-linear-replayssm-spec
```

## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA H200, TP1
- SGLang: v0.5.17 (`29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`)
- Torch: `2.11.0+cu130`
- Triton: 3.6.0
- `sgl_kernel`: 0.4.5
- GSM8K: canonical 1,319-example test set

The serving logs confirmed that the tuned H200 files were selected for both up/gate and down projections.

title: [Memory] Borrow CUDA graph pool storage for EAGLE sampling
author: cctry
body:
## Summary

- expose wholly-free runs in the shared CUDA graph pool through a persistent `torch.cuda.MemPool`
- allow stable, externally managed graph storage to register fixed borrow extents
- guard graph capture/replay and borrowed eager allocations with exclusive pool ownership
- reuse those runs for EAGLE's step-local full-vocabulary verification probabilities
- generalize the existing KV VMM bump allocator to support multiple caller-owned extents
- keep the feature opt-in with `SGLANG_ENABLE_GRAPH_POOL_BORROW=1`

## Safety

- only inactive runs from wholly-free graph-pool segments are exposed
- allocations fail normally if no single run can satisfy them; there is no silent fallback
- capture retires stale borrow extents before re-carving the graph pool
- capture, replay, and borrowing are mutually exclusive and report the conflicting users
- cross-stream deferred frees are drained before the persistent borrow pool is retired
- CUDA-only and default-off; the disabled path remains a no-op

title: [Spec] Generalize hybrid SWA MTP draft pool routing
author: paulzhang-tm

## Motivation

Multi-layer draft KV pools for hybrid sliding-window models are currently selected through Inkling-specific architecture checks. Other hybrid SWA models can expose the same per-depth attention pattern and should use the same SWA/full pool routing and memory accounting.

## Modifications

- Detect hybrid SWA multi-layer drafts from generic configurator state instead of an architecture name.
- Route each draft depth to the SWA or full-attention pool using the model's attention-layer metadata.
- Account for full-capacity draft SWA rings from optional `mtp_local_layer_ids` metadata across hybrid SWA architectures.
- Simplify comments that described the previous model-specific behavior.

This changes KV-pool configuration only. The relevant upstream unit suites pass:

title: [Diffusion] Support MiniMax-H3 pruned safetensors checkpoints
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- Build on the generic diffusion GGUF support merged in #35370; this PR no longer carries a duplicate GGUF loader or GGUF tests.
- Auto-detect MiniMax-H3 AdaLN-pruned BF16 and Comfy `pruned_fp8_scaled` transformer checkpoints.
- Reuse the native static-FP8 linear path where possible and preserve Comfy's `full_precision_matrix_mult` semantics for layers that require dequantized computation.
- Reject unsupported `pruned_int8_convrot` checkpoints before model construction instead of failing later with misleading missing-weight errors.

## Loading and compatibility

- `--transformer-weights-path` accepts a local file, a direct Hugging Face file URL, or an `owner/repo/path/file.safetensors` reference.
- FL2VA and Ref2VA checkpoint/model-variant mismatches are rejected explicitly.
- TP, Ulysses/Ring sequence parallelism, and component offload remain available. Pruned BF16 supports FSDP; Comfy mixed-FP8 checkpoints reject FSDP because their per-layer quantization metadata cannot be represented by the current FSDP loading path.
- Self-described Comfy FP8 checkpoints reject a conflicting explicit `--quantization` setting.
- `quality=high` continues to require the audited official BF16 transformer rather than a replacement DiT.

## Documentation

- Document pruned BF16 and scaled-FP8 loading commands, compatibility, and unsupported ConvRot checkpoints in the MiniMax-H3 cookbook.
- Update the diffusion quantization matrix to distinguish generic GGUF support from the Comfy scaled-FP8 format added here.

## Verification

- Inspected the published Comfy FP8 safetensors metadata: 200 per-layer format markers, including 50 `full_precision_matrix_mult` layers, with scalar weight/input scales matching the implemented dispatch.
- Added focused unit coverage for checkpoint inspection and validation, Hub file resolution, per-layer FP8 dispatch, full-precision dequantized linear numerics, quantization conflicts, and TP-aware MiniMax-H3 QKV loading.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` passed before the final focused change; all hooks also pass on the final changed files.
- Focused tests on the exact final commit in the remote CUDA environment: `56 passed, 16 subtests passed`.
- Real H100 end-to-end validation loaded the published 20,958,205,608-byte Comfy FP8 checkpoint, instantiated the 19.61 GB pruned DiT, and completed text encoding, denoising, video/audio decode, and muxing. The 2-step 1344x768 request produced 107 video frames plus stereo audio in 48.43 seconds with 21,236 MB peak VRAM. `ffprobe` reported H.264 video and 32 kHz two-channel AAC in the 4.458-second output.
- The shared H100 host killed additional worker processes during NCCL initialization before model loading, so multi-GPU end-to-end validation is left to CI. The TP-specific FP8 grouped-QKV copy path is covered directly for TP1/2/4 in the focused tests.

title: [CPU] Fix wrongly causal-masked bidirectional attention
author: chunyuan-w
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

On the Intel AMX CPU attention backend, `extend_attention_cpu` always masked the extend stage of attention as causal. This is correct for decoder-style self-attention, but wrong for bidirectional, encoder-only self-attention (e.g. BERT-family rerankers/embedders like bge-reranker). Such models silently got causally-masked attention scores, producing incorrect outputs.

When running `BAAI/bge-reranker-base` on CPU:
For the below request:
```
{
  "model": "BAAI/bge-reranker-base",
  "query": "what is panda?",
  "documents": [
    "hi",
    "The giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca), sometimes called a panda bear or simply panda, is a bear species endemic to China."
  ],
  "return_documents": true
}
```
Before this fix:
`"hi"` and  `"The giant panda ..."` both get the same score: 2.611328125, which is not reasonble.

After this fix:
Scores diverge correctly, matching what a real cross-encoder should produce:
`"The giant panda ..."`: score is 6.1875 (more relevant to the query so got a higher socre)
`"hi"`: score is -8.15625

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
- `python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/cpu/extend.cpp`: add an `is_causal` parameter (default `true`) to `extend_attention_cpu`. The stage-2 loop now iterates over the full extend range and only applies the causal mask when `is_causal` is set, instead of unconditionally limiting keys to `[0, m + BLOCK_M)` and masking `n + n_size - 1 > m`.

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/intel_amx_backend.py`: compute `is_causal = not (layer.is_cross_attention or layer.attn_type == AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY)` and pass it into `extend_attention_fwd`, mirroring the existing pattern in `triton_backend.py`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/ee1f2e8dfdbb264727134aeac4b8dec155ec6efe/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/triton_backend.py#L1360-L1368.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

```sh
python test/registered/cpu/test_extend.py -k test_extend_attention_bidirectional
```

title: [docs] Add a fused-kernels page for SGLang Diffusion
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Following the [`ops/diffusion` reorganization](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35114), the fused kernels that replace eager elementwise chains — adaLN modulate, residual gating, QK-norm, RoPE, norm epilogues, VAE layout kernels — have no user-facing page. The package `README.md` added in that PR is a selection matrix aimed at kernel authors, so there is nowhere to point someone who asks what is already fused, whether it changes their output, or how to turn on the parts that do.

This adds that page, in the spirit of Sol-Engine's [kernel techniques](https://nvlabs.github.io/Sana/Sol-Engine/docs/techniques/kernel/) page but following this site's conventions.

## Modifications

New page `docs/sglang-diffusion/fused_kernels.mdx`, registered under **Performance Optimization** and cross-linked from the overview's output-preserving lever table.

Contents:

- **The two numerical contracts.** Bit-exact fusions mount unconditionally and still verify themselves against the live eager chain on first sight, falling back permanently on mismatch. Fusions that differ from eager at half-precision rounding level mount only for `quality="high"`, at batch boundaries, all-or-nothing per transformer. The page explains why the distinction is not pedantic: multi-step denoising turns a per-step rounding difference into visible quality loss.
- **How to opt into the request-gated set** — `--quality high` on the CLI, and the `quality` field on the OpenAI-compatible endpoints — plus the list of families that mount.
- **An inventory by operator domain** (normalization, adaLN modulation, RoPE/QK-norm, activation, attention, data movement): what each of the 34 registered operators replaces, on which backend, under which contract.
- **Coverage by model**, since these kernels target a specific eager chain in a specific model rather than being general-purpose operators.
- **How to query the registry** and pin a backend, and the import contract (import from the package, predicate-plus-kernel pairs, lazy resolution).

Docs-only; no code changes.

## Accuracy

Every table row is derived from the merged tree rather than written from memory:

- the operator list, backends and capability sets come from the registry's `_SPECS` in `ops/diffusion/__init__.py` (34 operator ids across 38 implementations);
- the model-coverage table comes from the actual import sites under `multimodal_gen/runtime/models`;
- `--quality` and the OpenAI `quality` field were traced to `SamplingParams.quality` / `_runtime_sampling_quality` before being documented;
- both Python snippets were executed against the live registry:

```
diffusion ops: 34
  KernelBackend.TRITON   norm.rmsnorm_scale_shift_bitexact:fused_scale_residual_rmsnorm_scale_shift_bitexact  [CUDA]
  KernelBackend.CUTE_DSL norm.scale_residual_norm_cutedsl:fused_scale_residual_norm_scale_shift               [CUDA]
  KernelBackend.FLYDSL   norm.fused_residual_norm_flydsl:flydsl_fused_residual_norm_scale_shift               [HIP]
select_kernel -> KernelBackend.CUTE_DSL KernelSpec has load(): True
```

Relative links resolve to existing pages, `docs.json` parses, the page is reachable from the navigation, and headings follow the sentence-case rule in `docs/AGENTS.md`. The Mintlify CLI needs Node ≥ 20.17 and this machine has 18, so `mint broken-links` was replaced with an equivalent scripted check.

title: [Fix] Harden FlashAttention CUDA graph metadata bounds
author: aurickq
body:
## Motivation

Full-prefill CUDA graph buckets are sized by aggregate batch tokens, which can exceed the maximum context length of any single request. The FlashAttention sliding-window write-location buffer is currently allocated from max_context_len, so a valid aggregate-token bucket can exceed its capacity. Separately, idle graph batches may expose an empty CPU sequence-length tensor, for which max() is invalid.

## Modifications

- Size the full-prefill sliding-window write-location buffer from the captured token capacity.
- Validate replay token counts before copying into the graph-stable buffer.
- Use the static context bound when CPU sequence lengths are absent or empty.
- Add CPU regression tests for aggregate-token capacity, replay overflow detection, and empty idle batches.

## Accuracy Tests

No attention math is changed. The tests validate metadata sizing and fallback behavior.

- 2 focused unit tests passed.

title: [Quant] Load compressed-tensors kv_cache_scheme scales
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

compressed-tensors checkpoints that declare a `kv_cache_scheme` ship calibrated per-tensor attention `k_scale` / `v_scale` tensors, but they are silently dropped at load (`Parameter model.layers.N.k_scale not found in params_dict`), so `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` runs the cache unscaled. Three gaps compound:

- `CompressedTensorsConfig.from_config` never forwarded `kv_cache_scheme`, leaving it `None` even when declared.
- `get_quant_method` had no `RadixAttention` branch, so the `k_scale` / `v_scale` parameters were never created (ModelOpt has `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod` for this; the compressed-tensors equivalent was missing).
- The qwen3_5 weight mapper only knew the ModelOpt-style `.k_proj.k_scale` serialization; compressed-tensors stores the scales on the attention module (`.self_attn.k_scale`).

## Modifications

- Forward `kv_cache_scheme` in `from_config`.
- New `CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod(BaseKVCacheMethod)`, returned for `RadixAttention` when a `kv_cache_scheme` is declared. It accepts only what `BaseKVCacheMethod` can represent — static, symmetric, per-tensor FP8. A declared-but-unsupported scheme is skipped with a warning instead of failing the boot: such checkpoints serve correctly with an unquantized-scale KV cache, so refusing to load them would regress working deployments.
- A `kv_cache_quant_algo` property on the config: `configure_kv_cache_dtype` duck-types this field to resolve `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, so a declared supported scheme gets the fp8 pool its scales calibrate (ModelOpt parity). Without this, an auto-resolved bf16 pool would store unscaled entries while the attention backends apply the loaded scales on read.
- Two `orig_to_new_substr` entries in `QWEN3_5_KV_SCALE_MAPPER` for the attention-level scale names, and the mapper applied in the Qwen3.5 MTP loader for symmetry.
- Unit test: `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_kv_cache.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`).
- The pre-existing `kv_cache_scheme` remap in `apply_weight_name_mapper` (dead until this PR forwarded the scheme) is removed: the scheme holds schema fields, never module names, and `apply_dict` drops keys that match a mapper deletion rule.

Checkpoints without a `kv_cache_scheme` are unaffected (`get_quant_method` returns `None` for `RadixAttention` as before), and unloaded scales keep the existing default-to-1.0 behavior in `BaseKVCacheMethod.process_weights_after_loading`.

## Accuracy Tests

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, Qwen3.8-27B mixed-precision compressed-tensors checkpoint with a declared FP8 `kv_cache_scheme`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200`:

- Before: 32 `k_scale`/`v_scale` drop warnings at load; GSM8K 0.960 (cache unscaled — accuracy-benign on this checkpoint because the calibrated scales are near 1, but incorrect).
- After: zero drop warnings; GSM8K 0.965, invalid 0.000. Parity within the script's documented variance — this is a correctness fix for the calibration path, not an accuracy rescue.
- With `--kv-cache-dtype` left as `auto`: the pool now auto-resolves to `float8_e4m3fn` (previously bf16, ignoring the checkpoint's declared KV calibration); zero drop warnings; GSM8K 0.940 / 0.960 across two runs — statistically identical to the explicit-fp8 lane, as expected since both resolve to the same pool and scales.

Note: an MTP draft loaded from the same checkpoint carries the same config, so the draft worker's pool auto-resolves to fp8 as well (its scales default to 1.0; write/read stay symmetric). A standalone bf16 draft export without a `quantization_config` keeps a bf16 pool.

Known limit: an explicit bf16 `--kv-cache-dtype` override on a checkpoint with declared scales attaches scales to an unquantized pool — the same pre-existing exposure ModelOpt has today; a shared fix belongs in `BaseKVCacheMethod`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No runtime impact: scale resolution happens once at init; the scales feed the existing fp8 KV cache path.

title: [Spec] Support quantized target lm_head in the DFlash2 selector
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

DFlash2's selector matmuls draft hiddens against the target `lm_head.weight` directly, so quantized targets (ModelOpt NVFP4, compressed-tensors FP8) fail with `RuntimeError: DFlash2 selector requires a dense FP16/BF16/FP32 target lm_head` — on 32GB GPUs those checkpoints are the only way to serve Qwen3.8-27B. #34859 fixed the same problem for DSpark via `quant_method.apply`; this does the same for the DFlash2 selector.

Overlaps #35462 (@ryou315, credited as co-author): this PR additionally keeps the quantized logits contiguous by masking the padded tail instead of cropping — a padded local vocab crop otherwise fails flashinfer's radix top-k `CHECK_INPUT` at TP=1 and can hang TP>1, since only the rank holding the tail errors while its peers enter the all-gather.

Follow-ups split out of this PR so each stays reviewable on its own: #35580 (degenerate-config guard), #35581 (optional cleanup).

## Modifications

- `models/dflash.py`: `_project_candidate_logits` projects draft hiddens through the target head, restricted to the org vocab. When `should_apply_lm_head_quant_method` admits the head it runs `quant_method.apply` over the padded local vocab and masks the padded tail to `-inf` (a packed weight cannot be row-sliced like the dense path; masking keeps the logits contiguous with no copy, and does nothing when the vocab is unpadded). Both TP branches call it; their control flow is unchanged.
- `speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py` `_maybe_build_draft_sampler`: the selector branch accepts a dense head or one the quant gate admits, so quantized and dense heads take the same graph-folded `_SelectorDraftSampler` path (the captured kernel is the one the target's own logits path already runs under CUDA graphs). The dense-only screen still guards the non-selector static-matmul sampler.

## Accuracy Tests

RTX 5090, target `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (NVFP4-packed head), draft `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, greedy: both arms are byte-deterministic across fresh server boots (8/8 prompts each); spec vs target-only outputs fork only at near-tie tokens and 22/28 completed chains reach the same final answer — a stable numerics offset, not corruption. `sgl-eval run gsm8k` 200q: 95.5% with spec vs 98.0% target-only.

`test_dflash_logits.py`: 7/7 pass. The quant-path test asserts `apply()` runs on the packed weight, dominant padded garbage never reaches the candidates, and the logits handed to top-k are contiguous with `sorted`/`deterministic` set — the fake quant method returns a deliberately strided view and the top-k stub mirrors flashinfer's call contract, so an unmaterialized output fails the way the real kernel would. The TP test pins the per-shard org-vocab restriction, the global id offset, and the fp32 cast before the all-gather. A worker test pins the pre-capture screen: a gate-passing packed head is admitted to the folded selector sampler and attached before construction, an unsupported one stays eager. All mutation-verified: dropping the mask, the `.contiguous()`, the top-k flags, the id offset, the fp32 cast, or the worker admission each turns a test red. The dense-rejection test is kept for the negative branch.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No effect on dense-head targets (same matmul, same screen outcome). Quantized targets go from refusing to serve to serving. Same cell (RTX 5090, fp8 KV, concurrency 1):

- `sglang.benchmark.serving` random 8192/1024: TTFT 746.9 ms, median TPOT 7.10 ms, 129.5 output tok/s, accept 3.01 (DSPARK on the same cell: 7.73 ms, 116.5 tok/s, accept 2.59).
- GSM8K 200q: 186.5 output tok/s vs 66.6 target-only, accept length 4.85.
- Folded vs eager selector sampler isolated on 1024/1024: 5.58 vs 5.61 ms median TPOT with bit-identical accept lengths — the worker change is path consistency, and the two samplers demonstrably compute the same candidates.

title: [AMD] Improve K3 dspark draft attn kernel perf
author: 1am9trash
body: ## Motivation With DSpark on Kimi-K3, every step runs 5 draft attn layers (qwen-style, non-causal). Draft attn dominates their cost. In a trace study, the 5 draft layers took 2.368 ms, of which the 5 attn kernels alone accounted for 1.244 ms (>50%). The reason is that this falls back to `extend_attention_fwd`. This generic extend kernel is a poor fit for a shared-KV shape. > Note that draft attn is a common path. `--attention-backend` only selects the target-verify kernel. `aiter` is not among the draft worker's supported backends, so on ROCm the draft always falls back to `triton`. Both `--attention-backend triton` and `aiter` therefore reach the kernel this PR changes. ## Modifications Route DSpark draft attn to `verify_shared_kv`, and extend that kernel to cover the two cases it previously rejected. - **Non-causal situation**: The prefix loop never applies a causal mask, so only modify the stage-2 kernel. - **`h_kv > 1`**: Both stages add a KV-head offset (`head // kv_group_num * stride_h`). A `HAS_KV_HEADS` constexpr keeps the single-KV-head (MLA/MQA) path free of that arithmetic, so the existing Kimi-K3 target-verify path compiles exactly as before. Also adds a tuning entry for `head_dim=64` (`BLOCK_N=256`, 4 warps) and `is_dspark_draft()` in `model_config.py` for the gate. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8k, 1319: ``` 100%|███████████| 1319/1319 [02:00<00:00, 10.98it/s] Accuracy: 0.955 Invalid: 0.001 Latency: 120.085 s Output throughput: 1108.066 token/s ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Tested with docker image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260818`.
