title: fix(moe): support Llama4 NVFP4 router input weights on SM120
author: janbernloehr
body:
## Motivation

Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34192.

Llama 4 constructs its MoE layers with `apply_router_weight_on_input=True`. For ModelOpt NVFP4 on SM120/SM121, SGLang selects the FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE runner, which previously rejected this configuration during server warmup.

For top-1 routing, the required semantics can be implemented exactly by multiplying each token's hidden states by its router weight before activation quantization and passing unit final scales to CUTLASS. This follows the existing pattern in the AITER MoE runner.

The fix remains intentionally restricted to top-1 routing. With top-k greater than one, each selected expert would require a differently scaled copy of the input.

## Modifications

- Add top-1 router-weight pre-scaling to the common FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE execution path.
- Replace the kernel's output-side router scaling with float32 unit `token_final_scales` when pre-scaling is active.
- Normalize all `token_final_scales` passed through this CUTLASS path to float32, as required by the binding.
- Remove the ModelOpt NVFP4 and FlashInfer CUTLASS assertions that rejected `apply_router_weight_on_input=True`.
- Preserve explicit rejection for:
  - top-k greater than one;
  - activations already quantized before dispatch, including the FlashInfer CUTLASS FP4 all-gather path.
- Add focused CPU unit tests covering:
  - top-1 activation pre-scaling;
  - float32 unit final scales;
  - preservation of expert IDs;
  - top-k greater than one rejection;
  - pre-quantized dispatch rejection.

The normal `apply_router_weight_on_input=False` path is unchanged apart from enforcing the CUTLASS binding's float32 scale requirement.

## Accuracy Tests

Added:

```text
test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_flashinfer_cutlass_router_weight.py
```

The tests compare the transformed hidden states and final scales against the expected top-1 formulation and verify that unsupported configurations fail explicitly.

Local validation:

```text
python -m py_compile \
  python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py \
  python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_flashinfer_cutlass_router_weight.py
```

Result: passed.

All commit-time pre-commit checks passed, including Python AST validation, isort, Ruff, Black, codespell, and registered-test validation.

The focused pytest test could not be executed in the local development environment because PyTorch is not installed. No real-checkpoint accuracy test was run for this checkout.

The equivalent patch and its SM120/SM121 validation evidence are documented in #34192. That validation used dummy weights for end-to-end liveness, so it is not claimed as a model-accuracy result.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed test or profiling was run for this checkout.

The equivalent patch validation documented in #34192 completed both SM120 scenarios without errors and did not show a decode throughput regression. Those results used dummy weights and a separate validated build, so they are included only as prior evidence, not as performance results for this commit.

title: [Deepseek-V4] Enable shared-experts fusion on the flashinfer_mxfp4 (trtllm-gen) MoE path
author: shikicloud
body:
## Summary

Enable shared-experts fusion for DeepSeek-V4-Flash on the `flashinfer_mxfp4` (trtllm-gen) path: the shared expert is routed as expert slot 256 through the same MoE kernel, so the whole MoE runs on a single stream instead of a separate FP8 MLP on an alternate stream (~4 fewer kernel launches + 2 fewer stream syncs per layer). The machinery already existed (#27349); this PR enables and validates it. Also adds a guard rejecting fusion under EP without per-rank shared slots, which would silently compute wrong results.

## Scope

- `deepseek_v4.py`: EP guard in the fusion gate (11 lines).
- New CPU unit test for the load-time FP8→MXFP4 shared-expert requant (byte-level packing/scale contract).
- Docs: new "Shared experts fusion (Blackwell, flashinfer_mxfp4)" subsection in the DeepSeek-V4 cookbook (usage, gains, no-EP constraint). Recipe commands left unchanged per review.

## Testing

- Kernel: verified out-of-tree on GB200 with a standalone test at the fused shape (257 experts / top-k 7, every token hits the shared slot), 12/12 vs a dequantized torch reference; no flashinfer change needed. Test available on request.
- Unit: `test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_mxfp4_shared_expert_requant.py`.
- Profiler: with fusion on, the shared-expert kernels disappear and the MoE runs on a single stream.

## Results

GB200 tp4, only variable is the fusion flag.

Accuracy:

| Benchmark | baseline (off) | fused (on) |
|---|---|---|
| gsm8k 8-shot 1319q (3 runs) | 0.949 / 0.954 / 0.954 | 0.951 / 0.952 / 0.948 |
| AIME25 pass@1[avg-of-16] (thinking, effort max) | 99.79% ± 0.83 | 99.17% ± 1.49 |
| AIME25 pass@16 / majority@16 | 100% / 100% | 100% / 100% |

Performance (bench_serving, random 1024in/512out):

title: [GDN] Amortize ReplaySSM checkpoint materialization
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

ReplaySSM speculative decoding currently materializes the full GDN checkpoint state on every target step, even though most speculative iterations only append a small amount of history. Deferring that work removes repeated state materialization from the decode critical path.

## Modifications

- Store speculative GDN updates in a bounded circular history and materialize the checkpoint once per accepted verify window.
- Preserve recurrent BF16 behavior with compensated high/low representations for the compact update vector and normalized key.
- Keep replay history and cursors request-scoped while keeping the physical checkpoint Mamba-slot-scoped.
- Size ReplaySSM scratch by active request capacity, and preserve reset, donation, retraction, and recovery lifetimes.

The review scope is limited to the ReplaySSM kernel, the request/state ownership and accounting needed by that kernel, and one existing accounting test. The larger experimental compatibility framework and additional defensive abstractions are not part of this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

- Nine targeted GPU tests passed, covering existing accounting/support checks plus BF16 and FP32 64-window recurrent comparisons and request-capacity allocation.
- A monolithic aggregate TP4 serving smoke test completed successfully and returned exactly 512 output tokens.
- ReplaySSM scratch is `0.857 GB/GPU` versus `0.849 GB/GPU` before the PR. CUDA-graph startup available memory is `36.129-36.131 GB` versus `36.143-36.145 GB`; the earlier approximately `3.6 GB/GPU` headroom regression is removed.

### AIME25 128K x4

The comparison uses Qwen3.5 on one 4-GPU node, aggregate TP4/DP1/PP1/EP1 serving, MTP, ReplaySSM, BF16 SSM state, 128K context, four repeats, and the same 30 problems.

| Configuration | ReplaySSM | pass@1 | majority@4 | pass@4 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before PR: old ReplaySSM implementation | Enabled | 86.67% | 88.33% | **96.67% (29/30)** |
| Current ReplaySSM implementation | Enabled | 87.50% | 96.11% | **100.00% (30/30)** |

| Configuration | Repeat 0 | Repeat 1 | Repeat 2 | Repeat 3 | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before PR: old ReplaySSM implementation | 28/30 | 26/30 | 25/30 | 25/30 | 104/120 |
| Current ReplaySSM implementation | 26/30 | 27/30 | 26/30 | 26/30 | 105/120 |

The current run produced all `120/120` predictions with zero harness errors and `3,019,855` completion tokens.

### AIME25 128K x8

For additional confidence, the old and current ReplaySSM implementations were rerun with the same serving/evaluation contract and eight repeats. `pass@N` is the fraction of the 30 problems with at least one correct answer among `N` attempts; it is not the average accuracy across repeats.

| Configuration | ReplaySSM | pass@1 | majority@8 | pass@8 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before PR: old ReplaySSM implementation | Enabled | 91.67% | 96.67% | **100.00% (30/30)** |
| Current ReplaySSM implementation | Enabled | 92.08% | 97.78% | **100.00% (30/30)** |

| Configuration | R0 | R1 | R2 | R3 | R4 | R5 | R6 | R7 | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before PR: old ReplaySSM implementation | 28/30 | 26/30 | 28/30 | 29/30 | 28/30 | 27/30 | 27/30 | 27/30 | 220/240 |
| Current ReplaySSM implementation | 26/30 | 26/30 | 28/30 | 28/30 | 27/30 | 29/30 | 28/30 | 29/30 | 221/240 |

Both arms produced all `240/240` predictions with zero harness errors and passed all 30 problems at pass@8. The current implementation is `+1/240` in total correct attempts (`92.08%` versus `91.67%`).

### Logits and long-sequence stability

- Four independent AIME27 traces completed successfully; all four produced the correct answer (`248`).
- Over the token-aligned common prefix with the old implementation (406 tokens on average), top-1 agreement is `99.92%`, mean top-5 Jensen-Shannon divergence is `3.82e-4`, and mean absolute chosen-logprob delta is `7.42e-3`.
- An independent rerun of the compact implementation gives `100%` top-1 agreement and a `7.61e-3` mean absolute chosen-logprob delta over its common prefix, placing the old-versus-current delta at the same scale as run-to-run variation.
- After token paths diverge, the values are confidence diagnostics rather than token-aligned numerical error. Across a 34,816-token horizon, chosen-logprob variance decreases from `0.0194` to `0.0105` and entropy decreases from `0.0706` to `0.0464`; there is no evidence of error or variance accumulating with generation length.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- Setup: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 on one node with 4 GB300 GPUs in DP4, MTP with 6 draft tokens, TRTLLM-MHA split 1, ReplaySSM `extra_buffer`, radix-cache page size 64, and the same frozen 112-request cohort in both arms.
- Workload: every request uses exactly 88,737 input tokens and generates exactly 8,192 output tokens. Requests are prefetched before measurement; no new prefill is admitted during the pure-generation interval.
- Acceptance criteria: 112/112 HTTP 200 responses, routed distribution `[28, 28, 28, 28]`, achieved batch 28 on every rank, CUDA graph enabled, queue depth 0, no replenishment, and measurement ending before the first completion.

title: [Qwen3.5][MTP] Preserve online NVFP4 draft quantization for mixed checkpoints
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

When a mixed ModelOpt checkpoint is used with an explicitly configured `nvfp4_online` speculative draft model, checkpoint detection currently overwrites the explicit draft quantization choice with `modelopt_mixed`. This prevents the MTP draft MoE from using the intended load-time NVFP4 conversion and FlashInfer CuTeDSL execution path.

## Modifications

- Preserve an explicitly selected `nvfp4_online` draft quantization mode for both `modelopt_fp4` and `modelopt_mixed` checkpoints.
- Keep the existing default behavior unchanged: when the user does not explicitly select draft quantization, the draft model still inherits the target model quantization.
- Do not change the speculative decoding algorithm or automatically enable online NVFP4 on unsupported configurations.

## Accuracy Tests

- The Blackwell production serving validation completed 112/112 identical requests with HTTP 200, fixed input length 88,786 tokens, exact output length 860 tokens, all four ranks at achieved batch 28, all CUDA graph captures enabled, zero queueing/retractions/errors, and natural mean acceptance length 4.79792.
- This path is explicitly opt-in and limited by the existing SM100+ and FlashInfer MoE backend checks.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- Setup: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 on one node with 4 GB300 GPUs in DP4, fixed ISL 88,786, exact OSL 860, 112 identical requests, MTP with 6 draft tokens, TRTLLM-MHA split 1, ReplaySSM circular history, and no request replenishment during the pure-generation measurement window.
- Patch-level result with the same candidate command: before this change, checkpoint detection overwrites the explicit `nvfp4_online` draft setting with `modelopt_mixed`, which creates an incompatible draft runner/dispatcher combination and fails before serving; after this change, the command completes 112/112 requests. Because the unpatched control does not reach the benchmark, there is no patch-only throughput ratio.
- The throughput numbers below compare two valid end-to-end draft backend configurations and are not an apple-to-apple attribution of the three-line compatibility fix.
- Valid legacy baseline command; orchestration-only and identical arguments are omitted:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4> --dp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --attention-backend trtllm_mha --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 --speculative-moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --speculative-moe-a2a-backend deepep
```

- Candidate command enabled by this fix:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4> --dp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --attention-backend trtllm_mha --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 --speculative-moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl --speculative-moe-a2a-backend flashinfer --speculative-draft-model-quantization nvfp4_online
```

- Full configuration change used by the throughput experiment:

```diff
--- baseline
+++ candidate
- --speculative-moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --speculative-moe-a2a-backend deepep
+ --speculative-moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl --speculative-moe-a2a-backend flashinfer --speculative-draft-model-quantization nvfp4_online
```

| Valid configuration | Natural mean acceptance length | Target-step time (ms) | Output tokens/s/GPU | Configuration-level change | SGL/TRT ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DeepGEMM + DeepEP draft baseline | 4.80208 | 31.13983 | 4,317.890 | — | 90.1891% |
| FlashInfer CuTeDSL + FlashInfer A2A + online-NVFP4 draft | 4.79792 | 30.71904 | 4,373.238 | +1.282% | 91.3452% |
| TRT-LLM reference | 4.8 (forced) | 28.07256 | 4,787.594 | Reference | 100% |

- Relative to the legacy configuration, profiling of the complete candidate tuple removes approximately 1.3672 ms/target-step of draft DeepGEMM work and 0.4218 ms/target-step of draft DeepEP communication; overlap limits the end-to-end gain, so these times are not added arithmetically.
- The measured +1.282% belongs to the full runner, A2A backend, and draft-quantization tuple. This PR only preserves the explicit quantization request so that tuple can start; it does not establish an online-NVFP4-only or same-backend speedup.
- `Output tokens/s/GPU` is measured only from the all-rank fixed-B28 pure-generation interval after the final prefill and before the first request completion; it is not a service-level AIPerf total-throughput metric.

title: [EAGLE] Prune draft-extend logits to selected rows
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

During EAGLE draft extension under CUDA graph execution, the model computes full-vocabulary logits for every draft row even though the speculative worker only consumes selected per-request rows. The unnecessary LM-head rows increase graph time and temporary memory usage on the decode critical path.

## Modifications

- Select the rows consumed by the speculative verifier before applying the LM head during draft-extend CUDA graph execution.
- Keep the full six-row draft forward unchanged so hidden-state and speculative-state evolution remain identical.
- Preserve the eager path and existing output contract while sizing the graph logits buffer for the selected rows.

## Accuracy Tests

| Natural-acceptance metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Completed requests | 112 / 112 | 112 / 112 |
| Output length | 860 | 860 |
| Mean acceptance length | 3.684250 | 3.652805 |
| Acceptance rate | 0.536375 | 0.530488 |
| CUDA graph enabled | Yes | Yes |
| Queue / retractions / errors | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- Setup: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 on one node with 4 GB300 GPUs, TP4/DP4/EP4 with DP attention, FP8 KV cache, TRTLLM-MHA, FlashInfer CuTeDSL MoE plus FlashInfer A2A for target and draft, NEXTN with 5 speculative steps and 6 draft tokens, online-NVFP4 draft weights, ReplaySSM circular history, Mamba `extra_buffer`, and CUDA graph tiers through batch 32.
- Workload: one frozen 88,786-token input repeated as a 112-request cohort, 112 warmup requests with OSL 64, 112 measurement requests with exact OSL 860, temperature 0, fixed AL 4.8, and no request replenishment during the measured pure-generation interval.
- Measurement gate: all four ranks must simultaneously report achieved batch 28, CUDA graph enabled, queue depth 0, and no completion/drain row inside the selected interval.

| Fixed-AL4.8 output tokens/s/GPU | 4,526.977 | 4,635.007 | +2.3864% |

- To remove the small context difference, an independent exact-context match paired 40 windows at the same mean context of 102,342.4 tokens/rank and measured 4,542.499 to 4,653.987 output tokens/s/GPU (+2.4543%).
- The final zero-resident-context drain row is excluded from both arms.

| Nsight metric for draft-extend graph `10658` | Baseline | Candidate | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Graph time/GPU-step | 1.113471 ms | 0.974980 ms | -0.138491 ms / -12.44% |
| Selected-row projection | 0.371574 ms | 0.296726 ms | -0.074848 ms |
| Large output copy | 0.098430 ms | 0.017771 ms | -0.080659 ms |
| Graph capture memory | 0.15 GB | 0.07 GB | -0.08 GB / -53.3% |

- `Output tokens/s/GPU` is an engine-side pure-generation metric derived from the fixed-B28 target-step window, not a service-level AIPerf total-throughput metric.
- As a cross-engine diagnostic only, applying the measured within-SGL gain to the fixed-work authority gives 4,608.074 output tokens/s/GPU versus TRT-LLM at 4,791.788, or 96.166% with a 3.834% remaining gap; this does not replace a direct final integration comparison.

title: [sampling] Fix int32 offset overflow in top-k renorm Triton kernels
author: merrymercy
body:
## Motivation

The top-k renorm Triton kernels in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/renorm_triton.py` compute flattened element offsets as `row * vocab_size + offsets` and `program_id * BLOCK_SIZE + arange(...)`. Both products are computed in int32, so for large `batch x vocab_size` tensors the offsets can silently overflow, corrupting loads/stores.

## Modifications

Cast the row / program id to `tl.int64` before the multiplication in `_mask_and_partial_sum_kernel` and `_normalize_kernel`, so offset arithmetic is done in 64-bit.

## Checklist

- Ran `pre-commit` on the changed file (passed).
- Verified on an internal setup exercising the top-k renorm path.

## Original commits

- `49831150a`

body:
## Motivation

The fused QK-norm + RoPE and fused LayerNorm + modulate kernels were previously gated to CUDA only. This PR enables these fused paths on ROCm, giving FLUX.2 the same eager-mode optimizations on AMD GPUs that already exist on NVIDIA.

Additionally, the single transformer block's packed-QKV unflatten produced strided views that the in-place fused kernel couldn't consume without implicit copies. Instead of forcing `.contiguous()` copies, we plumb `allow_strided_qk=True` so the kernel handles strided views natively.

## Modifications

- **Enable fused QK-norm + RoPE on ROCm**: Gate the fused in-place path on `_is_cuda or _is_rocm` instead of `_is_cuda` alone in `apply_qk_norm` and `apply_qk_norm_rope` (`layernorm.py`).
- **Enable fused LayerNorm + modulate on ROCm**: The `_flux2_norm_modulate` helper (already platform-agnostic via `.is_cuda` tensor check) now runs on ROCm for both double and single transformer blocks (`flux_2.py`).
- **Support strided QKV views**: Add `allow_strided_qk` parameter to `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope` and pass `allow_strided_qk=True` in `Flux2ParallelSelfAttention` and `Flux2SingleTransformerBlock`, avoiding unnecessary `.contiguous()` copies.

## Results

Benchmarked on MI350 (ROCm) with FLUX.2 at two resolutions for TP=1, ULLYSSES=8. Times are per-step per-layer GPU kernel time in microseconds. Estimated E2E uplift is extrapolated from per-layer kernel savings; measured E2E is in Accuracy Tests below.

### Kernel microbenchmarks — 1024×1024 (~10% estimated E2E uplift)

| Transformer Component | Q/K Shape | Unfused (us) | Fused (us) | Speedup | Total savings (50 steps, us) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Double Stream (Text) | `[1, 64, 48, 128]` | 101.7 | 8.4 | 12.11x | 37,320 |
| Double Stream (Image) | `[1, 512, 48, 128]` | 131.6 | 14.7 | 8.95x | 46,760 |
| Single Stream (Joint) | `[1, 576, 48, 128]` | 153.5 | 15.8 | 9.72x | 330,480 |

### Kernel microbenchmarks — 2048×2048 (~6% estimated E2E uplift)

| Transformer Component | Q/K Shape | Unfused (us) | Fused (us) | Speedup | Total savings (50 steps, us) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Double Stream (Text) | `[1, 64, 48, 128]` | 104.9 | 8.5 | 12.34x | 38,560 |
| Double Stream (Image) | `[1, 2048, 48, 128]` | 257.1 | 40.0 | 6.43x | 86,840 |
| Single Stream (Joint) | `[1, 2112, 48, 128]` | 339.1 | 44.4 | 7.64x | 707,280 |

### Accuracy tests

Verified that the fused ROCm paths (QK-norm + RoPE, LayerNorm + modulate, strided QKV) produce identical accuracy to the unfused baseline on AMD MI350X using SGLang's built-in diffusion consistency test suite (`test_server_1_gpu.py -k flux_2_image_t2i`).

**Setup:** FLUX.2-dev, 1 GPU, 1024×1024, 50 denoising steps, seed=42, prompt: "Doraemon is eating dorayaki"

#### Results

| Build | CLIP Score | SSIM | PSNR | Mean Abs Diff | E2E (ms) | Avg Denoise (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unfused (baseline) | 0.9837 | 0.7330 | 10.0566 | 33.7260 | 16331.11 | 283.85 |
| Fused (this PR) | 0.9843 | 0.7329 | 10.0570 | 33.7424 | 15179.06 | 248.37 |

- **No accuracy regression.** CLIP score (semantic similarity) is identical or marginally better with fused paths (0.9843 vs 0.9837). All pixel-level metrics (SSIM, PSNR, mean abs diff) are within noise across builds.
- **Performance improvement.** Fused paths reduce average denoise step time from ~284 ms to ~248 ms (**~12.5% faster**), and E2E latency from ~16.3 s to ~15.2 s (**~6% faster**).

> Note: SSIM/PSNR/mean_abs_diff values reflect AMD-vs-H100 ground truth comparison. The relevant comparison is across builds on the same platform, where all metrics are consistent.

title: [Bugfix] Fix full prefill CUDA graph padding and EAGLE capture
author: aurickq
body:
## Motivation

Full prefill CUDA graphs replay fixed token buckets that may be larger than the live batch. Models that mask padded hidden states need the live `num_token_non_padded` boundary even when attention tensors are not gathered. Without it, padded rows can propagate through the captured graph.

EAGLE target prefill also consumes the full target hidden-state sequence. FullCG previously captured the configured return-hidden-state mode, which could be insufficient and force target prefill back to eager execution.

## Modifications

- Register and populate `num_token_non_padded` for FullCG, including non-gathered execution.
- Capture `FULL` hidden states for EAGLE target prefill under FullCG while retaining `LAST` for breakable draft workers.
- Keep the EAGLE eager fallback specific to `tc_piecewise`, whose fixed capture ceiling can remain below `FULL`.
- Add focused regression tests for the non-gathered token boundary and FullCG EAGLE admission.

## Accuracy Tests

No model math or kernels are changed.

- 42 focused unit tests passed, including 2 parameterized subtests.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The changes update CUDA graph metadata and capture mode; they do not add work to attention or model kernels.

title: [Fix] Support 128-aligned hidden sizes in the W4AFP8 DeepEP low-latency requant kernel
author: alexnails
body:
## Motivation

`fp8_per_token_to_per_tensor_quant_triton()` requantizes DeepEP low-latency's per-token-group
fp8 payload into the per-tensor fp8 that the first CUTLASS W4A8 grouped GEMM consumes. It
required the hidden size to fill a whole number of 1024-element blocks:

```python
K_BLOCK_SIZE = 1024
assert x.size(2) % K_BLOCK_SIZE == 0
grid = (x.size(2) // K_BLOCK_SIZE, 32, x.size(0))
```

so it rejected any expert hidden size that is only 128-aligned — 3584, for example. Since
`W4AFp8MoEMethod` pins the low-latency wire format to fp8
(`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/w4afp8.py:286-295`) and `apply_deepep_ll()` rejects a
payload that carries no per-token-group scales (`w4afp8.py:347-351`), such a model has no
working low-latency path at all: the fp8 payload it is handed trips the assert during decode
CUDA-graph capture.

1024 was the only constraint of its kind on that path. `w1_scale` is `[E, K // 512, N * 8]`, so
512-alignment is genuinely required; DeepEP's low-latency fp8 scales are `[E, M, hidden // 128]`
(column-major in the last two dims for TMA), so the payload is always a whole number of 128-wide
scale groups. A hidden size of 3584 satisfies both — 7 × 512, 28 groups — and was rejected only
by the 1024 block.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/ep_moe_kernels.py`:

- Take the grid from `triton.cdiv` and drop the assert.
- Mask the k lanes in `_fp8_per_token_quant_to_per_tensor_quant_kernel`: on the hidden load, on
  the store, and on the scale load, whose offsets derive from `k_offsets` and would otherwise
  read past the scale tensor in the tail block.
- Put the masked form behind `HAS_K_TAIL: tl.constexpr`, so hidden sizes that fill every block
  keep the original unmasked loads and the same launch geometry. This mirrors
  `_silu_and_mul_post_per_tensor_quant_kernel` in the same file, which already pairs a `cdiv`
  grid with a masked fast axis.

Adds `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_fp8_per_token_to_per_tensor_quant.py`
(`base-b-kernel-unit`, `1-gpu-large`).

## Accuracy Tests

The new test checks k ∈ {7168, 3584, 1152} — one exact multiple of 1024 and two tailed, so both
specializations compile — against a torch reference, and asserts that rows past `masked_m` are
left exactly as the caller wrote them. Inputs are integers in [-8, 8] with power-of-two group
scales, so every intermediate is exactly representable in e4m3 and the comparison can be
`rtol=0, atol=0`.

(The kernel saturates fp8 overflow — `cvt.rn.satfinite`, clamping to 448.0 — where
`Tensor.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)` produces NaN, so a torch-reference test has to stay inside range
deliberately.)

One H200, torch 2.11.0+cu130 / triton 3.6.0:

```
test_masked_rows_and_k_tail[7168] PASSED
test_masked_rows_and_k_tail[3584] PASSED
test_masked_rows_and_k_tail[1152] PASSED
3 passed in 16.75s
```

Swapping this commit's kernel for the current `main` file makes the two tailed cases fail while
7168 still passes, so the test covers the change rather than just passing alongside it.

A wider matrix run out of tree — both scale layouts (contiguous and DeepEP's column-major) ×
`masked_m` ∈ {0, 1, 17, m} × E ∈ {4, 8, 56} × K_BLOCK ∈ {1024, 2048} × num_warps ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8} —
is bit-exact against the reference everywhere, with padding rows untouched.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hidden sizes that already worked are unaffected, checked two ways on H200 and B200 (torch 2.11 /
triton 3.6; kernel timed inside a CUDA graph so Triton's Python launch cost is excluded; DeepEP
scale layout, `K_BLOCK_SIZE=1024`, m-grid 32).

Codegen: the compiled kernel has the same opcode multiset as before at num_warps ∈ {2, 4, 8},
differing only in instruction scheduling order. Access widths are unchanged in the tail path too
(warps=2 → `ld/st.global.v4.b32`, warps=4 → `v2.b32`, warps=8 → scalar `b32`), so the mask costs
no vectorization.

Timing at k=7168, relative to the kernel this replaces:

| live rows / expert | H200 w8 | H200 w4 | B200 w8 | B200 w4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 32 | −0.18% | −0.38% | −0.59% | +1.11% |
| 256 | −0.65% | −0.10% | −1.66% | +1.46% |
| 1024 | +0.09% | +0.20% | −0.32% | 0.00% |

For reference, a newly-working shape (no prior number — it asserted): k=3584, 8 experts, 1024
live rows per expert — 25.4 µs on H200, 14.6 µs on B200.

Reproduction note: in a CUDA-graph A/B loop the first variant measured reads roughly 10% fast on
sub-2 µs shapes; interleave the variants and swap their order before trusting a small gap.

Not covered here: a multi-node end-to-end decode run on a model whose routed-expert hidden size
isn't 1024-divisible. This change unblocks the fp8 low-latency path for those models at the
kernel level; that e2e run is still outstanding.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [AMD] Increase gfx950 DSA model indexer topk_transform kernel occupancy
author: wufann
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
Improve gfx950 DSA model indexer topk_transform kernel performance.

- dsv4 : deepseek_v4_topk_transform_512

- dsv3.2/glm5:  fast_topk

On gfx95x (MI350/MI355) the dsv4 top-k kernels requested a 128KB dynamic LDS budget, which pinned occupancy to **1 block/CU** and left ~2/3 of the CU's thread capacity idle. The large buffer is unnecessary: it only backs the radix tie-candidate list, which needs ~`length/256` entries. Shrinking the per-arch budget to **40KB** lifts the 512-thread block to **3 blocks/CU** while keeping a `SMEM_INPUT_SIZE` of 5120 entries — enough to cover ~1.3M-token sequences, comfortably clear of DeepSeek-V4's 1M-token default context. 

This is the **performance/precision balance point**: it captures ~2x of the ~2.5x available speedup on gfx950 without shrinking the tie buffer onto that 1M correctness boundary.

gfx942 (MI300, 64KB LDS/CU) is left at 48KB — it is capacity-bound at 1 block/CUeither way.

#### LDS usage
gfx950: 160KB LDS/CU, 2048 threads/CU

LDS/block = static (~7KB: `_s_histogram_buf[2][288]` + `s_topk_indices[1024]`
+ a few `alignas(128)` scalars) + dynamic `kSMEM`.

| kSMEM | LDS/block | LDS limit | thread limit | occupancy |
|-------|-----------|-----------|--------------|-----------|
| 128KB | ~135KB    | 1         | 4            | **1 block/CU** (LDS-bound) |
| 48KB  | ~55KB     | 2         | 4            | **2 blocks/CU** (LDS-bound) |
| 40KB  | ~47KB     | 3         | 4            | **3 blocks/CU** (LDS-bound) — chosen |
| 32KB  | ~39KB     | 4         | 4            | **4 blocks/CU** (thread-bound) |

#### covered kv length
| kSMEM | entries/half | covers kv length up to | note |
|-------|--------------|---------------------|------|
| 128KB | 16384        | ~4.2M               | massive |
| 40KB  | 5120         | ~1.3M               | chosen: margin over DSV4 1M |
| 32KB  | 4096         | ~1.05M              | fastest, but margin sits on the 1M context floor |
<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
`setup_rocm.py`: for gfx95x/gfx1250, `topk_dynamic_smem_bytes` 128KB -> 40KB; 
## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->
This change does not affect accuracy.
## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->
gfx950, deepseek_v4_topk_transform_512, page_size=256

Swept four dynamic-LDS budgets — 128KB (baseline), **40KB (chosen)**
— each a full rebuild. Latencies in us; speedup columns are vs the 128KB baseline.

| B | S | 128KB | **40KB** | 40KB speedup |

title: [NPU] Adapt DFlash2 speculative decoding to Ascend NPUs
author: syd520zy
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

DFlash2 ([#35371](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35371)) landed on main as the successor to DFlash. It uses a block-diffusion drafter with local grouped convolutions and a candidate selector.

First-generation DFlash drafts already run on Ascend NPUs ([#23122](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23122), [#31739](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31739)), but DFlash2 checkpoints could not serve on NPU because the target verification path assumed CUDA behavior.

This PR adapts the DFlash2 draft and verification paths for Ascend NPUs while preserving the existing CUDA behavior.

The validated Ascend environment includes `triton-ascend`; this PR assumes Triton is available in the runtime environment.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->


- Fix target verification metadata handling on NPU.
  - Non-NPU devices preserve the existing `skip_attn_backend_init=True` behavior because `prepare_for_verify` has already planned the attention metadata.
  - NPU passes `None`, allowing the target forward path to initialize the required attention metadata.
  - This prevents the NPU graph runner from skipping initialization and accessing an uninitialized `raw_num_token`.

- Align DFlash2 selector verification with the existing NPU behavior of EAGLE and first-generation DFlash.
  - On CUDA, selector sampling verification remains unchanged.
  - On NPU, the full-vocabulary selector sampling verification is skipped and target verification uses argmax.
  - The full-vocabulary path scatters a dense `[batch_size, gamma, vocab_size]` draft-probability buffer and performs vocabulary-wide operations whose cost does not shrink with the verification window.
  - This is an NPU-specific performance policy, not a limitation of the selector algorithm itself: the probability-based path can execute in the validated `triton-ascend` environment, but it added about 6 ms of TPOT on the tested 910C setup and is unnecessary for lossless greedy requests.

- Keep draft proposal and target verification consistent on NPU.
  - Selector sampling support is resolved once as a worker-level capability; graph-captured and eager paths consume that semantic state instead of repeatedly checking the device.
  - The capability is disabled on NPU, forcing both selector draft paths to greedy proposal.
  - `_selector_sample` is staged only when selector sampling is enabled, and acceptance dispatches from that staged state rather than rechecking the hardware.
  - This avoids stochastic draft proposals being verified by a greedy target, which would unnecessarily reduce the acceptance length.
  - CUDA and other non-NPU devices continue to use the original request sampling parameters.

- Handle non-greedy requests on NPU explicitly.
  - The request is currently accepted.
  - Both draft proposal and target verification fall back to greedy.
  - A warning is emitted once to state that the requested sampling distribution is not preserved.
  - Lossless behavior on NPU is currently guaranteed only for greedy requests such as `temperature=0` and `top_k=1`.

- Keep DSpark NPU sampling support outside this PR.
  - This PR does not add a torch chain speculative-sampling implementation or a DSpark NPU sampling fallback.
  - The scope is limited to DFlash2 serving and greedy verification on Ascend NPUs.

- Update the Qwen3.8-27B cookbook with the DFlash2 NPU behavior, validated configuration, greedy-only losslessness boundary, and benchmark setup.

### Why the remaining NPU guards are necessary

The runtime changes contain two direct NPU decisions, each representing a separate backend constraint:

1. Selector sampling policy is decided once when the worker is initialized. Ascend currently uses greedy proposal and verification because selector rejection sampling materializes a dense `[batch_size, gamma, vocab_size]` probability buffer and performs full-vocabulary work. All downstream selector paths use the resulting capability state.
2. Target verification metadata is handled differently on Ascend. Non-NPU `prepare_for_verify()` pre-plans graph or attention metadata, while the NPU path must defer planning until DP/EP padding finalizes runtime shapes. Passing `skip_attn_backend_init=True` on NPU would incorrectly mark uninitialized metadata as ready and can make `NPUGraphRunner` access uninitialized state such as `raw_num_token`.

The existing `is_dflash_sampling_verify_available()` helper cannot replace the selector capability decision: it describes a different target-only verification implementation and using it here would change existing behavior on other backends such as HIP.

### Runtime Validation

- Verified DFlash2 on Ascend NPU with greedy decoding (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`).
- Three repeated requests with the same prompt produced identical output hashes.
- Verified both NPU graph-enabled and eager (`--disable-cuda-graph`) execution paths.
- Non-greedy requests complete successfully and emit the expected one-time warning before falling back to greedy DFlash2 proposal/verification.
- Full deterministic non-greedy validation was not performed because the test image does not include the NPU `batch_invariant_ops` extension required by `--enable-deterministic-inference`.

### Reviewer question: non-greedy requests on Ascend

DFlash2 currently cannot preserve the requested non-greedy sampling distribution on Ascend because selector verification falls back to argmax.

The current implementation keeps the request valid, emits a warning once, and forces both the draft proposal and target verification to greedy so their behavior remains consistent.

Another option is to reject non-greedy requests explicitly instead of allowing this fallback.

Which behavior would be preferred for this PR?

1. Accept the request, warn once, and run both draft proposal and verification greedily.
2. Reject non-greedy requests on Ascend with an explicit error.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

The accuracy setup follows [#23122](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23122) and [#16818](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/16818), except for the hardware and models.

- Hardware: Ascend 910C
- Tensor parallelism: `--tp-size 2`
- Target model: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` with BF16 weights
- Draft model: `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`
- Draft tokens: `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 8`
- Attention backend: `--attention-backend ascend`
- Mamba configuration: `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer`
- Dataset: GSM8K, zero-shot
- Sampling: greedy, with `temperature=0.0`, `top_p=1.0`, and `top_k=1`
- Maximum new tokens: `2048`
- Samples: 128 per concurrency level
- RadixCache: disabled for both baseline and DFlash2 to keep the comparison independent of cache warm-up and prefix reuse

### Baseline accuracy

| Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Accuracy | 0.820 | 0.836 | 0.836 | 0.828 | 0.820 |

### DFlash2 accuracy

| Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Accuracy | 0.820 | 0.836 | 0.836 | 0.828 | 0.820 |

### DFlash2 acceptance length

The configured block size is 8. The following values are the windowed mean acceptance lengths reported by scheduler decode logs.

| Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Mean acceptance length | 5.8 | 5.8 | 5.8 | 5.8 | 5.8 |

The log-reported mean acceptance length was approximately 5.8, with an acceptance rate of approximately 0.68.

End-to-end validation on Ascend 910C confirmed that:

- The target and DFlash2 draft models load successfully.
- The selector draft initializes successfully.
- Both NPU graph captures complete successfully.
- Greedy requests complete successfully.
- Baseline and DFlash2 produced identical aggregate GSM8K accuracy at every tested concurrency level.

Focused unit-test coverage includes:

- Warning once when selector sampling is disabled and a non-greedy request falls back.
- Propagating the worker-level selector sampling capability into the graph sampler.
- Forcing greedy selector draft parameters when sampling is disabled.
- Preserving selector sampling parameters when the capability is enabled.
- Verifying that acceptance uses staged selector state and otherwise takes the greedy fallback.
- Keeping the generic/CUDA Mamba verify-hook ordering test isolated from NPU-specific DSV4 bundle setup.

Local static validation completed:

- `python -m compileall`
- `git diff --check upstream/main`

Focused Python unit tests were executed in the Ascend validation environment and passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

The throughput benchmark used the same hardware, model configuration, workload, and RadixCache setting as the accuracy test.

### Baseline output throughput

| Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Output tok/s | 33.182 | 60.925 | 109.544 | 176.193 | 247.068 |

The end-to-end speedup decreases from 3.05x at concurrency 1 to 1.75x at concurrency 16 as target-model batching and speculative-decoding overhead become more prominent at higher concurrency.

Local profiling showed:

- DFlash2 and NEXTN have matching kernel-level draft behavior.

- The original full-vocabulary selector sampling verification added approximately 6 ms of TPOT on the tested setup: about 51 ms with selector sampling verification versus 45 ms with greedy verification.

title: [Feature] Add DeepEPv2 (ElasticBuffer) MoE A2A backend
author: MengYu10151
body:
> Reland of #29525, reverted by #35568 because its e2e test used an
> unregistered CI runner name. This reland restores the backend and fixes that
> registration without changing unrelated CI configuration.

## Motivation

Add DeepEP v2 `ElasticBuffer` as a standalone MoE A2A backend named
`deepep_v2`, alongside the existing `deepep` backend. Its fixed-capacity
communication shapes make decode CUDA-graph capturable with both single-node
and multi-node topologies.

## Supported scope

| Area | Supported in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| Models | `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM`, `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`, `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` |
| Expert precision | Dynamic blockwise FP8, 128x128 weight blocks |
| MoE runner | `deep_gemm` |
| Backend modes | `--deepep-v2-mode direct|hybrid` |
| DeepEP package | `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.2` (`deep_ep 2.1.0`) |

`direct` and `hybrid` select the ElasticBuffer topology; they are not aliases
for legacy DeepEP `low_latency` and `normal`. Decode uses the expanded masked
layout, while extend/prefill uses the contiguous layout in either mode.

This intentionally does not claim support for other MoE architectures or
quantization contracts. In particular, Qwen3.8
(`Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`), BF16 experts, MXFP8, non-DeepGEMM runners,
deterministic inference, and a speculative draft worker using `deepep_v2` are
not supported by this landing. These configurations now fail before A2A
execution instead of reaching a model-specific forward path with incorrect
post-expert reduction or incompatible activation scales.

## Implementation

- Adds an independent `DeepEPv2Dispatcher` using ElasticBuffer dispatch and
  combine. Legacy `deepep` objects and mode semantics are not reused.
- Adds masked-slab repack kernels and DeepGEMM adapters for contiguous prefill
  and masked decode, including Hopper FP32 scales and Blackwell packed UE8M0
  scales.
- Stores ElasticBuffer state in `RuntimeContext` resources so context reset and
  sequential engine construction release ownership consistently. The cache key
  includes the process group and a new buffer is published only after collective
  construction succeeds.
- Treats dispatch handles as single-use and preserves the dispatch-selected SM
  settings for combine. `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_SMS=0` delegates automatic SM/QP
  selection to `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.2`.
- Enables the backend's minimum NCCL symmetric-memory requirement with
  `os.environ.setdefault("NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE", "1")`; an explicit user setting
  still wins, and `--enable-symm-mem` remains optional.

## Capacity and fail-fast behavior

`SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` configures ElasticBuffer's
per-rank capacity; it is a memory reservation, not a semantic token limit.
Startup checks cover the canonical prefill budget, decode CUDA-graph batch,
per-DP-rank running-request bound, and speculative width. The dispatch adapter
also checks the actual runtime row count, which remains the authoritative guard
for dynamic batches.

Errors include actionable guidance for adjusting the capacity,
`--chunked-prefill-size`, or `--cuda-graph-max-bs`. Unsupported model, runner,
quantization, deterministic, and draft-backend combinations fail at startup or
MoE layer initialization.

## Validation

- Relevant CPU suite: 204 tests and 15 subtests passed.
- Qwen3 FP8: `direct` and `hybrid` booted and returned correct capital,
  arithmetic, and translation answers.
- DeepSeek V3 FP8: both modes passed the same functional gate; GSM8K was 0.960
  (`direct`) and 0.965 (`hybrid`) versus 0.955 for legacy DeepEP.
- DeepSeek V4 Flash FP8, TP8/DP8/EP8 with DP attention and DeepGEMM:

| Platform / metric | v2 direct | v2 hybrid | legacy DeepEP |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| H20 x8 MMLU (500) | 0.888 | 0.890 | 0.888 |
| H20 x8 GSM8K (100) | 0.980 | 0.980 | 0.970 |
| B200 x8 MMLU (500) | 0.886 | 0.884 | - |
| B200 x8 GSM8K (100) | 0.950 | 0.970 | - |

Representative back-to-back serving results:

| Workload | deepep_v2 | legacy DeepEP | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| H20 x8 decode | 4,339 tok/s | 4,379 tok/s | -0.9% |
| H20 x8 prefill | 22,353 in_tok/s | 21,651 in_tok/s | +3.2% |
| B200 x8 decode | 8,429 tok/s | 8,675 tok/s | -2.8% |
| B200 x8 prefill | 32,447 in_tok/s | 31,533 in_tok/s | +2.9% |

Multi-node `hybrid` was also validated on 2 x H20 x8 over RoCE at 4,610 tok/s
decode and 20,688 in_tok/s prefill. There is no same-fabric legacy DeepEP
baseline because its NVSHMEM data plane did not complete on that setup.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and static checks.
- [x] Unit and boundary tests.
- [x] Functional accuracy validation.
- [x] Single-node and multi-node performance validation.
- [ ] User documentation in a follow-up PR.

Co-authored-by: @jianxiongzhang

title: [docs] Add DFlash2 speculative cells to the Qwen3.8-27B cookbook
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

#35496 (quantized target `lm_head` in the DFlash2 selector) is merged, so the NVFP4 checkpoint can run DFlash2. This adds a DFLASH2 option to the Qwen3.8-27B cookbook's Speculative Decoding row, on every platform with a cell. Validation is graded: NVFP4 measured end-to-end on RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 5090, the RTX PRO 6000 BF16/FP8 cells validated to boot and serve, and the remaining platforms (H200, DGX Spark, GB300) offered with a **Final Verification In Progress** badge while the DFLASH2 pick is selected.

## Modifications

- `qwen3.8-27b.jsx`: DFLASH2 Deploy-panel overlay option (draft `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 8`) and the matching Playground card entry. On the RTX 5090 the option re-pins `--mem-fraction-static` (0.90 bf16 / 0.945 fp32), and for fp32 also re-pins `--mamba-full-memory-ratio 10` in place of the calculator's balanced value — the L=9216 ratio leaves the fp32 state pool one slot short at every serviceable mem-fraction.
- `Qwen3.8-27B.mdx`: DFlash2 bullet in Configuration Tips (including the 5090 fp32 caveats), DFLASH added to the ratio accordion's `D` term, validation Note updated.
- `_deployment.jsx`: `verificationStatus` may now be a function of the selection (overlay picks included), so a cell can report "Final Verification In Progress" for one speculative option while staying Verified for the rest. Backward compatible — string/boolean forms unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A (docs only). Serving correctness of the quantized-head path was validated in #35496 (GSM8K 95.5% spec vs 98.0% base, 200q).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

All 8 cells validated at ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, concurrency 1 (bench_serving random, 1 warmup + 4 prompts, exact-shape checks, real acceptance):

| Card | Tier | SSM dtype | mem-frac | ratio | TPOT | tok/s/user | accept |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RTX PRO 6000 | Low-Latency | float32 | 0.85 | 6.63 | 7.56 ms | 132.3 | 3.41 |
| RTX PRO 6000 | Low-Latency | bfloat16 | 0.85 | 3.38 | 7.64 ms | 130.9 | 3.09 |
| RTX PRO 6000 | High-Throughput | float32 | 0.85 | 6.12 | 7.58 ms | 131.9 | 3.41 |
| RTX PRO 6000 | High-Throughput | bfloat16 | 0.85 | 3.12 | 7.84 ms | 127.6 | 3.20 |
| RTX 5090 | Low-Latency | bfloat16 | 0.90 | 3.38 | 6.11 ms | 143 | 3.30 |
| RTX 5090 | High-Throughput | bfloat16 | 0.90 | 3.12 | 6.12 ms | 143 | 3.30 |
| RTX 5090 | Low-Latency | float32 | 0.945 | 10 | 8.30 ms | 120.3 | 3.09 |
| RTX 5090 | High-Throughput | float32 | 0.945 | 10 | 8.32 ms | 120.1 | 3.09 |

5090 fp32 boundaries, all measured: mf 0.94 → state pool one slot short; mf 0.95 → runtime OOM on the first request; balanced ratios 6.63/6.12 → `max_mamba_cache_size` below the required slots at every mem-fraction. Low-Latency fp32's KV pool is a single-request envelope (9,454 tokens), documented in the Tips bullet.

RTX PRO 6000 BF16/FP8 boot grid (same cell command + DFLASH swap, calculator ratios; each arm booted, answered a greedy completion, and logged the selector folded into the draft CUDA graph):

| Checkpoint | LL+fp32 (6.63) | LL+bf16 (3.38) | HT+fp32 (6.12) | HT+bf16 (3.12) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 | OK | OK | OK | OK |
| FP8 | OK | OK | OK | OK |

(Both checkpoints keep a dense `lm_head` — no weight scales in their indexes — so these ride the classic dense path; NVFP4 is the only checkpoint exercising the quantized-head gate.)

title: [AMD] Enable draft_extend CUDA graph for HIP DSA backend
author: jiaryang
body: Allow DeepseekSparseAttnBackend on HIP so GLM MI355 MTP can capture the draft_extend graph instead of falling back to eager launches. ## Motivation On HIP, `draft_extend` CUDA-graph capture is only allowlisted for aiter multi-step / DSV4 radix. GLM MI355 MTP uses `DeepseekSparseAttnBackend` for draft_extend, so capture is skipped and every extend is eager. This PR adds DSA to that HIP allowlist. ## Modifications In `python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py`, OR `isinstance(self.draft_extend_attn_backend, DeepseekSparseAttnBackend)` into the HIP `supports_hip_*_draft_extend_graph` check (local import so non-HIP builds do not require the DSA backend). ## Accuracy Tests Same node (`smci355-ccs-aus-m11-13`, MI355, TP=4, `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`, docker 0818). Baseline without this PR vs this PR (`draft_extend` graph captured). GSM8K 5-shot, 2000 questions, 3-run mean. title: [diffusion] docs+skill: which components to stream under layerwise offload
author: mickqian
body:
Documents what belongs in `--layerwise-offload-components`, and corrects four things the first version of this PR got wrong about it.

## Motivation

The docs never said what belongs in the component list, so it reads like a memory dial to turn all the way up. The rule is cost per pass, not component size: streaming pays one host-to-device transfer of a component's weights per pass over that component, overlapped with that pass's compute.

Four things decide whether that is cheap, and the first version of this PR had three of them backwards:

1. **Count passes from the code.** A "one-shot" component need not be one pass. H3's `_decode_temporal_streaming` re-runs the whole video decoder per temporal chunk, so streaming its 36 blocks pays 36 transfers per chunk.
2. **There are three placements, not two.** A component can be declared streamed and still hold its blocks (`--layerwise-resident-layers video_vae=36`), which transfers them once instead of per pass and releases the VRAM when the component finishes. Telling the reader to drop a one-shot component from the list instead keeps it resident for the whole process, which is the VRAM a 12-24 GB budget does not have.
3. **Host memory is one budget.** Pinning a one-shot component competes with the page cache that a streamed component's mapped weights read through, so per-component placement is not independent.
4. **Bytes are not the cost.** A pinned source transfers asynchronously; an unpinned or mapped source is synchronous whatever the call requests, because the driver stages it through its own buffer.

It also read 132 ms of a 1.04 s step as 0.5%. The measured fact is that the sweep is flat because prefetch hides the transfer, not because the bytes are negligible, so the guidance is now to measure rather than to divide bytes by bandwidth and stop there.

## Modifications

Four subsections in Section 1 of `sglang-diffusion-performance`, the mirrored guidance in `deployment_cookbook.mdx`, and an RTX 4090 entry in the H3 deployment config.

## Accuracy Tests

Documentation only. Residency and prefetch are lossless: a residency sweep on Wan2.1-1.3B produced one SHA-256 across every setting.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MiniMax-H3 fl2va, 1x RTX 4090, 864x480 / 124 frames / 20 NFE, bf16, seed 1101.

Video VAE, 36 blocks, decode only:

| placement | decode |
|---|---|
| streamed | 150 s |
| streamed, blocks resident | **13 s** |

DiT denoise, same bytes per step, only the host-side source differs:

| DiT weight source | denoise | per step | configuration |
|---|---|---|---|
| pinned host memory | **122.84 s** | 6.10 s | host uncapped, 116.7 GB pinned |
| checkpoint mapping | 330.74 s | 17.4 s | host 32 GiB, allocator 23 GiB |
| checkpoint mapping | 318.94-356.37 s | 16.8-18.7 s | host 32 GiB, allocator 12 GiB |

The last row is one configuration measured twice; the 12% spread tracked host load on a shared machine, so smaller differences than that are unresolved here.

For scale on the same card and shape, ComfyUI runs these unpruned bf16 weights at 6.58-6.59 s/step. Its `--fast-disk` mode holds 57.5 GiB of anonymous host memory instead of 116.5 GiB at the same 6.57-6.60 s/step, so the pinned path is at parity and the mapped path is a host-side tax rather than a GPU result.

Prefetch depth is left unquantified on purpose: it is not monotonic and the direction depends on model, resolution and card, so the docs say sweep it.

Related: #35813 (the alias fix these numbers depend on), #35812 (auto streams the DiT instead of OOMing on a 12 GB card).

- [x] Update documentation as needed, including docstrings or example tutorials.

title: [NPU] DeepSeek-V4 adapt sgl-kernel-npu ops (compressor/sparse-attn/sparse-attn-metadata)
author: unclezhou486
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
Adaptation of  DSV4 sparse attention for NPU platforms, with host-side metadata computation and a unified op namespace.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

1. Compute sparse_attn_sharedkv_metadata on the CPU host instead of the NPU device: device tensors are mirrored to CPU (actual_seq_lengths_q_pa_cpu, seq_lens_cpu_int), and the new host op torch.ops.npu.sparse_attn_sharedkv_metadata_host reads CPU int32 inputs directly, eliminating the D2H sync that drains/stalls the stream and hurts overlapped scheduling.
2. Unify the DSV4 op namespace — replace torch.ops.custom.* and torch.ops._C_ascend.* calls with the shared torch.ops.npu.* namespace, covering the DSpark draft-worker path, so normal and draft paths use identical kernels.
3. Adapt the fused compressor to torch.ops.npu.compressor (including the FP32 state-cache constraint in the memory pool).
4. Update extra_ops_loader to drop npu_sparse_attn_sharedkv_metadata from the DSpark _C_ascend required ops, since metadata is now produced on host.
5. Fix _use_host_sparse_metadata definition and the seq_lens_cpu_int fallback when the flag is off.

title: [diffusion] Refresh eager optimization skills and benchmark safeguards
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- refresh the checked-in SGLang Diffusion skills for recently added LongCat-Image, SANA-Video, LingBot Video MoE, Cosmos3 Edge/distilled, and LTX-2.5 paths
- make the denoise benchmark helper eager by default, with `--torch-compile` as an explicit labeled comparator, while keeping nightly presets aligned with the CI comparison config
- add task-owned Hugging Face/ModelScope cache isolation, handled-interruption cleanup, zero-residual accounting, and a JSONL cleanup ledger
- add dependency-light unit coverage for recent presets, eager/compile behavior, nightly drift, cleanup safety, errors, and interruptions

Background survey: https://github.com/BBuf/how-to-optim-algorithm-in-cuda/issues/21

## Why

The existing skill still assumed compile was the default fast path and did not cover several model families added recently. That makes eager-kernel opportunity discovery harder and makes repeated model-backed profiling risky on hosts with limited disk.

The helper now treats eager as the ground truth, keeps compile as a separate control, and can guarantee that a newly created per-model download cache is removed after success, failure, or a handled interruption. SGLang JIT caches are deliberately not redirected or deleted.

## Validation

- `uvx ruff format ...`
- `uvx ruff check ...`
- `python3 python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_diffusion_benchmark_skill.py` (6 tests)

title: [diffusion] MiniMax-H3 Spectrum skip-step + fused RMSNorm/AdaLN
author: niehen6174
body:
## Summary

Wires training-free Spectrum skip-step into MiniMax-H3 and fuses RMSNorm + indexed AdaLN. 
On one 24GB GPU, 50-step BF16+FA (**1008.6 s**) drops to **285.3 s (3.53×)** with exact attention, up to **219.0 s (4.61×)** with Sage→Sol hybrid + Spectrum.

1344×768 · 107 frames · 50 NFE · same process: warmup (seed 0) → timed (seed 42), timed only. PSNR is per-frame vs the **same-tree** INT8+FA video (Spectrum off).

| Config | timed e2e | vs BF16+FA | PSNR mean / min |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BF16 + FlashAttention (baseline) | 1008.6 s | 1.00× | — |
| `kitchen_int8` + FA (Spectrum off) | 718.5 s | 1.40× | — |
| **`kitchen_int8` + FA + Spectrum `11/5/1.0`** — recommend | **285.3 s** | **3.53×** | **27.37 / 25.28** |
| `kitchen_int8` + FA + Spectrum `15/5/0` | 387.4 s | 2.60× | 30.82 / 28.69 |
| `kitchen_int8` + `sage_attn` + Spectrum `15/5/0` | 245.3 s | 4.11× | 23.56 / 21.01 |
| `kitchen_int8` + Sage→Sol hybrid + Spectrum `15/5/0.5` | **219.0 s** | **4.61×** | 20.57 / 17.75 |
| *(external reference)* ComfyUI INT8 workflow | 752.6 s | 1.34× |- |

ComfyUI is a 24GB yardstick only. Same-INT8 gap is 752.6 vs 718.5 s (**1.05×**). 


## Motivation

[#34581](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34581) already moved the 24GB path onto `kitchen_int8` + FlashAttention (~14 s/step). H3's default is **50 steps**, so the remaining cost is running the 50-layer stack every step (~12 min).

Cache-DiT (`quality="high"`) is the in-tree skip-compute for multi-GPU H3, but it cannot combine with `--dit-layerwise-offload`, so a 24GB card that must stream the DiT cannot use it. 
On the audited 4×H200 recipe it is also only 1.40× and still walks the first blocks. Spectrum ([arxiv:2603.01623](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01623)) is already wired for FLUX.1 / Wan / HunyuanVideo / SD3: it forecasts DiT features and **skips the whole stack**, and it works with layerwise offload. H3 could not use it because the packed sequence is not a uniform video stream.

## Modifications

### 1. Spectrum on MiniMax-H3

Opt-in via `--enable-spectrum`. Off path does not enter the mixin — bit-exact vs today's H3.

- Forecast only the packed **target** suffix: contiguous target audio immediately before `infer_out_pos` video. Earlier reference-audio rows are dropped (Wan2GP `hidden[audio_start:]`).
- Comfy blends: **audio hold** (0), **video lerp 0.5**.
- History on CPU, default `history_size` 100 → **8** (24GB).
- `layer_names = ["blocks", "token_refiner.blocks"]` so a skip is the 50-layer stack, not a Cache-DiT wrap. Works with DiT layerwise offload.
- Fail-closed with `quality="high"` / `enable_cache_dit`, and with sequence-parallel `sp_ws > 1`.

Generic Spectrum defaults (`warmup=5, window=2, flex=0.75`) are the 20 NFE row. H3's model default is 50 steps; **`warmup=5` is a quality cliff there**. The recommended 50-step schedule is `11 / 5 / 1.0` (all frames >25 dB vs FA).

Sage / Sol + Spectrum is faster but the PSNR ceiling is the attention backend (~23.6 dB vs FA at 50 NFE). If the bar is "looks like FA", keep `fa`.

### 2. Fused RMSNorm + indexed AdaLN

`fused_indexed_rmsnorm_scale_shift` writes `RMSNorm(x) * (1+scale[idx]) + shift[idx]` without materializing the normalized tensor. Gate: BF16, not `torch.compile`; otherwise the existing eager modulate.

Lossless (1 ULP; `mean|Δ|≈2e-8`). Exclusive 20 NFE INT8+FA: 290.8 → **289.7 s** (−1.06 s, ~0.3%). Same kernel every step, so ~−2.3 s at 50 NFE. On whenever the Triton path matches; no flag.

## Accuracy Tests

Same prompt and seed (42). First pair is 50 NFE, exact attention; the Spectrum row is the recommend schedule. Second pair is 20 NFE library defaults.

**`kitchen_int8` + FA, 50 NFE — 718.5 s**

**`kitchen_int8` + FA + Spectrum `11/5/1.0`, 50 NFE — 285.3 s (27.4 dB)**

**`kitchen_int8` + FA + Spectrum `5/2/0.75`, 20 NFE — 189.5 s (25.6 dB)**

## Example

Exact-attention recommend (**3.53×** vs BF16) — INT8 Linear, FlashAttention, Spectrum `11/5/1.0`:

```bash
pip install comfy-kitchen   # required only for --quantization kitchen_int8

sglang generate \
  --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \
  --model-variant fl2va \
  --quantization kitchen_int8 \
  --attention-backend fa \
  --enable-spectrum \
  --spectrum-warmup-steps 11 \
  --spectrum-window-size 5 \
  --spectrum-flex-window 1.0 \
  --performance-mode memory \
  --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \
  --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \
  --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0 \
  --enable-torch-compile false \
  --prompt "A cat walking on a sunny beach, gentle waves." \
  --save-output
```

Speed ceiling (**4.61×** vs BF16) — same offload, Sage→Sol hybrid on the DiT and Spectrum `15/5/0.5`. Approximate attention; PSNR 20.6 / 17.8 dB vs FA.

```bash
sglang generate \
  --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \
  --model-variant fl2va \
  --quantization kitchen_int8 \
  --attention-backend sol_attn \
  --attention-backend-config dense_backend=sage_attn,dense_steps=10 \
  --component-attention-backends text_encoder=torch_sdpa,transformer=sol_attn \
  --enable-spectrum \
  --spectrum-warmup-steps 15 \
  --spectrum-window-size 5 \
  --spectrum-flex-window 0.5 \
  --performance-mode memory \
  --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \
  --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \
  --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0 \
  --enable-torch-compile false \
  --prompt "A cat walking on a sunny beach, gentle waves." \
  --save-output
```

`--layerwise-offload-components` omits `vae` (same as #34581). Omit `--enable-spectrum` and the three `--spectrum-*` flags for the 718 s INT8+FA path. At 20 NFE, `--enable-spectrum` alone is enough (library defaults). Drop `--quantization` for BF16.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

RTX 4090 D 24GB · CUDA 13.0 · 1344×768 / 107 frames / euler · `torch.compile` and Cache-DiT **disabled** · load → warmup (seed 0) → timed (seed 42), **timed pass only**.

Cross-framework PSNR vs Comfy (~16 dB) is TE NVFP4 vs BF16 — not a quality column.

The `kitchen_int8` SwiGLU fuse (`int8_linear(input_act=swiglu)`) is **not** on in these numbers. Released `comfy-kitchen==0.2.26` leaves `silu*up` in fp32 and rewrites INT8 rows (50 NFE vs unfused: **22.0 / 19.8 dB** — a different sample). [comfy-kitchen#124](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/comfy-kitchen/pull/124) rounds to the storage dtype first; fc2 is then bit-exact and the fuse is about **−4.4 s / 20 NFE** (~−10 s at 50). Leave it off until that lands.

Results are in the table at the top. Text encoding and VAE decode are unchanged; Spectrum only skips selected DiT stacks.

title: [diffusion] fix: fix loading a block-FP8 quantized MiniMax-H3 DiT
author: decajoin
body: Quantizing the MiniMax-H3 DiT with SGLang's own per_block_cast_to_fp8 yields a standard block-FP8 checkpoint that loads without error and then generates broken output: H3 stores qkv grouped per head, so the DiT already permutes those rows into [q_all, k_all, v_all] as it loads, but the accompanying weight_scale_inv tensor was passed through untouched, leaving every 128x128 tile scaling rows it no longer covered. Apply the same reorder to the scale, counting its rows in blocks rather than channels; head_dim and the block are both 128 so each head's q/k/v occupies whole scale rows, a block size that straddles heads cannot be fixed by a row permutation and now raises. ## Motivation A block-FP8 MiniMax-H3 DiT loads **without any error** and then generates a blank frame. Nothing in the log says anything is wrong: dtypes match, shapes match, `Detected fp8 checkpoint` is printed, the server reaches ready and serves requests at normal speed. Only the output is gone. H3 checkpoints store qkv grouped per attention head — `[h0_q, h0_k, h0_v, h1_q, ...]` — while `QKVParallelLinear` expects `[q_all, k_all, v_all]`. The DiT has always handled this: `_install_qkv_weight_loader` permutes those rows at load time. A block-FP8 checkpoint carries a second tensor alongside the weight, one scale per 128x128 tile, and #35740's row-count gate passes that tensor through untouched: it compares against 21504, while the scale's leading dim is 168. Once the weight rows moved, every tile was still scaling the rows it covered *before* the permutation. This is not specific to any one quantizer. The scale is produced in checkpoint layout — which is correct, a checkpoint should keep the released layout — and applying the reorder is the runtime's job, so any standard block-FP8 H3 checkpoint hits this. `per_block_cast_to_fp8` is SGLang's own quantization helper, so the bug reproduces with SGLang alone: ```python from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp8_utils import per_block_cast_to_fp8 # blocks.0.attn.qkv_proj.weight of MiniMax-H3: [21504, 5376] bf16, 56 heads x 128 q, s = per_block_cast_to_fp8(weight.cuda()) # q [21504, 5376] fp8_e4m3 # s [168, 42] fp32 (168 = 56 heads x 3, so one scale row per head's q / k / v) ``` ## Modifications `_install_qkv_weight_loader` now scales both the permutation and the row count gating it down by the block height for a `BlockQuantScaleParameter`, so the same `_install_qkv_row_reorder` from #35740 covers both layouts and the `weight_loader` and `rank_local_weight_transform` paths stay in step. A new module-level `_qkv_scale_block_rows` reads `weight_block_size[0]` off the projection's quant config. - `head_dim` and the block size are both 128, so each head's q/k/v occupies whole scale rows and the row permutation is exact. - A `weight_block_size` that straddles heads cannot be repaired by a row permutation and now raises instead of silently corrupting the model. - Anything not block-quantized — BF16, online fp8, per-tensor fp8, NVFP4 — reports one weight row per scale row and takes the previous path unchanged. - The GGUF path is unaffected: it already stores qkv as `[q_all, k_all, v_all]` and is gated out of the reorder entirely. Files:`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/minimax_h3.py`, `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_minimax_h3_dit_contract.py`. ## Accuracy Tests **End to end.** Served on 2x RTX 5090, TP=2, layerwise offload for dit and text_encoder, same prompt / seed 42 / 10 steps / 4s / 768p. | | output | frame contrast | frame-to-frame motion | encoded size | |---|---|---|---|---| | BF16 (reference) | normal | 62.5 | 13.6 | 1.7 MB | | block-FP8, **with** this fix | normal | 67.5 | 15.9 | 1.9 MB | | block-FP8, **without** this fix | blank | **4.0** | **0.7** | **0.5 MB** | Without the fix the frame carries no content at all: spatial contrast collapses 16x and inter-frame motion 19x. With the fix, block-FP8 tracks the BF16 reference at PSNR-Y 16.5 dB / SSIM-Y 0.68; the residual difference is sampling-trajectory divergence from fp8 rounding rather than corruption — the two videos show the same scene, subject and action with a mild composition drift. **Unit tests.** New cases in `test_minimax_h3_dit_contract.py` cover the reorder itself, the straddling-block guard, and the untouched non-block-quantized path. The H3 and quantization suites under `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/` pass. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Same configuration as above. This PR does not change any compute path — it only fixes what the loader writes into the scale parameter — so the speed difference is simply block-FP8 versus BF16 weights under layerwise offload: | | time | |---|---| | BF16 | 104.7s | | block-FP8 with this fix | **70.4s** (1.49x) | ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing surface changes; block-FP8 checkpoints were already meant to load. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #33395837881](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33395837881) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #33395837928](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33395837928) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :x: [Run #33395837967](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33395837967)

title: [AMD] Fix Qwen3.5 MTP dropping fused shared-expert weights
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

Since #33889, Qwen3.5 MXFP4 with MTP speculative decoding on MI355X lost about 12% throughput. The cause is that the MTP draft model is loaded without its shared-expert weights.

**What fusion does to the weight layout.** When a Qwen3.5 MoE layer fuses its shared expert, it deliberately does not build a separate `shared_expert` module — the shared expert becomes one more routed expert, living in slot `num_experts`. Any loader for such a layer therefore has to route `mlp.shared_expert.*` into that slot. `qwen3_5.py` does exactly that; `qwen3_5_mtp.py` never learned to.

**Why the target model is unaffected.** In this checkpoint the target's routed experts are MXFP4 while its shared expert stays bf16. Fusing them would push a higher-precision tensor through the quantized routed-expert path, so `can_fuse_shared_expert()` refuses. The target therefore always takes the unfused path, keeps its `shared_expert` module, and loads normally — the gap in the MTP loader is invisible from here.

**Why the draft model is affected, and only recently.** The MTP module is excluded from quantization in full: all 1536 `mtp.*` routed-expert tensors and its shared expert alike. The draft is thus uniformly bf16, nothing is mixed-precision, and fusing it is perfectly valid — the gate correctly says yes. It simply never had the chance before. Until #33889, the target's Quark config installed a single process-wide `disable_shared_experts_fusion` override, which switched fusion off for every runner, draft included. #33889 made that decision per-runner, so the draft started fusing for the first time and immediately ran into the loader gap.

**Why nobody noticed.** With fusion on there is no `shared_expert` module to load into, and the expert mapping only covers slots `0 .. num_experts-1`, so each `mlp.shared_expert.{gate,up,down}_proj.weight` matches nothing and ends at `logger.warning_once("Parameter ... not found in params_dict, skip loading")` — three tensors per TP rank, one suppressed log line, no error. The draft then runs with an uninitialized shared expert. Since a speculative draft cannot corrupt verified output, accuracy is unaffected; the damage appears only as a fall in accept rate, from 0.65 to 0.51, and hence in throughput.

This PR teaches the MTP loader to place those weights into the fused slot, so the draft that #33889 legitimately enabled actually receives them.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`, mirroring `qwen3_5.py`:

- Size the expert mapping as `num_experts + num_fused_shared_experts` so slot `num_experts` has an entry. The fusion count is read from the constructed modules, because `num_fused_shared_experts` is set on `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration` and the MTP wraps a `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM`, which does not carry it.
- Rewrite `mlp.shared_expert.` to `mlp.experts.{num_experts}.` before the mapping loops.

Both are keyed on the model's actual fusion state rather than on a platform check. When nothing fuses, `num_fused_shared_experts` is `0`, the mapping size is unchanged and the rewrite never fires, so this is a no-op for every non-fusing configuration.

Not covered: the fused-checkpoint variant (a single `experts.gate_up_proj` tensor). `qwen3_5.py` handles that with a dedicated branch that chunks the tensor into `w1`/`w3`; the MTP loader's `load_fused_expert_weights` indexes per expert id and cannot serve a single shared-expert tensor. Adding that path untested seemed worse than leaving it, since no checkpoint on hand exercises it.

## Accuracy Tests

No accuracy change is expected: only the draft model changes, and a speculative draft cannot alter verified output. The visible effect is the accept rate. Measured over ~100 decode-batch samples per point.

| conc | accept_len before | after | accept_rate before | after |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 2.5278 | 2.9533 | 0.5097 | 0.6509 |
| 8 | 2.5507 | 2.9374 | 0.5168 | 0.6457 |
| 16 | 2.5144 | 2.9508 | 0.5054 | 0.6501 |

Skipped weights during load go from 3 per TP rank to 0.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Summary at conc=4

| Config | Total Throughput | Median E2E (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `eda0ddc260d4` (last good) | 5365.74 | 5992.71 | 326.84 | 6.25 |
| `b61a06921e` (#33889) | 4716.15 | 6662.60 | 322.72 | 7.05 |
| `b61a06921e` + PR #35719 | 5429.77 | 5912.64 | 326.93 | 6.11 |

The third row was obtained by switching shared-expert fusion off on `b61a06921e`, which removes the unloaded-shared-expert condition from the draft; this PR removes the same condition by loading the fused weights instead of dropping them.

### Full sweep

MI355X, `amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4`, TP=2, EAGLE MTP (3 steps / topk 1 / 4 draft tokens), page-size 16, `fp8_e4m3` KV, `--attention-backend aiter`, ISL=8192 / OSL=1024, `num_prompts = 10 x conc`, server relaunched per concurrency with `--max-running-requests = conc`. Server flags follow `benchmarks/single_node/fixed_seq_len/qwen3.5_fp4_mi355x_mtp.sh`. Before and after were run back to back on the same GPU pair, both at `7f8f030000`.

| conc | Total Throughput before | after | Delta | Median E2E (ms) before | after | Median TTFT (ms) before | after | Median TPOT (ms) before | after |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 4746.11 | 5417.31 | **+14.14%** | 6726.7 | 5969.1 | 333.3 | 336.7 | 7.07 | 6.22 |
| 8 | 6835.64 | 7626.54 | **+11.57%** | 9243.7 | 8370.3 | 336.4 | 335.9 | 9.67 | 8.82 |
| 16 | 9011.82 | 10141.08 | **+12.53%** | 13997.8 | 12840.5 | 346.1 | 361.6 | 14.86 | 13.48 |

The gain is decode-side, as expected from an accept-rate change: TTFT is flat, TPOT improves by 9–12%.

This restores the configuration to its previously published InferenceX level. The last sweep on image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260730` recorded 582.84 / 852.30 / 1130.14 output tok/s at conc 4 / 8 / 16; with this patch the same setup measures 602.47 / 857.12 / 1123.38. Bisecting `accept len` over the 759 commits between that image's sglang and `63d783bbe0` lands on #33889, with a clean split (2.84–2.92 before, 2.50–2.57 after, no intermediate values).
