title: [diffusion] Enable LongCat breakable CUDA graphs
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- enable the existing diffusion breakable CUDA graph runner for `meituan-longcat/LongCat-Image`
- keep LongCat's fixed 512-token DiT prompt shape unchanged so the generic BCG buckets do not capture unused expanded signatures
- document the deployment command and refresh the checked-in diffusion performance/profile skills

## Why

LongCat's native eager DiT trace is launch-heavy between attention calls. The existing BCG runner can capture those regions as 31 graph segments, but LongCat was not admitted by the model and pipeline allowlists.

LongCat always sends the full 512-token prompt body to the DiT. A small model-specific pass-through padder therefore preserves one reusable signature for short and long raw prompts instead of applying generic prompt padding.

## Production-shape visual and end-to-end A/B (B300)

Prompt from the checked-in LongCat diffusion benchmark preset: `A red panda reading a book beside a sunlit window.`

Configuration: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, native `--backend sglang`, BF16, 1 GPU, 1024x1024, 50 steps, guidance 4.5, seed 42, prompt rewrite disabled, `quality=lossless`, `--performance-mode manual`.

![LongCat main eager versus PR BCG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/35724/main-vs-pr.jpg)

The main and PR PNGs are byte-exact (`sha256=6a44ff30a185993f50d23da660b3cbe42fb8fdf8ac1d0d612d0086f35c723372`).

| Path | Saved-request e2e runs | Mean e2e | Mean denoise stage |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| main, eager | 7.422 / 7.421 / 7.445 s | 7.429 s | 7.109 s |
| this PR, BCG | 7.178 / 7.174 / 7.175 s | 7.175 s | 6.261 s |

That is a **3.42% end-to-end reduction** and an **11.93% denoise-stage reduction** on B300. Request e2e starts immediately before `generate()` and ends after the output file exists and its SHA256 is recorded, so it includes prompt encoding, DiT, VAE decode, materialization, and PNG saving. Model loading, the one-time 16.43 s BCG capture, and one benchmark warmup are excluded. Logs confirm the native backend with no diffusers fallback.

The task-owned B300 LongCat cache was deleted after this model group: 29,316,959,360 bytes removed and zero residual model-cache files verified.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files ...` on all changed files
- `python -m pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_diffusion_bcg_padding.py`: 22 passed
- H200, BF16, 1 GPU, 1024x1024, 50 steps, guidance 4.5, prompt rewrite disabled, lossless quality:
  - eager: 177.3 / 177.0 / 177.2 ms per denoise step across three different prompt lengths
  - BCG: 173.1 / 173.3 / 173.1 ms per denoise step (about 2.3% faster)
  - all three BCG outputs were pixel-exact against eager
  - one 31-segment graph was captured and reused for all three prompts
- default BCG text buckets also captured exactly one graph without bucket warnings; the 8-step output remained pixel-exact
- task-owned LongCat cache cleanup: removed 58,644,690,730 bytes and verified zero residual model-weight files

BCG remains opt-in and resolution-specific. The H200 peak was about 33.4 GB with BCG versus 31.7 GB eager.

title: [kernel] Split the custom all-reduce communicator into push/pull planes
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> Generated by Claude.

## Motivation

Every JIT collective in `csrc/distributed` and `csrc/kimi_k3/comm` took one flat `CommunicatorObj` that carried every buffer any of them might want: `2 * world_size` push slots, a pull workspace, per-block semaphores, a rank-local counter, and one of the three multicast addresses. Consequences:

- The other two multicast addresses travelled out of band. `ws_mc_base` was an `int64_t` argument repeated at five call sites, always the same constant; `pull_sem_mc_ptr` went through a per-world-size Python dict populated by `register_comm()`, duplicated in three modules.
- A push-only owner (the fused qk-norm instances in `minimax_m2`) had to allocate a placeholder 1 KB pull buffer plus one semaphore purely to satisfy the constructor.
- Only `custom_all_reduce.cuh` ever read `pull_workspaces` / `pull_bytes` / `pull_mc_workspace`. The K3 pull kernels reduce in place on the caller's own symmetric input and borrow the plane just to barrier on, so half the object was dead weight for most callers.
- `custom_all_reduce.cuh` defined helpers at `namespace sglang` scope and was `#include`d by three K3 files across directories, so renaming anything inside it silently broke downstream kernels.

## What changed

Split the object by lifetime rather than by direction:

| | contents |
|---|---|
| `sgl.distributed.PushPlane` | zero-filled symmetric push slots, rank-local phase counter, multicast base |
| `sgl.distributed.PullPlane` | symmetric pull buffers + per-block semaphores, both multicast bases. Either half may be a 0-element tensor |
| `sgl.distributed.Communicator` | the two planes (either optional) + the pull launch widths; what every kernel takes |

Both *fixed* multicast addresses now live on the planes. That deletes the `ws_mc_base` parameter from five entry points and the `_PULL_SEM_MC_MAP` registry from three modules. The *per-call* multicast address — a slice of the caller's own symmetric buffer, so it changes every call — stays a plain `intptr_t`, which is what it should be.

`PullPlane`'s optional halves replace the placeholder-buffer trick: `minimax_m2` now constructs `Communicator(push=..., pull=None)` and a kernel that needs a missing plane fails with a message instead of reading a dummy buffer.

### Shared vocabulary moved under `include/`

- **`include/sgl_kernel/distributed/ptx.cuh`** collects the inline PTX the collectives share into `sglang::device::ptx`, which `mbarrier.cuh` and the two K3 files reopen. Removed: three identical copies of the multimem flag increment, three copies of the "multicast alias of a semaphore's flag" helper (now `Semaphore::mc_flag`), and the 16B access helpers that were defined at `namespace sglang` scope inside `custom_all_reduce.cuh`. `csrc/kimi_k3/comm/ptx_sys.cuh` is deleted. The five communication kernels now contain zero inline PTX.
- **`Barrier` / `McBarrier`** (unicast fan-out and one-`multimem.red` variants of the same window protocol) and **`LamportTrait`** (the pos-zero marker) live next to the planes, so each protocol has one implementation instead of one per kernel.
- The three `csrc` → `csrc` includes of `custom_all_reduce.cuh` are gone. What they actually used — `reduce_vec`, the marker traits — moved under `include/`.
- `alloc_workspace_tensor` moved to `host::ffi`, so `utils.cuh` no longer depends on `ffi.h`.

`tp_qknorm`'s 8B `ld.volatile` / `st.volatile` pair became `ld_relaxed_8B` / `st_relaxed_8B` at `.sys` scope (PTX defines volatile as relaxed at system scope, and the store is cross-GPU). Load scope measured identical at `.gpu`, so the `.gpu` load variant was dropped and the vocabulary has one scope.

## Verification (8×B200, SM100)

**Correctness — 291 tests, all passing**

| test | |
|---|---|
| `test_custom_all_reduce.py` (8 GPU) | 180 passed |
| `test_ar_fusion.py` (8 GPU) | 58 passed |
| `test_tp_qknorm.py` (8 GPU) | 42 passed |
| `test_collectives.py` (8 GPU) | 5 passed |
| `test_compute.py` | 6 passed |
| `test_custom_all_reduce_v2_capability.py` | 4 passed |
| `test_attn_residual.py` | 1 passed |

All 11 affected JIT modules build; `fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm_sm120` verified with a direct SM120 nvcc compile. clangd reports zero diagnostics on every touched file except two pre-existing cutlass include-path gaps in `.clangd`.

**Registers / spills** — `cuobjdump -res-usage`, this branch vs the merge base, kernels paired by hand where the refactor renamed them:

- **No spills anywhere** (`STACK=0`, `LOCAL=0` for every kernel).
- Unchanged or better everywhere except `1shot_push`: bf16 60→63, fp16 61→63, fp32 56→58. That kernel is 2.7–6.2 % *faster* — `LamportTrait`'s 4-byte-atom marker test replaces a per-bf16-half test, cutting its SASS from 512 to 344 instructions.
- `2shot_pull` eager improves (bf16 53→51) and the multicast variants drop one register.

**Performance** — kernel time only, measured by replaying a CUDA graph of 20 chained calls so host dispatch is excluded; three interleaved rounds per arm, per-arm spread under 1 %:

| variant | delta vs merge base |
|---|---|
| `1shot_push` / eager (dispatched ≤ 768 KB) | **−2.7 % … −6.2 %** |
| `2shot_pull` / multicast (dispatched > 768 KB) | −0.03 % … +0.39 % |
| `1shot_pull` eager and multicast | −1.1 % … +0.6 % |
| `2shot_pull` / eager | +0.5 % … +0.9 % |

33 points: median +0.32 %, worst +0.92 %. On the path the tuned SM100/world-8 config actually dispatches: median **−3.30 %**, worst +0.39 %.

One note on how that number was reached. An earlier revision of this branch regressed `2shot_pull` eager by 7–18 %. Bisecting with self-contained reference kernels showed the params layout, the `Barrier` object and the `Impl` abstraction were all innocent — an exact transplant of the old body still regressed. The cause was the address form: folding the shard offset into the eight base pointers as a typed 32-bit vector index keeps the peer table on the uniform datapath (`UIMAD.WIDE` off a constant-bank base), whereas biasing `vid` per access, or using a 64-bit byte offset, makes all eight addresses thread-varying and costs ~12 registers per thread. Also, binding a params array address to a named local that stays live across the kernel breaks the same proof. Both are noted in comments at the point of use, since either one silently costs ~10 %.

title: [multimodal] Fix NVFP4 diffusion models on sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 50xx)
author: whn09
body:
## Motivation

NVFP4 diffusion checkpoints cannot be served on sm_120 GPUs (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / RTX 50xx). Two independent defects in the shared ModelOpt FP4 path are involved; neither is model-specific.

**1. The default FP4 GEMM backend does not exist on sm_120.**
`CudaPlatformBase.get_modelopt_flashinfer_fp4_backend()` defaults to `"trtllm"`, and `flashinfer.mm_fp4` rejects it there:

```
ValueError: mm_fp4 does not support backend 'trtllm' with capability 120
```

so the first quantized linear aborts and no NVFP4 model runs at all.

**2. The block-scale layout is chosen by a heuristic whose negative branch is unreachable.**
In `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading()` the `trtllm` branch fetches its own shuffled scale layout and **returns**. Everything still executing below it is therefore a TMA-layout consumer (`cutlass`, `cudnn`, `auto`) — but the layout was instead selected by a module-name test:

```python
uses_flux1_scale_layout = not getattr(
    self.quant_config, "checkpoint_uses_packed_qkv", False
) and getattr(layer, "prefix", "").startswith(
    ("transformer_blocks.", "single_transformer_blocks.")
)
if flashinfer_backend is None or uses_flux1_scale_layout:
```

Any model whose blocks are not named with the FLUX.1 prefixes skips the swizzle and hands the kernel block scales in the wrong layout. This does not raise — it silently produces broken output.

## Modifications

- `runtime/platforms/cuda.py`: default the FP4 GEMM backend to `"auto"` on sm_120 (which resolves to flashinfer's sm_12x NVFP4 kernel) and keep `"trtllm"` elsewhere. `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_BACKEND` still overrides. Uses the pre-existing `is_sm120()`, so no other capability changes behaviour.
- `runtime/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py`: apply the 128x4 TMA reshape unconditionally, and delete the unreachable heuristic. This also removes two defensive `getattr()`s and the now-redundant second `_get_fp4_gemm_op()` call.
- `test/unit/test_modelopt_fp4_backend.py`: new unit test pinning the default-backend resolution (sm_120 vs other, all explicit env spellings, unknown value falls back to the platform default).

## Accuracy Tests

Verified on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120) with an NVFP4 MiniMax-H3 checkpoint:

- before: startup fails on (1); forcing a backend past it renders grey noise, which is (2).
- after: output is **bit-identical** (md5 of the produced mp4) to the previously env-forced workaround, with no environment variables set. Same seed, same request, three runs.

title: [multimodal] MiniMax-H3: fix quantized qkv scales and missing-param policy
author: whn09
body:
## Motivation

Two MiniMax-H3 model-side defects that only appear on a quantized checkpoint (NVFP4 or fp8).

**1. Per-output-row quantization metadata is not reordered with its rows.**
MiniMax-H3 checkpoints store qkv grouped, so `_install_qkv_weight_loader()` permutes the fused qkv weight's output rows into `q|k|v` order via `_reorder_grouped_qkv_to_qkv()`. NVFP4 block scales and fp8 per-channel scales are indexed by that same output row, and they were loaded unpermuted — every scale ends up attached to the wrong row. The weights are correct; the dequantized values are not. The symptom is grey mush, with no error anywhere.

**2. `_mark_missing_params_required()` overwrites each quant method's own missing-parameter policy.**
A quant method declares in `create_weights()` what it can synthesize when a scale is absent from the checkpoint — weight-only NVFP4 has no `input_scale` and marks it `missing_param_init = "ones"`. H3 then blanket-stamps every parameter `"error"`, so the declaration is lost and the loader raises:

```
ValueError: Required checkpoint parameter '...input_scale' was not loaded
```

## Modifications

- New module-level helper `_install_qkv_row_reorder()` wraps a qkv parameter's weight loader (and its `rank_local_weight_transform`, needed by rank-local FSDP) with the same row permutation used for the weight. Applied to every `qkv_proj` parameter except the weight itself.
  The gate is the row count: a tensor whose leading dim is not the checkpoint's qkv row count is passed through untouched, which covers per-tensor scalars and swizzled block-scale layouts that are not row-indexed. It reads the **loaded checkpoint tensor**, not the local parameter, so it also holds under tensor parallelism, where the local parameter only owns its own shard of the rows.
- `_mark_missing_params_required()` now only claims parameters that have no declared policy.
- `test/unit/test_minimax_h3_qkv_scale_reorder.py`: new unit test covering both branches of the row-count gate (row-indexed metadata is permuted, swizzled and per-tensor metadata is not) on the wrapped loader and on `rank_local_weight_transform`.

Depends on nothing else, but on sm_120 both this and #35739 are required to get a working NVFP4 MiniMax-H3 (the two fixes are in different layers, hence separate PRs).

## Accuracy Tests

On one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120) with an NVFP4 MiniMax-H3 checkpoint:

- (2) alone is a hard load failure.
- With (2) fixed, (1) renders grey mush.
- With both fixed, output is structurally the same as the bf16 checkpoint, and bit-identical across repeated runs at the same seed.

The reorder is only reachable for a quantized checkpoint with per-row scales; a bf16 run has no parameters other than the weight on `qkv_proj`, so it is unaffected.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Weight-load-time only; no change to the forward path and none measured (paired runs within 0.2%).

title: Fix overlap prebuilt row reuse race
author: jasonjk-park
body:
Wait for outstanding overlap forward work before prebuilt batch processing can seed a reused request-pool row.

## Motivation

Bug fix for race condition in FutureMap.

publish() call can happen in two cases:
(1) in forward stream after draft+verify.
(2) in schedule stream, when PD disagg is enabled, and prefill request is arriving.

publish() modifies shared states in FutureMap, so they must be ordered correctly to avoid race.

publish_ready cannot be used for synchronization because stash() after record also has FutureMap shared state modification.

## Modifications

(1) schedule stream to wait for forward stream before calling publish in PD disagg
(2) remove unnecessary chaining in record as (1) guarantees ordering
(3) unit test

title: [XPU] Support GPT-OSS MXFP4 checkpoints on Intel XPU
author: jmunetong
body:
## Enable GPT-OSS MXFP4 checkpoints on Intel XPU via the native W4A16 grouped GEMM

### Motivation

`openai/gpt-oss-20b` and `-120b` ship MXFP4-quantized MoE weights. Every SGLang MXFP4 kernel targets CUDA (`triton_kernels` / Marlin / FlashInfer cutlass), HIP (aiter) or CPU (AMX), so on `--device xpu` the checkpoint was rejected before any layer was built:

```
ValueError: Unknown quantization method: mxfp4. Must be one of ['fp8', 'mxfp8', ...]
  configs/model_config.py:_verify_quantization
```

This PR enables the checkpoint on XPU and serves it through the **sgl-kernel-xpu W4A16 grouped GEMM**: the packed MXFP4 weights are consumed **directly, at 4 bits, with no bf16 upcast**. Weights stay 4-bit in HBM and are dequantized per tile in registers inside the kernel — the whole point of MXFP4 on XPU.

> **Supersedes / consolidates #35742.** An earlier revision of this PR added a device-neutral *bf16-upcast* fallback (dequantize MXFP4 → bf16 at load, serve through the unquantized MoE). That path has been **removed**: it cost ~3.1× the weight memory and doesn't fit 120b. The native W4A16 routing from #35742 now lives here, so #35742 can be closed in favor of this PR.

### Modifications

Net **5 files, +117/-2** on top of upstream.

| # | Change | File | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Register `mxfp4` for XPU, gated on `is_xpu()` | `quantization/__init__.py` | Passes `_verify_quantization` on XPU so the checkpoint is accepted; backends with no MXFP4 kernel keep the existing clean error rather than silently upcasting. |
| 2 | Route MXFP4 MoE to the sgl-kernel-xpu W4A16 grouped GEMM: post-load is a free `.view(torch.int8)` of the packed nibbles, no upcast | `quantization/mxfp4.py` | The XPU grouped GEMM consumes the checkpoint layout (packed e2m1 `[E,N,K/2]` + N-outer ue8m0 g32 scales) directly. |
| 3 | Pad the per-rank MoE intermediate to a multiple of `mxfp4_block` (32) | `quantization/mxfp4.py` | See **Intermediate padding** below. |
| 4 | Forward the GPT-OSS swiglu config (`activation`, `gemm1_alpha`, `gemm1_clamp_limit`, `swiglu_limit`, `routed_scaling_factor`) that was previously dropped | `moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py` | Without it the experts silently computed a plain `silu*up` instead of the clamped `gate*sigmoid(gate*alpha)*(up+1)` the config asks for. |
| 5 | XPU quantization docs | `docs/…/quantization.mdx`, `docs/…/xpu.mdx` | Document the supported path. |

CUDA / HIP behaviour is unchanged: the generic post-load `else` is the upstream `triton_kernels.upcast_from_mxfp` fallback, and XPU never reaches it (it returns after the `.view(int8)`).

Rebased onto current `main`. #34492 removed `use_intel_xpu_backend()` and the `SGLANG_USE_SGL_XPU` flag behind it, since the XPU backend is unconditional now, so the gate is `is_xpu()` -- read via a module-level `_is_xpu`, matching the existing `_is_cpu` / `_is_hip` constants in `mxfp4.py`.

### Intermediate padding (`mxfp4.py`, `create_weights`)

`models/gpt_oss.py` shards the MoE intermediate by **whole MXFP4 blocks** — a block of 32 shares one scale and cannot be split across ranks — so a rank's slice is `ceil(intermediate/32 / tp) * 32`, which can **exceed** `intermediate / tp`. For gpt-oss-20b at tp=4 that is `736` against `2880/4 = 720`, and the loader's copy overflows an unaligned buffer with `size of tensor a (360) must match … b (368)`.

The fix rounds the per-rank intermediate **up to a multiple of `mxfp4_block`**, which reproduces the loader's shard exactly (736), so the copy fits with **no wasted rows**:

```python
elif _is_xpu:
    intermediate_size_per_partition_after_pad = round_up(
        intermediate_size_per_partition, mxfp4_block   # 32
    )
```

That padded value dimensions every expert buffer — `w13_weight [E, 2*N, hidden//2]`, `w13_weight_scale [E, 2*N, hidden//32]`, `w2_weight [E, hidden, N//2]`, `w2_weight_scale [E, hidden, N//32]` — and the grouped GEMM recovers K/N from the packed shapes, so the kernel sees the true dims. It is numerically inert (the padded rows are zero, scale byte `127` → ×1) and only ever triggers when `intermediate/tp` isn't already a multiple of 32 (i.e. never at tp=1/2; it bites at tp=4/8).

### Accuracy

GSM8K, 5-shot, 200 questions, `--max-new-tokens 512`, `--temperature 0.0`. `bare server` (no `--chat-template` / parser flags) to match `bench_sglang.py`'s raw `/generate` path.

**gpt-oss-20b, tp=4** — native W4A16 is what this PR delivers:

| Metric | W4A16 native (**this PR**) | Cookbook B200 |
|---|---|---|
| **Accuracy** | **0.555** (111/200) | 0.535 |
| Wilson 95% CI | [0.486, 0.622] | [0.466, 0.603] |
| Invalid | 0.095 | 0.165 |
| Weight memory / rank | **3.30 GB** | n/a |
| Load time / rank | **2.57 s** | n/a |

**gpt-oss-120b, tp=8** — native W4A16 (this PR); bf16 could never fit (26.7 GiB/rank against 23.9 GiB cards):

| Metric | W4A16 native (**this PR**) | Cookbook B200 |
|---|---|---|
| **Accuracy** | **0.870** (174/200) | 0.880 (176/200) |
| Wilson 95% CI | [0.816, 0.910] | [0.828, 0.918] |
| Invalid | 0.015 (3/200) | 0.005 (1/200) |

- **This PR reproduces the reference.** 0.555 vs 0.535 (20b) and 0.870 vs 0.880 (120b) are within the Wilson half-width (±0.07 at N=200) — do not over-rank them; what they establish is that the dequantization is sound (a mis-unpacked weight would collapse the score, not move it by a few questions).
- The removed bf16-upcast fallback previously scored 0.520 (104/200) on 20b, i.e. also reference-consistent — but at **3.1× the weight memory and 2.0× the load time** of native, which is why native supersedes it.
- The 20b `0.555` figure was provided by the user rather than observed by our harness (client concurrency unrecorded); the 120b `0.870` was measured by our harness.

### Functional

4× / 8× Intel Arc Pro B60, `--attention-backend intel_xpu`; server reaches `ready to roll`. Streaming reasoning (`--reasoning-parser gpt-oss`) returns the correct answer with its verification step; streaming tool calling (`--tool-call-parser gpt-oss`) emits valid JSON args and handles the tool-result follow-up turn. The `moe_w4a16::GemmCuteName<bf16, uint8, uint8, bf16, …>` kernel is confirmed in the profiler trace with **no activation-quantize or bf16-upcast kernel present**.

### Speed

The forward path is the sgl-kernel-xpu W4A16 grouped GEMM (bf16 activations, 4-bit weights). Per-op profile-vs-projection breakdowns exist separately; no end-to-end speed claim is made in this PR beyond the memory/load figures above.

### Known limitations

- Needs context/concurrency capped on 24 GB cards; with defaults SGLang derives a large `context_len` / `max_running_requests` and warmup can OOM on the attention page table.
- The `mxfp4` registration is gated on `is_xpu()` rather than on the presence of the kernel. Since #34492 made sgl-kernel-xpu a hard requirement of `--device xpu`, `is_xpu()` carries the same meaning in practice, but one property is weaker than in earlier revisions of this PR: an XPU build whose sgl-kernel-xpu predates the W4A16 grouped GEMM now fails at the first forward (`ImportError` on `sgl_kernel.fused_experts`) instead of at config-verify time. There is no bf16-upcast fallback on XPU.

### Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [ ] Add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation (XPU quantization docs included).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: fix: FA4 paged-KV zero-size page-table registers on SM90
author: razorback16
body:
## Motivation

Serving `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` with `--attention-backend fa4` on a GH200 (Hopper, SM90) crashes in the scheduler during startup warmup, before the server ever accepts a request:

```
Generate warm up request for compiling DeepGEMM...
[2026-08-20 14:09:01] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 5174, in run_scheduler_process
    scheduler.run_event_loop()
  [...]
  File "sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py", line 1212, in self_attention
    attn_output = self.attn(q, k, v, forward_batch)
  File "sglang/srt/layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py", line 1134, in forward_extend
    return self.full_attn_backend.forward_extend(
  File "sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashattention_backend.py", line 1496, in forward_extend
    result = flash_attn_with_kvcache(
  File "sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attention_v4.py", line 276, in flash_attn_with_kvcache
    result = flash_attn_varlen_func(
  File "sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attn/cute/interface.py", line 1628, in _flash_attn_fwd
    _flash_attn_fwd.compile_cache[compile_key] = cute.compile(
  [... CUTLASS DSL trace-building frames elided ...]
  File "sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm90.py", line 806, in then_block_9
    self.load(
  File "sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm90.py", line 983, in while_after_block_2
    paged_kv_manager = PagedKVManager.create(
  File "sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attn/cute/paged_kv.py", line 119, in create
    tPrPage = cute.make_rmem_tensor((page_entry_per_thread,), Int32)
  [...]
  File "nvidia_cutlass_dsl/dsl_packages/cutlass/cute/core.py", line 339, in _check_shape
    raise ValueError(
        f"Expected size in shape to be strictly positive, but got {shape}"
    )
ValueError: Expected size in shape to be strictly positive, but got 0
```

Environment: GH200 480GB (SM90), CUDA 13.2, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` 4.6.2, sglang built from source at `eac91ac36` (line numbers above are from that commit). Reproduced with:

```
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \
  --attention-backend fa4 --kv-cache-dtype auto \
  --speculative-algorithm DFLASH \
  --speculative-draft-model-path z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 8
```

### Root cause

`PagedKVManager.create()` sizes its per-thread page-table registers with a floor division:

```python
page_entry_per_thread = n_block_size // num_threads   # num_threads = 128
```

When `tile_n < 128` this evaluates to `0`, and `cute.make_rmem_tensor((0,), Int32)` fails the shape check above.

Qwen3.8-27B's full-attention layers have `head_dim=256`, and `_tile_size_fwd_sm90()` returns `tile_n = 80` for that head dim (64 with a sliding window). sglang's default `page_size=1` never equals `tile_n`, so the non-TMA cp.async path — the one that stages the page table in registers — is always the one selected. So every paged-KV FA4 run on SM90 at `head_dim=256` hits this; `head_dim=192` is affected too (`tile_n` 112 / 96).

This is the same assertion seen in #32118 (merged) and #31903, but those addressed the SM100 diff-headdim split-KV case by not shrinking `tile_n` to 64 in `interface.py`; the division itself was left as-is. That doesn't cover SM90, where `tile_n = 80` is not a conditional shrink but the tile the heuristic picks unconditionally — there is no configuration that steers around it.

Upstream FA4 (`Dao-AILab/flash-attention`, `flash_attn/cute/paged_kv.py`) already uses ceiling division here, with a comment about counting the final partially populated wave of rows. sglang's vendored copy diverged.

## Modifications

One line in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attn/cute/paged_kv.py`: use `cute.ceil_div` instead of floor division.

Why `ceil` is the right size rather than merely non-zero: `load_KV()` indexes `tPrXPtr[m // gmem_threads_per_row]` for `m` in `range(n_block_size * gmem_threads_per_row / num_threads)`, so the largest index used needs exactly `ceil(n_block_size / num_threads)` entries. The entries this over-allocates when `n_block_size < num_threads` are already predicated off by the `row < n_block_size` check in `load_page_table()` (which writes `page = 0`), and are never consumed by the `shuffle_sync` in `load_KV()`.

Risk is limited to configurations that cannot currently run: `ceil == floor` whenever `n_block_size % num_threads == 0`, which is true of every tile that compiles today, so those kernels are bit-identical.

## Accuracy Tests

Standalone script calling `flash_attn_with_kvcache` on the paged path, checked against an fp32 SDPA reference, on GH200 (SM90). Deliberately shuffled page tables so page-index/offset mix-ups can't hide. Every case fails to compile on `main` and passes with this change:

| case | page_size | causal | window | max abs err |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| b1, s_q=s_k=512 | 1 | yes | – | 0.0156 |
| b3 ragged, s_q=[300,17,128], s_k=[300,1000,128] | 1 | yes | – | 0.0156 |
| b4 spec-decode, s_q=8, s_k=[513,80,81,1024] | 1 | yes | – | 0.0039 |
| b2, non-causal | 1 | no | – | 0.0039 |
| b2, multi-token pages | 64 | yes | – | 0.0156 |
| b2, sliding window (tile_n=64) | 1 | yes | (256, 0) | 0.0078 |

(`ref_absmax` ≈ 1.3–4.1, so these are bf16 rounding.)

End-to-end: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` on GH200 with `--attention-backend fa4` now completes startup warmup and serves. A 7044-token prompt with a needle placed mid-context returned the needle exactly, which exercises many `n_block` iterations of the cp.async page-table path rather than just compilation.

Not covered: SM100. `ceil == floor` for the tiles that arch uses, so no behavior change is expected there, but I don't have Blackwell hardware to confirm.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No impact. `page_entry_per_thread` is a compile-time constant and the generated kernel is unchanged for every configuration that compiles today.

## Follow-up (deliberately not in this PR)

With the root cause fixed, the `not (page_table is not None and q_stage == 1)` guard added by #32118 could likely be relaxed to restore its SMEM-saving `tile_n = 64` for SM100 diff-headdim decode. I can't validate that without Blackwell, so I've left it alone.

## Note on test coverage

`test/registered/attention/unittests/dense/test_fa4.py` runs `HEAD_DIM = 64` only, which is why this went unnoticed — no FA4 test exercises a `tile_n` that isn't a multiple of 128. Precedent: #32118 fixed the same assertion in this subsystem and validated it with a standalone repro rather than a committed test. Happy to add a regression case (here or under `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/`) gated to SM90 if reviewers want one; `1-gpu-large` is an H100 runner, so it would genuinely guard this.

title: [Perf] Tune the W4AFP8 DeepEP low-latency requant launch geometry
author: alexnails
body:
## Motivation

`fp8_per_token_to_per_tensor_quant_triton()` turns DeepEP low-latency's per-token-group fp8
payload into the per-tensor fp8 that the first CUTLASS W4A8 grouped GEMM consumes. It is a pure
streaming pass — two bytes moved and two multiplies per element — but three properties of its
launch shape cost more than the arithmetic does.

**Access width.** A 1024-element tile over 8 warps is 4 B/thread, which is exactly where Triton
stops vectorizing: the compiled kernel contained only `ld.global.b32` / `st.global.b32` on every
part tested. 4 warps put 8 B/thread in flight and restore `v2.b32` accesses (2 warps reach
`v4.b32`, but measured slower than 4).

**Scale addressing.** Scales were indexed on the element axis
(`(k_offsets // 128) * stride2`), so each 1024-lane load resolved to 8 distinct addresses read
128 times each. The dispatcher returns the last two scale dims column-major for TMA
(`[E, M, hidden // 128]` with `stride1 == 1`), so those 8 addresses are `m` elements apart — a
scattered gather, replicated per row, per tile.

**Grid shape.** The m-grid was pinned to 32 programs per expert regardless of how many rows were
live, so at low-latency decode row counts most programs only loaded `masked_m`, compared, and
exited. This is by far the largest effect, and it grows with the local expert count: at 256 local
experts and one row each, the kernel spent 35 µs to move 3 µs of data.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/ep_moe_kernels.py`

- Tile the payload as `[G_BLOCK_SIZE, 128]` — whole scale groups — instead of a flat run of
  elements. The per-group scale becomes one scalar load, the fast axis stays contiguous, and a
  partial `k` masks whole groups. (`K_BLOCK_SIZE` is renamed `G_BLOCK_SIZE` because the constexpr
  changed units: it counted hidden elements, it now counts 128-wide scale groups, so 8 groups is
  the old 1024 elements.)
- Launch with 4 warps.
- A 1024-element tile per program, widening to 2048 once there are >= 32 local experts, where the
  expert axis alone fills the machine. The tile is kept in *elements* and divided by the scale
  group width to get `G_BLOCK_SIZE`, because bytes-per-thread is the tuned quantity -- a different
  group width would otherwise silently halve or double the measured tile. It is also rounded down
  to the payload, so a small hidden size never runs a mostly-masked tile.
- `requant_launch_geometry()` sizes the m-grid from `expected_rows`: one program per expected row,
  floored at 4, never above the historical 32, and additionally capped by the expert count while
  fewer than 64 rows per expert are live — past that the extra programs carry real work rather
  than early exits, and the cap costs a few percent. The estimate is rounded **down** to a power
  of two because `dispatch_a` already rounds up (it adds the expert count before dividing), so a
  uniform average of 8 rows arrives as 9 and must not launch 16 programs. The m-grid therefore
  only ever *shrinks*, which is why no measured cell regresses.
- `expected_rows=None` keeps the previous **m-grid** for any other caller; note the tile width and
  warp count change regardless of that argument.

`cutlass_w4a8_moe.py` / `w4afp8.py` — thread the dispatcher's `expected_m` (already computed
host-side in `dispatch_a`, and constant for a captured CUDA graph) down to the requant. It is a
launch hint only: correctness does not depend on it, and an expert that receives more rows than
expected simply loops over more of them.

Tests: the GPU unit test covers the geometry combinations (row estimates, 4/40/128 experts,
row-major and column-major scales, uneven per-expert row counts); a CPU test pins the heuristic's
contracts; and a new `base-b-kernel-benchmark` entry compares the shipped geometry against the
previous one.

## Accuracy Tests

Output is **bitwise identical to the merged kernel** on H100, H200 and B200 — every shape below at
0, 1, 3, 7, 64 and all padded rows live, both scale layouts, plus a skewed `masked_m` where every
expert gets a different row count:

```
== bitwise equality vs main, high expert counts ==
   ok  k7168 E64    ok  k7168 E128   ok  k7168 E256
   ok  k3584 E112   ok  k3584 E256   ok  k3584 E512
   ALL PASS
```

Unit tests: **48 passed** on H100, H200 and B200 — and across two toolchains, `torch 2.11.0+cu130`
/ `triton 3.6.0` and `torch 2.13.0+cu130` / `triton 3.7.1` (the newer pair matters because the
access-width behaviour this PR exploits is Triton codegen, not hardware). That count includes the
existing W4AFP8 dtype and post-reorder CPU tests.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Merged `main` vs this branch, DeepEP column-major scales, timed inside a CUDA graph, variants
interleaved and order-swapped (the first variant measured reads ~10% fast on sub-2 µs shapes).
`rows` is live rows per expert, and the row estimate passed in is what `dispatch_a` would report
for that dispatch.

**8 to 56 local experts**

| shape | rows | H100 | H200 | B200 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7168, 8 experts | 8 / 32 | 1.03x / 1.11x | 1.08x / 1.10x | 0.98x / 1.18x |
| | 512 / 1024 | 1.18x / 1.18x | 1.25x / 1.24x | 1.33x / **1.48x** |
| 3584, 8 experts | 8 / 32 | 1.23x / 1.15x | 1.27x / 1.14x | 1.01x / 1.14x |
| | 512 / 1024 | 1.15x / 1.06x | 1.28x / 1.07x | 1.22x / 1.24x |
| 3584, 56 experts | 8 / 32 | **2.43x** / 1.85x | **2.51x** / 1.92x | **2.32x** / 2.00x |
| | 128 / 256 | 1.30x / 1.21x | 1.52x / 1.39x | 1.74x / 1.84x |
| 1152, 8 experts | 8 / 32 | 1.06x / 1.06x | 1.11x / 1.07x | 1.01x / 1.05x |
| | 512 / 1024 | 1.18x / 1.19x | 1.19x / 1.20x | 1.16x / 1.19x |

The single sub-1.00x cell is B200 at 8 rows: 1.84 vs 1.87 µs, a 0.03 µs tie.

**64 to 512 local experts** — where the old fixed grid hurt most (`main` µs -> branch µs on H100):

| shape | rows=1 | rows=8 | rows=32 | rows=128 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7168, 64 experts | 9.3 -> 1.9 (**4.9x**) | 9.6 -> 3.1 (3.1x) | 13.3 -> 7.3 (1.81x) | 53.2 -> 44.4 (1.20x) |
| 7168, 128 experts | 18.1 -> 2.1 (**8.6x**) | 18.2 -> 4.5 (4.1x) | 33.5 -> 23.5 (1.42x) | 101.5 -> 84.0 (1.21x) |
| 7168, 256 experts | 35.3 -> 3.3 (**10.6x**) | 35.8 -> 7.9 (4.6x) | 64.8 -> 44.5 (1.46x) | 195.2 -> 161.4 (1.21x) |
| 3584, 112 experts | 9.5 -> 1.8 (5.2x) | 9.6 -> 2.8 (3.5x) | 13.5 -> 6.4 (2.10x) | 47.5 -> 38.7 (1.23x) |
| 3584, 256 experts | 20.6 -> 2.2 (9.2x) | 20.7 -> 4.1 (5.0x) | 37.7 -> 22.6 (1.67x) | 102.2 -> 82.4 (1.24x) |
| 3584, 512 experts | 40.3 -> 3.3 (**12.1x**) | 41.0 -> 8.2 (5.0x) | 73.7 -> 44.7 (1.65x) | — |

H200 and B200 are the same shape and generally better at >= 32 rows: e.g. 3584 / 512 experts at 32
rows is 2.07x on H200 and 2.86x on B200, and 7168 / 256 experts at 128 rows is 1.39x / 1.87x.

**Rounding the row estimate down rather than up** (both directions measured at the same shapes):

| shape | true rows | H100 (triton 3.6 / 3.7.1) | H200 | B200 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7168, 8 experts | 4 | +12.1% / +0.3% | +12.5% | +12.3% |
| 3584, 56 experts | 8 | +3.5% / +3.0% | +4.9% | +6.1% |
| 3584, 128 experts | 4 | +7.4% / +8.0% | +8.1% | +8.9% |

Positive means rounding up is slower. Triton 3.7.1 closes the 7168 case to a tie but never
reverses the direction.

The in-tree benchmark reproduces the low-expert-count end (H200, µs):

```
      hidden  num_experts    m   rows |    tuned    legacy-geometry
        7168            8 1024      8 |   1.5698             2.2400
        7168            8 1024    256 |   8.9140            11.0138
        3584           56  256      8 |   2.3238             5.5467
        3584           56  256    256 |  28.9774            39.4359
```

Two things I would flag rather than hide. The heuristic was fitted from sweeps of
`m_grid ∈ {1..64}` x `g_block ∈ {8, 16, 32}` over hidden sizes 1152/3584/7168, expert counts 8 to
512 and row counts 1 to 256, on all three parts; the shipped choice lands within ~0-5% of the
per-cell optimum in the low-latency decode range, with a few ~8-12% outliers on sub-4 µs shapes at
very high expert counts. And the *best* tile/warp pair is architecture-dependent at high expert
counts — the parts disagree there — so the values here are the ones that win on all of them, and
closing the remaining few percent would need autotuning rather than constants.

Not covered: a multi-node end-to-end decode run. This is a kernel-level change with bitwise-equal
output, so the risk is confined to performance, but the e2e number is still outstanding. H20 was
not measured — it is not present in either of our GPU fleets.

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [PD] Pack DCP1→DCP-N PD KV transfers into dest-contiguous RDMA blocks
author: kpham-sgl
body:
Cyclic DCP ownership made the relayout path emit one RDMA per token. Gather owned MLA rows on prefill first so Mooncake/NIXL can send page-sized or larger blocks. DSPARK is left to a follow-up.

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

DCP assigns KV ownership round-robin **per token** (`owned_offsets = arange(rank, num_kv_tokens, dcp_size)`), so on a DCP1 -> DCP-N PD transfer the source indices are strided and `group_concurrent_contiguous` cannot merge them: the relayout emits **one RDMA descriptor per token per layer** (`tokens x layers` per chunk). The transfer becomes descriptor-bound rather than bandwidth-bound.

## Modifications

- **Pack cyclic DCP rows:** Added a raw-pointer Triton gather and common packing path that turns strided MLA source rows into contiguous blocks, reducing transfer descriptors from one per owned token per layer to destination-contiguous runs.
- **Reuse a dedicated gather stream:** Each worker pack buffer lazily creates and reuses its CUDA gather stream. The stream waits for default-stream KV writes, and packing completes before the transport reads the buffer.
- **Keep pack memory bounded and reusable:** Allocate and register one buffer per transfer worker, size it from the maximum prefill chunk, and assign each DCP rank a fixed region. TP peers sharing a DCP rank reuse the same packed source.
- **Integrate both transports:** Mooncake sends the packed blocks directly. NIXL submits immutable rank regions asynchronously and relies on the existing chunk barrier before repacking the buffer.

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/disaggregation/test_kimi_linear_pd_dcp4.py` on 8xB300: **6 passed**, GSM8K **0.91** (threshold 0.88). Covers token + output-logprob parity against a monolithic TP4 reference at 9 chunk/virtual-page boundary lengths, and a 32k needle-in-a-haystack at depths 0.1/0.5/0.9.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Setup.** 8xB300, `Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct`. `main` @ `20621aa14b` vs this PR @ `539b78567f`, on both transfer backends.

- **Topology:** prefill TP4/EP4 `dcp=1` (GPU 0-3) -> decode TP4 `dcp=4` (GPU 4-7). `tokenspeed_mla`, `fp8_e4m3` KV, `--page-size 64`, `--chunked-prefill-size 8192`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.80`.
- **Workload:** OSL 32, 2 warmup requests + cache flush per point, freshly launched servers per condition. TTFT/throughput client-measured by `sglang.benchmark.serving --pd-separated`.
- **Controls:** bytes moved identical per point (26.1 / 136.2 / 513.8 MB at ISL 4k / 32k / 128k); packed path verified active on the PR (`4 x 31.5 MB` pack buffers per prefill TP rank) and absent on `main`.

### NIXL

| ISL | conc | TTFT p50 main -> PR | out tok/s main -> PR |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| 4096 | 1 | 115.8 -> 83.0 ms (**-28.3%**) | 158.6 -> 187.4 (**+18.2%**) |
| 4096 | 8 | 3470.2 -> 3076.3 ms (-11.3%) | 69.2 -> 77.8 (+12.4%) |
| 32768 | 1 | 511.0 -> 311.7 ms (**-39.0%**) | 53.5 -> 79.5 (**+48.8%**) |
| 32768 | 8 | 3749.3 -> 2298.4 ms (**-38.7%**) | 64.4 -> 102.6 (**+59.2%**) |
| 131072 | 1 | 2198.7 -> 1426.3 ms (**-35.1%**) | 14.0 -> 21.0 (**+50.1%**) |
| 131072 | 8 | 16300.5 -> 10280.2 ms (**-36.9%**) | 15.0 -> 24.2 (**+60.7%**) |

### Mooncake

| ISL | conc | TTFT p50 main -> PR | out tok/s main -> PR |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| 4096 | 1 | 93.2 -> 85.5 ms (-8.4%) | 172.6 -> 180.4 (+4.5%) |
| 4096 | 8 | 3207.1 -> 3166.5 ms (-1.3%) | 74.7 -> 77.2 (+3.4%) |
| 32768 | 1 | 360.8 -> 310.6 ms (**-13.9%**) | 71.5 -> 79.2 (+10.7%) |
| 32768 | 8 | 2556.4 -> 2230.2 ms (**-12.8%**) | 93.0 -> 104.7 (+12.6%) |
| 131072 | 1 | 1575.6 -> 1429.9 ms (-9.2%) | 19.2 -> 21.2 (+10.5%) |
| 131072 | 8 | 11467.3 -> 10207.1 ms (-11.0%) | 21.7 -> 24.3 (+12.1%) |

**Summary.** Backend-dependent: NIXL **-28% to -39% TTFT** and up to **1.6x** output throughput at ISL >= 32k; mooncake **-9% to -14%** and ~1.1x. Mooncake's baseline is already faster at every point, and packing converges the two to within ~3% -- per-token descriptors penalise NIXL far more, and this PR removes that penalty. ISL 4096 / conc 8 barely moves on either backend (~3.1-3.5 s in all conditions), so something other than descriptor count dominates there. Cost: 4 x 31.5 MB pack buffers per prefill TP rank, leaving the KV pool essentially unchanged.

title: [AMD] Optimize Kimi-K3 Triton MLA prefill on gfx950
author: clintg6
body:
## Motivation

Kimi-K3 uses two attention representations during prefill at TP8 on MI355X:

- Fresh/zero-prefix MHA: 12 heads with QK/V dimensions 192/128.
- Cached-prefix absorbed MLA: 12 query heads, one KV head, and QK/V
  dimensions 576/512.

Current Triton prefill leaves performance on the table for both shapes:

1. The exact K3 kernels use one pipeline stage and natural-exponential
   online softmax.
2. Absorbed 576/512 prefill processes one full 512-wide value accumulator,
   increasing register pressure.
3. FP8 cached-prefix P·V can underflow small softmax probabilities.
4. Aiter supports native FP8 zero-prefix prefill, but Triton lacks an
   equivalent opt-in path.

## Changes

### K3 prefill tuning

- Use two pipeline stages for exact gfx950 K3 192/128 and N32 576/512
  prefill kernels.
- Fold `log2(e)` into the attention scale and use `exp2` for unmodified K3
  logits.
- Convert stored LSE back to natural-log units.
- Preserve current compact ragged-grid scheduling and the generic
  Triton-3.7 fallback.

### 4×128 absorbed MLA kernel

Add a dedicated split-dimension kernel for cached-prefix K3 MLA:

```text
Q/K latent: 4 × 128
Q/K tail:       64
V/output:   4 × 128
```

The kernel maintains one online-softmax state and four independent FP32
value accumulators before concatenating the normalized 128-wide outputs.

Dispatch is restricted to:

- gfx950;
- 12 query heads and one KV head;
- QK/V dimensions 576/512;
- BF16 current Q/K/V and output;
- BF16 cached prefix with unit scales, or opt-in FP8 cached prefix with
  supported descales;
- causal attention;
- page size 1;
- contiguous last dimensions;
- no custom mask, sliding window, logit cap, XAI temperature, sink, LSE,
  score modifier, auxiliary tensor, or skipped stage.

Unsupported calls immediately use the existing generic kernel.

### FP8 prefill

Add:

```bash
SGLANG_TRITON_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=1
```

This is enabled by default. Set `SGLANG_TRITON_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=0` to disable
native FP8 prefill.

On exact K3 gfx950 shapes:

- Zero-prefix 192/128 Q/K/V are cast from BF16 to FP8 before launch,
  matching Aiter behavior.
- Absorbed 576/512 prefill keeps current-chunk Q/K/V in BF16 while using
  the FP8 cached prefix.
- Softmax probabilities are multiplied by `FP8_MAX` before FP8 P·V and
  the accumulator contribution is divided by the same factor.
- Non-unit cached-prefix K/V descales are supported.

The default-on path achieved 98% GSM8K accuracy in model-level validation.

## Performance

MI355X measurements used a device warmup and HIP-graph replay.

Against unmodified current main:

| K3 prefill case | Current main | This change | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Zero-prefix BF16, 8K | 0.726 ms | 0.415 ms | 1.75× |
| Zero-prefix FP8, 8K, casts included | 0.726 ms | 0.420 ms | 1.73× |

| Length | BF16 | FP8, casts included | Result |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| 16K | 1.500 ms | 1.400 ms | FP8 1.07× faster |
| 32K | 6.255 ms | 5.145 ms | FP8 1.22× faster |

every length despite the small 8K crossover loss.

ratios at concurrency 2, 4, 8, and 16.

effectively unchanged in both comparisons.

- BF16 absorbed split versus current-main generic output:
  relative L2 approximately `9.5e-5`.
- FP8 absorbed split versus the corrected generic FP8 path:

title: [Fix] compressed-tensors: Honor .linear-wrapped ignore entries on fused shards
author: Smallfu666
body:
Fixes #28018.

The reported llm-compressor checkpoint spells its vision-tower `ignore` entries against the `CompressedLinear` wrapper (`...q_proj.linear`). For fused `qkv_proj` / `gate_up_proj`, SGLang expands the layer into shard names without that suffix, so `should_ignore_layer` misses those wrapped entries and quantizes the corresponding fused projections. That is 135 of its 189 wrapped entries; the other 54 name `o_proj` / `down_proj`, which `ClippableRowParallelLinear` already nests at `.linear`, so those already match.

The change is therefore on the fused path only: retry the wrapper spelling once per expanded shard, after the existing comparator misses. Four lines, no new matching primitive; #32736's no-prefix invariant is untouched.

Verified on one H200 with `google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-w4a16-ct`:

- **before** — the load reaches `compressed_tensors_wNa16` → `gptq_marlin_repack` and aborts with `size_n = 8608 is not divisible by tile_n_size = 64`, the message in #28018;
- **after** — the model loads, all 108 vision-tower projections come up `UnquantizedLinearMethod`/bf16, and `language_model.layers.0` stays `CompressedTensorsLinearMethod`;
- **minimal** — a third arm that also retried on the unfused path produced a byte-identical result.

Two behavior changes, your call:

- naming **only some** fused shards in the wrapped spelling previously loaded silently quantized, and now raises the existing inconsistent-scheme `ValueError` (whose message does not mention `.linear`);
- **mixing** plain and wrapped spellings previously raised, and now resolves to ignored.

`should_ignore_layer` is shared with `w8a8_int8.py`, where a 10-case probe moves only the three cases whose ignore list holds a `.linear` entry, and with diffusion `modelslim.py`, which passes a nested mapping and so never takes the fused path.

Tests are CPU-only and matcher-level: 10 cases, 5 red on main; the largest drives the checkpoint's 189-entry list at the tower's real runtime names. One checkpoint on one GPU, and no accuracy or throughput measurement.

#24929 identified this mechanism first; its hunk sits in `check_contains`, which the ignore path no longer reaches since #32736.

title: fix: use a bf16-relative tolerance in the DSA indexer K kernel test
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsv32_indexer_fusion.py::test_k_norm_rope_matches_reference` is flaky in `base-b` / `1-gpu-large` at roughly a 1% rate. A recent instance:

```
AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
Mismatched elements: 1 / 4736 (0.0%)
Greatest absolute difference: 0.061458587646484375 at index (24, 34) (up to 0.06 allowed)
Greatest relative difference: 0.002833961509168148 at index (24, 34) (up to 0.0 allowed)
```

The kernel is correct; the test's tolerance model is not.

The test compares a **bf16** kernel output against an fp32 reference with a purely **absolute** tolerance:

```python
torch.testing.assert_close(out.float(), ref, atol=0.06, rtol=0.0)
```

bf16 keeps 8 significand bits, so its quantization step is relative: for outputs in `[16, 32)` one ulp is `0.125` and half an ulp is `0.0625`, which already exceeds `atol=0.06`. The single fp32 → bf16 rounding at the end of `fused_k_indexer_norm_rope` can therefore break the assertion on its own, with no numerical error in the kernel at all.

The test reaches those magnitudes routinely: `cos`/`sin` here are `randn` (not real cosines bounded by 1) and the LayerNorm `gamma`/`beta` are `randn` as well, so outputs reach `|v| ~ 30`.

Two further points made this show up as a random CI failure rather than a deterministic one:

- `_make_inputs()` uses a seeded generator, but `key` / `weight` / `bias` were drawn from the global RNG, so every CI run used different inputs.
- The same `atol=0.06` is used for the second bf16 comparison in `test_indexer_uses_replaced_rope_cache_for_fused_kernels`, which passes today only because its inputs happen to be seeded.

The tolerance has been this way since the test was introduced in #27705; this is not a recent regression.

## Modifications

- Replace the absolute tolerance at both bf16-vs-fp32 comparison sites with a bf16-aware one: `rtol = 2**-7` (2x margin over the `2**-8` pure-rounding bound) plus `atol = 1e-3` for values driven near zero by cancellation.
- Seed `key` / `weight` / `bias` in `test_k_norm_rope_matches_reference` with the same generator convention the rest of the module already uses, so a failure is reproducible.

No kernel or runtime code is touched.

## Accuracy Tests

Measured on an H200, replaying the exact test body.

**Reproduction of the flake with the current tolerance** (400 draws, unseeded inputs, as CI runs it today):

```
failures at atol=0.06, rtol=0   : 4 (1.0%)
worst max_abs_err               : 0.062300 at ref=-22.3127
  bf16 half-ulp at that ref     : 0.062500
worst relative error            : 9.615e-03
max |ref| seen                  : 30.426
trials whose err exceeds the bf16 half-ulp bound: 0
```

The last line is the point: across 400 draws, **no** element ever deviated from the fp32 reference by more than half a bf16 ulp, so the whole discrepancy is representation, not kernel error.

**The new tolerance** (2000 draws, unseeded inputs):

```
trials 2000: failures at (atol=1e-3, rtol=2^-7) = 0
worst err/allowed ratio = 0.490  (>=1.0 would fail)
pinned-seed(1) err/allowed ratio = 0.459
```

The check never came closer than 2x to failing, and the seed the test now pins sits at the same margin.

**The test file itself**, run 10 consecutive times on an H200:

```
7 passed  x 10
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — test-only change.

title: [Spec] Fix CDF boundary handling in `TreeSpeculativeSamplingTargetOnly`
author: nanjiangwill
body:
## Motivation

`TreeSpeculativeSamplingTargetOnly` draws coins from `[0, 1)` but selects a target CDF bucket with `coin <= cumulative_probability`. At the lower endpoint (`coin == 0`) that accepts a draft token whose target probability is zero, and exact interior CDF boundaries land in the preceding bucket instead of the next positive-mass one.

Fixes #35771.

## Modifications

- Use the half-open condition `coin < prob_acc / threshold_acc` and require `target_prob_single > 0` before either acceptance path can take a draft, in the shared device header `sgl_kernel/speculative/sampling.cuh`.
- Add regression cases for zero-mass drafts (permissive and default thresholds), an exact interior CDF boundary, and both coin endpoints; update the zero-threshold expectation, which previously encoded the zero-mass acceptance.

Single-site change: the shared header backs the CUDA/ROCm JIT launchers and the MUSA AOT build, so all three pick the fix up. Rebased onto #40033, which moved these kernels to JIT — CUDA compiles them at runtime, so the fix ships without an `sgl-kernel` release.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_speculative_sampling.py`: `7 passed`.
- Reverting only the kernel predicate turns that into `4 failed, 3 passed` — `zero-mass-zero-threshold`, `zero-mass-default-threshold`, `interior-boundary`, and the zero-threshold tree case all regress, confirming the new coverage is what guards the fix.

title: [AMD] Skip full-vocab softmax in EAGLE topk==1 draft on ROCm
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

EAGLE `topk=1` only needs the largest-logit token. For finite logits, a full-vocabulary softmax cannot change the argmax and is redundant. AITER `greedy_sample` has an unmasked vector-tail correctness issue; on MI355X it returned an out-of-vocabulary index for vocabulary size 151,666. SGLang’s existing Triton split-argmax masks offsets `>= vocab_size` and safely handles NaNs.

## Changes

- Use the existing masked Triton split-argmax for ROCm EAGLE `topk=1` in both draft-decode and draft-extend.
- Make position advancement optional so the implementation can be reused in draft-extend.
- Add AMD coverage for aligned and misaligned vocabularies, NaN, `-inf`, and all-negative logits.
- Keep rejection sampling, `topk > 1`, and all non-ROCm paths unchanged.
- Apply the optimization generically to supported ROCm EAGLE, EAGLE3, and MTP models without model-name gating.

## Correctness

title: [diffusion] optimization: transfer mapped layers through a courier thread
author: mickqian
body:
A copy whose source is a checkpoint mapping is synchronous however it is requested — the driver stages unpinned memory through its own buffer — and the prefetch hooks run on the compute thread, so every mapped layer stalled the denoise step for its whole transfer. This adds a courier: a worker thread that stages a mapped layer's bytes into one of two pinned slots (a plain memcpy when the page cache holds them) and issues the device copy on its own stream, where it is genuinely asynchronous. Parameters are still rebound on the compute thread at collect time, so module state is never touched concurrently; blocking callers and any courier failure keep the direct synchronous path.

Measured on MiniMax-H3 fl2va, one RTX 4090, 12 GiB allocator cap, 32 GiB host envelope, 864×480 / 124 frames / 20 NFE, interleaved same-window A/B: baseline 538.8 s of denoise (median 25.0 s/step) against 369.1 s (median 18.0) with the courier — 31% faster, and the effect grows with host memory-bandwidth contention, because that contention is exactly what the compute thread stops paying for. Output equivalence was checked at the video level: SSIM against a baseline run equals the baseline's own run-to-run SSIM (0.9941 = 0.9941), and the audio stream is bit-identical.

Stacked with per-layer pinning (#35867) and the VAE staying on its mapping (#35862), the same budget runs the lossless bf16 denoise at a **median of 11.0–12.0 s/step across two interleaved rounds — ahead of ComfyUI's 13.0** measured under the same 32 GiB psutil convention on the same GPU in the same bandwidth window.

Tests cover the ship/collect handshake, release_all draining an in-flight layer, and the fallback when the courier dies mid-flight; the first two fail with the courier disabled.

Merge note: this PR and #35867 touch the same file; whichever lands second rebases (the resolution is mechanical — both sides add independent methods).

title: config: borrowed-record reads follow the config bags
author: ch-wan
body:
## Stack

Part of a series that moves `ServerArgs` from "mutate the record at construction" to "resolve once, publish into config bags". Each PR stands alone (builds, passes its own tests); review bottom-up.

| # | PR | base |
|---|----|------|
| 0 | #35904 | `main` |
| 1 | #35905 | #35904 |
| 2 | #35906 | #35905 |
| 3 | #35907 | #35906 |
| 4 | #35908 | #35907 |
| 5 | #35909 | #35908 |
| 6 | #35910 | #35909 |

Whole-series CI vehicle (not for merge): #35917


## Motivation

Components reached the startup record through whatever object happened to hold it — `model_runner.server_args.field`, `self.scheduler.server_args.field`. A reference lifted off another object carries no contract, and no read census counted that spelling: it had grown to 105 reads across 36 files unnoticed. Once the record stays at the user's raw input, these reads answer with the CLI default.

## Modifications

- Every borrowed-record chain read of a resolution-written field moves to the config bags (weight loading, graph capture, pool configurator, forward-batch construction, KV pool runtime, disaggregation and elastic-EP paths, HTTP/gRPC surfaces, attention backends).
- Reads that follow the *configured* topology rather than live process groups use the `configured_*()` accessors (a draft runner shares the target's process groups, so the live property would answer for the wrong runner).
- Reads of raw input (host, ports, paths the caller chose) stay on the record — that is what the record is for.
- The chain-read ratchet pins the converted set at zero: the written-field set is derived from four channels (handler keywords, the live override registries, post-process pass returns, late resolution), so a field that stops being resolution-written drops out of scope instead of pinning a stale name.

## Verification

- Chain-read ratchet: zero borrowed chain reads of resolution-written fields at this commit (105/36 on base, same scanner).
- Guard suite and lint green at this boundary; every touched test file re-run per-file in isolation.
- A/B: resolved end-state identical to base across the 11-configuration matrix.

title: config: pin two orderings resolution relies on
author: ch-wan
body:
## Stack

Part of a series that moves `ServerArgs` from "mutate the record at construction" to "resolve once, publish into config bags". Each PR stands alone (builds, passes its own tests); review bottom-up.

| # | PR | base |
|---|----|------|
| 0 | #35904 | `main` |
| 1 | #35905 | #35904 |
| 2 | #35906 | #35905 |
| 3 | #35907 | #35906 |
| 4 | #35908 | #35907 |
| 5 | #35909 | #35908 |
| 6 | #35910 | #35909 |

Whole-series CI vehicle (not for merge): #35917


## Motivation

Two orderings inside resolution hold today by accident, and nothing would notice them breaking. Tests only — no production change.

## Modifications

- `ModelConfig` is built from resolved input: the pin derives both sides from source — the fields `ModelConfig.from_server_args` reads, and the pipeline step each is declared at — and fails if a field it reads is declared after the first build. Two documented exceptions are named and asserted with equality, not membership:
  - `is_embedding` is read for what the caller asked for (passed through, never stored) — resolution later overwrites the field with a different quantity sharing the name;
  - four fields the model-override registries decide *after* the handler builds and caches the configuration (`dtype`, `quantization`, `enable_multi_layer_eagle`, `disable_hybrid_swa_memory`). The build/collect positions are read from the one handler body that contains both, and the registry-declared set is imported from the chain ratchet's derivation rather than re-derived — a copy that drifts narrower would make the check quietly vacuous. A fifth field arriving in that position fails; so does fixing the ordering — either way someone has to look.
- The chain-read ratchet unions all four declaration channels (handler keywords, live registries, pass returns, late resolution) with per-channel floors, so a channel whose derivation collapses fails loudly instead of narrowing the check.

## Verification

- Both pins verified by injection: reversing the build/collect comparison reports exactly the four named fields; a shape reaching a stale field reddens the main assertion.
- Guard suite and lint green at this boundary.

title: [diffusion] Load serialized BnB4 components with Transformers
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Diffusion component paths can address Hub subfolders, but standard serialized BitsAndBytes 4-bit checkpoints had no shared admission boundary for model components that Transformers can already materialize. The initial implementation placed this behavior in the text encoder loader, which also made image encoder fallback inherit text-specific precision handling.

## Modifications

- Validate standard top-level serialized BitsAndBytes 4-bit metadata in the shared component loader.
- Let any model component using the native Transformers fallback reuse the same loading, residency, precision, and rejection contract, independent of architecture.
- Keep plain checkpoints and model-managed quantization on their existing native SGLang paths.
- Preserve T5/UMT5/MT5 encoder-only class resolution through a narrow text-encoder hook.
- Fix image encoder native fallback to use `image_encoder_precision` rather than a text encoder precision.
- Reject BnB8, nested/compression metadata, and native-only component fallbacks instead of silently changing the checkpoint contract.
- Document `diffusers/FLUX.1-dev-bnb-4bit/text_encoder_2` as one validated component layout and clarify that Diffusers DiT components use their separate quantization backends.

Production code: 91 additions / 68 deletions across two existing loader files.

New production files: none.

Tests: 169 additions / 16 deletions.

Docs: 21 additions.

## Accuracy Tests

Focused coverage crosses the shared Transformers fallback with both text and image encoder component semantics, including encoder-only class resolution, component precision, BnB4-only validation, metadata-source rejection, native-only fallback, model-managed quantization, and residency.

title: [diffusion] Admit compatible quantized native encoders
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Quantized native encoders were admitted through a model-class allowlist even though compatibility is determined by the loader and the linear modules constructed from checkpoint metadata. That required a new model-specific declaration for every otherwise-compatible checkpoint and did not provide day-0 behavior.

## Modifications

- remove the per-model checkpoint-quantization capability type and model declarations
- pass detected checkpoint metadata to any registered native text or image encoder
- fail closed before reading weights unless the constructed implementation contains compatible quantized linear layers
- preserve Transformers-managed BnB4 and model-managed quantization lifecycles
- replace duplicated model-specific quantization sections with one generic CLI/materialization contract

This generalizes the native encoder loader; it does not claim that unrelated component materializers support every format.

Existing production files: +22 / -43 lines.
New production files: none.
Tests + docs: +44 / -62 lines.

## Accuracy Tests

Focused coverage checks generic native admission, structural rejection for incompatible implementations, post-load processing, and one real packed Q/K/V scale-loading contract.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: this changes checkpoint admission and removes static allowlisting; inference kernels are unchanged.

title: Add Spark3 Model
author: KnightYao
body:
## Summary

This PR adds native support for the Spark 3 model architecture in SGLang.

The implementation introduces the Spark 3 configuration and causal language model, including sliding-window and full attention, head-wise attention output gating, tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, and checkpoint weight loading.

## Changes

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `python/sglang/srt/configs/spark3.py` | Adds `Spark3Config`, including model dimensions, attention layout, sliding-window configuration, layer types, RoPE parameters, and tied word embeddings. |
| `python/sglang/srt/models/spark3.py` | Implements `Spark3ForCausalLM`, including grouped-query attention, interleaved sliding/full attention, head-wise output gating, gated MLP, parallelism support, split prefill, and checkpoint weight loading. |
| `python/sglang/srt/configs/__init__.py` | Exports `Spark3Config` through the SGLang configuration package. |
| `python/sglang/srt/utils/hf_transformers/common.py` | Registers `Spark3Config` in SGLang's Hugging Face configuration registry. |
| `python/sglang/srt/function_call/spark3_detector.py` | Adds `Spark3Detector` for parsing Spark3 `<tool_call>`, `<arg_key>`, and `<arg_value>` blocks, validating tool names, converting argument types, and handling complete or truncated streaming blocks. |
| `python/sglang/srt/function_call/function_call_parser.py` | Registers `Spark3Detector` under the `spark` tool-call parser name. |
| `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_spark3_detector.py` | Adds coverage for registration, multiple non-streaming calls, JSON Schema type conversion, unknown-tool handling, character-by-character streaming, partial markers, and stream termination. |

## Key Technical Details

1. Efficient Architecture：The models adopt an efficiency-oriented architecture with Sliding Window Attention (SWA) and other structural optimizations, improving the balance between model quality, memory usage, and inference efficiency.
2. Native 1M Context：Both the 1.7B and 4B models natively support up to 1 million tokens of context, enabling long-document understanding, repository-level coding, and long-horizon agent tasks.
3. Strong Coding & Agent Capabilities：The models deliver leading coding and agent performance among models of comparable size, with strong capabilities in code generation, tool use, multi-step execution, and long-context reasoning.
4. Faster Inference：Through model architecture and inference-stack optimizations, the models achieve higher inference efficiency and throughput than many comparable-size models, especially in long-context scenarios.
5. Strong K–12 and Gaokao Performance：The models achieve leading K–12 question-answering performance at comparable parameter scales, with particularly strong results on challenging Chinese Gaokao-style tasks.
6. Advanced Post-Training：The release applies a comprehensive post-training recipe based on Scaled Reinforcement Learning and MOPD, improving reasoning, coding, instruction following, agentic capabilities, and alignment.
7. Controllable Thinking Budget：The models support configurable reasoning levels — none, low, medium, and high — allowing applications to dynamically trade off reasoning quality, latency, and inference cost.
8. 200+ Languages：Multilingual coverage has been expanded to more than 200 languages, supporting broad cross-lingual understanding, generation, translation, and localized applications.



## Performance

title: [diffusion] Accelerate LingBot Video RMSNorm in quality=high
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- replace LingBot Video's handwritten FP32 RMSNorm chain with existing diffusion Triton RMSNorm kernels under `quality=high`
- use the row kernel for wide FP32-weight sites and the tiled one-pass kernel for BF16-weight or narrow sites, with guarded fallback to the reference implementation
- leave `quality=lossless` unchanged, add CUDA coverage for both checkpoint weight dtypes, and document the mounted fast path

## H200 results

Native SGLang, BF16, 1x H200, 384x640, 17 frames, 12 steps, seed 0, text encoder CPU offload, `quality=high`. Runs used one isolated model cache and an ABBA order on the same otherwise-idle GPU:

| Run | Denoise | Saved-request e2e | Peak reserved |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main 1 | 3.9293 s | 4.5685 s | 69.131 GiB |
| this PR 1 | 2.9145 s | 3.5533 s | 69.131 GiB |
| this PR 2 | 2.9299 s | 3.5689 s | 69.131 GiB |
| main 2 | 3.9311 s | 4.5684 s | 69.131 GiB |

Using the two-run means, denoise improves by **25.65%** and saved-request e2e by **22.05%**, with no increase in peak reserved memory. GPU process snapshots were empty before the group and after every cell.

The main full-stage trace contains 7,226 handwritten `pow` / `mean` / `rsqrt` RMSNorm chains. The candidate trace contains 6,936 fused RMSNorm launches and only 290 remaining reference chains.

## Cookbook video comparison

Prompt from `docs/cookbook/diffusion/LingBot-Video/LingBot-Video-MoE.mdx`: a small silver robot arm reaches toward a red cube on a white table.

![LingBot Video quality=high main versus PR, frames 0/8/16](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/lingbot-rmsnorm/contact-sheet.jpg)

[Side-by-side video](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/lingbot-rmsnorm/side-by-side.mp4) · [main video](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/lingbot-rmsnorm/main.mp4) · [PR video](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/lingbot-rmsnorm/pr.mp4)

After the ABBA group, its isolated cache removed 129,952,880,506 bytes and 29 weight files to zero. The separate profile group removed 129,952,926,770 bytes and 29 weight files to zero.

title: [diffusion] Flatten Wan VAE RMSNorm row addressing
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- address dense channels-last-3d Wan VAE activations as flat `[pixel, channel]` rows
- remove the per-program `b/t/h/w` div/mod chain and general stride reconstruction
- keep the normalization, dtype boundaries, SiLU path, launch geometry, and output layout unchanged
- add the dense-row guard, unit coverage, a registered benchmark, and kernel documentation

## Why

Nsight Compute on the representative FastWan2.1 shape (`[1, 96, 4, 480, 832]`, BF16 input / FP32 affine) shows 80.58% SM throughput but only 9.14% DRAM throughput and 93.93% achieved occupancy. Source counters attribute 120,771 / 196,793 samples to integer/index instructions. The hottest PCs are the reciprocal-based lowering of the row-to-`b/t/h/w` div/mod chain (`I2F.RP`, `IABS`, and `MUFU.RCP`).

Dense channels-last-3d already stores every pixel as a contiguous channel row, so those coordinates are unnecessary. `stride(C) == 1` is checked explicitly because size-one channel tensors can satisfy the memory-format predicate with channel-first strides.

## Performance

Single NVIDIA H200, cold-L2 registered benchmark:

| Shape | main | PR | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FastWan2.1 BF16 `[1,96,4,480,832]` | 1550.848 us | 972.576 us | 37.29% |
| FastWan2.2 FP32 `[1,256,4,384,576]` | 921.184 us | 553.760 us | 39.89% |

FastWan2.1 end-to-end ABBA, one H200, eager, 832x480x61, 3 steps, no compile, resident DiT:

| Mode | main mean denoise / e2e | PR mean denoise / e2e | e2e change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| lossless | 0.8554 / 2.2129 s | 0.8553 / 2.2151 s | -0.10% (control; kernel is not mounted) |
| quality=high | 0.8513 / 1.9575 s | 0.8533 / 1.8823 s | **+3.84%** |

The quality-high full-stage trace reduces all 415 Wan RMSNorm+SiLU launches from 215.234 ms to 127.128 ms (40.94%). The largest C96 shape falls from 171.438 ms to 101.697 ms over 105 launches. Peak reserved memory stays at 31.402 GiB.

TurboWan2.1 T2V 1.3B provides a second model-level check at 832x480x81, 4 steps, quality=high, and no compile. Its main trace spends 286.083 ms across 545 Wan RMSNorm+SiLU launches (11.84% of GPU time). A clean main/PR/PR/main ABBA measured:

| Model | main mean denoise / e2e | PR mean denoise / e2e | e2e change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TurboWan2.1 T2V 1.3B | 1.0106 / 2.4235 s | 1.0163 / 2.3325 s | **+3.76%** |

Denoise is 0.57% slower, confirming that the request gain comes from the VAE path rather than timing drift in the DiT. Peak reserved memory remains 30.729 GiB.

The 14B TurboWan checkpoints provide resolution scaling checks with the same 545 launches:

| Model | main mean denoise / e2e | PR mean denoise / e2e | kernel time | e2e change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 14B 480P | 6.6050 / 8.3559 s | 6.6067 / 8.2559 s | 289.647 -> 169.135 ms (-41.61%) | +1.20% |
| 14B 720P | 17.6763 / 21.2482 s | 17.7044 / 21.0438 s | 669.365 -> 389.957 ms (-41.74%) | +0.96% |

Both ABBA brackets are byte-exact across main and PR. These longer DiT-heavy requests dilute the VAE gain, but independently confirm the kernel reduction at both production resolutions.

TurboWan2.2 I2V A14B adds a four-H200 CFG/Ulysses check at 1280x720x81. Main averaged 7.6857 / 12.1847 s and the PR averaged 7.6780 / 12.2241 s. Rank-0 recorded GPU time fell from 12,020.198 to 11,866.292 ms (-1.28%), but synchronized e2e regressed 0.32%, so this checkpoint is validation evidence rather than a claimed request speedup. All five outputs are byte-exact.

## Output comparison

Prompt: `A curious raccoon walks through a sunlit forest.` Seed: `42`.

![main and PR contact sheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/wan-rmsnorm-flat-rows/contact-sheet.jpg)

[main video](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/pr-media/diffusion-prs/wan-rmsnorm-flat-rows/main.mp4) · [PR video](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/pr-media/diffusion-prs/wan-rmsnorm-flat-rows/pr.mp4) · [side-by-side video](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/pr-media/diffusion-prs/wan-rmsnorm-flat-rows/side-by-side.mp4)

title: [diffusion] Fix Hunyuan3D stale extension lock hangs
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

`hunyuan3d_shape_gen` can hang indefinitely during server warmup on a reused CI runner. The failing runner repeated the same timeout seven times, while the same commit completed warmup in about 24 seconds on other H100 runners.

PyTorch's cpp-extension `FileBaton.wait()` only polls whether its `lock` file exists. If a process is killed during compilation of Hunyuan3D's rasterizer or mesh processor, the lock remains and every subsequent server on that runner waits forever.

A separate runner-dependent failure was also observed when a preinstalled `tokenizers==0.23.0rc0` was retained: `CLIPTokenizer` failed while constructing `RobertaProcessing`. Passing runners use `tokenizers==0.22.2`.

## Modifications

- Serialize Hunyuan3D cpp-extension loads with a process-lifetime `flock`.
- Remove PyTorch's stale inner lock only after acquiring the outer advisory lock.
- Preserve the existing broken-extension cache recovery under the same lock.
- Pin `tokenizers==0.22.2` until the incompatible prerelease is no longer accepted by the pinned Transformers version.
- Add unit coverage for stale-lock cleanup and broken-extension rebuilds.

The Hunyuan3D test remains fully enabled, including server warmup and the complete shape + paint pipeline. No performance or consistency threshold is relaxed.

## Validation

H100 remote validation:

- Extension loader unit tests: `2 passed`
- Seeded stale locks for both `custom_rasterizer_kernel` and `mesh_processor_kernel`: both were removed and rebuilt successfully
- Full cold-cache Hunyuan3D shape + paint pipeline completed; the deliberately induced compile time was correctly visible in the stage metric
- Normal-cache `hunyuan3d_shape_gen` e2e: passed
  - server warmup: 23.41 s
  - e2e: 238.07 s
  - runtime peak VRAM: 6102 MiB
- Pre-commit checks: passed

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit
- [x] Add unit tests
- [x] Run a real H100 end-to-end test
- [x] Preserve existing model output and test thresholds

title: [NPU] Revert fused Triton MRoPE for Qwen3.x and fall back to native multimodal RoPE
author: gjsheu
body:
## Description

Revert the fused Triton MRoPE integration for Qwen3.x on NPU (#35817) and fall back to the native multimodal RoPE implementation for consistent text and multimodal position handling.

## Changes

1. **Revert "[NPU] Use fused Triton MRoPE for Qwen3.x (#35817)"** (reverts 47129c650)
   - `qwen3_5.py`: switch back from `triton_split_qkv_rmsnorm_mrope` to `split_qkvgate_gemma_rmsnorm_rope`
   - Restore the native forward path logic, including the `full_attention_interval`-based cos/sin computation
   - Force the native path in extend / draft_extend / mixed forward modes

2. **fix(npu): fall back to native multimodal RoPE**
