title: [diffusion] Load serialized Comfy ConvRot INT8 DiTs
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- load serialized Comfy ConvRot INT8 DiT weights and F32 row scales directly
  into the existing `comfy_kitchen.int8_linear` backend
- auto-detect per-layer `int8_tensorwise` metadata from an explicit
  `--transformer-weights-path`; no additional CLI flag or format registry is
  introduced
- validate marker, dtype, scale shape, ConvRot group size, FSDP, and TP
  compatibility before model execution
- preserve the existing online `--quantization kitchen_int8` path for BF16
  checkpoints
- fix MiniMax-H3 Comfy FP8 and INT8 QKV admission: Comfy files already store
  `[q_all, k_all, v_all]` and must not receive the official checkpoint's
  grouped-QKV reorder
- document the generic format contract and the verified H3 usage

## Scope

This is the next small slice after #35979. Generic component paths already
resolve local files and exact Hub file references; this PR adds one real
serialized materialization backend for compatible native DiTs. It does not
claim support for arbitrary Comfy INT4/mixed formats or quantized auxiliary
components.

The implementation reuses the existing Kitchen INT8 config, linear method,
component weight source, and transformer loader. No new files or parallel
loader hierarchy are introduced. Production runtime churn is below 200 lines.

MiniMax-H3 is the first admitted consumer:

```bash
sglang serve \
  --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \
  --model-variant fl2va \
  --transformer-weights-path \
    Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/diffusion_models/minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors \
  --num-gpus 4 \
  --tp-size 2 \
  --ulysses-degree 2 \
  --performance-mode speed
```

The checkpoint's 256-element ConvRot grouping admits H3 TP1/2/4. TP8 is
rejected because a row-parallel input shard would split a rotation group.
Sequence parallelism and component/layerwise offload remain compatible; FSDP
is rejected for marker-driven Comfy checkpoints.

## Validation

- changed-file pre-commit suite passes on the rebased head
- focused unit coverage checks marker validation, serialized INT8/F32 parameter
  construction, online-vs-serialized dispatch, device postprocess admission,
  and native QKV layout selection
- runtime tests were not run locally; PR CI provides the registered NVIDIA
  coverage

### Public checkpoint contract

Header-range inspection, without downloading the model manually, found:

- official Comfy-Org pruned FL2VA DiT: 200 `int8_tensorwise` markers
- every marked layer has an I8 2D weight, an F32 `[out_features, 1]` scale,
  `convrot=true`, and `convrot_groupsize=256`
- the Ref2VA file exposes the same validated tensor contract

The QKV layout was compared directly with the official MiniMax BF16 weight.
ConvRot preserves each output row's norm, so the serialized INT8 row and its
scale identify the source row unambiguously. Representative results:

| Comfy row | official native-layout source | norm error | error against unchanged row |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 128 | 384 | 0.00010 | 0.73967 |
| 7168 | 128 | 0.00168 | 10.54723 |
| 14336 | 256 | 0.00123 | 1.65143 |

This establishes that the Comfy tensor is already ordered as
`[q_all, k_all, v_all]`; applying H3's official grouped-QKV reorder again would
silently corrupt conditioning rather than necessarily crash.

### Prior GPU probe

An earlier 1× RTX 5090 exploratory run used normal `sglang serve`, the same
Comfy-Org pruned INT8 DiT representation, the fused Kitchen kernel, and the
native-QKV layout. A fixed-seed 8-step request produced the intended
bedroom/cat-band scene instead of the grey-wall output observed with the extra
QKV reorder. This is supporting E2E evidence for the path, not a claim that the
exact rebased PR head was rerun locally.

## Performance

No compute kernel changes. Relative to online Kitchen INT8, serialized loading
avoids temporarily materializing and requantizing the full BF16 DiT. Forward
continues to use the existing fused ConvRot + dynamic activation INT8 kernel.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add focused unit coverage.
- [x] Update quantization and model documentation.
- [x] Validate the public checkpoint format and QKV numerical contract.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance.

title: [Kernel] Skip reserved writes in MLA KV cache
author: tanth47
body:
## Motivation

Related to #36207.

SGLang reserves physical KV-cache slot 0 as a finite padding source for CUDA
graph and DP-attention padding. Generic KV stores protect that invariant after
#32477, but MLA-specific writers bypass `store_cache()` and still accept
`loc == 0` as a write destination.

Undefined graph/DP-padding rows can therefore overwrite slot 0 with NaNs. A
later padded attention row may read the poisoned slot and propagate NaNs into
attention output and model logits. During the GLM-5.2 investigation, affected
requests produced short nonsensical output followed by one repeated token.

## Root-cause boundary

This PR fixes the SGLang-owned MLA writers:

| Writer | Covered here |
| --- | ---: |
| BF16 Triton MLA writer | Yes |
| FP8 quantized MLA writer | Yes |
| MLA scale writer | Yes |
| CUDA TMA/JIT MLA writer | Yes |
| AITER fused GLM rope/cat/cache writer | No |

The fused ROCm path through `aiter.fused_qk_rope_cat_and_cache_mla` writes KV
internally and then invokes attention with `save_kv_cache=False`. It bypasses
the writers changed here and requires a separate API-safe integration fix.
This PR should therefore not be interpreted as resolving the complete GLM ROCm
path by itself.

## Modifications

- Add `reserved_skip_index=0` to the Triton MLA data, FP8-quantized, and
  scale-buffer writers.
- Apply the same runtime guard to the CUDA TMA bulk-store writer.
- Preserve static launch shapes and DCP ownership behavior; no Python-side
  compaction is introduced.
- Support `reserved_skip_index=-1` to opt out, matching `store_cache()`
  semantics.
- Add focused CUDA and AMD regression tests.

## Deterministic reproduction

Initialize slot 0 to a finite sentinel and invoke an MLA writer with
`loc=[0, 2]`. The source row mapped to slot 0 may be NaN because it represents
padding, while the row mapped to slot 2 is valid.

Without this patch:

- slot 0 is overwritten by the padding row;
- the valid positive slot is written normally.

With this patch:

- slot 0 remains byte-for-byte unchanged;
- the valid positive slot is still written;
- passing `reserved_skip_index=-1` restores the legacy behavior explicitly.

The tests exercise this contract directly instead of depending on
uninitialized allocator contents.

## Accuracy tests

- Added kernel tests for BF16 MLA writes with int32 and int64 locations.
- Added FP8-quantized and scale-buffer reserved-slot tests.
- Added CUDA TMA/JIT writer coverage.
- Added the explicit opt-out path.
- Python syntax compilation and `git diff --check` pass locally.
- Local GPU tests were not run for this PR; the focused tests are registered
  for CUDA and AMD CI.

The broader real-weight GLM investigation separately demonstrated the same
invariant violation in the fused AITER writer: `slot_mapping=[0]` with a NaN
padding row changed a finite slot 0 into 576 NaNs. That result motivates the
system-level issue but is outside this PR's implementation scope.

## Speed tests and profiling

Not run. The kernels add one scalar comparison to the existing store predicate
without changing launch grids or tensor shapes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code according to the project style.
- [x] Add focused CUDA and AMD tests.
- [x] Document the API behavior in the writer docstrings.
- [x] Preserve existing behavior through an explicit opt-out.
- [x] Clarify the fused AITER scope boundary.

title: [AMD][DSV4] perf: use full 1024-thread block for indexer top-k on ROCm
author: karverma-amd
body:
## Motivation

`deepseek_v4_topk_transform` launches **one block per row** and is latency-bound on its `O(c4_len)` histogram and emit passes, not throughput-bound. Measured kernel time is essentially flat from batch 8 to batch 256 at 128k context (~36.8 us), confirming the cost is per-block scan latency rather than occupancy.

On CDNA the wavefront is 64 lanes, so a 512-thread block is only 8 wavefronts and uses half the scan width a block can provide. Raising `kBlockSize` to 1024 on ROCm doubles per-block scan parallelism.

## Modification

`kBlockSize` becomes 1024 under `USE_ROCM`. The CUDA path keeps 512. One file, 9 lines added.

## Accuracy

GSM8K 5-shot, all 1319 test questions:

```bash
python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 2000 --parallel 1200
```

| arm | correct | accuracy |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | 1248/1319 | 94.62% |
| this PR  | 1246/1319 | 94.47% |


## Performance

DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MI355X (gfx950) TP8, 128k input / 256 output, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260821`.

```bash
# per arm, CONC in {16, 32, 48, 64}
SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton \
SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_COMPRESS_NORM_ROPE=1 \
SGLANG_OPT_NATIVE_BPRESHUFFLE_SCALE=1 \
AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 \
SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM=1 \
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --attention-backend dsv4 \
  --page-size 256 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --enforce-shared-experts-fusion \
  --context-length 133120 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.89 \
  --max-running-requests $CONC \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs $CONC
```

Client: `$CONC` concurrent `/generate` requests, 128000-token prompts, `max_new_tokens=256`, `temperature=0`, `ignore_eos=true`. Total token throughput is the server's steady-state `Decode batch ... gen throughput (token/s)` while `#running-req == $CONC`; TPOT is derived as `CONC / throughput`.

| conc | TPOT base (ms) | TPOT PR (ms) | TPOT | Total tput base (tok/s) | Total tput PR (tok/s) | Tput |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 15.52 | 15.07 | -2.9% | 1031.1 | 1061.6 | +3.0% |
| 32 | 17.98 | 17.45 | -2.9% | 1780.1 | 1833.7 | +3.0% |
| 48 | 19.84 | 19.46 | -1.9% | 2418.8 | 2466.8 | +2.0% |
| 64 | 22.49 | 22.13 | -1.6% | 2845.3 | 2891.5 | +1.6% |

The gain shrinks as concurrency rises because the top-k cost is batch-invariant while the rest of the decode step grows with batch, so a fixed saving becomes a smaller share of a larger step. Same-server repeats at conc 16 were tight (0.15% baseline, 0.71% this PR).

### Kernel level

Isolated, at the real decode shapes (`topk=1024`, `page_size=256`):

| context | c4_len | baseline | this PR | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128k | 32768 | 36.8 us | 23.0 us | 1.60x |
| 64k  | 16384 | -        | -       | 1.43x |
| 32k  | 8192  | -        | -       | 1.30x |
| 8k   | 2048  | -        | -       | 1.07x |

No regression at any context length.

A torch-profiler capture of a full decode step (batch 48, 128k) shows the kernel runs 30 times per step at 44.26 us, dropping to 29.90 us with this change: 431 us saved out of a 21.5 ms step, i.e. 2.0%, which matches the measured end-to-end 2.0% at conc 48.

## Unit test

`deepseek_v4_topk_transform_512` had no test, so this PR adds one to the existing
`python/sglang/kernels/aot/tests/test_topk.py`, reusing that file's `assert_equal`
helper (which forgives equal-score ties but nothing else):

```bash
pytest python/sglang/kernels/aot/tests/test_topk.py -k deepseek_v4_topk_transform
```

It asserts the selected index set matches `torch.topk` for `c4_len` in {2048, 8192, 32768}
x batch in {1, 48}, with `c4_len=32768` being the 128k-context decode shape this PR
targets. Passes with both 512 and 1024 (6 passed each) — it pins the kernel's contract
rather than the block size, so it keeps guarding the CUDA path too. The op is only
exported when `torch.version.hip is not None`, so the test is skipped on NVIDIA.

## Checklist

- [x] Correctness: selected index set is identical to the current kernel across 3860 rows (`c4_len` 2048-32768, batch 1/64/128, 4 seeds), and covers `torch.topk` ground truth.
- [x] End-to-end benchmarked on MI355X TP8 (table above).
- [x] CUDA path unchanged (`#else` branch keeps 512).
- [x] Unit test added for the previously untested op; passes at both 512 and 1024.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

title: [diffusion] Fix Hunyuan QKV pack indexing at production video shapes
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- keep Hunyuan QKV-pack row indexing in int64
- add a production-shaped regression whose merged-projection offset crosses INT32_MAX

## Root cause

FastHunyuan at 1280x720x125 frames produces 115,200 image tokens. The merged projection has a 21,504-element row stride, so the final row offset is 2,477,239,296 elements. The Triton program ID was inferred as int32 and overflowed while addressing the strided V view, causing an illegal memory access.

Casting the token index to int64 keeps the derived row-address arithmetic wide without changing the kernel layout or numerics.

## H200 validation

- production shape: FastVideo/FastHunyuan-diffusers, 1280x720, 125 frames, 6 steps, BF16, native SGLang
- lossless: 103.456 s denoise / 120.824 s saved-request e2e
- quality=high: 102.366 s denoise / 119.697 s saved-request e2e
- PyTorch-reference fallback versus fixed kernel ABBA: 121.001 s -> 120.393 s mean e2e (0.505%); all four MP4 files are byte-exact
- output SHA256: f4a8bffb62398b23e0884ea07b823d5857b436253bf0809fca65a28cf79016e2
- 41.91 GB isolated model caches were deleted after each model group, with zero weight files left

This is a production-shape correctness fix, not a >=1.5% performance claim.

## Tests

- python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_model_fast_paths.py -k hunyuan_qkv_rope_pack (3 passed on H200)
- pre-commit run --files python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/rope/hunyuan_qkv_pack_triton.py test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_model_fast_paths.py

title: [Perf] dsv4: Add native H16 CuTe sparse prefill backend
author: xuqianmamba
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4-Pro has 128 global query heads, so tensor parallelism with TP=8 leaves
16 logical query heads per rank. The existing SM90 FlashMLA sparse-prefill path
operates on an H64-padded query.

This PR adds an explicit, experimental native-H16 CuTe DSL backend:

```bash
--dsv4-prefill-backend cutedsl_h16
```

The backend avoids computing and materializing the 48 padded query heads and
returns a compact `[TQ, 16, 512]` output. The default `auto` behavior is
unchanged.

## Modifications

- Add an SM90 BF16 native-H16 CuTe DSL sparse-prefill kernel using an `m64n16`
  WGMMA decomposition and online softmax.
- Add `cutedsl_h16` to the DeepSeek-V4 sparse-prefill backend selection.
- Validate the supported launch contract:
  - CUDA SM90;
  - BF16 query and sparse workspace;
  - exactly 16 TP-local logical query heads;
  - Q/K/V width 512;
  - combined TOPK aligned to 128 and no greater than 16384.
- Use a configuration-sized aligned C128 TOPK bucket so changing live chunk
  lengths does not introduce a new JIT specialization.
- Cache the padded combined-index representation for reuse across layers.
- Keep decode, speculative, TBO, CP, bounded-tail, non-eager EXTEND, and CUDA
  graph/capture forwards on their existing paths.
- Reject explicit `cutedsl_h16` selection on unsupported HIP/NPU platforms
  instead of silently ignoring it.
- Reuse existing sparse-MLA kernel/backend tests for targeted H16 parity and
  cache coverage, retain dispatch/CLI checks, and document usage.

## Validation after refreshing main (2026-10-29)

Tested executable code: `50f2dbc5ab20561ff45b5c74e268230955fb3a9b`, merging
main `b960aa903aad354fb2e484041e5e33e3eb061e9b`. The subsequent commit
`2e57492ddbf81b94cbee7ef330f02c1e5a1242d1` only bounds the context length in
the documentation launch example. Executable code is unchanged.

The refresh uses the current kernel configuration, typed KV layouts,
compressed gather, and shared dequantization workspace. Native-H16 kernel
math is unchanged from the original PR.

- 17 selected package dispatch/CLI tests passed, with no failures or skips.
- 15 SM90 kernel/numerical tests passed, with no failures or skips.
- Repository-pinned formatting, Ruff selection, codespell, AST, whitespace,
  and test-registration checks passed.
- All 24 serving measurement points passed independent verification:
  864 successful requests with exact input/output lengths and no errors.
- The native-H16 dispatch marker was present on all eight TP ranks.

### End-to-end serving

DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 8x H20-3e, TP=8, context length 49152,
`flashinfer_mxfp4` MoE runner, chunked prefill 4096, max prefill tokens 16384,
max running requests 16, radix cache disabled, prefill CUDA Graph disabled,
decode CUDA Graph enabled, seed 1234, temperature 0. Only the prefill backend
changes between `flashmla_sparse` and `cutedsl_h16`.

Fixed-length token-ID prompts are derived from GSM8K questions using the
same dataset, tokenizer, and seed in both arms. Lengths and deterministic
prompt hashes are checked before model loading. Each case has three
repetitions with two warmup requests per repetition. Compilation, autotuning,
model loading, and request warmup are excluded from the reported times.

Values below are medians of three measurements. Throughput counts input plus
output tokens. The raw three-run ranges and per-request data are preserved.

| Input / output tokens | Concurrency | Requests / repetition | BF16 H64 tok/s | Native H16 tok/s | Throughput gain | Mean TTFT reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096 / 1 | 8 | 64 | 5286.37 | 5969.72 | 12.93% | 11.45% |
| 16384 / 1 | 8 | 32 | 5028.81 | 5839.60 | 16.12% | 13.87% |
| 32768 / 1 | 4 | 16 | 4875.40 | 5702.65 | 16.97% | 14.49% |
| 4096 / 128 | 16 | 32 | 4224.03 | 4641.04 | 9.87% | 11.64% |

### Accuracy

Legacy `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`: 5 shots, 1314 questions,
512 maximum output tokens, parallelism 32, temperature 0. Answers are
independently regraded from the complete saved state dumps. This legacy
protocol includes its first five in-context examples in the score;
the held-out score below excludes those five.

| Backend | Correct / 1314 | Accuracy | Held-out correct / 1309 | Held-out accuracy | Invalid answers |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| flashmla_sparse | 1253 / 1314 | 95.3577% | 1248 / 1309 | 95.3400% | 0 |
| cutedsl_h16 | 1249 / 1314 | 95.0533% | 1244 / 1309 | 95.0344% | 0 |

The H16 result is 4 fewer correct answers (0.3044 percentage points lower) in this run; this is not a claim of identical full-model accuracy. Paired comparison: 9 questions correct only on the baseline; 5 correct only on H16. Accuracy was evaluated once per backend at temperature zero with identical settings.

### Sparse-prefill operator benchmark

TQ=4096, SKV=49152. Each value is the median of three warmed public-API
CUDA-event p50 measurements, with provider order rotated across repeats.

| TOPK | FlashMLA BF16 H64 (us) | FlashMLA Q8 H64 (us) | CuTe BF16 H16 (us) | vs BF16 | vs Q8 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 690.032 | 534.944 | 236.368 | 2.919x | 2.263x |
| 384 | 1656.816 | 1127.968 | 559.040 | 2.964x | 2.018x |
| 512 | 2140.992 | 1427.264 | 720.272 | 2.972x | 1.982x |
| 640 | 2625.536 | 1726.656 | 882.464 | 2.975x | 1.957x |
| 1152 | 4557.568 | 2915.232 | 1525.600 | 2.987x | 1.911x |

Q8 inputs are prequantized; query casting and KV gather/dequantization/
requantization are excluded. FlashMLA returns H64 plus max/LSE, while
CuTe returns compact H16. These operator timings have different output
contracts and must not be read as end-to-end serving speedups.

Timed shapes pass BF16 parity with maximum absolute error <= 2.44140625e-4
and mean absolute error <= 1.9168e-6.

### Runtime

H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0, driver 580.82.07. The serving environment passes
the complete platform-applicable dependency audit against the merged
`python/pyproject.toml`. Core package versions:

- `torch==2.14.1`
- `triton==3.8.0`
- `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.8.0`
- `sglang-kernel==0.4.10`
- `sgl-flash-mla==1.0.0`
- `sgl-deep-gemm==0.2.3.post2`
- `flashinfer-python==0.7.2`
- `transformers==5.19.0`
- `deepseek-recipe==0.2.0`
- `openai==2.8.0`
- `timm==1.0.25`
- `tml-renderers==0.1.0`

### Integration check

The tested branch can merge cleanly with main
`1ab008f5b090e6595479ba57934e9211ab083565` as checked on 2026-10-29 using
`git merge-tree`. The H20 results above were measured on the explicitly
identified source commits, not on this later main revision.

## Runtime and test simplification (2026-10-30)

Commit `76defc8432d55b68e7520b506f05f21fcca18834` reduces the PR from
2,590 additions / 11 deletions to 1,253 additions / 12 deletions across
11 files. Runtime code shrinks by 183 net lines: remove redundant dispatch
validation and forwarding wrappers, share compilation/execution arguments,
and simplify the cached C128 padding. The 15 device-side computation and

## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 has 128 global query heads, so tensor parallelism with TP=8 leaves
16 logical query heads per rank. The existing SM90 FlashMLA sparse-prefill path
operates on an H64-padded query.

This PR adds an explicit, experimental native-H16 CuTe DSL backend:

```bash
--dsv4-prefill-backend cutedsl_h16
```

The backend avoids computing and materializing the 48 padded query heads and
returns a compact `[TQ, 16, 512]` output. The default `auto` behavior is
unchanged.

## Modifications

- Add an SM90 BF16 native-H16 CuTe DSL sparse-prefill kernel using an `m64n16`
  WGMMA decomposition and online softmax.
- Add `cutedsl_h16` to the DeepSeek-V4 sparse-prefill backend selection.
- Validate the supported launch contract:
  - CUDA SM90;
  - BF16 query and sparse workspace;
  - exactly 16 TP-local logical query heads;
  - Q/K/V width 512;
  - combined TOPK aligned to 128 and no greater than 8192.
- Use a configuration-sized aligned C128 TOPK bucket so changing live chunk
  lengths does not introduce a new JIT specialization.
- Cache the padded combined-index representation for reuse across layers.
- Keep decode, speculative, TBO, non-eager EXTEND, and CUDA graph/capture
  forwards on their existing paths.
- Reject explicit `cutedsl_h16` selection on unsupported HIP/NPU platforms
  instead of silently ignoring it.
- Add SM90 kernel tests, independent oracle/parity coverage, dispatch and CLI
  tests, a three-provider CUDA benchmark, and user documentation.

Validation used source commit
`5d0e688a3ca49bb521be4e20e835d415bb4f72af` on 8x NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90), with
CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1,

`sgl-deep-gemm==0.1.5.post3`, and FlashInfer 0.6.17. A later docs-only commit

title: [Diffusion] Reuse SRT quantization contracts and MXFP8 kernels
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- make diffusion quantization configs and methods extend the shared SRT contracts
- reuse SRT parsing, validation, and helpers for FP8 and BitsAndBytes while retaining diffusion layer dispatch
- use one SRT-backed MXFP8 adapter across NVIDIA, ROCm, and Ascend, deleting the duplicate NPU implementation
- infer self-describing per-layer MXFP8 safetensors while leaving unmarked layers unquantized
- admit MiniMax-H3 community MXFP8 transformer overrides without an explicit quantization flag

## Design

Diffusion keeps only the adapter code required by its LinearBase and component loader. Weight creation, post-load scale preparation, activation quantization, and MXFP8 GEMM dispatch live in SRT. Serialized scale metadata is validated before model construction, and mixed per-layer checkpoints fail closed under FSDP.

ModelOpt, ModelSlim, GGUF, and MXFP4 retain their diffusion adapters because their current dense checkpoint layouts, matching rules, or backend semantics are not equivalent to the corresponding SRT paths.

title: [AMD][DSV4] perf: retune decode split-K heuristic for MI355X
author: karverma-amd
body:
## Motivation

`_kv_splits_heuristic` picks how many KV splits DSv4 decode attention launches.
It over-split by exactly one power of two across the whole decode range: at
`H=128`/`block_h=64` it chose 8/4/2 splits for `T=32/64/128` where 4/2/1 measure
faster.

Split-K only pays while the base grid underfills the device. Each extra split
adds a partial-buffer write plus reduce-kernel work, and once per-split K gets
short that overhead is no longer amortized.

## Modification

Two constants in one file: `target_wg_per_cu` 2.0 -> 1.5 and the
`_MAX_KV_SPLITS` cap 64 -> 16. No kernel changes, no new code paths.

Swept `T` in {1..256} x `kv_len` in {128, 512, 1024} at `H=128` on MI355X,
scoring each candidate by distance from the per-shape optimum:

| constants | geomean regret | worst case |
| --------- | -------------- | ---------- |
| (2.0, 64) — current | 33.5% | 119% |
| (1.5, 16) — this PR | **3.7%** | 36% |

The per-shape optimum does depend on per-token K, which is not knowable at
CUDAGraph capture time, so the residual 3.7% is the price of capture-time
safety rather than a tuning gap.

### Kernel level

Decode attention at the production shape (`T=32`, `top-k 1024`, `H=128`):
**55.7 us -> 44.1 us, a 20.8% improvement**. Selection is unchanged, so results
are identical modulo bf16 reassociation of the split reduction.

## Performance

DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MI355X (gfx950), `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x-20260822`,
8192 in / 1024 out, TP8 + DP8 attention + EP8/MoRI + EAGLE MTP. Both arms are the
same image and the same flags; the only difference is the two constants.

| conc | tput base (tok/s) | tput PR (tok/s) | tput | TPOT base (ms) | TPOT PR (ms) | TPOT |
| ---- | ----------------- | --------------- | ------ | -------------- | ------------ | ------ |
| 4    | 860.07            | 873.28          | +1.5%  | 39.79          | 39.11        | -1.7%  |
| 8    | 1508.46           | 1545.51         | +2.5%  | 42.92          | 42.17        | -1.8%  |
| 16   | 2590.30           | 2610.88         | +0.8%  | 50.02          | 49.62        | -0.8%  |
| 32   | 4001.04           | 4073.41         | +1.8%  | 65.30          | 64.24        | -1.6%  |
| 64   | 5539.24           | 5776.29         | +4.3%  | 96.41          | 92.41        | -4.2%  |

Throughput rises and TPOT falls at every concurrency, and the two move together
at each point, which is harder to explain as drift than either alone. The gain
grows with concurrency because more tokens per rank makes decode attention a
larger share of the step.

One run per cell. Note the effect is specific to DP attention: with plain TP8,
the 128 heads sharded to 16 per rank, the same build measures flat (all deltas
under 1%, signs alternating). DP attention keeps all 128 heads resident per rank,
which is the shape the constants were tuned on.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```
# Server, per arm; $CONC in {4, 8, 16, 32, 64}
SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton \
SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_COMPRESS_NORM_ROPE=1 \
SGLANG_OPT_NATIVE_BPRESHUFFLE_SCALE=1 \
SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM=1 \
AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 \
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \
SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1 SGLANG_DP_SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL=1 \
SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1 SGLANG_DP_USE_REDUCE_SCATTER=1 \
GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=5 MORI_SHMEM_MODE=ISOLATION MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE=8G \
MORI_EP_LAUNCH_CONFIG_MODE=AUTO \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention \
  --ep-size 8 --moe-a2a-backend mori --deepep-mode normal \
  --moe-dense-tp-size 1 --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --attention-backend dsv4 --page-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --enforce-shared-experts-fusion \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --context-length 16384 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.78 \
  --max-running-requests $CONC --cuda-graph-max-bs $CONC

# Perf client, per concurrency
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang-oai \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port $PORT --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts $((CONC * 10)) --max-concurrency $CONC

# Accuracy
python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 1319 --parallel 1319
```

Note: under DP attention `--max-running-requests` is divided by `dp_size`, so a
value below the DP degree floors to 0 per rank and trips
`assert max_running_request > 0`. At `$CONC` 4 it was raised to 8; the client's
`--max-concurrency` is what bounds the load either way.

</details>

## Accuracy

GSM8K, 1319 questions, parallel 1319: **0.958** and **0.946** across two runs,
**invalid 0.000** both times.

## Unit test

`_kv_splits_heuristic` had no test. This PR adds
`test/registered/unit/layers/test_dsv4_kv_splits_heuristic.py` (38 cases),
pinning the contract rather than the constants:

- result is always a positive power of two within the cap — the reduce kernel
  indexes partial buffers by pow2 stride, so a bad value corrupts results rather
  than merely running slowly
- splits never rise as token count rises
- no splitting once the base grid saturates the device
- CUDAGraph safety: depends only on capture-time scalars, never reads a tensor

One clearly-marked table pins the six tuned operating points, so retuning for a
future architecture touches that test and nothing else.

```
pytest test/registered/unit/layers/test_dsv4_kv_splits_heuristic.py
```

## Checklist

- [x] Kernel-level and end-to-end benchmarked on MI355X (tables above)
- [x] Accuracy verified, 1319 questions, zero invalid
- [x] Unit test added for a previously untested function
- [x] No new code paths, no monkeypatching; two constants in one file
- [x] CUDA path unaffected — this file is the ROCm-only dsv4 unified_kv backend

title: [AMD][DSV4] perf: MXFP8 MoRI dispatch to match the w4a8 MoE input format
author: karverma-amd
body:
## Motivation

DSv4's MoE runs `per_1x32` (MXFP4 weights), so AITER wants fp8 activations
carrying group-32 e8m0 microscales. None of MoRI's three shipped dispatch dtypes
produce that:

| dispatch | payload | scales | consequence |
| -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| bf16 | bf16 | none | receiver must quantize |
| fp8 | fp8 | group-128 fp32 | wrong group size -> fp8->bf16 upscale round trip |
| fp4 | fp4x2 | group-32 e8m0 | right scales, wrong payload -> `upscale_mxfp4` |

bf16 wins by default only because it is the one with no upscale kernel. But it
pushes the bf16->fp8 conversion to the **receive** side, and that is where the
cost is: AITER sizes its quant grid from the input row count
(`aiter/csrc/kernels/quant_kernels.cu`, `rows = input.numel() / cols`), and the
input is MoRI's *padded* receive buffer
(`num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank * world_size` = 3072 * 8 = 24576 rows) rather
than the ~112 live tokens decode actually carries. `num_rows` is a device
pointer used only for a per-block early exit, so it cannot shrink the grid.

DSR-1 never hits this: it is w8a8, its dispatch delivers fp8 with per-128 fp32
scales which is already the MoE's input format, so AITER takes the
`hidden_states.dtype == q_dtype_a` branch and runs no quant kernel at all.

## Modification

Adds an `mxfp8` dispatch mode that quantizes on the **send** side, over live
tokens, emitting the fp8 + group-32 e8m0 layout the MoE kernels consume
directly. Opt-in via `SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_DTYPE=mxfp8`; the default stays
`bf16`, so existing deployments are untouched.

**Depends on the matching aiter change** (a8w4 mxfp8 passthrough in
`fused_moe.py`), which must land first.

## Performance

DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MI355X (gfx950), `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x-20260822`,
8192 in / 1024 out, TP8 + DP8 attention + EP8/MoRI + EAGLE MTP. Both arms are the
same build; the only difference is `SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_DTYPE`.

| conc | tput bf16 (tok/s) | tput mxfp8 (tok/s) | tput | TPOT bf16 (ms) | TPOT mxfp8 (ms) | TPOT |
| ---- | ----------------- | ------------------ | ------ | -------------- | --------------- | ------ |
| 4    | 1022.03           | 1121.97            | +9.8%  | 33.30          | 30.19           | -9.3%  |
| 8    | 1818.01           | 1969.84            | +8.4%  | 35.52          | 32.73           | -7.9%  |
| 16   | 3080.51           | 3277.43            | +6.4%  | 42.12          | 39.52           | -6.2%  |
| 32   | 4527.58           | 4905.24            | +8.3%  | 57.79          | 53.17           | -8.0%  |
| 64   | 6264.62           | 6827.92            | +9.0%  | 85.21          | 78.19           | -8.2%  |

TPOT mirrors throughput at every point, which is harder to attribute to drift
than either metric alone. For scale: repeat runs of an identical build on this
setup span 0.5-2.7%, so every cell here is well outside run-to-run noise.

One run per cell.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```
# Server, per arm; $CONC in {4, 8, 16, 32, 64}
# baseline arm: SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_DTYPE=bf16
# this PR:      SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_DTYPE=mxfp8
SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton \
SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_COMPRESS_NORM_ROPE=1 \
SGLANG_OPT_NATIVE_BPRESHUFFLE_SCALE=1 \
SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM=1 \
AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \
SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1 SGLANG_DP_SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL=1 \
SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1 SGLANG_DP_USE_REDUCE_SCATTER=1 \
GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=5 MORI_SHMEM_MODE=ISOLATION MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE=8G \
MORI_EP_LAUNCH_CONFIG_MODE=AUTO \
SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_DTYPE=$DTYPE \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention \
  --ep-size 8 --moe-a2a-backend mori --deepep-mode normal \
  --moe-dense-tp-size 1 --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --attention-backend dsv4 --page-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --enforce-shared-experts-fusion \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --context-length 16384 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.78 \
  --max-running-requests $CONC --cuda-graph-max-bs $CONC

# Perf client, per concurrency
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang-oai \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port $PORT --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts $((CONC * 10)) --max-concurrency $CONC

# Accuracy
python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 1319 --parallel 1319
```

Note: under DP attention `--max-running-requests` is divided by `dp_size`, so a
value below the DP degree floors to 0 per rank and trips
`assert max_running_request > 0`. At `$CONC` 4 it was raised to 8.

</details>

## Accuracy

GSM8K, 1319 questions, parallel 1319: **0.945, invalid 0.000.**

## Unit test

`test/registered/unit/layers/test_moriep_mxfp8_dispatch.py` (9 cases) pins the
byte layout and env wiring, which are the parts that regress silently -- an fp8
payload with the wrong scale group or dtype still runs, but reintroduces the
upscale round trip this mode exists to remove, and the only symptom is lost
throughput:

- scale group size is 32 (group-128 would force the upscale back)
- one scale per 32 channels; a mismatch under-allocates the scale buffer
- e8m0 scales are 1 byte -- the dispatch buffer is sized from this
- every `DispatchDtype` value is distinct, and `mxfp8` is reachable from the env
- the zero-live-token decode path still emits a correctly shaped scale tensor

```
pytest test/registered/unit/layers/test_moriep_mxfp8_dispatch.py
```

## Checklist

- [x] End-to-end benchmarked on MI355X across conc 4-64 (table above)
- [x] Accuracy verified, 1319 questions, zero invalid
- [x] Unit test added
- [x] Opt-in; default behaviour unchanged
- [ ] **Blocked on the aiter side landing first** (a8w4 mxfp8 passthrough)

title: [AMD] Quark shared-experts gate: recognise a trailing MTP layer
author: Jacob0226
body:
## Summary

`can_fuse_shared_expert()` recognises the MTP draft stack only by an `mtp.` prefix. GLM-5.2-MXFP4 spells it `model.layers.78` (`num_hidden_layers=78`), so three excluded draft projections veto fusion for all 78 target-model layers. `from_config()`'s prequantized branch also never forwarded `hf_config`, leaving the layer count unavailable.

Losing fusion costs more than the fused shared expert alone:

|                      | fused (expected)    | unfused (today)               |
| -------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| aiter `fused_moe` key | 257 experts, topk 9 | 256, 8                        |
| tuned FlyDSL config  | hit                 | **miss — heuristic fallback** |

Introduced by #35200, which restored the gate after the load-time-override removal.

## Scope

Quark MXFP4 checkpoints whose draft layer sits at the end of the main decoder. An `mtp.` prefix (Qwen3.5), a model with no draft layer, and every non-Quark path keep current behaviour; without `hf_config` the helper falls back to the prefix test.

## Test plan

Stock `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260820`, no PRs applied; GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X TP4, in8192 / out1024, DSA backends `tilelang`. The gate is the only variable.

title: [AMD][DSV4] perf: bound the MoRI receive buffer during decode
author: karverma-amd
body:
## Motivation

AITER sizes its quantization grid from the input row count
(`aiter/csrc/kernels/quant_kernels.cu`, `rows = input.numel() / cols`). Under
MoRI that input is the **padded** receive buffer
(`num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank * world_size` = 4096 * 8 = 32768 rows), not
the live tokens. `num_rows` is a device pointer used only for a per-block early
exit, so it cannot shrink the grid.

In decode the padding dominates: at concurrency 64 a rank carries at most 32
tokens, whose entire expert fan-in is 1792 rows, yet every kernel still launches
blocks covering 32768. The narrower the batch, the larger the share of that work
that is pure waste.

## Modification

Bound the row count at the worst case the receive buffer can actually see:
every rank routing a full decode graph's worth of tokens to this one,
`max_graph_tokens * world_size * topk`. `topk` already includes the fused shared
expert (`deepseek_v2.py` folds `num_fused_shared_experts` into `top_k`), so this
is a bound, not an estimate — at conc 64 it is `32 * 8 * 7 = 1792`, the exact
case where every rank sends every token-expert pair here.

The subtlety is *which* token count is safe to use. This code runs while a cuda
graph is **captured**, so the value is frozen into the graph and has to hold for
every later replay, including replays where a peer carries a wider batch than
the one seen at capture. Deriving it from the batch in hand would break as soon
as ranks replay different tiers — which they do in this configuration, since
neither `require_mlp_tp_gather()` nor `require_attn_tp_gather()` holds under
`--enable-dp-lm-head` with `--moe-dense-tp-size 1`.

So it is derived from the widest decode graph *any* rank will replay, taken from
`capture_bs` (already clamped by `req_to_token_pool.size`) and reduced with an
explicit `all_reduce(MAX)` at runner init, outside capture where a collective is
safe. `req_to_token_pool.size` is sized from measured free memory and so is not
guaranteed identical across ranks, hence a reduction rather than an assumption
of symmetry. A peer replaying a wider tier is then covered by construction, and
there is no synchronized-graph-tier requirement left to guard.

Two cases stay unbounded, because a bound below the real fan-in silently drops
rows from the all-to-all — wrong output rather than an error:

- **Prefill**, whose per-rank counts are uneven and not knowable here.
- **Anything outside capture.** Eager decode runs precisely when the batch
  exceeds every captured tier, so the published width would not bound it, and
  there is no graph to bake a saving into anyway.

The bound logs once when it engages. An optimization that silently computes zero
still serves tokens and still produces a plausible table, so the run says what
it did.

Opt-in via `SGLANG_MORI_RECV_BOUND`; default off. 93 lines across two files.

## Performance

DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MI355X (gfx950), `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x-20260822`,
8192 in / 1024 out, TP8 + DP8 attention + EP8/MoRI + EAGLE MTP. Both arms are the
same build; the only difference is `SGLANG_MORI_RECV_BOUND`.

| conc | tput off (tok/s) | tput on (tok/s) | tput | TPOT off (ms) | TPOT on (ms) | TPOT | bound |
| ---- | ---------------- | --------------- | ------- | ------------- | ------------ | ------ | ------------- |
| 4    | 858.46           | 2012.83         | +134.5% | 39.78         | 16.13        | -59.5% | 32768 -> 224  |
| 8    | 1532.61          | 3267.40         | +113.2% | 42.21         | 18.78        | -55.5% | 32768 -> 224  |
| 16   | 2590.76          | 4590.32         | +77.2%  | 50.07         | 27.43        | -45.2% | 32768 -> 448  |
| 32   | 4048.76          | 5957.94         | +47.2%  | 64.54         | 43.48        | -32.6% | 32768 -> 896  |
| 64   | 5666.15          | 7323.05         | +29.3%  | 93.65         | 72.71        | -22.4% | 32768 -> 1792 |

The gain shrinking monotonically with concurrency is the mechanism showing
through rather than a coincidence: more live tokens means proportionally less
padding wasted, so the saving has to fall as concurrency rises. TPOT mirrors
throughput at every point.

The last column is the bound each ON server logged. It scales with
`--cuda-graph-max-bs` as the derivation predicts, all 8 ranks report it, and the
OFF servers log zero occurrences — so the measured arm is demonstrably the arm
doing the work.

One run per cell. For scale, repeat runs of an identical build on this setup
span 0.5-2.7%, measured across three separate baseline sweeps.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```
# Server, per arm; $CONC in {4, 8, 16, 32, 64}
# baseline arm: SGLANG_MORI_RECV_BOUND=false
# this PR:      SGLANG_MORI_RECV_BOUND=true
SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton \
SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_COMPRESS_NORM_ROPE=1 \
SGLANG_OPT_NATIVE_BPRESHUFFLE_SCALE=1 \
SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM=1 \
AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \
SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1 SGLANG_DP_SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL=1 \
SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1 SGLANG_DP_USE_REDUCE_SCATTER=1 \
GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=5 MORI_SHMEM_MODE=ISOLATION MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE=8G \
MORI_EP_LAUNCH_CONFIG_MODE=AUTO \
SGLANG_MORI_RECV_BOUND=$ARM \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention \
  --ep-size 8 --moe-a2a-backend mori --deepep-mode normal \
  --moe-dense-tp-size 1 --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --attention-backend dsv4 --page-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --enforce-shared-experts-fusion \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --context-length 16384 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.78 \
  --max-running-requests $CONC --cuda-graph-max-bs $CONC

# Perf client, per concurrency
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang-oai \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port $PORT --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts $((CONC * 10)) --max-concurrency $CONC

# Accuracy
python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 1319 --parallel 1319
```

Note: under DP attention `--max-running-requests` is divided by `dp_size`, so a
value below the DP degree floors to 0 per rank and trips
`assert max_running_request > 0`. At `$CONC` 4 it was raised to 8.

</details>

## Accuracy

GSM8K, 1319 questions, parallel 1319: **0.948, invalid 0.000**, with the bound
logged active at `32768 -> 1792` on all 8 ranks.

## Checklist

- [x] End-to-end benchmarked on MI355X across conc 4-64
- [x] Accuracy verified, 1319 questions, zero invalid
- [x] Bound confirmed active in the measured arm, and absent in the baseline
- [x] Opt-in; default behaviour unchanged
- [x] Prefill and eager decode deliberately left unbounded

author: michaelzhang-ai

## Motivation

MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 has accuracy coverage in the ROCm 7.2 nightly on MI35x (#30613, tuned in #33402) but no perf coverage. M2.5 sits next to it as a second 4-GPU MI35x MiniMax job, and gfx950 serves M3's MXFP8 MoE weights natively, so M3 is the one worth the slot: this PR gives it M2.5's MI35x slot and spends the freed time on a perf benchmark. Net runner cost is roughly unchanged — one job is removed, one perf step of comparable length is added, both across the workflow's `rocm724` + `rocm720` matrix.

## Modifications

**`test/registered/amd/perf/mi35x/test_minimax_m3_perf_mi35x.py` (new)** — registered as the `nightly-perf-4-gpu-mi35x-minimax-m3` suite.

- TP=4 with the exact recipe `test_minimax_m3_tp4_eval_mi35x.py` validated (`--quantization mxfp8`, aiter attention, `fp8_e4m3` KV, radix cache off, the block-fp8 linear path from #32036, custom/quick INT4 all-reduce from #32230), so a throughput regression cannot be confused with a configuration difference. It adds only multithread weight load and a decode graph capped at the largest timed batch.
- Sweeps batch 1 / 8 / 16 / 64 at 1K input / 1K output, the decode-weighted shape the cookbook publishes for MI355X, which is what matters for a model that spends most of its tokens inside `<mm:think>`.
- Uses the current MI35x perf convention (`NightlyBenchmarkRunner` + `generate_simple_markdown_report(..., default_gpu_config="MI35x")`), same as the Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.2 benchmarks.

**`.github/workflows/nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`**

- Added a `Performance Test MI35x ROCm 7.2 (4-GPU MiniMax-M3 MXFP8)` step to `nightly-4-gpu-mi35x-minimax-m3-rocm720`, after the eval. Accuracy gates perf, both steps reuse the cached checkpoint and one MI35x slot, and perf is `continue-on-error: true` so a throughput blip does not fail a job whose eval passed — the arrangement the GLM-5.2-FP8, GLM-5-MXFP4, Kimi-K3 and M2.7 jobs already use.
- Removed the `nightly-4-gpu-mi35x-minimax-m25-rocm720` job, its `job_select` dropdown entry, and its `check-all-jobs` `needs` entry. M2.5 keeps its 4-GPU MI35x accuracy job in the ROCm 7.0 nightly (`nightly-test-amd.yml`), so its test files stay in use and none are deleted. No running M2.5 perf coverage is lost either: the `nightly-perf-8-gpu-mi35x-minimax-m25` suite is registered but referenced by no workflow.

## Accuracy Tests

No model, kernel, or runtime code is touched. M3 accuracy on MI35x continues to run unchanged via the existing `nightly-amd-4-gpu-mi35x-minimax-m3-tp4` suite, which scored GSM8K chat + thinking **0.970** (rocm720) and **0.968** (rocm724) against its 0.95 threshold, 0 invalid, in the validation runs below — immediately before the new perf step in each.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Dispatched on MI35x hardware for both images the nightly matrix runs — rocm720 ([32768402397](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32768402397)) and rocm724 ([32813993930](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32813993930), torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2). Each ran the eval and then the new perf step in one job; all four steps passed.

`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 (TP4+MXFP8+aiterAttn+fp8KV+blockFP8+quickAR) [MI35x]`, 1K input / 1K output:

| batch size | latency (s) rocm720 / rocm724 | input tok/s | output tok/s | ITL (ms) |
| ---------- | ----------------------------- | ----------- | ------------ | -------- |
| 1  | 14.33 / 14.53 | 8948.94 / 8837.72  | 72.05 / 71.04     | 13.88 / 14.08 |
| 8  | 17.17 / 17.50 | 34673.21 / 34945.74 | 483.79 / 474.49  | 16.54 / 16.86 |
| 16 | 20.41 / 20.70 | 35359.94 / 35635.71 | 821.53 / 809.41  | 19.48 / 19.77 |
| 64 | 29.95 / 30.48 | 36148.01 / 35951.29 | 2328.79 / 2286.65 | 27.48 / 27.99 |

Output throughput scales 32x from batch 1 to 64 while ITL only grows 13.9 -> 27.5 ms, and prefill saturates by batch 8. The two images agree within 2% on every cell, so the benchmark is reproducible across the matrix rather than image-specific. Accuracy alongside them: 0.970 (rocm720) and 0.968 (rocm724) against the 0.95 threshold, 0 invalid on both. Each job took ~37 minutes (20 eval, 12 perf, rest setup), well inside the two 120-minute step budgets.


Also verified in-repo: the workflow parses with M2.5 absent from the job list, dropdown and `check-all-jobs`; the AST registry resolves `nightly-perf-4-gpu-mi35x-minimax-m3` to exactly the new file; `black` and `isort` are clean.

title: [kernel] Share the warp vectorized copy and enforce its alignment
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> Generated by Claude.

## Motivation

Four JIT kernels hand-rolled the same thing: a warp cooperatively moving one contiguous row. `concat_mla`, `set_mla_kv_buffer`, `store_cache` and `set_mla_kv_concat_q` each had their own vector-width selection, their own tail handling, and their own idea of what alignment they required. `warp_inclusive_sum` existed in four separate copies.

That duplication was not just untidy — it hid a bug class. The vector width a copy picks is derived from the row **size** (a 1024 B row gets 16 B accesses), but the address it lands on is `base + index * stride`, and nothing constrains a stride to match the size. Two real faults came out of that gap during this work, both reproduced:

- a `kv_buffer` row stride of 1048 B (`ROPE_DIM=12`) took 16 B stores on odd `loc` → `CUDA error: misaligned address`
- `store_cache` with `num_threads=256` on a 100 B row silently dropped the last 4 B of **every** row, because `kKBytes / kNumSplit` truncated with no guard

## What changed

**One shared copy path.** `warp::load_bytes<kBytes, kPattern>` / `store_bytes` in `warp.cuh`, backed by `LoadStorePattern`. Handles arbitrary widths down to 1 byte, including odd ones, and the ragged tail. The four hand-rolled versions are gone.

**Alignment becomes a stated precondition, not an assumption.**
- `TensorMatcher::ensure_alignment(bytes)` validates the data pointer and every stride but the innermost (size-1 dims skipped, since their strides are arbitrary).
- `LoadStorePattern::get_vec_bytes` is now `SGL_DEVICE_HOST`, so the launcher and the kernel share **one** formula. Both previous faults traced to host and kernel each hand-rolling a different `gcd`.
- The `store_cache` split carries `static_assert(kKBytes % kNumSplit == 0)`, turning the silent truncation into a compile error.

**`warp::reduce` generalised.** `<kNumThreads, kInner>` → a symmetric `<kStart, kFinish>` bit range that expresses both old modes: `<N, 1>` is the old inner reduce, `<kFullWidth, N>` the old inter-group one. Verified against an independent reference on 9 configurations.

**New primitives.** `inclusive_reduce` / `inclusive_sum` / `_max` / `_min` (with `lane_id` defaulted so the segment-relative contract can't be got wrong), `broadcast`, `atomic::Event` (cross-CTA arrive/wait in one 32-bit word), and `bits.h`.

**`get_lane_id<N>()`, per platform.** Reads the lane register on CUDA — worth 8 instructions and 2 registers in a two-tile warp copy, because the modulo form makes the compiler re-derive the mask at every address scale. On HIP it masks `threadIdx.x`, since AMD has no lane register and the intrinsic lowers to a `v_mbcnt` pair, making the "optimisation" a 2-instruction pessimisation there.

**`store_cache` now supports arbitrary row widths** and picks its split in Python (`_jit_kvcache_module`) instead of through a C++ dispatch ladder gated on byte-alignment `if constexpr`s.

## Verification

- **Kernel battery**: 10 suites, **6259 passed / 11 skipped**, against the shared-header changes.
- **`test_store_cache.py`**: 316 tests, re-run after the final alignment tightening.
- **SASS parity**: `concat_mla_absorb_q` on the shared helpers is **byte-identical** to the hand-rolled original (79 instructions, 20 registers, 3 LDG / 3 STG). A/B over 20 shapes: mean −0.36%, and the residual ±1.8% on sub-1.5 µs shapes is one timer tick.
- **ROCm**: compiled with the exact HIP flags (no `--expt-relaxed-constexpr`) and run on a real **MI350X / gfx950, hipcc 7.0**. All `get_lane_id` specialisations, `reduce`, `inclusive_sum` and `broadcast` correct on a 64-wide wave; the unguarded `__shfl_up_sync` / `__shfl_sync` verified to work on HIP.
- Arbitrary widths exercised down to 1, 3, 7, 97, 195, 1023 bytes, plus asymmetric K/V.

## Behaviour changes worth reviewing

- **Strides are now validated rather than assumed.** A padded row that previously produced a misaligned-address fault now raises a clear host-side error instead. Callers relying on an unchecked stride will see a new error rather than a crash.
- **`concat_mla_k`'s base requirement drops 16 → 8**, which is what its widest access (`v2.s32`) actually needs, while *gaining* the stride check its `>> 2` stride stepping always silently relied on.
- `set_mla_kv_buffer`'s buffer alignment was `min(nope, rope)`; it is now `max`. The buffer row carries both halves, so the narrower one let a nope-misaligned stride through — this is what allowed the first fault above.

The `add-jit-kernel` skill is updated in the same commit, since this changes `warp::reduce`'s signature, removes `copy_bytes`, and adds `load_bytes` / `ensure_alignment` / `Event`.

title: [Model] Support Nemotron 3.5 Lightning speculative decoding
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

Add clean, minimal-intrusion speculative decoding support for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. This supersedes the implementation approach explored in #33554 while keeping useful ModelOpt and Nemotron model changes narrowly scoped.

## Modifications

- Add ModelOpt W4A16 NVFP4 support needed by the published DFlash/DSpark draft checkpoints.
- Add Nemotron 3.5-specific DFlash and DSpark layouts, including draft embeddings, packed projections, attention sinks, residual-layer capture, and bonus-anchor handling.
- Derive DSpark anchor sampling and the Nemotron-specific Markov layout from the already-loaded draft model config; no public ServerArgs knob is added.
- Avoid hidden-state selection and `contiguous()` on the legacy sample-from-anchor path.
- Resolve Blackwell target/draft attention backends without overriding explicit user choices.
- Keep generic speculative APIs and existing non-Nemotron behavior unchanged; risky layout behavior is guarded by structural Nemotron 3.5 checks.
- Preserve Nemotron server-argument override unit coverage.
- Replace the registered Nemotron Nano E2E with Nemotron 3.5 NVFP4 Normal, DFlash, and DSpark cases.
- Update the cookbook install command to consume the latest main branch.

## Accuracy Tests

Ran the full 1,319-example single-shot GSM8K set on a 4x GB300 devbox with the eight published B200 cookbook command variants (ports/NCCL ports adjusted only for parallel execution):

```bash
sgl-eval run gsm8k \
  --base-url http://localhost:30000/v1 \
  --num-threads 32
```

| Target | Strategy | GSM8K | Avg accepted length | Derived accept rate | Error rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| NVFP4 | Normal | 95.38% | N/A | N/A | 0.00% |
| NVFP4 | MTP | 94.62% | 5.378 / 6 | 87.6% | 0.00% |
| NVFP4 | DFlash | 95.22% | 4.173 / 6 | 63.5% | 0.00% |
| NVFP4 | DSpark | 95.45% | 3.708 / 4 | 90.3% | 0.00% |
| BF16 | Normal | 95.15% | N/A | N/A | 0.00% |
| BF16 | MTP | 95.53% | 4.838 / 6 | 76.8% | 0.00% |
| BF16 | DFlash | 95.83% | 3.684 / 6 | 53.7% | 0.00% |
| BF16 | DSpark | 95.45% | 3.554 / 4 | 85.1% | 0.00% |

Derived accept rate uses `(avg_accept_length - 1) / (verify_width - 1)`. All accuracy results exceed the 80% criterion; all speculative variants have healthy acceptance, with some variants exceeding the illustrative 0.5-0.8 range on the high side.

After addressing review feedback, I synced the rebased final source to a separate GB300 directory and reran both external-draft paths over the full dataset:

| Final rebased source | GSM8K | Mean logged accept rate | Error rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| BF16 + DFlash | 95.45% | 73.3% | 0.00% |
| BF16 + DSpark | 95.75% | 92.1% | 0.00% |

The mean logged rate is the arithmetic mean of SGLang's periodic `accept rate` values. DSpark's high value is driven partly by a long, highly accepted tail and indicates strong—not low—acceptance.

Additional verification:

- Final rebased `test/registered/unit/test_model_overrides.py`: 87 tests passed on GB300.
- Registered E2E: 3 tests collected; all resolve to sgl-eval, threshold 0.80, 200 examples, 32 threads, thinking enabled.
- Modified Python files pass `py_compile`.
- Pre-commit formatting, AST, isort, ruff, codespell, registry, and related checks pass.
- `check_no_bare_pytest_main.py` passes under Python 3.12.
- Cookbook configuration validation passes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This PR makes no performance claim. The accuracy runs used one server per GPU in parallel; server logs showed stable generation and no serving-time runtime/CUDA errors.

- [x] Add unit tests and registered E2E coverage.

title: [AMD] Fix nightly ROCm 7.0 image build: patch missing <optional> include in AITER topk kernel
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## Motivation

[Release Docker Images Nightly ROCm7.0 (AMD)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/workflows/release-docker-amd-nightly.yml) has failed on `main` for four consecutive nights (Aug 21–24), on both `gfx942` and `gfx950`, so no `rocm/sgl-dev:*-rocm700-*` or `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:*-rocm700-*` image has been published since Aug 20.

Both legs fail in the AITER build step with the same compile error:

```
/sgl-workspace/aiter/aiter_meta/csrc/kernels/topk_per_row_kernels.cu:2849:33: error: no template named 'optional' in namespace 'std'
/sgl-workspace/aiter/aiter_meta/csrc/kernels/topk_per_row_kernels.cu:2854:75: error: no member named 'nullopt' in namespace 'std'
5 errors generated when compiling for gfx942.
RuntimeError: [aiter] build [module_top_k_per_row] under /sgl-workspace/aiter/aiter/jit/build/module_top_k_per_row/build failed !!!!!!
```

Failing runs: [32480722324](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32480722324) (first), [32572178966](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32572178966), [32638562658](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32638562658), [32725844614](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32725844614) (latest). Last green run was [32367609479](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32367609479) on Aug 20.

Root cause: the failures start with the AITER pin bump to `c16d44b` in #35810, which merged Aug 21 07:02 UTC — a few hours before the first failing nightly. At `ROCm/aiter@c16d44b`, `csrc/kernels/topk_per_row_kernels.cu` uses `std::optional` / `std::nullopt` but does not include `<optional>`; it used to get the declaration transitively from `<torch/all.h>` and `<ATen/hip/HIPContext.h>`, which ROCm/aiter#4702 ("[module_topk_*] refactor and remove torch") dropped in favor of aiter's own `aiter_tensor.h` / `aiter_stream.h`.

That is why only the ROCm 7.0 flavors break. ROCm 7.2's newer toolchain still exposes `<optional>` through some other header in the include chain, so `release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly` and the miles ROCm 7.2 nightly keep passing on the same AITER pin, while `rocm/sgl-dev:rocm7-vllm-20250904` does not. `topk_plain_kernels.cu` has the same missing include but compiles fine everywhere — it pulls `<optional>` in via `opus/opus.hpp` — so `topk_per_row_kernels.cu` is the only affected translation unit.

Upstream already fixed this in ROCm/aiter#4853 (`ROCm/aiter@97d2e6a`, Aug 20), which is 27 commits ahead of the pinned commit. Rather than bump the pin across all six flavors — including the ROCm 7.2 ones that are currently green — and pull in 27 unvalidated AITER commits, this applies the one-line upstream include locally.

`docker/rocm.Dockerfile` also backs `release-docker-amd.yml`, so this unblocks the next tagged ROCm 7.0 release build as well.

## Modifications

`docker/rocm.Dockerfile`: after the AITER checkout and before `setup.py build_ext`, insert `#include <optional>` into `csrc/kernels/topk_per_row_kernels.cu`, in the same position as upstream's fix. The patch is guarded so it is a no-op when the file already has the include, does not use `std::optional`, or is absent — i.e. it self-disables as soon as `AITER_COMMIT` reaches `ROCm/aiter@97d2e6a`, at which point the block can be deleted. The comment records the upstream PRs on both sides so the removal condition is explicit.

The patch is placed as its own `RUN` before the build step (the existing `torch_utils.py` hot-patch sits after the build because it only touches a runtime Python file). `aiter_meta/csrc` is a `copytree` of `csrc` made by `setup.py`, so patching the repo path before the build propagates to the compiled copy.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — no model or kernel code changes. The added `#include` matches upstream ROCm/aiter#4853 exactly and only makes an already-used declaration visible; it does not alter generated code.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

## Verification

`release-docker-amd-nightly.yml` was dispatched on this branch: **run [32771593845](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32771593845), both legs green.** The two modules that had been failing now compile, with zero `no template named 'optional'` / `no member named 'nullopt'` errors in either log:

Both legs published their images, so this run also fills in the ROCm 7.0 nightly tags that have been missing since Aug 20:

- `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.18-rocm700-mi35x-20260824` + `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.18-rocm700-mi35x-20260824`

title: [Performance] Tune FlashInfer EXTEND for DP prefill
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

The explicit FlashInfer EXTEND autotune warmup used `max_prefill_tokens`, which remains the global DP token budget in a DP-attention prefill worker. With a global/local chunk size of `32768/8192`, each rank therefore warmed an unrepresentative 32768-token shape instead of its production 8192-token scheduler buffer. The path also skipped speculative PD prefill targets and text-only serving through multimodal generation wrappers, leaving the production FlashInfer MoE EXTEND bucket untuned.

## Modifications

- Size the EXTEND dummy from `max_prefill_buffer_tokens()`, matching the largest buffer one scheduler rank can submit, and fall back to the legacy `max_prefill_tokens` ceiling when chunked prefill is disabled.
- Allow a non-draft PD prefill target to retain the explicitly requested EXTEND mode while preserving the existing skip for ordinary speculative runners.
- Permit the corresponding packed EXTEND shape in `BaseRunner._dummy_run` for a speculative PD prefill target; ordinary speculative targets remain rejected.
- Allow text-only EXTEND warmup for multimodal generation wrappers instead of silently skipping the model.

The feature remains opt-in through `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_EXTEND`.

## Accuracy Tests

A production-shaped, non-simulated GSM8K run completed successfully on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 with speculative decoding, FlashInfer attention, the packed PD-prefill EXTEND contract, and EXTEND autotune enabled: job `3178955`, 200 examples, score `0.985`, mean accepted length `4.4966`, acceptance rate `0.6994`, CUDA graph request fraction `1.0`, zero retracts, and zero error markers.

Two focused CPU regression tests cover the review findings: packed speculative EXTEND is accepted only for a PD prefill target, and disabling chunked prefill falls back to `max_prefill_tokens` instead of silently skipping the explicit autotune opt-in.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The matched A/B used Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 on GB300, one DEP4 prefill worker plus one DEP4 decode worker, RadixCache enabled, HiCache disabled, OSL 1, global/local chunk size `32768/8192`, FlashInfer A2A plus CuteDSL MoE, Breakable CUDA Graph, and the same frozen request manifest. Jobs `3177457` and `3177572` had identical source, backend, topology, cache work, request stream, rank load, and 36/36 cohort contracts; the only runtime difference was enabling `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_EXTEND=1`. All four prefill ranks logged and completed the extra EXTEND autotune pass at 8192 tokens.

| Total concurrency | Before TPS/chip | After TPS/chip | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 25,369.772 | 26,682.219 | +5.173% |
| 8 | 29,105.925 | 30,543.648 | +4.940% |
| 16 | 30,974.960 | 33,070.931 | +6.767% |
| 32 | 32,138.435 | 34,139.581 | +6.227% |
| 64 | 32,204.009 | 34,346.322 | +6.652% |

At the stable saturation points, C32 and C64 had wave CVs of `0.262%` and `0.322%`. The C128 cell measured `32,093.066 -> 33,268.215 TPS/chip` (`+3.662%`) but is intentionally excluded from the performance claim because its candidate wave CV was `3.954%`, above the preregistered `1%` gate, due to one shared execution stall.

title: [NVIDIA] Add CUDA 13.4 container for initial Rubin support
author: trevor-m
body:
## Motivation

[CUDA 13.4 Developer Preview](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/developer-preview/13.4/index.html) provides initial support for Rubin hardware (sm_107). This PR adds a new docker image with CUDA 13.4 for functional Rubin support, which would be built alongside the current cu12 and cu13 containers.

## Modifications

Adds `docker/Dockerfile.cu134` which is based on the standard sglang container Dockerfile, with a few key changes. Use `diff` between both dockerfiles to easily see 13.4 specific changes.
* Base image:`nvidia/cuda` base images for 13.4 are not available yet. Instead, start with ubuntu base and install cuda 13.4 toolkit from the developer preview. Note: There's no 13.4 specific NCCL yet, so install the standard public one.
* Torch 2.15 nightly is required for CUDA 13.4 support. Some hacks are needed to pin this nightly version across various stages of the build.
* `sgl-kernel`, `sgl-deep-gemm`, and `sgl-deep-ep` rely on the torch API for bindings. Since we upgraded to torch 2.15, we need to rebuild these from source. I added an inline build stage for this.
* Torch 2.15 also upgrades the C++ standard from c++17 to c++20, requiring patches in some of the wheel builds and a new config for sgl-kernel.
* Cutedsl 4.6.2 doesn't support sm_107 yet, so target sm_100f for all cutedsl kernels using `CUTE_DSL_ARCH` and `CUTE_EXPERIMENTAL_DSL_ARCH`.
* No flashinfer-jit-cache is released yet for Cuda 13.4, so skip installation. **Expect long startup times for flashinfer kernels**
* Bumps the flashmla commit in `sgl-kernel` to include https://github.com/sgl-project/FlashMLA/commit/15f13e5030374295491c5ce31b02d7e63a7772c6

Also adds a github workflow to build and push the new image.

title: [MegaMoE] Respect padded MXFP8 scale row strides in pre-dispatch
author: merrymercy
body:
Replaces #36007. This branch was rebuilt directly on the latest required `main` commit (`1ec20fd`) because the prior branch was blocked by the CI rebase gate.

## Summary

Update `mega_moe_pre_dispatch` to honor the physical row stride of DeepGEMM's MXFP8 scale output instead of assuming packed rows.

DeepGEMM stores one scale byte per 32 hidden elements and aligns each token row to 16 bytes for TMA:

    logical row bytes  = H / 32
    physical row bytes = align_up(H / 32, 16)

Under DeepGEMM's `H % 128 == 0` layout requirement, padding is needed whenever `H % 512 != 0`:

| H | Logical row | Physical row | Padding |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2176 | 68 B | 80 B | 12 B |
| 2304 | 72 B | 80 B | 8 B |
| 2432 | 76 B | 80 B | 4 B |
| 2560 | 80 B | 80 B | 0 B |

Packed addressing misplaces scale rows after token 0. Once DeepGEMM exposes the correct physical stride, the existing contiguous-tensor check rejects the view instead.

Accept padded row-major scale views, validate their logical width and alignment, and use `buf_x_sf.stride(0)` when addressing each token row. Already-aligned layouts are unchanged.

## Modifications

- Accept row-major scale views with a contiguous inner dimension and a padded outer stride.
- Pass the physical row stride in bytes to the CUDA kernel and use it for each token's scale row.
- Validate the logical row width and the 16-byte alignment required by the DeepGEMM buffer.
- Add a Blackwell regression test that verifies logical scale bytes are written while row padding and unused rows remain unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Ran the focused regression test on an NVIDIA GB300, applying the test to both revisions:

```text
upstream main cce0a1244: FAILED, Tensor is not contiguous as expected
this PR:                 1 passed in 14.44s
```

```bash
python -m pytest -q -s test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_mega_moe_pre_dispatch.py
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run for this upstream commit. The change only replaces the scale-row address calculation and does not change GEMM or dispatch shapes.

## Original commits

- `a5d4e626f513e6b1c37257e2f03e16c9e56252e2`

- [x] Formatted the CUDA and Python changes.
- [x] Added a focused unit test for the padded-stride regression.
- [x] No documentation update is needed for this buffer-layout fix.
- [x] Followed the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [PP] Support prefill CUDA graph proxy tensors
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

Pipeline-parallel prefill could not use the breakable prefill CUDA Graph path because PP stages expose globally indexed attention layers and exchange `PPProxyTensors`, while the graph runner previously assumed a non-PP layer list and rejected proxy inputs and outputs. This leaves genuine small aggregate forwards dominated by launch and control overhead. On Qwen3.5 PP4 with `max_prefill_tokens == chunked_prefill_size == 2048`, the eager path peaked at 34,857 tok/s at concurrency 16.


## Modifications

- Keep attention and companion-layer lists aligned with global layer IDs and evaluate graph eligibility only on the local PP stage.
- Allocate and register stable graph buffers for PP hidden states, residuals, and optional top-k indices, then copy live proxy values into those buffers before replay.
- Pass proxy tensors through the captured stage forward and trim padded proxy outputs back to the real token count.
- Keep PP breakable prefill CUDA Graph explicit opt-in. When enabled, capture actual aggregate forwards up to 8K tokens by default and use eager above that threshold; explicit `max_bs` or `bs` settings still override the default.

This does not change scheduler admission, request grouping, chunk boundaries, or aggregate prefill budgets. A 2K configuration still executes at most 2K aggregate new tokens in one model forward.

## Accuracy Tests

| path | GSM8K score | correct |
|---|---:|---:|
| eager prefill | 0.990 | 198/200 |
| graph prefill | 0.980 | 196/200 |

Both arms used the same 200 GSM8K five-shot chat prompts, 128 threads, `max_tokens=16000`, `temperature=0.6`, `top_p=0.95`, `top_k=20`, and runtime decode seed 42. The captured request payload files were byte-identical. Requests do not carry a sampling seed, so the observed 1.0 percentage-point difference is not treated as an accuracy change.

Targeted CPU tests cover global-layer alignment, stable PP proxy replay inputs (including hidden-only contracts), signature-safe proxy/embed binding, proxy output slicing, PP opt-in policy, and default and explicit capture limits.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### AgentX end-to-end benchmark

The largest matched dual-axis end-to-end gain in the 900-second AgentX screen was at C44 on aggregate TP2 with B3/CG4. The source, model, container, Dynamo and AIPerf commits, MTP, cache policy, routing, chunking, and decode batch and graph caps were fixed. The effective runtime change was eager prefill versus breakable prefill CUDA Graph.

| prefill path | job | Total TPS/GPU | P90 output TPS/user | P50 output TPS/user |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| eager | `3411173` | 42,847.978 | 205.992 | 340.182 |
| breakable CUDA Graph | `3411823` | 48,733.914 | 245.690 | 374.802 |
| change |  | **+13.74%** | **+19.27%** | **+10.18%** |

The eager and graph arms retained 862 and 974 requests with zero request errors. The graph arm had 15 credits still in flight at the phase-end grace timeout; the eager arm had none. These are 900-second screening results, not 3,600-second submission numbers.

### Prefill-only throughput benchmark

Configuration: GB300, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B NVFP4, one TP1×PP4 prefill worker and one TP4 decode worker, 8K ISL, 1 OSL, radix cache off, MTP off, and `max_prefill_tokens == chunked_prefill_size`. Throughput is aggregate input-plus-output tokens per second; all points completed `10 × concurrency` requests with exact 8192/1 token lengths and zero request errors.

Each concurrency cell is `eager → graph` tok/s. Both paths use the same source and differ only in `cuda-graph-backend-prefill=disabled/breakable`.

| aggregate cap | C16 | C32 | C64 | C128 | C256 | eager peak | graph peak | peak change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2K | 34,857 → 86,476 | 34,852 → 86,561 | 33,274 → 86,433 | 33,942 → 86,100 | 33,660 → 85,912 | 34,857 @ C16 | 86,561 @ C32 | **2.48× / +148.33%** |
| 4K | 65,670 → 127,903 | 66,194 → 126,598 | 65,977 → 127,942 | 64,931 → 127,732 | 64,909 → 127,804 | 66,194 @ C32 | 127,942 @ C64 | **1.93× / +93.28%** |
| 8K | 131,807 → 146,105 | 131,714 → 149,428 | 134,906 → 150,121 | 131,560 → 151,261 | 131,703 → 151,349 | 134,906 @ C64 | 151,349 @ C256 | **1.12× / +12.19%** |
| 16K | 129,637 → 115,657 | 174,196 → 169,433 | 177,064 → 171,809 | 178,023 → 173,620 | 177,080 → 174,068 | 178,023 @ C128 | 174,068 @ C256 | **0.98× / -2.22%** |
| 32K | 94,412 → 74,474 | 143,688 → 124,359 | 186,020 → 177,690 | 186,828 → 180,068 | 186,224 → 181,276 | 186,828 @ C128 | 181,276 @ C256 | **0.97× / -2.97%** |

The benefit is concentrated in small forwards, so PP uses breakable prefill CUDA Graph only when the backend is selected explicitly. Its default capture limit is 8K actual aggregate tokens, the last measured size with a positive peak result; larger forwards automatically use eager. Operators can override the limit with `--cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill` or explicit capture buckets. Fixed-2K peak rises from 18.66% of eager 32K peak to 47.75% of graph 32K peak, a 2.56× recovery of the relative small-batch throughput.

At matched C64, fixed 2K improves from 33,274 to 86,433 tok/s, or 2.60×. The graph sweep logged 95,596 full 2K forwards as graph replays and zero as eager; no forward exceeded the 2K aggregate cap.

### Stage profiling

| PP rank | eager `run_batch` median | graph `run_batch` median | eager kernel busy/step | graph kernel busy/step |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 73.06 ms | 19.82 ms | 18.56 ms | 18.34 ms |
| 1 | 75.24 ms | 21.29 ms | 17.40 ms | 17.19 ms |
| 2 | 73.86 ms | 20.10 ms | 16.29 ms | 16.20 ms |
| 3 | 56.12 ms | 16.27 ms | 12.23 ms | 12.15 ms |

The graph reduces stage wall time by 71–73% while kernel busy time stays within 1.2%, consistent with removing launch and control bubbles without changing model compute. In the common trace window, average kernel-active GPUs increased from 0.709/4 to 2.009/4. Profiler overhead affects cadence, so throughput numbers come only from unprofiled runs.

title: [Mamba] Warm cache COW kernel before serving
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

The first fused Mamba cache copy-on-write operation can pay Triton compilation cost on the serving path, inflating the first cache-hit wave.

## Modifications

- Warm the fused slot-copy kernel while the Mamba pool is initialized.
- Use the reserved dummy slot as the source and one free slot as the destination, only when fused slot operations are enabled and at least two slots exist.
- Add a focused mock test for the warmup helper.
