title: [Performance] Optimize Qwen3.5 GDN prefill projection layouts
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

Qwen3.5 GDN prefill materializes QKV/Z/B/A projection slices early, then performs separate Q/K/V layout copies before FlashInfer prefill. These data-movement kernels are material at long cached-prefix prefill sizes.

## Modifications

- Keep QKV, Z, B, and A as strided projection views for CUDA non-speculative extend.
- Teach gated RMSNorm to consume the 3D strided Z view directly.
- Reuse already-contiguous Q/K/V from the CUDA fused split; materialize only strided inputs before the existing L2Norm kernels for FlashInfer prefill.
- Preserve the input dtype in the fused prepare path and restrict the projection-view fast path to CUDA.
- Add focused BF16/FP16 tests for projection views, QKV preparation, dtype preservation, strided gated norm, and the production fused-split-to-FlashInfer chain.

## Accuracy Tests

| Configuration | Job | GSM8K score | Samples | Mean speculative accept length | Graph request fraction | Runtime errors / retracts |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| With GDN layout | `3154788` | `0.990` | 200 | `4.527011` | `1.0` | `0 / 0` |
| With GDN layout in the final combined configuration | `3178955` | `0.985` | 200 | `4.4966` | `1.0` | `0 / 0` |

Both runs used non-simulated five-shot GSM8K normal generation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### AgentX cache-on workload

AgentX cache-on A/B from jobs `3177414 -> 3177457`: identical manifest, request stream, actual cached/new work, rank load, and 36/36 exactly-once cohorts.

| Global concurrency | Without GDN layout | With GDN layout | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | `24,122.423` | `25,369.772` | `+5.171%` |
| 8 | `27,587.790` | `29,105.925` | `+5.503%` |
| 16 | `29,825.887` | `30,974.960` | `+3.853%` |
| 32 | `30,627.018` | `32,138.435` | `+4.935%` |
| 64 | `30,803.719` | `32,204.009` | `+4.546%` |
| 128 | `30,831.462` | `32,093.066` | `+4.092%` |

Matched `prefix=57,344`, `new=8,192` profiling:

| Profile metric | Without GDN layout | With GDN layout | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GDN layout time | `15.185688 ms` | `2.760650 ms` | `-81.821%` |
| GPU union, with the MoE fix present in both arms | `250.885729 ms` | `240.355773 ms` | `-4.197%` |
| GPU union versus matched TRT | `241.837455 ms` (TRT) | `240.355773 ms` (SGLang candidate) | SGLang `-0.613%` |

The comparison isolates the GDN layout change while keeping the workload and execution contract fixed.

### Kernel microbenchmark and profiling

Contiguous-input reuse was validated on GB300 with the production `fused_qkv_split_gdn_prefill -> gdn_prefill_qkv_prepare_fwd` chain. Job `3291878` used BF16 Qwen3.5 local dimensions `T=8192`, `H_QK=4`, `H_V=16`, `D=128`, with 50 warmup iterations and medians over nine repeats of 100 iterations.

| Production-path metric | Without contiguous reuse | With contiguous reuse | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FlashInfer QKV prepare | `0.105018 ms` | `0.067229 ms` | `1.562x` (`-35.98%`) |
| Fused split + FlashInfer prepare | `0.135026 ms` | `0.098273 ms` | `1.374x` (`-27.22%`) |

Nsight Systems job `3291970` confirms the structural result over 100 full-chain iterations: `gdn_prefill_qkv_prepare_kernel` drops from 100 calls to 0, while fused split remains at 100 calls and Q/K L2Norm remains at 200 calls. The redundant V copy is removed by reusing fused-split storage.

### Static workload E2E

A clean same-node E2E A/B from job `3293694` compares base `67853c580482dbc9b69aad5022a0cdd3a1606570` with candidate `09173bc2619ccc678533e54ff7c9b1a91c11a08a`. Both arms use Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4-V2 on one GB300 node with TP4, exact `ISL=8192` / `OSL=1`, seed 42, radix cache disabled, and 32,768 aggregate prefill tokens. C32/C128 use 64/256 warmup requests followed by 96/384 formal requests.

| Concurrency | Base input tok/s | Candidate input tok/s | Throughput change | Mean E2E change | Successful requests |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 | `100,392` | `102,139` | `+1.74%` | `-1.73%` | `96/96` |
| 128 | `100,595` | `102,126` | `+1.52%` | `-1.50%` | `384/384` |

All formal requests completed without errors, and server logs confirm that the 32,768-token prefill batches used the breakable CUDA graph. Reported prefill graph capture memory also decreased from `6.20 GB` to `5.88 GB` per TP rank (`-5.16%`).

title: [AMD][CI] Pass USE_PDL explicitly in the fused MoE gate
author: bingxche
body: ## Motivation Fixes #35348, `test_torch_compile_moe.py` in [stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-rocm720 (linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang, 0)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32367546070/job/96420375810#logs) ROCm 7.2.4 with torch 2.11 and AMD Triton 3.7 fails while capturing Qwen1.5-MoE with torch.compile: TypeError: launcher() missing 1 required positional argument: '_grid_2' On HIP, PDL is unsupported, so the fused gate launch omitted the default constexpr USE_PDL=False. The newer compile stack produces inconsistent launcher metadata when that constexpr is omitted. ## Modifications - Compute PDL support once. - Always pass USE_PDL explicitly to the fused gate kernel. - Continue passing launch_pdl only on PDL-capable architectures. ROCm 7.0 and older ROCm 7.2 stacks still execute with USE_PDL=False; CUDA PDL behavior is unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests - Targeted ROCm 7.2.4 stage: [run 32832700890](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32832700890) passed . ## Speed Tests and Profiling No performance change is expected. The generated specialization remains USE_PDL=False on ROCm and retains the existing PDL-enabled path on supported CUDA architectures. ## Checklist - [x] Format checked with git diff --check. - [x] Existing registered integration test covers the failing model path. - [x] Documentation is not applicable for this internal compiler-compatibility fix. - [ ] ROCm 7.2.4 GPU CI passes. - [x] Change is limited to the directly failing kernel launch. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #32864597889](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32864597889) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32864595138](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32864595138) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :x: [Run #32864600377](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32864600377)

title: [AMD][Bugfix] Skip invalid fused MoE reduction for direct top-1 output
author: bingxche
body: ## Motivation ROCm 7.2.4 [stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd (rocm724, linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang, 7)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32725797196/job/97426719871#logs) fails `TestFusedMOE.test_single_expert_routing` for `topk=1` and `routed_scaling_factor=1.0`. In this path, the second GEMM writes directly to `out_hidden_states`, so `intermediate_cache3` is not populated. The HIP epilogue nevertheless reduces `intermediate_cache3` into the output, overwriting the valid result with uninitialized data. CUDA and XPU already skip the reduction under the same conditions. ## Modifications Add the existing CUDA/XPU direct-output guard to the HIP epilogue. The change is limited to `topk == 1`, unit routed scaling, and the no-intermediate path. title: [Spec][DSA] Add --speculative-dsa-topk-backend
author: zianglih
body:
## Motivation
@humansand

- **Scope:** Split DSA indexer top-k selection between the target model and
  speculative draft workers.
- `--dsa-topk-backend` currently reaches both roles because target and draft
  runners share one `ServerArgs`. A target override such as `flashinfer`
  therefore also changes repeated MTP draft top-k.
- Add `--speculative-dsa-topk-backend`, defaulting to `sgl-kernel`, so the
  draft stays on the usual fast path unless it is explicitly overridden.
- Default launches are unchanged. To use the same non-default backend for both
  roles, pass both selectors.

## Modifications

- Keep `--dsa-topk-backend` as the target-model selector.
- Add `--speculative-dsa-topk-backend` for speculative draft workers with the
  same `sgl-kernel`, `torch`, and `flashinfer` choices and a
  `sgl-kernel` default.
- Resolve the backend per runner from the post-publish config namespaces:
  - target: `exec.kernel.dsa_topk_backend`;
  - draft: `spec.speculative_dsa_topk_backend`.
- Use the common resolver in both `DeepseekSparseAttnBackend` (DSA/GLM) and
  `DeepseekV4AttnBackend` without mutating the shared `ServerArgs`.
- Make the existing DSA test runners explicit target workers so their mocks
  satisfy the same role contract as production `ModelRunner`.
- Document the independent selector in the server-argument and speculative
  decoding references, including the DSA MTP path and FlashInfer environment
  switches.
- **Compatibility:** Existing launches that set only
  `--dsa-topk-backend=<non-default>` now apply that override only to the
  target. Pass the new flag as well to restore the previous target/draft
  pairing.
- **Non-goals:** No kernel implementation changes. `SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK`,
  `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2`, and the FlashInfer deterministic/tie-break
  settings remain process-wide. Selecting `torch` for either role still
  requires `SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK=false`, which disables fused top-k for both
  roles.

title: [diffusion] perf: fuse tanh-GELU into the LongCat-Image DiT FFN up-proj
author: ITerydh
body:
## Motivation
  
The LongCat-Image DiT runs tanh-GELU as a separate op after its FFN up-projection GEMM, in both the dual-stream FFN (`ff` / `ff_context`) and the single-stream block's `proj_mlp`. sglang already ships the AOT cublasLt `linear_gelu_tanh` epilogue that folds bias-add and tanh-GELU into the GEMM (used today by FLUX.1, Qwen-Image, GLM-Image, LTX-2, HunyuanVideo), but LongCat never marked its sites, so the fusion could not engage. These sites execute 4000 times per generation on LongCat-Image-Edit (50 steps x 80 sites), which makes the standalone activation a measurable slice of denoise time.
   
This PR wires LongCat-Image into that existing mechanism.

## Modifications

Single file, `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/longcat_image.py`:
- `_LongCatFFN.__init__`: `mark_fused_gelu_site(self.net[0], "proj")`, covering `ff` and `ff_context` in every dual-stream block. The marked module is the `ModuleDict` that holds `proj` in `_modules`, so `getattr` resolves it for the fusion helper.
- `_LongCatFFN.forward`: take `fused_linear_gelu_tanh` when `fused_gelu_active()` and `can_use_linear_gelu()` both hold; otherwise fall back to the original `proj` + `nn.GELU(approximate="tanh")` chain, unchanged.
- `_SingleTransformerBlock.__init__` / `.forward`: the same treatment for `proj_mlp` / `act_mlp`.
No kernel, gate, or mount code is touched. `mount_fused_linear_gelu` `unmount_fused_linear_gelu` in the denoising stage already discover marked sites at batch boundaries, all-or-nothing per transformer, and `quality` already participates in the dynamic-batch signature.

## Speed Tests and Profiling
Same case (LongCat-Image-Edit, A800, 50 steps, seed 42). The GELU region was measured with temporary instrumentation bracketing "up-proj GEMM + tanh-GELU", removed before submitting:

| Config | GELU region (50-step total) | Per call | vs baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lossless` (un-fused) | 9638 ms | 2.410 ms | - |
| `high` (fused) | 9044 ms | 2.261 ms | -594 ms / -6.2% |

- 4000 calls per generation (50 steps x 80 sites); two repeats, variance < 0.2%.                                                                                                                                            
- The GELU region itself is 6.2% faster, saving 0.148 ms per call.

End-to-end denoise, 5 runs per config:

| Config | Denoise (mean) | vs baseline |                                                                                                                                                                                   
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lossless` | 45.496 s | - |
| `high` | 44.812 s | -0.68 s / -1.50% |
                       
## Checklist
- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). No new kernel is introduced; the site mechanism is already covered by `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_sites.py`.
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). The mechanism and the `--quality` switch are documented in `docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/fused_kernels.mdx`; happy to add a LongCat-Image row to its per-model coverage table if reviewers prefer.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [NPU]Strip padding before FIA kernel for vision encoder padded sequences
author: Estrella-xx

title: [AMD] Optimize Qwen3.5 MTP unified attention on gfx950
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

Qwen3.5 target verification on MI355X uses a short multi-token query (`max_seqlen_q <= 4`) with 16 query heads, one KV head, head size 256, page size 16, and FP8 KV cache. AITER's generic 3D unified-attention configuration processes one query token per workgroup and reloads the same paged KV data for each speculative token, leaving this latency-sensitive path substantially slower than the comparison implementation.

## Modifications

- Add an SGLang-owned Triton 3D unified-attention kernel and segment-reduction kernel specialized for the measured gfx950 Qwen3.5 MTP shape.
- Process two speculative query tokens per workgroup with `BLOCK_M=32` and `BLOCK_Q=2`, reusing each loaded KV tile across both tokens.
- Use `TILE_SIZE=32` and select 8-64 segments using both CU parallelism and per-segment KV work.
- Dispatch to the specialized kernel only for gfx950, BF16 query, FP8 KV, 16 query heads, one KV head, head size 256, page size 16, non-sliding attention, and no softcap or attention sinks. All other shapes retain the existing AITER path.
- Add an AMD unit test comparing the SGLang kernel against AITER for mixed speculative query lengths.

## Accuracy Tests
IL70000 / OL300: gsm8k
| Validation | Result |
|---|---|
| End-to-end accuracy | 0.927 |
| End-to-end invalid rate | 0.003 |

GPQA (`/raid/models/amd-Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4`, 198 questions, repeat 8)
| Validation | Result |
|---|---|
| Mean score | 0.879 |
| Reference ([Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B)) | 0.884 |
| Output throughput | 714.3 token/s |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

MI355X microbenchmark configuration: batch 20, query length 4, 16 query heads, one KV head, head size 256, page size 16, BF16 query, and FP8 KV cache. Values are kernel-path latency measured with `triton.testing.do_bench` after warmup.

| KV length | AITER baseline | SGLang optimized | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8,192 | 117.5 us | 51.3 us | 2.29x |
| 40,960 | 367.5 us | 186.4 us | 1.97x |
| 89,088 | 684.1 us | 347.6 us | 1.97x |

Decode-phase trace at input length 70,000. Before is `kernel_unified_attention_3d` (`TILE_SIZE=16`, `NUM_SEGMENTS=128`); after is `qwen35_mtp_unified_attention_3d` (`TILE_SIZE=32`, `NUM_SEGMENTS=64`).

| Measurement | Concurrency 4 (us) | Concurrency 64 (us) |
|---|---|---|
| Attention kernel, per layer | 137.4 -> 85.9 (-37.5%) | 140.3 -> 86.5 (-38.3%) |
| Decode total | 12,218 -> 11,285 (-7.6%) | 12,146 -> 11,043 (-9.1%) |

The 51.5 us and 53.8 us saved per layer, across the 15 attention layers on this path, show up as a 933 us and 1,103 us drop in total decode time.

End-to-end serving on MI355X, TP2, input length 70,000 and output length 300 (`tok/s/gpu` is `total tok/s` divided by 2):

| Concurrency | Median E2E (ms) | Total tok/s | tok/s/gpu | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|

title: feat(kv-cache): support SM100 NVFP4 GenMHA and speculative decoding
author: samuellees
body:
# SM100 Native NVFP4 KV Cache

Part of #29913.

## What this implements

- Native packed NVFP4 KV-cache prefill and decode on SM100/SM103 through TRT-LLM GenMHA.
- An optional FlashInfer prefill path that dequantizes the stored FP4 cache into a shared FP8 E4M3 workspace.
- Eager/CUDA Graph execution, normal decode, top-k-1 EAGLE/EAGLE3/NEXTN, and breadth-1 NGRAM.
- FlashInfer NVFP4 quantization plus a fused incremental slot-scatter kernel that writes GenMHA K/V scale layouts directly.

Main modules touched: argument resolution, NVFP4 quantization/storage and KV-pool sizing, FlashInfer/TRT-LLM attention integration, and registered SM100 unit/E2E tests.

## Options

```bash
--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4
--prefill-kv-cache-dequant-dtype {auto,nvfp4,fp8_e4m3}
```

- `nvfp4`: TRT-LLM GenMHA consumes packed FP4 directly during prefill, with no additional dequantization.
- `fp8_e4m3`: FlashInfer dequantizes FP4 into an FP8 prefill workspace.
- `auto`: selects `nvfp4` on SM100 and `fp8_e4m3` on SM120.

The stored cache and decode input remain NVFP4 in every mode. Here `nvfp4` explicitly means that prefill reads the native packed cache without any additional dequantization.

## KV layout

- Packed K/V stays slot-major: `[slot, head, head_dim / 2]`; GenMHA reads it through a strided HND view without a data copy.
- Native scales use `[num_pages, num_heads, page_size, head_dim / 16]`.
- K scales are token-linear. V scales use GenMHA four-token interleave: `(t, s) -> ((t // 4) * 4 + s // G, (s % G) * 4 + t % 4)`, where `G = (head_dim / 16) / 4`.
- Native prefill requires `page_size % 4 == 0`, `head_dim % 64 == 0`, and page-aligned KV-pool rows.

## Performance

GB300, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8, TP4, batch 1, 1M input tokens, 128 output tokens; medians of three runs. Parentheses show speedup over FP8 KV for the same stage and mode.

| Mode | Prefill: FP8 KV | Prefill: FP4 + FP8 DQ | Prefill: native FP4 | Decode: FP8 KV | Decode: FP4/FP8-DQ | Decode: native FP4 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| MTP off | 13.3608 s (1.000x) | 82.2351 s (0.162x) | 14.8440 s (0.900x) | 0.5065 s (1.000x) | 0.4945 s (1.024x) | 0.4860 s (1.042x) |
| MTP on | 14.1005 s (1.000x) | 83.4245 s (0.169x) | 15.8238 s (0.891x) | 0.2278 s (1.000x) | 0.2431 s (0.937x) | 0.2481 s (0.918x) |

At 1M context, native FP4 improves the non-MTP q_len=1 attention kernel by 1.355x and the full decode phase by 1.042x. The MTP q_len=4 target-verification kernel is not performance-positive yet. Native NVFP4 reduces MHA KV bytes/token by 43.75% versus FP8, giving 1.778x FP8 KV-token capacity.

## Accuracy

Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, EAGLE top-k-1 with four draft tokens:

| Evaluation | FP8 KV | FP4 + FP8 prefill | Native FP4 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K, 8-shot | 0.979405 | 0.977117 | 0.978642 |
| GPQA Diamond, 8-pass mean | 0.830177 | 0.829545 | 0.821970 |
| AIME26, 24-pass mean | 0.925000 | 0.912500 | 0.916667 |
| SWE-bench Verified, 3-pass mean | 0.358000 | 0.370000 | 0.350000 |

## Validation

- SM100 review suite: 22 CPU tests + 19 registered subtests, and 170 GPU tests passed.
- Registered Qwen3.5-9B TP4 E2E: 200 GSM8K examples, 8-shot, MTP on/off and both prefill paths; all four cases passed.

| Mode | Prefill path | GSM8K | Mean accepted length |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| MTP off | Native FP4 | 0.900 | N/A |
| MTP off | FP8 DQ | 0.905 | N/A |
| MTP on | Native FP4 | 0.905 | 3.5032 |
| MTP on | FP8 DQ | 0.885 | 3.5055 |

- Ruff, isort, compile, registered-test checks, CUDA Graph, and speculative decoding coverage passed.

title: [AMD][Diffusion] Migrate FlyDSL fused norm kernels to the v0.3.0 stable API
author: yctseng0211
body:
## Motivation

Migrate FlyDSL fused norm kernels to the v0.3.0 stable API, this migration is required for upcoming AITER/FlyDSL versions: the current code depends on non-public FlyDSL internals that already broke once, and when they break again the kernels silently fall back to `forward_native`.

Rebase of #33144 onto the post-#35114 layout: the kernel now lives at norm/fused_residual_norm_flydsl.py and #34536's import fallback is dropped, since the capability guard supersedes it.

Co-authored-by: Phil Li <haicli@amd.com>
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->


### FlyDSL 0.3 API migration

v0.3.0 both removed `flydsl.expr.buffer_ops` (the upstream kernel carries an aiter fallback for exactly this) and introduced FlyDSL's stability contract, [`docs/api_stability.md`](https://github.com/ROCm/FlyDSL/blob/v0.3.0/docs/api_stability.md), which is absent at v0.2.4. Under that contract the rest of the old imports are unstable too: §2.4 covers `flydsl._mlir.*`, underscore-prefixed names, and direct upstream-MLIR dialect calls; §2.2 excludes deep `flydsl.compiler.*` paths such as `kernel_function.CompilationContext`. None of it appears in the §3 deprecation table, so none of it was protected.

Each replacement is documented at the v0.3.0 tag:

| before | after | reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `buffer_ops.create_buffer_resource` / `buffer_load` / `buffer_store` / `_unwrap_value` | `fx.rocdl.make_buffer_tensor`, `fx.make_copy_atom(fx.rocdl.BufferCopy128b(), ...)`, `fx.memref_load_vec` | [authoring §4.3](https://github.com/ROCm/FlyDSL/blob/v0.3.0/docs/kernel_authoring_guide.md), [layout §9](https://github.com/ROCm/FlyDSL/blob/v0.3.0/docs/layout_system_guide.md) |
| LDS via `_memref.ViewOp` / `StoreOp` / `LoadOp` | `@fx.struct` + `fx.SharedAllocator`, `fx.memref_load` / `_store` | [authoring §6.1](https://github.com/ROCm/FlyDSL/blob/v0.3.0/docs/kernel_authoring_guide.md) |
| `_gpu.ShuffleOp(..., mode=ShuffleMode.XOR)` | `fx.gpu.shuffle_xor(x, offset, width)` | [api_stability §3](https://github.com/ROCm/FlyDSL/blob/v0.3.0/docs/api_stability.md) |
| `math_ops.RsqrtOp`, `arith_ops.*`, `scf.IfOp` | `fx.math.rsqrt`, plain Python operators and `if` | [arithmetic_types](https://github.com/ROCm/FlyDSL/blob/v0.3.0/docs/language/arithmetic_types.md) |
| `CompilationContext` | dropped; `@flyc.jit` owns compilation | [authoring §1.1](https://github.com/ROCm/FlyDSL/blob/v0.3.0/docs/kernel_authoring_guide.md) |


## Accuracy and Speed Tests 

### e2e validation on WAN2.2 T2V-A14B

Ran the rebased kernel end-to-end against WAN2.2; no regression.

**Environment**

- Image: `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.18-rocm700-mi35x-20260824`
- Single MI355X (gfx950), FlyDSL 0.3.1
- A/B method: only `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/norm/fused_residual_norm_flydsl.py` was swapped between the upstream-main version and this PR's version. Everything else in the tree is identical, and both runs used a warm torch.compile cache.

**Command**

```bash
export SGLANG_USE_ROCM_FLYDSL=1
export SGLANG_USE_ROCM_VAE_CONV2D_BF16=1
export SGLANG_DIFFUSION_AITER_FP8_ATTN=1

sglang generate \
  --model-path /models/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers \
  --prompt "A cat and a dog baking a cake together in a kitchen. The cat is carefully measuring flour, while the dog is stirring the batter with a wooden spoon. The kitchen is cozy, with sunlight streaming through the window." \
  --negative-prompt " " \
  --720p --num-frames 193 --num-inference-steps 8 --seed 42 \
  --num-gpus 1 \
  --dit-layerwise-offload true --dit-cpu-offload false \
  --vae-cpu-offload false --text-encoder-cpu-offload true \
  --warmup-mode request --enable-torch-compile true
```

**Result** (from `[DenoisingStage] average time per step`)

| kernel | s/step | denoising total |
|---|---|---|
| upstream main | 31.026 | 260.90 s |
| this PR | 30.922 | 260.96 s |
| upstream main (repeat) | 30.937 | 261.12 s |

The two upstream runs differ by 0.29%, so this PR's 0.05% delta sits inside run-to-run noise. The full pipeline finished with no GPU faults and the decoded video was written normally.

A microbenchmark at the shapes WAN2.2 actually uses (LayerNorm, seq 176400, dim 5120, `elementwise_affine=False` for `norm1`/`norm_out`) agrees: the total time these kernels spend per DiT forward goes from 147.8 ms to 147.1 ms.

**Output quality**

Both upstream main and this PR produce a byte-identical video at seed 42 (720p, 193 frames, 8 steps):

| run | md5 |
|---|---|
| upstream main | `4959325aeb967ce0dcfd6bce405a271f` |
| upstream main (repeat) | `4959325aeb967ce0dcfd6bce405a271f` |
| this PR | `4959325aeb967ce0dcfd6bce405a271f` |

The two upstream runs matching each other confirms the pipeline is deterministic under a fixed seed, so this is a meaningful comparison rather than a coincidence: the kernel rewrite changes nothing in the generated output.

This is consistent with the numerics checks at the lower levels — the 22 kernel unit tests pass against the reference implementations, and at the layer level `forward_hip` matches `forward_native` to within bf16 tolerance (max abs diff 0.125).



Note: e2e was run on the rocm700 image because torch.compile currently core dumps on the rocm720 image for unrelated reasons.

title: fix(lora): build the MoE LoRA align JIT kernel on ROCm
author: Arist12
body:
## Problem

`moe_lora_align_block_size` is JIT-compiled, and the JIT build does not run hipify. On ROCm the kernel therefore fails to compile: `cub/cub.cuh` does not exist, `cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin` / `cudaFuncSetAttribute` / `cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize` have no HIP spellings in the JIT tree, and `hipFuncSetAttribute` takes a `const void *` rather than a function pointer.

MoE LoRA inference reaches this kernel from `_compute_lora_alignment`, so serving a MoE model with a LoRA adapter on ROCm aborts on the first such forward:

```
python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/lora/moe_lora_align_kernel.cu:9:10: fatal error: 'cub/cub.cuh' file not found
```

## Change

On ROCm, include hipCUB, alias `cub` to `hipcub`, and map the three attribute spellings to HIP — all local to `moe_lora_align_kernel.cu`. The kernel is passed as `const void *` through `std::bit_cast`, matching `setup_kernel_smem_once` in `deepseek_v4/topk_v1.cuh`. CUDA keeps CUB and the same call contract.

The aliases are deliberately *not* added to `sgl_kernel/utils.cuh`. A JIT cache leaf is keyed on the content of its transitive dependency closure, and `utils.cuh` is in the closure of essentially every module (140 of the 190 JIT sources include it directly, the rest transitively via `tensor.h`). Editing it invalidates the whole cache. Measured on MI355X against a warm cache, appending a single comment to `utils.cuh` took three unrelated kernel tests from 5 s / 7 s / 5 s to 14 s / 89 s / 10 s; editing only `moe_lora_align_kernel.cu` left them at 5 s / 7 s / 5 s. That is what made an earlier revision of this PR time out `jit-kernel-unit-test` and `base-b-test-1-gpu-large` against the 30-minute step budget.

`test_moe_lora_align_block_size.py` is also registered for AMD CI. It was CUDA-only, so no job compiled this kernel on ROCm and the build break it fixes could not be caught.

## Validation

MI355X (`gfx950`), ROCm 7.2, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x-20260826`:

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_moe_lora_align_block_size.py`: 32 passed from a cold JIT cache, in 27 s. The same suite is 32 failed on the base commit, on `cub/cub.cuh` not found.
- Qwen3-30B-A3B served with a rank-32 adapter over all attention and expert projections (`lora_backend=triton`, `moe_runner_backend=triton`) loads and generates. On the base commit the same configuration aborts in `_compute_lora_alignment` with the error above.

title: Support speculative decoding with unified SWA memory
author: ZYHowell
body:
## Motivation

Unified-memory hybrid-SWA targets need speculative draft pools to address the target allocator's full virtual-ID range even when the SWA pool has a smaller physical capacity. Without this, draft KV allocation and locked-node SWA recovery can use inconsistent mappings or under-size the shared pool.

## Modifications

- Separate virtual-page capacity from physical-page capacity for non-owner unified allocators.
- Size speculative draft pools from the shared virtual-ID span and register identity mappings when draft SWA layers consume those IDs directly.
- Preserve SWA page bindings while recovering locked full-attention entries.
- Account for target and draft allocations together when sizing unified hybrid-SWA pools.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable; this changes KV-pool allocation and mapping rather than model numerics.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run; no kernel or model-forward changes.

title: Fix Kimi-K3 MLA output gate dispatch on non-CUDA devices
author: xuzijian629
body:
## Motivation

The fused Kimi-K3 MLA output gate is implemented as a CUDA JIT kernel, but its eligibility check only excluded NPU. Other non-CUDA devices could therefore select the CUDA implementation and attempt to compile or load CUDA sources instead of using the existing PyTorch fallback.

## Modifications

- Require both input tensors to be CUDA tensors before selecting the fused MLA output-gate kernel.
- Remove the NPU-specific eligibility check.
- Add a CPU regression test verifying that non-CUDA tensors use the fallback path.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. This does not change the CUDA kernel or its numerical behavior. Unsupported devices now select the existing PyTorch fallback instead of attempting to use the CUDA kernel.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. The CUDA execution path is unchanged. This only corrects kernel eligibility on non-CUDA devices.

title: [Perf] Optimize Qwen3-VL unique-image serving on H100
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

The target traffic is one-pass streaming: an image is normally processed once and is not seen again. The previous cache-hot version automatically reserved 16 GiB for preprocessing artifacts plus 8 GiB for multimodal embeddings, which wasted memory and hid preprocessing, feature-transport, and scheduling costs.

This revision keeps preprocessing and embedding retention disabled for unique-image traffic, retains the request-local Qwen3-VL fast path, and removes the remaining per-image CUDA IPC reconstruction copy. After the review fixes and current-main merge, the refreshed three-run median is **68.551 requests/s**. The historical vLLM median under the same workload is **61.657 requests/s**, so the refreshed SGLang result is **+11.18%**.

## What changed

- Build request-local Qwen3-VL image artifacts without preprocessing-cache lookup, single-flight state, or retention. The fast path directly produces prompt IDs, image offsets, and M-RoPE metadata.
- Cache only normalized chat-template rendering/tokenization metadata in a bounded 128-entry LRU.
- Skip raw prompt tokenization when the Qwen-VL processor produces the final expanded input IDs.
- Split the reusable prompt KV boundary from the generated suffix and prioritize the prompt node in radix eviction.
- Keep high-concurrency decode inside CUDA graph, use stock FlashInfer decode/page size 1, and use the profiled prefill/decode interval 22.
- Reserve eager-prefill activation headroom independently of embedding-cache retention.
- Defer CUDA IPC feature reconstruction for single-GPU Qwen3-VL. When an entire image is consumed by the current prefill chunk, the ViT borrows a zero-copy view of the bounded IPC pool and acknowledges it on the CUDA stream after reads are enqueued. Multi-GPU, cross-chunk, cache-hit, uncached-handle, and failure paths keep the existing copy/ack behavior.
- For the profiled large-Hopper configuration (`max_running_requests >= 400`, no preprocessing/embedding retention), increase the bounded IPC pool from 1 GiB to 3 GiB.

Automatic serving defaults remain restricted to Qwen3-VL/Qwen3-VL-MoE on SM90 GPUs with at least 60 GiB. Explicit cache, transport, attention, interval, CUDA-graph, IPC-pool, and radix-eviction choices remain authoritative.

## Review follow-up fixes

The branch now includes the following merge-readiness fixes and regressions:

- Mark `prefill_decode_interval`, `radix_eviction_policy`, `mm_preprocess_cache_size_mb`, and `mm_feature_transport` as valid model-resolvable fields. This fixes the startup failure reported by DoorDash.
- Preserve an explicit `--radix-eviction-policy lru`, including CLI `--flag=value` and YAML configuration; `priority` is applied only when the option is omitted.
- Do not load Hugging Face model configuration from the decode-graph memory hook when GPU-memory information is unavailable.
- Add coverage for the Qwen3-VL override contract, chat-template cache isolation, request-local media artifacts, CUDA IPC one-shot borrowing, and prompt-prefix KV retention in both legacy and unified radix caches.

The final diff against `main` modifies 18 implementation files and 7 test files.

## Reproduction

### Environment

- Final PR head: `00a555c5dadd11fbc6b27842dd2e896898a75060`
- Merged `main`: `12735c2d7684647454efb033a143cad92bfd305a`
- GPU: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, TP=1
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`
- Model revision: `ebb281ec70b05090aa6165b016eac8ec08e71b17`
- Validation base image: `lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:4c44c95626c7601f19259266342341976e848f835fbe33ebb4b09a28dff3063c`
- Dependency overlay: FlashInfer Python/cubins 0.6.18, JIT cache 0.6.18+cu130, CUTLASS 4.6.2, QuACK 0.6.4

The candidate source was bind-mounted into the validation container. The dependency overlay is recorded here explicitly; the CI image from this pushed head should be used as the single-digest external reproduction image.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3 \
taskset -c 0-31,64-95 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct \
  --revision ebb281ec70b05090aa6165b016eac8ec08e71b17 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31000 \
  --enable-metrics \
  --max-running-requests 400 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 65536 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.95 \
  --context-length 4096 \
  --tp-size 1
```

Resolved Qwen3-VL/Hopper defaults were preprocessing cache 0 MiB, CUDA IPC feature transport with a 3 GiB pool, priority radix eviction, prefill/decode interval 22, FA3 prefill, FlashInfer decode, and decode CUDA graph max batch 400.

### Workload

- deterministic performance-equivalent surrogate with 1,200 distinct synthetic shelf-tag JPEGs plus 16 separate warm-up images;
- 600 images at 512x480 and 600 at 512x512, median 248 merged vision tokens;
- manifest SHA-256: `d92eebbe2ac9bc3421e68ac09a1db3e9c60c1a7faff8e209ef8599e32e100c8f`;
- 5,178-character shared text prefix before the image;
- streaming OpenAI chat, concurrency 373;
- `max_completion_tokens=256`, `temperature=0.1`, `repetition_penalty=1.1`, EOS enabled;
- fresh server and 16-image warm-up before each measured stream;
- GPU process snapshots empty before launch and after shutdown.

This surrogate matches the documented vision shapes but is not DoorDash's private production corpus.

## End-to-end performance

| Engine / snapshot | Requests/s | Wall time | Completed / fields present | Median TTFT | Output tokens |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Historical SGLang before PR | 57.090 | 21.020 s | 1,200 / 1,200 | 2.620 s | 128,268 |
| Historical PR before one-shot IPC borrowing | 66.104 median | 18.153 s | 1,200 / 1,200 | 1.323 s | — |
| Historical vLLM median | 61.657 | 19.463 s | 1,200 / 1,200 | 0.378 s | — |
| Original PR report median | 69.925 | 17.161 s | 1,200 / 1,200 | 1.304 s | — |
| Refreshed SGLang run 1 | 68.143 | 17.610 s | 1,200 / 1,200 | 1.301 s | 128,264 |
| Refreshed SGLang run 2 | 68.551 | 17.505 s | 1,200 / 1,200 | 1.310 s | 128,261 |
| Refreshed SGLang run 3 | 68.702 | 17.467 s | 1,200 / 1,200 | 1.323 s | 128,262 |
| **Refreshed median** | **68.551** | **17.505 s** | **1,200 / 1,200** | **1.310 s** | — |
| Final-head confirmation after last main merge | 68.379 | 17.549 s | 1,200 / 1,200 | 1.297 s | 128,266 |

The refreshed three-run mean is 68.465 requests/s, sample standard deviation is 0.289 requests/s, and CV is 0.422%. The final-head confirmation is inside that range. The refreshed median is 1.97% below the original 69.925 report and 11.18% above the historical 61.657 vLLM median. vLLM was not rerun during this review-fix pass.

## Semantic accuracy

The manifest provides ground truth for nine parsed fields. The final-head confirmation produced:

| Metric over 1,200 requests | Final head |
|---|---:|
| All fields present | 1,200 |
| All 9 fields exact | 639 |
| Variant + regular/sale/loyalty/unit prices exact | 1,200 |
| MSID exact | 1,189 |
| Barcode exact | 1,186 |
| Descriptive name exact | 1,065 |
| Tag name exact | 648 |
| Median completion tokens | 105 |

The three refreshed runs contained 640, 640, and 643 all-nine-field exact matches. Sampling causes small movement in free-text fields, while all deterministic variant and price fields remain exact. This is within or slightly above the earlier PR accuracy range.

## MFU and profile evidence

For the median run, an operator-level count of the vision encoder/merger, uncached text prefill, decode projections, LM head, and dense attention gives 4.599 PFLOP over 17.505 seconds: **262.7 TFLOP/s, approximately 26.6% of the dense H100 SXM BF16 peak**. The estimate accounts for shared-prefix KV reuse and excludes elementwise/host work, so it is useful model MFU rather than a hardware-counter FLOP rate. Active one-second telemetry averaged 97.2% SM activity, 47.6% memory activity, and 617.8 W.

Stage-separated torch traces show BF16 nvJet GEMMs consuming about 71% of decode and 70% of extend device time. FlashInfer decode attention is about 10%; FA3 extend attention is about 8.5%.

Focused Nsight Compute evidence on the exact gate-up projection:

| Shape | Throughput | Applicable-roof efficiency | Key limit |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `M=336, K=2560, N=19456` | 542.2 TFLOP/s | 55.3% | one wave/SM, register/shared-memory pressure, shared-store conflicts |
| `M=8, K=2560, N=19456` | 20.0 TFLOP/s | 74.8% | bandwidth-bound, 2.58 TB/s, only 76 blocks / 0.58 wave per SM |

The most evidence-backed follow-up is a separate Hopper BF16 small-M gate-up path for M=1/2/4/8 that increases weight-streaming parallelism. Image caching is intentionally unavailable for this one-pass workload, and attention is not the dominant device-time consumer.

## Validation

```text
test_model_overrides.py: 94 passed
test_server_args.py: 192 passed
test_serving_chat.py: 123 passed
multimodal preprocess-cache: 27 passed, 1 skipped
multimodal GPU feature transport: 37 passed
H100 CUDA IPC transport: 6 passed
media artifact, feature materialization, async processor, abort cleanup: passed
legacy + unified radix prompt-retention tests (page sizes 1/4/16): passed
pre-commit, AST, ruff, format, codespell, CI registry validation: passed
H100 final-head stream: 1,200/1,200 completed, fields present, no competing GPU process
```

## Residual risk

- The zero-copy path is intentionally limited to TP=1 and an image fully consumed by the current chunk. Multi-GPU and cross-chunk inputs retain the old reconstruction copy.
- The 3 GiB bounded IPC pool trades approximately 4.6% KV capacity for avoiding CPU fallback in the profiled 400-request wave. It is restricted to the no-retention Hopper profile and can be overridden explicitly.
- The prompt/output radix split affects all model families and should receive a radix-cache-owner review in addition to the existing unit coverage.
- Public VLM accuracy suites, multi-GPU configurations, and a single-digest CI image remain useful follow-ups.

## Checklist

- [x] Unique images; no measured image reuse.
- [x] Shared text-prefix KV is the only intentional cross-request reuse.
- [x] Startup failure reported by the external reproducer fixed and covered.
- [x] Semantic accuracy, stage profiler, workload MFU, and NCU evidence collected.
- [x] Latest `main` merged and final-head H100 confirmation completed.
- [x] No custom CUDA or FlashInfer kernel added by this PR.

title: Fix DSV4 shared-fusion CPU unit test after the EP guard landed
author: alisonshao
body:
## Motivation

`test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_shared_expert_fusion.py` fails in `base-a-test-cpu` with:

```
AssertionError: expert model parallel group is not initialized
```

#35505 added an EP guard to `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM.shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason`:

```python
if get_parallel().moe_ep_size > 1 and not uses_per_rank_fused_shared_slots():
```

`moe_ep_size` resolves through `get_moe_ep_group()`, which asserts when no MoE EP group is installed — as on a CPU runner. Before that commit the gate only read the quant config and an exec flag, so the test was fine.

Six of the seven tests in the class reach the gate, either directly or via `_install()` → `install_shared_experts_fusion_decision`. `run_unittest_files` invokes each file with `-f` (failfast), so only the first one gets reported.

## Modifications

Override `moe_ep_size=1` in `setUp`, stating a single-rank topology for every case in the class. With the override installed, `_v` returns it directly and the canonical getter is never called.

This is what `test/registered/unit/models/test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py` already does for every other family's gate, for the same reason.

title: [Kernel] Declare the PyTorch ABI dependency in sglang-kernel wheels
author: kuma-loong
body:
## Motivation

`sglang-kernel` contains native extensions compiled against a specific PyTorch C++ ABI, but its wheel metadata currently does not declare a runtime dependency on PyTorch.

This allows package resolvers to install incompatible combinations. For example, `sglang-kernel==0.4.6.post1`, which is built against PyTorch 2.13.0, can be installed alongside PyTorch 2.11.0. Importing `sgl_kernel` then fails with an unresolved PyTorch symbol.

The build-system requirement is also currently `torch>=2.8.0`, so an isolated source build could select a different PyTorch ABI from the version documented and used by the CUDA release workflow.

Fixes #36462.

## Modifications

Update `python/sglang/kernels/aot/pyproject.toml` to:

- require `torch==2.13.0` in the isolated build environment;
- add `torch==2.13.0` to the generated package runtime dependencies.

This matches the PyTorch version currently documented in the AOT kernel README, installed by the CUDA kernel build container, and required by the main SGLang Python package.

The exact public-version requirement remains compatible with CUDA local versions such as `torch==2.13.0+cu129` and `torch==2.13.0+cu130`.

This change is limited to the CUDA package configuration. CPU, ROCm, and MUSA use separate build configurations and should declare their respective ABI requirements independently.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This change only affects package dependency metadata and does not modify kernels, model execution, or numerical results.

Metadata validation:

```text
Name: sglang-kernel
Version: 0.4.6.post1
Requires-Python: >=3.10
Requires-Dist: torch==2.13.0
```

PEP 440 requirement validation:

```text
2.13.0: True
2.13.0+cu130: True
2.13.0+cu129: True
2.11.0+cu130: False
2.14.0: False
```

`git diff --check` also passes. A complete CUDA wheel build was not run locally because it requires the project's CUDA kernel build environment.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This change does not affect runtime code or kernel performance.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the change according to the project style.
- [x] Validate the generated package metadata; no runtime unit test is applicable.
- [x] Confirm that no documentation update is required; the existing AOT README already specifies PyTorch 2.13.0.
- [x] Confirm that accuracy and speed benchmarks are not applicable.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [diffusion] fuse Helios paired transposed RoPE
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Helios applies the same transposed RoPE chain to already-normalized Q and K in
every self-attention block. At the production `[8640, 40, 128]` BF16 shape,
the eager reshape/chunk/mul/add/stack path takes about 1.62 ms per Q/K pair and
accounts for thousands of launches in a short denoise profile.

## Modifications

- Add a lightweight JIT CUDA kernel that applies Helios' transposed RoPE to Q
  and K together, in place. Explicit FP32 round-to-nearest operations preserve
  the eager multiply and add/subtract boundaries before casting back to
  FP16/BF16.
- Dispatch it from `HeliosSelfAttention` only for compatible CUDA dtype, shape,
  layout, device, and pair alignment. Tensor-parallel RMSNorm and unsupported
  inputs keep the existing eager path.
- Register the lazy diffusion-kernel export and add unit, compile, import, and
  production-shape benchmark coverage.
- Document the fast-path contract in the diffusion kernel README and profiling
  skill reference.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["HeliosSelfAttention.forward"] --> B["Q/K projection and RMSNorm"]
    B --> C["Unflatten to B, S, H, D"]
    C --> D{"TP RMSNorm disabled and can_use_helios_qk_rope"}
    D -->|"compatible"| E["fused_inplace_helios_qk_rope"]:::changed
    E --> F["helios_qk_rope_kernel updates Q/K pairs"]:::changed
    D -->|"fallback"| G["apply_rotary_emb_transposed for Q and K"]
    F --> H["USPAttention"]
    G --> H

    L["Legend: dashed border = added or modified"]:::changed
    classDef changed stroke-dasharray:5 5,stroke-width:2px;
```

The model keeps normalization unchanged. The new branch only replaces the two
post-normalization RoPE ladders; all unsupported layouts and TP RMSNorm return
to the original eager implementation before attention.

## Accuracy Tests

Final branch base: `8eaffdf382e06b7dc50fc5c76cc5aad9c36bb0e4`.

H100 kernel/import regression:

```text
pytest -q \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_helios_qk_rope.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_import_surface.py

22 passed
```

Coverage includes:

- FP16 and BF16, head dimensions 64/128/256, and production
  `[8640, 40, 128]`; every supported result uses `torch.equal` against eager.
- in-place pointer preservation, invalid dtype/shape/layout/device and odd
  storage-offset fallback, TP RMSNorm fallback, public import registration,
  direct custom-op fullgraph capture, and model-dispatch
  `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)`.
- `BestWishYsh/Helios-Base`, native SGLang, 640x384x33, 50 steps, guidance 5,
  quality high, seed 42: baseline/candidate MP4 files have the same SHA256
  (`192fe3acbf0abe9ad7c6b01203074903985322a62efe310fbda514e004e482e6`).
  First/middle/last decoded RGB frames have SSIM 1.0 and infinite PSNR.

Helios-Mid and Helios-Distilled are process-nondeterministic even for repeated
same-seed baselines. For Mid, baseline/baseline mean key-frame SSIM was 0.342,
candidate/candidate was 0.329, and the two baseline/candidate pairings were
0.344 and 0.323. For Distilled, baseline/baseline was 0.597 and
baseline/candidate was 0.587. These variations are indistinguishable, so this
PR does not claim byte-identical model output for those checkpoints; their
correctness evidence is the production-shape bit-exact operator test plus the
within-path/cross-path matrix above.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hardware: one NVIDIA H100 80GB, native SGLang backend, BF16, eager request
path. Helios is not on the BCG allowlist, so this PR makes no BCG claim.

Latest-main production-shape microbenchmark:

```text
python test/registered/kernels/benchmark/diffusion/bench_helios_qk_rope.py \
  --tokens 2160 8640 --heads 40 --head-dim 128 --dtype bfloat16

tokens   eager (us)   JIT (us)
2160       416.640      39.584
8640      1617.312     139.680   # 11.58x
```

Strict Helios-Mid saved-request A2-B3-B4-A3 comparison at 640x384x33, 20
steps, quality high, seed 42:

| Metric | Baseline mean | Candidate mean | Baseline / candidate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Denoise | 51.135 s | 46.838 s | 1.0917x |
| E2E | 53.418 s | 49.103 s | 1.0879x |

On Helios-Base at the immediately preceding diffusion-identical main commit
`413df1f8db`, the same native saved request measured:

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Baseline / candidate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Denoise | 81.241 s | 75.207 s | 1.0802x |
| E2E | 82.136 s | 76.095 s | 1.0794x |

The two commits after `413df1f8db` only add/update the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
cookbook; final GPU unit tests and the microbenchmark were rerun after rebasing
onto them.

In a five-step Helios-Mid trace, total GPU time fell from 2009.2 ms to
1833.9 ms and launches fell from 25,611 to 18,411. The candidate adds 480
Helios kernel launches totaling 23.05 ms while removing 1,920 FP32 adds, 3,840
FP32 multiplies, and 1,920 BF16 copies.

All task-owned Helios-Mid, Helios-Distilled, and Helios-Base checkpoint caches
were removed after validation; the cleanup ledger reports zero residual weight

title: [diffusion][kernel] support transposed residual-gate add
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- extend the shared diffusion `residual_gate_add` JIT op to the mixed layout used by SANA-Video: a transposed-dense `[B, tokens, hidden]` residual/output, contiguous update, and `[1, 1, hidden]` gate
- use a 32x32 padded shared-memory tile so update reads and residual/output traffic stay coalesced without inserting a full `.contiguous()` copy
- preserve the residual stride and keep all unsupported dtype/layout/device cases on the existing eager fallback
- add production/edge-shape, storage-offset, fullgraph, and CUDA Graph tests; update the registered benchmark and diffusion fast-path documentation

## Motivation

On an NVIDIA H100 80GB profile of native SGLang SANA-Video (832x480x17, 8 steps), the two gated residual sites per transformer block did not reach the existing contiguous-only fusion:

```text
residual shape/stride: [1, 7800, 2240] / (17472000, 1, 7800)
update shape/stride:   [1, 7800, 2240] / (17472000, 2240, 1)
gate shape:            [1, 1, 2240]
```

The lossless 5-step trace attributed 106.1 ms across 720 BF16 add launches to this residual/update shape. Materializing the residual as contiguous would add another full-tensor copy at every site, so this patch handles the mixed layout directly.

## H100 results

Environment: NVIDIA H100 80GB, CUDA 13.0.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1. Base: `sgl-project/sglang@8eaffdf382e06b7dc50fc5c76cc5aad9c36bb0e4`.

Registered production-shape microbenchmark (BF16):

| Workload | PyTorch | JIT CUDA | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| SANA-Video `[1, 7800, 2240]` mixed layout | 195.83 us | 85.47 us | 2.291x |

Native SGLang real-model A-B-B-A, `Efficient-Large-Model/SANA-Video_2B_480p_diffusers`, 832x480x17, 8 steps, guidance 6.0, seed 42:

| Path | Mean denoise | Mean E2E | Baseline / candidate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline | 1.75350 s | 2.50571 s | - |
| candidate | 1.68327 s | 2.43629 s | 1.0417x / 1.0285x |

All four generated MP4 files have the same SHA256: `b2801dd499743f8414062817c6e8e77d7521a94654fb715b86764fdca425ad88`.

Model-level BCG timings are intentionally excluded: the current default SANA-Video warmup captures an 81-frame signature, while this serving request has 17 frames and therefore misses the captured signature. The custom op itself is covered by CUDA Graph capture/replay below.

## Validation

```bash
pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_modulate.py -k residual_gate_add
# 29 passed, 960 deselected

pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_modulate.py
# 989 passed

python test/registered/kernels/benchmark/diffusion/bench_residual_gate_add.py

pre-commit run --files \
  python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/diffusion/residual_gate_add.cuh \
  python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/modulate/residual_gate_add_jit.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_modulate.py \
  test/registered/kernels/benchmark/diffusion/bench_residual_gate_add.py \
  python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/README.md \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/.claude/skills/sglang-diffusion-benchmark-profile/existing-fast-paths.md
```

The focused suite covers FP16/BF16/FP32, non-tile-aligned and production shapes, batches greater than one, nonzero storage offsets, exact output stride preservation, `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)`, and CUDA Graph capture/replay.

title: [ROCm][Perf] aiter: page-level KV view for gfx950 fp8 page-64 asm prefill
author: omirosh
body:
## Motivation

This is a ROCm performance change for gfx950 fp8 hd256 chunked prefill: at `--page-size 64` it hands aiter's paged-varlen ASM kernel ([ROCm/aiter#4971](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4971)) a page-level view of the KV pool, replacing the gather that main (#36758) runs on every layer to copy the prefix KV into a contiguous buffer, and is worth **+1.1% to +1.9% output tok/s at 60k/600 and +0.9% to +1.6% at 128k/1k**, with TTFT 2% to 7% better, for `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4` on 8x MI355X, TP8, fp8 KV, measured on two nodes against the released `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19-rocm10-mi35x` image at its default `--page-size 1`.

The gather exists because without a page-level table aiter reads a page-64 call as `page_size=1` and this shape falls to CK. It works, but it pays for a copy and a scratch buffer sized by the total KV in the forward, not by the chunk. Reading the pool in place removes both. Per prefill call that is 1.04x to 1.22x faster than the gather (2.8x to 3.7x over CK), and the gap grows with context length and with the number of requests prefilling together. The gather's scratch peaks at 451 MB in the largest case measured, eight prefills over a 111k-token prefix; this path allocates none. At 8k/1k the end-to-end result is flat, -0.1% to +0.9% throughput.

The change is contained. It only engages on gfx95 at `--page-size 64` with fp8 KV, head dim 256, a power-of-two GQA ratio and the plain NHD pool (not the sliding-window or vectorized 5D pool). Everywhere else prefill runs exactly as on main, and `SGLANG_AITER_PAGED_PREFILL_ASM=0` restores main's behaviour even there. Page 64 is the only page size aiter's kernel is compiled for, so at `--page-size 16`, where #37465 puts the MTP ASM verify kernel, this path is a no-op. The two cannot both be active on one server until one of them supports the other's page size.

main's `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` pins aiter `acf8fdf` (2026-09-12), which already contains aiter#4971, so no aiter bump is needed.

## Modifications

**`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py`**

- `_build_paged_kv_view()` converts the token-level KV table into `(page_indptr, page_ids, last_page_len)`. The allocator packs each page contiguously, so a slot's page id is `slot // page_size`; the arithmetic runs off `seq_lens_cpu`, so only the gather touches the GPU.
- `ForwardMetadata.paged_kv_view` carries it. It is built once per batch in `init_forward_metadata`, and only where the whole batch can use it: gfx95, page 64, and the plain NHD pool. Off gfx95 there is no kernel for this shape, so the view is never built rather than built and discarded.
- `forward_extend` computes `paged_asm_available` once per layer (view present and power-of-two GQA ratio via `_paged_prefill_asm_supports_gqa()`). The #36758 gather branch requires it to be `False`; the paged branch requires it to be `True`, and then swaps in the 4D K/V views, the page-level indptr/table and `kv_last_page_lens`. One flag read at both sites keeps the two branches mutually exclusive. The guard mirrors aiter's own: there is no CK arm for 4D LINEAR page-64 fp8 hd256, so a call aiter rejects raises `no matching kernel found` instead of falling back.
- `SGLANG_AITER_PAGED_PREFILL_ASM` (default on) gates whether the view is built at all.

**`python/sglang/srt/environ.py`** - `SGLANG_AITER_PAGED_PREFILL_ASM = EnvBool(True)`.

**`docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx`** - documents the flag, including that it is inert at any page size other than 64.

**`test/manual/test_aiter_paged_kv_view.py`** - CPU-only. `TestAiterPagedKVView` checks the conversion against a shuffled allocation with a ragged last page, since an identity table would pass even if the arithmetic were wrong; `TestPagedPrefillAsmSupportsGqa` covers the GQA guard, including indivisible and zero/negative head counts.

The flag is a plain on/off rather than a context-length heuristic. The paged path wins at 60k and above and is flat at 8k, but the crossover sits inside this host's noise, so a threshold picked from this data would not be defensible. Default on because the long-context win is the larger effect.

## Accuracy Tests

`amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8 on MI355X (gfx950), gsm8k 200 questions, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size 512` (reduced from 16384 so gsm8k prompts actually get chunked), `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x`. All at `--page-size 64`:

| stock | main (#36758 + #36852) | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.985 | 0.990 | **0.995** |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Against the released image, two nodes

Stock `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19-rocm10-mi35x` at its default `--page-size 1` (#36758 gather) versus the same image with this PR at `--page-size 64`. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --disable-radix-cache`, TP8, everything else identical. Ratios are this PR over stock, ranges span both nodes:

| ISL/OSL | conc | output tok/s | mean TTFT | mean E2E |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8k/1k | 4 | 0.999 | 1.007 - 1.009 | 1.001 |
| 8k/1k | 8 - 256 | 1.002 - 1.009 | 0.887 - 0.970 | 0.991 - 0.998 |
| 60k/600 | 4 | 1.011 - 1.012 | 0.952 | 0.988 - 0.989 |
| 60k/600 | 16 | 1.014 - 1.015 | 0.933 - 0.935 | 0.985 - 0.986 |
| 60k/600 | 64 | **1.019** | 0.973 - 0.976 | 0.982 |
| 128k/1k | 4 | 1.009 - 1.012 | 0.966 - 0.969 | 0.989 - 0.991 |
| 128k/1k | 16 | 1.014 - 1.016 | 0.955 - 0.966 | 0.984 - 0.986 |

The two nodes agree on throughput to within 0.003 in every cell. Absolute throughput differs between them but the ratio does not, which is what running it twice was for. Per-cell numbers are in [the sweep comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36505#issuecomment-5662364516).

### Against main at the same page size

One node, one day, identical server args at `--page-size 64`; only the aiter build and the patch differ.

- Server: `--attention-backend aiter --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --tp-size 8 --max-running-requests 256 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --disable-radix-cache`
- Bench: `bench_serving --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 0.8`

Output throughput, tok/s:

| ISL/OSL | conc | stock | main | this PR | vs main |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1k/1k | 4 | 228.4 | 228.6 | 228.1 | 99.8% |
| 1k/1k | 16 | 668.7 | 672.6 | 671.6 | 99.9% |
| 1k/1k | 64 | 1509.9 | 1515.3 | 1504.7 | 99.3% |
| 8k/1k | 4 | 226.1 | 226.0 | 222.5 | 98.5% |
| 8k/1k | 16 | 576.1 | 576.3 | 567.0 | 98.4% |
| 8k/1k | 64 | 1086.4 | 1093.4 | 1092.4 | 99.9% |
| 60k/600 | 4 | 103.0 | 107.6 | 108.8 | 101.1% |
| 60k/600 | 16 | 145.3 | 157.1 (*) | 158.9 (*) | 101.1% |
| 60k/600 | 64 | 161.8 | 178.1 | 180.8 | 101.5% |
| 128k/1k | 4 | not run | 92.3 | 93.5 | 101.3% |
| 128k/1k | 16 | not run | 123.0 | 125.6 | 102.1% |
| 128k/1k | 64 | not run | 131.2 | 134.0 | 102.1% |
| **geomean, 1k-60k** | | | | | **99.9%** (102.6% vs stock) |
| **geomean, 60k** | | | | | **101.3%** (108.9% vs stock) |
| **geomean, 128k** | | | | | **101.8%** |

At 1k and 8k the two paths are the same code below the branch and land within 1.6%, inside this host's noise floor; the 8k cells here are the ones the two-node sweep resolves as flat. The 128k rows come from a separate sweep on the same node and day, which is why stock was not repeated there. TTFT at 128k: 8.4 s -> 8.1 s at conc 4, 22.6 s -> 21.8 s at conc 16, 239.8 s -> 234.9 s at conc 64.

The 60k trace confirms the swap: prefill attention is `aiter::fmha_fwd_hd256_fp8_causal_paged_varlen_gfx950` (299 calls, 465 ms) where an unpatched run runs `ck_tile::...FmhaBatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheKernel`.

Moving off `--page-size 1` costs nothing on its own: holding the code fixed and changing only `--page-size`, page 64 over page 1 is 99.9% for stock and 100.1% for main across the nine 1k-60k cells, and 99.1% to 99.6% at 128k.

<details>
<summary>(*) the 60k/16 cell, measurement noise, and two caveats</summary>

This host shows reproducible whole-server stalls: the scheduler stops logging and no requests complete for 13-18 s, roughly every 2-4 minutes, with occasional 30-55 s events. They cost 5-9% of wall time in every run and appear in every arm including unpatched stock, so they are not attributable to any patch. Aligned to each run's first scheduler log line, five runs taken hours apart share one schedule to within 2-3 s, so they are workload-driven and in-process rather than host noise. Per-cell deltas below a few percent are therefore not resolvable from a single run.

60k/16 is where they hit hardest, so it was run three times per arm. main: 155.4, 156.7, 157.1, none carrying a stall. This PR: 158.9 with no stall, 139.3 on a run that lost 47 s to one, and 135.5 on a run that lost 10 s and is not fully explained by it. The table shows each arm's stall-free run. Taking instead each arm's worst run would move the nine-cell geomean to 98.5% and the 60k geomean to 96.9%, so this cell alone spans the whole result.

Two caveats. At 128k conc 64 the KV pool saturates and the scheduler runs only 26-28 requests with 37 queued at 0.94-1.00 token usage, so that cell is capacity-bound rather than prefill-bound; conc 4 and conc 16 are the cleaner read. And the page-1 gather arm ran later on a different node, carrying 8k/16 and 60k/16 as anchors; those came back at 98.6% and 99.1% of the same cells on the original node, so cross-node page-1 comparisons in this table are directional only. The two-node sweep above is the clean version of that comparison.

</details>

### Op-level: why not just gather

Both paths reach the same ASM family, so the choice is measurable on one prefill call. aiter with #4971, page 64, hd256, GQA 8:1, causal, medians of three runs. Wall clock per call, so the gather's copy and index arithmetic are inside the timed region. The budget is held at 16384 new tokens, what `--chunked-prefill-size` caps, and split across the batch:

| prefilling reqs | chunk each | KV prefix | CK | gather + contiguous asm | page view + paged asm | ratio | gather scratch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 16384 | 0 | 1544 us | 570 us | **549 us** | 1.04x | +8 MB |
| 1 | 16384 | 43,616 | 9213 us | 2892 us | **2595 us** | 1.11x | +30 MB |
| 1 | 16384 | 111,616 | 21310 us | 6577 us | **5685 us** | 1.16x | +64 MB |
| 4 | 4096 | 0 | 432 us | 230 us | **203 us** | 1.14x | +8 MB |
| 4 | 4096 | 43,616 | 8185 us | 2673 us | **2355 us** | 1.14x | +95 MB |
| 4 | 4096 | 111,616 | 20354 us | 6527 us | **5523 us** | 1.18x | +230 MB |
| 8 | 2048 | 0 | 251 us | 176 us | **150 us** | 1.18x | +8 MB |
| 8 | 2048 | 43,616 | 8019 us | 2720 us | **2334 us** | 1.17x | +181 MB |
| 8 | 2048 | 111,616 | 22373 us | 6859 us | **5602 us** | 1.22x | +451 MB |

The scratch is the gathered K/V buffer, `2 * total_k * H_kv * D`, allocated and freed per layer, so the column is the transient peak. This path allocates none of it; both paths need the same 128 MB for q and the output.

<details>
<summary>Where the time goes, and two controls</summary>

Timed separately, the index arithmetic costs 74-152 us and the copy 102-514 us, so together they cover about a fifth of the 892 us gap at one request and about half of the 1257 us gap at eight. The rest is the kernel: the contiguous ASM kernel on a gathered buffer is slower on this shape than the paged ASM kernel reading the pool in place, so even with a free gather this path stays ahead. Those splits are upper bounds, since measuring them adds device syncs.

A device-side kernel-time measurement would show none of this - the copy runs as separate `index_select` kernels before the attention call and the index arithmetic is host-side - so wall clock per call is the framing that charges each path for what it does.

Controls: the gather is page-size-insensitive at long context, page 64 landing within 0.3% of page 1 at both 43k and 111k prefix, as it should since `kv_indices` is token-level at either page size; at no prefix page 64 is 8-12% faster, where the scattered page-1 allocation costs the copy its locality. The batch-1 cells reproduce within 4% on a second node.

</details>

title: [diffusion][kernel] avoid 4D scale-shift autotuning
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- replace request-time Triton autotuning in the 4D causal-video scale/shift path with a capped power-of-two tile heuristic
- add 4D BF16/FP16 correctness coverage and a registered production-shape kernel benchmark
- document the cold-start constraint in the diffusion kernel README and benchmark/profile skill

## Why

LingBot-World invokes this bandwidth-bound kernel once per transformer block. In a full-stage H100 trace, 199 Python calls expanded to 3,820 Triton autotune launches, making tuning dominate the first denoise step. The selected 64/128/256/512 tiles were bit-identical across the tested production shapes; the capped power-of-two choice was fastest or within measurement noise.

## H100 validation

Native SGLang only, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2, LingBotWorldCausalDMDPipeline, 832x480x9, 4 steps, lossless, seed 42. ABBA used independent Triton caches so both paths paid their real cold-start cost.

| metric | baseline mean | candidate mean | improvement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| denoise | 3909.57 ms | 3083.09 ms | 21.14% |
| request E2E | 12416.27 ms | 11467.29 ms | 7.64% |

All four ABBA MP4 files have the same SHA256: fe5c7d6860d5c11432834ef4419c102ab1081f6f4b92897626481151b4483290.

A fresh isolated Triton cache reduced the production [1, 4680, 5120] first call from 1338.47 ms to 714.77 ms. Steady-state H100 speedups from the registered benchmark were 2.36x (Wan), 2.29x (SANA Video), 1.33x (LongLive), and 2.24x (LingBot-World).

LingBot causal DMD does not support breakable CUDA graphs, so this PR makes no BCG performance claim.

The model ABBA ran at c8b56b1f4; the branch was then rebased onto f8cc1f952, whose intervening change is documentation-only, and the focused tests and benchmark were rerun.

## Tests

- pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_modulate.py — 993 passed
- pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/realtime/test_lingbot_causal_denoising.py — 28 passed
- post-rebase 4D selection — 16 passed
- pre-commit on all changed files — passed

## LingBot-World V2 sibling validation

The independent robbyant/lingbot-world-v2-14b-causal-fast-diffusers checkpoint uses the same native causal pipeline and production shape. A fresh-cache A-B-B-A gives 3882.74 vs 3015.31 ms mean denoise (22.34% faster) and 12953.80 vs 12168.34 ms request E2E (6.06% faster). All four MP4 files are byte-identical with SHA256 ace7fb75f5f3a7837b8e704cddfceef8ff573bc0e126483ad17c3ae6cccca4fb.

The latest-main high-quality lane stays within the repository video gate versus lossless: first/middle/last SSIM 0.98398/0.97955/0.97701 and PSNR 43.86/42.83/42.35 dB. BCG remains statically unsupported for this pipeline.

title: MiniMax-M3: share the sparse index top-k across layers and reuse the decode top-k buffer
author: zcnrex
body:
# MiniMax-M3: share the sparse index top-k across layers and reuse the decode top-k buffer

MiniMax-M3's sparse attention runs a lightning-indexer pass in every sparse layer
to choose the top-k KV blocks that the main attention then reads. On the
value-disabled sparse layers that indexer has no output of its own — `idx_o` is
`None` there, only the block selection is consumed — so its result can be
computed once and shared by a run of consecutive layers. This PR adds
`SGLANG_MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_TOPK_FREQ=N` (default 2), which groups every N such
layers: the group's first layer computes and stores the reduced top-k, and the
remaining layers reuse it, skipping both the flash-index attention and the
group-reduce. In decode the selection is written straight into a persistent
per-batch-size `int32` buffer (`topk_out=`) rather than a freshly allocated
tensor per layer, which removes an allocation from every sparse decode layer and
keeps the destination address fixed so CUDA-graph capture never allocates. The
buffer is only useful because of the sharing, so the two changes ship together.

Sharing the selection **changes which KV blocks the skip layers attend to** — see
`## Correctness` below. It is therefore gated: `index_topk_freq` is pinned to `1`
on every non-ROCm platform and whenever two-batch overlap is enabled, and at
freq 1 no buffer is allocated and every new argument is `None`/`False`, so the
default CUDA path is byte-for-byte main's.

Two smaller changes in the same files ride along:

- The layer-invariant prefill seqblock metadata (`cu_seqblocks_q`,
  `max_seqblock_q`, `all_seqblock_q`) is computed once per `ForwardBatch` in the
  backend and passed down, instead of being recomputed inside each sparse layer.
  Same values. The owning `ForwardBatch` is part of the cache key because a
  single metadata init can be followed by more than one `ForwardBatch` reaching
  the layers (two-batch overlap splits into two children with different
  `extend_seq_lens`), so a hit requires the same object, not just a live cache.
- `forward_decode` gets the `_is_sparse_kv_cached_by_fusion` guard that the
  extend path already has on main, so the decode sparse-KV store is not repeated
  when the fused qk-norm-rope kernel already wrote it. Idempotent write either
  way; this only removes the launch.

The decode score kernel's autotune space now drops configs whose token tile is
smaller than a sparse block (`BLOCK_SIZE_N < block_size`), and on ROCm the sweep
is replaced by one fixed config plus a `BLOCK_SIZE_N` heuristic, because runtime
autotune can fire under CUDA-graph capture and mistune there.

## Performance
Measured on 8x MI350X (gfx950), MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, TP8, 80k input / 600 output.
Two bench reps per boot; the warm (second) rep is reported and the two agreed
within 0.1%. Noise floor is +/-0.4%. Tables are the harness output verbatim,
trimmed to the first five columns. Baseline is `upstream/main`.
**Baseline (`upstream/main`)**

```
Input lens: [80000]. Output lens: [600]. Cache hit rate: 90.0%.
|   batch size |   input len |   latency (s) |   input throughput (tok/s) |   output throughput (tok/s) |
|--------------|-------------|---------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------|
|            1 |       80000 |         11.26 |                     187984 |                       55.35 |
|            2 |       80000 |         11.88 |                     191222 |                      108.68 |
|            4 |       80000 |         13.39 |                     192965 |                      204.62 |
|            8 |       80000 |         16.27 |                     193687 |                      370.13 |
|           16 |       80000 |         22.2  |                     193188 |                      616.28 |
|           32 |       80000 |         33.78 |                     193245 |                      934.92 |
```
**With this PR**

```
Input lens: [80000]. Output lens: [600]. Cache hit rate: 90.0%.
|   batch size |   input len |   latency (s) |   input throughput (tok/s) |   output throughput (tok/s) |
|--------------|-------------|---------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------|
|            1 |       80000 |         10.44 |                     209588 |                       59.67 |
|            2 |       80000 |         11.14 |                     210417 |                      115.61 |
|            4 |       80000 |         12.35 |                     213259 |                      221.18 |
|            8 |       80000 |         14.41 |                     215085 |                      419.8  |
|           16 |       80000 |         19.37 |                     214509 |                      716.39 |
|           32 |       80000 |         28.94 |                     215010 |                     1127.4  |
```
Output throughput +6.38%..+20.59%; input throughput +10.04%..+11.49%.

## Accuracy
gsm8k, 512 examples, `max_tokens 2048`, `temperature 0`, `seed 0`, against the
same server boot as the perf run.
**Baseline**

```
== gsm8k ==
512 examples (single-shot)  |  109.0s  |  1338 tok/s  |  146K tokens

* score           =  97.07%
  stop_rate       =  98.44%
  truncated_rate  =  1.56%  [warn: hitting max_tokens]
  error_rate      =  0.00%
```
**With this PR**

```
== gsm8k ==
512 examples (single-shot)  |  97.7s  |  1463 tok/s  |  143K tokens

* score           =  96.68%
  stop_rate       =  98.44%
  truncated_rate  =  1.56%  [warn: hitting max_tokens]
  error_rate      =  0.00%
```

## Note on the launch command

`--moe-runner-backend aiter` is **not honoured on current `main`** for mxfp8. Arg resolution logs:

```
mxfp8 quantization supports only cutlass, deep_gemm, flashinfer_trtllm,
flashinfer_trtllm_routed, triton backends. Overriding 'aiter'.
```

and falls back to **triton**. Both sides of this A/B therefore ran the Triton MoE runner, so the comparison is apples-to-apples and the deltas stand — but `AITER_CONFIG_FMOE` is inert under this configuration and the aiter MoE path is *not* what was measured. The flag is kept in the command above only because it matches the invocation actually used; anyone reproducing will get triton and should see the same numbers.

title: [Fix][XPU/ROCm/NPU] Defer sgl_kernel.quantization import in expert_pack
author: arathi-hlab
body:
## Problem

`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/expert_pack.py` (introduced in #35314) has an unconditional top-level import:

```python
from sgl_kernel.quantization import ggml_moe_a8_vec
```

`sgl_kernel.quantization` is CUDA/MUSA-only — see the guard pattern in `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/gguf.py:44-70`, which explicitly falls through for `_is_hip`, `_is_npu`, and everything else (including XPU) and emits *"Only CUDA, MUSA and NPU support GGUF quantization currently."*

Any import chain that pulls in `expert_pack` on a non-CUDA/MUSA device now dies at module load. The DeepSeek-V2 forward hits this in the wild:

```
deepseek_v2.py:1185  forward_normal
  -> mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py:385  maybe_fuse_routed_scale_and_shared_add
    -> expert_pack.py:10  from sgl_kernel.quantization import ggml_moe_a8_vec
       ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sgl_kernel.quantization'
```

Failing XPU job (`stage-b-test-1-gpu-xpu` / `test_intel_xpu_backend.py::test_mla_decode_attention_backend`):
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32946854301/job/98212193462

The failure surfaces even though the actual Kimi-K3 expert-pack code path is never entered on XPU — the import alone is enough to blow up.

## Fix

Move the `ggml_moe_a8_vec` import inside `_kimi_vec` (the only function that uses the kernel). CUDA/MUSA behavior is unchanged: Python resolves `sgl_kernel.quantization` once and caches it in `sys.modules`, so subsequent calls incur only a dict lookup.

Mirrors the guard convention already used in `gguf.py:44-70` for the same module.

## Effect per vendor

| Vendor | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| CUDA | works | works (identical behavior; module cached after first call) |
| MUSA | works | works |
| ROCm (\`_is_hip\`) | broken at import time | fixed |
| NPU (\`_is_npu\`) | broken at import time | fixed |
| XPU | broken at import time (this PR's motivation) | fixed |

## Test plan

- [ ] \`stage-b-test-1-gpu-xpu\` — the \`test_intel_xpu_backend.py::test_mla_decode_attention_backend\` case that currently red-boxes should now pass, since \`expert_pack\` becomes importable on XPU.
- [ ] No functional change on CUDA / MUSA — \`_kimi_vec\` still resolves to \`sgl_kernel.quantization.ggml_moe_a8_vec\` via cached module lookup.
- [ ] Static check on the file: \`sgl_kernel.quantization\` is no longer among the module's top-level imports.

/cc @beyondHJM (author of #35314)

title: [DSV4][BCG] Optimize the heavy memory use of C4 Indexer when BCG is enabled
author: SYChen123
body: ## Motivation When enabling BCG on deepseek v4, C4 indexer leads to heavy memory pressure. The root reason is that the indexer logits with shape of [N, context_length] is padded to [N, max_position_embeddings]. For deepseek v4, model's max_position_emb is 1048576. When N=8192, the logits itself will cost 8192 * 1048576 // 4 * 4 = 8GB. Therefore, we propose to add a new parameter named --cuda-graph-prefill-max-context and the logit is padded to the user-specified max context size instead model's maximum context. ## Modifications 1. Add --cuda-graph-prefill-max-context parameter which accepts only 1 value and currently only takes effect on deepseek v4. The c4_max_seq_len used in C4 indexer is padded to this user-specified value, rather than model's maximum context. 2. During replay, if the kv context length of any of the request exceeds the --cuda-graph-prefill-max-context, fallback to eager. ## Accuracy Tests gsm8k test on deepseek-v4-flash-0731 is good. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Memory usage reduction Before this pr, capture will cost 43GB when --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill=16384. With this pr, the capture memory cost is reduced to 18GB. **58% memory reduction**. ### E2E test on deepseek-v4-flash-0731 E2E latency has 10% performance gains with BCG enabled. Without this pr, the server will OOM when chunk-prefill-size and max-captured-size are both set to 16384. | Setup | TTFT / TPOT (ms) | E2E (ms) | Input throughput (token/s) | |--------------|------------------|----------|----------------------------| | Baseline | 1075.57 / 1.68 | 1912.69 | 278674.46 | | With this pr | **830.93** / 1.82 | **1737.34** | **306275.00** | Server launching and benchmark commands are shown below. ``` # launch server sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --tp 2 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \ --max-prefill-tokens 16384 \ --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 16384 \ --cuda-graph-prefill-max-context 262144 \ --enable-deepseek-v4-fp4-indexer \ --max-running-requests 256 \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --enable-strict-thinking \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-ratio 2 \ --enable-cache-report \ --enable-metrics \ --log-requests \ --log-requests-level 1 \ --host 192.168.153.127 \ --port 9090 > server-0.log 2>&1 & # benchmark python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --flush-cache \ --host "${HOST}" \ --port "${PORT}" \ --backend sglang \ --dataset-name generated-shared-prefix \ --dataset-path ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json \ --num-prompts 512 \ --gsp-num-groups 1 \ --gsp-prompts-per-group 512 \ --gsp-system-prompt-len 61440 \ --gsp-question-len 4096 \ --gsp-output-len 500 \ --max-concurrency 32 \ --warmup-requests 10 \ > "benchmark.log" 2>&1 done done ``` ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). -
