title: MiniMax-M3: run the sparse prefill main attention through AITER Gluon paged attention
author: zcnrex
body:
# MiniMax-M3: Gluon paged-attention sparse prefill with Triton fallback

MiniMax-M3's sparse prefill runs three steps: a lightning-index attention that
produces per-query block scores, a top-k reduction over those scores, and a
sparse main attention that attends only to the selected KV blocks. Step 3 is
currently a Triton kernel (`flash_prefill_with_gqa_share_sparse`) that walks the
paged KV pool one 128-token block at a time via `req_to_token`. This PR adds a
second implementation of step 3 that calls AITER's Gluon paged attention
(`pa_decode_gluon(..., ps=True)`) instead, selected by
`SGLANG_OPT_USE_GLUON_PREFILL`. The main KV pool layout is unchanged — it stays
NHD `[max_slots, 1, head_dim]` — so each request's context is first gathered
into persistent SHUFFLE 5D scratch pages (`GLUON_PAGE_SIZE = 64`, two pages per
128-token sparse block, `x = 16 // dtype.itemsize`), and the per-query sparse
block table is expanded into a page table plus a per-query effective context
length. Scratch grows in 1024-page steps and is capped at 512 MiB per buffer;
past the cap the entry point raises and the caller falls back. The indexer and
the top-k reduction (steps 1 and 2) are untouched by the dispatch. Two prefill
kernels this path shares also change: a score-only index-attention kernel for
`disable_index_value` layers (it skips the index-value output and, when a sparse
block spans few enough pages, reads one base slot per page instead of one
`req_to_token` entry per token), and CDNA KV sub-tiling (`SUB_K`) in the Triton
sparse kernel so each QK/PV MFMA is right-sized on gfx942/gfx950.

title: MiniMax-M3: allocate the lightning-indexer K cache in fp8 on gfx95
author: zcnrex
body:
# MiniMax-M3: allocate the lightning-indexer K cache in fp8 on gfx95

MiniMax-M3's sparse attention keeps a second, much narrower KV cache — the
lightning-indexer K cache — whose only job is to produce the per-block scores
that pick which KV blocks the main attention reads. It is sized over every
sparse layer at `head_num=1, head_dim=sparse_index_dim`, and on ROCm it was
allocated in the model dtype (bf16) while the main K/V follow
`kv_cache_dtype`. This PR allocates it in `fp8_e4m3fn` on gfx95 (MI350/MI355)
behind `SGLANG_OPT_MINIMAX_M3_FP8_INDEX_CACHE`, exactly halving that pool. It
is a widening mode — bf16 q against fp8 k in the score kernels — which is the
same contract `m3_fp8_attn_gemm_enabled` already uses for the SM100 fp8
attn-GEMM path; this change makes the same `index_dtype=fp8` choice reachable
on gfx95 without requiring fp8 main KV. The Triton qk-norm-rope kernel now
stores into the index cache in *that cache's* dtype rather than q's, so the
value is rounded once from fp32 instead of twice through bf16 (a no-op cast
when the two dtypes match).

The change is **selection-only**: `dtype=self.kv_cache_dtype` for the main
attention K/V is untouched, and only `index_dtype` moves.

## Changes

- `KVCacheConfigurator.minimax_sparse_index_dtype()` is the single source of the
  index dtype. Both the pool builder and `pool_configurator`'s per-token cell
  size call it, so the sizing cannot drift from the allocation (same pattern as
  `is_unified_kv_fp8()` for DSV4).
- gfx95 only: OCP `e4m3fn` is only safe where it is native; on gfx94x sglang's
  fp8 is `e4m3fnuz` (max 224), so MI300 keeps the bf16 index cache and the flag
  is a no-op there.
- The flag defaults to `True`, i.e. on for gfx95 MiniMax-M3 sparse serving.
  This is a precision change, not a free fusion — see Accuracy below. Set
  `SGLANG_OPT_MINIMAX_M3_FP8_INDEX_CACHE=0` for a bf16 index cache.

## Behaviour on other platforms

- **CUDA, default config:** no change. The index dtype still resolves to the
  model dtype and the Triton store cast is an identity.
- **CUDA SM100 with fp8 attn-GEMM mode (`m3_fp8_attn_gemm_enabled`):** the index
  cache was already fp8 there, but the cell-size estimate counted it at bf16.
  It now counts the real fp8 size, so this configuration gets slightly more
  `max_total_num_tokens` at the same `mem_fraction_static`. Not measured.
- **MI300 (gfx94x) / NPU:** no change.

## Memory

The index pool is allocated as
`size x page_size x 1 x idx_head_dim x sizeof(index_dtype)` per sparse KV layer,
so bf16 -> `fp8_e4m3fn` is an exact **2x reduction of the index cache** with no
change to the main K/V pool.

Measured on 8x MI350X (gfx950), MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, TP8,
`--mem-fraction-static 0.80`, one boot per row, identical launch command
throughout (only the flag / the commit under test differs):

| run | index K cache | max_total_num_tokens | available_gpu_mem |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (`SGLANG_OPT_MINIMAX_M3_FP8_INDEX_CACHE=0`) | bf16, 43.34 GB | 3189113 | 41.12 GB |
| commit 1 -- fp8 index cache | fp8, 21.67 GB | 3189113 | **62.98 GB** |
| commit 2 -- + cell-size accounting | fp8, 25.05 GB | **3686422** (+15.6%) | 45.22 GB |

Commit 1 halves the index pool exactly (43.34 -> 21.67 GB), but the saving
surfaced as *free GPU memory* rather than capacity: the per-token cell-size
estimate that converts the profiled byte budget into `max_total_num_tokens`
still assumed a bf16 indexer, so the pool was sized as if nothing had been
saved and `max_total_num_tokens` did not move.

Commit 2 makes that estimate use the same dtype the pool is actually built
with. The saving then becomes capacity instead — **+15.6% `max_total_num_tokens`
at the same `mem_fraction_static`** — and free GPU memory returns to roughly the
baseline level, i.e. the freed bytes are spent rather than stranded.
`max_running_requests` is 2048 on all three rows.

Load-tested on the final state at bs44 / 80000 input = 3,520,000 tokens, beyond
the 3,189,113 the first two rows can hold: runs clean, peak token usage 0.95, no
OOM and no retraction.

## Performance
Measured on 8x MI350X (gfx950), MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, TP8, 80k input / 600 output.
Two bench reps per boot; the warm (second) rep is reported and the two agreed
within 0.1%. Noise floor is +/-0.4%. Tables are the harness output verbatim,
trimmed to the first five columns. Baseline is `upstream/main`.
**Baseline (`upstream/main`)**

```
Input lens: [80000]. Output lens: [600]. Cache hit rate: 90.0%.
|   batch size |   input len |   latency (s) |   input throughput (tok/s) |   output throughput (tok/s) |
|--------------|-------------|---------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------|
|            1 |       80000 |         11.26 |                     187984 |                       55.35 |
|            2 |       80000 |         11.88 |                     191222 |                      108.68 |
|            4 |       80000 |         13.39 |                     192965 |                      204.62 |
|            8 |       80000 |         16.27 |                     193687 |                      370.13 |
|           16 |       80000 |         22.2  |                     193188 |                      616.28 |
|           32 |       80000 |         33.78 |                     193245 |                      934.92 |
```
**With this PR**

```
Input lens: [80000]. Output lens: [600]. Cache hit rate: 90.0%.
|   batch size |   input len |   latency (s) |   input throughput (tok/s) |   output throughput (tok/s) |
|--------------|-------------|---------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------|
|            1 |       80000 |         11.23 |                     191515 |                       55.5  |
|            2 |       80000 |         11.9  |                     196762 |                      108.27 |
|            4 |       80000 |         13.11 |                     197873 |                      208.82 |
|            8 |       80000 |         15.69 |                     198566 |                      384.87 |
|           16 |       80000 |         21.13 |                     198257 |                      654.2  |
|           32 |       80000 |         31.54 |                     198355 |                     1030.4  |
```

## Accuracy

same server boot as the perf run.
**Baseline**

## Validation

No unit test is added: the sizing/allocation agreement is enforced by the
shared `minimax_sparse_index_dtype()`, and a dtype-selection test would only
restate its condition. Evidence is end-to-end (memory, perf and gsm8k above).
These numbers were measured before the `kvcache.cuh` change was dropped from
this PR (it is no longer touched; the slot assert does not break hipGraph
capture) and before the latest merge of `main`; they have not been re-run.

title: MiniMax-M3: Triton split-K router GEMV with in-kernel fixup
author: zcnrex
body:
# MiniMax-M3: Triton split-K router GEMV with in-kernel split-K fixup

The MiniMax-M3 MoE router gate is a skinny GEMV — `[M, K]` bf16 x `[N, K]` bf16 -> `[M, N]` fp32, with `N ~ 128` experts and `M <= 64` at decode — and the vendor BLAS solutions picked for that shape run far off the memory roofline on gfx950 (~0.1 TB/s for a ~1.6MB weight read at `M<=8`, `N=128`). This PR adds `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/router_gemv.py`, a Triton split-K kernel that reads the gate weight once at near-bandwidth, and routes `MiniMaxM3MoE._compute_router_logits` through it when `router_gemv_supported()` says the shape qualifies. Configs are per-M-bucket (`BLOCK_K` 512 throughout, `BLOCK_N` and `SPLIT_K` chosen by batch size, with a dedicated `BLOCK_M == 1` GEMV path that uses `tl.sum` instead of `tl.dot`) covering `M <= 8 / 16 / 32 / 64`. The split-K reduction is done inside the same kernel: the last CTA to finish a `(n-block, row-tile)` pair reduces all `SPLIT_K` partials and resets its counter slot to zero on the way out, so the scratch buffer stays reusable across launches without either a zero-init launch or a separate reduce launch — each extra launch costs ~2us on gfx950, which is a meaningful fraction of the kernel itself at these sizes. Anything the kernel does not cover — wrong dtype, non-contiguous last dim, `N` not divisible by `BLOCK_N`, `K` not divisible by `BLOCK_K`, or `M > 64` — falls through `router_gemv_supported()` to the existing `torch.mm` path unchanged.

## Performance
Measured on 8x MI350X (gfx950), MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, TP8, 80k input / 600 output.
Two bench reps per boot; the warm (second) rep is reported and the two agreed
within 0.1%. Noise floor is +/-0.4%. Tables are the harness output verbatim,
trimmed to the first five columns. Baseline is `upstream/main`.
**Baseline (`upstream/main`)**

```
Input lens: [80000]. Output lens: [600]. Cache hit rate: 90.0%.
|   batch size |   input len |   latency (s) |   input throughput (tok/s) |   output throughput (tok/s) |
|--------------|-------------|---------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------|
|            1 |       80000 |         11.26 |                     187984 |                       55.35 |
|            2 |       80000 |         11.88 |                     191222 |                      108.68 |
|            4 |       80000 |         13.39 |                     192965 |                      204.62 |
|            8 |       80000 |         16.27 |                     193687 |                      370.13 |
|           16 |       80000 |         22.2  |                     193188 |                      616.28 |
|           32 |       80000 |         33.78 |                     193245 |                      934.92 |
```
**With this PR**

```
Input lens: [80000]. Output lens: [600]. Cache hit rate: 90.0%.
|   batch size |   input len |   latency (s) |   input throughput (tok/s) |   output throughput (tok/s) |
|--------------|-------------|---------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------|
|            1 |       80000 |         10.92 |                     189401 |                       57.16 |
|            2 |       80000 |         11.68 |                     191857 |                      110.63 |
|            4 |       80000 |         13.14 |                     194266 |                      208.74 |
|            8 |       80000 |         16.1  |                     195607 |                      374.08 |
|           16 |       80000 |         21.94 |                     194140 |                      625.66 |
|           32 |       80000 |         33.42 |                     194545 |                      947.49 |
```
Output throughput +1.07%..+3.27%; input throughput +0.33%..+0.99%.

## Accuracy
gsm8k, 512 examples, `max_tokens 2048`, `temperature 0`, `seed 0`, against the
same server boot as the perf run.
**Baseline**

```
== gsm8k ==
512 examples (single-shot)  |  109.0s  |  1338 tok/s  |  146K tokens

* score           =  97.07%
  stop_rate       =  98.44%
  truncated_rate  =  1.56%  [warn: hitting max_tokens]
  error_rate      =  0.00%
```
**With this PR**

```
== gsm8k ==
512 examples (single-shot)  |  109.5s  |  1334 tok/s  |  146K tokens

* score           =  97.27%
  stop_rate       =  98.05%
  truncated_rate  =  1.95%  [warn: hitting max_tokens]
  error_rate      =  0.00%
```

## Correctness

**Not bit-identical.** Split-K reassociates the fp32 accumulation in the router GEMV, so the router logits differ in the last bits from the `torch.mm` path. That is why this carries an accuracy gate rather than a bit-identity claim.

gsm8k is **97.27% against a 97.07% baseline (+0.20 pp)**, `truncated_rate` 1.95% vs 1.56%, `error_rate` 0.00% on both. On a fixed 512-question greedy run +0.20 pp is one answer flipping -- read this as "no measurable accuracy cost", not as an improvement.

**Scope is wider than ROCm.** `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TRITON_ROUTER_GEMV` no longer exists; the path is selected by `router_gemv_supported()`, which tests `x.device.type == "cuda"` -- true for ROCm torch builds as well as NVIDIA. `SGLANG_OPT_USE_BF16_ROUTER_GEMM` already defaults true on `main`. So this is **on by default on NVIDIA too**, not an opt-in ROCm path, and reviewers should judge it on that basis. If you would rather it ship behind a flag, that is a code change and I am happy to make it.

The kernel fires roughly 57 launches per decode step, and its configs are per-M-bucket, so the win is batch-size dependent by construction -- hence the full bs 1-32 sweep rather than a single point.
## Reproduction

Server (identical on both sides):

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \
AITER_CONFIG_FMOE=/path/to/minimax_m3_mxfp8_tuned_fmoe.csv \
SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \
  --trust-remote-code --tp 8 --quantization mxfp8 \
  --moe-runner-backend aiter --fp8-gemm-backend auto \
  --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion --attention-backend triton \
  --dtype bfloat16 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
```

Benchmark:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server \
  --model None --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \
  --output-len 600 --skip-warmup \
  --batch-size 1 2 4 8 16 32 \
  --input-len 80000 --show-report --cache-hit-rate 0.9
```

Accuracy gate:

```bash
sgl-eval run gsm8k --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 \
  --num-examples 512 --num-threads 64 \
  --max-tokens 2048 --temperature 0 --seed 0
```

Two bench reps per boot, warm rep reported; noise floor +/-0.4%, established by a separate PR measuring flat under a config where its code cannot fire.

## Note on the launch command

`--moe-runner-backend aiter` is **not honoured on current `main`** for mxfp8. Arg resolution logs:

```
mxfp8 quantization supports only cutlass, deep_gemm, flashinfer_trtllm,
flashinfer_trtllm_routed, triton backends. Overriding 'aiter'.
```

and falls back to **triton**. Both sides of this A/B therefore ran the Triton MoE runner, so the comparison is apples-to-apples and the deltas stand — but `AITER_CONFIG_FMOE` is inert under this configuration and the aiter MoE path is *not* what was measured. The flag is kept in the command above only because it matches the invocation actually used; anyone reproducing will get triton and should see the same numbers.

title: MoE: small-batch sorting path with fused mxfp8 quantisation
author: zcnrex
body:
# MoE: single-launch small-batch sorting with fused mxfp8 activation quant

aiter's opus MoE sorting kernel is sized for thousands of tokens; at decode batch sizes it
costs roughly 7us/layer of launch and ramp overhead, and the separate
`fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort` stage1 activation quant costs another ~4us on top. When
the number of routing pairs `P = M * topk` is at most 64, the whole sorting job — stable
sort-by-expert, per-expert block padding, the expert-id table, `num_valid`, and the `moe_buf`
zero-fill — fits into one small Triton program built on `P x P` rank compares, and the stage1
mxfp8 quant rides the same launch on dedicated CTAs that recompute the (cheap) pair math
rather than cross-CTA synchronizing. This is installed as three runtime patch points on the
`aiter.fused_moe` module namespace (`fused_moe`, `_moe_sorting_impl`,
`fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort`), each falling back to the original aiter function
whenever the fast path does not apply, so a stock aiter install needs no changes; the patch is
applied lazily and idempotently from `AiterRunnerCore.__init__`, so nothing outside the aiter
MoE runner is affected. Two supporting changes ship in the same area: `sanitize_topk_ids`,
which lets the native gfx950 MXFP8 MoE skip its defensive `topk_ids` copy when expert
parallelism cannot produce a non-local id (see **Correctness**), and `aiter_swiglu_oai_limit`,
which recognizes the exact SwiGLU-OAI configuration that aiter's `ActivationType.Swiglu` bakes
in as compile-time constants (`alpha=1.702`, `(up + 1.0)`) so the bf16 aiter runner uses that
kernel instead of silently running plain SiLU — and, where the aiter CK bf16 fused-MoE has no
SwiGLU-OAI codegen at all, so that `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod` reports *why* the layer is
unsupported and falls back to the Triton runner.

Everything here is behind ROCm/aiter gates. `moe_sorting_small.py` is reachable only through
`apply_aiter_small_moe_sort_patch()`, called from `AiterRunnerCore.__init__`. The
`sanitize_topk_ids` plumbing only reaches a live code path inside
`quant_info.use_mxfp8 and is_hip() and is_gfx95_supported()`, and its default value is `True`,
i.e. exactly today's behaviour for any caller that does not pass it. The `unquant.py` changes
sit entirely inside the existing `_use_aiter and ... and get_moe_a2a_backend().supports_aiter()`
block. The default CUDA path is unchanged.

## Performance
Measured on 8x MI350X (gfx950), MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, TP8, 80k input / 600 output.
Two bench reps per boot; the warm (second) rep is reported and the two agreed
within 0.1%. Noise floor is +/-0.4%. Tables are the harness output verbatim,
trimmed to the first five columns. Baseline is `upstream/main`.
**Baseline (`upstream/main`)**

```
Input lens: [80000]. Output lens: [600]. Cache hit rate: 90.0%.
|   batch size |   input len |   latency (s) |   input throughput (tok/s) |   output throughput (tok/s) |
|--------------|-------------|---------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------|
|            1 |       80000 |         11.26 |                     187984 |                       55.35 |
|            2 |       80000 |         11.88 |                     191222 |                      108.68 |
|            4 |       80000 |         13.39 |                     192965 |                      204.62 |
|            8 |       80000 |         16.27 |                     193687 |                      370.13 |
|           16 |       80000 |         22.2  |                     193188 |                      616.28 |

|--------------|-------------|---------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------|
|            1 |       80000 |         10.82 |                     189765 |                       57.68 |

Output throughput +2.68%..+4.21%; input throughput +0.31%..+0.95%.

## Accuracy
gsm8k, 512 examples, `max_tokens 2048`, `temperature 0`, `seed 0`, against the
same server boot as the perf run.
**Baseline**

```
== gsm8k ==
512 examples (single-shot)  |  109.0s  |  1338 tok/s  |  146K tokens

* score           =  97.07%
  stop_rate       =  98.44%
  truncated_rate  =  1.56%  [warn: hitting max_tokens]
  error_rate      =  0.00%
```
**With this PR**

```
== gsm8k ==
512 examples (single-shot)  |  103.1s  |  1433 tok/s  |  148K tokens

* score           =  96.88%
  stop_rate       =  98.44%
  truncated_rate  =  1.56%  [warn: hitting max_tokens]
  error_rate      =  0.00%
```

The fast path is gated on `M * topk <= 64` and `<= 2 * block_size`, so the win concentrates at low batch (+4.2% at bs1) and tapers as the batch grows. bs32 holding at +2.7% is the check that matters on the other side: the fast path is inactive there, so those rows confirm the added wrapper predicates cost nothing on the fallback path.

## Correctness

`sanitize_topk_ids` is skipped only when the rank owns every expert. Solving the call-site condition `num_experts == num_local_experts` against `FusedMoE.__init__` -- where `num_local_experts = _num_global_routed // storage_ep_size + nfse` and `num_experts = _num_global_routed + num_shared_slots` -- yields `storage_ep_size == 1` in both branches of `num_shared_slots`. Under that condition every id the router can emit, routed ids and fused-shared slots alike, is in range by construction, so the sanitising mask has nothing to catch. This is textually the same predicate `main` already computes as `filter_expert` in `TritonRunnerCore.run` for the non-MXFP8 path, so the PR reuses an established notion rather than inventing one.

Two side conditions worth noting because they could have broken it: the skip path's `topk_ids.to(torch.int32)` can alias the caller's tensor where the default path used `copy=True`, which is safe only because `moe_align_block_size` is read-only on `topk_ids` and nothing after the branch mutates it; and the parameter defaults to `True`, so out-of-tree callers keep main's behaviour.

Accuracy was gated rather than assumed. gsm8k is **96.88% against a 97.07% baseline (-0.19 pp, one question of 512)**, with `stop_rate` 98.44% and `truncated_rate` 1.56% -- both **identical to baseline** -- and `error_rate` 0.00%. So the single flip is a real numerical difference, not a truncation artifact.

```bash

AITER_CONFIG_FMOE=/path/to/minimax_m3_mxfp8_tuned_fmoe.csv \
SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \
  --trust-remote-code --tp 8 --quantization mxfp8 \
  --moe-runner-backend aiter --fp8-gemm-backend auto \
  --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion --attention-backend triton \
  --dtype bfloat16 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
```

Benchmark:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server \
  --model None --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \
  --output-len 600 --skip-warmup \
  --batch-size 1 2 4 8 16 32 \
  --input-len 80000 --show-report --cache-hit-rate 0.9
```

Accuracy gate:

```bash
sgl-eval run gsm8k --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 \
  --num-examples 512 --num-threads 64 \
  --max-tokens 2048 --temperature 0 --seed 0
```

Two bench reps per boot, warm rep reported; noise floor +/-0.4%, established by a separate PR measuring flat under a config where its code cannot fire.

## Note on the launch command

`--moe-runner-backend aiter` is **not honoured on current `main`** for mxfp8. Arg resolution logs:

```
mxfp8 quantization supports only cutlass, deep_gemm, flashinfer_trtllm,
flashinfer_trtllm_routed, triton backends. Overriding 'aiter'.
```

and falls back to **triton**. Both sides of this A/B therefore ran the Triton MoE runner, so the comparison is apples-to-apples and the deltas stand — but `AITER_CONFIG_FMOE` is inert under this configuration and the aiter MoE path is *not* what was measured. The flag is kept in the command above only because it matches the invocation actually used; anyone reproducing will get triton and should see the same numbers.

title: MiniMax-M3: wave64 histogram-select decode top-k, and raise kMaxNumBlocks for CUDA graphs
author: zcnrex
body:
# kernels: wave64 histogram-select for the MiniMax-M3 decode top-k

The MiniMax-M3 decode block top-k (`minimax_decode_topk` / `minimax_decode_topk_page_table`) picks the `topk` highest-scoring KV blocks per (head, batch) row with one CTA per row. This PR adds a wave64 histogram-select implementation of that selection for ROCm, and raises `TopKTrait::kMaxNumBlocks` from 4096 to 16384. The ROCm path packs `(score, ~block_id)` into a `u64` total order, runs one coarse histogram round (256 bins for rows up to 1024, else 2048), refines with 11-bit rounds while more than 128 candidates remain, and finishes with a wave-0 bitonic sort over the survivors; bins above the threshold bin are emitted immediately, bins below die, and the threshold bin survives to the next round, so the row is still read from global memory exactly once. The block-id kernel's ascending-order emit now uses a single 64-lane ballot instead of two width-32 shuffle reductions, and `TopKTrait` becomes `TopKTraitImpl<kNumThreads>` so the ROCm launchers can select a 1024-thread instantiation when `max_seqblock > 1024` (CUDA still instantiates only the 512-thread trait). The `kMaxNumBlocks` bump is the part that matters beyond ROCm: under CUDA graph capture the sparse backend bounds `max_seqblock` by the model's **full** context length rather than by the batch's real sequence lengths (capture runs on tiny dummy `seq_lens`, so replay must not be able to exceed the captured bound), which means any context above `4096 * block_size` — 524288 tokens at `block_size = 128` — trips the `max_seqblock` `RuntimeCheck` at capture time and the kernel cannot be used under graphs at all. 16384 blocks lifts that to 2M tokens at `block_size = 128`. `_MAX_NUM_BLOCKS` in the Python wrapper mirrors the C++ constant and is asserted in both `minimax_decode_topk` and `minimax_decode_topk_page_table`.

Note for reviewers on the CUDA path: the selection code is untouched on CUDA, but `kIters = kMaxNumBlocks / kCTASize` is derived from the bumped constant, so the multi-element regime (`num_blocks > 512`) now caches up to 32 keys per thread in registers instead of 8. That is still exactly at the `static_assert(kIters <= 32)` liveness-bitmask limit and the per-slot `idx < num_blocks` guard makes the extra slots inert, but it does raise the register footprint of that regime on CUDA.

## Performance
Measured on 8x MI350X (gfx950), MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, TP8, 80k input / 600 output.
Two bench reps per boot; the warm (second) rep is reported and the two agreed
within 0.1%. Noise floor is +/-0.4%. Tables are the harness output verbatim,
trimmed to the first five columns. Baseline is `upstream/main`.
**Baseline (`upstream/main`)**

```
Input lens: [80000]. Output lens: [600]. Cache hit rate: 90.0%.
|   batch size |   input len |   latency (s) |   input throughput (tok/s) |   output throughput (tok/s) |
|--------------|-------------|---------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------|
|            1 |       80000 |         11.26 |                     187984 |                       55.35 |
|            2 |       80000 |         11.88 |                     191222 |                      108.68 |
|            4 |       80000 |         13.39 |                     192965 |                      204.62 |
|            8 |       80000 |         16.27 |                     193687 |                      370.13 |
|           16 |       80000 |         22.2  |                     193188 |                      616.28 |
|           32 |       80000 |         33.78 |                     193245 |                      934.92 |
```
**With this PR**

```
Input lens: [80000]. Output lens: [600]. Cache hit rate: 90.0%.
|   batch size |   input len |   latency (s) |   input throughput (tok/s) |   output throughput (tok/s) |
|--------------|-------------|---------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------|
|            1 |       80000 |         10.74 |                     188221 |                       58.15 |
|            2 |       80000 |         11.43 |                     192364 |                      113.24 |
|            4 |       80000 |         13.08 |                     194179 |                      209.9  |
|            8 |       80000 |         15.8  |                     194488 |                      383.69 |
|           16 |       80000 |         21.69 |                     194105 |                      635.86 |
|           32 |       80000 |         33.11 |                     193734 |                      964.84 |
```
Output throughput +2.58%..+5.06%; input throughput +0.13%..+0.63%.

## Correctness

The top-k selection semantics are unchanged -- this is a different reduction strategy (wave64 histogram select) over the same scores, not a different selection rule. Verified by gate rather than asserted: gsm8k **97.27% against a 97.07% baseline (+0.20 pp, one question of 512)**, `truncated_rate` **1.17% vs 1.56%** (i.e. below baseline) and `error_rate` 0.00%. Read as "no measurable accuracy cost".

Caveat on precision: this is a **single gate run**. The eval is not as deterministic as `temperature 0, seed 0` suggests -- SGLang batches requests dynamically, so fp accumulation order (and therefore greedy token choices) varies between runs. Repeating the same gate on another PR in this series gave 96.88% and 96.29% on two independent, uncontaminated runs, i.e. a **~0.6 pp run-to-run spread**. So read +0.20 pp as "within run-to-run noise", not as a measured improvement, and treat any single number here as having roughly that uncertainty.

## What the kMaxNumBlocks bump actually unblocks

`kMaxNumBlocks` 4096 -> 16384 is the load-bearing half of this PR, and it is not cosmetic. `MiniMaxSparseAttnBackend` pins `_max_seqlen_k = self.max_context_len` during CUDA-graph capture (capture runs on tiny dummy `seq_lens`, so replay must not exceed the captured bound), which makes `max_seqblock = ceil(context_len / block_size)`. At 4096 that caps out at 524288 tokens with `block_size = 128`; anything longer trips the `max_seqblock` `RuntimeCheck` **at capture time**, which is why the kernel was unusable under graphs at long context. 16384 lifts the ceiling to ~2M. The existing registered tests already sweep `max_ctx` up to exactly 524288 at block 128 -- i.e. the old ceiling.

The evidence that matters for this half is therefore a **graph-capture-on** run (no `--disable-cuda-graph`), which is how every number above was measured, not a microbenchmark.

One consequence a reviewer will want flagged: the bump is **not** a no-op on the CUDA path. `kIters = kMaxNumBlocks / kCTASize` is derived from it, so the `num_blocks > 512` regime now caches 32 keys per thread in registers instead of 8. It remains correct -- exactly at `static_assert(kIters <= 32)`, the uint32 liveness-bitmask limit, with the per-slot `idx < num_blocks` guard making extra slots inert -- but the register footprint of that regime grows.

`_MAX_NUM_BLOCKS` in the Python wrapper must stay in sync with `TopKTrait::kMaxNumBlocks`; it is asserted in both entry points (`minimax_decode_topk` and `minimax_decode_topk_page_table`).
## Reproduction

Server (identical on both sides):

```bash

AITER_CONFIG_FMOE=/path/to/minimax_m3_mxfp8_tuned_fmoe.csv \
SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \
  --trust-remote-code --tp 8 --quantization mxfp8 \
  --moe-runner-backend aiter --fp8-gemm-backend auto \
  --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion --attention-backend triton \
  --dtype bfloat16 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
```

Benchmark:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server \
  --model None --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \
  --output-len 600 --skip-warmup \
  --batch-size 1 2 4 8 16 32 \
  --input-len 80000 --show-report --cache-hit-rate 0.9
```

Accuracy gate:

```bash
sgl-eval run gsm8k --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 \
  --num-examples 512 --num-threads 64 \
  --max-tokens 2048 --temperature 0 --seed 0
```

Two bench reps per boot, warm rep reported; noise floor +/-0.4%, established by a separate PR measuring flat under a config where its code cannot fire.

## Note on the launch command

`--moe-runner-backend aiter` is **not honoured on current `main`** for mxfp8. Arg resolution logs:

flashinfer_trtllm_routed, triton backends. Overriding 'aiter'.

Both sides of this A/B therefore ran the Triton MoE runner, so the comparison is apples-to-apples and the deltas stand — but `AITER_CONFIG_FMOE` is inert under this configuration and the aiter MoE path is *not* what was measured. title: perf: skip redundant scheduler metadata gather for DP1
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

When the attention DP size is 1, scheduler metadata is already local and rank-invariant. Gathering the same batch mode, graph eligibility, and token counts across the TP schedulers adds a device collective and host synchronization without reconciling any cross-DP state.

SGLang already exposes `SGLANG_SCHEDULER_SKIP_ALL_GATHER` as a manual override. This PR makes the skip the default for DP1 while preserving the existing opt-in behavior for larger DP sizes.

## Modifications

- Skip the scheduler metadata all-gather automatically when `dp_size == 1`.
- Preserve the existing environment override for deployments that explicitly skip the gather with multiple DP ranks.
- Finalize the single-rank metadata locally so TBO split metadata, global/recv forward mode, token counts, graph eligibility, and optional DP metrics remain available without the collective.
- Keep the existing multi-DP no-override path unchanged.
- Add registered CPU unit coverage for the skip policy and the DP1 local-metadata/TBO path.

## Accuracy Tests

This does not change model math or model outputs; it changes scheduler-side metadata synchronization for DP1.

Targeted checks:

- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Python syntax compilation for the changed source and test: passed.
- The two focused unit-test cases pass in an isolated import harness.
- GitHub lint check: passed.
- The current-main A/B below completed all 2 warmup and 8 measurement requests per arm with HTTP 200 and exact prompt/completion token counts.

The local macOS environment cannot collect the full SGLang test module because its installed dependency set conflicts with the repository (`transformers` duplicate `qwen3_asr` registration and missing optional packages such as `dill`, `datasets`, and `openai`). Full CPU CI is therefore left to the registered `base-a-test-cpu` shard.

Remaining validation scope:

- DP1 extend and mixed batches.
- Overlap scheduler enabled and disabled.
- PP configurations.
- DP1 with DP attention enabled.
- Confirm multi-DP configurations retain the existing gather path unless the override is explicitly enabled.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

A direct matched A/B was run on main commit `8739d56a319a5e2e5cb46eb557971d0b43bd2443`. The candidate applied the exact PR head patch (`ae16c5ccfec8c7ba0a1edda07e690d592b3a5074`) to that base; it did not set `SGLANG_SCHEDULER_SKIP_ALL_GATHER`, so the candidate exercised the automatic DP1 path implemented by this PR.

- Baseline job: `3325732`
- PR candidate job: `3325736`

| Metric | Main | PR candidate | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Pure decode TPS/user | 351.46 | 391.70 | **+11.45%** |
| Pure decode TPS/GPU | 43.93 | 48.96 | **+11.45%** |
| Mean decode step latency | 14.336 ms | 12.852 ms | **-10.35%** |
| Full-request completion TPS | 168.87 | 178.37 | **+5.63%** |
| Mean request latency | 6.064 s | 5.741 s | **-5.33%** |
| Mean TTFT | 3.148 s | 3.128 s | -0.64% |

Matched runtime contract:

- 2 nodes x 4 GB300 GPUs, TP8/DP1/EP1/PP1.
- DP attention disabled, actual sequential batch size 1, CUDA Graph bucket 8.
- Radix cache disabled; observed prefill cached-token values were `[0]`.
- Exact ISL/OSL 89,472/1,024, 2 warmup requests, and 8 measurement requests per arm.
- Same model, container, input hash, client hash, backend configuration, and effective simulated acceptance length (5.04).
- Observed batch values `[1]`, CUDA Graph values `[True]`, queue values `[0]`, with no fallback or hard-error markers during measurement.

The benefit is decode-specific: mean TTFT was effectively unchanged while mean decode step latency dropped by 10.35%. The full-request result includes the unchanged prefill portion, so its improvement is smaller than the strict pure-decode result. This run also confirms that the redundant DP1 gather can affect configurations with DP attention disabled.

This is a focused one-job-per-arm measurement on separate matched two-node allocations, not a repeated statistical benchmark. Historical testing of the pre-existing manual override on the frozen benchmark stack showed the same direction with an 18.01% TPS/user improvement; the direct current-main A/B above is the primary result for this PR.

Evidence and broader experiment context:

- [S1 upstream plan and attribution boundary](https://github.com/YAMY1234/task-status/blob/main/agentx-tp8-low-latency-gap/UPSTREAM-PLAN.md#s1--dp1-%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E8%B7%B3%E8%BF%87-scheduler-metadata-all-gather)
- [Historical matched fixed-B1 decode results](https://github.com/YAMY1234/task-status/blob/main/agentx-tp8-low-latency-gap/DECODE-ONLY-A2A.md#optimization-result)

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not applicable: this is an internal scheduler optimization.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (No model math/output change; direct current-main speed evidence and its scope are above.)

title: MiniMax-M3: MXFP8 dense-only block convert + aiter MXFP8 MoE on gfx950
author: zcnrex
body:
# MiniMax-M3: MXFP8 dense-only block convert + aiter MXFP8 MoE on gfx950

Branch: `m3/mxfp8-dense-block-convert` · base: `main` · **depends on #36559** (land it first) · `m3/fused-norm-fp8-quant` sits on top of this

> **Merge order:** #36559 must land before this PR. This PR's aiter MXFP8 MoE path passes `activation` through `fused_moe_kwargs`. On `main`, the aiter runner also passes `activation=` explicitly, so `fused_moe` raises `TypeError: got multiple values for keyword argument 'activation'`. #36559 pops it (`extra.pop("activation")`). Without #36559, this head reproduces the TypeError at graph capture on MI350X with `--moe-runner-backend aiter`.

MXFP8 checkpoints on gfx950 currently offer two all-or-nothing choices. Either every weight stays on the native MX per-1x32 `dot_scaled` path, or every weight is converted to block-fp8 `[128, 128]` at load (`SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT`) and runs on the aiter block-scale kernels. Neither works for MiniMax-M3. The dense linears want the block-scale kernels, but converting the fused-MoE weights as well routes the MoE to a block-scale kernel that has no SwiGLU-OAI activation.

This PR adds four things:

- **`SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE`** (HIP only, default off). It converts only the MXFP8 dense linears to block-fp8. The fused-MoE weights stay MX per-1x32.
- **Small-M rowwise-fp8 path.** When the block-fp8 runner is `aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` on gfx950, each converted dense layer also caches a rowwise-fp8 (per-token x per-channel) copy of its weight. At or below `MXFP8_DENSE_PTPC_DECODE_MAX_M = 128` tokens, the ptpc GEMM is used.
- **aiter MXFP8 MoE.** MXFP8 MoE weights are pre-shuffled with `shuffle_weight_a16w4` / `shuffle_scale_a16w4` and run through the aiter `PER_1X32` path with SwiGLU-OAI (`GateMode.INTERLEAVE`). Any `gemm1_alpha` other than 1.702 is rejected with `NotImplementedError`.
- **Making that MoE path reachable.** `_moe_runner_backend_quant_constraints` used to override `--moe-runner-backend aiter` to triton for every MXFP8 model. On gfx950 it now keeps `aiter` when `SGLANG_USE_AITER` is set; `maybe_get_hip_aiter_quant_info` builds nothing without aiter. Without aiter the request still falls back to triton. A case in `test_model_overrides.py::test_moe_runner_quant_constraint_pass` pins both branches.

## Behaviour notes

- **CUDA is unaffected.** Every new path is gated on `_is_hip`, `_is_gfx95_supported` or `_use_aiter`, or on the new env var.
- **Defaults do not move.** `--moe-runner-backend auto` still resolves to triton for gfx950 MXFP8, and the env var defaults off. The new paths need an explicit `--moe-runner-backend aiter` together with `SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1`.
- **The rowwise-fp8 path also applies under the existing `SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT=1`** on gfx950 with aiter, because both modes produce converted dense layers.

## Scope trimmed during review

An earlier revision also carried a `torch._scaled_mm` Blockwise-1x32 route, which silently moved the gfx950 `auto` default for every MXFP8 model. It also carried a `--fp8-gemm-backend bf16` choice, behaviour-neutral refactors of `dispatch_w8a8_mxfp8_linear` and the `minimax_m3` fused-QKV holder, and a `_fp8_qinput` consumer whose producer is in `m3/fused-norm-fp8-quant`. None of these is reachable in the measured configuration, so all were removed.

A load-time `NameError` (`shuffle_weight` is only imported with aiter) under `SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT(_DENSE)=1` with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0` was fixed.

## Validation

8x MI350X (gfx950) devbox, GPUs 4-7, **TP4**, MiniMax-M3-MXFP8. Setup: ROCm 10 venv, triton 3.8, aiter `acf8fdf93` (the `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` pin). `bench_one_batch_server` was run with two reps per boot, and the warm (second) rep is reported. gsm8k is 512 examples, 5-shot chat, `max_tokens 2048`, `temperature 0`, `seed 0`.

**aiter vs triton MoE**, both on this head merged with #36559 and `SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1`:

| MoE backend | gsm8k | output tok/s, 80k in / 600 out, cache hit 0.9, bs 1 / 4 / 16 | output tok/s, 1k in / 256 out, bs 64 / 128 / 256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `triton` | 97.66% | 88.39 / 294.39 / 720.66 | 2182 / 3664 / 5956 |
| **`aiter`** | **97.85%** | **121.02 / 384.39 / 910.29** | **2747 / 4669 / 7379** |

With aiter MoE, output throughput is +37% / +31% / +26% at bs 1 / 4 / 16 and +24% to +27% at bs 64-256. Input throughput is about +21%.

**Dense path vs `main`** (triton MoE, this PR before #36559, before the latest `main` merge):

| tree | gsm8k | output tok/s bs1 / bs4 / bs16 (80k / 600) |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (default launch) | 97.66% | 67.03 / 231.88 / 614.91 |
| this PR, dense-only convert | 98.44% | 80.84 / 258.60 / 685.84 |

Other checks:
- `MXFP8_DENSE_PTPC_DECODE_MAX_M = 128` is a conservative cutoff, not a tuned crossover. A single-GPU microbenchmark of `aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` on the M3 TP4 dense shapes has ptpc faster than block-fp8 at every M up to 512 on qkv, o_proj and the dense MLP. It is slower only on the narrow shared-expert shapes past M = 64 (K = 768) or M = 256 (N = 1536). Per-GEMM relative error against bf16 is 3.9% for ptpc and 3.8% for block-fp8.
- `SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1` with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0` loads and serves (the earlier revision raised `NameError`).
- gsm8k noise: runs of the same tree differ by a few questions out of 512. Earlier TP8 `sgl-eval` runs read -1.17 pp for the dense path; treat both as noise-level.

Not executed: TP8 on this head, and a `max_tokens 4096` gsm8k run.

## Reproduction

With #36559 applied:

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto \
  --tp 4 --quantization mxfp8 --dtype bfloat16 \
  --moe-runner-backend aiter --fp8-gemm-backend auto \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31000
```

```bash
python3 -m sglang.bench_one_batch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 --base-url http://127.0.0.1:31000 \
  --batch-size 1 4 16 --input-len 80000 --output-len 600 \
  --cache-hit-rate 0.9 --show-report
```

title: MiniMax-M3: allow shared-experts fusion on ROCm gfx942 and newer
author: zcnrex
body:
# MiniMax-M3: allow shared-experts fusion on ROCm gfx942 and newer

`shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason` currently refuses on any non-CUDA device, so ROCm never gets shared-experts fusion even where the hardware supports it. This lifts that guard and gates it at gfx942 instead.

`minimax_m3_vl.py` carries the identical gate. `MiniMaxM3SparseForCausalLM` and `MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration` are separate `EntryClass`es with separate `shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason` classmethods, and the served MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 checkpoint is the **VL** variant (`model_type: minimax_m3_vl`, per `configs/minimax_vl.py`) — so patching only one file would be a silent no-op on the model people actually run.

## Measurement status — stated plainly

**This PR has no benchmark or accuracy numbers of its own, and I am not claiming any.**

The earlier combined change (this gate + the alternate-stream overlap + a `prefill_attention_backend=aiter` serving default) measured +46.6%..+55.4% output throughput on 8x MI350X. That number belongs to the bundle, not to this PR, and decomposing it showed the input-throughput share came **entirely** from the serving default, not from either code change.

More importantly: in every run measured, the server reported `shared_experts_fusion=False` on both sides — the fusion this PR enables **never actually engaged**, because it also requires the model config and serving flags to request it. So the throughput effect of *this* gate specifically is unmeasured.

What this PR is, therefore, is an enablement gate: it removes a platform restriction that has no reason to exist on gfx942+. It should be reviewed on that basis, and someone with a configuration that genuinely turns fusion on should measure it before it is treated as a performance change.

The serving-defaults and cookbook half is a separate change and is not part of this PR.

title: [Diffusion][Kernel] Fuse Wan FFN GELU epilogue
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Wan's feed-forward blocks execute the first projection and `gelu_pytorch_tanh`
as separate kernels. On H100, the standalone GELU accounts for 401 launches and
159.064 ms in a five-step denoising profile of Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B.

This PR reuses the existing quality-gated cublasLt linear+GELU epilogue so the
optimization remains opt-in under `quality=high`; `quality=lossless` keeps the
existing operator sequence and output exactly.

## Modifications

- add a Wan-specific `_WanGELUMLP` for the standard and VSA transformer blocks;
- mark its input projection as an existing fused-linear-GELU site and dispatch
  to `fused_linear_gelu_tanh` only when the quality gate and shape/backend guards
  pass;
- preserve the original `fc_in -> gelu_pytorch_tanh -> fc_out` fallback;
- add a CUDA unit test for the unmounted, mounted, and exact restored paths; and
- document the Wan `quality=high` path in the diffusion performance skill.

## Accuracy Tests

Hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB.  
Model: `Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers` at revision
`0fad780a534b6463e45facd96134c9f345acfa5b`.  
Workload: 832x480, 81 frames, 50 denoising steps, guidance 3, seed 42,
native SGLang backend.

Two repeated candidate outputs had the same SHA-256. Against the unfused
`quality=high` baseline, first/middle/last key frames measured:

| Frame | SSIM | PSNR (dB) |
|---|---:|---:|
| first | 0.960655 | 36.12 |
| middle | 0.954638 | 34.32 |
| last | 0.947188 | 33.75 |

The unit test also verifies that unmounting the fast path restores bit-exact
lossless output.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same-GPU A-B-B-A results, with one warmed request per process:

| Run | Path | Denoising (ms) | End-to-end (ms) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| A1 | baseline high | 45,206.34 | 47,033.41 |
| B1 | fused high | 44,332.17 | 46,159.79 |
| B2 | fused high | 44,396.44 | 46,224.51 |
| A2 | baseline high | 45,268.19 | 47,095.86 |
| mean A | baseline high | 45,237.27 | 47,064.64 |
| mean B | fused high | 44,364.31 | 46,192.15 |

This is a **1.93% denoising** and **1.85% end-to-end** speedup.

Five-step GPU traces on the same source revision show:

| Metric | Baseline high | Fused high |
|---|---:|---:|
| GPU kernel time | 5,859.373 ms | 5,720.200 ms |
| Kernel launches | 14,268 | 13,911 |
| Standalone GELU | 159.064 ms / 401 | 0.030 ms / 12 |

The same path was also validated on
`FastVideo/FastWan2.2-TI2V-5B-FullAttn-Diffusers` revision
`3e187042a324f6f5fb68fd22110a78725253de8f` at 1280x720x81, using its native
three-step `WanDMDPipeline` preset. Against current main `5adc2880f9`, the
same-GPU A-B-B-A means were 1,374.930/1,352.524 ms denoise and
7,106.139/7,070.196 ms E2E (baseline/fused): **1.63% denoise** and **0.51%
end-to-end**. Candidate outputs were repeatable within the arm; candidate
versus baseline first/middle/last key frames measured SSIM
0.938424/0.928753/0.931103 and PSNR 32.16/30.47/30.27 dB.

Its three-step trace confirms the kernel mechanism independently: total CUDA
launches fall from 2,400 to 2,311, standalone BF16 GELU falls from
90 launches / 32.571 ms to 2 launches / 0.007 ms, and the corresponding GEMM
uses the cublasLt `gelubias` epilogue. Total GPU kernel time falls from
1,330.489 to 1,310.310 ms (1.52%). This sibling result is supporting evidence;
the primary Wan2.1 workload above remains the end-to-end performance gate.

Wan does not currently support BCG, so no BCG performance claim is made.

Tests:

```text
pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_sites.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_wan_gelu_mlp.py
23 passed
```

Selected pre-commit checks for the changed files also pass. After rebasing onto
official main `a3ae667d67`, the same 23 tests passed again on H100 at exact PR
head `cdbe8b63b8`. Official targeted H100 CI run
[`33034992448`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33034992448)
also passed `test_wan_gelu_mlp.py` at that exact head.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [AMD] Enable GLM-5.3-Flash on gfx942 and gfx950
author: andyluo7
body:
## Motivation

[#36507](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36507) adds the upstream GLM-5.3-Flash model implementation. This stacked PR makes that implementation run correctly and efficiently on AMD ROCm gfx942 and gfx950 without adding model-name checks to shared engine paths.

This PR intentionally targets `xinyuan/glm-5.3-flash-support`. Its current dependency head is `c4d5d45e506dcd978a65661a503eda1a272c39a4`.

## Modifications

### ROCm enablement and loading

- Add the ROCm KPool/AITER paged-MQA path and its required preshuffled cache layout.
- Use the portable unfused Torch DSA top-k path on non-gfx95 ROCm while preserving gfx950's fused SGL-kernel path.
- Support KPool tail widths in the DSA index transform while preserving the existing 2,048-column single-program path.
- Handle GLM's zero-width RoPE tail and gate unavailable DeepGEMM/TileLang mHC paths on ROCm.
- Keep AITER weight preshuffling owned by the selected MoE runner and apply the SwiGLU clamp contract on the Triton ROCm path.
- Support mixed Quark MXFP4 and explicitly block-quantized FP8 checkpoint loading.

### gfx950 performance paths

- Enable shared-expert fusion for GLM when the AITER gfx95 path is active.
- Enable the existing fused k-pool top-k/expand/page-transform JIT path on HIP for supported group-top-k sizes.
- Dispatch GLM mHC pre/post through AITER on HIP gfx95 when `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`.
- Fuse the attention mHC post operation with the following FFN mHC pre operation through the existing AITER boundary implementation.

The mHC paths are gated on HIP + gfx95 + `SGLANG_USE_AITER`. CUDA retains its existing dispatch and behavior.

## Accuracy validation

The original ROCm enablement was validated on the earlier engine head `9e692c9216c3b5e5c443fecf6b995700eb68d2e4`:

| GPU | Full GSM8K | Request accounting |
|---|---:|---|
| MI300X / gfx942 | 1,284 / 1,319 = **97.35%** | 1,319 unique records; 0 errors or empty generations |
| MI355X / gfx950 | 1,288 / 1,319 = **97.65%** | 1,319 unique records; 0 errors or empty generations |

The current performance head adds backend-equivalent mHC dispatch and boundary fusion. Its focused validation is listed below; full GSM8K has not been rerun on this head.

## MI355X performance validation

### Provenance and workload

- PR head: `9d208769398882e20220cb97722bf610397e66d8`
- Hardware: 8x AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`)
- Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x`
- Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, revision `3f1971b7b5f7a528c9c4ef6212c8785298a8c24a`
- TP8 / EP1, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, AITER MoE, TileLang DSA
- Full decode graphs at batch sizes 1 and 32; prefill graphs disabled
- Random dataset, seed 42, 1,024 input tokens, 1,024 output tokens
- Ignore EOS enabled, radix cache disabled, infinite request rate
- AITER BF16 table from [ROCm/aiter#5060](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5060)

`total throughput` is input plus output tokens divided by benchmark duration. `median interactivity` is `1000 / median TPOT_ms`.

| Case | Requests | Total throughput | Median TPOT | Median interactivity |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| concurrency 1 | 10/10 | **287.85 tok/s** | 6.8675 ms | **145.61 tok/s/user** |
| concurrency 32 | 320/320 | **5,731.36 tok/s** | 10.6696 ms | **93.72 tok/s/user** |

All 330 measured requests completed with exactly 1,024 input and 1,024 output tokens and empty error strings. Both clients and the supervisor exited zero; server exit 143 is the intentional post-benchmark SIGTERM. Post-run process, port, KFD, GPU-use, and kernel-fault checks were clean.

### B200 comparison

The matched B200 reference used TP8/EP8, FP8 KV cache, DeepGEMM MoE, TRT-LLM DSA, the same random 1K/1K workload, and the same request accounting. Its raw JSON is no longer available locally, so these are recorded outputs from that preceding run.

| Case | B200 total | MI355X total | MI355X/B200 | B200 interactivity | MI355X interactivity | MI355X/B200 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| concurrency 1 | 319.18 | 287.85 | **90.18%** | 163.40 | 145.61 | **89.11%** |
| concurrency 32 | 5,670.46 | 5,731.36 | **101.07%** | 95.30 | 93.72 | **98.35%** |

Both workloads exceed the target of 80% of B200 for total throughput and median interactivity.

### Why the mHC integration is required

The published pre-mHC head `91c66b874ac56ad9a79598de5f89156a9d33014a` was run with the same MI355X serving configuration:

| Case | Pre-mHC total throughput | Current total throughput | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| concurrency 1 | 53.08 tok/s | 287.85 tok/s | **5.42x** |
| concurrency 32 | 1,326.39 tok/s | 5,731.36 tok/s | **4.32x** |

The pre-mHC log enabled shared-expert fusion but never selected AITER mHC. The current log reports both `Using AITER gfx950 mHC pre/post kernels` and `Using fused AITER mHC attention-to-FFN boundary` on all eight ranks.

### K-pool kernel evidence

For the 1K-to-2K decode interval, the fused k-pool operation measured about 8.8–9.6 us versus 159–164 us for the previous ROCm path, a 16.9–18.2x kernel-level speedup. The focused test verifies identical selected physical-token sets. The select-all fast path can produce a different ordering than `torch.topk`; DSA attention is permutation-invariant over the selected set, but this is not a bitwise-output-equivalence claim.

## Tests

- AITER mHC and fused-boundary tests on MI355X: `18 passed`, `5 subtests passed`.
- GLM/shared-expert/k-pool focused selection on MI355X: `53 passed`, `4 subtests passed`, `1 deselected`.
  - The deselected dependency-owned case is explicitly an off-ROCm assertion and observes valid ROCm behavior when executed on gfx950.
- All changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, isort, clang-format, codespell, and registered-test validation.
- Current GitHub lint check passes. GPU suites remain skipped until maintainers apply the repository's CI labels.

## Checklist

- [x] Keep CUDA behavior unchanged through explicit backend gates.
- [x] Add CPU and gfx95 regression coverage.
- [x] Validate exact request/token accounting and post-run GPU health.
- [x] Publish model-specific BF16 tuning separately in ROCm/aiter#5060.
- [ ] After ROCm/aiter#5060 merges, advance SGLang's `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT` to a merged AITER commit that contains it, unless a routine AITER pin update lands it first.
- [ ] Request `run-ci` and AMD CI labels from a maintainer.
- [x] Publish the cookbook/performance recipe separately in #36732.

title: docs(cookbook): fix Qwen3.8 Flash Next H200 MTP verify with BF16 SSM state
author: huangzhilin-hzl
body:
## Summary

- pin Triton as the linear-attention verify backend for the H200 BF16 and FP8 low-latency recipes
- keep FlashInfer as the prefill and decode backend

## Motivation

The H200 low-latency recipes combine NEXTN with `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16`. On SM90, the FlashInfer MTP verify path requires fp32 SSM state, so auto-selecting it can fail during target verify CUDA graph capture with:

```text
AssertionError: initial_state must be float32, got torch.bfloat16

#34592 made SGLang honor an explicitly selected Triton verify backend while intentionally leaving auto selection unchanged. The verified Cookbook commands therefore need to opt into that backend explicitly.

## Validation

- `node docs/scripts/check_cookbook_configs.mjs`

- H20 SM90, TP8/EP8, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`: server startup, target verify CUDA graph capture, `/health`, and a Chat Completions smoke request succeeded

title: Add SGLANG_CRASH_ON_JIT_COMPILE to forbid on-the-fly JIT compilation
body:
## Motivation

Container deployments can pre-seed the JIT build cache at image build time:
the build key is a deterministic function of source content, compiler/package
versions, and target arch — no device, host, or timestamp inputs — so a cache
compiled without a GPU is valid at runtime. What such deployments need from
the loader is not a second lookup location but a guarantee: if the seeded
cache silently stops matching (e.g. dependency-hash drift between the build
and runtime environments), startup should fail loudly instead of silently
paying a multi-second cold compile.

## Modifications

- `SGLANG_CRASH_ON_JIT_COMPILE` (default off): when set, `load_jit` raises
  instead of compiling when a module misses the cache. The check runs before
  taking the build lock — with the flag set no process ever publishes a
  build, so waiting on the lock cannot turn the miss into a hit. The error
  names the module and the searched scope.
- Extract `cache_root()` from `build_key_dir()` so external tooling that
  seeds the cache resolves the root exactly the way the loader does.

This replaces the earlier revision of this PR (a read-only fallback cache
directory): seeding the regular cache dir externally needs no extra lookup
tier or env var in the loader, and the crash flag gives the fail-loud
guarantee. Verified on an internal deployment: cache pre-seeded at image
build time, a per-arch verification pass reloads every module with the flag
set (so dependency drift fails the image build), and at runtime all seeded
modules load as plain cache hits.

## Original commits

- `5e7a84fc82`
- `1a54aa4e14`

title: [Cohere Command-A-Plus] Optimize decode and BCG capture on SM10X
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

Three changes, all SM10X.

**One stream, not one per layer.** `Cohere2MoeSparseMoeBlock.__init__` called `torch.cuda.Stream()`, so the model built 32 of them. The caching allocator segments its pool per stream, and prefill capture then ran to 19.02 GiB of graph pool plus 23.83 GiB stranded as reserved-but-unallocated, past the ~45.7 GiB of headroom. It OOM'd, which is why the breakable CUDA graph (BCG) prefill backend was unusable here. Leasing the shared `get_stream("alt")` cuts capture to 5.34 GB and puts the arch on the breakable allowlist.

**Overlap the parallel block.** `y = x + attn(norm(x)) + mlp(norm(x))` makes the two halves independent, but they ran back to back on one stream, and at decode neither fills the GPU. The MLP moves to a second side stream, giving three concurrent chains. Two things come with that. `FusedMoE` takes `inplace=False`, since the default aliases the routed-expert output onto its input and would overwrite the post-layernorm buffer while `qkv_proj` still reads it on the other stream. And the fork/join runs only under `forward_mode.is_decode()`, since `get_is_capture_mode()` covers prefill chunks too.

**Pin the MoE runner.** `auto` emits routing, `expandInputRows`, activation and finalize as separate kernels around the expert GEMM, all of which trtllm-gen folds into one. The gate fires only on unquantized or positively-NVFP4 checkpoints — compressed-tensors FP8 stays on `auto`, since `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8MoE` hands trtllm-gen a `TritonMoeQuantInfo` it rejects at the first forward.

## Results

4x GB300 (SM103), tp=4, random 8192-in / 1024-out, `--num-prompts 4*C`, `--warmup-requests 2*C`.

Both sides run `--mem-fraction-static 0.75` and `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`, so the tables measure this change rather than the backend switch. That framing is generous to the baseline: at the default mem-fraction there is no before column at all, because capture OOMs, and 0.75 only buys it back by giving up ~10% of the KV cache (6,362,112 -> 5,710,976 tokens).

### w4a4 (NVFP4)

|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

title: [Sampling] Capture masks from sampler support
author: ByronHsu
body:
## Problem

Sampling-mask replay must return the exact final support

```
S_t = {i | w_t[i] > 0}
```

and the sampled token logprob under that filtered distribution. The previous implementation reconstructed top-k/top-p/min-p support from the original probabilities after sampling, then repaired the reconstruction by adding the sampled token when necessary. Backend cutoff, tie, and filter-order semantics could make that reconstruction differ from the support actually used by the sampler. Sampled-token repair ensured only that the action was present; it could not restore other missing tokens or remove extra tokens, so replay could normalize over the wrong action space.

## Changes

- Add a private `_SamplingMaskCapture` carrying post-filter weights, an optional token-ID permutation, and the selected weight.
- Make `_sample_from_probs` return capture data only when sampling masks are requested.
- Reuse the exact sorted and filtered weights used by the PyTorch multinomial path.
- Reproduce FlashInfer effective joint top-k/top-p support with matching renormalization and intersection semantics; apply FlashInfer min-p capture sequentially as top-k → top-p → min-p.
- Represent greedy support as the selected-token singleton.
- Attach masks after token synchronization, define support strictly as `weights > 0`, and compute `log(w[y] / sum(w))` from the same capture.
- Treat a sampled token outside positive captured support as an internal invariant failure instead of repairing the mask.
- Remove post-hoc support reconstruction and sampled-token repair.
- Keep the existing synchronous ragged CPU return path and public response fields. Fixed-cap async D2H transport and overlap-scheduling support remain for a follow-up PR.

## Tests

- Registered sampling-mask suite in `test/registered/sampling/test_sampling_mask.py` covering FlashInfer and PyTorch.
- Exact support and selected-token logprob checks, including cutoff ties whose support exceeds `top_k`.
- `/generate`, chat completions, output alignment, rejection behavior, and seeded deterministic sampling coverage.
- H200 validation with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`: 9 tests passed.
- Python compilation, `git diff --check`, and relevant pre-commit hooks passed.

title: [Sampling] Support sampling masks with overlap scheduling
author: ByronHsu
body:
## Motivation

Sampling masks currently do not support overlap scheduling because materializing the masks inside the sampler synchronizes the GPU with the CPU.

## Modifications

1. Remove CPU synchronization from sampling-mask capture. Keep sampling-mask outputs on the GPU inside the sampler, then copy them asynchronously to the CPU and materialize the response data during result processing.
2. Introduce `--sampling-mask-max-tokens` (default: `4096`) to set the maximum number of tokens per sampling mask.
3. Reject sampling-mask requests upfront if `top_k` exceeds the configured mask capacity.
4. Abort the request with an overflow error if the realized mask exceeds the capacity, including when cutoff ties produce more tokens than `top_k` even though `top_k` is within the limit.
5. Mark sampling results as invalid if validation fails, such as when the selected-token logprob is non-finite (`NaN` or infinity). Abort the request before committing the failed step's sampled token.
6. Replace `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_SAMPLING_MASK_MAX_TOKENS` with the server argument `--sampling-mask-max-tokens` for both ordinary and disaggregated serving. PD metadata remains off by default: set `SGLANG_ENABLE_DISAGG_SAMPLING_MASK=1` on both prefill and decode servers. Without it, requests asking for masks receive HTTP 400 with the required setting; unused metadata buffers are neither allocated nor transferred. Startup rejects the retired `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_SAMPLING_MASK_MAX_TOKENS` variable with explicit migration instructions.

## Accuracy Tests

Current head `d73bc1bd7f`; review fixes verified at `1d542447e5` on BJ job `3439034` (NVIDIA H200, `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13`):

- 240 affected unit tests and 35 subtests passed. Before-fix tests reproduced premature KV slot reuse during offload, lost error types/cleanup interruption on prefill abort, and all eight legacy-env configurations silently starting.
- Live TP2/PP1 and TP1/PP2 sampling-mask tests passed with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`: masks with and without ordinary logprobs, followed by ordinary generation; four tokens per request. Checks cover selected-token membership, support IDs, aligned lengths, capacity, and finite sampling logprobs.
- TP2 uses overlap and the real status collective. PP2 uses the existing pipeline scheduler (which automatically disables ordinary overlap) and real cross-stage send/receive.
- After consolidating the distributed cases into the existing sampling-mask file, all 29 tests passed in 249.286 seconds on BJ with a runtime-only `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` override for the existing fixtures. The normal run passed both distributed tests and ten capture/packing tests; three existing fixtures could not access the gated Llama model (HTTP 401). The committed default model is unchanged.
- All 24 current feature files differing from merged main were SHA-256 matched to the BJ source tree.
- Ruff configured lint/format, isort, whitespace, and registered-test validation passed. Current-head CI is complete: 106 passed, 25 failed, 45 skipped, 2 cancelled. CUDA Base passed after one failed-jobs-only retry; the NPU reference-image retry passed. Remaining failures are the separate MLX fixture issue, shared AMD/NVFP4 failures, Xeon package/test mismatch, and NPU Wan timing plus dependent-job failures; no confirmed sampling-mask regression remains. Monitoring is paused.

Run the distributed tests with:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=python python3 test/registered/sampling/test_sampling_mask.py TestDistributedSamplingMask -v
```

Earlier verification also covered FlashInfer/PyTorch HTTP requests with overlap on/off, seeded parity, and two live Mooncake P/D cases (disabled/error and enabled metadata handoff).

Upstream main `5177a3ec08` remains merged through `92774ddb48`; no history was rebased. `spec/` remains removed.

Review follow-up commits:
- `90eab32d48`: defer abort release until pending KV offload completes; preserve the optional backend hook and leave base classes unchanged.
- `084b80efce`: reuse prefill abort retirement and preserve `err_type` despite sender exceptions.
- `520e7f7541`: reject the retired environment variable at startup.
- `f79c5a9466`: revert the unrelated MLX test repair. That fix is split into #38739; main still reproduces its two shutdown-fixture failures, so MLX CI may remain red here until the separate repair lands.
- `1d542447e5`: live TP2/PP2 coverage.
- `d73bc1bd7f`: merge distributed coverage into the existing sampling-mask test file; use the two-GPU CUDA runner and preserve the one-GPU AMD suite with only the distributed class skipped.

The earlier three review fixes remain separate commits: `e511bfc998` (opt-in PD metadata), `6f53732040` (bulk CPU copy), and `a723a1a55a` (capture-only helper allocation).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen3-8B BF16, TP1 on one NVIDIA H200, with FlashInfer sampling and attention and CUDA graphs enabled. Each request uses 128 input tokens, 512 output tokens, `temperature=1`, `top_k=4096`, `top_p=1`, and `return_sampling_mask=true`. The PR uses `--sampling-mask-max-tokens=8192` to accommodate cutoff ties; observed masks contained 4096–4396 tokens.

**Before:** upstream `756d0e0a85`, overlap disabled. **After:** PR `cb30f7c6a9`, overlap enabled. This measures the combined implementation and scheduling change.

Median steady decode throughput from three measured runs after one warmup per configuration; parentheses show the run range.

| Batch size | Before (tokens/s) | After (tokens/s) | Change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 155.47 (154.90–155.56) | 182.37 (181.99–182.40) | +17.30% |
| 16 | 1659.03 (1650.52–1665.77) | 2216.61 (2216.46–2219.79) | +33.61% |
| 64 | 3179.15 (3174.73–3201.97) | 4826.58 (4637.89–4837.76) | +51.82% |

Throughput uses scheduler decode logs over full-batch intervals. Prefill, warmup, and final HTTP response serialization are excluded; sampling-mask capture, copying, and decode result processing are included. All 18 measured trials and six warmups completed with aligned masks/logprobs and no overflow or invalid-result failures.

[Reproducer, exact commands, and full per-run evidence](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/76bac722f43640f004b7d1083e175940891ad227/spec/evidence/feature-00-sampling-mask.md#qwen3-8b-decode-throughput).

title: [XPU] Re-add intel xpu on triton paths in diffusion platforms
author: mehersai07
body:
`platform_key()` probed cuda/hip/npu/mps/musa and returned "cpu" for anything else. XPU is not in that list, so it reported "cpu" and `select_impl` handed it every `cpu=` fallback instead of the Triton implementation.

`select_impl`'s contract is that an unlisted platform keeps the Triton impl, which is what the per-module `if current_platform.is_*()` chains did before #35114 -- `is_cpu()` is False on XPU, so the Triton binding survived. Routing through `platform_key()` inverted that: XPU is not unlisted, it is actively reported as cpu.

All five `select_impl` sites declare `cpu=`, so XPU silently lost apply_rotary_embedding, fuse_scale_shift_kernel, norm_infer, rms_norm_fn and triton_one_pass_rms_norm. The kernels were written to run there -- scale_shift_triton.py asserts `x.is_xpu` -- but the dispatch made them unreachable.

Measured on Z-Image-Turbo (1024x1024, 8 steps, bs 1, Intel Arc Pro B60), bisected to #35114: denoise 5.5310s -> 6.0124s (+8.7%/step), end-to-end 8.42s -> 8.94s. A torch profile shows `_rotary_embedding_kernel` going from 308 launches to 0, replaced by ~3000 extra elementwise launches. With this change, end-to-end returns to 8.42s.

Also added the `xpu` in the forced_map as override env `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_PLATFORM_OVERRIDE=xpu` fails.

title: [SM120] Use exact query-head widths for DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA decode
author: LinPoly
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 on SM120 pads TP4 decode queries from 16 real heads to 64 even
though FlashInfer supports the native width. This makes sparse attention
process four times as many query heads. This change selects the native width
for supported FlashInfer decode shapes and supplies a matching attention sink.

The native-width prefill path introduced by #29927 is preserved. This PR adds
the corresponding optimization for decode-sized batches.

## Modifications

- Use `get_platform().is_sm120` for the platform check.
- Cache the installed FlashInfer DSV4 decode capabilities and select native
  heads for supported batches up to the decode token limit.
- Preserve native prefill query widths above the SM120 decode boundary and
  padding for unsupported decode shapes/backends.
- Return attention-sink views from one persistent backing allocation, retaining
  stable pointers across shape transitions and DSpark's no-argument contract.
- Extend the existing registered GPU test with native-versus-padded comparisons
  for H8/H16, T=1/64/65, and single/dual cache inputs.

## Validation of the current revision

Revision `8729ebafc1778481e64507bc1f057cba4c300715` is rebased onto
`c0b790cf7fe6dc1516c3ec1f23de9b37baca654a`.

On an exclusively held SM120 GPU, using the revised SGLang source with
FlashInfer 0.6.18 and PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130:

```text
python3 test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_flash_mla_backends.py -v
Ran 15 tests: 14 passed, 1 pre-existing skip
```

All 12 native-versus-padded comparisons passed at `atol=rtol=5e-2`, including
the decode/prefill boundary and attention sinks. The existing skipped test
probes a legacy FlashInfer module name; the new test exercised the actual
FlashInfer implementation. GPU ownership remained exclusive throughout.

All applicable pre-commit hooks passed on the three changed files, including
formatting, lint, AST parsing, and CI registration checks.

## Historical serving and performance validation

The following results were measured on the earlier PR revision `4f5a119dc1`
against base `8005df61d3`. They have not been rerun for the current rebase.

Official `sgl-project/sgl-eval` AIME25 repeat-8, using the same four RTX PRO
6000 GPUs and model/server settings, produced **235/240 (97.92%) pass@1,
100% pass@8, and 100% majority@8 on both variants**, with zero request errors.
See the [full accuracy qualification](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36655#issuecomment-5448183791).

Unprofiled decode-only A/B used DeepSeek-V4-Flash, pure TP4, FP8 KV, page size
256, FlashInfer sparse MLA and `flashinfer_mxfp4` MoE, speculative decoding
disabled, and CUDA graphs/autotuning enabled. Each case had one full-output
warmup wave, then five timed requests per concurrency slot with 1,024 output
tokens and byte-identical prompts across variants.

| KV / output | C | Main output tok/s | Patch output tok/s | Throughput change | Main mean TPOT | Patch mean TPOT |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1K / 1K | 32 | 1,219.85 | 1,453.25 | +19.13% | 26.206 ms | 21.994 ms |
| 1K / 1K | 64 | 1,653.77 | 1,944.41 | +17.57% | 38.679 ms | 32.893 ms |
| 8K / 1K | 32 | 1,213.97 | 1,379.15 | +13.61% | 26.342 ms | 23.186 ms |
| 8K / 1K | 64 | 1,517.69 | 1,753.77 | +15.56% | 42.146 ms | 36.468 ms |

Every point completed its exact request/token totals, reached its declared
concurrency, and had zero request errors. These are one-repeat synthetic-KV
decode diagnostics, not PD or full-capacity measurements.

title: [multimodal_gen] fix: make tail_attn_meta CUDA-graph capturable
author: AgainstEntropy
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

`tail_attn_meta` builds `cu_seqlens_tail` with `torch.tensor([valid, num_pad], device=cuda)`, which stages the Python list through pageable host memory. That H2D copy is illegal inside CUDA graph capture:

```
RuntimeError: Cannot copy between CPU and CUDA tensors during CUDA graph capture unless the CPU tensor is pinned.
```

The meta is built inside the DiT forwards that breakable-cuda-graph captures (`flux_2.py`, `qwen_image.py`, `mova.py` all call it), and it runs on every forward call, so any SP-sharded stream with tail padding aborts capture for its whole signature and silently falls back to eager.

No allowlisted model reaches the padded path in default configs today (Qwen-Image's BCG text buckets divide the usual power-of-two SP sizes), so on current main this is hardening for the BCG x SP surface. It is not far from the surface, though: Klein's fixed 512 does not divide non-power-of-two SP sizes (e.g. `--ulysses-degree 3`), and any SP model whose sharded stream picks up tail padding inside a captured forward trips it immediately.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- `sp_shard_utils.tail_attn_meta`: build the cumulative segment lengths from device-side `arange` arithmetic instead of a host-staged `torch.tensor`. Values are unchanged.
- New regression test `test_tail_meta_is_cuda_graph_capturable`: captures the construction inside `torch.cuda.graph`. It fails on main with the exact production error above and passes with the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

- The existing CPU value tests (`test_tail_meta_*`) pin the produced `cu_seqlens_tail` values; the whole `test_sp_shard.py` suite passes (24 tests).
- End to end on 2x H200 (a local experiment: the Qwen-Image BCG prompt padder was temporarily made a no-op so the unmasked text stream takes the SP shard path and picks up tail padding): `Qwen/Qwen-Image --num-gpus 2 --ulysses-degree 2 --enable-breakable-cuda-graph` with an odd-length prompt aborts every capture with the exact error above on main, and captures 61 segments with this fix. No in-tree config reaches the line today; the unit test is the standing regression guard.
