title: [Kernel] Add KDA NVFP4 GEMM for Qwen3.x on SM120
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- Add `python/sglang/kernels/kda_kernels` as the home for kernels generated by kernel-design agents and register their provenance as `KernelBackend.KDA`.
- Move the existing KDA diffusion implementations and their JIT CUDA sources into that implementation home while keeping `sglang.kernels.ops` as the stable public facade.
- Import the Qwen3.x ModelOpt NVFP4 SM120 GEMM generated by the Humanize2 / Kernel Design Agents workflow from [BBuf/KDA-Pilot#195](https://github.com/BBuf/KDA-Pilot/pull/195) at `516c976cee824a236679adf6eb525275a0a9a120`.
- Dispatch it from ModelOpt when the E2E-qualified SM120 shape allowlist matches; every other call falls back to FlashInfer.

This supersedes #36043, which has been closed.

## Production dispatch contract

The Qwen3.5 decode fast path accepts `M in {1, 2, 4, 8}` for these exact `(K, N)` pairs:

| Model / role | K | N |
|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5-4B gate/up | 2560 | 18432 |
| Qwen3.5-4B down | 9216 | 2560 |
| Qwen3.5-9B gate/up | 4096 | 24576 |
| Qwen3.5-9B down | 12288 | 4096 |

Qwen3.5 `M=9` remains callable through the low-level API for testing but is not production-dispatched. Qwen3.8 keeps its deliberately narrow production path: only the DSpark-qualified down projection `(M, K, N) = (9, 17408, 5120)` dispatches to KDA. The captured Qwen3.8 M=1/M=9 decode and M=4369 prefill shapes remain available through the low-level API.

All paths also retain the exact dtype, layout, device, and SM120 capability gates. Unsupported Cartesian combinations fall back to FlashInfer.

## Why Qwen3.8 remains narrow

The original isolated-GEMM policy persisted each layer's 5.6--11 MiB weight-scale tensor in L2. That helped repeated single-kernel benchmarks but displaced attention/SSM state in the complete serving pipeline. Enabling every captured Qwen3.8 decode shape preserved acceptance but regressed end-to-end output throughput by 0.76%.

Streaming both the one-pass FP4 weights and their scales, then dispatching only `(9, 17408, 5120)`, changed the three-round Qwen3.8-27B DSpark mean from 128.35 to 129.60 output tok/s (**+0.98%**) with unchanged accept length and fixed-prompt output.

The Qwen3.5 paths are not inferred from that microbenchmark. They have their own model-specific shape allowlist, CUDA Graph correctness coverage, and end-to-end concurrency sweep below.

## Qwen3.5 SM120 validation

Hardware and software:

- NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, SM120, 96 GB
- PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`
- `flashinfer-python==0.6.18`; stale 0.6.17 cubin/JIT-cache packages were removed rather than bypassing FlashInfer's package-version guard
- `AxionML/Qwen3.5-4B-NVFP4` at `4521f321dc8c46d255929203ae6d3062e51d52fa`
- `AxionML/Qwen3.5-9B-NVFP4` at `97aef92393f126bf649f310cd40861be8dad3279`

### GPU correctness and CUDA Graphs

GPU correctness on SM120 was checked against FlashInfer for Qwen3.5 M=1/2/4/8/9 decode shapes, Qwen3.8 decode/prefill, CUDA Graph replay, ModelOpt dispatch, and unsupported-shape fallback.

The multi-weight benchmark rotates eight distinct weights inside a CUDA Graph, alternates FlashInfer/KDA timing order across five trials, and uses the median per-call latency. All 20 Qwen3.5 rows passed `rtol=1e-2`, `atol=2e-2`.

| Model shape | M | Gate/up speedup | Down speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5-4B | 1 | 1.052x | **2.023x** |
| Qwen3.5-4B | 2 | 1.031x | **2.024x** |
| Qwen3.5-4B | 4 | 1.055x | **2.026x** |
| Qwen3.5-4B | 8 | 1.052x | **2.047x** |
| Qwen3.5-4B | 9 | 1.027x | **2.039x** |
| Qwen3.5-9B | 1 | **1.135x** | **1.258x** |
| Qwen3.5-9B | 2 | **1.134x** | **1.259x** |
| Qwen3.5-9B | 4 | **1.139x** | **1.251x** |
| Qwen3.5-9B | 8 | **1.132x** | **1.252x** |
| Qwen3.5-9B | 9 | **1.124x** | **1.262x** |

The geometric-mean speedup is **1.319x** across the 16 production-dispatched M=1/2/4/8 rows and **1.318x** across all 20 rows.

### End-to-end concurrency sweep

Protocol: 32 fixed-seed `random-ids` requests per round, 2048 input tokens, 512 output tokens, concurrency 1/2/4/8, cache flush before every round, three baseline rounds, three KDA rounds, and one adjacent baseline round. Every formal round completed all 32 requests (65,536 input and 16,384 output tokens).

| Model | Concurrency | Baseline tok/s | KDA tok/s | Adjacent baseline | Throughput | TPOT | E2E latency |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5-4B | 1 | 266.218 | 289.452 | 265.647 | **+8.73%** | **+8.31%** | **+8.03%** |
| Qwen3.5-4B | 2 | 522.936 | 558.694 | 522.736 | **+6.84%** | **+6.85%** | **+6.41%** |
| Qwen3.5-4B | 4 | 960.507 | 1028.929 | 962.763 | **+7.12%** | **+7.02%** | **+6.65%** |
| Qwen3.5-4B | 8 | 1427.207 | 1520.322 | 1427.246 | **+6.52%** | **+6.63%** | **+6.10%** |
| Qwen3.5-9B | 1 | 184.624 | 190.493 | 184.476 | **+3.18%** | **+3.19%** | **+3.08%** |
| Qwen3.5-9B | 2 | 359.919 | 369.908 | 360.482 | **+2.78%** | **+2.82%** | **+2.71%** |
| Qwen3.5-9B | 4 | 678.651 | 697.802 | 680.757 | **+2.82%** | **+2.81%** | **+2.74%** |
| Qwen3.5-9B | 8 | 1022.864 | 1050.453 | 1024.721 | **+2.70%** | **+2.78%** | **+2.62%** |

Adjacent-baseline throughput stays within 0.32% of the original baseline mean. TTFT changes range from -1.93% to +3.57%, while TPOT and total E2E latency improve at every concurrency, consistent with a decode-focused kernel.

## Validation summary

- Fused-op dispatch tests: 56/56 passed
- LayerNorm fused-op backend tests: 20 passed, 1 environment skip
- Kernel namespace tests: 61/61 passed
- All pre-commit hooks passed, including Python AST, isort, Ruff, codespell, and registered-test CI checks

KDA ownership and per-kernel provenance are documented in `python/sglang/kernels/kda_kernels/README.md`.

Related benchmark protocol: #34934.

title: [CI] Slim JIT kernel unit tests
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

The H100 JIT kernel unit-test step has started hitting its 30-minute timeout. A recent successful unsplit run took 27m59s and launched roughly 100 test files in separate Python processes.

This PR reduces the underlying suite runtime instead of increasing the timeout. It is complementary to #36775: partitioning lowers wall time, while this change lowers total H100 time in both the split and unsplit layouts.

## Changes

- Add an opt-in preloaded fork worker and enable it only for the H100 JIT kernel unit lane. The preloader stays CUDA-free and every test file runs in a fresh fork child, preserving file-level CUDA and Python-state isolation. The worker restarts every 20 files; per-file fail-fast, timeout, result, and TIMINGS reporting remain intact. The default runner behavior and other suites are unchanged.
- Replace Cartesian PR sweeps with representative pairwise/boundary cases in five current hotspots:
  - Hadamard: 145 -> 29 cases
  - attention RoPE: 230 -> 26 cases
  - diffusion QK-norm RoPE parameter sweep: 144 -> 10 cases
  - per-token group quant: 51 -> 35 cases
  - sconv extend metadata: 50 -> 14 cases
- Keep the complete Cartesian sweeps in scheduled/full and nightly runs through `get_ci_test_range`.
- Add a CPU protocol test proving that consecutive files run in isolated children.

## Timing evidence

- Historical H100 baseline: 27m59s for the unsplit 110-file suite.
- Controlled H200 direct-vs-fork comparison on the same seven warmed files: 85.80s -> 61.21s, saving 24.59s (28.7%); both modes passed 7/7 files.
- The first 20 files of the full H200 suite passed with the fork worker, including the worker restart boundary.
- The new sconv PR matrix passed 14/14 on H200.

The five matrix reductions are expected to save roughly 3-4 minutes from the historical H100 profile. The controlled worker result projects another several minutes across roughly 100 files, targeting about 10 minutes total. The final H100 CI measurement from this PR will replace the projection once the runner is assigned.

## Validation

- Python bytecode compilation for all changed Python files
- pre-commit formatting, YAML, AST, registry, and lint checks
- workflow job-name checker with PyYAML supplied explicitly
- fork-worker CPU protocol test
- H200 GPU validation described above

title: [Feature] Unified memory: support decode context parallelism for Kimi-Linear
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

`--enable-unified-memory` asserted `dcp_size == 1`, so the unified memory pool
and decode context parallelism could not be used together. This enables the
combination for Kimi-Linear (MLA hybrid Mamba).

The two features each rewrite the KV location space, and they had never been
composed:

- DCP hands out a **widened** virtual id space — `dcp_size` logical ids share
  one stored row, and a rank owns the ids with `loc % dcp_size == dcp_rank`.
- The unified pool adds its own transform on top, virtual -> physical -> dense
  (`translate_kv_loc_dense`, the page-major envelope's dense per-layer views).

## Modifications

The composition rule is that **every DCP index kernel already collapses
`loc // dcp_size` when it builds an index** (`create_triton_kv_indices_for_dcp_triton`,
`update_kv_lens_and_indices`, `filter_dcp_local_kv_indices`, and the
`dcp_local_prefix_kv_indices` slice). So `translate_kv_loc*` keeps speaking the
collapsed id space, and only the allocation surface widens.

**Allocator (`multi_ended_allocator.py`).** `MultiEndedAllocator` splits its
page size in two: `page_size` stays the VIRTUAL one (`ps * dcp_size`) that the
scheduler and tree cache read — matching `PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator`'s
existing DCP contract — and a new `pool_page_size` is the PHYSICAL rows one page
occupies. Page ids are invariant under the widening, so `virtual_to_physical` /
`physical_to_virtual`, compaction and the byte budget are all unchanged;
capacity scales by `dcp_size` over the same rows. Both are equal when
`dcp_size == 1`, so the non-DCP path is byte-for-byte unaffected.

**Write path.** `out_cache_loc` is the one location that reaches the pool still
widened, so the write side gets its own hook, `translate_write_loc_dense` /
`HybridLinearKVPool._full_write_translate`, split from the read-side
`_full_translate`. It resolves ownership, collapses, and translates, sending the
rows this rank does not own to dense id 0 — the reserved padding sink the MLA
write kernels already skip. `UnifiedMLATokenToKVPool` then writes with
`dcp_resolved=True` so `set_mla_kv_buffer_triton` does not apply the owner rule
a second time.

**flashinfer-MLA.** Decode ran the unified translate *before* the DCP shard;
that order is swapped, and `plan_dcp_decode_metadata` now returns the compacted
shard length so only that prefix is translated. Its paged prefill reads the
all-gathered `dcp_kv_buffer` and has `attn_dcp_metadata.dcp_kv_indices`
overwrite `kv_indices`, so the translate there is skipped entirely rather than
reordered — on widened ids `virt // page_size` walked off the end of the v2p
table.

**Guard** (`arg_groups/kv_cache_hook.py`). The blanket assert in
`handle_unified_memory_pool` becomes `_validate_unified_memory_dcp`, which
still rejects, with reasons: the MHA unified pool (no DCP-aware masked write
path), hybrid-SWA (`UnifiedSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` does not widen), and the
`trtllm_mla` / `cutedsl_mla` / `tokenspeed_mla` family (they build the MLA block
table from raw `req_to_token` page ids through
`create_flashmla_kv_indices_triton`'s v2p gather, while the DCP variant
`create_mla_kv_page_table_for_dcp` has no v2p gather at all — one has to be
wired through the other, and neither is testable on SM90).

**Tests.** A CPU unit test class pins the widening contract (capacity scales but
physical pages do not, alloc returns whole widened pages, all ranks resolve a
widened page to the same physical page, the write translate tombstones
un-owned ids, `dcp_size == 1` is unchanged). `test_full_loc_fast_path.py`'s MLA
routing tests are extended to pin that writes go through the write hook and
reads through the read hook. A nightly e2e class
`TestKimiLinearUnifiedMemoryDCP` is added next to the existing unified-memory
one.

Note for reviewers on Hopper: `triton` and `flashmla` both crash under MLA+DCP
today, independently of this PR (Triton MLA decode is not DCP-aware; FlashMLA
returns `(o, lse)` that `forward_absorb_core` does not unpack). `flashinfer` is
the working backend there, and is what `test_dsv31_dcp8_gsm8k.py` already uses.

## Accuracy Tests

Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct, 2x H200, TP2, `--attention-backend flashinfer`,
`--linear-attn-backend triton --mamba-backend triton`, GSM8K 5-shot @400:

| config | score (pre-rebase) | score (re-run on the rebased tree) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unified + DCP2 (this PR) | **0.912** | **0.912** |
| static + DCP2 | 0.915 | 0.910 |
| unified, no DCP | 0.907 | - |
| unified, no DCP, `--attention-backend triton` | 0.912 | 0.915 |

Invalid 0.000 throughout. The spread is within 1 sigma (~0.015 at n=400). The
last two rows are the pre-existing unified-memory paths this PR touches, re-run
after the change.

Compaction under DCP is the sharpest risk and is not reachable at the default
`--mem-fraction-static` (the pool is far larger than the workload), so it was
forced with `--mem-fraction-static 0.40` and
`SGLANG_LOG_LAZY_COMPACTION_STATS=1`: a 400-prompt 8k-in / 1k-out
`bench_serving` at concurrency 200 pushed 2.33M input tokens through a
1.29M-logical-token pool and logged **199,729 full-pool page moves with zero
errors**, followed by GSM8K@400 = 0.910 on the same server.

CPU suites: `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/` (1827 passed) and the
`server_args` suites (231 passed), plus `run_suite.validate_all_suites` over all
2263 registered tests.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same 400-prompt 8k-in / 1k-out run at concurrency 200, unified vs static, both
with DCP2:

| | output tok/s | mean TPOT (ms) | duration (s) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| unified + DCP2 | 2684.7 | 14.74 | 105.0 |
| static + DCP2 | 2734.7 | 14.38 | 103.1 |

~2% slower, consistent with the unified pool's known overhead without DCP; DCP
adds no measurable cost of its own here.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: feat: add optimized Domino rollout to DFlash V2
author: jianuo-huang
body:
## Summary

This PR adds optimized Domino projector support to DFlash V2 for the public
`Qwen3-8B-Domino-b16` checkpoint. It is based on the latest upstream
`main` and supersedes the earlier Domino PRs #31328 and #36860.

The target verification, continuous-prefix acceptance, bonus-token handling,
and KV-cache commit paths remain unchanged.

## Included implementation

- Parse, validate, instantiate, and load the bias-free prefix GRU and the
  two-layer SiLU correction projector.
- Generate the 15-token Domino proposal chain for block size 16, feeding each
  realized proposal back into the GRU.
- Precompute all base LM-head logits in one step-major projection.
- Capture the complete rollout in the DFlash draft CUDA Graph, with eager
  fallback when graphs are unavailable.
- Use ATen `GRUCell` for one-token feedback updates to avoid repeated cuDNN
  weight packing.
- Add a request-local, block-shared K=2048 candidate vocabulary pool for the
  correction head. `K=0` remains the full-vocabulary reference path.

## Scope

- BF16, CUDA, TP=1, Qwen3-8B, DFlash block size 16.
- Greedy decoding path; target verification remains full-vocabulary and is the
  correctness boundary.
- The candidate pool is a draft-side approximation; it does not alter target
  verification semantics.
- Non-greedy sampling and tensor-parallel Domino are covered by follow-up work
  in PR #37069.

## Validation

### Unit and registered tests

Focused tests:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/spec/test_dflash_domino.py

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH=python3 -m pytest -q -s \
  test/registered/spec/dflash/test_dflash_domino.py
```

The focused suite covers config parsing, strict Domino projector weight loading,
shape validation, full-chain rollout parity, candidate-pool boundaries,
batched-vs-single-row parity, eager fallback, and CUDA Graph replay.

### Serving validation setting

We validated the Qwen3-8B DFlash/Domino serving path with the following fixed setting:

- Target: `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`
- Drafts: `Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16` and `Qwen3-8B-Domino-b16`
- CUDA, BF16, TP=1, FA3 attention backend
- DFlash block size: 16 (15 proposed tokens)
- Domino candidate pool: K=2048
- Greedy sampling: `temperature=0`, `top_p=1`, `top_k=1`
- Qwen3 tokenizer chat template, thinking disabled
- Workloads: GSM8K-128, HumanEval-164, MT-Bench-80
- Concurrency: 1, 8, 32; maximum generation length: 2048
- Server: `max_running_requests=32`, `cuda_graph_max_bs=32`,
  `mem_fraction_static=0.70`, `page_size=1`
- Warmup: 3 requests, warmup maximum generation 1024, first request skipped
- One measured run per configuration, timeout 3600 seconds

The serving validation completed successfully for both DFlash and Domino on this setting.
Numerical throughput and acceptance-length comparisons are reported separately in PR #37069.

## Changes

This branch is rebased directly onto the current upstream `main`; no unrelated
benchmark or training scripts are included.

title: [Memory] Size the CUDA graph pool from warmup measurements and fix graph-pool borrowing
author: cctry
body:
## Motivation

This PR sizes the CUDA graph pool from measurements taken during graph warmup, and hardens graph-pool borrowing (#35375) against failure modes we hit under speculative-decoding serving loads.

Warmup-based sizing:

- **Pre-carve** (opt-in): the graph pool grows segment by segment during capture, fragmenting free space. Measuring the eager warmup's reserved footprint and minting it as one contiguous span right before capture carves the pool out of a single region.
- **Sampling prewarm hook**: sampling paths allocate full-vocabulary temporaries after graph capture; a rehearsal hook right after capture lets their memory needs surface at startup instead of under traffic.

Borrow-path fixes:

1. **Supply was counted per segment.** Only wholly-free segments counted as borrowable, so a single live block hid an entire segment's free space. Anything that stays live inside the graph pool (e.g. lazily initialized workspaces that land in the pool during the first capture) could hide multiple GB. On a GB300 TP4/EP4 speculative-decoding shape this hid 2.3 GB of borrowable space even on a healthy tree.
2. **First fit starved large borrows.** Extents are sorted largest first, so first fit carved every small allocation out of the run that a full-vocabulary probability matrix needs, and the arena could refuse a ~340 MiB request with GBs free in aggregate.
3. **The arena rebuilt itself too eagerly.** Rebuilding the borrow `MemPool` once the bump cursor passed half the extents discarded the caching allocator's reusable segments. A cold borrow must serve each request from a single extent, so a large request could raise an allocator OOM even though the arena was ~73% free in aggregate.

Separately, keeping EAGLE verify sampling inside the borrow scope (as introduced in #35375) turned out to be unsafe: with stochastic sampling enabled, probability temporaries reuse graph-owned inactive blocks that are not safe across EAGLE's repeated graph pipeline, and decoding can hang. EAGLE sampling now stays on the normal allocator.

## Modifications

- `runner_utils/pool.py`
  - New `GraphPoolPrecarve` (opt-in via `SGLANG_ENABLE_GRAPH_POOL_PRECARVE`): measures the eager warmup's reserved-memory footprint and mints it as one contiguous span right before capture, so the graph pool is carved out of a single region instead of grown segment by segment.
  - `find_free_graph_pool_runs` now walks contiguous inactive runs across **all** pool segments; live and pending-free blocks break runs, so a returned run never overlaps live data (the borrow protocol already assumes the next replay may rewrite any inactive range). Measured on the shape above: borrowable free 7.35 GB → 9.68 GB (+32%), largest run 1.13 GB → 2.30 GB (+103%).
  - The borrow arena now only rebuilds when the caching allocator actually released an arena segment (`freed_bytes`), not on a high cursor. Measured with the cursor guard removed: 1,200 sampling steps over batch sizes 1–32 in a 514 MiB arena held a 388 MiB high-water mark with 9 cached segments and zero raw frees.
  - `disable_graph_pool_borrow` now also tears down a live borrow pool, so disabling borrowing at runtime falls back cleanly to the normal allocator.
- `utils/cuda_vmm_utils.py`: `BumpArenaStub` gains an opt-in best-fit mode (`set_best_fit`); the borrow path enables it. First fit remains the default for callers that map physical pages at the offsets they are handed.
- `speculative/eagle_utils.py`: revert the `borrow_graph_pool` scope around EAGLE verify sampling (see Motivation).
- `model_runner.py` / `scheduler.py` / `base_spec_worker.py`: after graph capture, the scheduler runs a `prewarm_sampling` rehearsal hook on the forward stream (delegated to the spec worker when one exists). title: [AMD] Fix eager metadata for AITER EAGLE draft extend
author: zijiecode
body:
## Motivation

The AITER unified-attention path for non-MLA EAGLE draft extend can pass stale query sequence metadata to the kernel during eager execution. The regression was introduced by #30105, which enabled this path by default through `SGLANG_AITER_UNIFIED_DRAFT_EXTEND`.

The CUDA Graph metadata path builds the correct query indptr, so tests whose batch sizes remain within the captured graph range do not expose the issue. The failing path is the eager fallback used when CUDA Graph is disabled or when the live batch exceeds the captured maximum.

The issue was reproduced on the latest `main` at `2a96ebf6486de5016f40c3f8c6b43536c01f5cc5` using AMD MI355X, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, TP2, AITER attention, EAGLE with 3 speculative steps and 4 draft tokens, FP8 KV cache, and real draft acceptance. With CUDA Graph disabled, server warmup deterministically failed before the server became ready. With CUDA Graph enabled but `--cuda-graph-max-bs 32 --max-running-requests 64`, the high-concurrency workload entered the same eager fallback.

Instrumentation of the failing eager batch showed the metadata mismatch on both TP ranks:

```text
DRAFT_EXTEND_DEBUG q_shape=(4, 4096) qo_indptr=[0, 80] expected_q_len=4 metadata_max_q_len=0 kv_indptr=[0, 80] seq_lens=[84]
```

The query and output tensors contained 4 token rows, but `cu_seqlens_q=[0, 80]` instructed `unified_attention` to process 80 query rows. The resulting out-of-bounds write was reported as:

```text
Memory access fault by GPU node-3 (...) on address (...). Reason: Write access to a read-only page.
Memory access fault by GPU node-2 (...) on address (...). Reason: Unknown.
```

In longer CUDA Graph-enabled runs, the asynchronous corruption could first surface in speculative decode accounting before the HIP fault was reported:

```text
File "sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py", line 1260, in update_spec_correct_drafts_histogram
    self.spec_correct_drafts_histogram[num_correct_drafts] += 1
IndexError: list index out of range

HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_APERTURE_VIOLATION: The agent attempted to access memory beyond the largest legal address. code: 0x29
Fatal Python error: Aborted
```

`generate_attn_arg_prefill()` already returns the token-level `kv_indices`, `kv_indptr`, and `qo_indptr` required by this speculative batch, but the eager draft-extend setup discarded those values, left `ForwardMetadata.qo_indptr` unset, and later passed the backend's reusable `self.qo_indptr` buffer to `unified_attention`.

## Modifications

- Build eager non-MLA draft-extend `ForwardMetadata` directly from the values returned by `spec_info.generate_attn_arg_prefill()`.
- Preserve the current batch's token-level `kv_indices`, `kv_indptr`, and `qo_indptr`.
- Set `max_q_len` from `spec_info.num_tokens_per_req` and retain the computed `max_kv_len`.
- Pass `self.forward_metadata.qo_indptr` to `unified_attention` so the query sequence boundaries match the current query tensor.

## Accuracy Tests

Deterministic TP2 warmup A/B on the same latest-main commit and with identical launch arguments except for this patch:

| Configuration | Server ready | Memory-access faults | Scheduler exceptions |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Latest main, CUDA Graph disabled | No | 2 | 0 |
| Latest main + this fix, CUDA Graph disabled | Yes | 0 | 0 |

The fixed candidate was then tested with CUDA Graph enabled, `--cuda-graph-max-bs 32`, `--max-running-requests 64`, and a 512-thread GSM8K evaluation. The server log recorded 15 decode batches with 64 running requests and `cuda graph: False`, confirming that the repaired eager path was exercised rather than hidden by graph replay.

| Validation | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Completed examples | 1314/1314 |
| GSM8K score | 0.9414003044 |
| Memory-access faults | 0 |
| Scheduler exceptions | 0 |
| Mean speculative accept length | 3.5051 |

The latest-main base includes #36541, so the restored mean accept length also confirms that this fix composes correctly with the existing int64 `seqused_k` correction.

Additional validation:

```text
python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py
git diff --check
```

title: perf(gdn): select ReplaySSM verify loop unrolling by shape
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

The CuTe DSL wide-vector GDN kernel uses the generic one-way Phase-B loop schedule even for the short ReplaySSM verify path. That path also writes the raw ReplaySSM ring, and measurements show that exposing two-way instruction-level parallelism improves decode throughput without changing the generic path.

## Modifications

Select two-way Phase-B unrolling only when `cache_ring=True` and the compile-time sequence length is in the measured `3..8` range. Keep one-way unrolling as the explicit fallback for non-ReplaySSM calls and shapes outside that range, include the selected schedule in the kernel cache key, and add selector coverage to the existing GDN ring-verify test.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K was run before and after on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4-V2 with 200 examples, 5 shots, `max_tokens=16384`, 128 threads, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, and top-k 20. Both runs used natural speculative acceptance and completed with no runtime error markers.

| Version | Job | GSM8K | Mean speculative accept length |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Upstream main `24c9251ac5` | `3394634` | 0.990 | 4.6371 |
| This PR `24d2738a06` | `3394635` | 0.985 | 4.6488 |

Both scores pass the 0.95 gate. The 0.005 difference is one question at this sample size.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The performance A/B used direct SGLang on one GB300 node with DP4/TP4/EP4, FlashInfer linear-attention verify, 28 running requests per rank, identical fixed inputs, OSL 860, simulated acceptance length 4.8, and decode CUDA Graph enabled. The reverse-order same-node pair ran the candidate first and then control; all 112/112 measured requests returned HTTP 200 with exact OSL 860, four-rank coverage, CUDA Graph, and zero queue at the selected intervals.

| Metric | Control | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Matched-context step time | 34.5434 ms | 33.9925 ms | -1.59% |
| Fixed-AL4.8 output throughput/GPU | 3,890.752 tok/s | 3,953.811 tok/s | +1.62% |
| Fixed-AL4.8 TPS/user | 138.96 tok/s | 141.21 tok/s | +1.62% |
| Whole-cohort throughput | baseline | candidate | +1.77% |

title: config: six more runtime readers ask the bags
author: ch-wan
body:
## The series

Stacked, each PR based on the one above it. Read them in order; every boundary is
self-sufficient and green on its own.

1. [#36896](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36896) — the resolution pipeline's dispatcher leaves the record
2. [#36972](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36972) — the callbacks into the record go to zero
3. [#36973](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36973) — six more runtime readers ask the bags ← **you are here**
4. [#36974](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36974) — the dead record parameters go
5. [#36975](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36975) — the lazy imports that buy nothing become eager
- [#36925](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36925) — CI vehicle — runs the whole series against `main`, not for merge

## Motivation

The previous PR took the *resolution* package off the record. This one is about the **runtime**:
code that runs after publish, holds a `ServerArgs`, and reads raw fields off it.

A census of `srt/` finds 295 such reads in 53 files, every field of them in a published namespace.
Not all are convertible, and the criterion is not the field — it is the process. The launcher trio
(`http_server`, `engine`, `data_parallel_controller`) reads the record *before* its process
publishes; those 117 reads have to stay, and this PR does not touch them.

`expert_distribution.py` is the clearest case of the rest. `ExpertDistributionRecorder` was handed
a `ServerArgs` and threaded it through six constructors — recorder, gatherer, accumulator and
their subclasses — to reach four reads. Two of the classes stored it; one subclass took it and
never touched it. The file already asked `get_exec().moe` for the recorder mode, so the record was
travelling alongside a bag that already answered.

## Modifications

**The EPLB recorder.** The four reads go to the bag and the parameter goes with them: five call
sites in `model_runner.py`, six signatures, two stored attributes.

`eplb_min_rebalancing_utilization_threshold` is an `exec.moe` leaf. The three balancedness
predicates were members of the record — `should_log_expert_balancedness_to_server_log` and its
Prometheus sibling, read from four places across three files, each through a record someone was
holding for that purpose. They become published accessors in `runtime_context`, the way
`uses_mla_backend` and `cutedsl_moe_max_num_tokens` already pair with their pre-publish
equivalents. Both members are gone from `ServerArgs`.

`resolve_collector_class` was the one thing keeping the record in the chain: it took a `ServerArgs`
to read `stat_loggers`, an `observability` leaf, and three of its six callers were reaching for
`get_server_args()` to pass it straight back. It asks the bag now, and `server_args=None` — which
meant "no config, use the default" — becomes "the namespace is not published", the same case in
the context's own terms.

**Six more runtime readers**, each already reading its other configuration from a bag:

| file | reads | bag |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hybrid_pool_assembler` | 6 × `hicache_host_memory_mode` | `memory` |
| `scheduler` | 3 × `hicache_host_memory_mode` | `memory` |
| `kt_ep_wrapper` | 7 × six `kt_*` leaves | `exec.moe` |
| `expert_backup_client` | `nnodes`, `node_rank` | `parallel` |
| `dspark_planner` | three `speculative_dspark_*` | `spec` |
| `prefill_delayer` | three prefill-delay leaves | `schedule` |

Three of them were carrying the record only for those reads, so it goes: `PrefillDelayer` and
`ExpertBackupClient` lose the constructor parameter and the stored attribute, and
`build_sps_cost_table` — whose body was already entirely `get_spec()` and `get_schedule()` — loses
its keyword-only `server_args`, which takes it out of `DsparkPlanner` too.

Removing a constructor parameter reaches further than the file that declares it. Three call sites
outside `srt/` had to follow: the DSpark worker constructs `DSparkVerifyPlanner` (a P1 — every
DSPARK startup would have raised `TypeError`), and the registered prefill-delayer and SPS-table
tests both passed the keyword. The delayer test now publishes its per-case schedule leaves through
`override_server_args` instead of handing in a stand-in.

Dropping the argument leaves the local that fed it: `base_prefix_cache.init_metrics_collector`
still bound `server_args = get_server_args()` for a call that no longer takes one. Its two sibling
sites had already lost both.

The accessor docstrings say what a caller needs and no more: `reports_expert_balancedness` names
`overrides.should_report_expert_balancedness` as its pre-publish equivalent, the way
`cutedsl_moe_max_num_tokens` already did, and drops the sentence about why the accessors exist.

`TestResolveCollectorClass` drove `resolve_collector_class` with a `_StubArgs` stand-in. A stand-in
proves nothing about a function that reads a bag, so the cases force the leaf through
`override_server_args` and the stand-in is deleted.

## Accuracy Tests

The 62-shape resolution probe is byte-identical to the base commit. The affected suites
(`observability`, `mem_cache`, `managers`, `spec`, `server_args`) report the same failure set as
`main`, file for file — 3038 passed on both sides, with the same three pre-existing failures.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

None. A bag read is a dataclass attribute read.

title: config: the lazy imports that buy nothing become eager
author: ch-wan
body:
## The series

Stacked, each PR based on the one above it. Read them in order; every boundary is
self-sufficient and green on its own.

1. [#36896](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36896) — the resolution pipeline's dispatcher leaves the record
2. [#36972](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36972) — the callbacks into the record go to zero
3. [#36973](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36973) — six more runtime readers ask the bags
4. [#36974](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36974) — the dead record parameters go
5. [#36975](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36975) — the lazy imports that buy nothing become eager ← **you are here**
- [#36925](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36925) — CI vehicle — runs the whole series against `main`, not for merge

## Motivation

`arg_groups.overrides` is already imported at module scope by thirty-five files, `server_args`
among them. Importing it is neither a cycle nor a cost — by the time any resolution step runs, the
module is loaded. Ninety-three `from ...overrides import` statements were nonetheless written
inside the functions that use them, which reads as though laziness were required when mostly it
was habit.

Eight of the twenty files this touches had the lazy form *before* this series, so it is not only a
cleanup after it.

## Modifications

The statements that buy nothing become module-scope imports.

Twenty-three more were **mixed**: a name the tests patch, plus names riding along on the same
statement that nothing patches. Splitting those frees thirty-six more riders. The `_dsa_*` pass
callables in `model_hook` are the shape of it —

```python
from sglang.srt.arg_groups.overrides import (
    _dsa_kv_cache_dtype_default,      # only ever an argument
    _dsa_split_backend_resolution,    # only ever an argument
    run_post_process_pass,            # patched through the module
)
```

— three names, one reason. The two passes are handed to `run_post_process_pass` and never looked
up through the module, so they were lazy only by association. The seam stays a call-site import;
they go to the top.

`model_hook` and `moe_hook` are the exception: their import block also carries the two properties
PR 2 lifted, so the two changes cannot be separated by hunk without an intermediate commit that
does not compile. Their split lands in PR 2 with the move it is entangled with, and the counts
below are for the whole series.

What is left is load-bearing, for exactly two reasons and nothing else. They are worth writing
down because they decide where the next one goes.

**The module is a test seam.** `use_mla_backend`, `attention_backends_of`, `model_config_of` and
`supports_mamba_cache_extra_buffer` are patched as `patch("...overrides.<name>")`. The four
declaration paths — `declare_resolution`, `declare_late_resolution`, `declare_direct_writes`,
`run_post_process_pass` — are wrapped by `setattr` on the module in
`test_no_entry_changes_after_it_is_recorded`, which watches *every* declaration a resolution
makes.

A `from ... import` name is a **copy**. Hoisting these turns one seam into six or twenty: a test
that patches the source module reaches none of the copies, and a test that patches one consumer
reaches only that one. Hoisting the declarers is what this commit tried first, and the census
guard failed exactly as it was designed to — it recorded nothing, because the wrapper it installed
on the module was no longer what the callers called.

**Import order.** `runtime_context` is imported by `utils.common`, which `overrides` needs, so it
sits *below* `overrides` and cannot import it at module scope. That one is a cycle, not a
preference; it was found by the import smoke check, not by reasoning.

That leaves a rule a reader can check:

| function-local `overrides` import | count |
| --- | --- |
| the module is a patched or watched seam | 54 |
| import order (`runtime_context`) | 8 |
| **neither** | **0** |

## Accuracy Tests

The 62-shape resolution probe is byte-identical to the base commit. A dummy resolution is
unchanged at ~9 ms and loads the same six `arg_groups` modules — which is the point: the laziness
these statements were written for was already provided by the families' own import placement, not
by the `overrides` import.

605 registered config tests pass, `test_no_entry_changes_after_it_is_recorded` among them — it is
the guard that fails the moment a declarer is hoisted.

Two properties worth stating because a hoist can break them silently: every newly module-bound name
is actually used in its file (no unused hoist), and no function still imports locally a name the
same file now binds at module scope (no `UnboundLocal` from late shadowing). Both hold by AST over
the commit. The newly eager modules are also off the `overrides` → `utils.common` →
`runtime_context` path, which is the cycle the keep-list's second reason protects.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

None beyond the dummy-resolution timing above.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

Mechanical apart from the keep-list, and the table above is the whole of it: eight names stay lazy
because the module is where tests patch or watch them, `runtime_context` stays lazy because of
import order, and nothing else stays lazy at all. A reviewer can check the claim by re-running the
same scan.

title: [Kernel] Fix SM90 FP8 decode regression with benchmarked M/K/N routing
author: RunFMe
body:
## Motivation

The SM90 row/column-scaled FP8 selector introduced by #34318 can route decode GEMMs to `torch._scaled_mm` based on K/N alone. The [reported H100 W8A8 regression](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34318#issuecomment-5461656173) is:

- model: `Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-dynamic`
- test: `test/registered/quant/test_w8a8_quantization.py::TestW8A8Fp8.test_throughput`
- batch size: 1
- throughput: approximately 215 tok/s before #34318, approximately 190 tok/s after it
- affected down projection: `M=1, K=14336, N=4096`

Direct profiling of that shape on both H200 and H100 showed that the AOT kernel is substantially faster at decode M, even though K and N are large.

## Modifications

Constrain Torch/NVJet routing to the benchmarked large-prefill envelope (doing m >= 6144 is not really worth the gain from my measurements):

```python
m >= 8192 and (
    (k >= 4096 and n >= 6144) or
    (k >= 7168 and n >= 5376)
)
```

This keeps the following on AOT:

- all decode and small-prefill calls with `M < 8192`
- the reported `K=14336, N=4096` Llama down projection
- narrow TP8 projections `K=5376, N=3584` and `K=3584, N=5376`
- shapes outside the measured projection envelope

Torch remains selected for stable large-prefill wins: wide QKV/gate/up projections and broad down projections.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Common software:

- PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130 (`70d99e998b4955e0049d13a98d77ae1b14db1f45`)
- CUDA 13.0
- `sgl_kernel==0.4.4`
- CUDA-event timing with randomized/interleaved AOT and Torch samples

The broad grid used 11 projection families and 12 M values (132 cases): 1, 16, 64, 256, 1024, 2048, 4096, 6144, 8192, 8320, 12288, and 16384. Percentages below are Torch speedups over AOT.

### H200 (SM90)

Protocol:

- broad grid: 5 warmups and 15 samples per arm
- two randomized boundary confirmations: 44 cases and 33 cases, with 8–10 warmups and 30–40 samples per arm
- exact-workload conditioning before timing

Reported regression shape:

| M | K | N | AOT | Torch | Result |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 14336 | 4096 | 26.50 µs | 51.12 µs | AOT is 1.93× faster |

Routing boundary:

| K | N | Projection family | M=8192 | M=8320 |
|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 4096 | 28672 | gate/up | 1.74% | 3.30% |
| 4096 | 6144 | QKV | 0.94% | 2.14% |
| 5376 | 21504 | QKV | 2.59% | 4.64% |
| 5376 | 28672 | gate/up | 2.39% | 5.17% |
| 5376 | 14336 | gate/up TP2 | 2.91% | 2.62% |
| 7168 | 5376 | down TP4 | 1.26% | 3.29% |
| 14336 | 5376 | down TP2 | 1.82% | 3.25% |
| 28672 | 5376 | down TP1 | 1.66% | 3.09% |

Across the H200 broad grid, every one of the 32 measurements selected by the new predicate favored Torch. Their median speedup was 2.50%, with a measured range of 0.17–5.97%. Two independent randomized boundary passes added 48 repeated routed measurements, all of which also favored Torch.

### H100 80 GB HBM3 (SM90)

Protocol:

- randomized broad grid: 5 warmups and 20 samples per arm after 0.5 s of exact-workload conditioning per case
- randomized boundary confirmation: 44 cases, with 10 warmups and 40 samples per arm after 2 s of conditioning per case

Reported regression shape:

| M | K | N | AOT | Torch | Result |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 14336 | 4096 | 32.19 µs | 53.55 µs | AOT is 1.66× faster |

Routing boundary:

| K | N | Projection family | M=8192 | M=8320 |
|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 4096 | 28672 | gate/up | 21.02% | 43.21% |
| 4096 | 6144 | QKV | 5.39% | 3.07% |
| 5376 | 21504 | QKV | 25.44% | 57.38% |
| 5376 | 28672 | gate/up | 26.58% | 52.16% |
| 5376 | 14336 | gate/up TP2 | 15.87% | 48.31% |
| 7168 | 5376 | down TP4 | 2.72% | 4.43% |
| 14336 | 5376 | down TP2 | 8.72% | 7.08% |
| 28672 | 5376 | down TP1 | 10.02% | 8.57% |

Across the H100 broad grid, every one of the 32 measurements selected by the new predicate favored Torch. Their median speedup was 19.48%, with a measured range of 1.36–56.53%. The stronger randomized boundary pass added 24 repeated routed measurements, all favoring Torch, with a 21.02% median and a 2.72–57.38% range.

On both GPUs, the excluded Llama down and narrow TP8 families had weak large-M results that were near parity or changed sign across passes, so this change deliberately leaves them on AOT rather than routing on noise.

title: [Diffusion][Kernel] Fuse Wan2.2 NVFP4 bias + GELU on Blackwell
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation Wan2.2 ModelOpt NVFP4 MLPs currently execute the `fc_in` hot path as three separate operations: ```text NVFP4 GEMM -> BF16 bias add -> tanh GELU ``` On GB300, the bias add and GELU are memory-bound and account for a meaningful part of denoising time. This PR fuses the last two operations while preserving the eager half-precision rounding boundary. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["DenoisingStage._maybe_toggle_quality_fusions"] --> B{"request quality"} B -->|"lossless"| C["unmount_nvfp4_bias_gelu
reference path"] B -->|"high"| D["mount_nvfp4_bias_gelu
eligible Wan NVFP4 sites only"]:::changed D --> E["ColumnParallelLinear.forward
NVFP4 GEMM returns output and deferred bias"]:::changed E --> F["bias_gelu_tanh
fused BF16/FP16 bias add plus tanh GELU"]:::changed C --> G["NVFP4 GEMM with bias
then native GELU"] F --> H["fc_out"] G --> H L["Legend: dashed border = added or modified"]:::changed classDef changed stroke-dasharray:5 5,stroke-width:2px; ``` The request-scoped quality gate only defers `fc_in` bias when the live linear method is `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod`. Unquantized checkpoint-excluded linears and the default `quality=lossless` path remain unchanged. ## Modifications - Add a lightweight JIT CUDA bias + approximate-GELU kernel with: - FP16/BF16 support; - 16-byte vectors before Blackwell and 32-byte vectors on Blackwell; - occupancy-capped persistent launch geometry; - PDL wait/trigger support; - an explicit half-precision rounding boundary after the bias add. - Add a request-scoped Wan NVFP4 fusion site and integrate it with the existing diffusion `quality=high` lifecycle. - Add registered H100 and B200 kernel tests, a registered kernel benchmark, and Wan mount/unmount plus excluded-linear regression tests. ## Accuracy Tests Hardware: NVIDIA GB300 (compute capability 10.3). - 11 focused GPU tests pass on the rebased PR: ```bash python3 -m pytest -q \ test/registered/kernels/ops/elementwise/test_bias_gelu.py \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_wan_gelu_mlp.py # 11 passed ``` - The fused kernel is bit-exact with `F.gelu(input + bias, approximate="tanh")` for FP16 and BF16, including the production `(1, 4096, 13824)` shape. - Main A/B and PR A/B `quality=high` MP4 files are byte-identical. A direct 81-frame comparison gives: | Accuracy metric | Main vs PR | | --- | ---: | | Decoded frames | 81 | | Mean / worst-frame SSIM | `1.000000 / 1.000000` | | Mean / worst-frame PSNR | `inf / inf` | | Maximum decoded-pixel difference | `0 / 255` | | LPIPS | `0` (identical decoded frames) | | MP4 SHA256, main | `d68d70a1cc7efc04bc6c5fbcf985d2f9f7b41edc4e54a23497541bbf821cd961` | | MP4 SHA256, PR | `d68d70a1cc7efc04bc6c5fbcf985d2f9f7b41edc4e54a23497541bbf821cd961` | The following comparison shows frames 1, 41, and 81 from the exact artifacts used for the metrics (same prompt, seed, shape, steps, guidance, and GPU): ![Wan2.2 NVFP4 main versus PR generated-frame comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-assets-37075/pr-assets/37075/wan22-nvfp4-main-vs-pr.png) - Candidate `quality=lossless` is byte-identical to the unmodified lossless baseline: `d75f78b4264618a0b8e170cd8d2649f18434787baee27374052dc4867b8205e5`. - Existing `quality=high` versus `quality=lossless`, measured over all 81 decoded frames: mean/worst SSIM `0.986642 / 0.983460`, mean/worst PSNR `41.092099 / 39.520000 dB`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling End-to-end workload: - Model: `nvidia/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers-NVFP4` - Snapshot: `ac69f2655787c3af65e1756d001303cd4a4daa46` - GB300, one GPU, eager native SGLang, synchronized stage profiling - 832x480, 81 frames, 40 steps, guidance 4, seed 42 - Prompt: `A cat and a dog baking a cake together in a kitchen.` - Performance base: `89816a21a1b5e9cf1f21dc407256e73905151ecc` | Run | Denoise | End-to-end | Peak reserved | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Baseline A | 71.726712 s | 72.719473 s | 55.580 GiB | | Candidate A | 69.585341 s | 70.579956 s | 55.580 GiB | | Candidate B | 69.607537 s | 70.602064 s | 55.580 GiB | | Baseline B | 71.748749 s | 72.746630 s | 55.580 GiB | Mean improvement: - Denoise: `71.737731 s -> 69.596439 s`, **2.984889% faster**. - End-to-end: `72.733052 s -> 70.591010 s`, **2.945073% faster**. - Paired denoise improvements: `2.985458%` and `2.984320%`. - Peak reserved memory is unchanged. Five profiled denoise timesteps after warmup: | Metric | Baseline | Candidate | | --- | ---: | ---: | | CUDA time | 11,316.079 ms | 11,005.284 ms | | CUDA events | 22,688 | 22,282 | | BF16 add | 1,553.063 ms | 1,138.976 ms | | Native GELU | 218.014 ms | 36.028 ms | | Fused bias + GELU | 0 ms | 207.587 ms | The targeted add + GELU chain decreases from `1,771.077 ms` to `1,382.591 ms` (`388.486 ms` saved). FP4 GEMM and attention kernel counts remain stable. The registered microbenchmark was repeated on GB300 after rebasing onto `032fe91bf1`: | Rows x hidden | JIT | PyTorch add + GELU | Speedup | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 32760 x 5120 | 171.9725 us | 498.9286 us | 2.90x | | 32760 x 13824 | 457.6064 us | 1338.7175 us | 2.93x | ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit (all applicable hooks pass). - [x] Add unit tests (registered H100/B200 kernel coverage and Wan integration coverage). - [x] Update documentation (N/A: no new public option or user-facing behavior). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #33283700621](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33283700621) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #33317400114](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33317400114) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :x: [Run #33283700582](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33283700582)

title: [Config] Round 5.1: the published-side readers ask the bags, and a platform fact gets one address
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

Round 4 got `arg_groups` to the point where resolution never writes a field on
`ServerArgs`: handlers *declare* what they decide, and `publish()` projects the
result into read-only config bags. The reader side was still half-converted —
runtime code read raw `server_args` fields, two production names existed only so
tests could patch them, and a platform fact such as "this box is SM100" had one
copy per importing module, so it could only be stated to one reader at a time.

That last one had already cost a round-4 CI failure (the module choosing an
attention backend and the module validating the choice held different copies of
the same fact) and was blocking the per-model split in #37087.

This PR finishes the reader side. Part 2 is **#37087**, stacked on this branch;
merge this one first.

## Modifications

Ten commits, each standing on its own.

1. **The last two patch seams leave the module.** `attention_backends_of` (3
   patch sites) and `supports_mamba_cache_extra_buffer` (2). Both are stated as
   inputs now — the first reads three backend fields, and those fields are what
   the tests wanted to control anyway.

2. **86 function-local `runtime_context` imports across 48 files become eager.**
   Lifting all of them, then importing each affected module *first* in a fresh
   interpreter, found 16 that broke; the pass runs to a fixed point with a
   revert-on-failure step, ending at 86 → 4. The 4 that stay are real cycles
   (`eplb/expert_distribution` ×2, `musa/flashattention_backend`,
   `moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm`).

3. **81 runtime reads across 27 files ask the bags**, and `_apply_fields` — the
   last channel through which anything wrote back onto the record — is closed.
   The criterion is not "can this field be mapped" but "has the reader's process
   published yet": the launcher's own pre-publish reads (172 across 9 files) stay
   on the record.

4. **A platform fact gets one address.** `from ... import is_cuda` binds a *copy*
   into each importing module; `get_platform().is_cuda` puts the value in one
   object, so one `override_platform(...)` reaches every reader. The probes in
   `utils/common.py` remain the only real implementation — this is their address,
   not a second copy.

5. **The sm-family probes follow**, plus `device_sm` / `device_capability`, which
   are not yes/no facts but want the same override.

6. **The KV-events descriptor leaves the record** — 117 lines of published-side
   description move to where the published config lives.

7. **`configure_logger` reads the record it was handed** — a defect introduced by
   commit 3 and fixed here (details under Accuracy Tests).

8. **83 remaining device-probe reads in `arg_groups` go through the address.**
   This is what makes #37087 possible: a family that moves to its own module
   takes its probe reads with it, and a module-scoped patch would have to move too.

9. **Parameters nobody reads leave the signatures** — functions that kept a
   `server_args` argument they no longer name, dropped with the argument at every
   call site.

10. **Per-worker placement goes back to being read per worker.** Two readers
    converted in commit 3 decide which GPU a worker draws on, which the standing
    rule routes through a constructor argument rather than the config tier.

New tests: `test_platform_context.py`, `test_pre_publish_readers.py`,
`test_platform_address_not_frozen.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

No kernel or model-forward code is touched; this changes where configuration
values are read from. The equivalent check is that the resolved configuration is
unchanged:

- **62-shape resolution probe: IDENTICAL.** Each shape runs `resolve_once()` +
  `check_server_args()` and the full resolved configuration is compared field by
  field, along with the exception type and message. Identical on the branch tip
  and on each of the ten commits individually.
- **Every registered unit test file run on its own**, branch and base, comparing
  the two failure sets: **0 regressions** — every failure on the branch is also
  on `main`.
- **A real server boots and serves**: Qwen3-0.6B to `/health`, then a `/generate`
  round trip.

Three defects were found this way rather than by the suite, and each has a guard:

- `configure_logger` (commit 7) runs before `publish`, and `multimodal_gen` calls
  it with a `ServerArgs` that never publishes these bags. Reading
  `get_observability()` took the server down on **every** launch while the whole
  CPU suite stayed green, because every unit test publishes first. Caught by
  booting a server; `test_pre_publish_readers.py` now derives the protected set
  from `_launch_subprocesses` and drives each callee against an unpublished
  context.
- Four module-scope bindings (`_is_sm120 = get_platform().is_sm120` and three in
  `fp8_utils`) read the fact once at import and kept it, so an override could not
  reach them and the answer depended on import order — the substitution *looked*
  converted without being converted. `test_platform_address_not_frozen.py` fails
  on any module-scope `x = get_platform().y`.
- `sparsity/factory.py` still read `hisparse_config` off the record after the
  write-back closed, which turned a registered `base-a-test-cpu` test red.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The probes behind `get_platform()` are `@lru_cache(maxsize=1)`; a call measures
**26.2 ns**. The reads this replaces were module-level constants, so the change
is one cached call per decision instead of an attribute load, off the per-request
path. Resolution time is unchanged — the 62-shape probe runs in the same time
before and after.

No change to the forward path, the scheduler loop, or any kernel.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

Commit 3 is where the risk is; commits 7 and 10 are its two escapes. Three
questions to ask of any reader it converted, in this order, because each one
caught a real defect: **when does this run**, **whose record is it holding**, and
— for the reads it did *not* convert — **did closing the write-back just break
this one**.

Merge this before #37087. The repo force-deletes heads on merge and auto-retargets
children to `main`, so #37087's base needs checking afterwards.

title: [BugFix][DSA] Bound prefill Triton specializations for page-table stride
author: HZY-Wade
body:
## Motivation

In a long-lived disaggregated prefill worker using DSA with EAGLE, the process ran normally for a long time and then failed while loading a newly JIT-compiled Triton kernel. The batch immediately before the failure contained 16,384 new prefill tokens:

```text
Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 16384, #cached-token: 0,
token usage: 0.10, #running-req: 0, #queue-req: 1,
#pending-token: 724687, cuda graph: False
```

The prefill server was launched with the following relevant SGLang arguments:

```bash
sglang serve --model-path <model-path> \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --attn-cp-size 4 \
  --enable-prefill-cp \
  --cp-strategy interleave \
  --disaggregation-mode prefill \
  --disaggregation-transfer-backend mooncake \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --max-running-requests 64 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --page-size 64 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --speculative-num-steps 3
```

The OOM occurred in Triton's CUDA module loading path, not while allocating an inference tensor:

<details>
<summary>Observed OOM stack</summary>

```text
Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 4678, in run_scheduler_process
    scheduler.run_event_loop()
  File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 1502, in run_event_loop
    dispatch_event_loop(self)
  File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 4536, in dispatch_event_loop
    scheduler.event_loop_overlap_disagg_prefill()
  File "sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py", line 572, in event_loop_overlap_disagg_prefill
    batch_result = self.run_batch(batch)
  File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 3390, in run_batch
    batch_result = self.model_worker.forward_batch_generation(...)
  File "sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py", line 1204, in forward_batch_generation
    self.draft_worker._draft_extend_for_prefill(...)
  File "sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py", line 858, in _draft_extend_for_prefill
    logits_output = self.draft_runner.forward(forward_batch).logits_output
  File "sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 1295, in forward
    output = self._forward_raw(...)
  File "sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 1485, in _forward_raw
    ret = self.eager_runner.execute(...)
  File "sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/eager_runner.py", line 203, in execute
    return self._execute_extend(forward_batch, pp_proxy_tensors)
  File "sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/eager_runner.py", line 332, in _execute_extend
    ret = model_runner.model.forward(...)
  File "sglang/srt/models/deepseek_nextn.py", line 412, in forward
    hidden_states = self.model(input_ids, positions, forward_batch)
  File "sglang/srt/models/deepseek_nextn.py", line 273, in forward
    hidden_states, residual, topk_indices = self.decoder(...)
  File "sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 2214, in forward
    hidden_states = self.self_attn(...)
  File "sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 1975, in forward_core
    return self.forward_absorb_core(*inner_state)
  File "sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py", line 732, in forward_absorb_core
    attn_output = self.attn_mqa(...)
  File "sglang/srt/layers/radix_attention.py", line 272, in forward
    return get_attn_backend().forward(...)
  File "sglang/srt/layers/attention/base_attn_backend.py", line 202, in forward
    return self.forward_extend(...)
  File "sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa_backend.py", line 1940, in forward_extend
    return self._forward_trtllm(...)
  File "sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa_backend.py", line 2964, in _forward_trtllm
    page_table_1 = transform_index_page_table_prefill(...)
  File "sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/transform_index.py", line 185, in transform_index_page_table_prefill_fast
    transform_index_page_table_prefill_kernel[grid](...)
  File "triton/runtime/jit.py", line 743, in run
    launch_metadata = kernel.launch_metadata(grid, stream, *bound_args.values())
  File "triton/compiler/compiler.py", line 482, in launch_metadata
    self._init_handles()
  File "triton/compiler/compiler.py", line 465, in _init_handles
    self.module, self.function, ... = driver.active.utils.load_binary(...)
RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: out of memory
```

</details>

`page_table_stride_0` was declared as `tl.constexpr`. For an expanded EAGLE page table, the tensor is contiguous and this row stride varies with the exact context length. Consequently, every previously unseen stride created another Triton specialization/cubin. A long-lived process accumulated loaded CUDA modules as it observed more input lengths, and eventually a later specialization failed in `load_binary()` with CUDA OOM.

This also explains why the failure happened after the worker had been healthy for a long time: compilation and module loading are deferred until a new shape/stride is first observed. Warming up a finite set of lengths can move the failure earlier but cannot cover an effectively unbounded set of context lengths.

## Modifications

- Make `page_table_stride_0` a runtime kernel argument.
- Explicitly add it to Triton's `do_not_specialize` list so integer-value specialization cannot recreate the same unbounded cache growth.
- Limit the change to the DSA **prefill** kernel. The decode kernel is unchanged.
- Add regression coverage that verifies both the parameter metadata and the compiled-kernel cache count across page-table row strides corresponding to context lengths 4096, 4160, and 4224.

## Accuracy Tests

The CUDA test file was run on a production-like online GPU pod with Triton 3.6.0 and PyTorch 2.11.0a0:

```text
test_decode_fast_correctness_and_strides                         PASS
test_decode_fast_extreme_shapes                                  PASS
test_large_batch_size                                            PASS
test_large_context_lengths                                       PASS
test_mixed_lengths_padding_and_empty_batch                        PASS
test_prefill_dynamic_page_table_row_strides                       PASS
test_prefill_page_table_row_stride_is_not_specialized             PASS
test_prefill_uses_dedicated_kernel                                PASS
test_prefill_uses_device_cu_seqlens                               PASS

Ran 9 tests in 5.007s
OK
```

The dynamic-stride test compares every result against the PyTorch gather reference with `rtol=0, atol=0`. It also verifies that changing the expanded page-table context length from 4096 to 4160 and 4224 does not increase the prefill kernel specialization count.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No end-to-end speed benchmark was run. This patch does not change the indexing algorithm, launch grid, or memory access pattern; it changes one row stride from a compile-time constant to a runtime scalar. It removes repeated JIT compilation/module loading for new context lengths and bounds the associated module-memory growth.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the changed files with pre-commit (all applicable hooks passed).
- [x] Add CUDA unit tests for the regression.
- [x] Provide exact-output accuracy results and specialization-cache validation.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.
- [x] Documentation is not required because there is no user-facing API or configuration change.

title: [Diffusion] Fuse FLUX.2 NVFP4 FC1, SwiGLU, and FC2 quantization
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary > [!IMPORTANT] > The fused path is request-scoped and enabled only for `quality="high"`. The default `quality="lossless"` keeps the original BF16 intermediate and remains on the reference path. This PR fuses the FLUX.2 double-stream ModelOpt NVFP4 feed-forward chain `FC1 NVFP4 GEMM -> BF16 SwiGLU -> FC2-input NVFP4 quantization` into the existing SM100 CuTe DSL `nvfp4_gemm_swiglu_nvfp4_quant` epilogue. The packed E2M1 activation and swizzled E4M3 block scales are passed directly into the FC2 projection, avoiding the BF16 intermediate and two launches per feed-forward invocation. This is the FLUX.2 SwiGLU + NVFP4 quantization optimization described in [Agentic Kernels in Production](https://www.baseten.co/blog/agentic-kernels-in-production/) ([original X post](https://x.com/BrianLi23/status/2093487934448214351)). The article reports a 3.8% FLUX.2 NVFP4 gain for this optimization; the native SGLang result below is a 3.36% denoise reduction on one GB300. ## Execution flow ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Flux2FeedForward.forward] --> B{SM100 + both linears
use ModelOpt NVFP4?} B -- no --> C[Existing FC1 -> BF16 SwiGLU -> FC2] B -- yes, load time --> D[Interleave gate/up weight rows
and swizzle block scales] D --> E[Register non-persistent derived buffers] B -- yes, eager forward --> F[Quantize FC1 input to NVFP4] F --> G[NEW: FC1 GEMM + SwiGLU
+ FC2-input NVFP4 quant] G --> H[Pass packed activation + scales
directly to FC2] H --> I[FC2 GEMM + existing TP reduction] B -- compile/capture --> C ``` ## Implementation - Prepare the fused kernel's `[up; gate]` 64-row interleaved weight and swizzled scale layout from the logical FLUX.2 `[gate; up]` checkpoint layout before the normal backend-specific transform. - Keep derived layouts as non-persistent module buffers so layerwise offload tracks them without adding them to the checkpoint state dict. Reprocessing a reloaded checkpoint updates compatible buffers in place to preserve tensor identity. - Allow an explicitly opted-in ModelOpt NVFP4 linear to consume a prequantized `(E2M1 values, E4M3 scales)` tuple. - Enable the path only for `quality="high"` requests on SM103, and only when both projections are ModelOpt NVFP4, aligned, and bias-free. `quality="lossless"`, unquantized, other architectures, `torch.compile`, and CUDA graph capture retain the existing path. - Limit this PR to the 8 double-stream blocks (image FFN + text FFN = 16 invocations per denoise step). FLUX.2 single-stream blocks concatenate attention and MLP outputs before their output projection and need a separate concat + quant fusion. ## GB300 benchmark > [!NOTE] > This benchmark was collected before the request-scoped gate was added, with the fused path active. It measures the fusion delta; the current PR exposes that behavior only under `quality="high"`. Hardware/software: - GPU: 1x NVIDIA GB300, 288 GB - PyTorch: `2.13.0+cu130` - Model: [`black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev-NVFP4), mixed NVFP4/BF16 checkpoint - Native SGLang diffusion backend; no Diffusers fallback - Baseline: `0438b16154` - Final PR commit: `4397a9503e`, rebased on `512df615de`. The two intervening main commits are unrelated to diffusion. The measured candidate source is inference-identical to the final commit (the post-benchmark change only strengthens reload-pointer test coverage). ### End-to-end Workload: 1024x1024, 50 steps, guidance scale 4.0, seed 20260830, `quality=lossless`, all text encoder/VAE/DiT components resident. One request warmup preceded each process. Results are five fresh processes per revision in balanced order `main, PR, PR, main, PR, main, main, PR, main, PR`. | Metric | main, mean +/- stdev | PR, mean +/- stdev | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Denoise / step | 136.198 +/- 0.078 ms | 131.623 +/- 0.332 ms | **-3.36% / 1.035x** | | Denoise / request | 6809.906 +/- 3.920 ms | 6581.171 +/- 16.601 ms | **-3.36% / 1.035x** | | End-to-end | 6940.312 +/- 6.424 ms | 6709.956 +/- 18.654 ms | **-3.32% / 1.034x** | ### Production-shape feed-forward microbenchmark Each row uses 10 warmups and 50 timed iterations with `hidden=6144`, `inner=18432`. | Flattened rows M | Existing three-op chain | Fused chain | Speedup | `_calc_diff` | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 512 | 0.678960 ms | 0.424448 ms | **1.600x** | 3.729e-4 | | 4096 | 1.684320 ms | 0.737136 ms | **2.285x** | 3.797e-4 | ### Profiler evidence The profiler captured two complete denoise steps per revision at the same 1024x1024 shape. Counts below are per step and identical across both captured steps. | Kernel family | main | PR | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Standalone NVFP4 GEMM | 128 | 112 | -16 | | Standalone NVFP4 quantization | 128 | 112 | -16 | | Standalone packed SwiGLU | 64 | 48 | -16 | | Fused FC1 + SwiGLU + quant | 0 | 16 | +16 | | All GPU kernel launches | 1121 | 1089 | **-32 (-2.85%)** | This is the expected replacement for 16 double-stream FFNs: remove three old kernels and add one fused kernel for each invocation. ### Memory tradeoff The ordinary FC1 layout remains available for the compile/capture fallback, so this PR stores an additional fused FC1 layout. | Metric | main | PR | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Reported transformer size | 22.90 GB | 24.79 GB | +1.89 GB | | Peak GPU memory in the benchmark | 72,930 MB | 74,316 MB | +1,386 MB | The fast path is restricted to Blackwell datacenter GPUs, where this model has ample headroom; the tradeoff is explicit rather than silently dropping the fallback layout. ## Accuracy and generated-image comparison The values below measure main against the fused path and therefore document `quality="high"` behavior. The current `quality="lossless"` path does not use this fusion. Both benchmark revisions were deterministic across their five independent runs; because the fused epilogue quantizes before materializing the old BF16 intermediate, its output is not expected to be byte-identical to the reference path. | Check | Result | |---|---:| | main SHA-256 (all 5 runs) | `2355e44b507e2f70a24594890d3d2d859348bb46c70f7cd4732372dbac86f8a1` | | PR SHA-256 (all 5 runs) | `0ea81ce944c5149b01c6483ea3f93e60d23de02dd5884cf618f16cdd27a19ab4` | | SSIM | **0.956636** | | PSNR | **28.908 dB** | | LPIPS (AlexNet) | **0.027606** | | Pixel cosine similarity | **0.986711** | | Mean absolute pixel difference | **3.123 / 255** | ![FLUX.2 NVFP4 main vs PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/flux2-nvfp4-swiglu/main-vs-pr.png) Prompt: `A cinematic technical poster of a red panda GPU engineer in a dark research laboratory, inspecting a luminous Blackwell accelerator board, with a notebook clearly labeled SGLANG NVFP4, realistic fur, intricate electronics, dramatic rim lighting` ## Validation - Request-scoped quality-gate lifecycle and lazy import-surface checks: passed locally. - `ruff format --check` / `ruff check` / `git diff --check` - `python -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_diffusion_nvfp4_scaled_mm.py`: **9 passed** on GB300 - `python -m pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_modelopt_fp4_capability_gate.py python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_modelopt_fp4_backend.py`: **7 passed, 12 subtests passed** - Full native FLUX.2 generation with `--dit-layerwise-offload true`: passed and produced an image - Full native FLUX.2 generation with whole-model `--enable-torch-compile`: passed and produced an image; title: [Diffusion] Fuse FLUX.2 gated residual normalization on Blackwell
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a Blackwell JIT fast path for FLUX.2's gated residual update followed by LayerNorm and adaLN scale/shift. It is the gated-residual-normalization optimization described in [Agentic Kernels in Production](https://www.baseten.co/blog/agentic-kernels-in-production/).

The production BF16 path previously launched `residual_gate_add` and LayerNorm/modulation separately. The new path carries an eligible FFN residual update to the next block and materializes both results with one model-specific CUDA kernel:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R[residual] --> F[fused CUDA JIT kernel]
    U[FFN or attention update] --> F
    G[gate] --> F
    M[next LayerNorm scale and shift] --> F
    F --> RO[updated BF16 residual]
    F --> NO[normalized and modulated BF16 input]
    X[unsupported shape, dtype, device, or compile mode] --> E[existing eager kernels]
```

In a profiled denoise step, 80 gated-residual and 80 norm/modulate calls become 77 fused calls plus 3+3 boundary calls. This removes 77 GPU launches per step.

## Implementation details

- Adds a dedicated D=6144, 128-thread CUDA JIT kernel for FLUX.2 instead of widening the generic norm/custom-op surface.
- Preserves eager numerics: BF16-rounds the gate product before the residual add, reproduces PyTorch's four-warp Welford reduction tree, and preserves BF16 rounding through normalization and modulation.
- Re-reads the updated residual in the output pass to reduce register pressure and retain occupancy.
- Defers eligible block-final residual updates only until the next LayerNorm. Pending values are always materialized at double-stream/single-stream and model-output boundaries.
- Keeps the original `nn.LayerNorm` modules and checkpoint/state-dict layout unchanged.
- Limits the fast path to Blackwell+, BF16, batch 1, hidden size 6144, non-empty dense contiguous tensors, and 32-byte alignment. FP16, batch >1, other architectures, `torch.compile`, and unsupported layouts use the existing path.

## End-to-end benchmark

Hardware/software: 1x NVIDIA GB300 288 GB (SM 10.3), driver 580.105.08, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. Model: FLUX.2-dev ModelOpt NVFP4. Native SGLang backend; transformer, text encoder, and VAE resident.

Workload: 1024x1024, 50 denoise steps, guidance scale 4.0, seed 20260830, lossless PNG, one request warmup per fresh process. Five main and five PR runs used balanced order `main, PR, PR, main, PR, main, main, PR, main, PR`.

| Metric | main, mean ± stdev | PR, mean ± stdev | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Denoise / step | 136.191 ± 0.094 ms | 135.133 ± 0.044 ms | **-0.7768%** |
| Warmed end-to-end | 6937.505 ± 5.735 ms | 6888.294 ± 4.031 ms | **-0.7093%** |

### Kernel microbenchmark

Median CUDA-event time after 25 warmups, 200 samples. The baseline is `residual_gate_add` followed by the production LayerNorm/modulation helper.

| Shape | baseline | fused | Speedup | Output / residual max abs diff |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `[1, 512, 6144]` | 158.656 us | 73.744 us | **2.151x** | 0 / 0 |
| `[1, 4096, 6144]` | 146.368 us | 98.224 us | **1.490x** | 0 / 0 |
| `[1, 4608, 6144]` | 146.576 us | 103.136 us | **1.421x** | 0 / 0 |

### Profile evidence

Two profiled denoise steps per side at the formal 1024x1024 shape:

| Metric / step | main | PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total GPU kernel launches | 1121 | 1044 | **-77 (-6.87%)** |
| Standalone gated residual | 80 | 3 | -77 |
| Standalone norm/modulate | 80 | 3 | -77 |
| Fused gated resnorm | 0 | 77 | +77 |
| Relevant kernel time | 4056.527 us | 3170.237 us | **-21.85%** |

## Accuracy and generated-image comparison

The same formal runs were used for performance and quality measurement. All five images within each side were deterministic, and main and PR produced the same PNG bytes.

title: [diffusion] perf: absorb Qwen-Image output projection biases
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Qwen-Image's ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4 path materializes output-projection bias before the attention and feed-forward residual updates. In a GB300 profile, the denoiser launched 673 BF16 add kernels per profiled step; 224 of those launches disappear when the four per-block output biases are consumed by the following residual operation.

This implements the Qwen-Image bias-absorption optimization described in [Agentic Kernels in Production](https://www.baseten.co/blog/agentic-kernels-in-production/).

## What changed

- defer attention and FFN output bias for ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4 with the existing `skip_bias_add` contract;
- extend the hidden-3072 JIT norm kernel with `bias + gated residual + LayerNorm + scale/shift`;
- add a JIT `bias + gate * output + residual` kernel for the final block residual;
- use native BF16 `__hfma` so the residual can break BF16 midpoint ties exactly like the production `MulAdd` kernel;
- keep Nunchaku, non-ModelOpt, unsupported shape/device/dtype, and torch.compile/BCG paths on their existing implementation.

The eager fast path is deliberately narrow: CUDA SM 10.3, BF16, batch 1, hidden size 3072, contiguous/aligned tensors, and row-broadcast bias/gate/scale/shift. B200/SM 10.0 and other architectures retain the original GEMM bias epilogue because moving that BF16 rounding point has only passed end-to-end image-quality validation on GB300.

## End-to-end benchmark

Hardware/software:

- 1x NVIDIA GB300 288 GB, SM 10.3
- driver 580.105.08, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130
- native SGLang backend; no diffusers fallback
- `Qwen-Image-2512` ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint
- 1024x1024, 50 denoise steps, true CFG 4.0, seed 20260830
- resident text encoder / DiT / VAE; lossless PNG output
- five fresh-process runs per variant, balanced order: `main, PR, PR, main, PR, main, main, PR, main, PR`

| Metric (5 runs) | main, mean ± stdev | PR, mean ± stdev | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Denoise / step | 489.077 ± 8.723 ms | 459.205 ± 9.888 ms | **-6.108%** |
| End-to-end | 24,577.675 ± 438.444 ms | 23,084.933 ± 496.267 ms | **-6.074%** |

Profiler evidence (per profiled denoise step):

| Kernel group | main | PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| BF16 `aten::add` launches | 673 | 449 | **-224 (-33.3%)** |
| BF16 `aten::add` kernel time | 13.975 ms | 10.959 ms | **-3.016 ms** |
| Bias-aware residual kernels | 0 | 240 | replaces the downstream residual/norm passes |

Microbenchmark on the same GB300 (production operators as baseline, 100 iterations):

| Shape | bias + residual norm | fused | Speedup | bias + final residual | fused | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `[1, 512, 3072]` | 133.808 us | 56.448 us | 2.37x | 75.264 us | 46.304 us | 1.63x |
| `[1, 4096, 3072]` | 122.416 us | 64.544 us | 1.90x | 74.080 us | 46.784 us | 1.58x |
| `[1, 4608, 3072]` | 120.464 us | 66.528 us | 1.81x | 76.704 us | 45.920 us | 1.67x |

All microbenchmark outputs, updated residuals, and final residuals are bit exact against `ScaleResidualLayerNormScaleShift` and `MulAdd`.

## Accuracy and generated-image comparison

The five main outputs are byte-identical to one another, and the five PR outputs are byte-identical to one another. Main and PR are not byte-identical to each other: excluded BF16 output projections add bias in the cuBLASLt accumulator epilogue, while this PR defers that bias until the following operation, changing the BF16 rounding point. The kernel-level post-GEMM composition itself is bit exact; the table below reports the end-to-end effect instead of claiming a lossless optimization.

| Metric | main vs PR |
|---|---:|
| SSIM | **0.950545** |
| PSNR | **29.262 dB** |
| LPIPS (AlexNet) | **0.042544** |
| Pixel cosine similarity | **0.995333** |

| Max absolute pixel difference | 154 / 255 |

Negative prompt: `blurry, low quality, distorted text, extra fingers`

![Qwen-Image main vs PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-image-bias-absorption/main-vs-pr.jpg)

## Validation

- `pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_model_fast_paths.py` — 44 passed
- `pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_diffusion_bcg_padding.py` — 25 passed
