title: [AMD] CI: fix Lean decode crash on the EAGLE path
author: mqhc2020

## Motivation
#33576 added four Lean persistent-grid buffers to `ForwardMetadata`, but filled them in at only 2 of the 5 construction sites. The spec-decode capture path (`triton_backend.py:667`) is decode-mode, so it reaches the Lean kernel — with `locks=None`. `locks.zero_()` then kills the scheduler, and both EAGLE test files report 0 tests run on AMD CI:
```
File "python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/decode_attention.py", line 2004, in _decode_lean_attention_fwd
    locks.zero_()
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'zero_'
```
ROCm-only, since the Lean dispatch is `_is_hip`-gated.
## Modifications
- `triton_backend.py`: pass the same `cuda_graph_lean_*` buffers the non-spec capture path already passes.
- `decode_attention.py`: require `lean_locks is not None` to select Lean, so a missing buffer falls back to the standard kernel instead of crashing.
## Accuracy Tests
Not applicable — restores a code path that currently aborts. Lean numerics unchanged.
## Speed Tests and Profiling
Not applicable.
## Test
On MI355X, `decode_attention_fwd` with `enable_lean=True` and the buffers absent: reproduces the `AttributeError` before, returns finite output after.

title: [Diffusion] Fuse Qwen-Image FP8 QKV projection and Blackwell epilogue
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

This PR optimizes the Qwen-Image ModelOpt attention projection pipeline on
Blackwell in two precision-specific ways:

- **FP8:** merge each image/text Q/K/V triplet into one packed projection,
  preserving every checkpoint shard's original FP8 weight and scale through
  CUTLASS channelwise scaling. The packed BF16 result is split into zero-copy
  strided Q/K/V views.
- **NVFP4 and FP8:** one JIT CUDA epilogue performs per-head Q/K RMSNorm,
  interleaved RoPE, V copy, and joint `[text, image]` Q/K/V output packing.

For FP8 this changes six projection GEMMs and six activation-quantization calls
per block invocation into two packed GEMMs and two quantization calls, then
feeds their views directly to the epilogue without contiguous copies.

The first FP8 prototype requantized all three checkpoint weight shards to their
largest scale. It was fast but failed the quality gate (SSIM 0.883575, LPIPS
0.075531), so that implementation was rejected. The final implementation uses
CUTLASS's existing per-output-channel scale support and is pixel-exact against
main after 50 denoise steps.

The JIT epilogue remains restricted to eager CUDA Blackwell+, BF16 batch-1,
head dimension 128, aligned Q/K/V storage, FP32 RoPE caches, and an
unpadded/unsharded text stream. Unsupported cases use the original contiguous
PyTorch/kernel composition. The NVFP4 projections remain separate because
their activation and weight scale layouts are not interchangeable.

## End-to-end benchmarks

Common setup: 1x NVIDIA GB300 288 GB (SM103), GPU clock locked to 1800 MHz,
CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0, native SGLang backend, 1024x1024, 50 denoise steps,
true CFG 4.0, lossless PNG, seed 20260830, and resident text encoder/VAE/DiT.
Each side ran five fresh processes after one request warmup in the balanced
order `main, PR, PR, main, PR, main, main, PR, main, PR`.

### Qwen-Image ModelOpt FP8

Checkpoint: `lmsys/qwen-image-modelopt-fp8-sglang-transformer` with the base
components from `Qwen/Qwen-Image`.

| Denoise / step | 310.168 +/- 8.553 ms | 245.247 +/- 5.511 ms | **20.93%** | 310.401 ms | 244.832 ms | **21.12%** |
| Denoise / request | 15508.380 +/- 427.670 ms | 12262.370 +/- 275.541 ms | **20.93%** | 15520.053 ms | 12241.579 ms | **21.12%** |

### Qwen-Image-2512 ModelOpt NVFP4

| Metric | main (mean +/- stdev) | PR (mean +/- stdev) | Mean reduction | main median | PR median | Median reduction |

title: [ROCm] Take the fused DSA metadata kernels and drop redundant work from the absorb path
author: xiaobochen-amd
body:
Three ROCm-only changes on the DSA decode path. All numbers are GLM-5.2-MXFP4 /
MI355X / TP4, agentic replay at concurrency 4, paired per request against the
same branch without the change.

## Fused DSA metadata kernels

The five sites that build DSA's per-step metadata read `is_cuda() and not
_is_hip`, so HIP falls back to a PyTorch sequence of seven or eight ops. The
kernels they skip are three `@triton.jit` functions in
`kernels/ops/attention/dsa_metadata.py` — no `tl.dot`, no atomics, no CUDA
intrinsics. Their only device references are `.is_cuda` asserts, which are True
for HIP tensors.

The fallback is worse than its op count suggests. On target-verify it does a
`req_to_token[req_pool_indices, :max_seqlen_k]` gather where `max_seqlen_k` is
the *graph buffer's* width, not the request's kv length. At `context_len`
1048576 that is a `[bs, 1.05M]` int32 gather, a `[bs*6, 1.05M]` transient and a
100 MB copy — every decode step. The Triton kernel writes `page_table_1`
directly and returns early on column blocks past `kv_len`, so at this workload's
median 62k context it touches ~6% of them.

**ITL ratio p50 0.984** over 82 requests, 58 of them faster, sign test
p = 0.0002. TTFT 0.998.

2% is small enough that the direction matters more than the magnitude: 58/82 is
what says it reproduces, and the effect is the size the traffic argument
predicts rather than something larger, because PyTorch's caching allocator
reuses the same 100 MB block every step and only the bandwidth is recovered.

## q_all cat-skip on target-verify

`_fused_rope_cat_and_cache` already returns the concatenated absorbed query, and
decode hands it to `attn_mqa` with `q_rope=None` so the backend reuses it as a
view. Target-verify instead split it back into two views and let
`forward_extend` run `concat_mla_absorb_q_general` over them — rebuilding a
tensor byte-identical to the one it started from, one `CatArrayBatchedCopy` per
layer per step.

`assert q_rope is not None` in `forward_extend` sat directly above an
`if q_rope is not None ... else` whose else branch is exactly the zero-copy path,
so the assert was what made that branch dead code. `forward_decode` already had
the shape this needs — a `q_all=None` sentinel and `if q_all is None or not
_is_hip` at the point of use, the `not _is_hip` clause keeping CUDA
byte-identical. This mirrors it into `forward_extend`.

Real prefill keeps the split form: the Triton sparse-MLA kernel reads `q_nope`
and `q_rope` separately, and its own gate (`q_nope.shape[0] >= 512`) never
matches target-verify at this batch size.

**ITL ratio p50 0.971** (60 of 80 faster) and **0.976** (59 of 79) against two
baselines. TTFT 0.995 and 1.003 — unchanged, which is the check that it landed
on the decode path.

## Constant work in the absorb bmms

The bf16 fallback in `rocm_absorb_q_bmm` / `rocm_absorb_v_bmm` redoes
`w.to(bfloat16) * w_scale` every forward. `w_kc`/`w_vc` are weights and
`w_scale` is a load-time scalar; when the checkpoint ships `kv_b_proj` as bf16,
`w_scale` stays at its 1.0 default and this is a full elementwise pass over the
weight to multiply it by one — 4.4 us for `w_kc` and 4.8 us for `w_vc` per
layer, 0.71 ms across 78 layers.

The v-side then materialized its output a second time. The mxfp4 and fp8
branches allocate `_bmm_buf` as `(batch, heads, dim)` so the post-GEMM flatten
is a view; the bf16 branch fell through to `.transpose(0, 1).flatten(1, 2)` on a
non-contiguous tensor, which copies — another 4.7 us per layer, 0.37 ms per
forward. Give it the same layout, guarded by `is_in_tc_piecewise_cuda_graph()`
for the same reason `forward_mla.py:882` guards its equivalent path: dynamo
rejects `out=` with a non-contiguous output tensor.

**Together 1.08 ms of a 16.7 ms 78-layer forward — 7.9% of per-layer kernel
time.**

## Platform scope

Every change is either behind `_is_hip` or lives in `forward_mla_rocm.py`. CUDA
and every other platform are byte-identical.

title: [Diffusion] Fuse Qwen-Image residual norm and NVFP4 quantization
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

This PR implements the Qwen-Image NVFP4 `resnorm_quant` optimization described
in [Agentic Kernels in Production](https://www.baseten.co/blog/agentic-kernels-in-production/).
For the image and text FFN branches, one Blackwell JIT kernel now performs:

- `residual_out = residual + gate * (attention_output + output_bias)`;
- FP32-accumulated LayerNorm and BF16 scale/shift modulation;
- direct E2M1 activation packing; and
- direct 128x4-swizzled E4M3 scale writes for the following ModelOpt FP4 FC1.

This removes the large BF16 modulation intermediate and the following
`flashinfer.fp4_quantize` launch. The conversion uses the same
FlashInfer/TensorRT-LLM helper as the production quantizer, so packed values,
scales, and residual output are byte-exact.

The model fast path is limited to eager ModelOpt FP4 on SM10x, BF16 batch-1
Qwen hidden-size-3072 tensors. Dynamic CFG modulation selection, `torch.compile`,
breakable CUDA graphs/stream capture, affine LayerNorm, incompatible FlashInfer
quantization modes, and unsupported shapes/layouts/devices retain the original
path. The NVFP4 wrapper has its own JIT module and optional internal-header
dependency, so the existing BF16 norm JIT does not acquire a FlashInfer build
dependency.

This PR is now standalone on the current `main`. It carries a narrow
`apply_nvfp4_gemm_prequantized` helper for the already-packed Qwen activation
path and does not include, depend on, or modify the FLUX.2 optimization from
#37096. The helper leaves `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod.apply` unchanged, so ordinary
linear calls retain their reference behavior.

## End-to-end benchmark

Hardware: 1x NVIDIA GB300 288 GB (SM103), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0. The SM
clock was locked to 1800 MHz for this comparison and restored afterwards.

Model/workload: Qwen-Image-2512 ModelOpt NVFP4, native SGLang backend,
1024x1024, 50 denoise steps, true CFG 4.0, lossless quality, seed 20260830,
resident text encoder/VAE/DiT. Each side ran five fresh processes after one
request warmup in balanced order:
`main, PR, PR, main, PR, main, main, PR, main, PR`.

| Metric | main (mean +/- stdev) | PR (mean +/- stdev) | Mean reduction | main median | PR median | Median reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

All runs are included in the statistics; no outlier was removed.

The 224 fused calls correspond to 56 quantized transformer blocks, two streams,
and the two profiled denoiser passes. The four checkpoint-excluded blocks keep

The committed production-composition microbenchmark is byte-exact for all

title: [AMD] Fix the QuickReduce bf16 cast failing to build for CDNA
author: yctseng0211
body:

## Motivation

#34484 blocked the `(bf16_as_f32 * scale) -> fp16` reassociation by naming `v_cvt_pk_f16_f32` in inline asm, but that instruction is not part of the CDNA ISA, so every gfx942 build now fails to assemble (`error: instruction not supported on this GPU`) and takes the AMD CI down with it.
What stopped the reassociation was making the scaled values opaque to the optimizer rather than the choice of instruction, so this swaps the named instruction for an empty asm barrier and leaves the narrowing to `__float22half2_rn` — portable to every target, and the same round-to-nearest conversion the quantized path in this file already uses.
Verified on gfx942, gfx950 and gfx90a: the generated gfx942 asm keeps `v_mul_f32` ahead of `v_cvt_f16_f32`, and removing the barrier makes the multiply vanish entirely, which is exactly the reassociation #34484 set out to prevent.

title: [ROCm] Fix EAGLE spec-decode verify silently sampling greedy on HIP
author: xiaobochen-amd
body:
## Problem

EAGLE spec-decode verify has been committing `argmax` on ROCm, ignoring
`temperature` and `top_p` entirely, with nothing in the log saying so. At
`temp > 0` it degenerates into repetition loops.

The cause is one line in `eagle_sample`:

```python
if sampling_info.is_all_greedy or _is_cpu or _is_npu or _is_hip or _is_xpu:
    target_predict = torch.argmax(next_token_logits, dim=-1)
```

`_is_hip` sits next to `is_all_greedy`, so HIP takes the greedy path
unconditionally. It is there because the sampling branch needs
`tree_speculative_sampling_target_only`, `top_k_renorm_prob` and
`top_p_renorm_prob`, all of which are CUDA/MUSA-only in `sgl_kernel`.

## Fix

Route HIP through the pure-Triton chain sampler in `reject_sampling.py` when
rejection sampling is active and the batch is not all-greedy, with a Triton
renorm (`_renorm_top_k_top_p_hip`) standing in for the CUDA-only renorm ops.

The gate becomes a pure helper, `_verify_uses_greedy`. On every non-HIP platform
it reduces to the predicate it replaces: with `is_hip` False the added term drops
out and the expression is the original one.

`_renorm_top_k_top_p_hip` follows the same shape as the op it replaces — a
threshold search, matching `top_p_renorm_prob`'s ternary pivot search on
`f(x) = sum(probs[probs > x])` — so it agrees with CUDA rather than with a
sort-based nucleus. `top_p >= 1.0` short-circuits to an exact pass-through, to
stay bit-exact with CUDA's `top_p_renorm_prob(p, 1.0) == p`. top-k uses a sort,
skipped entirely when no row restricts it.

Defaulting the flag on matters: without it the fix only reaches users who pass
`--speculative-use-rejection-sampling`, and everyone else still silently gets
argmax verify. It flips only on HIP, for EAGLE/EAGLE3 with `topk=1`, default
accept thresholds and non-deterministic inference — the same conditions the
validation below raises on, so the flip can never turn a working config into an
error. Setting it also makes the draft worker emit the target-vocab proposal
(`draft_probs`) the Triton chain sampler consumes.

## Two shapes that come from the current tree, not from the fix

Worth pointing out so they don't read as gratuitous:

**`sampling_fn` dispatch.** It used the eager `A if cond else B` form, which
resolves `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only` whether or not that branch is
taken. HIP must not import it at all, so the dispatch becomes an `if`/`else`
that imports inside the arm needing it. Non-HIP behaviour is unchanged.

**One `cfg` read becomes `resolved_view`.** `_handle_eagle_family` writes through
`declare_resolution`, whose contract is that a field it decides is *not* visible
to a later `cfg.` read. The rejection-sampling validation immediately below was
reading `cfg`, so it would have skipped every auto-enabled config — including its
own "rejection sampling is enabled" log. That read becomes
`resolved_view(server_args)`, which is what the `declare_resolution` docstring
prescribes for exactly this case.

## Test

- `test/registered/unit/spec/test_eagle_gate_routing.py` — gate truth table, CPU.
  Pins that the helper reduces to the original predicate off HIP, and that HIP
  only leaves greedy when rejection sampling is on and the batch is not
  all-greedy. 4 tests.
- `test/registered/spec/eagle/test_rocm_eagle_renorm.py` — renorm numerical
  equivalence against an independent torch reference, plus the `top_p == 1.0`
  exact-no-op and `top_p -> 0` edges. Registered for both CUDA and AMD runners;
  the kernel is device-agnostic. 5 tests.

`ruff`, `isort` and `black` clean.

title: [AMD] fix: use the hardware fp8 e4m3 convert on gfx950
author: amd-danli103
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
`pack_fp8` is the fp8 quantization step in the DSv4, DSv3.2-indexer, MiniMax and Kimi-K3 kernels. On ROCm it is a hand-written bit twiddle, and it converts part of its input range wrong.

The overflow check is `exp8 >= kMaxExp`, and that is off by one. `exp8 == kMaxExp` is not overflow, it is the top exponent of the format, and e4m3 holds plenty of values there. So on gfx950 everything from 256 to 448 gets written out as 448. At the bottom of that range, that is 75% too big. Rounding is biased upward as well: ties go away from zero instead of to even, and one bf16 input in sixteen lands exactly on a tie.

This is not an edge case. Every caller picks a scale that puts its largest element at or just under the format maximum, which is exactly where the broken range sits. With a ue8m0 scale, about 4.5% of a group of 64 falls in it. With the plain fp32 amax scale that the indexer paths use, the maximum lands on 448 every single time, and the figure is 11.4%.

Nobody caught this because a wrong byte does not look like a bug from outside. Every caller quantizes `value * inv_scale`, so a bad conversion just makes fp8 look lossier than expected. No NaN, no crash, no failing test. And the conversion had never been tested on its own, only inside fused kernels that cannot tell a bad byte from ordinary quantization loss.

While gfx950 and gfx12xx can do this in hardware. `v_cvt_pk_fp8_f32` converts two floats to e4m3 with round-to-nearest-even in a single instruction, HIP exposes it as `__hip_cvt_float2_to_fp8x2`, and this tree already uses the scalar form in `per_token_quant_fp8.cu`. This PR just routes those archs through it.


## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
There are two copies of this cast in the tree. Each gets a new branch, and neither existing implementation is touched.

* `jit/include/sgl_kernel/deepseek_v4/fp8_utils.cuh` (+23 / −2). The software cast becomes the `#else`. The two deleted lines are a stale comment above it.

* `aot/csrc/elementwise/dsv4_norm_rope.cu` (+12 / −0). The same branch, added as an `#elif` between the CUDA one and this file's own copy of the cast.

  Why this file needs its own branch rather than including the shared header: `elementwise.py` sends `fused_q_indexer_rope_hadamard_quant` to `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.dsv4_fused_q_indexer_rope_hadamard_quant` when `_is_hip`, so on ROCm the DSv4 indexer's q quantization runs the AOT op and never sees the JIT header. Including the header here would also be wrong: this file hardcodes `kFP8Max = 448` on every arch, because its caller allocates a `float8_e4m3fn` tensor, while the header's clip is meant to follow the arch.

The two files gate the new branch differently, and that is on purpose.

In the AOT file `hip_fp8.h` is already in scope through torch, so it can just test `HIP_FP8_TYPE_OCP && !HIP_FP8_TYPE_FNUZ`. Both macros, not only OCP: HIP sets both to 1 on the host pass and on targets it does not know about.

The JIT header cannot test them at all — nothing in its include tree pulls `hip_fp8.h` in, so they are undefined there. Adding the include to read them would break gfx942. The software cast further down the same header picks its bias and saturation constants with `#if HIP_FP8_TYPE_FNUZ`. That reads 0 today, so it compiles the fn constants; put the include above it and it reads 1 and switches to fnuz. One `pack_fp8` call goes from 189 instructions to 181 — a silent change to the one arch this PR is meant to leave alone. So the header includes `hip_fp8.h` only under `__gfx950__ / __gfx1200__ / __gfx1201__`, and gates on that.
We clip the values before the call instead of passing `__HIP_SATFINITE`, because the x2 fast path converts what you handed it rather than the clamped value (ROCm 7.2).

gfx942 is left as it is. It writes E4M3FNUZ, which this instruction does not produce there, so it keeps the software cast in both copies and needs a separate fix. Nothing is deleted, so any arch other than gfx950/gfx12xx converts exactly the same bytes as before.

Also added: `cvt_fp8_e4m3`, a thin wrapper over `pack_fp8` so the conversion can be tested on its own — nothing in the serving path calls it — and `test/registered/amd/test_dsv4_fp8_cast.py`.


## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->
All on gfx950 (MI355X, ROCm 7.2).

**JIT copy.** `test_dsv4_fp8_cast` compares `pack_fp8` byte for byte with torch's `float8_e4m3fn` cast over 148346 values: every representable value, every midpoint between two of them, every bf16 bit pattern in range, plus a 100k sweep. Before, 41630 bytes differ.
After, all 148346 match. The test only runs on gfx95 and is registered to the mi35x suite, since the default AMD runner is mi300 and that still takes the software path.

**AOT copy.** `test_dsv4_indexer_quant` already covers that op, but it was skipped on HIP entirely. This un-skips it for gfx95 with int32 positions, and moves the file's AMD registration to the mi35x suite: gfx942 still runs the software cast there, so the mi300 registration was only ever producing skips. All six cases failed before; all six pass now.
`weights_out` matches to 1e-3 in both runs, so the only thing that changed is the quantized bytes. To be clear, `main` is not red today — on HIP the whole file skips.

**the other tests.** The other kernel tests that share `pack_fp8` give identical results before and after: 16 passed / 36 failed / 22 skipped. Those failures are `test_dsa_indexer` patching `deep_gemm`, which does not exist on ROCm. `aot/tests/test_dsv4_norm_rope.py`, which covers the rest of the AOT file, is 16 passed either way.

The instruction really is being used, not just compiled in: the JIT module the test loads has exactly one `v_cvt_pk_fp8_f32`, and the AOT file's gfx950 code object has 11, up from 0. No gfx942 hardware here, but the compiler settles it: building the same `pack_fp8` call for gfx942 against the base header and against this one gives identical assembly — 138 instructions each, no `v_cvt_pk_fp8_f32`, and the only textual difference is the `__hip_cuid_*` symbol, which is just a hash of the file path. gfx942 emits exactly what it emitted before. Its bytes do not change, so there is nothing there to regress.

No end-to-end accuracy run. How much this matters at model level depends on which callers a given recipe hits.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->
Instruction counts instead of wall clock, from a single `-O3` compile for `gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-`: 15 instructions per value with the hardware convert, versus 85 for the software twiddle. Fixing the software cast's rounding would take it to 126, because proper round-to-nearest-even needs the sticky bits. That is the argument for taking the instruction on gfx950 even after someone fixes the software path.

No wall clock numbers. Whether this shows up depends on the caller — the norm+rope kernels are close to bandwidth bound and will probably hide it. Memory traffic and vectorization are unchanged, and archs on the software path see no change at all.

## Known, not fixed here

- **The software cast still has both bugs, in both copies.** That is what gfx942 runs. The AOT copy also masks off a subnormal carry with `& 0x7u`, which writes the min normal out as zero. #36390 may be related.
- **The ROCm AOT op only accepts int32 positions.** It rejects int64 with a `TORCH_CHECK` while the CUDA path takes both, which is why the un-skip is narrowed. It refuses cleanly rather than returning something wrong.
- **The ROCm AOT op reads the weight linearly**, so a non-contiguous slice comes out wrong.
  `test_v4_strided_weight_matches_contiguous` stays CUDA-only for that reason. Nothing hits it today, since the indexer passes the contiguous `weights_proj` output.
- **The JIT header's arch selection is dead on ROCm.** `type.cuh` picks `kFP8E4M3Max`  with `#if HIP_FP8_TYPE_FNUZ`, and the software cast picks its bias and saturation constants the same way, but nothing in that include tree defines the macro, so both `#if`s read 0 and the fnuz branches never compile. gfx942 gets a 448 clip and fn-encoded bytes today. Untouched here — I have no gfx942 to check a fix on — but it looks worth a look alongside #36390.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Diffusion] Fuse FLUX.2 token concatenation and NVFP4 quantization
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

This PR fuses the FLUX.2 single-stream output sequence

```text
torch.cat([attention_bf16, swiglu_bf16]) -> FlashInfer NVFP4 quantize -> to_out GEMM
```

into one SM103 JIT kernel that reads both BF16 branches and writes the concatenated E2M1 values and 128x4-swizzled E4M3 scales directly. A standalone ModelOpt helper feeds the packed activations and scales directly to the existing FP4 `to_out` GEMM; this PR has no dependency on #37096.

This removes one 24,576-wide BF16 materialization and one full-width quantization read in each of the 48 single-stream blocks. Unsupported shapes, TP > 1, non-SM103 devices, compile/capture, alternate FP4 modes, or missing layout guarantees retain the existing path.

> [!NOTE]
> This PR is now based directly on current `main` and contains no #37096 commits. The benchmark below was originally collected with #37096 present in both baseline and candidate, so the reported delta still isolates only the token-cat fusion.

## Implementation

- add a lightweight JIT CUDA kernel using TensorRT-LLM's `cvt_warp_fp16_to_fp4`, the same conversion primitive used by FlashInfer;
- add a standalone prequantized-input ModelOpt GEMM helper so this PR does not depend on #37096's tuple interface;
- write packed values and swizzled scale factors in the exact layout expected by the existing NVFP4 GEMM;
- enable it only for FLUX.2-dev's TP1 `(6144 attention | 18432 MLP)` projection on SM103;
- keep eager BF16 cat + quantization as the fallback for torch.compile, CUDA graph capture, unsupported FP4 modes, shapes, devices, and row counts;
- fail clearly if the installed FlashInfer package does not provide the required NVFP4 headers.

## End-to-end benchmark

Hardware and workload:

- 1x NVIDIA GB300 288 GB, GPU clock locked to 1800 MHz
- `/scratch/models/FLUX.2-dev-NVFP4`
- native SGLang backend, all components resident
- 1024x1024, 50 denoising steps, guidance 4.0, seed 20260830, lossless PNG
- one request warmup per process
- 5 baseline + 5 PR processes in balanced order: `main, pr, pr, main, pr, main, main, pr, main, pr`
- historical isolated baseline: #37096 head `f37a2a874f`; candidate: `e423a737d3` (the same parent was present on both sides)

| Metric | Parent mean +/- stdev | PR mean +/- stdev | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Denoise / step | 136.883 +/- 0.176 ms | 133.580 +/- 0.099 ms | **2.413%** |
| Denoise / request | 6844.131 +/- 8.819 ms | 6678.984 +/- 4.943 ms | **2.413%** |
| End-to-end / request | 6980.339 +/- 14.099 ms | 6813.233 +/- 4.094 ms | **2.394%** |

The committed microbenchmark measures `cat + flashinfer.fp4_quantize` against the fused producer:

| Tokens | Baseline | Fused | Speedup | Packed/scales exact |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | :---: |
| 17 | 68.78 us | 45.60 us | 1.51x | yes |
| 512 | 66.50 us | 44.53 us | 1.49x | yes |
| 4096 | 103.09 us | 43.95 us | 2.35x | yes |
| 4608 | 114.31 us | 47.70 us | 2.40x | yes |

## Profile evidence

A torch-profiler comparison of two denoise steps at 1024x1024 shows:

| Per denoise step | Parent | PR | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Total kernel launches | 1089 | 1041 | **-48** |
| Single-block BF16 cat launches | 48 | 0 | **-48** |
| Standalone NVFP4 quant launches | 104 | 56 | **-48** |
| Fused token-cat quant launches | 0 | 48 | +48 |
| Target cat + quant GPU time | 5464 us | 2261 us | **-58.625%** |
| Total GPU kernel duration | 129355 us | 126017 us | **-3337 us** |

## Accuracy and generated-image comparison

### Isolated effect of this PR

All ten 50-step images in the 5+5 parent/PR run have the same SHA256:

```text
345079f4c6e1638499b3a55fd98d563d1ae71248efa0ef92723075066e7bab97
```

| Metric | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Pixel exact | **yes** |
| SSIM | **1.000000** |
| PSNR | **infinity** |
| LPIPS (Alex) | **0.000000** |
| Pixel cosine similarity | **1.000000** |
| Max / mean absolute pixel difference | **0 / 0** |

The committed kernel test additionally requires the E2M1 bytes and swizzled E4M3 scale bytes to exactly match `flashinfer.fp4_quantize(torch.cat(...))`.

### Independent-branch accuracy scope

The token-cat producer is byte-exact against `flashinfer.fp4_quantize(torch.cat(...))`, and the isolated parent/candidate image comparison above is pixel-exact. The previously shown upstream-main vs complete-stack drift came from #37096, which is no longer part of this branch, so that comparison has been removed.

## Validation

Current independent head:

- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `compileall`, and `git diff --check`: passed locally;
- diffusion import-surface suite: **9 passed** locally;
- a committed GPU test checks the standalone prequantized-input helper against the regular ModelOpt quantize + GEMM path for both default and TensorRT-LLM FlashInfer backends; GPU execution is delegated to CI because no SM103 development assignment is currently active.

Historical SM103 validation of the unchanged token-cat kernel at `e423a737d3`:

- exact GB300 kernel comparison against FlashInfer;
- native SGLang 1024x1024 eager smoke;
- `--enable-torch-compile --enable-breakable-cuda-graph` native FLUX.2 smoke;
- parent/candidate image comparison was pixel-exact.

## Reproduction

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
python test/manual/kernels/bench_flux2_token_cat_nvfp4.py
```

The full A/B runner, raw JSON summaries, profiler summary, and lossless comparison images are retained in the local validation artifact bundle.

title: [PD] Optimize paged allocator free-list release
author: wangwenmingaa
body:
## Motivation

This PR is a follow-up to #33998, which defers free-list concatenation for
`LogicalHostPool`.

`PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator` still eagerly concatenates released page IDs on
every `free()` when `need_sort=True`:

```python
self.release_pages = torch.cat((*page_ids, self.release_pages))
```

This path is used by PD disaggregation allocators. Under workloads with frequent
SWA page releases, every release reallocates and copies the growing
`release_pages` tensor, even though these pages are not reused until the primary
free list runs low.

If the current release list contains `F` pages and the current call releases
`K` pages, each release performs `O(F + K)` free-list maintenance. Repeating
this operation during cache eviction introduces unnecessary allocator overhead.

This PR moves the concatenation out of the release hot path. Released page
tensors are queued as chunks and materialized only when an allocation cannot be
satisfied by the primary free list.

## Modifications

Apply deferred free-list merging to `PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator` when
`need_sort=True`:

- Keep released page-ID tensors in `pending_release_page_chunks` instead of
  concatenating them immediately.
- Track the number of pending released pages with
  `num_pending_release_pages`.
- Include pending pages in `available_size()`.
- Continue allocating from the primary `free_pages` tensor while it has
  sufficient capacity.
- Concatenate and sort pending chunks only when allocation pressure requires
  the released pages.
- Avoid recording empty releases.
- Reset all pending-release state in `clear()`.
- Include pending pages in duplicate-page and memory-leak invariant checks.
- Preserve the existing sorted page-reuse behavior.

The behavior for allocators with `need_sort=False` is unchanged.

The patch does not add runtime logging, configuration flags, or model-specific
behavior.

Unit tests cover:

- deferred release without rebuilding the primary free list;
- allocation from the primary free list before merging pending pages;
- sorted reuse of released pages after a deferred merge;
- merging multiple released chunks;
- pending-page availability accounting;
- state reset through `clear()`;
- preservation of the existing non-PD allocation behavior;
- duplicate-page detection across pending releases.

## Accuracy Tests

This change only modifies allocator free-list metadata.

It does not modify:

- model weights or model forward execution;
- KV cache tensor contents;
- cache keys or page-table mappings;
- attention, sampling, or CUDA kernels;
- PD KV transfer contents or protocols.

The allocator regression tests verify that the same page IDs are released and
reused in sorted order. Therefore, model output accuracy is not expected to
change.

Added and updated tests:

```text
test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_paged_allocator_lazy_release.py
test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_paged_free_segment.py
```

Local checks completed:

```text
PASS: Python syntax compilation for the modified source and test files
PASS: scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py
PASS: git diff --check
```

The registered CPU unit tests will also be executed by GitHub CI:

```bash
python3 test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_paged_allocator_lazy_release.py
python3 test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_paged_free_segment.py
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Before this change, every release may concatenate new page IDs with a growing
release list:

```text
Release-side free-list maintenance: O(F + K)
```

After this change, `free()` only records the released tensors and updates a
counter:

```text
Release-side free-list maintenance: O(1)
```

The larger concatenation and sort are deferred until the primary free list
cannot satisfy an allocation. Multiple releases can therefore be combined into
one allocation-side merge.

| Behavior | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `torch.cat` during every release | Yes | No |
| Primary allocation fast path | Tensor slice | Tensor slice |
| Released-page accounting | Eager tensor rebuild | Append chunk and update counter |
| Large merge | Once per release | Only when released pages are needed |
| Page reuse order | Sorted before reuse | Unchanged |
| `need_sort=False` behavior | Existing behavior | Unchanged |

The allocator was profiled on a DeepSeek V4 Flash PD prefill workload with
CP=4 and page size 256. Baseline and optimized runs used the same request
workload and serving configuration. The following results aggregate comparable
steady-state windows across four CP ranks.

### SWA allocator

| Metric | Eager baseline | Deferred merge | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Release calls | 5,792 | 6,004 | Comparable load |
| Released pages | 229,652 | 238,720 | Comparable load |
| Release-time `torch.cat` calls | 5,792 | 0 | -100% |
| CPU release-list update | 17.544 us/call | 1.506 us/call | -91.4% |
| CPU amortized queue cost | 20.590 us/call | 4.987 us/call | -75.8% |
| GPU release-list update | 0.03076 ms/call | 0.01202 ms/call | -60.9% |
| GPU amortized queue cost | 0.03514 ms/call | 0.01698 ms/call | -51.7% |

### Full-attention allocator

| Metric | Eager baseline | Deferred merge | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Release calls | 5,968 | 6,016 | Comparable load |
| Released pages | 237,208 | 239,224 | Comparable load |
| Release-time `torch.cat` calls | 5,968 | 0 | -100% |
| CPU release-list update | 19.041 us/call | 1.517 us/call | -92.0% |
| CPU amortized queue cost | 41.373 us/call | 32.900 us/call | -20.5% |
| GPU release-list update | 0.02866 ms/call | 0.01175 ms/call | -59.0% |
| GPU amortized queue cost | 0.06039 ms/call | 0.05236 ms/call | -13.3% |

The SWA allocator benefits more because multiple out-of-window releases can
accumulate before the released pages are needed. Full-attention pages are more
often evicted immediately before an allocation retry, so pending chunks are
merged more frequently.

These measurements isolate allocator hot-path overhead. This PR does not claim
an end-to-end throughput improvement.

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the
  [unit-test guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Documentation is not required because this change does not introduce or
  modify a user-facing interface.
- [x] Provide accuracy and performance analysis.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the
   [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from
   [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS)
   and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with the documented CI comments or contact an authorized
   user.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, and
     `/rerun-failed-ci`.
4. After CI is green and required approvals are collected, ask Merge Oncalls or
   a maintainer with write permission to merge the PR.

title: [ROCm] Widen the HiCache JIT copy rounds and enable the K-only host pool
author: jiejingzhangamd
body:
Depends on #35233. That PR makes registered host pointers usable from the
transfer kernels on ROCm; this one is the part that decides how much of the KV
cache can actually take that path, and how fast it moves once it does. An
earlier revision of this PR carried its own pointer fix (pin_memory allocation,
an unregister guard, and an io-backend downgrade for storage-owned memory);
those are dropped in favour of #35233, which solves the same problem more
generally and does not have to give up the kernel backend for storage-owned
pools.
 
## What is left here
 
**Copy rounds narrower than 128 B.** The JIT transfer kernels tiled each element
in 128 B rounds only, so an element size 128 does not divide could not use them
at all. MLA's fp8 row is 576 B. `pick_group_bytes()` now takes the widest round
of 128/64/32/16 that both divides the element and splits across the lanes into a
package the hardware has (4, 8 or 16 B).
 
**A block quota that suits ROCm.** 2 on CUDA, 16 on ROCm. The per-layer read path
loses bandwidth below that, which is also why the narrow rounds are worth their
extra instantiations only on ROCm.
 
**`MHATokenToKOnlyPoolHost` can use the JIT path.** `can_use_jit` accepted CUDA
only; the kernels are not CUDA-specific.
 
## CUDA is unchanged
 
Not "verified by inspection" — the narrow rounds are behind `#ifdef USE_ROCM`,
and the `#else` branch reduces to `group_fits(bytes, num_threads, 128)`, whose
three conditions are the two original `static_assert`s plus the package-size
constraint `PackageType` already imposed. `DEFAULT_BLOCK_QUOTA` and `GROUP_BYTES`
are gated the same way in Python. Non-ROCm builds generate the code they did
before.
 
## Tests
 
`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_copy_rounds.py`, CPU-only, in
`base-a-test-cpu`. `kvcache/hicache.py` screens element sizes with a Python copy
of `pick_group_bytes()`, and the two have to answer alike: a size the screen
wrongly admits fails a `static_assert` at JIT compile time, and one it wrongly
rejects silently loses the JIT path. The test sweeps element sizes against the
rule on both platforms and names 576 B as the boundary the narrow rounds exist
for. 5 cases, 963 subtests.
 
The lane count the screen derives from is a literal 32 mirroring
`device::kWarpThreads`; `kvcacheio/hicache.cuh` now `static_assert`s that
constant, so a wavefront-size change fails at the rule instead of silently
disagreeing with the screen.
 
## Measurements
 
TODO: re-measure on top of #35233. The numbers in the previous revision of this
description were taken with the pointer fix that has since been dropped, so they
do not describe this change.
 
ruff (F401,F821,UP037), ruff-format and isort clean.

title: [Diffusion] Fuse Qwen-Image FP8 norm and activation quantization
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

This PR implements the Qwen-Image FP8 norm + activation-quantization fusion
described in [Agentic Kernels in Production](https://www.baseten.co/blog/agentic-kernels-in-production/)
for SGLang's native diffusion backend on Blackwell.

The new JIT CUDA paths fuse:

- LayerNorm + AdaLN scale/shift + static E4M3 quantization for the image/text
  attention inputs; and
- gated residual add + LayerNorm + AdaLN scale/shift + static E4M3
  quantization for the image/text MLP inputs.

Each kernel returns both the original BF16 modulation output and its
prequantized FP8 representation. The ModelOpt FP8 projections consume the FP8
tensor directly, while the BF16 tensor remains live through the corresponding
projection to preserve the original allocation/lifetime semantics. On the
official checkpoint this enables 240/240 block paths.

The fast path is deliberately narrow: CUDA Blackwell+, BF16 batch-1 contiguous
tensors, hidden size 3072, affine-free LayerNorm, finite positive scalar FP32
ModelOpt input scales, no indexed modulation, no zero-condition-timestep path,
and no breakable CUDA graph. Separate Q/K/V projections must have identical
input scales; packed QKV from #37123 uses its materialized packed scale. Every
unsupported case keeps the existing path.

### Numerical exactness

Triton's reference static quantizer lowers its reciprocal to PTX
`div.full.f32`. A normal CUDA reciprocal differs by one FP32 ULP for real
checkpoint scales such as `0.4754464328` and can move values across an E4M3
midpoint. The fused kernel therefore uses the same PTX instruction. Those
checkpoint scales are included in the regression matrix, and both BF16 outputs
and FP8 bytes are checked exactly.

## End-to-end benchmarks

Common setup: 1x NVIDIA GB300 288 GB (SM103), GPU clock locked to 1800 MHz,
CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0, native SGLang backend,
`lmsys/qwen-image-modelopt-fp8-sglang-transformer` with `Qwen/Qwen-Image`
components, 1024x1024, 50 denoise steps, true CFG 4.0, lossless PNG, seed
20260830, and resident text encoder/VAE/DiT. Each side ran five fresh processes
after one request warmup in the balanced order
`main, PR, PR, main, PR, main, main, PR, main, PR`.

### Standalone against main

Baseline: main `5ab97c4f44`. Candidate: this PR `84cb0f246d`.

| Metric | main (mean +/- stdev) | PR (mean +/- stdev) | Mean reduction | main median | PR median | Median reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Denoise / step | 306.059 +/- 8.662 ms | 240.868 +/- 4.253 ms | **21.30%** | 306.791 ms | 239.230 ms | **22.02%** |
| Denoise / request | 15302.926 +/- 433.102 ms | 12043.390 +/- 212.630 ms | **21.30%** | 15339.551 ms | 11961.478 ms | **22.02%** |
| End to end | 15428.447 +/- 437.339 ms | 12168.591 +/- 214.548 ms | **21.13%** | 15464.279 ms | 12086.846 ms | **21.84%** |

### Incremental on top of fused FP8 QKV (#37123)

To make overlap explicit, I also compared QKV-only `f9a57d0adb` with the
QKV + norm/quant combination `ad8228e34b` under the same 5+5 protocol.

| Metric | #37123 only (mean +/- stdev) | + this PR (mean +/- stdev) | Mean reduction | #37123 median | combined median | Median reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Denoise / step | 245.724 +/- 4.698 ms | 201.361 +/- 3.408 ms | **18.05%** | 245.517 ms | 199.914 ms | **18.57%** |
| Denoise / request | 12286.207 +/- 234.917 ms | 10068.028 +/- 170.415 ms | **18.05%** | 12275.841 ms | 9995.701 ms | **18.57%** |
| End to end | 12414.678 +/- 238.680 ms | 10193.610 +/- 172.649 ms | **17.89%** | 12405.276 ms | 10118.819 ms | **18.43%** |

## Kernel benchmark

The fused measurements include both the BF16 output write and the FP8 output
write; this is not an FP8-only microbenchmark.

| Rows | Path | split norm + quant | fused | Speedup |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | norm | 3.6470 us | 2.9978 us | **1.217x** |
| 128 | residual norm | 3.9338 us | 3.2989 us | **1.192x** |
| 1024 | norm | 6.1866 us | 5.4285 us | **1.140x** |
| 1024 | residual norm | 7.4563 us | 6.3709 us | **1.170x** |
| 4096 | norm | 16.7030 us | 14.7062 us | **1.136x** |
| 4096 | residual norm | 22.5603 us | 20.3590 us | **1.108x** |

## Accuracy and generated-image comparison

For both the standalone and stacked 5+5 experiments, all main/baseline outputs
were mutually identical, all candidate outputs were mutually identical, and
the two sides shared the same PNG SHA256:
`e3a1d9840e96867cfb352589c9496db8531e3e4b581459fb5a1fb5dcd49c50ae`.

| Metric | main vs PR |
|---|---:|
| Pixel exact | **yes** |
| SSIM | **1.000000** |
| PSNR | **infinity** |
| LPIPS (AlexNet) | **0.000000** |
| Pixel cosine similarity | **1.000000** |
| Mean / max absolute pixel difference | **0 / 0** |

![Qwen-Image FP8 main vs PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-image-fp8-norm-quant/main-vs-pr.png)

## Validation

- full pre-commit suite on all changed files: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed
- standalone rebased branch on GB300: **75 passed**
  (`test_model_fast_paths.py`, 30 exact kernel cases, and 3 model gate cases)
- QKV-only rebase validation: **110 passed**, plus **16 subtests**
- combined QKV + norm/quant validation: **143 passed**, plus **16 subtests**
- exact BF16, residual BF16, and FP8-byte checks at 1/127/1024 rows across
  ordinary scales and two real checkpoint midpoint-sensitive scales
- two native 1024x1024 5+5 model-backed experiments, with native-backend
  fallback treated as a hard failure

title: [Kernel] Add tuned LFM2.5 Triton MoE configs on B300
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

LFM2.5-8B-A1B uses two BF16 Triton MoE GEMMs on B300 (`SM103`):

- gate/up projection: `E=32, N=3584, K=2048, topk=4`
- down projection: `E=32, N=2048, K=1792, topk=1`

The generic Triton path previously fell back to heuristic schedules for this
model/device pair. A shape-specific KDA kernel improved over that fallback, but a
separately tuned generic Triton baseline was faster for medium/large token counts
and high-concurrency serving. Therefore this PR has been converted to a
**config-only** change, following the same conclusion as #37159.

## Changes

Add B300 (`NVIDIA_B300_SXM6_AC`) Triton 3.7.1 configs for LFM2.5:

- gate/up config with 8 tuned M buckets
- down config with 8 tuned M buckets
- TMA enabled in every selected config

There is no custom kernel, dispatch branch, or model-specific runtime code in the
final diff.

## Tuning setup

Hardware: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (`SM103`). Software: CUDA 13.0, PyTorch
2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1.

The tuner ran on PR base `771e613d96de0ee89631bc308a2525aaeae9f13e`, where
the former KDA dispatch did not exist:

- 100 deterministic `E=32, topk=4` routing samples
- M grid: `1, 8, 32, 256, 1024, 2048, 4096, 16384`
- 240 focused configs per M
- `BLOCK_M`: 16/32/64/128/256
- schedules covering `BLOCK_N` 32/64/128/256, `BLOCK_K` 64/128,
  4/8 warps, 3/4/6 stages, and group sizes 1/8/16/32
- both gate/up and down TMA variants tested

The runtime uses nearest-M selection between the tuned buckets. Gate/up and down
configs use the same `BLOCK_SIZE_M` at each bucket, as required by the shared
expert-row alignment.

## Kernel results

The table compares the tuned generic Triton configs in this PR with the removed
KDA candidate. Times are microseconds per CUDA-Graph replayed gate/up + down pair.
A negative final-column value means tuned Triton is faster.

| M | Tuned Triton total (us) | KDA total (us) | Tuned vs KDA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 20.017 | 20.660 | -3.11% |
| 2 | 32.027 | 31.309 | +2.29% |
| 4 | 52.441 | 55.971 | -6.31% |
| 8 | 75.484 | 79.210 | -4.70% |
| 16 | 101.460 | 98.284 | +3.23% |
| 32 | 110.967 | 111.268 | -0.27% |
| 64 | 113.710 | 137.305 | -17.18% |
| 128 | 121.576 | 138.931 | -12.49% |
| 256 | 131.048 | 140.796 | -6.92% |
| 512 | 147.158 | 168.365 | -12.60% |
| 1024 | 167.568 | 244.532 | -31.47% |
| 2048 | 238.466 | 328.062 | -27.31% |
| 4096 | 413.532 | 551.839 | -25.06% |
| 16384 | 1242.570 | 1974.426 | -37.07% |

KDA has two small wins at M=2 and M=16 and is effectively tied at M=32. Tuned
Triton is consistently faster from M=64 onward. At M=4096, KDA's specialized
gate/up kernel is 3.4% faster, but its down projection is much slower, so the
combined path still loses by 25.06%.

## LFM2.5-8B-A1B serving results

Two TP1 servers were benchmarked concurrently. GPU assignments were then swapped
and the full matrix repeated. Each assignment used seeds 1001/1002/1003. Results
pair the same physical GPU and use the geometric mean of GPU0/GPU1 ratios to
remove multiplicative card-to-card bias.

- concurrency: `1, 4, 16, 32, 64`
- decode: input 1, output 256, `max(16, 4 * concurrency)` prompts
- mixed: input 1024, output 256, `max(8, 2 * concurrency)` prompts
- fixed lengths with `--random-range-ratio 1.0`
- cache flushed before each trial

Positive throughput means tuned Triton is faster. Positive ITL means KDA has
higher (worse) ITL.

| Workload | Concurrency | Tuned throughput advantage | KDA ITL penalty |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| decode 1/256 | 1 | +0.38% | +0.44% |
| decode 1/256 | 4 | -0.78% | -0.36% |
| decode 1/256 | 16 | +0.67% | +0.73% |
| decode 1/256 | 32 | -0.56% | -0.38% |
| decode 1/256 | 64 | **+6.36%** | **+6.29%** |
| mixed 1024/256 | 1 | +1.06% | +1.20% |
| mixed 1024/256 | 4 | +1.94% | +1.45% |
| mixed 1024/256 | 16 | +1.86% | +1.07% |
| mixed 1024/256 | 32 | +1.31% | -0.14% |
| mixed 1024/256 | 64 | **+10.20%** | **+8.56%** |

Decode through concurrency 32 is effectively tied (all throughput differences
within 0.8%). The tuned configs win clearly at concurrency 64 and win every mixed
throughput point after GPU crossover correction.

## Correctness and validation

- Tuned generic Triton and the former KDA candidate matched exactly (`rtol=0`,
  `atol=0`) for both projections at M =
  `2, 4, 8, 16, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 4096, 16384` (22 cases).
- Completed 60 paired serving runs plus two additional concurrency-16 sanity
  runs, including the GPU0/GPU1 crossover.
- Both JSON files parse successfully, contain the expected 8 M buckets, enable
  TMA in every bucket, and keep gate/up and down `BLOCK_SIZE_M` aligned.
- `git diff --check` passes; the final PR diff contains only the two config files.

## Conclusion

The initial KDA work identified a real missing-config problem, but the custom
kernel is not the best fix after tuning the existing Triton path. The final PR
keeps the useful artifact—the tuned generic Triton configs—and removes 951 lines
of custom kernel, dispatch, and test code.

## Checklist

- [x] Tune generic Triton on the PR base, including gate/up and down TMA.
- [x] Compare 14 kernel token counts.
- [x] Validate exact output across decode and prefill shapes.
- [x] Compare concurrency 1/4/16/32/64 with three seeds and GPU crossover.
- [x] Convert the final diff to config-only.

title: [Kernel] Add GB300 Triton MoE configs for GLM-4.5 FP8
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

GLM-4.5-FP8 uses per-channel FP8 Triton MoE with the per-rank TP8 geometry
`E=161,H=5120,I=192,topk=9`. SGLang had no Triton 3.7.1 GB300 config for this
exact lane and therefore used the generic heuristic.

The missing tuned baseline was identified while validating
[KDA-Pilot PR #197](https://github.com/BBuf/KDA-Pilot/pull/197). A larger custom
kernel was also evaluated, but the tuned generic kernel was faster, so this PR
only adds the smaller configuration change. Validation uses current SGLang main
at `5ab97c4f441462f3d2adb1ffa954cc92518beece`.

## Modifications

- Add a sparse Triton configuration map for `E=161,N=192`, NVIDIA GB300,
  `fp8_w8a8`, `per_channel_quant=True`, and Triton 3.7.1.
- Cover decode/small batch through 16K-token prefill. The existing optional
  down-projection fallback reuses the same tuned map.
- Add a CPU test that pins the expected token grid and verifies the config is
  packaged.

The filename's device, Triton, dtype, and scale-mode selectors keep all other
hardware, Triton versions, quantization modes, and MoE shapes on their existing
fallbacks.

## Accuracy Tests

Hardware: 2 nodes, 4x NVIDIA GB300 (SM103) per node, TP8 over the same NVLink
domain. Software: CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_fused_moe_triton_config.py
```

Result: `4 passed`.

An exact-production-shape comparison of the default and tuned schedules used
`[161,384]` / `[161,5120]` per-channel scale tensors. For M=1/16/256/2048,
the largest observed absolute difference was `2.4e-7` and the largest mean
relative difference was `1.67e-8`. The real TP8 server loaded the exact config
on all ranks and completed all 74 prefill and 52 decode CUDA Graph captures.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Full FP8 fused-experts call under CUDA Graph

This includes up GEMM, SiLU-and-mul, down GEMM, routed weighting, and combine.

| Tokens | Default (us) | Tuned (us) | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 32.788 | 30.730 | 1.067x |
| 16 | 121.018 | 84.050 | 1.440x |
| 256 | 236.390 | 136.889 | 1.727x |
| 512 | 244.532 | 160.625 | 1.522x |

The sweep used the production `E=161,H=5120,I=192,topk=9` geometry and real
`[E,N]` per-channel scale layout.

### GLM-4.5-FP8 serving

Two-node TP8, concurrency 16. Each number is the median of three trials with
seeds 1001/1002/1003. `--random-range-ratio 1.0` fixes every request at the
stated lengths, and each trial flushes the cache.

| Workload | Baseline output tok/s | This PR output tok/s | Change | Mean TPOT change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 input / 256 output, 256 prompts | 1016.42 | 1238.80 | **+21.88%** | **-19.16%** |
| 1024 input / 256 output, 128 prompts | 926.13 | 1125.10 | **+21.48%** | **-19.52%** |

Per-trial output throughput was 1024.44/1010.58/1016.42 vs
1238.80/1234.85/1241.27 tok/s for decode, and 926.15/922.44/926.13 vs
1125.10/1124.37/1129.06 tok/s for mixed.

Server (run on both nodes with the corresponding rank):

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /scratch/models/GLM-4.5-FP8 --trust-remote-code \
  --quantization compressed-tensors --tp-size 8 --nnodes 2 \
  --node-rank ${RANK} --dist-init-addr ${RANK0_IP}:29501 \
  --moe-runner-backend triton --attention-backend trtllm_mha \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.902 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
  --max-prefill-tokens 16384 --page-size 64 \
  --disable-chunked-prefix-cache --enable-tf32-matmul \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm --port 30000
```

Benchmark (decode; mixed changes input length to 1024 and prompts to 128):

```bash
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \
  --model /scratch/models/GLM-4.5-FP8 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1 --random-output-len 256 \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 16 \
  --seed 1001 --warmup-requests 16 --flush-cache --disable-tqdm
```

## Checklist

- [x] Validate JSON and format/check the changed test.
- [x] Add a registered CPU config test.
- [x] Documentation is not required for this device/version-specific config.
- [x] Provide accuracy, microbenchmark, and repeated real-model serving results.

title: [Diffusion] Fuse FLUX.2 ModelOpt FP8 producers and QKV packing
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

This PR implements the remaining FLUX.2 ModelOpt FP8 producer/packing optimizations from [Agentic Kernels in Production](https://www.baseten.co/blog/agentic-kernels-in-production/):

- fuse bit-exact LayerNorm + adaLN modulation + static FP8 quantization for all 80 eligible double/single-block producer paths;
- merge image/text QKV checkpoint shards into two channelwise-CUTLASS FP8 GEMMs per double block while preserving every shard's original FP8 bytes and scale;
- fuse double-block QK RMSNorm + RoPE + text/image joint QKV packing into one Blackwell JIT kernel that consumes the packed GEMM views directly;
- fuse single-block `[attention | MLP]` concatenation with static FP8 quantization, avoiding the full-width BF16 intermediate.

The three runtime changes share the packed checkpoint and prequantized-activation interface. The isolated norm producer measured only **-0.565%** e2e, and norm + merged QKV/epilogue measured **-0.768%**; I kept them together with token-cat + quant rather than opening sub-threshold performance PRs. The complete path reaches **-3.20% e2e / -3.25% denoise**.

## Scope and fallbacks

- Merged FP8 QKV and its epilogue are enabled only on **Blackwell, TP=1**.
- The token-cat FP8 producer is also TP=1 and Blackwell-only.
- BF16, Hopper FP8, TP>1, `torch.compile`, CUDA Graph capture, unsupported layouts, and SP text-tail padding retain the existing path.
- Packed NVFP4 behavior is unchanged by the new QKV epilogue.
- Mixed-precision packed shards are rejected instead of silently constructing a partially quantized fused layer.
- The post-load log confirms the producer coverage: `Enabled FLUX.2 FP8 norm+quant fusion for 80/80 block paths`.

## End-to-end benchmark

Hardware and workload:

- NVIDIA GB300 288 GB, GPU0 exclusive, SM clock locked at 1800 MHz
- base commit: `5ab97c4f441462f3d2adb1ffa954cc92518beece`
- transformer: [`lmsys/flux2-dev-modelopt-fp8-sglang-transformer`](https://huggingface.co/lmsys/flux2-dev-modelopt-fp8-sglang-transformer)
- native SGLang backend, all components resident (`--performance-mode manual`)
- 1024x1024, 50 steps, guidance 4.0, seed 20260830, `quality=lossless`
- request warmup, synchronized stage timing, 5 measured processes per variant
- interleaved order: `main, PR, PR, main, PR, main, main, PR, main, PR`

Representative command (run once from each source root; output/report names were changed per run):

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$SOURCE_ROOT/python" \
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \
SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1 \
sglang generate \
  --model-path /scratch/models/flux2-dev-modelopt-fp8-composed \
  --model-id FLUX.2-dev \
  --backend sglang \
  --component-paths.transformer /scratch/models/flux2-dev-modelopt-fp8-sglang-transformer \
  --performance-mode manual \
  --warmup-mode request \
  --warmup-steps 1 \
  --disable-autocast \
  --prompt "A cinematic technical poster of a red panda GPU engineer in a dark research laboratory, inspecting a luminous Blackwell accelerator board, with a notebook clearly labeled SGLANG FP8 NORM, realistic fur, intricate electronics, dramatic rim lighting" \
  --width 1024 --height 1024 \
  --num-inference-steps 50 \
  --guidance-scale 4.0 \
  --seed 20260830 \
  --quality lossless \
  --save-output \
  --output-file-path "$OUTPUT.png" \
  --perf-dump-path "$REPORT.json"
```

| Metric (5-run mean) | main | PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| End-to-end | 6847.800 ms | 6628.402 ms | **-3.204%** (1.0331x) |
| Denoise, 50 steps | 6708.975 ms | 6491.215 ms | **-3.246%** (1.0335x) |
| Denoise / step | 134.179 ms | 129.824 ms | **-3.246%** |
| E2E standard deviation | 9.359 ms | 9.781 ms | — |
| Denoise standard deviation | 6.519 ms | 8.247 ms | — |
| Runtime peak reserved memory | 81,130 MB | 80,692 MB | **-438 MB** |

### Ablation

All ablations used the same locked-clock 1024x1024/50-step protocol and were pixel-exact.

| Candidate | E2E change | Denoise change |
|---|---:|---:|
| Norm + FP8 quant producer only | -0.565% | -0.548% |
| + merged QKV and joint epilogue | -0.768% | -0.797% |
| + token-cat and FP8 quant producer (this PR) | **-3.204%** | **-3.246%** |

### Producer microbenchmarks

The registered benchmarks run in eager mode because the production fast paths deliberately fall back during CUDA Graph capture.

| Kernel / shape | Split main | Fused PR | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| token-cat + FP8 quant, 512 tokens, `[6144 | 18432]` | 24.224 us | 13.664 us | **1.77x** |
| token-cat + FP8 quant, 4096 tokens, `[6144 | 18432]` | 136.896 us | 52.576 us | **2.60x** |
| LN + modulate + FP8 quant, 512 rows x 6144 | 10.996 us | 9.184 us | **1.20x** |
| LN + modulate + FP8 quant, 4096 rows x 6144 | 47.000 us | 45.915 us | **1.02x** |
| LN + modulate + FP8 quant, 4608 rows x 6144 | 53.042 us | 50.328 us | **1.05x** |

## Profiler evidence

Torch profiler captured five active 1024x1024 denoise timesteps (the scheduled trace also contains its profiler warmup). Counts below are whole-trace counts, not normalized estimates.

| CUDA trace item | main | PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total kernels | 7,335 | 5,878 | **-1,457 (-19.9%)** |
| Static FP8 quant kernels | 1,196 | 199 | **-997 (-83.4%)** |
| QKV/GEMM kernels | 1,196 | 1,008 | **-188 (-15.7%)** |
| `cat` kernels | 836 | 386 | **-450 (-53.8%)** |

title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Clear deferred init metadata before speculative decode
author: aurickq
body:
## Why is this change needed?

Deferred Mamba clear/COW indices are one-shot metadata for an EXTEND forward. The target forward consumes them from `ForwardBatch`, but the original `ScheduleBatch` retains them. For a hybrid Mamba model using built-in multi-layer EAGLE/MTP, subsequent `DRAFT_EXTEND_V2` batches can copy those stale indices and replay the completed operation against live draft-pool state.

Clear the three fields at the EXTEND-to-DECODE boundary:

```diff
- EXTEND consumes clear/COW -> DRAFT_EXTEND_V2 replays the stale operation
+ EXTEND consumes clear/COW -> DRAFT_EXTEND_V2 sees no deferred operation
```

The issue was reproduced through the public Inkling integration. A one-step configuration makes the effect observable because multi-step boundary repair is inactive; it does not uniquely cause the stale metadata.

## Test Plan

- `PYTHONPATH=python python3 test/registered/unit/managers/test_schedule_batch_prepare_for_decode.py`: fails on upstream `main` with `tensor([1]) is not None`; passes with all three deferred fields cleared.
- Deterministic end-to-end A/B using Inkling with TP4, Mamba `extra_buffer`, chunked prefill 4096, one EAGLE step/top-k 1, and 24 fixed prompts x 32 output tokens. An identical baseline rerun reproduced the acceptance and output trace exactly.

| Metric | Baseline | Fix |
|---|---:|---:|
| Stale draft-pool replays across TP ranks | 2,312 | 0 |
| Accepted drafts / verify passes | 243 / 510 | 276 / 481 |
| Draft acceptance | 47.65% | 57.38% |

For one aligned prompt, after the same first verification, baseline proposed token 5517 (`p=0.18048`) and rejected it; the fix proposed token 25 (`p=0.27758`) and accepted it. The final target-verified output remained identical.

All 24 final output hashes matched across arms, as expected: target verification protects returned tokens while the fix changes draft acceptance and verify work. The diagnostic instrumentation synchronized both arms, so this is not a latency benchmark and makes no speed claim.

- `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_schedule_batch_prepare_for_decode.py`

title: [unified-memory] Drop the vacated 'dense' qualifier and the restating comments
author: ch-wan
body:
Stacked on #34613.

Two cleanups the unified-memory stack left behind.

**1. Drop the vacated `dense` qualifier from the KV vocabulary.** `dense` named a
per-layer KV view only in contrast to the strided MHA view, which no longer
exists, so the word marks nothing. Where it qualified a view it is dropped; where
it named the id space the views index it becomes `kernel-facing`, the term the
translator already uses.

Deliberately untouched, because the word still carries meaning there: MoE dense
layers and `first_k_dense_replace`, dense-vs-sparse attention (DSA fallback,
minimax `dense_layer_ids`, dual-chunk), trtllm_mla's dense `[bs, draft_token_num]`
query indptr, and the mamba conv/SSM "dense pitch" -- that pool really is
envelope-strided, so its contrast is live.

**2. Cut the comments that restate the line below them.** Eight copies of a
mock-runner comment that narrated its own call, four copies of the argument for
seeding a field to `None` (the house rule already says to), a duplicated
"check the fast path" line detached from the branch it described, and one
ungrammatical restatement. Also replaces the em-dashes this stack introduced in
comments and docstrings with `--`, per `.claude/rules/comment-style.md`.

No behavior change. Identifier renames are file-local (verified) apart from the
test-class and test-method names, which nothing outside their own files reads.

title: [CI][RFC] Replace black-jupyter with ruff-format
author: alexnails
body:
## Motivation

black-jupyter is now the dominant cost of the lint job: **218s** of the ~6min job (measured on run [33360547828](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33360547828/job/99390908592)), up from 143s in June — it re-formats every file each run, scales with the repo, and swings ±20% with runner CPU (observed 218s→260s across two runs of the same commit). Its on-disk cache can never work in CI (keyed on mtime; every fresh checkout misses).

`ruff format` produces black-compatible style in **~2s** (measured 1.8s over the full tree), formats the repo's notebooks natively, and consolidates onto the ruff binary the pre-commit config already pins (v0.15.1). This roughly halves lint job time and removes its only growing term (everything else was flattened by #37203).

**Draft / RFC**: this is the concrete migration for discussion — the one-time churn is real and worth an explicit maintainer decision on timing.

## What changes

Two commits, structured for review:

1. **Config swap** — `ruff-format` replaces `black-jupyter` in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, taking its exact position (after the ruff lint hook) and exclude list. Unlike the lint hook it has no `files:` restriction and no `.ipynb` exclusion, matching black-jupyter's coverage. black ran with no `[tool.black]` config anywhere (pure defaults), which are also ruff-format's defaults.
2. **Mechanical reformat** — nothing but the output of `pre-commit run ruff-format --all-files` at commit 1.

### How to review the 1397-file commit without reading it

```bash
git checkout <commit 1>
pre-commit run ruff-format --all-files
git diff <commit 2>   # empty
```

### What the diff actually is

All 3016 hunks fall into three deviations ruff [documents](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/formatter/black/) relative to black — none semantic:

| Class | Hunks | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Implicit string-concat literals joined when they fit on one line (incl. f-strings; runtime strings byte-identical) | ~1970 | `"a " "b"` → `"a b"` |
| Blank line at the top of a class/function body removed | 779 | `class X:` followed by a blank line before the first method |
| Same tokens, re-wrapped | 268 | multi-line f-string pieces onto one line |

Verified: a second `ruff-format` pass is a no-op; isort makes no counter-changes; the ruff lint hook passes; full local pre-commit suite passes on the reformatted tree.

## Rollout notes

- **Open PRs**: ~800 of the 1397 reformatted files were touched on main in the last 30 days, so conflicts are expected. Resolution recipe for PR authors: merge main, resolve conflicts either way, then `pre-commit run --all-files` — the formatter is deterministic, so everything converges. Best merged at a quiet moment (e.g. right after a release cut) with a heads-up announcement.
- **Blame**: after the squash-merge, a tiny follow-up PR adds the resulting main commit SHA to `.git-blame-ignore-revs` (GitHub blame honors it natively; the repo doesn't have one yet).
- **Contributor tooling**: editors configured to run black will produce diffs pre-commit reverts; nothing in docs references black directly (they point at pre-commit), so no doc changes are needed.
- **Style stability**: same model as black — the style only changes when the pinned `ruff-pre-commit` rev is deliberately bumped.
- Optional later consolidation: fold isort into ruff's `I` rules (another ~14s and one less hook env) — kept out of scope here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci).
- [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation).
- [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy).
- [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR.
- [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR.

title: [XPU] Qwen3.8-flash-next enablement
author: Xia-Weiwen
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (generic model support merged into `main` via #37500)
introduces several architectural features new to SGLang — a sparse-attention
indexer (QSA), HyperConnection (gated multi-stream residual mixing), a
PLE/N-gram auxiliary embedding, and MTP/NEXTN speculative decoding on top of
a hybrid linear+full attention backbone. This work enables the model
end-to-end on the XPU backend, since the current implementation of these
new features assumes CUDA in several places.

## Plan

Staged enablement:
1. **Functionality ready** (this PR) — model runs E2E on XPU without errors, exercising every new feature at least once, using existing portable (Triton/torch) kernels where a custom SYCL kernel isn't required.
2. **Acceptable performance** (future) — remove the worst algorithmic bottlenecks (unbatched ops, Python-loop fallbacks) without necessarily writing new SYCL kernels.
3. **Peak performance** (future) — write/optimize dedicated SYCL kernels in sgl-kernel-xpu for any remaining hot paths.

This PR covers Stage 1.

## Current Status

Stage 1 (functional E2E correctness) is complete. Per-component implementation status:

| Component | Status | Implementation on XPU |
|---|---|---|
| QSA sparse-attention indexer | Fixed a real OOB gather bug in compressed-KV update (`update_key_state_and_compress`), plus added a `forward_xpu` dispatch | Reuses the existing device-generic Triton/torch fallback path (same code CUDA falls back to when its fast custom kernel isn't applicable); underlying dense attention math uses sgl-kernel-xpu's existing FMHA SYCL kernel |
| HyperConnection (gated residual mixing) | Fixed hardcoded `cuda` device selection | Pure torch-native, no custom kernel needed |
| PLE / N-gram embedding | Works out of the box, no changes needed | Pure torch embedding lookup + all-reduce |
| MTP / NEXTN speculative decoding | Fixed 4 device-portability bugs: hardcoded CUDA device in the Mamba state pool, hardcoded CUDA sync calls, a missing kernel arg in the GDN Triton wrapper, and an int64-overflow bug when packing XPU pointers into scatter-kernel metadata | Uses existing Triton GDN kernel and Triton-based Mamba-state-scatter kernel; no new SYCL kernel required |
| MoE (routed + shared experts) | Verified working | Existing sgl-kernel-xpu `moe_align_block_size` SYCL kernel |
| Vision encoder | Verified working | Existing sgl-kernel-xpu non-paged-prefill FMHA SYCL kernel |

Stage 2 (performance tuning) has not started yet.

Re-verified (all scenarios above, BF16 + FP8, 1×B60 + TP=4) after rebasing
onto `main` on two machines. One new requirement surfaced by the rebase:
QSA's forced `page_size=64` conflicts with the mamba radix-cache's
`no_buffer` strategy, and `extra_buffer` is currently unsupported on XPU
(`supports_mamba_cache_extra_buffer()` hardcodes `False` for XPU regardless
of model) — so `--disable-radix-cache` is required on XPU for this model
until that gap is addressed (tracked in `docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md`).

## Upstream PRs to Track

- **#37500** — "Squash-merge Qwen 3.8 Flash Next integration into main":
  **merged** 2026-09-08. Supersedes #36497 (below); this is now our base.
- ~~#36497~~ — "Introduce Qwen 3.8 Flash Next": **superseded/closed** by
  #37500. Kept here for history only.
- **#36601** — "[AMD] Support Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on ROCm": parallel
  per-vendor enablement PR. Useful reference for how device-specific
  speculative-decoding/graph-replay code is layered on top of the generic
  model support.
- **#36644** — "[Qwen3.8] Fix FP8 KV cache support in QSA": still open; QSA
  correctness fix worth checking once XPU FP8 KV-cache support is tackled.
- **#36651** — "[Qwen3.8] Add PD state transfer for Flash Next": **merged**,
  inherited via the `main` rebase. Adds prefill/decode-disaggregation
  transfer of QSA/PLE recurrent state — out of scope for this PR, but
  required reference for a future XPU PD-disaggregation effort.
- **#38346** — "Fix QSA compress-group OOB gather clamp": **merged**,
  inherited via the `main` rebase. Superseded our own hand-rolled clamp in
  `qsa_indexer.py`; we removed our duplicate and kept upstream's fix.
- **#35051** — "Fix XPU USM pointer overflow via uint64 ptr tables":
  **merged**, inherited via the `main` rebase. Superseded our own
  `_signed_i64()` workaround in `mamba_state_scatter_triton.py`, which we
  removed since it became actively incompatible with upstream's fix.
- **sgl-kernel-xpu #341** — "[MoE] Add Xe2 FP8 W8A16 grouped GEMM support":
  adds a real, Xe2-native FP8 MoE kernel to sgl-kernel-xpu (dispatches FP8
  weights × BF16 activations internally, since Xe2/BMG has no native FP8×FP8
  MMA; reports 1.18x-2.15x speedup vs. the evaluated W8A8 path). This is the
  long-term/performant fix for XPU FP8 MoE, complementary to the Stage-1
  generic-Triton-fallback stopgap already implemented in this branch (see
  `docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md`). **Merged** on 2026-09-04.

### Design precedents (already merged, informational only)

Not dependencies — these are past XPU-enablement PRs for earlier
Qwen-family models, useful as coding-pattern references for Stage 2/3
kernel work (e.g. adding a fused sgl-kernel-xpu kernel, following the same
structure):

- #33354 — fused GDN kernel from sgl-kernel-xpu for Qwen3.5
- #32227
- #35775
- #24390

title: fix: resolve remaining GLM-5.3 rebase regressions
author: Fridge003
body:
## Summary

Follow-up fixes for deterministic CI regressions found after #37235 was merged into #36507:

- honor Helion KDA prefill `beta_is_raw` and cover the raw-beta contract
- make GLM5 hybrid-config detection tolerate minimal and non-GLM fixtures
- update the DSA CP unit test for the generalized DCP LSE helper name
- align adaptive-spec expectations with the current GLM-5.3 defaults
- restore plan-stream handoff initialization and verify-event publication for Frozen-KV MTP

The fused sigmoid-gating split-grid fix originally carried here is now present in the base branch through #37250, so it no longer appears in this PR diff.

## Root causes

- Helion KDA accepted `beta_is_raw` only through `**kwargs`, silently ignoring it.
- `glm5_next_config` assumed every model/config fixture exposed `model_type` and `is_draft_model`.
- Tests retained a private helper name and GLM-5.3 adaptive defaults from before the rebase.
- Plan-stream handoff support initialized its event state only in the regular EAGLE worker. Frozen-KV MTP inherited code that consumed `_pending_verify_handoff_event` without ever creating or publishing it.
- The first raw-beta fixture used a mathematically expansive unnormalized recurrence, which amplified ordinary BF16 differences and produced a false failure. The final fixture keeps the no-QK-L2 path while using contractive keys and deterministic raw beta spanning `[-2, 2]`.

## Validation

No full CI was requested for this PR. Validation used dedicated devboxes and precise `/rerun-test` jobs only; queued reruns were cancelled after equivalent devbox coverage completed.

On H100 RX devboxes:

- `test_kda_helion.py` with Helion 1.4.0: 26 passed
- `test_frozen_kv_mtp.py`: both top-k configurations passed, each with 200 GSM8K samples
- `test_gemma4_mtp_31b_extra.py`: passed the complete real-model Frozen-KV MTP e2e; top-k 1 and 3 both exceeded the 0.75 accuracy threshold
- adaptive-spec, decode-bookkeeping, and SWA KV-pool regression set: 37 tests plus 12 subtests passed
- complete Kimi-K3 prerequisite kernel file: 12 passed
