title: [Feature] DeepEP v2: expanded (do_expand=True) prefill dispatch
author: cyhdmjzzy
body:
## Motivation

DeepEP-V2 (`--moe-a2a-backend deepep_v2`, DeepEP `ElasticBuffer`) already has an expanded, non-masked dispatch branch, but prefill never took it: dispatch bound `use_masked = use_expand_layout = not is_extend`, so prefill always used the non-expanded layout plus SGLang's `ep_scatter` bridge. This PR routes prefill through the expanded layout (`do_expand=True`), where DeepEP's own dispatch copy lays rows out per (token, expert) grouped by expert. That removes `ep_scatter`'s full-hidden copy and its host-to-device count copy on every MoE layer. Decode (expand + masked slab) is unchanged.

## Modifications

- **`token_dispatcher/deepep_v2.py`**: split the layout choice into `use_masked = is_decode` and `use_expand_layout = is_decode or <prefill expand enabled>`, so prefill can expand without becoming masked. Expanded dispatch quantizes the activation scale column-major only under UE8M0; otherwise it stays row-major and the contiguous GEMM TMA-aligns it. Router-weight capacity is checked once for both expanded layouts.
- **`kernels/ops/moe/ep_moe_kernels.py`**: `fill_m_indices_from_psum` labels contiguous-GEMM rows from DeepEP's device-side per-expert prefix sum (each expert's whole aligned segment gets its id; rows past the last segment keep DeepGEMM's `-1` skip sentinel). It replaces `ep_expand_init_m_indices_from_psum`, which is deleted and also assumed a 128-row alignment. `scale_expanded_rows_` is an in-place row scale of an fp32 tensor, with shape and dtype checks.
- **`moe_runner/deep_gemm.py`**: the expanded non-masked pre-permute uses `fill_m_indices_from_psum`. `DeepGemmRunnerInput.hidden_states_scale_tma_aligned` is removed: no caller sets it any more, and DeepEP's UE8M0 scales, the only ones that arrive TMA-aligned, are exactly those `DEEPGEMM_NEED_TMA_ALIGNED_SCALES` already skips. Expanded combine ignores `topk_weights`, so the router weight is applied before combine:
  - without UE8M0 (Hopper), it is folded into the down-proj fp32 input scale. Down-proj is linear and fp8 dequant is `q * scale`, so this is numerically equivalent (not bitwise identical) to weighting the output, and it touches an `[M, I/128]` fp32 tensor instead of the `[M, H]` bf16 output;
  - with UE8M0 (Blackwell) scales are powers of two and cannot absorb the weight, so `post_permute` weights the down-proj output in place with the fp32 weights (one rounding, no fp32 temporary). Casting the weights to bf16 first cost ~1.5 GSM8K points in the measurement below;
  - with `no_combine`, neither runs and raw rows plus 1-D weights are returned for the routewise finalizer.
- **`model_runner.py` + `model_runner_components/moe_ep_setup.py`**: build the ElasticBuffer at the end of `init_cuda_graphs`, so a server whose decode CUDA-graph capture did not already build it does not pay the collective allocation on the first request. The buffer is process-wide and shared by every MoE layer, so the first deepep_v2 dispatcher builds it.
- **`arg_groups/moe_hook.py`**:
  - the prefill budget divides the prefill-buffer ceiling by `tp_size // attn_dp_size`, the number of ranks a per-DP chunk is scattered over before dispatch (under any a2a backend, including pure TP). A model that registers `prefill_dispatch_tokens` still receives the undivided ceiling, as `register_deepep_v2_model` documents, and owns the whole per-rank computation;
  - `--deepep-v2-mode direct` with `nnodes > 1` is rejected at server-args time (direct is NVLink-only); multi-node needs `--deepep-v2-mode hybrid`.
- **`models/mimo_v2.py`, `configs/moe_model_registry.py`, `arg_groups/model_overrides/mimo_v2.py`**: register `MiMoV2ForCausalLM` / `MiMoV2FlashForCausalLM` for deepep_v2. MiMoV2's MoE now selects `forward_deepep` with `is_deepep_class_backend()` (plus Ascend FuseEP) instead of a hand-written backend list that omitted deepep_v2, mori and pplx. On SM100, the FP8 `flashinfer_trtllm` runner pin applies only without an all-to-all backend, as the packed-MXFP4 pin already did, so deepep_v2 resolves the `deep_gemm` runner it requires.
- **`environ.py`**: `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_ENABLE_PREFILL_EXPAND`, unset by default. Unset, prefill expands when the DeepGEMM scales are not UE8M0 (Hopper) and stays non-expanded under UE8M0 (Blackwell), which has not been validated end to end. `1` or `0` forces either layout on any platform.
- **`docs/src/snippets/configs/Qwen/qwen3.8.jsx`**: the GB300 deepep_v2 recipes set `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_EXPAND_PREFILL=1`, which no code reads. The line is dropped; the recipes keep the non-expanded prefill they were verified with, which is also the UE8M0 default.

## Accuracy Tests

MiMoV2, TP16/DP2 over 2 nodes (Hopper, DeepEP 2.0.0), `--disaggregation-mode null` so deepep_v2 drives both prefill and decode; `few_shot_gsm8k`, 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy:

| MoE a2a backend | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---|---|
| `deepep` (V1) | 0.958 | 0.002 |
| `deepep_v2` | 0.964 | 0.002 |

Qwen3-30B-A3B on 8xH200 (Hopper, DeepEP 2.1.0), TP4/EP4, `--moe-a2a-backend deepep_v2 --deepep-v2-mode direct`, `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`, `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=1024`; `few_shot_gsm8k`, 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy. (The cookbook deploys this model at TP1 without EP; EP is required to exercise this path.)

| checkpoint / dispatch | prefill layout | GSM8K runs |
|---|---|---|
| FP8 | non-expanded (`SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_ENABLE_PREFILL_EXPAND=0`) | 0.914, 0.908, 0.911, 0.912 |
| FP8 | expanded, weight folded into the down-proj scale (Hopper default) | 0.900, 0.895, 0.895, 0.903, 0.904 |
| FP8 | expanded, fold forced off, fp32 output weighting (the UE8M0 branch) | 0.895, 0.904 |
| FP8 | expanded, fold forced off, weights cast to bf16 before the multiply (for comparison) | 0.879, 0.884 |
| BF16 | non-expanded | 0.906 |
| BF16 | expanded | 0.911 |
| FP8 | TP1, no EP (cookbook) | 0.866 |
| BF16 | TP4, no a2a | 0.911 |

HellaSwag on the same setup (all 10,042 validation questions, 20-shot, choices scored by log-probability, so every question is pure prefill through the path this PR changes):

| checkpoint / dispatch | prefill layout | HellaSwag runs |
|---|---|---|
| FP8 | non-expanded | 0.761, 0.761, 0.762 |
| FP8 | expanded (Hopper default) | 0.762, 0.763, 0.763 |

On GSM8K the expanded FP8 layout lands ~1.2 points lower across repeated runs; on HellaSwag it is level with (marginally above) the non-expanded layout. An op-level check on the same hardware (real ElasticBuffer, dispatch, pre/post permute, DeepGEMM contiguous FP8 GEMM and combine; random block-FP8 experts at this model's shapes) finds both layouts equally close to an fp32 dense reference (median per-token relative error 2.34e-2 each) and 3.8e-3 apart. The GSM8K shift is read as greedy long-form generation amplifying a rounding-order difference, not a loss of accuracy; for scale, the cookbook TP1 FP8 deployment scores 0.866 on the same GSM8K setup.

Not validated here: Blackwell (UE8M0) end to end, so expanded prefill is off there unless `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_ENABLE_PREFILL_EXPAND=1`.

## Speed Tests

End-to-end prefill throughput, MiMoV2, TP8/EP16/DP2 over 2 nodes (Hopper), 32k chunk per DP, `bench_serving` input-token throughput (tok/s). The last two columns are this PR's expanded layout (with the scale fold) and its gain over V1.

| request len (k) | requests | `deepep` V1 | `deepep_v2` non-expanded | Δ vs V1 | `deepep_v2` expanded | Δ vs V1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8   | 512 | 25255.66 | 27028.59 | +7.0% | 29106.99 | +15.2% |
| 16  | 512 | 25313.40 | 27189.06 | +7.4% | 28690.07 | +13.3% |
| 32  | 256 | 24334.59 | 26097.61 | +7.2% | 27480.15 | +12.9% |
| 64  | 256 | 22680.25 | 24432.20 | +7.7% | 25692.17 | +13.3% |
| 128 | 128 | 20537.96 | 21686.12 | +5.6% | 22272.49 |  +8.4% |
| 256 |  64 | 16922.24 | 17753.09 | +4.9% | 18226.55 |  +7.7% |
| 512 |  24 | 12291.39 | 12766.78 | +3.9% | 13027.60 |  +6.0% |
| 768 |  16 |  9707.58 | 10036.62 | +3.4% | 10121.12 |  +4.3% |
| 960 |   8 |  8175.53 |  8345.79 | +2.1% |  8585.99 |  +5.0% |

Over the non-expanded deepep_v2 path the expanded layout gains +2% to +8%, from removing `ep_scatter`'s full-hidden copy and host-to-device count copy, and from weighting the `[M, I/128]` fp32 down-proj scale instead of the `[M, H]` bf16 output (~112 µs to ~4 µs per layer at these shapes; Hopper only, since UE8M0 cannot take the fold).

## Environment notes

- DeepEP `ElasticBuffer` (2.0.0 or 2.1.0). `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` is required and is set automatically.
- Single node runs `--deepep-v2-mode direct` (NVLink); multi-node needs `--deepep-v2-mode hybrid`.
- `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` must cover the per-rank prefill budget (the prefill-buffer ceiling divided by `tp_size // attn_dp_size`); startup validation reports the required value.

title: fix: initialize Inkling safely on ROCm
author: guapisolo
body:
## Summary

Load Inkling on ROCm without CUTE and read pure-SWA value dimensions safely.

## Symptom & Reproduction

- **Symptom:** [Miles MI350 job `99118506030`](https://github.com/radixark/miles/actions/runs/33259345919/job/99118506030) failed at Miles revision `721c020bc3cde81b07ee6189d2f571f440ff1824`: missing `cutlass` prevented Inkling registration, followed by a misleading Transformers/`auto_map` error.
- **Reproduction:** `python3 /__w/miles/miles/tests/e2e/megatron/model_scripts/test_inkling_small_4layer_ci.py` failed before the SGLang engine became healthy. Pure-SWA initialization also failed when querying the value dimension of an empty full-attention pool.

## Root Cause

1. `inkling_common.attn` imported the CUTE-only `is_batch_invariant` helper during model discovery.
2. `ModelRegistry.register` skipped Inkling when the import failed without `cutlass`.
3. `SWAKVPool.get_v_head_dim` indexed a nonexistent value buffer when the full-attention pool had zero layers.

## Fix

Move the batch-invariance helper into the existing optional CUTE import block and guard its use when unavailable. The CUTE path retains its existing behavior. Delegate the value dimension query to `full_kv_pool.get_v_head_dim()`, which reads construction-time metadata even when no full-attention buffer exists.

## Verification

Rebased both commits onto `sglang-miles` at `e5bba1f9c433da5352e521a8bb826bab960e7836`. The following checks passed on candidate `2264a736cfaf43eb54c569cabfc40392d4e7f807`:

- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_swa_pool_v_head_dim.py`: the existing CPU test passed.
- A standalone CPU probe using real `SWAKVPool` instances passed for zero full-attention layers, interleaved full/SWA layers, and a nonzero pipeline start layer. Each returned the full-attention value dimension of 16 while the SWA dimension was 24.
- `python -m py_compile` for both changed files and `git diff --check`: passed.

GPU/ROCm inference and full CI have not been rerun on this rebased candidate; the earlier MI350 result applies to the original head only.

## Review Focus

- Optional CUTE absence must allow the ROCm Triton path to register Inkling.
- `SWAKVPool.get_v_head_dim` must report the full-attention dimension without reading a buffer, including empty pools and pipeline stages.

## Summary

- Preserve the original request-slot capacity before building customizable ragged verification token buckets.
- Size attention CUDA graph token buffers from the token buckets that are actually captured.
- Keep existing non-ragged and default ragged behavior unchanged.

## Motivation

Ragged target verification has two independent capacities: the maximum number of request slots accepted by a graph and the maximum number of packed token rows represented by captured graph keys. Custom runners may prune the packed-token bucket grid while retaining the full request capacity. Coupling both capacities through `max_bs * captured_req_width` overallocates token-row buffers, while deriving `max_bs` after bucket customization can incorrectly reduce request admission capacity.

The default ragged bucket builder still produces `bs * captured_req_width` for every capture batch size, so this change is behavior-preserving for existing runners. Non-ragged decode continues to use the original expression.

## Tests

```text
python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_decode_cuda_graph_runner.py
12 passed
```

Pre-commit hooks passed for the changed file.

title: Disable Hopper GLM shared-expert fusion for modelopt_fp4 Marlin
author: nvpohanh
body:
## Summary

- disable shared-expert fusion by default for `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` when using `modelopt_fp4` with the Marlin MoE backend on Hopper GPUs
- keep `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` as an explicit override
- add unit coverage for the new Hopper gate and the explicit override path

## Repro

Issue: #37268

I updated local `sglang` to `origin/main` (`079afaffb19abbe42c09f0ebb8322d6e9f6f2905`) and reproduced the problematic Hopper path on Tuesday, September 1, 2026 on AIHub H100s with the GLM-5.3 NVFP4 recipe reported in the issue:

```bash
SGLANG_FORCE_NVFP4_MARLIN=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path incoai/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 \
  --tp 8 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --fp4-gemm-backend marlin \
  --moe-runner-backend marlin
```

and then enters the failing shared-expert fused path on Hopper for this quantization/backend combination. The issue reporter also confirmed `--disable-shared-experts-fusion` as a workaround.

The narrower kernel-level support path would require larger Marlin/shared-expert fusion work. This change applies the known-safe workaround automatically for the affected Hopper GLM + `modelopt_fp4` + Marlin combination, while preserving the force flag for explicit testing.

title: Fix nondeterministic FlashInfer GDN alignment test
author: nvpohanh
body:
[by Codex]

## Summary

- initialize the misaligned `a` and `b` test views with deterministic finite values
- keep their values distinct so the test still verifies that both FlashInfer arguments are copied independently and without corruption
- avoid comparing allocator-provided `torch.empty` contents, which can contain NaNs and make `assert_close` fail nondeterministically

## What failure does this fix?

This fixes the `base-a-test-cpu` failure observed while testing [#33922](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33922):

- CI job: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33459311788/job/99706092418
- test: `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_gdn_flashinfer_alignment.py`
- test case: `TestFlashInferGDNAlignment::test_decode_repairs_read_only_arguments_before_flashinfer`
- CI signature: `torch.testing.assert_close(captured["a"], a)` reported 2/8 mismatched elements with a greatest absolute difference of `nan`

The same test failed standalone on latest `main` in `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` on a computelab node. In that run, `captured["b"]` reported 8/8 mismatched elements with a greatest absolute difference of `nan`. Which tensor/elements fail depends on the contents returned by the allocator, but both failures have the same root cause.

### Additional confirmed CI occurrences

I scanned 600 failed `PR Test Base` workflow runs after #35758 introduced this test and inspected the logs of their failed `base-a-test-cpu` root jobs. The exact failure was confirmed in three pipeline runs across two unrelated PRs:

- [Run 33353343812 / job 99370860899](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33353343812/job/99370860899) — PR #37179, 2026-08-31 03:16 UTC
- [Run 33459311788 / job 99706092418](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33459311788/job/99706092418) — PR #33922, 2026-09-01 01:35 UTC
- [Run 33460931970 / job 99710903533](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33460931970/job/99710903533) — PR #37179, 2026-09-01 02:00 UTC

All three failed in `TestFlashInferGDNAlignment::test_decode_repairs_read_only_arguments_before_flashinfer` with the same signature: 2/8 mismatched elements and a `nan` difference at index `(0, 0, 2)`. The recurrence across unrelated PRs and separate workflow runs supports that this is an intermittent main-branch test defect rather than a regression caused by any one target PR.

## Root cause

`_view_with_pointer_mod()` intentionally builds misaligned views from `torch.empty` backing storage. In this test, `a` and `b` were never initialized before `kernel.decode()`:

```python
a = _view_with_pointer_mod((1, 1, 8), torch.bfloat16, 16)
b = _view_with_pointer_mod((1, 1, 8), torch.bfloat16, 16)
```

The alignment-repair path correctly copies these views into aligned scratch buffers. The test then compares the copied tensors against the original uninitialized tensors with `torch.testing.assert_close`. If the allocator-provided bit patterns contain NaNs, the comparison fails because `assert_close` does not consider corresponding NaNs equal by default.

Therefore:

- the failure is **intermittent in manifestation**, because it depends on allocator reuse and the uninitialized bit patterns;
- it is **not an infrastructure-only flake**—there is a concrete test-code defect;
- it is **not caused by #33922**; the exact test also reproduces on latest `main` without that PR;
- the defective test was introduced by [#35758](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35758) (`qwen 3.8 rebase`), merge commit `5f216fc33f315ade378bc7cd295ee88f5322d4d3`, which added this test file and the uninitialized setup.

## Fix

Initialize `a` and `b` with distinct finite sequences before calling `decode()`. This removes allocator-dependent NaNs while preserving the test's intended coverage:

- both source views remain deliberately 16-byte-offset/misaligned;
- the test still verifies 32-byte alignment at the FlashInfer call boundary;
- distinct values ensure the two live argument buffers cannot be accidentally aliased or swapped;
- the final `assert_close` checks still verify lossless copy behavior.

## Validation

After rebasing onto `60f881b40c`:

- exact failing pytest node: passed
- full `test_gdn_flashinfer_alignment.py`: 10 passed
- 500 allocator-poison stress iterations: passed
- `BLACK_NUM_WORKERS=1 SKIP=no-commit-to-branch pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure`: passed

title: [AMD] Enable FP4 indexer for Deepseek V4
author: RolaoDenthu
body: Co-authored-by: @AMD-yanfeiwang @1am9trash This PR is originally based on the work of @AMD-yanfeiwang. - Original FP4 indexer enablement on ROCm gfx950 and the early integration work are from [#36581](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36581). - We also rely on the AITER fix from @AMD-yanfeiwang. - [aiter#5034](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5034): Merged. Cherry-pick at [#37083](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37083). - [aiter#5126](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5126): Not merged. Apply change in this PR. ## Motivation Enable the DeepSeek V4 FP4 indexer on gfx95x GPUs through AITER. AITER’s FP4 paged-MQA kernels use a different K-cache layout from the existing fused SGLang path. The 64-byte FP4 payload and 4-byte UE8M0 scale for each compressed token are stored in separate preshuffled tensors: - payload: `[num_pages, 1, 4, 64, 16]` - scale: `[num_pages, 1, 4, 64]` Supporting this layout requires more than switching the kernel dispatch. This PR adds the corresponding device-pool representation, routes the Q/K RoPE, Hadamard rotation, FP4 quantization, cache writes, and paged-MQA logits through AITER, and introduces reusable scheduling metadata for prefill, decode, and EAGLE MTP. The cache sizing is updated to reflect the 68-byte FP4 indexer entry. HiCache is also made aware of the split representation by mirroring the payload and scale as separate page-level regions, ensuring that host backup and restore preserve AITER’s physical layout. ## Modifications ### ROCm dependency - `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` - Patch fix [aiter#5126](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5126). ### FP4 kernel adapters - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/fp4_indexer_hip.py` - Add the gfx95 AITER adapter for Q RoPE/Hadamard/FP4 quantization. - Add guarded page-table construction and decode/prefill schedule workspaces. - Dispatch decode and prefill FP4 paged-MQA logits. - Build per-forward K write positions and cache slots. - Dispatch fused RMSNorm, RoPE, Hadamard, FP4 quantization, and paged cache writes. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/compress.py` - Route HIP FP4 indexer cache writes through the AITER fused writer. - Pass the separate payload/scale buffers, precomputed RoPE tables, and prebuilt write metadata. ### Attention runtime - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py` - Select the AITER FP4 path on HIP while preserving the existing CUDA/DeepGEMM and FP8 paths. - Quantize indexer Q through AITER. - Read the split K payload/scale cache with AITER paged-MQA kernels. - Reuse per-forward decode and prefill workspaces. - Keep padded FP4 query rows at zero context length. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py` - Attach FP4 decode/prefill workspaces, K write metadata, and widened Q positions to DSV4 metadata. - Size target-verification metadata for draft tokens crossing a page boundary. - Derive sequence lengths and output cache locations independently for every EAGLE draft step. - Build decode schedules during graph capture while keeping prefill schedule construction outside capture. - Reuse page tables and schedules across all C4 layers in a forward pass. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/compressor.py` - Maintain a BF16 mirror of the indexer RMSNorm weight required by the AITER K writer. - Refresh the mirror through the normal weight-loader path. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/compressor_v2.py` - Emit BF16 compressed indexer K directly on HIP. - Select the split FP4 payload/scale cache. - Forward cached RoPE tables and per-forward write metadata to the fused writer. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/metadata.py` - Skip unnecessary DeepGEMM metadata construction for HIP indexer backends. - `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py` - Reuse the model-owned BF16 RoPE cos/sin cache for FP4 Q and K transforms. - Refresh the indexer’s RoPE references after module `_apply` operations. - `python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/serving_hook.py` - Allow `--enable-deepseek-v4-fp4-indexer` on supported gfx95 GPUs. ### Device memory and sizing - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py` - Share the FP8/FP4 indexer bytes-per-token calculation. - Allocate AITER FP4 K payload and UE8M0 scale buffers separately. - Add payload/scale accessors for the attention and compressor paths. - Expose page-row views for cache transfer paths. - `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/pool_configurator.py` - Account for the FP4 indexer’s 68-byte compressed-token footprint instead of the FP8 132-byte footprint. ### HiCache integration - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py` - Add a dedicated pool identifier for the FP4 indexer scale region. - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py` - Resolve fused FP8 and split FP4 indexer layouts into page-contiguous regions. - Build separate host pools for FP4 payload and scale data. - Register the scale region as a KV-derived HiCache sidecar. - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/linker_pool_assembler.py` - Export each FP4 indexer region through the direct external-linker device-pool group. - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool_host.py` - Mark grouped FP4 indexer rows as whole-page-only transfers. - Reject unsupported token-granular payload/scale transfers instead of copying with the fused-layout kernel. - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py` - Register Mooncake component keys for the FP4 indexer scale pool. ### Tests - `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_fp4_indexer_hip.py` - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mem_pool_host.py` ## Accuracy Tests - sglang gsm8k 1319: 0.948 - inferenceX lm-eval: ``` |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9674|± |0.0049| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9682|± |0.0048| ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Fixed length benchmark: - input length: 68k - output length: 200 InferenceX Agentic: - conc=48, using hicache | Metric | Baseline (SA curve) | FP4 indexer | Delta | |---|---|---|---| | Throughput / GPU | 20,251 tok/s | 21,430 tok/s | +5.8% | | TTFT (median) | 887 ms | 838 ms | -5.5% | | GPU KV cache capacity | 10,221,824 tokens | 11,006,208 tokens | +7.7% | | GPU cache hit rate | 91.3% | 93.0% | +1.7% | | CPU cache hit rate | 5.3% | 3.8% | -1.5% | - title: [Perf] [AMD] moe: Resolve MoRI dispatch from the AITER activation contract
author: Duyi-Wang
body:
MoRI's auto dispatch picks the wire format from the expert weight dtype alone,
which does not say what the receiving kernel consumes. MXFP4 weights run a16w4,
a8w4 or a4w4 depending on the activation, gate mode, arch and token count; and
fp8 activations have two formats that share a payload but not a scale layout.

Ask AITER instead, through `resolve_activation_dtype()` (ROCm/aiter#5221), and
pass the quant type alongside the weight dtype so those two stay apart.
AITER owns the kernel dtype decision; an AITER without that API dispatches bf16
and warns.

| quant type | AITER consumes | dispatch | scales |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| per_1x128 | fp8 | fp8 | fp32 per 128 |
| per_1x32 | fp8 | **mxfp8** | e8m0 per 32 |
| per_1x32 | fp4x2 | fp4 | e8m0 per 32 |
| anything else, or an answer that depends on M | — | bf16 | — |

`per_Token` lands in the last row on purpose: MoRI has no per-token fp8 format.

On DeepSeek-V4-Pro the MoE is a8w4. Selecting mxfp8 dispatch matches the
activation format consumed by AITER and avoids an unnecessary
`upscale_mxfp4` plus re-quantization on the receive side.

The selection applies to the shared MoRI EPv1/EPv2 dispatcher and follows the
layer's activation and gate layout. Execution-kernel
`DISPATCHER_QUANT_CONFIG` overrides, explicit dispatch overrides, and the
existing combine selection are preserved.

## Why the answer is so often bf16

A dispatch format is fixed when the all-to-all buffers are sized — before any
token exists — while AITER's answer may depend on M. So M is not passed, and
AITER returns None wherever it would have been needed.

The two directions are not symmetric. Sending bf16 when AITER wanted fp8 costs
a quantize on the receive side. Sending a quantized format when the kernel
expects bf16 can cause a kernel-dispatch failure or incorrect output.
Unknown or batch-dependent answers therefore fall back to bf16.

`AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND` is a common reason M matters. For the interleaved
SwiGLU path, its default of 256 allows bf16 activations for small batches,
so auto must fall back to bf16. Setting it to 0 pins fp8 for every M and allows
mxfp8 dispatch. That fallback warns and names the variable; fallbacks that
follow from the hardware stay at info.

MXFP8 dispatch also requires AITER to both emit group-32 e8m0 scales and consume
them through the receive-side passthrough. If either capability is missing,
auto falls back to bf16.

## Validation

Validated on **8× MI355X** with
`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi35x-20261028` and AITER
`285579b6211b0da30f35b91a890c29c823597cd1`:

- Full local pre-commit checks passed.
- AITER MXFP8 passthrough numerical tests: **3 passed**.
- Eight-rank MoRI EPv2 identity round trips with **automatic bf16, fp8, fp4,
  and mxfp8** selection: all passed
  (64 tokens/rank, hidden size 7168, top-k 6).
- SGLang AITER runner at **1, 8, and 112 tokens**: automatic mxfp8 output was
  **bit-identical** to bf16 input followed by internal quantization.
  The batch-dependent bf16 fallback was also exercised.
- Missing resolution API, missing MXFP8 receive capability, absent numerics,
  and separated-gate fallback checks passed.
- **DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, TP8 / DP8 attention / EP8 / MoRI EPv2**:
  all ranks automatically selected mxfp8; startup and decode CUDA graph
  capture succeeded. **17 completion requests**, including eight-way
  concurrency, returned the expected leading arithmetic answer and completed
  32 generated tokens each.

The model requests validate serving functionality; they are not a full
accuracy or performance benchmark.

## Related

- #36119 introduced `DispatchDtype.mxfp8` and the receive-side handling.
- ROCm/aiter#4954 provides the MXFP8 receive-side passthrough.
- ROCm/aiter#5221 exposes `resolve_activation_dtype()`.

title: [kernel] add fused silu mul quant fp8
author: xieminghe1
body: ## Motivation Reduce MoE launch and memory-traffic overhead by fusing `silu_and_mul` and `per_token_group_quant_fp8`. The fused Triton kernel computes the gated activation, derives per-token-group FP8 scales, and writes the FP8 down-projection input in one pass. > The no-flag auto-dispatch update is in [xieminghe1/sglang#1](https://github.com/xieminghe1/sglang/pull/1). The original PR head has **Allow edits from maintainers** disabled, so it must be merged by the fork owner before this PR updates. ## Changes - Add `fused_silu_mul_quant_fp8` and its H200 benchmark. - Feed the fused FP8 tensor and generated activation scales directly into the down MoE GEMM. - Preserve the DeepSeek-V4 `swiglu_limit` clamp inside the fused kernel. - Automatically dispatch to the fusion from the Triton MoE path. No environment variable or new server argument is introduced. - Add standalone kernel coverage, dispatch-condition coverage, and an end-to-end fused-vs-fallback MoE comparison. ## Automatic dispatch The fast path is selected only when all of the following are true: - NVIDIA CUDA; BF16 or FP16 activation. - Blockwise FP8 W8A8 MoE with a valid positive K-group size that evenly divides the post-SwiGLU width. - Standard gated SiLU, with no `gemm1_alpha` or `gemm1_limit` modifier. - No expert filtering, LoRA hooks, or interleaved SwiGLU GEMM epilogue. `swiglu_limit` is supported for DeepSeek-V4. Every incompatible case keeps the existing activation + quantization fallback. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Gate-up MoE GEMM] --> B{CUDA blockwise FP8\nand all contracts match?} B -->|yes| C[Fused SiLU × up + group FP8 quant] B -->|no| D[Existing activation path] D --> E[Existing per-token-group quant] C --> F[Down MoE GEMM with fused scales] E --> F ``` ## Validation H200 (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4`): ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python test/registered/unit/test_legacy_global_ratchet.py CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4 PYTHONPATH=python \ pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_fused_silu_mul_quant_fp8.py pre-commit run --files \ python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py \ python/sglang/srt/server_args.py \ test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_fused_silu_mul_quant_fp8.py ``` Results: - CPU legacy-global ratchet: passed (`1 test`). - H200 kernel and dispatch suite: passed (`32 tests`). - End-to-end synthetic blockwise-FP8 MoE: the automatic path invoked the fused kernel and matched the forced fallback within FP8 tolerance. - Pre-commit on changed files: passed. ## Accuracy results DeepSeek-V4: ## Performance results H200 activation-boundary benchmark: End-to-end baseline: End-to-end fused path (captured on the earlier opt-in revision; after the follow-up merges, the same path is selected automatically with no extra flag): Comparison: ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add registered unit/kernel tests. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed evidence. - [x] Preserve unsupported-path fallbacks and DeepSeek-V4 clamp semantics. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #34007782658](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34007782658) Latest PR Test (Extra): :no_entry_sign: [Run #34007782493](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34007782493) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :x: [Run #34007782660](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34007782660)

title: fix(modelopt_fp4): skip NVFP4 swiglu-fusion interleave for shared experts with swiglu_limit
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Symptom

Serving an NVFP4 (`modelopt_fp4`) checkpoint of a clamped-swiglu MoE model (GLM-5 family, `swiglu_limit=10.0`) with expert parallelism (`--ep-size 4`) crashes on the first real forward pass, on every rank:

```
deepseek_v2.py _forward_shared_experts → DeepseekV2MLP.forward
  gate_up, _ = self.gate_up_proj(x)
→ linear.py quant_method.apply
→ modelopt_quant.py ModelOptFp4LinearMethod.apply
    w_n, _ = layer.weight.shape
ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)
```

TP-only (same flags minus `--ep-size`) is unaffected.

## Root cause

`DeepseekV2MoE.__init__` gates the shared-expert NVFP4 swiglu-fusion weight interleave on SM100 + `fc1_n % 128 == 0` (`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py`, the `_interleave_for_swiglu_fusion` block), but `DeepseekV2MLP.forward` only takes the fused path when `self.swiglu_limit is None`:

```python
if (
    getattr(self, "_enable_nvfp4_gemm_swiglu_fusion", False)
    and self.swiglu_limit is None
    and not isinstance(x, tuple)
):
```

For a clamped-swiglu model (`swiglu_limit=10.0`) with a *separate* shared-experts MLP, the two gates disagree: `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading` sees `_interleave_for_swiglu_fusion`, builds the interleaved weight, and frees `layer.weight` (`torch.empty(0)` — 1-D), while forward falls back to the unfused `apply`, which unpacks the now-1-D `layer.weight.shape` and crashes.

Under TP-only this path is never exercised because shared-experts fusion folds the shared expert into the FusedMoE (`num_fused_shared_experts=1`, no separate `shared_experts` module). With `moe_ep_size > 1`, `shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason` disables that fusion ("Shared experts fusion is not supported together with expert parallelism yet."), the separate shared-experts MLP is built, and the mismatched gate fires.

Note on serve logs with NEXTN enabled: you will see *both* "Shared experts fusion optimization enabled." and "Config does not support fused shared expert(s). ... disabled." in the same TP-only log. These come from two different model builds with two different gates:

- The **target** model gate (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration.shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason`) has no `n_routed_experts` allowlist: TP-only -> fusion enabled (first message, no separate MLP is ever constructed; the spec-off TP-only log shows *only* this message), EP -> vetoed by `moe_ep_size > 1` (separate MLP built -> this bug).
- The **NextN draft** model (`Glm5NextForConditionalGenerationNextN` -> `DeepseekV3ForCausalLMNextN`) uses the `DeepseekV2` gate, whose allowlist (`n_routed_experts in (256, 384)`) rejects 288-expert configs (second message). The draft does build a separate shared-experts MLP, but `deepseek_nextn.py` forces `quant_config=None` for `modelopt_fp4` drafts, so that MLP is unquantized BF16 (`UnquantizedLinearMethod`) and the NVFP4 interleave machinery is never involved. Verified with an init-time probe on the TP-only NEXTN serve: the only separate shared-experts instance is the draft's, with `qm=UnquantizedLinearMethod`, `interleave=False`.

So on a stock TP-only serve of this checkpoint there is no NVFP4 shared-experts MLP instance at all; the bug is specific to the EP target-model path.

## Fix

Add the missing `swiglu_limit is None` condition to the init-time interleave gate so it exactly matches the forward-time condition: no interleave → weight stays 2-D → unfused apply works (with the swiglu clamp applied in `DeepseekV2MLP.forward` as before).

## Verification

Hardware: 4x NVIDIA B300 (SM103), checkpoint GLM-5.3-Flash class NVFP4 (`modelopt_fp4`, `moe_intermediate_size=2048`, `n_shared_experts=1`, `swiglu_limit=10.0`), flags: `--quantization modelopt_fp4 --dsa-prefill-backend trtllm --dsa-decode-backend trtllm --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass --tp-size 4`.

| Config | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| EP (`--ep-size 4`), spec off | crash on first chat (all schedulers die) | healthy; smoke chat `content='42'`, `finish_reason=stop`; bench isl1024/osl256 c16 n80: **787.13 tok/s**, 80/80 ok |
| EP + NEXTN 5/1/6 spec | crash during server-init forward | healthy; bench c16 n80: **1053.91 tok/s**, 80/80 ok |
| TP-only, spec off (regression) | works | still works: healthy, smoke `'42'` / `stop` (unchanged code path — shared experts fused into MoE) |

TP-only reference numbers from the same box/ckpt (pre-fix): spec-off c16 n80 = 863.82 tok/s; NEXTN c16 n80 = 1139.83 tok/s.

title: [Unified Cache][5/N]: Integrate external linker mode end to end
author: hzh0425
body:
## Motivation

Motivation
Unified Radix Cache manages heterogeneous model states, including full-attention KV, SWA KV, and model-specific sidecars.

On GB platforms, deployments may need to aggregate larger memory regions into a shared Global Memory pool. This requires an efficient way for Unified Radix Cache to access remote memory directly without overhead on the inference critical path.

This PR adds an optional external-cache linker mode. It allows the tree to access a Global Memory pool through backends such as Mooncake or UMBP .. while retaining ownership of allocation, insertion, component consistency, and cache-node lifetime.

The existing hierarchical cache path remains unchanged. The linker is an opt-in alternative for deployments that need a larger shared memory pool while preserving inference performance.

This is the fifth PR split from https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35687. It completes the Mooncake external-linker path.

Previous splits: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37091, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37098, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37151, and https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37205.

## Modifications

- Wire external-linker arguments, registry, scheduler lifecycle, and cache-pool configuration.
- Add GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4 Mooncake direct load-back KL E2E tests.

## Tests

- GLM-5.2-FP8: 5 tests passed with 2 skipped; max average KL 0.006497 under 0.03.

title: [Cookbook] Add the DFlash2 speculative option to GLM-5.3
author: zijiexia
body:
## Motivation

The GLM-5.3 Playground's **Speculative** card only exposes the in-checkpoint MTP head (EAGLE 5-1-6 / 1-1-2) and "off". [`incoai/GLM-5.3-DFlash2`](https://huggingface.co/incoai/GLM-5.3-DFlash2) is a trained block-diffusion drafter for `zai-org/GLM-5.3`, but its draft lives in a separate checkpoint, so no Deploy cell can ship it — it only makes sense as a Playground chip. GLM-5.3-Flash already got the same treatment; this brings GLM-5.3 to parity.

## Modifications

- `docs/src/snippets/configs/zai-org/glm-5.3.jsx` — a `dflash` option on the Speculative card emitting:
  ```
  --speculative-algorithm DFLASH
  --speculative-draft-model-path incoai/GLM-5.3-DFlash2
  --speculative-draft-attention-backend fa4
  ```
  No `--speculative-num-draft-tokens`: the block size comes from the draft checkpoint's own `dflash_config`. Two disable rules, both matching `_handle_dflash` in `python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/speculative_hook.py`: DP-Attention on (rejected at startup) and ROCm (DFLASH is CUDA/NPU only). A `note` flags that the DFlash2 drafter (#35371) merged **after v0.5.18**, so neither the release wheel nor the `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` image this page pins carries it.
- `docs/cookbook/autoregressive/GLM/GLM-5.3.mdx` — a Configuration Tips entry covering the same ground plus the draft's CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 research/evaluation license.

Docs only — no runtime code touched. Unlike GLM-5.3-Flash (which needed #36708), GLM-5.3 needs no engine change: `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` inherits `set_dflash_layers_to_capture` from `DeepseekV2ForCausalLM` on `main`.

## Accuracy Tests

Verified end-to-end on **8×B200** (`b200-masscompute`, sglang `0.0.0.dev1+g07c8f7294`) with the exact command the chip generates:

```
sglang serve --model-path zai-org/GLM-5.3 --tp-size 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --speculative-algorithm DFLASH \
  --speculative-draft-model-path incoai/GLM-5.3-DFlash2 \
  --speculative-draft-attention-backend fa4
```

- Server reaches ready in ~7 min (`load_weight=187.8 s`, `scheduler_e2e=397.8 s`); 163.7 / 183 GB per GPU.
- `/get_server_info` confirms `speculative_algorithm: DFLASH`, **`speculative_num_draft_tokens: 8`** — the block size is auto-inferred from the draft config, so the chip is right to omit the flag — and `speculative_draft_attention_backend: fa4`. Target stays on `attention_backend: dsa` with `kv_cache_dtype: fp8_e4m3`.
- **GSM8K (sgl-eval, `--num-threads 32`): 97.34%** on 1318/1319 questions.

One caveat on that last figure: question 1319 drove the model into a degenerate repetition loop and, because `sgl-eval run gsm8k` sends no `max_tokens`, it ran to 235,264 generated tokens before being aborted. The score is therefore over 1318/1319, not the full set. This is a property of the existing cookbook GSM8K command rather than anything DFLASH introduces (the same runaway was seen previously on GLM-5.3-Flash), so it is left out of scope here.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked — this PR deliberately does not claim performance numbers. The page cites the vendor's own 4×GB300 figures and marks the recipe as a starting point.

Observed accept length during the GSM8K run was **6.19–7.97** under greedy decoding (excluding the 580 decode batches at a saturated 8.00 that belong to the runaway above), directionally consistent with the vendor's reported 5.94 on GSM8K at temperature 1.0.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).

- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — accuracy above; speed intentionally not claimed.

title: [AMD][DSV4] feat: enable fp8 two-pool unified_kv on gfx950
author: amd-danli103
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->
## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
Under `unified_kv`, DSv4 keeps KV in bf16 across the full latent — `qk_nope_head_dim` 448 plus `qk_rope_head_dim` 64, **1024 B per token per layer**. The nope half actually does not need that precision. Storing nope as fp8 with per-tile E8M0 scales while leaving rope in bf16 cuts the row to **640 B** (512 B of fp8 nope at a fixed stride, plus the same 128 B of bf16 rope), which measures out at **1.51× the KV capacity at identical memory** on gfx950. At fixed HBM more tokens stay resident, so longer contexts and higher concurrency fit on the same node.

Off by default behind `SGLANG_DSV4_UNIFIED_KV_FP8`; it requires gfx950 and implies `is_unified_kv_triton()`. Other architectures warn and fall back to bf16, so nothing on the existing path changes.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
Two pools instead of one, then every writer and reader of the pool:
- **layout / sizing** — nope is a 512 B fp8 row (448 values + inline e8m0 scales, padded so the stride stays a power of two); rope stays 128 B of bf16. PD disaggregation and HiCache offload are refused for now because both assume one pool per layer.
- **writers** — SWA scatter, fused QK norm+RoPE store, compressor norm+rope store, and the packed ring store used by prefill and target-verify.
- **readers** — decode through aiter's `mla_a8w8` v4 nm asm kernel; prefill through aiter's opus kernel.
- **decode overhead** — drop a `masked_fill_` on empty segments the builders cannot produce, cache `qo_indptr` (it only depends on the token count), skip a `kv.contiguous()` the group-quant kernel does not need (it already takes the row stride), and cap `num_kv_splits` to 4 above 40 tokens where aiter's occupancy heuristic over-splits.

Everything stays behind `SGLANG_DSV4_UNIFIED_KV_FP8` (default off) plus the gfx95 gate. The DSv4 unified_kv path is ROCm-only; the only common-code touch is one new `elif` in the JIT norm+rope-store template, existing branches unchanged.

## What this buys: KV capacity

Four configurations, each a pair of servers with byte-identical CLI differing only in the env switch. Taken on this rebase (`ec07b65ed6 `):

| config | `available_bytes` | bf16 `full_token` | fp8 `full_token` | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8 | 135.59 GB | 16,126,208 | 24,223,744 | **1.5021×** |
| TP8 + MTP | 132.97 GB | 15,417,344 | 23,161,088 | **1.5023×** |
| TP8 + DP8 | 119.85 GB | 14,399,488 | 21,605,120 | **1.5004×** |
| TP8 + DP8 + MTP | 115.35 GB | 13,612,288 | 20,424,448 | **1.5004×** |

`available_bytes` matches exactly within every pair, which it has to — otherwise a weight-footprint difference would land in the ratio. `bytes_per_full_token` goes 8918.00 → 5945.00 in the no-MTP cells and 9064.20 → 6042.46 in the MTP cells: **0.6666× in all four**, not the row's 0.625, because the indexer term in `_get_bytes_per_full_token` does not scale with the KV row width — it was already fp8 with its own scales.
A fifth pair at a different `mem-fraction` on the previous stack gave 14,211,840 → 21,451,520 (**1.5094×**), so the ratio is not an artefact of one memory setting.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->
GSM8K, all 1319 questions, paired runs differing only in the fp8 switch, all four cells on this rebase, on top of #37140's rebuilt AOT. Prefix caching on. No regression observed.

| DP | MTP | fp8 | bf16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| off | off | 0.949 | 0.940 |
| off | EAGLE | 0.948 | 0.945 |
| 8 | off | 0.947 | 0.952 |
| 8 | EAGLE | 0.946 | 0.947 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->
Same machine, MI355X, radix cache off. The first four tables are TP=8; the last is DP=8 + dp-attention. Two servers, byte-identical CLI within each table, differing only in `SGLANG_DSV4_UNIFIED_KV_FP8`. 
`ttt ratio` is fp8 ttt / bf16 ttt (higher is better). The trade is a small decode cost for 1.50× `full_token`.

**ISL/OSL: 8k /1k (no MTP)**
| conc | bf16 ttt | fp8 ttt | ttt ratio | bf16 TTFT | fp8 TTFT | bf16 ITL | fp8 ITL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 4837 | 4470 | 0.924 | 1472 | 1486 | 12.57 | 13.75 |
| 16 | 7377 | 7146 | 0.969 | 2806 | 2827 | 14.79 | 15.39 |
| 32 | 11035 | 10800 | 0.979 | 5176 | 5204 | 16.77 | 17.29 |
| 48 | 13050 | 12855 | 0.985 | 7564 | 7615 | 19.09 | 19.50 |

**ISL/OSL: 8k /1k (MTP, accept length 2.13–3.04, against 2.00–3.04 for bf16)**
| conc | bf16 ttt | fp8 ttt | ttt ratio | bf16 TTFT | fp8 TTFT | bf16 ITL | fp8 ITL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 6115 | 5850 | 0.957 | 1716 | 644 | 9.29 | 9.77 |
| 16 | 10417 | 10261 | 0.985 | 639 | 362 | 8.11 | 8.32 |
| 32 | 14255 | 13967 | 0.980 | 665 | 630 | 9.94 | 10.28 |
| 48 | 16115 | 15749 | 0.977 | 673 | 681 | 11.73 | 12.20 |

**ISL/OSL: 68k/200 (no MTP)**
| conc | bf16 ttt | fp8 ttt | ttt ratio | bf16 TTFT | fp8 TTFT | bf16 ITL | fp8 ITL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 20064 | 19665 | 0.980 | 7165 | 7245 | 12.65 | 13.50 |
| 16 | 23071 | 22798 | 0.988 | 23901 | 24119 | 15.20 | 16.00 |
| 48 | 24009 | 23792 | 0.991 | 68289 | 68906 | 20.03 | 20.42 |

**ISL/OSL: 68k/200 (MTP, accept length 2.40 / 2.84 / 2.95 against 2.25 / 2.84 / 2.95 for bf16)**
| conc | bf16 ttt | fp8 ttt | ttt ratio | bf16 TTFT | fp8 TTFT | bf16 ITL | fp8 ITL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 20426 | 20468 | 1.002 | 3514 | 5841 | 8.95 | 6.45 |
| 16 | 22930 | 22676 | 0.989 | 9244 | 12048 | 8.52 | 8.71 |
| 48 | 23502 | 23233 | 0.989 | 17511 | 14785 | 12.58 | 13.17 |

**ISL/OSL: 8k /1k, TP8/DP8 Attn(no MTP)** 
| conc | bf16 ttt | fp8 ttt | ttt ratio | bf16 TTFT | fp8 TTFT | bf16 ITL | fp8 ITL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 15383 | 15321 | 0.996 | 7730 | 7702 | 24.29 | 24.52 |
| 128 | 21912 | 21916 | 1.000 | 13622 | 13552 | 27.64 | 27.73 |

The cell to flag is **8192/1024 at c=8** under TP=8: 7.6% less throughput, ITL +1.18 ms. That is the worst of the 14 TP=8 cells; everything else there is within 4.3%, and every cell at concurrency ≥ 16 is within 3.2%. 

The leftover gap is the decode reader, not anything this PR still owns. fp8 goes through aiter's `mla_a8w8` asm kernel, which is tuned for 64 q heads; TP=8 leaves 16 local heads, so it is occupancy-bound — it loads *less* per row (640 B vs 1024 B) and is still slower. The DP=8 table above shows the gap falls into noise. A Triton rewrite was measured and was slower at every shape, so it was dropped. Closing the TP=8 gap needs an `mla_a8w8` variant for 16 q heads on the aiter side; that is a separate PR.

## Reproducing this
One branch, one env variable, two commands, no code edits to switch arms. Taken on MI355X, ROCm 7.2, TP=8, DeepSeek-V4-Pro.

**1. Rebuild `sgl_kernel`** — needed for #37140's AOT half, if your image is earlier than #37140, you need to rebuild as so, otherwise 6 related tests would fail.
```
cd python/sglang/kernels/aot
cp pyproject_rocm.toml pyproject.toml
AMDGPU_TARGET=gfx950 MAX_JOBS=$(nproc) python3 setup_rocm.py build_ext --inplace
cd -
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD/python/sglang/kernels/aot/python:$PWD/python
```
AMDGPU_TARGET is not optional — `setup_rocm.py` defaults to gfx942, which keeps the software cast.
**2. Start a server.** This is the CLI the accuracy matrix was taken on. The two arms differ only in the last export.
```bash
export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1
export SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=high
export SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=0
export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton
export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0
export SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM=1
export SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1
export SGLANG_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=900
export SGLANG_DSV4_UNIFIED_KV_FP8=1      # the fp8 arm adds exactly this line

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <DeepSeek-V4-Pro> --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8888 --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --attention-backend dsv4 --page-size 256 \
  --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --enforce-shared-experts-fusion \
  --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.89 \
  --max-running-requests 64 --cuda-graph-max-bs 64 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --watchdog-timeout 3600
```

**3. For the capacity number** the server need not finish starting — the sizing line comes before CUDA-graph capture, and `unified_fp8=True` is the only reliable confirmation that the switch took effect, since `is_unified_kv_fp8()` also requires gfx95 and `is_unified_kv_triton()`.

```
DSV4 memory calculation: unified=True, unified_fp8=True, bytes_per_full_token=6042.46, available_bytes=132.97 GB, ..., full_token=23161088
```

**4. For accuracy**, once the server is ready:

```bash
python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 1319 --parallel 256 --port 8888
```

**5. Unit tests**, single GPU.

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python3 -m pytest $(git diff --name-only origin/main..HEAD -- test/) -q
```

title: [unified-memory] Enable prefill cuda-graph capture
author: ch-wan
body:
**Stack 2/3:** main → #37506 → #37418 → #37507. Base: #37506.

Enable unified-memory prefill CUDA graphs. Full-prefill FA3/FA4 metadata rebuilds read tables from the current virtual-to-physical mapping and derives SWA write locations from the already translated full-attention write locations. Replay refreshes the existing buffers and clears inactive SWA write slots.

The FULL graph compatibility gate checks the resolved **prefill** backend, including mixed prefill/decode configurations. Unsupported or unresolved prefill backends fall back to disabled FULL prefill graphs; the decode backend does not disable a supported prefill backend.

Validation on `cheng-wan-b200-4gpu`: all four Inkling FA4 full-prefill graph tests passed, covering generation, input/output logprob consistency, prefix reuse, and decoding beyond the SWA window. Eight metadata/backend-gate tests plus 12 subtests passed, including relocation between capture and replay with stable buffer addresses. Repository pre-commit checks passed.

title: [Diffusion] Add cumulative extra-high quality tier
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

The existing diffusion request quality contract overloaded `high`: it enabled both request-gated kernel fusions and model-specific approximate paths. This made it impossible to opt into fusion-only acceleration or measure those fusions independently.

Introduce a cumulative three-tier contract:

- `lossless`: selected reference path plus unconditional bit-exact replacements
- `extra-high`: everything in `lossless`, plus request-gated DiT/VAE fusions only
- `high`: everything in `extra-high`, plus model-owned high-only approximate paths

## Modifications

- Add `extra-high` to the validated sampling/CLI/API quality levels.
- Centralize fusion eligibility so both `extra-high` and `high` mount the same DiT and VAE fusion set.
- Keep MiniMax-H3 Cache-DiT and LingBot BF16 VAE decode high-only.
- Extend BCG compatibility checks and the quality/BCG benchmark matrix to all three tiers.
- Add regression coverage for cumulative fusion behavior, API pass-through, H3 Cache-DiT isolation, and decode precision isolation.
- Refresh diffusion quality documentation across the CLI/API, performance guide, model cookbooks, benchmark skills, and kernel package README.
- Reconcile the fused-kernel inventory with current main: 43 registered operators across 47 implementations, including the recent FLUX.2/Qwen QKV epilogues, Helios QK RoPE, segmented varlen pack, NVFP4 residual/norm producer, and FLUX.2 FP8/NVFP4 token-cat producers.

## Accuracy Tests

No kernel arithmetic changes in this PR. Existing `lossless` and `high` behavior is preserved; the new tier reuses the already existing high-gated fusion implementations while excluding high-only approximate paths.

Validated routing with unit coverage for:

- `lossless -> no request-gated fusion`
- `extra-high -> request-gated fusion`
- `high -> the same fusion set plus existing high-only paths`
- explicit MiniMax-H3 `extra-high` suppressing generic/quality-owned Cache-DiT
- LingBot `extra-high` retaining the non-high decode precision

The full GPU-backed diffusion suite was not run locally because the local environment has no PyTorch/CUDA installation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. This PR adds a request-policy tier and does not change a kernel implementation. The benchmark helper now emits separate `lossless`, `extra-high`, and `high` ABBA rows so model-specific fusion speed/quality evidence can be collected without mixing in approximate paths.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files <all changed files>`
- `python3 python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_diffusion_benchmark_skill.py` (15 tests passed)
- Python compile check for all changed Python files
- `mint validate`
- `mint broken-links`
- registry-to-document inventory check (43/43 operators documented)

title: [CI] Double JIT kernel unit test timeout
author: BBuf

## Motivation

JIT kernel refactors can invalidate compiled artifacts and force broad recompilation during the unit-test lane. In that case, the current 30-minute step timeout can terminate an otherwise progressing run, as seen in #36176.

Increasing the timeout threshold does not increase normal CI runtime; it only gives full-rebuild runs more headroom.

## Changes

- Increase the H100 JIT kernel unit-test `Run test` timeout from 30 to 60 minutes.
- Keep the dependency-install timeout and 240-minute job-level timeout unchanged.

title: [Spec] Add LiLiCorr: a candidate-lattice reranker for DFlash drafts
author: mrusanovsky
body:
## Motivation

DFlash is trained on per-position marginals rather than on the joint block distribution, so its
drafted tokens are individually plausible yet **jointly incoherent** — slot 3 may be a fine
continuation of the prompt while contradicting the token DFlash itself chose for slot 2.

**LiLiCorr** keeps the top-`k` candidates DFlash already produces at each block position and scores
_transitions_ between adjacent candidates with a small two-layer transformer, then commits a path
through the resulting lattice greedily, left to right, instead of taking the per-slot argmax. One
network pass produces every vector, the pairwise scores are a single batched matmul, and only the
greedy walk stays sequential. **Verify is untouched, so outputs remain distributionally identical to**
**the target model's** — only acceptance length and throughput change.

* Paper: LiLiCorr: Lightweight Likelihood Correlation of Parallel Drafts for Speculative Decoding (arXiv:2608.20530)
* Blog: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/nemotron/lilicorr/
* **Companion PR — training:** NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer#2342

This PR is the **serving** half. It ships no checkpoints and no training code; the companion PR
above trains the drafters and exports them in the format this loader reads.

## Performance

**How these were produced.** Six drafters for a **Qwen3-8B** target, all trained in **NVIDIA**
**ModelOpt** on one matched contract — the same corpus, schedule and block geometry for every arm, so
no row carries a training advantage. Training data is NVIDIA's Nemotron Post-Training Dataset v2
with the multilingual split excluded, generated from the target with **thinking disabled**;
**6 epochs**; block size 16 (15 drafted slots, 16 verified); DFlash decay objective at gamma 7;
**8 nodes × 8 H100, global batch size 64** (one sequence per device, no gradient accumulation).

All six were then exported and **served through the code in this PR** on a **single H100 80GB**,
`tp_size 1`, at concurrency 1, greedy `T=0`, `--attention-backend fa3`, `draft_length 15`, mean of
two replicates, with the **whole node held exclusive per benchmark** so nothing else shared it.
Speedup is output tokens/s against an autoregressive baseline measured **in the same allocation**,
because a denominator borrowed from another node carries that node's clock into every ratio.

Three of the five alternatives — `DFlash`, `DSpark`, `Domino` — already live in this repo.

Cells are `acceptance length / speedup-vs-AR`; **★ fastest, ☆ second fastest**:

| benchmark       | LiLiCorr+conv   | LiLiCorr        | DSpark        | DFlash2         | Domino        | DFlash        |
| --------------- | --------------- | --------------- | ------------- | --------------- | ------------- | ------------- |
| gsm8k           | ★ 7.715 / 5.26x | ☆ 7.557 / 5.22x | 7.375 / 4.86x | 7.252 / 5.06x   | 7.225 / 4.87x | 6.341 / 4.59x |
| math500         | ★ 9.241 / 6.54x | ☆ 9.064 / 6.52x | 9.012 / 6.15x | 8.999 / 6.49x   | 8.976 / 6.25x | 7.909 / 5.88x |
| aime25          | ★ 8.285 / 6.03x | ☆ 8.156 / 6.03x | 8.043 / 5.61x | 7.967 / 5.91x   | 8.066 / 5.77x | 7.126 / 5.44x |
| humaneval       | ★ 7.393 / 4.01x | 7.077 / 3.93x   | 7.163 / 3.72x | ☆ 7.081 / 3.95x | 6.864 / 3.73x | 6.156 / 3.68x |
| mbpp\_sanitized | ★ 5.999 / 4.18x | ☆ 5.849 / 4.13x | 5.888 / 3.95x | 5.685 / 4.05x   | 5.679 / 3.91x | 5.027 / 3.70x |
| livecodebench   | ★ 7.975 / 5.40x | ☆ 7.754 / 5.33x | 7.775 / 5.10x | 7.601 / 5.26x   | 7.553 / 5.04x | 6.808 / 4.88x |
| alpaca\_eval    | ☆ 3.697 / 2.69x | ★ 3.656 / 2.70x | 3.588 / 2.52x | 3.467 / 2.58x   | 3.627 / 2.59x | 3.222 / 2.46x |
| mtbench         | ★ 4.014 / 2.94x | ☆ 3.939 / 2.93x | 3.957 / 2.78x | 3.748 / 2.80x   | 3.948 / 2.84x | 3.478 / 2.67x |

**Against every other approach in the table, LiLiCorr with convolutions is the fastest on all eight**
**benchmarks.** Plain LiLiCorr is the fastest on seven of the eight; the exception is humaneval, a
164-prompt slice, where DFlash2 is ahead by 0.5%.

`DFlash` is the deliberately head-free control. Against it, the reranked drafter is worth
**+9.1% to +14.6% output tokens/s** — the number to read if the question is "what does this buy over
what I already run":

| benchmark                      | gsm8k      | mbpp\_sanitized | math500    | livecodebench | mtbench   | humaneval |
| ------------------------------ | ---------- | --------------- | ---------- | ------------- | --------- | --------- |
| throughput vs head-free DFlash | **+14.6%** | **+12.9%**      | **+11.1%** | **+10.5%**    | **+9.9%** | **+9.1%** |

Every head also clears that control by **+7.60% to +21.67%** on acceptance, on every arm and every
benchmark, which is the check that a head actually loaded rather than silently falling back.

**Acceptance length is bit-reproducible under greedy decoding; throughput is not.** The replicate
spread on acceptance was 0.00% on every benchmark; on throughput it is about 0.2% within one
allocation, and about 1% across allocations.

ⓘ **Reproducing these needs `--attention-backend fa3`.** Backends that publish `seq_lens_cpu` every
step pay a device-to-host sync per block, worth about 8% here. That is a property of DFlash decoding
rather than of LiLiCorr, and the new docs subsection explains which backends are affected and why.
Backends also differ in attention numerics, so acceptance measured on different backends does not
belong in one table.

## Modifications

**No new `SpeculativeAlgorithm`, no worker subclass, no registration, no CLI flag, and no new**
**entry in any choices list.** Two environment variables gate the opt-in sampled commit described
below; nothing else reads the environment. LiLiCorr rides `--speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and is
selected by the checkpoint declaring `architectures: ["LiLiCorrDraftModel"]`, exactly as
`DFlash2DraftModel` selects the candidate selector. If you go looking for the registration, that is
why there isn't one.

10 files, **+3,076 / −1**. The single deleted line is one `if` in the draft loop that gained a
branch; everything else is an addition.

**Only four files already existed — +164 / −1 between them:**

| file                                              | added        | what                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| srt/speculative/dflash\_worker\_v2.py             | **+95 / −1** | five dispatch seams: two `__init__` assignments, the fold branch in `_maybe_build_draft_sampler`, the guarded anchor publication inside `_append_target_hidden_to_draft_kv_by_loc`, and a fourth arm on the existing three-way draft-loop branch |
| srt/models/dflash.py                              | **+2**       | `DFlashDraftModel` declares `lilicorr: Optional[nn.Module] = None` beside the existing `candidate_selector`, and stores the `rms_norm_eps` it already computes                                                     |
| docs/.../speculative\_decoding.mdx                | +34          | two subsections under "DFlash Decoding"                                                                                                                                                                           |
| test/registered/unit/spec/test\_dflash\_logits.py | +33          | one worker-stub test: the sampled arm's device gate                                                                                                                                                               |

For scale, `selector` (DFlash2 — the closest precedent, also a head on the same draft model, also
checkpoint-selected) appears on 43 lines of that worker; `lilicorr` appears on 30.

**New, self-contained:**

* `srt/models/lilicorr.py` (632) — the head, `LiLiCorrDraftModel(DFlashDraftModel)`, `EntryClass`, and the two weight-coverage checks
* `kernels/ops/speculative/lilicorr.py` (520) — three Triton kernels; see "Why the custom kernels" below
* `srt/speculative/lilicorr_utils.py` (656) — head geometry, the candidate lattice, the eager draft seam and the CUDA-graph-folded draft sampler, in one module beside `dflash_utils.py`
* `test/registered/unit/spec/test_lilicorr.py` (805) — 46 CPU tests
* `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_lilicorr_cuda.py` (216) — 18 GPU tests pinning the Triton kernels against their torch references
* `test/registered/e2e/speculative/test_dflash_lilicorr.py` (84) — the E2E server test, registered `disabled=` until a drafter is published

## The head runs inside the draft CUDA graph, and that is the whole optimization

The head is a long tail of small kernels, so what it costs is **host dispatch**, not FLOPs. It
therefore rides the seam DFlash already has for exactly this: `_maybe_build_draft_sampler` runs
before `init_cuda_graphs`, and the sampler is registered on
`draft_model_runner.capture_tail_hooks` through `make_draft_sampler_capture_hook` — the same
mechanism DFlash2's `_SelectorDraftSampler` and DSpark's `DsparkDraftSampler` use, and
`LiLiCorrDraftSampler` has the same shape as the latter: static buffers sized from the capture
buckets, host-side staging of the per-row sampling params before the replay, an in-graph philox
draw, and the drafted tokens written into a static `out` the worker reads after the replay.

Nothing in the head is capture-hostile: static shapes, no collectives at `tp=1`, no host syncs, a
fixed decode trip count, and every parameter-derived buffer built by
`materialize_inference_buffers` before capture.

**There is no `torch.compile` anywhere in this PR.** An earlier revision compiled the captured
body, on the theory that the graph removes the launches' host cost while leaving their number and
memory traffic alone. Measured end to end on one H100 — Qwen3-8B, gsm8k, greedy, `fa3`, `tp_size 1`,
both arms as sequential cells in **one allocation** so the node term cancels — it is a null:

| requests | concurrency | compiled | no compile | Δ acceptance | Δ output tok/s |
| -------: | ----------: | -------- | ---------- | -----------: | -------------: |
| 1319     | 1           | 6.9951 / 731.5 | 6.9947 / 735.6 | −0.005% | +0.56% |
| 1319     | 1           | 6.9951 / 739.7 | 6.9947 / 735.0 | −0.005% | −0.62% |
| 1319     | 32          | 7.0085 / 10179.5 | 7.0022 / 10131.9 | −0.090% | −0.47% |
| 320      | 32          | 7.0650 / 9410.8 | 7.0576 / 9489.0 | −0.105% | +0.83% |

Four pairs straddling zero, against a 1.12% spread for the *same* arm measured in two different
allocations. The fold, by contrast, is load-bearing: in the same allocation and on the same tree,
forcing the head out of the graph with `SGLANG_DFLASH_EAGER_DRAFT_SAMPLER=1` costs **−8.4%**.

So there is no dynamo surface here at all — no compile prewarm, no recompile-limit handling, no
`torch._inductor.config` mutation. The one operational note that remains is that the head should run
on the folded path: an eager fallback exists for the steps the graph cannot serve and is correct but
costs a large fraction of throughput, and because acceptance is identical either way that shows up
only in tokens/s. `build_lilicorr_draft_sampler` warns with a reason when it declines to fold, and
the worker warns once if a decode step lands on the eager head.

Two capture gaps remain, both shared with the existing DFlash heads. Prefill and extend run eager —
the eager seam is the third arm of the same `elif` chain that already carries the selector's and
plain DFlash's. And `tp>1` declines to fold, because the candidate top-k needs a packed all-gather
inside the graph.

## Convolutional drafters are supported, and the support is a refusal

The leading column of the table above is LiLiCorr composed with the grouped dynamic convolutions
that wrap each DFlash sublayer. It serves through this PR, and that is worth stating precisely,
because it is **not** a feature this PR adds.

The convolution belongs to the **DFlash backbone**, not to the reranker: `LiLiCorrDraftModel`
extends `DFlashDraftModel` and therefore inherits the `__init__` that builds it from
`conv_kernel_size` and `conv_group_size` in `dflash_config`. Both the plain and the convolutional
drafter already load and run through the same path, with no new flag and no new code.

What this PR contributes is the **refusal**. Both geometry keys default to `0`, so a checkpoint whose
config lost them builds no convolution modules at all — and the backbone loader then drops every
convolution tensor it cannot resolve. That is correct behaviour for rotary caches and the worst
possible behaviour here: all 20 tensors of a five-layer drafter disappear in silence, the draft
serves as its convolution-free parent, and the only symptom is an acceptance length that is lower
than it should be and entirely believable. `check_conv_weight_coverage` refuses any checkpoint whose
convolution tensors and built modules disagree, in either direction. Five of the CPU tests cover it:
the matched case, the convolution-free case, both silent-drop directions, and a partial checkpoint.

## Sampling the committed path (opt-in)

At `T > 0` the target samples, but the head committed the per-slot argmax and verify was handed a
point mass, so each slot was paid `p(argmax)` rather than the overlap of the two distributions.
`LILICORR_SAMPLING=1` draws each slot from `softmax(scores / T)` over that slot's candidates, at the
request's own temperature, and publishes the proposal it drew from into the same buffers the DFlash2
selector already fills — so the accept path is untouched and verify stays exact. Greedy requests
sharing the batch take the argmax and report a one-hot proposal. On Qwen3-8B it is worth about 6%
acceptance and 6% end-to-end at `T = 1`, at under 1% of the per-block wall.

Off by default, and with it unset the captured body is `select` itself rather than something
equivalent to it, so `T = 0` output is unchanged bit for bit.
`SGLANG_LILICORR_REQUIRE_SAMPLING=1` refuses to start if the mode was asked for but is not enabled.
Both are read once at import: the sampler is replayed from a captured draft graph, so a per-call
read would be a host-side branch inside a replay — happy to move them to `ServerArgs` fields
resolved at init if you would rather.

The sampled commit is additionally gated on the same supported-device condition as the selector's,
on both the folded and the eager path, because it publishes into an accept kernel that does not run
everywhere. Where it is unsupported the arm falls back to the argmax commit and the existing verify.

## Why the custom kernels

`kernels/ops/speculative/lilicorr.py` is the single largest new file after the head itself, so it is
worth saying up front what it buys. All three kernels dispatch to a value-identical torch
implementation off CUDA, which is also what makes the head exercisable in a CPU unit test.

**`lilicorr_topk_lse` — exact per-row top-k _and_ the full-vocab log-partition from one pass over**
**`[n, V]`.** The head scores log-probs normalized over the whole vocabulary, so it needs the partition
as well as the top-k. Composing that from existing ops (`torch.topk` followed by a `logsumexp`
epilogue) **reads the vocabulary logits three times and materializes two more `[n, V]` temporaries**,
and at a 150k vocabulary that read is the single largest cost in the block. Fusing them makes it one
read and no temporaries. The tile pre-selection is **exact, not approximate** — the argument is in the
function docstring and worth reading before trusting the kernel: if a top-k element's tile were not
among the k tiles with the largest maxima, k other tiles would each hold an element at least as
large, contradicting its rank.

**`lilicorr_greedy_path` — the whole left-to-right commit in one kernel.** The torch form issues
roughly three kernels per slot over `[bs, k]` tensors, so at 15 slots the decode is dozens of
few-microsecond launches and is pure launch overhead rather than arithmetic. Same recurrence, and
`tl.argmax` breaks ties toward the lower index as `Tensor.argmax` does, so the committed path is
identical.

**`lilicorr_sample_path` — that same walk with a sampled commit**, emitting the per-slot proposal the
verify needs to accept it by rejection sampling. A row with `greedy_mask` set takes `tl.argmax` on
the same fp32 node values as the greedy kernel, so one captured graph serves greedy and sampling
batches and the greedy rows walk a bit-identical path.

## Correctness

Verify is unmodified, so **this change cannot alter the distribution of emitted tokens.** Every
drafted token is still checked against the target model exactly as before; a worse drafter would show
up as lower acceptance, never as different output. That is the primary correctness argument, and it
is why the section above measures acceptance rather than task scores.

**Unit tests:** **46 CPU tests** (`test_lilicorr.py`), one worker-stub test in
`test_dflash_logits.py`, and **18 GPU tests** (`test_lilicorr_cuda.py`) pinning all three Triton
kernels against their torch reference implementations on device — vocabulary sizes straddling the
kernel's tile boundary in both directions, bf16 logits as production uses, the narrow-vocabulary
fallback, and the greedy commit at k = 1…16 including tie-breaking. Verified on an H100: 75/75 pass
across the three files. The registry validates — `validate_all_suites()` is clean over 2,487
registered tests — and every pinned pre-commit hook passes over the PR range.

**E2E:** `test/registered/e2e/speculative/test_dflash_lilicorr.py` serves the head through
`--speculative-algorithm DFLASH` with only the draft path changed, and asserts GSM8K accuracy plus
two acceptance floors. It is registered `disabled=` because no drafter is published yet, but it has
been run against one on an H100: `1 passed in 177.19s`, GSM8K 0.950, accept length 5.0392 against a
head-free DFLASH control reading 4.1694 on the same eval.

## Checklist

* Format your code according to Format code with pre-commit — every pinned hook passes over the PR range
* Add unit tests according to Run and add unit tests — 46 CPU tests (`register_cpu_ci`), 18 GPU kernel-parity tests (`register_cuda_ci`), and an E2E server test on the DFlash fixture (`register_cuda_ci`, `disabled=` pending a published drafter)
* Update documentation according to Write documentations — a subsection under "DFlash Decoding"
* Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — see **Performance**
* Follow the SGLang code style guidance

## Design notes

The choices most likely to prompt a question, each also commented at the site.

1. **The head geometry is parsed in `srt/speculative/lilicorr_utils.py`, not as a field on
`DFlashDraftConfig`.** The shared DFLASH config therefore carries no knowledge of this head, at the
cost of one extra `dflash_config` read at model build, and `dflash_utils.py` stays at **zero**
changes.
2. **The lattice attention bias is materialized `[batch*heads, S, S]` rather than broadcast.** The
broadcast form is mathematically identical and saves a copy, but a stride-0 mask measured
**−1.75pp**. Please measure before changing it back.
3. **`F.rms_norm` rather than `sglang.srt.layers.layernorm.RMSNorm`, and a hand-rolled attention**
**module carrying `nn.MultiheadAttention`'s parameter layout.** Same math and the same state\_dict
keys in both cases. The custom-op norm is not capturable here, and the module's Python control flow
and `need_weights` bookkeeping are what make it uncapturable.
4. **The weight loader raises in both directions** — missing head tensors _and_ surplus ones — and
`candidate_topk` must be a power of two, refused at config parse. The surplus direction is live,
not hypothetical: one projection is an `Identity` when the head is as wide as the draft, so a
config omitting the head width would otherwise silently drop it and serve a different architecture
than the one trained. The power-of-two constraint comes from the tiled top-k holding its selected
tiles in a single Triton lane group; supporting other widths would mean serving the head on the
slow reference path, so it is refused at load instead of silently deoptimized.
5. **The convolution coverage check is separate from the head coverage check**, because the two look
at different namespaces: the convolution tensors are backbone parameters named
`layers.*.{attention,mlp}_conv.*`, none of which is under `lilicorr.`, so the head check cannot
see them. See "Convolutional drafters" above for why a missing check is dangerous rather than
merely untidy.
6. **The anchor is worker-owned rather than carried on `DFlashDraftInputV2`.** Carrying it there so
that filter and merge keep it aligned with the batch is the tidier design, but it measured
**−4.67% acceptance** at concurrency 32, and the drift it prevents is not detectable: reordering
cannot happen at concurrency 1 and happens constantly at 32, where acceptance reads 7.5573 and
7.5669. The measurement is recorded at the site in `set_anchor`.

## Known gaps

* **Checkpoints are not yet published.** The docs example carries a placeholder path. The companion
ModelOpt PR linked at the top adds the training and checkpoint export, including the optional
convolutions.
* **`tp>1` serves the head eagerly.** Folding it needs the candidate top-k's packed all-gather
inside the draft graph.
