title: [AMD] gfx950 assembly attention for EAGLE verify, draft extend and decode
author: zijiecode
body:
## Motivation

On MI355X, one EAGLE/MTP decode cycle of Qwen3.5-397B runs three attention calls through Triton split-K kernels: the target verify step (4 query tokens per sequence), the draft-model extend (q_len 1 to 4 per sequence) and q_len-1 decode. All three use head size 256, FP8 KV cache with page size 16, and 16 or 8 query heads per KV head. The Triton verify kernel streams KV at about 2.2 TB/s and the draft extend path is slower still; together they are most of the decode cycle at long contexts.

This PR serves all three with one hand-written gfx950 assembly kernel (`vattn_asm`) that reads the paged FP8 cache in place at about 5 TB/s, 2.0-3.4x the Triton path. The kernel ships as `.s` source under `sglang.kernels` and is assembled at first use by the ROCm clang that every gfx950 image includes (validated on ROCm 7.2.0 and 7.2.4; the ROCm 7.0.0 assembler produces byte-identical code, but the path is gated to 7.2 or newer), so nothing changes at build time and no aiter release is needed.

## Modifications

- Add `sglang/kernels/ops/attention/vattn_asm_gfx950/`: the attention kernel (`vattn3_core.s`), its split-KV reduce (`vred.s`) and a small loader that assembles them with ROCm clang at first use and launches them through `hipModuleLaunchKernel`. The kernel handles q_len 1 to 4 per sequence in-kernel, so the draft paths need no padding or gather and stay cuda-graph capture safe.
- `unified_attention_3d_mtp.py`: route the verify call to the assembly kernel when the shape is supported; add two thin entry points for draft extend (ragged q_len) and q_len-1 decode that return False and leave the batch to the existing Triton path when they cannot serve it.
- `aiter_backend.py`: call those entry points from the verify, draft_extend and decode paths on gfx950 (head size 256, page size 16, FP8 KV, no sliding window, softcap or sinks). The verify gate also accepts 8 query heads per KV head (TP4).
- On by default on gfx950 (exact `gcnArchName` match) with ROCm 7.2 or newer (`get_hip_version() >= (7, 2, 0)`) when ROCm clang is present; `SGLANG_ASM_VERIFY_ATTN=0` keeps everything on the Triton path. If assembling or loading the kernel fails at first use, it is disabled for the process with one warning line and the call continues on the Triton path. Other shapes and GPUs are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Verify path: outputs are bit-identical to the kernel build validated in the previous revision of this PR, so its GSM8K and GPQA results carry over. Draft extend and decode paths: outputs are bit-identical to the verify path on the same rows, and cuda-graph replay is bit-identical to eager. With a deliberately broken assembler, the first call returns without error, the kernel is disabled for the process, and the output is bitwise identical to the Triton path.

GSM8K, 1319 questions, TP4, real EAGLE decoding (3 steps, top-k 1, 4 draft tokens), `--attention-backend aiter --page-size 16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`:

| Attention kernel                                    | Accuracy | Invalid |
|-----------------------------------------------------|---------:|--------:|
| `unified_attention_3d_mtp` (Triton)                 | 0.921    | 0.006   |
| `vattn_asm`, verify only                            | 0.918    | 0.005   |
| `vattn_asm`, verify + draft + decode (this branch)  | 0.919    | 0.005   |

GPQA diamond (198 questions, repeat 8), verify path:

| Validation                                           | Result |
|------------------------------------------------------|-------:|
| Mean score                                           | 0.879  |
| `unified_attention_3d_mtp` (Triton, from #36330)     | 0.879  |
| Reference (Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B model card)        | 0.884  |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

All numbers on MI355X (gfx950, ROCm 7.2), Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4: head_dim 256, fp8 page-16 KV.

### Kernel microbenchmarks

Verify shape (4 query tokens per sequence), single GPU, cold L2 (16 rotating KV replicas, randomly permuted page tables), kernel plus segment reduce, per layer:

| Kernel                                                                   | 16 x 35k, GQA 16     | 16 x 70k, GQA 16 | 16 x 35k, GQA 8     |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------:|-----------------:|--------------------:|
| `unified_attention_3d_mtp` + `unified_attention_3d_mtp_reduce_segments` | 131.6 us (2.2 TB/s)  | 261 us (2.2 TB/s)| 197 us (fallback)   |
| `vattn_asm` + `vred_asm`                                                 | 67 us (5.0 TB/s)     | 105 us (5.3 TB/s)| 57 us (5.5 TB/s)    |

Draft shapes, single GPU, per layer:

| Batch                                                   | `unified_attention` (Triton) | `vattn_asm` |
|---------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------:|------------:|
| draft_extend, 8 seqs x 105k, ragged q_len 1..4          | 396 us                       | 226 us      |
| decode q_len 1, 8 seqs, contexts 6 to 105k              | 100.5 us                     | 66.2 us     |

A streaming-read microbenchmark puts the device's practical read ceiling at 5.9-6.9 TB/s; ablating the compute phases of `vattn_asm` changes its time by less than 5%, i.e. the kernel is bound by K/V traffic.

### End-to-end serving, real agentic traces (InferenceX)

Same tree, two runs differing only in `SGLANG_ASM_VERIFY_ATTN` (0 = all Triton, 1 = this PR: verify, draft_extend and decode on the asm kernel). The server is started by the unchanged MI355X InferenceX recipe (https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/main/benchmarks/single_node/agentic/qwen3.5_fp4_mi355x_sglang_mtp.sh, as used by the `qwen3.5-fp4-mi355x-sglang-agentic-mtp` entries of https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/main/configs/amd-master.yaml), and aiperf replays real agent sessions from the public `cc-traces-weka-062126-256k` dataset over a 1200 s window (`AIPERF_EXPERIMENTAL_FAST=1`, one warmup request per lane).

```
aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp \
    --url http://localhost:$PORT --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --endpoint-type chat --streaming \
    --model amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4 --tokenizer amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4 --tokenizer-trust-remote-code \
    --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126_256k --num-dataset-entries 393 --apply-chat-template \
    --concurrency $CONC --benchmark-duration 1200 --warmup-requests-per-lane 1 --warmup-grace-period 1800 \
    --trajectory-start-min-ratio 0.25 --trajectory-start-max-ratio 0.75 --trace-idle-gap-cap-seconds 300 \
    --random-seed 42 --failed-request-threshold 0.10 --use-server-token-count \
    --server-metrics http://localhost:$PORT/metrics --stats-interval 30 --slice-duration 1.0 --no-gpu-telemetry
```

TP2, concurrency 32, KV offloading to DRAM with HiCache (the `kv-offloading: dram` TP2 entry of the sweep; `KV_OFFLOADING=dram KV_OFFLOAD_BACKEND=hicache`). Both runs: 0 failed requests, 94% prefix cache hit.

| TP2 c32 (HiCache)                | `SGLANG_ASM_VERIFY_ATTN=0` | `SGLANG_ASM_VERIFY_ATTN=1` | Delta   |
|----------------------------------|---------------------------:|---------------------------:|--------:|
| TPOT p50                         | 16.34 ms                   | 13.99 ms                   | -14.4%  |
| TPOT mean                        | 20.93 ms                   | 17.83 ms                   | -14.8%  |
| TPOT p90                         | 25.70 ms                   | 22.71 ms                   | -11.7%  |
| Interactivity p50 (tok/s per user) | 61.2                     | 71.5                       | +16.9%  |
| Interactivity p90                | 95.5                       | 120.7                      | +26.5%  |
| Output throughput                | 828 tok/s                  | 894 tok/s                  | +8.0%   |
| Requests completed in the window | 1336                       | 1433                       | +7.3%   |
| E2E latency p90                  | 34.2 s                     | 28.0 s                     | -18.0%  |
| TTFT p50                         | 1.33 s                     | 1.27 s                     | -5.0%   |

Matched-request check (the 1336 requests, identified by session and turn, that both runs completed): decode time per token 17.81 -> 15.21 ms (-14.6%), request latency -13.2%, TTFT -2.1%. This removes the effect of trace-replay phase drift from the per-request numbers.

TP4, concurrency 16, no KV offloading (the `kv-offloading: none` TP4 entry of the sweep). Both runs: 0 failed requests.

| TP4 c16                          | `SGLANG_ASM_VERIFY_ATTN=0` | `SGLANG_ASM_VERIFY_ATTN=1` | Delta   |
|----------------------------------|---------------------------:|---------------------------:|--------:|
| TPOT p50                         | 6.15 ms                    | 4.58 ms                    | -25.6%  |
| TPOT mean                        | 7.47 ms                    | 6.39 ms                    | -14.4%  |
| TPOT p90                         | 8.48 ms                    | 6.53 ms                    | -23.0%  |
| Interactivity p50 (tok/s per user) | 162.7                    | 218.6                      | +34.4%  |
| Interactivity p90                | 249.5                      | 298.4                      | +19.6%  |
| Output throughput                | 550 tok/s                  | 586 tok/s                  | +6.5%   |
| Requests completed in the window | 692                        | 736                        | +6.4%   |
| E2E latency p90                  | 14.3 s                     | 10.3 s                     | -28.4%  |
| TTFT p50                         | 0.68 s                     | 0.61 s                     | -9.8%   |

Matched-request check (692 requests completed by both runs): decode time per token 6.02 -> 4.60 ms (-23.7%), request latency -21.9%, TTFT -7.2%.

Note on metrics: TPOT and total throughput are the stable comparison metrics for this benchmark; the interactivity mean is dominated by streaming chunk-coalescing outliers (it averages per-request 1/ITL), so interactivity is quoted at p50/p90.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the [SGLang code style guidance](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html).

title: [Bugfix] Load Qwen3.5 MTP embedding under PP
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Summary

- Load the shared target embedding into the Qwen3.5 MTP draft when pipeline parallelism places the draft on the last PP stage.
- Handle both text and VL checkpoint embedding names.
- Add regression coverage for both checkpoint layouts.

## Root cause

The Qwen3.5 MTP draft is colocated with the target last PP stage, while the target embedding exists only on PP0. The draft therefore retains its local embedding, but the MTP weight loader previously skipped the non-`mtp` checkpoint embedding key. This left the underlying `torch.empty()` allocation uninitialized and could produce NaNs during draft embedding lookup; CUDA Graph padding made the latent issue reproducible by changing allocation reuse.

## Testing

- `python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_5_pipeline_parallel.py` — 5 passed.
- AGA AgentX PP+MTP+disaggregation regression, 3 prefill + 4 decode workers, concurrency 565, 900 seconds, `disable_cuda_graph_padding=False`, breakable prefill CUDA Graph:
  - 6,182 warmup requests, 0 errors.
  - 23,541 profiling requests, 0 errors.
  - Slurm job 634992 completed with exit code 0.

The change only initializes the already-allocated draft embedding during weight loading and does not add a serving hot-path operation.

title: [diffusion] model: support FastH3 (4-step VSA-distilled MiniMax-H3) with a VSA-H3 attention backend
author: kevin-mii
body:
## Motivation

Add [FastVideo/FastVideo-FastH3-4-step-Preview-v1-VSA-DataFree](https://huggingface.co/FastVideo/FastVideo-FastH3-4-step-Preview-v1-VSA-DataFree), the 4-step DMD2 distillation of MiniMax-H3 trained with Video Sparse Attention (0.9 sparsity, 64-token tiles), together with the `video_sparse_attn_h3` backend it was trained for.

4x B300, 1344x768 at 24 fps with audio, bf16 eager, Ulysses 4, `VSA_sparsity` 0.9, seed 1000. Clean E2E is the client wall clock of a `/v1/videos` request against `sglang serve` including decode, muxing and file output (median of three after one warm request); the stage columns are the server timings of the same request. H3 aligns the requested durations to 124, 243 and 362 frames.

| Requested / aligned | Encoder | DiT total / per forward | Video + audio VAE | Transport + MP4 | Clean E2E | Client RTF | x real time | Peak HBM |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 5 s / 124 | 0.07 s | 2.18 s / 0.545 s | 0.87 s | 0.9 s | **4.1 s** | 0.79 | 1.26 | 94 GB/GPU |
| 10 s / 243 | 0.07 s | 4.83 s / 1.21 s | 1.71 s | 1.3 s | **8.0 s** | 0.79 | 1.27 | 103 GB/GPU |
| 15 s / 362 | 0.07 s | 8.80 s / 2.20 s | 2.56 s | 1.8 s | **13.3 s** | 0.88 | 1.13 | 111 GB/GPU |

All three satisfy client RTF <= 1.0. For reference, FastVideo's published 4x B200 VSA numbers for the same shapes are 6.1 / 12.0 / 15.5 s, and vllm-project/vllm-omni#6909 reports 8.68 s clean E2E at 10 s and 14.18 s at 15 s on 8x B300 (1.383 s and 2.379 s per forward). Dense FA4 on the same weights and GPUs: 3.77 / 9.84 / 18.45 s (`sglang generate`, stage sum).

## Modifications

- **Model.** `FastH3PipelineConfig` / `FastH3SamplingParams` / `FastH3Pipeline` are thin MiniMax-H3 variants that reuse every H3 stage, loader and admission path; no core files change. The flat native-Diffusers repo is materialized into the base-H3 layout by a revision-pinned model overlay (`kevin-mi/FastH3-4step-Preview-overlay@f769cb80`, same mechanism as the LTX-2.3 / JoyAI / SANA-WM entries). The distilled schedule is the standard shift-12/3 sigma grid at `num_inference_steps=5` (four DiT forwards); no DMD plumbing. `has_gate_compress` adds the trained per-block `to_gate_compress` projection, kept bf16 and unquantized; base H3 loads zeros and runs pure sparse.
- **VSA-H3 backend** (`--attention-backend video_sparse_attn_h3`). Segment-pure prefix tiles plus (4, 4, 4) video tiles over H3's packed `[text | keyframes | audio | video]` sequence; the FastVideo tile-64 Triton kernel with TMA loads and a pinned launch config; one fused pack-and-pool kernel, top-k emitted directly as kernel index lists, one fused untile with the compression branch folded in. Knobs: `VSA_sparsity`, `vsa_mode` (`exempt` / `compete`), `vsa_dense_first_n_steps`, `vsa_dense_layers`. Only the DiT runs sparse; the token refiner, text encoder and VAEs keep their dense defaults. Ulysses supported; ring, `torch.compile` and breakable CUDA graph rejected. Validated on SM90, SM100 and SM103.
- **Rejections.** `--model-variant`, `quality="high"`, `fl2va` / `ref2va`, any `num_inference_steps` other than 5, `vsa_tile_size != 64`, a checkpoint missing any trained `to_gate_compress.weight` (required parameter, never synthesized), and the sibling FastH3 LoRA bundles (their `.diff` / `.diff_b` / `set_weight` tensors match no LoRA mapping rule and would otherwise be dropped silently).
- **Tests and docs.** `test_minimax_h3_fasth3.py` (5), `test_vsa_h3_attention.py` (6, including a sparsity-0.5 masked-dense reference with gates for both modes), GPU case `fasth3_t2va_vsa_4gpu_h100`, cookbook section, attention-backends and compatibility-matrix entries, `fasth3-t2va-vsa` benchmark preset.

Validated deployments on 4x B300 at 5 s: tp2 x ulysses2 (3.42 s, 61 GB), `--use-fsdp-inference` (3.42 s, 50 GB), `--quantization fp8` (2.93 s, 63 GB, gates stay bf16), `--quantization kitchen_int8` (functional), `num_outputs_per_prompt` fan-out, `torch_sdpa` and `sage_attn` dense fallbacks. Rejected with a clear message: `subblock_sparse_attn` on SM103 (sm_100a-only kernel), the AdaLN cache (requires `--model-variant`), and the LoRA bundle. `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=1` behaves as on FastWan: mounts, never hits at four forwards, output unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

The port follows FastVideo's `video_sparse_attn_h3` backend and `block_sparse_attn_triton.py`: same tile geometry, pooling, top-k budgets (`exempt` / `compete`), compression branch and online-softmax kernel. On 4x H200 the VSA-H3 output was checked frame by frame against the FastVideo upstream reference for the same prompt and seed and judged at parity. The fused data path is bit-identical to the original port without the gate and within one bf16 ulp with it; the unit test compares the kernel against an fp32 masked-dense reference at sparsity 0.5 with gates in both modes.

4x B300, 1344x768, 5 s, seed 1000, t = 0.5 / 2.5 / 4.5 s:

![VSA-H3 frames](https://huggingface.co/datasets/kevin-mi/fasth3-pr-assets/resolve/main/b300_5s_vsa_t0.5_2.5_4.5.png)

Note for reviewers: the 4-step schedule amplifies rounding-level differences (Ulysses vs TP2 x Ulysses2, fp8, one-ulp kernel changes) into a different but equally coherent sample from the same seed, so SSIM against a single-seed reference is not a meaningful gate for this model.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`compare_perf.py`, dense FA4 baseline vs VSA-H3 on the same weights (`sglang generate`, 4x B300, 2-step warmup):

| Video | Dense FA4 E2E | VSA-H3 E2E | Diff |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 5 s | 3765 ms | 3183 ms | -15.5% |
| 10 s | 9844 ms | 6683 ms | -32.1% |
| 15 s | 18454 ms | 11471 ms | -37.8% |

Profile-driven: the first trace showed the sparse kernel at 10 ms per DiT layer next to 12 ms of tile gather/scatter, stack, transposes and mask-to-index; the fused path brings that bookkeeping to about 1 ms per layer (35 to 24 ms per layer at 10 s). Remaining per-layer budget at 10 s: attention 9.0 ms, GEMMs 8.4 ms, all-to-all 2.5 ms. The kernel launch config is pinned from a 12-config sweep on B300 (`num_warps=4`, `num_stages=5`), so a fresh process pays 0.3 s on its first sparse call instead of a 2.3 s autotune per sequence length.

## Known limitations

- t2va only; fl2va / ref2va were not distilled.
- Upstream labels the checkpoint a preview; quality gaps versus base H3 on hard motion and fine detail are properties of the distillation.
- The sibling `FastVideo-FastH3-4-step-Preview-v1-LoRA` adapters are out of scope by design: fusing them onto base H3 reproduces the merged checkpoint this PR serves.
- **License note for maintainers:** the checkpoint inherits the MiniMax-H3 Community License. FastH3 is listed where FastWan is (README support line, compatibility matrix) plus the MiniMax-H3 cookbook section; drop it from those lists if the license needs review first.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: Temporarily Remove GLM-5.3 Flash decode CP support
author: kpham-sgl
body:
Follow-up to #36507, companion to #37484. Decode CP re-lands in a PR based on main after the day-0 PR merges.

**Why.** DSA × DCP here is the merge half without the partition half — nothing under `attention/dsa/` calls `get_dcp_lens` or `update_local_kv_lens_for_dcp`, unlike every other DCP-capable MLA backend, and no CI case covers the combination.

**Commit 1 — data path**
- `_should_return_dsa_dcp_lse` and its three call sites (tilelang decode/verify, trtllm decode), plus the `_forward_tilelang` LSE branch
- `return_lse` on `sparse_attention_fwd_kernel_v1/v2` and `tilelang_sparse_fwd`, and the per-call LSE allocation it forced on the non-DCP path
- the `Optional` `prefix_k_pe` NoPE accommodation in `all_gather_kv_cache_for_dcp`
- the `eager_runner` target-verify skip — model-agnostic, so this restores main for DeepSeek-V2, Kimi-K2.5/K3 and Kimi-Linear
- `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration.prepare_context_parallel_metadata_for_dcp`, the DCP opt-in hook
- the two `_should_return_dsa_dcp_lse` tests

**Commit 2 — DCP-only pool sizing** (no-ops at `attn_dcp_size == 1`, reachable only under DCP)
- the draft-pool `× attn_dcp_size` multipliers in `DefaultPoolConfigurator` and `HybridSWAPoolConfigurator`
- `kv_cache_configurator._dsa_pool_geometry`, and the tests pinning both

DFLASH/DSPARK are unaffected: both blocks sit under `is_eagle() or is_standalone()`, and dflash's DCP factor lives in `_dflash_draft_cell_size` / `scale_kv_cell_size_per_token_for_dflash`, untouched.

**Kept.** Prefill CP, KPool/DSA core, NoPE MLA, generic DCP for models that already had it, and the GLM-5.3 B200 e2e. Plus the DCP *exclusion* guards, which keep new code out of DCP rather than implement it: `not dcp_enabled` in `_ingraph_verify_metadata_eligible`, and the two `attn_dcp_metadata is None` guards in `flashinfer_mla_backend`.

**No regression vs main.** Every removed line is new in #36507 — `return_lse`, `_should_return_dsa_dcp_lse` and `_dsa_pool_geometry` are all absent from `origin/main`, so DSA × DCP stays exactly as unsupported as it is there. `dcp/comm.py`, `eager_runner.py` and `test_dcp_layout_unit.py` land byte-identical to main, and `tilelang_kernel.py` to `f040cc72e6^`, leaving NoPE (`tail_dim == 0`) kernel selection and the `topk % 64` relaxation untouched. Models defining the DCP hook go 5 → 4, dropping only `glm5_next.py`. `return_lse` was a trace-time flag, so DCP-off kernels never contained the LSE epilogue: output is bit-identical, minus one allocation per tilelang decode call.

**Validation.** compileall and pre-commit clean; no dangling reference to any removed symbol. Rebased onto `545bd6f839` after #37484 merged. No GPU run yet — hence draft.

title: Size the unified read-table grid from bs, and fuse the allocator's tombstone scatters
author: ch-wan
body:
> **Stack** — first of four. Nothing depends on it upstream; #37512 → #37550 → #37560 sit on top, in that order.

## Motivation

Two independent costs in the unified memory pool's hot path.

**The read table's cuda-graph grid was sized by `max_context_len`.** `build_kv_read_table` launched `(bs, cdiv(max_pages, BLOCK))` blocks. The eager path passes the batch's live maximum, but the captured path passes `max_context_len` — and a cuda-graph capture bakes the grid. Every decode replay ran 4096 column blocks per row for sequences 8k long: 99.2% of the 262144 blocks loaded two scalars, failed the `cols < n_pages` mask, and exited.

The tell is that the cost did not vary with the sequence length — 158.5us at seq=1024 and 160.2us at seq=131072, one launch per step. It was pure block-scheduling overhead, and it grows with `cuda_graph_max_bs`: 631us per step at bs=256.

**The allocator's free path issued five kernels where one suffices.** `_free_lazy`'s v2p gather and both tombstone scatters are one lane's work per page, so they collapse into a single kernel — the inverse of the `alloc_bind_inplace` the alloc fast path already uses.

## Modifications

- `build_kv_read_table`'s grid comes from `bs` alone; each program strides over its columns with the loop bound read from the device-side `seq_lens`. The grid stays static so a capture bakes it, and the work tracks the real lengths at replay. `BLOCK` 512 / 8 warps / 1024 blocks is the joint optimum over bs 1..256 × seq 1k..128k, flat within ~10%.
- `_free_lazy` and `bind` in `MultiEndedAllocator` use two new fused Triton kernels (`free_unbind_inplace`, `bind_inplace`), each with a pure-torch CPU path because the allocator's unit tests run on CPU.
- The two `torch.cat`s stay: `_free_phys_pages` is a `_CapacityField` whose contract is rebind-never-mutate, and the rebind is what invalidates the `available_size` memos.
- `test_free_paths_actually_use_index_fill` asserted the free path's source contains `index_fill_`. The fusion writes the tombstones inside the kernel instead, which serves that file's real invariant — the `-1` never crosses the bus — strictly better. It now checks for any of the sanctioned no-sync forms.
- `virtual_slot.py` had **no test in the tree at all**, and on CPU both launchers take their reference path, so the kernel doing the tombstoning was never executed by the suite. Added CUDA-gated coverage over 20 randomized bind/free rounds.

## Accuracy Tests

Kimi-Linear-48B TP2 + `--enable-unified-memory`, GSM8K over 400: **0.9125 on both sides**.

Treat that as a sanity check, not the argument: the same unchanged server returns 0.9175 / 0.9175 / 0.9125 across three runs, so 400-example GSM8K on this box carries a ±2 question band.

The correctness argument is the kernel-level equality. The page table is verified against an independent CPU model over 30 randomized cases — page_size 1..4, mixed `seq_lens`, `-1` holes in `req_to_token`, tombstoned v2p rows, and a non-zero `out` so the prefix-only contract has to leave the tail intact — plus both degenerate shapes. A captured graph replays bit-identically to a fresh launch as `seq_lens` moves over 1 / 64 / 999 / 4096, which is the property the static grid exists for.

The fused allocator kernels are checked against the torch implementation over 20 randomized page sets (both tables plus the returned physical pages), empty input, and CPU/CUDA agreement. Dropping `tl.store(p2v_ptr + p, -1)` from the kernel turns two of the new tests red.

`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/`: 2128 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Read-table grid, H100, under graph replay:

| shape | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| bs=64 seq=8224 | 158.7us | 2.6us | 61x |
| bs=64 seq=1024 | 158.9us | 1.7us | 92x |
| bs=256 seq=8224 | 631.3us | 4.9us | 129x |
| bs=256 seq=131072 | 642.8us | 81.4us | 8x |
| bs=1 seq=8224 | 3.4us | 1.6us | 2x |

Allocator fusion, Kimi-Linear TP2 + unified, bs=64 / 8k in / 10 decode steps:

```
_free_lazy  305 launches / 430us -> 183 / 259us
bind        140 launches / 220us ->  70 /  70us
```

End to end, Kimi-Linear TP2, bs=64 / 8k input / 64 output, three runs a side on the same idle GPU pair:

```
main    5164.96 / 5166.33 / 5167.17 tok/s
branch  5239.63 / 5241.60 / 5250.28 tok/s      +1.50%
```

That is 172us per decode step against the 156us the kernel saves — the same number within run-to-run spread. A fresh decode profile confirms it: `build_kv_read_table_kernel` 1606us → 47us over the same 10 launches, 1.18% → 0.03% of decode kernel time, with every large kernel (moe, all_reduce, MLA attention) inside noise.

Both sides ran sequentially on the same idle GPU pair. That is not a formality on a shared box: a TP pool is sized from the minimum free memory across ranks, so a side-by-side run on two GPU sets measures whoever else is resident.

Kernel timings were taken under `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` replay. A plain Python launch loop floors every Triton launch at ~16us regardless of the work, which made a 60-config sweep read as uniformly optimal.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing surface changes.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Not in this PR

The `out` buffer these kernels fill is still `max_bs x max_context_len` int32 — 1.0 GiB at 1M context — for the same reason the grid was. That is #37512.

title: Build the unified read stream directly, without the page-table rectangle
author: ch-wan
body:
> **Stack** — second of four. **Depends on #37511** (its base branch); review only the commits above `Test the fused tombstone by what it must do`. #37550 → #37560 sit on top.

## Motivation

Three of the seven backends that read the unified pool never wanted a page table. They built a `[max_bs, max_pages]` rectangle and handed it straight to `create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton` to repack into the indptr-addressed stream a paged wrapper plans over; no attention kernel ever read the rectangle.

A rectangle's width is bounded by `max_context_len`, because any single request could be that long and every row must be as wide as the widest. At ps=1, max_bs 256 and a 1M context that reserves 268M slots against a pool that holds 8.15M tokens — 32x more than any reachable state. The stream holds one id per resident token, so its length is `sum(seq_lens)`, which the pool bounds exactly.

## Modifications

One gather-and-translate, two delivery forms:

```
PAGE TABLE    out[b, c] = entry(b, c)                              rows a uniform stride apart
TOKEN STREAM  out[row_starts[b] + p] = entry(b, p//ps)*ps + p%ps   indptr-addressed
```

The rule that comes out of it is stateable: **a consumer that plans over a stream calls `fill_packed_read_stream` (flashinfer_mla, flashinfer, triton); a consumer whose kernel reads a page table fills the table it already owns, via `fill_read_table` (flashattention, trtllm_mha, trtllm_mla, flashmla).**

- The two forms share one `@triton.jit`, differing by two constexpr: `row_starts` null means a uniform stride, and `EMIT_PER_TOKEN` selects page or token granularity. The CPU reference paths share `_entries` for the same reason.
- flashinfer_mla, flashinfer and triton fill the stream directly. `kv_view` was threaded through five frames of each flashinfer updater chain; the decode chains never needed the real pool indices (a rectangle is indexed by batch lane, so its row ids were `arange(bs)`) and now take them instead.
- The second half of the rule was already half-true: trtllm_mla and flashmla pass their own block table and consume it in place. flashattention and trtllm_mha each held a *second* rectangle — trtllm_mha's own `page_table` is explicitly not written under unified (`skip_page_table=unified`) while `kv_read_tables` is what gets bound, so one of its two identically-shaped buffers was dead. Both now match their siblings, and **`make_capture_tables` is deleted.**
- `normal_decode_set_metadata` gains `SKIP_PAGE_TABLE`, a constexpr early-out after the prefix sum, so the translator can write fa3's page tables directly. Its now-unreachable `src_is_read_table` path goes with it: -41 lines, one mechanism in the file instead of two.
- Two predicates get names of their own: `KVIndexTranslator.reads_are_translated` (unified, minus the DCP defer), which callers need *before* picking a source, and `fill_packed_read_stream(sliding_window=...)`, selecting the swa sub-pool's own v2p.
- **Bug fix, pre-existing:** the page table was built one length and read another. The builder got `seq_lens`; fa3's fused kernel and trtllm_mha's attention kernels bound their reads by `cache_seqlens` = `seq_lens + delta` on a draft decode or target verify. The columns in between were read and never translated. A comment claimed this was unreachable — "Spec is asserted off under the unified pool" — but `kv_cache_hook` allows `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK`, a chain draft with topk 1, which is exactly that branch. Both now fill to `metadata.cache_seqlens_int32`.
- **Bug fix, pre-existing:** `fill_read_table` asserted `is_translating`, but `build_index_table` returns the passthrough without touching `into` when reads are deferred, which is what DCP does. trtllm_mla returns early on `dcp_enabled`; flashmla does not, and its `block_kv_indices` is a reused buffer, so unified + DCP + flashmla would have read the previous batch's indices. The precondition is now `reads_are_translated`, so that combination fails by name.

## Accuracy Tests

Branch vs base, GSM8K over 400 unless noted:

| config | base | branch |
|---|---|---|
| Kimi-Linear TP2, flashinfer_mla | 0.9125 | 0.9175 |
| Kimi-Linear TP2 + `--dcp-size 2` | 0.9175 / 0.9225 | 0.9150 / 0.9175 |
| Falcon-H1-1.5B, flashinfer | 0.7725 / 0.7850 / 0.7825 | 0.7850 / 0.7775 / 0.7775 |
| Falcon-H1-1.5B, triton | 0.7850 / 0.7825 / 0.7775 | 0.7750 / 0.7850 / 0.7850 |
| Falcon-H1-1.5B, fa3 (5 runs) | mean 0.7775 | mean 0.7850 |
| gpt-oss-20b, triton (SWA, 4 runs) | mean 0.9387 | mean 0.9387 |

Means match on the Falcon and gpt-oss rows; the Kimi rows sit inside this box's ±2 question band, which three runs of one unchanged server reproduce. Two rows carry their own weight: the **DCP** row is the one path where `fill_packed_read_stream`'s return value is load-bearing (the stream comes back deliberately virtual and the caller finishes it), and the **gpt-oss** row is the sliding-window stream, which nothing else here exercises.

On the fa3 row: at three runs a side the two bands looked disjoint (base 0.7625–0.7800, branch 0.7825–0.7975). They are not — the base's own spread is 11 questions over five runs.

Kernel level: the stream builder is bit-identical to the two steps it replaces over 40 randomized cases (page_size 1..4, mixed `seq_lens`, `-1` holes, tombstoned v2p rows, half the trials driving `kv_start_idx`). A CPU test pins `packed[indptr[b] + p] == ids[b, p // ps] * ps + p % ps`, so a change to either builder alone turns red.

`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/`: 2127 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**This PR buys memory, not speed.** Kimi-Linear TP2, 1M context, `cuda_graph_max_bs` 256:

```
decode CUDA graph memory   2.89 GB -> 1.89 GB        (2.97 -> 1.97 under --dcp-size 2)
```

Throughput is unchanged, and that is the honest framing: the repack this removes costs ~5.8us per step against ~780ms of decode, two orders of magnitude under the run-to-run spread. (At kernel level the fused build is 2.1–6.5x the two steps it replaces; that ratio does not survive contact with a decode loop.)

A caveat on the memory figures: they come from the `CUDA graph end ... mem usage` log line, which is `empty_cache()` + `mem_get_info()` — true device-free memory, and therefore a **lower bound** rather than the allocation delta. On gpt-oss-20b it reports 0.67 GB on both sides while `torch.cuda.memory_allocated()` across `init_cuda_graph_state` reports `base +545.3 MiB` vs `tip +289.3 MiB` — 256.0 MiB, exactly the two rectangles. The caching allocator satisfies the request out of the block it already holds for the KV pool, so device-free does not move. Non-zero deltas are real; zero ones prove nothing.

Also removed: one kernel launch per step per backend (the repack), and for fa3 the verbatim copy of the read table into `page_table`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing surface changes.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## On #35245

That PR introduced `KVIndexTranslator` to give id-space translation a single owner, after every backend reached for the hook itself through `getattr(allocator, "translate_kv_loc_for_kernel", None) or getattr(...)`. **That design is kept in full** — no backend here gains a v2p read or a translate hook; `grep` for `v2p_page_table|kernel_page_multiplier|translate_kv_loc_for_kernel` outside `mem_cache/` still returns nothing. The converted call sites know strictly less than before: they used to drive the repack kernel themselves with four fields of the table's internal layout (`ids`, `row_ids`, `row_stride`, `entry_page_size`), and now hand over a buffer and get back a bool.

What this PR replaces is that PR's choice of a *shared, memoized rectangle* as the universal intermediate. Those two are in tension — a rectangle is shareable precisely because it is consumer-independent, while a stream's layout is that consumer's indptr — and the trade resolves against the cache at every batch size, because the thing being cached is cheaper than the thing the cache forces afterwards:

```
rectangle build (shared, once)     2.66 us
repack, per consumer               5.64 us
fused stream build, per consumer   2.83 us

consumers   cached rect + N repacks    N fused builds
    1              8.73 us                2.79 us
    2             14.23 us                5.46 us
    4             25.20 us               10.75 us
```

`2.83N < 2.66 + 5.64N` for every N.

## Known gap

**trtllm_mha has no end-to-end run behind it.** No configuration on this box reaches trtllm_mha with unified memory: Falcon-H1 OOMs in `forward_extend` and gemma-4 is rejected for `head_dim: 512`. Its change is a mechanical swap onto the API its two MLA siblings already use and the unit suite passes, but it wants a reviewer with the hardware.

## Cross-shape validation

Benchmarked against the static pool across four hybrid shapes -- same build, only
`--enable-unified-memory` differing. Schedulable KV, accuracy and throughput all
match; graph memory moves in both directions.

| model | type | KV tokens | graph GB | GSM8K | tput |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gemma-4-E2B-it | SWA | -0.00% | 0.84 -> 0.84 | 0.8717 -> 0.8600 | +2.00% |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 18 linear + 6 full | +0.00% | 1.20 -> 0.74 | 0.5400 -> 0.5350 | +1.67% |
| Kimi-Linear-48B | MLA + KDA | 0.00% | 0.92 -> 1.93 | 0.9075 -> 0.9100 | -0.63% |
| Inkling-Small | full + SWA + ShortConv | 0.00% | 0.57 -> 0.47 | 0.975 -> 0.975 | +1.21% |

Inkling at TP4 is identical down to the token: `max_total_num_tokens=450605` and
`max_mamba_cache_size=207` on both sides, from the same `rest=4.962 GB` budget.
Kimi at TP2 likewise, `4536315` both sides. At `--mem-fraction-static 0.9` both
also boot with `74778` tokens, so unified needs no extra headroom.

Accuracy is clean throughout -- the worst gap is gemma's 2.3 questions per 200,
against 1 sigma of 0.0236, i.e. 0.49 sigma. Kimi's +1.01 GB of graph memory is
*not* the index buffers: probing `init_cuda_graph_state` reports +1025.0 MiB on
**both** sides, so that 1.0 GiB `cuda_graph_kv_indices` is a static-pool cost too.

One methodology note, because the first pass got it wrong: a multi-GPU A/B run
side by side on two GPU sets is not a valid comparison on a shared box. The TP
pool is sized from the *minimum* free memory across ranks, so one foreign 1.2 GB
process on one card of one set shrinks that whole side's KV -- it read as a 22.5%
Inkling regression and a 1.57% Kimi one, both of which vanish when the two sides
run sequentially on the same cards.

## Follow-ups

**`cuda_graph_kv_indices` is still sized `max_bs * max_context_len`**; the stream's
length is bounded by the pool, so it can be ~32.6 MB instead of 1.07 GB.

title: [diffusion] feat: add --async-output-save to overlap output saving with the next request
author: AgainstEntropy
body:
## Motivation

The diffusion scheduler event loop is strictly serial: `forward -> frame
materialization -> image/video encode -> disk write -> ZMQ reply -> dequeue next`.
Every CPU-side byte of the save pipeline is therefore GPU-idle time that sits
directly in front of the next request's GPU work, and it grows with the output
size. Measured tails on an otherwise saturated server:

| Model | Output | Save tail | Share of one request |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Krea-2-Turbo 1024², PNG | ~1.3 MB | 88 ms | 5.4% of 1.63 s |
| Krea-2-Turbo 2048², PNG | ~6.2 MB | 336 ms | 4.2% of 7.91 s |
| MiniMax-H3 1344×768, 124f mp4 | ~1.5 MB | 0.78 s | 2.6% of 26.2 s (8 evals) |
| Krea-2-Turbo 1024², JPEG | ~100 KB | 12 ms | 0.8% of 1.56 s |

This is throughput lost for no reason: none of that work needs the GPU, and the
next request is already queued.

## Modifications

New `--async-output-save` server flag, **off by default**. When enabled, an
eligible request's finalize tail runs on a background thread while the event loop
dequeues the next request immediately.

**`server_args.py`** — the flag and its documented caveats.

**`gpu_worker.py`** — the finalize tail (materialize/save, peak-memory record,
`empty_cache`, perf dump) is extracted into `_finalize_output_batch()`. With
`defer_finalize=True` and an eligible request, it is stashed as a closure the
scheduler retrieves via `take_deferred_finalize()` instead of running inline. The
background run uses a dedicated CUDA side stream ordered after the producing
forward through a recorded event, so its D2H copies and uint8 conversions stay off
the next request's compute stream. Deferred finalize also skips the per-request
`empty_cache()` — releasing the allocator cache while the next request is
mid-forward causes malloc churn.

Eligibility (`_can_defer_finalize`): output rank, CUDA, non-warmup, save-to-file
path, and no perf instrumentation. Perf-instrumented requests stay synchronous
because their finalize runs a replica-wide `all_reduce` that must not fire from a
second thread. Warmup, raw-frame and non-save requests are excluded too.

**`scheduler.py`** — `_DeferredOutput` wraps the forward result; a single-worker
`ThreadPoolExecutor` runs finalize and stages the reply into a queue the event loop
flushes each iteration. In-flight finalizes are bounded at 2, since each one pins
one request's output tensor on the GPU.

One implementation note worth flagging for review: when the request queue is idle
and a finalize is in flight, the loop polls with a 1 ms timeout instead of
hot-spinning. The idle spin is pure Python plus non-blocking ZMQ, and it convoys
the finalize thread — each of its short GIL-releasing C calls then waits a full
switch interval to get the GIL back. Without this, a 0.7 s save was measured
stretching to 80 s.

## Accuracy Tests

Outputs are **byte-identical** with the flag on and off, across every workload
below (same server code, same prompts, flag toggled):

| Model | Workload | Files compared |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Krea-2-Turbo | 1024² JPEG / 1024² PNG / 1024² PNG @c=2 | 32 / 32 / 32, all md5-identical |
| Krea-2-Turbo | 2048² PNG | 16, all md5-identical |
| MiniMax-H3 | 8 evals @c=4 / @c=2 | 8 / 8, all md5-identical |
| MiniMax-H3 | 50 steps @c=2 | 4, all md5-identical |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same server binary in both arms, only the flag differs. Within-process
reproducibility was ~0.05% (repeat runs 49.29/49.28 s and 49.23/49.26 s).

**Krea-2-Turbo, 1× H200, 8 steps, native backend.** `bench_serving --task
text-to-image --dataset vbench`, `--extra-body '{"size":...,"output_format":...}'`.

| Workload | Requests | flag off | flag on | Throughput |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1024², JPEG, concurrency 4 | 32 | 49.61 s | 49.23 s | +0.8% |
| 1024², **PNG**, concurrency 4 | 32 | 52.12 s | **49.29 s** | **+5.7%** |
| 1024², PNG, concurrency 2 | 32 | 52.05 s | **49.28 s** | **+5.6%** |
| 2048², PNG, concurrency 4 | 16 | 126.51 s | **121.14 s** | **+4.4%** |

With the flag on, the PNG wall clock equals the JPEG wall clock (49.29 s vs
49.23 s, inside noise). Encoding leaves the critical path entirely, so choosing a
lossless output format stops costing throughput.

**MiniMax-H3 FL2VA t2va, 2× H200 Ulysses-2 resident**, 1344×768, 124 frames @24fps,
5 s joint audio+video, mp4 out.

| Workload | Requests | flag off | flag on | Throughput |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8 evals (26.2 s/req), concurrency 4 | 8 | 209.64 s | 204.66 s | +2.4% |
| 8 evals, concurrency 2 | 8 | 209.51 s | 207.52 s | +1.0% |
| 50 steps (143.9 s/req), concurrency 2 | 4 | 575.43 s | 575.29 s | +0.02% |
| 8 evals, concurrency 1 (serial client) | 1 | 27.08 s | 27.08 s | 0 |

The gain is `save tail / request duration`, so it favors fast models with large
outputs. A 144 s H3 request amortizes the same 0.78 s tail down to 0.5%, and a
serial client has no next request to overlap with, so it sees nothing — both
expected.

An earlier revision of this change measured FastWan2.2-TI2V-5B (1× H200, 4
concurrent requests) at 38.12 s -> 36.13 s with trace GPU utilization 93.8% ->
98.6% and all inter-request GPU gaps eliminated. Those numbers were taken on the
original base commit and are quoted for the mechanism, not as current CI figures.

## Known costs and limits

- **Reply latency.** Staged replies flush at the top of the next event-loop
  iteration, so a concurrent client can see up to one extra forward of
  per-request latency. On H3 that forward is long and the cost is visible
  (concurrency 4: mean 85.3 s -> 92.7 s). On Krea-2 it is one 1.6 s forward, so it
  is roughly a wash on JPEG (5.91 s -> 6.00 s) and a net win on PNG, where the
  removed 88 ms tail more than pays for it (6.21 s -> 6.00 s). Serial clients are
  unaffected (H3: 27.08 s both ways).
- **Shallow queues on slow models.** Because of the above, a client that keeps
  only a couple of requests in flight against a slow model can starve the server
  for one poll interval per request, cancelling the gain — this is exactly the H3
  50-step / concurrency-2 row. Fast models are immune (Krea-2 at concurrency 2
  matches concurrency 4). A follow-up that sends the reply as soon as finalize
  completes, rather than at the next loop iteration, would remove both this and
  the latency cost.
- Per-request memory metrics may include the next request's allocations, and the
  per-request allocator cache release is skipped in deferred mode.
- Up to 2 in-flight finalizes pin their output tensors in GPU memory.
- Output rank and CUDA only. Verified at sp=2 (H3 Ulysses-2); other ranks are
  unaffected because they do not save output.
- Requests on the frame-return path (`save_output=false`, including
  `/rollout/generate`) keep the synchronous path. Their tail is also GPU-idle CPU
  work and is deferrable in principle, but it is out of scope here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: [1/N] Quantization Refactor: remove dead code and dedup the FP4 marlin helpers
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

`layers/quantization/` is ~101 files / ~40k LOC and carries a measurable amount of code nothing calls. This is the first of a series of small cleanups there, and deliberately the least interesting one: get the dead code out before any file gets split, so later moves do not have to carry it.

Everything removed here has zero callers anywhere in `python/`, `test/` or `docs/`, re-verified per symbol immediately before deletion. Two items are worth calling out:

- **`MarlinConfig` / `MarlinLinearMethod` were unreachable.** `MarlinConfig` is not in `QUANTIZATION_METHODS`, so `--quantization marlin` passed argparse and then died in `get_quantization_config` with `ValueError: Invalid quantization method: marlin`, and its `override_quantization_method` (the `checkpoint_format == "marlin"` detection) was never reached either, because `ModelConfig._verify_quantization` iterates the registry. Deleting `MarlinLinearMethod.apply` also removes the **last runtime `from vllm import _custom_ops`** in the quantization module.
- **`DummyConfig`** is a placeholder bound to `CompressedTensorsConfig` and then unconditionally rebound by the real import ten lines below it, so it never reaches a caller.

## Modifications

Removed (zero callers):

| Symbol | File |
| --- | --- |
| `MarlinConfig`, `MarlinLinearMethod`, `marlin_make_empty_zp` | `marlin_utils.py` |
| `prepare_moe_fp8_layer_for_marlin`, `marlin_quant_fp8_torch` | `marlin_utils_fp8.py` |
| `prepare_humming_layer` | `humming_utils.py` |
| `assert_fp8_all_close` | `utils.py` |
| `transform_scale_ue8m0_inplace` | `fp8_utils.py` |
| `input_to_int8` | `int8_utils.py` |
| `quant_dequant_mxfp4` | `mxfp4.py` |
| `FP4KVCacheRecipe` | `kvfp4_tensor.py` |
| `DummyConfig`, `original_isinstance` | `__init__.py` |

Plus the two strings that named deleted code:

- `"marlin"` from `server_args.QUANTIZATION_CHOICES`. With `MarlinConfig` gone the method is unimplementable, so the choice is a pure trap. Nothing in the repo passes it, and no config's `override_quantization_method` returns `"marlin"`, so no checkpoint can auto-select it either.
- `"MarlinLinearMethod"` from `linear.py:WEIGHT_LOADER_V2_SUPPORTED`.

Imports left unused by the deletions are dropped in the same files.

Finally, `marlin_utils_fp4.py` had two pairs of **identical** closures, duplicated between `prepare_moe_mxfp4_layer_for_marlin` and `prepare_moe_nvfp4_layer_for_marlin`. They are hoisted to module level as `_repack_moe_fp4_weight_for_marlin` / `_permute_moe_fp4_scales_for_marlin`, with the per-caller differences as arguments: the w13/w2 shapes, the group size (32 vs 16), and the per-scale post-process. The NVFP4 `.to(param_dtype)` cast moves to its call sites. The shape locals are computed after the last padding mutation in both callers, so the hoist preserves the closures' late binding of `intermediate_size` / `padded_intermediate_size`.

Net: **+110 / -663** over 12 files. No behavioral change intended.

### Deliberately left alone

`optimized_quantization_methods` in `configs/model_config.py` still lists `"marlin"`. It is unreachable (the `supported_quantization` check raises for anything outside `QUANTIZATION_METHODS` before that warning is consulted) and it is not alone there: `gptq_marlin_24`, `experts_int8` and `compressed_tensors` are not registry keys either, so the list needs its own pass. The other stale entries in `WEIGHT_LOADER_V2_SUPPORTED`, and its `multimodal_gen` copy, are left alone for the same reason.

## Accuracy Tests

No accuracy run. This PR deletes uncalled code and hoists two closures without changing their bodies; it does not touch any live numeric path.

Correctness evidence instead:

- `QUANTIZATION_METHODS` is byte-identical before and after, compared as JSON (registry key -> fully-qualified class name).
- Every touched module imports, and all 12 files are `py_compile` clean.
- `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization`: 169 passed / 7 failed, the same 7 as the parent commit (they need GPU kernels unavailable on the machine used here).
- `test/registered/unit/server_args`, `.../cli`, `.../configs`: 376 passed.
- `pre-commit run` clean on all changed files.

**Known coverage gap:** the two FP4 marlin `prepare_*` paths need a GPU and are not exercised by the CPU tests, so the hoist is verified by construction (identical bodies, capture order checked) rather than by execution. Worth a look from anyone with an MXFP4/NVFP4 marlin MoE setup.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable - no change to any executed path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (Deletion-only; no new behavior to cover.)
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No doc mentions any removed symbol or the `marlin` choice.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (N/A, see above.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [NPU] Support DFlash speculative decoding for MiMo-V2.5-Pro (mxfp4)
author: iridiumine
body:
## Motivation

Enable DFlash speculative decoding for MiMo-V2.5-Pro (mxfp4) on Ascend NPU, covering the full inference path: mxfp4 expert weight loading, DFlash draft/verify execution, NPU graph replay, DP attention, and PD disaggregation. DFlash was previously blocked on this stack by missing weight adaptation, graph-mode metadata bugs, and DP-attention layout mismatches.

## Modifications

- MiMo-V2 mxfp4 on Ascend : load routed expert weights from mxfp4 checkpoints (ckpt scale-name mapping + HF MXFP4 → NPU W4A8 kernel layout conversion) and adapt the DFlash draft to MiMo-specific training params ( attention_sink_bias , attention_value_scale ).
- DFlash capture & draft : capture target aux hidden states (pre-attention outputs of configured layers) in MiMoV2, with TBO disabled during capture rounds; remove the dead per-position mask embedding path.
- NPU graph mode fixes : derive FIA verify KV-length metadata from the DFlash worker's CPU mirror (already includes the verify block, avoiding double counting); refresh dynamic state ( out_cache_loc , seq_lens , block tables, DP buffers, deepep_adapter.replay() ) on the pre-planned replay path; keep seq_lens_cpu_list rebindable by graph.update so KV lengths are not frozen at capture time.
- DP attention support : run draft collectives inside per-DP attn-TP groups; idle ranks join the target verify collective with an empty forward and skip draft KV materialization; add symmetric guards forcing eager verify when any DP rank is idle ( min(original_global_num_tokens_cpu) == 0 ) or when a mixed round (extend + verify across ranks) is detected via aggregated is_extend_in_batch , since spec-scaled global_num_tokens disagree with raw scheduler counts on the DP-gather layout.
- Review fixes : scope the KV-length fix to DFlash only (other spec algorithms keep +draft_token_num ); hoist imports; replace per-rank broadcasts with a single all_gather for full-embed caching; rename build_dflash_family_disagg_draft_input → build_dflash_disagg_draft_input .
- PD disaggregation : add the is_dflash() route in build_spec_info with build_dflash_disagg_draft_input , and add device_urma / device_uboe transfer protocols for the Ascend PD transfer engine.

## Accuracy Tests

title: [Feature] Add Aaronson-Gumbel text watermarking
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Motivation

Some deployments need a machine-readable signal that text was generated by an AI system, including provenance workflows and transparency obligations such as [Article 50 of the EU AI Act](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj/eng). This PR adds opt-in text watermarking to sampled generation without adding tokens or changing default serving behavior.

## What this PR adds

- Keyed Aaronson-Gumbel sampling over the post-penalty, grammar-masked, top-k/top-p/min-p distribution, with model-free Gamma-test detection from token IDs.
- Returned logprobs reflect the pre-watermark target distribution (the sampler computes them from the unforced distribution when `return_logprob` is set, matching the speculative-decode semantic).
- Server configuration through `--enable-watermark` plus one `--watermark-config` JSON object, given as a file path or inline (`key`, `key_b`, `context_window`, `mixing_probability`, `max_probability`, `default_enabled`, `enforce_all`), with explicit opt-in, default-on, and enforce-all policy modes and secret redaction.
- Per-request enablement, keys, and context windows, including mixed watermarked and unwatermarked batches.
- Opt-in dual-key selection with a deterministic per-context coin and matching detector views; single-key behavior is unchanged when key B is absent.
- Verified normal decode plus NGRAM, EAGLE, EAGLE3, and NEXTN, including TP2/TP4 and DP2/TP2 normal/NEXTN service gates.
- An in-tree `WatermarkDetector` that also works as a copied package without SGLang or PyTorch, plus a reference HTTP detection server that uses the same `--watermark-config`.
- Repeated-context loop prevention, greedy bypass, fused normal/speculative state kernels, and a host-gated path that launches no watermark kernels for fully disabled batches.
- Fail-closed admission for unsupported modes, including DFLASH/DSPARK, pipeline-parallel speculation, rejection-sampling speculation, beam search, PD disaggregation, custom logit processors, and non-CUDA devices.

## Performance and evidence

Relative results are within-engine ON/OFF comparisons. Finite-top-k and speculative rows use random 1,024/512 requests, c8, temperature 0.8, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, 10 warmups, 100 measured requests, and three repetitions unless noted.

| Workload | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Qwen3-8B, GSM8K-100 (sgl-eval) | 95-97% accuracy / 100% stop across normal decode (B200), NGRAM with `--disable-overlap-schedule` (H200), and EAGLE3; detection ON p=`1.09e-20` to `4.18e-27`, OFF p=`0.325-0.995`; greedy stopped safely in every gate |
| Qwen3-8B H200, no spec, finite top-k, c1 / c8 | Output throughput `+0.13% / +0.02%` (run-to-run noise) |
| Qwen3-8B GB300, no spec, unlimited top-k, c8 | `224.88 → 212.84` output tok/s per stream (`−5.35%`) |
| Qwen3.5-9B GB300 TP2, NEXTN 3/1/4 | TPOT `2.246 → 2.451 ms` (`+9.17%`); final-head same-pair spot check `+8.92%` |
| Capability enabled, fully disabled EAGLE3 traffic | TPOT `2.465 → 2.469 ms` versus merge-base (`+0.14%`) |
| Dual key versus single key, GB300 | Output throughput `−0.21%` c1 / `−1.50%` c8, within repetition variance |
| Speculative accept length | `2.759 → 2.783` (`+0.85%`) |

The DP2/TP2 gate used Qwen3-8B on two H200 GPUs: GSM8K-100 was 95% with 100% stop, both ranks detected at p=`1.84e-23`, disabled controls were p=`0.358`, repeated one-rank-idle batches remained healthy, and a DP2/TP2 NEXTN smoke detected at p=`2.14e-36` on both ranks.

## Cross-engine reference

Compare each engine's within-engine ON/OFF delta rather than absolute throughput.

| Workload | SGLang | vLLM nightly |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3.5-9B MTP, TP2 GB300, c8, top-k 20 | TPOT `+9.17%`; accept length `+0.85%` | `dual_key_gumbel`: TPOT `+14.24%`; accept length `+0.72%` |
| Qwen3-8B H200, no spec, top-k 20, c1 / c8 | Output throughput `+0.13% / +0.02%` | Plain Gumbel: `−1.70% / −2.11%` |

## Limitations

- Temperature 0 carries no signal. Short or low-entropy spans are weaker, and `max_probability` trades signal for ordinary sampling at low-entropy positions.
- Paraphrase and translation erase the signal; edits reduce the number of usable contexts.
- Murmur32 is a keyed, non-cryptographic mix. Key holders can both detect and forge; inline `--watermark-config` JSON is process-visible, and core dumps may contain in-memory keys.
- Unlimited top-k requires a full-vocabulary sort and measured `−2.8%` to `−7.2%` per-stream throughput; finite `top_k=20` was within noise. Unlimited-top-k speculative verification uses the slower tensor path.
- Watermarking stops after `min(4,096, per-request token-pool capacity)` admitted contexts. Runtime uses 32-bit context-hash admission while the detector deduplicates exact tuples; rare collisions and conservative sibling suppression only dilute signal.
- Speculative cost and acceptance are model- and workload-dependent, especially for top-k-1 draft chains, although the public NEXTN/EAGLE3 measurements above preserved acceptance.

The in-tree [`watermarking/README.md`](https://github.com/JustinTong0323/sglang/blob/watermark/python/sglang/srt/sampling/watermarking/README.md) is the design reference. Evaluation results remain in **Performance and evidence** and **Cross-engine reference** above. Configuration, request semantics, the normative detector contract, standalone use, and the compatibility matrix are in the [`text_watermarking.mdx` operator guide](https://github.com/JustinTong0323/sglang/blob/watermark/docs/docs/advanced_features/text_watermarking.mdx).

Co-authored-by: Nihar Patel <nihpat95@gmail.com>

## Test plan

CUDA selector/state parity suites, OpenAI endpoint e2e, the Rust `wire.rs` schema test, registry entries in `test_parity.py` and `test_model_overrides.py`, full changed-file pre-commit/taxonomy checks, and public-model GSM8K/detection/greedy/speculative/TP/DP service gates.

title: [ROCm] Make DSA indexer top-k exact with cooperative selection
author: jiejingzhangamd
body:
## Summary

- add a ROCm-specific cooperative top-k implementation for the three DSA indexer entry points
- use an fp32 coarse histogram, exact radix tie refinement, and an overflow rescan
- split long rows across blocks when a low batch size would otherwise leave the GPU underutilized
- preserve the raw, paged, and ragged interfaces and guard launches to the score device
- keep the CUDA implementation unchanged; ROCm tracks the native `topk.hip` source and does not hipify `topk.cu`

## Motivation

The previous ROCm path used `topk.hip` generated by hipifying `topk.cu`. Its fp16 coarse key can collapse a large part of a real indexer row into one bucket, and overflowing the candidate buffer can silently drop valid winners. On captured GLM-5.2 logits, selected-value recall fell as low as 0.53.

The new native HIP kernel keeps the selection exact by refining the full fp32 key and rescanning the row when the tie buffer overflows. It reaches 1.0 selected-value recall against `torch.topk` on the same inputs.

## Performance vs. the original `topk.hip`

Baseline `old generated` is the original ROCm `topk.hip` produced from `topk.cu`, rebuilt from xiaobochen-amd/sglang `main` at [`92562f066`](https://github.com/xiaobochen-amd/sglang/commit/92562f0660b1c05d2de5b823e8b471be8def44cd). `new native` is the tracked `topk.hip` in this PR. Measurements are on MI355X (gfx950), graph replay, width 131,072, 100,500 live positions, top-k 2,048, page size 1. Times are microseconds per call; lower is better.

```
distribution  batch   old generated   new native   speedup
tiny              1            95.2         31.6      3.02x
tiny              2            95.5         30.0      3.18x
tiny              4            95.6         31.2      3.06x
tiny              8            96.0         31.4      3.06x
tiny             14            95.8         32.7      2.93x
tiny             32            96.3         36.9      2.61x
tiny             64            98.4         48.1      2.04x
tiny            128           119.9         58.5      2.05x
tiny            256           121.9         62.7      1.94x

diffuse           1            54.3         31.6      1.72x
diffuse           2            55.1         30.9      1.78x
diffuse           4            55.5         31.5      1.76x
diffuse           8            56.7         31.7      1.79x
diffuse          14            56.4         33.1      1.70x
diffuse          32            56.3         36.6      1.54x
diffuse          64            77.3         49.4      1.56x
diffuse         128            96.7         59.1      1.64x
diffuse         256           103.4         63.2      1.64x

clustered         1           160.9        102.2      1.57x
clustered         2           161.6        101.0      1.60x
clustered         4           161.8        102.1      1.59x
clustered         8           162.1        103.4      1.57x
clustered        14           162.0        104.9      1.54x
clustered        32           162.7        111.4      1.46x
clustered        64           162.6        122.9      1.32x
clustered       128           185.9        169.0      1.10x
clustered       256           186.9        174.2      1.07x
```

On captured GLM-5.2 decode shapes, row splitting gives a further 2.1-2.8x speedup over the original generated kernel.

## Comparison with `topk_v2`

This is a same-run comparison against the current JIT [`topk_v2.cuh`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/topk_v2.cuh) on MI355X (gfx950). Both kernels use graph replay, width 131,072, 100,500 live positions, top-k 2,048, and page size 1. Times are microseconds per call; lower is better.

### GLM-5 ROCm shape and score distribution

The synthetic sweep uses a GLM-5 long-context decode-like shape: float32 scores `[B, 131072]`, live length 100,500, top-k 2,048, and a page-size-1 transform, with `B` swept from 1 to 256. Separate logits captured from an actual GLM-5.2-MXFP4 ROCm decode had 20 score rows per call and live context up to 134,849 tokens.

The real captured scores were approximately 0.04-180, not tiny `1e-16` values. They were nevertheless highly concentrated under the fp16 coarse key: an 8-bit fp16 key populated only 4-126 bins, and the largest bin held 6%-88% of a row. Whether the top-2,048 boundary landed inside that dominant bin varied by call.

The sweep distributions should therefore be read as follows:

- `diffuse`: broad random control; less concentrated than captured GLM-5 logits.
- `tiny`: scale-invariance stress (`1e-16 * randn`); not the literal GLM-5 value range.
- `clustered`: single-bin-style overflow stress; more concentrated than typical captures.

Real GLM-5 lies between `diffuse` and the synthetic `clustered` case in coarse-bin concentration. The actual captures are the reason candidate-buffer overflow must remain exact, while `tiny` separately verifies that fp16 conversion cannot erase score ordering.

```
distribution  batch   native topk.hip   topk_v2
tiny              1              31.5       73.1
tiny              2              30.1       73.2
tiny              4              30.8       73.1
tiny              8              30.9       73.2
tiny             14              32.5       73.2
tiny             32              37.1       73.3
tiny             64              48.8       73.3
tiny            128              58.7       74.6
tiny            256              63.2       76.1

diffuse           1              31.9       34.2
diffuse           2              31.0       34.2
diffuse           4              31.3       34.5
diffuse           8              31.6       34.5
diffuse          14              33.1       34.7
diffuse          32              36.6       35.1
diffuse          64              49.5       38.1
diffuse         128              59.2       39.6
diffuse         256              62.9       46.5

clustered         1             102.2      109.2
clustered         2             101.0      109.4
clustered         4             102.2      109.5
clustered         8             103.1      109.6
clustered        14             105.1      109.6
clustered        32             111.1      109.6
clustered        64             122.9      109.9
clustered       128             168.9      110.6
clustered       256             174.5      111.0
```

For tiny scores, the native HIP kernel is 1.20-2.43x faster. On diffuse scores it is 1.05-1.10x faster through batch 14, while `topk_v2` becomes 1.04-1.49x faster from batch 32 onward. For shorter diffuse rows (4K-65K live positions), `topk_v2` is 1.24-2.96x faster because its register and one-block streaming paths avoid the native kernel's row-split launch overhead.

Correctness is not equivalent. `topk_v2` uses an fp16 coarse histogram and caps the threshold-bin candidate buffer at 2,048 without an overflow rescan. Selected-value multiset recall against `torch.topk` at batch 1 is:

```
distribution   native topk.hip   topk_v2
tiny                    1.0000     0.0420
diffuse                 1.0000     1.0000
clustered               1.0000     0.0220
```

Therefore the apparent `topk_v2` advantage on high-batch clustered inputs is not a valid like-for-like speedup: it does not return the exact top-k on that distribution. The native HIP kernel rescans the row when the candidate buffer overflows and remains exact.

## Test plan

- [x] ROCm `sgl-kernel` build for gfx950 using the tracked native `topk.hip`
- [x] `pytest python/sglang/kernels/aot/tests/test_topk.py -q` - 161 passed
- [x] pre-commit checks on all changed files
- [x] mixed-device launch and rejection coverage
- [x] both one-block and row-split paths

title: [diffusion] loader: filter duplicate precision variants across custom loaders
author: dujifeng
body:
## Motivation

Some Diffusers-style checkpoints contain both canonical safetensors files and precision-specific copies, for example `model.safetensors` and `model.fp16.safetensors`. Loading both can produce duplicate tensor names or make the selected value depend on file order.

The original fix covered transformers and text encoders, but the same checkpoint discovery pattern exists in other customized component loaders.

## Modifications

- Define precision-variant selection in the shared weight-source layer and apply it by default during local safetensors discovery.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Accumulate chunked LoRA merges with addmm
author: Levius-Fubuki
body:
## Purpose

The 2D diffusion LoRA merge path currently materializes `B @ A` for every chunk and then launches a separate in-place add. At the configured 32 MiB chunk limit, this creates a large temporary allocation and an additional kernel launch.

This PR:

- uses `Tensor.addmm_` to accumulate each 2D LoRA product directly into the base weight;
- preserves the existing chunk-size and scaling policies, including ordered multi-adapter accumulation;
- adds coverage for FP32/FP16/BF16, contiguous and transposed non-contiguous tensors, negative strength, `alpha / rank` scaling, and forced multi-chunk execution;
- checks in a standalone CUDA microbenchmark that validates numerical parity before measuring latency and peak allocation.

This does not change LoRA loading, merge precision policy, stacked/greater-than-2D fallback behavior, non-tensor handling, or model-specific behavior. It uses a standard PyTorch matrix primitive with no device or compute-capability branch, consistent with the torch-native LoRA optimization merged in #20562.

## Test Plan

### LoRA regression tests

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_lora_inference_mode.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_lora_commit_as_base.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_fused_lora_compose.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_lora_merge_cache.py
```

### Formatting and lint

```bash
pre-commit run black-jupyter --files \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/lora/linear.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_lora_inference_mode.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/manual/bench_lora_merge_addmm.py
pre-commit run isort --files <same-files>
pre-commit run ruff --files <same-files>
git diff --check
```

### RTX 4090 operator benchmark

```bash
python python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/manual/bench_lora_merge_addmm.py \
  --warmups 50 --repetitions 500 \
  --output /tmp/lora-merge-addmm.csv \
  --profile-output /tmp/lora-merge-addmm-profiler.txt
```

Hardware/software: NVIDIA RTX 4090 (SM89), driver 595.71.05, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. No configuration changes.

Each of 30 dtype/shape/rank cases ran seven alternating-order rounds. The table shows representative paired medians; latency is in microseconds and allocation is the extra PyTorch peak during one merge.

| Dtype | Shape | Rank | Scale | Old / New (us) | Speedup | Old / New allocation | Max abs diff |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| BF16 | 320x320 | 4 | 1.0 | 29.805 / 20.484 | 1.455x | 0.20 / 0 MiB | 0 |
| BF16 | 4096x4096 | 32 | -0.5 | 42.408 / 21.207 | 2.000x | 32 / 0 MiB | 1.53e-5 |
| BF16 | 12288x4096 | 64 | 1.0 | 428.542 / 225.182 | 1.903x | 64 / 0 MiB | 3.05e-5 |
| FP16 | 4096x4096 | 32 | -0.5 | 42.899 / 21.074 | 2.036x | 32 / 0 MiB | 3.81e-6 |
| FP32 | 1280x1280 | 8 | 1.0 | 29.098 / 23.919 | 1.217x | 6.25 / 0 MiB | 9.31e-10 |
| FP32 | 12288x4096 | 4 | 0.25 | 1284.776 / 484.248 | 2.653x | 64 / 0 MiB | 4.66e-10 |

Across all 30 cases:

- geometric-mean speedup: `1.695x`
- minimum case speedup: `1.217x`
- maximum case speedup: `2.653x`
- regressed cases: `0/30`
- candidate extra peak allocation: `0` bytes in every case
- maximum old/new difference: BF16 `3.05e-5`, FP16 `3.81e-6`, FP32 `9.31e-10`

The profiler changes the hot-path operator sequence from `matmul/mm + add_` to `addmm_`.

`torch.compile`, CUDA Graph replay, and concurrency scaling are not applicable: this helper is decorated with `@torch.no_grad()` and runs while loading or merging adapters, outside the compiled model forward and serving request path. The claim is limited to merge latency and temporary allocation, not end-to-end generation throughput.

title: perf(lfm2): fuse gating and short convolution on SM90
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

LFM2-MoE's short-convolution path currently materializes `B * x`, transposes
the result for the generic causal-convolution kernel, and then materializes
`C * conv(B * x)`. On the BF16 TP1 LFM2.5-8B-A1B serving profile, these
separate launches and the transpose are a measurable prefill bottleneck.

## Modifications

- Add SM90 Triton prefill and decode kernels that fuse both gates with the
  width-3 depthwise convolution while preserving the two BF16 materialization
  points and in-place recurrent-state update.
- Dispatch only for the qualified CUDA/BF16/no-bias/width-3/hidden-size-2048
  domain; all other calls retain the existing causal-conv implementation.
- Keep target verification on the existing implementation.
- Add coverage for variable-length prefill, decode, padded slots, dispatch
  guards, recurrent state, and CUDA Graph replay with changed live inputs.

## Accuracy Tests

On one NVIDIA H200:

```text
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 PYTHONPATH=python pytest -q \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/mamba/test_lfm_short_conv.py
4 passed in 14.69s
```

- Recurrent state is bit-exact against the existing causal-conv path.
- Active BF16 outputs are numerically equivalent. Decode mean/p99/max absolute
  error: `0.00149 / 0.03125 / 0.0625`; prefill: `0.00128 / 0.015625 / 0.25`.
- Fixed-shape serving produced identical generated text for 8/8 retained
