title: Fix overflow in legacy and v1 DSA top-k selectors
author: ormandj
body:
## Motivation

Legacy DSA top-k selection can drop candidates when a coarse radix bin reaches its fixed buffer capacity, selecting lower-scoring tokens before full scores are compared. This patch covers the DeepSeek-V4 JIT v1, legacy CUDA AOT and DeepSeek-V4 AOT selectors. KPool JIT already rescans overflowing bins on main (#39273), so its kernel is unchanged here and only gains regression coverage.

## Modifications

Keep normal-bin selection. For a coarse bin larger than the stash, find the exact FP32 cutoff one key byte per row scan; each scan also emits the scores the previous byte placed strictly above the cutoff, and the last scan emits the remaining ones and the cutoff ties (six scans of the row including the coarse histogram, down from seven). Preserve page mapping, `-1` padding and synchronization around shared-memory reuse. The JIT header takes its CUDA/HIP types from `sgl_kernel/utils.cuh`. Retain the additive ROCm tests. Co-authored with Benjamin Oldenburg (@bold84).

Add a CUDA test for `topk_transform_paged` (JIT v1) covering threshold bins on both sides of the 8192-entry stash, strictly higher values ahead of an oversized bin, cutoff ties, clusters that separate only in one of the lower three FP32 key bytes, runtime `topk` values, short rows, score rows padded past their lengths, a noncontiguous score view, and both raw and page-mapped outputs. Add KPool regressions at its 4096-entry stash for oversized and exact-capacity bins, cutoff ties, clusters that separate in the lower three key bytes, padded rows and page-table expansion, registered for CUDA and AMD.

The v2 changes are removed from this PR so the legacy/v1 fix can be reviewed and merged independently. I will submit the v2 changes in a separate PR.

## Accuracy Tests

On RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), a combined build passed 12 KPool JIT tests/38 subtests and 7 focused legacy CUDA AOT cases, including oversized coarse bins. One ROCm-only case was skipped. Those results predate the rebase onto main's KPool implementation.

On RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), torch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0, at this branch, `test_topk_v1.py` passed (15 tests) and `test_dsa_kpool_topk_transform.py` passed against main's KPool kernel (12 tests, 38 subtests). Against main's unpatched `topk_v1.cuh`, 9 of the 15 v1 tests fail (the overflow cases). The AOT header was compiled for sm_120 in a standalone harness and matched a CPU reference on random rows, single-bin rows above the stash, and strictly higher values plus cutoff ties. The AOT test matrix and ROCm tests have not been run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Rows whose coarse threshold bin exceeds the stash take six row scans; other rows are unchanged. No speed benchmark was run.

## Checklist

- [x] Format changed code.
- [x] Run regression tests described above.

Developed with AI assistance.

title: [unified-memory] Speculative decoding on the unified memory pool: translate every read and write path
author: caihuali95
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42753
* #40492
* #40491
* #37628
* __->__ #37627

## Motivation

Under `--enable-unified-memory` a KV slot has two names: the **virtual** id the
scheduler allocates and the **physical** id where the slot currently sits, which
compaction can change. A non-speculative forward already routes every read and
write through `KVIndexTranslator`, so the two stay consistent.

Speculative decoding did not. Verify reads a **widened** window — the request's
live prefix plus the draft tokens being checked — and several backends built that
window's page table straight from `req_to_token` rows, or from a captured graph's
persistent buffer, without translating. On a plain pool that is invisible, since
the two id spaces coincide. On the unified pool it silently reads the wrong KV,
and because speculative decoding *rejects* wrong tokens rather than crashing, it
surfaces as degraded output rather than as a failure.

That is why `--enable-unified-memory` refuses every speculative algorithm except
DSPARK, and DSPARK only on the MLA verify family and Triton.

## Modifications

The speculative verify read paths of Triton, flashmla, flashinfer and fa3 go
through `KVIndexTranslator`, and those backends are admitted for DSPARK verify.

**Translator.** The index-table builders take a `seq_len_delta`, and
`widened_index_table()` builds a verify read covering the live prefix *and* the
draft tail in one translated table. Its width comes from the live lengths (a
DSPARK verify batch carries `seq_lens_cpu` already expanded by the window and the
live lengths on `spec_info.live_seq_lens_cpu`) and never exceeds the
`req_to_token` row it reads. The speculative info types gather their CSR
arguments through `fill_packed_read_stream`.

**Read-table kernel.** `build_kv_read_table`'s CUDA kernel stops each row at the
table's width, as the CPU path does, so a widened window that outruns a
fixed-width table (a captured fa3 verify near the context limit) can no longer
write into the next row.

**Backends.** Each is converted on its own terms: flashmla's eager spec branches
(filled through the translator when its reads come out physical,
`reads_are_translated`, the predicate the fill asserts),
flashinfer's verify gather (from the sliding-window id space, not the full one),
and fa3's paths — the eager verify read, the captured verify page table (with the
captured build reading the same mode→delta map as the eager one), and the
draft-extend rebuild. Under translation fa3 records no in-graph draft-extend
gather: the draft-extend runners call `init_forward_metadata_in_graph`
unconditionally at capture, and a recorded raw `req_to_token` gather would
overwrite the translated tables on every replay.

**Gate.** The DSPARK allow-list admits flashmla, flashinfer and fa3 alongside
Triton and the MLA verify family. Only the target's prefill/decode pair is
checked: a DSPARK draft owns a pool indexed directly by virtual id, so its
translator is a passthrough and its backend — which a model hook may declare, as
Kimi-Linear / Kimi-K3 + DSPARK on SM100 declares `trtllm_mha` — needs no
translation. Under `--dcp-size > 1` flashinfer stays refused for DSPARK verify,
since its verify CSR path has no DCP read translation. The per-arm tree-drafting
refusals collapse into one unconditional `speculative_eagle_topk in (None, 1)`
check next to the algorithm allow-list.

One prerequisite fix rides along; it is described under *Notes for reviewers*.

## Accuracy Tests

The DSpark draft loads with `--speculative-draft-load-format dummy` — random
weights — so every proposal is rejected and accept length is pinned at 1.00 by
construction. **These runs check that the verify rails are functionally correct,
not that speculative decoding is fast or accurate with a real drafter.** A
translation bug on the verify read path corrupts the target's own output, since
speculative decoding is lossless only when verify is correct, so accuracy is the
signal.

**B200 (SM100), this head.** Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct, TP2 (the cookbook
deploys it at TP4), DSPARK with a dummy draft, GSM8K at n=200:

| configuration | GSM8K |
|---|---|
| no unified memory, trtllm_mla | 0.905 |
| unified, trtllm_mla (draft on `trtllm_mha`, declared by the Kimi hook) | 0.910 |
| unified, flashinfer | 0.895 |

All three at `--mem-fraction-static 0.45`, accept length 1.00 by construction. The
first two pin the Kimi-Linear + DSPARK + SM100 configuration whose model hook
declares the draft's backend; the unified arms stay within the run-to-run floor of
the control.

**B200, greedy parity, this head.** Temperature 0, 24 ShareGPT prompts × 128
tokens, one request at a time, token ids and logprobs compared with `main` at the
stack's base: Qwen3.5-4B on flashinfer, spec-off on the static and the unified
pool, and with its MTP head (EAGLE 3/1/4) on the static pool, gives identical tokens
and logprobs (max |Δlogprob| 0).

**H20 (SM90), the pre-rebase revision of this PR.** The verify rails were scored on
Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B with DSPARK on Triton, fa3, flashinfer and flashmla against a
spec-off control on the same backend; Qwen3.5-9B, gpt-oss-20b and Falcon-H1-7B ran
spec-off as unified-vs-baseline controls, and a `cache × schedule × page size`
grid added Inkling, Inkling-Small and Llama-3.1-8B. GSM8K at n=200, unified
against a baseline on the same model, backend and configuration:

- verify rails: median **−0.50 pt**, spread sd 2.31 pt
- broader spec-off grid: median **+0.50 pt**, spread sd 2.03 pt

Both spreads sit under the measured same-arm floor of ±2.9 pt. The widest single
deviation, −6.5 pt on gpt-oss-20b with fa3, is smaller than the 7.0 pt spread of
that configuration's baseline arm across two backends.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

H20, the pre-rebase revision: unified against baseline, median inter-token
latency **+0.43%** in the product configuration and **+1.24%** in a verify-rails
probe at `page_size 1`. Split by page size, the overhead falls from +1.29% at 1
to +0.12% at 256, consistent with translate work proportional to
`seq_len / page_size`. With a dummy draft these numbers only show the rails add no
per-step cost; they are not a speculative-decoding speedup measurement.

B200, adjacent heads: Qwen3.5-4B on flashinfer, arms interleaved on one GPU, median
inter-token latency with one request in flight — spec-off unified 2.53 ms on `main`
and 2.54 ms here; MTP on the static pool 1.24 ms on both. `max_total_num_tokens`
is identical (1,381,150 spec-off, 1,592,686 MTP). Throughput at 32 concurrent
requests stays within ±2%, the size of the run-order effect on this box (the arm
of a pair that runs first gains about 2%).

fa3's captured target-verify metadata now goes through `normal_decode_set_metadata`,
the kernel fa3's decode replay already uses, instead of five eager ops. fa3 does
not run on SM100, so that path was benchmarked on its own (B200, bs 1–256, page
size 1 and 64): its outputs are bit-identical to `main`'s, the eager per-step cost
falls from 39 µs to 16–20 µs, and GPU time rises by 1–10 µs at bs ≥ 128, where the
kernel's serial prefix sum costs more than `torch.cumsum`.

## Notes for reviewers

**One commit has no reachable path here, deliberately.** It gates the Falcon-H1
causal-conv on `forward_mode.is_target_verify()`, fixing an assertion that fires
on `main` whenever a speculative algorithm reaches a Falcon-H1 target verify
without the token-major layout flag set. No admitted algorithm can pair with
Falcon-H1 on this branch; the line becomes live once chain drafting is admitted
in the follow-up.

**A DSPARK draft's private pool on a unified mamba host is not priced by the boot
solve**, here as on `main`: the unified buffer takes the whole profiled KV budget
and the draft pool, sized to the virtual id span, is allocated on top of it. On
B200 Kimi-Linear TP2 at `--mem-fraction-static 0.6` that does not fit (the draft
pool alone is ~82 GB); 0.45 does.

**Not yet validated end to end:** cutedsl_mla and tokenspeed_mla on SM100, and
`--dcp-size > 1` with DSPARK. The MHA and sliding-window spec-verify paths are not
reachable with the only DSpark draft checkpoint available, so those host kinds are
covered spec-off and by the unit tests.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [unified-memory] Fuse the draft model's KV into the target's page envelope (mechanism)
author: caihuali95
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42753
* #40492
* #40491
* __->__ #37628
* #37627

## Motivation

A speculative draft model owns a KV pool of its own, separate from the target's.
That means a second allocator, a second id space, a second set of page tables, and
memory reserved up front for the draft that the target can never use.

Under `--enable-unified-memory` the target's slot entries already have room. This
PR puts the draft's K/V rows **inside** the host entry, after the host's own parts:

```
[ K_0 | V_0 | ... | K_n | V_n | dK_0 | dV_0 | ... | dK_m | dV_m | pad ]
  \___________ host ___________/ \_________ draft _________/
```

One slot id then addresses both. One allocation, one free, and one whole-page
relocation carry the target's KV and the draft's together — a compaction move gets
the draft bytes for free instead of needing a second, separately-indexed move.

**This PR builds that mechanism and leaves it unreachable.** The admission gate is
untouched — `speculative_algorithm in (None, "DSPARK")` — and the fuse decision
additionally requires an EAGLE-family algorithm, which DSPARK is not. Admitting the
algorithms that can fuse is #40491's job, which keeps this PR reviewable as
mechanism and the behavior change it enables in a diff of its own.

## Modifications

**Layout and pool.** `DenseDraftRegion` describes the draft's K/V geometry as two
more parts of the host entry at `draft_offset_in_entry()`, and
`UnifiedDraftKVPool` presents those parts to the draft as an ordinary KV cache
whose write doors take physical ids only (`requires_physical_write_loc`). The unit
of the region's layer dimension is a **lane**, not a layer, because the two draft
head shapes place runners oppositely: a replicated head gives every runner all the
draft's layers and so needs a range each (3 runners × 2 layers = 6 lanes), while a
per-depth head gives each runner one depth (8 layers across 2 runners = 2 lanes).
The runners' ranges must tile the region exactly, in runner order, which
`FusedDraftPlacement.__post_init__` asserts.

**Id space.** The fused-draft disposition on `KVIndexTranslator`: a fused draft
runner translates through the **target's** v2p table, exactly as the target does.
A dense fused draft has no second id space, so its window index table falls back
to the one dense table.

**Multi-step draft decode.** `generate_draft_decode_kv_indices` translates the ids
it copies when handed the runner's v2p table (`KVIndexTranslator.full_flat_v2p()`),
in all four multi-step containers; a negative id lands on the page-0 sink, as
`translate_kv_loc` does. Static pools pass `None` and keep the raw copy.

**Boot.** The target resolves the placement from the draft's config read in draft
mode (`SpecAuxHiddenStateConfig.draft_model_config` / `draft_kv_num_layers`).
That reading feeds only the fused decision: a private draft pool keeps its
historical size, so a path-less MTP deployment's token budget is unchanged. The
pool solve prices the exact fused entry — host rows plus draft rows plus alignment
pad, through the same spec the pool factory builds — in the cell size and in the
bytes the unified pool is handed, for both the ratio solve and the SWA chunk-cap
solve. `_init_pools` runs twice per server: the target pass stores the placement on
the `UnifiedKVPool`, the draft pass reads it back and binds the draft worker to the
region.

## Scope: full-attention draft KV only

The fused region is dense and full-attention. `place_fused_draft` declines, with
the reason logged, and the draft keeps its private pool over the unified virtual
id space, whenever the draft needs something the dense region cannot express:

| draft shape | status here |
|---|---|
| full-attention K/V, symmetric rows | **fused** |
| asymmetric K/V rows (`head_dim != v_head_dim`) | declines to a private pool |
| sliding-window layers of its own | declines to a private pool |
| recurrent / Mamba state layers of its own | declines to a private pool |
| K/V rows not a multiple of the 16-B part alignment | declines to a private pool |
| explicit `--speculative-draft-kv-cache-dtype` unlike the host's | declines to a private pool |

A draft whose `auto` KV dtype resolves unlike the host's is only known once the
draft runner loads; it then fails the bind with a message naming the flag, instead
of reading the host's rows as another dtype.

## Accuracy Tests

Because no draft can fuse on this branch, this tests the claim that the machinery
is **dormant**: the host entry layout changed and the translator gained a
disposition, and both run on every forward regardless.

H20, the pre-rebase revision of this PR: GSM8K at n=200, unified against the same
build without it on the same model, backend and configuration — **26 matched
pairs, median +0.25 pt, sd 2.18 pt**. The two pairs more than 2.9 pt (the measured
run-to-run floor) below baseline are both gpt-oss-20b, whose baseline alone spans
6.5 pt in the same run; excluding it, 22 pairs, median +0.75 pt, worst −1.5 pt.

B200, this head: a path-less MTP deployment off the unified pool keeps main's
token budget — Qwen3.5-0.8B, EAGLE (3 steps, topk 1, 4 draft tokens), flashinfer,
`--mem-fraction-static 0.5`: `max_total_num_tokens` 5,233,400 here against
5,253,582 on main, the difference being the two runs' free memory at load
(176.97 vs 177.58 GB); GSM8K 0.330 on both.

B200, greedy parity, this head: Qwen3.5-4B on flashinfer, spec-off on the unified
pool and MTP on the static pool, temperature 0, 24 prompts × 128 tokens one at a
time — identical tokens and logprobs to `main` (max |Δlogprob| 0), and the same
`max_total_num_tokens` (1,381,150 / 1,592,686).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

H20, the pre-rebase revision: median inter-token latency, unified against the same
build without it, speculative decoding off — **20 matched pairs, median +0.48%**,
every measurement between −1.9% and +2.2%. That is the unified pool's standing
overhead on this matrix, not a cost this PR adds.

B200, adjacent heads, the same unified spec-off configuration (Qwen3.5-4B,
flashinfer, interleaved on one GPU): median inter-token latency with one request in
flight 2.53 ms on `main`, 2.54 ms on #37627, 2.53 ms here.

## Notes for reviewers

**Nothing on this branch can reach a fused draft, deliberately.** The new code
paths are exercised here by unit tests — geometry, placement tiling, translator
disposition, boot-time pricing, the draft-worker binding, and the translated
multi-step kernel — and end to end by #40491's GPU runs.

**Lane count is not layer count**, in either direction, and the two draft head
shapes disagree about which way. The module docstring in
`mem_cache/layout/fused_draft.py` states the convention; `lanes_for(runner)` is per
runner, which is what makes `len(full_ids) == len(full_lanes)` hold at bind.

title: [Bugfix] Key CUDA graph dedup signatures on kernel function identity
author: cctry
body:
## Motivation

`cudaGraphExecUpdate` keeps the exec's originally instantiated values for launch attributes that `cuGraphKernelNodeGetAttribute` cannot read back (e.g. `CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_PREFERRED_CLUSTER_DIMENSION`) and reports success instead of `cudaGraphExecUpdateErrorAttributesChanged`. We root-caused a deterministic hang on GB300 to this: updating an exec from a cuBLASLt kernel captured with preferred cluster (4,1,1) to a variant without fallback-cluster support launches it under 4-CTA clusters and deadlocks in an mbarrier wait.

The dedup registry keys exec groups on kernel name + geometry + queryable attributes, but names are not identities: JIT compilers (triton, `torch.compile`) can emit different kernels with identical names from different modules, so an exec-update could still cross functions whose capture-only attributes differ.

## Modifications

Add the kernel/function handles to `kernel_node_payload` so only launches of the same loaded function share a graph exec. One-line diff; dedup coverage is unchanged for real workloads since repeated captures of the same kernel reuse the same handles.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Verified on GB300: same-kernel captures still produce equal signatures (dedup preserved); two modules loaded from identical PTX (same name/geometry, different functions) now produce different signatures.

title: [AMD] Parallelize aiter spec-decode KV index building over token blocks
author: zijiecode
body:
## Motivation

`generate_draft_decode_kv_indices` and `create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton` gather each request's token-level KV indices into a flat CSR stream with one Triton program per request (× draft step × topk), and each program crawls the whole context serially in a scalar loop. At long-context speculative decoding this becomes a per-iteration cost that scales linearly with batch context. 

## Modifications

Add token-block parallelism to both kernels while keeping the historical launch shapes:

- `generate_draft_decode_kv_indices` gains a `NUM_STEPS: tl.constexpr = 0` parameter. With `NUM_STEPS == 0` (default) the kernel is the historical one: the same 128-wide copy loop and load order, with the token-block branches folded away at compile time. With `NUM_STEPS > 0`, the first grid axis packs `(step, token_block)` as `step + NUM_STEPS * block`, each program copies a strided subset of its request's index range with 512-wide blocks, and the per-step tail (draft-token entries and the `kv_indptr` update) is computed on token block 0 only.
- `create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton` gains a `TOKEN_BLOCK_PARALLEL: tl.constexpr = False` switch. When set, the kernel reads a second grid axis (`tl.program_id(1)` / `tl.num_programs(1)`) and stripes its copy loop across it; by default it compiles the historical one-program-per-request loop, so the existing 1D launch sites are unchanged.
- The block count is sized by the parallelism the launch already has: `kv_indices_num_token_blocks()` tops the grid up to ~512 programs, caps at one block per 8192 tokens of table width, and returns 1 whenever the base grid is already wide, so large batches and large topk keep their old launch. Blocks that own no copy work exit before the O(bs) prefix-sum.
- Enablement is confined to where the cost shows up: the aiter backend's speculative-decoding paths (draft decode, draft_extend, target_verify) on servers with `max_context_len >= 32k` (`_KV_INDEX_BLOCKS_MIN_CONTEXT`). These sites pass `TOKEN_BLOCK_PARALLEL` / `NUM_STEPS` only when the helper picks more than one token block, so a single-block launch still runs the historical program. The aiter backend's normal decode and prefill call sites, and every other backend, do not pass either switch.

Generated-code check for the default paths, old kernel vs this PR with identical launch arguments, on MI355X (ROCm 7.2.4 image) and GB300 (Triton 3.7.1): the draft kernel at `NUM_STEPS == 0` and `create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton` on a 1D grid (`ENTRY_PAGE_SIZE` 1 and 16) produce identical LLVM IR on both; the only differences in the final ISA/PTX are DWARF debug strings (source path and line numbers). On GB300 the default launches are also bit-identical to main over sentinel-filled buffers (60 old-vs-new comparisons across lengths 0..100k, topk 1/4, page 1/16, int32/int64) at 1.00x the main kernels' time.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, temperature 0, max new tokens 2048; Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, TP2, MI355X, real EAGLE decoding (3 steps, top-k 1, 4 draft tokens), `--attention-backend aiter --page-size 16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`:

| KV index building | Accuracy | Correct | Invalid |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| main | 92.6% | 1222/1319 | 6/1319 |
| this PR (run 1) | 92.8% | 1224/1319 | 6/1319 |

GPQA diamond (198 questions, 8 repeats, 1584 samples):

| KV index building | Mean score | 
|---|---:|
| this PR  | 0.881 | 
| reference: Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B model card | 0.884 | 


Unit test: `test/registered/kernel/speculative/test_spec_kv_indices_grid.py` checks 1D-vs-2D bit equality over sentinel-filled buffers (catching unwritten and overwritten regions) across lengths 0/1/511/512/513/8191/8192/8193/100k, ragged and skewed batches, topk 1/4, page_size 1/16, `NUM_STEPS` 2/3/4, and int32/int64 index dtypes, plus a Python reference that validates the draft kernel's prefix, extension (both the token-granular and the page-granular topk layout) and `kv_indptr` contents directly. The suite passes on MI355X and B200.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel microbench (MI355X, bs 8 × ~105k-131k context, 3 draft steps, topk 1; outputs bit-identical to the 1D launch):

| kernel | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `generate_draft_decode_kv_indices` | 124 us | 15 us |
| `create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton` | 84 us | 30 us |



End-to-end agentic test A/B (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B FP4, MI355X TP2, EAGLE 3+4, aiperf trace replay of a 256k-context agentic dataset at concurrency 16):

| metric | baseline | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| TPOT p50 | 6.23 ms | 5.87 ms (−5.8%) |
| TPOT p90 | 9.56 ms | 8.97 ms (−6.2%) |
| interactivity p50 (tok/s/user) | 160.5 | 170.2 (+6.0%) |
| total throughput | 59.8k tok/s | 60.2k tok/s (+0.7%) |

title: [AMD] Fix FP4 indexer OOR
author: RolaoDenthu
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
On MI355X, DeepSeek-V4-Pro with the FP4 indexer aborts under long-running agentic workloads:
```
HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES ... Available Free mem : 0 MB
  at fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:1353 fused_append_shared_experts
```
The indexer allocates a fresh torch.empty(num_tokens, max_seq_len) for logits on every layer of every forward. If no cached block is large enough to reuse, it has to allocate a new one. Torch does release the tensor when it's done, but only back to its own caching allocator — the driver still sees that memory as taken. And max_seq_len follows the context length, which in an agentic session only grows, so each request is slightly larger than the last, the older blocks never get a chance to be reused, and they just pile up in the pool. Driver-visible memory drains block by block until the allocation fails with out of resources.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
1. Pooled fixed-size logits buffer (fp4_indexer_hip.py)

Prefill logits are served as a view into one pre-allocated block instead of a fresh torch.empty per call. The request size becomes constant, so the block is always reused and nothing strands. Decode keeps the plain allocation: its rectangle is bounded by the capture shapes and lives in the graph memory pool, and creating the pooled block mid-capture would hand graph-pool memory to later replays. Budget is set by SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_LOGITS_BUDGET_MB (default 2048).

2. Row chunking (indexer.py)

A fixed block alone isn't enough — a batch that doesn't fit would fall back to a dynamic allocation and start stranding again. logits_rows_per_chunk() reports how many rows fit, and the FP4 prefill path loops over row chunks, running each chunk's top-k before reusing the block. This decouples peak scratch from context length. Rows are scored and reduced independently, so the result is elementwise-identical to a single pass; the single-chunk case (the common one) passes the whole batch through without slicing. The KV payload/scale getters are hoisted out of the loop since they await the layer's KV transfer, and topk_v2 metadata is re-planned per chunk because the cached plan routes rows by their index in the full range.

## Accuracy Tests

## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: [diffusion] perf: FastH3 8-Step V2 native support, native Blackwell VSA, batched H3 VAE decode
author: kevin-mii
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #37480 (FastH3 with the VSA-H3 backend). This PR:

- moves native FastH3 support to the current checkpoint, [FastVideo/FastVideo-FastH3-8-Step-V2](https://huggingface.co/FastVideo/FastVideo-FastH3-8-Step-V2), which replaces the 4-step preview;
- adds FastVideo's native Blackwell VSA kernel;
- speeds up the rest of the request path: denoise, VAE decode, and MP4 output. Encoding the MP4 while the VAE decodes is left to #41819.

The target is the workload from the [UniServe FastH3 post](https://haoailab.com/blogs/uniserve-fasth3/): 1344×768 at 24 fps with audio, 1K / 10K-token prompts, 5 / 10 / 15 s, latency measured from submission to the last byte of the MP4.

## Results: 4× GB300, FastH3 8-Step V2

Setup:
- Recipe: `sglang serve --model-path FastVideo/FastVideo-FastH3-8-Step-V2 --num-gpus 4 --component-attention-backends transformer=video_sparse_attn_h3`.
- Defaults (`quality: "extra-high"`, sparsity 0.8), BF16, eager, Ulysses 4, `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0`.
- Workload: 72 requests at concurrency 1 after one warm request per shape. That is six scene families × {1K, 10K} tokens × {5, 10, 15} s × two seeds.
- Every prompt is unique, so no conditioning cache hits.
- **Measured with streaming on:** the MP4 was encoded while the VAE decoded, as #41819 does; that encoder is not in this PR. Without it, E2E is about 0.2 s higher at 5 s and 0.5 s higher at 10 s (5.39 s and 11.24 s in a spot check).
- E2E is the client wall clock from submission to the last MP4 byte. All 72 outputs are valid: 1344×768 H.264 at 24 fps with 32 kHz stereo AAC.

| Shape (median of 12) | Text | Denoise (8 fwd) | Decode | **E2E** | UniServe (blog, 4× GB200) | SGLang (blog, 4× GB200) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 5 s / 1K | 0.10 s | 3.84 s | 0.56 s | **5.20 s** | 5.62 s | 8.50 s |
| 10 s / 1K | 0.10 s | 8.45 s | 1.12 s | **10.74 s** | 11.73 s | 17.81 s |
| 15 s / 1K | 0.10 s | 14.85 s | 1.72 s | **18.24 s** | 20.27 s | 29.36 s |
| 5 s / 10K | 0.18 s | 6.31 s | 0.55 s | **7.90 s** | 8.80 s | 11.56 s |
| 10 s / 10K | 0.18 s | 12.35 s | 1.12 s | **14.98 s** | 16.75 s | 22.52 s |
| 15 s / 10K | 0.18 s | 20.28 s | 1.67 s | **24.01 s** | 27.31 s | 35.80 s |
| p50 / p90 / p95 (72 req) | | | | **12.94 / 23.94 / 24.08 s** | 14.24 / 27.30 / 27.32 s | 20.19 / 35.79 / 35.81 s |

The blog columns are from different hardware (GB200) and a different prompt set, the blog's frozen manifest, which is not public. My prompt set has the same shape. Treat them as a reference, not a same-machine A/B. Peak memory is 94–100 GB/GPU.

Where the latency went on this host, from the same V2 checkpoint on this branch before the new commits (10 s / 1K):

| Change | E2E |
| --- | ---: |
| Merged branch, V2 checkpoint | 14.62 s |
| + system ffmpeg instead of imageio's aarch64 4.2.2 build | 13.05 s |
| + batched VAE tiles | 12.12 s |
| + sort-free top-k lists | 11.75 s |
| + streamed MP4 encode (#41819, not in this PR) | 11.26 s |
| + fused RoPE kept on batched tiles | 10.72 s |

## Modifications

### FastH3 8-Step V2, replacing the 4-step preview
- The H3 release block (`model_index.json` `_minimax_h3`) gains an optional `dmd_denoising_steps`.
- Timestep preparation shifts those unshifted rungs `[999, 874, ..., 125]` once per modality, as FastVideo's `_set_dmd_schedule` does. The uniform `linspace` grid is not the trained schedule: it gives 1.0 vs 0.999, 0.875 vs 0.874, and so on.
- Requests default to nine sigma points. The pipeline config carries the trained sparsity 0.8; the base H3 default stays 0.9.
- The flat Diffusers upload is materialized through the pinned `kevin-mi/FastH3-8step-V2-overlay` (revision `308e2dd`), which has the same materializer as the preview overlay, video/audio shifts 10/3, and the rungs.
- CI case, benchmark preset, cookbook and model catalog move to V2.

### Output path
- **System ffmpeg.** The direct CUDA save used imageio's bundled ffmpeg, which is 4.2.2 on aarch64. It took 2.9 s to H.264-encode 243 frames at 1344×768; the system ffmpeg 6.1 takes 1.0 s. The save now prefers a PATH ffmpeg that has libx264.
### VAE decode
- **Batched tiles for FastH3.** `FastH3PipelineConfig` sets `MiniMaxH3VideoVAEConfig.stack_tiling`, so a rank's spatial tiles go through the decoder as one batch at every quality level; base MiniMax-H3 still decodes tile by tile. Before this, a 10 s clip issued 53k kernels on rank 0 and was launch-bound on the Grace host.
- **Fused RoPE on batched tiles.** The tiles share one token grid, so RoPE is built from one row with positions repeated per tile. That keeps the fused qk-norm+RoPE kernel on the flattened batch, bit-identical to one tile at a time. Without this, batched tiles silently fell back to the unfused path.
- Effect on 4× GB300: decode 1.36 → 0.56 s at 5 s, 2.65 → 1.12 s at 10 s, 4.19 → 1.72 s at 15 s (`extra-high`). Under `lossless`, 5 s decode goes 1.36 → 0.73 s.

### VSA-H3
- **Native Blackwell block-sparse kernel** (`kernels/jit/csrc/diffusion/vsa_block_sparse_sm100/`), vendored from hao-ai-lab/FastVideo#1719, with the sm_103a device pass.
  - I diffed it against FastVideo HEAD: the forward is byte-identical apart from comments and arch-guard layout.
  - FastVideo's later VSA commits (#1812, #1833, #1858, #1819, #1866) are build plumbing or training-only, so there was nothing to port.
  - The workspace pads the tile axis to an even count. The top-k lists, pack and untile size themselves from the real tile count.
- **Sort-free kv-tile lists.** `topk(sorted=False)` scatters into a persistent int8 mask. A Triton prefix sum per query tile then writes the ascending list and the prefix tiles straight into the kernel index buffer.
  - The lists are identical, so attention is bit-identical.
  - The list step drops from 0.31 / 1.2 / 2.0 ms to 0.23 / 0.50 / 0.91 ms per layer at the 5 / 10 / 15 s shapes.
- **Gate fold after the output all-to-all.** Under Ulysses the per-tile compression output is all-gathered and folded into the row shard. This is bit-identical to the in-kernel fold.

### From the earlier revision of this PR (unchanged)
- VAE decoder fast path under `quality`: the fused QK RMSNorm + RoPE JIT kernel and cuDNN SDPA. `lossless` keeps the original decoder kernels (per-tile for base H3; FastH3 still batches tiles).
- Transformer-scoped recipe: `--component-attention-backends transformer=video_sparse_attn_h3`.
- FastH3 defaults to `quality: "extra-high"`.

Measured on 4× B300 with the retired 4-step preview (#37480 head → this PR, stage sums): 3.16 → 2.73 s at 5 s, 6.68 → 5.60 s at 10 s, 11.47 → 9.37 s at 15 s.

## Accuracy

- From the earlier revision, on the retired 4-step preview before tile batching: with the Triton kernel, a 10 s `lossless` request was byte-identical to the baseline.
- Sort-free lists: the lists equal `sort(topk)` exactly, so attention is bit-identical.
- Batched fused RoPE: bit-identical to per-tile.
- Batched VAE tiles change GEMM shapes, so FastH3 output differs from per-tile decode at rounding level at every quality level. Base H3 is unaffected.
- Frames spot-checked from the served V2 outputs are coherent.

## Tests

- `test_minimax_h3_fasth3.py`: the DMD sigmas equal FastVideo's served values (literal, so a double or missing shift fails), and a wrong step count or non-decreasing rungs are rejected. Also pins the trained sparsity 0.8.
- `test_vsa_h3_attention.py`: the list kernel equals the sorted top-k and leaves its scratch mask zeroed, for real, prefix-free and near-dense shapes. The odd-tile-count case now runs at the shipped 0.8.
- `test_minimax_h3_vae_parallel_modes.py`: the fused (quality) and native (lossless) RoPE kernels over batched tiles are bit-identical to per-tile. I confirmed it fails before the fix.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_vsa_block_sparse_sm100.py`: native kernel vs masked fp32 reference, and odd-count rejection.

Results: `pytest` on the H3 unit files, 112 passed; kernel test, 3 passed. `pre-commit run` on the PR files is clean.

**Not executed:**
- A multi-rank test of the Ulysses gate fold. The all-gather head order and `row_start` sharding are checked only by a single-process row-shard emulation (`test_return_compress_fold_on_row_shards_is_bit_identical`) and by the served 4-GPU runs above.
- H100 / SM90 CI case (`fasth3_t2va_vsa_4gpu_h100`) and AMD.
- Throughput at concurrency > 1.
- NVFP4. The blog's NVFP4 tier uses FastVideo's NVFP4 checkpoint, which SGLang does not load.

## Deliberately not in this PR
- Encoding the MP4 while the VAE decodes: #41819.
- Overlapping the Ulysses all-to-all with projections (head-sharded QKV). Denoise is 97% GPU-busy; NCCL is about 0.8 s of 8.9 s at 10 s.
- Decoder CUDA graphs. Decode is now GPU-bound, and the remaining cost is fp16 LayerNorm and elementwise ops.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Speculative Decoding] Add native UNO serving support
author: akhauriyash
body:
## Motivation

Add native SGLang serving support for UNO, a diffusion-augmented LLM. UNO uses two model pathways:

- The `diffusion pathway` combines the autoregressive (AR) weights with diffusion weights implemented as LoRA adapters.
- The `AR pathway` uses only the base AR weights.

The diffusion pathway drafts a block of tokens in parallel, and the AR pathway verifies those proposals against the base model's autoregressive distribution.

UNO is **lossless** like speculative decoding; however, it does not employ a separate draft model.

Each decoding cycle performs two target-model forward passes:

1. A diffusion-pathway forward pass that produces the first output token and a block of draft proposals.
2. An AR-pathway forward pass that verifies the proposals.

The integration supports two UNO sampling modes. The diffusion pathway constructs marginal distributions for a block of `B` tokens:

1. `Linear sampler:` Samples each token independently from its marginal distribution. This mode is designed to maximize system throughput and uses `B` as its primary hyperparameter.
2. `Tree sampler:` Considers `V` candidate sequences by selecting the top `K` candidates from each marginal distribution. Its hyperparameters are `(B, K, V)`.

## Modifications

- Register `UNO` as a native speculative-decoding algorithm with
  `--uno-lora-path`.
- Validate UNO's CUDA, FA3, parallelism, LoRA, and tree configuration
  constraints at startup.
- Reuse SGLang's existing multi-LoRA manager, adapter representation, layer
  wrappers, and stacked A/B weight buffers. Add an optimized single-adapter
  cuBLAS execution backend that overlaps LoRA-A computation with the base
  GEMMs.
- Apply the UNO LoRA to all but the first row of each draft forward. Use the
  base model alone for target verification.
- Implement sparse and dense proposal and rejection sampling for linear UNO.
- Implement tree UNO sampling and reuse SGLang's existing EAGLE
  tree-verification path.
- Use sparse target sampling for tree verification when eligible; otherwise
  use EAGLE's dense sampling path.
- Add an UNO-only fused kernel for tree-suffix attention and LSE merge, with
  SGLang's existing FlashAttention and state-merge path as fallback.
- Reserve and page-align KV space for UNO's two-pass decode, and extend
  scheduler bookkeeping for its `B + 1` output layout.
- Integrate UNO's carried decode state with SGLang's overlap scheduler.
- Add CUDA-graph support:
  - Linear mode captures separate graph variants for the `B`-wide LoRA draft
    and base-only verification passes.
  - Tree mode uses separate graph runners for the `B`-wide LoRA draft pass and
    `V`-node EAGLE cascade-attention verification pass.
- Add registered CPU dispatch and sampling tests, a CUDA kernel and CUDA-graph
  correctness test for the fused suffix merge, and an end-to-end CUDA-graph
  smoke test using a trained UNO adapter.


## Changes to shared SGLang infrastructure

UNO is implemented primarily in UNO-specific modules. The following extensions
touch shared runtime interfaces but are opt-in or preserve existing defaults:

- LoRA interfaces gain optional support for overlapped LoRA-A execution,
  explicit token-row routing, and skipping inactive internal adapters. Only
  the UNO backend enables these capabilities.
- The shared FlashAttention backend uses the fused suffix-attention merge only
  for eligible UNO tree verification. All other cases retain the existing
  cascade-attention path.
- EAGLE verification accepts optional UNO sampling metadata to select sparse
  target sampling; calls without it retain the existing sampling behavior.
- `GenerationBatchResult` gains optional output-stride and non-draft-token-count
  fields. Scheduler bookkeeping uses them to slice UNO's `B + 1` output rows
  and count accepted proposals; existing algorithms retain their previous
  defaults.
- Speculative allocation sizing uses an UNO-specific branch to reserve the
  additional KV position required by its two-pass decode.
- Model-runner and speculative-registry hooks select the UNO worker and
  CUDA-graph runner only when `--speculative-algorithm UNO` is active.


## Validation

### H200 unit and CUDA smoke validation

The CPU regression tests and the registered H200 CUDA smoke test passed. The
smoke test captured and replayed both linear and tree CUDA-graph paths using
three fixed GSM8K prompts with 128 generated tokens per prompt.

| Mode | B | K | V | TPF |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Linear | 8 | 1 | 8 | 2.462 |
| Tree | 8 | 16 | 8 | 2.783 |

TPF is useful output tokens divided by both target-model forwards per UNO
cycle: `tokens / (2 * spec_verify_ct)`. Tree TPF exceeded linear TPF.

### H200 math evaluation

The runs used `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` in BF16 on one NVIDIA H200 with FA3, a 40,960-token context, and the published [UNO Qwen3-8B adapter](https://huggingface.co/s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B) for UNO modes. All modes used temperature 1, top-k 50, top-p 0.95, random seed 42, and up to 32,768 output tokens. GSM8K and MATH500 used one sample per problem; AIME25 used 10 samples per problem (300 completions). Each dataset was run separately so it has an independent throughput measurement.

| Mode          | Dataset | Requests | Accuracy |   TPF |   tok/s | tok/s/request |
| ------------- | ------- | -------: | -------: | ----: | ------: | ------------: |
| AR            | GSM8K   |       64 |   96.10% | 1.000 | 6095.61 |         95.24 |
| Linear 8/1/8  | GSM8K   |       64 |   96.00% | 2.590 | 7197.80 |        112.47 |
| AR            | MATH500 |       64 |   96.00% | 1.000 | 3148.58 |         49.20 |
| Linear 8/1/8  | MATH500 |       64 |   95.60% | 2.720 | 5534.55 |         86.48 |
| AR            | AIME25  |       64 |   69.70% | 1.000 | 1894.82 |         29.61 |
| Linear 8/1/8  | AIME25  |       64 |   68.00% | 2.730 | 3841.41 |         60.02 |
| AR            | GSM8K   |        1 |   95.90% | 1.000 |  190.09 |        190.09 |
| Tree 16/32/32 | GSM8K   |        1 |   96.00% | 3.130 |  470.47 |        470.47 |
| AR            | MATH500 |        1 |   96.00% | 1.000 |  183.12 |        183.12 |
| Tree 16/32/32 | MATH500 |        1 |   96.80% | 3.450 |  508.56 |        508.56 |
| AR            | AIME25  |        1 |   68.00% | 1.000 |  178.32 |        178.32 |
| Tree 16/32/32 | AIME25  |        1 |   67.30% | 3.430 |  488.67 |        488.67 |

For UNO modes, the three numbers are `B/K/V`: draft width, top-k candidates kept per position, 
and verification width. Thus, `Linear 8/1/8` uses an
8-token draft width, one candidate per position, and an 8-token verification
width. `tok/s/request` is aggregate throughput divided by the number of
concurrent requests.

### Reproduction

The table was generated with `benchmark/uno/run_math_eval.py`, which
instantiates `sglang.Engine` in-process and excludes engine startup from the
timed interval. Exact commands for reproducing every row are provided in
`benchmark/uno/README.md`.

The equivalent server launch commands for the two UNO configurations are:

```bash
export MODEL_PATH=Qwen/Qwen3-8B
export UNO_LORA_PATH=s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B

# Linear UNO: B/K/V = 8/1/8, 64 concurrent requests
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --attention-backend fa3 \
  --context-length 40960 \
  --max-running-requests 64 \
  --random-seed 42 \
  --speculative-algorithm UNO \
  --uno-lora-path "$UNO_LORA_PATH" \
  --speculative-num-steps 1 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 8

# Tree UNO: B/K/V = 16/32/32, one concurrent request
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --attention-backend fa3 \
  --context-length 40960 \
  --max-running-requests 1 \
  --random-seed 42 \
  --speculative-algorithm UNO \
  --uno-lora-path "$UNO_LORA_PATH" \
  --speculative-num-steps 15 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 32 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 32
```


### Test coverage

Added regression coverage for:

- Invalid tree dimensions exceeding the current EAGLE parent-list
  representation.
- Clearing stale internal LoRA metadata before base-only verification.
- Sparse tree target-sampling dispatch and compact-support sampling.
- UNO-only fused suffix-attention dispatch with fallback for unsupported
  attention features and layouts.
- Numerical correctness and CUDA-graph replay of the fused suffix-attention
  merge kernel.
- Linear and tree CUDA-graph capture, replay, generation, and nontrivial
  acceptance.

Current test files:

- `test/registered/unit/spec/test_uno_tree_config.py`
- `test/registered/unit/lora/test_uno_inactive_lora_batch.py`
- `test/registered/unit/spec/test_uno_tree_sparse_sampling.py`
- `test/registered/unit/spec/test_suffix_attention_merge_dispatch.py`
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_suffix_attention_merge.py`
- `test/registered/spec/uno/test_uno.py`

## Checklist
- [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance.
- [x] Add unit tests for the new dispatch, sampling, kernel, and end-to-end
  paths.
- [x] Use the published [s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B](https://huggingface.co/s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B) adapter.

title: [GraniteMoE] Load split per-expert quantized MoE weights
author: jlqibm
body:
## Motivation

Compressed-tensors checkpoints (llmcompressor) store MoE experts one tensor per expert per projection -- `experts.<id>.{gate,up,down}_proj.{weight,weight_scale}` -- while the unquantized HF checkpoint packs them into `input_linear`/`output_linear`. GraniteMoe only understood the packed layout, so every split expert tensor matched no mapping and fell through to mixtral's `logger.warning(...not found in params_dict)`.

The result was a silent failure: the server started, reported no error, and generated garbage. On granite-5.0-20b that dropped 13440 expert tensors for fp8 and 20160 for w4a16, and "The capital of France is" completed as "capital capital capital..." instead of " Paris.".

This affects any `GraniteMoeForCausalLM` checkpoint quantized with llmcompressor, which is the standard tool for producing compressed-tensors Granite MoE models.

## Modifications

- Add `granitemoe_load_split_experts`, which resolves the split names via `FusedMoE.make_expert_params_mapping(ckpt_gate_proj_name="gate_proj", ...)` and loads them into the fused `w13_*`/`w2_*` parameters, yielding everything it does not claim for the existing packed-layout path.
- The mapped name deliberately keeps the checkpoint's trailing suffix (`.weight` vs `.weight_scale`), which is what routes a scale to the scale branch of `FusedMoE._weight_loader_impl` rather than the weight branch.
- An expert tensor that matches no mapping now raises instead of being warned about and dropped, so this failure mode cannot recur silently. Packed-layout w1/w2/w3 names still pass through untouched.
- Small helpers `_match_split_expert` / `_is_packed_expert` keep `load_weights` readable as a three-step pipeline.

Scoped to `python/sglang/srt/models/granitemoe.py`. No changes to `mixtral.py` (shared with other models) or to the quantization layer.

## Accuracy Tests

Verified on H100 (SM90) with granite-5.0-20b, one offline `Engine` per checkpoint, prompt `"The capital of France is"`:

| Checkpoint | Dropped experts (before -> after) | Output after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fp8-dynamic` | 13440 -> **0** | `" Paris."` |
| `fp8-block` | 13440 -> **0** | `" Paris."` |
| `w4a16` (int4) | 20160 -> **0** | `" Paris."` |
| bf16 (packed, regression check) | 0 -> **0** | `" Paris."` (unchanged) |

Before the fix, all three quantized checkpoints produced "capital capital capital..."-style output.

The four fp4 variants (`mxfp4a16`, `mxfp4`, `nvfp4a16`, `nvfp4`) are unaffected by this PR -- they fail earlier, during quantization-scheme construction on the first attention linear, and never reach expert loading. Those are separate issues in `compressed_tensors.py` and are tracked separately.

New unit tests: `test/registered/unit/models/test_granitemoe_split_expert_loading.py` -- 13 CPU tests (`register_cpu_ci`, `base-a-test-cpu`), verified to fail on pre-fix code and pass with the fix. Beyond the split/scale/pass-through cases, the packed-shard predicate is pinned so that relaxing `.w1.` to a bare `w1` substring test fails 3 cases; that relaxation would silently send an unknown expert tensor down the pass-through path instead of raising.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable -- this is a weight-loading path change only. It does not touch the model forward path or any kernel, so steady-state inference speed is unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). **N/A** -- no user-facing behavior, CLI, or config change.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Accuracy results above; speed **N/A** -- weight-loading path only, no forward or kernel change.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: [Feature] Unified memory: support decode context parallelism for the trtllm_mla family
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

#36890 added decode context parallelism to the unified memory pool, but gated `--enable-unified-memory --dcp-size > 1` to `--attention-backend flashinfer`. That excludes `cutedsl_mla`, which is the DCP-native MLA decode kernel on Blackwell (flashinfer accepts `enable_dcp=True` for no other backend) and what the B300 hosts run. So the feature was unusable there.

The reason for the gate is that unified memory plus DCP has two read-index production routes, and #36890 converted only one:

1. **flashinfer** — `plan_dcp_decode_metadata` compacts this rank's widened ids in place, then the caller converts them with `KVIndexTranslator.translate_dcp_read_ids`.
2. **the `trtllm_mla` family** (`trtllm_mla`, `cutedsl_mla`, `tokenspeed_mla`) — a block table built by `create_mla_kv_page_table_for_dcp`, which gathers a rank's cyclic slice straight out of `req_to_token`, bypassing `build_index_table` entirely.

Route 2 collapsed the widened virtual id (`// dcp_size`) and stopped there. That is correct on a static pool, where the collapsed page *is* the physical page, but under the unified pool it is still virtual and needs one more hop through the pool's page table.

## Modifications

- `create_mla_kv_page_table_for_dcp` takes the pool's virtual-to-physical page table (`HAS_V2P`) and scales the physical page by `kernel_page_multiplier` — the same conversion `build_kv_read_table` already performs for the non-DCP block-table backends. A `-1` in `req_to_token` and a freed v2p row both clamp to entry 0, the reserved padding page.
- `KVIndexTranslator` exposes `full_v2p_table` / `full_page_multiplier`, for the one class of producer `build_index_table` cannot serve.
- `_validate_unified_memory_dcp` admits the `trtllm_mla` family. `flashmla` and `cutlass_mla` stay out: neither has a DCP-local page-table builder to extend.

Two write-path defects the same configuration exposes, both fixed here:

- The `cutedsl_mla` / `tokenspeed_mla` DCP decode wrote KV at `forward_batch.out_cache_loc`. A captured decode on the unified pool must not: `rebind_write_loc` returns a *fresh* tensor, so the graph replays against a buffer it never recorded. Both now use the base class's capture-stable `_decode_kernel_loc`, as the non-DCP `trtllm_mla` decode already did.
- The fused fp8 KV scatter passed `dcp_world_size=attn_dcp_size` unconditionally. The unified pool declares `write_loc_is_dcp_resolved`, so its loc arrives already collapsed with non-owned rows sent to the padding sink; applying the owner rule a second time divides a kernel-facing id.

## Accuracy Tests

4x B300, `moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct`. Every backend the gate now admits, each as a matched unified-vs-static pair, GSM8K @200 (1 sigma ~= 0.02):

| Configuration | Unified memory | Static pool |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TP4 DCP4, `cutedsl_mla` (prefill `trtllm_mla`) | 0.910 | 0.900 |
| TP2 DCP2, `cutedsl_mla` | 0.905 | 0.905 |
| TP2 DCP2, `trtllm_mla` | 0.895 | 0.895 |
| TP2 DCP2, `tokenspeed_mla` (fp8 KV) | 0.890, 0.890 | 0.895, 0.885 |

The DCP2 `cutedsl_mla` and `trtllm_mla` pairs reproduced exactly. `tokenspeed_mla` moved on a repeat of the same questions on *both* pools, so its 0.005 spread is the backend, not the pool.

The DCP4 row matters beyond the extra data point: it widens the virtual page to 4 x 64 = 256, a wider factor than any DCP2 configuration exercises.

The argument gate was exercised directly through `run_resolution_pipeline`, which is where it actually runs:

```
cutedsl_mla      ACCEPTED  resolved=('trtllm_mla', 'cutedsl_mla')
trtllm_mla       ACCEPTED  resolved=('trtllm_mla', 'trtllm_mla')
tokenspeed_mla   ACCEPTED  resolved=('tokenspeed_mla', 'tokenspeed_mla')   [with fp8 KV]
flashinfer       ACCEPTED  resolved=('flashinfer', 'flashinfer')
flashmla         REJECTED  requires ['cutedsl_mla', ...]
triton           REJECTED  requires ['cutedsl_mla', ...]
fa3              REJECTED  requires ['cutedsl_mla', ...]
```

**`flashinfer` is untested here** — the verification host has `flashinfer_python` 0.6.17 against main's 0.6.18 floor. It cannot regress from this change: every hunk in the attention backends lands in `TRTLLMMLABackend` or a subclass, never in the `FlashInferMLAAttnBackend` parent; the modified kernel has exactly one caller (`_fill_dcp_block_kv_indices`); the translator only gains two read-only properties; and the gate only widens. Worth a confirming run on a host with a current flashinfer.

Also smoke-tested the speculative route the same page table feeds — DSPARK with dummy draft weights, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--dcp-comm-backend a2a`:

| Configuration | Score | Accept length (mean / min / max) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unified memory | 0.915 | 1.0125 / 1.0019 / 1.0323 |
| static pool | 0.915 | 1.0125 / 1.0019 / 1.0323 |

The accept-length distributions match to every digit reported, so the two pools agree request by request.

Test additions:

- `test/registered/models_e2e/test_kimi_linear_unified_memory_dcp_blackwell.py`, in `extra-b-test-4-gpu-b200` next to the other four-GPU Blackwell DCP tests. One server on the whole runner at TP4 DCP4, `cutedsl_mla` decode with `trtllm_mla` prefill, so a single launch covers both halves of the page-table contract at the widest DCP factor. Both tests pass in 3.5 min on B300, GSM8K 0.930. `test_prefix_cache_branching` is the sharp one: a radix hit replays widened virtual locs whose pages may have moved under compaction. `trtllm_mla` and `tokenspeed_mla` share the page-table builder and are covered by the hand-run pairs above rather than a CI server each.
- Three CUDA unit tests in `test/registered/dcp/test_trtllm_mla_family_dcp_metadata.py` pinning the block table's id space against a reference derived from the page tables, including the freed-page clamp. Without the fix the failure mode is stale KV rather than a crash, so the reference is computed independently rather than read back from the kernel.
- Existing related suites: 154 passed (`test_trtllm_mla_family_dcp_metadata`, `test_dcp_layout_unit`, `test_multi_ended_allocator`, `test_full_loc_fast_path`, `test_unified_out_cache_loc_rebind`).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change to any hot path. The added v2p gather is one extra load inside the existing page-table kernel, compiled out on the static pool by the `HAS_V2P` constexpr; the write-path changes swap which tensor a kernel reads.

title: [sglang-miles] Kimi K3 colocated RL: LoRA fixes and in-place MXFP4 Marlin reload
author: yueming-yuan
body:
The Kimi K3 RL serving work reached `sglang-miles` through `main`, and the miles K3 PR (radixark/miles#1825) now runs against `sglang-miles` instead of the old `sglang-miles-k3` branch. Running it on `radixark/miles:dev` found five places where the merge lost or never had what colocated K3 LoRA RL needs. Each commit is one of them; all were found by reading the traceback back to the branch diff, and the last two by `--check-weight-update-equal` / `--check-lora-weight-equal`.

- `num_shared_experts` (K3's config key) was not recognized when sizing the shared-expert LoRA buffers, so `init_state` died with `KeyError('gate_up_proj')` on the first dense layer.
- The output gate K3 installs by patching `o_proj.forward` never ran under LoRA: `RowParallelLinearWithLoRA` calls `quant_method.apply` on the base layer, so the MLA output went out ungated and the gate GEMM on the alt stream was never joined (`capturing stream has unjoined work`). Restores the `lora_input_transform` hook from the K3 branch (3768a8788a).
- Routed-expert LoRA buffers were sized by `hidden_size`; K3's latent MoE feeds the experts `routed_expert_hidden_size` (3584).
- `post_load_weights` read `o_proj.params_dtype` through the LoRA wrapper.
- `_merge_bfa_weights` stored `f_b_proj.weight` as a second Parameter on the attention module, which hides `f_b_proj.weight` from `named_parameters()`; every weight update silently skipped it (fb03504c93). Alias the storage instead.

Running the full model on 16 GB300 nodes (TP16, Marlin, `--no-lora-use-virtual-experts`) then showed the train/rollout KL growing with the adapter norm (0.0023 at step 0, 0.0047 by step 60) while the July stack stayed flat. A line-by-line diff of the LoRA path against that stack found four more losses, each its own commit:

- `Mxfp4MoEMethod` never exposed `get_marlin_quant_info`, so `FusedMoEWithLoRA` refused the Marlin backend outright; the LoRA Marlin runner also only ran `silu_and_mul`, so K3's gated SiTU experts failed at CUDA-graph capture.
- The Marlin tile padding of the expert intermediate (K3 at TP16: 192 -> 256) was ignored by the MoE LoRA hooks: the up delta was written at the logical stride into the gate padding and the down LoRA-A consumed the padded activation. Restores `output_slice_stride` in `fused_moe_lora` and the `marlin_intermediate_size` plumbing.
- The interleaved gate/up LoRA-B layout keyed on `gemm1_alpha` alone; K3 sets it for SiTU but loads w1/w3 contiguously, so every routed-expert gate/up delta was scrambled.
- The fused MoE front read the shared-expert base weights straight through the LoRA wrappers, so the shared_experts adapters the trainer streams were never applied.
- The LoRA Marlin runner used atomic-add for MXFP4 where the base runner does not.
- `--lora-no-cpu-backup`: the streamed adapter no longer keeps a per-TP-rank host copy (~45 GB/rank for the 896-expert adapter); the IPC views are installed into the pool at apply time.

Full-parameter RL re-pushes the MXFP4 base on every sync, which needs one more piece:

- `Mxfp4MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading` repacked the experts into fresh Parameters, so a later `load_weights` found no `weight_loader` on them and the runner's `begin_weight_update` had nothing to restore. The method now records the checkpoint and Marlin layouts per layer, `restore_weights_before_loading` views the storage back to the checkpoint shape, and the repack runs expert by expert into the same storage, so the Parameter objects (and their `weight_loader`) survive. Unit test: `test/registered/e2e/rl/test_mxfp4_marlin_inplace_reload.py`.
- The last commit (`Mxfp4MarlinComparable` accepting the checker's `is_shuffled`) is a temporary cherry-pick of a standalone fix for `sglang-miles`; it drops out of this PR once that lands.

## Validation

miles CI (radixark/miles#1825, `run-ci-model-scripts` on 8xH200, `radixark/miles:dev` + this branch synced at test time) on `Pinaster/Kimi-K3-4layer-64experts`:

- `test_kimi_k3_4layer_lora_ci.py`: two rollouts and syncs; `--check-lora-weight-equal` matches on every rank and the base weight checker compares equal after each sync.
- `test_kimi_k3_4layer_ci.py` (full-parameter): the MXFP4 base is re-quantized and re-pushed on every sync; `--check-weight-update-equal` compares the Marlin experts equal in dequantized space (sgl-project/sglang#40028) after the in-place reload.

The Marlin-padding, interleave and shared-expert fixes were validated on the 4-layer TP8 layout with a trained adapter re-sharded from the 16-node run (rollout-0 logprob abs diff back to the zero-adapter floor); the padded-intermediate path itself only triggers at TP16 and was validated on the 16-node GB300 run.

sglang's own CI does not run on `sglang-miles` PRs (the `check-changes` maintenance gate), so the registered tests that exercise the touched files were run by hand on a fresh 8xH200 devbox (`radixark/miles:dev`, this branch at `e5dbafcada` installed in place of the baked sglang):

| test | result |
|---|---|
| `e2e/rl/test_mxfp4_marlin_inplace_reload.py`, `e2e/rl/test_weight_checker_mxfp4_marlin.py` | 1 + 9 passed |
| `unit/utils/test_weight_checker_comparator.py` | 11 passed |
| `lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py` | 108 passed |
| `quant/test_marlin_moe.py`, `kernels/ops/moe/test_moe_wna16_marlin.py` | 2 passed / 678 subtests; 7 passed, 24 skipped |
| `lora/test_virtual_experts_kernels.py`, `unit/lora/test_experimental_sgl_marlin_{multi_prefill,shared_outer_reduce}.py` | 13 + 2 + 4 passed |
| `unit/models/test_kimi_k3_bfa_overlap.py`, `kernels/ops/test_kimi_k3_prerequisite_ops.py`, `unit/layers/quantization/test_mxfp4_sm90_cutlass.py` | 4 + 12 + 19 passed |
| `rl/test_lora_load_from_tensor.py`, `lora/test_multi_lora_backend.py`, `lora/test_lora_overlap_loading.py`, `lora/test_lora_eviction.py` | 6 + 3 + 9 + 2 passed |
| `lora/test_lora_qwen3_8b_logprob_diff.py`, `lora/test_lora_moe_tp_logprob_diff.py` (TP2) | 2 passed; 2 passed, 1 skipped |
| GPT-OSS-20B MXFP4, Marlin runner vs `triton_kernel`, greedy 32 tokens x 4 prompts | 3/4 identical text, max abs logprob diff <= 0.056; the 4th diverges after 20 identical tokens |

Five files fail identically on plain `sglang-miles` (reproduced on the same devbox with the base branch installed) and are not touched by this PR: `unit/utils/test_weight_checker.py` (a helper returns 2 values, the test unpacks 3), `rl/test_weight_checker_e2e.py` and `rl/test_update_weights_from_tensor.py` (they push weights without `begin_weight_update`, which the scheduler has asserted on since the RL session protocol), `lora/test_moe_lora_info.py` (its fake `forward_batch` lacks `global_dp_buffer_len`), `lora/test_lora_spec_decoding.py` (EAGLE3 draft context-length check). Not runnable on H200: the B200/B300-only registrations.

## Follow-ups not in scope

- The AR-fusion (`_symm_o_proj_forward`) and SP-MoE (`_sp_o_proj_forward`) patches on `o_proj.forward` are bypassed by the LoRA wrapper the same way the output gate was; neither is active in the smoke run (auto-probe off, no symm mem). They need an output-side hook before K3 LoRA runs with AR fusion.

title: [PD] Transfer the DCP-replicated DSPARK draft KV in DCP1->DCP-N relayouts
author: kpham-sgl
body:
Follow-up to #35762: ship DSpark draft KV from a DCP1 prefill to a DCP-N decode.

## Design

Decode publishes one virtual page list. A virtual page is `P*N` tokens (`P` = physical page, `N` = decode DCP size). Each pool then lays that page out at its own width:

```
page = dst_pages[pos // (P*N)]
off  = pos % (P*N)                 # offset inside that virtual page

draft  row = page * (P*N) + off    # page is wide; keep every token
target row = page * P + off // N   # page is narrow; keep every Nth token (owner pos % N)
```

Target: strided pick + #35762 pack. Draft: full copy, no pack.

## Code

- `KVArgs.num_draft_entries` marks the draft tail of `kv_data_ptrs`.
- `build_dcp_token_transfer_plan` fills both index maps in one call.
- `prepare_dcp_token_item_lens` scales draft dest pages by `N`. Pack buffers stay target-only.
- Mooncake and NIXL send both parts from that plan (NIXL: two xfers, existing `_part_{i}_{n}` notif).

Out of scope: DCP>1 prefill, heterogeneous P/D TP × DSPARK.

## Tests

- `test_dcp_pack.py`: golden rows, chunk crossing, pack vs no-pack grouping, item-len scale.
- `test_kimi_linear_pd_dcp4_dspark.py`: Kimi-Linear TP4 DCP1 → DCP4 DSPARK, GSM8K.

## Speed Tests

8xB300, `Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct`, dummy DSPARK + `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=4` (measured accept length 4.00). Same topology as #35762. OSL 32. title: [CPU] Implement fused QK Norm and RoPE kernels
author: cyxlily
body:
## Motivation

This PR adds a CPU fused QK Norm and RoPE kernels to cut redundant kernel-launch/dispatch overhead for models (e.g. Qwen3-MoE) that apply RMSNorm to Q/K per head before RoPE. CUDA reference: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/elementwise/qknorm.cuh, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/moe/fused_qknorm_rope_kernel.cu

## Modifications

 - python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/cpu/norm.cpp: Added fused_qk_norm_cpu (fused per-head RMSNorm for Q/K) and fused_qk_norm_rope_cpu (fused per-head RMSNorm + RoPE). The RoPE op takes (q, k, q_weight, k_weight, eps, is_neox, position_ids, cos_sin_cache, rotary_dim) — no base/factor/low/high/attention_factor — and indexes into the caller-supplied cos_sin_cache via position_ids[token] * rotary_dim. Both interleaved (GPT-J) and NeoX RoPE styles are vectorized with at::vec (AVX512-capable), avoiding per-element scalar sin/cos calls and a per-call heap allocation from the original implementation.
 - python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/cpu/torch_extension_cpu.cpp: Registered fused_qk_norm_cpu and fused_qk_norm_rope_cpu op schemas (Tensor(a!) in-place markers on q/k).
 - python/sglang/srt/models/utils.py: Added _has_cpu_fused_qk_norm() / can_use_fused_qk_norm_cpu() and wired fused_qk_norm_cpu into the shared apply_qk_norm() helper (used by many models) as a CPU fast path, gated on dtype (bf16/fp16), contiguity, and op availability.
 - python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py: Added _has_cpu_fused_qk_norm_rope() and Qwen3MoeAttention.use_fused_qk_norm_rope_cpu eligibility check (CPU, non-MRotaryEmbedding, even rotary_dim, op available). Restructured apply_qk_norm_rope so CUDA and CPU fused paths share a single use_fused branch (if _is_cuda: ... elif _is_cpu: ...), with the CPU path calling torch.ops.sgl_kernel.fused_qk_norm_rope_cpu using self.rotary_emb.cos_sin_cache / rotary_dim (built once, reused every call) instead of recomputing sin/cos per call; falls back to the original separate apply_qk_norm + rotary_emb() path otherwise.
 - test/registered/cpu/test_norm.py: Added unit tests for fused_qk_norm_cpu and fused_qk_norm_rope_cpu, including building a reference cos_sin_cache and comparing against a separate RMSNorm+RoPE reference implementation for both interleaved and NeoX RoPE styles.

## Accuracy Tests

 - pytest test/registered/cpu/test_norm.py — 12 passed, covering fused_qk_norm_cpu and fused_qk_norm_rope_cpu (bf16/fp16, interleaved/NeoX, various shapes) against a separate-ops reference implementation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

fused_qk_norm_rope_cpu > fused_qk_norm_cpu > separate QK-Norm+RoPE, consistently across batch sizes and dtypes.

batch_size | num_head | num_head_kv | head_dim | dtype | norm_speedup | norm_rope_speedup
-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --
1 | 32 | 8 | 128 | bfloat16 | 1.738 | 2.176
1 | 32 | 8 | 128 | float16 | 1.693 | 2.127
1 | 16 | 2 | 128 | bfloat16 | 1.730 | 1.968
1 | 16 | 2 | 128 | float16 | 1.606 | 1.851
128 | 32 | 8 | 128 | bfloat16 | 1.375 | 2.345
128 | 32 | 8 | 128 | float16 | 1.529 | 2.514
128 | 16 | 2 | 128 | bfloat16 | 1.429 | 2.366

1024 | 32 | 8 | 128 | bfloat16 | 1.019 | 2.290
1024 | 32 | 8 | 128 | float16 | 1.267 | 4.330
1024 | 16 | 2 | 128 | bfloat16 | 1.200 | 2.313

title: [AMD][Diffusion] FlyDSL fused norm kernels on wave32 targets (gfx1250)
author: yctseng0211
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation


Applies on top of #36349 (FlyDSL v0.3.0 stable-API migration).

## Problem

`SGLANG_USE_ROCM_FLYDSL=1` aborts at kernel compile time on gfx1250 (MI450):

```
LLVM ERROR: Cannot select: intrinsic %llvm.amdgcn.permlane32.swap
```

This is not a regression from #36349 -- the pre-migration kernel fails
identically. Both versions carry the same wave64 assumption.

## Root cause

`fused_residual_norm_flydsl.py` hardcodes `WARP_SIZE = 64` and
`_SHUFFLE_OFFSETS = (32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1)`. gfx1250 is a wave32 part
(`torch.cuda.get_device_properties().warp_size == 32`), so the leading stride-32
XOR shuffle of width 64 crosses the wave boundary. The lowering can only express
that as `permlane32_swap`, which exists only in the wave64 ISA, so instruction
selection fails.

## Fix

Derive the three wave-dependent constants from the device warp size:

- `WARP_SIZE` from `torch.cuda.get_device_properties().warp_size`, falling back
  to 64 when no device is visible.
- `_NUM_WAVES` from a fixed 640-thread block, so `BLOCK` and the public
  `FLYDSL_NORM_MIN_ALIGNED_DIM` (5120) stay identical on both wave sizes and
  callers are unaffected.
- `_SHUFFLE_OFFSETS` starting at `WARP_SIZE // 2`.

No other change is needed: both reduction sites go through `wave_reduce_add`,
which already iterates `len(_SHUFFLE_OFFSETS)`.

On wave64 every derived value is identical to before (`_NUM_WAVES = 10`, offsets
`(32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1)`), so gfx950 codegen is unchanged.

## Validation

gfx1250 (MI450), ROCm 10, Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, 480x832, 33 frames, 4 steps,
`HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=0`:

| | FLYDSL=0 | FLYDSL=1 before | FLYDSL=1 after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| result | ok | LLVM ERROR | ok |
| latent neighbour corr (w/h/frame) | .9433 / .9020 / .9488 | -- | .9430 / .9064 / .9494 |
| latent corr vs FLYDSL=0 | -- | -- | 0.9778 |
| denoise | 8.95 s/step | -- | 8.48 s/step |

Structural metrics match the FLYDSL=0 reference to within 0.005 (pure noise
scores ~0.001 on the same metric) and the decoded video is visually
indistinguishable. The residual latent difference is the expected bf16 rounding
drift from a different reduction order, and it grows with step count as it
accumulates -- at 17 frames / 2 steps the same comparison gives 0.9991.

## Note for reviewers

FlyDSL 0.3.1 separately misclassifies gfx1250 as CDNA: `is_rdna_arch()` only

this fix -- verified by A/B running with and without a shim that corrects the
classification, both produce correct output -- but the same predicate also
drives buffer descriptor flag selection, so it is worth fixing upstream.

title: [CI][NPU] Fix kimi_k2_6 16p in64k perf test and dsv4-flash testcases

## Motivation

1. The kimi_k2_6 W4A8 16p in64k/out1k performance test uses `--chunked-prefill-size 262144`. With the full 64K-token input prefilled in one chunk, peak activation memory is high and the server is prone to recomputation/oom-adjacent behavior on A3 devices, which destabilizes the nightly latency measurement.
