title: [AMD][DSv4] Fuse the DSv4 FP4 indexer prefill-schedule preamble into one kernel
author: heachary
body: ## Motivation The FP4 indexer (#37353) builds its persistent-grid schedule with a torch-op preamble that runs once per C4 layer. Every op touches only a few hundred elements, so the whole block is launch latency bound. On a DeepSeek-V4-Pro 128k/1k conc-64 DP8TP8 MTP trace (MI355X) that is **33 dispatches and 146 us per layer per step.** These 33 kernels can be fused into a single kernel. ## Trace results ### Before ### After The trace shows all 33 kernels being fused into a single kernel. ## Summary of changes Adds `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/fp4_indexer_schedule_hip.py`, which collapses the preamble into a single Triton kernel. Everything it computes is a reduction or a scan over the row count; the only real dependency is that AITER's `_prefill_cta_info_kernel` needs the finished prefix sums, so the schedule now costs two dispatches instead of 33. - **Split-factor search.** AITER picks the smallest `s` with `sum_i ceil(chunks_i / s) <= P` by materialising an `[s_max, T]` tensor and extracting the first feasible index arithmetically (~18 of the 27 ops). That sum is monotonically non-increasing in `s`, so a binary search over `s` returns the identical answer in registers, with no intermediate tensor. - **Page-table pad** is one kernel that writes every output element, so the destination no longer needs pre-zeroing. - **`row_to_batch` / `local_starts`** are emitted in-kernel â sglang always schedules one row per query token over its whole window. - **Pinned `cta_info`** lets the logits kernel skip its `-inf` pre-fill, the same way the existing workspace path already does: the length-aware top-k only reads `[0, c4_seq_len)`, which is always covered by a CTA. - Rows past `MAX_FUSED_ROWS` (one row per lane) keep AITER's preamble â a prefill that wide is compute-bound and does not care about ~30 extra launches. No new flags; active whenever `--enable-deepseek-v4-fp4-indexer` is on (HIP). ## Accuracy GSM8k (1319 questions, DP8TP8 + MTP + FP4 indexer): 0.940 / 0.920 before, 0.948 / 0.931 after. ## Performance ### Fixed length isl/osl = 8k1k, conc=4/64, mtp=on, image = lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x-20260902 | Concurrency | Output Throughput â baseline (tok/s) | Output Throughput â fusions (tok/s) | Delta | |---|---|---|---| | 4 | 311.66 | 359.43 | +15.3% | | 64 | 2592.46 | 2677.55 | +3.3% | The launch latency bound kernels are a fixed cost and the benefits of fusing them are more pronounced at lower latencies. ### Agent-X conc64, mtp=on, image = lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x-20260902 | Config | Throughput per GPU (tok/s) | p50 ITL (ms) | Mean accept length | Decode step (ms) | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | baseline | 20295 | 32.36 | 2.48 | 85.0 | | fp4_indexer_fusion | 20752 | 31.27 | 2.49 | 82.5 | ~3% improvement in decode step time --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #33844863732](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33844863732) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #33844863368](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33844863368) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #33844863663](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33844863663)

title: [HiSparse] Add speculative decoding support with multi-step KV cache swapping
author: huangtingwei9988
body:
## Prerequisite

- Kernel implementation #32162 provides the multi-step gather/commit swap kernel, including cross-step miss deduplication, extra-page lookup, scratch-space management, cache commit, and device-location resolution. This PR focuses on integrating that kernel into the SGLang serving path.

## Motivation

This PR adds end-to-end HiSparse support for multi-step speculative decoding, currently targeting linear EAGLE/MTP decoding with multiple draft tokens. It integrates the multi-step swap kernel from #32162 into the HiSparse coordinator and speculative-decoding lifecycle, covering logical target-slot reservation, per-layer scratch and cache state, verify preparation, accepted-token commit, host backup, and request cleanup. Draft KV remains in its logical GPU address space instead of reusing the HiSparse target KV physical mapping, while the target KV continues to use HiSparse host/device placement. The PR also preserves speculative state when requests transition through HiSparse staging and, for Mooncake PD serving, carries separate target host/physical page indices and draft logical-device page indices. Together, these changes make HiSparse compatible with multi-step speculative decoding without falling back to sequential per-step LRU swapping.


## Accuracy Tests

- Model: GLM-5.2-W4AFP8
- Serving topology: 1P1D, TP8/DP8 with DP Attention
- KV cache: FP8
- Speculative decoding: EAGLE, 3 steps, top-k 1, 4 draft tokens
- CUDA Graph: enabled
- HiSparse: top-k 2048, 4096-slot device buffer, host/device ratio 4
- The only A/B variable was whether HiSparse was enabled.

| Benchmark | HiSparse ON | HiSparse OFF | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K 20-shot (200 samples) | 195/200 (97.50%) | 192/200 (96.00%) | +1.50 pp |
| GPQA-Diamond (198 samples) | 180/198 (90.91%) | 182/198 (91.92%) | -1.01 pp |

title: [ROCm][DSV4] Enable breakable CUDA graph prefill
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
## Summary

Enable breakable CUDA graph (BCG) prefill for the ROCm DeepSeek-V4 HIP radix backend.

## Changes

- Add captured-metadata support for HIP radix prefill capture and replay.
- Refresh attention, unified-KV, indexer, compressor, and FP4 workspace metadata in place.
- Preserve the existing CUDA memory-pressure guard while allowing explicit HIP BCG selection.
- Keep ROCm DSV4 mixed prefill/decode batches eager under DP attention; pure TP and other backends retain their existing replay policy.
- Pass host-proven `repeat_interleave(output_size=...)` and `extend_start_loc` metadata to avoid implicit GPU-to-host scalar synchronizations.
- Add focused coverage for capture/replay metadata, DP admission, address stability, underfilled buckets, and the no-D2H guard.

BCG remains opt-in through `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`.

### Validation

| Item | Configuration |
|---|---|
| Source | Current head `6c62e78486` |
| Hardware | 8 x MI355X, TP8 + DP8 attention, DP LM head |
| Image | `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.19-rocm724-mi35x-20260905` (`sha256:1951b978...121115d`) |
| Runtime | `unified_kv_triton`, full decode graphs, no speculative decoding |
| Comparison | Same node/image/source; only prefill backend differs (`disabled` vs `breakable`) |
| Method | 3 repeats per arm/point, seeds 42/43/44, `2 * concurrency` requests, exact token gates |

#### Performance

| Workload | C | Eager output tok/s | BCG output tok/s | Delta | Paired median | BCG graph-token share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `1024 -> 1024` | 4 | 247.587 | 250.037 | +0.990% | +1.108% | 80.556% |
| `1024 -> 1024` | 8 | 485.620 | 483.977 | -0.338% | -0.482% | 12.500% |
| `1024 -> 1024` | 16* | 861.178 | 867.745 | +0.763% | +0.007% | 4.380% |
| `1024 -> 1024` | 32 | 1,548.698 | 1,532.551 | -1.043% | -0.557% | 2.326% |
| `1024 -> 1024` | 64 | 2,606.849 | 2,649.817 | +1.648% | +0.427% | 1.205% |
| `8192 -> 1024` | 32 | 1,262.841 | 1,245.668 | -1.360% | -0.119% | 19.718% |
| `8192 -> 1024` | 128 | 2,613.743 | 2,649.922 | +1.384% | +0.053% | 5.412% |

\* C16 uses the stable follow-up (eager/BCG CV `0.677% / 0.577%`); the first pass had 7.709% eager CV and was excluded from interpretation.

| Signal | Result |
|---|---|
| Highest-admission point (1K, C4) | TTFT `282.634 -> 188.345 ms` (-33.361%); output throughput +0.990% |
| Stable C16 follow-up | Output +0.763%, but same-seed paired median +0.007%: throughput-neutral |
| Production-like 8K | C32/C128 paired medians -0.119% / +0.053%: throughput-neutral |
| Admission policy | Zero graph records with running decode requests; DP-attention `MIXED` remains eager |
| Ready-state memory | BCG +0.943 GiB/GPU versus eager |
| Recommendation | Keep BCG opt-in; no material aggregate throughput regression or broad throughput-win claim |

#### Isolated prefill latency (earlier-image controls)

Pure-TP8 controls on `1e8531972` with the `20260904` image isolate graph replay from DP `MIXED` traffic:

| `1024 -> 64`, C1 (10 repeats) | Eager | BCG | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Output throughput | 74.817 tok/s | 81.987 tok/s | +9.584% |
| TTFT | 146.219 ms | 73.194 ms | -49.942% |
| E2E | 850.839 ms | 777.850 ms | -8.579% |

With receive coalescing and `[1K, 2K, 4K, 8K]` buckets, graph-token admission reached 100%:

| Workload / metric | C1 | C4 | C8 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `1024 -> 64` output-throughput delta | +8.935% | +0.346% | -0.534% |
| `1024 -> 1` request-throughput delta | +74.298% | +1.167% | +0.440% |
| `1024 -> 1` TTFT (eager -> BCG) | 164.864 -> 92.969 ms | 196.895 -> 194.525 ms | 320.755 -> 321.345 ms |

#### Correctness

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| Focused tests | 20 tests + 2 subtests passed |
| Primary performance samples | 42/42 completed exact request/input/output totals |
| Cold/warm all-rank parity | 64/64 eager/BCG pairs: exact 64-token completion, text, and token IDs across DP0-DP7 |
| Server health | 3/3 lifecycles exited 0; no post-ready HTTP 500, traceback, runtime error, or OOM |

### AgentX validation: DSpark + HiCache, eager vs breakable prefill CUDA graph

#### Requirements

- **Depends on #39007.** It adds `record_stream_for_v2_verify` / `record_stream_each` to the DSpark verify path; without it the target-verify tensors are not stream-lifetime-safe.
- **ROCm requires `SGLANG_ENABLE_WAR_BARRIER=1`.** The scheduler sets `_war_barrier_enabled = is_cuda() or SGLANG_ENABLE_WAR_BARRIER`, and `is_cuda()` is False on ROCm builds (`torch.version.cuda is None`), so the WAR barrier is on by default on NVIDIA but **off by default on ROCm**. title: [Diffusion] MiniMax-H3 VAE decoder: unfused w2 bias on SM12.x (cuBLAS 16x16 kernel mis-dispatch)
author: mickqian
body:
## What

On a DGX Spark (GB10, SM 12.1, CUDA 13.0 cuBLAS) the MiniMax-H3 video VAE decoder spends 40% of its time in one GEMM that cuBLAS mis-dispatches. The feed-forward's `w2` projection, `[~1800, 8192] × [8192, 2048]` in fp16/bf16 **with a fused bias** (`addmm`), lands on a `cutlass_80_wmma_tensorop 16x16` kernel at 14 TFLOPS (4.0 ms per call). The same product without the fused bias epilogue gets the normal tensor-op kernel at 76–91 TFLOPS (0.8 ms). The other three decoder GEMMs (qkv, out, w1) already run at 83–90 TFLOPS.

Tiled decode of an 864×480×124f video runs this GEMM 3780 times (105 tiles × 36 blocks): about 12 s of a 32 s decode.

## Fix

`FeedForward._forward_impl` computes `w2` as `matmul` + a separate in-place bias add on SM12.x only (`_unfused_bias_linear`); every other architecture keeps the fused `addmm`. The gate is a cached capability check, the extra bias pass is a 7 MB elementwise op per call. Numerically the two forms differ only in the order of the fp32-accumulated bias add.

## Measurements (GB10, fp16, M=1797)

| form | TFLOPS | per call |
|---|---|---|
| `F.linear` (fused bias) | 15.0 | 4.02 ms |
| `x @ wᵀ` + separate bias | 76–91 | 0.66–0.79 ms |
| batched tiles (M=3594), fused bias | 82 | 1.47 ms |

`cublasLt`, `allow_fp16_reduced_precision_reduction=False`, an NN layout and bf16 all still pick the 16×16 kernel for the fused form; the bias epilogue is what steers the heuristic. End-to-end on the Spark recipe (MiniMax-H3 fl2va, 864×480×124f, 20 steps, planner-chosen placement), same server code otherwise:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| VAE decode | 32.4 s | 19.2 s |
| warm request | 258 s | 245 s (ComfyUI 302.6 s) |

Text encoding (4.8 s) and denoise (205.5 s) unchanged.

title: Fix mamba radix cache ssm state indexing
author: ispobock
body:
## Motivation

Supersedes #33450 and closes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/31833, which was closed as completed but never landed a fix. The root-cause analysis and the kernel-side fix in the first commit are @adityakamat24's work from #33450, rebased onto current main.

With `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer` on a Mamba2 model, the mamba radix cache stores the wrong intermediate SSM state for most requests in a multi-request prefill batch. No crash, no assert, just a state taken at the wrong token position, so later prefix-cache hits continue from a corrupted state.

`_init_track_ssm_indices` indexes the packed per-chunk states `h` as a per-request concatenation of chunk grids. For Mamba2 it is one global grid over the flattened batch: `_chunk_state_fwd` computes `nchunks = ceil(seqlen / chunk_size)` where `seqlen` is the whole prefill batch, and `mamba.py` calls the kernel with `hidden_states_p.view(1, num_prefill_tokens, ...)`. The state for request `i` lives at flat token `query_start_loc[i] + aligned_len`, which is on the grid only when `query_start_loc[i]` is chunk-aligned. The first request in a batch always is, later ones generally are not, which is why single-request batches never see it.

The FLA branch is a genuine per-request grid and is untouched, so GDN/KDA models are unaffected. This is Mamba2 only.

The second commit keeps the read path where the position is on the grid, and rebuilds only the off-grid positions. Rebuilding everything is numerically correct but not bit-exact, and the rebuilt value depends on the flat offsets, so a chunk-aligned batch stops being reproducible.

Measured with sglang's own KL helpers on `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2` (`--mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer --enable-deterministic-inference`):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `logprobs_match` (floor) | 1.6608e-4 | 1.6608e-4 |
| `prefill_cache_hit` | 2.5834e-2 | **1.6835e-4** |
| `decode_cache_hit` | 5.2860e-5 | 5.2860e-5 |

`prefill_cache_hit` drops **153x** onto the model's own prefill/decode floor. The other two are bit-identical to main, so nothing outside the tracked-state path moved.

A cached state must not depend on what else was in the prefill batch that produced it. Filling the cache at concurrency 1 vs 16 and rescoring serially, on chunk-aligned prompt lengths:

| | main | #33450 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| max abs logprob delta | 0.000000 | 1.059 | 0.000000 |

## Accuracy

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 \
  --trust-remote-code --tp 1 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \
  --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer
```

```bash
sgl-eval run aime26 --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 \
  --n-repeats 8 --max-tokens 64000 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 \
  --num-threads 64
```

```
== aime26 ==
30 examples x 8 repeats  |  1804.8s  |  2901 tok/s  |  5.2M tokens

* pass@1[avg-of-8]  =  80.83% +/- 2.95% (SEM 1.04%)
  pass@8            =  93.33%
  majority@8        =  88.33%
  no_answer         =  0.83%
  stop_rate         =  99.17%
  truncated_rate    =  0.83%
  error_rate        =  0.00%
```

title: [AMD] Enable GLM DSA prefill top-k to the v2 kernel
author: EricKing626
body: ## Motivation **Add a packed-row top-k kernel to the DSA top-k v2 family and route GLM-5.x prefill through it. The prefill top-k kernel drops ~66% per launch; at ISL 70000 / OSL 300 that is +4.9% token throughput per GPU, −3.5% median TPOT and −4.8% median TTFT (geomean over concurrency 4-64); GSM8k 0.937 against 0.935 on the baseline.** PR #36684 and PR #36851 brought the v2 fused top-k to GLM-5.x on ROCm, but only decode ever reached it; prefill stayed on the legacy fused transform, which gathers the wide `page_size=1` table. The blocker was addressing, not math. The paged v2 entry assumes each row starts at column 0 of its own score row and owns one page-table row. DSA extend breaks both: all requests share one packed score buffer, so a row starts at some column in the middle, and every row of a request reads the same page-table row. Two lookup tables fix that, with no copy of the score buffer and no per-row page table, which at 327K context would be hundreds of MB per forward. The layout gets its own kernel because prefill row lengths vary within a launch: the level (register-2 / register-4 / streaming) has to be chosen per row at runtime, which the paged kernel, sized once off `max_seq_len`, cannot do. The packed entry also needs no `topk_v2_plan`, no cluster path and no compile-time level. ## Modifications **`topk_v2.cuh`** -- add `TopKPackedParams` and `topk_packed_kernel` next to `topk_ragged_kernel`, plus the `TopKKernel::transform_packed` host entry. Addressing, against the paged layout: | | paged entry (decode layout) | `transform_packed` (extend layout) | | --- | --- | --- | | score window of row `i` | `scores[i, :seq_lens[i]]` | `scores[i, row_starts[i] : row_starts[i] + seq_lens[i]]` | | page-table row | `page_tables[i]` | `page_tables[row_to_batch[i]]`, identity when `row_to_batch` is null | `row_starts` is required, `row_to_batch` optional. Shifting the score pointer keeps the selected index row-local, so the output path is untouched; the page-table row count must match the score row count only when `row_to_batch` is absent. Vector loads need the read base on a 4-float boundary, so the kernel rounds `row_starts[i]` down and masks the <= 3 columns ahead of the window in place. The level is then picked from the widened length, which keeps a row of exactly 8192 with a 3-column residue out of the register-2 implementation. Kernel, host entry and wrapper registration are behind `USE_ROCM`: only the ROCm DSA prefill emits this layout, and CUDA gets the same fusion from the ragged path. **`dsv4/topk.py`** -- register the `topk_transform_packed` wrapper when `is_hip_runtime()`, and add `topk_transform_packed_v2(scores, seq_lens, page_tables, out_page_indices, page_size, *, row_starts, row_to_batch=None)`. **`dsa/dsa_topk_backend.py`** -- route packed PAGED extend to `_topk_transform_v2_packed`, passing `ks` as `row_starts`. The row -> request map arrives whole-forward as `token_to_batch_idx` or per row-chunk as `batch_idx_list`, and both take this path: since #36960 capped the MQA-logits budget at aiter's 2 GiB `buffer_store` limit, a 70K prefill splits its rows on every forward but a request's first chunk, so routing only the whole-forward shape left 126 of 147 launches in a 70K trace on the legacy kernel (fixed by a6d769e). Two shapes fall back, checked in the dispatch so they do not trip the helper's asserts: a row stride that is not a multiple of 4, which the vectorized load needs and which an extend stride -- the batch's total KV length -- only satisfies by luck, and a `batch_idx_list` that is not a per-row tensor. The decode condition is left byte-identical, because `dsa_drop_wide_page_table` keys off exactly that condition. **`test_topk_v2.py`** -- `test_topk_v2_packed_rows` packs several requests into one score buffer, each with its own page-table permutation so a row/request mix-up cannot pass, and checks a row-local `torch.topk` reference; `test_topk_v2_packed_level_boundary` covers rows of exactly 8192 and 16384 with a 1-3 column masked residue, the case that overflows a register implementation if the level is picked from the un-widened length. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8k, 8x MI355X (gfx950), GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP=4, non-MTP: ``` $ python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1200 --parallel 1200 baseline: Accuracy: 0.935 Invalid: 0.000 this PR: Accuracy: 0.937 Invalid: 0.000 ``` `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_topk_v2.py` on gfx950: `300 passed`, including the 12 new packed cases. GSM8k prefills in one chunk, so the chunked route is covered separately: four concurrent ~78K-token prompts, three embedded access codes each, retrieved 12/12 with no cross-request leakage. Rows in those forwards span several requests, which is what `row_to_batch` addresses. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Baseline is main as merged (top-k v2 on, prefill still legacy); this PR is the prefill routing on top of it. Same build, same flags, non-MTP, 8x MI355X, TP4, `--max-running-requests 8`. **Kernel-level** -- prefill now launches `topk_packed_kernel`, which this series ran as `sglang::topk_main_kernel` up to 4bbbd19, while the packed addressing still lived in `TopKPagedParams`. It replaces `coop_topk_kernel`, the name ROCm traces show for the legacy transform since #37591 replaced the hipified source with a native one (`topk_transform_prefill_kernel` on CUDA), which is gone from the traces entirely. ISL 70000 / OSL 300 at concurrency 4, TP rank 0, same seed, grouped by launch grid (one block per score row): | grid.x | baseline | this PR | Δ | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 16384 | 896.8 µs/launch | 319.7 µs/launch | **−64.3%** | | 16383 | 1972.3 µs/launch | 649.1 µs/launch | **−67.1%** | | 10922 | 1679.8 µs/launch | 568.6 µs/launch | **−66.2%** | | 8191 | 1644.5 µs/launch | 570.5 µs/launch | **−65.3%** | | 5462 | 955.1 µs/launch | 315.4 µs/launch | **−67.0%** | Per rank over the profiled window (4 extend steps): 185.3 ms → 63.8 ms of top-k, against 2.8 s of extend kernel time. **End-to-end** -- ISL 70000 / OSL 300. title: sm120 32GB mem-tier: raise decode cuda-graph max_bs 24->48 + chunked_prefill 2k->4k
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation
On RTX 5090 (32GB, sm_120), the previous decode cuda-graph cap of max_bs=24 forced eager decode at bs>=32, collapsing high-concurrency throughput vs vLLM. 32GB Blackwell can hold decode cuda graphs well past bs=24.

## Change
- 32GB mem-tier (A10/4090/5090): decode cuda-graph max_bs 24->48 (tp<4) / 80->160 (tp>=4); chunked_prefill_size 2k->4k.
- Net effect on mem_fraction_static for 32GB is positive (~+2GB KV pool): the activation-token term is unchanged (clamped at max(chunked_prefill,2048)) while the larger cuda-graph workspace is captured before KV sizing, so only the real capture cost is reserved.

## Validation (RTX 5090 x8, vs vLLM 0.28, out_tok/s)
- Qwen3.5-9B: bs32 +4.4% vs vLLM (was -71% collapse before this fix).
- Qwen3.5-4B: bs4 +12.2%, bs16 +15.7%.
- Qwen2.5-VL-7B: bs1/4/16/32 all faster than vLLM (+2.4%/+1.1%/+4.6%/+4.9%).
- gpt-oss-20b: bs16 +6.6%, bs32 +8.3%.

Fixes eager-decode throughput collapse at bs>=32 on 32GB GPUs.

title: [diffusion] model: support VDN-H3 (hybrid window softmax + Video Delta linear attention MiniMax-H3, 8-NFE distill) with a hybrid_window_attn_h3 backend
author: kevin-mii
body:
## Motivation

Add [OpenVDN/vdn-minimax-h3](https://huggingface.co/OpenVDN/vdn-minimax-h3) (VDN-H3): MiniMax-H3 with hybrid attention (chunked window softmax + a Video Delta linear branch), 8-NFE DMD2 distill, t2va only, with the `hybrid_window_attn_h3` backend it was trained for.

8x B200, 1344x768 at 24 fps with audio, 14.375 s (345 frames, ~104k packed rows), `num_inference_steps: 9` (8 DiT forwards), seed 1000, Ulysses 8, eager, warmup at the served clip shape:

| Config | s/NFE | Denoise (8 forwards) | Request after warmup | Peak HBM |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| OpenVDN published (fp8, 5+3 branch-parallel Ulysses) | 1.40 | 11.2 s | - | - |
| SGLang default (online `mxfp8`) | **0.93** | **7.45 s** | **9.3 s** | 77.7 GB/GPU |

## Modifications

- **Model.** `VDNH3Pipeline` / `VDNH3PipelineConfig` / `VDNH3SamplingParams` live in their own `minimax_h3_vdn*` modules next to the H3 ones. The base H3 code changes in four places: the arch config gains a `hybrid_attention` field and one name-mapping rule, `MiniMaxH3Attention` builds one `hybrid` submodule and dispatches to it when the hybrid backend is selected, `MiniMaxH3MLP` hands `fc2` the fused SwiGLU+quant output when its quant method accepts it, and the denoising stage asks the VDN module for the request-static attention metadata. A revision-pinned model overlay (`kevin-mi/VDN-H3-overlay@2bf8c736`) materializes the repo into the base-H3 layout: prefused `default` + `turbo` LoRAs, the linear-branch weights, `hybrid_attention` in the transformer config. Admission forces `hybrid_window_attn_h3` for the transformer (a dense backend would silently skip the linear branch and the gates) and rejects `--model-variant`, `quality="high"`, ring, `torch.compile` and breakable CUDA graph.
- **`hybrid_window_attn_h3`.** Chunk-5 / radius-1 window with anchor frames as a union of FlashAttention varlen calls (dense-query rows against all keys, per-chunk gathered K/V passes bounded by `vdn_max_gather_rows`), softmax gate epilogue, request-static metadata built once per request.
- **Linear branch** (`minimax_h3_vdn.py`): short conv, TF32 frame statistics, Cholesky delta rule, forward/reverse scans, alpha-bridged boundary gather, gated RMSNorm readout, text-state seed; per-head independent, so Ulysses shards it exactly. Fused Triton kernels for the conv + SiLU + L2 norm (q written frame-major for the readout), statistics prologue, boundary gather and epilogue. The scans fold each chunk into one affine map and run one chain over the chunks with both directions per launch, since the chunked gather reads states at chunk boundaries only; the prompt's text state joins the frames' Cholesky/solve batch as a leading virtual frame.
- **Hybrid attention module** (`minimax_h3_vdn_attention.py`): out-of-place fused QK-norm + RoPE (a JIT variant of the H3 kernel, bit-equal to the in-place one) so the branch keeps the raw q/k. Under Ulysses q, k, v and the per-head scalars travel as four async field-major all-to-alls that land contiguous; only the 128-wide output-gate hidden is all-gathered (`up` runs on the head shard); the frame mean is a reshape-sum all-reduce. Served-shape warmup (`--warmup-num-frames` / `--warmup-resolutions`) landed separately in #37945.
- **fp8.** Online MXFP8 for bf16 checkpoints: `MXFP8OnlineLinearMethod` (`mxfp8_online.py`) sits behind the existing `MXFP8Config` when the checkpoint is not fp8-serialized. Weights quantize at load to e4m3 with one E8M0 scale per 32 elements in the cuBLASLt swizzled layout, and the GEMM is cuBLASLt's block-scaled `torch.nn.functional.scaled_mm`. The activation quant is fused into the producers (Triton kernels in `kernels/ops/diffusion/quantization/`, each byte-exact against `flashinfer.mxfp8_quantize` of the bf16 result): adaLN modulation + quant for the qkv and fc1 inputs (the qkv site keeps the bf16 rows for the VDN branch), SwiGLU + quant for fc2, and a plain quantizer for out_proj; linears take the `(fp8, scales)` tuple through `LinearMethodBase.accepts_mxfp8_input`. Layers with K not a multiple of 32 or fp32 params keep the per-channel path. VDN-H3 defaults to it on SM100+ (`--quantization fp8` selects it too, `--quantization bf16` opts out; before SM100 `fp8` stays per-channel); other models are unchanged.
- **Tests and docs.** `test_minimax_h3_vdn.py` (branch algorithm vs a from-scratch reference, boundary scans and fused kernels vs the plain chain through the real forward, head-slice contract, gather invariants, frame sums, config/registry contracts), `test_hybrid_window_h3_attention.py`, `test_vdn_ulysses_exchange_2_gpu.py`, `test_mxfp8_online_gemm.py`, the registered kernel tests `test_vdn_linear_branch.py`, `test_mxfp8_swizzled.py` and `test_qknorm_rope_out_of_place.py` (each kernel has a `can_use_*` predicate and a README row), GPU case `vdn_h3_t2va_4gpu_h100`, cookbook section and B200 / RTX PRO 6000 tables, attention-backend entry, the `vdn-h3` benchmark preset.

## Accuracy Tests

Block-level parity against OpenVDN's `HybridAttention` on blocks 0 / 25 / 49 with the prefused weights: relative L2 5e-3 to 7e-3 (the same band as the dense base+LoRA smoke). Ulysses 2 and 4 against the single-process full-sequence path on one real block: relative L2 2e-5, bitwise on most ranks. MXFP8, per-tensor and per-channel fp8 all sit at 5.8% relative L2 from bf16 on that block. The branch with the boundary scans and fused kernels matches the plain frame-chain / eager chain through the real forward, including the anchor-frame shift of the chunk grid.

Note for reviewers: two identical 8-GPU runs of the 8-step sampler agree at only ~19 dB PSNR (bf16 and atomic reduction order amplified over 8 steps), so end-to-end PSNR is not a meaningful gate for this model.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Profile-driven on 8x B200 (`--profile --num-profiled-timesteps 2`, kernels attributed to aten ops): the first port ran 1.24 s/NFE with ~30k launches per forward, half of them 6 us fp32 GEMMs from the 102-step frame scan. Chunk-boundary scans, contiguous K/V gathers, gate hidden + reshape-sum frame means, fused SwiGLU/quant + batched chains, the field-major exchange, MXFP8 into cuBLASLt with the quant fused into the producers, and the text state batched into the frame solve bring it to 0.93 s/NFE. Rank profile before the last two: 32% window FlashAttention, 24% fp8 GEMM, 12% NCCL, ~19.7k launches per forward.

Measured and not shipped: OpenVDN's branch-parallel layout (softmax and linear branches on disjoint rank groups) at 1.39 s/NFE (5+3) and 1.49 (6+2); two-group head-pipelined all-to-alls at 1.10; a static-tile Triton window kernel at 226 vs 169 ms per block; breakable CUDA graph capture runs out of memory at 104k rows. MXFP8 GEMM backends at the fc1/qkv shapes: cuBLASLt 3.40 ms, FlashInfer cuDNN 3.61, DeepGEMM 3.73, FlashInfer CUTLASS 4.18, CuTe-DSL 5.06, TRT-LLM 17.9 (decode-shaped).

## Deliberately not in this PR

- A switch for the branch-overlap schedule under Ulysses: the alternatives were measured (8x B200, steady s/NFE: no overlap 0.890, reordered collective 0.879, side stream 0.855; output bit-identical) and only the side-stream schedule ships.

## Known limitations

- t2va only; fl2va / ref2va were not trained. TP > 1 untested for the branch parameters.
- The 50-step checkpoint (`stage-b-step-2000`) is out of scope.
- **License note for maintainers:** the checkpoint inherits the MiniMax-H3 Community License.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [diffusion] Support LLaDA-Image BF16 generation and editing
author: rwang5203
body:
## Motivation

Add native SGLang Diffusion serving for [inclusionAI/LLaDA-Image](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/LLaDA-Image) and [inclusionAI/LLaDA-Image-Turbo](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/LLaDA-Image-Turbo) in BF16 on a single GPU. The integration supports text-to-image generation and single-image editing through the OpenAI-compatible Images API. Sequence parallelism and the FP8 checkpoints follow in a separate PR.

## Contributors

- InclusionAI, Ant Group. Kun Chen (@kunchengit), Chengzhang Wu (@Anmuliar), Chaoyang Wang (@wzy-ustc)
- SGLang community. Kaige Li (@stephenkgli), Yuhan Zhou (@Dayuxiaoshui), Yihao Wang (@AgainstEntropy), Mick Qian (@mickqian), Richard Wang (@rwang5203)

## Modifications

- **Pipeline.** Add the LLaDA-Image DiT, pipeline configuration, sampling parameters, flow-match scheduler support for its sigma schedule, an embedded LLaDA2 MoE text encoder, source-image conditioning, and its registration in the model's own config module.
- **Serving.** Support `/v1/images/generations` and `/v1/images/edits`, with request validation for image dimensions and text length. Request validation errors from the Images API now return 400 with their message instead of 500 for every image model, as the video API already does.
- **Text encoder.** The LLaDA2 MoE text encoder runs as an embedded srt model with its own runtime context, its own srt process groups, and a FlashInfer attention backend that applies the conditioning mask. While it builds its groups it sets aside the TP, attention TP, and MoE groups that the diffusion runtime mirrors into srt, restores them afterwards, and uses its own groups for each encode. The srt changes below act only when the LLaDA-Image pipeline builds this encoder, except the LLaDA2 loading step, which leaves existing LLaDA2 checkpoints loading as before.
- **srt attention backend.** `llada2_cfg_flashinfer` subclasses the FlashInfer backend. When a forward batch carries LLaDA-Image conditioning text lengths, it plans one ragged prefill with a per-request mask in which text tokens attend only to text tokens and query tokens attend to the whole sequence, and it refuses decode, speculative, cached-prefix, and multi-wrapper batches. Every other batch runs the stock FlashInfer path.
- **srt forward batch.** `ForwardBatch.llada_image_conditioning_text_lens_cpu` carries those lengths through batch rebuilds. It defaults to `None`, so other batches are unchanged, and the encoder raises an error if a forward ran without the mask.
- **srt runtime context.** `create_context` builds a runtime context for the embedded encoder without replacing the diffusion worker's published config, and `use_context` activates it around encoder setup and each encode, restoring the previous context on exit and on error. `publish` now shares its configuration step with `create_context` and behaves as before.
- **srt LLaDA2 model.** `LLaDA2MoeModelLM` gains `get_input_embeddings`, and its weight loading maps the encoder checkpoint's `model.language_model.*` and `model.lm_head.*` names and its fused expert tensors to the native layout.
- **Safety and lifecycle.** Propagate the checkpoint revision and remote-code trust into the embedded encoder, keep the encoder resident, and reject multi-GPU, quantized, and cache-dit launches at startup with a clear error.
- **Defaults.** `inclusionAI/LLaDA-Image` uses the model card recipe of 50 steps and guidance 5.0, and `inclusionAI/LLaDA-Image-Turbo` registers its own 4 step defaults without CFG.
- **Input limits.** Generation sizes must be multiples of 16 and editing sizes multiples of 32, as in the reference pipeline, checked when the request is validated. An editing size whose image tokens alone exceed the 32768-row sequence RoPE table is refused there too, and the DiT checks the exact length with the prompt before the RoPE lookup, so an oversized edit no longer breaks the worker for later requests.
- **Editing source.** The source image is resized to the full output frame instead of center cropped, matching the reference pipeline for sources whose aspect ratio differs from the output.

## Reproduction

Start Turbo.

```bash
sglang serve --model-path inclusionAI/LLaDA-Image-Turbo --revision f4afc52d925bbac4e22a1c947111fc1f127e37e5 --trust-remote-code --port 30000
```

Start Base.

```bash
sglang serve --model-path inclusionAI/LLaDA-Image --revision e4e2703f410f7ddb6ee8d6b09dac6a8ec5093039 --trust-remote-code --port 30000
```

Generate an image with Turbo.

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/images/generations -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"A cinematic photograph of a red fox standing in fresh snow at golden hour, detailed fur, shallow depth of field","size":"1024x1024","n":1,"response_format":"b64_json","num_inference_steps":4,"guidance_scale":1.0,"seed":42}'
```

Edit an image with Turbo.

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/images/edits -F "image=@input.png" -F "prompt=Place the subject on a beach" -F "size=1024x1024" -F "n=1" -F "response_format=b64_json" -F "num_inference_steps=4" -F "guidance_scale=1.0" -F "seed=42"
```

For Base, use `"num_inference_steps":50` and `"guidance_scale":5.0`.

## Accuracy Tests

These quality results were measured with the BF16 single-GPU path at an earlier revision of this branch. A re-run on the final commit with the same prompts, seeds, and evaluators is in progress, and this section will be updated with its results.

The benchmark generated and decoded all 6704 expected artifacts, 2212 GenEval images, 1280 LongText images, 1212 GEdit images, and 2000 CVTG images.

| Configuration | GenEval macro | LongText en | LongText zh | CVTG Word Accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Base BF16 | 0.8404 | 0.9120 | 0.9198 | 0.7792 |
| Turbo 4-step | 0.8190 | 0.8959 | 0.9123 | 0.8267 |

Base used 20 steps for GenEval and CVTG and 50 steps for LongText, all with CFG 5. Turbo used 4 steps with CFG 1.

| Turbo GEdit metric | Score |
| --- | ---: |
| en semantic / quality / overall | 7.9242 / 7.3682 / 7.5728 |
| zh semantic / quality / overall | 7.7375 / 7.3867 / 7.4347 |

The GEdit scores predate the editing source change above, which resizes the source to the full output frame instead of center cropping it.

The final commit also passes these checks.

- Both registered LLaDA-Image server cases, text to image and editing, pass in CI, including their performance baseline checks.
- The srt unit tests touched here pass in the CPU CI job.
- The new LLaDA2 loading step yields every tensor of LLaDA2.0-mini, LLaDA2.1-mini, and LLaDA2.2-mini with its name and data unchanged, so these checkpoints load as they do on main.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The following values are median client-wall latency measured on this branch before its latest merges of main, on one NVIDIA H200 at 1024x1024 with one request at a time. Each cell pools 40 measured requests from four fresh server processes, each running two warmups and then ten measured requests.

| Task | Turbo 4-step | Base 50-step |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| T2I | 0.5822s | 13.1110s |
| Edit | 1.4372s | 31.4010s |

## Known Limitations

- The embedded text encoder requires reviewed remote code, so deployments must use `--trust-remote-code` and should pin the checkpoint revision.
- Sequence parallelism and the FP8 checkpoints are not served by this PR and are refused at startup. They follow in a separate PR.
- The embedded text encoder must remain resident and does not support generic memory sleep or hot weight updates.
- An edit with more than one source image, or an edit whose prompt and image together exceed the 32768-row sequence limit, is refused by the worker without affecting later requests, but the client receives a 500 response instead of a 400. A follow-up PR moves both checks into request validation.

title: [Diffusion] Fuse LingBot per-token gated residual and RMSNorm modulate
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

LingBot Video (MoE 30B-A3B) applies a per-token gated residual and an adaLN modulation chain at every DiT block:

- `x = x + (gate * update).to(x.dtype)` with a per-token `gate [B, S, 1]`
- `(rmsnorm(x) * (1 + scale) + shift).to(dtype)` with per-token `scale`/`shift` that are non-contiguous `[B, S, 6D]` chunk views

On a single B300 the extra-high profile shows a large elementwise/copy ladder around these chains. Neither was fused: the existing bit-exact `residual_gate_add` had no per-token gate mode, and the bit-exact `rmsnorm_scale_shift_bitexact` is ERNIE-specific (it replicates one platform's exact RMSNorm reduction order, which does not match LingBot's custom FP32 RMSNorm).

## Modifications

- **`residual_gate_add` per-token gate mode (JIT CUDA).** Add a third gate mode (`kPerToken`): one scalar per row, broadcast along the hidden dim. Full and row-broadcast modes are unchanged (backward-compatible).
- **New `rmsnorm_scale_shift_per_token` (Triton).** Fuses RMSNorm + `* (1 + scale) + shift` + output cast in one pass, reading the strided `[B, S, 6D]` adaLN chunk views directly via their row stride (no `.contiguous()` copies). Runs the whole chain in fp32 with a single rounding to the output dtype.
- **Request-gated wiring.** Both are mounted through a `QualityGatedFusion` site for `quality="extra-high"`/`"high"`. The default `quality="lossless"` path is unchanged and bit-exact. These fusions are numerically equivalent only at half-precision rounding level (not bit-exact), matching the existing quality-gated LingBot RMSNorm fusion precedent.

## Reproduction command

Single B300, LingBot Video MoE, `384x640`, 17 frames, 12 steps, request warmup:

```bash
sglang generate --backend=sglang \
  --model-path robbyant/lingbot-video-moe-30b-a3b \
  --prompt "A cat walks across a sunny garden." \
  --width 384 --height 640 --num-frames 17 --fps 16 \
  --num-inference-steps 12 --performance-mode manual \
  --num-gpus 1 --seed 42 --quality extra-high --warmup-mode request \
  --save-output
```

## Accuracy Tests

- `quality="lossless"` (default): unchanged and bit-exact. Two identical lossless runs produce identical output (`md5` `395ec1ff…` both), and the lossless helper path is the unmodified reference chain.
- New unit coverage in `test_modulate.py`: per-token `residual_gate_add` (bit-exact `torch.equal`, 3 dtypes) and `rmsnorm_scale_shift_per_token` (bf16/fp16 rounding tolerance vs the eager reference, including non-contiguous `[B, S, 6D]` chunk views and guard rejections).

```text
pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_modulate.py
1020 passed

pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_import_surface.py
passed (all kernel imports routed through the sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion facade)
```

The `extra-high` output differs from `lossless` only at bf16 rounding level, the same quality class as the already-merged quality-gated LingBot RMSNorm fusion.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hardware: one NVIDIA B300 (275 GB). Model: `robbyant/lingbot-video-moe-30b-a3b`, `384x640`, 17 frames, 12 steps, BF16.

| Measurement | Denoise | Note |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| main, `quality=lossless` | 3.242 s | reference |
| main, `quality=extra-high` (RMSNorm fusion only) | 2.450 s | already on main |
| **this PR, `quality=extra-high`** | **2.363 s** | **-3.5% vs main extra-high, -27.1% vs lossless** |

Per-site microbenchmark (`[1, 4813, 2048]` bf16, real serving shape): the fused `rmsnorm+scale+shift` kernel is **6.84x** the eager chain (251 µs → 37 µs), and the strided-read design avoids the `.contiguous()` copies that otherwise cancel the gain.

The extra-high torch.profiler trace confirms `_rmsnorm_scale_shift_kernel` and `residual_gate_add_vec_kernel` replace the corresponding elementwise ladder; the fused-MoE GEMM (46%) is untouched and remains the dominant compute-bound term.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code with pre-commit (ruff-format, clang-format).
- [x] Add unit tests (`test_modulate.py`).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results above.
- [x] Update documentation (`fused_kernels.mdx` request-gated set + model summary).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance.

title: [Perf] Unified memory: close the DCP decode gap on Blackwell
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

Unified memory (`--enable-unified-memory`) under decode context parallelism was
measurably slower than the static pool on Blackwell. The Hopper fix (#37511) did
not carry over: on a B300 with Kimi-Linear at TP2/DCP2 and `cutedsl_mla`, the
unified pool ran **1.96% behind static** (worst config -4.06%).

Profiling showed the gap is entirely CPU-side. GPU kernel time was slightly
*lower* for the unified pool, while it issued ~456 more `cudaLaunchKernel` calls
per profiled window. A Blackwell decode step is short enough that per-step
launch overhead is visible; the same overhead hides inside a Hopper step.

Two structural causes, both fixed here.

**The write-loc translate ran as an eager op chain.** Converting a virtual write
loc to kernel-facing ids is `v2p[t // ps] * ps * mult + t % ps` clamped at 0,
which is ~6 torch ops, and ~12 once the DCP owner rule (`loc % dcp_size ==
dcp_rank`) is resolved on top. It runs per forward, outside any CUDA graph, so
every op is a real launch on the critical path. It is now one Triton kernel.

**The unified pool was excluded from the mamba fused replay state-indices
path.** The gate's stated reason was that its mapping is "not a flat table
gather", which was not true: `UnifiedMambaSlotAllocator.translate` is exactly
`virtual_to_physical[virtual_ids]`. Teaching the fused kernel one optional v2p
gather lets the unified pool take the single-launch path like every other pool.

## Modification

Three commits.

1. **Fuse the write-loc translate into one kernel.** New
   `write_loc_to_kernel_ids` in `kernels/ops/memory/virtual_slot.py`, with a
   pure-torch CPU branch so the allocator's CPU suites still exercise it. An
   `out_width` argument fills a live prefix and zeroes the tail in the same
   launch.
2. **Let the unified pool take the fused replay state-indices path.**
   `_fused_replay_state_indices_kernel` gains an optional `v2p` gather, and the
   backend gate becomes `pool.mamba_translate_is_fusable` instead of a hand
   list, so a pool answers for itself.
3. **Translate the write loc straight into the capture buffer.** Replaces the
   copy-and-zero the trtllm_mla and triton backends did over an
   already-translated loc.

The write-loc translate stays where it was, at `ForwardBatch` construction. An
earlier revision of this PR moved it to attention-metadata-init time so a
backend could name its own destination. That was dropped: it broke captured
decode for every unified-memory backend that did not implement the new hook,
because the capture-time translate rebound `out_cache_loc` to a transient
tensor whose address the graph then baked. `TestKimiLinearUnifiedMemory`
caught it in CI, since the default backend there resolves to fa3, which has no
such hook. Neither fa3 (SM 80-90 only) nor flashinfer (package version) can run
on the B300 this was developed on, which is why local testing missed it.

Two bugs surfaced only once the translate moved later, both appearing as
`index >= ... (out of range): set_mla_kv_buffer` with GSM8K 0.000, far from
their cause:

- **Slot 0 was being sent through v2p.** It is the reserved padding anchor in
  every id space, and the runner pads a write loc with zeros to mean that sink.
  Construction never saw those zeros because padding ran after the translate.
  Since the pool grows *down*, `v2p[0]` can name a top physical page whose
  kernel id runs past the KV buffer's rows, so this was an illegal write rather
  than merely an out-of-range index.
- **`capture_write_loc_dest` was forwarded by neither wrapper layer.** For
  Kimi-Linear the runner hands the translate a `HybridLinearAttnBackend`
  wrapping a `HybridAttnBackend` wrapping the MLA backend. Both now forward.

## Accuracy

Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct, B300, TP2, DCP2, `cutedsl_mla`, with
`SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT=1` armed so a virtual id reaching a write door is
caught:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_kimi_linear_unified_memory_dcp_blackwell.py` | 2 passed, GSM8K 0.905, zero write-door probe hits |
| Unit sweep over mem_cache, model_executor, attention, DCP metadata, mamba kernels | 3031 passed, 2662 subtests |

Both re-run after rebasing onto current main.

## Benchmark

Unified vs static, same server args, sequential (one server at a time) with
`flush_cache` before every measurement, 8 reps, paired per-rep ratios, bootstrap
CI. Kimi-Linear, B300, TP2/DCP2, `cutedsl_mla`, batch 1/8/31 at 2048/128 and
8192/64.

| Stage | Pooled median vs static | 95% CI | Worst config |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before this PR | -1.96% | [-2.21%, -1.23%] | -4.06% |
| + write-loc fusion | -1.96% | [-2.21%, -1.23%] | -4.06% |
| + mamba fused replay | -0.51% | [-0.59%, -0.37%] | -0.94% |
| + capture-buffer translate (this PR) | -0.18% | [-0.59%, +0.13%] | -0.60% |

These three commits bring the unified pool to parity, inside the 0.5% target,
and it is faster than static in 3 of 6 configs.

**Methodology note for anyone reproducing this.** Do not compare a number from
one session against a number from another. Between two back-to-back sessions the
*untouched* static arm drifted +0.58% while the arm under test moved -1.74%,
manufacturing a 1.78 pp regression that interleaving showed to be -0.25%.
Session drift on this box is worth about +-0.6% on identical code.

## Capacity

No capacity regression. Both pools report 2,172,096 usable tokens when
`--max-running-requests` is matched. An apparent 4.5x loss in an earlier
measurement was an artifact of requesting 128 concurrent requests against a
mamba state cache that supports 31.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#running-unit-tests-adding-file-to-test-suite).
- [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#writing-documentation).

title: [Bugfix] Keep a shared MAX_LEN prefill CUDA graph bucket when the graph captures a DP gather (MegaMoE sparse-DP hang)
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #37561. Thanks to @shyeh25 for reporting the hang and bisecting it to #33871.

#33871 lets MegaMoE DP ranks replay prefill CUDA graphs under `SUM_LEN` with per-rank buckets and exempts MegaMoE from the sparse-DP eager fallback. That is only safe when nothing captured in the graph depends on the DP token geometry. The graph body is captured with `MAX_LEN` geometry (`dp_padding_mode = get_default_mode_in_cuda_graph()`, `global_num_tokens_gpu = [bucket] * dp_size`, frozen after capture), so a DP gather/scatter recorded inside it only matches when every DP rank replays the same bucket. Kimi-K3's dense layer 0 runs `dp_gather_replicate` over the full TP group inside the graph (`first_k_dense_replace=1`, `enable_dense_mlp_attn_tp` off by default), and two failure modes follow:

- **Idle DP rank** (the report): under `SUM_LEN` the 0-token rank never gets the fabricated `EXTEND` row (that conversion only runs under `MAX_LEN`), stays `IDLE` and runs eager, issuing the `SUM_LEN` `tp all_reduce(8 x 7168 = 57344)`; the busy rank replays the graph containing `attention_tp reduce_scatter + tp all_gather`. NCCL deadlocks with exactly the two signatures in the issue.
- **All ranks busy, different buckets**: DP0 on bucket 8 and DP1 on bucket 256 replay `all_gather` calls with 1 row and 32 rows per GPU into the same 16-GPU collective. Reproduced on the first same-step pair; the earlier probes had missed it because decode steps kept the two ranks' prefills apart.

DSV4-Flash does not route its dense layer through the TP-group gather under an a2a backend, which is why the #33871 validation did not hit either case.

## Modifications

- `DpFlags.capturing_prefill_graph` is set for the duration of `PrefillCudaGraphRunner.capture()`; `_dp_gather`, `dp_scatter` and `dp_reduce_scatter_tensor` latch `DpFlags.prefill_graph_has_dp_gather` when they run inside it.
- `prefill_graph_tolerates_sum_len()` returns `False` for graphs that captured a DP gather/scatter. Those models keep the pre-#33871 shared `MAX_LEN` bucket, which also covers their idle-rank case (the idle rank gets its fabricated row and replays with the others). Graphs without such a collective keep the #33871 per-rank `SUM_LEN` buckets, including sparse-DP steps.
- The gate is a graph-capability check, not a per-model list; the runner logs `Prefill CUDA graph captured a DP gather/scatter; DP ranks will replay a shared MAX_LEN bucket.` when it triggers.
- Regression tests in `test_prefill_cuda_graph_padding.py` (fail on the pre-fix code, pass with the fix).

## Validation

All runs use the issue's container `nightly-dev-cu13-20260901-07c8f729` with the patch applied in place, `--cuda-graph-bs-prefill 8 16 32 64 128 256`, `--dist-timeout 300`, and a probe that fires prefill-only requests to different DP ranks behind a barrier so they land in the same scheduler step.

| Run | Config | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Kimi-K3 mxfp4, 4 nodes x 4 GB300, TP16/DP2/EP16, MegaMoE, breakable BCG (issue recipe), unpatched | issue's 8-token request to DP0 | hang; watchdog `ALLREDUCE NumelIn=57344` (tp) + `ALLREDUCE NumelIn=0` (attention_tp) |
| same, with only the zero-token fallback (earlier revision of this PR) | same-step pair 8 tok -> DP0, 200 tok -> DP1 | hang on round 0; `global_num_tokens_cpu=[8, 200]`, `dp_padding=SUM_LEN`, DP0 bucket 8 / DP1 bucket 256 |
| same, this PR | detection fires (`captured a DP gather`); 16/16 same-step unequal-length pairs plus sparse requests | pass, every step `MAX_LEN` with a shared bucket, no watchdog |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash fp8, 1 node x 4 GB300, TP4/DP4/EP4, MegaMoE, breakable BCG, this PR | detection does not fire; 12 rounds mixing all-busy (`[8, 40, 100, 200]` -> buckets 8/64/128/256 under `SUM_LEN`) and sparse (`[8, 0, 0, 0]`, `[0, 40, 100, 0]`, ...) | pass, per-rank buckets kept, outputs match alone runs, no watchdog |
| CPU unit tests in the same container | pre-fix / post-fix | 3 failed / 6 passed |

## Accuracy Tests

Not affected: graphs with a captured DP gather take exactly the pre-#33871 `MAX_LEN` path; graphs without one are unchanged from #33871.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Every #33871 optimization is preserved: graphs without a shape-sensitive DP collective keep per-rank `SUM_LEN` buckets for all-busy and sparse-DP steps (DSV4-Flash + MegaMoE above), and the idle-rank dummy-token masking is untouched. Only graphs that captured a DP gather (Kimi-K3 default config) fall back to the pre-#33871 shared `MAX_LEN` bucket, which is the only geometry those graphs can replay correctly today.

## Follow-up: restoring per-rank buckets for graphs with a DP gather

The gate is conservative by design. We plan a follow-up PR that brings the per-rank bucket optimization to Kimi-K3-style models by making the in-graph DP gather geometry-independent rather than by relaxing the check; once that lands, the detection here simply stops firing for those models. Candidate approaches:

- Mark the shape-sensitive DP gather/scatter (or the dense MLP that owns it) as an `eager_on_graph` break so it runs eagerly with the live `SUM_LEN` sizes, exactly like the MoE a2a break already does. Kimi-K3 has one dense layer, so this costs one extra graph break.
- `--enable-dense-mlp-attn-tp` shards the dense MLP inside the attention-TP group and removes the DP gather entirely (the detection then does not fire). On GPU + MegaMoE it currently hangs on a plain sparse request even with the shared bucket, so it needs its own fix before it is a usable opt-in. The follow-up will start from the first option.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Perf] Vectorize alloc_extend_naive to remove the per-request Python loop
author: alexnails
body:
# Vectorize `alloc_extend_naive`

## The contract

For each request `i`, `alloc_extend_naive` fills `out_indices[start_pos[i] : end_pos[i]]`
(the request's extend span) with up to three consecutive runs of KV-cache slot
indices:

1. **Finish the current partial page** — up to `num1` tokens, continuing directly
   after `last_loc[i]` (i.e. `last_loc[i] + 1, last_loc[i] + 2, ...`). This only
   exists if `prefix_lens[i]` isn't already page-aligned.
2. **Whole new pages** — `num2` tokens (a multiple of `page_size`), each new page's
   slots taken in order from `free_pages`.
3. **Start of one final new page** — `num3` tokens, the remainder from the last
   page this request touches.

`num1 + num2 + num3 == extend_lens[i]` always, and each phase is skipped when its
count is 0. This rewrite computes exactly this, with no behavioral change — it
just computes every request's phases in parallel instead of in a Python loop.

## Phase-by-phase mapping (loop -> vectorized)

The old loop, per request `i`:

```python
num1 = min(seq_lens[i], ceil(prefix_lens[i])) - prefix_lens[i]
if num1: out_indices[start_pos[i]:start_pos[i]+num1] = last_loc[i] + 1 + arange(num1)
if prefix_lens[i] + num1 == seq_lens[i]: continue
num2 = (floor(seq_lens[i]) - ceil(prefix_lens[i]))
if num2: out_indices[...] = free_pages[start_new_pages[i]:end_new_pages[i]-need_page[i]] * page_size + arange(page_size) broadcast
if prefix_lens[i] + num1 + num2 == seq_lens[i]: continue
num3 = seq_lens[i] - floor(seq_lens[i])
if num3: out_indices[end_pos[i]-num3:end_pos[i]] = free_pages[end_new_pages[i]-1] * page_size + arange(num3)
```
(`ceil(x) = ceil_div(x, page_size) * page_size`, `floor(x) = (x // page_size) * page_size`.)

The new code computes, once, for the whole batch:

- `num1 = clamp(seq_lens, max=ceil_prefix) - prefix_lens` — identical formula,
  vectorized (`min` -> `torch.clamp(..., max=...)`).
- `done_after_1 = (prefix_lens + num1) == seq_lens` — this is exactly the loop's
  first `if ... == seq_lens[i]: continue` condition, computed for every request
  instead of tested per-iteration.
- `num2 = where(done_after_1, 0, floor_seq - ceil_prefix)`,
  `num3 = where(done_after_1, 0, seq_lens - floor_seq)` — identical formulas to
  the loop's `num2`/`num3`, but masked to 0 whenever the loop would have hit
  `continue` before computing them (so a request that finishes in phase 1 never
  contributes phantom phase-2/3 tokens or page demand — this is what makes
  `pages_per_req` below match the loop's actual page consumption, not the
  unconditional `num_new_pages` formula the loop computes up front but only
  partially uses).
- `pages_per_req = num2 // page_size + (num3 > 0)`, then
  `start_new_pages`/`end_new_pages` via cumsum — same role as the loop's
  `start_new_pages[i]`/`end_new_pages[i] - need_page[i]` (for phase 2) and
  `end_new_pages[i] - 1` (for phase 3); page assignment order across the whole
  batch is unchanged because it derives from the same running total of pages
  consumed so far, now computed once as a cumsum instead of incrementally by
  the loop.

Then, per **output slot** `j` (not per request):

- `owner = torch.searchsorted(end_pos, j, right=True)` maps slot `j` to its
  owning request `i` — `end_pos` is the exclusive-cumsum of `extend_lens`, so
  this is precisely "which request's `[start_pos[i], end_pos[i])` range contains
  `j`". `local = j - start_pos[owner]` is the offset within that request's
  extend, i.e. the loop variable that ranges implicitly over
  `pos_in_page[:numK]` / `arange(numK)` inside each `if numK:` block.
- `is_phase1 = local < num1_g`, `is_phase2 = ~is_phase1 & (local < num1_g + num2_g)`,
  else phase 3 — this is exactly which of the three loop branches slot `j`
  would have landed in.
- `val_phase1 = last_loc_g + 1 + local` — identical to the loop's phase-1 RHS.
- `val_phase2 = free_pages[start_new_pages_g + (local - num1_g) // page_size] * page_size + (local - num1_g) % page_size`
  — the loop's phase-2 RHS was `(free_pages[start:end].view(-1,1) + pos_in_page.view(1,-1)).view(-1)`,
  i.e. page `(local - num1) // page_size` of the slice, offset `(local - num1) % page_size`
  within it. Same page, same offset, computed directly instead of via a 2D
  broadcast + reshape.
- `val_phase3 = free_pages[end_new_pages_g - 1] * page_size + (local - num1_g - num2_g)`
  — identical to the loop's phase-3 RHS (`free_pages[end_new_pages[i]-1]`, offset
  `local` within the final page, which is `rel3` here since `num1+num2` tokens
  were already consumed).
- `out_indices = where(is_phase1, val_phase1, where(is_phase2, val_phase2, val_phase3))`
  selects the one formula that actually applies, per slot — this replaces the
  loop's `if numK:`/`continue` control flow with a per-slot select.

## Edge cases preserved

- **Zero-length extends** (`extend_lens[i] == 0`): contributes no slots to `j`
  (its `[start_pos[i], end_pos[i])` range is empty), exactly as the old loop's
  body would do nothing meaningful for it (there are no output indices to write).
- **Prefix exactly on a page boundary** (`prefix_lens[i] % page_size == 0`):
  `ceil_prefix == prefix_lens[i]`, so `num1 = 0` and phase 1 is skipped for
  every slot of that request — same as the loop never entering its `if num1:`
  block.
- **`num1 == 0`**: `is_phase1` is `False` for all of that request's slots;
  `val_phase1` is still computed (torch.where doesn't short-circuit) but never
  selected.
- **`num2 == 0`**: `is_phase2` is `False` for all of that request's slots
  (`num1_g + num2_g == num1_g`); `val_phase2` is still computed but never
  selected.
- **Tight free-page pool** (`free_pages` sized to exactly `num_new_pages.sum()`):
  `page_idx2`/`page_idx3` land exactly in `[0, free_pages.numel()-1]` for every
  slot whose phase actually needs a page, by construction of `start_new_pages`/
  `end_new_pages` as a running cumsum over the same total.

## Two bugs this surfaced, and why the fix is a host-side shape guard

`torch.where` evaluates **both** branches for every element — unlike the loop's
`if num2:` / `if num3:`, which never touch `free_pages` at all when a phase is
absent for a given request. So `val_phase2`/`val_phase3` are computed for every
slot regardless of whether that phase is ever selected there, which means the
index expressions feeding `free_pages[...]` must be valid for *every* slot, not
just the ones where the branch is live.

A 20,000-case randomized differential test against the original loop (see
below) initially crashed with `IndexError: index is out of bounds for dimension
with size 0`. The generator explicitly includes the shapes that produce this:
every request's extend fitting entirely inside its already-partially-used page
(so `pages_per_req.sum() == 0` and, for a tight pool, `free_pages` is empty),
the same shape mixed with requests that do need real pages in the same batch,
and `page_size=1` with an empty pool. Root-caused to two instances of the same
defect:

- `page_idx2` was clamped only on the upper bound (`max=free_pages.numel()-1`),
  which is `-1` when `free_pages` is empty, and `free_pages[-1]` on an empty
  tensor raises.
- `page_idx3`, which the fix was first modeled on by analogy, had the *identical*
  defect in the other direction (`min=0`, no upper bound) — and reproducing it
  in isolation confirmed indexing an empty `free_pages` at index `0` raises just
  as much as at index `-1`. **No amount of clamping rescues an index into a
  zero-length tensor** — there is no valid index into an empty array.

The actual fix is a host-side shape guard:

```python
if free_pages.numel() == 0:
    out_indices.copy_(last_loc_g + 1 + local)
    return
```

`free_pages.numel()` is static shape metadata, not a value read off the tensor's
data — reading it costs no host<->device sync on any backend, so this doesn't
reintroduce the kind of stall the rewrite is trying to remove. The guard is
correct because **`free_pages.numel() == 0` at this call site can only mean
every request in the batch needs zero new pages** (verified below, not
assumed), in which case every output slot is phase 1 by construction and no
`free_pages` read is needed. `page_idx2`/`page_idx3` are also now defensively
`min`/`max`-clamped to `[0, free_pages.numel()-1]` for the surviving (non-empty)
path — this is a no-op for well-formed inputs (the cumsum construction already
keeps them in range), it just closes the same class of gap if that ever stops
holding.

**Verifying the invariant, not assuming it.** Both real callers of
`alloc_extend_naive` guard the call:

- `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/allocator_npu.py` (`alloc_extend`):
  `if num_new_pages_item > len(self.free_pages): return None` before calling
  `alloc_extend_naive` with `self.free_pages` unchanged.
- `tools/sglang-simulator/.../mem_cache_allocator.py` (`_alloc_extend_cpu`):
  same pattern, `if num_new_pages > len(self.free_pages): return None`.

So by the time either caller reaches `alloc_extend_naive`, `free_pages.numel() >=
num_new_pages.sum()` always holds; `free_pages.numel() == 0` therefore implies
`num_new_pages.sum() == 0`. If a caller ever violated that contract instead
(passed a `free_pages` smaller than actually needed), **the original loop is
already broken for that input too** — confirmed directly: passing a
genuinely-too-small `free_pages` to the original raises `RuntimeError: The
expanded size of the tensor (16) must match the existing size (0)` from the
phase-2 slice-assignment shape mismatch. The new code fails differently (either
via the shape guard's now-safe path, if the whole-batch-zero case doesn't apply,
or via the same class of crash the clamps guard against), but it does not
silently produce wrong output for contract-violating input — it was never a
supported input for the old implementation either, and this PR does not try to
make it one.

## Measured speedup (CPU, `torch.set_num_threads(1)`)

| bs   | page_size=1 | page_size=16 | page_size=64 | page_size=128 |
|-----:|------------:|-------------:|-------------:|--------------:|
| 1    | 0.86x       | 1.15x        | 1.13x        | 0.94x         |
| 8    | 3.42x       | 5.20x        | 4.46x        | 4.47x         |
| 64   | 9.14x       | 12.61x       | 12.20x       | 12.89x        |
| 256  | 12.00x      | 17.24x       | 14.73x       | 16.00x        |
| 1024 | 11.52x      | 15.40x       | 13.85x       | 13.40x        |

At `bs=1` both implementations take roughly 40-55us/call and the two are within
measurement noise of each other; across repeated runs the vectorized version
came out mildly *slower* for `page_size` in `{1, 128}` (0.84x-0.94x) and mildly
*faster* for `{16, 64}` (1.09x-1.15x). Reporting this honestly rather than
rounding it into a win: there is no consistent speedup at `bs=1`, and for two of
the four page sizes tested it's a small regression. The benefit is entirely a
function of batch size — vectorizing a loop that only ever ran once doesn't pay
for the extra tensor ops it replaces it with, but by `bs=8` it's already a clear
win everywhere, growing to 9-17x by `bs=64` and beyond.

The speedup also depends strongly on **extend length**, not batch size alone,
because the two implementations scale differently: the old loop's cost is
O(batch) Python dispatch and is nearly independent of how many tokens each
request extends by, while the vectorized version's cost scales with the total
token count. Same page_size=16, varying the per-request extend length:

| extend length per request | bs=64 | bs=1024 |
|---------------------------|------:|--------:|
| 1-8 tokens (decode-like)  | 20.3x | 109.5x  |
| 32-64 tokens              | 24.5x |  47.9x  |
| 256-512 tokens (prefill-like) | 5.5x | 4.9x |

So "how much faster" has no single answer: ~5x on long prefill extends, ~100x
on large decode-shaped batches. The table above happens to sit in the middle of
that range. Quoting one headline number in either direction would misrepresent
it.

## No tests added

This PR adds no test file and modifies no test file, per the task's explicit
instruction. Exactness was instead verified out-of-band: a throwaway
randomized differential script (not part of this PR, not committed) ran
**20,000 cases** comparing `torch.equal(out_indices_old, out_indices_new)`
against the original loop implementation (copied verbatim from
`origin/main:python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/paged.py`), covering batch
sizes 1-256, page sizes `{1, 4, 16, 64, 128}`, prefix lengths including 0 and
exact multiples of `page_size`, extend lengths including 0, free-page pools
both tight (sized to exactly the demand) and slack, and — added explicitly
after the bugs above surfaced, not left to chance — the all-zero-new-pages
shape, a mixed batch of zero- and real-page requests, and `page_size=1` with an
empty pool. **0 mismatches, 0 crashes**, across all 20,000 cases, after the two
fixes described above.

title: [Fix] dsa: Make the fused top-k exact on an overflowing threshold bin
author: xiaofei-zheng
body:
## Motivation

The coarse histogram bin comes from the top bits of the fp16 cast, so one bin spans a quarter-binade. The collect pass stores at most 2048 threshold-bin candidates; when the bin is larger, `handle_tie` ranks whichever arrived first and silently returns a wrong top-k set.

Found while profiling GLM-5.2 decode on MI355X: ~0.04% of rows entered this path across all 8 ranks, with a largest observed bin of 4139 against the 2048 cap and none of those rows bit-identical. #35257 reports the same defect independently from the CUDA side — referenced, not closed.

## Modifications

When the threshold bin overflows, narrow it with three exact-key radix rounds (12 / 12 / 8 bits), then make one final input scan to emit candidates above the selected bucket and re-stage the bucket for the existing tie handler. The refinement histogram overlays the dead arrival-order buffer, so LDS is unchanged.

The cold scan uses a separate reversed-lane load path. This keeps its load-address state out of the fast path's registers and restores most of the CUDA regression reported in review.

Replace the fp16-bin boundary conversion with exact fp32 bounds. In particular, when a bin's high edge is `+0.0`, the boundary advances to the smallest positive subnormal so `-0.0` cannot be misclassified as above the bin.

The ROCm long-row split path from #39931 gets the same refinement: each block publishes its uncapped bin count, and the last block refines the whole row when the bin overflows.

The fast path only adds the overflow comparison. The ROCm `__launch_bounds__` argument also states the physical floor of 4 waves/SIMD; the CUDA spelling is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

The exactness test covers register, streaming and split (4×65536) shapes with six distributions, including adjacent fp32 values and `-0.0`; on CUDA it skips rows longer than 24576, which can reach the still-unrefined cluster path.

| suite | result before the fix |
|---|---|
| 300 pre-existing cases | 300 passed |
| 10 overflowing non-identical cases | 10 failed |
| 2 `all_equal` controls | 2 passed |

The signed-zero cases also fail on the pre-review refinement and pass with the new boundary conversion. All 330 cases pass on the merged tree; on the split shape, 4 of the 6 distributions failed before the refinement.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

MI355X (gfx950), five paired runs per arm on one GPU, 200 iterations after warmup:

| distribution | shape | main | this PR | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `randn` (hot path) | 6×8192 | 5.430 µs | 5.338 µs | −1.7% |
| `randn` (hot path) | 4×32768 | 12.270 µs | 12.188 µs | −0.7% |
| `narrow_bin` | 6×8192 | 16.821 µs | 20.937 µs | +24.5% |
| `narrow_bin` | 4×32768 | 29.652 µs | 50.030 µs | +68.7% |
| `two_values` (32-bit refinement) | 6×8192 | 11.487 µs | 34.862 µs | +203.5% |
| `two_values` (32-bit refinement) | 4×32768 | 36.314 µs | 117.756 µs | +224.3% |

The cold-path delta is the cost of exact work that main skips by returning a wrong answer. It is entered on ~0.04% of rows in the serving traffic above. Against the previous PR implementation, the new scan is 2.6–5.3% faster on `narrow_bin`. On the latest tree, a clean local JIT build is 10.50 s versus 10.02 s on main (+4.8%), rather than the nearly 2× CUDA increase reported before this rewrite.

Without overflow the split path is unchanged (15.5–20.1 µs for batch 1–8, 64K–128K, before and after).

On gfx950: 63 → 71 VGPRs, zero spills, LDS unchanged at 26928 B. We do not have NVIDIA hardware; CUDA register pressure and B200 performance need CI/reviewer measurement.

## Known gap

The CUDA-only `TopKCluster` path still truncates. Refining there needs cluster-wide histogram and emit counters rather than the block-local ones used here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add exactness tests.
- [x] Provide accuracy and performance results.
- [x] Keep documentation and comments synchronized.

title: [Perf] prefill-cuda-graph: Make prefill shared-read completion explicit and default-on
author: weireweire
body:
## Summary

Prefill publishes the shared-read-done event by default. With overlap scheduling, the next step's writes to `req_to_token` and `full_to_swa` then wait only for prefill metadata preparation instead of the whole prefill forward. It is enabled only where the prefill forward reads none of those tables after the event.

## Changes

- `SGLANG_ENABLE_PREFILL_WAR_READ_DONE` defaults to `True`; `0` keeps the whole-forward barrier for prefill.
- `AttentionBackend.resolve_prefill_shared_read_ends` returns a batch's prefill read end, and the runners pass it to `maybe_publish_prefill_shared_read_done`. With `build_snapshot`, a backend first snapshots its late reads in `_prepare_prefill_shared_reads`; full graphs and breakable graphs with captured metadata use the static `shared_read_ends`.
- DeepSeek V4 builds its sparse-prefill chunk cache in that hook instead of in the first layer, and the hook and the forward share one `_use_sparse_prefill` gate. The `prefill_shared_reads_snapshotted` flag is removed.
- `HybridAttnBackend` forwards the hook to its prefill backend.
- `HybridLinearAttnBackend` no longer calls the removed `prepare_prefill_shared_read_snapshot`, which was a no-op for it.

## Where prefill keeps the whole-forward barrier

- DeepSeek V4.1: the low-ratio indexer reads `req_to_token` in every layer.
- DeepSeek V4 with HiSparse: `full_to_hisparse` is translated in every layer.
- DSPARK: the draft KV inject reads the SWA mapping after the target prefill.
- Dots: an eager prefill may rebuild metadata from the live tables when DP padding changes the batch.
- DeepSeek V4 with CP, a request window, or a breakable prefill graph with captured metadata.
- HiCache, a HiCache storage backend, or LMCache: write-through and offload copy a stashed chunk's KV ordered only behind the schedule stream, so they could copy it before the forward writes it.
- EAGLE-family, NGRAM and UNO, as before.

## Behavior for existing users

- On CUDA with overlap scheduling, EXTEND batches with no speculative decoding or with DFLASH now publish the event for:
  - `trtllm_mha`, the default attention backend for MHA models on SM100, directly or through the hybrid and two-batch-overlap wrappers;
  - DeepSeek V4 (not V4.1) without HiSparse, in eager or piecewise prefill.
- Decode, other attention backends and non-CUDA platforms are unchanged.
- With `SGLANG_ENABLE_PREFILL_WAR_READ_DONE=1` set explicitly, DSPARK, DeepSeek V4.1, HiSparse and Dots no longer take the prefill fast path.

## Verification

- Unit: `test_prefill_shared_read_done.py`, `test_prefill_cuda_graph_padding.py`, `test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py`, `test_dots_hybrid_backend.py`, `test_deepseek_v4.py`.
- Accuracy: `test_gpt_oss_4gpu_mxfp4.py` (`trtllm_mha`, GPQA), `test_deepseek_v4_flash_fp4_b200.py` and `test_deepseek_v4_flash_fp4_b200_trtllm.py` (GSM8K), `test_basic_sanity_dspark.py`.
- Runs: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37958#issuecomment-6286440471

title: [Diffusion][MiniMax-H3] Add SM90 Sage compute for SubBlock sparse attention
author: IPostYellow
body:
## Motivation
Inspired by the combination of block-sparse attention and Sage FP8 compute in [FlashInfer's SM100 backend](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4612), this PR adds optional SageAttention2 compute to MiniMax-H3's SubBlock sparse attention backend on SM90.


The new mode is opt-in. BF16 remains the default, and Sage compute currently targets SM90.

## Modifications

- Add `compute_mode="sage_fp8"` with online INT8-QK / FP8-PV computation and BF16 inputs and outputs. Model weights remain unchanged.
- Adapt SubBlock routing to the native SM90 kernel's Q64 × K128 block layout.
- Preserve the existing BF16 Q64 × K64 defaults on SM90, SM100, and SM120.
- Check GPU capability and the optional SpargeAttention dependency at server startup.
- Add regression tests and documentation.

Enable Sage compute with:

```bash
--attention-backend subblock_sparse_attn \
--attention-backend-config '{"compute_mode":"sage_fp8"}'
```

## Accuracy Tests

- Native SM90 kernel tests: **2 passed**, covering full-budget attention with a ragged tail and sparse attention with variable block counts.
- MiniMax-H3 end-to-end tests: **81/81 completed** — 3 methods × 3 cases (T2VA, FL2VA, REF2VA-V) × 3 durations (5/10/15 seconds) × 3 seeds (0/1/2).
- Video SSIM is measured against the matching dense FA output. All frames are included, with YUV420 weighting `(4 × Y + U + V) / 6`; results are averaged across three seeds.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `git diff --check` passed.

### Video SSIM

Dense FA is the reference (SSIM = 1). SB denotes SubBlock BF16.

| Case | Duration | SB | SB+Sage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| T2VA | 5s | 0.821579 | 0.818747 |
| T2VA | 10s | 0.870746 | 0.865564 |
| T2VA | 15s | 0.891421 | 0.884516 |
| FL2VA | 5s | 0.851103 | 0.841919 |
| FL2VA | 10s | 0.778914 | 0.777729 |
| FL2VA | 15s | 0.815655 | 0.814308 |
| REF2VA-V | 5s | 0.943797 | 0.939980 |
| REF2VA-V | 10s | 0.980822 | 0.979227 |
| REF2VA-V | 15s | 0.963598 | 0.959587 |

### Audio similarity

Decoded audio is compared against Dense FA for the same case, duration, and seed. Values are means across three seeds, in dB. Higher waveform SNR and lower log-mel MAE indicate closer signals.

The original 32 kHz stereo audio is retained. Log-mel MAE uses 80 mel bands, a 2048-sample FFT, a 512-sample hop, and a shared floor 80 dB below the reference mel peak.

| Case | Duration | SB SNR ↑ | SB+Sage SNR ↑ | SB log-mel MAE ↓ | SB+Sage log-mel MAE ↓ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| T2VA | 5s | 12.450 | 11.507 | 2.006 | 1.989 |
| T2VA | 10s | 13.332 | 12.356 | 1.693 | 1.761 |
| T2VA | 15s | 13.146 | 11.232 | 1.733 | 1.810 |
| FL2VA | 5s | 11.090 | 11.617 | 2.353 | 2.281 |
| FL2VA | 10s | 10.627 | 11.074 | 2.358 | 2.113 |
| FL2VA | 15s | 6.215 | 5.885 | 2.468 | 2.612 |
| REF2VA-V | 5s | 15.819 | 13.038 | 0.552 | 0.916 |
| REF2VA-V | 10s | 22.119 | 19.429 | 0.435 | 0.586 |
| REF2VA-V | 15s | 14.882 | 11.927 | 1.245 | 1.528 |

Comparing SB+Sage directly against SB, group-mean SNR ranges from 15.08 to 20.78 dB and log-mel MAE from 0.484 to 1.386 dB.


## Speed Tests and Profiling

Benchmarked MiniMax-H3 on 8 H200 GPUs with identical inputs and generation settings across methods. Sparse settings: `sparsity=0.75`, `n_q=n_k=4`, `skip_first_steps=10`. The benchmark explicitly sets `n_k=4`; Sage's default is `n_k=8`.

### Generation time

Time is the mean server-side generation time across three seeds, excluding warmup. The ↓ columns report time reduction relative to Dense FA: `(dense baseline time - method time) / dense baseline time`.

| Case | Duration | Dense FA (s) | SB (s) | SB ↓ | SB+Sage (s) | SB+Sage ↓ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| T2VA | 5s | 39.21 | 30.38 | 22.52% | 28.46 | 27.42% |
| T2VA | 10s | 111.84 | 78.16 | 30.11% | 67.90 | 39.29% |
| T2VA | 15s | 218.72 | 144.44 | 33.96% | 121.35 | 44.52% |
| FL2VA | 5s | 42.51 | 33.55 | 21.09% | 30.92 | 27.26% |
| FL2VA | 10s | 116.30 | 81.78 | 29.68% | 70.92 | 39.02% |
| FL2VA | 15s | 224.70 | 149.94 | 33.27% | 126.07 | 43.89% |
