title: [Diffusion] Keep the Wan VAE decoder channels_last and add a Triton NHWC nearest upsample
author: Dayuxiaoshui
body:
<!-- PR body draft for branch `qwen-image-vae-fast-path` (commit e684f0cc9), follow-up to #38020. Local working note, do not commit this file. -->

## Motivation

Follow-up to #38020. The degenerate-stride layout issue found on the Qwen-Image VAE also affects the Wan 2.1 video VAE, where the decoder is a much larger share of a request: on TurboWan2.1-T2V-1.3B (4 steps, 81 frames, 480x832) a warm request spends ~0.93 s denoising and ~1.56 s in `DecodingStage`, i.e. the VAE is ~60% of the request.

Two things were going on in the Wan decoder at `quality=high`:

1. `resample_forward`'s upsample3d frame interleave (`reshape / stack / reshape`) materialises NCDHW, and the attention residual's operand order drops channels_last_3d too, so every up block started with an NCDHW tensor: 4 of the 29 `RMSNorm+SiLU` sites fell back to eager per chunk, the residual adds ran strided, and cuDNN converted the resample conv2d input to NHWC and back.
2. Once the decoder does run channels_last, aten's `upsample_nearest2d_nhwc` kernel is several times slower than its NCHW sibling on the same bytes (0.458 ms vs 0.190 ms for `[1, 192, 240, 416]` bf16 on H200); the decoder hits it once per up block per chunk.

## Modifications

**New kernel, lossless (bit-exact, unconditional)**

- `kernels/ops/diffusion/layout/nearest_upsample_nhwc_triton.py`: integer-factor nearest upsample of a dense channels_last `[N, C, H, W]` tensor as a pure gather. For an integer factor `f`, writing `i = k*f + r` with `0 <= r <= f-1`, `nearest` reads `floor(i/f) = k` and `nearest-exact` reads `floor((i+0.5)/f) = k` since `(r+0.5)/f < 1`, so both read `i // f` and the result is bitwise identical to `nn.Upsample` in either mode. Walks the output in NHWC memory order so loads and stores are contiguous along `C`. 0.061 ms for the shape above. Registered as `diffusion.nearest_upsample_nhwc` with `can_use_nearest_upsample_nhwc`; raises on unsupported input.
- `GatedChannelsLastUpsample` runs it whenever the upsample input already has canonical NHWC strides. In that case aten itself would run its NHWC kernel and return the same dense channels_last tensor, so the replacement is layout- and value-identical and is enabled on the lossless path too.

**Quality-gated (`extra-high` / `high`)**

- `wanvae.py`: `_interleave_time_pairs` writes the interleaved frames straight into a `channels_last_3d` buffer with one `copy_` (both views are valid: the channel dim has stride 1 so `[B, 2C, ...] -> [B, 2, C, ...]` is a view; the output's `2T` dim splits into `(T, 2)`), replacing the NCDHW-materialising `stack`. Gated because the NHWC conv2d it enables need not pick the same cuDNN algorithm.
- The Wan installer wraps `WanUpsample` with `GatedChannelsLastUpsample` (stride canonicalisation, from #38020) and hands the gate to `WanResample` and `WanAttentionBlock` (residual operand order). All 29 norm sites now hit the fused kernel. The operand order is commutative but changes the reduction order of the eager norm that follows under fp32 autocast, which is how Wan pipelines decode (fp32 VAE weights, bf16 autocast); measured end-to-end as non-bit-exact, hence gated.

**Tests / docs**

- `test_layout.py`: `nearest_upsample_nhwc` vs `F.interpolate` for bf16/fp16/fp32, factors 2 and (3, 2), `nearest` and `nearest-exact`, N = 1/2/4; predicate rejections.
- `test_model_fast_paths.py`: interleave vs `stack` (values and layout), upsample wrapper dispatch on canonical / degenerate / NCHW inputs with gate on and off, installer wiring.
- README selection matrix and `existing-fast-paths.md` updated.

## Accuracy Tests

1x H200, Wan 2.1 VAE (`Wan-AI/Wan2.1-I2V-14B-480P-Diffusers` VAE weights), 81 frames 480x832.

**Lossless path**

- Standalone decode, bf16 weights: `torch.equal` vs `main` output: True.
- Standalone decode, fp32 weights + bf16 autocast (the Wan T2V pipeline setting, `vae_precision=fp32, vae_decode_precision=bf16`): `torch.equal` vs `main`: True.
- End-to-end `sglang generate` on TurboWan2.1-T2V-1.3B, 6 prompts, seed 1, 4 steps: all 6 mp4s md5-identical to `main`.
- Peak decode memory unchanged: 4.577 GB in both modes.

**Quality path**

- `main`-high vs this-PR-high (DiT path identical and confirmed deterministic across runs), 81 frames: PSNR mean 36.3 dB, min 35.0 dB. The extra difference vs `main`-high comes from the 4 additional norm sites per chunk now reaching the pre-existing `wan_rmsnorm_silu` kernel; the layout-only part was measured at 89.6 dB on Qwen-Image in #38020.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Standalone VAE decode** (torch.profiler GPU kernel self time, 81f 480x832):

| weights / autocast | path | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 | lossless | 1342 ms / 7850 kernels | 1324 ms / 7850 |
| bf16 | high | 1178 ms / 4580 | 1112 ms / 4006 |
| fp32 + bf16 autocast (pipeline setting) | lossless | 1633 ms | 1593 ms |
| fp32 + bf16 autocast | high | 1311 ms | 1215 ms |

**End-to-end**, TurboWan2.1-T2V-1.3B, 4 steps, 81f 480x832, idle H200, `main` and this PR run interleaved (`main` from a `git worktree` of the base commit), 6 prompts per run, median of the 5 warm requests:

| stage | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `DecodingStage`, lossless | 1565.7 ms | 1531.5 ms (-2.2%) |
| `DecodingStage`, high | 1061.7 ms | 942.7 ms (-11.2%) |
| `DmdDenoisingStage`, lossless | 925.5 ms | 929.4 ms |
| `DmdDenoisingStage`, high | 883.9 ms | 887.4 ms |

Denoising is unchanged, so the effect is confined to the VAE. With decode at ~60% of a warm request, `high` saves ~5% of the request and lossless ~1.4%.

Qwen-Image also picks up the Triton upsample on its `high` path: 44.6 -> 42.9 ms at 1024x1024.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (ruff format / ruff check / isort / codespell clean; ruff format re-checked with the pre-commit pinned v0.15.1)
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (`test_model_fast_paths.py` + `test_layout.py`: 195 passed, 1 skipped; `test_import_surface.py`: 9 passed)
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: [AMD][Spec] Enable GDN ReplaySSM target-verify on ROCm
author: chuyeh
body:
## Motivation

[#35544](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35544) added ReplaySSM speculative verify for GDN: reconstruct the draft window from a frozen checkpoint plus a circular `(d, k, g)` ring, instead of materializing full SSM state on every target step.

The merged kernel hard-codes Triton's `tl.dot(..., input_precision="tf32")`. Triton only accepts TF32 on Ampere-or-newer NVIDIA GPUs. On AMD the kernel fails at compile/launch, so `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec` cannot start on MI355X. Other FLA kernels already fall back with `is_tf32_supported` (`chunk_fwd.py`, `chunk_intra.py`); ReplaySSM did not.

Once IEEE precision is used, the default verify tile is still `block_v=64` with `num_stages=2`. Qwen3.5 GDN has `V=128`, so that tile launches two programs along V and repeats the same q/k and gate work. On gfx950, one `block_v=128` program with `num_stages=1` covers the full V dimension in a single pass.

## Modifications

- Default `dot_precision` to `"tf32"` only when `is_tf32_supported` is true; otherwise `"ieee"`. NVIDIA Ampere+ is unchanged.
- Signature defaults stay `block_v=64` and `num_stages=2`. On gfx950, for the Qwen3.5 MTP verify shape (batch ≥ 32, ring length 16, spec length 4, `K=V=128`), the function overwrites those to `block_v=128` and `num_stages=1`, even if the caller passed `64` / `2`. Serving does not pass them. Below batch 32 the signature defaults remain. The flush launch still uses `block_v_flush=64`.
- No new user-facing option.

## Correctness Tests

Compared the previous tile (`block_v=64`, `num_stages=2`) with the gfx950 tile (`block_v=128`, `num_stages=1`) on the same IEEE `tl.dot` operands and the Qwen3.5 TP2 verify shape:

- Batch size: 32
- Query heads: 8
- Value heads: 32
- Draft tokens: 4
- Ring length: 16
- Head dimension: 128
- Activations: BF16
- Checkpoint: FP32

Outputs and ring writes (`d`, `k`, `g`) matched bit-exactly. The flush / exact-fold kernels are unchanged. This comparison is tiling-only; AMD cannot run the TF32 path.

GSM8K (`sglang.test.run_eval`, 5-shot, 1314 questions, temperature 0, max new tokens 2048, TP2, real EAGLE decoding, aiter backend, page 16, fp8 KV). ReplaySSM off vs `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec` (enablement, not tile vs tile):

| | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---:|---:|
| baseline | 0.933 | 19/1314 (0.014) |
| this PR | 0.944 | 5/1314 (0.004) |

## Performance

### Kernel benchmark

#### Environment

- Hardware: MI355X (`gfx950`)
- Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.18-rocm10-mi35x-20260901`
- Shape: Qwen3.5 TP2-local, 8 query heads / 32 value heads, `K=V=128`
- Draft tokens: 4
- Ring length: 16
- Batch: 32
- Triton `input_precision`: IEEE (AMD)
- Checkpoint: FP32
- Timing: Triton `do_bench`, warmup 100, repeat 500, median of 7 samples

| Tile | Latency | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|
| `block_v=64`, `num_stages=2` (previous default) | 43.13 µs | 1.00x |
| `block_v=128`, `num_stages=1` (this PR) | **29.33 µs** | **1.47x (−32%)** |

The wide V tile removes the second V program, so q/k and gate work run once instead of twice.

### End-to-end serving benchmark

#### Environment

- Hardware: one MI355X host; TP2
- Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.18-rocm10-mi35x-20260902`
- Model: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4

title: [Bugfix] Llama4 local attention: read page ids from the graph tables in CUDA-graph capture/replay (page_size > 1)
author: MartinHua
body:
## What

Fixes a CUDA illegal memory access on Llama4 (FA3) with `--page-size 16` under concurrent decode with CUDA graphs. Stacked on #37733; only the last commit is the fix.

## Root cause

In the decode-graph path `metadata.page_table` holds page ids and `metadata.swa_page_table` is the same table translated into the SWA pool. The local-attention replay refill instead ran `translate_loc_from_full_to_swa(metadata.page_table[:bs, :max_seq_len])`: page ids through the token-slot `full_to_swa_index_mapping`, never divided by `page_size`, so FA3 read SWA token slots as page ids (up to 16x out of range). `page_size == 1` masks it; #32902 fixed the eager extend path only. Located with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` (fault in `full_cuda_graph_backend.replay`); `SGLANG_DEBUG_MEMORY_POOL=1` showed no allocator duplicate.

## Fix

`_graph_page_table` reads `metadata.swa_page_table` (SWA pool) or `metadata.page_table`, sliced by `bs` rows and `cdiv(max_seq_len, page_size)` columns, in both `build_for_capture` and `update_for_replay`. Eager `build` unchanged. At `page_size == 1` the new source equals the old result. Three CPU regression tests added.

## Validation

4xH100, Llama-4-Scout, tp=4, GSM8K (1319, parallel 128): `main` with `--page-size 16 --disable-decode-cuda-graph` 0.924 (no fault, confirms the path); this branch `--page-size 16` with graphs **0.926, completes** (faulted before); `--page-size 1` 0.917, unchanged. Unit tests 12/12.

title: [AMD][DSV4] Reland unified-KV pool sizing and SWA ring accounting, fully gated
author: yuttian1
body:
## Motivation

Under unified-KV, the DSV4 kernels address SWA and C4 state as per-request
rings, but the pool sizer still charged both as token-scaled pools. It reserved
memory the runtime never allocates, so full-token capacity came out well below
what the card can hold.

#30315 fixed the sizing but was reverted in #38163 because it was not fully
gated. This reland keeps the fix and puts every branch behind the unified-KV
gate; the non-unified FP8 path is untouched.

## Modifications

- `pool_configurator`: under unified-KV, SWA and C4 state are sized per request
  slot (`_fixed_swa_bytes`, `_fixed_c4_state_bytes`); the remainder goes to
  full KV.
- `deepseek_v4_memory_pool`: C4 state pool becomes `num_req_slots *
  c4_ring_size`, resolved from the same gate as the sizer so the two cannot
  drift.
- `swa` allocator: `swa_available_size()` reports ring capacity in tokens
  (free req slots x per-slot cost) instead of page counts.
- `schedule_policy`: a request is charged one ring slot at first admission
  rather than a per-chunk token budget; continuations are not charged again.
- `c_plan.cuh`: the C4 plan uses request-ring addressing
  (`req_pool_idx * ring_size + pos % ring_size`).

## Results

- Full-token capacity per DP worker:
  6,848,000 -> 12,569,600 (+83.55%).
- The increase comes from accounting C4 state and the SWA ring as
  request-scoped allocations instead of token-scaled pools.
- GSM8K accuracy:
  95.2% -> 95.1% (1 question difference; no observed accuracy regression).
- Serving benchmark on 8x MI355X:
  no measurable throughput, TTFT, or TPOT regression within run-to-run variance
  at concurrency 512 (replicated); concurrency 256 is a single run per arm.

## Validation

- GSM8K: 1319 questions
- Serving benchmark: TP8 + DP8, 8x MI355X
- Added regression tests for request-ring addressing, request-slot reuse,
  unified/non-unified gating, and token-cap monotonicity.
- CI: `pr-gate` fails on the current head, which skips the downstream suites.
  Not yet diagnosed.

## Caveat

The unified-KV BF16 layout is pre-existing and is outside the scope of this PR.

title: [perf] Optimize w4a8 MoE for glm5.2 on H200
author: cognaiger9
body:
## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
 `dispatch_w4a8_moe_mm_sm90 (python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/moe/cutlass_moe/w4a8/w4a8_grouped_mm_c3x.cu)` picks a CUTLASS config for the W4A8 grouped GEMM by matching on (n, k). Every named branch was tuned for DeepSeek's 7168-hidden shapes on H20. GLM-5.2 (hidden=6144, moe_intermediate_size=2048, E=256, topk=8) matches none of them, so both of its production sharding layouts - TP-8 and EP-8 without DeepEP - fall through to the generic fallback tail and run untuned.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
Add four named branches to `dispatch_w4a8_moe_mm_sm90` for GLM-5.2's actual GEMM shapes, one per GEMM per layout:
  - TP-8: all 256 experts local, intermediate size partitioned by tp_size=8 -> gemm1 (n=512, k=6144), gemm2 (n=6144, k=256).
  - EP-8, no DeepEP: 32 experts local at the full intermediate size -> gemm1 (n=4096, k=6144), gemm2 (n=6144, k=2048).

This tuning adds four unique CUTLASS configurations, increasing the W4A8 configuration count from 12 to 16. These add compilation work and binary size.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->
Correctness is covered by `python/sglang/kernels/aot/tests/test_cutlass_w4a8_moe_mm.py`'s extended parametrization

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->
 `test/manual/layers/moe/bench_w4a8_sm90_dispatch.py` times the complete
  `cutlass_w4a8_moe` call (preprocess/reorder/quant → GEMM1 → silu+requant →
  GEMM2 → post-reorder) - the full MoE-layer boundary across both of its production sharding layouts:

  - **TP-8** (`mode="tp"`).
  - **EP-8, no DeepEP** (`mode="ep"`): the script builds only the 32 local-expert weights and remaps global routing ids to local ids (or a drop sentinel for the other 224), reproducing what a real EP-8 rank sees.

Shapes with `m<=2048` run captured under a CUDA graph, larger shapes run eager. Each shape reports median and min latency across 30 timed calls (5 warmup calls beforehand).

  The results below is produced from running the script on 1x H200.

title: [Sampling] Allow sampling-mask replay with DisallowedTokensLogitsProcessor
author: ByronHsu
body:
## Motivation

Not all custom logit processors are compatible with `return_sampling_mask`. Rule of thumb for a valid custom processor for sampling-mask replay: **do not change the relative probabilities of surviving tokens**. This PR introduces an explicit allowlist containing `DisallowedTokensLogitsProcessor`.

For example, Qwen3.5-4B sets `vocab_size=248320` in [config.json](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B/blob/main/config.json), but [tokenizer.json](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B/blob/main/tokenizer.json), including added tokens from [tokenizer_config.json](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B/blob/main/tokenizer_config.json), defines only **248,077 token IDs**. This leaves **243 unmapped IDs (`248077–248319`)**. Without `DisallowedTokensLogitsProcessor`, the inference engine can sample these unmapped IDs during RL rollouts, producing invalid training data and potentially corrupting policy-gradient updates. Supporting this processor with `return_sampling_mask` lets callers exclude these IDs while preserving correct sampling-mask replay.

For example, with no additional top-k/top-p filtering:

**DisallowedTokensLogitsProcessor (valid)**

```text
                                  hi       you      hey
Original probabilities           50%       30%      20%

DisallowedTokensLogitsProcessor: ban "hi"
Returned mask                     no       yes      yes
Actual probabilities              0%       60%      40%
Replayed probabilities            0%       60%      40%   MATCH
```

**Hypothetical TokenBiasLogitsProcessor (invalid)**

This processor adds `ln(2)` to the logit for `hey`, doubling its probability weight before normalization. The returned mask cannot record this change.

```text
                                  hi       you      hey
Original probabilities           50%       30%      20%

TokenBiasLogitsProcessor: multiply "hey"'s weight by 2
Returned mask                    yes       yes      yes
Actual probabilities            41.7%      25%     33.3%
Replayed probabilities           50%       30%      20%   MISMATCH
```

## Modifications

- Accept `DisallowedTokensLogitsProcessor`, including subclasses that implement hard exclusion, with `return_sampling_mask`.
- Reject unsupported or malformed processors with HTTP 400 during request validation, before they reach the scheduler.
- Check `--enable-custom-logit-processor` before deserializing. Apply the compatibility check only to requests returning sampling masks.

## Accuracy Tests

- 86 unit and sampler tests passed, including hard exclusion in mixed batches on PyTorch and FlashInfer.
- 13 HTTP tests passed on an H200 with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, covering both sampling backends, excluded tokens and replay log probabilities, rejection/recovery, and deterministic sampling.
- The rejection regression fails on unmodified main and passes with this change.
- Full pre-commit checks passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The change adds request validation only; sampler kernels and per-token execution are unchanged. No speed benchmark was run.

title: [Kernel] Wait for the PDL dependency before loading the router bias (Triton + radix)
author: Jiminator
body:
Targets `qwen4-main-squashed`, on top of #38308 (the cherry-pick of #36811, merged).

## Motivation

Two PDL-launched routing kernels load their `bias` before the programmatic-dependent-launch wait and load `scores` after it:

- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py::_router_triton_kernel` (Triton, `launch_pdl=True` on compute capability >= 9)
- `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/moe/route_radix.cuh::route_radix_block` (the radix fast path that `moe_fused_gate` dispatches covered sigmoid inputs to; also reused by `route_quant_fused.cuh`)

Under PDL a grid may start once the preceding kernel's blocks have exited, before that kernel's stores are visible; the wait (`griddepcontrol.wait`) is what establishes completion and visibility. A load placed before it must not depend on prior work. Both kernels assumed the bias is a frozen weight, but the callers do not guarantee that: `fused_topk`'s sigmoid path passes `correction_bias.to(torch.float32)` (a fresh tensor when the parameter is fp16/bf16) or a fresh `torch.zeros` when there is no correction bias (`topk.py:1047-1054`), the grouped and ungrouped wrappers cast as well, and before #36811 the softmax path passed a fresh `torch.zeros` on every call. The compiled sm_121 Triton kernel confirms the pre-fix order: four `LDG.E.128` bias loads precede `ACQBULK`, the score loads follow.

This is the mechanism behind #37111 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 with NEXTN on DGX Spark, output collapsing to repeated `!`), confirmed by capturing the values the kernel consumed during an organic collapse. With an instrumented copy of the unmodified kernel that additionally stores, per row, the bias it loaded before the wait, the scores it loaded after the wait, and a volatile re-read of the bias after the wait, an onset step (32 rows, 23 with NaN top-k weights) showed for every bad row: the bias loaded before the wait contained NaN (256 of 512 elements in most rows; in others the first 64 were zero and the next 64 to 128 NaN), the bias re-read after the wait was all zero, and the scores loaded matched the settled logits exactly. Every clean row had seen an all-zero bias before the wait. Upstream of the router the block input and the gate logits were finite; downstream, the expert kernel produced NaN in exactly those rows and the batch collapsed. #36811 already removed the fresh-zero trigger from plain softmax routing; dynamic-bias paths still need correctly ordered loads.

## Modifications

Move the wait above the bias load in both kernels so every dependent load sits after it. No change to routing semantics, dispatch, launch geometry, or the outgoing `gdc_launch_dependents()`; the `HAS_BIAS=False` register-zero path is unaffected.

## Accuracy / performance

On 1x DGX Spark (GB10), RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4, NEXTN 3/1/4, radix cache off, 8 running requests, GSM8K 1319 (chat, greedy, 8192 max tokens) plus a churn client, on the pre-#36811 build `9b2aee2283` where the collapse reproduced within 2 to 25 minutes in most runs: with only the Triton reorder applied (PDL on, zero-bias still allocated) the full set completed at 0.967 with 0 invalid answers, 0 NaN events, and 0 routing mismatches against a reference top-k recomputed after the kernel on the same stream. Two workarounds that also remove the dependency (PDL off for the kernel; `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_FUSED_TOPK=0`) each completed the same set clean (0.970 / 0.971). Author-reported; the radix change was not exercised by these runs (softmax routing does not dispatch to radix).

Cost: the bias load no longer overlaps the tail of the previous kernel, so a program pays that load's latency after the wait instead of hiding it. Per launch, not per row (rows run concurrently); zero on the softmax path with #36811 since no bias is loaded. Not measured here.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- A deterministic regression check: compile a bias-present specialization and assert every `ld.global` in the PTX comes after `griddepcontrol.wait`.
- `moe_fused_gate.py` grouped routing removes all tied group maxima when computing the second maximum (`vals2 = tl.where(vals >= top1, ...)`), so tied top-1 values yield the wrong group score. Pre-existing, unrelated to this change.
- `kernels/jit/include/sgl_kernel/utils.cuh:170-172` describes the PDL trigger as covering writes issued before it; it is a launch hint, and consumers must wait.

title: [qwen4-main-squashed] Cherry-pick #36811: avoid zero-bias allocation in fused softmax routing (fixes GB10 NEXTN collapse)
author: Jiminator
body:
Cherry-pick of #36811 (main commit 221a6273ce) onto `qwen4-main-squashed`. One trivial conflict resolved: this branch still had the `assert bias.dtype == torch.float32` line that #36811 deletes.

## Why

On DGX Spark (GB10) every NEXTN cell of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 built from this branch sporadically collapses to repeated `!` (NaN logits, #37111). Root cause: `fused_topk` passes a fresh `torch.zeros` bias to the Triton router kernel, which loads it before its PDL wait, so under programmatic dependent launch it can read the buffer's previous bytes; on GB10 the MTP draft leaves NaN there. An instrumented run captured the kernel consuming NaN bias before the wait, zeros after it, with correct logits. #36811 removes the zero-bias allocation for softmax routing, so there is no buffer left to read early.

## Validation (1x DGX Spark, RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4, NEXTN 3/1/4, radix cache off, 8 running requests, GSM8K 1319 + churn client, the shape that collapsed within 2 to 25 min in most runs on this branch tip)

With only this cherry-pick applied: 0.971 accuracy, 0 invalid, 1319/1319 stopped normally, 0 NaN events, 0 routing mismatches against a settled reference recomputed after the kernel. The unpatched branch collapsed twice in the same hours on the same shape.

The kernel-side hardening (wait before the bias load, Triton + radix) is proposed separately against main in #38290 and is not required for this branch's cells.

title: [AMD] Fix EAGLE crash when no kv_index_translator is bound on the DSA fp8 read door
author: jiaryang
body:
## Motivation

`_get_mla_kv_buffer_from_fp8_for_dsa` translates its read ids through the attention backend's `kv_index_translator` unconditionally:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py#L659

But only the FlashAttention and FlashInfer backends bind a translator. `BaseAttentionBackend` documents its `None` default as meaning "no translate":

```python
# The runner's KVIndexTranslator; backends that read through it set the
# instance attribute in __init__. None means "no translate" -- a backend
# that never set it cannot serve the unified pool, which the server-args
# allow-list enforces.
kv_index_translator = None
```

The DSA backend keeps that default. Under EAGLE the draft model runs on the DSA backend and reaches this door, so on gfx950 with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` every TP rank dies on the first request:

```
  File "python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha_rocm.py", line 211, in forward_normal_rocm_prepare
    kv_a, k_pe = self._get_mla_kv_buffer_from_fp8_for_dsa(forward_batch)
  File "python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py", line 659, in _get_mla_kv_buffer_from_fp8_for_dsa
    kv_indices = get_attn_backend().kv_index_translator.translate_dcp_read_ids(
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'translate_dcp_read_ids'
```

The server comes up fine and dies the moment the first request arrives, taking down all four ranks. A target-only (non-speculative) run has no draft model and never reaches this door, which is why the crash is specific to speculative decoding.

Repro (crashes on current `main`, serves normally with this PR):

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --tp 4 --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend triton --dsa-decode-backend triton \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1
```

## Modifications

Honor the documented contract at the read door: skip the translation when no translator is bound. With no translator the ids were never widened to VIRTUAL, so there is nothing to collapse. Behavior for the backends that do bind a translator is unchanged.

```python
translator = get_attn_backend().kv_index_translator
if translator is not None:
    kv_indices = translator.translate_dcp_read_ids(kv_indices)
```

One file, guard only, no functional change on any path that previously worked.

## Accuracy Tests

GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X (gfx950), TP4, GSM8K, three runs. Before the fix the speculative server could not serve a single request, so there was no MTP result to compare against.

| | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EAGLE (this PR) | 0.941 | 0.932 | 0.927 |
| target-only, same build | 0.929 | 0.932 | 0.932 |

Speculative decoding lands in the same band as the target-only reference, as expected.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the change adds a single `None` check and leaves every previously working path byte-for-byte identical.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [MoE][ROCm] Admit the unified Triton router on ROCm, including single-group routing
author: xiaobochen-amd
body:
The opt-in unified Triton router (`SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK`, off
by default) was gated on CUDA and on more than one expert group. Nothing in the
kernel is CUDA-specific, so admit ROCm and single-group routing. CUDA's condition
is unchanged, and with the flag off every path is byte-identical to before.

Three things follow:

- **Width.** The kernel wants the total top-k, shared slots included, but
  `select_experts` passes `num_routed_topk if _use_aiter else top_k`. Only the
  aiter caller adds the shared slots back.
- **Shared expert once.** `_post_process_topk_ids` appends shared slots for an
  aiter runner; this router emits them itself. Appending again writes the id
  twice and evicts a real routed expert. Now it appends only when the row comes
  back short.
- **Scaling.** An aiter runner skips the post-MoE multiply, so the routed weights
  must carry `routed_scaling_factor` and the shared slot must be 1.0.

`gating_output` loses its torch-side fp32 cast; the kernel widens on load.

## Tests

`test/registered/kernel/moe/test_jit_grouped_topk.py`, 10 cases, registered on
CUDA (`base-b-kernel-unit`) and AMD (`jit-kernel-unit-test-amd`).

Compared against `biased_grouped_topk_impl`, not `select_experts` with the flag
off — on ROCm that is the aiter path, which casts the correction bias down to the
gating dtype, and GLM-5.2 keeps that bias where bf16 cannot separate neighbours.
Measured on MI355X: 8 rows in 256 differ, all by less than one bf16 ULP at that
offset. It reorders routing on its own.

Width is pinned separately for both `_use_aiter` values, since whichever GPU runs
the suite fixes that flag and can only exercise one half.

MI355X / ROCm 7.2: 10 passed. `ruff`, `ruff-format`, `isort`, `codespell` clean.

title: [AMD][Fix] Fix regression in jit build error with FLUX.2-dev on gfx1250
author: sogalin
body:
## Motivation
FLUX.2-dev fails on gfx1250 as soon as denoising starts:
```
Failed to build JIT module sgl_kernel_jit_flux2_gated_resnorm
flux2_gated_resnorm.cuh:57:9: error: invalid output constraint '=&f' in asm
flux2_gated_resnorm.cuh:64:43: error: invalid output constraint '=f' in asm
amd_warp_sync_functions.h:297:62: error: static assertion failed due to requirement
    'sizeof(unsigned int) == 8': The mask must be a 64-bit integer.
3 errors generated when compiling for gfx1250.
```
The kernel added in #37112 is CUDA-only — it uses PTX inline asm with
float-register operand constraints and `__shfl_down_sync` with a 32-bit mask,
and AMDGPU has neither.
It gets selected because `_blackwell_or_newer()` only tests the device
capability. On ROCm that capability is derived from the gfx number, so gfx1250
reports `(12, 5)` and clears the `major >= 10` test, with
`torch.cuda.is_available()` already true under HIP.
Same class of issue as #34481, for a kernel added after it.
## Modifications
Require a CUDA build in `_blackwell_or_newer()`, matching the guard
`rope/qwen_qkv_epilogue_jit.py` already applies to the same capability test:
```python
 def _blackwell_or_newer(device: torch.device) -> bool:
     return (
-        torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device)[0] >= 10
+        torch.version.cuda is not None
+        and torch.cuda.is_available()
+        and torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device)[0] >= 10
     )
```
Both entry points, `can_defer_flux2_gated_residual()` and
`can_use_flux2_gated_resnorm()`, route through the guard, so ROCm now takes the
`residual_gate_add` + eager norm path for both. CUDA is unaffected.
## Accuracy Tests
ROCm falls back to the same unfused path it used before #37112, so there is no
new numerical behavior to validate on either platform.

title: [ROCm] Fuse the MLA q absorb into the RoPE + KV-write kernel on gfx950
author: xiaobochen-amd
body:
## Motivation

On gfx950, the absorbed q BMM and the fused RoPE + cat + KV write are two
separate launches -- `rocm_absorb_q_bmm` in prepare, `_fused_rope_cat_and_cache`
in core. At decode shapes neither fills half the CUs, so they run back to back
with most of the machine idle.

aiter ships `fused_fp8_bmm_rope_cat_and_cache_mla`, which does all three in one
grid. It is present at the pinned `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT` (`4ad9983`).

## What this does

`_can_fuse_bmm_rope_cat_and_cache` enumerates the conditions under which the
fused kernel is exactly equivalent to the two it replaces: gfx95 with AITER, an
fp8 absorbed weight, a rope to fuse, the skip-rope DSA path (`tilelang` or
`triton` backend), an absorb-capable attention backend, and no deep-gemm BMM,
experimental LoRA, or active `kv_b` LoRA. The caller adds `not q_replicate_active`
-- DCP all-gathers `q_nope_out` before core runs, and the fused path has none to
hand it. Anything else falls back to the two-launch path unchanged.

It also guards the new aiter import behind `is_gfx95_supported()`.
`rocm_linear_utils` is imported wherever AITER is on, gfx942 included, but the op
is gfx95-only -- without the guard an aiter build lacking it would break every
DeepSeek import on those cards.

## Perf

MI355X, GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP8, EAGLE MTP 5/6, ISL 100k / 1k out, concurrency 1.
Same build in both arms with the gate as the only variable, two reps each.
Accept length is pinned (`SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.61`) so the comparison
measures kernel time rather than divergence in which draft tokens get accepted.

`triton` DSA backend (the HIP default since #30575), ROCm 10 CI image:

| | fused | unfused | |
|---|---|---|---|
| median ITL | 3.40 ms | 3.45 ms | -1.45% |
| P90 ITL | 4.53 ms | 4.60 ms | -1.41% |
| mean TPOT | 3.76 ms | 3.81 ms | -1.18% |

`tilelang` backend, measured earlier on a ROCm 7.0 image:

| | fused | unfused | |
|---|---|---|---|
| median ITL | 5.570 ms | 5.640 ms | -1.24% |
| mean TPOT | 6.145 ms | 6.245 ms | -1.60% |

The saving is one kernel launch per layer, so it does not depend on which
attention backend consumes the output -- the two backends agree to within the
run-to-run spread.

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/models/test_rocm_mla_absorb_fusion_gate.py` (CPU, 4 tests /
6 subtests): each gate term independently disables the fusion, and off gfx95
nothing else is consulted.

`ruff`, `ruff-format`, `isort`, `codespell` clean.

title: fix(qsa): clamp the compress gather to the rows this forward has
author: ehuaa
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Related to the IMA error described in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/37633.
In the indexer every group spans`compress_ratio` rows, so a padded entry gathers rows `0..ratio-1` of `token_k`.
A forward that carries fewer than `compress_ratio(4)` token rows — the 1..3 token chunk that ends a request under chunked prefill — therefore reads past `token_k`.
The read almost always lands in neighbouring allocated memory and is absorbed silently, it faults only when it happens to cross an unmapped page.


## Modifications
Clamp the gather row index to the rows this forward actually has:

```python
group_locs = group_locs.clamp_max(source_keys.shape[0] - 1)
```

This is exact rather than a mask over the symptom: padded entries write the
reserved slot 0 and their gathered values are discarded, and real entries are
provably in range, so the clamp cannot change any real computation.

title: [Config] Retire get_global_server_args, and clear the deprecated flags that have a replacement
author: ch-wan
body:
Two cleanups on the config tier, plus the review rounds they went through.
Separate commits, in order.

## `get_global_server_args` is retired

It was the last spelling of "reach for the whole record and pick a field off
it". Nothing in `srt` called it any more -- the two remaining references were
bare imports, one a deliberate re-export -- so this is where keeping it costs
more than removing it. The name still worked, still returned a `ServerArgs`,
and still answered with the operator's *input*: a caller who reached for it to
read something resolution had decided got a stale value and no error at all.

It raises. Not a warning first: a `DeprecationWarning` is filtered by default
outside `__main__`, so no production caller would ever have seen it, and under
`-W error::DeprecationWarning` it would have changed the exception type a
caller catches. One `RuntimeError`, one message, and `-> NoReturn` so a type
checker rejects the call rather than accepting the attribute access after it.

The message names both replacements, because they answer different questions:
the value in effect comes from its namespace bag, and `get_server_args()`
still answers for the raw input. The name stays in `server_args` so an
out-of-tree caller lands on that message instead of an ImportError.

## Seventeen deprecated CLI flags go

Deprecated between 2026-05-20 and 2026-08-16, each either an alias for a flag
that still exists or a warn-and-discard no-op. Long options go from 522 to 505.
No field is removed: the three no-op flags never had one, because
`DeprecatedAction` warns and stores nothing.

The mapping is not guessed -- every deprecated action carries `new_flag=`, so
the rewrite reads the intent out of the code:

| removed | replacement |
|---|---|
| `--stream-output` | `--incremental-streaming-output` |
| `--nsa-prefill-backend` / `--nsa-decode-backend` | `--dsa-*-backend` |
| `--cuda-graph-bs` / `--cuda-graph-max-bs` | `--cuda-graph-*-decode` |
| `--piecewise-cuda-graph-tokens` / `-max-tokens` / `-compiler` | `--cuda-graph-bs-prefill` / `-max-bs-prefill` / `--cuda-graph-tc-compiler` |
| `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph` / `--disable-piecewise-cuda-graph` / `--enforce-piecewise-cuda-graph` | `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill={breakable,disabled,tc_piecewise}` |
| `--mamba-scheduler-strategy` | `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy` |
| `--speculative-dflash-draft-window-size` | `--speculative-draft-window-size` |
| `--enable-gdn-replayssm-spec` | `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec` |
| `--collect-tokens-histogram`, `--enable-expert-distribution-metrics`, `--prefill-round-robin-balance` | none; dropped |

`--disable-cuda-graph` stays. Its replacement is two flags rather than one, so
it is a migration rather than a rename; its field is `no_cli=True`, so the
deprecated spelling is the only command-line way in; and with every other
alias gone it is the one worked example of the shape for whoever retires the
next flag. The four `Deprecated*Action` classes stay with it, one per
migration shape, now tested -- three have no registration, so nothing else
would notice them rotting.

### What a name-swap alone got wrong, and did

* Two flags are **prefixes of live ones**, so they are not "unrecognized" --
  argparse rejects `--cuda-graph-bs` as *ambiguous* between the `-decode` and
  `-prefill` pair. Four `sglang serve` commands still passed them, two of them
  tests that would fail at setup. An unanchored count also claimed 384 usages
  of `--cuda-graph-max-bs` where there are 64.
* Three are `store_const` aliases, so the replacement carries a **value**, not
  a flag name. One doc had `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph true`, which becomes
  `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill=breakable true` with a stray positional; three
  argument tables ended up listing `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill=disabled` as
  though it were a flag, with a `False` default.
* Rewriting the name inside prose about the deprecation produced sentences
  calling a live flag a deprecated alias **of itself** -- twelve rows of the
  argument table, two test files, and a `DeprecatedStoreConstAction` docstring.
* In one comment the substitution **deleted** the name instead of replacing it,
  leaving a sentence with no subject.
* **`multimodal_gen` has its own `ServerArgs`.** Fifteen diffusion-scoped files
  were rewritten and reverted. But the blanket exemption was wrong too: four of
  the commands above are `srt` launch lines that happen to live in diffusion
  tests and docs, and the diffusion parser has no such flag either.
* Two files came back with **every line rewritten**, because the script
  normalised CRLF to LF on files that had CRLF. `glm-5.2.jsx` showed 2516
  changed lines for 30 real ones.

Repo-wide count of the removed spellings is now zero, checked against the real
parser rather than by grep.

## The fallback pilot loses its over-defensive half

`test_declared_fallbacks.py` goes from 17 tests to 7. What went: assertions
that a sentinel is not `None`, that a non-dataclass has no fallbacks, that
`Arg().fallback` differs from `None` -- restatements of the implementation, or
of Python. The `NO_FALLBACK` sentinel and a container deepcopy went with them,
which is what let `with_fallback` come down to four lines.

The one invariant those tests did carry is now asserted where a new
declaration passes through: `fallbacks_of` rejects a mutable fallback (the
function is cached, so one list would be shared by every reader) and a field
whose dataclass default is not `None` (it could never reach the fallback, so
the declaration would be dead).

## Review

Both CPU jobs that went red are fixed and demonstrated:

* The exposure ratchet caught a supplied-instance read of a resolution-written
  field. Reading the record there is correct -- the provenance question is
  about the input -- and the read is back off `cfg`, where the base commit had
  it, so `_EXPOSED` stays empty.
* A test I added asserted `Backend.BREAKABLE` for the no-flag prefill default,
  which is the answer on a CUDA box. `default_prefill_backend()` returns
  `TC_PIECEWISE` off CUDA and the file runs on the CPU runner. It compares
  against the resolver now, checked with `is_cuda` forced False.

Also from review: `test_disagg_trace.py` reaches from `multimodal_gen` into
`sglang.srt.server_args` and caught the `ValueError` the accessor used to
raise; two cuda-graph hook docstrings described the lock as value-specific when
the check is membership; the ViT example claimed a prefill graph runs for an
arch on neither allowlist; and a runtime-context skill named a ratchet test
that no longer exists.

Two excursions are reverted and net to nothing in the diff, kept as commits so
the reasoning survives: deleting
`_speculative_draft_quantization_explicitly_set` (and with it the
`_underscore_field_names` fold -- restoring the field alone leaves it on the
exempt side of the write seal, measured), and an `input_of` accessor that
turned out to return exactly the value it wrapped, since the write seal
freezes every field at the moment `_raw_input` is snapshotted.

## Testing

213 files, +626/-893. `test/registered/unit/server_args/` plus the ratchets,
the migration tests and the runtime-context tests: 389 passed. Sweeps are one
file per process, which is the shape CI runs -- a shared interpreter lets a
sibling publish a context and hides a pre-publish failure.

`TestPortArgs` flaked here for a reason unrelated to this branch (it asks the
host whether six fixed ports are free, and `main` fails identically under the
same condition); that is split out into #38377.

title: Revert "[kernel] add fused silu mul quant fp8"
author: hnyls2002
body:
Reverts sgl-project/sglang#37376

## Why

#37376 enables a fused silu+mul+FP8-quant kernel on the block-wise FP8 MoE path. It is not numerically equivalent to the two-kernel path it replaces, and the difference is large enough to cost speculative-decoding acceptance on GLM-5.2-FP8 EAGLE MTP.

`test/registered/e2e/models/test_dsa_glm52_tp_mtp.py::test_bs_1_speed` asserts `accept_length > 4.0` and is currently failing on main.

## Bisect

Two `Rerun Test` dispatches of that test on the `8-gpu-h200` pool, at #37376 and its direct parent:

| commit | Acc Length | Tokens | Speed (token/s) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `503511c963` (parent) | **4.727** | 1092 | 323.28 | pass |
| `a8b2f36dee` (#37376) | **3.949** | 778 | 265.40 | fail |

- [run at parent](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34173127970) / [run at #37376](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34173132321)
- 4.727 is the value every scheduled main run produced before #37376 landed; 3.949 reproduces identically across all three attempts in the run.
- Net effect on this recipe: **-16.5% accept length, -18% bs=1 decode speed**.

## Mechanism

- `_can_use_fused_silu_mul_quant_fp8` turns the kernel on from shape/dtype alone. There is no flag or env var to disable it, so an affected model cannot opt out.
- The fused kernel emits the FP8 down-GEMM input directly, skipping the bf16 `intermediate_cache2` round-trip, so its output differs from the two-kernel path.
- The unit test added in #37376 states the tolerance explicitly: `fp8_match > 0.95` (up to 5% of FP8 bytes may differ) and `assert_close(fused_output, fallback_output, rtol=0.02, atol=0.02)`.
- Accuracy-style evals absorb that (`cosine_sim > 0.9999`), but acceptance length is a discrete draft/target token-agreement rate compounded over 5 draft steps, and target and draft share the same MoE, so the perturbation accumulates instead of averaging out.

## Note

Reverting rather than gating because no switch exists today. A reland could keep the kernel behind an opt-in flag, or disable it when speculative decoding is enabled.

title: [Diffusion] Optimize LTX-2 QKNorm and split RoPE on Hopper
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- enable the existing fused LTX-2 Q/K RMSNorm + split-RoPE CUDA kernel on exact SM90 when the request opts into `quality="high"` or `"extra-high"`
- keep Hopper `quality="lossless"` on the current eager chain; keep the existing SM100+ default unchanged
- route the Hopper opt-in through the existing request-scoped quality-fusion mount/unmount policy
- add SM90 guard, numeric-tolerance, and mount-policy coverage

## Profile evidence

Workload: `Lightricks/LTX-2`, 768x512x121, 40 first-stage + 3 refinement steps, CFG parallel on 2x H200, eager mode.

The source all-stage trace recorded 41,316 BF16 LayerNorm launches (271.51 ms) and 16,512 split-RoPE launches (85.37 ms). A two-step candidate trace records 1,152 fused kernel launches, zero split-RoPE launches, and removes a net 192 launches per step.

## End-to-end result

Fixed H200 GPUs, two fresh-process repeats per side:

| Path | Mean denoise | Mean E2E | Peak reserved / rank |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| source, `quality=high` | 8.5027 s | 9.7970 s | 64.56 GiB |
| candidate, `quality=high` | 7.6832 s | 9.0633 s | 64.56 GiB |
| improvement | **9.64%** | **7.49%** | unchanged |

The candidate repeats are byte deterministic. The fused operator differs from the Hopper eager BF16 chain by at most 0.0625 for Q and 0.125 for K, which is why this path is quality-gated instead of enabled for lossless requests. Candidate versus source high-mode video measures PSNR 25.5355 dB / FFmpeg SSIM 0.897576; visual review preserves the scene, composition, and broad motion. Source high mode itself differs more from lossless by frame metrics.

## Validation

- `test_rope_ltx2.py` on H200: 2 passed, 5 Blackwell-only cases skipped
- `test_model_fast_paths.py -k ltx2` on H200: 6 passed
- pre-commit on all changed files: passed

title: [Fix] Wait for PDL before reading DeepSeek V4 K cache locations
author: aurickq
body:
## Motivation

The fused DeepSeek V4 K normalization/RoPE kernel reads `out_loc` before `PDLWaitPrimary`. Cache locations can be produced immediately before this kernel: [`get_swa_out_cache_loc`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5aab054ec8ce6b6100fbfb7aafe67d632a7df3aa/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py#L1633-L1654) falls back to gathering the SWA mapping and converting it to int32, and its result is passed directly to the fused cache-store call.

[CUDA's PDL contract](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/04-special-topics/programmatic-dependent-launch.html#api-description) requires the dependency wait before consuming the preceding kernel's results, including when the producer uses an implicit launch trigger. Reading `out_loc` before that wait can select a stale cache slot.

## Modifications

Move only the `out_loc` load after the existing wait. Preserve the early position load and frequency-pointer calculation, retaining their prefetch overlap and the existing assumption that positions are already prepared.

```diff
   const auto position = static_cast<int32_t>(static_cast<const PosT*>(params.positions)[work_id]);
-  const auto out_loc = params.out_loc[work_id];
   const auto freqs_cis = params.freqs_cis + position * kRopeDim;

   PDLWaitPrimary<kUsePDL>();
+  const auto out_loc = params.out_loc[work_id];
```

## Accuracy Tests

Standalone GPU validation on GB300 with CUDA 13.2 (`sm_103a`): **320/320 trials passed**, covering 20/128/512/2048 rows, int32/int64 positions, stream/CUDA-graph launches, and PDL enabled/disabled. Positions were precomputed; an ordinary preceding kernel freshly converted valid cache locations from int64 to int32. Full cache output bytes matched the reference with prepared metadata and PDL disabled.

This checks ordinary producer-to-consumer execution, not a failing-before/passing-after reproduction of the ordering bug. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed. No test or documentation files are added.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Standalone CUDA-graph benchmark on GB300, with fully initialized immutable inputs and 128 invocations per chain. Median paired change across four interleaved rounds versus the unmodified kernel:

| Rows | Change in time per invocation |
| ---: | ---: |
| 20 | +0.11% |
| 128 | +1.73% |
| 512 | +1.69% |
| 2048 | +0.04% |
| 8192 | -0.02% |

The largest median increase was approximately 24 ns. These measure steady-state kernel-chain time, not end-to-end serving throughput or overlap with a cache-location producer.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [ ] Add unit tests.
- [x] Documentation: no interface or usage changes to document.
- [x] Provide runtime accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [Feat] [NPU] DSpark: DeepSeek-V4 support DSpark compact mode
author: randgun
body:
## Motivation

DSpark on the Ascend DSV4 backend currently falls back to a uniform verify window or eager-side post-processing for parts of speculative decoding. This leaves two sources of avoidable overhead:

1. the target model verifies the full draft window even when the SPS policy selects a shorter per-request verify length;
2. accept/finalize and hidden/KV commit remain outside the target verify graph.

This PR enables the compact DSpark path on NPU, adds token-tiered graph replay for ragged target verify, and folds the eligible verify epilogue into the graph.

## Modifications

### 1. DSpark compact verify on NPU

- Build packed/ragged verify windows from per-request verify lengths selected by the DSpark planner.
- Add NPU-safe compact row mapping, verify-ID gathering, cache-location handling, and compact-to-strided scatter.
- Construct DSV4 SWA, sparse-attention, C4/C128 compressor, position, state, and page-table metadata from the live compact layout.
- Preserve eager fallback when the selected attention backend does not support ragged verify graphs.

### 2. Compact target-verify graph

- Advertise ragged verify graph support for the DSV4 Ascend backend.
- Select target-verify graphs by compact token tier while retaining fixed graph-owned buffers.
- Refresh query indptr, sequence lengths, cache/page tables, compressor locations/state, and sparse indices before replay.
- Add an NPU-local bucketed-layout cache so the Ascend and DSV4 metadata consumers reuse the same derived layout.
- Use the safe last-location Triton path for DSV4 NPU allocation metadata.

### 3. Verify epilogue graph

- Add a DSV4 NPU-specific target-verify tail hook that uses the committed/live prefix lengths from DSV4 metadata.
- Fold greedy accept/finalize and eligible hidden/KV commit into the compact target-verify graph.
- Keep sampling, grammar-constrained decoding, logits adjustments, and other ineligible cases on the existing eager epilogue path.
- Keep the adaptation NPU/DSV4-specific so the existing CUDA behavior remains unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

- GPQA-Diamond accuracy: **0.91** with DSpark on Ascend NPU.
- The compact path preserves the target-model verification result; it changes the number of draft tokens verified and where graph-safe post-processing executes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling
The expected gain comes from reducing target-verify tokens according to the SPS-selected compact lengths and removing eligible verify epilogue launches from the host path.
| Metric | Compact | Static | Delta |
|--------|---------|--------|-------|
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 2027.13 | 1949.98 | Compact +4.0% |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 20.87 | 26.27 | Compact -20.6% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 36563.48 | 38385.26 | Compact -4.7% |

## Validation

- Python syntax compilation passed for all Python files changed by this PR.
- Added scheduler coverage for exact eager token counts when the backend does not support ragged verify graphs.

## Checklist

title: [diffusion] Support MiniMax-H3 Singularity hybrid checkpoints
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

Support [Singularity v1.3](https://huggingface.co/WarmBloodAban/Minimax-h3_Singularity) through the existing native H3 pipeline, without another loader or quantization implementation.

- Normalize `model.diffusion_model.` in H3's parameter mapping, shared with Comfy format markers and pruned AdaLN metadata.
- Preserve a valid intermediate parameter name when a later alias is absent from the constructed model. This fixes prefixed INT8 `weight_scale` becoming a nonexistent FP8 `weight_scale_inv`; valid final mappings, QKV merge metadata and explicit dropped keys retain their semantics.
- Add explicit `--model-variant hybrid` for supplied merged transformer weights. It uses the base Ref2VA component configuration and admits T2VA, FL2VA and Ref2VA. Official partition admission stays strict; hybrid without an explicit weight override is rejected.
- Update the WebUI task selector, H3 format table, copyable recipe and CLI reference.

## Validation

Reproduced standard `sglang serve` failure on main `b83a59835dca`: required time-embedding/AdaLN parameters were missing. Both published files now download through standard serve and load into native `MiniMaxH3DiTModel`.

Six completed audiovisual generations on **2×B300, Ulysses2**, using 50 schedule points (49 denoiser evaluations), seed 1101 and 1344×768 / 5.17s aligned output:

| Singularity v1.3 file | Native requests exercised |
| --- | --- |
| Pruned INT8 | T2VA; FL2VA first frame; Ref2VA image; Ref2VA 5.17s video with audio |
| Full INT8 | T2VA; Ref2VA 1.08s video with audio → 5.17s output |

All outputs passed full video/audio decoding and frame inspection. The final full-weight reference request omitted character, clothing and instrument descriptions from the prompt, and retained the supplied cat/piano scene. First-frame FL2VA SSIM against its input was 0.9824 (a first-frame check, not whole-video GT alignment).

- Focused remote suite: **124 passed, 20 subtests passed** (H3 admission, WebUI, checkpoint quantization/mapping, FSDP loading and LoRA format adapter).
- Pre-commit, cookbook config check, Mint build validation, broken-link checks and Lint passed.
- Environment: Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Transformers 5.12.1, Diffusers 0.37.0, comfy-kitchen 0.2.33.

These are approximate third-party checkpoints, not the official consistency baseline. No GT changes or performance claims. The author's optional Turbo LoRA combination was not validated here; its sampler/scale contract remains explicit.

Scope: 71 lines of existing production-code churn, no new production files; 183 lines of tests/docs churn.

title: [Diffusion][CI] Per-case timing tolerance for host-I/O-bound perf guards
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

`minimax_h3_t2va_consumer_budget_1gpu_5090` fails the e2e guard on unrelated PRs. The case is not measuring the code under test:

- it streams a 66 GiB model against `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_TEST_CAP_DEVICE_MEMORY_GIB=12` and `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_TEST_FORCE_HOST_AVAILABLE_GIB=32`, so its wall clock is the runner's page cache and disk;
- it runs with `--performance-mode memory`, so `auto_residency_args_skip_reason` short-circuits the whole residency planner — a residency PR cannot change this case's placement at all.

Two jobs on the **same runner** (`5090-e-runner-3`), same config:

| job | samples | e2e (s) |
|---|---|---|
| #37917 (green) | 4 | 33.5, 36.4, 43.8, 52.3 |
| #37918 (red) | 14 | 34.4, 34.4, 37.1, 40.6, 44.4, 46.4, 47.0, 50.5, 51.7, 53.9, 57.0, 60.0, 67.7, 75.2 |

And on another runner (`5090-d-runner-7`), a green job on a PR that touches no residency code:

| job | samples | e2e (s) |
|---|---|---|
| #38441 (green) | 12 | 38.2, 42.6, 43.0, 45.0, 45.8, 46.5, 47.7, 48.4, 49.5, 50.8, 52.3, 57.1 |

Baseline 42763 ms, `pr_test` e2e tolerance 25% → limit 53454 ms. The spread on one runner is 2.2×, so pass/fail is a coin flip. In the same two jobs the other five 5090 cases are flat (17.6 vs 18.5 s, 4.5 vs 4.8 s, 2.2 vs 2.5 s, 1.8 vs 2.1 s, 22.7 vs 22.8 s) — the machine is not globally slower, only the host-I/O-bound case swings.

## Modifications

- `ScenarioConfig.timing_tolerance`: optional per-case override for the wall-clock tolerances only — e2e, avg/median denoise, per-step, stages and frame time. Memory guards (load/runtime peak VRAM, allocated peaks, host anon) keep the profile tolerance; those are what this case actually protects (a 12 GiB device cap and a 32 GiB host cap).
- The override is a ceiling, applied as `max(profile, override)`, so it can only widen, never tighten.
- `_dump_baseline_for_testcase` carries the field into the suggested entry, so refreshing a baseline cannot silently drop it.
- Applied to `minimax_h3_t2va_consumer_budget_1gpu_5090` at `0.9` (limit ≈ 81 s): covers all 18 samples measured so far with headroom, and still fails a ~2× regression.

No other case changes behavior — `timing_tolerance` defaults to `None`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — CI harness only, no runtime code touched.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not applicable — this PR changes no runtime path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests: `test_timing_tolerance_override_widens_wall_clock_checks_only`, `test_timing_tolerance_override_leaves_memory_guards_alone`.
- [x] `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_performance_metrics.py` (20 passed), `test_suite_partitioning.py` + `test_sequential_server_requests.py` (56 passed) on an H200 box.

title: [Diffusion] Support mixed INT8 embeddings and Comfy NVFP4 encoders
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Load existing H3-compatible Qwen3-VL checkpoint variants through the standard component overrides, without repository-specific loader branches or manual quantization selection.

Real exports exposed three gaps: scalar-scale INT8 embeddings alongside quantized linears, Comfy NVFP4 layers that do not request full-precision matmul, and complementary header/per-layer quantization metadata.

## Modifications

- Share packed scalar/per-row INT8 embedding lookup across INT8, W4A8 and NVFP4 configurations. Preserve the fused CUDA scalar lookup, scale rounding and vocabulary sharding; dequantize only requested rows.
- Dispatch Comfy NVFP4 by each layer's metadata: retain the existing BF16/FP16 path for `full_precision_matrix_mult`, otherwise use dynamic activation quantization and NVFP4 matmul through comfy-kitchen on NVIDIA SM100+. Match Comfy's activation-scale rounding and handle padding/zero inputs.
- Merge complementary quantization metadata fields while continuing to reject conflicting values.
- Update the H3 cookbook format table and shared quantization documentation. Reuse `--component-paths.text_encoder` for complete components and `--component-weights-paths.text_encoder` for weights-only files.

H3's Qwen3-VL component includes the vision tower; no separate image-encoder loader is introduced.

## Accuracy Tests

Remote single-B300 validation:

| Checkpoint | T2VA | First-frame FL2VA |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [BF16 Ultra Heretic](https://huggingface.co/llmfan46/Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct-ultra-uncensored-heretic) | Passed | Passed |
| [INT8 ConvRot Ultra Heretic](https://huggingface.co/ethanfel/Qwen3-VL-32B-Ultra-Heretic-H3-ComfyUI-INT8-ConvRot) | Passed | Passed |
| [NVFP4 Heretic](https://huggingface.co/sakamakismile/Qwen3-VL-32B-Heretic-MiniMax-H3-NVFP4) | Passed | Passed |

All six used normal `sglang serve` downloading, 1344×768, a 5-second request, 50 steps, seed 1101 and `quality=lossless`, without Cache-DiT, compilation or a DiT override. Audio/video streams and full media decoding passed. BF16 used c0fef860870f5; INT8/NVFP4 used 452d713708bcb, whose only subsequent change is metadata merging.

At 452d713708bcb, the focused encoder/transformer quantization suite on B300 passed **118 tests and 21 subtests**:

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_text_encoder_loader.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_transformer_quant.py \
  -k 'not test_native_encoder_restoration_checks_checkpoint_before_fallback'
```

Four existing T5 fixture cases were excluded after reproducing their uninitialized-world-group failure on baseline; their assertions were not changed.

Coverage includes exact BF16/FP16 parity against Comfy NVFP4 activation quantization/matmul, CUDA scalar embedding parity, real safetensors metadata-to-loader coverage, and TP1/TP2 embedding sharding contracts. Multi-GPU E2E and cross-checkpoint quality equivalence are not claimed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This is checkpoint compatibility work, not a latency-speedup claim. Observed resident encoder weights were 48.09 GiB (BF16), 24.68 GiB (INT8) and 14.73 GiB (NVFP4); these are not full-pipeline peak memory. Single smoke-run timings are not treated as a controlled benchmark.

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit formatting and checks.
- [x] Focused unit and real-kernel tests.
- [x] Cookbook and quantization documentation updated; cookbook config, Mintlify validation and broken-link checks passed.
- [x] Remote end-to-end validation and numerical kernel checks.
- [x] Code-quality review; shared embedding implementation replaces duplicate code.

title: Add Opt-In for GLM-5.3 Flash breakable prefill CUDA graphs
author: willhu-jpg
body:
## Motivation

Enable opt-in breakable prefill CUDA graphs (BCG) for GLM-5.3 Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) with Triton KDA, TRTLLM DSA prefill/decode, and FP8 E4M3 KV. Other backend combinations remain eager unless BCG is explicitly selected. Its KDA gates, pooled DSA indexer and recurrent-state operations need capture handling before the architecture can pass the existing default compatibility checks.

## Task accuracy against ordinary eager

September 9 run: `20260909T170520.859362Z-bcg-latest-main-quality`, source `8b27ee67f7759e36dc386d04ff2933f5bd7b5e78` on main `ffe98a4279ba6e42d1f87dc4eeb6edb4887b9ea4`. One four-B300 allocation, fresh servers in BCG → eager → eager → BCG order, identical question sets and payloads, fixed two-request waves, no retries or profiling during accuracy measurement.

| Suite | Questions per arm | BCG accuracy | Eager accuracy | BCG − eager | One-sided 95% lower bound |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K, 5-shot, low reasoning | 1,319 | 95.60% | 95.64% | −0.04 pp | −0.49 pp |
| MMLU, fixed subset, 0-shot, low reasoning | 1,024 | 86.82% | 86.62% | +0.20 pp | −0.78 pp |
| GSM8K, fixed subset, 0-shot, max reasoning | 128 | 99.22% | 98.05% | +1.17 pp | +0.39 pp |

GSM8K uses the full test split with the first five training examples as demonstrations. MMLU samples 1,024 questions with seed 0; the max-reasoning GSM8K subset uses seed 479309393. Output limits are 4,096 tokens for low reasoning and 8,192 for max reasoning.

The validated image is `im-dpE65TM3SbmUUiVLdUKGvC`: Transformers 5.16.0.dev0 / Tokenizers 0.23.1 with the GLM image/video processors verified, FlashInfer 0.6.18, DeepGEMM 0.1.7, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 and NCCL 2.30.7.

## Performance

September 7 measurements on release source `b418d1c0387a0f4deb83796c2c0f217feb0be103`, using the same four B300 GPUs and BCG → eager → eager → BCG order. Each concurrency point used 250 measured agentic requests per pass, EOS enabled and a 4096-token output ceiling; conditioning was excluded and the prefix cache flushed before each point. These are medians of two passes, not confidence intervals.

| Concurrency | Eager output tok/min/GPU | BCG output tok/min/GPU | Change | Eager interactivity | BCG interactivity |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 | 23,675 | 28,525 | +20.5% | 66.2 | 73.6 |
| 32 | 30,973 | 37,074 | +19.7% | 27.3 | 40.7 |

Interactivity is `1000 / P90 request TPOT_ms`, in tokens/s/user. At concurrency 32, P90 TTFT increased from 3.95 s to 4.24 s. These compare serving configurations, including attention dispatch/padding and potentially differing output lengths; they do not isolate graph-launch overhead or measure a live-production speedup.

title: Add Ling-3.0-flash-VL model support
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Summary

This PR adds native SGLang support for [`inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-VL`](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-VL), including text, image, and video serving through the OpenAI-compatible API. It supports the official [BF16](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-VL), [FP8](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-VL-fp8), [INT4](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-VL-int4), and [FP4](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-VL-fp4) checkpoints.

Ling-3.0-flash-VL is a roughly 125B-parameter, 5.1B-active hybrid MoE VLM. Its 42-layer language backbone interleaves KDA and MLA attention and uses 512 routed experts with 8 selected per token. The public checkpoint uses one sigmoid router with correction bias per MoE layer. A 27-layer vision encoder and external two-layer `linear_proj` connect image and video features to the language model; the checkpoint has no deepstack tensors and disables the vision merger projection. Position encoding uses centered Bailing mRoPE with sections `[8, 12, 12]`.

The companion cookbook and deployment recipes are in [#38434](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38434).

## Motivation

The public model needs native integration beyond architecture registration: nested text and vision configuration, public checkpoint-name mapping, hybrid-attention state management, image and video preprocessing, centered multimodal RoPE, MoE topology exposure, and Ling-specific reasoning and tool-call parsing. This PR adds those paths while preserving compatibility with explicitly configured internal MultiRouter variants.

## Modifications

- Register the Bailing text and VL configurations, hybrid architecture, nested vision configuration, model entry points, and normalized language configuration used by the runtime.
- Add the V3 VL wrapper and image/video embedding flow, including PP-aware encoder ownership and explicit rejection of unsupported audio input.
- Add a single-pass loader for the public language, vision, projector, and router names, with required-weight coverage checks and no deepstack requirement when deepstack is absent from the configuration.
- Match the public MoE contract: one standard router per sparse layer with required `mlp.gate.weight` and `mlp.gate.expert_bias`; modality-specific gates remain opt-in and unreachable for the public checkpoint.
- Add the multimodal processor for image and video token expansion, feature preparation, and Bailing mRoPE position construction.
- Carry request-scoped modality metadata through batching and forward state for explicitly configured MultiRouter checkpoints, and route their per-token correction bias through the standard TopK reference path for correctness.
- Add centered Bailing mRoPE with a 2x symmetric cache, correct negative-origin cache growth, and YaRN `rope_scaling` overrides for the published 256K-context recipe.
- Resolve `--reasoning-parser auto` and `--tool-call-parser auto` to the existing `ling3` parsers through both Bailing architecture fallback and the public chat-template signature.
- Expose routed and shared expert topology to EP/EPLB and fix local expert mapping when the shared expert is fused.
- Auto-select the `flashinfer_mxfp4` MoE runner for the official mixed FP8/MXFP4 checkpoint with model- and format-specific guards, so the FP4 checkpoint requires no extra runner flag.
- Add registered CPU regression coverage for checkpoint loading, required weights, modality metadata, processor behavior, mRoPE/YaRN, parser selection, expert topology/location delegation, EPLB mapping, and MXFP4 backend selection.

## Validation

| Gate | Result | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Static and unit checks | Passed | Targeted Bailing CPU regression suites, `py_compile`, and all applicable pre-commit checks. |
| BF16 serving | Passed | Text and image requests completed on 2x NVIDIA GB300 with TP=2 and 4x NVIDIA H200 with TP=4. |
| Eager execution | Passed | Deterministic text and image requests completed with `--disable-cuda-graph` and `finish_reason=stop`. |
| Streaming protocol | Passed | Streamed deltas separated `reasoning_content` and `content`, emitted no `<think>` tag leakage, and ended with `finish_reason=stop`. |
| Structured output | Passed | A JSON Schema-constrained request returned valid schema-conforming JSON. |
| Parser protocol | Passed | Auto-detected Ling3 reasoning and tool-call parsers produced split reasoning, structured `tool_calls`, and direct content with `enable_thinking=false`. |
| KDA state | Passed | Warm rerun, prefix-reuse, and sequence-boundary probes completed successfully. |
| Expert parallelism | Passed | `--tp 4 --ep 4` completed text and image requests on 4x NVIDIA GB300 with and without EPLB. |
| Public quantized checkpoints | Verified | FP8 and INT4 text/image serving passed; FP4 text/image serving passed with the MXFP4 runner, and this PR auto-selects the same `flashinfer_mxfp4` backend. |

## Accuracy

MMMU-Pro uses all 1,730 examples. GSM8K uses all 1,319 examples. The measured BF16 results are:

| Benchmark | Hardware | Parallelism | Score | Stop rate |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| MMMU-Pro | 4x NVIDIA GB300 | TP=4 | 75.78% | 99.08% |
| MMMU-Pro | 4x NVIDIA H200 | TP=4 | 76.71% | 99.19% |
| MMMU-Pro | 2x NVIDIA GB300 | TP=2 | 77.86% | 99.65% |
| GSM8K | 4x NVIDIA H200 | TP=4 | 97.35% | 100.00% |

The official FP8 checkpoint scored 77.34% on MMMU-Pro (stop rate 99.77%, measured at TP=4 with EP=4) and 97.19% on GSM8K.

The 2x GB300 MMMU-Pro run used the chat template's default thinking mode, temperature 0, top-p 0.95, and 64 request threads. It had a 0.35% truncated rate, 0 errors, and 2,105 output tokens/s.

## Performance

`bench_serving` used an image workload with one random 720p JPEG per request, adding 883 vision tokens to the listed text input length. Runs used BF16, 2x GB300, TP=2, fixed input/output lengths, cache flushes between points, and no request errors. Throughput includes text input, vision, and output tokens; latency columns are P50.

| Text ISL/OSL | Concurrency | Prompts | TTFT (ms) | TPOT (ms) | ITL (ms) | Output tok/s | Total tok/s | Total tok/s/GPU |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1024/1024 | 1 | 8 | 339.27 | 4.41 | 4.41 | 209.56 | 612.45 | 306 |
| 1024/1024 | 16 | 32 | 1,486.45 | 8.75 | 8.87 | 1,561.24 | 4,556.41 | 2,278 |
| 1024/1024 | 64 | 128 | 4,005.60 | 15.36 | 15.06 | 3,295.52 | 9,621.62 | 4,811 |
| 256/128 | 16 | 64 | 1,480.46 | 7.91 | 7.85 | 810.19 | 8,209.02 | 4,105 |
| 256/128 | 64 | 256 | 3,198.87 | 16.95 | 12.33 | 1,477.54 | 14,967.18 | 7,484 |

These measurements apply only to the listed hardware, topology, precision, and workload; they are not a cross-platform performance claim.

## Limitations

- DeepEP all-to-all is not usable at this revision: normal mode rejects the unquantized MoE path, while low-latency mode reaches a deprecated DeepGEMM masked path. Plain EP is verified as described above.
- PP, DP, PD, and EPD are not claimed by this PR.
- Audio is absent from the public checkpoint and is rejected by the processor.
- No full accuracy result is claimed here for the INT4 or FP4 checkpoints.
- Broad video-quality evaluation is not included.
- Dynamic per-token router bias for explicitly configured MultiRouter checkpoints uses the correctness-oriented standard TopK path rather than a backend-specialized fast path; the public checkpoint uses a single static correction-bias router and does not enter this path.
- The companion cookbook uses the development image until this support is available in a published image.

## Evidence

- Public model, configuration, processor, chat template, and weights: [`inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-VL`](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-VL).
- The public checkpoint contract is visible in [`config.json`](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-VL/blob/main/config.json) and [`model.safetensors.index.json`](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-VL/blob/main/model.safetensors.index.json).
- Thinking and tool syntax are defined by the public [`chat_template.jinja`](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-VL/blob/main/chat_template.jinja).
- Implementation and regression evidence is contained in the source and tests in this PR; no private repository or unreleased checkpoint is used as evidence.

## Checklist

- [x] Code is formatted and all applicable pre-commit checks pass.
- [x] CPU unit tests are added and registered.
- [x] BF16 and FP8 accuracy results are recorded.
- [x] Eager, streaming, structured-output, KDA, and EP/EPLB paths are validated.
- [x] Companion cookbook PR is open.
- [ ] Re-run required CI on the final public PR revision.
- [ ] Replace the development image reference after a release image contains this support.
