title: [Diffusion] Optimize SANA-WM convolution post-processing and streaming GDN
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- Extend the existing SANA convolution post-processing kernels to NCHW and to an already-biased GLU input; use them in SANA-WM's spatial FFN.
- Traverse streaming's exclusive backward GDN recurrence directly in reverse frame order, removing full-video flip/shift/cat intermediates. Preserve the forward recurrence and carried state.
- Verify each supported signature against the original implementation before enabling the path; fall back on mismatch, JIT failure, gradients, compilation, or unverified graph capture.
- Add convolution rounding, streaming state, changed-input graph replay, and fallback tests.

## H200 results

Setup: **1x H200**, PyTorch `2.11.0+cu130`, native `SanaWMTwoStagePipeline`, 1280x704, 49 requested frames, 16 fps, seed 42. Prompt: `a camera moving forward and turning left`; input: the SANA-WM cat image, camera actions `w-16,wl-16,l-16`. Bidirectional uses 20 main denoise steps and guidance 4.5; streaming uses its native preset with `--streaming --refiner-chunked`.

Each quality mode uses fresh processes in **A-B-B-A** order on the same GPU, with request warmup and output saving. E2E is the SGLang perf dump's `total_duration_ms`, not process startup time; loading, warmup, and profiled requests are excluded. The main-denoise metric excludes the refiner and decoding stages.

The measured baseline was `77fb7a72889a7155b0af34739a409d4517219530`, with candidates `f49ed7f8edfdb6053ce8b0bbe59e4e143f332a7e` (bidirectional) and `00a7c22370aa8d3483b0f3e5d3c1be05f86144c0` (streaming). This PR is rebased onto `482e9f257bb9d9ac57c2245c93768a96ec70edbe`. The kernel and recurrence arithmetic match the measured implementation; the rebase adds only lazy facade lookup after the CUDA guard and formatting to the model code. The E2E numbers below were collected on the recorded benchmark commits, not rerun on the rebased PR; unrelated pipeline changes between those bases may affect absolute latency.

### Eager end-to-end

| Model | Quality | Baseline runs | PR runs | Mean latency reduction |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Bidirectional | lossless | 11.284110 / 11.401986 s | 10.886620 / 10.984227 s | **3.594%** |
| Bidirectional | high | 11.218915 / 11.249977 s | 10.882883 / 10.880532 s | **3.140%** |
| Streaming | lossless | 4.031260 / 3.976402 s | 3.901933 / 3.915875 s | **2.371%** |
| Streaming | high | 4.110855 / 3.978998 s | 4.009085 / 3.891730 s | **2.337%** |

### Main denoise stage

| Model | Quality | Baseline runs | PR runs | Mean latency reduction |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Bidirectional | lossless | 9.321119 / 9.291558 s | 8.944371 / 8.953174 s | 3.842% |
| Bidirectional | high | 9.288189 / 9.293075 s | 8.943616 / 8.946158 s | 3.721% |
| Streaming | lossless | 1.683968 / 1.663815 s | 1.555888 / 1.546329 s | 7.335% |
| Streaming | high | 1.664033 / 1.658613 s | 1.667980 / 1.529492 s | 3.767% |

Both high streaming samples are retained despite larger variation. Convolution-only streaming improved E2E by just 0.408%; its final result above includes the reverse-scan optimization. Bidirectional peak reserved memory is 79.139 -> 79.133 GiB; streaming fits within 87.289 GiB. GPU allocation snapshots found no extra process on the measured GPU during the final matrices; these are sampled checks, not continuous exclusivity guarantees.

### Breakable CUDA Graph

Both native SANA-WM presets were actually launched with BCG requested. The pipeline support gate logged `[Diffusion BCG] disabled`; there was no capture. The eager fallback timings are excluded. Kernel-level graph replay tests pass, but this PR makes no model-level BCG performance claim.

### Kernel and profile evidence

The initial trace exposed repeated conv bias/SiLU and GLU chains. The convolution experiment preserved all BF16 intermediate rounding. Extracting the depthwise convolution bias caused 45,490,650 mismatched elements out of 165,580,800, so the final implementation keeps that native biased convolution intact.

| Profile-shaped experiment | Original | Candidate | Scope |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1x1 conv + bias + SiLU, input `[14,2240,22,40]` | 3.3192 ms | 2.8615 ms | Full conv sequence |
| GLU after biased depthwise, input `[14,13440,22,40]` | 0.4313 ms | 0.1183 ms | Post-processing only |
| Main cached GDN, 4 frames, contiguous D/N | 1.4480 ms | 1.0153 ms | Full forward + backward recurrence |
| Camera cached GDN, 4 frames, contiguous D/N | 1.0928 ms | 0.7887 ms | Full forward + backward recurrence |

The [original microbenchmark scripts and raw results](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/tree/pr-media/diffusion-prs/sana-wm-conv-gdn-h200) are included. These CUDA-graph device microbenchmarks are prototype measurements used to choose the edit, separate from the native eager request measurements above. GDN uses `[B,H,D,S]=[1,20,112,880]`, FP32; convolution uses BF16.

Paired full-stage profiles confirm the mechanism in the actual model:

| Main-denoise profile | Baseline | PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Bidirectional kernel launches | 92,068 | 91,268 |
| Bidirectional cumulative kernel time | 9,276.882 ms | 8,929.363 ms |
| Streaming kernel launches | 79,555 | 70,755 |
| Streaming cumulative kernel time | 1,557.402 ms | 1,433.840 ms |
| Streaming flip kernels | 2,850 | 600 |
| Streaming copy kernels | 14,531 | 13,031 |
| Streaming cat kernels | 2,589 | 1,989 |

Bidirectional adds 400 fused bias-SiLU calls (71.440 ms total) and 400 GLU calls (45.299 ms). Streaming removes 400 post-convolution launches plus 8,400 reverse-scan launches. Native depthwise counts are unchanged (1,600 bidirectional, 800 streaming), as are other-stage kernel counts. Cumulative kernel time is diagnostic, not wall-clock E2E.

## Output comparison

All eight formal videos for **each** model are byte-identical across lossless/high and baseline/PR. Independently decoded frames have **SSIM 1.0 and zero pixel error**. Bidirectional saves 48 frames because the refiner removes the first sink anchor; streaming saves 49 frames.

| Model | Full baseline video | Full PR video | SHA256 shared by all 8 formal outputs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bidirectional | [MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/sana-wm-conv-gdn-h200/bidirectional-baseline.mp4) | [MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/sana-wm-conv-gdn-h200/bidirectional-pr.mp4) | `706642d6d8daf304f0a3ca5d7aaa94b88841e1d9a686f151143ddeedff5f272d` |
| streaming | [MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/sana-wm-conv-gdn-h200/streaming-baseline.mp4) | [MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/sana-wm-conv-gdn-h200/streaming-pr.mp4) | `433929d59ec7efec9b566218e63896b5ebfd732f08b8978e2f9e586d0394686f` |

Bidirectional frame comparison (baseline above, PR below):

![Bidirectional baseline and PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/sana-wm-conv-gdn-h200/bidirectional-comparison.jpg)

Streaming frame comparison (baseline above, PR below):

![Streaming baseline and PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/sana-wm-conv-gdn-h200/streaming-comparison.jpg)

[All 16 individual measurements and output hashes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/sana-wm-conv-gdn-h200/benchmark-results.json).

## Reproduce

Run each command on the baseline and PR with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` selecting one idle H200, for each of `--quality=lossless` and `--quality=high`. `cat.png` is the SANA-WM benchmark image (SHA256 `b3596420d2f0bdf3122f04c89b550d7ff504045312b6b1e075a0c2841531543d`).

```bash
SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1 sglang generate \
  --backend=sglang --model-path Efficient-Large-Model/SANA-WM_bidirectional \
  --pipeline-class-name=SanaWMTwoStagePipeline \
  --prompt 'a camera moving forward and turning left' --image-path cat.png \
  --width=1280 --height=704 --num-frames=49 --fps=16 --seed=42 \
  --num-inference-steps=20 --guidance-scale=4.5 --action=w-16,wl-16,l-16 \
  --performance-mode=manual --quality=lossless --warmup-mode=request \
  --save-output --perf-dump-path bidirectional.json

SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1 sglang generate \
  --backend=sglang --model-path Efficient-Large-Model/SANA-WM_streaming \
  --pipeline-class-name=SanaWMTwoStagePipeline --streaming --refiner-chunked \
  --prompt 'a camera moving forward and turning left' --image-path cat.png \
  --width=1280 --height=704 --num-frames=49 --fps=16 --seed=42 \
  --action=w-16,wl-16,l-16 --performance-mode=manual \
  --quality=lossless --warmup-mode=request --save-output --perf-dump-path streaming.json
```

Add `--profile --profile-all-stages` for separate diagnostic runs. Add `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph --warmup-resolutions 1280x704 --warmup-num-frames 49` to reproduce the native BCG support check.

## Validation

- Final rebased head `8218a2455f4100ba3d87edbadf631707431e1988`: **9 H200 tests passed** (5 convolution + 4 reverse-scan), with an idle-GPU precheck.
- Full pre-commit on all four changed files and `git diff --check`: passed.

- Original measured commits: 5 convolution tests and 4 reverse-scan tests passed on H200, plus 24 exact GDN prototype output/state checks.
- Covers both convolution layouts/bias modes, real convolution rounding, multiple GDN chunks and beta layouts, updated graph inputs and carried states, unverified capture, mismatch fallback, autograd fallback, and nonfinite queries.
- Model weight cleanup verified zero remaining task-owned files/bytes/weights after each model: bidirectional 215,530,433,392 ledger bytes / 1,115 weight files -> 0; streaming 187,560,006,533 bytes / 22 weight files -> 0. The ledger counts cache hardlinks, not unique physical storage.

title: [Diffusion] Preserve BF16 rounding in Hopper LTX QKNorm and RoPE fusion
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

Preserve eager BF16 rounding in the opt-in Hopper LTX QKNorm + split-RoPE kernel. The existing high-quality path from #38396 keeps the normalized value and cosine product in FP32; on the tested LTX-2.3 TI2V workload this produces visible frame differences and audio drift. This patch restores those two BF16 boundaries while retaining the fused launch.

A compile-time specialization selects the Hopper arithmetic. The existing SM90 quality gate and SM100 FP32 specialization remain unchanged. Recorded H200 validation covered exact Q/K equality at production shapes and changed-input CUDA graph replay.

**Comparison scope:** this is a numerical-correctness fix. The E2E table compares the rounded fusion with a matched **unfused** reference, demonstrating the useful fusion benefit after fixing rounding. It is **not** a measured speedup over current main's approximate Hopper fusion. All five device microbenchmarks are slower with fusion; that result is included below.

## H200 setup and E2E

Native `Lightricks/LTX-2.3`, `LTX2TwoStagePipeline`, 768x512, 121 frames, native 30 first-stage + 3 refinement steps, seed 42. Prompt: `The cat starts walking slowly towards the camera.` Input is linked below. 2x H200, CFG parallel 2, TP1/SP1, resident two-stage DiTs and auxiliary components, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130. No torch.compile.

Measured unfused reference: `414ffd7115c60ef0c2e0e3aa27db80a8cfa98d1e`; rounded candidate: `1142b373a1bbb6ec8dbedda92ec0904305ea2962`. The PR is rebased onto `482e9f257bb9d9ac57c2245c93768a96ec70edbe`, which already includes the earlier Hopper opt-in. GPU unit tests were rerun at validation revision `dc9f4fb8458cb30ca6aeef35f356715e27851c39`. The two production implementation files are unchanged from that revision; the full-model matrix was not rerun after rebase.

Fresh-process A-B-B-A on the same two physical GPUs, request warmup, saved outputs. E2E is the synchronized SGLang perf-dump request duration; loading, warmup and profiler overhead are excluded.

| Order | High/eager implementation | Denoise | E2E |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| A1 | Unfused reference | 13.700956 s | 14.949595 s |
| B1 | Rounded fusion | 12.000513 s | 13.851976 s |
| B2 | Rounded fusion | 12.406684 s | 14.199766 s |
| A2 | Unfused reference | 13.296953 s | 15.066272 s |
| A mean | | 13.498954 s | 15.007933 s |
| B mean | | 12.203599 s | 14.025871 s |
| Reduction vs unfused | | **9.596%** | **6.544%** |

Peak reserved memory is 110.666 GiB/rank for all four rows. Ten-second GPU snapshots contain only the three expected process IDs on the selected pair; they do not prove continuous exclusivity. Earlier cells affected by competing jobs/OOM are excluded.

## Kernel benchmark and profile

BF16, batch 1, one H200. The recorded benchmark compares the actual native RMSNorm + split-RoPE chain against this rounded fused kernel, including both Q and K.

| Q sequence | K sequence | Heads | Head dim | Unfused | Rounded fused |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1536 | 1536 | 32 | 128 | 37.6058 us | 57.1917 us |
| 1536 | 1024 | 32 | 128 | 34.2397 us | 46.5396 us |
| 126 | 126 | 32 | 64 | 13.0746 us | 15.1814 us |
| 126 | 1024 | 32 | 64 | 15.2884 us | 17.4531 us |
| 6144 | 6144 | 32 | 128 | 141.0940 us | 154.4066 us |

[Raw microbenchmark output](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/ltx-hopper-rounded-rope-h200/kernel-benchmark.log).

Matched high/eager diagnostic traces, two profiled timesteps:

| Profile measurement | Unfused | Rounded fusion |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Total kernel launches | 38,841 | 36,549 |
| BF16 RMSNorm launches | 5,748 | 3,456 |
| Standalone split-RoPE launches | 2,292 | 0 |
| Fused QKNorm/RoPE launches | 0 | 2,292 |
| Cumulative kernel time | 582.563 ms | 591.247 ms |

Fusion removes 2,292 launches while increasing cumulative GPU time. Reduced host launch overhead is a plausible explanation for the whole-request improvement; these measurements do not establish a device-kernel speedup.

## Output comparison

All four formal MP4 hashes were reverified. Every decoded video frame is pixel-identical across A1/B1/B2/A2: 121 frames, SSIM 1, zero pixel error. The earlier approximate fusion was rejected on this workload: mean frame SSIM 0.912, worst 0.835, cross-path audio SNR 10.38 dB.

Audio has native repeat variability, so MP4 files are not byte-identical. With the rounded kernel:

| Audio pair | SNR |
| --- | ---: |
| A1 / A2 | 37.796 dB |
| B1 / B2 | 37.993 dB |
| A1 / B1 | 37.635 dB |
| A2 / B2 | 38.169 dB |

Cross-path audio differences are comparable to within-path repeats. This model-level result is limited to the fixed LTX-2.3 TI2V preset; it does not establish acceptable high-mode quality for other LTX-family models.

| Input | Actual output contact sheet: unfused above, rounded below |
| --- | --- |
| ![Input cat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/ltx-hopper-rounded-rope-h200/input-cat.png) | ![Matched video frames](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/ltx-hopper-rounded-rope-h200/comparison.jpg) |

Actual videos with audio: [A1 unfused](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/raw/refs/heads/pr-media/diffusion-prs/ltx-hopper-rounded-rope-h200/a1.mp4), [B1 rounded](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/raw/refs/heads/pr-media/diffusion-prs/ltx-hopper-rounded-rope-h200/b1.mp4), [B2 rounded](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/raw/refs/heads/pr-media/diffusion-prs/ltx-hopper-rounded-rope-h200/b2.mp4), [A2 unfused](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/raw/refs/heads/pr-media/diffusion-prs/ltx-hopper-rounded-rope-h200/a2.mp4).

[Raw model measurements, profile counts and media hashes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/ltx-hopper-rounded-rope-h200/benchmark-results.json); [decoded audio measurements](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/ltx-hopper-rounded-rope-h200/audio-metrics.json).

## BCG applicability

High + BCG is rejected by the runtime (`cannot be used with breakable cuda graphs`) and contributes no performance result. A separate single lossless eager/BCG direction check captured successfully and produced identical video, but showed no speed benefit: E2E 14.6516 / 18.8123 s, denoise 12.7195 / 13.1070 s. This single pair is not a repeated regression estimate. BCG peak reserved memory was 119.734 GiB. This patch retains the existing quality gate and makes no BCG speedup claim.

## Reproduce

Select two idle H200s with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`. Download the linked input to `cat.png`.

```bash
SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1 sglang generate \
  --backend=sglang --model-path=Lightricks/LTX-2.3 \
  --pipeline-class-name=LTX2TwoStagePipeline \
  --image-path=cat.png --prompt 'The cat starts walking slowly towards the camera.' \
  --width=768 --height=512 --num-frames=121 --seed=42 \
  --num-gpus=2 --cfg-parallel-size=2 \
  --ltx2-two-stage-device-mode=resident --component-residency=all=resident \
```

title: [AMD] [GLM-5.3-Flash Day 0] Route mHC through AITER on gfx950
author: Raiden-Makoto
body:
## Summary

Replacement for #37626, which GitHub closed when its deleted support base was merged into main.

GLM-5.3-Flash uses mHC in all 45 decoder layers (`hc_mult=4`, `hidden_size=4096`). The support branch already carries the flattened mHC state contract and `MHCLayerCommunicator`, but `hc_pre` and `hc_post` have no AITER dispatch: enabling `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` still leaves them on TileLang when its flags are set, or on the Torch fallback otherwise.

This is a Day-0 correctness blocker on gfx950, not a performance-only path. Every attention and FFN sublayer crosses an mHC pre/post boundary before DSA, KDA, or MoE can produce a model output.

| Condition | Before | With this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HIP + gfx95 + `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` | no AITER mHC route | `aiter.ops.mhc.mhc_pre` / `mhc_post` |
| AITER symbol missing | no probe | one warning, latch disabled, Torch fallback |
| AITER runtime failure | request failure | one warning, latch disabled, Torch fallback |
| HIP + DeepGEMM mHC flag | reaches NVIDIA-only prenorm path | rejected by the backend gate |
| non-HIP TileLang/DeepGEMM | existing optimized route | unchanged |

The AITER imports stay lazy because this module is imported during model-registry discovery. No AITER symbol is required until the gfx950 runtime actually selects this backend.

## Scope

`python/sglang/kernels/ops/layernorm/mhc.py` is the only production file changed.

- Add the HIP + gfx95 + AITER dispatch and failure latch.
- Gate TileLang mHC pre/post and DeepGEMM prenorm to their non-HIP route.
- Preserve the existing Torch, TileLang, gfx1250, communicator, model, and tensor contracts.
- Add one gfx950 test file (`test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_mhc_aiter_hip.py`): gate selects AITER, HIP with AITER off stays on Torch and never loads TileLang, import/runtime failures latch to Torch, and `mhc_pre`/`mhc_post` match the Torch oracle.

The fused `mhc_post_pre` boundary is intentionally untouched. It is a later launch-fusion optimization; this PR enables the standalone `mhc_post -> mhc_pre` sequence required for correctness. DSA, k-pool, MLA, MoE, CUDA graphs, and full-model serving are outside this PR.

## Test plan

Combined main-based integration (`RM/glm53-day0-main-integration` tested at `9d0d62b744`; current integration head `4e2f84ff3c`; TP8/TP4 validation predates the above-cap guard, whose below-cap path is unchanged, pinned AITER `d9e5ef7ce0`, fresh caches): TP8 GSM8K **97.50%** in 87.0s with 0.00% errors; TP4 GSM8K **96.97%** in 320.2s with 0.00% errors. Decode CUDA graphs were enabled in both runs.

Recovery base: `main` @ `30e7a3072d`.  
Recovery validation on MI355X: scoped pre-commit passed; 6 CPU, 3 gfx950, and 3 checkpoint tests passed at the time. The test set was since cut to one gfx950 file with 4 cases; the CPU dispatch file and the checkpoint-driven manual test were removed (see below).


Docker: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x-20260901`.  
Base: `xinyuan/glm-5.3-flash-support` @ `545bd6f839`.  
The same test files were run in both arms; `mhc.py` is the only variable.

| Arm | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline | CPU dispatch: **1 passed, 5 errors**; every AITER-specific gfx950/checkpoint case fails because `_try_aiter_mhc_pre` / `_try_aiter_mhc_post` do not exist. The checkpoint-only tensor audit passes. |
| This PR | CPU dispatch: **6 passed**; isolated gfx950: **3 passed**; checkpoint-driven: **3 passed**. Not re-executed after the test cut: the surviving gfx950 file runs in `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`. |

The gfx950 file covers production `hidden_size=4096`, `hc_mult=4`, token counts 1/8/17/32/64/128, 2 and 20 Sinkhorn iterations, norm fused/unfused, plus the gate, the HIP-never-TileLang path, and the failure latch, all unmocked on device.

The checkpoint arm (one-time, test file removed) used `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` and `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4@b5688f2549` without loading either model. It verified all 270 mHC tensors are complete and byte-identical, ran every real attention and FFN parameter set across layers 0-44 through AITER against the Torch oracle, and ran the complete two-sublayer flow for every layer. The file was dropped because no sglang diff can turn it red; the evidence is recorded here.

| Check | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Registration | `register_amd_ci(suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x")` only; nothing registers on CPU or CUDA |
| `pre-commit` | all hooks pass on all four files, including registered-test CI validation |
| Accuracy | **not measured** — GLM-5.3-Flash still depends on the remaining Day-0 enablement PRs before server-level accuracy is meaningful |
| Speed | **not measured** — this PR establishes standalone mHC correctness and does not add post/pre fusion |

title: [AMD] [GLM-5.3-Flash Day 0] Enable zero-RoPE TileLang DSA on gfx950
author: Raiden-Makoto
body:
## Summary

Replacement for #37653, which GitHub closed when its deleted support base was merged into main.

GLM-5.3-Flash sparse DSA uses a 256-wide NoPE latent with a zero-width RoPE tail. The HIP TileLang BF16 partial kernel still emits zero-extent tail allocation/copy/gather/GEMM work, while the HIP FP8 kernel and scaled cache helpers are specialized for the existing DeepSeek-style 512+64 layout.

This PR enables GLM's 256+0 geometry without changing the established 512+64 behavior.

| Contract | Before | With this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HIP BF16 tail | zero-width tail buffers and operations are emitted | tail allocation, copy, gather, and GEMM are compiled out |
| HIP FP8 main width | fixed to four 128-wide tiles (`d_v=512`) | supports two tiles for `d_v=256` and retains four for `d_v=512` |
| HIP FP8 RoPE tail | fixed 64-wide tail | supports zero or 64 elements and compiles out zero-tail work |
| scaled FP8 cache row | fixed 656 bytes (`512 FP8 + 16 scale + 128 RoPE`) | also supports 264 bytes (`256 FP8 + 8 scale + 0 RoPE`) |
| paged dequant/gather | fixed 512+64 offsets and launch geometry | derives dimensions, scale count, offsets, and output width from the packed row |

## Scope

Four production files:

- `tilelang_kernel.py`: compile out HIP BF16 zero-tail work and specialize the HIP FP8 kernel for either 256+0 or 512+64.
- `quant_k_cache.py`: infer or accept the NoPE width, derive the number of 128-element scale tiles, and permit an empty RoPE tensor.
- `dequant_k_cache.py`: recognize 264-byte and 656-byte packed rows and use their derived dimensions in direct, paged, and gather/dequant/requant paths.
- `memory_pool.py`: document the dimension-derived scaled layout and optional RoPE payload at the existing write sites.

One MI35x test file directly covers the TileLang kernels and scaled cache helpers. No model loading, server launch, accuracy benchmark, scheduler/backend policy, dense MHA path, mHC path, MoE path, or CUDA TileLang FP8 behavior is changed.

The FP8 kernel keeps the existing 512+64 allocation, GEMM, accumulation, normalization, and store order. The 256+0 specialization emits only the first two 128-wide tiles and no tail operations.

## Test plan

Combined main-based integration (`RM/glm53-day0-main-integration` tested at `9d0d62b744`; current integration head `4e2f84ff3c`; TP8/TP4 validation predates the above-cap guard, whose below-cap path is unchanged, pinned AITER `d9e5ef7ce0`, fresh caches): TP8 GSM8K **97.50%** in 87.0s with 0.00% errors; TP4 GSM8K **96.97%** in 320.2s with 0.00% errors. Decode CUDA graphs were enabled in both runs.

Recovery base: `main` @ `30e7a3072d`.  
Recovery validation on MI355X: scoped pre-commit passed; all 4 BF16/FP8 TileLang and cache-layout test groups passed.


Docker: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x-20260830`.  
Hardware: one MI350X (`gfx950`).  
Base: `xinyuan/glm-5.3-flash-support` @ `545bd6f839`.  
The same new test file was run in both arms; the four production files are the only variables.

| Arm | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline | **FAILED (6 failures, 8 errors)**. All six BF16 256+0 cases hit the generated zero-tail kernel failure; the 256+0 scaled-cache case is rejected by the fixed layout; FP8 256+0 does not match the Torch oracle. |
| This PR | BF16 256+0 matrix: **passed**; FP8 256+0 matrix: **passed**; 256+0 and 512+64 cache round-trip/paged-gather checks: **passed**; BF16/FP8 512+64 controls: **passed**. |

Direct GLM geometry coverage:

- Q `[tokens, 64, 256]`, KV `[slots, 1, 256]`, output BF16 `[tokens, 64, 256]`;
- token counts 1, 8, and 17;
- top-k widths 2048 and 2112;
- fully valid rows and 2051 logical entries padded with `-1` to 2112;
- explicit Torch gather/mask/score/softmax/value oracle;
- BF16 and native gfx950 FP8 inputs;
- finite shape/dtype checks and bit-identical repeated execution;
- 264-byte (`256+0`) and 656-byte (`512+64`) scaled-cache round trips and repeated-page gathers;
- BF16 and FP8 512+64 sparse-attention regression controls.

| Check | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Registration | `register_amd_ci(suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x")` |
| Formatting | File-scoped syntax, isort, Ruff, Black, codespell, and registered-test validation pass. The whole-tree package-location hook separately reports a pre-existing file outside this PR: `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_triton_store_cache_local.py`. |
| Accuracy | **not measured** — this is component-level Day-0 correctness; full-model serving is intentionally outside scope. |
| Speed | **not measured** — no server or performance benchmark was run. |

title: [Spec] Allow speculative workers to stage prefill shared reads
author: paulzhang-tm
body:
## Motivation

Speculative workers with later draft-prefill readers cannot publish the early prefill read-done event, even when those reads can be staged before target replay. Add an optional callback so workers can opt in after staging their shared reads.

## Modifications

- Add `ModelRunner.prefill_shared_read_stager: Optional[Callable[[ForwardBatch], bool]]`, defaulting to `None`. The speculative worker installs the callback for its forward call and returns `True` only after staging its shared reads before event recording.
- Invoke the callback after the prefill flag, mode, and backend checks. An absent or unsuccessful callback retains the existing fallback; non-speculative and DFLASH/DSPARK behavior is preserved.

## Accuracy Tests

`python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_prefill_shared_read_done.py` — **12 passed**. Covers staging before event creation, unsuccessful/missing staging, existing prefill gates, and DFLASH/DSPARK compatibility.

Upstream pre-commit hooks passed for all three changed files.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No benchmark: this PR adds the hook without enabling it in an upstream worker. Model-specific staging and performance validation remain with the worker implementation.

title: [Spec] Support large MTP batches in short-convolution metadata
author: paulzhang-tm
body:
## Motivation

Inkling MTP batches above 1,023 requests can fail during target-verify or draft-extend CUDA graph capture. The fused short-convolution metadata helper rejects these shapes, and the backend cannot use its allocating unfused fallback on the graph path. For example, a 1,264-request batch hits this assertion during startup.

## Modifications

- Support variable-length batches through 2,047 requests. For batches above 1,023, halve the token tile from 256 to 128 as the boundary tile doubles to 2,048, keeping the maximum comparison tile at 262,144 elements.
- Exempt uniform-length target verification from this batch-size cap: its boundary and sequence-index calculations use arithmetic rather than the cumulative sum and comparison reduction.
- Add exact-reference checks at the new boundaries and CUDA graph replay coverage with changed lengths, initial-state flags, and padding slots. Preserve representative PR CI cases and the complete nightly matrix.

## Accuracy Tests

- Offline Triton compilation passed for all four metadata modes on both `sm_90` and `sm_100` (eight variants), using the larger variable-length tile and verification beyond the variable-length bound.
- Both metadata test suites collect successfully: 119 tests skipped because no CUDA device is available in this checkout. GPU numerical comparisons and replay execution remain to be run in CI.
- The representative PR CI selection collects 25 extend-metadata tests, including the new large-batch and replay cases.
- Ruff formatting/lint, isort, registered-test validation, and repository Python test-layout checks passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No end-to-end benchmark was run. Existing batches through 1,023 requests retain their kernel tile dimensions; larger variable-length batches use more token tiles while keeping the maximum comparison tile size unchanged.

title: [Fix] sampling: deterministic top-p / top-k renorm when tp_size > 1 (TP rank divergence in DFlash/DSpark)
author: gilfordting
body:
## Summary

flashinfer's default top-p / top-k renorm kernels are non-deterministic (float `atomicAdd`); because of this, TP ranks that renormalize the same logits can produce different results. Every consumer of this output (plain sampler, spec-verify) samples against a deterministic coin and commits the result to per-rank KV/radix state. A coin that lands in between the cross-rank gap causes divergence across ranks, and NCCL collectives hang.

Previous PRs (#33549, #33289; #33614) work around this issue by broadcasting rank 0's decision. This PR addresses the root cause and avoids an extra collective, by routing the renorm through flashinfer's `is_deterministic=True` variants. This is turned on where it matters:

| configuration                         | renorm kernels  | why                                                            |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| single rank                           | fast            | nothing to agree with                                          |
| `attn_tp_size > 1`                    | deterministic   | each rank computes the same result; bit-identical across ranks |
| `--enable-deterministic-inference`    | deterministic   | self-explanatory                                               |
| `SGLANG_RENORM_DETERMINISTIC=1` / `0` | forced on / off | explicit override                                              |

Repro + results are below. With all relevant broadcasts turned off, the fast kernels reproduce the hang on H100 and B200 in every run. The deterministic kernels never diverge, and the end-to-end cost to TPOT is marginal.

## Root cause

- `sgl_kernel.top_p_renorm_prob` and `top_k_renorm_prob` forward to flashinfer.
    - Top-p on rows longer than 2048 uses the AIR radix kernel (>= 0.6.7, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#2752) whose default histogram is a float atomic.
    - Top-k (`RadixTopKRenormProbMultiCTA`) pools the kept mass with a float atomic.
    - flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4831 (0.7.x, sglang pins 0.7.2) added a fixed-point `is_deterministic=True` at unchanged latency.
- In non-greedy verification, each rank compares its own `target_probs` (top-p/top-k output) against a shared coin and samples the bonus token from `relu(q - p)`.
    - If ranks differ slightly, the coin might cross the acceptance or bonus thresholds on some ranks and not others; this will cause KV state to drift and a later prefix match will cause NCCL collectives to hang.
- The sampler's `min_p` path calls the same kernels with no broadcast (`SGLANG_SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP` is off by default).
- Earlier synthetic repros were clean because they used `top_p=1.0`, which skips the kernel entirely.

## Repro

**Setup**

- Image: current main (nightly `ed8c3139`, flashinfer 0.7.1, sgl_kernel 0.4.10) with this PR applied.
- Model, config, workload: TP=2 DFlash, Llama-3.1-8B + `z-lab/LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct-DFlash-UltraChat`, `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.9`, 32 concurrent multi-turn streams, fp8 KV.
- Broadcast collectives off:
    - Hard-coded broadcast is only on for the EAGLE path. We use DFlash.
    - `SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC=off` turns off #33614's broadcasts.
    - `SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP`, `SGLANG_SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP` are off by default.
- Deterministic renorm kernels on using a new environment variable, `SGLANG_RENORM_DETERMINISTIC=1`.
- A probe all-gathers per-verify-step fingerprints of `{rng state, prefix_lens, draft_tokens, target_logits, target_probs, accept_len, bonus, commit_lens, out_tokens}` and reports the first field that differs.
    - It also calls `top_p_renorm_prob` twice on the same input on one rank, counting mismatches after.

**Results**

"knob" below refers to the new env-var, `SGLANG_RENORM_DETERMINISTIC=1`.
| broadcast | renorm | runs | requests per run | first cross-rank `target_probs` difference | rank-local mismatches (top-p calls) | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| off | fast (knob=0, same kernels as main) | 4 x H100, 2 x B200 | 1.4k to 6.5k | 1 to 22 s | 0.4 to 0.9 % | **all 6 hung**, at 190 to 610 s |
| off | deterministic (knob=1) | 3 x H100, 2 x B200 | 22.6k to 35.4k | never | 0 of 276,000 | all 5 clean, full 30 min |
| all (#33614) | fast (knob=0) | 1 x H100 | 25.2k | 14 s | 0.9 % | clean: 436 `target_probs` divergences, none reaches a token |
| all (#33614) | deterministic (knob=1) | 1 x H100 | 24.4k | never | 0 of 46,000 | clean, 0 divergences |

Every fast-kernel run with the broadcast off hung, with the same recorded chain each time:

- `target_probs` differs between ranks while logits, `prefix_lens` and RNG are identical.
- `bonus` / `out_tokens` differ on one rank.
- Next step's `draft_tokens` differ.
- Hang.

Toggling only the knob to 1 on the same image, model, load and probe consistently results in zero divergences, zero rank-local mismatches, and no hang.

## Kernel measurements

We perform 99 repeated calls on byte-identical input. Settings: flashinfer 0.7.1, vocab 128256, H100. B200 and B300 give the same results.

`nondet` refers to calls that differ from call 0.

| rows | input distribution | kernel | current default        | `is_deterministic=True` |
| ---- | ------------------ | ------ | ---------------------- | ----------------------- |
| 32   | flat               | top-p  | 0.136 ms, nondet 99/99 | 0.169 ms, 0/99          |
| 32   | peaky              | top-p  | 0.127 ms, 0/99         | 0.149 ms, 0/99          |
| 32   | flat               | top-k  | 0.042 ms, 99/99        | 0.042 ms, 0/99          |
| 32   | peaky              | top-k  | 0.042 ms, 77/99        | 0.042 ms, 0/99          |
| 256  | flat               | top-p  | 0.603 ms, 98/99        | 0.815 ms, 0/99          |
| 256  | flat               | top-k  | 0.288 ms, 99/99        | 0.289 ms, 0/99          |

We observe the following:

- Top-k performs near-identical between both fast and deterministic arms.
- Top-p adds 20 to 45% to a 0.1 to 0.8 ms kernel. We measure how much this matters in the next section.
- The deterministic wrapper adds no host sync and no `cudaMalloc`, so there is no overhead.

## End-to-end speed

**Setup**

- Workload: `sglang.bench_serving`, random 512-in / 256-out, 400 prompts, concurrency 32.
- Model, config: Llama-3.1-8B, fp8 KV, triton attention, H100.
- One container boots four servers in sequence with the knob 1 / 0 / 1 / 0, two trials each, so both arms share a host and an image.
- We look at TPOT, since this code change is exercised during decode. The first trial (warmup) is dropped, and we calculate mean TPOT. We see that differences are on the order of 0.01 ms.

| config                                                                           | knob=1   | knob=0   | delta  | accept len    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- | ------ | ------------- |
| plain TP2 `min_p=0.05` (the path the default policy makes deterministic), host A | 4.974 ms | 4.976 ms | -0.0 % |               |
| same, host B, order 0 / 1 / 0 / 1                                                | 5.058 ms | 5.062 ms | -0.1 % |               |
| plain TP1 `min_p=0.05`                                                           | 8.065 ms | 8.067 ms | -0.0 % |               |
| DFlash TP2 `top_p=0.9` (knob=1 forces the verify path deterministic too)         | 3.992 ms | 3.983 ms | +0.2 % | 4.563 / 4.564 |
| EAGLE3 TP2 `top_p=0.9`                                                           | 7.191 ms | 7.175 ms | +0.2 % | 1.929 / 1.930 |

Thus, we see that there is no measureable end-to-end cost, including the forced-deterministic verify path; the accept length is also unchanged.

The renorm kernel runs once per step over `batch_size` rows (sampler) or `batch_size x draft_tokens` rows (verify), so deterministic top-p adds ~0.03 ms at 32 rows and ~0.2 ms at 256 rows, which is small compared to a step of several ms.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/sampling_renorm.py` (new):
    - `renorm_deterministic(ranks_agree)` policy.
    - `top_p_renorm_prob` / `top_k_renorm_prob` for the sampler and `spec_top_p_renorm_prob` / `spec_top_k_renorm_prob` for verify, calling flashinfer with `is_deterministic=True` when appropriate (`sgl_kernel` as before otherwise).
    - The flag's presence is checked once at import (`inspect.signature`), so an older flashinfer degrades to the fast kernel rather than failing on the first sampled request.
    - Without flashinfer (MUSA, XPU) `sgl_kernel`'s own single-CTA kernel is already deterministic; no int32-sensitive code is added there.
- `layers/sampler.py`, `speculative/dflash_utils.py`, `speculative/eagle_utils.py` are the only renorm call sites, and now they import from the module above.
    - The `_sync_token_ids_across_tp` and `spec_tp_sync.py` comments name the renorm kernels as a known source of nondeterminism and point at the knob.
- `environ.py`: `SGLANG_RENORM_DETERMINISTIC` next to the other determinism knobs.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/sampling/test_renorm.py`: existing correctness tests run through the new module; regression tests call each deterministic renorm 30 times on a flat 256 x 128256 input and assert bit-identical output (the default kernels fail this 30 of 30); scoped runtime-context fixture.
- `test/registered/unit/sampling/test_renorm_policy.py` (CPU): single rank fast; TP=2 sampler deterministic and verify fast; `--enable-deterministic-inference` forces on; env overrides both ways.

The fix lives in `sglang` rather than the `sgl_kernel` wrappers, because `sglang-kernel` ships as a pinned prebuilt wheel. A wrapper change there is not testable in CI, and is not delivered until the next kernel release.

This fix is Complementary to #33614: the broadcast keeps replicated state safe against any future non-deterministic operator. This removes the one we found, so rank 0's own output and every other consumer of `target_probs` (logprobs, sampling masks) become reproducible too.

title: [LoRA] Support MoE in full and breakable prefill CUDA graphs
author: jybsuper
body:
## Motivation

Enable MoE LoRA in full and breakable prefill CUDA graphs, including batches above 32 requests.

## Modifications

- Separate prefill MoE LoRA scratch; preserve request slots and clear unused tails.
- Capture MoE LoRA hooks, including base-only batches.
- Compact Triton dense prefill LoRA grids.
- Size LoRA metadata from Breakable token/request capacity or Full's configured slots. Remove Triton's 32-request cap and avoid oversized CSGMV request metadata. Full defaults are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

B200, `8e8e2a4508`: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 TP2 (rank-16/32 adapters) and Inkling-NVFP4 TP8 (Gutenberg rank-32 adapter).

- **15 focused tests pass**, including 64 mixed adapter/base requests with Triton/CSGMV and breakable/full graphs. Check prompt and first-token scores against eager, plus replay without fallback.
- **Qwen TP2:** prompt logprobs and generated IDs match exactly before/after for both backends at B8/I4096 and B64/I128, including base resets and two repeats.
- **Inkling TP8:** original-scale generated IDs match at B1/I512, B8/I1024 and B64/I128. At B64/I128, prompt-logprob MAE is 0.0912 versus repeat 0.0886/0.0907; individual differences can exceed observed repeat variation.
- An **untimed 32×-alpha diagnostic at B64/I128** retains all 64 adapter slots and clean base resets. Eager-to-Full prompt-score MAE is **0.1135**, versus repeat **0.1138/0.1112**; generated IDs match. This tests retention, not trained-adapter quality or bit-exact FP4 scores.

All-files pre-commit passes, with test admission checked against the PR base (`30e7a3072d`).

## Speed Tests

### GB300 feature comparison: graphs versus eager

- **Qwen breakable graphs:** GB300 measured **+39.5–40.9%** with Triton LoRA and **+12.9–14.0%** with CSGMV versus pre-feature eager.

**Qwen TP2:** 4,096 input tokens/request, TRT-LLM MHA, legacy Triton MoE. Pre-feature `30e7a3072d` runs MoE LoRA eagerly; `6fd9e673b5` replays breakable graphs. Values are prefill ktok/s.

The PR also removes the 32-request Triton LoRA graph cap; Full defaults are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>B200 capacity comparison, including BS64</summary>

**B200 capacity comparison:** `8fcca750da` → `8e8e2a4508`, identical serving commands and inputs. Qwen uses TP2; Inkling uses TP8. title: [ROCm] GLM-5.2: gfx950 four-kernel fused DSA indexer decode path
author: JohnQin-llm
body:
## Motivation

GLM-5.2 runs the DSA indexer in 78 layers (plus the MTP draft layer) on every decode step. At low concurrency on MI355X its short launches are a measurable part of inter-token latency. This PR adds a gfx950 decode path that does the whole indexer in four HIP kernels.

It is on by default where it is supported: gfx950, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, aiter preshuffle, and GLM-5.2's indexer shape. `--no-enable-dsa-fused-indexer` turns it off.

## Modifications

Four kernels, header-only `.cuh`, JIT-built through `sglang.kernels.jit`:

| Kernel | What it does |
|---|---|
| `dual_gemv_bf16` | `q_lora @ wq_b.T` and `x @ [wk; weights_proj].T` in one launch |
| `qk_rope_hadamard_quant` | k LayerNorm, rope, 128-point Hadamard on q and k, fp8 quant of q, index-K cache write, head gate |
| `paged_mqa_logits` | fp8 paged MQA logits, plus the histogram the top-k needs |
| `topk_transform` | top-2048 and the page-table transform, split over 64 blocks per row using that histogram |

- `dsa_indexer.py`: a static gate in `Indexer.__init__` and a per-call gate. The fused path serves decode and target-verify with up to 48 rows (batch 8 × 6 draft tokens). Everything else (prefill, draft extend, CP, LoRA on the indexer weights, more than 48 rows) keeps the existing path.
- **Hadamard and #40710.** The fused kernels keep the Hadamard-rotated index-K cache that the ROCm path used before #40710. #40710's AITER fused FP8 writer skips the rotation, and prefill and decode must write the same cache format. So on layers where the fused path is enabled, this PR turns that writer off, the same way #40710 falls back when its rope cache is missing. Keeping the rotation is deliberate; see the long-context results below. If `Indexer._maybe_rotate` stops applying the Hadamard, the path turns itself off at startup.
- `dsa/utils.py`: runtime checks (aiter, preshuffle, kernel build). If they don't pass, the server logs why and uses the standard path; with `--enable-dsa-fused-indexer` passed explicitly, the log is a warning.
- `jit/utils/deps.py`: registers aiter as a JIT include dependency; kernel 2 uses its reduction helpers.

On CUDA and non-gfx950 ROCm the gate stops at the hardware check, so nothing is built there.

## Accuracy Tests

GLM-5.2-MXFP4, 8× MI355X, TP8, EAGLE MTP 5 steps / 6 draft tokens with real acceptance, fp8 KV cache, `--max-running-requests 8`. Passkey: one key hidden in a 64K-token prompt at 30 depths, greedy decode.

| | Index-K cache | GSM8K (1319, 5-shot) | Passkey 64K, repetitive filler | Passkey 64K, natural text |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| main | no Hadamard | 0.935 | 24/30 | 30/30 |
| This PR | Hadamard | 0.932 | 28/30 | 30/30 |

The difference is on the repetitive haystack; on natural text both find every key. Across all our runs, the repetitive haystack scores 114/120 with the Hadamard (four runs) and 60/90 without (three runs).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same setup, `--max-running-requests 1`, acceptance pinned with `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.61`. InferenceX AgentX trace replay, concurrency 1, 1200 s per arm, against main at 8ca82118e0. Two nodes ran the arms in opposite order; on each, the 105 to 108 requests present in every run are paired by (trace, turn), and the table is the mean of the two nodes.

| | main | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ITL p50 | 3.54 ms | 3.37 ms | −4.7% |
| ITL p90 | 3.81 ms | 3.56 ms | −6.7% |
| ITL p99 | 4.30 ms | 4.02 ms | −6.6% |
| ITL, paired median | | | −5.3% |
| Request latency, paired median | | | −5.9% |

Only decode is replaced. 

`bench_serving` against main at 8ca82118e0, with the server below but `--max-running-requests 8 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 8`. One node, two counterbalanced runs per arm, random prompts, 1024 output tokens, median TPOT:

| Concurrency, input | main | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1, 32K | 3.40 ms | 3.26 ms | −4.0% |
| 1, 100K | 3.49 ms | 3.33 ms | −4.6% |
| 4, 32K | 4.33 ms | 4.21 ms | −2.8% |

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

Server (base arm: add `--no-enable-dsa-fused-indexer`):

```
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.61 \
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected \
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path $MODEL --served-model-name $MODEL --trust-remote-code \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8888 \
  --tp 8 --ep-size 1 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \
  --chunked-prefill-size 32768 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --max-running-requests 1 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 1 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \
  --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion --enable-fused-qk-norm-rope \
  --enable-metrics
```

Client:

```
aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp \
  --url http://localhost:8888 --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --endpoint-type chat --streaming \
  --model $MODEL --tokenizer $MODEL --tokenizer-trust-remote-code \
  --concurrency 1 --benchmark-duration 1200 --random-seed 42 \
  --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126 \
  --num-dataset-entries 393 \
  --trajectory-start-min-ratio 0.25 --trajectory-start-max-ratio 0.75 \
  --warmup-requests-per-lane 10 --trace-idle-gap-cap-seconds 300 \
  --use-server-token-count \
  --output-artifact-dir $ARM/aiperf_artifacts
```

</details>

## Tests

- `test/registered/amd/test_dsa_gfx950_fused_indexer.py` (MI35x lane): `dual_gemv_bf16` against `torch.mm`, and `topk_transform` against the existing v2 paged transform at both page-table widths, including that its histogram is left zeroed.
- `test/registered/unit/dsa/test_dsa_gfx950_fused_workspace.py` (CPU): one workspace per device for all layers, no allocation during graph capture, and a too-narrow workspace falls back with a warning instead of reallocating.

## Changes since the last review

- Rebased onto main, which now has #40710. Without the writer change above, the server failed at startup on gfx950.
- Removed `SGLANG_DSA_HIP_FUSED_INDEXER_MAX_CTX`. It only capped the workspace width, and any cap below the decode page table turned the path off.
- Nothing in this path stops startup any more: an explicit `--enable-dsa-fused-indexer` on a runtime that cannot serve it, or a `_maybe_rotate` that no longer applies the Hadamard, logs a warning and uses the standard path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Flag help only; no docs page change.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Diffusion] Optimize Qwen-Image-Edit attention on Hopper
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Qwen-Image-Edit's Hopper profile contains repeated QK normalization/RoPE and joint-QKV concatenations in the DiT, plus 96 separate SDPA window calls per window-attention layer in the vision encoder. Reuse the existing Qwen QKV epilogue on Hopper and process packed vision windows through PyTorch's public varlen attention API.

On one H200 with main's PyTorch 2.13 dependencies, lossless eager engine E2E falls from **32.8171 s to 32.3141 s (1.533%)**. All saved before/after images are byte-identical within each quality mode. This is a modest combined full-model gain; the much larger microbenchmark ratios do not represent E2E speedups.

## Modifications

- Enable the existing BF16, batch-one, head-dimension-128 QKV epilogue for eligible unquantized SM90 Qwen attention. Support independent image/text token strides; retain mask, shard/padding, layout and alignment fallbacks and the existing environment opt-out.
- Vectorize adjacent RoPE-cache loads and paired V-head copies, and move Q/K/V dispatch into the grid's second dimension. Explicit `fmaf`/`fmul` preserves the original RoPE contraction and intermediate rounding. Odd head counts retain a smaller final copy.
- Use public `torch.nn.attention.varlen.varlen_attn` for eligible Hopper Flash SDPA inference with packed windows. No token reordering or padding. CPU/HIP/MPS, other SDPA subclasses, compilation, gradients, dropout, missing API, and unsupported inputs retain the existing path. The new SDPA dispatch is SM90-only; the shared QKV kernel also serves the existing SM100 path, whose B200 regression now passes CI (14 QKV epilogue tests).
- Update the kernel inventory's SM90 capability and extend the existing kernel, model-path and registry tests.

## Accuracy Tests

Rehashed **16 formal PNGs**: four A-B-B-A runs × two quality modes × two Torch versions. Within each mode, A/A, B/B and A/B are byte-identical, with SSIM 1 and maximum pixel error 0. Actual output resolution is 1024×1024.

The contact sheet shows baseline and candidate in columns, lossless and high in rows:

![Actual Qwen-Image-Edit before and after outputs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/comparison.png)

| Quality | Actual baseline PNG | Actual candidate PNG |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lossless | [Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/lossless-baseline.png) | [After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/lossless-candidate.png) |
| High | [Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/high-baseline.png) | [After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/high-candidate.png) |

**Use lossless for this recipe.** High already changes this input visibly: high versus lossless has SSIM **0.830311**, PSNR 17.3808 dB and maximum difference 255/255, identically for baseline and candidate. The high timing below documents compatibility with that existing mode; it is not a lossless-equivalent result or a new quality optimization.

[Torch 2.13 image comparisons](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/torch213-image-quality.json), [Torch 2.11 comparisons](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/torch211-image-quality.json), [all formal hashes, source checks and selected-GPU samples](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/artifact-gpu-audit.json).

- **35 H200 tests passed on each of Torch 2.11.0+cu130 and 2.13.0+cu130**. Coverage includes QKV exactness, separate and packed strides, odd head counts, misaligned cache/token-stride fallbacks, masked attention, packed SDPA BF16/FP16, causal/ragged/empty/single windows, strided V, and training/dropout/missing-API fallbacks.
- **28 CPU registry tests passed** at the final PR head. All nine changed files passed pre-commit and `git diff --check`.
- Production microbenchmarks check six QKV cases and fourteen SDPA cases exactly. The existing B200 CI lane passes all 14 QKV epilogue tests, including the production 8,152/1,365-token shape, odd heads, and mask/shard/alignment guards. A Hopper lane is added.

[Final checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/final-checks.json), [2.11 test log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/torch211-tests.log), [2.13 test log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/torch213-tests.log), [registry test log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/registry-tests.log).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Native `QwenImageEditPipeline`, `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit@ac7f9318f633fc4b5778c59367c8128225f1e3de`; one H200, BF16, 1024×1024, 50 steps, guidance 4, embedded guidance 6, seed 42, official Qwen Edit input, prompt `Make the cat wear a red hat.` Automatic residency in both arms, including the existing text/image encoder layerwise offload. Eager only, no torch.compile. Native BCG probes were disabled for both qualities, so no BCG fallback timings are counted.

A is main `482e9f257bb9d9ac57c2245c93768a96ec70edbe`. Lossless measurements and microbenchmarks use candidate `60def09d35c8912db76144e7ca6691dca554bc94`; final head `7df1e941ca7782d9a964a98a9720d4ddd1cd7fa4` adds only registry capability metadata, README and CPU tests. The four runtime files are byte-identical ([audit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/runtime-equivalence.json)). Primary high and paired profiles measured the actual final head. Runtime import paths and perf-dump commits were verified.

Each row uses fresh processes in A-B-B-A order on the same selected GPU. No rows were discarded. Primary environment: PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1, driver 595.71.05. It was installed in a private venv; the separate legacy 2.11 environment was unchanged.

| Primary Torch 2.13 eager | A1 / A2 engine E2E | B1 / B2 engine E2E | Mean A → B | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Lossless | 32.805944 / 32.828280 s | 32.300505 / 32.327791 s | 32.817112 → 32.314148 s | **1.533%** |
| High, existing quality tradeoff | 32.290089 / 32.280895 s | 31.610836 / 31.596315 s | 32.285492 → 31.603576 s | **2.112%** |

| Environment / quality | Mean denoising A → B | Denoising reduction | Mean engine E2E A → B | E2E reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Torch 2.13 lossless | 31.821445 → 31.486249 s | 1.053% | 32.817112 → 32.314148 s | 1.533% |
| Torch 2.13 high | 31.296227 → 30.783327 s | 1.639% | 32.285492 → 31.603576 s | 2.112% |
| Torch 2.11 lossless | 31.936158 → 31.592483 s | 1.076% | 32.930535 → 32.441389 s | 1.485% |
| Torch 2.11 high | 31.378467 → 30.879241 s | 1.591% | 32.385151 → 31.710122 s | 2.084% |

The legacy lossless result is below the campaign's 1.5% acceptance threshold; it is not rounded up or pooled with 2.13. Only one input/seed and two measurements per arm are reported, so this does not establish a universal 1.5% improvement across Qwen models or inputs.

Engine E2E is synchronized stage `total_duration_ms`, excluding model loading, request warmup and PNG saving. Profile-export wall times are excluded. In unprofiled primary lossless runs, image encoding is 792.848 → 632.484 ms and denoising saves 335.196 ms. Selected GPUs were idle at every cell entry. Ten-second samples, including two legacy NVML query timeouts, are preserved; they do not prove continuous host exclusivity.

[Primary lossless ABBA](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/torch213-lossless-abba.json), [primary high ABBA](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/torch213-high-abba.json), [legacy lossless ABBA](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/torch211-lossless-abba.json), [legacy high ABBA](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/torch211-high-abba.json).

### Kernel and profile evidence

The initial trace identified actual DiT shapes of 8,152 image tokens and 1,365/1,358 text tokens, 24 heads, head dimension 128. Vision attention has 5,400 tokens over 96 ragged windows, 16 heads, dimension 80. Measurements below are cumulative GPU kernel durations from separate tiny Torch 2.11 traces, excluding CPU launch gaps; they are not full request timings.

| Production operation | Baseline kernels / device time | Candidate kernels / device time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| QK norm + RoPE + joint QKV, 8,152 + 1,365 tokens | 7 / 179.617 µs | 1 / 109.023 µs |
| Packed vision SDPA, 5,400 tokens / 96 windows | 96 / 517.984 µs | 2 / 38.240 µs |

The two SDPA kernels are FlashAttention and an auxiliary zero-RNG fill; dropout is zero and no random numbers are consumed. Copy events are separate from kernel counts. QKV input restoration is outside the timed interval; the reference's packed-input materialization cost is conservatively excluded.

NCU localized 7,309,056 excess L2 sectors to four stride-two scalar RoPE-cache loads. Vector loads remove those sectors, but alone do not improve duration (121.248 → 121.760 µs). Paired V-head copies alone regress to 131.840 µs; hoisting dispatch/index work into `grid.y` reduces it to **112.544 µs**, with 63,691,368 executed instructions and 93.204% occupancy. Explicit FMA operations are necessary to retain bit-exact arithmetic. These are NCU diagnostics with clock/cache control disabled, not E2E measurements.

The final matched Torch 2.13 full-stage captures contain two denoising steps each. Overlapping image-encoding GPU annotations are unioned before counting each kernel once; no boundary-crossing kernels were found.

| Rank-0 stage, two-step request | A kernels → B kernels | A cumulative GPU time → B |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Denoising | 7,113 → 5,673 | 1,233.223 → 1,221.776 ms |
| Image encoding | 11,042 → 5,778 | 190.449 → 164.337 ms |

Other stage kernel counts are unchanged. The vision reduction is 56 window-attention invocations × (96 − 2) = 5,264 launches. These short instrumented requests establish the changed paths; the full 50-step unprofiled ABBA establishes E2E.

[QKV microbenchmark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/qkv-microbenchmark.json), [SDPA microbenchmark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/sdpa-microbenchmark.json), [NCU iterations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/ncu-comparison.json), [paired profile and trace hashes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/profile-comparison.json), [profile aggregation script](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/summarize_qwen_attention_profile.py).

### Reproduce

Run the same command on the stated baseline and candidate, in A-B-B-A order, with the same idle H200 and environment:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1 sglang generate \
  --backend sglang --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit \
  --revision ac7f9318f633fc4b5778c59367c8128225f1e3de \
  --num-gpus 1 --performance-mode auto --enable-torch-compile false \
  --quality lossless --warmup-mode request --width 1024 --height 1024 \
  --num-inference-steps 50 --guidance-scale 4 \
  --seed 42 --prompt 'Make the cat wear a red hat.' \
  --image-path https://github.com/lm-sys/lm-sys.github.io/releases/download/test/TI2I_Qwen_Image_Edit_Input.jpg \
  --save-output --output-path outputs/qwen-edit --perf-dump-path qwen-edit.perf.json
```

For high, change only `--quality high` in both arms and retain its quality caveat. Capture full stages in separate diagnostic requests with two inference steps, `--profile` and `--profile-all-stages`; exclude their wall times. Exact executed [QKV harness](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/bench_qwen_qkv_hopper_production.py) and [SDPA harness](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/bench_native_varlen_final.py) are included; their output directory and commit assertions record the original experiment.

Task-owned checkpoint caches on both H200 hosts were deleted after model validation: 57,722,203,391 and 57,722,164,005 logical bytes before cleanup, zero files/weights/bytes afterward. These are logical cache counts, not unique physical storage freed. [First ledger](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/ion9-cache-cleanup.jsonl), [second ledger](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/ion8-cache-cleanup.jsonl), [independent zero-residual check](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/cleanup-verification.json), [media manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/manifest.json).

title: [Attention] Size FlashInfer MLA indptr buffers to the padded max batch
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

Under MLP sync (DP attention, DeepEP, or `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`) the eager and cuda-graph runners pad the request count to the attn-tp alignment (`get_eager_max_batch_size` / `get_cuda_graph_max_batch_size`), so the warm-up dummy batch and the largest captured decode batch can be wider than `req_to_token_pool.size`.

`FlashInferMLAAttnBackend` sized `kv_indptr`, `qo_indptr` and `q_indptr_decode` to the raw pool size (and the cuda-graph buffers are clones of those), so the server died at startup:

```
File ".../flashinfer_mla_backend.py", line 889, in call_begin_forward
    kv_indptr[1 : bs + 1] = torch.cumsum(paged_kernel_lens, dim=0)
RuntimeError: The expanded size of the tensor (14) must match the existing size (16) at non-singleton dimension 0.  Target sizes: [14].  Tensor sizes: [16]
```

Hit with Kimi-K3 TP8 + `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe` on the flashinfer MLA backend (the mamba state cache capped `max_running_requests` to 14, attn_tp=8 padded the batch to 16). Any MLA model on the flashinfer backend with an MLP-sync feature and a request cap that is not a multiple of attn_tp reproduces it, e.g. `--tp 4 --enable-dp-attention --dp 2 --attention-backend flashinfer --max-running-requests 3` (per-rank pool 1, padded batch 2). The non-MLA `flashinfer_backend.py` already sizes these buffers with `get_cuda_graph_max_batch_size`; the MLA backend was the only one left on the raw pool size.

## Modifications

- `flashinfer_mla_backend.py`: size `kv_indptr` / `qo_indptr` / `q_indptr_decode` (and the multi-step draft backend's buffers) to `get_cuda_graph_max_batch_size(req_to_token_pool.size)`, matching the non-MLA flashinfer backend.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerics change; the buffers are only allocated larger. Generations were identical before and after the fix in a Kimi-K3 TP8 megamoe run on the flashinfer and trtllm_mla backends.

Manual reproduction with DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct, `--tp 4 --enable-dp-attention --dp 2 --attention-backend flashinfer --flashinfer-mla-disable-ragged --max-running-requests 3`:
- without the fix: startup crash, `The expanded size of the tensor (1) must match the existing size (2)`
- with the fix: server starts and serves requests at the request cap

(`--flashinfer-mla-disable-ragged` is there because the ragged prefill wrapper rejects the DP-padded q rows, `q.shape[0] (2) does not match qo_indptr[-1] (1)`, which is a separate pre-existing issue not addressed here.)

No new CI test: the combination needs 4 GPUs with DP attention to trigger, and the fix is a one-time alignment with the non-MLA backend rather than a path that is likely to regress.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable (startup-time buffer sizing only).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
