title: [unified-memory] Token-major dense views for the unified memory pool (3/7)
author: caihuali95
body:
> **This is one of seven PRs split out of #38592.** That PR was +2105/−1366 across 41
> files, twelve of them attention backends on the serving hot path, and it interleaved
> hardening, a layout change and dead-code deletion in a single diff — a reviewer could not
> tell which hunk was safe-by-construction and which changed behaviour. #38592 is retained as the token-major
> layout PR (3/7), which is the core of the series.
>
> **Stack** — each PR is based on the one above it, and every one is green on its own:
>
> | # | PR | what it does | size |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | 1 | #40326 | derive KV row addresses from strides, not shapes | 21 files, +733/−118 |
> | 2 | #40327 | build paged KV views through one helper | 13 files, +704/−47 |
> | 3 | #38592 | **token-major layout** | 36 files, +1215/−1108 |
> | 4 | #40328 | mark the write loc physical and check it at every write door | 45 files, +935/−132 |
> | 5 | #40329 | remove the kernel-page multiplier plumbing | 17 files, +117/−230 |
> | 6 | #40330 | stride the KV translate kernel and route every translate through it | 11 files, +361/−159 |
> | 7 | #40331 | name the fused KV translate for what it computes | 28 files, +119/−121 |
>
> Review order is the table order. 1 and 2 are no-ops on today's contiguous pools (2 also
> fixes how HND pools with more than one KV head are read); 3 is where the behaviour changes
> and deserves the most attention; 4 adds the physical write-loc check; 5 is deletion; 6
> consolidates the translate; 7 is naming only.

# 3/7 — token-major dense views: a kernel-facing id IS the physical id

Base: #40327 (2/7). 15 commits, 36 files, +1215/−1108.

**This is the core of the series and the PR that changes behaviour.** The other six are
hardening, adoption sweeps, deletion or consolidation around it. If you review one, review
this one — and specifically its `layout-switch` commit.

## Why the layout has to change

Before, one page held a uniform array of row-blocks, one per layer per side:

```
page bytes = [L0_K * ps | L0_V * ps | L1_K * ps | L1_V * ps | ...]
```

Every per-layer view was contiguous, and the block origin was folded into its storage
offset, so layer `l` had to be addressed by a re-numbered id
`(t // ps) * (ps * blocks_per_page) + t % ps`. Views ran past the last page envelope, which
is what `view_tail_pad_bytes` sized.

That scheme is only valid **when every block has the same row width.** The old builder said
so itself, and asserted it:

> The page envelope `[L0_K*ps | L0_V*ps | L1_K*ps | ...]` is a uniform array of
> `2*layer_num` row-blocks **when K and V rows are equally wide**, so it is a valid paged
> pool under `kernel_id(t) = (t // ps) * (ps * 2 * layer_num) + t % ps`

```python
assert head_dim == v_head_dim, (
    "build_mha_views requires uniform rows (head_dim == v_head_dim); "
    "Asymmetric-KV models cannot use the unified pool (screened out at startup).")
```

One multiplier, one row shape, one stride can only address a page that is a uniform array of
equal-width blocks. Heterogeneous row widths are not *hard* under that scheme — they are
**unrepresentable**.

Now one slot's ENTRY holds every part of that token at a fixed offset:

```
page bytes  = [ entry(slot 0) | entry(slot 1) | ... ]
entry bytes = [ K_0 | V_0 | K_1 | V_1 | ... ]
```

so the per-layer view is strided with the entry as its slot stride and is indexed by
`page * ps + slot` directly.

### What that buys

Each part now carries its own geometry — `DensePart` has its own `row_shape`,
`offset_bytes` and `layer_stride_bytes`; `MHASubPoolSpec.entry_bytes()` sums `k_row_bytes`
and `v_row_bytes` **separately**. No uniform-row assert survives. `DenseEntryLayout.validate()`
checks that every part stays inside the entry and that no two overlap, and it requires
alignment instead of equal widths: every row, part offset and layer stride is a multiple of
16 bytes (the store kernels' vector width) and the entry a multiple of 32. A model whose
per-rank K, V or latent row is not a multiple of 16 bytes is refused with a `ValueError`
naming the row when the unified pool is built.

1. **Asymmetric KV** — the *layout* no longer forbids it. Startup still refuses such models,
   because the backends' read and write paths are not audited for it; what this PR removes is
   the structural obstacle, not the screen.
2. **More parts per entry.** A part carries its own row width **and its own count**, so
   further per-token state — for example a draft model's K and V as extra lanes of the same
   entry — can be added as parts without a new builder. Under a uniform-block page that is
   not expressible at all. Nothing in this series adds such a part.

### Three more consequences

- **No re-numbering.** `kernel_page_multiplier` is pinned to 1 (asserted, not read from the
  spec), and `translate_kv_loc_for_kernel` now computes what `translate_kv_loc` does. The
  plumbing that carried the multiplier is dead as of this PR and is removed in **5/7** — it
  is left in place here so this PR stays the layout change and nothing else.
- **No tail pad.** The views end exactly at the last slot, so the raw buffer is allocated at
  `total_bytes`.
- `entry_bytes()` is rounded up to `ENTRY_ALIGN_BYTES` in the switch commit rather than in
  the layout types, because it feeds `page_bytes()`, buffer sizing, the sub-pool anchors,
  `move_kv_cache` envelopes and PD transfer — the alignment has to flip together with them.

## The commits, and where to spend review

| commit | what | review weight |
|---|---|---|
| `layout-types` | introduce `DensePart` / `DenseEntryLayout` / `build_dense_views` alongside the old builders. No caller changes. | low — additive |
| **`layout-switch`** | switch `unified_memory_pool.py` to them: `layout()`, `entry_bytes()` alignment, `view_rows = num_pages * ps`, raw sizing, the sub-pool multiplier pin, the hook message, and the byte-law tests. | **the whole behaviour change lives here** |
| `layout-cleanup` | delete the page-major builders, the per-page offset and tail-pad helpers, and the id-space probe that the new layout makes vacuous. | low — pure deletion |
| `refuse trtllm_mha decode cuda graphs` | a startup gate; see *trtllm_mha* below. | low |
| `keep main's test edits` | the rewritten tests keep `main`'s `est_time` values and docstrings and do not bring back tests `main` pruned; the free `*_entry_bytes` helpers go, and tests derive the entry in closed form. | low — tests |
| `drop the pass-through CPU-copy overrides` | see #39477 below. | low — deletion |
| `describe the token-major entry` | help text, docs and comments that still described the layer-major page. | low — text |
| `import the paged-view helpers …`, `tidy the token-major layout code`, `take a part name and a slot count …` | follow 2/7's module move; `build_dense_views(raw, layout=, part_name=, num_slots=)`; comments. | low |
| `name the entry-layout module token_major` | `mem_cache/layout/page_major.py` → `token_major.py`, `build_page_major_mamba_views` → `build_mamba_entry_views`, and the Mamba view test after the module. Pure rename; the `--enable-page-major-kv-layout` flag keeps its name. | low — mechanical |
| `tag HiCache storage keys …` | see *HiCache storage* below. | medium |
| `refuse misaligned per-rank rows …`, `state the backend requirement …`, `keep the addressing rule in docstrings …` | the `ValueError` above; help text and docs that still said the Triton backends are required; shorter docstrings. | low |

## Interaction with #39477 (PD page-envelope transfers)

That PR added `_physical_to_kernel_indices` to both unified pool classes, re-numbering
physical ids by `kernel_page_blocks`. Under the token-major entry that formula is the
identity, so the method is removed together with the `get_cpu_copy` / `load_cpu_copy`
overrides that called it: the parents' methods take physical ids directly. Verified numerically on **both** pool
classes at page sizes 1 and 4, including the round trip and that neighbouring slots are
untouched. #39477's own SWA tail-allocation tests (17 CUDA cases) pass under this series.

The one upstream test that asserted the *scaled* form
(`test_swa_transfer_page_is_physical_not_kernel_scaled`) is adapted here to assert both
paths are physical, since the multiplier it pins is what this PR removes.

## Tests

The view tests are rewritten against the new byte law `byte(t, l, K) = t * entry + l * (k + v)`,
each cross-checked against an **independent (page, slot) description** of the same bytes at
page sizes 1 and 4, for uniform and asymmetric K/V rows. That independent description is the
safety net for the whole PR: the flat builder's addressing is verified against a second
derivation rather than against itself. `test_byte_addresses_match_envelope_formula` pins the
same law in closed form, independent of the builder.

## Validation

Model families exercised — a hybrid of every pool shape the unified pool supports, plus a
non-hybrid control. Perf covers the gated-deltanet hybrid (Qwen3.5-9B), the MLA hybrid
(Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B), the sliding-window hybrid (gpt-oss-20b), the tri-pool hybrid
(Inkling and Inkling-Small), and dense Llama-3.1-8B as a control. Accuracy covers the same
set and additionally the Mamba hybrid, Falcon-H1-7B. Each model is run unified against a
baseline on the same model, backend and configuration, so every delta isolates the pool.

Median inter-token latency, unified vs baseline: **+0.91%** (measured run-to-run noise floor
for this metric: 1.9%). Median GSM8K delta at n=200: **−0.25 pt** (binomial delta-sigma ≈ 3.0 pt).

Re-validated on the previous base (0318a8d0af) after review feedback: the stack tip (7/7) gives **+0.95%** median inter-token latency over 40 paired configurations (median per-configuration shift against the previous run of the same 40: +0.12 pp) and **−0.25 pt** median GSM8K over 26, with the full unit scope green.

The accuracy median excludes trtllm_mha with decode cuda graphs, which is refused at startup
for the reason given below; including it the median is −0.50 pt.

## End-to-end on B200

From this commit on, every allowlisted kernel reads per-layer views whose slot stride is a
whole entry. Besides the 2/7 kernel parity tests, each admitted SM100 backend was run with
unified memory against a baseline on the same model, flags and box (GSM8K 5-shot, n=200):

| model | backend | unified | baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B, tp1, cuda graphs off | trtllm_mha | 0.915 | 0.915 |
| gpt-oss-20b, tp1 | fa4 | 0.545–0.555 | 0.550–0.560 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, tp2 | trtllm_mla | 0.900 | 0.900 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, tp2 | cutedsl_mla | 0.900 | 0.910 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, tp2, fp8 KV | tokenspeed_mla | 0.900 | 0.900 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, tp2, dcp2, fp8 KV | tokenspeed_mla | 0.910 | 0.910 |

trtllm_mha with decode cuda graphs is refused at startup under unified memory (below);
without graphs it decodes 9–13% slower than baseline, from the translate launches an eager
step adds. Not covered: fa4 on the gated-deltanet hybrids (fa4 cannot run head_dim 256 with a
paged cache on SM100, with or without this PR) and trtllm_mha at tp > 1.

## trtllm_mha decode cuda graphs are refused under unified memory

A defect that predates this series makes trtllm_mha decode under cuda graphs read
untranslated page-table columns: under the unified pool, the page table is refilled out of
graph before each replay, bounded by `cache_seqlens_int32`, which only the in-graph metadata
kernel writes — so the refill uses the previous replay's lengths. Measured: GSM8K
0.000/0.020 with graphs on against 0.900/0.900 with them off, baseline 0.905/0.900 in both.

Before this PR that configuration could not boot (its prefill path OOM'd copying a whole
sub-pool). This PR makes it bootable, so it also refuses it: `--enable-unified-memory` with
trtllm_mha as the decode backend and decode cuda graphs on fails at startup, pointing at
`--disable-cuda-graph` or another decode backend. trtllm_mha as the prefill backend only
still boots. The gate goes once the refill derives its lengths from the batch.

## HiCache storage

The unified host pool persists whole page envelopes. Their size does not change with this
PR, but their byte order does (layer-major → token-major), and storage keys recorded only the
model and ranks. Host pools now declare a `storage_format_tag`; `UnifiedPageEnvelopeHostPool`
sets one, and the controller appends it to the model name every storage backend keys pages
on. Pages written by an older build, or by a static pool, therefore miss instead of being
read back in the wrong layout. The page hash is unchanged, since it has to match the
router's.

title: Fix KV-canary workspace accounting after graph capture
author: cctry
body:
## Motivation

Eager KV-canary forwards allocate plans after post-capture KV sizing has assigned the available memory to the KV pool. On large pools, this unaccounted workspace can approach a gigabyte and cause an otherwise memory-tight configuration to OOM.

## Modifications

Compute the workspace from the installed `VerifyPlan`, `WritePlan`, `ExpectedInputs`, and `PlanInput` capacities, and subtract it in addition to the existing headroom. Target and draft forwards execute sequentially, so reserve their largest workspace. Canary-disabled configurations retain exactly the same byte budget.

Canary capacities remain fixed across post-capture resizing. The reserve uses those actual capacities, including the three verify entries per pool slot.

Add regression coverage for allocation byte counts, pool-slot scaling, additive headroom, canary-disabled budgets, and draft-runner forwarding.

## Accuracy Tests

- Sizing, headroom, startup, and capacity tests: **82 passed, 50 subtests passed**.
- Canary unit and kernel tests on GB300: **390 passed, 23 subtests passed**.
- Canary mock tests: **9 passed**; E2E helper tests: **2 passed**.
- Final startup-forwarding test rerun: **22 passed, 18 subtests passed**.
- `python -m pytest -q test/registered/mem_cache/test_post_capture_kv_sizing.py`: **3 passed** in 178.97 s, including the GSM8K accuracy check. Post-capture sizing backed a 230.25 GiB KV pool.
- `SGLANG_ENABLE_POST_CAPTURE_KV_SIZING=1 python -m pytest -q test/registered/kv_canary/test_self_e2e_baseline.py::TestBaselineMha`: **1 passed** in 193.80 s.
- `pre-commit run`: passed.

Server tests used a separate environment with the upstream PyTorch 2.13 and kernel dependencies. No multi-GPU, SWA, speculative, or disaggregated serving validation was run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput benchmark or profiling run.

title: [BCG][DSV4-Flash][CP] Support DeepSeek V4 prefill with interleave CP and breakable CUDA graphs
author: BJWang-ant
body: ## Summary Enable DeepSeek V4 prefill with interleave context parallelism (CP) and breakable CUDA graphs (BCG). Previously, CP metadata and buffer layouts were not compatible with DSV4 graph capture and replay. - Add support for interleave CP with the DSV4 attention backend under the existing PP=1 and attention CP size=TP size constraints. - Keep per-rank replay buffers and graph write capacities stable while preserving actual request lengths for attention metadata. - Gather DSV4 hidden states and DSpark auxiliary outputs, restore global token order, and trim padding before logits processing. - Fall back to eager execution when a batch does not activate CP. Also fix large CP prefill batches entering the sparse prefill path through the query-count heuristic, despite its environment switch being disabled. That path builds global query offsets against CP-local buffers, which can cause out-of-bounds writes. Route active CP batches through paged attention and validate sparse metadata buffer capacity before launching kernels. ## Validation - Passed 8 isolated CPU regression checks covering configuration eligibility, capture buckets, replay buffer stability, output gathering, metadata lengths, and sparse prefill routing and bounds checks. - Passed Python syntax and diff whitespace checks. - Observed successful GPU graph capture and small-request replay before the final sparse prefill routing fix. Full GPU end-to-end validation of the final patch is pending. title: [Kimi-K3] Accept fp32 routing weights in the fused MoE finalize
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

The trtllm-gen deferred finalize returns its routing weights at the dtype the caller passed in, so K3's unpacked `(topk_ids, topk_weights)` routing yields fp32 weights where the packed form yielded bf16. The fused finalize kernel matched bf16 only and a 72-token decode batch killed the server during CUDA-graph capture. #38588 stopped that by casting to bf16 at the call site. This PR makes the kernel take either dtype instead, and reverts the cast.

`finalize_vec` is templated on the routing-weight dtype, the kernel's `kFinalize` bool becomes `typename FinWeight = void`, and the host dispatches on `expert_weights.dtype()` at the `TensorMatcher` that already validates the tensor.

| | #38588 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Weight precision | bf16, rounded before the kernel | fp32 as the router emits it |
| Per call | +2.3 to +11 us | no measurable change |
| Added work per MoE layer | cast launch + alloc before the collective | none |

Per call on 8x B300, best of 3 interleaved repeats of 200 iterations:

| bs | This PR | #38588 | Delta | Spread |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 9.35 us | 18.29 us | -8.94 us | 2.6 / 3.0 |
| 8 | 10.13 us | 19.60 us | -9.48 us | 3.4 / 1.7 |
| 32 | 11.41 us | 22.57 us | -11.15 us | 2.8 / 1.0 |
| 72 | 16.31 us | 18.88 us | -2.57 us | 1.6 / 2.0 |
| 128 | 21.95 us | 24.20 us | -2.25 us | 1.7 / 1.7 |

The routing row is 64 B/token at fp32 against ~114 KB/token of gemm2 gathers, so the wider load is free. The cast's cost is the launch and allocation ahead of the collective, which also skews rank arrival at the push barrier.

Both dtypes are live in production: the packed path caps at 64 tokens (`moe_route_quant_fused.covered`) while the push finalize fits 73, so batches of 65 to 73 defer with fp32 weights.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_ar_fusion.py` (8x B300) | 63 passed, `finalize_push_norm` parametrized over both dtypes |
| Same test on the old kernel | 5 fp32 cases fail with the reported dtype error |
| Kimi-K3 B300 Balanced e2e | bs=72 capture clean, GSM8K 0.98 against a 0.95 gate |

title: [MiniMax-M3] Instantiate the decode block top-k in register buckets
author: thanhhao98
body:
## Motivation

The single-stage radix block top-k is gated on `max_seqblock <= 4096` on CUDA, matching the `kIters` register array in `TopKTrait::forward`. `max_seqblock` is derived from the decode graph's capture-time bound, which is the configured context length — not the live sequence. So `--context-length 1048576` yields 8192 blocks and drops to the two-stage Triton top-k even when the running sequence is a few dozen blocks.

MiniMax-M3's default context is 1M, so this is the default configuration. #36560 lifted the cap to 16384 on ROCm, where the kernel is a histogram select; CUDA still stops at 4096.

## Modifications

Raising the CUDA cap alone is not free: all three size branches share one `__global__` kernel, so a larger `kIters` raises register pressure for every launch, including the short rows that take the cheap branches.

Instead, the CUDA radix path is instantiated per register bucket: `forward` and both kernels take the bucket as a template argument, and the launchers dispatch on `max_seqblock` over `{4096, 8192, 16384}`. Launches with `max_seqblock <= 4096` (context ≤ 512K at block size 128) still instantiate `kIters == 8`, so their codegen is unchanged. The bucket follows `max_seqblock`, not a row's live length, so at the default 1M context every launch, short rows included, runs the 8192 bucket (`kIters == 16`) instead of the 16384 one. `kMaxNumBlocks` becomes the 16384 cap on both platforms (on CUDA `32 * kCTASize`, the existing `static_assert` bound), and the Python gates that mirror it follow — except on XPU, where the op is sgl-kernel-xpu's own kernel and still stops at 4096. ROCm launches are unchanged.

## Accuracy

GSM8K 1319 q, both arms on the same node: **main 0.857 vs this PR 0.869**, parity within sampling noise (1σ of the difference ≈ 0.013). The 200 q gate, a bs=1 canary and a generation-termination check pass on every arm benchmarked below.

`test_minimax_decode_topk.py` gains cases on both sides of each bucket boundary (4096 / 4097 / 8192 / 8193 / 16384 blocks) asserting the selected-score multiset and the ascending-output contract, and a rejection check one block past the cap (16385 blocks) that asserts both the Python wrapper's assert and the JIT launcher's `RuntimeCheck`. The 2097152-token case of `test_decode_topk_distinct`, ROCm-only since #36560, now runs on CUDA too. `test_minimax_decode_topk_page_table.py`'s flattened DP test now reaches the page-table kernel's 8192 and 16384 buckets too (600000 and 1048577 tokens); its 38 cases pass on GB300.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

MiniMax-M3-NVFP4, one 4-GPU GB300 node, TP4, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, `--context-length 1048576`, `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260929-79cafec0`. Every arm, main included, runs `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill=disabled` and carries the same two small Dynamo-safety patches (the `is_musa()` probe and the deprecated parallel-getter warning), neither of which touches top-k: on this nightly MiniMax-M3 cannot compile its prefill CUDA graph, independently of this PR.

Top-k path per decode step, cc=1, nsys, device 0:

| | kernel | µs/step |
|---|---|---|
| before | `_topk_index_partial_kernel` + `_topk_index_merge_kernel` | 359 |
| after | `minimax_decode_topk_block_kernel` | **129** |

End-to-end with **this PR alone** against main. Each pair ran back to back on one node, on three nodes, in both orders. Median TPOT (ms), mean over the pairs; the tok/s/user row is the mean of the per-pair gains (TPOT_main / TPOT_PR − 1), so it can differ by 0.1 pt from a ratio of the rounded means:

| cc | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 | 128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 4.88 | 5.54 | 6.30 | 7.60 | 9.87 | 13.74 | 19.76 | 30.09 |
| this PR | **4.61** | **5.20** | **5.90** | **7.16** | **9.46** | **13.24** | **19.16** | **29.59** |
| tok/s/user | +6.0 % | +6.4 % | +6.8 % | +6.1 % | +4.3 % | +3.8 % | +3.1 % | +1.7 % |

**+6.0 % to +6.8 % tok/s/user at cc 1–8.** Every pair is positive at every concurrency; the smallest single-pair gain is +0.6 % (cc=128).

title: docker(xpu): unblock nightly build (setvars.sh + sgl-kernel rename)
author: arathi-hlab
body:
## Summary
Unblock the `Release Docker Images Nightly (Intel XPU)` build. The nightly hits two independent failures in the same pipeline; this PR fixes both.

## 1. `torch_memory_saver` step exits 3 with no visible error
Failing run: [34225492633 step #14](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34225492633/job/102058474661) — layer added by #29935 (2026-09-08).

Offending RUN in `docker/xpu.Dockerfile`:

```dockerfile
RUN . /opt/intel/oneapi/setvars.sh --force >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
    TMS_PLATFORM=xpu pip install --no-cache-dir --no-build-isolation \
    git+https://github.com/fzyzcjy/torch_memory_saver.git@${TORCH_MEMORY_SAVER_REF}
```

- `>/dev/null 2>&1` silences setvars.sh, so which component env script failed never made it into CI.
- `&&` short-circuits: setvars.sh sources many per-component `vars.sh` scripts and returns the last non-zero it hit. An optional component (debugger, MPI, …) can exit non-zero while the compiler / SYCL vars torch_memory_saver actually needs are still exported. When that happens, pip never runs.

Fix — rewrite the RUN to:
1. Keep setvars.sh's stderr so future failures are diagnosable.
2. Log-and-continue on setvars.sh non-zero instead of gating pip on it.
3. Keep pip's failure fatal via `set -e`.

If SYCL really isn't set up, pip will now fail with the actual missing-toolchain error instead of an unexplained exit 3.

## 2. `sgl-kernel` dependency name drifted from the source package
`sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#462` renamed the Python package to `sglang-kernel-xpu` (2026-09-09). pip enforces name consistency between a URL requirement's left-hand identity and the metadata built from the source, so the existing line in `python/pyproject_xpu.toml`:

```
sgl-kernel @ git+https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu.git
```

now trips:

```
WARNING: Generating metadata for package sgl-kernel produced metadata for project name sglang-kernel-xpu.
Discarding git+https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu.git: … expected 'sgl-kernel', but metadata has 'sglang-kernel-xpu'
```

pip then falls back to the unrelated CUDA `sgl-kernel` on PyPI and the resolver bails with `No matching distribution found for sgl-kernel (unavailable)`.

Fix — one-line rename of the requirement identity to match the source package name. (Analogous CUDA path in `python/pyproject.toml` already tracks this rename; only the XPU line was missed.)

## Test plan
- [ ] Retrigger `Release Docker Images Nightly (Intel XPU)` on this branch → build reaches `Push intel/sglang-dev` and succeeds.
- [ ] `pip install -e .` against `pyproject_xpu.toml` on a Python 3.12 XPU env resolves cleanly (no `Discarding git+…` warning, `sglang-kernel-xpu` builds and installs).
- [ ] If the docker build still fails, the CI log now shows the real setvars.sh error (or the real pip build error), which we couldn't previously see.

title: [diffusion] ci: don't fail the nightly when a perf dump is unreadable
author: mickqian
body:
## Problem

The diffusion nightly has been red since 2026-09-05 on `Server did not write performance data to ...`, and the case it hits moves around:

| run | failing cases |
|---|---|
| [09-05](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33970864867) | `ltx2.3_twostage_ti2v_2gpus` (repeat 2), `wan22_i2v_a14b_720p` (repeat 2) |
| [09-07](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34131440112) | `ltx2.3_twostage_ti2v_2gpus` (repeat 1), `wan22_t2v_a14b_720p` (repeat 2) |

Only the heavy video cases are ever affected. In **both** runs the server had already logged `Metrics dumped to <the exact path the client then reported missing>` about ten seconds before the client gave up:

```
15:30:35.839  [server] Metrics dumped to: .../perf_wan22_t2v_a14b_720p_measured_2.json
15:30:45.998  ERROR: Server did not write performance data to .../perf_wan22_t2v_a14b_720p_measured_2.json
```

The paths match byte for byte, `dump_benchmark_report` writes synchronously before it logs, and client and server share a filesystem (no container in this job), so I could not reproduce the race from the logs. **This PR does not claim to fix that race.**

## What it does change

**The reaction is disproportionate.** The measurement is the client-side latency, already recorded by the time the dump is read; the server dump is supplementary stage telemetry, and `generate_diffusion_dashboard.py` already renders rows whose `server_latency_s` is absent. Failing the case — and with it the whole nightly — because the extra telemetry could not be read conflates the two. An unreadable dump is now counted in `missing_perf_dumps` on the result and reported, and the case keeps its latency.

**The message covered three different faults,** which is why the logs cannot settle the cause: the file never appeared, it never parsed, or it parsed without `total_duration_ms`. Those are now distinguished, and the warning lists what the directory actually holds, so the next occurrence is diagnosable:

```
WARNING: no server perf dump after 30s — parsed but has no total_duration_ms (keys: [...]).
  /path/comparison-logs holds: ['perf_..._measured.json', ...]
```

Poll timeout goes 10s → 30s, since 10 was arbitrary and every failure landed exactly on it.

## Testing

Exercised all four paths of `_read_perf_dump` directly: a good dump returns; a missing file, a dump without `total_duration_ms`, and an unparseable dump each return `None` with their own reason and a directory listing. pre-commit clean.

title: [Diffusion] Fuse the Wan VAE conv bias epilogue and tile the RMSNorm+SiLU kernel
author: Dayuxiaoshui
body:
<!-- PR body draft for branch `wav` (commit 0e2a6f4df). Local working note, do not commit this file. -->

## Motivation

Follow-up to #38020 and #38182. Two costs in the Wan 2.1 VAE decoder that kernel-level profiles hide, found by grouping a `quality=high` decode at the aten-op level (`key_averages(group_by_input_shape=True)`):

1. **The conv bias is a separate, unvectorised kernel.** PyTorch's cuDNN path runs `cudnn_convolution` and then `output.add_(bias.view(1, C, 1, 1, 1))`. On channels_last outputs aten does not vectorise that broadcast add: 1.5 TB/s on H200 for `[1, 96, 4, 480, 832]` bf16. It shows up only as `aten::conv3d` minus `aten::cudnn_convolution`: 797 launches, 278 ms of a 2847 ms lossless decode and 227 ms of a 1876 ms high decode on a shared GPU (~10% in both modes).
2. **`wan_rmsnorm_silu` ran one pixel per program** with 4 warps over 96-384 channels: 0.63 TB/s on the largest shape, 16% of the high-quality decode.

## Modifications

**New kernel, lossless (bit-exact, unconditional)**

- `kernels/ops/diffusion/modulate/conv_bias_epilogue_triton.py`: `x.dtype(float(x) + float(bias))`, the exact arithmetic of aten's `add_` (fp32 opmath, one rounding), optionally fused with the residual add as `x.dtype(x.dtype(x + bias) + h)`, i.e. the two roundings of the eager `conv(x) + h` chain. 4.1 TB/s. `bias` may be fp32 on a half-precision `x` (autocast): it is cast to `x.dtype` first, which is what autocast does before the conv call. The output is `empty_like(x)`, so it keeps the dense channels_last(_3d) strides like the in-place `add_`. Predicate requires `C > 1` with canonical strides and never raises; the kernel validates and raises `ValueError`.
- `WanCausalConv3d._conv_with_epilogue`: runs the conv without bias and applies it through the kernel; falls back to the exact aten ops (`out.add_(bias.to(out.dtype).view(...))`).
- `residual_block_forward`: conv2's bias and the block's residual add become one pass (`residual=h`); conv1's bias is deferred into norm2 (`skip_bias=True` + `WanRMS_norm.forward(x, conv_bias=...)`, where the eager norm adds it first with the same arithmetic).

**Quality-gated**

- `wan_rmsnorm_silu` tiles `[ROWS, C]` consecutive pixels per program (32 rows at `C <= 128` down to 4 at `C = 1024`): 0.63 -> ~3 TB/s at `C = 96`. The 2D reduction tree moves ~2e-6 of the elements by one bf16 ulp relative to the previous kernel, while both differ from eager on ~20% of elements, so the gated contract is unchanged. Optional `conv_bias=` folds the deferred conv1 bias into the same pass, applied exactly like aten's `add_` before the statistics.
- `FusedWanRMSNormSiLU.forward(x, conv_bias=None)`: folded under the gate, otherwise applied by the bit-exact epilogue kernel before the eager chain.

**Tests / docs**

- New `test_conv_bias_epilogue.py`: aten oracle (`x.clone().add_(bias)`, `+ h`) for bf16/fp16/fp32 x fp32/half bias, 4D and 5D, stride identity; `F.conv3d` with bias vs conv-without-bias + epilogue; predicate rejections (NCDHW, wrong bias width/dtype, residual layout/dtype, empty, `C == 1`, `requires_grad`).
- `test_norm.py`: ragged multi-row tiles at the three tile configurations; `conv_bias` fold equals the kernel on the pre-biased tensor bit for bit.
- `test_model_fast_paths.py`: a three-chunk tiny `WanDecoder3d` decode through the feature cache, fused path vs pure aten (`torch.equal`); deferred bias through the gated wrapper with the gate off (exact) and on (bounded relative error).
- README selection matrix and `existing-fast-paths.md` updated.

## Accuracy Tests

1x H200, Wan 2.1 VAE weights (`Wan-AI/Wan2.1-I2V-14B-480P-Diffusers`), 81 frames 480x832.

**Lossless**

- Standalone decode, bf16 weights: `torch.equal` vs `main`: True.
- Standalone decode, fp32 weights + bf16 autocast (the Wan T2V pipeline setting): `torch.equal` vs `main`: True.
- End-to-end `sglang generate`, TurboWan2.1-T2V-1.3B, 4 steps, seed 1, 6 prompts: all 6 mp4s **md5-identical** to `main` (and to the outputs of the two previous PRs).
- Peak decode memory unchanged.

**Quality path**

Standalone high vs `main` lossless on the same latent: PSNR 58.4 dB (bf16), 59.1 dB (fp32 + autocast), unchanged from before this PR; the multi-row norm kernel differs from the previous gated kernel on ~2e-6 of elements by one bf16 ulp.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Standalone VAE decode**, torch.profiler GPU kernel self time, idle H200:

| weights / autocast | path | before | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 | lossless | 1324 ms / 7850 kernels | 1253 ms / 7599 |
| bf16 | high | 1112 ms / 4006 | 935 ms / 3420 |
| fp32 + bf16 autocast | lossless | 1593 ms | 1530 ms |
| fp32 + bf16 autocast | high | 1215 ms | 1056 ms |

Per-kernel (bf16, high): `_wan_rmsnorm_silu_kernel` 177 -> 57 ms over 609 launches; the 797 aten bias `add_` launches are replaced by 396 `_conv_bias_epilogue_kernel` launches totalling 22 ms (649 launches / 35 ms on the lossless path). Qwen-Image 1024x1024 high: 43.3 -> 39.4 ms (shared norm kernel), lossless unchanged and still bit-exact.

**End-to-end**, TurboWan2.1-T2V-1.3B, 4 steps, 81f 480x832, `main` from a `git worktree` of the base commit, 6 prompts, median of the 5 warm requests. The decode stage is ~60% of a warm request. This box is shared; runs whose `DmdDenoisingStage` (identical code on both sides) drifted were discarded, and the cleanest interleaved pair is reported:

| stage | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `DecodingStage`, high | 932 ms | 785 ms (-15.8%) |
| `DecodingStage`, lossless | 1535 ms | 1501 ms (-2.2%) |
| `DmdDenoisingStage` | ~890 ms | ~890 ms |

Micro-benchmarks behind the design (idle H200, bf16 `[1, 96, 4, 480, 832]`): aten bias `add_` 0.409 ms (1.5 TB/s), Triton bias add 0.150 ms (4.1 TB/s), aten `add_` + residual `add` 0.621 ms vs fused 0.215 ms; norm 0.970 ms -> 0.201 ms.

title: [Fix] observability: Correct speculative FPM timing and decode lengths
author: tedzhouhk
body:
## Summary

Fix speculative-decoding FPM timing ownership and decode-length statistics. Each result retains its own timing span and immutable count/sum/variance instead of combining overlapped iterations or reading a missing/stale CPU length mirror. Attention-DP ranks with no local requests retain their timed dummy-forward records. Idle heartbeats now follow scheduler state, so a long forward cannot look idle merely because the publisher queue is quiet.

## Implementation

DeviceTimer exposes generic interval observers. FPM timing, schemas and publication live in `forward_pass_metrics.py`; all corresponding test cases and fixtures live in `test_forward_pass_metrics.py`, with one CPU CI registration. The DeviceTimer dependency is imported only for type checking. FPM groups existing intervals by run_batch result, preserves the same-stream check, and carries timing through rank-local PP metadata, including PREBUILT recursion, skipped output communication and the speculative-output relay. PP metadata retains both the upstream forward-time microbatch/KV snapshot and rank-local FPM timing. At _resolve_spec_v2_tokens entry, after existing result-copy synchronization and before settlement, supported EAGLE/EAGLE3/DSPARK paths freeze req.seqlen - 1 statistics on the result. Queued statistics remain a per-rank scheduler-queue snapshot and stay immutable during deferred publication.

Remove unused start/end-event fields and the unreachable monotonic fallback, inline the extra timing context manager with exception-safe sealing, remove duplicate emission-time polling, and skip per-interval elapsed-time calculations when there are no reporters. Algorithm selection is a module-level constant; shared test fixtures replace duplicate fake intervals. Full PP round-trip and skip-output regression coverage remains.

## Overhead

Production adds no CUDA events, GPU kernels, D2H transfers or explicit synchronization. FPM-off keeps the original forward method and skips decode-statistics reduction. FPM-on performs CPU bookkeeping, stream checks, statistics reduction and asynchronous publication. wall_time is the first-start/last-end span of existing instrumented intervals on one stream, including segment gaps; work outside those boundaries is excluded. The FPM v1 wire schema is unchanged. These structural checks do not quantify CPU overhead; the earlier AgentX comparisons remain in the performance-evidence comment.

## Validation

- 98 CPU tests across eight focused files passed at head `8d8616abd2778ab2c9341fbc55d664ced38449d9`, including FPM timing/publication, speculative grammar/bookkeeping, auxiliary output, PP rank offsets/DSpark relay, PP communication overlap and scheduler metrics. CPU tests stub optional compiled operators. Changed-file pre-commit and git diff --check passed. The timing regression now uses real interval completion caching and confirms active-state sampling does not consume or duplicate FPM callbacks. title: Relax GSM8K thresholds for the GLM-5.2 DSA-MTP variants
author: alisonshao
body:
`test_dsa_glm52_nvfp4_dp_mtp.py` fails gsm8k about twice a week with scores of 0.926–0.934 against a 0.935 threshold — 13 of its 19 recorded failures since July are this one assert, spread across every B200 host and unrelated commits.

Nothing is regressing. The 0.935 default was calibrated on DeepSeek-V3.2, which scores 0.960, and has been inherited unchanged through two model swaps. On GLM-5.2 NVFP4 it lands 1.3σ below the mean.

Measured from CI job logs, 08-30 → 09-09:

| test | n | mean | sd | min | headroom at 0.935 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `test_dsa_glm52_dp_mtp` (FP8) | 95 | 0.9495 | 0.0058 | 0.930 | 2.5σ |
| `test_dsa_glm52_tp_mtp` (FP8) | 90 | 0.9492 | 0.0058 | 0.932 | 2.4σ |
| `test_dsa_glm52_nvfp4_dp_mtp` | 61 | 0.9439 | 0.0069 | 0.928 | 1.3σ |
| `test_dsa_glm52_nvfp4_tp_mtp` | 55 | 0.9477 | 0.0066 | 0.934 | 1.9σ |

All four minima are already below 0.935.

The distribution has not drifted since the NVFP4 tests were added on 07-03 — it has been landing under 0.935 since its first full week:

| week | n | mean | min | attempts <0.935 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 07-06 (first full week) | 13 | 0.9462 | 0.930 | 2 |
| 07-13 | 14 | 0.9459 | 0.940 | 0 |
| 07-20 | 14 | 0.9461 | 0.932 | 1 |
| 07-27 | 13 | 0.9477 | 0.940 | 0 |
| 08-03 | 13 | 0.9443 | 0.930 | 2 |
| 08-17 | 8 | 0.9472 | 0.940 | 0 |

First week (n=18) mean 0.9457 / sd 0.0087 vs recent (n=61) mean 0.9439 / sd 0.0069; Welch t=0.79, variance ratio F=1.62, neither significant. The threshold never had adequate headroom rather than losing it.

Currently 9.0% of eval attempts (6/67 over the last 10 days) land under 0.935; the `retry()` wrapper rescues most of them, which is why this surfaces as an occasional red job rather than a constant failure.

Fix: shared default 0.935 → 0.925, which gives the FP8 pair 4.2σ, plus 0.92 overrides on the two NVFP4 variants for 3.5σ and 4.2σ. Every value sits below all ~300 observed scores and still catches a real break — the one genuine accuracy failure on this fixture scored 0.046.

title: [Quant] ModelOpt mixed precision: dispatch block-FP8 MoE experts and derive the block size
author: zhendonghua
body:
## Motivation

`ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig` dispatches both `FP8_PB_WO` and `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES` for Linear layers, but only `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES` for FusedMoE, and it hard-codes the block-FP8 block size to `[128, 128]` in two field-identical sub-configs.

`nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` labels its MTP experts (`mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts`) `FP8_PB_WO` (`group_size` 128) in the inline `config.json` and `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES` in `hf_quant_config.json`. Today the file copy wins only because the inline copy carries no KV-cache key and is discarded as incomplete (`weight_utils.py`). If the inline copy became authoritative, the FusedMoE branch would fall through to `return None`, FusedMoE would install the unquantized method, and the fp8 expert weights would be cast to bf16 with `weight_scale_inv` silently dropped — no error.

Mirrors vllm-project/vllm#55513 (`_BLOCK_FP8_MOE_ALGOS`, block size from `group_size`, conflicting sizes rejected).

## Modifications

- `_BLOCK_FP8_ALGOS = ("FP8_PB_WO", "FP8_BLOCK_SCALES")`; the Linear and FusedMoE branches both dispatch on it to the single block-FP8 sub-config `fp8_block_config`. The field-identical `fp8_pb_wo_config` that sat next to it is removed (constructor parameter, attribute, construction, kwarg).
- That sub-config's `weight_block_size` is derived from the checkpoint's block-FP8 `group_size` (default 128) instead of being hard-coded; a MIXED_PRECISION map whose block-FP8 layers disagree on it raises.

## Test

- `test_modelopt_loader.py::TestModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig`: both names dispatch to `Fp8MoEMethod` with `[128, 128]`; block size follows `group_size`; conflicting sizes raise. The full file passes (36 tests) and the repo's pinned pre-commit hooks (isort / ruff / ruff-format / codespell) pass on the changed files.

## Validation (Modal, 4x B300 SXM6 AC, `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` = v0.5.20 cu130, whose pins equal `main`; this branch `pip install -e --no-deps` on top)

Checkpoint `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` @ `fc694b54`. Serve flags = the cookbook datacenter cell plus `--mamba-ssm-dtype float32 --linear-attn-decode-backend triton --page-size 64 --context-length 262144`, no `--quantization` (resolved to `modelopt_mixed` from `config.json`; MoE runner auto-pinned to `flashinfer_trtllm`). Evals via `sgl-eval` 0.1.2.

**Sampling per the model card** (`temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=20, max_tokens=131072, reasoning_effort=xhigh`):

| Config | Bench | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `--tp 4`, no EP, no MTP | AIME26, 30 x 16 | **pass@1 98.54** (sem 0.43), majority@16 100, pass@16 100, **0/480 truncated**, 0 server errors |
| `--tp 4`, no EP, no MTP | GSM8K, 1319 x 1 | **97.80**, stop_rate 1.0, **0 truncated**, 356 s eval wall, 0 server errors |

**MTP path exercised by this PR** (`--tp 4`, no EP, `NEXTN` steps 3 / topk 1 / draft tokens 4, greedy):

- Starts **without EP**; draft `Qwen4ExpForCausalLMMTP` loads with `quant=modelopt_mixed` and its block-FP8 experts on `Fp8MoEMethod` (scale grid `[5, 20]` for `[640, 2560]` weights).
- Accept length **2.99** on GSM8K at 64-way concurrency (max 4.0), ~3.5 on AIME26 reasoning — a mis-scaled draft shows ~1.6.
- GSM8K greedy 97.35 with MTP vs 97.65 without (4 / 1319 questions, batch-numerics noise at `temperature=0`). GSM8K wall time 204 s vs 273 s.
- 8 generations ran to the 262k context ceiling with speculation on; no IMA / CUDA error.

Note for reviewers running greedy evals: at `temperature=0`, the `--tp 4` no-EP configuration produces early repetition loops on one AIME26 problem (5/120 and 8/120 truncated in two runs). It reproduces without MTP, does not occur at `--tp 1`, and vanishes under the recommended sampling above — a greedy-decoding artifact of that TP layout, independent of this change.

title: Add out-of-tree DFlash extension points
author: yuhanchan
body:
## Motivation

  Out-of-tree platforms currently cannot use DFlash without patching SGLang
  internals. DFlash support, draft attention backend selection, speculative KV-
  cache location assignment, and graph-capture behavior are hard-coded for
  built-in platforms.

  ## Modifications

  - Add conservative DFlash capability APIs to `SRTPlatform`.
  - Allow out-of-tree platforms to provide speculative KV-cache locations.
  - Allow custom draft attention backends and platform-specific fallback
  backends.
  - Respect `support_cuda_graph()` when initializing the DFlash draft worker.
  - Add unit coverage for capability defaults, backend validation and fallback,
  and cache-location dispatch.

  Existing behavior for built-in platforms remains unchanged.

  ## Accuracy Tests

  This changes platform integration and dispatch rather than model computation.

  Added focused unit tests covering:

  - Conservative defaults for platforms without DFlash support.
  - Acceptance of an out-of-tree draft attention backend.
  - Fallback to the platform’s default attention backend.
  - Actionable errors when no default backend is implemented.
  - Cache-location dispatch following the active platform.

  Local runtime tests were not run because the checkout does not currently have
  `torch` or `pytest` installed. Python syntax validation passed.

  ## Speed Tests and Profiling

  Not run. No model kernels or numerical operations are changed. Built-in
  platforms retain their existing implementations; the new dispatch path is
  used only by out-of-tree platforms.

title: [AMD] Quantize the bf16 MTP draft experts online to MXFP4 for Qwen3.5
author: zijiecode
body:
## Motivation

`amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4` (Quark) leaves the whole MTP stack in bf16: its `exclude` list has 1547 `mtp.*` entries, including the 512 routed experts of the draft layer. The NVFP4 checkpoint used on the NVIDIA side does the same (`mtp.layers.0*` excluded). With EAGLE/MTP decoding on MI355X this means:

- the draft model loads 7.9 GB per rank at TP2 (6.4 GB of bf16 experts), memory the KV pool could use;
- every draft step and the draft-extend step run the draft MoE through the bf16 ck 2-stage path (E=513, top-11, `QuantType.No`), ~610 us per step at bs ~20 versus ~150-200 us for the MXFP4 a4w4 kernels the target model uses. Three draft steps plus draft extend per decode cycle make this the largest single item of the draft chain at medium and high batch sizes.

SGLang already has the online-requantization plumbing (`--speculative-draft-model-quantization quark_mxfp4`, `REQUANTIZATION_METHODS`, `QuarkConfig(online_scheme="quark_mxfp4")`), but for a draft whose checkpoint carries a Quark config the explicit CLI request was overridden by the "use the draft model's detected quantization" branch, so the flag was silently a no-op for exactly this case.

## Modifications

- `configs/model_config.py`: the draft-model branch that falls back to the checkpoint's detected quantization no longer applies when the draft quantization was given explicitly, is one of `REQUANTIZATION_METHODS`, the build is HIP and the draft is the Qwen3.5 MoE MTP draft (`is_qwen3_5_mtp_draft`, next to the other model predicates: `architectures[0] == "Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP"`, which `_config_draft_model` sets before quantization is resolved, and `model_type == "qwen3_5_moe"`). Everything else keeps the previous behaviour.
- `model_loader/weight_utils.py`: `_quark_draft_online_quant_config()` — for that same combination, when the checkpoint's Quark config lists `mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts*` under `exclude`, return `QuarkConfig(online_scheme="quark_mxfp4")` for the draft so its routed experts are quantized online to MXFP4 at load time. Only the draft model is affected; the target model keeps its serialized Quark scheme. The attention projections, shared expert and lm_head of the draft stay bf16 (the online scheme's own exclusion list for `qwen3_5_moe`).
- No change for other models, for CUDA, or when the flag is not passed.

Usage (added to the InferenceX MI355X recipe in the A/B below): `--speculative-draft-model-quantization quark_mxfp4`.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K (`few_shot_gsm8k`, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, temperature 0, max new tokens 2048, TP2, real EAGLE decoding, aiter backend, page 16, fp8 KV), draft experts online MXFP4:

| | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---:|---:|
| baseline | 0.921 | 8/1319 (0.006) |
| this PR | 0.926 | 5/1319 (0.004) |

GPQA diamond (198 questions, 8 repeats). Accept length = mean over every decode step of the run (server log):

| | Mean score | Unparsable | EAGLE accept length (mean / p50) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline, draft experts bf16 | 0.879 | 0.25% | 3.30 / 3.30 |
| this PR, draft experts online MXFP4 | 0.876 | 0.06% | 3.29 / 3.28 |

Per-run standard error of the score is about 0.008 (sample std 0.32), so the two are within noise; the accept length, the only thing the draft's precision can move, is unchanged. Draft model memory at TP4: 2.45 GB per rank.

Speculative decoding leaves the output distribution to the target model's verification; the draft only proposes, so its precision can only move the accept length, which is unchanged here and in the serving runs below (3.39 vs 3.39 at TP2 c32).

## Benchmarking and Profiling

InferenceX agentic recipe with aiperf replay of the public `cc-traces-weka-062126-256k` traces (fast harness, 1200 s window), MI355X TP2 c32 with HiCache DRAM offload, same tree with and without the flag, runs back to back on the same GPUs (n10):

| TP2 c32 HiCache | main | this PR | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT p50 (ms) | 16.29 | 14.62 | -10.3% |
| TPOT p90 (ms) | 35.2 | 28.8 | -18% |
| interactivity p50 (tok/s/user) | 61.4 | 68.4 | +11.4% |
| total throughput / GPU | 40.5k | 46.0k | +13.6% |





## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit guide.
- [ ] Add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation (mention the flag for Quark checkpoints with bf16 MTP experts).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [AMD][CI] Publish ROCm 10 release images and kernel wheel
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #38659, which made ROCm 10 the default flavor for AMD PR and nightly tests. The release side was left behind: the two release workflows called out there still produce 7.x artifacts only.

- `release-docker-amd.yml` builds `rocm700`, `rocm720` and `rocm724` on a version tag, so `lmsysorg/sglang` has no `v<version>-rocm10-mi30x` / `-mi35x` tag even though `release-docker-amd-rocm10.yml` publishes the same images nightly to `rocm/sgl-dev` and `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm`.
- `release-whl-kernel.yml` builds `sglang-kernel` wheels for ROCm 7.0 and 7.2 only, so the flavor AMD CI now gates on has no published wheel and no `rocm1000` wheel index.

## Modifications

**`release-docker-amd.yml`** — add `rocm10` to the release matrix and to the manual flavor selector, mapping it to the `gfx942-rocm1000` / `gfx950-rocm1000` Dockerfile stages and the `rocm10-mi30x` / `rocm10-mi35x` tags the nightly images already use. gfx1250 (mi45x) is deliberately left out: it is bring-up only, which is why the nightly keeps it in its own job.

**`release-whl-kernel.yml`** — add a `1000` leg to the ROCm build matrix, a `rocm1000` option to the dispatch target selector, and a `release-rocm1000` job that publishes the wheel and updates the `rocm1000` index (`scripts/update_kernel_whl_index.py --rocm 1000`, no change needed there). A dispatch that names one ROCm flavor now builds and publishes only that flavor: each leg is an image build on the shared AMD node, and each release job appends its wheel to the index again, so pulling all three along was both expensive and a source of duplicate index lines. A push still runs the full set.

**`3rdparty/amd/wheel/sgl-kernel/build_rocm.sh`** — teach it ROCm 10, building against `rocm/pytorch:rocm10.0_ubuntu24.04_py3.12_pytorch_release_2.11.0`. That image matches the Ubuntu 24.04 / Python 3.12 / torch 2.11 stack the released ROCm 10 images carry and is built with `AMDGPU_FAMILY=device-all`, so a single wheel still covers gfx942 and gfx950. ROCm 10 ships as pip packages that unpack into site-packages, so the container has no `/opt/rocm` tree for `CMakeLists_rocm.txt` to find hip-lang under and, being a runtime image, no devel tree to compile against; the new setup block applies the same fixups `docker/rocm.Dockerfile`'s `rocm1000-base` stage makes for the images.

**`3rdparty/amd/wheel/sgl-kernel/rename_wheels_rocm.sh`** — accept the ROCm version for the wheel's local version tag from the caller, since the pip-installed SDK leaves no `/opt/rocm-<version>` directory to read it from. The 7.x flavors pass nothing and keep the existing probe.

## Compatibility

- Existing flavors are untouched. The generated in-container build script for `700` and `720` is byte-identical to today's apart from one blank line and a trailing space, and `rename_wheels_rocm.sh` falls back to the same `/opt/rocm-*` probe when no version is passed.
- Workflow names, job IDs, and the tag scheme for existing images are unchanged. `rocm700` / `rocm720` / `rocm724` still publish on every version tag.

## Validation

**ROCm 10 kernel wheel — dispatched and green.** [Run #34422339330](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34422339330) on this branch with `target: rocm1000`. Only the `1000` leg was created, confirming the new flavor scoping, and both `build-rocm-matrix (3.10, 1000)` and `release-rocm1000` passed. The build log confirms each piece of the ROCm 10 path:

- `rocm-sdk-devel==10.0.0` installed, so the runtime image did need the devel tree added.
- CMake resolved hip-lang through the `/opt/rocm` symlink: `Found HIP: /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel`.
- `Using AMDGPU_TARGET from environment: gfx942;gfx950` / `Multi-arch build: Enabling both HIP_FP8_TYPE_FNUZ (gfx942) and HIP_FP8_TYPE_E4M3 (gfx950)`, so one wheel covers both archs despite the Python 3.12 container.
- Renamed to `sglang_kernel-0.4.6.post1+rocm1000-cp310-abi3-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl`.

The artifact is live: it is attached to the `v0.4.6.post1` release in `sgl-project/whl` next to the `+rocm700` and `+rocm720` wheels, `rocm1000/sglang-kernel/index.html` on `gh-pages` has the matching entry, and the wheel contains the built `sgl_kernel/common_ops.abi3.so`.

**ROCm 10 release image — dispatched and green.** [Run #34422374614](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34422374614) on this branch with `rocm_version: rocm10`, `version: 0.5.19`. The flavor selector expanded to exactly `publish (rocm10, gfx942, all)` and `publish (rocm10, gfx950, all)` and both passed, publishing `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19-rocm10-mi30x` and `-mi35x` (new tags, colliding with nothing). Inspecting the published image configs confirms the flavor-to-stage mapping: the mi30x image carries `GPU_ARCH=gfx942-rocm1000` and the mi35x image `GPU_ARCH=gfx950-rocm1000`, both with `ROCM_HOME` under `site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel` as the ROCm 10 stack expects.

**Local:** captured the in-container script `build_rocm.sh` generates for `700`, `720` and `1000`, syntax-checked each, and diffed the `700` / `720` output against the pre-change script to confirm ROCm 10 support does not alter them. `pre-commit run --files` over the changed files passes.

## Follow-ups

`3rdparty/amd/wheel/sglang/pyproject.toml` carries `rocm700` and `rocm720` extras that pin a published `sglang-kernel` wheel URL. Now that a `+rocm1000` wheel exists, a `rocm1000` extra can be added in a follow-up.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — release workflow change; model outputs are unaffected.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: [AMD][CI] Retire the ROCm 7.0 kernel wheel
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## Motivation

#38763 added a ROCm 10 kernel wheel, making the ROCm wheel matrix `["700", "720", "1000"]`. `rocm700` is now the only leg with no CI behind it, and it is the last ROCm 7.0 artifact SGLang still publishes on every kernel version bump.

Scope note: this PR was originally a broader ROCm 7.0 retirement (workflows, nightly image build, release image matrix). #38632 supersedes all of that with a better end state — it consolidates the AMD workflows back onto a single `pr-test-amd.yml` / `nightly-test-amd.yml` pair and retires ROCm 7.0 CI as a consequence. Rather than conflict with it on the same four workflow files, this PR is now reduced to the one ROCm 7.0 surface #38632 does not touch: the kernel wheel.

## Modifications

Retire the ROCm 7.0 kernel wheel end-to-end:

- `.github/workflows/release-whl-kernel.yml`: drop the `rocm700` dispatch option, the `rocm700` clause in the `build-rocm-matrix` guard, the `"700"` matrix entry, and the `release-rocm700` job (which published the artifact and ran `update_kernel_whl_index.py --rocm 700`). The ROCm wheel matrix becomes `["720", "1000"]`.
- `3rdparty/amd/wheel/sgl-kernel/build_rocm.sh`: drop the `700` build image (`lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.8.post1-rocm700-mi35x`) and its pinned `rocm-rel-7.0.2` torch/triton/torchaudio/torchvision install branch. `720` and `1000` are unchanged, and an explicit `700` argument now fails with a clear message.
- `3rdparty/amd/wheel/sglang/pyproject.toml`: remove the `rocm700` optional-dependency extra (which pinned `sglang_kernel-0.4.0+rocm700`) and the stale install comment. `rocm720` is unchanged.
- `3rdparty/amd/wheel/README.md`: remove the ROCm 7.0.0 `pip install "amd-sglang[all-hip,rocm700]"` recipe and the ROCm 7.0.0 Triton upgrade note, and correct the extras description. Also fixes the section heading typo `Revolving triton` → `Resolving triton`.

`#38763`'s ROCm 10 wheel path is untouched.

## What this does not touch

The remaining ROCm 7.0 references are deliberately out of scope:

- The ROCm 7.0 workflows, nightly image build, and `release-docker-amd.yml` matrix leg — all handled by #38632.
- `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_start_container*.sh` still default to `ROCM_VERSION=rocm700`. This cannot change independently: all 58 container-launch sites in the current `pr-test-amd.yml` / `nightly-test-amd.yml` omit `--rocm-version` and rely on that default, so flipping it to `rocm10` before those workflows are deleted would silently repoint the ROCm 7.0 runs at ROCm 10 images. It belongs with #38632 or a follow-up.
- `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` retains the unsuffixed `gfx942` / `gfx950` ROCm 7.0 stages for local builds.
- `SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A` is misleadingly named but gates a workaround current ROCm 7.2 images still set.
- Cookbook pages pin historical `rocm700` image tags for reproducibility.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — release-artifact configuration only; no runtime or kernel code changed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. Removes one wheel build leg on the shared `amd-docker-scale` node plus its release job from every kernel version bump.

## Verification

- No `rocm700`, ROCm 7.0 dependency URL, `"700"` build input, or `--rocm 700` remains in `release-whl-kernel.yml` or `3rdparty/amd/wheel/`.
- `release-whl-kernel.yml` parses as YAML; the surviving legs are `rocm720` / `rocm1000` in the dispatch menu, the `["720", "1000"]` matrix, and the `release-rocm720` / `release-rocm1000` jobs.
- `build_rocm.sh` passes `bash -n`; `720` and `1000` still resolve their images, and `700` exits 1 with `Only '720' and '1000' are supported.`
- `pyproject.toml` parses with `tomllib`; the only remaining `rocm*` extra is `rocm720`.
- `python3 scripts/lint/check_workflow_job_names.py` passes.

title: Fix: post-load staging regression breaks offload meta/sharded_gpu modes
author: Hide-on-bushsh
body: ## Motivation The offloader (V2, `--offload-group-size`) intentionally parks offloaded parameters on the meta device through weight post-processing: - `--offload-mode=meta`: all offloaded params become meta at build time (weight loading is a no-op via a replaced `weight_loader`). - `--offload-mode=sharded_gpu` / `shm_cpu`: non-rank-0 DP ranks park params on meta during loading (rank 0 owns the real data). This is by design: device kernels skip meta params (e.g. `npu_format_cast` has an explicit meta skip), and the old `device_loading_context` passed meta tensors through untouched. Since #35180, `process_weights_after_loading` hits the new upfront check and the scheduler dies during startup: RuntimeError: Cannot post-process meta tensor FusedMoE.w13_weight The bug is device-agnostic (same code path on CUDA/NPU); it was caught by the NPU offload CI suites (`test_npu_offload_modes.py`, `test_npu_offload_group_size.py`). ## Modifications In `stage_module_for_post_load()`, record tensors that are already meta at context entry and pass them through untouched — no staging, no restore — restoring the pre-#35180 behavior for offloader-parked params. The original guard is preserved: tensors that *become* meta during post-load processing still raise, so genuine kernel bugs keep failing fast. for test_npu_offload_modes.py before after ## Accuracy Tests ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. title: [Bug] Guard FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE against 0-token inputs
author: Betelgeu
body:
TBO + DP attention can produce empty child batches. CUTLASS fused MoE asserts a non-null input_activations pointer, and PyTorch 0-row tensors have data_ptr()==0, which crashes flashinfer_mxfp4.

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Fixes #38773.

FlashInfer CUTLASS flashinfer_mxfp4 asserts on 0-token MoE batches because empty PyTorch tensors have data_ptr() == 0. DP attention + TBO hits this on idle ranks / bs=1 decode (child_a or idle hidden states are [0, H]). TBO is especially important on communication-bound GPUs such as L20N; this crash currently blocks enabling it together with flashinfer_mxfp4.

## Modifications

In `_fused_experts_flashinfer_mxfp4_cutlass`, return `StandardCombineInput(hidden_states=x)` when `x.shape[0] == 0`, before pad / CUTLASS. Same identity early-return as `moe_runner/aiter.py` and `moe_runner/humming.py`.

title: [PP][DeepSeek V4] Overlap communication and optimize SM120 prefill
author: jmydurant
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4-Flash prefill on 4-way pipeline parallelism showed two avoidable sources of serialization on RTX 6000D (SM120): pipeline tensor communication ran through scheduler-stream synchronization, and the SM120 model path did extra work for attention output projection and SWA KV page repacking.

This PR overlaps PP tensor communication with compute and adds guarded SM120 fast paths for DeepSeek-V4. The new paths are disabled by default, or require an explicit SM120 opt-in, so unsupported configurations keep the existing behavior.

## Modifications

- Add a dedicated PP CUDA communication stream (`SGLANG_PP_COMM_OVERLAP`). Sends wait on the producer event on the communication stream instead of fencing the scheduler stream.
- Add vLLM-style lazy PP activation receive (`SGLANG_PP_VLLM_ASYNC_RECV`): metadata remains synchronous, tensor payloads use `irecv`, and `PPProxyTensors` waits only on first consumption. Proxy traffic uses a separate process group to preserve message ordering. This path is currently limited to `attn_tp_size == 1`.
- Allow explicit FP8 `wo_a` on SM120 when the installed DeepGEMM exposes compatible `fp8_einsum` and UE8M0 scale-layout APIs.
- Add `SGLANG_OPT_SM120_DIRECT_SWA_KV`: retain 256-token logical allocator pages while storing SWA KV directly as 64-token physical pages consumed by the FlashInfer SM120 kernel, eliminating the per-layer 256-to-64 repack.
- Add CPU unit coverage for lazy wait-once behavior, sliced proxy access, and deferred payload receive.

## Accuracy Tests

Full 5-shot MMLU (`cais/mmlu`, all 57 subjects), with 4 x RTX 6000D, TP=1, PP=4, layer partition `10,11,11,11`, chunk size 16384, `temperature=0`, `max_new_tokens=1`, and parallelism 16:

| Configuration | Successful requests | Correct | Exact accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| All four optimization switches enabled | 14,042 / 14,042 | 12,307 | 87.6442% |
| All four optimization switches disabled | 14,042 / 14,042 | 12,315 | 87.7012% |
| Delta | - | -8 | **-0.0570 pp** |

Both runs completed without request errors, traceback, OOM, illegal memory access, or NCCL fatal errors. Of 14,042 answers, 302 changed correctness state in the A/B comparison: 147 moved from incorrect to correct and 155 moved from correct to incorrect. The nearly symmetric movement and 0.057 percentage-point aggregate delta show no material accuracy regression.

Additional validation:

```text
python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/distributed/test_pp_async_recv.py
3 passed, 1 warning in 4.44s
```

The warning is the environment's pre-existing unknown pytest `asyncio_mode` configuration warning.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Common setup: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, 4 x RTX 6000D, TP=1, PP=4 (`10,11,11,11`), 320 prompts, concurrency 32, ISL=8192, OSL=1, radix cache disabled, FP8 KV cache, FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE, and `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1`. Each formal configuration was measured three times after warmup. Metric is input token throughput.

PP communication strict A/B with an 8192-token chunk budget:

| Configuration | Mean input tok/s | Delta vs origin |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Unmodified SGLang (`4d5d50648`) | 22,948.41 | baseline |
| Patched build, PP features disabled | 22,966.15 | +0.077% |
| Dedicated PP communication stream | 23,222.64 | **+1.195%** |
| Communication stream + lazy async receive | 23,222.85 | **+1.196%** |

The gain comes from the dedicated communication stream; lazy receive is correctness-preserving but neutral for this workload.

SM120 model-path A/B with a 16384-token chunk budget (three-run median):

| Configuration | Median input tok/s | Incremental | Cumulative |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PP overlap + lazy receive | 23,682.37 | baseline | baseline |
| + FP8 `wo_a` | 24,508.21 | **+3.49%** | **+3.49%** |
| + direct 64-token SWA KV layout | 25,116.06 | **+2.48%** | **+6.05%** |

Nsight Systems inspection was also used to verify PP stream overlap and to attribute the model-path gains. Experiments that did not improve performance (DeepGEMM routed MoE, output shortcut, and eager attention multistream) are not included in this PR.

title: [NPU][Hicache] Optimize HiCache L2 IO with Memfabric acc_offload
author: jamesjxliu
body: ## Motivation On Ascend NPU, the existing HiCache L2 (host DRAM) IO path uses `transfer_kv_dim_exchange` with default host memory allocation. This works functionally but has two issues: 1. **Host memory not AIV-de-referencable**: The default `torch.pin_memory` host buffers are only reachable by the SDMA engine; the fused AIV sparse-copy kernel (`offload.kv_exchange_copy`) from the Memfabric `acc_offload` library can only de-reference host VAs that were mapped into the device VA space via the Memfabric offload entity. 2. **Stream synchronization on H2D upload**: A pageable `.to(device)` on NPU completes with `aclrtStreamSynchronize` that drains everything queued on the current stream, serializing the layer-group pipeline and stalling compute. This PR adds the Memfabric-mapped host DRAM allocation and the AscendC sparse-copy IO path, gated behind a single environment variable `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_MEM_BACKEND=memfabric`. **Depends on #L3PR** (Ascend MemCache L3 storage backend). ## Modifications - **`pool_host/common.py`** (+154): Add Memfabric host memory allocator (`alloc_with_memfabric`), lazy initialization (`ensure_memfabric_capacity`), single-switch detection (`memfabric_host_memory_enabled`, `ascendc_io_enabled`), and sync-free H2D upload helpers (`to_device_no_sync`, `track_pinned_staging`) using pinned memory + `torch.npu.Event`. - **`pool_host/mla.py`** (+266): In `MLATokenToKVPoolHost`, add Memfabric host pool allocation path (sizes the GB-aligned reserve from `--hicache-size`/`--hicache-ratio`), add `_transfer_ascendc_sparse_copy` method that launches the fused `offload.kv_exchange_copy` kernel (builds compact per-component metadata array, converts host pointers to DVAs, uploads indices without stream sync), and wire it into H2D/D2H paths when `ascendc_io_enabled()`. - **`managers/cache_controller.py`** (+17): In `submit_device_to_host`, when `ascendc_io_enabled()`, keep token indices on device and upload via `to_device_no_sync` instead of `.cpu()` sync. - **`hardware_backend/npu/utils.py`** (+7): Extend `set_default_server_args` to also handle `disaggregation_decode_enable_offload_kvcache` config resolution. Single switch: `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_MEM_BACKEND=memfabric` enables both the Memfabric host pool allocation and the AIV sparse-copy IO path simultaneously. ## Accuracy Tests No impact on model outputs — this PR only affects the HiCache L2 IO transfer path (D2H backup and H2D load). The KV data content is identical; only the transfer mechanism changes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling before: after: ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. title: [kernel] DSA top-k v2: long-context cluster rework, and NaN padding for the lanes outside a row
author: DarkSharpness
body:
## What

Brings the DSA top-k v2 rework of sgl-project/sglang#38640 onto `dsv4.1` (its six commits, unchanged) and fixes how the reworked kernels treat the lanes outside a row, which broke selection on rows with more `-inf` than finite scores.

## Why

The rework represents every lane outside a row with a sentinel score: the register path pads the last vector's tail with `-FLT_MAX` and counts it in the histogram, the ragged kernel masks the <= 3 aligned-prefix columns before a window in place with `-FLT_MAX`, and inactive tie entries are `-FLT_MAX` too. A valid score may itself be `-inf` (masked positions), and every one of these sentinels outranks it. On a 51-wide paged row with 3 finite scores and k = 16 the rework returned `[0, 1, 2, 51, -2 x 12]`: index 51 is the padding lane past the row, and 12 slots stay unwritten because `-FLT_MAX` inactive entries displaced the valid `-inf` ties. Ragged windows likewise selected prefix columns of the previous request.

## Fix (last commit)

A NaN score is not a valid input, so NaN is free to mean "drop":

- The lanes outside a row and the inactive tie entries become NaN. The collect pass rejects them for free (both `>=` tests fail), so they are never emitted nor tie candidates; the tie phase needs no index bookkeeping.
- The histogram's fp16 conversion canonicalises NaN to +NaN, the highest key, so after the histogram pass one thread moves the padding count from the top bin to bin 0 (two shared-memory atomics). Bin 0 is the negative-NaN key space that no real value reaches, so it can never become the threshold bin, and `coarse_bin_lower_bound(0)` is already `-inf`.
- The ragged kernel passes the prefix width (`input_start`, warp-uniform) for that count. The per-element loops of every path are unchanged.

`TopKProblem.input_start` and a NaN `TieValue::invalid()` are the only interface changes; the paged instantiations see `input_start = 0`.

## Tests

- `test_topk_v2.py`: **283 passed** on GB300, including five new regression cases (paged rows with more `-inf` than finite scores at 48 and 96 ties; ragged windows at every nonzero alignment residue). The ragged-window test no longer asserts an untouched score buffer: the prefix columns are written, as in the rework.
- A sweep of 852 cases: rows with 50 / 90 / 99 / 99.9 / 100 % `-inf` scores over the register2 / register4 / streaming / cluster paths, both kernels, k 512 / 2048, tie counts from 20 (warp branches) to thousands (radix path), three unaligned ragged starts. Every index in-window and unique, `-1` padding exact, selected-value multiset equal to torch's. 0 failures. The same sweep on the rework alone fails 75 cases; on the branch head's kernels the five regression cases pass but the rework's speed is missing.

## Performance (GB300, `bench_topk.py` inputs, `jit_v2`, us)

Against the branch head (`85f8105f5`), which carries the pre-rework kernels:

| paged, page 64, k 512 | bs 1 | bs 8 | bs 32 |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 3.77 -> 3.54 | 3.89 -> 3.67 | 3.99 -> 3.77 |
| 16384 | 6.18 -> 5.63 | 6.39 -> 5.86 | 6.59 -> 6.08 |
| 65536 | 9.67 -> 7.37 | 9.88 -> 8.25 | 16.22 -> 12.14 |
| 131072 | 11.18 -> 8.25 | 11.35 -> 9.81 | 24.09 -> 14.31 |
| 262144 | 14.01 -> 9.75 | 14.20 -> 12.65 | 31.02 -> 18.16 |

| ragged, k 2048 | bs 8 | bs 128 |
|---:|---|---|
| 4096 | 4.16 -> 3.85 | 4.55 -> 4.26 |
| 16384 | 8.29 -> 7.25 | 8.70 -> 8.00 |
| 65536 | 20.88 -> 19.97 | 21.93 -> 21.04 |
| 131072 | 34.46 -> 33.01 | 36.62 -> 35.20 |

Against the six rework commits alone (same base, without the last commit), the last commit is neutral within +-0.5% on every row of both tables; the per-element loops are byte-for-byte the rework's.

title: [JIT] Port the expert-pack MXFP4 kernels to load_jit and fix their launch limits
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

`expert_pack_mxfp4` was built with `torch.utils.cpp_extension.load`, whose `FileBaton` waits on a lock **file** and only releases it in a `finally`. A build killed mid-flight leaves the file behind, and every later run against that cache spins on it forever with no output — a 7s test can burn a full CI timeout, and the cache outlives the job. Ported to `load_jit`, which uses `fcntl.flock` (released by the kernel when the holder dies), then fixed three latent bugs the rewritten validation now owns.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Build lock | stale lock file wedges every later run, silently | `flock`, freed on process death |
| `records` → `grid.y` (cap 65535) | 16384 tokens × top-k 4 = 65536, the first failing value → launch aborts at stock settings | `grid.x` (cap 2³¹-1); both dims checked |
| `hidden_size % 64` | partial Marlin tile reads a neighbouring slot *inside* the tensor; memcheck clean, no diagnostic | rejected |
| `role_bytes` in repack | unchecked; inconsistent value silently produced wrong output | asserted, as matvec already did |
| `#pragma once` | absent | added (insurance, not a fix) |

Device kernels unchanged apart from the matvec block-index swap. Public Python API and all callers unchanged.

**Verified on a 5090:** 4 + 11 tests pass; cold JIT rebuild; matvec re-derived against the CPU reference across 1–9 row tiles, both dtypes, the dual path, and up to 200k records; stream binding confirmed by CUDA-graph capture; `pre-commit` clean. `mxfp4_marlin_repack` is test-only, so the two stricter repack checks carry no production risk — all of it sits on the grid fix.
