title: [Score API] Setwise Scoring Support
author: sundar24295s
body: # Setwise Scoring Support ## Summary Adds **setwise scoring** to the score API: a SequenceClassification deployment can read its classification head **at every occurrence of a caller-chosen extraction token** in each `query + item` sequence, instead of only at the last token. A candidate set is packed into one item with one extraction token per candidate, and the head is pooled at each of those positions in a **single forward pass**, so `scores` comes back as one `[N_i x num_labels]` matrix per item (nested per item). This is a generic multi-position pooling primitive (`token_indices_to_pool`) that setwise scoring is the first consumer of; it is designed to extend to token classification, multi-vector embeddings, etc. The feature works in both execution modes: - **Batched (default):** each item is scored as an independent `query + item` sequence in one batch. - **Fused (`--enable-mis`):** the items are fused into one multi-item sequence (block-diagonal mask, shared query-prefix KV). Both modes return the same nested per-item shape. ## Motivation Rerankers and listwise/setwise rankers score a *set* of candidates jointly. Without this feature a caller must issue one request per candidate (last-token pooling), paying the query-prefix cost N times and losing any cross-candidate context. Setwise scoring packs the whole candidate block into one prompt with one anchor token per candidate and returns all N scores from a single prefill, cutting redundant prefill work and giving the head a single fused view of the set. ## API ### Engine (in-process) ```python result = engine.score( query="", # optional shared prefix items=[prompt_with_anchors], # one item = one candidate set score_extraction_token_id=anchor_id, apply_softmax=False, return_pooled_hidden_states=False, ) # result.scores -> [num_items][N_i x num_labels] (nested per item) # result.pooled_hidden_states (optional) parallels scores: per-item, per-anchor vectors ``` `async_score(...)` takes the same `score_extraction_token_id` argument. ### HTTP (`POST /v1/score`) ```json { "query": "", "items": ["Rank the candidates. ... Scores:<|object_ref_start|><|object_ref_start|>"], "score_extraction_token": "<|object_ref_start|>", "apply_softmax": false } ``` - Request adds `score_extraction_token: Optional[str]` (resolved to an id in the tokenizer-manager process, which owns the tokenizer). - `ScoringResponse.scores` is now a union: `[num_rows x num_labels]` (pointwise) or nested `[num_items][N_i x num_labels]` (setwise). `pooled_hidden_states` follows the same nesting. ### Semantics & validation - SequenceClassification only, and specifically models whose forward routes the head through `score_and_pool` (per-position pooling) — an explicit allow-list (`is_score_and_pool_model`). Generation (CausalLM), cross-encoder (`CrossEncodingPooler`), reward, and embedding models are rejected **before** inference, and `item_first` is incompatible. - An omitted `query` is normalized by item type (`[]` for pre-tokenized items, `""` for text) so token-ID items with no query take the token-ID path. - Every item must contain at least one extraction token; the shared query prefix must not contain it (both raise a clean `400` before inference). - The fused (`--enable-mis`) path carries the standard MIS delimiter tokens, so its scores differ slightly from the independent batched path — the inherent MIS trade-off, not specific to score extraction. ## Deployment / server start Pooling positions are full-prompt coordinates and all positions must be processed in one prefill, so setwise scoring requires radix cache and chunked prefill to be off. These constraints are validated at request time. Batched setwise: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --disable-radix-cache \ --chunked-prefill-size -1 ``` Fused multi-item setwise (adds MIS): ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --enable-mis \ --disable-radix-cache \ --chunked-prefill-size -1 ``` (`--enable-mis` already auto-disables CUDA graph / radix cache / chunked prefill.) `--allow-auto-truncate` is rejected, since truncation would leave pooling positions pointing past the truncated length. ## Worked example Serving a real multi-task setwise ranker (`num_labels = 7`): ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /shared/public/elr-models/sjsmodels/downloaded_models/sps_l3_multitask_ranker_setwise_history_0_0_4_0_peoplesearch-oc_sps_l3_multitask_ranker_setwise_history/proxima/model_resources \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --dtype float16 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --chunked-prefill-size -1 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.15 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` Two items (candidate sets), each with three anchors → nested `[num_items][N_i x num_labels]` (2 items × 3 rows × 7 labels): ```bash curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/score \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "query": "", "items": [ "Rank the candidates. Candidate 0. Candidate 1. Candidate 2. Scores:<|object_ref_start|><|object_ref_start|><|object_ref_start|>", "Rank the candidates. Candidate 0. Candidate 1. Candidate 2. Scores:<|object_ref_start|><|object_ref_start|><|object_ref_start|>" ], "score_extraction_token": "<|object_ref_start|>", "apply_softmax": false }' | python -m json.tool ``` ```json { "scores": [ [ [0.7158203125, -0.326171875, -2.576171875, -5.640625, -5.984375, -1.6240234375, -7.328125], [0.72314453125, -0.333984375, -2.560546875, -5.6015625, -5.8203125, -1.6318359375, -7.25390625], [0.7353515625, -0.35302734375, -2.587890625, -5.6171875, -5.6796875, -1.6337890625, -7.1875] ], [ [0.7158203125, -0.326171875, -2.576171875, -5.640625, -5.984375, -1.6240234375, -7.328125], [0.72314453125, -0.333984375, -2.560546875, -5.6015625, -5.8203125, -1.6318359375, -7.25390625], [0.7353515625, -0.35302734375, -2.587890625, -5.6171875, -5.6796875, -1.6337890625, -7.1875] ] ], "pooled_hidden_states": null, "model": "default", "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 42, "total_tokens": 42, "completion_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens_details": null, "reasoning_tokens": 0 }, "object": "scoring" } ``` (The two items are identical here, so their matrices match; each item independently yields one `[3 x 7]` matrix — one row per candidate anchor, seven task labels wide.) ## Implementation | Area | File | Change | |---|---|---| | Pooling kernel | `layers/pooler.py` | `pool_at_positions()` (pool AT positions, no `delimiter-1` shift, no discarded row) and a multi-position branch in `score_and_pool()`. | | Request plumbing | `managers/io_struct.py` | `token_indices_to_pool` on `EmbeddingReqInput` / `TokenizedEmbeddingReqInput`, split in `__getitem__`. | | | `managers/schedule_batch.py` | `Req.token_indices_to_pool`. | | | `managers/scheduler.py` | Partition prefill batches by pooling mode in `get_new_batch_prefill` so pooling-readout (setwise) and standard requests never share a forward batch — valid requests are never rejected based on concurrent traffic. | | | `managers/scheduler.py` (io), `managers/tokenizer_manager.py` | Thread the field through request construction. | | Forward batch | `model_executor/forward_batch_info.py` | Build per-request `token_indices_to_pool` CPU tensors in `init_new` (mirrors `multi_item_delimiter_indices`; read-only over the ScheduleBatch). | | | `model_executor/model_runner.py` | Skip the prefill CUDA-graph path when `token_indices_to_pool` is set. | | Score engine | `managers/tokenizer_manager_score_mixin.py` | Extraction-token resolution/scanning, omitted-query normalization, capability-based validation, per-item anchor bucketing for MIS, and nested per-item result grouping (`per_item_matrix`). | | | `configs/model_config.py` | `is_score_and_pool_model()` allow-list of SequenceClassification architectures that pool the head per position. | | Entry points | `entrypoints/engine_score_mixin.py` | `score_extraction_token_id` on `score()` / `async_score()`. | | | `entrypoints/openai/protocol.py`, `entrypoints/openai/serving_score.py` | `score_extraction_token` field, token→id resolution, recursive tensor→list conversion for nested `pooled_hidden_states`. | | Tests / bench | `test/registered/unit/...`, `test/registered/e2e/scoring/test_setwise_scoring.py`, `benchmark/prefill_only/bench_setwise_score.py` | Unit + HF-parity + MIS tests and an Engine benchmark. | 16 files, +2080 / -45. ## Review feedback addressed - **Mixed-traffic reliability (High).** Setwise and pointwise requests share the `/v1/score` endpoint and scheduler queue, so a client cannot guarantee homogeneous batches. Rather than reject setwise requests that happen to be batched with pointwise ones, the scheduler now **partitions prefill batches by pooling mode** (`get_new_batch_prefill`): a batch admits only the pooling mode of its first request, and the other mode runs in the next batch. The earlier traffic-dependent 400 abort is removed, restoring the additive/backward-compatible contract. Guarded by `test_mixed_setwise_and_pointwise_concurrent_batch`. - **Omitted `query` for tokenized input (Medium).** `query` now normalizes to `[]` for pre-tokenized items and `""` for text before path selection, so `engine.score(items=[[...token ids...]])` (and HTTP requests with no `query`) take the token-ID path instead of being rejected by the text builder. Guarded by `test_setwise_tokenized_items_omitted_query_match_hf`. - **Eligibility tied to `score_and_pool` (Low).** Validation now uses an explicit allow-list (`is_score_and_pool_model`) of SequenceClassification architectures that pool the head per position, so reward/embedding models (which pool a single vector and would ignore the readout positions) are rejected up front instead of after a wasted forward. Guarded by `test_validation_rejects_reward_model` / `test_validation_rejects_embedding_model`. ## Validation Environment: H200, `flashinfer 0.6.18`, `Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B-seq-cls` (anchor `<|object_ref_start|>`), engine `float16` on `flashinfer`. ```bash # CPU unit tests (no GPU / model needed) python test/registered/unit/layers/test_pooler_score_and_pool.py -v python test/registered/unit/managers/test_setwise_score_mixin.py -v # E2E (GPU); setwise uses a SequenceClassification checkpoint export TEST_CLASSIFICATION_BASE_MODEL=/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B-seq-cls python test/registered/e2e/scoring/test_setwise_scoring.py -v # Regression on the existing scoring paths export TEST_MODEL_NAME=/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct python test/registered/prefill_only/test_score_engine.py -v python test/registered/prefill_only/test_score_api.py -v python test/registered/prefill_only/test_serving_rerank.py -v ``` Results — all passing (106 cases): | Suite | Cases | Result | |---|---|---| | `test_pooler_score_and_pool.py` (CPU) | 12 | PASS | | `test_setwise_score_mixin.py` (CPU) | 44 | PASS | | `test_setwise_scoring.py` (E2E: HF-parity + MIS + mixed-batch + tokenized) | 10 | PASS | | `test_score_engine.py` (E2E regression) | 19 | PASS | | `test_score_api.py` (HTTP regression) | 8 | PASS | | `test_serving_rerank.py` (mock) | 13 | PASS | The E2E setwise tests assert **numerical parity** against a HuggingFace reference (gather the final hidden state at the anchor positions, apply the model's own classification head) — a wrong pooling position or head application changes the numbers, not just the shape. The MIS tests assert the nested per-item shape and block-diagonal set isolation (a set's scores are unchanged by other sets). ## Backward compatibility Purely additive. `score_extraction_token` / `score_extraction_token_id` default to `None`; when unset, the pointwise last-token path and its `[num_rows x num_labels]` shape are unchanged, as confirmed by the score-engine, score-api, and rerank regression suites. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #36041483134](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36041483134) Latest PR Test (Extra): :warning: **Not run on latest push** -- push again to dispatch. title: [DeepSeek-V4.1] Optimize small DSpark batches on Blackwell (BS1 803 tok/s)
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

DSpark's small target-verify and draft batches still spend time in small WO-A GEMMs, separate mHC combine/RMSNorm launches, and a stacked KV projection that bypasses the selected MXFP8 backend.

On 4x B300, BS1 output throughput increases from **762.41 to 803.25 tok/s (+5.36%)** with real DSpark acceptance.

## Modifications

- Add an eight-way split-K BF16 WO-A kernel for the TP4 shape and 2–8 token rows. Accumulate partials in FP32 and write the final BF16 result in token-major layout.
- Fuse four-stream mHC combine and RMSNorm for small batches, preserving the intermediate BF16 rounding. Schedule it before the side-stream statistics projection so the two short operations do not compete; statistics still overlap the following attention/FFN.
- Reuse the prepared MXFP8 weights and swizzled scales for stacked draft KV projections. Both FlashInfer CUTLASS and CuTe-DSL backends are covered.

Existing fallbacks remain for other shapes/backends. No new environment flags. Production changes only; benchmark and validation harnesses are outside the source diff.

## Accuracy Tests

Same checkpoint, five-shot GSM8K prompt and scorer; 1,314 held-out questions, concurrency 1, temperature 0, top-p 1, seed 0, max output 4096. The serial run exercises the small draft/verify kernels.

| | Baseline | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K | 1266/1314 (96.35%) | 1271/1314 (96.73%) |
| Request errors / empty outputs / truncations | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |

Paired results: 10 correct-to-incorrect and 15 incorrect-to-correct. Outputs are not bitwise identical; no aggregate accuracy loss was observed in this evaluation.

AIME 2026, same checkpoint and serving settings as the benchmarks; baseline `824bb45e1bf7`, candidate `0669e3d9464c`. Both runs use the same MathArena prompt, thinking mode, reasoning effort `max`, top-p 0.95 and max output 65,536.

| AIME 2026 | Baseline | This PR | Budget truncations (base / PR) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 30 questions, concurrency 1, temperature 0 | 27/30 (90.00%) | 27/30 (90.00%) | 3 / 3 |
| 30 questions × 16 samples, concurrency 64, temperature 1 | 445/480 (92.71%) | 451/480 (93.96%) | 13 / 15 |

All requested samples completed with zero request errors. Budget truncations stay in the score. The repeated score is correct samples / 480 (mean pass@1), not pass@16. Serial requests use seed 0; repeated requests leave the seed unset.

Serial paired results: 1 correct-to-incorrect and 1 incorrect-to-correct. Both flips involve a token-budget truncation in one arm and a correct completed answer in the other.

Evaluator: `sgl-eval==0.1.0`, vendored NeMo-Skills revision `645cf567ff08c0ae9cc3fc8e1edbb975b3067816`. Source files and installed serving packages were checked unchanged during each arm.

<details><summary>AIME input checksums</summary>

Dataset SHA256: `6a43e48d55eb7736003f53074fef041a3da2b78d902d3fcd0b1974b2523221fc`

Prompt SHA256: `12d8c6381b0191d2e8f6b1ecd39a65229f35af6f7aff21716bb951d456133afb`

</details>

<details>
<summary>AIME 2026 commands</summary>

The run uses `sgl-eval==0.1.0` with its bundled NeMo-Skills data/prompt (`645cf567ff08c0ae9cc3fc8e1edbb975b3067816`). The evaluator is installed outside the serving environment. Both arms use the same files and sampling settings.

```bash
# Run with the serving checkout on PYTHONPATH.
python -m pip install --target /tmp/sgl-eval-pinned --no-deps \
  sgl-eval==0.1.0 math-verify==0.9.0 latex2sympy2_extended==1.11.0 \
  antlr4-python3-runtime==4.9.3 editdistance==0.8.1
export PYTHONPATH="/tmp/sgl-eval-pinned:$PWD/python"
EVAL_DATA=/tmp/sgl-eval-pinned/sgl_eval/_vendored/nemo_skills/dataset/aime26/test.txt
EVAL_PROMPT=/tmp/sgl-eval-pinned/sgl_eval/_vendored/nemo_skills/prompts/matharena-aime.yaml
python -m sgl_eval.cli run aime26 \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30021/v1 --model "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --from-dataset "$EVAL_DATA" --prompt "$EVAL_PROMPT" \
  --num-threads 1 --n-repeats 1 --thinking --reasoning-effort max \
  --temperature 0 --top-p 0.95 --max-tokens 65536 --seed 0 \
  --out-dir results/aime-serial30
python -m sgl_eval.cli run aime26 \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30021/v1 --model "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --from-dataset "$EVAL_DATA" --prompt "$EVAL_PROMPT" \
  --num-threads 64 --n-repeats 16 --thinking --reasoning-effort max \
  --temperature 1 --top-p 0.95 --max-tokens 65536 \
  --out-dir results/aime-repeat16
```

The repeated lane leaves the request seed unset. Accuracy is the fraction of correct samples, not pass@16. Errors and token-budget truncations are counted separately.

</details>


Kernel validation:

- WO-A: 105 production-kernel comparisons against an FP64 reference, including cancellation, zero/large/small inputs, M=2–8 and strided rows; preceded by a 525-case sweep of five configurations.
- mHC combine/RMSNorm: 128 precision cases and 16 CUDA Graph replays with changed inputs.
- Stacked KV: M=1/2/5/6/8/64/320/384 on both MXFP8 backends; bitwise equal to separate MXFP8 projections. Packed scale concatenation checked against independent packing.
- Existing `commit_kv_proj` parity case and repository pre-commit hooks passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Base: `824bb45e1bf7486e49034bfa4bcad59aba799540` on `dsv4.1`. Candidate: `0669e3d946`.

4x B300 SXM6 AC, TP4/EP4; PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.6.18, Triton 3.7.1, sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1, sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.7, CUTLASS DSL 4.6.2. Same checkpoint and dependencies, DSpark block size 5. Checkpoint config aliases were normalized once in a separate directory for both arms; tensor values and weights were unchanged.

Two independent server launches per arm in baseline / candidate / candidate / baseline order. Each launch has one warmup, ten BS1 measurements and three BS64 measurements. All measurements are included in these medians. The candidate medians from each launch are 804.86 and 801.91 tok/s.

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| BS1, input 4096/output 1024, post-first-event output tok/s | 762.41 | **803.25** | +5.36% |
| BS1 median accept length | 5.802 | 5.818 | |
| BS64, input 4096/output 2048, stable decode output tok/s | 13,346.69 | 13,327.61 | -0.14% |
| BS64 median accept length | 5.387 | 5.335 | |
| BS64 full-request output tok/s, including prefill and drain | 6,356.42 | 6,242.74 | -1.79% |

The input is a fixed repeated weather-notes summarization prompt, with a different Notebook ID per BS64 request. It is easy to predict; these acceptance lengths are workload-specific. BS1 excludes the first streamed event. BS64 uses consecutive CUDA Graph decode log intervals with exactly 64 live requests, excluding prefill. Its acceptance length varies across runs; this PR targets BS1 and does not claim a BS64 speedup.

<details>
<summary>All unprofiled measurements</summary>

| Run | BS1 tok/s | BS64 decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|

import argparse

"""BS64 serving regression measurement; raw requests and log intervals retained."""
import argparse
import os
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import statistics
import threading
import time
import urllib.request

from tokenizers import Tokenizer


def save(path, value):
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n')


def post(url, route, body=None):
    request = urllib.request.Request(url + route, data=json.dumps(body or {}).encode(),
                                     headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=1800) as response:
        if route.startswith(('/flush_cache', '/start_profile', '/stop_profile')):
            return response.read().decode()
        return json.load(response)


def decode_samples(log):
    rows = []
    previous_bs = None
    for line in log.replace('\r', '\n').splitlines():
        if 'Prefill batch' in line:
            previous_bs = None
        if 'Decode batch' not in line:
            continue
        bs = re.search(r'#running-req: (\d+)', line)
        tps = re.search(r'gen throughput \(token/s\): ([0-9.]+)', line)
        al = re.search(r'accept len: ([0-9.]+)', line)
        graph = re.search(r'(?:CUDA graph|cuda graph|cuda_graph|full graph): (True|False)', line)
        if not bs or not tps:
            continue
        batch = int(bs.group(1))
        rows.append(dict(batch_size=batch, tps=float(tps.group(1)),
                         accept_length=float(al.group(1)) if al else None,
                         graph=graph.group(1) == 'True' if graph else None,
                         eligible=(batch == 64 and previous_bs == 64), line=line))
        previous_bs = batch
    return rows


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--out', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--server-log', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--url', default='http://127.0.0.1:30021')
    parser.add_argument('--no-spec', action='store_true')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    tok = Tokenizer.from_file(str(Path(os.environ['MODEL_PATH']) / 'tokenizer.json'))
    unit = tok.encode('The observatory records the temperature, wind, and rainfall each day. Researchers compare the measurements across seasons.\n', add_special_tokens=False).ids
    suffix = tok.encode('\nWrite a detailed summary of the notes above.\n', add_special_tokens=False).ids
    inputs = []
    for i in range(64):
        prefix = tok.encode(f'Notebook {i:03d}. Read these notes and summarize them.\n', add_special_tokens=False).ids
        n = 4096 - len(prefix) - len(suffix)
        inputs.append(prefix + (unit * ((n + len(unit) - 1) // len(unit)))[:n] + suffix)
    assert len({tuple(ids) for ids in inputs}) == 64
    assert all(len(ids) == 4096 for ids in inputs)
    save(args.out/'inputs.json', inputs)
    input_hash = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(inputs).encode()).hexdigest()
    waves = []
    for rep in range(4):
        warmup = rep == 0
        output_length = 256 if warmup else 2048
        post(args.url, '/flush_cache?timeout=30')
        offset = args.server_log.stat().st_size
        barrier = threading.Barrier(65)

        def request_one(i):
            body = {'input_ids': inputs[i], 'sampling_params': {
                'temperature': 0, 'max_new_tokens': output_length, 'ignore_eos': True}}
            barrier.wait()
            begin = time.perf_counter()
            response = post(args.url, '/generate', body)
            elapsed = time.perf_counter() - begin
            meta = response['meta_info']
            assert meta['completion_tokens'] == output_length, meta
            assert meta['prompt_tokens'] == 4096, meta
            if not args.no_spec:
                assert meta.get('spec_verify_ct', 0) > 0, meta
                assert meta.get('spec_accept_length', 0) > 0, meta
            return dict(index=i, elapsed_s=elapsed, response=response)

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=64) as executor:
            futures = [executor.submit(request_one, i) for i in range(64)]
            start = time.perf_counter()
            barrier.wait()
            responses = [future.result() for future in futures]
            elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
        save(args.out/f'wave-{rep}-responses.json', responses)
        # Drain scheduler request cleanup before the next cache flush.
        time.sleep(1)
        with args.server_log.open('rb') as log:
            log.seek(offset)
            text = log.read().decode(errors='replace')
        (args.out/f'wave-{rep}-server.log').write_text(text)
        rows = decode_samples(text)
        eligible = [row for row in rows if row['eligible']]
        if not warmup:
            assert len(eligible) >= 3, ('Insufficient actual BS64 intervals', rows)
            assert all(row['graph'] is True for row in eligible), eligible[:3]
        completed = sum(r['response']['meta_info']['completion_tokens'] for r in responses)
        verifies = sum(r['response']['meta_info'].get('spec_verify_ct', 0) for r in responses)
        wave = dict(repeat=rep, warmup=warmup, requests=64, input_tokens=4096,
                    output_tokens_per_request=output_length, input_sha256=input_hash,
                    elapsed_s=elapsed, aggregate_full_request_tps=completed/elapsed,
                    weighted_accept_length=completed/verifies if verifies else None,
                    bs64_decode_median_tps=statistics.median(row['tps'] for row in eligible) if eligible else None,
                    bs64_decode_intervals=len(eligible), decode_intervals=rows)
        waves.append(wave)
        save(args.out/'performance.json', waves)
        print('WAVE', rep, 'warmup', warmup, 'actual BS64 decode', wave['bs64_decode_median_tps'],
              'intervals', len(eligible), 'full-request', wave['aggregate_full_request_tps'],
              'AL', wave['weighted_accept_length'], flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

title: Reduce decode bootstrap latency with request-owned speculative KV
author: inkcherry
body:
## Problem

Optimistic prefill reduces decode bootstrap latency by overlapping decode-side allocation with prefill. Under `write_through` HiCache, however, speculative KV follows the normal publication path before the bootstrap result is known, making ownership unsafe across retries and aborts.

## Changed

- Keep pending-bootstrap KV request-owned and out of the shared radix cache.
- Advance multi-chunk requests without publishing speculative KV.
- Release retry, bootstrap failure, and abort paths without inserting unfinished KV or releasing it twice.
```
before:
Request
  → Decode bootstrap and KV preallocation
  → Wait for decode readiness
  → Prefill computation
  → Publish KV to radix cache and async write-through L2
  → Transfer KV to decode
  → First token

after:
Request
  ├─ Decode bootstrap and KV preallocation
  └─ Prefill computation
       → Keep KV request-owned and unpublished while bootstrap is pending
       → Bootstrap succeeds: publish once and async write-through L2 and transfer to decode
       → Bootstrap fails/retries/aborts: release unpublished KV and requeue
```
## Validated


DeepSeek-V4-Pro was tested twice on MI355X with 1P1D TP8/DP8, concurrency 256.

- Baseline:  [InferenceX action 33837253408](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/33837253408).
- Basline+this PR : the same code and configuration + this PR with  `--optimistic-prefill-attempts 2`. 
(https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34666940659)

| Metric | Baseline | Optimized | Change |
|--------|----------|-----------|--------|
| TTFT mean | 19.433s | 15.087s | -22.36% |
| TTFT p50 | 13.359s | 10.833s | -18.91% |
| TTFT p90 | 38.542s | 27.873s | -27.68% |
| TTFT p95 | 49.845s | 37.629s | -24.51% |
| Total throughput/GPU | 38,966.51 tok/s | 41,201.55 tok/s | +5.74% |
| Output throughput/GPU | 296.06 tok/s | 309.44 tok/s | +4.52% |

title: [Deps] Bump transformers to 5.17.0
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

Bump `transformers` 5.12.1 -> 5.17.0 (`tokenizers` 0.22.2 -> 0.23.2, required by it), drop the compat patches upstream has made dead, and port the 5.17.0 vision rotary refactor.

The `tokenizers<0.23` note goes away: CLIPTokenizer round-trips identically on slow and fast backends at 0.23.2.

### Patches removed

| Patch | Why it is dead |
|---|---|
| `_patch_nemotron_h_pattern` | Upstream maps `M`/`*` -> `linear_attention`/`full_attention` and handles `-`. Forcing the legacy names now makes the config's own validator reject it. |
| `_ensure_clean_up_tokenization_compat` | `clean_up_tokenization` is back on `PreTrainedTokenizerBase`. |
| `is_flash_attn_greater_or_equal_2_10` half of `_patch_removed_symbols` | Back on `transformers.utils`. |
| ROCm `dynamic_module_utils` symlink hot-patch | Fixed upstream in 5.13.0 (transformers#46618). |

`is_torch_fx_available` is still absent, so that patch stays.

### Changes that are not mechanical

**Config registration.** transformers now ships native configs for types SGLang defines its own classes for, and `AutoConfig.register` without `exist_ok` silently lost to them. Register with `exist_ok=True` only where no `_CONFIG_REGISTRY` re-parse backs the entry up (`zaya`, `cosmos3_edge`). `_LazyAutoMapping` keys on the config class `__name__`, so a differently-named shadow would drop out of PROCESSOR/TOKENIZER/MODEL_MAPPING. `cosmos3_omni` keeps losing to the native `Cosmos3OmniConfig` for that reason.

**Gemma4 attention shapes.** transformers now states Gemma4's global/SWA split as a heterogeneous `per_layer_config` -- the base attributes are the sliding-window values and the full-attention layers override `head_dim` (plus `num_key_value_heads` where the checkpoint sets it) -- and consumes `global_head_dim` / `num_global_key_value_heads` building it. A plain `text_config.head_dim` read raises `AmbiguousGlobalPerLayerAttributeError`, so every Gemma4 launch died in `get_config`. The parser takes both shapes off concrete layer indices, then drops the spec once it has flattened them onto SGLang's base / `swa_*` pair. A spec declaring anything beyond those two attributes, or a layer type carrying more than one shape, is rejected rather than silently flattened: SGLang carries one shape per layer type, and dropping the spec would revert the rest to the global value with the weights still loading.

**`embedding_rowwise`.** transformers appends `embed_tokens: embedding_rowwise` to `base_model_tp_plan` for every tied-embedding config. The style targets an `nn.Embedding`, which the Transformers backend shards itself in `replace_vocab_embed_class`, but `_normalize_tp_plan` rejected the unknown name up front and those models stopped loading.

**`layer_types` length.** Step-3.5-Flash lists an entry per main *and* next-n-predict layer (45 + 3), which the strict `validate_layer_type` in 5.17 rejects. The new patch re-runs the original validator against the wider count, so every other rule it applies -- per-list vocabularies, legacy remapping -- still holds.

**`_patch_rope_parameters_validation`.** Narrowed to swallow the missing `max_position_embeddings` rather than skip `standardize_rope_params` outright. The call also resolves `default_rope_type`, so the blanket early return left every config without `max_position_embeddings` on `"default"`. Pixtral's vision config is exactly that, and its tower refuses to build unless it sees `"axial"`.

Pixtral's rope table is unchanged: the axial `PixtralVisionRotaryEmbedding` indexes the `(h, w)` grid pairs that this file's own `position_meshgrid` already produces, instead of the flattened `h * max_width + w` offsets. `TestPixtralVisionRope` pins it to the closed form so an upstream change to the recomposition cannot silently rotate every patch by the wrong angle.

### Verification

4x GB300. Unit suites for configs, utils, tokenizer, parser, multimodal, managers, models, model_executor, server_args and entrypoints pass (3021 cases).

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| GSM8K 200q greedy, Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 | 0.880 (5.12.1 baseline: 0.875) |

title: [Diffusion] Recover IPC JIT initialization after interrupted builds
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

The two-rank Ulysses IPC synchronization loader uses `torch.utils.cpp_extension.load_inline` with persistent per-device build directories. If a build is interrupted, its FileBaton `lock` can remain after the owner exits. Later workers wait indefinitely in `FileBaton.wait()` during the first IPC operation, preventing server warmup from completing.

This addresses a reproducible interrupted-build failure mode investigated after [a diffusion CI warmup timeout](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34540781070/job/103093386761). The historical job did not capture a blocked-worker stack, so this PR does not claim conclusive attribution of that particular timeout.

## Modifications

- Load the existing IPC sequence-counter kernels through SGLang's shared JIT loader, which uses process-lifetime `flock` locking and atomic cache publication.
- Preserve the IPC signaling protocol, peer timeout propagation, current-stream execution, and CUDA Graph support.
- Add a bounded two-GPU regression test with orphaned legacy lock files and an isolated cold JIT cache. Register it in the diffusion two-GPU CUDA suite, once on partition 0.
- Do not delete existing caches or increase CI timeouts.

## Accuracy Tests

The added regression checks exact IPC input/output round trips on a nondefault stream and three CUDA Graph replays. NVIDIA CI results are pending on this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This is an initialization reliability fix, not a throughput optimization. No speedup claim.

## Checklist

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style and pre-commit requirements.
- [x] Add a registered regression test.
- [x] No user-facing API or documentation change required.
- [ ] Complete NVIDIA CI validation on this PR head.

title: [HiCache][Perf] fix: batch HiCache D2H submits per step for hybrid pools
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-hierarchical-cache` on a hybrid model (Inkling-Small-NVFP4: 7 full-attention layers + 35 sliding-window layers + mamba conv/temporal state), end-to-end throughput is ~5% below the same run with the host tier disabled.

The cost is not the D2H bandwidth. `write_through` backs up every new radix node on its own: `HybridCacheController.write()` calls `start_writing()` immediately, so one finished request turns into a kernel submit per pool plus one index upload per mamba conv tensor. The transfers themselves are async on a side stream, but issuing them runs on the scheduler thread. This workload finishes up to 64 requests in the same scheduler step, so the submits arrive in bursts that the overlap scheduler cannot hide, and the GPU idles until the next step is launched.

Measured on the reported configuration (4x GB300, Inkling-Small-NVFP4, TP=4, `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`, 128 concurrent lanes x 16 turns): 12,288 backup submits over the timed window for 89.6 GiB of payload.

## Modifications

- `HybridCacheController.write()` takes `flush: bool = True`. With `flush=False` the operation is left on the queue instead of being submitted immediately.
- `UnifiedRadixCache._execute_kv_backup()` passes `flush=False`, and `check_hicache_events()` calls `start_writing()` once per scheduler step. Every node backed up during that step, across all pools and all requests, becomes a single submit. `writing_check(write_back=True)` flushes what is still queued before waiting for acks, so the blocking path keeps its old semantics.
- `MambaPoolHost.backup_from_device_all_layer()` moves the host index tensor to the device once in the page-first path, instead of converting it again for every conv and temporal tensor inside `_copy_tensor_all_layers_lf_pf`.

No behaviour change other than batching: the same bytes are copied by the same kernels, and the ack accounting is unchanged (one ack per submit, carrying every node id in it).

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to kernels or model forward. Host restores were byte-compared against the device copy (payload, scales, mamba conv state) on all four ranks before and after the change, and a shape-matched L1-hit vs L2-restore probe produced identical text and identical per-token logprobs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same workload as above, no profiler attached, two repetitions per arm:

| build | L1 tok/s | L2 tok/s | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 12,181 | 11,564 | 5.1% |
| after | 12,211 / 12,159 | 11,913 / 11,952 | 2.0% |

Backup submits over the timed window drop from 12,288 to ~700 for the same 90 GiB of payload. In a torch profiler trace covering 400 steps, the scheduler stall when 64 requests finish in one step drops from 170/153 ms to 107/98 ms (the L1 baseline is 94/82 ms), and mean `cache_finished_req` from 1.54 ms to 1.14 ms (L1: 0.97 ms).

The residual 2% is per-node Python bookkeeping in the write-through path, which is a policy question rather than a submission-path one.

## Checklist

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Unit tests: `test_hicache_staged_write_back_dispatch.py` gains two cases (a chain of `flush=False` writes merges into one submit that keeps both node ids; the default still flushes per call). `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/` is green: 2340 passed, 1366 skipped, 430 subtests.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Keep quantization for mixed Quark Qwen3.5 MTP checkpoints
author: omirosh
body:
## Motivation

Speculative decoding is currently not working for amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4 (NEXTN, TP8, gfx950), because MTP does not load on mixed Quark MXFP4 Qwen3.5 checkpoints. This PR fixes the issue by addressing two separate problems:

`_mtp_quant_config` drops the draft's quant config as soon as any `mtp.*` layer appears in the Quark exclude list. That is correct for checkpoints whose MTP module is entirely bf16 (#23146), but here it builds the whole draft unquantized, so the MoE loader allocates bf16 experts that the MXFP4 checkpoint shards no longer fit.

`Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP` declares no `packed_modules_mapping`, which the loader reads off the model class so the quant config can expand `qkv_proj` into `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` before matching the exclude list. Without it an excluded attention projection is allocated MXFP4 - half as wide once packed - against bf16 shards.

## Modifications

Two changes in `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`:

- `_mtp_quant_config`: the Quark branch now takes the whole-module skip only when the routed experts are excluded as well, rather than on any `mtp.*` entry. They are the bulk of the draft, and the ordinary per-layer exclusions keep attention, the shared expert and `fc` in bf16 on their own.
- `Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP`: declare `packed_modules_mapping`, aliasing the target model's as `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` already does. That is also what the `TODO` above the Quark block in `_get_quantization_config` asks for.

`test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_5_mtp_quant_config.py` is new, covered under Accuracy Tests below.

Nothing else changes behaviour. The `mtp.*` exclude lists of the two published AMD checkpoints are identical apart from the routed experts:

| checkpoint | `mtp.*` excludes | of which `mlp.experts` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4 | 1546 | 1536 (= 512 x 3) |
| amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4 | 10 | 0 |

So the 397B still takes the skip and is unaffected. The only lists whose behaviour changes are Quark lists naming some `mtp.*` layers but not the routed experts, which is exactly the mixed case.

One side effect worth flagging: `_get_quantization_config` mutates the mapping it reads off the class, so a Quark run now adds `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` to `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM.packed_modules_mapping` process-wide. It is harmless here and `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` already aliases the same dict, but I can copy instead if you prefer.

## Accuracy Tests

The draft loads and serves on `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, NEXTN 3/1/4, TP8, MI350X; without this change it fails at load. New CPU-only unit tests cover both checkpoint shapes, using the real exclude entries, including a regression guard for #23146.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

None; this only changes which weights are allocated quantized at load time.

title: [DSV4.1] Fuse DSpark verify compression, indexer and projections
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

DSpark target verify launches many short kernels around compression, sparse-index selection and attention projections. On 4×GB300, TP4/EP4, BS1 random 4096-input / 1024-output tokens with simulated acceptance target 5.5, the PR improves median streamed decode throughput from the recorded **761.03 to 853.49 tokens/s (+12.15%)**. The C2 verify integration adds **6.37%** over the preceding 802.38-token/s version.

- Apply fused ratio-2 compression to fixed-width target verify at L2/L8/L14. The first row reads its previous partner from the per-request ring; subsequent rows read the preceding projected input directly. Fuse pair softmax, RMSNorm, RoPE, quantization and main-KV writes, then reuse the fused index-K store. Compact-ragged, draft-worker, prefill and unsupported-backend paths retain the existing implementation. Kernel contribution by DarkSharpness, with backend integration and validation in this PR.
- Fuse selected-score validation, invalid-index masking, logical-to-physical page mapping and optional raw-index output. Preserve Top-K index order, NaN/-inf rejection, +inf validity and -1 padding.
- Keep the existing PyTorch candidate-block selection, disable unused sorting, and fuse candidate scatter with token-mask expansion. The block budget remains 2048 blocks of 8 positions.
- Apply Q RoPE while writing the padded attention buffer for tiny BF16 batches, preserving the existing FP32 operation order and BF16 rounding.
- Fuse WO-A split-K reduction with MXFP8 activation quantization for the small TP4 path. Preserve intermediate BF16 rounding, exact UE8M0 conversion and the 128x4 scale layout. An explicit `Mxfp8SwizzledInput` distinguishes these inputs from ordinary block-FP8 tuples; the existing plain-tuple path is unchanged.


The fast paths retain shape/backend guards. The tested head is `835c39094ad017c2f54f8ea598002e669e6fa30d`, from a clean checkout; source and installed-package manifests are checked before and after each validation phase.

## Correctness

- `test_dsv4_indexer_postprocess.py`: 3 tests passed, including exact reference checks, invalid/NaN/Inf values, ties, strided metadata, production candidate dimensions, underfilled rows and CUDA Graph replay.
- `test_dsv4_q_rope_store.py`: 2 tests passed, with bitwise comparison to existing CUDA RoPE + copy, unchanged input/padding and graph replay.
- `test_block_fp8_as_mxfp8.py`: 2 tests passed. The added test compares FP8 bytes, swizzled scales and full WO-B outputs exactly for M=2..8; covers strided WO-A input, graph replay with changed data/poisoned scale padding, and legacy tuple dispatch.
- Repository pre-commit hooks passed on all changed files.


- C2 kernel and backend integration tests: **33 passed, 4 subtests passed, 4 all-padding combinations skipped**. Cover request-major verify with 2/5/6/9 rows, padding, both metadata integer dtypes, ring wrap, every accepted-prefix length followed by rollback, CUDA Graph replay, reference arithmetic and real cache writes. Compact-ragged fallback dispatch is also checked.

### Dataset accuracy

Acceptance simulation is **disabled** for all accuracy runs. DSpark uses genuine draft/target agreement, with the same checkpoint revision as the performance test. Per the requested protocol, the prior completed accuracy run is reused instead of rerunning a baseline.

Historical reference: `0669e3d9464c` on 4×B300. Current candidate: `835c39094ad017c2f54f8ea598002e669e6fa30d` on 4×GB300. These are historical accuracy comparisons across different code revisions and hardware, not a fresh paired A/B of this PR's parent.

| Evaluation lane | Historical reference | Current PR | Request errors | Current truncated outputs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| gsm-serial1314 | 1271/1314 (96.73%) | 1282/1314 (97.56%) | 0 | 0 |
| gsm-concurrent1314 | — | 1276/1314 (97.11%) | 0 | 1 |
| aime-serial30 | 27/30 (90.00%) | 28/30 (93.33%) | 0 | 2 |
| aime-repeat16 | 451/480 (93.96%) | 469/480 (97.71%) | 0 | 8 |

GSM8K: 1314 held-out questions, with the first five test rows used only as demonstrations; temperature 0, top-p 1, seed 0, max output 4096, legacy prompt/scorer. Both current GSM lanes have zero empty answers. The concurrent lane's one truncated answer repeatedly debates the wording “two times more”; it remains an incorrect sample in the denominator.

AIME 2026: `sgl-eval==0.1.0`, MathArena prompt, thinking enabled, reasoning effort max, top-p 0.95, max output 65536. Serial: 30 questions, temperature 0, seed 0, concurrency 1. Repeated: 16 responses per question (480 total), temperature 1, no fixed request seed, concurrency 64. Report correctness over all responses, not pass@16; retain truncations and errors. Historical AIME truncations were 3/30 and 15/480 respectively, with zero request errors.

All four evaluation lanes completed. No lower aggregate score than the historical reference was observed in the matched serial/repeated lanes; this does not establish bitwise equivalence or isolate hardware effects.

## Performance

title: [DSV4.1] Support raw-index output in TopK v2 (port of #33672)
author: DarkSharpness
body:
## Motivation

Port of #33672 (@weireweire, "Support raw-index output in TopK v2") onto the `dsv4.1` branch. The top-k v2 kernel could emit either raw indices or page-table-transformed indices, not both, so every caller that also needs raw positions (verify / sparse prefill) had to fall back to the v1 kernel. With both outputs from one launch the v1 fallback and its `raw_indices is None` dispatch conditions can go.

The commit is the original author's (cherry-picked from a103b0dfa9); the `topk_v2.cuh` part is re-implemented on this branch's reworked kernel structure (`PageTransform` / `trivial_transform` / `paged_transform`), the Python, indexer and test parts apply as they were.

## Modifications

- `TopKMode::DUAL_OUTPUT`: `page_indices` receives the page-table transform and `raw_indices` the selected raw indices, same `-1` padding. `PageTransform` carries the row's raw output pointer; `trivial_transform` and `paged_transform<kMode>` write it only in this mode, so the existing `INDICES` and `PAGE_TABLE` instantiations compile to the same code as before.
- Host `transform_paged(..., metadata, raw_indices: Optional)`, mode chosen from the two optional tensors.
- `topk_transform_paged_v2(..., out_raw_indices=None)`; the C4 indexer passes its raw-index buffer to v2 instead of falling back to v1 (XPU keeps the v1 path).
- Tests: `test_topk_v2_dual_output` (selection identical before and after the transform, checked against the reference) and a raw-index case in `test_dsv4_nonpaged_indexer.py`.

## Checks

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_topk_v2.py`: 288 passed; `test/registered/unit/layers/test_dsv4_nonpaged_indexer.py`: 10 passed (B200).
- SASS of the JIT module before/after (sm100a): every existing instantiation (`topk_main_kernel` L0-L3 x {INDICES, PAGE_TABLE}, `topk_small_batch_cluster_kernel` c8/c16, `topk_persistent_cluster_kernel`, `topk_ragged_kernel`) has the same instruction count and register count; the only textual differences are the kernel-parameter constant-bank offsets (one pointer added to `TopKPagedParams`).

title: [PD][OpenAI] Gate /v1/responses persistence behind --enable-response-store, default off
author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Motivation

The Responses serving path keeps two unbounded in-memory dicts (`response_store`, `msg_store`) with no TTL or eviction. This PR started as a fix for two PD-specific symptoms, but the review surfaced deeper problems with the per-node approach:

1. **A prefill node's Responses bookkeeping is unreachable by construction** — the PD router discards its reply and sends every retrieval call (`GET /v1/responses/{id}`, `/cancel`) to decode. With `store` defaulting to true (and forwarded to both legs), every PD `/v1/responses` request permanently grows both dicts on the prefill node.
2. **The per-node fix has a hole**: the background queued insertion (`status="queued"`) is unconditional — it isn't gated on `request.store` at all — so prefill leaks one entry per background request even with per-node gating of the other three write sites.
3. **Chaining under PD is fundamentally broken either way**: `previous_response_id` requires reading the store to rebuild the prompt, and the prefill leg must build the *same* prompt as decode. "Prefill doesn't store" and "prefill supports chaining" cannot both hold; gating only prefill's writes makes chained requests 404 on the prefill leg *before generation*, leaving decode waiting for KV that never comes.
4. **A built-in tool call cannot continue under disaggregation**: each `web_search`/`code_interpreter` call costs another generation, but a PD router dispatches exactly one prefill/decode pair per HTTP request — the continuation has no prefill peer to hand it KV.

## Approach

Replace per-node gating with an explicit opt-in server capability, default **off**:

- **`--enable-response-store`** (default off). Startup rejects enabling it with `--disaggregation-mode=prefill|decode`, so every PD deployment runs with storage disabled and stateful features are rejected *before either leg generates* — no KV-wait failure mode.
- When disabled: `create_responses` rejects `previous_response_id` and `background` at admission (400, before prompt construction or generation); `GET /v1/responses/{id}` and `/cancel` return a capability 400 before any lookup or abort side effect.
- All four persistence write regions (initial messages, queued background insertion, full completion, streaming completion — including message-history writes) are gated on `enable_response_store && store`.
- `background=true` with `store=false` is rejected outright (400): the result would be irretrievable, and today this combination leaks a permanent `in_progress` entry. This matches the OpenAI platform's own contract.
- Built-in tools (`web_search`, `code_interpreter`) are rejected under PD at admission, with a backstop in `_generate_with_builtin_tools` before any tool side effect. Standalone tool use is unaffected and works with storage off.

## Migration notice

**Responses storage is now disabled by default, including standalone servers.** To retain standalone retrieval, `previous_response_id` chaining, or background requests, start the server with `--enable-response-store`. Foreground generation and streaming still accept the API's default `store=true` without retaining responses when storage is disabled. Background requests require `store=true`. PD deployments cannot enable response storage and reject stateful Responses features; send explicit conversation history in foreground requests instead. Enabled storage remains process-local, in-memory, and unbounded, with no TTL.

The response's `store` field continues to echo the client request; the server capability controls actual retention.

## Tests

- 22 new unit cases across 10 test functions (`test_serving_responses.py`), one representative per failure mode: config publication and PD startup rejection; persistence across both completion finalizers with capability off/on; admission precedence (empty-predecessor, disabled/streaming background, null-store background); disabled and enabled GET/cancel semantics; detached-background success/failure/queued-cancel/running-cancel lifecycle; active-stream cancel 404; cancelled-record preservation in both finalizers; PD tool admission and continuation backstop; standalone built-in tools executing end-to-end with storage off. Each retained case was verified to turn red under a targeted in-memory mutation of the guard it protects (11/11 detected).
- Two existing stateful suites migrated to explicit opt-in so the default flip doesn't silently drop their coverage.
- `test_serving_responses.py` + `test_serving_responses_stream.py`: 78 passed, 10 subtests passed. Pre-commit clean.

## E2E verification (real hardware, Qwen3-0.6B on 4090)

- **Standalone, flag off (7/7 PASS)**: foreground + streaming generation normal; GET / chaining / background / background+`store:false` all rejected with the capability 400 in ~1ms (admission, pre-generation); `/v1/chat/completions` unaffected.
- **Standalone, flag on (7/7 PASS)**: store/retrieve round-trip matches; chaining 200; background request observed through queued → in_progress → completed; cancel → `cancelled`; `background+store:false` → 400 `param=store`.
- **PD startup rejection (PASS)**: `--disaggregation-mode prefill --enable-response-store` exits with the `ValueError` at ServerArgs resolution, before model load.

- **Combined with #36141 (PD router Responses dispatch, head `e3488b4f7b`) on real hardware (PASS)**: default buffered and streaming Responses generate through the PD router with dual-dispatch confirmed on both legs; `previous_response_id` is rejected in ~3ms through the router with this PR's admission message in the gateway envelope; a follow-up foreground request succeeds immediately after a rejected one (decode never waits on KV); detached background is rejected at the router in <1ms; zero KV/bootstrap/transfer errors in either leg's log. Note `/v1/responses` PD dual-dispatch does not exist on main without #36141 — this PR is its prerequisite safety gate.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Real storage backend with TTL/eviction; enabled storage remains unbounded.

title: [DSV4.1] Paged KV cache layouts for FlashMLA's V4.1 fp8 / fp4 formats
author: DarkSharpness
body:
Adds the DeepSeek-V4.1 paged KV cache formats read by FlashMLA's V4.1 sparse decode kernels (`3e18517` in the sgl-project fork, upstream `07a1089`): **V41**, 528 B/token (512 e4m3 incl. the RoPE dims, 16 ue8m0 scales, one per 32 values) and **V41_FP4**, 288 B/token (512 e2m1 codes, 32 e4m3 scales, one per 16 values; extra-cache only). The 584-byte V4 layout stays the default; nothing changes unless `SGLANG_DSV4_KV_LAYOUT=v41` is set.

## What

- `kv_layout.cuh` / `kv_layout.py`: the layouts as one `KVLayoutTraits` per format, `PagedKV<layout, page_bits>` for the page / row / scale-row addressing every writer shares (compile-time constants only; the V4 writers produce the same SASS as before), and the row quantizers `store_row<layout, vec>(data_row, scale_row, tx, const float (&v)[vec])`: any even power-of-two elements per thread, vectorized stores, ue8m0 exponent taken from the amax bits instead of a division. `torch_quant.py` is the pure-torch reference the kernels are checked against byte for byte.
- All DSV4 KV writers take a `layout`: the FlashMLA store (with optional in-kernel RoPE), the fused K norm+RoPE store, the ratio-1 / ratio-2 compressor writers (c1 / c2, decode and verify) and the ratio-4 / 128 writer. The fp4 cache stores the compressed latents' e2m1 codes directly, so the fp4 rounding happens once.
- `dequant_k_cache.py` dequantizes V4.1 pages into the bf16 prefill workspace.
- `DeepseekV4MemoryPool` carries `kv_layout` / `compressed_kv_layout` (bytes per token, page bytes, per-layer accessors); `SGLANG_DSV4_KV_LAYOUT` (`v4` | `v41` | `auto`) and `SGLANG_DSV4_COMPRESSED_KV_LAYOUT` (`auto`: fp4 for ratios 1 / 2, fp8 for 4 / 128; `fp8`; `fp4`). The backend reads the layout and bytes per token from the pool instead of hard-coding 584.

## Store kernel latency (B200, CUDA-graph replay, median us)

Baseline -> this PR, median us per call; the V4 layout is unchanged (bit-identical SASS for the c2 / fused writers), the fp4 rows are within noise.

| kernel | layout | bs=1 | bs=8 | bs=64 | bs=512 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| store | V41 | 1.02 -> 0.96 | 1.04 -> 0.98 | 1.09 -> 1.02 | 1.49 -> 1.39 |
| store + RoPE | V41 | 1.02 -> 0.98 | 1.04 -> 1.00 | 1.09 -> 1.04 | 1.54 -> 1.41 |
| fused K norm + RoPE | V41 | 1.21 -> 1.17 | 1.19 -> 1.17 | 1.23 -> 1.20 | 1.62 -> 1.62 |
| c1 | V41 | 1.47 -> 1.43 | 1.54 -> 1.41 | 1.52 -> 1.50 | 2.05 -> 1.95 |
| c2 | V41 | 1.82 -> 1.78 | 1.88 -> 1.84 | 1.97 -> 1.92 | 2.62 -> 2.52 |
| store (V4, reference) | V4 | 0.94 | 0.94 | 0.96 | 1.37 |

## Tests

`test_v41_kv_store.py`, `test_v41_kv_dequant.py`, `test_v41_kv_pool.py` (new), `test_c2_verify.py`, `test_dsv41_fused_compress.py`: 46 passed / 4 skipped / 53 subtests. No e2e run yet: the V4.1 formats need a FlashMLA build that reads them (the fork's `3e18517` also wants `kv_format="V41"` for the 528-byte cache, not passed yet).

title: fix(kda_prefill): fence shared writes before async proxy reads
author: willhu-jpg
body:
## Motivation

`chain_body` writes the widened L tile to shared memory through the generic proxy, then consumes it through the tcgen05 async machinery. `__syncthreads()` synchronizes participating threads, but it does not establish ordering between generic-proxy shared-memory writes and async-proxy reads. On affected SM103 KDA prefill runs, that missing proxy fence can race and cause incorrect results or device faults.

## Modifications

Add a small PTX helper for `fence.proxy.async.shared::cta` and issue it immediately after `widen_map_tf32`, before the existing tcgen05 thread fence and CTA synchronization.

## Accuracy Tests

- `clang-format` 20.1.7 passes.
- `git diff --check` passes.

An isolated A/B stress test on B300 (SM103) compiled two extensions from the
same source. The second variant removed exactly the three-line fence helper and
its one call. A CUDA profile confirmed all tested shapes selected
`kda_fused<0, true, true>`, which exercises the multi-piece prefix-composition
path containing this fence. Two fixed input sets were alternated between calls
to expose stale shared-memory data.

| Tokens | Heads | Fenced mismatch vs. its baseline | Unfenced mismatch vs. fenced baseline | Unfenced mismatch vs. its own first result |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8,192 | 12 | 0 / 100 | 86 / 100 | 100 / 100 |
| 16,384 | 12 | 0 / 100 | 82 / 100 | 89 / 100 |
| 8,192 | 16 | 0 / 100 | 75 / 100 | 100 / 100 |

The unfenced mismatches affected both BF16 output and FP32 final state. Sampled
mismatches were finite, and this run did not produce a device fault. The
fenced variant was bitwise stable across every repetition.

A CPU unit test would not exercise this hardware memory-ordering requirement. A regression test intended to provoke the race on SM103 would also be nondeterministic, so this PR does not add one.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not separately benchmarked. The change adds one CTA-scoped proxy fence only on the affected chain path; this PR makes no performance claim.

## Checklist

- [x] The code is formatted with the repository-pinned clang-format version.
- [x] The change is limited to the KDA prefill memory-ordering fix.
- [x] Accuracy evidence and its limitations are described above.
- [x] No documentation update is needed for this internal kernel synchronization change.

title: [Qwen3.8] Enable NVIDIA NVFP4 on DGX Spark with file-backed PLE and PDL router fix
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

Combining these changes into one PR also saves CI resources by avoiding three separate PRs running overlapping CI suites.

Enable single-node DGX Spark / GB10 deployment of `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` from upstream main, with or without its embedded MTP head. Main still lacks the NVIDIA mixed-precision loader handling and file-backed PLE storage needed for this deployment, and both PDL routers read bias before waiting for the preceding producer.

Consolidates and supersedes #38568, #38569 and #38570. Preserves their commits and authorship, upstreaming the original PDL fix #38290, NVIDIA loader work #38121 / #37752, file-backed PLE backend #37068 by @hashd1ve, and TP prefetch correction #38123 by @yhyang201.

## Modifications

- Move the PDL dependency wait before bias and score loads in both Triton and radix routers. Preserve register zeros for the no-bias path.
- Resolve ModelOpt mixed-precision checkpoint prefixes, normalize omitted exclusion lists, dispatch FP8_BLOCK_SCALES layers, and select FP8 PLE storage from the mixed config. Preserve existing FP8_PB_WO support.
- Retain mixed quantization for checkpoints with quantized `mtp.*` layers; preserve BF16 MTP behavior otherwise. Add the original mixed-expert runner selection and use the Triton FP8 MoE fallback when the global NVFP4 runner is FlashInfer CUTLASS/CuteDSL.
- Add `--ple-offload-backend {pinned,file}` and `--ple-offload-dir`, using a sparse file-backed table on supported unified-memory devices. Add prefetching and resident-memory trimming.
- Filter prefetch IDs to the local TP vocabulary shard and subtract the shard start before computing file offsets.
- Include the original ports' regression tests and CLI/environment documentation.

Based on `main@45715e7f20629d1813ff8f543a23bb437128db2e`. All three changes merge cleanly, and the combined tree is identical to merging the empirically tested integration branch onto this base. No additional source edits were introduced during consolidation. Direct source review confirms all three gaps remain in this main revision.

## Accuracy Tests

**Empirical host deployment on 1x DGX Spark / GB10 (sm121), TP=1; no patched Docker image.** SGLang and its native extensions were installed from the combined source checkout. NVIDIA checkpoint revision: `fab0aecb760cec45227f6656abcaafa11abca87a`.

September 11 tests used `main@165d8dd17736fa4938f2e73018f26835cd6e0778` plus these exact component heads:

- #38568: `626f614f7bcd5dc531de5c268a694ff1a9f31f28`.
- #38569: `825663897b1fd9ee5c341eeb113b795e4ecfc3f8`.
- #38570: `b14d2c55f37f8d3dc2b5fe21175b56fbe62771e1`.

Tested combined revision: `69d38ccbd8a03646cae9168c971b3783883c2903`. The newer PR base received source and clean-merge review; the numbers below are not relabeled as a GPU run on that newer base.

GSM8K first 200 test questions, greedy chat API, thinking disabled, 8,192-token generation limit:

| Configuration | Accuracy | Request errors / invalid / truncated | Ready | Effective max input |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| MTP, concurrency 8 | **195/200 (97.5%)** | **0 / 0 / 0** | 763.26 s | 180,282 tokens |
| Non-MTP, concurrency 24 | **194/200 (97.0%)** | **0 / 0 / 0** | 633.17 s | 262,138 tokens |

Both arithmetic smoke tests passed and CUDA graphs were active. MTP selected the intended FP8 Triton expert fallback and reported average draft acceptance **3.52925**. No serving NaN/OOM/CUDA-error/exception reports appeared before intentional shutdown. This is log-level evidence, not internal NaN instrumentation. Cancellation tracebacks during intentional SIGTERM were recorded separately; both servers stopped after evaluation.

Environment: Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.173.02, FlashInfer 0.6.18, Triton 3.7.1, sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1, Transformers 5.12.1. The isolated host environment was updated from main and native extensions rebuilt. Runs reused previously compiled host kernels with `MAX_JOBS=2`; startup timings exclude cold kernel compilation. The NVIDIA cuSPARSELt package reports a platform-tag warning on aarch64; GPU imports and both deployments succeeded.

Common serving flags (using the local NVIDIA checkpoint copy and a fresh local-NVMe PLE directory per boot):

```bash
sglang serve \
  --model-path nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 \
  --tp 1 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --page-size 64 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
  --context-length 262144 \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \
  --ple-offload-embedding --ple-offload-backend file
```

MTP adds `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --max-running-requests 8 --max-mamba-cache-size 40`. Non-MTP adds `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy --max-running-requests 24 --max-mamba-cache-size 96`.

Prior component checks recorded in the superseded PRs: 15 router GPU tests; 18 mixed-loader tests; 3 FP8 fallback tests; 34 fusion-gate tests; 2 Qwen MoE override tests; 26 file-table/Qwen argument tests; 13 embedding tests. Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed on the component ports. Consolidation passes `git diff --check` and exact merged-tree comparison; these component tests were not rerun merely to combine branches.

Scope: TP=1 text/chat validation, not a deterministic PDL-race reproduction, TP>1 prefetch validation, other-hardware validation, or the full 1,319-question benchmark. No full-length 262K prompt was tested; the configured MTP memory budget limits effective input to about 180K.

Known PLE startup limitation: populated files are rewritten on boot and can be much slower than fresh sparse files. Stop all servers using the directory before removing its `ple_table_*.bin` files for a fresh boot. Automatic cache lifecycle changes are not included.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

| Configuration | Generated tokens | Evaluation wall time | Aggregate output |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| MTP, concurrency 8 | 79,489 | 855.91 s | **92.87 tokens/s** |
| Non-MTP, concurrency 24 | 79,954 | 893.02 s | **89.53 tokens/s** |

These are end-to-end chat-evaluation aggregates including prefill and the lower-concurrency tail, not a controlled before/after speed comparison or an isolated measurement of the router fix. The final non-MTP response discussed salary timing for 4,632 tokens, finished normally, and was scored incorrect against the dataset label.

## Checklist

- [x] Preserve component changes, regression tests, documentation and authorship.
- [x] Record component pre-commit and test results, and verify the combined diff/tree.
- [x] Provide combined single-node deployment accuracy and throughput results with exact revisions.
- [ ] Run the full 1,319-question evaluation and validate other hardware/TP configurations.
- [ ] Complete CI and maintainer review for the combined PR.

title: Add triton autotune on the Mamba2 SSD kernels
author: elvischenv
body: ## Motivation The Mamba2 SSD Triton kernels were adapted from vLLM without their `@triton.autotune` decorators: sglang's original import (#10988) carried them commented out, and #10909 deleted the commented blocks while re-syncing the ops. The launchers still size their grids from `META["BLOCK_SIZE_*"]`, so every kernel silently ran at its signature default of `BLOCK_SIZE_* = 16` -- a 10x+ loss on the prefill kernels. Upstream vLLM has these decorators live today. ## Modifications - Restore `@triton.autotune` on `ssd_bmm`, `ssd_chunk_scan`, `ssd_chunk_state` and `ssd_state_passing`. The config lists and keys are verbatim from current `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/`, so these blocks stay diffable on the next upstream sync. - `_chunk_state_varlen_kernel` is sglang-only -- vLLM replaced it with `gather_initial_states.py` driven by `cu_chunk_seqlens` -- so it reuses the `_chunk_state_fwd_kernel` list (same tile-shape family). - Add `**autotune_cache_kwargs` (the existing sglang FLA idiom, `kernels/ops/attention/fla/utils.py`) so a tuning result survives process restarts instead of being re-measured on every server launch. - Add `prune_configs_by` / `prune_oversized_tiles`, which caps each `BLOCK_SIZE_*` at `next_power_of_2` of the dimension it tiles. A tile wider than its dimension computes a fully masked remainder over the same grid, so it is dominated. This is the fix for the `test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` CI timeout -- see below. - Fix `bench_one_batch` on Mamba models: `selective_state_update` dispatches through a process-global backend that only the Scheduler installs, so every Mamba model died during decode CUDA-graph capture inside `load_model`. It is now initialized from a helper shared by `latency_test` and `correctness_test`, so `--correctness-test` is covered too. ## CI cost The 30-minute timeout on the previous run was real and caused by this PR. Autotuning is per distinct key, and `test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` spans many: `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel` alone sees ~22 keys over the CI-reduced matrix (Triton folds the tensor dtypes into the key on top of `chunk_size`/`hdim`/`dstate`), at 23 configs each -- ~500 compile+bench cycles for one kernel, and ~4x that across all six. A persistent cache does not help here, since the cold pytest process never gets a hit. The prune collapses the small CI shapes to a handful of configs each (`hdim=5, dstate=5, chunk_size=16` -> 1 config; `hdim=32, dstate=32, chunk_size=8` -> 1), without touching the test matrix. ## Accuracy Tests Autotuning selects `BLOCK_SIZE_K`, which sets the K-split of the fp32 `tl.dot` accumulation, so output is **not** bit-identical to the `BLOCK_SIZE_* = 16` defaults. `lm_eval` GSM8K (5-shot), Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4, TP4: | | main | + autotune | | --- | ---: | ---: | | flexible-extract | 0.9401 ± 0.0065 | 0.9409 ± 0.0065 | | strict-match | 0.9378 ± 0.0067 | 0.9393 ± 0.0066 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling **End-to-end serving**, Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4 on GB300 TP4, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024: | Concurrency | Total tok/s (main) | Total tok/s (+autotune) | Speedup | tok/s/user (main) | tok/s/user (+autotune) | Speedup | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 16 | 10,981 | 13,264 | **1.21x** | 104.9 | 110.2 | **1.05x** | | 32 | 15,728 | 17,751 | **1.13x** | 78.0 | 85.4 | **1.10x** | | 64 | 20,772 | 23,662 | **1.14x** | 53.0 | 59.5 | **1.12x** | | 128 | 24,877 | 29,892 | **1.20x** | 33.9 | 39.0 | **1.15x** | | 256 | 28,190 | 35,747 | **1.27x** | 20.0 | 24.3 | **1.22x** | | 512 | 29,558 | 37,776 | **1.28x** | 16.8 | 20.5 | **1.22x** | ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #36831003022](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36831003022) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #36831002809](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36831002809) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #36831002974](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36831002974)

title: [DeepSeek-V4.1] Commit the engram decode history inside the hash kernel
author: hnyls2002
body:
In decode every token is its request's newest token, so the engram hash kernel already holds the row that becomes the request's new n-gram history. This writes it from the kernel instead of the five torch ops that followed the kernel (`req_pool_indices` cast, `out_cache_loc == 0`, `where`, `flip`, `index_put`). The kernel keeps one pure entry point, `engram_hash_ids`, and gains a decode one, `engram_hash_ids_and_commit`, which advances `history` in place (rows whose out_cache_loc is 0 are graph padding and write nothing) and skips the predecessor table that only the extend commit reads. The hasher is one node in the decode CUDA graph; extend keeps the torch commit, and verify is unchanged.

Hash ids are integers, so the change is bitwise. `test_engram_hash.py` adds a 5-row decode case (a padded row aliasing a live slot) and a 100-row case over four programs, both checked against the naive oracle and the expected history table.

A/B against the `dsv4.1` base on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4/EP4 on 4x GB300, one server at a time:

| | base | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| 28-prompt greedy, 64 tokens, first-token top-5 logprobs | | 28/28 identical, all deltas 0 |
| bs=1 decode, 1k in | 227.9 tok/s | 228.1 tok/s |
| bs=1 decode, 16k in | 196.8 tok/s | 197.5 tok/s |
| bs=64 decode, 1k in | 5225 tok/s | 5240 tok/s |
| 16k-prompt TTFT | 0.422 s | 0.424 s |
| gsm8k 5-shot 1319 | 0.895 | 0.902 |
