title: [AMD] GLM-5.2 NextN: cast draft fused MoE to per-channel FP8
author: jiejingzhangamd
body:
Re-submission of #38476 on behalf of @fanxingran. The four original commits retain their original author attribution; the original discussion and comments remain on #38476.

## Motivation

Layer 78 of GLM-5.2 is the MTP draft layer. The MXFP4 checkpoint ships its routed
and shared experts in bf16 — 71.7 MB per expert against 19.0 MB for an MXFP4
decoder layer — and MTP reads that layer once per draft step. In bandwidth-bound
decode it therefore costs more than its share of the parameter count suggests.

While wiring the quantized path up it turned out `QuarkW8A8FP8MoE` could never
reach its AITER runner, so every quark per-channel FP8 MoE on ROCm was silently
running Triton.

## Modifications

- **Cast the GLM NextN fused-expert weights to per-channel FP8 at load time**
  (`deepseek_weight_loader.py`), and point quark's per-module scheme selection at
  the matching `QuarkW8A8FP8MoE` scheme (`glm4_moe.py`). Off by default behind
  `SGLANG_GLM_NEXTN_MOE_PTPC`. The loader additionally requires a GLM
  `model_type`: the mixin is shared with DeepSeek, where no matching scheme
  exists and the cast weights would have nowhere to load.

- **Fix the AITER runner selection in `QuarkW8A8FP8MoE`.** The AITER branch was
  gated on `moe_runner_config.apply_router_weight_on_input`, which no model that
  resolves to a quark scheme sets, so the branch was unreachable. Select the
  runner from what the kernel actually requires — per-channel weight scales,
  AITER built in, and an a2a backend that supports it — and route `apply_weights`
  through `AiterMoeQuantInfo`. Preshuffling now keys off the selected runner
  rather than the same dead flag, so the canonical layout is preserved when
  Triton runs.

- **Copy the `QuarkConfig` before the NextN remap** in
  `_resolve_nextn_quant_config`. The caller keeps that object for the target model
  and for `lm_head`, so the draft-only rewrite was mutating shared state. A no-op
  for GLM-5.2-MXFP4, whose `layer_quant_config` is empty, but wrong for any
  checkpoint that sets one.

### On the runner default

`auto` now resolves to AITER for this scheme, matching what its siblings in the
same directory already do — `quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py` and
`quark_w4a8_mxfp4_moe.py` both promote `auto` to AITER when the a2a backend
supports it. `QuarkW8A8FP8MoE` was the one left on Triton, and only because of
the dead flag, so this restores consistency rather than introducing a new default.

It does matter which runner wins: FP8 experts on the Triton path are *slower*
than the bf16 they replace (TPOT p50 +7.5% to +11.6% across five synthetic
scenarios), because that path dequantizes inside the kernel. AITER's per-token CK
fused MoE consumes the FP8 weights and per-channel scales directly. Leaving the
runner as-is would therefore make `SGLANG_GLM_NEXTN_MOE_PTPC=1` a regression.

`--moe-runner-backend triton` restores the previous path, and the resolution is
logged once at startup (`QuarkW8A8FP8MoE runner=...`) so a fallback is visible
rather than surfacing later as an unexplained regression.

### Why per-channel and not 128x128 block FP8

Both are FP8, so the weight bytes are identical (9.0 GB either way); only the
scale metadata differs, by 8 MB out of 9 GB. Decode here is purely
bandwidth-bound, so the two hit the same roofline — measured, both reach
5.5–6.0 TB/s on MI355X.

Benchmarked on the real layer-78 shape with both formats tuned by aiter's MoE
tuner, the best non-FLAT block kernel is 1.6–25% *slower* than the best
per-channel one at every token count from 1 to 128. Block's one win — 55.5 us
against 114.9 us end-to-end at token 1 — comes from a FLAT kernel that skips
host-side sorting, and that kernel drops `expert_mask`, so it faults under EP.
Accuracy is a wash (mean relative error vs bf16: 0.065 per-channel, 0.064 block).

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K 5-shot, `lm_eval` `local-chat-completions`, temperature 0, 1319 problems,
MTP enabled with real verification (no synthetic acceptance length).

| | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---:|---:|
| baseline (bf16 draft experts) | 0.9416 ± 0.0065 | 0.9424 ± 0.0064 |
| this PR (`SGLANG_GLM_NEXTN_MOE_PTPC=1`) | 0.9371 ± 0.0067 | 0.9371 ± 0.0067 |
| delta | −0.45 pp | −0.53 pp |
| 2 × combined stderr | ±1.86 pp | ±1.85 pp |

Both deltas are well inside noise.

Speculative decoding is lossless at temperature 0 — an accepted draft token is by
construction the target model's argmax — and only the draft layer is requantized,
so this is a regression guard rather than a precision measurement. It is what
would catch a bad weight scale or the shared-config mutation fixed above.

### Draft acceptance is unchanged

The end-user speedup is the kernel gain multiplied by any change in acceptance, so
the cast is only worthwhile if the FP8 draft proposes as well as the bf16 one.
Measured on the GSM8K run above, with synthetic acceptance disabled:

| | accept len | accept rate | decode steps |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline | 2.810 ± 0.030 | 0.362 | 1057 |
| this PR | 2.829 ± 0.036 | 0.366 | 1142 |

+0.68%, against a 95% CI of ±1.7% on the difference, and it holds per batch size.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

aiperf AgentX trace, GLM-5.2-MXFP4 on MI355X, TP4/EP4, concurrency 8, 3600 s per
arm, one run per arm, 0 errors on both. All 473 other `ServerArgs` identical.
Acceptance was pinned in both arms with `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.61` to isolate
the kernel from the acceptance measurement above.

| | baseline | this PR | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **Interactivity p90** (tok/s/user) | 110.42 | 120.66 | **+9.3%** |
| Interactivity p50 | 173.42 | 181.74 | +4.8% |
| TTFT p50 | 0.597 s | 0.528 s | −11.5% |
| TTFT p90 | 1.555 s | 1.367 s | −12.1% |
| TTFT p95 | 2.200 s | 1.819 s | −17.3% |
| TPOT p50 | 5.77 ms | 5.50 ms | −4.7% |
| TPOT p90 | 9.06 ms | 8.29 ms | −8.5% |
| TPOT p95 | 10.79 ms | 10.36 ms | −4.0% |
| E2E p50 | 3.80 s | 3.45 s | −9.2% |
| E2E p95 | 29.12 s | 26.80 s | −8.0% |
| Output throughput | 355.2 tok/s | 359.4 tok/s | +1.2% |
| Requests completed | 1143 | 1153 | +0.9% |
| GPU prefix-cache hit | 95.80% | 95.88% | +0.08 pp |
| NextN weights per GPU | 5.46 GB | 3.17 GB | **−2.29 GB** |

Interactivity is `1/ITL` at the matching percentile, so those rows restate TPOT
rather than measuring separately.

**Where the decode win comes from.** The server's own decode log, compared at
matched `#running-req` (99% of decode steps), separates the kernel from the
scheduling response to it:

| avg ITL | ms | vs baseline |
|---|---:|---:|
| baseline | 5.259 | — |
| swap in this PR's per-batch kernel timings, hold the batch mix | 5.168 | **−1.74%** |
| hold baseline kernel, swap in this PR's batch mix | 5.229 | −0.57% |
| this PR | 5.144 | −2.19% |

The kernel itself is worth about 1.7%. Faster decode shortens residency, so at
fixed concurrency the batch-size distribution shifts down (37.6% → 40.1% of steps
at batch 1, where ITL is lowest), worth another 0.6%. The client-side percentiles
move further still, from prefill interleaving and scheduling outside the decode
step, which the decode log does not resolve.

That 1.7% is what the weights predict. MoE decode only reads routed experts, and
the draft runs one token per forward while verify runs six: at batch 1 the draft
touches 8 of 256 experts and each target layer touches 44.4. Those two effects
nearly cancel, so one draft forward reads 1.198 GB against 1.201 GB for one target
layer — five draft forwards cost about five target layers out of 78, or 6.1% of
the bytes moved per iteration. Halving the draft's expert bytes takes each draft
forward to 0.876 GB, i.e. 1.67% of the total at batch 1, 1.99% at batch 2 and
2.43% at batch 4, against measured 1.41%, 2.18% and 1.68%.

The corollary is that this lever is now spent: eliminating the draft forwards
entirely would only be worth 6.5%, and the remaining 4.8% is per-forward fixed
cost — five kernel launches, five all-to-all rounds under EP4, five sync points —
which no change in weight precision can reach.

**Controls checked.** The 1.9% KV-pool difference did not bind: peak pool
occupancy was 0.78 / 0.67 and theoretical cache hit rate was identical (0.97627 /
0.97632). The baseline arm paid 52 JIT compiles in-window (none in the second arm,
which inherited the warm cache), but that inflates only the moments, not the
percentiles, so `itl.mean` and `itl.std` are excluded here and only percentiles
are quoted. Decode gain by time window is +1.50% (0–10 min, containing the
compiles), +1.72%, +2.17%, +1.55% — the compile-affected window shows the
*smallest* gain, so the JIT is not driving it.

**Not quoted:** per-chip total throughput (+1.47%), because input is 99.2% of that
counter and 95.8% of it is prefix-cache reads — GEMM-bearing prompt tokens rose
only 0.44%.

Single run per arm, so treat the magnitudes as indicative.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

No unit test: the path needs a ROCm GPU with AITER and a GLM-5.2 MXFP4 checkpoint,

title: [AMD][DSV4] feat: enable PD-disagg with fp8 unified_kv on gfx950
author: amd-danli103
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
#37413 stores unified_kv as two pools (fp8 nope 512 B/row + bf16 rope 128 B/row). Prefill/decode PD registration still advertised a single pointer per layer priced at `buf[0].nbytes`, so the rope pool was dropped. Decode then attended with stale RoPE — wrong output, no crash. The pool refused PD at startup.
This PR only changes how the pool **reports** `(ptr, nbytes, item_len)` to the existing transfer backends. We do not add new mori/mooncake/nixl send paths. 

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
AMD DSV4 unified_kv only. Still off unless `SGLANG_DSV4_UNIFIED_KV_FP8=1`.

- **Register both pools.** PD now advertises the bf16 rope pool next to the fp8 nope pool — compressed pages via `get_contiguous_buf_infos`, the sliding-window ring via `get_unified_swa_ring_buf_infos`. Same page indices; rope rows are 128 B. mooncake / nixl / mori send paths are unchanged.
- **Same layout on both sides.** Prefill and decode must both have the env on or both off. A mixed pair fails at startup instead of shipping a truncated region list.
- **Still refused under fp8 unified_kv + PD.** `pp_size>1` and `--enable-hisparse` still index KV regions by layer count; the extra rope groups would shift that index. 
- **Tests.** CPU: region order, 512 B vs 128 B, a fake two-pool copy, mixed-peer / PP / HiSparse rejects. Manual Flash E2E (`test/manual/dsv4/test_dsv4_pd_disagg_fp8_nixl.py`): GSM8K plus two RoPE probes (inside the window, and past it into compressed pages).

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->
Deepseek-V4 Flash, 8×MI355X, P/D symmetric TP4+DP4, EAGLE 3/1/4. Pair differs only in `SGLANG_DSV4_UNIFIED_KV_FP8`. Same-node transfer: `mooncake_tcp`. 5-shot GSM8K.

| arm | n=1319 | rope (SWA / compressed) |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| fp8 two-pool | **0.927** | both recalled |
| bf16 pool | **0.923** | / |

Nightly bar on this checkpoint is 0.92.

Further evaluated DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, 16×MI355X 1P1D (`--tp 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention`), no speculative decoding, 5-shot GSM8K n=1319, client parallel 8. Same two-pool env as Flash.

| backend | n=1319 | invalid |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `mooncake_tcp` | **0.937** | 0 |
| `mori` (mlx5) | **0.938** | 0.001 |
| `mooncake` RDMA (mlx5) | — | — |

`mooncake` RDMA fails in the transfer engine (`ibv_reg_mr` / `RdmaTransport: Failed to register memory`) before any chunk is sent. The same GPU pointers register and copy with `mori` and `mooncake_tcp`, so this is not the two-pool `(ptr, nbytes, item_len)` contract.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->
Not in this PR. This PR is the registration contract. No serving matrix.

## Reproducing this

MI355X, ROCm 7.2.

**1. Unit tests**:

```
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<card> python3 -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_dsv4_unified_fp8_pd.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_wire.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsv4_compressed_pools.py \
  test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_pool_configurator.py \
  -q
```

**2. V4 Flash PD E2E** (8 GPUs). Same-node default backend is `mooncake_tcp`.

```
export SGLANG_TEST_DSV4_FLASH_MODEL=<DeepSeek-V4-Flash>
export SGLANG_TEST_PD_TRANSFER_BACKEND=mooncake_tcp
export SGLANG_TEST_PD_GSM8K_N=1319
export SGLANG_TEST_PD_GSM8K_BAR=0.92
export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0

python3 -m pytest test/manual/dsv4/test_dsv4_pd_disagg_fp8_nixl.py -s
```

Expect no `does not support PD disaggregation`. The two `test_rope_probe_recalls_marker_*` methods are the RoPE-transfer check; GSM8K alone is not.

**3. 2-node 1P1D.** Same env, one node prefill / one node decode, `--tp 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention`, pin `--disaggregation-ib-device mlx5_*`. `mooncake_tcp` and `mori` both transferred; `mooncake` RDMA still fails KV MR on this cluster. Keep GSM8K client parallelism modest (8, not 64).

title: [AMD] gfx950 assembly attention: length-aware split-KV for dynamic workload
author: zijiecode
body:
## Motivation

#37465 splits every sequence of a verify / draft batch into the same number of KV segments, `max(1, min(64, pow2floor(256 / (bs * kv_heads))))`, one work-group per (segment, sequence, kv head). That is the right split when all sequences have similar length, not optimal when one batch holds requests that varies heavily in length. Two things then happen:

- the layer finishes when the longest request's segments finish, so short requests' work-groups sit idle while a 248k request streams 8x longer segments;
- above 16 sequences the per-sequence segment count halves (bs 17-32 -> 8 segments; on TP4 with 2 kv heads per rank bs 9-16 -> 8, bs 17-32 -> 4), so a 248k request runs as 31k-token segments and the kernel degrades to Triton speed. Half of the decode steps of the TP2 c32 leaderboard point are at bs 17-30.

This PR picks the segment length from the batch's actual sequence lengths and hands the kernel a compact work list, so every sequence gets as many segments as its length needs while the total work-group count stays at one per CU.

## Modifications

The planned split is the default for bs > 1; bs == 1 keeps the fixed split of #37465 (`plan_ptr == 0`), which already uses 64 segments there. No new switch. Kernel build and the gfx950 / ROCm gating are unchanged from #37465.

- `vattn_asm_gfx950/__init__.py`: a small Triton plan kernel (grid = num_seqs, graph-capture safe) picks one segment length `T` from `seq_lens` (smallest `T` with total segments <= num_CUs / kv_heads and per-sequence segments <= `seg_max`) and writes a work list `plan[1 + i] = seq << 16 | seg` (`-1` past the end) plus a per-query-token segment count. The attention kernel is launched as a 1-D grid over the work list; `bs == 1` bypasses the plan. The plan is built once per forward (cached on the `seq_lens` / `cu_seqlens_q` tensors, cleared at the start of every forward, keyed on the stream-capturing flag).
- `vattn3_core.s`: kernarg 128 -> 136 B (`plan_ptr`); the prologue decodes `(seq, seg)` from the work list and exits on `-1` before touching memory; tiles per segment come from `plan[0]`.
- `vred.s`: kernarg 56 -> 64 B (`tok_nseg_ptr`); the reduce reads only that token's segment count.
- `unified_attention_3d_mtp.py` / `aiter_backend.py`: `reset_verify_attn_plan_cache()` called from `init_forward_metadata` and `init_forward_metadata_out_graph`.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/kernel/attention/test_vattn_segplan.py` (`stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`, 22 s on MI355X): 16 cases (GQA 16 and 8; uniform 16x70k; agentic skew including 0/1/5/17-token sequences; bs 1 / 2 / 24 / 64; ragged q 1..4) against an fp32 torch reference and against the fixed split. Same error vs. reference as the fixed split (max 0.0141 bf16 on the skew case, dominated by the fp8 KV); plan vs. fixed split differ by at most 0.007 (different fp32 reduction order across segment boundaries). Plan contents (`T`, work list, `tok_nseg`) checked against a Python reference in every case.
- same file, plan cache: 15 calls in one forward -> 1 plan launch; reset -> recompute; in-place `seq_lens` change or a different tensor -> recompute; cached output bit-identical to uncached.
- GSM8K, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, temperature 0, max new tokens 2048:

| Attention kernel | Accuracy |
|---|---:|
| baseline | 0.921 | 
| this PR | 0.924 | 

## Benchmarking and Profiling


| shape | Triton `unified_attention_3d_mtp` | asm, fixed split (#37465) | asm, this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| verify 16 x 119k uniform | 379 us (2.6 TB/s) | 176 us (5.5) | 176 us (5.5) |
| verify bs16, agentic length distribution, 1.85M tokens | 518 us (1.8) | 266 us (3.6) | 179 us (5.3) |
| verify bs20, agentic length distribution, 2.32M tokens | 516 us (2.3) | 482 us (2.5) | 254 us (4.7) |
| draft extend ragged q=1..4, bs20 agentic | 748 us (1.6) | 472 us (2.5) | 251 us (4.7) |
| bs1 110k / 248k | - | 44 / 79 us | same (bypass) |

End to end, InferenceX agentic recipe (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B MXFP4, MTP, aiperf trace replay; official harness mode: full aiperf, 3600 s, 10 warmups), MI355X, same tree and flags; off = fixed split of #37465, on = this PR. TP4 pairs ran one server at a time on the same GPUs; TP2 pairs ran off and on simultaneously on separate GPU pairs of the same node.

| point | TPOT p90 (ms) off | on | interactivity p90 (tok/s/user) off | on | throughput / GPU |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP2 c32 HiCache | 28.02 | 27.00 (-3.6%) | 35.7 | 37.0 (+3.6%) | +0.9% |
| TP2 c8 | 6.12 | 5.85 (-4.4%) | 163.5 | 170.9 (+4.5%) | +0.5% |
| TP4 c16 | 7.19 | 6.86 (-4.6%) | 139.1 | 145.8 (+4.8%) | +0.5% |
| TP4 c4 | 4.31 | 4.11 (-4.6%) | 231.9 | 243.5 (+5.0%) | 0.0% |

Server-side accept length is identical between off and on at every point (3.38-3.40). Same-tree A/B via a development-only switch that this PR does not ship. The p90 tail improves by 4-5% at every point (a long request joining a small batch no longer runs as 8 or fewer oversized segments); the median moves only at TP2 c32 (TPOT p50 12.47 -> 11.57 ms, -7.2%), where half of the decode steps are at bs 17-30 and the fixed split degrades. A same-configuration repeat on this replay differs by about 0.8%.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit guide.
- [x] Add unit tests (`test/registered/kernel/attention/test_vattn_segplan.py`).
- [ ] Update documentation.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.

title: [Perf] Fuse the glm5_next mHC attn->MLP boundary
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

GLM-5.3-Flash crosses 90 mHC post-then-pre boundaries per forward (45 layers, twice each). Each ran as three launches — `mhc_post`, the tf32 pre-norm GEMM, `mhc_pre_big_fuse` — which at a 6-token verify batch is launch cost, not work.

`mhc_fused_post_pre` and `apply_mhc_post_pre_boundary` already exist and are live for DeepSeek-V4. `glm5_next` never called them: it routes through `MHCLayerCommunicator`, not DeepSeek-V4's layer code.

## Modifications

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `MHCState.hc_ffn_post_pre` | optional callable tried first in `attn_to_mlp`; `None` keeps the unfused chain |
| `Glm5NextDecoderLayer.hc_ffn_post_pre` | GLM adapter onto the shared dispatcher |
| `_MHC_FUSED_BOUNDARY_MAX_TOKENS = 16` | conservative cap; declines above it |

Folds `mhc_post` into the pre-norm GEMM — `mhc_pre_big_fuse` still launches separately, so **two launches instead of three**. 45 of 90 boundaries fuse; the rest need DeepSeek-V4's cross-layer deferral. `fn_transpose=True` matches DeepSeek-V4's call sites but is read only by the ROCm Triton tier, so it is unexercised on CUDA. Scope is `glm5_next` with `mhc=True` (config default is `False`).

## Why 16

CUDA-graph replays, GLM-5.3-Flash's `hc_mult=4` / `hidden_size=4096`:

| tokens | ≤6 | 8–16 | 24 | 32 | ≥33 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DeepGEMM on | 1.40x | 1.17x | 1.00x | 0.88x | 1.00x |
| DeepGEMM off | 1.37x | 1.17x | 1.00x | 0.87x | **0.21x** |

Past the crossover the fused pre-norm GEMM drops the split-K kernel `mhc_pre` uses to 2048 tokens. 16 is conservative — parity is at 24, 17–23 unmeasured. The gate is in the GLM callback, not the shared dispatcher, which also serves DeepSeek-V4 at `hc_hidden_size=28672` — these numbers cover one shape on one hardware config.

Verify batch is `bs * speculative_num_draft_tokens`: c=1 is 6 tokens and fuses, c=64 is 384 and declines.

## Accuracy Tests

GPQA Diamond, thinking on: **92.42%** (183/198), 0 truncated, 0 errors. `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `max_tokens=131072`, 1 repeat.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GLM-5.3-Flash, tp4 on 4x GB300, 8192 in / 1024 out at c=1. 12 runs: 3 per arm across 4 server sessions, arms interleaved. The metric is verify steps per second, tok/s divided by accept length — the decode-loop rate, which is what a per-forward change moves. Raw tok/s scales with accept length, which clusters per server process.

| session | fused | unfused | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **79.07** | 78.55 | +0.66% |
| 2 | **79.82** | 77.99 | +2.34% |

Faster in both, with each session's run ranges disjoint.

At c=64 the gate declines and throughput is unchanged: 3466.9 vs 3456.3 tok/s.

title: [Diffusion] Guard E2E/loading latency with runner-aware baselines
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

Require valid inference E2E and loading metrics for every diffusion CI case, including `run_perf_check=False`. Keep loading (process launch to all workers ready, excluding warmup) and inference E2E as independent guards; their sum is reporting-only. Realtime E2E covers the requested generation session, not only its final chunk.

## Changes

- Fail on missing, non-finite or non-positive measurements/baselines. Preserve failed measurements in the existing test reports.
- Stop repeated requests after a performance failure and retry only failed pytest items, with at most six retries. Two-H100 jobs additionally admit retries only if their estimated duration fits a 40-minute budget measured from job setup, leaving headroom within the existing 45-minute job timeout. Insufficient budget or retry exhaustion preserves failure; consistency failures remain non-retryable.
- Apply denoising tolerances by stage role, including serialized/disaggregated metrics.
- Refresh live PR labels during reruns so the fast-fail health check honors current labels rather than the original event payload.
- Populate observed per-GPU loading references and enable measured Qwen extra-high / LTX-2.5 performance checks.
- Keep explicit warmup frame counts and matched SANA/LTX-2.5 warmup shapes; warm up the mesh processor and avoid CUDA tensor formatting on the timestep debug path.
- Support test-only runner-prefix baseline overrides for DeepInfra B200 and the measured Cirrascale runner. Verda and unmatched runners retain the defaults. No global tolerance increase.

| B200 case | Default E2E | DeepInfra E2E | Cirrascale E2E | Tolerance |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Flux1 NVFP4 | 836.71 ms | 1334.16 ms | 1574.32 ms | 25%, unchanged |
| Qwen-Image-2512 NVFP4 | 9650.06 ms | 16126.87 ms | 17742.04 ms | 25%, unchanged |

The DeepInfra values are medians of three warmed, unprofiled requests per case at the same CI merge commit and original case configuration. Cirrascale overrides match only `b200-cirrascale1-0123` and use the minimum recorded E2E for each case from historical same-configuration CI, not the slow outliers. These overrides do not change loading, stage/step/memory limits or other cases. Sources and calibration boundaries are documented in `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/runner/PERFORMANCE.md`.

## Scope

Temporary process/GPU diagnostic sampling, its workflow uploads and diagnostic-only tests have been removed. This PR keeps the metric guards, necessary runtime fixes, calibrated test data and regression coverage. It does not claim a completed root-cause analysis of the Qwen runner-pool performance difference.

## Validation

- At `1f5fcc112b54101994dbea310a192c9f130c18bf`, 125 focused tests plus one real nested-pytest retry-exhaustion integration test passed in an isolated Linux development environment. These results apply to that commit, not the later merged head.
- At `f148cf5fd0a594eb156af94bb1b888895e46eefa`, 18 focused failure-policy tests passed remotely, including two retry-exhaustion integration variants; seven other variants were deselected.
- Current-head [diffusion unit CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35450227723/job/105916085933) passed: 3136 tests, 113 skipped and 332 subtests.
- Actual two-H100 CI exercised both budget outcomes: [partition 0](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35450227723/job/105916108966) retained its four loading failures when the estimated retry would not fit; [partition 1](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35450227723/job/105916108989) retried only three failed items and passed. This verifies the retry behavior, not that all model checks pass.

Full current-head Base CI is not yet green; loading and separate Base failures remain under follow-up. No blanket CI-pass claim is made.

title: [Fix] Don't write conv state from the fused KDA verify kernel
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

`fused_kda_conv_gating_verify` rolled the conv state back into `conv_state` at the end of the kernel. Every V tile loads that same Q/K conv history at entry, but only `i_v == 0` writes it, so a tile scheduled in a later wave reads what the owner already overwrote.

The writeback is also dead: verify is speculative, and the commit scatter sets `conv_state` from the selected intermediate window. `accept_lens` is at least 1, so `last_correct_step_indices` is never negative for a real request and the scatter always overwrites.

So the stores are removed rather than guarded. `conv_state` and the SSM state are read-only in verify.

## Modifications

| | |
| --- | --- |
| kernel | drop the 9 `tl.store(cs_base, ...)` at the end of `fused_kda_conv_gating_verify_kernel` |
| docstring | state ownership: conv and SSM state are read-only, the commit scatter advances them |
| tests | `conv_state` must come back untouched; output must not vary with CTA scheduling |

Reached only with `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_KDA_VERIFY=1` (default off), on the KDA Triton verify path at `topk == 1`.

## How the race shows

H=1 with HV=16, so 16 V tiles share one Q/K history. Same inputs, against the unfused pair:

| | max abs | max rel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| full GB300, one wave | 2.98e-8 | 7.2e-3 |
| 8-SM green context, waves serialized | **5.0e-2** | **188** |

Removing the stores makes both configurations identical. The residual ~1 ulp is reduction-order difference and is unaffected by the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

Ling-3.0-flash BF16, 4x GB300 TP4, NEXTN, fused verify on. Full GSM8K, thinking on, `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `max_tokens=8192`, 1 repeat.

| | score | stop | error |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | 96.06% | 99.70% | 0.00% |
| after | 95.83% | 99.17% | 0.00% |

Unchanged — the gap is inside the ~0.55pp 1-sigma band at n=1319. The race is below eval resolution when the grid fits one wave.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same server, 8192 in / 1024 out at concurrency 1, 64 warmup, `--flush-cache`, 3 runs per arm. Accept length 3.01 on all six.

| | runs (tok/s) | mean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before | 355.23, 361.47, 363.72 | 360.14 |
| after | 370.64, 369.38, 375.18 | **371.73** |

**+3.22%**, arms disjoint. The kernel does strictly less work with the stores gone.

## Checklist

- [x] `pre-commit` clean
- [x] 9 cases in `test_fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py`; all 9 fail against the unfixed kernel
- [x] Accuracy and speed measured above

title: [Perf] trtllm_mla: reuse the fused fp8 KV/Q prepare on target verify
author: zhendonghua
body:
## Motivation

Closes #39107.

`TRTLLMMLABackend.forward_decode` already fuses the fp8 no-RoPE preparation (bf16 -> fp8 quantize + KV scatter + `[q_nope | q_rope]` concat) into one `set_mla_kv_concat_q_fp8` launch. Target verify dispatches through `forward_extend`, which on the same inputs still ran the unfused chain unconditionally: `concat_mla_absorb_q` + three aten fp8 casts + the pool's Triton scatter, i.e. five launches per MLA layer instead of one. This is the `cos_sin_cache is None` case, hit by MLA models with no RoPE on the absorbed path (Kimi K3, `skip_rope=True`); RoPE models take the flashinfer `mla_rope_quantize_fp8` path and are unaffected.

Nothing about the fused kernel is decode-specific: it is per-token / per-(token, head), its q/k row strides are runtime parameters, and the capture-stable write loc (`_decode_kernel_loc`) is already filled for `TARGET_VERIFY` under the unified pool. `CuteDslMLABackend` and `TokenspeedMLABackend` inherit `forward_extend`, so their verify takes the same path (including Kimi K3's default DCP config, which routes verify to cutedsl_mla via `speculative_attention_mode="decode"`).

## Modifications

- `forward_extend`, fp8 + `is_target_verify()` + `cos_sin_cache is None`: try the same guarded fused prepare as decode (`save_kv_cache` and `_fused_set_kv_concat_q_fp8` on, `_resolve_fused_write_loc` yields a loc, `covered_fp8` accepts). On success the pool write and the concat are skipped; otherwise the existing `mla_quantize_without_rope_for_fp8` + `set_mla_kv_buffer` chain runs unchanged. No new kernel and no change to the static gate: this is the dispatch fix from the issue, on the existing CUDA JIT kernel.
- New `test/registered/kernel/attention/test_trtllm_mla_fp8_prepare.py`, on the same bare-backend fixture as `TestFusedFp8WriteGate`: `forward_extend` in `TARGET_VERIFY` takes the fused prepare, writes at the capture-stable loc under a translating pool, and keeps the unfused chain with the gate off, pinned to the aten fp8 reference for the pool rows and the query. The pool's writer is a stand-in that refuses on the fused branch and writes on the fallback.

## Accuracy Tests

The fused kernel produces byte-identical rows and query to the aten chain (`test_kimi_k3_prerequisite_ops` already pins that at batch 64); the new test pins the same contract on the verify path. Draft: the GPU tests have not been run locally yet, and a Kimi K3 + trtllm_mla + fp8 KV + MTP accuracy run is still pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Launch count on the verify prepare drops from 5 to 1 per MLA layer. #39107 reports about 1.8% TPOT on a B300 TP8 dummy Kimi K3 with MTP1 for the same dispatch change; real-weight numbers to follow.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (n/a)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (pending)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: perf(sampling): avoid GPU syncs when applying custom logit processors
author: draftbk
body:
Cache CPU request rows and GPU indices to avoid synchronization when applying custom logit processors. ### Latency Qwen3.5-0.8B · B200 · BF16 · batch size 1 · greedy + token ban. Profiler off; 10 requests × 128 output tokens per version. | Metric | Before | After | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Time to first token | 18.60 ms | 17.59 ms | | Inter-token latency | 2.41 ms | 1.35 ms | Median across requests (ITL: median of per-request means). Outputs matched. ### Profile One decode call's CPU duration, batch size 1. Different zoom levels; not end-to-end latency. **Before: 1.253 ms** **After: 0.125 ms** ### GSM8K 200 prompts, continuous batching up to 16 requests, mixed processors. 5-shot, non-thinking, greedy, 4,096-token output limit. | Result | Before | After | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Accuracy, no processor | 107/200 (53.5%) | 107/200 (53.5%) | | Accuracy, mixed processors | 107/200 (53.5%) | 107/200 (53.5%) | | Ban violations | 0 | 0 | | Outputs reaching limit, each run | 9 | 9 | **200/200 output sequences matched exactly** in each comparison (71,675 tokens per mode).
Test details - 84 sampling tests and pre-commit passed. CUDA regression covers widths 1 and 3; restoring the original sampler makes it fail. - Baseline: `7ae4af8`. Latency/profile: `cedd50f`; GSM8K: `91579c1`. Latency was not rerun after subsequent refactors. - Latency: Engine API including IPC, excluding HTTP; two warmups, prefix cache cleared per request. Triton attention, CUDA graphs and overlap enabled. Workload-specific results. - GSM8K: Engine driver using SGLang's answer extraction; first 200 test questions, five training examples. Four groups of 50: no processor, ban ` eggs`, same processor banning ` dollars`, second processor banning both. IDs: `18237`, `10867`. Only one control request emitted an assigned banned token; this does not establish general accuracy neutrality of bans. - Dependencies differ from repository pins: Torch `2.13.0a0+8145d630e8.nv26.6.54250401`, Transformers `5.15.1`, FlashInfer `0.6.18`, Triton `3.7.0+gitb7fa781f.nv26.6`.
### Breaking change `index_copy_` writes the processor's result back row for row, so a `CustomLogitProcessor` must return a tensor with as many rows as it was given. Assignment through a boolean mask broadcast, so a processor returning a reduced shape such as `(1, vocab)` worked before and now raises at decode time. Both built-in processors return full-shape logits and are unaffected; only third-party processors that relied on broadcasting need updating. `CustomLogitProcessor.__call__` states the requirement. ### Implementation A processor, the CPU list of batch rows it applies to and the device copy of those rows are held together in one `ProcessorEntry`, so `from_schedule_batch`, `filter_batch`, `merge_batch` and the sampler each read and update a single mapping. - `merge_batch` concatenates the two index tensors on the device rather than rebuilding one through pinned host memory: 60us -> 49us per merge at batch size 128, with the host copies gone from the profile. - `filter_batch` builds one old-to-new position map per call instead of rescanning `keep_indices` once per processor key. - Before applying anything, the sampler checks that the cached rows and indices agree and that `custom_params` covers the batch. - Speculative-decoding token offsets are built on the batch info's device, the one the row indices they are combined with live on. The CUDA coverage lives at `test/registered/kernels/ops/sampling/test_apply_custom_logit_processor.py`. Its module basename differs from the CPU unit test of the same subsystem, which pytest requires when both are collected. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #35310994662](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35310994662) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #35310994429](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35310994429) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #35310994582](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35310994582)

title: [Perf] weight-sync: Allocate packed receive buffers from metadata
author: zianglih
body:
## Motivation

@humansand

Packed distributed weight updates allocate every destination tensor and concatenate their uninitialized bytes immediately before the broadcast overwrites that buffer. Allocate the receive buffer directly from metadata to remove the discarded concatenation and temporary tensor allocations.

- **Roadmap:** [Miles #3734 — NVFP4 weight update enhancements](https://github.com/radixark/miles/issues/3734) tracks the broader weight-sync work.
- **Merged counterpart:** [SGLang #39265](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39265) merged the corresponding receiver-allocation optimization into `sglang-miles`. This PR brings it to `main`.

## Modifications

- **Allocation:** add `FlattenedTensorBucket.empty(names, dtypes, shapes, device)` to allocate one contiguous uint8 receive buffer. Preserve sender byte offsets, dtype, shape, and shared-storage reconstruction.
- **Activation:** use the factory only for distributed updates requesting `load_format="flattened_bucket"`. Ordinary per-tensor updates and tensor IPC are unchanged. This optimization is not specific to NVFP4.
- **Validation:** reject inconsistent metadata lengths, negative dimensions, empty metadata, and offsets incompatible with dtype alignment. Keep the existing wire format without padding or dtype promotion.
- **Lifecycle:** preserve the single broadcast, target-runner receive, selected-runner loading, and separate begin/restore and end/postprocess operations. No loader, quantization, or collective-group changes.
- **Scope:** two commits and three changed files, directly based on upstream `main` at `86cc2e02ecb207853377e2c034337e9e0442ce60`. Validated head: `8e987e1256ada5575245fa47a75cecce340c1a9f`. Both feature and CI-entry-point patches are unchanged by rebase. Full-model weight-sync benefit remains unmeasured.

## Accuracy Tests

**Current-head validation (2026-10-16):** macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Python 3.12.12, PyTorch 2.14.1, pytest 9.1.1. CPU only; no container or GPU used.

- Strict CI discovery passed for all 2,408 registered files / 2,937 registrations. The test has an executable `__main__` entry point that propagates pytest exit status; running the actual file with CI's `-f` argument executes all six tests successfully.
- Six registered tests passed: mixed uint8/FP8/FP32/BF16 bytes, dtype objects/strings, scalar/empty shapes, signed zero/infinity/NaN payloads, reconstruction aliases, and invalid metadata.
- Four bounded receiver cases passed using the actual receiver method body and an intercepted broadcast. They check one broadcast, exact bytes/names/shapes/dtypes, shared storage, and receive-only behavior.
- The CPU test launcher bypasses only top-level `sglang/__init__.py` bootstrap; the production bucket, test module, and CI registration are unchanged. The receiver harness extracts the actual method through AST. Neither qualifies full serving imports, GPU/NCCL, or model-loader integration.
- All configured pre-commit hooks applicable to the three changed files passed without edits: pre-commit 4.5.1, isort 7.0.0, Ruff 0.15.1, codespell 2.4.1, and repository CI-registration checks. Syntax compilation and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Upstream CI fix included:** [#44843](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44843) resizes the allocator before allocating backed pages in `test_unified_post_capture_sizing.py`, addressing the unrelated CUDA test failure seen in the preceding hosted run. Current-head GPU validation is pending.
- The receiver implementation preserves upstream byte layout and receive/load lifecycle. The registered test also satisfies the CI runner's script-entry-point contract. The title passes the current repository validator.

title: [AMD] [GLM-5.3-Flash] Enable FP8 and MXFP4 serving on gfx950
author: hdt98
body:
## Motivation Serve the official GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 checkpoint and [`OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4`](https://huggingface.co/OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4) on MI355X (gfx950) at full speed and correct output. The target stack is zero-RoPE sparse attention, FP8 KV cache, and graph-enabled EAGLE 5/1/6. `main` now includes all ten Day-0 enablement PRs (#38545, #38546, #38547, #39317, #39338, #39339, #39340, #39341, #39778, #39779). This PR adds the remaining correctness fixes and optimizations for serving Flash on gfx950. On the same four MI355X GPUs and AgentX replay, it measures **+14.3%** geomean output throughput over `main` at c1–c32, with higher P90 interactivity at every rung. At c48, `main` falls off the frontier, while this PR holds it. The four CI and test-hygiene fixes that used to be here now live in #40721. ## What changed Runtime paths are relative to `python/sglang/`; tests are excluded. | Area | Kind | Change | Files | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | K-pool top-k | Correctness (CUDA and HIP) | A threshold bin holding more than 4,096 candidates is rescanned with unique score/index keys, so ties or late higher scores are never clipped. The ordinary fast path is unchanged. HIP sets the dynamic shared-memory attribute. | `kernels/jit/csrc/dsa/kpool_topk_transform.cuh` | | K-pool scoring memory | Correctness · HIP | The logits row budget counts AITER's 256-column row padding, so a chunk cannot exceed AITER's 2 GiB limit, and page indices are promoted to int64 before offsetting. | `srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer_kpool.py`
`srt/layers/attention/dsa/kpool_fp8_index.py` | | Unfused top-k memory | Correctness · all backends | Ragged batches above 4,096 rows run in 4,096-row chunks (`_TOPK_ROW_CHUNK`). Each row's top-k depends only on that row, so results are identical on every backend; only the scratch peak changes. | `srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_topk_backend.py` | | Graph variants | Correctness / capture cost | K-pool has no dense-skip path, so it is captured once instead of as a dense/sparse pair. Without a host length mirror, sparse is chosen without a device sync. | `srt/layers/attention/graph_variants.py` | | Attention backend lookup | Correctness | GLM-5.3-Flash wraps DSA inside the hybrid KDA backend, so on `main` the FP8 MHA prefix read takes the outer backend and fails with `forward_metadata is None` on the first image request (reproduced on MI355X). `resolve_attn_backend` now unwraps to the full-attention child. AITER extend also prefers the per-batch `qo_indptr`. | `srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py`
`srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py` | | Visible-prefix / Mamba ownership | Correctness | A verify step can commit past the stop token; only client-visible tokens are cached. The other ping-pong slot's length is tracked, so a shorter key donates the state that actually matches it. Freed rows can no longer scatter into a reused slot. | `srt/managers/schedule_batch.py`
`srt/managers/scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py`
`srt/mem_cache/{base_prefix_cache,common,memory_pool}.py`
`srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/components/mamba.py` | | Mamba chunk fill | Correctness | Exact chunk fill is disabled for Mamba caches, because checkpoints only land on page-aligned chunk ends. | `srt/managers/schedule_policy.py` | | Graph read fences | Correctness | Without an in-graph marker (HIP), the read-done event is published after replay rather than before. Draft extend follows the backend's declared read end. | `srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`
`srt/speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py` | | EAGLE draft on ROCm | Optimization · measured | ROCm enables rejection sampling (#37134), but verify takes argmax for all-greedy batches and never reads the draft distribution. The draft now skips the full-vocab softmax, Gumbel sample and probs stack for those batches and captures a matching greedy graph variant. | `srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py`
`srt/speculative/eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py` | | KDA fused verify | Correctness + optimization · HIP only | On top of #39524: separately rounded conv products (bit-exact with the reference on gfx950), a one-wave default, and BV16 for measured GLM shapes. The HIP gate keys on gfx950, bf16 QKV, fp32 conv weights, T ∈ {6, 8}, and batch 1–16. | `kernels/ops/attention/fla/fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py`
`srt/layers/attention/linear/kda_backend.py` | | Chat serving | Optimization / correctness | Send the token ids already rendered instead of re-tokenizing long text-only prompts. Apply the GLM47 full-assistant grammar only when tools are present, since its terminal state ends requests even under `ignore_eos`. | `srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py` | | Quark loading | Correctness | Block-FP8 is claimed only when the activation grouping matches the weight block. `ignore` is materialized once. Quark `weight_scale` maps to `weight_scale_inv` only when the name is missing. | `srt/layers/quantization/quark/{quark,utils}.py`
`srt/models/glm5_next.py` | | Vision downsample | Optimization · measured | The non-overlapping 2×2 merge uses `Conv2dLayer`'s unfold + linear path, which avoids the MIOpen search. | `srt/models/glm5_next.py` | | Small ROCm fixes | Correctness | `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only` accepts any GPU device (`kDLGPU`), and a comment in the AITER MoE runner is corrected. | `kernels/jit/csrc/speculative/sampling.cuh`
`srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/aiter.py` | | MI355X cookbook | Docs | FP8 and MXFP4 on the GLM-5.3-Flash selector, with TP4/EP4 commands and the ROCm runtime environment used for the measurements below. | `docs/cookbook/autoregressive/GLM/GLM-5.3-Flash.mdx`
`docs/src/snippets/configs/zai-org/glm-5.3-flash.jsx`
`docs/src/snippets/_playground.jsx` | Footprint against `main`: 26 production files (+361 / −80), 14 test files (+563 / −21), 3 docs files (+179 / −26). ## Serving performance Setup: four MI355X VFs, TP4/EP4, FP8 E4M3 KV, EAGLE 5/1/6, 393-entry AgentX corpus, 900 s per rung, image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.20-rocm724-mi35x-20260918`. The client and server are pinned to the same NUMA placement, and `main` and this PR ran back to back on the same GPUs.
Serving command (identical for both arms; only the source differs) ```bash SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_ONLINE_TUNE=0 \ SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_KDA_VERIFY=1 SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK=0 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=false \ SGLANG_ENABLE_WAR_BARRIER=1 SGLANG_FORCE_COARSE_WAR_BARRIER=1 \ HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1 ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=NONE \ PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4 \ --tp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --quantization quark --trust-remote-code \ --context-length 262144 --page-size 64 --mem-fraction-static 0.82 \ --max-running-requests 96 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 96 --min-free-slots-delay 1 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 --prefill-decode-interval 0 \ --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \ --linear-attn-verify-backend triton --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --moe-runner-backend aiter \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 --speculative-attention-mode prefill \ --speculative-accept-threshold-single 1.0 --speculative-accept-threshold-acc 1.0 \ --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant --speculative-moe-a2a-backend none \ --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 0.50 --hicache-write-policy write_through \ --hicache-io-backend direct --hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct \ --reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 --mm-feature-transport cpu ``` Transformers is pinned to `e4052f55` for the GLM-5.3-Flash configuration classes.
| Concurrency | This PR tok/s | `main` tok/s | vs `main` | This PR P90 tok/s/user | `main` P90 tok/s/user | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 252.9 | 237.9 | +6.3% | 374.4 | 365.0 | | 2 | 443.2 | 394.6 | +12.3% | 337.5 | 326.1 | | 4 | 768.7 | 657.2 | +17.0% | 293.1 | 287.5 | | 8 | 1,253.1 | 1,137.4 | +10.2% | 237.1 | 226.8 | | 16 | 1,849.9 | 1,608.5 | +15.0% | 172.4 | 157.8 | | 32 | 2,304.8 | 1,829.2 | +26.0% | 111.0 | 94.7 | | 48 | 2,411.3 | off frontier | — | 78.1 | off frontier | Geomean output throughput: **+14.3%** over `main` at c1–c32. P90 tok/s/user is the 90th percentile of each request's reciprocal mean inter-token latency. ![AgentX frontier on four MI355X GPUs: this PR vs main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/34d8e433-a9c8-41f0-a492-96cd51fe3610) ### Checkpoint and hardware context These replays were measured at `5fd4387a75`, before the Day-0 merges; this PR's head matches that source within run-to-run noise on the same AgentX ladder. Against the official `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` FP8 checkpoint on the same four-GPU MI355X serving policy, OneNexus MXFP4 measures **+12.4%** geomean output throughput and **+18.2%** geomean P90 per-user rate over c1–c48, with zero request errors in both runs. This compares complete checkpoints, not an isolated quantization kernel. ![Measured OneNexus MXFP4 versus official FP8 AgentX frontiers on four MI355X VFs](https://huggingface.co/OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4/resolve/main/assets/fp8-mxfp4-agentx-frontier.png) Against `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` under the identical serving setup, OneNexus is within 0.1% geomean output throughput and +1.0% geomean P90 per-user rate over c1–c48 (9,223 vs 9,264 requests, zero errors in both).
OneNexus vs AMD MXFP4, per rung | Concurrency | OneNexus tok/s | AMD tok/s | Output delta | OneNexus P90 tok/s/user | AMD P90 tok/s/user | P90 delta | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 261.76 | 258.89 | +1.1% | 379.08 | 364.96 | +3.9% | | 2 | 444.88 | 444.09 | +0.2% | 333.60 | 330.21 | +1.0% | | 4 | 764.52 | 769.09 | −0.6% | 295.25 | 297.03 | −0.6% | | 8 | 1,283.08 | 1,278.38 | +0.4% | 241.23 | 237.75 | +1.5% | | 16 | 1,845.35 | 1,857.38 | −0.6% | 178.88 | 179.39 | −0.3% | | 32 | 2,279.72 | 2,290.16 | −0.5% | 110.35 | 110.00 | +0.3% | | 48 | 2,331.22 | 2,340.38 | −0.4% | 74.85 | 73.89 | +1.3% |
The next plot places the measured MI355X MXFP4 frontier next to **supplied four-GPU B300 estimates**. The B300 runs were not reproduced here, and the DSA backend and serving installation differ, so this is context rather than a controlled cross-hardware claim. ![Measured OneNexus MXFP4 MI355X frontier and supplied B300 estimate](https://huggingface.co/OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4/resolve/main/assets/final-agentx-frontier.png) The [matched serving protocol](https://huggingface.co/OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4/blob/main/reproduction/fp8-mxfp4-agentx-protocol.md) has per-rung cache, capacity and acceptance data. ## Measured operator optimizations **KDA fused verify.** At batch 8 with eight verification tokens, the reference graph launches convolution and recurrence separately (**38.9 μs**). The single fused kernel with BV4 tiles is slower (**41.7 μs**), because it repeats the Q/K convolution across 32 value tiles. BV16 cuts the grid to 8 tiles and the paired time to **28.4 μs**, **27.0% less operator time**. For the six-token EAGLE 5/1/6 shape: **31.50 → 23.02 μs** at batch 8 and **37.66 → 33.03 μs** at batch 16. On this PR's head, the tuning still measures about 26% faster at batch 8 on top of #39524, with bit-exact output. ![KDA before/after GPU traces and paired graph timings: reference, initial fusion, and tuned fusion](https://huggingface.co/OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4/resolve/main/assets/kda-trace-optimization.png) This is an isolated MI350X VF (gfx950) study with synthetic GLM TP4-shaped tensors, not model throughput. See the [study and full data](https://huggingface.co/OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4/blob/main/reproduction/kda-trace-study.md). **Vision merge.** The 2×2 downsample has a non-overlapping kernel and stride, no padding and one group, so each patch is a linear projection. See the [operator study](https://huggingface.co/OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4/blob/main/reproduction/mhc-vision-operator-study.md). title: [dsv4.1] Exact bf16 consumer top-k adapted from DeepSelect
author: DarkSharpness
body:
## Motivation

The DeepSeek-V4.1 two-level sparse indexer's consumer step picks the top-512 of up to 16384 bf16 sparse logits per row and writes them through the per-row physical block table (`topk_transform_bf16_small`). The kernel behind it was a placeholder: a single 13-bit fp16-derived histogram (approximate at the selection boundary), 1024 threads x 16 elements, and untuned.

## Modifications

Replace it with an exact selection **adapted from [DeepSelect](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSelect)**. DeepSelect's kernel starts by selecting the top-k of a 32 KiB "init window" that lives entirely in registers; our consumer rows (<= 16384 bf16) are exactly that window, so our kernel agent took that part of the algorithm, dropped the TMA/streaming machinery around it, rewrote it in plain SIMT and specialised it for 16384-wide rows at k = 512. The result was then reviewed and wired into the existing host API here.

What is kept from DeepSelect:
- two radix passes on the raw bf16 bytes: a 256-bin histogram of the high byte, then of the low byte among the elements sharing the pivot's high byte, which locates the k-th largest value exactly;
- the "distorted" value order (`x ^ (x < 0 ? 0xFFFF : 0x8000)`: negatives reversed and below positives, -0 below +0), applied once per lane while walking the histogram instead of once per element;
- the packed hit test: `__hgt2_mask` / `__heq2_mask` on bf16x2, `prmt` + `dp4a` to turn the flags into one bit per element, one warp prefix plus one shared atomic per warp for the block-wide (gt, eq) prefix, and an equal quota so exactly k elements are taken.

What is specific to this port:
- one CTA of 512 threads per row, each thread keeping a contiguous slice of up to 32 scores (4 x 16 B vectors) in registers for the whole kernel; 40 registers per thread, 3 CTAs per SM, no spills;
- the negative half of the high-byte histogram is offset by 16 words so that +x and -x with the same exponent (the common case for centred scores) do not hit the same smem bank on every atomic;
- the partial last vector of a row is padded with a negative NaN, which sits below -inf in the distorted order and fails every ordered compare, so it is never counted nor selected;
- a -0 pivot is handled separately (the float census sees +0 == -0 while the histogram ranked them apart);
- the selected indices are staged in shared memory (a union with the histograms, 9 KiB in total) and written with one coalesced page-transformed copy.

The host API is unchanged: per-row `seq_lens` (prefetched ahead of the PDL wait, like the streaming top-k), the fused page-table transform, `-1` past `min(k, seq_len)`. `k` is now at most 2048 (was 4096). NaN scores are never selected (no ordered compare matches them): a row with n positive NaNs yields its top (k - n) real scores and `-1` in the remaining slots, derived from the census totals so nothing reads stale shared memory; a negative NaN orders below `-inf` and is simply never picked.

## Accuracy

`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_topk_bf16.py` (100 cases): the existing configurations plus odd row widths (partial last vector), heavy ties / constant / all `-inf` rows, signed zeros around the pivot, denormals and full-range bf16 bit patterns, and rows with positive / negative NaNs below and above k. Every case checks the selected values as a multiset against `torch.topk` (elements of equal value may swap) and the page transform through the inverse table. `test/registered/attention/unittests/dsv4/test_dsv41_sparse_indexer.py` passes.

## Performance

B200, `marker.do_bench` (CUDA graph, L2-rotated inputs), k = 512, page transform included, random bf16 scores, permuted block table. Old kernel -> this PR, in us:

| valid len | rows = 1 | rows = 32 | rows = 128 | rows = 512 |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 16384 | 5.24 -> 4.93 | 5.51 -> 5.18 | 7.09 -> 6.58 | 15.94 -> 12.38 |
| 9000 | 4.36 -> 4.06 | 4.71 -> 4.36 | 5.08 -> 5.07 | 13.03 -> 9.03 |
| 4096 | 3.97 -> 3.49 | 4.32 -> 3.81 | 4.74 -> 4.32 | 10.83 -> 7.36 |

Beyond ~450 rows the GPU is saturated (3 CTAs/SM) and time is linear in rows: 36 us at 2048 rows and 134 us at 8192 rows for full-width rows.

k = 2048 stays supported but is not the target shape: it is 10-15% slower than the old kernel at small batch (the epilogue runs on 512 threads instead of 1024) and 10% faster at 512 rows.

title: fuse shared experts with routed experts in MegaMoE's DeepGEMM
author: xikronz
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->
for #38700 (* - *)

## Motivation
<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
Context: Deepseek-v4-pro uses DeepseekMoE (served as MegaMoE) as its mixure of experts with a shared expert that is activated across all tokens and a fine-grained routed experts. 
- flash model: 1 shared + 256 routed
- pro model: 1 shared + 384 routed 
>Note that the authors also chose to use FP4 with QAT such that routed expert weights are in MXFP4 while all other parameters (including the shared expert in the official checkpoints) stay in blockwise fp8 format. 

For each token $t_i$ , a V4 MoE layer does two different GEMM operations:
1. shared - dense MLP on every token (in FP8)
2. routed - grouped GEMM over the top 6 selected experts (MXFP4)

Launching each kernel independently wastes launches and stream syncs on every layer (this is true even if they shared a dtype). DeepGEMM already caught this and added native MegaMoE support via (num_shared_experts, separate shared_l1/shared_l2 weights, mixed FP8 and MXFP4).

The existing Sglang fusion logic in `deepseek-v2.py` 
```python
        # num_fused_shared_experts drives weight remapping in deepseek_weight_loader:
        # mlp.shared_experts → mlp.experts.256 when > 0.
        self.num_fused_shared_experts = 0 if _fusion_disabled else n_shared_experts
```
only works if shared and routed share a dtype/layout (from `deepseel-v4.py`):
```python 
        # Need to disable if quant precision mismatch, even if
        # --enforce-shared-experts-fusion is specified
        if quant_blocks_shared_experts_fusion(quant_config):
            return (
                "Quantization keeps shared experts at a higher precision than the "
                "routed experts, so they cannot be fused into the quantized "
                "routed-expert path."
            )
```
but the official deepseek-ai checkpoints do not, so that path does not apply on MegaMoE (it can still run on the trtllm-gen runner if you `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` and requantize shared FP8→MXFP4, which is what #35505 did)

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

Changes mainly in mega_moe.py: 
This PR went through a lot of iterations, starting with a naive index implementation that was supposed to be easier to maintain and more local w.r.t. number of files changed. The memory and throughput overhead of maintaining a python cache of expert indices was pretty bad (as seen below) which motivated for a kernel level change in `mega_moe_predispatch.cuh`. 

Placing the FP8 shared expert inside routed MegaMoE (removing six standalone kernels per layer) does this but it regressed throughput because it bypassed the existing alternate-stream fork in `mega_moe.py`. In the unfused profiles, the shared expert’s second GEMM overlapped with the routed MegaMoE in 184/184 observed calls per rank, covering a median 94.1–95.6% of its duration. Naively fusing the path without modifying `forward_mega_moe()` function returned before the existing alternate-stream fork, leaving the whole router/top-k/pre-dispatch/MegaMoE region on the current stream...

```python
  if moe.mega_shared_l1_weights is not None:
          return _run_mega_routed(
              moe, hidden_states, forward_batch, input_ids_global, num_tokens
          )
  
      sbo_overlap_flag = (
          moe.alt_stream is not None
          and moe.num_fused_shared_experts == 0
          and num_tokens > 0
          and get_is_capture_mode()
      )
```

The current iteration of this PR keeps the same kernel changes but forks the whole fused region in `forward_mega_moe()` which lets other graph work overlap it; at BS1, main, kernel-only, and kernel-plus-fork achieved 756.90, 721.97, and 759.08 tok/s.

Major files changes:
1. `_get_mega_moe_symm_buffer` includes `num_shared_experts` in its cache key and allocates the shared-expert buffer for the fused configuration
2. `_run_mega_routed` forwards the shared-expert count and transformed L1/L2 weights through gate and top-k to `run_mega_routed_experts`
3. `run_mega_routed_experts` selects the consuming MegaMoE `BLOCK_M`, passes the shared-scale destination to pre-dispatch, and launches `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` with the shared weights
4. `forward_mega_moe` forks the entire fused router/top-k/pre-dispatch/MegaMoE region onto the existing alternate stream during CUDA-graph capture and joins before returning

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

Accuracy evals are run on `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` with the bundled DSpark draft via 4x B300 (SM103) with sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.7. On GPTQA-diamond with sgl-eval and thinking enabled, reasoning effort `max`, `max_tokens=200000`, and
`top_p=0.95`: 

| Workload | n | main | fusion index (no kernel) | fusion kernel | fusion kernel + fork (PR) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Greedy accuracy | 198 | 0.899 | 0.894 | 0.883 | 0.897 |
| Greedy empty at cap | 198 | 8 | 4 | 8 | 8 |
| Sampled pass@1 | 792 | 0.900 | 0.922 | 0.910 | 0.910 |
| Parsing failure | 792 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Request failures | - | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

paired per-request comparison:

| Workload | Pair | Answer flips | main right, arm wrong | arm right, main wrong | One-sided empty answers |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Greedy | main vs fusion index | 14 | 2 | 8 | 6 |
| Greedy | main vs fusion kernel | 17 | 5 | 7 | 8 |
| Greedy | main vs fusion kernel + fork | 22 | 5 | 11 | 10 |
| Sampled | main vs fusion index | 50 | 11 | 28 | 0 |
| Sampled | main vs fusion kernel | 55 | 19 | 27 | 0 |

title: [AMD] [GLM-5.3-Flash Day 0] Honor fused and per-expert names in quark `exclude`
author: Raiden-Makoto
body:
## Summary

Replacement for #37673, which GitHub closed when its deleted support base was merged into main. The original author and review history remain credited there.

`amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` contains BF16 layers that are explicitly excluded from MXFP4 quantization. Without this change, weight loading can allocate an MXFP4-packed parameter for one of those BF16 tensors and abort in `load_qkv_weight` with a 2x width mismatch:

```text
AssertionError: param_data.shape=torch.Size([128, 512]),
                loaded_weight.shape=torch.Size([128, 1024])
```

`should_ignore_layer()` currently checks `exclude` only after rewriting a fused module name into its component shards. GLM-5.3-Flash uses two exclusion forms that do not survive that rewrite:

1. **Already-fused modules named directly.** The vision tower serializes `visual.blocks.N.attn.qkv_proj` as one tensor and excludes that fused name directly. Expanding it to `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` misses the exclusion.
2. **Per-expert MoE exclusions.** The checkpoint lists `model.layers.{3,5,6}.mlp.experts.{0..287}.{down,gate,up}_proj`, while SGLang constructs one fused `model.layers.N.mlp.experts` module.

Measured on the original checkpoint used for #37673:

```text
exclude entries total                     2552
  ... mentioning "experts"                1860
  ... per-expert (experts.<N>.<proj>)     1728   -> layers 3, 5 and 6 only
  ... mentioning "visual"                  125
```

The affected expert tensors confirm the packed-versus-unpacked boundary:

```text
layers.5.mlp.experts.0.down_proj.weight   BF16   (4096, 2048)     no weight_scale
layers.7.mlp.experts.0.down_proj.weight   U8     (4096, 1024)     + weight_scale
```

At TP8, 2048/8 = **256** while 1024/8 = **128**, matching the original assertion exactly.

## Scope

Two files only:

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/utils.py`: honor a direct fused-module exclusion before packed-module expansion, and treat a fused `...experts` module as excluded when its individual experts are excluded.
- `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_quark_utils.py`: add non-vacuous bug catchers for both exclusion forms and regression guards for empty excludes, shard-level excludes, and unrelated expert layers.

The existing packed-shard path is unchanged when no direct match exists. The per-expert rule applies to whole-layer expert exclusions; SGLang cannot represent a checkpoint that mixes quantization schemes among experts inside one fused MoE module. No kernel, model forward path, backend policy, scheduler behavior, environment variable, or checkpoint tensor is changed.

## Test plan

Combined main-based integration (`RM/glm53-day0-main-integration` @ `22f233a853`, fresh checkpoint-specific caches):

- TP4 `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4@b5688f2549` on MI355X/gfx950: **20/20 GSM8K (100.00%)**, 100.00% stop rate, 0.00% truncation, 0.00% errors.
- The server loaded all 62 shards, completed decode graph capture, and returned a correct stopped generation (`17 + 25 = 42`).

Recovery base: `main` @ `6220f45d8e`.  
Replacement head: `25b9f7f658`.  
Original head: `de98483df0`.  
Container: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.19-rocm724-mi35x-20260910` (`sha256:391afe1da11d`).  
Recovery validation on MI355X: scoped pre-commit passed; **15 unit tests passed**.

Original #37673 A/B validation used the same test cases in both arms:

| Arm | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline | Directly excluded fused QKV and per-expert-to-fused-MoE cases fail; all three regression guards pass. |
| This PR | Both bug catchers and all three guards pass. |

| Check | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Registration | Existing CPU unit-test location; no GPU kernel is introduced |
| Formatting | Scoped pre-commit passed, including Ruff, format, codespell, and registered-test validation |
| Unit tests | `test_quark_utils.py`: **15 passed** |
| Accuracy | TP4 MXFP4 integration smoke: **100.00% GSM8K (20 examples)** |
| Speed | Not measured; this restores checkpoint loading semantics and does not modify execution kernels |

None of the other recovered Day-0 PRs modifies `quark/utils.py`; this exclusion gap is independent of their DSA, k-pool, mHC, MoE-runner, and TileLang changes.

title: [AMD] [GLM-5.3-Flash Day 0] Build the fused DSA k-pool top-k JIT kernel on HIP
author: Jacob0226
body:
## Summary

GLM-5.3-Flash cannot run on ROCm: the kernel that picks its sparse-attention candidates fails to build under hipcc.

```text
fatal error: 'cuda_fp16.h' file not found
no member named 'cudaFuncSetAttribute' in the global namespace
```

Both come from the same file assuming CUDA. This is a hard stop rather than a slow path — GLM-5.3-Flash's pooled top-k has no other kernel to fall back to, so the indexer cannot run at all.

## Scope

Two edits, both inside `USE_ROCM` blocks that already exist: give the fp16 include a HIP arm, and add two names to the shim's alias list. Every CUDA line in the diff is unchanged context. No kernel body, launch configuration, tile size or numeric path moves; no environment variable, no architecture gate.

The kernel has no direct test on any platform — CUDA only reaches it through a full GLM-5.3-Flash serving test, which JIT-compiles it every commit. This adds a focused one on the mi35x per-PR suite.

## Test plan

Unit base `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x-20260901`, the image family `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml` resolves to, on `xinyuan/glm-5.3-flash-support` @ `515e865189` with no other PRs applied. Both builds run the same new test file; the shim aliases are the only variable. JIT caches were cleared between builds and the build hashes differ, so neither result is a stale artifact.

| Build | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline | **4 errors** — every case dies in the JIT build, `group_topk` 128 and 512 alike, on `'cuda_fp16.h' file not found` and `no member named 'cudaFuncSetAttribute' in the global namespace` |
| This PR | **4 passed** on gfx950 |

End to end, since no single PR here can serve the model on its own: `main` plus the eight open Day-0 PRs — #39338, #39339, #39340, #39341, #38545, #38546, #38547 and #39317 — which all merge cleanly onto it. `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.19-rocm720-mi35x-20260909`, MI355X TP4, decode CUDA graphs on, 1,319 GSM8K examples, one scoring pass each. Only the checkpoint differs between the two rows:

| Checkpoint | GSM8K |
| --- | --- |
| `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, block FP8 | 97.27% |
| `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` | 96.51% |

**Accuracy:** not attributable to this PR in isolation, and there is no standalone baseline — GLM-5.3-Flash does not start on ROCm without the rest of the stack.

title: [AMD] [GLM-5.3-Flash Day 0] Support non-2048 top-k widths in the DSA page-table transform
author: Jacob0226
body:
## Summary

GLM-5.3-Flash's sparse attention picks 512 pools, expands them to 2048 tokens, then adds up to 3 leftover tokens from the end of the sequence. So the width it hands downstream is **2051**, not 2048 — and the code that receives it asserts the width is exactly 2048, and rejects it.

Nobody has hit this yet: the default setup uses a single combined kernel that does the whole job itself, so the rejecting code never runs. Three supported setups split that job in two, and the second half is the part that rejects. **None of them is AMD-specific — the assert fires on CUDA the same way.**

| Setup | How often it hits |
| --- | --- |
| **HiSparse** | **every decode step** |
| PD disaggregation with MTP index share | every prefill, on the draft step |
| `--dsa-topk-backend torch` | every step |

## Scope

`transform_index.py` only. No environment variable, no architecture gate. The 2048 path keeps its own kernel, so every current caller keeps its performance:

| Width | Decode | Prefill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2048 | existing single-program kernel, untouched | untouched |
| anything else | new tiled kernel, trailing tile masked | already width-generic; only its assert is dropped |

Only the decode kernel needed work. It bakes 2048 in as a literal `constexpr`, reuses it as the row stride, and covers a row with one unmasked `tl.arange`, which requires a power of two. The prefill kernel already takes the width as an argument and masks on it, so its assert only rejected widths the kernel handles.

The tiled kernel produces identical output to the 2048 one at that width. The branch is there to leave the existing path alone, not because the tiled kernel is wrong.

## Test plan

Unit base `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x-20260901`. The two 2048 asserts and the tiled kernel `transform_index_page_table_decode_tiled_kernel` are the only variables. `cd test && python3 registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsa_transform_index.py`.

| Build | Result |
| --- | --- |

title: fix: stop shadowing the DSpark shared-experts fusion guard
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

`DeepseekV4ForCausalLMDSpark` defines `shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason`
twice. The second definition wins, so the first one, the only one with the NPU
branch, is dead code:

```python
    @classmethod
    def shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason(cls, hf_config, quant_config):
        if _is_npu:
            return (
                "NPU DSpark ModelSlim weight loading does not support mapping "
                "shared experts into fused expert slots."
            )
        return DeepseekV4ForCausalLM.shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason(...)

    @classmethod                                   # <- this one shadows it
    def shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason(cls, hf_config, quant_config):
        return DeepseekV4ForCausalLM.shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason(...)
```

The effect is that on NPU, shared-experts fusion is not disabled for the DSpark
draft even though the guard was written to disable it. Per the message that
guard carries, NPU ModelSlim weight loading cannot map shared experts into
fused expert slots, so the draft ends up fusing experts on a path that does not
support it.

CUDA is unaffected: both definitions fall through to the same base
implementation there.

The NPU-aware version arrived in #33676 alongside the plain one from #33312; the
overwrite looks like a merge artifact rather than an intentional revert.

## Modifications

Delete the second, shadowing definition. No other change.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable on CUDA, where both definitions were equivalent and behavior is
byte-identical.

I do not have NPU hardware, so the restored branch is not exercised here. It
restores the behavior #33676 intended; an NPU reviewer confirming that intent
would be the right check before merge.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. Dead-code removal with no CUDA behavior change.

title: [DSV4.1] Combine DSpark decode and prefill kernel optimizations
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash spends substantial decode time in communication, small normalization/quantization launches and speculative metadata handling. This combines #39301/#39336 with the current `dsv4.1` improvements and automatically selects supported paths. Current head: **`9623e9040af55bc2fdd2a05fddae362011be4359`**, merged with upstream **`1e9679db59ea7cf72a3ce2f2a547bc6e54c09ebc`**.

- Remove the custom small-batch paged attention kernel, its dedicated tests, backend dispatch and fused inverse-RoPE plumbing. Attention uses the upstream backend and the model applies the ordinary inverse RoPE. Earlier small-attention throughput/accuracy results do not describe this final implementation.
- Retain compact greedy argmax transport over NVLink, model-specific metadata/KV handling, small-row all-reduce/mHC/norm/quant fusion, Q RMSNorm + MXFP8 quantization and prefill improvements. Preserve the separate wo_a projection/quantization path and required BF16 intermediate rounding.
- Preserve **large-row compensated mHC**, including TF32 high/residual and BF16x3 paths, original FP32 weights, invariant/unsupported fallbacks and weight-update guards. Respect the existing `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM` switch.
- Preserve upstream #39420 side-stream recording order: record deferred mHC statistics after the sublayer and immediately before their join, including fused communication consumers; routed pre-quantization remains after router/top-k. Integrate the latest upstream metadata-buffer and compressed-pool fixes. No new optimization environment-variable definitions are added relative to `8bd60a9913`.

## Latest upstream merge smoke check (`9623e9040a`)

Resolved the relocated communication-test runner conflict using the upstream B200 runner and kept the upstream deletion of the development-only `bench_c2_verify.py`. The mHC graph cases remain intact. No subsequent optimization experiments are included.

On 4×GB300, with the upstream-required `sglang-kernel 0.4.7` and `sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.0` in an isolated environment:

- All 96 mHC epilogue CUDA-graph test cases passed on all four TP ranks.
- The TP4/EP1 DSpark server started and completed a 4096-token input / 128-token output request.
- A batch of 64 requests completed with 64 output tokens each; the server log confirms 64 concurrent decode requests with CUDA Graph enabled.
- Acceptance simulation was disabled for both generation checks. This is a functional smoke check; throughput benchmarks and full accuracy suites were not rerun on this merge commit.

## Previous 4×GB300 validation (`7322accddb`)


Same checkpoint revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, FlashInfer 0.6.18, sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1, sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.7, Transformers 5.12.1 and driver 580.105.08. No dependency overlay. Each arm uses a clean immutable checkout and a fresh server; GPU jobs are serial.

| Workload | Upstream `8bd60a9913` | Final `7322accddb` |
|---|---:|---:|
| BS1 median output tps | 901.33 | **1070.80** |
| C64 output tps | 5659.61 | **7621.19** |
| C64 median TTFT (ms) | 3832.24 | 2677.61 |
| C64 completed requests | 1024/1024 | 1024/1024 |

Relative to this fresh upstream control, the complete PR improves observed C64 throughput by 34.66%. Earlier `c495` C64 throughput was 7626.35 on the same node; that is historical evidence and is not substituted for the fresh upstream comparison.

BS1: TP4/EP1, static DSpark block 5, fixed 4096 input/1024 output, simulated acceptance 5.5, temperature 0, ignore_eos; one warmup and six measured requests per start. Output tps excludes prefill and is timed from the first to last output event. Two independent final starts are pooled with every sample retained. C64: TP4/EP4, simulated acceptance 5.4, frozen 4096/1024 corpus, 64 warmups and 1024 measured requests, same pinned client. These are simulated-acceptance performance measurements, not real-acceptance throughput.

| Profiled workload | Upstream kernel streams / including copies | Final kernel streams / including copies | Target-graph kernel streams (both) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| BS1, 4K input, TP4/EP1 | 11 / 12 | 11 / 12 | 7 |
| BS1, 64K input, TP4/EP1 | 11 / 12 | 11 / 12 | 7 |
| C64, 4K input, TP4/EP4 | 9 / 10 | 9 / 10 | 5 |

The 40 attention-combine kernels use two streams at BS1 (first layer, then the remaining 39 layers), and a single stream at C64. The same pattern appears upstream. The final C64 target graph contains 160 compensated TF32 projection calls and 80 Sinkhorn calls per replay on one statistics stream, confirming that large-row compensated mHC remains active. The final 64K check exercises the filtered graph beyond the 16K candidate budget (target graph ID 41, versus ID 38 at 4K); upstream uses the same full-filter graph at both lengths. No per-layer stream proliferation is observed in these traces.
