title: Fix disagg PP MTP for GLM-5.2
author: nvpohanh
body:
Supersedes #39052 while @nvjullin is OOTO. The original two commits are preserved with Julien as their author; this branch rebases the change onto current `main` and addresses every review comment on the original PR.

## Motivation

GLM-5.2 could not run disaggregated PP prefill with MTP because:

1. PP + speculative decoding was rejected outside NPU even though the prefill path already forwards PP proxy tensors from stages that do not host the draft.
2. The NextN draft is hosted on the last PP stage and borrows the target embedding, but only the first PP stage materialized and loaded `embed_tokens`.
3. The PP ring dropped the draft model's DSA IndexShare seed (`dsa_topk_indices`), which could make decode ranks diverge between eager and CUDA-graph paths.
4. NIXL needed to map each heterogeneous PP prefill stage to the corresponding layer span in an unpipelined decode worker's MLA pool.

## Modifications

- Allow single-layer EAGLE with PP only for disaggregated prefill on the DeepSeek/GLM model path that supplies the last-stage draft embedding. Decode/null PP + speculative decoding and unsupported model families remain rejected.
- Materialize and load `embed_tokens` on the last DeepSeek/GLM PP stage when speculative decoding is enabled.
- Preserve `dsa_topk_indices` through PP serialization and reconstruction.
- Map heterogeneous plain-MLA NIXL transfers through one destination-index dispatcher, while retaining layer-ID/positional pairing for other layouts.
- Add regression coverage for PP/MLA transfer mapping, PP/EAGLE validation, embedding ownership, and DSA seed round trips (including the `None` case).

## Accuracy Tests

Negative control on the exact parent commit (`f539c1fc65e3a0de79b2a0d08805b096fdc85865`): launching the same GLM-5.2-NVFP4 PP4 disaggregated-prefill configuration with EAGLE steps 3 on a GB300 failed before server readiness in `check_server_args`:

```text
AssertionError: Pipeline parallelism is not compatible with overlap schedule, speculative decoding
```

This confirms that PP4 prefill with EAGLE did not start before this PR; the failure is the pre-change non-NPU PP + speculative-decoding restriction removed by this change.

GLM-5.2-NVFP4 on GB300 with Dynamo router:

- Prefill: 1 worker, PP4, EAGLE steps 3
- Decode: 1 worker, TP4, EAGLE steps 3
- GSM8K: 1,319-example dataset, 20-shot (1,299 scored examples), `--max-tokens 16384`
- Model revision: `53e0691e21895a3863a606dfd12910c69eba94ab`
- Hardware: 2 GB300 nodes in one NVL72 segment

| configuration | GSM8K score | decode acceptance length |
|---|---:|---:|
| PP4 prefill + TP4 decode, steps 3/3 | 94.69% (1230/1299) | 3.745 mean (3.00-4.00) |

This is within 0.76 percentage points of the original PR's 95.45% steps1/steps3 result. The decode acceptance length is the mean of 143 scheduler samples and is higher than the original PR's reported 3.589.

## Tests

- `BLACK_NUM_WORKERS=1 SKIP=no-commit-to-branch pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure`
- Targeted PP/MLA, PP/EAGLE, embedding-ownership, and PP DSA round-trip unit tests on the GB300 validation container: 28 passed, 264 deselected, 32 subtests passed.

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation (not applicable; no user-facing interface change).
- [x] Provide accuracy results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance.

title: [NPU][Diffusion] Optimize SenseNova-U1 batched generation
author: syd520zy
body:
## Motivation

SenseNova-U1 denoising on Ascend uses SDPA and unfused RMSNorm and SwiGLU operations. This PR uses native NPU operators to reduce this overhead.

Depends on #39377.

## Modifications

- Use `torch.ops.npu.npu_fused_infer_attention_score` with a BNSD KV cache and per-sample KV lengths, with masked SDPA as the fallback.
- Reuse SGLang's shared `RMSNorm` on NPU while keeping non-NPU execution on the native path.
- Use fused SwiGLU, reuse packed MLP weights, and precompute timestep embeddings.
- Keep the SenseNova `Qwen3MLP` because its checkpoint has separate `gate_proj` and `up_proj` weights and base/MoT-generation modules, while the shared encoder implementation uses a merged tensor-parallel projection.
- Add runtime capability checks, unit coverage, and Ascend benchmark results.

## Accuracy Tests

Ascend 910C, BF16, four concurrent 1024×1024 requests, 5 denoising steps, CFG 4:

- FIA and the SDPA fallback each completed 4/4 requests.
- FIA matched compact SDPA references with a maximum absolute error of `0.0009766` at `atol=rtol=0.02`.
- Images generated with the fused operators were visually checked for obvious regressions.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Single run on one Ascend 910C with BF16, four concurrent 2048×2048 requests, 50 denoising steps, and CFG 4:

| Batch size | NPU operators | Duration (s) | Throughput (images/s) | Mean latency (s) | Improvement |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | Disabled | 234.28 | 0.01707 | 146.47 | — |
| 1 | FIA + RMSNorm + SwiGLU | 205.94 | 0.01942 | 128.80 | +13.76% |
| 2 | Disabled | 234.83 | 0.01703 | 176.06 | — |
| 2 | FIA + RMSNorm + SwiGLU | 195.02 | 0.02051 | 146.33 | +20.42% |

Optimized batch size 2 improves throughput by 5.60% over optimized batch size 1.

title: [MegaMoE] Preserve W13 layout for ModelOpt NVFP4 experts
author: shyeh25
body:
Depends on #38080.

This PR is stacked directly on the current #38080 head (`2f9270f891`). Until #38080 merges, GitHub may show the parent PR's changes as part of this PR. The additional commits to review are `f6d2ef53f9` (two production files, 17 insertions and 2 deletions), `71697cb8ba` (one focused CPU regression-test file), and `79456378e0` (Ruff formatting only).

## Motivation

DeepSeek V4 ModelOpt NVFP4 can retain `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` as its nominal MoE runner while `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe` bypasses that runner and sends the expert weights to DeepGEMM MegaMoE.

The loader previously selected W31 from the nominal runner. MegaMoE consumes canonical W13 and interprets the first half as gate and the second half as up. The mismatch therefore swaps the SwiGLU nonlinear operands and causes a large accuracy loss. The same mismatch can be reproduced by explicitly pairing a TRT-LLM nominal runner with MegaMoE on Qwen NVFP4.

## Modifications

- Add a ModelOpt-NVFP4-specific `use_flashinfer_trtllm_weight_layout` decision. It selects W31 only when the effective consumer is TRT-LLM; MegaMoE always selects canonical W13.
- Use that decision for the W1/W3 shard mapping and for optional interleaved W13 deinterleaving.
- Assert the canonical-W13 invariant before building MegaMoE NVFP4 weights.
- Keep the existing layer-level runner flag unchanged. FP8, MxInt4, unquantized/BF16, padding, runner selection, and existing guards retain their previous behavior.
- Add a registered CPU unit suite covering the backend/layout matrix, real shard placement for weights and scales, unchanged non-ModelOpt loading, interleaved post-load handling, the invariant guard, and the online ModelOpt subclass.

The DeepSeek V4 fix is the loader shard mapping. The deinterleave change keeps the Inkling-style interleaved loader consistent with the same contract; that path is covered by focused unit tests but was not part of the DeepSeek GPU evaluation.

## Accuracy Tests

All reported full GSM8K runs evaluated 1,314/1,314 examples and completed without an inference-time product error.

| Model/path | GB300 | B300 |
|---|---:|---:|

title: fix(dsv4): support R3 capture and MXFP4 online updates
author: bobboli
body:
Replaces #38282, which GitHub auto-closed when its base branch was deleted and recreated.

## Summary

- Capture logical expert IDs from DeepSeek V4 HashTopK before logical-to-physical remapping for R3 replay. Mask CUDA-graph padding, disable target capture from draft modules, and reject the unsupported HashTopK waterfill/capture combination.
- Synchronize CUDA IPC tensor imports in the weight updater before returning to the producer, including flattened buckets and other tensor load formats.
- Support repeated TRT-LLM MXFP4 online loads: permute expert weights in place, retain checkpoint-layout scale parameters, and maintain separate shuffled scale copies with stable kernel addresses. Pass unsigned byte views at the FlashInfer packed-FP4 call boundary without changing load parameters.
- Register the GEMM1 clamp limit as a non-persistent buffer so memory offload preserves it.
- Keep the padded-row Triton fast path off CPU tensors.

## Current rebase (2026-10-02)

Rebased the PR-only commits onto `sglang-miles` at `6c94e57f9ff5b84ba9746f5983ff13ce7e84c68b`. Current head: `0f0a367bad0d693ed8af044316111c25d919ed67`.

- `091bc49cf3`: restore the capture helper's original API, keep device checks at launch sites, validate routed MXFP4 hardware before model construction, and make the flattened-bucket helper's exception-only return contract explicit.
- `ec8a0fbf1c`: integrate upstream expert padding and input prequantization with hot reload. Recognize signed packed weights when computing hidden size and clear padding before repeat shuffles. Adapt existing tests to the current loader/runtime-context interfaces.

## Experiment terminology

- **P1:** TE MXFP8 training with MXFP8 rollout.
- **P2:** TE MXFP8 training with MXFP4 weights × MXFP8 activations for rollout routed experts, without trainer-side QAT.
- **P3:** The P2 setup with routed-expert MXFP4 fake quantization during training; trainer GEMMs still use TE MXFP8.

## Review follow-up (2026-10-02)

`0f0a367bad` adds inverse-shuffle restore for partial MXFP4 updates, live layer-buffer ownership for the clamp, XPU-compatible launch guards, in-place activation constant refresh, and first-build-only allocator cleanup. Empty/weight-only/scale-only sessions failed all six new cases before the restore fix and pass afterward.

The source stack also passed an ARM/GB300 preflight: 69 Miles integration tests, 6 QAT GPU tests and 30 SGLang tests (7 HashTopK, 9 MXFP4 GPU, 5 FP8 ownership, 9 UE8M0). Checkpoint metadata, optimizer/scheduler/RNG state and rollout data-state were audited before the pending P2 resume. This preflight is not an end-to-end training pass.

GitHub CI remains gated on `run-ci`. The PR author's attempt to add it was denied by GitHub permissions; a maintainer must add the label.

## Validation of the preceding rebase

- **320 CPU tests passed**, run one test file per process: HashTopK (7), model loader (3), derived-weight cache (2), FP8 runner fallback (4), runner ownership/static buffers (5), MegaMoE (6), routed capture (5), UE8M0 requantization (9), and server arguments (279).
- **3 B300 GPU tests passed**: fresh-load versus hot-reload parity and storage-address preservation for aligned/padded expert sizes, plus real MXFP4 x MXFP8 forward/reload with standard and FlashInfer dispatch inputs.
- All applicable changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- No new end-to-end RL run was performed after this rebase. These local checks do not establish a full GitHub CI pass.

The results below are historical, from earlier heads.

## FP8/MXFP8 activation-state follow-up (2026-09-23)

Commit `104716dc91` also fixes the TRT-LLM activation tensors introduced in the new base's FP8/MXFP8 path. These alpha/beta/clamp tensors were ordinary attributes, so the memory-saver static-state backup omitted them. Repeated postprocessing also replaced their storage even though CUDA graphs retained the old addresses. Register them as non-persistent buffers and copy into existing storage on reload.

Evidence: an isolated reproduction using the actual preparation and static-state export/import functions left the old clamp at zero after simulated storage loss; re-preparation created a different pointer holding 10. The same function-level check passes after the fix (restored values, stable storage, no checkpoint entries). The existing runner-ownership test fixture now also covers this lifecycle.

The prior `23837cdabf` source passed 7 HashTopK tests and the GPU MXFP4 hot-reload test on GB300, but an end-to-end P1 run subsequently exhibited repetitive output and could not collect valid training groups. The activation-state defect is confirmed; attributing the complete rollout failure to it still requires a new RL run. Updated-source integration job completed successfully on GB300: 51 Miles integration tests, 6 GPU MXFP4 QAT tests, and 12 SGLang tests (HashTopK, MXFP4 hot reload, and FP8 runner ownership/activation-state lifecycle). Changed-file pre-commit passed with `GITHUB_BASE_REF=sglang-miles`. P1 smoke, with all other source/config pins unchanged, collected valid normal-mode samples and completed one valid optimizer step (`ppo_kl=0`, rollout/train log-prob absolute difference 0.02877). It then failed with host-memory OOM during trainer CPU offload; this is not a three-step end-to-end pass. The first `actor_train` timer was 703.9 seconds, not a steady-state performance measurement. P1 retry subsequently **passed all three optimizer steps** and exited successfully (1:03:47), with the same source pins and training settings and additional host-memory diagnostics. `actor_train`: 699.8 / 127.0 / 105.5 seconds; `ppo_kl=0` for all three steps; train/rollout log-prob absolute difference 0.02852 / 0.02860 / 0.02731. No host or CUDA OOM was observed in this run. This does not establish the earlier host-OOM root cause: the physical nodes and Ray-head/PP-stage placement differed. P2 and P3 both failed during the initial SGLang autotune forward, before online weight sync or training: `ValueError: Unsupported trtllm-gen input tensor`. The MXFP4 method passed signed checkpoint parameters directly to FlashInfer instead of zero-copy unsigned-byte views; the same issue exists in the pre-rebase PR head. The idle outer launchers were cancelled. SGLang commit `f9cfbec2d2` fixes that boundary with zero-copy uint8 views, preserving signed load parameters and storage. The new real-kernel case fails with the original exception before the fix; after the fix, all 13 local B300 SGLang tests pass (including real MXFP4 x MXFP8 forward and reload). ARM preflight completed successfully: **70 tests passed** (51 Miles, 6 GPU QAT, 13 SGLang), exit `0:0`. P2 retry and P3 retry used `f9cfbec2d2` and subsequently failed at initial FP32 export quantization, as detailed below. The completed P1 run above used SGLang `104716dc91`; it predates this MXFP4-only follow-up.

## FP32 export compatibility follow-up (2026-09-23)

P2 retry and P3 retry passed SGLang initialization but failed during initial online weight sync, before any optimizer step: the UE8M0 blockwise-FP8 helper rejected Bridge's FP32 export (`[2048, 4096]` shared-expert weight). This is separate from the preceding packed-MXFP4 kernel boundary bug.

SGLang commit `becddd92ece674066025b3e132768391b658214a` accepts BF16 or FP32 without changing the quantization math or rounding through BF16. Both new CPU regression cases fail before the fix. After it: 9 CPU tests and 13 related B300 GPU tests pass; the actual failing shape produces byte-identical FP8 weights and packed scales for BF16 weights versus their lossless FP32 exports. Changed-file pre-commit passes with `GITHUB_BASE_REF=sglang-miles`.

ARM preflight completed (`0:0`, 4:35): **79 tests passed** (51 Miles, 6 GPU QAT, 22 SGLang).

### Completed direct-HF smoke, without Bridge #36

All three arms completed **three valid optimizer steps**, including repeated online weight updates and normal-mode rollout, and exited successfully. No host/CUDA OOM was observed in these successful runs; all nine logged `ppo_kl` values are zero, and loss/gradient norms are finite.

| Arm | Elapsed | Three actor_train timers (seconds) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | 1:03:47 | 699.8 / 127.0 / 105.5 |
| P2 | 1:04:46 | 698.6 / 122.6 / 115.9 |
| P3 | 1:04:32 | 704.2 / 118.8 / 141.3 |

Pins: Miles P1 `946b00a41c`, P2/P3 `f7c4529350`; unmodified Bridge `bridge` base `2e09c234a`; Megatron-LM `f2fc0efcb`. P1 used SGLang `104716dc91`; P2/P3 used `becddd92ec`, which adds the packed-MXFP4 boundary fix and FP32 UE8M0 input support. **P1 was not rerun at the final SGLang head.** All code was committed source; no runtime/site-packages patches or offline weight conversion.

Setup: Preview, TE MXFP8 training, native/cuDNN attention, 8 x 4 GB300, normal mode, R3 enabled, 4K response cap, eval disabled, GPU optimizer with CPU trainer offload; independent experiment records. P3's routed-expert QAT hook installation was confirmed in the runtime log.

This establishes that Bridge #36 is not required for this tested recipe. It does not establish long-run stability, eval quality, QAT benefit, or the cause of the earlier host-OOM failure. First-step timings include warm-up; the subsequent 105.5–141.3 seconds are below the historical 185-second reference-attention figure but are not a controlled comparison with the historical 82.6-second cuDNN result. This is targeted validation, not a full CI pass.

title: [DSV4.1] NVLink collectives, and the DSpark draft head's vocab gather on them
author: DarkSharpness
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1's DSpark draft head shards `markov_w2` over TP and, for every draft token, all-gathers its fp32 step logits (`[bs, vocab/TP]`) before sampling. At bs=1 that is a 129 KB shard per rank going through the NCCL ring at 13–18 µs, five times per verify cycle (~75 µs), plus a 5 µs NCCL broadcast of each sampled token. NVLink multicast moves the same shard in ~3.5 µs.

## Modifications

1. **NVLink collectives** — the first six commits of #36720, unchanged: all-reduce / all-gather / reduce-scatter on the CustomAllReduceV2 push and pull planes (`nvlink_comm.cuh`, `ops/communication/nvlink_comm.py`, bench), the copy-engine all-gathers, the folded residual and its tail fix, and the v2 push round-robin. The K3 migration from that PR is not included.
2. **`VocabGather`** (`srt/distributed/device_communicators/vocab_gather.py`): one interface for the TP vocab-parallel row gather, `[rows, local] -> [rows, world_size * local]` with the ranks side by side (the `all_gather(dim=-1)` layout). `make_vocab_gather` picks the transport once at init — `LocalVocabGather` for a group of one, `NVLinkVocabGather` when the group's CustomAllReduceV2 has a multicast plane, `NcclVocabGather` otherwise — so the caller has no branches. `NVLinkVocabGather` uses the push kernel while the shard fits a push slot, the pull kernel into a symmetric-memory output sized for the server's largest batch (one row per request, allocated at construction) beyond that, and the NCCL ring past both. The stacked-by-rank result is transposed into place and never aliases the shared output.
3. **DSpark**: `DSparkV4MarkovHead.configure_tp_shard` builds the gather; `_apply_step_logits_sharded` calls it. `SGLANG_DSPARK_NVLINK_VOCAB_GATHER` (default on) is the switch; without a multicast plane the NCCL path is taken as before.

The per-token broadcast of the sampled draft token still goes through NCCL; that is the next step.

## Accuracy / tests

Two registered 4-GPU tests (`base-c`, `4-gpu-b200`), run on 4x B200:

- `test/registered/kernel/communication/test_nvlink_comm.py` — 54 passed: the six collectives x {push, pull} x {residual, no residual} x tokens {1, 7, 128, 1024} against an fp32 NCCL reference (gathers bit-exact, reductions within bf16 ordering), plus the multicast and unicast copy-engine gathers (bit-exact).
- `test/registered/kernel/communication/test_vocab_gather.py` — 11 passed: factory choices on a server-style TP `GroupCoordinator`, every path of the NVLink gather (push at 1/3/6 rows, pull at 25/64/200, NCCL at 257) equal to the NCCL gather, results never aliasing the shared output, consecutive pull results preserved, CUDA-graph replay at 1 and 64 rows.

End-to-end results on GB300 (gsm8k, bs=1 traces) will be posted as a comment.

## Performance

4x B200, TP4, one draft-token step logits shard = `[rows, 32320]` fp32 per rank, `marker.do_bench` inside a CUDA graph:

| rows | path | NVLink | NCCL `all_gather(dim=-1)` |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | push | 3.6 µs | 16.5 µs |
| 6 | push | 10.0 µs | 27.4 µs |
| 32 | pull | 41.9 µs | 70.9 µs |
| 128 | pull | 142.4 µs | 154.8 µs |

The push slot on this configuration is 3 MB (24 rows of this shard); the pull output for 256 requests is 126 MB per GPU.

- [x] Update documentation / docstrings as needed.

title: [DSV4.1] Record side-stream work right before its join to keep CUDA-graph replay on one stream
author: DarkSharpness
body:
### Motivation

A DSpark verify cycle on DeepSeek-V4.1 replays its CUDA graphs across ~144 distinct CUDA streams (TP0, bs=1, 64K context): 85 opened by `_hc_mix_stats_partial_kernel`, 45 by the routed MXFP8 pre-quant, three new streams per layer, and the main chain moves onto a fresh stream at every mHC join. Traces become hard to read (every layer lands on new stream ids) and the graph does not run the way it was captured.

The rule, established on the running model: at replay, a node that joins several branches continues on the lane of its **first-recorded** parent. Both offenders record their side-stream block before the main-stream kernels that block is later joined with: the mHC statistics right after the combine (before attention / MoE), the routed pre-quant before the router top-k. The join then follows the side lane and drags the main chain with it. Reordering at the fork does not help (tested: 144 -> 144); recording the side-stream work right before its join does.

### Changes

- `deepseek_v4.py`: `_hc_mix_and_combine` becomes `_hc_combine` (the combine on the current stream plus the fork of `stats_stream`, keeping the tiny-input rule of forking after the combine) and `_hc_mix_stats` (the statistics on `stats_stream`). `forward_hc_pre_from_prev` records `_hc_mix_stats` after the attention / MoE, right before it joins the stream. The DSpark stage does the same.
- `deepseek_v2.py`: the routed MXFP8 pre-quant on `routed_quant_stream` is recorded after the router top-k, right before the routed MoE joins its event. The fork point is unchanged.

Graph topology is unchanged: the fork events stay where they were, so at replay the statistics and the pre-quant still overlap the same main-stream kernels; only the capture order moves.

### Validation (4x GB300, TP4/EP4, DSpark, bs=1, 64K context, TP0 trace, one verify cycle)

| | distinct streams | opened by mix-stats | opened by routed pre-quant |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 144 | 85 | 45 |
| pre-quant reorder only | 103 | 85 | 4 |
| both | **19** | 2 | 4 |

The remaining 19 are one per DSpark segment plus a handful of singletons. Overlap is preserved: the mix-stats kernel still starts ~3.4 us after the combine and runs alongside the wqkv GEMM (3.7 us before); 62% of mix-stats launches overlap another kernel in both traces; attention layer time 122.3 -> 122.9 us and verify cycle 6.36 -> 6.41 ms are within single-launch noise. gsm8k, 1319 questions: 0.974 (0.970-0.972 across launches before). Graph capture succeeds; smoke outputs are byte-identical.

The split methods were checked in isolation against the fused kernels called directly: bit-equal in eager mode, with a side stream, and under CUDA-graph replay.

title: [DSV4.1] Multi-stream prepare for ratio-1/2 layers, fused ratio-1 verify compression, PDL on _q_rope_store
author: DarkSharpness
body:
### Motivation

On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 38 of the 40 attention layers have compress ratio 1 or 2. Their decode / verify prepare kept the fused KV-cache write (`fused_k_norm_rope_flashmla`) on the main stream right behind the Q chain (`wq_b` GEMM + `_q_rope_store`), so attention waited for both; only the compressor / indexer went to a side stream, and only in the eight layers that have them. The multi-stream prepare (`_forward_prepare_multi_stream`) was excluded for these layers, and the special case lived inside `_forward_prepare` as `early_sources`.

Two smaller things showed up in the same trace: the ratio-1 KV-source layer still ran the torch compression chain in target-verify (the fused verify path was gated on ratio 2 although c1 is stateless), and `_q_rope_store` sat behind a launch bubble on the critical path.

### Changes

1. **`_forward_prepare_low_ratio_multi_stream`** (`deepseek_v4.py`): the ratio-1/2 decode / target-verify prepare on three streams: compressor + indexer (`forward_low_ratio_sources`) on one side stream, the KV write on another, the Q chain on the current stream. Each fork is followed by main-stream work and the side blocks are recorded right before their join, so CUDA-graph replay keeps the main chain on one lane (#39420). `_forward_prepare` loses the `early_sources` branches; dispatch is the former `early_sources` condition, now for every ratio-1/2 layer.
2. **Fused verify compression for ratio 1** (`deepseek_v4_backend.py`): `_low_ratio_compress` takes the fused path for `compress_ratio in (1, 2)` in target-verify. c1 has no pair state, its kernel takes any row count and suppresses padded rows, and `c1_out_loc` is built for verify. New test `test_static_verify_dispatch_ratio_1` (dispatch + pool bytes equal to the unfused chain on a verify-shaped batch). The int64 conversion of `positions` at the sources entry is dropped (every consumer takes int32 or int64).
3. **PDL on `_q_rope_store`** (`q_rope_store.py`): `gdc_wait` before the first load, `launch_dependents` after the store, `launch_pdl` where supported. Output bit-identical; in a captured GEMM -> kernel chain the kernel-attributable time drops from ~2.0 us to 1.2-1.5 us per call (m = 1..8).

### Validation (4x GB300, TP4/EP4, DSpark, bs=1, 64K context, TP0 trace, one verify cycle)

| | before | after (1)+(2) |
|---|---|---|
| `fused_k_norm_rope_flashmla` on the `_q_rope_store` lane | 38 / 40 layers | 0 / 40 (finishes ~6 us before the Q RoPE starts) |
| attention-layer time (median, `_q_rope_store` spacing) | 122.9 us | 121.0 us |
| distinct CUDA streams per verify cycle | 19 | 12 (main lane 240 -> 914 kernels; the eight per-layer lanes are gone) |
| `_rmsnorm_fp32` / `_rope_fake_quant_pack_indexer` / `_rope_tail_fake_quant_fp4` per cycle | 2 / 1 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `flash_c1_decode_kernel` per cycle | 0 | 1 |

gsm8k (1319 questions, 64 threads) with (1)+(2): 0.9697, stop rate 1.0, no runaways; per-question agreement with the unchanged tree is at the launch-to-launch level (sampling). Graph capture succeeds; smoke outputs byte-identical. Unit tests: `test_dsv41_fused_compress` 4/4 (incl. the new case), `test_dsv41_indexer_prefill` 2/2, `test_dsv4_q_rope_store` 2/2; the split methods were also checked in isolation (eager, side stream, graph replay). A gsm8k run of the full branch including (3) is in flight and will be posted as a comment.

title: [HiCache] Optimize buffer-mode storage existence bookkeeping
author: xiezhq-hermann
body:
## Motivation

`StorageExistenceCache` is on the buffer-mode hot path: every prefetch decision and write-through admission walks the page-hash chain through `contains_all` / `covers_all`. Under long-context workloads the 128K-entry LRU also churns positives out of the belief set faster than they can be reused, so the cache re-writes pages it already stored.

## Modifications

- Raise `HICACHE_EXISTENCE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES` from 128K to 512K (~125 MiB worst case; ~32M tokens at page size 64 across all pools).
- `contains_all` / `covers_all` walk the chain with one bound `OrderedDict.move_to_end` per page (a `KeyError` is the miss signal) instead of a generator over `contains`, and only consult `extra_cover` when it is non-empty.
- `add` / `invalidate_beyond` hoist the bound dict methods out of the loop; `add` evicts a computed count instead of re-checking `len` on every pop.
- Import `Container` / `Iterable` / `Sequence` from `collections.abc`.

Semantics are unchanged: positive lookups still LRU-touch, eviction order is the same, and the `invalidate_beyond` cut behaves identically.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerical change; this only touches host-side bookkeeping of which pages are believed stored.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not run for this PR. The change reduces per-page Python overhead on the existence-check path and the larger LRU avoids redundant storage writes on long-context traffic; no absolute numbers are included.

title: perf(engine): avoid timed waits for Engine responses
author: jthomson04
body:
## Summary

Engine calls pass no HTTP request object, but each response wait still uses `asyncio.wait_for`. Its timeout path checks for an HTTP disconnect and otherwise starts another wait.

Await `state.event.wait()` directly when `request is None`. HTTP callers keep the timed wait and disconnect check. Both paths continue through the existing iterator, output handling, and request cleanup. This adds no public API and does not change notification settings or scheduler emission.

## Validation

- Focused request-lifecycle tests: **30 passed, 6 subtests passed** using `pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py`.
- New coverage checks available and delayed output order, terminal output, cancellation releasing the event waiter, abort/error delivery, and HTTP timeout disconnect detection. Status 503 coverage exercises error delivery, not a full Engine shutdown integration test.
- All applicable checks passed with `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py`.

The patch changes one conditional in the response iterator and adds coverage to the existing CPU CI test file. It does not change model or kernel code.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

In one matched Dynamo SGLang TCP push comparison, this wait change improved output token throughput by **37.7%** at `batch_notify_size=16`, SGLang's default. Both controls used fixed concurrency 1024, ISL/OSL 33/1024, `stream_interval=1`, and no worker runtime thread override. Only the response wait changed.

| Response wait | Output tokens/s | Completed requests | Duration including drain (s) | p99 TTFT (s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Existing timed wait | 18,494.13 | 3072 | 170.093 | 0.936 |
| Direct event wait | 25,464.63 | 3072 | 123.533 | 1.375 |

Throughput uses completed output tokens divided by actual duration including drain. Each control used 2048 separate warmup requests, a 120-second measurement, and a 90-second grace period. Both controls completed without request errors and had exact token lengths. Separate diagnostic captures retained one token per token-bearing backend frame. TTFT tails increased, as shown above.

For context, native SGLang HTTP serving in the same campaign had **45.243 seconds p99 TTFT**, versus **1.375 seconds** for the patched Dynamo control. Both used notification size 16 and fixed concurrency 1024. Native used 4 tokenizer / 4 detokenizer processes; Dynamo used 1/1. The patched Dynamo TTFT therefore remained well below this native reference, despite increasing relative to the unchanged Dynamo control.

This is one control per configuration, so the result does not establish repeatability or a GIL mechanism. GPU measurements used SGLang main `5c2de3f35567ffceec6cea86ba18e075692e9101` plus this patch, before the PR was applied to the current main base.

title: [PD] Add optional KV transfer checksums
author: cctry
body:
## Motivation

Detect corrupted KV transfers before decode generates tokens. Add an optional Adler-32 integrity check for prefill/decode disaggregation, disabled by default.

## Modifications

- Add GPU checksum kernels for contiguous regions and indexed KV/state pages. Prefill sends the checksum with the final chunk; decode verifies it before batching and retains it across retraction.
- Add `--disaggregation-enable-kv-checksum` to the disaggregation argument group. Enable it on both prefill and decode engines with matching KV layouts; it adds an optional metadata buffer.
- Abort a mismatching request and increment the transfer-failure counter. Raise in CI instead, and skip health-check requests.
- Register CUDA tests for reference parity, corruption detection, optional metadata layouts, health checks, and failure-counter behavior. Update an existing handoff test fixture for the disabled default.

## Accuracy Tests

- `uv run --no-project --with pre-commit pre-commit run --from-ref main --to-ref HEAD` — passed, including Python syntax and CI registration checks.
- Source comparison confirmed the checksum implementation is preserved apart from formatting, and the existing scheduling implementations are unchanged behind the new checks.
- [Focused CUDA checks](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34919315517) at `78d0c0fca0` — 23 tests passed, no skips: `registered/kernel/memory/test_adler32_checksum.py` and `registered/kernel/disaggregation/test_kv_checksum.py`, each run with `python3 <file> -f` from `test/` on an H100 runner.
- [CPU compatibility checks](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34919318407) at `78d0c0fca0` — 58 tests passed, no skips: `registered/unit/managers/test_batch_result_processor_spec_grammar.py`, `registered/unit/managers/test_priority_scheduling_disaggregation.py`, and `registered/unit/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_wire.py`, each run with `python3 <file> -f` from `test/`.

title: [AMD] Use exact CU share for gfx950 segment-plan headroom
author: chuyeh
body:
## Motivation

On gfx950 (MI355X), the assembly attention kernel from #37465 serves EAGLE/MTP verify by splitting each sequence's KV cache into *segments*, one workgroup each; the segment count sets how much of the GPU a sequence can use. #39172 made a length-aware planner the default for batch size > 1, but it still caps any one sequence at twice the legacy fixed-split count:

```text
seg_max = clamp(2 * pow2_floor(num_cus / (batch_size * num_kv_heads)), 16, 64)
```

The `pow2_floor` is inherited from the fixed split, which needs a power-of-two grid; the planner does not. The rounding wastes headroom at any batch size that is not a clean divisor. On a 256-CU MI355X with one KV head, going from 16 to 17 sequences halves the cap from 32 to 16 (the exact share of 15 rounds down to 8), so a long request can use only 16 of the planner's 256 workgroups while short batch mates leave the device idle.

This PR uses the exact equal share instead:

```text
seg_max = clamp(2 * floor(num_cus / (batch_size * num_kv_heads)), 16, 64)
```

Only the per-sequence ceiling rises; the planner's total workgroup budget is unchanged, so the device cannot be oversubscribed. Uniform batches already saturate the GPU and are unaffected; the headroom helps skewed batches where a few long requests own most of the KV traffic.

Related work applies the same CU-aware-cap idea to other split-KV verify paths: #35521 raises the flat split cap on the gfx942 Triton kernel, and #39316 ports split-KV verify to CUDA. This PR is the gfx950 assembly-planner counterpart.

## Modifications

- `vattn_asm_gfx950/__init__.py`: `mtp_verify_attn_seg_max` uses the exact equal-share CU budget, not a power-of-two floor of it. An optional `num_cus` (default: current device) keeps the cap device-independent — a CPX partition exposes 32 of 256 CUs — and testable without a GPU.
- `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_vattn_asm_segment_plan.py` (new, CPU CI): pins the batch discontinuity, both GQA layouts, the 16/64 clamps, and monotonicity.

4 lines of logic. The legacy fixed split, Triton fallback, planner/assembly kernels, kernarg ABI, and HIP-graph cache are untouched. Behavior changes only on gfx950 with the planner active (batch > 1).

## Accuracy Tests

A wrong cap produces wrong output, not just a slowdown, so correctness is the real gate. The existing `test_vattn_segplan_mi35x.py` compares planned-split output against an fp32 reference and the legacy split, across both GQA ratios (16, 8), skewed/tiny/ragged lengths, batch 1/2/24/64, plus plan contents and the plan cache. The new cap exercises non-power-of-two strides (e.g. 20, 30) the old formula could never produce.

MI355X, ROCm 7.2 — `7 passed`, covering the new CPU contracts, `test_vattn_segplan_mi35x.py`, and `test_unified_attention_3d_mtp.py` (asm vs aiter parity). Non-gfx950 hardware and the planner-inactive path do not read this cap and are unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2, head_dim 256, fp8 page-16 KV. Both arms are current `main` after #39172; only `seg_max` changes. 50-100 launches, 5+ repeats, baseline bracketed around the candidate.

| shape | cap | active WGs | current main | exact share | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| hkv1, uniform bs17 x 70k | 16 → 30 | 255 → 255 | 109.7 us | 109.8 us | 1.00x |
| hkv1, agentic skew bs17 | 16 → 30 | 49 → 83 | 238.0 us | 134.0 us | 1.78x |
| hkv1, agentic skew bs24 | 16 → 20 | 56 → 65 | 238.3 us | 193.0 us | 1.23x |
| hkv2, uniform bs9 x 70k | 16 → 28 | 126 → 126 | 111.9 us | 112.2 us | 1.00x |
| hkv2, agentic skew bs9 | 16 → 28 | 41 → 69 | 223.1 us | 139.1 us | 1.60x |
| hkv1, one 70k request in bs17 | 16 → 30 | 32 → 46 | 75.6 us | 46.7 us | 1.62x |

Context sweep for one long request in bs17: neutral to 8k, then 1.21x/1.40x/1.62x at 16k/32k/70k; 1k within 2.2% on both GQA layouts. Trade-off: the fp32 partial buffers grow ~17 → 32 MiB at the bs17 q_len=4 16-head shape; the cap of 64 is unchanged and uniform kernel time stays flat.

### End-to-end serving (InferenceX agentic replay)

Both tables use the [MI355X InferenceX recipe](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/main/benchmarks/single_node/agentic/qwen3.5_fp4_mi355x_sglang_mtp.sh) replaying the public `cc-traces-weka-062126-256k` dataset (seed 42), Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, TP2, concurrency 20, `SGLANG_ASM_VERIFY_ATTN=1`. Each tree runs once per GPU pair and the two runs are averaged, so per-pair speed differences cancel; both arms run concurrently on the same host. The cap was confirmed live in every container (16 base / 30 PR at batch 17). Comparing merge base `2cb51f5d22` with this PR.

**HBM only, 900 s/run (4 runs, 0 errors):**

| TP2 c20, HBM | Merge base | This PR | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT p50 | 10.42 ms | 10.26 ms | -1.6% |
| TPOT p90 | 17.86 ms | 17.57 ms | -1.6% |
| TPOT p95 | 24.74 ms | 23.98 ms | -3.1% |
| TTFT p50 | 1.063 s | 1.012 s | -4.8% |
| Output | 705.5 tok/s | 707.0 tok/s | +0.2% |

**HiCache DRAM tier, 3600 s/run, balanced two-round crossover (4 runs, 12040 req, 0 errors):**

| TP2 c20, HiCache 1.5 | Current `main` | This PR | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT p50 | 9.63 ms | 9.58 ms | -0.52% |
| TPOT p90 | 15.22 ms | 14.90 ms | -2.10% |
| TPOT p95 | 20.00 ms | 19.57 ms | -2.13% |
| TTFT p50 | 1.110 s | 1.065 s | -4.02% |
| Output | 754.2 tok/s | 762.2 tok/s | +1.07% |

**Read these as "no regression", not a speedup.** The deltas are smaller than run-to-run noise: within one arm, TPOT p90/p95 vary 6-9% across GPU pairs, and a third HiCache round flipped the tail signs (p90 +2.1%, p95 +5.5%). That is expected here — 55% of decode steps run at batch sizes where both formulas return an identical cap, and the rest only benefit when a sequence is long enough for the ceiling to bind. The kernel A/B above is the performance evidence; the E2E result shows this workload has no serving regression.

Reproduction note: HiCache on current `main` needs `sgl_kernel.kvcacheio.get_device_accessible_ptr` (#35233, 14 Sep); older images abort at startup on ROCm with `KV_OFFLOADING=dram`. These runs used `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.19-rocm720-mi35x-20260915`.

author: chuyeh
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

#37465 puts EAGLE verify / draft-extend / q_len-1 decode on the gfx950 `vattn_asm` kernel, launched through ctypes `hipModuleLaunchKernel` on the current torch stream. On ROCm 10 images, `SGLANG_ASM_VERIFY_ATTN=1` fails during EAGLE verify HIP-graph capture:

```
RuntimeError: vattn_asm: hipModuleLaunchKernel failed: 709 (context is destroyed)
```

`hipModuleLoad` succeeded, so the kernel reports itself active, and the default stream (handle 0) still works. Only a torch stream fails — graph capture included, which is the path decode takes.

#### Root cause

ROCm 10 ships the HIP runtime (`_rocm_sdk_core`) and the toolchain (`_rocm_sdk_devel`) as separate wheels. Torch maps core's `libamdhip64.so.7`, which the unversioned `CDLL("libamdhip64.so")` does not match, so the loader takes devel's copy off `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` as a **second** HIP runtime: the module loads in devel while the stream belongs to core.

Unpatched, on MI355X:

| Image | torch | HIP runtimes mapped | `CDLL("libamdhip64.so")` binds | Fix needed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rocm720` | 2.9.1 | 1 | torch's, via the `/opt/rocm` symlink | no |
| `rocm724` | 2.11.0 | 1 | torch's, `torch/lib/libamdhip64.so` | no |
| `rocm10` | 2.11.0 | **2** | devel's, **not** torch's | **yes** |

So the trigger is the SDK split, not torch 2.11 — `rocm724` has torch 2.11 and one runtime — and the change is a no-op wherever the soname already resolves to torch's object. Same failure mode #30870 fixed for CUDA, where TileLang's `libcudart_stub.so` could win over the real runtime.

## Modifications

- `vattn_asm_gfx950/__init__.py`: initialize CUDA so torch's HIP is mapped, then bind ctypes to it with the existing `find_loaded_library()` helper from #30870 rather than to the SONAME. Ten lines in one function; no new private API, no second `/proc/self/maps` parser.

No disambiguation between the two ROCm 10 copies is included, because none is needed: only torch's copy is ever mapped. After `import torch`, after CUDA init, and after importing `aiter`, `unified_attention_3d_mtp` and `aiter_backend`, `/proc/self/maps` holds exactly one `libamdhip64`:

```
maps after torch import: [.../_rocm_sdk_core/lib/libamdhip64.so.7]
maps after cuda init:    [.../_rocm_sdk_core/lib/libamdhip64.so.7]
maps after sglang+aiter: [.../_rocm_sdk_core/lib/libamdhip64.so.7]
```

The devel copy only enters the process if something explicitly `dlopen`s it, which is precisely the bug being removed. Should a future image map both, `find_loaded_library()` is the single place to teach the preference, for CUDA and HIP at once.

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/amd/test_vattn_segplan_mi35x.py::TestVattnSegPlan::test_launches_on_a_side_stream_and_under_graph_capture` (`stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`) launches the kernel on a torch side stream, then captures and replays it in a HIP graph, checking both against the file's existing fp32 reference. It lives with the other gfx950 asm kernel tests and reuses their fixtures.

Verified on MI355X (gfx950):

| Image | Unpatched | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `v0.5.18-rocm10-mi35x-20260902` | `FAILED ... 709 (context is destroyed)` | `3 passed, 16 subtests passed` |
| `v0.5.19-rocm720-mi35x-20260913` | passes | `3 passed, 16 subtests passed` |
| `v0.5.18-rocm724-mi35x-20260825` | passes | `3 passed, 16 subtests passed` |

The ROCm 10 unpatched column is a negative control: reverting only `_hip_lib()` to `CDLL("libamdhip64.so")` makes the new test fail with exactly the reported 709, so the test guards the regression rather than merely passing. With the fix, ctypes binds `/opt/venv/.../_rocm_sdk_core/lib/libamdhip64.so.7`, the same runtime torch uses.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed change: one extra library-path lookup, once per process, at kernel load. This restores the assembly verify path under ROCm 10 HIP-graph capture; the kernel and launch geometry are untouched.

title: [Fix] HiCache startup ImportError on the pinned kernel wheel
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

#35233 landed an AOT op and its caller in one PR, skipping the order [Update sglang-kernel](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#update-sglang-kernel) asks for. PR CI builds a PR-local wheel, so it went green. Main and scheduled CI run the pinned `sglang-kernel==0.4.7`, where any server that builds a registered host pool dies at startup on `ImportError: cannot import name 'get_device_accessible_ptr'`. That was 32 jobs in the last scheduled run.

Reverting re-breaks MI355X, since ROCm builds the kernel from this tree and is already running the fix, and it drops an op that has to ship anyway. So this takes the exception that section allows: check the op is there, keep an equivalent fallback until a released wheel catches up.

The CUDA fallback is the raw host address, which under UVA is the device alias, so nothing changes past one warning. ROCm gets no fallback, since the two addresses really do differ there and a missing op means a broken build, so it raises. The registered test goes through the same helper and skips without the op, and a new test checks that the aliased and fallback tables match on CUDA.

Once a released kernel carries the op and the pin moves, those skips run for real and the fallback can go or stay as skew insurance.

title: [Fix] Don't write conv state from the fused KDA verify kernel
author: mmangkad
body:
> Reland of #39219, which was reverted in #39405 because it was merged by mistake.

## Motivation

`fused_kda_conv_gating_verify` rolled the conv state back into `conv_state` at the end of the kernel. Every V tile loads that same Q/K conv history at entry, but only `i_v == 0` writes it, so a tile scheduled in a later wave reads what the owner already overwrote.

The writeback is also dead: verify is speculative, and the commit scatter sets `conv_state` from the selected intermediate window. `accept_lens` is at least 1, so `last_correct_step_indices` is never negative for a real request and the scatter always overwrites.

So the stores are removed rather than guarded. `conv_state` and the SSM state are read-only in verify.

## Modifications

| | |
| --- | --- |
| kernel | drop the 9 `tl.store(cs_base, ...)` at the end of `fused_kda_conv_gating_verify_kernel` |
| docstring | state ownership: conv and SSM state are read-only, the commit scatter advances them |
| tests | `conv_state` must come back untouched; output must not vary with CTA scheduling |

Reached only with `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_KDA_VERIFY=1` (default off), on the KDA Triton verify path at `topk == 1`.

## How the race shows

H=1 with HV=16, so 16 V tiles share one Q/K history. Same inputs, against the unfused pair:

| | max abs | max rel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| full GB300, one wave | 2.98e-8 | 7.2e-3 |
| 8-SM green context, waves serialized | **5.0e-2** | **188** |

Removing the stores makes both configurations identical. The residual ~1 ulp is reduction-order difference and is unaffected by the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

Ling-3.0-flash BF16, 4x GB300 TP4, NEXTN, fused verify on. Full GSM8K, thinking on, `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `max_tokens=8192`, 1 repeat.

| | score | stop | error |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | 96.06% | 99.70% | 0.00% |
| after | 95.83% | 99.17% | 0.00% |

Unchanged — the gap is inside the ~0.55pp 1-sigma band at n=1319. The race is below eval resolution when the grid fits one wave.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same server, 8192 in / 1024 out at concurrency 1, 64 warmup, `--flush-cache`, 3 runs per arm. Accept length 3.01 on all six.

| | runs (tok/s) | mean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before | 355.23, 361.47, 363.72 | 360.14 |
| after | 370.64, 369.38, 375.18 | **371.73** |

**+3.22%**, arms disjoint. The kernel does strictly less work with the stores gone.

## Checklist

- [x] `pre-commit` clean
- [x] 9 cases in `test_fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py`; all 9 fail against the unfixed kernel
- [x] Accuracy and speed measured above

title: [AMD] Fix deferred Kimi-K3 forget gate in fused in-projection
author: tomjen12
body:
## Motivation

Fix a ROCm Kimi-K3 decode CUDA Graph capture failure in the fused input-projection path. When `defer_f_b=True`, this path applies `f_b` prematurely, causing the KDA backend to project an already-expanded forget gate again:

```text
RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (1x1536 and 128x1536)
```

## Modifications

- Return raw `f_a` when `defer_f_b=True`; preserve the existing projected path otherwise.
- Add an MI35X regression test covering both deferred and non-deferred paths.

## Accuracy Tests

No model accuracy benchmark was run because the affected configuration crashes before serving requests. The focused ROCm test verifies both deferred and non-deferred outputs:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python3 \
  test/registered/amd/test_kimi_k3_kda_inproj_fusion.py
```

```text
Ran 4 tests in 6.224s
OK
```

On MI355X, decode CUDA Graph capture fails without the fix and the server reaches the ready state with it.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: this fixes a startup crash and does not add an operation. The existing KDA backend applies `f_b` exactly once.

title: perf(multimodal): offload CPU feature hashing with bounded admission
author: Denji-kk
body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_MM_PRECOMPUTE_HASH=1`, CPU feature hashing runs synchronously on the tokenizer event loop. Large multimodal inputs can delay unrelated requests while their bytes are hashed.

Tracking: #39532

## Modifications

- Offload missing hashes for CPU tensors, NumPy arrays, and CPU tensor lists to a dedicated pool with two workers per multimodal processor.
- Acquire capacity before submission. Cancelled requests retain their inputs and capacity until the native reader finishes, including repeated cancellation.
- Preserve the existing hash/pad algorithm, caller overrides, precomputed hashes, and the calling thread for device-dependent or opaque transports.
- Shut down the pool with the processor. Threads start on demand; the existing precompute flag and its default are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Base: `b510881157b8f12b98387340c7fbfc266dbbb35e`. Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Transformers 5.12.1.

89 CPU tests pass, including hash/pad equivalence for strided tensors, bfloat16, arrays and nested lists; caller overrides and skip mode; scheduler hash reuse after pickle; cancellation/admission; errors/shutdown; and existing processor/request cleanup regressions.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_mm_hashes.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_mm_process_config.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py
```

No model-level serving accuracy evaluation was run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Synthetic CPU features, 8 requests, two hash workers, PyTorch CPU threads = 1, 8-CPU container limit on Intel Xeon 6767P. Median of five measured repetitions after warmup. The inline baseline uses the unchanged `set_pad_value()` path in the same benchmark.

| Feature per request | Inline wall time | Offload wall time | Inline maximum heartbeat gap | Offload maximum heartbeat gap |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 MiB | 4.79 ms | 4.49 ms | 4.82 ms | 1.17 ms |
| 16 MiB | 75.00 ms | 39.76 ms | 75.04 ms | 2.01 ms |
| 64 MiB | 293.31 ms | 161.48 ms | 293.39 ms | 1.82 ms |

```bash
bench_dir=$(mktemp -d)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Denji-kk/sglang-upstream/ac3e86ce4104e540d50cab6fc80bef3b36bcd75e/benchmark/multimodal/bench_hash_executor.py -o "$bench_dir/bench_hash_executor.py"
PYTHONPATH=python python "$bench_dir/bench_hash_executor.py"
```

These measurements cover hashing and event-loop responsiveness; end-to-end TTFT and serving throughput were not measured.

## Checklist

- [x] Ruff formatting/lint, isort, and registered-test validation.
- [x] Focused CPU tests registered in `base-a-test-cpu`.
- [x] Benchmark results and reproduction commands provided.

title: [Perf] [AMD] quark: Add opt-in AITER ASM FP4 GEMM for Quark dense linear
author: vorapolsiloai
body:
## Motivation

On ROCm, Quark W4A4 MXFP4 dense linear layers always run AITER's Triton `gemm_afp4wfp4`. That kernel does not read the tuned `a4w4_blockscale_tuned_gemm.csv` tables, which AITER's `gemm_a4w4` and vLLM both use. So SGLang cannot use the per-model CK/ASM tuning that vLLM gets (for example ROCm/aiter#5350), and we would have to keep a separate set of Triton tunings for SGLang.

This PR adds an opt-in path that runs these layers through `gemm_a4w4`, so SGLang uses the same tuned kernels.

## Modifications

- Add `SGLANG_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM` to `Envs` (default off). It only takes effect on gfx95.
- After weight loading, preshuffle the FP4 weights and the E8M0 weight scales once into the layout that `gemm_a4w4` expects.
- At run time, quantize activations with AITER's `per_1x32_f4_quant` (shuffled scales) and call `gemm_a4w4` with `bpreshuffle=True`. AITER then picks the model-specific CSV entry if there is one.
- Both AITER calls are registered as custom ops with fake implementations, so torch.compile can trace them.
- If a layer's scale shape cannot be swizzled (rows must be a multiple of 32, scale columns a multiple of 8), that layer keeps the existing Triton path and a warning is logged once.

**Limitation:** Quark's tuple-input fusion projections are not supported on this path. The weights are preshuffled at load time, so we cannot fall back to Triton per call. These projections raise an error that tells the user to turn the flag off.

## Open question for maintainers

Should this stay behind its own env var, or should gfx95 with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` use CK/ASM by default (as vLLM does) and keep Triton as the fallback? Details: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39598#issuecomment-5679491881

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X, synthetic GEMM `(M, N, K) = (16, 1024, 5120)`:

- AITER loaded the Qwen3.8-27B tuned A4W4 CSV entry and selected `f4gemm_bf16_per1x32Fp4_BpreShuffle_32x128`.
- `process_weights_after_loading` + `apply_weights` gave exactly the same output as a separately dequantized FP4 reference (`rtol=0`, `atol=0`).
- CPU unit tests (`test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_quark_mxfp4_asm.py`) cover which scale shapes are supported and check the scale permutation against AITER's tile order (all 3 tests pass cleanly).
- Re-validated post-rebase on AMD Instinct MI355X (ROCm 10, AITER): env var registration in `Envs` and `QuarkW4A4MXFP4` module imports pass cleanly.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

TODO: add a serving comparison on one image, flag off (Triton) vs flag on (CK/ASM).

- [ ] Update documentation.

title: [HiCache] Add staged write-back for the page-unified KV cache layout
author: huangtingwei9988
body:
## Motivation

Add staged write-back support for the `page_unified` KV cache layout, building on the unified storage layout discussed in #33651 and the GPU staging approach introduced in #21631.

The destination layouts are:

- **MHA:** `(page, head_group, layer, 2, page_size, head_in_group, dim)`, where K=0 and V=1.
- **MLA:** `(page, layer, page_size, dim)`, storing one compressed KV tensor per layer.

## Changes

- Add `hicache_page_unified_relayout_kernel` to gather per-layer GPU KV data into contiguous staging pages using 16-byte vectorized loads and stores.
- Support MHA and MLA through compile-time specialization. MLA has no head-group, separate K/V, or head axes.
- Reuse the existing whole-page D2H copy helpers after GPU relayout.
- Support transfers larger than the caller-provided staging buffer by processing chunks on the current CUDA stream.
- Add MHA and MLA Python entry points and correctness tests in existing files.

This PR implements the write-back primitives and tests. Host-pool integration and load-back support are outside its scope.

## Correctness

**160 test cases passed on NVIDIA H20 after merging `sgl/main`: 80 MHA and 80 MLA cases.**

Tests compare the complete host output against an independently constructed CPU reference using exact equality, including untouched destination pages.

Coverage includes:

- Different head-group counts, layer counts, page sizes, and dimensions.
- MLA compressed KV dimensions of 512 and 576.
- BF16, FP16, and uint8 data.
- int32 and int64 source page indices.
- Reordered pages and repeated source pages.
- Empty transfers, staging reuse, and partial final chunks.
- Execution on a non-default CUDA stream.
- Invalid shapes, alignment, staging capacities, and destination indices.

Ruff, clang-format, and diff whitespace checks passed for the implementation changes.

## Performance

The MHA write-back path was benchmarked on one NVIDIA H20 with PCIe Gen5 ×16, PyTorch 2.9.1 / CUDA 12.8, and CPU/memory bound to the GPU's NUMA node.

Configuration:

- BF16
- 61 layers
- 8 KV heads
- Head dimension: 128
- Page size: 64
- 5 warmup iterations and 25 measured iterations
- Median CUDA-event latency

Bandwidth includes **GPU relayout + D2H transfer**. GB/s counts the KV payload once.

| Tokens | Payload | 1 head group | 2 head groups | 4 head groups | 8 head groups |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 122 MiB | 52.32 GB/s | 52.34 GB/s | 52.33 GB/s | 52.33 GB/s |
| 2048 | 488 MiB | 52.53 GB/s | 52.52 GB/s | 52.53 GB/s | 52.52 GB/s |
| 8192 | 1952 MiB | 52.74 GB/s | 52.74 GB/s | 52.74 GB/s | 52.74 GB/s |

The measured contiguous D2H baseline was **55.0–55.2 GB/s**, so staged write-back reached approximately **95%** of that baseline.

Using a 32-page staging buffer for the 8192-token transfer sustained approximately **52.6 GB/s**.

For 2048 tokens, profiling showed approximately **0.34 ms for GPU relayout** and **9.39 ms for D2H**, indicating that PCIe transfer dominated total latency.

These performance measurements were collected before the MLA extension and the subsequent merge of `sgl/main`. MLA correctness was validated; MLA bandwidth has not been measured.

title: Accept MXFP8 dispatch in FlashInfer A2A TRT-LLM MoE
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

Serving an MXFP8 model with FlashInfer A2A and `--flashinfer-a2a-dispatch-type mxfp8` dies during init:


title: [Qwen4-Exp] Optional fp8 (e4m3) storage for the compressed QSA indexer cache
author: zhendonghua
body:
## Motivation

The QSA block selector of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`qwen4_exp`) keeps one compressed indexer key per `compress_ratio` tokens and dots every index query against that cache. Both operands are bf16 today. vLLM added an fp8 indexer cache in vllm-project/vllm#54890 (`--attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`, GB300: decode 1.0–1.5×, prefill 1.4–1.7× on the indexer). This PR adds the same option to SGLang, implemented in the existing TileLang scoring kernels and JIT prep kernels.

`--qsa-indexer-dtype {auto,bfloat16,fp8_e4m3}`, default `auto` (bf16, no behaviour change).

## Modifications

Data path today: per token the JIT kernel `qsa_index_q_prep` RMS-norms + MRoPEs the index Q and writes the raw index K into a per-request pending ring; every `compress_ratio` tokens `qsa_index_k_compress` averages the ring rows (fp32), norms, ropes and writes one compressed key; the TileLang MQA kernels score Q against the compressed cache (fp32 logits), `qsa_fast_topk` picks the blocks, and sparse attention then reads the main bf16 KV cache. Only the storage dtype of the compressed keys / index Q and the scoring GEMM operand dtype change:

- **JIT prep kernels** (`qsa_indexer.cuh`): `TOut` template parameter. The compute path (fp32 norm reduction, per-op bf16 rounding in RoPE, fp32 group mean) is unchanged; only the final vector store casts through `qsa_storage_cast<TOut>` (identity for bf16, CUDA saturating e4m3 cast for fp8, no scale: the rows are RMS-normed, this checkpoint's indexer norm weights have max |1+w| = 1.41). `TensorMatcher` pins `q_out` / `compressed_k_buffer` to `TOut`. The Python wrapper compiles per `(dtype, out_dtype)` and only accepts `out_dtype in {dtype, float8_e4m3fn}`.
- **TileLang scoring kernels** (`qsa/mqa.py`): the kernel factories take the operand dtype, Q/K global and shared tensors are declared in it, `T.gemm` accumulates in fp32 and the logits stay fp32. `_scoring_dtype(q, k)` requires both operands to agree (mixed dtypes raise) so the pool is never copied.
- **Pool** (`qsa_kv_pool.py`): `resolve_qsa_indexer_dtype`, `QSATokenToKVPool(qsa_indexer_dtype=...)`, the compressed cache is allocated in that dtype and `qsa_bytes_per_token(compressed_dtype=...)` charges the KV budget accordingly. The pending ring stays bf16 (it is the input of the group mean).
- **Config**: the field lives in `arg_groups/fields/model.py` and is read via `get_model().qsa_indexer_dtype`. The qwen4_exp override admits `fp8_e4m3` only on CUDA SM90/SM100 with a compressed QSA profile; the KV-cache configurator rejects a non-auto value for models without one; `pool_configurator._compute_qsa_cell_size` passes the dtype to the memory profiler.
- **Layer glue** (`qsa/qsa_indexer.py`): `project_qk` hands `out_dtype=pool.qsa_compressed_dtype` to the fused Q prep (and casts in the eager fallback), so Q always matches the cache.

Not covered by this PR (unchanged / untested): the MTP draft indexer under fp8, TP > 1 kernel tests, hardware other than B300 (the SM90 gate is by analogy with the existing DSA fp8 TileLang path), speed (accuracy only).

## Accuracy check

Baseline is pure `main` at 935cbf2, the fp8 arm is this branch rebased on that same commit with `--qsa-indexer-dtype fp8_e4m3` added (the branch has since been rebased on current main without code changes). `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`, one B300 node, `--tp 4 --ep 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --linear-attn-prefill-backend flashinfer --linear-attn-decode-backend triton --mamba-ssm-dtype float32`, no speculative decoding. Bare `sgl-eval run` commands: gsm8k `--thinking --max-tokens 16384`; aime26 / gpqa `--temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --reasoning-effort xhigh --thinking --max-tokens 131072 --seed 0` with n_repeats 4 / 8. Zero KV-pool retractions during every run.

| indexer | GSM8K 1319 (greedy) | AIME26 pass@1 (30×4) | GPQA Diamond pass@1 (198×8, sem) | GPQA majority@8 | GPQA truncations /1584 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 (main) | 97.80 (1 trunc) | 98.33 (0 trunc) | 92.11 (0.29) | 93.18 | 2 |
| **fp8 (this PR)** | 97.65 (0 trunc) | 99.17 (0 trunc) | 91.98 (0.50) | 92.93 | 1 |

Per question: GSM8K 1284 both right / 25 both wrong / 4 vs 6; AIME26 27 of 30 both all-correct, 2 vs 1; GPQA 162 both all-correct / 5 both wrong / 11 vs 14.

## Tests

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/qsa/test_qsa_indexer.py` (B300, 25 passed): fp8 variants of the fused compress / Q-prep tests against the eager chain with a 1-ulp e4m3 contract (a bf16 last-ulp RMSNorm flip may move the e4m3 code by one step, the bf16 cases stay bit-comparable), TileLang prefill/decode for fp8 and bf16 vs a torch fp32 reference on the same operands (finite mask equal, logits 2e-3, top-512 selection compared as score multisets so ties cannot fail the test), and mixed-dtype rejection. The whole file also ran under `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` with no kernel memory errors.
- CPU: `test_qwen4_fp8_indexer_dtype_platform_gate` in `test_model_overrides.py` (fp8 admitted only on CUDA SM90/SM100 with a compressed QSA indexer, the bf16 spellings never consult the platform), plus the namespace / config-bag coverage lints for the new field.

title: [Perf] [AMD] dsv4: fp8 target lm_head GEMM for DSPARK verify logits
author: karverma-amd
body:
## Summary

On the DeepSeek-V4 DSPARK speculative-decode path, the target `lm_head` projection that produces the **verify logits** runs a bf16 matmul `[num_verify_tokens, hidden] x [hidden, vocab_slice]` in `project_through_lm_head`. This is a per-decode-step cost that scales with the verify batch (≈ `concurrency × (gamma+1)` tokens) and, on the trace, dispatches to a `Cijk_*` (rocBLAS/Tensile) bf16 GEMM. This PR adds an **opt-in fp8 path** for that GEMM (`torch._scaled_mm`, per-token activation scale + per-output-channel weight scale, weight quantized once and cached on the module), behind a new env flag, with the bf16 matmul as fallback.

**What this change is:** an opt-in fp8 replacement of the DSPARK verify-head GEMM. Off by default, it roughly halves that one kernel; end-to-end it is a **small, decode-bound win (~+1–1.5% tput / −3% TPOT at high concurrency)** with **no GSM8K accuracy regression**.

## Motivation

Attributing the DSV4 DSPARK decode step kernel-by-kernel (torch-profiler) shows the target-head GEMM that produces the `[num_verify_tokens, vocab]` logits is one of the per-step GEMMs, and it grows with the verify batch. It is a plain bf16 `[M, K] x [K, N]` with a very large `N` (vocab) and small `M`, so it is weight-read (memory) bound — halving the weight bytes in fp8 nearly halves the kernel. This is the last per-step decode GEMM on this path not already running in a reduced precision.

## What changed

* `dspark.py`: two module helpers — `_fp8_quant_per_row(x)` (per-row symmetric fp8 quant) and `_fp8_lm_head_matmul(hidden, lm_head)` (`hidden @ weight.T` via `torch._scaled_mm`, caching the fp8 weight + scale on the `lm_head` module). `project_through_lm_head` calls the fp8 path when the flag is on, the head is floating-point (non-quantized), `hidden.shape[0] > 0`, and the vocab slice is 16-aligned; otherwise it uses the original `torch.matmul`. A quantized head keeps its own kernel; the tiny `M=1` sample head stays bf16.
* `environ.py`: new `SGLANG_OPT_DSPARK_FP8_LM_HEAD = EnvBool(False)`.
* The flag is read **once at module import** (`_DSPARK_FP8_LM_HEAD`) so the per-token decode path has no env lookup.

No behavior change unless the flag is set.

## Validation (MI35X, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 FP4, TP8 + DP-attention, DSPARK gamma=6)

**Numerics** — model-free parity check of `torch._scaled_mm` (per-row act + per-channel weight fp8) vs the bf16 matmul on this stack (gfx950): mean abs error ~0.076, p99 relative error ~2.4% (fp8 rounding); output magnitudes match. The precision loss is bounded and does not move greedy argmax on real (peaked) LM logits — see accuracy.

**Accuracy** — 5-shot GSM8K, 1319 questions, `--parallel 1319`, greedy (temp 0), cuda-graph on, **real speculative acceptance** (`SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_*` unset so outputs are true model outputs):

| lm_head dtype | Accuracy | Invalid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bf16 (flag off) | 0.939 | 0.000 |
| fp8 (flag on) | 0.948 | 0.000 |

No regression — the +0.9pt is within greedy-divergence run-to-run noise, 0% invalid on both.

**Kernel swap (trace-confirmed)** — profiled TP8, conc16, rank-0, over the decode window. The verify-head GEMM flips 1:1 between arms and nothing else changes:

* off: `Cijk_Alik_Bljk_BBS_..._MT512x16x64` (bf16) — ~0.567 ms/step (2 launches/step)
* on:  `Cijk_Alik_Bljk_F8BS_..._MT256x16x256` (fp8) — ~0.153 ms/step (1 launch/step)

≈73% cheaper on that GEMM. Amortized over the accepted-token count this reconciles with the measured +1.1% at conc16.

**Throughput** (ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, decode-inclusive shape; flag off vs on):

| conc | metric | off (bf16) | on (fp8) | Δ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16 | median TPOT | 9.58 ms | 9.57 ms | ~flat |
| 16 | decode tok/s | 777.5 | 785.8 | +1.1% |
| 128 | median TPOT | 25.58 ms | 24.80 ms | **−3.0%** |
| 128 | decode tok/s | 2670.5 | 2707.2 | **+1.4%** |

Honest framing: a small, decode-bound win that grows with the verify batch (bigger `M` at higher concurrency). Under prefill-dominated shapes it is ~neutral.

## How to enable

```
SGLANG_OPT_DSPARK_FP8_LM_HEAD=1
```

Applies to the DSPARK target verify head only; requires a floating-point (non-quantized) `lm_head`. Off by default.

## Checklist

* Opt-in (default off); quantized head, `M=1` sample head, and the bf16 fallback are unchanged
* Numerically validated (bounded fp8 error; GSM8K accuracy preserved on real acceptance)
* Kernel swap trace-confirmed (bf16 `Cijk_*` → fp8 `Cijk_*_F8BS_*`, 1:1)
* Repeated A/B throughput (TPOT + decode tok/s) at conc 16 / 128
* Flag read once at module import (no per-token env lookup)
