title: [ROCm] fix: remove extra bf16 -> fp32 cast in jit grouped topk kernel path
author: RuibinCheung
body: ## Motivation On ROCm with `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK=1`, every MoE layer pays an avoidable `bfloat16 -> float32` copy kernel on the routing bias. `select_experts` unconditionally converts `correction_bias` into the gating dtype whenever `_use_aiter and use_grouped_topk`: ```python if _use_aiter and use_grouped_topk and correction_bias is not None: correction_bias = topk_config.correction_bias_for_dtype(router_logits.dtype) ``` That conversion exists for `aiter_biased_grouped_topk`, which wants the bias in the same dtype as the gating logits. But when the JIT router is enabled, `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` returns from its `jit_grouped_gate` branch long before the aiter branch is reached, and that branch immediately converts the bias back: ```python return jit_grouped_gate( gating_output, correction_bias.to(dtype=torch.float32), ... ) ``` So a model that stores `e_score_correction_bias` in fp32 (GLM-5.2 does, deliberately — its bias sits at an offset whose spread is only a few bf16 ULPs wide) gets downcast to bf16 once, then upcast back to fp32 on **every call, for every MoE layer**. The consumer that wanted the bf16 copy never runs. The upcast is also redundant on its own terms: the Triton `moe_fused_gate` already accepts a fp32/fp16/bf16 bias and `_router_triton_kernel` widens it in-register on load, so no host-side copy is needed in either direction. Measured on GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, 78 layers, 256 routed experts), MI355X / TP8 / conc 1 / ISL 100k / MTP: **76 extra kernel launches per target-verify forward, 0.32 ms/step.** Each launch is ~4 us of pure launch overhead for a `[256]` tensor. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py` — skip the downcast when the JIT grouped-topk router is the actual consumer: ```python # Only aiter_biased_grouped_topk wants the bias in the gating dtype. The JIT # router returns before it in biased_grouped_topk_gpu and upcasts the bias # in-register, so downcasting here would only buy it a per-call cast back. if ( _use_aiter and use_grouped_topk and correction_bias is not None and not envs.SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK.get() ): correction_bias = topk_config.correction_bias_for_dtype(router_logits.dtype) ``` Scope: - `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK` is `EnvBool(False)` by default, so the default path is byte-for-byte unchanged — the aiter branch still receives the bias in the gating dtype exactly as before. - With the flag on, `correction_bias.to(dtype=torch.float32)` in the `jit_grouped_gate` branch degenerates to a no-op for an fp32 bias, and still converts correctly for a model that genuinely stores the bias in bf16. It is kept rather than deleted so the branch stays correct regardless of what dtype the caller hands it. - The CUDA grouped-fallback branch further down `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` has the same `correction_bias.to(...)` call and is left untouched. It was never affected by this downcast anyway, since the downcast is guarded by `_use_aiter`. ## Accuracy Tests The bias reaching `_router_triton_kernel` is now the original fp32 tensor instead of a `fp32 -> bf16 -> fp32` round trip, so if anything this removes a precision loss rather than introducing one. For a model whose bias is stored in bf16 the value is identical, since bf16 -> fp32 widening is exact. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Setup: GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X (gfx950), TP8, ROCm 7.2.26015, torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.0, conc 1, ISL 100k, MTP with `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.61`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK=1`. Numbers are steady-state means over decode steps 2-4 (steps 0-1 are skipped, they carry JIT warmup). Before, per `step[TARGET_VERIFY]`: | kernel | count | time | | ------------------------------------------------ | ----- | -------- | | `at::native::bfloat16tofloat32_copy_kernel_cuda` | 76 | 0.321 ms | Expected after: 76 -> 1 per verify (only the `logits_processor` one remains), about -0.32 ms/step. trace: ## Checklist - Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #35549170704](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35549170704) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #35549170601](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35549170601) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #35549170702](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35549170702)

title: [AMD] [GLM-5.3-Flash Day 0] Enable speculative decoding (MTP) on ROCm
author: Jacob0226
body:
## Summary

#39341 brought the k-pool indexer's paged path to gfx950, but the speculative entry point still refuses ROCm: `_forward_cuda_target_verify` asserts CUDA-only, and `update_kpool_write_plan` returns before filling the write plan. Opening both to `is_hip()` is the whole change.


| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| history visible to the first speculated token | 0 tokens | the whole prompt |
| indexer scratch destination | request slot 0, every request | the request's own slot |
| GSM8K | 2.00% | **97.0%** |
| draft tokens accepted per step, of 6 | 1.33 | **4.01** |

## Scope

The two gates above, on the GLM-5.3-Flash k-pool path. CUDA takes the branch it already took. ROCm without `--speculative-algorithm` is unchanged, because ordinary decode keeps using its own fallback.

Both gates must open together: fill the plan without removing the assert and the code never runs; remove the assert without filling the plan and `plan is not None` still passes, so target-verify runs on an all-zero plan instead of failing.


## Test plan

Base `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.19-rocm720-mi35x-20260914`, sglang `main` plus the eight open Day-0 PRs (#39338, #39339, #39340, #39341, #38545, #38546, #38547, #39317). This PR is the only variable. zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash, MI355X TP4, EAGLE with 5 steps and 6 draft tokens, decode CUDA graphs on. GSM8K, 200 examples, temperature 1.0, one scoring pass each.

| Build | GSM8K | accepted per step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| baseline, MTP off | 99.5% | — |
| baseline, MTP on | 2.00% | 1.33 |
| **this PR, MTP on** | **97.0%** | **4.01** |

B200 reference for the same model and MTP settings: 97.50%, 3.25–4.12 accepted per step. MTP off staying at 99.5% is the check that ordinary decoding still uses its fallback.

## Dependency  

#39341 brought the k-pool indexer's paged path to gfx950; this PR opens the speculative entry point to it.

title: [AMD] [GLM-5.3-Flash Day 0] Load the MXFP4 MTP draft layer
author: Jacob0226
body:
## Summary

Serving `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` with MTP aborts while loading the draft: a uint8 parameter meets a bfloat16 tensor of twice its width. That ratio is an MXFP4-packed parameter meeting an unpacked weight — a block-FP8 module got built as MXFP4, its entry never found.

Two lookups miss.

1. The export pins the draft layer's 288 experts one at a time, 864 block-FP8 entries, while SGLang builds one fused module named `...mlp.experts` matching none.
2. Names are rewritten at most once — longest matching rule, then stop — so the draft's renames competed with the target's prefix strip instead of chaining.

| Draft-layer lookup | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `...layers.45.mlp.experts` resolves to | fp4 per_group (model default) | fp8_e4m3 per_block [128,128] |
| `...layers.45.eh_proj` rewrites to | `model.decoder.eh_proj` (no such module) | `model.eh_proj` |

## Scope

`_find_matched_config`'s per-expert resolution, and the GLM-5.3-Flash draft's name mapping. Checkpoints whose entries already match a module by name resolve exactly as before, and the FP8 build of the same model is untouched. Experts have to agree for a fused module to mean anything, so partial or conflicting coverage raises rather than handing one expert's scheme to the whole bank; `can_fuse_shared_expert` already reads that as cannot-fuse. The draft's rules spell out both namings instead of changing `WeightsMapper` semantics, to keep the change off every other model's mapping.

## Test plan

Base `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.19-rocm720-mi35x-20260914`, sglang `main` plus the eight open Day-0 PRs (#39338, #39339, #39340, #39341, #38545, #38546, #38547, #39317) and #39778. This PR is the only variable. Same checkpoint, MI355X TP4, EAGLE 5 steps / 6 draft tokens, CUDA graphs on. GSM8K, 200 examples, temperature 1.0.

| Build | GSM8K | accepted per step, of 6 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| baseline, MTP on | server aborts while loading the draft | — |
| **this PR, MTP on** | **99.0%** | **4.00** |
| this PR, MTP off | 99.5% | — |

Acceptance needs #38546's `weight_scale` suffix match, without which the draft's expert scales stay at 1.0.

Name resolution is also checked against the checkpoint's 924-entry `layer_quant_config` and its six draft-layer `exclude` entries. Mapper only: before this PR the `.experts` resolution did not exist.

| Draft name mapper | queried from | experts under `model.decoder.mlp.experts` | draft-layer excludes hitting a runtime module |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | checkpoint names | 0 / 864 | 0 / 6 |
| before | normalized names | 864 / 864 | 5 / 6 |
| **this PR** | checkpoint names | **864 / 864** | **6 / 6** |
| **this PR** | normalized names | **864 / 864** | **6 / 6** |

CPU unit tests cover both namings and the four coverage cases.

title: [ROCm] feat: enable aiter allreduce fusion for GLM models
author: RuibinCheung
body:
## Motivation

Two problems, both around `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` on ROCm.

**The auto-enable never shipped, but the log announcing it did.** The ROCm
auto-enable for this fusion landed commented out in #13747, while the
`logger.info` that announces it did not. A single-node ROCm run without DP
attention has since reported the fusion as on with nothing actually setting it.
Two sites are affected: the DeepSeek-family HIP arm and the GptOss arm of
`handle_model_specific_adjustments`.

**The switch is all-or-nothing, but the fusion is not equally worthwhile in both
phases.** Fusing the post-MLP all-reduce into the next layer's residual+RMSNorm
pays off in decode, where the collective is latency-bound and the launch count
dominates. Prefill is a different regime, and there is currently no way to keep
the fusion where it pays and drop it where it does not — the operator only gets
one boolean for the whole run. For GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) we want it
on for decode and off for prefill.

## Modifications

### 1. Per-phase opt-outs under the existing master switch

`python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/exec_.py` — two new resolvable fields next
to `enable_aiter_allreduce_fusion`:

- `disable_aiter_allreduce_fusion_in_prefill`
- `disable_aiter_allreduce_fusion_in_decode`

Both default to `False`, so `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` keeps meaning
"fuse everywhere" and a run that does not pass the new flags is unchanged.

### 2. Phase-aware gate

`python/sglang/srt/layers/communicator.py` — the master-switch read moves into a
helper, and `apply_aiter_all_reduce_fusion` now takes the `ForwardBatch`:

```python
def aiter_all_reduce_fusion_enabled_for(forward_mode: ForwardMode) -> bool:
    comm = get_exec().comm
    if not comm.enable_aiter_allreduce_fusion:
        return False
    if forward_mode.is_extend_or_draft_extend_or_mixed():
        return not comm.disable_aiter_allreduce_fusion_in_prefill
    return not comm.disable_aiter_allreduce_fusion_in_decode
```

### Compatibility

- All three switches default off; a run that passes none of them behaves exactly
  as before, on every platform.
- The new fields need no `field_order.py` entry. A name that is not listed there
  sorts after every name that is, which is the only backward-compatible
  position for a new field — so `ServerArgs`' positional signature is unchanged.
- The two `assert not cfg.enable_aiter_allreduce_fusion` guards in
  `parallel_hook.py` (context parallelism, `moe_dp_size > 1`), the
  deterministic-inference override in `attention_hook.py`, and the MiniMax-M3
  override in `model_overrides/minimax_m3.py` are all untouched and stay sound:
  they gate the master switch, and the new switches can only narrow it.
- `qwen3_5._fused_ar_quant_enabled` still reads the master switch. It feeds
  `LayerCommunicator(enable_fused_ar_quant=...)` at construction time, which
  decides whether the next linear receives an fp8 tuple or bf16, so it is not a
  per-phase decision and is intentionally left alone.

title: [Feat] xing4_0: Add model support
author: PaddyXj
body:
# Add Xing4.0-29B-A4B (Xing4_0) model support

## Summary

Adds native support for the open-weights **Xing4.0-29B-A4B** model: https://huggingface.co/XingChen-AGI/Xing4.0-29B-A4B (also available on ModelScope: https://modelscope.cn/models/XingChen-AGI/Xing4.0-29B-A4B)

- **Model**: 29B total / 4B activated MoE, 40 layers, 64 routed experts (top-4), first 2 layers dense
- **Architecture**: DeepSeek-V2 building blocks (MLA attention) with Xing4-specific extensions:
  - **mHC** (multi-head residual, `hc_mult=4`) residual streams with fused `mhc_pre` / `mhc_post` TileLang kernels registered as torch custom ops for torch.compile compatibility
  - **KTEP** CPU-offloaded experts (partial expert offloading)
  - **DSA** (DeepSeek Sparse Attention) support
  - **MTP**: DeepSeek-V3-compatible MTP head reused as the EAGLE draft model (draft weights carried in the main checkpoint)
- Reuses `DeepseekV2MoE` / `DeepseekV2MLP` / `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA` / `DeepseekV2WeightLoaderMixin` and integrates with the `layer_boundary` (`append_stages`) stack abstraction
- Includes `xing4_0` reasoning parser and tool-call parser (auto-detected via `reasoning_config`)

## Changes

- `python/sglang/srt/models/xing4_0.py`: model implementation (adapted to the `append_stages` layer-boundary refactor: boundary declarations, `reduce_results=False` MLP/MoE with boundary-managed output sums, explicit TP `sum_output` in the mHC branch)
- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/layernorm/mhc.py`: `mhc_pre` splitk kernel support for `hc_hidden_size=14336`
- `python/sglang/srt/configs/xing4_0.py`: `Xing4_0Config` registered in the config registry
- `python/sglang/srt/function_call/xing4_0_detector.py`, parser name lists: `xing4_0` tool-call parser (also wired into the static CLI choices)
- `python/sglang/srt/parser/reasoning_parser.py` + names: `xing4_0` reasoning parser
- `python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/`: auto-detection hooks (reasoning/tool-call parser defaults for the architecture)
- `test/registered/moe/test_xing4_0_model.py`: GSM8K e2e regression test (nightly, `2-gpu-large`, tp=2) with the xing4_0 reasoning/tool-call parsers enabled — so future interface refactors that break this model are caught by CI
- Docs entries in `supported-models/generative_models.mdx` and `advanced_features/tool_parser.mdx`

## Test Evidence

- Server launches successfully with `--tp-size 2 --speculative-algorithm EAGLE` (auto-selected steps=3, topk=1, draft_tokens=4), MTP draft weights loaded from the main checkpoint
- Greedy decoding produces coherent Chinese output; health check passes
- Added test collected and registered for the nightly CUDA CI

```bash
sglang serve --model-path XingChen-AGI/Xing4.0-29B-A4B \
  --trust-remote-code --tp-size 2 \
  --reasoning-parser xing4_0 --tool-call-parser xing4_0 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE   # uses the checkpoint's native MTP layer

curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "model": "XingChen-AGI/Xing4.0-29B-A4B",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Introduce yourself in one sentence."}]
}'
```

## Notes for Reviewers

- The GSM8K score floor in the new test is intentionally conservative (0.3) until a reference score is established; happy to tighten after a full eval run
- mHC branch bypasses the stage boundary and completes its MLP output sum explicitly via `sum_output(SumGroup.TP)`; the boundary-managed path is used everywhere else

title: [Fix] mem-cache: Budget the non-DSA EAGLE draft KV pool at its DCP-widened size
author: jiaqiang-dot-liu
body:
## Motivation

Under DCP a non-DSA EAGLE / MTP draft pool is allocated over the allocator's widened ids: `KVCacheConfigurator.loc_space_scale` is `dcp_size` for that draft worker, and `_derive_pool_sizes` allocates `max_total_num_tokens * dcp_size` draft rows per rank. `DefaultPoolConfigurator` prices the DSA draft term and the DFLASH draft term with `dcp_size`, but its non-DSA EAGLE / STANDALONE branch prices one row of the target's per-layer KV. For an MLA draft, whose latent is the size of the target's, that is `dcp_size` times too small: `max_total_num_tokens` comes out too large, and the static pools take `(dcp_size - 1)` draft layers' worth of KV per rank out of the memory that `--mem-fraction-static` leaves for activations and CUDA graphs. A GQA/MHA draft cannot be priced from the target's per-layer KV either way: `ModelConfig.get_num_kv_heads` replicates the target's KV heads over DCP but not the draft's.

This is the MTP + DCP deployment of MLA models such as DeepSeek-V3 / R1. On DeepSeek-R1 at TP8 / DCP8 the draft pool is 20.68 GB per GPU while the budget charges it 2.59 GB, so about 18 GB of the reserve is gone before the first request. The sizing code is shared by all platforms.

An MLA draft writes only its owner rows (`loc // dcp_size`), so most of its widened allocation is never written; #43599 sizes the MLA draft pool in physical rows. This PR does not change the allocation; it makes the budget price the draft rows the pool allocates today.

## Modifications

`DefaultPoolConfigurator`: price the non-DSA EAGLE / STANDALONE draft term as `dcp_size` rows per token, each at the draft's own per-layer KV size from `_compute_cell_size(..., dcp_size=1)`. For MLA that is the target's per-layer size; a GQA/MHA draft keeps its unreplicated KV heads. At `dcp_size == 1` nothing changes.

## Accuracy Tests

The patch changes only how many KV tokens the pools hold; no kernel or model path changes.

`test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_pool_configurator.py`: 71 passed, 36 subtests passed. `test/registered/unit/managers/test_dcp_logical_capacity.py`: 3 passed.

The new `test_eagle_dcp_replicated_draft_does_not_exceed_budget` runs an MLA model and a GQA model (8 KV heads, TP8) at `dcp_size` 1 and 4 and checks that the memory the pools take, with the draft at `dcp_size` rows of its own per-layer KV, stays within the budget and uses more than 99% of it. On `main` the MLA `dcp_size=4` subtest fails with `10907136 not less than or equal to 10000000`; pricing the GQA draft from the target's per-layer KV fails the GQA `dcp_size=4` subtest with `9157632 not greater than 9900000.0`.

## Pool Sizing Measurements

`amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4-v2` (61 layers + 1 MTP layer), MI355X, TP8, `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, default `--mem-fraction-static` (0.7718), with and without this patch. Numbers are TP0 startup logs with `--load-format dummy`. With the real weights at DCP 8 the token counts differ by fewer than 60 tokens (4,818,943 before, 4,330,064 after) and the free memory is the same.

| DCP | `max_total_num_tokens` before | after | Draft pool before | after | Free after pools before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5,035,505 | 5,035,505 | 2.70 GB | 2.70 GB | 63.43 GB | 63.43 GB |
| 4 | 4,842,479 | 4,618,980 (−4.6%) | 10.39 GB | 9.91 GB | 53.74 GB | 61.61 GB |
| 8 | 4,819,001 | 4,330,117 (−10.1%) | 20.68 GB | 18.58 GB | 43.69 GB | 61.76 GB |

"Free after pools" is the `Memory pool end. avail mem` line after the draft pool is allocated. Without the fix the unbudgeted draft rows take 7.9 GB (DCP 4) and 18.1 GB (DCP 8) out of that reserve.

The capacity change matches the layer count: the budget now prices `61 + dcp` layer-equivalents instead of `61 + 1`, and `4,842,479 × 62/65 = 4,618,980` and `4,819,001 × 62/69 = 4,330,117` match the measured values. The lower capacity is the cost of pricing the draft rows that are allocated today; the previous capacity was only reachable by spending the activation reserve.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The patch only changes how many KV tokens the pools hold; no kernel or scheduling path changes.

No end-to-end throughput comparison: DeepSeek-R1 with EAGLE and DCP does not serve on ROCm `main`, with or without this patch. The non-DSA NextN draft keeps `dcp_size > 1` (`DeepseekV2AttentionMLA.__init__` only resets it for DSA drafts), so `forward_absorb_rocm_core` sends `draft_extend_v2` into the DCP decode branch with `k_window=None`, and `AiterAttnBackend.forward_extend` fails on `k.shape` while capturing the draft-extend CUDA graph. Both builds stop there, with dummy and with real weights. Pool sizing happens before that point, so the measurements above come from the full startup path.

## Reproduce

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4-v2 --trust-remote-code --tp 8 --dcp-size 8 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --load-format dummy
```

Compare the two `KV Cache is allocated` lines (target, then draft) and the `Memory pool end. avail mem` line that follows each, at `--dcp-size 1` and `--dcp-size 8`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — internal sizing correction, nothing user-facing to document.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [2/N] [Kernel] Fuse padding-preserving HiSparse slot translation
author: salexspb
body:
## PR stack

Merge in order:

1. [[1/N] [AMD] Fix HiSparse slot translation in the fused MLA KV writer](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38776)
2. [[2/N] [Kernel] Fuse padding-preserving HiSparse slot translation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39837)

This PR builds on #38776. The first two commits carry that fix; review the final commit, which combines the kernel-fusion change and its CI registration, as this step of the stack.

## Summary

Keep the existing `translate_loc_to_hisparse_device()` API and use a single Triton kernel for one-dimensional CUDA and ROCm GPU slot lists. The kernel preserves padding, supports strided inputs, and produces a contiguous result for the AITER fused KV-cache writer.

## Why translation is needed

The model’s output locations identify tokens logically. HiSparse maps those locations to rows in its GPU cache, and the fused writer needs those physical row numbers.

Negative locations represent padding and must remain unchanged:

```text
Logical output locations:    [17, 18, -1]
                              |   |   |
HiSparse mapping:          17->3 18->5  padding
                              |   |   |
Physical write slots:        [ 3,  5, -1]
                              |   |   |
Fused KV writer:           row 3 row 5 skip
```

## Before

The fused writer calls the existing translation method, which directly indexes the mapping tensor:

```text
logical locations
       |
       v
mapping[locations]
       |
       v
make contiguous -> fused KV-cache write
```

This lookup also indexes the mapping for negative locations. For example, `-1` reads the mapping’s last entry, so preserving that padding marker depends on the sentinel stored there.

## After

Callers continue to use `kv_pool.translate_loc_to_hisparse_device(...)`. The pool selects the fused kernel internally for one-dimensional CUDA and ROCm GPU slot lists; scalar inputs, page tables, and CPU inputs retain the direct gather. The fused kernel handles valid locations and padding explicitly:

```text
For each logical location
           |
           +-> location >= 0: look up its physical slot
           |
           +-> location < 0:  keep the padding value unchanged
           |
           v
contiguous physical-slot tensor -> fused KV-cache write
```

The kernel reads the input using its actual stride and writes a contiguous output. It supports `int32` and `int64`, promoting the output type when the inputs differ, and leaves the original locations unchanged. Empty inputs return an empty output without launching the kernel.

Translation still happens at each participating layer. A follow-up will separately add reuse across layers within one forward.

## Regression coverage

Coverage is organized around the boundary each test exercises:

- The new portable translation-kernel test lives under `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/` and uses the staging API for CUDA (`base-b-kernel-unit` / `1-gpu-large`) and AMD (`jit-kernel-unit` / `amd`) CI. It checks contiguous and strided locations, every `int32`/`int64` input combination, empty and block-boundary sizes, multiple negative padding values, preservation of the input, and the weak-reference mapping type used by the production allocator.
- The generic pool-routing test lives under `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/` and uses the staging API for CPU (`base-a` / `cpu`) CI. It verifies that one-dimensional GPU slot lists select the fused kernel while CPU inputs, scalars, and page tables retain the gather path.
- The existing ROCm-specific AITER integration test remains unchanged under `test/registered/amd/`. It continues to cover the gfx95 fused KV-cache writer in eager execution and graph replay.
- The existing CPU model test also remains unchanged and continues to cover the ROCm writer call site.

Focused CPU validation passes 6 tests and 6 subtests. On B200, all 96 portable-kernel correctness checks passed across shapes, dtypes, strides, padding, and graph replay. The AMD integration test is registered on MI35x CI; a fresh AMD run of the current head remains pending.

## Performance

### AMD MI355X

Measured GLM-5.2 with FP8 weights and BF16 KV cache on four AMD MI355X GPUs using tensor parallelism. Each request has 32,768 input tokens; HiSparse keeps a 4,096-token GPU buffer and restores selected past-token K/V from host memory, with attention selecting up to 2,048 tokens. We test one and four concurrent requests, measuring 192 decode intervals after 64 warmup tokens.

The comparison enables fused slot translation in isolation, with other performance features disabled, and measures both prefetch settings. Values are decode latency in milliseconds per token per request; lower is better.

| Prefetch | Concurrency | Before → after | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Disabled | 1 | 21.836 → 21.160 ms/token | 3.10% |
| Disabled | 4 | 25.604 → 24.955 ms/token | 2.53% |
| Enabled | 1 | 19.259 → 18.337 ms/token | 4.79% |
| Enabled | 4 | 22.786 → 21.859 ms/token | 4.07% |

**These measurements use the earlier internal source `f11aefc` and its translation baseline.** The base branch uses the existing direct gather. The table therefore shows the isolated feature's measured effect on that earlier baseline; the incremental performance change from the base branch to this PR has not yet been measured. Each result is from a single measurement window.

### NVIDIA B200

Measured GLM-5.2 with NVFP4 weights and BF16 KV cache on four NVIDIA B200 GPUs using tensor parallelism. Each request has a 32,768-token prompt and generates 256 tokens with HiSparse enabled. Each configuration used one server launch and five timing trials per concurrency. Values are mean warmed decode latency after 64 warmup tokens; lower is better.

| Prefetch | Concurrency | Before → after | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Disabled | 1 | 12.195 → 12.082 ms/token | 0.93% |
| Disabled | 4 | 14.728 → 14.615 ms/token | 0.77% |
| Enabled | 1 | 10.601 → 10.488 ms/token | 1.07% |
| Enabled | 4 | 12.705 → 12.580 ms/token | 0.99% |

An isolated B200 kernel benchmark found 27–28% lower translation time for the one- and four-slot decode cases. All 96 kernel correctness checks and 20 generation checks passed. Generated continuations were not token-identical, so the generation checks do not establish numerical equivalence. These performance results apply to this workload and do not isolate server-restart variability.

title: Use runtime token widths for Triton speculative verification
author: merrymercy
body:
# Summary

Triton target verification can omit the bonus token when it uses the draft proposal count for query and mask offsets. Use the speculative input's runtime token width, falling back to the model runner's capture width when metadata is absent or unset. Deterministic sliding-window attention also uses the actual prefix length and resolved verification width.

Give speculative inputs a shared optional attention-mask default while preserving Eagle's required constructor fields. Add CPU regression coverage for eager metadata, capture, padded replay, and sliding-window offsets.

title: [AMD][bugfix] Fix dsv4 server launch
author: RolaoDenthu
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
#39652 (`13d593b6cf`) breaks the JIT build. It added the V4.1 row quantizers behind`#ifndef USE_ROCM` in `kv_layout.cuh`, 
branch that a V4 instantiation discards, but a discarded branch is still parsed and the
name does not depend on the template parameters, so lookup runs on it whatever the layout
being compiled, and every ROCm build of those headers fails:
```
fused_norm_rope_v2.cuh:507:18: error: no member named 'v41' in namespace 'sglang::deepseek_v4'
```
#37810 (`a813224e78`) breaks target-verify metadata. It added the `req_pool_indices_repeated` parameter to `_attach_unified_kv_prefill_meta` and updated one of its two call sites. The other one, in `make_forward_metadata_from_raw_verify`, is left one positional argument short, so `num_tokens` never binds and the call raises `TypeError`.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
- `kv_layout.cuh`: declare a `v41::store_row` stub under `USE_ROCM` so the name resolves there. Its `static_assert` depends on `kLayout`, so it fires only when a kernel really instantiates a V4.1 layout — which the Python side already refuses on ROCm (`compress.py`, `attn.py` and `elementwise.py` all assert "the V4.1 KV layouts are CUDA (sm100) only"). Nothing inside the `#ifndef USE_ROCM` branch changed, so CUDA codegen is untouched.
- `deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py`: pass `req_pool_indices_repeated` from `make_forward_metadata_from_raw_verify` as well.

title: [NPU] Fuse MXFP4 W4A8 MoE gmm1 + swiglu + requant into one kernel
author: iridiumine
body:
## Motivation

The unfused MXFP4 W4A8 MoE chain runs three kernels per MoE layer for the gate/up projection: gmm1, a separate swiglu activation kernel, and a dynamic MX requant. NPU A5 already provides `npu_grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2`, which folds all three into a single aclnn kernel.

## Modifications

- `NPUW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod` gains `apply_fused_gmm1_swiglu`, mirroring `NPUMXFP8MoEMethod`: same fused-kernel call shape, with the FP4 weight dtype and e8m0 weight/x scale dtypes. `pertoken_scale` handling matches the class's existing unfused `apply()` (quantize on the DeepEP bf16 path; pair-reshape when a scale is handed over).
- The Ascend MoE runner replaces the `NPUMXFP8MoEMethod` isinstance check with a `_uses_fused_gmm1(kernel)` probe, so both MXFP8 and MXFP4 W4A8 skip the separate activation step; the fail-loudly semantics of  `self.activation = None` are preserved.

## Accuracy Tests

title: [Moe] Fix flashinfer_trtllm silently dropping swiglu_limit clamped SwiGLU activation
author: Dovis01
body:
## Motivation

Models with a clamped SwiGLU activation (e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash / GLM-5-Next, Qwen3-Next style) plumb the clamp limit through `FusedMoE(swiglu_limit=...)` -> `MoeRunnerConfig.swiglu_limit`. All MoE runner backends are supposed to honor it: `triton` passes it into the fused kernel, `deep_gemm` applies it via `silu_and_mul_clamp` / `_apply_swiglu_limit`, but `flashinfer_trtllm` **silently ignores it**.

The flashinfer_trtllm FP8 path only materializes `gemm1_clamp_limit` (the TRT-LLM kernel parameter), which stays `None` for models that use the `swiglu_limit` field. With no error and no warning, the expert activation degrades from the trained `silu(clamp(gate, max=L)) * clamp(up, -L, L)` (with L = 10.0) to a plain `silu(gate) * up`, which measurably hurts accuracy.

On GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 (blockwise 128x128 FP8, 288 routed experts, top-8, 1 shared expert, `swiglu_limit=10.0`), GSM8K 5-shot with only `--moe-runner-backend` varying:

| moe_runner_backend | GSM8K strict-match (runs) | mean |
|---|---|---|
| triton | 0.9356 / 0.9363 | 0.9360 |
| deep_gemm | 0.9249 / 0.9287 / 0.9295 / 0.9310 / 0.9340 / 0.9348 | 0.9305 |
| flashinfer_trtllm (before) | 0.9265 / 0.9280 / 0.9287 | 0.9277 |
| **flashinfer_trtllm (this fix)** | **0.9348 / 0.9371** | **0.9360** |

Before/after ranges do not overlap (within-group variance is ~0.2pp); after the fix flashinfer_trtllm matches the triton baseline exactly. fix https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/39797. Thx for finding this issue. @NolenLiang

## Modifications

Single-file change in `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py`, `Fp8MoEMethod._prepare_flashinfer_trtllm_activation_params()`: when `gemm1_clamp_limit` is not explicitly set, fall back to `swiglu_limit`.

Why here and not in the model code: this function is the only consumer that builds the TRT-LLM SwiGLU parameters (`gemm1_alpha/beta/clamp_limit`), so the two naming pipelines (`gemm1_clamp_limit` used by gpt_oss / bailing_moe_v3, `swiglu_limit` used by DeepseekV2MoE-family models) converge at a single point; `triton` consumes both fields independently (`gemm1_limit` and `swiglu_limit`), so setting both at the model level would change behavior of unrelated backends, while this fallback is scoped to the flashinfer_trtllm preparation only. Models that already set `gemm1_clamp_limit` explicitly (gpt_oss, bailing_moe_v3) are unaffected, and the same silent drop is fixed for every other model that routes the clamp through `swiglu_limit` (e.g. Qwen3-Next) whenever flashinfer_trtllm is used.

The TRT-LLM kernel natively supports the clamp: with `ActivationType.Swiglu`, `gemm1_clamp_limit=L` computes `X2 = clamp(X2, max=L)`, `X1 = clamp(X1, -L, L)`, `out = X2 * sigmoid(alpha * X2) * (X1 + beta)` (alpha defaults to 1.0, beta to 0.0), which matches the reference `swiglu_clamped` in `models/glm5_next.py` exactly. Verified against flashinfer 0.6.18 (`trtllm_fp8_block_scale_moe`, `Fp8QuantizationType.DeepSeekFp8`).

## Accuracy Tests

Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (FP8, blockwise 128x128), 4x B200, TP=4/EP=4. Launch (only `--moe-runner-backend` varies between runs):

```bash
 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend trtllm --dsa-decode-backend trtllm \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
  --context-length 16384 --disable-radix-cache \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --served-model-name glm-5-next-fp8
```

Eval (lm-evaluation-harness, `local-completions`):

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args "model=glm-5-next-fp8,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None" \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --gen_kwargs temperature=0,max_gen_toks=512 --seed 1234 --log_samples
```

Results (exact_match, strict-match):

| config | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 | mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| flashinfer_trtllm before | 0.9287 | 0.9265 | 0.9280 | 0.9277 |
| flashinfer_trtllm **after** | 0.9371 | 0.9348 | – | **0.9360** |
| triton (baseline) | 0.9363 | 0.9356 | – | 0.9360 |

Fixed server sanity-checked with deterministic generation (temperature=0) on GSM8K-style prompts before running the evals.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not affected. The change only materializes one extra per-expert fp32 tensor (`[num_local_experts]`, 288 bytes here) once at weight-load time; the hot kernel call is unchanged (the `gemm1_clamp_limit` argument was already being passed, as `None`). No throughput regression expected or observed.

title: [DSV4] Generalize attention metadata, sparse prefill, and KV pool over compress ratios
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary
- Make the set of compressed-KV ratios data owned by the KV pool (`present_ratios`) and give the shared code one accessor per concept keyed by ratio, instead of hard-coding c4 / c128 in field names, branches and PD payload code
- No behavior change for V4: every existing path produces the same tensors and indices (see Verification); the new surface is consumed by #38798

## Changes
**Attention metadata (`DSV4AttnMetadata`)**
- Rename `c4_sparse_topk` -> `index_topk` (the indexer's top-k, not a c4 property); add required `present_ratios` from the pool
- Build compression metadata, FlashMLA schedules, compressor and indexer metadata only for present ratios; CP reindex treats per-ratio fields as optional; `copy_` / breakable-CUDA-graph refresh check `present_ratios`
- Add ratio-keyed `sparse_page_indices(r)`, `sparse_topk_lengths(r)`, `sparse_raw_indices(r)` and the writer `set_sparse_topk(r, ...)`; call sites and the attention test kit use them, `forward` dispatches on `compress_ratio != 0` (storage stays flat)

**Sparse prefill (`SparsePrefillChunkCache`, `combine_topk_swa_indices`)**
- Kernel takes each row's absolute `query_pos` instead of assuming rows are the trailing extend tokens, and keeps `-1` entries inside the top-k span as `-1` instead of shifting them by `compressed_base` (both identities on V4 inputs)
- `build()` takes `query_lens` / `query_pos` alongside `extend_seq_lens` (the SWA gather still spans the whole extend)
- Keep per-ratio gather state in `CompressedGather`, keyed by ratio in `cache.compressed` (c128 included); both sparse-prefill forwards share `cache.layer_inputs(...)`

**KV pool and PD state**
- Add `DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool.present_ratios`; `CompressStatePool.request_scoped` (set by the pool factory) replaces `ratio == 128` checks in the state-buffer bookkeeping
- PD prefill/decode call `request_state_transfer_indices(req_pool_idx, seq_len)` / `clear_request_scoped_state(req_pool_idx)` on the pool instead of combining an env lookup, `get_ring_size(128)` and a c128 helper; the index arithmetic moves to `deepseek_v4_compress_state.py` (`c4_state_transfer_indices`, `request_scoped_state_transfer_indices`, `CompressStatePool.transfer_indices`)
- Set `mla_compression_ratios` in `setup_state_kv_args` for both roles
- Add `get_swa_key_layout` / `get_extra_key_layout` / `get_*_bytes_per_token` so the attention kernel views each cache with its own row width (the extra cache previously reused the SWA width)

**Removed**
- `is_dsv4_c128_online_enabled` (the pool's `online` flag is the single source), `CompressedGather.page_size` (unused), `get_dsv4_c4_state_indices` / `get_dsv4_c128_state_indices` in `disaggregation/utils.py` (moved as above)

## Verification
- AST comparison against main per function: only the functions listed above differ
- Differential dump of the V4 paths (metadata init for prefill / decode / trtllm, `copy_`, refresh, CP reindex; chunk-cache build, c128 / c4 gathers and combines; pool state-buffer bookkeeping and request-state clear; PD request-state indices) between main and this branch: 274 shared entries, 0 mismatches (main-only entries are the renamed `c4_sparse_topk`)
- Registered tests pass: `test_deepseek_v4.py` (incl. real sparse-prefill c4 / c128 vs. torch reference), `test_q8kv8_sparse_prefill_backend.py`, `test_disaggregation_wire.py`, `test_dsv4_c4_state_lifecycle.py`, `test_dsv4_compressed_pools.py`, `test_dsv4_unified_fp8_pool.py`, `test_deepseek_v4_compress_state_runtime_shapes.py`
- New: `test/registered/kernel/attention/test_combine_topk_swa_indices.py` (torch oracle: trailing extend, `-1` holes, non-trailing `query_pos` with cross-chunk offset, SWA-only); metadata contract tests for `present_ratios` gating, accessor / writer routing and CP reindex; pool request-state transfer tests

title: [ROCm] topk v2: split one long row across blocks, the CDNA cluster-path equivalent
author: EricKing626
body: ## Motivation By default, top-k v2 launches one block per row, so a long row is scanned by a single block **while most CUs sit idle**. On NVIDIA Hopper+, rows above a length threshold are split across a block cluster that shares DSMEM. CDNA has no clusters or DSMEM, so ROCm do not support top-k v2's cluster path. This happens often in reasoning-model decode: small batch, long context. This PR adds a row split to top-k v2 for ROCm. It uses two launches: one to build the histogram, one to select the top-k from it, and global memory takes the place of DSMEM. - **When it engages:** small batch, long context: `batch_size <= 64` and rows longer than a batch-dependent floor (40K at small batch). Everything else runs the existing path unchanged. - **Kernel speedup:** 1.8–3.0x at batch 1–8 with 128K+ context; 1.56x geomean across all gated shapes. - **End to end (GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4, MI355X):** - Single request: - TP4, batch 1 and 120K context, the decode top-k kernel is 2.07x faster and median ITL drops 3.8%. - TP4, batch 1 and 600K context, the decode top-k kernel is 6.42x faster and median ITL drops **18.7%**. - Agentic replay: compared with the packed-only top-k v2 baseline, adding row split improves: - P90 interactivity by **+11.3%** at TP8 and +3.5% at TP4. - Token TPUT per chip by +1.9% at TP8 and **+5.9%** at TP4. - Each figure is a geomean over c1/c4 for TP8 and over c4/c8/c12 for TP4. ## Modifications Originally, one block handles one row, so batch 8 over 128K uses only 8 blocks on a 256-CU GPU. CUDA splits a row across a cluster; CDNA has no clusters or DSMEM, so on ROCm this shape runs narrow. With this PR, each row is split across 8 blocks, so the same shape uses 64 blocks **Row length L**: how many KV positions each query token picks its top-k from, i.e. its context length. **Score rows R**: how many query tokens one top-k launch handles, one row each: - decode without MTP: **batch size** - decode with MTP: batch size × draft tokens, since the verify pass scores every draft token A long row is split across several blocks so a small R no longer leaves most CUs idle. Two launches, with the kernel boundary as the sync (no spinning): 1. `topk_split_hist`: each block builds the histogram of its slice of the row. 2. `topk_split_select`: each block finds the threshold from the merged histogram and writes its candidates; the last block resolves ties and applies the page-table transform. Each row is split `clamp(64 / R, 4, 32)` ways, aiming at about 64 blocks per launch: more than that and the cross-block cost, which grows with `R * split`, outweighs the shorter scan. The split turns on only when: - `R <= CU count / 4` (64 on MI355X), since past that even a 4-way split oversubscribes the GPU, and - L is long enough to pay for the extra launch: from 40K at small R, higher as R grows. ```math \mathrm{TopK}_k(s)=\lbrace i: b(s_i)>b^{\ast}\rbrace \cup \mathrm{Tie}_{k-n_{>}}\lbrace i: b(s_i)=b^{\ast}\rbrace,\quad b^{\ast}=\max\Big\lbrace b:\sum_{r=1}^{S}\sum_{i\in C_r}\mathbf{1}[b(s_i)\ge b]\ge k\Big\rbrace,\quad S=\mathrm{clamp}\big(\lfloor 64/R\rfloor,4,32\big)\ \text{when}\ R\le N_{\mathrm{CU}}/4 \wedge L>F(R) ``` where - $s_i$: score of KV position $i$, $i=1..L$; $k$ = 2048 for GLM-5.2. - $b(s_i)$: the score's top 12 bits, i.e. its histogram bin. - $S$: blocks per row; $C_r$: the slice of the row block $r$ scans. - $n_{>}$: elements strictly above the threshold bin $b^{\ast}$; $\mathrm{Tie}_m$: the exact top $m$ inside that bin. - $F(R)$: shortest row worth splitting: ```math F(R)=\begin{cases}40960 & R\le 8\\ 49152 & R\le 16\\ 65536 & R\le 32\\ 114688 & R>32\end{cases} ``` ## Scope - CUDA untouched: preprocessed TU is byte-identical to baseline without `USE_ROCM`. - Decode only. Prefill / ragged / packed do not reach the new path. - One file (topk_v2.cuh‎) plus its test. ## Correctness - `test_topk_v2.py` on gfx950: **294 passed** (288 existing + 6 new). - Output matches `torch.topk` exactly, ties included. New `test_topk_v2_split_duplicate_scores` covers heavy ties at the threshold, which the existing suite didn't. - 12-bit histogram, same as the `TopKStreaming` path it replaces on ROCm. ## Performance **Baseline:** `topk_v2` at this PR's parent commit — the kernel this PR edits, and the one GLM uses on ROCm since #36851 made it the default. The other ROCm implementation, the native `topk.hip` cooperative kernel from [#37591](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37591), sits behind `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=0` and is not touched. MI355X, `k=2048`, `page_size=64`, vs. `topk_v2` at the parent commit. All 71 gated points are >= 1.00x: worst 1.06x, best 3.03x, geomean 1.56x. | B | L | before (us) | after (us) | speedup | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 128K | 33.50 | 16.70 | **2.01x** | | 8 | 128K | 33.78 | 18.94 | **1.78x** | | 32 | 128K | 33.95 | 25.29 | 1.34x | | 64 | 128K | 35.94 | 33.89 | 1.06x | | 4 | 256K | 53.71 | 19.07 | **2.82x** | | 128 | 128K | 38.11 | 38.08 | 1.00x (outside gate) | ## GLM-5.2 results GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4 on MI355X **End to end (median ITL):** | config | baseline (ms) | split (ms) | change | |---|---|---|---| | ISL 8K / OSL 1024, conc 8 (below floor) | 12.31 | 12.27 | -0.3% | | ISL 70K / OSL 300, conc 4 | 11.21 | 11.00 | -1.9% | | ISL 70K / OSL 300, conc 8 | 12.89 | 12.67 | -1.7% | | ISL 120K / OSL 300, conc 4 | 11.54 | 11.13 | -3.6% | | **ISL 120K / OSL 2000, conc 1** | 10.29 | 9.90 | **-3.8%** | | **ISL 200K / OSL 1000, conc 4** | 11.77 | 11.07 | **-6.0%** | | **ISL 300K / OSL 1000, conc 2** | 11.58 | 10.42 | **-10.0%** | | **ISL 400K / OSL 1000, conc 1** | 11.16 | 9.84 | **-11.8%** | | **ISL 600K / OSL 1000, conc 1** | 12.32 | 10.02 | **-18.7%** | No config is slower. TTFT is unchanged, so prefill is unaffected. **Accuracy (TP4)**: GSM8k 0.933 → 0.936, baseline → split (1200 questions). **Accuracy (TP8)**: GSM8k 0.934 → 0.933, baseline → split (1200 questions). ## Checklist - [x] `pre-commit` on changed files - [x] gfx950 correctness — 294 passed, incl. new duplicate-score test - [x] gfx950 kernel benchmarks - [x] CUDA compile check — preprocessed TU byte-identical; real `nvcc` run still needs CI - [x] GLM-5.2 A/B — 1.41x kernel, -1.7% to -3.8% median ITL, none slower, GSM8k within noise --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #36693493288](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36693493288) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #36693492711](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36693492711) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #36693493355](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36693493355)

title: [Moe] Honor swiglu_limit clamped activation in flashinfer_cutlass runner
author: Dovis01
body:
## Motivation

Models with a clamped SwiGLU activation (GLM-5 / GLM-5-Next, Qwen3-Next, GPT-OSS; configured as `swiglu_limit` or `gemm1_clamp_limit` in `MoeRunnerConfig`) silently lose the clamp on the `flashinfer_cutlass` MoE runner and run plain SwiGLU experts, for two stacked reasons: the runner's `_run_flashinfer_cutlass` never passed the per-expert SwiGLU parameters to the kernel, and its quant-info construction sites never filled them.

This path is not theoretical: on SM120 (RTX 50 series) `modelopt_fp4` is auto-pinned to `flashinfer_cutlass` because trtllm-gen MoE kernels are SM100-only (`arg_groups/overrides.py`), so NVFP4 GPT-OSS variants on SM120 hit exactly this gap today. The unquantized bf16 path is affected the same way.

For reference, the identical activation bug on the FP8 `flashinfer_trtllm` path cost GLM-5.3-Flash ~0.9pp GSM8K (92.77 -> 93.60, restored to the triton baseline; see companion PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39920).

## Modifications

Three files, all in the flashinfer_cutlass path; models without a configured clamp keep passing `None` and are bit-for-bit unchanged:

1. `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py`: add `swiglu_alpha/beta/limit` fields to `FlashInferCutlassMoeQuantInfo` (the mxfp4 sibling dataclass already had them) and pass them from `_run_flashinfer_cutlass` into `cutlass_fused_moe`.

2. `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py` (NVFP4 + cutlass branch): fill the fields from `MoeRunnerConfig` with the same `gemm1_clamp_limit or swiglu_limit` fallback and SiTU exception already used by the ModelOpt flashinfer_trtllm branch. When a clamp is configured, alpha/beta default to the silu-neutral 1.0 / 0.0 unless the model sets `gemm1_alpha` / `gemm1_beta`.

3. `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py` (bf16 + cutlass branch): same fill.

Unit convention: the CUTLASS kernel applies the clamp on dequantized values, so the limit is passed in physical units -- unlike trtllm-gen, where the limit must be divided by `g1_alphas` (see `modelopt_quant.py` trtllm branch). This was verified against flashinfer's own fp32-dequantized reference implementation in `tests/moe/test_trtllm_cutlass_fused_moe.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

No SM120 GPU was available, so verification was done at the kernel and runner level on B200:

Kernel-level bf16 A/B (E=8, H=256, I=128, T=64, top-2; 5.8% of gemm1 activations beyond the limit), comparing `flashinfer.cutlass_fused_moe` against a dequantized-fp32 reference:

| config | rel err vs reference |
|---|---|
| no clamp (all swiglu args None) | 0.0038 |
| clamp=10 (alpha=1.0, beta=0.0) | 0.0036 |

Clamp effect size matches the reference: 0.2185 (kernel) vs 0.2183 (reference). This confirms the kernel formula `silu(clamp(gate, max=L)) * (clamp(up, -L, L) + beta)` with the up half stored first in w13 (matching `_stack_up_gate_w13` in the mxfp4 path).

Integrated runner smoke test (single-process NCCL init, real `_run_flashinfer_cutlass` call with `FlashInferCutlassMoeQuantInfo` carrying the clamp tensors): plain rel err 0.0038, clamped rel err 0.0036, clamp effect 0.2185 -- the full quant_info -> runner -> kernel chain is verified. This smoke test also caught (and verified the fix of) a missing-dataclass-field error before commit.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not affected. The change adds three optional kernel arguments (already `None` by default) and three per-expert fp32 tensors materialized once at weight-load time only when a clamp is configured. The hot kernel call is unchanged for unconfigured models.

## Note
Known pre-existing gap: GPT-OSS bf16 expert biases are still dropped on the flashinfer_cutlass NVFP4 path — FlashInferCutlassMoeQuantInfo has no bias fields and _run_flashinfer_cutlass never passes fc1/fc2_expert_biases (only the MXFP4 sibling does). Fixing it needs a flashinfer cutlass_fused_moe API extension; out of scope here.

title: [Feat] [NPU] DSpark: Support dsv4 dspark on ascend 950
author: randgun
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Enable DeepSeek V4 DSpark speculative decoding on NPU Ascend 950 (arch35). The existing DSpark implementation only supported CUDA and older NPU (arch22). Arch35 hardware requires different sparse-attention operators, weight-loading strategies, and numerical compatibility workarounds. Several follow-up fixes address a regression where DSpark's unquantized `wo_a` path conflicted with the arch35 MXFP8 detection logic, plus NPU-specific numerical gaps.

## Modifications

- **arch35 DSpark sparse attention**: Added arch35-specific v2 sparse attention operators via a new `TorchOpLoader` extension; loaded during TP worker and DSpark draft worker initialization.
- **`wo_a` quantization fix**: `use_npu_arch35_mxfp8_wo_a()` now accepts a `wo_a_keeps_quant_config` parameter and returns `False` when DSpark explicitly disables `wo_a` quantization. This fixes a regression introduced by a previous commit that changed the assertion condition from `if fp8:` to `if quantize_wo_a:`, which caused an incorrect assertion on arch35 because DSpark's `wo_a` was not quantized. The model also caches this value instead of recomputing it at each call site.
- **DSpark stage configuration**: Added `_dspark_stage_config()` to apply draft-specific expert counts to draft stages and disable vision layers for text-only stages. Arch35 now falls back to standard vocabulary/fusion behavior instead of the arch31-specific path.
- **Weight loading**: Moved the NPU `weight_packed` → `weight` rename before stacked parameter mapping, eliminating duplicated branch logic.

## Accuracy Tests

| Model | Dataset | Metric | Subset | Num | Score |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 | GPQA-Diamond | Accuracy ↑ | gpqa_diamond | 198 | 89.9% |

## Speed Tests and Profiling
| Model | Dataset | Num | Avg Lat | Avg TTFT | Avg TPOT | Avg Thpt | Avg In | Avg Out |
|---|-----|------|---------|---------|---------|----------|------|-----|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash| GPQA-Diamond | 198 | 149.111 s | 1943.3 ms | 14.3 ms | 67 tok/s | 344 | 9991 |

title: [ci][xpu] Re-seed the wan2_1_t2v_1.3b perf baseline on Arc Pro B60
author: arathi-hlab
body:
## Motivation

The `multimodal-gen-test-1-gpu-xpu` lane is red on main after #36825. The failure is a stale baseline, not a regression: #36825 made `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b` **36% faster** on Arc Pro B60, but `expected_avg_denoise_ms` is computed over *all* steps including step 0, and step 0 now pays a one-time Triton JIT compile that lands inside the timed window.

From run [35074312985 / job 104723059209](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35074312985/job/104723059209):

| metric | baseline | measured | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DenoisingStage` | 114601.91 ms | 73363.89 ms | **-36.0%** |
| `expected_e2e_ms` | 116299.31 ms | 75344.43 ms | **-35.2%** |
| median denoise step | 86.07 ms | 103.18 ms | passed (limit 111.9) |
| avg denoise step | 88.83 ms | 169.74 ms | **failed** (limit 115.48) |
| step 0 | 208.34 ms | 3421.66 ms | 16x |

Exactly one assertion fires (`Average Denoise Step`). Steady-state steps 1-49 sit in the 101-109 ms band; excluding step 0 the mean is 103.37 ms, comfortably inside tolerance. The mean is poisoned by step 0 alone. The other three XPU cases pass unchanged.

## Modifications

Re-seed only the `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b` scenario in `xpu_b60.json` from the run above, and update `metadata`. No other scenario, tolerance, or sampling value is touched.

`estimated_full_test_time_s` is deliberately left at 331.5 — it is a suite-partitioning estimate rather than a gate, and this run does not give a clean replacement for it.

## Checklist

- [x] Baseline values transcribed from a real CI run on the target runner pool
- [x] JSON validated and self-consistent (`sum(denoise_step_ms)/50 == expected_avg_denoise_ms`)
- [x] Diff scoped to the one failing scenario plus metadata

## Note on verification

The seeded numbers come from a run at `2b93addf58`. main has advanced since (including `c525ed8f02`, "preserve explicit attention backends during autotune", which could plausibly shift XPU wan timings). This PR's own `multimodal-gen-test-1-gpu-xpu` run is the verification — if the lane is still red, the failure output will carry the numbers to re-seed with.

title: [ci][xpu] Record device time in the multimodal_gen perf lane
author: arathi-hlab
body:
## Motivation

`StageProfiler` brackets each stage and denoise step with `time.perf_counter()`, and only drains the device queue when `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1` -- which defaults off. Kernel launches are asynchronous, so what the XPU lane records for a denoise step is host submission cost, not execution.

CUDA gets away with the default because its launch queue is bounded (~1024 pending launches): the host blocks on backpressure and the wall-clock timer incidentally tracks device time. The SYCL/Level-Zero queue is deep enough that a step returns long before its work runs.

A stage should be roughly the sum of its steps. In `xpu_b60.json` on current `main`:

| scenario | steps | sum(step_ms) | DenoisingStage | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `zimage_image_t2i` | 9/9 | 7524.0 | 8361.1 | 1.11 |
| `flux_2_klein_image_t2i` | 4/4 | 135.3 | 2518.5 | **18.61** |
| `flux_2_klein_base_image_t2i` | 50/50 | 1841.5 | 55237.4 | **30.00** |
| `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b` | 50/50 | 4441.7 | 114601.9 | **25.80** |

Three of the four scenarios are 18-30x short, so `expected_avg_denoise_ms` and `expected_median_denoise_ms` guard an enqueue rate rather than the model. For wan that is ~89 ms against an actual ~2292 ms per step -- about 4% of the work, so a real DiT slowdown would not move the recorded number and the gate cannot detect it. The gate is also one-sided (`_assert_le`), so an understated baseline never fails on its own; it just quietly stops measuring.

Reported by @ckvermaAI.

## Modifications

One line in `.github/workflows/pr-test-xpu.yml`: pass `-e SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1` to the `docker exec` that runs the 1-GPU diffusion suite. The env var and the sync it controls already exist; this only turns them on for this lane. (`docker exec` needs the explicit `-e` -- a job-level `env:` does not cross into the container.)

Measured effect on wan: per-step timings go from ~101 ms to ~1444 ms, and `sum(steps)` vs `DenoisingStage` becomes 72200 vs 72314, a ratio of **1.002**. The 25.8x gap closes.

Second file: `xpu_b60.json`, re-seeded for all four scenarios (see *Baseline re-seed* below).

## Trade-offs

- **Cost:** serializing the stage boundaries adds ~3-4% end-to-end. Acceptable for a lane whose job is measurement.
- **Scope:** XPU-only. No other vendor's baseline or timing changes.
- **Limitation:** the flag serializes stage boundaries, so the lane becomes less sensitive to regressions that show up as lost pipelining rather than slower kernels. On the reference run `DenoisingStage` moved +0.06% while e2e moved +4.1% -- the added cost landed entirely outside denoising. The e2e assertion still covers that direction.
- **Limitation:** a queue drain does not exclude host work *inside* the timed window, so step 0 keeps its Triton JIT cost (3421.66 ms against a 208.34 ms baseline on the current wan run).

## Alternative considered

Timing with `torch.<dev>.Event(enable_timing=True)` inside `StageProfiler` needs no sync at all and costs nothing. It is the better long-term mechanism, but it changes the recorded quantity for all six platforms that carry a baseline file (`h100`, `b200`, `5090`, `xpu_b60`, `ascend/perf_baselines_npu`, `musa/perf_baselines_musa`), and several CUDA scenarios already sit at ratios of 1.13-2.00 against tolerances of 0.25-0.35 -- so flipping the source would need a coordinated re-seed per vendor. Deferred; the prototype is on `xpu/stage-profiler-device-events-archive`.

## Baseline re-seed

Done, from run 35563559050 job 106220948594 (this branch, flag on). Two separate things had to be fixed:

**`expected_load_ms` was absent for every XPU scenario.** This, not the enqueue numbers, is what the lane actually died on first. `_validate_and_record` calls `validate_load()` unconditionally on every platform, so all four cases raised `Load baseline missing or invalid` and `Ran 0 tests` before a single timing was compared. `h100.json` carries the key 73 times, `5090.json` 6, `b200.json` 5, `xpu_b60.json` zero -- the XPU file was never updated when the load gate landed, and the lane is path-filtered (it did not execute in the last ~150 `pr-test-xpu` runs), so it went unnoticed.

**Denoise references re-seeded.** As predicted above, only `zimage_image_t2i` had been seeded with the flag on; the other three were 14-31x below what the lane now measures.

| scenario | median step, old -> new | `expected_load_ms` |
|---|---|---|
| `zimage_image_t2i` | 927.61 -> 859.76 (already device time) | 33283.41 |
| `flux_2_klein_image_t2i` | 17.58 -> **537.70** | 26566.83 |
| `flux_2_klein_base_image_t2i` | 34.84 -> **1068.45** | 31539.71 |
| `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b` | 103.18 -> **1400.58** | 48009.32 |

e2e moves within a few percent everywhere, as expected -- the sync redistributes time into the steps rather than adding any.

Every value is the max over that job's 7 attempts, matching the aggregation in `_dump_baseline_for_testcase`. Variance across those attempts:

- **Denoise and e2e are stable:** <=2% spread, 0.0-0.1% on `zimage` and `wan2_1`.
- **`expected_load_ms` is not:** 22%, 40%, 41% and 84% spread, with `wan2_1` ranging 23.2s -> 48.0s. It is wall-clock to the worker's load marker, so it is dominated by shared-runner host I/O rather than by anything this PR touches. Seeded from the max and guarded only by the wide `e2e` tolerance; if it flakes, the fix is a per-case `timing_tolerance`, not a tighter number. The range is recorded in `metadata.description`.

Replaying every gate assertion (`calculate_upper_bound`, per-stage tolerance selection, sampled step indices, the step-0 exemption) over 4 scenarios x 7 attempts: 448 assertions, 0 failures.

Also adds the `estimated_full_test_time_s` CI asked for on `flux_2_klein_base_image_t2i`. It is advisory -- logged at teardown, never asserted -- so it was not part of the failure.

## Follow-ups (not in scope here)

- `expected_avg_denoise_ms` / `expected_median_denoise_ms` include step 0, while the per-step check already exempts it (`FIRST_DENOISE_STEP_TOLERANCE = 4.0`).
- The XPU cases run with no warmup (`enable_torch_compile=False` leaves `warmup_mode=None`), so step 0 pays compile cost every run.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci).
- [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation).
- [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/benchmark/gsm8k/README.md).
- [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR.
- [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR.

title: [DSV4.1] Big fused wo_a quant
author: DarkSharpness
body:
## Motivation

On small DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4 batches, inverse RoPE, WO-A projection, and MXFP8 quantization require separate kernel launches. This PR fuses the sequence to reduce launch and intermediate-memory overhead.

## Changes

- Add the SM100/SM103 fused inverse-RoPE + WO-A kernel, with BF16 or FlashInfer-swizzled MXFP8 output, for up to 32 token rows and the supported `(groups, rank, K) = (2, 1024, 4096)` shape.
- Dispatch it for eligible DSV4.1 layers; preserve main's model-type gating, NPU WO-A path, and the existing fallback for other shapes/backends.
- Add the JIT CUDA-driver link support and mbarrier helper required by the kernel.
- Keep 18 focused correctness cases in `test/registered/kernels/`: BF16/MXFP8 output, padded inputs, token-count boundaries, scale padding, and int32/int64 positions. Validate scales in bulk and update the WO-A imports in existing tests.

## Validation

Rebased onto `main` at `a6cf05817f11d22023fd951a76255ef50fb09f49`, after #38798 and #40039 landed. All local pre-commit checks on changed files passed. Full suite-registration validation passed for all 2,489 registrations; the experimental benchmark with an invalid B200 suite has been removed, along with its unrelated global benchmark changes. Vectorized scale indexing was checked against all 8,192 original offsets. CI is rerunning on the updated head. GPU tests and benchmarks have not yet been rerun on this new main-based revision.

Historical measurements on `e919e8be784473d2fb7ea10d10f45c23af658f68` and its direct parent:

- 4×GB300, TP4/EP1, concurrency 1, 4096 input / 1024 output, DSPARK block size 5, simulated acceptance length 5.5: median client decode throughput **1167.22 → 1202.65 tokens/s (+3.03%)**. The 18 added kernel correctness tests passed. [Full setup and results](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39957#issuecomment-5713670135).
- Real-acceptance accuracy checks covered GSM8K, AIME 2026, and GPQA, with repeated GSM8K runs. These are not a claim of exact numerical/statistical equivalence. [Accuracy results and limitations](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39957#issuecomment-5715581204).

title: [AMD] dsv4: pick kv_splits per index stream, not by occupancy alone
author: kkHuang-amd
body:
`_kv_splits_heuristic` splits only when the base grid underfills the device. That is the wrong question for the V4 sparse decode kernel. At bs=14 the grid nearly saturates (196 CTAs against a 384 target) so it picks splits=1, while the cost is set by ONE straggler CTA walking ~5,000 KV entries beside CTAs walking 200. Splitting breaks up that CTA; occupancy never sees it.

The discriminator is static and available at capture time: `compress_ratio`. CSA (ratio 4) is clamped to `index_topk`+128 = 1152 and is nearly uniform, so split-K loses on it (+5.1% at bs=14). HCA (ratio 128) is unclamped, kv_len is ~context/128 and reaches ~5,000, dispersion 0.70-0.78, and split-K wins at every kv_len the run traverses. Only HCA is overridden; SWA and CSA keep the existing heuristic.

`SGLANG_MLA_HCA_KV_SPLITS=0` restores the previous behaviour with no code change.

## Motivation

The MLA decode kernel sits at 1.2-3.1% of both the bandwidth and the flops roofline, so its cost is set by dispersion, not by the hardware: the batch's p50 token reads ~1,000 KV entries while its p99 reads ~3,100, and the kernel finishes when its slowest CTA does.

That dispersion lives in one of the three index streams. CSA (`compress_ratio` 4) is clamped to `index_topk`, so kv_len tops out at 1152 and the stream is nearly uniform. HCA (`compress_ratio` 128) has no such clamp — kv_len is ~context/128 and reaches ~5,000 at the ISL p99 of 634,941 — and `config.json` alternates the two per layer.

Split-K was previously set aside here because `_kv_splits_heuristic` reads only capture-time scalars and so cannot tell a ragged shape from a uniform one. That is true of the batch but not of the layer: `compress_ratio` is a static per-layer constant, so the discrimination is free.

The causal chain was tested under intervention before any of this was built, by clamping kv_len to 128 so the kernel does almost nothing: the step fell 17.07 ms at matched batch size against a pre-registered ~19.5. That run only sets the ceiling — its output is garbage — but it is the denominator this PR should be scored against.

## Modifications

Three files, +63/-1:

- `paged_decode.py` — adds `_kv_splits_for_stream(compress_ratio)` and the `SGLANG_MLA_HCA_KV_SPLITS` env gate (default 4, 0 disables), and threads a `kv_splits` argument through the public `sparse_attn_v4_paged_decode` wrapper. The Triton entry point already accepted `kv_splits` as a benchmark escape hatch; this makes it reachable from production.
- `runtime.py` — `decode()` forwards `kv_splits`.
- `deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py` — sets it at the one call site that knows the stream, right where `compress_ratio` already selects between the SWA/HCA/CSA index buffers.

No kernel changes. Nothing changes for SWA or CSA, or for any model that does not take this backend.

**Why 4 and not 8.** 4 wins outright at low kv_len (-41.8% vs -35.8%), gives ~93% of 8 at the steady-state operating point, halves the partial buffers (`acc_partial` is `T x splits x h_padded x D x 4 B` = 103 MB at splits=4 against 205 MB at 8 for bs=14, charged inside the cuda-graph pool), and — see the batch sweep below — is actually *faster* than 8 once bs ≥ 24. 4 degrades gracefully across the whole batch range; 8 only wins at small batch.

## Accuracy Tests

Split-K is a different code path from the fused one production captures today (partial buffers plus a reduce kernel), so it was validated before any benchmarking:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| stream gating, `_kv_splits_for_stream(0 / 4 / 128)` | `None / None / 4` |
| override actually reaches the kernel | heuristic would have picked 1, kernel ran 4 |
| **numerics vs the fused path, HCA shape at bs=14** | **relL2 2.47e-03** (bf16 accumulation order) |
| `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` capture + replay on the split path | succeeds, output finite |

End to end, across two hour-long agentic runs: `accept len` 3.78 → 3.77, cuda-graph replay 100% of steps in both, KV pool identical at 12,077,312, cache hit 96.00% → 96.12%, and **0 errors out of 10,488 requests** at c128 and 0 out of 14,260 at c256.

Not done, and worth a reviewer asking for it: no GSM8K/MMLU-style task-accuracy run. The argument here is numerical equivalence to the path it replaces plus error-free long runs, not a downstream score.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**End to end** — DSv4-Pro FP4, 8x MI355X, TP8 EP8 DP-attention, MTP, MegaMoE+EPLB, mem-fraction 0.85, agentic trace replay, 3600 s. Identical CLI flags to the baseline (46/46) and the same KV pool; the only difference is this patch. `Δstep` is the **n-weighted matched-batch-size** log-implied decode step delta, which is the claim — throughput at these run lengths has a 5.67% replicate spread and is quoted only as context.

| conc | step p50 | **Δstep** | ITL p50 | ITL p90 | tok/s/chip |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 baseline | 121.76 ms | — | 32.28 ms | 33.9 ms | 36,995 |
| **128 + this PR** | **114.12 ms** | **−7.50 ms (−6.2%)** | 30.24 ms | 31.8 ms | 40,346 |
| 256 baseline | 156.19 ms | — | — | 43.9 ms | 57,516 |
| **256 + this PR** | **150.51 ms** | **−5.37 ms (−3.4%)** | — | 43.1 ms | 58,508 |

For scale: the fake-kernel ceiling (kv_len clamped to 128, ~95% of MLA work deleted) is −17.07 ms at c128, so this captures **44% of the total available MLA headroom** without a new kernel.

**Kernel microbenchmark** — ragged per-token kv_len vectors drawn from the measured distribution (LogNormal, median 1,000, p99 3,096, capped at the observed 5,000), % against the heuristic's choice:

kv_len level, at bs=14, HCA shape:

| median kv_len | split 2 | split 4 | split 8 | split 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | −30.0% | **−41.8%** | −35.8% | −21.8% |
| 500 | −35.7% | −51.4% | **−51.9%** | −45.1% |
| 1300 (steady state) | −34.8% | −50.1% | **−54.0%** | −49.7% |
| 3000 | −13.5% | −23.8% | **−27.0%** | −22.4% |

Split-K never loses anywhere on the HCA shape, and 16 is always worse than 8, so the optimum is interior. On the **CSA** shape (cap 1152, dispersion 0.19) the same sweep gives **+5.1%** at splits=8 — split-K loses there, which is why the override is gated on `compress_ratio` instead of applied globally.

Batch size, at median kv_len 1300:

| bs | T | base CTAs | dispersion | split 2 | split 4 | split 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 14 | 98 | 196 | 0.699 | −35.1% | −50.3% | **−54.2%** |
| 18 | 126 | 252 | 0.707 | −25.6% | −41.8% | **−44.5%** |
| 21 | 147 | 294 | 0.701 | −24.3% | −34.1% | **−36.8%** |
| 24 | 168 | 336 | 0.706 | −13.8% | **−24.4%** | −22.7% |
| 28 | 196 | 392 | 0.713 | −16.8% | **−24.3%** | −21.9% |

Dispersion is flat at ~0.70 in every row, so the decay is not a change in the straggler — it is the base grid filling the device (target 1.5 × 256 = 384 CTAs). Split-K helps by giving idle CUs something to do, and past saturation there are none.

This also predicts the c256 result quantitatively. c256 runs at bs p50 21 against c128's 12-14, i.e. a per-call win of 34.1% instead of ~50.3%; scaling the c128 step delta by that ratio gives **−5.08 ms predicted against −5.37 measured**. The step composition differs between the two concurrencies, so treat that as strong support rather than proof.

**Caveats.** The c256 run also changed `--load-balance-method` to `total_tokens`, so it cannot attribute between the balancer and this patch on its own; a separate c128 A/B measured that balancer at +0.78 ms, i.e. null, which is why the −5.37 is presumed to be mostly this change. Absolute µs in the microbenchmark run above the in-situ per-call figures because one aggregate distribution is applied to every call whereas real layers alternate between the two regimes — the ratios transfer, the absolutes do not. A kernel-level trace confirming how the gain splits between MLA time and the downstream MoE `prepare` wait has not been captured yet.

title: [diffusion] model: support qwen-image-2.1
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Add native Qwen-Image 2.1 text-to-image generation and editing, including multiple reference images and RGBA input/output. SGLang owns the model components and preserves the checkpoint's Transformers 4.57.3 conditioning semantics.

## Modifications

- Add the DiT, RGBA VAE, Qwen3-VL conditioning, model registration, and CLI/server integration.
- Align conditioning and VAE normalization with [Diffusers #14804](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14804): training image markers, white alpha compositing for vision only, empty-prompt handling, pre-final-norm text features, and FP32 VAE normalization.
- Integrate request-scoped prefix caching, Cache-DiT, breakable CUDA graphs, TP/Ulysses/Ring/CFG parallelism, encoder sharding, VAE parallel decoding, component/layerwise offload, and adapter mapping.
- Add complex RoPE, Q/K normalization, and scale-only LayerNorm fusions with first-call equality checks and native fallbacks. Detect the running CUDA build's complex multiplication FMA order for Hopper and Blackwell.
- Scope vision RoPE recomputation after device transfers to Qwen-Image 2.1, preserving the existing MiniMax-H3 encoder behavior.
- Add `qwen_image21_t2i_tp2` for the two-GPU E2E suite (temporarily disabled until the checkpoint is accessible to fork PR CI): 1024×1024 PNG, 40 steps, CFG 1, seed 42, two consecutive requests, model API and pinned image-consistency checks. Reference image (merged): [ci-data-diffusion #7](https://github.com/sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion/pull/7).
- Add unit, CUDA, distributed, and supplemental full-checkpoint HTTP tests; update compatibility/quantization docs and the hardware-aware cookbook command picker.
- Add verified single-RTX PRO 6000 resident/offload recipes and retain non-default picker selections when a shared configuration link is refreshed.

## Speed tests

Incremental Q/K normalization on one B200 (resident, FlashAttention, eager, 1024×1024, 40 steps, seed 42, CFG 1; four fresh starts in new/base/base/new order, two warmups per start) reduced median generation latency from 3.114 to 2.828 s (9.17%; 10 samples per variant) and editing from 3.742 to 3.450 s (7.81%; six samples per variant).

The subsequent scale-only LayerNorm change reduced median generation latency from 2.831 to 2.748 s (2.92%) and editing from 3.436 to 3.358 s (2.26%), with identical corresponding output pixels. These measurements predate the latest conditioning correction and apply only to the tested commits/workload; they are not a new accuracy baseline.

On one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (96GB, SM120), corrected implementation `1eab5de5990` passed 1024×1024/40-step HTTP generation, editing, transparent generation, and repeated transparent-input editing with Torch SDPA. Resident generation/edit medians were 8.23/9.85 s with 40.1 GiB peak device memory; DiT offload measured 10.28/10.66 s and 26.1 GiB. All 13 corresponding RGBA outputs matched exactly across placements; 156 kernel/model tests passed (21 skipped). Multi-GPU and NVFP4 recipes on this GPU remain unverified.

## Checklist

Regression validation on two H200 GPUs at `2d7c5365fb0`: all 41 focused vision/Qwen tests passed, including exact CPU/GPU RoPE checks and the real component-offload path. Two consecutive H3 ref2va requests produced six sampled frames identical pixel-for-pixel to main `9784d5f979c9`; the previous PR head differed on every sampled frame. Both main and the corrected branch remain below the H100 reference-image SSIM threshold on this H200 environment, so this comparison establishes parity with main rather than an upstream H100 consistency pass. Reference images and thresholds are unchanged.

- [x] Format code with pre-commit; validate documentation and links.
- [x] Add unit, distributed, and HTTP tests; retain the temporarily disabled TP2 E2E definition.
- [x] Verify strict RoPE equivalence on Hopper and Blackwell.
- [x] Correct VAE input layout and validate transparent editing against Transformers 4.57.3.
- [x] Complete the corrected-conditioning LayerNorm feature matrix.
- [x] Pass upstream lint with the consolidated kernel-test taxonomy.
- [ ] Complete upstream NVIDIA CI.

The TP2 E2E case is temporarily disabled in `6078c9049b3` after [upstream CI returned HTTP 401 during checkpoint loading](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35321287777/job/105600776865). The case configuration, scheduling estimate, and pinned reference image are retained for re-enabling it when the checkpoint is accessible to fork PR CI. Earlier isolated B200 TP2 consistency tests passed.
