title: [AMD] Tune Qwen3.5 TP4 GDN recurrent launch on gfx950
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

Qwen3.5-397B has 45 Gated DeltaNet layers. At TP4, each rank runs the recurrent verify kernel with 4 key heads, 16 value heads, and K=V=128, but the shared Triton wrapper always uses a 32-column value tile and one warp. That launch geometry is under-occupied for the 1-32 request batches used by decode and speculative verification on MI355X.

A gfx950 sweep found a consistently faster configuration: BV=8 with four warps for batch 1, and BV=16 with two warps for batches 2-32. The measured kernel improvement is 14-40%, and a GPU profile confirms a 14.4% reduction across all 45 recurrent launches in target verify.

## Modifications

- Add `_select_recurrent_launch_config()` in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fla/fused_sigmoid_gating_recurrent.py`.
- Select the tuned launch only for HIP gfx95, non-KDA GDN, batch 1-32, H=4, HV=16, and K=V=128.
- Keep the original BV=32 / one-warp launch byte-for-byte for CUDA, KDA, other GDN shapes, and larger batches.
- Extend `test_fused_verify_triton_gdn.py` with the exact Qwen3.5 TP4 shape at batches 1, 3, and 16, plus positive and negative launch-envelope assertions.

## Accuracy Tests

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2, TP4, real EAGLE MTP, 200 GSM8K questions, five-shot chat template with thinking disabled:

| Configuration | Accuracy | Invalid | Gate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline | 0.970 | 0.000 | 0.92 |
| Tuned GDN launch | 0.960 | 0.000 | 0.92 |

Both arms pass the fixed gate. At 200 questions the two-answer difference is within the sampling resolution, so this result is reported as a passing accuracy gate rather than bit-identical model output. Kernel tests compare the tuned shape against the existing reference implementation at `rtol=atol=1e-2`; the full fused-GDN and non-contiguous-stride suites pass.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Hardware and software: 4x AMD MI355X, TP4/EP1, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.19-rocm720-mi35x-20260915`, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2, AITER attention and MoE, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, EAGLE 3 steps / top-k 1 / 4 draft tokens.

### GDN target-verify microbenchmark

The microbenchmark uses T=4, H=4, HV=16, K=V=128, BF16 activations, FP32 recurrent state, and the target-verify intermediate-state write.

| Batch | Baseline BV32 / 1 warp | Tuned | Delta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 17.88 us | 10.76 us | -39.82% |
| 2 | 18.24 us | 12.76 us | -30.04% |
| 4 | 19.48 us | 14.68 us | -24.64% |
| 8 | 21.56 us | 16.68 us | -22.64% |
| 16 | 25.68 us | 22.08 us | -14.02% |
| 32 | 48.40 us | 41.60 us | -14.05% |

The selected configurations are BV=8 / four warps at batch 1 and BV=16 / two warps at batches 2-32. Shapes outside that envelope retain BV=32 / one warp.

### Target-verify profile

GPU-only profiles used the same random 8K/256 workload and the same TP rank. Both target graphs contain 45 `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_kernel` launches.

| Metric | Baseline | Tuned | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Recurrent kernel per target verify, 45 launches | 528.359 us | 452.300 us | -14.4% |
| Recurrent kernel per layer | 11.741 us | 10.051 us | -14.4% |
| Full target-verify graph | 10.556 ms | 10.429 ms | -1.2% |

The recurrent launch saves 76 us, while the full graph saves 127 us. The same kernel name remains because this is a launch-configuration optimization; the shape-specific unit test pins which configuration is selected.

### InferenceMax AgentX, TP4 concurrency 4

Each arm ran the standard 1,200-second AgentX replay. AgentX admits more requests when an arm is faster, so the request mix is not byte-identical; the target-verify profile above is the attribution evidence and this table is the end-to-end direction.

| Metric | Baseline | Tuned | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Mean TPOT | 3.73 ms | 3.61 ms | -3.22% |
| P50 TPOT | 3.61 ms | 3.48 ms | -3.60% |
| P90 TPOT | 4.11 ms | 4.07 ms | -0.97% |
| P95 TPOT | 4.22 ms | 4.16 ms | -1.42% |
| Mean interactivity | 268.23 tok/s/user | 276.91 tok/s/user | +3.23% |
| Output throughput | 221.73 tok/s | 222.75 tok/s | +0.46% |
| Total throughput | 19,744.34 tok/s | 20,080.74 tok/s | +1.70% |
| P90 E2E latency | 10.24 s | 9.70 s | -5.24% |
| P50 TTFT | 0.449 s | 0.429 s | -4.60% |

### Canonical 8K input / 1K output, concurrency 4

| Metric | Baseline | Tuned | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total throughput | 8,176.02 tok/s | 8,479.57 tok/s | +3.71% |
| Output throughput | 901.16 tok/s | 934.62 tok/s | +3.71% |
| Mean TPOT | 3.80 ms | 3.60 ms | -5.26% |
| P50 TPOT | 3.56 ms | 3.33 ms | -6.46% |
| P50 TTFT | 494.41 ms | 503.86 ms | +1.91% |
| P50 E2E latency | 3,872.40 ms | 3,850.15 ms | -0.58% |

The canonical TTFT movement is opposite to the decode metrics and is called out rather than attributed to the recurrent kernel. The kernel and target-verify profile are the controlled evidence for this change.

title: [Perf] [XPU] usp: Enable packed Ulysses QKV all-to-all
author: ckvermaAI
body:
The packed-QKV input exchange was gated to CUDA by `is_cuda` checks in the relayout kernel and in both eligibility predicates, so XPU silently fell back to three separate collectives per attention layer and never populated the A2A staging cache.

Nothing on this path is CUDA-specific: the pack is an in-tree Triton kernel and the exchange is `all_to_all_single`. Relax those gates to a device-type set; "cuda" also covers ROCm, where `is_cuda` is True, so ROCm is unchanged.

Two CUDA-only calls on the same path had to move to `torch.get_device_module()`, which is exactly `torch.cuda` for a CUDA device:

- `_a2a_staging_buffer` called `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()`, which raises `RuntimeError: Tried to instantiate dummy base class` on an XPU-only build rather than returning False. It was unreachable only because the `device.type != "cuda"` test short-circuited ahead of it, so relaxing the device gate alone would have crashed.
- `drop_a2a_staging_buffers` guarded its synchronize on `torch.cuda.is_available()`, so on XPU it cleared the cache without waiting for collectives that may still be reading those buffers. Dormant until this change populated the cache on XPU. Its call site in `gpu_worker.py` already excludes only CPU/MPS and calls `torch.get_device_module().empty_cache()`.

Tests: resolve the accelerator once per module instead of hardcoding `device="cuda"`, so the six cases run on XPU as well; CUDA is probed first so a CUDA host keeps identical coverage. Add
`test_packed_path_issues_one_collective` -- the unpacked fallback is also bit-exact, so the equivalence test passes whether or not the packed path was selected, and only the collective count pins the device gate.

title: [Spec][PP] Fix hybrid recurrent-state commit and micro-batch pairing under PP x speculative decoding
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

#30775 enabled PP x speculative decoding (`SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC=1`). On hybrid linear-attention targets (KDA / GDN / Mamba-style recurrent state) it is currently incorrect in two independent ways, both found while validating PP + MTP across model families (tracking: #39634):

1. **Non-last PP stages never commit the accepted recurrent state.** The last stage commits KDA/Mamba state inside `run_eagle_verify`; earlier stages only run target verify and relay the result, so their recurrent state stays at the pre-verify value while the last stage advances. GLM-5.3-Flash PP2 + MTP: GSM8K 0.745 vs 0.990 without spec, accept length looks normal (3.5), so the bug is silent.
2. **With more than two stages the relayed accept result is paired with the wrong micro-batch.** The commit hook took its destination slots from the backend's active `forward_metadata`, which on a non-last stage still belongs to the previous forward (slot `(i-1) % N`), and the KDA verify scratch was written at positional rows `0..bs-1` that in-flight micro-batches overwrite before the relay returns. With PP2 `(i-1) % 2 == (i+1) % 2`, so both errors are masked; with PP4 the first concurrent batch crashes with `indices length mismatch: dst_indices_raw.shape[0]=7 vs step_indices_raw.shape[0]=12`, and after fixing only the destination the accuracy is 0.485.

Pipeline-parallel speculative decoding can receive verify acceptance after a later micro-batch has overwritten positional hybrid-state scratch. When `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC=1`, hybrid verify scratch and the delayed recurrent-state commit therefore use request-pool stable rows; with the gate off, the existing positional / active-metadata path is unchanged.

## Modifications

- `scheduler_pp_mixin`: relay `accept_index` unconditionally (chains too). On non-last stages `_pp_spec_commit_relayed_accept` commits the acceptance relayed for that same micro-batch (same `commit_mamba_states_after_verify` the last stage uses) before `seq_lens` advances, then compacts the accepted KV. The scheduler snapshots each PP-spec micro-batch and clones `req_pool_indices` (the Mamba-track tensor is rebound, never mutated, so the snapshot shares it).
- Gating: `pp_spec_stable_rows_enabled()` (`layers/attention/linear/utils.py`) is the single predicate for the stable-row policy; kernels take `stable_rows=` from the backend instead of reading the env.
- Hybrid Mamba commit (`hybrid_linear_attn_backend`, `mamba_state_scatter_triton`): under the PP-spec gate, when the caller carries `req_pool_indices`, rebuild and translate destination state indices from the matching forward snapshot instead of the active `forward_metadata`; with the gate off, or without rows, the existing path runs.
- KDA / GDN verify (`kda_backend`, `gdn_backend`, `gdn_flashinfer`): the request-pool slot is the stable scratch row (padding still goes to the discard row); row selection is shared in `select_verify_intermediate_state_indices`. The FlashInfer GDN MTP kernel writes positional `0..B-1` and takes no row indices, so the PP-spec path uses a positional scratch and remaps to the stable rows after the kernel. KDA PP verify falls back from the FlashInfer kernel to Triton; ReplaySSM verify reads its source rows from the same stable mapping (`src_indices_raw` / `dst_indices_raw` across backends).
- Qwen PLE short-conv / n-gram side state (`ple_state_pool`, `qwen4_exp`) gets the same request-row pairing.

No change to the attention math or the acceptance algorithm; only where state is stored and how relayed results are paired.

## Accuracy / validation (GB300, GSM8K 200 questions, `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC=1`, EAGLE/MTP steps 3 topk 1)

| Model | Config | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.3-Flash (KDA) | PP2xTP2 + MTP | 0.745 / AL 3.51 | 0.990 / 3.39 (TP4+MTP baseline 0.985 / 3.40) |
| GLM-5.3-Flash | PP2xTP2 + MTP + ReplaySSM | - | 0.995 / 3.40 |
| GLM-5.3-Flash | PP4xTP1 + MTP | crash (7 vs 12) | 0.990 / 3.39 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (GDN) | PP4xTP1 + MTP | crash (1 vs 12) | 0.965 / 3.02 (TP4+MTP baseline 0.980 / 3.16) |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next | PP2xTP2 + MTP, with #39643 and #40501 on main | - | 0.975 / 3.13 (0.955 / 3.02 without this PR) |

title: Support MXFP8 and deferred route weighting in DeepEP v2
author: metamergebot
body:
## Summary

DeepEP v2 rejects 1x32 MXFP8 experts and applies routing weights before model-specific expert finalization. Support group-32 activation scales through dispatch and DeepGEMM, with unweighted route outputs and an opt-in FP32 SiLU policy for registered model architectures.

## Motivation

Activation scale groups must be tracked independently of weight scale groups. Models that transform each expert output also need those outputs before router weighting and reduction.

## Modifications

Extend the existing SiLU/post-quant kernels to group 32, carry scale metadata through both dispatch layouts, and expose explicit route layouts for finalization. Preserve upstream's BF16 dispatch, FlashInfer adapter, and existing contiguous MXFP8 behavior. The SM120 contiguous producer records its group-128 activation scales independently of MXFP8 weight groups. The scatter expert-range arguments are already upstream and are not duplicated.

Import the quantizer from its defining module in DeepGEMM and the CUDA FP8/INT8 wrappers, so import order cannot replace a callable with the same-named submodule.

## Accuracy Tests

GB300 kernel checks compare packed UE8M0 scales and masked/contiguous FP8 codes, including empty experts and partial slabs. Route-output checks cover deferred weighting, nonlocal slots, and empty inputs. Existing BF16/FP8 masked-versus-contiguous DeepGEMM checks also pass.

The SM120 regression exercises its production quantizer and scatter path with platform selection forced on GB300. Before the fix, the resulting scales triggered `MXFP8 activation scale mismatch: block_size=32, K=512, scale_width=1, expected 4`. With explicit group-128 metadata, activation and weight recipes remain independent.

## Test plan

Ran with a Python 3.12 test environment selected through `.venv`:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python SGLANG_IS_IN_CI=1 uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_hpc_ops_runner_guard.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_moe_runner_extensions.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_deepep_v2_buffer_lifecycle.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_deepep_v2_wire_dtype.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_deepep_v2_masked_slab.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_per_token_group_quant.py::test_ue8m0_group_sizes \

  --disable-warnings --maxfail=2
```

Result: **114 passed, 12 subtests passed**. The SM120 regression was also run alone before the production fix and failed with the scale-width assertion above.

Also passed:

title: [Logprob] Serve input-logprob temporaries from CUDA-graph-pool dead space
author: metamergebot
body:
> Rebased onto `main` at 36aa8479 (after #40303 and #40290 repaired the lint and the fusion-gate mock that #40068 had broken on `main`). The only conflict on the way was #38792 adding `allocate_distinct_stream` directly above the `_async_d2h` this change moves to `sglang.srt.utils.common`; the resolution keeps the new helper. The patch is otherwise unchanged from the head that passed base-a/base-b (84a7303d4b). Earlier: rebased after #40007 merged (6a9c7001d3); this pull request is only its own commit.

## Motivation

#40007 (merged) borrows idle CUDA-graph-pool memory for the LM-head logits of a chunked input-logprob forward, but the scoring that follows each chunk still allocates from the reserved workspace: the gathered logprob rows, the out-of-place log-softmax, the top-k and token-id gathers. For long prompt-logprob requests those temporaries are the remaining peak, and every chunk also drained the stream with `.tolist()` and device-mask lookups before the next chunk could start. This change serves those temporaries from graph-pool dead space as well, and removes the per-chunk device synchronization.

## Modifications

- `InputLogprobProcessor` decides borrowing for the whole chunk, not just the logits. `_can_borrow_logits_memory` becomes `_can_borrow_logprob_memory(chunk_size, borrow_logits)`: the per-row budget is three FP32 vocab-width matrices when the TP gather is borrowed, otherwise one (fast path) or two (log-softmax path). Under NCCL symmetric memory only the gather is excluded from borrowing; scoring can still borrow. Chunk boundaries never change with graph-pool capacity, as in #40007.
- Inside the borrow scope the chunk's token logprobs are written straight into one pinned host tensor, and top-k / token-id results are copied to pinned host spans with `async_d2h` instead of `.tolist()`. A `torch.cuda.Event` recorded on the forward stream travels with the result as `LogitsProcessorOutput.input_logprobs_copy_done`; `finalize_input_logprobs()` waits on it and flattens the spans into the per-sequence row lists the scheduler already expects. Sampled logits are still allocated outside the borrow scope.
- `finalize_input_logprobs()` is called from `SchedulerBatchResultProcessor.move_logprobs_to_cpu` and, for pipeline parallelism, from `get_logprob_dict_from_result` before the payload is pickled. `PrefillCudaGraphRunner` forwards the event when it rebuilds the output.
- `LogitsMetadata` carries `sample_indices_cpu` and `input_logprob_indices_cpu` (the host lists the index tensors are built from), so `_forward_by_chunk` selects each chunk's rows with `bisect` on the sorted host lists instead of device masks and `torch.nonzero`.
- `_async_d2h` moves from `managers/utils.py` to `sglang.srt.utils.common.async_d2h` so the layers package can use it without importing the managers package; `managers/utils.py` re-imports it under the old name, so existing patches of `sglang.srt.managers.utils._async_d2h` keep working.
- Tests: `test_graph_pool_borrow.py` gains a replay-survival test over a growing chunk sequence (results read back after `graph.replay()` through the real `move_logprobs_to_cpu`) and a planned-chunk test that checks borrowing turns on and off with pool capacity and the disabled state without changing LM-head chunk shapes, and that the peak stays within two matrices per chunk. New `test/registered/e2e/layers/test_logprob_memory_distributed.py` (2-gpu-large, base-b; a two-process test cannot register from `unit/`, and it runs under `python3 file.py` like the other registered files) runs a TP-2 gather through the processor on both ranks, asserts both ranks plan identical chunks whether or not one rank has borrowing disabled, that every allocation lands on a free graph-pool run when borrowing, and that results survive replay. The chunk-stitching test covers `finalize_input_logprobs` request boundaries and the no-event (multi-item scoring) layout. The CPU sweeps pass the two new host index lists.

## Accuracy Tests

Same kernels at the same chunk shapes; only the allocator behind the transient scoring tensors and the result transport change. The new CUDA tests compare token logprobs, top-k values and indices, token-id logprobs and sampled logits against an eager `log_softmax` reference with `torch.equal`, after graph replay. On an internal TP4 deployment a strict input-logprob comparison against the previous code had zero maximum difference and zero KL over 73k scored tokens.

Ran on a 4x GB300 host against this branch (torch 2.11.0+cu130):

```
pytest test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner_utils/test_graph_pool_borrow.py        # 18 passed, 23 subtests
python3 test/registered/e2e/layers/test_logprob_memory_distributed.py -f                  # 1 passed (2 GPUs)
pytest test/registered/unit/layers/test_logprob_chunk_stitching.py \
       test/registered/unit/layers/test_logprob_fast_input.py \
       test/registered/unit/lora/test_lm_head_pruning.py \
       test/registered/unit/managers/test_auxiliary_output.py \
       test/registered/unit/model_executor/model_runner_components/test_startup_weight_load.py   # 70 passed
```

`isort --check-only`, `ruff check --select=F401,F821,UP037`, `ruff format --check` and `codespell` pass on the touched files.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The per-chunk `.tolist()` calls and `torch.nonzero` mask lookups are gone from the chunk loop, so a chunked input-logprob forward no longer synchronizes the device per chunk; one event synchronize happens when the scheduler consumes the result. The borrow decision is still one CPU all-reduce per chunked forward when TP gathering is active.

title: [Perf] [XPU] fp8: Optimize FP8 scale layouts
author: CaoE
body:
## Motivation

Optimizes XPU FP8 linear by pre-materializing scale layouts during weight loading and enabling fused rowwise `scaled_mm` for channelwise FP8 weights when the input shape and scale layouts are supported.

FP8 linear layers using Torch scaled_mm may perform redundant scale-layout conversions during every forward pass. For block-wise FP8, the required transpose-contiguous layout can be materialized once after weight loading. For channelwise FP8, XPU supports fused rowwise scaled_mm, but the path requires per-token activation scaling and a [N, 1] weight-scale layout.

## Modifications

- Materialize scale layout during weight loading.
- Enable `use_per_token_if_dynamic` and fused rowwise scaled_mm.

## Accuracy Tests

test_xpu_fp8_linear.py

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N=K=1024:
Block-scale layout materialization reduced block FP8 scaled_mm latency by approximately 8.7% to 10.0% across M=1, 8, 128.
Fused rowwise scaled_mm reduced latency by approximately:
  26.9% at M=8
  26.7% at M=128

title: Read process groups through the runtime context
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

The same process group can be asked for in two spellings: the free accessors in
`distributed/parallel_state.py` (`get_tp_group()` and friends) and the parallel
namespace on the runtime context (`get_parallel().tp_group`). Business code uses
both, so a scope that swaps a group — the draft worker's tensor-parallel scope,
for instance — has to be installed in both places to be seen, and any later
change to how a group is answered has to be made twice.

This collects the reads onto one spelling. It does **not** remove the accessors:
they stay as the definition, so this diff is a rename and nothing else, and the
changes that do move semantics are not mixed into a whole-repo sweep.

## Modifications

323 call sites across 147 files, one commit per subsystem (`layers` → `models` →
`model executor` → `scheduler`/`disaggregation` → memory/model loading →
speculative/LoRA → elastic EP/hardware backends → utils/multimodal). Every
commit is a rename with an identical answer at every call site: the context
property falls through to the same accessor.

Deliberately **not** converted, each for a stated reason:

- **The whole `srt/distributed/` package** (81 reads). It is the layer that
  defines the accessors and builds the groups; a read there would go through the
  context back into itself.
- **`get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()` and
  `get_attn_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()`** (9 reads). These answer with
  the *built group's* width, while `get_parallel().tp_size` / `.attn_tp_size`
  answer from the configuration. The two agree in a healthy process, but they
  are not the same question, so converting them is a behavior change rather than
  a rename. They belong with the change that makes the group build read the
  configuration and asserts the two agree.
- **`get_moe_cp_size()`** (6 reads). It is not `moe_dp_size`: the MoE-DP group is
  aliased to the attention-CP group when `attn_cp_size > moe_dp_size`, so this
  answers the real width of that communicator, which the configuration does not
  imply.
- **`get_shared_experts_tp_group()`** (1 read, in `models/kimi_k3.py`). The
  context has no name for that group, so there is nothing to rename it to.
- **`multimodal_gen/`**, which has its own parallel state.

`sglang/kernels/` is *not* excluded: its one direct reader
(`ops/layernorm/mhc.py`) is converted here too, so the accessors have no callers
outside the two exclusions above.

No module-level caching was introduced and no adjacent reads were merged: both
would freeze a live read at import time or at the wrong point in a scope.

## Accuracy Tests

Greedy decode, `temperature=0`, this branch vs its base commit, token for token
identical on `tp2`, `tp2+pp2`, `tp4+dp2 --enable-dp-attention`, and
`tp4 --ep-size 4`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The new read is not free: a context property resolves through the read chain and
then the canonical getter, where the old call was the getter alone — measured in
pure Python, ~38 ns becomes ~340 ns, and 42 of the converted reads sit in
forward-path functions (two in `RowParallelLinear.forward`, i.e. every TP
row-linear of an eager prefill or a non-graphed decode). Most of that gap is a
module import re-executed per read on the shared path; the next PR in the stack
caches it, which brings the read back to two attribute lookups. No change to
what is computed or communicated.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Tests that stubbed an accessor on the module under test now stub it on
`parallel_state`, the seam every spelling goes through. Two had been stubbing
the package re-export; those were consulted at base, because the readers
imported the name inside the function, and are not at this head — so the
re-target is what keeps them testing the same thing.

Stubs that fed a TP group to a kernel test are re-expressed as a scope: a
`stated_tp_group` fixture states `tp_group=None` on the context for the length
of the test, in five files and eight tests. Rebinding the module attribute is
not equivalent any more, because `use_symmetric_memory(get_parallel().tp_group,
...)` evaluates its argument before the context manager can decide to skip the
allocation — the group is read either way. The AMD sampler test states its
stand-in group the same way, permanently rather than scoped, since that process
has no distributed init and nothing tears the value back down.

## Review and Merge Process

Second of five stacked PRs; #40067 has landed, so this now targets `main`.

The previous revision was red on `test_aiter_greedy_sample_amd.py`: it stated
its stand-in TP group by calling `__enter__()` on a scope it did not keep a
reference to, so the value was taken back down in the same statement and the
read fell through to the live group. It states the group permanently now.
Ready for CI.

title: [MoE] Disable FlashInfer fused finalize by default for numerical accuracy
author: zianglih
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

@humansand

Default to unfused FlashInfer MoE finalize for better numerical accuracy. Users can opt in to fused atomic finalize with `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MOE_FUSED_FINALIZE=1` when they prefer more aggressive performance.

- **History:** [#28354](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28354) introduced this environment variable with `EnvBool(True)` and made deterministic inference force it to `0`.
- **Prior behavior:** immediately before #28354, the [CUTLASS calls](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c4271c3fe1262fc2adbd162c33b25de5255251c5/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py#L221-L238) and [CuTe DSL v2 wrapper](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c4271c3fe1262fc2adbd162c33b25de5255251c5/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutedsl.py#L287-L302) omitted `use_fused_finalize`. SGLang [pinned FlashInfer 0.6.17](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c4271c3fe1262fc2adbd162c33b25de5255251c5/python/pyproject.toml#L36), whose [CUTLASS API](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/a0a6b019b9b27d49d209f85d028a1ae5a9b347d7/flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py#L943) and [CuTe DSL wrapper](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/a0a6b019b9b27d49d209f85d028a1ae5a9b347d7/flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/fused_moe.py#L464) both defaulted to `True`. Thus #28354 exposed the existing fused-finalize default as a SGLang setting; this PR changes that default to `False` for the callers that honor it. The separate CuTe DSL v1 DeepEP masked path is outside this flag's scope.

## Modifications

- **Default:** change `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MOE_FUSED_FINALIZE` from `EnvBool(True)` to `EnvBool(False)`.
- **Documentation:** update the default and explain the performance opt-in.
- **Existing paths:** CUTLASS and CuTe DSL callers continue to read the same flag; deterministic inference continues to force it off. No kernel changes or new tests.

## Accuracy Tests

- **Static validation:** changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed at `e3bcc8f7b4337565baea1d2b44fd4f0f838b1953` (base: `6e1d9c14647e3e16f2a103b89dead95f1400ea48`).
- **Environment:** macOS 26.4.1, arm64, Python 3.14.6, pre-commit 4.6.1; local CPU checks only, no container or GPUs used.
- **Not run:** model accuracy tests; no tests added for this default-only runtime change. Mintlify build/link checks were not run because `mint` is unavailable locally.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- **Result:** Disabling fused finalize has a measurable W4A4 cost in this EP8 sweep. CuTe W4A4 per-tensor latency increases **21.75% at 1 token**. At **16,384 tokens**, latency changes by **+7.82% for CUTLASS**, **+12.55% for CuTe W4A4 per-tensor**, **+10.70% for CuTe W4A4 per-token**, and **-9.20% for CuTe W4A16**. These single sweeps do not support a blanket claim of negligible regression. Users can retain `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MOE_FUSED_FINALIZE=1` when this performance tradeoff matters.
- **Scope:** [`benchmarks/bench_moe_deepseek.py`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/8bc3b578027791336c6ae87db5c9d76f82cef8bc/benchmarks/bench_moe_deepseek.py) at official release [`v0.6.18.post1`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/tag/v0.6.18.post1), commit `8bc3b578027791336c6ae87db5c9d76f82cef8bc`. All four configurations were measured with simulated EP=8 using the benchmark-only patch below: forward the existing finalize option to CUTLASS and add a W4A4-only selector. No FlashInfer runtime/kernel changes. This directly compares the FlashInfer flag used by SGLang PR head `e3bcc8f7b4337565baea1d2b44fd4f0f838b1953`.
- **Hardware/image:** 1× NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (SM103; GPU 0 of an allocated 8-GPU node), 275,040 MiB reported memory, 1,100 W power limit, driver `590.48.01`. Image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260918-20518d85`, runtime digest `sha256:d46a59f4b98658f728a1e006c003ad5ee0628e999fd8b2bef71ac1bb61b814da`. Run date: 2026-09-18 UTC.
- **Software:** Python `3.12.3`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA toolkit `13.0.88`, `flashinfer-python==0.6.18.post1`, `flashinfer-cubin==0.6.18.post1`, `flashinfer-jit-cache==0.6.18.post1+cu130`, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.2`, `apache-tvm-ffi==0.1.11`, `cupti-python==13.4.0` (`nvidia-cuda-cupti==13.4.92`). The image shipped FlashInfer 0.6.18; all three FlashInfer packages were updated to the matched official post1 release before measurement.
- **Workload:** DeepSeek-V3 MoE: hidden 7,168, intermediate 2,048, 256 experts, top-8, 8 routing groups/top-4 groups, routed scale 2.5, random seed 42, routing bias scale 0.01; simulated EP=8, TP=1: rank 0 holds experts 0–31 of 256. The token count is the global input batch routed across all 256 experts; this single-GPU benchmark computes the local expert contribution. Powers of two from 1 through 16,384 tokens. CUTLASS uses NVFP4 W4A4 per-tensor activation scaling. CuTe DSL covers NVFP4 W4A4 per-tensor, NVFP4 W4A4 per-token, and NVFP4 W4A16 with BF16 input, using its wrapper API.
- **Timing:** one complete flag-True sweep followed by one flag-False sweep for each configuration; no repeated or reverse-order sweeps. Independent autotuning caches per backend/activation/finalize mode; 10 warmups, 100 measured iterations per case, native median GPU latency, CUDA graphs and CUPTI with cold-L2 flushing. Routing, input activation quantization (`--include-activation-quant`, for W4A4), both expert GEMMs, and finalize are included. Weight preparation, compilation, and autotuning are excluded. W4A16 consumes BF16 input directly. All six commands exited 0, yielding all 120 requested latency rows with no CUPTI fallback warnings.
- **Build/provenance:** all EP8 runs used the same physical GPU (UUID `GPU-aa4e94df-96de-22b9-87c2-9960d6b27cb8`), image, and package versions. JIT was left enabled. The release wheel provides `fused_moe_103.so` and `fp4_quantization_103.so` for CUTLASS MoE and FP4 quantization; no CUTLASS build was needed.
- **Limits:** single sweeps provide no repeat/order-variation statistics. This covers local MoE only: no inter-GPU communication, other EP/TP layouts, model accuracy checks, or end-to-end serving. No numerical-error reduction is measured here.

**Speedup = latency with `use_fused_finalize=True` (old default) / latency with `False` (proposed default); greater than 1 means disabling fused finalize is faster.** CUTLASS `True` permits eligible fused-finalize tactics; autotuning can still choose an unfused tactic.

```bash
  for MODE in fused unfused; do
    FLAGS=()
    [[ "$MODE" == unfused ]] && FLAGS+=(--no-fused-finalize)
    python benchmarks/bench_moe_deepseek.py \
      --backends "$BACKEND" "${COMMON[@]}" "${EXTRA[@]}" "${FLAGS[@]}" \
      --cache "$PWD/finalize-results/${BACKEND}-${MODE}-tactics.json" \
      2>&1 | tee "finalize-results/${BACKEND}-${MODE}.log"
  done
done
```

These are direct FlashInfer benchmarks; no SGLang environment override is needed. `--no-fused-finalize` controls the API argument. title: [Fix] [NPU] attention: Use FIA TND for MLA prefix attention and add Gemma norm fallback
author: McZyWu
body:
## Motivation

Replace the ATB RingMLA implementation of MLA prefix-cache prefill with FIA TND so this path works without ATB. The formerly RingMLA-based prefix path now always uses two FIA V2 calls and `npu_attention_update`; it requires no environment-variable opt-in.

Honor `SGLANG_NPU_FORWARD_NATIVE_GEMMA_RMS_NORM` in `Gemma3RMSNorm` on NPU.

## Modifications

- Remove the `self.use_fia` dispatch and both `torch_npu.atb.npu_ring_mla` calls from the MLA prefix path. Use FIA TND for current-token causal attention and prefix attention, then merge their outputs in FP32 and restore the query dtype.
- Remove the unused RingMLA mask allocation and backend mask reference, preserving the original attention mask builder interface.
- Gather cached latent and RoPE pages through `gather_mla_cache_pages`, restoring logical token order for PA-NZ storage before projection and attention.
- Preserve cumulative TND sequence lengths, contiguous inputs, empty-prefix handling and output padding.
- Test against full prefix-first dense SDPA with FP16/BF16, mixed zero/nonzero prefixes, padding and large logits. Verify two FIA calls plus one merge for either value of the backend FIA flag, with ATB unavailable.
- Apply the existing native Gemma RMSNorm flag to `Gemma3RMSNorm.forward_npu`. This flag remains disabled by default; `Gemma4RMSNorm` already falls back to native on NPU.

The MLA prefix path covered by this change uses FIA TND whether `ASCEND_USE_FIA` is unset, `0`, or `1`. Other attention paths retain their existing dispatch behavior. The existing equal-QK/V-dimension MLA path is unchanged.

To select the native Gemma normalization implementation on NPU:

```bash
export SGLANG_NPU_FORWARD_NATIVE_GEMMA_RMS_NORM=1
```

## Accuracy Tests

### Default FIA TND validation (2026-10-14)

At commit `dd8bbb875f7a0bc7f8cea96cf0123aace7e45e37`, all 59 CPU-compatible attention unit tests passed through an isolated runner that compiles the unchanged production definitions and repository test classes from their AST, avoiding unrelated NPU imports. FIA and merge kernels use the tests' numerical PyTorch reference implementations; this does not validate the full package import path or real NPU kernels. The prefix tests cover 13 scenarios, including `use_fia=False` and `True` with ATB unavailable, FP16/BF16, mixed zero/nonzero prefixes, output padding and large logits. A mask-builder initialization check also passed without RingMLA or environment flags.

Ruff 0.15.1 lint/format, isort, codespell, Python syntax parsing, debug-statement/merge-marker checks and `git diff --check` passed. An AST comparison confirms that `forward_extend` matches the prior implementation with only its RingMLA/FIA dispatch replaced by the existing FIA body, preserving the FIA computation and other attention branches.

No new NPU model accuracy or performance evaluation was run for this change. The records below belong to their explicitly named earlier commits; their FIA/ATB environment-flag comparisons describe the older implementation.

### Prefix dispatch refactor validation (2026-09-28)

Commit `ee3dfe96a1bcc93bcdf3d6f4c04eb489b659de28` reorganizes the MLA prefix path into one complete `if self.use_fia` / `else` block. For each fixed value of `self.use_fia`, the old and new Python ASTs contain the same executable statements in the same order, including operator arguments, NZ cache handling, empty-prefix handling and output padding. Ruff 0.15.1 formatting and lint (`F401,F821,UP037`), Python syntax parsing and `git diff --check` passed. No new unit tests or NPU model evaluations were run for this structural change; the numerical and performance results below retain their recorded commit attribution.

### NZ cache validation (2026-09-24)

Commit `0c8ebbce034c11b5e0b9c2fec3193def9de2aa74` passed the original full HiCache MLA GSM8K case on A3/151 with FIA enabled in both runs: NZ disabled **473/1319 (35.860500%)**, NZ enabled **465/1319 (35.253980%)**. Both exceed the 34% case threshold. The 18 operator-path cases and 6 independent reruns also passed, with fixed NZ outputs bitwise equal to the ND baseline. See the NZ validation section under **Speed Tests and Profiling** for the complete environment, comparison, numerical checks, performance table and limitations. Python syntax parsing and `git diff --check` passed; no new unit tests were added.

### Latest validation (2026-09-24)

At commit `ef8a80be18d4d1e6efa84252cca07dd31284850a`, Python syntax parsing and `git diff --check` passed for the three changed files. The quantization implementation and its test file match the PR base; the remaining PR changes concern MLA prefix attention and Gemma normalization. No additional unit tests or model evaluations were run for this update. The accuracy and performance measurements below remain attributed to their explicitly recorded earlier commits.

### Gemma native fallback validation (2026-09-22)

Commit `ec72a1dd7c4292477bdd8e317a55f87c44f04357` changes only `layernorm.py`. Python syntax compilation and `git diff --check` passed. No additional unit tests or NPU model evaluations were run for this change. The model accuracy measurements below belong to their explicitly recorded earlier commits.

### Validation of updated PR head 3ba07ddc43 on machine 216 (2026-09-21)

After the author merged community main, tested **the actual PR head `3ba07ddc43d55782e2195f5cd2457297b1eef9fd`**, which includes main `62ba9648482e1b0a253187c8dc6ac5d23bbbd403`. Main is already an ancestor of the PR; `git merge-tree` succeeds and GitHub reports MERGEABLE. This rerun uses the published PR commit directly, rather than the earlier temporary integration snapshot.

Ran its original `test/registered/npu/basic_function/HiCache/test_npu_hicache_mla.py` on machine **216**, physical **A3 devices 0–3**, with **CANN 9.1.0 / torch_npu 2.10.0.post4 / PyTorch 2.10.0 / Transformers 5.12.1**. Reused the same full DeepSeek-V2-Lite-W8A8 checkpoint and GSM8K dataset. Both modes used TP=4, mem_fraction_static=0.8, HiCache enabled (current defaults: ratio=2.0, host memory fraction=0.8), all **1319 questions**, 5-shot, temperature=0, max_new_tokens=512, concurrency=128, and seed=42. The PR smoke shortcut was disabled. No additional unit tests were added or run.

| ASCEND_USE_FIA | Correct / total | Accuracy | Invalid answers | Case result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| unset | 472 / 1319 | 35.784685% | 5 | passed |
| 1 | 469 / 1319 | 35.557240% | 5 | passed |

FIA minus baseline: **-3 correct answers / -0.227445 percentage points**. 681 final numerical predictions differed: 111 changed from correct to incorrect, and 108 from incorrect to correct. This single pair does not establish lossless replacement. The existing backend-wide ASCEND_USE_FIA flag also affects other attention paths, so this does not isolate the new prefix branch alone.

Source hashes (including files updated by the merged main), dataset, devices, model path, evaluation settings, and actual server argument dictionaries were checked for consistency. Device-prefix cache hits: 1319/1319 unset and 1319/1319 enabled, 1012992 and 1012992 cached tokens respectively. Host-cache reload hits: 0 and 0; this case does not force host-cache eviction/reload. Full logs, metrics and per-question answers were retained.

Observed accuracy-evaluation runtime / output throughput: unset **198.626 s / 794.967 token/s**, enabled **207.717 s / 755.773 token/s**. These are not controlled performance measurements. A2/A5 and CANN 9.2 remain untested. Earlier validation records are preserved below.

### Latest-main integration rerun on machine 216 (2026-09-21)

Community main `176dbcb85d3b7737564e4911947035cc0af65f0a` and PR head `1344e1e2a5ca3e07bf6140b8c606e38465fbc55c` merged without conflicts in both `git merge-tree` and an actual isolated merge. GitHub reports MERGEABLE; the CI gate is blocked by the missing `run-ci` label, independently of merge conflicts. Tested the resulting temporary merge `2b388ce85710f74030b266f8446a01b91c556d48` without pushing it to the PR branch.

During the run, main advanced to `ab03a8e7eb82d35907bfbeb645bf0af8b4ce290e` (#40201, import/startup changes). A final `git merge-tree` check against that main also succeeded and GitHub still reports MERGEABLE. It does not modify this PR's NPU attention/quantization files or the HiCache MLA case. The accuracy results below belong to the fixed merge snapshot above; the full model test was not repeated on this newer main commit.

Ran the current merged-source `test_npu_hicache_mla.py` on machine **216**, four **Ascend A3** devices (physical 0–3), **CANN 9.1.0 / torch_npu 2.10.0.post4 / PyTorch 2.10.0 / Transformers 5.12.1**. Used the same full DeepSeek-V2-Lite-W8A8 checkpoint as the previous runs, copied from machine 209, with TP=4, `mem_fraction_static=0.8`, HiCache enabled, all 1319 GSM8K questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, max 512 new tokens, concurrency 128, and seed 42 for both modes. The updated main test no longer explicitly sets `hicache_ratio=1.2`; this rerun preserved its defaults, resolving to **ratio 2.0 / host_memory_fraction 0.8**. No additional unit tests were added or run for this rerun.

| ASCEND_USE_FIA | Correct / total | Accuracy | Invalid answers | Case result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| unset | 473 / 1319 | 35.860500% | 3 | passed |
| 1 | 484 / 1319 | 36.694466% | 4 | passed |

FIA minus baseline: **+11 correct answers / +0.833965 percentage points**. This single paired run does not establish lossless replacement or isolate the new prefix branch: `ASCEND_USE_FIA` affects other existing attention paths too. 661 final numerical predictions differed; 102 changed from correct to incorrect and 113 from incorrect to correct.

Both runs used matching source, dataset, devices, model path, evaluation parameters and actual server argument dictionaries. All 1319 requests in each run reused 768 device-cached prefix tokens; neither run forced host-cache reload. Full logs, exact metrics, source hashes and per-question answers were retained. Observed evaluation runtime / output throughput: unset **227.836 s / 691.215 token/s**, enabled **205.004 s / 768.774 token/s**. Other devices on the host had existing workloads; these observations are not a controlled performance benchmark. A2, A5 and CANN 9.2 remain untested.

### Historical validation on machine 209 (2026-09-18)

Ran the existing `test/registered/npu/basic_function/HiCache/test_npu_hicache_mla.py` at commit `1344e1e2a5ca3e07bf6140b8c606e38465fbc55c` on four **Ascend910_9362 (A3)** devices with **CANN 9.1.0, PyTorch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post4 and Transformers 5.12.1**.

Used the full `vllm-ascend/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-W8A8` checkpoint, adapting its local filesystem path. Each run used TP=4, HiCache enabled, `hicache_ratio=1.2`, `mem_fraction_static=0.8`, all **1319 GSM8K questions**, 5-shot prompts, temperature 0, `max_new_tokens=512` and concurrency 128. The PR-pipeline single-request smoke shortcut was disabled.

| Run pair | ASCEND_USE_FIA | Correct / total | Accuracy | Invalid answers |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original case defaults | unset | 477 / 1319 | 36.163760% | 5 |
| Original case defaults | 1 | 469 / 1319 | 35.557240% | 7 |
| Both servers use `--random-seed 42` | unset | 481 / 1319 | 36.467020% | 6 |
| Both servers use `--random-seed 42` | 1 | 470 / 1319 | 35.633055% | 7 |

All four runs passed the case's 34% accuracy threshold. FIA scored **0.606520 percentage points lower** in the first pair and **0.833965 percentage points lower** in the fixed-seed pair. These measurements do **not** establish accuracy parity or lossless replacement; the ATB default and opt-in gate are retained.

In the fixed-seed pair, 686 final numerical predictions differed: 123 questions changed from correct to incorrect and 112 from incorrect to correct. Both actual server argument dictionaries matched, including seed 42. The first pair used automatically generated server seeds; both pairs are reported. The ATB runs themselves differed on 625 predictions between these two runs, so per-question changes cannot all be attributed to FIA from this experiment alone.

All 1319 requests in each run reused 768 device-cached prefix tokens, exercising prefix prefill with HiCache attached. This workload did not force host-cache eviction/reload. Source hashes, full server logs, exact metrics and per-question answers were retained. `ASCEND_USE_FIA` is an existing backend-wide flag, so this model comparison includes every path affected by the flag rather than isolating only the new prefix branch.

Additional validation performed before the model runs:

- CPU regression: 3 test methods / 11 parameter cases passed, covering FP16/BF16, variable lengths, mixed empty prefixes, noncontiguous inputs, padding, large logits and both operator routes. These tests use numerical substitutes for NPU kernels and compare with full dense SDPA.
- NPU quantization unit suite: all 25 tests passed in the torch_npu 2.10.0.post4 container. These are CPU/mocked tests, including shape, bias and dtype behavior for MXFP8 linear operations.
- Re-ran the gated production `forward_extend` prefix branch on **Ascend910_9362 (A3), CANN 9.1.0, PyTorch 2.10.0 and torch_npu 2.10.0.post4**: **18/18 cases passed**. Cache gather, KV projection, FIA, merge and padding execute on NPU; the reference attention executes on CPU. The branch is loaded unchanged from source with unrelated imports isolated; this is not a complete serving/model test.
- NPU cases cover page sizes 1/128, heads 2/4/8/16/128, query lengths up to 257, prefixes up to 2048, mixed empty prefixes and zero/nonzero padding. NoPE/RoPE/V dimensions are 128/64/128.

| dtype | Maximum absolute error | Maximum per-case RMSE | atol / rtol |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FP16 | 0.001953125 | 0.000209168 | 0.003 / 0.003 |
| BF16 | 0.015625 | 0.001710953 | 0.02 / 0.02 |

All NPU branch cases also check output device, shape, dtype, finite values and zero padding. A2/A5 and CANN 9.2 have not been hardware tested.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### NZ prefix-cache validation on A3 (2026-09-24)

Commit `0c8ebbce034c11b5e0b9c2fec3193def9de2aa74` uses the existing `gather_mla_cache_pages` helper from #39589 for both latent and RoPE prefix reads in the two-FIA branch. It restores logical token order before projection and TND attention when the KV cache uses PA-NZ storage. The helper is byte-identical to #39589 after newline normalization. ND behavior is preserved.

**Environment:** machine 151, Ascend910_9362 (A3), CANN 9.1.0, PyTorch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post6. The patch changes only the two cache-gather calls; it does not reintroduce the reverted quantization API changes.

**Operator-path validation and performance:** 18 cases plus 6 independent reruns passed. The fixture uses the actual `NPUMLATokenToKVPool._set_fia_nz_kv_buffer` and its index helper, executing real NPU scatter with randomized token write order. Both latent and RoPE readback are bitwise equal to the logical ND cache. Across all cases, the fixed NZ branch and fixed ND branch outputs are bitwise equal to the original ND branch output. Sampled CPU FP32 reference checks also pass (maximum RMS relative error 0.2995%). The unfixed NZ branch is retained as a negative control and shows RMS relative errors of 6.55%-119.16% on these synthetic cases.

The independent rerun below measures median amortized wall time for cache gather, BF16 projection, attention, copies and merge. QK=192, V=128, latent=512, page=128, H=4; BF16/eager. It uses 20 warmups and 9 rounds of 30 calls per method with randomized method order. NZ BSND explicitly selects the existing per-request branch for the same inputs, without changing production dispatch. NZ here describes cache storage; the two attention calls still use TND inputs after gathering.

| Case | ND before (ms) | ND fixed (ms) | NZ fixed (ms) | NZ overhead vs ND | NZ BSND (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| b1_q100_p768_h4 | 0.507 | 0.509 | 0.567 | +11.39% | 0.440 |
| b8_q100_p768_h4 | 0.563 | 0.565 | 0.627 | +11.04% | 2.061 |
| b32_q100_p768_h4 | 0.630 | 0.629 | 0.712 | +13.16% | 6.819 |
| b1_q1024_p8192_h4 | 0.550 | 0.552 | 0.611 | +10.60% | 0.494 |
| b4_q1024_p8192_h4 | 1.746 | 1.745 | 1.833 | +5.03% | 1.718 |
| b8_q1024_p8192_h4 | 3.365 | 3.364 | 3.502 | +4.09% | 3.518 |

NZ layout restoration adds about 4%-13% to the two-FIA prefix branch in this rerun. With NZ disabled, the helper adds no layout conversion; the first sweep measured ND before/after differences within approximately -0.34% to +0.65%. Short-query batched two-FIA remains faster than per-request BSND. These are branch measurements and do not establish whole-model speedup.

**Full model accuracy:** ran the original `test_npu_hicache_mla.py` on the same physical devices 0-3 with DeepSeek-V2-Lite-W8A8, TP=4, HiCache enabled, radix enabled, seed=42, all 1319 GSM8K questions, 5-shot, temperature=0, max_new_tokens=512 and concurrency=128. Both runs set `ASCEND_USE_FIA=1`; only `SGLANG_USE_FIA_NZ` changes. The source, model path, dataset, devices, launch arguments and evaluation settings match.

| SGLANG_USE_FIA_NZ | Correct / total | Accuracy | Invalid | Result | Eval runtime (s) | Output token/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 473 / 1319 | 35.860500% | 6 | passed | 229.363 | 701.845 |
| 1 | 465 / 1319 | 35.253980% | 5 | passed | 246.641 | 652.957 |

NZ minus ND: **-0.606520 percentage points**. Final numerical predictions differ on 581 questions (96 correct-to-incorrect, 88 incorrect-to-correct). These full-model runs exercise other NZ-dependent cache/decode paths as well, so model-level differences cannot be attributed to the prefix gather alone. Evaluation runtime and token/s are observations from accuracy runs with variable generation lengths, not a controlled serving performance benchmark. The host is shared; another process was observed on device 3 at the end of the NZ run, so model-run timing is not a device-exclusive measurement.

Device-prefix cache hits: ND 1319/1319, NZ 1319/1319; cached tokens: ND 1012992, NZ 1012992. Host-cache reload hits: ND 0, NZ 0. This does not establish host-cache eviction/reload correctness when those counts are zero. A2/A5 and CANN 9.2 are not hardware-validated by this run. Full logs, inputs, source hashes, timing samples and per-question predictions were retained.

### Controlled prefix-branch comparison on A3 (2026-09-22)

Measured commit `ec72a1dd7c4292477bdd8e317a55f87c44f04357` on 2026-09-22, machine 151: **one Ascend910_9362 (A3), CANN 9.1.0 (B070 container), PyTorch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post6**, BF16, NZ disabled, eager execution. The main shape uses QK=192 (NoPE=128 + RoPE=64), V=128, latent=512, page size=128 and H=4 per rank (the DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP=4 head shape); no TP communication is executed.

The comparison is between two **FIA** implementations of MLA prefix prefill:

- **Two FIA V2 + merge:** this PR's batched TND current-token attention and prefix attention, followed by `npu_attention_update`.
- **Concat + BSND FIA:** the existing `if layer.qk_head_dim == layer.v_head_dim` branch, concatenating prefix/current K/V and issuing one BSND FIA call **per request**. B requests therefore issue B FIA calls.

The benchmark extracts both branch bodies directly from the recorded source and uses identical Q/K/V, cache, projection weights and sequence metadata. To compare the same DeepSeek input, it explicitly selects the BSND body for QK=192/V=128 despite the production dispatch condition; this CANN build accepted that shape and passed the numerical checks. The production condition and kernel arguments were not changed. This is not a comparison with ATB or an end-to-end comparison of `ASCEND_USE_FIA` enabled/disabled.

Times include cache gather, BF16 `kv_b_proj`, FIA, concatenation/contiguous copies, dtype conversions and merge. They exclude the rest of the model, QKV preparation, scheduling, decode and TP communication, and do not reproduce W8A8 projection. Each value is the median amortized wall time per complete prefix branch, with synchronization at each measurement block. Method order is randomized with a fixed seed. The first sweep uses 12 warmups and 7 rounds of 20 calls per method; an independent rerun uses 20 warmups and 9 rounds of 30 calls. Individually synchronized calls and NPU event spans were also recorded; event spans can include host submission gaps.

**Independent rerun (8 cases).** B = requests, Q = new query tokens per request, P = cached prefix tokens per request, H = heads per rank. A BSND / two-FIA time ratio above 1 favors the PR's two-FIA path.

| B | Q per request | Prefix per request | H | Two FIA V2 + merge (ms) | Concat + BSND FIA (ms) | BSND / two-FIA time |
| ---: | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 100 | 768 | 4 | 0.513 | 0.395 | 0.77 |
| 2 | 100 | 768 | 4 | 0.520 | 0.629 | 1.21 |
| 8 | 100 | 768 | 4 | 0.524 | 1.862 | 3.55 |
| 32 | 100 | 768 | 4 | 0.619 | 6.677 | 10.80 |
| 128 | 100 | 768 | 4 | 2.434 | 26.031 | 10.70 |
| 1 | 1024 | 8192 | 4 | 0.542 | 0.457 | 0.84 |
| 4 | 1024 | 8192 | 4 | 1.715 | 1.645 | 0.96 |
| 8 | 1024 | 8192 | 4 | 3.306 | 3.374 | 1.02 |

**Result:** for Q=100/P=768, the two-FIA branch wins from B=2 in this sweep, reaching **3.55x at B=8** and **10.80x at B=32** in the rerun. At B=1, concatenation is faster: about **23% lower latency** for Q=100/P=768 and **16% lower** for Q=1024/P=8192. With Q=1024/P=8192, B=4 favors BSND by about 4%, while B=8 is near parity; a 1-2% gap should not be treated as a significant stable win. These are prefix-branch ratios, not whole-model speedups.

The source structure is consistent with the trend: per-request concatenation and B FIA submissions become expensive for short-query batches, while the TND path batches requests into two FIA calls plus one merge. B=1 avoids the second call and merge with BSND. This interpretation has not been confirmed by kernel-level profiling. The results support retaining the batched two-FIA path; a B=1 specialization is a possible follow-up, subject to device/version and full-model validation.

| 1 | 256 | 2048 | 4 | 0.500 | 0.381 | 0.76 |

The mixed B=10 case uses query lengths `[101,870,876,874,869,864,904,863,837,768]` and prefix lengths `[768,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]`, matching an earlier observed batch shape with synthetic tensor values. It favors two FIA by **2.84x**. B=128/Q=100 contains 12,800 query tokens and is an extended sweep point, not a claim that default chunk limits produce that batch.

**Numerical checks:** all 18 sweep cases and all 8 rerun cases passed full-output pairwise comparison (`atol=0.02`, `rtol=0.02`) and sampled CPU FP32 full-attention reference checks. Maximum full-output absolute difference between methods was **0.001953125**; maximum per-case pairwise RMS relative difference was **0.3022%**. Maximum sampled RMS relative error against CPU FP32 was **0.2995%** for two FIA and **0.2296%** for BSND. The CPU reference uses the same projected K/V. This checks the sampled operator paths; it is not a new GSM8K accuracy run. Hardware conclusions here are limited to this A3/CANN/torch_npu configuration.

### Historical accuracy-run timings

The fixed-seed full GSM8K runs measured 193.304 s / 814.391 output tokens per second with FIA unset, and 196.474 s / 801.729 output tokens per second with FIA enabled. The first pair measured 225.281 s / 697.903 and 195.270 s / 802.929 respectively. These are accuracy-run measurements with differing generation lengths and dynamic batches, not a controlled performance benchmark; no speedup is claimed. At the commits measured in this section, the FIA path was opt-in and used a separate merge with FP32 intermediate outputs. The current MLA prefix path selects FIA TND unconditionally.

title: [Fix] [Intel] cpu-kernel: Fix rope for VLA model
author: jianan-gu
body:
## Motivation
`torch.ops.sgl_kernel.apply_rotary_pos_emb_cpu` kernel only takes 3D `[num_tokens, num_heads, head_size]` inputs and had no `unsqueeze_dim` argument. Pi0.5 calls it with 4D `[batch, num_heads, seq_len, head_size]` q/k and `unsqueeze_dim=1`, so it failed on CPU:

```
"/python/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/vlas/pi05_core.py", line 382, in forward
    query_states, key_states = native_apply_rotary_pos_emb(
  File "//lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/_ops.py", line 1350, in __call__
    return self._op(*args, **kwargs)
RuntimeError: sgl_kernel::apply_rotary_pos_emb_cpu() expected at most 4 argument(s) but received 5 argument(s). Declaration: sgl_kernel::apply_rotary_pos_emb_cpu(Tensor query, Tensor key, Tensor cos, Tensor sin) -> (Tensor, Tensor)
```
- https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/vlas/pi05_core.py#L902C32-L902C59

## Modifications

- `apply_rotary_pos_emb_cpu` now takes `unsqueeze_dim` (default 1) and supports q/k of 3D and higher, with the head dim at `unsqueeze_dim` (e.g. `[B, H, S, D]` or `[B, S, H, D]`). It is out-of-place, matching `apply_rotary_pos_emb_native`.
- The neox rope path now handles float32 inputs, and the CPU graph fake op is updated for the new signature.

## Test Coverage

- pi0.5 model functionality

- `test_apply_rotary_pos_emb` in `test/registered/cpu/test_rope.py`. It compares against the native reference for:
  (1) 3D with GQA, 4D `[B, H, S, D]` with `unsqueeze_dim=1`, and (2) 4D `[B, S, H, D]` with `unsqueeze_dim=2`

title: [Spec] Reuse K3 auxiliary outputs across decode CUDA graph sizes
author: chromecast56
body:
## Motivation

With DFlash/DSpark, every captured decode CUDA graph keeps its own packed aux hidden-state output alive, so reserved graph memory grows with the sum of captured sizes. One buffer sized for the largest graph is enough: the worker writes target hidden states into draft KV before the next target forward on that stream.

## Modifications

- `AuxHiddenStatePacker` (#37329) takes an optional `out=` buffer, checks its shape and dtype on the first `append`, and writes captures into it.
- `DecodeCudaGraphRunner` keeps one `[max_num_token, K * hidden]` buffer per stream (so PD-multiplexed streams don't alias) and gives each captured size a row slice through `ForwardBatch.aux_hidden_states_buffer`. The buffer is used only for DFlash-family target runners with `pp_size == 1`, and only for models implementing `SupportsSharedAuxHiddenStates.get_packed_aux_hidden_size()`.
- Kimi K3 now captures through `AuxHiddenStatePacker` (PP stages keep the list, since inherited captures arrive already concatenated) and is the first model to opt in. Other packer users (DeepSeek V2, MiMo V2) and EAGLE3 are unchanged.

## Tests

- `test_spec_aux_hidden_state.py`: packing into an external buffer gives the same result as the list-path concat, lands in the caller's storage, and raises on a buffer that doesn't fit.
- `test_decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`: graph sizes 64/8/32 share one buffer; a second stream gets its own; non-DFlash, draft, PP and non-opt-in models get no shared buffer.

GPU check, Kimi K3 colocated TP8 on 8xB300 with DFLASH (block size 8), GSM8K 5-shot on all 1,319 questions. The comparison is main + #40794 (K3 DFLASH) with and without this PR. Target-verify CUDA-graph memory per GPU goes from 2.215 GB to **1.756 GB** (−0.46 GB, −21%), and startup free memory rises by the same amount. Accuracy and acceptance are unchanged: 95.0% / average accept length 5.07 without this PR, 95.6% / 5.06 with it.

title: Fix TopK v2 fallback when 16-block cluster capacity is zero
author: luoroger37
body:
## Motivation

TopK v2 can launch an unsupported 16-block cluster even when the device occupancy probe reports zero capacity. The loader swallows the zero-capacity exception and retains the default C16 capacity of `7`.

On NVIDIA H20, this was reproduced with `batch=4`, `seq_len=65536`, and `topk=512`, which failed with `cluster misconfiguration`.

This PR passes the zero-capacity result into JIT compilation so the unsupported path is disabled and the existing fallback is used.

## Modifications

- Handle the 8-block and 16-block probes in one loop and always emit the corresponding capacity macro after each successful query, including zero-capacity results.
- Distinguish zero schedulable clusters from unexpected probe errors. Zero disables the corresponding cluster path; other errors propagate for both probes.
- Default the optional 16-block path to disabled unless a positive probe result enables it.
- Reuse the existing dispatch guards: a zero C16 capacity falls back to C8 when available; zero C8 capacity skips the persistent pool and permits the existing non-cluster path.
- Remove the PR-specific mocked host tests and shape-only GPU regressions as requested in review. The existing upstream TopK v2 test file is unchanged.

The fix uses occupancy probing and requires no H20-specific device-name checks.

## Accuracy Tests

Previously recorded validation on NVIDIA H20 (78 SMs), PyTorch `2.11.0+cu130`, CUDA `13.0`, using upstream base `3401b75240d7` and the initial fix `f453a06894e7`:

| Check | Original upstream | Initial fix |

| `batch=4, seq_len=65536, topk=512` | `cluster misconfiguration` | Pass |
| TopK v2 regression file | Stops after 72 passes at the failing case | 292 passed |

The 292 passes included four PR-specific GPU cases that have now been removed. This is historical evidence for the initial fix, not a GPU rerun of the review revision.

Validation of the review revision:

- Local host-logic smoke checks passed for positive/zero capacities, unexpected probe errors, and architectures without cluster probing, using isolated source functions and mocked probe/JIT boundaries.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This is a launch compatibility fix; no performance improvement is claimed. The affected inputs fail before the fix, so there is no valid pre-fix execution time for comparison.

title: [diffusion] attention: add fp8_fa_sm120 FP8 backend for SM120 GPUs
author: emre570
body:
## Motivation

SM120 GPUs (GeForce RTX 50, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell) have FP8 tensor cores, but the diffusion
runtime has no FP8 attention path for them. On SM120 the default is Torch SDPA, and BF16
attention there is already near the hardware ceiling: cuDNN SDPA reaches 95% of the measured
BF16 mma.sync peak on an RTX 5080. The only way to go faster on these cards is lower precision.

On MiniMax-H3 (56 heads, head_dim 128, S=30272) attention is about 47% of the GPU time of a
denoise step, so this is where an FP8 kernel pays off.

This PR adds `fp8_fa_sm120`: an opt-in attention backend around an FP8 (E4M3) flash-attention
forward written in CuTe-DSL for SM120.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fp8_fa_sm120/`
  - `kernel.py`: the CuTe-DSL kernel. E4M3 QK and PV with FP32 accumulation, online softmax in
    registers, two-stage K/V prefetch so the copy overlaps the math, probabilities packed to
    E4M3 inside registers (no shared-memory round trip), 128 x 32 CTA tile.
  - `fused_prep.py`: two Triton passes that quantize strided BF16 Q/K/V views per head straight
    into the kernel buffers (amax, then pack). No FP32 intermediates, no layout copy.
  - `plan.py`: one compiled kernel plus its buffers per (S, H, strides, scale, device).
    `bind_inputs()` rebinds storage, so all DiT layers share one compilation.
- `multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/attention/backends/fp8_fa_sm120_attn.py`: the backend. Handles
  `forward` and `forward_varlen` (including the MiniMax-H3 trailing-padding packing). Falls back
  to cuDNN SDPA for causal, batch > 1, head_dim != 128, non-BF16 and non-SM120 calls, and logs
  each fallback reason once.
- `AttentionBackendEnum.FP8_FA_SM120` and a resolver in `platforms/cuda.py`. Nothing selects the
  backend automatically.
- Docs: two rows in `sglang-diffusion/attention_backends.mdx`.
- Tests: `multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_fp8_fa_sm120_attn.py` (skipped unless an SM120 GPU is
  present).

No new dependency: `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` and Triton are already required.

Limits: dense, non-causal, batch 1, head_dim 128, BF16 inputs. The device gate is SM120 only.
SM121 can get the same kernel later, but I have no SM121 hardware to test on, so it is not part
of this PR. Each new sequence length compiles once (about 10 s). The plan keeps E4M3 copies
of Q/K/V plus the output buffer (about 1.1 GB at S=30272, H=56), shared by all layers.

The kernel structure (tiled mma.sync, online softmax, register accumulators) follows the NVIDIA
CuTe FlashAttention-2 example. The TMA layout, swizzle and K/V scheduling choices were informed by Blake Ledden's CuTe-DSL FlashAttention-2 port for SM120 (NVIDIA/cutlass#3030), which was also the public FP8 reference on this hardware before the FlashInfer kernel landed; thanks to Blake for walking me through its design. 

The closest existing FP8 kernel for these GPUs is `fmha_v2_prefill_sm120` in FlashInfer. The diffusion runtime does not call it. It is the FP8 reference in the tables below.

## Accuracy Tests

Per call, against cuDNN SDPA BF16 on the same inputs (H=56, D=128, normally distributed
synthetic Q/K/V): relative RMS 0.0535 to 0.0539 at S=20440 and S=30272. The FlashInfer FP8 kernel
lands in the same band on the same inputs, so the error is the price of E4M3 Q/K/V, not
something specific to this kernel.

End to end, MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA, 768x768, 107 frames, 50 steps, seed 42, RTX PRO 6000:

| clip pair | PSNR (dB) | SSIM |
|---|---:|---:|
| stock Torch SDPA vs stock cuDNN SDPA (noise floor between two BF16 backends) | 22.9 | 0.82 |
| `fp8_fa_sm120` vs stock cuDNN SDPA | 19.75 | 0.707 |

So the FP8 clip sits about 3 dB below the spread between two stock BF16 backends. Subject,
composition and motion are the same and the clip is sharp. I did not find a visible artifact,
but this is a lossy backend and that is why it is opt-in only. Clips are deterministic across
pods (the cuDNN clip from two different pods is bit-identical).

Unit tests (7) cover: output against cuDNN at two sequence lengths including a masked tail,
plan reuse across calls and across impl instances, H3 trailing-padding varlen, multi-segment
varlen, causal fallback, and resolution by name.

Frames 0, 53 and 106 of the two clips, cuDNN SDPA on top and `fp8_fa_sm120` below. The full clips
are attached under the image.

<!-- drag pr/artifacts/h3-frames-cudnn-vs-fp8_fa_sm120.png, h3-cudnn-sdpa.mp4 and h3-fp8_fa_sm120.mp4 here -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel only, H=56, D=128, non-causal, CUDA events, 20 warmup, 5 x 10 iterations, times in ms.
cuDNN SDPA, Torch SDPA and FA4 have no FP8 path on SM120, so their BF16 kernels are the production
baseline this backend replaces. FlashInfer `fmha_v2_prefill_sm120` is the only other FP8 attention
kernel for these GPUs, so it is the FP8 reference.

RTX 5080:

| S | `fp8_fa_sm120` (FP8) | FlashInfer `fmha_v2_prefill_sm120` (FP8) | cuDNN SDPA (BF16) | Torch FlashAttention-2 SDPA (BF16) | SGLang FA4 SM120 (BF16) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 30272 | 123.6 | 131.8 | 226.2 | 245.4 | 251.8 |
| 20440 | 57.0 | 60.4 | 106.5 | 112.4 | 115.5 |

RTX PRO 6000:

| S | `fp8_fa_sm120` (FP8) | FlashInfer `fmha_v2_prefill_sm120` (FP8) | cuDNN SDPA (BF16) | Torch FlashAttention-2 SDPA (BF16) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 30272 | 43.7 | 53.7 | 73.7 | 74.4 |
| 20440 | 19.9 | 25.0 | 32.3 | 34.2 |

End to end on MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA (768x768, 107 frames, 50 steps, RTX PRO 6000, same pod, v0.5.19
tag with stock pins): 6.87 s/it with `torch_cudnn_sdpa`, 5.61 s/it with `fp8_fa_sm120` (-18.3%).

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [XPU] Enable fused QK-norm + RoPE for Qwen3-MoE
author: mehersai07
body:
## Motivation

Qwen3-MoE already has a fused QK-norm + RoPE path, but the gate in `Qwen3MoeAttention.__init__` requires `_is_cuda`. On XPU this falls back to two RMSNorm launches plus a separate RoPE launch per layer, even though `sgl-kernel-xpu` already has the kernel AOT as `fused_inplace_qknorm_rope` which uses the cos/sin cache from rotary embedding.

This enables that kernel on XPU, cutting the q/k-norm + RoPE stage from 3 launches per layer to 1.

## Modifications

The device dispatch lives in the kernel wrapper, so the model keeps a single code path and other callers get XPU support for free.

`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py`:

- New branch on XPU using the `fused_inplace_qknorm_rope`.

Kept opt-in behind the existing flag `--enable-fused-qk-norm-rope` to match CUDA.

## Accuracy Tests

The new `test/registered/xpu/test_fused_inplace_qknorm_rope_xpu.py` added to `nightly-xpu-1-gpu` nightly suite to cover the kernel beyond this model: the packed-qkv strided views this branch passes, a case against the model's unfused `apply_qk_norm` + `RotaryEmbedding` path with the fused call fed from `rotary_emb.cos_sin_cache` as this branch does (default and YaRN `rope_scaling`, `theta=1e6`).

**End-to-end**, GSM8K 1319 examples (1314 scored), greedy, Qwen3-30B-A3B, TP=4.
Both arms verified via `/get_server_info` to have actually resolved
`enable_fused_qk_norm_rope` as intended before running:

| | baseline | fused |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K | 94.14 | 94.6 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**q/k-norm + RoPE stage**, rank 0 over 40 profiled decode steps, Qwen3-30B-A3B TP=4 on 4x Intel Arc Pro B60, launches / device ms:

| component | baseline | fused |
|---|---|---|
| q/k RMSNorm (`FusedNormKernelFunctor`, 3 instantiations) | 3,858 / 79.6 ms | 18 / 0.52 ms |
| RoPE (`FusedRopeCacheKernel`) | 1,920 / 23.07 ms | 0 / 0.00 ms |
| `FusedQKNormRopeCacheKernel` | 0 / 0.00 ms | 1,920 / 40.80 ms |
| **stage total** | **5,778 / 102.67 ms** | **1,938 / 41.32 ms** |

**−66% launches, −60% device ms.**.  The kernel reads cos/sin from the existing `rotary_emb.cos_sin_cache` and takes the model's int64 positions directly, so no per-layer cast is needed. Total device time on rank 0 drops 5,672 → 5,495 ms (−3.1%).

**End-to-end**, `bench_serving`, input 1024 / output 256, one run per arm (baseline run-to-run spread ~1%):

| conc | baseline | fused | delta | TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 21.4 tok/s | 22.9 tok/s | +7.0% | 46.5 → 43.5 ms |
| 8 | 158.4 tok/s | 168.4 tok/s | +6.3% | 49.0 → 46.0 ms |
| 32 | 557.6 tok/s | 583.9 tok/s | +4.7% | 54.7 → 52.1 ms |

**+4.7-7.0% output throughput** with TPOT down 4.6-6.6%.

cc: @rahulvijayaraghavan @rbabukv

title: [Refactor] Deduplicate kernel helpers and remove unused code
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Several kernel integrations carry copies of the same TMA builders, warp primitives, alignment code and compiler policy. Fixes then need to be repeated across implementations, while unused fallback/cache helpers obscure the active paths. Consolidate these implementations and remove unused private code without changing the kernel algorithms or dispatch thresholds.

## Modifications

- Share the chunk and recurrent/output-state TMA descriptor builders across the six Blackwell GDN/KDA CuTe kernels. Keep their distinct state layouts, tile sizes, stages and swizzles.
- Reuse DSA's existing split-K reduction and split heuristics in sparse decode. DSV4's different architecture-specific heuristic stays separate.
- Reuse native LoRA token indexing and large-expert alignment in the experimental paths; update the Marlin runner's import to the canonical implementation.
- Use existing `warp`, `bits` and PDL helpers in packed KDA, MoE alignment and Inkling. Centralize the identical activation/SiTU fast-math policy while preserving the HIP/Blackwell precision rules.
- Remove unused DSV4 compression fallback, KDA repack caches, DSA reference dequantizer, MiMo ffprobe helper and NPU scaling helper.
- Remove two source-spelling-only test files and the scheduler's source-string assertions. Keep its MTP behavior test and the numerical, sentinel, layout, runtime-flow and CUDA import regression tests.

28 files; 191 insertions and 1,093 deletions. No new test files or benchmark artifacts.

## Accuracy Tests

On GB300 (SM103), PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, Triton `3.7.1`, CuTe DSL `4.6.2`:

| Existing tests | Result |
| --- | --- |
| GDN/KDA CuTe prefill, including pooled state | 15 passed |
| MoE alignment and virtual-expert sentinel/boundary cases | 52 passed, 5 abstract-base cases skipped |
| Activation and Kimi K3 SiTU | 100 passed |
| Retained Marlin runtime/import and scheduler MTP tests | 4 passed |

Additional baseline/candidate checks covered 20 seeded configurations over four runs: 126 exact tensor comparisons passed. GDN/KDA outputs and recurrent state, packed KDA with/without the gate bound, and sparse split-K reduction (including non-power-of-two active splits) were bitwise equal. Merged LoRA alignment matched an independent mapping/ownership/padding reference and the baseline after canonicalizing unspecified atomic scatter order. Both LoRA token-indexing specializations compiled and returned the expected positions.

SM80 and SM90 cross-compilation passed for activation, SiTU, packed KDA and both MoE alignment modules. Both Inkling wrappers (six exported entry points) compiled on SM103. Pre-commit passed.

AMD/NPU execution, model-level evaluation and multi-rank Inkling communication were not run; cross-compilation is not execution coverage.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel/pipeline checks against main `7714b182f2`, sequentially on the same GB300 with seeded inputs, warm CUDA graphs and baseline/candidate/candidate/baseline ordering. These are kernel checks, not serving-throughput results.

| Case | Main (us) | Cleanup (us) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GDN prefill, 257 sequences | 192.904 | 193.042 |
| Packed KDA, batch 64 | 11.927 | 11.923 |
| Sparse MLA reduction, 7 active splits | 2.818 | 2.818 |
| Merged LoRA alignment, 2048 tokens | 11.329 | 11.393 |

All separate-process cases were within 1% except KDA prefill at 257 sequences (+2.56%). A follow-up swapped only the three changed CuTe implementations in one process, sharing identical inputs and scratch buffers and alternating graph order for ten pairs: **606.254 vs 606.671 us (+0.069%)**, with bitwise-equal outputs. The initial difference did not persist under these controls; no speedup is claimed.

Rebased onto main `191172fa74`; the intervening changes concern GLM deployment docs and unified-tree host LRU, with no kernel overlap. Final kernel sources were checked against the validated snapshot and retained runtime tests rerun after rebasing.

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit formatting and lint checks.
- [x] Reused existing numerical/runtime tests; no new test files needed for this cleanup.
- [x] Kernel accuracy and timing results above.
- [x] Follow `sglang.kernels` conventions and retain architecture-specific behavior.
- [x] No public API or user-facing documentation changes required.
