title: [Perf] Fork-safe import: no CUDA context at import time, lighter argument parsing
author: xenshinu
body: Following #39683, decompose it into a stack of PRs for better management. # **WHAT IS IN THIS PR:** Motivation: importing sglang created a CUDA context in every process through device probes, and `server_args` pulled the parser registries and `sglang.kernels` into every process that parses arguments. A process with a CUDA context cannot be a `fork()` parent, which rules out forkserver-based worker startup (PR 2), and the import cost lands on the launcher's critical path (PR 3). Modifications: `get_device_sm()` answers from NVML while `torch.cuda` is uninitialized; `get_device_module()` picks the module from the platform checks; `GraphCaptureContext.stream` becomes a string annotation; DeepGEMM reads `SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE` at call time. CLI choices for `--reasoning-parser` / `--tool-call-parser` come from dependency-free name lists asserted in sync with the registries; the kv-canary enum, torchvision and `HfApi` are imported where used; flashinfer's JIT logger level is set by name. Always on; behaviour unchanged. Note for reviewers: `sgl_kernel` still initializes CUDA on import on the default path, so the launcher keeps a context until that is fixed upstream; PR 2 answers those probes from NVML inside the forkserver. Accuracy: no model code touched. Speed: `import sglang.srt.server_args` no longer imports the parser registries (about 3 s of imports on our hosts); end-to-end gains are measured in PR 3. Tests: `function_call/test_parser_names.py`, `parser/test_reasoning_parser_names.py`. # **OLD DESCRIPTION:** ## Motivation A cold `sglang serve` spends 15-25 s in process init before any model work starts: the launcher imports the server stack, then every spawned worker re-imports the same sglang/torch stack, and on the DP path the DP controller re-imports once more before it spawns the schedulers. Every process also created a CUDA context at import time, which wastes a context in the launcher, detokenizer and DP controller and rules out `fork()`-based worker startup. This PR makes the import fork-safe and, behind three opt-in environment variables, lets workers fork from a preloaded forkserver and start before the launcher imports its HTTP stack. With the variables unset every code path runs exactly as before. Time from `sglang serve` to `/health`, Qwen3-30B-A3B (bf16) on H200, mean of three warm passes per cell (the first, cold pass that fills the weight page cache and the kernel JIT caches is excluded; one pass ran with the launch order reversed; all agree within 1 s): | config | knobs off | forkserver + pre-spawn | + daemon | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Single GPU | 47.3 s | 39.8 s | 39.5 s | | DP2 | 56.0 s | 40.9 s | 40.5 s | | TP2 | 47.6 s | 40.5 s | 39.9 s | | EP2 (DeepEP low-latency, DP attention) | 46.6 s | 32.1 s | 31.4 s | Where the time goes, from the rank-0 log stages: | stage | knobs off | forkserver + pre-spawn | | |---|---:|---:|---| | process init (launcher imports, spawn, worker import, scheduler setup) | 15-23 s | 8-9 s | this PR | | weight loading (61 GB bf16) | 6-10 s | 6-10 s | unchanged | | CUDA graph capture, prefill + decode | 11-18 s | 11-18 s | unchanged | | distributed init, KV pool, tokenizer manager + HTTP server | 4-6 s | 4-6 s | unchanged | ## Modifications Four commits, each usable on its own: 1. **No CUDA at import** (always on). `get_device_sm()` answers from NVML while torch.cuda is uninitialized, `get_device_module()` picks the module from the platform checks, `GraphCaptureContext.stream` becomes a string annotation, DeepGEMM reads `SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE` at call time. A process without a CUDA context can be a `fork()` parent. 2. **Early forkserver** (`SGLANG_EARLY_FORKSERVER=1`, new `entrypoints/early_forkserver.py`). The multiprocessing forkserver starts at CLI entry with the scheduler, DP controller and detokenizer modules preloaded; workers fork from it instead of re-importing. The child re-applies the launcher's environment and stdio, re-derives the HF offline flags and reports the launcher as its parent. `python -m sglang.srt.entrypoints.early_forkserver` runs a long-lived daemon that publishes its address in `SGLANG_FORKSERVER_FILE`. 3. **Pre-spawn** (`SGLANG_PRESPAWN_WORKERS=1`, new `entrypoints/prespawn.py`, `entrypoints/worker_launch.py`, `managers/process_entry.py`). `run_server()` resolves the config and spawns the schedulers (or the DP controller) right after argument parsing, before importing the HTTP and tokenizer stack; `Engine._launch_subprocesses` adopts them. Weight-cache daemons, the engine-info bootstrap server and Ray stay on the normal path. 4. **Lighter launcher path** (`sglang/__init__.py`, `server_args.py`, `cli/utils.py`, `utils/common.py`). Under the pre-spawn flag the package applies the transformers patches when transformers is imported and resolves the frontend API lazily (`import sglang`: 4.6 s -> 0.24 s); by default it imports eagerly as before. CLI choices for the parsers come from dependency-free name lists asserted in sync with the registries; a few imports move to their call sites. > **IMPORTANT note on the copy of the engine's launch code.** `worker_launch.py` duplicates the launch preparation and the scheduler spawn loop of `engine.py` verbatim, against the "avoid duplication" style rule. This is deliberate for a first PR: pre-spawn cannot import `engine.py` (that import is what it overlaps), and we did not want to restructure the engine here, so `engine.py` keeps its code (19 added lines ignoring whitespace; the original preparation block moves into an `else:` branch, see `git diff -w`) and `test_worker_launch.py` fails when the copy drifts from the engine or when the light modules import the server stack. > **I am happy to remove the duplication based on the reviewers' opinion: the launch path moves into `worker_launch.py` and `engine.py` re-exports it. That variant exists and can go into this PR or a follow-up.** New environment variables (documented in `environment_variables.mdx`): `SGLANG_EARLY_FORKSERVER` (default off), `SGLANG_FORKSERVER_FILE` (default `/tmp/sglang_forkserver.json`), `SGLANG_PRESPAWN_WORKERS` (default off), `SGLANG_MP_START_METHOD` (set by `start_early()`, not meant to be set by hand). ## Accuracy Tests No change to model forward or sampling code. Greedy output for "The capital of France is" is identical across all 48 launches of the matrix above and, in an earlier run, identical to upstream main in the same environment. ## Speed Tests and Profiling See the tables and figure in Motivation (4 configurations x 3 settings x 3 warm passes on one H200 host; `experimental/startup/startup_matrix.sh` and `startup_matrix_report.py` in the foundry-org repo). Also on the branch: `import sglang` 4.6 s -> 0.24 s under the pre-spawn flag, `import sglang.srt.server_args` 5.3 s -> 3.0 s. With the knobs on, pre-spawn fires about 6.5 s after interpreter start: 1.7 s of imports and 4.5-5 s of `ServerArgs.resolve_once()`, which this PR keeps ahead of the spawn so the workers receive the same record as on the normal path. Unit tests (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`): `entrypoints/test_early_forkserver.py`, `entrypoints/test_prespawn.py`, `entrypoints/test_worker_launch.py` (copy matches the engine source-for-source; light modules never import the server stack), `cli/test_sglang_init.py` (eager default; lazy mode stays free of torch/transformers), `function_call/test_parser_names.py`, `parser/test_reasoning_parser_names.py`. ## How to reproduce Unit tests (about 15 s): ```bash cd test/registered/unit python3 -m unittest entrypoints.test_early_forkserver entrypoints.test_prespawn entrypoints.test_worker_launch cli.test_sglang_init function_call.test_parser_names parser.test_reasoning_parser_names ``` Launcher import cost with and without the lazy package init: ```bash time python3 -c "import sglang" # eager (default) SGLANG_PRESPAWN_WORKERS=1 time python3 -c "import sglang" # lazy ``` Time to `/health` for one configuration under the three settings (set `MODEL`, `ARGS` such as `--dp 2` or `--tp 2`, and a free `PORT`): ```bash serve_and_time() { # usage: serve_and_time "" t0=$(date +%s.%N) env $1 sglang serve --model-path $MODEL --port $PORT --host 127.0.0.1 $ARGS > server.log 2>&1 & until curl -fsS -m 2 http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 0.5; done python3 -c "import time; print(f'health after {time.time()-$t0:.1f} s')" curl -s http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/generate -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"text":"The capital of France is","sampling_params":{"max_new_tokens":8,"temperature":0}}' pkill -f "port $PORT"; sleep 3 } MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B PORT=31000 ARGS="" serve_and_time "" # knobs off serve_and_time "SGLANG_EARLY_FORKSERVER=1 SGLANG_PRESPAWN_WORKERS=1" # forkserver + pre-spawn SGLANG_FORKSERVER_FILE=/tmp/sglang_forkserver.json python3 -m sglang.srt.entrypoints.early_forkserver & # daemon, once per host sleep 8 serve_and_time "SGLANG_EARLY_FORKSERVER=1 SGLANG_PRESPAWN_WORKERS=1 SGLANG_FORKSERVER_FILE=/tmp/sglang_forkserver.json" ``` Run each setting once to warm the page cache and kernel caches, then measure. The stage breakdown comes from the rank-0 log timestamps in `server.log` relative to `t0`: `Init torch distributed begin` (end of process init), `Load weight begin/end`, `KV Cache is allocated`, first `Capture ... CUDA graph begin` to last `... end`, first `GET /health ... 200`. ## Follow-up work - **Graph capture is now the bottleneck.** After this PR, weight loading (6-10 s) and CUDA graph capture (11-18 s) dominate every bar above. The foundry integration ([CUDA graph save/restore across processes](https://github.com/foundry-org/sglang)) restores the captured graphs from an archive in a few seconds instead of re-capturing them on every launch, and it will be another PR once all tests are done. - **Make the daemon count.** A warm daemon saves only 0.5-1 s here because the fork waits for `ServerArgs.resolve_once()` (4.5-5 s), which this PR keeps ahead of the spawn so workers get the same record as the normal path. Two options keep a single resolution and still move the fork to about 2 s: make resolution cheaper (most of it is imports of the model stack, recoverable with lazy imports), or spawn the workers first and have the child block on the launcher's resolved record over the pipe before it does anything. With either, the daemon's instant fork becomes the critical-path win it was designed to be. - **Smaller items** measured on the research branch: memoize `get_tokenizer()` in the scheduler process (the tokenizer is loaded twice, about 0.6 s), lazy LoRA drainer/overlap-loader imports in the scheduler (about 0.5 s). - **De-duplicate the launch code** by moving it into `worker_launch.py`, if the reviewers prefer that over the guarded copy. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #35521688622](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35521688622) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #35521688477](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35521688477) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #35521688646](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35521688646)

title: [AMD] Small-M MXFP4 fused-MoE kernel for gfx950 (Qwen)
author: zijiecode
body:
## Motivation

For decode batches of 1 to ~40 tokens per rank, the MXFP4 MoE is the biggest cost per step on MI355X, and AITER
`fused_moe` only uses a small part of the HBM bandwidth there. This PR adds a HIP kernel pair for these shapes; above 40 tokens AITER is still used.

## Modifications

- New `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/smallm_moe_gfx950/` (`__init__.py`, `smallm_moe.hip`): built with `hipcc` on
  first use and launched through ctypes, no build-time or wheel change.
- Phase 1: gate/up GEMM per (expert slot, 16-column slice), FP4 expanded with `v_cvt_scalef32_pk_bf16_fp4`, MFMA
  16x16x32 bf16, `silu(g) * u` written as bf16. Phase 2: down GEMM per (token, 64-row slice) with `v_dot2_f32_bf16`,
  top-k weights applied in fp32.
- Uses AITER's existing weight and scale layouts, so loading and preprocessing are untouched. Activations stay bf16.
- `moe_runner/aiter.py`: one guarded call before `fused_moe`, taken for FP4x2 weights, bf16 hidden 4096, per-rank
  intermediate 256 (the TP4 shape), 10 or 11 slots, silu, `tok <= 40`, and none of `expert_mask` / `doweight_stage1` /
  bias / `a1_scale` / `no_combine` / `num_local_tokens`. Everything else is unchanged. The TP2 shape (intermediate 512)
  crosses over to AITER much earlier (~20 tokens) and is left to a follow-up.
- On by default on gfx950; `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_MOE=0` turns it off.
- Registered AMD unit test `test/registered/amd/test_smallm_moe_gfx950.py`: dequantized torch reference (rel L2 < 5e-3
  at 1 / 3 / 16 / 40 tokens), fallback above 40 and for the TP2 shape, the off switch, graph replay == eager. Passes on
  `v0.5.19-rocm720-mi35x-20260915` and `v0.5.18-rocm10-mi35x-20260902`.

## Accuracy Tests

title: [Kernel] Fuse hc_combine_norm for mid-size verify batches (9-96 rows)
author: Stelath
body:
## Motivation

Fuse combine + RMSNorm for 9–96-row speculative verification batches, which currently launch two kernels.

## Modifications

- Extend the existing kernel dispatch and model guard to 96 rows, using 4/2/1 column partitions.
- Preserve large-prefill and MXFP8 paths; add a registered boundary test.

title: [Runtime] Add decode CUDA graph hooks for eager logits processing
author: mxz297
body:
## Motivation

Runners that capture the transformer body and compute logits after replay need to retain every token-row hidden state across graph buckets. Request-count output sizing can truncate those states, and reconstructing `LogitsProcessorOutput` drops fields produced by the eager tail.

## Modifications

- Add explicit graph-output row and capacity hooks, and use them in the breakable backend when allocating and slicing shared output storage.
- Allow runners to override shared logits-buffer capacity and process graph outputs eagerly after replay, within the existing device timer.
- Preserve extra `LogitsProcessorOutput` fields with `dataclasses.replace` when slicing padded logits and hidden states.
- Add `ForwardBatch.defer_logits_to_eager` for model implementations that support transformer-only capture. Copy it into TBO child batches and test inheritance of both `False` and `True`; otherwise the TBO completeness guard rejects even the default value.

The hooks default to current sizing and pass-through behavior. This ports all six shared-runtime files from the source change and adds the TBO inheritance fix and regression subtest from #40226. Current upstream speculative pipeline-output slicing is preserved. Model-specific consumers and verification kernels are outside this port.

## Accuracy Tests

**46 tests and 16 subtests passed at `75b46430c5`.** These cover the complete batch-overlap unit directory, decode profiling, shared-read fences, hidden-state capture, backend selection, and adaptive logits-buffer sizing. Before the fix, all four marker tests reproduced the missing `defer_logits_to_eager` error. The previous head also failed both the marker and dummy-token-mask tests in base CI for the same reason.

**Earlier local CUDA smoke check passed at `066f3ef21e` (not rerun for the TBO-only follow-up):** real breakable-graph capture/replay with 1- and 4-request buckets, three token rows per request, and a padded 3-request replay. Checked shared output storage across capture sizes, eager-tail timing, preservation of subclass and auxiliary output fields, default hook behavior, and shared logits-buffer capacity. The smoke harness was run locally and is not added to CI.

<details>
<summary>Validation commands</summary>

Using an existing Python environment with the checkout's `python/` directory on `PYTHONPATH`:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4 uv run --no-project --active pytest -q -ra --disable-warnings \
  test/registered/unit/batch_overlap \
  test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_model_runner_decode_rows.py \
  test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_decode_cuda_graph_runner.py \
  test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_decode_cuda_graph_shared_read_fence.py \
  test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_hidden_state_graph_recapture.py \
  test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner_backend/test_backend_resolution.py \
  test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner_backend/test_full_cuda_graph_backend.py

uv run --no-project --active pre-commit run --from-ref main --to-ref HEAD
git diff --check main...HEAD
```

The unit-test invocation hides GPUs with a non-existent device index. The separate local smoke harness used one CUDA device, with graph deduplication, graph-pool borrowing, and pre-carving disabled.

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Full-model accuracy evaluations and performance benchmarks were not run for this port. No throughput or latency improvement is claimed here.

## Checklist

- [x] Upstream pre-commit checks pass.
- [x] Existing unit tests and a focused CUDA smoke check pass.
- [x] New extension points are documented in code.
- [x] Existing subclass/caller compatibility reviewed; current upstream pipeline-output slicing retained.
- [ ] Full-model accuracy and speed benchmarks (not run).

title: [HiCache] Preserve all MTP KV and recurrent state
author: paulzhang-tm
body:
## Motivation

An Inkling MTP request that reuses a HiCache prefix must recover every draft head's KV and convolution/recurrent state. The hybrid SWA/Mamba path omitted separate draft state, and its transfer schedule could leave later draft heads unrestored. Inkling also addresses draft SWA buffers with full-token IDs, while target SWA uses independently allocated physical IDs; packing both into the target SWA host pool copies the wrong draft rows.

This change supports all-SWA, mixed, and all-full MTP draft attention. A host hit restores every draft's state before the final target-layer completion event, using the indices owned by each pool.

## Modifications

- Expose Inkling's checkpoint MTP depth to packed-cache discovery and collect every separate draft convolution/temporal pool. Validate compatible state-slot ownership and avoid packing shared target state twice.
- Preserve Inkling's global MTP depth IDs during single-block runner setup, so SWA heads at depth 2 and later receive SWA pools.
- Pack full-attention draft KV into the full host pool. Pack SWA drafts that share target SWA indices into the SWA host pool. Give identity-mapped SWA drafts a separate host pool derived from full-token indices, preserving their SWA head geometry and including their memory in fixed HiCache budgets.
- Pack compatible draft convolution/temporal state, and schedule all packed KV/state restores within the target transfer range. Keep the portable per-layer NPU fallback for separate state allocations.
- Add registered CPU/GPU regressions for config setup, pool discovery, byte-exact restoration, distinct target/draft indices, mixed attention, and host-memory accounting.

No new flags. The existing MXFP8 host-cache restriction on packed MTP remains.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on base `248c202b46d4a44ad46a3f09d48661b0d9ce6257`:

- **105 tests and 16 subtests passed**, including assembly, HiCache dispatch, layer setup, and packed-state regressions.
- **64 GPU transfer cases** on NVIDIA GB300: all-SWA/mixed/all-full drafts and legacy shared-SWA indexing, BF16/FP16 KV, kernel/direct transfers, differing full/SWA head counts, two/four target layers versus three drafts, convolution-only/convolution-plus-temporal state, and ratio/fixed host sizing. Tests clear device buffers after backup and compare every restored byte at different destination slots.
- **Four end-to-end serving cases** with generated Inkling checkpoints: `sss`, `sfs`, and `fff` draft patterns with kernel I/O, plus `sfs` with direct I/O. All restored **768 host tokens and 0 device-cache tokens** after device eviction. Each generated **32 identical tokens with zero logprob difference** versus a cold run and reported 31 speculative verification steps.
- All applicable upstream pre-commit checks passed for the full PR diff, including CI registration against the PR base.

Serving used BF16, FA4, torch GEMM, TP1, write-through HiCache, and disabled CUDA graphs. The environment had sgl-kernel 0.4.6.post1+cu130, so serving bypassed the tree's 0.4.7 minimum-version check. These are synthetic-weight correctness tests, not trained-model accuracy or acceptance-rate measurements. GPU unit tests bypass controller background threads; serving exercises the actual scheduler/controller. NPU state copying was checked with CPU tensors, not NPU hardware. External L3 storage was not exercised.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput benchmark or performance claim. Host allocations account for packed drafts and the SWA sidecar, including fixed-budget coverage.

## Checklist

- [x] Run formatting and pre-commit checks on changed files.
- [x] Add and run registered CPU and GPU regression tests.
- [x] Run Inkling MTP + HiCache serving through device eviction and host restoration.
- [x] Explain behavior and validation limits.

Developed with AI assistance.

title: [Cleanup] Deduplicate kernel tests, diffusion fixtures and benchmark helpers
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Kernel and diffusion tests repeat input/reference code, fixture setup and whole test bodies. Some benchmarks also carry copied or unused helpers and stale import paths. This cleanup removes 1,426 net lines across 26 files while retaining the numerical checks, backend-specific dispatch, input matrices and CI registrations.

## Modifications

- Share paged-MQA fixtures, PyTorch reference and comparison logic between CuTe DSL and DeepGEMM tests; retain both complete backend matrices. Share the original AWQ input packer between dense and MoE repack tests.
- Parameterize metadata-copy small/large batches into one body per backend. Keep all 40 numerical cases and both dtype rejection tests. Delete unreachable reference branches and single-shot performance-print scaffolding from correctness tests.
- Consolidate diffusion gate/capture/fallback cases, FP32 LayerNorm cache checks and VAE defaults. Fold upsampler call counts into numerical tests and replace the copied full-model reference with an unfused GroupNorm + activation override; keep the independent ResBlock oracle and original CPU/GPU case boundaries. Reuse the existing parent server-args fixture in three SANA-WM suites.
- Share DeepSeek-V3 benchmark shape tables and FP8 input preparation; fix grouped-GEMM helper imports and use DeepGEMM's current testing-module import for `calc_diff`. Preserve the original unrounded FP32 scales rather than substituting the production UE8M0 quantizer.
- Delete the copied DeepEP benchmark utility file and reuse existing test helpers; keep its CLI-specific distributed initializer unchanged. Remove unused FA4 backward/profiling helpers, an uncalled vLLM GEMM wrapper/import and three uncalled MMMU data helpers.

## Accuracy Tests

Rebased onto main `d507accadc` and validated on GB300 (SM103), PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130:

| Existing tests | Result |
| --- | --- |
| CuTe DSL + DeepGEMM paged MQA, full matrices | 384 passed |
| Diffusion fusion, norm/cache, fallback and VAE loader | 69 passed, 8 subtests passed |
| Residual gate | 35 passed |
| Metadata copy + AWQ repack | 58 passed, 30 skipped |
| SANA-WM streaming/realtime suites | 23 passed |

Total: **569 passed, 30 skipped, 8 subtests passed**. The 30 skips are JIT-vs-AOT comparisons because this environment does not expose the old AOT repack operators; the independent JIT numerical checks ran. Metadata/AWQ and SANA-WM results match the before-cleanup run on the same base. Original first-pass diffusion cases also passed before consolidation. No numerical tolerance was relaxed.

Additional validation:

- 88 old/new FP8 payload-and-scale comparisons (CPU/CUDA, BF16/FP32, zero and padded inputs), 24 exact AWQ packer comparisons and all four original shape tables at TP 1/2/4/8/16 match.
- The generated metadata-copy parameter matrix is identical; all 11 CI registration calls are unchanged. Retained MMMU functions are AST-identical, with four prompt-construction smoke checks.
- All four affected DeepSeek/block-wise benchmark CLIs pass `--help` import smoke checks. Shared MQA and moved/reused DeepEP helpers retain their original implementations. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No inference behavior changes or inference speedup claim. The only runtime-file edit is a formatting-only change in `logits_processor.py` required by the repository-wide Ruff check (AST unchanged). DeepEP helpers pass 18 exact tensor/scalar comparisons and CUDA-event timer smoke checks; the retained FA4 forward timer passes with AMP off/on. Benchmark providers and timed callbacks are unchanged. Full multi-node DeepEP and GEMM tuning sweeps were not run.

title: [sgl-router] refactor - move policy-required states under src/state
author: sherlockwu
body:
Move the routing state required by policies to make routing decisions into src/state/. This includes load monitoring, KV events, and affinity stores such as session state.

Stack: main → #40272 (shared state) → #40241 (bucket routing and power-of-two) → #40379 (session-aware) → #40366 (cache-aware) → #40271 (admission) → #40292 (SLO ordering).

## Changes

- Move the KV-event index to `state::kv_events` and load monitoring to `state::load_monitor`.
- Distinguish engine-published measurements (`engine_reported_load`) from router-local request accounting (`router_inflight_load`).
- Extract worker-ID bindings, idle expiry, and concurrent binding updates into `AffinityStore`. Sticky routing reuses eligible bindings during concurrent first touches; session-aware routing retains its final-selection commit behavior.
- Sticky routing now identifies workers by discovery `WorkerId` instead of URL. Static discovery uses the URL as the ID, so nothing changes there; on Kubernetes the ID is the pod UID, so a replaced pod at the same address is remapped instead of reused, since the new pod has no warm cache.

## Validation after rebase

Rebased the stack onto `main` (`95521da18d`) after #39867 merged. All 31 commit patches and each PR's router tree are unchanged. Formatting and diff checks pass after this rebase. title: [HiCache] TMA-staged host<->device KV transfer kernel (sm_90+)
author: cctry
body:
**Before -> after** (HiCache host<->device KV transfer through the pool API, 8 layers x 32K tokens, GB300): H2D 97 -> 192 GB/s, D2H 93 -> 183 GB/s, about 2x, at the host link's copy-engine ceiling, using 4 of 152 SMs.

## Motivation

HiCache brings cached prefixes back from the pinned host pool into the device pool layer by layer, on a side stream, while the forward pass runs on the same GPU. Two properties of the transfer kernel therefore matter: how fast it moves a page, because the load gates the prefix hit, and how many SMs it takes from the forward pass to do so.

The register-staging JIT kernel in `hicache.cuh` is bounded by bytes in flight, not by the link. Each of its 1024 threads holds one 64 B slice of a row in registers between its load and its store, so a CTA has at most 64 KB outstanding at any time. With

```
bandwidth = bytes in flight / round trip
```

the measured ~48 GB/s per CTA on a GB300 (NVLink-C2C host link) corresponds to an effective host round trip of ~1.3 us. The copy-engine ceiling of the same link is ~210 GB/s H2D and ~192 GB/s D2H, so the default 2-block launch reaches ~90 GB/s, and saturating the link takes 6+ blocks of 1024 threads, every one of them issuing dependent loads for the whole transfer. Making the register pipeline deeper does not help: two rows in flight per thread measured 40 GB/s instead of 48, because at 1024 threads the extra registers cost more occupancy than the extra outstanding bytes buy.

TMA bulk copies remove that trade-off. One thread issues a 32 KB `cp.async.bulk` and the data lands in shared memory with no registers involved, so a single warp keeps a 192 KB ring in flight: three times the register kernel's outstanding bytes with nine warps per CTA instead of 32. Two hardware limits, measured with raw probe kernels on the same GPU, then set what any staged copy can reach:

| 1 SM probe | GB/s |
|---|---|
| stores to device memory (16 B vector stores or TMA bulk stores, 1 to 32 warps) | 66 |
| stores to pinned host memory | 53 |
| TMA bulk loads from host, 32 KB ops | 150-200 |
| TMA bulk loads, 512 B ops (one op per row) | 21 |

The SM write port (32 B/clk) caps one CTA around 66 GB/s in either design (Nsight Compute reports the L1-to-crossbar write peak as 4.86 KB/cycle for the whole GPU, i.e. 152 SMs x 32 B/clk, and a one-block store probe hits exactly that), and the TMA unit handles roughly one bulk op per ~50 cycles, which makes per-row bulk copies a trap. So no single-SM copy can reach the link. The design goal is therefore: run each CTA at its write port instead of at its load latency, and launch four of them by default so the host link is saturated with 4 of 152 SMs, where the register kernel needs 6+.

## Modifications

New JIT kernel `hicache_tma.cuh`, routed from the existing `transfer_hicache_*` entry points.

```
CTA = 1 loader warp + 8 store warps, smem ring of 6 x 32 KB stages
chunk = (K|V, layer, 2^k consecutive index positions)   # never straddles a page

loader warp, per chunk:
  prefetch next chunk's src/dst indices          # overlaps the ring wait
  if src rows are one run:
      contiguous (stride == row bytes) -> 1 x cp.async.bulk of the whole span
      strided (page-first host view)    -> 1 x cp.async.bulk.tensor 2D box
  else                                  -> 1 bulk op per row (lanes issue in parallel)
  stash dst indices in smem, arm mbarrier(expect_tx)

store warps, per chunk:
  wait mbarrier(full)
  if dst rows are one contiguous run: warp 0 bulk-stores half (2 groups in flight),
                                      warps 1..7 vector-store the other half
  else:                               vector stores with per-row addressing
  release stage (mbarrier empty, count = store warps)
```

1. **Deep loads without registers.** The loader keeps the whole ring in flight with `cp.async.bulk`; completion is counted on per-stage mbarriers, so no thread holds data.
2. **One op per run.** Contiguous page runs are one 1D bulk copy. A page run in a page-first host view (rows strided by `layers * row_bytes`) is one 2D tensor-map box (rows mapped as 8-byte elements, box `[rows_per_chunk][row_bytes/8]`), encoded per call with `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` via the driver entry point (no `-lcuda`). Per-row ops remain only for scattered tokens.
3. **Index prefetch.** Loading the next chunk's indices before blocking on the ring removed a ~0.5 us dependent-load bubble per chunk (3x on the loader loop).
4. **Store side at the port.** Bulk stores and vector stores split contiguous spans so the TMA engine's request generation and the LSU share the write port; destination indices come from smem and the unit-to-row division is a magic multiply, keeping the store loop branch-free.
5. **Runtime row size.** One compiled module serves every KV shape (multiple of 16 B), including rows the register kernel rejects (e.g. 1152 B MLA rows).
6. **Default on sm_90+, 4 CTAs.** `SGLANG_HICACHE_TMA_TRANSFER` (default on) selects the kernel when the GPU is sm_90+ and its opt-in shared memory holds the ~200 KB ring (`fits_device`; consumer Blackwell parts such as the RTX 5090 allow 99 KB and keep the register kernel), the row size is a multiple of 16 B, and `page_size % rows_per_chunk == 0` (pools now pass their page size); otherwise the register kernel is used. The TMA kernel launches `TMA_BLOCK_QUOTA = 4` CTAs, the register kernel keeps its 2-block default. ROCm and pre-Hopper are unaffected; `SGLANG_HICACHE_TMA_TRANSFER=0` restores the register kernel everywhere.

Invariants: correctness never depends on the run detection (it only picks the op shape); every stage is reused only after its readers release it through the `empty` mbarrier; bulk stores are waited with `cp.async.bulk.wait_group 0` before the grid completes.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hicache_tma.py`: H2D then D2H round trips through layer-first and page-first host views, int32 and int64 indices, whole pages and fully scattered rows, a partial tail chunk, untouched rows verified unchanged; all-layer pointer-table D2H into a page-first host; MLA single-buffer one-layer and all-layer. 10 cases pass (GB300).
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hicache.py` and `test_hicache_page_first_write_back.py` pass through the pool API with the new default (59, TMA at 4 CTAs) and with `SGLANG_HICACHE_TMA_TRANSFER=0` (47).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Before** = the register kernel at its 2-CTA default, which is what `--hicache-io-backend kernel` runs today. **After** = this PR's default, the TMA kernel at 4 CTAs. Both measured through the host-pool API (`MHATokenToKVPoolHost.load_to_device_per_layer` / `backup_from_device_all_layer`), 8 layers, 512 B bf16 rows (4 KV heads x 64), 128-token pages, GB300, process and pinned memory on the GPU's NUMA node.

H2D, one layer at a time from a page-first host pool (the prefix-load path):

| tokens per layer | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2048 | 73 GB/s (229 us) | 108 GB/s (155 us) | 1.5x |
| 8192 | 89 GB/s (751 us) | 168 GB/s (399 us) | 1.9x |
| 32768 | 97 GB/s (2779 us) | 192 GB/s (1398 us) | 2.0x |

D2H, all layers in one call into a layer-first host pool (the write-back path):

| tokens per layer | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2048 | 87 GB/s (192 us) | 164 GB/s (103 us) | 1.9x |
| 8192 | 92 GB/s (733 us) | 179 GB/s (375 us) | 1.9x |
| 32768 | 93 GB/s (2889 us) | 183 GB/s (1466 us) | 2.0x |

The copy-engine ceilings of the link measured with `cudaMemcpyAsync` are ~210 GB/s H2D and ~192 GB/s D2H, so "after" is at the link for large transfers. The gain comes from two things, separable in the kernel-level numbers below (one call, 512 B rows, 32K tokens, TMA / register at equal block counts): per block both kernels are near the SM write port, and the TMA kernel keeps scaling to the link at 4 blocks where the register kernel needs 6+.

| blocks | H2D page-first host | D2H layer-first host |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 52 / 48 GB/s | 46 / 45 GB/s |
| 2 | 101 / 97 GB/s | 90 / 87 GB/s |
| 4 | 190 / 175 GB/s | 175 / 164 GB/s |

Two measurement notes for anyone reproducing: pinned host memory on the remote NUMA node caps both kernels around 110-120 GB/s regardless of block count, and scattered single-token indices (`page_size=1`) still favor the register kernel for small rows, which is why the gate keeps it for pages that do not tile a chunk. `bench_hicache.py` gained a `tma` provider line, and its `jit` line now calls the register kernel directly so the two stay comparable.

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Test] Fix fusion-group mocks after runtime context migration
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

After #40068 migrated FlashInfer communication-group reads to the runtime context, `TestResolveFusionGroup` still patches `get_tp_group`, `get_moe_ep_group`, and `get_moe_tp_group` in `flashinfer_comm_fusion`. Those imports no longer exist, so all three group-resolution cases fail with `AttributeError` while entering the mock context. This also blocks the Base CPU suite ([failure log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35418955183/job/105832992563)).

## Modifications

## Accuracy Tests

title: Support GLM-5.3-Flash hybrid attention CPU offload and PD index mapping
author: zRzRzRzRzRzRzR
body:
## Motivation

Enabling CPU offload prevents GLM-5.3-Flash from starting in the tested TP8/EAGLE configuration. With the original offloader, `--cpu-offload-gb 0` starts and serves requests, while `--cpu-offload-gb 3` fails during CUDA graph initialization:

```text
ValueError: functional_call got multiple values for keys
['self_attn.A_log', 'self_attn.attn.A_log'], which are tied.
```

The same failure also occurs for the shared `dt_bias` parameter. The offloader copies aliases of a shared parameter to the GPU independently, producing distinct tensors that `functional_call` rejects. This change preserves the shared identity so the offload-enabled configuration can start and serve requests. It also keeps backing projection weights resident when attention modules cache derived MLA/KDA tensors.

PD with EAGLE introduces two related index-mapping requirements: KPool must preserve logical indices when metadata requests an unfused transform, and the prefill transform must accept widths such as 2051, arising from 2048 selected history positions plus up to three KPool tail positions.

## Modifications

- Build the offloaded device state with `state_dict(keep_vars=True)` and transfer each original tensor once, preserving shared parameter identity.
- Keep `kv_b_proj` parameters resident when the attention module caches `w_kc`/`w_vc`; keep `qkv_conv1d.weight` resident when cached convolution weights share its storage.
- Respect `force_unfused_topk` consistently across KPool fusion paths, preventing premature index mapping followed by a second transform.
- Replace the prefill transform's fixed 2048-column assertion with checks for a two-dimensional, nonempty top-k width. The decode transform is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

**Full-model offload control:** compare the current PR tree with a copy in which only `python/sglang/srt/utils/offloader.py` is restored to its upstream contents. All other source files, including the PD fixes, are identical. Both variants use the same model, dependencies, TP8/EP8, EAGLE settings, memory fraction, and random seed.

| Offloader implementation | `--cpu-offload-gb 0` | `--cpu-offload-gb 3` |
|---|---|---|
| Original offloader; only this file reverted | Starts; 3/3 requests pass | Fails during CUDA graph initialization with the tied-parameter errors above |
| This PR | Starts; 3/3 requests pass | Starts; 3/3 requests pass |

This isolates the observed startup failure to the offloader changes. The control is an isolated file rollback on the current PR tree, rather than a checkout of an older full repository revision.

All configurations used EAGLE 5/1/6, TileLang DSA prefill/decode, BF16 KV cache, DeepGEMM, and `SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK=1`. Requests covered arithmetic, long-context retrieval, and a repeated arithmetic request. The long request contained 8,228 tokens including the chat template and exercised 8192+36 chunked prefill. All successfully served requests returned HTTP 200, the expected final answer, and `finish_reason=stop`.

Final answers matched across the successful configurations. Intermediate wording varied in the long-context response, so these functional tests do not establish token-level equivalence or full-benchmark accuracy.

title: [Fix] Repair CI fixtures and ROCm speculative tree device checks
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Restore CI paths broken by recent main-branch interface migrations. Scheduler/MLX profiler fixtures still provide ranks through `ps`, the Q8KV8 prefill fixture lacks `swa_kv_pool`, and ROCm speculative tree launches are rejected by a CUDA-only tensor device check.

These failures are present on main `567d5925fe`, independently of #39957. The rank consumers changed in #40071, the KV-pool access changed in #38792, and the tree wrappers moved to JIT in #40033.

## Modifications

- Use scoped `get_parallel().override(...)` in the idle-counter and MLX profiler tests, including the PP size/depth configuration.
- Give the Q8KV8 test pool the `swa_kv_pool.page_size` interface used by the backend.
- Use the existing platform-dependent `kDLGPU` in all three speculative tree entry points. It resolves to CUDA for CUDA builds and ROCm for HIP builds, while retaining the same-device checks for the remaining tensors.

Four existing files changed; existing assertions and kernel computation are unchanged. No new test files or CI skips.

## Accuracy Tests

Compared unmodified main against the patch:

| Existing tests | Main | Patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_disagg_idle_step_counters.py` | Rank/group and PP fixture failures | 10 passed on Linux |
| `test_metal_profiler.py` | 1 failure out of 10: TP group not initialized | 10 passed on Apple Silicon, `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1`, PyTorch 2.13.0 / MLX 0.32.2 |
| `test_q8kv8_sparse_prefill_backend.py` | 3 failures: missing `swa_kv_pool` | 14 passed on H100 CI; 12 passed, 2 SM90-only tests skipped on GB300 |
| `test_build_eagle_tree.py`, `test_eagle_utils.py`, `test_ngram_utils.py` | — | 4 passed on both H100 CI and GB300 |

Pre-commit passed for all changed files. [Targeted H100 CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35435326799) passed all 18 tests on PR head `8985b2437bab2f119d53fa179d5fbef6469df3d5`, including the two SM90-only real-kernel cases. Native MI300/ROCm [Stage A](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35435306661/job/105876911749) passed, including `test_basic_sanity_eagle3.py`; the [JIT unit suite](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35435306661/job/105876911713) also passed. The [MLX CI suite](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35435306566/job/105876880179) passed, including all 10 profiler tests. All 10 Base A CPU partitions passed, with the idle-counter test confirmed in [partition 2](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35435306742/job/105877019022).

title: [unified-memory] Derive KV row addresses from strides, not shapes (1/7)
author: caihuali95
body:
> **This is one of seven PRs split out of #38592.** That PR was +2105/−1366 across 41
> files, twelve of them attention backends on the serving hot path, and it interleaved
> hardening, a layout change and dead-code deletion in a single diff — a reviewer could not
> tell which hunk was safe-by-construction and which changed behaviour. #38592 is retained as the token-major
> layout PR (3/7), which is the core of the series.
>
> **Stack** — each PR is based on the one above it, and every one is green on its own:
>
> | # | PR | what it does | size |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | 1 | #40326 | derive KV row addresses from strides, not shapes | 21 files, +733/−118 |
> | 2 | #40327 | build paged KV views through one helper | 13 files, +704/−47 |
> | 3 | #38592 | **token-major layout** | 36 files, +1215/−1108 |
> | 4 | #40328 | mark the write loc physical and check it at every write door | 45 files, +935/−132 |
> | 5 | #40329 | remove the kernel-page multiplier plumbing | 17 files, +117/−230 |
> | 6 | #40330 | stride the KV translate kernel and route every translate through it | 11 files, +361/−159 |
> | 7 | #40331 | name the fused KV translate for what it computes | 28 files, +119/−121 |
>
> Review order is the table order. 1 and 2 are no-ops on today's contiguous pools (2 also
> fixes how HND pools with more than one KV head are read); 3 is where the behaviour changes
> and deserves the most attention; 4 adds the physical write-loc check; 5 is deletion; 6
> consolidates the translate; 7 is naming only.

# 1/7 — derive KV row addresses from strides, not shapes

Base: `main`. 7 commits, 21 files, +733/−118.

## The problem

A per-layer K/V buffer is not always a contiguous `[slots, heads, head_dim]` tensor. The
unified memory pool hands out per-layer *views* into one page envelope, and such a view's
slot stride can exceed `heads * head_dim`.

Two things then go wrong, and **neither raises**:

- a consumer that computes a slot address from the tensor's **shape** addresses the wrong
  slot;
- a `.contiguous()` on such a view makes a private copy instead of aliasing the live pool,
  so writes land somewhere the kernels never read.

This PR fixes the sglang-side sites that did either. **On contiguous buffers every change
is a no-op**, so behaviour on today's pools is unchanged — which is why it ships first and
alone.

## What changes

Every sglang-side consumer that derived a KV row address from a tensor's **shape** now
derives it from the tensor's **stride**, and every gate that tested `is_contiguous()` as a
proxy for "addressable" now tests the property the kernel actually requires.

That covers three kinds of site: the pool's slot-stride table, which feeds the slot-move
engine; the write and fused-quantisation kernels, which step by a destination slot stride
instead of assuming a packed row; and the canary/debug sources, which alias the live layer
view rather than snapshotting a copy of it. The canary launch accepts such a view (it needs
packed rows, not a contiguous tensor), and checks a source's row *width*, not its stride,
against the bytes it is asked to hash — the bytes past a strided row's end belong to another
layer.

The tiled slot-move copy uses the slot stride as its copy width too, so it is only correct on
contiguous buffers. `_init_kv_copy_and_warmup` now asserts `is_contiguous()`: a strided pool
that turns the copy on fails at startup instead of spilling into the neighbouring slot. (The unified pool
builds its sub-pools with the copy off.)

The HiCache host pools (MHA and MLA) take the device row stride from the device buffers too,
instead of passing the row width as the device-side stride. A backup of strided rows goes
through the JIT all-layer kernel with that stride — for a `page_first` host as well, instead
of the staged write-back, which reads whole device pages — and the AOT transfer kernels,
which step device rows by the row width, refuse strided rows. The JIT per-layer load already
read the device tensor's stride. A pool whose device rows are packed records nothing and
behaves as before.

One stride helper is narrowed as part of this: it rebuilt every stride from the sizes, which
silently turned a strided view into a contiguous description of itself.

Four CUDA `.cuh` kernels gain a stride parameter. That is the one part of this PR whose blast
radius is not confined to Python, and it is the reason this lands first and by itself.

## Why this is worth its own PR

It is pure hardening: it fixes a class of bug (address derived from shape, not stride)
that is *latent today* and becomes reachable the moment a pool hands out strided views —
which is exactly what 3/7 does. Landing it separately means the layout change that makes
these paths live does not also have to carry their fixes.

## Tests

- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_kv_stride_hygiene.py` — CPU, pins each Python-side
  behaviour on a deliberately strided buffer, including the slot-move copy's contiguity
  check and the canary's row-width check.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/kv_canary/test_verify_hand.py`, `test_write_hand.py` — GPU,
  strided real-KV sources (the fixtures' `row_gap`) through the CUDA-vs-reference
  differential, so the kernels are shown to step rows by `stride(0)`.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_masked_set_kv_buffer_strided.py` — GPU, builds a
  buffer whose slot stride exceeds one K row via `as_strided` and asserts writes land at the
  slot stride. A hardcoded `loc * H * D` writes into the wrong slot **without any error**, so
  this test is the only thing that can catch a regression here.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_fused_fp8_qkv_kv_cache.py` — GPU, the strided
  fp8 path.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hicache_strided_device_rows.py` — GPU,
  round-trips strided device rows through the MHA host pool (`layer_first` and
  `page_first`) and compares them bit for bit; stepping device rows by the row width copies
  neighbouring bytes instead.

## Validation

Model families exercised — a hybrid of every pool shape the unified pool supports, plus a
non-hybrid control. Perf covers the gated-deltanet hybrid (Qwen3.5-9B), the MLA hybrid
(Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B), the sliding-window hybrid (gpt-oss-20b), the tri-pool hybrid
(Inkling and Inkling-Small), and dense Llama-3.1-8B as a control. Accuracy covers the same
set and additionally the Mamba hybrid, Falcon-H1-7B. Each model is run unified against a
baseline on the same model, backend and configuration, so every delta isolates the pool.

Median inter-token latency, unified vs baseline: **+0.79%** (measured run-to-run noise floor
for this metric: 1.9%). Median GSM8K delta at n=200: **+0.25 pt** (binomial delta-sigma ≈ 3.0 pt).

Re-validated on the previous base (0318a8d0af) after review feedback: the stack tip (7/7) gives **+0.95%** median inter-token latency over 40 paired configurations (median per-configuration shift against the previous run of the same 40: +0.12 pp) and **−0.25 pt** median GSM8K over 26, with the full unit scope green.

title: [unified-memory] Build paged KV views through one helper (2/7)
author: caihuali95
body:
> **This is one of seven PRs split out of #38592.** That PR was +2105/−1366 across 41
> files, twelve of them attention backends on the serving hot path, and it interleaved
> hardening, a layout change and dead-code deletion in a single diff — a reviewer could not
> tell which hunk was safe-by-construction and which changed behaviour. #38592 is retained as the token-major
> layout PR (3/7), which is the core of the series.
>
> **Stack** — each PR is based on the one above it, and every one is green on its own:
>
> | # | PR | what it does | size |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | 1 | #40326 | derive KV row addresses from strides, not shapes | 21 files, +733/−118 |
> | 2 | #40327 | build paged KV views through one helper | 13 files, +704/−47 |
> | 3 | #38592 | **token-major layout** | 36 files, +1215/−1108 |
> | 4 | #40328 | mark the write loc physical and check it at every write door | 45 files, +935/−132 |
> | 5 | #40329 | remove the kernel-page multiplier plumbing | 17 files, +117/−230 |
> | 6 | #40330 | stride the KV translate kernel and route every translate through it | 11 files, +361/−159 |
> | 7 | #40331 | name the fused KV translate for what it computes | 28 files, +119/−121 |
>
> Review order is the table order. 1 and 2 are no-ops on today's contiguous pools (2 also
> fixes how HND pools with more than one KV head are read); 3 is where the behaviour changes
> and deserves the most attention; 4 adds the physical write-loc check; 5 is deletion; 6
> consolidates the translate; 7 is naming only.

# 2/7 — build paged KV views through one helper

Base: #40326 (1/7). 6 commits, 13 files, +704/−47.

## The problem

Attention backends turn a per-layer `[slots, heads, head_dim]` buffer into the
`[num_pages, page_size, heads, head_dim]` form their paged kernels take with ad-hoc
`.view(-1, page_size, H, D)` calls. Splitting dim 0 keeps the slot stride as dim 1's
stride — **except at `page_size == 1`**, where `.view()` gives the size-1 dim the *row*
stride, which differs from the slot stride as soon as the per-layer buffer is strided.

Each site also re-derives the shape from the layer's config, and nothing states the stride
contract.

## What changes

Three helpers in a new `mem_cache/layout/paged_view.py`, and every pool-buffer page split in
the paged backends routed through them.

### Which helper to use

This is the rule a new backend should follow; it is the whole API surface:

| you hold | the kernel wants | use |
|---|---|---|
| a **raw MHA pool buffer** from `get_kv_buffer` — rank you do not control (3-D slot-major under NHD, 4-D already-paged under HND) | `[pages, ps, H, D]` | **`paged_kv_view(buf, ps, H, D)`** |
| a tensor **already shaped** the way the kernel wants its rows | same rows, pages split | **`paged_view(t, ps)`** |
| the same, but the kernel wants each row **flat** | `[pages, ps, row_elems]` | **`paged_row_view(t, ps)`** |

In one line: **`paged_kv_view` when the pool hands you the buffer; `paged_view` when you
have already shaped the rows; `paged_row_view` when the kernel takes a flat row.**

`paged_view` is the primitive — it builds the paged view from the buffer's own strides, so
dim 1 carries the slot stride at every page size. The other two differ only in how they
prepare rows before calling it: `paged_row_view` *is* `paged_view(flat.view(slots, -1), ps)`,
and `paged_kv_view` is `paged_view` with a row reshape to `[H, D]`, plus the HND case,
where it only swaps the head and token dims of the already-paged buffer. Only `paged_kv_view` knows about HND, because it is the only one receiving a buffer
whose rank it did not choose.

fa3 shows the contrast within 400 lines: the paged MHA cache calls `paged_kv_view` on the
raw buffer, while the cascade path does `.view(-1, H, D)` itself and then calls
`paged_view`, because it has already shaped its rows and only needs page-size-one blocks.

### Sites routed

Every pool-buffer page split in the paged backends now goes through one of the three
helpers — the MHA caches and the fused rope store through `paged_kv_view`, the MLA latent
and rope caches through `paged_view`, and the MLA backends whose kernels take a flat row
through `paged_row_view`. Each site keeps the page size it used before, including the case
where a draft worker's pool pages at a multiple of the backend's own.

Two shapes are deliberately left alone: a regrouping path that needs a contiguous page block
and raises rather than mis-addresses, and row views built inside stride-aware kernel wrappers
on their own arguments.

## Behaviour

On pools without strided views every site produces the same tensor as before — shape,
strides and storage offset — for NHD, fp8, nvfp4 and MLA buffers at any page size, and for
HND buffers with one KV head.

HND buffers with more than one KV head (`SGLANG_USE_HND_KVCACHE`) change, from wrong to
right. The old `.view(-1, ps, H, D)` only relabelled a `[pages, H, ps, D]` buffer's bytes,
swapping heads with in-page tokens, while `set_kv_buffer` writes true HND. `paged_kv_view`
now returns `buf.permute(0, 2, 1, 3)`, so fa3 reads the tokens that were written, and
trtllm_mha's own permute hands its kernel the HND buffer itself. The HND pools in use today
fold heads into pages and have one KV head, where both forms agree.

The one exception: fa3's absorbed-MLA views, whose size-1 dims (the single KV head, and the
page dim at `page_size 1`) now record a different stride. An index into a size-1 dim is
always 0, so this cannot change addressing; it is visible only to a kernel that reads that
stride.

## Tests

- `test_trtllm_mha_paged_kv.py` — pins the row-then-page order on strided packed and flat
  rows (at `page_size == 1` the `.view()` form gives the size-1 page dim the row stride), and
  that an HND buffer reaches the kernel head for head and token for token.
- `test_flashattention_paged_mha.py` — pins the paged MHA cache's page size, the HND
  head/token mapping, and the `head_group_num` refusal on a strided view.
- `test_paged_view.py` — pins the helpers' strides, including `page_size == 1`, and
  `paged_kv_view`'s HND mapping.
- `test/registered/attention/test_trtllm_mha_stride_parity.py`, `test_trtllm_mla_stride_parity.py`
  — SM100, registered on `4-gpu-b200`. Identical page contents go through a contiguous cache
  and through an over-strided view (slot stride widened to a whole entry), and the outputs
  must be bit-identical (`torch.equal`): trtllm-gen MHA decode and context with bf16 and fp8
  KV, and MLA decode through `paged_row_view` on trtllm_mla, cutedsl_mla and tokenspeed_mla.
  All pass on B200.

## Validation

Model families exercised — a hybrid of every pool shape the unified pool supports, plus a
non-hybrid control. Perf covers the gated-deltanet hybrid (Qwen3.5-9B), the MLA hybrid
(Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B), the sliding-window hybrid (gpt-oss-20b), the tri-pool hybrid
(Inkling and Inkling-Small), and dense Llama-3.1-8B as a control. Accuracy covers the same
set and additionally the Mamba hybrid, Falcon-H1-7B. Each model is run unified against a
baseline on the same model, backend and configuration, so every delta isolates the pool.

Median inter-token latency, unified vs baseline: **+0.87%** (measured run-to-run noise floor
for this metric: 1.9%). Median GSM8K delta at n=200: **+0.50 pt** (binomial delta-sigma ≈ 3.0 pt).

Re-validated on the previous base (0318a8d0af) after review feedback: the stack tip (7/7) gives **+0.95%** median inter-token latency over 40 paired configurations (median per-configuration shift against the previous run of the same 40: +0.12 pp) and **−0.25 pt** median GSM8K over 26, with the full unit scope green.

## End to end

These paths first see strided views in 3/7; #38592 lists the end-to-end runs of each
admitted SM100 backend under `--enable-unified-memory`, on top of the parity tests above.

# 4/7 — mark the write loc physical, and check the mark at every write door

Base: #38592 (3/7). 9 commits, 45 files, +935/−132.

## Why

A unified pool's write door needs physical token ids. The allocator hands out virtual ids,
and `KVIndexTranslator.rebind_write_loc` translates the batch's write loc at `ForwardBatch`
construction; every other pool allocates physically, so the two coincide. Under 3/7's
token-major views a virtual id is in range and, by value, the same kind of integer as a
physical one, so a loc that skipped the rebind writes to the wrong slots without any error.
3/7 deletes the only probe that could tell them apart, because the new layout makes it
vacuous. This PR replaces it with an explicit mark, checked at every write door.

## The contract

| piece | role |
|---|---|
| `ForwardBatch.out_cache_loc_is_physical` | the batch's write loc holds physical ids. `rebind_write_loc` sets it on every pool, translating or not; the capture-time and draft-runner constructors that build a batch outside `init_new` set it themselves |
| `KVWriteLoc.physical` | carries the mark to the pool; `False` unless stated |
| `KVWriteLoc.for_batch(forward_batch, *, swa_loc, full_loc)` | the batch's `out_cache_loc` with the batch's mark. It wraps nothing else, because the mark describes that tensor only |
| `KVWriteLoc.for_layer(forward_batch, layer, …)` | the same, except that a cross-attention layer gets `encoder_out_cache_loc`, which nothing translates and so is never marked |
| `KVCache.requires_physical_write_loc` | set by the unified pools. Their write doors raise `ValueError` on a loc not marked physical. The check is a flag read with no device sync, so it runs on every write-door call. Fused writers that scatter through `get_kv_buffer`, and a replayed cuda graph, do not pass through a door |

A loc produced separately states its own mark with `KVWriteLoc(loc, physical=…)`:
trtllm_mla's capture-stable decode buffer (the runner translates into it), triton's
rank-local DCP slot of a physical loc, and the dspark / dflash draft writes (draft pools are
always static). `HybridLinearKVPool` and the SWA composites forward the `KVWriteLoc` to their
sub-pools instead of unwrapping it, so the mark reaches the door that checks it.

## Completeness is enforced

`test_physical_write_loc.py` parses every file that can hand a write loc to a pool under
`--enable-unified-memory` — the attention backends on the unified allowlists (tied to
`kv_cache_hook`'s allowed sets, so a newly admitted backend joins the scan) plus `models/`,
`layers/cp/`, `speculative/`, `model_executor/` and `disaggregation/` — and requires the loc
argument of every write-door call to be `KVWriteLoc.for_batch` / `for_layer` or a
`KVWriteLoc(...)` with an explicit `physical=`. It follows local names, parameters and helper
returns, and a self-test shows it flags a bare tensor and an unmarked `KVWriteLoc`. The
adoption covers 44 write-door calls, including fa3's two MLA writes, triton's DCP writes and
the draft-model writes.

The pool side is enforced the same way. Producers now hand a `KVWriteLoc` to every pool,
static ones included, so the same file also requires every `set_kv_buffer` /
`set_mla_kv_buffer` override under `srt/` to unwrap its loc argument, forward it untouched to
another door, take only `*args`, or only raise. It covers 30 doors.

## When a new backend must wrap

If the backend can receive a unified pool, its write doors pass
`KVWriteLoc.for_batch(forward_batch, …)`, or `for_layer` when it serves cross-attention. If
it translates the ids itself, it passes `KVWriteLoc(loc, physical=True)`. The ratchet above
fails otherwise.

## Static-pool paths the new loc type reaches

Wrapping the loc changes what static pools and backends receive, not just unified ones:

- triton with `--dcp-size > 1` compares `positions.numel()` with the rank-local loc's length;
  it now reads the wrapped tensor (`loc.loc.numel()`). `test_dcp_layout_unit.py` drives the
  DCP write with a stub pool.
- `MLATokenToKVPoolFP4.set_mla_kv_buffer`, `HiSparseDSATokenToKVPool`'s two doors,
  `LayerSplitDSATokenToKVPool.set_mla_kv_buffer` and
  `PageInterleaveMLATokenToKVPool.set_mla_kv_buffer` take `loc_info` and unwrap it, like
  their siblings.
- Hand-built batch stubs that drive a write path carry `out_cache_loc_is_physical`
  (`test_cp_strategy_unit.py`, `test_fused_fp8_kv_write.py`).

On the H200, before the stack was rebased onto current main, each against the base it then had
(0318a8d0af) (GSM8K 5-shot, n=200):

| model | configuration | base | without these fixes | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B | tp2, dcp2, triton | 0.855 | `AttributeError` at the first KV write | 0.835 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `fp4_mx_block16` KV cache, flashinfer, `--max-total-tokens 262144` | 0.175 | `AttributeError` in graph capture | 0.180 |

DeepSeek-V2-Lite is a base model: with a bf16 KV cache on the same setup it scores
0.325, so the FP4 rows are to be read against each other. The token cap keeps
flashinfer's FP4 decode, which dequantizes the whole pool, inside memory at both commits.

## Validation

Model families exercised — a hybrid of every pool shape the unified pool supports, plus a
non-hybrid control. Perf covers the gated-deltanet hybrid (Qwen3.5-9B), the MLA hybrid
(Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B), the sliding-window hybrid (gpt-oss-20b), the tri-pool hybrid
(Inkling and Inkling-Small), and dense Llama-3.1-8B as a control. Accuracy covers the same
set and additionally the Mamba hybrid, Falcon-H1-7B. Each model is run unified against a
baseline on the same model, backend and configuration, so every delta isolates the pool.

Median inter-token latency, unified vs baseline: **+1.03%** (measured run-to-run noise floor
for this metric: 1.9%). Median GSM8K delta at n=200: **+0.50 pt** (binomial delta-sigma ≈ 3.0 pt).

Re-validated on the previous base (0318a8d0af) after review feedback: the stack tip (7/7) gives **+0.95%** median inter-token latency over 40 paired configurations (median per-configuration shift against the previous run of the same 40: +0.12 pp) and **−0.25 pt** median GSM8K over 26, with the full unit scope green.

Against the preceding PR's run on the same matrix the median per-model shift is −0.11 pp —
this PR moves nothing.

## End to end with the always-on check

Each run below boots with `--enable-unified-memory` and writes through the checked doors;
none refuses a write (GSM8K 5-shot, n=100). The unified-vs-baseline comparison for these
backends is in #38592.

| box | model | backend | GSM8K |
|---|---|---|---|
| H200 | Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, tp2 | fa3 | 0.890 |
| B200 | Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, tp2 | trtllm_mla | 0.900 |
| B200 | Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, tp2 | cutedsl_mla | 0.890 |
| B200 | Qwen3.5-9B, tp1, cuda graphs off | trtllm_mha | 0.900 |

aiter's write doors are marked, but aiter is not admitted under `--enable-unified-memory`, so
the ratchet does not scan it, and its doors have not been run on ROCm.

title: [unified-memory] Remove the kernel-page multiplier plumbing (5/7)
author: caihuali95
body:
> **This is one of seven PRs split out of #38592.** That PR was +2105/−1366 across 41
> files, twelve of them attention backends on the serving hot path, and it interleaved
> hardening, a layout change and dead-code deletion in a single diff — a reviewer could not
> tell which hunk was safe-by-construction and which changed behaviour. #38592 is retained as the token-major
> layout PR (3/7), which is the core of the series.
>
> **Stack** — each PR is based on the one above it, and every one is green on its own:
>
> | # | PR | what it does | size |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | 1 | #40326 | derive KV row addresses from strides, not shapes | 21 files, +733/−118 |
> | 2 | #40327 | build paged KV views through one helper | 13 files, +704/−47 |
> | 3 | #38592 | **token-major layout** | 36 files, +1215/−1108 |
> | 4 | #40328 | mark the write loc physical and check it at every write door | 45 files, +935/−132 |
> | 5 | #40329 | remove the kernel-page multiplier plumbing | 17 files, +117/−230 |
> | 6 | #40330 | stride the KV translate kernel and route every translate through it | 11 files, +361/−159 |
> | 7 | #40331 | name the fused KV translate for what it computes | 28 files, +119/−121 |
>
> Review order is the table order. 1 and 2 are no-ops on today's contiguous pools (2 also
> fixes how HND pools with more than one KV head are read); 3 is where the behaviour changes
> and deserves the most attention; 4 adds the physical write-loc check; 5 is deletion; 6
> consolidates the translate; 7 is naming only.

# 5/7 — remove the kernel-page multiplier plumbing

Base: #40328 (4/7). 5 commits, 17 files, **+117/−230**.

## What and why

3/7 pinned `kernel_page_multiplier` to 1: under the token-major entry a kernel-facing id
*is* the physical token id, so there is no per-page block scale left for an id to carry.
This PR deletes the plumbing that existed only to carry it.

Pure deletion. **Nothing left behind computes differently** — every site either multiplied
by a value that is now always 1, or passed it along.

What goes: the multiplier's keyword arguments and properties across the unified
allocators and the index translator, the `* mult` at every use site, the stride arguments
that existed only to re-derive the scaled id, and the corresponding parameters in the
kernels that took them. The read-table build loses its scaling step and reduces to a
clamped table lookup. The aiter MLA backend's DCP verify path passed the multiplier to
`create_mla_kv_page_table_for_dcp` too; it now passes the same arguments as trtllm_mla's.
The write-loc translate kernel's `stride` argument goes as well: its one caller passed the
page size, so the kernel computes `phys * page_size + offset` itself. The translator's module
doc now describes two id spaces, virtual and physical.

Both translate implementations are **left untouched** here. With the multiplier gone,
`translate_kv_loc` and `translate_kv_loc_for_kernel` compute the same id for any in-range
non-negative input, differing only in implementation (several torch ops vs one Triton
launch) and in how they treat a negative loc. Folding them is **6/7** — kept separate so
this PR carries no behaviour change at all.

## Why it is not merged into 3/7

They are different kinds of change, and the split is deliberate:

- 3/7 is the feature, and its middle commit is where a reviewer must think hard. Seventeen
  files of deletion would dilute exactly the focus the split was made to create.
- They are **independently revertible**. If this removal turns out to break a consumer we did
  not find, reverting it alone leaves the layout intact — and the layout is what 4/7, 6/7,
  7/7 and downstream work all stand on. Merged, that revert would take the layout with it.

## Review shape

Net −113 lines across 17 files, eight of them tests whose edits follow the removal; test
cases that only exercised a multiplier above 1 are converted to the page-size form or
dropped, and the two single-full-attention-layer tests (the multiplier-1 case), which the
removal turned into duplicates, are folded into the general ones. Checking this PR is
mostly confirming that every deleted argument was provably 1.

## Validation

Model families exercised — a hybrid of every pool shape the unified pool supports, plus a
non-hybrid control. Perf covers the gated-deltanet hybrid (Qwen3.5-9B), the MLA hybrid
(Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B), the sliding-window hybrid (gpt-oss-20b), the tri-pool hybrid
(Inkling and Inkling-Small), and dense Llama-3.1-8B as a control. Accuracy covers the same
set and additionally the Mamba hybrid, Falcon-H1-7B. Each model is run unified against a
baseline on the same model, backend and configuration, so every delta isolates the pool.

Median inter-token latency, unified vs baseline: **+1.30%** (measured run-to-run noise floor
for this metric: 1.9%). Median GSM8K delta at n=200: **+0.00 pt** (binomial delta-sigma ≈ 3.0 pt).

Re-validated on the previous base (0318a8d0af) after review feedback: the stack tip (7/7) gives **+0.95%** median inter-token latency over 40 paired configurations (median per-configuration shift against the previous run of the same 40: +0.12 pp) and **−0.25 pt** median GSM8K over 26, with the full unit scope green.

The median per-model perf shift against the preceding PR's run is −0.09 pp.

## End to end

The admitted SM100 backends were run with unified memory at the stack tip; see #40331.

title: [unified-memory] Stride the KV translate kernel and route every translate through it (6/7)
author: caihuali95
body:
> **This is one of seven PRs split out of #38592.** That PR was +2105/−1366 across 41
> files, twelve of them attention backends on the serving hot path, and it interleaved
> hardening, a layout change and dead-code deletion in a single diff — a reviewer could not
> tell which hunk was safe-by-construction and which changed behaviour. #38592 is retained as the token-major
> layout PR (3/7), which is the core of the series.
>
> **Stack** — each PR is based on the one above it, and every one is green on its own:
>
> | # | PR | what it does | size |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | 1 | #40326 | derive KV row addresses from strides, not shapes | 21 files, +733/−118 |
> | 2 | #40327 | build paged KV views through one helper | 13 files, +704/−47 |
> | 3 | #38592 | **token-major layout** | 36 files, +1215/−1108 |
> | 4 | #40328 | mark the write loc physical and check it at every write door | 45 files, +935/−132 |
> | 5 | #40329 | remove the kernel-page multiplier plumbing | 17 files, +117/−230 |
> | 6 | #40330 | stride the KV translate kernel and route every translate through it | 11 files, +361/−159 |
> | 7 | #40331 | name the fused KV translate for what it computes | 28 files, +119/−121 |
>
> Review order is the table order. 1 and 2 are no-ops on today's contiguous pools (2 also
> fixes how HND pools with more than one KV head are read); 3 is where the behaviour changes
> and deserves the most attention; 4 adds the physical write-loc check; 5 is deletion; 6
> consolidates the translate; 7 is naming only.

# 6/7 — stride the KV translate kernel and route every translate through it

Base: #40329 (5/7). 5 commits, 11 files, +361/−159.

## Why

`main` computes `v2p[t // ps] * ps + t % ps` in two places: the fused Triton kernel
(`_translate_loc_fused`, used by the read table, the SWA read and the write translate) and a
torch body (`translate_kv_loc`, used by the composites and the PD / HiCache transfer
translates). They disagree on the ids nobody looks at: the torch body faults on a negative or
past-the-table id and on 2-D input, while the kernel sends them to the page-0 sink. The
kernel could not take every caller, because it flat-addresses its input and so needs it
contiguous, while the SWA read path hands down `page_table[:bs, :max_seq_len]`, a column
slice of the capture-stable buffer.

## Commit 1 — walk the kernel by its strides

`loc` and `out` are walked as a `(rows, cols)` view with row and column strides passed per
launch. The decomposition sits behind a `STRIDED` constexpr, so a contiguous pair still takes
the flat path with no div/mod; that is what the per-forward write translate under cuda-graph
capture uses.

- **The strides are runtime arguments, not `tl.constexpr`.** A page table's live width
  changes every few decode steps, and a constexpr stride would recompile with it.
- **Offsets are computed in int64.** A row stride times a row count can exceed 2^31, and an
  int32 overflow here would mis-address silently.
- **`out_width` stays on the flat path, by assert.** That mode writes a packed lane range
  `[0, W)` with a zero tail; a non-contiguous 1-D `loc` would send the tail lanes over the
  live prefix, so the assert is load-bearing.
- The `out=None` allocation no longer mirrors a strided `loc`, so the caller gets a
  contiguous result.

## Commit 2 — one implementation

`translate_kv_loc` calls the fused kernel, and the torch body and `translate_kv_loc_for_kernel`
are deleted. For the callers that were on the torch path — the composites' `translate_kv_loc`,
the PD transfer translates, retraction's `get_cpu_copy` / `load_cpu_copy` and
`_materialize_inflight_write_set` (HiCache's transfer translate was already on the kernel) — a negative or past-the-table id now resolves to the
page-0 sink instead of faulting; 2-D, int32 and strided inputs are accepted; and each call is
one launch instead of up to six. Trading a fault for the sink is deliberate: these calls can
run inside a captured graph, where a device-side assert is not a diagnostic. Paths already on
the fused kernel — the read table, the SWA read, the pool's FULL→SWA — do not change, and
every id the torch body accepted translates to the same value.

## Tests

- `test_matches_reference_on_a_strided_view` and `test_translate_accepts_a_strided_page_table`
  fail on 5/7 (`loc must be contiguous`) and pass here.
- `test_a_loc_past_the_sentinel_lands_on_the_sink`, `test_an_out_of_range_loc_lands_on_the_sink`
  and `test_padding_loc_lands_on_the_sink` pin the sink semantics.
- `test_out_width_needs_a_packed_loc` pins the branch that would otherwise regress silently.
- `kernels/ops/memory/test_write_loc_to_kernel_ids_strided.py` (GPU) is the only test that
  enters the kernel, so it is the one that can catch a wrong `row * rs + col * cs`; its oracle
  is the kernel on a contiguous copy, plus the CPU reference. Its lanes cover non-zero
  in-page offsets, the `-1` sink, a tombstoned page, a loc below the sentinel and a page past
  the table, in int32 and int64. Dropping the past-the-table guard or the in-page offset from
  the kernel fails it.

## Validation

A GPU differential of `translate_kv_loc` against the closed-form definition matches in all 114
cases: int32 / int64; page sizes 1, 4, 64; 1-D, 2-D, stride-2, column-slice, transposed and
empty inputs; tombstoned pages; −1, −2, −(ps + 1) and past-the-table locs; `out=None`, packed,
column-slice (neighbours untouched) and in-place `out=`. The 5/7 implementation agrees on all 50
inputs it accepts. `UnifiedSWAKVPool.translate_loc_from_full_to_swa` is one CUDA launch at 5/7,
at this PR and at 7/7.

## Unit tests

At this head on the H200, the strided kernel test and `test_unified_mla_views.py` pass (24
tests), and the kernel test fails when the past-the-table guard or the in-page offset is
removed from the kernel. The stack tip (#40331) was run over the wider unit scope on the H200 and
end to end on B200; see its description.

## Follow-ups this PR does not do

- **Lift the fa3/fa4 local-attention refusal** under `--enable-unified-memory`. Commit 1 removes
  one technical reason for it, but validating the lift needs a local-attention model.
- **Fold the Mamba id translate.** `UnifiedMambaPool.translate` is still a plain torch gather; at
  page size 1 it computes the same value but does not clamp, so a tombstoned row returns `-1`
  rather than the sink.

author: caihuali95
body:

> files, twelve of them attention backends on the serving hot path, and it interleaved

>

> |---|---|---|---|
> | 1 | #40326 | derive KV row addresses from strides, not shapes | 21 files, +733/−118 |
> | 2 | #40327 | build paged KV views through one helper | 13 files, +704/−47 |
> | 3 | #38592 | **token-major layout** | 36 files, +1215/−1108 |
> | 4 | #40328 | mark the write loc physical and check it at every write door | 45 files, +935/−132 |
> | 5 | #40329 | remove the kernel-page multiplier plumbing | 17 files, +117/−230 |
> | 6 | #40330 | stride the KV translate kernel and route every translate through it | 11 files, +361/−159 |
> | 7 | #40331 | name the fused KV translate for what it computes | 28 files, +119/−121 |
