> fixes how HND pools with more than one KV head are read); 3 is where the behaviour changes
> and deserves the most attention; 4 adds the physical write-loc check; 5 is deletion; 6
> consolidates the translate; 7 is naming only.

# 7/7 — name the fused KV translate for what it computes

Base: #40330 (6/7). 5 commits, 28 files, +119/−121.

After 6/7 one kernel serves every KV translate, reads and writes alike, and the kernel-facing
and physical id spaces are the same. The names still said otherwise. This PR renames, with no
behaviour change:

| before | after |
|---|---|
| `write_loc_to_kernel_ids` / `write_loc_to_kernel_id_kernel` / `WRITE_LOC_BLOCK` | `translate_token_ids` / `translate_token_ids_kernel` / `TRANSLATE_TOKEN_IDS_BLOCK` |
| `translate_write_loc_for_kernel` (sub-allocator and composites) | `translate_write_loc` |
| `_assert_kernel_id_bound` | `_assert_physical_id_bound` |
| `test_write_loc_to_kernel_ids_strided.py` | `test_translate_token_ids_strided.py` |

The kernel registry entry, callers and tests follow. The kernel's argument comments now
describe its real inputs (1-D or strided `(rows, cols)`, int32 or int64, widened under DCP), an
unreachable 0-d branch goes, and the allocator docstrings say "physical" where they said
"kernel-facing".

Comments follow the identifiers: every comment, docstring and unified-memory error message
that called these ids "kernel-facing" now says "physical". Left alone are the sites that
state the equivalence on purpose, one that describes a historical bug, and two where the
word means something else (the Mamba checkpoint pool, the communicator). Three
descriptions that were wrong are corrected: the kernel's `out` under `out_width`, the
parity test's page-major formula, and the inkling test's account of a re-translated loc.

The first commit is a scripted mechanical rename; the next two are comments and the two
identifier renames; the last two are the corrections and the comment sweep, each
droppable on its own.

## Validation

The stack is rebased onto main 047be72a8c; every PR's own diff is unchanged file for file.

Unit and GPU tests on the H200, this head against that main, over every non-e2e test file the stack
touches plus `unit/mem_cache`, `cp`, `dcp`, `unit/layers/attention`, `kernels/ops/memory` and
`kernels/ops/kvcache`: no failure at this head that main does not also have; the extra passes are the
stack's own tests. The server-launching multi-GPU files under `cp/` and `dcp/` error the same way on
both sides on a one-GPU run.

End to end at this head on the H200, unified memory against a baseline on the same model and flags
(GSM8K 5-shot, n=200):

| model | backend | unified | baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B, tp1 | triton | 0.900 | 0.900 |
| gpt-oss-20b, tp1 | fa3 | 0.540 | 0.515 |

Before the rebase, at d509377055 — the whole stack — each admitted SM100 backend was run with
unified memory against a baseline on the same model, flags and box (B200, GSM8K 5-shot, n=100):

| model | backend | unified | baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B, tp1, cuda graphs off | trtllm_mha | 0.900 | 0.900 |
| gpt-oss-20b, tp1 | fa4 | 0.570 | 0.570 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, tp2 | trtllm_mla | 0.900 | 0.900 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, tp2, dcp2, fp8 KV | tokenspeed_mla | 0.930 | 0.930 |

No write was refused by the physical write-loc check and no device-side assert fired. trtllm_mha
without cuda graphs decodes about 7% slower under unified memory, from the translate launches
an eager step adds.

The commits added since that head fix static-pool write doors, tests and comments; none changes a
unified-memory read or write path.

title: Check the topology identities where the layout is written, and build at the published widths
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

`get_parallel().override(...)` validated key names and nothing else. A
self-contradicting topology -- a rank at or past its width, a `tp_size` that
does not factor into the attention widths, a group whose width is not the one
configured -- went in quietly and surfaced much later as a hang or a wrong
answer in a collective, with nothing pointing back at the write.

At the other end, `initialize_model_parallel` took seven widths as arguments,
so every caller translated the published configuration into them again: the
scheduler from a per-runner record, the weight-cache daemon from its own
fields, the media encoder from neither. Three translations of one configuration
are three places for it to come out different, and the encoder's did -- it
built a layout the context never described.

## Modifications

**One set of identities, checked wherever the layout is written.** Every rank
inside its width; `tp_size` factoring into the attention triple and into the
MoE triple; the attention rank layout the attention ranks are derived from; and
each built group's width equal to the configured one. They hold
unconditionally, on the four paths that write the namespace and at the group
build. The caller owns the arithmetic: stating one leaf without the quotients
that follow from it describes no real layout, so it is refused rather than
carried. Names that cannot be read are skipped -- a process that has published
nothing can still stamp a rank.

Two callers were stating a width the rest of the namespace disagreed with. The
shared-expert scope narrows `moe_ep_size` to one without sharding anything, so
it now says there is no expert-parallel group rather than leaving the wider one
installed. Publish stamped the placement in two calls, and the moment between
them described a half-placed process; it stamps once.

**The group build reads the widths it builds at.** The seven width parameters
are gone; the function reads them from the context. What is left in the
signature is not topology: the backend is decided by the device, two flags
belong to other namespaces, and the join parameters describe this particular
call. The encoder states the layout it has always built -- `tp_size` ranks
wide, no pipeline, no expert or MoE-DP dimension, no decode context parallelism
-- so what it answers and what it builds are the same thing again.

**An elastic scale-up and the launch topology stop sharing two names.** A
scale-up admits ranks into a WORLD that was pre-allocated to `--max-ep-size`;
it does not rebuild the process groups, which keep the width they were
constructed with. Writing the expanded replica count over `attn_dp_size` and
`attn_dp_rank` therefore left the launch names answering for groups of a
different size, and the identities say so: the rank lands outside its width and
`tp_size` stops factoring into the attention triple. `elastic_dp_size` and
`elastic_dp_rank` name the expanded replica set, each answering with its launch
counterpart until a scale-up moves it, and the readers that need the expanded
one -- the WORLD gather width, DP padding, KV routing, every place a gathered
list is indexed by replica, and KV-event sharding -- ask for it by name. That
includes the gather and scatter slices themselves: the list a scale-up gathers
spans WORLD, so indexing it by this process's place among the launch replicas
selects another rank's rows. The pair is range-checked like any other; it stays out of the identities
that describe the groups, because it does not describe them.

A draft on one context shard has no context-parallel communicator, and the
sampler asks for one only when there is more than one shard to reconcile --
otherwise the scope's answer, that there is no such group, is dereferenced.

The draft scope states a group for each width it narrows. It already said its
attention-TP width is the group it installs; it now hands over that group, and
says there is no attention-CP group, the way it already said there is no
expert-parallel one. The shared-expert scope states `moe_dp_size` for the same
reason -- narrowing two of the three MoE factors and leaving the third is a
triple that does not multiply out.

With the build checking what it made against what was configured,
`get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size` and its attention sibling answer the same
question as the configured widths rather than a second one, so their eight
readers move to the context.

## Accuracy Tests

Not run for this revision. The build now reads the widths the previous code
passed it, and the encoder states the layout it already built, so no
configuration changes what is constructed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The identity check is integer comparison on names already in
hand; it runs where a topology is written, not in a forward.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Each identity is injected in the direction that breaks it and in the direction
that keeps it, because a guard that only ever fires is as uninformative as one
that never does. Twenty-one tests that built a topology by passing widths
publish it first, and ten benchmark and example entries do the same. The
scale-up test now publishes a configuration before it asserts: without one
every term was unreadable and the check it claimed to make was skipped.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: [DSv4.1] Score prefill consumer index layers on candidate blocks with DeepGEMM
author: yuan-luo
body: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4.1's hierarchical sparse indexer picks attention positions in two levels on the dense fp4 prefill path (`DeepseekV4AttnBackend._low_ratio_index_topk_dense`). The first Full-mode index layer (layer 20, the candidate source) keeps the best `candidate_topk_blocks = 2048` blocks of `candidate_block_size = 8` compressed positions per query row and publishes them. The later index layers (24 / 28 / 32 / 36, the consumers) only run their top-512 over those candidates. Today both levels are torch glue over the full `[tokens, context]` fp32 score matrix that `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` writes, and every consumer computes that matrix again. For a 16384-token chunk at 262144 context the matrix is 17 GB per index layer: - the source masks the unreachable tail with an int64 broadcast compare plus `masked_fill_`, then runs `select_candidate_blocks` in 16 row chunks (padded copy, block `amax`, `torch.topk`, `scatter_`, `repeat_interleave`, `torch.cat`) into a `[tokens, context]` bool position mask of 4.3 GB; - each consumer scores all 262K columns (16 ms), builds `~mask` (another 4.3 GB), `masked_fill_`s its 17 GB of scores to `-inf`, runs the ragged top-k over the full row, and drops the `-inf` picks with `mask_topk_scores`. It uses 16K of the 262K columns it computed. On 4x B200 (TP4 / EP4, one 262144-token prompt) the indexer is about 240 ms of the last 544 ms chunk, and it is the only part of prefill that grows with context (+16 ms per chunk for every 16K tokens; the sparse attention itself is flat at 57 ms per chunk). The decode path does not have this problem: `DeepGemmCandidateIndexer` publishes a block table from the source layer's scores and the consumers score only their blocks with DeepGEMM's paged sparse logits kernel. This PR reduces 256K input's TTFT with -22%. (6.75 -> 5.23) For the backends other than SM100 will be tracked in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/40574. Related issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/42170. ## Design The source layer scores its whole context and keeps the 2048 best-scoring blocks of 8 positions per query row (1 in 16 at full context). Before, every consumer scored the whole context again and masked 15 of every 16 columns away; now it scores only the kept blocks, straight from its paged index-K pool, and picks its top-512 among them. Per chunk that turns four 17 GB dense matrices plus their masks into four 0.5 GB sparse rows. No kernel changes. Everything the two levels need already exists for the decode path; the PR puts the prefill side behind one interface and wires the DeepGEMM implementation to prefill rows. **The interface.** `CandidateIndexer` (`dsv4/candidate_indexer.py`) has three prefill methods. `publish_prefill(inputs)` returns what the source layer's consumers will select from; `select_prefill(published, inputs, out_positions)` is a consumer's top-k over that, written as flattened-K columns like the dense top-k writes them; `prefill_tail(published, tail_lens)` restricts what was published to the last rows of each request, for the late layers that run on the tail only. `PrefillIndexerInputs` carries a chunk's operands (fp4 query and head weights, compressed lengths, request starts, rows and lengths per request, the index-K pool view, the KV page table) plus a memoized `dense_scores()`, so an implementation that scores sparsely never computes the `[tokens, context]` matrix and one that needs it computes it once. Two implementations: `DeepGemmCandidateIndexer` (SM100), below, and `MaskCandidateIndexer`, the position masks that used to be inline in the backend, kept for Hopper and for the CP layout, whose local rows are not the page table's rows. `make_candidate_indexer` picks. The backend's dense prefill path only calls the three methods: a consumer calls `select_prefill`, the source computes its dense scores, calls `publish_prefill` and runs its own top-512; it never looks at what was published. **Level one, `publish_prefill` on DeepGEMM (source layer, once per chunk).** From the dense scores the source needs anyway, `amax8_varlen` writes one key per block of 8 positions below the row's `compress_len`, newest block forced to `+inf` so it is always kept: one read of the matrix, 4 bytes written per block. The plain ragged top-k over the keys (`k = 2048`) returns each row's block ids; rows with at most 2048 blocks take its trivial path and keep everything. `sort_candidate_blocks` sorts them ascending in place, `INT32_MAX` padded, and derives the pool slots, and `get_paged_sparse_mqa_logits_metadata` builds the DeepGEMM schedule for the rows. The result is a `PrefillSparseBlockTable`: one row per query token, with the `compress_lens` / `page_table` / `request_ids` it was built from kept attached, because `prefill_tail` has to rebuild the schedule for the tail rows (it is per row set and cannot be sliced). This replaces the compare, the `masked_fill_`, the row-chunk loop and the position mask; the scores are read once instead of five times. **Level two, `select_prefill` on DeepGEMM (each consumer layer).** `fp8_fp4_paged_sparse_mqa_logits` scores the consumer's queries against the source layer's index-K pool through the schedule, reading only the 2048 published blocks of each row, and writes bf16 `[tokens, 2048 x 8]` in ascending block order. `topk_transform_bf16_small` takes the top-512 of the first `valid_len` columns and applies its page transform with the block table as the page table (`column i -> blocks[row, i // 8] * 8 + i % 8`), which gives request-relative compressed positions, `-1` past `min(512, valid_len)`; adding the request start makes them the flattened-K columns of the interface, and the rest of the path (sort ascending, slot gather, raw indices) is unchanged. A consumer never computes, gathers or reads a dense score row, and no per-consumer mask exists. The consumers now score with bf16 weights and get bf16 scores, exactly what the decode path does for the same layers; the selection agrees with the mask implementation on 97-98% of positions, the rest are boundary picks a few bf16 ulps apart. **Tail rows.** The tail metadata exists when the source publishes, so `_publish_prefill` writes the full table on the forward metadata and, through `prefill_tail`, the tail rows' table on the tail metadata. `enter_late_layer_tail` has nothing to cut any more; the torch prefill path's inline masks take the same route. **Memory.** A published table outlives its chunk (the late layers and the overlap scheduler read it during the next one). In the shared caching-allocator pool its tensors (blocks, schedule, page table, about 700 MB) were carved from the free remainder of the block that held the source layer's 15 GiB dense scores, and that block could then neither be released nor reused for the next chunk's 16 GiB request: a flush / cold / cold / warm sequence at 262K ended in an OOM with 27 GiB reserved but unusable, while the plain version passed by luck. The DeepGEMM indexer allocates its tables from its own `torch.cuda.MemPool`, whose block sizes depend only on the row count, so it settles after one chunk and never touches the score blocks. (Putting the dense scores themselves in a private pool does not work: a private pool's cached blocks are not released under memory pressure, and the per-chunk sizes grow.) The protocol, and what the DeepGEMM kernels do with one query row from the source layer's dense scores down to the consumer's positions: ## Modifications **`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/candidate_indexer.py`** — `CandidateIndexer` (`publish_prefill` / `select_prefill` / `prefill_tail`), `PrefillIndexerInputs` (`msgspec.Struct`), `expand_index_page_table` (moved from the backend), `cut_request_masks`, and `MaskCandidateIndexer`: its `publish_prefill` is the block selection that was in the backend's `_publish_or_consume_candidates` (tail masked to `-inf`, row-chunked `select_candidate_blocks`), `select_prefill` masks the dense scores, runs `topk_transform_ragged_v2` and drops the `-inf` picks with `mask_topk_scores`, `prefill_tail` slices the masks. `make_candidate_indexer` returns the DeepGEMM indexer on SM100 (with the mask implementation for prefill under CP) and the mask indexer on Hopper. **`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/candidate_indexer_deep_gemm.py`** — `DeepGemmCandidateIndexer(CandidateIndexer)`: `publish_prefill` (`candidate_row_lens` -> `amax8_varlen` -> `topk_transform_ragged_v2` over the keys -> `_prefill_table`: `sort_candidate_blocks`, `build_sparse_indexer_schedule`, a CUDA event), `prefill_tail` (the table restricted to the tail rows, schedule rebuilt), `select_prefill` (`sparse_logits` + `topk_transform_bf16_small`, then the request start), the `PrefillSparseBlockTable` they share, and the `MemPool` the tables come from. The `TODO(dark)` for publish / select prefill is retired. **`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py`** — `_low_ratio_index_topk_dense` builds the `PrefillIndexerInputs` (`_prefill_indexer_inputs`; the dense scores are padded to 8 columns, `amax8_varlen` wants 32-byte aligned blocks where the top-k only needed 4). A consumer calls `select_prefill` and skips the index-K gather, the dense logits and the ragged top-k; the source computes its dense scores, calls `publish_prefill` and runs its own top-k. `_publish_prefill` writes the full table and, with `prefill_tail`, the late-layer tail's; `_publish_prefill_masks` does the same for the torch prefill path's inline masks. Removed: the candidate cut in `enter_late_layer_tail`, `_publish_or_consume_candidates`, the empty-batch mask publish (an empty chunk publishes `None`). The decode paths and the torch prefill path's own publish / consume are not touched. **`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsv41_prefill_sparse_indexer.py`** (SM100, one GPU) — `publish_prefill` returns the same blocks as `select_candidate_blocks` on the `-inf`-masked scores, block for block (ragged lengths, an empty row, block counts above and below 2048); the DeepGEMM `select_prefill` agrees with `MaskCandidateIndexer.select_prefill` on the same scores on at least 95% of the positions, picks inside its blocks, and every disagreement is within `2^-5` relative of the selection floor; `prefill_tail` carries the tail rows' blocks and selects what the full table selects for them. All pass on B200. ## Performance DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4x B200, TP4 / EP4, `flashinfer_mxfp4` MoE, `chunked_prefill_size=16384`, one 262144-token prompt plus 1024 output tokens, no speculative decoding. main (`567d5925f`) on GPUs 4-7 and this PR on GPUs 0-3 of the same box, requests alternating between the two. Warm numbers are after a 256K request on the same server; "cold" is the first request after `/flush_cache`, which empties the caching allocator. | | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | TTFT (262144 tokens, bs=1), warm | 6.75 / 6.90 / 7.07 / 7.17 s | **5.55 / 5.59 / 5.61 / 5.72 s (−18%)** | | TTFT, cold after `/flush_cache` | 10.8 / 13.0 s | 7.7 / 8.7 / 9.6 s | | TTFT, 200K natural-text prompt (sglang sources + a question) | 4.83 s | 4.17 s | | decode at 256K context | 3.8 ms / token | 3.8 ms / token | | prefill wall / GPU-busy (torch profiler, 16 chunks) | 6.77 / 6.55 s | 5.47 / 5.30 s | | last chunk (262K context) | 544 ms | 376 ms | | last chunk, indexer kernels | dense logits x8 104.9, ragged top-k x8 32.3, masked_fill 28.6, block amax 27.4, int64 compare 16.3, scatter / repeat 9.6, bitwise_not 8.7, torch.topk 7.0, copies 8.0 ms | dense logits x4 40.6, ragged top-k x5 13.5, schedule 13.9, sparse logits x4 5.8, amax8 2.7, small top-k x4 1.2, sort 0.5 ms | | four consumer layers, last chunk | 4 x (16 logits + 7.7 mask + 5 top-k + 0.3) = 116 ms | 4 x (1.45 + 0.3) = 7 ms | | chunk growth per 16K tokens of context | +16 ms | +4.8 ms | ## Accuracy GPQA Diamond (198 questions, single sample) through `sgl-eval run gpqa`, both servers with `--reasoning-parser deepseek-v41`, thinking on, `reasoning_effort=max`, temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95, `max_tokens 65536`, seed 1; main on GPUs 4-7 and this PR on GPUs 0-3 of the same box, run in parallel: | | main (`567d5925f`) | this PR | |---|---|---| | score | 87.88% | 91.41% | | truncated at `max_tokens` | 3.54% (7) | 1.01% (2) | | errors | 0 | 0 | | generated tokens / throughput | 2.2M / 3426 tok/s | 2.2M / 3560 tok/s | ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-writing-documentation). - [ ] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-writing-documentation). - [ ] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/accuracy_evaluation.html). - [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a reviewer when merging. - [ ] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #35706914278](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35706914278) Latest PR Test (Extra): :warning: **Not run on latest push** -- push again to dispatch. title: [NPU][BugFix] Avoid M-RoPE recompilation for variable sequence lengths
author: ltaodream
body:
## Motivation

On Ascend NPU, Qwen3-VL workloads with variable prompt and image lengths can trigger repeated Triton compilation during prefill.

The NPU preparation path calls:

```text
get_cos_sin_with_position
  -> apply_interleaved_rope_triton
  -> apply_interleaved_rope_kernel
```

`apply_interleaved_rope_kernel` currently declares the runtime sequence length `S` as `tl.constexpr`. As a result, every previously unseen sequence length creates a separate Triton specialization:

```text
S=112 -> compile
S=148 -> compile
S=205 -> compile
S=311 -> compile
...
```

This is especially expensive on Ascend because a Triton cache miss invokes the Ascend compiler toolchain. In profiling of variable-length Qwen3-VL requests on Ascend 910B2C:

- A 15-second scheduler sample spent about 14.0 seconds under `apply_interleaved_rope_triton`.
- About 13.6 seconds were spent in the Triton-Ascend compilation path.
- Nine prefill host scopes accumulated about 20.3 seconds, while the associated device computing events accumulated about 0.20 seconds.

These measurements indicate that the latency spikes are dominated by host-side compilation rather than NPU execution.

`S` is only used as a runtime boundary:

```python
mask_s = s_offsets < S
```

The launch grid is already computed from the actual sequence length:

```python
grid = (
    triton.cdiv(S, BLOCK_S),
    triton.cdiv(D, BLOCK_SIZE),
)
```

No static program shape depends on `S`: `BLOCK_S` determines the compile-time tile shape, while `S` is only passed as a runtime scalar for bounds checking. It therefore does not need to be a compile-time constant.

## Modifications

- Change `S` from `tl.constexpr` to a runtime kernel argument.
- Add `S` to Triton's `do_not_specialize` list so scalar-value specialization cannot recreate one compiled variant per sequence length.
- Keep `D`, `BLOCK_S`, and `BLOCK_SIZE` as compile-time constants because they define the static program shape.
- Preserve the existing launch grid and tail mask.

The functional change is limited to:

```diff
-@triton.jit
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["S"])
 def apply_interleaved_rope_kernel(
     x_ptr,
     out_ptr,
-    S: tl.constexpr,
+    S,
     D: tl.constexpr,
```

No model code, scheduling logic, or NPU-specific fused operator is changed.

## Accuracy Tests

The modified kernel was tested directly on Ascend 910B2C with:

```text
sequence lengths:
1, 63, 64, 65, 112, 148, 205, 311, 695

dtypes:
float16, bfloat16
```

For every length and dtype, the output was bit-exact with the PyTorch reference:

```text
max_abs_diff = 0
```

The Ascend Triton cache contained one specialization per dtype, with no additional variants created when only `S` changed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

An isolated kernel microbenchmark on Ascend 910B2C used the following sequence lengths:

```text
112, 148, 205, 228, 311, 338, 483, 620, 695
```

Results:

```text
First dynamic Triton compilation: approximately 7.2 seconds
Subsequent calls with different S: 0.11-0.31 ms
Compiled variants across S:       1
PyTorch reference, warm:          0.38-0.55 ms
```

The patch removes repeated cold compilation while retaining the fused Triton kernel. It does not change the launch grid, memory layout, or element selection logic.

Validation environment:

```text
Hardware:       Ascend 910B2C 64 GiB
Driver:         26.0.rc2
CANN:           9.0.0
SGLang:         0.5.20
torch:          2.10.0+cpu
torch_npu:      2.10.0
triton-ascend:  3.2.1.dev20260530
sgl-kernel-npu: 2026.6.1
```

CUDA and AMD execution are left to the registered upstream CI jobs.

## Checklist

- [x] Formatted the changed files and passed the applicable Ruff checks.
- [x] Verified exact output equality on Ascend NPU.
- [x] Provided kernel-level profiling and timing results.
- [x] Documentation is not required because this does not change a user-facing API or configuration.
- [x] Followed the existing SGLang kernel and test style.

title: [Diffusion] Fuse lossless SenseNova RoPE for 5% faster H200 inference
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

SenseNova-U1.5 eagerly applies three-axis RoPE using separate multiply, negate, concatenate and add kernels. Reusing the existing lossless bf16 rotate-half kernel reduces native 2048×2048/50-step **worker request E2E by 5.17% on one H200**, with byte-identical PNGs. Client E2E, including PNG save, improves 5.13% in the repeated isolated comparison.

## Modifications

- Route eligible bf16 CUDA Q/K tensors through the existing `fused_rope_rotate_half_bitexact`; preserve the original bf16 rounding after each product. Materialize the spatial head slices in BSHD layout, then return BHSD views to the existing attention path.
- Keep eager fallback for short prefixes, unsupported shapes/dtypes/table broadcasting, gradients and compilation. No normalization reduction, RoPE table computation, weights or attention backend changes.
- Forward the standard profiling/perf fields through SenseNova's sampling whitelist. Previously `--profile` was silently dropped, and stage timings were absent. Both benchmark arms contain this instrumentation-only fix.

This follows the shared-kernel reuse/rounding approach in #34004 and #38530. It is independent of the open RoPE-table reuse (#38927), RMSNorm dispatch (#39705), and host-sync (#38905) changes.

## Benchmark

title: [Diffusion] Fuse rounded SwiGLU for quantized MiniMax-H3 MLPs
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Quantized MiniMax-H3 MLPs disable reuse of the packed fc1 buffer because fc2 needs contiguous rows. This also skips the existing SwiGLU fusion, leaving separate BF16 SiLU and multiply kernels. FastH3's native profile shows this chain in all 50 DiT blocks.

Reusing the existing rounded **out-of-place** SwiGLU reduces **FastH3 FP8 worker E2E by 1.92%** and **saved-video client E2E by 1.88%** on two H200s. Peak reserved memory drops **85.4961 → 84.5156 GiB**. Generated video and audio are byte-identical.

## Modifications

- Route supported non-reusable BF16 CUDA fc1 outputs through `silu_and_mul_with_activation_rounding`, which allocates a contiguous output and preserves the eager BF16 rounding after SiLU and multiplication.
- Keep the existing in-place path when storage is reusable, the MXFP8 producer path, and fallback for unsupported layouts/dtypes/platforms.

No new kernel arithmetic, quantization scheme, attention policy or sampling change. This reuses the existing activation kernel, following the lossless fusion approach in #38530 and #38396. FastH3 uses the native support from #37480. The gate-communication and VAE optimizations in open #37662 and indexed RMSNorm/AdaLN in #34784 are separate changes.

## Benchmark

Native `FastVideo/FastVideo-FastH3-4-step-Preview-v1-VSA-DataFree` at `5ea076f35b84da4c3c82217112fa733d8eea2ae1`, with the built-in overlay `kevin-mi/FastH3-4step-Preview-overlay@f769cb8001dae335089de7b250364335bc7cb183`. **2× H200**, FP8 transformer with native Hopper per-token activation/per-channel weight scaling, lossless BF16 activations, Ulysses2/ring1, eager, no torch.compile, GPU-resident components. VSA is scoped to the transformer (`VSA_sparsity=0.9`) in both arms; text encoder and VAEs keep their native dense backends.

Fixed T2VA workload: short edge 768, 16:9, 10s requested → **1344×768, 243 frames, 10.125s at 24fps**, audio enabled; 5 sigma points/4 DiT evaluations, CFG1, seed1000. Prompt: “A curious raccoon peers through a vibrant field of yellow sunflowers, its eyes wide with interest.” Same-shape request warmup, two warmup steps.

Baseline `993d1fccbaafe3e79d91567d2fc1d665cc94fa50`; candidate `8ec2a429aeb1999303165925859b47a30a7aaf37`. Torch2.13.0+cu130, Triton3.7.1, CUDA13.0, driver595.71.05. [Environment](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/16a96416a527b3bd259ca57be9ab3edddbfe5514/diffusion-prs/fasth3-swiglu-h200/environment.json).

Fresh native CLI requests on the same idle GPUs, A–B–B–A; all microbench/profile analysis jobs finished before this group. Seconds:

| Run | Worker E2E | Denoise | Decode | Client E2E incl. MP4 save |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A1 | 18.4091 | 13.2930 | 4.9971 | 19.67 |
| B1 | 18.0807 | 12.9698 | 4.9955 | 19.29 |
| B2 | 18.0692 | 12.9580 | 4.9901 | 19.34 |
| A2 | 18.4501 | 13.3136 | 5.0062 | 19.70 |

| Mean | Baseline | Candidate | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Worker E2E | 18.4296 | 18.0749 | 1.92% |
| Client E2E including MP4 save | 19.6850 | 19.3150 | 1.88% |
| Denoise | 13.3033 | 12.9639 | 2.55% |

Worker E2E is perf-dump `total_duration_ms`, measured before `SAVE_OUTPUTS`, excluding model loading/warmup and MP4 file transport. Client E2E is the native timer around the scheduler request and saved output, logged to 0.01s precision. Decode is unchanged within measurement variation. [Raw perf dumps, source SHAs, configs and logs](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/16a96416a527b3bd259ca57be9ab3edddbfe5514/diffusion-prs/fasth3-swiglu-h200/raw), [timing summary](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/16a96416a527b3bd259ca57be9ab3edddbfe5514/diffusion-prs/fasth3-swiglu-h200/swiglu-r1-detailed-summary.json). Profiler/export timings are excluded from speed rows.

BCG was actually attempted and disabled by the native FastH3 pipeline. Its eager fallback is excluded from BCG performance claims. [Probe log](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/16a96416a527b3bd259ca57be9ab3edddbfe5514/diffusion-prs/fasth3-swiglu-h200/bcg-disabled.log).

## Profile and operator benchmark

The actual MLP input is `[36704, 28672]` BF16. A complete synchronized DiT iteration contains 50 SwiGLU calls. The source-attributed chain changes from **100 → 50 kernel launches** and **157.8448 → 45.1263 ms cumulative GPU time**. Both slices have zero boundary-crossing kernels. This removes the intermediate activation allocation and one launch per MLP; device-time totals are diagnostic and do not directly equal wall-clock savings.

[Baseline complete-iteration trace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/16a96416a527b3bd259ca57be9ab3edddbfe5514/diffusion-prs/fasth3-swiglu-h200/baseline-denoise-step2.trace.json.gz) · [Candidate trace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/16a96416a527b3bd259ca57be9ab3edddbfe5514/diffusion-prs/fasth3-swiglu-h200/candidate-denoise-step2.trace.json.gz) · [Baseline attribution](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/16a96416a527b3bd259ca57be9ab3edddbfe5514/diffusion-prs/fasth3-swiglu-h200/baseline-profile-evidence.json) · [Candidate attribution](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/16a96416a527b3bd259ca57be9ab3edddbfe5514/diffusion-prs/fasth3-swiglu-h200/candidate-profile-evidence.json). Original native traces, three-table triage, extraction script and SHA256 manifest are also included.

Exact committed-wrapper microbenchmark, including dispatch/output allocation; **mean milliseconds**, A–B–B–A, 100ms warmup +300ms measurement per cell. Outputs match bitwise and inputs are preserved.

| Packed fc1 shape | Eager SiLU × up | Rounded fused SwiGLU |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 × 28672 | 0.0079 | 0.0057 |
| 1024 × 28672 | 0.0881 | 0.0296 |
| 36704 × 28672 | 2.7222 | 0.8463 |

[Raw microbenchmark samples](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/16a96416a527b3bd259ca57be9ab3edddbfe5514/diffusion-prs/fasth3-swiglu-h200/swiglu-committed-microbench.json) · [Harness](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/16a96416a527b3bd259ca57be9ab3edddbfe5514/diffusion-prs/fasth3-swiglu-h200/scripts/bench-fasth3-swiglu.py).

## Output comparison

All four unprofiled MP4s and both profiled MP4s are **byte-identical**. Independently decoding all four ABBA videos gives **243/243 identical frames per run**, pixel max difference0, aggregate/worst-frame SSIM1 and PSNR∞. Decoded stereo float32 PCM samples are also identical (max error0/RMSE0). Before/after contact sheets were visually inspected.

![Before and after: frames 0, 80, 161, 242](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/16a96416a527b3bd259ca57be9ab3edddbfe5514/diffusion-prs/fasth3-swiglu-h200/output-comparison/comparison.jpg)

[Original baseline video with audio](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/16a96416a527b3bd259ca57be9ab3edddbfe5514/diffusion-prs/fasth3-swiglu-h200/baseline.mp4) · [Original optimized video with audio](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/16a96416a527b3bd259ca57be9ab3edddbfe5514/diffusion-prs/fasth3-swiglu-h200/candidate.mp4) · [Per-frame and audio audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/16a96416a527b3bd259ca57be9ab3edddbfe5514/diffusion-prs/fasth3-swiglu-h200/output-comparison/comparison.json).

MP4 SHA256: `a765db2889260898f21f911e97f060471530510281804908d5e2237300542069`.

## Validation and reproduction

- **Historical validation: 15 tests passed on H200 at the pinned benchmark candidate**: [4 SwiGLU CUDA checks](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/16a96416a527b3bd259ca57be9ab3edddbfe5514/diffusion-prs/fasth3-swiglu-h200/new-tests.log), [11 existing FastH3/VSA tests](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/16a96416a527b3bd259ca57be9ab3edddbfe5514/diffusion-prs/fasth3-swiglu-h200/existing-tests.log). The dedicated SwiGLU test file was subsequently removed from the PR; these logs document the earlier benchmark-candidate validation.
- [Pre-commit passed](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/16a96416a527b3bd259ca57be9ab3edddbfe5514/diffusion-prs/fasth3-swiglu-h200/precommit.log) at the pinned benchmark candidate, before removal of the dedicated test file; clean source at the measured head.
- Campaign-owned model weights and materialized overlay were deleted after validation: **zero residual files, weight files or bytes**. [Cleanup audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/16a96416a527b3bd259ca57be9ab3edddbfe5514/diffusion-prs/fasth3-swiglu-h200/cache-cleanup.json).

title: [Diffusion] Fuse LongCat GELU+cat and support Edit-Turbo BCG
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

LongCat's single-stream DiT blocks materialize BF16 tanh GELU and then concatenate it with attention output. The native Edit-Turbo profile shows 20 such sites per denoising step. A fused kernel removes the intermediate store/reload and one launch per site while preserving the eager BF16 result.

Edit-Turbo also lacks BCG registration. Simply registering it does not work for a non-square edit: the synthetic square input changes the warmup output grid and VL prefix, so the real request misses the captured signature. This patch makes the existing model-owned synthetic warmup hook preserve the explicitly requested aspect ratio and enables BCG for Edit-Turbo.

On **one H200**, the combined patch reduces native saved-image request E2E in two A–B–B–A groups: **worker 2.46% / 2.65%, client including PNG save 2.89% / 2.62%**. Baseline is original eager; candidate uses the fused kernel, corrected warmup and actual BCG. All valid lossless outputs are byte-identical.

## Modifications

- Add a vectorized JIT CUDA `cat(attention, gelu(mlp, approximate="tanh"))` kernel. It copies attention unchanged, matches aten's FP32 operation order and BF16 store, and queries device SM count/occupancy at runtime.
- Use it in the LongCat single block behind BF16, layout, alignment, device and first-sight exactness checks. Preserve the existing quality-mounted GEMM+GELU path. Grad-enabled, compiled and unsupported calls retain the eager path; unverified graph capture does not attempt a host equality check.
- Build the synthetic edit image at the explicit warmup resolution. Preserve the complete VL prefix plus 512-token prompt body and image position IDs. Register **Edit-Turbo** for BCG; ordinary Edit is not added to the model-ID allowlist.
- Keep focused CUDA rounding/replay tests and the edit warmup geometry/BCG padding regressions.

This follows the lossless rounding approach in #38530 and #38396. Native edit conditioning comes from #35829 and is unchanged for user requests. There is no checkpoint, sampling, attention or quantization change.

## Benchmark

`meituan-longcat/LongCat-Image-Edit-Turbo@6a7262de5549f0bf0ec54c08ef7d283ef41f3214`, **1× H200**, BF16/lossless, resident components, no torch.compile. Prompt: **“Make the cat wear a red hat.”**, seed 42, 8 steps, CFG 1, prompt rewrite disabled. The fixed input produces **1264×848**; the explicit warmup resolution is 1264×848 in both arms. DiT has 10 joint blocks and 20 single blocks; the single-stream sequence has 9233 tokens (8374 image + 859 conditioning), width 3072, MLP 12288.

Baseline `993d1fccbaafe3e79d91567d2fc1d665cc94fa50`; candidate `10410a20b6d2716c1489a3132dc79c775dc297bb`. Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, CUDA 13.0, driver 595.71.05. [Environment](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/c5224b77806b9c5d902986c0c6089dc476c845fd/diffusion-prs/longcat-edit-turbo-gelu-cat-bcg-h200/environment.json).

Fresh native CLI processes on the same idle GPU, two complete A–B–B–A groups. A=original eager; B=combined BCG. Seconds, excluding load/warmup:

| 2 | B2 | 1.5260 | 1.2462 | 1.67 |

Worker timing is native perf-dump `total_duration_ms`, measured before output saving. Client timing wraps the native request and saved PNG, logged to 0.01 s precision. Profile/export requests are excluded. Peak reserved memory is **32.805 GiB baseline, 31.328 GiB candidate eager, 35.248 GiB candidate BCG**; graphs need additional memory. [All raw perf dumps, source SHAs, configs and logs](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/c5224b77806b9c5d902986c0c6089dc476c845fd/diffusion-prs/longcat-edit-turbo-gelu-cat-bcg-h200/raw) · [Audited evidence](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/c5224b77806b9c5d902986c0c6089dc476c845fd/diffusion-prs/longcat-edit-turbo-gelu-cat-bcg-h200/final-evidence.json).

**Scope of the gain:** kernel-only eager ABBA did not establish saved-request E2E improvement (worker 0.19%). Combined eager denoise improved 1.62% / 1.57%, but saved-client outliers of 2.87 s and 5.79 s prevent an eager E2E claim. These rows are retained in the evidence. The headline is the repeated combined BCG configuration above; it does not attribute the whole gain to graph replay alone.

## Profile and operator benchmark

The complete synchronized baseline denoising step has 699 GPU kernels. Joining aten operators to kernels through trace `External id` identifies **20 GELU +20 channel concat kernels, 5.7457 ms**. The candidate eager step has 679 kernels, including **20 fused calls, 3.2138 ms**. Other joint-block GELUs remain unchanged.

The candidate BCG full trace records **248 `cudaGraphLaunch` calls = 31 segments × 8 steps**, with no serving-signature miss or eager fallback. Its complete-step slice has 31 graph launches, 36 individual launches and 679 GPU kernels. All three step slices have zero boundary-crossing kernels. [Baseline trace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/c5224b77806b9c5d902986c0c6089dc476c845fd/diffusion-prs/longcat-edit-turbo-gelu-cat-bcg-h200/profiles/baseline/denoise-step2.trace.json.gz) · [Candidate eager](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/c5224b77806b9c5d902986c0c6089dc476c845fd/diffusion-prs/longcat-edit-turbo-gelu-cat-bcg-h200/profiles/combined-eager/denoise-step2.trace.json.gz) · [Candidate BCG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/c5224b77806b9c5d902986c0c6089dc476c845fd/diffusion-prs/longcat-edit-turbo-gelu-cat-bcg-h200/profiles/combined-bcg/denoise-step2.trace.json.gz) · [Replay audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/c5224b77806b9c5d902986c0c6089dc476c845fd/diffusion-prs/longcat-edit-turbo-gelu-cat-bcg-h200/graph-replay-evidence.json). Full native traces, source attribution and three-table triage accompany each slice.

Archived marker benchmark, rotating inputs, default median, exact benchmark-candidate wrapper including output allocation:

| Tokens | Attention /MLP width | Eager GELU+cat (us) | Fused (us) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

NCU full/source reports confirm DRAM traffic **981.626→548.146 MB** for the production pair. NCU timing is 302.336→183.360 us under profiling clocks and is kept separate from marker/native timing. Fused source stalls point to the MLP load and GELU arithmetic; the kernel has 32 registers and no spills. A `tanh.approx` experiment changed 60 finite BF16 outputs and was rejected. [Baseline NCU](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/c5224b77806b9c5d902986c0c6089dc476c845fd/diffusion-prs/longcat-edit-turbo-gelu-cat-bcg-h200/ncu/baseline/REPORT.md) · [Fused NCU](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/c5224b77806b9c5d902986c0c6089dc476c845fd/diffusion-prs/longcat-edit-turbo-gelu-cat-bcg-h200/ncu/fused/REPORT.md), including report files.

title: [Diffusion] Accelerate Cosmos3 Edge on Hopper with lossless fusions
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Cosmos3 Edge's single-image path still uses separate Q/K normalization, RoPE and KV concatenation on Hopper. Its dense MLP also materializes ReLU before a separate square. Native profiles identify both chains in all 28 generation blocks, with separate positive and negative CFG passes.

This enables the existing rounded QK norm/RoPE/KV packing for the validated Edge shape and reuses the unary ReLU² kernel with fast math disabled. On **one H200**, two native A–B–B–A groups reduce **image worker E2E by 29.61–32.23%** and **saved-image client E2E by 26.92–30.59%**. Video worker E2E improves about **2.2%**. All generated images and all 81 video frames remain exact.

## Modifications

- Admit the 2048-wide dense Edge T=1 shape to the existing Hopper TP1/SP1 QK norm/RoPE/KV-pack path. Preserve the rounded BF16 cache and Edge's separately normalized UND keys. Larger dense, parallel and compiled configurations retain the previous gate.
- Expose the existing activation compiler's `fast_math` option through the unary wrapper, defaulting to the existing behavior. Cosmos contiguous BF16 CUDA inference uses `fast_math=False` for ReLU²; other model paths retain Torch.
- Add finite-domain, production-shape, storage-ownership, changed-input CUDA-graph replay and fallback tests, plus a registered marker benchmark. No CUDA arithmetic implementation or checkpoint change.

The first fast-math experiment flushed 511 BF16 subnormal products to zero and was rejected before native combined benchmarks. Disabling fast math preserves all **65,280 finite BF16 encodings**, including signed zero and subnormal results. [Rejected experiment](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/rejected-fast-math-experiment), [source review](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/source-review.md).

This builds on the actual rounded Cosmos T1 and Hopper Nano implementations in #34932 and #36571, following the lossless fusion approach in #38530. Edge's architecture comes from #31590. Closed #34618 does not provide a usable BCG path in the current custom denoising stage.

## Benchmark

`nvidia/Cosmos3-Edge@344d602b128d1bbdacb43b08d0a3626f46343e29`, **1× H200**, TP1/SP1, BF16, native eager, `quality=lossless`, manual performance mode, GPU-resident components, no torch.compile. Native same-shape request warmup, two warmup steps; fixed sampling in both arms:

| Workload | Output | Steps / CFG / seed | Prompt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T2I | 640×640, 1 frame | 35 / 7 / 0 | A warehouse robot folds a blue cloth on a clean workbench. |
| T2V | 832×480, 81 frames, 24 fps (3.375 s) | 35 / 5 / 42 | A warehouse robot carefully places a blue box on a shelf. |

Baseline `993d1fccbaafe3e79d91567d2fc1d665cc94fa50`; candidate `18f1417a8b189fcb80b38d6ca3b487ecca89f39d`. Torch2.13.0+cu130, Triton3.7.1, CUDA13.0, driver595.71.05. [Environment](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/environment.json). Both arms use the existing native helper's Cosmos guardrail setting; the checkpoint already disables its safety checker.

Fresh native CLI processes, same idle GPU, two A–B–B–A groups per workload. Profile and microbenchmark runs are excluded. Seconds, with reduction from each group's arithmetic means:

| T2V-R2 | 6.2865 → 6.1464 (2.23%) | 4.5580 → 4.4190 (3.05%) | 7.550 → 6.490 (14.04%) |

T2V-R2 contains a baseline client-only outlier (A1 **8.47 s**, worker **6.2879 s**). All rows are retained; its inflated client percentage is not treated as a repeatable benefit. T2V-R1 saved-client reduction is about 2.3%; both video groups have consistent worker reductions. The image result independently exceeds 1.5% in both worker and saved-client E2E in both groups.

The current PR head `1430010b7b20f9d56d6d6d4caeebee1980e28c73` adds only a test coverage correction after the measured head: the newly enabled Hopper split-path parity checks are registered on the Hopper CI lane and skipped on other architectures. B200 continues to run all four ReLU² tests, which passed in the first CI run. That run exposed three failures from applying the Hopper split-path bitwise contract to the unchanged Blackwell QK path. Runtime files and all benchmark measurements are unchanged.

The corrected seven-test file passed on H200 (14.27 s). In the next CI run, the H100, B200 and BCG jobs were skipped by fast-fail after the unrelated [CPU fixture failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35475607241/job/105984387058): `test_auxiliary_output.py` supplies a mock batch without `split_index`, which the existing scheduler reads. ## Profile and operator benchmark

Each slice is one complete second CFG iteration, covering both positive and negative passes. CPU model-call boundaries are joined to GPU execution through CUDA launch correlations; all five retained slices have **zero boundary-crossing GPU kernels**. The baseline video path already uses the QK fusion; its gain comes from ReLU².

Cumulative profile device times explain the changed operators and are not E2E measurements. | QK norm + RoPE + KV pack, S1024, Q16/KV8, D128 | 85.8332 | 8.9444 |
| ReLU², [1, 400, 9216] | 8.6710 | 4.0407 |
| ReLU², [1, 8190, 9216] | 146.1616 | 71.6109 |

[Raw marker output](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/cosmos3-edge-combined-marker-retry1.log). Mutable Q/K views belong to the current forward; V and cached UND K/V remain unchanged, as tested.

## Output comparison

The audit covers **39 output records**: **33 valid eager requests**, plus six explicitly unsupported BCG requests. Every valid image/video, including separate lossless/high checks and profiled requests, is byte-identical within its workload. All videos independently decode to **81/81 identical frames**, SSIM1, PSNR∞, no audio stream. Before/after image and video contact sheets were visually inspected. The T2I native result contains a blue cloth/workbench but no visible robot in either arm; this comparison establishes output preservation.

BCG was actually attempted for T2I/T2V and in the lossless/high T2I matrix. Every attempt reports `[diffusion bcg] disabled` with no capture, so fallback outputs are retained only as applicability evidence. **No Cosmos BCG speedup is claimed.** High eager T2I/T2V checks are exact, with no separate high-mode performance claim.

## Validation and reproduction

- **145 Cosmos/kernel tests and 46 subtests passed**, including the new CUDA tests and existing model tests. [Log](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/cosmos3-edge-combined-tests-retry1.log).

title: [Diffusion] Enable lossless SANA-Video eager conv fusions for 12.6% lower latency
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

SANA-Video's frame-batched GLUMB activations are much larger than Sana's image workload. Its native eager profile is more than 99% GPU busy, with **80 convolution-bias additions taking 97.77 ms per complete CFG iteration**, before the separate SiLU and multiply kernels. The existing exact convolution post-processing only runs in BCG contexts.

Reuse those fusions for SANA-Video eager inference. Two native A–B–B–A groups on **one H200** reduce worker E2E by **12.58–12.63%** and client E2E including saved video by **12.54–12.67%**. All lossless output videos remain byte-identical.

## Modifications

- Add an explicit eager opt-in to the shared convolution bias+SiLU and bias+GLU helpers; SANA-Video's GLUMB temporal block opts in. The Sana image default-stream policy stays intact.
- Reuse the existing BF16 rounding boundaries, first-sight exactness checks and permanent fallback on mismatch. Gradient-enabled default-stream calls and compiled/non-CUDA paths keep Torch.
- Keep this dispatch-only change focused on the existing helpers; standalone test and benchmark files are omitted. No new CUDA/Triton arithmetic, LayerNorm policy, approximate attention, sampling or checkpoint change.
- Update the existing SANA-Video fusion-coverage row for eager convolution post-processing.

The implementation reuses #34928 and the SANA-Video wiring in #35961. The image-specific CPU-launch regression discussed in #34015 motivates retaining the original default for image callers. This video profile has a different cost distribution. [Source review and execution flow](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/source-review.md).

## Benchmark

`Efficient-Large-Model/SANA-Video_2B_480p_diffusers@db5f398b13ca086d09a50ce156c20527773841b1`, **1× H200**, TP1, native backend, GPU-resident components, BF16 DiT/Gemma2, native FP32 linear-attention accumulation and FP32 latent/VAE policy. Manual performance mode, no torch.compile.

Official video shape: **832×480, 81 frames, 16 fps, 5.0625 s**, 50 requested sampling steps, CFG6, flow shift8, seed42. Fixed 300-token text window and native negative prompt. Prompt: `A curious raccoon walks through a sunlit forest. motion score: 30.` Same-shape warmup at 832×480/81 frames.

Baseline `993d1fccbaafe3e79d91567d2fc1d665cc94fa50`; measured candidate `275113434ffe34412f807514399ba00ef70fa38e`; PR head `64e1e8a92a1942f058b9d6c175f5342198b34709`. Any documentation-only follow-up does not change the measured runtime. Torch2.13.0+cu130, Triton3.7.1, CUDA13.0, driver595.71.05. [Environment](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/environment.json).

Fresh native CLI processes on the same idle GPU; A–B–B–A in each group. The eager comparison is repeated twice. BCG runs use actual capture/replay in both arms and provide a regression comparator. Seconds; parentheses show reduction from each group's arithmetic means:

| Group | Worker E2E | Denoise | Client E2E including MP4 save |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| eager-r1 | 44.7324 → 39.1040 (12.58%) | 41.7766 → 36.1501 (13.47%) | 45.210 → 39.480 (12.67%) |
| eager-r2 | 44.7479 → 39.0949 (12.63%) | 41.7929 → 36.1431 (13.52%) | 45.125 → 39.465 (12.54%) |
| bcg-r1 | 37.7962 → 37.7986 (-0.01%) | 34.8571 → 34.8603 (-0.01%) | 38.175 → 38.175 (0.00%) |

<details><summary>All 12 unprofiled native measurements</summary>

| Group | Arm | Worker E2E | Denoise | Client E2E incl. save | Peak reserved GiB |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| eager-r1 | A1 | 44.6694 | 41.7160 | 45.04 | 20.9199 |
| eager-r1 | B1 | 39.0674 | 36.1122 | 39.45 | 21.0176 |
| eager-r1 | B2 | 39.1406 | 36.1880 | 39.51 | 21.0176 |
| eager-r1 | A2 | 44.7954 | 41.8371 | 45.38 | 20.9199 |
| eager-r2 | A1 | 44.7547 | 41.8005 | 45.14 | 20.9199 |
| eager-r2 | B1 | 39.0982 | 36.1451 | 39.47 | 21.0176 |
| eager-r2 | B2 | 39.0916 | 36.1411 | 39.46 | 21.0176 |
| eager-r2 | A2 | 44.7412 | 41.7853 | 45.11 | 20.9199 |
| bcg-r1 | A1 | 37.7978 | 34.8597 | 38.18 | 23.6758 |
| bcg-r1 | B1 | 37.7905 | 34.8525 | 38.16 | 23.6758 |
| bcg-r1 | B2 | 37.8067 | 34.8682 | 38.19 | 23.6758 |
| bcg-r1 | A2 | 37.7946 | 34.8545 | 38.17 | 23.6758 |

</details>

Worker E2E is perf-dump stage duration before saving, excluding loading/warmup. Client E2E is the native scheduler-request/output-save timer, logged to 0.01 s. Profile and benchmark-export timings are excluded. [All raw perf dumps, configs, source SHAs and logs](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/raw), [complete evidence](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/final-evidence.json).

## Profile and operator benchmark

Each slice contains a complete second positive/negative CFG iteration. CPU third-to-fifth model/graph calls are joined to GPU kernels using CUDA launch correlations. All four slices have zero boundary-crossing GPU kernels. Both BCG profiles contain **eight single-segment graph launches**, with **two in the selected CFG iteration**; no signature miss or eager fallback is accepted.

| Native profile | All kernels | Separate conv post kernels / GPU ms | Fused conv post kernels / GPU ms | Graph launches in slice |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| baseline-eager-profile | 2349 | 200 / 168.9436 | 0 / 0.0000 | 0 |
| baseline-bcg-profile | 2023 | 0 / 0.0000 | 80 / 36.9273 | 2 |
| conv-eager-profile | 2229 | 0 / 0.0000 | 80 / 36.0984 | 0 |
| conv-bcg-profile | 2023 | 0 / 0.0000 | 80 / 36.7944 | 2 |

The fusion removes materialized bias and activation intermediates. Other native operations retain their original implementation. Cumulative device times explain the operators and are not E2E measurements. [Original/sliced traces, source attribution and three-table triage](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/profiles).

Committed-wrapper marker benchmark, rotating inputs, median microseconds. These rows include the **actual convolution and post-processing**, with normal output allocation:

| Operation | Native shape | Eager | Fused |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Pointwise conv + bias + SiLU | [21,2240,30,52] → C13440 | 4459.0695 | 3476.4716 |
| Depthwise conv + bias + GLU | [21,13440,30,52] → C6720 | 3127.3782 | 1174.3818 |

[Raw marker output](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/sana-video-conv-marker.log). Output parity is checked separately against the complete native convolution chain, including temporal convolution.

## Output comparison

The audit covers 26 request records. All **22 valid lossless videos**, including unprofiled and profiled eager/BCG runs, are byte-identical. Independent decoding verifies **81/81 identical frames**, SSIM1, PSNR∞, and no audio stream. The before/after contact sheet was visually inspected.

![Baseline eager, optimized eager and optimized BCG; frames 0,26,53,80](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/output-comparison/comparison.jpg)

[Original baseline MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/baseline.mp4) · [Original optimized eager MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/candidate.mp4) · [Original optimized BCG MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/candidate-bcg.mp4) · [Per-frame hashes](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/output-comparison).

Lossless MP4 SHA256: `bd995912646f473f711d30e452891f7bd61dd594dbc6b4987d6f92bc3210f8a5`.

Separate quality/applicability matrix at the candidate, lossless/high in A–B–B–A order per mode:

| Request | Quality | Applicability | Comparison against lossless |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| quality-bcg-a1 | lossless | valid | exact |
| quality-bcg-a2 | lossless | valid | exact |
| quality-bcg-b1 | high | rejected: cannot be used with breakable cuda graphs | no artifact |
| quality-bcg-b2 | high | rejected: cannot be used with breakable cuda graphs | no artifact |
| quality-eager-a1 | lossless | valid | exact |
| quality-eager-a2 | lossless | valid | exact |
| quality-eager-b1 | high | valid | SSIM mean/min 0.938866/0.923584, PSNR mean/min 31.27/29.93 dB |
| quality-eager-b2 | high | valid | SSIM mean/min 0.938866/0.923584, PSNR mean/min 31.27/29.93 dB |

High-mode rows validate the existing quality policy and are excluded from the lossless performance claim. Any rejected BCG quality request remains an invalid row, with its native reason retained. [Quality matrix](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/quality-matrix.json).

## Validation and reproduction

**Validation scope:** The test counts, logs and GPU measurements below are historical results from the recorded benchmark revisions, before test cleanup. title: [Diffusion] Fuse lossless Wan VAE post-ops for LongLive 2 I2V
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

LongLive 2's lossless Wan VAE decoder executes five separate FP32 pointwise passes after normalization. In the native I2V profile, the 464 norm/SiLU scopes take **690.82 ms across 3248 kernels**. Keeping Torch's reduction and fusing only the exact post-ops reduces that to **275.26 ms / 1834 kernels**, including first-sight reference checks and fallback calls.

On **one H200**, final-source I2V A–B–B–A groups reduce worker E2E by **5.53–5.88%**. The representative final group reduces client E2E including video save from **5.980 to 5.665 s (5.27%)**. All lossless before/after videos are byte-identical. T2V worker latency improves, but retained client outliers prevent a T2V client E2E speed claim.

## Modifications

- Keep native autocast-aware L2 normalization and epsilon clamp, then fuse divide, scale, affine multiplication, bias addition and SiLU into one JIT CUDA kernel. Inputs/gamma may be BF16, while the normalized intermediates and output remain FP32.
- Use explicit FP32 round-to-nearest operations and `expf`, with FMA contraction disabled and no fast math. Support dense NCDHW and channels-last-3D layouts through the existing JIT utilities.
- Integrate through the shared Wan VAE wrapper with per-signature integer-bit verification and permanent fallback on mismatch. Unsupported dtype/layout, gradient-enabled, compiled and unverified-capture calls retain the native path. Unsupported post-op inputs reuse the already-computed denominator.
- Preserve the existing high-quality full RMSNorm+SiLU dispatch. Keep three focused tests for autocast/layout/affine behavior, numerical boundaries and graph replay, and update fusion-coverage documentation.

The existing Wan full-norm fusion (#33546, #35981) and the open conv-bias/full-norm tiling work in #38650 are distinct from this lossless post-only path. The shared wrapper also serves other Wan/Qwen VAEs; this PR's native model evidence covers LongLive 2 T2V and I2V. Other model families are protected by the first-sight exactness gate but are not claimed as benchmarked here.

[Source review and execution flow](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/5af31ea3b6b434c21b2014ea2834876317818058/diffusion-prs/longlive2-wan-norm-post-h200/source-review.md). Native SiLU arithmetic was checked against the [installed Torch source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytorch/pytorch/cf30153c4c131c8164ee7798e5022d810682e2cb/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/ActivationSiluKernel.cu).

## Benchmark

Model `Rabinovich/LongLive-2.0-5B-Diffusers@37664a64cfc38cdc5fabe88576961ef10646e4f1`. Native SGLang eager, 1×H200 / TP1, unquantized BF16 DiT, native VAE/autocast precision, all components resident. Automatic performance mode resolves CPU/layerwise offload to false in both arms. No torch.compile or approximate cache. Four steps, CFG1, flow shift5, seed42, 61 frames at24fps (2.5417s), no audio.

- I2V: native helper requests960×928; the input-image aspect handling produces **1152×768** in all24 accepted I2V videos. The helper's supported-resolution advisory is retained. Prompt: `The cat starts walking slowly towards the camera.`
- T2V: requested and actual832×480. Prompt: `A curious raccoon`.
- Both modes use the same native helper warmup in every arm: **960×928×29 frames, two of four steps**. Warmup is excluded from request timing; the requested warmup flags do not override that helper's synthetic request geometry.

Baseline `993d1fccbaafe3e79d91567d2fc1d665cc94fa50`; final measured/PR candidate `be05e7e6c24252db11458621f2d06f3969be08d1`. Earlier r1/r2 use `a98b0875c4`; final r3/r4 include the reviewed fallback fix and unique custom-op name. The CUDA device implementation and marker/NCU harness are unchanged. Torch2.13.0+cu130, Triton3.7.1, CUDA13.0, driver595.71.05.

[Environment](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/5af31ea3b6b434c21b2014ea2834876317818058/diffusion-prs/longlive2-wan-norm-post-h200/environment.json) · [fixed input image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/5af31ea3b6b434c21b2014ea2834876317818058/diffusion-prs/longlive2-wan-norm-post-h200/input-cat.png).

Each group uses fresh native CLI processes on the same idle GPU in A–B–B–A order. Seconds; reductions are calculated from arithmetic means, with no sample removal.

| Workload / group | Worker E2E | Denoise | Client E2E including save |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| i2v-r1 | 5.6111 → 5.2703 (6.07%) | 1.5028 → 1.5025 (0.01%) | 6.0000 → 5.6600 (5.67%) |
| i2v-r2 | 5.6117 → 5.2834 (5.85%) | 1.5018 → 1.5000 (0.12%) | 6.0100 → 5.8400 (2.83%) |
| i2v-r3 | 5.5972 → 5.2878 (5.53%) | 1.4977 → 1.5007 (-0.20%) | 5.9800 → 5.6650 (5.27%) |
| i2v-r4 | 5.6159 → 5.2855 (5.88%) | 1.5038 → 1.5011 (0.18%) | 6.5400 → 5.7200 (12.54%) |
| t2v-r1 | 2.3925 → 2.2465 (6.10%) | 0.5832 → 0.5813 (0.32%) | 2.6900 → 4.2350 (-57.43%) |
| t2v-r2 | 2.3906 → 2.2615 (5.40%) | 0.5827 → 0.5843 (-0.28%) | 2.6950 → 2.5650 (4.82%) |
| t2v-r3 | 2.3984 → 2.2782 (5.01%) | 0.5858 → 0.5856 (0.04%) | 2.7350 → 2.5800 (5.67%) |
| t2v-r4 | 2.3905 → 2.2704 (5.02%) | 0.5848 → 0.5821 (0.47%) | 2.6850 → 3.8750 (-44.32%) |

All four I2V groups clear1.5% in both saved-request worker and client means. I2V r4A1 has a7.08s baseline client outlier, inflating r4's12.54% client reduction; **5.27% from final r3 is the representative client figure**. Denoise is essentially unchanged because the optimization is in VAE decoding.

T2V r1B1 and r4B2 clients take5.93s and5.18s despite worker times2.2457s and2.2708s. These delays occur after the output-saved log. A separate fixed diagnostic ABBA also reproduces a post-save delay on the unmodified baseline (6.09s client /2.3921s worker). Active-thread py-spy and GC callbacks did not determine its cause. **No T2V client E2E speedup is claimed**, and none of these samples is removed.

[Diagnostic evidence](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/5af31ea3b6b434c21b2014ea2834876317818058/diffusion-prs/longlive2-wan-norm-post-h200/client-diagnostic-summary.json). The original [all-workloads audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/5af31ea3b6b434c21b2014ea2834876317818058/diffusion-prs/longlive2-wan-norm-post-h200/final-evidence.json) retains `qualified:false`; [workload qualification](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/5af31ea3b6b434c21b2014ea2834876317818058/diffusion-prs/longlive2-wan-norm-post-h200/qualification-review.json) explicitly accepts I2V alone.

Profile, marker, sampler and initial admission runs are excluded from performance claims. Final peak reserved memory increases **59.6426→61.0195GiB (+1.377GiB)**.

## Profile and kernel benchmark

Full native all-stage profiles are used because this causal loop does not advance the denoise-step profiler. CPU norm-wrapper scopes are joined to kernels through CUDA launch correlations; nested stage totals are not double-counted. Each full request has464 decoder norm/SiLU scopes.

| Workload / source | Attributed kernels | Attributed GPU ms | Fused post-op calls | Fused GPU ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| t2v-baseline-profile-retry1 | 3248 | 312.4739 | 0 | 0.0000 |
| t2v-norm-final-profile | 1834 | 124.1225 | 434 | 47.5257 |
| i2v-baseline-profile | 3248 | 690.8231 | 0 | 0.0000 |
| i2v-norm-final-profile | 1834 | 275.2550 | 434 | 107.9946 |

Each final trace has434 fused calls (415 channels-last and19 NCDHW), with30 scopes retaining fallback. The first-sight reference work remains included. Cumulative GPU times explain the change and are not substituted for E2E latency.

[Original full traces, source attribution and three-table triage](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/5af31ea3b6b434c21b2014ea2834876317818058/diffusion-prs/longlive2-wan-norm-post-h200/profiles).

Archived whole-chain marker benchmark, rotating inputs, median microseconds. Both arms include the native norm/clamp and normal output allocation:

| Input N,C,T,H,W | Layout | Torch µs | Fused µs |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1,1024,1,30,52 | NCDHW | 51.008 | 24.288 |
| 1,1024,1,30,52 | channels-last-3D | 45.696 | 19.360 |
| 1,1024,2,60,104 | NCDHW | 216.192 | 63.520 |
| 1,1024,2,60,104 | channels-last-3D | 208.448 | 52.800 |
| 1,256,4,240,416 | NCDHW | 1484.960 | 357.696 |
| 1,256,4,240,416 | channels-last-3D | 1519.456 | 364.128 |

NCU isolates the five post-ops at the last channels-last shape, with the same precomputed native denominator in both arms:

| NCU measurement | Five Torch kernels | One fused kernel |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Sum of kernel duration |1599.136µs|315.104µs|
| DRAM reads |1,842,186,240B|206,129,664B|
| DRAM writes |1,930,885,632B|385,019,392B|

The isolated chain is **5.07× faster**, with **84.33% less measured DRAM traffic**. The fused launch uses30 registers/thread,1056 CTAs×256threads, zero local load/store sectors and70.62% active warps. Combined DRAM throughput is38.99% of peak; source/PM counters identify denominator-load long-scoreboard and SiLU dependency/MIO stalls. There is no claim of saturated HBM or tensor-core execution for this pointwise kernel.

## Test

**Validation scope:** The test counts, logs and GPU measurements below are historical results from the recorded benchmark revisions, before test cleanup. H200: **9 pytest cases plus16 subtests passed**. Coverage includes all65,280 finite BF16 patterns, FP32 SiLU/subnormal boundaries, BF16/FP32 input and affine tensors, both layouts, nonintegral sqrt(C), zero norms, changed-input/affine CUDA replay, first-sight/mismatch/capture fallback, unsupported dtype/layout, denominator reuse, compile guard, gradients, VAE-gate behavior and import isolation.

```bash
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_diffusion_import_isolation.py
```

Pre-cleanup validation covered all seven files and included Mint documentation and broken-link checks with Node22. The retained tests now use the single-GPU CUDA CI lane; the archived local GPU results were collected on H200.

[Test log](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/5af31ea3b6b434c21b2014ea2834876317818058/diffusion-prs/longlive2-wan-norm-post-h200/longlive2-norm-final-tests-retry2.log) · [Pre-commit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/5af31ea3b6b434c21b2014ea2834876317818058/diffusion-prs/longlive2-wan-norm-post-h200/final-seven-files-precommit.log) · [Documentation build](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/5af31ea3b6b434c21b2014ea2834876317818058/diffusion-prs/longlive2-wan-norm-post-h200/wan-norm-doc-mint-validate.log) · [Link check](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/5af31ea3b6b434c21b2014ea2834876317818058/diffusion-prs/longlive2-wan-norm-post-h200/wan-norm-doc-mint-links.log).

## Reproduce

Use the pinned model revision and fixed input image, with the same native helper command in baseline and candidate checkouts. The task-owned snapshot's main ref is pinned to the revision above; offline mode prevents a moving download.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 \
FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1 \
sglang generate --backend=sglang \
  --model-path=Rabinovich/LongLive-2.0-5B-Diffusers \
  --prompt='The cat starts walking slowly towards the camera.' \
  --image-path=/path/to/input-cat.png --seed=42 \
  --width=960 --height=928 --num-frames=61 \
  --num-inference-steps=4 --guidance-scale=1.0 \
  --num-gpus=1 --tp-size=1 --enable-torch-compile=false \
  --warmup-resolutions=960x928 --warmup-num-frames=61 \
  --quality=lossless --save-output --warmup-mode=request \
  --perf-dump-path=/tmp/longlive2-i2v.json \
  --output-path=/tmp/longlive2-i2v --output-file-name=longlive2-i2v
```

For T2V, use `--prompt='A curious raccoon'`, remove `--image-path`, and set width832/height480 and warmup-resolutions832x480. For diagnostic native profiles add `--profile --profile-all-stages` and set `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR`; exclude those runs from latency claims.

[Exact runners, fixed ABBA schedule and audit scripts](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/5af31ea3b6b434c21b2014ea2834876317818058/diffusion-prs/longlive2-wan-norm-post-h200/scripts). After the model cycle, **689 owned files, including five weight files (24,211,983,385 bytes total), were removed and zero residual files/weights/bytes were verified**. The shared cache was untouched. [Cleanup ledger](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/5af31ea3b6b434c21b2014ea2834876317818058/diffusion-prs/longlive2-wan-norm-post-h200/cache-cleanup.json) · [Artifact SHA256 manifest](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/5af31ea3b6b434c21b2014ea2834876317818058/diffusion-prs/longlive2-wan-norm-post-h200/SHA256SUMS.json).

### Upstream CI follow-up

[Base CI, attempt 2](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35487361647/attempts/2): both single-GPU JIT partitions, multi-GPU JIT, JIT benchmark, multimodal unit tests, BCG, RTX 5090 diffusion, and four 1-GPU diffusion partitions passed. The workflow is red because unchanged CPU fixtures lack `split_index` / `_prev_prefill_end_ts`; later B200, component-accuracy, remaining 1-GPU and 2-GPU jobs stopped at PR-health fast-fail before their tests, followed by incomplete diffusion coverage. The local H200 numerical, profile and native saved-output evidence above passed.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] deepseek-v4.1: Reuse dequantized compressed KV in PD CP prefill (7/N)
author: BJWang-ant
body: issue:https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/39700 base pr: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40179 ## Summary DeepSeek V4.1 consumer layers can share the same compressed KV storage, but sparse prefill currently dequantizes that storage into a BF16 workspace on every layer. Reuse the dequantized compressed KV within a forward to avoid repeated reads, dequantization, and workspace writes. ## Changes - Limit reuse to CP sparse BF16 prefill with compression ratios 1 and 2. - Keep separate workspaces per compression ratio. - Track validity by source layer and workspace address within the per-forward gather cache. - Refresh on producer execution, source changes, workspace reallocation, or a new forward. - Continue updating SWA and top-k inputs for every layer. This retains additional scratch memory for the separate workspaces. ## Validation - GPU regression tests cover shared sources, source updates, ratio interleaving, consecutive forwards, and workspace resizing. - All 16 short/long-context smoke-test outputs match the baseline. - In a six-step trace, compressed KV dequantization calls decrease from 228 to 24 (89.5% fewer). ### Performance DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on 8×B200 with PD disaggregation; prefill uses TP4/EP4, CP, BCG, MegaMoE, and DSpark. Results are medians of three unprofiled runs using the unchanged benchmark script, with 512 requests and an output length of 500, which is 60k unprefix cache of 64k all input length. ### precision gsm8k test result ## trace comparison before after --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #41813675179](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41813675179) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #41813675111](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41813675111) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #41813675138](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41813675138) > [!TIP] > Base CI only covers the core cases, and its workload may not exercise your change.
