title: [Diffusion] Fuse lossless LingBot World FP32 normalization
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

LingBot World V2 causal blocks materialize FP32 LayerNorm intermediates and launch separate modulation operations on BF16 activations. The self-attention residual also computes a normalized output that is discarded before camera conditioning and a second normalization.

Fusing these exact arithmetic chains reduces saved-client latency by **at least 2.98% in both fixed native thirty-chunk WebSocket ABBA groups** on one H200. The workload generates **357 frames at 832×480**, with unchanged raw RGB frames and byte-identical MP4s. Short nine-frame CLI measurements and their client variability are reported separately below.

## Modifications

- Extend the existing ATen-compatible, vectorized-four Welford Triton kernel with FP32 modulation and FP32 affine epilogues. Normalize and modulate in FP32, then store BF16 once. Affine uses the native explicit FMA; modulation retains separate FP32 multiplication/addition. Existing BF16/FP8 defaults and `shift=None` behavior remain intact.
- Compute only the self-attention residual when its normalized result would be discarded. Preserve the mixed-dtype arithmetic and negative zero without an extra `+0` gate operation.
- Reuse the existing rounded CUDA scale-shift kernel for camera modulation. Retain the existing packed QKV and SP-only camera-affine cache policy. That cache is inactive in this one-GPU measurement; camera-affine GEMMs remain unchanged.
- Gate the three new mixed-dtype paths by live bit comparisons outside capture and by device/dtype/layout/grad/compile eligibility. Reuse the existing versioned FP32 affine-parameter cache. Unsupported paths retain the native reference.

Related existing implementation: [ATen-order LayerNorm PR34008](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34008), [rounded modulation PR34004](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34004), and current main's [scale-only LayerNorm PR39983](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39983). The retained tests focus on LingBot normalization, residual arithmetic and changed-input/parameter graph replay. [Source review and numerical evidence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/source-review.md).

## Benchmark

- Baseline: `dd83b54611897a5f80f4df59e69756bd2fb4b8ab`; candidate: `89b3700dbc9146727cbb368b6859f5a18e79ae66`.
- Checkpoint: `robbyant/lingbot-world-v2-14b-causal-fast-diffusers@59cccf49f2d2dd27418ae7a04b82b10868d455c2`.
- One NVIDIA H200, GPU 0, TP 1/Ulysses 1. Torch 2.13.0+cu130 (`cf30153c4c131c8164ee7798e5022d810682e2cb`), Triton 3.7.1, sglang-kernel 0.4.7, driver 595.71.05, transformers 5.12.1, diffusers 0.37.0. [Environment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/environment.json).
- Eager, unquantized BF16, `quality=lossless`, `performance-mode=manual`; DiT and VAE resident, native text-encoder CPU offload. Four denoising steps, CFG 1, native flow shift 5, seed 42, 16 fps. No torch.compile or approximate cache.
- Input: [actual cat PNG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/input-cat.png); prompt: `A slow aerial orbit around a pastel island hotel in the ocean.` Camera action script holds `w` throughout. The input, prompt, revisions and sampling parameters are identical in every A/B.
- Native server warmup 832×480×9 plus a separate two-chunk seed 41 WebSocket warmup. The timed seed 42 session produces thirty chunks: 9 frames, then 29×12 frames. Each sample uses a fresh server and identical warmup. GPU work is serialized.

**Worker** sums the native `scheduler_forward_ms` statistics over all thirty chunks. **Saved client** measures WebSocket connection, receiving all raw RGB frames, MP4 encoding with the existing native CI helper, and writing the complete MP4. **Received client** stops before MP4 encoding/saving. Startup and warmup occur before these timers. No measured transport/save overhead is subtracted. Profiles and initial probes are excluded from these groups.

| Fixed ABBA group | Worker sum(s), reduction | Saved client(s), reduction | Received client(s), reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| r1 | 75.557500 → 73.264000 (3.04%) | 76.702326 → 74.414894 (2.98%) | 75.594154 → 73.298542 (3.04%) |
| r2 | 75.568500 → 72.916500 (3.51%) | 76.717485 → 74.073432 (3.45%) | 75.601582 → 72.949983 (3.51%) |

<details>
<summary>Every native streaming sample, in A-B-B-A order</summary>

| Sample | Worker sum(s) | Saved client(s) | Received client(s) | Evidence |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| r1 a1 | 75.561000 | 76.729841 | 75.596676 | [record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/raw/realtime30-r1-a1/result.json) |
| r1 b1 | 72.864000 | 74.049499 | 72.897961 | [record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/raw/realtime30-r1-b1/result.json) |

| r1 a2 | 75.554000 | 76.674812 | 75.591633 | [record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/raw/realtime30-r1-a2/result.json) |

| r2 b1 | 72.863000 | 73.984729 | 72.894706 | [record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/raw/realtime30-r2-b1/result.json) |

</details>

All first-chunk setup and saving costs remain included. The opening result uses the smaller of the two group improvements.

### Short CLI results and BCG applicability

The CLI preset generates only the first 9 frames for this realtime model. Its worker timer is `metrics.total_duration_ms`, measured around native worker forward before output materialization; its client timer is the native `Pixel data generated successfully` timer around scheduler response and output handling/saving. Worker peak reserved memory is 73.830078125 GiB in every final A/B. The streaming benchmark above did not separately sample its peak.

| CLI group | Worker mean(s), reduction | Baseline client A1,A2(s) | Candidate client B1,B2(s) | Client mean reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| r1 | 2.514728 → 2.457130 (2.29%) | 2.62, 2.62 | 2.59, 6.06 | -65.08% |
| r2 | 2.517657 → 2.454037 (2.53%) | 2.63, 2.62 | 2.56, 2.56 | 2.48% |
| r3 | 2.516916 → 2.453010 (2.54%) | 2.62, 2.62 | 2.56, 2.56 | 2.29% |
| r4 | 2.517515 → 2.451732 (2.61%) | 2.62, 2.62 | 2.56, 2.61 | 1.34% |

R1B2 saved its video before a roughly 3.5 s delay and reports 6.06 s client time. R4 client improvement is only 1.34%. All four groups are retained; **no stable short-CLI client speedup is claimed**. The two complete streaming groups above are the qualification workload, not a selected subset of these CLI rows. [Full evidence, including exploratory and older-source requests](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/final-evidence.json); [preserved CLI qualification decision](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/cli-final-evidence.json).

Native LingBot configuration explicitly disables BCG. Actual lossless/high BCG attempts reported `[diffusion bcg] disabled` and no capture; any resulting eager artifact is excluded from BCG performance. Standalone CUDA graph tests do not imply model BCG support. An exploratory CLI `--num-frames=117` also still produced 9 frames and is excluded from long-video evidence. [Workload audit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/full117-invalid-workload.json).

### Earlier ten-chunk streaming workload

| Group | Worker sum(s), reduction | Saved client(s), reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| r1 | 24.826500 → 23.370000 (5.87%) | 25.455890 → 23.995062 (5.74%) |
| r2 | 24.248500 → 24.041500 (0.85%) | 25.173037 → 24.657524 (2.05%) |

These 117-frame requests retain the first-chunk initialization variability: r1A1 first worker chunk 3.802 s, r2B1 first worker chunk 3.950 s, versus typical 2.66 s baseline / 2.58 s candidate. R2's complete worker mean did not pass 1.5%, although later chunks consistently improved. No chunk was removed from these totals. The 30-chunk groups above test a longer native session with the same bounded causal cache and include all initialization costs. [Preserved ten-chunk evidence and decision](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/ten-chunk-final-evidence.json).

## Profile and kernel evidence

Paired native full-stage traces contain five complete causal forwards, 200 blocks and 199 camera/cross-normalization sites. CPU launch correlation assigns kernels to four non-overlapping regions; norm1 includes its small block-entry affine setup. Times below are cumulative GPU kernel time, not request latency.

| Site | Calls | Kernel count A→B | GPU time A→B(ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| norm1_and_entry_setup | 200 | 1605 → 630 | 72.038135 → 12.320743 |
| residual_before_camera | 199 | 403 → 204 | 15.747938 → 8.793154 |
| camera | 199 | 597 → 199 | 18.539539 → 9.175137 |
| cross_attention_norm | 199 | 597 → 199 | 38.400541 → 7.965987 |

Total: **3,202→1,232 kernels**, **144.726153→38.255021 ms**. The five first-block norm1 calls retain the native path for the noncontiguous patch-embedding output; 195 later norm1 calls and 199 cross norms are fused. The separate forward3 slices contain only kernels owned by that forward, 1,583 baseline / 1,188 candidate. [Baseline full trace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/profiles/current-baseline-profile/native-full-stages.trace.json.gz), [candidate full trace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/profiles/current-profile/native-full-stages.trace.json.gz), [site attribution](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/profiles/current-profile/lingbot-sites.json), [three-table triage with manual interpretation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/profiles/current-profile/three-table-triage.md).

Whole-site CUDA-event markers, BF16 `[1,tokens,5120]` with the actual FP32 affine/residual contracts:

| Tokens | Site | Native(µs) | Fused(µs) |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
|4680|norm1|325.440|47.328|
|4680|cross norm|185.536|43.264|
|4680|camera|102.688|53.504|
|4680|residual|66.400|43.168|
|9360|norm1|624.416|81.728|
|9360|cross norm|349.920|73.568|
|9360|camera|188.704|97.344|
|9360|residual|124.128|78.720|

[Marker log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/validation-logs/lingbot-current-marker.log).

NCU 2025.3.1 separately profiles the whole native/fused normalization chains at 4,680 tokens, including input/output casts and post-ops:

| Site | Kernels | Time A→B(µs) | DRAM read+write A→B(bytes) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
|norm1|6→1|338.496→41.024|821,483,008→108,945,920|
|cross norm|3→1|188.320→40.480|475,884,800→91,410,688|

DRAM traffic falls 86.74% / 80.79%. The fused kernels use 32/38 registers with zero local-memory spill sectors. Source sampling concentrates remaining long-scoreboard waits at the input reload; the gains come from avoiding FP32 intermediates and launches. NCU replay timings differ from CUDA-event markers and are not E2E results. [NCU report, method and interpretation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/ncu/REPORT.md); [all metrics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/ncu/analysis/key-metrics.json). Full/source reports and PM/source evidence are included in the artifact tree.

## Output comparison

All valid final-source lossless 9-frame requests are byte/pixel-exact. Within each streaming length, all eight repeated 357-frame outputs and all eight earlier 117-frame outputs (plus the initial 117-frame pair) have identical raw RGB frames and MP4 bytes:

- 9-frame MP4: `550e6cbfe8c4c39b8d3556244c0c25240ae4749e15b20a1d8bd8f7e0be45612e`.
- 117-frame MP4: `fb24eced712fb5f337e2832477920b592421e83984576425903e1fda7f56571b`.
- 357-frame MP4: `1246de4a92e7b2f18e19f79b9b4b93c481a753992a90c6ceb95669e44f7ae78f`.
- No audio stream. Within-mode baseline/candidate lossless SSIM=1 and PSNR=∞ for every frame.
- The high-quality baseline and candidate also match each other byte-for-byte. Against lossless, decoded-frame SSIM mean/min=0.97989128/0.97729409; PSNR mean/min=42.93970/42.30205dB, passing the predeclared 0.92 / 24 dB bounds.

## Reproduction

The artifact scripts pin the checkpoint in an owned cache, verify the selected source/GPU, record native commands and requests, and retain all attempts. [Prepare pinned checkpoint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/scripts/prepare-lingbot-world-v2.py); [native streaming harness](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/scripts/run-lingbot-realtime.py); [fixed ABBA driver](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/scripts/validate-lingbot-realtime30-abba.py); [CLI driver](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/scripts/run-lingbot-world-v2.py); [NCU collection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8944261991f45f15dc1c49fa15bcf1304958c597/diffusion-prs/lingbot-world-fp32-norm-h200/ncu/collect.sh).

The streaming harness launches the native server with these settings (full environment and exact per-sample ports/requests are in raw/):

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 sglang serve \
  --model-path robbyant/lingbot-world-v2-14b-causal-fast-diffusers \
  --num-gpus=1 --tp-size=1 --ulysses-degree=1 \
  --performance-mode=manual --dit-layerwise-offload=false \

```

It calls the existing `collect_realtime_output` and `encode_realtime_frames_to_mp4` helpers. The msgpack init uses the pinned input PNG bytes, prompt above, `size=832x480`, `fps=16`, `num_frames=9`, `seed=42`, `num_inference_steps=4`, `guidance_scale=1`, `quality=lossless`, `max_chunks=30`, raw output and pacing disabled. title: [dsv4.1]Optimize FP4 indexer by skipping invisible tiles
author: shiyu7
body:
## Motivation

The legacy FP4 indexer replays a capacity-sized CUDA Graph grid even when the live context is short. Masking K loads and final logits still leaves dequantization, dot products, weighting, and reduction running on fully invisible tiles. In a measured shape with 1,048,896 output columns and at most 8,704 visible positions, more than 99% of columns are invisible.

This change skips the arithmetic for completely invisible tiles and writes `-inf` directly to valid output addresses.

## Modifications

- Add a CTA-uniform branch after loading the current device-side `n_vis`. Partially visible tiles retain the original arithmetic, BF16 rounding points, and masks.
- Express existing caller guarantees to Triton: zero-width inputs return before launch, and contiguous queries have a 128-element head stride when `H > 1`. Exclude singleton heads from the stride assumption.
- Preserve the function signature, output shape, cache layout, launch grid, and call sites. Each graph replay reads the current device length; no new feature flags are introduced.
- Extend the existing FP4 indexer tests with visibility boundaries, an independent PyTorch decoding/rounding reference, noncontiguous and nonfinite inputs, and graph replay after mutating inputs, mappings, and lengths.

## Validation

- Source PR on H20: 57 tests passed, 378 strict comparisons against the original, and compute-sanitizer checks passed.
- Source benchmarks: ~27.8× isolated-kernel speedup for short live contexts; ~38–67% lower TPOT on the ~8K shared-prefix PD workload.
- Service-level greedy-output equivalence remains unresolved due to baseline nondeterminism.
- Port: pre-commit, Python syntax, and `git diff --check` passed; GPU tests were not rerun locally.
### Accuracy Tests
Validated on H20 / SM90, Torch 2.13.0, Triton 3.7.1:

Existing FP4 kernel suite with the candidate staged in: 57 passed.
Independent harness: 36 boundary cases, 2 graph cases, 4 layout cases, 378 strict comparisons against the frozen original, and 175 special-value checks.
Coverage: H32/H64, single rows and six-row DSPARK groups, padding rows, random physical pages, partial tiles, mixed lengths, zero width, and lengths 0/1/63/64/65 and near/equal to output width.
Normal random inputs require atol=0, rtol=0; nonfinite inputs require matching original behavior and NaN locations (equal_nan=True). Invalid outputs must be -inf.
Replayed the same CUDA Graph after changing lengths, slots, queries, weights, and cache contents, including long → short → long transitions.
Representative small matrices passed compute-sanitizer memcheck, initcheck, and synccheck with 0 errors.

### Speed Tests and Profiling
Unprofiled CUDA Graph timing: medians of 15 randomly interleaved A/B rounds × 10 replays per round.

| Rows / heads / output width | Maximum visible length | Seed | Original µs | Optimized µs | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 48 / 32 / 1,048,896 | 8,704 | 719 | 17,731.581 | 637.523 | 27.81× |
| 48 / 32 / 1,048,896 | 8,704 | 721 | 17,731.462 | 637.254 | 27.82× |
| 96 / 32 / 524,448 | 4,352 | 721 | 17,736.810 | 638.291 | 27.79× |
---

title: [NPU] Skip fused gmm1+swiglu for swiglu_limit (SiLU-with-clamp) checkpoints
author: iridiumine
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #39881. The fused gmm1 kernel ( npu_grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2 ) applies plain SiLU with no clamp , but _uses_fused_gmm1 selected it for W4A8 MXFP4 MoE based only on the kernel type and use_fused_gmm1 — it never looked at the activation configuration.

Checkpoints whose MoE activation is SiLU-with-clamp ( swiglu_limit , e.g. DSV4) therefore lost the clamp when the fused kernel was selected, producing incorrect numerics. This silently bypassed the clamp path ( NPUSwigluMxfp8Quant ) that #38420 had just added for exactly this case.

## Modifications

Single-file change in python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/ascend.py :

- _uses_fused_gmm1(kernel, config) now takes the runner config and returns False when config.swiglu_limit is set and > 0 :
  - W4A8 MXFP4 + swiglu_limit (DSV4): falls back to the unfused path — w13 gmm + NPUSwigluMxfp8Quant(config.swiglu_limit) , which applies the clamp. This restores the pre-#39881 behavior
  - MXFP8 + swiglu_limit : raises NotImplementedError at init — this method has no unfused gmm1 path, so failing loudly beats silently serving wrong numerics (no known checkpoint hits this combination today)
  - Plain-SiLU models ( swiglu_limit unset or 0 ): keep the fused kernel, unchanged
- Both call sites ( __init__ and run() ) now pass the same config, so the activation selection and the fused/unfused branch decision can never disagree

## Accuracy Tests

- Dispatch logic verified locally with mocked kernels for all combinations: W4A8 ± swiglu_limit, MXFP8 ± swiglu_limit, use_fused_gmm1=False , and non-fused kernels — all resolve as intended
- DSV4 on NPU (fp4 experts → NPUW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod , swiglu_limit from HF config) now resolves to the unfused clamp path, bit-identical to the pre-#39881 serving path

## Speed Tests and Profiling

None — this PR intentionally trades the #39881 fusion gain back for correctness on clamp checkpoints. Plain-SiLU models (e.g. Kimi-K3 MXFP4) keep the full fused-path benefit (~15% per-layer MoE latency reduction from #39881). Recovering the fusion gain for clamp checkpoints would require adding a limit parameter to the fused kernel, which is kernel-side work out of scope here.

## Checklist

- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).

3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

title: [Model Loader] Add InstantTensor loader support
author: YitaoYuan
body:
## Motivation

Add [InstantTensor](https://github.com/scitix/InstantTensor) as an optional high-performance loader for Safetensors checkpoints.

InstantTensor supports distributed weight loading and pipelined prefetching. This integration lets users select it with `--load-format instanttensor` while preserving SGLang's existing checkpoint discovery and model-loading flow.

It has already been integrated into several other projects, such as vLLM. https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/models/extensions/instanttensor/

## Modifications

- Add `instanttensor` to the supported load formats and CLI choices.
- Add an InstantTensor weight iterator based on `instanttensor.safe_open`.
- Require PyTorch's `cuda` device interface (including CUDA and ROCm). Reject unsupported devices during server-argument validation and at the iterator entry, before importing InstantTensor or accessing the current CUDA device.
- Reuse the existing Safetensors file discovery, shard index filtering, and checkpoint selection logic.
- Validate selected filenames at the InstantTensor iterator entry and reject non-`.safetensors` files before opening any checkpoint. Keep SGLang's existing discovery, download, cache, and pattern-priority behavior unchanged; unsupported selections fail explicitly rather than being automatically replaced.
- Pass SGLang's initialized device process group to InstantTensor for distributed loading.
- Support tuning through `--model-loader-extra-config`, including `buffer_size`, `chunk_size`, `io_depth`, and `backend`.
- Convert JSON backend names or ordered candidate lists to InstantTensor backend/policy enums. Skip SGLang's extra-config validation for InstantTensor and forward optional parameters without filtering. Pass filename, framework, device, process group, and `copy=True` explicitly; Python rejects duplicate arguments, and InstantTensor handles unsupported parameters and values.
- Add the optional `sglang[instanttensor]` dependency with `instanttensor>=0.1.9` to support these tuning options.
- Document core tuning options in the shared loader configuration table and link to InstantTensor for the latest options.
- Extend `SRTRunner` to select the load format and pass extra loader configuration in model-loading tests.
- Add focused CPU unit tests and a weekly single-GPU output-consistency test comparing Safetensors with explicitly configured InstantTensor loading.

### Configuration example

```bash
pip install "sglang[instanttensor]"

python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B \
  --load-format instanttensor \
  --model-loader-extra-config '{"backend":"URING","chunk_size":8388608,"io_depth":64}'
```

For the tuning options shown above, explicit non-null values override the corresponding `INSTANTTENSOR_*` environment variables. Omitted or `null` values retain InstantTensor's environment-variable and automatic defaults. Backend names are case-sensitive; an ordered list such as `{"backend":["URING","AIO"]}` selects the first available candidate. Additional optional parameters are forwarded unchanged, except that `filename`, `framework`, `device`, `process_group`, and `copy` cannot be overridden. Unsupported parameters, including generic loader settings such as `enable_multithread_load` and `num_threads`, are not silently dropped; they are left for InstantTensor to reject.

## Accuracy Tests

### CPU unit tests

All 8 InstantTensor-related CPU tests passed: 6 iterator tests and 2 server-argument hardware-validation tests.

These tests cover configuration forwarding (including `copy=True`), backend conversion, current-device and process-group selection, and rejection of unsupported filename suffixes at the iterator entry. Hardware tests accept the CUDA and ROCm platform classes, reject non-CUDA device types before importing InstantTensor or calling CUDA APIs, and check that other load formats remain usable with CPU devices. These are CPU-only interface tests, not ROCm hardware validation; real NCCL behavior is not covered by the mocks.

Related regression tests, CI registration checks, and applicable pre-commit checks also passed.

### GPU generation consistency

The single GPU E2E test passed. It runs weekly, defaults to `Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B`, and launches two engines: a Safetensors baseline and InstantTensor with `backend="MMAP"`, `chunk_size=8388608`, and `io_depth=2`. It clears inherited `INSTANTTENSOR_*` variables while the engines run. MMAP avoids requiring io_uring support in the CI environment.

The latest local CUDA run used `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` with PyTorch 2.13.0 and InstantTensor 0.1.9, using FP16 inference. An earlier run also passed with deliberately conflicting InstantTensor environment variables set before launch:

```text
Ran 1 test in 46.021s
OK
```

InstantTensor produced identical generated text to the Safetensors baseline. The maximum differences in prefill and decode log probabilities were both zero. This is an output-consistency test, not a byte-for-byte comparison of the final model parameters or a loading-speed benchmark. Registered GPU CI covers this single-GPU MMAP path, not real TP2 loading or a backend matrix.

### Previously validated serving configurations

The original end-to-end serving validation also covered:

- Qwen3-30B-A3B, TP1
- DeepSeek-R1, TP8+EP8

For every configuration, Safetensors and InstantTensor produced the same response and token IDs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Test on 50GB/s storage

| Model         | GPU    | Backend                | Load Time (s) | Throughput (GB/s) | Speedup   |
|---            |---     | ---                    |---            |---                |---        |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | 1*H200 | Safetensors            | 57.4          | 1.07              | 1x        |
|               |        | fastsafetensors        | 22.2          | 2.75              | 2.59x     |
|               |        | RMS                    | 9.29          | 6.57              | 6.18x     |
|               |        | InstantTensor          | 1.77          | 34.5              | **32.4x** |
| DeepSeek-R1   | 8*H200 | Safetensors            | 160           | 4.30              | 1x        |
|               |        | fastsafetensors        | 75.8          | 9.08              | 2.11x     |
|               |        | RMS                    | 101           | 6.82              | 1.58x     |
|               |        | RMS (distributed mode) | 192           | 3.59              | 0.83x    |
|               |        | InstantTensor          | 15.3          | 45.0              | **10.5x** |

### Test on in-memory file system (tmpfs)

| Model         | GPU    | Backend                | Load Time (s) | Throughput (GB/s) | Speedup   |
|---            |---     | ---                    |---            |---                |---        |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | 1*H200 | Safetensors            | 12.7          | 4.81              | 1x        |
|               |        | fastsafetensors        | 16.7          | 3.66              | 0.76x     |
|               |        | RMS                    | 8.21          | 7.44              | 1.55x     |
|               |        | InstantTensor          | 1.26          | 48.5              | **10.1x** |
| DeepSeek-R1   | 8*H200 | Safetensors            | 22.6          | 30.5              | 1x        |
|               |        | fastsafetensors        | 63.4          | 10.9              | 0.36x     |
|               |        | RMS                    | 79.8          | 8.63              | 0.28x     |
|               |        | RMS (distributed mode) | 156           | 4.41              | 0.14x     |
|               |        | InstantTensor          | 12.1          | 56.9              | **1.87x** |

See [this document](https://github.com/scitix/InstantTensor/blob/main/docs/benchmark.md) for details.

The loading comparison uses SGLang's `Load weight` elapsed time. Server ready time is included for completeness but also covers model initialization, kernel compilation, and cache setup, so it is not used to calculate loading throughput.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [deepep_v2] support GLM-5.3-Flash (Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration)
author: whn09
body:
## Motivation

`--moe-a2a-backend deepep_v2` cannot be used with GLM-5.3-Flash
(`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`). There are two independent blockers.

**1. The architecture is not registered as v2-eligible.**
`moe_model_registry._DEEPEP_V2_MODELS` does not list it, so
`validate_deepep_v2_model_architecture()` rejects the server args before the
engine starts.

**2. `glm5_next.py` gates the a2a path on a v1-only predicate.**
`MoeA2ABackend.is_deepep()` is true only for `deepep`, not for `deepep_v2`, so
even past the first gate the model silently runs the non-a2a path:

`Glm5NextModel.__init__` computes
`enable_a2a_moe = is_deepep() or is_mooncake()`, which stays `False` under v2,
so the MoE layers never route through the dispatcher.

`deepseek_v2.py` — an already-validated v2 model — includes `is_deepep_v2()` in
that predicate. This change mirrors it.

> **Edit after review:** the first version of this PR also touched the
> `gemm_output_zero_allocator` sizing predicate and the
> shared-experts-fusion rejection reason. @mmangkad correctly pointed out that
> neither does anything here, and both are reverted as of 442125ed — see the
> Modifications section below.

## Modifications

Two lines, both load-bearing:

- `configs/moe_model_registry.py`: add `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` to
  `_DEEPEP_V2_MODELS` (`silu_mul_keep_fp32=False`, same as the other entries).
- `models/glm5_next.py`: include `is_deepep_v2()` in `enable_a2a_moe`.

Reverted after review (442125ed), both no-ops:

- the `is_a2a_moe` sizing predicate. Its enclosing block is gated on
  `_use_aiter_gfx95 and config.n_routed_experts == 256 and
  self.embed_tokens.embedding_dim == 7168`. Beyond being AMD gfx95 only,
  GLM-5.3-Flash is 288 routed experts with `hidden_size` 4096, so the block is
  unreachable for this architecture on any device.
- the `is_deepep_class_backend()` switch in
  `shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason`, plus its import. The
  `get_parallel().moe_ep_size > 1` check immediately above already returns for
  every DeepEP-family configuration.

## Accuracy Test

Hardware: 2x `p5.48xlarge` (8x H100 80GB, EFAv2), model GLM-5.3-Flash,
`--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm`, `deepep_v2_mode=direct`.

Both arms reach `The server is fired up and ready to roll!` and produce
correct output; before this change the server either fails server-arg
validation or runs without the dispatcher.

**TP=8 / EP=8, 1P1D PD-disaggregated (Mooncake over EFA):** PD warmup
completes; 7/7 requests correct, zero KV-transfer errors on either side.

**TP=16 / EP=16 across both nodes** (so dispatch/combine genuinely crosses the
network, not just NVLink):

```
$ curl .../v1/chat/completions -d '{... "用中文写三句话介绍长江..." , "temperature":0}'
长江是中国第一长河，全长约6300公里，也是亚洲第一、世界第三长河。它发源于青藏高原的唐古拉山脉，
自西向东流经11个省级行政区，最终在上海注入东海。长江流域物产丰富、经济发达，孕育了灿烂的中华文明，
被誉为中华民族的母亲河。
```

- 8 concurrent arithmetic prompts (`N * 13` for N in 3,5,7,9,11,13,17,19):
  8/8 exact.
- 4424-token prompt (3 chunks at
  `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=2048`): correct summary.
- zero errors/asserts in either node's log.

## Benchmark & Profiling

Not included — this change is about functional enablement, and the runs above
were correctness-focused. Happy to add throughput numbers if useful.

## Notes for other EFA users (deployment, not part of this change)

DeepEP v2's `ElasticBuffer` asserts on a non-NONE NCCL GIN
(`csrc/kernels/backend/nccl.cu`) even when EP fits inside a single NVLink
domain. On H100 + EFAv2 there is no GDAKI, so the aws-ofi-nccl GIN plugin
(self-reported type 5) is unusable and `NCCL_GIN_TYPE=2` (PROXY, layered over
aws-ofi-nccl via `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN`) is the only working setting. Separately,
`deep_ep/__init__.py:check_nccl_so()` matches the bare substring `libnccl`
against `/proc/self/maps`, so pointing `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN` at
`libnccl-net-ofi.so` trips its "Duplicate NCCL runtime" assert; a copy under a
name not containing `libnccl` avoids it.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add or update tests, or state why they are unnecessary: covered by the existing `test_deepep_v2_*` unit tests; this change only adds an architecture to the eligibility registry and aligns one predicate with `deepseek_v2.py`.
- [x] Update documentation as needed, or state why it is unnecessary.
- [x] Provide accuracy results (above).
- [x] For CI changes: n/a.

title: [diffusion] Enable lossless Cosmos3 Super T2I QK fusion on Hopper TP2
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Cosmos3 Super Text2Image uses the split QK-normalization/RoPE path on Hopper TP2. Its native profile shows repeated Q/K copies, rotary-cache casts, rounded pointwise operations and UND-prefix KV concatenation in every GEN layer, although the existing fused kernel supports this shape.

Enable the existing lossless path for this workload. Native **2× H200**, eager, saved-output measurements reduce worker E2E by **7.38–8.81%** and client E2E including PNG saving by **6.47–6.96%** in groups 1 and 3. Every lossless image is byte-identical. Group 2 has baseline latency outliers and remains reported below without using its inflated gains as the headline.

## Modifications

- Extend the T=1 Hopper eligibility guard to **TP2 / SP1 / hidden size 5120 / SwiGLU**. Preserve the older dense-MLP Super exclusion, single-GPU policy and compilation guards.
- Reuse the existing rounded BF16 QKNorm + RoPE + KV-pack implementation and once-per-request rounded rotary cache. No kernel arithmetic or attention backend changes.
- Keep model-level tests for the Hopper TP2 eligibility boundary and reuse the existing shared QK/RoPE kernel tests. Update fusion coverage documentation.

This extends the rounded T1 path in #34932 and the Hopper Nano eligibility work in #36571. The older dense Super regression is still excluded. Our Edge PR #40386 addresses a separate hidden-2048 ReLU² shape. [Source/prior-art review](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2bb5c040ec3d45b665347d923a67a9a25f90e86e/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-super-t2i-hopper-qk-pack/source-review.md).

## Benchmark

`nvidia/Cosmos3-Super-Text2Image@daf3d374804be4c512c2135568a7cb95d4341d79`, **2× H200**, TP2/SP1, native SGLang backend, BF16, `quality=lossless`, manual performance mode, resident DiT/VAE, no torch.compile. Both arms use the same guardrail setting and source-independent pinned checkpoint cache.

**1024×1024**, one image, 35 sampling steps, CFG4, seed42. Prompt: `A warehouse robot folds a blue cloth on a clean workbench.` Same-shape request warmup.

Baseline `80da4432d085ed4d6166ef643d9fd2b829dbb0c5`; measured/PR candidate `1a7e397700ad6f6d7c1bb5af719411c9937bec1f`. Torch2.13.0+cu130, Triton3.7.1, CUDA13.0, driver595.71.05. [Complete environment](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2bb5c040ec3d45b665347d923a67a9a25f90e86e/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-super-t2i-hopper-qk-pack/environment.json).

Fresh native CLI processes on the same assigned idle GPUs, A–B–B–A per group. Seconds; percentages compare arithmetic means:

| Group | Worker E2E | Denoise | Client E2E including PNG save |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| r1 | 4.2976 → 3.9802 (7.38%) | 4.2281 → 3.9058 (7.62%) | 4.7150 → 4.4100 (6.47%) |
| r2 (baseline outliers) | 4.8191 → 3.9648 (17.73%) | 4.7489 → 3.8908 (18.07%) | 6.2950 → 4.3950 (30.18%) |
| r3 | 4.3502 → 3.9669 (8.81%) | 4.2788 → 3.8947 (8.98%) | 4.8150 → 4.4800 (6.96%) |

Group 2 baseline A1/A2 are slower than group 1, including a 7.28 s client observation. Group 3 was added after observing that variability. No measurements were removed and no outlier-adjusted average is used.

<details><summary>All 12 unprofiled native measurements</summary>

| Group | Arm | Worker E2E | Denoise | Client incl. save | Peak reserved GiB |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| r1 | A1 | 4.2972 | 4.2273 | 4.70 | 69.06836 |
| r1 | B1 | 3.9720 | 3.8972 | 4.45 | 69.06836 |
| r1 | B2 | 3.9884 | 3.9144 | 4.37 | 69.06836 |
| r1 | A2 | 4.2980 | 4.2289 | 4.73 | 69.06836 |
| r2 | A1 | 4.9128 | 4.8438 | 5.31 | 69.06836 |
| r2 | B1 | 3.9612 | 3.8873 | 4.40 | 69.06836 |
| r2 | B2 | 3.9684 | 3.8944 | 4.39 | 69.06836 |
| r2 | A2 | 4.7254 | 4.6540 | 7.28 | 69.06836 |
| r3 | A1 | 4.2979 | 4.2281 | 4.76 | 69.06836 |
| r3 | B1 | 3.9663 | 3.8941 | 4.55 | 69.06836 |
| r3 | B2 | 3.9675 | 3.8953 | 4.41 | 69.06836 |
| r3 | A2 | 4.4026 | 4.3296 | 4.87 | 69.06836 |

</details>

Worker E2E is the native perf-dump stage duration before output saving, excluding loading and warmup. Client E2E is the native request/output-save timer, logged to 0.01 s. Peak memory is unchanged at 69.06836 GiB per worker. Profile/export timings are excluded. [All raw logs, perf dumps, source SHAs and presets](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2bb5c040ec3d45b665347d923a67a9a25f90e86e/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-super-t2i-hopper-qk-pack/raw), [complete audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2bb5c040ec3d45b665347d923a67a9a25f90e86e/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-super-t2i-hopper-qk-pack/final-evidence.json).

## Profile and kernel benchmark

Paired native three-step profiler requests, rank 0. Each slice selects the third complete model forward by **CUDA launch correlation**. The actual trace contains eight model calls; no assumed CFG call count is used. QK/RoPE scopes and the two UND-prefix cats are disjoint and matched by native tensor shape.

| Arm | Native model calls in trace | Kernels in selected forward | QK/RoPE scopes | Separate KV cat scopes | Kernels in QK/RoPE + pack chain | Chain GPU ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| baseline | 8 | 2133 | 64 | 128 | 1472 | 6.189829 |
| candidate | 8 | 725 | 64 | 0 | 64 | 0.747231 |

Cumulative device times are diagnostic. TP collective timings vary under profiling; total profile duration is not treated as the end-to-end gain. The three-table analyzer's generic routed-MoE/quantization suggestions do not apply to these dense BF16 GEN/UND pathways, and FlashAttention is attention. Existing packed QKV, residual-add/RMSNorm and SwiGLU remain existing optimizations. [Original/sliced traces, launch ownership and triage](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2bb5c040ec3d45b665347d923a67a9a25f90e86e/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-super-t2i-hopper-qk-pack/profiles).

Whole native QK-normalization/RoPE/KV-prefix-pack chain, **B1 / Q32 / KV4 / D128 / prefix23**, median microseconds over 40 samples after 10 warmups. Both paths use normal output allocation; request-owned QKV is restored before each timer because fusion mutates Q.

| GEN tokens | Timer mode | Native split µs | Fused µs | Speedup |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1024 | Eager CUDA events | 196.256 | 47.312 | 4.148× |
| 1024 | Standalone CUDA Graph | 98.592 | 14.656 | 6.727× |
| 4096 | Eager CUDA events | 311.488 | 56.576 | 5.506× |
| 4096 | Standalone CUDA Graph | 285.248 | 41.200 | 6.923× |

[Raw marker output](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2bb5c040ec3d45b665347d923a67a9a25f90e86e/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-super-t2i-hopper-qk-pack/validation-logs/cosmos3-super-final-marker.log). Standalone kernel Graph timing does **not** establish model BCG support.

## Output comparison

All **19 valid lossless outputs**, including admission, prototype, repeated measurements and profiles, are byte-identical. Independent pixel comparison verifies 1024×1024 RGB, SSIM1 and PSNR∞. SHA256: `cfd2735b1e5d3b64a888ccc631f48d173e95c32857e8cbebd9e80fde3bc90d5e`.

The actual baseline/candidate image grid was visually reviewed; the second row contains the separate high-quality checks.

![Baseline and candidate, lossless and high](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2bb5c040ec3d45b665347d923a67a9a25f90e86e/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-super-t2i-hopper-qk-pack/output-comparison/image-comparison.png)

[Original baseline PNG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2bb5c040ec3d45b665347d923a67a9a25f90e86e/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-super-t2i-hopper-qk-pack/baseline.png) · [Original candidate PNG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2bb5c040ec3d45b665347d923a67a9a25f90e86e/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-super-t2i-hopper-qk-pack/candidate.png) · [Baseline high PNG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2bb5c040ec3d45b665347d923a67a9a25f90e86e/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-super-t2i-hopper-qk-pack/baseline-high.png) · [Candidate high PNG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2bb5c040ec3d45b665347d923a67a9a25f90e86e/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-super-t2i-hopper-qk-pack/candidate-high.png).

| Request | Applicability | Comparison against lossless |
| --- | --- | --- |
| baseline-bcg-probe | BCG disabled; eager fallback excluded | SSIM 1 / PSNR ∞ (exact) |
| final-baseline-high-bcg | BCG disabled; eager fallback excluded | SSIM 1 / PSNR ∞ (exact) |
| final-baseline-high-eager | eager | SSIM 1 / PSNR ∞ (exact) |
| final-candidate-high-bcg | BCG disabled; eager fallback excluded | SSIM 1 / PSNR ∞ (exact) |
| final-candidate-high-eager | eager | SSIM 1 / PSNR ∞ (exact) |
| final-candidate-lossless-bcg | BCG disabled; eager fallback excluded | SSIM 1 / PSNR ∞ (exact) |

Native BCG requests explicitly report `[Diffusion BCG] disabled`; their saved eager fallback images are correctness artifacts only. This PR makes an eager performance claim. High-mode baseline/candidate PNGs are byte-identical and are excluded from lossless performance measurements.

## Validation and reproduction

**Validation scope:** The test counts, logs and GPU measurements below are historical results from the recorded benchmark revisions, before test cleanup. The current diff retains the Hopper TP2 model eligibility tests, alongside the pre-existing shared kernel tests. This cleanup does not change runtime code or claim a new GPU measurement.

- **137 Cosmos model tests + 50 subtests passed**, including precise Hopper TP2 eligibility and negative compile/SP/TP/dense-shape cases.
- **5 CUDA tests passed**: existing KV-pack coverage plus three native Super GQA cases, exact Q/K/V, unchanged source K/V and prefix tensors, and graph replay after changing QKV/prefix/norm weights. H200 validation; no untested hardware claim. [Logs](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2bb5c040ec3d45b665347d923a67a9a25f90e86e/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-super-t2i-hopper-qk-pack/validation-logs).
- [Changed-file pre-commit/registration checks](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2bb5c040ec3d45b665347d923a67a9a25f90e86e/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-super-t2i-hopper-qk-pack/final-precommit.log), [Mintlify build](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2bb5c040ec3d45b665347d923a67a9a25f90e86e/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-super-t2i-hopper-qk-pack/mint-validate.log) and [broken-link validation](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2bb5c040ec3d45b665347d923a67a9a25f90e86e/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-super-t2i-hopper-qk-pack/mint-links.log) passed.
- The first offline admission failed because seven README assets were omitted. Completing the same pinned snapshot resolved it; the failed record remains in the evidence.
- Campaign-owned checkpoint files were deleted after the final audit; **zero residual files, weights or bytes**. [Cleanup record](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2bb5c040ec3d45b665347d923a67a9a25f90e86e/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-super-t2i-hopper-qk-pack/cache-cleanup.json).

Run both clean revisions with the same checkpoint and settings:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 SGLANG_DISABLE_COSMOS3_GUARDRAILS=1 \
SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1 FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \
sglang generate --backend sglang \
  --model-path nvidia/Cosmos3-Super-Text2Image \

  --enable-torch-compile=false --performance-mode manual --quality lossless \
  --dit-cpu-offload=false --dit-layerwise-offload=false --vae-cpu-offload=false \
  --width 1024 --height 1024 --num-frames 1 --num-inference-steps 35 \
  --guidance-scale 4 --seed 42 \

  --warmup-mode request --warmup-resolutions 1024x1024 --warmup-num-frames 1 \
  --save-output --perf-dump-path perf.json --output-path outputs --output-file-name sample
```

Use `--profile --num-profiled-timesteps 3` only for separate diagnostics. The exact runner pins the owned HF cache to the recorded revision and checks native backend selection. [Reproduction/audit scripts](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2bb5c040ec3d45b665347d923a67a9a25f90e86e/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-super-t2i-hopper-qk-pack/scripts), [SHA256 manifest](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2bb5c040ec3d45b665347d923a67a9a25f90e86e/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-super-t2i-hopper-qk-pack/SHA256SUMS.json).

title: [diffusion] Fuse lossless Klein packed QK RMSNorm and RoPE on Hopper
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

Fuse the packed single-stream Q/K copies, RMSNorm and interleaved RoPE in FLUX.2 Klein Base4B on Hopper. The native profile identifies this remaining split chain after the existing AdaLN and SwiGLU fusions.

On **1× H200**, native eager **1024×1024 / 50 steps / BF16 / lossless**, the two fixed full-request-warmed ABBA groups reduce worker E2E by **2.53–2.60%** and client E2E including PNG saving by **2.43–3.41%**. Every valid lossless PNG is byte-identical. Initial one-step-warmup groups, including slower candidate observations, remain reported below.

## Modifications

- Add a Triton kernel that reads strided Q/K directly from the packed QKV/MLP projection and writes contiguous normalized/rotated Q/K. Adjacent V/MLP values are untouched.
- Preserve the native tiled RMSNorm reduction and its BF16 output rounding, followed by FlashInfer's interleaved RoPE cosine-FMA ordering. Explicit sign-bit negation preserves negative zero.
- Keep rotary pairs in registers: the initial gather implementation used 90 registers/thread; the NCU-driven pair layout uses 34, with no spills.
- Scope dispatch to Hopper, BF16, 24 heads ×128, supported dense outer strides, FP32 rotary cache and the actual native RMSNorm dispatch. Verify each new signature outside graph capture; mismatch/exception disables the path. Other layouts/devices, deterministic/native norm dispatch, compilation and unverified capture retain the original shared helper. The existing `SGLANG_ENABLE_FUSED_QKNORM_ROPE=0` switch is respected.
- Keep two focused tests for packed-input exactness, unchanged V/MLP storage, signed zeros and changed-input/weight/cache graph replay; document the numerical and hardware contract.

This follows the guarded lossless approach in #34616 and the packed-input handling in #34617. Those existing fusions are already in the baseline. #37112 targets a different Blackwell D6144 gated-residual chain. [Source and prior-art review](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/75e46a28aa3aa2d8a8fccd2e9ba006dbb00abc53/diffusion-prs/flux2-klein-base4b-strided-qk-rope-h200/klein-qk-source-review.md).

## End-to-end benchmark

Model `black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-base-4B@a3b4f4849157f664bdbc776fd7453c2783562f4d`. **1× H200, TP1/SP1**, resident transformer/text encoder/VAE, manual performance mode, native SGLang backend, BF16, `quality=lossless`, no torch.compile. **1024×1024**, one image, **50 steps, CFG4, seed42**. Prompt: `A futuristic cyberpunk city at night, neon lights reflecting on wet streets`.

Baseline `80da4432d085ed4d6166ef643d9fd2b829dbb0c5`; final candidate `a97bdd428b27aa550b491e7f02256af336e7ab37`. Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, CUDA 13.0, driver 595.71.05. [Environment](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/75e46a28aa3aa2d8a8fccd2e9ba006dbb00abc53/diffusion-prs/flux2-klein-base4b-strided-qk-rope-h200/environment.json).

Fresh processes on the same idle assigned GPU, fixed A–B–B–A order in each group. Seconds; percentages are latency reductions calculated from arithmetic means:

| Version / group | Worker E2E | Denoise | Client E2E incl. PNG save |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| v2 / 1 | 6.1680 → 6.1581 (+0.16%) | 6.0334 → 6.0212 (+0.20%) | 6.7850 → 6.9000 (-1.69%) |
| v2 / 2 | 6.1730 → 6.0580 (+1.86%) | 6.0394 → 5.9235 (+1.92%) | 6.3800 → 6.2650 (+1.80%) |
| v3 / 1 | 6.1719 → 6.0805 (+1.48%) | 6.0372 → 5.9452 (+1.52%) | 6.3750 → 6.8300 (-7.14%) |
| v3 / 2 | 6.1696 → 6.0149 (+2.51%) | 6.0374 → 5.8810 (+2.59%) | 6.3700 → 6.2550 (+1.81%) |
| fullwarm / 1 | 6.1856 → 6.0289 (+2.53%) | 6.0528 → 5.8931 (+2.64%) | 6.3900 → 6.2350 (+2.43%) |
| fullwarm / 2 | 6.1879 → 6.0269 (+2.60%) | 6.0544 → 5.8899 (+2.72%) | 6.4550 → 6.2350 (+3.41%) |

`v2` is the signed-zero-correct gather prototype; `v3` is the final pair kernel with default **1-step request warmup**. The first v3 group includes a **7.45 s candidate client** observation and does not establish a stable win. title: [unified-memory] Admit EAGLE/EAGLE3 onto fused draft KV, on mamba-MHA and MLA hosts
author: caihuali95
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42753
* #40492
* __->__ #40491
* #37628
* #37627

## Motivation

#37628 puts a draft model's K/V rows inside the target's slot entries, so one slot
id addresses both, and leaves the mechanism unreachable on purpose: the admission
gate reads `speculative_algorithm in (None, "DSPARK")`, and DSPARK is not an
EAGLE-family algorithm.

**This PR turns it on for EAGLE and EAGLE3, and provisions the region on the host
kinds those drafts actually run on.** That is the first configuration in which a
real drafter's KV lives inside the target's pages, and therefore the first in which
a real drafter's accept length is evidence that the addressing is right.

## Modifications

**Admission.** The gate admits `EAGLE` and `EAGLE3` alongside `DSPARK` on a unified
target — hybrid-SWA or a mamba hybrid — because that is where the draft's KV can
ride inside the full-attention page envelope. The target verifies on its own pages,
so its backend set follows the host kind: the MLA verify family on an MLA host, the
translated MHA rails (triton, flashinfer, fa3) otherwise. The draft, named or
inherited from the target, must be on the MHA rails on every host: a fused draft's
region holds dense K/V rows. `--enable-hierarchical-cache` is refused with an
EAGLE draft (it would build a draft host pool off a device pool that has no
transfer surface of its own), as is host-pool retraction.

**Host kinds.** The region is provisioned on **mamba-MHA** hosts and carried in
**MLA** pages; the tri-pool host takes the placement too. A draft whose attention
is not MHA declines fusion by its architecture, and the draft side checks the built
model before binding: a recurrent or linear-attention module in it fails the bind,
since the fused arm gives such layers no state pool.

**Fixes that a private-pool draft never triggers.**

- *Write rail on hand-built draft-extend views.* The draft-extend capture runners
  and the frozen-KV MTP worker build their `ForwardBatch` views by hand.
  `fill_capture_write_loc` translates the pre-translate loc
  (`out_cache_loc_virtual`) into the backend's capture buffer, so a view that drops
  it, or passes None, sends every draft-extend write to the page-0 sink. The rail
  travels with the frozen `out_cache_loc` because `replay` takes no `ForwardBatch`.
- *Require an swa sub-pool before reading the swa stream.* The Triton backend asked
  the translator for the sliding-window read stream whenever reads were translated,
  but the swa v2p table exists only when the **pool** has an swa side. A model can
  declare a sliding window while its unified pool is full+mamba — Qwen3.5 does — and
  capturing the target-verify graph then failed. The predicate now conjoins the pool
  check, matching flashinfer's `use_swa_source`.
- *Build the fused draft pool on the host's KV dtype.* fp8 rows are stored as
  uint8, so the region records the KV dtype its rows hold next to their storage
  dtype. The draft pool is built on the KV dtype, so an fp8 host's draft writes
  cast to fp8 and store its bytes, not an integer cast into uint8, and the bind
  compares KV dtypes, so an e5m2 draft cannot bind an e4m3 region.
- *Gate the unified fast path to the target worker.* The configurator's fast path
  keyed on `req_to_token_pool is None`, a proxy for "this is the target worker" that
  a compact-window DFLASH draft breaks; it now identifies by role.

## Scope: full-attention draft KV only

The fused region is dense and full-attention, as in #37628. A draft that declines
fusion (asymmetric rows, sliding-window or recurrent layers of its own, misaligned
rows, a different explicit KV dtype, a non-MHA architecture, DCP, or HiCache) is
refused at boot with the reason it declined, on every host kind; `main` refuses
EAGLE under unified memory altogether. A private draft pool cannot be budgeted
there:

- a **mamba or tri-pool** host hands the unified buffer the whole profiled KV
  budget, so a private pool sized to the virtual id span would be allocated on top
  of it;
- a **hybrid-SWA** host's solve prices a private draft at the target's per-token
  size, not at the draft's own heads, head_dim and KV dtype, so an EAGLE3 draft
  with twice the target's head_dim, or a bf16 draft over an fp8 host, would be
  charged half its rows.

## Accuracy Tests

**B200 (SM100), this head.** Qwen3.5-0.8B with its MTP head as an EAGLE draft
(3 steps, topk 1, 4 draft tokens — the cookbook's MTP settings), path-less, so the
draft fuses into the mamba-MHA host's pages
(`fused draft region in 'full': 1 lane x 2 kv heads x 256/256 head_dim = 2048
B/token`). GSM8K at n=200 and the server's mean accept length:

| configuration | GSM8K | accept length |
|---|---|---|
| main, no unified memory, flashinfer | 0.330 | 3.35 |
| this head, no unified memory, flashinfer | 0.330 | 3.34 |
| this head, unified, flashinfer | 0.335 | 3.33 |
| this head, unified, triton | 0.320 | 3.34 |
| this head, unified, flashinfer, `--page-size 64` | 0.335 | 3.35 |

gpt-oss-20b with the cookbook's EAGLE3 draft (`zhuyksir/EAGLE3-gpt-oss-20b-bf16`,
3 steps, topk 1, 4 draft tokens) on Triton, `--context-length 4096` to match the
draft's config — a hybrid-SWA host, where the draft fuses into the full sub-pool
(`1 lane x 8 kv heads x 128/128 head_dim = 4096 B/token`):

| configuration | GSM8K | accept length |
|---|---|---|
| this head, no unified memory | 0.560 | 1.28 |
| this head, unified | 0.585 | 1.28 |
| this head, unified, `--page-size 64` | 0.550 / 0.565 | 1.28 / 1.27 |

(This draft accepts little on any build; the parity is the result. At
`--page-size 64` the idle pool check reports an over-count after the run, with or
without unified memory and on `main` too — not something this stack changes.)

Accept length is the check that matters: a KV-addressing mistake inside a fused
region does not crash and does not slow anything down — the draft reads the wrong
slots, the target rejects its proposals, and acceptance falls toward 1.0. It is
unchanged with the draft's KV inside the target's pages. With
`--speculative-draft-kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` on the same host the draft declines
fusion and the server refuses to start, naming the reason.

**B200, greedy parity and memory, this head.** Temperature 0, 24 ShareGPT prompts ×
128 tokens, one request at a time, token ids and logprobs compared with `main`'s
static pool. Every arm below is identical to it (max |Δlogprob| 0):

| target + draft | host | arms | accept length | `max_total_num_tokens` static / fused |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-4B + its MTP head, flashinfer | mamba-MHA | static; unified, fused; cuda graphs on and off | 3.48 / 3.49 | 1,592,686 / 1,415,720 |
| same, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` | mamba-MHA | static; unified, fused | 3.47 / 3.48 | 3,185,372 / 2,831,441 |
| gpt-oss-20b + EAGLE3, triton | hybrid-SWA | static; unified, fused; page size 1 and 64; graphs on and off | 1.21 / 1.21 | 1,692,150 / 1,620,448 |

The fused arms hold fewer tokens because they price the draft exactly and stay
within the budget. `main`'s static pool does not: it leaves a path-less MTP draft
pool (6.1 GiB here) out of the budget, and it prices the EAGLE3 draft (head_dim
128) at the target's per-layer size (head_dim 64), about 3.2 GiB short here.

**H20 (SM90), the pre-rebase revision of this PR.** GSM8K at n=200,
`--enable-unified-memory` against the same build without it — **42 matched pairs,
median +0.50 pt, sd 3.00 pt**; the three pairs more than 2.9 pt below baseline are
all gpt-oss-20b, whose baseline alone spans 10.0 pt in that run (excluding it: 30
pairs, median +0.50 pt, worst −1.0 pt). Accept length, unified against the same
configuration without it:

| target | algorithm | backends | baseline | unified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B | NEXTN | fa3 / flashinfer / triton | 3.49–3.54 | 3.49–3.54 |
| gpt-oss-20b | EAGLE | fa3 / triton | 4.00 | 4.00 |

(The gpt-oss EAGLE draft is degenerate independently of this change and reads 4.00
on both builds.)

## Speed Tests and Profiling

H20, the pre-rebase revision: median inter-token latency, unified against the same
build without it across the fused-draft matrix — **84 matched pairs, median
+1.08%**. The largest single reading, +35.1% on gpt-oss EAGLE with fa3 (5.30 →
6.82 ms) on the balanced workload, is confined to that configuration: on Triton the
same moves +1.5%, and its skewed workload +0.9%.

B200, this head: median inter-token latency, fused against the static pool on the
same build, arms interleaved on one GPU.

| configuration | one request in flight | 32 concurrent |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-4B, spec-off (the unified pool alone) | 2.53 vs 2.50 ms | 3.58 vs 3.55 ms |
| Qwen3.5-4B, MTP, flashinfer | 1.27 vs 1.24 ms | 2.29 vs 2.29 ms |
| gpt-oss-20b, EAGLE3, triton | 4.03 vs 4.14 ms | 11.23 vs 11.33 ms |

The static pool against `main`, the same configurations, measured at the top of
the stack (its static path matches this head's): MTP 1.24 vs 1.24 ms, EAGLE3 4.13
vs 4.14 ms with one request in flight; at 32 concurrent the arms move within the
run-order effect on this box (the arm of a pair that runs first gains about 2%).

## Notes for reviewers

**DFLASH and DSPARK are still refused a fused region here**; they arrive in #40492.

**fa3 on Hopper (H200), this head and the stack's top.** gpt-oss-20b with EAGLE3
on fa3, the fused draft against the static pool on the same build, arms interleaved
on one GPU: mean TPOT 3.71 vs 3.69 ms with one request in flight, 11.03 vs 10.48 ms
at 32 concurrent (+5%). Greedy output is identical, accept length 1.204 on both, and
this head runs the same configuration at 3.74 / 11.10 ms. The +35.1% H20 reading
does not reproduce. The gap at 32 concurrent is not profiled yet; under unified
memory fa3 rebuilds its draft-extend metadata out of graph on every replay (6–8
small launches instead of one in-graph launch) and builds one translated table per
multi-step draft step.

**Not yet validated end to end:** an MLA host with a fused draft (no MLA EAGLE
checkpoint exists), the trtllm_mla / cutedsl_mla / tokenspeed_mla verify family
with EAGLE on SM100, and `--dcp-size > 1`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [unified-memory] Admit DFLASH and DSPARK with fused draft KV
author: caihuali95
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42753
* __->__ #40492
* #40491
* #37628
* #37627

## Motivation

#37628 builds the fused draft KV mechanism; #40491 admits EAGLE and EAGLE3 onto it.
Two algorithms are still refused a fused region: **DFLASH** (fused block draft) and
**DSPARK** (chain draft). DSPARK already runs on the unified pool, but with a KV
pool of its own; DFLASH is refused outright.

**This PR admits both**, so every speculative algorithm the unified pool supports
can put its draft KV inside the target's pages when the draft's geometry, backend
and deployment allow.

DFLASH is the interesting one. Its compact-window mode keeps a private
`req -> token` table whose entries are target virtual ids, so it narrows **which**
pages the draft reads while the KV itself stays fused in the target's pages. That
combination — a private read table over a shared, fused write space — is what the
first commit here has to make correct.

## Modifications

**1. Translate the target-hidden draft-KV writes.** Both the DFLASH worker and the
DSPARK injector write draft KV through direct `KVCache` calls, and the locs they
are handed are **virtual**: the callers read them off the target's `req_to_token`
after verify, or off the `ScheduleBatch` at prefill, and the write rebind leaves
those aliases virtual. Each writer now translates once at the single choke point
every call passes through, into a fresh tensor that its 2-D view reshapes — the
callers keep using their virtual copies afterwards, and the post-verify 2-D loc is
a persistent buffer that the compact `req_to_token` rebuild re-reads as virtual
ids. This is identity on a plain pool, so the private-draft path is untouched; a
fused draft gets the target's physical ids instead of virtual ones.

**2. Admit DFLASH and DSPARK with fused draft KV.** The gate admits `DFLASH`, with
the target on the translated MHA rails (triton, fa3, flashinfer). The placement
takes its layer count from the aux record's `draft_kv_num_layers`, which the
DFLASH-family resolver now fills as the EAGLE one does, and pins one depth block (a
DFLASH-family draft config inherits the target's NEXTN count), and the draft side
treats the family as fusion-capable. The fused arm builds the draft's
`req_to_token` when it arrives as None, which lets compact-window DFLASH keep its
private compact table while the KV stays fused. The hand-built draft
`ForwardBatch`es rebind their write loc through the translator explicitly, and
host-pool retraction stays refused with an EAGLE draft, as in #40491.

**3. Decline fusion where the fused region would be read wrong.** Before DSPARK
could fuse, its private pool kept its translator a passthrough, so the draft's
backend, DCP and host pools needed no audit. `_fused_draft_decision` now keeps a
draft on its private pool, logging the reason, when:

- *the draft runs off the translated MHA rails* (triton, flashinfer, fa3, one
  `TRANSLATED_MHA_RAILS` constant shared with the gate). A DFLASH or DSPARK draft's
  backend comes from `build_draft_tp_worker`'s own resolver, now the public
  `resolve_draft_worker_attention_backend`: the published
  `--speculative-draft-attention-backend`, which a model hook may declare, else the
  target's prefill backend or the platform default. An EAGLE draft runs the
  published draft backend, else the target's pair. This is what keeps the Kimi-Linear / Kimi-K3
  + DSPARK default on SM100 private: its hook declares `trtllm_mha`, whose graph
  replay refills the page table from the previous replay's lengths and whose eager
  table is not widened by the draft block.
- *`--dcp-size > 1`.* Each rank's host rows hold only its share of the widened id
  space, while the replicated draft reads every token.
- *HiCache or host-pool decode retraction.* Each builds the draft's host pool off
  a device pool of its own, which a fused draft does not have. The external cache
  linker would too; the gate refuses it on the unified pool. Both stay refused
  outright with an EAGLE draft, as in #40491.
- *an explicit draft KV dtype differs from the host's.* It is resolved the way the
  draft runner resolves it, so a mismatch declines here instead of failing the
  bind.

An EAGLE draft that declines is refused at boot rather than kept private, on every
unified host (#40491).

**4. Keep the linear-chain assert in one place.** `handle_unified_memory_pool`
refuses tree-shaped drafting for every admitted algorithm in one assert; the EAGLE
and DSPARK branches repeated it, and the copies go. The DSPARK branch's `if` stays,
since it also guards that branch's backend audit.

## Scope: full-attention draft KV only

The fused region is dense and full-attention, as in #37628. A draft that declines
fusion — for its geometry (asymmetric rows, sliding-window-routed or recurrent
layers of its own, misaligned rows, a non-MHA architecture), its KV dtype, its
backend, DCP, or a host-pool-backed cache — behaves by host kind:

- on a **hybrid-SWA** host a declined DFLASH or DSPARK draft binds a private pool
  over the unified virtual id space, which the hybrid-SWA solve prices;
- on a **mamba or tri-pool** host, which hands the unified buffer the whole KV
  budget, a declined EAGLE or DFLASH draft is refused at boot with the reason, rather
  than overcommitting the GPU; a declined DSPARK draft keeps its private pool there,
  unpriced, as on `main`.

## Accuracy Tests

**B200 (SM100), this head.** Greedy decoding — temperature 0, 24 ShareGPT prompts ×
128 tokens, one request at a time — compared token by token, with logprobs. Every
arm below is identical to its reference (max |Δlogprob| 0).

Qwen3.5-4B (a mamba-MHA host) with `z-lab/Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash` (block size 16),
flashinfer, `--mem-fraction-static 0.5`. The draft fuses into the host's pages
(`6 lanes x 8 kv heads x 128/128 head_dim = 24576 B/token`):

| arm | identical to | accept length | `max_total_num_tokens` | ITL, 1 / 32 in flight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main`, static | — | 7.15 | 775,733 | 0.38 / 2.05 ms |
| this head, static | `main`, static | 7.12 | 775,733 | 0.38 / 2.04 ms |
| this head, unified, fused | `main`, static | 7.16 | 775,733 | 0.40 / 1.99 ms |
| this head, unified, fused, `--speculative-draft-window-size 512` | `main`, static | 5.69 (static 5.66) | 775,733 | 0.51 / 2.13 ms |
| this head, unified, fused, `--page-size 64` | static at page size 64 | 7.04 (static 7.09) | 775,680 | 0.39 / 2.03 ms |
| this head, unified, fused, cuda graphs off | static, graphs off | — | — | — |

The window-512 row is compact-window DFLASH: a private `req -> token` table over
the fused KV. With `--speculative-draft-kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` the draft declines
fusion on its dtype and, on this mamba host, the server refuses to start, naming
that reason.

Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct, TP2, target on trtllm_mla, DSPARK with a dummy draft
(accept length 1.00 by construction, so this checks verify correctness, not
acceptance). Every arm is identical to `main`'s static pool:

| arm | draft KV | `--mem-fraction-static` | `max_total_num_tokens` | GPU memory / rank (GiB) | ITL, 1 / 32 in flight |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main`, unified, `trtllm_mha` draft (the Kimi hook's default) | private | 0.45 | 970,112 | 126.4 | 4.68 / 13.20 ms |
| this head, same | private: declined, off the rails | 0.45 | 970,112 | 126.3 | 4.68 / 13.20 ms |
| `main`, unified, flashinfer draft | private | 0.45 | 970,112 | 127.8 | 5.29 / 13.57 ms |
| this head, same | fused, 12,288 B/token | 0.45 | 970,112 | 90.8 | 5.35 / 13.65 ms |
| this head, no unified memory, flashinfer draft | private | 0.6 | 2,112,640 | | 5.26 / 13.55 ms |
| this head, unified, flashinfer draft | fused | 0.6 | 2,112,640 | | 5.37 / 13.66 ms |
| `main` / this head, no unified memory | private | 0.6 | 2,112,640 | | 4.66 / 13.20 ms |

The Kimi default is unchanged. With a flashinfer draft the fused region replaces a
private pool that, on a mamba host, sits outside the budget — 37 GiB per rank here,
and at `--mem-fraction-static 0.6` it does not fit — and its reads go through the
KV-index translator, which costs 1.1% at one request in flight (0.6% at 32).

**H200 (SM90), a real DSPARK draft.** Qwen3.8-27B with `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark`
on the cookbook's H200 BF16 recipe (fp8 KV, flashinfer), plus
`--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled`: at `--mem-fraction-static 0.85` the default
prefill graph capture runs out of memory on `main` as well. Unified memory with the
fused draft (5 lanes, fp8, 10,240 B/token) against the static pool, interleaved on one
GPU, at the stack's top:

| arm | accept length | TPOT, 1 / 32 in flight | output tok/s, 32 in flight |
|---|---|---|---|
| unified, fused draft | 3.40 | 5.59 / 11.45 ms | 1076 |
| no unified memory | 3.40 | 5.44 / 11.37 ms | 1006 |
| `main`, no unified memory | 3.41 | 5.43 / 11.43 ms | 1001 |

This head's fused arm gives the same output as the stack's top, at 5.56 / 11.41 ms.
Greedy output under unified memory differs from the static pool on this model with or
without speculation, on `main` too: without speculation 6 of 25 prompts identical, the
first token's logprob within 0.025. That is the unified pool on Qwen3.8, not the fused
draft; the static pool matches `main`'s exactly.

**H20 (SM90), the pre-rebase revision of this PR.** GSM8K at n=200, unified against
the same build without it: **60 matched pairs, median +0.00 pt, sd 2.81 pt**; eight
of the nine pairs more than 2.9 pt below baseline are gpt-oss-20b, whose baseline
alone spans 8.5 pt (excluding it: 40 pairs, median +0.00 pt, sd 1.26). Accept
length, unified against the same configuration without it:

| target | algorithm | backends | baseline | unified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B | DFLASH | fa3 / flashinfer / triton | 6.72–7.22 | 6.94–7.36 |
| Qwen3.5-9B | DFLASH compact | fa3 / triton | 6.66–7.31 | 6.72–7.13 |
| Qwen3.5-9B | NEXTN | fa3 / flashinfer / triton | 3.49–3.54 | 3.49–3.54 |
| gpt-oss-20b | DFLASH | fa3 / triton | 5.58–8.00 | 5.59–8.00 |
| gpt-oss-20b | DFLASH compact | fa3 / triton | 5.55–8.00 | 5.55–8.00 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

H20, the pre-rebase revision: median inter-token latency, unified against the same
build without it — fused-draft matrix, every admitted drafter: 120 matched pairs,
**median +0.53%**; default serving configuration, speculation off: 20 pairs,
**median +0.42%**, the unified pool's standing overhead.

B200, this head: the tables above; spec-off on Qwen3.5-4B, the unified pool alone
costs 2.53 vs 2.50 ms with one request in flight, the same on `main`.

## Notes for reviewers

**`NGRAM` and `speculative_eagle_topk > 1` stay refused.** Both need a per-token
`move_kv_cache` on the unified pool; the existing one moves whole page envelopes.

**A `trtllm_mha` draft stays on its private pool.** Fusing the Kimi default needs
trtllm_mha's draft paths — graph replay and the eager draft-block table — to read
through the translator; until then it keeps `main`'s layout.

**Not yet validated end to end:** a real (non-dummy) DSPARK draft on SM100,
cutedsl_mla / tokenspeed_mla, and `--dcp-size > 1`. Under DCP the decline fires at
boot (`fused draft KV disabled: --dcp-size 2 shards the host's rows ...`), but this
Kimi configuration does not serve speculative decoding under DCP on trtllm_mla with
or without this stack.

- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
