title: [Diffusion] Fuse Joy Image Edit QKV concatenation and avoid QK copies
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

Reduce data movement around Joy Image Edit's joint attention: reuse the existing out-of-place QK-Norm/RoPE operation to avoid copying packed image Q/K, then concatenate image/text Q/K/V with one pure-copy kernel.

On **2× H200**, native eager **1024×1024 / 40 steps / BF16 / lossless**, two fixed ABBA groups of persistent native generators using **native client-side PNG saving (`return_file_paths_only=False`)** reduce steady-state worker E2E by **3.16–3.27%** and client E2E including pixel transport and PNG saving by **3.13–3.25%**. All valid lossless images are byte-identical. The default worker-save path has allocator-release long tails and its repeated saved-client results did **not** qualify; no reliable default-path client speedup is claimed. All earlier measurements are retained below.

## Modifications

- Reuse the existing CUDA out-of-place QK-Norm/RoPE operation on large Hopper BF16 image Q/K with 32 heads ×128 and the native packed layout. This preserves the original arithmetic and contiguous outputs while removing two input copies per block. Packed Q/K/V remain intact, so even a partial-output exception can safely fall back.
- Add a Triton row-copy kernel for image-first Q/K/V concatenation. It accepts different input row/batch strides, including packed V, and writes three disjoint contiguous outputs in one allocation. It performs no floating-point arithmetic.
- Keep both paths behind first-signature bitwise verification. Small shapes, unsupported layouts/devices, compilation, gradients, unverified graph capture, exceptions and mismatches retain native execution. The QK path respects `SGLANG_ENABLE_FUSED_QKNORM_ROPE=0`; the joint-copy path is eligible for CUDA FP16/BF16 tensors of at least 32 MiB.
- Keep two focused joint-copy tests for bit patterns, strided inputs and changed-input graph replay, and document the dispatch contract.

The existing BBuf #34616/#34617 lossless guards and packed-input work informed this approach; they are already in the baseline. The existing out-of-place operation comes from #37903 (KevinMi) and is reused without changing its CUDA math. The actual Joy request's text branch has Q/K normalization but no RoPE. [Source/prior-art review](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/joy-qkv-source-review.md).

## End-to-end benchmark

Model `jdopensource/JoyAI-Image-Edit-Diffusers@4b41fb25d961f37668750178ccbb380da326201c`. **2× H200, CFG parallel 2, TP1/SP1**, resident transformer/text encoder/VAE, manual performance mode, native SGLang backend, BF16, `quality=lossless`, no torch.compile. **1024×1024**, one image, **40 steps, CFG4, seed42**, prompt `Make the cat wear a red hat`; [input image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/input.png).

Baseline `80da4432d085ed4d6166ef643d9fd2b829dbb0c5`; combined final candidate `4811f4d52aa2586412f699b3bb84ed184d76250a`. Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, CUDA 13.0, driver 595.71.05. [Environment](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/environment.json).

Same assigned GPUs and fixed A–B–B–A order. Every process uses **40-step same-shape native request warmup on both arms**. The headline client-save protocol uses the existing native `return_file_paths_only=False` API in **both** revisions and adds **one complete generated-and-saved warmup, then five measured saved requests per process**. Two groups contain **40 measured requests and 8 saved warmups**, all retained. Native generation, returned pixel transport, PNG saving and reporting remain inside the client measurement. Earlier worker-save persistent groups use the same repeat count; earlier oneshot groups each measure one saved request per fresh process. Seconds; percentages are latency reductions from arithmetic means:

| Version / group | Worker E2E | Denoise | Client E2E incl. PNG save |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| copy-only v2 / 1 | 14.2898 → 14.0491 (+1.68%) | 13.9068 → 13.6601 (+1.77%) | 14.9100 → 14.2250 (+4.59%) |
| copy-only v2 / 2 | 14.2731 → 14.0404 (+1.63%) | 13.9001 → 13.6513 (+1.79%) | 14.4500 → 14.2200 (+1.59%) |
| copy-only final / 1 | 14.2619 → 14.0580 (+1.43%) | 13.8927 → 13.6549 (+1.71%) | 14.4450 → 14.2500 (+1.35%) |
| copy-only final / 2 | 14.2683 → 14.0339 (+1.64%) | 13.8968 → 13.6559 (+1.73%) | 14.4450 → 14.2100 (+1.63%) |
| combined oneshot / 1 | 14.2650 → 13.8207 (+3.11%) | 13.8929 → 13.4392 (+3.27%) | 14.4500 → 14.0000 (+3.11%) |
| combined oneshot / 2 | 14.2675 → 13.8224 (+3.12%) | 13.8969 → 13.4446 (+3.26%) | 14.4450 → 15.0400 (-4.12%) |
| combined persistent / worker-save / 1 | 14.2230 → 13.7760 (+3.14%) | 13.8775 → 13.4270 (+3.25%) | 14.4440 → 14.3450 (+0.69%) |
| combined persistent / worker-save / 2 | 14.2201 → 13.7764 (+3.12%) | 13.8842 → 13.4232 (+3.32%) | 14.3850 → 14.7050 (-2.22%) |
| combined persistent / client-save / 1 | 14.2094 → 13.7599 (+3.16%) | 13.8752 → 13.4270 (+3.23%) | 14.3980 → 13.9470 (+3.13%) |
| combined persistent / client-save / 2 | 14.2323 → 13.7666 (+3.27%) | 13.8892 → 13.4309 (+3.30%) | 14.4230 → 13.9540 (+3.25%) |

`copy-only v2` is `0cff694f701987ba694954a4cf54257f7c3881e6`; `copy-only final` is `3b00154ddb33ac436906a493c9706ed3855ec918`. The latter adds backend-import guards and documentation, with the same copy kernel. Copy-only final group 1 reaches only about **1.43% worker / 1.35% client** and does not qualify. This prompted the profile-driven removal of the remaining image Q/K copies. Copy-only v2 group 1 contains a **15.36 s baseline client outlier**; its larger client percentage is not the headline. The earlier default one-step-warmup single-request screen improved worker time by about 1.1% and also remains non-qualifying.

Worker E2E is the native stage/perf-dump time before PNG saving. Client E2E is the native request-and-save timer, logged to 0.01s. Both exclude loading/warmup. No profiler request supplies an E2E row. Recorded lossless peak reserved memory: **45.83594, 45.87305 GiB per worker**.

Combined oneshot group 2 has a **16.08 s candidate client outlier despite 13.824 s worker time**, so that client's group does not qualify. Adding a complete saved-request warmup did not remove the issue: the worker-save persistent groups also fail saved-client qualification, including a **16.99 s candidate observation**. Separate instrumented diagnostic worktrees localize a **1.76 s output-rank `empty_cache` delay in baseline**, with PNG saving around 0.16 s and sub-millisecond peak collective/report writing. Candidate's twelve diagnostic requests did not reproduce its earlier long tail; the same cause for those particular earlier observations remains an inference. Startup/shutdown GC is recorded separately. The diagnostic runs are excluded from benchmark qualification.

The final protocol explicitly selects native client-side PNG saving in both arms, retaining pixel data through the worker response. The existing worker condition then does not call request-tail `empty_cache`; the native client saves the same PNG inside its timer. No allocator/GC function is patched, no output work is removed from the timed request, and no generation math changes. This is a supported **different output configuration**, with the default path's failed comparisons disclosed. [Predeclared client-save protocol](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/client-save-protocol.json) · [Earlier persistent protocol](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/persistent-protocol.json) · [Default-path audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/persistent-default-final-evidence.json) · [Tail diagnosis](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/request-tail-diagnostic-final.json).

The persistent driver also measures an unrounded outer wall timer around native `generate` plus the CLI performance dump, including input validation and the saved response. Output hashing and campaign JSON writing occur after this timer:

| Group | Baseline outer saved-client s | Candidate outer saved-client s | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 14.398472 | 13.949222 | 3.12% |
| 2 | 14.423400 | 13.954875 | 3.25% |

## Profile and kernel benchmark

Three-step native profiler requests select the third complete Joy model forward using CUDA launch correlation. These traces use the original worker-save configuration; the generation parameters and measured source revisions match the client-save benchmark, and the forward slice precedes either output transport/save path. Copy scopes are identified by their actual image/text input shapes. The optimized-chain subtotal includes image Q/K copies, image QK-Norm/RoPE and Q/K/V concatenations; unchanged position arange is excluded.

| Arm | Whole-forward kernels | Image Q/K copy kernels | Joint concat kernels | Optimized-chain kernels | Chain GPU ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline | 1268 | 80 | 120 | 240 | 24.047472 |
| candidate | 1108 | 0 | 40 | 80 | 8.776787 |

The **80 text Q/K copies and two unrelated FP32 concatenations remain**. Attention, GEMMs, MLP and modulation math are unchanged. FA3 is attention; the generic analyzer's GEMM/MoE classifications do not apply to every named kernel in this dense BF16 model. [Full/sliced traces and analysis](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/profiles).

Production helper versus the original image QK copy/norm/RoPE + three-cat chain, BF16, 32 heads ×128. Median of 40 CUDA-event samples after 10 warmups, normal output allocations, first-signature verification completed before timing:

| Batch / image tokens / text tokens | Mode | Native µs | Candidate µs | Speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 / 8048 / 1004 | eager | 541.360 | 271.440 | 1.994× |
| 1 / 8048 / 1004 | standalone_graph | 531.408 | 213.648 | 2.487× |
| 1 / 4096 / 512 | eager | 288.880 | 190.192 | 1.519× |
| 1 / 4096 / 512 | standalone_graph | 278.688 | 112.912 | 2.468× |
| 1 / 2048 / 256 | eager | 154.416 | 157.264 | 0.982× |
| 1 / 2048 / 256 | standalone_graph | 145.312 | 145.376 | 1.000× |
| 2 / 257 / 13 | eager | 110.880 | 118.432 | 0.936× |
| 2 / 257 / 13 | standalone_graph | 46.656 | 46.768 | 0.998× |

Smaller shapes retain native operations; their eager rows expose the wrapper/guard overhead and are not claimed faster. Standalone graph is a kernel diagnostic, **not native model BCG**. [Samples](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/outplace-chain-microbench-v1.json) · [Harness](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/scripts/bench-joy-outplace-v1.py).

Focused NCU on the production shape:

| Metric | Original chain | Combined candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Kernels | 7 | 3 |
| GPU duration | 678.560 µs | 229.568 µs |
| DRAM read + write | 855,088,640 B | 671,013,888 B |
| QK-Norm/RoPE duration | 108.512 µs | 118.368 µs |
| QK-Norm/RoPE registers/thread | 32 | 32 |
| Joint concat duration | 398.720 µs, three kernels | 109.152 µs, one kernel |

The out-of-place norm itself is slightly slower; avoiding the two input copies (169.120 µs combined) compensates. Joint-copy L2 throughput is 88.94%, versus 12.18% for the original generic V cat. No measured local-memory spills. Source stalls map to the new Triton loads/stores; the reused CUDA JIT norm lacks usable source-line mapping in this report. PM raw instances are preserved, with no unsupported tail-balance claim. [NCU reports, six-part analysis and limitations](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/ncu/REPORT.md) · [Earlier copy-only NCU](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/ncu-copy-only/REPORT.md).

## Output comparison

All **127 valid lossless PNGs** are byte- and pixel-identical, including profiles and all measured revisions: **SSIM 1, PSNR ∞**. SHA256 `76cfd40eb83feacb1b0292e171b9beb2a8cd7eb7fadc606cb1632e886d960ce6`.

All **5 valid high-mode PNGs** are also byte-identical to lossless and to each other for this request; they are correctness checks, excluded from the lossless timing table.

![Native baseline/candidate lossless and high images](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/output-comparison/image-comparison.png)

[Original baseline PNG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/baseline.png) · [Original candidate PNG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/candidate.png) · [Baseline high](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/baseline-high.png) · [Candidate high](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/candidate-high.png) · [Absolute pixel difference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/output-comparison/lossless-absolute-difference.png).

All **9 native BCG probes** report `[Diffusion BCG] disabled` and no capture. Their saved eager fallback images are independently hashed and excluded from performance claims. This PR improves eager execution and does not add Joy model BCG support.

## Validation and reproduction

**Validation scope:** The test counts, logs and GPU measurements below are historical results from the recorded benchmark revisions, before test cleanup. The current diff retains two joint-copy correctness/replay tests. This cleanup does not change runtime code or claim a new GPU measurement.

- H200: **8 tests + 8 subtests passed**, including production/batch-two shapes, bit patterns, unchanged packed inputs, non-overlapping outputs, changed-input/weight/cache graph replay, native fallback, explicit disable, forced mismatch and partial-output exception. After cleanup, the retained joint-copy tests use the single-GPU CUDA CI lane; the duplicate B200 registration and separate QK test file were removed.
- Changed-file pre-commit, Mintlify build and broken-link checks passed. [Validation logs](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/validation-logs), [pre-commit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/joy-outplace-precommit.log), [build](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/joy-outplace-mint-validate.log), [links](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/joy-outplace-mint-links.log).
- The initial native command used an unsupported CFG-parallel CLI flag; it was corrected before admission. The first profile auditor mistakenly included two unrelated FP32 concatenations in the QKV count; the retry distinguishes dtype and preserves those kernels. Failed logs and the superseded audit waiter's termination are retained. No failed/disabled run is counted as performance.
- The first persistent harness omitted native CLI `sys.argv` bookkeeping and failed before model initialization. Retry1 supplies the same explicit CLI arguments and preserves the original failed log.
- Campaign-owned model weights were deleted after completed output/visual audit: **zero remaining files, weights or bytes**. [Cleanup](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/cache-cleanup.json).

The following native CLI reproduces the workload and the earlier worker-save oneshot measurement. For the headline client-save protocol, use [run-joy-client-save.py](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/scripts/run-joy-client-save.py) and [validate-joy-client-save.py](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/f3100979390a029de41ec5f6aec485a11140783f/diffusion-prs/joy-image-edit-joint-qkv-cat-h200/scripts/validate-joy-client-save.py); they construct the same native CLI arguments and retain a local `DiffGenerator`, calling `generate(sampling_params_kwargs={..., "return_file_paths_only": False, "save_output": True})` for the saved warmup and five measured requests. Both revisions use the same pinned checkpoint and input. To select this output mode in a one-request CLI, pass a JSON config containing `{"return_file_paths_only": false}` with `--config`:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \
SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1 \
sglang generate --backend sglang \

title: [CI] Give the kernel lane a 5090 suite and move kernel-only tests off the general lane
author: hnyls2002
body:
Nine tests under `test/registered/kernels/` register `stage="base-b"`, so they run on every PR, while their 215 siblings use `base-b-kernel-unit`, which `pr-test.yml` dispatches only when `jit_kernel` changed (`test/registered/kernels/**` or `python/sglang/kernels/!(aot)/**`). Every import in these nine resolves inside that filter, so the lane they are on buys nothing.

Four of them sit on `1-gpu-small` and could not move, because the kernel lane had no 5090 suite. It does now: one row in the `jit-kernel-test` table added in #40495, plus the suite name in `run_suite.py`. `runner_configs.yml` gives `1-gpu-small` the same `install` script and artifact version as `1-gpu-large`, and `base-b-test-1-gpu-small` already runs on that pool through the same install step.

- 5090 rows: `test_flash_attention_4_sm120.py`, `test_gemma4_fused_routing.py`, `test_gather_spec_extras.py`, `test_spec_topk1.py`. The first is gated on `device_capability()[0] == 12`, so it can only ever run on the 5090 -- moving it to the H100 kernel lane would have made it skip silently.
- 1-gpu-large rows: `test_fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py`, `test_lfm_short_conv.py`, `test_dsa_metadata.py`, `test_dsa_transform_index.py`, `test_gdn_decode_fused_proj_conv.py`. `runner_config` is unchanged; only the stage moves.

AMD registrations are untouched: AMD has its own kernel lane with a different suite form, which is a separate decision. Seventeen files under `kernels/` stay on `base-b` because they also import from `sglang.srt`, which the `jit_kernel` filter does not cover; each needs its own call.

## Job naming

The five jobs in the table used three different conventions: a partition suffix with the runner implied (`jit-kernel-unit-test (0)`), an adjective (`jit-kernel-multigpu-unit-test`), and half a runner name (`jit-kernel-b200-test`). None of them said which suite it ran. They now spell the suite they run, with `base-b-kernel` swapped for this workflow's prefix:

| before | after |
|---|---|
| `jit-kernel-unit-test (0)` / `(1)` | `jit-kernel-unit-test-1-gpu-large (0)` / `(1)` |
| `jit-kernel-multigpu-unit-test` | `jit-kernel-unit-test-8-gpu-h200` |
| `jit-kernel-b200-test` | `jit-kernel-unit-test-4-gpu-b200` |
| `jit-kernel-benchmark-test` | `jit-kernel-benchmark-test-1-gpu-large` |

The `job_name` column drops out with it: a row is now a `(suite, runner_config)` pair, and both the job name and the `--suite` argument derive from `suite`. Adding a lane fills two fields.

Renaming is safe here. `main`'s required status checks are `["lint", "pr-test-finish"]`; `pr-test-finish` depends on the caller `call-jit-kernel-tests`, not on these names; `wait-for-jobs` matches only `base-a-test-*` / `base-b-test-*` prefixes; and `check-pr-test-health`'s carve-out names `base-c-test-8-gpu-h20`. Nothing else in the repo references them -- the `jit-kernel-unit-test-amd` hits are an AMD *suite* name.

## Also

Two speculative tests assert the same accept length twice against the same server:

- `e2e/models/test_deepseek_v3_mtp.py:59` asserts `acc_length > 2.8`, which `gsm8k_accept_length_thres = 2.8` (`:43`) already checks through `GSM8KMixin`, reading the same `avg_spec_accept_length` from `/server_info`. The `is_in_amd_ci()` branch beside it is dead -- this file registers CUDA only, and the AMD copy is `test/registered/amd/test_deepseek_v3_mtp.py` with its own thresholds.
- `spec/eagle/test_deepseek_v3_fp4_mtp_small.py:112` asserts `acc_length > 2.65`, weaker than the `> 2.7` at `:97` on the same server.

Both throughput gates stay: no other CUDA test asserts bs-1 decode speed for either model.

## Verification

A run with the new lane in place: all six `jit-kernel` jobs pass, including `jit-kernel-unit-test-1-gpu-small`, whose log shows the four files collected and `test_flash_attention_4_sm120.py` running its 53 cases rather than skipping.

title: [PD] Pack draft KV head slices for DCP transfers
author: kpham-sgl
body:
Avoid per-token Mooncake copies from #40045 when prefill draft KV rows are wider than decode rows. Pack head slices with the existing gather kernel, then transfer contiguous ranges; drain transfers before buffer reuse.

B200/NVLink, Kimi Linear + dummy DSpark, TP1 → TP2/DCP2, BF16 draft KV, OSL=1, two runs per variant. Same payload; packing included. Mean TTFT (main → PR):

| Prompt / prefill cache | Concurrency 1 | Concurrency 4 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 32K / cold | 1.20 → 0.58 s | 3.54 → 1.87 s |
| 90K / 83K | 2.90 → 0.21 s | 9.36 → 0.70 s |
| 170K / 164K | 5.48 → 0.28 s | 17.68 → 0.92 s |

170K draft microbenchmark: 1.71M → 13.3K descriptors per peer. Adds 320 MiB of bounded pack capacity for Mooncake in this setup; NIXL allocation is unchanged. Reverse-width mismatch retains fallback.

Validation: byte-exact transfer/kernel tests; GSM8K **90.5% (362/400)** with Kimi + dummy DSpark, TP2/PP2 → TP4/DCP4 on eight GB300s across two nodes using Mooncake RDMA (single rail). Speculative-verify smoke passes. The GSM8K topology change is uncommitted.

title: [Qwen3.8-Next] Pipeline-parallel serving and PD-prefill MTP for Qwen4-Exp
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`) could not run with `--pp-size > 1`. #38698 by @zhangxiaolei123456 added pipeline-parallel serving and PD-prefill MTP for it, but that branch no longer merges after #30775, #39378 and #40045. This PR carries the two commits from #38698 (authorship preserved) rebased onto main, plus the follow-ups we needed to run it end to end.

## Modifications

- `feat(qwen4): support pipeline parallel serving` and `feat(qwen4): support PP PD prefill with MTP` from #38698, cherry-picked with `-x`. Adapted to main: the PD-prefill gate they added is dropped in favour of `check_pipeline_parallel_compat` (#39378), and `get_embed_and_head` reads `self.model.embed_tokens` (main flattened the VL model).
- Fix the hyper-connection relay contract at PP boundaries (the widened hidden state carries the streams; no separate residual).
- Relay multimodal embeddings to the last stage, which runs the MTP draft prefill.
- Add `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration` to the PD-prefill PP + EAGLE architecture allowlist.

The standalone `test_qwen4_exp_pipeline_parallel.py` from #38698 is not carried over; coverage stays in the existing disaggregation-wire and EAGLE-worker tests. The QSA PD state-transfer commits on the #38698 branch are already on main via #36651 and are not repeated here.

## Accuracy Tests

GB300, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, GSM8K-200 via `sglang.test.run_eval`, MTP steps/topk/draft = 3/1/4 (reference TP4 + MTP: 0.980, accept length 3.16):

| arm | source | score | accept length |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| PD prefill TP2xPP2 + MTP -> decode TP4 + MTP (Mooncake, no `PYTHONOPTIMIZE`, regular gate) | this PR on main | 0.980 | 3.16 |
| aggregate TP2xPP2 + MTP, `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC=1` | this PR + #39643 + #40001 | 0.975 | 3.13 |
| aggregate, same, without #40001 | this PR + #39643 | 0.955 | 3.02 |

The aggregate path needs #39643 (draft-embedding loader; #30775's inline loader does not know Qwen4-Exp's embedding key) and #40001 (hybrid recurrent-state commit under PP + spec; Qwen4-Exp is a GDN hybrid). PD prefill depends on neither.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Prefill-only ISL 8192 / OSL 1, chunk 32768, MTP on, GB300, with #40499: TP1xPP4 38,310 tok/s/GPU vs DEP4 30,162 (1.27x); TP2xPP2 30,344 (1.01x).

title: [Test] Split the serving perf tests by topic into `basic_perf/` and route their thresholds through a kit
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary

- Move the per-PR serving perf tests out of `test/registered/perf/` (grouped by runner, `part1` / `part2`) into `test/registered/basic_perf/`, one file per topic.
- Add `perf_bench_kit` (`at_least` / `at_most` / `reported` / `check_perf`), so a threshold is one declaration instead of an `is_in_ci()` / `is_in_amd_ci()` ladder.
- `extra-a-test-1-gpu-large` drops from 4 shards to 3.

`test/registered/perf/models/` (the nightly per-model benchmark runners) is unchanged.

## Structure

- 6 files become 12, split by what each one measures rather than by which runner it happened to fit on.
- 19 `is_in_ci()` gates, 20 `is_in_amd_ci()` branches and 60 raw asserts become 60 bound declarations. The step-summary label is derived from the test method instead of repeated as a literal at every call site.
- File names no longer restate the registration: `test_moe_2gpu.py` -> `test_moe_throughput.py`, and so on.

## VLM serving pins its attention backend

`get_default_attn_backend` returns `fa3` on Hopper and falls through to `flashinfer` on SM120, so the two VLM perf tests were covering different kernels purely as a function of which runner they were registered to, and neither name said so.

- Split into `test_vlm_serving_{fa3,flashinfer,aiter}.py`, each passing `--attention-backend` explicitly, so a file keeps naming the right kernel after the default moves.
- The online phase drops from 250 prompts to 50, the sample size the existing test already documents as sufficient for a stable median.
- The two AMD registrations (`1-gpu-small-amd` and `1-gpu-large-amd`) were the same measurement on two GPU sizes; they collapse into the one `aiter` file.

## Speculative latency guard moves to EAGLE3

This is the only test in the tree that bounds speculative decoding *latency*; every other one bounds accept length, which says how many draft tokens survive, not what that buys. It ran `EAGLE` against a Llama-2-7b target, so it is retargeted to `EAGLE3` on Llama-3.1-8B. Registered for CUDA only: the EAGLE-specific `skipIf(is_hip())` is gone and no AMD bound for this configuration has been measured.

## Thresholds set from measured runs

Bounds sat between 1.16x and 1.61x of the measured value while run-to-run variance is about 0.2%, so most of them only caught very large regressions.

- 12 bounds re-derived at 1.10x of the worst of three measured runs.
- `test_embeddings_api_latency_throughput` asserted `throughput > 60` and measured 58.73: it failed and passed only on the built-in retry. Now 53.
- Bounds with no measurement behind them are untouched: every AMD bound, the 2-GPU lane, and the retargeted EAGLE3 test.

## One server per batch sweep

`run_score_benchmark` and `run_embeddings_benchmark` relaunched the server for every batch size, although batch size is a property of the request and the server arguments were identical. Added `run_score_benchmark_multi` / `run_embeddings_benchmark_multi` following the existing `run_bench_serving_multi`, taking 8 server launches down to 4.

## Test plan

- `/rerun-test` on the moved files.

title: [Perf] [NPU] deepep: enable MXFP8 low-latency dispatch for Fp8MoEMethod FP4 experts
author: iridiumine
body:
## Motivation

On NPU, FP4-expert models routed through Fp8MoEMethod ( is_fp4_expert=True , e.g. MiMo-V2.5-Pro with modelopt_fp4) delegate execution to NPUW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod kernels via the ASCEND MoE runner. However, process_weights_after_loading only runs Fp8MoEMethod 's own body, so the DeepEP dispatcher quant config was never set — dispatch fell back to BF16 and a separate DynamicMxQuant kernel ran before every grouped matmul (~15ms/layer at 16K-token prefill).

The native FP4 path ( NPUW4A8MXFP4FusedMoEMethod , DSV4) already sets the same dispatcher config; the Fp8MoEMethod path was simply missing it.

## Modifications

- Declare the dispatch wire format as a DISPATCHER_QUANT_CONFIG class attribute on NPUW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod ( low_latency=mxfp8 ; normal stays BF16 since A5 MXFP8 normal dispatch is intranode-only). The kernel that consumes the activations now owns the declaration, instead of each caller hand-writing platform-specific if/else patches.
- In Fp8MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading , pick the config up from the attached layer.w13_kernel when it declares one; otherwise keep the original checkpoint-dtype config. No _is_npu / is_fp4_expert branching — the attached kernel already encodes both.
- Reuse the same declaration in NPUW4A8MXFP4FusedMoEMethod , replacing its hand-written copy.
With this, A5 low-latency dispatch quantizes activations to MXFP8 in-kernel (with E8M0 block scales) and the GMMs consume them directly; the three previously duplicated config dicts collapse into a single kernel-owned declaration.

## Accuracy Tests

```
echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000
export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1

source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh

export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=300
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32
export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=600
export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
export ASCEND_USE_FIA=1
export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=32
export DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE=2500
export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_ROUND=20
export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_PER_ROUND_TOKENS=4096
export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
export HCCL_HOST_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE=auto
export SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1

sglang serve \
        --model-path $MODEL_PATH \
        --served-model-name $MODEL_PATH \
        --trust-remote-code \
        --attention-backend ascend \
        --device npu \
        --mem-fraction-static 0.92 \
        --tp-size 8 --nnodes 1 --node-rank 0 \
        --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-total-tokens 600000 \
        --max-running-requests 32 \
        --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto \
        --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 \
        --speculative-algorithm DFLASH \
        --speculative-draft-model-path $DFLASH_PATH \
        --speculative-num-draft-tokens 8 \
        --dp-size 2 --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head \
```

title: [Perf] [NPU] mem_cache: Add optional ScatterPa KV cache writes
author: Guozhong23
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

When FIA is enabled, the current Ascend MHA KV-cache write path launches two `npu_scatter_nd_update_` operators per layer: one for the key cache and one for the value cache.

CANN provides `ScatterPaKvCache`, exposed through torch_npu as `npu_scatter_pa_kv_cache`. It can update the paged key and value caches in a single operator, reducing kernel-launch and slot-mapping overhead for decode workloads.

Downstream profiling also shows that the optimal write path depends on the forward stage:

- Decode and speculative decode with a small number of new tokens can benefit from ScatterPaKvCache.
- Large prefill writes perform better with the existing ScatterNdUpdate path.

Therefore, this PR introduces ScatterPaKvCache as an optional, decode-oriented backend instead of replacing the existing implementation unconditionally.

Closes #39355.

## Modifications

This PR includes the following changes:

- Add the `SGLANG_NPU_USE_SCATTER_PA_KV_CACHE` environment variable.
  - Disabled by default.
  - Existing behavior remains unchanged when it is not enabled.
- Use `torch_npu.npu_scatter_pa_kv_cache` for:
  - regular decode;
  - decode graph execution;
  - speculative decode and MTP verification.
- Keep prefill and extend writes on the existing two-ScatterNdUpdate implementation.
- Use `cache_mode="Norm"` for the current PA-ND cache layout:
  - key/value: `[num_tokens, num_kv_heads, head_dim]`;
  - cache: `[num_blocks, page_size, num_kv_heads, head_dim]`;
  - slot mapping: one flattened physical slot per token.
- Convert the slot mapping to contiguous `int32`, as required by the operator interface.
- Forward the decode write-backend hint through hybrid SWA pools to the selected NPU KV-cache sub-pool.
- Add explicit validation for:
  - `ASCEND_USE_FIA=1`;
  - availability of `torch_npu.npu_scatter_pa_kv_cache`;
  - portable FP16, BF16, and INT8 KV-cache data types.
- Add registered NPU unit tests covering:
  - key/value paged-cache layout;
  - slot-mapping semantics and cache contents;
  - environment-variable gating;
  - prefill fallback to ScatterNdUpdate;
  - unsupported configuration errors;
  - hybrid SWA forwarding.
- Document the new environment variable in the Ascend NPU environment-variable reference.

The feature can be enabled with:

```bash
export ASCEND_USE_FIA=1
export SGLANG_NPU_USE_SCATTER_PA_KV_CACHE=1

title: fix(cuda-graph): remove unnecessary CP batch alignment
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
### Summary

Decode CUDA graph capture aligned batch sizes to `attn_cp_size`, even though prefill CP is inactive for `DECODE` and `TARGET_VERIFY`. DCP and `--enable-cp-decode-attn-tp` partition KV/head dimensions rather than token rows, so they do not require CP-width batch alignment.

Remove the CP factor while retaining the existing TBO and gathered-buffer attention-TP alignment.

## AgentX performance

This result requires the combined [#34200](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34200), [#39950](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39950), and [#40543](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40543) stack: HIP CP-v2 support, correct AITER B-preshuffled slicing, and removal of unnecessary CP decode-graph alignment.

Single-node DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 on 8×MI355X, TP8, DSpark gamma 6, static verify, 3,600 seconds per point. C4/C16 use GPU KV; C32/C48/C64 use HiCache. `PCP8 + DTP` enables `--enable-prefill-cp --attn-cp-size 8 --enable-cp-decode-attn-tp`.

Values are `TP8 → PCP8 + DTP`; latency is lower-is-better and throughput is higher-is-better. Deltas are relative to TP8.

| C | TTFT avg | TTFT p90 | TPOT avg | TPOT p90 | Total tok/s/GPU | Output tok/s/GPU |

title: [AMD] fix kda decode flydsl import
author: kangwangamd
body:
## Motivation
`test_kimi_k3_kda_decode.py` fails at **import**  as AITER is advanced to [`f0966b0ae`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/f0966b0aed0b38198e2e1ca1cff8cca343bbcb7e); 
due to aiter removed aiter.ops.flydsl.utils see table below
**Two independent AITER removals are involved, and only the first is test-only:**

| # | AITER file removed | AITER commit | breaks in SGLang |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `aiter/ops/flydsl/utils.py` | [`3b2a9ce60`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/3b2a9ce60) ([#5116](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5116), 09-02) | `is_flydsl_available` — **test only** |
| 2 | `aiter/ops/flydsl/kernels/vector.py` | [`08d73a192`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/08d73a192) ([#5303](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5303), 09-09) | `from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels import vector` — **production kernel code** |

## Modifications

**3 files, +4 / −14.** No behaviour change on the current pin.

### 1. Test — `test/registered/kernels/ops/kimi_k3/flydsl_ops/test_kimi_k3_kda_decode.py`

```diff
 pytest.importorskip("flydsl")
-from aiter.jit.utils.chip_info import get_gfx
-from aiter.ops.flydsl.utils import is_flydsl_available
+pytest.importorskip("aiter")

-def _gfx950_flydsl_available() -> bool:
-    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or not is_flydsl_available():
-        return False
-    try:
-        return get_gfx() == "gfx950"
-    except (AssertionError, KeyError, RuntimeError):
-        return False
-
 pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
-    not _gfx950_flydsl_available(),
+    not is_flydsl_kimi_k3_kda_decode_supported(),
     reason="gfx950 FlyDSL required",
 )
```

The removed gate asked three things; all three are still answered:

| old condition | now covered by |
|---|---|
| `torch.cuda.is_available()` | first line of `is_flydsl_kimi_k3_kda_decode_supported()` |
| `is_flydsl_available()` | `pytest.importorskip("flydsl")` + `importorskip("aiter")` — under AITER's new contract, importing `aiter.ops.flydsl` already fails when flydsl is missing or too old |
| `get_gfx() == "gfx950"` | `_rocm_arch(device) == "gfx950"` inside the same function (reads `gcnArchName`) |

`is_flydsl_kimi_k3_kda_decode_supported()` is **already imported by this test** and is the predicate the
production code itself uses to decide whether this kernel can run — so the skip condition can no longer
drift from what the kernel actually supports, which the duplicated local helper could.

### 2. Production kernels — `kimi_k3_kda_decode.py` and `kimi_k3_kda_decode_fb.py`

One line each, under `python/sglang/kernels/ops/kimi_k3/flydsl/kernels/`:

```diff
-from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels import vector
+from flydsl._mlir.dialects import vector
```

AITER's own #5303 migrated its internal callers the same way.

## Accuracy Tests

**Verified offline on real hardware before opening this PR** — m12-17 (MI355X, gfx950), **1 GPU**, with AITER **rebuilt commit-aligned from source**

Not applicable — no compute path changes.

title: [AMD] Drop the redundant scale zero-fill before AITER per-tensor FP8 quant
author: siliangchen-amd
body:
# [AMD] Drop the redundant `scale` zero-fill before AITER per-tensor FP8 quant

## Motivation

`dynamic_per_tensor_quant_fp8` zero-fills its one-element `scale` buffer before
handing it to the backend:

```python
scale = torch.zeros(1, device=input.device, dtype=torch.float32)
if _use_aiter:
    dynamic_per_tensor_quant(output, input, scale)
elif _has_vllm:
    torch.ops._C.dynamic_scaled_fp8_quant(output, input, scale)
else:
    _native_dynamic_per_tensor_quant_fp8(output, input, scale)
```

Only one of those three backends reads the incoming value.

| backend | how `scale` is written | needs the pre-fill |
|---|---|---|
| vLLM | `segmented_max_reduction` **atomicMax**-es into it | **yes** |
| AITER | launches `initializeScale(scale, 1, 0.0f)` first | no |
| native | ends in `scale.view(-1).copy_(...)`, a full overwrite | no |

For AITER, [`csrc/kernels/quant_kernels.cu`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/main/csrc/kernels/quant_kernels.cu)
`dynamic_per_tensor_quant` opens with its own fill in both the fp8 and int8
branches:

```cpp
aiter::initializeScale<<<dim3(1), dim3(64), 0, stream>>>(
    reinterpret_cast<float*>(scale.data_ptr()), 1, 0.0f);
aiter::data_to_scale_kernel<input_dtype, opus::fp8_t><<<grid, block, 0, stream>>>(
    reinterpret_cast<float*>(scale.data_ptr()), ..., cols);
```

So on the AITER path the buffer is zeroed twice per call, once by torch and
once by the kernel that was going to do it anyway. The torch one is a real
`vectorized_elementwise_kernel<FillFunctor<float>>` launch to write a single
float, and it happens on every quantized GEMM input — four per decoder layer,
so 128 per decode step on a 32-layer model, replayed out of the captured decode
CUDA graph for the life of the server.

## Change

Move the allocation inside each branch and zero only where a backend depends on
it. The vLLM branch is untouched in behaviour and keeps `torch.zeros`; AITER and
the native fallback take `torch.empty`.

## Correctness

Reading the source is not enough, since the shipped AITER is a binary wheel, so
the installed artifact was tested adversarially: pre-fill `scale` with values
that would visibly corrupt a max-reduction, then compare against the
zero-filled baseline.

```
shape 4096x4096  baseline scale = 2.666667e-01
   pre-fill zeros (baseline)   -> identical
   pre-fill +inf               -> identical
   pre-fill 1e30               -> identical
   pre-fill NaN                -> identical
   pre-fill -inf               -> identical
   pre-fill -1e30              -> identical
```

Bit-identical quantized output and identical scale for every poison value, on
all three shapes tested (4096x4096, 1024x5120, 17x4096). If the kernel ever
read the incoming buffer, `+inf` and `NaN` would not survive a max-reduction
unchanged.

The profiler shows the launch that disappears, and the one that stays:

```
torch.zeros (current)                        torch.empty (patched)
  10  aten::fill_                              10  aiter::dynamic_per_tensor_quant
  10  vectorized_elementwise_kernel<           10  aiter::initializeScale
        FillFunctor<float>>                    10  aiter::data_to_scale_kernel
  10  aiter::dynamic_per_tensor_quant          10  aiter::scaled_quant_kernel
  10  aiter::initializeScale
  10  aiter::data_to_scale_kernel
  10  aiter::scaled_quant_kernel
```

`aiter::initializeScale` is present on both sides — the zeroing still happens,
just once.

## Results

8x MI325X (gfx942), sglang `main`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, `--quantization fp8`,
`sglang.bench_serving` random 1024/1024, concurrency 64, 320 prompts, TP 8
(TP 4 where the head count does not divide by 8). Three reps per variant
against one server boot; the table reports the median of reps 2-3, with rep 1
dropped as server warm-up on both sides.

| model | arch | size | zeros (tok/s) | empty (tok/s) | delta | mean TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | Llama-3.1 | 8B | 8772 | 9593 | **+9.36%** | 6.80 -> 6.21 ms |
| Qwen3-8B | Qwen3 | 8B | 8106 | 8427 | **+3.96%** | 7.41 -> 7.11 ms |
| Qwen3-32B | Qwen3 | 32B | 4345 | 4469 | **+2.85%** | 13.55 -> 13.09 ms |
| Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 | Mistral | 7B | 9522 | 9734 | **+2.22%** | 6.29 -> 6.14 ms |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | Qwen3 MoE | 30B-A3B | 5925 | 6007 | **+1.39%** | 10.14 -> 9.98 ms |
| NeuralPizza-7B-V0.1 | Mistral | 7B | 9363 | 9939 | **+6.14%** | 6.38 -> 6.00 ms |
| DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B | Llama-3.1 | 8B | 8851 | 9238 | **+4.37%** | 6.75 -> 6.42 ms |
| WeirdCompound-v1.5-24b | Mistral | 24B | 6846 | 7062 | **+3.15%** | 8.54 -> 8.32 ms |
| Human-Like-Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct | Qwen2 | 7B | 10208 | 10446 | **+2.33%** | 5.75 -> 5.59 ms |
| Olmo-3-7B-Instruct | Olmo3 | 7B | 4191 | 4269 | **+1.86%** | 14.54 -> 14.29 ms |

Ten of ten improve, mean +3.76%, median +3.00%, spread +1.39% to +9.36%. The
top five rows are stock upstream checkpoints across four architecture families
and two sparsity regimes; the rest are community fine-tunes that widen the
architecture coverage.

Mean TPOT falls on every one of the ten, which is the signal the mechanism
predicts: the removed work is per decode step, not per request. The dense
8B models gain most, consistent with a fixed per-step launch cost amortised
against a smaller step.

## Scope and limits

- Only the AITER and native branches change. The vLLM path keeps its zero-fill
  because `segmented_max_reduction` accumulates into the buffer, and it is
  unexercised by the numbers above (all runs are `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`).
- Measured on gfx942 only. The change is not arch-specific, but the numbers are.
- The per-token path (`dynamic_per_token_quant`) is untouched.
- A microbenchmark of the call site in isolation prices the removed kernel at
  roughly 3.7 us of device time against a ~30 us call, but its totals were too
  noisy to quote as the headline; the serving numbers above are the claim.

title: [Test] Anchor `basic_perf` thresholds to each metric's measured spread
author: hnyls2002
body:
Three `basic_perf` thresholds sit inside the distribution of their own metric, so each fails a fraction of the time. `CustomTestCase` retries once, which turns most of those into green runs -- the signal is swallowed and the test silently runs twice.

Found by grepping `retry() failed` across today's CI logs, not by a red run:

| threshold | first attempt | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_score_api` `p95_latency_ms <= 32` | 32.51 | failed, retry 30.74 passed |
| `test_vlm_serving_flashinfer` `output_throughput >= 6900` | 6718.41 | failed, retry 7596.63 passed |
| `test_pp_throughput` `input_throughput >= 3000` (amd) | 2418.25 | failed, retry 3144.23 passed |

## Anchoring

Each CUDA threshold is re-derived from 2-4 measured runs as `worst * (1 + max(0.10, observed_spread))`, so it clears the whole observed range rather than a single sample. The flat `1.10` it replaces assumed every metric has the same run-to-run spread; they do not:

| metric family | spread across runs |
| --- | --- |
| offline throughput | 0.1% - 0.8% |
| median e2e / median itl | 0.2% - 1.4% |
| ttft | 3.3% - 25.4% |
| small-batch API avg / p95 | 6.6% - 43.9% |
| vlm output throughput | 7.3% - 13.1% |

One factor is simultaneously ~10x too generous for offline throughput and ~4x too tight for p95. The same metric also splits by backend: `test_pp_throughput`'s prefill input throughput spreads 1.2% on CUDA and 30.1% on AMD, which is why its AMD threshold was the one that kept failing.

## What the numbers do, against both baselines

Against `main` as it stands, every change relaxes -- 32 relax, none tighten, 13 unchanged. That is expected: #40505 set these to `worst * 1.10` off a single sample each, and a single sample systematically underestimates the range, so re-anchoring can only move a threshold outward.

Against the thresholds as they were before `basic_perf` existed, the direction is the opposite -- **33 tighten, 8 relax, 1 unchanged**:

| threshold | before `basic_perf` | here | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `test_vlm_serving_flashinfer` output throughput | 2000 | 5940 | +197% |
| `test_score_api` avg | 48 | 31 | -35% |
| `test_vlm_serving_fa3` itl | 8 | 5.2 | -35% |
| `test_vlm_serving_fa3` e2e | 16500 | 11000 | -33% |
| `test_embeddings_api` batch-25 avg | 115 | 72 | -37% |
| `test_vlm_serving_flashinfer` ttft | 150 | 83 | -45% |

The 8 that relax against that older baseline are the ones measurement shows were too tight, every one on a high-spread metric:

| threshold | before | here | spread |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `test_embeddings_api` p95 | 25 | 34 | 43.9% |
| `test_embeddings_api` batch-50 p95 | 195 | 200 | 39.3% |
| `test_pp_throughput` prefill, amd | 3000 | 2190 | 30.1% |
| `test_embeddings_api` avg | 20 | 23 | 18.9% |
| `test_embeddings_api` throughput | 60 | 45 | 18.9% |
| `test_pp_throughput` decode | 6700 | 6250 | 9.3% |
| `test_vlm_serving_flashinfer` e2e | 16500 | 17480 | 1.1% |
| `test_vlm_serving_flashinfer` itl | 8 | 8.4 | 0.7% |

So this is not a blanket loosening: it keeps the tightening and returns the eight that overshot to what measurement supports. All 45 thresholds now clear every sample observed today with at least a 1.10x margin.

A threshold wide enough to hold a 44% spread only catches large regressions. Whether those metrics are worth guarding at that width, or whether the measurement should be made less noisy instead, is a separate question this PR does not answer.

## AMD

Only the one AMD threshold with a measured breach changes. The rest have a single sample each -- not enough to estimate spread -- so they are left alone rather than re-anchored on n=1.

## Test plan

`rerun-test` dispatched on `main` across all three runner configs (`1-gpu-h100`, `1-gpu-5090`, `2-gpu-h100`); the numbers above come from those runs plus the CI runs on #40505. The diff is numeric only -- the AST is identical once numeric literals are normalized.

title: [ModelOpt][PP] Keep BF16 shared experts out of the NVFP4 fusion so TP1 pipeline stages can load
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

Reproduce with `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` (routed experts NVFP4, shared experts kept BF16 through `exclude_modules`) and `--quantization modelopt_fp4 --tp-size 1` (for example one stage of `--tp-size 1 --pp-size 4`). Weight loading fails:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (3072) must match the size of tensor b (6144) at non-singleton dimension 1
  python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:800, expert_data.copy_(loaded_weight)
```

With `--tp-size` > 1 (TP4, TP2×EP2 in our runs) the server starts with fusion nominally enabled and GSM8K stays in range (0.96–0.98), so whether the BF16 shared expert ends up fused correctly there is not established by this PR; the fix simply routes such checkpoints onto the non-fused shared-expert path at every TP.

Scope: the crash needs a `--tp-size 1` load of the checkpoint, and for a GLM-5.2-sized model that only happens as a pipeline-parallel stage (TP1×PP4 / TP1×PP8), so in practice pipeline parallelism is how this surfaces.

Root cause: `DeepseekV2ForCausalLM` (and `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, which subclasses it) decides shared-expert fusion through `quant_blocks_shared_experts_fusion()` in `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/utils.py`, which duck-types the quant config:

```python
can_fuse_fn = getattr(quant_config, "can_fuse_shared_expert", None)
return can_fuse_fn is not None and not can_fuse_fn()
```

`ModelOptFp4Config` has no `can_fuse_shared_expert`, so fusion is never vetoed even when the shared experts are excluded from quantization. `QuarkConfig` already implements this hook for the same situation.

## Modifications

Add `ModelOptFp4Config.can_fuse_shared_expert()` returning `False` when an excluded module is a shared-expert body, so those experts stay on their separate BF16 linear path. An excluded `shared_expert_gate` alone does not veto (same rule as `QuarkConfig`): `nvidia/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-NVFP4` excludes only the gate on all 48 layers and keeps fusing. Checkpoints whose shared experts are NVFP4 as well are unaffected.

## Tests

- `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_modelopt_nvfp4.py`: one case for the gate (body excluded → no fusion; gate-only excluded → fusion kept; nothing excluded → fusion kept).
- GLM-5.2-NVFP4 + RedHatAI DSpark on 4×GB300 after the change: `--tp-size 1 --pp-size 4` loads and serves (GSM8K-50 1.00), `--tp-size 4` GSM8K-50 0.98. Before the change TP1 could not start.

title: [Kimi K3] Fix CUDA graph stream explosion
author: kpham-sgl
body: ## Motivation Kimi K3 target CUDA graph replay expands to 96 streams on B300. Repeated attention forks move subsequent layers onto new replay streams. Record the main attention branches before their auxiliary kernels to fix this stream explosion: the same workload now uses 4 target streams on all eight TP ranks. ## Modifications - Record the KDA main projection before the side-stream gate GEMVs. - Fork the MLA output gate before attention, then record its kernel at the output-projection boundary after the attention core. Keep the original fork/join dependencies so the GPU work can still overlap, and close skipped gate branches. - Extend changed-input CUDA graph correctness coverage. ## Accuracy Tests `python test/registered/unit/models/test_kimi_k3_bfa_overlap.py`: **5 tests passed on B300**. [Overlap unit CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35662649445) and [B300 end-to-end CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35662661359) also passed on the current PR head; both Kimi K3 B300 end-to-end files passed two tests each. KDA bitwise parity covers token counts 1, 4, and 12, both `defer_f_b` settings, and three changed-input replays. MLA checks an in-graph input producer and changed-input parity, including eager and breakable-graph fallback selection. Full-model traces retain identical kernel-name/count multisets: 1,950 target kernels per replay on every rank. ## Speed Tests and Profiling In TP8/DCP1 traces, target replay streams fall from **96 to 4 on all eight TP ranks**, with stable assignments across 16 profiled replays and identical kernel-name/count multisets. This is reproduced with both real and dummy weights. Separate **N=5 unprofiled runs per variant and batch size**, using dummy MXFP4 target and dummy draft weights: 8× B300, CUDA 13.0, TP8, 60k input / 1k output, DSpark block 7, simulated acceptance 5.5, FP8 E4M3 KV, FP32 SSM, CuTe DSL MLA, FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE, connections=8. **TP8/DCP1:** | Batch size | Before, tok/s (mean ± SD) | After, tok/s (mean ± SD) | Change in mean | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 493.06 ± 2.41 | 498.12 ± 2.14 | +1.03% | | 16 | 3139.65 ± 252.29 | 3249.41 ± 15.07 | +3.50% | BS1 improves in all five matched pairs (+0.77% to +1.14%). **The BS16 mean is distorted by one slow baseline sample (2689.09 tok/s), retained in the results.** The other four matched pairs differ by −0.10% to −0.15%; these results do not establish a BS16 speedup. Full-batch steady-state throughput gives the same interpretation. Order: baseline (3 samples), patched (3), patched (2), baseline (2), each with a fresh server and a full-shape warmup pair excluded in advance. Client/server seeds are 42; actual acceptance lengths match in every corresponding pair. All requests generated the requested tokens. Measurements share two server launches per variant, so N=5 is limited evidence. Dummy weights and simulated acceptance do not test model accuracy. **TP8/DCP8**, same N=5 design and workload, with `fi_a2a` and replicated Q projection: | Batch size | Before, tok/s (mean ± SD) | After, tok/s (mean ± SD) | Change in mean | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 470.94 ± 2.23 | 474.87 ± 2.26 | +0.83% | | 16 | 3060.60 ± 14.24 | 3060.26 ± 13.92 | −0.01% | Every BS1 matched pair improves (+0.72% to +0.88%); BS16 decode is unchanged (paired changes −0.028% to +0.001%). Acceptance matches in every pair. All samples are retained and all requests complete their requested output length with a valid full-batch decode window. BS16 mean total latency is 44.845 → 45.105 s (+0.58%), driven by last-TTFT/prefill time (39.617 → 39.876 s), including one slower patched prefill sample. N=5 does not establish whether the small prefill difference is noise; the flat decode result is not a claim about all end-to-end timings. The DCP benchmark uses `--skip-token-capacity-check` because the client guard reads physical capacity while DCP exposes eight times the logical capacity; server memory settings are unchanged. Both repeated comparisons use baseline `0f6761b54` with the PR patch applied for the patched runs. DCP8 was not profiled in this timing experiment. ## Profile **Before** **After** ## Checklist - [x] Pre-commit checks pass for all changed files. - [x] Registered CUDA unit tests extended and run. - [x] Correctness and full-model profiling results provided above. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #35662490950](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35662490950) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #35662490698](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35662490698) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #35662491074](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35662491074)

title: [LFM2-VL] Add DSpark speculative decoding
author: tugot17
body:
## Motivation

LFM2-VL can't be served with DSpark today. The speculative stack looks up `lm_head` and
`set_dflash_layers_to_capture` on the top-level model, but
`Lfm2VlForConditionalGeneration` keeps the decoder under `language_model`, so both miss
and the server refuses to start.

## Modifications

Delegate both to `language_model`, same as `kimi_k25` and `gemma4_mm`. `lm_head` is a
property rather than a submodule alias so the state_dict keys don't change.

## Accuracy Tests

Draft model: [`tugot17/mango-9`](https://huggingface.co/tugot17/mango-9) (4 layers, block 9).

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path LiquidAI/LFM2.5-VL-3B \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
  --speculative-draft-model-path tugot17/mango-9 \
  --speculative-draft-attention-backend flashinfer \
  --speculative-dspark-block-size 9 \
  --disable-radix-cache
```

Full [MMSpec](https://github.com/killthefullmoon/MMSpec) `test` split (600 samples /
723 turns), greedy, 1xH100, 0 failures. Accept length 4.222; output tokens 108067 with
speculation vs 111089 without, the usual verify-shape numerics rather than a behaviour
change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same run, base/spec/base bracket: **2.08x** overall, 537 vs 258 tok/s. Per subset
1.66x (GQA) to 2.56x (MMMU-Pro). At batch 8 / 32 / 64: 1.55x / 1.32x / 1.18x, with
acceptance flat within 0.4%.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance

No unit test: there is no equivalent per-model test for the same delegation in
`kimi_k25` or `gemma4_mm`. Happy to add one if you'd prefer.

title: [DSpark] Fix draft CUDA graph stream explosion
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

DSpark draft CUDA graph replay expands to seven streams on B300 with TP8/DCP1. Its seven dependent token broadcasts go through ProcessGroupNCCL even while the graph capture context has enabled PyNccl.

## Modifications

Use the enabled PyNccl communicator for CUDA broadcasts, keeping broadcasts on the current capture stream. Preserve the torch.distributed fallback when PyNccl is disabled or unavailable. Keep the existing typed PyNccl broadcast unchanged. Audited SRT callers use supported integer or floating-point payloads; no bool/complex broadcast support is added.

## Accuracy Tests

Existing Kimi K3 B300 correctness tests are being retriggered on the updated head. Dummy weights and simulated acceptance do not validate model accuracy. Pre-commit checks passed for the runtime change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8× B300, TP8, 60k input / 1k output, DSpark block 7, simulated acceptance 5.5, dummy MXFP4 target and dummy draft weights, FP8 E4M3 KV, FP32 SSM, CuTe DSL MLA, FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE, CUDA device connections 8.

- TP8/DCP1 draft replay streams: **7 → 1**; target remains at **4**.
- The initial typed-broadcast DCP1 profile has the exact same runtime patch as the current head: 137 draft kernels and 1,950 target kernels per replay on all eight ranks, with stable stream assignments across 16 replays. The stream fix does not depend on byte broadcasting.

**Earlier-revision measurements:** the following N=5 table was collected at `ff17b2e04b`, which included byte broadcasting. These timings have not been rerun after restoring the existing typed broadcast at `e91dd97ff0`. The earlier DCP8 traces showed one draft stream and four target streams before and after.

**N=5 unprofiled samples per variant, topology, and batch size:**

| Configuration | BS | Before, tok/s (mean ± SD) | After, tok/s (mean ± SD) | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TP8/DCP1 | 1 | 498.28 ± 2.33 | 498.57 ± 2.38 | +0.06% |
| TP8/DCP1 | 16 | 3262.63 ± 19.96 | 3260.56 ± 19.76 | −0.06% |
| TP8/DCP8 | 1 | 474.95 ± 2.24 | 474.95 ± 2.20 | +0.002% |
| TP8/DCP8 | 16 | 3070.06 ± 19.06 | 3070.47 ± 19.26 | +0.01% |

Decode throughput is effectively unchanged in these runs; full-batch steady-state throughput gives the same conclusion. Mean total latency changes are +0.10%, +0.09%, +0.12%, and −0.26%, respectively. The last mean includes one slower baseline prefill, retained in the results; no end-to-end speedup is established.

Baseline is main `c4d3770a68`; patched is `ff17b2e04b`. Each variant/topology uses one fresh server, an excluded full-shape BS1/BS16 warmup pair, then five alternating measured pairs. Order: baseline DCP1, patched DCP1, patched DCP8, baseline DCP8. Client/server seeds are 42, corresponding acceptance lengths match, and all requests complete the requested output length. Samples share a server launch, so this is limited regression evidence rather than a general performance guarantee. DCP8 uses `fi_a2a` with replicated Q projection. The client capacity check is skipped because it reads physical capacity while DCP exposes logical capacity; server memory settings are unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit checks pass.
- [x] Typed-broadcast DCP1 profile verified; earlier-revision repeated timings identified above.
- [ ] Correctness CI on the updated head.

author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## What

Update `test_modulate.py` so its residual-gate tests expect the CUDA fast path to be unavailable on ROCm.

## Why

#42391 made `can_use_residual_gate_add_cuda` return False under HIP. Several cases in `test_modulate.py` still assert that the fast path is selected, or call `residual_gate_add_cuda` directly. The file is registered in `nightly-amd-kernel-1-gpu`, so on ROCm those cases now assert the opposite of what the code does.

On ROCm:
- `test_residual_gate_add_matches_torch` and `test_residual_gate_add_guards_and_eager_fallback` assert that the fast path is rejected, and still check that `residual_gate_add` matches the eager expression.
- The dtype, transposed-layout, storage-offset, `torch.compile` and CUDA-graph cases that exercise the CUDA kernel directly are skipped.

NVIDIA behavior is unchanged.

This PR originally also gated the residual-gate path in `residual_gate_add_jit.py` and relaxed a LoRA comparison in `test_qwen_image21_cuda.py`. #42391 covered both: it added the HIP check itself and skips that test file off NVIDIA. After merging main, those two files no longer differ from main.

## Test plan

ROCm, MI300, rocm10, at `9578a6ed`: [nightly-test-1-gpu-kernel](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38520223601/job/115707994833).

title: [Fix] Don't let a failed deep_ep import-time check kill servers that never use DeepEP
author: LiRunGuo
body:
## Motivation

Since #33932 (2026-08-07), `sgl-deep-ep` is a hard dependency of the `sglang` wheel, so `deep_ep` is always installed.
`deep_ep/__init__.py` runs host checks at import time:

- `check_nccl_so()` asserts that exactly one libnccl is mapped and that it is byte-identical to the pip NCCL (`AssertionError`, or `FileNotFoundError` when a mapping reads `(deleted)`).
- `find_cuda_home()` asserts that a CUDA home is found (`AssertionError`).
- `init_jit()` initializes the C++ JIT runtime.

The guard in `token_dispatcher/deepep.py` dates from when "not installed" was the only failure mode, and catches only `ImportError`; `deepep_v2.py` catches `(ImportError, OSError)`.
Every server process imports these modules, including the launcher:

```
launch_server -> http_server -> engine -> data_parallel_controller -> scheduler
  -> disaggregation/decode -> managers/utils -> layers/logits_processor
  -> layers/logprob_processor -> model_executor/runner_utils/__init__
  -> runner_utils/deepep_adapter -> layers/moe/token_dispatcher -> deepep -> deep_ep
```

So one failed check stops the server at import time, even for dense models where DeepEP is never requested.

### Reproduction (H200, Qwen3-1.7B, dense, no DeepEP flags)

```bash
# any second libnccl on the host; here a source build of NCCL 2.32.3 vs the pip 2.29.7
export LD_PRELOAD=/path/to/nccl/build/lib/libnccl.so.2
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B --port 30006
```

Before (main @ 00986c8): the launcher exits with code 1 during import.

```
File "python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/deepep.py", line 53, in <module>
File ".venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/deep_ep/__init__.py", line 91, in <module>
AssertionError: Duplicate NCCL runtime found in the current system: .../nccl/build/lib/libnccl.so.2.32.3 and .../site-packages/nvidia/nccl/lib/libnccl.so.2
```

After: the server starts with the custom NCCL mapped, and `/generate` returns ` Paris. The capital of the United States is Washington, D` for "The capital of France is".
The same failure also happened without `LD_PRELOAD` on a shared network filesystem, where the detokenizer saw the NCCL mapping as `(deleted)` and `filecmp` raised `FileNotFoundError`.

## Modifications

- `deepep.py`: catch any exception from the optional import, keep it in `_deepep_import_error`, and chain it into the `ImportError` raised when a DeepEP dispatcher is created. The message now says "not available" instead of "not installed", because the package usually is installed.
- `deepep_v2.py`: widen `(ImportError, OSError)` to `Exception` for the `deep_ep` import. The v2 module already stores and reports the original error.

Users who request DeepEP still get a hard error, now with the root cause instead of a misleading "not installed".
The v1 `try` block also covers the `sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8` import, as before; a failure there is reported the same way.

Follow-up, not in this PR: `runner_utils/__init__.py` eagerly re-exports `DeepEPCudaGraphRunnerAdapter`, so importing `runner_utils.pool` from `logprob_processor` pulls every MoE dispatcher (and `deep_ep`) into the launcher, tokenizer and detokenizer. Making that re-export lazy would stop these processes from loading DeepEP at all.

## Accuracy Tests

No model forward, kernel or sampling code is touched; only the import guard of the two DeepEP dispatcher modules changes.

- New CPU test `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_deepep_import_guard.py` runs a fresh interpreter with a stand-in `deep_ep` whose import raises `AssertionError`. It checks that the dispatcher package imports, that both `use_deepep` flags are false, and that creating a DeepEP dispatcher raises `ImportError` chained to the original error. It fails on main and passes with this change.
- Existing DeepEP unit tests: `test_deepep_v2_buffer_lifecycle.py`, `test_deepep_v2_masked_slab.py`, `test_deepep_v2_wire_dtype.py`, `test_w4afp8_deepep_dtype.py`, `test_w4afp8_deepep_post_reorder.py`, plus the new test: 39 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.
- No model code is touched; the dense end-to-end run above is the functional check.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The change only affects module import, not any runtime path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed: no user-facing option changes.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Not applicable: import-time change only.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [PD] Add opt-in prefill-complete decode KV allocation
author: ekrim
body:
## Motivation

In PD serving, decode can reserve a request's destination KV slots while its
prefill is still running. Long prefills can therefore occupy decode capacity
that other requests could use.

Add `--disaggregation-decode-allocation-policy prefill_complete` to delay
per-request destination KV reservation until the accepted final prefill result
is ready. Global KV pool creation and size are unchanged. The policy is opt-in;
`early` remains the default.

This policy targets workloads where decode KV capacity is constrained and
prefill completion times vary—for example, concurrent short and long prompts.
Early reservation lets unfinished long prefills occupy decode slots before they
can generate tokens, potentially delaying other requests that are ready.
Deferring reservation makes that capacity available until prefill finishes; it does
not make allocation itself or decode kernels faster.

## Modifications

- Add a Mooncake readiness control protocol with request ownership/nonces,
  subscription retry backoff, bounded waits, failure propagation, and
  pre-allocation cancellation.
- Signal readiness after accepting the final prefill result and preparing its
  output/logprob/speculative sidecars. Gate decode admission on that signal.
- Preserve the existing destination-metadata handshake and abort/drain protocol
  after destination pointers have been published.
- Keep exhausted optimistic retries eligible for prefill, and dispatch true
  retraction/rebootstrap recomputation before waiting for source readiness.
- Validate matching policies and supported configurations; add registered CPU
  regressions, a two-GPU lifecycle suite, and documentation.

Initial support is Mooncake (including TCP), the Python bootstrap registry, and
attention TP1/CP1/PP1 per rank, including attention DP. Prefill HiCache support is
limited to L2 `write_back` without storage. Decode radix/HiCache, staging,
runtime role switching, PD multiplexing, encoder disaggregation, decoupled
speculation, HiSparse, and non-DSA auxiliary state pools are excluded.

Enable the option on **both roles**. Upgrade all communicating workers with
`early` still enabled before switching policies; old decode workers cannot
enforce the new policy-mismatch check. Prefill resolves zero optimistic attempts
to one; model/cache configurations that disable optimistic prefill are rejected.

## Accuracy Tests

- Previous revision: **99 CPU tests and 27 subtests passed**, one
  Mori-dependent test skipped, across six files on Linux ARM64.
- All applicable pinned pre-commit hooks passed on the submitted files.
- **Pending:** CPU/GPU regression execution on the latest rebase. The local CPU
  attempt could not collect tests because `torchvision` is missing. GPU and
  performance results below predate both rebases.

The registered two-GPU suite,
`test/registered/e2e/disaggregation/test_prefill_complete_allocation.py`, covers
multi-chunk prefill, prefix reuse, concurrency, cancellation before/after
transfer, retract/resume, optimistic retry exhaustion, and timeout cleanup.

<details>
<summary>Validation commands, environment, and revision details</summary>

CPU command:

```bash
python -m pytest -q -ra \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_complete.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_complete_integration.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_abort_result_cleanup.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_register_to_bootstrap.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_pd_role_switch.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_admission_abort_not_enqueued.py
```

The run at `4f5fa4d7` had zero failures/errors and 14 warnings. Mori was
unavailable. No custom import shims or weakened assertions were used. Torch was
2.15 development rather than the source's 2.13 pin, so dependency-lock parity
remains unvalidated.

The earlier submitted commit `86d123ec` differs only in one test's line wrapping:
production code is byte-identical and all changed Python files are AST-identical.

Current HEAD `f7b24085` rebases that change onto `771c9d78`, retaining upstream's
new EFA allocator validation before our readiness initialization. All added and
removed feature lines are unchanged. Pre-commit passed again. The local attempt
also included `test_mooncake_efa_allocator.py`: seven collection errors from
missing `torchvision`, zero tests executed.

Before the rebase, the original candidate passed all eight registered GPU
lifecycle tests, additional attention-DP checks, and six TCP/prefill-HiCache
checks. In the isolated GLM comparison, all 1,280 measured requests completed at
exact lengths without client errors, and timed texts matched across all four
arms. Untimed probes had identical output tokens and finite logprobs, with a
maximum logprob difference of 0.002925. These are functional parity checks, not
a model-quality benchmark.

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Historical GLM-5.2-NVFP4 ABBA comparison: real MTP3, 12 Rubin GPUs, two prefill
replicas and one decode replica, each TP4/DP4/EP4, with FP8 KV and Mooncake.
Only the allocation policy differed; optimistic prefill was 1 in both policies.
Decode KV was deliberately capped at 163,840 tokens/rank to test capacity
pressure, rather than a production-default configuration.

| Mixed-workload metric | Early, two runs | Prefill-complete, two runs | Change in mean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Output tokens/s, system | 458.88 / 435.98 | 616.39 / 518.39 | +26.81% |
| TTFT p95, seconds | 71.22 / 79.97 | 36.03 / 41.27 | -48.87% |
| Mean TPOT, ms | 4.108 / 3.869 | 4.204 / 3.943 | +2.13% |
| ITL p99, ms | 34.40 / 12.03 | 46.40 / 43.10 | +92.77% |

Changes compare arithmetic means of the two per-run metrics, including
percentiles, not pooled percentiles or confidence intervals.

The throughput/TTFT gain comes with a worse ITL tail. Delayed allocation also
retains source KV longer and removes overlap between chunked prefill and KV
transfer. A separate Qwen3-8B policy-only comparison showed approximately 1%
throughput differences within run variation, without a clear mixed-workload
short-request tail improvement. These workload-dependent tradeoffs are why the
policy remains opt-in.

<details>
<summary>Historical benchmark protocol and provenance</summary>

Candidate `bd4b80dd`, based on `e4a6b090`, ran on identical hosts in
`early / prefill_complete / prefill_complete / early` order, with DP attention
enabled. Workers restarted between arms.

Each arm included 64 short requests (ISL 4,096, OSL 256, concurrency 8), followed
by 256 mixed requests (64 at ISL 131,072 and 192 at ISL 4,096; OSL 256,
concurrency 64). The table reports the mixed workload.

A separate larger-workload campaign did not pass its final provenance audit;
its apparent gains are not used as validated performance evidence here.

</details>
