title: [Perf] [AMD] qwen3.5: Route 512-expert softmax MoE routing through aiter topk_gating
author: omirosh
body:
## Motivation

This is a ROCm performance change: it routes Qwen3.8's 512-expert softmax MoE router through aiter's `topk_gating` instead of the vendored `vllm::moe::topkGatingSoftmax` launcher it reaches today. Against its merge-base on the aiter pin that SGLang ships (`285579b62`, since #45498, with [Rocm/aiter5334](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5334)), it gives **+1.27%** output tok/s without MTP on 8x MI355X, TP8, geomean over 12 serving shapes. On v0.5.19 with NEXTN MTP it gave **+2.22%**.

On SGLang v0.5.20 at the default page size the gain is +1.03% without MTP and +0.40% with MTP; see https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40708#issuecomment-5933064541. 

Qwen3.8 picks 10 experts out of 512 on every one of its 92 layers. On ROCm that pick is 0.878 ms per decode step, 4.8% of decode kernel time, against 0.440 ms/step on B300. `aiter.fused_moe.fused_topk` only hands off to its ASM router for `(experts, topk)` in `(128,4), (128,6), (128,8), (256,6), (256,8), (384,8), (640,8)`, and Qwen3.8 is `(512, 10)`. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next has the same `(512, 10)` softmax router at hidden size 2560 and takes the same path.

[#28399](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28399) tried the same wiring in August and got nothing for it (ITL +3.7%, throughput -1.9% on Qwen3.5 TP2). aiter has since gained the E=512 kernel and learned to honour `need_renorm` for softmax ([Rocm/aiter4460](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4460)).

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`: `_use_aiter_topk_gating_softmax()` decides, and the `_use_aiter` softmax branch calls `topk_gating` when it says yes. Every other shape keeps `aiter_fused_topk`.
- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: `SGLANG_ROCM_DISABLE_AITER_TOPK_GATING`, default off. Set it to 1 to fall back to `fused_topk`.
- `test/registered/amd/test_qwen38_moe_softmax_topk_gating.py`: agreement with the legacy launcher at 4, 128, 1024, 1025, 2048 and 4096 rows at hidden sizes 8192 and 2560, so both aiter kernels are covered up to the ceiling, plus every envelope boundary.

The dispatch: gfx95, AITER on, hidden size 8192 (Qwen3.8) or 2560 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next), BF16 hidden states, BF16 contiguous gating output, 512 experts, at most 4096 rows, no correction bias, no fused shared slots, no packed output.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X node, TP8, SGLang v0.5.19. GSM8K is 5-shot, 1314 items, thinking on. NIAH is `niah_single_2` at 65,536 / 131,072.

| Arm | GSM8K | NIAH 65k / 131k |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MTP baseline | 0.978 | 0.998 / 1.000 |
| MTP this PR | 0.978 | 0.990 / 1.00 |
| non-MTP baseline | 0.979 | 0.998 / 0.998 |
| non-MTP this PR | 0.978 | 0.998 / 0.994 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8x MI355X, TP8, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4, `chunked-prefill-size 16384, page-size 64`. 12 cells per arm: 8k/1k at concurrency 4 through 256, 60k/600 at 4, 16 and 64, 128k/1k at 4 and 16. Geomeans of output tok/s. 

The four arms ran on the same node and differ only in which kernel the softmax router call reaches:

- **baseline**: v0.5.19 as released. Every router call goes through `aiter_fused_topk`, which for `(512, 10)` lands on the vendored `topkGatingSoftmax`.
- **aiter `topk_gating`, no ceiling**: this PR without the 4096-row limit. Every router call, including the 16384-token prefill chunks, goes to `topk_gating`. Above 1024 rows `topk_gating` switches from the E=512 kernel to a shared-memory kernel, which loses to `topkGatingSoftmax` above 4096 rows (see the microbenchmark below).
- **this PR**: `topk_gating` up to 4096 rows, which covers decode, verify, draft-extend and short prefill chunks. Larger calls stay on `topkGatingSoftmax`.
- **#39986 Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024**: [#39986](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39986) sends 512-expert softmax routing to a Triton kernel, but only at hidden size 4096 (Qwen3.5) and at most 128 rows, so on main it never fires for Qwen3.8. For this arm its gate was widened to hidden size 8192 and at most 1024 rows, enough for every decode and verify step in this sweep. Larger calls stay on `topkGatingSoftmax`.

Non-MTP:

| Arm | out tok/s geomean | TTFT geomean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| baseline, `topkGatingSoftmax` | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
| aiter `topk_gating`, no ceiling | 1.0142 | 0.9872 |
| **this PR** | **1.0148** | 0.9859 |
| [#39986](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39986) Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024 | 1.0160 | 0.9891 |

NEXTN MTP, 3 steps / eagle-topk 1 / 4 draft tokens:

| Arm | out tok/s geomean | accept length | TTFT geomean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 1.0000 | ~4.00 | 1.0000 |
| aiter `topk_gating`, no ceiling | 1.0211 | ~4.00 | 0.9906 |
| **this PR** | **1.0222** | ~4.00 | 1.0009 |
| [#39986](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39986) Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024 | 1.0199 | ~4.00 | 0.9966 |

On v0.5.19 at page size 64, MTP gains more because verify and draft-extend add router launches per accepted token. On v0.5.20 at the default page size it gains less. Decode, verify and draft run in CUDA graphs; prefill runs eager (`prefill.backend='disabled'` in the server log, confirmed in the traces).

The #39986 Triton arm lands within 0.25% of this PR in both modes (0.12% above without MTP, 0.23% below with MTP), inside run-to-run spread, so end to end the two routers tie on Qwen3.8. The microbenchmark below shows where each kernel is faster and why this PR uses `topk_gating`.

End to end, the ceiling is worth 0.06% without MTP and 0.11% with it, inside run-to-run spread, so the case for it rests on the kernel census. Concurrency 4, TP0 trace, router launches (one per layer per forward):

| Arm | Cell | `topkGatingSoftmax` | E=512 kernel | aiter smem | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 8k/100 | 9476 | 0 | 0 | 9476 |
| baseline | 60k/100 | 10580 | 0 | 0 | 10580 |
| no ceiling | 8k/100 | 0 | 9200 | 276 | 9476 |
| no ceiling | 60k/100 | 0 | 9202 | 1380 | 10582 |
| **with ceiling** | 8k/100 | 276 | 9200 | 0 | 9476 |
| **with ceiling** | 60k/100 | 1380 | 9201 | 0 | 10581 |

Without a ceiling the prefill chunks (3 x 92 at 8k, 15 x 92 at 60k) land on aiter's slower shared-memory kernel; with it they go back to the legacy launcher and decode keeps the E=512 kernel.

Microbenchmark, gfx950, E=512, topk=10, softmax, bf16, median of 3 runs of 200 iters, us. Graph times 20 calls replayed from a CUDA graph, which is what decode sees. Triton is #39986's router.

| rows | eager: legacy | eager: `topk_gating` | eager: Triton | graph: legacy | graph: `topk_gating` | graph: Triton |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 14.70 | **11.47** | 20.50 | 9.26 | 4.74 | **4.20** |
| 1024 | 15.56 | **12.28** | 21.18 | 9.42 | 5.50 | **4.75** |
| 2048 | 15.57 | **11.98** | 21.18 | 9.44 | 9.73 | **6.57** |
| 4096 | 15.53 | **12.00** | 21.61 | 11.50 | 11.63 | **10.78** |
| 5120 | 14.86 | **12.53** | 20.66 | **11.51** | 12.92 | 12.66 |
| 6144 | 15.02 | **13.68** | 20.82 | **11.58** | 14.10 | 14.55 |
| 7168 | **14.88** | 15.16 | 20.84 | **11.58** | 15.18 | 15.95 |
| 8192 | **14.89** | 16.55 | 20.85 | **11.64** | 16.51 | 17.93 |
| 16384 | **18.74** | 28.20 | 32.30 | **18.56** | 28.58 | 32.60 |

Graph times approximate kernel GPU time; eager times include launch overhead. On GPU time `topk_gating` leads through 1024 rows, is within 0.3 us of legacy at 2048 and 4096, and falls clearly behind from 5120 (12.92 vs 11.51 us, 28.58 vs 18.56 at 16384). Eager it stays ahead through 6144. The ceiling is 4096, the largest size where it is within noise on GPU time and still ahead eager.

Why `topk_gating` rather than extending #39986 to Qwen3.8. Under CUDA graphs the Triton kernel is the fastest of the three, 0.5-0.75 us per call up to 1024 rows. Decode, verify and draft replay from graphs, so that lead is real, but it is small next to a decode step: in the TP0 traces Triton saves 9-20 us per graph replay of 7.7-14.2 ms, 0.1-0.15% of GPU time, which is why the end-to-end numbers above tie.

Where they differ is eager. Triton is the slowest of the three there (about 21 us per call, against 12 us for `topk_gating` and 15 us for `topkGatingSoftmax`), but those times are mostly launch overhead, so this matters only for prefills short enough to be launch-bound, which this sweep did not measure.

The two PRs don't conflict. #39986 fires only at hidden size 4096 (Qwen3.5) and this PR only at 8192 (Qwen3.8) and 2560 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next). 

Without [Rocm/aiter5334](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5334), `topk_gating` falls back to a generic kernel at 8.0-9.2 us in graphs through 1024 rows, barely ahead of legacy.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, measured by @amd-nprotaso in review: output tok/s +2.17%, median TPOT 7.71 -> 7.54 ms (-2.25%). Accept length came out 0.7% higher on the patch side, so per decode step the gain is -1.4% (17.84 -> 17.59 ms). 

Not measured: other 512-expert models, which keep their current dispatch; short-prompt prefill (chunks <= 4096 rows) end to end; gfx942; anything outside TP8/EP1.

title: [ROCm][DSA] Enable AITER fused FP8 indexer writer
author: fanxingran
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

On HIP, the DSA FP8 indexer writer currently issues a chain of small kernels (K LayerNorm, joint Q/K RoPE, optional Hadamard, Q/K FP8 quant, and the paged index-K cache store). That launch overhead shows up on decode ITL, especially the tail.

CUDA already fuses the analogous indexer writer (`SGLANG_DISABLE_DSA_INDEXER_FUSION`, default on). This PR adds the ROCm counterpart via AITER `indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache`, so HIP can fuse RoPE + K LayerNorm + FP8 quant + cache write into one kernel. Hadamard is omitted, matching the CUDA fused writer (pre-quant logits stay aligned).

The path is **default-on** when AITER is available and indexer geometry matches (`head_dim=128`, `rope_dim=64`, `quant_block=128`, index-K LayerNorm). Models that do not match (including RMSNorm index-K) keep the legacy split writer. Set `SGLANG_AITER_FUSED_FP8_DSA_INDEXER=0` to force the split path.

Validated on GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (gfx950). Any DSA indexer with the same geometry can take this path; it is not hardcoded to a model name.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/fp8_fused_writer_hip.py`: AITER adapter (geometry checks, RoPE table reshape, fused Q/K write).
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer.py`: enable fused writer when HIP + AITER + geometry match; LayerNorm in fp32 only on the fused path; warn only if the env is explicitly set and unsupported.
- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: `SGLANG_AITER_FUSED_FP8_DSA_INDEXER = EnvBool(True)`.
- Tests:
  - `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_fp8_fused_writer_hip.py`
  - `test/registered/amd/test_fp8_fused_dsa_writer_gfx950.py`

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K via local `sglang.test.run_eval` (1314 questions), GLM-5.2-MXFP4, baseline = fused off (`SGLANG_AITER_FUSED_FP8_DSA_INDEXER=0`).

| | Baseline | Fused |
|---|---:|---:|
| Score | 0.935 | 0.936 |

No accuracy regression. Server log contains `Enabled AITER fused FP8 DSA indexer writer`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hardware: gfx950. Workload: InferenceX AgentX, **1200s** (not the 3600s publication window). Toggle only `SGLANG_AITER_FUSED_FP8_DSA_INDEXER`. Interactivity = output token throughput per user; TPOT = ITL.

### TP4 / EP4 / concurrency 8, HiCache DRAM

Request mix is aligned (510 vs 518 completed; ISL/OSL mean 103925/568 vs 104042/563).

| Metric | Baseline | Fused | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| P90 interactivity (tok/s/user) | 190.02 | 194.48 | **+2.4%** |
| P90 E2E-norm interactivity | 153.12 | 157.97 | **+3.2%** |
| P50 interactivity | 135.78 | 137.08 | +1.0% |
| TTFT p90 | 1.197 s | 1.225 s | +2.3% |
| TPOT p90 | 13.0 ms | 12.5 ms | **−3.8%** |
| TPOT avg | 9.19 ms | 8.64 ms | **−6.0%** |
| TPOT p99 | 40.5 ms | 34.1 ms | **−15.7%** |
| E2E latency p90 | 10.85 s | 9.80 s | −9.6% |
| Throughput / chip | 10832 tok/s | 11013 tok/s | +1.7% |
| Output throughput | 235.5 tok/s | 236.9 tok/s | +0.6% |
| Completed requests | 510 | 518 | — |

Gain is mainly decode tail latency (p99 ITL), not prefill.

### TP8 / EP1 / concurrency 1, no HiCache

Request count 155 vs 157; ISL aligned. **OSL mean 646 vs 582**, so E2E and output throughput are **not** causal. Use interactivity / ITL.

| Metric | Baseline | Fused | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| P90 interactivity (tok/s/user) | 244.64 | 252.77 | **+3.3%** |
| P90 E2E-norm interactivity | 214.62 | 224.71 | **+4.7%** |
| P50 interactivity | 234.51 | 241.99 | +3.2% |
| TTFT p90 | 1.689 s | 1.557 s | **−7.8%** |
| TPOT p90 | 4.64 ms | 4.53 ms | **−2.3%** |
| TPOT p99 | 7.20 ms | 6.92 ms | **−4.0%** |
| Completed requests | 155 | 157 | — |

title: [Fix] [NPU] mtp: fix darft fias-v2 branch when fias v2 on
author: hanwlax
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

When using `SGLANG_NPU_USE_FIAS_V2_BSND=1` to forward with fias v2, the draft should use fias v2 too.

title: [AMD] Critical fix enabling Qwen3.8 FP8: restore dropped fused shared-expert weights
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

Text-only Qwen3.5-MoE checkpoints (architecture `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`, e.g. `Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8`) load into `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`, whose `load_weights` was missing the shared-expert fusion remapping that the multimodal `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration.load_weights` already implements. On ROCm with aiter shared-expert fusion enabled (`SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`), `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock` serves the shared expert as an extra fused MoE slot at index `num_experts`, but `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM.load_weights` kept `num_experts` unchanged and never remapped `mlp.shared_expert.*` onto that slot. Every layer's shared-expert weights were therefore silently dropped ("Parameter ...mlp.shared_expert... not found in params_dict") and the fused slot was left uninitialized, zeroing the shared expert across all layers and collapsing accuracy (gsm8k near random) while the server still loaded and served.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py`, class `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`:
  - `__init__`: compute `num_fused_shared_experts` / `enable_shared_expert_fusion` when aiter fusion is active, via a new `_get_num_fused_shared_experts()` that scans local MoE layers (PP-safe: non-local slots are `PPMissingLayer` with no `.mlp`).
  - `load_weights`: grow `make_expert_params_mapping(num_experts=...)` by the fused shared count when fusion is on; extend `fused_expert_params_mapping` with the shared-slot entries; remap `mlp.shared_expert.* -> mlp.experts.{num_experts}.*`; load the fused shared slot into `experts.w13_weight` / `experts.w2_weight`.
- This mirrors the existing, working handling in `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration.load_weights` (added in #20736 for the multimodal path) so the text-only entry class behaves identically.

## Accuracy Tests

Verified on `Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8`, TP8 / PP2, 2x MI300X, `--attention-backend aiter`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`:

| Metric | Before fix | After fix |
|---|---|---|
| `mlp.shared_expert.* not found in params_dict` warnings (per rank set) | 1104 | 0 |
| Shared expert loaded (per layer) | dropped (zeroed) | loaded into fused slot |
| Sample gsm8k generations | incoherent / wrong | coherent and correct |

Full gsm8k sweep (sglang few-shot, 1314 questions):

| Run | gsm8k score |
|---|---|
| Reference (known-good, pre-regression) | 0.9749 (97.49%) |
| After fix | 0.9741 (97.41%) |

The shared expert is loaded and accuracy matches the known-good baseline.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

N/A - this change only fixes weight loading; it does not alter the compute path or inference speed.

title: [Perf] spec: Let the FlashAttention backend capture the draft-extend CUDA graph
author: ZhouYuxuanYX
body:
## Motivation

`EagleDraftWorker._capture_cuda_graphs` decides whether to capture the
draft-extend CUDA graph from `graph_supported_backend_types`. FlashAttention
(`fa3` / `fa4`) implements that graph path already, but it is not in the list, so
EAGLE / EAGLE3 served with `--attention-backend fa3` runs **one eager
draft-extend forward per accepted chunk** while every other phase (target
verify, draft decode) replays a captured graph.

This is the common path rather than an exotic one.
`get_default_attn_backend` (`python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/model_override_base.py`)
documents and implements "We will turn on FA3 on hopper unless user use spec
decode with topk > 1 or page_size > 1", so on Hopper:

* chain-mode EAGLE (`--speculative-eagle-topk 1`) resolves to `fa3` and silently
  loses the draft-extend graph;
* tree mode (`topk > 1`) falls back to flashinfer / triton, which are in the
  list, and keeps it.

So two rows of the same benchmark table are not directly comparable today, and
the chain rows are the penalised ones.

The behaviour also contradicts the documentation.
`docs/docs/advanced_features/attention_backend.mdx:531` states:

> CUDA Graph: the decode backend is always captured; the prefill backend is
> captured only when `--speculative-attention-mode prefill`.

`--speculative-attention-mode prefill` is the default and `fa3` is the Hopper
default, so with both defaults the docs promise a captured prefill/draft-extend
graph that the code does not capture.

Finally, the symptom is invisible in the log: the server prints
`Capture target verify ...` and `Capture draft decode ...`, and simply never
prints a draft-extend line. Nothing errors out, throughput is just lower.

## Modifications

Add `FlashAttentionBackend` to `graph_supported_backend_types` in
`python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py`, plus the import. One file,
two lines.

`FlashAttentionBackend` already supports the phase on both sides:

* `init_forward_metadata_in_graph` branches on
  `forward_mode.is_draft_extend_v2()` and reads `self.draft_extend_metadata[bs]`;
* `init_forward_metadata_out_graph` has the matching `is_draft_extend_v2()`
  branch;
* `init_cuda_graph_state` allocates `draft_extend_metadata` whenever
  `speculative_num_draft_tokens` is set and `> 0`, so the capture buffers always
  exist when speculative decoding is on.

Nothing else changes: no new flags, no behaviour change for backends already in
the list, and the eager path remains the fallback for backends that are not.

## Accuracy Tests

Acceptance length is unchanged. Runs before and after the change agree to four
decimal places on the same fixed prompt set with greedy decoding, so the
captured graph is numerically equivalent to the eager path it replaces. This is
expected: the change only decides whether an already-supported forward is
replayed from a graph, not what it computes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

One 8-GPU node, an MoE target with a single-layer MoE drafter, EAGLE chain mode,
greedy, batch size 1, fixed prompt set:

* **roughly 1.5x decode throughput** after the fix
* acceptance length unchanged (see above)
* graph capture costs about 1.5 s and 0.5 GB of device memory

The gain scales with how expensive the drafter is relative to the target,
because the eager forward is paid once per accepted chunk. A large target with a
light drafter will see much less -- there the eager draft-extend is a few
percent of a target forward and hides in run-to-run noise, which is the likely
reason this went unnoticed. Conversely a small target with a heavy drafter pays
the most.

After the fix the log gains the previously missing phase:

```
Capture draft extend CUDA graph begin. backend=full, ...
Capture draft extend CUDA graph end. elapsed=1.54 s, mem usage=0.45 GB
```

## Notes

**Why no unit test.** I tried to add a regression test asserting that every
member of `graph_supported_backend_types` really implements the draft-extend
graph, checked along the MRO so inherited implementations count (for example
`TokenspeedMLABackend` inherits it from `TRTLLMMLABackend` and overrides only
kernel-level methods). It does not work as a static assertion, because the
backends do not share a graph API surface: `FlashAttentionBackend` carries the
branches in `init_forward_metadata_in_graph` / `init_forward_metadata_out_graph`,
while `DeepseekV4AttnBackend` expresses the same capability through its own
`_GraphBucket.DRAFT_EXTEND`. Any such test ends up either special-casing each
backend or restating the list, so it would assert nothing. Happy to add an
end-to-end test instead if maintainers prefer -- the natural assertion is that
`cuda_graph_runner_for_draft_extend` is not `None` for a chain-mode EAGLE server
launched with `--attention-backend fa3`, which needs a GPU runner.

**Docs.** `attention_backend.mdx:531` (quoted above) becomes true for `fa3` with
this change, but it is still unconditional in a way the code is not: the prefill
backend is captured only when it is also in `graph_supported_backend_types`.
Flashinfer on an MLA model, for instance, resolves to `FlashInferMLAAttnBackend`
(`draft_utils.py`, `_create_flashinfer_prefill_backend`), which is not in the
list. Happy to add the qualifying clause in this PR or a follow-up, whichever
maintainers prefer.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (See Notes.)
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (See Notes.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [JIT] Add an occupancy-preserving L1 carveout preference
author: metamergebot
body:
# Summary

A PDL secondary can inherit a preceding GEMM's large shared-memory partition and lose L1 capacity. Add an opt-in L1 preference to the shared kernel launcher that searches for the smallest shared-memory carveout retaining the kernel's default occupancy.

The preference is memoized per kernel and device and can be configured at module load or lazily through `LaunchKernel`. Existing upstream kernels retain their default policy; this exposes the reusable API for callers that need it. ROCm retains its occupancy query without setting a CUDA attribute. Memoized callers must use fixed block dimensions and dynamic shared-memory size for each kernel/device pair.

Beyond the port, add a CUDA regression test covering occupancy preservation, default-policy launches, raw-stream and device-based launches, repeated calls, exact output equality, and isolation from unused GPUs; document the memoization preconditions.

# Test plan

- `PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda uv run --no-project --python ../venv/bin/python pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/elementwise/test_launch_carveout.py`: **1 passed** on GB300 with CUDA 13.1 and PyTorch 2.9.0+cu130. This local environment differs from the repository's pinned PyTorch version.
- `uv run --no-project --python ../venv/bin/python pre-commit run --files python/sglang/kernels/jit/include/sgl_kernel/utils.cuh test/registered/kernels/ops/elementwise/launch_carveout.cuh test/registered/kernels/ops/elementwise/test_launch_carveout.py`: **passed**.
- Standalone CUDA probe: **passed** occupancy preservation, output identity, memoization, and configuration on a second device with restoration of the current device. A MaxL1-only control failed the occupancy assertion as expected.
- Not run locally: ROCm compilation, model evaluation, or end-to-end performance benchmarks. This PR enables no production caller and claims no upstream model speedup.

title: [NVIDIA][MegaMoE] Fix the default spec decoding moe backend when the target model uses flashinfer megamoe
author: wenscarl
body:
## Summary

- Fixes an `illegal memory access` crash (sgl-project/sglang#40623) that occurs when `--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_megamoe` is combined with `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE` on a checkpoint whose MTP/NextN draft layer is unquantized (e.g. GLM-5.2-NVFP4, DeepSeek-NVFP4). The draft's MoE runner/a2a backend silently inherited the target's `flashinfer_megamoe`, so `StandardDispatcher.skip_local_expert_mapping` (`token_dispatcher/standard.py`) assumed the mega kernel's own global-expert-ID routing and skipped the EP global->local expert-id remap — but the unquantized draft layer actually falls back to the plain Triton MoE kernel, which needs that remap. Under EP (`ep_size > 1`) this feeds Triton out-of-range expert indices into EP-sharded local weight tensors, crashing `invoke_fused_moe_kernel`.
- `_speculative_moe_runner_default` (`arg_groups/overrides.py`) now falls back to `auto` instead of `flashinfer_megamoe` when defaulting the speculative runner backend from the target's backend; `initialize_moe_config()` (`layers/moe/utils.py`) applies the same default for both `speculative_a2a_backend` and `speculative_runner_backend` for call paths that construct the MoE flags directly (e.g. benchmark scripts) rather than through the full CLI resolution pipeline. `--speculative-moe-runner-backend` / `--speculative-moe-a2a-backend` still take precedence when set explicitly.
- Adds `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` (GLM-5.2/5.3-NVFP4) to `validate_flashinfer_megamoe_model`'s supported-architectures list, so megamoe is reachable for this family at all.

## Root cause

- `create_moe_dispatcher` (`layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py`) routes both `a2a_backend.is_none()` and `a2a_backend.is_flashinfer_megamoe()` to the same `StandardDispatcher` class.
- `StandardDispatcher.__init__` (`layers/moe/token_dispatcher/standard.py`) independently reads `get_moe_runner_backend()` to decide `skip_local_expert_mapping`; it skips the remap whenever the ACTIVE runner backend is `flashinfer_megamoe`, trusting the mega kernel to route by global expert ID internally.
- `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod.create_moe_runner` (`layers/quantization/unquant.py`) has no `flashinfer_megamoe` branch, so an unquantized layer (the MTP/NextN draft) always falls through to the plain Triton runner regardless of the configured backend.
- Because `speculative_moe_runner_backend` defaulted to inheriting the target's `moe_runner_backend`, the draft's dispatcher believed it was running the mega kernel (skipping the remap) while its actual runner was Triton (which needs the remap) — global-space expert IDs then index into EP-sharded local weight tensors sized for only `num_experts / ep_size` experts.

## Repro

DEP4 on Blackwell:

​```bash

python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/glm-5.2-nvpf4 \
  --load-format dummy \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --dp-size 4 \
  --enable-dp-attention \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_megamoe \
  --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.7
​```

Before this fix: crashes during CUDA graph capture of the draft decode step with `RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered` (`invoke_fused_moe_kernel`). `--speculative-moe-a2a-backend none --speculative-moe-runner-backend triton` is necessary to workaround. After this fix, `server_args` resolves `speculative_moe_runner_backend=auto` / `speculative_moe_a2a_backend=none`, the server starts cleanly, and `/generate` requests (and a gsm8k `bench_sglang.py` smoke run) complete without crashing.

cc. @nvpohanh 
## Test plan

- [x] Manual repro above on a Blackwell (SM100) node: server starts and serves requests without the illegal-memory-access crash.
- [ ] `test/registered/unit/test_runtime_context.py::TestMoeFlagsGroup`: add a case asserting `speculative_a2a_backend`/`speculative_runner_backend` default to `none`/`auto` when the target backend is `flashinfer_megamoe` and the speculative flags are unset, and that explicit `--speculative-moe-runner-backend`/`--speculative-moe-a2a-backend` still override.

title: [JIT] Fuse FP8 KV-cache quantization into the prefix-valid commit kernel
author: JiaFengYu
body:
## Motivation

  MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid commits accepted-prefix KV rows after DFLASH verification. With --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 and checkpoint KV scales, the existing path performs:

  1. In-place scale division for K
  2. In-place scale division for V
  3. K cast to FP8
  4. V cast to FP8
  5. Triton byte-copy/scatter

  This is five GPU kernel launches per layer and introduces full HBM round-trips for the intermediate scaled tensors. Without explicit scales, the path still requires two casts plus the scatter kernel.

  This PR fuses source-dtype scaling, FP8 conversion, and prefix-valid scatter into one Triton kernel.

  ## Modifications

  - Added set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid_tiled_fp8 in cache_move.py.
      - Preserves the existing (batch, row, tile) structure, commit_lens early exit, and loc_2d indirection.
      - Uses element-based offsets and strides rather than byte-based addressing.
      - Receives typed source and FP8 destination pointers.
      - Divides in FP32 registers, rounds back to the source dtype to reproduce eager div_ semantics, then casts directly to the destination FP8 type.
      - Supports BF16, FP16, and FP32 sources.
      - Performs no intermediate allocation, source-tensor write, or HBM round-trip.

  - Added _set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid_impl_fp8 in memory_pool.py.
      - Mirrors the original empty-input and contiguity guards.
      - Computes its grid, strides, and tile sizes in elements.
      - Passes zero-copy FP8 views of SGLang’s uint8-backed KV buffers so Triton infers correctly typed destination pointers.

  - Added narrow dispatch in MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid.
      - Fused path requires an E4M3 KV cache and safely resolved K/V scales.
      - Python scalars and CPU scalar tensors are accepted directly.
      - GPU layer scale parameters use their existing k_scale_float/v_scale_float shadows without host synchronization.
      - Unsupported tensor scales, missing scales, non-FP8 caches, CPU execution, and asymmetric K/V rows retain the existing fallback.
      - The eager fallback continues using the original scale objects, including GPU tensors.

  - Threaded the draft model’s resolved quant_config into DFlashAttention’s RadixAttention.
      - This enables the existing Fp8KVCacheMethod for online-FP8 DFLASH drafts.
      - It initializes the KV scale parameters and float shadows required by the fused dispatch.
      - No new scale-loading mechanism or global configuration mutation was added.

  - Unlike the eager div_ path, the fused path does not mutate the input K/V tensors. Intermediate scaled values remain in registers and only the final FP8 cache is written.

  ## Accuracy Tests

  Added test_prefix_valid_fp8.py with coverage for:

  - Exact FP8 byte parity against the eager div_ → FP8 reference for BF16, FP16, and FP32 inputs.
  - Every tile-size branch and masked epilogue rows using row dimensions 63, 2048, and 4097.
  - Mixed per-request commit_lens.
  - Noncontiguous source tensors.
  - Separate K/V scales.
  - Representable FP8 limits, NaN, and signed zero.
  - Untouched destination slots.
  - GPU scale parameters with float shadows.
  - GPU tensor scales without float shadows taking the eager fallback.
  - Missing-scale fallback.
  - Non-FP8 cache fallback.
  - Input non-mutation on the fused path.

  Local CUDA validation:

  NVIDIA B200
  PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130
  Triton 3.7.1
  7 tests passed

  ROCm coverage is registered in jit-kernel-unit-test-amd but has not yet been run locally.

  ## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Test configuration

- **GPU:** NVIDIA B200
- **CUDA:** CUDA 13
- **Target model:** `NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`
- **Draft model:** `z-lab/LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct-DFlash-UltraChat`
- **KV-cache dtype:** `fp8_e4m3`
- **Draft quantization:** `fp8`
- **Attention backends:** Triton target and draft
- **Batch size:** 4
- **Output length:** 48 tokens per request
- **Acceptance length:** fixed at 4 to deterministically exercise prefix commits
- **CUDA graphs:** enabled

The benchmark-only baseline retained the same DFLASH quantization configuration and scales, but forced `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid` through the existing eager fallback.

### Kernel engagement

The profiler recorded 65 prefix commits in both variants:

| Variant | Legacy `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid_tiled` | Fused `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid_tiled_fp8` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Eager fallback | 65 | 0 |
| Fused | 0 | 65 |

This confirms that the A/B comparison exercised the intended implementations without mixing the legacy and fused commit paths.

### Prefix-commit GPU time

| Variant | Kernel sequence | Median GPU time per layer |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Eager fallback | K division + V division + K FP8 cast + V FP8 cast + byte-copy store | 14.528 us |
| Fused | Required source-layout copy + fused FP8 quantize/store | 4.864 us |
| **Speedup** |  | **2.99x** |

The fused Triton kernel alone measured 1.951 us per layer. The 4.864 us result above includes the preceding source-layout copy and is therefore the fair implementation-level comparison.

This establishes a **2.99x improvement in the prefix-valid FP8 commit GPU cluster for this fixed-shape B200 workload**. It is not a claim of a 2.99x end-to-end request speedup.

### End-to-end A/B

A separate process-level benchmark ran 10 alternating A/B pairs. Each variant received 10 warmup batches followed by 100 measured batch-4 requests per pair.

The mean paired request-p50 saving was 0.25 ms, with a 95% bootstrap confidence interval of `[-0.96, +1.11]` ms. Because the confidence interval crosses zero, no statistically significant end-to-end latency improvement is claimed.

title: [Fix] Use cached prefix lengths for FlashInfer full-attention ragged prefill
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

In a mixed sliding-window/full-attention model, FlashInfer ragged prefill plans the full-attention layer's paged read over `seq_lens`. The new K/V is not written to the cache until after attention, and the ragged wrapper already handles those tokens. Reading their cache slots can therefore mix stale K/V into the result.

## Modifications

- Plan the full-attention paged read over `prefix_lens` when ragged prefill is active. Use the host prefix total when available, retaining the existing device-sum fallback pattern.
- Add one deterministic GPU regression to the existing FlashInfer SWA suite. It poisons unwritten extend slots and checks the real attention output. No model checkpoint is needed.

Paged-only execution is unchanged. Two files; eight backend lines added.

## Accuracy Tests

On NVIDIA B300, using upstream `7b977ce5dcce6e61f0a5f8ef8b4235e42eb00299`, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.6.18, and sglang-kernel 0.4.7+cu130:

- New regression on unmodified upstream: fails numerically, maximum absolute error **14.0** against tolerance **0.04**. The same test passes with the fix.
- FlashInfer SWA suite: **8 passed**. Dense suite: **8 passed**. No skips. The regression also passes with the optional host prefix list omitted.
- Public-model reachability: `unsloth/gemma-3-1b-it` at `5b11413a10db4e486ef16a20101fd028f8f2499c`, BF16, TP1, FlashInfer, page size 1, eager execution. Actual full-attention forwards use the ragged path. With a 384-token prompt and 257 cached tokens, the full wrapper plans 384 cache slots before the fix and 257 afterward.
- For three frozen prompts below the sliding-window boundary, full-vocabulary next-token KL between cold and cached prefill changes from **3.50e-5 / 8.75e-5 / 4.17e-7** to **1.89e-8 / 2.76e-6 / 6.55e-8**. This is numerical cache consistency, not a model-quality evaluation. A separate cold-versus-cached discrepancy above the sliding window remains outside this fix.

Reproduce the regression:

```bash
python3 test/registered/attention/unittests/swa/test_flashinfer.py \
  TestFlashInferSWAAttentionBackendCorrectness.test_full_layer_ragged_prefill_reads_cached_prefix_only -v
```

Changed-file pre-commit hooks pass. The all-files run passes its non-Rust hooks; four Rust hooks could not execute because the local host lacks cargo/rustup. No Rust files are changed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput improvement is claimed. The normal ragged-prefill path uses the existing CPU prefix lengths without adding a device-to-host scalar read.

title: [Fix] Reduce Nemotron MTP attention outputs once
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #40871
* #40870
* #40869
* #40868
* #40867
* #40801
* __->__ #40800
* #40799

## Motivation

Under DP attention with attention TP greater than one, Nemotron MTP reduces an Attention output before calling its parent MoE forward. The parent's `prepare_mlp` already performs the reduction, so the Attention contribution is summed twice before residual addition and normalization.

## Modifications

Remove the extra MTP reduction and its now-unused predecessor flag/imports. Add a regression through the actual MTP forward and parent communicator, checking both numerical results and a single attention-TP reduction.

## Accuracy Tests

Stacking and comment cleanup preserve the executable AST of the tested revisions.

- The new regression fails on main and passes with this fix (TP1/TP2).

- Pre-commit checks pass, including CI registration validation.

The GPU probe supplies synthetic Attention partials and uses an identity MoE to isolate preparation. Full-checkpoint MTP decoding has not been run.

No performance benchmark. This removes one redundant attention-TP all-reduce per affected MTP MoE invocation.

title: [RL] Keep DSA cuda-graph state and the graph pool intact across TMS pause/resume
author: yueming-yuan
body:
## Motivation

In RL colocation the engine releases the `GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_CUDA_GRAPH` torch-memory-saver region while the trainer runs and resumes it before the next rollout. Two things break on main:

1. The full-cuda-graph pool holds capture-time-initialized device state that replays read but never rewrite. Pausing discards it, so the first replay after resume reads garbage.
2. DSA's wide `page_table` (`max_num_tokens x max_ctx_len` int32) and the flashmla metadata stay resident during training even though they are rewritten in full before every replay.

## Modifications

- `FullCudaGraphBackend`: pass `enable_cpu_backup=True` to the memory-saver `cuda_graph` context so the pool is backed up on pause and restored on resume.
- `DeepseekSparseAttnBackend.init_cuda_graph_state`: allocate `page_table` and `flashmla_metadata` inside the pausable cuda-graph region (gated on `--enable-memory-saver` and `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH`). The other decode metadata is written once at init and stays outside the region.

Squash of sglang-miles #32718, #33479 (authors credited as co-authors).

## Testing

pre-commit clean. Relying on CI for GPU: `test/registered/rl/test_release_memory_occupation*.py` and the DSA cuda-graph paths under `test/registered/rl/`.

title: [AMD][Quark] Serve the Kimi-K3 MXFP4 checkpoint on ROCm
author: yuychang
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Loading [AMD Quark's Kimi-K3 checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/amd/Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8) (per-channel FP8 dense layers + MXFP4 MoE) on ROCm fails or runs incorrectly in several places:

- hipBLASLt needs the FP8 GEMM's N to be a multiple of 16. K3's KDA `b_proj` has 12 output channels at TP=8, so `torch._scaled_mm` raises.
- AITER's MLA absorb GEMM only takes a scalar `w_scale`, but Quark stores `kv_b_proj` with one scale per channel. Collapsing those into a single per-tensor scale gives ~2.3% relative error on real K3 weights.
- K3's fused KDA projection merge concatenates `.weight` only. On a quantized checkpoint this silently drops the scale tensors.
- AITER pads the MXFP4 MoE W2 width from 384 to 512 at TP8. That adds 33% zero work and stops the native-shape tuning table from matching. The SiTU activation path also expects a GU-interleaved preshuffled layout, which Quark's MoE scheme didn't produce.

## Modifications

- **`quark_w8a8_fp8.py`**: On ROCm, if an FP8 linear's output partition width isn't a multiple of 16, dequantize it to `out_dtype` at load time and serve it with a dense matmul. At that width the layer is memory-bound, so this costs little.
- **`kimi_k3_rocm_quant.py`** (new): `_k3_channel_fp8_to_bf16` converts a per-channel FP8 weight to bf16 using each channel's own scale (~0.12% error, compared with ~2.3% for a single per-tensor scale).
- **`kimi_k3.py`**:
  - On ROCm, fold `kv_b_proj`'s per-channel FP8 scale into a bf16 weight before the `w_kc`/`w_vc` head split. `w_scale` stays at its 1.0 default in that case, and also whenever the scale isn't a single scalar.
  - Add a `_merge_dtype_ok` check (bf16/fp16 only) so quantized weights skip the fused `b_proj`/`f_a_proj` and `qkvg` merges.
- **`quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py`**:
  - When `SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT` is set, skip AITER's 128-alignment padding and keep the checkpoint's intermediate width.
  - For SiTU, when AITER selects the A8W4/A16W4 kernels, preshuffle into the GU-interleaved layout with `shuffle_weight_a16w4`/`shuffle_scale_a16w4`.
- **Tests**: Add CPU unit tests for the narrow-partition dequant fallback (including the aligned-width and non-ROCm cases where it must not run), the per-channel dequant, and the merge dtype check.

## Accuracy Tests

| Benchmark | Accuracy |
|---|---|
| GSM8K | 0.942 |


## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. Correctness fixes, except the opt-in `SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT` path, which removes 33% of the zero-padded MoE W2 work at TP8.

title: [sglang-miles] Colocated RL for hybrid-state models: flush order and bf16 MoE weight-update layout
author: Zhichenzzz
body:
Fixes needed for colocated RL on hybrid-state models (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, GLM-5.3-Flash) on current `sglang-miles`. Supersedes #40815, which is folded in here as the first commit.

## Motivation

1. **Hybrid state pools fault with CUDA error 700 at memory release.** `release_memory_occupation` paused (unmapped) the KV cache memory-saver region and only then called `flush_cache()`. The hybrid pools cleared there (mamba states, qwen4_exp PLE `ShortConvPool` / `NgramPool`, KDA state) live inside that region and their `clear()` writes device memory, so the write hits unmapped memory. With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` the fault lands on `ShortConvPool.clear()` via `release_memory_occupation -> flush_cache -> HybridReqToTokenPool.clear`. The trainer's later `/flush_cache` while the engine is offloaded faults the same way.
2. **bf16 MoE weight update crashes on plain `flashinfer_trtllm`.** The TRT-LLM bf16 postprocess repacks `w13`/`w2` into block layout for every TRT-LLM MoE runner variant, but `maybe_restore_flashinfer_trtllm_bf16_weight_shape_for_load` only restored the canonical shape for `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`. On GB300 the auto backend resolves to plain `flashinfer_trtllm`, so the first weight sync failed with `size of tensor a (64) must match tensor b (4096) at dimension 2`.

## Modifications

1. `weight_updater.py`: flush before tagging the KV region as offloaded and pausing it (the tag is what makes the later flush a no-op). `Scheduler.flush_cache`: return success without clearing while the KV region is released (the pools were flushed right before the pause).
2. `unquant.py`: gate the shape restore on `self.use_flashinfer_trtllm_moe`, the same flag that gates the repack.
3. `qsa/mqa.py`: the prefill indexer walks its key tiles with a serial loop. tilelang 0.1.14 only pipelines constant trip counts and rejected `T.ceildiv(end_max - start_min, block_n)` at codegen (`Downcast from tirx.Sub to ir.IntImm failed`), which broke every Qwen4Exp prefill on images built with that release (the miles CI image). Logits are bitwise identical on 0.1.9; an 8k x 8k prefill costs about 10% more per QSA layer on GB300.

## Validation

Full-model colocated RL e2e, 8 nodes x 4 GB300, latest `radixark/miles:dev`, `--colocate`, R3 routing replay, CUDA graph on:

- radixark/miles#2777 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next): without fix 1, all four engines die with CUDA error 700 at the first memory release. With it: 5 rollouts / 5 train steps, weight-update equality check passes, `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` 0.0083 to 0.0131, raw reward 0.47 to 0.75.
- radixark/miles#2786 (GLM-5.3-Flash bf16): 4 rollouts / 3 train steps, `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` 0.0085 / 0.0098 / 0.0087, raw reward 0.50 to 0.72; routed experts were captured with the triton runner, which the miles launcher now pins for routing replay (the resolver guard was dropped from this PR).

title: [Feat] [NPU] kimi-k3: Support DCP with shared compact communication
author: qybnb
body:
## Motivation Enable decode context parallelism (DCP) for Kimi-K3 on Ascend NPU, including DSPARK speculative decoding. Sharding the target model's MLA KV cache across DCP ranks reduces per-rank KV storage for a given logical context capacity. ## Implementation - **KV layout:** distribute target MLA latent and RoPE buffers by physical page. Localize cache-write locations to the owning rank, while keeping draft KV replicated. - **Prefill/extend:** all-gather the cached target prefix and restore token order before the existing MLA attention computation. Replicated draft workers read their complete local cache. - **Decode/target verify:** reuse the common Q all-gather, compute attention over each rank's local KV pages, and merge partial results through compact AllToAll with BF16/FP16 outputs and FP32 LSE. Eager target verification with no real queries returns zero partial outputs and `-inf` LSE for collective participation. - **Eager and graph execution:** derive rank-local KV lengths, block tables, and per-query visibility from page ownership. Graph replay uses the backend's prepared local CPU lengths and pads graph-only request rows with zero; the FIA CPU length mirror is required. - **P/D transfer:** support prefill DCP=1 to decode DCP=N with Ascend page transfers. Hybrid MLA uses the common layer-ID pairing helper across PP stages and selects local target pages and global replicated draft pages directly in `AscendKVManager.send_kvcache_dcp()` using `num_draft_entries`. DSA retains its per-entry pool layout metadata; KDA state uses its existing state-transfer path. Shared pool and prefill files are unchanged. ## Validation - 17 CPU regression tests pass with production imports in an isolated CANN 9.2 overlay. Coverage includes 20 hybrid PP/draft/buffer-width transfer combinations that reject layout-helper calls, DSA index-buffer transfer addresses, and invalid metadata/draft-count rejection. - CPU prefix-reconstruction checks pass across 450 configurations and 2,104 rank outputs, covering DCP2/4/8, token/page interleaving, partial pages, mixed and empty prefixes, and 128K/512K contexts. - Syntax, repository-selected Ruff rules, Ruff formatting, isort, and diff checks pass for the tested files. Two existing E402 findings remain in `npu_graph_runner.py`. These CPU checks do not validate native NPU kernels or full-model serving. Full-model accuracy, throughput/latency, and P/D end-to-end validation for the current head remain pending. The model results below are reference measurements and have not been reproduced on this head. ## Run Four-node DSPARK example. Replace the paths, node addresses, distributed initialization address, and network interface with the deployment values. Ascend DCP requires `ASCEND_USE_FIA=1`; this example uses `--dcp-comm-backend a2a`.

title: [Fix] Give the full prefill CUDA graph replay view the captured bucket's input_ids
author: metamergebot
body:
# Summary

Full prefill CUDA graph replay refreshes the attention metadata through `init_forward_metadata_out_graph` on a slot-padded shallow view of the live `ForwardBatch`. The view already carries the captured bucket's `batch_size`, `seq_lens`, `req_pool_indices`, `extend_seq_lens`, `extend_prefix_lens` and `max_seq_len_override`, but its `input_ids` was still the live batch's, i.e. fewer token rows than the captured kernels run over.

An attention backend that sizes anything in that hook from `forward_batch.input_ids` (a per-row plan, a scratch buffer, a token count) therefore planned for the real token count while the replayed kernels consume the padded one, and had to re-plan per call to stay correct. The view now takes `input_ids` from the static captured batch, so the hook sees the same token rows as the graph it prepares for. One line in `PrefillCudaGraphRunner._prepare_forward_metadata_for_replay`; no kernel or backend changes.

Beyond the port, the existing full-replay padding unit test now passes a distinct static batch and asserts the padded view's `input_ids` is the static batch's; without the fix that assertion fails on the 2-row live tensor.

# Test plan

- `PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_prefill_cuda_graph_padding.py`: **10 passed, 3 subtests passed** with the fix; the extended case **fails** with the production line reverted (`tensor([0, 1]) is not tensor([0, ..., 15])`).
- isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1 (`check` and `format --check`) and codespell 2.4.1 on both files: **clean**.
- Not run locally: the GPU full prefill CUDA graph suite (`test/registered/cuda_graph/full_prefill/`); left to CI.

# Source commit

`11cc4a715480d708dca16a0c8698b33c95ea5c15`

title: [mem_cache][PD] Fix decode radix cache ownership and allow EAGLE/EAGLE3 with decode radix cache
author: pyc96
body:
## Motivation

Fix KV ownership during post-insert repointing and allow `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache` with EAGLE and EAGLE3. These combinations previously failed startup validation.

### Observed failure

Seen on a 1-prefill / 1-decode deployment of gpt-oss-120b (hybrid SWA, page size 64) with EAGLE3 (3 steps, top-k 1, 4 draft tokens) and `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache` on the decode server, with the speculative-decoding guard relaxed and a 65,536-token decode KV pool. Single-turn traffic, including 500 GSM8K requests at 16 concurrency, ran clean. Multi-turn traffic (second turn = first-turn prompt + first-turn output, so the prefix hit lands on KV the decode server generated itself) then killed the decode scheduler at the next idle moment, after every request had returned HTTP 200:

```
ValueError: pool memory leak detected! [full] total=65536, available=768, evictable=65152, protected=0, session_held=0, uncached=0
[swa] total=52224, available=19136, evictable=33152, protected=0, session_held=0, uncached=0
```

`available + evictable` exceeds `total` by 384 tokens (6 pages) in the full pool and by 64 (1 page) in the SWA pool. With `SGLANG_DEBUG_MEMORY_POOL=1` and a tree walk at the failure point: the tree's size counters matched the recomputed per-node sums and `sanity_check` passed, the allocator's free list held no duplicate page, but exactly 6 full pages and 1 SWA page were referenced by a tree node **and** present on the free list — real double ownership, not a counting drift. The first shared SWA page had been freed by `maybe_evict_swa` (called from `eagle_prepare_for_decode`) for a running request while a tree node still owned it. A later run tripped the pre-existing assertion directly, in `cache_unfinished_req` during decode-side admission: `AssertionError: new_prefix_len=256, len(new_indices)=0` — the insert had overlapped 256 tokens already in the tree, and the re-match returned nothing.

The same multi-turn loop reproduced the failure within 1–5 rounds in three of four runs on the base commit. Without speculative decoding, 12 rounds did not trigger it; the bigram key is what makes the short re-match likely, not what makes it possible.


### Root cause

The previous code re-matched the prefix after insertion. A normal SWA match requires a full live window, but disaggregated decode can allocate SWA slots only for the prompt's recent tail. EAGLE's bigram key can move the page-aligned insert boundary back one page, leaving less than a full live window inside the inserted range.

The re-match can therefore stop short even though the tree already owns the whole inserted range. This leaves `cache_protected_len` too small: subsequent SWA eviction or finished-request insertion can free tree-owned slots, corrupting allocator ownership and triggering the scheduler's idle pool check.

## Modifications


Repoint unfinished requests using canonical indices collected from the final insert node to the root, and assert that they cover the entire page-aligned insert. With this ownership fix in place, extend the speculative-algorithm allowlist and update the CLI help to match.

title: [AMD][DSV4] fp8 unified_kv decode: wave-aware split count past 40 tokens
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
## Motivation

In the fp8 two-pool unified_kv decode path (#37413), `decode_fp8_2buff` pins `num_kv_splits=4` for every call with more than 40 tokens. The aiter v4 nm kernel it calls holds one workgroup per CU and launches T × splits workgroups. On MI355X (256 CUs), once T > 64 the fixed 4 needs two or more waves, and the call roughly doubles. DSpark verify hits this early, since T = 6 × concurrency.

## Modifications

- `decode_fp8_2buff` takes `compress_ratio`. For T > 40 it picks the largest split count up to 4 that fits one wave (`CU // T`), and uses 1 for the 128-row SWA stream.
- The backend passes the layer's `compress_ratio`. Callers that pass nothing keep the old fixed 4. T ≤ 40 is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

gsm8k (1319 questions, `few_shot_gsm8k --parallel 64`), DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 with DSpark, so decode goes past 40 tokens:

| | runs | accuracy |
|---|---|---|
| fp8, before | 3 | 0.942 / 0.944 / 0.943 |
| fp8, this PR | 3 | 0.947 / 0.950 / 0.947 |
| bf16 unified_kv | 1 | 0.942 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X, 16 heads (TP8), stock aiter, one v4 nm call including the merge, µs, fixed 4 → this PR:

| stream | T=96 | T=128 | T=192 | T=256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HCA (192 rows) | 27.7 → 20.5 | 30.2 → 21.5 | 41.4 → 20.5 | 52.4 → 21.7 |
| CSA (1152 rows) | 54.4 → 46.6 | 57.1 → 48.4 | 83.6 → 68.2 | 108.2 → 69.5 |

DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, TP8, fp8 unified_kv, DSpark, 8192/1024, image `v0.5.20-rocm724-mi35x-20260922`. Median ITL in ms, mean of 6 runs:

| concurrency | before | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 4.58 | 4.49 | −2.1% |
| 32 | 5.84 | 5.66 | −3.2% |
| 64 | 8.05 | 7.69 | −4.5% |

At c=8 DSpark T is 48, where the split count stays at 4. Plain decode up to c=64 keeps T ≤ 64, so it is unaffected.

title: [AMD] Drop the unreachable vLLM fallback from ROCm FP8 activation quant
author: siliangchen-amd
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #40557: The reviewer asked why `_has_vllm` is still kept.

`_has_vllm` in `fp8_kernel.py` is only ever set inside `if _is_hip:`, and only in the arm where `_use_aiter` is false:

```python
if _is_hip:
    _has_vllm = False
    if _use_aiter:
        from aiter import dynamic_per_tensor_quant, ...
    else:
        try:
            import vllm._C
            _has_vllm = True
        except ImportError:
            _has_vllm = False
```

So the vLLM arm is selected in exactly one configuration: **ROCm, `SGLANG_USE_AITER` off, and `vllm._C` importable**. Nothing shipped reaches it:

| configuration | `SGLANG_USE_AITER` | vLLM present | vLLM arm |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` | `1` | — | never selected |
| `docker/rocm-gfx1151.Dockerfile` | `0` | not installed | never selected (native path) |
| `nightly-test-amd.yml` | `1` | — | never selected |
| `python/pyproject.toml` | — | not a dependency | — |

And the one configuration that does select it **cannot complete a forward pass on current `main`**. `RMSNorm.forward_hip` calls `fused_add_rms_norm` with AITER's 6-argument out-of-place signature; with AITER off, `layernorm.py` binds that name to vLLM's 4-argument in-place op instead. Replaying layer 0's calls in execution order in that configuration:

```
fp8_kernel: _use_aiter=False _has_vllm=True
layernorm.fused_add_rms_norm bound to vllm._custom_ops.fused_add_rms_norm

  [ok]    input_layernorm      rms_norm(out, x, w, eps)                        [4 args]
  [ok]    qkv_proj fp8 quant   scaled_fp8_quant -> vLLM arm
  [ok]    o_proj   fp8 quant   scaled_fp8_quant -> vLLM arm
  [FAIL]  post_attention_norm  fused_add_rms_norm(out, x, r_out, r, w, eps)    [6 args]
TypeError: fused_add_rms_norm() takes 4 positional arguments but 6 were given
```

A real `RMSNorm` module called with a residual fails the same way, from the dispatch it actually takes:

```
TypeError: fused_add_rms_norm() takes 4 positional arguments but 6 were given
  at sglang/kernels/fused_op.py:659 in forward
  at sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:766 in forward_hip
```

So the vLLM FP8 arm runs twice in layer 0 and then the first residual norm raises. The `fused_add_rms_norm` signature is the same in vLLM 0.26.0 and 0.27.1.

## Modifications

- Remove `_has_vllm`, the `vllm._C` import probe, and the three `elif _has_vllm:` arms (dynamic per-token, dynamic per-tensor, static). The import guard becomes `if _is_hip and _use_aiter:`.
- With AITER on, nothing changes. With AITER off, the native path takes over — the path gfx1151 already runs.
- In the per-tensor branch both remaining backends take a `torch.empty` scale, so the allocation is hoisted. The comment added in #40557, which explained why only vLLM needed the pre-zero, goes with the vLLM arm.
- The native fallbacks' docstrings said "when vLLM is unavailable"; they now say "when AITER is disabled".

One file, +13/−36.

## Accuracy Tests

The native fallback against the vLLM ops it replaces, on all three call sites: 144 cases over bf16/fp16, six shapes from `1x4096` to `4096x4096`, and gaussian, heavy-tailed and zero-row inputs. Run against both vLLM 0.27.1 and 0.26.0 with identical results.

| call site | byte agreement native/vLLM (worst) | scale ratio native/vLLM | worst reconstruction-error gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| static, calibrated scale | **100%** | 1.0000 | 0 |
| static, scale saturating 224–240 | **100%** | 1.0000 | 0 |
| dynamic per-token | 93.73% | 0.9967 – 1.0033 | +1.6e-4 |
| dynamic per-tensor | 95.01% | 0.9971 – 1.0032 | +3.4e-4 |

Static is bit-identical, including scales chosen to push values between 224 and 240 — so vLLM caps `float8_e4m3fnuz` at 224 exactly as sglang does.

The dynamic gap is a dtype effect, not an algorithmic one. The native path divides in the input dtype, and the scale spread tracks that dtype's epsilon:

| input | native/vLLM max \|ratio−1\| | dtype epsilon | same formula in fp32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 | 3.33e-3 | 3.91e-3 | 5.0e-8 |
| fp16 | 4.18e-4 | 4.88e-4 | 5.1e-8 |

For scale: AITER, which every shipped ROCm image runs, divides by the type maximum 240 where vLLM and sglang divide by 224. Its scale is a constant 224/240 = 0.9333 of vLLM's and it agrees with vLLM on ~20% of dynamic-quant bytes. Bit-compatibility with vLLM is not something this code relies on today.

After the patch, the public `scaled_fp8_quant` is bit-identical to calling AITER directly with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, and to calling the native fallback directly with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`, on all three call sites (18 cases per mode).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**The native path is 2.4–11x slower per call than vLLM's fused ops.** µs per call on MI325X, bf16, vLLM 0.26.0, median of 7×300:

| call site | shape | vLLM (graph) | native (graph) | native/vLLM | AITER (graph) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dynamic per-token | 1×4096 | 3.68 | 29.46 | 8.0x | 2.40 |
| dynamic per-token | 64×4096 | 3.98 | 41.30 | 10.4x | 2.59 |
| dynamic per-token | 4096×4096 | 18.69 | 115.84 | 6.2x | 12.87 |
| dynamic per-tensor | 1×4096 | 10.92 | 26.52 | 2.4x | 6.06 |
| dynamic per-tensor | 64×4096 | 11.55 | 35.14 | 3.0x | 6.72 |
| dynamic per-tensor | 4096×4096 | 63.99 | 115.09 | 1.8x | 54.96 |
| static | 1×4096 | 2.41 | 11.57 | 4.8x | 2.31 |
| static | 64×4096 | 2.58 | 13.28 | 5.1x | 2.50 |
| static | 4096×4096 | 14.40 | 88.94 | 6.2x | 12.38 |

Eager timings show the same ordering (per-token 5.9–7.9x, per-tensor 1.7–3.0x, static 3.8–6.1x).

No working deployment pays this: the only configuration that reached the removed arm cannot serve a model (see Motivation), and gfx1151 was already on the native path. If the AITER-off + vLLM mode is ever repaired at `layernorm.py:766`, its FP8 activation quant should get a fused kernel rather than fall through to the native path.

## Not in scope

Left alone on purpose, each for a reason:

- `layernorm.py` `_has_vllm_rms_norm` — also set `True` when AITER is on, where it means "a fast rms_norm is available", so it needs restructuring rather than deletion. It is also where the AITER-off + vLLM breakage actually lives.
- `moe/.../fused_moe.py` `_has_vllm_ops` — gated on `not _is_cuda and not _is_hip and not _is_xpu`, so it serves other platforms, not ROCm.
- `rotary_embedding/base.py` — a previous attempt to drop the vLLM dependency there was reverted in #12028 after it broke GPT-OSS.

## The manual quant test under `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`

`test/manual/quant/test_custom_ops.py` (not run in CI) passes 6/6 with AITER on, before and after this change. With AITER off it exercises whichever fallback is selected, so it is worth being explicit about:

| host | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| AITER off, vLLM installed | 6/6 via the vLLM arm | native path |
| AITER off, no vLLM (e.g. the gfx1151 image) | native path | native path, unchanged |

On the native path it passed 11 of 60 across ten runs. That is the native fallback as it already is on any ROCm host without vLLM; this change does not touch its arithmetic. Two things fail:

- The per-tensor and per-token assertions require exact agreement with an fp32 reference, and the native path divides in the input dtype — the dtype effect quantified above. The test was adapted from vLLM's kernel test, where that bar fits a fused kernel checked against its own formula; for a fallback it is stricter than it needs to be, and AITER does not meet it either.
- `test_scaled_fp8_quant_with_padding` hits a genuine shape bug: with `num_token_padding` the native fallback copies an `input`-sized result into a taller `output` and raises. On ROCm, `apply_fp8_linear` pads compressed-tensors FP8 activations to at least 17 rows unless torch.compile is on, so a batch of fewer than 17 tokens reaches it on a host running without AITER or vLLM. It predates this change and is left for a separate one.

## Checklist

- [x] `ruff format --check`: clean. `ruff check`: 48 findings before and after the change on this file, none introduced.
- [x] No new unit tests: this removes a branch no working configuration reaches, and nothing references `_has_vllm`. The existing manual test is covered in the section above.
- [x] Accuracy and speed results above.

title: [Perf] [NPU] mimo: fold attention_value_scale into o_proj weights
author: iridiumine
body:
## Motivation

MiMo-V2.5-Pro defines a per-model `attention_value_scale` that the attention forward applies to V before writing the KV cache and before the attention output (`v = v * v_scale`). On NPU this materializes as an extra `aclnnMuls` kernel per layer in every decode/verify step — ~2 ms/layer on MiMo-V2.5-Pro EP6 profiling (~8% of the attention section).

Attention is linear in V:

    softmax(qk) @ (s · V) ≡ s · (softmax(qk) @ V)

so multiplying the layer's `o_proj.weight` by `s` at load time reproduces the runtime `v * v_scale` exactly, and the per-token kernel disappears.

## Modifications

- Add `MiMoV2ForCausalLM._fold_attention_value_scale_into_o_proj`, called at the end of `load_weights`: for each attention layer with a `v_scale`, multiply `o_proj.weight.data` by `attention_value_scale` (when the config defines one) and clear `attn.v_scale` so the runtime multiply is skipped.
- Only floating-point o_proj weights are folded (MiMo FP4 checkpoints keep o_proj in bf16, so this covers the shipped configurations); a quantized o_proj keeps the runtime multiply and logs a warning.
- The KV cache now stores unscaled V. This stays self-consistent because every consumer of V (decode, target-verify, DFlash draft KV materialization) goes through the same layer's (folded) o_proj.
- MTP draft (`mimo_v2_nextn.py`) and DFlash draft (`dflash.py`) have independent weight loading and their own v_scale handling; they are unaffected.

## Accuracy Tests

title: [AMD] Gate flashinfer and TRT-LLM DSA paths on CUDA
author: jiaryang
body:
## Motivation

GLM DSA on gfx1250 enters the CUDA-only flashinfer and TRT-LLM paths. Those kernels do not run on AMDGPU.

`device_sm_major >= 10` is what selects them. On ROCm the reported capability is derived from the gfx number, so gfx1250 reports `(12, 5)` and clears that test. `torch.cuda.is_available()` is already true under HIP, so it does not keep ROCm out either.

## Modifications

Gate both sites in `dsa_backend.py` with `is_cuda()`, which is true only for a CUDA build with a visible device:

- TRT-LLM workspace allocation (`device_sm_major >= 10` or `dsa_decode_impl == "trtllm"`)
- flashinfer ragged attention for SM100+

ROCm falls through to the existing aiter path. CUDA behavior is unchanged: `is_cuda()` stays true, so SM100+ still takes flashinfer.

## Accuracy Tests

Dispatch only. On this gfx1250 host, `torch.version.cuda` is `None`, `torch.cuda.is_available()` is true, and `get_device_capability()` is `(12, 5)`, so `is_cuda()` is false and these two sites no longer import flashinfer.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No CUDA speed change. ROCm no longer tries to build or launch the CUDA kernels.

title: Declare hybrid Mamba indexer host pool
author: ispobock
body:
## Motivation

Part 3 of 5 of https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40608. Hybrid Mamba plus DSA models (GLM-5.3-Flash) restore KV from host without the indexer on main, so a host hit runs attention on stale block selection. Host restore KL against warm is 0.06 to 0.71 on main. build_hybrid_mamba_stack now assembles the full attention pool's declarations next to the Mamba host pool, and _MambaStrategy raises when a declared pool is missing. HybridLinearKVPool.host_pool_decls() declares only the buffers of its full attention sub pool. Mamba state stays with its owner and the existing Mamba host path.

The DSA indexer is already declared by its pool since https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40913, but each strategy assembled its own host pools and the Mamba path never added it. With declarations the pool owner lists its host buffers once, and every strategy holding that pool builds them from the same list instead of repeating a per-strategy branch. A strategy that drops a declared pool now fails at startup instead of restoring stale state. On main the same check only logs `declares host pools ['indexer'] that _MambaStrategy did not assemble`, which is how this gap showed up.


Stack: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40913 (declarations and DSA target), https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40914 (separate draft), https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40915 (hybrid Mamba), https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40916 (QSA), https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40917 (plain KV and cleanup). Each PR is based on the previous one.
## Accuracy

GLM-5.3-Flash tp8, page 64, hicache size 20 GB, extra_buffer strategy: stack KV + INDEXER + MAMBA, indexer host 1.76 GB, host restore KL against warm 1.9e-3, 1.6e-3, 3.5e-3 at the finished sequence length. Main on the same runs: 0.06 to 0.71.

title: [Refactor] Retire the model-specific Kimi K3 kernel namespace
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

`sglang.kernels.ops.kimi_k3` collects unrelated activation, attention, GEMM, MoE and communication kernels under a model name. Retire this package and restore the logical operator grouping from #29630.

## Modifications

- Move SiTU into `activation`, masked SiTU/quantization into `moe`, and the shape-tuned tiny GEMM adapter into `gemm`.
- Move attention-residual, MLA output gating, KDA MTP and FlyDSL KDA implementations into `attention`.
- Move fused collectives and GEMM/collective kernels into `communication`, together with their GB300 tuning tables. Preserve shared communicator state.
- Rewrite runtime/test imports and the dynamic FlyDSL loader; remove the old package and eager group registration, without compatibility shims. Add 21 lazy `KernelSpec` inventory entries.
- Split the existing mixed compute tests by operator, relocate collective/FlyDSL tests and benchmark, and extend CPU namespace coverage. Document the grouping rule.

CUDA sources, kernel names, launch arguments, tuning values and existing CUDA/HIP/NPU dispatch guards are preserved. Of 18 moved source/config files, 15 are byte-identical; the others only adjust import paths or comments. All moved implementation ASTs and all six original compute-test method ASTs match after import-path normalization.

## Accuracy Tests

- `pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-commit`: passed, including registered-test validation.
- `PYTHONPATH=python python3.11 -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_kernels_namespace.py -k 'not amx_backend_probe'`: **39 passed, 2 deselected**.
- Full namespace run: 40 passed, with one existing isolated AMX-import test failing because the macOS subprocess cannot import Triton.
- CPU import smoke: all nine relocated JIT/Triton wrapper modules import; GEMM/all-reduce share the same communicator map; both relocated GB300 tuning tables load; tiny GEMM fallback and the forced NPU guard match `torch.nn.functional.linear` on CPU tensors.
- GPU numerical and multi-GPU tests were not run: available remote GPU connections were blocked by SSH/access issues. The migrated GPU tests retain their CI registrations.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This is a namespace refactor with unchanged kernel computation and launch configuration. No performance benchmark was run.

title: [Diffusion] Remove unused standalone benchmarks and deduplicate kernel tests
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

The diffusion kernel directories carry disabled standalone benchmark scripts and duplicate test setup. Remove six unreferenced benchmark tools and consolidate repeated guard and VAE wrapper tests, reducing maintenance by 1,745 lines.

title: [AMD][DSV4] moe: enable shared-expert fusion on the grouped-topk path (megamoe)
author: karverma-amd
body:
> Stacked on top of the Aiter MegaMoEv2 integration, **sgl-project/sglang#35619** — that PR adds the FlyDSL MegaMoEv2 backend but requires `--disable-shared-experts-fusion` on ROCm because of the bug below. This change removes that restriction. Base is the `20260922` image commit; #35619 is bind-mounted on top for the megamoe path.

## Motivation

`select_experts` already computes `num_fused_shared_experts_for_gate` — `0` on the per-rank fused shared-slot / aiter path, because the shared expert is appended afterwards by `_post_process_topk_ids` — and uses it at the **non-grouped** gate call sites. But the two **grouped** call sites (`grouped_topk` / `biased_grouped_topk`) still pass the raw `num_fused_shared_experts`, so on the per-rank fused shared-slot path the gate double-emits the shared marker:

- a routed expert is dropped — the gate is asked for `K_routed = top_k - num_fused_shared_experts` and spends one of those slots on its own marker (top-6 → top-5); and
- that marker lands at id `num_experts`, which the DeepEP per-rank remap shifts one past the end of the expert space (`384 → 392` on EP8, valid ids `0..391`).

DeepSeek-V4 routes through grouped `biased_grouped_topk`, so it hits this path. On the FlyDSL MegaMoEv2 backend (#35619) the out-of-range id faults the dispatch with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION 0x1016` — which is exactly why #35619 has to run with `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`, forcing the shared expert to run as a separate per-layer GEMM instead of being fused into the megamoe dispatch/combine chain.

## What changed

* `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`: pass `num_fused_shared_experts_for_gate` (not `num_fused_shared_experts`) to `grouped_topk` and `biased_grouped_topk` in `select_experts`.

Two lines. No-op off the per-rank fused shared-slot / aiter path (there `num_fused_shared_experts_for_gate == num_fused_shared_experts`). No behavior change on CUDA / non-fused-shared-slot paths.

## Validation (MI355X gfx950, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, TP8 / DP8 attention / EP8, `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`)

With the fix, `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` boots and serves — no `0x1016`; the dispatch/combine runs at `topk=7, local_experts=49` (48 routed + 1 fused shared per rank), confirming the shared expert is fused into the megamoe chain rather than run as a separate GEMM.

**Accuracy** — 5-shot GSM8K:

| arm | accuracy | invalid |
| --- | -------- | ------- |
| shared-off (`--disable-shared-experts-fusion`) | 0.940 | 0.000 |
| shared-on (`--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`) | **0.970** | 0.000 |

Same fp4-MoE run-to-run band, no regression (200 questions; the gap is within noise).

**Throughput / interactivity A/B** (`random`, ISL/OSL 8192/1024, `num-prompts = 4 × conc`), shared-off vs shared-on:

| conc | out tok/s off → on | Mean TPOT off → on | Δ TPOT |
| ---- | ------------------ | ------------------ | ------ |
| 256  | 2814.5 → 2775.9    | 74.2 → **67.9 ms** | **−8.4%** |
| 512  | 3974.6 → 3873.3    | 90.8 → 90.1 ms     |  (flat) |

Fusing the shared expert removes a separate per-layer GEMM from the decode critical path: a **−8% mean-TPOT (decode interactivity) win at conc256** and +5.5% per-rank decode throughput; flat at conc512 (workload-dependent). Aggregate output tok/s is within noise at ISL 8192 (prefill/TTFT-dominated).

## Commands

Server (shared-on arm; drop `SGLANG_AMD_USE_FLYDSL_MEGA_MOE` etc. and swap `--enforce-` for `--disable-shared-experts-fusion` for the off arm):

```bash
# image: lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.20-rocm724-mi35x-20260922  (+ #35619 srt + this patch)
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_AMD_USE_FLYDSL_MEGA_MOE=1 \
SGLANG_AMD_FLYDSL_MEGA_MOE_MTPR=8192 SGLANG_AMD_FLYDSL_MEGA_QUANT=a8w4 \
MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE=17179869184 MORI_EP_LAUNCH_CONFIG_MODE=AUTO \
SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=0 SGLANG_DP_SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL=0 \
SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=0 SGLANG_DP_USE_REDUCE_SCATTER=0 GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=5 \
SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813> --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention --ep-size 8 \
  --enable-dp-lm-head --enable-dp-attention-local-control-broadcast \
  --moe-a2a-backend megamoe --moe-dense-tp-size 1 --enforce-shared-experts-fusion \
  --attention-backend dsv4 --enable-deepseek-v4-fp4-indexer \
  --page-size 256 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 65536 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --max-running-requests 512 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 128
```

Throughput A/B:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang-oai --model <served-name> \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts $((4*CONC)) --max-concurrency CONC --disable-tqdm
```

Accuracy:

```bash
python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 200 --parallel 64 --num-shots 5 --port <port>
```

## Checklist

- [x] Two-line change; no-op off the per-rank fused shared-slot / aiter path
- [x] Enables `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` on FlyDSL MegaMoEv2 (no `0x1016`; `topk=7`)
- [x] GSM8K accuracy preserved (0.970 vs 0.940 baseline band)
- [x] Decode-interactivity A/B measured (conc 256/512), −8% TPOT at conc256
- [x] Stacked on #35619

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

title: [Fix] Recover from stale torch extension locks in every `cpp_extension` loader
author: hnyls2002
body:
