title: dsv4.1-amd: gfx950 MXFP8 matmul kernels and fp8-grid producers
author: kevin-mii
body:
> This PR was "stack 1/4" of the DeepSeek-V4.1 AMD series (#41018 to #41021). It now follows the CUDA dsv4.1 layout (#39646, #39652, #39653, #39656, #39664, then #38798): kernel PRs by domain, each on `main` with no callers, then one integration PR. This is the first kernel PR.

## Summary
- Native MXFP8 dense route for 32x32-block ue8m0 fp8 checkpoints on gfx950 (`ops/quantization/mxfp8_native_amd_gfx95.py`, `csrc/deepseek_v4/mxfp8_gemv_gfx95.cuh`): the weight is reordered once at load into the scaled-MFMA lane order and stays fp8, with K zero-padded to a multiple of 128 and the activation tail masked. M <= 32 runs a HIP GEMV on `v_mfma_scale_f32_16x16x128_f8f6f4`, larger M a Triton `tl.dot_scaled` GEMM. The input is bf16, bf16 on the fp8 grid, or fp8 + ue8m0 scales, and all three give the same bits.
- Tile tables (`mxfp8_gemv_gfx95_configs.json`) tuned at DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's TP4 shapes, fastest config per M bucket; `benchmark/kernels/quantization/tuning_mxfp8_native_gfx95.py` regenerates a shape's rows.
- fp8-grid helpers in `mxfp8_amd_gfx95.py`: `fake_quant_fp8_activation` / `fp8_grid_quantize` with the ue8m0 rule of CUDA's `per_token_group_quant`, the bf16-dequant linear for shapes the native kernels cannot tile, and the `Fp8GridActivation` / `Mxfp8Activation` wrappers that let a consumer skip its own quant.
- Fused producers of those wrappers: RMSNorm (+ residual) + quant (`rmsnorm_fake_quant_amd_gfx95.py`), clamped SiLU-mul + quant (`silu_and_mul_clamp_hip.py`), and the wo_a batched GEMM with the quant in its epilogue (`gfx95_batched_gemm_bf16_fp8_grid.py`, fixed-order split-K up to 64 rows).
- Model call sites are in the integration PR of this stack.

## Changes to existing kernels
- `mxfp8_amd_gfx95.py`: new code appended; existing functions and callers unchanged. Every other file is new and HIP-only, and the `.cuh` refuses to build for any target but gfx950.

## Verification
- MI350X (ROCm 10.0.0, torch 2.11, triton 3.8, aiter at the Dockerfile pin): `test_mxfp8_amd_gfx95.py` and `test_fp8_grid_producers_gfx95.py` pass (fp64 references, bitwise agreement of the three input encodings including non-finite activations, bitwise match to aiter `batched_gemm_bf16`), and so does the existing `test_minimax_m3_mxfp8.py`.
- With the integration PR's callers, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 loads every dense block-FP8 linear on the native route. Tuned tiles are up to 2.2x faster than the defaults; the native K tail takes 0.63-0.93x the time of the bf16-dequant route at (5120, 576) up to M 4096.
- Not executed on this branch alone: end-to-end serving and accuracy.

title: dsv4.1-amd: KV cache layouts, FP4 indexer, compressor and router kernels
author: kevin-mii
body:
> This PR was "stack 2/4" of the DeepSeek-V4.1 AMD series (#41018 to #41021). It now follows the CUDA dsv4.1 layout (#39646, #39652, #39653, #39656, #39664, then #38798): kernel PRs by domain, each on `main` with no callers, then one integration PR. This is the second kernel PR; it does not depend on #41018.

## Summary
- Build the V4.1 KV layouts on ROCm (`include/sgl_kernel/deepseek_v4/kv_layout.cuh`, `fp4_utils.cuh`): `v41::store_row` quantizes `V41` (fp8, ue8m0 per 32) and `V41_FP4` (e2m1, e4m3 per 16) rows on gfx950 with round-to-nearest-even as on CUDA, so `fused_store_cache`, `compress_norm_rope_store`, `fused_k_norm_rope_flashmla` and `dequantize_k_cache_paged_v41` serve both layouts there.
- FP4 indexer on ROCm: the RoPE pack kernels build with wave64-aware shuffles (`fp4_indexer_rope.cuh`); `fp4_indexer_rope_hip.cuh` writes the split FlyDSL index-K layout; `fp4_indexer_hip.py` adds the split writer and reader, the FlyDSL query packer, a one-launch index-Q pack + head weights and a page-table bucket width.
- In-tree FP4 indexer decode schedule (`fp4_indexer_schedule_hip.py`, next to the existing in-tree prefill schedule): `build_decode_schedule` writes aiter `compute_varctx_schedule`'s `cta_info` in two dispatches whose registers do not grow with the row count. aiter's single kernel spills past ~1K rows and could not reserve its scratch at DSpark batch 256 (1,536 rows), which crashed decode graph capture.
- ROCm decode router: a batch-invariant split-K bf16 GEMV (`ops/gemm/router_gemv_hip.py`, beside main's `router_gemv.py`) and a sqrtsoftplus top-k gate over its partials bitwise equal to aiter's `topk_gating_kernel_opt` (`ops/moe/rocm_router_gate.py`). It is here because `indexer_head_weights` runs the GEMV.
- The low-ratio compressors (`c1.cuh`, `c2.cuh`, `c2_decode_pool.py`) run on ROCm, taking the fp8 pool as bytes there (`low_ratio_compress.py`); `fused_k_norm_rope_flashmla(q=...)` ropes the query heads in the K launch on ROCm; `sglang/test/kernels/deepseek_v4/dsv41_kv_quant_reference.py` is an independent torch oracle for `V41_FP4` pages.
- Model call sites are in the integration PR of this stack.

## Changes to existing kernels
- CUDA-visible, same outputs: `main_norm_rope.cuh` gains a defaulted `kRopeQ` template flag; `fp4_indexer.py` and `fp4_rope_fake_quant.py` move their row math into `@triton.jit` helpers (`positions=None` keeps the old call); `c1.cuh` and `fp4_indexer_rope.cuh` match `kDLGPU`, which is `kDLCUDA` on CUDA; `c2_decode_pool.py` divides with `tl.div_rn` instead of `libdevice.div_rn` (both IEEE round-to-nearest; Triton's HIP libdevice has no `div_rn`).
- ROCm numerics: with `SGLANG_USE_AITER`, `linear_bf16_fp32` now takes the default fp32 `torch.mm` path instead of aiter's bf16-rounded `tgemm` (V4 compressor and router logits), and the aiter branch is removed. The V4.1 paths are asserted gfx950-only, and gfx942 code is unchanged.

## Verification
- New tests: `test_v41_kv_store.py` (byte-exact stores and dequant for both layouts, query rope in the K launch), `test_rocm_router_gate.py` (bitwise to aiter on ties and non-finite logits, the fused split-K gate), `test_router_gemv_hip.py` (the batch-invariant GEMV, and `linear_bf16_fp32` staying in fp32, which fails on the removed aiter route); `test_fp4_indexer_hip.py` is extended (split index-K writer bitwise to the Triton RMSNorm + RoPE + FP4 chain, decode schedule bitwise to aiter).
- MI350X (ROCm 10.0.0, torch 2.11, triton 3.8, aiter at the Dockerfile pin): these tests and the existing tests on the modified kernels (`test_c4_v2.py`, `test_c128_v2.py`, `test_deepseek_v4_compress_state_runtime_shapes.py`, `test_dsv4_unified_fp8_compress_store.py`, `test_dsv4_fp8_cast.py`) pass on this branch, as do the AMD-registered DSV4 attention, MXFP8, mHC and HiCache kernel tests.
- With the integration PR's callers, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 / EP4 with DSpark captures decode graphs up to batch 256 and scores 0.885-0.900 on GSM8K (200 questions, three runs).
- [ ] Pending on a CUDA runner: `test_v41_kv_store.py` (SM100), `test_fp4_indexer.py`, `test_deepseek_v4.py`.

## Stack
- Base: `main`. Independent of #41018 (gfx950 MXFP8 matmul kernels).

title: dsv4.1-amd: gfx950 sparse decode attention and sorted top-k
author: kevin-mii
body:
> This PR was "stack 3/4" of the DeepSeek-V4.1 AMD series (#41018 to #41021). It now follows the CUDA dsv4.1 layout (#39646, #39652, #39653, #39656, #39664, then #38798): kernel PRs by domain, each on `main` with no callers, then one integration PR. This is the third kernel PR; it does not depend on #41018 or #41019.

## Summary
- `ops/attention/sparse_decode_reduce_hip.py`: `gfx_sparse_split_reduce` combines the split-KV partials of aiter's gfx950 `pa_decode_sparse(..., skip_reduce=True)`, bitwise equal to aiter's own reduce, with the attention sink and an optional inverse RoPE of each head's tail.
- `ops/attention/dsv4/compact_attention_hip.py`: sparse decode attention that reads the compact V4.1 pages (528 B fp8 + ue8m0, 288 B e2m1 + e4m3) directly through aiter's gfx950 `_qkpv_fp8`, with main and extra slot ranges and 16-head groups.
- `ops/attention/dsv4/swapab_gluon_hip.py`: the 16-head swap-AB Gluon kernel for HIP, argument-compatible with the SM100 kernel (CDNA4 MFMA, bf16 hi + lo compensated PV). It reuses the SM100 module's `_load_v4`, which is plain Gluon; `swapab_attention` gains `inv_rope=None`.
- `ops/attention/dsv4/attn_glue_hip.py`: single-launch Triton replacements for the torch glue around the V4.1 sparse decode metadata, each bitwise equal to the torch expression in its docstring.
- ROCm AOT top-k (`deepseek_v4_topk.cu`, `sgl_kernel/top_k.py`): `sort_output` sorts each row's picks ascending with a block-wide bitonic sort, `-1` padding last; the selected set is unchanged; the sort is ROCm-only (under `USE_ROCM`). Strides below the wave width use lane shuffles and the rest LDS, so it is also right on 32-lane waves (gfx1250). `benchmark/bench_dsv4_topk_transform.py` times it: on MI350X the sort adds ~3.4 us per call, where a separate `torch.sort` costs ~17-20 us.
- `q_rope_store.py` on HIP rounds like the batched HIP RoPE kernel.
- `ops/attention/dsv4/candidate_blocks_hip.py`, beside main's `candidate_blocks.py`: the V4.1 two-level indexer's level-one block scores and top blocks, the top-k within the chosen blocks and the paged top-k sorted in the AOT epilogue, graph-safe.
- Model call sites are in the integration PR of this stack.

## Changes to existing kernels
- `decode_attention_sm100.py`: `swapab_attention` takes an optional `partial_gluon` (`swapab_gluon_hip.swapab_attention` binds the gfx950 kernel), with no HIP branch in the SM100 file; `_combine` compiles the inverse RoPE out when `inv_rope=None`, so SM100 output is unchanged. `decode_attention_sm100_gluon.py` is untouched.
- `q_rope_store.py`: the new branch is a HIP-only constexpr; CUDA arithmetic is unchanged.
- The top-k epilogue, op schema and declaration are ROCm-only (`setup_rocm.py`); with `sort_output=False` the kernel is the same, plus a 4 KB static LDS array. The wrapper always passes `sort_output`, so sgl-kernel must be rebuilt from this PR.
- Rollout: this PR is kernel-only, and no caller passes `sort_output=True` yet (the one existing caller, `ops/attention/dsv4/topk.py`, still uses the 6-argument form, which the default keeps working). Callers will only pass `sort_output=True` after sgl-kernel is released and the `sglang-kernel` pin is bumped to 0.4.8 or later, following [How to update kernels in SGLang](https://lmsysorg.mintlify.app/docs/developer_guide/contribution_guide#how-to-update-kernels-in-sglang).

## Verification
- New tests: `test_swapab_attention.py` (SM100 and gfx950: fp64 reference over padded and poisoned pages, `-1` / out-of-range slots, sinks, graph replay, and the combine's inverse RoPE bitwise to `fused_rope_inplace`); `test_compact_attention_hip.py` (both packed layouts, a second cache, `-1` slots and a key-less row against a torch softmax with sink); `test_topk.py::test_deepseek_v4_topk_transform_sorted_output`; `test_dsv41_decode_glue_hip.py` (candidate blocks against main's `select_candidate_block_ids` with garbage past each row's reach, the sorted mapping, and the `attn_glue_hip` builders bitwise to their torch forms). `test_dsv4_q_rope_store.py` is now also registered for AMD.
- MI350X (ROCm 10.0.0, torch 2.11, triton 3.8, aiter at the Dockerfile pin): these tests pass on this branch. The top-k epilogue built from this source matches the installed op over 120 shapes (sorted rows bitwise, unsorted rows the same set) and compiles for gfx1250.
- With the integration PR's callers, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 / EP4 with DSpark serves and scores 0.900-0.905 on GSM8K (200 questions, two runs).
- [ ] Pending on an SM100 runner: `test_swapab_attention.py`, `test_dsv4_q_rope_store.py`.

## Stack
- Base: `main`. Independent of #41018 (gfx950 MXFP8 matmul kernels) and #41019 (KV cache layouts, FP4 indexer, compressor and router kernels).

title: dsv4.1-amd: fused mHC boundary and all-reduce + mHC post kernels
author: kevin-mii
body:
> This PR was "stack 4/4" of the DeepSeek-V4.1 AMD series (#41018 to #41021). It now follows the CUDA dsv4.1 layout (#39646, #39652, #39653, #39656, #39664, then #38798): kernel PRs by domain, each on `main` with no callers, then one integration PR. This is the fourth kernel PR; #41018 has merged, and it does not depend on #41019 or #41020. The model wiring moved to the integration PR, #41308.

## Summary
- `ops/layernorm/mhc_boundary_hip.py`: the fused mHC sublayer boundary for ROCm. One launch applies the pending `hc_post` onto the residual, collapses it with the previous `pre` and takes the split-K mixing statistics. The reduce + Sinkhorn stays pending in `HcCoefficients`, and `rmsnorm_with_sinkhorn` runs it in the same launch as the next RMSNorm (optionally with the gfx950 fp8-grid fake quant). A row's result does not depend on M, so it is batch invariant like main's mHC.
- `jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/mhc_boundary_gfx95.cuh`: the prefill regime (M >= 1024) of that boundary on gfx950, with LDS DMA and `v_permlane*_swap`. It follows the Triton kernel's operation order, so each row is bitwise equal in both regimes.
- `ops/communication/all_reduce_mhc_hip.py` + `jit/csrc/distributed/all_reduce_mhc_hip.cuh`: a TP4 all-reduce fused with `hc_post` for 1-8 rows of hidden size 5120, on aiter's `CustomAllreduce` peer buffers. aiter's `fused_allreduce_mhc_post_one_stage` has the same math, but it rejects hidden sizes above 4096 in bf16 (512 packs), so it cannot serve V4.1's 5120. It is a `load_jit` module like the other JIT kernels; the one aiter header it includes is `custom_all_reduce.cuh`, for the `CustomAllreduce` whose peer buffers and signals SGLang's ROCm custom all-reduce owns. It is compiled with `-ffp-contract=off`, so it is bitwise equal to the unfused all-reduce followed by `hc_post`.
- Model call sites are in the integration PR of this stack.

## Changes to existing kernels
- `ops/layernorm/mhc.py`, HIP only: `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn` uses `ieee` dot precision (CDNA has no TF32) and one row tile at every M, and reduces through the boundary's reduce + Sinkhorn row. CUDA is unchanged.

## Verification
- New tests: `test_hc_boundary_hip.py` covers the boundary forms against torch and fp64, batch invariance of the boundary and of HIP `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn`, the hosted norm against the standalone launches (fp8-grid, MXFP8 and no fake quant), and the gfx950 prefill kernel bitwise to the Triton kernel on full and partial row blocks.
- MI350X (ROCm 10.0.0, torch 2.11, triton 3.8, aiter at the Dockerfile pin): these tests pass on `main` + this PR.
- `test_all_reduce_mhc_hip.py` (four GPUs) checks the fused all-reduce bitwise against the unfused all-reduce + `hc_post` for 1, 3 and 8 rows, eager and under graph capture. #41308's four-GPU `test_deepseek_v4_amd_tp4.py` also covers it: it compares eager (registered-buffer copy-in) and graph-replay outputs of the fused and unfused handoff; all 10 cases pass.
- With #41308's callers, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 / EP4 with DSpark scores 0.905 on GSM8K (200 questions) and serves random 4K/1K at 521 / 1,840 / 3,307 tok/s at concurrency 1 / 8 / 32; see #41308.

## Stack
- Base: `main`. Independent of #41019 (KV cache layouts, FP4 indexer, compressor and router kernels) and #41020 (gfx950 sparse decode attention and sorted top-k).

title: [AMD] Eliminate remaining gfx95 FP8 scale relayout copies
author: xiaofei-zheng
body:
## Motivation

Six gfx95 block-FP8 producers request row-major scales and then materialize the bpreshuffle layout with an extra GPU copy. This was visible in GLM-5.3 decode as one relayout launch per affected layer. Native `Fp8LinearMethod` checkpoints reach these branches after #39409; block-FP8 implementations exposing `weight_scale` can reach them on current main.

This supersedes #34589 and #24476 with a current-main implementation, based on the approaches from @amd-mvarjoka and @Jacob0226.

## Modifications

Use the existing `emit_transposed_bpreshuffle_scale` gate at the remaining communicator, MLA, and MHA fused-RMS producers. For `M >= 2`, AITER emits the target layout and SGLang applies a zero-copy stride view; `M == 1` keeps the existing materialize path. Extend fused-RMS tests across residual and unquantized-output combinations.

## Accuracy Tests

- Transposed and row-major producer paths are bit-exact for quantized values, scales, residual output, and the DSA bf16 payload.
- GLM-5.3 EAGLE sentinel: 949 samples, mean accept length 3.7189, p50 3.60, with no observed regression.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GLM-5.3 MXFP4, MI355X, TP8, EAGLE 5 steps, concurrency 6 (`M=36`):

- Decode step: 17.175 ms to 16.943 ms (-1.35%), three runs per arm with disjoint ranges.
- Kernel launches: 2078 to 2000 per step; the 78 removed launches match the affected layer count.
- Trace attribution measured the removed relayout copies at 0.297 ms per step.

Measurement: three alternating runs per arm after graph capture/warmup; 50 replays per op, 20 calls per graph.

<details><summary>Commands and local checks</summary>

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_TOPK_MB=1 SGLANG_MQA_VARCTX=1 \
python3 profile_decode.py --tp-size 8 --ep-size 1 \
  --model-path /shared_nfs/models/GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --context-length 262144 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.80 --trust-remote-code --max-running-requests 32 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 --ISL 100000 --CONC 6

pre-commit run --files \
  python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/residual/add_norm.py \
  python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha_rocm.py \
  python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla_rocm.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_fused_rms_fp8_group_quant.py
```

The three methods in `TestFusedRMSFP8GroupQuant` passed in parallel on GPUs 4–6 (four subtests each).

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Documentation is not needed; no user-facing interface changes.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [Perf] Lazy-load built-in model definitions and nixl_ep at startup
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

Importing `sglang.srt.models.registry` eagerly imports every module under `sglang.srt.models` (over 200 model files, on the order of 10-20 s on a typical dev box) even when `SGLANG_EXTERNAL_MODEL_PACKAGE` points at an out-of-tree package that provides the model actually being served. `sglang.srt.layers.moe.token_dispatcher.nixl` likewise probes `nixl_ep` at module import time, which every server pays for whether or not NIXL EP is used. This PR defers both until they are needed, which cuts startup time for deployments that serve out-of-tree models.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/models/registry.py`
  - When `SGLANG_EXTERNAL_MODEL_PACKAGE` is set, the registry starts with only the external package's models and imports the built-in package on the first lookup that needs it: `get_supported_archs()`, `register()`, or a `resolve_model_cls()` whose first architecture is not already registered. The merged view keeps the external models as overrides, exactly as `register(external_pkg, overwrite=True)` did.
  - Without the environment variable nothing changes: the built-in models are registered at import time as before.
  - New `is_arch_supported(arch)`, which answers from the already-registered models before falling back to the full set.
- `python/sglang/srt/model_loader/utils.py`: `get_model_architecture()` uses `is_arch_supported()` so that checking an external architecture does not trigger the built-in import.
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/nixl.py`: `nixl_ep` is imported inside a cached `_load_nixl_ep()` helper called from `NixlEPBuffer.get_buffer()` and the dispatcher constructor. A missing `nixl_ep` raises the same `ImportError` message at first use instead of at import time, and `topk_idx_t` is resolved there and stored on the dispatcher instance instead of a module global.
- `test/registered/unit/models/test_model_registry.py` (new, CPU suite, not part of the original commit): an external architecture resolves without importing the built-in package; the built-in package is imported exactly once when a built-in architecture is requested; external models still override built-ins after that import; `register()` still detects duplicates against the built-ins.

## Original commits

title: [diffusion] Add native Ming-Image Design and Design-Layer support
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Add native support for the public Ming-Image family:
- `inclusionAI/Ming-Image-0.1-Design`: text-to-image and single-image editing, with RGBA output.
- `inclusionAI/Ming-Image-0.1-Design-Layer`: decomposition into ordered transparent layers.

## Modifications

- Implement the Bailing multimodal MoE encoder and query connector with native attention, TP linears, Qwen vision, and fused experts. Reuse Z-Image DiT blocks, the RGBA Qwen VAE, standard stages, and existing component loaders. No remote modeling code or checkpoint conversion is required.
- Preserve checkpoint-specific padding, BF16 activation rounding, CPU noise ordering, CFG, reference-image preprocessing, and layer output semantics.
- Wire TP/SP, CFG parallelism, encoder folding, layerwise offload, Cache-DiT, LoRA, spatial VAE decoding, and exact-shape breakable CUDA graphs into the existing runtime.
- Fix integration failures found by real requests: FA2's call signature, generators lost during sequential output expansion, explicit offload validation over partial stage execution, and stale MoE TMA descriptors after offload rebinds parameters. Existing Z-Image norm/fusion defaults and existing MoE activation defaults are unchanged.
- Add a cookbook with a scoped command picker, model catalog entries, compatibility notes, and regression tests. Fix the shared ComfyUI snippet's export scope so the new cookbook can render it.

Scope: existing production files +90/-25 lines; new production files 1,365 lines; tests +425 lines; docs +448/-37 lines.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on an isolated Linux development host with 2 x H200 141 GB, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Transformers 5.12.1, and Diffusers 0.37.0. Final runtime revision: `8d0f9e7b8ec`; subsequent commit only adds documentation.

- **183 tests passed**, including six real HTTP configurations: Design/Layer cold start, Design/Layer request warmup, Layer VAE tiling, and Layer encoder+DiT layerwise offload. Each exercises `n=1,1,2,2`, checks RGBA shape/cardinality, requires identical repeated pixels, and checks that the first generation is unchanged by `n=2`. Design covers both generation and editing.
- The same run covers Ming unit tests and Z-Image, multi-output grouping, SenseNova, component residency, and pipeline executor regressions.
- The CUDA TMA regression also passes using the registered CI entry point: `python test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_moe_tma_cache.py -f`.
- Separate full-checkpoint runs cover 2048-square Design, 1024-square four-layer decomposition, TP2, Ulysses2, Ring2, Layer CFG2, encoder folding, spatial VAE decoding, SageAttention, enabled Cache-DiT, and synthetic dynamic LoRA load/remove. Repeated fixed-workload outputs match; LoRA removal restores the original output. Layer offload matches resident output exactly across three requests.
- Breakable CUDA graphs performed 24 Design and 48 Layer serving replays, rather than merely enabling the flag.

Reference comparison uses official Ming-Image code `578e21e081a7cd385b6c79e36df7e419155681b1`, Design weights `208087ada1486931692c1896f38d4cd16ff3df82`, and Layer weights `9fabca8b62a67f1f53a957d46389c00451c11e52`. Both paths use seed 42 and 12 steps, with FA2 for the encoder and SDPA for the DiT. Metrics below include RGBA channels:

| Sample | PSNR | SSIM |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Design, 1024-square red teapot | 21.9556 | 0.94262 |
| Layer, 512-square reference, first layer | 33.4839 | 0.96960 |
| Layer, same reference, second layer | 41.4316 | 0.98588 |

These are sample comparisons, not a quality-equivalence claim. The matched text tower is bit-identical; connector/vision/DiT attention retain numerical differences. The reference environment uses Transformers 4.57.1, Diffusers 0.36, and Transformer Engine 2.19 rather than the documented 1.11, so this is not an identical-environment official baseline. Cross-topology results and lossy optimizations are not expected to be bit-identical.

The full-checkpoint HTTP suite is opt-in, not part of the default checkpoint CI matrix:

```bash
SGLANG_TEST_MING_IMAGE=1 python -m pytest -q \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_ming_image.py
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This PR adds model support and makes no speedup claim. Functional runs are not a controlled performance comparison. Other GPU families, quantized checkpoints, and ComfyUI layer output remain unverified; the cookbook states these boundaries.

## Checklist

- [x] Full-diff pre-commit checks.
- [x] Focused unit and GPU/HTTP integration tests.
- [x] Cookbook, README, model catalog, and compatibility documentation.
- [x] Cookbook config validation, Mintlify build validation, and broken-link checks.
- [x] Accuracy results and validation limitations recorded above.

title: [Bugfix] Skip post-experts EP all-reduce on the FlashInfer cutlass FP4 all-gather MoE path
author: mattteochen
body:
## Motivation

On the flashinfer cutlass FP4 all-gather MoE path, `post_experts_all_reduce()` issues an EP all-reduce that should not run. In DP-attention serving this crashes or hangs.

The path is active when `should_use_flashinfer_cutlass_moe_fp4_allgather()` holds: no a2a backend, `flashinfer_cutlass`, `modelopt_fp4`, DP attention, and `moe_ep_size == attn_dp_size`. Sparse MoE layers then run on each rank's DP-local tokens (`is_moe_input_scattered_across_dp_ranks()`). The standard dispatcher all-gathers tokens over `_TP` (`all_gatherv`) and reduce-scatters the expert outputs over `_TP` (`reduce_scatterv`). Since `_TP` spans the whole EP group, both post-experts reductions are already done, and each rank ends up holding only its own DP-local tokens.

`post_experts_output_is_complete` reports only the TP sum as complete on this route (`is_tp_path and should_use_flashinfer_cutlass_moe_fp4_allgather()`), so `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce` exempts only the TP path.
- **Before #32963:** `DeepseekV2MoE` issued only the TP reduction, so DeepSeek/GLM models ran no post-experts collective here.
- **Since #32963:** `DeepseekV2MoE` goes through `post_experts_all_reduce()`, which also issues `moe_expert_parallel_all_reduce` on the DP-local outputs. Those outputs hold different tokens and usually different token counts per rank. When every rank has the same token count, the all-reduce silently sums unrelated tokens (the negative control of the 4-GPU test below shows it); with idle ranks it crashes or hangs, as described below.

Observed with GLM-5.2 NVFP4 disaggregated prefill, TP4/DP4/EP4 with DP attention, on GB300 with `nightly-dev-20260923-06008c17` (the InferenceX GLM-5.2 AgentX recipe). Dynamo's prefill warmup leaves some DP ranks idle with zero tokens.
- **FlashInfer allreduce fusion on (SM100 → MNNVL backend):** the idle ranks' all-reduce fails, which kills the schedulers. The MNNVL one-shot kernel launches with `grid(num_tokens, ...)`, so a zero-size grid is `cudaErrorInvalidValue`:

  ```
  File ".../layers/moe/utils.py", in post_experts_all_reduce
  File ".../distributed/parallel_state.py", line 756, in all_reduce
      return flashinfer_allreduce(input_, group_name=self.unique_name)
  ...
  trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce_fusion failed with error code invalid argument
  ```

- **Idle ranks skip the collective:** tried in an earlier revision of this PR, which returned early from `all_reduce` for empty tensors. The idle ranks then move on to the EAGLE draft model while the busy rank waits in the target model's EP all-reduce forever (scheduler watchdog after 300 s). The mismatched collective is the actual bug; the MNNVL error was only its symptom.

## Modifications

- `post_experts_output_is_complete`: when the FP4 all-gather route is active, report both the EP and the TP sum as complete, so `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce` skips both post-experts all-reduces. That route already reduces over `_TP` in the dispatcher.
- New unit test `TestFp4AllgatherAbsorbsPostExpertsReductions` in `test_reduction_fusion.py`:
  - Under the FP4 all-gather route, `post_experts_all_reduce` issues no collective, for pure EP (`moe_ep_size=4`) and pure TP.
  - Without it, pure EP still issues the EP reduction.
- `test_moe_output_reduction.py`: `test_fp4_allgather_only_completes_the_tp_sum` pinned the TP-only result, which the #41097 refactor kept unchanged. It becomes `test_fp4_allgather_also_completes_the_ep_sum`.
- New 4-GPU test `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_fp4_allgather_moe_reduction.py` (real NCCL collectives, no model weights or FP4 kernels). On the FP4 all-gather route, each rank runs the real `StandardDispatcher.combine()` (`reduce_scatterv` over `_TP`), which leaves DP rank j holding exactly j + 1. `post_experts_all_reduce()` must then leave every rank's output unchanged. A control with the route off checks that the EP all-reduce still runs.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, via `python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`.

Setup:
- GLM-5.2 NVFP4 on one GB300 node (4 GPUs), `nightly-dev-20260923-06008c17`.
- Plain `sglang.launch_server`: TP4/DP4/EP4 with `--enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head`, `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutlass`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--dsa-{prefill,decode}-backend trtllm`, `--disable-cuda-graph`.
- This is the prefill configuration of the InferenceX GLM-5.2 AgentX recipe. It takes the FP4 all-gather route.

| Build | FP4 all-gather route | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **This PR**, `--enable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion` (MNNVL) | active | **0.945** (invalid 0.001) |
| `main`, `--disable-flashinfer-cutlass-moe-fp4-allgather` (reference) | off | 0.943 (invalid 0.000) |
| `main`, `--enable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion` | active | Crash on the first request after startup: `trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce_fusion failed ... invalid argument` via `_execute_idle` → `post_experts_all_reduce` |
| `main`, fusion off (NCCL all-reduce) | active | Deadlock: all 4 schedulers hit the 300 s watchdog, with ranks split between the dispatcher's NCCL `all_gatherv` and a host sync |

The "this PR" build is the nightly plus this change, plus two unrelated opt-in patches that are inactive in this test: the CUDA event pool from #39960 (off by default) and a HiCache host-memory opt-out (HiCache not enabled). The other rows use the unmodified nightly.

## Validation

- CPU node, aarch64, `nightly-dev-20260923-06008c17` image with this branch on `PYTHONPATH`:
  - `test/registered/unit/layer_boundary/` + `test_runtime_context.py`: 422 passed.
  - Negative control: against unmodified `main`, the new pure-EP test fails with `['ep'] != []`, and `test_fp4_allgather_also_completes_the_ep_sum` fails. The other 420 pass.
- One GB300 node (4 GPUs), same image, this branch on `PYTHONPATH`:
  - `test_fp4_allgather_moe_reduction.py`: 2 passed.
  - Negative control: against unmodified `main`, the reduction test fails with per-rank values `[[10.0], [10.0], [10.0], [10.0]]` instead of `[[1.0], [2.0], [3.0], [4.0]]`, i.e. every rank gets 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10. The route-off control passes.
- The earlier 4-rank GB300 repro (FlashInfer 0.6.18, MNNVL workspace as SGLang builds it) confirms the zero-token launch failure: 4 tokens give the correct sum, 0 tokens give the error above on every rank.
- End-to-end on GB300 with this change on `nightly-dev-20260923-06008c17`: GLM-5.2 NVFP4 disaggregated serving (InferenceX GLM-5.2 AgentX C48 recipe; prefill TP4/DP4/EP4 with DP attention, `flashinfer_cutlass` FP4 MoE, FlashInfer allreduce fusion enabled with `backend=mnnvl` on all ranks; two TP4 decode workers; NIXL KV transfer).
  - **Without this change:** 6/6 launches crashed in Dynamo's prefill warmup with the error above.
  - **With this change:** the prefill warmup passes on 3/3 independent allocations, including the idle-rank case: one warmup request, three idle DP ranks.
  - AgentX warmup at C48: 531/531 requests completed with 0 errors and 0 cancellations on each of 2 allocations. The full 3600 s AgentX measured phase then completed on both allocations with 0 request errors (6,071 and 6,274 requests completed). There were no scheduler watchdog timeouts or tracebacks.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit) (ruff 0.15.1 format/check, isort 7.0.0, codespell 2.4.1).
- [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci).
- [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed.

title: fix: load fused shared-expert LoRA weights and bound expert indices
author: yueming-yuan
body:
Fix fused shared-expert LoRA loading and prevent expert IDs from aliasing another adapter.

- Size each layer's LoRA expert pool from its actual fused MoE layout, including shared slots.
- Load shared-expert factors into those slots using the base module's EP mapping and existing TP slicing/scaling; merge packed routed factors regardless of checkpoint key order, and accept both `.shared_expert.` and `.shared_experts.` paths.
- Assert while allocating the pool that both A/B expert dimensions match the base fused MoE layout (local or global IDs); no device assert or GPU synchronization.
- Reject unsupported shared-outer factors and global-ID/per-rank shared-slot layouts; reject out-of-range expert IDs before adding adapter offsets.

Selected for the v0.1.1 cutoff. FP32 Qwen3-MoE router support remains after cutoff in #40997, paired with Miles #3697. No dtype or accumulation-policy change. 

Validation: existing coverage includes 60 passing tests (5 abstract-base skips), a distinguishing GPU bounds regression, and GLM-5.2 5L TP4/EP1 with fusion enabled. On 8 DAPO 4K sequences ×3, the shared-expert fix reduced slot mean logprob differences from 0.050144/0.039706 to 0.019414/0.015895 (base 0.013156); the additional Bridge row-parallel fix is separate and is not part of this cutoff PR. EP mapping is unit-tested; distributed EP, other backends and CUDA-graph combinations are not comprehensively validated. A host-only probe of the actual initialization check accepts matching global/local dimensions and rejects a missing shared slot on either A or B. CPU loader regression: packed-first and shared-first inputs failed in all 6 EP/order subcases before the fix; after merging packed routed views with shared factors, the full loader file passes 46 tests and 22 subtests. The 9 singular-name subcases also fail before the naming fix and pass afterward. Test fixture cleanup removes 45 net lines. Full local pre-commit passed; fresh split-head GPU CI is pending.

[Model tracking and release split](https://github.com/radixark/miles/issues/3284#issuecomment-5810394134).

title: [GLM-5.3-Flash] Capture the KDA extend in breakable prefill CUDA graphs
author: yuan-luo
body: ## Motivation GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`) interleaves 34 KDA linear-attention layers with 11 DSA layers. Prefill CUDA graphs are auto-disabled for KDA models, and `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable` (BCG) opts back in, but BCG breaks the graph at every linear-attention layer: the whole KDA extend runs eagerly on each replay, about sixteen Triton launches per layer plus their Python and the host syncs in `prepare_chunk_indices`. From profiling the eager prefill is CPU launch-bound, not GPU-bound. A prefill step issues about 2300 kernel launches, and with the profiler on it costs about 300 ms of CPU whether it carries 1K or 16K tokens; without the profiler a single 1K-token prompt still waits 152 ms for its first token. BCG halves the launches to 1182 per step, yet a 4K-token step still spends 116 ms on the CPU (with the profiler on), and the KDA chain with its glue is more than 60% of what is left. The KDA extend cannot simply be recorded: its launch grids and index tables come from host-side lengths that change on every replay of a bucket. - `prepare_chunk_indices` builds the (sequence, chunk) table with `.tolist()`; it and `prepare_chunk_offsets` are `tensor_cache`d on the tensor object, so inside a capture they would hand back capture-time tables without recording anything. - `causal_conv1d_fn` sizes its grid from `seq_lens_cpu`, and the delta-rule state kernel launches one program per sequence. - The prefix-cache track path selects rows with host lists or `nonzero` and scatters with data-dependent shapes. ## Design The KDA extend now runs inside the graph on static tables, and BCG breaks only at the DSA layers. - For each token bucket `T`, capture allocates tables at the bucket's bounds: `max_seqs = min(T, SGLANG_KDA_PREFILL_GRAPH_MAX_SEQS)` (128), `max_chunks = cdiv(T, 64) + max_seqs` and `max_conv_blocks = cdiv(T, 8) + max_seqs`. The captured kernels launch fixed grids over these bounds. - Before each replay, `KDAPrefillGraphMetadata.fill` rebuilds the tables from the batch's CPU lengths in numpy and ships them in one pinned asynchronous host-to-device copy; slots and prefix flags come from device gathers. Nothing synchronizes. - Padded rows cost nothing. Padded sequences are empty in `cu_seqlens`, padded chunk rows point past their sequence and return on an `i_t * BT >= T` guard, padded conv blocks and state slots carry `PAD_SLOT_ID`, and rows past the batch's tokens are zeroed so the MoE and the collectives see finite values. - Prefix-cache snapshots become a per-row table (none, final state, chunk-boundary state, conv window start, destination slot) read by two small Triton kernels, instead of host-selected scatters. - The hybrid backend follows the runner's existing captured-metadata contract for BCG (`init_forward_metadata_for_breakable_cuda_graph_capture` / `prepare_forward_metadata_for_breakable_cuda_graph_replay`, as DeepSeek-V4 already does). DSA keeps its eager metadata init. `RadixLinearAttention` skips the eager break when the backend runs the extend in the graph. - The path is active only under a breakable prefill backend, with the Triton KDA extend kernel and without fused-accept verify staging. A batch with more sequences than the cap runs eagerly through `can_run_prefill_cuda_graph`. `SGLANG_DISABLE_KDA_PREFILL_GRAPH_EXTEND=1` restores the per-layer break. ## Modifications - `layers/attention/linear/kda_prefill_graph.py` (new): per-bucket tables, their refresh, the track plan, and `kda_extend_in_graph`, the forward extend on those tables. - `kernels/ops/attention/fla/kda_prefill_graph_track.py` (new): the conv-window and SSM-state snapshot kernels over per-row modes. - `kernels/ops/attention/fla/kda.py`: out-of-range early return in the gate cumsum, `recompute_w_u` and chunk output kernels; `chunk_kda` accepts precomputed `chunk_indices` / `chunk_offsets`. - `kernels/ops/attention/fla/chunk_delta_h.py`: accepts `chunk_offsets` instead of deriving it through `tensor_cache`. - `kernels/ops/mamba/causal_conv1d_triton.py`: optional (sequence, block) table that sets the grid instead of `seq_lens_cpu`. - `layers/attention/linear/kda_backend.py`: capability checks, table capture and refresh, and the dispatch to the graph path. - `layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py`, `base_attn_backend.py`, `layers/radix_linear_attention.py`: the captured-metadata contract, the replay gate and the break decision. - `environ.py`: `SGLANG_DISABLE_KDA_PREFILL_GRAPH_EXTEND`, `SGLANG_KDA_PREFILL_GRAPH_MAX_SEQS`. - `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_prefill_graph.py` (new). ## Accuracy `test_kda_prefill_graph.py` captures one bucket and replays it for five batches of different shapes, against the production eager `forward_extend` on cloned pools. The batches cover several sequences, cached prefixes, padding, chunk-aligned and unaligned prefix-cache snapshots, and no tracking. Every replay matches bit for bit on the output, the conv and SSM pools and the track slots, and no other pool slot changes. The existing KDA, GDN, `causal_conv1d`, mamba2, radix linear attention and hybrid backend tests pass on B300 (13 files). End to end, the natural-language greedy probes produce exactly the text of main's BCG, and GSM8K (200 questions, greedy) scores within one question of eager prefill: | Config | GSM8K | |---|---| | eager prefill (cookbook default) | 98.5% | | main, BCG | 98.5% | | this PR, BCG | 98.5% | | this PR, BCG, 16K chunks | 98.5% | ## Performance 8x B300, GLM-5.3-Flash, cookbook B300 FP8 recipe (TP8, TRT-LLM DSA, FP8 KV, `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE), random-ids, all servers on one box and one tree, no profiler: | Metric | eager (default) | main, BCG | this PR, BCG | this PR, BCG, 16K chunks | |---|---|---|---|---| | TTFT, 1 x 1K tokens | 152 ms | 47 ms | 37 ms | 39 ms | | TTFT, 1 x 4K tokens | 177 ms | 152 ms | 113 ms | 95 ms | | TTFT, 1 x 16K tokens | 495 ms | 419 ms | 384 ms | 333 ms | | c64 1024/256 median TTFT | 968 ms | 767 ms | 696 ms | 708 ms | | c64 1024/256 output tok/s | 4291 | 4167 | 4268 | 4477 | | bs64 decode median ITL | 9.69 ms | 9.63 ms | 9.62 ms | 9.70 ms | With the profiler on, a 4093-token prefill step goes from 1182 eager launches and 116 ms of CPU under main's BCG to 439 launches and 42 ms, and the GPU now finishes 33-35 ms after the last launch: the step is GPU-bound. Prefill graph capture takes 85 s instead of 165 s. "16K chunks" adds `--chunked-prefill-size 16384 --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 16384 --mem-fraction-static 0.78`. GLM-5 defaults BCG prefill to 4096-token chunks, so 16K buckets alone never replay; the 16K buckets cost about 22 GB more graph memory per GPU. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #37721340383](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37721340383) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #37721340093](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37721340093) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #37721340434](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37721340434)

title: [Perf] mimo-v2: Optimize router GEMM with the HPC-Ops bf16xfp32 kernel
author: moehanabi
body:
## Motivation

MiMo-V2's `MoEGate` keeps an fp32 router weight, so every router GEMM upcasts the
bf16 hidden states and runs an fp32 cuBLAS GEMM on CUDA cores. For
MiMo-V2.5-Flash (hidden 4096, 256 routed experts, 47 MoE layers) that runs 47
times per forward pass.

#30247 added the HPC-Ops `gemm_bf16xfp32` path to `linear_bf16_fp32` for
LongCat-Flash. It splits the fp32 weight once into two cached bf16 halves
(`w = w_high + w_low / 256`) and runs both bf16 GEMMs fused on tensor cores with a
single fp32 accumulator. This PR routes the MiMo-V2 router through the same
dispatcher. No new kernel is added.

## Modifications

- `models/mimo_v2.py`: when `SGLANG_OPT_BF16_FP32_GEMM_ALGO=hpc` is set, the
  router weight is fp32, and the `(hidden_size, n_routed_experts)` shape has been
  benchmarked, `MoEGate.forward` dispatches to
  `linear_bf16_fp32(..., hpc_kernel_min_m=...)`.
  - The per-shape min-M table has one entry: `(4096, 256): 8`. On H100 the HPC
    kernel is at least as fast as cuBLAS for every m >= 8 on this shape.
  - Unbenchmarked shapes, bf16 routers, and the default algo keep the original
    path. Without HPC-Ops installed, or below min-M, `linear_bf16_fp32` falls back
    to the existing cuBLAS fp32 GEMM.
- Unlike LongCat, which calls `mark_hpc_bf16xfp32_gemm_enabled()` and is on
  whenever HPC-Ops is installed, the MiMo path is opt-in through the env var, for
  two reasons: the split weight makes generations differ from the cuBLAS path (see
  below), and the cached weight split makes online weight updates unsupported.
  With `algo=hpc`, `hpc_bf16xfp32_gemm_enabled()` is already True, so the
  weight-update guard from #31943 applies. MiMo users who do not set the flag,
  including RL / online-update users, are unaffected.
- Tests and benchmark:
  - `test/registered/unit/models/test_mimo_v2_router_hpc_gemm.py` (new, CPU):
    dispatch with `min_m=8`, default algo, unbenchmarked shape, bf16 router.
  - `test/registered/gemm/test_linear_bf16_fp32_hpc.py`: adds the MiMo router
    shape `(4096, 256)` to the numerical tests.
  - `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/gemm/bench_bf16xfp32_router_gemm.py`: adds
    the same shape.

## Accuracy

- `test_linear_bf16_fp32_hpc.py`: 5 passed on H100, including the MiMo shape.
- `test_mimo_v2_router_hpc_gemm.py` + `test_longcat_flash_router_hpc_gemm.py`:
  8 passed.
- Kernel-level max abs error vs an fp64 reference, using real MiMo-V2.5-Flash gate
  weights from 5 layers and 32768 random N(0,1) bf16 hidden states: cuBLAS fp32
  4.3e-5, HPC 8.5e-5. Top-8 expert selection differs from the fp64 reference for
  0.012% of tokens at worst.

Model-level accuracy is under "Model-level validation" below.

## Performance

Router GEMM microbenchmark, single idle H100, `(n, k) = (256, 4096)`:

    python test/registered/kernels/benchmark/gemm/bench_bf16xfp32_router_gemm.py

| m | cublas (us) | hpc (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 7.8 | 14.6 | 0.53x (below min_m; not used) |
| 8 | 21.0 | 15.0 | 1.4x |
| 64 | 16.9 | 16.8 | 1.0x |
| 512 | 45.8 | 24.0 | 1.9x |
| 1024 | 71.4 | 28.7 | 2.5x |
| 2048 | 127.7 | 28.0 | 4.6x |
| 8192 | 452.3 | 98.4 | 4.6x |

The ratio reproduced across three GPUs on the same node; the absolute times did
not (one GPU was uniformly ~2x slower in both providers, ratio still 5.1x), and
the cuBLAS fp32 baseline is unstable in the m=8..128 range (for example 21us and
40us at m=8 in different runs), so treat the absolute numbers as indicative.

## Model-level validation

MiMo-V2.5-Flash FP8, 8xH100, `--tp 8 --dp-size 2 --enable-dp-attention` (MiMo's
fused qkv weights require attention TP 4, so tp8 serving needs dp2 + DP
attention). A/B runs identical code; only `SGLANG_OPT_BF16_FP32_GEMM_ALGO`
changes. 5 independently launched servers per arm, 4 `bench_one_batch_server`
rounds each (`--dataset-name random-ids --input-len 1024 --output-len 128`), first
round dropped as warmup. Reported as the median of the 5 per-server medians.
HPC-Ops was verified mapped into the scheduler processes only in the hpc arm.

| bs | prefill tok/s | decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8665 -> 8850 (+2.1%) | 97.8 -> 105.2 (**+7.5%**) |
| 16 | 50102 -> 52331 (+4.4%) | 1400 -> 1472 (**+5.1%**) |
| 64 | 52796 -> 58633 (**+11.1%**) | 3788 -> 3900 (**+2.9%**) |

Decode is the solid result: per-server spread is under 1% and the two arms do not
overlap at any batch size. Decode improves even at bs=1 because DP attention plus
CUDA-graph padding already put the router's m at or above `min_m=8`.

For prefill only bs64 is conclusive (cuBLAS 49525-53080 vs HPC 55367-59049, no
overlap). At bs1 and bs16 the arms overlap: per-server spread reaches 26% at bs16
within the hpc arm alone, several times the effect size, so this setup cannot
resolve a prefill difference there. One bs1 cell (1 of the 5 hpc servers) was
dropped as a measurement failure: from round 2 on its ttft went 150ms -> 654ms and
decode fell to 6-24 tok/s while bs16/bs64 on the same server stayed normal, with an
unrelated process holding memory on the node's GPUs at the time. Including it would
make bs1 prefill read -0.0%.

GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot, parallel 128), two runs per arm:

| | accuracy | invalid |
|---|---|---|
| cublas | 0.9545 / 0.9568 | 0.000 |
| this PR | 0.9560 / 0.9591 | 0.000 |

Teacher-forced top-256 prompt logprobs over HTTP on real text (72 sequences,
71450 positions: 64 short GSM8K prompts plus 8 of ~8k tokens; requests sent one at
a time so batch composition is fixed):

| vs an fp64 router GEMM | top-1 agreement | mean KL |
|---|---|---|
| cublas fp32 (current) | 97.92% | 8.06e-3 |
| hpc (this PR) | 97.80% | 8.86e-3 |

Repeated runs of the same algo are bit-identical (greedy text 32/32, logprob KL
exactly 0), so the cross-arm difference (top-1 97.81%, mean KL 8.94e-3) is
entirely this change. MoE routing is sensitive to any router rounding: near-tied
experts reorder and the difference propagates through attention, so any change to
the router GEMM moves outputs by about this much. Measured against an fp64 router,
the HPC path is as close to exact as cuBLAS fp32 is, and it keeps the fp32-weight
routing precision that `moe_router_dtype=float32` asks for. It stays opt-in
because outputs are not bit-identical to the current default.

Environment: upstream main, torch 2.13.0+cu130, sglang-kernel 0.4.7,
flashinfer 0.6.18, HPC-Ops ab1a402 built for CUDA 13.0.

## Test commands

    python -m pytest test/registered/gemm/test_linear_bf16_fp32_hpc.py
    python -m pytest test/registered/unit/models/test_mimo_v2_router_hpc_gemm.py
    python test/registered/kernels/benchmark/gemm/bench_bf16xfp32_router_gemm.py

## Checklist

- [x] Format code according to the [Contribution Guide](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html).
- [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the Contribution Guide.
- [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to the Contribution Guide.
- [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to the [Test & Benchmark Guide](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/test_and_benchmark.html).
- [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR.
- [ ] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR.
```

title: [AMD] Add .co for deepseek v4 fp8 decode kernel and add group decode opt
author: 1am9trash
body: ## Motivation DSpark uses 7 draft tokens a step. They share the same compressed KV and their SWA windows differ by one token each, but the fp8 asm decode splits the grid per token, so that KV gets read 7 times over. aiter's v4 nm asm kernel already takes several q rows in one tile at head=16 (1, 2 or 4), but it doesn't mask between them. Every row sees the full compressed KV and SWA, so the results come out wrong. Once the mask is there, the 7 drafts can run as [4, 3] blocks, sharing the KV read and cutting the CTA count. ## Modifications **Kernel** - Disassembled aiter [PR#5195](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5195)'s .co), added a causal mask and a sliding-window band mask at each softmax exit, reassembled. Bit-identical to the shipped binary at `max_seqlen_q=1`. - Lives at `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/asm/gfx950/mla_v4/mla_a8w8_qh64_qseqlen1_gqaratio64_nm.co`. **sglang** - `unified_kv_kernels/grouped_verify_streams.py`: builds the grouped index streams, laid out [compressed tail][the group's SWA slice] so the kernel's existing bounds land on each draft's cutoff. - `unified_kv_kernels/runtime.py`: Make `decode_fp8_2buff` take `max_seqlen_q` (default=1) and counts sequences from `qo_indptr`. - `deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py`: metadata fields, env gate (off by default), concurrency threshold, and routing. Grouped only at `compress_ratio==128` and `head=16`. **dockerfile** - `docker/rocm.Dockerfile`: copy `.co` over aiter's after the clone. Use `SGLANG_DSV4_GROUPED_ASM` to trigger. ## Accuracy Tests Test gsm8k on both tp8, tp8/dp8, no impact on accuracy (0.95x). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Compare to aiter [PR#5195](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5195). We can get perf uplift on tp8 (head==16), conc >= 16 cases. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. title: [DSv4.1] Move the low-ratio index top-k into dsv4/low_ratio_indexer
author: DarkSharpness
body:
(auto generated by Claude)

## What

Move the DSv4.1 ratio-1/2 (low-ratio) index top-k out of `deepseek_v4_backend.py` into `layers/attention/dsv4/low_ratio_indexer/`. The attention backend only dispatches dense / candidate source / candidate consumer layers and keeps an opaque `CandidateMetadata` on the forward metadata.

- `DenseIndexer`: the plain top-k (DeepGEMM on SM100, the portable path with the fp4 decode logits kernel elsewhere) and the prefill-graph path.
- `CandidateIndexer`: `publish_*` / `consume_*` for prefill and decode, backed by DeepGEMM (sparse table), DeepGEMM CP (block ids) and torch (masks).
- Shared scoring helpers in `deep_gemm_utils.py` and `torch_utils.py`.

No behavior change intended; the chunked eager decode from #40637 is kept.

## Validation

GB300, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4/EP4, main vs this PR:

| Config | GSM8K main | GSM8K PR |
|---|---|---|
| DSpark low-latency | 0.875 | 0.875 |
| High-throughput + `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` | 0.900 | 0.910 |
| Same + `SGLANG_DSV41_TORCH_PREFILL_INDEXER=1` | 0.895 | 0.900 |

- The last two rows use `--chunked-prefill-size 2048 --mem-fraction-static 0.906` on both sides to avoid a pre-existing `flashmla_sched_meta` shared-memory overflow on main.
- A 35k-token request (beyond the candidate window) succeeds in every config.
- bs=1 DSpark verify with a fixed accept length of 3: TPOT 1.948 -> 1.940 ms at 1k input, 1.970 -> 1.963 ms at 32k input; every indexer kernel is within 1 us/step of main in the GPU profile.
- The portable decode/prefill path and the CP block publish/consume are element-wise identical to main in standalone comparisons (RTX A5000).

TODO: port the unit tests of the removed modules to the new package.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Move the index projections back into the layer. `PrefillInputs` / `DecodeInputs` still carry the `DeepseekV41Indexer` module and the backends call `queries()` / `head_weights()` themselves, while `CapturedPrefillInputs` already receives projected `q` / `weights`; the backends should take tensors and metadata only.
- Dispatch inside the ops. The DeepGEMM / torch choice (`use_deep_gemm_*` in `make_full_topk_indexer` / `make_candidate_indexer` and the `_deep_gemm_*` / `_torch_*` method pairs) belongs in `kernels/ops/attention/dsv4` as `BaseFusedOp` backends once the JIT and torch variants share one contract.

title: [AMD] One-launch small-M MoE router for Qwen3.5 on gfx950
author: chuyeh
body:
## Motivation

On MI355X at low concurrency, each Qwen3.5-397B MoE layer routes a verify batch of M = 4 or 8 tokens (4 MTP verify tokens × 1–2 running requests) through three launches before the small-M MoE kernel from #40204:

- the router gate GEMM (`[M, 4096] x [512, 4096]`)
- `_router_triton_kernel` (softmax over 512 experts, top-10, renormalize; one wave per token doing 10 serial argmax passes)
- `_fused_append_shared_experts_with_weights_kernel` (the shared-expert gate GEMV and slot 10)

All three are latency-bound at these sizes. Together they take 19.9 µs per layer in a verify step (eager trace, M = 4). Across 60 layers that is about 1.2 ms per verify step, and the MTP layer adds more in draft and draft extend. This PR replaces them with one launch.

## Modifications

- New `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/smallm_router_gfx950/` (`__init__.py`, `smallm_router.hip`). It is built with `hipcc` on first use and launched through ctypes, reusing #40204's `_hipcc`, `_hip_lib`, `_check` and `_Kernel`. No build-time or wheel change.
- One launch of 257 or 513 blocks, depending on M. Each block computes one or two of the 513 gate rows (512 routed experts plus the shared-expert gate, read in place from `gate.weight` and `shared_expert_gate.weight`) with fp32 accumulation. The last block to finish, elected by a self-resetting ticket counter so the kernel is graph-safe, rounds the routed logits to bf16, then runs top-10 (lowest id wins ties, as in `_router_triton_kernel`), softmax and renormalize. It writes slot 10 = (512, `sigmoid(shared logit) * scale`). The output is exactly the `topk_ids [M, 11] int32` / `topk_weights [M, 11] fp32` that `smallm_moe_gfx950` already consumes.
- `qwen2_moe.py`: one guarded call at the top of `_forward_router_experts` (5 lines). The guard requires gfx95, 1 <= M <= 8, bf16 hidden 4096, gate `[512, 4096]` and shared gate `[1, 4096]` in bf16, exactly one fused shared expert, EP 1, the auto/aiter MoE runner, top-10 with renormalize, no EPLB remap or simulated routing, and not inside a piecewise CUDA graph. Everything else takes today's path. The routed-expert capture and expert-distribution recorder hooks still run.
- The kernel is used for M <= 8 only. The single-block top-k tail makes it slower than today's path from 9 tokens up (0.80x at 9, 0.45x at 40), so c4 verify batches (16 tokens) keep today's path.
- On by default on gfx950; `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_ROUTER=0` turns it off. A build or load failure disables it for the process.
- Registered AMD unit test `test/registered/amd/test_smallm_router_gfx950.py`. It covers ids and weights against today's `moe_fused_gate` + `fused_append_shared_experts_with_weights` at 1 / 3 / 4 / 8 tokens on exactly representable inputs (many ties), fallback at 9 and 41 tokens and for unsupported dtype and shape, the off switch, and graph replay == eager. It passes on `v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260923`.

## Accuracy Tests

Router logits are rounded to bf16 before top-k, as today. Against an fp64-then-bf16 reference on real activations (10,022 token rows), this kernel agrees on 100% of expert choices. Today's path agrees on 98.3%, because its bf16 gate GEMM is not correctly rounded at M >= 2.

`amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2` (revision e17e5f0), MI355X TP4, InferenceX recipe (FP8 KV cache, EAGLE MTP
3 steps / 4 draft tokens, real draft), lm-eval `local-chat-completions` with chat template, 5-shot GSM8K (InferenceX
task), thinking disabled, 16384-token output budget, temperature 0. At most 2 running requests, so every verify batch (<= 8 tokens) is inside the kernel's range.

| Configuration | Strict-match | Flexible-extract |
|---|---:|---:|
| Baseline (main `1417345f5f`) | 97.73% (1289/1319) | 97.73% (1289/1319) |
| This PR | 97.57% (1287/1319) | 97.57% (1287/1319) |

GPQA diamond (198 questions, repeat 8, simple-evals grader), same servers, thinking on, temperature 0.6 / top_p 0.95 /
top_k 20, 32768-token output budget:

| Configuration | Score |
|---|---:|
| Baseline (main `1417345f5f`) | 0.871 (1379/1584) |
| This PR | 0.881 (1396/1584) |
| Reference (Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B model card) | 0.884 |

Same GSM8K task at TP2 (thinking disabled, at most 2 running requests):

| Configuration | Strict-match | Flexible-extract |
|---|---:|---:|
| Baseline (main `1417345f5f`) | 97.57% (1287/1319) | 97.57% (1287/1319) |
| This PR | 97.65% (1288/1319) | 97.65% (1288/1319) |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

### Kernel microbenchmarks

MI355X, one GPU, HIP-graph replay, 512 MB memset before each call to flush L2 / MALL, routing for one MoE layer, in µs:

| Tokens | 3 kernels today | This kernel | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 12.39 | 8.54 | −31% |
| 2 | 12.82 | 8.80 | −31% |
| 4 | 12.90 | 9.05 | −30% |
| 8 | 13.26 | 11.66 | −12% |

In the live server the step saves more than this table suggests: today's `_router_triton_kernel` runs at 11.2 µs per layer in verify and 23.6 µs in draft extend (about 7 µs in isolation), while the new kernel costs about the same everywhere.

### AgentX benchmark

Setup:

- Hardware: MI355X, TP4 / EP1.
- Model and recipe: the InferenceX MI355X agentic recipe for this model, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260923`.
- Server flags: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mem-fraction-static 0.80`, EAGLE MTP 3 / 1 / 4 with simulated acceptance length 3.39, BF16 MTP layer as in the recipe.
- Client: full 3600 s aiperf AgentX trace replay.
- Order: one configuration at a time on the same four GPUs, nothing else on the node.

Baseline is main `1417345f5f` (includes #39901, #39902 and #40204); this PR is the same commit plus this PR.

Concurrency 1:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT median (ms/token) | 2.60 | 2.48 | −4.6% |
| TPOT p90 (ms/token) | 3.04 | 2.94 | −3.3% |
| ITL p95 (ms) | 3.14 | 3.03 | −3.5% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 372 / 795 | 392 / 797 | +5.2% / +0.2% |
| Requests completed in 3600 s | 657 | 684 | +4.1% |
| Interactivity (1 / TPOT) p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 384.0 / 328.4 | 403.6 / 339.9 | +5.1% / +3.5% |
| E2E normalized interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 238.3 / 137.6 | 241.8 / 140.8 | +1.5% / +2.3% |

title: [AMD] Small-M W8A8 FP8 projection GEMM for Qwen3.5 AttnFP8 on gfx950
author: chuyeh
body:
## Motivation

`amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2` keeps the attention and GDN projections in FP8, with per-channel weights and dynamic per-token activations. At decode sizes on MI355X TP4, each layer runs two quant + GEMM pairs through `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle`.

The GEMMs are the first problem. They read their weights far below the bandwidth a plain streaming read reaches. At 4 tokens:

- packed GDN `in_proj` (21 MB): 10.0 us, versus 4.8 us for a streaming read of the same size
- `qkv_proj` (19 MB): 9.7 us, versus 4.5 us
- `out_proj` / `o_proj` (8 MB): 5.4 us, versus 2.8 us

The second problem is the output-side activation quant, after the GDN gated norm and the attention gate multiply. It runs as its own launch.

This PR adds a small-M GEMM for these shapes and folds the output-side quant into the kernel that produces the activation.

## Modifications

- New `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/smallm_fp8_gfx950/` (`__init__.py`, `smallm_fp8_gemm.hip`). It is built with `hipcc` on first use and launched through ctypes, reusing #40204's helpers. `_Kernel.launch` gains `block` / `shared` arguments whose defaults keep the MoE kernel unchanged.
- The GEMM reads the weight exactly as loaded: aiter's (16, 16)-preshuffled `[N, K]`, including #39902's packed QKVZ+BA buffer. There is no loader change and no extra weight copy.
  - Each wave issues all its 16 B non-temporal weight loads up front.
  - It uses `v_mfma_scale_f32_16x16x128_f8f6f4` with fp32 accumulation.
  - For small M on K = 4096, activations are staged once in LDS.
  - `x_scale * w_scale` is applied once per output, with a bf16 store.
- `apply_fp8_linear`: one guarded swap for `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle` on the aiter per-token path. It accepts an already-quantized `(fp8, x_scale [M, 1])` tuple through the existing pre-quantized branch, so it composes with #34502's input-side fusion. The input-side quant itself is unchanged here.
- Output-side quant fusion: `_layer_norm_fwd_1pass_kernel` (GDN `RMSNormGated`) and `_fused_sigmoid_mul_kernel` (attention gate) gain a `QUANT` constexpr that writes per-token FP8 plus scale, bit-identical to `_per_token_group_quant_8bit` on the unfused output. `qwen3_5.py` uses it for `out_proj` / `o_proj` when the consumer is a Quark W8A8 per-token linear and 1 <= M <= 40. The BF16 MTP layer is untouched.
- Guard: gfx950, ROCm >= 7.2, fp8 e4m3fn, bf16 output, and exact shapes with an M window per shape where the new GEMM is at least as fast as the old one:
  - packed `in_proj` (5184, 4096) and `qkv_proj` (4608, 4096): M <= 28;
  - `out_proj` / `o_proj` (4096, 2048): M <= 36.

  Everything else takes today's path.
- On by default on gfx950; `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_FP8_PROJ=0` turns both parts off. A build or load failure disables it for the process.
- Registered AMD unit test `test/registered/amd/test_smallm_fp8_proj_gfx950.py`:
  - the GEMM against `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle` for the three TP4 shapes at M in {1, 4, 16, 24, 29, 36, 41}, with dispatch inside the guard and fallback outside;
  - tuple input == bf16 input;
  - the off switch;
  - the producer guard;
  - bit-exactness of the fused quant for both producers;
  - graph replay == eager.

  It passes on `v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260923`, together with the existing `test_qwen35_gdn_packed_fp8_in_proj.py` and `test_smallm_moe_gfx950.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

The math stays W8A8. Against `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle` on the real shapes, outputs are bit-identical in 20 of 21 (shape, M) cases, and the rest differ by at most 1 bf16 ulp. The fused quant is bit-identical.

`amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2` (revision e17e5f0), MI355X TP4, InferenceX recipe (FP8 KV cache, EAGLE MTP
3 steps / 4 draft tokens, real draft), lm-eval `local-chat-completions` with chat template, 5-shot GSM8K (InferenceX
task), thinking disabled, 16384-token output budget, temperature 0. At most 7 running requests (GPQA at 5 and GSM8K at 2 on the same server), so verify batches (<= 28 tokens) are inside the GEMM's range.

| Configuration | Strict-match | Flexible-extract |
|---|---:|---:|
| Baseline (main `1417345f5f`) | 97.57% (1287/1319) | 97.57% (1287/1319) |
| This PR | 97.65% (1288/1319) | 97.65% (1288/1319) |

GPQA diamond (198 questions, repeat 8, simple-evals grader), same servers, thinking on, temperature 0.6 / top_p 0.95 /
top_k 20, 32768-token output budget:

| Configuration | Score |
|---|---:|
| Baseline (main `1417345f5f`) | 0.871 (1380/1584) |
| This PR | 0.869 (1376/1584) |
| Reference (Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B model card) | 0.884 |

Same GSM8K task at TP2 (thinking disabled, at most 2 running requests):

| Configuration | Strict-match | Flexible-extract |
|---|---:|---:|
| Baseline (main `1417345f5f`) | 97.57% (1287/1319) | 97.57% (1287/1319) |
| This PR | 97.73% (1289/1319) | 97.73% (1289/1319) |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

### Kernel microbenchmarks

MI355X, HIP-graph replay, weights streamed from HBM with buffers rotated over > 256 MB MALL, GEMM only:

| Shape | Tokens | `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle` (µs) | This kernel (µs) | % of streaming-read ceiling |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| packed GDN `in_proj` (5184 x 4096) | 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 | 9.97 / 10.00 / 10.03 / 8.39 | 5.66 / 5.85 / 5.87 / 6.37 | 85 / 82 / 82 / 75 |
| `qkv_proj` (4608 x 4096) | 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 | 9.70 / 9.72 / 9.75 / 8.17 | 5.43 / 5.53 / 5.62 / 6.12 | 82 / 81 / 79 / 73 |
| `out_proj` / `o_proj` (4096 x 2048) | 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 | 5.31 / 5.43 / 5.44 / 4.73 | 3.37 / 3.52 / 3.58 / 3.78 | 83 / 79 / 78 / 74 |

Fused producers at 4 tokens: GDN gated norm + quant 3.97 → 2.66 µs, attention gate multiply + quant 3.79 → 2.14 µs.
That removes 60 `_per_token_group_quant_8bit` launches per verify step.

### AgentX benchmark

Setup:

- Hardware: MI355X, TP4 / EP1.
- Model and recipe: InferenceX MI355X agentic recipe for this model, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260923`.
- Server flags: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mem-fraction-static 0.80`, EAGLE MTP 3 / 1 / 4, simulated acceptance length 3.39, BF16 MTP layer as in the recipe.
- Client: full 3600 s aiperf AgentX trace replay.
- Order: on the same four GPUs, one configuration at a time, nothing else on the node.

Baseline = main `1417345f5f` (includes #39901, #39902 and #40204), this PR = the same commit + this PR.

Concurrency 1:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT median (ms/token) | 2.60 | 2.44 | −6.2% |
| TPOT p90 (ms/token) | 3.04 | 2.88 | −5.3% |
| ITL p95 (ms) | 3.14 | 2.96 | −5.7% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 372 / 795 | 383 / 782 | +3.0% / −1.6% |
| Requests completed in 3600 s | 657 | 686 | +4.4% |
| Interactivity (1 / TPOT) p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 384.0 / 328.4 | 409.5 / 347.8 | +6.6% / +5.9% |
| E2E normalized interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 238.3 / 137.6 | 248.5 / 137.9 | +4.3% / +0.2% |

Concurrency 8, average of two full runs per configuration (the second pass in reverse order). Verify batches are
4 x running requests, up to 32 tokens: `out_proj` / `o_proj` and the fused quant stay in range at every batch,
`in_proj` / `qkv_proj` fall back above 28 tokens:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT median (ms/token) | 3.40 | 3.18 | −6.5% |
| TPOT p90 (ms/token) | 4.18 | 4.05 | −3.0% |
| ITL p95 (ms) | 4.62 | 4.47 | −3.0% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 602 / 1049 | 602 / 1043 | 0.0% / −0.6% |
| Requests / generated tokens in 3600 s | 1502 / 1.481M | 1504 / 1.486M | +0.1% / +0.3% |
| Interactivity (1 / TPOT) p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 294.4 / 239.5 | 314.3 / 246.8 | +6.8% / +3.0% |
| E2E normalized interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 194.4 / 101.1 | 205.3 / 103.4 | +5.6% / +2.2% |

TPOT is reported as median and p90 rather than mean: in this replay a few short-output requests wait behind another request's long chunked prefill (up to 4.3 s for a 2-token answer), and a single such request moves the mean of a 3600 s run by up to 3 ms/token. Matching every request across the six concurrency-8 runs (baseline, #41133, #41134, two runs each), no request stalled in both runs of a PR without also stalling in a baseline run.

At TP2 with the official HiCache high-concurrency setup, including the TP2 GEMM shapes, concurrency 20 TPOT median / p90 is 6.89 / 11.43 ms versus 6.97 / 11.39 ms for the baseline. At concurrency 40, with a 78.6% cache hit rate (the baseline runs are 78.2–78.7%), TPOT median / p90 is 15.17 / 42.12 ms versus 14.72–15.28 / 40.93–42.52 ms.

title: [AMD][DI][CI] Leave the GLM-5.2 MTP decode room to load its Triton kernels
author: Lzy17
body:
The 1P1D MTP test stops after concurrency 128. GSM8K passes at 0.955, then at 256 two schedulers die with `hipErrorLaunchOutOfResources`.

It is not a launch-config limit. MTP captures three CUDA graphs where the non-MTP sibling captures one, so the same `mem_fraction_static: 0.90` leaves 11.46 GB free after init instead of 25.07 GB:

| | graphs | free after init |
|---|---|---|
| `1p1d` | 2.05 GB | 25.07 GB |
| `1p1d-mtp` | 16.00 GB | 11.46 GB |

Concurrency 256 spends the rest. The DSA metadata kernels, which Triton first loads onto the device mid-serving, then have nothing left to load into; `triton_load_watch` logs the load at 0.00 GiB free just before ROCr aborts the queues.

Same shape as the kimik26 MTP fix in #41025. 0.85 on decode only; prefill and every other emitted value are unchanged.

Verified on ROCm 10 (`v0.5.20-rocm10-mi35x-20260923`); re-run in progress, will post the 7/7 sweep.

title: [JIT] Clean up kernel headers: move runtime helpers, add once.h
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> (auto generated by Claude)

## Motivation

Clean up the JIT kernel headers: move helpers that sit in the wrong header, make kernels reuse the existing runtime utilities instead of hand-rolling them, and unify host-side error checking and logging.

## Modifications

- `runtime.cuh`: move the L1 carveout helpers here from `utils.cuh` (`set_smem_carveout`, `set_prefer_l1_carveout`, `set_prefer_l1_carveout_with_occupancy`), and add `set_max_dynamic_smem`.
- `runtime.cuh`: add `init_per_device` / `set_max_dynamic_smem_per_device`, a relaxed per-device once-flag whose hot path is a single atomic load.
- `utils.cuh`: remove `prefer_l1_carveout` / `ensure_prefer_l1` and the `LaunchKernel` `prefer_l1` option (no remaining users), together with its test `test_launch_carveout`.
- Replace `allocator.h` with `once.h` (`init_once`, `CacheMap`, `CacheSet`), the host-side counterpart of the runtime helpers.
- Use the runtime helpers in `topk_v1`, `topk_v2`, `kpool_topk_transform`, `dsv3_fused_a_gemm`, `hicache_tma`, `hisparse`, speculative `sampling` and `wo_a_fused`. This replaces hand-rolled static once-guards, and stops `cudaFuncSetAttribute` from being called on every launch.
- `RuntimeDeviceCheck` / `CHECK_CUDA` accept both CUDA runtime (`cudaError_t`) and driver (`CUresult`) error codes, via `runtime::is_cuda_error` / `runtime::get_cuda_error_string`. The driver overload references `cuGetErrorString` only when a `CUresult` is actually checked, so other modules do not gain a `-lcuda` dependency.
- `utils.h`: `Error` exposes its stream directly through `SGL_PANIC`, so stream manipulators such as `std::endl` work; `CHECK_HOST` / `CHECK_CUDA` build on it and are fully qualified so they work outside `namespace sglang`.
- Add `logging.h`: `SGL_LOG_DEBUG` / `SGL_LOG_INFO` / `SGL_LOG_WARNING`, gated by `SGLANG_JIT_LOG_LEVEL` (registered in `environ.py`, default `WARNING`). The level is read once when each module is loaded.
- `convrot_int8`: include `tvm/ffi/extra/cuda/device_guard.h` explicitly instead of relying on `utils.cuh` pulling it in.
- Reuse `warp::get_lane_id` in `topk_bf16_small`, and mark `pack_w` / `unpack_w` in `c_plan` as host-device.

## Validation

- All touched JIT modules compile for sm_90a and sm_100a (`wo_a_fused` for sm_100a only), with the `topk_v2` cluster paths enabled; `convrot_int8` compiles for sm_120.
- `CHECK_CUDA` / `RuntimeDeviceCheck` / `CHECK_HOST` / `SGL_LOG_*` checked on success and failure paths for both error-code types, including a trailing user `else` binding to the user's `if`.
- Kernel correctness tests are left to CI.

title: [AMD] Fix int32 offset overflow in Triton DSv4 KV store kernels
author: RolaoDenthu
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
On ROCm, the Triton DSv4 KV store kernels (`triton_store_cache.py`) cast `loc` to int32 and compute cache offsets in int32. 

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's compress-ratio-1 KV pool is ~23.6 GB per layer, so the offsets overflow once `loc` passes ~3.67M tokens: writes land outside the buffer, silently at first, then as a `Memory access fault` at ~7.34M tokens (hit during AgentX warmup at conc >= 16). The CUDA kernel with the same functionality uses int64 offsets.
## Modifications
Load `loc` as `tl.int64` in both kernels (flashmla and indexer).

title: [Kimi-K3] Merge fused_qkvg_proj into the loader-seeded packed_modules_mapping
author: pengwu22
body:
## Motivation

- The model loader seeds a quant config's packed-modules mapping from the outer Kimi-K3 model class. That mapping is how fused layers (gate/up, qkv, the qkv conv1d) are expanded back to the per-shard names used by a checkpoint's exclude or per-layer quantization lists.
- The linear language model then registers its own fused projection through a call that replaces the mapping instead of extending it, so for every non-ModelSlim quant config only that one entry survives. The ModelSlim branch right above already merges.
- With a checkpoint that excludes per-shard modules, the fused layer is quantized instead of skipped and loading fails on a weight-shape assertion in the merged-column loader. The same lookup backs FP8/FP4 layer skipping, mixed-precision algorithm resolution, and Quark's layer matching.

## Modifications

- (-) The non-ModelSlim branch replaced the quant config's packed-modules mapping with the linear model's single fused entry.
- (+) It merges that entry into the loader-seeded mapping, matching the ModelSlim branch. A CPU unit test builds the model with mocked submodules and checks the merged mapping and per-shard exclusion (fails on main).

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: config-resolution fix, no numerics change.

title: Fix mixed chunk prefill with DP speculative coordination
author: Oasis-Git
body:
Follow-up to #40118.

With DP spec/prefill coordination and `--enable-mixed-chunk` enabled, a prefill rank containing local decode requests raises `Local mixed prefill/verify is not implemented`. Remove that guard so the mixed rank runs prefill with one-token local decode progress while decode-only peers retain speculative decoding. This does not add speculative verification within the local mixed batch.

Remove the unit test asserting the old rejection and add a standalone GPU regression registered for `base-c` on `4-gpu-h100`. It starts decoding on both DP ranks, injects a long prefill on each rank in turn, and checks exact isolated-versus-overlapped outputs and subsequent decode correctness. The assertions use deterministic inference and validate the generated counting sequence.

Validation:
- Local 2×B300 run with Triton attention, Qwen3-30B-A3B/EAGLE3, real speculative acceptance and strict memory checks: passed, 0 failures/errors.
- External observation confirmed five successful local mixed-prefill steps and five speculative-peer steps on each rank. Serving source was unchanged during validation.
- Pre-commit passed after cherry-picking the two follow-up commits onto current `main`.

The GPU run was performed before that cherry-pick. The registered H100/FA3 CI test has not been run yet.
