title: [Feat] hicache: Support MLA DCP with HiCache L3(file/mooncake)
author: ByronHsu
body:
## Why?

1. HiCache L3 rejects DCP.
2. This stack adds MLA + DCP + L3 support:
   - #41187 (this PR): file storage.
   - #41265: Mooncake storage.
   - #41591: hybrid MLA/KDA storage.

## What?

1. Allow file L3 with DCP for one materialized MLA host pool using `layer_first`, `page_first`, or `page_first_direct`. Keep existing validation; split buffers, separate scale buffers, and additional pools remain unsupported.
2. Pass `is_storage_owner` to file eviction instead of deriving ownership from `is_mla_model`. Select one writer per distinct MLA shard, avoiding duplicate writes and eviction accounting:

```text
TP=4 / DCP=2:
rank 0 writes shard 0 -> ranks 0,2 read
rank 1 writes shard 1 -> ranks 1,3 read
2 files per logical page
```

3. Translate logical page positions into physical rows and count only complete logical pages:

```text
64 physical tokens/shard x 2 = 128 logical tokens
logical start 256 -> physical start 128 on each rank

Both shards present -> complete page hit
Either shard missing -> stop before that page
```

KV-format/layout key separation remains deferred with a TODO; engines sharing files must use compatible formats and layouts.

## Tests?

- Six focused CPU tests added to existing CI-registered file-backend and host-pool tests. No new test files.
- CPU regressions: **62 tests and 40 subtests passed**, covering DCP keys/ownership, page mapping, file eviction, attachment, and prefetch.
- **Previously validated manually on H200**, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, BF16, TP=4/DCP=2, `page_first`, write-through, complete-prefetch waiting: **1 passed in 149.48 s**.

```text
Cold writer:  1,025 input tokens -> 16 files, zero cache hits
Fresh reader: 1,024 L3 tokens    -> identical output IDs
Missing shard in page 2:        -> 128 L3 tokens, identical output IDs
```

- Ruff, import ordering, registered-test validation, and whitespace checks passed. The history rewrite preserves the cleaned Git tree exactly. CI status is tracked below.

title: [Score API] Setwise scoring: CausalLM support (batched + --enable-mis)
author: sundar24295s
body:
# Setwise Scoring: CausalLM Support

Follow-up to **[Score API] Setwise Scoring Support (#38965)** (merged). That PR
added setwise scoring for SequenceClassification models; this PR extends the same
`token_indices_to_pool` primitive to generative (CausalLM) models.

## Summary

Extends **setwise scoring** to **CausalLM** models. A generative reranker can now
read **label-token logprobs at every occurrence of a caller-chosen extraction
token** in each `query + item` sequence, instead of only at the last token — the
generative analogue of the SequenceClassification setwise path. A candidate set is
packed into one item with one extraction token per candidate; the LM head is read at
each of those positions in a **single prefill**, so `scores` comes back as one
`[N_i x num_labels]` matrix per item (nested per item), where `num_labels =
len(label_token_ids)`.

The unifying signal is unchanged: `token_indices_to_pool` still names the readout
positions. For SequenceClassification the pooler pools the classification head there;
for CausalLM the LM head is applied there and the requested `label_token_ids`
logprobs are gathered — one row per anchor.

**Modes:** both **batched (default)** and fused **`--enable-mis`** are supported,
matching the SequenceClassification setwise paths.

## Motivation

Many rerankers are decoder-only models that express a candidate's score as the
probability the model assigns to specific label tokens (e.g. `yes`/`no`, a rating
digit) right after each candidate. Without setwise support such a caller must issue
one request per candidate, paying the shared query-prefix cost N times. This PR packs
the whole candidate block into one prompt with one anchor per candidate and returns
all N per-candidate label distributions from a single prefill.

## API

### Engine (in-process)

```python
result = engine.score(
    query="",                        # optional shared prefix
    items=[prompt_with_anchors],     # one item = one candidate set
    label_token_ids=[yes_id, no_id], # required for CausalLM
    score_extraction_token_id=anchor_id,
    apply_softmax=False,
)
# result.scores -> [num_items][N_i x num_labels]   (nested per item)
#   each row = per-anchor label-token scores: softmax over labels when
#   apply_softmax=True, else exp(logprob) probabilities (the existing pointwise
#   CausalLM conversion, applied per anchor).
```

### HTTP (`POST /v1/score`)

```json
{
  "query": "",
  "items": ["Rank the candidates. C0. C1. C2. Scores:<|object_ref_start|><|object_ref_start|><|object_ref_start|>"],
  "label_token_ids": [9454, 2753],
  "score_extraction_token": "<|object_ref_start|>",
  "apply_softmax": false
}
```

No new request/response fields: this reuses `score_extraction_token` /
`score_extraction_token_id` and the existing nested `ScoringResponse.scores` union.
`label_token_ids` is **required** for CausalLM (as for pointwise CausalLM scoring).

## Semantics & validation

- **Both execution modes.** Batched scores each item as an independent `query + item`
  sequence; fused `--enable-mis` packs the items into one sequence with a
  block-diagonal mask that isolates each set, and splits the flat result back per
  item. Both return nested `[num_items][Nᵢ x num_labels]`.
- The SequenceClassification `is_score_and_pool_model` allow-list is unchanged and
  still governs the non-generation path; generation skips that check.
- All other setwise constraints are shared: every item must contain at least one
  extraction token, the shared query prefix must not contain it, and radix cache /
  chunked prefill must be off with no `--allow-auto-truncate` (pooling positions are
  full-prompt coordinates). All raise a clean `400` before inference.
- `return_pooled_hidden_states` stays rejected for CausalLM (no task head).

## How it works

`token_indices_to_pool` already flows to every `ForwardBatch`. For SequenceClassification
the pooler consumes it; for CausalLM there is no task head, so the LM head is applied
at those positions instead — mirroring the existing multi-item (`--enable-mis`)
delimiter path, but pooling **AT** the anchor (no `delimiter - 1` shift, no discarded
row). The forward dispatch prioritizes the anchor readout over the delimiter path, so
it serves both modes; the block-diagonal MIS mask is applied independently by the
attention backend (gated on `enable_mis`), so a batched request never triggers it
while a fused one does.

## Implementation

| Area | File | Change |
|---|---|---|
| LM-head readout | `layers/logits_processor.py` | `compute_logprobs_at_positions()` — reads the LM head AT `token_indices_to_pool` and gathers `label_token_ids` logprobs (one row per anchor); a `forward()` branch dispatches to it for prefill-only requests carrying the field, taking precedence over the MIS delimiter path so it serves both modes. |
| Logprob bookkeeping | `managers/scheduler_components/logprob_result_processor.py` | Generalized "position-based scoring" (`_scoring_positions`): setwise anchors take precedence over MIS delimiters (a fused setwise request carries both), so the expected input-logprob count is `len(token_indices_to_pool)`. |
| Request plumbing | `managers/io_struct.py` | `token_indices_to_pool` on `GenerateReqInput` (per-item split in `__getitem__`) and `TokenizedGenerateReqInput`. |
| | `managers/tokenizer_manager.py`, `managers/scheduler.py` | Thread the field into the tokenized generate request and the `Req`. |
| Score engine | `managers/tokenizer_manager_score_mixin.py` | Validation allows CausalLM setwise (batched and `--enable-mis`); `score_request` sets `token_indices_to_pool` + `logprob_start_len=0`; the batched result branch reads per-request `input_token_ids_logprobs`, and the fused `_process_multi_item_extraction_results` gains a generation branch that reads the flat `input_token_ids_logprobs` and splits per item via `per_item_anchor_counts`. Both reuse `_convert_logprobs_to_scores` (per-item labels + temperature). |
| Docs | `entrypoints/openai/protocol.py`, `entrypoints/engine_score_mixin.py` | `score_extraction_token(_id)` docs note CausalLM support. |
| Tests | `test/registered/unit/managers/test_setwise_score_mixin.py`, `test/registered/e2e/scoring/test_setwise_scoring.py` | CPU result-grouping + validation tests and a CausalLM HF-parity / MIS set-isolation E2E suite. |

## Tests

```bash
# CPU unit tests (no GPU / model needed)
python test/registered/unit/managers/test_setwise_score_mixin.py -v
python test/registered/unit/layers/test_pooler_score_and_pool.py -v

# E2E (GPU); CausalLM setwise uses a decoder-only checkpoint
export TEST_CAUSAL_LM_MODEL=<path-to>/Qwen3-0.6B
python test/registered/e2e/scoring/test_setwise_scoring.py -v
```

- **Unit** (`test_setwise_score_mixin.py`): a `_GenHarness` (`is_generation=True`)
  plus a `TestGenerationSetwiseResults` suite covering nested grouping (batched and
  fused/MIS) from `input_token_ids_logprobs`, softmax on/off, missing-label → `0.0`,
  empty-logprobs / row-count-mismatch errors, and a pointwise-unchanged regression;
  validation tests assert CausalLM setwise is allowed.
- **E2E** (`test_setwise_scoring.py`): `TestGenerationSetwiseScoringHFParity` asserts
  numerical parity against a HuggingFace reference (gather `log_softmax(LM-head
  logits)` at each anchor, exponentiate for `apply_softmax=False`), single- and
  multi-item. `TestGenerationSetwiseMISScoring` asserts block-diagonal **set
  isolation** — the property only a real fused forward exercises. Shape/grouping/error
  cases live in the CPU unit tests, not duplicated in the GPU suite.

## Validation

Environment: H100 80GB, `flashinfer 0.6.18`, `sglang-kernel 0.4.7`, `Qwen3-0.6B`
(CausalLM base, anchor `<|object_ref_start|>`), engine `float16` on `flashinfer`.

| Suite | Cases | Type | Result |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `test_setwise_score_mixin.py` | 50 | CPU unit | PASS |
| `test_pooler_score_and_pool.py` | 12 | CPU unit | PASS |
| `test_token_scoring.py` | 10 | CPU unit | PASS |
| `test_setwise_scoring.py::TestGenerationSetwiseScoringHFParity` | 2 | E2E (HF parity, single + multi-item) | PASS |
| `test_setwise_scoring.py::TestGenerationSetwiseMISScoring` | 1 | E2E (fused set isolation) | PASS |
| lint: ruff / ruff-format / isort / codespell / registered-tests | — | lint | PASS |

### HTTP smoke test (`launch_server` + `curl /v1/score`)

- Setwise, 1 item × 3 anchors, `apply_softmax=false` → nested `[1][3 x 2]` probability
  matrix.
- Setwise, 1 item × 2 anchors, `apply_softmax=true` → nested `[1][2 x 2]`, each row
  sums to 1.0.
- Pointwise (no `score_extraction_token`), 2 items → flat `[2 x 2]` — backward
  compatibility intact.

## Backward compatibility

Purely additive. Pointwise CausalLM scoring is unchanged (`score_extraction_token_id`
unset → last-token `output_token_ids_logprobs` path, flat `[num_rows x num_labels]`).
SequenceClassification setwise behavior is untouched — the only shared-path change is
the logprob-count bookkeeping, which now recognizes `token_indices_to_pool` in
addition to MIS delimiters.
}

title: [Fix] Complete the all-reduce when the flashinfer fused norm declines a batch
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41200
* #41199
* #41191
* #41198
* #41197
* #41196
* #41195
* #41194
* __->__ #41193

## Motivation

`_forward_with_allreduce_fusion` (`layers/layernorm.py`) hands the all-reduce, residual add and RMSNorm to `flashinfer_allreduce_residual_rmsnorm`. That call returns `(None, None)` when it does not take the batch, for example when an input is not contiguous, or when the workspace has to be (re)initialized on that call and initialization fails.

On that path the flashinfer branch fell through to the plain norm, with two effects:

- the partial sum the caller left for the kernel was never all-reduced;
- `post_residual_addition`, which had already been folded into the residual, was added a second time.

The aiter branch already has a correct fallback.

The caller's gate, `apply_flashinfer_allreduce_fusion`, only rules out an unavailable flashinfer comm API. So a decline can still happen after the gate has passed. It was not observed in a shipped configuration: warmup pre-initializes the workspaces.

The fallback assumes every rank of the group declines together. That holds for a non-contiguous input and for a setup that fails on every rank. A setup that fails on only some ranks still leaves the ranks in different collectives, as it did before this PR.

## Modifications

- `layers/layernorm.py`, when the flashinfer kernel declines:
  - all-reduce over the group the kernel reduces over: the attention-TP group when `use_attn_tp_group` is set, otherwise the group `deferred_post_experts_all_reduce` uses (the same choice as `resolve_fusion_group`);
  - then add the residual and apply the norm into a new residual tensor.

  Like the kernel, this leaves the input residual unmodified. The Eagle3 aux capture keeps a reference to it on the fused path.
- New CPU test `test/registered/unit/layers/test_layernorm_allreduce_fusion.py`. On a decline it checks that:
  - exactly one all-reduce runs, over the kernel's group (attention TP, MoE-TP, MoE-EP, and mergeable EP × TP → TP);
  - `post_residual_addition` is added once;
  - the input residual is left unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

- **New test:** fails on the parent (9 failures: no all-reduce, numeric mismatches, mutated residual) and passes on this PR. The 20 related unit files pass, run one by one and together.
- **GPU, B200, Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP2:** fusion `auto` (resolves to MNNVL), 4 greedy requests × 32 tokens; text, token logprobs and top-5 logprobs compared. A per-process counter confirms both callers reached the forced decline (4,183 calls with `use_attn_tp_group=True` and 4,096 with `False` per rank):

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| This PR, fusion disabled | reference |
| This PR, fusion on, kernel forced to decline | **identical** to the reference |
| Parent, fusion on, kernel forced to decline | garbage output ("honey honey honey …") |
| This PR, fusion on, kernel running normally | differs from the reference only by the fused kernel's own rounding, as before |

Rebased onto main `9dc4c5d891`: every commit's patch is unchanged, and the related unit tests pass on the new base. The GPU results above were measured on the previous base, `5bb850d536`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The normal fused path is unchanged; only the decline path adds its all-reduce.

title: [Fix] Plan NextN / MTP draft layers as one-layer models and fix the Bailing V2 NextN draft
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41200
* #41199
* #41191
* #41198
* #41197
* #41196
* #41195
* __->__ #41194
* #41193

## Motivation

This PR fixes three defects in NextN / MTP draft layers. Each commit fixes one.

1. **Layout plan.** `LayerScatterModes` treats `layer_id == 0` as the first layer (it takes the model's input layout) and `layer_id == num_layers - 1` as the last (it returns the model's output layout). Two draft layers were planned as middle layers instead:
   - the Bailing V2 / V2.5 NextN layers, passed as layer 0 of `num_hidden_layers`;
   - the Step-3.5 MTP layer, passed as layer 45 of 1.

   When the draft's MLP runs on SCATTERED tokens with attention TP > 1, the draft returned this rank's shard of tokens to the logits and to the next step. The SCATTERED triggers are an a2a backend, dwdp, FP4 cutlass allgather, or `moe_dense_tp_size` 1. The Step-3.5 MTP layer also planned an all-gather for an input that is already full. Separately, the Bailing V2.5 NextN plan treated the layer as dense whenever the model's first layers are dense, even though the layer builds an MoE. DeepSeek NextN and Bailing V3 already pass layer 0 of 1 (the same fix as #7420 for DeepSeek).
2. **Unloaded Bailing V2 NextN MLP.** `BailingMoEBlock` chose between the MoE and the dense MLP with `is_nextn=False`. So the NextN layer (layer 0) became a dense MLP whenever `first_k_dense_replace >= 1`, while the checkpoint's NextN layer holds expert weights (Ling-mini-2.0: `model.layers.20.mlp.experts.*`). `load_weights` skips names with no matching parameter, so the draft ran an MLP whose weights were never loaded (all zeros).
3. **Bailing V2 NextN could not start.** Every Bailing draft is renamed `BailingMoeForCausalLMNextN`, and `_derive_model_shapes` sent that name down the MLA branch added for V2.5. V2 is GQA and has no `kv_lora_rank`, so NextN speculative decoding on a V2 target failed at startup with `'BailingMoeV2Config' object has no attribute 'kv_lora_rank'`.

## Modifications

- **`models/bailing_moe.py`, `models/bailing_moe_linear.py`, `models/step3p5.py`:** draft layers pass `layer_id=0, num_layers=1` to `LayerScatterModes.init_new`. The Step-3.5 layer id still indexes its per-layer config. The Bailing V2.5 NextN plan is sparse.
- **`models/bailing_moe.py`:** the NextN layer builds `BailingMoESparseMoeBlock`.
- **`configs/model_config.py`:** the MLA branch takes `BailingMoeForCausalLMNextN` only when the draft config carries `kv_lora_rank`, which the V2.5 and V3 drafts do. A V2 draft now derives its shapes the way its target does. V3 drafts still take this branch rather than the V3 one, as before.
- **Tests:**
  - `test_last_layer_communicator.py` now records the `LayerScatterModes.init_new` arguments. It checks that every draft layer is planned as layer 0 of 1, that the V2.5 NextN plan is sparse, and that the V2 NextN layer builds the MoE block.
  - `test_model_config_shapes.py`: a GQA and an MLA Bailing draft each keep their attention architecture.

  All of these fail on main.

Configurations whose MLP does not run on SCATTERED tokens plan the same layouts before and after.

## Accuracy Tests

**GPU, H200, Ling-mini-base-2.0 TP2.** 4 greedy requests × 32 tokens; text, token logprobs and top-5 logprobs compared. NextN speculative decoding with 1 step, topk 1 and 2 draft tokens; also the default 3 / 1 / 4. Accept length = completion tokens / verify steps.

Runs before the third commit need a test-harness shim that only derives the draft's shapes. It is applied identically to every tree and is not needed after the third commit.

| Tree | Config | Result | Accept length |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | speculative off | reference | – |
| main / first commit | speculative | identical to the reference | 1.600 / 1.600 |
| second commit | speculative | text identical to the reference | **1.939** |
| main / first / second | speculative, default 3 / 1 / 4 | text identical | 1.684 / 1.684 / **2.462** |
| main | speculative, `moe_dense_tp_size=1` | **crash** on the first draft forward: index out of bounds in `logits_processor._get_logits` | – |
| first / second commit | speculative, `moe_dense_tp_size=1` | identical to the target-only run with the same setting | 1.580 / 1.910 |
| third commit, no shim | the configurations above | starts; identical to each shimmed run | 1.939 / 2.462 / 1.910 |

- **Draft-layer audit:**
  - main under `moe_dense_tp_size=1`: `mlp=SCATTERED, layer_output_mode=SCATTERED`;
  - first commit: `layer_output_mode=TP_ATTN_FULL`;
  - second commit: the NextN layer is `BailingMoESparseMoeBlock`.
- **Weight checksums before and after `load_weights`:**
  - on main, the draft's dense `gate_up_proj` / `down_proj` stay all zeros;
  - after the second commit, only the `word_embeddings` / `lm_head` shared with the target are untouched.

**GPU, H200, Step-3.5-Flash BF16 TP8 MTP** (EAGLE 3 / 1 / 4):

- **Default configuration:** main and this PR are bit-identical (accept length 2.560).
- **With `moe_dense_tp_size=1`:** main crashes in the draft's CUDA graph capture (`size of tensor a (32) must match ... b (4)`: the MTP layer returned its shard), and this PR does not.
- **Caveat:** the Step-3.5 target and its MTP draft are not correct under that setting. `Step3p5MLP` always shards over TP and all-reduces, so on SCATTERED tokens it sums different ranks' tokens. Only the crash fix is verified here, not end-to-end output; the dense MLP under `moe_dense_tp_size=1` is left for a follow-up.

Rebased onto main `9dc4c5d891`: every commit's patch is unchanged, and the related unit tests pass on the new base. The GPU results above were measured on the previous base, `5bb850d536`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured. The layout plans change only under the SCATTERED triggers, and the second commit makes the draft's MLP the MoE the checkpoint was trained with.

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Refactor] Carry a deferred FFN all-reduce as UnreducedOutput and complete it in the next layer without the fused kernel
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41200
* #41199
* #41191
* #41198
* #41197
* __->__ #41196
* #41195
* #41194
* #41193

## Motivation

A decoder layer can leave its FFN all-reduce to the next layer's input norm. Until now it did so only when the fused all-reduce + residual + norm kernel took the batch, and it marked the output tensor with a `_sglang_needs_allreduce_fusion` attribute.

- **The marker was easy to lose.** Slicing, views and copies drop the attribute, and code that reads the tensor never sees it. So a consumer between layers could use the partial sum as if it were complete; the pipeline send, deepstack and aux capture fixes were each such a consumer.
- **The completion lived in two places.** The FFN reduced its own output whenever the fused kernel did not take the batch.

## Modifications

- **`UnreducedOutput`** (first commit): a small value holding the partial sum. It is not a tensor, so using it as one raises. Only the next layer's `prepare_attn` and an explicit `reduce_output()` read it.
  - `reduce_output()` replaces `complete_deferred_allreduce()`.
  - `layer_input_buffer()` serves the two layers that reuse their input's memory as the MoE output buffer.
  - `FfnExit.finish` returns the wrapper, and `finish_layer_stack` reduces it.
  - The CuteDSL communicator fuses the all-reduce of the wrapper's partial sum where it fused a marked tensor.
  - The models that set the marker themselves (Step-3.5, Qwen3.5, MiniMax-M3, GLM5-Next, Dots3, Nemotron-H) return the wrapper.
  - The deepstack additions and aux captures call `reduce_output()`. The two-batch-overlap entry reduces its input first, before it splits the batch and reads the input's length.
- **Next layer completes the sum** (second commit): `should_defer_ffn_reduction()`, used by `ffn_exit`, defers whenever the fused kernel would.
  - **Otherwise it defers** whenever the next layer would run exactly the reduction the FFN would have: one full-precision sum over the same TP group object, on a plain partial sum.
  - **Excluded:**
    - attention DP (handled in the next PR);
    - MoE combines that already sum (a2a, FP4 all-gather, DWDP);
    - quantized communication;
    - a replicated TP1 shared expert;
    - LoRA;
    - EP × MoE-TP hybrids;
    - MoE groups that are not the TP group object.
  - **Applies to `ffn_exit` models.** The models that call `should_fuse_mlp_allreduce_with_next_layer` themselves (Step-3.5, Qwen3.5, MiniMax-M3, GLM5-Next, Dots3, Nemotron-H) still defer only when the fused kernel runs. #41198 moves the first five onto `ffn_exit`.
  - When the fused kernel does not take the batch, or a post-residual addition must be added, `prepare_attn` all-reduces the pending sum and then takes the same quant-format residual step as a complete input. That fallback used to apply a plain norm and drop `quant_format` and `post_residual_addition`.

## Accuracy Tests

No numeric change: the next layer runs the same all-reduce over the same group on the same buffer.

- **`UnreducedOutput`:**
  - **`prepare_attn` call-sequence comparison** (all collectives and kernels stubbed): 24,576 cases identical to the parent.
  - **GPU, H200, 4 greedy requests × 32 tokens; text, token logprobs and top-5 logprobs compared; each configuration's audit shows the deferral happening.** Seven configurations are bit-identical: GLM-4.7-Flash TP2, PP2 × TP2 and TP2 + NextN; gpt-oss-120b TP2 + EAGLE3 (aux capture); Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-FP8 TP2; Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B TP2 image requests (deepstack); Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP2.
- **Deferral without the fused kernel:**
  - **Call sequences:** 22,528 of 24,576 cases are identical. The other 2,048 change in exactly one way: a pending sum is all-reduced first and then takes the normal path.
  - **GPU, H200, 15 configurations bit-identical to the parent:** GLM-4.7-Flash TP2 (fusion on, off, ~3000-token prompt, PP2 × TP2, + NextN); DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 (on / off); Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP2 (off); gpt-oss-120b TP2 (off, + EAGLE3 on / off); Ling-3.0-flash TP4 (on / off); Laguna-M.1 TP4 (on / off). In the fusion-off configurations the parent never defers and this PR does.

Under `torch.compile`, building the wrapper is a graph break: with `fullgraph=True`, torch 2.13 raises `Unsupported: object.__new__ user-defined class construction`. Decode compiles without `fullgraph`, so a deferring layer splits the compiled graph there. The `tc_piecewise` prefill backend compiles with `fullgraph` and cannot trace a deferring layer; with the second commit that includes prefill at TP > 1 without the fused kernel. The default `breakable` prefill backend is not traced. The `ffn_exit` fullgraph test is removed.

**Two-batch-overlap entry.**

- **CPU test:** a new test hands the entry an `UnreducedOutput` and checks that the split and the merge see the reduced tensor.
- **GPU, B200, DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 with two-batch overlap:** the previous revision of this stack crashes at the entry with `AttributeError: 'UnreducedOutput' object has no attribute 'shape'` in four configurations: DeepEP normal mode without attention DP, and attention DP2 with EP2, EP1 and DeepEP.
  - With the fix, each run passes the entry and then stops where main stops in the same configuration. Main stops on a flashinfer MLA ragged-prefill shape check, or on a missing global DP buffer length under two-batch overlap.
  - So there is no bit-identity comparison with two-batch overlap on this machine.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Decode latency, H200, GLM-4.7-Flash TP2 with fusion off, `bench_one_batch` input 512 / output 128, decode CUDA graph on. The two trees ran on separate GPUs, then swapped.

| Batch size | Parent median (ms) | This PR median (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6.51 / 6.49 | 6.45 / 6.46 |
| 8 | 8.73 / 8.78 | 8.53 / 8.64 |
| 32 | 12.19 / 11.99 | 12.16 / 11.66 |

The differences are within noise. The all-reduce moves from the end of the FFN to the next layer's `prepare_attn`; the count is the same.

title: [DeepEP v2] Let a model package supply its per-rank prefill dispatch bound
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

`validate_deepep_v2_dispatch_token_budget` compares the whole prefill-buffer ceiling (`--chunked-prefill-size` / `--max-prefill-tokens`) against `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK`. A model package that scatters each prefill chunk over its attention-TP group before the MoE dispatch (sequence-parallel prefill under DP attention) sends only a fraction of that ceiling from any one rank, so the unsharded check rejects configurations that fit. For example, a 32768-token per-DP ceiling scattered over 8 attention-TP ranks dispatches 4096 tokens per rank.

The DeepEP v2 registry already lets an external model package declare its architecture and its MXFP8 precision policy. This extends that same entry point so the package can also declare how its prefill dispatch is sized, without SGLang core learning anything model-specific.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/configs/moe_model_registry.py`: the registry value becomes a frozen `msgspec.Struct` policy holding `silu_mul_keep_fp32` and an optional `prefill_dispatch_tokens` callback. `register_deepep_v2_model` accepts `prefill_dispatch_tokens(cfg, tokens)`, which receives the resolved read-only configuration and the prefill-buffer ceiling and returns the maximum tokens one rank dispatches. Re-registering an architecture with a different policy still raises. `model_deepep_v2_prefill_dispatch_tokens(hf_config, cfg, default_tokens)` applies the primary architecture's callback, or returns the ceiling unchanged when none is registered. The built-in architectures keep the default policy, so their behavior does not change.
- `python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/moe_hook.py`: `required_deepep_v2_prefill_tokens_per_rank` sizes the prefill budget through the registry, and the prefill branch of `validate_deepep_v2_dispatch_token_budget` uses it. Scheduler and buffer settings and the decode-graph budget check are unchanged.
- `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_hpc_ops_runner_guard.py`: the registration test now covers the callback applied on the primary architecture, the unchanged ceiling when the primary architecture is unregistered, and the conflict raised when an architecture is re-registered with the same precision flag but a different callback.

The policy container is a `msgspec.Struct` rather than a dataclass, following `.claude/rules/no-dataclasses.md`.

## Original commits

- `3f86c79b66e`

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: this changes server-argument validation only, not any kernel or forward path.

title: [Perf] Mamba2 selective_state_update up to 2x faster on B200 via 8x1 launch config for dstate 128 (+7.5% Nemotron-3-Super serving)
author: TarzanZhao
body:
## Summary

The Mamba2 decode kernel `selective_state_update` is memory bound: each step it reads and writes every request's fp32 SSM state. For 64 < dstate <= 128 it launches with `BLOCK_SIZE_M=4, num_warps=4`, so each thread handles only 4 elements. That is too few loads in flight to fill HBM, and on B200 the kernel stays near 3.1 TB/s.

This PR changes that one entry to `BLOCK_SIZE_M=8, num_warps=1`, 32 elements per thread. On one B200 the kernel is **1.19x, 1.86x and 2.02x faster at batch 8, 128 and 512** (3.1 -> 6.3 TB/s at batch 512), with bitwise-identical outputs. Nemotron-3-Super on 8x B200 serves **+7.5%** output tokens/s. H200 numbers are in the comment below.

### Speedup Result

**Kernel alone**, one B200, CUDA graph timing with cold L2 (headdim 64, dstate 128, fp32 state, bf16 inputs, 16 heads per GPU as in Nemotron-3-Super TP8):

| batch | baseline, us | this PR, us | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 4.77 | 4.02 | 1.19x |
| 128 | 44.7 | 24.1 | 1.86x |
| 512 | 173.5 | 85.7 | 2.02x |

Other launch configs at the same batches, all bitwise identical to the baseline. Of the 20 configs I tried, `(8, 1)` is the fastest at batch 128 and 512, and 4% behind the fastest, `(8, 4)`, at batch 8.

| (BLOCK_SIZE_M, num_warps) | batch 8, us | batch 128, us | batch 512, us |
|---|---|---|---|
| (4, 4), baseline | 4.77 | 44.7 | 173.5 |
| (4, 1) | 4.26 | 36.6 | 138.1 |
| **(8, 1), this PR** | 4.02 | 24.1 | 85.7 |
| (16, 1) | 4.04 | 24.2 | 86.1 |
| (16, 4) | 3.96 | 25.6 | 94.7 |

**End to end**, 8x B200 (TP8), `sglang.bench_serving`, ShareGPT, 1000 prompts, request rate inf:

| | baseline (`567d5925fe`) | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| output token throughput, mean of 3 | 10,505 tok/s (10,499 / 10,516 / 10,499) | 11,289 tok/s (11,283 / 11,262 / 11,321) | **+7.5%** |
| peak GPU memory per GPU, max of 3 | 164.2 GB | 163.9 GB | |

## Correctness Verification

I ran the baseline and this branch as servers and compared greedy completions for the same requests: the token id and logprob of every generated token. I also ran the kernel alone with both configs from the same inputs and initial state, and compared its output and updated state bit for bit. I set the tolerance before the runs: exact equality, because the baseline server reproduces its outputs bit for bit across restarts. The scripts are not part of this PR, and I can share them.

Every compared value is identical.

| recorded | baseline vs this PR | tolerance |
|---|---|---|
| greedy token ids and logprobs, 64 ShareGPT prompts x 128 tokens, 3 server runs | identical | exact |
| same, 8 prompts of 3.2k to 3.5k tokens x 128 tokens, 3 server runs | identical | exact |
| kernel output and updated state, 5 head counts x 184 batch sizes (920 points) | bitwise identical | exact |

## Checklist

- [x] Format: `ruff format` and `ruff check --select=F401,F821,UP037` (the pre-commit rules) pass on the changed file.
- [ ] Unit tests: no new test. `test/registered/layers/mamba/test_mamba_ssm.py` covers this path and passes, 340 passed on B200.
- [ ] Documentation: none needed. The change is internal to a kernel launcher.
- [x] Accuracy and speed results: above.
- [x] Code style: one-value change inside the existing table, no new comments.

Scope: this affects every model that runs Mamba2 decode through the default Triton `selective_state_update` with 64 < dstate <= 128, on any GPU. I measured only B200. For the same shape, vLLM's tuned configs for H100 and H200 mostly pick 1 or 2 warps rather than 4x4, which points the same way but is not a measurement.

<details>
<summary>Details: hardware, model, full command, traces</summary>

**Hardware.** 8x NVIDIA B200 (183 GB, sm_100), driver 580.126.20, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1, flashinfer 0.6.18, sglang at `567d5925fe`.

**Model.** `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16`, TP8. 88 layers: 40 Mamba2, 40 MoE, 8 attention. Per rank the Mamba2 layers have 16 heads, headdim 64, dstate 128, and an fp32 SSM cache (`mamba_ssm_cache_dtype` in the checkpoint config).

**Kernel measurement.**
- Shapes follow the model: state pool `[pool, H, 64, 128]` fp32 with random `state_batch_indices`; x `[bs, H, 64]` and B/C `[bs, 1, 128]` are strided views of one tensor; dt, A, D and dt_bias are stride-0 broadcasts.
- Timing: max(20, K) calls captured in one CUDA graph, 20 replays timed with CUDA events, median of 5 repeats. Call i reads state slot set (i mod K); the K sets are disjoint and together hold at least 3x the 126.5 MiB L2, so every call reads state from HBM, as in real decode where each layer's state is touched once per step. Without this rotation, batches whose state fits in L2 looked up to 2.6x faster than they are.
- Speed tables: 16 heads, batch 8, 128, 512, 20 launch configs. Bitwise check (Correctness table): heads 8, 16, 32, 64, 128; batch 1 to 64, then every 8 up to 1024.
- The config is switched through a temporary override in the launcher, so both configs run the same compiled kernel code.

**End-to-end measurement.**
- Measured on base `567d5925fe` with only this one-line change applied. The branch is rebased onto `ec070ec8c8`; `mamba_ssm.py` is identical at both, and `test_mamba_ssm.py` passes on the rebased branch.
- Both versions run the same server command, including `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 1024`. That flag is not part of this PR; without it, decode batches above 512 run without CUDA graphs on this workload, which hides kernel differences.
- 3 interleaved runs per version on one node, warm caches, ShareGPT 1000 prompts, seed 42.
- Throughput is measured over the `Benchmark duration` window of `bench_serving`: first request sent to last response, excluding server startup, dataset loading and warmup.

**Server**, both versions:
```
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16 \
  --tp 8 --trust-remote-code --disable-radix-cache \
  --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 50}' \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 1024
```

**Client:**
```
python -m sglang.bench_serving --dataset-name sharegpt --num-prompts 1000 --seed 42 --request-rate inf --flush-cache
```

**Settings tried and rejected.**
- `--mamba-backend flashinfer`: similar end-to-end speed, but greedy outputs are not bitwise identical to the Triton kernel.

**Traces** (torch.profiler, 30 decode steps at batch ~360, ranks 0 and 7; open in https://ui.perfetto.dev):
- baseline: <share link> (local: `commits/c1-flag-cuda-graph-max-bs-decode-1024/trace/decode_graph_rank*.trace.json.gz`)

</details>

title: [Perf] [AMD] attention: Spread uneven Triton decode batches across XCDs
author: siliangchen-amd
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #41151.

HIP hands workgroups to the eight XCDs of an MI300-series GPU round-robin, and the Triton decode stage-1 kernels put the batch on the fastest grid axis, so with an even batch each request's workgroups stay on one XCD or a fixed subset of them. When the batch is uneven, from CUDA-graph padding rows (`seq_len=1`) or a mix of long and short requests, the XCDs that hold the long requests set the kernel time while the others idle.

On ROCm, the Triton backend is the default for Gemma 4, MiniMax-M3, Olmo 3 and EXAONE, and for MLA models whose heads per rank are not 16 or 128, such as Kimi-K2 at TP 8.

## Modifications

- `get_num_kv_splits_triton` also writes a one-element `uneven_batch` flag: 1 when the shortest decode sequence is still shorter than the longest after the existing near-uniform rule.
- On HIP, for an even batch, the stage-1 kernels read the flag and, when it is set, rotate the request index across the grid: by head and split in the per-head kernel, by split only in the grouped (GQA/MLA) kernel, so the head tiles of one request and split still share the KV they read. Balanced batches, odd batches and CUDA run as before.
- `TritonAttnBackend` passes the flag through, with a static buffer for CUDA graphs.

Outputs are bitwise identical with and without the rotation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

End to end on 1x MI325X (TP 1), main at `d8f85223` vs this PR, `sglang.benchmark.serving --dataset-name random-ids --seed 1`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.8` (the 26B-A4B runs also set `--context-length 135168`). Output tok/s, two runs each; "ragged" draws input and output lengths from 5–100% of the stated maximum.

| model | case | main | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gemma-4-31B-it | 5 × (16K in, 1K out), padded into the bs-8 graph | 174.2, 173.4 | 178.7, 178.4 | +3% |
| gemma-4-31B-it | 4 × (16K in, 1K out) | 132.6, 132.1 | 132.4, 131.1 | 0% |
| gemma-4-31B-it | 8 × (16K in, 1K out) | 239.1, 238.8 | 238.7, 238.6 | 0% |
| gemma-4-31B-it | 64 × ragged (16K in, 1K out), conc 16 | 213.1, 213.2 | 223.3, 223.4 | +5% |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | 5 × (32K in, 1K out), padded into the bs-8 graph | 317.6, 309.9 | 322.7, 313.9 | +1% |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | 4 × (32K in, 1K out) | 224.1, 197.0 | 223.4, 194.2 | −1% |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | 8 × (32K in, 1K out) | 480.6, 444.8 | 477.6, 447.5 | 0% |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | 64 × ragged (32K in, 1K out), conc 16 | 370.4, 397.1 | 393.5, 419.0 | +6% |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | 192 × ragged (4K in, 512 out), conc 32 | 1338.1, 1347.3 | 1364.6, 1373.6 | +2% |

With `--context-length 135168 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1` and 32K inputs, gemma-4-31B-it decodes five requests padded into the bs-8 graph at 179 tok/s instead of 145 (three runs; +11–18% output tok/s over the whole run), and 64 ragged 32K requests at conc 16 gain 4.5%.

title: [AMD][DI][CI] Give the dsv4pro-fp4 MTP decode more memory headroom
author: Lzy17
body:
dsv4pro-fp4-1k1k-1p1d-mtp clears GSM8K and then dies in the concurrency sweep at 256: seven of the eight decode ranks abort on the same RCCL kernel with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`.

The 112 GB the abort reports free is device memory, not the resource that ran out. Decode finishes init with 13.85 GB of headroom against the ~25 GB its passing siblings keep, and the draft model needs streams and queues out of what is left. This was the only MTP recipe still running decode at 0.90.

0.85 returns about 14 GB on decode only. Prefill and every other emitted value are unchanged.

Verified on ROCm 10: GSM8K 0.952, all seven sweep points including 256. `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=8` was tried first and ruled out -- the hung dispatch queue ids moved from 0/1 to 0/1/8, so it took effect, and the abort was unchanged.

title: [Refactor] Restore logical kernel groups and test organization
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Recent additions have drifted from the logical operator groups in the [kernels RFC](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29630): MiniCPM is a top-level group, Qwen PLE combines unrelated operators, attention modules own standalone GEMM/MoE operations, and quantization modules own matmul implementations. The corresponding tests also mix numerical kernels, runtime integration, and server evaluation.

This restores those boundaries, updates every in-tree caller, and documents the placement rules for future changes. The diff includes 178 byte-identical tuning-file moves.

## Modifications

- Group MiniCPM under attention; split Qwen PLE into embeddings, elementwise gates, and convolution-state operations. Rehome standalone DSV4 GEMM/MoE/normalization/quantization, Gemma routing, attention Top-K, Inkling projection/row operations, and hyperconnection matmul into their owning groups. Keep fused attention operations with attention.
- Separate FP8/INT8 GEMM from quantization and move its tuning files together, preserving relative config lookup. Update runtime, benchmark, test, and lazy registry references.
- Put active K3 communication adapters under `srt/layers/communication`. Remove the default-off K3 GEMM+all-reduce experiment, including its two `o_proj` wrapping call sites, environment flag, wrapper, CUDA source, and dedicated test. Retain the active all-reduce, sequence-parallel, and GEMM+all-gather paths.
- Classify numerical tests by operator, runtime tests under `unit`, and model/server quantization tests under `e2e/quantization`. Split mixed K3/Gemma/FP8 tests and move standalone debug programs and benchmarks out of production modules. Preserve existing CI lanes and total estimated time per lane when splitting registrations.
- Complete lazy operator metadata and add CPU checks for group placement, target-module existence, public-entry registration, and architecture boundaries. Preserve existing device policies on relocated entries; explicit Torch selection for BF16/FP32 GEMM uses the Torch implementation while the direct legacy entry retains its vendor dispatch.
- Add `.claude/skills/kernel-organization/SKILL.md`, link it from the kernel/test authoring skills, and update the kernels README and authoring examples.

The operator import paths and affected registry IDs intentionally follow their new groups; no compatibility forwarding modules are added. Semantic changes are separate from the four relocation commits and the follow-up mechanical import correction.

## Accuracy Tests

- Full-range pre-commit, `git diff --check`, CI registration checks, and new skill validation pass.
- CPU namespace/dispatch suites: **105 passed, 3 failed**. All three failures also reproduce on the unchanged base (**94 passed, 3 failed**): the AMX lazy-import subprocess needs Triton, and two compile-hook tests need a newer Transformers installation. The additional checks pass.
- Actual lazy target loading and CPU numerical smoke checks pass for Torch BF16/FP32 linear and image patchification.
- All 178 tuning files match their original Git blobs. CI registrations change from 2,601 to 2,615 due to file splits; summed estimates are unchanged for each original stage/runner/registration configuration.
- Local GPU tests were unavailable (H200 SSH authentication failed; no Radix credentials). On head `d60951402f`, [CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36208701555) has passed all 11 CPU partitions and all six CUDA JIT jobs: H100 partitions 0/1, the H100 benchmark, 5090, 4x B200, and 8x H200. Model integration jobs are still running.
- CI exposed one stale sibling import in the relocated K3 collective module. The follow-up points it to `srt.layers.communication`; all four previously failing CPU test files now pass. [B300 Kimi-K3 integration](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36208701476/job/108310796644) also passed: MMMU-Pro 0.825 and the existing single-request speed check. No test thresholds or skips were changed.
- [NPU 16-card CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36208701518/job/108311601503) also passed, including both HiCache cases that previously encountered a host-memory allocation error.

Current CI findings on `d60951402f`:

- H200 GLM-5.3-Flash passed (high-throughput GSM8K 0.942 after the built-in retry; low-latency 0.938). B200 Extra also passed all six files, including DSV4 Flash FP4 MegaMoE and Kimi Linear DCP.
- Xeon SPR fails an unchanged MiniMax-H3 mock target. The [exact main base fails identically](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36205671705/job/108301636277).
- NPU diffusion Qwen Image and MiniMax H3 consistency checks match [main's failures and exact metrics](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36194829294/job/108268654102).
- [H100 diffusion rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36208701555/job/108319525380) passed without source or threshold changes. LTX-2.5 denoise fell from 373.52 ms to 262.33 ms on its built-in retry (314.15 ms limit), consistent with main timing variation. All 9 single-5090 and 6 dual-H100 Base-B partitions now pass. Other queued/running jobs are still being checked; CI is not fully green.

CPU suite command:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python3.11 -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/kernels/test_kernels_namespace.py \
  test/registered/unit/kernels/test_fused_op.py \
  test/registered/unit/kernels/test_fused_op_dispatch.py
```

### Mechanical move — reproducible

The [proof scripts, self-contained engine, and chain report](https://gist.github.com/BBuf/16ab3a02bee0d0e733dcb9489db82e80) reproduce all **five mechanical commits byte-for-byte** (four relocations and the follow-up K3 sibling import correction). The three non-mechanical commits cover removal, metadata/docs, and follow-up guards; their `HUMAN_REVIEW` classification does not assert runtime equivalence.

From a checkout of this PR, with Git, Python, `pre-commit`, and `ruff` available:

```bash
gh gist clone 16ab3a02bee0d0e733dcb9489db82e80 ../kernel-layout-proof
python3 .claude/skills/mechanical-refactor-verify/scripts/mechanical_refactor_reproduction_cli.py \
  --base c842d32b0ab45753178c5f6420662d7812766aca \
  --branch HEAD \
  --proof ../kernel-layout-proof
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run; no performance improvement is claimed. Relocated computation and tuning data are preserved, while removal of the opt-in GEMM+all-reduce experiment is an intentional behavior change.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add CPU layout/metadata checks and preserve existing numerical coverage and CI registration budgets.
- [x] Update documentation and authoring skills.
- [ ] Provide GPU accuracy and speed benchmark results (environment unavailable; see above).
- [x] Follow SGLang code style guidance.

title: [Perf] Optimize DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Hopper paths and Blackwell prefill selection
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Hopper spends substantial decode time in group32 dense GEMMs, capacity-sized indexer work, mHC statistics, and padded Marlin MoE projections. This PR tunes those paths. On Blackwell, flattened prefill selection also launches separate mask, sort, slot-map and raw-offset operations; the added integer kernel combines them.

## Changes

- Tune Hopper group32 GEMMs and reuse exact BF16 expansions of eligible FP8 weights, preserving activation quantization boundaries and the original fallbacks.
- Use live paged indexer lengths and variable-length top-k; fuse masking, sorting and slot mapping.
- Enable guarded Hopper mHC combine/norm and compensated BF16 projection paths, with decode statistics overlap.
- Preserve intermediate activation rounding in fused clipped SwiGLU; defer MXFP4 padding until Marlin repacking.
- On SM100-family CUDA GPUs, fuse flattened prefill selection into one integer kernel. Keep the changing visible slot count as a non-specialized runtime argument, so new context lengths do not create new JIT variants. Hopper retains its existing Torch selection path.

## Pinned validation

Checkpoint `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`; PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 and sgl-kernel 0.4.8; sgl-bench commit `a9da34ad1f997ca05878d858d3d01970e4a49af9`; sgl-eval 0.1.2. Both machines were allocated exclusively for these comparisons. All paired datasets, request counts, input/output lengths and API errors were validated from the request records. Timings exclude profiling and correctness instrumentation.

### H200: upstream main versus original PR runtime

8×H200, TP8/EP1, Marlin MoE, static memory fraction 0.8, bounded SWA replay, decode graph maximum batch64, Engram host table disabled. Main `ef867fa40d` versus PR `22e352d873`; `94d21e3162` differs from the measured PR only by a test mock accessor. Random8192 input /1024 output, seed42, temperature0, thinking disabled,64 warmup requests and cache flush. Request counts30/40/80/80/160/320 at concurrency1/4/8/16/32/64; three alternating paired sweeps. Ratios below are medians of the three paired ratios.

|Concurrency|User-speed ratio|Output-throughput/GPU ratio|TTFT speedup|
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|1|2.2067×|2.1515×|1.3398×|
|4|2.4842×|2.3498×|1.5062×|
|8|2.3599×|2.2322×|1.5551×|
|16|2.1674×|2.0574×|1.5555×|
|32|2.2540×|2.1077×|1.5658×|
|64|2.3975×|2.1929×|1.5583×|

The final Blackwell addition was checked separately against the original PR on the same H200 node: one complete paired six-point sweep and full GSM8K/AIME24 at4096/32768 output caps. User-speed ratios are0.9990–1.0029 and output-throughput/GPU ratios0.9989–1.0013. This additional check is one paired sweep, not the three-sweep main comparison above. Full GSM8K is1277/1319 on both arms; AIME24 is456/480→457/480, with23 truncations each. Hopper continues to use its Torch fallback; equal aggregate scores do not imply identical generations.

### GB300: added flattened prefill fusion versus ordinary PR

4×NVIDIA GB300/SM103, ARM64, TP4/EP1, flashinfer_mxfp4 MoE and flashinfer_cutedsl FP8 GEMM. Ordinary PR `94d21e3162` versus candidate `179b1ab2d3` (identical tested file hashes). Both arms use16384 for chunked-prefill-size and max-prefill-tokens. Three rotated paired sweeps; seed42, temperature0, thinking disabled,16 warmups and cache flush. Each shape uses64 requests at concurrency1 and128 at concurrency16.

|Input tokens|Output tokens|Concurrency|Median TTFT speedup|Individual paired ratios|
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
|8192|32|1|1.0170×|1.0227×, 1.0170×, 0.9902×|
|8192|32|16|1.0277×|1.0266×, 1.0485×, 1.0277×|
|32768|32|1|1.0209×|1.0209×, 1.0282×, 0.9794×|
|32768|32|16|1.0200×|1.0200×, 1.0239×, 1.0168×|

Both concurrency16 shapes improve in all three pairs. Each concurrency1 shape has one regressing pair, so this is a small prefill improvement, not a claim of universal or statistically proven acceleration. In the8192-input/1024-output suite, median output-throughput/GPU ratios are only1.0009–1.0081. The standalone selection helper improves5.45–14.33×; that microbenchmark is not an end-to-end speedup.

### Accuracy

Full GSM8K1319 problems, thinking disabled; full AIME24 is30 problems×16 repeats, thinking enabled. Seed42, temperature0,32 evaluation threads, no API errors. Repeats are not480 independent questions. Results are paired by question ID, problem text and expected answer.

|Machine|Dataset/output cap|Upstream main|Ordinary PR|Blackwell candidate|
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
|H200|GSM8K/2048|1278/1319|1278/1319|Not rerun at this cap|
|H200|AIME24/16384|440/480|437/480|Not rerun at this cap|
|H200|GSM8K/4096|1276/1319|1274/1319|See fresh paired run below|
|H200|AIME24/32768|451/480|454/480|See fresh paired run below|
|H200, fresh paired run|GSM8K/4096|Not rerun|1277/1319|1277/1319|
|H200, fresh paired run|AIME24/32768|Not rerun|456/480|457/480|
|GB300|GSM8K/2048|1277/1319|1278/1319|1279/1319|
|GB300|AIME24/16384|438/480|437/480|434/480|
|GB300, fresh paired run|GSM8K/4096|Not rerun|1279/1319|1277/1319|
|GB300, fresh paired run|AIME24/32768|Not rerun|456/480|453/480|

GB300 accuracy uses2048 prefill budgets, because upstream main's FlashMLA scheduling metadata exceeds its48KB shared-memory implementation limit on a GSM8K batch at the default16K budget. Performance comparisons use the same16K budget on every arm and are kept separate. AIME24 candidate versus ordinary PR changes by−0.625 percentage points; truncations40→42,14 correct→wrong and11 wrong→correct. There is also one additional wrong nontruncated answer. The higher-cap paired run still has AIME24 −0.625 percentage points (456→453 correct; truncations22→24;7 correct→wrong,4 reverse), and GSM8K −0.1516 percentage points (1279→1277; neither arm truncated). These scores do not prove identical generation or statistical accuracy equivalence.

### Correctness coverage

- Existing H200 focused regression:582 passed,60 skipped,16 subtests passed on the rebased runtime.
- New integer selection/CUDA Graph/cache-reuse cases:34 passed on real GB300 SM100 dispatch, and34 passed on H200 with the SM100 entry mocked to exercise the integer helper.
- Full GB300 indexer test file:133 passed,2 skipped.
- Real-model8K/32K prefill audit at concurrency1/16:1908 calls across four ranks, with both page and raw indices exactly equal to the original Torch operations. Rows1–16384, visible slots1–48900. This is integer-mapping evidence, not a substitute for generation-quality evaluation.
- A second actual-model audit dispatches fusion before any reference GPU work:1908 calls,477 per rank, with exact page/raw index agreement. Padding is separately covered by the unit tests.
- Actual model GPU traces contain40 `_finish_flat_indexer_topk_kernel` events per rank; all four original trace files are retained with source hashes.
- Pinned pre-commit and diff whitespace checks passed. CI is not fully green: the existing AMD raw-draft-metadata test still needs alignment with main's deferred metadata API; no ROCm validation is claimed.

## Memory and weight updates

The Hopper derived caches trade GPU memory for throughput. In the original weight-load measurement, memory increased72.71→75.43GB/GPU and max_total_num_tokens fell16,012,800→14,223,104 at the same static memory fraction. These are the original configuration's measurements, not newly measured final-commit memory numbers.

Online weight updates require disabling both derived caches with `SGLANG_OPT_HOPPER_BLOCK_FP8_BF16=0` and `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=0`; otherwise updates fail before writing weights. Other TP/EP layouts are not covered by the reported serving comparisons.

title: [Refactor] Choose prepare_attn / prepare_mlp steps and fused kernels at construction
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41257
* #41256
* #41255
* #41254
* #41253
* __->__ #41252

## Motivation

`prepare_mlp` went through `CommunicateWithAllReduceAndLayerNormFn.get_fn`, whose gather re-derived on every call facts fixed when the communicator is built: whether the residual must be gathered, whether attention DP is on, and which of the two DP orders applies. Whether a fused kernel may run was checked per call too.

Other code recognized these functions by identity:
- the CuteDSL communicator overrode both prepare methods and recognized the base gather by function identity;
- the MHC communicator mapped `get_fn`'s functions to its own by identity;
- Eagle3 aux capture predicted the post-attention kernel from the same identity.

## Modifications

- **`mlp_input_kind()` is the one table for this boundary.** From the layer's layouts it gives `NORM`, `GATHER`, `GATHER_MOE_CP`, `SCATTER` or `ATTN_TP_ALL_REDUCE`. `LayerCommunicator._select_mlp_input` builds that kind's steps once and `prepare_mlp` runs them. The gather runs `_mlp_input_without_dp`, `_mlp_input_dp_replicate` or `_mlp_input_dp_partial`, picked by `_mlp_input_order` with the facts bound, then the MoE-CP gather for `GATHER_MOE_CP`. `CommunicateWithAllReduceAndLayerNormFn` and its `get_fn` are removed.
- **MHC and DSA-CP override `_select_mlp_input`.** MHC takes its own function for the same kind, with its MHC state bound; its `prepare_mlp` override is gone. DSA-CP keeps its own table.
- **Fused kernels are entries chosen at construction and tried in order.** Each entry checks only whether its kernel takes this batch.
  - `prepare_mlp` gets the aiter / flashinfer entry when the norm has the fused method.
  - `prepare_attn` gets the same, with the aiter quant variant chosen once, and hands what the previous layer left to these entries before the LayerNorm SP, input-scattered and empty-batch checks. None of those sees a pending output: LayerNorm SP runs only `Qwen3ForCausalLM`, which never defers; no layer defers in an input-scattered forward; and both kernels refuse an empty batch.
- **`CuteDSLFusionLayerCommunicator` no longer overrides `prepare_attn` / `prepare_mlp`.** Its finalize handoff and its all-reduce + RMSNorm become the first entries. The function-identity and residual-mode checks in its eligibility become the conditions under which each entry is chosen.
- **Aux capture** reads the construction-time capability (`_mlp_input_may_fuse`) instead of the function identity.
- **Norms are construction inputs.**
  - GigaChat3.5 used to swap both norms of the communicator `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer` had built, which would leave entries chosen for the old norms.
  - `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer` now builds its communicator in `_build_layer_communicator`, and GigaChat3.5 builds one with its own norms.

## Accuracy Tests

No behavior change is intended. It was checked as follows:
- **Call sequences.** `prepare_mlp` and `prepare_attn` were run with every collective, kernel, buffer and platform flag stubbed and recorded; each tree selects through its own code. 53,248 `prepare_mlp` cases and 50,688 `prepare_attn` cases cover:
  - the base and CuteDSL communicators;
  - complete and pending inputs;
  - the finalize handoff.

  Everything matches the parent except:
  - kernel-availability queries are no longer made where no entry exists or before an empty-batch check (2,544 `prepare_mlp` and 1,560 `prepare_attn` cases);
  - the error text for a pending output without a residual (12,800 cases where both trees raise).
- **Unit tests.** 195 files under `unit/models`, `unit/layers` and `unit/batch_overlap` were run one process per file on parent and change; no file fails only on the change. New tests cover:
  - the kind of each layout pair, the steps each kind takes, and the order chosen per configuration;
  - MHC taking its own function for a kind;
  - the aux capability;
  - the CuteDSL entries preceding the base one.
- **GPU (B200).** 4 greedy requests × 32 tokens, decode CUDA graph on; text, token logprobs and top-5 logprobs are bit-identical to the parent in:
  - Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP2 with fusion on and off, GLM-4.7-Flash TP2, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B TP2;
  - DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 × DP2 (replicate order) and TP4 × DP2 (partial order), Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP4 × DP2 × EP2.
- **Rebase onto main** (after #36389, LoRA under DP attention, which publishes the LoRA token layout at the start of `prepare_attn` and `prepare_mlp`):
  - Both methods keep that call ahead of their steps. MHC's `prepare_mlp` override, removed here, published it too; the base `prepare_mlp` now does so for MHC.
  - `test_triton_dp_attention_unit.py` builds its communicator with the construction-time MLP input.
  - The 121 related unit files pass at this commit except three that fail on main as well. The GPU results above were measured before the rebase; after the rebase the six-PR stack is bit-identical to main on B200 in Qwen3-0.6B TP4 × DP2, TP4 × DP4 and TP2 × DP2 and DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 × DP2, TP4 × DP2 and TP4 × DP4 × EP4.
- **Not run on GPU:** CuteDSL, which only enables on Blackwell MNNVL; it is covered by unit tests and the call-sequence comparison.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel or collective changes. Per-call re-derivation of fixed facts moves to construction.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: [Refactor] Pick the two-batch-overlap split's layout moves once and remove execute
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41257
* __->__ #41256
* #41255
* #41254
* #41253
* #41252

## Motivation

The two-batch-overlap split moved its input to the splitter's attention-TP-full layout, then moved each microbatch on to the first layer's input layout. Both moves went through `CommunicateSummableTensorPairFn.execute`, which looks the move up in the table on every call. The split was `execute`'s only caller.

## Modifications

- **The split looks up both moves once**, from the same modes and context, and calls them with the same arguments. The second move still runs per microbatch, with that microbatch's `forward_batch`.
- **`CommunicateSummableTensorPairFn.execute` is removed.**

## Accuracy Tests

No behavior change is intended.
- **Call sequences, parent vs change: identical** across the `prepare_mlp`, `prepare_attn`, layout-move and FFN-exit comparisons. The related unit files pass on both trees, including `unit/batch_overlap`.
- **GPU (B200):** Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP4 × DP4 attention, DeepEP normal mode, two-batch overlap; 4 greedy requests × 32 tokens, decode CUDA graph on. Measured on this commit as it sits in this stack:
  - requests sent one at a time: bit-identical to the parent;
  - requests sent in one batch: bit-identical to the parent in a clean run. One earlier run of the parent tree hit a DeepEP assertion (`is_token_in_rank.size(0) == x.size(0)`); it did not reproduce, and the stack's base commit passed the same batched run.
- **Rebase:** the patch is unchanged by the rebase onto main after #36389 (same patch-id); the 121 related unit files pass at this commit except three that fail on main as well. The GPU results above were measured before the rebase.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel or collective changes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [AMD] Let the GLM DSA NextN draft declare its own shared-expert fusion architecture
author: xiaofei-zheng
body:
## Motivation

`ModelConfig` rewrites a GLM-5 draft's architecture to `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLMNextN`. The fusion gate compares that name with `fused_shared_experts_architecture`, which the class inherited as `"DeepseekV3ForCausalLMNextN"`, so the draft was rejected even though it has the same 256 routed + 1 shared expert layout as the target model.

## Modifications

Declare `fused_shared_experts_architecture = "GlmMoeDsaForCausalLMNextN"` on the draft class.

Keep fusion disabled whenever `SGLANG_GLM_NEXTN_MOE_PTPC=1` casts the routed experts to per-channel FP8: the cast skips the shared expert, so its weight (BF16 or quantized) would land in the FP8 slot without a matching scale. On GLM-5.2-MXFP4's real layer-78 shared expert that zeroes 7-8% of the weights. GLM-5.3 checkpoints do not exclude MTP routed experts, so PTPC never applies there and the draft fuses.

Tests cover the architecture name, the loader-style gate call, the PTPC guard with the shared expert excluded or quantized, and both routed/shared checkpoint names.

## Accuracy Tests

Initial GLM-5.3 MXFP4 validation of the architecture override loaded the draft weights and measured MTP accept length 3.56 versus 3.58 on base, with GSM8K unchanged. The final PTPC guard intentionally leaves the unsupported BF16-shared configuration unfused; a real checkpoint load was not rerun after adding that guard.

Local verification:

```bash
python3 -m pytest -n 4 \
  test/registered/unit/models/test_glm_nextn_moe_ptpc.py

python3 -m pytest -n 4 \
  test/registered/unit/models/test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py

pre-commit run --files \
  python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe.py \
  test/registered/unit/models/test_glm_nextn_moe_ptpc.py \
  test/registered/unit/models/test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py
```

Result: 58 tests passed. Two broader-suite failures reproduce on current `main`: the ROCm EP gate expectation and a local Transformers/Pixtral import mismatch.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not isolated. Supported drafts now use the same fused shared-expert path as the target model; the PTPC + BF16-shared case remains unfused for correctness.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add gate and PTPC regression tests.
- [x] Document the unsupported PTPC interaction in code.
- [x] Report validation and limitations.

title: [AMD][ROCm] Keep cos_sin_cache fp32 on HIP for fused QSA indexer kernel
author: ChangLiu0709
body:
## Motivation

On HIP (ROCm), the `cos_sin_cache` is converted from fp32 to bf16 through three independent code paths, silently disabling the fused QSA indexer JIT kernel (`qsa_indexer.cuh`) which requires `const float*` inputs. This causes a fallback to **42 eager PyTorch kernels per QSA layer** (190µs each), wasting ~2.28ms per decode step (~20% of the decode cycle) on hybrid GDN+QSA models like Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.

On CUDA, `cos_sin_cache` is already kept as fp32 via the init guard (`_is_cuda`). This PR extends the same fp32 behavior to HIP.

## Root Cause

Three code paths convert `cos_sin_cache` dtype on HIP:

| Path | File | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Init guard | `base.py:114` | `cache.to(dtype)` converts fp32→bf16 at creation |
| `_match_cos_sin_cache_dtype` | `base.py:156`, `mrope.py:173` | Converts to `query.dtype` (bf16) on first forward |
| `fallback_rotary_embedding` | `base.py:439` | Converts to `query.dtype` before fallback kernel |

The `_use_fused_prep()` check in `qsa_indexer.py` correctly requires `cos_sin_cache.dtype == torch.float32`, which always fails on HIP after any of these conversions.

## Modifications

- Add `_is_hip` to the fp32 init guard in `base.py` (matching CUDA behavior)
- Split `_match_cos_sin_cache_dtype` into device-match (always) and dtype-match (non-HIP only) in both `base.py` and `mrope.py`
- Keep fp32 in `fallback_rotary_embedding` path on HIP

All changes are **scoped to HIP only** — CUDA behavior is 100% unchanged.

## Why this is safe

`cos_sin_cache` is a read-only lookup table. Both the QSA fused JIT kernel (`qsa_indexer.cuh`) and `apply_rope_with_cos_sin_cache_inplace` document it as fp32. Downstream consumers (e.g., `cos_sin_cache[positions]` → mul with bf16 q/k) handle fp32→bf16 auto-casting implicitly on tiny indexed tensors. Memory overhead is negligible (~64MB at 256K context = 0.01% of GPU memory).

## Benchmarking

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next MXFP4, MI355X, TP=1, AgentX 3600s, CONC=8:

| Metric | Before (bf16 cache) | After (fp32 cache) | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Interactivity p50 | 91.2 tok/s | **117.1 tok/s** | **+28%** |
| Interactivity p90 | 45.3 tok/s | **79.4 tok/s** | **+75%** |
| ITL p50 | 11.0 ms | **8.5 ms** | **-23%** |
| TPOT mean | 13.7 ms | **10.4 ms** | **-24%** |
| TTFT p50 | 1,020 ms | **739 ms** | **-28%** |
| Throughput/GPU | 31,611 tok/s | **34,291 tok/s** | **+8.5%** |

0 request errors across 1,286 requests.

- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [Fix] compressed-tensors: Serve split-expert MXFP4 MoE via FP4 Marlin
author: jlqibm
body:
## Motivation

Stacks on #41288  (`fix/compressed-tensors-mxfp4-marlin`), which fixed MXFP4 **dense
linear**. This fixes MXFP4 **MoE**.

A compressed-tensors `mxfp4-pack-quantized` MoE checkpoint whose experts are
stored **split per expert** (`experts.{e}.{gate,up,down}_proj.*`, as emitted by
llmcompressor) cannot load today. The A/B control, same node and same venv:

- On #41288 : `KeyError: 'model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.experts.w2_weight_packed'`
  at `granitemoe.py:93`.
- On this PR: loads, 0 tensors dropped, coherent output.

The cause is a layout mismatch, not a missing kernel. `Mxfp4MoEMethod` and
`Mxfp4MarlinMoEMethod` handle the **fused** GPT-OSS layout and register
`w13/w2_weight`; a split-expert checkpoint's per-expert tensors have no
destination there.

## Modifications

Add `CompressedTensorsW4A16Mxfp4MoE`, a weight-only MXFP4 MoE scheme registering
the `_packed` parameter names and routing to the FP4 Marlin MoE runner. It serves
both `mxfp4a16` and `mxfp4` w4a4; the latter's activation quantization is
dropped, since the Marlin MoE kernel is weight-only. A w4a4 checkpoint still
ships input global scales and the split-expert loader raises `KeyError` on any
tensor with no registered destination, so they are registered and only then
dropped in `process_weights_after_loading`.

Unlike NVFP4 there is no `weight_global_scale`, so the compressed-tensors
reciprocal convention (CT stores `1/scale` where Marlin wants `scale`) does not
arise here.

`check_moe_marlin_supports_layer` is deliberately not called: it tests
`group_size` against the GPTQ/AWQ set and reports on int4 zero-point parameters
this layout does not have. The shape constraints it would have covered
(`hidden_size % 128 == 0`, `intermediate_size_per_partition % 64 == 0`) are
validated explicitly instead.

### How the two layouts are told apart

They cannot be told apart from the config. GraniteMoe and Kimi-K3 ship
indistinguishable `mxfp4-pack-quantized` configs — same `quant_method`, same
`format`, `config_groups` targeting `["Linear"]` in both, both using
`make_expert_params_mapping`. The real difference lives in the model loader:
Kimi-K3 renames `weight_packed`→`weight` and substitutes `Mxfp4Config` before
building its experts.

So the selection is an explicit opt-out rather than config sniffing: `FusedMoE`
gains a `serves_fused_mxfp4: bool = True` constructor parameter, and
`granitemoe.py` passes `False`. It must be a constructor parameter, not a
post-construction attribute, because `get_quant_method` runs inside
`FusedMoE.__init__`.

**Every existing fused MXFP4 MoE keeps the default and is unaffected.** That is
asserted in both directions by a new test, since a silent kernel change on the
GPT-OSS path would be the worst failure mode here.

## Accuracy Tests

Granite MoE (`GraniteMoeForCausalLM`), H100 80GB, all coherent text:

| model | TP | mxfp4 | mxfp4a16 | nvfp4 | nvfp4a16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20b  | 1 | OK | OK | OK | OK |
| 20b  | 2 | OK | OK | OK | — |
| 20b  | 4 | OK | OK | OK | — |
| 120b | 4 | OK | OK | — | — |

13 `[OK]`, rc=0, 0 tensors dropped. 120b is independently valuable: 128 experts
vs 56, hidden 3072 vs 2048.

18 CPU scheme-selection tests + 8 subtests, covering the MXFP4/NVFP4 predicate
boundary (both are FP4 group quant; only `group_size` and `strategy` separate
them, so a widened predicate would silently steal the other's checkpoints), the
registered-parameter contract against the checkpoint's names/shapes/dtypes, and
the fused-bypass gate in both directions.

Dense MXFP4 output is byte-identical to PR 2's, confirming the MoE scheme does
not perturb the dense path.

The fused GPT-OSS MXFP4 MoE path is covered by the CPU gate test rather than
end-to-end: GPT-OSS uses native `Mxfp4Config`, so it never enters
`CompressedTensorsConfig.get_quant_method`, and no compressed-tensors fused MXFP4
MoE checkpoint was available to test against. The gate test asserts the dispatch
branch directly, which is a stronger check than inferring it from generated text.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No benchmark run. Weight-only via the existing FP4 Marlin MoE runner — no new
kernel, and activations stay bf16. `get_min_capability()` is 80 and the routing
is capability-independent, so Blackwell takes the same MoE path as Hopper. The one
asymmetry: an **NVFP4** w4a4 MoE checkpoint on SM100 still keeps the native
`CompressedTensorsW4A4Nvfp4MoE` scheme (capability 100); the weight-only fallback
must not lower that gate, which is why they are separate classes and is asserted
by `test_nvfp4_w4a4_keeps_native_scheme_on_blackwell`.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dsv41: Use the fused low-ratio compressor on Hopper
author: ischencheng
body:
## Motivation

Hopper still runs the split DSv4.1 low-ratio compressor: two projection GEMMs, then pooling, RMSNorm, the index-K store and the FlashMLA cache store as separate launches. Hopper uses the V4 cache layout, which the fused c1/c2 and index-K kernels already write on SM100 and gfx950, and those kernels build and pass on SM90.

## Modifications

- `fused_low_ratio_compress_supported()` also returns True on SM90, so Hopper loads the packed `wkv_gate` weight and takes the same fused decode/verify path as SM100 (like #41308 did for gfx950).
- Run `test_dsv41_fused_compress.py` on the H100 runner and drop its three HIP-only skips. All four cases pass on H100.
- Since #41660 the same gate also sends eager extend through `c2_prefill_norm_rope_store`, so `test_c2_prefill_ring.py` now runs on SM90 and on the H100 runner too. It passes on H100.

## Accuracy Tests

As on SM100, the fused path is not bit-identical to the split path. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8xH200, TP8/EP8, no speculative decoding, each arm started twice:

| | GSM8K, 200 questions, 5-shot | greedy outputs identical to baseline (32 LongBench prompts x 512 tokens) |
|---|---|---|
| main | 179, 177 | 32/32 between the two runs |
| this PR | 175, 177 | 29/32 |

McNemar p >= 0.29 for every pair. Mean prefill/decode k3 on the sampled tokens: 0.00584 vs 0.00592.

With DSpark (`--speculative-dspark-block-size 5`), target verify takes the fused path with `draft_len=6` on every rank. Full GSM8K test split (1314 questions after the 5 shots), each arm started twice:

| | correct / 1314 | tokens per verify |
|---|---|---|
| main | 1172, 1170 | 3.45, 3.45 |
| this PR | 1181, 1185 | 3.44, 3.44 |

McNemar p is between 0.10 and 0.34 for every main/PR pair.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

One compressor layer on H100, including the projection GEMMs, CUDA graph, cold L2 (16 rotated weight sets, 160 MiB):

| | bs 1 | bs 64 |
|---|---|---|
| ratio 2, main -> this PR | 35.0 -> 14.3 us | 39.1 -> 20.0 us |
| ratio 1, main -> this PR | 27.4 -> 14.1 us | 30.6 -> 17.7 us |

Only the four kv_source layers (three ratio 2, one ratio 1) run a compressor, so that is about 75 us per decode step. End to end it is small but visible; median ITL from `bench_serving` (random ids, 1024 in / 512 out) on the 8xH200 setup above:

| concurrency | main (2 runs), ms | this PR (2 runs), ms |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 12.40 / 12.26 | 12.19 / 12.19 |
| 8 | 17.26 / 17.27 | 17.19 / 17.19 |
| 32 | 20.47 / 20.47 | 20.34 / 20.35 |

The per-layer table and both tests are from main at 4ae54e9 on 1x H100. The accuracy and ITL tables are from 4dfc0ac. On a34cba3 (after #41660) I reran the full model: GSM8K is 1178 vs 1182 / 1314 without speculative decoding, and decode and eager extend take the fused kernels on all 8 ranks. I have not rerun the full model on anything newer.
