title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] quantization: Add tuned W8A8 block-FP8 GEMM configs for H20
author: nankingjing
body:
## Motivation

`python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/configs` already treats H20 as a supported device
(26 config files for `[128,128]` blocks and channelwise FP8), but the block-`[32,32]` W8A8 path
has only the ten `NVIDIA_H200` entries for these shapes. On H20, `get_w8a8_block_fp8_configs` therefore misses
for every shape and each call falls back to the default tile config:

```python
config = {
    "BLOCK_SIZE_M": 64, "BLOCK_SIZE_N": block_size[0], "BLOCK_SIZE_K": block_size[1],
    "GROUP_SIZE_M": 32, "num_warps": 4, "num_stages": 3,
}
```

With `BLOCK_SIZE_K == block_k == 32` the K loop is fully serial, and at the small M this kernel
actually sees (decode M≈6, speculative-verify M=384, prefill M≤8192) the grid has too few CTAs to
fill the machine. The fallback is not silent — it logs a warning on every miss:

```
Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config. Performance might be sub-optimal!
```

On our 8×H20 deployment that warning fired 80 times per server start before this change.

## Modifications

Adds ten new config files, one per (N, K) shape, each covering 27 M tiers (`M = 1 … 8192`):

```
configs/N={512,576,1280,1536,1792,4096,5120,25600},K={288,1024,1280,5120,6144,15360},
device_name=NVIDIA_H20,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[32, 32].json
```

The ten tables are purely additive: deleting them restores the previous behaviour. One existing
file is touched — `kernels/ops/gemm/fp8_kernel.py` — so that enabling these tables cannot break
deterministic inference (see *Deterministic inference* below). Schema is identical to the existing
`NVIDIA_H200` files for the same shapes, including the use of `SWAP_AB` / `SPLIT_K` where they win.

Produced with the in-tree tuner:

```bash
python -m benchmark.kernels.quantization.tuning_block_wise_kernel \
    --block-n 32 --block-k 32 --input-type fp8 \
    --save-path python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/configs
```

### When is this table read?

On SM90, block-`[32,32]` W8A8 GEMMs take the native DeepGEMM path by default since
#42604 (merged 2026-10-10, after this PR was opened):

- `dispatch_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` (`srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`) returns
  `deepgemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback` when `weight_block_size == [32, 32]`,
  `SGLANG_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM` is on (the default), and the backend is `auto` or `deep_gemm`.
- `_deepgemm_block_fp8_supported` accepts any `[32, 32]` shape with `n % 8 == 0 and k % 32 == 0`
  on SM90. All ten shapes here satisfy that.

So the tables are read when the **Triton block-FP8 backend** is in use: with
`--fp8-gemm-backend=triton`, with `SGLANG_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=0`, when DeepGEMM is unavailable
for the build, or when its runtime fallback triggers. The Triton backend is the default on
non-SM90 hardware and on any SM90 build without DeepGEMM.

This matters for reading the numbers below: they are Triton-backend numbers, measured on the
default at the time this PR was opened. On today's H20 default path this PR changes nothing that
runs — the same is true of the ten `NVIDIA_H200` block-`[32,32]` tables already on `main`.

One case reaches these tables without an explicit backend choice: `triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear`
deliberately bypasses its bf16-weight expansion when `is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled()`, which
`--enable-deterministic-inference` turns on (`model_runner.maybe_enable_batch_invariant_mode`).
Under that flag the block-32 path runs the Triton matmul, reads this table, and therefore needs
the guard described next.

### Deterministic inference

`enable_deterministic_inference` promises batch-invariant ops. The lookup picks an entry by nearest
`M`, and in these files the reduction strategy changes with `M` — e.g. for `(N,K)=(1536,5120)`,
`M=96` uses `SPLIT_K=4` while `M=168` uses a single accumulator — so the same row would accumulate
K in a different order depending on the batch it ran in.

`w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_triton` now drops `SPLIT_K` and `SWAP_AB` from the selected entry when
deterministic inference is enabled. `BLOCK_SIZE_K` is constant (32) across every entry of each file
added here, so once the reduction meta-parameters are gone every `M` dispatches to the same
single-accumulator kernel and a row's result is independent of its batch. The check reads
`exec.deterministic` only when the `exec` namespace is published, so standalone callers (tools, unit
tests) keep their previous behaviour instead of raising
`ValueError("config namespace 'exec' not published")`.

**Which kernel path each tier takes.** Of the 270 entries, 77 set `SWAP_AB` (10) or `SPLIT_K > 1`
(67) and so dispatch to `_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_hopper`; the remaining 193 set neither and stay on
`select_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_kernel`. No entry sets both. This mirrors how #39657 populates the
H200 tables: the transpose/split-K variants are used only where they measure faster, not uniformly.

## Accuracy Tests

1. **fp64 reference.** An independent microbenchmark dequantizes the same fp8 operands with the same
   fp32 block scales and matmuls in fp64, so each candidate is checked for *accuracy*, not merely for
   agreement with the deployed default.
2. **Numerically lossless end-to-end.** `accept_len` — the speculative-decode accept length, a
   sensitive end-to-end correctness signal — is unchanged at 2.66–2.67 across all three arms measured
   (no configs / M≤64 configs / 27-tier configs).
3. **Candidate-vs-deployed parity.** For the 27-tier tables, 38 candidate configs were compared against
   the deployed configuration: **35 bit-identical, 3 differing by 1 bf16 ulp**.
4. **Caveat, stated plainly.** The 67 entries with `SPLIT_K > 1` accumulate K in separate fp32
   partials, so they are not bit-identical to the single-accumulator kernel by construction; this is
   why (1) and (2) exist. The remaining 203 entries use a single accumulator. The H200 files use
   `SPLIT_K` / `SWAP_AB` in the same way.

No model-output regression is claimed beyond the above.

The CPU config-table test from the first revision
(`test/registered/cpu/quant/test_w8a8_block_fp8_configs.py`) has been removed at review request; it
is not part of this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8× NVIDIA H20 (SM90, 96 GB), `torch 2.11.0+cu130`, `triton 3.6.0`,
`torch.cuda.get_device_name()` = `NVIDIA H20`, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP=8 / EP=8.
Workload: `vllm bench serve`, sharegpt 100 prompts, seed 42, temperature 0, closed-loop concurrency.
These figures come from one deployment, not a general claim.

**Microbenchmark, per shape, M=1** (CUDA-graph capture+replay timing): 4.3–6.7×; 3258 → 989 µs summed
over the ten shapes.

**End-to-end, before → after (output tok/s):**

| concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| default fallback | 127.53 | 204.86 | 316.27 | 458.63 | 586.42 | 757.83 | 999.78 |
| with H20 tables | **172.79** | **258.46** | **368.74** | **507.44** | **640.63** | **814.80** | **1133.32** |
| delta | +35.5% | +26.2% | +16.6% | +10.6% | +9.2% | +7.5% | +13.4% |

Extending the tables from `M ≤ 64` to 27 tiers (`M ≤ 8192`) moved the high-concurrency tier further,
where the lookup had been picking a small-M config for large-M calls:

| | concurrency 64 | `ttft_p50` |
|---|---:|---:|
| `M ≤ 64` table | 1048.83 tok/s | 1539.4 ms |
| 27-tier table | **1133.32 tok/s** (+8.1%, median of 7 samples) | **1052.2 ms** (−31.7%) |

The other six concurrency tiers moved within ±1.5% of the pre-extension values.

**Runtime confirmation.** After the change the server logs `Using configuration from ... NVIDIA_H20 ...`
for all ten shapes and the "default config / sub-optimal" warning count drops from 80 to 0 per start.

## Relation to other open PRs

#41098, #41035 and #39306 add block-`[32,32]` tables for `device_name=NVIDIA_H20-3e`. Those keys are
disjoint from `NVIDIA_H20` — the config filename is an exact-match lookup on
`torch.cuda.get_device_name()`, so neither set is reachable from the other's hosts. This PR adds the
`NVIDIA_H20` set and touches no file those PRs touch.

If you would rather have a single table keyed by one name, say so and I will fold this in; the two
are otherwise independent.

Worth flagging for whoever reviews them: all three write to
`python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/configs/`, which does not exist on `main` and has no reader.
The block-FP8 tables are loaded from `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/configs/` — see
`get_w8a8_block_fp8_configs` at `kernels/ops/gemm/fp8_kernel.py:553`, which joins
`os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__))` with `"configs"` (`:576`). Files placed under the old
path would never be opened.

## Checklist

- [x] Format: the ten JSON files are LF, end with a newline, and carry no trailing whitespace
      (i.e. `pre-commit` is clean on them); `fp8_kernel.py` is formatted with the repo's
      `pre-commit`.
- [x] Unit tests: none added — the CPU config-table test was removed at review request.
- [ ] Documentation: no doc change needed; `configs/README.md` already documents the filename schema.
- [x] Accuracy and speed benchmarks: provided above.
- [x] Code style: matches the existing `NVIDIA_H200` files for the same shapes.

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4.1: Keep the full SWA window for short bounded-replay extends
author: vineelbhat
body:
## Motivation

With DeepSeek-V4.1's `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay`, the layers after the last kv_source layer attend over only the last `min(window, extend_len)` rows of each prefill extend. An extend shorter than the window therefore gives the prompt's first sampled token a truncated window.

This happens on a prefix-cache hit that leaves fewer than `window` uncached rows, and on a chunked prefill whose final chunk is shorter than `window`.

## Modifications

- A prefix-cache hit now stops at least one sliding window short of the prompt when decoder bounded replay is on. Only a hit that would have left less than a window is shortened, by at most one page. `swa_reprefill_tail_tokens()` returns `sliding_window_size` when the new `CacheInitParams.decoder_swa_bounded_replay` is set.
- The late-layer window of a final prefill chunk shorter than the window is now floored at `seq_len - window` instead of at the chunk start, so the chunk reads the previous chunk's tail rows, which already hold their late-layer KV. This is a two line change in `late_layer_tail_layout`.
- A streaming session turn that borrows its slot's record skips the hold-back: the record is the request's own KV, whose last window is already written. `swa_reprefill_tail_tokens(req)` takes the request for this.
- A prefix hit now runs the same rows with the same window floors as a cold prefill. A short final chunk does not: its tail reads the previous chunk's tail rows, which were computed under that chunk's floor. The short-chunk table below measures the difference.

## Accuracy Tests

4xB200, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4/EP4, greedy, 12 prompts per row, at the first generated position. Flips count prompts whose sampled token changed; shift is the median change of the reference's sampled-token logprob, in nats.

**Prefix hit.** An 8192-token cached prefix plus N fresh tokens, against a cold prefill of the same prompt.

| uncached rows | flips, stock | flips, fixed | shift, stock | shift, fixed |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 10/12 | 1/12 | 2.40 | 0.03 |
| 2 | 7/12 | 3/12 | 0.90 | 0.15 |
| 8 | 3/12 | 2/12 | 0.44 | 0.09 |
| 32 | 2/12 | 0/12 | 0.003 | 0.002 |
| >= 127 | 0/12 | 0/12 | 0.000 | 0.000 |

**Short final chunk.** A cold 16384 + m token prompt prefilled with a 16384-token chunk size, so its final chunk has m rows, against the same prompt prefilled as one 8192 + m extend after priming its first 8192 tokens.

| final chunk rows m | flips, stock | flips, fixed | shift, stock | shift, fixed |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 5/12 | 0/12 | 0.45 | 0.000 |
| 2 | 4/12 | 1/12 | 0.26 | 0.000 |
| 4 | 1/12 | 0/12 | 0.005 | 0.000 |
| 8 | 1/12 | 0/12 | 0.003 | 0.000 |
| 16 to 127 | 0/12 | 0/12 | 0.000 | 0.000 |

`test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py`: 2789 run on 1xH100, OK (1504 config skips), 1 new case. `test_unified_cache_linker.py`: 32 passed, one existing test updated.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The prefix-match limit only applies when a hit would leave fewer than `window` uncached rows, and then recomputes at most one page. The floor change costs each token of a short final chunk at most a full window of 128 keys to score.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [KDA+Kimi K3] Speed up SANA-Video residual gate add on H200
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation and changes

Speed up SANA-Video's residual-gate add on H200 using the **KDA-1.5 + Codex CLI + Kimi K3** candidate. Its transposed residual layout makes the original CUDA implementation expensive; the Triton path tiles along the physical stride-1 token dimension and preserves the original multiply-round-add semantics, output strides, guards, custom-op/fake interface and fallback.

**This PR now changes one production file and retains one kernel family: `residual_gate_add`.** The other 39 families from the earlier version have been removed entirely: any family with a measured regression, or without established material end-to-end benefit, stays at the upstream implementation. No per-shape salvage was used. Existing repository tests are unchanged, and the `kernel-design-agents` coauthor is retained.

Baseline: `c842d32b0ab45753178c5f6420662d7812766aca`. Candidate: `76aa0c6c8db3efd275a250a4b9aa07fd13b23a5a`. All results below were freshly measured with this isolated one-file candidate, so the E2E results are attributable to the retained change. The earlier 40-family combined results are not used as evidence for this revision.

## Kernel validation

NVIDIA H200; three independent processes; CUPTI cold-L2 timing. Speedup is baseline latency / candidate latency. Every original frozen case remains included; two additional actual SANA-Video layouts are reported separately. All measured ratios are at least 1; this is a statement about the tested cases, not a guarantee for arbitrary inputs.

| Workloads | Cases | Three geometric-mean speedups | Worst ratio across all repeats |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Original frozen suite | 33 | 1.2702× / 1.2686× / 1.2698× | 1.0017× |
| SANA-Video captured layouts | 2 | 2.5418× / 2.5434× / 2.5416× | 2.5385× |

SANA layout: BF16 `[1, 32760, 2240]`, transposed residual/output, contiguous update, broadcast gate with the two captured storage offsets. Latency is approximately **331 μs → 130 μs**. Captured-layout correctness and changed-input prepared calls pass. **35 existing residual-gate tests pass**, including dtype/layout/offset, compile, graph and fallback coverage.

[Raw kernel results](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/kernel-benchmarks.json) · [Existing tests](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/existing-tests.log) · [KDA provenance](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/provenance.json) · [All 40 inclusion/removal decisions](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/selection.json)

## Isolated end-to-end results

Model: `Efficient-Large-Model/SANA-Video_2B_480p_diffusers`, revision `db5f398b13ca086d09a50ce156c20527773841b1`; one H200; 832×480, 81 frames, 50 steps, guidance 6, seed 42. Prompt: `A curious raccoon walks through a sunlit forest. motion score: 30.` Eager native SGLang backend; fixed settings and pinned checkpoint in both arms.

Each quality runs two independent **A–B–B–A groups**, eight full saved requests total. Each cell compares the mean of two baseline requests with the mean of two candidate requests. Saved E2E includes scheduler wait and output saving; loading and separately captured profiling runs are excluded. Both groups must improve by at least 1.5% to qualify.

| Quality | Saved E2E group 1 | Saved E2E group 2 | Actual before/after |
|---|---|---|---|
| lossless | 38.840 → 38.190 s (**−1.67%**) | 38.810 → 38.155 s (**−1.69%**) | ![Actual before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/lossless/comparison.gif) |
| high | 36.300 → 35.670 s (**−1.74%**) | 36.295 → 35.700 s (**−1.64%**) | ![Actual before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/high/comparison.gif) |

All eight generated videos per quality are **file-byte and decoded-pixel exact**. GIF previews show baseline left and candidate right. Separate profiles confirm the changed `_rga_transposed` device branch executes in the real request.

- **lossless:** [baseline MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/lossless/baseline.mp4), [candidate MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/lossless/candidate.mp4), [eight-run timing](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/lossless/abba.json), [exact-output audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/lossless/media-audit.json), [device dispatch](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/lossless/device-dispatch.json).
- **high:** [baseline MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/high/baseline.mp4), [candidate MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/high/candidate.mp4), [eight-run timing](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/high/abba.json), [exact-output audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/high/media-audit.json), [device dispatch](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/high/device-dispatch.json).

These claims cover the listed H200 workloads and this exact PR head. No end-to-end gain is claimed for other models. Further model expansion and the previously paused optimization jobs remain paused. [Reproducible source patch](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/source.patch) · [Artifact hashes](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/artifact-manifest.json).

title: dsv4.1-amd: serve DeepSeek-V4.1 on gfx950
author: kevin-mii
body:
## Motivation

Integration PR of the DeepSeek-V4.1 AMD (gfx950 / MI350X) series. It follows the CUDA dsv4.1 layout (#39646, #39652, #39653, #39656, #39664, then #38798): kernel PRs by domain with no callers, then this PR with the callers. With it, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash serves on gfx950 with DSpark.

**The kernel PRs #41018, #41019, #41020 and #41021 are merged; this branch is one commit on main with the callers.**

## Modifications

- **Attention.** `deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py` serves V4.1: the compact V4.1 KV pages through `compact_attention_hip` (#41020), the swap-AB Gluon kernel for small decode batches, DSpark draft and target-verify metadata, and breakable-CUDA-graph prefill. `dsv4/low_ratio_backend_hip.py` orchestrates the ratio-1 / 2 indexer, like main's `dsv4/v41_indexer`: FlyDSL fp4 paged MQA logits over the split index-K pools (#41019), then the candidate-block and sorted top-k kernels (#41020). `hip_flash_mla.py` routes the HIP decode kernels (`SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=auto`: aiter's sparse kernel on gfx950, tilelang elsewhere).
- **Dense fp8.** `fp8_hip.py` serves 32x32-block fp8 checkpoints as MXFP8 on the gfx950 native route (#41018); the RMSNorm, SiLU and wo_a producers hand it fp8-grid or MXFP8 operands (`deepseek_common/amd/deepseek_v4_gfx95_dense.py`, `deepseek_v2_hip_act.py`).
- **mHC.** `deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py` runs each sublayer boundary as one launch, with its Sinkhorn carried by the next RMSNorm, and the TP4 all-reduce fused with the mHC post for decode batches of 1-8 rows (#41021).
- **MoE and Engram.** The split-K router GEMV and gate for DeepSeek-V4 gates (#41019). Engram's all-reduce and reduce-scatter add BF16 rows as int32 on ROCm, so they are bit-exact.
- **Other.** DSpark runs on HIP. `SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM` now defaults to on for ROCm. The paths validated only on gfx950 are gated on gfx950, so MI300 (gfx942) keeps main's DeepSeek-V4 paths.
- **Kept on main.** No HIP attention CP (HIP prefill CP stays rejected), no torch prefill-indexer oracle on HIP, no fp32 V4 router `torch.mm`, and no diagnostic or cosmetic edits to main code; the fuller branch is kept on `kevin-mii/sglang:dsv41-amd-5-integration-full-20260928`.
- **Fixes from end-to-end testing.**
  - `hip_flash_mla._uniform_indptr` caches only row pointers built outside graph capture. V4.1 DSpark captures a `candidate_unfiltered` and a `candidate_filtered` verify graph per batch size with the same row-pointer shape; the filtered one (longest request above 16K tokens) reused a tensor only the unfiltered graph writes, in graph-pool memory other graphs overwrite, and `_pa_decode_sparse` faulted (`HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT`) at 32K context with concurrent requests.
  - An eager DSpark verify batch (past `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`, e.g. more than 64 requests under the default 256 running) no longer asserts on the missing host seq lens; it sizes metadata from `candidate_max_seq_len_upper_bound`, without a host sync.
  - DeepSeek-V4 (not V4.1) with EAGLE died on its first request on HIP: EAGLE fell back to the backend's `max_context_len` once the per-step `seq_lens.sum()` sync was gone, and `DeepseekV4HipRadixBackend` had none. It now builds a `QLEN_ONLY` verify mask like the CUDA V4 backend.
  - Cookbook: the MI350X cells export `AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE_REDUCE=1` and `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0` (the published cells could not start with the pinned aiter), keep DSpark in both cells, cap decode graphs at 128 (low-latency) / 256 (high-throughput), and enable `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay`.
  - `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay` crashed on HIP while capturing graphs (`window_layout()` got a stale `replay=` argument); the HIP backend now passes the per-request floor like the CUDA backend.

The ROCm code lives in `models/deepseek_common/amd/` and the HIP backend files. `deepseek_v4.py` and `deepseek_v2.py` call into it only on HIP.

### Changes visible off ROCm
Each of these is a no-op for CUDA / NPU:
- `deepseek_v4.py`: `q=`, `inv_rope=` and `router_logits_partials=` are passed only when set. The hc_mix gate keeps CUDA's conditions. The three input-norm sites keep their gfx95-only fp8 quant, so gfx1250 is unchanged.
- `dspark_draft_model.py`: the stacked-dequant path requires a 2-D weight.
- `deepseek_v4_backend.py`: the split index-K store is taken only when the pool reports the split layout, which is HIP only.

## Tests

- **Tests.** Runtime tests sit with their subsystem, as in #38798: the HIP backend, fused-compress and aiter_sparse backend tests in `attention/unittests/dsv4/`; the wo_a, MoE, fused-mHC and TP4 torchrun model tests in `unit/models/`; kernel cases live in the kernel PRs. All pass on MI350X on this branch with the kernel PRs' tests; the TP4 test compares fused and unfused mHC outputs eagerly (registered-buffer copy-in) and under graph replay.
- **End to end.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 4x MI350X, TP4 / EP4, DSpark, `--attention-backend dsv4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --page-size 256 --disable-radix-cache`, `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0`. The comparison is back to back on one node against this series' previous integration head (3e8187fa88, kept as `dsv41-amd-4-model-old-stack`), same flags, `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 128`. The old head aborts in aiter's `_varctx_cta_info_kernel` when it captures decode graphs above 128; #41019's in-tree schedule fixes that.

  This PR's numbers are from the current head (0a0c59e635) in an environment built as the contribution guide describes: `sglang-kernel` built from `python/sglang/kernels/aot/` with `setup_rocm.py install` and sglang installed from the checkout, as `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` and AMD CI do, keeping the Dockerfile's `apache-tvm-ffi` pin. GSM8K is five runs.

  | | previous head | this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | GSM8K (200 questions) | 0.895 | 0.890 (0.860-0.910) |
  | random 4096 in / 1024 out, concurrency 1 | 476.7 tok/s | 508.5 tok/s |
  | concurrency 8 | 1,779.6 tok/s | 1,863.6 tok/s |
  | concurrency 32 | 3,175.6 tok/s | 3,265.2 tok/s |
- **Fixes.** V4.1-Flash, cookbook low-latency flags, 4x MI350X: random 32768 in / 256 out at concurrency 4 faults on every run at `f84617215d` and completes 8/8 with this branch; 4096 in at concurrency 4 and 32K at concurrency 1 pass on both. Concurrency 80 (1K in / 256 out) asserts on `seq_lens_cpu` at `f84617215d`; with this branch it completes 160/160 at 2,599 tok/s and GSM8K at `--parallel 128` scores 0.915 / 0.915. `test_hip_flash_mla_aiter_sparse.py::TestUniformIndptrGraphs` fails on the old cache and passes now.
- **Cookbook.** Same node, V4.1-Flash, random 4096 in / 1024 out. Low-latency cell: 524 / 2167 / 4072 tok/s at concurrency 1 / 8 / 32, GSM8K 0.910 / 0.915 / 0.890. High-throughput cell: 523 / 2180 / 4089 at 1 / 8 / 32 and 5186 / 7558 / 8976 at 64 / 128 / 256, GSM8K 0.890 / 0.885 / 0.870; plain decode (the previous high-throughput cell) reaches 2751 / 4641 / 6125 at 64 / 128 / 256. At concurrency 1 with 128K in (90% prefix hit) / 1K out, decoder SWA replay cuts TTFT from 860 to 576 ms and E2E from 2.53 to 2.25 s; encoder SWA replay is correct (GSM8K 0.88-0.895) but slows decode by 78%, so the cells leave it off.
- **DeepSeek-V4 on MI350X.** V4-Flash (fp4), TP4 (the cookbook cells are TP8; this node has 6 GPUs), MI355X low-latency cookbook flags with EAGLE, against main at the merge base with main's sgl-kernel: 243 / 1265 / 3280 vs 227 / 1259 / 3274 tok/s at concurrency 1 / 8 / 32, GSM8K 0.97 vs 0.96. With `SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND` unset, the new `auto` default (aiter_sparse on gfx950) beats main's tilelang default: 252 / 1223 / 2815 vs 217 / 939 / 1720. Not run: TP8, V4-Pro (it does not start at TP4 on main either), MI300.

## Deployment note

Set `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0` until ROCm/aiter#5802 is in the aiter pin. At the default bound, small batches take aiter's BF16-activation MoE route, which does not apply `swiglu_limit` and, with the current pin, has no kernel for these experts: the server fails during decode-graph warmup. The MI350X cookbook cells export it.

## Not in this PR
- `deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py` is over 3k lines. Splitting out the late-layer tail and breakable-prefill sections, and binding more CUDA backend methods instead of HIP copies, are follow-ups.

title: [diffusion] Run an all-valid attention mask on the backend's unmasked kernel
author: mickqian
body:
## Problem

On sm100 the default attention backend resolves to `DYNAMIC_CUDNN_SDPA`, but `USPAttention`'s masked local path opens its varlen fast path only for `backend == FA`. Every other backend gets a dense additive mask for `torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention`, and any mask moves SDPA off flash and cuDNN onto PyTorch's `fmha_cutlassF_*_sm80` kernel, even when the mask masks nothing.

Ideogram4 passes such a mask on both guidance branches at batch 1: its text is never padded at batch 1, so `segment_ids > 0` is all true. Every attention call on B200 therefore took the cutlassF path:

- torch profile of the denoising loop: attention = **54% of GPU time on 1×B200, 47% at TP2**, all in `fmha_cutlassF_bf16_aligned_32x128_gmem_sm80`
- per call (`[1, 18, 4126, 256]` bf16): **2.19 ms with the mask, 0.81 ms without**

It is also consistent with Ideogram4 measuring only ~9% faster on B200 than on H200, against 1.7-2.6× for the other models: on Hopper the default backend is FA, whose varlen path already treats an all-valid mask as dense.

## Fix

When `attn_mask_meta` shows every key valid (its index count equals the mask's element count, known on the host, no device sync), the masked local path runs the backend's own unmasked kernel. Segmented-prefix inputs (Qwen-Image) are concatenated first, so the prefix is kept. Masks with real padding, and meta without indices (padding-gap meta), keep the masked path. The FA backend is untouched (its varlen branch returns before this point), and so are the sequence-parallel paths.

## Validation (4×B200)

- Unit: the new `test/unit/test_usp_all_valid_key_mask.py` drives `USPAttention.forward` through the masked local branch with real varlen meta. An all-valid mask runs the backend kernel once and matches unmasked attention; a real padding mask, and padding-gap meta without indices, keep the masked path; a segmented prefix is concatenated before dispatch. The two backend-kernel tests fail on `main`. The neighbouring attention/mask unit tests (ring tail-pad, K/V gather, varlen meta, replicated prefix, Ideogram4, BCG padding) pass.

- Ideogram4 serving, default B200 command (`--tp-size 2`), warmup then 5 measured requests, interleaved main/PR/main/PR on the same node:

  | | round 1 | round 2 |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | `main` | 3.424 s | 3.427 s |
  | this PR | **2.192 s** | **2.205 s** |

- Steady denoising step (single `sglang generate`, no warmup): 1 GPU 277.0 → 158.2 ms, TP2 160.8 → 126.1 ms.
- Kernels (torch profile, TP2): attention 78.0 → 8.7 ms per step. cuDNN 9.20 (bundled with torch 2.13) has no head_dim-256 kernel on sm100, so `DYNAMIC_CUDNN_SDPA` takes its FA4 fallback (`sm100_hd256_2cta_fmha_forward`, 128 µs per call against 1104 µs for cutlassF).
- Output: PR vs `main` PSNR 26.2 dB at TP2 and 26.5 dB on 1 GPU, against 22.7 dB between TP2 and 1 GPU on `main` itself. Ideogram4's guidance amplifies FP reordering; the all-valid additive mask is exactly zero, so the math is unchanged.

- Qwen-Image-2512 and Z-Image-Turbo, which also pass masks with varlen meta, produce bitwise-identical images before and after: at batch 1 they do not reach this branch.
- The second commit logs the cuDNN → FlashAttention fallback once per process. Routing these calls to the backend kernel made Ideogram4 log it once per attention layer, 68 times per start.

title: Make sliding-window caching and speculative batch padding extensible
author: merrymercy
body:
## Summary

Cache implementations and speculative inputs need to manage their own eviction and padding state. Add sliding-window eviction and recovery hooks, component-specific lock release, and a reusable unified-cache factory. Move EAGLE-specific tensor padding into the input classes, with a no-op default for other inputs.

Keep protected-prefix bounds separate from eviction-interval gating. Preserve the existing AMD forward-based eviction cadence and adapt the eviction regression test to the current cache classes.

## Test plan

- Focused tests: **54 passed**, including 7 subtests.

  ```bash
  uv run --no-sync python -m pytest -q --tb=short --maxfail=1 \
    test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_registry.py \
    test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_swa_cpu_copy_filter.py \
    test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_swa_eviction_interval.py \
    test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_swa_locked_full_recover_unified.py \
    test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_mlp_sync_pad_unpad.py \
    test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_tree_core_registry.py
  ```

- Unified-cache regression suite: **1,279 passed, 1,504 skipped**, including 70 passing subtests.

  ```bash
  LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib64/libcrypto.so.3 uv run --no-sync python -m pytest \
    -q --tb=short --maxfail=1 \
    test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py
  ```

  The initial run could not load the native hash extension's `libcrypto.so.3`; preloading the installed system library resolved it.

- `pre-commit run --from-ref main --to-ref HEAD`: passed using an existing pre-commit installation.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: passed.
- End-to-end serving, model accuracy, and throughput benchmarks were not run; no model server was launched for this port.

title: [Kernel] Expose FlashMLA kv_format in sgl-kernel sparse decode
author: DarkSharpness
body:
(auto generated by Claude)

## Motivation

The FlashMLA fork's V3.2-no-RoPE and V4.1 KV caches are both 528 bytes per token with head_dim 512, so the shape alone cannot tell them apart. sgl-kernel always passes no format, which currently makes FlashMLA read a V4.1 cache as V3.2-no-RoPE. sgl-project/FlashMLA#15 switches that default to V4.1, matching upstream FlashMLA.

## Modifications

- `sparse_decode_fwd` and `flash_mla_with_kvcache` take an optional `kv_format`.
- Sparse calls with tensor tile scheduler metadata (the DSA `flashmla_kv` path) now go through `sparse_decode_fwd`, and a 528-byte head_dim-512 cache defaults to `V32_NO_ROPE` there, so zero-RoPE DSA models such as GLM-5.3-Flash keep decoding correctly after the default flips.
- Regression tests for both paths in `kernels/aot/tests/test_flashmla.py`.

## Status

Draft until sgl-project/FlashMLA#15 merges; the FlashMLA pin bump will be added to this PR then. Validation on H200 and B200 follows the pin bump.

title: [diffusion] Qwen-Image 2.1: fuse Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE + KV packing into one CUDA kernel and project Q/K/V with one packed GEMM
author: triple-mu
body:
## Motivation

Profiling Qwen-Image 2.1 (1024x1024, 40 steps, bf16, `--attention-backend torch_sdpa`) on one SM120 GPU shows each transformer block spending ~10.8 ms per step: 81% GEMM, 14% attention and ~5% everything else. That last slice was not bandwidth-limited work but data movement and launches around attention:

- two Triton kernels for Q/K RMSNorm + complex RoPE (`_qknorm_complex_rope_onepass_kernel`, 38 us; `_qknorm_complex_rope_kv_kernel`, 119 us), the second of which re-copies the full V projection (64 MiB per block-step) just to place it behind the text prefix;
- three separate Q/K/V GEMMs (N=4096 each) with their own tile tails;
- a single-element `torch.cat` on the attention output that degrades to a 33.5 MB device copy.

All three are removed here without changing a single output bit: every new path is default-on and verifies its first call against the eager chain through `BitExactFusionGate`, falling back permanently on a mismatch (the existing Qwen-Image 2.1 convention).

## Modifications

One commit per optimization:

1. `bef0002567` **Skip the single-element `torch.cat`** on the attention output (pure aliasing; the multi-segment prefix path keeps the cat).
2. `50f14915a4` **`qknorm_complex_rope` JIT CUDA kernel** (`kernels/jit/csrc/diffusion/qknorm_complex_rope.cuh`, wrapper `ops/diffusion/rope/qknorm_complex_rope_jit.py`). One warp per 128-wide row; Q and K RMSNorm (`RMSNorm(cast_x_before_out_mul=True)`: aten's 128-wide fp32 reduction order and double bf16 rounding), the complex64 RoPE with the same FMA orientation as the Triton path (`_fuse_real_sin` probe), and the prefix K/V copies in a single launch. `run` (out of place, used by `apply_qk_norm_rope`) and `run_pack` (Q in place, K normalized in place behind the prefix rows, optional V copy) variants; registered as custom ops with fake impls; CUDA-graph safe.
3. `622f00a077` **K/V projections written straight into the packed KV buffers**: `torch.mm(x, W.t(), out=buffer[P:])` for K and V so V is never copied and the kernel normalizes K in place (`kCopyV=False`). Gated by a first-sight `torch.equal` against the module forward.
4. `30819672a1` **One packed Q/K/V GEMM**: `to_q/to_k/to_v` weights are re-pointed at slices of one `[3C, C]` storage in `post_load_weights` (the per-layer `weight` parameters stay views, so checkpoint loading, weight updates and LoRA base weights are unaffected); one N=12288 GEMM writes into a `[1, P+S, 3C]` buffer and Q/K/V are column views (token stride 3C) consumed by the pack kernel and SDPA. Gated by a first-sight compare with the three separate GEMMs.
5. `3a2dd56e1f` gate protocol tests, kernel README row, fast-paths inventory entry, pre-commit formatting (a marker benchmark added here was dropped again later in the series).

Fallbacks keep the previous Triton chain: batch > 1, sequence parallel > 1, LoRA-wrapped or quantized projections, head_dim != 128, ROCm, `torch.compile`, and any first-sight mismatch. Nothing is verified while a CUDA graph is being captured.

Per block-step the op sequence goes from 7 GEMM + 1 attention + 8 small kernels + 1 memcpy to 5 GEMM + 1 attention + 6 small kernels.

## Accuracy Tests

Everything in this PR is bit-exact by construction and verified at three levels:

- Kernel: `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_qknorm_complex_rope.py` (20 cases; `torch.equal` against `RMSNorm(cast_x_before_out_mul=True, force_native=True)` + eager complex RoPE; shapes (1,4096,32,128), (1,18,32,128), (2,17,4,128), (1,1,1,128); in-place and copy pack variants; token-strided views of a packed QKV buffer; CUDA graph replay).
- Wiring: `test_model_fast_paths.py::test_qwen21_cuda_qk_rope_*` (first-sight verify, mismatch -> permanent eager fallback, no verification during capture) and `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_qwen_image21_cuda.py` (head_dim-128 model: prefill + cached steps in t2i and edit mode with `atol=0`, prefix cache stays exact-size storage, breakable-CUDA-graph capture/replay `atol=0`, packed weights share storage and survive in-place updates, pack mismatch restores the reference).
- End to end: the same-seed 1024x1024 PNG (seed 42, `generator_device=cpu`) has the same sha256 as `main` in every launch of this series (`2781b27ac4b17cb1...`, 12 launches on two GPUs).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hardware: one cc 12.0 (SM120) GPU, 73 GB, 350 W power cap, clocks not locked (the GPU sits at the cap during the whole run); torch 2.13.0+cu132, cuDNN 9.20. Workload: `sglang serve --performance-mode speed --attention-backend torch_sdpa`, 1024x1024, 40 steps, guidance 1.0, bf16, eager. Each e2e number is one server launch with 1 warmup + 3 measured requests; stage times come from `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1`.

Kernel level (`marker.do_bench` on the production shapes, median us):

| site | eager | Triton (main) | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q RMSNorm + RoPE, (1, 4096, 32, 128) | 548.9 | 65.5 | 65.5 (same bytes; kept for the pack variant) |
| Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE + KV packing, S=4096, P=18 | 1133.6 | 190.5 (two kernels, copies V) | 124.9 (K in place, V never copied) |
| Q/K/V projection, M=4096, K=4096 | - | 3 x N=4096: 1786 | 1 x N=12288: 1707 |

End to end (denoising stage, 32 blocks x 40 steps; e2e HTTP latency of the DiT-only tree on the same GPU as its baseline):

| tree | denoising 40 steps (ms) | per block-step (us) | e2e HTTP (s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 13 715 | 342.9 x 1 / 32 | 13.890 |
| this PR | 13 533 (-1.3%) | -142 per block-step | 13.721 (-1.2%) |

The -142 us per block-step decomposes (nsys, same GPU) into -70 us from the packed GEMM (six 64x256 GEMM launches at 6717 us -> four at 6647 us), -55 us from the single norm-RoPE launch (104 us vs 38 + 119 us) and -15 us from the removed memcpy. Whole-image kernel launches drop from 24 699 to about 20 800. The GPU stays at its power cap; the fused tree runs ~18 MHz lower at the same 347 W, so the gain under locked clocks would be slightly larger. Run-to-run spread of the e2e latency is 0.3-1.0%; the -1.3% was reproduced in three interleaved rounds.

Smoke of this exact branch (rebased on `main` @ `3ed56a341b`, one launch each on a second GPU of the same type, stage-profiling cohort): `main` 13.894 s / denoising 13 585 ms; this PR 13.735 s / denoising 13 427 ms (-158 ms), PNG sha256 identical.

Not done here (measured and rejected): fusing the residual gate add with the following LayerNorm (the two-kernel chain is L2-resident and the fused kernel was slower, 114.5 vs 105.9 us), packing the gate/up GEMMs into one N=24576 GEMM (462 us/block-step slower on this GPU), and rewriting `_silu_mul_kernel` in CUDA (it already runs at 1.28 TB/s of a 1.34 TB/s roofline).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [diffusion] Qwen-Image 2.1 VAE decoder fast paths: bit-exact norm/bias fusions by default, channels_last decode under quality=extra-high
author: triple-mu
body:
Independent of the attention PR; both add entries to `kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py`, the kernel README and the fast-paths inventory (adjacent lines, trivial to rebase; the inventory section is numbered 18 assuming the attention PR's 17 lands first).

## Motivation

The Qwen-Image 2.1 VAE decode of a 1024x1024 image takes 186 ms on one SM120 GPU. Its decoder (dims 1152/1152/1152/576/288/144, five up blocks that run three residual blocks at their own resolution and then upsample) spends that time on cuDNN convs, but also on work that is pure data movement: cuDNN's NCHW/NHWC transposes around every conv (25 ms), aten's channel RMSNorm chain (fp32 copy + reduce + four pointwise passes + SiLU), a separate bias-add pass after every conv (46 launches, 10 ms) and nearest-2x upsampling that quadruples the pixels before a 3x3 conv.

This PR removes that overhead in two tiers, following the existing VAE fast-path conventions (`VaeFastPathGate` for quality-gated paths, `BitExactFusionGate` first-sight verification for default-on paths):

- **default (`quality=lossless`)**: bit-exact fusions only; the output PNG is unchanged;
- **`quality=extra-high` / `high`**: the decoder switches to channels_last and uses an NHWC norm kernel with its own reduction order plus fp32-folded upsampler weights; documented as close, not bit-exact.

## Modifications

One commit per optimization (`runtime/models/vaes/qwen_image21_vae_cuda_opt.py`, mounted from `platforms/cuda.py::optimize_vae`; parameter names are preserved so checkpoints load unchanged):

1. `a99db03979` **Lossless fast paths (default on)**: `channel_rmsnorm_finish_silu` JIT kernel keeps aten's fp32 `norm(dim=1)` reduction and fuses the pointwise finish (`max(norm, 1e-12)`, divide, scale, gamma, `+0.0`) with SiLU; `FoldedPadConv2d` folds the symmetric `F.pad` of every causal conv into the conv's own padding, verified per (dtype, shape, stride) signature because cuDNN may pick another algorithm; the fold is only attempted above 2^18 output elements, where a bit-exact first-sight match is decisive (two engines with different accumulation orders agree on all but ~1e-4 of the elements, so on a few thousand elements they can match by chance, as the H100 runner showed at a 4x4 test latent).
2. `a99052507b` **channels_last decode under the quality gate**: the decoder flips to channels_last (parameter memory only; flipping back restores the NCHW kernels exactly), `channel_rmsnorm_silu_nhwc` reduces each pixel's channels in a lane group (1-32 lanes per pixel with 16-byte loads, chosen from C by the Python wrapper so the C=144 last stage stays near bandwidth), and the nearest 2x upsample re-labels the merged-batch view with canonical NHWC strides and uses the bit-exact Triton NHWC gather.
3. `119ab3c768` **Upsampler fold (quality gate)**: each `nearest-2x + conv3x3(p1)` becomes one `ConvTranspose2d(k4, s2, p1)` whose kernel is the fp32 sum of the taps each output phase touches (2.25x fewer MACs, no 4x intermediate). The fold helper moves out of the FLUX.2 module into `vaes/conv_fold.py` so both VAEs share it.
4. `53da9a360c` **Conv bias fusions**: aten adds a conv's bias as a separate pass over the output. Each residual block's second conv now runs without its bias and the new bit-exact `bias_residual_add` JIT kernel applies bias and residual in one pass with aten's per-op bf16 rounding (default on, first-sight verified; channels_last-dense or NCHW-contiguous bf16). Under the quality gate the first conv hands its bias to the NHWC norm kernel, so that pass disappears too.
5. `8d1e569f15` **Upsampler bias into the shortcut add**: the shared Wan Triton kernel `dup_up3d_add` takes an optional per-channel bias (aten rounding), so the upsampler conv runs without its bias pass (default on, first-sight verified).
6. `16cadcebe6` kernel README rows, fast-paths inventory entry, pre-commit formatting (a marker benchmark added here was dropped again later in the series).

Fallbacks: spatial-parallel decode, ROCm, `torch.compile`, unsupported layouts and any first-sight mismatch keep the original module chain.

## Accuracy Tests

- Lossless (default) path, bit-exact: the `channel_rmsnorm_finish_silu` section of `test_norm.py` (14), the `bias_residual_add` section of `test_norm.py` (25, `torch.equal` in both layouts), the `dup_up3d_add` bias case in `test_layout.py`, and the Qwen-Image 2.1 VAE section of `test_model_fast_paths.py` (decode of an optimized tiny decoder with the real latent channel count equals the original bit for bit on a 64x64 latent, where every fold site's first-sight comparison is decisive, and again on a second latent while every gate reports verified; a mismatching kernel disables its gate and the decode stays bit-identical; `state_dict` keys unchanged). End to end the same-seed 1024x1024 PNG keeps `main`'s sha256 (`2781b27ac4b17cb1...`) in every lossless launch.
- `extra-high` path: the `channel_rmsnorm_silu_nhwc` section of `test_norm.py` (within two bf16 ulps of the eager chain, >95% of elements bit-identical, all lane-group specializations, fused bias) and the extra-high case in that section (channels_last decode close to the reference, gate off restores bit-identity). End to end, the extra-high image against the lossless image (RGBA, 1024x1024, seed 42; deterministic: the same sha256 on two GPUs and seven launches):

| channel | PSNR (dB) | global SSIM | max abs diff (/255) | changed pixels |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R | 57.75 | 0.99997 | 8 | 10.3% |
| G | 57.85 | 0.99995 | 11 | 9.7% |
| B | 58.90 | 0.99993 | 8 | 8.2% |
| A | 73.80 | 0.99995 | 1 | 0.3% |
| all | 59.35 | - | 11 | 7.1% |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hardware and workload as in the attention PR: one cc 12.0 (SM120) GPU, 73 GB, 350 W cap, torch 2.13.0+cu132, cuDNN 9.20; `sglang serve --performance-mode speed --attention-backend torch_sdpa`, 1024x1024, 40 steps, bf16. Decode times are the `DecodingStage` under `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1`, mean of 3 requests after a warmup request.

VAE decode, whole series on one GPU, interleaved with `main`:

| quality | decode (ms) | vs `main` | e2e HTTP (s) | output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 186.0 | - | 14.010 | sha256 `2781b27a...` |
| lossless (default) | 159.8 | -14.1% | 13.798 (with the attention PR) | identical to `main` |
| extra-high | 100.4 | -46.0% | 13.743 (with the attention PR) | PSNR 59.4 dB vs lossless |

Per commit (single launches on a second GPU of the same type; its `main` decode is 184.4 ms):

| after commit | lossless decode (ms) | extra-high decode (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 lossless fusions | 163.5 | - |
| 2 channels_last + NHWC norm | 163.6 | 126.4 |
| 3 upsampler fold | - | 112.7 |
| 4 conv bias fusions | 160.2 | 101.1 |
| 5 upsampler bias into shortcut add | 158.3 | 99.1 |

Smoke of this exact branch (rebased on `main` @ `3ed56a341b`, one launch each on a second GPU of the same type, stage-profiling cohort): `main` decode 184.4 ms; this PR 158.0 ms lossless (PNG sha256 identical to `main`) and 98.8 ms extra-high (PSNR 59.35 dB vs lossless, same sha256 as on the other GPU).

Kernel level (`marker.do_bench` on the decoder's production shapes, median us; `cuda` = lossless finish kernel with aten's reduction, `cuda_nhwc` = quality-gated kernel):

| channel RMSNorm + SiLU site | eager | Triton finish (main) | cuda | cuda_nhwc |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (1, 144, 1, 1024, 1024) | 5384 | 2432 | 1881 | 559 |
| (1, 288, 1, 1024, 1024) | 10823 | 4893 | 3811 | 1106 |
| (1, 288, 1, 512, 512) | 2657 | 1175 | 915 | 289 |
| (1, 576, 1, 256, 256) | 1249 | 538 | 421 | 147 |

Other measured pieces: the four upsampler `nearest-2x + conv3x3` sites go from 9754 us to 5529 us as ConvTranspose2d; the separate conv-bias adds go from 46 launches / 10.3 ms to 9 launches / 1.2 ms under extra-high (26 launches / 4.6 ms under lossless, where the first conv's bias cannot enter the aten norm reduction); cuDNN's NCHW/NHWC transposes (119 launches, 24.7 ms) disappear under extra-high. What remains of the extra-high decode (~100 ms) is ~80 ms of cuDNN conv, which `cudnn.benchmark` does not improve on this GPU.

title: [VLM] Introduce FA4 into ViT for SM100/SM103
author: yuan-luo
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

This PR is to fill gaps in FA4 path on Blackwell:
1. **The softmax row max ignores an sm_103 instruction.** Blackwell Ultra adds `tcgen05.ld.red`, a TMEM load that also returns a per-thread reduction of the loaded values. We can use it to get each row's max for free while reading S out of TMEM. Currently SGLang FA4 forward does not: on B300 every softmax step still reduces 128 values per row with FMNMX3.
2. **ViT attention on B300 falls back to Triton.** #25570 switched the default multimodal attention backend on SM103 from `fa4` to `triton_attn` because "FA4 is not yet validated on B300". Measured on B300, FA4's kernel is 2–20x faster than the Triton kernel on ViT shapes (head dims 64/72/80/128) and matches it numerically, so B300 ViTs pay a large, avoidable cost.
3. **The ViT CUDA graph runners do not support `fa4`.** `SGLANG_VIT_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1` only handles `triton_attn` and `fa3`; with `fa4` (already the default on SM100) the server dies at startup with `AssertionError: cu_seqlens must be a torch.Tensor`. Changing the SM103 default without fixing this would break every B300 deployment that turned the ViT graph on. The graph is also what removes FA4's per-call host overhead for small images (see Speed Tests).


## Modifications

- `flash_fwd_sm100.py`: on sm_103, build a second TMEM copy with `tcgen05.LdRed32x32bOp(redOp=MAX)`. In `softmax_step`, tiles that need no masking (`mask_fn is None`) in kernels without `score_mod`/bias load S with it — one `cute.copy_atom_call` per 32-column chunk, each also returning that chunk's max — and pass the reduced max to the softmax. Masked tiles keep the plain load and the software max, because the hardware max is taken over the raw S. On the tiles where it is used the hardware max equals the software reduction exactly, so **outputs are bit-identical** to the current kernel. The first-iteration tile is always masked (`mask_seqlen=True`), so only steady-state tiles change.
- `softmax.py`: `SoftmaxSm100.update_row_max` accepts an optional precomputed `tile_row_max`; everything after the max (fast `exp2`, rescale threshold) is unchanged.
- `interface.py`: `SGLANG_FA4_TMEM_LOAD_RED_MAX` (default `1`; `0` restores the FMNMX reduction). It is part of the compile key, so both variants can coexist in one process. The flag is ignored on non-sm_103 GPUs.
- `vision.py`: the platform default multimodal attention backend is `fa4` for all compute capability 10.x (SM100 and SM103). Explicit `--mm-attention-backend` and per-model overrides (e.g. Kimi-K3-VL's own SM103 heuristic) are unchanged.
- `vision.py` (`VisionFlash4Attention`): accepts the graph runners' `[cu_seqlens, max_seqlen]` list. Unlike the fa3/triton wrappers it keys off the argument type, not the env var, so models without a graph runner keep passing tensors when `SGLANG_VIT_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1` is set globally.
- `vit_cuda_graph_runner.py`, `internvl_vit_cuda_graph_runner.py`: pass `fa4` the same layout as `fa3`. FA4 JIT-compiles a kernel variant the first time it sees a configuration, which must not happen inside stream capture; for windowed ViTs (Qwen2.5-VL) the generic runner therefore warms up both the windowed and the full-attention layout before capturing (it previously warmed up only block 0's layout). The InternVL runner already warms up every layer eagerly.
- `test_vision_backend_selection.py`: covers the CUDA default per compute capability (9.0→fa3, 10.0→fa4, 10.3→fa4, 12.0→triton_attn) and `VisionFlash4Attention` with list-form and tensor seqlens, with the graph env var on and off.

## Accuracy Tests

All on 8x B300 (sm_103, 148 SMs), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.2.

**FA4 kernel, bit-exactness.** 16 configurations run on the unpatched tree and on this branch with the flag on; outputs and LSE are identical in every case (`torch.equal`): causal / non-causal, varlen, chunked prefill (q < k), GQA and `pack_gqa`, head dims 64 / 96 / 128 / (192,128) (incl. the 2-CTA path), sliding window, learnable sink, softcap (reducing load disabled there), split-KV, paged KV (page 128 TMA and page 64 cp.async), and fp8 e4m3 with descales. The compiled PTX (`.target sm_103a`) contains 4 `tcgen05.ld.red` instructions with the flag on and none with it off.

**FA4 unit tests.** `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_flash_attention_4.py`: 330 passed, 24 skipped, 0 failed.

**ViT attention, FA4 vs Triton.** sglang's own `VisionFlash4Attention` and `VisionTritonAttention` on the same inputs: max abs difference 5e-4 – 1.6e-2 in bf16 across GLM-5.3 / DeepSeek-V4.1 shapes (d=64) and Qwen2.5-VL shapes (d=80, windowed and full attention), consistent with bf16 rounding.

**End to end, MMMU validation (900 questions)** Two servers from the same base commit, one per GPU:

| model (serving config) | ViT | `triton_attn` (current B300 default) | `fa4` (this PR) | same final answer | same-config baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (1 GPU) | eager | 51.7% | 51.8% | 871 / 900 (96.8%) | eager vs graph, same backend: 887–891 / 900 |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (1 GPU) | CUDA graph | 52.0% | 51.6% | 875 / 900 (97.2%) | (same as above) |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP4 + EP4, cookbook flags, chat mode; 32-layer d=64 ViT) | eager | 67.8% / 66.9% / 67.2% (3 runs) | 68.0% | 830 / 900 (92.2%) | two identical `triton_attn` servers: 834 / 900 (92.7%) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

All on B300 (sm_103, 148 SMs, 1 GPU per measurement unless noted). Kernel numbers are CUDA-graph timed unless marked eager; "eager" includes the Python wrapper, as an un-graphed ViT sees it.

**`tcgen05.ld.red.max` in the FA4 forward, ViT shapes**

Command: `python benchmark/kernels/attention/bench_flash_attention_tmem_red_max.py`. It calls FA4 the way `VisionFlash4Attention` does (varlen, non-causal, no LSE, 16 heads, bf16).

Each of 10 rounds times the flag off and on back to back, alternating which goes first. "off" and "on" are the best round of each. "paired" is the median of the per-round off/on ratios, and "wins" counts the rounds where on was faster. Outputs are bit-identical for every shape.

| input | head dim | off | on | paired speedup | wins |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 images x 4096 tokens | 80 (Qwen2.5-VL) | 648.8 us | 588.0 us | **1.075x** | 10/10 |
| 8 images x 4096 tokens | 72 (Qwen3-VL) | 703.9 us | 681.6 us | 1.039x | 10/10 |
| 8 images x 4096 tokens | 64 (InternViT, GLM / DeepSeek-V4 ViT) | 527.4 us | 518.2 us | 1.023x | 8/10 |
| 64 images x 1024 tokens | 80 | 438.2 us | 415.7 us | 1.048x | 10/10 |
| 64 images x 1024 tokens | 64 | 360.5 us | 356.8 us | 1.010x | 10/10 |
| 1 image x 32768 tokens | 80 | 4861.1 us | 4572.3 us | **1.058x** | 10/10 |
| 1 image x 32768 tokens | 72 | 5217.1 us | 5070.5 us | 1.030x | 10/10 |
| 1 image x 32768 tokens | 64 | 3974.7 us | 3887.8 us | 1.022x | 10/10 |

**ViT attention kernel, `fa4` vs `triton_attn`** (the kernels behind the default switch):

Head-dim sweep, 16 heads, non-causal varlen, speedup of `fa4` over `triton_attn` (FA4 from the base commit, i.e. without item 1; the two wrapper tables below are on this branch):

| layout | d=64 | d=72 | d=80 | d=128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 images x 4096 tokens | 5.4x | 20.5x | 7.9x | 6.6x |
| 1 image x 16384 tokens | 5.4x | 19.3x | 7.8x | 6.4x |
| 64 images x 1024 tokens | 4.2x | 16.2x | 6.1x | 5.4x |

GLM-5.3 / DeepSeek-V4.1 ViT shapes (16 heads, d=64), sglang's `VisionFlash4Attention` / `VisionTritonAttention`, per call:

| input | fa4 eager | triton eager | eager ratio | fa4 graph | triton graph | graph ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 image 224² (256 tok) | 62.4 us | 38.4 us | 0.62x | 7.0 us | 14.4 us | 2.05x |
| 1 image 448² (1024 tok) | 61.5 us | 49.3 us | 0.80x | 13.1 us | 44.4 us | 3.38x |
| 4 images 448² | 62.0 us | 98.3 us | 1.59x | 25.5 us | 93.5 us | 3.67x |
| 16 images 448² | 94.2 us | 370.2 us | 3.93x | 90.7 us | 364.8 us | 4.02x |
| 64 images 448² | 361.2 us | 1522.1 us | 4.21x | 357.0 us | 1516.7 us | 4.25x |
| 1 image 896² (4096 tok) | 75.9 us | 357.7 us | 4.71x | 72.5 us | 352.8 us | 4.87x |
| 4 images 896² | 258.4 us | 1351.9 us | 5.23x | 254.6 us | 1347.1 us | 5.29x |
| 1 image 1792² (16384 tok) | 904.4 us | 5200.8 us | 5.75x | 944.3 us | 5187.9 us | 5.49x |
| 8 mixed-size images (11136 tok) | 124.9 us | 610.0 us | 4.88x | 120.6 us | 606.1 us | 5.03x |
| video, 32 frames x 256 tok | 61.2 us | 62.1 us | 1.01x | 28.7 us | 57.8 us | 2.01x |

Qwen2.5-VL-7B ViT (16 heads, d=80; windows of 64 patches, 28 windowed + 4 full-attention blocks), per layer and per image:

| image | windowed layer fa4 / triton (eager) | full layer fa4 / triton (eager) | per image, eager: fa4 / triton | per image, ViT graph: fa4 / triton |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 448x448 (16 windows) | 62.6 / 37.2 us | 61.2 / 42.3 us | 2.00 / 1.21 ms | **0.38 / 0.55 ms** |
| 720p (84 windows) | 62.3 / 64.9 us | 138.5 / 783.8 us | 2.30 / 4.95 ms | 2.11 / 4.81 ms |
| 1080p (180 windows) | 147.5 / 150.6 us | 478.0 / 3725.6 us | 6.04 / 19.12 ms | 5.98 / 18.79 ms |
| 4K (700 windows) | 977.7 / 561.5 us | 7399.8 / 60559.9 us | 57.0 / 258.0 ms | 57.6 / 257.7 ms |

Where `fa4` loses: (a) eager calls on tiny inputs (a single image of ≤1024 tokens), where its ~60 us per-call host overhead exceeds the kernel time; the ViT CUDA graph removes it (448x448: 0.38 ms vs 0.55 ms per image), and SM100 already carries this trade-off with `fa4` as its default. (b) Very many 64-token windows (Qwen2.5-VL at 4K, 700 windows): the windowed layer is 1.7x slower than Triton because FA4's 128-row tiles are half empty; the full-attention layers more than make up for it (4.5x per image). A smaller Q tile for short segments would be a follow-up, not part of this PR.

**End to end, eager ViT** (Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, 1 GPU per server, c=1, `bench_serving --dataset-name image`, fresh images per run):

| request | triton_attn median TTFT | fa4 median TTFT |
|---|---|---|
| 1 image 4K (2 runs) | 943 / 1021 ms | 752 / 868 ms (−15–20%) |
| 1 image 1080p (3 interleaved runs) | 235 / 169 / 211 ms | 194 / 171 / 159 ms |

At 1080p the per-image attention saving (~13 ms) is below the run-to-run noise of host-side image preprocessing (medians of the same server swing by ~60 ms), so it is not claimed from this table. GLM-5.3-Flash (TP4, 24-layer d=64 ViT) is neutral end to end within noise. Concurrent image benchmarks (c=16/32) were dominated by host-side image preprocessing (the same configuration varied 1.8x between runs) and are not used.

**End to end with the ViT CUDA graph** (`SGLANG_VIT_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1`, Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, c=1, fresh images per run). Preprocessing noise only ever adds latency, so the per-request p25 (2 interleaved runs of 40 / 20 requests) tracks the floor better than the median:

| request | triton_attn + graph, p25 TTFT | fa4 + graph, p25 TTFT | difference | attention-only prediction (item 2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 image 448x448 | 38.3 / 38.6 ms | 38.9 / 38.3 ms | none | −0.2 ms |
| 1 image 1080p | 181.9 / 182.3 ms | 168.7 / 166.7 ms | −13 to −16 ms | −13 ms |
| 1 image 4K | 866.7 / 901.7 ms | 673.9 / 747.5 ms | −150 to −190 ms | −200 ms |

title: [HiSparse] fix: reject speculative decoding and mixed chunk at startup
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

`validate_hisparse` accepts two combinations that crash the scheduler on the first request:

- **Speculative decoding + HiSparse.** The draft worker's `HiSparseDSATokenToKVPool` never gets a HiSparse mapping registered, so the first draft extend dies in `translate_loc_to_hisparse_device`:
  `AttributeError: 'HiSparseDSATokenToKVPool' object has no attribute 'full_to_hisparse_device_index_mapping'`.
- **`--enable-mixed-chunk` + HiSparse.** Mixing a prefill into the HiSparse decode batch fails in `merge_batch`:
  `TypeError: can only concatenate list (not "NoneType") to list`.

Both were reproduced on a 4-layer DeepSeek-V3.2 config with dummy weights (one H200, greedy, `--disable-radix-cache`). The control arms are identical to each other, so each crash is specific to the combination:

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| no spec, no HiSparse | reference |
| HiSparse only | identical to reference |
| EAGLE/MTP only | identical to reference |
| EAGLE/MTP + HiSparse | scheduler crash on the first request |
| mixed chunk only (concurrent requests) | ok |
| mixed chunk + HiSparse | scheduler crash on the first mixed batch |

## Modifications

Reject both at startup with a clear error, until HiSparse supports them (speculative decoding is in progress in #40670 / #37771, which can drop the check).

## Accuracy Tests

- With this change the speculative + HiSparse launch above exits at startup with `ValueError: --enable-hisparse does not support speculative decoding yet.`
- `test_server_args.py`, `test_model_overrides.py`: 385 passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- No new unit tests; this change only adds straightforward startup validation.

title: [DeepSelect] Add page-table transform to top-k and tighten the layout contract
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> (auto generated by Claude)

Adds `topk_page_transform` to the DeepSelect JIT top-k: for int32 indices without values, each selected column `i` of row `r` is written as `page_table[r, i // page_size] * page_size + i % page_size` directly from the epilogue, so callers get KV slot indices without a separate transform kernel. The vendored kernels gain three small hooks, each marked `[SGLang]`.

Also in this PR:
- Rename `csrc/deepselect` to `csrc/deep_select` to follow upstream naming (first commit, pure rename).
- Tighten the layout contract and reject violations instead of working around them: input base and row stride 128-byte aligned (was 1024), output pointer and row stride 32-byte aligned with `topk * sizeof` a multiple of 32 bytes. The output staging copy (`kernel_output_index`) is removed.
- Python interface: `indices_type` defaults to int32, only `input` and `topk` are positional, signature checks raise instead of assert and run once per cached module.
- Rewrite `test_deep_select.py` as functional checks against `torch.topk`, with fewer JIT signatures to cut CI compile time.

Validated on H200 and B200: `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_deep_select.py` passes.

title: feat(kda): integrate FlashInfer prefill checkpoints
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

[FlashInfer #5021](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5021) (0.7.0) adds indexed, floor-aligned checkpoints to CuTe DSL KDA prefill, which SGLang needs for radix prefix caching.

## Modifications

- Opt-in `--linear-attn-prefill-backend flashinfer` for BF16, 128-dim safe-gate KDA on SM100/SM103.
- Map FlashInfer checkpoints to radix-cache track rows (FP32 state pools, padded gate/beta); write only radix-tracked checkpoints.
- KDA models pass raw beta logits in every phase. Kernel adapters own activation, without backend-dependent model flags or model mutation during backend construction. FlashInfer tensor validation runs during warmup.
- Call `flashinfer.kda.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cute-dsl")` directly. FlashInfer owns scheduling and workspace allocation; SGLang maps radix-cache checkpoint destinations once per tracked batch. Invalid scheduler/checkpoint metadata raises an assertion.
- Reject incompatible checkpoint intervals, TBO, and full prefill CUDA graphs at setup. FlashInfer validates safe gates during warmup. BCG keeps linear attention eager; verify uses its separately configured backend.
- Retain Triton fallback for a packed prefill containing only one token, which FlashInfer's current packed-prefill API excludes.

This PR leaves dependency pins unchanged; the current tree already pins FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1.

## Accuracy Tests

Historical default-selection experiment (reverted by `c0d8467478`; FlashInfer remains opt-in): pre-commit passed. The [registered CPU rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37808499136) passed all 10 tests on `a231d574ae`, after correcting the policy fixture to publish a resolved CUDA graph config. The [B200 rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37715933478) passed FlashInfer KDA kernel tests and GLM-5.3-Flash low-latency GSM8K on `70b968ef19`: score 0.932 over 500 questions. The server log confirms `decode=triton, prefill=flashinfer, verify=nv_cutedsl`. The follow-up commit changes only the unit fixture.

Previously reported on 8xGB300, FlashInfer 0.7.0: the original five KDA prefill cases, existing KDA decode/verify (11), and CuTe DSL KDA + GDN checkpoint smoke (2) passed.

The current GPU test file contains six checkpoint/layout cases and two numerical backend cases (tracked prefill and single-token fallback). The direct-call cleanup passes pre-commit and focused CPU checks: eight checked-in test methods, 22 raw-beta contract checks, six checkpoint harness cases exercising the production adapter with a substituted numerical kernel, and six metadata-hook cases. GPU imports and numerical kernels were isolated for these local CPU checks. The eight GPU cases passed on pre-rebase head `ae9847e073` on B300 (SM103), FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 and CUDA 13.0, in 207.87 seconds. The exact rebased-head rerun is reported below.

### Exact rebased-head GLM-5.3-Flash checks

Reran both prefix-cache methods on the **exact rebased head `706048f3fd`** (before the default-selection change), with the full upstream fix and no diagnostic patch: real `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` weights (revision `eb9eb208eb0d988989d07a6a12d0fdeb5f52574a`), **4xB300 / TP4**, BF16 KV and SSM caches, TileLang DSA, Triton decode, 16K prefill chunks, eager execution, and `--mamba-track-interval 256`. FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1 (Python TreeCore), Transformers 5.17.0. Both arms use `SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0` to compile the exercised GEMM shapes on demand; the initial exhaustive startup compilation was stopped before probe requests.

**Kernel/configuration checks:** 23 tests passed, including all eight FlashInfer KDA numerical/layout cases, in 229.46 seconds. Pre-commit and focused CPU contract/metadata checks also passed.

**Cold versus cached continuation:** score the same fixed 167-token continuation after 32,769 / 36K / 72K context tokens. All target scores are finite; inputs are identical between backends.

| KDA prefill | Context | Cold/cached absolute logprob difference mean / p90 / max | Warm/repeat mean | Cached tokens warm / repeat |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| triton | 32769 | 0.022187 / 0.000521 / 2.914499 | 0.017015 | 32768 / 32768 |
| triton | 36000 | 0.006804 / 0.000954 / 0.562500 | 0.003408 | 35840 / 35840 |
| triton | 72000 | 0.005175 / 0.000746 / 0.500000 | 0.003549 | 71936 / 71936 |
| flashinfer | 32769 | 0.009283 / 0.000480 / 1.046875 | 0.003289 | 32768 / 32768 |
| flashinfer | 36000 | 0.003019 / 0.000722 / 0.312500 | 0.003292 | 35840 / 35840 |
| flashinfer | 72000 | 0.003710 / 0.000662 / 0.346874 | 0.002871 | 71936 / 71936 |

**Branching corruption check from #42178:** cache an 8,320-token prefix; score copying a 167-token span from branch A before and after an unrelated branch B extends the shared prefix. Three different spans/seeds per backend.

| KDA prefill | Copy mean logprob before | After competing request | Second request cache hit |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| triton | -0.015645 | -0.016829 | 8192 |
| flashinfer | -0.015597 | -0.016357 | 8192 |

The pre-rebase controls dropped from approximately -0.02 to -1.35 after the competing request. The rebased runs retain high copy scores with both KDA prefill backends and resume at 8,192, keeping the pooled index group private. This reproducer no longer shows the large branching collapse.

Warm repeats and the aligned-boundary control are **not bit-exact** on GLM. The Triton aligned control has a 2.9145 maximum cold/cached difference and a 2.0505 maximum warm/repeat difference despite a small p90; these outliers preclude claiming exact cache parity. These measurements do not isolate the residual drift to a specific operator. HiCache host restore and current-head speed were not tested.

### GLM-5.3-Flash checks before rebase

2026-10-07, head `ae9847e073`, real GLM-5.3-Flash weights, 4xB300 TP4, BF16 KV/SSM caches, TileLang DSA, 16K prefill chunks, eager execution, Triton decode. FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1 (Python TreeCore), Transformers 5.17.0. Model revision `eb9eb208eb0d988989d07a6a12d0fdeb5f52574a`.

Cold versus cached scoring uses identical contexts and a fixed 167-token continuation. Values are absolute logprob difference mean / p90 / max.

| Layout / prefill | 36K | 72K |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| PR head, Triton | 0.0044 / 0.0006 / 0.312 | 0.0023 / 0.0004 / 0.178 |
| PR head, FlashInfer | 0.0081 / 0.0009 / 0.550 | 0.0043 / 0.0007 / 0.344 |
| Device fix, Triton | 0.0089 / 0.0004 / 0.595 | 0.0040 / 0.0008 / 0.314 |
| Device fix, FlashInfer | 0.0045 / 0.0007 / 0.312 | 0.0054 / 0.0005 / 0.500 |

The branching check warms a prefix ending inside a 256-token index group, scores copying a span from the first suffix, then rescoring follows a competing request with unrelated text. Values below average three different 167-token copy spans.

| Layout / prefill | Copy mean logprob before | After competing request | Second request cache hit |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PR head, Triton | -0.0189 | -1.3455 | 8320 |
| PR head, FlashInfer | -0.0169 | -1.3452 | 8320 |
| Device fix, Triton | -0.0158 | -0.0147 | 8192 |
| Device fix, FlashInfer | -0.0145 | -0.0159 | 8192 |

Before rebase, head `ae9847e073` lacked #42178. Both backends reproduced its pooled-index branching corruption; the device-cache portion of that fix, ported only into the isolated test checkout, removed the collapse. The PR has now been rebased onto main `7760d5264a`, which contains the full merged #42178 fix. The earlier diagnostic measurements below retain their original source provenance.

Warm repeats and the 32,768-token aligned-resume control are not bit-exact on GLM; residual small drift is not isolated to KDA. At 72K on the old layout, warm/repeat cache depths also differ (65,536 / 71,936). Fixed-layout arms use the required 256-token decode tracking interval; old-layout arms use 64. Probe requests generate zero tokens, and prefill tracking follows page/chunk geometry. HiCache host restore and latest-head speed were not tested.

### Historical Kimi K3 measurements

The following Kimi K3 results predate the current direct-call cleanup.

Kimi K3 real weights, 8xGB300, BF16 KV, DSpark: cold vs prefix-cache-resume logprobs over a fixed 167-token continuation (|Δlogprob| mean / p90 / max). Warm vs warm is bit-exact in all cases.

| Config | 36k ctx | 72k ctx |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DCP8, Triton prefill | 0.044 / 0.149 / 0.69 | 0.050 / 0.174 / 1.04 |
| DCP8, FlashInfer prefill | 0.043 / 0.147 / 0.55 | 0.055 / 0.215 / 0.61 |
| TP8, Triton prefill | 0.051 / 0.190 / 0.69 | 0.059 / 0.213 / 0.86 |

FlashInfer matches Triton. The drift is from chunk layout, not state restore: a resume on a cold chunk boundary (32768) is bit-exact.

## Speed Tests

These are historical measurements from the wrapper-based integration. The current direct API can read packed sequence offsets on the host to size its workspace and allocates that workspace within each call; performance and D2H behavior need remeasurement on the latest head.

Kimi K3 NVFP4 dummy weights, 8xGB300 TP8/DCP8, bs1, 131k in / 1k out, 95% prefix hit, A/B/A x10:

| Metric | Triton | FlashInfer |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Normal TTFT, median | 0.429 s | 0.411 s |
| Output throughput, median | 406.5 tok/s | 407.4 tok/s |
| KDA GPU time per layer (EXTEND trace) | 421 µs | 219 µs |
| KDA-associated D2H copies | 0 | 0 |

An intermittent ~6.7 s TTFT stall appears with both backends and is not attributed to KDA.

Kernel-only KDA prefill (checkpoints off), K3 shape on one TP8 rank (12 heads x 128), single GB300, bf16 in / fp32 state, median of 5 (ms). Backends that fall back to Triton at these lengths are omitted: `nvidia_kda` (needs >1 sequence), `flashkda` (caps at 2048 tokens/seq).

| Case | Triton | FlashInfer | ptx_kda | cutedsl |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16k | 1.18 | 0.87 | 0.72 | 1.51 |
| 32k | 2.09 | 1.37 | 1.13 | 2.67 |
| 64k | 3.95 | 2.38 | 1.94 | 4.94 |
| 128k, one sequence | 7.76 | 4.36 | 3.65 | 9.61 |
| 128k as 8x16k chunks | 3.82 | 1.18 | 2.66 | 7.52 |

FlashInfer is 1.3-1.8x Triton on a single sequence and 3.2x on the 8x16k shape chunked prefill actually issues, where it batches the sequences into one kernel. `ptx_kda` is ~20% faster on a single sequence but 2.3x slower on that chunked shape; it is also not measured here with checkpoints on, which its own fallback note says routes tracked batches to Triton. `cutedsl` cannot serve K3 at all (no safe gate, no interior checkpoints).

## Checklist

- [x] Format and code style checks
- [x] Add registered tests
- [x] Kernel-level accuracy and speed results
- [ ] Full Kimi K3 output parity with real weights
