title: [perf] [multi-lora] remove empty CTAs from fused LoRA expand and add split-K to shrink
author: kailash109
body:
## Summary

CSGMV launches empty tiles for smaller packed QKV expand slices and leaves parallelism unused in rank-32 shrink operations. Compact the expand grid using existing CPU slice offsets, and add opt-in split-K shrink with FP32 partials and a separate reduction.

## Changes

- Calls without CPU slice offsets retain the rectangular expand path with early returns for empty tiles.
- `SGLANG_ENABLE_LORA_CSGMV_SPLIT_K=1` enables the existing BF16 rank-32 dispatch policy; it remains off by default. Deterministic inference retains the original shrink accumulation order because split-K changes rounding.
- Treat the partial-buffer row stride as a runtime parameter so different token counts reuse compiled split-K kernels.
- Use `split_k=None` for automatic dispatch, preserve explicit positive values, and reject invalid values before deterministic fallback.
- Keep one kernel benchmark and consolidate regressions into the existing CUDA-graph test script.

## Validation

Validated on H200 at `a7deef700821501c37fd1de266d4f1f42848d23a`:

- Existing CI entry point `python test/registered/kernels/ops/lora/test_chunked_sgmv_cuda_graph.py -f`: **8 tests passed**. Coverage includes FP32 partials, ragged and empty slices, output stride, mixed ranks, CUDA-graph metadata replay, explicit split factors, and deterministic fallback.
- The extended dispatch regression fails on the old argument logic when explicit split 4 is overwritten by 8.
- Eager token counts 7, 8, 9, and 17 pass the FP32 numerical oracle and reuse one compiled producer and reducer each.
- Full `pre-commit run --all-files` passed before both fix commits.

## Performance

The contributor's [corrected serving results](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41951#issuecomment-5925662323) report approximately 9.5–11.6% throughput improvement. These measurements predate the cleanup commits; no new serving or performance measurements are claimed for this head.

title: [Diffusion][MiniMax-H3] Fix int32 offset overflow in SubBlock router kernels
author: saatwiknagpal
body:
## Motivation

Without sequence parallelism (e.g. MiniMax-H3 on one GPU), each SubBlock attention call routes all heads; Ulysses SP would shard them across ranks. The pool (`S*H*D`), score (`L*Gq*Gk`) and top-k (`row*G`) kernels then compute element offsets past 2^31 in int32, which wrap and crash with an illegal memory access (Xid 13).

Boundary on B200, D=128: at S=491,520, H=34 passes and H=35 crashes; at H=56, S=299,584 passes and S=299,648 crashes.

## Modifications

Compute the overflowing offsets in int64: the program ids in `_pool_kernel` and `_topk_kernel`, and the per-head output base pointer in `_score_kernel` (its per-element offsets stay int32). Add one regression test that fails before the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

- At H=34 (where stock works), scores and index are bitwise equal to stock.
- With the fix at 491,520x56 and 299,648x56, the last heads' scores and index are bitwise equal to the same heads routed alone. Pooled values match torch (max abs err 0.002).
- `test_subblock_sparse_attention.py`: the new test fails on stock (illegal memory access) and passes with the fix. All other tests pass.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B200, mean +- std over 8 interleaved fresh-process runs of 100 reps each (ms). The pool and top-k kernels are unchanged within 0.001 ms.

| S, H | score kernel, stock | score kernel, fix | `route`, stock | `route`, fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 491,520, 14 | 19.677 +- 0.004 | 19.732 +- 0.008 (+0.28%) | 25.47 +- 0.05 | 25.54 +- 0.09 |
| 491,520, 7 | 9.828 +- 0.002 | 9.852 +- 0.004 (+0.24%) | 12.80 +- 0.08 | 12.78 +- 0.06 |
| 98,304, 56 | 3.192 +- 0.001 | 3.198 +- 0.001 (+0.19%) | 4.522 +- 0.001 | 4.543 +- 0.028 |

End to end, MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA 15 s at 1312x736 on 4xB200 (sparse, warm runs): 232.1 s and 232.0 s without the fix vs 232.1 s with it.

With this fix, the 1-GPU crash is gone. A 15 s H3 generation on one B200 then runs out of memory in the attention path; #41985 fixes that separately.

## Motivation

On gfx950, the wo_a batched gemm always launches with one fixed kernel config. That config was tuned for small M (M <= 64), so it gets slow as M grows.

title: [AMD][V4.1][*/N] Greedy dspark draft/accept under SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN
author: 1am9trash
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

co-authored-by: @kkHuang-amd 

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

When `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` is set, dspark overwrites `correct_len` with the simulated value right after verify. But the draft and accept steps still go through the full sampling path, and most of that result is thrown away. The only thing we still need from it is the bonus token, which should keep following the request's temperature.

```python
# python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_verify.py
# sampling accept
correct_len, bonus, cap_trim_lens = accept_draft_tokens(
    ...
)
# correct_len is overwritten right away
if self._simulate_acc_len > 0:
    correct_len = self._simulated_correct_len(
        bs=bs, dtype=correct_len.dtype, device=correct_len.device
    )
```

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

All changes only take effect on HIP with `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` set. 
No impact on the NV code path.

- **Accept**: For non-greedy requests, draft softmax, target softmax, and rejection sampling are no longer run. All requests take AcceptGreedy only.
- **Draft**: With `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_GREEDY` on (default), draft temperature sampling is no longer run for requests without grammar, penalties, top-p, top-k, or min-p. Other requests are unchanged.
- **Bonus**: For those draft requests, the bonus token is now temperature-sampled from the target-logit row at the simulated `correct_len`.
- **Env var gate:** adds `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_GREEDY` (default on) to turn off the greedy draft/accept path for temperature-only requests.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

- Unit test `test_dspark_simulated_bonus.py` passed.
- GSM8K (without simulation, on top of main): 0.906.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: [AMD] gfx950 small-batch MoE: expert-count gate for the small sort and FP8 block-scale small-M kernel
author: chuyeh
body:
## Motivation

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 on MI355X is slower than B200 at low concurrency in the AgentX benchmark ([InferenceX PR #3602](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3602)). One factor is the MoE sort from #36559: past its compact range, its distributed kernel scans every 64-expert chunk per pair, so with Qwen3.5's 513 experts it is slower than AITER's sort for mid-size decode batches (6 to 23 tokens). At TP8 with 16 verify tokens, going back to AITER's sort saves 1.7 ms per decode cycle.

This PR does two things:

1. Fix the slowdown: past the compact range, #36559's distributed kernel is only used up to 256 experts, and larger models go back to AITER. MiniMax-M3 (129 experts), which the kernel was written for, keeps it because it is faster there.
2. Add FP8 block-scale support to the #40204 small-M MoE kernel, which needs no sort and is much faster at small batches but only supported MXFP4.

With this PR, the interactivity improves by about 20% at concurrency 1 and 4.

## Modifications

- `moe_sorting_small.py`: past the compact kernel's range (`min(64, 2 * block_size)` (token, expert) pairs), the distributed kernel only runs for up to 256 experts; above that, the sort and the fused MXFP8 quantization go back to AITER (+13 / -3).
- `smallm_moe.hip`: `p1_body` / `p2_body` take an `F8` template flag. Shuffled FP8 weights have the same byte layout as fp4x2, so the load path is shared. e4m3 is converted to bf16 at scale 1.0 and each 128x128 block's fp32 scale is applied to the partial sum (`cvt_scalef32_pk_bf16_fp8` only applies the scale's exponent). New kernels cover TP4 (intermediate 256) and TP8 (intermediate 128); the MXFP4 kernels are unchanged.
- `smallm_moe_gfx950/__init__.py`: takes the FP8 path for shuffled `float8_e4m3fn` `w13` / `w2` with contiguous fp32 block scales, up to 20 tokens at TP4 and 48 at TP8. `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_MOE=0` still turns the kernel off.
- `moe_runner/aiter.py`: passes `w13_scale` / `w2_scale` to `smallm_moe_supported` (+2 lines).
- Tests (MI35x suite): `TestSmallMMoeFp8Gfx950` checks both shapes against a dequantized reference at 1 / 3 / 8 tokens and the cap, and that cap+1, per-channel or non-contiguous scales, and unshuffled weights fall back. New `test_moe_sorting_small.py` compares the sort and the fused MXFP8 quant with AITER on the compact path (Qwen3.5 shape) and the distributed path (MiniMax-M3 shape, 13 to 51 tokens), and checks the fallback at 513 experts.

## Accuracy Tests

All runs use image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260927` (same image as `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm` with that tag), InferenceX recipe flags, GSM8K 1319 questions.

| Model | Setup | Baseline | This PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` | TP4, real draft acceptance, `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k` | 0.933 | 0.941 |
| `amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2` (sort change) | TP2, lm-eval 5-shot, thinking off | 0.977 | 0.979 |

The FP8 kernel's rel L2 against the dequantized reference is at most 7.4e-4 over 5 seeds in the unit test. The sort output matches AITER's layout in every path, so the sort change only affects speed.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

### Kernel microbenchmarks

MI355X, one GPU, CUDA graph replay, Qwen3.5-397B shapes (`E=513`, 11 slots per token, hidden 4096).

FP8 MoE layer, AITER (`per_128x128`) vs the FP8 small-M kernel, in µs:

| Tokens | TP4 AITER | TP4 kernel | Change | TP8 AITER | TP8 kernel | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 61.3 | 26.6 | −57% | 42.3 | 22.7 | −46% |
| 4 | 66.5 | 43.4 | −35% | 46.1 | 30.1 | −35% |
| 8 | 74.0 | 63.7 | −14% | 57.6 | 41.4 | −28% |
| 16 | 106.3 | 97.5 | −8% | 75.3 | 60.4 | −20% |
| 20 | 117.3 | 115.3 | −2% (cap) | 77.3 | 68.7 | −11% |
| 24 | 130.1 | 133.1 | AITER used | 84.3 | 78.0 | −7% |

TP8 caps, 60 layers rotated so the weights are not cache resident:

| Tokens | AITER | Kernel | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 24 | 68.7 | 65.2 | −5% |
| 28 | 78.2 | 75.8 | −3% |
| 32 | 83.5 | 82.9 | ~0 |
| 36 | 119.0 | 92.0 | −23% |
| 48 | 124.6 | 111.6 | −10% (cap) |

AITER moves to a slower configuration from 36 tokens, so the TP8 cap is 48 rather than 32.

MoE sort past the compact range, in µs, block size as AITER picks it. MXFP rows include the MXFP8 quant in both arms (AITER runs it as a second launch). Up to the compact range the sort is unchanged, and the FP8 small-M path does not use the sort:

| Model | Tokens | Pairs | AITER | #36559 | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5 MXFP4 (sort + quant) | 7 | 77 | 10.5 | 10.3 | 10.5 |
| | 16 | 176 | 11.7 | 15.9 | 11.7 |
| | 23 | 253 | 13.5 | 15.5 | 13.5 |
| Qwen3.5 FP8 (sort only) | 16 | 176 | 6.9 | 15.7 | 6.9 |
| | 23 | 253 | 6.8 | 15.4 | 6.8 |
| MiniMax-M3 MXFP8 (`E=129`, top-4 + shared, sort + quant) | 16 | 80 | 12.0 | 8.1 | 8.1 |
| | 35 | 175 | 21.2 | 13.1 | 13.1 |
| | 51 | 255 | 24.6 | 13.0 | 13.0 |

AITER picks block size 32 for the MXFP shapes and mostly 16 for Qwen3.5 FP8, where the compact kernel covers only 1 to 2 tokens.

### AgentX benchmark

Setup:

- Hardware: MI355X, TP4.
- Model and recipe: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` with the InferenceX recipe `qwen3.5-fp8-mi355x-sglang-agentic`, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260927`.
- Server flags: as in the recipe. FP8 KV cache, EAGLE 3 / 1 / 4 with simulated acceptance 3.39, admission and decode CUDA graph batch at 2x concurrency.
- Client: the CI AgentX command, `aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp` on `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126_256k`, 3600 s per run.
- Order: one run at a time on the same GPUs (this PR c1, baseline c1, baseline c4, this PR c4).

Baseline is the image as shipped: AITER's FP8 MoE with #36559's sort (`SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_MOE=0`). With this PR, every decode batch at these concurrencies runs the FP8 small-M kernel and skips the sort, so the gain here comes from the kernel.

Concurrency 1:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ITL p50 / p90 (ms) | 3.69 / 4.07 | 3.01 / 3.50 | −18% / −14% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 389 / 861 | 373 / 859 | −4% / ~0 |
| Requests completed in 3600 s | 557 | 628 | +13% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 150 | 177 | +18% |
| Interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 271 / 283 | 332 / 349 | +23% / +23% |

Concurrency 4:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ITL p50 / p90 (ms) | 4.10 / 5.32 | 3.44 / 4.34 | −16% / −18% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 551 / 1096 | 519 / 947 | −6% / −14% |
| Requests completed in 3600 s | 926 | 992 | +7% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 243 | 263 | +8% |
| Interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 244 / 278 | 291 / 333 | +19% / +20% |

Each EAGLE verify pass sends 4 tokens per running request through the MoE. At TP4 the kernel therefore covers running batches of 5 or fewer, which is concurrency 4 and below here; concurrency 8 and up mostly uses AITER.

### Decode step time

Time for one EAGLE draft + verify cycle at a fixed batch size, same server flags and simulated acceptance.

TP4, image as shipped vs this PR, mean of two runs with the GPU sets swapped, in ms:

| Batch size | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 11.89 | 9.51 | −20% |
| 4 | 16.51 | 13.08 | −21% |
| 8 | 16.35 | 16.41 | ~0 (past the cap) |

TP8, this PR with `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_MOE=1` vs `0` (kernel vs AITER's MoE and sort), two runs per arm in ABBA order. Run-to-run noise is up to 0.23 ms:

| Batch size | Verify tokens | Change per cycle |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 16 | −0.78 ms |
| 6 | 24 | −0.51 ms |
| 7 | 28 | −0.30 ms |
| 8 | 32 | −0.07 ms (noise) |

With the kernel off at batch size 4 (176 pairs), #36559's sort takes 33.00 ms per cycle and this PR's 31.28 ms, the 1.7 ms in Motivation.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit guide.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [Kernel] Use Cake softmax for qualified SM103 sampling workloads
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Large-vocabulary, small-batch stochastic sampling spends about 64 us per BS1
decode step in Torch softmax on the measured GB300. Route the qualified domain
through FlashInfer's Cake Blackwell softmax while keeping sampling/filtering in
SGLang. On Qwen3.5-4B, the final same-GPU comparison improves output throughput
by 2.48% at concurrency1 and 1.09% at concurrency64.

**Dependency limitation:** SGLang currently pins FlashInfer0.7.0.post1, which
does not contain this kernel. This draft keeps the dependency pin and detects
the Cake module before enabling the path. The released wheel retains Torch;
the results below require FlashInfer `be92cab02e2818ac1a54e7181d15595a61342a20`
in both the baseline and candidate. This is not an out-of-box gain on the pinned
wheel. Submitting as a draft for integration/dependency review.

## Modifications

- Add a lazy `sglang.kernels.cake_kernels` ownership directory and a thin
  forwarding adapter to the public `flashinfer.sampling.softmax` API, following
  the namespace separation used by `kda_kernels`.
- Register `sampling.softmax` with the existing FlashInfer backend; enable it
  for CUDA SM103, contiguous FP32 `[B,V]`, B1–64, V128256–262144 divisible by8,
  and an installed Cake softmax module. Keep Torch elsewhere, including
  deterministic inference. No new environment variables or dependency changes.
- Preserve temperature scaling, the probability buffer copy, joint top-k/top-p
  filtering, RNG and the existing logprob paths. Cake's combined sampler has
  different filtering semantics and is not used here.

## Accuracy Tests

SGLang base: `3b6d37a56e8dfacc14a5f412886c2f1adb0ca523`; GB300 SM103/152SM,
PyTorch2.13.0+cu130, CUDA13, TP1. Research harnesses remain outside the repository;
no repository test files are added or modified.

- Existing `test/registered/unit/kernels/test_kernels_namespace.py`: 59 passed.
- 34 operator configurations across two matrices (32 unique
  shapes): B1/2/4/7/16/31/63/64, vocab32000/128256/151936/201088/248320/262144.
  Each configuration checks normal, wide, masked, one-valid-token and equal
  logits against FP64 softmax: finite, top1 equality and atol1e-7/rtol1e-5 all
  pass. The 32K timing regression is excluded by the runtime guard.
- Qwen3.5-4B: teacher-forced probabilities on 520 identical histories at BS1/64
  preserve top1 sets and pass logprob comparisons (maximum absolute difference
  3.82e-6). Checks include top128, 512 fixed vocabulary IDs and selected tokens.
  This exercises the changed stochastic branch. Independently sampled histories
  are not treated as deterministic accuracy references.
- Greedy sanity: 65/65 continuations and logprobs identical; 20-example GSM8K,
  thinking disabled, 18/20 for both arms. Greedy bypasses the changed branch,
  so these checks supplement rather than replace probability validation.
- Real released FlashInfer0.7.0.post1 and current-main guard probes pass,
  including CPU, unsupported dtype/shape and noncontiguous inputs; fallback
  outputs are bitwise Torch-equivalent. Ruff0.15.1, isort and diff checks pass.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen3.5-4B revision `851bf6e806efd8d0a36b00ddf55e13ccb7b8cd0a`;
same physical GPU, same FI revision, only sampler dispatch differs.
`sglang.bench_serving`, random-ids, nominal1024 input / exactly256 output,
temperature0.8, top_p0.9, fixed seed, cache flushed between windows.
Concurrency1 uses8 requests/window; concurrency64 uses128. Five measured windows
per arm after one warmup for each concurrency. Every request completes, output
lengths are256, and server-reported input-length vectors match between arms.
Random token IDs are decoded to text by this benchmark's default, so actual
server input lengths differ from the nominal1024. The reported metric is output
token throughput, not input throughput inferred from nominal lengths.

| Concurrency | Torch output tok/s | Cake output tok/s | Change | Median TPOT ms, Torch -> Cake |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 386.49 | 396.06 | +2.48% | 2.430 -> 2.368 |
| 64 | 7700.98 | 7784.64 | +1.09% | 5.349 -> 5.296 |

Final per-window output throughput ranges: concurrency1 Torch384.46–386.99,
Cake395.12–396.28; concurrency64 Torch7678.77–7736.34,
Cake7777.49–7799.73. Earlier same-GPU A1/B1/B2/A2 blocks are retained locally:
A1 was slower than A2/A3 and is not pooled into the headline. The final guarded
B3/A3 comparison above agrees with the earlier A2/B arms. This is a measured
single-model result, not a universal gain or a cross-device confidence claim.

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --tp 1 --random-seed 123 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.50 --context-length 32768 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-running-requests 64 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer

python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B \
  --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 \
  --random-range-ratio 1 --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 8 \
  --seed 123 --temperature 0.8 --top-p 0.9 --flush-cache \
  --warmup-requests 0 --disable-tqdm --output-details --output-file result.jsonl
# For concurrency64, use --max-concurrency 64 --num-prompts 128.
```

Separate decode profiles show eight softmax launches per capture:

| Batch | Torch softmax mean | Cake softmax mean |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 64.352us | 4.620us |
| 64 | 75.900us | 31.664us |

The candidate kernel is `kernel_flashinfer_blackwell_softmax_cached_c16_t8`.
Profiles use short prompts to verify dispatch; kernel durations exclude the
output copy and are not used as E2E timing. Unprofiled microbenchmarks include
the copy in both arms. Unsupported model/attention/Cake families are outside
this PR.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and static checks for changed files.
- [ ] Add unit tests (existing tests run; no repository test changes in this draft).
- [x] Document adapter ownership, guards and dependency limitation.
- [x] Provide operator correctness, model probability and performance evidence.
- [x] Keep a thin namespace adapter and existing backend provenance.

## Motivation

Two MoE fixes for DSV4.1-Flash When running it with `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` on ROCm.
1) Issue: Resolve the shared-expert requant accuracy lost
2) Perf opt: Fused decode routing kernels into one.

## Modifications

- On ROCm, requantize the FP8 shared expert to MXFP4 with round-to-nearest-even (aiter `dynamic_mxfp4_quant` scaling). The old cast rounded midpoints toward zero, which shrank the shared expert by ~5%. Other platforms keep the existing requant (output unchanged).

- Use aiter's multi-phase MoE sorting for small batches via `SGLANG_AITER_MOE_SORTING_DISPATCH_POLICY` (default 2; 0 restores aiter's auto policy).

GSM8K 1319 5-shot, TP2 with fusion: 0.891 -> 0.906 (3 runs), matching unfused (0.904 / 0.905). With the router change: 0.897 / 0.901 / 0.900.

title: [AMD][V4.1][*/N] Build DSpark draft metadata inside the CUDA graph on ROCm
author: kkHuang-amd
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

On MI355X (DSV4.1-Flash TP2 + DSpark), the draft replay rebuilds its attention metadata on the host before every step, right on the critical path after the spec sync (~0.4 ms at c1).

## Modifications

- Follow the existing `DSV4RawVerifyMetadata` pattern: pass the raw inputs to the draft graph and expand the metadata inside the captured graph.
- Gated by `SGLANG_HIP_DSPARK_DRAFT_RAW_METADATA` (default on for ROCm).

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K 1319 5-shot, TP2, real acceptance: 0.903 / 0.908 / 0.901. Accept length is unchanged (3.381 vs 3.386).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: [AMD][V4.1][*/N] OPUS sparse prefill on gfx950 through layout conversion
author: RolaoDenthu
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
In gfx950, DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill attention runs on the aiter_sparse decode kernel, the only aiter kernel that reads V4.1's radix KV cache as stored. aiter's OPUS sparse prefill kernel (`pa_sparse_prefill_opus`) is 1.4-1.7x faster over a 16384-token chunk, but it expects a different layout:
| | V4.1 radix cache | OPUS input |
|---|---|---|
| KV rows | fp8 nope + scales + bf16 rope packed into 584 B per token, in 256-token pages; SWA and compressed history in separate pools | contiguous bf16 rows of 512, one buffer per source |
| Index lists | fixed width per query, -1 padded | CSR (indices + indptr), every entry a valid row |

This PR converts V4.1's layout into OPUS's on the fly: it dequantizes the rows a chunk reads into bf16 workspaces and turns the index lists into CSR. V4.1 layers share their compressed KV and top-k with a few source layers, so most of this conversion runs once per source layer rather than once per layer, and it costs under 5% of the attention time. 
It is opt-in with `SGLANG_OPT_HIP_OPUS_SPARSE_PREFILL=1`.


## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
- Add an OPUS prefill path for DSV4.1 on gfx950, behind `SGLANG_OPT_HIP_OPUS_SPARSE_PREFILL` (default off). It converts the radix cache layout for the kernel: fp8 rows to bf16, -1 padded index lists to CSR. Layers that share a source layer's KV / top-k reuse its conversion.
- Fall back to the decode kernel for drafts, batches under 1024 tokens, context parallel, SWA bounded replay, or very long compressed history.
- Fill the raw top-k buffers with -1, so OPUS never reads a stale index.
- Add `test_dsv41_opus_sparse_prefill_hip.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

title: [Gemma4][Attention] Enable Gemma4 FA4 on SM90 with head-dim 512 support

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
Enable opt-in FlashAttention 4 serving for Gemma4 on Hopper GPUs.
Gemma4 combines sliding-window attention with head dimension 256 and global attention with head dimension 512. The existing SM90 FA4 implementation does not support the latter, preventing Gemma4 from using this backend.

## Modifications

- Add a generalized SM90 decode split heuristic that avoids splitting short KV spans when sufficient query/head blocks are available.
- Allow Gemma4 to select --attention-backend fa4; retain Triton as the default.
- Add compact image-range metadata and an FA4 mask callback for image-token bidirectional attention. Image spans crossing prefill chunks retain the existing Triton causal fallback.
- Extend the existing test_flash_attention_4.py with SM90 regression coverage.

title: [Spec][MegaMoE] Let the speculative draft choose its own W4A4 MXFP4 MegaMoE MMA type
author: nvpohanh
body:
[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

`--enable-w4a4-mxfp4-megamoe` is read process-wide, so a speculative draft whose MoE layers run through MegaMoE always uses the same MMA type as the target. For example, the DSpark head bundled in `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813` has 3 stages x 384 MXFP4 routed experts. `DSparkWorkerV2` builds and runs it under the target's `megamoe` A2A backend, and `--speculative-moe-a2a-backend` is ignored for DSpark. Users therefore cannot run the target with W4A4 (`mxf4xmxf4`) while keeping the draft on W4A8 (`fp8xfp4`), or the reverse.

## Modifications

- New tri-state server arg `--speculative-enable-w4a4-mxfp4-megamoe` / `--no-speculative-enable-w4a4-mxfp4-megamoe` (`spec` namespace). When unset (default `None`), the draft inherits `--enable-w4a4-mxfp4-megamoe`, so existing deployments are unchanged. This mirrors how `--speculative-moe-runner-backend` / `--speculative-moe-a2a-backend` inherit from the target.
- `draft_model_build_scope()` now also applies the draft's value to `exec.moe.enable_w4a4_mxfp4_megamoe` while the draft is constructed. It uses the same scoped config-bag override it already applies to `boundary_reduction`. Every draft worker (DSpark, DFlash, EAGLE/MTP, multi-layer EAGLE, frozen-KV MTP, standalone) builds its draft inside this scope.
- `FusedMoE` pins the choice at construction (`_mega_moe_w4a4`). `_mega_moe_mma_type(experts)` reads it from the layer, so weight repacking (`build_mega_moe_experts_weights`, `Mxfp4MoEMethod`), the symmetric-buffer key, and the forward kernel all use the layer's own MMA type after the build scope exits. `_mega_moe_mma_type` requires the layer and `_get_mega_moe_symm_buffer` requires `mma_type`, so no caller can fall back to the process-wide flag. Kimi K3's MegaMoE forward now passes its layer's MMA type to the buffer lookup as well.
- Help text and docs row in `server_arguments.mdx`, including the memory cost of a draft value that differs from the target.

Mixed configurations allocate one additional DeepGEMM MegaMoE symmetric buffer, because the buffer cache is keyed by MMA type (see memory numbers below).

## Accuracy Tests

Setup: 8x B300 (SM103), `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` (2026-10-01) with this branch on `PYTHONPATH` (head `b71c8568b2`, base `5733bcaad3`), `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813` (HF `72e1d32`). The recipe is the cookbook section 3.6 DEP8 DSpark + MegaMoE W4A4 command without the HiCache flags, which are unrelated to this change, run on B300 instead of B200:

```bash
SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=8320 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 8 --attn-dp-size 8 --enable-dp-lm-head --ep-size 8 \
  --moe-a2a-backend megamoe --enable-w4a4-mxfp4-megamoe \
  --enable-deepseek-v4-fp4-indexer --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune --mem-fraction-static 0.88 \
  --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.02 --chunked-prefill-size 49152 \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 6 \
  [--no-speculative-enable-w4a4-mxfp4-megamoe]   # arm B only

python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 1319 --parallel 128   # run twice per server
```

| | A: new flag unset (target + draft W4A4) | B: `--no-speculative-enable-w4a4-mxfp4-megamoe` (target W4A4, draft W4A8) |
|---|---|---|
| Resolved `speculative_enable_w4a4_mxfp4_megamoe` | `None` | `False` |
| Target MoE layers (61) built with | `mxf4xmxf4` | `mxf4xmxf4` |
| DSpark MoE stages (3) built with | `mxf4xmxf4` | `fp8xfp4` |
| MegaMoE symmetric buffers | 1 (`mxf4xmxf4`) | 2 (`mxf4xmxf4`, plus `fp8xfp4` with the draft's FP8 shared expert fused) |
| GSM8K accuracy, run 1 / run 2 (1319 q) | 0.948 / 0.946 | 0.945 / 0.944 |
| DSpark accept length, mean over 8 DP ranks, run 1 / run 2 | 4.347 / 4.342 | 4.349 / 4.348 |
| GSM8K output throughput, run 2 (tok/s) | 2686 | 2673 |
| `max_total_num_tokens` | 14,749,184 | 14,748,672 |
| Free memory on GPU0 after draft verify graph capture | 31.16 GB | 23.21 GB |

The MMA-type and buffer rows come from a temporary debug print in `build_mega_moe_experts_weights` / `_get_mega_moe_symm_buffer`; that print is not part of this PR. Arm A matches the pre-PR behavior: one buffer, and every MoE layer on `mxf4xmxf4`.

**Memory note:** the mixed configuration allocates a second DeepGEMM MegaMoE symmetric buffer, about 7.8 GiB per GPU at `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=8320` for V4-Pro. It is allocated lazily during draft CUDA-graph capture, after the KV pool is sized. KV capacity is therefore unchanged, but post-capture headroom drops by that amount, so lower `--mem-fraction-static` if capture runs out of memory.

### Unit tests

Run in the same container on the B300 node at `b71c8568b2`. All pass except `TestDcpCommBackendDefault::test_a5_npu_supports_dcp` in `test_server_args.py`, which fails the same way on base `5733bcaad3` and is unrelated (NPU DCP).
- `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_mega_moe_deepgemm_api.py`: new `test_draft_layers_keep_their_own_w4a4_choice` builds real `FusedMoE` layers inside and outside `draft_model_build_scope`. It fails (`'mxf4xmxf4' != 'fp8xfp4'`) when `_mega_moe_mma_type` reads the process-wide flag instead of the layer's pinned value.
- `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py`: new `test_speculative_w4a4_mxfp4_megamoe_is_tri_state` checks unset -> `None` (inherit), `--speculative-enable-...` -> `True`, `--no-speculative-enable-...` -> `False`.
- `test_server_args_namespaces.py`, `test_runtime_context_config_bags.py`, `test_moe_runner_extensions.py`: pass.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not a performance change by itself. The accept-length and throughput rows above show that W4A8 for the DSpark draft does not change accept length or GSM8K accuracy on this workload. The flag lets users trade the draft's W4A4 speedup for W4A8 numerics, or the reverse, without touching the target.

title: [Metrics] Label scheduler stage wall time by sampled forward overlap
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

`sglang:scheduler_stage_seconds_total` already splits scheduler-loop wall time into exclusive CPU stages, but it cannot say whether a stage ran while a forward pass was in flight or while the GPU sat idle. That is the first question when deciding which CPU-side scheduler cost is worth optimizing: stage time that overlaps a forward is mostly hidden, stage time with no forward in flight is exposed latency.

## Modifications

- Add a `forward_overlap` label to `sglang:scheduler_stage_seconds_total`, sampled from the forward timing events the reporter already records, at both endpoints of each exclusive stage span:

  ```text
                   end inactive   end active
  start inactive   none           partial
  start active     partial        full
  ```

  `none` also covers disabled or unavailable timing (no observed overlap, not confirmed GPU idle). These are endpoint estimates, not exact overlapped/exposed seconds: `full` can span a GPU gap and `none` can span an entire forward. Summing over the label recovers the previous per-stage totals, so existing dashboards keep working by aggregating it away.
- `DeviceTimer.is_active()` answers the sampling query without blocking, reusing the forward events the timer already records and caching completed events instead of polling them again. A later queued forward cannot hide an earlier active one. Sampling stays disabled under PDMux, where event polling across green-context streams is not validated; forward timing itself is unchanged.
- `record_scheduler_active(event_ns)` takes the monotonic timestamp of the event that ended idle. A successful `recv_requests` is active from the receive start (empty polls stay idle), delayed events are clamped to the still-unaccounted window, and the forward-occupancy idle window follows the accounting delta so the two cannot disagree. `record_scheduler_idle()` stays argument-free and samples the current time.

No new CUDA events, device waits, or scheduling-order changes.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: metrics labelling only, no change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Each exclusive stage span gains at most two nonblocking `torch.cuda.Event.query()` calls, and only while a forward interval is pending; completed events are not polled again. No throughput change is expected.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit): ruff, ruff-format, isort, codespell and the registered-test lint scripts pass on the changed files.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests): `test_scheduler_stage_metrics.py` covers the per-span overlap labels and the queued/active/completed interval query; `test_forward_pass_metrics.py` covers event-timestamp clamping, a receive that crosses the reporting deadline, and the idle-window delta; `test_metrics.py` checks every exported stage sample carries a valid `forward_overlap` value. Locally: `test_scheduler_stage_metrics.py` (7), `test_forward_pass_metrics.py` (19), `test_scheduler_pause_generation.py` (25), `test_disagg_idle_step_counters.py` (12) and `kv_canary/test_self_unit_violation.py` (9) pass.
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations): the new label is described in the counter's own documentation string.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results: not applicable, see above.

title: [CP] GLM-5.3-Flash Prefill CP implemented on layer boundaries
author: Fridge003
body:
## Summary

Based on main after #42036, #42038, and #42041 merged. This PR includes the GLM-5.3-Flash prefill-CP implementation, cookbook usage, and B200 acceptance coverage previously in #42045.

LayerSplit cache sharding method is not included in this PR.

## Validation

### CP + MTP accuracy after review fixes (2026-10-08 UTC)

Validated on `glm53-dev-v2`, **4 × NVIDIA B300**, with the launch arguments from `TestGLM53FlashB200ContextParallel` in `test/registered/cp/test_glm53_flash_cp.py` (local model snapshot/host/port substituted). DSA interleave CP4, KDA/MoE/dense TP4, EP1, native EAGLE MTP **5 steps / top-k 1 / 6 draft tokens**, multimodal enabled, no LayerSplit.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| AIME26, all 30 questions × 16 repeats | **94.17% mean pass@1 (452 / 480)** |
| AIME26 majority@16 / pass@16 | 100% / 100% |
| AIME26 length-truncated / request errors | **0 / 0** |
| Registered GSM8K, 500 examples / 20 shots | **93.8% (469 / 500)**; passes ≥93% |
| GSM8K average speculative acceptance length | **4.1221**; passes >4.0 |
| Registered red/blue image-input checks | Passed before AIME26 and after GSM8K |

AIME26 used **sgl-eval 0.1.2**, reasoning enabled (`--thinking --chat-template-kwarg enable_thinking=true`), **temperature=1, top_p=1, max_tokens=300000**, and client concurrency 64. All 480 responses ended with `stop` and had nonempty reasoning. Seven unparsed/missing final answers remain in the denominator. One complete run, with no excluded samples or cherry-picked retries. The server resolved max-running-requests=48 and chunked-prefill-size=16384. GSM8K acceptance was recorded after its cache/metrics reset, not taken from the AIME26 workload.

Model snapshot: `eb9eb208eb0d988989d07a6a12d0fdeb5f52574a`. Tested runtime source: `0fcf9d3e4a`; head `79f7c61075` adds only a main merge of CI orchestration changes, with identical Python/model/test code. SHA-256 verification covered all 4,259 tracked Python files. Isolated runtime: Torch 2.14.1 / CUDA 13.0, sglang-kernel 0.4.9, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, Transformers 5.17.0.

The historical CP-only result below (455/480) is not a paired same-revision/runtime baseline; the three-answer difference does not by itself establish an MTP regression. These are **B300 devbox results, not B200 CI results**. Raw responses, commands, runtime metadata, and independently recomputed audits are retained locally. The validation server has been stopped and all four GPUs released.

### CP vs TP P50 TTFT (2026-10-07)

Both arms use native EAGLE/MTP **5 steps / top-k 1 / 6 draft tokens**, TP4, MoE/dense TP4, EP1, TRT-LLM DSA, FP8 KV, and multimodal serving enabled (no `--language-only`). CP adds only `--enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave --attn-cp-size 4`: DSA runs CP4 while KDA and MoE remain TP4. Both use `--chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 16384 --max-running-requests 128 --random-seed 42`, at historical revision `ab2ba1e197` with Torch 2.13.0+cu130, sglang-kernel 0.4.8, and FlashInfer 0.6.18. This TTFT table has not been rerun after the review fixes.

Client workload: `bench_one_batch_server.py --model-path None --base-url http://127.0.0.1:32101 --batch-size <BS> --input-len 16384 --output-len 1024 --cache-hit-rate 0 --dataset-name random-ids --show-report`, with seed 42 and temperature 0.

Each arm/BS has the client's default 1024/16 warmup plus a separate full-shape warmup, followed by **one measured, unprofiled batch**. TTFT is measured client-side from the common batched POST start to each request's first token; the table reports the **median across requests within that batch**, not a median across repeated runs. Reduction is `100 × (1 − CP TTFT / TP TTFT)`.

| Batch size | TP4 + MTP P50 TTFT (ms) | CP4 + MTP P50 TTFT (ms) | CP TTFT reduction |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 382.84 | 349.80 | 8.63% |

| 32 | 6171.95 | 5606.01 | 9.17% |

Raw requests, launch/client commands, environment records, and the audit are retained locally.

title: [XPU CI] Optimize PR CI per-file timeouts and fail hanging tests fast
author: arathi-hlab
body:
## Motivation

XPU PR CI ran each test file with the default 1200s limit plus 600s on retry. Several files intermittently hang right after XPU device init with no output, so each hang burned the full 30 min before a retry that passes in seconds. Across 156 recent XPU stage-a jobs there were 45 such hangs.

Split out of #41857 so that PR only carries the nightly kernel-main/release split.

## Modifications

- `pr-test-xpu.yml`: cap every file at 600s for both attempts (`--timeout-per-file 600 --retry-timeout-increase 0`), and pass per-file overrides for the 7 files seen hanging.
- `run_suite.py`: add a repeatable `--timeout-override PATH=SECONDS`, matched by path suffix. It does nothing unless passed, and only `pr-test-xpu.yml` passes it.
- `ci_utils.py`: an override caps only the **first** attempt. The retry gets the full `--timeout-per-file`, so a slow-but-healthy run still gets a fair second chance.

Overrides are ~3x each file's observed max passing runtime:

| File | Normal | Hangs seen | First-attempt timeout |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xpu/test_xpu_basic.py` | 21-41s | 7 | 180s |
| `kv_canary/test_self_unit_req_to_expected_token_ids_manager.py` | 8-74s | 3 | 120s |
| `kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hisparse.py` | 6-9s | 11 | 120s |
| `kv_canary/test_self_unit_plan_input.py` | 7-11s | 6 | 120s |
| `xpu/test_layernorm_xpu.py` | 7-11s | 4 | 120s |
| `e2e/xpu/test_xpu_fp8_linear.py` | 8-72s | 7 | 240s |
| `xpu/test_intel_xpu_backend.py` | 58-112s | 7 | 360s |

A hang on one of these now costs about 3 min (cap + 60s wait + normal retry) instead of about 31 min.

No test file or `register_*_ci` change, so other vendors' CI behaviour is unchanged.

## Testing

- Ran `run_unittest_files` on dummy tests with a 2s override and a 10s base: attempt 1 was killed at 2s, the retry ran 3s (longer than the override) and passed; a non-hanging overridden file passed on attempt 1.
- `--timeout-override` rejects `x.py`, `x.py=0`, `=5`, `x.py=abc`.
- pre-commit (isort, ruff, ruff format, codespell, check-yaml) passes.

## Motivation

On the gfx950 MXFP8 dense routes (`--fp8-gemm-backend aiter`, or native), three producers hand their consumer bf16, and the consumer then runs its own per-32 MXFP8 quant as a separate launch (~4.5 us) in every layer.

- Shared expert SwiGLU -> down_proj: an MXFP8 down_proj now uses the Triton `silu_and_mul_clamp` epilogue, which emits fp8 + ue8m0 directly.

- FFN norm -> shared expert gate_up: use the existing `emit_fp8` output of the mHC rmsnorm launch.

Bit-exact against the unfused route (fp8 codes and ue8m0 scales). GSM8K 1319 5-shot, TP2, real acceptance: 0.904.

MI355X TP2 + DSpark, c1 decode: 1376 -> 1256 kernels per step, GPU time 9.458 -> 8.879 ms per step (-6.1%).

title: [Spec] LiLiCorr: named head MLPs and quantized head linears
author: mrusanovsky
body:
## Motivation

[#37462](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37462) added the LiLiCorr draft head. Its
checkpoints name the head's MLP weights by `nn.Sequential` index (`feature_mlp.1`,
`layers.N.mlp.0`). ModelOpt now exports descriptive names instead (`feature_mlp.up_proj`,
`layers.N.mlp.down_proj`, see [NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer#2601](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer/pull/2601)),
the layout vLLM loads, so one checkpoint serves on both engines.

This PR:

1. loads the new names (no checkpoint with the old ones is published);
2. loads quantized LiLiCorr drafters (e.g. ModelOpt NVFP4). On main they fail to load: the head's
   linears and the DFlash `fc` are plain `nn.Linear` that ignore `quant_config`, so packed weights
   and their scales have nowhere to go.

## Modifications

`models/lilicorr.py`
- Names: the head's MLPs were `nn.Sequential`; they are now `up_proj`/`down_proj` modules, with the
  input `LayerNorm` as a separate `feature_norm`.
- Quantization: the head's linears were `nn.Linear`; they are now `ReplicatedLinear` with
  `quant_config` and a module prefix, so a checkpoint's quantized layers and its exclude list are
  honored. Two kinds stay `nn.Linear`: `factor_input_proj`/`out_head`/`in_head`, whose raw weights
  are fused into inference buffers at load, and `feature_mlp`, whose five inputs fit no quantized
  kernel.
- Inputs to the head's linears are flattened to 2D, which quantized linear methods require.
- Loading check: a missing `input_scale` is allowed only for NVFP4 W4A16, which registers one it
  never reads.
- An NVFP4 head that runs on Marlin (W4A16, or W4A4 when `--fp4-gemm-backend` resolves to
  `marlin`, the default below SM100) is rejected at `tp_size > 1`: every rank runs the replicated
  head, and Marlin's atomic-add reduce does not give the same draft on each rank.
- Dtype and sizes are read from `slot_embedding` and `input_size`/`output_size`, which stay valid
  when a weight is packed to uint8.

`models/dflash.py`
- Only some DFlash drafts gave their layers a module prefix and built `fc` with `quant_config`. A
  `supports_quantization` class flag, set by LiLiCorr, now opts a draft into that path; other DFlash
  drafts are unchanged.

`speculative/lilicorr_utils.py`
- Reads sizes from `input_size`/`output_size`, for the same reason as above.
- At `tp_size > 1` the head is folded into the draft CUDA graph instead of running eager. Its
  pre-projected token table is replicated on every rank, as DFlash2's selector codebooks are: each
  rank projects its vocab shard and the shards are all-gathered once at load, so candidates, which
  carry global ids, index it directly and the per-step path is the same as at `tp_size 1`.

## Accuracy Tests

Qwen3-8B target, one H100, gsm8k (1319), greedy, fa3, `draft_length 15`, one server at a time on
the node.

| draft | tree | concurrency 1: acceptance length | tok/s | concurrency 4: acceptance length | tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16, old names | main | 6.9953 | 730.8 | 6.9995 | 2613 |
| bf16, new names | this PR | 6.9953, bit-identical | 731.0 | 6.9762 | 2607 |
| W4A16 NVFP4 | main | fails to load: `fc.weight shape mismatch` | | | |
| W4A16 NVFP4 | this PR | 6.9672 | 716.5 | 6.9678 | 2495 |
| bf16, target `--quantization fp8` | main | 6.9822 | 953.1 | 6.9662 | 3031 |
| bf16, target `--quantization fp8` | this PR | 6.9812 | 951.9 | 6.9449 | 3053 |

- bf16 rows: at concurrency 1 the renamed checkpoint gives the same tokens as main. Above that, 2D inputs
  change bf16 rounding in the head; acceptance moves by ±0.02 either way (concurrency 2 / 4 / 8:
  main 6.992 / 7.000 / 6.994, this PR 7.005 / 6.976 / 6.981).
- W4A16: the newly supported case, a drafter in ModelOpt's `W4A16_NVFP4` format. Main stops at
  the first packed weight, `fc` (uint8 `(4096, 10240)` against the `(4096, 20480)` `nn.Linear`).
- `--quantization fp8` rows: sglang gives the draft the target's quantization by default. On main
  that reached only the draft's decoder layers; it now also reaches the head and `fc`, with acceptance within 0.001.
- `tp_size 2`, bf16, eager head (main) vs head in the draft graph (this PR): concurrency 1
  7.0196 / 1016 tok/s vs 7.0211 / 1040 tok/s; concurrency 4 6.9783 / 3144 vs 6.9860 / 3284;
  concurrency 64 6.9439 / 14998 vs 6.9684 / 15745. Target `--quantization fp8`, concurrency 1:
  main 7.0174, this PR 7.0203. W4A16 is rejected at load.
- `tp_size 4`, bf16, this PR: concurrency 1 7.0154 / 1322 tok/s; concurrency 64 6.9784 / 19305.

Each row is one run of ModelOpt's `examples/specdec_bench` (acceptance length is its
`Block_Weighted_AL`), with concurrency `C`:

```bash
python run.py --engine SGLANG --model_dir Qwen/Qwen3-8B --tokenizer Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --speculative_algorithm DFLASH --draft_model_dir $DRAFT --draft_length 15 \
  --dataset gsm8k --dataset_path gsm8k --num_requests 1319 --output_length 2048 \
  --temperature 0.0 --concurrency $C --tp_size 1 --runtime_params runtime.yaml
# runtime.yaml: chat_template_args: {enable_thinking: false}
#               engine_args: {attention_backend: fa3}   # plus quantization: fp8 for the fp8 rows
```

It starts `sgl.Engine` with the equivalent of:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B --tp-size 1 \
  --speculative-algorithm DFLASH --speculative-draft-model-path $DRAFT \
  --speculative-num-steps 15 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 16 \
  --attention-backend fa3 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --disable-radix-cache \
  --max-running-requests $C --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode $C --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill $C
  # plus --quantization fp8 for the fp8 rows
```

The drafts are not published. All three are one trained Qwen3-8B LiLiCorr draft: as trained,
with the head's MLP keys renamed, and packed by a short script into ModelOpt's `W4A16_NVFP4`
format.

title: [Fix] qwen3.8: Fix batch-invariant kernels for Qwen3.8 Flash-Next
author: Misaka9468
body:
## Motivation

With deterministic inference enabled, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next can produce different logprobs and generated tokens when the same prompt is placed in a different batch. Compiled HC projections use an unregistered `aten::mm.out` overload, shared-expert gating changes its reduction configuration at 1024 token rows, and QSA changes both its attention launch configuration and selected-index ordering.

## Modifications

- Register `aten::mm.out` using the existing batch-invariant matmul and write the result into the supplied output tensor.
- Apply the shared-expert gate's warp cap to every batch size in batch-invariant mode.
- Use one QSA prefill launch configuration in batch-invariant mode.
- Use FlashInfer deterministic CUDA QSA top-k with smaller-index tie breaking and canonical index ordering, including the decode shortcut.
- Add regressions for output-buffer semantics, cross-batch reductions, ragged top-k inputs, cutoff ties, and CUDA graph replay.

## Accuracy Tests

title: [Perf] Optimize MiMo local audio attention on Hopper
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

MiMo's input local audio transformer runs six attention layers with only four tokens and head dimension 16. cuDNN SDPA takes about 1.915 ms per layer at the observed 300-second audio shape on H200. A specialized Triton kernel reduces this to 43.25 µs while closely matching the tested cuDNN arithmetic.

## Modifications

- Add a one-warp kernel processing four batch/head pairs per program, with runtime group count to avoid recompilation for every audio length.
- Keep QK, exponential sums and accumulation in FP32. Round unnormalized exponential weights to the input dtype before PV, then normalize the weighted sum, matching the tested cuDNN path.
- Select the implementation once when building MiMo's input local transformer: Hopper, head dimension 16, and group size 1–4 use the specialized adapter; other configurations use SDPA. The adapter keeps only the runtime precision, mask, position-bias, dropout and attention-weight choices. Q/K/V shape, device, dtype consistency and stride checks live in the kernel host entry point. Keep registration next to the local transformer configuration. Give the Triton entry point a `_kernel` suffix, spell out stride arguments, and call the unnormalized exponentials `weights`. The arithmetic, launch parameters and SDPA mask factory are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Prior H200 validation covered BF16/FP16, token/head strides, causal and noncausal attention, partial groups, changed-input CUDA Graph replay, SDPA fallback, and real Hugging Face Qwen2 integration. BF16 relative RMS error against cuDNN was below 1e-4 on the tested Hopper shapes; Compute Sanitizer memcheck reported zero errors. These are the original kernel results, not a fresh end-to-end measurement of the dispatch cleanup.

The added test file has been removed from this PR. Local pre-commit and [GitHub lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37254914571/job/111589812255) pass on commit `90eea33f29c0f649ae13e361da7b1e641652b39a`.

[H100 validation on that exact commit](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37255152818/job/111590971820) passed: the original numerical/stride/causal/CUDA Graph checks, 24 Qwen2 model cases with bitwise-identical outputs, 16 actual fast-kernel calls, 16 model fallback cases and four dynamic SDPA options. The model cases exercise `AudioEncoderMixin.build_audio_encoder`, with tokenizer loading stubbed. Another 40 kernel cases are bitwise identical before/after renaming, with identical PTX instructions and register/spill/shared-memory usage after excluding symbol names and source debug metadata. Non-Hopper selection was emulated; execution was on H100. Validation scripts remain outside this PR. Full automatic PR CI is still gated by the required main baseline and missing `run-ci` label.

On 64 fixed real English clips from LibriSpeech dummy validation, every candidate repeat preserves original WER 0.0352381 and CER 0.0194301, with no empty or truncated outputs. One raw transcript differs in the full candidate run without changing aggregate errors. This small set does not establish general quality equivalence.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Fresh cleanup comparison on one H100 80GB, driver 580.126.09, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1: original `955d63e6ae1bce4e5f34c7561ad5a81a0c50b82e` versus refined `90eea33f29c0f649ae13e361da7b1e641652b39a`. Every individual timed attention call, including every CUDA Graph replay, is preceded by a 256 MiB eviction-buffer fill. Eviction is excluded from timing. One call per graph, external CUDA events; seven blocks of 31 samples per variant with shuffled variant order. The table reports the median of block medians. Q/K/V have shape `[groups,64,4,16]`, strides `[4096,16,1024,1]`, and noncausal attention.

| Dtype | Audio groups | Before cleanup (µs) | After cleanup (µs) | Change | cuDNN SDPA (µs) | Speedup vs. cuDNN |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BF16 | 32 | 7.968 | 7.968 | +0.00% | 41.984 | 5.27x |
| BF16 | 188 | 11.040 | 11.168 | +1.16% | 196.800 | 17.62x |
| BF16 | 376 | 15.584 | 15.648 | +0.41% | 377.184 | 24.10x |
| BF16 | 1876 | 46.976 | 46.912 | -0.14% | 1842.912 | 39.28x |
| FP16 | 32 | 7.808 | 7.840 | +0.41% | 41.696 | 5.32x |
| FP16 | 188 | 10.880 | 10.912 | +0.29% | 198.144 | 18.16x |
| FP16 | 376 | 15.296 | 15.296 | +0.00% | 377.408 | 24.67x |
| FP16 | 1876 | 45.952 | 46.016 | +0.14% | 1842.944 | 40.05x |

No material kernel regression was observed in these eight cases (maximum increase 1.16%). This is kernel latency coverage, not a fresh end-to-end ASR benchmark. The [successful run log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37255152818/job/111590971820) includes all samples under `MIMO_COLD_L2_FULL_JSON` and the [validation harness](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/c7c5cd46e12ae06c719f49ac2e51f775a94be2c1/test/manual/run_mimo_refine_validation.py) is pinned separately from this PR.

The following H200 measurements are the original pre-cleanup results and used warm L2; they are retained as historical evidence:

H200, driver 580.105.08, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1. Source base: 3ed6367d3f28f11674f72fd298c355f72aee540f. Checkpoint: XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5-ASR at 98641d537df521ac6df05f74090475694d9510b7. Full serving uses BF16 and TP2 on two H200s; the local kernel uses one GPU.

Median of seven samples, each 100 warm CUDA Graph replays; Q/K/V [groups,64,4,16] with strides [4096,16,1024,1]:

| Audio groups | cuDNN SDPA (µs) | Candidate (µs) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32 | 39.165 | 3.386 |
| 188 | 197.813 | 6.656 |
| 376 | 389.136 | 10.796 |
| 1876 | 1914.866 | 43.247 |

Torch Profiler confirms six candidate calls totaling ~242 µs for 300-second audio, versus ~11.508 ms for the six baseline cuDNN calls. This GPU time overlaps host dispatch, so it is not an additive request-latency improvement. Nsight Compute counters were unavailable (`ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM`); the evidence is operator timing and Torch Profiler.

Three fresh-server rounds, with rotated stock/candidate/vLLM order:

| Round | Stock / candidate, mixed-noise rate | Stock / candidate, real-speech rate | vLLM / candidate, mixed-noise rate |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 0.9927 | 1.1515 | 1.1399 |
| 2 | 1.0204 | 1.1422 | 1.2043 |
| 3 | 0.9754 | 1.1022 | 1.1666 |

Each ratio is baseline mean latency divided by candidate mean latency. Mixed noise: four warmups and 32 unique requests, equal counts of 5/30/60/300-second audio, concurrency one. **There is no stable end-to-end patch gain on this workload.** Real speech is a separate secondary measurement: two warmups and 64 clips of varying length; it is not a fully warmed per-shape benchmark. SGLang's default embedding cache remains enabled for both versions, including the two repeated quality warmup clips.

The stronger working stock vLLM-Omni comparator uses PIECEWISE capture with a text-only MiMo pipeline; EAGER was slower and FULL capture failed on a CPU copy inside capture. The framework lead over vLLM predates this patch and is not attributed entirely to the kernel.

[Reproduction scripts, launch commands, immutable revisions, all operator samples and complete serving-round summaries](https://gist.github.com/BBuf/f22481fb15340c5e8846b966e2e1ce74).

## Checklist

- [x] Keep input-contract validation in the kernel host entry point.

- [x] Document reproduction commands and immutable revisions.

title: [PD] Make the prebuilt last-token H2D copy non-blocking under overlap
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

With overlap scheduling on the decode side of PD disaggregation, `_get_new_prebuilt_batch` makes the schedule stream wait on the forward stream before `process_prebuilt` runs, so that a prebuilt request never seeds a row an in-flight forward may still touch. `process_prebuilt` then built the last-token tensor with `torch.tensor(..., device=self.device)`, which is a blocking host-to-device copy. Its implicit stream sync made the host wait behind that fence for the entire in-flight forward, so the scheduler could not prepare the next step while the GPU was busy, and the GPU went idle after every decode-side admission.

## Modifications

Build the last-token tensor in pinned host memory and copy it with `non_blocking=True`, the same idiom `ScheduleBatch.filter_batch` already uses for its per-step last-token copy. GPU-side ordering is unchanged (forward -> copy -> stash / draft input -> next forward), so the fence still guarantees what it did; only the host-side wait goes away. `is_pin_memory_available` falls back to a pageable tensor on devices without pinned memory. Non-PD and non-overlap paths are unaffected.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the copy produces the same tensor; only the host-side synchronization changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Standalone check of the mechanism on one GPU: enqueue a synthetic delay kernel on a "forward" stream, make a second stream wait on it, then build a small int64 tensor from that second stream.

- blocking `torch.tensor(..., device="cuda")`: the host does not return until the delay kernel has finished
- pinned + `non_blocking=True`: the host returns immediately, and the values are correct after `synchronize()`

Unit suites that touch this path pass locally against this branch, each run as its own process:

- `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_wire.py` (63 passed)
- `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_kv_checksum.py` (16 passed, 1 GPU)
- `test/registered/unit/managers/test_priority_scheduling_disaggregation.py` (27 passed)
- `test/registered/unit/constrained/test_reasoner_grammar_backend.py` (34 passed)

ruff, ruff-format, isort and codespell are clean at the pre-commit pins.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). No new test: this swaps one copy for the idiom already used in `filter_batch`, and the existing suites above cover the call path.
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not applicable.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [XPU] Use the shared fused decode-metadata kernel in the intel_xpu ba…
author: xinchen9
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

`XPUAttentionBackend.init_forward_metadata_out_graph()` built the decode page
table with separate PyTorch ops each step: strided gather from `req_to_token`,
floor-divide by `page_size`, cast to `int32`, copy into the preallocated
`page_table`, zero the trailing columns; plus separate ops for
`cache_seqlens_int32` and `cu_seqlens_k`, and a separate SWA page-table copy.

The NVIDIA FlashAttention backend already does all of this with one fused Triton
kernel, `normal_decode_set_metadata()` in
`python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/metadata.py`. The kernel is plain Triton
with no CUDA-specific intrinsics and runs unchanged on Triton's XPU backend,
but the XPU backend did not use it.

This change calls that existing kernel from the XPU backend. No new kernel is
introduced; the Intel attention kernels, the graph runner and the KV-cache
allocator are untouched.

## Modifications

**`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/xpu_backend.py`** (modified)

- Import `normal_decode_set_metadata` alongside the other helpers already
  imported from `flashattention_backend`.
- New private method `_set_decode_page_metadata()` issues one fused launch for
  `cache_seqlens_int32`, `cu_seqlens_k`, `page_table` and, for hybrid-SWA
  models, `swa_page_table`. It forwards `seq_len_delta` (= `kv_len_offset`) so
  target-verify and draft-decode keep their KV extension, and passes the tight
  bound `max_seq_pages = cdiv(max_seq_len_k, page_size)`.
- `init_forward_metadata_out_graph()` calls it for the ordinary
  (non-encoder-decoder) branch. The encoder-decoder branch keeps its original
  PyTorch implementation; the seq-len cast and cumsum moved into that branch.
- The separate SWA page-table gather/translate/copy block is removed. The fused
  kernel writes `swa_page_table` through `full_to_swa_index_mapping`, which is
  what `SWAKVPool.translate_loc_from_full_to_swa()` does.
- Net ~ -30 / +40 lines; one Triton launch replaces 6-8 PyTorch ops per decode step.

**`test/registered/attention/test_normal_decode_set_metadata.py`** (modified)

- Existing kernel test now runs on XPU as well as CUDA/ROCm (device from
  `get_device()`, skip only if neither is available).
- Registered for XPU CI: `register_xpu_ci(est_time=15, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-xpu")`.

**`benchmark/kernels/bench_xpu_decode_metadata.py`** (new)

- Standalone correctness + latency comparison of the previous PyTorch block vs
  the fused kernel on XPU. Loads the kernel from the repo file, so it needs only
  torch and triton. Exits non-zero if any live entry differs.

**Behavioral note: page-table tail columns.** The previous XPU block zeroed
columns past the batch-wide max page count every step. The fused kernel writes
only each request's live prefix (`cdiv(seq_len + delta, page_size)` pages) and
leaves the rest untouched. This is the kernel's documented contract and what the
FlashAttention backend already relies on: attention kernels bound their reads by
`cache_seqlens_int32`, and stale tail entries are always in-range page ids from
earlier steps (or zero from allocation), so whole-table gathers in the
chunked-attention path stay in bounds. Validated end to end below.

**Reproduction notes for XPU.** The decode graph is opt-in on XPU
(`--cuda-graph-backend-decode full`); without it decode runs eagerly through
`init_forward_metadata()` and this change is not exercised. The `intel_xpu`
backend accepts `--page-size` 64 or 128 only; other values are coerced to 128.

## Accuracy Tests

Environment: 1x Intel Arc Pro B70, torch 2.13.0+xpu, Triton 3.7.2,
sglang-kernel-xpu 0.3.0, image built from `docker/xpu.Dockerfile`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `python3 -m pytest test/registered/attention/test_normal_decode_set_metadata.py` on XPU | 16 passed, 8 subtests passed |
| `benchmark/kernels/bench_xpu_decode_metadata.py`: `cache_seqlens`, `cu_seqlens_k`, all live `page_table` entries vs previous PyTorch block | exact match, 36 configs (bs 1-32, ctx 1K-8K, page 1/16/64) |
| GSM8K 5-shot, 200 questions, temperature 0, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct BF16, `--page-size 64 --cuda-graph-backend-decode full`, fused path | accuracy 0.625, 0 invalid |

Server log confirmed the decode graph captured (3.4 s) and every decode batch
ran through it, so the fused path was exercised on each decode step.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Metadata preparation, standalone** (host-inclusive latency per call,
`python3 benchmark/kernels/bench_xpu_decode_metadata.py --markdown`):

| bs | ctx | page | pytorch (us) | pytorch + .item() sync (us) | fused (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8192 | 64 | 97.4 | 124.3 | 31.5 | 3.1x to 3.9x |
| 4 | 8192 | 64 | 103.8 | 130.6 | 31.3 | 3.3x to 4.2x |
| 16 | 8192 | 64 | 104.0 | 131.5 | 32.5 | 3.2x to 4.0x |
| 32 | 1024 | 64 | 103.5 | 130.8 | 32.3 | 3.2x to 4.0x |
| 32 | 8192 | 64 | 104.8 | 131.6 | 32.5 | 3.2x to 4.0x |

Latency is flat in batch size and context on both sides: the cost is launch
overhead, not bandwidth. Absolute microseconds vary with GPU clock state; the
ratios are stable.

**End-to-end serving** (`python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang
--num-prompts 300 --max-concurrency {1,32}`, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct BF16,
`--attention-backend intel_xpu --page-size 64 --cuda-graph-backend-decode full
--mem-fraction-static 0.8`; only `xpu_backend.py` differs between the servers;
one run per cell):

| Concurrency | Metric | Before | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Median ITL | 6.33 ms | 6.31 ms | -0.3% |
| 1 | Median TPOT | 6.32 ms | 6.30 ms | -0.3% |
| 1 | Output throughput | 155.1 tok/s | 155.4 tok/s | +0.2% |
| 32 | Output throughput | 2494 tok/s | 2724 tok/s | +9.2% (*) |
| 32 | Median TPOT | 10.88 ms | 9.95 ms | -8.5% (*) |
| 32 | Median ITL | 8.27 ms | 8.29 ms | 0 |

(*) The baseline run at concurrency 32 contained a ~1 s stall (max ITL 886 ms
vs 133 ms after), so these cells are single-run observations, not a claimed gain.

Interpretation: at concurrency 1 the end-to-end effect is neutral, as expected.
With the overlap scheduler the host-side metadata work runs while the device
executes the previous step, so removing ~70-100 us of host time does not
shorten a 6.3 ms step; the ~20 us that does show up matches replacing several
tiny device kernels with one. The value of this change is 3-5x faster metadata
preparation, 5-7 fewer launches per decode step, and the XPU backend sharing
the fused path with the FlashAttention backend instead of maintaining its own
PyTorch version.

title: [Diffusion] FLUX 3 Action: CUDA graphs for observation encoding and denoising steps
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

Eager FLUX 3 Action is partly host-launch-bound:

- The VAE frame encode issues about 2200 kernels: 18 ms of host time for 9.3 ms of GPU work.
- One CFG denoising step issues about 49 ms (BF16) / 61 ms (FP8r) of host-side launch work, measured with tiny inputs so the GPU time is negligible.

On RTX 5090 the denoising steps are GPU-bound (166-272 ms per CFG step), so most of that launch time is hidden and the observation encoding is where the win is. On faster GPUs the launch time is a larger share of each step.

The bit-exact fused kernels (LN+modulate, SwiGLU, QK-norm+RoPE) were also disabled during any capture, which made a captured step slower than eager (272 -> 311 ms per CFG step).

## Changes

Two CUDA graphs per request, both on by default and opt-out when they cannot run:

- **Observation encoding** — the video VAE frame encode plus the `video_cond` / state stream mode blocks.
- **Denoising step** — the target stream mode blocks plus every CFG pass, one graph per step shape.

Graphs are used only on a single GPU with resident weights. Multi-GPU (TP / SP / CFG parallel) and offloaded components fall back to eager, as does any signature whose capture fails. `enable_cuda_graph` (default on) and `cuda_graph_max_entries` (default 4 per stage) are on the pipeline config.

Already verified fused kernels now run inside a capture. Only the first-sight verification, which runs the eager chain plus a host sync, still stays out of capture.

## Benchmark setup

One RTX 5090, `python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.benchmarks.bench_flux3_action`: OpenPI WebSocket, msgpack numpy images, three 360x640 uint8 cameras, 10 warmup + 50 sequential requests, median and p90 of server-side `server_timing.infer_ms`, NATTEN VAE, eager mode (no `torch.compile`), caption cached.

Peak memory is the maximum of `nvidia-smi memory.used` sampled every 300 ms over the whole server lifetime, so it includes the CUDA context and the benchmark's own allocations.

Baseline is this branch's parent commit, measured back to back in the same session.

## Latency and memory

| Variant | Eager | CUDA graph | Change | p90 eager | p90 graph | Peak eager | Peak graph | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `base` | 1141 ms | 1125 ms | -1.4% | 1145 ms | 1130 ms | 23.3 GiB | 23.5 GiB | +216 MiB |
| `fp8r` | 930 ms | 899 ms | -3.3% | 933 ms | 902 ms | 17.9 GiB | 18.2 GiB | +320 MiB |
| `gd` | 627 ms | 614 ms | -2.0% | 629 ms | 616 ms | 23.3 GiB | 23.5 GiB | +214 MiB |
| `gd-fp8r` | 521 ms | 494 ms | -5.0% | 522 ms | 495 ms | 17.9 GiB | 18.2 GiB | +310 MiB |
| `sd` | 179 ms | 168 ms | -6.1% | 180 ms | 168 ms | 23.3 GiB | 23.5 GiB | +208 MiB |
| `sd-fp8r` | 158 ms | 140 ms | -11.6% | 159 ms | 140 ms | 17.9 GiB | 18.2 GiB | +304 MiB |

The extra memory is the graph memory pool: about 210 MiB for BF16 and 310 MiB for FP8r, roughly flat across step counts because both graphs hold one step's intermediates.

## Which graph earns the gain

Measured by disabling the denoising graph only:

| Variant | Eager | Observation graph only | Both | Observation | Denoising |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `base` | 1141 ms | 1133 ms | 1125 ms | -8.7 ms | -7.6 ms |
| `fp8r` | 930 ms | 919 ms | 899 ms | -11.3 ms | -19.0 ms |
| `sd` | 179 ms | 169 ms | 168 ms | -10.0 ms | -0.9 ms |
| `sd-fp8r` | 158 ms | 143 ms | 140 ms | -15.3 ms | -3.0 ms |

The observation graph saves 9-15 ms on every variant. The denoising graph varies with how many kernels a step issues: 19 ms on `fp8r`, 7.6 ms on `base`, but under 3 ms on the one-step variants.

## Stacked with the fused FP8 quantization (#41671)

#41671 cuts the FP8r activation quantization from 8 launches per linear to 1. The two changes are close to orthogonal: the graph still wins 16-22 ms on top of it.

| Variant | main | #41671 | #41671 + graph | Graph on top | Total vs main | Peak #41671 | Peak both | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `fp8r` | 930 ms | 718 ms | 696 ms | -3.1% | -25.2% | 17.4 GiB | 17.6 GiB | +254 MiB |
| `gd-fp8r` | 521 ms | 405 ms | 385 ms | -4.9% | -26.0% | 17.4 GiB | 17.6 GiB | +248 MiB |
| `sd-fp8r` | 158 ms | 128 ms | 111 ms | -12.9% | -29.6% | 17.4 GiB | 17.6 GiB | +242 MiB |

Per CFG step on `fp8r`, the fused quantization drops the quantization kernels from 53.9 ms to 4.2 ms, and the graph then removes the remaining launch gap (kernel time 163.3 ms vs 166.5 ms of replay wall time).

## Accuracy

A replay runs the same kernels as eager, so outputs are bit-identical.

- Actions on 4 frames of the public Cosmos3-DROID episode 0 (frames 40, 120, 232, 320) are identical to the parent commit for `base`, `fp8r` and `sd-fp8r`. Mean / max error against the `flux-action` reference is unchanged: `base` 0.0034 / 0.0348 rad, `fp8r` 0.0101 / 0.0841 rad, `sd-fp8r` 0.0055 / 0.0312 rad.
- `--dit-layerwise-offload` captures nothing, runs eager, and matches the reference as before.
- New unit test `test_cuda_graph_replays_match_eager_denoise_steps`: replays with fresh inputs match eager bit for bit, with one capture and one cache hit. `test/unit/test_flux3_action.py`: 31 passed.

title: [diffusion] Qwen-Image 2.1: load ComfyUI/ai-toolkit fused `gate_up` LoRAs and diffusers metadata alpha
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

The community Qwen-Image 2.1 LoRAs on Hugging Face were checked against SGLang's loader. Each safetensors header was replayed through SGLang's own normalize and name-mapping code, and the results were then confirmed end to end on the real model. **Two of the three most-downloaded LoRAs loaded wrong, and neither raised an error.**

- **Fused `img_mlp.gate_up` was dropped.** ai-toolkit and ComfyUI train against ComfyUI's native checkpoint, which fuses the SwiGLU inputs into `img_mlp.gate_up` with rows `[gate; up]`. SGLang has separate `gate_layer` and `proj`, so these tensors matched no layer and were skipped. Only the attention layers and `img_mlp.out` took effect: 160 of 224 block layers. The only signal was an info log, `covers 160/232`. This covers BFS-Best-Face-Swap (the most-liked 2.1 LoRA), AnyAngle, Consistency, Outpaint and others.
- **diffusers alpha was ignored.** `save_lora_weights` stores `lora_alpha` only inside the `lora_adapter_metadata` JSON (`transformer.lora_alpha`). SGLang read top-level `lora_alpha`/`alpha` keys only and fell back to alpha = rank. Pruna has rank 64 and alpha 128, so it ran at **half strength**. Its 5-step output came out dark and under-denoised, and was pixel-identical to forcing `lora_alpha=64`.

## Modifications

- **`QwenImage21Transformer2DModel.prepare_lora_adapter`** (`runtime/models/dits/qwen_image21.py`) splits `transformer_blocks.N.img_mlp.gate_up` onto `gate_layer` and `proj`:
  - `lora_A` is shared.
  - `lora_B[:ffn]` goes to `gate_layer` and `lora_B[ffn:]` goes to `proj`.
  - A per-layer `.alpha` is copied to both.
  - It raises when the shape is wrong or the same MLP has both fused and split keys.
  - Row order was checked byte for byte against ML-Intern-lab's own fused and pre-split copies of one LoRA.
- **`load_peft_config`** (`runtime/pipelines_core/lora/peft_adapter.py`) now merges the `transformer.*` LoraConfig from `lora_adapter_metadata`: `lora_alpha`, `alpha_pattern`, `use_rslora`, `use_dora` and the rest.
  - `text_encoder.*` sections are ignored.
  - A conflict with `adapter_config.json` or with a top-level alpha raises, as before.
  - Unsupported fields such as DoRA keep failing closed.

## LoRA coverage

Popularity numbers come from the Hugging Face API on 2026-10-01: downloads over the last 30 days, and likes. Repos created in the past two weeks still show 0 downloads, so likes are the better signal for them.

- **Coverage** is the fraction of the 232 wrappable Linear layers that get the LoRA. Block-only LoRAs top out at 224/232.
- **Verified**:
  - *e2e*: real Qwen-Image-2.1 on one H200 through `DiffGenerator`.
  - *header*: safetensors header replayed through the real loader code, with names and shapes checked against the DiT.

### Fixed by this PR

| LoRA | Downloads (30d) | Likes | What it is | Before | After | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Alissonerdx/BFS-Best-Face-Swap](https://huggingface.co/Alissonerdx/BFS-Best-Face-Swap) (`*_qwen_2.1` files) | 173,323 (882k all-time, shared with other bases) | 1,065 | head / body swap (edit) | 120–160/232 (`gate_up` dropped) | 152–224/232 (every layer each file trains) | header |
| [PrunaAI/Pruna-Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/PrunaAI/Pruna-Qwen-Image-2.1) | 98,442 | 132 | **few-step**, 5 / 8 steps | half strength (alpha 64 instead of 128) | alpha 128 | e2e (5-step), header (8-step) |
| [lilylilith/QI_2.1_AnyAngle](https://huggingface.co/lilylilith/QI_2.1_AnyAngle) | new | 95 | multi-angle view (edit) | 160/232 | 224/232 | header |
| [ausboss/Qwen-Image-2.1-Consistency-LoRA](https://huggingface.co/ausboss/Qwen-Image-2.1-Consistency-LoRA) | new | 59 | edits without pixel drift | 160/232 | 224/232 | e2e |
| [ausboss/Qwen-Image-2.1-Outpaint-LoRA](https://huggingface.co/ausboss/Qwen-Image-2.1-Outpaint-LoRA) | new | 47 | outpainting (edit) | 160/232 | 224/232 | header |
| [WarmBloodAban/Qwen-Image-2.1-LoRAs](https://huggingface.co/WarmBloodAban/Qwen-Image-2.1-LoRAs) `Anything2RealCharacters` | 11,355 (repo) | 105 (repo) | anime → real | 160/232 | 224/232 | header |
| [ML-Intern-lab/Qwen-Image-2.1-doodle-in-LoRA](https://huggingface.co/ML-Intern-lab/Qwen-Image-2.1-doodle-in-LoRA) (fused file) | 280 | 15 | scribble → object (edit) | 160/232 | 224/232 | e2e |
| [Danrisi/lenovo_qwen2.1](https://huggingface.co/Danrisi/lenovo_qwen2.1) | 1,004 | 7 | photo-realism style | 160/232 | 224/232 | header |

BFS files train only some of the blocks; `bfs_body_swap_v1.0` and `bfs_head_v1.1` carry `gate_up` in 16 of 32. After this PR every tensor in each file is applied.

### Already supported before this PR (unchanged)
