| [alibaba-pai/Qwen-Image-2.1-Fun-Acc-LoRAs](https://huggingface.co/alibaba-pai/Qwen-Image-2.1-Fun-Acc-LoRAs) (+ t8star ComfyUI copy) | 6,566 | 35 | **few-step** 4-step PDD. It replaces full `norm_q`/`norm_k`/`text_norm` weights and swaps `proj_out` for a [4, 64, 4096] per-step head, which needs an architecture change. Today its LoRA part loads but the rest is ignored. |
| [houseofboern/…-lokr](https://huggingface.co/houseofboern/realism-nano-banana-qwen-image-2.1-lokr) | new | 2 | LoKr (`lokr_w1/w2`); matches 0 layers |

### Few-step LoRAs

| LoRA | Steps | Weights load | Recommended schedule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Viggle turbo (+ t8star, xingewh conversions) | 6 (4/5/6; 9 with the LoRA switched off for the last 2 steps) | yes | custom sigmas `[1, .9375, .875, .75, .5, .25]` and `shift_terminal: null` |
| Pruna (+ NidAll conversion) | 5 / 8 | **yes, after this PR** | custom sigmas; `shift=1`, dynamic shift off |
| ThakiCloud FewStep | 5 / 8 | yes | custom sigmas; dynamic shift off |
| Turbo8 | 8 | yes | `shift_terminal=None`, max_shift 0.6935 |
| alibaba-pai Fun-Acc | 4 | no | PDD architecture |

**Follow-up:** every few-step LoRA ships its own sigma schedule, and none of them uses the base one. The Qwen-Image 2.1 pipeline exposes no request-level `sigmas` and always uses the base scheduler config (dynamic shift, `shift_terminal=0.02`). These LoRAs therefore apply correctly but run on the base schedule, so their output quality is below the authors' reported numbers.

## Accuracy

### Unit tests

- `test_published_lora_layouts_match_weight_delta_and_restore_base` (`test_qwen_image21_cuda.py`) is now parametrized over the diffusers, diffusers-metadata-alpha and ComfyUI fused `gate_up` layouts, in both dynamic and merge mode. In each case the forward must match a reference model with `B @ A` (times alpha / rank) added by hand, and unmerge must restore the base model bit for bit.
- `test_diffusers_adapter_metadata_supplies_transformer_peft_config` (`test_lora_peft.py`) covers the transformer-section alpha and `alpha_pattern`, ignoring `text_encoder.*`, and the `adapter_config.json` conflict.
- On the pre-fix code, all 5 new cases fail: 4 CUDA layout cases and 1 PEFT case. With the fix, the Qwen-Image 2.1 and LoRA suites pass: 111 passed.

### End to end

Setup: `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1` on one H200 through `DiffGenerator`, 1024×1024, seed 42, CFG 1, merge mode. The same script ran on main and on this branch.

| base T2I, base edit, split LoRA, explicit-alpha runs | — | identical to main |

title: [Performance] Optimize Qwen3.8-Flash-Next BF16 decode on Blackwell
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Single-token BF16 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next decode launches separate HC combine/norm and MoE shared-gate/finalize/collective work, while the packed GDN value tile leaves substantial register pressure at this shape. On four B200 GPUs, this patch raises the measured 8k-input/1k-output decode rate from fresh stock **242.443** to **270.982–271.759 token/s**, preserving the sampled stock accuracy in four native runs.

## Modifications

- Overlap the HC gate with block computation, fuse HC apply with grouped Gemma RMSNorm, and pass the prepared norm tensors explicitly across layers. PLE and PP boundaries retain the normal handoff.
- Extend the existing collective with an FP32 shared gate, preserving routed BF16 rounding before the shared-expert FMA. Defer BF16 MoE finalize and overlap the shared branch through a guarded single-token TP4/EP1 path with its own communication buffer.
- Use the smaller GDN value tile for the packed single-token BF16/FP32-state Blackwell shape, preserving the one-warp reduction order. Existing dispatch remains for unsupported shapes.

The MoE specialization requires hidden size 2560, 512 experts/top-10, BF16, SM10, TP4/EP1, attention DP1, with LoRA, speculative decoding and two-batch overlap disabled. No extra command-line switch enables the kernels. The benchmark selects the existing faster custom-all-reduce deployment option for both stock and candidate.

## Accuracy Tests

Stock and all four native candidate runs score **126/128 GSM8K, zero invalid answers, zero truncations**. These use identical frozen tokenized prompts, normal EOS and the same 2,048-token cap. All 128 per-question correctness and finish-reason verdicts match the fresh stock run.

Historical GPU validation before the standalone test cleanup: 6 HC unit configurations; 12 independent torch-reference GDN configurations; 6 collective configurations on each of 4 ranks, including the original ungated API; 90 trained HC-chain comparisons; 324 changed-input trained collective graph comparisons; 192 seeded GDN output/state bit comparisons. Isolated HC memcheck: zero errors. Full-stack communicator checks have the same handled PyTorch FABRIC capability API errors in stock and candidate, so they are not claimed as clean full-stack sanitizer runs. Pre-commit passes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: [DSA] k-pool: 256-token logical page so index page id = logical page id
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #41494: GLM-5.3-Flash (DSA with `index_kpool=4`) loses the NIAH needle at 16K when prefixes are shared. Supersedes #41645.

A pooled index key covers 4 consecutive tokens, i.e. 4 physical KV pages of 64. Before this PR the radix tree page was 64, so a prefix hit could end inside a pooled-key group. The resuming request then wrote its pooled keys into the group-head page owned by another request's cached prefix, and later readers of that prefix saw the wrong keys.

## Modifications

- **Logical page = 64 × `index_kpool` (256)** for the allocator, radix tree, PD and HiCache. KV kernels and the DSA backend's `real_page_size` keep 64-token physical pages. Logical page `L` owns physical pages `4L .. 4L+3`.
- **Index page id = logical page id.** Each index page holds 64 pooled keys (`slots_per_page`). Pooled key `j` of a request lives at index slot `req_to_token[r, 4j] // 4`, and the index page table is `page_table_64[:, ::4] // 4`. Every group-head lookup in the k-pool kernels and planners now divides by `POOL_SIZE`.
- **Index pool sized per pooled key:** one key per `index_kpool` tokens, which frees about 9% more KV capacity on H200 (see below). The HiCache host declaration is sized the same way.
- `--dcp-size > 1` with `index_kpool > 1` is rejected at startup, because a pooled key spans positions owned by different DCP ranks.
- Every change is a no-op for `index_kpool == 1`. DeepSeek-V4's pool falls back to `page_size` (`_index_page_slots`).

## Accuracy Tests

H200×8, TP8, tilelang DSA, bf16 KV, same flags for both builds.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| NIAH 16K, 20 samples, random needle-depth order (RULER-style) | 11/20 | **20/20** |
| NIAH 16K, 20 samples, increasing depth | 19/19, then crash (see below) | 20/20 |
| Prefix-hit lengths | multiples of 64 (960, 2496, ...) | multiples of 256 |
| `max_total_num_tokens` | 3,531,072 | **3,861,760** (+9.4%) |
| `test_glm53_flash_h200.py` LowLatency (EAGLE) GSM8K, repeated runs | 0.942 / 0.930 / 0.926 (mean 0.933) | 0.934 / 0.924 / 0.924 / 0.936 (mean 0.930) |
| LowLatency accept length / bs1 speed | — | 4.14 / pass |
| HighThroughput (attn-DP 8) GSM8K | — | 0.944 |

The GSM8K difference is within run-to-run noise (one run's std ≈ 0.011); `main` also dips below the 0.93 threshold.

Unit tests: the new `test_kpool_index_addressing.py` fails 3/3 on `main` and passes here. The existing k-pool kernel and unit tests pass with the updated page geometry.

### Known issues, also present on `main`

- **HiCache does not restore the indexer for hybrid mamba + DSA models:** `_MambaStrategy` never assembles the `indexer` host pool and logs `HybridLinearKVPool declares host pools ['indexer'] that _MambaStrategy did not assemble`. NIAH after a cache flush loses needles on host-restored prefixes. This PR does not change that path.
- **Intermittent CUDA illegal memory access in decode** at about 16K+ tokens (`copy_done.synchronize`). Intermittent on both `main` and this PR, about 1 in 3 shuffled-NIAH runs with EAGLE, and also seen once without EAGLE on `main`; not tied to a specific sample or length.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Perf] [AMD] custom-all-reduce: Select the fused AR+RMSNorm 1-stage kernel by token count and read volume
author: ZhengGong-amd
body:
## Motivation

On ROCm, `GroupCoordinator.fused_allreduce_rmsnorm` uses AITER's 1-stage fused AR+RMSNorm kernel only up to a 128 KiB payload, a cutoff that only fits TP=8; this PR bounds the kernel's read volume (`payload × world_size`) and token count instead, so TP=2/4 decode batches get the faster 1-stage kernel.

Each 1-stage rank reads every peer's full payload, so cost grows with `world_size × payload`; at bf16, hidden 6144, the fixed cutoff is hit at 10 tokens.

## Modifications

- Select 1-stage when `token_num <= 80` and `payload * world_size <= 8 * 128 KiB`. The budget is today's TP=8 cutoff and where 1-stage stops winning at TP=4. 80 is the 1-stage grid size (`kMaxBlocks`); the cap only binds when `hidden × world_size ≤ 6472` (bf16).
- TP=8 is unchanged. At hidden 6144, batches of 11–42 tokens (TP=2) and 11–21 tokens (TP=4) move to 1-stage.
- `SGLANG_USE_1STAGE_ALLREDUCE` still overrides; `fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_quant_per_group` keeps its own rule (#24651).
- `test_aiter_allreduce_fusion_amd.py`: `TestFusedArRmsStageSelection` (CPU) pins the selection at TP=2/4/8, the token cap and the env override.

AITER's own `CudaCommunicator` already scales this cutoff with world size (ROCm/aiter#3745); SGLang calls `custom_fused_ar_rms` directly, with a lower budget (1 MiB of reads, not 1.75 MiB). GLM-5.x enables the fusion for decode by default on ROCm; other models reach it at TP=2/4 with `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K 5-shot, greedy, 1319 items, `lm_eval`, `num_concurrent=16` (decode batches in the new window), strict-match. 8× MI355X, main `0072e2cc08` on sglang build `0.5.21.dev20261002+gedee4308bc`, amd-aiter `0.1.23.dev183`.

| model | TP | main | PR |
|---|---:|---|---|
| GLM-5.3 (FP8) | 4 | 0.9271 (0.9189–0.9310, 5 runs) | 0.9253 (0.9212–0.9287, 5 runs) |
| Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B MXFP4 (control, same kernel) | 8 | 0.8355 / 0.8415 | 0.8393 |

- GLM-5.3: every PR run is inside main's range; per-sample verdict agreement is 95.1–96.7 % main vs. PR and 95.5–96.5 % main vs. main.
- Same inputs through both kernels (TP=4, hidden 6144, m = 8–20): residual is bit-identical; normed output differs in ~6 per million elements by 1 bf16 ulp.
- Test file on 2× MI355X (main `b960aa903a`, amd-aiter `0.1.26.dev144`): 15 passed, 1 skipped (8-GPU benchmark); the new selection tests fail on main.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same build, torch `2.11.0+rocm10.0.0`. Arms run in blocks of 4, first run discarded, two blocks in opposite order; e2e uses a fresh server per run.

Micro, `benchmark_fused_ar_rms_amd.py`, graph-mode p50, block-minimum gain per shape:

| TP | switched shapes | median gain | range | unchanged |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 13 | **+17.2 %** | +13.7 … +23.2 % | −0.1 % ¹ |
| 4 | 14 | **+5.7 %** | +0.8 … +14.6 % | −0.5 … +0.1 % |
| 8 | 0 | — | — | −1.6 … +0.6 % |

¹ 131 × 6144; 3 × 6144 (8 µs) reads −2.3 % / +0.5 % across blocks.

At TP=4 the gain falls to +0.8 … +2.8 % at the edge of the read budget. At TP=2, with `use_1stage` forced, 1-stage is faster at every size measured (+15.6 % at 43 × 6144, +8.1 % at 81 × 2048, +7.8 % at 1024 × 7168), so the bounds are conservative.

e2e, GLM-5.3 TP=4, `sglang.benchmark.serving` random 1031/509, median of 6 warm runs:

| metric | c15 main → PR | c11 main → PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Total tok/s | 1848.8 → 1866.3 (+0.95 %) | 1495.8 → 1521.4 (+1.71 %) |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 23.30 → 23.08 (−0.91 %) | 21.29 → 20.93 (−1.69 %) |

Median TPOT −1.04 % / −1.56 %; TTFT −2.05 … +0.45 %, within spread. Only graph bs 12 and 16 switch kernel; 156 fused calls per decode step × 0.7–1.5 µs is 0.1–0.23 ms per step, consistent with TPOT. Controls Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 TP=4 (path not called) and Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B MXFP4 TP=8 (same kernel) move −0.70 … +1.51 % on every metric, within spread.

title: [Fix] Guard DeepSeek NVFP4 shared-expert fusion for LoRA and FP4 backends
author: jybsuper
body:
## Problem and fix

DeepSeek's NVFP4 shared-expert GEMM + SwiGLU fusion can be enabled with incompatible configurations:

- With LoRA, the fused path accesses quantization attributes on a LoRA wrapper and bypasses the gate/up adapter computation.
- With Marlin or TRT-LLM, weight preparation does not create the interleaved weights required by the fused path.

This PR disables that fusion when LoRA is enabled or the FP4 GEMM backend does not support it, using the ordinary unfused path instead.

## Tests

- New backend compatibility test in `test_modelopt_nvfp4.py`: **PASS**, covering all five backends in a dependency-isolated local run.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: **PASS**.
- The three before/after server tests below ran on **4× GB300** with **DeepSeek-V3-0324-FP4**. Each successful server completed **3/3 generation requests** with nonempty output and finite output-token logprobs. These are startup/generation smoke tests, not a full accuracy benchmark.

### 1. TRT-LLM, no LoRA

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 /opt/sglang/bin/python3 -B -m sglang.launch_server \
```

title: [MoE] Skip block-padding rows in the TMA down activation and quant
author: wanghemeng
body:
## Motivation

With a `*_down.json` config that sets `USE_TMA: true`, the up-GEMM output is kept in the sorted, block-padded layout and sized for the worst case. `silu_and_mul` and the down-input `per_token_group_quant` process the whole buffer, but the down GEMM only reads the `M*topk` rows that `token_mask` keeps. In decode with E=256, topk=8 and BLOCK_SIZE_M=16, the buffer holds 16x the rows actually read. With the TMA down config, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 runs 2.2% slower end to end than without it.

## Modifications

Skip the rows the down GEMM never reads: rows past `num_tokens_post_padded`, padding sentinels, and `-1` expert blocks. The kept rows are computed by the same kernels with the same math.

- `act_and_mul` (JIT): a separately compiled sorted-row variant next to the existing `expert_ids` filter. It is exposed as keyword-only args on `silu_and_mul`, `gelu_and_mul` and `gelu_tanh_and_mul`.
- `per_token_group_quant` (JIT): a new `sorted` layout next to `flat` and `masked`.
- `_fused_moe_kernel_sequence`: passes the row filter to the activation and pre-quantizes the block-FP8 down input in the sorted layout. `invoke_fused_moe_kernel` is unchanged.

The kernels already compiled for the existing paths are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Bit-identical to the non-TMA path:
- New `test_moe_tma_down_padding_rows.py`: the MoE layer with the TMA down path is `torch.equal` to the non-TMA path, for FP8 and BF16.
- New cases in `test_activation.py` and `test_per_token_group_quant.py`: kept rows are bit-identical to the unfiltered kernels, and skipped rows stay untouched.
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 produced identical output tokens before and after the change, both with TP=4/EP=4 and with EAGLE MTP. The MTP accept length was unchanged (3.1411 at batch 1, 3.1030 at batch 32).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Setup:
- H100, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8, CUDA graph on (decode and piecewise prefill).
- The H200 `E=256,N=512` FP8 up/down configs, where down has `USE_TMA`.
- Input 256 / output 32 tokens.
- Before, after and non-TMA runs interleaved in one job.

**Routed-expert SiLU per MoE layer during decode (us, from profiler traces):**

| batch | before | after | non-TMA |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 2.37 | 0.86 | 0.86 |
| 32 | 6.41 | 1.20 | 1.18 |
| 128 | 7.46 | 2.24 | 2.11 |

**Kernel level (us, L2-cold):**
- At M=32, SiLU goes from 10.58 to 2.03 us and the down-input quant from 4.07 to 1.77 us.
- At M=1024, SiLU goes from 53.06 to 20.05 us and the quant from 26.41 to 7.24 us.

**End to end (tok/s):**

| batch | TP=1 before | TP=1 after | TP=1 non-TMA | TP=4/EP=4 before | TP=4/EP=4 after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 857.5 | 871.0 (+1.6%) | 874.4 | 1476.2 | 1502.1 (+1.8%) |
| 32 | 1756.6 | 1800.7 (+2.5%) | 1797.0 | 3402.3 | 3469.8 (+2.0%) |
| 128 | 2354.7 | 2388.2 (+1.4%) | 2376.6 | 5587.0 | 5719.0 (+2.4%) |

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). N/A: no user-facing change.

title: [Perf] [AMD] qwen3.5: Fuse activation quant into small-M FP8 block-scale GEMM on gfx950
author: chuyeh
body:
## Motivation

On MI355X, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 decode at low concurrency runs two latency-bound kernels for each dense FP8 projection: AITER's 1x128 activation quant (about 4 µs) and the block-scale GEMM (about 9 µs). EAGLE with four draft tokens runs these projections at 4 to 32 tokens per rank for concurrency 1 to 8.

This PR fuses them into one HIP kernel for M ≤ 32 at the TP4 and TP8 shapes; larger inputs and other shapes keep the AITER path. With the InferenceX recipe, interactivity improves by 5 to 10% at TP8 and about 3% at TP4.

## Modifications

- New `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/smallm_fp8_blockscale_gfx950/`: one HIP kernel that quantizes bf16 activations to fp8 in registers (1x128 groups, bit-exact with `aiter_per1x128_quant`) and runs the block-scale GEMM on the existing AITER-preshuffled weight and `weight_scale_inv`, so weight loading is untouched. It is built with `hipcc` on first use through the `smallm_moe_gfx950` helpers (#40204), with no build or wheel change.
- `SHAPES` covers the Qwen3.5-397B-A17B dense FP8 projections up to M = 32:

  | (N, K) | TP | Layer |
  |---|---|---|
  | (5120, 4096) | 4 | GDN `in_proj_qkvz` |
  | (4608, 4096) | 4 | attention `qkv_proj` |
  | (4096, 2048) | 4 | GDN `out_proj`, attention `o_proj` |
  | (2560, 4096) | 8 | GDN `in_proj_qkvz`, attention `qkv_proj` |
  | (4096, 1024) | 8 | GDN `out_proj`, attention `o_proj` |

- `fp8_utils.py`: `aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` calls `try_smallm_fp8_bs_linear` on the gfx950 bpreshuffle path when the input is not pre-quantized and there is no bias (+8 lines). It returns `None`, and AITER runs, for any shape, M, dtype, or layout it does not support. `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_FP8_BS=0` turns it off.
- Tests (MI35x suite): `test_smallm_fp8_blockscale_gfx950.py` matches AITER at M = 1 to 32 on all five shapes, checks the quant is bit-exact, covers the fallback cases (M = 33, fp16, unaligned rows, unshuffled weight, off switch), and checks graph replay against eager.

## Accuracy Tests

All runs use image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260927`, InferenceX recipe flags with real draft acceptance, `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`, 1319 questions. `--max-running-requests 8` keeps every verify pass at 32 tokens or fewer, so all dense FP8 projections take the new kernel. "main" is the image's tree (main at `a0ba1968b1`); baseline is the same tree with `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_FP8_BS=0`.

| Model | Tree | Baseline | This PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` TP4 | main, 2 runs | 0.958 / 0.955 | 0.952 / 0.951 |
| | Mean of 2 runs | 0.957 | 0.952 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` TP8 | main, 2 runs | 0.951 / 0.949 | 0.963 / 0.943 |
| | Mean of 2 runs | 0.950 | 0.953 |

One run's standard error at 1319 questions is about 0.006.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

### Kernel microbenchmarks

MI355X, one GPU, CUDA graph replay, weights rotated over 24 copies so they are not cache resident. AITER `aiter_per1x128_quant` + `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle` (tuned Qwen3.5 config) vs this kernel, in µs.

TP4 shapes:

| Tokens | `in_proj_qkvz` 5120 x 4096 | `qkv_proj` 4608 x 4096 | `out_proj` / `o_proj` 4096 x 2048 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 13.7 → 6.8 (−51%) | 13.7 → 6.6 (−51%) | 6.8 → 4.0 (−42%) |
| 4 | 15.8 → 7.3 (−54%) | 15.8 → 7.0 (−56%) | 8.8 → 4.1 (−54%) |
| 8 | 16.0 → 7.7 (−52%) | 16.0 → 7.8 (−51%) | 8.8 → 4.2 (−53%) |
| 16 | 16.5 → 9.0 (−46%) | 16.6 → 8.3 (−50%) | 9.0 → 4.7 (−48%) |
| 32 (cap) | 16.8 → 12.8 (−24%) | 16.7 → 12.6 (−24%) | 10.0 → 7.7 (−23%) |

TP8 shapes:

| Tokens | `in_proj_qkvz` / `qkv_proj` 2560 x 4096 | `out_proj` / `o_proj` 4096 x 1024 |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 12.8 → 5.2 (−60%) | 5.7 → 3.2 (−44%) |
| 4 | 14.6 → 5.6 (−62%) | 7.3 → 3.3 (−54%) |
| 8 | 15.2 → 6.0 (−60%) | 7.6 → 3.3 (−57%) |
| 16 | 14.9 → 7.3 (−51%) | 7.6 → 3.4 (−55%) |
| 32 (cap) | 15.2 → 11.3 (−26%) | 8.2 → 4.9 (−40%) |

Max relative difference to AITER over all TP4 points is 3.1e-3; the quantized activations are bit-exact on all five shapes.

### Decode step time

Time for one EAGLE draft + verify cycle at a fixed batch size. MI355X TP4, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260927`, InferenceX recipe flags without `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` (FP8 KV cache, EAGLE 3 / 1 / 4 with simulated acceptance 3.39). Mean of two runs with the GPU sets swapped, in ms:

| Batch size | Verify tokens | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4 | 11.93 | 11.10 | −7% |
| 4 | 16 | 16.53 | 15.86 | −4% |
| 8 | 32 | 16.29 | 16.22 | ~0 (at the cap) |

### AgentX benchmark

- Hardware: MI355X, TP4 and TP8.
- Model and recipe: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` with the InferenceX recipe `qwen3.5-fp8-mi355x-sglang-agentic`, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260927`.
- Server flags: as in the recipe, including `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`. FP8 KV cache, EAGLE 3 / 1 / 4 with simulated acceptance 3.39, admission and decode CUDA graph batch at 2x concurrency. The recipe has no TP8 point, so TP8 uses the same flags with `--tensor-parallel-size 8`.
- Client: the CI AgentX command, `aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp` on `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126_256k`, 3600 s per run.
- Baseline is the same tree with `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_FP8_BS=0`.

TP8, concurrency 1:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT p50 / p90 (ms) | 3.61 / 4.08 | 3.32 / 3.88 | −8% / −5% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 353 / 832 | 377 / 894 | +7% / +7% |
| Requests completed in 3600 s | 557 | 578 | +4% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 150 | 162 | +8% |
| Interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 277 / 301 | 301 / 332 | +9% / +10% |

TP8, concurrency 4:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT p50 / p90 (ms) | 4.10 / 4.97 | 3.90 / 4.65 | −5% / −6% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 514 / 957 | 509 / 969 | −1% / +1% |
| Requests completed in 3600 s | 936 | 928 | −1% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 245 | 242 | −1% |
| Interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 244 / 291 | 257 / 314 | +5% / +8% |

TP8, concurrency 8:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT p50 / p90 (ms) | 4.74 / 5.50 | 4.53 / 5.35 | −4% / −3% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 723 / 1197 | 691 / 1158 | −4% / −3% |
| Requests completed in 3600 s | 1449 | 1456 | ~0 |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 372 | 373 | ~0 |
| Interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 211 / 275 | 221 / 298 | +5% / +8% |

TP4, concurrency 1:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT p50 / p90 (ms) | 2.94 / 3.22 | 2.84 / 3.11 | −3% / −3% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 355 / 843 | 357 / 836 | ~0 / −1% |
| Requests completed in 3600 s | 633 | 635 | ~0 |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 178 | 178 | ~0 |
| Interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 340 / 357 | 352 / 368 | +3% / +3% |

TP4, concurrency 4:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT p50 / p90 (ms) | 3.17 / 4.24 | 3.07 / 4.05 | −3% / −4% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 501 / 913 | 505 / 912 | +1% / ~0 |
| Requests completed in 3600 s | 1011 | 1026 | +1% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 274 | 278 | +2% |
| Interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 315 / 349 | 325 / 361 | +3% / +3% |

With `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`, the fused all-reduce + RMSNorm already quantizes the input of `in_proj_qkvz` and `qkv_proj` to FP8, so those layers keep the AITER GEMM. The kernel runs on `out_proj` / `o_proj` in every layer, the first layer's `in_proj_qkvz`, and the MTP layer's `qkv_proj`. At TP8 those projections are a larger share of each decode step, so the gain is larger than at TP4. Each EAGLE verify pass sends 4 tokens per running request through every projection, so the kernel covers running batches of 8 or fewer. The kernel does not run in prefill.

title: [Perf] Reduce multi-detokenizer router IPC sends
author: hope1262946533
body:
## Motivation

In a multi-tokenizer/multi-detokenizer deployment, `MultiDetokenizerRouter`
currently converts each scheduler output batch into one message per request.
Each request is serialized and sent separately, even when multiple requests in
the same scheduler batch have the same target detokenizer.

This creates serial Python and IPC overhead in the single router process. Under
sustained decode-only workloads, the output path can become a bottleneck,
causing the scheduler `Batchsize` to stay below the available CUDA Graph
capacity and form a deep sawtooth pattern. `#prealloc-req` can also remain
close to zero for extended periods.

This PR is related to #42217.

## Modifications

- Group requests from one `BaseBatchReq` by the existing target selected by
  `_pick(http_worker_ipc)`.
- Construct one `BatchTokenIDOutput`, `BatchStrOutput`, or
  `BatchEmbeddingOutput` sub-batch per target detokenizer.
- Preserve the original request order within each target group.
- Preserve each request's `http_worker_ipc` ownership value.
- Send each grouped sub-batch once to its target detokenizer.
- Do not merge requests across separate scheduler messages.
- Keep single-request, empty-batch, control-message, and broadcast-message
  behavior unchanged.
- Fall back to the existing per-request path when a payload cannot be sliced
  exactly.
- Construct all grouped sub-batches before the first grouped send, preventing
  partial grouped sends followed by duplicate fallback sends.
- Keep send-time exceptions propagating without resending the batch.

The change is limited to the following path:

Scheduler -> MultiDetokenizerRouter -> Detokenizer

It does not modify the Detokenizer -> TokenizerWorker path, HTTP worker
connection allocation, or `SO_REUSEPORT` behavior.

## Accuracy Tests

This change only changes the batching and IPC-send strategy between the
scheduler output path and detokenizer workers. It does not change token
sampling, decoding, routing decisions, or model computation.

No model accuracy test is required for this change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The optimization targets the number of serialization and IPC-send operations
performed by `MultiDetokenizerRouter`.

A controlled DSV4 decode-only A/B test on the multi-tokenizer/multi-detokenizer
topology showed the following observations:

- Client throughput: `33,035.76 -> 42,334.27 token/s`
- Total elapsed time: `2,402.25 s -> 1,874.60 s`
- Per-rank Batchsize p50: `187 -> 310`
- Per-rank average Batchsize: `186.73 -> 285.67`
- Scheduler-to-router p50 latency: `89.88 s -> 11.30 ms`
- Router CPU utilization p50: `127.5% -> 43.9%`
- Router sends per scheduler batch: approximately `180 -> 10.8`

These measurements were obtained from the earlier controlled test environment
and are included as diagnostic evidence for the bottleneck. They are not
claimed as universal gains for all workloads or hardware configurations.

Local unit tests cover:

- Mixed target ownership.
- Target grouping and per-target ordering.
- Preservation of `http_worker_ipcs`.
- Latest `msgspec.Struct` output fields.
- `BatchTokenIDOutput`, `BatchStrOutput`, and
  `BatchEmbeddingOutput` handling.
- Conservative fallback behavior.
- Send exception propagation.
- Pickle IPC enabled and disabled configurations.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the
      [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the
      [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to
      [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide speed benchmark results according to the
      [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style
      [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Test Results

- Router unit tests: `15 passed`
- Pickle IPC disabled: `13 passed`
- Pickle IPC enabled: `13 passed`
- `git diff --check`: passed
- Ruff checks: passed
- Pre-commit checks: passed
- Registered test checks: passed

Related to #42217

title: [Perf] Accelerate DiffusionGemma with FA4 and CUDA graphs on Blackwell
author: leonardHONG
body:
## Motivation

Speed up DiffusionGemma's BF16 denoising on Blackwell by using FA4 and capturing repeated input preparation and context encoding in CUDA graphs.

## Modifications

- Add FA4 paths for D256 sliding-window and D512 global attention, reusing Triton's paged-KV metadata and cache writes. Support strided Q/K/V inputs and fixed-window graph variants.
- Capture self-conditioning input preparation and subsequent 256-token context passes. Cache temperature schedules on GPU and reuse request-level RNG state and buffers.
- Fuse QKV normalization with RoPE, share RMSNorm reduction across three outputs, and add B300 up/down MoE configurations.
- Fuse logits conversion with softcap and sampling division with the existing two-stage argmax.
- Reuse BBuf's chunked vocabulary statistics from #42099, retaining FP32 sampling probabilities and writing the BF16 self-conditioning copy in the same pass.

## Accuracy Tests

The earlier FA4-enabled 12-request ablation improved throughput from **413.50 to 548.05 tok/s (+32.5%)**, with identical output IDs and denoising step counts. Existing CPU, attention, RNG and CUDA graph regression checks passed on the recorded snapshots.

The reused statistics kernels passed five GPU checks covering numerical accuracy, non-finite values, BF16 probability output, RNG and changed-input graph replay. Reduction ordering changes generated outputs and stopping trajectories: the 96-request statistics comparison is not a bitwise-equivalence result. Model quality evaluation for this combination is pending, so this PR is a draft.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

One B300, TP1, BF16, `sglang-kernel==0.4.8`. Both versions use the same FA4, graph and B300-tuned MoE settings, the same frozen workload, and the [published benchmark script](https://gist.github.com/BBuf/1af02ba70257c7f45a8e4ef7b051e4db): 8,000 input tokens, 1,024 output positions, 3 warmups and 96 measured requests.

| Metric | Original branch | + vocabulary statistics from #42099 | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Generation throughput | 1103.46 tok/s | **1187.02 tok/s** | **+7.57%** |
| Mean E2E latency | 1.090 s | **1.023 s** | **-6.10%** |
| First-block latency | 0.394 s | **0.376 s** | **-4.45%** |
| Mean timed denoising forwards | 57.14 | 56.73 | -0.71% |

All 96 requests completed successfully. Timed forwards decreased by only 0.7%; amortized time per forward, including context encoding, decreased by about 6.4%.

The statistics microbenchmark at `[1, 256, 262144]` measured **2.602 ms to 0.237 ms** when including the BF16 probability copy. This operator result is separate from the service throughput above.

As in the published script, timing ignores EOS and measures the final 768 output positions, including subsequent context encoding. Performance measurements were taken on the recorded pre-rebase snapshots; this branch has since been rebased onto current main.

## Checklist

- [x] Reuse existing backend metadata, graph buffers and kernel registration mechanisms.
- [x] Retain the registered regression tests and provide benchmark results.
- [x] Credit the statistics implementation reused from #42099.
- [ ] Complete model quality validation for the combined statistics path.

title: [diffusion] fix: keep residual_gate_add on the JIT CUDA path for cont…
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

#41305 replaced the shared `residual_gate_add` JIT CUDA operator with Triton kernels, benchmarked on SANA-Video on H200 where it gained 1.6–1.7% E2E. That PR's profiling confirmed the branch executing there is `_rga_transposed`.

The kernel is also shared by Ideogram, Flux-2, Qwen-Image 2.1, ERNIE-Image and LTX-2, which call it on **contiguous** layouts. There the Triton path costs **13–15.6 µs more host time per call**. The cost is flat in tensor size, so it is per-call dispatch overhead, not slower math — negligible when bandwidth-bound, dominant when launch-bound.

LTX-2 is launch-bound: ~800 calls per denoise step at `(1, 384, 4096)` and `(1, 26, 2048)`, from 8 call sites across 48 layers. That adds ~8 ms per step and moved `ltx_2_two_stage_t2v` and `ltx_2_3_two_stage_ti2v_2gpus` from ~1.12× to 1.20–1.23× of their `h100.json` baselines. The `pr_test` limit is 1.20×, so about half of CI runs now cross it.

Found by bisecting 315 commits on 2× H200. Reverting this one file on current main removes the regression entirely.

## Modifications

One file, +9/−4.

1. Take the Triton path only for the transposed-dense layout it was benchmarked on; contiguous layouts go back to the JIT CUDA kernel. The SANA-Video path is untouched.
2. Drop two redundant `can_use_residual_gate_add_cuda` calls — it ran 3× per invocation at ~2.7 µs each (pre-#41305 ran it twice).
3. Call the custom op directly from `residual_gate_add`, which has already run the same predicate. `residual_gate_add_cuda` stays public and keeps validating.

## Accuracy Tests

The CUDA and Triton backends were compared on **37 configurations** (bf16/fp16, six shapes, full / broadcast / per-token gates, plus transposed-dense) and are **bit-identical** on all of them (`torch.equal`). Both already claimed bit-exact rounding, so routing between them by layout cannot change output.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

2× H200, dependencies pinned, sglang commit the only variable.

Host time per call, bf16, at the shapes LTX-2 actually issues (confirmed by counting dispatch branches over a real run):

| shape | gate | #41305 | this PR | pre-#41305 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `(1, 26, 2048)` | broadcast | 36.50 µs | **23.80 µs** | 23.46 µs |
| `(1, 384, 4096)` | broadcast | 39.18 µs | **23.92 µs** | 23.43 µs |
| `(1, 1536, 4096)` | full | 34.43 µs | **19.91 µs** | 19.19 µs |

`ltx_2_two_stage_t2v` avg denoise step, three runs each:

| build | runs | median |
|---|---|---:|
| `544e46c080` (current main) | 164.7 / 162.5 / 161.6 | 162.5 ms |
| **main + this PR** | 158.2 / 158.1 / 157.4 | **158.1 ms** |
| main + whole file reverted | 157.1 / 156.8 / 157.0 | 157.0 ms |
| `fc9e1c8d29` (before #41305) | 156.3 / 157.9 / 154.7 | 156.3 ms |

Recovers 4.4 ms of the 6.2 ms regression. A ~1.1 ms gap to the full revert remains: 672 of 24000 calls (gate same shape as residual) still fall through to the eager path. Can follow up separately.

The microbenchmark covers contiguous layouts only — I did not measure whether Triton also wins there at SANA-Video's sizes. If it does, the dispatch can be widened on the back of a benchmark covering the other models sharing this kernel; `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/diffusion/bench_residual_gate_add.py` already has workloads for most of them.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — no new behaviour; existing kernel tests plus the bit-exactness check above apply
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing change
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

cc @BBuf

title: [DeepSeek-V4.1] Unify mHC into one state machine and drop medium-batch fusion variants
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> (auto generated by Claude)

This refactors DeepSeek-V4.1's manifold-constrained hyper-connections into a single module (`deepseek_v4_mhc.py`): one state machine for cross-layer state, one dispatch point per mHC step, and no contextvar hooks threaded through unrelated code.

**Design**

- `HcState(streams, pre, input)` is the only thing a layer hands the next one: `streams` is the residual or (HIP fused boundary) the still-pending post, as one Union member; `input` is the next sublayer's input when the previous post already built it (`HcNormed | HcQuantized`), dropped whenever the residual is rewritten (Engram, late-layer tail).
- `DeepseekV2MoE` gains a generic `return_moe_output` that hands back a `MoEOutput` (deferred-finalize handle or raw rows, plus the pieces to merge/reduce); all mHC knowledge leaves `deepseek_v2.py` and `mhc_post_fusion.py` is deleted.
- `combine + norm` always take the one fused `hc_combine_norm` form; the 128-384 medium-batch combine-only collectives and their kernels (`all_reduce_mhc_combine`, `mhc_post_combine`) are removed.
- `layer.hc_post` routes to `mhc.post`, the single post dispatch across NPU/XPU/CUDA/HIP; gates read `HcConfig` instead of tensor shapes, and by-construction dtype/contiguity/alignment/zero-row checks move to kernel-side asserts.
- The fused collectives stage through the TP group's own `CustomAllReduceV2` push plane (registered once at load) instead of a dedicated 4 MiB plane; the per-layer fuse gates are `cached_property`, invalidated on weight updates.
- AMD: the fused boundary keeps its own gates and kernels; its fusion requests are now hard asserts rather than silent fallbacks, and a pending post crosses the late-layer tail narrowed instead of materialized (matching the previous behavior).
- Dropped for now: wide-prefill stats multistream overlap; LayerNorm SP is fenced by one assert (dsv4.1 is not in the SP allowlist).

**Fix included**: the deferred-finalize gate restructure had silently lost the fused MoE finalize+all-reduce (the mxfp4 trtllm runner is not in the `supports_deferred_finalize` whitelist); `return_moe_output` now takes the deferred path whenever that runner serves the block.

e2e validation on 4x GB300 (accuracy, decode/prefill bench, per-regime kernel traces) is running on this exact head; results will be posted as a comment.

title: [Perf] srt: Native tensor output and prefill scoring optimizations
author: t06085
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Improve the embedding and prefill-only scoring paths by preserving native-dtype embedding outputs, removing avoidable metadata and padding work, and making raw-K/V attention selection agree with the existing no-cache opt-in.

This combines four changes on current OSS `main`. The implementation commits remain separate to make each change reviewable.

Updated to `main` at `20036b7a` (merge commit `dc960f09`). `main` now carries per-request stats in `request_stats`, so `BatchEmbeddingOutput` keeps that field and adds only the PR's `tensor_embeddings`.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

1. **Native tensor embedding output.** Add optional `encoding_format` after `dimensions` in `Engine.encode()` and `async_encode()`, matching the source port without a keyword-only restriction. For dense outputs, `None` and case-insensitive `"float"` preserve list responses; other format strings retain detached CPU tensors at the model's output dtype. Carry the format through batch slicing, tokenization, scheduler admission, and mixed batches. Keep `_convert_embeddings` and `_convert_embedding_for_response` as separate steps, as in the source port. Use a dedicated typed IPC tensor field compatible with msgspec and preserve it through multi-tokenizer routing and response reconstruction. Do not add request-format normalization or HTTP/sparse-head rejection beyond the source port.
2. **Host-side FlashInfer MIS metadata.** Build relative positions, padding, and per-item maxima on the CPU, where delimiter indices already reside. Transfer each completed metadata tensor to the device once, preserving metadata dtypes, shapes, prefix-cache offsets, and position updates.
3. **Explicit FA raw-K/V gate.** Require `get_schedule().prefill_only_disable_kv_cache` in `fa_skip_kv_cache`, retaining the existing embedding, unchunked-prefill, disabled-radix-cache, and non-MLA conditions. Internal auto-enables such as EmbeddingGemma continue to work.
4. **Skip padded-tail zeroing for unquantized dense CUDA models.** Avoid per-layer tail-zeroing operations only on CUDA, for models with no MoE layers and no quantization (`quant_config` and `model_config.quantization` both unset). Retain zeroing for non-CUDA devices, CUDA MoE (including mixed dense/MoE layer lists), and every quantized model: the eager attention output tail is uninitialized graph-pool memory, and per-tensor dynamic activation quantization reduces its amax over all padded rows. Preserve the separate idle-rank/zero-real-token output-zeroing path.

**Intentional behavior change:** embedding configurations that previously selected raw-K/V attention implicitly now use paged attention unless `--prefill-only-disable-kv-cache` is enabled. Already-opted-in configurations retain their existing path.

**Scope:** unrelated VSA imports, FastAPI telemetry, and HiCache fixes and their tests are excluded. Existing attention and multimodal tests receive only the fixture fields required by the ported code (`moe_layers=[]` and `encoding_format=None`). The GPU tensor-encoding regression comes from the source port; the additional encoding unit-test file and padded-tail test cases are removed.

The tensor format is an in-process API, not a new JSON wire encoding:

```python
# Using an already initialized dense embedding engine:
result = engine.encode("A short document", encoding_format="tensor")
embedding = result["embedding"]  # CPU torch.Tensor, preserving output dtype
```

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

- [x] Local code review completed.

Combined CPU/component regression command:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q --disable-warnings \
  test/registered/prefill_only/test_multi_item_scoring_metadata.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_fa_skip_kv_cache_gating.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/test_radix_attention.py \
  test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_gpu_feature_transport.py \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_embedding.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_multi_tokenizer_mixin.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_msgpack_ipc_roundtrip.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_io_struct.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_output_streamer_customized_info.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_batch_result_processor_hidden_states.py \
  test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner_helpers.py
```

**Result after merging `main` at `20036b7a`: 315 passed; 138 subtests passed** (on an H100 pod, so the 2 GPU-only tests skipped on CPU also run).

Additional local-only conversion and IPC checks outside the PR: **10 passed; 33 subtests passed.** These exercise FP16/BF16/FP32 dtype preservation, mixed formats, case-insensitive and non-float source semantics, variable output shapes, request slicing, both IPC codecs, and stream-to-router-to-tokenizer reconstruction. They are not added to the repository.

Compared the tensor port's changed lines against the source: all ten files match, apart from formatter-only wrapping and unchanged import ordering. The earlier `retraction_counts` forwarding is no longer needed: `main`'s `request_stats` carries it.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q --disable-warnings --collect-only \
  test/registered/prefill_only/test_embedding_models.py
```

**Result: 3 tests collected**, including the source port's default-vs-tensor GPU cosine-parity regression. Collection is not a GPU accuracy result.

Formatting and lint commands, all **passed** on the 18 changed Python files:

```bash
git diff --name-only upstream/main...HEAD -- '*.py' | xargs ruff check --select F401,F821,F823,UP037
git diff --name-only upstream/main...HEAD -- '*.py' | xargs ruff format --check
git diff --name-only upstream/main...HEAD -- '*.py' | xargs isort --check-only
git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
```

The full pre-commit hook suite was not run. ROCm hardware execution remains pending; GPU/ROCm CI is required before merging.

**Padded-tail check on H100** (Qwen3-0.6B served as an embedding model, prefill CUDA graph enabled, 2 runs per row). Each run encodes four short prompts, then a 1,500-word prompt three times, then the short prompts again; "history drift" is the largest change between the two encodings of the same prompt. The "skipped" rows force the gate in-process to reproduce the previous behavior.

| Model | Tail zeroing | History drift | Max abs diff vs eager |
|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 | skipped (this PR) | 0 | 2.9e-3 (min cos 0.99992), bit-identical to zeroed |
| bf16 | zeroed (`main`) | 0 | 2.9e-3 (min cos 0.99992) |
| FP8 online, per-tensor dynamic | zeroed (this PR) | 0 | 0 |
| FP8 online, per-tensor dynamic | skipped (previous revision) | 0 | 0 |

The FP8 corruption did not reproduce in this run, since the stale tail held finite values, but zeroing is kept for quantized models because nothing guarantees that. Environment caveat: the pod mirror lacked the pinned wheels, so this used torch 2.13.0+cu130 and sglang-kernel 0.4.8 with `SGLANG_SKIP_SGL_KERNEL_VERSION_CHECK=1`, built without Rust extensions.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

Padded-tail zeroing (change 4), H100, Qwen3-0.6B embedding, 300 sequential ~150-word requests, 2 runs per row:

| Model | Tail zeroing | p50 | p90 |
|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 | eager (no prefill graph) | 15.2–15.7 ms | 15.6–16.1 ms |
| bf16 | skipped (this PR) | **6.27–6.38 ms** | **6.34–6.72 ms** |
| bf16 | zeroed (`main`) | 6.56–6.58 ms | 6.77–6.80 ms |
| FP8 | zeroed (this PR) | 6.54–6.59 ms | 6.70–6.90 ms |
| FP8 | skipped (previous revision) | 6.34–6.49 ms | 6.43–6.63 ms |

No other hardware performance measurement is claimed for this upstream port.

- Tensor output avoids conversion to Python floats; default float-only batches retain the existing bulk `.tolist()` path.
- MIS metadata construction removes small eager device-side arithmetic operations.
- Unquantized dense CUDA padded buckets avoid a tail-zeroing operation per attention layer; quantized, MoE, and non-CUDA models keep it.
- The explicit raw-K/V gate intentionally moves previously implicit users to paged attention, which may add KV-cache costs until they opt in.

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [KDA] Add an opt-in decode-parity mode to the Triton multi-token recurrence
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

A speculative-decoding target verify runs `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` over a chain of candidate tokens in one launch and keeps the recurrent state in FP32 for the whole chain. Decode runs one token per launch and, with a BF16 state pool, persists BF16 after every token. Both compute the same recurrence, but not the same numbers: after a few tokens the verify states no longer match the states the decode path would have produced from the same tokens, so the verified logits drift away from the decode logits. When decode runs on FlashInfer's `recurrent_kda` CuTe DSL kernel (`--linear-attn-decode-backend flashinfer`) the gap widens further, because that kernel forms its gate in base 2 with `ex2.approx`/`lg2.approx`, reduces the Q/K norms lane-striped with packed f32x2 FMA, decays and updates the state through FMA, and receives beta already sigmoided.

This PR gives the shared Triton recurrence an opt-in decode-parity mode so a KDA multi-token verify (the Triton verify is still the only chain-plus-tree KDA verify) can reproduce that decode kernel step for step instead of approximating it.

## Modifications

- `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update(..., match_cutedsl_decode=False)`: a new keyword, off by default. The default path is byte-for-byte the previous instruction sequence. When set (KDA softplus gate only):
  - a BF16 state pool is rounded to BF16 after every token of a multi-token launch (`ROUND_STATE_TO_BF16`, derived from the pool dtype, so an FP32 pool keeps the FP32 accumulator);
  - `b` is taken as the already-sigmoided FP32 beta;
  - the gate multiplier is `ex2.approx.ftz(-exp(A_log) * lg2.approx.ftz(1 + exp(x)))`, with `exp` itself formed through `ex2.approx.ftz`;
  - the Q/K sum of squares is reduced lane-striped (lane `l` owns `l + i * 32`, even and odd `i` streams accumulate separately through FMA, then a 32-lane sum) followed by `rsqrt`;
  - state decay and the rank-1 update go through explicit `tl.fma`.
- `match_cutedsl_decode` with `is_kda=False` or with the safe gate (`lower_bound`) raises instead of compiling a half-defined mode, and the lane-striped reduction static-asserts `head_k_dim <= 128`.
- Nothing is switched to the new mode here: `KDAAttnBackend` and `TritonKDAKernel.target_verify` are unchanged. The in-tree `cutedsl_kda.py` decode kernel forms its gate in natural-log form and reduces norms one element per thread, so against that backend only the per-token BF16 rounding part of this mode is bit-relevant.

## Accuracy Tests

New `TestKDAVerifyDecodeParity` in `test/registered/attention/test_kda_kernels.py` (same CI registration as the file):

- with a BF16 state pool, a 16-token verify launch in parity mode is bitwise equal, outputs and all cached intermediate states, to 16 single-token launches in parity mode (head_k_dim 128 and 64);
- the default path is not: its cached states differ from the single-token launches at the BF16 level while the outputs still agree within the usual tolerance, which is the drift described above;
- an FP32 state pool in parity mode is also bitwise equal to the single-token launches and is not rounded to BF16.

Run locally on a Blackwell GPU: the whole of `test/registered/attention/test_kda_kernels.py` passes (18 tests, 5 subtests), including the existing default-path references; `test_gdn_noncontiguous_stride.py` and `test_fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py`, which share the kernel's default path, pass as well.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured here. The mode is opt-in and off by default, and the default path's instruction sequence is unchanged.

title: [unified-memory] Copy page envelopes in place during compaction
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

`UnifiedMHATokenToKVPool.move_kv_cache` and `UnifiedMLATokenToKVPool.move_kv_cache` relocate whole page envelopes when the allocator compacts the unified pool. They do it with a gather/scatter on a `[num_pages, page_bytes]` view of the raw buffer (`env[tgt] = env[src]`), which materialises a temporary the size of every moved page before writing it back. With MiB-scale envelopes and many pages per compaction that is a payload-sized GPU allocation on the compaction path, taken from the same device the pool was sized to fill.

## Modifications

- Add `sglang/kernels/ops/kvcache/copy_pages.py`: a Triton kernel that copies the listed page envelopes within the pool buffer directly, one program per (page pair, block of words). It views the buffer as int64 words when the page size and storage offset are 8-byte aligned and falls back to a byte view otherwise, so no layout is rejected. The CPU path keeps the existing gather/scatter.
- Both unified `move_kv_cache` overrides call it instead of building the envelope view. Every byte of the envelope moves, including any per-page metadata, exactly as before.

The kernel requires unique destinations disjoint from the source set. The allocator already guarantees this for compaction moves: destinations are taken from free space, and overlapping shifts are issued as ordered single-page moves. First use compiles the Triton kernel.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the copy is byte-exact and the existing tests assert raw-byte equality after `move_kv_cache`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The change removes the payload-sized temporary; the kernel itself is a plain strided copy. Checked on one NVIDIA GPU with a throwaway script against the gather/scatter reference: the int64 and byte paths, unaligned storage offsets, strided and int32 page-id tensors, empty copies, a non-default stream, and bytes past the envelope region all match the reference byte for byte, and peak extra allocation during the copy is only the page-id tensors.

Unit tests run locally, each file in its own process:

```bash
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_mha_views.py        # 23 passed (CPU path)
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_mla_views.py        # 20 passed (CPU path)
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_mla_gpu_parity.py   # 4 passed, exercises the kernel on GPU
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_tri_pool.py         # 47 passed
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_multi_ended_allocator.py    # 98 passed
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_pd_envelope_transfer_layout.py test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_layout_compat.py test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_handout_zeroing.py
```

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). No new test: `test_move_kv_cache_relocates_whole_envelopes`, `test_move_kv_cache_moves_page_envelopes` and `test_move_kv_cache_page_envelope_gpu` already cover the overrides on both paths.

title: [diffusion] Fix native FP8 format handling for FLUX 3 rowwise linears
author: Tokha233
body:
## Motivation

The MI300 diffusion unit run on #42121 fails the FLUX 3 FP8r checkpoint test with `Expected b.dtype() == at::kFloat8_e4m3fnuz, got Float8_e4m3fn` ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37030627223/job/110916375120)). The rowwise linear currently passes serialized E4M3FN weights and activations directly to `_scaled_mm`, although gfx94 requires FNUZ. ModelOpt already normalizes that format, but two of its regression tests still assume FN and unadjusted scales.

## Modifications

- Normalize FLUX 3 FP8r weights at load time on FNUZ platforms and match activation format before `_scaled_mm`, reusing the existing FN-to-FNUZ helper. Both scales are adjusted; negative zero is normalized to avoid NaN. Clone checkpoint weights before the helper's in-place byte normalization.
- Preserve the CUDA FN path and the serialized FP8r format.
- Cover both native formats, padded zero rows, tensor/tuple outputs, exact dequantized values and checkpoint immutability. Update ModelOpt tests to verify native dtype/scales and dequantized equivalence, including negative zero and CPU offload.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested on an isolated RTX 5090 D v2 host, Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, based on upstream `f6fcda8`.

- New FLUX format regressions against unchanged production code: **2 failed / 2 passed**; only the FNUZ contract cases fail.
- Candidate: `test_flux3_action.py`, `test_modelopt_fp8_layerwise_offload_load.py`, `test_transformer_quant.py`: **107 passed, 24 subtests passed**. Includes the real CUDA FP8 `_scaled_mm` checkpoint forward.
- FNUZ contract tests use CPU tensors and a checked/dequantized GEMM substitute; they are **not MI300 GPU execution**. ModelOpt tests parameterize format conversion and check exact dequantized values.

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_flux3_action.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_modelopt_fp8_layerwise_offload_load.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_transformer_quant.py
```

Please authorize AMD CI to verify the actual MI300 GEMM/offload path. This fixes the concrete format mismatch; it does not yet establish that the separate full FLUX Action non-finite-output failure is resolved. No thresholds or tolerances were relaxed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Compatibility fix; no throughput claim. CUDA uses its existing FP8 path. The FNUZ path adds format normalization to make the previously invalid GEMM operands usable.

- [x] Changed-file pre-commit checks pass.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Accuracy results and platform limits documented above.

title: [Speculative] Add opt-in block verification
author: maocheng23
body:
## Motivation

Add the block verifier from [Block Verification Accelerates Speculative Decoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10444), Algorithm 2. Standard rejection sampling stops at the first rejected draft token. Block verification selects the longest accepted prefix and can accept a longer prefix after an earlier rejection, with a scaled correction distribution that preserves target sampling.

## Modifications

- Add opt-in `--speculative-use-block-verification`; this flag automatically enables the required proposal sampling and draft-probability storage. `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` alone selects token-wise rejection sampling, and passing both flags remains supported. Support the existing linear EAGLE/EAGLE3/NEXTN proposal path (`--speculative-eagle-topk 1`) on CUDA/ROCm, with startup validation for unsupported configurations.
- Extend the existing Triton chain sampler with a compile-time branch. Compute `r_i = min(1, r_(i-1) * p(x_i) / q(x_i))` forward, then test prefixes longest-first and stop at the first acceptance. The original per-prefix random samples are retained, so skipped shorter-prefix tests cannot change the selected prefix. Commit that prefix once and sample correction from normalized `(r_tau * p - q)+`; full acceptance samples the bonus token from the target.
- Skip a prefix's vocabulary reduction when its coin is already at least `r_i`, using `h_i <= r_i` for normalized distributions. Reuse the selected prefix's residual mass for correction normalization. Use a separate reduction tile capped at 32768 with 8 warps for large vocabularies; keep the final CDF tile at 4096. Token verification retains its original acceptance loop and 4-warps launch.
- Add a reproducible sampler benchmark with optional comparison against a saved baseline kernel.
- Reuse proposal buffers, output indices, TP synchronization, and the greedy verification path. No scheduler or KV-cache changes; the existing verification defaults remain unchanged.
- Document the option and add focused kernel and configuration tests.

## Accuracy Tests

The optimized sampler at `42d866ccd5` was validated on one NVIDIA GB300 (Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1):

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_block_verification.py \
  test/registered/unit/spec/test_block_verification_args.py
```

**25 passed, 12 configuration subtests passed.** Coverage includes both token/block paths against a reference, accepting past an earlier rejection, longest-prefix selection for every accepted length, strict acceptance-threshold boundaries (including `h_i == r_i`), scaled residuals, zero/unit probabilities, zero/one/multiple drafts, strided tensors, vocabulary tails up to 131073, and global output-index mapping. Statistical tests use 65,536 samples each to check the paper's expected acceptance lengths and the complete output joint distribution, including context-dependent targets with two and five drafts.

Compute Sanitizer memcheck passed all **17 non-statistical kernel cases with 0 errors**. An additional **4800 per-sequence comparisons** against the pre-optimization kernel covered three seeds, 0/1/3/5/8 drafts, five vocabulary sizes through 131073, and both verification modes: accepted lengths, output indices, and all valid output tokens matched exactly in these cases. This is observed parity, not a general bitwise guarantee for block verification after changing floating-point reduction order.

Independent exact rational enumeration reproduced the paper's `10/9` versus `11/9` accepted-draft example and target joint distributions for context-dependent binary models with draft lengths 1–5. A separate 42,252-case rational check validates longest-first selection and the `h_i <= r_i` shortcut across draft lengths 0–6.

Local configuration tests and CLI parsing passed. All pre-commit hooks applicable to the changed files passed; `git diff --check` passed. The full-model results below were obtained before this sampler optimization and have not been rerun on the optimized kernel. ROCm execution is not yet validated.

The subsequent CLI change (`25fca89325`) passed **17 CPU tests and 23 subtests** across block-verification configuration, EAGLE gate routing / ROCm defaults, and CLI metadata. A block-only CLI smoke test also verified that the published scheduler configuration enables both required sampler settings while preserving raw user arguments. The kernel is unchanged; GPU benchmarks were not repeated for this CLI change. Mintlify validation could not run locally because its CLI is unavailable.

The CI follow-up (`3e5cd56c29`) fixes the custom-algorithm and bootstrap-registration test fixtures. The random sampler reference now uses FP64 arithmetic and checks the final token's CDF interval with a `1e-6` probability tolerance; accepted lengths, draft tokens, and output indices remain exact. This handles FP32 boundary rounding without tolerating arbitrary token-ID differences. Validation: **57 CPU tests and 21 subtests passed**, plus **all 23 sampler tests on GB300** (Torch 2.13.0 / Triton 3.7.1). No production code changed in this follow-up; the original H100 job will be checked by the CI rerun.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Qwen3.8-27B / AIME25 end-to-end

These are historical measurements at `b40ee2c99a17341d35ff1e47684bc8a471797d74`, before the sampler optimization.

| Metric | Token-wise | Block | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Acceptance length (includes bonus) | 2.9802 | 3.0063 | +0.88% |
| Output throughput (tokens/s) | 988.43 | 995.36 | +0.70% |
| Boxed score over entire response | 76/90 (84.44%) | 77/90 (85.56%) | +1.11 pp |
| Boxed score after `</think>` | 70/90 (77.78%) | 65/90 (72.22%) | -5.56 pp |
| Responses hitting the 32,768-token cap | 20/90 | 22/90 | |

AL increased in all three seed pairs. The pooled throughput increase is small (+0.70%); per-seed changes were +2.71%, +0.41%, and -0.99%, so this does not establish a consistent throughput speedup. The original entire-response score counts boxes inside reasoning, including 6 token-wise and 12 block responses that hit the cap. The added post-`</think>` score uses only the answer text after that marker and counts missing answers as incorrect. The 32k cap and three sampled runs limit quality comparisons; neither score difference establishes a quality change. All 23 responses without a parsed integer hit the token cap.

One NVIDIA GB300, TP1, Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B BF16 revision `1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0`, native MTP, three proposed tokens (`EAGLE`, steps=3, topk=1, draft-tokens=4). BF16 KV cache, FP32 recurrent state, FlashInfer attention and Triton GDN, CUDA graphs enabled, concurrency 8. Thinking enabled, xhigh template setting, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, maximum 32,768 new tokens. All 30 MathArena/aime_2025 questions for each of three seeds; 90 attempts per arm, 180 total.

Both arms use commit `b40ee2c99a17341d35ff1e47684bc8a471797d74` and `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling`. The block arm adds only `--speculative-use-block-verification`. Each run warms eight slots and flushes the cache before timing. Arm order alternates by seed. Startup and warmup are excluded. Incremental native streaming avoids repeatedly transferring the entire output prefix.

Acceptance length is total completion tokens / total verification steps, including the bonus token. Throughput is total output tokens / total measured wall time, including prefill and the final partially occupied batches. Both answer scores use the last boxed integer in their specified text region; cap hits are retained in the denominator. These are stochastic runs at one concurrency and draft length.

Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, sglang-kernel 0.4.8, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, Transformers 5.17.0, NVIDIA driver 590.48.01.

| Seed | Token AL | Block AL | Token tok/s | Block tok/s | Token entire-response correct | Block entire-response correct |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 980406 | 2.9725 | 3.0225 | 959.37 | 985.39 | 26/30 | 25/30 |
| 981406 | 2.9736 | 2.9890 | 995.39 | 999.45 | 25/30 | 25/30 |
| 982406 | 2.9947 | 3.0069 | 1011.64 | 1001.61 | 25/30 | 27/30 |

### Sampler microbenchmark

Paired sampler-only measurements of the pre-optimization kernel (`b40ee2c99a17341d35ff1e47684bc8a471797d74`) and optimized kernel on the same GB300, Torch 2.13.0+cu130 / Triton 3.7.1. FP32, five drafts, vocabulary 131072, `q = 0.7*p + 0.3*softmax(random logits)`, seed 2026. Each cell is the median of three `triton.testing.do_bench` runs with 100 ms warmup and 500 ms measurement; implementation order alternates between repetitions.

| Batch | Token before | Token after | Block before | Block after | Block latency reduction |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 62.08 µs | 61.97 µs | 159.69 µs | 58.07 µs | 63.6% |
| 16 | 104.81 µs | 105.12 µs | 207.87 µs | 132.83 µs | 36.1% |
| 128 | 133.91 µs | 133.39 µs | 250.78 µs | 146.25 µs | 41.7% |

Additional paired block-sampler measurements (before → after):

| Drafts | Vocabulary | Batch 1 | Batch 16 | Batch 128 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3 | 131072 | 127.61 → 57.32 µs | 163.45 → 113.39 µs | 184.65 → 131.07 µs |
| 5 | 131073 | 233.53 → 79.08 µs | 334.14 → 166.65 µs | 334.20 → 166.38 µs |

Reproduce the primary comparison:

```bash
git show b40ee2c99a17341d35ff1e47684bc8a471797d74:python/sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/reject_sampling.py > /tmp/reject_sampling_before.py
PYTHONPATH=python python benchmark/kernels/bench_block_verification.py \
  --baseline-file /tmp/reject_sampling_before.py
```

The final CDF sampling still scans vocabulary tiles; block verification additionally reduces vocabulary rows only for unresolved candidate prefixes. Longest-first selection eliminates those extra reductions when the full block is accepted. The remaining cost depends on the sampled proposals and prefix acceptance, so these results do not establish that block verification is always faster than token verification. They measure sampler cost only; the historical end-to-end results above have not been rerun after this optimization.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add registered unit tests.
- [x] Update documentation.
- [x] Provide output-distribution checks and sampler speed measurements.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style.

title: [LoRA] Reorganize kernels and add CODEOWNERS
author: jybsuper
body:
## Motivation

LoRA kernels and their tuning data are spread across the generic GEMM and MoE directories, which makes assigning LoRA-specific code ownership difficult. Group the existing LoRA implementations together so LoRA owners can maintain the kernels and their runtime assets in one place.

## Modifications

- Move LoRA Python/Triton kernels into `python/sglang/kernels/ops/lora/{dense,moe}` and the LoRA-specific CUDA sources into `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/lora`.
- Keep the experimental TRT-LLM LoRA implementation and its FlashInfer overlay together, and move CSGMV tuning data beside its loader.
- Update imports, JIT source paths, tuning output paths, tests, documentation, and registry targets. Register the 14 LoRA operations as `lora.<name>` instead of `gemm.<name>` / `moe.<name>`, matching the new operator group. No in-repository callers use the old registry IDs; external selector callers must adopt the new IDs. Kernel implementations are preserved; `virtual_experts.py` is a byte-identical move.
- Give both LoRA kernel directories the same CODEOWNERS as `python/sglang/srt/lora`.
- Correct the experimental alignment helper import left stale by the earlier helper deduplication in #40197. The selected helper has identical executable code to the removed duplicate.

## Accuracy Tests

GPU correctness and performance validation below compares the reorganization commit `22244bd872` against its OSS baseline `f6fcda8827`, using separate source snapshots on the same GPU for each pair. Wheel-packaging validation also covers `22244bd872`. The follow-up commit `d971ed8600` changes only registry IDs, ownership metadata, and documentation; it does not change kernel implementations or registry targets/backends/capabilities. GPU inference and performance tests were not rerun for that follow-up.

- At `d971ed8600`, the complete kernel namespace/registry/selector CPU test module passed on the GB300 devbox with GPUs hidden: **67 passed** in 21.33 seconds (one pytest configuration warning). The 14 LoRA registrations were also checked for unique IDs and unchanged targets/backends/capabilities; all new IDs select successfully.
- Pre-push checks for the five files changed by `d971ed8600`: passed.
- At `22244bd872`, full `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed.
- CSGMV loader: 5 existing CPU tests passed; all 7 relocated JSON files were read through exact-version and fallback lookup (14 checks with device/version discovery mocked).
- Built a Python/resource wheel with native extensions disabled: all 51 files in the LoRA kernel directories match the `22244bd872` Git blobs, including all 7 CSGMV JSONs, 4 CUDA source/header files, and 7 overlay data files. All 47 moved old paths are absent.

| GPU | Coverage | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H200 | Shipped CSGMV configs, FP16/BF16, rank 64, two adapters | All 7 configs loaded through real device discovery and Triton 3.7.1 fallback; 28 numerical cases and selected launch parameters match baseline; 4 existing CUDA graph tests pass per revision. |
| H200 | Common alignment wrapper with both experimental flags enabled | Baseline reproduces the stale import error; candidate executes the real CUDA helper and matches the semantic reference. |
| GB300 | Qwen3-4B FP16 with two trained adapters, `csgmv` and `triton` | All 12 paired generated texts exactly match; adapter requests meet the existing HF threshold. |
| GB300 | Online FP8 Qwen3-4B, both LoRA backends | Generated text matches across all 8 shape/backend cells; distinct adapter effects and decode graph execution observed. |
| B200 | Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B BF16 with trained expert-only LoRA, Triton | All 12 requests / 192 generated tokens and prompt/output logprobs exactly match. The 20 cached reference texts and maximum-logprob bounds pass; this is not a claim that the complete registered reference test ran. |
| B200 | Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 with nonzero synthetic expert-only LoRA, virtual experts, Triton | Runtime, expert adapter effects, and decode graph execution verified. Controlled batching gives exact prompt logprobs for 12/12 requests, but full decode parity is **inconclusive**: both revisions produce varying decode outputs on repeated identical inputs. Synthetic adapters test execution/parity, not trained-model quality. |

B200 used isolated matching FlashInfer Python/cubin `0.7.0.post1`, CUDA 13.0 JIT cache and SM100a provider, plus `sglang-kernel==0.4.8`; version checks were not bypassed.

Known failures and coverage limits:

- The existing dense no-adapter HF ROUGE mismatch (0.7655 versus 1.0) occurs identically on both revisions.
- FP8 MoE initially matched 10/12 generated sequences with different scheduler batch composition. Under controlled batching, prompt logprobs match for 12/12 requests and full generated sequences for 11/12. Repeated identical inputs still produce different decode outputs within each revision, including the unchanged baseline, so full decode parity remains inconclusive.
- Full experimental TRT-LLM overlay execution remains unverified. Both versions retain a reference to `trtllm_fused_moe_routing_custom.cu`, removed by FlashInfer 0.7. Path resolution at `22244bd872` and all nine overlay files (`jit.py`, `SOURCE.md`, and seven data files) are verified; ordinary FlashInfer execution does not cover the custom overlay.
- Earlier broader GPU testing reproduced an out-of-bounds alignment error for invalid expert IDs on both the original baseline and the then-current reorg snapshot. It is not fixed here; those earlier test counts are not presented as passes for `22244bd872`.
- No NVFP4/4-bit Marlin end-to-end validation in this matrix.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GB300 FP16 serving used ABBA ordering with both LoRA backends, batch sizes 1/8, input lengths 128/1024, and 64 output tokens. Each cell has six measured samples per revision after warmup, with startup and initial JIT excluded. All 96 measured segments contain decode CUDA graph evidence, and outputs match exactly.

Across the eight cells, candidate median latency changes range from **-0.11% to +0.22%** (positive means slower). No material regression was observed within this matrix. H200's 28 CSGMV graph microbenchmarks have a worst median latency change of **+0.24%**.

Online FP8 and MoE timing samples are diagnostic only; they do not establish broad performance parity across quantization modes or backends.

title: [Fix] Step-3.5 DeepEP routed scaling and Sarvam shared expert under dense TP1
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42312
* #42311
* #42310
* #42309
* #42308
* #42307
* #42306
* #42305
* #42304
* #42303
* __->__ #42302
* #42301
* #42300

## Motivation

Two independent defects found while migrating these models to stage boundaries, both on `main` today.

## Modifications

**Step-3.5, DeepEP path does not apply the routed scaling factor.** The non-DeepEP path scales the routed experts' output by `routed_scaling_factor`; the DeepEP path returns the combine result unscaled, so every DeepEP run produces a differently weighted mixture. The gate is also computed in a lower precision than the non-DeepEP path.

**Sarvam counts the shared expert twice under `--moe-dense-tp-size 1`.** With a fully-DP dense FFN the shared expert is replicated on every rank, and the MoE output still owes a TP sum, so the replicated part is multiplied by the TP width. Build the shared expert sharded over TP when the output still owes a sum.

## Accuracy Tests

Both are verified against a TP1 reference on H200. The Step-3.5 scaling fix brings the DeepEP path back to the non-DeepEP output; the Sarvam fix brings `--moe-dense-tp-size 1` back to the default dense TP layout.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change to the collective sequence; the Sarvam fix shards a replicated GEMM, which is less work per rank.

author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42312

## Motivation

Two independent defects on `main`.

## Modifications

- **Jet-Nemotron no longer builds or runs.** Fix the construction so the model loads again.
- **Granite MoE hybrid re-adds a stale residual in its final norm.** The layer stack's last output already carries the residual; adding it again in the final norm counts it twice.

## Accuracy Tests

**The Granite final-norm fix changes this model's output, by design.** Granite MoE hybrid h-1b at TP2 produces different logits from `main`, and the change comes from this fix alone: `main` normalized the stream plus a second copy of the last layer's pre-FFN stream, and one of those two addends should not be there. The models without a MoE are otherwise bitwise identical to the parent, and h-tiny's output is verified against a TP1 reference.

Jet-Nemotron builds and runs at TP1, which it does not do on the parent at all -- there it raises `TypeError: JetNemotronDecoderLayer.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'start_layer'` during construction.

**TP > 1 is out of scope for Jet-Nemotron and still does not work**, for a reason this PR does not touch: its linear-attention block splits the `qkvabz_proj` output with `total_k_dim` / `total_v_dim` / `num_heads` taken straight from the config, while the projection is a `MergedColumnParallelLinear` whose output is sharded, so at TP2 the split sizes sum to exactly twice the tensor width. `A_log` and `dt_bias` are allocated unsharded for the same reason. That is pre-existing on `main` and is only observable now that the model gets past construction.
