title: [Refactor] Let the remaining placement consumers read the parallel context
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* __->__ #42348
* #42347
* #42346

## Motivation

Placement values (ranks, widths, process groups) are threaded through constructors and stored as copies, so a reader cannot tell which copy is authoritative and a copy can go stale. This is the last batch of consumers that were still handed placement instead of reading it where they run.

It also makes one latent class of bug loud: several layers shard their weights over the attention-TP group but all-reduce over the full TP group. The two groups differ only when attention DP or attention CP makes attention TP narrower than TP, and there the reduction mixes ranks that hold other requests.

## Modifications

**Consumers read their own placement.**
- `MoeRunnerConfig` carries the layer it belongs to, and the FlashInfer CUTLASS (standard and MXFP4) and HPC-Ops fused funcs read the MoE placement off it. Seven quant-info producers stop copying four fields on every apply. The layer is the single address: DWDP's `bind_full_expert_weights` updates it alone, and the CompressedTensors MXINT4 scheme follows that bind instead of recording the deployment rank at construction.
- `get_dp_tp_group()` replaces six inline copies of "the attention-TP group under attention DP, otherwise the TP group".
- Scheduler components take their groups from the parallel context. Components whose reads can land inside PD multiplexing's prefill scope keep the handle they were built with, which is the group they used before.
- The KV cache builder, the HiCache controller, the KV senders and the LoRA memory pool read their own placement; `LoRAInfo` drops fields that `fully_sharded` being always false made dead.

**A layer that shards over attention TP must reduce over it.** `reject_attn_tp_shard_with_tp_reduce` refuses such a layer at construction, before weights load, naming both group widths and the ways out. It covers `VisionAttention` and the CLIP, PhiMoE, Step3 and MoonViT layers that reduce over TP, and the Qwen3-VL and MiniMax-VL layers that reduce over attention TP only under attention DP. IQuest-Q1 is checked only when its attention owns the reduction (`reduce_results=True`): the decoder now returns partial outputs to its attention boundary. EXAONE-MoE already delegates its attention reduction to that boundary on current `main`, so it is not gated. Each site keeps a TODO: the real fix is to reduce over the attention-TP group so these models can run those layouts.

Most models build their multimodal tower unconditionally, and several kinds of worker hold one they never forward: an encoder-disaggregated language instance, a language-model-only instance, and a PD decode instance, which embeds nothing. The encoder sites say they are encoders and `multimodal_encoder_runs_here` answers for all three, so none of them is refused over a reduction it never reaches. Adaptive dispatch is the exception on the first: it keeps the requests it does not send to the encoder and forwards the tower for them, so that layout is still checked. Text attention is checked on every worker, including a language-only one, where its output projection runs just the same.

The MiMo audio encoder is exempt for now, with a TODO: it shards over attention TP and reduces over TP, and refusing it would refuse MiMo-V2.5's documented `--tp 8 --attn-dp-size 2` deployment.

**Deprecation.** `--dp-size N` under DeepSeek context parallelism still means N attention-DP groups and now logs a deprecation warning; it will be rejected after 2026-12-31. `ServerArgs.resolved_dict` keeps reporting the deprecated `enable_dp_attention` for clients that read it from `/server_info`, so `--enable-dp-attention` beside `--attn-dp-size` is redundant rather than rejected and a config read back resolves to the same layout.

## Compatibility

Two deliberate changes in observable behaviour:

- **Some configurations now refuse to start.** A model that builds one of the layers above refuses a layout where attention TP is narrower than TP, which today starts and computes the wrong reduction. Concretely, that is a multimodal model with `--attn-dp-size` between 1 and `--tp-size`, or with `--attn-cp-size` greater than 1, on a worker that forwards its tower; and PhiMoE text attention at the same widths; an IQuest-Q1 attention that owns its reduction is checked too. `--attn-dp-size` equal to `--tp-size` and `--mm-enable-dp-encoder` are unaffected. No cookbook recipe is affected: the deployments documented for these models either set `--attn-dp-size` equal to `--tp-size` or are MiMo, which is exempt for now.
- **`/server_info` reports `enable_dp_attention` again.** It had become `false` under attention DP when `--attn-dp-size` replaced the flag; it now reports whether an attention-DP width is configured, as before, until the flag is removed after 2026-12-31. `dp_size` keeps its new meaning of replicas, so a client counting DP ranks should read `dp_size * attn_dp_size`.

## Accuracy Tests

The results below precede the landing rebase. That rebase retains upstream DeepSeek-V4 HIP validation, conditions the IQuest-Q1 gate on ownership of the reduction, and removes the obsolete EXAONE-MoE gate/test after its boundary migration. Tests and benchmarks were not rerun for landing.

H200, this PR vs its base.

| model | config | GSM8K this PR / base |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite, `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass` | `--tp 2` | 0.380 / 0.390, 0.370 |
| same | `--tp 2 --ep-size 2` | 0.377 / 0.387, 0.367 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite, default runner backend | `--tp 2` | 0.387 / 0.387, 0.380, 0.383 |
| gpt-oss-20b, `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4` | `--tp 2` | 0.537 / 0.557, 0.530 |
| same | `--tp 2 --ep-size 2` | 0.580, 0.580 / 0.577, 0.570, 0.577, 0.580 |
| Qwen3-8B | `--tp 2`, `--tp 2 --attn-dp-size 2` | 0.950 / 0.953, 0.947 |

Greedy output is not deterministic for these models, so each configuration was run several times on the base: every difference seen against this PR is reproduced between base runs alone. A probe on the kernel boundary shows the FlashInfer CUTLASS call receives identical `tp_size/tp_rank/ep_size/ep_rank` per rank on both sides in all four MoE configurations.

Qwen3-VL-2B with a real image answers identically to the base, md5-for-md5, at `--tp 2`, `--tp 2 --attn-dp-size 2`, and with `--mm-enable-dp-encoder`; Kimi-K2.5's MoonViT encoder likewise. DeepSeek CP resolution warns exactly once per deprecated spelling and rejects replicas combined with attention DP before warning. `/server_info` reports the same layout for both spellings, and every readback re-resolves to the same layout.

`test/registered/unit` at this PR's head, compared with its base: no new failures.

**Not exercised.** Five of the nine quant producers that stopped copying placement have no checkpoint here or need Blackwell (ModelOpt FP8 and NVFP4, CompressedTensors NVFP4 and MXINT4, SM120 CUTLASS); their kwargs are unchanged and were read from the same layer before. The gated layers in MiniMax-VL, Step3, PhiMoE and IQuest-Q1 have no checkpoint either, so the check on them is covered by unit tests against the layer classes rather than a server. DWDP's full-expert bind is covered by a unit test that runs the fused func, not by a DWDP deployment.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

title: [diffusion] Name the quality tiers after what they guarantee
author: mickqian
body:
## Why

`quality` named its strictest tier `lossless` and the tier above it
`extra-high`, which reads as if the faster tier gives up quality. It does not.
The fusions that tier mounts compute the same function; their rounding is no
further from the exact value than the reference's own rounding is, and the
reference path is only one sample of that rounding — it already moves with the
cuBLAS version, the GPU model and the parallel layout, so a TP2 run can never
be bit-identical to a single-card HF reference anyway. Bit-identical output
describes reproducibility, which is worth keeping as its own tier, not quality.

## What

Tiers are named after what they guarantee, and each level includes the ones
before it:

| tier | guarantee | admits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exact` | bit-identical to the reference path in the same environment | scheduling, placement, data movement, reuse of strictly invariant values |
| `lossless` (default) | the same math and the same operand and accumulator precision; only the place or order of the rounding moves | fusions, other kernels, reassociated reductions, higher intermediate precision |
| `high` | may change what is computed | lower precision, sparsity, reuse across steps |

`extra-high` is kept as an alias of `lossless`. **Two things change for
existing callers.** A request that passed `quality="lossless"` for
bit-identical output has to pass `quality="exact"` now: that name is reused,
not just renamed. And `lossless` is the default, so a deployment that never
set `quality` moves off the bit-exact path onto it. In-repo callers are
updated.

### The mechanisms now match the tiers

`BitExactFusionGate` backs paths that are bit-exact by construction and says so
— that is the `exact` tier's mechanism, and its first-sight check exists to
catch a dispatch that changed underneath it. `QualityGatedFusion` mounts per
request, and every entry in `_QUALITY_FUSION_HANDLERS` now declares the lowest
tier that may mount it, instead of one boolean for "any fusion".

Three of the thirteen do not belong where that boolean put them and move to
`high`:

- **FLUX.2 NVFP4 FC1+SwiGLU+quant** quantizes FC2's input before the reference
  BF16 intermediate exists.
- **Ideogram's BF16-native gate RMSNorm** rounds norm statistics the reference
  (`F.rms_norm`) keeps in fp32.
- **SANA-Video BF16-input linear attention** feeds BF16 to a GEMM the reference
  promotes to FP32.

The other ten keep the reference's math and precision and stay in `lossless`.
No fusion moves into `exact`: the default mounts nothing it did not mount
before.

### One admission template instead of per-case tolerances

`test/quality_tier_admission.py`. A hand-picked `atol` cannot separate the two
cases the tier is about — a reassociated reduction and a kernel that dropped
mantissa bits both land "close". The template scores every implementation
against an fp64 evaluation of the same math and judges the candidate against
the path the model runs today: no more than 1.5x its RMS and max error, and no
systematic sign in the error, since a biased rounding accumulates over layers
and steps where a symmetric one cancels. It also pins NaN/Inf/non-contiguous
behavior and exposes a flip rate for the case where a quantizer or threshold
reads the output.

The static conditions stay a review gate: an accumulation below fp32, a lowered
operand precision or a less stable formulation is approximate by construction
and no tolerance admits it. The end-to-end drift band needs a server run and
stays with the model's consistency suite.

### The two library defaults underneath the tiers

`torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32` and
`allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction` are approximate by the definitions
above, and the runtime never set either, leaving every tier's contract to
whichever PyTorch is installed. Each worker now sets both from
`--allow-cudnn-tf32` / `--allow-bf16-reduced-precision-reduction` and logs what
it runs. They stay process-global because they are: a server mixes tiers across
concurrent batches.

The defaults keep PyTorch's own values. Turning TF32 off moves fp32
convolutions — the VAE decoders that default to `vae_precision="fp32"` — off
tensor cores, so making the strict setting the default would slow `exact` down
to buy a guarantee it does not currently promise. A deployment that wants it
passes both as false.

## Validation (1xB200, FLUX.1-dev 1024x1024, 20 steps, seed 42)

The default tier has to be no slower than it was, so it is checked for being
the *same computation*, interleaved main/PR/main/PR on one box:

| arm | output md5 | ms/step |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `origin/main`, default (`lossless`) | `f1e7e33bd68a9558…` | 72 |
| this PR, default (`exact`) | `f1e7e33bd68a9558…` | 69 |
| `origin/main`, default, repeat | `f1e7e33bd68a9558…` | — |
| this PR, default, repeat | `f1e7e33bd68a9558…` | 69 |

Bit-identical output across the four arms: the default runs the same kernels,
and its denoise stage lands at 1.80–1.84 s either way. The tier system itself
works on the same build — `--quality lossless` mounts the fused linear+GELU and
moves to 66 ms/step with a different md5 at 34.5 dB against the exact output
(rounding-level, as the tier claims), and `--quality extra-high` reproduces the
`lossless` output bit for bit, so the alias resolves.

### Why `lossless` is the default

The default already ran 58 unconditionally-mounted fused kernels; what it
withheld were the 13 request-gated ones. Measured on FLUX.1-dev, 1xB200,
interleaved, same seed:

| | output md5 | steady rate |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| default before (`exact`) | `fb4c78b8…` | 14.39 it/s |
| default after (`lossless`) | `f3bf24b8…` | **14.97 it/s** |
| after, with `--quality exact` | **`fb4c78b8…`** — bit-identical to the old default | 14.38 it/s |
| BCG, default before | `fb4c78b8…` | 18.21 it/s |
| BCG, default after | `f3bf24b8…` | **21.96 it/s** |
| BCG, `--quality exact` | **`fb4c78b8…`** | 13.85 it/s |

The default gets faster on both paths, and `exact` still reproduces the old
default bit for bit, so the strict contract costs a request parameter rather
than being lost.

**Flipping it required closing a silent hole first.** A breakable CUDA graph
bakes in whichever fusions were mounted when it was captured, warmup captures
at the default level, and the capture signature covers only tensors. Once the
default mounts fusions, an `exact` request would unmount them and then replay
the fused graph anyway. The old guard could not catch that: it fired on
"something is mounted", which is exactly what an `exact` request is not. The
BCG runner is now keyed by `(module, level)`, so a level warmup never captured
finds an empty runner and takes the eager fallback the runner already has. The
last row above is that fix under test — without it the md5 there would read
`f3bf24b8…`. Removing the old guard also ends the rule that `quality` and BCG
were mutually exclusive.

**Known cost, deliberately not addressed here:** the 79 server cases that take
the default now compare against goldens recorded on the exact path. The image
thresholds are PSNR 28 / SSIM 0.95 and the measured drift is 34.5 dB, so they
pass, but the regression budget is thinner until the goldens are refreshed.

### The tier assignments, measured

Each fusion's tier above was read off what it does to the numbers. The
admission gate then scored those transformations on **real FLUX.1-dev MLP
activations** captured at the fused GELU site (4096x3072 bf16, max/p99 = 8.1,
so the outlier channels are present), against an fp64 evaluation of the same
math and relative to the path the model runs today:

| classified | transformation | RMS error vs the reference path's | gate |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| `lossless` | fused linear+GELU (cublasLt epilogue) | **0.66x** | pass |
| `lossless` | reassociated fp32 reduction (split-K shape) | 0.98x | pass |
| `lossless` | per-token gated residual (Helios / LingBot) | **1.01x** | pass |
| `high` | bf16-accumulated norm statistics (Ideogram) | ~3.8e4 x | reject |
| `high` | BF16-input attention GEMM (SANA-Video) | ~9.9e3 x | reject |
| `high` | quantized FC2 input (FLUX.2 NVFP4) | ~6.9e5 x | reject |

The GEMM epilogue comes out *more* accurate than the reference chain, which is
what the tier predicts: it rounds once where the reference rounds the GEMM
output and then the GELU output. The gated residual is the case that could not
be settled by reading the code -- it moves one rounding earlier, so the
taxonomy only admits it if it measures that way, and at 1.01x it does.

The two groups separate by three to six orders of magnitude, so none of these
verdicts sits near the 1.5x threshold. `test/unit/test_quality_tier_boundary.py`
keeps them honest in CI on DiT-shaped activations.

### The end-to-end gate: the tier moves the pixels less than the GPU count does

The operator-level numbers above say the rounding is small. Whether that is
*small enough* is the tier's end-to-end question, and the standard for it is
the drift the reference path already shows between two legal environments.
Measured on the same box, FLUX.1-dev, same seed:

| comparison | PSNR |
| --- | --- |
| control: `exact` TP1 vs `exact` TP1 again | bit-identical |
| **the band**: `exact` TP1 vs `exact` **TP2** | **32.5 dB** |
| the tier: `exact` vs `lossless`, TP1 | 34.5 dB |
| the tier: `exact` vs `lossless`, TP2 | 37.3 dB |
| both at once: `exact` TP1 vs `lossless` TP2 | 33.0 dB |

Higher PSNR is a smaller difference, so switching tier (34.5 / 37.3 dB) changes
the image *less* than moving the same tier from one GPU to two (32.5 dB) — and
nobody treats TP2 as a quality setting. The control reruns bit-identically, so
this is not run-to-run noise. The tier's drift is inside the band, which is
what the end-to-end gate asks.

### Running the gates against the real kernels found one bug — in the gate

`assert_special_values_match` rejected the real fused linear+GELU on a NaN
input. The kernel was fine: NaN positions matched and the NaN stayed inside
its own row in both paths. The finite values differed by 3.1e-02 where one
bf16 ulp at that magnitude is 3.8e-01 — ordinary rounding — and the gate was
comparing them with `torch.allclose` defaults (rtol=1e-5), which no bf16 fast
path can meet. It now checks what it is for (NaN positions, signed infinities,
shape, exception type) and leaves magnitude to the operator-level gate. Both
real kernels pass all ten special-value cases after the fix.

Unit tests: the quality, fusion-gating, precision, admission, OpenAI-API and
partitioning tests pass (163), plus the new coverage for the taxonomy, the
alias, per-tier mounting, the admission template and the numerics policy.

title: [diffusion] move kernel validation into launchers and simplify dispatch
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Diffusion model code repeatedly scans tensor ranks, shapes, dtypes, devices and strides through `can_use_*` predicates before calling launchers that need the same information. Flattening tensors before native validation also hides errors such as swapped batch/sequence dimensions with the same element count. After #42240, residual-gate still retains unreachable alternative implementations.

## Modifications

- Remove 18 tensor capability predicates across RoPE, activation, conditioning, normalization and QKV layout. Narrow five selectors to algorithm configuration: dtype, reduction/head width and hardware capability.
- Validate original tensor dimensions in the C++ launchers for Helios RoPE, SANA FP64 RoPE, LTX-2.5 decoder RoPE, GELU+cat and VDN delta factors. Triton launchers own their input validation.
- Let Qwen native QKNorm/RoPE consume packed projection views through its existing stride-aware device implementation. Validate the complex cache rank and vector alignment in C++. Keep the first-use reference comparison independent of the candidate.
- Keep contiguous residual-gate on JIT CUDA and transposed-dense residual-gate on its tuned Triton implementation. Delete unused kernels and catch-all failure caches. Retain numerical gates, request quality, autograd/compile policy and algorithm-specific fallbacks.
- Let Ideogram pass original 4D cos/sin tables into the RoPE launcher; remove its duplicate tensor scan and flattening while retaining unsupported-layout fallback.
- Select CPU/CUDA from the actual input device. A CPU call must not enter a CUDA launcher and permanently disable a process-wide GPU fusion gate; existing Wan tests reproduce the regression before this fix and pass afterward.
- Preserve device arithmetic and launch tuning; Helios additionally instantiates its existing arithmetic for FP32. Document the selection/validation boundary in the diffusion kernel README.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    M[Model call] --> S[Platform / numerical policy / algorithm configuration]
    S --> C[CHANGED: thin JIT wrapper passes original tensors]
    C --> V[CHANGED: C++ host validates tensor relationships]
    S --> T[CHANGED: Triton launcher validates once]
    V --> K[Existing device kernel and launch tuning]
    T --> K
    S --> E[Existing reference implementation]
```

The paired Helios kernel requires matching Q/K heads and full per-token frequency tables, as produced by the attention module. Unsupported direct kernel inputs now raise before launch; the generic eager helper's arbitrary broadcasting is not a paired-kernel contract. TP RMSNorm retains the separate reference path.

This is a broad launcher cleanup, not a deletion of all backend selectors. Quantization formats, channels-last algorithms, numerical/quality policy and non-NVIDIA implementations retain their own selection. The [expanded design, remaining audit items and reproducible evidence](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/tree/bbuf/diffusion-kernel-cleanup-evidence-20261003/v2) describe the boundaries explicitly.

## Accuracy Tests

Cold-L2 benchmark revision: `290c078825`. Baseline: `5916999afbc`. Dedicated B200, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1.

| Validation | Baseline | Benchmarked revision |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full diffusion kernel directory + namespace | 3002 passed, 89 skipped, 4 failed | **3011 passed, 89 skipped, the same 4 failures** |

Both runs pass 40 subtests. The failures are the existing Ernie QKNorm/RoPE gate verification and three split-rounding/full-width NeoX/packed-KV cases in `test_rope.py`, reproduced on baseline in this environment.

- Existing Ideogram, Ernie RoPE/GeGLU and Wan model tests: **11 passed**.
- Ideogram fullgraph compilation and CUDA Graph replay with replacement inputs: passed for both tested shapes, including B=2.
- 84 cold-L2 workloads plus 7 additional model helpers: output bytes, shapes and strides match baseline in every A/B repetition.
- The previous CPU-fix revision `88882677ee` passed the full model-unit CI (3787 passed, 134 skipped, 3 xfailed, 351 subtests). Its local run additionally executes one sparse-attention ragged-tail case that fails with NaN; the same failure reproduces in the unchanged baseline. The final two-file Ideogram change is covered by the tests/benchmarks above, and the [benchmarked-revision full model-unit CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37139995184/job/111252398758) has also passed.

Validation found and fixed two PR regressions: a CPU call disabling Wan's process-wide CUDA fusion gate, and Ideogram performing model-side checks plus the new launcher checks. No input-legality tests were added. Existing numerical, layout, graph, compilation and backend-selection coverage is retained.

[Full cold-L2 report, source manifests, raw samples, profiling evidence and reproduction scripts](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/tree/bbuf/diffusion-kernel-cleanup-evidence-20261003/v3-cold-l2).

This PR was merged as `bc5a055dd7` on 2026-10-04. Its final head was `a42c97419b`, merging main `1e490772e5`. The conflict-resolution regressions passed: **7 overlay tests and 6 CLIP tests**, within **3806 diffusion unit tests and 351 subtests** (134 skips, 3 xfails). Changed-file pre-commit and [lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37192902988) passed. All final-head CUDA JIT logs were audited: **100/100 + 99/99 H100 files, 66/66 B200 files, 6/6 small-GPU files and 66/66 benchmark files**. H200 selected zero tests. Component accuracy, BCG, B200, 5090, all four single-GPU and all three dual-GPU diffusion partitions passed, some after existing retries. The last dual-GPU partition initially failed LTX2.3 ti2v latency in seven attempts. Its [bounded rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37192903261/job/111426610916) then passed **all 10 assigned generation cases on the first attempt**, with the same final-head integration checkout `3eb5e884dd`. LTX2.3 ti2v measured **277.77 ms average / 277.39 ms median denoise**, below the unchanged **300.192 / 291.348 ms** limits, and passed image consistency (minimum CLIP 0.9801, SSIM 0.7801, PSNR 22.0396). The additional IPC recovery test was skipped and provides no coverage. This was ordinary CI; cold-L2 A/B measurements are reported separately. Several AMD/NPU jobs were canceled at merge; canceled jobs are not counted as passes. The [NPU shard rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37192903089/job/111417707245) passed all four assigned cases; all four final-head NPU diffusion shards have now actually passed. Original final-head CUDA diffusion and NPU diffusion shards are now all audited as passed; AMD follow-up validation remains incomplete.

The [same-runner model A/B diagnostic](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37195886518) completed eight alternating samples under PyTorch 2.14.1, with 5x L2 eviction on both GPUs before each request. Main `1e490772e5` failed 3/4 samples; cleanup `a42c97419b` failed 4/4. Median average-denoise timing was **302.832 -> 308.924 ms (+2.01%)** and median E2E **11148.282 -> 11692.407 ms (+4.88%)**. Both variants varied substantially; these data reproduce baseline failures but do not exclude a small cleanup regression or establish the dependency upgrade as the cause. Original assertions and all failures are retained; the diagnostic job correctly failed. Candidate image checks were not reached.

The [focused H100 kernel comparison](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37197396567/job/111422045296) completed all eight ABBAABBA runs on PyTorch 2.14.1/Triton 3.8.0. All **40 BF16 workloads matched output bytes, shapes and strides**. Before **every measured invocation**, it read/wrote 250 MiB (5x L2), excluded from timing. GPU changes ranged **-0.58% to +0.31%**; all 32 default-path eager cases were faster in this measurement. Three optional `quality=high` cases added **0.410-2.212 us** (up to +5.76%). All raw measurements remain in the job log. These results do not replace the model performance and consistency gates.
 The detailed completed results below belong to the previous head `05027d0ab8`, not the final head. The B200 cold-L2 measurements are from `290c078825` on PyTorch 2.13; they have not been rerun on the merged PyTorch 2.14 stack.

CI fixes included in this branch:

- Update bootstrap/prefill sender and CLIP parallel-context fixtures for upstream constructor changes. Targeted runs passed [13 bootstrap tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37175739799), [40 prefill-allocation tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37172500683) and [6 CLIP tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37172498329).
- Compare fused-store FP8 results by representable code distance. The old 15% relative-error approximation rejects adjacent subnormals: H100 returned codes 3 and 4, a **1-ULP / 25%** difference. The test still permits at most one FP8 step and includes this boundary input. [All 14 tests passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37174338666); the kernel is unchanged. A [diagnostic](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37174121022) checked 10,485,760 random elements across 20 seeds, with maximum distance 1 ULP.
- Pin JoyAI-Echo source weights to `4187f9a53c6eff3a76c51e79bd27f70d10f7591b`: upstream removed the monolithic checkpoint, breaking fresh downloads. Initial downloads, cache repair and cache identity respect the pin. [All 6 overlay tests passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37174734623).
- Correct CUDA-only test markers and synthetic NVIDIA performance-policy fixtures on ROCm. Split all 242 AMD unit files exactly once across four existing shards, preserving assertions, retry coverage and the 30-minute step timeout. [All 220 affected tests passed on H100](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37180035574), including all 18 Qwen CUDA tests and all 3 Wan tests without skips.
- Replace the NPU wheel mirror, which returned HTTP 403, with the official Triton Ascend **3.2.2** ARM release through the existing proxy. Version and dependency constraints are unchanged. [All four diffusion shards passed on the earlier `af1c292ebd` candidate](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37177530891).

Completed verification on previous head `05027d0ab8` (October 4, 2026):

- [Lint passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37181100651), as did changed-file pre-commit. No numerical, quality or performance threshold has been increased.
- [CUDA JIT and diffusion jobs all passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37181101074). JIT file totals: H100 **100/100 + 99/99**, B200 **66/66**, benchmark **66/66**, small **6/6**. The green H200 job selects **zero tests** and provides no H200 coverage.
- Diffusion units passed **3797 tests and 351 subtests**, with 134 skips and 3 xfails; the registered bridge passed 4/4 files. Component accuracy, BCG, B200, 5090, all four single-GPU partitions, all three dual-GPU partitions and the coverage check passed (**47/47 single-GPU and 29/29 dual-GPU cases executed**). Some model cases needed the existing retry policy.
- [Qwen cache-dit passed on its first attempt](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37181101074/job/111373836276): step 49 **63.02 ms < 65.11 ms**, average denoise **80.56 ms**, E2E **4316.95 ms**, with an exact reference-image match. That partition retried Hunyuan3D load latency, not Qwen. [LTX-2.5 passed on attempt 4](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37181101074/job/111373836362) at **260.27 ms** average denoise, below the unchanged **314.148 ms** limit. [JoyAI-Echo and its entire partition passed on attempt 3](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37181101074/job/111373836350).
- [AMD](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37181100988): JIT unit **40/40 files** and benchmark **23/23 files** passed. All four single-GPU shards passed **947 + 894 + 722 + 1015 = 3578 unit tests and 351 subtests**, with 115 skips, 3 xfails and 5 deselections. All **242 files** were assigned across **61 + 61 + 60 + 60** files per shard; logs contain test records from 241 distinct files with no overlap. The remaining file is the existing CUDA-only `ltx2_vae_channels_last` exclusion. Their generation tests also passed. The slowest unit shard, including all nine real-pytest performance-failure/retry cases, finished in **24m 36s**, within the unchanged 30-minute timeout. Dual-GPU shard 0 also passed. Dual-GPU shard 1 failed on MiniMax H3's missing ROCm platform branch, a quantization/linear circular import during standalone AR test collection, and gated LTX-2.5 downloads (HTTP 403).
- [All four NPU diffusion shards passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37181100773) on the same PR merge. One shard initially could not download Wan's pinned reference image; the original URL returned HTTP 200 (1,234,650 bytes), and [the rerun passed all four assigned cases](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37181100773/job/111379951945), including Wan's image-consistency check. No reference image or validation threshold changed. Unrelated SRT failures keep the broader NPU workflow red.

AMD validation is not yet green. Candidate `51c527f781` adds the missing H3 ROCm branch, defers quantization implementation imports until config lookup, and forwards the existing diffusion HF CI credential to the AMD test container. All 11 quantization mappings are unchanged, and changed-file pre-commit passed. Fresh-process import regression tests accompany the fix. [H100 targeted validation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37186081793) passed **134 tests** across five files; the standalone AR file also collected its test successfully (collection only). [The full AMD dual-GPU stage](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37186084061) failed. Shard 0 passed on its first attempt: **13 generation tests and 1 standalone test passed**, with 1 generation and 4 standalone skips. Shard 1 first passed 11 cases, failed two H3 cases because media probing needs the missing `ffprobe`, and timed out starting LTX-2.5's diffusion decoder. Repeated failures exhausted the 180-minute step timeout; standalone AR tests were not reached. H3 denoising and LTX-2.5 weight downloads now work. A follow-up installs `ffmpeg` for diffusion containers; a [separate instrumented diagnosis](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37199681696) is tracing the remaining LTX-2.5 warmup stall. The candidate was not included in the merged PR; fixes are in [Draft PR #42494](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42494). No test or numerical, quality, performance or startup threshold was relaxed. The earlier [credential-enabled CUDA run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37180355847) remains on `1fcc28877c`, which differs only by four subsequently removed modulation dispatch tests. Results from that run are not substituted for the current-head checks above. Workflow secret rules are unchanged.

The [same-H100 Qwen cache-dit diagnostic](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37175345433/job/111356754040) ran A/B/B/A twice, comparing main `5606fb8592` with `715a644848`. Before each request it evicted 250 MiB (5x the reported 50 MiB L2), outside request timing. E2E medians were **4408.09 -> 4342.33 ms (-1.49%)**; average denoise medians were **81.34 -> 80.23 ms (-1.37%)**. No aggregate slowdown reproduced in these eight samples. Step 49 varied from **11.58–67.32 ms on main** and **40.89–66.75 ms on the branch**; both exceeded the unchanged 65.11 ms limit. Three baseline and two candidate pytest runs failed performance checks; the diagnostic's green status only means all measurements completed. All samples, including the unfavorable main outlier, are in the log. This clears L2 before requests, not before every internal kernel, and does not establish a universal performance guarantee.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Before **every measured invocation**, read/write a **632.5 MiB buffer (5x the reported 126.5 MiB L2)**. Input reset and eviction are excluded from timing. Fixed seed, A/B/B/A process order, 10 warmups and 100 measurements per workload. Ordinary CUDA events measure queued GPU work; a separate eager wall-time measurement includes Python/C++ dispatch and synchronization. Empty timing controls and all raw samples are retained.

- **72 kernel/attention-entry cases:** GPU interval changes **-4.62% to +0.46%, geometric mean -0.19%**. No reproducible device-kernel regression observed.
- **12 Qwen/GLM/Ernie/Wan model helpers:** eager changes **-78.25% to +2.08%**, with a maximum increase of **0.82 us**. Packed Qwen projections benefit from the existing native stride-aware implementation.
- **7 additional Ernie/Ideogram/Sensenova helpers:** eager changes **-7.33% to -0.91%**. Ideogram's duplicate-validation regression previously added about 5.6 us; the final implementation no longer reproduces it.

Bare Triton launcher calls now include checks previously paid by their callers: those eager microbenchmarks can add **2–6 us**. Actual model-helper comparisons include both the old caller checks and the new launcher checks. This is not a claim of zero host overhead for every direct API call or of full-model throughput improvement.

External CUDA Graph event timing showed capture-dependent ~2 us shifts on some tiny operations. Same-revision recaptures, ordinary events and Nsight kernel durations were used to investigate; unfavorable raw runs remain in the report. The four small-kernel profiler medians differ by 0–32 ns. Final-head FP16 residual profiles confirm the same CUDA broadcast kernel/grid, with medians 5216→5216 ns and 31648→31680 ns.

The source comparison confirms 36 retained device definitions unchanged (normalizing only Helios' FP32 type assertion); five deleted definitions belong to dead residual-gate alternatives. These measurements cover the listed B200 shapes and helpers, not every architecture/input or multi-GPU/model configuration. Earlier rotating-input benchmarks are archived as historical data: their capped rotation count did not guarantee cold L2 for small cases.

## Checklist

- [x] Changed-file pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Registered GPU regression tests.
- [x] Kernel entry-point documentation.
- [x] Reproducible accuracy/performance evidence with coverage limits.

title: Pick the default nccl_port below the kernel ephemeral range
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

Without `--nccl-port`, `PortArgs.init_new` takes the rendezvous port from `get_free_port()`: a `bind(0)` that is released immediately, so the port comes from the kernel's ephemeral range (`32768` and up by default on Linux). The scheduler process binds it for the `torch.distributed` `TCPStore` only later, after process spawn and whatever JIT compilation sits in between, and in that gap any `bind(0)` or outbound `connect()` on the host can be handed the same port. With several servers or test clients sharing a host (for example CI runners on `--network host`), this surfaces intermittently as:

```text
torch.distributed.DistNetworkError: The server socket has failed to listen on any local network address. port: <port>, useIpv6: false, code: -98, name: EADDRINUSE, message: address already in use
```

Because the conflicting port is selected dynamically, retrying can succeed, which is the signature of losing the port to another process in the gap rather than of a real conflict.

## Modifications

- Add `get_free_port_below_ephemeral()` to `sglang/srt/utils/network.py`. It reads the lower bound of `/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range` (falling back to `32768` if the file is unreadable or unparseable), clamps a `22000-29999` candidate band to one below that bound, and returns the first of up to 64 randomly sampled ports that accepts an explicit IPv4 bind without `SO_REUSEADDR`. The kernel never auto-assigns a port from that band, so only an explicit bind of the same port can still collide. Explicit IPv4 matters because the `TCPStore` binds the IPv4 side of the port (`useIpv6: false`); a wildcard probe on an IPv6-only host would leave that side unchecked. If the clamped band is narrower than the probe budget, or no candidate binds, it falls back to `get_free_port()`.
- `PortArgs.init_new` uses it when `--nccl-port` is not given. An explicit `--nccl-port` is unchanged.

Scope: this covers the default `nccl_port` used by every `launch_server` and `Engine()` path. The other `get_free_port()` rendezvous picks (`entrypoints/engine.py` daemon rendezvous, `disaggregation/encoder/runtime.py`) follow the same pattern and are left for a follow-up.

Related: #37458 proposes a broader allocator for the same site (any port outside the ephemeral range, plus an exclusion list of this instance's planned listener ports). This change is the minimal version: a fixed band below the range, no exclusion bookkeeping, and the existing behaviour as the fallback.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. This only changes which port the default rendezvous uses.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. Startup-only; one short probe loop before the scheduler is spawned.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (No new test: the race needs a third process to take the port in the gap, and a deterministic reproduction would only mirror the helper.)
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing change.)

title: [sglang-miles] Fix the bf16 triton MoE path and mhc_pre splitk for DeepSeek-V4.1
author: Zhichenzzz
body:
## Motivation

Two startup failures hit while validating DeepSeek-V4.1 RL support (radixark/miles#3179) on GB300 with the **unquantized (bf16)** model. Both kill the engine before serving starts; neither affects the native fp8/fp4 path.

**1. The triton fused-experts path crashes on packed topk output.** `StandardTopKOutputPacked` carries a fourth field (`packed_topk_ids`), so the strict 3-tuple unpack in `triton_utils/fused_moe.py` raises `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)` for any model whose router emits the packed format and which runs the unquantized triton runner. DSV4.1 bf16 dies in warmup.

**2. `mhc_pre` splitk refuses `hc_hidden_size` 20480.** The splitk kernel hardcoded `hidden_block` for hc_hidden_size 16384/28672 and raised `NotImplementedError` otherwise. DSV4.1 (hidden 5120 × hc_mult 4 = 20480) dies in cuda-graph warmup on the non-deepgemm prenorm path.

## Modifications

- `triton_utils/fused_moe.py`: read `topk_weights`/`topk_ids` by attribute, which works for every `TopKOutput` variant (both the main unpack and the xpu branch). The same latent unpack exists in `fused_moe_native.py`, `kt_ep_wrapper.py`, `ascend_tp.py` and `moe_runner/deep_gemm.py`; left untouched here because those paths were not exercised.
- `kernels/ops/layernorm/mhc.py`: derive `hidden_block` instead of hardcoding shapes — pick the largest value in {256, 128} that divides both `hc_hidden_size` and `hc_hidden_size // split_k`, matching the kernel's own asserts. This reproduces the existing choices exactly (16384→256, 28672→128) and admits 20480→128.

## Accuracy Tests

On GB300 (2 nodes × 4 GPUs), DSV4.1 bf16 (dequantized from the fp8/fp4 drop) with these two patches:

- 4-layer cut, first-token top-5 logprobs vs the native fp8/fp4 engine: match within quantization noise at tp1, tp4 and tp8-across-2-nodes (e.g. top-2 logprobs −0.796/−0.921 bf16 vs −0.887/−1.012 fp8, same token ids).
- Full 40-layer bf16 serving generates coherent text (temperature-0 `/generate` probe).
- miles RL e2e with the patched engines: 10 rollouts, `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` 0.019–0.023 every step, raw rewards 0.57–0.79.
- The mhc derivation was regression-checked against the previous hardcoded mapping (16384→256, 28672→128 unchanged).

Without fix 1 the bf16 engine dies at startup in warmup; without fix 2 it dies in cuda-graph warmup — so these paths had no passing baseline to compare against.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel behavior changes for previously-working shapes: the unpack rewrite is loader-side Python, and the mhc derivation selects the same `hidden_block` values as before for 16384/28672.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code and run the relevant lint checks (repo pre-commit: ruff, ruff format, isort, codespell all green on the touched files).

title: [diffusion] Reset DiT cache state at the start of each request
author: fusheng-ji
body:
TeaCache and Spectrum reset a DiT's state at denoising step 0. A boundary expert, Wan2.2's `transformer_2`, only runs the low-noise steps and never sees step 0. Its TeaCache counters, residuals and L1 history and its Spectrum schedule and forecaster therefore carried over from the previous request. A request with a different shape then crashed with `Spectrum feature shape must remain constant`; one with the same shape silently started from the previous request's state.

`DenoisingStage` now resets the TeaCache and Spectrum state of every DiT when it sets up a request, in `_maybe_enable_cache_dit_and_torch_compile`, which the base stage and MiniMax-H3's stage both call once per request. This covers both experts on every CFG rank. Only enabled caches are reset, modules without cache state are skipped, and the in-model step-0 resets are unchanged.

Independent of #42422 and #42423, which fix the step-0 reset logic itself; this PR covers the DiTs that never reach step 0. The three merge in any order.

### Validation

**Unit:** the new tests run a second expert from its first low-noise step across two requests with different shapes, and compare it with a fresh expert:

| Test | `main` | `main` + this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_disabled_caches_and_plain_modules_are_left_alone` | ❌ | ✅ |
| `test_second_expert_spectrum_restarts_like_fresh` | ❌ | ✅ |
| `test_second_expert_teacache_restarts_like_fresh` | ❌ | ✅ |

On `main` the stage has no reset hook yet; the end-to-end table below shows the behaviour this fixes. With #42422 and #42423 stacked on top, the Spectrum/TeaCache lifecycle tests, existing Spectrum forecaster, MiniMax-H3 Spectrum, CFG gating/policy, DiT config boundary and sampling-parameter tests give 80 passed and 59 subtests passed. Repository pre-commit hooks pass.

**End to end** on B200 with `Erland/tiny-wan2.2-t2v-a14b-debug` (Wan2.2 T2V A14B layout with `transformer` and `transformer_2`, random weights, boundary ratio 0.875), 64x64, 16 steps, Spectrum, Torch SDPA. A 9-frame request runs first, then the 5-frame target is compared with a fresh instance:

| Tree | Reused vs fresh |
|---|---|
| `main` | crash: `Spectrum feature shape must remain constant` (second expert's forecaster from the previous request) |
| `main` + #42422 + #42423 | same crash |
| `main` + this PR | bit-identical to fresh (frames and latents), same per-step Spectrum decisions |
| `main` + all three | bit-identical to fresh |
| `main` + this PR, no cache (control) | bit-identical to fresh |

The no-cache control shows this checkpoint is deterministic, so bit-identity is a meaningful check here.

The validation above was run locally and on our cluster. GPU CI needs the `run-ci` label from a maintainer.

title: [AMD][CI] Fix ROCm kernel wheel sources: drop eagle_utils, add DSV4 kernels
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## What

Bring the ROCm kernel wheel's source lists (`3rdparty/amd/wheel/sgl-kernel/CMakeLists_rocm.txt` and `rocm_hipify.py`) back in line with `setup_rocm.py` and `common_extension_rocm.cc`:

- Remove `csrc/speculative/eagle_utils`.
- Add `csrc/elementwise/deepseek_v4_topk` and `csrc/elementwise/dsv4_norm_rope`.

## Why

The release workflow does not build with `setup_rocm.py`. `build-rocm-matrix` copies `3rdparty/amd/wheel/sgl-kernel/*` into the AOT directory, and `build_rocm.sh` builds with `CMakeLists_rocm.txt`. Those lists have drifted, which causes two problems.

**The build fails (0.4.8, 0.4.9).** #40033 moved the EAGLE tree kernels to JIT. It reduced `eagle_utils.cu` to an include of `python/sglang/kernels/jit/include/sgl_kernel/speculative/eagle.cuh`, and dropped the file from `setup_rocm.py` and its op registrations from `common_extension_rocm.cc`. The wheel lists still compiled it, and the JIT include directory is neither on that include path nor mounted into the build container:

```
/sgl-kernel/csrc/speculative/eagle_utils.hip:28:10: fatal error: 'sgl_kernel/speculative/eagle.cuh' file not found
```

- 0.4.9: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37155260604/job/111315213887
- 0.4.8: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36649756025/job/109710303032

No ROCm wheels were published for either version.

**The published wheels fail at import.** `common_extension_rocm.cc` registers `deepseek_v4_topk_transform_512` and the three `dsv4_fused_*` ops, and `setup_rocm.py` compiles their sources, but the wheel lists never included them. In the published `0.4.6.post1+rocm720`, `0.4.7+rocm720` and `0.4.7+rocm1000` wheels, `common_ops.abi3.so` has all four as undefined `R_X86_64_GLOB_DAT` relocations. Those are resolved at load time, so loading the library fails. The ROCm Docker images build with `setup_rocm.py` and are not affected.

## Test plan

Built both ROCm wheel legs with `release-whl-kernel.yml` at version 0.4.9 on a test branch, with all publish steps disabled: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37189886891

| Leg | Result |
|---|---|
| `build-rocm-matrix (3.10, 720)` | pass, `sglang_kernel-0.4.9+rocm720` built |
| `build-rocm-matrix (3.10, 1000)` | pass, `sglang_kernel-0.4.9+rocm1000` built |

- All 16 sources compile for gfx942 and gfx950 together, so both `HIP_FP8_TYPE_FNUZ` and `HIP_FP8_TYPE_E4M3` are defined. The DSV4 files had previously only been built single-arch through `setup_rocm.py`.
- A build-only step ran `nm -D --undefined-only` on `common_ops.abi3.so` in each wheel. No sgl_kernel op is left unresolved; the only undefined symbols are from Python and torch.
- The wheels were not imported or run on a GPU.

title: [Fix] Offer the fused MoE finalize all-reduce only to a block that owes the sum
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42481
* #42480
* __->__ #42479
* #42478
* #42477

## Motivation

The fused MoE finalize kernel in `DeepseekV2MoE` carries a tensor-parallel all-reduce inside it and sets `all_reduce_done`, but its eligibility never consulted `reduce_results`, while the unfused path below it does. A DeepSeek V4 MoE built with `reduce_results=False` would therefore still sum its output there and have its caller sum it a second time, scaling the block's contribution by the tensor-parallel width with nothing raised.

No block reaches it that way today: the fused path needs `is_deepseek_v4`, and the only construction that passes it leaves `reduce_results` at its default. So this changes no behavior; it makes the contract hold for a block built either way, which the DeepSeek V4 decoder needs once its stage boundary, rather than the MoE, completes the sum.

## Modifications

- Offer the fused finalize only when the block owes its own sum (`reduce_results`).
- `test_stage_producers_leave_sums.py` could not see this case. It matched a sum by call name, so a fused kernel that performs the sum internally was invisible; and it recognized the `reduce_results` guard only when spelled inline in the branch, so a predicate computed once and branched on later read as unguarded. It now counts every `moe_finalize_all_reduce*` kernel as a sum (the plain one and its `_mhc`, `_mhc_combine` and `_mhc_quant` variants), and follows a name bound from a condition that requires `reduce_results`. Only such a condition guards a sum: the flag itself, or an `and` with it as a conjunct; a negation, a comparison such as `is False`, or an `or` does not require it. Across the 57 files that build stages, the second change admits exactly one predicate, the one in this file.
- A synthetic case pins both: a fused finalize variant under a guard computed earlier is accepted, while sums under a negated guard computed earlier, an inline `not`, an `is False` comparison and an `or` are all reported.

## Accuracy Tests

No behavior change by construction: the added condition is always true on the only path that reaches the fused kernel today (DeepSeek V4 builds its MoE with the default `reduce_results=True`).

The guard reports no violation across the 57 files that build stages; removing the new `reduce_results` condition makes it report all four fused finalize calls. CPU: the 114 test files that import the models or the layer boundary package show no new failure against `main`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: no path that runs today changes.

title: [Kernel] Use explicit reciprocal scaling for recurrent Q/K normalization
author: merrymercy
body:
## Motivation

Make the default recurrent Q/K normalization explicitly compute a reciprocal norm and then multiply, keeping reciprocal formation and vector scaling as separate source operations.

## Modifications

- Compute `1 / sqrt(sum(x*x) + epsilon)` once for each Q/K vector in the default KDA and GDN path, then multiply by it. The CuTe decode-parity branch continues to use `rsqrt` and shares the final multiplication.
- Add bitwise output/state coverage against separately normalized inputs for both recurrences at head dimensions 32, 64, and 128. Exact sums of squares keep the test independent of the standalone normalizer's reduction layout.

## Accuracy Tests

On a Blackwell GPU with PyTorch 2.13 and Triton 3.7.1:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \

  test/registered/attention/test_gdn_noncontiguous_stride.py \

```

title: [Perf] Improve GLM-5.3-Flash DFlash decoding on B300
author: leonardHONG
body:
## Motivation

Reduce synchronization and kernel overhead in GLM-5.3-Flash DFlash decoding. The DFlash/KDA-only comparison improves average decode throughput from **1091.85 to 1199.72 tokens/s (+9.88%)** on 8×B300, with essentially unchanged memory usage.

## Modifications

- Reuse CPU-side sequence lengths to avoid blocking GPU-to-CPU copies during DFlash input preparation.
- Build pooled page tables once per verification batch and reuse them across sparse attention layers.
- Tune KDA recurrence and gated norm launch configurations on SM103 while preserving the tested rounding behavior.
- Extend the sigmoid RMSNorm BT8 dispatch to BF16, D=128 workloads with 8–256 rows.

The FP8 MoE weight-layout optimization has been split out of this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

Paired service checks matched output tokens and speculative acceptance statistics. Real-rejection cases also matched the checked generated-token logprobs.

Kernel checks cover KDA output/state parity and output/rstd parity for nearby norm shapes. Regression checks cover pooled metadata CUDA Graph replay and sequence-length bounds.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GLM-5.3-Flash + DFlash2, 8×B300, TP8, concurrency 1, 8192 input / 1024 output tokens, draft block size 8. Target linear-attention verification explicitly uses **Triton** (`--linear-attn-verify-backend triton`); draft attention uses **FA4**.

Three warmups followed by three rounds of two requests, without a profiler. The comparison pairs the same six measured inputs from the baseline and candidate records and aggregates decode throughput over those requests.

| Configuration | Average decode tokens/s |
| --- | ---: |
| Baseline | 1091.85 |
| DFlash/KDA optimized | 1199.72 |
| Improvement | **+9.88%** |

Timing runs from receipt of the first token to SSE `[DONE]`. Timed requests had an acceptance length of 8; real-rejection cases were validated separately.

Before optimization, NSYS identified blocking sequence-length transfers and repeated pooled-page-table work; NCU showed low parallelism in KDA recurrence and gated norm.

## Memory and KV Capacity

Both runs use the same model, draft, dependencies, and TP8 settings. Target and draft graph buckets are `bs=[1]` on both sides. Memory was measured separately, after all graphs were captured and before any inference requests.

| Metric | Comparison |
| --- | --- |
| Target-load NVML sampled peak | Per-GPU difference no greater than **2 MiB** |
| Draft-load NVML sampled peak | Identical on each GPU |
| Post-graph NVML resident memory | Identical on each GPU, **43.715–44.027 GiB/GPU** |
| Post-graph PyTorch allocated | Candidate increases by **2.5 KiB/GPU** |
| Post-graph PyTorch reserved | **41.863281 GiB/GPU** on both |
| Resolved `max_total_num_tokens` | **32768** on both |

Loading peaks are **total process-memory samples** from NVML with a target 50 ms sampling interval. Capacity was confirmed through the scheduler and server interface.

Performance and memory were measured on the recorded snapshots before the subsequent main merge.

author: BBuf
body:
ROCm Llama startup fails during graph capture because #41282 keeps the RoPE cache in FP32 while the fallback kernel assumes the query dtype. Let the kernel read FP32 caches and round cos/sin to the query dtype before the existing arithmetic. This preserves the FP32 cache used by QSA without converting the whole cache on every forward.

The diffusion fixes defer quantization imports to break the linear-layer import cycle, enable the existing MiniMax H3 denoising path on HIP, pass the existing HF credential to dual-GPU tests, and install ffmpeg/ffprobe for H3 media validation.

The existing ROCm RoPE test now runs even with AITER enabled, checks FP32-cache outputs against the same-dtype kernel bit for bit, and runs in Stage A so it catches this failure before the longer suites. Correctness, performance and startup thresholds are unchanged.

Validation:
- Changed-file pre-commit checks passed, including clang-format and test registration.
- Latest-head AMD Stage A: 9/9 test files passed, including Llama and EAGLE3 (18 tests each, MMLU 0.69 for both) and the ROCm RoPE regression: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37210510566/job/111460697051.
- AMD kernel unit tests: 7,141 passed, 123 skipped. CUDA kernel unit tests: 13,992 passed, 2,132 skipped. Both tested the merge containing bf114442d1. Latest-head GitHub lint passed.
- MI300X cold-L2 diagnostic: 24 cases were bitwise equal to the query-dtype cache path. Each timed call follows a 512 MiB read/write eviction outside event timing. This compares cache specializations in the same candidate, not a full baseline commit. A repeat using identical Q/K addresses and 1,500 interleaved samples per path measured a 1.008 geomean latency ratio (individual medians 0.989–1.036). BF16 shows a small 1–3.6% kernel overhead; this is not a claim of zero performance impact. Diagnostic run: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37212045202/job/111465214461.
- LTX-2.5 warmup and the remaining diffusion CI results are still under investigation; this PR does not claim all checks have passed.

Follow-up to #42391. The RoPE failure was already present in the base code and is fixed here as part of the ROCm CI follow-up.

title: [diffusion] CI: fix qwen cache-dit step 10/49 perf baselines
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

`qwen_image_t2i_cache_dit_enabled` fails its H100 per-step perf check at random. From 09-30 to 10-04, 71% of attempts went over the step-49 limit. Every final 1-GPU failure in that window came from this case.

The cause, found in the debug runs in #42546, is how the step time is measured. It is not a regression.

- Steps 10 and 49 are the first cached step after a full step.
- Per-step times are host wall times with no device sync.
- The cache-dit residual check in that step is the first point where the host blocks, so that step absorbs the previous full step's queued GPU work.

Debug run on CI H100, 3 launches per arm, times in ms:

| Arm | Full step | Steps 10 / 49 | Other cached steps | E2E |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Fused QK-norm/RoPE epilogue on, unsynced (CI today) | 178 | 64 / 66 | 6.3 | 4310 |
| Fused off, unsynced | 196 | 55 / 56 | 6.5 | 4455 |
| Fused on, `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1` | 238 | 7.0 / 7.1 | 6.3 | — |
| Fused off, synced | 245 | 7.2 / 7.1 | 6.5 | — |

With synced timing, steps 10 and 49 take about 7 ms, like every other cached step. #38584 enabled the fused epilogue on Hopper, which cut host launches from 3031 to 2007 per profiled window. The real GPU time got about 3% faster. But the host now enqueues faster too, so more GPU work spills into steps 10 and 49.

## Modifications

`perf_baselines/h100.json`: steps 10 and 49 of `qwen_image_t2i_cache_dit_enabled` are set to their CI medians, 64.58 / 66.38 ms (previously 48.7 / 45.11). The medians come from 328 H100 CI measurements between 09-30 and 10-04. They are the unsynced host wall times this check measures. No other baseline or tolerance changes.

The `ltx_2_5_diffusion_decoder_2gpus` timing tolerance from earlier commits is dropped. Its host-bound slowdown will be handled in a separate PR.

## Validation

PR CI on fe3b48d passed with the same qwen baselines.

title: [Refactor] Simplify GDN, vision RoPE and MLA kernel dispatch
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

GDN decode checks the same input shapes in its dispatch predicate and operator wrapper. Kimi K3 duplicates vision RoPE eligibility and immediately recomputes a decision already stored in forward metadata. MLA dispatch repeats shape checks performed by its C++ launcher.

## Modifications

- Keep GDN fusion eligibility limited to supported dtypes, layouts, convolution widths and activations; validate tensor relationships in the Triton host wrapper.
- Share the vision RoPE selector with Kimi K3 and reuse the prepared metadata decision.
- Leave MLA shape validation to the C++ launcher while retaining dtype, width and alignment fallback gates.

Device kernels, launch settings and supported-input computation are unchanged. Invalid tensor relationships raise at the operator entry instead of selecting a fallback. Existing tests remain, with one call updated for the narrower GDN selector signature.

## Accuracy Tests

[H100 validation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37205513777/job/111445835177) checked PR head `35bc03557c` against base `35f3c96ff4`:

- 74 existing tests and 4 subtests passed: GDN projection/Conv1D, vision RoPE, MLA scatter/concat, Kimi vision metadata, GDN noncontiguous strides, and MLA DCP metadata.
- 38 baseline/candidate cases had bitwise-identical outputs and cache updates. These include 18 GDN cases, 12 vision RoPE cases, 6 BF16/FP8 MLA cases, and 2 actual Kimi encoder forwards with identical random weights. Kimi used fused RoPE with both prepared and unprepared metadata.
- All five Triton device-function ASTs and the allocation/launch sections are unchanged; no C++ changes.

[Qwen3.5-4B model accuracy](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37205809168/job/111446701076): the existing `TestUnifiedQwenHybridTriton.test_gsm8k` passed on the same PR head with **0.875** accuracy over 200 questions (unchanged threshold **0.80**). Logs confirm fused GDN decode was selected and prefill/decode CUDA Graph capture completed. This also exercises strided convolution state in the unified pool.

The Kimi encoder comparison above uses random weights; it is integration parity, not checkpoint task accuracy. Cross-platform and full PR CI remain separate from these targeted H100 results.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

H100 80GB (50 MiB L2), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0. Each individual timed invocation was preceded by a 256 MiB eviction-buffer write, outside its CUDA-event interval. 150 samples per side, interleaved in randomized order. For encoder forwards, L2 was evicted before the whole forward, not between its kernels.

| Path | Cases | Median GPU time change | Range across cases |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GDN | 18 | +0.43% | -0.91% to +2.30% |
| Vision RoPE | 12 | -0.19% | -1.15% to +1.43% |
| MLA | 6 | 0.00% | -3.40% to +1.72% |
| Kimi encoder | 2 | -0.68% | -1.25% to -0.11% |

No material GPU regression observed in these cases. Separately measured CPU selector time fell from 2.96 to 1.06 us for GDN and from 5.48 to 4.56 us for MLA (medians across cases). These are operator/encoder measurements, not serving-throughput claims. [Validation script](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/a3d0542013da0686f494b7bfa138011758bd27a9/test/manual/test_llm_vlm_cleanup_validation.py) is on a separate branch and is not part of this PR.

## Checklist

- [x] Applicable pre-commit hooks pass on all changed files.
- [x] Retain existing numerical and fallback tests; no new legality-only tests.
- [x] No user-facing configuration or documentation changes required.
- [x] GPU correctness and cold L2 performance validation (scope above).

title: Revert "[AMD][ROCm] Keep cos_sin_cache fp32 on HIP for fused QSA indexer kernel (#41282)"
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## Motivation

#41282 keeps `RotaryEmbedding.cos_sin_cache` fp32 on HIP. On HIP, every rope without a fused KV-cache write goes through the `sgl_kernel.rotary_embedding` fallback, which reads the cache as the query dtype, so CUDA graph capture now fails:

```
File ".../sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py", line 455, in forward_cuda
File ".../sgl_kernel/elementwise.py", line 414, in rotary_embedding
RuntimeError: expected scalar type BFloat16 but found Float
Exception: Capture cuda graph failed: expected scalar type BFloat16 but found Float
```

This fails `stage-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` (`test_basic_sanity.py` / `test_basic_sanity_eagle3.py`) on every AMD PR, so all AMD stage B/C lanes are skipped. Examples: [run 37180583674](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37180583674/job/111372273784), [run 37187809051](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37187809051/job/111393476849). #41282's own PR Test (AMD) runs stopped at the label gate, so stage-a never ran on it.

Reverting unblocks AMD CI now. The forward fix that keeps the fp32 cache for the QSA indexer is #42483; it can re-land on top of this.

## Modifications

`git revert f6fcda8827`: `base.py` and `mrope.py` are byte-identical to before #41282. Nothing has touched either file since.

Effect on the QSA indexer: `_use_fused_prep` already requires `cos_sin_cache.dtype == torch.float32`, so on HIP it goes back to the unfused prep path it used before #41282. No functional break, only the fused prep on HIP is lost until #42483 lands.

## Checklist

- [x] Clean revert, no conflicts
- [ ] CI: `stage-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` passes

title: [diffusion] fix: load community ComfyUI-GGUF Qwen-Image-2.1 transformers
author: niehen6174
body: ## Motivation Community ComfyUI-GGUF exports of Qwen-Image-2.1 (e.g. [`abenzerps/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-GGUF`](https://huggingface.co/abenzerps/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-GGUF)) fail to load. Unlike the native-name exports validated earlier, they also quantize the plain `nn.Linear` layers outside the blocks (`modulation`, `time_text_embed`, `norm_out`, `proj_out`), which have no packed-weight parameter to load into. ## Modifications - Dequantize those layers to BF16 on load through a new `gguf_dequantize_prefixes` on the DiT, the same mechanism the GGUF text-encoder path uses. - `packed_qkv_weight` skips quantized projections instead of reading `.weight`, which GGUF layers do not have. - CPU unit tests for both fixes (they fail on `main`), plus a GGUF docs/cookbook validated-scope update. ```bash sglang generate --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1 \ --component-weights-paths.transformer abenzerps/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-GGUF/qwen-image-2.1-UC-Q4_K_M.gguf \ --prompt "..." --save-output ``` ## Accuracy Tests 1x RTX 5090, default sampling params (1024x1024, 40 steps, guidance 1.0), seed 42, default auto memory policy. | Transformer | PSNR vs official BF16 (fox prompt) | | --- | ---: | | `qwen-image-2.1-Q8_0.gguf` (`base` revision, plain quantization) | 38.8 dB | | `qwen-image-2.1-UC-Q4_K_M.gguf` | 23.8 dB | The UC checkpoint is not a pure quantization. A tensor-level diff of its BF16 export against the official weights shows that every non-attention tensor is bit-identical. The attention `to_q/k/v/out` weights equal `bf16(W + 1.0 * B @ A)` using the rank-16 LoRA shipped in the same repo, which explains the lower PSNR. Visually, the UC Q4_K_M output keeps the composition, subject, text rendering, and lighting of the official model on all three prompts tested: ## Speed Tests and Profiling Same setup as above, `main` + this PR: | Transformer | DiT weights | Peak VRAM | Denoise s/step | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Official BF16 | 14.2 GB | 17.0 GB | 0.43-0.48 | | GGUF Q8_0 | 7.6 GB | 11.1 GB | 0.47 | | GGUF Q4_K_M | 4.6 GB | 8.25 GB | 0.47 | As the GGUF guide notes, GGUF is a capacity option: the packed linears are dequantized each step and then run the native GEMM, so per-step latency is slightly higher. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). Not covered: TP, cache-dit, editing / RGBA with these files, other GGUF types (Q4_0/Q5_K_M/Q6_K), and the FP8 / INT8-ConvRot / NVFP4 safetensors in the same repo. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #37465558588](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37465558588) Latest PR Test (Extra): :warning: **Not enabled** -- add `run-ci-extra` label to opt in. title: [Feat] paged-experts: Serve MoE models whose weights do not fit VRAM
author: N3mezis
body:
# [Feature] Paged Experts: serve MoE models whose weights do not fit in VRAM

<!-- Successor to #29971 (closed), cut down to a reviewable first step. -->

This is a smaller, first-iteration version of #29971. That PR tried to make the feature fast and complete at once (pinned windows, a disk tier, breakable decode graphs, NVFP4, six new flags; ~7k lines). This one ships only the core: **page experts between host RAM and the GPU, keep the computation on the GPU, change no results.** Everything else is a follow-up that plugs into the seams added here.

## Motivation

A lot of laptops and gaming PCs typically pair 4–16 GB of VRAM with 32–64 GB of RAM. MoE models are increasingly the default open-weight architecture (Qwen3/3.5 MoE, DeepSeek, GLM, gpt-oss, Mixtral), and their expert weights are most of the parameters. For example, Qwen3-30B-A3B in int4 has ~15 GB of expert weights, which is all of the usable VRAM on a 16 GB card. Currently, SGLang either does not load such a model on these machines, or loads it with `--cpu-offload-gb`, which streams *every* offloaded weight to the GPU on every forward pass, whatever the routing.

llama.cpp and Ollama keep the experts of some MoE layers in system RAM and **compute them on the CPU** (`--n-cpu-moe N`, or `--cpu-moe` for all of them).

**What this PR does instead.** Each token is routed to only `top_k` of the `E` experts per layer, and consecutive tokens reuse most of them. Paged Experts keeps **K of the E experts per layer in a K-slot table on the GPU**, holds all E in pinned host memory, and copies in only the experts a step needs that are not resident. The layer's own fused-MoE kernel then runs on the GPU as usual. It is the HiCache idea applied to expert weights: the GPU holds the working set, host RAM the rest.

**It is a memory knob as much as a speed feature.** K trades directly against the KV cache, so a deployment can choose more context or concurrency (smaller K, more paging) or more speed (larger K). Models that already fit can give up some resident experts for longer context, or to share the GPU with another model.

## Where it helps, and where it does not

Measured against each alternative at its best setting (methodology and full numbers in [Speed Tests](#speed-tests-and-profiling)):

- **Against SGLang today** (`--cpu-offload-gb`): paging moves only the experts a step routes to and does not have, instead of every offloaded weight. 12× (int4) and 30× (FP8) faster single-stream decode on the 16 GB card, 27× on the 8 GB laptop.
- **Against llama.cpp tuned** (`--n-cpu-moe` at the best fitting value, byte-matched `IQ4_XS` / `Q8_0`):
  - when most of the model fits (a 16 GB int4 model on a 16 GB card), or the host link is slow (int4 on an 8 GB laptop over PCIe 4.0 x8), the two are **close**: 205.7 vs 194.4 tok/s single-stream decode and 379 vs 312 tok/s with 4 requests on the 16 GB card; 30.6–32.9 vs 23.0–32.4 tok/s single-stream decode on the laptop;
  - when a large share of the experts must live in host RAM and the host link is fast (FP8 on a 16 GB card over PCIe 5.0 x16), paging **decodes faster**: 87.7 vs 45.2 tok/s;
  - **llama.cpp has the lower time-to-first-token on short prompts.** A prefill touches nearly every expert, so it pages in all non-resident experts once (≈4 GB for Qwen3-30B int4 at K=92, ≈80 ms over PCIe 5), while llama.cpp computes its few CPU-side layers in place. For long prompts paging wins, since its transfer is a fixed cost and the GPU computes the tokens faster: 2,048-token prompt 267 vs 344 ms (int4, 16 GB), 443 vs 984 ms (FP8, 16 GB), 1,441–1,538 vs 2,396 ms (laptop); short prompts 89–90 vs 68 ms, 284–285 vs 226 ms, 872–953 vs 620 ms;
  - **with several concurrent requests and a small K/E**, each step routes to more experts than fit, and paging can fall behind: 11–12 vs 41 tok/s with 4 requests on the laptop (K = 26 of 128); FP8 on the 16 GB card gives 84 tok/s at K = 40 but 31 at K = 24 (llama.cpp: 55).

Note: #29971 compared only against llama.cpp `--cpu-moe` (all experts on the CPU), which overstated the advantage. The numbers here compare against llama.cpp's tuned offloading.

## Scope

**In this PR**
- Unquantized (bf16/fp16), block-quantized FP8 (triton runner) and GPTQ int4/int8 (Marlin runner) experts.
- A single GPU.
- Works with SGLang's default CUDA graphs: decode is captured (full graph) up to `K // top_k` concurrent requests, and in breakable prefill graphs the paged MoE layer runs as an eager break. CUDA graphs can also be off entirely.
- K is sized automatically from the memory budget, or set with `--paged-experts-num-resident`.
- **Results are unchanged.** Bit-identical logprobs for bf16 and FP8 versus the unpaged model, eager and with CUDA graphs; GPTQ stays within Marlin's own batch-to-batch noise.

**Not in this PR** (each is a follow-up on the seams below)
- Stores larger than pinnable RAM (pinned window, pageable or disk cold tier).
- Capturing decode beyond `K // top_k` requests (breakable decode graphs fail on these models upstream, with or without paging, so they are rejected for now).
- Computing a short prefill's non-resident experts on the CPU instead of paging them (the short-prompt TTFT gap above).
- More formats: NVFP4 (via Marlin W4A16 for exact results), AWQ, MXFP4.
- Tensor or expert parallelism.

Two new server flags: `--enable-paged-experts` and `--paged-experts-num-resident`.

## Modifications

**New package `srt/layers/moe/paged_experts/`** (~1,150 lines). It wraps a layer's existing fused-MoE method and splits paging into replaceable parts:

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `method.py` | `PagedExpertsMoEMethod`. Creates the layer's expert tensors with K rows and redirects their weight loaders into a host store, so checkpoints load through SGLang's **native** per-expert loader (sharding, gate/up order, scale layout). Also holds the startup guard and the capture-size cap. |
| `formats.py` | One `ExpertFormat` per quantization method: which tensors are loaded and paged, and what happens after loading. GPTQ's Marlin repack runs over the host store K experts at a time; a check rejects post-load transforms the store would not replicate. **Adding a quantization is one subclass.** |
| `runners.py` | One `RunnerContract` per runner backend (triton, Marlin). The runner returns router-weighted per-(token, expert) outputs (`no_combine`), and the contract performs the same top-k sum the runner would. That is what makes multi-wave steps bit-identical. |
| `store.py` | The pinned host store: `page_in` for host-planned steps, `gather` for device-planned steps. |
| `residency.py` | LRU slot assignment and wave planning on the host, plus `DeviceResidency`, the same LRU state on the GPU. |
| `executor.py` | `EagerExecutor`: host-planned waves, any step; inside a breakable prefill graph it runs as an eager break. `DeviceExecutor`: one wave decided and paged on the GPU with no host sync, so the decode graph captures it. |
| `sizing.py` | Auto-K from exact checkpoint bytes (safetensors headers), `--mem-fraction-static`, and a KV reserve. |

**New JIT kernel** `kernels/jit/csrc/moe/paged_experts.cuh` with wrapper `kernels/ops/moe/paged_experts.py` (~290 lines; no sgl-kernel change):
- an on-device LRU decide that writes the page-in plan to GPU buffers;
- one gather launch that copies every paged tensor from the pinned host store through its UVA address, reading the count on the device.

**Upstream touches** (82 lines):
- `MoeRunnerConfig.no_combine_keep_router_weight`;
- the triton fused-MoE tail factored into `moe_combine_topk`;
- `fused_marlin_moe(no_combine=)`;
- `FusedMoE.weight_load_method` and the paged-experts hook in `FusedMoE.__init__`;
- the two server flags.

**Docs:** `docs/advanced_features/paged_experts.mdx` and the server-argument entries.

## Accuracy Tests

Logprobs against the unpaged server, prompt plus 16 greedy tokens, 3 prompts. Settings: `--enable-deterministic-inference --attention-backend triton`, K = 8, so every prompt runs in several waves and every decode step pages. "With CUDA graphs" means full decode plus breakable prefill.

| Model | Experts | Eager | With CUDA graphs |
|---|---|---|---|
| OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct | bf16 (triton) | **bit-identical** | **bit-identical** |
| OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct, FP8 block 128×128 | fp8 (triton) | **bit-identical** | **bit-identical** |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 | int4 (Marlin) | within tolerance (max 0.1, mean 0.01) ‡ | within tolerance ‡ |

‡ Marlin's stream-K split depends on the batch shape, so the unpaged kernel is not batch-invariant either.

GSM8K, the same `sgl-eval` chat evaluation for both engines (thinking off), on models that cannot run unpaged on these cards:

| Model | this PR | llama.cpp (byte-matched GGUF) |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B int4, 16 GB card (200 q) | 0.955 | 0.965 (`IQ4_XS`) |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B FP8, 16 GB card (200 q) | 0.945 | 0.955 (`Q8_0`) |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B int4, 8 GB laptop (100 q) | 0.98 | 0.98 (`IQ4_XS`) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Machines:** an RTX 4070 Laptop (8 GB, PCIe 4.0 x8, 54 GB RAM under WSL2) and an RTX 5070 Ti desktop (16 GB, PCIe 5.0 x16, 62 GB RAM, native Linux).

**Methodology** (each engine at its best setting, identical workload):
- Real prompts (ShareGPT, 256 output tokens) as the headline workload: paging speed depends on how consecutive tokens route, so synthetic prompts mis-measure it. One 2,048-token prompt phase for long-prompt TTFT.
- Fixed prompt set per phase (a seed each, identical across engines and runs, never repeated across phases); prefix caching off in both engines; warm-up before measuring.
- Same KV capacity for both (10,240 tokens, 4 slots); byte-matched quantization (GPTQ int4 vs `IQ4_XS`, FP8 vs `Q8_0`).
- llama.cpp at its best: `--n-cpu-moe` searched in steps of 1 and counted only when its own memory projection fits physical VRAM, thread count swept per machine, `--load-mode none` and mmap both tried; `--fit on` and `--cpu-moe` reported too.
- Each headline cell measured twice.

## Tests

- **Unit** (CPU): paged forward against unpaged over 1, 2 and 64 tokens and several steps; padding; LRU and waves; host-loader layout and tags; the K-at-a-time repack; device↔host residency round trip; sizing.
- **Kernel** (CUDA): decide against a Python reference over 200 random steps; the multi-tensor gather; decide + gather across 20 CUDA-graph replays with changing routing; rejection of more than K entries.
- **e2e** (`test/registered/e2e/moe/`): bf16, FP8 and GPTQ, each eager and with CUDA graphs (full decode, breakable prefill) against unpaged.

Run on RTX 5070 Ti (SM120) and RTX 4070 (SM89), with an image whose torch / sgl-kernel / FlashInfer predate this branch's upstream base (`SGLANG_SKIP_SGL_KERNEL_VERSION_CHECK=1`); CI on the current image may differ slightly.
