title: Revert "Revert "[AMD][ROCm] Keep cos_sin_cache fp32 on HIP for fused QSA indexer kernel (#41282)""
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## Motivation

#42541 reverted #41282 because the HIP `sgl_kernel.rotary_embedding` fallback could not read an fp32 `cos_sin_cache`. #42494 had already fixed that kernel to read an fp32 cache, about 12 hours before #42541 merged, and it moved `test_rope_rocm.py` into AMD stage A with a check that the HIP cache stays fp32.

With #41282 reverted, HIP casts the cache to the query dtype again, so that check fails `stage-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` and every AMD stage B/C job is skipped:

```
File "/sglang-checkout/test/registered/rotary/test_rope_rocm.py", line 62, in _run_case
    self.assertEqual(rope_hip.cos_sin_cache.dtype, torch.float32)
AssertionError: torch.bfloat16 != torch.float32
```

#42541's own stage A run already failed this way ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37250822085/job/111615153216)). Since it merged, 18 of the 19 completed stage A jobs failed the same way, e.g. [run 37272668001](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37272668001/job/111642894134) and [run 37275678823](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37275678823/job/111652177894). The one pass is a stacked PR whose base branch does not contain #42541.

With #41282 and #42494 both on main, stage A passed 9/9, including Llama, EAGLE3 and `test_rope_rocm.py`: #42494's own run ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37210510566/job/111460697051)) and later PRs such as [run 37254377497](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37254377497/job/111588311545) and [run 37265045192](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37265045192/job/111620051932), the last one 12 minutes before #42541 merged.

## Modifications

`git revert 456d533e` (#42541). `base.py` and `mrope.py` go back byte-for-byte to their state after #41282; the patch is identical to f6fcda8827, and nothing else has touched either file since.

This brings back the fp32 `cos_sin_cache` on HIP that `test_rope_rocm.py` checks for, and with it the fused QSA indexer prep on HIP (`_use_fused_prep` requires an fp32 cache; benchmarks in #41282).

## Checklist

- [x] Clean revert onto current main, no conflicts
- [ ] CI: `stage-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` passes

title: [Fix] dsa: Fix ragged seed indices before MTP draft decode
author: cognaiger9
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
Fused DSA prefill can produce top-k indices into the batch’s flattened logical KV space. The draft model captures these indices as MTP seeds and reuses them in the next draft decode, which expects physical KV slots.
This mismatch can select incorrect KV entries or cause out-of-bounds reads, particularly when long requests share cached prefixes and logical offsets exceed physical cache capacity.

The engine config that exercises this error:
```
SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK=1 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/PhalaCloud/GLM-5.3-W4AFP8 \
  --quantization w4afp8 \
  --tp 8 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse_q8 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4
```

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Add `prepare_mtp_seed_indices()` to map fused RAGGED seeds through the producer’s page table before capture.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->
CPU: tests added in `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_index_topk_share.py`

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->
The conversion applies only to fused RAGGED seed export at the draft-prefill (EXTEND) → next draft-decode (DECODE) boundary. Post-verification draft extend (DRAFT_EXTEND_V2) already exports PAGED seeds and requires no conversion.

title: [Fix] Quantize reloaded FP8 weights after native sharding
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42590
* #42589
* #42588
* #42587
* #42586
* __->__ #42585
* #42484
* #42468
* #42426

## Motivation

Reloading an unchanged checkpoint can change FP8 weights and scales because reload quantization runs before native TP sharding and scale updates use the wrong partition. With Qwen3-0.6B, TP4/attention-DP2, this caused GSM8K subset accuracy to fall from **45% to 1.5%** after QKV reload.

## Changes

- Quantize each local destination after its native parameter loader performs sharding and packing. Write into the existing FP8/scale storage and preserve untouched per-channel rows.
- Preserve one native `model.load_weights()` call with the complete input. Defer FP8 parameter callbacks, then replay each destination with one local BF16 staging matrix; non-FP8 parameters, including norms and tied embeddings, follow native loading.
- Avoid old-weight dequantization, cross-call BF16 staging caches and duplicate quantization at session finalization.
- Validate per-tensor destination coverage and checkpoint names before mutation. Require the audited deferred-write contract: Qwen2 legacy/v2 and Qwen3 loaders are supported; other loaders fail during initialization.

## Validation

Rebased PR head `e2d57acc14` on main `59740a728f`. Prior validation is recorded at combined stack head `5a863f8592`. No CI or GPU tests were rerun for this rebase.

**Accuracy fix.** Four B200 GPUs, Qwen3-0.6B online FP8, TP4/attention-DP2; first 200 GSM8K test questions, 5-shot, greedy non-thinking decoding, maximum 512 new tokens:

| Reload path | Cold | After unchanged reload |
|---|---:|---:|
| Unfixed QKV scale placement | 90/200 (45%) | 3/200 (1.5%) |
| Correct destination layout, QKV reload | 90/200 (45%) | 90/200 (45%) |
| Fixed complete-checkpoint public update session | 90/200 (45%) | 90/200 (45%) |

The complete session updates all **311 keys in 29 chunks** through public begin/update/end APIs. All 200 output texts/token sequences, **21,082 generated token logprobs** and **3,995 teacher-forced gold token logprobs** match cold inference exactly. The 200-question complete-session measurement uses loader `0d891b82de`; the audited single-call loader also passes a 32-question cold/reload smoke with identical outputs and logprobs (15/32 in both runs). These are bounded subset measurements, with CUDA graphs disabled.

**Reload latency and memory.** Complete Qwen2.5-0.5B checkpoint, 24 layers / 290 keys / tied embeddings, one B200, TP1, per-channel FP8, GPU BF16 inputs; 5 warmups and 25 alternating repeats (`fbc7656eb6`). The parent-loader comparison holds the native model method constant:

| Native loader | Parent median | Fixed median | Parent extra allocated peak | Fixed extra allocated peak |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen2 legacy | 12.92 ms | 10.47 ms | 350.71 MiB | 16.63 MiB |
| Qwen2 v2 | 15.53 ms | 12.37 ms | 350.71 MiB | 16.63 MiB |

Both use one native call per reload; fixed parameters match cold loading and retain storage addresses. These are reload-only timings, not serving throughput.

**Correctness coverage.** The TP4/attention-DP1/2 integration matrix passes 104 native cold-load comparisons, including Qwen2/Qwen3 KV replication, independent query/KV layouts and full/partial per-channel updates. Retained native Qwen2 legacy/v2 and Qwen3 regressions cover tied-head copying, storage stability, failure restoration and rejection before mutation. Tests use kernel 0.4.8 with the documented compatibility override; these results do not certify every current-head model/format combination.

title: [SM90] Use native block32 DeepGEMM for DeepSeek-V4.1
author: vladnosiv
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash stores its dense FP8 weights in [32,32] blocks, compared with [128,128] in DeepSeek-V4-Flash.
These GEMMs cover attention, the shared expert, indexer, Engram, and DSPARK linears.
On Hopper, the SGLang dispatcher routes K-block != 128 to Triton, while the DeepGEMM wrapper only accepts [128,128]. Larger prefill GEMMs can use the existing BF16 weight-cache fast path.
https://github.com/sgl-project/DeepGEMM/pull/95 added native SM90 block32 support. This PR integrates that path into SGLang using sgl-deep-gemm==0.2.2

## Modifications

Routes supported SM90 block32 linears through the existing DeepGEMM wrapper with:
`fp8_gemm_nt((Aq, As), (Wq, Ws), D, recipe=(1, 32, 32))`
The integration preserves checkpoint FP8 weights and UE8M0 activation rounding, passes the block dimensions through the GEMM wrapper, and prepares block32 scale buffers during kernel warmup.
Both prefill and decode use native DeepGEMM. The unused BF16 weight expansion is skipped when DeepGEMM is selected. Explicit Triton selection and unsupported shapes retain their fallback.

Server configuration for the tests listed below

```
SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1 \
sglang serve \
  --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --random-seed 42 \
  --tp 4 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
  --attention-backend dsv4 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
  --ep-size 4 \
  --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \
  --reasoning-parser auto \
  --tool-call-parser auto \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
  --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000
```

## Accuracy Tests

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| 1279/1319 | 1285/1319 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: [Diffusion] Fuse Anima AdaLN modulation and cache the FFI callable
author: cuzmi
body:
## Motivation

With Anima's default 28-block configuration, each transformer forward evaluates 85 AdaLN modulation chains:

`LayerNorm(x) * (1 + scale) + shift`

Reuse the existing bit-exact modulation kernel to reduce intermediate tensor traffic and kernel launches. Also cache the shared kernel's exported FFI callable to avoid repeated function lookup.

## Modifications

- Route Anima's eager CUDA FP16/BF16 modulation through `modulate_scale_shift`.
- Convert strided scale/shift views into contiguous `[B, D]` rows when necessary, without copying the `[B, S, D]` activation.
- Cache the exported FFI callable.
- Preserve the original expression for CPU, FP32, and `torch.compile` tracing.

LayerNorm reduction, CUDA arithmetic, launch geometry, and the shared wrapper's eligibility checks, fallback, and error propagation remain unchanged.

## Correctness

Validated on H200 against baseline `affa261e3d`, with candidate `05bee50b2f`:

- **Anima AdaLN:** 36/36 bit-exact comparisons covering FP16/BF16/FP32, batch sizes 1/2, sequence lengths 17/1024/4096, hidden size 2048, and gated/ungated modules. Eligible cases assert fused dispatch; FP32 cases assert fallback. BF16 batch-2 CUDA graph replay also passes.
- **Shared callers:** 48 component cases per version cover FLUX, Ideogram, LingBot, and LTX-2 video/audio. Output byte hashes and dispatch counts match across versions. Five changed-input CUDA graph replays per version pass.
- **Existing tests:** 42 passed per version across the modulation kernel, FLUX/LTX model-site, LTX layout, and Anima test suites.
- **Full-model generation:** all 16 images across the two benchmark experiments have identical decoded pixels and PNG bytes.
- Pre-commit passes for both modified files.

The AdaLN and shared-caller checks use external validation scripts with synthetic inputs. No new repository unit tests are added. Other models were validated at the component level.

[Correctness report, test logs, and source provenance](https://github.com/cuzmi/sglang/tree/codex/pr-results/diffusion-prs/anima-modulate-fusion/rebase_validation)

## Performance

**Workload:** H200, BF16, TP1, FA attention, one 1024×1024 image, 30 steps, CFG 4, seed 42. `torch.compile` and CUDA graph are disabled.

**Model:** `circlestone-labs/Anima-Base-v1.0-Diffusers`, revision `073c3a9db359c31ad0e8aa268d15775473c2176c`.

Both versions run on the same GPU in ABBA + BAAB order. Each arm starts a fresh CLI process, performs a one-step same-resolution request warmup, and then measures one 30-step request: **four process samples per version**.

The metric is worker request wall time with CUDA synchronized at request boundaries. Both versions receive the same timing-only instrumentation, which is excluded from this PR. Model loading, warmup, output transport, and PNG saving are excluded. No profiler or per-stage synchronization is enabled.

| Version | Mean request (ms) | Range (ms) | Sample SD (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline `affa261e3d` | 3185.73 | 3164.03–3229.58 | 29.95 |
| Candidate `05bee50b2f` | 3065.52 | 3051.42–3099.78 | 22.94 |

Mean latency decreases by **120.21 ms (3.77%)**. The ABBA and BAAB blocks separately show **3.98%** and **3.56%** reductions.

All eight requests complete 30 steps with identical outputs. Source hashes and timing instrumentation are verified for the experiment.

These results cover one fixed prompt, seed, resolution, and GPU instance. The two code changes are measured together; their individual contributions are not isolated.

[Benchmark reports, configuration, and measurements](https://github.com/cuzmi/sglang/tree/codex/pr-results/diffusion-prs/anima-modulate-fusion/rebased_perf)

[Published evidence index](https://github.com/cuzmi/sglang/blob/codex/pr-results/diffusion-prs/anima-modulate-fusion/PUBLISHED.md) · [Raw synchronized run: logs, timings, and eight PNGs](https://github.com/cuzmi/sglang/tree/codex/pr-results/diffusion-prs/anima-modulate-fusion/results/anima-rebased-sync-perf-20261004T164048Z-a9b075f6)

<details>
<summary>Additional measurements and historical evidence</summary>

A separate eight-arm experiment using the unmodified native worker timer measured **3151.82 → 3016.00 ms (4.31% lower)**. That timer does not explicitly wait for CUDA completion before stopping. It ran on another H200 instance, so these samples are not pooled with the primary result, and the difference between experiments does not measure the CUDA tail.

Earlier experiments against `6fa3fe69e2` included an integration-only run that regressed by **4.93%** and a later combined run that improved by **4.15%**. The latter included duplicate-check removal already present in the current baseline. These historical results are retained in the archive and are not used as the current PR's performance result.

Historical profiling showed modulation launches decreasing from 510 to 170 in a denoising step containing 170 AdaLN calls. This was not reprofiled after rebasing.

[Historical experiment archive](https://github.com/cuzmi/sglang/tree/codex/pr-results/diffusion-prs/anima-modulate-fusion/evidence)

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [ ] Add unit tests. No new repository tests are added; existing suites and external validation results are listed above.
- [x] Review documentation requirements. No user-facing API or configuration changes.
- [x] Provide correctness and performance results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [Diffusion] Fuse Anima FP32 split-half Q/K RoPE
author: cuzmi
body:
## Motivation

Anima applies split-half RoPE separately to Q and K, materializing negation, concatenation, FP32 casts, and arithmetic intermediates. The eager chain launches 16 GPU kernels per paired Q/K call.

## Modifications

- Replace this chain with one paired Triton kernel, mounted after the unchanged Q/K RMSNorm.
- Preserve separate FP32 multiplication and addition boundaries with `enable_fp_fusion=False`, then cast once to the output dtype.
- Retain eager fallback for unsupported inputs, gradient-enabled execution, and `torch.compile`.
- Verify each new signature with `BitExactFusionGate`; disable fusion on mismatch or kernel failure.

## Accuracy Tests

- **50 numerical cases passed**, covering FP16/BF16, multiple batch sizes, sequence lengths, head counts, signed zero, and finite extremes.
- **17 existing Anima tests passed**.
- Fallback, gradient parity, first-use/warmed CUDA graph capture, and compiled-eager comparison checks passed.
- All eight generated outputs, including separate profiling runs, have identical PNG and decoded-pixel hashes.
- Pre-commit passed. No new persistent unit tests were added.

### Output comparison

Original 1024×1024 outputs, without resizing or recompression:

| Baseline | Fused FP32 RoPE |
| --- | --- |
| ![Baseline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cuzmi/sglang/fdae78b0b6a4763bfd272fcce961437284106aca/diffusion-prs/anima-fp32-rope/pr_assets/baseline.png) | ![Fused](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cuzmi/sglang/fdae78b0b6a4763bfd272fcce961437284106aca/diffusion-prs/anima-fp32-rope/pr_assets/fused.png) |

Both PNGs are byte-identical:

`17057f6295cd6cf1a2affc7c2c8ae45889199edf9bde129a4a3dc1b15f9e212d`

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Configuration:** one H200, Anima-Base-v1.0-Diffusers, 1024×1024, 30 steps, seed 42, CFG 4, FlashAttention, compile/BCG disabled.

Same-container A/A control followed by ABBA, with fresh processes and warmup excluded. Each variant has two independent measured processes.

| Metric | Baseline mean | Fused mean | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Denoise | 2843.80 ms | 2250.42 ms | **20.87%** |
| Framework request duration | 3110.29 ms | 2520.63 ms | **18.96%** |

A/A denoise variation was **0.07%**. Request duration excludes process startup and model loading.

At BF16 `[1,4096,16,128]`, the paired operator benchmark improved from **411.50 μs to 24.12 μs**, including wrapper checks and output allocation. Separate traces confirm **16 → 1 kernel launches** per Q/K call. Full-model profiling confirms actual fused dispatch without fallback. Profiled timings are excluded from the speed table.

### Evidence and scope

[Raw results, pinned configuration, reproduction scripts, traces, and original images](https://github.com/cuzmi/sglang/tree/fdae78b0b6a4763bfd272fcce961437284106aca/diffusion-prs/anima-fp32-rope)

- Measured candidate: `6143cce2d2f5701b07ae155ad652705cabe7b646`
- Model revision: `073c3a9db359c31ad0e8aa268d15775473c2176c`

Results cover one GPU and one generation configuration. They do not establish performance under compile, BCG, multi-GPU execution, or other workloads. After merging upstream main, the Anima and kernel files remain unchanged; the numbers above remain measurements of the original candidate commit.

title: [Fix] Make the fused KDA beta sigmoid bit-identical to torch.sigmoid
author: vincentzed
body:
Part of #41609. This PR fixes the sigmoid part of that issue.

- #39688 moved the beta sigmoid into the `kda_gate_chunk_cumsum` kernel and wrote it as `tl.sigmoid`.
- `tl.sigmoid` does not return exactly the same bits as `torch.sigmoid`, because `tl.exp` and Triton's `/` are approximate on CUDA. KDA feeds its state back into itself, so this small difference grows along the sequence.
- This PR uses `tl.div_rn(1.0, 1.0 + libdevice.exp(-x))` instead. It matches `torch.sigmoid` on all 2^32 fp32 inputs. `tl.sigmoid` differs on 95.7M of them.
- The tests now require exact equality and check every finite bf16 value.
- Not fixed here: the fused KDA projection and the separate projections still give different results (mean |Δlogp| 0.255 in the same test). One concatenated GEMM is not bit-identical to the separate GEMMs. To match v0.5.20 exactly, the projection fusion from #39688 also has to be turned off for these checkpoints.

Test on a B300 with `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`. I feed the same 8 x 2048 tokens to each build (teacher forcing) and compare the logprobs. The reference is main with the `beta.float().sigmoid()` that was used before #39688.

| | mean \|Δlogp\| | p99 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 0.240 | 2.35 |
| this PR | 0.000 | 0.000 |

There is no slowdown. Kernel time measured with CUPTI at H=64, K=128: 54.8 -> 54.4 us at 2857 tokens, and 2327 -> 2312 us at 131072 tokens.

title: [AMD] MiniMax-M3 indexer CP: packed scoring for EAGLE verify rows
author: kevin-mii
body:
## Motivation

With #41488 merged, MiniMax-M3 indexer context partitioning serves EAGLE chain verify: the ROCm verify
funnel hands the indexer each request's `ndt` draft rows as ordinary decode queries. The CP scorer then
scores them one row at a time. Its 16-row tile holds `WORLD`=4 live rows per program (one head per lane),
so it runs 25% occupied and reads every index-K block once per draft row -- four times per request at
the default 4 draft tokens.

## Modifications

1. **Packed scorer** (`kernels/ops/attention/minimax_sparse/decode/indexer_cp.py`). `score_local_blocks`
   takes `packed_queries`; when a request's rows fit the tile it launches `_score_shard_packed`, which maps
   tile row `i` to (draft row `i // WORLD`, head `i % WORLD`). That fills the tile and reads each K block
   once per request. Rows in a group can straddle a block boundary, so the K-read branch uses the group's
   longest row, while masking and the forced init/local blocks use each row's own length. A pack that does
   not fit the tile falls back to the existing kernel. Like `_score_shard`, it skips the K read for a slot
   past the request table (graph padding).
2. **Wiring** (10 lines). `minimax_sparse_decode` and `MiniMaxIndexerCP` pass `packed_queries` through;
   the backend passes the draft-token count for target-verify batches and 1 otherwise. Only the CP branch
   reads it, and CP already serves score-only layers alone, so no other path changes.

The packed kernel stays separate from `_score_shard`. Folding the plain path in as `PACK=1` reproduces it
exactly, but the vector row addressing measured 3.6% slower on ordinary decode (30/30 shapes).

## Accuracy Tests

Selection is exact, not approximate: the packed kernel must pick the same block IDs the native selector
picks for each row.

- `test_packed_verify_rows_match_the_native_selector` (registered AMD, 1 GPU) builds verify rows the way
  the funnel lays them out -- 4 requests x 4 draft rows -- ending at 32767..32770, so one tile mixes
  256- and 257-block rows with different local windows. bf16 and fp8: exact ID equality on every head.
  Each of these injected bugs fails it: the group's block count in place of each row's, sizing the group
  by its shortest row (fails only because the rows straddle a block boundary), dropping the forced local
  window, a wrong score-row index, and dropping the fp8-to-bf16 cast (fp8 subtest only).
- The shared `_inputs` now gives each request a permuted, gapped slot that never equals its row or group
  index. A packed kernel that addresses K by group index instead of through the slot table now fails (2
  subtests); before this change it passed. `test_minimax_indexer_cp.py` on gfx950 (MI355X): 2 passed,
  6 subtests.
- The test moves to the MI35x suite and skips off gfx950: its reference kernel needs more shared memory
  than MI300 has, and the CP path is gfx950-only.
- GSM8K-500, 5-shot: 0.896 packed vs 0.892 unpacked (same A/B as below). On the main A/B below:
  0.864 / 0.866 packed vs 0.884 / 0.886 unpacked; this raw few-shot gate moves about +-3.5 points between
  server instances of the same build, so read it as no change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MiniMax-M3 MXFP4 (`amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4`), TP4 on MI350X, EAGLE3 (`Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA`,
3 steps / 4 draft tokens, real acceptance), `SGLANG_MINIMAX_M3_INDEXER_CP=1`,
`SGLANG_MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_TOPK_FREQ=1`. AgentX agentic traces (SemiAnalysis AIPerf, seed 42), 900 s per
point, both arms side by side on the node's two GPU halves with identical flags. The unpacked arm forces
`pack = 1` -- the scorer main runs today. Total tok/s per GPU:

| | unpacked (main today) | packed (this PR) | change | ITL p50 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| c=24 | 26,576 | **28,380** | **+6.8%** | 12.4 -> 10.2 ms |
| c=32 | 32,294 | **34,282** | **+6.2%** | 17.1 -> 12.7 ms |

Measured on a development branch whose CP kernel is identical to this PR and whose verify wiring is
equivalent (packing applies only to CP's score-only layers).

**On main.** A-B-B-A on one TP4 replica (MI350X, hostcall-capable node, `sgl_kernel` built from main),
main `44a2558d40` vs main + this PR, same flags as above, c=24, 900 s per arm:

| arm | total tok/s/GPU | ITL p50 |
|---|---:|---:|
| main | 16,912 / 16,983 | 30.8 / 31.0 ms |
| main + this PR | **17,728 / 17,731** | **28.5 / 28.0 ms** |

+4.6% throughput, -8.6% ITL p50; repeated arms agree within 0.4%. A 20-step decode profile of the PR arm
shows only `_score_shard_packed` (57 launches per rank per step, one per sparse layer) and no `_score_shard`.
Both arms ran with `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled`, because main crashes on its first M3 prefill
with breakable prefill graphs (fixed by #41845); the decode/verify path this PR changes is unaffected.
The gain on main is smaller than on the development branch because main's other per-step costs are larger.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation -- not applicable; no user-facing interface change.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.

title: [DSpark] Mask uncommitted slots before commit-inject cache lookups
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

`_commit_inject_layout_kernel` looks up `req_to_token` and then `full_to_swa_mapping` for **every** verify slot, and only afterwards replaces uncommitted slots (`col >= commit_len`, including graph-padding rows with `commit_len == 0`) with `-1`. The second lookup uses the first lookup's value as an address, so a stale or garbage `req_to_token` entry in a discarded slot is still dereferenced. Writing `-1` afterwards does not undo that read.

In practice this rarely goes out of bounds, because `req_to_token` is zero-initialized and stale entries are usually still valid locations. That is also why the existing parity test, whose random entries are all in range, never caught it.

## Modifications

- Triton kernel: compute `committed = mask & (c < commit_len)` first and use it as the load mask for both lookups (`other=0` and `other=-1`). Positions are still written for every slot.
- Torch reference (`build_commit_inject_layout`): stop going through `assign_extend_cache_locs_func` and index `req_to_token` directly. Uncommitted rows and columns are clamped to 0 with `torch.where`, so the result has a fixed shape (no data-dependent boolean indexing, no host sync), matching `build_unified_commit_inject_layout`.
- Test: in the existing `commit_len` edge case of `test_dspark_kernel_parity.py`, the uncommitted row's `req_to_token` entries are set to `1 << 40`, far beyond the mapping, and the case now also checks Triton/torch parity.

## Accuracy Tests

On B300 (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13), running this branch:

- `test/registered/spec/dspark/test_dspark_kernel_parity.py`: 1 passed, 22 subtests passed. The commit-inject case also runs clean under `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` (0 errors). On unpatched `main`, the same test fails with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access`.
- Standalone poison driver (commit_lens 0 / 2 / full) under `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck`:

| Kernel | memcheck | `swa_loc` |
|---|---|---|
| unpatched `main` | **8 errors** (`Invalid __global__ read`) | n/a |
| this PR | **0 errors** | `[-1]*7`, `[10, 11, -1, ...]`, `[10..16]` (as expected) |

- Earlier, on a downstream branch, the same masking gave GSM8K 1278/1319 vs a 1281/1319 baseline.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput claim. The kernel now skips two loads for discarded slots.

title: [Perf] moe: Enable deferred finalize for NVFP4 on the routed TRT-LLM runner
author: vincentzed
body:
## Motivation

This PR covers the NVFP4 case of #39299.

- Deferred finalize means the MoE kernel skips its last step, the weighted sum over the selected experts. A later fused kernel then does that step together with the shared-expert add.
- Today NVFP4 experts on the `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` runner can never use it. The hybrid FP8 + NVFP4 DeepSeek V4 / V4.1 checkpoints always use this runner, because the routing options built into the kernel (`RoutingMethodType`) cannot describe their routing.
- The routed FlashInfer op already accepts `do_finalize=False`, and the MXFP4 method uses it (#38798). The NVFP4 routed path was never connected to it. Three places block it:

1. `FusedMoE.supports_deferred_finalize` requires `is_flashinfer_trtllm()`, which is false for the routed backend.
2. `DeepseekV2MoE` only defers when the top-k output format is `BYPASSED`. The routed runner receives regular top-k ids and weights.
3. `fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp4` only set `defer_finalize` when `use_routed_topk` was false, and the routed call always passed `do_finalize=True`. #44666 has since changed this on main, so the routed call can now defer. Blockers 1 and 2 remain on main.

wenchen76 is working in the same direction in wenchen76/sglang#1.

## Modifications

- `FusedMoE`: new flag `supports_routed_deferred_finalize`. It is true for `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod` on `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`, when there is no A2A backend and the routed scaling factor is already folded into the top-k weights. `supports_deferred_finalize` is not changed, so the CuTe DSL layer-boundary fusion, Kimi and Qwen paths behave as before.
- `DeepseekV2MoE`: picks which flag to check from the top-k output format. `BYPASSED` top-k checks the old flag. Regular top-k checks the new one.
- `fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp4`: #44666 (merged 2026-10-18) now makes the routed call defer on main, and this PR uses that code. This PR only adds the workaround below to it.
- Workaround: the deferred routed call still passes a `[T, hidden]` output buffer, although the kernel does not write to it in deferred mode. FlashInfer's autotune cache key includes the output shape. With `output=None` the lookup misses the tuned entry and the expert GEMMs run with a fallback tactic. On FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 each call was 9 to 14% slower. I filed this as flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6077 with a standalone repro. The lookup still misses on 0.7.2 (see below). The buffer can be removed once that is fixed.
- `SGLANG_ENABLE_MOE_DEFERRED_FINALIZE=0` turns the new behavior off.
- `test_deepseek_v4_amd_tp4.py`: the MoE stub gets the new attribute.

Since #42245, the V4 block asks the MoE for deferred output whenever the fused mHC kernel can be used. With this PR the NVFP4 routed runner can return it. So NVFP4 now uses the single fused kernel that does the finalize, the shared-expert add and the all-reduce, and no other condition has to change.

## Accuracy Tests

**Kernel level.** I compute the same MoE output in two ways and compare them:

- the routed op with the finalize inside the op, followed by the shared add
- the routed op with deferred finalize, followed by `moe_finalize_fuse_shared`

The weights are synthetic NVFP4 weights with the V4.1-Flash expert shapes (hidden 5120, intermediate 2304, 384 experts, top-6). There are 28 cases: T in {1, 2, 8, 33, 96, 192, 384}, with all experts local and with an EP slice of 96 local experts, and with per-tensor and per-token activation scales.

| metric | worst case |
|---|---|
| max abs diff / max abs ref | 1.06e-3 |
| cosine similarity | 0.99999964 |

**End to end.** `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4`, TP4 + EP4, no speculation, 12 prompts x 48 greedy tokens with logprobs. "main" is the same code with `SGLANG_ENABLE_MOE_DEFERRED_FINALIZE=0`.

| comparison | tokens that match before the first difference | prompts with identical output |
|---|---|---|
| main vs main (second server launch) | 508 / 508 | 12 / 12 |
| PR vs PR (second server launch) | 505 / 505 | 12 / 12 |
| PR vs main | 246 / 504 | 2 / 12 |

Each build gives the same output on every launch. The two builds differ from each other because `moe_finalize_fuse_shared` adds the routed and the shared output in FP32 and rounds to BF16 once. The old path rounds after the finalize and again after the add.

**GSM8K**, 500 questions, greedy, same serving config:

```bash
python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 500 --num-threads 32 --port 47311 --temperature 0 --max-tokens 2048
```

| arm | score | std error (n=500) |
|---|---|---|
| main (`SGLANG_ENABLE_MOE_DEFERRED_FINALIZE=0`) | 0.982 | 0.006 |
| this PR | 0.984 | 0.006 |

**Unit tests**, run on this branch and on unmodified main (`70f0b7351e`) in the `nightly-dev-cu13-20261005` image:

```bash
python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/layers/quantization test/registered/unit/layers/moe \
  test/registered/unit/layer_boundary test/registered/unit/models \
  test/registered/unit/kernels/test_fused_op_dispatch.py test/registered/unit/test_mxfp8_moe_runner_backend.py
```

Both give 1163 passed, 330 failed, 29 skipped. The same tests fail on main.

<details><summary>Failing files, identical on main</summary>

| file | failing |
|---|---|
| `layer_boundary/test_append_stages.py` | 1 |
| `layer_boundary/test_declared_attention_cp.py` | 5 |
| `layer_boundary/test_dp_attention_cp_gather.py` | 6 |
| `layers/moe/test_copy_weight_views_before_h2d.py` | 3 |
| `layers/moe/test_flashinfer_cutlass_swiglu_params.py` | 1 |
| `layers/moe/test_fused_moe_native.py` | 1 |
| `layers/quantization/test_fp4_kv_cache_quant_method.py` | 3 |
| `layers/quantization/test_modelopt_nvfp4_moe_scales.py` | 7 |
| `layers/quantization/test_nvfp4_embedding.py` | 1 |
| `layers/quantization/test_nvfp4_moe_backends.py` | 3 |
| `models/test_deepseek_v4_mxfp4_shared_expert_requant.py` | 5 |
| `models/test_draft_entry_hook_parity.py` | 1 |
| `models/test_gpt_oss_runai_ownership.py` | 1 |
| `models/test_inkling_per_expert_sync.py` | 3 |
| `models/test_kimi_k25.py` | 5 |
| `models/test_kimi_k3_mla_output_gate.py` | 1 |
| `models/test_kimi_k3_vision.py` | 2 |
| `models/test_kimi_vl_moonvit.py` | 2 |
| `models/test_locate_anything.py` | 1 |
| `models/test_paddleocr_vl_vision.py` | 2 |
| `models/test_qwen3_vl_feature_materialization.py` | 1 |
| `models/test_qwen4_exp_ple_table.py` | 1 |
| `models/test_zaya_cca.py` | 8 |

The table counts top-level test ids. The 330 includes subtests.

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

4x B300, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1. The baseline is the same code with `SGLANG_ENABLE_MOE_DEFERRED_FINALIZE=0`.

```bash
SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC=rng SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static \
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=5.4 SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected \
sglang serve --trust-remote-code --model-path nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --tp 4 --ep-size 4 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 47311 \
  --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64
```

```bash
aiperf profile -m nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 --url http://127.0.0.1:47311 \
  --endpoint-type chat --streaming --use-server-token-count \
  --concurrency 8 --request-count 48 --warmup-request-count 8 \
  --isl 8192 --isl-stddev 0 --osl 1024 --osl-stddev 0 \
  --extra-inputs '{"ignore_eos": true, "min_tokens": 1024, "temperature": 1.0, "top_p": 0.95}'
```

ITL p50 in ms. This is the branch after merging main `abed685de1`, which includes #42245. Each column is one server launch. Two launches of the same build differ by up to 2.2% per cell.

| concurrency | deferred finalize off | this PR | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.005 | 1.004 | -0.1% |
| 4 | 1.529 | 1.455 | -4.8% |
| 8 | 2.042 | 1.945 | -4.7% |

GSM8K on the merged branch is 0.984 (500 questions, same command as above).

Before #42245, the same change was within noise (-0.3% to -1.1%, with 4 launches of main and 2 of the PR). Deferring alone only removes the finalize step, which is about 1.5% of GPU time (#39299). The gain now comes from the fused kernel also doing the all-reduce.

## Rerun after merging main at `7bc92100ad`

Image `nightly-dev-cu13-20261031-a2cafa56`, FlashInfer 0.7.2. This branch also merges cleanly with main at `c757c4bb7c`.

- The merge had one conflict, in `FusedMoE`. #46140 added `packed_nvfp4_routed_deferred` to `supports_deferred_finalize`. I kept it and kept `supports_routed_deferred_finalize` next to it.
- The serve commands now add `--revision 3431dde3247c13b5957f682b1e3c6fcae2566079`. The current revision of `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4` stores the Engram tables as MXFP4, and SGLang cannot load them. The model card says the same.
- Kernel level, same 28 cases as above: worst max abs diff / max abs ref is 1.06e-3. All cases pass.
- Unit tests, same command as below, on this branch and on unmodified main `7bc92100ad`: both give 1864 passed, 392 failed, 50 skipped, with the same failing tests.
- GSM8K, 500 questions, greedy, one run per arm: deferred finalize off gave 0.974 in 46.6 s, this PR gave 0.976 in 44.5 s. The gap is 1 question. These scores come from sgl-eval 0.1.3 because `run_eval` is deprecated, so do not compare them with the `run_eval` scores above.
- The longer wall time reported in the check against `ce329c85fa` did not appear in this run.

```bash
sgl-eval run gsm8k --base-url http://127.0.0.1:47311/v1 --num-examples 500 --num-threads 32 --temperature 0 --max-tokens 2048
```

- Decode speed, same commands as the check against `ce329c85fa`, one server launch per arm:

| server | concurrency | out tok/s, off | out tok/s, this PR | ITL p50 ms, off | ITL p50 ms, this PR | ITL delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plain | 8 | 1432.4 | 1521.7 | 5.194 | 4.849 | -6.6% |
| Plain | 32 | 3394.2 | 3565.3 | 8.519 | 7.978 | -6.4% |
| Plain | 64 | 5130.1 | 5395.4 | 10.991 | 10.351 | -5.8% |
| DSpark | 8 | 3431.4 | 2857.0 | 1.835 | 1.742 | -5.1% |
| DSpark | 32 | 7391.5 | 7778.6 | 3.205 | 3.108 | -3.0% |
| DSpark | 64 | 10539.2 | 10502.9 | 4.619 | 4.607 | -0.3% |

- The DSpark row at concurrency 8 has 32 requests. It took 5.7 s with this PR and 4.8 s with deferred finalize off, and TTFT p99 was 1462 ms against 301 ms. I have not found why. Median per-user decode in that row was 574 tok/s with this PR and 545 tok/s off.
- The servers logged no scheduler exceptions.

## Check against main at `ce329c85fa`

This branch still merges with main cleanly, so nothing was pushed. #44901 changed where the routed scaling factor is applied, and the deferred routed path adds the shared output without scaling, so I checked this branch again with main `ce329c85fa` merged in locally. Image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261019-3c560089`, 4x B300.

- Kernel level, same 28 cases as above: worst max abs diff / max abs ref is 1.06e-3. All cases pass.
- Unit tests, same command as below: this branch and unmodified main both give 1567 passed, 348 failed, 40 skipped, with the same failing tests.
- GSM8K, 500 questions, greedy, run twice with the arm order swapped: deferred finalize off gave 0.982 and 0.984, this PR gave 0.978 and 0.976. The gap is 2 and 4 questions; one standard error is about 0.006.
- The GSM8K wall time was longer with this PR in both orders (60.6 s against 52.3 s when the baseline ran first). I have not found why. The fixed-length runs below show no decode slowdown.
- Decode speed at higher concurrency, ISL 2048, OSL 512, the aiperf command above with `--concurrency N --request-count 4N`, one server launch per arm. "Plain" is the serve command above without the four env vars and the `--mem-fraction-static`, DSpark and `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` flags, plus `--max-running-requests 256`. "DSpark" is the serve command above.

| server | concurrency | out tok/s, off | out tok/s, this PR | ITL p50 ms, off | ITL p50 ms, this PR | ITL delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plain | 8 | 1100.4 | 1236.0 | 6.502 | 6.080 | -6.5% |
| Plain | 32 | 2840.4 | 3157.8 | 9.695 | 9.045 | -6.7% |
| Plain | 64 | 4666.9 | 4982.5 | 12.111 | 11.254 | -7.1% |
| DSpark | 8 | 3033.9 | 3145.2 | 1.878 | 1.786 | -4.9% |
| DSpark | 32 | 7929.7 | 7866.4 | 2.950 | 2.990 | +1.4% |
| DSpark | 64 | 10479.1 | 10495.8 | 4.503 | 4.485 | -0.4% |

- With DSpark at 64 requests a decode step has 320 rows, above `SGLANG_MOE_DEFERRED_FINALIZE_MAX_TOKENS` (192), so deferral is off there.
- The servers logged no scheduler exceptions.

## Rerun after merging main at `19cb24f1e1`

Same image, FlashInfer version and commands as the rerun below.

- The merge had one conflict, in `fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp4`. #44666 added deferred finalize to the routed call, which was this PR's runner change. I kept main's version, including its check that rejects an unsupported top-k format. The only change left in that function is the workaround buffer: it is now passed whenever it is set, so a deferred routed call still hits the tuned autotune entry.
- flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6077 repro on 0.7.2, CUPTI median in us:

| T | `do_finalize=True`, `output=[T, H]` | `do_finalize=False`, `output=None` | `do_finalize=False`, `output=[T, H]` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 141.9 | 138.1 | 138.1 |
| 64 | 711.2 | 713.4 | 698.6 |

- Kernel level, same 28 cases as above: worst max abs diff / max abs ref is 1.06e-3. All cases pass.
- GSM8K, 500 questions, greedy: 0.984 with deferred finalize off and 0.984 with this PR.
- ITL p50 in ms, one server launch per column:

| concurrency | deferred finalize off | this PR | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.187 | 1.140 | -4.0% |
| 4 | 1.567 | 1.504 | -4.0% |
| 8 | 1.893 | 1.848 | -2.4% |

- Unit tests, same command as below, on this branch and on unmodified main `19cb24f1e1`: both give 1530 passed, 342 failed, 40 skipped, with the same 76 failing test ids.
- The servers logged no scheduler exceptions.

## Rerun after merging main at `14ad64c411`

This rerun uses image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261018-b234b5c3`, FlashInfer 0.7.2 (the version main pins) and 4x B300. The serve, aiperf and GSM8K commands are the same as above.

1. The merge had no conflicts. `deepseek_v2.py` now reads `supports_routed_deferred_finalize` inside the short-circuit chain, at the point where main reads `supports_deferred_finalize`. Before the merge, it read the attribute on every MoE forward pass.
2. The CuTe DSL layer-boundary fusion for DeepSeek-V3/GLM (`can_defer_finalize` in `DeepseekV2Model`) still checks only `supports_deferred_finalize`. This PR does not turn it on for the routed runner. See Follow-ups.
3. MiMo-V2, Qwen2-MoE, Qwen3.5, the Qwen4 decode path and Kimi-K3 defer only with bypassed top-k or on the MXFP4 runner. This PR does not change them.
4. flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6077 is still open, and 0.7.2 does not fix it. A deferred call with `output=None` still misses the tuned entry. FlashInfer logs `No tuned config covers flashinfer::trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe input_shapes=((64, 0), ...); falling back to runner=MoERunner tactic=-1`. In the standalone repro from the issue, the fallback tactic is now within 2% of the tuned one (CUPTI median, in us):

| T | `do_finalize=True`, `output=[T, H]` | `do_finalize=False`, `output=None` | `do_finalize=False`, `output=[T, H]` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 142.0 | 137.9 | 138.1 |
| 64 | 711.8 | 712.5 | 699.6 |

The buffer stays until the lookup is fixed. flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6549 proposes a fix and is still open.

**Kernel level**, same 28 cases as above: worst max abs diff / max abs ref is 1.06e-3. All cases pass.

**GSM8K**, 500 questions, greedy:

| arm | score | std error (n=500) |
|---|---|---|
| deferred finalize off (`SGLANG_ENABLE_MOE_DEFERRED_FINALIZE=0`) | 0.984 | 0.006 |
| this PR | 0.978 | 0.007 |

The difference is within one standard error.

**ITL p50 in ms**, one server launch per column:

| concurrency | deferred finalize off | this PR | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.197 | 1.132 | -5.4% |
| 4 | 1.562 | 1.498 | -4.1% |
| 8 | 1.914 | 1.858 | -2.9% |

Both arms are slower at concurrency 1 than they were at `fc3385d530` (1.13 to 1.20 ms now, 1.00 ms then), and TTFT p50 dropped from about 146 to 94 ms. These changes came from main. They show up with deferred finalize both on and off.

**Unit tests**, on this branch and on unmodified main `14ad64c411`:

```bash
python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/layers/quantization test/registered/unit/layers/moe \
  test/registered/unit/layer_boundary test/registered/unit/models \
  test/registered/unit/kernels/test_fused_op_dispatch.py test/registered/unit/test_mxfp8_moe_runner_backend.py \
  test/registered/unit/eplb/test_waterfill_eplb.py test/registered/unit/layers/test_mla_parallel_groups.py \
  test/registered/unit/lora test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_modelopt_loader.py \
  test/registered/cuda_graph/breakable/test_deepseek_dual_stream_outputs.py
```

Both give 1527 passed, 342 failed, 40 skipped, with the same 76 failing test ids.

## Rerun after merging main at `fc3385d530`

- The merge had one conflict. #39199 added NVFP4 weights with a padded hidden size, and it turns deferred finalize off for them. This PR keeps that rule: the routed path defers only when the hidden size is not padded.
- GSM8K, 500 questions, same command as above: 0.980.
- Unit tests, same command as above: 1197 passed, 333 failed, 35 skipped. Unmodified main at `fc3385d530` gives the same counts and the same failing tests.
- ITL p50 in ms, same serve and aiperf commands as above, one server launch per column:

| concurrency | deferred finalize off | this PR | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.008 | 0.997 | -1.1% |
| 4 | 1.601 | 1.443 | -9.9% |
| 8 | 2.050 | 1.947 | -5.0% |

## Follow-ups

1. MXFP8 experts on the routed runner (`Fp8MoEMethod` with `use_mxfp8`, the RL rollout path from #28676). #46387 by wenchen76 does this. It needs the same change in `fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp8`, limited to `use_mxfp8`. The kernel-level comparison passes at V4.1-Flash shapes (worst max abs diff / max abs ref is 4.9e-3). It still needs an end-to-end run on an MXFP8 checkpoint before I open a PR for it.
2. The MXFP4 method should pass the output buffer on every deferred call. Today it only does so for 96 < T <= 384, so smaller batches hit the same autotune miss. On V4.1-Flash MXFP4, passing it on every call moved ITL p50 from 1.020 to 1.002 ms at concurrency 1, with no change at concurrency 2 to 8.
3. Remove the dummy output buffers in both the NVFP4 and the MXFP4 paths once flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6077 is fixed (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6549 proposes a fix).
4. Turn on the DeepSeek-V3/GLM CuTe DSL layer-boundary fusion for the routed runner. That needs an end-to-end run on a V3 or GLM NVFP4 checkpoint served with `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`.

title: perf(mla): use native SATFINITE FP8 conversion in MLA KV/Q preparation
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

The FP8 MLA KV/Q preparation kernel (`set_mla_kv_concat_q`) converts BF16 → FP8 E4M3 with `__NV_NOSAT`. With CUDA 13.4 this lowers to a software (FP64-mediated) conversion; `__NV_SATFINITE` lowers to the native packed `F2FP.SATFINITE.E4M3` instruction and removes most of the kernel's latency.

## Modifications

Change only the conversion mode and its comment.

Semantic change: finite overflow and ±inf now clamp to ±448 instead of becoming NaN; NaN stays NaN. TMA stores, DCP indexing, PDL sync and the launch heuristic are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

- Q-output reference checks passed for 1, 8, 32, 64, 128, 512 and 1024 rows.
- Conversion helper checked over all 65,536 BF16 encodings (PDL on/off): non-NaN outputs match the clamped reference bitwise, and NaN stays NaN.
- GSM8K (full 1319, FP8 KV, TP8, with speculative decoding): NOSAT 95.00% vs SATFINITE 94.84% (-0.15 pt, within noise; 28 paired regressions and 26 improvements).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel microbenchmark (H=12, DCP=1), CUDA-graph warm medians and cold medians after a 512 MiB L2 flush. Measured on SM107 (Vera Rubin); the conversion change itself is not architecture-specific.

| Rows | Warm, SATFINITE vs NOSAT | Cold, SATFINITE vs NOSAT |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | -67.2% | -61.0% |
| 8 | -59.7% | -58.1% |
| 32 | -58.0% | -62.9% |
| 64 | -59.6% | -63.4% |
| 128 | -59.1% | -63.7% |
| 512 | -66.9% | -63.2% |
| 1024 | -67.5% | -59.1% |

title: [Bugfix] Guard merge_state sgl_kernel import on non-CUDA platforms
author: rumitdesai
body:
## Motivation
`sglang.srt.layers.attention.merge_state` imported `merge_state_v2` from
`sgl_kernel` unconditionally, although that implementation is only used when
`is_cuda()` is true.

On non-CUDA installations where `sgl_kernel` is unavailable, importing the
wrapper raises `ModuleNotFoundError` before its existing Triton fallback can be
selected.

## Modifications

Move the `sgl_kernel` import behind the existing CUDA predicate.

CUDA behavior remains unchanged, while non-CUDA platforms can import the
wrapper and reach `merge_state_triton` as intended.

Other unconditional module-level `sgl_kernel` imports were observed during the
investigation, including imports in FlashAttention, FlashMLA, XPU, and MiniCPM
backend modules. Most appear to be hard dependencies of explicitly selected
backends, unlike this portable wrapper, which already has a non-CUDA fallback.

Whether those imports should also be guarded or made lazy can be discussed
separately. They are intentionally outside the scope of this focused change.

## Validation

From the repository root:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib
import sys
from unittest.mock import patch

import sglang.srt.utils as utils

# Simulate a non-CUDA installation without sgl_kernel.
sys.modules["sgl_kernel"] = None

with patch.object(utils, "is_cuda", return_value=False):
    module = importlib.import_module(
        "sglang.srt.layers.attention.merge_state"
    )

assert callable(module.merge_state)
print("PASS")
PY
```

Before this change, the command raises `ModuleNotFoundError`. After the change,
it prints `PASS`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This change does not modify kernel execution or model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This change only guards an import that is unused on non-CUDA
platforms and does not alter the runtime hot path.

title: perf(kda): rebalance MTP verify precompute and state synchronization
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

The Kimi-K3 KDA MTP verify kernel (`fused_kda_decode_mtp_dspark`) spends much of its time on precompute dependencies and state synchronization. Rebalancing that work cuts kernel latency by up to 1.37× on B300, and outputs stay bitwise identical.

## Modifications

All changes are in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/kda_decode_mtp.py`:

- Keep convolution weights in producer registers, removing their shared-memory staging and the initial CTA barrier.
- Reorder independent convolution/gate work and prefetch output-normalization inputs using spare producer capacity.
- Use warp-level synchronization for warp-local state transfers, and overlap resident-state loads with precompute while keeping the cross-warp barriers.
- Public wrapper, launch dispatch, persistent AOT cache, ReplaySSM, padding, output normalization and caller-owned output buffers are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

B300 (SM103), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13, CuTe DSL 4.6.2:

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_decode_mtp.py` and `test/registered/unit/layers/test_kda_decode_mtp_slot_stride.py`: pass on both main and this PR.
- **Bitwise identical to main**: 56 configurations (N ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64}, H=12, num_spec ∈ {3, 7}, ReplaySSM ring on/off, fused output norm on/off). All 420 output tensors were compared (output, intermediate SSM/conv states, ReplaySSM rings, recurrent state), with 0 differences.
- `compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck`: 0 hazards across 4 shapes covering ring/full-snapshot and norm on/off.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B300, H=12, K=V=128, same process. **Warm** = per-call time from a CUDA graph of 50 back-to-back calls (median of 11 replays). **Cold** = in-graph `[512 MiB L2 flush, kernel] × 20` minus a flush-only graph (median of 21).

Speedup range (main → PR) across N = 1…64:

|---|---|---|---|
| ReplaySSM ring + output norm | 3 | 1.22–1.29× | 1.22–1.35× |
| ReplaySSM ring + output norm | 7 | 1.22–1.33× | 1.26–1.37× |

| Full snapshots | 3 | 0.98–1.04× | 0.98–1.04× |
| Full snapshots | 7 | 1.02–1.04× | 1.02–1.04× |

<details><summary>Per-shape timings (µs)</summary>

| N | num_spec | ring | onorm | warm main → PR | cold main → PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| 1 | 3 | 1 | 1 | 6.145 → 4.957 | 10.246 → 8.195 |

title: [Fix] quantization: Preserve BF16 NaNs in per-token FP8 quantization
author: aurickq
body:
## Motivation

BF16 NaNs currently become finite FP8 values during per-token group quantization. For example, the UE8M0 path converts a NaN lane to `+448`, hiding invalid activations from downstream NaN checks. Preserve those NaNs so callers can detect the original numerical failure.

This intentionally changes the BF16 FP8 sanitization behavior introduced in #32188 and optimized in #32296. FP16 retains its existing behavior because its scaling multiplier can overflow for finite inputs.

## Modifications

- Use NaN-preserving clipping for BF16 with UE8M0 scales.
- Use the saturating FP8 conversion directly for BF16 with FP32 scales. It preserves NaNs while still saturating infinite and out-of-range scaled values.
- Keep FP16, FP32-input, and INT8-output behavior unchanged.
- Add plain/fused and flat/masked regression cases, including fully NaN groups, masked padding, and CUDA graph capture/replay. Retain the existing non-finite sanitization cases for FP16.

## Accuracy Tests

- Python syntax, Ruff checks/formatting, Clang-format 20.1.7, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Full CUDA regression suite: **123 passed, 0 skipped** on GB300 with CUDA 13.2. Command: `SGLANG_JIT_KERNEL_RUN_FULL_TESTS=1 pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_per_token_group_quant.py`. This includes finite-input regressions, BF16 NaN preservation, FP16 sanitization, and capture/replay with finite and NaN-containing inputs.
- Graph tests cover the quantizer itself. Full-model graph warmup with async assertions enabled remains a separate validation requirement because warmup may read uninitialized buffers.

## Speed Tests

No benchmark completed on this upstream revision. The change adds no host synchronization or separate GPU kernel.

title: [CI] Keep diffusion-only kernels and tests out of the srt stages
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

`main_package` in `_pr-test-check-changes.yml` matches every file under `python/sglang/kernels/` and `test/`, so a diffusion PR that only touches diffusion kernels or diffusion tests runs the whole srt pipeline (base-a, base-b, base-c). Those PRs then fail or stall on srt tests they cannot affect. Examples from the last two days:

| PR | Diffusion-only paths it touched | What blocked it in srt stages |
|---|---|---|
| #41906 | `kernels/ops/diffusion/`, `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/` | `test_multi_lora_backend` (base-b), `base-c-test-8-gpu-b300` queued |
| #41830 | `kernels/ops/diffusion/`, `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/` | `test_multi_lora_backend` (base-b) |
| #36318 | `kernels/ops/diffusion/attention/` | `test_multi_lora_backend` (base-b), `base-c-test-8-gpu-b300` queued |
| #41894 | `test/registered/unit/diffusion/` | `test_disaggregation_dp_attention` on H20 (base-c), `base-c-test-8-gpu-b300` queued |
| #41819 | `test/registered/unit/diffusion/` | `test_multi_lora_backend` (base-b) |

Most of these paths are already listed under `multimodal_gen`, and all of them are under `jit_kernel` where relevant, so the diffusion CI and the kernel unit tests still run for them.

## Modifications

1. **`main_package` no longer matches diffusion-only paths.** `dorny/paths-filter` counts a file if it matches any pattern, so a subdirectory cannot be excluded with a `!` pattern; instead the two catch-all globs (`kernels/!(aot)/**` and `test/**`) are rewritten level by level to skip:
   - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/**`
   - `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/diffusion/**`
   - `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/**`
   - `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/diffusion/**`
   - `test/registered/unit/diffusion/**`
   - `test/registered/e2e/diffusion/**`

   `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/common/**` stays in `main_package`: srt reaches it through `kda_kernels/layernorm_modulate_triton.py` (used by `srt/layers/attention/linear/kernels/kda_flashinfer.py`). `kda_kernels/` (including `kda_kernels/csrc/diffusion/`) is shared with srt and is unchanged.

2. **`multimodal_gen` gains the two diffusion paths it was missing:** `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/diffusion/**` and `test/registered/e2e/diffusion/**`, so every path dropped from `main_package` still starts the diffusion CI.

Only `pr-test.yml` and `pr-test-extra.yml` are affected on PRs. The nightly and weekly workflows that reuse this job force `run_all_tests`. `pr-test-amd.yml` has its own filter and is out of scope here.

## Trade-offs

- **`kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py` is excluded, although srt imports it.** `sglang/kernels/ops/__init__.py` eagerly imports every operator group, so any of the ~320 srt files that import `sglang.kernels.ops.*` executes the diffusion facade. Importing `sglang.kernels.ops` loads only that one module (`sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion`); its implementations are resolved lazily (PEP 562). An import-time break in this file is still caught before merge: the 39 test files under `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/` registered in `base-b-kernel-unit` all import `sglang.kernels.ops`, and that stage runs through `jit_kernel` for any change under `python/sglang/kernels/`; the diffusion CI imports it as well. Keeping the file in `main_package` would have kept most diffusion kernel PRs on the srt pipeline: 20 of the 28 commits that touched `kernels/ops/diffusion/` since Sep 5 also touched this `__init__.py`.
- **`test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_sites.py` is registered in `base-a-test-cpu`,** which is gated by `main_package`. A diffusion-only PR no longer runs it at PR time. It still runs on scheduled and full runs.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A, CI configuration only.

## Verification

The `main_package`, `multimodal_gen` and `jit_kernel` filters, before and after this change, were evaluated with picomatch using the options `dorny/paths-filter@v3` passes (`{dot: true}`), over all tracked files (10,131):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Files that leave `main_package` | 176, all under a `diffusion/` directory |
| Files under `kernels/ops/diffusion/common/` that leave it | 0 |
| Files that newly enter `main_package` | 3: `test/README.md`, `test/registered/README.md`, `test/registered/unit/README.md` |
| Files that leave `main_package` and match neither `multimodal_gen` nor `jit_kernel` | 0 |

Replaying the changed-file lists of recent PRs:

| PR | `main_package` | `multimodal_gen` | `jit_kernel` |
|---|---|---|---|
| #41906, #41830, #36318, #41894 (diffusion kernels/tests) | true -> **false** | true -> true | true |
| #41819 (diffusion unit tests) | true -> **false** | true -> true | false |
| #41839 (touches `python/pyproject.toml`) | true -> true | true -> true | true |
| #42391 (touches shared `kda_kernels/`) | true -> true | true -> true | true |
| #42348 (srt-only) | true -> true | false -> false | false |

Checked that srt does not use the excluded paths: no Python import of `kernels.ops.diffusion` outside diffusion code except `ops/diffusion/common` (kept); `kda_kernels` resolves its `diffusion/*.cuh` sources from `kda_kernels/csrc/`, not `jit/csrc/diffusion/`; no C++/CUDA `#include` of diffusion headers outside the diffusion directories.

`actionlint` and `pre-commit` pass on the changed workflow.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).

title: [Spec] Fix wrong tokens from compact-verify CUDA graphs when a token tier is captured more than once
author: ormandj
body:
## Motivation

With compact ragged verify (`SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact`), `DecodeCudaGraphRunner` captures a token tier more than once when there are several attention graph variants (for example the DSv4.1 candidate graphs `candidate_unfiltered` / `candidate_filtered`) or several PD-mux streams. Each capture calls `_capture_ragged_verify_layout`, which allocated a new `RaggedVerifyLayout` and replaced `_captured_ragged_layouts[num_tokens]`. At replay, `_stage_ragged_verify_layout` copies the live `verify_lens` / `qo_indptr` only into that registered layout, which belongs to the last capture. Graphs from the earlier captures still read the layout they were captured with. That layout holds synthetic capture offsets, and replay no longer refreshes it.

A graph that reads an earlier capture's layout tensors directly computes with the wrong offsets whenever the live layout differs from the capture-time one. On current main, PD-mux with the TRT-LLM MLA backend is exposed: its ragged verify path pads and unpads queries with the captured `verify_lens` / `qo_indptr` inside the graph. For DSv4.1 target verify on current main the defect is latent, because its backend copies the live layout into its own buffers outside the graph. The ragged Engram hashing and `token_req_indices` in #40567 read `qo_indptr` inside the DSv4.1 verify graph; with them, the `candidate_unfiltered` graphs map tokens to the wrong requests.

I measured an A/B on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP4, 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, SM120, DSpark gamma 5, compact verify, #40567 applied) with an earlier revision of this fix, which copied the live layout into each capture instead of sharing one layout per tier. I compared the log-prob of each generated token with a plain prefill of the same text:

- Without the fix, per-token differences reached 14.4 nats. At temperature 1, 9 of 32 streams looped to the length cap.
- With the fix, the maximum difference was 0.79-0.86 nats, and none of the 32 streams looped or hit the cap.

Eager verify was correct in both builds.

## Modifications

`_capture_ragged_verify_layout` creates the layout once per token tier and returns the same object for later captures of that tier. Every graph of the tier now captures the tensors that replay refreshes.

## Accuracy Tests

- `TestRaggedVerifyLayoutPerTier` (CPU, `test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`) calls the capture-layout helper twice for tier 24 with two variant labels, stages a live layout, and checks both returned layouts' `qo_indptr_device` / `verify_lens` against the live padded layout. On main the first layout keeps its synthetic offsets (7 of 9 `qo_indptr` entries differ).
- The end-to-end A/B in Motivation (earlier revision of the fix).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked. The replay staging code is unchanged; capture reuses one registered layout per token tier across attention variants and PD-mux streams.

title: [Fix] dsv41: Run DSpark compact verify by mapping packed verify tokens to their requests
author: ormandj
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #39173.

With `SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact`, DSpark target verify can pack unequal numbers of tokens per request. A compact CUDA graph tier can also hold more requests than full verify windows: for example, 42 tokens over 8 slots captures as `[6, 6, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5]`. Two DeepSeek-V4.1 components still assume `draft_token_num` tokens per request:

- `EngramHasher.forward` asserts `num_tokens == bs * draft_token_num`. Capture fails with `engram target-verify expects one equal block per request, got 42 tokens for 8 requests of 6`.
- `token_req_indices` calls `repeat_interleave(req, draft_token_num, output_size=num_tokens)`, which fails, or maps tokens to the wrong request, once the layout is not uniform.

As a result, DeepSeek-V4.1 compact verify fails on these layouts.

#40567 by @lidekang160122 identified both call sites and fixes them as part of a larger PD change. This PR fixes only the crash. It derives the token-to-request mapping in one shared helper and reuses Engram's existing extend kernel path, so it needs no kernel changes.

Depends on the shared-layout fix from #42709, now in main: both components read the verify layout inside the CUDA graph, and without it the DeepSeek-V4.1 graph variants captured first for a token tier would read a layout that replay does not refresh.

## Modifications

- `ragged_verify.py`: add `ragged_verify_token_rows(layout, num_tokens)`. It is a fixed-size `searchsorted` over the layout's `qo_indptr`, so it is safe under CUDA graph capture. Empty rows own no tokens, and the graph-padding tail maps to row `bs`.
- `EngramHasher.forward`: with a ragged layout, target verify uses the existing `MODE_EXTEND` path with `row = ragged_verify_token_rows(layout, num_tokens).clamp_max(bs - 1)` and `starts = layout.qo_indptr_device[:-1]`. As before, verify commits no history. Graph-padding tokens are hashed with the row the staged layout assigns them (a padding row, or the last row for the tail) and then discarded.
- `token_req_indices`: with a ragged layout, each token gets its request's pool index. The tail past the last request gets pool slot 0, like the padded rows of a dense verify graph; padding the staged layout assigns to a row gets that row's slot.
- Without a layout (static verify), both functions take the existing dense path unchanged.
- No change to capture slot sizing. The current `min(num_tokens, max_bs)` slots are valid once these components accept unequal rows.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/test_dsv41_compact_verify.py` (CPU tests and a CUDA graph replay test; all pass on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell):
  - Packed Engram hashes equal the hashes of each request verified alone on the dense path. Cases: the 42-token / 8-slot capture geometry, a batch with empty rows and a graph-padding tail, and one request in a 3-token graph. All three cases run with maximum n-gram sizes 4 and 8 and include a short prefix; the first two also include an image token. Engram history is unchanged.
  - A uniform layout gives the same Engram hashes and request indices as the dense path.
  - `token_req_indices` maps empty rows and the padding tail correctly.
  - A CUDA graph captured once is replayed with three different layouts, and Engram hashes on real tokens and request indices on all tokens match eager.
- `TestCapturedVariantsReadStagedLayout` (CPU, same file) calls `DecodeCudaGraphRunner`'s layout-capture helper twice for a 12-token tier, as the two DeepSeek-V4.1 attention variants do, stages live lengths [6, 1] for request slots 7 and 9, and checks that `token_req_indices` and `EngramHasher` read the live boundaries from either variant's layout. Without the shared layout from #42709, the first variant maps the real tokens to [7, 7, 9, 9, 0, 0, 0]. All six tests in the file, including the CUDA graph replay test, pass on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell.
- `test/registered/spec/dspark/test_ragged_verify.py`: unit test of `ragged_verify_token_rows`.
- An ad-hoc comparison with #40567's implementation on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), not part of this PR, gave bit-identical Engram hashes on real tokens and bit-identical request indices on all tokens. Coverage was 146 eager layouts (73 at each of n-gram sizes 4 and 8) and 22 CUDA graph replays, including the 42-token geometry, single-request graphs of 1 to 5 tokens, empty rows, and padding tails.
- End to end, I served DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with #40567's implementation and #42709 (not with this exact diff). Setup: 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, PCIe), TP4/EP2, DSpark gamma=5, compact verify with a profiled SPS table. I compared target log-probs of generated tokens with a plain prefill of the same text. The maximum per-token difference was 0.79-0.86 nats, the same as static verify. A temperature-1 run of 32 streams had no repetition loops.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The change itself adds one `searchsorted` per Engram call and per low-ratio request lookup in compact verify. Static verify is unchanged. Not benchmarked separately.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [diffusion] model: support Kandinsky 6
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Add native Kandinsky 6.0 audio/video generation and distilled video super-resolution to SGLang-Diffusion.

Opening as a draft for public review. The implementation has real GPU and HTTP coverage, but official-reference alignment and standard model CI baselines are not complete.

## Modifications

- Native Pro / Pro-distill text- and image-conditioned joint video/audio generation, Reason1 and CLIP conditioning, PiFlow scheduling, and audio/video decoding. No external model pipeline at runtime.
- Native distilled SR pipeline with video uploads, audio preservation, x2/x4/fractional scaling, latent upsampling, and tiled KVAE decoding.
- TP, Ulysses, Ring, CFG parallelism, FSDP, component/layerwise offload, LoRA and request-level Cache-DiT integration. Support and numerical limits are documented per pipeline; this is not a claim that every combination is validated.
- Matrix-RoPE and FP32 residual-gate kernels, plus shared fixes required by this model: exact LoRA base-weight restoration, CFG-local cache decisions, batched Ring attention, and PCIe-safe IPC selection.
- Unit/distributed tests, opt-in full-checkpoint HTTP regressions, and two cookbooks using the shared command picker. Hardware extrapolations are explicitly marked unverified.

Cookbooks: [Generation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/codex/kandinsky6-native-support/docs/cookbook/diffusion/Kandinsky/Kandinsky6.mdx), [Super-resolution](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/codex/kandinsky6-native-support/docs/cookbook/diffusion/Kandinsky/Kandinsky6-SR.mdx).

Thanks to @leffff, Kirill, and Artem Borisov for the original implementation and contributions; authorship is retained in the commit.

## Accuracy Tests

- Prior GB300 integrated suite: **348 passed, 5 skipped, 2 subtests passed**. Additional real multi-GPU generation, SR and HTTP tests cover repeated requests, shape changes, conditioning isolation, LoRA restoration, Cache-DiT opt-out, and offload.
- Latest RTX PRO 6000 SR matrix: **22 full-size offline requests and 18 HTTP requests completed** across resident, layerwise, serial, whole-tile and spatial-decode cases, including a separate allocator-budget probe.
- Whole-tile SR decoding matched serial RGB and raw audio exactly on the tested inputs/topologies. Spatial decoding is **not bitwise lossless**: RTX test PSNR **57.54 dB**, minimum first/middle/last-frame SSIM **0.99919**, maximum pixel difference **4/255**; audio exact.
- TP/Ring, encoder folding, SageAttention and Cache-DiT have separate numerical/quality boundaries in the cookbooks. Tile batching changes seeded output. None is implicitly presented as lossless.
- These comparisons use the initial native implementation or same-topology serial decoding, **not verified parity with an official Kandinsky6 Diffusers implementation**.

The latest main was integrated before publication. Pre-commit and all 23 cookbook-picker tests pass; merged-head Cache-DiT/LoRA/API regressions are being checked separately from the earlier benchmark runs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Representative SR E2E measurements, distilled checkpoint revision `3e3e10bcd23659eeeb23cac740258ee4fc14aa7d`, BF16, seed 42, tile batch 1, two steps per tile, 768x512x121-frame input at 24 fps, x2 output. Median of three hot requests after one initial request; no compile/startup warmup; includes MP4 saving and raw-frame return, excludes loading.

**Two RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs**, 96GB each, PCIe across CPU sockets without NVLink; 499.2 GiB host RAM. Driver 595.84, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.17.0, Diffusers 0.37.0, SDPA:

| Configuration | Hot E2E | Sampled per-GPU peak | Comparison with single-GPU resident |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 1 GPU, resident, serial | 134.09 s | 48.91 GiB | Reference |
| Ulysses2, resident, serial | 122.11 s | 48.81 GiB | Exact RGB/audio |
| Ulysses2, resident, whole-tile | 83.04 s | 48.81 GiB | Exact RGB/audio |
| Ulysses2, resident, spatial | 73.62 s | 37.45 GiB | RGB differs as quantified above |
| 1 GPU, layerwise, serial | 133.60 s | 37.43 GiB | Exact RGB/audio |

Memory is the maximum NVML sample across ranks during requests, sampled every 0.5 s, not summed usage or an exact instantaneous peak. The 30 GiB PyTorch allocator-budget probe is **not a 5090 measurement**. H100/H200/5090 SR recipes remain extrapolations. Other GB300 measurements and generation topology comparisons are in the cookbooks; input clips differ across hardware, so do not derive cross-hardware speed ratios.

The benchmarks predate the final main integration; they are not represented as a fresh exhaustive benchmark of the published head.

## Remaining Before Merge

- [ ] Review shared-path changes and pass upstream CI.
- [ ] Register standard model cases with approved video/audio GT, performance and VRAM baselines.
- [ ] Establish official-reference accuracy alignment when the corresponding implementation is available.

Explicitly unsupported: non-distilled VSR checkpoints with an incompatible output head, generation disaggregation, and production breakable CUDA graphs for this model. These are documented limits, not silently enabled features.

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit formatting and lint.
- [x] Unit/distributed and opt-in full-checkpoint tests.
- [x] Deployment cookbooks and command-picker regression tests.
- [x] Real GPU measurements with numerical and memory scopes stated.

title: [DSA] Fix pooled page table refresh for target verify CUDA graph replay
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

Fixes wrong DSA indexer page ids in speculative verify under CUDA graphs, which dropped `TestGLM53FlashB200DFlash2` below its GSM8K threshold. Caused by a semantic conflict between two PRs:

- #42178 changed `build_pooled_page_table_64` to return logical page ids (`real page id // pool_size`).
- #42489, branched before that change and merged ~6h later without a rebase, added a target-verify refresh in `update_pooled_paged_mqa_metadata` that writes the undivided `real_page_table[:, ::pool_size]`.

On main, target-verify replay therefore passes page ids `pool_size`× too large (4× for GLM-5.3-Flash).

## Modifications

Refresh the table with `torch.floor_divide(real_page_table[:, ::pool_size], pool_size, out=pooled_real_page_table)`. This matches `build_pooled_page_table_64` exactly and writes in place into the captured buffer in a single kernel.

## Accuracy Tests

`test_glm53_flash_b200.py::TestGLM53FlashB200DFlash2`, 4× GB300, GSM8K (500 questions, 20-shot, threshold 0.93):

| | GSM8K |
|---|---|
| Before | 0.892 |
| After | 0.930 |

`test_dsa_metadata_replay.py` fails on main (1596/12288 mismatched pooled page-table entries in `TARGET_VERIFY`) and passes after.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Per-call cost of the refresh on GB300 (24×2048 int32 table, `pool_size=4`):

| Variant | Time |
|---|---|
| `build_pooled_page_table_64` + `copy_` | 55.0 µs |
| `floor_divide(..., out=)` (this PR) | 16.9 µs |
