title: [Refactor] Translate each KV loc once per iteration
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* __->__ #42753
* #40492
* #40491
* #37628
* #37627

## Motivation

On the unified memory pool a KV slot has a virtual id (what the scheduler
allocates and `req_to_token` stores) and a physical id (what kernels index).
The conversion between them was done wherever an id was needed: every
`ForwardBatch` translated its own write window, every attention backend built
its own translated page table (some per forward, some per layer group, some
per captured mode), the multi-step draft kernel translated every id it
gathered, and the speculative KV writers translated the ids they were handed.
Within one speculative iteration the same window was translated three to four
times (draft, verify, draft extend, target-hidden KV writes), and a captured
graph translated its write ids a second time into a private buffer.

Besides the wasted launches, every one of those sites had to agree on which
ids were already physical, and a site that translated twice, or not at all,
silently read or wrote the wrong slot.

**This PR translates an iteration's write window once per sub-pool, in one
place, and gives every read exactly one translation, in one place too: the
translator's read primitives. A read table exists only once a reader that reads
the table form asks for it -- built into that reader's own capture-stable table
when it has one -- and every later reader takes it; every reader before it
translates in its own gather. No table is built that no reader asked for.**

## Modifications

**`KVLocPlan`** (`mem_cache/kv_loc_plan.py`, new) names one iteration's ids,
in every sub-pool of the pool. A sub-pool is an **`IdSpace`**: how it maps the
iteration's virtual token ids (`write`) and the page table its reads go through
(`read_v2p`). A runner's translator holds one per sub-pool its pool has
(`space(IdSpaceKind.FULL / SLIDING_WINDOW)`), keyed so that runners sharing a
sub-pool (a fused draft and its target) share the plan's results; adding a
sub-pool means registering a space, not adding fields. The window itself
stays in allocator-global ids: an NPU DCP target, which writes rank-local
slots, has its own full space mapping the window to them, while the
replicated draft binds the same window global. The plan holds:

- its write window, translated once into the full sub-pool
  (`write_physical`); the virtual window it was built from is never mutated
  (radix tree, accept path and lazy compaction still read it);
- `write_ids(reader, kind=, cols=)`: the window in any sub-pool's ids, derived
  on first use and kept for the iteration -- physical for the target and a
  fused draft, virtual for a static or private draft pool's full sub-pool;
  `cols` selects the part a forward writes (a draft step's columns, a flat
  index for a ragged verify's packed rows, or a run of the window's tokens
  for one half of a two-batch-overlap split, `TokenSpan`, read as a view);
- `read_table(kind=, rows=)`: a sub-pool's page table over
  `[0, seq_lens + read_extent)`, built when a reader that reads the table form
  (a page-table kernel, or a captured graph's table: `copy_page_table`) first
  asks for it, and then shared by every later reader of the iteration; built
  straight into a captured reader's own buffer -- no table of the plan's own,
  no copy; without host lengths (fa3's speculative overlap steps) the build
  stops at that buffer's width. A captured graph's padded lanes are appended by copy, reading the
  sink, and a reader that asks for its batch's rows gets exactly those, a view
  of a wider table a captured reader built. Until a table exists no reader
  waits for one: a CSR stream is gathered and translated straight into the
  reader's buffer, and the multi-step draft kernel gets the virtual rows with
  the sub-pool's page table (`KVIndexTable.v2p`), applied in its own gather.
  Whether to share is local -- does the plan hold a table yet -- so nothing
  predicts which runners will read one;
- `bind(batch, reader, cols)`: the one way a forward gets its write ids. A
  forward carries only the plan and its columns (`ForwardBatch.kv_loc_cols`);
  a backend that writes another sub-pool asks its translator at metadata time
  (`KVIndexTranslator.write_ids(batch, kind)`), padded to the batch's
  `out_cache_loc` with the sink, so padded batches, replay views and the
  halves of a two-batch-overlap split need nothing of their own.

`KVIndexTranslator` keeps what a plan needs: `plan` / `own_plan`, the plan's
table builder (`build_iteration_table`), the readers
(`read_source` for gather kernels, `pack_read_stream` for CSR streams,
`copy_page_table` for captured tables, `read_table`, each by `IdSpaceKind`),
`write_ids` for a backend's sub-pool, the dispositions, and
DCP's read production (`translate_dcp_read_ids`, the one translation that
stays outside a plan: which ids a rank reads is only known where the DCP index
kernels select them). A reader takes a plan's table only when it reads
through it -- same v2p table, same `req_to_token` rows (`is_read_by`).

The commits are layered:

1. **One plan per forward.** `ForwardBatch.init_new` builds a plan and binds
   it; replay views carry it.
2. **Writes.** A captured forward writes through the graph runner's own
   `out_cache_loc` slot, which already holds the batch's physical ids; triton
   and the trtllm_mla family drop the private capture buffers that translated
   them again. Batches a runner builds itself (captures, warmup runs) bind
   their own buffer as it is (`bind_runner_slots`). A forward
   whose lengths do not count the window it writes -- a verify, a speculative
   draft decode, a draft extend -- plans its reads that far
   (`window_read_extent`).
3. **Reads, per backend.** triton, the multi-step draft kernel, fa3, the
   trtllm_mla family, flashmla, trtllm_mha, flashinfer, flashinfer_mla, aiter,
   the speculative inputs' `generate_attn_arg_prefill` and DeepSeek's one-shot
   and chunked-prefix MHA indices read the plan's table instead of
   translating. The plan is passed explicitly through the index updaters (no
   hidden backend state).
4. **One plan per speculative iteration.** EAGLE (single- and multi-layer)
   plans the verify window when the draft gathers it -- in the same launch --
   and the draft decode, verify and draft extend share it. DSPARK and DFLASH
   plan their window where it is allocated; the draft block, the verify
   (including DSPARK's ragged verify, by index) and the target-hidden KV
   writers share it, and a compact DFLASH draft reads its own rows over the
   shared write ids (`reads_from`). At prefill, the target forward hands back
   its plan (`return_kv_loc_plan`), and the draft writes into the same slots
   take their ids from it.
5. **Removal.** The per-forward translate API goes (`index_table_for_batch`,
   `widened_index_table`, `build_index_table`, `fill_read_table`,
   `fill_packed_read_stream`, `translate_full_attn_ids`, `full_flat_v2p`,
   `sliding_window_write_loc_for`); `rebind_write_loc` becomes
   `bind_own_plan`. A padded (DP-attention) batch pads its eager page table
   along with its write ids. DiffusionGemma's FA4 prefill graphs build their
   streams from the batch's plan and take their sliding-window write ids from
   `write_ids`; their private capture buffer of translated write ids goes, as
   triton's did.
6. **Sub-pools as id spaces.** Every sub-pool, the sliding-window one
   included, goes through `IdSpace` (as above): a batch carries no ids of its
   own per sub-pool, a table no per-sub-pool twin, a reader no per-sub-pool
   flag. trtllm_mha's ragged-verify refill takes its sliding-window ids from
   the plan as well, instead of mapping `out_cache_loc`, which on the unified
   pool is already physical.
7. **Tests and comments of the stack.** The stack's tests that duplicate
   another test, pin a development-time detail, or only catch a failure that
   already stops the boot are dropped (about 60); the ones kept check the ids,
   rows, columns and bytes a kernel or captured graph gets. The fused-draft
   bind gate and the speculative aux-state resolver tests run weekly. The
   stack's comments and docstrings are cut to contracts and invariants.

A static pool does no translation work and runs no kernel for it: its plan
is a few host objects over the batch's own write ids, and every read is the
`req_to_token` passthrough, as before.

## Translations per iteration

Counted in the server processes over the 25-prompt greedy run (scheduler
iterations, prefill included), H200, against this PR's previous revision, which
shared a table whenever two runners read the same rows:

| configuration | write translations / iter | reads / iter, previous revision | reads / iter, this head |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-4B, MTP (EAGLE), fused draft, flashinfer | 1.00 | 1 table build, read 2.95 times | 2.00 stream gathers + 0.97 in the draft kernel's gather; no table |
| gpt-oss-20b (sliding window), EAGLE3, fused draft, triton | 1.00 | 1 table build, read 2.98 times; 1 sliding-window stream | 3.00 stream gathers + 0.99 in the draft kernel's gather; no table |
| Qwen3.8-27B, DSPARK, fused draft, flashinfer | 1.00 | 1 table and the first stream, read 0.97 times | 1.97 stream gathers; no table |
| gpt-oss-20b (sliding window), EAGLE3, fused draft, fa3 | 1.00 | 2 table builds | 2 table builds (fa3 reads the table) |

A forward that is the only reader of its rows -- every configuration without
speculation -- takes the same path as before. On B200: 1.00 read gather per
iteration for Qwen3.5-4B (flashinfer) and Kimi-Linear-48B (trtllm_mla, its table
built in the captured buffer) without speculation, and 2.00 for gpt-oss-20b (one
stream per sub-pool). Kimi-Linear-48B with DSPARK and a fused flashinfer draft
reads 0.99 stream gathers (the draft's) and 0.99 table builds (in the trtllm_mla
verify's captured buffer) per iteration: the reads it made before this PR,
without the target-hidden write translation it also made per iteration.

## Accuracy Tests

Greedy parity, 24 prompts x 128 tokens (token ids and per-token logprobs),
B200, every configuration against the stack tip (#40492) or `main`:
**identical in every arm, max |dlogprob| 0.0000.**

| target | speculation | attention | pool |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-4B | none | flashinfer | unified, static |
| Qwen3.5-4B | MTP (EAGLE) | flashinfer | unified (fused draft), static |
| Qwen3.5-4B | DFLASH | flashinfer | unified (fused; page size 1 / 64; compact window), static |
| gpt-oss-20b (sliding window) | none | triton | unified, static; TP2 DP2 with DP attention |
| gpt-oss-20b (sliding window) | EAGLE3 | triton | unified (fused; page size 1 / 64) |
| gpt-oss-20b (sliding window) | none / EAGLE3 | trtllm_mha | unified (eager: decode graphs are not supported there yet), static |
| Kimi-Linear-48B (TP2) | DSPARK, dummy draft | trtllm_mla target; trtllm_mha (private) / flashinfer (fused) draft | unified; ragged verify on flashinfer |
| Kimi-Linear-48B (TP2) | none; 8 requests over a 6.8k-token cached prefix (chunked-prefix MHA) | trtllm_mla | unified |

The whole stack against `main` (its merge base), H200: greedy parity over
25 prompts x 128 tokens, one at a time -- short prompts, 11k-15k-token
prompts (chunked prefill, past the sliding window), and requests that extend
a cached 6.8k-8.2k-token prefix. **Identical in every arm, max |dlogprob|
0.0000.**

| target | speculation | attention | pool |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b (sliding window) | none | triton | unified (page size 1 / 64), static |
| gpt-oss-20b (sliding window) | none | fa3 | unified |
| Qwen3.5-4B | none | flashinfer | unified, static |
| Qwen3.5-4B | none | triton, fa3 | unified |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | none / NGRAM | flashinfer | static |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | none | fa3 | static |

gpt-oss-20b with EAGLE3 on fa3, H200 (context 4096, so the long prompts are
2.5k tokens): the fused draft against the static pool on the same build and
against `main`, all three identical, accept length 1.204 in every arm.

Qwen3.8-27B with a real DSPARK draft (`RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark`, accept
length about 3.4), H200, fused draft under unified memory: identical to the stack
tip (#40492), accept length 3.396 on both. Qwen3.5-4B MTP (flashinfer), gpt-oss-20b
EAGLE3 (triton, fa3) and Qwen3.8-27B DSPARK, fused, are also identical between
this head and its previous revision, which read through a shared table: the
draft kernel's in-gather translation and the per-reader streams give the same
ids.

This head against the stack tip, B200, rerun: identical for Qwen3.5-4B (no
speculation, MTP, DFLASH), gpt-oss-20b (no speculation, EAGLE3 on triton) and
Kimi-Linear-48B DSPARK; and against its previous revision, H200: identical for
gpt-oss-20b EAGLE3 (fa3, and an fa3 target with a triton draft), Qwen3.8-27B
DSPARK and Qwen3.5-4B MTP.

The draft KV lands where it did: the accept length is identical log line for
log line against the stack tip (DFLASH 3.7465, MTP 2.8355, mean over the
run's decode logs).

Under page relocation: GSM8K, 400 questions 128 at a time, on a small unified
pool (`--mem-fraction-static 0.15`) where lazy compaction moved about 31k pages
of live requests in each run (Qwen3.5-4B, flashinfer; no invalid answers):

| speculation | stack tip | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| MTP (two runs each) | 0.873 / 0.865 | 0.882 / 0.875 |
| DFLASH | 0.887 | 0.890 |
| none | 0.868 | 0.873 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Against `main`, DSPARK on the unified pool, servers booted alternately on the
same GPUs, the same `bench_serving` load as below; greedy output identical to
`main` in every row:

| configuration | draft KV, `main` -> this head | c1 mean TPOT | c32 | GPU memory |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kimi-Linear-48B TP2 (B200), dummy draft on `trtllm_mha` (the default) | private -> private | 4.735 -> 4.710 ms (-0.5%) | median ITL 13.21 -> 13.20 ms | same |
| Kimi-Linear-48B TP2 (B200), dummy draft on flashinfer | private -> fused | 5.297 -> 5.357 ms (+1.1%), 5.377 -> 5.460 ms (+1.6%) on a second GPU pair, 3 runs each | median ITL +0.9% | 127.8 -> 90.7 GiB per rank |
| Qwen3.8-27B (H200), `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark`, triton target, flashinfer draft, fp8 KV | private -> fused | 5.945 -> 5.967 ms (+0.4%), 4 runs each | 965 tok/s both | 14.1 GiB less after pool allocation |

`main` admits DSPARK on the unified pool only with a triton or MLA-family
target, hence the triton target for Qwen3.8 (its cookbook recipe uses
flashinfer). The fused rows pay for one launch on the host path ahead of the
draft's graph: the plan translates the iteration's write window before the
draft runs, which writes physical ids into it, and at one request in flight
that is idle GPU time. `main`'s private draft writes virtual ids, and `main`
translates the target's window after the draft is launched. A flashinfer
draft that keeps a private pool on this stack pays the same launch.
Translating inside the iteration's first captured graph would remove it; the
plan build carries a FIXME for that.

B200, this head against the stack tip (#40492), the two trees' servers booted
alternately on the same GPUs (A/B/B/A), `bench_serving` random 1024 in / 256
out, 24 prompts at concurrency 1 (mean TPOT, output throughput) and 192 at
concurrency 32 (output throughput). Unified pool, CUDA graphs on. Greedy output
is identical to the tip in every row.

| configuration | runs per tree | c1 TPOT | c1 tok/s | c32 tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-4B, no speculation, flashinfer | 2 | 2.530 -> 2.530 ms (0.0%) | 0.0% | +0.9% |
| Qwen3.5-4B, MTP, flashinfer | 2 | 1.425 -> 1.425 ms (0.0%) | +0.1% | -2.7% |
| Qwen3.5-4B, DFLASH, flashinfer | 2 | 0.875 -> 0.865 ms (-1.1%) | +1.4% | +2.7% |
| gpt-oss-20b (sliding window), no speculation, triton | 2 | 1.865 -> 1.840 ms (-1.3%) | +1.5% | +10.8% |
| gpt-oss-20b (sliding window), EAGLE3, triton | 2 | 3.380 -> 3.340 ms (-1.2%) | +1.1% | -0.5% |
| Kimi-Linear-48B TP2, DSPARK, fused flashinfer draft | 6, on two GPU pairs | 5.412 -> 5.412 ms (0.0%: +0.3% on one pair, -0.3% on the other) | 0.0% | -0.6% |

At concurrency 32, two runs of the same tree differ by up to 18% on this box (a
gpt-oss tip run read 5,768 tok/s against 7,025), so that column resolves no
direction at two runs per tree; concurrency 1 holds to about 0.3%.

H200, this head against its previous revision, interleaved on one GPU, four
runs each, mean TPOT at concurrency 1 / 32; greedy output and accept length
identical in every pair. The previous revision already translated reads in
each reader's own gather when no reader read a table; this head also stops
building a table before a table reader asks for one:

| configuration | concurrency 1 | concurrency 32 |
|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b, EAGLE3, fa3 target, triton draft (the draft reads first) | 3.767 vs 3.765 ms (+0.1%) | 11.481 vs 11.463 ms (+0.2%) |
| gpt-oss-20b, EAGLE3, fa3 | 3.716 vs 3.713 ms (+0.1%) | 11.076 vs 11.092 ms (-0.1%) |
| Qwen3.8-27B, real DSPARK draft, fused, flashinfer | 5.563 vs 5.562 ms (0.0%) | 11.389 vs 11.372 ms (+0.1%) |
| Qwen3.5-4B, MTP, fused draft, flashinfer (path unchanged; runs overlap) | 1.703 vs 1.697 ms (+0.4%) | 5.411 vs 5.370 ms (+0.8%) |

Qwen3.8-27B DSPARK matches the stack tip: 5.56 ms here, and 5.56 ms for the tip
in an earlier interleaved run against an older revision of this PR that
measured 5.59 ms -- the time its table build spent on the critical path between
the verify and the next draft. The static pool on this stack matches `main`
(H200, gpt-oss-20b EAGLE3 on fa3: 3.69 / 10.48 vs 3.70 / 10.47 ms,
interleaved).

On an earlier revision of this PR, which built at least the tables this head
builds: long, mixed lengths (input 1.6k-16k tokens, 128 out, 64 prompts at
concurrency 16), with the transient peak the CUDA caching allocator reaches
above its warm baseline (worst rank), the same A/B/B/A order:

| configuration | tok/s | median ITL | transient peak allocated |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kimi-Linear-48B TP2, no speculation, trtllm_mla (captured table read first) | +3.7% | 5.29 -> 5.25 ms | -0.3 MiB |
| Kimi-Linear-48B TP2, DSPARK, fused flashinfer draft | -0.4% | 12.50 -> 12.54 ms | +0.1 MiB |
| gpt-oss-20b (sliding window), no speculation, triton, page size 1 | +0.2% | 4.07 -> 4.00 ms | -8.1 MiB |
| Qwen3.5-4B, no speculation, flashinfer, page size 1 | -0.7% | 3.55 -> 3.57 ms | -0.9 MiB |

A captured graph that reads the plan's table first has it built straight into
its own buffer, as the stack tip's capture fill did; a stream read before any
table reader is gathered on its own, as the stack tip did.

## Memory

`max_total_num_tokens` is identical between the stack tip and this PR in
every configuration above (1,381,150 / 1,415,720 / 775,733 / 1,808,890 /
1,620,448 / 970,112 / 2,357,632). gpt-oss-20b TP2 DP2 with DP attention boots
with slightly more (1,933,216 vs 1,913,256, the same in two separate rounds).

At run time the transient peak above the warm baseline matches the stack tip
within 8 MiB in every long-context configuration (the table above). No read
table is built that no reader asked for: a fused target and draft that both
read CSR streams or row gathers (flashinfer, triton) each translate in their own
gather, as before this PR, so no `rows x longest row` table appears (128 MiB at
page size 1 for 256 requests with one 128k-token row); and a stream read before
a captured table reader leaves the table to that reader, built in its own
graph buffer, rather than building one of the plan's own for it to copy. The
caching allocator's reserved peak is not compared: it varied by gigabytes
between two runs of the same tree.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Not validated end to end here:** NPU (its DCP write ids are covered by
  a unit test), fa3 with DFLASH or DSPARK (its draft and verify metadata
  paths are covered by unit tests), multi-layer EAGLE
  (no such model on the test machine), cutedsl_mla / tokenspeed_mla /
  flashmla, `--dcp-size > 1`, and two-batch overlap (the unified pool refuses
  it; a split batch's columns on a static sliding-window pool are covered by
  unit tests).
- **One translation stays outside a plan by design:** DCP's read production
  (`translate_dcp_read_ids`): which ids a rank reads is only known where the
  DCP index kernels select them.
- trtllm_mla's eager block table past a row's live pages now reads the sink
  (0) within the plan's width instead of -1; the kernels bound their reads by
  `seq_lens`, and a draft extend's padded queries (whose outputs are dropped)
  read valid memory.

title: [Perf] diffusion: fuse FLUX3 SwiGLU with rowwise FP8 quantization
author: trebladev
body:
## Motivation

FLUX3 FP8r MLP output projections materialize a BF16 SwiGLU activation, then launch a separate rowwise FP8 quantization kernel. Fuse these producers to remove the intermediate activation write/read and one kernel launch while preserving the existing quantized linear output.

## Modifications

- Add `fused_packed_swiglu_fp8_rowwise`: packed/row-strided BF16 `[B,T,2*K]` → padded E4M3 activations and FP32 per-row scales. Preserve both BF16 rounding boundaries, the scale floor, FP8 conversion and padding semantics.
- Integrate the fusion into FLUX3 FP8r MLP output projections on NVIDIA SM89+ for supported layouts and widths. Unsupported inputs and compilation retain the existing path. The downstream GEMM remains `torch._scaled_mm`.
- Use nine 1024-element tiles for SM89 `K=9216`, avoiding a masked 16384-element row. Other supported widths/devices retain the full-row implementation.
- Add lazy kernel registration, numerical and model integration tests, operator documentation, and a standalone microbenchmark.

## Accuracy Tests

Local GPU validation: RTX 4090 D (SM89), PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1.
For both `fp8r` and `sd-fp8r`, final action arrays are **byte-identical** before and after fusion on two synthetic observations (seeds 0 and 42) and one real DROID observation (seed 0):

- Maximum absolute difference: **0**
- Output shape: `(32, 8)`
- All output values are finite

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Standalone fused kernel

Measured on one **RTX 4090 D**, using synthetic BF16 packed slices with row stride `3*K`.

- **Before:** existing fused packed SwiGLU kernel followed by the existing rowwise FP8 quantizer.
- **After:** the new single fused SwiGLU + FP8 producer.

GEMM is excluded from this table. Measurements use 10 warmup calls per path, five alternating-order rounds of 100 ms, and median GPU time. The microbenchmark uses `triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph` to exclude Python launch overhead.

| Rows M | Width K | Before (µs) | After (µs) | Latency reduction | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 9216 | 9\.38 | 4\.27 | 54\.40% | 2\.19× |
| 32 | 9216 | 7\.25 | 2\.71 | 62\.63% | 2\.68× |
| 340 | 9216 | 20\.19 | 8\.76 | 56\.63% | 2\.31× |
| 2720 | 9216 | 223\.98 | 136\.75 | 38\.95% | 1\.64× |
| 3173 | 9216 | 264\.62 | 159\.22 | 39\.83% | 1\.66× |
| 3173 | 3072 | 31\.04 | 26\.84 | 13\.53% | 1\.16× |

### End-to-end model

Measured with local `flux-3-action-droid` checkpoints on one **RTX 4090 D**, using default eager serving settings, concurrency 1, and a warm caption cache.

Each configuration runs three rounds of 20 measured requests, with 10 initial warmups and two warmups before subsequent rounds. Results are the median of the three server-side inference latency medians, excluding network and client serialization. Only SwiGLU + FP8 fusion changes between the baseline and this PR.

| Variant | Before (ms) | After (ms) | Latency reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| fp8r | 1164\.04 | 1144\.74 | **1\.66%** |
| sd-fp8r | 209\.68 | 204\.84 | **2\.31%** |

Denoising latency also decreases:

| Variant | Before (ms) | After (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|
| fp8r | 1110\.23 | 1090\.08 |
| sd-fp8r | 153\.71 | 150\.10 |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [AMD] Keep MiniMax decode-score tile at 128 tokens off gfx950
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## What

On ROCm, `_decode_score_kernel` now uses the 512-token `BLOCK_SIZE_N` tile for batches of 4 or fewer only on gfx950. Other archs use 128, which is what every ROCm arch already uses for larger batches.

## Why

The ROCm heuristic was tuned on gfx950, which has 160 KB of LDS. A 512-token bf16 K tile needs 128 KB, and gfx942 (MI300X/MI325X) has only 64 KB, so `flash_decode_with_topk_idx` fails to load there at batch ≤ 4:

```
triton.runtime.errors.OutOfResources: out of resource: shared memory, Required: 131072, Hardware limit: 65536
```

`amd/test_minimax_indexer_cp.py` (added in #41488) is the first MI300 test to reach this path. It has failed in `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd` part 7 since it landed, e.g. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37395620023/job/112050816832

## Test plan

- [x] Compiled `_decode_score_kernel` for a gfx942 target with Triton 3.8.0, using the test's batch=1, 8K-context bf16 inputs. LDS was 131072 bytes with the 512 tile (same as CI) and 32768 bytes with the 128 tile.
- [x] On MI355X (gfx950), `test_minimax_indexer_cp.py` passes unchanged (512 tile). It also passes with the arch check forced to non-gfx950 (128 tile), so the selected top-k IDs match across both tile sizes.
- [x] On MI300 (gfx942) in `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd` part 7: [passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37481699749/job/112346794455) (`Ran 1 test in 20.070s / OK`), so the indexer-CP kernels are now exercised on gfx942.
- [x] Control: the same partition on a branch without this change still fails with `OutOfResources: shared memory, Required: 131072, Hardware limit: 65536` ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37478665740/job/112347556006)) — the 131072 figure matches the gfx942 compile measured above.

title: [Perf] speculative: Parallelize EAGLE spec-decode KV index building over token blocks (flashinfer draft decode; verify/draft-extend for flashinfer, flashinfer_mla, aiter)
author: brandonfzhang
body:
## Motivation

With EAGLE speculative decoding, every decode step rebuilds the paged KV index arrays for the draft and verify passes by copying live rows of `req_to_token`. The Triton kernels that do this launch one program per request and walk the row serially, so at long context (90k-170k KV tokens per request) they cost 0.3-0.6 ms of a ~22 ms decode step while moving only a few hundred KB.

#37659 already added token-block-parallel versions of both kernels (`NUM_STEPS` on `generate_draft_decode_kv_indices`, `TOKEN_BLOCK_PARALLEL` on `create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton`, plus `kv_indices_num_token_blocks`) but wired them only into the aiter backend's own launch sites. This PR enables them at the remaining EAGLE launch sites: the flashinfer draft-decode launch, and the shared verify / draft-extend builders in `eagle_info.py`, which serve the flashinfer, flashinfer_mla and aiter backends. Enablement only: no kernel change, no FlashInfer change, outputs bit-identical by construction (int32 index copy).

## Modifications

- `sglang/kernels/ops/kvcache/kv_indices.py`: one threshold and one sizing helper next to `kv_indices_num_token_blocks`: `SPEC_KV_INDEX_BLOCKS_MIN_CONTEXT = 32768` and `spec_kv_index_token_blocks(table_width, kv_lens_sum, batch_size, base_programs=None, length_cap=None)` (re-exported from `sglang.kernels.ops.attention.utils`). It returns 1 below the context gate; otherwise it sizes the block count from the batch's mean live KV length when the length sum is a host int (optionally capped), and from the table width when the sum lives on the device or is not passed (the sync-free bound). `eagle_info.py`, `flashinfer_backend.py` and `aiter_backend.py` import it; the private copies and duplicated constants are gone. AITER passes no length sum and its own `max_context_len` as the gate, so its block counts are unchanged (checked against the previous formulas on a 2025-case sweep: 0 mismatches).
- `eagle_info.py`: `EagleVerifyInput` and `EagleDraftExtendInput.generate_attn_arg_prefill` launch `create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton` on `(bs, nb)` with `TOKEN_BLOCK_PARALLEL = nb > 1`. These two methods are shared by the flashinfer, flashinfer_mla and aiter backends, so all three get the token-block grid at the verify and draft-extend sites (aiter already uses these kernels token-block parallel at its own sites).
- `flashinfer_backend.py`, `FlashInferMultiStepDraftBackend.common_template` (draft decode): same helper, with `base_programs = steps * num_seqs * topk`, sized from `forward_batch.seq_lens_sum` (a host int here, also at CUDA-graph replay) and capped by `draft_window_size + draft_sink_size` when a draft window is set. Launch `(steps * nb, num_seqs, topk)` with `NUM_STEPS = steps` when `nb > 1`; `nb == 1` compiles to the historical 128-wide kernel. With a 256K table, steps 3, bs 4 and 512 live tokens this is the historical `(3, 4, 1)` grid rather than 396 programs; at 4 x 169k it is 21 blocks. Any block count is correct because the kernel strides its blocks over the row; the launch runs outside the captured draft graph, so the grid may change per step.
- Tests (GPU): `test_draft_decode_window.py` gains `test_token_block_grid_matches_window_oracle`: `NUM_STEPS > 0` with 2 / 3 / 33 token blocks against the closed-form `kv_indptr` oracle and the `[sink + recent] + tree` slot oracle (windowed, pure-recent, cap > seq_len, tree, paged tree, 262145 / 1029306-token rows), plus bit-for-bit equality with the one-block grid. `test_spec_kv_indices_grid.py::test_draft_grid_equivalence` now runs every case with and without a 4032 + 64 draft window.

Scope: only servers with `context_len >= 32768`, and only the EAGLE draft-decode, verify and draft-extend index builders (flashinfer draft decode; verify / draft extend for flashinfer, flashinfer_mla and aiter). Non-speculative prefill/decode builders, the wave backend and aiter's own draft launch are untouched. No environment switch.

## How to reproduce

Server (8x H200, SGLang v0.5.19-cu130 image for the numbers below; `main` with this PR behaves the same):

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
  --tp-size 8 --expert-parallel-size 8 --mem-fraction-static 0.75 --context-length 262144 \
  --max-running-requests 4096 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --trust-remote-code \
  --quantization fp8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
  --attention-backend flashinfer --enable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --stream-interval 50 --scheduler-recv-interval 10 \
  --tokenizer-worker-num 6 --enable-metrics --enable-cache-report
```
Environment: `SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1`. The A/B in the tables was this exact server with the three token-block launches on vs off (a source patch of v0.5.19 with an environment kill switch); on `main` the equivalent is this PR vs its base commit, there is no runtime switch.

End-to-end replay: [aiperf](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/aiperf) 0.12.0 (git `b7b16cf8`), the InferenceX AgentX MVP scenario on its public agentic-coding trace set, one hour per arm:

```bash
aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp --url localhost:8000 \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 --endpoint-type chat --streaming --use-server-token-count \
  --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126_256k --num-dataset-entries 393 \
  --max-context-length 262144 --concurrency 10 --benchmark-duration 3600 \
  --trajectory-start-min-ratio 0.25 --trajectory-start-max-ratio 0.75 \
  --system-idle-gap-cap-seconds 10 --trace-idle-gap-cap-seconds 300 \
  --warmup-requests-per-lane 10 --warmup-grace-period 1800
```

GSM8K: 20 questions, greedy, max 8192 new tokens, concurrency 10, run against the same server with the launches on and off. The harness used its own prompt file; the equivalent with the in-tree script (5-shot prompt, so absolute scores differ, the paired comparison is what matters):

```bash
python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --port 8000 --num-questions 20 --max-new-tokens 8192 --parallel 10 --temperature 0
```

Kernel microbenchmark (one GPU, no server; needs only `sglang.kernels`):

<details>
<summary>bench_spec_kv_indices.py</summary>

```python
"""Microbenchmark: serial vs token-block grids for the EAGLE KV-index kernels.

Times generate_draft_decode_kv_indices (draft decode) and
create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton (verify twin) on one GPU for a few
(running requests x KV tokens per request) points, CUDA-event medians over
`iters` launches with an L2 flush before each, and checks byte-equality of the
outputs between the two grids.  Standalone: only needs sglang's kernel ops.

    python bench_spec_kv_indices.py --table 262144 --steps 3 --iters 200
"""
import argparse, statistics
import torch
from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.utils import (
    create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton,
    kv_indices_num_token_blocks,
)
from sglang.kernels.ops.speculative.cache_locs import generate_draft_decode_kv_indices
from sglang.srt.utils import next_power_of_2

def timed(fn, iters, flush):
    ts = []
    for _ in range(iters):
        flush.zero_()
        s, e = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        s.record(); fn(); e.record(); torch.cuda.synchronize()
        ts.append(s.elapsed_time(e) * 1000)
    return statistics.median(ts)

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--table", type=int, default=262_144)
    ap.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=3)
    ap.add_argument("--topk", type=int, default=1)
    ap.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=200)
    ap.add_argument("--points", default="2x87609,4x169336,4x146494,4x512")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    dev = torch.device("cuda")
    flush = torch.empty(256 << 20, dtype=torch.uint8, device=dev)
    print(f"{'R x KV/req':>12} | {'draft serial':>12} {'draft blocks':>12} {'nb':>3} | "
          f"{'verify serial':>13} {'verify blocks':>13} {'nb':>3} | equal")
    for pt in a.points.split(","):
        R, L = map(int, pt.split("x"))
        bs = R * a.topk
        r2t = torch.randint(0, 6_000_000, (R + 1, a.table), dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
        req_pool = torch.arange(R, dtype=torch.int64, device=dev)
        seq_lens = torch.full((R,), L, dtype=torch.int64, device=dev)
        positions = torch.repeat_interleave(seq_lens, a.topk)
        width = a.topk * (L + a.steps) + 64
        kv_i = torch.zeros((a.steps, bs * width), dtype=torch.int64, device=dev)
        kv_p = torch.zeros((a.steps, bs + 1), dtype=torch.int64, device=dev)
        def draft(nb):
            generate_draft_decode_kv_indices[(a.steps * nb, R, a.topk)](
                req_pool, r2t, seq_lens, kv_i, kv_p, positions, a.table,
                kv_i.shape[1], kv_p.shape[1], next_power_of_2(R),
                next_power_of_2(a.steps), next_power_of_2(bs), 1, 0, 0,
                NUM_STEPS=a.steps if nb > 1 else 0)
        # verify twin: one program per request over the live prefix
        kv_indptr = torch.zeros(R + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
        kv_indptr[1:] = torch.cumsum(seq_lens, 0)
        out = torch.zeros(int(kv_indptr[-1]), dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
        def verify(nb):
            create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton[(R, nb)](
                r2t, req_pool, seq_lens, kv_indptr, None, out, a.table,
                TOKEN_BLOCK_PARALLEL=nb > 1)
        # mean-live-length sizing, as in the PR
        nb_d = kv_indices_num_token_blocks(L, a.steps * R * a.topk)
        nb_v = kv_indices_num_token_blocks(L, R)
        draft(1); ref_i, ref_p = kv_i.clone(), kv_p.clone(); draft(nb_d)
        verify(1); ref_o = out.clone(); verify(nb_v)
        eq = torch.equal(ref_i, kv_i) and torch.equal(ref_p, kv_p) and torch.equal(ref_o, out)
        d1, dn = timed(lambda: draft(1), a.iters, flush), timed(lambda: draft(nb_d), a.iters, flush)
        v1, vn = timed(lambda: verify(1), a.iters, flush), timed(lambda: verify(nb_v), a.iters, flush)
        print(f"{R:>5} x {L:<6}| {d1:>9.1f} us {dn:>9.1f} us {nb_d:>3} | {v1:>10.1f} us {vn:>10.1f} us {nb_v:>3} | {eq}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

Output on an H100 NVL with this branch (`--table 262144 --steps 3 --iters 200`; the fourth row is the short-prefix case the live-length sizing exists for):

```
  R x KV/req | draft serial draft blocks  nb | verify serial verify blocks  nb | equal
    2 x 87609 |     284.0 us      14.8 us  11 |       97.2 us       13.5 us  11 | True
    4 x 169336|     540.5 us      18.4 us  21 |      181.8 us       14.5 us  21 | True
    4 x 146494|     467.0 us      17.7 us  18 |      158.0 us       14.5 us  18 | True
    4 x 512   |       6.4 us       6.4 us   1 |        4.7 us        4.7 us   1 | True
```

## Accuracy Tests

Paired probe on the same server (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, EAGLE, TP8 on 8x H200) with the token-block launches on vs off:

- GSM8K, 20 questions, greedy, max 8192 tokens: 18/20 vs 18/20, all 20 transcripts character-identical, identical completion lengths.
- 32 greedy long-context continuations x 256 tokens at concurrency 10: 0 repetition loops, 0 flags on the patched side.
- Kernel level: 15 of 15 shapes byte-identical to the serial kernel for both ops.

The change only copies int32 indices, so no numerical difference is possible. The kernel tests above were run on an H100 with this branch: `test_draft_decode_window.py` and `test_spec_kv_indices_grid.py`, 9 tests, all pass, including the new token-block window-oracle test and the windowed grid-equivalence cases.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel level on H200 (CUDA-event medians over 200 iterations, L2 flushed, eager and CUDA-graph replay), serial grid vs token-block grid (the script in "How to reproduce" reproduces this on an H100):

| kernel | running requests x KV tokens/request | serial | token-block | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `generate_draft_decode_kv_indices` | 2 x 88k | 252 us | 11 us | 22.5x |
| | 4 x 169k | 490 us | 15 us | 32.1x |
| | 4 x 146k | 425 us | 14 us | 31.1x |
| `create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton` | 2 x 88k | 78 us | 8 us | 9.3x |
| | 4 x 169k | 147 us | 12 us | 12.6x |
| | 4 x 146k | 128 us | 11 us | 11.9x |

End to end: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, SGLang v0.5.19, TP8 on 8x H200, EAGLE (steps 3, topk 1), 256k context, agentic-coding trace replayed at concurrency 10, one hour per arm, 0 request errors on both. The replay sets the request rate, so throughput is flat by design and latency is the signal.

| | stock | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| ITL p50 | 6.55 ms | 6.05 ms (-7.6 %) |
| ITL avg | 8.56 ms | 7.44 ms (-13 %) |
| ITL p90 | 10.06 ms | 9.22 ms (-8.3 %) |
| request latency p50 | 3.24 s | 3.03 s (-6.5 %) |
| output tok/s | 472 | 470 (trace-paced; flat by design) |
| normalized interactivity p50 | 113.6 tok/s per user | 121.6 (+7.1 %) |
| normalized interactivity p90 | 64.0 | 68.8 (+7.6 %) |
| EAGLE accept length | 3.279 | 3.281 |

Normalized interactivity is output tokens per second per user: each request's end-to-end latency divided by its output tokens, then the reciprocal of the p50 / p90 of that ratio across requests. p90 is therefore the slow-tail user and sits below p50.

nsys attribution: the two index kernels fall from 0.92 to 0.03 ms per decode step and the step shortens by about 0.5 ms, matching the ITL p50 move. The host gap after the draft launch is unchanged, so the saving was not absorbed by the host.

Notes: the measurements were taken on the v0.5.19 container with the #37659 kernels backported and these three launch-site changes applied as a source patch with an A/B kill switch; this PR is the clean enablement on `main`, where the kernels already exist. One deliberate difference: mean-length block sizing at all sites (21 blocks instead of 33 at the measured point), same kernel, not re-measured.

title: [kernel] SwiGLU-OAI MXFP8 producer; move swizzled MXFP8 producers to ops/quantization
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

Models with a clamped SwiGLU-OAI MLP (e.g. MiniMax-M3's dense and shared experts) that feed an MXFP8 down projection currently run the activation and `flashinfer.mxfp8_quantize` as two separate kernels. The existing diffusion `_silu_mul_mxfp8_kernel` already writes FlashInfer's 128x4 swizzled E8M0 scales, so this PR adds a SwiGLU-OAI branch to it.

## Modifications

- `_silu_mul_mxfp8_kernel` takes `ALPHA` / `LIMIT` as constexpr. `ALPHA=None` keeps the SiLU path unchanged. Otherwise it computes `clamp(gate, max=limit) * sigmoid(alpha * gate) * (clamp(up, ±limit) + 1)` in the op order Inductor emits for `swiglu_no_interleaved_with_alpha_and_limit`, rounding to bf16 once.
- New `swiglu_oai_mxfp8(hidden, alpha, limit)`, registered as `quantization.swiglu_oai_mxfp8`.
- Move `mxfp8_swizzled_triton.py` from `kernels/ops/diffusion/quantization/` to `kernels/ops/quantization/`, since the quantizer and SwiGLU producers are not diffusion-specific. The diffusion facade still re-exports `mxfp8_quantize_swizzled`, `silu_mul_mxfp8`, `indexed_scale_shift_mxfp8_` and the `can_use_*` predicates by their full module path, so diffusion callers don't change. The test moves to `test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/`.
- The kernel now writes the scale padding itself (padded rows and columns get 0), so the `torch.zeros` memset on the scale buffer goes away. Batches of up to 1024 rows use 4-row tiles.

## Accuracy

Payload and swizzled scales, padding included, are byte-identical to the unfused `swiglu_no_interleaved_with_alpha_and_limit` + `flashinfer.mxfp8_quantize` chain: 0 of 63.4M bytes differ over 1–5800 rows and input scales from 1e-2 to 100.

## Tests

`test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_mxfp8_swizzled.py` adds:
- SwiGLU-OAI vs the eager chain, with rows {1, 7, 128, 333}, n {768, 1056} and scale {1e-3, 1, 30}. The input is a strided view, and the allocator is dirtied first so a missing padding write would show up.
- A CUDA graph replay test.

On B300 (SM103) with this branch: 30 passed in `test_mxfp8_swizzled.py`, plus `multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_mxfp8_online_gemm.py` (33 passed, 1 skipped across both files). All four registry specs pointing at the moved module resolve.

## Benchmark

Width 768, CUDA graphs: 1.3–1.5 µs for 1–256 rows (unfused: 2.2–3.1 µs) and 6.3 µs at 5800 rows (unfused: 8.9 µs).

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] custom-all-reduce: Add 2shot_push all-reduce and retune SM100 TP4/TP8
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

`CustomAllReduceV2` has no good option between about 0.5 MB and 8 MB at TP4 and TP8 on Blackwell: `1shot_push` moves `W` copies of the tensor per rank and runs out of steam, while `2shot_pull` pays two barriers and remote loads. A push-plane two-shot (Lamport markers, no barriers) beats both across that band. This PR adds it as `2shot_push` and retunes the SM100 world 4 / 8 rows from a B300 sweep.

The kernel follows the design in #35192 by @lyppg (rotated per-peer scatter and gather, owner reads its own partial from the input, split reduce and gather loops). The difference is the plane layout: this PR keeps both halves of a chunk in one existing push slot, so the push plane, its workspace and the `PushPlane` constructor are unchanged, and no multicast variant is added. @lyppg is a co-author on the kernel commit.

## Modifications

**Kernel** (`custom_all_reduce.cuh`): `all_reduce_2shot_push_kernel`, next to `all_reduce_1shot_push_kernel`.
- The flat tensor is split into `W` chunks of `ceil(num_vecs / W)` 16 B vectors; rank `c` owns chunk `c`.
- Reduce-scatter: each rank pushes chunk `c` only to its owner. The owner polls its own slots, reduces in rank order, keeps the sum, and pushes it to every other rank. All-gather: each rank drains the peers' sums into its output.
- Same bytes on the wire as `2shot_pull`, but every remote operation is a posted store and every wait is a local poll: no barriers, no remote loads, no staging copies.
- A slot `(dst, src)` holds `[partial of chunk dst | reduced chunk src]`, two `chunk_vecs` halves. The `(r, r)` slot is unused.
- Scatter and gather give each warp one peer, starting at `r + 1`, so every peer's ingress is busy from the first wave and the slot pointer is warp-uniform. The host raises the block size when a small grid has fewer warps than peers.
- Reduction order is rank order on every rank, so all ranks hold identical bits, and `2shot_push` matches `1shot_push` bit for bit.

**Push-plane sizing** (`configs/custom_all_reduce_v2.py`, `custom_all_reduce_v2.py`):
- A 2shot slot needs `2N / W` bytes instead of `N`. `Heuristic.max_push_bytes(world_size)` sizes the slot for both push algorithms; `clip()` caps the 2shot threshold at what the slot fits (`two_shot_push_slot_bytes` and its inverse `two_shot_push_max_bytes`).
- Symmetric memory per rank with the new rows: TP4 24 MB to 32 MB, TP8 12 MB to 32 MB.

**Picker**:
- New `AllReduceAlgo.TWO_SHOT_PUSH`; it is a push algorithm (`is_push()`), needs no graph pointer table, and behaves the same in eager mode and under CUDA-graph capture.
- `Heuristic.two_shot_push_threshold` defaults to 0, so untuned (arch, world size) rows are unchanged. Table rows set it by keyword (`two_shot_push=`).
- Order of preference is now `1shot_push -> 2shot_push -> 1shot_pull -> 2shot_pull mc -> 2shot_pull`.

**SM100 table** (graph and eager use the same thresholds):

| World size | `1shot_push` up to | `2shot_push` up to |
|---|---|---|
| TP4 | 640 KB (was 2.25 MB graph / 3 MB eager) | 8 MB |
| TP8 | 256 KB (was 0.5 MB graph / 0.75 MB eager) | 8 MB |

Multicast `2shot_pull` still takes over above 8 MB at TP8 where it was configured. The rows were swept on B300; B200 and GB200 inherit them as SM100 (see follow-ups).

**Tests** (`test_custom_all_reduce.py`): `TWO_SHOT_PUSH` joins the algorithm matrix, with an odd size (3 MiB + 24 elements, uneven chunks).

Exact equality against NCCL; fp16, bf16, fp32; eager and CUDA graph; 11 sizes from 16 elements to 4 Mi elements, including sizes that leave chunks empty.

title: [sglang-miles] Support P2P replica loading and target/draft weight updates
author: yueming-yuan
body:
Provide the engine-side support for the Miles P2P stack (radixark/miles#3939 through radixark/miles#3985). Land together with the stack: radixark/miles#3969 replaces `ParameterMapper`, and radixark/miles#3985 adds draft updates.

- **Replica construction:** add `initialize_model_without_storage`, preserving parameter subclasses, attributes and ties while returning built shapes. Buffers remain on meta.
- **Reload layout and storage:** restore TRT-LLM BF16 MoE weights to canonical shapes in place before updates; assert published parameter addresses and byte counts survive restore and postprocess.
- **Runner registration:** key weight tables and parallelism configs by `(role, tp_rank)`, defaulting to target. Publish drafts after memory-pool setup binds shared embeddings/heads, avoiding stale addresses.
- **Mapping removal:** remove `ParameterMapper` and its model hooks; Miles now discovers dependencies by probing `load_weights`.
- **Remote-instance loading:** `RemoteInstanceModelLoader` asks the seed for the table of the role it loads, so a draft loads from the seed's draft weights instead of finding none in the target's.

The model-specific derived-state fixes (`GemmaRMSNorm.gemma_weight`, the GLM-lite NextN post-load) moved to sgl-project/sglang#43251 with the other model- and format-specific fixes, so this PR keeps the general engine support.

## Recorded validation

- H200 CPU unit runs passed model construction, MoE restore, published storage, runner roles and remote-instance role checks. Relevant pre-fix revisions fail the corresponding regression checks.
- GPU equivalence: two updates of a two-layer GLM-5.2 model match sglang's own update, including parameters, buffers and attributes, with published storage unchanged. The initial five-format run used Miles #3950 and the earlier mapper; loader-probe results and MTP e2e results are tracked in radixark/miles#3985.
- Removing mapper hooks preserved all 4,816 tensor checksums across GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-4.5-Air-FP8 with drafts, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Qwen3-30B-A3B, GLM-4-9B-0414, Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen2.5-0.5B and TinyLlama-1.1B. DeepSeek V3 NextN and the modelopt KV-scale remap were not exercised in that comparison.
- Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and GLM-4.7-Flash P2P MTP e2e passed with these changes and sgl-project/sglang#43251's, with equality checked on target and draft.
- Merged `sglang-miles` (MXFP4 online updates). Its MXFP4 TRT-LLM postprocess and restore permute weights in place, refill reload padding in place, and copy the shuffled scales into existing parameters, so published storage stays put; this is read from the code, since the MXFP4 hot-reload test needs SM100. On the merged tree its changed unit tests (17, five files) pass on H200, and the remote-instance role test fails on the merge commit.

title: [Fix] moe_sum_reduce: gate the bf16 vectorized path on hidden % 16
author: Monishver11
body:
## Motivation

`moe_sum_reduce` has a vectorized bf16 path for `token_num > 256` that sums 16-element chunks per lane (`VEC = 16` in `moe_sum_reduce_warp_per_token_vec_kernel`), but the launcher gates it on `hidden_dim % 8 == 0` and sizes the grid from `hidden_dim / 8`. A bf16 input whose hidden dim is 8 mod 16 (e.g. 104, 120, 1032) therefore takes the vectorized path and its last 8 columns are never written, so the output keeps whatever the buffer held. At `hidden_dim = 8` no column is written at all. No shipped model config has such a hidden dim, so this is latent, but the kernel is reachable from the Triton fused-MoE runner for any `topk != 2` and it silently returns garbage for those shapes.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/moe/moe_sum_reduce.cu`: the gate and the chunk count now derive from one shared `BF16_VEC` constant that the kernel also uses, so the three literals cannot drift again. Rows that are 8 mod 16 fall through to the scalar warp-per-token path, which writes every column. Also drops a redeclared `stream` inside the fast path that shadowed the one three lines above. 13 lines.
- `python/sglang/kernels/aot/tests/test_moe_sum_reduce.py`: regression test, three cases at 257 tokens: hidden 8 and 104 (the broken shapes) and 2048 (still on the vectorized path, guards the gate change). The output buffer is pre-filled with NaN so an unwritten column cannot pass.

## Accuracy Tests

RTX 4090, torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0. The patched `.cu` was built standalone with `torch.utils.cpp_extension` against the installed `sglang-kernel==0.4.7` wheel's headers and compared with the wheel's kernel.

| bf16, 257 tokens, topk 8 | wheel (main) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| hidden 8 | 8 NaN columns | matches fp32 reference |
| hidden 104 | 8 NaN columns | matches fp32 reference |
| hidden 2048 | correct | correct |

On the shapes the wheel handles correctly the output is bit-identical to the wheel (`torch.equal`) across fp16/bf16/fp32, tokens {1, 32, 257, 1024}, topk {2, 8, 9, 17}, hidden {16, 100, 2048, 7168}: 0 mismatches over 192 combinations.

The new test fails 2 of 3 cases on the current wheel and passes with the fix.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance change. Shapes with `hidden_dim % 16 == 0` take exactly the same path and launch as before; the only shapes that move are the broken ones, which now go to the scalar path instead of producing unwritten columns.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [GLM-5.3-Flash] Enable breakable prefill CUDA graph by default
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

Enable breakable prefill CUDA graph by default for GLM-5.3-Flash.

- Exempt `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` from the KDA rule that disables BCG; other KDA models are unchanged.
- Rename `apply_glm5_prefill_cuda_graph_policy` to `apply_glm5_next_prefill_cuda_graph_policy`, since it applies only to GLM-5.3-Flash.

## Verification

GB300, without `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill`:

```
sglang serve --model-path zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tp-size 4 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend trtllm --dsa-decode-backend trtllm \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Enable Helion across KDA prefill, decode, and EAGLE/MTP verification for models such as GLM-5.3-Flash. The existing prefill adapter omits the raw-beta flag, bounded-gate decode bypasses the Helion packed kernel, and Helion target verification is missing.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Forward `beta_is_raw` in the Helion prefill adapter.
- Enable Helion packed decode for bounded-gate KDA.
- Add Helion chain/tree verification with per-candidate state snapshots and register the verify backend.
- Add numerical and dispatcher regression tests, including CUDA Graph coverage.

Existing backend defaults are unchanged. MTP verification uses state snapshots; ReplaySSM verification is outside this PR's scope.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

Validated GLM-5.3-Flash on 4 × H200 with Helion 1.4.0, using Helion for all three KDA phases and EAGLE with 5 steps, top-k 1, and 6 draft tokens.

GSM8K: 100 examples, 5-shot, 8 threads, two runs, max tokens 4096, temperature 0, `reasoning_effort=low`.

title: [Perf] Serialize OpenAI chat/completion responses in one pass
author: HJSang
body:
This is the `main` counterpart of #42834 on `sglang-miles`, which becomes its cherry-pick once this merges. The diff is identical; the measurements below were taken with it on `sglang-miles` (`f19dcfb12`).

## Motivation

RL rollouts that request `top_logprobs` through `/v1/chat/completions` (non-streaming, `return_meta_info=True`) spend most of the extra latency after the engine has finished. On an H200 box, a 160-token response took about 7 ms from `response_sent_to_client_ts` to the client at `top_logprobs=0`, and about 380 ms at `top_logprobs=128`. Decode throughput was unchanged.

The chat, completion and SageMaker `/invocations` endpoints return the pydantic response model to FastAPI. With no `response_model` or `response_class`, FastAPI then runs `jsonable_encoder`: `model_dump(mode="json")`, then a pure-Python walk over the whole dumped payload, then stdlib `json.dumps`. With top-k the payload holds `completion_tokens * k` candidates twice: `choices[].logprobs` and `meta_info.output_top_logprobs`. That makes the Python walk the dominant cost, and it runs on the HTTP/TokenizerManager event loop.

## Modifications

- `utils/json_response.py`: add `model_json_response`. It renders a pydantic result with `model_dump_json(by_alias=True)` in one pass and passes any other result (for example an error `ORJSONResponse` or a `StreamingResponse`) through unchanged.
- `http_server.py`: use it for `/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` and `/invocations`.
- `OpenAIServingChat` and `OpenAIServingCompletion` still return models, so the Anthropic adapter, token scoring and the gRPC bridge are unaffected.
- **Why not `response_model=`:** FastAPI ≥ 0.141 also serializes a declared `response_model` with pydantic's `dump_json`. SGLang doesn't pin FastAPI, and these routes return unions of models and `Response` objects, so the helper gives one pass on any FastAPI version.
- **Scope:** only the three routes that return chat/completion responses change; they carry the large top-k payloads. `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/classify`, `/tokenize`, `/detokenize`, `/v1/score`, `/v1/decisions`, `/v1/rerank` and `/v1/systemone` still go through `jsonable_encoder`. Moving every route (e.g. in `ORJSONRoute`) changes serialization for their downstream consumers and needs its own testing, so it's left for a follow-up.

**Behavior:**
- **Same values.** The JSON values match FastAPI's output, aliases included. FastAPI's encoder is `model_dump(mode="json", by_alias=True)` plus a no-op walk. Float spelling can differ (for example `1e-05` vs `0.00001`), but the parsed values are equal.
- **Non-finite floats are unchanged.** `-inf`/`NaN` logprobs serialize as `null` on both paths: the chat and completion response models' wrap `model_serializer`s already map them on FastAPI's path, and `model_dump_json` does the same.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output change. On the H200 host, I posted the real `http_server.app` `/v1/chat/completions` route with a stubbed serving object. The response was built by `_build_token_logprobs_from_raw` with the Qwen3.5-9B tokenizer and carried `meta_info` top-k. I compared the bodies from `f19dcfb12` and from this branch:

| completion tokens × top_logprobs | values equal | bytes equal |
|---|---|---|
| 160 × 0 | yes | yes |
| 160 × 32 | yes | yes |
| 160 × 128 | yes | yes |
| 1000 × 32 | yes | yes |
| 1000 × 128 | yes | no (float spelling only) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same setup, real endpoint, median of 7, CPU only:

| completion tokens × top_logprobs | body | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 160 × 0 | 25 KB | 3.2 ms | 0.9 ms |
| 160 × 32 | 0.68 MB | 79.8 ms | 13.2 ms |
| 160 × 128 | 2.6 MB | 310.4 ms | 52.8 ms |
| 1000 × 32 | 4.2 MB | 830.1 ms | 85.0 ms |
| 1000 × 128 | 16.4 MB | 2554.0 ms | 391.6 ms |

At 160 × 128, this accounts for most of the ~380 ms measured end to end. The remaining top-k cost is outside this PR and could be follow-ups:
- `_build_token_logprobs_from_raw`: about 77 ms locally for 160 × 128, from per-candidate `token_id_to_bytes` and pydantic construction.
- Per-position single-token `batch_decode` in `TokenizerManager.detokenize_top_logprobs_tokens`.

## End-to-end on H200

The `sglang-miles` version of this change (#42834) ran in the patched stack of the end-to-end check in #42838 (Qwen3.5-9B on H200 behind the miles session server and gateway): k=0 and k=128 requests, 32-way concurrency and three short training runs, with no serialization errors. With greedy decoding, the patched engine's nested response gives the same tokens and top-k candidates as `f19dcfb12`'s. Most of the latency gain there comes from #42838, which shrinks the payload this PR serializes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1, codespell 2.4.1, registered-test lints)
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). `test/registered/unit/utils/test_json_response.py` covers parity with FastAPI encoding on a top-k `ChatCompletionResponse`, the response model's wrap serializer, aliases, non-finite logprobs and pass-through. On `main` (`c0df52be2`), `test_json_response.py`, `test_flat_raw_top_logprobs.py`, `test_serving_chat.py` and `test_serving_completions.py` give 213 passed vs 208 on `main`; `test/registered/unit/managers`, `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai` and `test/registered/unit/utils` give the same failure set as `main` on a CPU-only host (60 failed and 2 errors from the missing GPU), with 4 more passing (run on `012cd3858`, before the rebase and the review follow-up).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Fix] Merge DeepSeek-V4 two-batch-overlap microbatches without a residual
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42936
* #42898
* #42897
* #42896
* #42895
* #42894
* #42893
* #42892
* __->__ #42891

## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 runs its own two-batch-overlap layer loop (`DeepseekV4Model._forward_layers_tbo`), and its layers carry no residual between them, so each microbatch's output has `residual=None`. Since #42307, the shared `_model_forward_tbo_merge_outputs` reads both outputs' residual as a `ResidualStream`, so DeepSeek-V4 prefill with `--enable-two-batch-overlap` fails at the first merge:

```
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'pending'
```

The AMD nightly `test_deepseek_v4_flash_fp8_tbo.py` fails with this error; there is no NVIDIA test for DeepSeek-V4 two-batch overlap.

## Modifications

- Move the token-range concatenation into `_model_forward_tbo_merge_key(output_a, output_b, name, original_len)`. DeepSeek-V4 merges its hidden states with it directly; the stream-carrying merge keeps its single caller, `model_forward_stages`. The old path only completed an owed sum on DeepSeek-V4's output, and `hc_post` returns a plain tensor, so dropping it changes no value.
- Add the NVIDIA counterpart of the AMD nightly: `test_deepseek_v4_flash_fp4_b200_tbo.py` (registry `nightly-4-gpu-b200`) launches DeepSeek-V4-Flash with TP 4, attention DP 4, DeepEP and `--enable-two-batch-overlap`, gated on GSM8K ≥ 0.93.

## Accuracy Tests

- The 13 two-batch-overlap and DeepSeek-V4 unit test files give the same results on `main` and with this change.
- 4× B200, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, launched as the new nightly test does:
  - `main` (`6cc661f223`, and again at `a34cba3c62`): the first two-batch-overlap prefill raises the `AttributeError`.
  - This change on `6cc661f223`: the nightly test passes with GSM8K 0.970. Each of the 4 DP ranks enters and merges the overlapped layer loop 8 times, on prefills of up to 3,907 tokens.

* __->__ #42893
* #42892
* #42891

## Motivation

`inference-optimization/Kimi-K3-0.40B`, a small Kimi K3 checkpoint, fails on `main` at two places that the full-size model never reaches:

1. `KimiK3DeltaAttention` takes its value head size from `config.v_head_dim`, which is the MLA layers' value head size. The KDA layers use `linear_attn_config["head_dim"]` for keys and values alike, as the reference modeling code and the KDA state cache do. When the two sizes differ (32 vs 64 here), the value projection and the decode output do not match the state cache, and the first packed decode fails:
   ```
   ValueError: `out` must have shape (512, 1, 4, 32) (got out.shape=(512, 1, 4, 64)).
   ```
2. `situ_and_mul` passes a row-strided 2D input straight to the kernel, which reads each row in vectors of up to 32 bytes and rejects a stride that is not a whole number of them. Kimi K3's fused MoE front hands it the shared experts' `gate_up` as a slice of `[gate_up | router logits | latent]`. With few experts, that slice's stride is not a vector multiple.

## Modifications

- Size the KDA values by `linear_attn_config["head_dim"]`.
- `situ_and_mul` takes the dense copy for a row stride that is not a whole number of the kernel's 32-byte vectors of the wider dtype, as it already does for any other input the kernel cannot read in place.

## Accuracy Tests

- With the full-size Kimi K3 dimensions, neither path changes: the KDA head size equals the MLA value head size (128), and with 896 experts the slice's stride is aligned.
- Kimi-K3-0.40B now gets past both failures. On B200, serving it end to end still needs an MLA backend that accepts its `kv_lora_rank=128` and `qk_rope_head_dim=32`; `trtllm_mla` rejects those, and the triton backend does not compile them.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the copy is taken only for misaligned strides, which the full-size model does not produce.

title: [Fix] Run attention on a padded extend batch's real rows
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42936
* #42898
* #42897
* __->__ #42896
* #42895
* #42894
* #42893
* #42892
* #42891

## Motivation

MLP sync pads each rank's extend batch to a multiple of attention TP (`input_ids`, `positions`, `out_cache_loc`), while the attention metadata still covers only the real tokens. The prefill CUDA graph path already runs attention on the real rows. In eager mode, though, the backends got the padded queries:

- flashinfer's paged and ragged prefill and flashinfer MLA's ragged path reject them. Qwen3-30B-A3B with DeepEP at TP 2 fails as soon as prefill runs eager, as it does by default under pipeline parallelism:
  ```
  q.shape[0] (6) does not match qo_indptr[-1] (5)
  ```
- The other backends compute only the rows their metadata covers and leave the rest of the output uninitialized.

## Modifications

- `RadixAttention` does in eager what the prefill graph path does:
  - it runs the backend on the real rows, with the cache locations and positions narrowed for the call;
  - it allocates the padded output up front, with the graph branch's allocation (`_new_attention_output`, now shared). A backend that writes into `forward_batch._attn_output` (flashattention, triton, aiter, trtllm_mha's NVFP4 output) fills the real rows in place; another backend's output is copied in. Only the padded tail is zeroed. A backend that returns more than its output (its LSE, or a sparse indexer's output beside it) returns a tuple, which is padded as it comes, so no output is allocated for that call.
- K and V go with the queries unless the caller gives them an extent of their own, the layer is a cross-attention (K and V are the encoder's), or they have a different row count. K and V that hold a cached prefix declare their extent: the chunked-prefix chunks did, and DeepSeek's one-shot MHA, whose K and V cover every token of the sequences, now does too, so they are never taken for padded rows when their row count happens to equal the padded query count.
- The other per-row inputs are narrowed with the rows they belong to:
  - `rel_bias`, `aux_tensors`, the q/k/v descales and the mxfp8 deferred norm/RoPE inputs, from the list the graph path's extra-kwargs route already narrows (`_PER_ROW_EXTRA_KWARGS`, now shared);
  - `k_rope` and the k/v descales follow K and V; a sparse indexer's `idx_q` follows the queries and its `idx_k` / `idx_v` the keys, as the prefill graph's sparse attention already narrows them (MiniMax's backend trimmed them itself only while it received the padded queries).
- The FA4 wrappers (`flash_attn_varlen_func` and `flash_attn_with_kvcache` in `flash_attention_v4.py`) pass `out=` on to the kernel. They dropped it, so FA4 allocated a second output that was then copied in; the output the prefill graph path preallocates now reaches FA4 too. Where the wrapper pads MLA query heads, or the kernel is a released flash-attn-4 build without `out=`, the result is still a new tensor.
- trtllm_mha's FMHA-v2 prefill (SM90 and SM120) also writes into the output it is given, as its other prefill kernel already did, so the padded call and the prefill graph path no longer copy a second output in.
- DeepSeek's born-FP8 query for DSA's `flashmla_sparse_q8` prefill (`SGLANG_ENABLE_DSA_Q8KV8_BORN_FP8_Q`) is prepared for every row but handed to the backend for the rows its attention call takes: the stash records the real rows of a padded extend (`padded_extend_real_tokens`, the same test the narrowing uses), which the backend reads as a prefix of the rows written.
- Target verify, which plans its padded rows itself, is left as it is.
- The real count comes from `global_num_token_non_padded_cpu`, which every batch carries.
- Kimi K3 trimmed its own attention to the real rows for the same reason, counting them from `extend_seq_lens_cpu`, which GPU-only batches leave unset. That trim is removed, together with:
  - the padded o_proj output it kept for the SP collectives;
  - the trimmed `out_cache_loc` it left on the batch.
- `test_radix_attention_padded_extend.py` covers:
  - only padded extend batches are narrowed;
  - the backend sees the real rows and the tail is zero;
  - keys with their own extent or row count, or a cross-attention's, are left whole, also when they are as long as the padded queries (a cached prefix, or encoder rows);
  - the per-row inputs follow the rows they belong to, a sparse indexer's too (each index output shaped by the query rows);
  - the output is written in place or copied, with `_attn_output` restored afterwards.

## Accuracy Tests

- Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepEP, TP 2, deterministic inference (flashinfer), eager prefill, on B200: crashes on `main`, both with and without PP 2; runs with this change.
- `trtllm_mha` in eager prefill, which ran on the padded batch before: identical before and after.
- The output buffer handling and the per-row narrowing change no value. Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepEP, TP 2, deterministic inference, eager prefill, 24 prompts of uneven length (every process takes the padded path 51–351 times): with the backend's own output copied in (flashinfer) or written in place (triton and fa4 on B200, fa3 on H200), input and output logprobs are bit-identical to narrowing Q, K and V alone.
- FA4 output reuse, counted at the FA4 kernel call (Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepEP, TP 2, deterministic inference, B200), two launches per tree:
  - eager prefill: all 381 padded attention calls per process now hand the preallocated output to FA4 and get it back (none before). A padded attention call's peak memory drops from 609 KiB to 309 KiB, one real-row output (75 rows × 2048 × 2 bytes);
  - prefill CUDA graph: the 6,465 FA4 calls that have a preallocated output now write into it (none before);
  - input and output logprobs are bit-identical to before in both modes.
  - the same on an HGX B300 (SM103): the same counts and peak memory, and bit-identical logprobs in both modes.
- DeepSeek one-shot MHA over a cached prefix on a padded extend (a 4-layer DeepSeek-V3 config with dummy weights, DeepEP TP 4, flashinfer, eager prefill, `SGLANG_CHUNKED_PREFIX_CACHE_THRESHOLD=1`, B300): a 3-token cached prefix and 9 new tokens padded to 12, so K and V have as many rows as the padded queries. Without the declared extent, K and V were cut to 9 rows on every MLA layer and the greedy tokens changed; with it, the output is bit-identical to the same request without the prefix cache, in two launches.
- MiniMax-M3's sparse attention (its released config cut to 6 layers, index values on in two of the five sparse layers, dummy weights), TP 4 × DP 2 attention, eager prefill, on B300. Narrowing q, K and V without the indexer's inputs fails in `store_kv_index`, whose `idx_k` keeps the padded rows. With them narrowed, every padded call hands the backend the real rows for q, `idx_q` and `idx_v`, and the index output comes back on those rows. Sending the 24 prompts one at a time, so that each launch runs the same batches (9 of the 24 prefills padded), the greedy tokens match `main` on all 24 prompts. The logprobs differ from `main`'s by at most 0.0073; `main` differs from its own second launch by 0.0068.
- trtllm_mha's FMHA-v2 on H200 (Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepEP TP 2, eager prefill, requests one at a time): all 192 padded attention calls per process now hand FMHA-v2 the preallocated output and get it back (none before), saving one real-row output per call; input and output logprobs are bit-identical to before.
- DSA's born-FP8 query (`SGLANG_ENABLE_DSA_Q8KV8_BORN_FP8_Q=1`, `flashmla_sparse_q8` prefill, FP8 KV cache) on H200: a DeepSeek-V3.2 config cut to 4 layers with bf16 dummy weights, TP 4 × DP 2 attention, eager prefill, 12 long prompts sent one at a time. On the padded prefill, every layer's stash records the real rows the attention call reads; stashing every written row instead fails the backend's check (`q8kv8 born-fp8 q stash mismatch: stashed (num_tokens=2082, layer_id=0) but consuming (num_tokens=2081, layer_id=0)`). Input and output logprobs are bit-identical to `main`, to the same run with the born-FP8 query off, and across two launches.
- Inkling-Small-NVFP4 with FA4's sheared relative bias, TP 4 × DP 2 attention, eager prefill on B200: narrowing Q, K and V alone fails FA4's `assert rel_bias.shape == (total_q, num_head, rel_extent)` on all four ranks; with the per-row inputs narrowed too it serves. (Inkling's output under DP attention is wrong on `main` as well, GSM8K 0.03, so that configuration has no accuracy to compare; at TP 4 this PR and `main` both score 0.74 with identical answers on the first questions.)
- Kimi K3 (synthetic, DeepEP TP 2, eager prefill, 5-token prompt padded to 6 rows), its own trim against this narrowing, per layer and per rank:
  - with the attention-residual bank: real and padded rows identical;
  - standard residual path: identical, except one launch of the trimmed tree that also differs from the trimmed tree's own second launch.
- H200 (fa3, deterministic inference), Qwen3-30B-A3B GSM8K at the top of this stack, against `main`: TP 4, TP 4 × DP 2 attention, TP 2 × PP 2, TP 4 × EP 4 DeepEP, and TP 4 × DP 4 attention × EP 4 DeepEP all give the same accuracy (0.915–0.930) and 200/200 identical answers.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: unpadded batches are unchanged; a padded eager batch now runs the backend on its real rows only, and FA4 writes into the output buffer it is given instead of allocating another.

Memory, on B300 (Qwen3-30B-A3B's config with dummy weights, DeepEP TP 2, eager prefill, deterministic inference):
- A padded attention call's own peak, 127 real of 128 rows × 2048: triton, which writes in place, 528,384 bytes, the padded output; flashinfer, whose output is copied in, 1,044,480 bytes, the padded output plus its real-row output, released at the end of the call. FA4 writes in place too (above).
- The whole run's peak allocated and reserved memory per rank is identical to `main`'s to the byte with triton and with FA4.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
