title: [Refactor] Run Kimi K3's fused collectives through stage boundaries
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42936
* __->__ #42898
* #42897
* #42896
* #42895
* #42894
* #42893
* #42892
* #42891

## Motivation

Three Kimi K3 configurations still ran the decoder's own communication, because each fuses a collective with work that stage boundaries had no way to hand to a model-supplied kernel:

- **Fused all-reduce.** With the attention-residual bank, attention TP equal to TP, and a multicast-capable node, K3 writes o_proj's output into a multicast buffer. It then completes the all-reduce together with the pending residual add in one kernel (`k3_ar_fusion.all_reduce`).
- **Tuned SP collectives.** On a node with K3's SP collectives (multicast, a tuning table for the device, DeepEP or MegaMoE), the bank completes the attention output's sum onto each rank's attention-TP shard in a tuned reduce-scatter that also adds the residual. Each MoE layer's output goes back to every row through a tuned all-gather.
- **Shard mode (`SGLANG_K3_SP_ATTN_RES`).** The residual stream and the bank stay on each rank's attention-TP shard across consecutive SP-MoE layers. Each read happens on the shard and is then gathered.

## Modifications

**Stage boundaries**
- A stage's read may supply kernels of its own (`completing_fusions`, `ReadoutFusion`) that complete the sum its input owes together with the residual add:
  - the all-reduce entry tries them first, for a plain residual add, and reads the stream such a kernel wrote;
  - a kernel that declines the batch leaves the sum to the boundary's own collective;
  - `ReadoutFusion.scatters` marks one that completes the sum onto this rank's slice, which the reduce-scatter entry tries;
  - `ReadoutFusion.reads` marks one that also performs the read and returns its result.
- A stage may declare its own implementation of the gather over attention TP its boundaries run (`attn_tp_gather`, on `declare_ffn` and `declare_attn`). It is tried before the default per batch, and declaring one that no batch variant runs is an error. Neither kind of kernel is registered globally: the tuned kernels' own eligibility checks would also take other models with the same hidden size.
- `ExitRows.SLICE`: an FFN that declares it leaves its output on the rows it ran on, at the stack's end too, so the model's final read takes the slice. An unpadded batch, whose rows stay whole, keeps them whole.
- A read may supply `gathering_reads`, kernels that read the slice and gather what they read in one call; the entry then skips its own gather. They take a pending residual add themselves, so the entry binds them only after a plain add or when the producer writes the stream at its exit (`EdgeContract.arrives_written`).
- `ops.attn_tp_gather(..., owned=True)` gathers into a buffer of its own, for an output that outlives the layer stack.

**Kimi K3**
- The bank's FFN read supplies the fused all-reduce for an o_proj output in the multicast buffer, the condition under which the decoder used it. When o_proj cannot write into that buffer (a quantized o_proj), the attention leaves the sum to the boundary's all-reduce.
- The bank's FFN read on the shard supplies the tuned reduce-scatter, and the bank's MoE layers declare the tuned all-gather.
- Shard mode is decided at construction, since it changes which rows each stage leaves its output on. It requires all of these:
  - an a2a MoE backend with attention TP;
  - the bank;
  - K3's tuned SP collective;
  - `SGLANG_K3_SP_ATTN_RES`;
  - a single pipeline rank;
  - no EAGLE3, DFLASH or DSPARK draft capturing the target's hidden states;
  - every layer from the first MoE layer on is an SP-MoE layer.

  A model built in this mode raises when asked to capture hidden states.
- In shard mode:
  - the SP-MoE layers declare `ExitRows.SLICE`;
  - the bank's FFN read reduce-scatters, adds the residual and aggregates in one kernel;
  - the attention read and the final read aggregate and all-gather in one kernel;
  - the final read falls back to the tuned or the boundary's all-gather (`owned`).
- `AttnResidual` raises on a read of every row after a write of only this rank's rows, which would aggregate stale snapshots of the other ranks' rows.
- Two move-only commits: the stage declarations move into `_declare_stages`, and the SP-MoE o_proj setup moves into the attention classes. Neither changes behavior.
- With this PR every Kimi K3 configuration builds stage boundaries, so the decoder's own communication code becomes unreachable; #42936 removes it.

**Tests**
- `test_append_stages.py`:
  - `TestSliceExitRows`: the last FFN stays on its slice; an unpadded batch leaves it on the attention rows; the next attention gathers in the declared gather; a gathering read needs a plain add or a written stream.
  - `TestReadKernels`: a gathering read passes through the entry gather; a kernel that reads returns the read.
- `test_attn_bank_residual_ops.py`:
  - `TestAttnBankFusedAllReduce`: the stream the fused kernel writes reads as the entry's own all-reduce and add would leave it.
  - The exit gather falls back when its kernel declines; the shard entry reads the tuned reduce-scatter's stream as its own.
  - `TestAttnBankOnShards`: the final read of a shard gathers what it read; a read of every row after a shard write is refused.
- `test_kimi_k3_stage_kernels.py`, driving the layer's stage declarations with both collectives stubbed available:
  - The standard residual path keeps the boundary collectives; the bank takes the fused all-reduce and the tuned reduce-scatter and gather.
  - Consecutive MoE layers stay on their shards.
  - The shard mode is decided at construction.

## Accuracy Tests

B200, synthetic Kimi K3 (`moonshotai/Kimi-K3` config at full width, 8 layers, 64 experts, dummy weights), deterministic inference.
- **Fused all-reduce**, where it does not run (custom all-reduce off under deterministic inference): bank TP 4 is equivalent to the decoder's own path, with decode 1606 = 1606 and extend 431 = 431 kernels.
- **Tuned SP collectives**, where unavailable (no tuning table for B200): bank SP-MoE at DeepEP TP 2 is bit-identical to the decoder's own path, with decode 1462 = 1462 and extend 465 = 465 kernels.
- **Shard mode with its criterion forced on** (the three fused kernels then fall back to NCCL), TP 4 + DeepEP, with block sizes 2 and 4: every pair of runs from the two trees whose layer 0 matches is bit-identical on all 8 layers and in its outputs. All 80 terminal reads per run took the shard.
- At the top of this stack against `main`, per layer: TP 4 with and without the bank, the bank with SP-MoE at TP 4 × EP 4, and PP 2 are equivalent.

- **Fused all-reduce with the real kernel.** Deterministic inference turns the custom all-reduce's multicast off, so these launches are not deterministic: TP 4 with the bank, custom all-reduce on, 4 launches per tree. Every rank logs `K3 all-reduce fusion enabled` on both trees, and both call the fused all-reduce on the attention sum 1264 times per rank per run. All 10 pairs of a `main` and a stack launch whose layer-0 outputs match are bit-identical on every layer and in their outputs. The spread between the trees (2–3 of 3 prompts identical, logprobs within 0.023) is the same as within each tree.

**Tuned SP collectives, shard mode and the fused all-reduce with the real kernels**, at the top of this stack against `main`, on an HGX B300 (SM103, NVLink multicast). The SP collectives' tuning tables name the GB300 (TP 4 / 8 / 16) and GB200 (TP 16); for this run the GB300 tables were copied under the B300's device name (`NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC`) in both trees. Synthetic K3 as above, with the bank; custom all-reduce on, which these kernels need, so launches are not deterministic; 4 launches per tree per configuration.
- Every rank of both trees logs `K3 SP collective enabled`, plus `K3 SP attention-residual carry enabled` in shard mode and `K3 all-reduce fusion enabled` at TP 8 without SP-MoE. Counted at the kernels, the tuned ones take every call: the reduce-scatter with the residual add and the all-gather (SP-MoE); the bank's fused reduce-scatter-and-read and aggregate-and-gather, and the attention-residual reduce-scatter and gather (shard mode); the fused attention all-reduce (208 per rank per run). In shard mode every final read takes the shard.
- Grouping each configuration's 8 launches by bit identity over every layer of every rank and the outputs, the largest group always holds launches of both trees. A launch outside it differs as much from its own tree's other launches as from the other tree's.

  | Configuration | Largest group (`main` + stack) | Other groups |
  |---|---|---|
  | SP-MoE, DeepEP TP 4 × EP 4 | 3 + 3 | 1 + 1 |
  | SP-MoE, DeepEP TP 8 × EP 8 | 4 + 3 | 0 + 1 |
  | Shard mode, TP 4 × EP 4 | 4 + 2 | 0 + 2, already apart at layer 0 |
  | Shard mode, TP 8 × EP 8 | 3 + 3 | 1 + 0, 0 + 1 |
  | Fused all-reduce, bank TP 8 | 3 + 3 | 1 + 0, 0 + 1 |

- Output spread between the trees equals the spread within each tree in every configuration (2–3 of 3 prompts identical, logprobs within 0.008).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B200 with custom all-reduce on, where K3's fused all-reduce is enabled on both trees (`K3 all-reduce fusion enabled`). `offline_throughput`, generated-shared-prefix 16 × 16, synthetic K3, bank, TP 4: 10742 output tok/s on `main`, 10708 at the top of this stack (median of 6 launches each; ranges overlap).

HGX B300, the same benchmark at TP 8 (DeepEP EP 8 for SP-MoE), with the GB300 tables as above. Every run logs the tuned collectives (or the fused all-reduce) enabled on all 8 ranks of both trees. Output tok/s, median (range):
- SP-MoE: `main` 5631 (4066–5853), this stack 5643 (5395–5720), 6 launches each.
- Shard mode: `main` 5548 (5273–5996), this stack 5463 (5194–5829), 9 launches each; the ranges overlap and a rank-sum test does not separate them.
- Bank, fused all-reduce: `main` 12474 (12442–12755), this stack 12882 (12691–12936), 3 launches each.
- Memory after init is the same in every pair (`max_total_num_tokens` and free memory).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Perf] deepseek-v4.1: Skip wasted layer 20 work on earlier prompt tokens under decoder bounded replay
author: vincentzed
body:
## Motivation

- DeepSeek-V4.1 has an option called decoder bounded replay (`--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay`). When it is on, the last layers of the model only process the last 128 prompt tokens of each request during prefill.
- Today this starts at layer 21. Layer 20 still processes every prompt token.
- Layer 20 does two things. It writes the compressed KV cache that decoding reads later, and that needs every token. It also runs its own indexer, attention and MoE to produce its output, and layer 21 only reads the last 128 tokens of that output.
- So the indexer, attention and MoE work of layer 20 on all the earlier tokens is thrown away. The indexer of layer 20 scans the whole context, so this wasted work grows with the prompt length.

## Modifications

- When decoder bounded replay is on, layer 20 now writes its compressed KV cache for every token first, and then runs the rest of the layer on the last 128 tokens only.
- The compressed KV cache that layer 20 writes is the same as before.
- Layer 20 now writes its indexer results directly for the last 128 tokens. The code that copied those rows out of the full-size buffers is no longer needed, so this PR removes it.
- No flag is added. Nothing changes when decoder bounded replay is off.
- ROCm keeps the old behavior, because its fused layer path runs all of layer 20 in one call.
- This also works with the prefill CUDA graph that #43736 added for decoder bounded replay. Inside the graph, the step that prepares the layer 20 inputs now computes only the part the caller asked for. Before, it always computed the indexer inputs too, and the new full-prompt KV write does not have them.

One behavior change to review:

- For the last 128 tokens, layer 20 now uses the same shortened sliding window as layers 21 to 39. Before this PR, layer 20 saw the full window.
- This matches how the DeepSeek-V4.1 report describes decoder replay: "feed their encoder outputs through the decoder layers under the same SWA truncation".

## Accuracy Tests

- Hardware and model: 4x B300, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, TP4 and EP4.
- "main" is commit `2f6e0ec45d`. The two files this PR changes are the same on current main.

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tp 4 --ep-size 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 --max-running-requests 16 --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay
# The DSpark row adds: --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5
python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 1319 --parallel 32
```

| GSM8K, 1319 questions | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No speculative decoding | 0.907 | 0.907 |
| DSpark, block size 5 | 0.902 | 0.914 |

- Each number is one run. Two runs of the same setup can differ by about 0.007.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- Same launch command as above, without speculative decoding.
- The numbers are time to first token. Requests are sent one at a time, as token ids.
- Each number is the median of 3 to 5 requests. The two numbers in a cell come from two separate server starts.

| Request | main | this PR | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| New prompt, 16K tokens | 139.6 / 139.5 ms | 132.8 / 131.6 ms | 5% faster |
| New prompt, 64K tokens | 577.5 / 564.9 ms | 526.6 / 524.5 ms | 8% faster |
| New prompt, 200K tokens | 2009.6 / 2015.4 ms | 1800.5 / 1811.9 ms | 10% faster |
| New prompt, 500 to 8K tokens | 81.7 to 85.7 ms | 82.5 to 84.4 ms | No change |
| 2K new tokens after 16K cached tokens | 85.8 / 87.2 ms | 84.4 / 85.5 ms | No change |
| 2K new tokens after 64K cached tokens | 93.5 / 89.4 ms | 93.2 / 91.4 ms | No change |
| 2K new tokens after 200K cached tokens | 112.4 / 113.9 ms | 115.2 / 113.3 ms | No change |
| 128 new tokens after 200K cached tokens | 109.3 / 107.8 ms | 114.2 / 113.0 ms | 5 ms slower |

Time spent in layer 20 for one 16K-token prefill chunk, measured with a GPU sync around each layer:

| Prefill chunk | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Early in the prompt | 11.9 ms | 3.3 ms |
| Late in a 200K-token prompt | 27.0 ms | 5.2 ms |

- Short requests do not get faster. Prefill without a CUDA graph costs about 80 ms per batch no matter how short the prompt is, and this PR does not change that.
- The last row of the first table is the only one that got slower. In a third pair of server starts it was 109.2 ms on main and 107.3 ms with this PR, so I think it is noise between server starts.

## Rerun after merging main at `684fea8af3`

- Main now runs decoder bounded replay inside the breakable prefill CUDA graph (#43736), so I tested both with and without the graph.
- Same hardware and model as above. The graph rows add `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable --mem-fraction-static 0.7`. Current main ran out of GPU memory with the graph at 0.8, so both sides use 0.7 there.
- Each number is one run from one server start.

| GSM8K, 1319 questions | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No prefill graph | 0.906 | 0.911 |
| Prefill graph | 0.898 | 0.908 |
| Prefill graph and DSpark, block size 5 | not run | 0.911 |

| Time to first token, new prompt | main | this PR | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 14,795 tokens, no prefill graph | 152.5 ms | 143.2 ms | 6% faster |
| 14,795 tokens, prefill graph | 172.6 ms | 159.5 ms | 8% faster |
| 6,318 tokens, prefill graph | 97.8 ms | 90.7 ms | 7% faster |
| 590 tokens, prefill graph | 32.5 ms | 32.4 ms | No change |

- No scheduler exceptions in any run.
- Unit tests under `test/registered/unit/layers/test_dsv4*.py`: 70 passed.

## Rerun after merging main at `abf92826ee`

- Main now also allows the TRT-LLM attention backend with decoder bounded replay under the prefill graph (#44326), so this run includes TRT-LLM rows (`--dsv4-attn-backend trtllm`).
- Main also moved the DeepSeek-V4 layer code into separate stage files (#43607). This PR's new layer method and its changes to the model loop carried over without changes.
- Every row uses `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable --mem-fraction-static 0.7`. Each number is one run from one server start.

| GSM8K, 1319 questions | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FlashMLA | 0.908 | 0.904 |
| FlashMLA and DSpark, block size 5 | not run | 0.905 |
| TRT-LLM | 0.897 | 0.897 |

| Time to first token, new prompt | main | this PR | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 14,795 tokens, FlashMLA | 165.9 ms | 155.8 ms | 6% faster |
| 14,795 tokens, TRT-LLM | 161.2 ms | 149.1 ms | 8% faster |

| 6,318 tokens, TRT-LLM | 89.9 ms | 86.3 ms | 4% faster |
| 590 tokens, FlashMLA | 31.6 ms | 32.9 ms | No change |

- Two runs of the same setup can differ by about 0.007 on GSM8K.
- No scheduler exceptions in any run.
- Unit tests under `test/registered/unit/layers/test_dsv4*.py`: 71 passed.

## Not tested

- Prefill context parallelism together with decoder bounded replay.
- ROCm. Its behavior is unchanged.

## Follow-up

- `CandidateMetadata.tail` and its implementations are now only called by their own tests. A later PR can remove them.

title: [AMD] Fuse prefill index-Q RoPE fake-quant and fp4 quantize kernels in DSV4.1
author: RolaoDenthu
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
On gfx950, the V4.1 low-ratio indexer has a fused index-Q kernel (RoPE + fp4 quantize + FlyDSL pack) only for ≤ 64 tokens. Prefill and large decode-verify batches fall back to two kernels that write the query to memory as bf16 and read it back. For a 16k-token prefill chunk this takes ~1.4 ms per indexer layer (~2% of prefill time at 68k input).

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

- Add `index_q_rope_pack_flydsl`: a dedicated Triton kernel (one program per token and 16 heads) that does the RoPE, the fake-quant and the FlyDSL fp4 pack in one launch for any number of tokens. Its output is bitwise identical to the two standalone kernels it replaces.
- Use it in `_indexer_inputs` for > 64 tokens. The ≤ 64-token decode path is unchanged.
- Tests: bitwise match against the standalone kernels (up to 16k tokens, 16/32/64 heads, inf/nan inputs), non-contiguous positions, and inputs around both quantization floors.

title: [FA4] Keep stream last in the SM100 MLA kernel so disk-cached objects load
author: nvpohanh
body:
[by Claude Code]

Fixes #42925

## Motivation

Since #42239 merged, `test/registered/cuda_graph/full_prefill/test_full_cuda_graph_prefill.py` fails on the B200 PR Test Base job (`base-b-test-4-gpu-b200 (0)`) with:

```text
TypeError: Expects 18 parameters when calling: `__call__(mQ, mQv, mK, mV, mO, mLSE, softmax_scale, mP, mRowMax, mCuSeqlensQ, mCuSeqlensK, mSeqUsedQ, mSeqUsedK, mIndexTopk, mPageTable, window_size_left, window_size_right, mValue)`
```

#42239 added `mValue` to `FlashAttentionMLAForwardSm100.__call__` as a keyword-only parameter after `stream`. The MLA (`qv`) path in `interface.py` calls the kernel with 17 positional arguments. A freshly compiled kernel accepts that, but the persistent CuTe JIT cache exports the kernel to disk. When a later process reloads it, the loaded TVM-FFI function requires every parameter before the implicit stream, so the call fails. The first process on a runner passes (which is why #42239's own CI passed), and later ones fail. See #42925 for the failing jobs.

## Modifications

- `flash_fwd_mla_sm100.py`: move `mValue` before `stream` so that `stream` stays the last parameter.
- `flash_attn/cute/interface.py`: pass `None` for `mValue` explicitly at the `qv` compile and call sites. Only `FlashAttentionMLAForwardSm100` uses this branch (`qv` is asserted Blackwell-only).

`forward_gqa` (#42239's GQA-512 path) passes `mValue` and `stream` by keyword, so it is unaffected.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested on a B200 (CuTe DSL 4.8.0, tvm-ffi 0.1.11, the same versions as CI). Each check runs as two processes against one fresh `SGLANG_CUTE_AOT_CACHE_DIR`, so process 2 loads the object that process 1 exported.

| Check | main `2889158792` (process 1 / process 2) | this PR (process 1 / process 2) |
|---|---|---|
| FA4 MLA prefill: `flash_attn_with_kvcache(q=q_rope, qv=q_nope, ...)`, 16 heads, rope 64 + latent 512, page size 1, causal | OK / `TypeError: Expects 18 parameters` | OK / OK, max abs err 0.0094 vs a torch reference in both processes |
| `flash_attn_gqa_512`, 16 q heads / 2 kv heads, d=512, causal and non-causal | OK / OK | OK / OK, max abs err 0.0040 / 0.0098 vs a torch reference |

title: [Perf] Cache compiled ModelOpt exclusion patterns
author: Chillee
body:
## Motivation

Large ModelOpt exclusion lists can exceed `regex`'s 500-entry cache. `is_layer_excluded()` scans these patterns for each layer, repeatedly compiling the same expressions during model construction.

## Modifications

Cache up to 8,192 compiled exclusion patterns with `functools.lru_cache` and the public `regex.compile()` API. Keep the existing wildcard conversion, prefix variants, component matching, and fused-name checks. The cache is keyed by pattern text, so changing or remapping the exclusion list uses the updated names. No private regex globals are modified.

## Accuracy Tests

- 1,372 CPU comparisons against the original matcher passed, covering large exclusion lists, matches/misses, wildcards, literal dots, `language_model.` prefix variants, and fused components.
- Checked that changing the exclusion list uses the new patterns and that the cache remains bounded at 8,192 entries.
- Repository pre-commit checks passed for the changed file.

These checks execute the actual matching methods extracted from the source, without importing GPU dependencies. Full GPU inference and startup benchmarks have not been run against upstream.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

CPU microbenchmark: 1,200 synthetic exclusion patterns, 90 unmatched layer checks per trial, Python 3.13.13, `regex==2026.7.10`, aarch64 CPU.

| Matcher | Time for 90 checks |
| --- | ---: |
| Before, three trials | 8.306 / 8.280 / 8.330s |
| After, initially empty cache | 0.176s |
| After, two subsequent trials | 0.101 / 0.101s |

These are matcher-only timings for full-list scans, not end-to-end sampler startup times.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce from this PR branch (requires only Python and regex)</summary>

```python
import ast
import subprocess
import time
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

import regex as re

path = "python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py"


def load(source):
    nodes = ast.parse("from __future__ import annotations").body
    for node in ast.parse(source).body:
        if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name == "_compile_exclusion_pattern":
            nodes.append(node)
        if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef) and node.name == "ModelOptQuantConfig":
            nodes.extend(
                n for n in node.body
                if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == "is_layer_excluded"
            )
    namespace = {"re": re, "lru_cache": lru_cache}
    exec(compile(ast.Module(body=nodes, type_ignores=[]), path, "exec"), namespace)
    return namespace["is_layer_excluded"]


sources = {
    "before": subprocess.check_output(["git", "show", f"HEAD^:{path}"], text=True),
    "after": Path(path).read_text(),
}
config = SimpleNamespace(
    exclude_modules=[f"model.layers.{i}.mlp.gate_proj" for i in range(1200)]
)
prefixes = [f"model.layers.{i}.mlp.down_proj" for i in range(90)]
for name, source in sources.items():
    match = load(source)
    re.purge()
    for trial in range(3):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        results = [match(config, prefix) for prefix in prefixes]
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
        assert not any(results)
        print(name, trial, elapsed)
```

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Format and lint the changed file with the repository's pre-commit configuration.
- [x] Verify matching semantics and provide a reproducible CPU benchmark.
- [ ] GPU inference / end-to-end startup benchmark (not run).

-Robot

title: [Perf] dsv4: Vectorize paged KV cache dequantization
author: yuan-luo
body:
## Summary

The V4 paged KV-cache dequant kernel processes one token per program, issuing small loads when gathering a long compressed history. This PR processes four tokens per program while preserving the per-element dequantization arithmetic and BF16 RoPE copy.

Compressed-cache reuse across a `kv_source` group is already provided by upstream. This PR is limited to the V4-layout dequant kernel and its correctness test.

Related issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/42170

## Implementation

- Vectorize the V4-layout kernel to four tokens per program: a `[4, 8, 64]` FP8 load, a `[4, 8]` scale load, and a `[4, 64]` BF16 RoPE load. Mask the padded scale tile and incomplete token groups.
- Preserve the existing output row stride and 64-bit cache-offset arithmetic.
- Add a registered zero-tolerance dequant test against the Torch reference, covering token tails, both page sizes, an int64 page table, and a shared-workspace output slice.

![V4 dequant kernel: one to four tokens per program](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ac92803-f3b2-4807-8c3b-f751e2a6af06)

## Performance

Previously recorded kernel measurements on an idle B200, page size 256, V4 layout:

| Gathered rows | One token/program | Four tokens/program |
|---|---|---|
| 262K | 0.381 ms | 0.089 ms |
| 524K | 0.754 ms | 0.171 ms |
| 16K | 0.019 ms | 0.020 ms |

These are measurements from before the rebase, not a fresh benchmark of the current head. The long-gather kernel speedup is approximately 4.3–4.4×; the 16K case remains launch-bound. End-to-end TTFT has not been remeasured against the rebased base, which already includes dequant reuse. The vectorization applies to `KVLayout.V4`; V4.1 layouts continue to dispatch to their existing dequant kernels.

## Validation

- The retained kernel test compares against the Torch reference with `atol=0`, `rtol=0`, and `equal_nan=True`.
- The original B200 run recorded three test methods passing in 4.5 s. GPU tests have not been rerun after the rebase and scope reduction.
- Local validation: Python syntax, kernel/reference import symbols, and `git diff --check`. This host has no PyTorch/Triton installation.

```bash
python3 test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsv4_dequant_k_cache.py
```

## Checklist

- [ ] Run GPU tests and benchmark on the current head.
- [x] Add a registered dequant correctness test.

title: [Fix] unified-memory: enabling trtllm_mha with decode graphs and speculative decoding
author: caihuali95
body:
## Motivation

Under `--enable-unified-memory`, trtllm_mha could not run with decode CUDA graphs (the gate refused them, because each replay's page-table refill took the previous replay's lengths), and it was not in `TRANSLATED_MHA_RAILS`, the MHA backends allowed to read a speculative draft's KV through the unified pool's index translation, so no speculative algorithm could use it as a target or a draft. #42753's per-iteration `KVLocPlan` closes the read side: the graph refill copies the plan's table, built from this batch's `seq_lens` plus the window it writes, and the graphs-off path reads the same table. This PR fixes the remaining trtllm_mha defects on the unified pool, two of which also affect the static pool, and adds trtllm_mha to `TRANSLATED_MHA_RAILS`. Seven commits on main: 11 files, +840/-61.

## Modifications

1. **Lift the decode-graph refusal** (`arg_groups/kv_cache_hook.py`). With #42753 the refill covers every page a replay reads: plain decode, and the draft decode, target verify and draft extend replays of speculative decoding.
2. **Zero MHA pages when they are handed out** (`allocator/unified_sub_pool.py`, `unified_memory_pool.py`, `kernels/ops/kvcache/zero_pages.py`). trtllm_mha's fmha_v2 prefill (SM90/SM120) loads K and V a whole page at a time and masks the positions past a request's length only in the scores, so their V rows still enter P·V with a zero probability, and 0 × NaN is NaN; XQA decode does the same with an fp8 KV cache (its bf16 kernel zero-fills those rows). MLA pools already zero on hand-out (#33974); MHA pools did not, and under a mamba hybrid those bytes can hold fp32 recurrent state that reads as bf16 Inf/NaN (Qwen3.5-9B GSM8K 0.49 against 0.90 at `--mem-fraction-static 0.30`).
3. **Require packed page tables on the graphs-off path** (`layers/attention/trtllm_mha_backend.py`). XQA decode and fmha_v2 prefill are handed only a page table's data pointer and take its row length from its width; they ignore its strides. The plan's table is a column view of a wider tensor only when a captured graph had it built in its own buffer earlier in the same iteration and the batch is narrower than that buffer, which no known configuration produces; such a table would be misread silently. The backend now asserts that both of its tables (full and sliding-window) are packed. These tables stay as wide as the batch needs, while the captured and static ones are `max_num_pages` wide, and XQA sizes its multi-block split from the width: graphs-off decode can round differently, the same attention but not bit-identical.
4. **Keep the reserved page 0 out of the debug poison fill** (`unified_memory_pool.py`). `SGLANG_DEBUG_POISON_POOL` also filled page 0, which the pool reserves as the target of a sliding window's freed slots and which XQA reads at zero weight, so a poisoned window-model run reported NaN that serving never sees.
5. **Keep fmha_v2 prefill out of XQA's workspace semaphores** (`trtllm_mha_backend.py`; static pool too). On SM90/SM120 both kernels share one workspace, and fmha_v2's tile counter sat on XQA's first multi-block semaphore. After any prefill, the next small-batch XQA launch dropped a tile of its output: Qwen3.5 with NextN or DFLASH on trtllm_mha hit NaN in the first draft step and scored 0.19-0.55 on GSM8K, against 0.89 on triton. XQA's 8 MiB of semaphores now come on top of the configured workspace, and fmha_v2 gets the part past them, so fmha_v2 and XQA's scratch each keep the whole configured size.
6. **Copy only the batch's pages for the fmha_v2 prefill** (`trtllm_mha_backend.py`; static pool too). fmha_v2 takes K and V as one `[pages, 2, page_size, heads, head_dim]` tensor, and the backend stacked the layer's whole pool for every prefill layer: 0.4-2.6 ms per layer, about 6x that on the unified pool's strided views. It now copies each row's own pages, back to back, straight into one buffer, so a prefill's extra memory is the copy itself; a batch that reads no fewer pages than the pool holds keeps the whole-pool stack.
7. **Add trtllm_mha to `TRANSLATED_MHA_RAILS`** (`kv_cache_hook.py`, `mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py`). trtllm_mha reads every path a draft forward takes through the plan, so it joins that list, which gates the EAGLE/EAGLE3 target of an MHA model, every EAGLE/EAGLE3 draft, the DFLASH target, and the decision whether a draft's KV is fused into the target's pages. DSPARK's target set is unchanged. The comment and docstring that named trtllm_mha as a draft that declines fusion go.

Tests (each fails without its change):

- `test_trtllm_mha_graph_metadata.py`: decode, draft-decode, target-verify, draft-extend and ragged-verify replays, through the real `KVLocPlan` and a page map rewritten before every replay, read only the current replay's pages (a refill bounded by `cache_seqlens_int32`, or a table without the read extent, fails them); a graphs-off table that is a strided view of a wider buffer fails the packed-table assert; fmha_v2's workspace stays off the semaphores and keeps the configured size, at the default and at an explicit `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_SIZE`; its prefill copies only each row's own pages, and the copy's peak memory stays within the copy's own size, from a packed and a strided pool alike.
- `test_unified_handout_zeroing.py`: MHA pools, Mamba pools and pools that combine Mamba state with sliding-window layers zero pages on hand-out; the poison fill spares page 0.
- `test_unified_prefill_cuda_graph_gate.py`, `test_unified_memory_spec_gate.py`, `test_fused_draft_placement.py`: decode capture boots; trtllm_mha is admitted for EAGLE/EAGLE3 (target and draft) and DFLASH and stays refused for DSPARK's target; a trtllm_mha draft fuses.

## Accuracy Tests

SM90, TP1, radix cache, trtllm_mha on both arms (page size 64). Baseline: the static pool. Unified: `--enable-unified-memory` with lazy compaction (the default), plus eager compaction (`SGLANG_DISABLE_LAZY_COMPACTION=1`) where a table lists it. GSM8K, all 1314 test questions, 5-shot, greedy. Every unified arm ran on a poisoned pool (`SGLANG_DEBUG_POISON_POOL=1`, every never-written byte a bf16 NaN), so a read of a slot nobody wrote collapses the score instead of hiding. Everything below ran on this PR's current commits, based on main 7224fce1b5 with FlashInfer 0.7.1.

No speculation (`--mem-fraction-static 0.8`):

| model | CUDA graphs | baseline | unified | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B | off | 0.896 | 0.896 | +0.0 |
| Qwen3.5-9B | on | 0.894 | 0.894 | +0.0 |
| gpt-oss-20b | off | 0.534 | 0.529 | -0.5 |
| gpt-oss-20b | on | 0.552 | 0.565 | +1.3 |

Qwen3.5-9B with NextN and DFLASH on trtllm_mha (`--mem-fraction-static 0.3`, overlap scheduler). The draft fuses into the target's pages on every unified arm; the NextN draft runs on trtllm_mha itself.

| draft | CUDA graphs | GSM8K baseline / unified eager / unified lazy | accept length |
|---|---|---|---|
| NextN | off | 0.897 / 0.897 / 0.893 | 3.50 / 3.50 / 3.51 |
| NextN | on | 0.895 / 0.893 / 0.897 | 3.50 / 3.50 / 3.50 |
| DFLASH | off | 0.896 / 0.895 / 0.896 | 6.32 / 6.32 / 6.27 |
| DFLASH | on | 0.897 / 0.896 / 0.896 | 6.26 / 6.31 / 6.29 |

The same NextN and DFLASH configurations on main's static pool score 0.186-0.188 (NextN) and 0.554-0.559 (DFLASH): the workspace collision that commit 5 fixes.

gpt-oss-20b with EAGLE3, page size 64, `--mem-fraction-static 0.3`, overlap scheduler, with per-step pool checks and the allocator invariants on (`SGLANG_ENABLE_STRICT_MEM_CHECK_DURING_BUSY=1 SGLANG_CHECK_KV_PAGE_INVARIANTS=1 SGLANG_INVARIANT_CHECK=1`), the static pool run twice. These ran with the four fixes listed below applied (#43168 is needed for gpt-oss EAGLE3 at a page size above 1 on any backend). No leak, double free, invariant violation or illegal memory access on any arm; accept length 1.27-1.28 on every arm.

| backend | CUDA graphs | baseline / baseline repeat / unified eager / unified lazy |
|---|---|---|
| triton | off | 0.543 / 0.492 / 0.557 / 0.557 |
| trtllm_mha | off | 0.570 / 0.532 / 0.545 / 0.552 |
| triton | on | 0.556 / 0.554 / 0.559 / 0.502 |
| trtllm_mha | on | 0.511 / 0.537 / 0.524 / 0.535 |

gpt-oss-20b's GSM8K score moves by several points between identical runs: the two static-pool runs of the triton graphs-off row differ by 5.1. Paired per question, the triton graphs-on unified lazy arm sits within that spread, and its accept length matches the other arms.

GPU unit tests for unified memory: 4123 passed, 0 failed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`bench_serving` with random prompts at concurrency 64, in two shapes: 2048 input / 512 output tokens (200 prompts) and 8192 input / 64 output tokens (100 prompts). trtllm_mha on both arms, radix cache, overlap scheduler, CUDA graphs on, `--mem-fraction-static 0.55`, one server at a time. The baseline runs twice, and each delta is unified against the mean of the two baseline runs, with the spread between those two runs (A/A) beside it. These ran on this PR's current commits with the four fixes below applied: without #43170 and #43171, main's own unified-pool costs on these two models (host syncs in gpt-oss-20b's sliding-window frees, Triton GDN prefill on Qwen3.5) dominate the gaps.

2048 input / 512 output tokens:

| model | speculation | req/s | mean TTFT | mean ITL | mean TPOT | mean E2E |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B | none | -0.7% (A/A 0.3) | +3.2% (0.4) | +0.3% (0.3) | -0.1% (0.2) | +0.7% (0.3) |
| gpt-oss-20b | none | -0.3% (0.2) | +0.2% (0.0) | +0.3% (0.2) | +0.3% (0.2) | +0.3% (0.2) |
| Qwen3.5-9B | NextN | -0.2% (0.0) | +0.4% (0.0) | -0.1% (0.0) | -0.6% (0.0) | +0.2% (0.0) |
| Qwen3.5-9B | DFLASH | +0.8% (0.0) | -0.8% (0.0) | -1.4% (0.1) | -3.4% (0.0) | -0.9% (0.0) |

8192 input / 64 output tokens:

| model | speculation | req/s | mean TTFT | mean ITL | mean TPOT | mean E2E |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B | none | -0.5% (A/A 0.1) | +1.3% (0.1) | -0.1% (0.2) | -0.2% (0.1) | +0.4% (0.1) |
| gpt-oss-20b | none | -0.2% (0.0) | +1.0% (1.9) | -0.3% (1.3) | +0.2% (0.6) | +0.2% (0.0) |
| Qwen3.5-9B | NextN | -0.4% (0.1) | +0.6% (0.1) | +0.5% (0.1) | +0.7% (0.1) | +0.5% (0.1) |
| Qwen3.5-9B | DFLASH | -0.3% (0.1) | +0.2% (0.1) | +0.2% (0.0) | +0.1% (0.0) | +0.2% (0.1) |

- Qwen3.5-9B's higher TTFT without speculation comes from scheduling: on the unified pool the radix cache keeps more (79.2k vs 23.6k cached tokens over the run), so the arms schedule different prefill batches.
- On prefill batches with identical new and cached token counts in both arms' logs, unified prefill throughput is 0.997-1.000 of the baseline's in every configuration above.
- Accept length is the same on both arms: NextN 3.49, DFLASH 7.09 (median over each run).
- On the static pool alone, this PR is faster than main (same configuration, no speculation, the static pool run twice on each side), because the fmha_v2 prefill no longer copies the whole pool: at 2048 input / 512 output tokens, Qwen3.5-9B +3.6% req/s and -4.0% mean ITL, gpt-oss-20b +11.6% req/s and -11.7% mean ITL; at 8192 input / 64 output tokens, Qwen3.5-9B +1.5% and gpt-oss-20b +5.8% req/s.

## Notes for reviewers

- The gpt-oss-20b EAGLE3 accuracy runs and the unified-pool speed tests ran with four other unified-memory fixes applied on top of this PR: #43168 (page-aligned sliding-window retention for unaligned windows), #43170 (sliding-window frees without a host sync), #43171 (FlashInfer GDN prefill on page-major pools) and #43169 (allocation eviction against the joint full/sliding-window fit). Each is independent of this PR.
- Validated on SM90 only. Through the same list, a draft that a model hook puts on trtllm_mha on SM100 (Kimi-Linear / Kimi-K3 with DSPARK) now fuses into the target's pages, and an MLA target's EAGLE draft may run on trtllm_mha; neither runs on this hardware.

title: [Refactor] Remove Kimi K3's own layer communication and let the consumer set an FFN's exit
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* __->__ #42936
* #42898
* #42897
* #42896
* #42895
* #42894
* #42893
* #42892
* #42891

## Motivation

After #42898 every Kimi K3 configuration builds stage boundaries (`_uses_stage_boundaries()` returns `True`), so the communication the decoder runs itself is unreachable. This PR removes it. `kimi_k3.py` goes from 4286 to 3832 lines; `main` has 4014.

It also moves two decisions from an FFN to the stage that reads its output. Kimi K3's FFN declared the rows its consumer needs and the gather that brings them (`declare_ffn(exit_rows=..., attn_tp_gather=...)`), so the producer described its consumer. Now the consumer's read and declaration carry both.

## Modifications

Removing Kimi K3's own communication:
- Remove the decoder's own forward for the standard residual and the attention-residual bank:
  - its completion of o_proj's sum (`_finish_attn_reduce`);
  - the loop that kept rows sharded across layers.
- Remove the model's own pipeline handoff, bank and final aggregation.
- Remove the MLP's and the MoE's own DP gather around their body, and their `reduce_results` switches, since the boundary completes those sums.
- Remove the pending residual add in the dense MLP and the non-latent MoE. Only the latent MoE, which writes the next stream itself, still takes it.
- Remove the attention classes' `reduce_results` switch; they always leave the attention-TP sum to the boundary.
- Remove `_sp_all_gather_rows`, `_sp_local_rows`, `_dp_local_buffer_group` and `_uses_stage_boundaries`.
- Comments that described the removed communication now describe what the stage boundaries do.
- The bank tests compare the stage path against a reference written out in the test instead of the removed decoder.
- `test_kimi_attention_parallel_groups.py` and `test_kimi_mlp_parallel_groups.py` expect o_proj and the MLP's down_proj to leave their sums to the stage boundary (`reduce_results` off), and no longer build `KimiK3MLP` with a `reduce_results` argument.

An FFN's exit rows and gather come from its consumer:
- A read that needs every row of the attention's declares `reads_after_attn_tp_gather` (an optional `ResidualReadout` attribute). An FFN that would leave its output on this rank's attention-TP slice then returns it to the attention's rows. Kimi K3's bank read declares it unless the bank stays on the slices, and so does Qwen4-exp's PLE read. They replace `exit_rows` on the FFN before them (`_ffn_exit_rows` in Qwen4-exp).
- An exit runs its consumer's `attn_tp_gather`: the next stage's, or the final read's. `declare_ffn` no longer takes `attn_tp_gather`. Across a pipeline boundary the consumer's declaration comes from the neighbouring layer built on the meta device, so a declared gather may use only the communication state of the rank it runs on, not the declaring layer's weights or buffers.
- `make_layers` / `make_pp_layers` / `layer_stack` take the model's final read when it is more than a norm (`final_read=`). Kimi K3's `AttnBankOutputRead` is built before the layers and passed there. A final read with `reads_attn_tp_slices` keeps the last FFN on its slice, replacing Kimi K3's FFN declaring `ExitRows.SLICE`.
- The check that a declared gather runs moves from a single stage to the layer stack, since the gather may now run at the stage's entry or at its producer's exit.
- `declare_ffn(exit_rows=...)` stays as on `main`. Nemotron-H uses it to carry each FFN's sum to its consumer on the attention's rows, which a read's row requirement does not express.
- `layer_boundary.mdx` documents the read attribute, the final read, where a declared gather runs and what it may use across a pipeline boundary.

## Accuracy Tests

Removing the decoder's communication changes no reachable path. B200, synthetic Kimi K3 (`moonshotai/Kimi-K3` config at full width, 8 layers, 64 experts, dummy weights), with deterministic inference unless noted.

**Against the parent (#42898's head):**
- Per layer and in outputs: every pair of runs whose layer-0 outputs match is bit-identical. This covers TP 2 / TP 4 with the bank, SP-MoE (DeepEP) at TP 2 and TP 4 with and without the bank, SP-MoE with DP attention, `--disable-attn-tp-gather`, and the dense attention-TP MLP.
- DSpark draft captures, compared call by call: from the fifth forward on, every run of both trees is bit-identical.
- Kernel counts per rank are identical (TP 4, PP 2, SP-MoE TP 4, `--disable-attn-tp-gather`; with and without the bank). Under DP attention, decode is identical, and in extend only the KDA chunked-prefill kernels' launch counts vary, as they do between launches of one tree.

**At the removal commit against `main`:**
- Per layer: TP 4 with and without the bank, the bank with SP-MoE at TP 4 × EP 4, and PP 2 are equivalent.
- The fused all-reduce with the real kernel is equivalent. This run is not deterministic: custom all-reduce on, TP 4 with the bank, 4 launches each.
- Qwen3-30B-A3B GSM8K on H200 (fa3, deterministic): 200/200 identical answers in TP 4, DP attention, PP 2 and DeepEP configurations.

**At this PR's head against `main`, with K3's tuned SP collectives, shard-mode kernels and fused all-reduce running** (HGX B300, SM103; method in #42898): every configuration's largest group of bit-identical launches holds launches of both trees, at SP-MoE TP 4 / TP 8, shard mode TP 4 / TP 8 and the fused all-reduce at TP 8. This covers the tuned all-gather now reaching the MoE layers' exits through the stage that reads their output.

**Exit rows from the consumer, against the removal commit:**
- Stage plans, compared field by field: 732 constructions on CPU (Kimi K3 with and without the bank, bank kept on the slices, dense attention-TP MLP, PP 2; Qwen4-exp with PLE layers; five Nemotron-H layer patterns; across TP, DP attention, a2a, unpadded batches, two-batch overlap and both boundary reductions). Every plan a model can run is identical. Removing the new read rule changes 128 of them, so the comparison sees it.
- B200, synthetic Kimi K3, deterministic: both trees build and run the bank with SP-MoE at TP 4 × EP 4, TP 4, PP 2 with and without SP-MoE, and the dense-FFN configuration above. With the bank kept on the slices (`SGLANG_K3_SP_ATTN_RES=1`, its multicast requirement bypassed alike in both trees), outputs are bit-identical between the trees and between launches of each. In the other configurations two launches of one tree already differ (up to 0.32 in a logprob), and the trees differ by no more than that.

title: [DSA] Support TileLang FP8 KV cache on CUDA
author: Jzz1943
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Enable TileLang DSA with FP8 KV cache on CUDA, removing the backend restriction and reducing KV memory usage for models such as GLM-5.3-Flash.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Dispatch CUDA FP8 KV to the existing TileLang partial/combine kernels.
- Allocate raw FP8 KV rows without the scaled-cache metadata.
- Disable the incompatible one-shot MHA path and validate backend/layout compatibility.
- Extend existing GPU and configuration tests to cover CUDA FP8 KV and CUDA Graph replay.

Requires TileLang for both DSA prefill and decode; DCP and HiSparse are not supported by this path.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

Validated GLM-5.3-Flash on 4 × H200 with BF16 and FP8 KV, with and without MTP.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 sglang serve \
  --model-path /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --served-model-name llm \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --ep-size 4 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \
  --max-mamba-cache-size 240 \
  --max-running-requests 48 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 8192 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 48 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang \
  --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \
  --moe-a2a-backend none \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --random-seed 42 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000
```

Configuration/GPU tests (13 tests, 4 subtests) and pool-configurator tests (51 tests, 11 subtests) passed.

GSM8K: 1,314 scored questions per run, 5-shot, temperature 0, two runs with Prefill BCG enabled.

| KV dtype | MTP | Run 1 (rounded) | Run 2 (rounded) | Mean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BF16 | Off | 95.8% | 95.9% | 95.852% |
| FP8 E4M3 | Off | 95.7% | 95.7% | 95.738% |
| BF16 | 5/1/6 | 95.4% | 95.6% | 95.472% |
| FP8 E4M3 | 5/1/6 | 95.2% | 95.2% | 95.205% |

Tested both KV dtypes with EAGLE/MTP516 by adding:

```bash
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 5 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6
```

Target and draft KV use the selected dtype. Mean acceptance length was 4.15 for BF16 and 4.16 for FP8; prefill and speculative CUDA Graphs passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

4 × H200, TP4/EP4, TileLang DSA, DeepGEMM MoE, EAGLE 5/1/6 and Prefill BCG. Only `--kv-cache-dtype` changes between cases.

Workload: 32,768 input / 1,024 output tokens, concurrency 8, 64 requests. Values are medians of three warmed-up runs, using mean TTFT/TPOT per run and the final KV token capacity reported at startup.

| KV dtype | KV capacity (tokens) | TTFT (ms) | TPOT (ms) | Output throughput (tok/s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BF16 | 607,232 | 2,664.34 | 12.76 | 518.63 |
| FP8 E4M3 | 1,177,856 | 2,804.25 | 13.35 | 495.48 |

FP8 provides **1.94× KV token capacity**. At this fixed concurrency, TTFT increases by 5.3%, TPOT by 4.6%, and output throughput decreases by 4.5%.

title: [Perf] DeepSeek-V4.1: Support indexer TP shard
author: yuan-luo
body: ## Motivation On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash the ratio-1/2 sparse indexer is fully replicated across the attention-TP group: `wq_b` and `weights_proj` are `ReplicatedLinear`, `n_local_heads == n_heads`, and every attention-TP rank holds the same query rows of a prefill chunk. So under TP4 each of the four ranks runs the identical dense `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` scan over every row against the whole compressed context, then the identical top-k on it, and arrives at the identical selection. Three quarters of that work is redundant. That redundant work is the largest O(context²) term of a long prefill. In a 1 M-token prefill on 4× B200 (TP4 + EP4, DSPARK, the cookbook low-latency recipe) the dense index logits are **6.8 s of kernel time per rank** across 2 746 launches, and the ragged top-k that reads the same score tiles is another **1.9 s**. Both grow with context per chunk, so the share keeps rising with length. ## Modifications Behind `SGLANG_OPT_DSV4_INDEXER_TP_SHARD` (default **off**), each attention-TP rank scores a contiguous share of the chunk's rows and the selections are all-gathered, so every rank still ends up with the full selection. - **`RowShard`** (`v41_indexer/types.py`) partitions the rows into rank-ordered shares of `ceil(rows / world)` rounded up to the score kernel's `128 // heads` row grouping, so every MMA tile holds exactly the rows it holds unsharded. `gather` is one `all_gather_into_tensor` over the attention-TP group; the last share's padding rows fall past the row count and are dropped. - **Full top-k path** (`scoring.py`, `full_topk.py`): `score_tiles` and `dense_prefill_topk` take an optional row range (default: all rows, so the replicated path is unchanged), and `sharded_dense_prefill_topk` scores this rank's share and all-gathers the `[rows, topk]` selection. - **Candidate publish path** (`sparse_table.py`): the row-parallel half of `publish_prefill_table` is split out as `select_prefill_rows`. With a shard, each rank computes its share's own top-k and its top candidate blocks, all-gathers both, and then builds the sparse table over every row: DeepGEMM's schedule is built per row set and cannot be sliced, and the build is cheap next to the scan. - **Gate** (`deepseek_v4_backend.py`): the shard is attached to `PrefillInputs` only on the eager extend path, when attention TP > 1 and the chunk has at least 512 rows. Prefill context parallelism keeps the replicated path, since each CP rank already holds its own interleaved subset of rows. Decode and the captured prefill graph are untouched. **Why this is exact.** A dense score depends only on its own query row, and the aligned shares keep every MMA tile's row set the same, so each rank computes the same bits for its rows as the replicated path would, and the gathered selection is bitwise the replicated one. Every input of the gate is identical on all attention-TP ranks, so either all of them reach the all-gather or none does. The indexer runs on the `stream_sources` side stream, and the all-gather is the only collective issued during that window of `forward_prepare`; the main stream joins it before attention. ## Accuracy GSM8K, 200 examples, `--temperature 0`, both servers built from the same tree in the same session: | | score | score:std | |---|---|---| | flag off | 0.990 | 0.0995 | | flag on | 0.995 | 0.0705 | The one-question difference is run-to-run nondeterminism, not the change: the selection is bitwise the replicated one (see Tests), and two replicated runs of this model already differ, because the consumer layers' bf16 top-k breaks ties at the selection floor by race. ## Benchmarks 4× B200, TP4 + EP4, DSPARK block 5, `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64`, `--context-length 1050624`, bs = 1, random-token prompts, 16 K prefill chunks. Same tree on both servers; only the flag differs. One warm-up, then three seeds per point: | context | flag off TTFT | flag on TTFT | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | 1 M (1 048 000) | 27.73–27.80 s | 20.93–21.00 s | **−6.8 s (−24.5 %)** | | 256 K (262 144) | 4.91–4.92 s | 4.50 s | −0.42 s (−8.5 %) | TP-0 kernel time over the 1 M prefill. The baseline trace was taken on a tree that differs from this one only in the compressed-cache dequant path, so only the indexer kernels below are compared; the consumer-side kernels (`sm100_paged_sparse_mqa_logits`, `topk_bf16_small`) are unchanged to the launch, as expected: | kernel | flag off | flag on | |---|---|---| | dense `sm100_mqa_logits` | 2 746 launches, 6.80 s | 775 launches, 1.73 s | | `topk_ragged` | 3 827 launches, 1.90 s | 1 067 launches, 0.47 s | | `amax8_varlen` (block keys) | 1 087 launches, 0.36 s | 298 launches, 0.09 s | | `AllGather` (new) | — | 320 launches, 0.10 s | Net, the indexer loses 6.66 s of kernel time per rank, which matches the −6.8 s of TTFT: at 1 M the side-stream indexer is on the critical path, so the saving passes straight through. Decode is unaffected. **Stacked with per-ratio candidate publishing.** Same session, one tree that also carries the compressed-cache dequant dedup and per-ratio candidate publishing (#TBD) with both their flags on; only this flag differs: | context | without this PR | with this PR | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | 1 M (1 048 000) | 23.78–23.83 s | 19.19–19.21 s | **−4.6 s (−19.3 %)** | | 256 K (262 144) | 4.70–4.71 s | 4.42–4.43 s | −0.28 s (−6.0 %) | The saving on top of per-ratio publishing is smaller than on main (−4.6 s instead of −6.8 s), because that change already removes two of the dense scans and leaves less to split. Together the three changes take a 1 M prefill from 27.73–27.80 s on main to 19.19–19.21 s (−8.6 s, −31 %). GSM8K on the stacked tree: 0.995 with this flag, 0.990 without. ## Tests Two cases are added to `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsv41_prefill_sparse_indexer.py` (`base-b-kernel-unit`, 4-gpu-b200), which already holds the publish/consume tests these paths share. Both run the sharded code as every rank of an attention-TP group inside one process, through a two-pass all-gather: pass one runs the production code as each rank and records the share it contributes, pass two returns every rank's recorded share in rank order, which is what the NCCL all-gather returns. The unsharded path is the oracle. - `test_row_shards_publish_the_replicated_table`: the own top-k, `blocks`, `phys_blocks` and `valid_lens` match the replicated publish bit for bit on every rank; the schedule is compared by the sparse scores it drives on every valid position. Its buffer holds bytes the build never writes, so two replicated builds of one input already differ in about a third of its bytes and a byte comparison would be meaningless. - `test_row_shards_select_the_replicated_full_topk`: the sharded full top-k equals the replicated one on every rank. Cases cover a padded last share, an even split, an empty share, and shares that cut a request in two. A precondition that the shares tile the rows fails cleanly before any kernel runs; without it, a broken partition hands uninitialized block ids to the schedule build, which crashes and poisons the CUDA context for every later test in the file. Shifting each share by one row turns all seven new subtests red on that precondition and leaves the six existing tests green. On B200 the file runs 8 tests in 1.6 s warm. ## Reproduction ```bash # server (the A/B above: flag on vs off, everything else equal) SGLANG_OPT_DSV4_INDEXER_TP_SHARD=1 SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --trust-remote-code \ --tp 4 --ep-size 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \ --context-length 1050624 --port 31000 # sharded vs replicated selection python3 test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsv41_prefill_sparse_indexer.py # accuracy python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 200 --num-threads 32 --temperature 0 --port 31000 ``` ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code: `pre-commit run --all-files` (not run locally; the changed files pass `ruff format`, `isort` and `codespell` at the pinned versions, and `ruff check` reports nothing new) - [x] Add unit tests: two cases in the existing indexer test file, results in Tests - [x] Update documentation as needed: the new env var is documented at its definition in `environ.py` --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #41379835388](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41379835388) Latest PR Test (Extra): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #41379835394](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41379835394) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :white_check_mark: [Run #41379835379](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41379835379) > [!TIP] > Base CI only covers the core cases, and its workload may not exercise your change. Use `/rerun-test` to run the tests your change touches, or copy this prompt for an agent: > > ```text > Find the registered tests this PR affects and run them with /rerun-test, following https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.agents/skills/rerun-test/SKILL.md > ```

title: [Feat] KVShard: Integrate GLM DSA/MTP with PD and CPU HiCache
author: HZY-Wade
body:
## Motivation

Co-author: @Shunkangz

Connect GLM DSA/MTP serving to page-sharded KV caches so prefill, P/D transfer and CPU HiCache preserve the same ownership for target/draft latent KV and DSA indexer keys/scales.

## Dependencies and review scope

Base: upstream main `5987ec82ed`. Current head: `346068aaa329cf1692fbb6031f60469fdac77dcb`.

DSA attention/indexer support (#44280), MTP pool/scratch support (#40929), and the control-plane/pool/basic-PD prerequisites are already merged.

The remaining unmerged prerequisite is **#43778**, pinned at `6d1e510b2429a36fe499943ff075472d995d8457`. Its three implementation commits are rebased onto this main base with Shunkang's author attribution preserved. The dependency snapshot is `152e93348ad825449c484fbee2068fc614116c67`.

**Review the integration increment:** https://github.com/HZY-Wade/sglang/compare/codex/kvshard-glm-dependencies-20261026-clean...codex/kvshard-dsa-hicache

GitHub's main-based Files changed view also includes #43778. **Rust support is separate in #46445**; this PR contains no Rust implementation and selects Python for sharded launches when the tree backend is unset.

## Modifications

- Select page-sharded DSA target and single-layer GLM NextN draft pools. Validate matching cache geometry and budget latent/indexer scratch for both runners.
- Preserve the shared sender lifecycle. Pair source/destination DSA pages before owner filtering, transfer every owner's target/draft state, retain empty-final-chunk completion, and account for physical transfer bytes.
- Compose a standalone sharded allocation facade with native host pools. Reuse HybridCacheController and L2TransferEngine; resolve owner-local indices through existing preparation hooks before the H2D start event. Preserve logical queue indices and ACK counts.
- Scope scratch bookkeeping to sharding, cache the controller's sharding flag, retain ordinary transfer descriptor builders, and remove the redundant FULL eviction retry.
- Pass `start_owner` to backups only when the tree node has a shard owner. Preserve owner zero and the non-sharded controller's existing call signature.
- Add a four-GPU GLM P2/D2 E2E with CP2, EAGLE MTP and CPU HiCache. Use fabric NVLink with Mooncake's exportable KV allocator, matching the existing P2/D2 test on the same GB300 runner. CPU tests follow the registered `CustomTestCase` convention.

Supported configuration: CUDA PD-prefill, interleave CP > 1, PP1, TRTLLM DSA prefill/decode, FP8 E4M3/page64, Mooncake, and uncompressed index_kpool=1. Optional MTP is single-layer GLM NextN EAGLE with topk=1. CPU HiCache uses cache mode, kernel I/O and layer_first/page_first. L3, external linkers, DSA layer splitting, HiSparse and two-batch overlap are outside this combination. Decode remains unsharded.

[Configuration requirements, paired launch example and validation guidance](https://github.com/HZY-Wade/sglang/blob/codex/kvshard-dsa-hicache/docs/docs/advanced_features/pd_disaggregation.mdx#glm-dsa-kv-sharding-with-cpu-hicache)

## Accuracy Tests

- Runtime regression on `f01f901a6a` (runtime source unchanged by the following documentation/fixture commits): **200 tests and 140 subtests passed**, 2 skipped, 1 deselected. This covers owner-aware PD transfer, allocator/rotation invariants, scratch sizing, scheduler admission, host-transfer dispatch, launch compatibility and controller event ordering.
- Both new CPU test files also pass when executed directly with fail-fast, as CI invokes them: 4 PD transfer tests and 2 controller tests.
- The unsharded host-prefix backup setup independently reproduces the published head's `unexpected keyword argument 'start_owner'` failure and passes with `8620dbdaa1`.
- Local CPU runs bypass only the Mac Torch/MPS version preflight. A platform-specific NPU host-pool test is deselected because the local host-memory reserve cannot be met; GPU-dependent tests are skipped. These runs do not validate CUDA/NCCL or physical host transfers.
- Pre-commit and `git diff --check` pass. Mintlify 4.2.559 reports no broken links with anchor/redirect checks. Both documented launch commands pass the CLI parser and their shell block passes `bash -n`.

### Hardware E2E status

**Passed on current head `346068aaa329cf1692fbb6031f60469fdac77dcb`, Base attempt 2.**

- [Four-GB300 hardware job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40354128180/job/121958752142): `test_dsa_glm52_pd_kv_shard_hicache.py` actually ran and passed, with a 273-second suite duration. The test method completed with `Ran 1 test ... OK`; this was not a collection-only or skipped result.
- The test retains P2/D2, CP2, EAGLE MTP and all cold/device-hit/host-reloaded answer, speculative-verification, host-hit and rank-specific H2D assertions. Two 6,144-token pressure requests exceed the 8,192 logical GPU slots while fitting with the target prefix in the larger host cache.
- [CPU partition 17](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40354128180/job/121958700456): all 52 files passed, including `test_decode_hicache_l2.py` (36 seconds), which previously exposed the non-sharded backup signature regression.
- The existing AARCH64 P2/D2 accuracy test also passed in the same GB300 job (89 seconds). This fixture uses its supported fabric configuration: `MC_FORCE_MNNVL=true` and `SGLANG_MOONCAKE_CUSTOM_MEM_POOL=NVLINK`. The NVLink allocator supplies exportable KV buffers; the runner's wheel does not provide `nvlink_intra`.

The launch example has separate prefill/decode commands with one option per line, addressing review comment 4379290548. CLI arguments are unchanged; both examples match the E2E transport settings. Shell syntax, CLI parsing, allocator selection equivalence, pre-commit and Mintlify anchor/link checks pass.

The separate existing [GLM-5.2 layer-split accuracy rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40354126514/job/122014411774) **passed at 0.9422632794457275**, above the unchanged **0.935** GSM8K threshold; the full job passed 2/2 test files. The previous attempt scored 0.9345650500384911. Both attempts tested merge `e79b8b8c52735038eb60edcacff7a3e6f24ea69e` with KV sharding disabled, and no code or threshold changes were made between them. The successful rerun does not establish the cause of the score variation.

title: [AMD][Fix] Saturate FP8 KV commits instead of reproducing e4m3fnuz NaN overflow
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## Motivation

`jit-kernel-unit-test-amd` has been red on `main` since #40785 merged. Every run that has executed the job since has failed identically — #40785's own run, two on #34537, and one on an unrelated branch, all reporting `30732 / 65536` mismatched elements at the same index. The job only runs when a PR touches `python/sglang/kernels/`, so most PRs skip it and it went unnoticed.

Full evidence in #42981.

## Modifications

torch's `float8_e4m3fn` cast saturates to its max finite value. `float8_e4m3fnuz` has no infinity, so `fp8e4m3fnuz_from_fp32_value` returns NaN (`0x80`) for every magnitude at or above 256.0. Triton's cast saturates on both types, so the fused commit kernel from #40785 matches eager on CUDA and diverges on gfx94x.

This is not only a test problem. `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid` has a fused path and an eager fallback, and on ROCm they now write different bytes for the same input — the fallback writes NaN into a committed KV slot, which poisons attention for that slot on every later read.

Rather than have the test chase whichever cast runs, this makes saturation the defined contract and clamps before the FP8 cast in all three places:

- `cache_move.py` — the kernel clamps, with the limit passed as a `tl.constexpr`; NaN falls through both `tl.where` arms. Two vector ops added to a memory-bound kernel.
- `memory_pool.py` — the eager fallback clamps identically, so the two production paths agree.
- `test/kernels/prefix_valid.py` — the shared oracle clamps identically.

The limit is `torch.finfo(fp8).max`, not the conservative `fp8_max` constant (224.0 on fnuz): clamping at 224.0 would pull values that eager rounds to 240.0 down a step.

All three are no-ops on CUDA, where the eager cast already saturates to 448.

## Test plan

`jit-kernel-unit-test-amd` on MI300 / ROCm 10: **42/42 files passed** ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37648241557/job/113082433719)), including `test_prefix_valid_fp8.py` and `test_prefix_valid_fp8_pool.py`. For reference, the same job on current `main` fails at 6/42 with 30732/65536 mismatched elements.

An earlier revision of this branch clamped in FP32, which turned the `bf16/fp16 -> fp8` cast into `fp32 -> fp8`; those lower to different conversions and left 2/65536 elements off by one FP8 subnormal step at fp16 with a host scalar scale. Clamping in the source dtype restores the original lowering, and that is the version here.

Still red on this PR, all reproducing on #40785 or unrelated to this path:

- `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd (7)` — MiniMax sparse decode kernel requests 128 KiB LDS against a 64 KiB limit (`OutOfResources`), same partition red on #40785.
- `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x (1)` — red on #40785.
- `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` — `test_e2e_spec_eagle.py`; the server stops responding mid-stream (`RemoteDisconnected`), with no CUDA/HIP fault, scheduler exception or OOM in the log. That test runs `kv_cache_dtype=auto`, so `self.dtype` is not FP8 and neither the fused branch nor the eager clamp in this PR is reached — the non-FP8 commit path goes through `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid_tiled`, which is untouched here. The same job is also red on #40785, on a different test.
- NPU jobs — `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid` returns early for non-CUDA/non-HIP before reaching any line this PR touches.

If you would rather the kernel reproduce eager's `e4m3fnuz` NaN-on-overflow instead of saturating, I can invert the patch — but that writes NaN into the KV cache on AMD and diverges from the CUDA path, so saturation looks like the better contract.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Speculative] Support block verification for the DFlash family
author: maocheng23
body:
## Motivation

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42297 added `--speculative-use-block-verification` ([Block Verification Accelerates Speculative Decoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10444), Algorithm 2) for linear EAGLE / EAGLE3 / NEXTN only. The DFlash family (`DFLASH`, `DSPARK`) already verifies sampled drafts through the same Triton chain sampler, but the flag was rejected for these algorithms at startup.

## Modifications

- **Startup gate** (`speculative_hook.py`): accept `DFLASH` and `DSPARK` with `--speculative-use-block-verification` on CUDA/ROCm. NPU stays rejected because `sgl_kernel_npu`'s chain sampler has no block mode. Only EAGLE/EAGLE3 still auto-enable `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling`. DFlash-family sampled paths always pass their proposal distribution and never read that flag.
- **Shared accept path** (`dspark_accept.py`): `AcceptSampling` / `accept_sampling` / `_accept_sampling_core` take an explicit `block_verification` keyword and call `chain_speculative_sampling_triton(..., block_verification=True)` when it is set. The kernel is unchanged from #42297.
- **Callers**:
  - DSpark: `DSparkWorkerV2` passes the flag to `TargetVerifyExecutor`, which forwards it through `accept_draft_tokens` to both the all-sampling branch and the mixed greedy/sampling branch.
  - DFlash: `DFlashWorkerV2._selector_sampling_accept` forwards it. This method serves the candidate-selector drafts and the sampled LiLiCorr drafts (`SGLANG_ENABLE_LILICORR_SAMPLING=1`).
- **Greedy DFlash drafts**: plain DFlash, Domino, and LiLiCorr without sampling propose argmax tokens. The proposal is a point mass, so `q(x_i) = 1`, `r_i = prod p(x_j)`, and token-wise verification already reaches the per-prefix upper bound `P(accept >= i) = r_i`. Block verification therefore accepts the same prefixes, so these paths keep the existing target-only verifier. The worker logs a warning that the flag has no effect.
- Ragged/cutoff verify (`cutoff_verify_lens`) still truncates the sampler's result afterward, as it does in token-wise mode. A prefix of a target-distributed sample is still target-distributed, so the cutoff does not affect correctness.
- Updated the docs and the CLI help.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_block_verification_args.py`:
  - DFLASH/DSPARK are accepted, and block verification does not switch on rejection sampling for them. The per-algorithm handlers are patched out because they need a real draft checkpoint.
  - DFLASH/DSPARK on NPU are rejected.
  - The rejected-algorithm case moves from DFLASH to NGRAM.
- `test_block_verification.py::test_dflash_family_accept_uses_block_verification` (GPU): calls DSpark's real `accept_draft_tokens`, in both the all-sampling and the mixed-greedy branches. The proposal uses `q(x1) = 1, p(x1) = 1/2` and `q(x2) = 1/2, p(x2) = 1`, so `r_1 = 1/2` and `r_2 = 1`.
  - With block verification, every sampled row accepts both drafts and the bonus token from the target.
  - Without it, each row rejects the first draft with probability 1/2, so the test asserts that at least one of 63 rows does.

Local (macOS, CPU, Torch 2.14.1):

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/spec/test_block_verification_args.py \
  test/registered/unit/spec/test_spec_registry.py \
  test/registered/unit/spec/test_eagle_gate_routing.py \
  test/registered/unit/spec/test_spec_cpu_overlap_constraint.py
# 45 passed, 21 subtests passed
```

GPU (one NVIDIA GB300; Torch 2.14.1+cu130, sglang-kernel 0.4.9, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, Triton 3.8.0, Transformers 5.17.0; source snapshot of `c8699a8046`):

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_block_verification.py \
  test/registered/unit/spec/test_block_verification_args.py \
  test/registered/spec/dspark/test_dspark_kernel_parity.py
# 30 passed, 43 subtests passed
```

Pre-commit passed on all changed files.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2 / AIME25 end-to-end

Block verification increased acceptance length on all three seed pairs, by +3.31% pooled. That is larger than the +0.88% that #42297 measured for MTP with three proposed tokens. DFlash2 proposes seven tokens per step, so there are more prefixes for block verification to rescue after an early rejection. The pooled throughput gain of +1.76% was not consistent: per seed it was +2.75%, +2.67%, and -0.29%. The accuracy and cap-hit differences are within run-to-run noise for three sampled runs.

| Metric | Token-wise | Block | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Acceptance length (includes bonus) | 4.0091 | 4.1416 | +3.31% |
| Correct drafts per verify step | 3.0091 | 3.1417 | +4.40% |
| Output throughput (tokens/s) | 1260.93 | 1283.17 | +1.76% |
| Boxed score over entire response | 76/90 | 76/90 | |
| Responses hitting the 32,768-token cap | 18/90 | 21/90 | |

| Seed | Token AL | Block AL | Token tok/s | Block tok/s | Token correct | Block correct |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 980406 | 4.0106 | 4.1573 | 1219.29 | 1252.76 | 25/30 | 24/30 |
| 981406 | 3.9919 | 4.1371 | 1260.97 | 1294.64 | 24/30 | 27/30 |
| 982406 | 4.0256 | 4.1306 | 1306.96 | 1303.13 | 27/30 | 25/30 |

**Setup**:
- **Hardware and models**: one NVIDIA GB300, TP1. Target `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` BF16, revision `1d4bf0f2ff`. Draft `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, revision `015e795645` (`DFlash2DraftModel`: candidate selector with top-k 16, block size 8).
- **Speculative settings**: `--speculative-algorithm DFLASH --speculative-num-draft-tokens 8`.
- **Server settings**: BF16 KV cache, FP32 recurrent state, FlashInfer attention, CUDA graphs on, radix cache off, concurrency 8.
- **The two arms**: they run identical commands, except that the block arm adds `--speculative-use-block-verification`. The server log confirms that selector sampling is folded into the draft CUDA graph (`sampling_enabled=True`), and neither arm logged the no-effect warning.

**Protocol**: same as #42297.
- **Workload**: all 30 MathArena/aime_2025 questions, with the same frozen dataset (SHA256 `b4bdeba5...`). Thinking is enabled at xhigh. Sampling uses temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, and top-k 20, with at most 32,768 new tokens.
- **Seeds and arm order**: three base seeds, offset by problem ID. Arm order alternates by seed.
- **Warmup**: each run warms up eight slots and flushes the cache before timing.
- **Metrics**: acceptance length is total completion tokens divided by total verification steps. Throughput is total output tokens divided by measured wall time. An independent pass over the raw per-request records reproduced every aggregate and checked request coverage, the sampling seeds, and that the commands match.

### Qwen3.8-27B + DSpark / AIME25 end-to-end

DSpark shows the same effect. Block verification increased acceptance length on all three seed pairs, by +3.13% pooled (+3.02%, +2.42%, +3.96% per seed). Throughput was flat at +0.54% pooled, and per seed it was +1.51%, +0.42%, and -0.45%. Other jobs were running on the same node's other GPUs during this run, so its throughput is noisier than the DFlash2 run's. The differences in score and cap hits are within run-to-run noise for three sampled runs.

| Metric | Token-wise | Block | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Acceptance length (includes bonus) | 4.0134 | 4.1390 | +3.13% |
| Correct drafts per verify step | 3.0135 | 3.1393 | +4.17% |
| Output throughput (tokens/s) | 1296.61 | 1303.58 | +0.54% |
| Boxed score over entire response | 77/90 | 82/90 | |
| Responses hitting the 32,768-token cap | 19/90 | 17/90 | |

| Seed | Token AL | Block AL | Token tok/s | Block tok/s | Token correct | Block correct |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 980406 | 4.0068 | 4.1278 | 1269.98 | 1289.17 | 25/30 | 27/30 |
| 981406 | 4.0597 | 4.1582 | 1283.60 | 1288.97 | 26/30 | 27/30 |
| 982406 | 3.9731 | 4.1306 | 1337.45 | 1331.40 | 26/30 | 28/30 |

**Setup**: same code, image, target model, server settings, and protocol as the DFlash2 run above. The differences are:
- **Speculative settings**: `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK` with draft `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark`, revision `b9a5dbdf03` (`DSparkDraftModel` with a vanilla Markov head and a confidence head). Gamma 7 is read from the checkpoint, so the verify window is 8. `SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE` is left at its default, `static`.
- **The two arms**: they run identical commands, except that the block arm adds `--speculative-use-block-verification`. Every server logged `DSpark draft proposal (greedy + sampling) folded into the draft cuda graph`, so the sampling batches drafted from `softmax(corrected_logits / T)` and verified on the eager accept path, where the flag is wired. The folded in-graph accept serves all-greedy batches only.
- **Audit**: an independent pass over the raw per-request records reproduced every aggregate.

### Sampler

No kernel change. The sampler cost is the block-mode cost measured in #42297. Paths that do not opt in are unchanged: the flag defaults to off, and greedy DFlash drafts never reach the block sampler.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add registered unit tests.
- [x] Update documentation.
- [x] End-to-end acceptance-length and throughput comparison for DFlash2 and DSpark.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style.
