title: [Perf] Fuse short-convolution checkpoint tracking metadata
author: ekzhang
body:
**This reduces CPU/host overhead when running TML Inkling architecture models at low-latency.**

## Motivation

Short-convolution prefix-cache tracking computes each checkpoint window with several eager Torch operations. Even on the prefill CUDA-graph path, the metadata refresh launches those operations before replaying the model graph.

## Modifications

Replace the NVIDIA CUDA tracking-index calculation with one Triton launch into the existing output buffer. Preserve signed floor division for negative offsets, token-buffer clamping, zeroed padding, and absent prefix lengths during graph capture. Keep the existing Torch path for other devices, as well as current draft-decoding guards and physical checkpoint-slot handling.

Register the operator lazily under `sglang.kernels.ops.mamba` and add a CUDA CI parity test.

## Accuracy Tests

- 43 new kernel tests pass: empty/live/padded batches, int32/int64 lengths, negative chunk offsets, large prefixes, non-power-of-two chunk sizes, clamping, and CUDA graph replay with changed inputs and stable output storage.
- All 17 existing Inkling checkpoint tests pass, including 29 subtests covering compaction, checkpoint destinations, draft decoding, and graph replay.
- All 67 kernel namespace tests pass.
- Upstream pre-commit checks and CI registry collection pass.

GPU validation: NVIDIA GB300, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu132, Triton 3.6.0. The checkout's pinned PyTorch 2.14.1 environment has not been tested locally.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/mamba/test_sconv_tracking.py test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_inkling_checkpoint_indices.py
PYTHONPATH=python pytest -q test/registered/unit/kernels/test_kernels_namespace.py
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Cold-L2 eager CUDA elapsed time, median, measured with `triton.testing.do_bench` (100 ms warmup and measurement). The reference is the original Torch sequence with preallocated output and offset buffers; measurements include gaps caused by host dispatch. These are metadata-refresh microbenchmarks, not end-to-end inference latency.

| Rows | Live rows | Original | Fused |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32 | 32 | 161.1 µs | 7.2 µs |
| 32 | 16 | 161.0 µs | 6.9 µs |
| 128 | 128 | 146.2 µs | 7.1 µs |
| 128 | 64 | 172.3 µs | 7.1 µs |
| 1024 | 1024 | 151.0 µs | 7.1 µs |
| 1024 | 512 | 159.9 µs | 7.1 µs |

At 32 rows, the metadata refresh saves approximately 154 µs per invocation.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with upstream pre-commit.
- [x] Add kernel tests with CUDA CI registration.
- [x] Provide numerical parity and microbenchmark results.
- [x] Follow the kernel namespace and code-style conventions.
- [ ] Run upstream CI with the pinned dependencies.

title: [Build][CI] Drop Python 3.10: require Python 3.11+ and run CUDA CI on Python 3.12
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Motivation

Python 3.10 reaches end of life in October 2026. This PR raises sglang's minimum Python to 3.11 and moves the CUDA CI stages onto uv-managed Python 3.12, the interpreter the `lmsysorg/sglang` image has used since #42612, where GPU CI previously tested the runners' system Python 3.10. It also unblocks dependencies that ship only 3.11+ wheels, e.g. `tml-renderers` (`cp311-abi3`); the code already uses unguarded 3.11-only APIs (`BaseException.add_note`, `tomllib`, `asyncio.TaskGroup`).

## Release note

**sglang now requires Python >= 3.11.** On Python 3.10, `pip install sglang` does not fail. Instead it resolves to the last release that still supported 3.10. Users on Python 3.10, such as the Ubuntu 22.04 system Python, need to move to 3.11+ to get new releases. Python 3.11 is a transitional floor: it will be dropped later with advance notice, around its October 2027 end of life or earlier if a core dependency such as torch drops it.

## Modifications

**CI runs on Python 3.12**

- `scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh` installs into a uv-managed venv at `/opt/sglang-ci-py${SGLANG_TEST_CI_PYTHON}` (default `3.12`) on every runner, whatever Python its image ships.
  - Every job upgrades uv with pip and puts it first on `PATH`. It downloads a managed Python only when none is installed or the installed build lacks `os.memfd_create`, since the download comes from github.com, which some runner pools reach slowly enough to time out the install step.
  - The venv persists across jobs. The install writes a completion marker when it finishes, and a venv without one (a job cancelled mid-install) is recreated.
  - It is wired through the existing `VIRTUAL_ENV` / `GITHUB_PATH` / `BASH_ENV` mechanism.
  - A runner without fast github.com access can set uv's `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_MIRROR` for that download; no CI runner sets it today.
- Rust extensions are built for cp312 only (`rust-ext-*-cp312` artifacts and cache keys). The CPU stages, the simulator stage and `rerun-test` pin setup-python 3.12 to match.
- `diffusion-ci-gt-gen.yml` installs its extra LTX dependencies into the active interpreter instead of the system Python.
- The unit-test coverage job (`ci-coverage-overview.yml`) installs into a throwaway venv under `$RUNNER_TEMP` and no longer touches the persistent venv.
- `pyarrow<26` is pinned wherever CI installs a package that pins numpy 1.26.4: next to `lmms_eval==0.5.0` in the CUDA install and in the simulator's `aic` extra (`aiconfigurator`); the NPU install already pins `pyarrow==23.0.1` on main (#43308). pyarrow 26 requires NumPy 2 at import without declaring it, so a fresh resolve would otherwise break `import datasets`.

**Minimum Python 3.11**

Python 3.10 reaches end of life in October 2026. CI and the production image run Python 3.12; 3.11 stays installable as a transitional floor until it is dropped with advance notice.

- `requires-python = ">=3.11"` in:
  - `python/pyproject.toml`, `pyproject_cpu.toml`, `pyproject_npu.toml`, `pyproject_xpu.toml`
  - `rust/sglang-{grpc,mm,server}/pyproject.toml`
- The `tomli ; python_version < '3.11'` dependency is removed.
- `release-pypi.yml` builds wheels for 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13; the sglang wheel bundles a version-specific native gRPC extension, so the floor needs its own wheel. Nightly and PR wheels are built on 3.12.
- The install docs, `bench_serving` and backend-plugin guides, and the MiniMax-M3 cookbook now state Python 3.11+. The Laguna-XS.2 cookbook's Python 3.10 note now refers only to its pinned cp310 nightly, since nightlies are built on 3.12.

**`memfd_create` on uv-managed Python**

python-build-standalone builds before 20260718, which uv older than 0.11.30 installs, have no `os.memfd_create`; on them the MiniMax H3 reference-video decode and the shared engram host table raise `AttributeError`. The install script replaces such a build with the latest one, which keeps CI off them, and users on one should upgrade uv and run `uv python upgrade 3.12`. The call sites are unchanged from main; the streamed-encode tests no longer skip when `os.memfd_create` is missing.

**FastAPI native telemetry**

FastAPI 0.142 traces every request once a global tracer provider exists, and sglang's tracing init sets one, so HTTP spans were exported even at trace level 0. Fresh installs, including new images, get 0.142+, while the runners' existing environments (0.136.1) hid it. Every sglang FastAPI app that can share a process with tracing init now passes `telemetry={"tracing": False, "metrics": False, "logs": False}`. FastAPI before 0.142 has no native telemetry and takes the keyword through `**extra`, so the dependency needs no version floor.

**Test fix for Python 3.12**

`test_vit_npu_graph_runner.py` patched a module that `patch.dict(sys.modules)` had already dropped; on 3.12, `mock` re-imports it through `pkgutil.resolve_name` without its `torch_npu` stub. The test now patches the module object.

**Unchanged**

- `python/pyproject_other.toml` (ROCm, MUSA, HPU, MPS), `kernels/aot/pyproject_rocm.toml` and `pyproject_musa.toml` keep `>=3.10`: the ROCm 7.2.0 images and MUSA still run on Python 3.10.
- `sglang-kernel-cpu` (`kernels/aot/pyproject_cpu.toml`) keeps `>=3.10`.
- `sglang-kernel` (`kernels/aot/pyproject.toml`) keeps `>=3.10`. It is built on 3.10 as a `cp310-abi3` wheel, which installs unchanged on 3.11+.
- `sgl-model-gateway` keeps its own interpreter range.

## Notes for hardware maintainers

- **AMD**: the ROCm 7.2.0 flavor uses `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1` (`docker/rocm.Dockerfile`) and `3rdparty/amd/wheel/sglang` pins cp310 ROCm wheels. Those still work because `pyproject_other.toml` keeps 3.10, but they need a 3.11+ base before ROCm can follow. rocm724 and rocm10 are already on Python 3.12.
- **Moore Threads**: `srt_musa` pins the `torch 2.11.0.post1` series (torch, torch_musa, torchaudio, torchvision, deep_ep), which has only cp310 wheels on the MTHREADS index. The `.post2` series has cp312 wheels. `docker/musa.Dockerfile` uses the ubuntu:22.04 system Python, and `scripts/ci/musa/musa_install_dependency.sh` pins the cp310 Triton wheel by sha256. Moving MUSA to 3.12 means repinning those, which needs MUSA hardware to validate.
- **Ascend**: `pyproject_npu.toml` now requires 3.11. Both component sets in the install guide satisfy it: CANN 9.0.0 (`python==3.11`, the set the prebuilt SGLang NPU images use) and CANN 9.1.0 (Python 3.12, the set NPU CI runs).

## Accuracy Tests

No model forward or kernel changes.

## Verification

This PR's own GPU CI is the end-to-end check: every CUDA stage installs into the 3.12 venv and runs against the unchanged `cp310-abi3` sgl-kernel wheel and the cp312 Rust extensions. On `efd68ddc523`, before the install script stopped downloading Python on every job, PR Test [Base](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38139972257) and [Extra](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38139971932) pass. On `0defd83f2d3` (run [37784357976](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37784357976/attempts/1)), runners whose image ships Python 3.10 recreated `/opt/sglang-ci-py3.12` in a 48–323 s cold install, and later jobs on the same runner took about 35 s.

- memfd: `multimodal-gen-unit-test` in run [37704464694](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37704464694/job/113077362818) ran on a pre-20260718 3.12.13 build, and 6 of its failures came from the missing `os.memfd_create` (4 in `test_minimax_h3_media`, 2 in `test_layerwise_offload`).
- Locally, with `os.memfd_create` deleted to simulate that build, main fails the same 6 tests; with the function present, all 205 pass.
- `test_tracing.py::test_trace_level_0` fails on main with FastAPI 0.143 (5 FastAPI spans exported) and passes with this PR.
- Local checks: `bash -n` and YAML load of changed scripts and workflows, `pre-commit`, `scripts/ci/test_diffusion_rust_gate.py`, and `configure_environment` against real `uv` (venv creation, marker-gated reuse, exported environment).

title: [Diffusion] Add ModelOpt FP8 checkpoint quantization for Pi0.5
author: trebladev
body:
## Motivation

Add Pi0.5 checkpoint calibration and native FP8 inference using SGLang’s existing ModelOpt FP8 linear backend.

The quantization coverage and synthetic calibration recipe follow https://jetson-ai-lab.com/tutorials/openpi\_on\_thor/.

## Modifications

- Add a calibration/export tool supporting observation datasets and explicitly selected synthetic inputs.
- Quantize PaliGemma and action-expert fused projections, SigLIP encoder projections, the multimodal projector, and action input/output heads using per-tensor E4M3 weights and static activation scales.
- Preserve existing tensor/tuple interfaces and output dtypes. Keep embeddings, convolutions, norms, AdaRMS dense layers, and time MLPs unquantized.
- Add checkpoint validation, projection replacement, and FP8 weight finalization.
- Support resident BF16 inference on a single SM89+ NVIDIA GPU; reject TP/SP and component offload.
- Add CPU contract tests and a CUDA calibration, checkpoint-loading, and graph-replay test.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on RTX 4090 D with PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, ModelOpt 0.47.0, and Transformers 5.12.1.

- Full Pi0.5 Libero checkpoint: calibrated all five supported components using one synthetic observation, then validated on four separate synthetic observations.

Consistency metrics use only the **10 predicted steps and 7 returned action dimensions**:

| Comparison | Mean absolute difference | Maximum absolute difference | Cosine similarity |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| BF16 vs native FP8 | 0\.008364 | 0\.100873 | 0\.999526 |
| Fake quant vs native FP8 | 0\.006177 | 0\.059110 | — |

Cosine similarity flattens the four observations into one vector. Per-observation BF16/FP8 cosine similarities range from **0\.999384 to 0.999659**.

All returned actions were finite. Eager and CUDA Graph outputs matched exactly for both BF16 and FP8 across the four observations, including changed inputs.

These results validate numerical behavior on synthetic observations. Real robot task accuracy and success rates have not been evaluated.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Measured full Pi0.5 Libero model inference on one RTX 4090 D, batch size 1, three 224×224 camera inputs, 200 tokens, and 10 denoising steps, using `torch_sdpa`.

Each mode uses 5 warmup runs and 30 timed runs with CUDA synchronization. Timing includes prefix encoding and action sampling from preprocessed inputs, without prefix-cache reuse. It excludes preprocessing, network overhead, checkpoint loading, and initial graph capture.

| Mode | BF16 median latency | FP8 median latency | BF16/FP8 speedup | BF16 peak allocated memory | FP8 peak allocated memory |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Eager | 248\.44 ms | 360\.67 ms | 0\.69× | 6\.71 GiB | 4\.22 GiB |
| CUDA Graph | 70\.97 ms | 55\.53 ms | 1\.28× | 6\.72 GiB | 4\.22 GiB |

CUDA Graph latency decreased by **21\.8%**, with **37\.2% lower peak allocated memory**. Eager latency increased by **45\.2%**; the measured speed improvement applies to CUDA Graph execution.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit (https://docs.sglang.io/developer\_guide/contribution\_guide.html\#format-code-with-pre-commit)](<https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit>). All applicable hooks passed.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests (https://docs.sglang.io/developer\_guide/contribution\_guide.html\#run-and-add-unit-tests)](<https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests>).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations (https://docs.sglang.io/developer\_guide/contribution\_guide.html\#write-documentations)](<https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations>).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy (https://docs.sglang.io/developer\_guide/contribution\_guide.html\#test-the-accuracy)](<https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy>) and [Benchmark the speed (https://docs.sglang.io/developer\_guide/contribution\_guide.html\#benchmark-the-speed)](<https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed>). Synthetic consistency and latency results are included; real-task accuracy remains unverified.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance (https://docs.sglang.io/developer\_guide/contribution\_guide.html\#code-style-guidance)](<https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance>).

title: [diffusion] Remove unused helpers and write-only state
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

Remove unused helpers, write-only state and duplicated implementations:

- USP's obsolete collective wait wrapper and its unused import, NVFP4's unused tensor-shape wrapper, and SVG2's unused kwargs checker.
- Qwen edit's unused condition-image sizing method and Qwen VAE's unused constructor-time convolution counts.
- Old Cache-DiT step-count/warmup fields; mounting still uses the complete active cache key.
- LTX's old LoRA phase field; switching still uses the active phase/strength signature.
- Unused disaggregation configuration copies and RIFE's unused resolved-path field.
- Encoder's unused mapping copy and the unused stage logging setter.
- Empty HF config registry and unreachable config reloading; standard AutoConfig registration remains supported.
- Obsolete disagg_args compatibility shim and its alias-only test; actual role/CLI definitions stay in server_args/disagg.py.
- Share spatial VAE tile geometry across tiled encode/decode and parallel tiled/patch decode, retaining independent traversal, blending and communication.
- Share SLA/SageSLA projection initialization, feature-map setup and reference linear-attention math within the existing backend module; keep sparse kernels separate.
- Share identical TP query/KV head partition rules across Llama, Qwen3, Gemma2 and Gemma3; retain model-specific projections, RoPE, QK norm and sliding attention.
- Reuse the existing linear weight allocator for ConvRot INT8 JIT and comfy backends; keep their validation, scale storage and postprocessing independent.
- Share MOVA audio/video text and time embeddings, time projection and block initialization, preserving registration order and distinct heads/patch convolutions.
- Reuse common sampling request extras for action policies without changing their fields, inheritance or action-specific request merge.
- Share Qwen-Image/JoyImage/Krea2 channelwise VAE decode normalization without changing tensor construction or reciprocal/cast order.
- Share LTX2/SANA-WM video latent normalization in the existing VAE config module.
- Inherit identical CUDA/MUSA unsupported-device methods and the default XPU communicator.
- Reuse identical ModelOpt FP8 inference dispatch while retaining separate postprocessing.
- Reuse the existing unquantized linear weight allocator for embeddings, without changing the embedding method's base class or its apply/embedding implementations.
- Unused diffusion CPU-architecture probe (the SRT implementation remains used and unchanged), plus eight obsolete test-only HTTP/port/memory/video/GT helper functions and their typing-only import.
- Uncalled post-training SP reduce, temporary logger suppression and error-formatting helpers.
- Inline the single-caller AutoConfig wrapper and remove redundant NVFP4 list forwarding.
- Share Wan/LingBot 3D sequence-shard RoPE coordinate construction in the existing NDRotaryEmbedding class, keeping their independent model-level LRU caches.
- Share identical generic/H3 latent input verification in the existing latent-preparation module, preserving H3's inheritance and noise-generation path.
- Unwired function-level Python tracing and its unused env entry. Setting the removed env emits a retirement warning; --enable-trace request tracing is unchanged.
- Superseded CLI cleanup, safetensors shard filtering, single-file NVFP4 wrapper, and unused HF helpers/context-length constant. Active file-selection and quantization paths are unchanged; SRT's same-named utilities are untouched.

- Share H3 positive-finite float validation between sampling configuration and canonical requests through the existing configuration utility module, preserving accepted inputs and error messages.

- Share 2x2 latent packing across Qwen-Image, FLUX.1 and LongCat through the existing pipeline configuration base, removing FLUX's dependency on a private Qwen helper. FLUX.2's distinct layout is unchanged.

- Share Cosmos3's QKV/output projection initialization within its existing model module; causal and cross-attention retain separate head checks, norms and execution paths.

- Reuse the existing prequantized NVFP4 GEMM implementation for the ordinary linear path's duplicated tail, preserving activation quantization, tuple opt-in rejection and output reshape.

- Share SANA-WM AdaLN modulation preparation between dense and streaming block entry points, without merging their attention, cache or FFN control flow.

- Remove thirteen unused parallel-state/communication and WebUI argument helpers. Keep process-group initialization/destruction, active DP accessors and the declared distributed exports unchanged.

- Remove unused LTX2 latent denormalization helpers, Z-Image padding inspection and the obsolete sequence-rank alias. Active decoder normalization and canonical SP accessors remain unchanged.

- Remove superseded capacity-blind disaggregation selection, its unused maximum-slot setting and kwargs plumbing, and the empty completion hook. Capacity-aware selection is now the abstract policy contract; production algorithms, counters, locks and pool routing are unchanged.

- Store disaggregation request start timestamps directly instead of allocating a private dataclass with an unused stage timestamp; preserve exported statistics, locking and formulas. Remove LTX2's unused generic coordinate wrapper while retaining the directly used video/audio methods.

- Remove forward-context batch-size timing that was permanently disabled with no configuration or caller, together with its unused globals/imports and unwritten attention-backend field/setter. Preserve active timestep, metadata, batch and nested-context restoration; request/stage observability is unchanged.

- Remove the unused pipeline JSON-export method and its exclusive imports, plus empty stage hook/offload methods with no callers or overrides. Keep CLI JSON loading and active stage load_model fallback intact.

- Remove MOVA scheduler's uncalled training target/weight and reverse-recovery methods, unused training branch/argument and write-only training state. Retain train_timesteps/train_sigmas because inference step_from_to uses their lookup tables.

- Share the validation and construction logic of MOVA's directional sequential and single-modality pair modes within their existing scheduler method, retaining each direction's tensor operation order and errors.

143 existing production files: net 1,820 lines removed, including the obsolete disaggregation shim. 109 net lines removed from existing test files, including obsolete helper definitions; one stale source reference corrected. No test cases or assertions were removed. No new files, configuration, tests, or numerical-path changes.

- Reuse offload component-name normalization for load ordering; remove its duplicate implementation without changing suffix handling or risk ranking.

- Share identical model unwrapping between Ideogram and Z-Image BCG prompt padders in their existing prompt-padding utility; preserve wrapper lookup order and the separate model-identification semantics.

- Remove six obsolete `channels_last_3d` API-existence checks in VAE loading/layout and parallel convolution. Keep device-policy gates, tensor-layout checks, conversion exceptions, and environment overrides unchanged.

- Use the public PyTorch schema-inference API directly for custom-op registration; remove the obsolete PyTorch 2.4 private fallback and a catch-and-rethrow-only AttributeError handler. Preserve duplicate-registration protection and fake implementation registration.

- Remove catch-and-rethrow-only wrappers from default weight loading and Qwen2.5-VL parameter lookup. Keep scalar filling, shape validation, extra-bias skipping, and missing-parameter errors unchanged; do not remove exclusion handlers ahead of broader recovery catches.

## Validation

- Loader rethrow cleanup: two retained full-module AST contracts match after unwrapping only the redundant tries. Forty-eight native CPU/CUDA scalar/copy cases, twelve shape-error cases, and twenty-four Qwen production-method dispatch/error cases match, including parameter-storage identity. Existing weight-utils/Qwen-generation/text-loader suites pass (79 tests, 9 subtests, 3 skips); pre-commit passes. No full-checkpoint E2E claim.

- Custom-op registration cleanup: retained full-module AST matches on the supported public-schema branch after removing the redundant rethrow handler. Twelve native CPU/CUDA cases cover schemas, duplicate registration, mutation, and FakeTensor for FP32/FP16/BF16; three error contracts match. Existing OOT-platform/quantization suites pass (90 tests, 31 subtests); pre-commit passes. No model E2E or performance claim.

- channels_last_3d guard retirement: four retained full-module AST contracts match when the supported PyTorch API is present; 48 CPU/CUDA layout cases, six simulated device policies, and six native conversion states agree with the frozen parent. Existing VAE-loader, Wan-frame, and LTX channels-last tests pass (49 tests, 8 subtests); pre-commit passes. No real non-CUDA or multi-GPU execution claim.

- BCG unwrap deduplication: three retained full-module AST contracts match; 42 CPU/CUDA comparisons preserve wrapper object identity, rotary outputs, and metadata-cache reuse. Existing BCG padding/coordinate suites pass (34 tests, 5 subtests); pre-commit passes. This is not a full CUDA-graph or checkpoint E2E benchmark.

- Component-name deduplication: retained full-module AST matches after replacing the helper; 132 frozen-parent name/risk-rank cases agree, including Unicode and repeated suffixes. Existing component-loading-order and layerwise-offload suites pass (202 tests) on RTX PRO 6000; pre-commit passes.

- Share Llama/Qwen3 encoder loading in existing weight_utils.py: preserve rotary-cache filtering, KV-scale remapping, stacked shard loading and Qwen3-only model. prefix removal; no other encoder adopts this helper. TP1 native frozen/current checks cover 64 real safetensors loads, 128 forwards, 8 FP8 shard loads, 32 successful dispatches and 32 matching dispatch errors. Weight/output/hidden-state values and ATen sequences match, source tensors stay unchanged and measured load peak allocation does not increase. 76 existing tests and 9 subtests pass, 3 skip; pre-commit passes. Tiny loader-only medians remain about 1 ms; no full-checkpoint E2E or speedup claim.

- Remove four identity assignments in packed linear loading, VSA metadata and PIL input handling; replace the no-op PIL branch with the same invalid-input check. Three full-module AST comparisons account for only these no-ops; 32 frozen/current PIL/bytes/path/data-URL image conversions and invalid-input errors match. 49 existing linear/VSA/image API/input-validation tests and pre-commit pass. No kernel, tensor math or full-checkpoint performance claim.

- Share legacy Column/RowParallelLinear checkpoint slicing and copying within linear.py, eliminating two self-assignments. Keep each loader entry point and all constructor, forward, packed/QKV and v2 loader bodies unchanged. 360 frozen/current CPU/CUDA FP32/FP16/BF16 rank-loading comparisons cover TP1/2/4 rank slices, already-sharded checkpoints, scalar scales, shape assertions and unchanged parameter storage; retained module AST matches. 145 existing tests and 27 subtests pass; pre-commit passes. Rank slicing validation is not a multi-GPU collective E2E or speedup claim.

- Hunyuan3D denoising and Kandinsky6 decoding: inherit shared stage initialization instead of forwarding-only constructors. Existing call signatures remain accepted; base-class optional arguments are now exposed. All remaining module AST matches the frozen parent. 16 CPU/CUDA FP32/BF16 frozen/current initialization comparisons preserve state keys, component references, pipeline weakrefs and attention backend selection; 80 existing tests and pre-commit pass. No full-checkpoint E2E or speedup claim.

- Stateless initialization: remove super-only constructors from SiluAndMul, MOVA MulAdd, T5MultiHeadAttention and NPUMXFP4Config. Four complete-module AST comparisons preserve every other method; inherited initialization and 12 CPU/CUDA FP32/BF16 operation checks pass, as do NPU configuration metadata checks (no physical NPU kernel claim). 150 existing tests and 34 subtests pass, 3 skip; pre-commit passes. No full-checkpoint E2E or speedup claim.

- LoRA linear initialization: remove five parameter-forwarding constructors and inherit the existing common initialization. Preserve argument names/order/defaults, snapshots, state registration, adapters and every forward/slicing body; complete retained module AST matches. 80 real linear/LoRA CPU/CUDA FP32/BF16 constructor comparisons preserve state, RNG and snapshot clone/view semantics for positional/keyword arguments. 59 existing LoRA tests pass; pre-commit passes. No full-checkpoint E2E or speedup claim.

- Constructor/state cleanup: remove unused LTX audio VAE z_shape copies, communicator global_world_size copy, obsolete CustomOp.default_on stub and two super-only GELU constructors. Keep inherited initialization, explicit platform-forward overrides, registration and all numerical bodies. Four complete retained module ASTs match; 32 native CPU/CUDA FP32/BF16 activation-gradient/audio-VAE comparisons and real single-rank Gloo retained-state comparison match the frozen parent. 75 existing OOT/distributed/model-boundary/disaggregation tests plus 14 subtests pass; pre-commit passes. No full-checkpoint E2E or performance claim.

- Inherited defaults: reuse Platform device-capability/default-communicator methods in MPS/NPU, parent Diffusers pipeline initialization and default replicated Helios stage parallelism; remove uncalled no-op NPU/ROCm/XPU warning hooks. Retained ASTs in six modules match after explicit removals. Frozen-parent native-module checks preserve query values, initialization return and parallelism; 103 existing platform/OOT, Helios, disaggregation and selector tests plus 31 subtests pass. Pre-commit passes. Preserve Qwen cache-policy overrides and CustomOp overrides whose presence affects OOT dispatch. No physical MPS/NPU/ROCm or full-model benchmark claim.

- Metadata-builder lifecycle: remove the unused abstract prepare hook, all 14 no-op implementations, abstract constructor and 13 empty constructors. Keep VSA-H3 workspace-cache initialization and every build method unchanged. All 14 retained module ASTs match after explicit removals. 11 real imported builder constructors/state/signatures match the frozen parent; three optional backends lack dependencies and are statically checked only. Build remains mandatory; build-only extensions instantiate. 119 existing attention/H3 tests and 33 subtests pass, three tests skip; pre-commit passes. No backend-kernel or E2E speedup claim.

- Unwired interfaces: remove the unreferenced VideoRemixRequest schema, UnspecifiedPlatform placeholder and obsolete check_sampling_param wrapper. Platform fallback still selects CPU; native/OOT contracts and active sampling validation are retained. Wan progressive denoising inherits the identical no-op resolution hook. Four retained module ASTs match after explicit removals. 104 existing platform/OOT, API, sampling and progressive tests plus 74 subtests pass; pre-commit passes. Retired interfaces have no compatibility shim.

- Dead configuration/constants: remove the unconsumed logging dictionary and its exclusive import/format aliases, unused RoPE cache and six unused model/video constants. Retained code in all six modules has identical ASTs after the explicit removals. 57 existing logging, RoPE, SR tiling, LingBot and realtime tests pass; pre-commit passes. Active logger setup, encoding and video transport remain unchanged.

- Retired placement interface: remove unwired ResidencyTarget/RankResidencyReport types and their exclusive constants/imports; preserve WarmupMemoryRecord and all active estimation formulas. Complete retained AST matches; JSON wire format and 2,048 frozen-parent estimate comparisons match. 79 existing auto-residency, warmup, RoPE and FLUX2 tests pass after merging main. No checkpoint E2E or performance claim.

- SANA refiner blocks: reuse the existing video-block body across ordinary and streaming refiners, with explicit self-attention callbacks. Preserve independent attention implementations, KV prefix/capture, modulation, cross-attention and FFN operation order. Complete module ASTs match after the explicit helper/call-site normalization. 120 real Diffusers LTX2 block CPU/CUDA FP32/BF16 comparisons preserve output/layout, ATen sequence and captured KV across interleaved/split RoPE, context boundaries and pre/post capture/history modes. 92 existing SANA tests and two subtests pass. No full-checkpoint E2E or speedup claim.

- GLM/mesh state: remove unread GLM default-size calculation and MeshRender camera/bake attribute copies; retain constructor arguments, request sizing and projection selection. Two complete module ASTs match after three assignment removals. 48 native CPU/CUDA mesh projection comparisons and nine GLM constructor/component-policy comparisons pass; 25 existing GLM/Hunyuan3D tests and three subtests pass. No full rendering, checkpoint E2E or performance claim.

- Coordinator/postprocessing state: remove unread SRVGG constructor copies, Qwen layered default-size state and retired coordinator flags/annotation. Constructor interfaces and active communicator creation remain unchanged. Three complete module ASTs match after exact state deletions; 48 native SRVGG CPU/CUDA FP32/BF16 registration, weight, RNG and forward comparisons pass across activations, depths and scales. 60 existing distributed/graph/role tests and five subtests pass. No multi-GPU inference or performance claim.

- Realtime text-cache copying: consolidate two single-caller list wrappers into the existing field-copy function. Preserve tensor identity, independent outer lists and nested sequence-length lists, including None/empty inputs. 120 native CPU/CUDA FP32/BF16 copy-contract checks and 184 existing cache/model-boundary/residency tests pass, with one existing skip. No numerical or performance claim.

- RealESRGAN transfer wrappers: inline the single-caller H2D/D2H pass-throughs, retaining preprocessing, postprocessing and every existing timing region. Whole-module AST matches after exact inlining. 48 native small SRVGG/RRDB CPU/CUDA FP32/BF16 batch upscales preserve pixel output, layout, ATen calls, RNG and input arrays across batch 1/2 and native/downsample/extra-upsample output sizes; empty and mismatched inputs retain their behavior. No pretrained-checkpoint E2E or performance claim.

- Encoder/shape component copies: remove eight unused attributes in T5Stack, Pi05 RMSNorm and Hunyuan3D VAE helpers, retaining constructor signatures and actual branch, projection and attention settings. Three remaining complete module ASTs match. 64 native CPU/CUDA FP32/BF16 constructor/state/RNG comparisons pass, including 56 Pi05/Hunyuan3D forwards with exact output/stride. 94 existing encoder/Pi05/Hunyuan3D tests and three subtests pass, with three existing skips. T5 coverage is construction only; no pretrained-checkpoint E2E or performance claim.

- Audio component copies: remove six unused scalar attributes from DAC/H3 audio encoders, AliasFree activation, LTX audio patchifier and LTX vocoder, retaining actual channel/filter/layout/dilation settings. Five complete module ASTs match after assignment removal; 40 native CPU/CUDA FP32/BF16 waveform or patchify/unpatchify comparisons preserve output/stride, state, registration and RNG. 47 existing audio/VAE/configuration tests and five subtests pass. No pretrained-checkpoint E2E or performance claim.

- Unread DiT constructor copies: remove seven ordinary attributes from Wan/causal Wan, Qwen-Image, FLUX/FLUX.2, Cosmos3 and LTX2. Keep constructor arguments, projection bias/domain sizing and parameter-loader closures unchanged. Seven complete module ASTs match after assignment removal; 56 native CPU/CUDA FP32/BF16 constructor comparisons preserve registration, parameter metadata, ATen calls and RNG across flag/domain/epsilon settings. 168 existing model tests and 56 subtests pass. No multi-rank, full-checkpoint E2E or performance claim.

- MOVA image-position state: remove unused model copies and an empty placeholder, retaining the configuration fields and all checkpoint parameters. title: [DeepSeek-V4.1] Use num_stages=1 for the hc_mix stats partial kernel
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> (auto generated by Claude)

## Motivation

In low-latency DeepSeek-V4.1 decode, `_hc_mix_stats_partial_kernel` runs on the mHC stats side stream next to the MoE sublayer. On a 4x B300 bs1 profile (DSpark verify, M=6), it takes 14.3 us next to attention but 36.5 us next to the MoE GEMMs. The MoE post then waits on it for a median of 8.1 us per layer, about 6% of the forward.

The kernel used `num_stages=2` for every M except 64..384 on Blackwell. With 2 stages the tf32x3 loop is a long serial chain per warp, so it is slow on its own and any kernel sharing the SM stretches it further.

## Modifications

Use `num_stages=1` for the partial kernel on CUDA at every M, and drop `_num_stages_for`. AMD keeps 2.

## Accuracy

`num_stages` only changes the order in which memory is issued, not the arithmetic. Outputs of stages 1/2/3 are bitwise identical for M in 1..200 on both B300 and H200. A row computed alone also matches the same row inside a batch, so batch invariance is unchanged.

## Benchmark

Partial kernel time in us, K=20480, standalone:

| M | B300 s2 -> s1 | H200 s2 -> s1 |
|---|---|---|
| 1-8 | 13.6 -> 4.6 | 14.9 -> 5.6 |
| 18-48 | 25.9 -> 6.4 | 28.3 -> 7.6 |
| 52-60 | 49.9 -> 11.2 | 42-54 -> 13.8 |
| 512 | 224 -> 56 | 266 -> 56 |
| 4096 | 1206 -> 525 | 1383 -> 576 |

s3 and s4 are slower than s2 at every M. With an SM-occupying kernel running on another stream (M=1-8), s2 goes to 36 us on B300 and 39 us on H200, while s1 stays at 6-7.5 us.

title: Fuse MiMo verification RoPE and KV cache writes
author: leonardHONG
body:
## Motivation

Reduce KV preparation overhead during MiMo DFlash target verification.

## Modifications

- Fuse BF16 RoPE, V scaling, and KV-cache writes into one kernel while preserving the existing BF16 operation order.
- Reuse attention-backend KV buffers and SWA slot mapping in the MiMo verification path.
- Use the existing tensor matcher and typed launch helpers to define the dtype and layout contract.

## Performance

MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL + DFlash on 8×B300, TP8, FA4/page128, MNNVL, KV capacity 32768, concurrency 1. Both arms use the same frozen random-topic essay inputs: 8000 input tokens, 1024 output tokens, `ignore_eos=True`, 3 warmups followed by 96 measured requests. One fresh service per arm; timing without a profiler.

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Improvement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Decode throughput | 302.70 tok/s | 318.04 tok/s | **5.07%** |
| E2E throughput | 285.60 tok/s | 298.77 tok/s | **4.61%** |

E2E includes prefill. Decode timing starts after the first token emission. Baseline: `6e7beace14`; measured candidate: `cdc52f549e`.

## Validation

- All 96 measured output token sequences and speculative acceptance/proposal/verification counters and histograms match the baseline.
- All measured requests have real draft rejection; acceptance is 21.38% in both arms.
- GPU checks cover int32/int64 KV-slot indices, int64 positions, V scaling, KV padding, and CUDA Graph replay with updated positions and slots.

Reproduction commands, pinned model/draft and dependency versions, benchmark scripts, and the existing GPU check: https://gist.github.com/leonardHONG/b55f9d6d4045db6fa8e4fd939b88bf67.

title: [diffusion] perf: decode plain base64 MiniMax-H3 materials without a per-character loop
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-H3 writes base64 material URIs (Ref2VA references, keyframes, reference audio) to a local file on the HTTP path, before the request is queued. The payload was validated and decoded one character at a time in Python. A reference image at a 2048-px short edge is a ~14.5 MB PNG, about 19 M base64 characters: 3.53 s per request on the B300 host's Xeon 6787P, all of it inside the client's measured latency.

## Modifications

- A payload that is plain base64 text (the standard or URL-safe alphabet, then at most two `=`) is decoded window by window: the same 1 Mi-character windows and the same `_decode_base64_chunk` as before, one interpreter step per window instead of per character.
- Payloads with percent escapes or whitespace, which material URIs may carry, and every malformed payload, keep the per-character path. Accepted inputs, error messages, and partial-file cleanup are unchanged.
- The two paths share the length and padding checks (`_check_base64_size`).

## Accuracy Tests

The decoded file is byte-identical to the per-character path. Unit tests (`test/unit/test_minimax_h3_media.py`, 43 passed):
- Both paths agree on standard, URL-safe, and unpadded payloads at sizes that cross window boundaries (windows shrunk to 16 characters).
- Each invalid payload (empty, bad length, over-padding, data after padding, a character outside the alphabet) raises the same error and leaves no partial file.
- Escaped and whitespace payloads still decode.
- A plain payload never reaches the per-character iterator.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- Decode of a 14.5 MB PNG reference: 3.53 s → 0.058 s.
- Ref2VA end-to-end client latency, 50 steps, 2 GPUs, Ulysses 2, all else equal: −0.75 s on 4×H200 and −0.85 s on 4×B300. The output MP4 is byte-identical.

title: [Diffusion] Fix int32 offset overflow in the Ulysses packed-QKV pack kernel
author: saatwiknagpal
body:
## Motivation

With Ulysses SP, `_pack_qkv_destination_major_kernel` packs each rank's q/k/v rows for all heads using int32 offsets. Once a rank packs more than 2^31 elements (`rows*3*H*D`), the offsets wrap: part of the output is never written and attention reads garbage. When q/k/v are views of a fused qkv projection, the load offsets wrap too.

Boundary for MiniMax-H3 (H=56, D=128): 99,865 rows per rank. A stock 15 s Ref2VA request at 1312x736 packs 358,667 rows, so Ulysses 2 (179,334 rows/rank) renders pure noise while Ulysses 4 works. At Ulysses 2, 8 s works, 9 s breaks partway, and 10 s or longer is noise.

## Modifications

Add an `IDX64` constexpr, as in `wan_causal_cache_triton.py`: the launcher picks int64 offsets only when the output or a strided q/k/v view can pass 2^31 elements. Smaller shapes keep the int32 kernel. Add one regression test that fails before the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

- H3 Ref2VA 15 s at 1312x736, Ulysses 2 on 2xB200: stock is noise on all 362 frames (SSIM 0.17 vs the Ulysses-4 render). With the fix, SSIM is 0.95, the expected cross-degree difference. Peak memory is unchanged. (Run with an always-int64 build, which takes the same path at this shape.)
- `test_layout.py`: the new test fails on stock (illegal memory access) and passes with the fix; it covers the output, the q/k/v views, and both passing 2^31. All other tests pass.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B200, H=56, D=128, mean +- std over 8 interleaved fresh-process runs of 100 reps each (ms).

| rows, world size | stock | fix |
|---|---|---|
| 89,667, 4 | 1.152 +- 0.004 | 1.153 +- 0.002 (+0.1%) |
| 44,834, 8 | 0.584 +- 0.000 | 0.586 +- 0.000 (+0.3%) |
| 41,750, 8 | 0.545 +- 0.000 | 0.547 +- 0.000 (+0.4%) |
| 179,334, 2 | n/a (overflows) | 2.548 +- 0.006 |

Always-int64 offsets cost +9.5 to +10.5% at the same shapes in the same run, hence the `IDX64` switch.

title: [diffusion] perf: pipeline MiniMax-H3's Ulysses exchange against attention over the copy engine
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

With Ulysses, every MiniMax-H3 block exchanges q/k/v before dense attention and the output after it. Both exchanges run on SMs: an NCCL send/recv for q/k/v, and SM copies for the output. They sit between kernels that keep every SM busy (FlashAttention is ~63% of a denoise step on 2×H200), so their time is fully exposed.

## Modifications

Four commits. Each one is bit-identical to the sequential exchange.

1. **Copy-engine all-to-all with head-group pipelining** (`ipc_a2a_multi.py`, `_minimax_h3_pipelined_dense_attention`).
   - The transport is the two-rank `ipc_a2a` design widened to N same-host ranks: each rank writes its chunk straight into its peers' staging buffers with device-to-device copies on the copy engine, and a per-peer sequence flag orders data before flag.
   - Pipelining: group g's copies run while group g−1 attends; each group attends on its own stream; stream memory operations (`cuStreamWriteValue32` / `cuStreamWaitValue32`) order copies and kernels without holding an SM.
   - It falls back to the sequential exchange when any rank lacks peer access or stream memory operations (agreed across the group before any handle exchange), during graph capture, under `torch.compile`, and for other attention backends, VSA and ring.
2. **QK-norm + RoPE writes straight into the exchange.** The out-of-place QK-norm kernel writes each destination block's normalized q/k, plus v, in place of the in-place norm followed by a pack. Blocks for this rank go straight into its own receive slot, so they skip a device-to-device copy. Groups are produced in order, so the norm of later groups overlaps the attention of earlier ones.
3. **Each head group is merged into the output as it arrives.** Group streams write this rank's rows, and then each peer's, directly into the final tensor. This replaces the trailing merge kernel and the own-rank output copy.
4. **On by default.** `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ULYSSES_PIPELINE_GROUPS` now defaults to `-1`:
   - it picks 7 groups for MiniMax-H3's 56 heads at Ulysses 2, 4 and 8;
   - when the buffers (11 × rows per rank × heads × head_dim; 3.9 GB for Ref2VA at Ulysses 2) would not fit on some rank, every rank keeps the sequential exchange;
   - `0` disables it, and `N ≥ 2` forces N groups.

   `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_IPC_A2A_MULTI` (the plain all-to-all over the copy engine) stays opt-in. The cookbook's configuration notes describe the default.

## Accuracy Tests

- The MP4 md5 matches main for T2VA (Ulysses 2 and 4) and Ref2VA (Ulysses 2) after every commit.
- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/single_test_file/test_ipc_a2a_multi_gpu.py` (new; passes at 2 and 4 ranks on the final commit) checks, byte for byte:
  - the pipelined attention against the sequential exchange, over repeated calls (slot alternation);
  - the fill path;
  - the automatic group count;
  - a head count the groups cannot split, which must decline;
  - the N-rank exchange against NCCL.

Unrelated to this PR: `test_ipc_a2a_2_gpu.py` fails the same way on plain main ("AllToAll4D never took the IPC path").

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Client end-to-end latency, 4×H200, 50 steps, `--performance-mode speed`, eager, median of 2 requests, G=7. Arms are interleaved on one box: adjacent columns ran back to back. The box drifts ~0.3% across sessions, so compare within a row only.

| Case | main | 1: pipeline | 2: + fused QK-norm | 3: + per-group merge |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| T2VA 5 s, 2 GPUs, Ulysses 2 | 144.33 s | 142.24 s (−1.45%) | −0.62% vs 1 | 141.33 s (−0.42% vs 2, 141.92 s) |
| Ref2VA 5 s, 2 GPUs, Ulysses 2 (with #43117) | 223.19 s | 221.11 s (−0.93%) | −0.79% vs 1 | 219.97 s (one arm, not paired with 2) |
| T2VA 5 s, 4 GPUs, Ulysses 4 | 73.81 s | 72.55 s (−1.71%) | −0.78% vs 1 | 72.23 s (flat vs 2, 72.18 s) |

- **4: on by default.** With no environment variable set, the pipeline picks G=7 and runs as fast as the explicit G=7 arms: T2VA Ulysses 2 141.27 s (141.33 s with G=7), Ulysses 4 72.20 s (72.23 s). Outputs are md5-equal to main.
- **All four commits against main, one interleaved pass, no env:** T2VA Ulysses 2 144.80 → 141.32 s (−2.4%), Ulysses 4 74.19 → 72.23 s (−2.6%). For Ref2VA the chain of paired steps above gives about −1.7% on top of #43117.

- **Per-layer budget, Ref2VA at Ulysses 2 after commit 1 (ms):** wall 88.38, made up of the compute union 87.45, exposed exchange 0.58 and idle 0.36. The copy engine moves 2.53 ms/layer underneath the attention.
- **Why the gains are below the exposed time:** the H200s sit at their 700 W cap during denoise, so part of the freed SM time comes back as a lower clock.

Current head `2509d740d3`, based on main `47eeddcd18`. Stack predecessor: #43168. This PR targets `main` after its stack predecessor merged.

## Motivation

`UnifiedSWAAllocatorBase` (`--enable-unified-memory` with a hybrid sliding-window model) filtered every segment free by swa liveness with a boolean mask (`reps[swa_v2p > 0]`). A mask index runs `nonzero`, which copies its count to the host and blocks the scheduler until the in-flight forward drains, so under the overlap scheduler the next batch is prepared only after the GPU went idle. In gpt-oss-20b serving traces (SM90, page size 256) the free of tokens that left the window (`free_swa_segment`) and the request release (`_release_page_reps` at `free_group_end`) issued about 2.6 such syncs per prefill. Prefill cycles ran +1.3..+3.3% (speculative) and +2.5..+7.0% (non-speculative) longer than with the paged SWA allocator at matched batch size, all of it GPU idle.

## Modifications

Two-pool allocation reclaim flushes the deferred FULL-only segment queue before sizing eviction. A regression test fills that queue alone and verifies allocation succeeds without evicting the tree.

The paged SWA allocator frees the same segments with a fixed shape: its callers split a kv row by host bookkeeping, and it trusts that split. The unified callers make the same split: `free_kv_row_segments` sends `[swa_dead_lo, swa_evicted_seqlen)` through `free_full_segment`, the tree picks `FreeDeviceKV` or `FreeDeviceKVFullOnly` per node, and the out-of-window free releases only tokens above `swa_dead_lo`, with a cursor that only moves up. So `free_swa_segment` and `free_segment` now free every page they are handed on the swa side, and `free_full_segment` releases the full side only, through its own deferred list for the free group (`full_free_group`), which `flush_deferred_full_frees` also drains when Mamba state needs memory. Each checks its premise with `expect`, as the paged allocator's `swa.peer_mapped` does: asynchronous, and loud from `SGLANG_INVARIANT_CHECK=warn` up. The two invariants are declared in `allocator/swa.py` beside the paged allocator's: the registry refuses a name it already holds, and a test fixture that patches `sys.modules` makes the next test import `unified_hybrid_swa` again. Page size 1 takes the same path. The set-shaped `free()` and `free_swa()` keep their filter; `RecoverSWAWithLockedFull` relies on it.

A second out-of-window free over the same range was filtered to a no-op. No caller issues one; under strict checks it is now reported instead.

Tests (CPU):
- `test_segment_frees_dispatch_no_data_dependent_shape` records, with a `TorchDispatchMode`, every op whose output shape depends on values (a boolean-mask index, `nonzero`, `unique`, `item`). Before: three mask indexes at page size 1 and at 4. After: none, and both sides' capacity comes back.
- `test_a_double_ratchet_is_reported` (replaces `test_double_ratchet_is_filtered_not_crashed`) and `test_a_full_only_free_of_a_bound_swa_page_is_reported` fail before (nothing raises) and pass after.
- The test that reclaims full-attention KV for Mamba state (on a model with both Mamba state and sliding-window layers) and the eviction fixture name the new list.
- `test_importing_the_module_again_registers_nothing_twice` runs the module again as such a fixture does: a duplicate-invariant error before, none after (`test_lmcache_component_cursors.py` errors in 3 of its 4 cases with the invariants in `unified_hybrid_swa` and passes with them in `allocator/swa.py`).
- The unified-memory CPU tests pass with `SGLANG_INVARIANT_CHECK=2` exactly as without it, so none of them frees an already released sliding-window page through a segment free.

## Accuracy Tests

Earlier combined stack `b550cacde6` adds a test-fixture correction in #43326: the Gemma4 read-stream fixture declares its FULL address space, and the HiSparse registry test uses real `CacheInitParams` for the retained-window calculation. Both complete test files pass locally with GPUs hidden: 4 Gemma4 tests and 26 registry tests. Pre-commit passed. The five descendant patches are unchanged (`git range-diff`); this follow-up changes no production code. The earlier 455-test run did not cover these two files; GitHub CI has not yet been revalidated for this head.

Validation before the test-fixture follow-up, on combined stack `4cf27a551c`: 455 tests and 921 subtests passed on B300, plus the two widened-history regressions against Rust TreeCore. The new FULL-fallback metadata cases cover eager execution and CUDA graph replay. New allocation-reclaim, explicit-prefill and JIT-reuse regressions fail on the previous code and pass with the fixes. These are combined-stack checks, not independent model reruns of each PR.

The measurements in this section are historical results from before this rebase, at the revisions/configurations stated below. Current combined-stack validation is linked above.

SM90, TP1, gpt-oss-20b, no speculation, radix cache, overlap scheduler, CUDA graphs on, `--mem-fraction-static 0.8`. Baseline: the default pool. Unified: `--enable-unified-memory`. Every server ran with the per-step pool checks and the allocator invariants on (`SGLANG_ENABLE_STRICT_MEM_CHECK_DURING_BUSY=1 SGLANG_CHECK_KV_PAGE_INVARIANTS=1 SGLANG_INVARIANT_CHECK=1`), so a free that this change gets wrong stops the server or is reported. These ran on this commit over main 7224fce1b5. GSM8K, all 1314 test questions, 5-shot, greedy:

| page size | backend | baseline | unified |
|---|---|---|---|
| 256 | triton | 0.502 | 0.515 |
| 256 | fa3 | 0.553 | 0.558 |
| 1 | triton | 0.533 | 0.536 |
| 1 | fa3 | 0.566 | 0.535 |

gpt-oss-20b's GSM8K score moves by several points between identical runs (up to ~6 in our runs of one configuration), and three of the four rows favour the unified pool.

Under the same checks, two load tests at page size 256: one with a shared prefix (one 4096-token system prompt, 192 requests with 128-token questions and 2048 output tokens, concurrency 192) and one with long outputs (100 requests, 512 input / 4096 output tokens, concurrency 128). Every request completed on both arms and both backends, and no server reported a leak, double free, invariant violation or illegal memory access.

GPU unit tests for unified memory: 4104 passed, 0 failed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The measurements in this section are historical results from before this rebase, at the revisions/configurations stated below. Current combined-stack validation is linked above.

`bench_serving` with random prompts at concurrency 64, in two shapes: 2048 input / 512 output tokens (200 prompts) and 8192 input / 64 output tokens (100 prompts). gpt-oss-20b, no speculation, page size 256, radix cache, overlap scheduler, CUDA graphs on, `--mem-fraction-static 0.55`. author: caihuali95
body:

* #43170
* #43168

Current head `7006d22143`, based on main `ba50ea3d77`. Stack predecessor: #43170. This PR targets `main` after its stack predecessor merged.

## Motivation

`flashinfer_gdn_prefill_default` declined whenever `enable_page_major_kv_layout` was set. `--enable-unified-memory` runs page-major, so Qwen3.5 GDN prefill stayed on the Triton chunk kernels there while the default pool on the same GPU auto-selected FlashInfer. On SM90 (Qwen3.5-9B, page size 256, no speculative decoding) unified prefill cycles ran +1.24..+1.41% longer than the default pool's at matched batch size, all of it GPU time: the Triton chunk kernels cost +17.8 ms per cycle where the FlashInfer GDN kernels cost 10.7 ms. End to end that was -1.1..-1.5% throughput on every attention backend.

## Modifications

Explicit `--linear-attn-prefill-backend flashinfer` is accepted by the page-major gate, matching automatic GDN selection. The test covers this explicit configuration.

`layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py`: page-major no longer disqualifies the FlashInfer prefill. For prefill the layout does not matter: `forward_extend` gathers a non-contiguous pool's conv and SSM state into contiguous per-sequence copies before any prefill kernel runs and scatters them back after (`needs_state_gather`), so FlashInfer's extend sees the same contiguous, identity-indexed state as on the default pool. Decode and verify are unaffected; their backends resolve separately (verify follows decode, Triton by default).

Test (`test_gdn_prefill_backend_policy.py`): `test_selects_flashinfer_for_a_page_major_pool` (SM100 with a bf16 state, SM90 with an fp32 state) fails before (the policy returns None) and passes after; page-major leaves `test_rejects_unvalidated_runtime_modes`.

Earlier combined stack `b550cacde6` adds a test-fixture correction in #43326: the Gemma4 read-stream fixture declares its FULL address space, and the HiSparse registry test uses real `CacheInitParams` for the retained-window calculation. These are combined-stack checks, not independent model reruns of each PR.

title: Clamp default decode CUDA graph max_bs to max_running_requests
author: cctry
body:
When --max-running-requests is small (e.g. single-request latency tiers) and --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode is unset, the GPU-capacity default (up to 512) dwarfs the running batch. The server then captures - and reserves memory for - batch sizes it can never replay.

This clamps the default to the running limit. An explicit --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode keeps its existing semantics, and the materialized capture list follows via the existing max_bs filter.

## Test plan
- New CPU unit test test/registered/unit/server_args/test_decode_graph_max_bs_default.py (3 cases: clamp to 1 with bs == [1]; default kept at 512 with no running limit; explicit 64 preserved) - passes; the clamp case fails without the fix.
- Existing test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py - passes except one pre-existing upstream failure (TestDcpCommBackendDefault::test_a5_npu_supports_dcp), which also fails on clean origin/main and never invokes the touched code path.

title: Overlap scheduler startup with the data parallel controller
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

With attention data parallelism, `Engine._launch_scheduler_processes` starts the data parallel controller process first, and the controller then spawns every scheduler process on the node. The schedulers only begin importing and initializing after the controller has finished its own setup (ZMQ sockets, worker port broadcast, dispatcher wiring), so the two startup phases run back to back instead of overlapping. On a multi-GPU node this adds the controller's whole setup time to the critical path of server startup.

## Modifications

- `engine.py`: when the DP controller is used, attention DP is enabled, and neither elastic EP nor EP join is in use, the launcher pre-spawns the per-rank scheduler processes itself, in parallel with the controller. Each child is started with `run_scheduler_process_with_init_pipe` and a duplex pipe; the controller receives the `(pid, pipe)` map as `prelaunched_schedulers`. In that mode the launcher already knows the scheduler PIDs, so it skips `SCHEDULER_PIDS_ARG`, and on follower nodes `block_until_scheduler_exits` runs a `SubprocessWatchdog` over the pre-spawned processes so that a scheduler crash still tears the node down.
- `data_parallel_controller.py`: `DataParallelController` accepts an optional `prelaunched_schedulers` map. `launch_tensor_parallel_group` keeps computing rank, GPU id, port args and display ranks exactly as before, but when a pre-spawned process exists for `(pp_rank, tp_rank)` it sends those arguments down the pipe instead of calling `mp.Process`. The new `run_scheduler_process_with_init_pipe` target blocks on that pipe, then runs the unchanged scheduler entrypoint with the same pipe for its ready reply, so the ready handshake is unchanged. `run_data_parallel_controller_process` reports the pre-spawned PIDs and, because it does not own those processes, waits on their pipes instead of joining them.
- Launches without attention DP, with elastic EP, or on EP joiners take the existing path and are unchanged. `RayDataParallelController` is unaffected: the new parameter is keyword-optional and defaults to `None`.
- `test_data_parallel_controller.py`: the bare `__new__` controller fixture in `test_controller_collects_all_scheduler_sources` sets `prelaunched_schedulers = None`, because `launch_tensor_parallel_group` now reads that attribute (the file's docstring asks for exactly this when a new attribute is read).

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no numerics are touched. Scheduler initialization runs the same entrypoint with the same arguments.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Startup only; steady-state serving is unchanged. The scheduler import now overlaps the controller's setup instead of following it. No benchmark numbers are attached to this PR.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). No new unit test: the change is in multi-process launch wiring and is exercised by the existing DP-attention server tests in CI.
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed: no user-facing flag or behavior changes.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Not attached, see above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Feat] cp: Enable GLM-5.3 Flash interleave BCG with batched prefill and DFlash2
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

Enable breakable prefill CUDA graphs by default for GLM-5.3 Flash interleave CP, and replay captured token shapes across multiple prefix-free requests. This builds on #44022's shared CP/BCG policy.

## Changes

- Organize CP BCG helpers under `layers/cp/bcg/`: shared capture/replay code in `bcg.py`, interleave-specific support/metadata/positions/token IDs in `interleave_bcg.py`, and zigzag shard geometry in `zigzag_bcg.py`. Deduplicate common support checks, token alignment, and the capture-support wrapper.
- Register `(interleave, dsa)` for GLM-5.3 Flash with CP = TP > 1 and DP/PP/EP = 1. Keep graph defaults in the shared CUDA graph policy and honor explicit disabling.
- Keep fixed-address CP-local embeddings/positions and rank-major token IDs. KPool retains global positions; KPool and KDA graph breaks consume the live request layout.
- Admit multi-request replay based on the concatenated token count and aligned local shard capacity. Prefix-cache-hit, multimodal, and non-bucket batches still use eager CP. Draft prefill remains eager.
- Switch the registered GLM CP test to `DFLASH`, `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2`, and draft attention `fa4`; inherit the default prefill capture ceiling (the 2048-limit change is handled separately in #45473), with `--mem-fraction-static 0.85`.
- Run the DFLASH draft under ordinary TP for CP targets, keeping its model, attention backend, KV pool, and KV memory budget consistent with the target's borrowed TP-sharded LM head. Preserve attention-DP isolation.
- Cover uneven multi-request token boundaries and draft DP isolation. Restore the fused draft placement test to its base version and remove the requested CP draft topology test.

## Validation

title: [Mamba] Describe the track snapshot dtype by its kernel instead of fp32
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

`MambaAttnBackendBase._track_mamba_state_extend` documents the in-kernel `h_track_buf` snapshot as fp32. The method itself does not depend on that: it copies the selected snapshot rows into `ssm_states` with an index assignment, which casts into the state dtype on the way in. The in-tree snapshot writers allocate fp32 because that is the dtype their extend kernels keep the recurrent state in, so the docstring happens to be true for them, but it reads as a contract. An extend kernel that keeps its recurrent state in another dtype can hand that buffer over directly, and a subclass author reading the current docstring would instead add an unnecessary up-cast before calling.

## Modifications

Docstring only. `_track_mamba_state_extend` now says the snapshot arrives in the kernel's native state dtype rather than promising fp32. No code changes.

title: [Fix] Unblock CUDA graph startup for hybrid parallelism
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

`test_hybrid_dp_ep_tp_mtp.py::Test03` times out during server startup in the weekly H200 suite. With TP=8, `--moe-dense-tp-size 1`, and FlashInfer all-reduce fusion, prefill CUDA graph capture stalls at the 28-token shape. The capture batch bypasses eager padding, leaving different token-shard widths across ranks. The same failure appears in the [October 4 weekly run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37166616108/job/111330769101) and the August 16 run, on different H200 runners.

Running the rest of the file also exposed a startup OOM in Test12 (V3, attention DP8, DeepEP). DeepGEMM's warmup memory estimate excludes FP8 scale buffers: it estimates 8.375 GiB for a masked GEMM executor whose buffers actually need about 8.485 GiB. With 8.459 GiB available, decode graph initialization fails while allocating the output buffer. Test17 exposes a second omission: DeepGEMM also needs a 112 MiB temporary TMA-aligned LHS scale copy on Hopper. Its executor buffers fit into the 8.498 GiB available, but scale conversion runs out of memory.

## Modifications

- Round prefill capture buckets up using the existing CUDA graph parallelism alignment helper, then sort and deduplicate them. Capture buffers and replay padding use the same aligned buckets. A custom maximum such as 28 tokens rounds up to 32 rather than losing its coverage.
- Include FP32 token and block scale buffers and architecture-specific scale-conversion workspace in all FP8 DeepGEMM warmup memory estimates. Hopper needs a temporary TMA-aligned LHS copy; Blackwell needs packed UE8M0 scales, RHS broadcasting, and any grouped packing fallback buffers. MUSA does not receive the Hopper workspace allowance. The existing budget check can then choose a smaller warmup range before allocating the buffers.
- Add regression coverage for TP8, attention DP, configurations that do not require gathered token buffers, capture/replay at an unaligned custom ceiling, and memory estimates against the actual buffers constructed by every warmup executor and the strided storage needed for scale conversion. The memory test uses meta tensors and includes non-aligned scale dimensions and the V3 OOM shape across Hopper, Blackwell, and MUSA. Remove the redundant warmup-memory comment.

Keep the weekly file's models, launch flags, and accuracy thresholds.

## Accuracy Tests

- **All 60 configurations passed across batches before the architecture-specific review follow-up**, retaining the weekly file's models, launch flags, 64-example / 32-thread MMLU evaluation, and `score > 0.48` threshold. Scores range from **0.546875 to 0.921875**, with request error rate **0** in every configuration.
- Test00–Test09 passed after capture-bucket alignment. They use the BF16 Lite model and are unaffected by the FP8 memory-budget changes. With the Hopper scale-workspace fix, Test10–Test16 passed together (**7 tests**) and Test17–Test59 passed together (**43 tests**).
- Before fixing alignment, Test03 reproducibly stalled at the 28-token capture shape. After alignment it scored **0.625**. Before the budget fixes, Test12 failed while allocating executor buffers and Test17 failed while converting scales, each in both startup attempts. Both now pass without changing launch flags or reducing test coverage.
- Prefill helper suite: **22 tests passed**. The expanded memory regression passes **36 cases**: six executor variants, two shapes, and three architecture settings. It measures meta-tensor storage and live scale-conversion allocations, including the grouped packing fallback. The review follow-up fails 12 Blackwell/MUSA cases on the preceding implementation and passes afterward.
- Real Blackwell scale-conversion probes pass for all three FP8 executors with both direct packing and the grouped fallback, allowing for CUDA allocator rounding. The review follow-up preserves Hopper budgets exactly in **24 comparisons**; the 60-configuration GPU suite was not rerun after this follow-up.
- Applicable pre-commit checks passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Prefill graph capture for the original failing configuration completed in approximately 17 seconds after alignment. No throughput benchmark was run.

title: [Perf] Enable fast-math for JIT activations on Blackwell
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

On Blackwell the JIT activation kernels are built without fast-math. For SiLU, `x / (1 + expf(-x))` then compiles to an IEEE division. In the SASS (sm_103a, default 16-element vector), every element gets its own `BSSY`/`BSYNC` region: `MUFU.EX2` → `MUFU.RCP` → Newton `FFMA`s → `FCHK` → conditional `CALL` to the division slow path. That is 16 `FCHK`s and 16 `CALL`s per thread, so the elements run back to back instead of interleaving (~46 ns per element on B300). At decode sizes there are too few warps to hide this, and SiLU-and-mul costs 1.7–1.8 µs/layer even for a single token.

The precise-math choice was not specific to activation. The AOT sgl-kernel stopped using `-use_fast_math` for SM100 builds when Blackwell FP8 blockwise GEMM landed (#4278, #4376), and #10701 later split AOT `common_ops` into an SM90 fast-math build and an SM100+ precise build. The JIT activation (#22094) mirrored that policy. Hopper has always run these kernels with fast-math.

## Modifications

`get_activation_cuda_cflags()` now returns `["--use_fast_math"]` whenever `is_cuda()`, and `[]` otherwise. That drops the SM100+ exception. Fast-math turns the IEEE division into a branch-free approximate one, uses the approximate `expf`, and flushes subnormals to zero.

**Affected kernels:** everything built with these flags.
- The gated activations (`silu_and_mul`, `gelu_and_mul`, `gelu_tanh_and_mul`).
- `relu2` when called with its default `fast_math=True`. Callers that need BF16 subnormals already pass `fast_math=False` (e.g. Cosmos3).
- `situ_and_mul`.

The rounding variants (`*_with_activation_rounding`) still build the precise `rounded_activation` module. HIP still gets no fast-math. MUSA previously received `--use_fast_math`; it now follows whatever `is_cuda()` returns under `torchada`, which I have not tested.

## Accuracy Tests

**Kernel numerics.** Outputs on Blackwell are **not** bitwise identical to main. The difference is almost entirely flush-to-zero of BF16 subnormal results: BF16 shares fp32's exponent range, so BF16 subnormals are fp32 subnormals.

Exhaustive check of SiLU-and-mul on B300 over all 65,536 gate bit patterns, fast-math against precise, with 7 `up` cases (±1, 0.5, 3, randn ×2, randn×100):

| dtype | outputs that differ | what they are |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BF16 | 0.78–1.22% | Precise gives a subnormal and fast-math gives 0, at \|g\| < 1e-36 or g < −80. Over the 47,819 gates in −80 ≤ g, \|g\| ≥ 1e-36 there are 0 differences at `up=1` and one 1-ulp rounding flip with random `up`. |
| FP16 | 1–3 values | 1-ulp rounding flips (FP16 subnormals are normal in fp32, so there is no FTZ effect) |

Against an fp64 reference rounded to BF16 (`up=1`), precise is correctly rounded on 65,263 / 65,280 finite outputs and fast-math on 64,752. The gap is the flushed subnormals. GELU, GELU-tanh, ReLU² and SiTU were covered by the unit tests below, not by an exhaustive sweep.

**End-to-end.** `test_inkling_small_nvfp4.py` (Inkling-Small-NVFP4, TP4, DSpark speculative decoding, `--enable-deterministic-inference`) asserts bitwise prefill/decode logprob consistency. In this server the JIT SiLU runs in the DSpark draft model. On 4× B300, with #43447 applied:

| build | three KL checks (`avg_kl_div`) | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| this PR (fast-math) | 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 | 3 passed |
| main policy (precise) | 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 | 3 passed |

The earlier CI failure of this test (KL 0.0015) was the main regression from #41887, fixed in #43447 after this branch's last merge of main. On the unfixed base, fast-math and precise both gave the identical KL (0.00013463538375007566 on B300) across four sequential runs.

**Unit tests on B300:**

| test | result |
| --- | --- |
| `kernels/ops/activation/test_activation.py` | 452 passed, 6 skipped |
| `kernels/ops/activation/test_situ_and_mul.py` | 1 passed |
| `kernels/ops/moe/test_situ_and_mul_quant.py` | 1 passed |
| `kernels/ops/diffusion/test_activation.py` | 10 passed |
| `kernels/ops/diffusion/test_cosmos3_edge_fusions.py` | 4 passed, 3 skipped |
| `unit/kernels/test_kernels_namespace.py` | 71 passed |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Setup:** one B300 (sm_103, 148 SMs), BF16 SiLU-and-mul, activation only: 36 disjoint layer buffers captured in one CUDA graph, 20 replays, median of 11 runs. Main and this PR alternated 3× on the same GPU.

| hidden × tokens | main µs/layer | this PR µs/layer | speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2432 × 8 | 1.77 | 1.14 | 1.55x |

title: [Perf] Fuse BF16 writes to native HND KV cache storage
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

With the optional HND KV cache layout (`SGLANG_USE_HND_KVCACHE`), `MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer` writes K/V by advanced indexing (`k_buf[pages, :, offs, :] = cache_k`). That costs several small kernels per layer per step. The existing Triton cache writer can do the same write in one kernel if it is given the destination's real token and head strides.

## Modifications

- `reshape_and_cache_flash` (Triton) takes separate key/value block, token and head strides for the destination, so it can write into a strided view of HND storage. For existing callers with the `[blocks, block_size, heads, dim]` layout, these strides equal the values the kernel previously assumed.
- `MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer` uses `launch_reshape_and_cache_flash` for HND writes on CUDA when the key and value head dims are equal. Inputs have already been cast and viewed to the pool's store dtype at this point, so the write is a plain copy for any KV dtype. Other cases keep the indexing path.
- The default NHD layout is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Standalone cache-writer validation: 20 cases covering both layouts, negative slots, sliding-window destinations and non-contiguous inputs, plus six BF16/FP16/FP8-with-scale regressions that match the original NHD outputs. These GPU checks have not been re-run on this branch.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Standalone B300 BF16 HND cache-write timing:

| Tokens | Indexing writer (µs) | Fused writer (µs) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64 | 10.2 | 1.45 |
| 8192 | 86.64 | 10.18 |

No end-to-end serving throughput change is claimed.

## Checklist

- [x] Repository pre-commit checks pass.
- [ ] Upstream CI and review.

title: [Perf] Route BF16 mixed-batch decode tails through decode attention
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

In ordinary BF16 mixed prefill/decode batches, one-token decode tails run through context attention. In the measured Qwen3-VL workload, enabling mixed chunking therefore reduces concurrency-128 throughput from approximately 3765 to 3201 output tokens/s.

## Modifications

Identify the trailing one-token requests in eligible extend batches. Run context attention for the prefill prefix and the existing fixed-query-length decode kernel for the tail, preserving request order, page-table slices and shared output-buffer reuse. Restrict the split to BF16 causal decoder attention without speculative metadata; retain the existing paths for other batches. No new kernel or launch flag is added.

This change is based directly on upstream main `2e64740442` and has no dependency on the other optimization PRs. Repository pre-commit checks pass on this branch. GPU results below are prior measurements of the extracted implementation, not fresh validation of this new main-based branch. No serving tests were restarted.

## Accuracy Tests

Prior standalone validation: 18 mixed-attention cases covering heterogeneous lengths and output-buffer aliasing; maximum absolute difference 0.001953125. This routing change uses a different attention execution path and is not a bitwise-equivalence claim. Main has since changed surrounding KV metadata code; fresh integration validation on this branch remains outstanding.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Prior one-B300 Qwen3-VL-4B BF16 measurements, nominal 8192-input/1024-output text requests:

| Measurement | Original mixed routing | Split decode tails |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| C128 output tokens/s | 3201.14 | 3777.27 |
| Representative attention batch: 8192 prefill tokens + 128 decode rows | ~3.79 ms | ~1.00 ms |

The serving change is +18.0% for this measured mixed-chunk configuration. Both arms already contained the same GEMM tuning; this is not a clean-main full-stack comparison. Single sweeps used different GPUs and do not establish a general speedup or repeatability bound.

## Checklist

- [x] Record prior numerical and speed validation.
- [x] Keep benchmark and test additions outside the code PR.

title: [KDA] Default safe-gate Blackwell prefill to FlashInfer
author: kpham-sgl
body:
Follow up to #41400: safe-gate KDA models now select FlashInfer prefill by default on SM100/SM103, including Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3-Flash. The choice is resolved once per model runner through the existing linear-attention backend resolver.

The CPU policy test covers model/hardware eligibility, operator overrides, and phase isolation. Its fixture publishes the resolved CUDA graph configuration, fixing the fixture failure from the earlier default-enablement attempt.
