title: Quantized weight-update fixes: Qwen3.5 draft KV budget, UE8M0 partial blocks, mxfp8 fused indexer, NVFP4 input scales
author: yueming-yuan
body:
Stacked on #42820. The model- and format-specific engine fixes miles' p2p weight update needs; #42820 keeps the general engine support.

**Derived state after writes that bypass a model's loader** (moved from #42820, plus one gap the review found):

| fix | symptom | cause |
|---|---|---|
| GemmaRMSNorm `gemma_weight` | Qwen3.5 serves the old norm after a p2p update; fused allreduce kernels read `gemma_weight` | the norm's weight loader derives `gemma_weight = weight + 1`, and p2p, remote-instance, sharded-state and dummy loads write the weight without it; `post_load_weights` now refreshes it |
| `gemma_weight` at every session end | a session whose `direct` or custom load wrote the norm weight kept the old `gemma_weight` | those loads bypass the norm's loader yet mark the session loaded, so `end_weight_update` skipped `post_load_weights`; it now refreshes `gemma_weight` either way |
| GLM-lite NextN post-load | the GLM-4.7-Flash draft skipped its NextN post-load after a p2p update | `post_load_weights` ran the target's path on the draft; the NextN draft now pins `is_nextn=True` |

**Quantized checkpoints.** Four fixes found by running miles' p2p weight-update e2e with quantized rollout checkpoints on GB300 (fp8 block, mxfp8, nvfp4 on GLM-5.2 cut to 5 layers; fp8 on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B cut to 4 layers with its MTP draft). None is specific to p2p: each also hits sglang's own weight update or its startup. One commit each.

| fix | symptom | cause |
|---|---|---|
| EAGLE draft KV budget for Qwen3.5 | the draft's KV pool is allocated outside `mem_fraction_static`; OOM at startup on the 4-layer cut (127.6 GB draft pool, 82 GB left at 0.7) | `_resolve_eagle_aux_hidden_state` reads the draft depth from `num_nextn_predict_layers`; Qwen3.5 names it `mtp_num_hidden_layers`, so the target's per-token cost counted no draft layer |
| UE8M0 scales of non-128-multiple rows | `RuntimeError: shape '[20, 128, 48]' is invalid for input of size 125952` in the weight checker on every GLM-5 fp8 update on Blackwell | `_inverse_transform_scale_ue8m0_impl` viewed the per-row packed scales as whole 128-row blocks; GLM-5's fused q_a + kv_a has 2624 rows |
| mxfp8 shards of the fused indexer | the fused bf16 `wk_weights_proj` off by up to 5e4 after loading an mxfp8 checkpoint with a quantized `wk` | `_load_fused_indexer_wk` dequantized with `block_quant_dequant`, multiplying by the uint8 UE8M0 exponents as integers |
| NVFP4 MoE input scales in the weight check | every NVFP4 MoE update fails the check on `w13_input_scale` / `w2_input_scale` only | they are calibrated activation scales no update carries (miles' quantizer emits `weight`, `weight_scale`, `weight_scale_2`); the checker reset them to random before the update. Now `_skip_weight_check`, as the KV cache scales |

On the draft budget: with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's 10 full-attention layers the unbudgeted draft is a tenth of the KV pool, which fits at 0.6–0.7 and so went unnoticed; the 4-layer cut makes it as large as the target's.

**Tests**
- `unit/model_loader/test_default_model_loader.py`: `gemma_weight` follows a norm weight written without its loader (CPU).
- `unit/model_executor/model_runner_components/test_weight_updater_published_storage.py`: a session whose load bypassed the norm's loader still refreshes `gemma_weight` (CPU); fails on its parent.
- `unit/models/test_glm4_moe_lite_nextn_post_load.py`: the GLM-lite NextN draft runs the NextN post-load (CPU).
- `unit/model_executor/model_runner_components/test_spec_aux_hidden_state.py`: an MTP depth named `mtp_num_hidden_layers` counts as the EAGLE draft's layers (CPU).
- `unit/layers/quantization/test_fp8_utils.py`: the UE8M0 round trip also covers GLM-5's (2624, 6144) (CUDA).
- `unit/models/test_deepseek_fused_indexer_mxfp8.py`: mxfp8 `wk` and `weights_proj` reach the fused param dequantized with their UE8M0 scales (CPU).
- `unit/layers/quantization/test_modelopt_nvfp4_moe_weight_check.py`: the checker skips the NVFP4 MoE input scales and still checks the weight scales (CPU).

On an H200 devbox (`radixark/miles:dev`), all changed test files of this branch and #42820 pass (35 passed, 1 skipped: an SM100-only case). On #42820's head each quantized case fails for its cause: `None == 1`, the `[20, 128, 48]` view error, the fused `wk` mismatch, `w13_input_scale` not skipped.

End to end on GB300 with the UE8M0 fix applied: GLM-5.2 5-layer fp8 compares every fp8 tensor within quantization ULP, `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` included. What remains there is on miles' side: its fp8 / mxfp8 converters quantize the interleaved indexer's `wk`, which sglang keeps in bf16 and the trainer sends in bf16.

title: [Perf] dsv41: Integrate DeepGEMM MegaGate routing
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1 MegaMoE decode and verify spend several launches on the gate GEMM, the sqrtsoftplus top-k and the routing copy; DeepGEMM's `bf16_mega_gate` does this in one kernel.

## Modifications

- `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_GATE` routes MegaMoE decode/verify (up to 2048 rows) through `bf16_mega_gate`, including vision-biased and hash-routed layers and the padded-row mask.
- Unless routed experts are being captured, the gate writes straight into MegaMoE's routing buffer and the pre-dispatch only quantizes (`kCopyTopk`). EPLB static and dynamic placements are applied in-kernel via `to_physical_map`/`logical_count` (dynamic spreads replicas by rank and token instead of `randint`), and the expert distribution recorder reads the buffer. `lp`/`fake` dispatch falls back to the regular router.
- `SGLANG_SIMULATE_*` keeps the gate on: the balanced override runs after it, masking padded rows and applying the routed scale in its one launch.
- Tests: `test_mega_gate.py` (kernel vs reference under CUDA graph replay), a masked/scaled case in `test_round_robin_ep_balance.py`, and MegaGate unit tests in `test_mega_moe_deepgemm_api.py`.

title: [diffusion] perf: tile MiniMax-H3's indexed modulation kernels by 2048 columns
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-H3's AdaLN modulation (`indexed_scale_shift_bf16_`) and gated residual (`indexed_gate_bf16[_]`) Triton kernels launched one program per row with `BLOCK_N = next_power_of_2(hidden)`. For H3's 5376-wide rows that is 8192 lanes per program, and 37.5% of them are masked off. Each kernel runs twice per DiT block.

## Modifications

- Both kernels take a 2-D grid of rows × 2048-column tiles (`BLOCK_N = min(2048, next_power_of_2(hidden))`, 4 warps).
- The kernels are elementwise, so every output element is computed exactly as before.

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_indexed_modulation.py` (new) checks both kernels against the same arithmetic written in torch, byte for byte, including the in-place gate. It covers 1, 37 and 1025 rows at widths of one tile, a partial tile, whole tiles, and 5376. 24 passed on H200.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Per call on H200, 5376-wide rows; the row counts are H3's Ulysses 2 Ref2VA, Ulysses 2 T2VA and Ulysses 4 T2VA shards:

| Rows | scale_shift before → after | gate before → after |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 24826 | 168.6 → 149.0 µs (−11.6%) | 213.2 → 192.1 µs (−9.9%) |
| 18871 | 129.2 → 114.4 µs (−11.5%) | 163.1 → 147.1 µs (−9.8%) |
| 9436 | 67.4 → 59.1 µs (−12.3%) | 84.4 → 75.9 µs (−10.1%) |

That is about 80 µs per DiT block at Ulysses 2, or ~0.2 s per 50-step Ref2VA request.

title: [Fix] DSA/KDA: Handle MoE padding in hybrid MTP verification
author: Jzz1943
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

GLM-5.3-Flash can fail during MTP verification with TP4/EP4 MegaMoE when Decode CUDA Graph is disabled. MoE pads the token tensors, while attention metadata still describes the valid verification sequences. For example, one 6-token verification sequence is padded to 8 rows.

This mismatch causes KDA verification to fail when reshaping QKV. After correcting that path, DSA KPool verification also fails at `assert bn % num_draft_tokens == 0` because it includes the extra padding rows.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Use the logical verification length from attention metadata to trim KDA QKV and gate inputs before convolution and state updates. Restore zero padding in the output to preserve the downstream tensor layout. Keep the ragged verification path unchanged.
- Restrict DSA KPool key, score, and cache-location writes to the token rows covered by the verification write plan.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

Validated on 4×H200 with GLM-5.3-Flash, BF16 KV, TileLang DSA, MegaMoE, and MTP 5/1/6.

### Reproduction and validation command

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 sglang serve \
  --model-path /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --served-model-name llm \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --ep-size 4 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \
  --max-mamba-cache-size 240 \
  --max-running-requests 48 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 8192 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 48 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang \
  --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \
  --moe-a2a-backend megamoe \
  --speculative-moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \
  --speculative-moe-a2a-backend none \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 5 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --random-seed 42 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8090
```

Before the fix, this configuration fails during startup warmup. After the fix, startup and requests at concurrency 1/3/7/19 pass. The same request checks also pass with `--cuda-graph-backend-decode full`.

### Full GSM8K evaluation

```bash
python -m sglang.test.run_eval \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8090 \
  --api chat \
  --eval-name gsm8k \
  --num-examples 1319 \
  --num-shots 5 \
  --num-threads 8 \
  --repeat 2 \
  --max-tokens 4096 \
  --temperature 0.0 \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_effort": "low"}' \
  --gsm8k-data-path /path/to/gsm8k/test.jsonl
```

The evaluator uses 5 examples as demonstrations and scores the remaining 1,314 examples per repeat. Scores below are the two-repeat means.

| Configuration | GSM8K |
| --- | ---: |
| Before fix, Decode Graph enabled | 96.12% |
| After fix, Decode Graph enabled | 95.70% |
| After fix, Decode Graph disabled | 95.97% |

All post-fix evaluations completed without the verification errors above.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

This is a correctness fix. No dedicated throughput benchmark was run. Mean GSM8K evaluation time per repeat with Decode Graph enabled was 206.03 seconds before the fix and 204.99 seconds after the fix.

title: [cuda_graph] Size dp-local decode graphs by the runner's own gather requirement
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

`get_batch_sizes_to_capture` filters the decode capture buckets by
`get_cuda_graph_batch_size_alignment()`, which multiplies the alignment by
`attn_tp_size` whenever the global `require_gathered_buffer()` is true.
`DecodeCudaGraphRunner` already exempts a dp-local forward from the MLP gather
through `_forward_is_dp_local` (the dense draft that drafts attn-TP-locally
with no cross-DP collective), but the bucket filter never saw that exemption.

So under DP attention a dp-local draft runner keeps only buckets whose
`bs * rows_per_request` is a multiple of `attn_tp_size`, pads a one- or
two-request local batch up to that bucket, and runs its attention kernels at a
shape many times the real batch. A small user-supplied bucket list (for
example `--cuda-graph-bs 1 2 4`) fails startup with
`AssertionError: capture_bs=[]` for the same reason.

## Modifications

- `get_cuda_graph_batch_size_alignment` and `get_batch_sizes_to_capture` take
  an optional keyword `gathered_buffer_required`. Omitting it keeps the global
  `require_gathered_buffer()` behaviour, so every existing caller is unchanged.
- `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.decode_graph_gather_requirements(model_runner)`
  (classmethod) owns the `(mlp_tp_gather, attn_tp_gather)` pair the runner's
  graphs actually need, including the `_forward_is_dp_local` exemption.
  `__init__` derives its instance predicates from it and passes
  `require_gathered_buffer` into both `get_batch_sizes_to_capture` calls.
- `ModelRunner.decode_graph_gather_requirements()` delegates to the runner
  class, so `max_decode_logits_rows` and `BaseRunner._widest_decode_rows` size
  the shared logits buffer and the reduction workspace with the same alignment
  the runner captures with, instead of re-deriving a global one.
- `get_batch_sizes_to_capture` pads `num_max_requests` with the alignment it
  computed (`ceil_align(num_max_requests, mul_base)`) rather than the global
  `get_cuda_graph_max_batch_size`.
- `capture_decode_graph` reports `bs=` from the constructed runner's
  `capture_bs` in the end-of-capture log instead of re-deriving the list with
  global alignment before the runner exists. All in-tree graph runners
  (`DecodeCudaGraphRunner` and its NPU/XPU subclasses, `CPUGraphRunner`)
  expose `capture_bs`.

Behaviour change: a runner whose `_forward_is_dp_local` is true now captures
the plain decode bucket list (1, 2, 4, ...) and replays the graph sized to its
local batch. Every other runner keeps the global alignment.

Tests:

- `test_cuda_graph_setup.py::test_draft_startup_preserves_runner_local_capture_sizes`:
  a dp-local draft runner with `attn_tp_size=16` and buckets `[1, 2, 3, 4, 8]`
  keeps all five and the end-of-capture log reports them. On current main the
  same case fails at startup with `AssertionError: capture_bs=[]`.
- `test_model_runner_decode_rows.py`: the logits-row derivation forwards the
  runner's gather requirement to `get_batch_sizes_to_capture`.
- Ran with CUDA hidden:
  `pytest test/registered/unit/model_executor/model_runner_components/test_cuda_graph_setup.py test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_model_runner_decode_rows.py`
  -> 7 passed; the neighbouring graph-runner unit suites under
  `test/registered/unit/model_executor/` -> 186 passed, 10 skipped.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` -> passed.

## Accuracy Tests

Graph bucket selection only; no kernel or model-forward change. Not run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run here. The effect is confined to dp-local decode runners, whose
attention now runs at the local batch instead of an `attn_tp_size`-aligned
padded one.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Feat] unified-memory: Support asymmetric KV rows
author: caihuali95
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #44973
* #44972
* #44971
* #44970
* #44969
* #43326
* __->__ #43325
* #43171
* #43170
* #43168

Current head `cba61d6e7f`, based on main `1d17066bad`. Stack predecessor: #43171. This PR targets `main` after its stack predecessor merged.

## Motivation

MiMo-V2-Flash has asymmetric K/V rows: 192-wide K heads and 128-wide V heads, on its full-attention and its sliding-window layers alike. `--enable-unified-memory` refuses any such model at boot ("does not yet admit asymmetric K/V rows"), so MiMo serves only on the default pool. That pool splits its memory between the two layer kinds at boot, and under long decodes it retracts requests while the other kind's memory still has room.

## Modifications

Backend rejection reports the applicable allowed set without incorrectly attributing symmetric or MLA failures to asymmetric KV rows.

1. **Admit asymmetric K/V rows on the backends that carry `v_head_dim`** (`8523eb5e81`). The unified pool stores each token's K and V rows side by side in one per-token entry, each at its own offset, so a V row narrower than K needs no pool-level refusal. What remains is a backend property: whether the kernel is told the V width at all. FlashInfer's `paged_kv_t` keeps separate K and V strides but one `head_dim` for both tiles, and sglang's MHA plan path never passes `head_dim_vo`; trtllm_mha refuses unequal QK/V dims. For a model with asymmetric rows, the attention backends that `--enable-unified-memory` accepts therefore narrow to `ASYMMETRIC_KV_BACKENDS`: triton, fa3 and fa4, which pass `layer.v_head_dim` through. fa4 is the resolved default for an asymmetric-K/V model on SM100, so leaving it out would make such a model unbootable in its own default configuration; it also runs on SM90, and the accuracy table below includes it. A speculative draft whose KV is fused into the target's pages follows the same rule (it fuses only when the target's and the draft's backends all carry `v_head_dim`), its share of each entry is sized with the draft's own `v_head_dim`, and the check that every row is 16-byte aligned covers the V row as well as the K row.
2. **Build pools from the actual full/SWA head geometry** (`2aaa913354`). Both hybrid-SWA factories and fused FULL host sizing share `_unified_swa_head_geometry`, so the bytes priced at startup match the entries allocated. The GPU path reads ModelConfig's full/SWA KV-head counts and K/V widths; the NPU compress path retains its HF-config geometry. Non-SWA Mamba/full hosts also carry their actual V width. This removes duplicated geometry decisions and covers asymmetric rows outside the compress-model list.

Tests (CPU): `TestUnifiedSWAHeadGeometry` runs both factories on a model outside the compress list whose sliding-window layers have 8 KV heads against 4 and 128-wide V rows against 192-wide K, and checks the head geometry each hands its pool constructor: `(4, 192, 192, 4, 192, 192)` before this change, `(4, 192, 128, 8, 192, 128)` after it. The test stubs for models with both Mamba-style state and sliding-window layers gain the SWA head fields and `v_head_dim`.

## Accuracy Tests

Earlier combined stack `b550cacde6` adds a test-fixture correction in #43326: the Gemma4 read-stream fixture declares its FULL address space, and the HiSparse registry test uses real `CacheInitParams` for the retained-window calculation. Both complete test files pass locally with GPUs hidden: 4 Gemma4 tests and 26 registry tests. Pre-commit passed. The five descendant patches are unchanged (`git range-diff`); this follow-up changes no production code. The earlier 455-test run did not cover these two files; GitHub CI has not yet been revalidated for this head.

Validation before the test-fixture follow-up, on combined stack `4cf27a551c`: 455 tests and 921 subtests passed on B300, plus the two widened-history regressions against Rust TreeCore. The new FULL-fallback metadata cases cover eager execution and CUDA graph replay. New allocation-reclaim, explicit-prefill and JIT-reuse regressions fail on the previous code and pass with the fixes. These are combined-stack checks, not independent model reruns of each PR.

The measurements in this section are historical results from before this rebase, at the revisions/configurations stated below. Current combined-stack validation is linked above.

The fa4 runs and the GPU unit tests used this PR's current commits over main 7224fce1b5. The triton and fa3 GSM8K runs used the same main, the load tests and the Qwen comparison under Speed Tests the earlier main 4b384df0c9, and both used an earlier form of commit 2 that built the same pools for every model below.

SM90, MiMo-V2-Flash, TP4, no speculation, radix cache, overlap scheduler, CUDA graphs on. Default pool against `--enable-unified-memory`. GSM8K, all 1314 test questions, 5-shot, greedy:

| attention backend | default pool | unified |
|---|---|---|
| triton | 0.839 | 0.838 |
| fa3 | 0.837 | 0.836 |
| fa4 | 0.830 | 0.849 |

With CUDA graphs off, fa4 scores 0.844 on the default pool and 0.830 on the unified pool. In the fa4 runs the unified pool filled every byte that is never written with NaN (`SGLANG_DEBUG_POISON_POOL=1`), so a read of a slot nobody wrote would show up as lost accuracy. Over 1314 questions one run's score has a sampling error of about one point, so both fa4 pairs are within noise.

On both layer kinds, the unified pool stores MiMo's K and V rows at their real 192 and 128 widths, in entries of the size the startup memory sizing computes.

The triton and fa3 MiMo runs used the head of the next PR in this stack, which changes what a speculative draft binds and leaves a run without a draft as it is in this PR.

GPU unit tests for unified memory, on this PR's current commits: 4141 passed, 0 failed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The measurements in this section are historical results from before this rebase, at the revisions/configurations stated below. Current combined-stack validation is linked above.

The same MiMo configuration under two load tests: 100 requests of 512 input / 4096 output tokens at concurrency 128, and 192 requests that share a 4096-token system prompt, each with a 128-token question and 2048 output tokens, at concurrency 192. Every request completed on every server, and no server reported an error.

| attention backend | requests × input / output tokens | default pool req/s | unified req/s | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| triton | 100 × 512 / 4096 | 0.615 | 0.896 | +45.6% |
| triton | 192 × (4096 shared + 128) / 2048 | 0.867 | 1.259 | +45.2% |
| fa3 | 100 × 512 / 4096 | 0.611 | 0.874 | +43.2% |
| fa3 | 192 × (4096 shared + 128) / 2048 | 0.824 | 1.156 | +40.3% |

The gain is capacity: from the same memory, the unified pool lets either layer kind take the bytes the default pool splits between them at boot, so it retracts fewer requests.

A model this PR does not admit is unaffected: Qwen3.5-9B without speculation (200 requests of 2048 input / 512 output tokens at concurrency 64), run back to back on one host with and without this PR, keeps its unified-vs-default-pool req/s gap at −0.4% (fa3), −0.5% (triton) and −0.4% (trtllm_mha), against −0.3%, −0.2% and −0.5% without it. The default pool runs twice per configuration, and its two runs differ by at most 0.2%.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Feat] unified-memory: Fuse drafts with sliding-window and recurrent-state layers
author: caihuali95
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom): * #44973 * #44972 * #44971 * #44970 * #44969 * __->__ #43326 * #43325 * #43171 * #43170 * #43168 Current head `451831a6e6`, based on main `19cb24f1e1`. Stack predecessor: #43325. This PR targets `main` after its stack predecessor merged. ## Motivation Under `--enable-unified-memory` a speculative draft's KV lives inside the target's pages (a fused draft), but only a draft whose layers are all full-attention can fuse: it goes into the full-attention sub-pool. An MTP head with sliding-window layers (MiMo-V2-Flash) or with recurrent state (Inkling's per-depth conv-chain head) declines, and for a hybrid sliding-window or Mamba-hybrid target, main then refuses to boot ("needs the draft's KV fused into the target's pages, but this draft cannot fuse"). So neither model can run NEXTN with `--enable-unified-memory`. ## Modifications The Gemma4 graph and HiSparse registry test fixtures now follow the window-reader and retained-history interfaces. Window layers build clipped decode indices whether placement uses FULL or SWA storage. Cache retention, locks, matching, replay floors and transfers share the widened draft history span in both Python and Rust TreeCore. 1. **Place fused drafts through a registry of sub-pool kinds** (`938efad6b4`). A placement separates what the draft has (full-attention, sliding-window and state layers) from what a sub-pool can carry (a `HostKind`, keyed by sub-pool name). `place_fused_draft` walks the registered kinds over the sub-pools the target builds; the draft's share of each sub-pool's entries, and which part of it each draft runner uses, are keyed by sub-pool. Only "full" is registered in this commit, so every draft places or declines exactly as before. 2. **Register the "swa" kind** (`dc703be11b`). A draft's sliding-window layers fuse into the target's sliding-window sub-pool when the draft's window is no wider than the target's; otherwise they fold into the full sub-pool with their own geometry, or the draft declines when the geometries differ. The sliding-window sub-pool now retains what the draft reads: a multi-layer MTP draft's extend starts a few tokens below the committed length, so `CacheInitParams.swa_retain_window` takes the wider of the target's window and the draft's reach; the tree's locks, prefix matching, backup/load-back and request retention all use that same span. Window layers fuse only on the Triton multi-step draft backend, the one that builds per-step sliding-window KV indices. The draft worker binds `UnifiedDraftSWAKVPool`, routed per layer like the target's composite. A multi-layer draft plans each draft extend once, through its first depth's runner, and a later depth can route window layers the first one does not: `KVLocPlan.has_read_table` and `read_table` now resolve the sub-pool through the reader, as `write_ids` already does, so every depth still shares one table per sub-pool. 3. **Register the "mamba" kind** (`696947f22f`). A per-depth conv-chain MTP head's recurrent state goes into the mamba sub-pool, laid out after the target's own state in each slot's entry. `UnifiedMambaPool.clear_slots`, `copy_from` and `move_kv_cache` act on whole entries, so a radix checkpoint, a slot reset and a compaction move carry the draft's state with the target's. The rebase preserves main's whole-page compaction copy and invokes sibling reset/copy callbacks for ShortConv and NGram state as well. The draft binds `UnifiedDraftMambaPool`, whose own slot ops reset the draft block on decode and draft extend. The memory sizing at startup counts the larger entry. 4. **Per-step sliding-window read indices for the multi-step draft** (`22c9d158b2`). A draft's window layer at step s attends the last `min(seq_len + s + 1, window)` tokens of its own chain, which no existing builder produced: a window draft layer reached the Triton decode kernel without window indices. `generate_draft_decode_window_kv_indices` is the window-clipped sibling of `generate_draft_decode_kv_indices`, selects FULL or SWA addresses through the runner's reader, and fills both an eager buffer and a persistent buffer for CUDA graph replay; the captured draft extend builds these indices too. 5. **Per-step sliding-window write target** (`dcb671120b`). Each per-step backend took its sliding-window write ids as a prefix of the whole draft window, which is laid out step-minor per row, so eager window writes landed in other steps' slots and the captured path had no target. Each step now binds its own columns of the iteration's write window in eager, capture and replay. 6. **Three fixes that also affect the default pool.** The Triton extend kernel narrows its int8 custom mask to i1 before combining it (`b3102250ff`): with both a custom mask (speculative verify) and a `score_mod` (Inkling's relative bias), Triton failed to build the kernel. `SWAKVPool.get_v_head_dim` answers from whichever side has layers (`a3f8458c59`): an MTP depth whose block is sliding-window has an empty full side and raised `IndexError` at backend construction. The Inkling MTP head reports its window the way the trunk does (`7ed6dfa304`): it ran one token wider than the trunk's window layers. Tests (CPU unless noted): window, state and fold placement rows, including the declines; per-runner binding against a clipped config; the KV index translator handing a fused draft the target's sliding-window write ids and window table byte for byte, including from a plan a dense first depth built; the retained window on the radix cache, enabled and disabled; the fused state entry math and the whole-entry clear, copy and move; the window index kernel against a reference, at page sizes 1 and 2 and topk 1 and 2 (CUDA); each draft step's sliding-window write ids; and the head's window convention (CUDA). ## CI registration updates Updated `est_time` in 10 affected test files from observed file-level CI timings, including process/import cost and margin. Existing estimates with sufficient margin are retained. The expanded weekly configurator test also passed all 11 cases in a 30.1-second CPU measurement. The full page/top-k/window-translation kernel matrix runs in `nightly-test-1-gpu-large`. Eager and CUDA-graph FULL/SWA placement regressions remain in base CI. The Inkling MTP window-convention test runs in `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small`; it requires the CUDA image for its model imports. The CI registry check validated 2,960 registrations before landing. An AST comparison confirmed that this follow-up changes registration metadata only. Runtime test measurements elsewhere in this description refer to their stated earlier revisions. ## Accuracy Tests Earlier combined stack `b550cacde6` adds a test-fixture correction in #43326: the Gemma4 read-stream fixture declares its FULL address space, and the HiSparse registry test uses real `CacheInitParams` for the retained-window calculation. Both complete test files pass locally with GPUs hidden: 4 Gemma4 tests and 26 registry tests. Pre-commit passed. The five descendant patches are unchanged (`git range-diff`); this follow-up changes no production code. The earlier 455-test run did not cover these two files; GitHub CI has not yet been revalidated for this head. Validation before the test-fixture follow-up, on combined stack `4cf27a551c`: 455 tests and 921 subtests passed on B300, plus the two widened-history regressions against Rust TreeCore. The new FULL-fallback metadata cases cover eager execution and CUDA graph replay. New allocation-reclaim, explicit-prefill and JIT-reuse regressions fail on the previous code and pass with the fixes. These are combined-stack checks, not independent model reruns of each PR. The measurements in this section are historical results from before this rebase, at the revisions/configurations stated below. Current combined-stack validation is linked above. SM90. Unless marked, runs used this stack over main 7224fce1b5. Runs marked ‡ used the stack over the earlier main b130f8af02, and runs marked † used main 4b384df0c9, where this PR differed only in how a plan read names its sub-pool (item 2), which resolves to the same tables for every configuration in those rows. Default pool against `--enable-unified-memory`; GSM8K, all 1314 test questions, 5-shot, greedy. **The drafts this PR fuses**: NEXTN with `--attention-backend triton` (MiMo-V2-Flash at TP4, Inkling-Small at TP8), radix cache, overlap scheduler, CUDA graphs off and on. The unified pool runs with `SGLANG_DEBUG_POISON_POOL=1`, which fills every byte that is never written with NaN, so a draft that reads a slot nobody wrote loses accept length or accuracy. Accept length is the median of the server's logged values. | model | speculative decoding | CUDA graphs | GSM8K default / unified | accept length default / unified | |---|---|---|---|---| | MiMo-V2-Flash | `--speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4` | off | 0.852 / 0.836 | 2.71 / 2.70 | | | | on | 0.843 / 0.844 | 2.72 / 2.72 | | Inkling-Small | `--enable-multi-layer-eagle --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4` | off | 0.826 / 0.820 | 2.75 / 2.78 | | | | on | 0.820 / 0.818 | 1.51 / 1.50 | Every unified server boots with its draft fused: MiMo's draft layer in the sliding-window sub-pool, Inkling-Small's draft across the full-attention, sliding-window and mamba sub-pools. Inkling-Small's lower accept length with CUDA graphs is the same on the default pool. Paired per question, every unified run is within run-to-run noise of its default-pool run.
Drafts that already fused (the registry moves every placement): GSM8K and accept length at parity ‡ Radix cache, overlap scheduler, CUDA graphs on; the unified pool runs with lazy (default) and eager (`SGLANG_DISABLE_LAZY_COMPACTION=1`) compaction. | model | drafts | attention backends | GSM8K default | GSM8K unified | accept length | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Qwen3.5-9B | NEXTN, DFLASH, DFLASH (compact table) | triton, fa3, flashinfer | 0.894-0.900 | 0.892-0.900 | NEXTN 3.52-3.53 and DFLASH 6.33-6.41 on both pools | | Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B | DSPARK, a draft with a real config and dummy weights (no public DSPARK draft exists for it), which exercises the fused path | triton, flashmla | 0.895-0.896 | 0.897-0.902 | n/a (dummy weights) | | gpt-oss-20b | EAGLE3, DFLASH, DFLASH (compact table) | triton, fa3 | 0.522-0.573 | 0.521-0.577 | EAGLE3 1.27-1.28 on both; DFLASH within 0.07 | gpt-oss-20b's GSM8K score moves by several points between identical runs. Inkling-Small with DSPARK (`--speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-draft-model-path RadixArk/Inkling-Small-DSpark`, `--attention-backend triton`, TP8, radix cache, overlap scheduler), whose draft layers are all full-attention and fuse into the full-attention sub-pool: GSM8K 0.814 / 0.823 (default / unified) with CUDA graphs off and 0.828 / 0.833 with them on, accept length 4.08-4.27 on both pools.

title: [diffusion] perf: fuse MiniMax-H3's RMSNorm and indexed AdaLN under quality lossless
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Each MiniMax-H3 DiT block normalizes its residual stream twice, before attention and before the MLP. Each time it runs two memory-bound kernels: `nn.RMSNorm`, then the indexed AdaLN modulation `x * (1 + scale[idx]) + shift[idx]`. That is one full read and write of the `[tokens, 5376]` activations more than the math needs, and the chain rounds to BF16 after the norm and again after each modulation op.

A fused RMSNorm + AdaLN kernel was removed from this path before, because it drifted the 2-GPU consistency goldens. That drift is exactly what the `lossless` tier allows: same math and operand precision, only the rounding moves. So this PR brings the fusion back under the quality gate. `exact` and every CI golden keep the reference chain.

## Modifications

- `rmsnorm_indexed_scale_shift` (Triton): computes `rmsnorm(x) * (1 + scale[idx]) + shift[idx]` in one FP32 pass with a single rounding. It reads the AdaLN tables per row by index, so they are never materialized per token.
  - Launch config: one row per program, 8 warps. Packing 16 rows into a program, which is the per-token kernel's heuristic, spills the FP32 row tiles. At H3's width that variant took 4.5 ms for 32768 rows: 24× the one-row launch and 10× the unfused chain.
- New `QualityGatedFusion` site "MiniMax-H3 fused RMSNorm + AdaLN", registered at tier `lossless` in `_QUALITY_FUSION_HANDLERS`. Every DiT block marks it, and both modulate sites use the fused kernel while it is mounted.
  - `quality="lossless"` (the default) and `"high"` mount it.
  - `"exact"` unmounts it and keeps `nn.RMSNorm` plus `indexed_scale_shift_bf16_` bit for bit.
- Cookbook: the quality-level section now says what `lossless` changes in the denoise path.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_rmsnorm_indexed_scale_shift.py` (new): checks the kernel against the same math in FP32 with one rounding, and against the reference rounding chain, at widths 1024 and 5376 and 1/37/1025 rows.
  - Max error against the FP32 math is 0.0156, which is one BF16 step at these magnitudes. The reference chain is at 0.061.
- No H3 CI golden moves. Every MiniMax-H3 consistency case pins `quality="exact"`, as `testcase_configs.py` does for any case that names no level.
- End to end, with the fusion against without it (both at the default level, same seed, 4×H200), the outputs are not pixel-close. Neither are two `exact` runs that split the work differently: H3's 50-step trajectory turns rounding differences into a different sample.

  | pair | video PSNR | audio log-spectral distance |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | Ref2VA, Ulysses 2: with vs without | 20.8 dB | 3.0 dB |
  | T2VA, Ulysses 2: with vs without | 23.2 dB | 2.0 dB |
  | T2VA, Ulysses 4: with vs without | 17.9 dB | 6.2 dB |
  | reference: `exact` at Ulysses 2 vs `exact` at Ulysses 4 | 21.9 dB | 1.6 dB |

  Side by side, the frames show the same scene, subject and quality, with different camera framing and details. At Ulysses 4 the shot is closer and the shirt differs, as it also does between the two `exact` topologies. Both runs of every arm are md5-identical, so the fused path is deterministic.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel, H200, D=5376. For scale, H3's rows per rank are 24826 for Ref2VA at Ulysses 2, 18871 for T2VA at Ulysses 2 and 9436 at Ulysses 4.

| rows | `nn.RMSNorm` + `indexed_scale_shift_bf16_` | fused | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 10240 | 147.5 µs | 62.6 µs (3.5 TB/s) | 2.4× |
| 20480 | 280.7 µs | 115.7 µs (3.8 TB/s) | 2.4× |
| 32768 | 440.2 µs | 182.0 µs (3.9 TB/s) | 2.4× |

End to end, client latency, 4×H200, 50 steps, `--performance-mode speed`, default quality. The arms ran ABBA on one box (without, with, with, without), on top of the Ulysses copy-engine pipeline (#43164):

| Case | without | with | e2e | denoise stage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Ref2VA 5 s, 2 GPUs, Ulysses 2 | 220.15 / 219.75 s | 218.90 / 218.93 s | −0.47% | 213.65 → 212.52 s (−0.53%) |
| T2VA 5 s, 2 GPUs, Ulysses 2 | 141.33 / 141.37 s | 140.68 / 140.73 s | −0.45% | 137.65 → 136.94 s (−0.52%) |
| T2VA 5 s, 4 GPUs, Ulysses 4 | 72.27 / 72.31 s | 71.90 / 71.86 s | −0.57% | 70.48 → 70.07 s (−0.58%) |

Each cell is the two runs of an arm. The two arms differ only by this PR.

title: [ROCm][Spec] Route NGRAM tree reconstruction to the JIT kernel on HIP
author: jiaqiang-dot-liu
body:
## Motivation

NGRAM speculative decoding crashes on ROCm on the first batch, so a server launched with `--speculative-algorithm NGRAM` never becomes healthy:

```
  File "python/sglang/srt/speculative/ngram_worker.py", line 433, in forward_batch_generation
  File "python/sglang/srt/speculative/ngram_worker.py", line 345, in _prepare_for_speculative_decoding
  ...
AttributeError: '_OpNamespace' 'sgl_kernel' object has no attribute 'reconstruct_indices_from_tree_mask'
```

`ngram_worker.py` picks the tree-reconstruction kernel by platform:

```python
if is_xpu():
    from sglang.kernels.ops.speculative.reconstruct_tree import (...)
elif is_cuda():
    from sglang.kernels.ops.speculative.tree import reconstruct_indices_from_tree_mask
else:
    from sgl_kernel.speculative import reconstruct_indices_from_tree_mask
```

`is_cuda()` is `False` on ROCm, so HIP falls through to `sgl_kernel.speculative`. The Python wrapper imports fine, but the ROCm `sgl_kernel` build does not register the op, so the call fails at runtime rather than at import.

The JIT `tree` module used on CUDA already runs on HIP: EAGLE uses it there (`eagle_utils.py` imports it under `_is_cuda or _is_hip`), and #40325 made its entry points accept ROCm tensors.

## Modifications

- `ngram_worker.py`: route HIP to the JIT `tree` module, the same implementation CUDA and EAGLE-on-HIP use. XPU and the remaining platforms are unchanged.
- `test_ngram_utils.py`: import the JIT kernel unconditionally (it is what both CUDA and ROCm now run) and register the test in AMD CI (`jit-kernel-unit`).
- `test_spec_ngram_extra.py`: register the file in AMD CI. Only the triton-backend class runs on ROCm; the two flashinfer classes are skipped on HIP, following `test_spec_standalone_extra.py`.

An earlier attempt (#29346, closed) built `ngram_utils` into the ROCm `sgl-kernel` instead. Reusing the JIT kernel adds no new compiled op and no third implementation.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X (gfx950, 256 CU), ROCm 7.2.0, torch 2.9.1, Triton 3.7.0. sglang `main` @ `c44a42e6d3`, `sgl-kernel` built from the same commit, AITER `e7d2453f` (the commit pinned in `docker/rocm.Dockerfile`).

Before this PR, the NGRAM server fails on the first batch with the error above (reproduced with Qwen3-8B, default attention backend).

After this PR:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_ngram_utils.py` | 1 passed |
| `test/registered/spec/test_spec_ngram_extra.py` | 1 passed (triton), 3 skipped (flashinfer, CUDA-only) in 127 s |

GSM8K with the CI fixture (`Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct`, triton backend, 200 questions, 5-shot, greedy):

| Server | GSM8K |
|---|---|
| NGRAM, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 16` | 0.810 |
| Same server args, no speculation | 0.800 |

Average accept length on a GSM8K run with the same NGRAM server args, read from `/server_info`: **1.95** (the fixture threshold is 1.8). On a repeated prompt, once the n-gram corpus holds the first answer, the accept length reaches 15.06 of 16 draft tokens.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: this enables a code path that previously crashed on ROCm.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). The open docs PR #42687 lists NGRAM devices; ROCm can be added once this lands.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [GDN] Fix CuTe DSL decode to read the [N, HV, V, K] state layout
author: SunskyXH
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Fixes #43331. Since #20283 the GDN state pool uses `[N, HV, V, K]`, but the CuTe DSL decode kernel still indexes it as `[N, HV, K, V]`, so `--linear-attn-decode-backend cutedsl` produces garbage output.

## Modifications

- `cutedsl_gdn.py`: the kernels get a transposed `(pool, HV, K, V)` view of the pool and are compiled for that layout. State loads (128-bit `cp.async`) and stores now run along K, the contiguous dimension, through a K-contiguous shared-memory tile padded to 136 floats per row to keep the compute reads bank-conflict-free. The compute loops are unchanged.
- `test_cutedsl_gdn.py`: re-enable the precision test skipped in #20436 and compare the outputs and the whole state pool against Triton on one shared pool (small and large batch, dense and varlen). It fails on main and passes with this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

Qwen3.5-4B, BF16, TP=1, MTP disabled, `--mem-fraction-static 0.8`, one H200. GSM8K, 200 questions, 5-shot:

| decode backend | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| triton | 0.870 | 0.870 |
| cutedsl | 0.010 | 0.875 |

Kernel level, one decode step against an fp32 reference: the CuTe DSL output error is 1.4 on main and 1.7e-3 with this PR, the same as Triton (bf16 output rounding).

title: [diffusion] perf: run MiniMax-H3's QK-norm + RoPE two rows per warp, bit-identical
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-H3 normalizes and rotates q/k with `fused_qknorm_rope_warp`. With head_dim 128 the kernel gives each warp one (token, head) row, so a lane moves only 8 bytes per row. The kernel is issue-bound, not bandwidth-bound: ncu shows 0.69 IPC per scheduler with 48% of stalls on L1TEX, and it reaches 2.5 TB/s on H200. It runs on every block: in place on the sequential Ulysses path, and once per head group and destination on the pipelined path (#43164).

## Modifications

- `fused_qknorm_rope_half_warp`: the same kernel with two rows per warp. Each row gets 16 lanes, and each lane moves 16 B of q/k and 16 B of the cos/sin cache.
- **Bit-identical by construction.** Each lane covers two lanes of the warp kernel. It keeps their two partial sums, accumulated in the same order, and replays that kernel's xor butterfly:
  - offsets 16..2 become 8..1, applied to each partial;
  - the final xor-1 step becomes `part0 + part1`.

  The per-element norm and RoPE expressions are unchanged.
- It is chosen at compile time for head_dim 128, NeoX, the norm rounded before RoPE, a half-width cache, and CUDA. Every other instantiation keeps the warp kernel.
- `_jit_qknorm_rope_module(half_warp=False)` keeps the warp kernel for the new test.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_qknorm_rope_out_of_place.py::test_two_rows_per_warp_match_one_row_per_warp` (new) compares the two kernels' bytes. It covers:
  - in-place and out-of-place;
  - BF16 and FP16 activations, with BF16, FP16 and FP32 caches;
  - rope_dim 32, 96 and 128;
  - int32 and int64 positions;
  - an odd row count, so the last warp gets one row.

  The file is now registered on `1-gpu-large` as well as `4-gpu-b200`, so both Hopper and Blackwell check the claim.
- `test_rope.py` passes all 1264 cases on H200, including the `torch.equal` checks against the split QK-norm + `sgl_kernel` RoPE baseline at H3's shape.
- Old and new outputs are byte-identical at H3's per-rank shapes (24826 / 18871 / 9436 tokens, in place and per exchange block).
- End to end on 4×H200, the MP4 md5 is unchanged in every arm: Ref2VA at Ulysses 2 (four runs), and T2VA at Ulysses 2 and 4.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Per call on H200 (the same GPU for every column), 56 + 56 heads in place, or one exchange block on the pipelined path:

| tokens | path | before | after |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 24826 | in place, 56 + 56 heads | 567.5 µs (2.5 TB/s) | 430.5 µs (3.3 TB/s), −24% |
| 24826 | exchange block, 4 + 4 heads | 51.9 µs | 40.5 µs, −22% |
| 18871 | in place | 430.0 µs | 329.1 µs, −23% |
| 18871 | exchange block, 4 + 4 heads | 40.5 µs | 32.5 µs, −20% |
| 9436 | in place | 218.6 µs | 170.0 µs, −22% |
| 9436 | exchange block, 2 + 2 heads | 15.0 µs | 13.0 µs, −13% |

Two rows per warp with scalar cos/sin loads already gave 440.6 / 45.4 µs at 24826 tokens. The 16 B cache loads add the rest.

End to end, client latency, 4×H200, 50 steps, default quality. These runs sit on top of #43164 and #43327, and the arms differ only by this PR:

| Case | before | after | e2e | denoise stage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Ref2VA 5 s, Ulysses 2 (ABBA) | 218.71 / 218.97 s | 218.47 / 218.70 s | −0.12% | 212.49 → 212.24 s |
| T2VA 5 s, Ulysses 2 | 140.76 s | 140.30 s | −0.33% | 137.01 → 136.55 s |
| T2VA 5 s, Ulysses 4 | 71.83 s | 71.68 s | −0.20% | 70.03 → 69.86 s |

On the pipelined path the kernel runs once per head group and destination, interleaved with attention. The H200s sit at their 700 W cap during denoise, so part of the freed time comes back as a lower clock.

body: ## Motivation enable and optimize Grok-2 model on xeon cpu. ## Modifications * enable: * add the required `allow_patterns_overrides` arg in `grok.py`. (have fixed in upstream PR #45217) * fix the `weight_start` when `use_presharded_weights == True` on xeon in `layer.py` * optimization - add fused CPU operators for Grok * **K1 — fused dual-residual RMSNorm:** combines RMSNorm, residual addition, and a second RMSNorm while preserving the required reduced-precision rounding points and out-of-place residual semantics. cherry-pick from https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43343 * **K2 — fused MoE router:** fsued_moe_router, cheery-pick from https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41004 ## Accuracy Tests The gsm8k acc results is: 0.78. ```bash # server python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path xai-org/grok-2 \ --tokenizer-path /tokenizer.tok.json \ --device cpu \ --tp-size 6 \ --trust-remote-code # client python -m sglang.test.run_eval \ --eval-name gsm8k \ --num-examples 200 \ --num-shots 1 \ --num-threads 1 ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### End-to-end benchmarks Speedup is calculated as **naive latency / configuration latency**; **higher is better**. The naive baseline uses PyTorch only for the two target operations; other CPU optimizations remain unchanged. | Configuration | E2E latency speedup | TTFT speedup | TPOT speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Naive PyTorch | 1.000× | 1.000× | 1.000× | | K1 only | 1.04× | 1.17× | 1.04× | | K2 only | 1.02× | 1.11× | 1.02× | | **K1 + K2** | **1.05×** | **1.19×** | **1.05×** | ### CPU profiling Captured TP0 CPU traces with `sglang.benchmark.one_batch`, including tensor shapes and Python stacks. title: [Perf] [XPU] server_args: Enable fused QK-norm + RoPE by default
author: mehersai07
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

[#40190](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40190) wired the fused QK-norm + RoPE kernel (`sgl_kernel.fused_inplace_qknorm_rope`) into Qwen3-MoE on XPU behind the existing opt-in `--enable-fused-qk-norm-rope`. Its A/B on Qwen3-30B-A3B (TP=4, 4x Arc Pro B60) showed +4.7-7.0% output throughput, -60% q/k-norm + RoPE stage device time, and no accuracy change (GSM8K 0.9414 vs 0.9460).
The flag is opt-in on CUDA for a reason that does not apply to XPU: on CUDA the unfused path already fuses RoPE with the KV-cache write (`fused_set_kv_buffer`), and the fused QK-norm path gives that up. `enable_fused_set_kv_buffer` is CUDA/HIP-only, so the XPU unfused path has nothing to lose. This PR makes the fused path the XPU default; everything else is unchanged.

## Modifications

- `arg_groups/fields/exec_.py`: `enable_fused_qk_norm_rope` becomes a tri-state (`Optional[bool] = None`, `BooleanOptionalAction`, `resolvable=True`), the same shape as `enable_dsa_fused_indexer`. `--enable-fused-qk-norm-rope` keeps working; `--no-enable-fused-qk-norm-rope` is the new opt-out.
- `arg_groups/platform_hook.py`: `handle_xpu_backends` declares `enable_fused_qk_norm_rope=True` when the device is XPU and the user did not choose, next to the existing XPU `sampling_backend` default.
- Docs: the flag's rows in `server_arguments.mdx` and the Ascend support table.

On every other platform the field stays `None`. Its two readers (`qwen3_moe.py`, `mellum.py`) use it only in `and` chains and truthiness checks, so `None` behaves exactly like the old `False`. No model code changes.

One visible difference: off XPU, `/get_server_info` now reports `enable_fused_qk_norm_rope: null` instead of `false`, matching how `enable_dsa_fused_indexer` reports.

## Accuracy Tests

No new numerics: the kernel and call site are the ones #40190 measured (GSM8K above). The nightly `test/registered/xpu/llm_models/test_xpu_qwen3_30b_a3b.py` (TP=4 GSM8K, threshold 0.90) now runs the fused path by default.

Resolution, checked through `prepare_server_args` + `resolve_once()`:

| device | flag | resolved |
|---|---|---|
| xpu | none | `True` |
| xpu | `--enable-fused-qk-norm-rope` | `True` |
| xpu | `--no-enable-fused-qk-norm-rope` | `False` |
| non-XPU | none | `None` (off) |
| non-XPU | `--enable-fused-qk-norm-rope` / `--no-enable-fused-qk-norm-rope` | `True` / `False` |

title: [diffusion] fix: keep MiniMax-H3 VAE fused norms off ROCm
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

Since #41906, `minimax_h3_ref2va_video_audio_2gpu_h100` fails on AMD MI300 in the scheduled PR Test (AMD) runs on main. `MiniMaxH3DecodingStage` returns a video that is entirely NaN: 331,333,632 NaN values in a `[1, 3, 107, 768, 1344]` tensor ([example job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37709475489/job/113091795394)).

In the scheduled AMD runs on main:

- **Before #41906 merged (10-05 09:30 UTC):** this case either passed or failed with a server startup timeout, never with NaN.
- **After the merge:** every run that reached the case (7 runs, 10-06 to 10-09) failed with the all-NaN decode.

#41906 enables its fused Triton kernels (block RMSNorm, scale-add-RMSNorm, and the QK RMSNorm+RoPE) when the tensors satisfy `is_cuda`. On ROCm, `tensor.is_cuda` is also true, so MI300 takes the fused path.

## Modifications

- `vae_vit._fused_blocks_available` and `attention._try_fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope` now also require `current_platform.is_cuda()`, which is true only on NVIDIA. ROCm keeps the unfused fp32-norm path. NVIDIA behavior is unchanged.
- The fused-vs-unfused unit test now runs only on NVIDIA.
- A new unit test simulates a non-NVIDIA platform and checks that neither fused kernel is called.

Re-enabling the fused path on ROCm needs a separate root-cause fix on AMD hardware.

## Validation

- On an RTX 5090, `test_minimax_h3_vae_parallel_modes.py` passes (15 tests). The new test fails if the gate is removed.
- To confirm on MI300: PR Test (AMD) should run `minimax_h3_ref2va_video_audio_2gpu_h100` without the NaN decode.

title: [diffusion] perf: move MiniMax-H3's pipelined Ulysses copies off the SMs
author: mickqian
body:
Follow-up to #43164 (merged). The branch carries #43164's original commits and a merge of main, so against main the diff is only this change.

## Motivation

After #43164 (and #43327 / #43337), a profile of MiniMax-H3's pipelined Ulysses attention shows almost no exposed exchange left: 0.09–0.24 ms per layer. What remains on the SMs is the exchange's own data movement. Per head group and destination, two PyTorch strided copies run:

- v into the exchange block, from the fill;
- this rank's and each peer's rows into the merged output.

That is 28 elementwise copy kernels per layer at Ulysses 2 and 56 at Ulysses 4. Measured alone they move 0.8–1.4 TB/s (read plus write), and inside the pipeline they compete with FlashAttention, which wants every SM. Their SM time per layer, from isolated timings at the real shapes:

| Case (rows per rank) | merge copy | v copy | per layer | share of the layer |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Ref2VA, Ulysses 2 (24826) | 35.7 µs | 37.6 µs | 14 × 73 µs = 1.03 ms | 1.2% |
| T2VA, Ulysses 2 (18871) | 28.6 µs | 30.2 µs | 14 × 59 µs = 0.82 ms | 1.5% |
| T2VA, Ulysses 4 (9436) | 12.2 µs | 12.6 µs | 28 × 25 µs = 0.69 ms | 2.4% |

## Modifications

Every copy of the exchange now runs on the copy engine, as a pitched `cuMemcpy2DAsync` issued next to the stream memory operations it already uses. Nothing moves on the SMs, and the result stays bit-identical: it is pure data movement, and attention sees the same values.

- **Receive slots are split by part:** `[2, groups, 3, world, chunk]`. Group g's q, k and v from every rank are each one contiguous `[S, group_heads, head_dim]` tensor, and attention reads them directly.
- **v moves straight from the projection output** into every destination's receive slot, this rank's own included. It no longer passes through the send buffer.
- **q/k:**
  - With a `fill` (H3's QK-norm), the fill writes q and k into the send buffer, and one 2-row copy takes both to the peer.
  - Without a `fill`, q, k and v all move straight from their sources, and the pack kernel is gone.
- **The merge:** this rank's rows and each peer's rows land in their output block with a pitched copy on the group stream.
- **`fill(head_start, head_count, q_dst, k_dst)`** now writes only q and k.
- **Memory:** the send buffer holds q/k only, so the buffers are 10 × (rows per rank) × heads × head_dim instead of 11 ×, which is 3.6 GB for Ref2VA at Ulysses 2. The cookbook note says so.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_ipc_a2a_multi_gpu.py` passes at 2 and 4 ranks. It compares against the sequential exchange byte for byte, with and without a fill, including the automatic group count and the head count that must decline.
- End to end on 4×H200, the MP4 md5 is unchanged in all twelve runs: T2VA at Ulysses 2 and 4, and Ref2VA at Ulysses 2.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Client end-to-end latency, 4×H200, 50 steps, default quality. These runs sit on top of #43164, #43327 and #43337. The arms ran ABBA on one box (without, with, with, without):

| Case | without | with | e2e | denoise stage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| T2VA 5 s, 4 GPUs, Ulysses 4 | 71.66 / 71.69 s | 70.88 / 70.95 s | −1.06% | 69.88 → 69.09 s (−1.13%) |
| T2VA 5 s, 2 GPUs, Ulysses 2 | 140.40 / 140.38 s | 139.91 / 139.87 s | −0.36% | 136.63 → 135.82 s (−0.59%) |
| Ref2VA 5 s, 2 GPUs, Ulysses 2 | 218.50 / 218.74 s | 217.82 / 218.00 s | −0.32% | 212.27 → 211.07 s (−0.57%) |

The gain is largest at Ulysses 4, which ran 56 copy kernels per layer against 28 at Ulysses 2. It is below the SM time the copies held, because part of that time overlapped attention tails anyway, and the H200s sit at their 700 W cap, so part of the freed time comes back as a lower clock.
