title: [diffusion] torch.compile: keep Cosmos3's fused kernels in the graph
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-torch-compile`, Cosmos3 is slower than eager: on 2xGB300 (T2I, CFG-parallel) eager is 0.93 s and compile is 1.43 s, while vLLM-Omni's compile is 0.97–1.02 s. Profiling the compiled run shows more kernels than eager (2264 → 3344 per 4 steps), and `TORCH_LOGS=graph_breaks` shows two causes:

1. `cosmos3video.py` (relu2, fused K/V packing, T=1 fused QK-norm+RoPE) and `layernorm.apply_qk_norm_rope` skip their fused kernels when `torch.compiler.is_compiling()`. Those kernels are already registered custom ops (`_run_unary_activation_inplace`, `fused_qknorm_rope_pack_kv`, `fused_inplace_qknorm_rope`), which dynamo keeps as opaque calls. The gates only replaced them with the unfused forms, and inductor emitted extra kernels for those.
2. The non-fused T=1 path calls the bare JIT `fused_inplace_qknorm`. Its tvm_ffi launch graph-breaks inside every decoder layer (`tvm_ffi/module.py:188 ... Function.__call__`).

## Modifications

- Remove the four `is_compiling()` gates around custom-op fused kernels (three in `cosmos3video.py`, one in `layernorm.apply_qk_norm_rope`).
- In `layers/layernorm.py`, register `fused_inplace_qknorm` as an opaque custom op (mutating `q`, `k`), the same way `srt/models/utils.py` already does. Both register the same function under the same name, so whichever imports first wins with identical semantics. `sglang/kernels` is untouched.

## Accuracy Tests

Cosmos3-Nano T2I 1280x720, 35 steps, CFG 6.0, served on GB300, image of the 3rd request:

| Pair | Result |
|---|---|
| eager, main vs this PR | bit-identical |
| compile, main vs this PR | bit-identical (the gates switched between mathematically identical forms) |
| compile vs eager (main and this PR alike) | PSNR 21.3 dB, pre-existing (inductor re-associates the rest of the layer; 35 steps at CFG 6 amplify it) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

2xGB300, Cosmos3-Nano T2I CFG-parallel, served. Median of 5 requests after 2 warmups, fresh server per arm, 2 interleaved rounds. NUMA-bound workers (#43565) in all arms.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| eager | 0.935 / 0.937 s | 0.933 / 0.939 s |
| compile | 1.424 / 1.435 s | **0.884 / 0.876 s** |
| graph breaks (compile) | 8 | 0 |

With this PR, compile beats eager by ~6% and vLLM-Omni's compile (0.97–1.02 s on the same box). FLUX.1 TP2 on the same tree: compile 3.93–4.03 s vs eager 3.86–4.06 s (it was 35% slower before NUMA binding and these fixes); vLLM-Omni compile is 4.86–5.26 s.

Known follow-ups, not in this PR: the first request after startup still recompiles the 36 Cosmos3 gen layers, because the warmup prompt length differs and the layers compile with `dynamic=False`. TP all-reduce is not traceable (`Communicator.get_world_size`) and graph-breaks FLUX TP compile.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests: `test_regional_torch_compile.py::test_diffusion_qknorm_is_an_opaque_op_for_torch_compile` (the op exists after importing the layer and its schema marks `q`, `k` as written). `test_regional_torch_compile.py` + `test_cosmos3.py` pass on GB300: 151 passed.
- [ ] Update documentation: N/A.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [diffusion] torch.compile: skip inductor's saved multi-kernel pick (Z-Image warm starts crash or hang)
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Since #35755, Z-Image compiles with `multi_kernel_hints`. With `--enable-torch-compile`, every server start after the first fails: the first start fills the inductor FX-graph cache, and each later start hits it.

| Z-Image-Turbo, 1x GB300, `sglang generate --enable-torch-compile true`, fresh cache root | Result |
|---|---|
| 1st start (cold cache) | OK, 112 s wall |
| 2nd start (warm cache) | **fails**: `BackendCompilerFailed: TypeError: 'NoneType' object does not support the context manager protocol` (4x) |
| 2nd start, `TORCHINDUCTOR_FX_GRAPH_CACHE=0` | OK, 89 s wall (recompiles) |
| 2nd and 3rd start with this PR | OK, 54 s / 51 s wall |

With TP the failure becomes a hang. Only the rank that hits the cache raises and abandons the request. Its peer keeps waiting in the custom all-reduce, and its next `cuModuleLoadData` blocks behind the spinning kernel:

```
Z-Image-Turbo, 2x GB300, --tp-size 2 --enable-torch-compile true, warm cache
TP0  idle in recv_reqs -> broadcast            (warmup request failed: backend='inductor' raised)
TP1  cuModuleLoadData <- triton _init_handles   (100% CPU for 10+ min; GPU1 at 100%)
```

Cause (torch 2.13, triton 3.7). On a cache hit, the loaded module builds `SizeHintMultiKernelCall` at import time, and its constructor reads the saved pick (`MultiKernelCall.load_cache`). That hashes every sub-kernel through `k.fn.cache_key` (`with self._hash_lock`). The sub-kernels come back from the compile workers with `_hash_lock = None` (`CachingAutotuner.prepare_for_pickle`), and they are not restored until `async_compile.wait()` runs later in the same module.

## Modifications

`apply_inductor_config` sets `TORCHINDUCTOR_DISABLE_MULTI_KERNEL_CACHE=1` (via `setdefault`) whenever a model sets `multi_kernel_hints`. Inductor then skips `load_cache`, and each process re-picks during warmup. The FX-graph and autotune caches are unaffected.

## Accuracy Tests

The output is bit-identical to an unpatched warm start that recompiles (`TORCHINDUCTOR_FX_GRAPH_CACHE=0`): md5 `0d6093d6…` for that start and for both patched starts.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change at run time. `SizeHintMultiKernelCall.run` picks a sub-kernel per input shape (`_select_kernel_by_shape`, cached in memory) and overwrites `picked_kernel` on every call, so the saved pick never decides anything for these kernels. Skipping `load_cache` only removes the crash. Startup with a warm cache: 54 s / 51 s, against 112 s cold and 89 s recompiling with the FX-graph cache off.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests: `test_torch_compile_inductor_config.py`. Covers: hints drop the saved pick; other overrides leave it alone; an explicit environment setting wins. 3 passed on GB300.
- [ ] Update documentation: N/A.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [DSpark] Add `MarkovSampleStep`, one op for a markov draft step's add and token pick
author: hnyls2002
body:
Stacks on #43620.

- `MarkovSampleStep` adds a step's bias to the base logits, rounds the sum to the head's step dtype, and picks one token per row: the argmax at temperature 0, a Gumbel-max sample otherwise. Triton and torch implementations.
- The noise is Philox4x32-10 computed in the kernel, keyed by the server seed and countered by (global token id, row, step, a per-block offset). It needs no noise tensor, does not touch the torch generator, and every TP rank draws the same values from the same inputs.
- TP-sharded vocab: without kept logits each rank reduces its shard to one (value, index) pair per block and only those pairs are all-gathered; with kept logits the step logits are gathered once and every rank picks from the full vocab. Either way a step takes one collective.
- A greedy-only variant (no temperature read, no noise code) compiles when no row samples.
- Replaces `sharded_greedy.py`; the DeepSeek-V4.1 greedy graph tail now calls the op.
- Tests: Triton against the torch reference, the greedy-only variant against the mixed one, NaN and inf, ties across blocks, strided rows, the tempered-softmax distribution, noise keying, and sharded against full vocab in both gather modes.

No behavior change: greedy picks are the same argmax with the same lowest-index tie rule.

## Verification

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_dspark_markov_sample.py`: 9 passed on GB300 (torch 2.14.1, Triton 3.8.0).
- Per launch, against the kernels it replaces: the greedy-only variant is no slower than the old sharded greedy step, and sampling rows run 2.0-2.3x faster than the old sampling path. 1024-wide blocks cut a one-row sampled step over a 129280-token vocab from 5.6 to 2.4 us.

title: [Perf] Enable native MXFP4 routing and CuTeDSL fusion for MiMo
author: leonardHONG
body:
## Motivation

MiMo MXFP4 currently computes routing separately and finalizes the MoE output before communication. Use FlashInfer native routing and deferred finalization with the existing CuTeDSL layer-boundary fusion to reduce this overhead.

## Modifications

- Add native grouped routing and deferred finalization for supported MiMo MXFP4 configurations.
- Support CuTeDSL layer-boundary fusion without shared experts.
- Automatically select CuTeDSL for supported configurations, preserving explicit backend choices.
- Keep standard routing for expert capture, distribution recording, simulated routing and expert remapping. Exclude PDMux from automatic selection.

RoPE/KV-store fusion remains in #43106.

## Accuracy Tests

The same 128 frozen GSM8K questions, normal EOS and generation settings were used for both versions. Exact numerical-answer scoring changes from 123/128 to 124/128, with two gains and one loss. Strict answer-string scoring is 119/128 and 120/128, respectively.

Fixed-prefix full-vocabulary log-probabilities were compared on 24 cases. Exact argmax matches in 22 cases; one additional mismatch falls within the baseline's tied top-1 set, while one changes the top-1 choice outside that set. Mean total variation distance is 3.15%, with a maximum of 14.10%.

FlashInfer native routing returns BF16 expert weights, while the precomputed route retains FP32 weights. Generated outputs and DFlash acceptance trajectories are not identical. These checks do not establish numerical equivalence or general quality equivalence.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL revision `73875d00b30a`, 8×B300, TP8, concurrency one, FA4, page size 128, KV capacity 32768 and prefix caching disabled.

Baseline: `6e7beace143964386ce2e4418401b7369f0dabd0`.
Candidate: `d7b192133f73ef2068debc349eda85a1d0dce218`.

Each comparison uses one fresh server per revision, three warmups and 96 frozen random-topic essay requests with 8,000 input tokens and 1,024 output tokens. EOS is ignored only for timing. Both versions use the same model, dependencies and requests; DFlash comparisons also use the same draft checkpoint.

Decode throughput uses tokens emitted after the first emission divided by the first-to-last emission interval. E2E throughput and TTFT are reported separately. Timing excludes profiling and log-probability collection.

| Mode | Decode tok/s | E2E tok/s | TTFT ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DFlash, baseline | 302.44 | 285.44 | 204.75 |
| DFlash, candidate | 338.01 | 315.72 | 216.63 |
| Without DFlash, baseline | 176.54 | 170.75 | 202.17 |
| Without DFlash, candidate | 186.58 | 179.74 | 214.21 |

With DFlash, decode throughput improves by 11.76% and E2E throughput by 10.61%. All 96 requests have partial rejection; acceptance changes from 21.38% to 21.61%, so the measured gain includes verification-workload differences.

Without DFlash, decode throughput improves by 5.69% and E2E throughput by 5.26%. Mean TTFT increases by approximately 12 ms in both modes.

These results cover the measured single-concurrency workload and are single fresh-server pairs, not multi-run confidence estimates.

title: [AMD] Use the preallocated EAGLE topk=1 draft chain on HIP
author: xiaofei-zheng
body:
## Motivation

`EagleDraftWorker.draft_forward` writes the topk=1 draft chain straight into the preallocated parents/indices buffers only when `_is_cuda`. HIP already runs the Triton `draft_topk1_postprocess` kernel that fills those columns (#35872), but the gate still sends it through the token-list path: the eager `_select_top_k_tokens_first` (with `repeat_interleave`) on step 0, the compiled `_select_top_k_tokens_later` on each later step, and a final `cat`.

## Modifications

- Take the preallocated chain on `_is_cuda or _is_hip`. The other conditions (topk 1, batch fits the buffers, no `hot_token_id`, no draft probs) are unchanged, so EAGLE3 token maps and non-greedy batches under rejection sampling keep the token-list path.

## Accuracy Tests

Bit-exact: the same Triton argmax runs per step and the chain buffers hold what the `cat` path builds. On MI355X, `test_eagle_worker_v2_topk1_fastpath.py` passes 11 tests and 7 subtests, and `test_spec_topk1.py` passes 6 tests and 12 subtests. A draft-forward probe at GLM-5.3 shapes (vocab 154880, hidden 6144, 5 steps) gives `torch.equal` outputs at bs 1-64.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same probe with the draft model stubbed out, so only the draft glue is measured. Kernels per draft cycle drop from 27 to 9 at every batch size. HIP-graph replay per cycle (min of 5 x 200 replays):

| bs | main (us) | this PR (us) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 53.4 | 24.5 |
| 4 | 58.2 | 23.5 |
| 8 | 57.8 | 26.0 |
| 32 | 72.5 | 36.9 |
| 64 | 86.5 | 47.7 |

That is about 0.25-0.3% of a GLM-5.3 TP4 decode cycle (~12 ms), too small to resolve end to end.

title: [Perf] [AMD] dsa: Run DSA prefill under breakable CUDA graphs on HIP
author: xiaofei-zheng
body:
## Motivation

`--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable` cannot run DSA prefill on ROCm. With the flag set, GLM-5 / DeepSeek-V3.2 on MI355X hit `AssertionError: Internal error: in-graph DSA prefill must go through the graph DSA split-op dispatch`, for two reasons:

- `is_graph_dsa_split_op_surface` is CUDA-only, so the indexer never takes the split op inside the graph.
- `pcg_dsa_indexer_prefill_split` asserts CUDA, imports the Triton `act_quant`, and cannot receive the `(x, x_s[, x_bf16])` tuple that the ROCm fused RMSNorm + quant produces.

Separately, on non-CUDA platforms the runner sends every extend with a prefix to eager whenever MHA companion layers exist, but DSA sets `use_mha=False` inside piecewise and breakable graphs, so the companion never runs there.

## Modifications

- Allow the split-op surface on HIP.
- In the split op, pick the tilelang `act_quant` on HIP (same rule as `forward_cuda`), take the quantized tuple as separate tensors, and use the AITER fused FP8 Q/K writer when it is active, sliced to the unpadded token count.
- Size `topk_result` from the activation's row count so tuple inputs work.
- Skip the prefix veto when the attention backend is DSA.
- Add a test: a breakable prefill with a nonzero prefix on a non-CUDA platform with DSA must not be vetoed. It fails without the runner change.

CUDA paths are unchanged. ROCm only reaches this with the breakable flag; the default prefill graph backend there is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

GLM-5.3 MXFP4, first 4 layers with real weights, TP1 on MI355X, breakable graph vs eager in the same process. The graph replays for prefixes 0 and 4096 (`can_run_graph:prefix:True`, the split op and fused writer run inside the graph). Logits are finite, and the max abs difference from eager is 0.43-0.64, against 0.03-0.61 between two eager runs. Argmax matches in all 6 graph cases. A seventh case (3000 new tokens) is above the capture size and runs eager on both sides; its argmax still differs, which is eager run-to-run noise.

GSM8K, GLM-5.3 MXFP4 TP4/EP4 on the 0.5.21 image: 0.9735 with this change and the flag, 0.9750 stock (SE ~0.004).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same 4-layer model, `model_runner.forward` for one extend, median ms:

| new tokens | prefix 0: eager / graph | prefix 32768: eager / graph |
|---|---|---|
| 16 | 5.82 / 2.46 | 7.22 / 3.42 |
| 128 | 5.75 / 3.16 | 7.09 / 4.13 |
| 512 | 5.92 / 4.18 | 7.02 / 5.28 |
| 1024 | 6.04 / 6.28 | 8.43 / 8.12 |
| 2048 | 7.34 / 10.66 | 13.97 / 13.65 |

Small extends gain the most. A 2048-token extend with no prefix is 45% slower in the graph, so a lower `--cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill` (for example 1024) may suit workloads with long cold prompts.

GLM-5.3 MXFP4 TP4/EP4 agentic replay (CONC 10, 1 h, 0.5.21 image), with this change and `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 2048` vs stock: P50 interactivity 112.26 vs 109.49 (+2.5%, 95% CI [+0.2, +5.0]), TTFT P50 441 vs 459 ms. An earlier version of this change measured +8.75% P50 at TP8/EP1 CONC 4 on 0.5.20.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add a unit test.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results.

title: [Perf] [AMD] dsa: Enable the gfx950 fused DSA indexer for block-FP8 wq_b/wk
author: xiaofei-zheng
body:
## Motivation

The gfx950 fused DSA indexer (#38583) only accepts bf16 `wq_b`, `wk` and `weights_proj`, and only plain bf16 hidden states. GLM-5.3 checkpoints ship block-FP8 `wq_b`/`wk` and run the gfx95 fused RMSNorm + quant, which hands the indexer an `(fp8, scale, bf16)` tuple, so GLM-5.3 never takes the fused path on MI355X.

## Modifications

- Accept `wq_b`/`wk` when both are bf16 or both are block-FP8 (`weights_proj` stays bf16).
- With FP8 weights, node 1 runs the layers' own GEMMs (the same ones the standard path runs) instead of the merged bf16 GEMV. Node 2 reads `k` and `weights` through their row stride, so the GEMM outputs are not copied into the workspace.
- Accept the `(fp8, scale, bf16)` hidden-state tuple: the bf16 GEMV takes `x[2]` and the FP8 GEMMs take the tuple.

bf16 checkpoints keep the existing path.

## Accuracy Tests

Top-k overlap on GLM-5.3 MXFP4 layers 0 and 38, real indexer weights, decode rows 1/8/48 and verify rows 6/12/24/48, contexts 4k-200k:

| comparison | overlap |
|---|---|
| fused vs the stock chain with the same index-K format | 99.80% |
| stock vs stock, two runs | 99.82% |
| fused vs stock with the AITER fused writer | 94.75% |
| stock chain vs stock with the AITER fused writer | 94.75% |

On main, GLM-5.3 runs the AITER fused writer, which stores the index K without the Hadamard rotation that the non-fused chain and the fused kernels apply. That rotation accounts for the 5% gap, and the two stock paths already differ by the same amount. Against the chain with the same format, the fused kernels match to run-to-run level.

GSM8K (GLM-5.3 MXFP4 TP4/EP4, 0.5.21 image): 0.9735 with this change, 0.9750 stock (SE ~0.004).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`Indexer.forward_cuda`, layer 0, real weights, CUDA graph replay, median time per layer vs stock (stock is 37-362 us across these cases):

| context | decode 1 row | decode 8 | decode 48 | verify 6 rows | verify 24 | verify 48 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4k | -9% | +1% | +25% | -6% | +3% | +17% |
| 16k | -17% | -15% | +10% | -18% | -14% | +4% |
| 64k | -22% | -26% | -13% | -32% | -31% | -30% |
| 200k | -14% | -22% | -11% | -35% | -40% | -42% |

Long contexts gain 11-42%. Short contexts with many rows are slower, as with the bf16 path. Like #38583, enabling the fused path turns the AITER fused writer off for the layer, so batches above 48 rows and prefill run the stock chain without that writer.

GLM-5.3 MXFP4 TP4/EP4 agentic replay (CONC 10, 1 h, 0.5.21 image) vs stock: P50 interactivity 116.90 vs 109.49 (+6.8%, 95% CI [+3.9, +9.4]). Per-request decode speed at a fixed number of running requests goes from 221/181/157/141 to 229/187/168/155 tok/s at bs 1/2/3/4.

This merges cleanly with #34394, but #34394 merges `wk`/`weights_proj` on ROCm only while the AITER fused writer stays on, and this PR turns that writer off for GLM-5.3, so whichever lands second needs to reconcile the two.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results.

title: [Diffusion] Speed up LTX-2 guidance and video output
author: BBuf
body: ## Motivation LTX-2's advanced CFG/STG/modality-guidance branches bypass the existing breakable CUDA graph runner. Video decoding also introduces avoidable channels-last layout copies and full-video CPU conversion work. This PR reduces those costs while preserving eager video and audio outputs. ## Modifications - Route the existing advanced-guidance calls through the shared BCG runner and preserve guider/LoRA settings during synthetic warmup. Construct mixed perturbation masks on the device so capture does not copy from unpinned host memory. - Let LTX's fixed-shape, single-GPU SDPA attention stay inside the captured region. Other attention backends, sequence-parallel paths and varlen metadata keep their existing eager breaks. Request-level backend overrides bypass graphs captured with the default backend. - Extend the existing residual-gate kernel to read one `[B, 1, D]` gate row per batch. Noncontiguous AdaLN gate views copy only the small gate, without expanding it over tokens. FP16/BF16 product/add rounding is unchanged. - Keep LTX VAE reflection padding in channels-last storage for ordinary CUDA Conv3d. Convert raw-frame output on the GPU in chunks of at most 64 MiB of FP32 data (or one frame), then complete the pinned CPU transfer before returning NumPy storage. Pinned allocation or CUDA conversion OOM falls back to CPU postprocessing. The generic NumPy thread-pool change has been removed. Merged main through `11bfd868ac36` (#43656): preserve the shared bounded MP4 encoder, audio-first ordering on eligible requests, and encoder fallback. Successful MP4 encoding skips raw-frame materialization; only raw output/fallback calls the chunked postprocessor. No new test files remain: coverage lives in the existing LTX BCG, VAE, frame-output, and modulation suites. SGLang uses eager + BCG, with torch.compile disabled. BCG still requires the existing enable flag; the VAE/output improvements apply without it. ## Accuracy Tests - The existing LTX BCG, VAE layout, frame callback/output, video encoding, Wan streamed-encoding and modulation suites pass **1,089 tests / 58 subtests on GB300** at cleanup commit `5c377d8`. After the final fallback-buffer cleanup, the frame-output suite passes again at `dfd8189`: **19 tests / 15 subtests**. - Coverage retains changed-input/mask replay, request backend fallback, advanced-guidance warmup, batched gates, reflection padding/cache, exact raw-frame conversion, output ownership and MP4/audio fallback ordering. Bounded-conversion and CUDA-conversion-OOM cases extend the existing frame-output suite. All five standalone test files from the initial PR have been consolidated or removed; the existing registered diffusion bridge discovers the retained cases. - Full-model A-B-B-A regression at final head `dfd8189` against main `11bfd868ac36` checks **32 outputs across two prompts/seeds**. Raw video hashes after canonical RGB8 conversion and audio hashes match the eager controls; all saved MP4 files match byte for byte. Native SGLang execution, actual BCG capture, identical schedules and BF16 untiled decode settings are verified. - A real CUDA allocator-cap probe uses BF16 `[1, 3, 121, 1024, 1536]` input with 512 MiB of headroom. The previous full-clip FP32 conversion raises CUDA OOM; the chunked path matches the CPU reference exactly with a 1,258,291,200-byte peak under the 1,679,818,752-byte cap. This is a controlled allocator-cap test, not a claim about a physically full production GPU. - Pre-commit passes. [Targeted H100 CI for the final head](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38147640089) is dispatched separately. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Regression after integrating #43656 Compare main `11bfd868ac36` with final head `dfd8189` on the same GB300 and PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, using the pinned checkpoint and native BF16 recipe below. A-B-B-A uses four fresh processes. Each process runs two prompts/seeds with one warmup and one measurement per prompt in each output mode: 16 timed requests total. The SDK timer includes complete CPU output or complete MP4 writing; evidence hashing is outside the timer. BCG is enabled only for the candidate; torch.compile is disabled in both. | Output mode | Main A / D median | Candidate B / C median | Paired latency reduction | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Raw CPU video/audio | 30.204 / 30.363 s | 26.595 / 26.578 s | 11.95% / 12.47% | | Fully written MP4 | 29.673 / 29.657 s | 27.842 / 27.833 s | 6.17% / 6.15% | The pooled medians improve by **11.97% for raw CPU output** and **6.16% for fully written MP4**. This is a small matched two-prompt regression, not a broad workload performance study. The saved-output comparison includes main's shared bounded encoder; it does not reuse the older baseline numbers below. ### Original benchmark and profiling evidence The following table records the original implementation against `33d2ef175666`; it is not a benchmark against main after #43656. Updated-main validation is recorded above. One GB300, resident BF16 weights, uncached text encoding, 1536×1024×121 output at 24 fps. Stage 1 uses 768×512×121 for 40 steps; stage 2 uses three refinement steps. Both frameworks use the same observed sigma schedules, BF16 VAE input and weights, untiled decoding and disabled autocast. CPU affinity is fixed to cores 8–15 on NUMA node 0. Stage 1 uses video/audio CFG 3/7, STG 1, modality guidance 3, rescale 0.7 and STG block 29. Distilled LoRA strength is 0/1 across the two stages. A benchmark adapter selects these existing request-extra fields in both SGLang baseline and candidate, because the original LTX-2 sampling class does not expose the later per-modality fields. Each fresh process has nine warmup requests and fifteen measured requests across three prompts/seeds. Run order is stock → candidate → Omni → Omni → candidate → stock. The metric ends when the native SDK returns complete CPU video frames and audio; file saving and evidence hashing are excluded. | Mode | Repeat 1 median | Repeat 2 median | | --- | ---: | ---: | | SGLang eager baseline | 29.984 s | 29.864 s | | SGLang eager + BCG candidate | **26.161 s** | **26.185 s** | | vLLM-Omni + regional torch.compile | 26.221 s | 26.242 s | | Latency reduction vs SGLang eager | 12.75% | 12.32% | | Latency reduction vs Omni compile | 0.23% | 0.22% | The cross-framework median advantage is small (about 0.22%); the repeatable within-SGLang improvement is the main performance result. This is a result for the measured workload, not a claim that every prompt or configuration outperforms Omni. A separate profile confirms one real captured segment for each denoising stage, without signature misses. VAE GPU time falls from 1,048.8 ms to 529.2 ms, with copy-kernel time falling from 546.1 ms to 25.5 ms. Profiled runs are excluded from the latency table; those stage timings are not additive estimates of end-to-end gain. Native peak reserved GPU memory decreases from 102,350 MiB to 99,222 MiB (−3.05 GiB) in a separate one-warmup/one-measurement diagnostic for the same workload. This diagnostic's latency is excluded from the table. Omni compilation is verified on all 48 transformer blocks and with nonzero Dynamo graph counters. SGLang and Omni use their supported PyTorch environments, 2.14.1+cu130 and 2.13.0+cu130 respectively; the within-SGLang comparison isolates this PR's gain. Their native noise generators use different packed/unpacked layouts, so matching seeds do not imply cross-framework pixel equality. Exact-output validation compares the candidate against its SGLang baseline. Revisions: SGLang baseline `33d2ef17566685f596b82512e8264456716527f7`; Omni `194b936637f4e7356cc998c2796c67d14d52d854`; Lightricks/LTX-2 checkpoint `dfcc2108383fe1aaa0584bdf55d368a4bdadd90c`. ## Generated video frame comparison Original PNG frames 0, 60, and 120 from the seed-42 benchmark video (1536×1024, 121 frames, 24 fps). These are sampled frames from the actual generated video, not a separate text-to-image run. Only their display width is reduced. SGLang eager and candidate match across the **entire video and audio**, not just these selected frames. Omni is a visual reference; the frameworks use different native RNG layouts. Prompt: “A red fox walks slowly through a snowy forest. The camera follows at eye level. Soft morning light filters through pine trees. Snow crunches softly beneath its paws.” | Frame | SGLang eager | SGLang eager + BCG candidate | Omni regional compile | |---|---|---|---| | 0 | | | | | 60 | | | | | 120 | | | | ## Reproduction [Complete SGLang and vLLM-Omni commands, pinned environments/model revisions, and measurement caveats](https://github.com/BBuf/how-to-optim-algorithm-in-cuda/tree/a03c28c4e30ccd59490bcbc60e61ce51c3d0a50c/artifacts/gb300-diffusion-20261011/README.md); [per-request data and compilation evidence](https://github.com/BBuf/how-to-optim-algorithm-in-cuda/tree/a03c28c4e30ccd59490bcbc60e61ce51c3d0a50c/artifacts/gb300-diffusion-20261011/results). The scripts retain the tested sampling settings and include both stock/candidate and Omni controls. ## Checklist - [x] Format with pre-commit. - [x] Extend existing diffusion and kernel test suites without adding test files. - [x] Complete final repeated accuracy and speed validation. - [x] Follow SGLang code style. - [ ] Documentation: no new CLI option; activation and validation scope are described above. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #38335860874](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38335860874) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #38335860413](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38335860413) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #38335860762](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38335860762)

title: [DSpark] Run the same markov block in the draft graph tail; drop `SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_SAMPLING`
author: hnyls2002
body:
Stacks on #43622.

- The draft graph tail (`DsparkDraftSampler`) calls the same `draft_markov_block` as the eager path, over the graph's hidden states, so graph and eager compute the same tokens and logits.
- The tail always keeps the step logits in a static `[max_bs, gamma, vocab]` buffer and serves greedy and sampling rows in one capture; temperatures and greedy rows are staged once per replay.
- Deletes `StepSampler`, `run_markov_block`, `sample_block`, `sample_block_greedy_fused`, and the `SampleStepTokens` and `BuildStepLocal` kernels.
- Removes `SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_SAMPLING`, its free-memory probe, and the greedy-only tail that sent sampling batches back to the eager path. Removes `SGLANG_DSPARK_OPT_FUSED_GREEDY_MARKOV`. Both are registered as deprecated.
- Drops the redundant `SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_SAMPLING=0` from the Kimi-K3 NPU recipes and test; they already set `SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_PROPOSAL=0`.
- Tests: a captured block replays the eager block (tokens, logits, noise offset), and the captured sampler matches the eager draft of the same batch.

Behavior changes:
- The step-logits buffer `[max_bs, gamma, vocab]` is always allocated when the proposal is folded (FP32 on DeepSeek-V4: about 165 MB per rank at `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64` and gamma 5, about 2 GB at max_bs 256 and gamma 15). It is no longer skipped on a low free-memory reading; a deployment that relied on that fallback can now fail at startup instead.
- The greedy-only tail is gone in this PR, and its replacement, `SGLANG_DSPARK_USE_GREEDY_DRAFT=1`, lands two PRs up the stack. In between, a deployment that set `SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_SAMPLING=0` or `SGLANG_DSPARK_OPT_FUSED_GREEDY_MARKOV=1` runs the sampling tail for temperature-0 batches, which is slower (step logits are written and, on a TP-sharded V4 head, gathered whole each step). This PR and the greedy-draft PR are meant to land together.
- `SGLANG_DSPARK_OPT_FUSED_GREEDY_MARKOV` no longer has an effect; the fused one-row kernel serves the greedy draft.

## Verification

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4x GB300 with the recommended low-latency deployment (TP4, EP4, block size 5, `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64`, custom allreduce on), random 2048-in / 1024-out. The stack column is the top of this stack with the greedy draft off, which runs this layer's tail; main and stack ran back to back.

- `test_dspark_draft_graph.py` and `test_dspark_kernel_parity.py` pass on GB300.
- Draft proposal cost per decode step. "Sampling" is the graph tail from the lm_head on.

| temperature | concurrency (reqs) | main sampling (us/step) | stack sampling (us/step) | main whole draft (us/step) | stack whole draft (us/step) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | 185.0 | 158.3 | 770.8 | 733.7 |
| 0 | 16 | 376.6 | 302.2 | 1218.0 | 1155.4 |
| 1 | 1 | 184.6 | 163.2 | 770.2 | 742.6 |
| 1 | 16 | 376.7 | 327.2 | 1214.0 | 1159.5 |

- TPOT, three runs each:

| temperature | concurrency (reqs) | main TPOT (ms) | stack TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | 0.908 / 0.909 / 0.906 | 0.898 / 0.898 / 0.901 |
| 0 | 16 | 3.968 / 4.247 / 4.148 | 4.226 / 4.078 / 4.142 |
| 1 | 1 | 1.696 / 1.896 / 1.479 | 1.573 / 1.493 / 1.357 |
| 1 | 16 | 5.275 / 5.470 / 5.334 | 5.345 / 5.294 / 5.100 |

- The per-step vocab gather runs inside the draft graph (NVLink push); no communication kernel runs eagerly in the draft proposal.
- GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, on an earlier revision of the stack: main 0.906, stack 0.913.

title: [DSpark] Add `SGLANG_DSPARK_USE_GREEDY_DRAFT`, an argmax draft accepted as one-hot
author: hnyls2002
body:
Stacks on #43669.

- `SGLANG_DSPARK_USE_GREEDY_DRAFT=1` (off by default) drafts every row by argmax, sampling requests included, and keeps no step logits, in the graph tail and in the eager path alike.
- The accept treats the draft as a one-hot distribution, which keeps the rejection and block-verification accepts exact: outputs still follow each request's sampling distribution, at a lower acceptance for high-temperature traffic.
- On a TP-sharded DeepSeek-V4 head each step gathers only per-block candidates. On a vanilla markov head a one-row step folds the bias GEMV, the add and the argmax into one kernel (`MarkovGreedyStep`, kept from before this stack).
- At temperature 0 the outputs are identical to the default draft's.
- Each draft step still broadcasts its tokens under the default `SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC=all`, as every draft path now does; main's greedy-only fused paths skipped it. Narrowing the default sync set drops it.
- The fused kernel is used only when the head's bias is the plain `w2` GEMV of the previous token's embedding (vanilla heads; not Nemotron, gated or RNN) and `w2` has one row per base-logit column; otherwise the shared op runs.
- Tests: the one-row fused block runs the fused kernel, replays the eager block in a graph, and matches the FP32 argmax; which heads may fuse; a greedy draft returns argmax tokens and no step logits; the sampling accept receives a one-hot draft at the target vocab width.

No behavior change unless the variable is set.

## Verification

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4x GB300 with the recommended low-latency deployment (TP4, EP4, block size 5, `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64`, custom allreduce on), random 2048-in / 1024-out, main and this branch back to back.

- `test_dspark_draft_graph.py`, `test_dspark_markov_sample.py`, `test_dspark_kernel_parity.py` and `test_block_verification.py` pass on GB300, as do `test_dspark_draft_block.py`, `test_dspark_greedy_draft_accept.py` and `test_spec_tp_sync.py`.
- Greedy draft at temperature 0, concurrency 1. "Sampling" is the graph tail from the lm_head on.

| server | TPOT (ms) | sampling (us/step) | whole draft (us/step) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.908 / 0.909 / 0.906 | 185.0 | 770.8 |
| this branch, greedy draft | 0.896 / 0.901 / 0.897 | 146.2 | 729.6 |

- GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, on an earlier revision of the stack: greedy draft 0.901 and 0.904 over two runs, main 0.906.
- ShareGPT at temperature 1: the greedy draft's accept length is about 14% lower than the default draft's, as expected from drafting by argmax.

title: [diffusion] perf: layerwise offload for the LTX-2.5 Gemma-4 text encoder
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

LTX-2.5's text encoder is Gemma-4-Unified: 23.9 GB in bf16. Its 48 decoder layers are 21.8 GB and its vocab table is 2.0 GB. It has no SGLang port and loads through `transformers.AutoModel`, so it lacks `LayerwiseOffloadableModuleMixin`. As a result, `--layerwise-offload-components text_encoder` raises:

```
ComponentResidencyError: Components selected for layerwise-offload do not support it: ['text_encoder']
```

On a 32 GB card the only remaining placement is component offload. Every request moves the whole text encoder, the 6 GB connectors and the VAE onto the GPU and back: roughly 60 GB of PCIe traffic and a 31.2 GB peak.



## Modifications

Three commits:

1. **Layerwise-offload adapter for Gemma-4-Unified**, in the new file `runtime/models/encoders/gemma_4_unified.py`.
   - After the native load, the module's class is swapped for a subclass that also carries the mixin, with `layer_names=["language_model.layers"]`. Weights, forward, signature and class name are unchanged.
   - The 2.0 GB vocab table is declared host-resident (`host_resident_table_names`).
   - Gemma's embedding multiplies by a 0-dim `embed_scale` buffer, which follows the module to the device. A host-side gather cannot use it there, so the embedding forward moves the scale to the gather's device. The result is bit-exact.
   - Adapters are registered by transformers class name in `NATIVE_LAYERWISE_ADAPTERS`.
2. **Apply native layerwise adapters in `TextEncoderLoader.load_native`** (+21 lines). The loader looks up the adapter by class name, so only `Gemma4UnifiedModel` changes; every other encoder loads as before.
3. **Docs:** LTX-2.5 cookbook presets for 1x and 2x 32 GB GPUs.

New unit test `test_gemma4_unified_layerwise_offload.py` checks that outputs are identical after the class swap and with the host-resident embedding table.

## Accuracy Tests

- **Text encoder:** all 49 hidden states are identical (max-abs 0) between the resident and layerwise encoder, on a 1024-token prompt.
- **1 GPU, end to end** (960x544x121f, 8 steps, seed 42): the output mp4 is **byte-identical** to before.
- **2 GPUs:** the same placement with tiled decode is pixel-identical to before. With the untiled parallel decode used in the 2-GPU preset (`--vae-tiling false --vae-sp false`), it is 34.1 dB PSNR against the tiled output. That difference comes from tile blending; the frames look the same and show no seams.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Setup: RTX 5090 32 GB (SM120, PCIe, no P2P), LTX-2.5 distilled one-stage T2V, 960x544x121f, 8 steps, conv VAE. Client wall-clock median of 3 runs after 1 warmup run.

| Config | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 GPU, `--dit-layerwise-offload true --layerwise-offload-components dit text_encoder` (connectors and VAEs resident) | 17.0 s (component offload), peak 31.2 GB | **15.2 s**, peak **17.1 GB** |
| 2 GPUs Ulysses2, same + `--vae-tiling false --vae-sp false` | 21.8 s | **18.2 s** |
| 2 GPUs, + `--dit-layerwise-resident-layers 12` | – | **17.1 s**, peak 25.9 GB |

1-GPU stage times:
- text encoding: 1.03 → 0.84 s
- connectors: 1.08 → 0.04 s, now resident
- a 0.2 s timestep-preparation stall is gone


## Notes

- **Host memory:** on 2 GPUs, each rank now pins about 55 GB of host memory (DiT 35 + TE 20), up from about 35 GB. Sharing one host copy across ranks is not part of this PR.
- **The LTX2 VAE overrides `decode()`**, so it does not take the generic parallel tiled decode. Its own height-split parallel decode needs tiling off; the 2-GPU preset documents the flags.

title: [Perf] async-probe: Fuse asynchronous NaN validation into one kernel
author: sshleifer
body:
## Motivation

Enabled NaN validation launches separate `isnan`, reduction, negation, and device-assert kernels. This adds overhead to logits and probability checks, including non-contiguous vocabulary slices.

## Modifications

Fuse CUDA floating-point NaN validation into one read-only Triton kernel. Support contiguous tensors and strided 2D views, including transposes, storage offsets, and broadcast rows. Use 64-bit offsets and a flat launch grid for large strides and tall views.

Keep device assertions enabled with `TRITON_DEBUG=0`, including during CUDA graph replay. Keep the Torch fallback for compiled callers: compilation can eliminate the read-only Triton call and silently lose the assertion. Other devices/dtypes and higher-rank non-contiguous inputs also retain the Torch path.

NaNs still fail asynchronously, infinities remain valid, and inputs remain unchanged. The existing flags and their defaults are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

26 tests passed on NVIDIA GB300 (202 seconds). Coverage includes fatal NaNs in eager execution, CUDA graph replay, compiled callers, strided/transposed inputs, and strided graph replay; FP16/BF16/FP32/FP64 finite and infinite inputs; block boundaries; both enable flags; disabled CUDA checks; excluded NaN padding; storage offsets; row/column strides; and empty, broadcast, and 65,537-row views. Each fatal assertion runs in a subprocess so its invalid CUDA context cannot affect other tests.

Registered in `base-b-test-1-gpu-small`.

Reproduce:

```bash
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/utils/test_async_probe.py -q
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

NVIDIA GB300, PyTorch 2.11, Triton 3.6. Median GPU microseconds over three CUDA-graph rounds. Each large-input round cycles through disjoint tensors totaling at least 512 MiB; the 16×8 case measures launch overhead. Baseline is the existing Torch expression.

| Input | Torch (μs) | Fused (μs) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| FP32 contiguous 16x154856 | 24.87 | 3.34 |
| FP32 vocabulary slice 16x154856 | 29.20 | 3.47 |
| FP32 vocabulary slice 64x154856 | 47.22 | 7.86 |
| BF16 vocabulary slice 16x154856 | 29.03 | 3.02 |
| FP32 transposed vocabulary slice 16x154856 | 29.29 | 3.36 |
| FP32 contiguous 16x8 | 12.94 | 1.07 |

These are isolated operator timings; full-model throughput was not measured.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark reproduction script</summary>

Save as `bench_async_nan.py` and run `python bench_async_nan.py` on one CUDA GPU with this checkout installed.

```python
import json
import os
import statistics

os.environ['SGLANG_ENABLE_NAN_LOGITS_CHECK'] = '1'
os.environ['SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT'] = '0'

import torch
import triton
from sglang.srt.utils.async_probe import maybe_detect_nan


def baseline(x):
    torch._assert_async(~torch.any(torch.isnan(x)), 'NaN detected! benchmark')


def fused(x):
    maybe_detect_nan(x, 'benchmark')


def measure(fn, tensors):
    for x in tensors:
        fn(x)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    def check_all():
        for x in tensors:
            fn(x)
    return statistics.median(triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph(check_all, rep=1000) * 1000 / len(tensors) for _ in range(3))


print(json.dumps({'gpu': torch.cuda.get_device_name(), 'torch': torch.__version__, 'triton': triton.__version__}), flush=True)
for label, dtype, rows, cols, sliced, transposed in (
    ('FP32 contiguous 16x154856', torch.float32, 16, 154856, False, False),
    ('FP32 vocabulary slice 16x154856', torch.float32, 16, 154856, True, False),
    ('FP32 vocabulary slice 64x154856', torch.float32, 64, 154856, True, False),
    ('BF16 vocabulary slice 16x154856', torch.bfloat16, 16, 154856, True, False),
    ('FP32 transposed vocabulary slice 16x154856', torch.float32, 16, 154856, True, True),
    ('FP32 contiguous 16x8', torch.float32, 16, 8, False, False),
):
    n = max(1, triton.cdiv(512 * 1024**2, rows * cols * torch.empty((), dtype=dtype).element_size())) if cols > 8 else 1
    tensors = [torch.randn(rows, cols + int(sliced), dtype=dtype, device='cuda')[:, :cols] for _ in range(n)]
    if transposed:
        tensors = [x.T for x in tensors]
    before = measure(baseline, tensors)
    after = measure(fused, tensors)
    print(json.dumps({'input': label, 'tensors': n, 'torch_us': round(before, 2), 'fused_us': round(after, 2)}), flush=True)
    del tensors
```
</details>

title: [Perf] deepseek-v4.1: Replay the breakable prefill CUDA graph at any context length
author: jyizheng
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1's breakable prefill CUDA graph is captured at a 16,384-token context width, and every batch with a longer context runs eager. The width is the candidate window (2,048 blocks of 8 tokens): inside it the captured full top-k equals the two-level candidate selection, and past it it does not. Eager DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill is bound by host kernel launches, so long-context requests lose the graph where it would help most.

## Modifications

The graph replays at any context length when the two-level candidate indexer runs on DeepGEMM (SM100, no prefill context parallelism, no ratio-4/128 layers):

- The full top-k layers (the ratio-2 index sources and the ratio-1 candidate source) score as eager breaks over the live batch, at the real context length, and write the sparse indices the attention break reads (`_prefill_graph_full_topk_break`). The candidate source also returns its block table (`SparseTableBackend.publish_prefill_graph`), which is copied into the addresses the consumers were captured with.
- The ratio-1 consumers always take the two-level path inside the graph (`SparseTableBackend.consume_prefill_captured`) and score only the published candidate blocks, so nothing captured depends on the context length.
- The replayed context limit moves from the DeepSeek-V4.1 server-args hook into the attention backend. `prefill_cuda_graph_default_max_seq_len` (None for every other backend) is 16,384 while the captured indexer bounds the context and None when any context replays. The runner uses it only when `cuda_graph_config[prefill].max_seq_len` is unset, so an explicit `--cuda-graph-max-seq-len-prefill` always applies.
- Replay metadata is built at the live context, decided once for the full rows and the decoder-replay late-layer tail (`_prefill_graph_context_width`). In two-level mode the ratio-1/2 indexer metadata is reference-assigned on refresh instead of copied in place.
- With decoder SWA bounded replay (the default), the candidate source is the late-layer tail's first layer, so its break takes the tail's request rows and positions.
- An idle DP-attention rank that replays the graph scores its fabricated rows instead of asserting.
- Each layer's candidate table is shared by all captured buckets.

Configurations without the candidate indexer (no candidate blocks, the torch prefill path, prefill context parallelism, or pre-SM100 GPUs) keep the 16K limit and today's behavior. The prefill graph stays opt-in for DeepSeek-V4.1 (`--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`).

## Accuracy Tests

GB300 with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4 (DSPARK, chunked prefill 8192) and DEP2 with MegaMoE, against main:

- First-token top-20 distributions, as total variation distance from main eager with decoder replay on:
  - two text needles (134K and 284K tokens): at most 0.019; main's own 16K graph is at 0.026, and a second main eager run at 0.013;
  - 155,648- and 327,680-token prefixes, cold and with 256 or 1,024 new tokens after them: at most 0.010; main's 16K graph is at 0.011, and the second eager run at 0.010.
  - Results are similar with decoder replay off and with encoder replay on, and both needles are retrieved in every run.
- GSM8K (200 questions, 8-shot prefix): 97.0% on TP4 and 97.5% on DEP2, against main eager's 97.0% and 98.0%.
- With an explicit `--cuda-graph-max-seq-len-prefill 16384`, and with `SGLANG_DSV41_TORCH_PREFILL_INDEXER=1` (no two-level candidates, so the backend default of 16,384 applies), 14 of the same 123 prefill batches replay, as on main's 16K graph; by default 121 do.
- One unit test checks the replay limit and the metadata width: a replay that is exact at any length has no default limit and its metadata spans the live context; otherwise both stay at the captured indexer width (16K).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

TTFT, TP4, one request, decoder replay on, median of 3:

| Cached prefix (tokens) | New tokens | main, 16K graph (ms) | this PR (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 256 | 34.8 | 39.7 |
| 0 | 1,024 | 43.2 | 43.9 |
| 0 | 8,000 | 109.7 | 101.2 |
| 155,648 | 256 | 187.8 | 66.0 |
| 155,648 | 1,024 | 195.4 | 76.7 |
| 155,648 | 8,000 | 199.6 | 140.5 |
| 327,680 | 256 | 226.3 | 106.0 |
| 327,680 | 1,024 | 236.9 | 119.8 |
| 327,680 | 8,000 | 244.8 | 197.5 |

- A cold prefill of 155,648 / 327,680 tokens takes 1,856 / 4,150 ms, against main's 3,031 / 6,586 ms.
- Short prompts pay for the four breaks: one-step traces show the same GPU time as main and more host time at the breaks.
- Prefill graph capture memory with decoder replay on: 5.33 GB per GPU, against main's 5.35 GB.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [DCP] Decode context parallelism for DSA (GLM-5.2 / GLM-5.3) with MTP
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

`--dcp-size > 1` does not work for the RoPE DSA models (GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V3.2): the sparse backend returns no LSE, the index-K cache and the MTP draft pool are sized per rank while the allocator hands out widened slots, and the TRT-LLM buffers are sized for one rank's heads. Builds on the approach of #42536 (co-authored with @vincentzed) and the Flash stack #40433 / #40434.

## Modifications

- **Target KV** stays striped by position (unchanged `main` layout). The **index-K cache is replicated** and addressed by the widened allocator slot, so every rank scores the whole sequence and selects the global top-k.
- **Attention**: one Triton kernel keeps the top-k slots this rank owns, maps them to local rows and compacts them; the TRT-LLM sparse kernel runs on the DCP group's gathered query heads with `return_lse`, and the existing MLA DCP merge combines the partials. Decode, target verify and extend all take this path (no prefix-KV gather). Shared-top-k layers reuse the localized table (21 remaps per step instead of 78).
- **MTP draft (nextn)**: the pool is replicated over the widened slots (`dcp_replicated`, kernel page stays 64) and the draft attends without the DCP group (`is_nextn` / `is_draft_worker`, as the Qwen3.5 draft does), so MTP index share feeds the draft directly.
- **Accounting**: index keys and the draft pool are charged `dcp_size` times per physical token on every platform (the NPU-only guards are dropped).
- **Launch validation**: the generic DCP hook now rejects prefill CP with `--dcp-size > 1`; the DSA override rejects HiSparse, HiCache, PD disaggregation and tree drafting, and defaults the DSA backends to `trtllm` (`index_kpool > 1` was already rejected on `main`).
- **Fast follows** (rejected at launch for now): HiCache and PD disaggregation need the replicated index-K cache's widened page geometry in the host pool and the transfer page-id lists; other DSA backends need to return the LSE under DCP.
- Kept from #42536: the LSE combine keeps all-empty padding rows at zero. Not kept: the head folding to at most 32 heads per trtllm call. Vincent's reproducer (comment below) does fail on B300 with FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, for exactly 64 heads with short KV at >= 1024 rows per call (16, 32 and 128 heads are clean up to 65535 rows), so this is a kernel bug that only DCP8 extend can hit. It will be filed with FlashInfer once the cause is narrowed down; the gathered heads go to the kernel in one call.

Design notes with permalinks: `dsa-dcp-design.md` (shared separately).

## Accuracy Tests

`zai-org/GLM-5.3` (FP8), 8xB300, `--tp 8 --mem-fraction-static 0.88 --max-running-requests 64`, branch at `28bb3d6074`. MTP = `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6`. GSM8K: `few_shot_gsm8k`, 8-shot, 1319 questions. AIME26: `sgl-eval run aime26 --n-repeats 4` with the GLM-5.2-FP8 preset (200k max tokens).

| Config | GSM8K acc | AIME26 pass@1 (avg of 4) | AIME26 pass@4 | AIME26 gen tok/s | MTP accept len |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8 | 0.912 | 99.17% | 100% | 1140 | - |
| TP8 + DCP2 | 0.917 | 99.17% | 100% | 1041 | - |
| TP8 + DCP2 + MTP | 0.919 | 95.83% | 100% | 1876 | 3.51 |
| TP8 + DCP8 | 0.914 | 95.00% | 100% | 838 | - |
| TP8 + DCP8 + MTP | 0.919 | 95.00% | 100% | 1784 | 3.62 |

Spot checks (GSM8K, 300-400 questions): `--dcp-comm-backend ag_rs` DCP2 + MTP 0.907; an 8192-token-per-rank pool so the last allocator page is in use, DCP2 0.903 and DCP2 + MTP 0.907; without head folding, DCP8 0.943 and DCP8 + MTP 0.913 (the 64-head case).

AIME26 pass@1 spread is sampling noise: every run loses problem 14 to the 200k cap (including TP8), and the remaining misses are either a correct final line without `\boxed{}` (3 in DCP2 + MTP, 2 in DCP8) or single-sample arithmetic slips; no run shows degenerate output. The DCP2 + MTP run surfaced one bug, fixed in `28bb3d6074`: the DSA draft's one-shot MHA prefill keyed its prefix all-gather on the global DCP flag instead of the layer's `dcp_size`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format with pre-commit.
- [x] GPU kernel test (localize kernel, merged shards vs the unsharded kernel at 64 heads) and a registered 4-GPU GLM-5.3 TP4 + DCP2 + MTP GSM8K test.
- [x] Update `docs/docs/advanced_features/dcp.mdx`.
- [x] Accuracy results (above).

title: [DeepSeek-V4.1] Run decoder SWA bounded replay inside the breakable prefill CUDA graph
author: jyizheng
body:
## Motivation

`--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` refuses every prefill CUDA graph backend, so DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill runs eager whenever bounded replay is on. On GB300 the eager prefill step is host-launch-bound (~2.5k launches per request per rank, ~10 ms of GPU work inside a ~230 ms step), so this is the dominant TTFT cost at low and medium concurrency.

This is the same gap #42078, #42909, #43440 and #43534 address. The variant here keeps the late layers on their bounded-replay tail **inside the same breakable prefill graph** instead of capturing separate late-layer graphs or running the captured late layers on full rows; the measurements below are why.

## Modifications

- The late layers (after the last KV source layer) run over a per-shape tail block inside the captured graph: `tail_rows = min(max_running_requests x 128, shape tokens)`. The tail's extend/positions/scatter indices and SWA write locations live in persistent, block-sized buffers (padding rows point at slot 0), so the graph replays with no reallocation; one tail metadata per block size is built the prefill-graph way (`use_prefill_cuda_graph=True`) and refreshed in place on every replay (`_prefill_graph_tail_metadata`, `prefill_graph_enter/exit_late_layer_tail`).
- `DeepseekV4Model.forward` switches to the tail at the `enter`/`exit` eager breaks and scatters the tail rows back (`_scatter_tail_rows` graph branch); the outer forward slices logits by `hidden_states_token_indices`, which the runner's `_trim_logits_output` now carries so the DSpark injector sees the right rows.
- `init_forward_metadata_in_graph` clears `tail_forward_metadata` on the decode/target-verify graph paths: the prefill graph capture/replay leaves it set, and the decode graph capture that follows otherwise slices a decode publish in `_publish_candidate_metadata` (`NotImplementedError: _SparseTable is not a prefill publish`).
- `validate_deepseek_v41_features` admits `Backend.BREAKABLE` with decoder bounded replay (encoder replay still eager).

With this, `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` and `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable` work together; the capture width (`--cuda-graph-max-seq-len-prefill`, default 16k) is unchanged. #43733 builds on this to replay the graph at any context length.

## Accuracy Tests

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 1P1D on GB300 (prefill TP4 + decode TP4, DSpark PD, FlashMLA): capture of 74 shapes; needle prompts at 4.5k / 11k / 40k and greedy 24k / 40k / 86k-token prompts return the expected key with text matching the eager run (divergence within eager run-to-run noise); six-rung real-trace replay (300 s per rung) 100% success at every rung. Validated on the Sep-24 nightly series and on the Oct-8 nightly (7760d526) stack; the rebase onto current `main` applies cleanly and is compile- and lint-checked. A GPU run on `main` itself is still owed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same deployment, real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash production trace (ISL median 6.7k / p90 127k), three arms that differ only in the late-layer handling: eager + bounded replay (today), breakable graph with the late layers on full rows (bounded replay off inside the graph), and this PR (late layers on the tail inside the graph). All graph arms capture at 16k.

| conc | TTFT p50 eager / full rows / tail | TTFT p90 | output tok/min per chip | TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 272 / 179 / **152** ms | 1,071 / 1,162 / **1,026** | 2,292 / 2,268 / **2,375** | 2.67 / 2.75 / 2.64 |
| 4 | 496 / 362 / **327** | 1,903 / 1,900 / 1,940 | 7,687 / 7,618 / **7,989** | 2.87 / 2.97 / 2.87 |
| 8 | 748 / **519** / 545 | 2,498 / 2,561 / **2,149** | 12,790 / 12,813 / **13,870** | 3.11 / 3.24 / 3.11 |
| 16 | 1,215 / 1,397 / **1,226** | 6,419 / 10,017 / **6,512** | 17,123 / 16,270 / **17,340** | 3.64 / 3.73 / 3.70 |
| 32 | 3,304 / 3,667 / **3,415** | 17,899 / 19,676 / **17,841** | 20,115 / 19,833 / 20,073 | 4.12 / 4.12 / 4.15 |

title: [Test] Re-anchor the VLM flashinfer throughput floor
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

`test_vlm_serving_flashinfer` fails its offline throughput check (`output_throughput >= 5940`) on 5090 runners, with measurements of 5176–5939 tok/s.

#43564 reserves the full remaining output for running `ignore_eos` requests during prefill admission. Those requests always generate their full `max_new_tokens`, so admission no longer discounts them by `new_token_ratio`.

In this benchmark:
- **Workload:** 200 fixed-length requests, each about 410 input + 2048 output tokens.
- **KV pool:** 411,675 tokens, enough for about 167 of these requests at full length.
- **Admission:** 170 requests run at once, with no retractions. The other 30 wait in the queue and run afterwards as a small-batch tail.

This lowers offline output throughput by design.

Only offline output throughput is affected. The online phase sends 50 requests at 1 per second and stays well below the admission limit. Its medians, all within their limits:

| Metric | Limit | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| e2e | 17480 ms | 16031–16159 ms |
| TTFT | 83 ms | 66–77 ms |
| ITL | 8.4 ms | 7.61–7.72 ms |

## Modifications

Lower the floor from 5940 to 4510, using the `basic_perf` anchoring rule from #40617, worst sample / (1 + max(0.10, spread)), on 8 CI attempts on 5090 runners:

`5851.86, 5831.51, 5471.16, 5295.27, 5210.99, 5175.67, 5939.31, 5918.90`

That gives a worst of 5175.67, a spread of 14.75% and a floor of 5175.67 / 1.1475 = 4510.2. Every sample clears the new floor by at least 10%.

title: [Fix] Link cuda_ipc JIT against CUDA driver stubs dir
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## What

`_init_ipc_manager` links the `cuda_ipc` JIT module with a bare `-lcuda`. Where `libcuda.so` isn't on the linker search path, the build fails (`ld: cannot find -lcuda`); `parallel_state.py` catches it with a warning and continues with custom allreduce disabled, so affected setups fall back to NCCL (~5x slower per call in the incident we measured). Fix: use `cuda_stubs_dir()`, same as `dsv4/wo_a.py` and `kda_ptx_prefill`.

## Why it wasn't caught before

Not a recent regression — bare `-lcuda` dates to the v2 rewrite (#31049). It's masked only in images that symlink the stub into the system libdir (AOT, sgl-deep-ep). The main `docker/Dockerfile` (release + dev images) doesn't; we hit it on a dev-image GB300 box with no `/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so`.

Sibling with the same flags: `vsa_block_sparse_sm100_jit.py` (untouched here — different subsystem, source-level exposure only).

## Verification (GB300, previously failing)

- old flags → build fails (control)
- fixed flags → links, `register_once()` succeeds
- no change where the link already worked

title: [Perf] dsa: Route the k-pool indexer top-k through the top-k v2 kernel
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

The GLM-5.3-Flash k-pool indexer selects its top-k pooled groups with `kpool_topk_transform`, which runs one thread block per row. At decode time there is one row per request, so a single block scans the whole pooled history while the rest of the GPU idles. At 1M context this costs about 84 us per DSA layer per decode step, which is most of the decode slowdown from short to long context.

The top-k v2 kernel already splits long rows across thread-block clusters. This PR routes the k-pool indexer through it, with pool expansion, tail append and the output transform fused into the same kernel.

## Modifications

- **Fused k-pool mode in top-k v2** (`TopKMode::KPOOL`, `transform_kpool`): selection over pooled scores plus pool expansion, tail append and page-table or offset mapping in one launch, on every dispatch route (register, streaming, cluster, persistent cluster). The launch dispatch is shared with `transform_paged` through `launch<kMode>()`.
- **Ragged k-pool entry point** (`transform_kpool_ragged`): per-row windows (`row_starts`, `page_table_row_index`) for prefill and for any caller without a plan. Its select-then-transform body is shared with the ROCm `topk_packed_kernel` through `ragged_select_transform`.
- **Plans live in metadata**: decode and verify metadata build the top-k v2 plan once per forward, before the logits kernel, and refresh it on CUDA-graph replay. Rows without a matching plan take the ragged path.
- `topk_from_pooled_history_logits` dispatches to the planned path, then the ragged path, then the existing kernels. `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=0` keeps the existing kernels.

## Accuracy Tests

- Kernel parity against the existing fused kernel: every output mode (no transform, page table, page table with row index, offsets), with and without tail columns, aligned and unaligned `row_starts`, short and zero-length rows. All selections match, up to exact score ties at the cut-off.
- CUDA-graph replay with the plan refreshed between replays, batch 1 to 300, covering every cluster dispatch route including the persistent cluster: 0 mismatches.
- GSM8K with `sgl-eval run gsm8k --max-tokens 16384 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95` (1319 questions), GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 on B300 with the cookbook commands:

| Configuration | main | this PR | Eval time main | Eval time this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High Throughput | 97.04% | 96.89% | 1m 55s | 1m 55s |
| Low Latency (MTP 5/1/6) | 97.12% | 96.89% | 1m 37s | 1m 28s |

Both gaps are 2 to 3 questions, within run-to-run spread at temperature 1.0. GSM8K sequences mostly stay below the 2048-token top-k budget, so this run validates the metadata, plan and transform path end to end.

- Long-context selection with `sgl-eval run ruler2 --max-tokens 16384 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95` (all 12 subtasks, the same generated datasets on both servers), High Throughput cookbook command. Score is the RULER2 headline; the family columns average the four multi-key NIAH, four multi-value NIAH and four QA subtasks:

| Context | Samples | Score main | Score this PR | MK-NIAH main / PR | MV-NIAH main / PR | QA main / PR | Eval time main / PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128K | 300 | 86.63% | 88.41% | 93.0 / 95.0 | 79.9 / 79.2 | 87.0 / 91.0 | 21m 0s / 18m 44s |
| 512K | 120 | 79.12% | 77.66% | 92.4 / 92.5 | 54.9 / 53.0 | 90.0 / 87.5 | 28m 5s / 25m 50s |
| 1M | 60 | 72.72% | 72.94% | 95.0 / 85.1 | 23.2 / 43.7 | 100.0 / 90.0 | 27m 55s / 26m 48s |

The headline differences change sign across lengths and stay within sampling noise (about 2 points at 128K and 3.5 points at 512K). At 1M each subtask has 5 samples, so family averages move by up to 20 points per sample in both directions. Error rate is 0% and truncation at most 3.3% on every run.

Eval times are the wall-clock time of each `sgl-eval` run (256 concurrent requests for GSM8K; 16 for RULER2 at 128K and 512K, 8 at 1M). In total the accuracy evals took 2h 35m: GSM8K 6m 55s (four runs), RULER2 1h 17m on main and 1h 11m on this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Top-k op on B300, GLM-5.3-Flash shapes (`index_topk` 2048, `index_kpool` 4).

Decode (CUDA graph, score width fixed at 1M context, time per call in us). Scores are written by the logits kernel immediately before top-k, so the L2-hot measurement matches serving:

| Batch \ context | 4K | 32K | 131K | 262K | 1M |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6.7 -> 2.8 | 9.1 -> 4.1 | 14.9 -> 7.2 | 30.3 -> 7.5 | 83.3 -> 8.9 |
| 8 | 6.9 -> 3.2 | 9.3 -> 4.3 | 15.2 -> 7.6 | 30.9 -> 8.2 | 83.0 -> 11.2 |
| 32 | 6.7 -> 3.7 | 9.7 -> 5.4 | 15.4 -> 10.7 | 30.9 -> 11.3 | 83.5 -> 16.0 |
| 128 | 7.1 -> 4.8 | 10.3 -> 6.1 | 16.2 -> 10.9 | 31.7 -> 15.6 | 160.4 -> 82.4 |

Prefill (ragged path, causal rows ending at the given context, time per call in us; the score buffer far exceeds L2):

| Rows | Context | main | this PR | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 1M | 2429.2 | 1298.5 | 1.87x |
| 4096 | 262K | 598.4 | 333.6 | 1.79x |
| 16384 | 65K | 881.5 | 480.6 | 1.83x |
| 16384 | 16K | 450.8 | 241.9 | 1.86x |
| 2048 | 8K | 62.1 | 33.1 | 1.87x |

End to end, `python -m sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server` at batch 1 with 256 output tokens (cache flushed per case), High Throughput cookbook command on B300. Each sweep ran three times per server; the first pass includes one-time JIT compilation, so the table is the mean of passes 2 and 3:

| Input | TTFT main (s) | TTFT this PR (s) | ITL main (ms) | ITL this PR (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8K | 0.214 | 0.214 | 4.68 | 4.61 |
| 128K | 2.279 | 2.216 | 4.76 | 4.68 |
| 512K | 10.530 | 10.178 | 5.17 | 4.76 |
| 1M | 24.917 | 23.240 | 5.66 | 4.86 |

At 1M context, ITL drops 14.2% and TTFT 6.7%.

title: [Perf] DeepSeek-V4: Fuse inverse RoPE into wo_a FP8 quantization
author: Phoenix3334
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 applies inverse RoPE to attention output before the `wo_a` projection. The CUDA UE8M0 FP8 path currently launches inverse RoPE separately, writes rotated BF16 values to memory, and reloads them for activation quantization.

This PR folds inverse RoPE into the `wo_a` quantization kernel, keeping rotated values in registers and preserving the intermediate BF16 rounding boundary. It complements [#39957](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39957), which fuses inverse RoPE with a small-batch BF16 wo_a projection. This PR instead quantizes the activation before the FP8 wo_a DeepGEMM path.

[#37658](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37658) introduced the analogous inverse-RoPE + FP8 input-quantization optimization on ROCm/aiter and the existing `SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_FUSED_INVROPE` flag. This PR extends that flag to the CUDA UE8M0 path. The BF16 and FP8 wo_a gates are mutually exclusive, so their reported speedups are not additive.

## Modifications

- Fuse inverse RoPE into the CUDA wo_a activation quantization kernel, rotating the last 64 dimensions of each 512-dimensional head.
- Preserve BF16 rounding before quantization, native packed-int32 UE8M0 scale storage and PDL dependencies.
- Issue position/frequency loads early and vectorize frequency loads; keep the selected launch configuration.
- Share the quantization / packed-scale epilogue and host tensor validation between fused and unfused kernels; reuse Python output allocation.
- Cache configuration-derived eligibility in `MQALayer.__init__`; check graph state, pre-applied inverse RoPE and current tensor properties at execution time.
- Reuse `SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_FUSED_INVROPE`, off by default, with existing fallbacks.
- Add only two focused GPU tests to the existing test file: production numerical equivalence and CUDA Graph replay with updated inputs. An existing CPU fixture that bypasses initialization receives the new attribute's default.

## Accuracy Tests

### Current-head upstream kernel validation (2026-11-02)

PR head: `fb4e80ea8474e8fdb7aab692119202f4834a424c`. CI checked out merge `5da168b82470b256b49f494dc27ceb991c4399c1`, combining this head with upstream main `1599b166ac856f4fd192feb2c16304fae7860a72`.

The [B200 kernel job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41413851551/job/125186911527) executed `test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_fp8_wo_a.py`: **all 7 tests passed**.

```text
[CI Test Method] TestDeepSeekV4FP8WoA.test_fused_inverse_rope_quant_cuda_graph
[CI Test Method] TestDeepSeekV4FP8WoA.test_fused_inverse_rope_quant_matches_production
.......
Ran 7 tests in 12.830s
OK
```

The runner summary also records this file as `"passed": true` (`elapsed: 23` seconds for the file subprocess, distinct from unittest's 12.830 seconds). This covers both new tests—production-path numerical equivalence for FP8 codes and packed scales, and CUDA Graph capture/replay with updated inputs—alongside the existing quantization-path tests. [Hosted Lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41413851247/job/125172847972) also passed on this head.

These are kernel correctness and graph-replay results for the current head. They do not establish full-model serving accuracy, bitwise-equal serving logits, or post-refactor performance gains. Full-model serving and performance validation after the refactor remain pending.

### Historical local GPU validation (B300, aiopt v0.5.21)

**Local GPU validation uses aiopt v0.5.21 on 8×B300.** It shares upstream's packed-int32 UE8M0 contract. On that backport:
- Both new tests passed: strided BF16 inputs, T ∈ {0,1,32,100,777,2047,8192,8193}, G ∈ {2,16}, FP8 codes, packed scales and strides; graph capture/replay with updated input.
- Serving startup completed decode CUDA Graph capture.
- Five greedy prompts, up to 64 generated tokens each: two additional independent baseline startups matched each other and the fused run on all returned texts.
- The first baseline startup differed on one prompt. Subsequent comparisons matched; the cause remains unresolved. Returned-text equality does not establish bitwise-equal logits or internal serving tensors.

These local GPU results **predate cleanup commit `7c5d3eb7ce`**. That commit shares the quantization code and caches eligibility. Subsequent main-based B200 kernel validation is documented below; full-model serving validation after the refactor remains pending. No full model accuracy evaluation is claimed.

Local checks on the cleanup: Python syntax, Ruff, isort and clang-format passed. An exhaustive static eligibility comparison matched the previous predicate for configurations with attention output width equal to the configured head dimension.

### Source preparation and current head (2026-11-02)

The branch was originally rebased onto main `c757c4bb7c55d1eb69fdb2bdc6e6fb8507acb7a0` and subsequently updated by merging main. The current head is `fb4e80ea8474e8fdb7aab692119202f4834a424c`, with upstream main `1599b166ac856f4fd192feb2c16304fae7860a72` incorporated.

The quantization helper and kernel tests follow upstream's `ops/quantization` paths, with imports updated accordingly. The shared host validation retains upstream's `kDLGPU` device definition. Repository-pinned pre-commit checks on the six changed files, Python syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed during the earlier rebase preparation. Current-head hosted Lint and B200 kernel results are documented above. Full-model serving and performance validation after the cleanup/rebase remain pending; the historical performance results below are not measurements of this current head.

### Upstream CI and DCP fixture correction (2026-11-01)

At `38c39bddb75b4b53fdcc1fd2d791307f4f973fdc` (via CI merge `769fc5fcce14`), [B200 CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41303149108/job/124869681626) executed `test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_fp8_wo_a.py`: **7 tests passed** (`Ran 7 tests in 11.821s; OK`). This includes production-path numerical equivalence, CUDA Graph replay, and the existing quantization-path tests. These are main-based kernel correctness results; they do not revalidate the historical performance gains or full-model serving behavior.

That run's [CPU failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41303149108/job/124869681607) was the independent DCP replay fixture missing `skips_prefill_metadata_on_idle_dp_rank`. The test file was identical in the PR head and its main base (Git blob `ef5beb976949ec8fb56be440812c166c5e2b2177`).

Follow-up commit [`289c324`](https://github.com/Phoenix3334/sglang/commit/289c324cf5d64108e73a52580172913ec6bc7b4d) carries the **one-line test-fixture correction from mickqian's [#47736](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47736)** (source commit `be43d568ca8115e173bd4b9f5d106a3060ae1f8b`): set `skips_prefill_metadata_on_idle_dp_rank=False` on the mocked backend. The corrected file matches that source exactly. No production kernel/model code or B200 tests changed after the passing run. The subsequent CI run was stopped by the independent decode-queue fixture failure described below.

### Decode-queue scheduler fixture correction (2026-11-01)

The next [CPU run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41316331423/job/124877244394) stopped in `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py::TestHeldDestinationPublication::test_publishes_while_retracted_requests_wait`: its mocked scheduler lacks `tree_cache`, which `process_decode_queue` now reads even with HiCache disabled. Both the failing test and `disaggregation/decode.py` are identical between that CI merge (`632c7f4`) and its actual upstream main parent (`e298298`), so this is a second independent baseline fixture issue. That shard stopped before executing its scheduled DCP test.

Commit [`fddd180`](https://github.com/Phoenix3334/sglang/commit/fddd18005f0a6f91469390132141660bf3553612) carries the one-line correction from **DarkSharpness's [#47758](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47758)** (source `44b1e4b35608c8e388b1d16dc86ceec34514bcc3`): `tree_cache=SimpleNamespace(linker=None)`. It models the no-linker-offload case while preserving the existing metadata-publication assertion. No test is skipped and no assertion is removed.

The corrected file matches #47758 exactly. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed locally on that file. The source PR's [targeted CPU run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41311097837/job/124861547391) passed **12 tests** at its own source head; this is separate from validation of our updated head. [CI on the earlier head `fddd180`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41317407949) was triggered but stopped at the per-user 120-minute cooldown gate before tests executed. The logged previous accepted trigger is 2026-11-01 14:28:02 UTC, so the earliest retry under that cooldown is 16:28:02 UTC / 2026-11-02 00:28:02 UTC+8. Production code and B200 tests remain unchanged from the previous passing B200 run. After the cooldown expired, empty commit `ddcabbe` triggered [another historical CI run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41376972480) on 2026-11-02. It has since been superseded by the main merges leading to `fb4e80e`; see the current-head validation above.

### Non-main adaptation

The backport omits `and inv_rope is None` because v0.5.21 lacks that local variable. Main defines it, so this PR retains the guard to avoid double rotation. Local full-model serving validation is on the available aiopt build; the current main-based head has the hosted B200 kernel coverage documented above. Full-model serving validation on that head remains pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B300 ×8, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, aiopt v0.5.21, TP8/DP8, MegaMoE, 60k input / 1 output, C16, N160, seeds 1/2/3. Radix cache disabled; prefill-delayer enabled. aiakperf uses random token IDs through the `sglang` runner, so this benchmark does not measure real-text tokenization throughput.

| Arm | Mean input tok/s | Mean of per-run median TTFT (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline | ~101,710 | ~9.600 |
| Fused | ~103,349 | ~9.452 |
| Change | ~+1.61% | ~-1.54% |

Each arm used one fresh server startup and three seed runs; fused preceded baseline. These are not three independent paired startups. Fused per-seed throughput: 103,476.7 / 103,283.0 / 103,287.0 tok/s; TTFT: 9.4312 / 9.4523 / 9.4514 s. Baseline raw per-run values and exact dependency/image identifiers are not included in this summary.

These measurements predate the cleanup commit and remain evidence for the preceding implementation; performance after the refactor needs confirmation. Cross-build absolute throughput is not attributed to fusion. No v0.5.21 multi-shape sweep is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Prior v0.5.17-derived B300 evidence</summary>

B300, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP8 / DP8, MegaMoE, prefill-dominated workload (output length 1). Each working point is the mean of 3 runs per arm.

| Input | Concurrency | Baseline input tok/s | Fused input tok/s | Throughput Δ | Median TTFT Δ |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 60k | 1 | 13,645.6 | 14,008.5 | +2.66% | -2.46% |
| 60k | 4 | 29,141.7 | 29,654.1 | +1.76% | -1.33% |
