title: [AMD][Kimi-K3] Use public FlyDSL APIs in KDA decode kernels
author: kkHuang-amd
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

The Kimi-K3 KDA FlyDSL decode kernels import a private helper from aiter (`_to_raw`) and build raw MLIR ops by hand. Both break easily when aiter or FlyDSL change, and the private import already broke here once. This PR moves the kernels to the public FlyDSL API.

## Modifications

- Remove the `_to_raw` import from aiter's `tensor_shim`.
- Replace raw `gpu.ShuffleOp`, `vector.ReductionOp` / `FMAOp` / `BroadcastOp` / `extract` / `from_elements` and `ArithValue` with `fx.gpu.shuffle_xor/idx`, `fx.Vector(...).reduce`, `fx.fma`, `fx.full`, `fx.Vector` indexing and `fx.Float32`.
- Replace `scf.IfOp` + `ir.InsertionPoint` with Python `if` over local closures.
- The `llvm.amdgcn.fdot2.f32.bf16` call has no FlyDSL wrapper yet, so it stays raw, isolated in `_fdot2_f32_bf16`. No env knobs or defaults change.

## Accuracy Tests

Kimi-K3 GSM8K (1319, 5-shot), 8x MI355X TP8/DCP8 with `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND=aiter`: 0.951 before -> 0.954 after. `test_kimi_k3_kda_decode.py` passes 16/16, and generated ISA is identical (ignoring `.loc`) for all compiled specializations.

The ISA is identical, so kernel performance does not change.

title: [Perf] hicache: Parallel THP-backed host pool allocation (opt-in)
author: whybeyoung
body:
## Motivation

HiCache host pools are allocated by `alloc_mmap` as one `MAP_SHARED | MAP_ANONYMOUS` mapping prefaulted with `MAP_POPULATE` from a single thread, then pinned with `cudaHostRegister`. An anonymous shared mapping is shmem: every page fault takes the backing shmem file's locks, so the prefault runs at ~1.5–2 GB/s single-threaded and plateaus at ~2–4.5 GB/s with 32–64 threads (ablation below), and shmem THP is disabled by default (`shmem_enabled=never`), so every page is 4 KB.

With large host pools this becomes a significant part of engine startup. On a single node with 4x B300 and a ~306 GB host pool per rank, allocating and pinning the host pools takes ~185 s of every start.

## Modifications

Opt-in via `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_PARALLEL_ALLOC_THREADS=<n>` (default `0` = off; with it unset the code path is unchanged):

- `mmap_allocator.py`: new `_mmap_private_parallel_prefaulted(alloc_bytes, num_threads)`:
  - maps the pool `MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS` (regular anonymous memory, no shmem lock contention);
  - `madvise(MADV_HUGEPAGE)` so it is backed by 2 MB transparent huge pages under the common `enabled=madvise` policy (best effort; still correct on 4 KB pages);
  - `madvise(MADV_DONTFORK)`: this is what makes `MAP_PRIVATE` safe to pin. The reason the existing path uses `MAP_SHARED` is that a private page goes copy-on-write in a forked child and a parent write after `fork()` would move the parent off the page `cudaHostRegister` pinned. With `MADV_DONTFORK` the mapping is not inherited at all, so there is no COW to race with — the same treatment the CUDA driver gives `cudaHostAlloc` memory. Consequence: a `fork()`ed (not spawned) child cannot see this buffer;
  - prefaults the whole range before returning (as `cudaHostRegister` requires) with a THP-aligned chunked `memset` from `n` threads (32 in the runs below). ctypes releases the GIL around the libc call, so the threads fault in parallel. (`MADV_POPULATE_WRITE` per chunk was measured to be noticeably slower than `memset` with the same thread count.)
- `alloc_mmap`: when `n > 0`, the plain (non-hugetlb) path uses the function above; any `OSError` logs and falls back to the existing shared prefaulted mapping. The explicit hugetlb path (`SGLANG_HUGEPAGE_SIZE`) is untouched.
- `environ.py`: `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_PARALLEL_ALLOC_THREADS` (`EnvInt(0)`), documented in `docs/references/environment_variables.mdx`.
- Tests (`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mmap_allocator.py`, CPU CI):
  - the mapping is fully resident and zero-filled for 1 / 4 / 64 threads with a ragged, non-THP-aligned size;
  - a forked child touching the buffer gets `SIGSEGV` (i.e. `MADV_DONTFORK` is in effect; mutation-checked — removing the `madvise` makes this test fail);
  - with the flag on, `alloc_mmap` does not take the shared path, and an `OSError` on the new path falls back to it;
  - with the flag unset (default), the new path is never taken.

Note: `alloc_mmap` is also used by `utils/weight_checker.py` for its snapshot arena, which therefore follows the same flag.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — host memory allocation only; the pool contents are zero-filled exactly as before and no model-output code is touched.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

End to end, one B300 node, 4 ranks allocating concurrently, 306 GB host pool per rank, real `alloc_mmap` + `_cuda_host_register` path, two runs (per rank):

| | allocation + prefault | `cudaHostRegister` | total (slowest rank) |
|---|---|---|---|
| default (`MAP_SHARED`, single-thread `MAP_POPULATE`) | 115–172 s | 13–47 s | 185–189 s |
| `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_PARALLEL_ALLOC_THREADS=32` | 4–27 s | 12–29 s | 46 s |

~4x faster overall (~140 s saved per start); with 4 concurrent ranks, allocation is bound by memory bandwidth / page allocator rather than threads.

Ablation, 64 GB prefault, one B300 node (256 cores, kernel 6.8, THP `enabled=madvise`, `shmem_enabled=never`), chunked `memset`, two runs:

| mapping | 1 thread | 8 threads | 32 threads | 64 threads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| default: shared + `MAP_POPULATE` | 1.4–1.8 GB/s | – | – | – |
| shared (4 KB; `MADV_HUGEPAGE` has no effect on shmem here) | 1.1–1.4 | 1.7–3.8 | 1.7–4.5 | 1.9–4.6 |
| private, 4 KB (`MADV_NOHUGEPAGE`) | 1.2 | 4.1–5.4 | 7.6–8.9 | 8.4–14.4 |
| private + THP (100% 2 MB pages) | 2.2–2.3 | 10.2–10.4 | 30–43 | 47–48 |

So multithreading alone on the shared mapping gives at most ~2x and is noisy; going private gives most of the scaling, and THP another ~4x on top.

title: [AMD][DI][CI] kimik26 2p1d-ep16: capture CUDA graph on decode (eager decode is slow)
author: Lzy17
body:
## What
In the two kimik26 `2p1d-ep16` recipes, replace `--disable-cuda-graph` on decode with `--cuda-graph-bs-decode 1..64` (`1..128` for `-mtp`).

For `-mtp`, the decode MORI settings also change, from 64 / 332 / 128 to 512 / 2048 / 1024. These are the values the dsv4pro and glm52 `-mtp` recipes use: capture needs batch size x 4 draft tokens to stay within the dispatch limit. The comment in the `-mtp` recipe that said to revisit CUDA graph once the test is green is updated.

## Why
Both tests are green but slow, about 1 h 20 min (plain) and 40 min (`-mtp`) a night, because decode runs eagerly.

This changes what the tests measure: throughput will be higher than the eager baseline.

## Validation
On pit2 (4 nodes), main `6a7abcf`, same image as the nightly. Each run once. Decode logs show `cuda graph: True`, no capture errors, no timeouts, 7 of 7 result files.
- plain: 25 min, GSM8K 0.936.
- `-mtp`: 18 min, GSM8K 0.934.

title: [Fix] [AMD] kda: Match the fused verify Q/K norm to its reference kernel
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
#42486 switched the default Q/K L2 norm in `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` to "compute `1 / sqrt(...)`, then multiply", but `fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify` still computes `b_q / sqrt(...)`. `x / y` and `x * (1 / y)` round differently, so the fused verify kernel stopped matching its reference bit for bit, and the ROCm-only `test_glm_fp32_weights_bit_exact_on_rocm[8,9]` fails on MI35x:

```
assert torch.equal(ic_fus[valid], ic_ref[valid])
AssertionError: assert False
```

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38317177892/job/115041491933

The test's `_run_reference` is `causal_conv1d_update` + `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update`, so this switches the fused kernel to the same reciprocal form, with the same order of operations. The case only runs on ROCm, which is why #42486's validation reports "2 ROCm-only cases skipped".

The other KDA failure on ROCm (`TestKDAVerifyDecodeParity`) has an unrelated cause and is fixed separately in #44089.

## Notes for the reviewer

This changes the fused verify kernel's numerics on every platform, not just ROCm, by moving it onto the form its reference already uses. `fused_recurrent.py`, `gdn_replayssm_spec_{decode,fold}.py` and `kda_replayssm_spec_decode.py` still divide. I left them alone because no test compares them bit for bit against `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update`.

## Test plan

Locally on MI355X (gfx950), `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm10-mi35x-20261007`:

- [x] `test_glm_fp32_weights_bit_exact_on_rocm`: 2 failed → 2 passed
- [x] Full `test_fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py`: 25 passed, 1 skipped (CUDA green contexts)

CI, `test_fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py`:

- [x] MI35x, `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` part 0, the partition that failed on it before: passed on the [current head](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38519810686/job/115714219438) and [before the main merge](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38355361655/job/115164272858)
- [x] NVIDIA, `jit-kernel-unit-test-1-gpu-large`: passed on the [current head](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38519810721/job/115706908811) and [before the main merge](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38355361603/job/115157428852). This is the change in the pair that affects NVIDIA

## Remaining red checks

- `stage-b-test-1-gpu-large-amd` part 2 fails `TestKDAVerifyDecodeParity.test_bf16_state_verify_matches_single_token_launches` ([log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38519810686/job/115714219452)). That is the other half of the KDA ROCm fix, in #44089.

The other base-b partitions fast-fail behind it, and it fails the same way on #44089.

title: [DSV4.1] Skip Mega mHC fusion on 0-row (DP-idle) batches
author: shyeh25
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #43992.

With `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MEGA_MHC_PREFILL=1` (#42808), DeepSeek-V4.1 with MegaMoE (`--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`) and DP attention (`--attn-dp-size > 1`) crashes as soon as one DP rank runs an idle (0-row) batch, e.g. on the server's startup warmup request:

```
RuntimeError: Tensor match failed for Tensor<0, 5120>[strides=<20480, 1>, dtype=bfloat16, device=cuda:1]
  at python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/mega_moe_pre_dispatch.cuh:189
- Root cause: Tensor is not contiguous as expected
```

On the idle rank, `_post_fusion()` takes the Mega mHC branch with a `[0, 5120]` view whose stride is `(20480, 1)`. `mhc_mega_boundary()` allocates its output with `torch.empty_like(x)`, which keeps that stride for a 0-element tensor; the result becomes the next sublayer's cached input and is handed to MegaMoE, whose pre-dispatch rejects it. The non-Mega path is fine because `post()` already returns a fresh `(0, mult, hidden)` tensor for 0 rows.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_mhc.py`: in `_post_fusion()`, take the Mega mHC branch only when `y.shape[0] > 0`; 0-row inputs fall back to `post()`. Non-empty batches are unchanged, and the idle rank still runs the MoE dispatch / all-to-all.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K (`python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 1319`), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash FP4, B300, `--tp 2 --attn-dp-size 2 --ep 2 --moe-a2a-backend megamoe`, DSpark (block size 5, real acceptance):

| | `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MEGA_MHC_PREFILL` | accuracy |
|---|---|---|
| main (`c2dfd5d3d6`) | 0 | 0.907 |
| this PR | 1 | 0.906 |

(main with `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MEGA_MHC_PREFILL=1` cannot be measured: it crashes at startup.)

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput claim. This is a correctness fix; the added check reads tensor metadata only, and non-empty batches take the same path as before.

title: [Perf] [AMD] dsv4: FP4 indexer on aiter's row-group kernel for decode and target-verify (5/8)
author: kkHuang-amd
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
The FP4 indexer re-reads each key per query row. aiter's row-group FP4 MQA logits kernel (ROCm/aiter#6145) shares key loads across a request's rows. This uses it for V4.1 low-ratio layers and, opt-in, for the DeepSeek-V4 C4 indexer. Includes #43073 (not merged yet).

Depends on: #43073 (open, included here); ROCm/aiter#6145 (in aiter main, needs the aiter pin bump in #44035).

## Modifications
- V4.1 low-ratio indexer on the row-group kernel with candidate-only scoring (#43073; `SGLANG_HIP_FP4_INDEXER_ROWGROUP`, default on for HIP; page-8 index-K pool `SGLANG_HIP_DSV41_INDEX_K_PAGE8`, default off).
- DeepSeek-V4 C4 indexer decode and target-verify (>= 64 rows) on the row-group kernel, workspace built inside the graph (`SGLANG_HIP_DSV4_C4_INDEXER_ROWGROUP`, default off).
- All three paths fall back to the schedule kernels / page-64 pool with a warning when the installed aiter has no row-group kernel; tests skip there.

## Accuracy Tests
GSM8K: main 0.953 -> 0.948 (default), 0.946-0.954 with `SGLANG_HIP_DSV4_C4_INDEXER_ROWGROUP=1` (aiter 02575f1c3a).

title: [Perf] Bind scheduler CPUs to the GPU's NUMA node when memory policy is not permitted
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

Without NUMA binding, scheduler processes can drift across sockets, losing their CPU caches and touching host memory on the remote node, which adds per-step overhead and makes tail latency noisy. In a container without `SYS_NICE`, LLM serving skips binding entirely and logs `User lacks permission to set NUMA affinity, skipping NUMA node configuration for GPU`.

Only the memory-policy syscalls (`get_mempolicy` / `set_mempolicy`) are denied there; `sched_setaffinity` needs no privilege, so each rank can still be pinned to its GPU's NUMA node, and the default first-touch policy places its host memory there too. #43756 added this CPU-only fallback for the diffusion worker only; the LLM paths never opted in.

## Modifications

- `_is_numa_available()` no longer requires memory-policy permission, so a host where only CPU affinity can be set still gets bound. The `cpu_only_ok` / `require_mempolicy` opt-in is removed, so every caller gets the fallback.
- `configure_subprocess` strips the `--membind` segment before the numactl probe when memory policy is not permitted, so each rank does not log two expected rejections first.
- The `binding CPUs only` INFO line is logged where memory binding is actually skipped (the strip above, and `numa_bind_to_node`), so it also covers an explicit `--numa-node`.
- The diffusion worker call site drops the now-removed kwarg; the unit test that asserted the old skip is replaced, and the strip wiring gets a test. The diffusion CLI and env-var docs note that only CPU affinity is set without `CAP_SYS_NICE`.

Checked on 8x B300 without `SYS_NICE`: with this PR, TP0-3 are pinned to `0-85,172-257` (node 0) and TP4-7 to `86-171,258-343` (node 1); with `SGLANG_AUTO_NUMA_BIND=0` (the same no-bind path the old code took here), all ranks have affinity `0-343`. Memory placement is not enforced; `--cap-add SYS_NICE` is still needed for `--membind`.

Behavior change: with `SGLANG_CRASH_ON_NUMA_BIND_FAILURE=1`, an unprivileged pod whose allowed CPUs don't overlap the GPU's node used to start unbound (binding was skipped earlier); it now fails at launch, as the flag intends.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --tp-size 8` on 8x B300 without `SYS_NICE`, bound (this PR) vs unbound (`SGLANG_AUTO_NUMA_BIND=0`). `python -m sglang.benchmark.serving`, random-ids, 256 in / 256 out, `--max-concurrency 64`, 1024 prompts, 256 warmup requests, `--flush-cache`. Mean ± stdev over 3 alternating rounds:

| metric | bound | unbound | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| output tok/s | 23,584 ± 222 | 22,915 ± 528 | +2.9% |
| TPOT p50 (ms) | 2.35 ± 0.02 | 2.42 ± 0.06 | -2.9% |
| TPOT p99 (ms) | 2.72 ± 0.03 | 3.03 ± 0.27 | -10% |

Bound was ahead on all three metrics in each of the three rounds, and the runs were more repeatable: run-to-run spread was 2.4x lower for throughput (±222 vs ±528 tok/s) and 9x lower for TPOT p99 (±0.03 vs ±0.27 ms).

title: [Perf] KVShard: 0SM KV Cache Allgather for KV Cache Sharding
author: Shunkangz
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Zero-SM KV-Shard Gather

The sharded pool's per-layer prefix allgather previously used NCCL ring/LL kernels. When overlapped with attention and GEMMs, these kernels competed for SMs and HBM bandwidth.

`SGLANG_ENABLE_KV_SHARD_ZERO_SM_GATHER` enables **zero-SM** gathering and is on by default. The gather communicator is created with `NCCL_CTA_POLICY_ZERO`, allowing NCCL to run the in-place allgather on copy engines instead of SM kernels.

### Memory Allocation

Both scratch slots are carved from a single `ncclMemAlloc` buffer registered as a symmetric window. Each slot uses a 4 KiB-aligned offset that is identical across all ranks.

- `_scratch_tensor_specs` returns a mapping of `name -> (shape, dtype)`.
- The mixin handles allocation.
- The buffer is deregistered and freed when its last tensor view is destroyed.

### Activation and Fallbacks

The engine defaults `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` when zero-SM gathering applies to a single-node deployment.

The pool retains Torch allocation when any of the following applies:

- `SGLANG_ENABLE_KV_SHARD_ZERO_SM_GATHER` is disabled.
- A memory saver or custom memory pool is active.
- The NCCL version is older than 2.28.
- The shard group spans multiple nodes. NCCL would use its hierarchical inter-node RMA path in this case, which remains unverified.

If window registration returns a `NULL` window because NCCL cuMem is disabled, the pool logs one warning and gathering remains on SM kernels.

### NCCL 2.30 Race Workaround

With NVLS enabled, NCCL 2.30 lazily builds the multicast team during the first copy-engine collective's synchronization, without a barrier. This race can cause the first gather to hang.

The pool works around the race by building the multicast team during registration and issuing a barrier afterward.

### GPU Test Coverage

The GPU test profiles a batch of gathers and verifies that:

- No NCCL kernels are launched.
- Peer copies occur.

A gather communicator that loses `NCCL_CTA_POLICY_ZERO` therefore fails the test.

@humansand

Add opt-in NVFP4 W4A16 to FlashInfer MegaMoE for serialized ModelOpt checkpoints
and `nvfp4_online`, reusing `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_NVFP4_W4A16=1`. The default
NVFP4 MegaMoE path remains W4A4.

This is the remaining integration from [#39210](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39210)
on top of merged [#43789](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43789).
Startup autotuning, cache ownership, native workspace pooling and DP token-count
synchronization are already upstream and are not changed here. The original PR's
branch and history are preserved.

**Dependency:** the existing FlashInfer 0.7.1 pin includes
[FlashInfer #5019](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5019).
No Dockerfile or dependency changes.

## Modifications

- **Precision and preparation:** extend the existing MegaMoE adapter with the
  native W4A16 config/preprocessing. Keep packed NVFP4 weights/block scales,
  per-expert FP32 weight scales, BF16 activations/EP transport/combine and
  post-FC2 routing. Neutralize serialized checkpoint activation scales and
  bypass activation quantization for online W4A16. Retain the existing source
  precision and excluded-layer behavior for online weight conversion.
- **Activation and model wiring:** support gated SiLU/SwiGLU and SiTU for NVFP4
  W4A4/W4A16. Kimi K3 uses standard TopK and local EP/shared-expert handling;
  its GEMM1 alpha/clamp fields map to SiTU beta/linear-beta, separately from
  SwiGLU clamps. MXFP8/DeepGEMM reject unwired SiTU. Nemotron ReLU-squared is
  unsupported. Requirements remain SM100/SM103 and attention-DP=TP=EP;
  W4A16 additionally requires BF16 model dtype and combine.
- **Reload:** restore canonical loading views over the four prepared
  weight/block-scale allocations, then copy newly prepared data into those
  allocations. Share this loader/preparation lifecycle between W4A4 and W4A16. Keep the live
  MegaMoE layer, tuned profiles and workspace owner so CUDA graph pointers remain
  stable; per-expert runtime scales are staged on each forward. FlashInfer 0.7.1
  captures W4A4 input normalization as a scalar: reloading a different input
  scale is rejected and requires a server restart. Weight, weight-scale and
  per-expert FC1-output scale updates remain supported. The registered
  W4A16 serialized reload test covers both cache-flush modes; the existing
  storage regression covers both precisions.
- **Dummy weights:** initialize FP4 global `weight_scale_2` tensors to one,
  preserving ordinary random-weight initialization. Retain the simple
  neutral-scale regression test.
- **FC2 reduction:** default `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_IN_KERNEL_FC2_REDUCE=0`
  uses external FP32 accumulation. Setting it to `1` permits nondeterministic
  BF16 atomic candidates; tuning can still select external reduction.
- **Current upstream contracts:** preserve the default non-MegaMoE draft runner
  and A2A behavior. An unset draft A2A backend now resolves to `none` for a
  FlashInfer MegaMoE target, and the NVSHMEM guard accounts for that default.
- **Tests:** extend the existing adapter/storage and architecture cases, plus
  the registered online NVFP4 GSM8K and serialized weight-reload classes.
  No full Kimi K3 E2E or dedicated NVSHMEM environment tests are added.

### Single-node NVSHMEM defaults

For single-node FlashInfer MegaMoE, with no speculative decoding or a default/
explicit `none` draft A2A backend, set these defaults before initialization:

```bash
NVSHMEM_REMOTE_TRANSPORT=none
NVSHMEM_IB_ENABLE_IBGDA=0
NVSHMEM_DISABLE_LOCAL_ONLY_PROXY=1
```

Explicit environment settings are preserved. These defaults apply to all
supported FlashInfer MegaMoE formats and select direct peer memory access,
avoiding the uninitialized proxy global-exit state fixed by
[NVIDIA/nvshmem commit `af9e2391a849`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvshmem/commit/af9e2391a849d1a36b4be09c3f6f20d622dada1b).
The closed [NVIDIA/nvshmem#110](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvshmem/pull/110) has
additional background. Remote IB/UCX transport and proxy-based global-exit/
timeout polling are disabled; bootstrap networking is unaffected. All EP GPUs
must support peer memory access. Multi-node jobs and explicit other draft A2A
backends receive no automatic defaults.

### Example server command

Four Blackwell GPUs, FlashInfer 0.7.1, online expert-weight conversion:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
SGLANG_FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_NVFP4_W4A16=1 \
SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_IN_KERNEL_FC2_REDUCE=0 \
SGLANG_FP4_IGNORED_LAYERS='' \
SGLANG_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=False \
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8 \
  --quantization nvfp4_online --dtype bfloat16 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_megamoe \
  --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe \
  --tp-size 4 --attn-dp-size 4 --ep-size 4 \
  --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \
  --max-running-requests 64 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.7
```

Convert every routed expert for this example; excluded FP8 expert layers cannot
use the NVFP4 MegaMoE runner. With attention DP4, the 16384-token configured
prefill chunk resolves to 4096 tokens per rank. The existing startup autotuner
therefore prepares a 4096-token per-rank prefill profile.

## Pinned registered-model runner

Save this local runner outside the checkout. It downloads or reuses the exact public snapshot, changes only its model path and port, and invokes the actual registered test. For the W4A4 control it changes the same reload class's environment flag and display label in this process; it adds no upstream test class and keeps the inherited assertions intact.

```bash

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import socket
import unittest
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download

parser.add_argument("case", choices=("online", "reload-w4a16", "reload-w4a4"))
parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()
root = Path(os.environ["TASK_VALIDATION_ROOT"])
with socket.socket() as probe:
    probe.bind(("127.0.0.1", args.port))
for key in ("NVSHMEM_REMOTE_TRANSPORT", "NVSHMEM_IB_ENABLE_IBGDA", "NVSHMEM_DISABLE_LOCAL_ONLY_PROXY"):
    assert key not in os.environ, f"Unset {key} to exercise production defaults"

if args.case == "online":
    repo = "Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8"
    revision = "5a5a776300a41aaa681dd7ff0106608ef2bc90db"
    filename = "backends/test_flashinfer_nvfp4_online_moe_backend.py"
    class_name = "TestFlashinferMegaMoeBackendNvFp4OnlineW4A16"

    repo = "nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4"

index = json.loads((snapshot / "model.safetensors.index.json").read_text())

source = root / "sglang/test/registered" / filename
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("registered_megamoe_reproduction", source)
module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)

    "model_path": str(snapshot), "url": case.base_url,
    "launch_env": getattr(case, "launch_env", getattr(case, "extra_env", {})),
    "extra_args": getattr(case, "extra_args", None),
    "backend_test_suites": getattr(case, "backend_test_suites", None),

```

The example server configuration in the PR body is separate: its graph/running caps are 64 and configured chunk is 16384. Those values are not substituted into this registered accuracy test.

## Serialized W4A16 reload and local W4A4 control

Run sequentially:

```bash
cd "$TASK_VALIDATION_ROOT/sglang"
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 timeout --kill-after=30s 120m \
  python -B "$TASK_VALIDATION_ROOT/run_registered.py" reload-w4a16 --port 31010

  python -B "$TASK_VALIDATION_ROOT/run_registered.py" reload-w4a4 --port 31011
```

Both retain `flush_cache=True` and `False` with `abort_all_requests=False`, weight/KV/graph release-resume, exact text/token-ID comparisons, and log-probability tolerance `1e-4`. A W4A4 checkpoint changing the captured input activation scale requires an engine restart.

No full Kimi K3/GLM-5.2 E2E, online RL reload, or speedup claim is included.

title: [Perf] [AMD] batch-invariant: Tune the bf16 matmul for gfx950
author: aarnetalman
body:
## Motivation

This PR speeds up deterministic inference on MI350X/MI355X (gfx950): about 6% more throughput with 1k-token inputs and about 1.5% with 8k-token inputs. It gives the batch-invariant bf16 matmul a launch configuration tuned for gfx950.

With `--enable-deterministic-inference`, every linear layer goes through the persistent batch-invariant Triton matmul (`_matmul_persistent_triton`). That kernel uses one bf16 configuration on every GPU (128x128x64 tiles, 3 stages, 8 warps), with no AMD-specific options. On gfx950, a 128x64x128 tile with 16-wide MFMA instructions is up to 2x faster at decode batch sizes.

The configuration is still fixed for every M, so each output element keeps the same reduction order whatever the batch: batch invariance is unchanged.

## Modifications

- `batch_invariant_ops.py`: on gfx950 only, the bf16 entry becomes `BLOCK_SIZE_M=128, BLOCK_SIZE_N=64, BLOCK_SIZE_K=128, GROUP_SIZE_M=8, num_stages=3, num_warps=8, matrix_instr_nonkdim=16`.
  - It needs about 147 KB of LDS, so it is limited to gfx950 (160 KB).
  - Other GPUs, fp16/fp32 and the non-deterministic path are unchanged.
  - In deterministic mode every unquantized bf16 linear layer (`aten::mm`/`addmm`) runs this kernel on ROCm, so the change applies to any bf16 model. Quantized layers, MoE experts (Triton MoE runner) and attention don't use it.
- Chosen from a sweep of about 2,900 configurations on MI350X, each checked bitwise for batch invariance.
- The launch configurations are now built by a small helper, `_matmul_persistent_configs()`, and a new CPU test (`test/registered/unit/batch_invariant_ops/test_matmul_persistent_configs.py`, `base-a-test-cpu`) guards the preset: on gfx950 the bf16 entry must be exactly this configuration and fit gfx950's 160 KB of LDS, and on other GPUs it must stay the original one.

## Accuracy Tests

MI350X, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261012` with this change applied, Qwen3-8B BF16, TP1, `--attention-backend triton --enable-deterministic-inference`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`:
- `python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic --test-mode prefix --return-logprob` and `--test-mode radix_cache` (50 trials): pass.
- Bitwise comparison of 1,275 responses (batch sizes 1-50) against batch size 1: 1275/1275 token IDs and log-probabilities identical.
- `test/registered/unit/batch_invariant_ops/test_batch_invariant_ops.py`: 6 passed, 54 subtests, before and after (also with the helper refactor).
- `test_matmul_persistent_configs.py`: 2 passed (2 failed on the code before this PR, which has no helper).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**End to end**, deterministic mode as above, `python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf --seed 1`, median of 3 runs each:

| Workload | | Output tok/s | ITL p50 | TTFT p50 | Request latency p50 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ISL/OSL 1024/1024, 256 prompts, concurrency 256 | main | 3,370 | 66.79 ms | 5.03 s | 77.7 s |
| | this PR | 3,585 (**1.064x**) | 61.98 ms (**-7.2%**) | 5.28 s (+4.8%) | 73.0 s (**-6.0%**) |
| ISL/OSL 8192/1024, 256 prompts, concurrency 128, GPU A | main | 686.9 | 121.61 ms | 34.5 s | 190.8 s |
| | this PR, GPU B | 695.4 (1.012x) | 118.34 ms (-2.7%) | 35.1 s (+1.7%) | 188.4 s (-1.3%) |
| same, GPUs swapped | main, GPU B | 686.0 | 121.36 ms | 34.8 s | 191.0 s |
| | this PR, GPU A | 697.6 (1.017x) | 118.27 ms (-2.5%) | 34.8 s (0.0%) | 187.9 s (-1.6%) |

- 1k/1k: same GPU, before and after; an earlier run with the GPUs swapped gave the same gain (1.059x on both GPUs).
- With 8k inputs most of the time goes to prefill, where the new tile is about 5% slower at the GEMM level (table below), so the gain is smaller. Decode is still faster, and request latency still improves.

**Kernel**, speed-up over the current configuration (`triton.testing.do_bench`, weights passed transposed as `F.linear` does):

| N x K | M=1 | M=16 | M=64 | M=256 | M=1024 | M=4096 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6144 x 4096 | 1.77x | 1.92x | 1.84x | 1.60x | 1.16x | 0.96x |
| 4096 x 4096 | 1.98x | 1.94x | 1.85x | 1.57x | 0.95x | 0.96x |
| 24576 x 4096 | 1.02x | 1.01x | 1.00x | 1.14x | 0.95x | 0.96x |
| 4096 x 12288 | 2.05x | 2.02x | 1.87x | 1.56x | 0.96x | 0.95x |
| 16384 x 5120 | 1.16x | 1.15x | 1.15x | 0.88x | 0.94x | 0.94x |
| 5120 x 6144 | 2.03x | 1.99x | 1.87x | 1.58x | 1.15x | 0.98x |
| 34816 x 5120 | 1.21x | 1.20x | 1.21x | 1.04x | 0.99x | 0.96x |
| 5120 x 17408 | 2.13x | 2.11x | 1.96x | 1.57x | 1.11x | 0.95x |

The shapes are the linear layers of Qwen3-8B and Qwen3.8-27B. The geomean is 1.59x at M <= 64 and 0.99x at M >= 1024. A per-(N, K) configuration could recover the prefill shapes later; the configuration must never depend on M.

title: [DeepSeek-V4.1] DeepSelect cluster top-k for long rows and bf16 index logits
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> (auto generated by Claude)

Speeds up DeepSelect top-k for small-batch, long-context decode (the DeepSeek-V4.1 indexer case) and lets the V4.1 index layers run on bf16 scores.

**DeepSelect cluster kernel** (bf16, topk <= 1024)
- Rewritten cluster kernel: each CTA takes a contiguous slice of the row; a slice of up to 32K stays in registers, a longer one streams through a bulk-copy ring behind a cluster-wide pivot taken from a window (three pseudo-random stages plus the slice's tail). The cluster agrees on the final pivot by pushing 256-bin histograms to every CTA, then writes its output directly (DSMEM atomics for unsorted, a bitmap prefix for `sorted_index`).
- Dispatch keys only on the row count, never on the (CUDA-graph padded) width: cluster sizes 16/8/4/3/2 are tiered by an occupancy probe of how many clusters fit in one wave; the per-row `end` decides everything else inside the kernel.
- All modules of a call signature are compiled in parallel (`parallel_compile` in the JIT utils).
- Without abort, a NaN row now selects index 0 in every slot instead of writing a `0x3F3F3F3F` sentinel to slot 0; `return_value` and `abort_when_nan_found` default to False.

**DeepSeek-V4.1 indexer**
- `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_BF16_INDEX_LOGITS` (default off): the DeepGEMM fp4 MQA logits are emitted in bf16 (the reference ranks bf16 scores), their top-k goes through DeepSelect, and `amax8_varlen` reads bf16 scores (now templated on input/output dtype).

**Kernel latency** (B200, cold L2, width 1M, topk 1024, us at `end` 128K / 1M). Before, the cluster kernel only ran for rows <= 6 at width >= 512K; every other case took one CTA per row.

| rows | one CTA per row | cluster (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 19.0 / 81.8 | 6.1 / 13.0 |
| 8 | 19.3 / 82.7 | 6.5 / 15.5 |
| 32 | 19.5 / 82.8 | 8.6 / 22.3 |
| 66 | 19.8 / 83.2 | 13.2 / 40.9 |

**Validation**
- B200 and H200: `test_deep_select.py`, plus randomized checks of every cluster size against `torch.topk` (ties, constants, -inf, +-0, NaN, ascending/descending rows, ragged `end`, offsets, int64, page transform, values, `sorted_index`).
- B200: DeepSeek-V4.1 indexer kernel tests pass with the flag off; with it on, only tests whose references use fp32 logits differ (bf16 rounding and ties at the selection floor).
- 2x GB300, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash end to end, flag on vs off: no crash, GSM8K within run-to-run noise (0.893 vs 0.913 / 0.897 on a rerun), passkey correct at 125K and 209K; decode top-k in the index layers 51.1 -> 27.6 us per step at 128K.

title: [Fix] [AMD] kda: Reject match_cutedsl_decode on ROCm and skip its parity tests
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
`match_cutedsl_decode` (#42251) reproduces FlashInfer's CuTe DSL decode kernel, including PTX `ex2.approx` / `lg2.approx` emitted through `inline_asm_elementwise` with `"=f,f"` constraints. AMDGCN rejects that asm (`error: could not allocate output register for constraint 'f'`), but the launch still runs and returns wrong values. So on ROCm both `TestKDAVerifyDecodeParity` tests that set `match_decode=True` fail. CI shows only the first because the suite stops early:

```
FAIL: test_bf16_state_verify_matches_single_token_launches (head_dim=128)
AssertionError: False is not true
```

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38317177892/job/115041491883

No production caller sets `match_cutedsl_decode`; the parity test is its only user. So the wrapper now raises `NotImplementedError` on ROCm instead of returning wrong values. The two parity tests skip on ROCm, and a ROCm-only test checks that the error is raised. The default-path test in the same class keeps running on ROCm.

Everything here is gated on `_is_hip`, so NVIDIA behaviour is unchanged.

The other KDA failure on ROCm (`test_glm_fp32_weights_bit_exact_on_rocm`) has an unrelated cause and is fixed separately in #43991.

## Test plan

Locally on MI355X (gfx950), `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm10-mi35x-20261007`:

- [x] `TestKDAVerifyDecodeParity`: 2 failures + 1 error → OK (2 skipped; the default-path test and the new ROCm guard test pass)
- [x] Full `test_kda_kernels.py`: 20 run, OK (2 skipped). The `constraint 'f'` errors go from 22 to 0

CI, `test_kda_kernels.py`:

- [x] MI300 (gfx942), `stage-b-test-1-gpu-large-amd` part 2: passed on the [current head](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38519830491/job/116268071498) and [before the main merge](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38422141166/job/115392034837). `test_default_path_keeps_fp32_state_across_the_chain` and `test_parity_mode_is_rejected_on_rocm` ran, the two parity tests skipped, and there are no `constraint 'f'` errors
- [x] NVIDIA, base-b: [passed before the main merge](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38422140921/job/115390318091), with all three `TestKDAVerifyDecodeParity` tests still running there. It didn't run on the current head, because base-b stops earlier on the unrelated failure below

## Remaining red checks

- `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` part 0 fails `test_fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py` ([log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38519830491/job/116268072880)). That is the other half of the KDA ROCm fix, in #43991.

title: [Fix] [XPU] nightly: Fix rerank, zimage, flux2 and EAGLE parity
author: arathi-hlab
body:
## Motivation

Four tests fail in the Intel XPU nightly on `sglang-kernel-xpu==0.4.0`:

| Test | Suite | CI error |
|---|---|---|
| `test_xpu_rerank` (exit -9) | 1-GPU | `RuntimeError: store_cache only supports k/v dtype in {fp16, bf16, uint8}; got Float` |
| `test_xpu_zimage_turbo` (exit 1) | 1-GPU | `fixture 'perf_results' not found` |
| `test_spec_eagle_parity` (exit 1) | 1-GPU | `torch.OutOfMemoryError: XPU out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.25 GiB` |
| `test_xpu_flux2_dev` (exit 1) | 4-GPU | `fixture 'perf_results' not found` |

Seen in e.g. `nightly-xpu-kernel-wheel-1-gpu` [run 38281560127 / job 114919788483](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38281560127/job/114919788483) and the kernel-main [run 38299359135](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38299359135).

The workflow split that was originally in this PR moved to a separate PR.

## Modifications

- `test_xpu_rerank.py`: sgl-kernel-xpu 0.4.0 `store_cache` rejects fp32 K/V, and the bge-reranker-v2-m3 cross-encoder runs fp32. Per review, `memory_pool.py` is left unchanged because more XPU KV cache dtypes are being upstreamed. `TestXPUCrossEncoderRerank` is skipped (`@unittest.skip` with the error and a re-enable note) until then. `TestXPUDecoderRerank` (bf16) still runs.

title: [Perf] session: Cache multimodal prompt token counts across turns
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

Usage reporting counts the image, audio and video prompt tokens of a request by scanning every item in `req.multimodal_inputs`. The output streamer does this for each output row, and the PD metadata buffer does it once more on the prefill node. A streaming session shares its media history across turns, so a session that appends one audio chunk per turn rescans the whole accumulated history on every turn: the cost of reporting usage grows linearly with the number of turns instead of with the media actually added.

A second, smaller problem sits in the same code: disaggregated decode treated an all-zero transferred count as "not computed" and fell back to recounting locally, so the prefill-side result was authoritative only when it was non-zero.

## Modifications

- `Req` gains `get_mm_token_counts()`, which computes the per-modality counts at most once and caches them with an explicit `mm_token_counts_ready` flag, and `inherit_mm_token_counts(other)`, which copies the counts of a request whose media history is shared.
- `Session.create_req` inherits the counts from the previous turn when the new turn is a plain continuation. It does not inherit on abort or when a `session_params.offset` truncates the inherited history, so those cases fall back to a full count.
- `Req.extend_image_inputs` adds only the counts of the newly appended items when the counts are already cached.
- The output streamer and `MetadataBuffers.set_buf` both read through the accessor. `DecodeTransferQueue` marks the counts received from prefill as ready, so a transferred zero is final.

Behaviour of a single-turn request is unchanged; the change is that repeated reads are served from the cache.

Tests: a new `test_mm_token_counts.py` covers memoisation of all-zero counts and inherit-then-extend across a session turn; `test_session_token_share_unit.py` gains a case where an aborted turn's edits to the counts do not leak into the next turn. The existing `_FakeReq` fixtures in the output-streamer tests and the PD wire test gain the accessor. The three new cases fail on `main` and pass with this change.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: usage token counts are bookkeeping and do not affect generation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable beyond the mechanism described above: with a cached count, appending one item to a history of N items costs one item scan instead of N+1.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] qsa: Keep sparse decode scratch in FP8 for FP8 KV pools
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

#38851 fixed QSA sparse-decode corruption with three changes:

- zero-filling the scratch tail;
- int64 pool offsets;
- dequantizing FP8 pool rows into a BF16 scratch.

The first two fix the bug. The third was a conservative choice: it makes TRTLLM-gen decode always run BF16-q + BF16-KV.

FlashInfer's `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` supports BF16-q + FP8-E4M3-KV. With an FP8 pool, keeping the packed scratch in FP8 halves gather and attention KV traffic and removes the dequant from `fused_kv_prepare`.

## Modifications

- `_forward_trtllm_sparse` allocates the packed K/V scratch in FP8 when the KV pool is `float8_e4m3fn` and the device is SM10x. Otherwise it uses the query dtype, as before.
  - The query stays BF16.
  - The scratch cache is already keyed by dtype.
- Unchanged:
  - the zero-fill, int64 offsets and scale-free handling from #38851;
  - BF16 pools;
  - the FA2/FA4 fallback;
  - prefill;
  - SM120.
- `test_qsa_fused_kv_prepare` and `test_qsa_strided_zero_fill` now cover FP8 pool → FP8 scratch.

## Accuracy Tests

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 on VR200: TP1, FP8 KV, FP8 QSA indexer, NEXTN MTP (3 steps, 4 draft tokens).

Sampling: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, `max_new_tokens` 131072. No sample reached the length limit.

| Eval | Main (BF16 scratch) | This PR (FP8 scratch) | Paired diff |
|---|---|---|---|
| AIME24+25, 60 × 16 samples | 90.52% | 92.08% | +1.56 pp, 95% CI [−0.47, +3.59] |
| GPQA, 100 × 8 samples | 87.25% | 88.62% | +1.38 pp, SE 1.09 |
| GSM8K, 200 | 198 | 198 | 0 |

- Output length is unchanged (+0.15%).
- Attention output error against an FP32 reference is the same on both paths, about 2.1e-3. It does not grow with KV length up to 64K and beyond.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same model and configuration on VR200, C64 with MTP.

**Per decode step:**

| | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `fused_kv_prepare` | 135.19 µs | 86.69 µs |
| FMHA | 97.61 µs | 89.42 µs |
| Step time | 20.686 ms | 19.908 ms (−3.76%) |

**Agentic multi-turn serving, 3 paired 1-hour runs:** median per-user throughput (P90) +1.49%, median total throughput per GPU +2.29%.

This matches the expected gain: decode is about 68% of wall time, so −3.76% per step gives about +2.6% end to end.

title: [Perf] DFLASH: build the draft num_token_non_padded scalar with torch.full
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

The DFLASH draft step builds its `num_token_non_padded` device scalar with `torch.tensor(bs * block_size, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)` on every step. Building a CUDA tensor from a Python int this way is a pageable host-to-device copy, and the host blocks until the stream drains. If GPU work is already queued, the host waits for all of it before it can launch the draft.

## Modifications

Use `torch.full((), bs * block_size, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)` instead. It produces the same 0-dim int32 tensor with the same value, but the fill runs on device and the host does not wait.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerical change: the tensor has the same value, dtype, and shape.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Host time to produce the 0-dim int32 scalar on B300, torch 2.13.0+cu130, median of 50 calls. The "5 ms queued" column has 5 ms of GPU work already on the stream when the scalar is created.

| variant | GPU idle | 5 ms queued |
|---|---|---|
| `torch.tensor(n, device=cuda)` (before) | 14.8 µs | **4978.5 µs** (waits for the queue) |
| pinned host tensor + `non_blocking=True` | 7.6 µs | 9.4 µs |
| `torch.full((), n, device=cuda)` (this PR) | 6.1 µs | 6.2 µs |

title: [Fix] moe: gated NVFP4 MoE intermediate alignment for FlashInfer TRTLLM
author: Qiaolin-Yu
body: ## Summary Gated NVFP4 experts using FlashInfer TRTLLM currently round each intermediate partition to a multiple of 128 before the quantization method allocates weights. This unnecessarily expands a 192-wide partition to 256. The gated FP4 layout needs 64-aligned intermediate partitions because gate and up are combined. Let the NVFP4 method select alignment before allocating weights and scales: 64 for gated TRTLLM layout, 128 otherwise. Keep the existing generic TRTLLM alignment for other quantization methods and synchronize the runner configuration with the allocated dimensions. No new base-class API is introduced. ## Memory impact Measured on 4x B200 with a 48-layer, 512-expert gated NVFP4 MoE model at TP4 (rank-local intermediate 192), FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE, identical launch configuration and `mem_fraction_static` for both runs; only this PR's source differs. Per GPU (all four ranks identical): | | Before | After | Change | |---|---|---|---| | Target model weights after load | 29.14 GB | 22.86 GB | **-6.28 GB** | | `max_total_num_tokens` | 11,610,688 | 12,311,616 | **+700,928 (+6.0%)** | | Attention KV cache (K+V) | 66.44 GB | 70.44 GB | +4.00 GB | | Mamba cache slots | 2082 | 2203 | +121 (+5.8%) | The weight reduction matches the removed MoE padding (192 -> 256 per rank across 48 layers x 512 experts, 6.33 GiB). Total device usage at startup is unchanged; the freed memory goes to the KV and Mamba caches. ## Validation - B200: real checkpoint-shard loading, weight processing and TRTLLM forward against the existing independent dequantized reference at intermediate widths 160, 192, 256 and 1024. - New regression fails on the unchanged baseline for widths 160 and 192 (256 allocated instead of 192). - Constructor checks preserve 128 alignment for non-gated NVFP4, FP8 and unquantized TRTLLM paths. - All applicable pre-commit hooks pass (formatting, lint, AST, CI registration and secret checks). verified on AIME26, not affected Kernel time doesn't change before, after, --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #39313778552](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39313778552) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #39313778702](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39313778702) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #39313778587](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39313778587)

title: [Feat] moe: Allow SiTU on the CuTe DSL NVFP4 MoE (Kimi-K3 W4A16)
author: ByronHsu
body:
## Why?

- Kimi-K3's routed experts use the SiTU activation. Two checks only allowed `silu`/`relu2`: the CuTe DSL MoE runner and the ModelOpt NVFP4 activation guard. That blocked K3 from FlashInfer's NVFP4 W4A16 CuTe DSL kernel (NVFP4 weights, BF16 activations).
- FlashInfer already supports SiTU in this kernel (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4394, `situ_beta` / `situ_linear_beta`).

## What?

- `modelopt_quant.py`: allow `situ` on the CuTe DSL v2 NVFP4 path, as already done for TRT-LLM.
- `flashinfer_cutedsl.py`:
  - accept `situ` (FlashInfer selects SiTU through the gated Swiglu path);
  - pass `situ_beta` / `situ_linear_beta` (K3's `gemm1_alpha` / `gemm1_clamp_limit`) to `CuteDslMoEWrapper`. Without them the kernel would compute plain SwiGLU.
- New GPU test `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_nvfp4_cutedsl_w4a16_situ_moe.py`.
- Usage is the same as other W4A16 models: `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl` with `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_NVFP4_W4A16=1`.
- Checkpoint requirement (documented, not enforced): gate (`w1`) and up (`w3`) must share one `weight_scale_2` per expert, because the kernel applies one GEMM1 scale before SiTU's `tanh`.

## Verification?

```text
Before:  K3 NVFP4 + SGLANG_FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_NVFP4_W4A16=1 + --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl
         -> AssertionError: activation='situ' is unsupported by flashinfer_cutedsl
After:   same command
         -> routed experts run CuTe DSL W4A16 with SiTU fused into GEMM1
```

Observed on GB300 with the same kernel path on a development branch (5-layer truncated K3 converted to ModelOpt NVFP4, TP4, CUDA graphs), CuTe DSL W4A16 vs Marlin on the same NVFP4 weights:

```text
mean |prompt logprob diff| = 0.026, max = 0.20, first token equal 7/8   (observed)
```

Reproduce:

```bash
SGLANG_FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_NVFP4_W4A16=1 \
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <Kimi-K3 ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint> \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl \
  --tp 4 --trust-remote-code
```

## Test?

- `test_nvfp4_cutedsl_w4a16_situ_moe.py` on GB300 with this branch and the upstream pins (flashinfer 0.7.1, torch 2.14.1+cu130, GB300): **passed** (observed). The test checks two things:
  - CuTe DSL W4A16 SiTU output matches a dequantized torch reference;
  - a SiLU reference does *not* match (cosine < 0.99), so the test proves SiTU is applied.
- `test_nvfp4_moe_backends.py::TestNvFp4MoeBackends::test_flashinfer_cutedsl` (existing SiLU path), same run: **passed** (observed; `2 passed in 415.95s` together with the test above).
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: all hooks passed (observed).
- CI: **pending**.

author: Qiaolin-Yu
body:
## Summary

During breakable prefill CUDA graph capture, `eager_on_graph` keeps a strong reference to each eager break's return value so replay can copy fresh output into it. That return value is allocated outside the graph pool, so a break that returns a newly allocated tensor keeps one buffer per captured size for the lifetime of the graphs.

`_breakable_ple_forward` returned a fresh `[num_tokens, hc_count * hidden_size]` tensor, so the PLE layer retained one such buffer for every prefill capture size. With the default prefill capture sizes up to 16384 tokens this adds up to several GiB per GPU, while only the largest size can ever be live.

Use the output-argument pattern already used by `breakable_unified_attention_with_output` and the DSA indexer: `_add_ple_embedding` allocates the output inside the captured segment, from the graph pool, and the eager break writes `residual + ple(...)` into it in place and returns nothing. Graph-pool memory is then reused across capture sizes, and the residual add no longer needs a second graph-pool tensor.

## Memory impact

Measured on 4x B200 with a Qwen4 PLE model at TP4 using breakable prefill CUDA graphs (74 capture sizes up to 16384 tokens), identical launch configuration for both runs; only this change differs. Per GPU (all four ranks consistent):

| | Before | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Target prefill CUDA graph capture | 14.59 GB | 8.42 GB | **-6.17 GB** |
| Device memory used after startup | 167,601 MiB | 161,549 MiB | **-5.91 GiB** |

The removed retention matches the PLE output size summed over all capture sizes (296,032 tokens x 20,480 B = 5.65 GiB). KV and Mamba cache sizes are unchanged because they are sized before graph capture; the freed memory is left free at startup.

## Validation

- Greedy generation (64 tokens) for prompts of 43, 395, 1931, 7051 and 16651 tokens, cache flushed before each request, with output logprobs, compared against three independent runs of the unchanged code.
  - 43, 395 and 1931 tokens: all 64 output tokens identical and logprob differences exactly 0 against every baseline run.
  - 7051 and 16651 tokens: the unchanged code already diverges between its own runs (first differing token 5-16, max logprob difference up to 0.66); this change stays within that range.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks pass.

title: [Perf] custom_op: Call register_custom_op ops directly in plain eager execution
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Every op registered with `register_custom_op` is called through `torch.ops.sglang.<name>`, even in plain eager execution. The op is registered for a single device key and has no autograd formula. So for ordinary tensors the dispatcher does nothing except box the arguments and re-enter the same Python implementation, and that costs several microseconds per call. For diffusion models this is a noticeable share of host time per denoising step. In a py-spy profile of FLUX.2, Qwen-Image and Ideogram (H200, 2 GPUs, eager, at a size where the host bounds the step), `torch/_ops.py __call__` alone accounts for 5–8% of host time. On Grace hosts (GB200/GB300) and with several TP ranks, the step is host-bound and this time reaches end-to-end latency.

## Modifications

`CustomOpWrapper.real_impl` (`sglang/srt/utils/custom_op.py`) now returns a thin caller. It calls the op's Python function directly only for plain device tensors under `no_grad` / `inference_mode`, which is how both srt and multimodal_gen run. It calls the registered op in every other case:
- under `torch.compile` / export tracing (`torch.compiler.is_compiling()`);
- while a dispatch mode is active: fake tensors, `make_fx`, `FlopCounterMode`, or any `TorchDispatchMode`;
- while a `TorchFunctionMode` is active;
- while the profiler is enabled, so traces keep their `sglang::<op>` spans;
- with grad enabled;
- when an argument is a tensor subclass, or a host or meta tensor. These keep their previous `NotImplementedError` or fake output.
- when another function registered the name first;
- when kernel API logging is enabled.

The dispatcher sets no device guard for Python-registered kernels, so the current-device behavior is unchanged. One difference remains: the dispatcher converted arguments to the schema's types (e.g. a 0-d tensor passed for a `float`), and the direct call passes them as given. The call sites checked pass Python scalars.

No memory is involved. Compiled graphs are unchanged, because they reference `torch.ops.sglang.*` directly. Ops registered with `direct_register_custom_op` and called as `torch.ops.sglang.*` are untouched.

## Accuracy Tests

The same Python implementation runs with the same arguments, so outputs are identical. In every end-to-end configuration below, the output image md5 matched main.

`test/registered/unit/utils/test_custom_op_eager_direct.py` checks four things:
- an eager call enters the implementation directly;
- a `TorchDispatchMode` still sees `sglang.<op>`;
- grad mode, a `TorchFunctionMode` or a tensor subclass goes through the dispatcher;
- the profiler records the op;
- host tensors are still rejected;
- a name registered first by another function keeps that function;
- `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` traces the op.

On GB300 (sm103) and H200, the existing suites that exercise these ops pass:
- diffusion kernels: `test_modulate`, `test_activation`, `test_rope`, `test_complex_rope`, `test_qknorm_rope_out_of_place`, `test_flux2_gated_resnorm`, `test_model_fast_paths`, `test_sites`, `test_residual_gate_fp32`;
- compile and communication: `test_regional_torch_compile`, `test_group_coordinator_compiled_all_reduce`, `test_torch_compile_decoration`.

The only exception is `test_rope`, whose three `test_anima_rope_bit_exact` failures also occur on main on that GPU.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Base `8afe107`, torch 2.13, triton 3.7.1, GB300 (Grace host). Processes were pinned to the GPUs' NUMA node.

**Host time per call** (µs, inference mode):

| op | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `residual_gate_add` | 30.8 | 25.9 |
| `modulate_scale_shift` | 19.0 | 13.8 |
| `fused_silu_mul_bitexact` | 28.0 | 23.9 |
| `fused_rope_rotate_half_bitexact` | 31.5 | 25.4 |
| `qknorm_complex_rope_cuda` | 27.1 | 18.7 |
| `fused_inplace_qknorm_rope` | 15.3 | 8.8 |

On an x86 host (H200, Xeon 8558P) the dispatcher is cheaper and the saving is 0.2–2.4 µs per call.

**End to end.** Client wall clock, median, TP2 eager on GB300 ×2. Servers for main and this PR were resident together and requests alternated over 10 pairs.

| | main | this PR | | this PR faster in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 512² | 1568.3 ms | 1495.9 ms | −4.6% | 10/10 |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 1024² | 1686.5 ms | 1583.3 ms | −6.1% | 10/10 |
| FLUX.1-dev 512² | 3848.7 ms | 3798.2 ms | −1.3% | 10/10 |
| FLUX.1-dev 1024² | 4029.3 ms | 3841.6 ms | −4.7% | 10/10 |

**Stacking with #43859.** #43859 replays small Triton wrappers' launches; it is independent of this PR and the gains add up. The table below was measured with an earlier revision of this PR, before the profiler, grad and device guards were added. Its per-call saving was the same as the final version's. All four servers were resident together, with requests rotated over 8 rounds.

| | main | this PR | #43859 | both |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 512² | 1536.9 ms | 1452.8 ms | 1424.3 ms | 1323.0 ms (−13.9%) |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 1024² | 1632.3 ms | 1561.6 ms | 1520.6 ms | 1437.0 ms (−12.0%) |
| FLUX.1-dev 512² | 3930.4 ms | 3745.6 ms | 3701.6 ms | 3539.8 ms (−9.9%) |
| FLUX.1-dev 1024² | 3966.7 ms | 3809.9 ms | 3763.9 ms | 3650.1 ms (−8.0%) |

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] sampling: Enable Cake softmax on SM100
author: bvolpato
body:
## Motivation

Sampling softmax currently enables FlashInfer's Cake kernel on SM103 but falls back to `torch.softmax` on SM100. FlashInfer 0.7.1 supports Cake on both. This change enables the existing fast path on SM100 without changing its dtype or shape limits.

## Modifications

Extend the runtime and registry gates to SM100 and update the kernel documentation. Extend the existing GPU test with Cake-eligible dense and masked inputs, and run it in B200 CI.

| Sampling case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Qualified, non-deterministic SM100 workload | `torch.softmax` | Cake softmax |
| Qualified, non-deterministic SM103 workload | Cake softmax | Cake softmax |
| Inputs outside the existing Cake dtype or shape limits | `torch.softmax` | `torch.softmax` |
| Deterministic sampling | `torch.softmax` | `torch.softmax` |

This also affects non-deterministic sampling in the regular sampler. The existing dtype and shape limits are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

On `71b2b2769`, the GPU temperature-softmax suite and focused CPU routing tests pass locally on an RTX 5070 Ti (SM120), using normal package imports. Scoped pre-commit checks pass. The local GPU uses the Torch fallback, so this does not establish native Cake accuracy on SM100.

The existing `test_temperature_softmax.py` now covers:

| Coverage | Before this review update | After this review update |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FP32 GPU shapes inside Cake's domain | Existing shapes miss the Cake gate | `(1, 131072)`, `(4, 154880)`, `(64, 131072)`, `(1, 262144)` |
| Dense softmax calls | Per-row temperatures | Plain softmax and per-row temperatures |
| Sparse grammar masks with fully masked splits | Vocabulary 65537 | Vocabularies 65537 and 131072 |
| CUDA CI hardware | 5090 | 5090 and B200 |

The existing AMD registration is retained. The B200 lane runs the same numerical comparisons against Torch on SM100, where the eligible inputs use Cake. Its result on this head is pending CI.

Earlier B200 checks with FlashInfer 0.7.1 compared Cake with Torch and a float64 reference. Maximum absolute error was 6.0e-7 against Torch and 2.3e-6 against float64, with finite normalized outputs and the same argmax.

The earlier GLM-5.3-Flash decode/prefill comparison produced:

| Metric | Before (main) | After (Cake enabled) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Mean absolute decode/prefill log-prob difference | 0.0218 to 0.0234 | 0.0225 to 0.0242 |
| Argmax agreement | 0.980 to 0.984 | 0.980 to 0.984 |

These results were within baseline variation. Those GPU checks used a nightly overlay and predate the latest base update. Current-head B200 serving accuracy and performance comparisons for regular and speculative sampling remain unmeasured because no B200 host is available for those runs.

Run the kernel test with `PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/sampling/test_temperature_softmax.py`. Run the focused routing checks with `PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/kernels/test_kernels_namespace.py -k sampling_softmax`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The server comparison used GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 with EAGLE 4/1/5 on TP4 B200. The branch files were overlaid on nightly commit `7224fce1b5e4`, before the latest base update. No server run of the updated branch is available.

| Streams | Before (main nightly) | After (Cake overlay) | Reduction per verify step |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 8.413 ms | 8.231 ms | 182 us (2.2%) |
| 4 | 12.119 ms | 11.936 ms | 183 us (1.5%) |
| 16 | 18.329 ms | 18.186 ms | 143 us (0.8%) |

This was a restart A/B comparison. At 16 streams, the observed change was only a few times larger than server-to-server variation. The 80-row verify call remains on Torch because the current gate supports at most 64 rows. The 16-stream result comes from other Cake call sites. TP8, other GPUs, non-speculative workloads and the regular sampler on SM100 remain unvalidated.

title: [Perf] diffusion: convrot_int8 comfy_kitchen issues one GEMM per layer by default
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

`convrot_int8`'s comfy_kitchen backend splits tall GEMMs into 8192-row calls (`SGLANG_KITCHEN_INT8_MAX_ROWS`) to keep them off comfy_kitchen's Stream-K schedule. Every extra call also copies its slice of the output, and with comfy-kitchen 0.2.37 whole-model runs are faster unsplit on every GPU we measured.

## Modifications

- Default `SGLANG_KITCHEN_INT8_MAX_ROWS` to `0` (one call per layer). A positive value still splits.
- Update the comment in `convrot_int8_comfy_kitchen.py`, `environment_variables.mdx` and `quantization.mdx`.

## Accuracy Tests

Splitting rows does not change any row's arithmetic. Outputs are bit-identical with and without the split (same-input ablation on all three GPUs).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MiniMax-H3 pruned INT8 checkpoint, comfy_kitchen backend, SGLD ComfyUI workflow, 4 steps × 3 seeds. Steady model-time gain going from rows 8192 to 0:

| GPU | 480p / 124 frames | 768p / 124 frames | Ref2VA / 4 refs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| RTX 4090 | +3.91% | +2.40% | +2.14% |
| RTX 5090 | +2.96% | +1.62% | +1.26% |
| H200 (kitchen forced) | +2.20% | +1.56% | +1.48% |

H200, B200 and RTX 5090 default to the JIT backend, which does not use this setting. RTX 4090 (sm89) always uses comfy_kitchen.

title: [Perf] MiniMax-H3: fused indexed modulation for FP32 AdaLN tables
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

Serialized INT8 MiniMax-H3 checkpoints keep their AdaLN shift/scale/gate tables in FP32. `_modulate_scale_shift` and `_modulate_gate` only had BF16 kernels, so these checkpoints fell back to eager `index_select` + multiply + add + cast. That is about 100 gate calls and 1 scale/shift call per forward, each making several full-size passes.

## Modifications

- Add `indexed_scale_shift_fp32_`, `indexed_gate_fp32` and `indexed_gate_fp32_` next to the BF16 kernels in `kernels/ops/diffusion/modulate/indexed_modulation_triton.py`, export them from the diffusion facade, and document them in the kernels README.
- They keep eager torch's rounding: the product goes through `mul_rn_f32` so the following add cannot contract into an FMA, and the result rounds to BF16 once at the store.
- `minimax_h3.py` dispatches to the FP32 kernels by table dtype. It also requires unit column stride on the tables before taking any kernel path, because the kernels index columns contiguously. The eager fallback is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

- New tests in `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_indexed_modulation.py` require `torch.equal` with eager. They use strided slices of a `[rows, 6*hidden]` table and include cancellation cases. 48 passed on H200.
- H3 unit tests pass.
- H3 whole-model outputs are bit-identical with and without the change (4090, 5090 and H200).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel at [32700, 5376] on H200: gate 1720 µs → 256 µs, scale/shift 2121 µs → 180 µs.

H3 pruned INT8, SGLD ComfyUI workflow, 4 steps × 3 seeds, comfy_kitchen backend. Steady model-time gain:

| GPU | 480p | 768p | Ref2VA / 4 refs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| RTX 4090 | +5.51% | +3.10% | +2.79% |
| RTX 5090 | +4.55% | +2.69% | +2.18% |
| H200 | +4.75% | +3.10% | +2.99% |

H200 with the default JIT backend: +3.44% on 480p. Whether the change applies depends on the checkpoint having FP32 AdaLN tables, not on the GPU or INT8 backend. The full BF16 H3 checkpoint does not hit these kernels.

title: [Perf] diffusion: fused gate/up + SwiGLU MLP on comfy_kitchen INT8 for Qwen-Image 2.1
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

On the comfy_kitchen INT8 backend, Qwen-Image 2.1's MLP ran three GEMMs plus a standalone SiLU-mul: `gate_layer`, `proj`, `silu(gate) * up` written to HBM in BF16, then `out`. ComfyUI runs the same checkpoint as one `[gate | up]` GEMM and a down-projection that applies the SwiGLU inside its quantizer (`int8_linear(..., input_act="swiglu")`).

## Modifications

- `convrot_int8_comfy_kitchen.py`: add `comfy_kitchen_swiglu_mlp`, which makes the two kitchen calls. The linear method's `apply` is unchanged.
- `qwen_image21.py`:
  - `pack_gate_up_weights()` runs from `post_load_weights` and from `_apply`, so packing survives `.to()` and CPU offload. It puts the `gate_layer`/`proj` INT8 weights and row scales into one storage each. This mirrors `pack_qkv_weights`: parameters keep their names and shapes, and no reference to the shared storage is kept.
  - `packed_gate_up()` re-derives the stacked views on every forward.
  - LoRA wrappers, layerwise-offload placeholders, TP > 1, torch.compile and the JIT backend keep the separate projections.

## Accuracy Tests

- The stacked GEMM computes the same per-column arithmetic as the two separate projections.
- The fused quantizer keeps `silu(gate) * up` in FP32 instead of rounding it to BF16 first, so outputs are **not bitwise** the previous path.
  - Against an FP32 reference, relative L2 error is 1.33% for the fused path vs 1.35% for eager at (2048, 3072→1024), and 1.44% vs 1.46% at (4096, 12288→4096).
  - It is the same call ComfyUI makes for this model.
- New unit test (`test_convrot_int8_backends.py`) checks:
  - the fused error vs FP32 is no worse than eager's;
  - re-packing after a CPU round trip;
  - the fallback is bitwise the eager path once the shared storage is gone.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen-Image 2.1 INT8 checkpoint, comfy_kitchen backend, SGLD ComfyUI workflow, 8 steps × 3 seeds. Steady model-time gain:

| GPU | CFG 1 | CFG 4 |
|---|---:|---:|
| RTX 4090 | +4.75% | +4.46% |
| RTX 5090 | +4.44% | +4.16% |
| H200 (kitchen forced) | +3.17% | +2.46% |

H200, B200 and RTX 5090 default to the JIT backend, where this path is inactive. RTX 4090 (sm89) always uses comfy_kitchen.

title: [Fix] [AMD] mamba: Import the causal conv1d kernels for Mamba2 layers on ROCm
author: aarnetalman
body:
## Motivation

Mamba2 hybrid models (Granite 4.0-H, Falcon-H1, Nemotron-H) do not start on ROCm. `mamba.py` binds `causal_conv1d_fn`, `causal_conv1d_update` and their Triton variants only in its CUDA, NPU and XPU branches, so on ROCm none of them is defined. The server fails while capturing the decode CUDA graphs:

```
NameError: name 'causal_conv1d_update_triton' is not defined
```

(`causal_conv1d_update` for Falcon-H1). `mamba1.py` imports those names from `mamba.py`, so it cannot be imported on ROCm either ("Ignore import error when loading sglang.srt.models.mamba").

`causal_conv1d.py` already handles ROCm: the compiled kernel is CUDA-only, and it falls back to the Triton kernels there.

## Modifications

- `mamba.py`: take the CUDA import branch on ROCm too (`is_cuda() or is_hip()`).
- No change on CUDA, NPU, XPU or CPU.

## Accuracy Tests

MI350X, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261019` (upstream/main of 2026-10-19) with this change applied, `--attention-backend triton`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`. GSM8K: all 1,319 questions, temperature 0, `sgl-eval` 0.1.2.

| Model | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tiiuae/Falcon-H1-7B-Instruct` | `NameError: name 'causal_conv1d_update' is not defined` at startup | serves; GSM8K 85.37% (85.82% on the 2026-10-12 nightly); with `--enable-deterministic-inference` 86.05% |
| `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny` | `NameError` at startup | serves; GSM8K 86.20%; with `--enable-deterministic-inference` 86.73% |
| `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2` | fails at startup | needs ReLU2 on ROCm as well, added by #44198 (merged); with both, starts; with `--enable-deterministic-inference` GSM8K 75.28% (26% of answers hit the 2,048-token limit) |

Not addressed here, for reviewers trying other settings on ROCm:
- With AITER enabled (`SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, the ROCm image default), Falcon-H1 serves but its output is wrong (GSM8K 0.5%, on the 2026-10-13 to 2026-10-19 nightlies alike) and a 50-sequence prefill batch hit a GPU memory fault. Granite 4.0-H is fine with AITER (GSM8K 86.35% with Triton attention, 72.25% with the default AITER attention).
- `--enable-deterministic-inference` without `--attention-backend` selects FA3, which the ROCm image does not ship; with `--attention-backend triton` these models start.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance change on other platforms; on ROCm these models did not run before.

title: [Feat] watermark: Add DSPARK speculative decoding support
author: JustinTong0323
body:
> Note: the first commit on this branch is the EAGLE verify-append hotfix from #44199 (watermarked EAGLE/EAGLE3 output is undetectable on main without it). This branch will be rebased to a single commit once #44199 lands.

DSPARK verifies a linear draft chain. Each verify row's context is the committed watermark tail followed by the earlier draft tokens, so the existing speculative selector applies with a lower-triangular chain mask. The DSPARK worker forces those rows before acceptance. After acceptance it records the accepted rows' contexts and appends the committed tokens to the ring.

**Design: verify-side forcing.**
- A forced row's target distribution is one-hot, so DSPARK's rejection-sampling accept — with or without block verification — emits exactly the watermarked token.
- Detection therefore follows the unchanged contract: no DSPARK-specific detector logic, single and dual key alike.
- Draft-side keyed sampling would raise acceptance, but it needs the selector inside DSPARK's folded draft graph and a cropped-vocabulary hash contract. It is left as follow-up given the measured cost below.

**Evidence** (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 8×H200, TP8/EP8, DSPARK block size 5):
- Detection: 40 essays × 512 tokens, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95. DSPARK median request z is 2.73 (16/40 at p < 1e-3) against 3.06 (18/40) without speculation on the same prompts; wrong key z 0.91. OFF: median z 0.21, 0/40.
- GSM8K-100 (temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95): 99% with 100% stop rate, both watermarked and not, 0 truncated, 0 errors.
- Throughput: bench_serving random 1024/512, c8, 100 prompts, temperature 0.8, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, six reps over two launches: TPOT +3.73%, output throughput −2.25%, accept length −3.27%.

**Also fixes** an EAGLE/NEXTN regression (#44199): the fused verify-commit path (#41175) skipped the watermark ring append, so watermarked EAGLE3 output on main is undetectable. On Qwen3-8B with EAGLE3 3/1/4, 0/40 requests reach p < 1e-3 before the fix and 40/40 after; tree 5/8/32 is also 40/40.

**Tests:**
- CUDA watermark selector/state suites, plus a DSPARK chain case. The case checks that rejection-sampling accept, with and without block verification, emits the forced tokens, and that the committed ring and context history equal those of non-speculative decode (22 passed total).
- Endpoint e2e `test_watermark.py` (5 passed).

Not covered: DSPARK with DP attention or PD disaggregation (PD stays rejected by validation). DFLASH stays rejected; its chain can reuse `force_speculative_chain` in a later PR.

title: [Fix] DeepSeek-V4.1: Align paged indexer score rows for DeepSelect decode
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

On SM90 the full top-k decode of the ratio-1/2 index layers (`FullTopKIndexer._torch_decode`) runs DeepSelect `topk_page_transform` on the paged fp4 index scores from `fp4_index_logits_paged`. DeepSelect requires 128-byte-aligned rows, but the scores were padded to eight floats only, so any score width that is not a multiple of 32 floats fails:

```
Tensor<256, 524290>[strides=<524296, 1>, dtype=float32]
Root cause: Tensor stride for dimension 0 is not aligned to 128 bytes
```

With the cookbook H200 recipe for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, every TP rank hits this at startup and the server exits.

`test_fp4_indexer.py::test_hopper_indexer_backends_replay` also fails on main, first with `AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'page_table'`, because its fake metadata predates the DeepSelect path.

## Modifications

- `fp4_index_logits_paged`: allocate the scores with `aligned_new_empty` at DeepSelect's input stride alignment (128B) instead of padding rows to eight floats; that alignment also covers candidate-amax.
- `decode_scores`: build the top-k v2 plan only when the caller uses it. The SM90 full top-k selects with DeepSelect and never read it, so it no longer launches the plan kernel every decode step; `select_decode` asserts the plan is present.
- `test_hopper_indexer_backends_replay`: give the full top-k a real per-row page table, kept in sync with the shuffled request table on every replay, and an output buffer of exactly live rows by `topk`, as at runtime. The candidate outputs keep their padded shape and padding checks.

## Tests

- The updated test fails on main with the 128B stride error and passes with this change.
- On H200, each registered file that exercises this code passes when run as CI does (`python3 <file> -f`): `test_fp4_indexer.py`, `test_deep_select.py`, `test_dsv4_nonpaged_indexer.py`, `test_dsv41_candidate_blocks.py`, `test_dense_prefill_indexer.py`, `test_dsv41_prefill_sparse_indexer.py`, `qsa/test_qsa.py`, `test_dsv32_indexer_fusion.py`, `test_dsv4_indexer_quant.py`.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash launches and serves on 8xH200 with the cookbook H200 Low-Latency recipe, which fails at startup on main.
