title: [Fix] cuda_graph: Wait for in-flight layer-wise cache loads before prefill graph replay
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

HiCache L2 load-back, HiCache storage load-back (e.g. `buffer_only`), and the unified-cache external linker load KV/SWA/Mamba state into the device pools layer by layer, overlapped with the prefill forward. The forward waits for each layer inside the pool accessors (`get_key_buffer`, `mamba2_layer_index`, ...) through the registered `layer_transfer_counter`.

A prefill CUDA graph replay never runs those Python-level waits: the captured graph is launched as a whole. Nothing stops the graph from replaying a batch whose load is still in flight (`scheduler.py` has carried `# todo: disable cuda graph execution if hicache loading triggered` since 2025-06). The forward then reads layers that have not landed yet and produces wrong logits silently. Computed KV for the following pages is built on the corrupted state, and can be cached and backed up under the same content-addressed keys.

This is reachable on main today whenever a model replays the prefill graph for a loading batch. Inkling defaults to the Full prefill CUDA graph backend, so its HiCache path is affected. Whether it shows up depends on the race between the H2D copies and the replay: the existing Inkling HiCache bit-exact tests pass on main only because the copies usually win.

## Modifications

- `PrefillCudaGraphRunner.execute`: before a Full replay, if the KV pool's layer transfer counter has an active consumer (this batch is loading), wait until the last layer has landed. Works for both counters (HiCache `LayerDoneCounter`, a stream wait; linker `LayerWiseLoadCounter`, a CPU wait), since both complete layers in order.
- Eager and breakable prefill are unchanged and keep per-layer load/compute overlap: breakable replay runs the pool accessors at its eager breaks, so their per-layer waits still apply (except a captured state-reading linear extend, see below). A loading batch that replays a Full graph now waits for the whole load first; batches without a load are unaffected.
- Test hook `SGLANG_TEST_HICACHE_H2D_DELAY_CYCLES` (default 0, off): a GPU sleep on the host-to-device stream before each layer's load, so a replay that skips the load wait reliably reads unloaded layers.

## Accuracy Tests

Inkling (`thinkingmachines/Inkling --revision test`, deterministic inference, Full prefill graph default).

New `TestUnifiedHybridHiCacheSlowLoadBitExact` (the existing HiCache bit-exact class with `SGLANG_TEST_HICACHE_H2D_DELAY_CYCLES=50000000`):

| GPU | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1x H200 (CI arch) | avg KL 4.4e-3 (fail) | 0.0 |
| 1x GB300 | avg KL 1.7e-2 (fail) | 0.0 |

The existing `TestUnifiedHybridHiCacheBitExact` passes on both trees: without the delay the H2D copies usually win the race, which is why CI has not caught this.

Earlier probe on 1x GB300 with the same kind of injected H2D delay, also covering storage load-back; the logs confirm graph replays with an in-flight load:

| Tree | Injected H2D delay | `TestUnifiedHybridHiCacheBitExact` (L2) | `TestUnifiedHybridBufferOnlyBitExact` (L3) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | no | avg KL 0.0 | avg KL 0.0 |
| main | yes | **avg KL 3.1e-3 (fail)** | **avg KL 6.4e-3 (fail)** |
| this PR | yes | avg KL 0.0 | avg KL 0.0 |

The same fix also restores KL 0.0 for the Mooncake direct linker on Inkling (#41343), which hits the race without any injected delay (avg KL 2.5e-3 before; 0.0 in 3/3 runs after, and 0.0 with a 0.2 s per-layer injected load delay).

Breakable check: Inkling forced to `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable` with the same injected delay gives avg KL 0.0 on main and on this PR (4 replays with an in-flight load each); its state reads run at eager breaks.

**Out of scope, fixed in #44414:** a breakable graph that captures a state-reading linear extend (the Triton KDA extend captured since #41105) skips those reads' waits. GLM-5.3-Flash on 4x GB300 with the Triton KDA extend forced and the same delay: median KL 3.5-4.1e-3 on main and on this PR vs a 1.9e-4 floor; 1.4e-4 when every replay waits or when the KDA capture is disabled. Not a regression from this PR.

## Benchmark and Profiling

Host-tier (L2) hit TTFT, Inkling-Small bf16, TP4 on 4x GB300, Full prefill graph, 512 new tokens on a cached prefix, median of 5 (ms). `eager` is the alternative of running a loading batch eagerly instead of replaying the graph.

| Prefix | main (no wait) | this PR | eager |
|---|---|---|---|
| 160k | 113.0 | 115.0 | 195.4 |
| 320k | 176.0 | 182.2 | 247.7 |
| 500k | 254.9 | 255.0 | 306.7 |

Cold and device-hit TTFT are unchanged.

## Tests

- `test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py::TestPrefillCudaGraphRunnerLayerLoads`: the replay wait blocks until the last layer of an in-flight load completes, and is a no-op without a counter. Negative control: removing the wait fails `test_replay_waits_for_every_layer_of_an_inflight_load`.
- `test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py`: 18 passed, including `test_breakable_replay_keeps_per_layer_load_overlap` (fails if the wait is not limited to Full).
- `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_hybrid_bitexact.py::TestUnifiedHybridHiCacheSlowLoadBitExact`: fails on main, passes with the fix (table above); about 70 s per class.

- [x] Provide accuracy evaluation results.

title: [Perf] distributed: Skip the DLPack re-wrap of custom all-reduce results
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

`custom_all_reduce` in `sglang/kernels/ops/communication/all_reduce.py` ends with `torch.from_dlpack(result)`. With apache-tvm-ffi 0.1.11 and torch's DLPack exchange API loaded (`torch_c_dlpack_ext`, present in the `lmsysorg/sglang` image), the tvm-ffi call already returns a `torch.Tensor`. So `torch.from_dlpack` does a pure torch → DLPack → torch round trip. Along the way it also builds a current-stream object from a device string and makes a `__dlpack__` call that may be retried.

On a Grace host (GB300) this round trip costs about 20 µs per call. That is about half of the ~42 µs host time of an eager TP all-reduce, and twice the cost of the tvm-ffi call itself. Diffusion DiTs run several all-reduces per block in eager mode, so on GB300 with TP the step is host-bound and this cost shows up directly in end-to-end latency.

## Modifications

Return `result` as is when it is already a `torch.Tensor`. Otherwise, e.g. with `TVM_FFI_DISABLE_TORCH_C_DLPACK=1`, keep `torch.from_dlpack`.

The returned tensor aliases the same memory as before. `torch.from_dlpack` passed the current stream, so the round trip never added a cross-stream wait, and dropping it changes no ordering. No memory is involved, and CUDA-graph capture and the compiled path (`diffusion_all_reduce`) are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_custom_all_reduce.py --num-gpu 2` on GB300 ×2:
  - 180 passed with the exchange API loaded;
  - 180 passed with `TVM_FFI_DISABLE_TORCH_C_DLPACK=1`, which covers the `from_dlpack` branch.
- End to end: every configuration below produced the same output image md5 as main.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Base `c54ba66cd4`, torch 2.13, apache-tvm-ffi 0.1.11, GB300 ×2 (Grace host). Processes were pinned to the GPUs' NUMA node.

**Host time per call** (µs, eager, inference mode; the GPU is kept busy so only submission is timed):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `GroupCoordinator.all_reduce` (diffusion TP group), 0.4 MiB | 42.0 | 20.7 |
| same, 4.5 MiB | 39.2 | 18.2 |
| same, 27 MiB | 43.7 | 20.6 |
| for reference: the tvm-ffi call alone | ~10 | ~10 |

**End to end.** Client wall clock, median, TP2 eager. Servers for main and this PR were resident together and requests alternated over 10 pairs.

| | main | this PR | | this PR faster in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 512² | 1462.4 ms | 1298.3 ms | −11.2% | 10/10 |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 1024² | 1548.4 ms | 1391.3 ms | −10.1% | 10/10 |
| FLUX.1-dev 512² | 3794.0 ms | 3559.2 ms | −6.2% | 10/10 |
| FLUX.1-dev 1024² | 4019.0 ms | 3696.4 ms | −8.0% | 10/10 |

The same applies to srt's eager TP all-reduces through `CustomAllReduceV2`, e.g. extend/prefill outside CUDA graphs. Those were not measured here. This change is independent of #43859 and #44158, which cut host time elsewhere.

**H200 (x86 host), added 2026-10-16.** Base `c15edf314d`, 2xH200 (Xeon 8558P), TP2 eager.

- Host time per call of `custom_all_reduce` in `kernels/ops/communication/all_reduce.py` (bf16 [1, 4096, 3072]): 22.39 µs on main, 6.42 µs with this PR. The round trip costs about 16 µs on x86 too.
- End to end, client wall-clock median at 512². The second column is from #44642's in-process A/B, which bypasses this wrapper and so also drops the re-wrap; it measured −0.2% (Qwen-Image-2.1) and −2.4% (FLUX.1) on top of this PR.

| | main | this PR (different server instance) | in-process A/B: main vs main + #44642 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 TP2 512² | 797.0 ms | 686.6 ms | −14.4% (10/10) |
| FLUX.1-dev TP2 512² | 2196.0 ms | 1856.9 ms | −15.2% (8/8) |

Two identical co-resident servers differed by up to 3.5% on this box, so the cross-instance column is indicative only; the gap here is far larger.

- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (Existing `test_custom_all_reduce.py` covers both branches, see above.)

title: [Feat] sgl-router: Fix cache-aware routing for MTP/EAGLE on hybrid (Mamba/KDA) models
author: sherlockwu
body:
Stacked on https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44243.

## Motivation

With `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE` (MTP), cache-aware routing never matches on hybrid linear-attention models (Qwen3.5, GLM-5.3-Flash):

- The router picks bigram block hashing whenever `speculative_algorithm` is EAGLE-family (`classify_bigram`).
- The engine uses bigram radix keys for EAGLE only when the model has **no** Mamba/linear-attention layers (`unified_tree_core.py`, `rust_tree_core/adapter.py`).

So hybrid workers publish unigram block hashes, the router queries with bigram hashes, and same-prefix requests spread by load instead of following the cache.

## Modifications

Router only. `/server_info` already reports `uses_mamba_radix_cache`, so both discovery paths (`workers/introspect.rs`, primary; `state/kv_events/discovery.rs`, fallback) now use
`is_bigram = classify_bigram(speculative_algorithm) && !uses_mamba_radix_cache`.
No engine change is needed, so this also fixes routing for engines already deployed.

Known gap: `uses_mamba_radix_cache` comes from an architecture list (`arg_groups/overrides.py`), while the engine's bigram rule uses `uses_ssm_state()`. They agree for every hybrid model I checked (GLM-5.3-Flash / `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`, the Qwen3.5/3.8 family, Kimi Linear, NemotronH), except `MiniCPMSALAForCausalLM`. That model with EAGLE would still hash bigrams, which is no worse than today.

## Verification

- `cargo test --lib -- is_bigram introspect kv_events::discovery`: 35 passed, including a new test (EAGLE + `uses_mamba_radix_cache: true` gives `is_bigram=false`).
- End to end against the **stock** engine (no engine patch): 2× Qwen3.5-27B workers with the cookbook MTP flags (`--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`), `--policy cache_aware`, and 11 same-prefix chat requests after flushing both caches:

| Router | `is_bigram` at subscribe | Split |
|---|---|---|
| base | `true` | 5/6 |
| this PR | `false` | 11/0 |

title: [Fix] [AMD] qwen3: Fix KV cache write in the fused QK-norm + mRoPE decode path
author: jiaqiang-dot-liu
body:
## Motivation

On ROCm with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` (the default in the ROCm images), dense Qwen3-VL decode goes through `Qwen3Attention.forward_prepare_aiter_fused_mrope`, which calls aiter's `fused_qk_norm_mrope_3d_cache_pts_quant_shuffle` to run QK-norm + 3D mRoPE + the KV cache write in one kernel. That path currently produces garbage:

| `Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct`, default server args | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K (1319 questions, chat API, greedy) | **0.005** | **0.942** |
| "What is the capital of France? Answer in one sentence." | `The capital of France's capital of France is Paris of France is Paris is Paris is …` | `The capital of France is Paris.` |
| Image with the text "MI355X 2026", a red circle and a blue square | `BasedThe text: The text: The text: The text: …` | `… The text written at the top of the image is: M1355X 2026 … Left Shape: A solid red circle. Right Shape: A solid blue square.` |

**Root cause.** Since ROCm/aiter#4531 (in the AITER pin since #37784), the kernel reads `k_cache` / `v_cache` strides as `(block, token, head, head_dim)`: dim 1 is the per-token stride and dim 2 the per-head stride. `Qwen3Attention` passes the NHD pool buffers `(slots, num_kv_heads, head_dim)`, whose dim-1 / dim-2 strides are `head_dim` / `1`, so the K/V of slot `s`, head `h` is written at element offset `s * head_dim + h` instead of `(s * num_kv_heads + h) * head_dim`. The decode token's own slot is not written by it, and other slots — including the prompt KV of running requests — are overwritten. Nothing faults and throughput is unchanged, so performance runs do not notice. Prefill uses the unfused path, which is why the first token is still sensible.

Affected: dense Qwen3-VL (`Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration`) on ROCm with the default aiter attention backend. Qwen3-VL-MoE uses `Qwen3MoeAttention` and does not take this path; the AMD VLM accuracy test runs `Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct`, which is why CI did not catch it.

The same path also cast `cos_sin_cache` to the activation dtype on every layer of every decode step. On HIP that cache is kept in fp32, and for Qwen3-VL-8B (`max_position_embeddings = 262144`) it is 128 MiB, so each step moved about 6.75 GiB (36 layers × 128 MiB read + 64 MiB write) just to recreate the same bf16 table.

## Modifications

- `aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope_set_kv` (new, `models/qwen3.py`) holds the kernel call and passes the NHD buffers as one-slot blocks, `k_cache.unsqueeze(1)` → `(slots, 1, num_kv_heads, head_dim)` with `block_size = 0`, which gives the kernel the token stride `num_kv_heads * head_dim` and the head stride `head_dim`.
- `Qwen3Attention.forward` takes the fused path only when the pool buffer is that 3D NHD layout in the activation dtype. The kernel's quantized write uses a fixed per-tensor scale of 1.0 rather than the layer's `k_scale` / `v_scale`, and the HND and `vectorized_5d` layouts are not NHD; those configurations use the unfused path.
- `RotaryEmbedding.cos_sin_cache_as(dtype)` returns `cos_sin_cache` in `dtype` and reuses the cast copy until `cos_sin_cache` is replaced (`_ensure_cos_sin_cache_length`, device moves). The first call happens in the eager warmup before CUDA graph capture, so the captured graphs contain no cast.
- `test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope.py` calls the helper with NHD buffers and checks q and the K/V written at `out_cache_loc` against `RMSNorm.forward_native` + `MRotaryEmbedding.forward_native`, that no other slot is written, and the `cos_sin_cache_as` reuse/invalidation. With the 3D buffers passed as before, 98% of the written K elements mismatch; with this PR it passes.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.0, torch 2.9.1, Triton 3.7.0, transformers 5.19.0, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, default server args (attention backend resolves to `aiter`, decode CUDA graphs on). The pinned AITER `e7d2453f` has the same stride handling in both fused kernels.

**Unit test.** `test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope.py`: 2 passed, 8 subtests passed.

**`Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct`, end to end:** see the table above. GSM8K via `python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 1319 --max-tokens 2048`; the text and image prompts are single chat requests at temperature 0.

Dense Qwen3 (plain RoPE) does not take this path and is unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct`, `python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 1.0`, `--num-prompts = max(16, 4 × concurrency)`, prefix cache flushed before each run, one benchmark at a time. Both servers generate the same number of tokens per request, so the comparison holds even though the `main` output is wrong.

| Concurrency | Median TPOT `main` (ms) | Median TPOT this PR (ms) | Delta | Output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.960 | 4.818 | **−19.2%** | +14.5% |
| 8 | 6.782 | 5.462 | **−19.5%** | +22.5% |
| 32 | 8.797 | 7.490 | **−14.9%** | +15.9% |
| 64 | 12.359 | 11.190 | −9.5% | +9.2% |

The saving is a roughly constant 1.1–1.3 ms per step across concurrencies, the order expected for the ~6.75 GiB per-step `cos_sin_cache` cast that is no longer launched.

## Reproduce

```bash
MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path $MODEL --port 30000
python -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 30000 --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 1319 --max-tokens 2048
python -m pytest test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope.py
```

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Perf] [AMD] qwen3: Fuse QK-norm + RoPE + KV cache write for dense Qwen3 decode
author: jiaqiang-dot-liu
body:
Follow-up to #44266, which fixed the KV cache write of the same fused path for Qwen3-VL (3D mRoPE).

## Motivation

On ROCm with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` (the default in the ROCm images), every decode layer of dense Qwen3 runs QK-norm, RoPE and the KV cache store as four small kernels of about 4.5 µs each. GPU kernel time in one Qwen3-8B decode step at batch 8 on MI355X (36 layers), from a torch profiler trace:

| Kernel | Baseline launches | Baseline time | This PR launches | This PR time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aiter::add_rmsnorm_quant_kernel` (q_norm, k_norm) | 72 | 319 µs | 0 | 0 |
| `rotary_embedding_kernel` | 36 | 165 µs | 0 | 0 |
| `sglang::store_kvcache_kernel` | 36 | 164 µs | 0 | 0 |
| `mrope_utils::fused_mrope_rms_kv_kernel` (1D instantiation) | 0 | 0 | 36 | 156 µs |
| **Total** | **144** | **648 µs** | **36** | **156 µs** |

The fused kernel does the same work in one launch per layer, 0.49 ms less GPU time per step at batch 8. `qwen3.py` already uses it for 3D mRoPE (Qwen3-VL); dense Qwen3 uses 1D RoPE and never reached it, and `apply_qk_norm`'s fused path is CUDA-only.

## Modifications

- `aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope_set_kv` dispatches on the rotary type: `MRotaryEmbedding` keeps `fused_qk_norm_mrope_3d_cache_pts_quant_shuffle`, plain `RotaryEmbedding` uses `fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_pts_quant_shuffle`. Both share the NHD cache views and the cached `cos_sin_cache` cast from #44266.
- `Qwen3Attention.use_fused_qk_norm_rope` enables the 1D kernel only for exactly `RotaryEmbedding` (YaRN / NTK / linear-scaling subclasses keep the unfused path), full-width rotary, head sizes the kernel is instantiated for (64/128/256/512), and a single eps for both norms. The decode-only, NHD-only, activation-dtype-only conditions from #44266 apply unchanged, so prefill, speculative verify, FP8 KV cache and non-NHD layouts keep the unfused path.
- The unit test gains the 1D case: Qwen3-8B head layouts at TP1 and TP4, 1–256 tokens.

Numerics: the unfused HIP RoPE kernel already converts the fp32 `cos_sin_cache` to the activation dtype before rotating (`test/registered/rotary/test_rope_rocm.py` asserts equality with `cos_sin_cache.to(dtype)`), so reading a bf16 table here does not change RoPE precision. The norms are computed in fp32 inside the kernel.

Besides `Qwen3ForCausalLM`, the path is reached by multimodal models whose language model is `Qwen3ForCausalLM` (InternVL, Intern-S1, MiniCPM-V, LightOnOCR, Step3-VL-10B, Qwen3-ASR); those were not benchmarked here.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.0, torch 2.9.1, Triton 3.7.0, transformers 5.19.0, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, default server args (attention backend resolves to `aiter`, decode CUDA graphs on). Baseline is `3b72b70ef4` with #44266 applied; this PR is measured on top of it.

**Unit test.** `test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope.py`: 3 passed, 16 subtests passed.

**GSM8K**, `python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 1319 --max-tokens 4096` (chat API, greedy):

| Model | Baseline | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | 0.944 | 0.946 |
| Qwen3-14B-FP8 | 0.955 | 0.957 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 0.635 | 0.626 |
| Qwen3-8B, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` (unfused path on both) | 0.947 | 0.948 |

The standard error of one run is about 0.006 for the 8B / 14B rows and 0.013 for 0.6B, so every gap is within one standard error. With `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` the decode trace of this PR contains `rotary_embedding_kernel` and no fused kernel, confirming the fallback.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 1.0`, `--num-prompts = max(16, 4 × concurrency)`, prefix cache flushed before each run, one benchmark at a time. Median TPOT:

**Qwen3-8B**, two rounds with the GPU assignment swapped, mean of the two (per-round deltas: −5.0 / −9.2 / −9.3 / −6.3 / −5.5% and −5.8 / −11.8 / −9.1 / −5.9 / −4.5%):

| Concurrency | Baseline (ms) | This PR (ms) | Delta | Output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4.859 | 4.596 | −5.4% | +5.6% |
| 8 | 5.282 | 4.727 | **−10.5%** | +11.1% |
| 32 | 6.300 | 5.719 | **−9.2%** | +8.1% |
| 64 | 8.116 | 7.622 | −6.1% | +5.8% |
| 128 | 13.093 | 12.437 | −5.0% | +4.5% |

**Qwen3-14B-FP8**, one round:

| Concurrency | Baseline (ms) | This PR (ms) | Delta | Output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8.967 | 8.710 | −2.9% | +2.9% |
| 8 | 9.589 | 9.038 | −5.7% | +5.7% |
| 32 | 11.080 | 10.567 | −4.6% | +4.4% |
| 64 | 13.292 | 12.816 | −3.6% | +3.3% |
| 128 | 19.339 | 18.830 | −2.6% | +1.8% |

**Qwen3-0.6B**, one round:

| Concurrency | Baseline (ms) | This PR (ms) | Delta | Output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.552 | 1.360 | **−12.3%** | +13.7% |
| 8 | 1.996 | 1.613 | **−19.2%** | +22.6% |
| 32 | 2.683 | 2.287 | **−14.8%** | +16.0% |
| 64 | 3.759 | 3.341 | **−11.1%** | +11.5% |
| 128 | 6.238 | 5.824 | −6.6% | +7.0% |

The absolute saving is 0.19–0.26 ms per step at concurrency 1 and 0.38–0.66 ms from concurrency 8 up, so the relative gain is largest for small models and moderate batches, where the per-layer small kernels are a larger share of the step.

## Reproduce

```bash
MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-8B
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path $MODEL --port 30000
python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --model $MODEL \
  --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 8
python -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 30000 --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 1319 --max-tokens 4096
python -m pytest test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope.py
```

title: [Fix] moe: Fix --enable-fused-moe-sum-all-reduce outside CUDA and with LoRA hooks
author: ZhengGong-amd
body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-fused-moe-sum-all-reduce` (#19672) the Triton down GEMM sums the experts into `out_hidden_states` and leaves `intermediate_cache3` unwritten, but `_fused_moe_kernel_sequence` honours that only under `_is_cuda or _is_musa` and ignores LoRA's `after_down` hook; this PR handles the fused case before the platform dispatch and disables the fusion when `hooks.after_down` is set.

On HIP, XPU and the fallback, the combine reduces the unwritten `intermediate_cache3` over the result. On every platform the LoRA down delta, added to `intermediate_cache3`, is dropped. On ROCm every Triton-runner MoE layer with `topk > 2` breaks; GSM8K is 0 % for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Kimi-Linear-48B with `--moe-runner-backend triton`, and for GLM-5.3, MiniMax-M2.7 and Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next FP8 with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`. gemma-4-26B-A4B (I=704) runs Triton by default, so the flag alone breaks it.

## Modifications

- In the fused case, apply `routed_scaling_factor` as the platform's unfused combine does: everywhere except the aiter path, whose `moe_sum` skips it too. The CUDA/MUSA code is moved, not changed.
- An empty `LoRAHooks()` (LoRA enabled, no active adapter) keeps the fusion on.
- Add `TestFusedMoeSumAllReduce`: flag-on output must match flag-off and the fused kernel launch is asserted, for routed scale None/2.5 with no hooks, empty hooks or an `after_down` hook. Without the LoRA guard the 6 `after_down` cases fail with ~20 % relative error.

## Accuracy Tests

On MI355X at main `b960aa903a`, `TestFusedMoeSumAllReduce` passes with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0` and `=1` (main fails 18/18 in both), as does the rest of `test_fused_moe.py`.

`sgl-eval` gsm8k, temperature 0, MI355X. First two rows: 1319 items, Triton runner, main flag-off run twice as noise control. Rest: 200 items, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`, `auto` resolves to Triton:

| model | main off | main on | this PR, on |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | 94.09 / 94.16 | 0.00 | 94.31 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B (routed scale 2.45) | 91.28 / 91.96 | 0.00 | 92.42 |
| GLM-5.3 FP8, TP4 | 51.5¹ | 0.0 | 49.0 |
| MiniMax-M2.7, TP2 | 96.0 | 0.0 | 96.0 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 | 96.5 | 0.0 | 96.0 |
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-FP8 | 96.0 | 0.0 | 96.0 |

¹ GLM-5.3 loops on most answers in this aiter-off config regardless of the flag; the gap is within n=200 noise.

Block-FP8 MoE with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` and `--moe-runner-backend triton` is broken on main even flag-off; #41636 fixes that separately.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed change is intended. gemma-4-26B-A4B-it, cookbook command, flag off, TP1, `sglang.benchmark.serving` random 1937/389, 307 prompts, concurrency 61, median of runs 2–4 of 4: total 13870.9 → 13935.4 tok/s (+0.5 %), TTFT and TPOT flat. With the flag on, gemma-4 runs ~60 % below its flag-off throughput on gfx950 (`acq_rel` atomics), so the flag should stay off on ROCm.

title: [Perf] detokenizer: Group return IPC sends by tokenizer worker
author: hope1262946533
body:
# Summary

Fixes #43096.

Add opt-in grouping for the **Detokenizer → TokenizerWorker** return path. Requests from one already-produced output are grouped by their original `http_worker_ipc` and sent once per destination instead of once per request.

**Measured benefit: +2.1% whole-machine client output throughput**, from a trace-free, single-variable, 16-round comparison on DeepSeek-V4-Pro (see "Benchmark evidence" below). The same change cuts return-hop IPC sends by ~94% and roughly halves return-worker CPU.

1. Register `SGLANG_OPT_DETOK_TOKENIZER_GROUP_SEND` as `EnvBool(False)` and read it once when the multi-HTTP-worker detokenizer event loop starts.
1. Reuse `_handle_output_by_indices()` from the merged Router grouped-send change (#42238); do not duplicate, downgrade, or modify the current message-field slicing logic.
1. Group only when at least two requests share a destination; when every request has a distinct owner, keep the original per-request path unchanged.
1. Construct every destination payload before sending the first one. If the splitter raises `_CannotSplitBatch`, fall back for the entire output to the original per-request path.
1. Keep send failures outside the fallback handler so an earlier successful send is never duplicated by a fallback/retry.

Enable before launching the service:

```bash
export SGLANG_OPT_DETOK_TOKENIZER_GROUP_SEND=1
```

Unset or `0` preserves the existing per-request path. The benchmark prototype used `SGLANG_DETOK_TOKENIZER_GROUP_SEND`; this upstream extraction uses the canonical `SGLANG_OPT_*` name and the typed `Envs` API. The prototype name is not an alias in this patch.

# Dependency and scope

The Router hop is addressed by #42238 (`[Perf] Reduce multi-detokenizer router IPC sends`), which is **merged into main** (merge commit `cb9bd1d`, 2026-10-09). This commit is its follow-up: it reuses the merged `_handle_output_by_indices()` helper and does not modify it, so the Router path is unchanged.

The incremental commit changes only:

1. `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` — default-off optimization switch.
1. `python/sglang/srt/managers/multi_tokenizer_mixin.py` — owner-grouped return sends and event-loop wiring.
1. `test/registered/unit/managers/test_multi_tokenizer_mixin.py` — actual message-class regression coverage.
1. `docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx` — environment-variable documentation.

Excluded: HTTP listener/reuse-port changes, Scheduler diagnostics or admission changes, output-chain trace/profiling, changes to the Router routing rule, and deployment-specific code.

Preserved: per-request owner, intra-destination order, first-destination order, current single/control request handling, watchdog behavior, and default-disabled behavior. No cross-message merge, delay window, or new output protocol is introduced.

# Benchmark evidence

Measurements use SGLang 0.5.17 at `29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`: DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP8/DP8, no MTP, 32 tokenizer and 32 detokenizer workers, decode graph maximum 310, maximum running requests 2480, memory fraction 0.96859, server seed 81095743. Upstream Router grouping was enabled for every run.

Client settings were identical: aiakperf streaming generate API, random dataset, concurrency 4960, 79,360 requests, input/output 60,000/1,000, 16 client processes, seed 0, temperature 0, top-p 1, fake bootstrap and ignore EOS enabled.

## Measured end-to-end benefit

1. **Trace-free whole-machine client output throughput (clean net gain).** Default shared-listener configuration, no tracing and no in-process probes, three runs each, only this switch changed (2026-10-11): disabled `42,297.97 / 42,564.88 / 42,306.00 token/s`; enabled `43,740.88 / 43,106.29 / 43,025.66 token/s`. Derived from the three-run means, **+2.13%**. Total duration moved from `1876.21 / 1864.45 / 1875.86 s` to `1814.32 / 1841.03 / 1844.48 s`.
1. **Instrumented A/B six-run** (all runs with output-chain tracing enabled; three disabled followed by three enabled): disabled `42,463.52 / 42,350.61 / 42,426.76 token/s`; enabled `43,547.89 / 42,816.95 / 43,280.41 token/s`. Derived from the three-run means, **+1.89%**. Reported separately from item 1 because reducing sends also reduces instrumentation work.
1. **Return-hop IPC calls:** disabled `79,376,257 / 79,376,257 / 79,376,257`; enabled `4,790,103 / 4,325,743 / 5,063,191`. The same `79,376,257` output events were carried in each run, so the enabled condition reduced actual return-hop send calls by approximately 93.62%-94.55%. Send counters include warmup/non-formal output events.
1. **Return-worker CPU:** detokenizer p50 decreased from `288.56% / 276.91% / 289.95%` to `107.51% / 99.74% / 105.75%`; TokenizerWorker p50 decreased from `731.38% / 732.34% / 730.86%` to `373.87% / 384.82% / 364.64%`. Percentages use single-core process-group CPU units.
1. **Batchsize and preallocation:** per-rank Batchsize p50 was `309 / 309 / 309` disabled and `310 / 310 / 310` enabled; p10 was `235 / 209 / 178` disabled and `307 / 215 / 307` enabled. The preallocation-queue p50 was `151 / 176 / 168` disabled and `282 / 293 / 284` enabled; `#transfer-req` was zero in all six runs.
1. **Correctness and completion:** all formal requests succeeded in all runs; output-stage request IDs were conserved and output lengths were 1,000. Text/token-ID bitwise equivalence was not measured.

## Qualification

1. The benefit is **conditional on the default HTTP listener topology**. When new connections are spread across HTTP workers per-worker (SO_REUSEPORT or an equivalent multi-listener server), grouping stops paying off: a same-workload comparison measured grouping enabled versus disabled at `42,733` versus `42,764 token/s` (means of three runs each) under per-worker listeners, compared with `43,291` versus `42,390` under the default shared listener. Grouping helps when one output batch concentrates in few HTTP workers, which is what the default listener produces; it does not itself fix connection imbalance.
1. This does not claim uniform latency improvement: median TTFT was `33.12 / 39.85 / 37.33 s` disabled versus `52.06 / 52.44 / 52.53 s` enabled; median E2EL was `86.02 / 92.89 / 89.93 s` versus `104.96 / 105.27 / 105.31 s`. Remaining HTTP-worker ownership imbalance and long tails are outside this patch.

# Validation and unit-test benefit

The unit tests demonstrate send-count reduction at the component level, not a timed performance speedup: the noncontiguous three-request/two-owner case produces two sends instead of three; the two-request/same-owner case produces one send instead of two. When every request has a different owner, the send count and per-request payloads remain unchanged. No standalone CPU microbenchmark or unit-test throughput gain was measured.

They also provide regression protection for the correctness and failure-boundary properties that make the optimization safe to enable:

1. They verify noncontiguous owner grouping preserves first-destination order, per-destination request order, and the original `http_worker_ipc` ownership.
1. They verify current string and token-ID message classes are grouped correctly, and that an embedding batch falls back to the per-request path (the shared splitter only covers `BatchTokenIDOutput`/`BatchStrOutput`), including optional wire fields through both pickle and msgpack round trips.
1. They verify the input output object is not mutated, unique-owner batches preserve the original per-request payload behavior, and outputs from separate messages are never accumulated together.
1. They verify `_CannotSplitBatch` falls back for the whole output before any grouped send, while a send error propagates without resending an earlier successful payload.
1. They verify the default-off behavior and the event-loop switch behavior.

Tests run separately in their own CPU Python processes:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_multi_tokenizer_mixin.py -q
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_msgpack_ipc_roundtrip.py -q
```

1. The return-path component tests and the existing IPC serialization tests pass, run separately in their own CPU Python processes. (The local CPU environment is Python 3.10 / torch 2.5.1, which cannot import current `main`; the suite is re-run in CI.)
1. Repository-selected Ruff checks (`F401,F821,F823,UP037`) plus `F811`, Ruff formatting, isort and `git diff --check` passed.

Added coverage checks noncontiguous owner grouping and ordering, unique-owner equivalence with the original per-request path, no input mutation, no cross-message accumulation, latest optional fields through both pickle and msgpack, token-ID grouping with embedding fallback, default-off and enabled event-loop behavior, fallback after an earlier group has been constructed but before any send, and send errors without resending earlier results.

# Submission note

The Router dependency (#42238) is merged into main, so this commit rebases directly onto current `main`. The comparison base is `main` and the diff contains only the files listed under "Dependency and scope".

title: [Feat] simulator: Add baseline collection and ML latency predictor training tools
author: littlefatfat
body:
## Motivation

The simulator can load an ML step-latency predictor, but users also need a way to collect measurements from a real SGLang server and train a compatible model. This PR adds that workflow to the installable simulator package.

## Modifications

- Add `sglang-simulator-collect` under `sglang_simulator.tools.collect_baseline`. It reuses the simulator hook infrastructure to collect request traces and synchronized batch latency. `/start_profile` and `/stop_profile` control collection and export.
- Add `sglang-simulator-train` under `sglang_simulator.tools.train_ml_time_predictor`. It trains monotonic histogram gradient boosting models with squared-error or median-quantile loss, supports independent evaluation data, and saves bundles accepted by the existing ML predictor.
- Share the ordered 18-feature extraction between training and inference. Include usage guides and a small example step dataset in the package.
- Add one basic collection-flow test and one train/load/predict test to the existing CPU CI workflow.

The collector requires `--disable-overlap-schedule`. Device synchronization changes execution timing; the initial scope is ordinary text generation without speculative decoding or multimodal feature modeling.

## Accuracy Tests

- Repository pre-commit checks and explicit Ruff checks on all changed Python files.
- Built and installed the wheel; verified both CLI entry points, packaged documentation, example data, and bootstrap module.
- CPU compatibility suite: 11 passing tests across collection, training, runner, serving, cache accounting, and OFFLINE/BLOCKING behavior.
- Training on DSv4-Pro TP4 measurements: 3,650 training steps and 3,503 steps from an independent trace. Held-out step MAPE is **1.42%** for squared-error loss and **1.38%** for median-quantile loss.
- CPU simulation of all 1,932 requests in the independent trace, modeling TP4:

  | Loss | Held-out step MAPE | Mean TTFT relative error |
  | --- | ---: | ---: |
  | Squared error | 1.42% | -0.61% |
  | Median quantile | 1.38% | -0.89% |

  Request/token identities and aggregate cache-hit statistics match.

The real-data experiment uses L1 cache only, original trace arrival times, and one output token per request. These measurements validate prefill latency; they do not establish long-decode or general L2/L3 prediction accuracy. The example dataset demonstrates usage rather than production accuracy.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No inference speedup is claimed. Collection is opt-in and synchronizes the device around `Scheduler.run_batch` to measure latency.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with the repository's pre-commit checks.
- [x] Add tests to the existing simulator CPU CI workflow.
- [x] Document collection, training, installation, and limitations.
- [x] Provide latency-prediction accuracy results and describe profiling overhead.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

## Co-authors
- @RulinJuice
- @YunongBao
- @aaronwangyi0201

title: [Perf] [AMD] Qwen3.8: Enable fused GDN packing for ratio-3 heads
author: amd-nprotaso
body:
## Motivation

The change makes AMD use one fused packing kernel for this model’s QKVZ/BA outputs, replacing the separate copy-and-concatenate path. It changes how the tensors are prepared, while preserving their values.

## Modifications

This model has 16 key heads and 48 value heads, so its head ratio is 3. The patch adds that ratio to AMD’s supported list.

## Accuracy Tests
All four end-to-end performance runs completed 80 measured requests with zero errors or cancellations.

Full AgentX GSM8K accuracy evaluation of patch commit `ff27193485` passed the supplied InferenceX score validator: **97.50% strict-match and flexible-extract (1286/1319)**, against the default **90%** threshold.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Compared fresh `origin/main` at `bab9c81fea` against the same base plus this patch on one AMD Instinct MI355X, TP=1. Two unprofiled runs per revision, with a server restart between revisions and a cache flush plus 16 warmup requests before each 80-request measurement.

Workload: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4-PLEFP8, concurrency 8, approximately 1000 input tokens and exactly 1000 output tokens, seed 42, temperature 0, `ignore_eos=true`, NEXTN (3 steps / 4 draft tokens). Server-reported input lengths matched across all runs: mean 1000.1625, range 1000–1002. The synthetic content length was set to 948 to account for the chat template.

| Metric | Main (mean of two runs) | Patched (mean of two runs) | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Output throughput | 945.820 tokens/s | 970.162 tokens/s | +2.57% |
| Mean request latency | 8.457 s | 8.245 s | -2.51% |
| Mean TTFT | 297.821 ms | 283.724 ms | -4.73% |
| Mean time per output token | 8.167 ms | 7.969 ms | -2.43% |

Individual output throughput: main **945.50 / 946.14 tokens/s**; patched **967.19 / 973.13 tokens/s**.

Runtime: PyTorch `2.11.0+rocm10.0.0`, AITER `9539fd397005117c7b2387b55e469675edc76ce4`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`. The benchmark launcher retains simulated speculative acceptance length **2.32** and stream interval **50**. Results describe this configuration; the token-time metric is an average rather than token-by-token delivery timing. Runs were ordered main/main then patched/patched, so this is not a randomized multi-session study.

title: [Test] [AMD] diffusion: Expect CUDA-only fast paths to be off on ROCm in kernel tests
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## What

Follow-up to #40660. Update the remaining ROCm failures in `test_modulate.py` and `test_model_fast_paths.py` so they expect the CUDA-only fast paths to be off on ROCm. With this change the `nightly-test-1-gpu-kernel` job passes on ROCm.

## Why

Both files are in `nightly-amd-kernel-1-gpu`. After #40660, `test_modulate.py` still had 104 failing cases on ROCm and `test_model_fast_paths.py` had 5. Each one asserts a fast path that is off on ROCm, and in each case the output still matches eager:

- `can_use_modulate_scale_shift_cuda` and `can_use_residual_gate_add_cuda` return False under HIP, and `try_fused_scaled_residual_add_exact` returns None off CUDA.
- `Timesteps.forward` only uses the JIT `timestep_embedding` on CUDA and uses diffusers' implementation otherwise. On HIP the JIT kernel doesn't build.
- The Qwen VAE fused cat+pad and the Qwen-Image 2.1 fused Q/K norm and LayerNorm modulation are gated on `is_cuda()`. The Hunyuan QK norm needs FlashInfer CuTe. On HIP, the ERNIE fused QKNorm+RoPE JIT kernel fails to build, so its gate disables itself and the call falls back to eager.

Changes on ROCm:
- `test_modulate.py`: `test_modulate_scale_shift_matches_eager`, `test_modulate_scale_shift_accepts_adaln_chunk_views` and `test_residual_gate_add_batched_rows` assert that the fast path is rejected and that the public wrapper still matches eager. `test_residual_gate_add_batched_rows_cuda_graph`, `test_scaled_residual_add_is_bit_exact` and `test_timestep_embedding_matches_diffusers` call the CUDA kernel directly and are skipped.
- `test_model_fast_paths.py`: the five cases that assert the fused path engaged are skipped. This follows the file's existing convention (`requires_inline_ptx`): the eager fallback stays covered by the neighboring tests, such as `test_ernie_qknorm_rope_first_attempt_exception_uses_pristine_inputs` and `test_hunyuan_quality_qknorm_stays_unmounted_without_cute_kernel`.

NVIDIA behavior is unchanged. The two modulate tests now also check the public `modulate_scale_shift` wrapper on NVIDIA.

## Test plan

ROCm, MI300, rocm10, at `ceeda9922a`: [nightly-test-1-gpu-kernel](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38597193680/job/115966863434) passes, 19/19 files.
- `test_modulate.py`: 84 passed, 97 skipped (104 failing on main).
- `test_model_fast_paths.py`: 37 passed, 53 skipped (5 failing on main).

Not run on NVIDIA.

author: EricKing626
body: ## Motivation This PR enables `--dcp-size > 1` for the RoPE DSA models on the `triton` DSA backends, which is the path ROCm runs. Previous work [#43735](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43735) brought DCP to these models on the `trtllm` backends; this builds on that work and supplies the pieces the triton path additionally needs: - The triton sparse-MLA kernel now returns its LSE(Log-Sum-Exp), so the per-rank partials can be merged. - The HIP FP8 KV cache now works under DCP: writes land on the row the reader looks up. - Fixes the GPU memory access fault the ROCm DSA MTP draft hit under DCP, by putting the draft on the target's sharding and addressing rule. ## Correctness MI355X, `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`, TP4/EP4, FP8 KV, MTP (EAGLE, 5 steps, 6 draft tokens), real draft acceptance. | check | no DCP | PR after; DCP=4 | |---|---|---| | passkey 8K / 34K / 96K | 3/3 | 3/3 | | GSM8K (400 questions, few-shot) | 0.953 | 0.953 | | MTP accept length (4 prompts x 400 tokens, greedy) | 3.11 | 3.47 | | KV capacity (tokens) | 2.83M | 8.81M (2.20M rows per rank x 4) | The FP8 write kernel test passes with 4 simulated ranks, and the triton LSE matches at the kernel level. ## Performance InferenceX agentic replay on this head, TP4/EP4 + DCP4 with MTP (simulated AL 3.61), 1 h per point. All four points finish with no GPU fault. The TP4 rows without DCP but with HiCache are for reference only. Table baseline: 10/19/2026 commit: 33dd8f6a2e TP4 + DCP4: 10/28/2026 commit: b8a0a1ac70 | Conc | Config | P90 Interactivity (tok/s/user) | TPUT per Chip (tok/s/GPU) | Chip Cache Hit Rate | CPU Cache Hit Rate | Theoretical Cache Hit Rate | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 16 | TP4 | **53.07** | **17,396** | 71.1% | 22.7% | 97.0% | | 16 | TP4 + DCP4 | 41.19 | 17,196 | 96.7% | — | 97.0% | | 24 | TP4 | 14.07 | 10,872 | 18.6% | 57.5% | 96.2% | | 24 | TP4 + DCP4 | **31.32** | **23,416** | 96.8% | — | 97.3% | | 40 | TP4 | 7.19 | 5,144 | 31.2% | 0.9% | — | | 40 | TP4 + DCP4 | **16.79** | **24,740** | 95.5% | — | 97.0% | | 48 | TP4 | **6.30** | 4,781 | 27.3% | 0.9% | — | | 48 | TP4 + DCP4 | 2.56 | **10,774** | 82.6% | — | 96.1% | - At c24 and c40, DCP4 keeps almost the whole working set in HBM (chip hit rate 95–97%): throughput per GPU is 2.2x and 4.8x the baseline, and P90 interactivity is 2.2x and 2.3x. - At c16 the baseline still fits most of its working set in HBM plus host memory, so DCP4 brings no gain: throughput per GPU is on par (0.99x), and P90 interactivity is 0.78x. - At c48 the DCP4 pool fills up (chip hit rate 83%) and DCP rejects HiCache, so evicted prefixes are recomputed: throughput per GPU stays 2.3x the baseline, but P90 interactivity falls to 0.41x of it. ## Modifications Correctness: - **`DSA DCP on the triton sparse-MLA backend`** 811248c80b - The triton sparse-MLA decode now returns an LSE, which DCP needs to merge each rank's partial result — letting decode, target verify and paged extend reuse upstream's DCP path. - **`Shard the DSA FP8 latent KV write under DCP`** fa4f2fc48f - The FP8 quant write only writes `slot % dcp_size == dcp_rank`, at row `slot // dcp_size`, the same rule as the BF16 write. - **`Shard the DSA MTP draft KV like the target under DCP`** 20107f85b8 - Fixed GPU memory access fault on DSA EAGLE/NEXTN draft. Puts the ROCm DSA draft on the target's allocator page and owner rule, with extend on the owned-slot path. Performance: - **`Bound the triton DCP sparse-MLA scan by the owned top-k count`** 171e960082 - `localize_dcp_page_table` already returns the per-row owned count, but the triton path dropped it and scanned all top-k slots, masking about (W-1)/W of them. The kernels now stop after the owned tiles. - **`Split DSA prefill indexer rows across the DCP group`** d7f9605feb - DCP now splits the rows evenly across ranks instead of computing the same top-k `W` times. The results are all-gathered directly into the destination buffer when possible. - **`Gather the DSA DCP Q in the FP8 KV dtype`** b8a0a1ac70 - Halves the Q traffic between DCP ranks with no change in results, because the kernel converted Q to that same format on arrival anyway. Scope: Without DCP nothing changes: the new arguments default to the old behavior. CUDA is untouched; the draft sharding is gated on `is_hip()`. On ROCm, pass `--dsa-prefill-backend triton --dsa-decode-backend triton`, because #43735 defaults to `trtllm` when they are unset. ## Known issues - DCP rejects HiCache, so once the DCP pool is full (c48 above), evicted prefixes are recomputed rather than reloaded from host. HiCache under DCP is a #43735 fast follow. - Add feature to enable DCP+HiCache at #45205 ## Checklist - [x] `pre-commit` - [x] Kernel tests (FP8 write, triton LSE) - [x] GLM-5.2 DCP4 end-to-end sanity (math, passkey up to 379K) - [x] GSM8K, DCP4 vs. no DCP - [x] Agentic replay at c16 / c24 / c40 / c48 - [x] Unit tests in repo --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #40516763996](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40516763996) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #40516763980](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40516763980) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #40516764530](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40516764530)

title: [Feat] diffusion: Add support for the MOSS-Image family
author: CloudRipple
body:
## Motivation

Add native text-to-image inference for `OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base`, including the latest DiT weights and small FLUX.2 decoder. Load its Diffusers component export through SGLang's standard component loaders and run the model through the native diffusion runtime.

## Modifications

- Register `OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base` and `OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-SFT` identifiers. End-to-end checkpoint evidence below covers Base only; SFT is name registration only until its weights are updated and validated.
- Expose `uncond_skip_layers` and `slg_*` through model-owned sampling fields and the existing Images API whitelist. DiT `skip_layers` is an internal forward argument.
- Register the pipeline, DiT, Qwen3.5 text encoder, training V2 nearest-grid Euler scheduler and sampling configuration. Keep flow shift 5, BF16 DiT/text encoder and FP32 VAE.
- Support ordinary CFG, two-pass skipped-unconditional guidance and three-pass additional skipped-conditional guidance. Defaults: CFG 3, layer 22 unconditional skipping, window 0.01–1.0. Ordinary CFG uses `uncond_skip_layers=[]`; three-pass uses CFG 5, `slg_layers=[22]`, `slg_scale=3`.
- Sampling defaults intentionally retain the recommended recipe used here: `slg_start=0.01` leaves the first denoising step at full CFG, and selecting three-pass SLG without an explicit `uncond_skip_layers` uses a complete unconditional branch so the extra skipped-conditional term is evaluated independently. The official pipeline at the tested revision defaults to `slg_start=0.0` and keeps unconditional skipping enabled even with three-pass SLG. Set `slg_start=0.0, uncond_skip_layers=[22]` explicitly to request that official behavior.
- Add exact DiT activation/normalization/RoPE fusion with numerical gates and eager fallback; precompute step-invariant conditioning and reuse the framework text-conditioning cache.
- Declare component residency and support DiT/text-encoder layerwise offload through existing managers. Reuse shared FLUX.2 VAE decoding helpers; LLaDA-Image only changes its helper import. The existing native VAE already accepts decoder channels 96/192/384/384 from the updated checkpoint.

## Accuracy Tests

**Numerical parity: with cuDNN SDPA disabled in both processes, the official reference and SGLang Torch SDPA produce identical float RGB (maximum absolute error 0) for all three guidance recipes.** An independent repeat also confirms that each reference policy is reproducible across two fresh processes. This validates the tested Base diet-guide workload; default FA comparisons are reported separately below.

On the final commit, 171 tests passed across `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_moss_image.py` and `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_qwen3_5_encoder.py`. Pre-commit passes. Images API checks cover all three guidance recipes and a default request after three-pass; returned pixels match native offline output. The reproduction commands below were also run for all three recipes with both native default component backends and native Torch SDPA (six HTTP requests); all six outputs match the corresponding measured images. The new reference script reproduces all three controlled float-RGB outputs exactly. The displayed images, timing, offload and profile results were collected on an earlier revision with equivalent inference computation; the unit tests and API checks were rerun on the final commit. Component, DiT-only, text-encoder-only and combined layerwise offload preserve the resident float RGB output with `quality=exact`.

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_moss_image.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_qwen3_5_encoder.py
```

The reference is the unmodified `pipeline_moss_image.py` bundled at Base revision 355120bd6b44ff67b8df18f57e40b928fc886cd3, using Diffusers 0.38.0 for its small decoder. Native SGLang uses Diffusers 0.37.0 for configuration utilities and its own model/VAE implementation. PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 and Transformers 5.19.0 are shared. All guidance arguments are explicit: the comparison uses slg_start=0.01, and three-pass reference calls set uncond_skip_layers=[] to keep the unconditional branch complete. These override the new reference's start=0 and unconditional-skip defaults.

Main images show the reference's original SDPA policy (cuDNN allowed), native Torch SDPA (framework cuDNN policy disabled), and native default FA. The main table therefore reports actual backend differences. A separate controlled lane disables cuDNN SDPA in the reference; all three guidance outputs are float-RGB identical to native SDPA, with matching branch order and layer 22 execution counts. SSIM uses float RGB in [0,1], a 7×7 local window, sample covariance and channel averaging; PSNR uses data_range=1. This single-prompt/seed agreement check is not a semantic-quality or GenEval benchmark. `quality=exact` does not imply equality across attention backends. Over 50 denoising steps, small floating-point differences between attention kernels can accumulate into composition changes; three-pass guidance can amplify them further. The matched-SDPA result isolates port correctness from those backend differences. The default request quality is `lossless`; these measurements explicitly use `exact`. MOSS-Image DiT fusions use bit-exact gates at either level, but the shared FLUX.2 VAE has additional quality-gated fast paths enabled at `lossless`, so the two end-to-end paths must not be treated as identical. No default-lossless pixel-parity result is claimed here.

| Native backend | SSIM vs reference default policy | PSNR (dB) |
|---|---|---|
| Torch SDPA, cuDNN disabled | 0.80671 | 20.37 |
| Default FA | 0.81201 | 20.87 |

![Diet guide: reference, native SDPA, native FA](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5940cdd8-b1c7-45cc-8dbc-e61764669854)

| Guidance | Controlled SDPA float RGB | FA vs controlled reference SSIM | PSNR (dB) | DiT calls / layer 22 calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| recommended | Identical | 0.79524 | 19.78 | 100 / 51 |
| ordinary | Identical | 0.86967 | 21.98 | 100 / 100 |
| three_pass | Identical | 0.52907 | 14.43 | 149 / 100 |

Controlled comparisons: [recommended two-pass](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6efd0588-ac48-4b89-98e7-46af04d52bcc), [ordinary CFG](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9757c70-5b4e-4b10-87ad-bf88571c7405), [three-pass SLG](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc0edda7-a71f-4c02-b62e-722467eaace1).

### Reproduction

Use this PR's checkout with its diffusion dependencies installed. Native validation used PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0 and Diffusers 0.37.0. Run on one otherwise idle H200; the resident configuration needs approximately 33 GiB of GPU memory.

```bash
sglang serve --model-path OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base \
  --revision 355120bd6b44ff67b8df18f57e40b928fc886cd3 \
  --backend sglang --num-gpus 1 \
  --disable-autocast true --warmup-mode off --performance-mode manual \
  --component-residency all=resident \
  --served-model-name OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000
```

Leave `--attention-backend` unset for the displayed default-attention results: on the tested H200 this selects `text_encoder: torch_sdpa` and `transformer: fa`. Setting it globally to `fa` also changes the text encoder and does not reproduce these images. Confirm these component choices in the startup log. For the matched-SDPA accuracy lane, restart with `--attention-backend torch_sdpa`; both components should then log `torch_sdpa`. Keep `quality=exact` and use the cuDNN-disabled reference below.


</details>

Create the three request files:

```bash
python - <<'PY'
import json
from pathlib import Path

base = json.loads(Path("moss-request.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
recipes = {
    "recommended": dict(guidance_scale=3.0, uncond_skip_layers=[22],
                        slg_start=0.01, slg_stop=1.0),
    "ordinary": dict(guidance_scale=3.0, uncond_skip_layers=[],
                     slg_start=0.01, slg_stop=1.0),
    "three_pass": dict(guidance_scale=5.0, uncond_skip_layers=[],
                       slg_layers=[22], slg_scale=3.0,
                       slg_start=0.01, slg_stop=1.0),
}
for name, overrides in recipes.items():
    Path(f"{name}.json").write_text(json.dumps(base | overrides, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
PY
```

Send each recipe and decode its PNG (requires `curl` and `jq`):

```bash
for mode in recommended ordinary three_pass; do
  curl --fail-with-body http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/images/generations \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data-binary "@${mode}.json" -o "${mode}-response.json"
  jq -r '.data[0].b64_json' "${mode}-response.json" | base64 --decode > "${mode}.png"
done
```

Omitting all guidance fields selects the recommended two-pass defaults. Repeat `recommended.json` to exercise conditioning-cache reuse. Restart with `--disable-conditioning-cache` to disable it. These commands reproduce serving behavior and images; HTTP/client elapsed time includes serialization and transport and is not the pipeline-only latency reported below.


<details>
<summary>Reference pipeline: reproduce all three recipes</summary>

Use a separate environment with Diffusers **0.38.0**, PyTorch **2.14.1+cu130** and Transformers **5.19.0**, plus `huggingface_hub`, NumPy and Pillow. The tested reference uses Transformers' PyTorch fallbacks for causal convolution and gated delta attention (`causal_conv1d` and `flash-linear-attention` are not installed). Installing either package may change the reference's numerics; use the same dependency versions and keep both packages absent when reproducing the bit-exact result. Run from the directory containing the three request JSON files above. Save this as `moss_reference.py`; it loads the pinned checkpoint's own pipeline code and does not import SGLang.

```python
import argparse
import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys

import numpy as np
import torch
from diffusers import AutoencoderKLFlux2
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
from PIL import Image
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--cudnn", choices=("enabled", "disabled"), default="disabled")
parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=Path("reference-sdpa"))
args = parser.parse_args()
args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
# Run in a separate process that has not imported SGLang.
torch.backends.cuda.enable_cudnn_sdp(args.cudnn == "enabled")
model = Path(snapshot_download(
    "OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base",
    revision="355120bd6b44ff67b8df18f57e40b928fc886cd3",
))
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    "reference_moss_image", model / "pipeline_moss_image.py"
)
module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
sys.modules[spec.name] = module
spec.loader.exec_module(module)
transformer = module.MOSSImageTransformer.from_pretrained(
    str(model / "transformer"), torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16
).eval()
encoder = AutoModel.from_pretrained(
    str(model / "text_encoder"), dtype=torch.bfloat16, attn_implementation="sdpa"
).eval()
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(str(model / "tokenizer"))
vae = AutoencoderKLFlux2.from_pretrained(
    str(model / "vae"), torch_dtype=torch.float32
).eval()
scheduler = module.MOSSImageScheduler.from_config(
    json.loads((model / "scheduler/scheduler_config.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")),
    shift=5.0,
)
pipe = module.MOSSImagePipeline(transformer, scheduler, encoder, tokenizer, vae).to("cuda")
for name in ("recommended", "ordinary", "three_pass"):
    req = json.loads(Path(f"{name}.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    width, height = map(int, req["size"].split("x"))
    guidance = {key: req[key] for key in (
        "guidance_scale", "uncond_skip_layers", "slg_layers", "slg_scale",
        "slg_start", "slg_stop",
    ) if key in req}
    rgb = pipe(
        req["prompt"], width=width, height=height,
        negative_prompt=req["negative_prompt"],
        num_inference_steps=req["num_inference_steps"],
        generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(req["seed"]),
        output_type="np", **guidance,
    ).images
    np.save(args.output / f"{name}.npy", rgb)
    # Match the Images API's uint8 truncation when comparing downloaded PNGs.
    Image.fromarray(np.clip(rgb[0] * 255, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(
        args.output / f"{name}.png"
    )
    print(name, "saved", flush=True)

```

```bash
# Matched-SDPA accuracy comparison (native server uses torch_sdpa).
python moss_reference.py --cudnn disabled --output reference-sdpa
# Reference's original attention policy for the main image comparison.
python moss_reference.py --cudnn enabled --output reference-default
```

The script saves original float RGB as `.npy` and PNGs using the same uint8 truncation as the Images API. With the native SDPA server, compare the downloaded PNGs:

```python
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

for name in ("recommended", "ordinary", "three_pass"):
    native = np.asarray(Image.open(f"{name}.png").convert("RGB"))
    reference = np.asarray(Image.open(Path("reference-sdpa") / f"{name}.png").convert("RGB"))
    assert np.array_equal(native, reference), name
```

PNG equality checks the public API export; the reported float-RGB identity was checked before uint8 conversion. The composed figures resize images for display and use rounded float RGB for PNG export, so compare the original pixels rather than the resized panel files.

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

One H200, batch 1, eager execution, quality=exact, autocast disabled, BF16 DiT/text encoder and FP32 VAE. Every displayed result uses the 1024×1024 diet-guide prompt, seed 0, 50 steps, empty negative prompt and flow shift 5. The timed recipe is CFG 3 with zero-indexed unconditional layer 22 skipped for 0.01 ≤ step_index / num_steps < 1.0. Each arm runs in a fresh process, one warmup followed by three measured calls; the table shows arithmetic means and sample standard deviations. CUDA-synchronized timing covers the complete pipeline through CPU float RGB, excluding load, PNG encoding/saving, HTTP and profiling. The cached arm reuses the exact same positive/negative prompt; it is not cold-prompt latency. The speed baseline uses the reference's default PyTorch SDPA policy with cuDNN enabled, its faster configuration on this GPU. SGLang leaves the global attention override unset, selecting FA for the DiT and Torch SDPA for the text encoder, with explicit `quality=exact`. The cuDNN-disabled reference is used only for numerical parity, not for the speedup calculation.

| Execution | Mean ± SD (s) | Min–max (s) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| Official reference | 20.832 ± 0.024 | 20.807–20.855 | 1.000× |
| SGLang, cache disabled | 11.459 ± 0.001 | 11.458–11.460 | 1.818× |
| SGLang, repeated prompt cached | 11.213 ± 0.031 | 11.179–11.240 | 1.858× |


| Execution | GPU kernel launches | Summed kernel time (ms) | Kernel busy union (ms) | DiT kernels (ms) | TE kernels (ms) | VAE kernels (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| reference | 352144 | 20239.6 | 20239.6 | 19987.2 | 165.6 | 85.8 |
| native_uncached | 77963 | 11232.3 | 11232.3 | 10973.1 | 166.4 | 89.0 |


Profiles are separate warmed single-request diagnostics; their wall times are excluded from the latency table. Component attribution follows CUDA launch correlation IDs into explicit CPU annotations. Summed kernel durations and GPU busy union are different quantities, and neither is an additive end-to-end speedup estimate. Both profile outputs match their respective unprofiled outputs. The dominant measured change is DiT kernel time and launch count; this whole-path comparison does not isolate the contribution of each fusion from conditioning precomputation or the attention backend.

| Residency | CUDA allocated (GiB) | CUDA reserved (GiB) | Process NVML (GiB) | Host PSS (GiB) | Host RSS (GiB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reference resident | 28.993 | 32.613 | 33.285 | 6.897 | 6.911 |
| SGLang resident | 28.170 | 31.770 | 32.990 | 12.570 | 12.588 |
| Component offload | 15.449 | 15.688 | 16.896 | 35.269 | 35.287 |
| DiT layerwise | 16.267 | 16.506 | 17.715 | 32.928 | 32.946 |
| TE layerwise | 10.160 | 10.588 | 11.799 | 32.231 | 32.250 |
| DiT + TE layerwise | 4.530 | 7.418 | 8.639 | 32.517 | 32.535 |


CUDA allocated/reserved values are maxima over measured requests; NVML and host PSS/RSS are sampled process peaks including loading. Reference telemetry covers initialization and the measured diet-guide requests. Component/DiT/TE rows each run one recommended request; combined layerwise runs recommended twice then three-pass. PSS accounts for shared pages proportionally; RSS includes them. Sampling can miss short peaks. Offload uses prefetch 1 and zero resident DiT/TE layers. DiT-only layerwise offload does not improve the whole-pipeline peak over component offload in this measurement; compare the TE and combined rows before choosing a policy. These H200 measurements do not establish physical 8 GB-card capacity.

Scope of the tables above: Base, single-H200 eager text-to-image, batch 1, the diet-guide prompt, seed 0 and 50 steps. SFT is registered by identifier only; no SFT checkpoint quality or speed claim is made. Multi-GPU checkpoint E2E, editing, LoRA, quantization, graph/compile, Cache-DiT and VAE slicing remain unvalidated. SP and CFG use shared runtime infrastructure and have two-process CPU/Gloo tests; those do not replace multi-GPU checkpoint E2E. Standard model GPU/performance baseline registration is deferred. Follow-up batching evidence is reported separately.

Website documentation now includes a MOSS-Image cookbook, command picker, model catalog and navigation entries. Hardware recipes without direct measurements are marked unverified.

title: [Fix] lora: Load fused-module members into their own buffer slots
author: yueming-yuan
body:
## Motivation

An adapter may target any subset of the members SGLang packs into one fused LoRA module: `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` -> `qkv_proj`, `gate_proj`/`up_proj` -> `gate_up_proj`, `q_a_proj`/`kv_a_proj_with_mqa` -> `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa`, Inkling `wq_du`/`wk_dv`/`wv_dv`/`wr_du` -> `qkvr`. The loader concatenated the members into the fused key at normalization time, assuming specific members are present. On Qwen3-0.6B with `sglang-miles`:

| adapter targets | before |
|---|---|
| q, o | `KeyError: ...self_attn.v_proj.lora_A.weight` |
| k, v | `ValueError: Cannot find target module name` |
| up, down | `ValueError: Cannot find target module name` |

A trainer could only work around this by exporting zero A/B pairs for untrained members, with widths computed from its own copy of the engine's layout.

## Modifications

Members are no longer concatenated in `LoRAAdapter`. The memory pool writes each member into its own slot of the fused buffer:

- A: member `i` goes to rows `[i*r, (i+1)*r)`; B: member `i` goes to the member's row range of the local output. Absent members are left zero, so the fused module computes exactly the partial adapter.
- The per-member geometry (full rows, TP-local offsets, TP slice incl. KV-head replication and MLA `first_output_dim`) comes from the `*WithLoRA` wrapper that already owns the fused layout: `lora_b_member_full_rows()`, `lora_b_member_local_offsets()`, `slice_lora_b_member()`. `slice_lora_b_weights` is rebuilt from the same methods, so there is one definition per wrapper. `packed_modules_mapping` is not used; it is absent on Llama/Qwen2/Qwen3 and does not match the LoRA modules on Qwen3.5 / NemotronH.
- `LORA_FUSED_MEMBERS` in `lora/utils.py` is the single member table; `params_mapping` and `stacked_rank` derive from it.
- An adapter that already carries the fused key (`qkv_proj`, `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa`, ...) is split by the same geometry; carrying both the fused and the per-member form is rejected.
- MoE (routed / shared expert) gate/up keep the existing stacked path.

Behavior: an adapter covering all members loads byte-identical buffers to the old concatenating loader (unit test, all TP ranks, `max_lora_rank` = r and r+1). Partial adapters that raised before now load. An MLA adapter with a fused `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` key is newly accepted.

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/lora/test_lora_fused_member_load.py` (CPU, 37 cases) on fake QKV / MergedColumn / Inkling qkvr / MLA wrappers:

- complete adapter == old concatenating loader (oracle copied from `sglang-miles@4076a68579`), every TP rank, `max_lora_rank` in {r, r+1}
- every member subset loads, absent members are zero
- fused-key adapters (shared and stacked A) match their per-member form; fused + per-member is rejected
- `LoRAAdapter` keeps dense members separate and still stacks expert gate/up

E2E on H200, Qwen3-0.6B, r=8: each adapter is compared against the same SGLang running the PEFT-merged weights (`merge_and_unload`). Mean |logprob diff|, rows = LoRA run, columns = merged model:

| | full | q_o | k_v | up_down |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| full | **0.046** | 0.610 | 0.545 | 0.650 |
| q_o | 0.613 | **0.038** | 0.212 | 0.243 |
| k_v | 0.543 | 0.226 | **0.045** | 0.236 |
| up_down | 0.649 | 0.258 | 0.241 | **0.037** |

The diagonal is bf16 rounding of the merged weights; every LoRA run matches only its own merged model. The full adapter's logprobs are identical (`==`) to `sglang-miles` before this change.

## Not in this PR

Fused modules whose members are not plain row blocks of B, and MoE gate/up, keep the current path: GDN `in_proj_qkvz` / `in_proj_ba`, Mamba `in_proj`, routed/shared-expert `gate_up_proj`.

## Consumer

radixark/miles#4101 drops the trainer-side zero-fill and exports only the trained members.

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] allreduce-fusion: Decline MNNVL fusion across NVLink cliques
author: wenscarl
body:
## Motivation

On a multi-node TP group whose GPUs are in different NVLink cliques (e.g. a SLURM job placed across topology blocks), MNNVL allreduce fusion fails at workspace creation with `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE`. SGLang then logs one warning and silently falls back to NCCL ring allreduce. On our TP8 (2 nodes x 4 GPUs) decode workload this raised the verify step from 8.756 ms to 31.975 ms (3.65x), and AllReduce from 14.3% to 72.6% of the step, with no error.

Root cause: the fabric-handle decision uses `is_mnnvl_fabric_supported(device)`, a per-GPU query that is True on every rank, while whether rank A can import rank B's fabric handle is a property of the group. The group-aware `is_one_nvlink_clique` already exists (used by custom-AR v2) but the fusion path never called it.

Evidence: NVML probe on two nodes in different NVLink blocks gives different `clusterUuid`, same `cliqueId` (65534), and `is_mnnvl_fabric_supported` True on both. TP8 jobs placed inside one block enable fusion normally (`backend=mnnvl, world_size=8`).

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py`, `FlashInferWorkspaceManager.initialize`:
- For `backend == "mnnvl"` and a group that spans nodes, run `is_one_nvlink_clique` once (all ranks reach it, result cached on the manager so re-creation does not issue a second collective). If False: set `_flashinfer_allreduce_unavailable`, warn with the topology reason, and return before any CUDA allocation. No POSIX-FD fallback (host-local handles cannot work across nodes).
- If `INVALID_HANDLE` is still hit on a cross-node group, the warning now carries a topology hint.
- The success log includes `one_nvlink_clique=...`.

`_make_flashinfer_workspace_allocation_prop` is intentionally untouched: it is only the memory-sizing preflight, not the path that throws.

## Behavior before / after

Same TP8 job (2 nodes x 4 GPUs) placed across two NVLink blocks.

**Before**
```
[TP0] [SymmDeviceMemory] Rank: 0, Group size: 8, device_idx: 0, Signal pad offset: 150994944
[TP0] Failed to initialize FlashInfer workspace (backend=mnnvl): CUDA error code=400(b'CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE'). Disabling flashinfer allreduce fusion permanently.
```
Only a raw CUDA code, no cause, raised after allocation started. The run then completes with no error on `ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_bf16_RING_LL`.

**After**
```
[TP0] FlashInfer AllReduce fusion disabled: the 8 ranks of this group span more than one NVLink clique, which the MNNVL backend does not support. On SLURM this usually means the job was placed across topology blocks; set --segment equal to --nodes.
```
Names the cause and the fix; no `SymmDeviceMemory` allocation and no `CUDA error code=400`. The NCCL fallback still happens, but is now visible and actionable.

**Same job inside one NVLink block (unchanged behavior, one new field)**
```
FlashInfer AllReduce Fusion enabled and workspace initialized: backend=mnnvl, rank=0, world_size=8, one_nvlink_clique=True, max_token_num=..., hidden_dim=...
```

The "before" log is from a production run; the "after" text is the new warning string, covered by `test_declines_when_not_one_clique`. A real cross-block cluster run is not included.

## Accuracy / Tests

Unit tests in `test/registered/unit/layers/test_flashinfer_comm_fusion.py` (`TestMnnvlCliqueGate`): declines without creating a workspace and warns "NVLink clique"; proceeds when one clique; clique collective runs exactly once across a re-create. `pytest test/registered/unit/layers/test_flashinfer_comm_fusion.py`: 24 passed.

This PR is irrelevant to any compute/accuracy.

title: [CI] python: Move the remaining CUDA build paths off Python 3.10
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

#43021 raised sglang to Python >=3.11 but left the CUDA `sglang-kernel` wheel (`cp310-abi3`) and several CI and release jobs on 3.10. This PR moves the remaining CUDA and hardware-neutral paths off 3.10. Other hardware platforms are out of scope.

## Modifications

- **`sglang-kernel` (CUDA):** `requires-python >=3.11` and `wheel.py-api = "cp311"`, so the wheel is `cp311-abi3`. The PR build, release build and build Dockerfile use Python 3.11. The artifact `wheel-python3.10-cuda*` is renamed `wheel-python3.11-cuda*` in every consumer, and `ci_install_dependency.sh` matches `cp311-abi3`.
- **ROCm kernel wheels stay `cp310-abi3`:** `build_rocm.sh` builds from the CUDA `pyproject.toml`, so it now sets `>=3.10` / `cp310` back before building (the result is byte-identical to main), then runs `pip install --dry-run` on the image's Python so an uninstallable wheel fails the job.
- **cuda-tile:** the `==1.6.0rc5` pin from #34321 (rc6 lacked cp310 wheels) is dropped. rc5 is a stub sdist that downloads its wheel at install time; 1.6.0 ships real wheels for cp310–cp314, and `flashinfer-python==0.7.1` now resolves to it.
- **DeepEP:** release matrix and `build_sgl_deepep.sh` drop 3.10.
- **Workflows on 3.12:** coverage, multimodal-gen, diffusion GT gen, release-pypi index steps, bot-bump, runner utilization, slash commands, est-time update. The bot-bump jobs no longer install `tomli`; the release scripts import `tomllib` directly.

**Unchanged:** ROCm, MUSA, NPU, XPU and MLU, `pyproject_other.toml`, and the shared runtime's 3.10 compatibility code, since those platforms still install sglang on 3.10.

**Notes:** the first kernel build starts with a cold buildx cache (the cache tag includes the Python tag). `diffusion-ci-gt-gen`'s `kernel_wheel_run_id` only accepts runs made after this change.

## Verification

- scikit-build-core 1.1.1: `py-api cp311` gives `cp311-abi3` on 3.11/3.12 and silently falls back to `cp310-cp310` on 3.10, which the CI install's `cp311-abi3` match catches.
- The `pip --dry-run` check rejects both bad ROCm wheels on 3.10 and accepts `cp310-abi3` on 3.10 and 3.12.
- pre-commit, `bash -n`, YAML load, and `scripts/release/test_utils.py` (14 passed) all pass.
- Not run: a full CUDA or ROCm kernel build. Run `release-whl-kernel.yml` with `target: rocm720` for ROCm; this PR's CI covers CUDA.

## Accuracy Tests

No model forward or kernel source changes.

title: [Feat] [CPU] cpu-graph: Add prefill torch compile graph and dynamic graph support
author: CaoE
body:
## Motivation

Ported from the internal implementation.

Add CPU torch.compile graph support for both prefill and decode on Intel AMX systems, including static bucket graphs and optional dynamic-shape fallback graphs.

The implementation supports:

- Static prefill graphs using total-token buckets.
- Optional dynamic fallback graphs through `SGLANG_TORCH_DYNAMIC_SHAPE=true`.
- Exact buckets first, padded buckets second, and dynamic fallback last.

CPU prefill graphs are experimental and remain disabled by default; they must be explicitly enabled with the `full` backend.

## Modifications

- Extend `CPUGraphRunner` with CPU prefill graph capture and replay.
- Add static and dynamic graph support for both decode and prefill.
- Add prefill padding and hidden-state trimming.
- Define CPU decode configuration precedence:
  `decode.bs` > `decode.max_bs` > `--torch-compile-max-bs`.
- Generate prefill buckets from `prefill.max_bs` when needed.
- Reject unsupported CPU graph backends such as `breakable` and `tc_piecewise`.
- Add a stable prefill forward dispatcher to avoid unnecessary recompilation.
- Make layer-boundary objects compatible with TorchDynamo during CPU graph capture and replay.
- Fix graph breaks, runtime recompiles, and `InternalTorchDynamoError` failures related to `msgspec.Struct` objects and
  Python-side CPU capability checks.
- Update required CPU custom-op schemas, fake registrations, rotary embedding handling, and related kernels.
- Update CPU graph documentation and tests.

## Tests

- Cover backend gating, bucket generation, option precedence, padding, dispatcher stability, dynamic fallback, and encoder-decoder decode graph reuse.
- Reuse the existing real-model benchmark and MMLU test while enabling explicit CPU prefill graphs and dynamic-shape fallback.
- Verify graph and eager accuracy and graph execution without graph breaks or runtime recompiles.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen3.5-35B (BF16, TP4) Prefill graph:  ~6% TTFT Speedup (BS=1, Input=1024).
