title: [Perf] DSv4.1: Enable decoder bounded replay by default
author: Oasis-Git
body:
[codex/claude generated]

## Motivation

Enable decoder SWA bounded replay by default for supported standalone CUDA DeepSeek-V4.1 configurations, while preserving an explicit full-prefill opt-out. In our paired accuracy runs, AIME 2026 without an explicit output cap was identical (469/480 each); DeepSWE differed by one solved task and MMMU-Pro by five correct responses. These are finite, stochastic accuracy measurements, not proof of numerical equivalence or a universal speedup.

## Modifications

- Enable decoder replay by default on CUDA DSv4.1 unless `disable_decoder_bounded_replay` is set for eager/breakable prefill, with the existing DP-attention compatibility checks. Keep PD, context parallelism, encoder replay, other platforms, and incompatible configurations out of automatic enablement.
- Preserve explicit `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay`; add `--disable-decoder-bounded-replay` to retain full prefill, including prompt-logprob support. Bounded replay remains numerically different from full prefill and does not support prompt logprobs.
- Include the candidate-table capacity fix needed for speculative verification beyond the 1,048,576-token boundary. Select the existing 16 KiB or expanded 32 KiB bitmap according to page-table capacity; reject unsupported capacities above 2M tokens. This fixes a shared indexer issue, not a replay-only failure, and does not enlarge the model context limit.
- Add default-resolution/CLI coverage and eager/CUDA-graph sorter boundary regressions; update the model cookbook and CLI help.

Base: upstream main `9d68ecce2e811d908551d58a2a8792c75245d181`. Main already includes breakable-prefill replay support; this PR does not reapply the historical #43440 patch wholesale.

## Accuracy Tests

### Completed benchmark results

Each arm used one 4×GB300 node and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, checkpoint `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`. Replay off/on was the intended server-setting difference. TP=4, EP=4, attention DP=1, DSPARK block size=5, FlashMLA, static memory fraction=0.8, max running requests=64, decode graph max batch=64, breakable prefill max tokens=4096, prefill graph max sequence length=16384, chunked prefill=16384, and server random seed=0 were shared.

| Workload | Samples per arm | Replay off | Replay on | Truncations off / on | Harness/request errors off / on |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSWE | 113 tasks, one attempt | 78/113 = 69.03% resolved | 77/113 = 68.14% resolved | Not aggregated by this harness | 0 / 0 |
| AIME 2026, initial 32,768-token cap | 30 questions × 16 = 480 | 453/480 = 94.38% | 447/480 = 93.13% | 25 / 31 | 0 / 0 |
| AIME 2026, no explicit output cap | 30 questions × 16 = 480 | 469/480 = 97.71% | 469/480 = 97.71% | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| MMMU-Pro standard (10 options), repaired runs | 1,730 questions × 1 | 1,152/1,730 = 66.59% | 1,147/1,730 = 66.30% | 18 / 28 | 0 / 0 |

AIME majority@16 was 96.67% for both capped runs and 100% for both uncapped runs. The capped results are included for completeness; the uncapped rerun removes the artificial 32K cutoff. Its largest observed outputs were 120,168 tokens off and 107,673 on.

DeepSWE used deep-swe `0b9fabbb63b9104d678fe965e1632f2dd9eaa2ea`, Pier `4d3c14041d16443f3f9f460dcdf23629994a304e`, mini-swe-agent 2.4.6, Docker task environments, four concurrent trials per arm, temperature=1, top_p=.95, max_tokens=32768, seed=0, and reasoning effort high. No sgl-eval changes were involved in that agent harness.

AIME/MMMU used unmodified sgl-eval 0.1.2 at `93bc2d851a59e57d54fe755202756589a04d3d86`: concurrency=16, temperature=1, top_p=.95, thinking enabled, reasoning effort high, no per-request seed. MMMU used the existing image loader, prompt and MCQ grader for `MMMU/MMMU_Pro`, configuration `standard (10 options)`, test split. This is `mmmu_pro`, not `mmmu_pro_vision` or `mmlu_pro`.

Example full MMMU command (use separate output directories and endpoints per arm):

```bash
sgl-eval run mmmu_pro \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:31000/v1 \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --n-repeats 1 --num-threads 16 \
  --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 \
  --thinking --reasoning-effort high \
  --out-dir results
```

A one-image smoke evaluation (`--num-examples 1`) passed on each arm before the full run. Full MMMU artifacts were checked for 1,730 distinct matching IDs, matching question text/expected answers and generation settings, zero exit codes, and recomputed accuracy/finish-reason counts. Saved server configurations differ only in replay selection after excluding runtime metadata. The installed repaired kernel hashes match. The loader did not pin the Hugging Face dataset revision; final prediction files do not contain image bytes for independent byte equality checks.

### Revision scope and the original MMMU failure

These full benchmark runs predate the PR base above. DeepSWE/AIME ran on main `b60444c62169c7992b98f102cbc4e86d9d117294` plus #43440 head `729c1584e597c915f6dbb6207b89e90a09fcef33`, integrated locally as `b273c67e75a70c1971eb7715910d15c148136883`. Repaired MMMU added local fix `6dc4fa29df069c92668de2fc5ed7766dd49e378b`, transplanted in this PR. The full benchmarks have not been rerun on the new main/default-selection patch.

Both original MMMU arms crashed at the context boundary with `logical_page_idx < block_table_stride`. A minimal sorter reproducer passed at 1M tokens but lost the newest candidate at 1M+1, returning `INT32_MAX`. Original interrupted scores are invalid and excluded from the accuracy table. Both arms were rerun fresh with the same fix; both completed without request errors.

Omitting max_tokens still permits context-limit truncation. Repaired MMMU reached maximum generated lengths of 1,048,271 off and 1,048,285 on. The remaining truncations reflect length stopping, not a recurrence of the server crash.

Historical fix validation also included six sparse-indexer tests, sorter boundaries at 1,048,575 / 1,048,576 / 1,048,577 / 1,048,586 / 2,097,152 tokens in eager and captured execution, and an end-to-end DSPARK request with 1,048,544 input tokens plus 30 output tokens followed by a healthy server. The text-only boundary reproducer shows that images are not necessary to trigger this bug.

### Validation on the new PR base

- Seven default-resolution and CLI tests passed against the updated source on a GB300 node, including the disable flag and conflicting-flag rejection.
- The candidate boundary regression passed: five lengths × eager/captured execution (ten subcases).
- Six existing sparse-prefill indexer tests passed against the new source on GB300.
- Scoped pre-commit checks passed, including formatting, AST checks, and registered-test validation.

These ran in isolated test processes with the new source; the benchmark servers were not restarted. Full workload reruns, a complete documentation-site build, and upstream CI are not claimed here. Recommended CI covers the new server-argument test, encoder/decoder replay row tests, candidate boundary and sparse-indexer tests, and the GB300 DSv4.1 E2E. The current B300 PD+CP E2E is disabled upstream.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

| Workload | Replay off evaluation time | Replay on evaluation time |
|---|---:|---:|
| AIME 2026, 32K cap | 876.22 s | 869.16 s |
| AIME 2026, no explicit cap | 1,064.43 s | 1,037.55 s |
| MMMU-Pro, repaired | 7,291.75 s | 8,635.92 s |

DeepSWE took approximately 6h 5m per arm, including agent tool execution and task grading. These are end-to-end workload durations, not isolated prefill latency measurements.

MMMU generated 31,363,333 completion tokens off versus 42,100,497 on. Aggregate output rates were 4,301 versus 4,875 tokens/s, but different output lengths, reasoning loops, and batch occupancy prevent treating that ratio as a controlled replay speedup. The controlled fixed-token comparison below measures speed separately from these accuracy workloads. Single stochastic runs also do not establish statistical equivalence of accuracy.

Recorded runtime: PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, sgl-kernel 0.4.9, FlashInfer/cubin 0.7.1, FlashInfer JIT cache 0.7.1+cu130; Python UnifiedTreeCore fallback on both arms.

### Controlled fixed-token comparison on 4×GB300

Measured October 16, 2026 on the same node, sequentially replay off then on. Identical deterministic synthetic token-ID prompts, temperature=0, `ignore_eos=true`, exact output lengths, and three repetitions per case. Shape-specific warmup and server startup are excluded; the radix cache was flushed before each repetition. All 348 measured requests per arm passed exact prompt/output-length checks with zero cached tokens.

Both arms used DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4/EP4, attention DP=1, FlashMLA, DSPARK block size 5, breakable prefill, 16,384-token chunks, and a 16,384-token prefill graph context limit. Encoder replay was disabled. Effective server settings matched apart from decoder replay and runtime metadata.

**Single-request time to first token**, with one output token and five requests per repetition. Values are medians of the three per-repetition medians; speedup = off/on. This is client-observed first-token latency, not GPU-kernel-only time.

| Input tokens | Replay off TTFT | Replay on TTFT | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,024 | 42.89 ms | 42.92 ms | 0.999× |
| 8,192 | 174.50 ms | 172.54 ms | 1.011× |
| 32,768 | 480.92 ms | 346.89 ms | 1.386× |
| 65,536 | 974.77 ms | 700.62 ms | 1.391× |

**End-to-end output throughput**, with concurrency 16, 32 requests per repetition, and exactly 128 output tokens per request. Values are median repetition throughput; speedup = on/off.

| Input tokens | Replay off output tokens/s | Replay on output tokens/s | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,024 | 2054.97 | 2107.11 | 1.025× |
| 8,192 | 792.69 | 885.98 | 1.118× |
| 32,768 | 256.38 | 337.22 | 1.315× |

Long-prompt first-token latency improved by approximately **1.39× (28% lower latency)** at 32K/64K input; 32K concurrent throughput improved **1.315×**. Short single-request latency was essentially unchanged. Concurrent TTFT did not improve uniformly: at 1K input it was 163 ms off versus 184 ms on.

**Revision and interpretation limits:** these measurements use the retained repaired accuracy-test runtime, not a fresh checkout of current main or this PR head. The installed package reports `0.0.0.dev1+g67eab5705`; that build-version string alone does not identify later local patches. The candidate-table header SHA-256 matches the repaired benchmark (`d7088c2ac6c282ef2ae42cadcf527b21c36b165501add4d449b1c596bbbd16a2`). Synthetic token IDs control input shape but do not represent natural-language quality or every production workload. DSPARK acceptance can differ between modes even with fixed output counts. The sequential order was not counterbalanced, and three repetitions do not establish statistical confidence.

## Checklist

- [x] Format changed code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add default-selection, CLI, and candidate-boundary tests.
- [x] Document default scope and opt-out.
- [x] Provide accuracy results and workload timings with revision and interpretation limits.

## Motivation

DSpark / spec-v2 decode on HIP waits on the host every step to read the accept lengths. This removes that sync so the next step can be scheduled while the GPU is still busy. HIP only; other platforms are unchanged. Independent of the monokernel PRs that follow (part 1 of 4).

## Modifications

- Skip the per-step host read of the accept lengths in the overlap scheduler when no attention backend needs CPU sequence lengths (HIP only).
- Fold the simulated accept / bonus into the verify epilogue so it stays inside the graph (`SGLANG_DSPARK_SIMULATE_FOLD`, default on; HIP only, and only with `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` set).

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K 1319: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 DSpark 0.906; DeepSeek-V4-Pro TP8 EAGLE 0.951 before / 0.948 after.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 DSpark decode, c1 TPOT: -6.8% without the per-step sync, a further -1% to -3% with the fold.
DeepSeek-V4-Pro TP8 EAGLE, 8k TPOT c1 / c4: -0.8% / -1.2% (within run-to-run noise; no regression).

title: [Feat] diffusion: support FLUX 3 Image Klein
author: AgainstEntropy
body:
## Motivation

Add native FLUX.3 Image text-to-image and multi-reference editing support, using the self-contained `black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base` and `black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein` release packages, including FP8R/NVFP4 variants.

## Changes

- Reuse the FLUX.3 transformer, native parallel linears, attention dispatcher, loader, residency manager, and existing grouped-request scheduler.
- Support concurrent requests and multiple outputs without mixing prompts, seeds, references, CFG branches, or output order. Bucket text encoding and VAE decoding; pack independent DiT samples.
- Fail attention initialization explicitly instead of silently dropping SP collectives through a local fallback.
- Honor CPU-first loading and reuse strict meta/assign loading. Replace custom config parsing and boolean handling with shared utilities.
- Add an opt-in full-checkpoint HTTP regression and a cookbook picker covering RTX 5090, Hopper, and Blackwell with one to eight GPUs. Unmeasured recipes remain labeled unverified.

The follow-up adds batching while reducing production code by 44 lines relative to the original implementation after merging main. No separate scheduler or new runtime dependency is introduced.

## Validation

- 92 focused tests and 21 subtests passed on H200; pre-commit and 64 cookbook command-generation combinations passed.
- Base BF16 single-request PNGs match the original branch exactly at 512x512/4 steps and 1024x1024/50 steps, seed 42, Torch SDPA.
- Real HTTP tests cover T2I, I2I, independent concurrent requests, `n=2`, and exact repetition of a single request after batching. Also exercised TP2, Ulysses SP2, CFG2, distilled sampling, and layerwise/component offload.
- PNG batch-1/batch-2 comparison: SSIM 0.9885-0.9955 across four 512x512/8-step samples. Batching changes floating-point reductions; it is not a bitwise-equality promise across batch sizes.

The full-checkpoint test is opt-in because checkpoint access is required. Official Diffusers parity is deferred; no official GT or universal fidelity guarantee is claimed. Release BF16/FP8R were exercised on GB300/H200, NVFP4 on GB300, and Base BF16 on RTX 5090. Four-GPU validation is in progress.

## Release Checkpoint Validation

- Base/Distilled: 1024x1024 T2I/I2I, 50/16 steps, two prompts/seeds, repeated PNG requests. Repeats matched within each tested configuration.
- GB300 Base FP8R/NVFP4: T2I 2.18/2.14s vs BF16 3.21s; I2I 4.49/4.31s vs 6.31s. Quantization is lossy: observed minimum SSIM 0.958/0.919 (T2I) and 0.981/0.958 (I2I).
- Request-scoped fixed conditioning reuse and full-context FP32 VAE attention reduce work/workspace without pruning attention. For a 2048x2048 reference, peak allocated GPU memory fell from 54.3 to 29.5 GiB on GB300; latency was effectively unchanged. Reduction order can change pixels; exact keeps the original VAE path.
- BF16 synthetic rank-4 LoRA: dynamic/merge, repeatability and exact base restoration verified. Late LoRA on PrimsTS-packed weights is rejected before wrapping; startup LoRA selects the generic layout.
- Image-edit Cache-DiT form fields now reach sampling params and are validated; GB300 Base I2I 6.31→3.08s at threshold 0.12, observed SSIM 0.9786–0.9975. Approximate and opt-in.
- Cookbook includes measured profiles and explicit unverified combinations. Software/timing boundaries and full precision limitations are recorded there.

## Pre-release Batching Measurements

One GB300 (about 277 GiB), Base BF16, resident components, eager, Torch SDPA, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0. Checkpoint revision `5de4fe32f17aee3dbc34375a94935f09206dba2c`. Three-round medians, two different prompts/seeds, local HTTP and JPEG serialization included; both shapes and reference encoding warmed.

| Workload | Serial pair | Batch-2 pair | Throughput ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T2I, 512x512, 8 steps | 0.649 s | 0.324 s | 2.00x |
| I2I, 512x512, 8 steps | 0.737 s | 0.546 s | 1.35x |
| T2I, 1024x1024, 50 steps | 6.248 s | 6.050 s | 1.03x |
| I2I, 1024x1024, 50 steps | 13.171 s | 12.996 s | 1.01x |

The 8-step runs test short-request behavior, not recommended Base sampling quality. The standard 50-step workload gains little; FlashAttention shows the same limitation. Batch 1 remains the default. For the measured 50-step requests, batch-1 versus batch-2 JPEG SSIM was 0.9920-0.9977. These samples are not a general quality bound.

title: [Fix] imports: Bind FlashInfer lazily at four import sites so the server starts without it
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

Four modules import FlashInfer at module level behind `is_cuda()` alone: `layers/sampler.py`, `speculative/dflash_utils.py`, `layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py` and `layers/attention/vision.py`. Importing `sglang.srt.entrypoints.http_server` reaches all four, so a CUDA environment without FlashInfer fails at import time before any backend is chosen:

```
File ".../sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py", line 255, in <module>
    from flashinfer import bmm_fp8 as _raw_bmm_fp8_batched
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'flashinfer'
```

Every other FlashInfer-dependent path is already selected at runtime (attention backend, sampling backend, the per-tensor fp8 helper guarded by `is_flashinfer_available()`); these four were the remaining hard import-time dependencies.

## Modifications

- Replace the four eager imports with `LazyImport` from `sglang.utils`, which resolves the attribute on first call. With FlashInfer installed the bound names resolve to the same objects (checked with `is` for all six names), so behaviour is unchanged. Without it the server imports and starts, the sampling backend defaults to `pytorch` as it already does when FlashInfer is absent, and a path that really needs FlashInfer still raises `ModuleNotFoundError` at the call instead of at import.
- Add `test/registered/unit/test_import_without_flashinfer.py` (base-b, 1-gpu-small): imports the HTTP entrypoint in a subprocess with `flashinfer` blocked in `sys.modules`. It fails on current main at the `fp8_utils` import and passes with this change.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no numerics change. The lazily bound names are the same FlashInfer functions once resolved.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: `LazyImport.__call__` adds one attribute lookup per call after the first resolution; the four names are called from already Python-dispatched paths.

title: [Feat] [NPU] scheduler: align cross-request ViT batching with CUDA and fix NPU graph buffer ownership
author: Suxing224
body:
[**Related issue**: [#25598 — NPU Development Roadmap 2026 H2](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25598) 

---

## Motivation

NPU currently encodes per-image cache misses separately for each request. Enable the existing CUDA cross-request batching path on NPU, so eligible cache misses from multiple requests can be encoded together, without introducing a new environment variable. Retain the existing per-request behavior on HIP/XPU.

Cross-request batching also requires cached embeddings to remain valid after later ViT invocations. The NPU graph runner must preserve caller inputs and returned embeddings across capture, replay, and reuse of the shared graph pool.

## Modifications

1. **Scheduler:** remove NPU from the per-request fallback condition so eligible cache misses follow the existing CUDA batching path. Keep deduplication, cache refill, and request-order assembly. HIP/XPU retain the per-request path. No new environment variable or model capability flag is introduced.
2. **NPU graph ownership:** give captured inputs and returned embeddings independent storage where needed, preventing in-place vision blocks and later graph executions from overwriting caller inputs or retained embeddings.
3. **Regression tests:** cover cross-request merge/split behavior and graph input/output ownership, plus NPU image association, multi-image ordering and embedding-cache reuse. The block/deepstack/merger computation and graph lifecycle retain the main implementation.

## Unit tests and static checks

| Test | Result |
|---|---:|
| Chunked multimodal embedding unit tests | Included in combined run: 32 passed |
| NPU ViT graph runner unit tests | Included in combined run: 1 passed |
| CUDA ViT graph runner unit tests | Included in combined run: 6 passed (CPU test; no CUDA hardware validation) |
| Combined current-runner test command | 39 passed, 15 warnings, 13.58s |

<details>
<summary>Execution command and output summary</summary>

```bash
python -m pytest test/registered/chunked_prefill/test_mm_chunked_embedding_unit.py test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_vit_npu_graph_runner.py test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_vit_cuda_graph_runner.py -q
# 39 passed, 15 warnings, 13.58s

python -m py_compile \
  python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/vit_npu_graph_runner.py \
  test/registered/chunked_prefill/test_mm_chunked_embedding_unit.py \
  test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_vit_npu_graph_runner.py
git diff --check
# Exit 0 for both checks.
```

</details>

The embedding tests exercise merge/split, deduplication, cache refill and request ordering. The NPU runner test covers attention-boundary keys and independent input/output storage. These tests include mocked device boundaries; real-device checks are described separately.

Applicable checks passed using an isolated tool environment: Ruff0.15.1 (lint and format), isort7.0.0, codespell2.4.1, py_compile, git diff --check and the repository bare-pytest-main/registry/package-registration scripts. GitHub CI is not yet confirmed for the final commit.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Small-/large-image benchmarks

The following measurements use the final CUDA-parity scheduler and the tested graph-runner fix. On Ascend 910 / CANN 9.1, Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct ran at TP1/BF16 with context length 8,192, chunked prefill 8,192, max running requests 64, static memory fraction 0.80, and LLM graph enabled. ViT graph was not explicitly enabled for these runs; these results are not graph-on measurements.

All requests used one image, input length 30, seed 1, and `--random-range-ratio 1`. Each condition ran three paired rounds; version order alternated between rounds. The first three workloads used 128 measured requests plus 32 warmup requests per round; the last used 152 plus 38. All 24 benchmark cells exited successfully, every measured request completed, and all error entries were empty. Each round generated 4,096 output tokens for output-length-32 workloads and 38,912 for output-length-256 workloads.

Values below are medians across rounds. Arrows show reference -> candidate; throughput percentages compare those medians. The reference restores the recorded main scheduler while retaining the candidate tree and graph-runner fixes, as in the other paired comparisons.

| Workload | Request throughput | Mean TTFT | p99 TTFT | p99 E2E latency |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 448 x 448, c16, output 32 | 13.62 -> 17.75 req/s (**+30.3%**) | 641.66 -> 389.75 ms (**-39.3%**) | 711.66 -> 473.79 ms | 1,190.50 -> 938.41 ms |
| 448 x 448, c32, output 32 | 16.84 -> 23.90 req/s (**+41.9%**) | 1,224.42 -> 649.94 ms (**-46.9%**) | 1,530.34 -> 826.38 ms | 2,059.37 -> 1,375.65 ms |
| 1920 x 1080, c16, output 32 | 3.24 -> 3.27 req/s (+0.9%) | 3,130.25 -> 3,105.33 ms | 4,222.85 -> 4,195.23 ms | 5,016.72 -> 5,005.19 ms |
| 1920 x 1080, c42, output 256 | 2.26 -> 2.25 req/s (-0.4%) | 6,217.16 -> 6,208.27 ms | 10,887.37 -> 10,799.23 ms | 18,391.22 -> 18,510.38 ms |

With three rounds and 128/152 measured requests per round, these results describe the tested workloads; they do not establish statistical significance or a general tail-latency improvement. The multi-model matrix reports a separate run set; the graph-on comparison explicitly enables ViT graph. Interpret each table using its stated workload and settings.

title: [Perf] [NPU] mem_cache: Increase GLM-5.2-W4A8C8 KV cache capacity with compact DSA indexer allocation
author: xiedeyantu
body:
## Motivation

Increase KV cache capacity for GLM-5.2-W4A8C8 on Ascend 910B4 by avoiding indexer cache allocation for DSA layers that reuse the previous layer’s top-k indices, while preserving model accuracy.

- Allocate indexer cache slots only for layers that compute top-k indices.

title: [Fix] mem_cache: Move FP4 MLA block scales with their KV in `move_kv_cache`
author: gkswns0531
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Speculative decoding relocates KV rows with `move_kv_cache`: accepted draft tokens are moved into place after verification (`spec_utils.py`, EAGLE with topk > 1 and NGRAM), and with page_size > 1 the prefix tail page is copied to each branch (`eagle_worker_common.py`). `MLATokenToKVPoolFP4` inherits `MLATokenToKVPool.move_kv_cache` (#26982), which copies `kv_buffer` rows only. Each moved FP4 latent is then dequantized with whatever block scales were left at its target slot, typically a rejected draft token's, and nothing reports an error.

The other quantized pools already move scales with their data (`MHATokenToKVPool`, `MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8`, `DSATokenToKVPool`).

## Modifications

- `MLATokenToKVPoolFP4.move_kv_cache`: run the MLA move for the latent, then copy the `kv_scale_buffer` rows with the same indices.
- `test_quantized_kv_pool.py`: a CPU `MLATokenToKVPoolFP4` test that moves two slots and checks that data and scales arrive in every layer.

Out of scope: other methods inherited from `MLATokenToKVPool` also handle `kv_buffer` only (`get_cpu_copy`/`load_cpu_copy`, `get_contiguous_buf_infos`, the HiCache host pool, `get_kv_size_bytes`). As with MXFP8 (#35888, #35718), each needs its own PR.

## Accuracy Tests

Found by code inspection and verified at the unit level; not reproduced end to end, which needs an MLA model served with the FP4 KV cache and EAGLE topk > 1 or NGRAM decoding. The change only moves the scale rows of slots that the existing move already relocates.

- `python3 test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_quantized_kv_pool.py`: OK (2 tests). On main the new test fails at the scale assertion.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

One extra gather and `index_put_` per layer per move, on `[n, kv_cache_dim / 16]` uint8 rows. Only moves on an FP4 MLA cache pay it.

title: [Feat] [NPU] GLM-4.1V: Add ModelSlim W8A8S support with multimodal serving optimizations
author: cx22757
body:
## Motivation

Make GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking servable on Ascend NPUs with ModelSlim W8A8S quantized weights, and fix the largest remaining vision-prefill gaps found by CANN profiling of the running server: every ViT block re-issued a `cu_seqlens` NPU→CPU transfer (plus a `seq_lens.max().item()` sync) per forward pass, serializing the host behind 27 blocks per image batch and stalling the scheduler under concurrent prefill; and the patch downsampling step ran Conv2D with unfold/permute layout copies (plus internal TransData on non-contiguous inputs) per image batch.

This contributes to the Ascend multimodal workstream in the NPU roadmap #43519.

## Modifications

**Uncompressed ModelSlim W8A8S weights** 
- New `ModelSlimW8A8SInt8` scheme for uncompressed W8A8S exports: dense INT8 weights with encoded INT64 `deq_scale` (requires `--dtype float16`; the encoding is only meaningful for FP16 output), plus per-tensor `input_scale` / `input_offset` / `quant_bias` described by `quant_model_description.json`.
- `NPUW8A8Int8LinearMethod` skips the unused `weight_scale`/`weight_offset` fields that W8A8S exports omit, and creates `aclnn_input_scale` / `aclnn_input_scale_reciprocal` / `aclnn_input_offset` in the expanded per-channel layout the aclnn ops expect.

**CPU sequence-length metadata reuse across ViT blocks** (`32092d1599`)
- `Glm4vVisionModel.forward` (NPU branch) prepares the attention metadata's CPU cumulative sequence endpoints (`actual_seq_lengths_cpu`) and max seqlen once per forward pass, merging the two per-forward D2H transfers and removing the `seq_lens.max().item()` sync point.
- `VisionAscendAttention.forward` consumes the prepared CPU list for every ViT block instead of re-issuing a `cu_seqlens.to("cpu")` round-trip per block, and `seq_len_arg.tolist()` runs only for tensor inputs.

**GEMM-based patch downsampling without layout copies** (`7982403c61`)
- On NPU, the spatial-merge downsampling after the ViT blocks runs as a plain `F.linear` over the natural NHWC layout: the `[N, 2, 2, C]` post-layernorm output is reshaped directly to `[N, K*K*C]`, and the `[O, K*K*C]` GEMM weight is derived once from the already-loaded conv weight and cached — no unfold/permute/reshape copies and no Conv2D TransData on non-contiguous inputs.
- Non-NPU platforms keep the original `nn.Conv2d` path; parameter names, weight shapes/dtypes and checkpoint loading are unchanged. An intermediate variant that enabled `Conv2dLayer(disable_linear=False)` was evaluated and rejected: its unfold/permute copies offset the GEMM gain (±2% on microbenchmarks).

## Usage

Single-card launch (validated configuration, 64GB Ascend NPU):

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking-w8a8s \
  --device npu --attention-backend ascend --tp-size 1 --dtype float16 \
  --context-length 32768 --mem-fraction-static 0.65 --max-running-requests 16
```

`--dtype float16` is required for this export (INT64 `deq_scale` encoding). The vision-path optimizations activate automatically on the NPU GLM-4V path; nothing needs to be configured. BF16 original weights benefit from them the same way.

## Accuracy Tests

Full MMBench DEV EN v1.1 (4876 rotated samples, 1292 CircularEval groups), deterministic answer extraction, greedy decoding, single Ascend NPU, same W8A8S weights as this PR ships:

| Metric | BF16 | W8A8S (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CircularEval (GLM extraction) | 87.31% | 86.30% |
| Strict boxed exact-match CircularEval | 87.15% | 86.30% |
| Per-sample accuracy | 90.83% | 90.28% |

The vision-path optimizations are numerically equivalent to the baseline chain: CPU sequence-length metadata is bit-identical (prompt_tokens identical to baseline on all multi-image behavior cases), and the downsample GEMM matches Conv2D to 1.6e-5 relative error (±1 LSB FP16 rounding, same magnitude as quantization noise). Each optimization individually and the combination on this branch pass GSM8K official test first 10 (10/10 after granting the one over-long chain-of-thought a 3072-token budget, invalid=0) plus 3 image QA smoke cases, with greedy outputs semantically identical to the baseline (only benign wording forks inside thinking segments).

## Performance

Fixed-length streaming benchmark, single NPU, same card, three configs run back-to-back in the same order, 4 trials per cell with trial 0 discarded as warmup, per-request P50 over the steady trials; 1024 requests per config, 0 errors, all outputs at requested length. The three columns change one variable at a time: BF16 weights → W8A8S weights (same code) → W8A8S weights + this PR's vision-prefill optimizations:

| Workload | c | TTFT P50 (ms) BF16 / W8A8S / +opt | TPOT P50 (ms) BF16 / W8A8S / +opt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| image_normal (896px, 1024 img tokens) | 1 | 318.5 / 292.8 / **275.8** | 18.6 / 14.8 / **14.9** |
| image_normal | 16 | 2757.6 / 2695.7 / **2273.2** | 23.9 / 18.8 / **19.1** |
| image_large (1792px, 4096 img tokens) | 1 | 1318.8 / 1217.0 / **1182.6** | 19.4 / 15.5 / **15.5** |
| image_large | 16 | 12111.1 / 11319.0 / **10513.1** | 45.3 / 38.3 / **37.5** |
| image_long | 1 | 313.5 / 291.4 / **269.6** | 19.0 / 15.2 / **15.3** |
| image_long | 16 | 2785.1 / 2620.4 / **2289.7** | 23.2 / 18.6 / **18.8** |
| text4096 | 16 | 3761.2 / 2984.7 / **2974.9** | 35.3 / 28.3 / **28.4** |
| text512 | 1 | 78.2 / 72.1 / **73.1** | 17.6 / 13.8 / **13.9** |

Headline numbers:

- **W8A8S vs BF16** (same code): TTFT `−2~−21%` (text4096 c16 −20.6%), TPOT `−15~−22%`. Quantization is a latency win across every workload, not only a memory one.
- **This PR on top of W8A8S**: TTFT image_normal c1 −5.8%, c16 −15.7%, image_large c1 −2.8%, c16 −7.1%, image_long c1 −7.5%, c16 −12.6%; text workloads flat (text4096 c16 −0.3%, text512 c1 +1.0ms/+1.3%, within run-to-run noise for that 72ms cell). No vision scenario regresses.
- TPOT is unchanged by the vision-prefill changes (decode path untouched): every c1 cell moves by <0.1 ms, image_large c16 −2.1%.
- Known follow-up (not in this PR): `down_proj` and the vision tower remain FP16 in the current export; quantizing `down_proj` is the next-largest decode win (est. ~32% of the decode step).

title: [Fix] [AMD] mhc: Bound the Triton fused post+pre buffer cache
author: maning00
body:
## Motivation

`_get_fused_hc_post_pre_buffers` caches one set of `mhc_post_pre` buffers per distinct `num_tokens` and never evicts them. The cache was added together with the `num_tokens <= _FUSED_HC_POST_PRE_M_THRESHOLD` (64) gate in #26383, so it stayed small. Since #36871, gfx1250 runs the Triton fused post+pre for every batch size, so each distinct prefill size adds a set that is never freed. For DeepSeek-V4-Pro (hidden 7168, `hc_mult` 4), one set is about 160 KB per token, or about 330 MB at 2048 tokens; over half of that is the fp32 `acc_partial`.

On gfx1250, a DeepSeek-V4-Pro prefill server (TP4, `--chunked-prefill-size 2048`) running a multi-turn agentic workload kept growing until it hit `torch.OutOfMemoryError` about an hour in. Live-tensor scans showed a growing set of `(896, M, 24)` fp32 buffers, one for each distinct M.

## Modifications

- Cache buffers only for `num_tokens <= _FUSED_HC_POST_PRE_M_THRESHOLD`, the bound the cache was designed for. The bound applies to every caller.
- Larger calls allocate their buffers per call; they go back to the caching allocator after use. Small (decode) batches keep using cached buffers.
- Today only gfx1250 runs this path above the threshold, so that is the only place behavior changes:
  - gfx95 enters it only for up to 64 tokens, when the aiter HIP kernel declines;
  - GLM-5-Next calls the boundary only for up to 16 tokens;
  - other platforms never reach it.
- Add a CPU regression test, `TestAmdFusedMhcBufferCache`. It fails on main (sizes 65 and 2048 stay cached) and passes with this change.

## Accuracy Tests

Outputs are not expected to change. The kernel and the buffer shapes are the same; for `num_tokens > 64` the buffers are just no longer reused across calls.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked separately. Calls above 64 tokens make six extra caching-allocator allocations, and small batches are still served from the cache.

End-to-end memory on gfx1250: DeepSeek-V4-Pro, PD disaggregation 1P (TP4) + 1D (TP4), multi-turn agentic benchmark at concurrency 64, `--mem-fraction-static 0.82`. The run used a downstream build whose `deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py` matches main, with an env-gated variant of this change that caches up to 512 tokens.

| Prefill server | TP0 `torch.cuda.memory_allocated` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| main | 427 GiB at failure (432 GiB device) | OOM about 58 min into the benchmark |
| bounded cache | 362.6 GiB -> 363.0 GiB over 2 h 11 min | benchmark completed (3,042 requests, 0 errors) |

cc @inkcherry

title: [Doc] [AMD] cookbook: Refresh DeepSeek V4 AgentX PD recipe optimizations
author: Duyi-Wang
body:
## Motivation

title: [Perf] [AMD] lm_head: Use aiter tgemm for the bf16 lm_head on gfx1250
author: jiaryang
body:
## Motivation

On gfx1250 the unquantized bf16 lm_head goes through `torch.matmul`, which lands on hipBLASLt and is several times slower than aiter's GEMM at decode batch sizes.

## Modifications

With `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` on gfx1250, a 2D bf16 lm_head matmul uses `aiter.tuned_gemm.tgemm.mm`, as `unquant.py` already does for linear layers on HIP. Other dtypes, shapes and devices keep the existing path. A CPU unit test covers the gate.

## Setup

Kimi-K2-Thinking-MXFP4, TP8, MI455X (gfx1250), image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi45x-20261019` with sglang 36978d6c4d and aiter 2bb549102 plus Kimi-K2 GEMM configs.

Server: `--tp 8 --attention-backend aiter --prefill-attention-backend aiter --decode-attention-backend aiter --page-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --disable-radix-cache --disable-custom-all-reduce --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 128 --max-running-requests 128 --mem-fraction-static 0.8`.

## Accuracy Tests

The lm_head output is bit-identical to `torch.mm` at batch sizes 1, 4, 32 and 128.

GSM8K with `few_shot_gsm8k` (8-shot, 1319 questions, `max_new_tokens` 512, the settings of sglang's AMD Kimi accuracy tests):

| | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---|---|
| Before (two runs) | 0.939 / 0.945 | 0.000 / 0.000 |
| After | 0.944 | 0.000 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

lm_head of Kimi-K2 at TP8 (vocab shard 20480 x 7168, 293 MB of weights, far larger than L2), MI455X, CUDA-graph replay:

| batch | torch.mm (ms) | tgemm.mm (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.131 | 0.070 |
| 4 | 0.129 | 0.062 |
| 32 | 0.285 | 0.074 |
| 128 | 0.986 | 0.232 |

End to end, TP8, 8k input / 1k output, concurrency 4, `bench_serving`:

| | Output tok/s | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 137.42 | 414.54 | 27.90 |
| After | 142.08 (+3.4%) | 414.09 | 26.92 (-3.5%) |

At batch 4 the kernel saves about 0.07 ms per decode step, so most of the end-to-end difference is run-to-run variance (the two before runs differ by 2.1%); the saving grows with batch size (0.75 ms per step at batch 128).

title: [Perf] [AMD] mla: Use aiter bf16 batched GEMM for the absorb BMMs on gfx1250 decode
author: jiaryang
body:
## Motivation

On gfx950 the absorbed MLA weights are converted to MXFP4 and run on aiter. On gfx1250 they stay bf16 and the two absorb BMMs per layer (`q_nope @ w_kc`, `attn_output @ w_vc`) go through `torch.bmm`, which lands on hipBLASLt.

## Modifications

With `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` on gfx1250, both absorb BMMs use aiter `batched_gemm_bf16` when both operands are bf16, `w_scale` is 1.0 and the batch has at most 256 rows (the same limit as the gfx95 fp8 path):

- q: the Gluon backend up to 4 rows, Triton above (faster at larger batches);
- v: the Gluon backend, writing into the existing `(batch, heads, dim)` buffer through `YQ`, so the flatten stays a view.

Prefill-sized batches, quantized weights and the piecewise CUDA graph path keep `torch.bmm`. The piecewise path skips aiter for the q absorb as well as the v absorb. If `batched_gemm_bf16` cannot be imported, both BMMs stay on `torch.bmm` instead of failing the model import.

### Dependency on aiter

None beyond the aiter in the gfx1250 Docker image (`batched_gemm_bf16` with `backend=` and `YQ=`). Shape-specific gfx1250 configs for these BMMs are proposed in ROCm/aiter#6573; without them aiter uses its default config.

## Setup

Kimi-K2-Thinking-MXFP4, TP8, MI455X (gfx1250), image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi45x-20261019` with sglang 36978d6c4d and aiter 2bb549102 plus Kimi-K2 GEMM configs, including the ROCm/aiter#6573 configs.

Server: `--tp 8 --attention-backend aiter --prefill-attention-backend aiter --decode-attention-backend aiter --page-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --disable-radix-cache --disable-custom-all-reduce --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 128 --max-running-requests 128 --mem-fraction-static 0.8`.

## Accuracy Tests

Both BMM outputs are bit-identical to `torch.bmm` at batch sizes 1, 4, 32 and 128.

GSM8K with `few_shot_gsm8k` (8-shot, 1319 questions, `max_new_tokens` 512, the settings of sglang's AMD Kimi accuracy tests):

|---|---|---|
| Before (two runs) | 0.939 / 0.945 | 0.000 / 0.000 |

title: [Perf] attention: Skip the triton MLA K rescale when k_scale is 1.0
author: jiaryang
body:
## Motivation

For MLA, the triton backend divides K by `k_scale` before writing the KV cache, because `MLATokenToKVPool` takes no scale: a clone plus a divide on extend and an in-place divide on decode. Quark checkpoints create `k_scale` for every layer and leave it at 1.0 when there is no KV scale, so every layer divides by one.

## Modifications

When `k_scale_float == 1.0`, write K directly on both paths. A `None` `k_scale_float` keeps the divide. Non-MLA paths are unchanged. On extend, that direct write still goes through `kv_layers.layer(layer.layer_id).store` (the MLA pool's `set_kv_buffer`). It does not switch to `_set_kv_buffer`, which under DCP rewrites the location and passes a `dcp_kv_mask` that `MLATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer` does not take.

This touches the same extend block as #42181 (out-of-place divide) without overlapping it; the two are independent.

## Setup

Kimi-K2-Thinking-MXFP4, TP8, MI455X (gfx1250), image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi45x-20261019` (sglang ed0b8f433f; aiter 2bb549102 with Kimi-K2 GEMM configs).

Server: `--tp 8 --attention-backend aiter --prefill-attention-backend aiter --decode-attention-backend triton --page-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --disable-radix-cache --disable-custom-all-reduce --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 128 --max-running-requests 128 --mem-fraction-static 0.8`. The checkpoint has no KV scales, so `k_scale` stays 1.0 with the fp8 KV cache. Before and after differ only by this commit on top of the image's sglang.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K with `few_shot_gsm8k` (8-shot, 1319 questions, `max_new_tokens` 512, the settings of sglang's AMD Kimi accuracy tests):

| | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 0.941 | 0.000 |
| After | 0.939 | 0.000 |

Dividing by 1.0 does not change any value, so the difference is run-to-run variance of batched serving.

With `--prefill-attention-backend aiter` the extend change is never reached, so the extend path was checked separately with `--prefill-attention-backend triton --chunked-prefill-size 512` (512-token chunks so that later chunks of each prompt are extends with a prefix, which go through the triton MLA KV write): GSM8K 0.940, invalid 0.000. A `py-spy` sample during that run shows `forward_extend` on the new direct-write branch.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

TP8, 8k input / 1k output, concurrency 4, `bench_serving`:

| | Output tok/s | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 125.22 | 951.86 | 29.94 |
| After | 130.45 (+4.2%) | 946.31 | 28.93 (-3.4%) |

Decode profile at batch 4 (20 steps, per-step kernel time on rank 0): the elementwise bucket, which holds the divide, goes from 6.93 ms to 5.84 ms (-1.09 ms), matching the 1.0 ms TPOT drop.

title: [Perf] [AMD] mla: Fuse RoPE, concat and KV-cache write for MLA decode on gfx1250
author: jiaryang
body:
## Motivation

On gfx950, aiter MLA decode runs RoPE, the q/k concat and the KV-cache write in one `fused_qk_rope_cat_and_cache_mla` kernel. On gfx1250 these are still separate: native RoPE, two `torch.cat` and `set_kv_buffer`, more than a dozen elementwise kernels per layer. This PR extends the gfx950 fused branch to gfx1250.

## Modifications

With `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` on gfx1250, MLA decode with the aiter or triton backend skips the standalone RoPE and takes the fused branch, as aiter MLA does on gfx950. gfx950 is unchanged.

- As on gfx950, the gate is evaluated per call: decode, the aiter or triton backend, no DSA, one DCP rank, a rope module of exactly `RotaryEmbedding` or `DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding`, and a bf16 or FP8 KV pool. The pool check reads the pool's dtype, so an fp16 pool, which the kernel rejects, stays on the unfused path.
- sglang's rope keeps cos and sin in one `cos_sin_cache`; the kernel gets the two halves as strided views.
- Q keeps `q_nope_out`'s dtype, which is bf16 on gfx1250: MLA decode there takes an unquantized Q even over an FP8 KV cache.
- Prepare's rope-skip condition moves into `_applies_rope_in_prepare`, so the unit test can check that prepare skips RoPE exactly when core fuses it.
- CPU unit tests are added to `test/registered/unit/models/test_rocm_mla_absorb_fusion_gate.py`.

Requires ROCm/aiter#5501, which both ROCm Docker pins in `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` already contain. On main, gfx1250 MLA decode runs the triton backend, which the gate covers, and the first set of numbers below is main with the triton decode backend. With #44458's aiter decode backend the same fused branch applies; the second table measures that.

Validated on gfx1250 with Kimi-K2-Thinking-MXFP4 at TP8, with the triton decode backend on main and the aiter decode backend from #44458.

## Accuracy Tests

The fused kernel matches the unfused path (q and the written KV rows) for bf16 and FP8 KV, batch 1 to 128.

GSM8K, 8-shot, 1319 questions, triton decode backend on main:

| | KV cache | Runs | Accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | FP8 | 4 | 0.942 (0.950, 0.939, 0.939, 0.939) |
| After | FP8 | 4 | 0.940 (0.942, 0.938, 0.934, 0.945) |
| Before | bf16 | 1 | 0.947 |
| After | bf16 | 1 | 0.938 |

Unchanged main moves by 0.011 between server launches (0.950 and 0.939), so the single bf16 run is within that spread.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

RoPE, concat and KV write per layer, Kimi-K2 TP8 shapes, CUDA graph replay:

| batch | unfused (us) | fused (us) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 37.6 | 1.9 |
| 4 | 40.8 | 1.6 |
| 32 | 55.6 | 1.7 |
| 128 | 81.6 | 1.9 |

`bench_serving`, 8k input / 1k output, FP8 KV, triton decode backend on main:

| Concurrency | | Throughput per GPU (tok/s/GPU) | Interactivity (tok/s/user) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | Before | 171.4 | 39.7 | 416.8 | 25.20 |
| 4 | After | 217.7 | 51.2 | 406.4 | 19.54 |
| 4 | Change | +27.0% | +29.0% | -2.5% | -22.5% |
| 16 | Before | 398.8 | 22.9 | 440.6 | 43.63 |
| 16 | After | 483.4 | 28.0 | 427.1 | 35.68 |
| 16 | Change | +21.2% | +22.3% | -3.1% | -18.2% |
| 64 | Before | 647.9 | 9.4 | 677.0 | 106.87 |
| 64 | After | 745.6 | 10.7 | 518.1 | 93.66 |
| 64 | Change | +15.1% | +14.1% | -23.5% | -12.4% |

In the decode profile (concurrency 4, 8k context), each layer's RoPE, concat and KV write go from about 14 PyTorch kernels taking about 82 us to the fused kernel taking about 3 us, and the decode step goes from 30.0 ms to 23.6 ms. The triton decode attention kernels are unchanged.

Concurrency 4 with #44458's aiter decode backend on both sides:

|---|---|---|---|---|

Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

On DSV4.1 with TP only, the draft's head are split by vocab. Each GPU computes logits for its own slice, and picking a draft token never needs the whole vocab.

But verify runs rejection sampling over the whole vocab, so the draft all-gathers its logits at every step, once per draft token.

This PR keeps the draft logits on their shards and adds a support to sharded rejection sampling, so verify only exchanges a few statistics per row instead of the whole-vocab logits.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

**Gating**
- Add `SGLANG_DSPARK_SHARDED_ACCEPT`, on by default on HIP.
- With the flag off, nothing changes.

**Draft side**
- With the sharded accept on, the draft keeps each step's logits on its own vocab shard instead of all-gathering them.

  ```python
  # python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py, L328
  # Use the sharded accept only when the vocab is sharded and logits are kept.
  self._sharded_accept = (
      envs.SGLANG_DSPARK_SHARDED_ACCEPT.get()
      and not self._greedy_draft
      and markov_head is not None
      and markov_head.vocab_shard is not None
  )

  # python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_draft.py, L224
  sharded = (
      {}
      if shard is None
      else dict(
          vocab_start=shard.start,
          gather=shard.gather.gather_stacked,
          gather_logits=None if sharded_accept else shard.gather,  # skip the all-gather
      )
  )
  ```

- Pass the draft's noise to the verify, so every rank reaches the same accept decision and bonus token.

**Verify side**
- Add `sharded_accept_hip.py` with two triton kernels:
  - `_stats_kernel`: each gpu reduces its vocab shard to a few stats per row (max logit, sum-exp, the drafted token's logit).
  - `_accept_kernel`: each gpu merges the stats into p(x) and q(x) and runs the accept test. The bonus is a Gumbel-max race on each shard. The gpus exchange their candidates, and the draft's existing finish kernel picks the token.
- `accept_draft_tokens`: temperature-only batches use the sharded accept. Top-k, top-p, or block verification gather the logits once and fall back to `AcceptSampling`, matching main.

**Other**
- `dspark_block_accept_estimator.py`, `dspark_observability.py`: the block accept estimator (a diagnostic tool, off by default) skips sharded logits instead of computing on half the vocab.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

 **GSM8K**:

| Temperature | Sharded accept off | Sharded accept on |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | 85.7% | 86.3% |
| 0.0 | 90.4% | 90.2% |

**Accept length** is unchanged: 
- Client: in/out=8k/1k, temperature=1.0
- Server: tp2, no radix-cache

| Concurrency | Sharded accept off | Sharded accept on |
|---|---|---|
| 4  | 4.43 | 4.48 |
| 16 | 4.37 | 4.54 |
| 64 | 4.49 | 4.54 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

**Fixed length workload**
- Client: in/out=8k/1k, temperature=1.0
- Server: tp2, no radix-cache

> Real mode

title: [Perf] diffusion: Replay Triton launches without the runner's per-launch hook metadata
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

`@replay_launches` (#43859) replays a Triton wrapper's launches through `compiled[grid](*args)`, which is Triton's per-call runner. In Triton 3.7, `knobs.runtime.launch_enter_hook` and `launch_exit_hook` are `HookChain` objects and are never `None`. So on every launch the runner:
- builds a `LazyDict` of launch metadata;
- has the C launcher call into two empty Python hook chains.

That costs about 2 µs per launch on an x86 host. It is now one of the larger pieces of a replayed call.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/common/fast_launch.py`:
- When no launch hook is registered, a replayed launch calls `compiled.run(...)` directly. It passes the current stream, exactly as the runner does, and no hook metadata.
- When a hook is registered (e.g. proton or another profiler), replay keeps going through the runner, so hooks still see every launch.
- The launcher handles (`run`, `function`, `packed_metadata`) are read when the plan is built. If Triton's compiled-kernel API moves, `_record`'s existing guard therefore leaves that signature on the normal path instead of failing at replay.

No memory is involved, and the recording path is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

- New test `test_launch_hooks_see_replayed_launches`: a hook registered on `knobs.runtime.launch_enter_hook` sees the replayed launch.
- On H200:
  - `test_fast_launch.py` 33 passed;
  - `test_norm.py` 254 passed;
  - `test_layernorm_modulate.py` 21 passed;
  - `test_activation.py` 10 passed;
  - `test_flux2_strided_qknorm_rope.py` 2 passed (9 subtests);
  - `test_model_fast_paths.py` 97 passed, 1 skipped.
- End to end, output image md5 matched main in every configuration below.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Base `f7ad4345b8`, torch 2.13, triton 3.7.1, H200 (Xeon 8558P), with processes pinned to the GPU's NUMA node.

**Host time per call** of each replayed wrapper in `test_fast_launch.WRAPPERS` (µs, inference mode; the GPU is kept busy so only submission is timed):

| wrapper | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `flux2_qknorm_rope` | 17.93 | 16.40 |
| `layernorm_modulate` | 14.18 | 12.77 |
| `layernorm_modulate_scale_only` | 13.44 | 11.77 |
| `packed_silu_mul` | 11.04 | 9.73 |
| `rmsnorm_scale` | 13.57 | 11.90 |
| `rmsnorm_tanh_residual` | 14.52 | 12.93 |
| `rope_rotate_half` | 15.04 | 13.50 |
| `silu_mul` | 13.79 | 12.21 |
| `zimage_qk_rmsnorm` | 12.49 | 11.10 |

**End to end.** On H200, two identical main servers resident together differed by 3.5% in an A/A run at Qwen-Image-2.1 TP2 512², which is as large as this change. So both paths were built into one server and chosen per request, and requests rotated through the arms in the same process. An extra base arm in each round measures in-process noise. Values are client wall-clock medians, eager:

| | vs base | faster than base in | in-process A/A |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 TP2 512² | −2.4% | 7/10 | +0.5% |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 TP2 1024² (GPU-bound) | +0.1% | 2/10 | +0.1% |
| FLUX.1-dev TP2 512² | −2.1% | 8/8 | −0.4% |
| FLUX.1-dev TP2 512², together with #44478 | −3.9% | 8/8 | |
| Z-Image-Turbo 1 GPU 512² | −0.3% | 13/16 | −0.2% |

Output images are unchanged: the same kernels are launched with the same arguments. The gain shows wherever the host bounds the step, and more so on Grace hosts (GB200/GB300), where the same Python costs roughly twice as much. No GB300 was available for this run.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Classify residual_gate_add operands once per call
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

`residual_gate_add` is the most expensive kernel wrapper on the host in several diffusion DiTs. In a py-spy profile (H200, TP2 eager, at 256² so that the host bounds the step) it takes 12.5% of the denoise host time in Qwen-Image-2.1 and 10.3% in FLUX.1-dev. The CUDA launch is only about a fifth of that. The rest goes to:
- three separate classifications of the same operand layout: `can_use_residual_gate_add_cuda`, the transposed-layout test inside the op, then `_gate_mode`;
- a `torch.cuda.device` guard entered on every call (~1.7 µs);
- `torch.empty_strided`, where `empty_like` gives the same layout.

## Modifications

All changes are in `python/sglang/kernels/kda_kernels/residual_gate_add_jit.py`:
- `_route()` classifies the operands once and returns the gate mode, `_TRANSPOSED`, or `None`. `can_use_residual_gate_add_cuda`, `residual_gate_add_cuda` and `residual_gate_add` all use it, and the chosen mode is passed into the custom op as an `int`.
- The op enters the device guard only when the residual is not on the current device.
- The CUDA path allocates with `empty_like`; its residual is contiguous.
- `_is_transposed_dense_residual` tests the stride first, so contiguous inputs leave it early.

Accepted layouts and kernel choice are unchanged, with one exception. A full-shape `[B, 1, D]` gate with gaps between rows was accepted, because it also matched the batched-row rule, and then raised in `gate.view(-1)`:

```
RuntimeError: view size is not compatible with input tensor's size and stride
```

It now runs eager. No memory is involved, and the compiled path still goes through the custom op.

## Accuracy Tests

- New test `test_residual_gate_add_strided_full_gate_runs_eager` covers the case above. It fails on main.
- On H200:
  - `test_modulate.py` 1038 passed. It includes the existing acceptance-rule, dtype, transposed, CUDA-graph and `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` tests.
  - `test_model_fast_paths.py` 97 passed, 1 skipped.
  - `test_sites.py` 24 passed.
  - `test_residual_gate_fp32.py` 40 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Base `f7ad4345b8`, torch 2.13, H200 (Xeon 8558P), with processes pinned to the GPU's NUMA node.

**Host time per call** (µs, inference mode, bf16; the GPU is kept busy so only submission is timed):

| residual / gate | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `(1, 4608, 3072)` / `(1, 1, 3072)` (FLUX, Qwen) | 20.40 | 16.08 |
| `(1, 4608, 3072)` / `(1, 4608, 3072)` | 17.30 | 14.28 |
| `(2, 1024, 3072)` / `(2, 1, 3072)` | 22.18 | 16.57 |

**End to end.** On H200, two identical main servers resident together differed by 3.5% in an A/A run at Qwen-Image-2.1 TP2 512², which is more than this change. So both paths were built into one server and chosen per request, and requests rotated through the arms in the same process. An extra base arm in each round measures in-process noise. Values are client wall-clock medians, eager:

| | vs base | faster than base in | in-process A/A |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 TP2 512² | −1.9% | 10/10 | +0.5% |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 TP2 1024² (GPU-bound) | 0.0% | 6/10 | +0.1% |
| FLUX.1-dev TP2 512² | −1.4% | 8/8 | −0.4% |
| FLUX.1-dev TP2 512², together with #44471 | −3.9% | 8/8 | |

Output images are unchanged: the kernels and their inputs are the same. On Grace hosts (GB200/GB300), where these Python costs are about twice as large and the step is host-bound, the gain should be larger. No GB300 was available for this run.

title: [Perf] [AMD] deterministic: Allow AITER decode attention on gfx950
author: aarnetalman
body:
## Motivation

This PR lets deterministic inference on MI350X/MI355X (gfx950) use AITER for decode attention: `--decode-attention-backend aiter`, with prefill attention still on a deterministic backend such as Triton. Decode attention is a large part of the cost of deterministic mode on these GPUs, and with AITER decode, deterministic throughput is 1.27-1.91x higher for Qwen3-8B, 1.53-1.61x for Qwen3-30B-A3B and 1.09-1.13x for Qwen3.8-27B, with every determinism check still passing and unchanged GSM8K.

AITER's paged decode attention (`paged_attention_ragged`) splits each request's KV cache into fixed 256-token partitions and reduces them per request. The split depends only on the request's own context length, never on the batch, so a request gets the same result whatever it is batched with.

This builds on #44438, which makes deterministic mode check `--prefill-attention-backend` and `--decode-attention-backend`. Decode has to be set explicitly: `--attention-backend aiter --prefill-attention-backend triton` stays refused, because `--attention-backend` itself must be a deterministic backend.

### Refused in deterministic mode, and why

| Configuration | Why |
| --- | --- |
| AITER as `--attention-backend` or `--prefill-attention-backend` | AITER prefill attention is not batch-invariant (in our tests its results changed with the batch from about 480 tokens, and with mixed batches) |
| AITER decode for MLA models | MLA decode sizes its KV splits by the batch size |
| AITER decode on other GPUs than gfx950 | not tested |
| AITER decode with speculative decoding | target verify (`--speculative-attention-mode decode`) and some draft workers would run AITER's verify and extend kernels, which are not verified |
| AITER decode with sliding-window models, `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` or the vectorized 5D KV-cache layout | these run AITER's unified-attention or 5D-pool decode kernels instead of `paged_attention_ragged`; not verified. Refused when the AITER backend starts |
| `--enable-mixed-chunk` (any backend) | a mixed batch runs its decode tokens through the prefill kernels; handled separately in #44701, which switches it off in deterministic mode |

## Modifications

- `arg_groups/overrides.py` (`_deterministic_attention_backend`): the allowed backends are built per phase first; `aiter` is added for decode on gfx950, for non-MLA models and without speculative decoding. Both phases are then checked in one loop. When AITER decode is refused, the error says why. The per-phase fields are read directly.
- `layers/attention/aiter_backend.py`: in deterministic mode, the AITER backend refuses to start when decode would not run `paged_attention_ragged` (unified attention or the vectorized 5D KV-cache layout), so an accepted configuration always runs the kernel that was verified.
- `test_model_overrides.py`: a table test (gfx950 or not, MLA or not, AITER prefill or not, speculative decoding or not) for which configurations are accepted. #44438's refusal test pins `is_gfx95_supported` to `False` and sets both per-phase fields, so it does not depend on the machine it runs on.
- Unchanged: deterministic mode off; every configuration that does not set `--decode-attention-backend aiter`; the radix cache (it follows `--attention-backend`, which stays a deterministic backend).

## Accuracy Tests

Environment: 8x MI350X, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261013` (SGLang `27b68303d0`, AITER `e7d2453f2`), `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` (the image default); `aiter_backend.py` is identical to upstream main. Deterministic mode on MI350X also needs the open fixes #43788 (AITER GEMM and MoE bypass; not merged yet) and #34543 (all-reduce for oversized inputs), which were applied in all runs, together with our other open PRs. These runs used the image without #44438, where `--decode-attention-backend aiter` was not checked yet; the server arguments are the ones this PR accepts:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B --tp $TP \
  --attention-backend triton --prefill-attention-backend triton --decode-attention-backend aiter \
  --enable-deterministic-inference
# Qwen3.8-27B additionally: --linear-attn-prefill-backend triton --linear-attn-decode-backend triton
```

Checks, each on a fresh server:
- `python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic --test-mode {single,prefix,radix_cache} --n-trials 50`, and `--test-mode prefix --return-logprob`;
- a bitwise batch-size check: `single`'s batches (the same prompt repeated 1 to 50 times, 1,275 responses), requesting logprobs and comparing every response's token IDs and selected-token logprobs with the batch-size-1 response, exact equality.

| Model | TP | single | prefix | prefix logprobs | radix_cache | bitwise (token IDs and logprobs) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-8B | 1 | 1 output | 1 per prompt | identical | pass | 1,275 / 1,275 |
| Qwen3-8B | 2 | 1 output | 1 per prompt | identical | pass | 1,275 / 1,275 |
| Qwen3-8B | 4 | 1 output | 1 per prompt | identical | pass | 1,275 / 1,275 |
| Qwen3-8B | 8 | 1 output | 1 per prompt | identical | pass | 1,275 / 1,275 |
| Qwen3.8-27B | 1 | 1 output | 1 per prompt | identical | pass | 1,275 / 1,275 |
| Qwen3.8-27B | 2 | 1 output | 1 per prompt | identical | pass | 1,275 / 1,275 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B (MoE) | 1 | 1 output | 1 per prompt | identical | pass | 1,275 / 1,275 |
| Qwen3-8B, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` | 1 | 1 output | 1 per prompt | identical | pass | 1,275 / 1,275 |
| Qwen3.8-27B, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` | 1 | 1 output | 1 per prompt | identical | pass | 1,275 / 1,275 |

The TP1 Qwen3-8B row was repeated on two more fresh servers with this PR's final code, with the same result.

Long contexts: `test_deterministic`'s prompts stay near 1k tokens (at most about 4 KV partitions per request). So we also sent 8k, 12k and 16k-token prompts (token IDs), each alone twice and in one batch with 12 other requests of 64-4,096 tokens, with 4 different sets of batchmates, and compared the generated token IDs and logprobs exactly with the first batch-of-1 result: identical in 15 / 15 comparisons for Qwen3-8B at TP1 and TP2 and for Qwen3.8-27B at TP1.

GSM8K (`sgl-eval`, all 1,319 questions, temperature 0, thinking off), Triton decode / AITER decode: Qwen3-8B 93.56% / 93.48%; Qwen3-30B-A3B 94.77% / 94.39%; Qwen3.8-27B 96.06% / 95.83%.

A per-layer check at TP1 and TP2 (Qwen3-8B; batch sizes 2-50 and mixed batches; forward hooks hashing each op's inputs and outputs) found no op whose output changed while its input was bitwise equal; attention was compared 5,940 times in decode per rank.

`--test-mode p_vs_d` (prefill vs decode logprobs of the same tokens) differs, as it does with Triton for both phases; it is not part of the AMD deterministic CI.

Unit tests, `python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/test_model_overrides.py -k deterministic` (MI350X, same image): with #44438 only, the new test fails (1 failed, 6 passed); with this PR, 6 passed.

With this PR applied, a Qwen3-8B server with the command above starts with AITER decode and Triton prefill (radix cache on) and passes a short bitwise batch check; with `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1` it refuses to start with the new error; with `--speculative-algorithm NGRAM` it is refused: "... but --decode-attention-backend is 'aiter' (aiter decode is accepted only on gfx950, for non-MLA models and without speculative decoding)". With only `--prefill-attention-backend triton --decode-attention-backend aiter` (no `--attention-backend`) the server starts with AITER decode and Triton prefill; `--attention-backend` itself then resolves to the existing deterministic default (`fa3`), which only the per-phase backends override.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

| Qwen3-8B | 8 | 1k/1k | 12,356.0 | 15,627.0 | **1.27x** | 16.0 / 11.6 ms |
| Qwen3-8B | 8 | 8k/1k | 2,907.8 | 3,795.3 | **1.31x** | 22.3 / 12.0 ms |
| Qwen3.8-27B | 1 | 1k/1k | 1,811 | 2,032 | **1.12x** | 46.6 / 39.2 ms |
| Qwen3.8-27B | 2 | 1k/1k | 3,833 | 4,332 | **1.13x** | 49.7 / 42.0 ms |

Qwen3.8-27B gains less because only a quarter of its layers use attention (the rest are Gated DeltaNet). title: [Perf] qwen3: Fuse SiLU*mul with the NVFP4 quantization of down_proj in Qwen2MLP
author: gkswns0531
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Qwen3.5's dense MLP runs SiLU*mul and the NVFP4 quantization of the down_proj input as one FlashInfer kernel. Qwen3 uses `Qwen2MLP`, which lacks that path, so its NVFP4 W4A4 MLPs write the activation in 16 bits (`act_and_mul`) and read it back (`fp4_quantize`).

## Modifications

- Move the fused call and its enabling check from `Qwen2MoeMLP` / `qwen3_5.py` to `models/utils.py` and give `Qwen2MLP` the same branch, enabled only by `Qwen3DecoderLayer` when both projections use ModelOpt NVFP4 W4A4. Other `Qwen2MLP` users are unchanged.
- Keep it off where down_proj cannot use the fused output. Qwen3.5's dense MLP shares these checks, so it gets them too.
  - NVFP4 AWQ: the fused kernel skips `pre_quant_scale` (#38864 adds the same check to the Qwen3.5 copy).
  - The Marlin FP4 GEMM backend, the default on SM80-SM90: it takes a floating-point input.
  - A down_proj K that is not a multiple of 64: the fused kernel leaves the padded scale columns unwritten.
  - Per forward, sequence parallelism or a LoRA-wrapped down_proj: both read the activation tensor (as `DualGemm.can_run` does). Without the LoRA check, a Qwen3 NVFP4 server with a down_proj adapter fails at startup.
- CPU unit tests for each gate, and that the fusion turns on for W4A4.

## Accuracy Tests

- The fused FP4 data and block scales are bit-identical to the two-kernel path (M = 128 to 40960, intermediate size 9728).
- `Qwen3-Embedding-4B` NVFP4 on 60 questions each of Ko-StrategyQA / MIRACL-ko: Recall@10 0.876 / 0.767 and the distance to BF16 scores are identical to main.
- `Qwen3-Reranker-4B` NVFP4 as a causal LM (CUDA graphs on), and `Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B` NVFP4 with a down_proj LoRA adapter: greedy outputs match main.
- On an L4 (SM89, `auto` picks Marlin), greedy outputs and logprobs match main (`Qwen3-Reranker` 0.6B and 4B NVFP4).
- `test_qwen3_5_modelopt_fp4.py`: 15 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), FlashInfer 0.7.1. `Qwen3-Embedding-4B` NVFP4, GPU time of one `encode` call on 128 sequences:

| 128 sequences | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 320 tokens | 455.6 ms | **419.0 ms** (-8.0%) |
| 640 tokens | 925.1 ms | **844.2 ms** (-8.7%) |

Decode throughput of `Qwen3-Reranker-4B` NVFP4 at batch 1 / 16 / 64 is unchanged.

<details>
<summary>The kernels alone (CUPTI, cold L2), SiLU*mul + NVFP4 quantization of a [M, 2 x 9728] BF16 input</summary>

| M | `silu_and_mul` + `fp4_quantize` | fused |
|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 28.4 us | 9.4 us |
| 8192 | 444.1 us | 249.9 us |
| 40960 | 2294.8 us | 1251.9 us |

</details>

title: [Fix] diffusion: stabilize FLUX.3 serving and reuse static conditioning
author: mickqian
body:
Follow-up to #44418, now merged. Latest `origin/main` (`09b7383624c1`) is merged into this branch; the PR now contains only the serving fixes, hoisting, tests and cookbook updates.

## Changes
- Stabilize reference SDPA priority across requests. A preceding DiT forward could otherwise switch the text encoder from cuDNN to memory-efficient attention, changing an identical request's output.
- Hoist invariant text/reference embeddings, modulations and positional preparation into request-owned state, extending the existing mode-block reuse. No model-global conditioning cache or new public knob.
- Check exact repeatability both before and after grouped requests and multi-output generation, without loosening assertions.
- Update measured deployment recipes and document TP/SP, streaming, consumer GPU and numerical-validation boundaries. Keep untested resource shapes explicitly unverified.

## Validation
- H200 after merging current main: **81 tests and 21 subtests passed** across native DiT, quantized loading, served configuration, stages, VAE, SDPA priority and normalization dispatch.
- Fresh H200 server: real Base T2I/I2I, concurrent requests, `n=2`, immediate/final repeated requests, and mixed-size multi-reference edits pass.
- Pre-commit, cookbook config validation and 64 generated command combinations pass.

### Hoisting A/B

Same H200, Base BF16 checkpoint `d8acde427a698bdb98b5c1c941c60fa4c97e9f28`, Torch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0, Torch SDPA, eager, all components resident. Both arms include the SDPA-priority fix. Batch 1, 1024x1024 output/reference, 50 steps, CFG 3.5, exact-quality PNG; two prompts/seeds and two timed repetitions after warmup. Local HTTP submission through client PNG decoding; loading and warmup excluded.

| Workload | Existing partial hoist | Full hoist | Runtime peak allocated, before / after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| T2I | 7.2853 s | 7.2844 s | 22265.63 / 22263.13 MiB |
| I2I | 15.2640 s | 15.0395 s | 22267.76 / 22265.26 MiB |

T2I is effectively unchanged; I2I latency is 1.47% lower in this small sample. These are allocator peaks, not node-wide NVML totals. Both arms repeat exactly internally; cross-arm outputs are **not bit-exact** (SSIM 0.9957-0.9989, MAD 0.158-0.373 / 255 across four PNGs). Component tests cover the unchanged function, not official full-checkpoint accuracy.

## Follow-up Experiments
- [x] Matched hoisting E2E latency/memory comparison.
- [x] Measured recipe and numerical-boundary documentation.
- [x] Matched GB300 FlashInfer 0.7.1 versus 0.7.2rc3, with matching cubin packages; no change to the main dependency pin.
- [x] NVFP4 startup-LoRA generation and unload/restore check on merged-main head `f674e9537bb`: synthetic rank 4, 512x512, 8 steps. Startup and API-applied adapters agree exactly; adapted output changes, repeats exactly, and unloading restores the same generic-layout base output exactly. API memory release succeeds.
- [ ] CI on the latest follow-up head.

Official Diffusers parity remains deferred as requested.

### FlashInfer version A/B

Single GB300, same code `78f3ef2182a`, Torch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0, FA4, eager, all components resident, batch 1, exact quality, PNG. Base revision `17333191c36bae1b61b0a247e33ba284f1df07fa`; distilled revision `875076bf83d4364b68dccdbf8307f4f01475f68d`. Base: 50 steps/CFG 3.5; distilled: 16 steps/no CFG. 1024x1024 output and reference; two prompts/seeds, two timed repeats after warming each request shape. HTTP submission through client PNG decoding, excluding loading/warmup/JIT. Only one server generates at a time. FlashInfer Python and cubin versions match in each environment; no version-check suppression or jit-cache package.

| Checkpoint / precision | T2I 0.7.1 / 0.7.2rc3 | I2I 0.7.1 / 0.7.2rc3 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Base BF16 | 3.200 / 3.208 s | 6.261 / 6.280 s |
| Base FP8R | 2.156 / 2.172 s | 4.424 / 4.448 s |
| Base NVFP4 | 2.120 / 1.932 s | 4.255 / 3.921 s |
| Distilled BF16 | 0.688 / 0.688 s | 1.298 / 1.302 s |
| Distilled FP8R | 0.676 / 0.665 s | 1.012 / 1.015 s |
| Distilled NVFP4 | 0.615 / 0.640 s | 0.974 / 0.918 s |

All 24 version-paired PNGs match pixel-for-pixel, each arm repeats exactly, and per-server runtime peak allocated memory is unchanged in all 12 workload rows. This does not make FP8R/NVFP4 lossless relative to BF16. Base NVFP4 improves by 8.88% T2I / 7.84% I2I; distilled NVFP4 T2I instead regresses by 4.05% in this sample. BF16 and FP8R show no consistent material gain. Keep the stable dependency pin rather than requiring an RC globally for this model-specific benefit.

Both performance experiments leave cuDNN TF32 and BF16 reduced-precision reduction at their enabled runtime defaults. They are matched SGLang-path comparisons, not a strict FP32 or official-reference accuracy claim.

title: [Fix] step5: Register Step5 HiCache pool names in the Rust tree core
author: alphabetc1
body:
`_reduce_prefetch_ack` passes every Python `PoolName` member to the Rust tree core, but `parse_pool_name` does not know the three Step5 pools. The first L3 prefetch commit then crashes every scheduler with `ValueError: unknown pool name: step5_fp8_k_scale` (BF16 KV included). This adds `step5_compressed_index_key`, `step5_fp8_k_scale` and `step5_fp8_v_scale` to the Rust `PoolName`.

Verified on Step-5-Preview, 4x GB300 TP4, BF16 KV, HiCache + Mooncake L3: greedy outputs on storage hits match device hits bit for bit (8/8), and no scheduler crash. Before the fix it crashed on the first storage prefetch.

title: [Fix] runtime: Version FlashInfer caches for default-tactic tuning.
author: leejnau
body:
## Motivation

#43927 enables FlashInfer v2's default-tactic (`-1`) comparison on cache misses. Existing v1 winners are accepted before that comparison, and their cache paths did not change. Version the cache identity so fresh startup retunes these configurations with the expanded candidate set.

This continues v2 candidate-selection adoption with existing v1 persistence.

## Modifications

Add a stable `candidate_selection=v2_default` component to the existing cache key.

All previous cache files become cold once, including caches created since #43927 and MegaMoE namespaced records sharing the file. Existing files remain untouched for rollback; subsequent startups reuse the new namespace through the existing v1 load/save path.

Measurement policy remains unspecified. Cache-disabled behavior, skip controls, streams, and distributed synchronization are unchanged. No managed-store migration or MegaMoE integration changes.

## Accuracy Tests

- Current head `6a32decdb5a216b53f35cfb53659308f223da91c`: existing registered autotune suite **12 tests in 19.625 seconds; 11 passed, 1 CUDA-only skipped**. macOS arm64, Python 3.12.12, Torch 2.14.1, installed FlashInfer 0.7.1.
- Applicable commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed. No new unit test is included in the final diff.
- [Newest-head Base H100 FP8 accuracy](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38825807936/job/116737629686): **2 tests passed in 139.761 seconds**, zero skips; standard and Rust frontend GSM8K scores **0.755** and **0.745**, 200 examples each, required **> 0.70**. Actual checkout `55eb0808e8ca008163a7fa10ff59c4bb2d9a1be3` merges this PR head `6a32decdb5` into upstream `4cca7fcd3e644f22a61c7a6e6b57bb89b568d62a`. H100 80 GB, Torch 2.14.1, FlashInfer 0.7.1.
- [Earlier targeted H100 cache persistence](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38762530869/job/116517436033): existing target/draft cache-persistence case passed on prior head `332a055bae` (identical production code). This is historical validation, not a new-head rerun of that unit case.
- **Base status:** all 16 Stage A jobs and seven Stage B jobs passed. The H100 job above subsequently failed in `TestRustMmMMMU.tearDownClass`: its accuracy test passed, but `kill_process_tree` could not reap a process within 60 seconds after SIGKILL. Eleven other Stage B jobs then failed fast; Stage C was skipped. Full Base remains incomplete pending recovery of this cleanup failure; no retry has been triggered.
- **Coverage limits:** explicit eager/graph numerical comparison and controlled fresh-process cold/warm zero-profiling validation have not run. Passing FP8 startup/graph accuracy does not establish those additional properties.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance measurements or serving-performance claim. Upgrading incurs a one-time startup retune.
