title: [Feat] nemotron: Port Nemotron 3.5 Super serving changes
author: Jiminator
body:
## Summary

Bring Nemotron 3.5 Super MTP serving optimizations for SM120 into SGLang: small-M NVFP4 MoE execution, SM120 GEMV, FlashInfer host planning, and hybrid prefill CUDA graphs.

## Scope

- Native SM120 NVFP4 MoE for 1–4 token rows on Nemotron's expert shape, dispatched from the FlashInfer CUTLASS runner when FlashInfer's fused finalize is enabled. Unsupported shapes and quantization recipes keep the stock runner.
- Opt-in reversible pair-major FC2 weight layout for serial verify (`SGLANG_SM120_NVFP4_PHASE_LAYOUT`). Nemotron owns the layout, and the runner reaches it through an optional `prepare_for_forward` hook. Weight updates reuse the existing derived-cache guard, and weight export is rejected while the layout is enabled.
- The BF16 and FP8 GEMV kernels gain PDL and SM120-tuned launch shapes. `--bf16-gemm-backend gemv` is accepted on SM12x.
- An opt-in M=2–16 Triton router inside the existing fused-gate operator (`SGLANG_SM120_MTP_ROUTER_TOP22`), with unchanged device arithmetic.
- Opt-in FlashInfer host planning for EAGLE draft and verify (`SGLANG_FLASHINFER_DRAFT_HOST_INDPTR`, `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_VERIFY_HOST_PLAN`).
- Hybrid prefill CUDA graphs for Nemotron on SM120, with shared experts overlapped on one explicit stream.
- The logits processor, Eagle worker, top-k dispatcher and Mamba SSD kernels are unchanged from main.
- Upstream changes this PR previously carried are no longer part of it:
  - #34535 (DP request-split floor and DP decode-relabel fixes, with their tests) stays under its own review.
  - The #42746 prefill-then-decode regression test is dropped. Main already keeps fmha_v2 out of XQA's workspace semaphores through #42930, which superseded #42746.
  - #43685 (Nemotron-H EPLB) and #43054 (DFLASH verify mask policy) are in main. This PR relies on main's MoE `forward_batch` plumbing instead of duplicating it.
- The diff now contains **23 files, +1,825/−58 lines**, down from 38 files, +2,111/−80.

## Validation

For this revision (`4631e828b8`), only CPU and static checks were run, on macOS:
- `git diff --check`, the repository's pinned ruff 0.15.1 (hook rule selection and format check), isort 7.0.0, codespell 2.4.1, clang-format 20.1.7, `check-ast`, `debug-statements`, and the registered-test lint scripts all pass on the changed files.
- A focused CPU check confirms the Nemotron-H MoE decoder layers, including the MTP layer, still pass `forward_batch` to the MoE core (the input the SM120 prefill-overlap gate reads). Results match the previous head `d3f59dd9a6`.
- Eight CPU-registered Nemotron-H unit test files give identical results on this revision, the previous head and main. In each case 151 pass and 1 is skipped. The remaining 134 fail on all three in this Mac environment; sampled failures hit the Torch ≥ 2.13 MPS requirement (the available environment has Torch 2.11).

No GPU tests, E2E serving runs or benchmarks were run for this revision.

### Historical E2E evidence (not rerun)

The measurements below come from earlier heads, before main was merged (`d3f59dd9a6`) and before the carried upstream changes were removed. Both measured heads still included the carried changes. They compare the earlier public head `af2628444e` with the cleanup head `ce427d4d9b`. Both ran on the same RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), EA1008 NVFP4 checkpoint, pinned container, launch settings and request token IDs. Settings: TP=1, concurrency=1, real EAGLE acceptance (3 steps / 4 draft tokens). Each run has two warmups and 80 measured requests of 8,192 input / 1,024 output tokens, with the prefix cache flushed before every measured request.

| Check | `af2628444e` | `ce427d4d9b` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Output throughput | 243.6717 tokens/s | 242.6594 tokens/s |
| Mean TTFT | 845.7203 ms | 858.7892 ms |
| Mean TPOT | 3.2812 ms | 3.2856 ms |
| Mean acceptance length | 3.9798 | 3.9798 |
| Same fixed 100-question GSM8K slice | 95/100 | 95/100 |

Throughput changed by **-0.42%** and TTFT by **+13.07 ms (+1.55%)**. All 80 complete output-token sequences and all 100 GSM8K answer texts match exactly. Both runs had zero cached prompt tokens, zero request retractions, and no competing GPU process during measurement. The workload uses repeated text and has high acceptance. These results do not establish general conversational throughput or performance on other GPU architectures.

Earlier hardware recipes and model-support validation are recorded in [cookbook PR #44510](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44510).

title: [DSv4.1] Fuse request-window KV copies
author: Oasis-Git
body:
[codex/claude generated]

## Motivation

Encoder bounded replay copies packed request-window KV data and scales using advanced indexing, which materializes byte-index grids and launches multiple operations per layer. This adds substantial overhead when replaying long prefills.

## Modifications

- Copy each token's data and scales in one Triton kernel, respecting physical page strides and strided location arrays.
- Call the kernel directly for the existing GPU request-window path. Its state and workspace pools allocate separate packed uint8 buffers, so per-copy device, shape, stride, and storage-alias checks are unnecessary.
- Add byte-exact tests for both KV formats, page sizes, counts, padding, strided locations, and graph replay with changed locations.

## Accuracy Tests

Local validation covers 2 GPU tests (including 48 layout/page/count subcases), 5 encoder-replay tests, and 13 compressed-pool tests. Copies are compared byte-for-byte against an independent reference. Workload records were checked for expected cache accounting and output lengths. These synthetic replay checks are not model-quality evaluations; no GSM8K/MMLU result is claimed.

The performance-tested patch is based on `f2b73d4f9b4e64415b8d775b0f811c7801f1728b`. The PR is transplanted onto `bba535ebb4d176c6bf8361619e0c29fa263642fe`; focused validation is repeated there. Pre-commit passes locally. GitHub CI has not been run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4x GB300, TP4/EP1, FlashMLA, chunked prefill 16384, memory fraction 0.8, max running requests 128, prefill CUDA graphs disabled. DSPARK uses block size 5 and simulated acceptance 5.4; decoder bounded replay is disabled. Runtime: PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.1, fastokens 0.3.4.

Unchanged synthetic high-load subset: 816 scheduled arrivals over 300 seconds, client concurrency cap 64, 891,421 total output tokens in each run. Measurements below use the same base revision and workload; this is a fixed-arrival replay, not maximum-throughput or semantic-accuracy testing.

| Configuration | Median TTFT (ms) | p95 TTFT (ms) | Median E2E (ms) | p95 E2E (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Encoder replay, original copy | 524.70 | 2089.57 | 8692.07 | 54291.49 |
| Encoder replay, fused copy | 395.92 | 1687.73 | 3397.61 | 19216.46 |
| Encoder replay, fused copy repeat | 393.83 | 1748.74 | 3390.33 | 19603.67 |

Both candidate runs reduce median E2E latency by approximately 61% and median TTFT by approximately 25%. Low-load serial replay completed 895 requests before versus 1152/1148 after within 300 seconds.

Encoder replay disabled remains faster: median TTFT 343.42 ms, median E2E 2443.99 ms, p95 E2E 13863.49 ms, and 1280 low-load completions. This patch reduces copy overhead; it does not eliminate the remaining replay regression. Full performance runs have not been repeated on the newer PR base.

title: [Fix] dsa-eagle-topk: Copy token keys and scales when relocating index cache
author: sshleifer
body:
Fix for dsa with speculative_eagle_topk=2


## Motivation

`DSATokenToKVPool.move_kv_cache` passes token-slot IDs to `IndexKeyCache.move`, but that method indexes its page buffer with them. With 64-token pages, slot 319 is page 4, offset 63; treating it as page 319 can access out of bounds. Small IDs that fit in the page dimension silently copy entire pages and overwrite unrelated keys.

This matters when speculative decoding relocates accepted tree tokens. The ordinary single-chain (`speculative_eagle_topk=1`) path skips that compaction.

## Modifications

Move each selected token's FP8 index key and scale within the physical-page view used by the cache writers and readers. Advanced-index gathering before assignment preserves overlapping swaps. Layers that reuse another layer's indexer remain skipped.

Nonempty moves with pooled index keys (`index_kpool > 1`) now fail explicitly: relocating individual tokens would require rebuilding their pooled keys.

## Accuracy Tests

On upstream main `87211088c98ae4f5b60625eebcce007db36aa6af`, the new small-ID regression fails: swapping slots 1 and 2 corrupts neighboring keys without a CUDA error. With this patch, all three GPU cases pass on one GB300:

- Small token IDs that previously selected whole pages.
- Cross-page overlapping swaps, including the final allocated slot.
- Empty moves.

The tests use a real DSA pool and its production key/scale writers and readers, checking exact key bytes, scales, unchanged neighbors, latent KV, and a layer that reuses another layer's indexer.

```bash
python -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_dsa_index_cache_move.py
# 3 passed
```

These are cache correctness tests; no full-model branching-speculation accuracy run was performed for this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Correctness fix; no performance claim or benchmark.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit (all applicable hooks passed).
- [x] Add and register GPU regression tests.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style.
- Documentation: no user-facing configuration change.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] scheduler: Pageable host staging and inline hidden-state/DSpark readback under Confidential Computing
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to the async device->host readback worker for NVIDIA Confidential Computing (CC). Two things it left on the table:

1. **Host staging stayed pinned.** Under CC host<->device copies go through a bounce buffer; this change selects pageable staging there through `is_pin_memory_available()`.
2. **Two batch kinds must not take the worker.** Batches that return hidden states, and DSpark batches, read views of CUDA graph buffers that the next replay rewrites. Only a copy queued right behind the forward on `copy_stream` reads them in time; a copy issued later from the worker thread can race the next replay.

## Modifications

- `is_pin_memory_available()` answers `False` under CC. `async_d2h()` already falls back to a pageable copy when it does, so the overlap scheduler's readback buffers and every other staged copy are pageable there. Off CC nothing changes: staging stays pinned.
- Both scheduler submit sites (`run_batch` and `launch_batch_sample_if_needed`) go through one `_copy_result_to_cpu` helper. Under CC it hands the readback to the worker unless the batch returns hidden states or runs DSpark; those stay inline on `copy_stream`, as before the worker existed.
- The prefill result-polling scheduler fake borrows the helper, as it already borrows `launch_batch_sample_if_needed`.

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/managers/test_async_d2h_copy_worker.py` gains two cases:

- `TestConfidentialComputeStaging`: `async_d2h` lands in pageable memory with the force override on and pinned memory with it off.
- `TestSchedulerReadbackRouting`: the source tensor is written behind a long `torch.cuda._sleep`, so a readback that does not wait for the forward reads zeros. Under CC only the plain batch gets a `HostCopyDone`; hidden-state and DSpark batches keep a CUDA event, and every host buffer is pageable. Each case was verified to fail with the corresponding branch removed.

Ran on a single GPU: the whole file (8 tests) and `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_result_polling.py` (20 tests) pass; `ruff`, `ruff format`, `isort` and `codespell` are clean with the repository's configuration. No CC host was available, so the behaviour under real CC was not measured here.

title: [Fix] attention: Opt FlashMLA scheduler into dynamic shared memory
author: Oasis-Git
body:
[codex/claude generated]

## Motivation

The FlashMLA scheduling kernel can fail with `CUDA error: invalid argument` near its accepted shared-memory limit. Its guard permits up to 48 KiB of dynamic shared memory, but the kernel also declares static shared memory. Without explicit opt-in, the combined allocation can exceed the default launch allowance.

On GB300 (152 SMs), a standalone call with 2,211 rows succeeds, while 2,212 rows requests 49,108 dynamic bytes and fails. The existing guard permits up to 2,214 rows. This reproducer calls only the scheduling kernel, independently of request-window KV copying.

## Modifications

- Use the existing per-device initialization helper to opt the kernel into 48 KiB of dynamic shared memory before launch.
- Preserve the schedule algorithm and existing dynamic-memory bound.
- Add four boundary cases validating schedule entries and split offsets against independently calculated expectations.

## Accuracy Tests

All 41 scheduling tests passed locally on GB300: 37 existing tests and four boundary cases. Existing coverage compares metadata with FlashMLA and checks attention-output parity where applicable. Pre-commit passes.

The patch applies to main at `91f6ef232`; the affected kernel, runtime helper, and existing test file are unchanged from the tested base. GitHub CI has not been run for this fix.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speedup is claimed. Initialization uses the existing per-device cache to avoid setting the attribute on every launch.

A longer AgentX run previously failed at this scheduling launch. The standalone failure is reproduced and fixed, but the original log did not record the failing shape, and the full AgentX run has not yet been repeated. This PR does not claim end-to-end workload recovery.

title: [Perf] unified-memory: Prewarm the compaction move at startup and copy whole page envelopes by page id
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

The first compaction of the unified memory pool pays its first-use costs while serving: the move kernel compiles and loads, the commit's `.all()` reduction and `_assert_async` run for the first time, and the kernel's first launch can need device memory outside every pool (the context's local-memory reservation for a spilling kernel). When that first compaction is an urgent one under a full pool, the launch fails with `Triton Error [CUDA]: out of memory` and the scheduler goes down with it. Even when it does not fail, the first-use work stalls the scheduler loop.

## Modifications

- **Startup prewarm.** `MultiEndedAllocator.prewarm_compaction()` runs the compaction commit's first-use work once at startup, on the reserved sink page 0 (a two-entry self-copy, so the `.all()` reduction kernel a real commit uses actually launches), and synchronizes. The scheduler calls it right after `init_memory_pools()` under `--enable-unified-memory`, before attention backend init, graph capture and post-capture KV sizing, so whatever it allocates is accounted like any other startup allocation. CPU pools return immediately. The hybrid-SWA and Mamba composites fan out to every member that compacts.
- **Whole-envelope page moves.** `UnifiedMHATokenToKVPool`, `UnifiedMLATokenToKVPool` and `UnifiedMambaPool` gain `move_physical_pages(tgt_pages, src_pages, page_size)`. The MHA and MLA versions go straight to the existing `copy_pages` kernel, which addresses each page envelope in-kernel and allocates nothing; the Mamba version moves state slots (one slot per page). `page_size` must equal the pool's own page size (asserted). The token-id `move_kv_cache` methods stay and delegate to it. The per-token index expansion (`pages[:, None] * ps + offsets`) in both compaction paths is gone.
- **Bounded launches.** `MultiEndedAllocator._move_pages` issues a move as consecutive launches of at most `SGLANG_COMPACTION_MAX_PAGES_PER_MOVE` pages (new env, default 4096, clamped to the pool's page count) within the same call, so an urgent compaction above the cap still completes before it returns. Copies are issued before the v2p/p2v remap on the same stream, so work ordered after the remap sees the moved pages.
- **One kernel variant.** `copy_pages` no longer specializes on the alignment of its page-id pointers (`do_not_specialize_on_alignment`): each program loads one scalar id, and a chunk slice at an odd element offset would otherwise compile a new variant mid-serving. The kernel now specializes on neither the move size (a grid dimension) nor the page-id alignment, so the startup launch selects the variant every serving-time move of that sub-pool uses.
- Test fakes and patch targets follow the renamed contract (`move_physical_pages`).

## Accuracy Tests

No numerics change: each moved page is the same envelope the previous path copied row by row, now copied once as a whole.

- CPU-only (`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified*.py`, `test_multi_ended_allocator.py`, `test_kv_index_translator_draft_disposition.py`, `test_dense_fused_draft_geometry.py`): all pass with this change applied.
- GPU smoke on one CUDA device with real unified full+SWA pools at page sizes 1, 16 and 128: `prewarm_compaction()` runs; a chunked `_move_pages` (cap 3 pages per launch, 7 pages moved, 3 launches) and the delegating token-id `move_kv_cache` both reproduce the torch reference bytes exactly, untouched pages are unchanged, and a page-size mismatch is rejected.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The move step is now one `copy_pages` launch per chunk of page ids and no index temporaries, instead of a per-move token-id expansion plus a per-(layer, token) row copy. The first compaction while serving no longer compiles, loads or allocates.

author: hnyls2002
body:
- Add `async_h2d_stack(tensors, *, device)` next to `async_h2d`: stacks per-request host tensors straight into pinned memory and moves them with one non-blocking copy; tensors already on a device are stacked there
- `build_eagle_disagg_draft_input`: `topk_p`, `topk_index`, `hidden_states` and the DSA seed rows go through `async_h2d_stack` instead of a per-request `torch.as_tensor(..., device=...)` / pageable `.to(device)` from the unpinned CPU metadata buffers
- `prepare_for_prebuilt`: `req_pool_indices`, `seq_lens` and `orig_seq_lens` go through `async_h2d` instead of `torch.tensor(list, device=...)`; `process_prebuilt` builds `last_tokens_tensor` with `async_h2d` instead of the same pattern written inline

Each replaced copy ran `cudaStreamSynchronize` on the schedule stream, which under overlap blocks the host until the in-flight forward clears the schedule stream's wait.

No behavior change: the copied values, dtypes and devices are identical.

Verification: on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, PD decode, EAGLE (3 steps, topk 1), TP4, 128 concurrent requests, step time is unchanged on its own (32.2 ms before and after), since an earlier blocking copy in decode preallocation absorbs the same wait; the host-side syncs in these functions are gone. `test_disaggregation_wire.py` and `test_pd_eagle_draft_proposal.py` pass.

title: [Test] [AMD] diffusion: Make multimodal_gen unit tests ROCm-aware
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## What

Seven multimodal_gen unit test files that landed recently fail on MI300 because they assume a CUDA host. Test-only changes; CUDA behavior of every test is unchanged.

Failing jobs: [scheduled run on main](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38563492873), and the AMD jobs on #44421 ([partition 0](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38755083928/job/116491534023), [1](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38755083928/job/116491534135), [2](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38755083928/job/116491534103), [3](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38755083928/job/116491534226)).

## Why, per test

- `test_flux3_prims_ts_config.py` (#44418): imports `flashinfer.prims_ts` at module level. ROCm images don't ship flashinfer, so collection errors and the whole unit-test step of that partition stops. Now `pytest.importorskip`.
- `test_rowwise_fp8.py::TestFp8LinearMethodRowwise` (#44418): hands `Fp8LinearMethod.apply` a raw OCP `float8_e4m3fn` weight. On ROCm, FP8 weights only reach `apply` after the loader converts them (fnuz / preshuffle), so aiter asserts and the hipBLASLt fallback returns `HIPBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`. Skipped on ROCm.
- `test_qwen3_5_encoder.py::test_text_attention_default_and_explicit_selection[fa]` (#44325): the ROCm platform resolves FA to SDPA, so the backend assert fails. Skipped on ROCm, same as the Kandinsky6 FA case in #44421.
- `test_residual_gate_add2.py` (#44418): fp16 output of the scalar path (hidden 250) is not bit-identical to `torch.addcmul` on MI300. CUDA still asserts `torch.equal`; ROCm now uses `assert_close` with dtype defaults.
- `test_flux3_image_dit_quant.py` (#44418): building the tiny DiT constructs attention layers that read the SP group size, but the file never initializes one. It only passes when an earlier test in the same process left the group set up. Now uses the `single_process_model_parallel` fixture, as `test_flux3_image_dit.py` does. Three cases reach the flashinfer-backed PrimsTS weight pack and are skipped when flashinfer is absent.
- `test_moss_image_parallel.py` (#44325): runs two CPU workers with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""`. On a ROCm build, importing sglang calls `is_gfx1250_supported()`, which reads GPU 0's properties and raises `No CUDA GPUs are available`. Skipped on ROCm.
- `test_kandinsky6_layerwise_offload.py[*-audio-vae]` (#42743, also fails on main): the offloaded fp32 audio VAE differs from the resident run by up to ~1.2e-6. ROCm uses `rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-5` for the forward outputs; the exact `state_dict` comparison after offload is unchanged.

## Notes for the reviewer

- The residual-gate kernel's docstring promises bit-identity with `addcmul`. That holds on CUDA but not on MI300 for fp16 in at least the scalar path. The kernel's ROCm behavior should get a look from its owner; this PR only stops the test from blocking ROCm CI.
- `is_gfx1250_supported()` (and its gfx942/gfx95 siblings) query the device at import time, so importing sglang on a ROCm build with no visible GPU fails. That is a product issue outside this PR.
- I did not confirm the cause of the audio VAE drift (likely conv algorithm selection, since the DiT components stay bit-exact).

## Test plan

- CUDA `multimodal-gen-unit-test` on the first commit: 5467 passed, 0 failed ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38824136906/job/116731491318)).
- MI300 on the first commit: `test_rowwise_fp8` skips its raw-FP8 case and the rest pass; the PrimsTS config file no longer stops partition 2, which surfaced the last two files above. The remaining failures in those jobs are the Kandinsky6 FA and FastH3 cases fixed by #44421.
- MI300 on the second commit ([partition 2](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38856869315/job/116830298549)): `test_moss_image_parallel` skips, and every `test_flux3_image_dit_quant` case passes or skips except the SwiGLU layout case, which the third commit skips for the same flashinfer reason. Partitions 0 and 3 are green. The other failures in partitions 1 and 2 are the Kandinsky6 FA and FastH3 cases fixed by #44421.

title: [Perf] [AMD] monokernels: Let a plugin skip per-step attention metadata
author: kevin-mii
body:
## Motivation

A monokernel forward may never read some of the attention metadata a backend builds every step. sgl-amd-mono's DeepSeek-V4.1 forward scores every index source with K2i, so on each step it runs, the HIP radix backend builds the aiter decode schedule of each low ratio and nothing reads it. The build is recorded in the decode CUDA graph, so it runs on every replay.

Co-authored with @kkHuang-amd: this is kevin-mii/sglang#19 with the plugin contract stated as data.

## Modifications

- `monokernels/spec.py`: a `StepMetadata` enum and `MonoSpec.unread_metadata`, the per-step metadata a spec's forward never reads. It defaults to empty, so existing plugins are unchanged and the API version stays 1.
- `monokernels/runtime.py`: `is_metadata_unread(model, forward_batch, metadata)`, true only on a step the forward switch routes, for metadata the spec lists.
- `deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py`: the low-ratio decode schedule build skips a ratio when `is_metadata_unread`, next to the identity-rows filter. Without `--monokernel-backend`, every schedule is built as before.
- CPU test `test_only_routed_steps_skip_the_metadata_a_spec_never_reads`.

- `pyproject_other.toml`: the plugin pin moves into one `monokernels_hip` extra that `srt_hip` and `srt_hip_rocm724` both include, at sgl-amd-mono e07665c (sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono#5), whose DeepSeek-V4.1 spec declares the schedule unread. A bump is one line, and the two extras cannot disagree. #5 merged first; until this PR merges, plugin main's DeepSeek-V4.1 spec needs it (it imports `StepMetadata`).
- `docker/rocm.Dockerfile`: the plugin install step from #44621 checks out the commit pip installed through `monokernels_hip`, read from the plugin's `direct_url.json`, instead of its own pin; `SGL_AMD_MONO_COMMIT` stays as an optional override, and the step skips SGLang versions that do not install the plugin. The image and pip then install the same commit. The step's text, run with git and `pip install` stubbed but the real `pip show` and metadata read, covers the installed, not-installed, override, gfx942 and opt-out cases; the image itself was not built.

## Accuracy Tests

MI350X, TP4, sgl-amd-mono's `test/e2e` (9 tests) on DSpark (verify steps) and decode servers. KL is against the standard path's prefill (limits 0.03, long prompts 0.06):

| | main ec7ab9d0c2, plugin 8f1bff3 | main + kevin-mii/sglang#19 (ec43db1bff), plugin 3970534 | this PR (9fd4430dd3), sgl-amd-mono#5 (ae2f020) |
|---|---|---|---|
| DSpark GSM8K / KL / long-prompt KL | 0.915 / 0.0139 / 0.0273 | 0.910 / 0.0101 / 0.0284 | 0.905 / 0.0139 / 0.0244 |
| decode GSM8K / KL | 0.905 / 0.0103 | 0.905 / 0.0101 | 0.905 / 0.0115 |
| tests | 9 passed | 9 passed | 9 passed |

`test/registered/unit/monokernels`: 18 passed. The measurements ran at 9fd4430dd3; 212f36daa1 after it changes only a docstring, a comment and a test variable name, and a3a83ffc88 pins sgl-amd-mono e07665c, the same plugin code as ae2f020. 31e3031b74 merges main (with #44405 and #44630), and 958d06d3e9 pins the plugin once and has the image check out what pip installed; 29 CPU tests (`test/registered/unit/monokernels` and the CUDA graph config tests) pass on it. The e2e on b3e0ba62aa with sgl-amd-mono e07665c: 9 passed (DSpark GSM8K 0.910, KL 0.0123, long-prompt KL 0.0319; decode GSM8K 0.910, KL 0.0103).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Decode time per output token (ms), MI350X, TP4, DSpark with simulated acceptance 3.51, median of 3 rounds of 1024 tokens, one server per arm. Main is ec7ab9d0c2 with sgl-amd-mono 3970534; kevin-mii/sglang#19 is ec43db1bff with 3970534; this PR is 9fd4430dd3 with sgl-amd-mono#5 (ae2f020):

The two skip runs take the same path and differ by up to 2% at 4 requests, which is the noise. At 1 request both are faster: 0.4-0.5% at 8k and 1.8-2.9% at 128k.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Defer full GC collections while importing the runtime
author: rwang5203
body:
## Motivation

A diffusion scheduler process imports about ten thousand modules before it builds its pipeline. Imports create long-lived modules, classes and functions and very little garbage, yet CPython runs a full collection every time the surviving heap has grown by a quarter, and each one traces every tracked object again. A scheduler process runs 12 of them during startup, which together take about 1.6 seconds of CPU, with or without compiled bytecode.

Where those collections fall also depends on the import order rather than on the work done. Moving an import, for example to load a module on first use, can add or remove a whole-heap collection inside a given span of startup, which makes import time changes hard to judge.

## Modifications

- `runtime/utils/process.py` gains `defer_full_gc_for_imports()`, a context manager that raises the third GC threshold so that no automatic full collection runs inside the block. Young collections keep running, so short-lived cyclic garbage is freed as usual. Restoring the original thresholds lets automatic full collections resume after the block. On CPython 3.14.0–3.14.4, which uses incremental GC and ignores the third threshold, the context manager is a no-op.
- On exit it restores the thresholds it found, also when the block raises. Nested and concurrent blocks restore them when the last one exits, a child forked inside a block restores them at fork, and the collector's enabled state is never changed, so a process that disabled the collector keeps it disabled.
- It is used where diffusion processes import their runtime in bulk, in the activation phase of `bootstrap_scheduler_process` (platform initialization through the `gpu_worker` import), the activation phase of `bootstrap_http_server_process`, and pipeline and config discovery in the registry. Pipeline discovery enters the block only on its first run, so the registry lookups that return early touch nothing.
- No new option, and nothing changes for srt.

Two simpler forms were measured first and not used. `gc.disable()` over the same blocks saved the same CPU, but it also stops young collections, so about 7 MB of short-lived cyclic garbage (frames of caught exceptions, closures, package metadata structures) stayed alive until the block ended, which showed up as 8 MiB more anonymous memory in the HTTP server child. `gc.freeze()` after the imports would keep import-time objects out of every later collection, but frozen objects are never collected again, so it changes steady-state serving memory, and freezing after warmup is the existing pattern for that.

## Accuracy Tests

No output path changes. Only the timing of garbage collections during startup imports changes.

`test_process.py` checks that full collection is deferred where the collector supports threshold2, that incremental GC is left unchanged on CPython 3.14.0–3.14.4, and that nesting, exception exits with GC disabled, and forked children restore the correct state. The file passes on CPython 3.11.16, 3.12.15, 3.13.15, 3.14.0, 3.14.4, and 3.14.5; only the threshold2-specific collection assertion is skipped on 3.14.0–3.14.4. The earlier CPU diffusion-unit comparison had the same per-test outcomes as the base, apart from the added GC coverage.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Measured on a CPU-only host with scripts that start each process the way it starts in a server, without touching a device. A scheduler child runs through `bootstrap_scheduler_process` up to the point where `build_pipeline` would construct the pipeline, and the `--webui` HTTP child runs through `bootstrap_http_server_process` up to `create_app`. After each run, the same process allocates 100,000 objects so that any collection this change postpones is paid inside the measurement. Each process ran once with compiled bytecode present, as in an installed package, and once with every module compiled from source.

The comparison ran as eight counterbalanced pairs with a local Cosmos3 Nano checkpoint, then eight fresh pairs with a local Wan2.1 T2V 1.3B checkpoint as an independent confirmation, each beside an A/A control that compared two separate copies of the base. A gain is listed only where both sets established it at 1 percent or more and the A/A control showed no difference. The table gives the mean change with this PR and its 95 percent interval over the pairs, for the Cosmos3 Nano and the Wan2.1 pairs.

| Process | Backend | Bytecode | CPU time | Wall time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| scheduler child | auto | compiled | -2.9 % [-3.3, -2.6] and -2.8 % [-3.5, -2.2] | -5.8 % [-6.5, -5.0] and -5.2 % [-6.4, -4.0] |
| scheduler child | auto | from source | -2.5 % [-2.6, -2.3] and -2.5 % [-2.9, -2.2] | -4.5 % [-5.1, -3.9] and -4.5 % [-5.5, -3.6] |
| scheduler child | sglang | compiled | -2.8 % [-3.5, -2.0] and -3.0 % [-3.2, -2.8] | -5.2 % [-6.6, -3.7] and -5.5 % [-6.2, -4.8] |
| scheduler child | sglang | from source | -2.7 % [-3.2, -2.2] and -2.8 % [-3.2, -2.4] | -4.8 % [-6.0, -3.6] and -5.2 % [-6.3, -4.1] |
| HTTP child (`--webui`) | auto | compiled | -2.2 % [-2.7, -1.6] and -2.9 % [-3.4, -2.4] | -4.7 % [-6.0, -3.5] and -5.6 % [-6.7, -4.6] |
| HTTP child (`--webui`) | auto | from source | -2.8 % [-3.2, -2.3] and -2.6 % [-3.0, -2.2] | no claim |

In absolute terms the scheduler child uses about 0.7 s less CPU, out of about 26 to 28 s, and reaches the point where it would build its pipeline 0.7 to 0.8 s sooner. It runs 8 full collections instead of 12 in every run, and spends about 0.8 s less in garbage collection. The HTTP child wall time from source has no claim because the A/A control of the Wan2.1 pairs read a difference of -0.53 % [-1.05, -0.02] on that metric.

No performance claim for the launcher and HTTP frontend process, where no full collection falls inside the blocks this change covers. In every process measured, including the launcher, anonymous memory (`Pss_Anon`), peak RSS (`VmHWM`), minor page faults and the number of full collections read no worse than without this change.

### Additional real-server check

Compared base `b234b5c32e0d` with `04c42400522d` on one H200 (143771 MiB), Xeon Platinum 8558P, driver 595.71.05, Python 3.12.15, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0, and Diffusers 0.37.0. The native SGLang backend used FA3, speed mode, GPU-resident components, and no torch.compile or CUDA graphs.

Model: `Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers`, revision `0fad780a534b6463e45facd96134c9f345acfa5b`. Server warmup: 256×256, 9 frames, one step. First API request: the same shape, two steps, seed 42, CFG 5, prompt “A small red boat floating on a calm lake.” We timed readiness via `/health` and the first completed `/v1/videos` job, polling every 100 ms. Checkpoint download and kernel priming were excluded. A/B/B/A order, two measured starts per revision; means below:

| Measurement | Base | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Process start → server ready | 41.97 s | 41.47 s |
| Process start → first request completed | 42.28 s | 41.78 s |
| First request after readiness | 0.309 s | 0.309 s |

All four output MP4s were byte-identical. This small sample observed about 0.50 s (1.2%) lower complete startup latency, not a general speedup guarantee. It does not establish a steady-state inference speedup. The scheduler and HTTP bootstrap ordering tests also passed.

title: [Perf] deepseek_v4: size the masked silu-mul-quant grid to the GPU, not the padded capacity
author: Monishver11
body:
## Motivation In short: the DeepSeek-V4 masked SiLU-mul-quant kernel runs on every MoE layer of DeepEP low-latency decode, and it launches one CTA for every row the padded DeepEP buffer could hold. At decode almost none of those rows are real, so most CTAs only scan the per-expert counts and exit. On the Flash TP4 shape that is 24,576 CTAs for about 400 real rows, and on H100 the kernel takes 15.9 us even with zero real rows. This PR sizes the grid to the GPU instead: 17.1 -> 3.3 us at 64 decode tokens per GPU, with bit-identical output. Details: `silu_and_mul_masked_post_quant` (`python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/silu_and_mul_masked_post_quant.cuh`) runs the SiLU-mul + FP8 quant between the two masked DeepGEMM GEMMs on the DeepEP low-latency path. DeepSeek-V4 takes it on every decode MoE layer because of its `swiglu_limit` (10.0 in the Flash config), through `_varlen_deep_gemm_silu_mul_quant` in `moe_runner/deep_gemm.py`. That covers the DeepEP balanced and high-throughput recipes in the DSV4 cookbook (B200/B300/GB200/GB300 FP4 with `--moe-a2a-backend deepep`, and the H200 FP8 ones). The input is the DeepEP buffer `[E_local, T, 2D]`, where T is the padded per-expert capacity (`SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` x ranks) and `masked_m[e]` (on the GPU) says how many rows of expert e are real. The host can't read `masked_m` without a sync, so the kernel launched `T * topk` CTAs, one per possible real row. Every CTA loads `masked_m`, does a block prefix scan with 2 `__syncthreads`, and then all but the CTAs that own a real row exit. On the Flash B200 TP4 recipe that is `4096 * 6 = 24,576` CTAs per call, for about 400 real rows at 64 decode tokens per GPU. On H100 the kernel costs 15.9 us with zero real rows and 17.1 us at 64 tokens per GPU; almost all of it is empty CTAs going through the scheduler. ## Modifications In short: launch only as many CTAs as the GPU can hold at once, instead of one per possible row, and let each CTA loop over the real rows. The output is bit-identical to main. On H100 the kernel goes from 15.9 to 1.6 us with no real rows and from 17.1 to 3.3 us at 64 decode tokens per GPU (Flash TP4 shape), and every decode point up to the dispatch cap is faster (1.09x-16.25x). The one slower case is when every one of the `T * topk` rows is real, 2-4%, which uniform routing doesn't get near (details in Speed Tests). How it works: the host still can't read `masked_m`, so the grid stays fixed, but it is now one resident wave (1,056 CTAs on H100) instead of `T * topk` (24,576 on the Flash TP4 shape). Each CTA prefix-scans `masked_m` once, keeps the result in shared memory, and then takes rows `b, b + grid, b + 2 * grid, ...` of the flattened real-row list. At decode there are fewer real rows than CTAs, so each CTA handles at most one row, exactly like before, just without the other ~23,500 CTAs (24,576 - 1,056) that found no row. Changes, in simple terms: - Smaller grid: sized to the GPU, not to the padded capacity. - One `masked_m` scan per CTA, kept in shared memory, instead of one scan per possible row. - A loop over real rows in each CTA; the per-row math is the same code as before. - A new test that checks every real row matches the contig kernel and no padded row is written. Details: - Launch `min(SMs x resident CTAs, T * topk)` CTAs instead of `T * topk` (1,056 on H100 at 256 threads; about 1,184 on B200, not measured). Occupancy comes from `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor`, cached per block size. - Each CTA scans `masked_m` once into shared memory (`s_row_end`, inclusive prefix, 1 KB), exits before the PDL wait if it has no row, then walks the flattened real rows with a grid stride. A row's expert comes from a binary search over `s_row_end`. - The per-row body moved verbatim into `silu_mul_quant_varlen_row`, so the math and the output bytes don't change. The PDL wait now runs once before the loop; the trigger stays where it was in the row body. - `max_rows = T * topk` keeps the old implicit cap (rows past it were never processed before and still aren't). - New test `test_masked_post_quant_writes_exactly_the_real_rows`: masked vs contig kernel byte-equal on real rows, sentinel untouched on padded rows, for both scale layouts and all-zero / one hot expert / uneven / full `masked_m`. Capacity is 4x the resident CTAs so "full" makes each CTA loop over several rows. Same idea as vLLM's Silu v2 `persistent_masked_m_silu_mul_quant` ([vllm-project/vllm#25074](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/25074)): fixed grid, one scan of the counts per CTA into shared memory, then each CTA walks the real rows. Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this kernel's grid (searched `silu_and_mul_masked_post_quant`, `masked silu quant`, `silu_mul_quant_varlen`). [sgl-project/sglang#32066](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32066) adds a launch guard on the same launcher lines, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase. ## Accuracy Tests The output is bit-identical to main, so model accuracy can't change. I checked it at the kernel level instead of with an e2e eval: - Bitwise vs main, in one process (main's kernel built from the base file under its own namespace), CPU-seeded inputs, outputs pre-filled with a sentinel and compared as whole buffers including padded rows: **464 identical, 0 mismatched**. Matrix: 5 shapes (up to 256 experts, and a `full` case where `sum(masked_m) > T * topk` to check the cap), group size 32 and 128, 3 scale layouts (fp32, UE8M0, transposed packed UE8M0), swizzle on/off, swiglu_limit on/off, 4 `masked_m` patterns. - `test_per_token_group_quant.py`: 121 passed (8 new). `test_humming_fp8_dispatch.py` (the other caller): 2 passed. - The new test fails on each of 3 broken mappings (wrong loop stride, `>=` in the binary search, wrong row offset). - Registers: 32/thread before and after (`__launch_bounds__(1024, 2)` cap), 0 spills. ## Speed Tests and Profiling H100 80GB HBM3, driver 595.71.05, nvcc 13.2, torch 2.14.1+cu130, triton 3.8.0. Validated on main 97d3150a6a; the branch is rebased onto ed8c3139f1 and neither the kernel nor the test file changed upstream in between. `triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph` on the op, 2 interleaved rounds (main, PR, main, PR) in one process. Shapes from the DSV4 cookbook DeepEP recipes, group 128, swiglu_limit 10. Real rows come from uniform top-6 routing at the given decode tokens per GPU, up to the dispatch cap; "all real" sets every one of the `T * topk` rows real. On H100 the kernel takes the fp32-scale layout; I didn't have a B200 for the transposed UE8M0 layout. All numbers are from one H100. The GPU in brackets is the cookbook recipe the shape comes from, not where it ran. | shape (cookbook recipe it comes from) | 0 rows | 64 tok/GPU | dispatch cap | all real | |---|---|---|---|---| | Flash EP4, T=4096 (B200/B300/GB200 TP4) | 15.92 -> 1.63 us (9.74x) | 17.10 -> 3.26 us (5.25x) | 1024 tok: 49.89 -> 45.89 us (1.09x) | 176.07 -> 180.88 us (0.97x) | | Flash EP8, T=8192 (B200 TP8) | 31.27 -> 1.92 us (16.25x) | 32.19 -> 3.32 us (9.70x) | 1024 tok: 61.68 -> 44.85 us (1.38x) | 350.95 -> 356.45 us (0.98x) | | Pro EP4, T=1024 (GB300 TP4) | 6.52 -> 1.57 us (4.15x) | 8.64 -> 4.32 us (2.00x) | 256 tok: 15.31 -> 11.50 us (1.33x) | 65.92 -> 68.74 us (0.96x) | | Flash EP4, T=1024 (H200 FP8 TP4) | 4.92 -> 1.96 us (2.52x) | 5.84 -> 3.17 us (1.84x) | 256 tok: 10.15 -> 8.24 us (1.23x) | 43.34 -> 44.38 us (0.98x) | | Pro EP16, T=2048 (H200 FP8 TP16) | 12.01 -> 1.66 us (7.25x) | 14.33 -> 4.29 us (3.34x) | 128 tok: 16.35 -> 6.01 us (2.72x) | 130.82 -> 132.89 us (0.98x) | Every decode point up to the dispatch cap is faster (1.09x-16.25x). title: [Perf] dp-attention: Exchange the scheduler's MLP sync rows with gather + broadcast on gloo
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

With DP attention every scheduler step exchanges one small `MLPSyncBatchInfo` row per attention rank on the CPU gloo group (token counts, attention pairs, the CUDA-graph votes, the forward mode). gloo implements `all_gather` as a ring of `world_size - 1` serial hops, so the latency of that exchange grows linearly with the attention world. A gather onto group rank 0 followed by a broadcast is one hop plus a log-depth tree and fills the same buffer.

## Modifications

- `exchange_sync_rows` in `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/dp_attn.py` fills the flat buffer in group-rank order exactly like `all_gather_single`. On a CPU group with more than two ranks it gathers every rank's row onto group rank 0 (directly into the row views of the output) and broadcasts the filled buffer; device tensors and two-rank groups keep `all_gather_single`, since at two ranks the ring is already the single hop.
- `MLPSyncBatchInfo.all_gather` calls it on its all-gather path; the existing `use_all_reduce` branch is unchanged.
- Tests (`test/registered/unit/managers/scheduler_components/test_dp_attn.py`): the two existing mocks of `all_gather_single` move to the new seam. `TestSyncRowExchangeGloo` spawns an 8-rank gloo world and, for sub-groups of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 ranks over four rounds with a random per-rank sleep and busy-wait before each exchange, asserts that the exchange matches the ring all-gather bitwise on every rank and that the real `MLPSyncBatchInfo.all_gather` still produces the right `global_num_tokens`, `global_attention_pairs` and decode CUDA-graph vote. The world is capped at 8 because every rank is a spawned interpreter and the hosted CPU runner's memory bounds it; the file's `est_time` is raised accordingly.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the exchanged rows are bitwise identical to the all-gather result, which the new test checks on every rank.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No benchmark is included. The change swaps a ring all-gather for gather + broadcast on CPU groups larger than two ranks, and the new test checks the exchanged rows are identical; two-rank groups and device tensors keep the previous path.

Local validation on this head: `python3 test/registered/unit/managers/scheduler_components/test_dp_attn.py` passes all 18 tests. `isort`, `ruff`, `ruff format`, `codespell`, `check_registered_tests.py` and `check_no_bare_pytest_main.py` at the pinned pre-commit versions report nothing.

## Checklist

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).

title: [Fix] monokernels: Honor resolved CUDA graph configuration
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #44353. Enabling a monokernel can override an operator's decode CUDA graph budget: with the AMD plugin, `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 4` expands the capture buckets from `[1, 2, 4]` to `1..48`. Explicit bucket lists are also replaced.

The runtime additionally checks the legacy disable booleans instead of the resolved decode backend. Disabling graphs through `--cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled` or JSON therefore leaves graph-key filtering active and can send supported eager draft shapes to the normal forward. Conversely, an explicit backend that overrides a disable flag is treated as disabled.

## Modifications

- Keep automatically aligned buckets within the configured capture ceiling, and preserve explicitly supplied decode bucket lists.
- Skip bucket alignment when the resolved decode backend is disabled.
- Use the resolved decode backend when building monokernel capture keys, so every graph-disable spelling retains full supported eager coverage and explicit backend precedence is respected.
- Extend the existing CPU tests for small ceilings, explicit buckets, unchanged default alignment, disabled graph configuration, eager draft dispatch, and backend precedence.

## Accuracy Tests

The new regression cases fail against the original production code. After the fix, the following passes on macOS ARM64 with Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.1, and Transformers 5.19.0:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/monokernels \
  test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_cuda_graph_config_backends.py -q
# 32 passed, 28 subtests passed
```

All applicable pre-commit hooks pass for the three changed files, including test registration checks. `git diff --check` passes. No GPU model-accuracy run was performed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No GPU timing or profiling was performed. CPU tests verify that capture sizes stay within the configured limit and that supported eager draft batches use the plugin when graphs are disabled.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add registered unit tests.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style.
- Documentation: no new flags or public API changes.
- GPU accuracy and speed benchmarks: not run; this change is validated with CPU configuration and dispatch tests.

title: [Perf] DeepSeek-V4.1: Raise the SM100 swap-AB decode cap to 40 rows
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

SM100 swap-AB decode attention for DeepSeek-V4.1 admits at most 8 query rows. DSpark verify sends 5 rows per request (block size 5), so only batch size 1 takes swap-AB; batch size 2 and up fall back to FlashMLA. FlashMLA pads q to 64 heads and runs split-KV, so its time is flat at about 24 µs across 5–40 rows, while swap-AB is 2.7x faster at 5 rows and grows with the row count.

## Modifications

- `decode_attention_sm100.py`: admit up to 40 rows (`MAX_ROWS`) on SM100, so TP4 verify up to batch size 8 takes swap-AB. The kernel grid is (rows, KV tiles) and no program depends on the row count, so the cap is only a dispatch choice. The gfx950 path keeps its 8-row `MAX_BATCH`.
- `test_swapab_attention.py`: add 20- and 40-row cases and a 40-row CUDA graph replay; the per-row lengths now repeat so they cover any batch.

## Kernel timing

GB300, 16 heads (TP4), one decode layer shape (SWA 128 + extra KV 512), CUDA graph timing, µs per call:

| rows | batch size (verify) | swap-AB | FlashMLA | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 1 | 8.8 | 23.7 | 0.37 |
| 10 | 2 | 9.3 | 23.9 | 0.39 |
| 20 | 4 | 12.5 | 23.9 | 0.52 |
| 24 | — | 13.1 | 23.8 | 0.55 |
| 40 | 8 | 20.1 | 24.2 | 0.83 |

Break-even is near 48 rows; 40 leaves a margin.

## Benchmark

AgentX, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash FP4 on GB300, TP4/EP1, one hour per run, DSpark with simulated acceptance length 3.51. Both arms use `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261012-e6072935`; "this PR" overlays the changed attention files onto the same image. Server flags: `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --expert-parallel-size 1 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 128 --max-running-requests 128 --swa-prefix-tails 4096 --tokenizer-worker-num 4`, with `--prefill-decode-interval` 0 at c8 and 192 at c16.

| conc | main: P90 tok/s/user @ tok/s/GPU | this PR | P90 | median tok/s/user |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 413.3 @ 16,089 | 411.3 @ 16,184 | −0.5% | 577 → 610 (+5.7%) |
| 16 | 422.0 @ 28,885 | 442.4 @ 29,108 | +4.8% | 538 → 559 (+4.0%) |

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, all 1319 questions, 5-shot, real MTP verification (no simulated acceptance), 64 concurrent requests, TP4 on GB300:

| main | this PR |
|---|---|
| 0.9696 | 0.9711 |

## Unit tests

`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/test_swapab_attention.py` passes on GB300.

title: [Perf] distributed: Cache the eager launch of custom all-reduce v2 per size
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

An eager TP all-reduce through `CustomAllReduceV2` spends about 3.8 µs in Python on top of the 5.2 µs launch, measured on H200 (x86) with #44251 applied. The cost is split across these layers:

| layer | µs |
|---|---|
| kernel wrapper (`get_all_reduce_module` lookup, `comm.world_size`, result check) | 1.18 |
| `CustomAllReduceV2.custom_all_reduce` (byte count, `_pick_config` again) | 1.04 |
| `should_custom_ar` (`_pick_config`) | 0.62 |
| coordinator and `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` | 0.8 |

Every eager call of a given size and dtype resolves to the same algorithm and module, so the repeated work is redundant.

## Modifications

All changes are in `custom_all_reduce_v2.py`:
- Eager calls without `override_algo` resolve `(module, algorithm name, multicast)` once per `(nbytes, dtype)`. Both `should_custom_ar` and `custom_all_reduce` read that entry, and `custom_all_reduce` launches the module directly. A tvm-ffi Tensor result is still converted with `from_dlpack`.
- The cache is tied to the `config` object it was built from, so `uncap_pull_thresholds()` or any replaced config rebuilds it.
- Graph capture (`_graph_mode_allowed`), `override_algo` and kernel API logging keep the full path.

Callers, srt and diffusion alike, are unchanged. No memory is involved.

## Accuracy Tests

`test_custom_all_reduce.py --num-gpu 2` on 2xH200: 211 passed. Every existing case sets `override_algo`, so the tuned path had no coverage. Two tests are added:
- `test_custom_all_reduce_tuned_eager`: without an override, `should_custom_ar` matches `_pick_config` at every test size and dtype, and two passes (the second from the cache) equal NCCL exactly.
- `test_custom_all_reduce_eager_plan_follows_config`: replacing the config flips the verdict, restoring it flips it back, and the result equals NCCL.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Base `c15edf314d` + #44251, torch 2.14.1, 2xH200 (Xeon 8558P), with processes pinned to the GPUs' NUMA node.

**Host time per call** (µs, bf16 [1, 4096, 3072]; the GPU is kept busy so only submission is timed):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` | 9.04 | 6.74 |
| `CustomAllReduceV2.custom_all_reduce` | 7.46 | 5.49 |
| `should_custom_ar` | 0.62 | 0.50 |
| bare module launch, for reference | 5.24 | 4.96 |

**End to end**, TP2 eager, client wall-clock median. Two identical co-resident servers differed by 3.5% in an A/A test on this box, so both paths were built into one server and chosen per request. Requests rotated through the arms in the same process, and an extra base arm measures in-process noise.

| | vs base (#44251 applied) | faster than base in | in-process A/A |
|---|---|---|---|
| FLUX.1-dev 512² | −2.43% | 11/12 | +0.33% |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 512² | −0.23% | 13/16 | 0.00% |
| both at 1024² (GPU-bound) | +0.1% | — | +0.0% |

Output images are unchanged: the same kernel runs with the same arguments.

On a base without #44251, the bypassed kernel wrapper also drops its DLPack re-wrap. Against plain main, this change measured −14.4% (Qwen-Image-2.1) and −15.2% (FLUX.1) at 512², 10/10 and 8/8. Most of that is the re-wrap that #44251 removes for every caller. The two PRs touch different files and combine cleanly.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Cache the fused linear-GELU verdict per linear
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

`can_use_linear_gelu` runs at every quality-gated GELU up-projection: FLUX, Qwen-Image, LongCat, LTX-2, HunyuanVideo, GLM-Image and Wan. On every call it re-ran the input-independent guards:
- the SM120 architecture check;
- the quantization, `skip_bias_add` and `gather_output` checks;
- the bias, weight rank and dtype checks.

That is 2.67 µs per call on an x86 host, mostly `getattr` misses on `nn.Module`. In a py-spy profile of FLUX.1 TP2 it was 1.3% of the denoise host time.

## Modifications

In `fused_linear_gelu_site.py`:
- The input-independent verdict is kept per linear in a `WeakKeyDictionary`.
- `mount_fused_linear_gelu` and `unmount_fused_linear_gelu` clear it, so a re-mount re-reads the linear.
- The per-input checks still run on every call: device, half dtype and `x.dtype == weight.dtype`.

No model call site changes. No memory is involved.

On H200:
- `test_sites.py`: 25 passed, including the new `test_linear_gelu_verdict_is_reused_until_remount`. It checks that three calls read the linear once and that a re-mount reads it again.
- `test_wan_gelu_mlp.py`: passed.

title: [Perf] kernels: Enter a JIT kernel's device guard only when the device differs
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

JIT kernel wrappers that launch through tvm-ffi enter `torch.cuda.device(t.device)` around the launch. Entering and leaving it costs about 1.6 µs per call on an x86 host, even when `t` is already on the current device, which is always the case in a one-device-per-process server. The qknorm complex RoPE wrappers used by Qwen-Image-2.1 run it on every attention layer.

## Modifications

- `sglang.kernels.jit.utils.device_guard(t)` returns a shared `nullcontext` when `t.get_device()` is the current device, and `torch.cuda.device(t.device)` otherwise.
- `qknorm_complex_rope_cuda` and `qknorm_complex_rope_pack_` use it.

Behaviour on another device is unchanged. Other wrappers can adopt the helper one line at a time.

## Accuracy Tests

On 2xH200:
- `test/registered/unit/kernels/test_device_guard.py`: 2 passed. With the tensor on the current device, `torch.cuda.device` is never constructed (it is monkeypatched to raise). With a tensor on `cuda:1`, the device is entered and restored.
- `test_complex_rope.py`: 38 passed.
- `test_qwen_image21_cuda.py`: 25 passed.
- `test_model_fast_paths.py`: 114 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Base `c15edf314d`, H200 (Xeon 8558P).

| | µs per call |
|---|---|
| `torch.cuda.device(t.device)` enter and exit | 1.64 |
| `device_guard(t)`, current device | 0.49 |

End to end the change is too small to resolve on H200. In Qwen-Image-2.1 TP2 512², with both paths in one server and chosen per request, it measured +0.27% (faster in 5/16) against an in-process A/A of 0.00%: the wrapper runs about 2,400 times per request. The saving is per call. Grace hosts pay roughly twice the x86 Python cost.

title: [Perf] [AMD] dsv4: Add a separate MegaMoE decode instance
author: RolaoDenthu
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.

Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

Decode currently shares a MegaMoEV2 instance sized for prefill. Even with a small decode batch, the large MTPR keeps it on the large-instance dispatch/combine path, preventing it from benefiting from kernel configurations optimized for small token counts.

Introduce a separate, smaller decode instance to enable the small-MTPR execution path while retaining the main instance for prefill.

## Modification

Add `SGLANG_AMD_FLYDSL_MEGA_MOE_DECODE_MTPR` (default: `0`, disabled). When enabled, maintain two cached `MegaMoEV2` instances:

- **Main instance:** uses `SGLANG_AMD_FLYDSL_MEGA_MOE_MTPR` for steps containing prefill.
- **Decode instance:** uses the smaller MTPR `SGLANG_AMD_FLYDSL_MEGA_MOE_DECODE_MTPR` for decode, target verify, and draft extend in decode-only steps. 

Both instances are constructed together in a fixed order across EP ranks before graph capture. They own separate communication buffers and synchronization state while sharing model weights through per-layer rebinding.

Instance selection follows the globally synchronized step type, ensuring all EP ranks use the same instance regardless of local batch size or graph/eager execution. Startup validation checks that the decode MTPR covers the maximum per-rank workload.

## Accuracy Tests
gsm8k 1319: 0.939

MegaMoEV2 per-layer time in µs, max across the 8 ranks (MI355X, EP8, DeepSeek-V4-Pro shapes, a8w4, uniform routing, CUDA-graph):

| 224 | 449 (1.28x faster) | 566 | 573 |
| 448 | 647 (2% slower) | 632 | 633 |
| 672 | does not fit | 797 | 790 |

The speedups are relative to the 16384 column.

author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

Split [#44530](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44530) into five review layers. This is layer 2/5, based on [#44664](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44664).

## Modifications

Adds the Muse Spark operators, CUDA JIT kernels, collective GEMM implementations, and shared kernel integration. AMD-specific kernels and capabilities belong to the AMD layer; the changes from radixark/sglang-muse-spark#224 belong to the final layer.

This layer changes **44 files (+13,752 / -17)** relative to its immediate base. Every split commit preserves all 32 `Co-authored-by` trailers from the original commit.

## Validation

- The remaining stack is based on `main` at `92580581da6fc8542a997a00c1a8b71b03497680`; CUDA Docker support from #44664 is already merged.
- Renamed `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/muse_spark_v12/` and `python/sglang/kernels/ops/muse_spark_v12/` to `muse_spark/`. Updated downstream imports, lazy group registration, JIT source/module names, test strings and comments. No old `muse_spark_v12` references remain in any of the four branch tips.
- Independently reproduced all four complete Git trees from their pre-rename trees using only that uniform rename plus the repository formatters. Full byte comparison passes; Python AST comparison confirms no functional edits. Per-layer file scope, dependency order and all 32 original coauthor trailers are preserved. The #224 layer is equivalent under the namespace rename plus formatter normalization.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks pass on affected files in every layer, including registered-test validation. Python compilation and import/JIT-source path resolution pass. An isolated kernel namespace/registry import smoke check passes without importing JIT or the old package.
- Full namespace/dispatch pytest collection is blocked locally by unavailable Triton; GPU correctness and performance tests were not run. The prior rebase's 11 targeted conflict checks remain recorded separately.
- Reproduction script and commands: [mechanical rename proof in #44665](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44665#mechanical-rename-proof).

## Mechanical rename proof

The kernels PR contains a separate `mechanical_provable` rename commit. The same transform was applied to each downstream tree, keeping later layers out of earlier PRs. All four reproductions passed.

<details>
<summary>Standalone reproduction script (Python 3.12+, Git and pre-commit)</summary>

Save the following as `reproduce_muse_spark_rename.py`. Ensure the base/target SHAs embedded in `records` are present in your local clone (`git fetch origin <sha>` if needed), then run:

```sh
python3 reproduce_muse_spark_rename.py --repo /path/to/sglang
```

The script checks a temporary shared clone; it does not edit the source checkout.

```python
"""Reproduce every stack tree from its pre-rename tree and compare all bytes.

Usage: python3 reproduce.py --repo /path/to/sglang 
Requires git and the repository's pre-commit environments. Fetch the base and
target SHAs embedded below into the source clone before running this script.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import pathlib
import subprocess
import tempfile

"""Rename the two Muse Spark kernel trees and all references, with no code edits."""
import pathlib
import subprocess

OLD = b"muse_spark_v12"
NEW = b"muse_spark"
DIRECTORIES = ("python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/", "python/sglang/kernels/ops/")


def transform(root):
    root = pathlib.Path(root)
    paths = subprocess.check_output(["git", "ls-files", "-z"], cwd=root).decode().split("\0")
    changed = []
    for relative in filter(None, paths):
        path = root / relative
        if path.is_symlink() or not path.is_file():
            continue
        source = path.read_bytes()
        target = source.replace(OLD, NEW)
        if target != source:
            path.write_bytes(target)
            changed.append(relative)
    moved = []
    for prefix in DIRECTORIES:
        source = root / (prefix + OLD.decode())
        target = root / (prefix + NEW.decode())
        assert source.is_dir() and not target.exists(), (source, target)
        moved.extend(str(path.relative_to(root)) for path in source.rglob("*") if path.is_file())
        source.rename(target)
    return dict(references=changed, moved=moved)





def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--repo', required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    records = [{'pr': 44665, 'base': '359030dbac3aeab909533411583646790c3ebcb9', 'target': 'a2ac2718795b16a10a6e221eefa38e234abcc9e0'}, {'pr': 44666, 'base': 'f60333c7412ef5001b4e7fbab13dcb7aa1b87993', 'target': '90785dc87625d82e18c148826f99e01fefdbb503'}, {'pr': 44667, 'base': 'caf6b36a44e01a91a1f21524ca086b04af4b3933', 'target': 'cbd25ea6497f6dcec269af385fa374e75b9e4e13'}, {'pr': 44668, 'base': '51abebf433801bd6bcfadedf398a5b9a3c27dbf3', 'target': 'e297cab65cafffc94f3224d49858820affac7019'}]
    env = dict(os.environ, SKIP='no-commit-to-branch')
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='muse-spark-rename-proof-') as temporary:
        checkout = pathlib.Path(temporary) / 'repo'
        subprocess.run(['git', 'clone', '--shared', '--no-checkout', '--quiet',
                        str(pathlib.Path(args.repo).resolve()), str(checkout)], check=True)

        def git(*argv):
            return subprocess.check_output(['git', *argv], cwd=checkout, env=env).decode().strip()

        for record in records:
            git('checkout', '--detach', '--quiet', record['base'])
            transform(checkout)
            git('add', '--all')
            changed = git('diff', '--cached', '--name-only', '--diff-filter=ACMR').splitlines()
            for attempt in range(2):
                result = subprocess.run(['pre-commit', 'run', '--files', *changed],
                                        cwd=checkout, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
                if result.returncode == 0:
                    break
                if attempt == 1:
                    raise RuntimeError(result.stdout + result.stderr)
                git('add', '--all')
            git('add', '--all')
            actual = git('write-tree')
            expected = git('rev-parse', record['target'] + '^{tree}')
            if actual != expected:
                raise AssertionError(git('diff', expected, actual))
            print(f"PASS #{record['pr']}: full tree reproduced exactly ({actual})", flush=True)
            git('reset', '--hard', record['target'])


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

```

</details>

## Stack

Merge/review order, from `main` upward:

1. [#44664](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44664) — CUDA Docker and DeepGEMM patches
2. [#44665](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44665) — Kernels and collective GEMM
3. [#44666](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44666) — SRT and registered tests
4. [#44667](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44667) — AMD / ROCm support
5. [#44668](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44668) — Helion verify megakernels (#224)

The original #44530 remains unchanged as the full-stack reference.

title: [Feat] srt: Add muse spark runtime, multimodal support and tests (3/5)
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

Split [#44530](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44530) into five review layers. This is layer 3/5, now based on `main` after [#44665](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44665) merged.

## Modifications

Adds Muse Spark text and Omni runtime support, multimodal processing, MoE and quantization integration, runtime defaults, shared runtime updates, and registered tests. AMD-specific hunks and the #224 megakernel integration/tests are deferred to their respective layers.

This layer changes **82 files (+9,175 / -224)** relative to its immediate base. Every split commit preserves all 32 `Co-authored-by` trailers from the original commit.

## Validation

- Temporarily disabled the CI registration for `test_muse_spark_12_b300_pd.py` until **2026-11-01**. [B300 job 117611788593](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39099912264/job/117611788593) failed during server startup and ran zero tests: the log shows whole-model Hugging Face cache cleanup immediately before tokenizer loading failed, consistent with a concurrent cache cleanup race. [#44975](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44975) is a one-file follow-up based on this PR that restores the registration; the cache issue still needs validation or a fix before merging that follow-up. CI registry parsing and pre-commit passed for both changes.
- Fixed the earlier failures in [Base run 39006509622](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39006509622) and [Extra run 39006509690](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39006509690): CUDA-decoded video tensors no longer go through CPU pinning; CuTeDSL/CUTLASS preserve Standard combine output for all-gather prefill; runtime group accessors, test fixtures, the model-default whitelist and the custom multimodal executor declaration are aligned.
- Set Muse Spark B300 speculative decoding speed to **500 token/s**; kept the **4.7** acceptance thresholds. The benchmark now flushes both PD workers directly with checked POST requests instead of ignoring mini-LB 405 responses.
- Five complete targeted unit-test files passed: **594 tests**, covering runtime context, server arguments, FlashInfer dispatch/runners, multimodal async call sites and model overrides. Added prefill/idle/decode format and workspace regression cases. Pre-commit and Python compilation passed; these local results do not imply that every GitHub CI suite has passed.
- On a 4x B200 devbox with the same Torch 2.14.1, Transformers 5.19.0 and FlashInfer 0.7.2 versions as CI, reproduced the original CuTeDSL and CUDA pin-memory errors before applying the patch. After the patch, real CPU/CUDA video preprocessing and the original Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-Omni video-chat tests passed.
- The original Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 TP4/EP4/DP4 CuTeDSL + FlashInfer server configuration booted successfully and passed six checked serial/concurrent generation requests. This is a smoke test; the full 1,319-question GSM8K suite remains for CI.
- Localized the Qwen3-Omni prefix-cache wording mismatch to Blackwell BF16 split-K numerics: six fixed-seed cold/cache comparisons failed on the default path, while six passed with only split-K disabled; the original base passed on two B200 GPUs. Moved the exact-equality case to a dedicated deterministic + Triton-attention fixture with radix caching explicitly enabled; kept the other nine modality tests on production defaults. The complete updated Qwen3-Omni file passed **10/10 tests** in 167 seconds. No output assertions were relaxed or test cases removed.
- The 8x B300 Muse Spark performance/accuracy suite was not rerun locally: no whole-node B300 capacity was available. Its latest CI attempt failed before reaching accuracy or throughput assertions. The temporary skip changes scheduling only; all test cases and thresholds remain intact.
- Preserved all user follow-up commits and all 32 original coauthor trailers. AMD and Helion changes remain in layers 4/5 and 5/5.

## Stack

Merge/review order, from `main` upward:

1. [#44664](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44664) — CUDA Docker and DeepGEMM patches (**merged**)
2. [#44665](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44665) — Kernels and collective GEMM (**merged**)
3. [#44666](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44666) — SRT and registered tests
4. [#44667](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44667) — AMD / ROCm support
5. [#44668](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44668) — Helion verify megakernels (#224)

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4.1: Keep the DSpark draft SWA out of the radix tree
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Under `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay` the target already keeps SWA in a per-request window, but the DSpark draft still forced a paged SWA allocator, so the radix tree kept an SWA component only the draft used. Evicting the draft's SWA then cut prefix hits on Main KV the target could still reuse (#42716 skips the same match gate).
- The DSpark draft SWA now lives in a per-request ring on CUDA: `swa_ring_rows` (`req_pool_idx * ring + pos % ring`) and `get_draft_swa_ring_size` (sliding window + max draft tokens) own its layout for every reader and writer. No pool needs `needs_paged_swa_allocator`, so the tree holds no SWA component.
- Writes reuse the existing ring path (`_ring_inject_loc`, and `build_unified_commit_inject_layout` renamed to `build_ring_commit_inject_layout`), now keyed on the draft pool's `swa_req_ring_size` instead of the unified_kv gate.
- Reads: `get_dspark_swa_page_indices` builds the draft window from the ring (`BuildDsparkSwaRingIndices`), and the draft block writes its ring rows, both eagerly and in the graph.
- A request placed by a prefix hit starts its ring at the hit (`swa_req_ring_valid_from`), so the draft masks earlier positions instead of reading rows left by the slot's previous request.
- The ring is budgeted as a fixed reservation next to the request windows instead of per SWA token.

Only DeepSeek-V4.1 with encoder SWA bounded replay and DSpark on CUDA changes; HIP keeps the paged draft SWA, and every other configuration is unchanged. After a prefix hit, the draft attends only to rows written since the hit until its window fills again.

On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (4x GB300, TP4, DSpark, encoder replay), a prompt whose draft SWA was evicted by 400 other prompts re-hits 8448 of its 8565 tokens instead of 0. GSM8K stays at 98.0% with and without decoder replay, and the average accept length is 3.81 against 3.78 before.

title: [Feat] dflash: Serve SpecForge MLA drafts through the target MLA attention
author: maocheng23
body:
Serve SpecForge DFlash MLA drafts (`dflash_config.attention_mode: "mla"`, SpecForge #758) with the target's DeepSeek MLA attention. SpecForge exports DeepSeek's MLA parameterization: the same projection names, an optional `q_lora_rank`, `rope_interleave` and `mscale_all_dim` scaling. The draft layer is therefore a thin `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA` subclass. It runs the target's absorbed-MLA forward and backend dispatch, and stores one latent row plus one RoPE key per token in `MLATokenToKVPool`.

Only the DFlash-specific parts are new:

- `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA` takes `attn_type` and `sliding_window_size`. The defaults are unchanged.
- `DFlashMLAAttention`:
  - sets the layer's DFlash causality (bidirectional by default, causal with `is_causal=true` and `layer_types`);
  - loads SpecForge's separate `q_a_proj` / `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` into the fused down projection;
  - absorbs `kv_b_proj` into `w_kc` / `w_vc` when that weight loads;
  - projects target-context latents for the worker.
- `ModelConfig` routes an MLA draft through the existing MLA branch.
- Each MLA layer writes its own target-context KV with `DFlashMLAAttention.write_context_kv`: latent rows through `set_mla_kv_buffer`, and accepted-prefix commits through the new masked `MLATokenToKVPool.set_mla_kv_buffer_prefix_valid`. The DFlash worker and DSpark's context-KV writer both call it, so DFlash, DFlash2, Domino and DSpark drafts share one MLA path. DSpark already builds the same layers, and its fused GQA write paths are skipped for MLA drafts.
- MLA drafts run on the default MLA draft backends: `flashinfer` on CUDA (SGLang's default MLA backend on Blackwell), `triton` on ROCm and XPU. The draft backend goes through the existing DFlash resolution: `--speculative-draft-attention-backend` if set, otherwise the target's backend, otherwise that default.
  - A target's MLA-only backend (`trtllm_mla`, `cutedsl_mla`) is not a draft backend, so an MLA target's draft falls back to the default.
  - `trtllm_mha` serves only non-MLA drafts. An MLA draft that would get it falls back to the default MLA draft backend, not to `fa4`, which main now picks for non-MLA drafts on SM100. DSpark resolves its backend outside the DFlash hook and applies the same `trtllm_mha` rule itself.
  - FlashInfer MLA fixes the mask once per batch, using the same helper the draft layers use. Triton takes it from each layer's `attn_type`, and only `triton` serves sliding MLA layers.

The following are rejected at load or launch:

- quantized draft weights;
- `attention_bias`;
- attention sinks and value scaling;
- RoPE types other than `default`, `yarn` and `deepseek_yarn` (the target layer serves scaling as DeepSeek YaRN);
- MLA mixed with GQA/MHA layers;
- `--dcp-size > 1`.

A BF16 MLA draft needs no extra flags on CUDA. To pin the backend and the draft KV dtype explicitly:

```bash
--speculative-draft-attention-backend flashinfer \
--speculative-draft-kv-cache-dtype bf16
```

### Validation

Rebased onto main `d0a7565436` as two commits: the PR as it was (11 commits, squashed) and the switch from `tokenspeed_mla` to the default MLA backends, since main removed `tokenspeed_mla` in #44803.

At `28405e8424`, on one GB300 (TP1, BF16), with torch 2.14.1+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2, sglang-kernel 0.4.10 and Transformers 5.19.0 (main's pins):

- **Draft MLA tests:** `test_dflash_mla_backends.py` (2 passed, 4 subtests, no skips) and `test_dflash_mla.py` with the hook tests (9 passed).
  - The GPU backend test runs real `triton` and `flashinfer` kernels, with bidirectional and causal masks, eagerly and after one CUDA graph replay with changed prefixes. The reference is independent FP32 SpecForge math, within relative L2 1.2% and element-wise tolerance 0.025.
- **Target MLA regressions:** the FlashInfer MLA suite and Triton eagle-verify in eager and CUDA-graph modes gave 8 passed and 1 skipped. The skip is main's known SM10.3 FlashInfer EAGLE-graph failure.
- **Real Engine smoke, one per draft backend:** a Qwen3 MHA target with a tiny MLA draft checkpoint in SpecForge's split `q_a_proj` / `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` layout.

  | Target backend | Draft backend flag | Draft backend built |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `flashinfer` | `triton` | `TritonAttnBackend` |
  | `triton` | `flashinfer` | `FlashInferMLAAttnBackend` |
  | `trtllm_mha`, page 32 | none | `FlashInferMLAAttnBackend`, after the `trtllm_mha` fallback warning |

  Each run checked:
  - three rounds of 24 tokens: single, batch 2, and a repeated batch 2 with prefix-cache hits;
  - target and draft CUDA graph replay at batch sizes 1 and 2;
  - batched prefix commits into a `[slots,1,576]` BF16 MLA pool.

  The checkpoints are deterministic random weights, so this validates integration only, not acceptance rate or quality.

- **CPU:** the unit tests and the arg-hook tests pass; ruff, isort and codespell are clean. The new resolver case fails on the pre-switch commit, where an MLA draft leaving `trtllm_mha` lands on `fa4`.

Before the rebase, the same draft math was validated on GB300 against independent FP32 SpecForge math (max relative L2 0.48% for triton BF16 and 0.50% for flashinfer BF16), together with Engine smokes for DSpark MLA drafts on triton and flashinfer.

Not yet validated: multi-rank TP, HIP, `fa3` / `fa4` as MLA draft backends, sliding MLA layers on triton, long-context RoPE scaling, and trained-checkpoint acceptance.

Compressed storage holds `kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim` values per token and layer, instead of per-head K and V. For latent 512, RoPE 64, 32 heads and K/V widths 192/128, that is 17.78x smaller. Measured on an earlier revision: 3,203 MiB vs 180 MiB in BF16 for 32,768 tokens and five layers.

Reproduction:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/spec/test_dflash_mla.py \
  test/registered/unit/spec/test_oot_dflash_hooks.py \
  test/registered/attention/test_dflash_mla_backends.py
```

Companion export normalization: sgl-project/SpecForge#982.
