title: [Refactor] kernels/diffusion/tests: Prune dead code and fix tests that never ran
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Six months of fast kernel and diffusion work left a lot behind in `python/sglang/kernels`, `python/sglang/multimodal_gen` and the kernel/diffusion test trees: kernels nothing calls, registry metadata nothing reads, per-model copies of the same fused-op glue, env knobs that do nothing, and tests that pass without testing anything. This PR removes that, and fixes the real bugs the audit turned up along the way (several were silently shipping).

**408 files, +3,629 / -26,346.** About 1.3K of the additions are test oracles and helpers moved out of production modules into `python/sglang/test/kernels/`.

## Bugs fixed (please review these first)

| Area | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| SANA (diffusion) | Since #37816 the VAE loader calls `vae.state_dict()` before `load_state_dict`; `AutoencoderDC` builds its inner diffusers model lazily, so that call built it with random init and the later load returned early. **All 375 VAE tensors were random; every SANA T2I image on main is noise.** | `load_state_dict` loads into an already-built inner model. Regression test in `test_vae_loader.py` (fails on main). |
| GLM-Image (diffusion) | #33555 added an unconditional `query[:, t:] = q_img` write-back after an in-place RoPE; torch 2.14 rejects the self-copy, so **every GLM-Image request fails** in the first DiT block. | Copy back only when the rotation returned new memory. Regression test `test_glm_image_attention.py`; `test_ar_models` re-enabled (fails on main, passes here in 175 s on 2xH200). |
| MiniMax-H3 VAE | The default-on `h3_vae_qk_rmsnorm_rope` path ran in `quality=exact` but was not bit-exact (~25% of rotated channels differ). A second, faster, quality-gated fused path for the same op already existed. | Removed the non-bit-exact path. **Behavior change:** the exact tier now runs the native chain (bit-identical to native); lossless is unchanged. |
| Diffusion CI | `STANDALONE_FILES` moved to `server/gpu_cases.py` in #24630 but the CUDA partition planner kept reading the runner, so **no CUDA standalone file has run since June** (12 2-GPU files + the 1-GPU ones). | Planner reads the case config. All 15 newly scheduled files were run on H200 through the CI code path; one rotted test fixed. |
| Env vars | Code read the legacy `SGL_*` names while docs/`environ.py` define `SGLANG_*`, and the rewrite is one-directional, so the documented names did nothing: `SGLANG_USE_DEEPGEMM_BMM` (5 models), `SGLANG_DG_USE_NVRTC`, `SGLANG_CPU_QUANTIZATION`, `SGLANG_DSA_TOPK_ROW_SPLIT`. | Read via `envs`; legacy names still work. |
| `BaseFusedOp` | `KernelBackend.FLYDSL` mapped to a missing `forward_flydsl`, so `SGLANG_FORCE_FUSED_OP_BACKEND=flydsl` raised `AttributeError`. | Stub added + test. |
| Tests that never ran | `test_fp8_kernel` returned early on every CUDA GPU with sm>=90; `test_swapab_attention` was registered on H100 but gated to sm_10x (production SM100 kernel had no CUDA coverage); sm_100 / sm_120 / 2-GPU / 4-GPU diffusion unit tests sat on a 1-GPU H100 lane; `test_qwen_image21` cache tests exercised a test-local re-implementation of the fix. | Each now runs on hardware that satisfies its gate (or was deleted with its dead kernel); the qwen_image21 tests drive the real block and fail when the fix is reverted. |
| SenseNova-U1 | `FlowMatchingHead` called `SimpleMLPAdaLN` with a signature the class doesn't have (crash for `fm_head_layers > 2`). | Restored the timestep-conditioned head; test fails on main. |

## Modifications

### Kernels (`python/sglang/kernels`, -13.8K)
- **Dead / test-only kernels removed** (each re-verified with whole-repo grep incl. string lookups): seg_la kernel, dsv4 `fused_ape_pool_norm_rope`, tilelang `fp8_index`, KDA prefill timing scaffolding, nvlink push/pull all-reduce wrappers, inkling two-shot all-reduce, `cutedsl_gdn_mtp_ring` T=1 entry, non-`f_b` FlyDSL KDA decode, dsa `GetK/GetS`, adler32 whole-tensor entry points, ReplaySSM circular commit, cvt helpers, mxfp8 v-cache update, fp8 ue8m0/hopper/transpose helpers, `w8a8_block_fp8_matmul`, `awq_gemm_triton`, rocm `tkw1`, `moe_fused_gate_jit`, inkling gate v1, `post_reorder_triton_kernel`, `fused_inplace_qknorm_across_heads`, elementwise `silu_and_mul_triton`/autotune path, `rms_normalize_triton`, stale `top_p_renorm_triton` copy, and others.
- **Legacy DSV4 compressor path removed** (`compress_old.py`, `fused_compress_triton.py`, srt `dsv4/compress_hip.py`, the old `CompressorBackendMixin`): every CUDA/HIP backend uses `compressor_v2`; `fused_norm_rope_inplace` (live) moved to `dsv4/elementwise.py`. AOT dsv4 q/k norm+RoPE ops (duplicates of the JIT ones) removed.
- **Registry (option A):** the KernelSpec inventory stays; write-only metadata goes (`FormatSignature`, `KernelSpec.format_signature/description/group/name`, `BaseFusedOp.format_signature/descriptions/dispatch_forward`, unused selector/platform helpers). `spec.CUDA_ONLY` replaces ~44 inline frozensets. Unused `BaseFusedOp`s (4 RMSNorm, Gelu/GeluTanh/ReLU2/QuickGELU) removed; facade wrappers nobody imports removed (this also fixes facade functions shadowed by same-named submodules). `Fp8ScaledMMOp` no longer declares an SM90 heuristic as a capability.
- **#42184 criteria applied** to the four remaining gate sites (route-quant, engram, vision_rope, minimax_m3): gates check eligibility, launchers enforce contracts.
- **Duplicates:** sparse-MLA decode reuses the shared kernels (bit-exact, 720 cases x 2 archs incl. fully masked rows); mxfp8 gfx95 reuses `mxfp8_quant`. Forks that are *not* bit-exact stay, each with a one-line comment (grok RMSNorm, gfx1250 qk-RMSNorm, int8 group quant on ROCm, marlin SiTU, minimax Gemma RMSNorm).
- **Test oracles shipped in op modules moved to `sglang.test.kernels`** (LPLB, dsa transform index, DCP LSE combine, dsv4 K-cache quant refs, extend attention, dspark window, multigpu launcher, mhc, per-token-group quant dispatch).

### Diffusion (`python/sglang/multimodal_gen`, -9.4K)
- **Dead code:** SenseNova-U1 unreachable chat/interleave/it2i paths (~2.6K; T2I output byte-identical), auto-residency estimators and the warmup stage-iteration calibration chain nothing read, SANA-WM parity debug harness (`SANAWM_*` env hooks incl. `torch.load` input injection), `MINIMAX_H3_USE_FUSED_NORM` path, unresolved MiniMax-H3 euler scheduler, registry subprocess-inspect path (pointed at a nonexistent module), delta-gzip realtime encoding (server + web UI), bundled-overlay lookup, `EncodingStage`, bitsandbytes 4-bit swap, `generate_with_lora` (could never run), `convert_hf_to_fp8.py`, unused platform hooks, unread `ServerArgs` fields, etc.
- **Env:** 12 `envs.py` entries nothing read removed (+ the docs rows presenting 5 of them as working knobs); raw reads of `SGLANG_ENABLE_FUSED_QKNORM_ROPE` / `MINIMAX_H3_VAE_*` declared in `envs.py` with identical parsing; unprefixed GDN dev knobs dropped.
- **Refactors (bit-exact):** `BitExactFusionGate.run()` replaces 24 hand-written verify-once/fallback blocks and the `mismatch_msg` boilerplate; one LayerNorm+modulate helper for FLUX.3/GLM/LongCat; `sites/` exports one `QualityGatedFusion` per family instead of four wrappers each (~50 facade entries, 28 imports gone). Sites that are hand-tuned for launch overhead, re-raise, verify inside the try, or differ in reference were left as they are (listed in the commit messages).

### Tests and CI
- Deleted always-skipped tests (env var set nowhere, `skipif(True)`, hard-coded dev paths), tautologies (default/literal echoes, `inspect.getsource` shape tests, log-format echoes, torch-behavior tests), duplicate cases and duplicate helpers; trimmed grids with no extra coverage (`fused_fp8_qkv_kv_cache` 1,344 -> 288 cases, AOT `moe_align` 4,368 -> 144, AOT per-token-group quant 3,632 -> 320). CI-tooling meta-tests are intentionally kept.
- New lane wiring: swapab on B200; Blackwell, SM120 and 4-GPU diffusion unit steps; 2-GPU diffusion unit files as 2-gpu standalone files; `quant-videogen` installed for its tests; comm benches no longer register no-op AMD runs; HPC-Ops tests (always skipped: the package isn't in the CI venv) disabled explicitly.
- **CI cost:** the standalone-file fix adds runners (1-GPU H100: 5 -> 6 partitions; 2-GPU: 3 -> 5 by current estimates). The estimates are 2-15x above the measured H200 times; I'll copy this PR's CI-measured values into `STANDALONE_FILE_EST_TIMES` before merge.

## Accuracy Tests

End-to-end, same GPU, fixed seed, base vs this branch (fused paths confirmed active by a gate tracer on both sides; no gate disabled):

| Model | Paths exercised | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ERNIE-Image, LongCat-Image, FLUX.2-klein-4B, Joy, MOSS-Image, Anima, Qwen-Image, Wan2.1-1.3B, Helios-Distilled | `BitExactFusionGate.run`, LN+modulate helper, QK-norm+RoPE, handler-table sites, gated residual | byte-identical |
| GLM-Image (1024², 30 steps) | LN+modulate helper, QK-LN | identical to main+fix; fused == native |
| SANA 600M (512², 20 steps) | VAE fix | identical to main+fix; reproducible across processes (main is noise) |
| SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT T2I | dead-path removal | PNG md5 identical |
| Z-Image-Turbo server warmup | residency/warmup cleanup | PNG identical, same peak memory |
| MiniMax-H3 VAE decoder | lossless in-place path / exact tier | lossless identical; exact == native |

Kernel dedups were checked bit-for-bit on H200 and GB300 (scripts in the commit messages' descriptions).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No perf-path changes intended. `BitExactFusionGate.run` was not applied to the launch-overhead-tuned sites (the closures add ~160-180 ns per call on the host).

## Validation

- **H200 (sm_90):** every file under `test/registered/kernels/ops`, `test/registered/unit` and `multimodal_gen/test/unit` (1,624 files). Failures were re-run on main: identical failing test ids (rust extensions not built in the source tree, NPU-only, multi-GPU tests on one GPU, pre-existing diffusion kernel failures); 2 port collisions from parallel runs pass alone. 
- **GB300 (sm_103):** every file under `test/registered/kernels/ops` (334 files): failing ids identical to main.
- **RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120):** FA4 sm120 + FA4 + dense FA4 + sm120 paged MQA logits + sm120 fp8 linear + mxfp4 sm120 + diffusion fp8 FA sm120 + kernel namespace: all pass, same as main.
- **Multi-GPU:** every CUDA diffusion standalone file run on 2xH200 through the CI runner path (incl. `test_ar_models` and `test_diffusion_bcg_tp2_zimage_turbo` at the final head); Kandinsky 6 4-GPU cases on 4xH200.
- `pytest --collect-only` over the test trees: no new collection errors; import walk over `sglang.kernels`, `sglang.multimodal_gen`, `sglang.srt.{layers,models,...}`: no new import failures.
- **Not validated:** ROCm, NPU, XPU, MUSA (HIP-only deletions are traced through backend selection and import-checked on CUDA), a full AOT wheel link (affected TUs compiled for sm90/sm100), 4-GPU cases on Blackwell.

title: [Perf] request_logger: skip per-token watermark redaction walk
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Motivation

#37577 (Aaronson-Gumbel text watermarking) added `redact_watermark_secrets` to the request-log formatters. Both `_dataclass_to_string_truncated` and `_transform_data_for_logging` redact the whole request object **before** truncation and **before** `skip_names` filtering, so every `--log-requests` call walks the full `input_ids` element by element (~0.5us/token). With long prompts this costs tens of ms per log call on the tokenizer-manager event loop, on receive and again on finish, and shows up directly in TTFT.

On main, formatting an 80k-token `GenerateReqInput` at `--log-requests-level 2` costs ~62 ms (text) / ~60 ms (json); with this PR it is ~0.3 ms / ~1.1 ms.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/utils/request_logger.py`:

- New `_redact_field`: redact by field/key name. Fields named `watermark_key` / `watermark_key_b` / `watermark_config` become `<redacted>`; `watermark` / `sampling_params` / `preferred_sampling_params` are redacted recursively; everything else passes through untouched. `skip_names` fields are dropped before redaction.
- The `str(...)` fallback in both formatters still redacts first, so a msgspec Struct carrying watermark fields under an ordinary key stays redacted, exactly as on main.
- The truncated-list branch of `_transform_data_for_logging` now transforms each printed item instead of returning raw items, so a truncated list of dataclasses/Structs no longer breaks `json.dumps`.

`python/sglang/srt/sampling/watermarking/core.py`:

- The watermark field-name sets are now module-level `WATERMARK_SECRET_FIELD_NAMES` / `WATERMARK_CONTAINER_FIELD_NAMES`, shared by all redact branches and the logger instead of being re-listed in five places.
- New scalar fast-path: `_SCALAR_TYPES.issuperset(map(type, value))` scans a sequence in C, and a plain-scalar sequence (e.g. token ids) can never hold a secret, since secrets only sit under dict keys or struct/dataclass fields. Mutable lists come back as copies (the crash-dump path pickles the result on a worker thread); immutable tuples may alias. The mixed-container walk skips scalar items inline. This bounds the other `redact_watermark_secrets` callers too — `dump_requests` / crash dump in `tokenizer_manager.py`, server info — and list-of-lists batched `input_ids`.

Log output is byte-identical to main at every `--log-requests-level`, with one intentional exception: Struct/dataclass items inside truncated json lists now print as redacted strings instead of crashing `json.dumps`.

## Accuracy Tests

Logging-only change; no model path touched.

New `test/registered/unit/utils/test_request_logger_redaction.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`):

- Secrets are redacted in both formatters, for 16 and 100k input ids, including the top-level `GenerateReqInput.watermark` field.
- A msgspec Struct with a `watermark_key` field under an ordinary key stays redacted (regression test for the string fallback).
- Truncated lists keep their printed halves redacted; a truncated json list of Structs stays `json.dumps`-serializable.
- The redaction walk is bounded at each level's real `(max_length, skip_names)` — this test fails on main.
- Scalar sequences skip the walk; mutable lists come back as copies while tuples may alias; containers are still redacted.

Output equivalence vs main was checked with both formatters over 22 payload shapes (levels 0-3 metadata, nested secrets, msgspec Structs under ordinary fields, long secret-bearing lists, batched `input_ids`, finish `out` dicts, tuples, None secrets, unicode text): byte-identical in all 44 runs, no secret string in any output.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

CPU, single thread:

| case | main (ms) | PR (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|
| level 2, text, 80k input_ids | 61.6 | 0.3 |
| level 2, json, 80k input_ids | 59.6 | 1.1 |
| scalar list redact, 100k ids | 74.4 | 2.3 |
| mixed 100k scalars + 1 dict | 74.2 | 5.8 |
| batched 32x4k `input_ids`, level 2 text | 204.6 | 14.0 |
| level 3, text, 80k input_ids (prints every id) | 127.0 | 9.2 |
| crash-dump-shaped redact (80k prompt + 20k `output_ids`) | 14.7 | 0.5 |

Level 3 and batched requests remain dominated by `str()` of the ids they print; the redaction on top is now a C-level scan.

Related: #44683 (closed) fixed the same logger path with a different split (it skipped the walk only for `skip_names` fields and long non-watermark lists). This PR redacts strictly by field name and additionally bounds the other `redact_watermark_secrets` callers via the core fast-path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). N/A, no user-facing change.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

| Video-MME short (96 frames) | 2.9567 | 3.6578 | +23.71% |


<details>
<summary>Mechanical move — reproducible</summary>

Save the script below outside the repository as `verify_muse_layers.py`, then run it from a checkout containing both commits with Python 3.12 and the repository's pre-commit dependencies available. It uses the verification utility already tracked in the repository, recreates the move in a temporary worktree, applies the configured formatters, and requires an empty diff against the relocation commit.

```bash
python3 /path/to/verify_muse_layers.py
```

```python
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys

FILES = (
    'muse_spark_audio.py',
    'muse_spark_bf16_moe.py',
    'muse_spark_fp4_moe.py',
    'muse_spark_int4_moe.py',
    'muse_spark_layers.py',
    'muse_spark_navit.py',
    'moe/muse_spark_megamoe.py',
    'quantization/muse_spark_nvfp4_moe.py',
)

def transform(root):
    root = Path(root)
    layers = root / 'python/sglang/srt/layers'
    target = layers / 'muse_spark'
    target.mkdir()
    replacements = {
        'sglang.srt.layers.' + path[:-3].replace('/', '.'):
        'sglang.srt.layers.muse_spark.' + Path(path).stem
        for path in FILES
    }
    tracked = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'ls-files', '-z'], cwd=root).split(b'\0')
    for entry in tracked:
        if not entry:
            continue
        path = root / entry.decode()
        if not path.is_file() or path.is_symlink():
            continue
        data = path.read_bytes()
        updated = data
        for old, new in replacements.items():
            updated = updated.replace(old.encode(), new.encode())
        if data != updated:
            path.write_bytes(updated)
    for path in FILES:
        (layers / path).rename(target / Path(path).name)
    (target / '__init__.py').touch()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd() / '.agents/skills/mechanical-refactor-verify/scripts'))
    from mechanical_refactor_reproduction_utils import verify_mechanical_refactor
    verify_mechanical_refactor(
        '90785dc87625d82e18c148826f99e01fefdbb503',
        'd6bcf11e3b9fdbf4afd6f0555411af9b36acf052',
        transform,
    )
```

Result: `PASS: transform reproduces the commit exactly.`
</details>

title: [Feat] [AMD] mamba: Store hicache checkpoints without a GPU slot
author: chien-an-chen
body:
## Motivation

Mamba radix checkpoints donate a GPU slot for every matched prefix. On a Kimi-K3 c=48 recipe that floor is `max_running_requests * 5` (480), so the GPU mamba pool stays large even when the checkpoint only needs to be reloaded from host.

## Modifications

Set `SGLANG_OPT_MAMBA_HOST_ONLY_CHECKPOINT=1` (default off). It requires `--enable-hierarchical-cache` and rejects `--enable-int8-mamba-checkpoint`. This is an environment variable, not a server argument.

With the variable unset, the server keeps the previous path: the same mamba ratio, the same donated GPU slot, the KDA ReplaySSM ring indexed by the mamba slot, a single in-flight load-back receipt, and a device match that follows GPU mamba slots. The new `InsertParams.allow_missing_mamba` bit stays false, so an insert that omits mamba still panics.

With the variable set:

- A finished request copies its flushed state into the hicache host pool and does not keep or donate a GPU slot.
- The mamba ratio drops to the live request plus the ping-pong tracking slots the extra-buffer kernel still writes. With extra buffer and overlap that is 3 (1 active + 2 ping-pong), so a 96-wide decode pool is 288 slots. `no_buffer` with page size 1 returns 1.
- The KDA ReplaySSM ring covers live requests (`max_running_requests // attn_dp + 1`) instead of every mamba slot. Padding rows are -1.
- The Rust insert accepts `mamba_host_value` without a donated `mamba_value`. A repeat insert that already found a checkpoint may omit both values; that permission is on the insert params and applies only to that insert.
- Under HiCache, a host checkpoint still counts as a device-prefix match, so the Full KV indices in front of it stay reachable. Load-back copies into the request slot and leaves the node on the host tier.

## Memory

Per-rank GPU, MI355, Kimi-K3 c=48, 96 running requests, page size 32, extra buffer, overlap, DCP 8, ReplaySSM on. The env-on pool is the size the ratio allows; `max-mamba-cache-size` has to be lowered with it. Leaving the pool at 480 keeps the 13 GB allocation and only raises the running-request cap.

| | Env off | Env on |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Mamba conv + ssm | 13.00 GB (480 slots, ratio 5) | 7.81 GB (288 slots, ratio 3) |
| KDA ReplaySSM ring | 9.14 GB (one row per mamba slot) | 1.84 GB (97 rows, one per live request) |

Env off is the earlier 0.87 log: conv 0.85 GB + ssm 12.15 GB, ring 9.14 GB. Env on conv + ssm is `ci355_ix_20261015_213315_c20e` (`max-mamba-cache-size 288`): conv 0.51 GB + ssm 7.30 GB. The same class of boot with `request_ring=True` keeps that 7.81 GB pool and sizes the ring at 97 rows (d = k = rawv = rawk = 0.306 GB, g = 0.613 GB, beta = 0.005 GB). The intermediate conv window stays 0.86 GB in both measurements. The checkpoint itself sits in the existing hicache host pool.

## Tests

Python:

- `test_flag_off_restores_original_ratios`, `test_flag_on_drops_base_but_keeps_no_buffer`, `test_host_only_drops_gpu_prefix_floor`: ratio is 3 / 4 / 5 with the flag off, and 1 / 2 / 3 with it on.
- `test_flag_off_keeps_a_donated_gpu_slot`, `test_host_only_no_buffer_frees_the_request_slot`.
- `test_kda_host_only_ring_follows_requests`: flag off charges every mamba slot; flag on charges `max_running_requests + 1` rows.
- `test_inflight_anchor_still_loads`: an anchor already in `ongoing_load_back` still load-backs. Moved out of the ratio file.
- `test_host_only_load_back_fills_request_slot_without_node_slot`, `test_host_only_second_load_back_on_inflight_anchor_retries`.

Rust (`sglang-radix-tree` mamba component):

- `missing_mamba_insert_keeps_the_existing_checkpoint_when_allowed`
- `insert_host_only_checkpoint_keeps_no_gpu_slot`
- `host_only_checkpoint_keeps_the_device_kv_prefix`
- `host_only_checkpoint_counts_gpu_kv_in_front_and_host_kv_at_the_boundary`
- `host_only_anchor_bumps_the_mamba_host_hit`
- `host_only_load_back_build_copies_into_the_request_slot_only`
- `host_only_load_back_commit_keeps_the_node_off_the_device_tier`
- `host_only_mamba_anchor_disables_branching_under_hicache`

On mi355, `test_mamba_donated_alloc_ratio.py` (18), `test_mamba_path_state_cap.py` (10), `test_replayssm_ring_accounting.py` (4), and `TestInflightAnchorStillLoads` passed. `cargo test --lib` for `sglang-radix-tree` passed 949 tests.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output change when the variable is unset. With it set, load-back still restores the request slot from the host checkpoint; the GPU tests above cover that copy.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The memory table above is the measured effect. This PR does not include a new throughput number.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).

title: [Perf] NIXL: prepared dlists for hybrid-model state transfer
author: iyastreb
body:
## Motivation

Hybrid-model state (Mamba/GDN, SWA, DSA indexer, QSA, MiniMax, MXFP8 block scales) was
sent with a fresh `initialize_xfer` per request, rebuilding and re-validating every
descriptor. With `NIXL_UCX_SGL_ENABLE=1` the data path is one SGL put per transfer, so
this host-side descriptor work is what remains on the transfer worker.

## Modifications
- At peer registration, build one strided source/destination dlist pair per decode peer
  covering all whole-slot state components; per request, one `make_prepped_xfer` with
  int32 selectors instead of one `initialize_xfer` per component.
- Decode advertises its state pool lengths (new registration frame 23) so prefill can
  size the destination dlist. An older decode without the frame stays on the generic path.
- Components the fast path cannot address (TP-sliced layouts, PP/CP/DCP, unpaired
  entries) stay generic per component. A stride mismatch is recorded at registration and
  fails every transfer to that peer with the reason, instead of addressing the decode
  with the prefill stride or killing the bootstrap thread.
- State completion is one standalone `{room}_state_{rank}` notification sent after every
  handle of the chunk settles (NIXL UCX flushes the endpoint before DONE). This replaces
  per-component attached notifs, which let decode treat the first component's arrival
  as state complete.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the same bytes move through prepared descriptors. Byte-for-byte
equivalence of the prepared and generic paths was checked with a memcpy fake agent
across Mamba, SWA on MHA, DSA with elided layers, QSA with layer ids, MLA peers with
mismatched TP, a decode with an extra DSA entry, and multi-component requests.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] diffusion/FLUX.3: Run dynamic LoRA through PrimsTS GEMMs
author: Linda-Stadter
body:
## Motivation

With dynamic LoRA, FLUX.3 disables the FlashInfer PrimsTS GEMMs and falls back to the generic quantized path, which makes LoRA requests much slower than base requests. flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6585 adds an optional `delta` epilogue input to the PrimsTS GEMMs, so the LoRA contribution can be added inside the fused kernels instead.

This PR depends on flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6585 for the speedup, but is safe to merge before that is released: the new path is only enabled when the installed FlashInfer exposes `delta` on all PrimsTS GEMM entry points. With current FlashInfer releases the behavior is unchanged.

## Modifications

- `BaseLayerWithLoRA.fused_lora_delta` computes the per-layer LoRA delta `[M, N]` (strength, runtime scale, alpha/rank, output offset, stacked QKV, SwiGLU row interleave) with cached factors.
- `flux3_fused_ops` passes the delta of LoRA-wrapped layers to the PrimsTS linear, SwiGLU and QKV/QK-norm/RoPE GEMMs. The NVFP4 packed SwiGLU handoff is skipped for layers with an active LoRA.
- PrimsTS stays enabled with LoRA, and runtime `set_lora` is accepted, only when the installed FlashInfer supports `delta` (`flux3_prims_ts_supports_lora`). With older FlashInfer, PrimsTS is disabled under `--lora-path` and late LoRA on PrimsTS weights is rejected, as before.
- Unit tests:
  - `test_lora_dynamic_delta_in_gemm.py`: the fused delta matches the LoRA layer forward (scaling, stacked QKV, runtime scale, output offset, SwiGLU order, cache invalidation, inactive layers).
  - `test_flux3_image_dit.py`: deltas reach the PrimsTS epilogues; LoRA skips the packed NVFP4 handoff.
  - `test_flux3_image_served.py`: late LoRA is rejected without `delta` support and accepted with it.

## Accuracy Tests

End-to-end images, PrimsTS + LoRA vs. the generic LoRA path (B200, 1024x1024, 50 steps, same seeds, mean PSNR over 4 images per prompt). "No LoRA" is the noise floor between the two GEMM paths; "LoRA effect" is generic LoRA vs. generic without LoRA, i.e. how much the adapter changes the image.

| Prompt | Variant | PrimsTS vs generic, no LoRA | PrimsTS vs generic, LoRA | LoRA effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Generic prompt | FP8R  | 39.8 dB | 37.0 dB | 13.8 dB |
| Generic prompt | NVFP4 | 32.8 dB | 28.8 dB | 13.7 dB |
| Adapter trigger prompt | FP8R  | 36.4 dB | 31.0 dB | 9.7 dB |
| Adapter trigger prompt | NVFP4 | 30.1 dB | 26.2 dB | 10.0 dB |

With LoRA, the two paths stay within 3-5 dB of their no-LoRA agreement, far above the 10-14 dB change the adapter itself makes.

Single DiT forward (FP8R): the LoRA effect (LoRA output minus base output) of the PrimsTS path matches the generic path with cosine similarity 0.92; swapping the SwiGLU value/gate column order drops it to 0.26.

The kernel-level `delta` epilogue is covered by the FlashInfer tests in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6585; the SGLang delta is unit-tested against the LoRA layer forward. With FlashInfer 0.7.1 (no `delta`), PrimsTS is disabled under `--lora-path` as before, and the unit tests pass against both FlashInfer versions.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B200, FLUX.3 image, 1024x1024, 50 steps, rank-16 LoRA, `bench_offline_throughput`, median latency per image, FlashInfer built from flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6585:

| Variant | LoRA, generic path | LoRA, PrimsTS + delta | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| FP8R  | 4.20 s | 3.29 s | 1.28x |
| NVFP4 | 3.79 s | 2.72 s | 1.39x |

title: [Perf] DSv4.1: Skip discarded KV rows during window commit
author: Oasis-Git
body:
[codex/claude generated]

## Motivation

Request-window commit copies every input KV row, routing discarded rows to a shared sink even though only the final window survives. Long prefills therefore move KV bytes that will never be read.

## Modifications

Add a Triton commit kernel that skips KV loads and stores for discarded rows, computes retained ring destinations, and writes position tags in the same launch. Keep history validation and the existing window retention policy unchanged. The launch grid still covers all input rows; this change removes discarded-row memory traffic rather than bounding the grid.

## Accuracy Tests

The tested patch passed 22 local tests on GB300: 4 packed-copy/commit GPU tests, 5 encoder replay CPU tests, and 13 compressed-pool CPU tests. Added byte-exact coverage for both KV layouts, ragged and 16K-token input, ring wrap, padded strides, untouched discarded destinations, layer isolation, and CUDA graph metadata refresh. These checks do not establish full-model semantic accuracy.

Transplanted onto main at 456231e25: all three changed files are byte-identical to the tested candidate, their baseline versions are unchanged, and syntax/diff checks pass. GPU results below were measured on base 30ca1dffc, not rerun on the new main revision. Pre-commit passed on the tested patch; CI on this PR is pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

On 4x GB300, TP4/EP4 with encoder bounded replay, the unchanged high-concurrency replay subset had median E2E latency of 3561.52 ms before this change and 3299.75 / 3315.78 ms in two candidate runs (6.9–7.4% lower). All 816 request/usage maps and cached-token totals matched. One baseline and two candidate runs were measured; DSPARK used simulated acceptance 5.4.

A 16K-token eager commit microbenchmark decreased from 142.24 us to 14.79 us. This includes destination calculation and tag updates and is not an end-to-end speedup. Later direct-packed and sparse-prefill experiments are excluded from this PR and these measurements.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the tested patch with pre-commit.
- [x] Add focused unit tests.
- [x] Provide scoped correctness and speed results with limitations.
- [ ] Run upstream CI on the PR revision.

title: [Perf] deepseek_v4: fuse block-FP8 shared experts into MegaMoE for any 32-aligned block size
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

Profiling DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash DEP2 prefill on GB300 (MegaAttention, MegaMoE, Mega-mHC, decoder bounded replay, eager prefill, 16K tokens per rank per step) shows the MegaMoE kernel instantiated with `kNumSharedExperts=0`, and the shared expert running as a standalone MLP instead: per layer two dense MXFP8 GEMMs, two activation quantizes, a `silu_mul_clamp` and an `add_`.

On one 16K-token cold prefill chunk per rank (rank 0, torch profiler):

| | Per step |
|---|---:|
| Dense MXFP8 GEMM launches, of which shared-expert | 210, 80 |
| Shared-expert GEMM time | about 18 ms |
| Shared-expert quantize, silu and add launches | 80 + 40 + 40 |
| Total kernel launches | 1,812 |

The eager prefill step is dispatch-bound (median inter-kernel gap 41 µs, about 65 µs of idle per launch), so the ~200 removed launches matter as much as the kernel time.

## Why the fusion was off

`should_fuse_mega_moe_shared_experts` required `shared_experts_weight_block_size == [128, 128]`. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's checkpoint quantizes the shared experts as block-FP8 `[32, 32]` with `scale_fmt: ue8m0`, so the gate silently fell back even though `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS` defaults on.

## Modifications

- `mega_moe_shared_block_size_supported`: accept any `(block_m, block_k)` with `block_k % 32 == 0`.
- `_transform_mega_moe_shared_sf`: expand the checkpoint block scale to the kernel's per-row 1x32 UE8M0 layout (each row of a block repeats the block's scale; each 32-wide K slice inside a K block repeats it), using the grouped `transform_sf_into_required_layout` API with a singleton group for the per-row recipe, the same way the routed experts are transformed. The existing `[128, 128]` recipe path and the DeepGEMM-packed int32 path are unchanged.
- Numerics: with `ue8m0` checkpoint scales the expansion is exact; for non-power-of-two scales the UE8M0 cast is the rounding the routed experts already take (`disable_ue8m0_cast=False`), same as before for 128x128.

## Measured

GB300, DEP2 (TP2 + DP attention, EP2), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MegaMoE, Mega-mHC, decoder bounded replay, eager prefill, 16K-token prefill budget per rank, rank 0. Same build with the fusion on (job 3467) and off through `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS=0` (job 3468). The trace shows the engagement: the MegaMoE kernel is instantiated with `kNumSharedExperts=1` (`sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_impl<17280u, 5120u, 2304u, 384u, 1u, ...>`, `0u` with the fusion off) and the per-layer shared-expert quantize, GEMM, silu and add launches are gone.

| One 16K-token cold chunk per rank | fusion off | fusion on |
|---|---:|---:|
| Step time, unprofiled, median of 3 (ms) | 241 | 235 |
| 128K-token prompt in eight 16K chunks, unprofiled (ms) | 1,925 | 1,842 |
| Profiled step annotation (ms) | 267 | 240 |
| Kernel launches per step | 1,847 | 1,607 |
| Dense MXFP8 GEMM launches per step | 212 | 132 |
| MoE section per layer (mHC kernel to the next layer's mHC kernel), sum over 21 layers (ms) | 107.0 | 100.8 |

Every layer's MoE section is shorter, by 0.17 to 0.44 ms. The MegaMoE kernel itself grows by 0.35 to 0.45 ms per layer since it now carries the shared expert; the six removed launches were worth 0.6 to 0.7 ms of kernel time plus their dispatch gaps.

Before: fusion off, layer 6, 4.53 ms and 13 kernels between the two mHC kernels.

![fusion off, layer 6 MoE section](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kpham-sgl/sglang/assets-prefill-h2h-2026-10-16/prefill-h2h-2026-10-16/pr44837-before-fusion-off-job3468-moe-section.jpg)

After: fusion on, same layer, 4.24 ms and 9 kernels.

![fusion on, layer 6 MoE section](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kpham-sgl/sglang/assets-prefill-h2h-2026-10-16/prefill-h2h-2026-10-16/pr44837-after-fusion-on-job3467-moe-section.jpg)

Not run yet: the GSM8K native-acceptance gate against the unfused path.

title: [Perf] deepseek_v4: fold the MegaAttention query layout into wq_b for block-FP8-as-MXFP8 checkpoints
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

`setup_mega_attention` folds the MegaAttention query head layout into `wq_b`'s rows (`interleave_query_rows`) only when `wq_b` is a native MXFP8 linear. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash ships a `[32, 32]` block-FP8 checkpoint whose dense linears run through the same FlashInfer MXFP8 GEMM via the block-FP8-as-MXFP8 view (`block_fp8_mxfp8_ready`), so `mega_wq_b_permuted` stays false and every layer packs the query at forward time with `pack_query`: a `new_zeros` of the `[tokens, 64, 512]` bf16 query and a strided transpose copy into it.

Measured on GB300, DEP2 (TP2 + DP attention, EP2, MegaMoE, decoder bounded replay, Mega-mHC on), one cold 16,384-token prefill chunk per rank, torch profiler:

| per 16K step, rank 0 | count | per launch | total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `aten::new_zeros` (vectorized fill) | 40 | 141 µs | 5.7 ms |
| `aten::copy_` (strided `direct_copy` elementwise) | 40 | 691 µs | 27.6 ms |

That is 33 ms of a 322 ms step (10%) and 80 launches on an eager step that is dispatch-bound (median inter-kernel gap 41 µs). Per layer it writes ~1.2 GB of zeros and moves ~2.4 GB through a non-contiguous copy.

## Modifications

- `_wq_b_uses_flashinfer_mxfp8` also accepts a block-FP8 `wq_b` served as MXFP8 (`block_fp8_as_mxfp8` on the FlashInfer CUTLASS / CuTe-DSL backend), so `mega_wq_b_permuted` is set for this checkpoint.
- In `setup_mega_attention`, for that case: `interleave_query_rows` moves 16-row groups, so the `[32, 32]` block scale is refined to 16 rows, permuted the same way as the weight, and rebound as `weight_scale_inv` with `weight_block_size = [16, 32]`. The existing post-load pass then builds the swizzled MXFP8 scale from it as for any block-FP8-as-MXFP8 layer. The native MXFP8 path is unchanged.

After this `pack_query` is skipped for the block-FP8 checkpoint exactly as for native MXFP8 ones.

Numerics: the same FP8 bytes and the same e8m0 scales reach the GEMM, only in the row order the attention kernel already consumes; refining a 32-row block scale to 16-row blocks is exact.

## Measured

GB300, DEP2 (TP2 + DP attention, EP2), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MegaMoE, Mega-mHC, decoder bounded replay, eager prefill, 16K-token prefill budget per rank, rank 0. Main (job 3470, `2d3dd3168d`) against this branch (job 3476). Startup log on the branch: `MegaAttention wq_b query-layout permute: applied=True (block-fp8 served as mxfp8)`.

| Unprofiled, median of 3 | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| One 16K-token cold chunk per rank (ms) | 247 | 235 |
| 128K-token prompt in eight 16K chunks (ms) | 1,906 | 1,764 |

| Profiled 16K step | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `new_zeros` fill and strided `copy_` launches per step | 80 (33.9 ms) | 0 |
| Kernel launches per step | 1,847 | 1,756 |
| Attention section per layer (mHC kernel to the MoE block's mHC kernel), median over layers (ms) | 5.03 | 3.39 |

The cached-prefix cells of the same run moved both ways by up to 15% between runs and are not reported.

Before: main, layer 6, 5.00 ms and 17 launches between the two mHC kernels; the fill (264 µs) and the strided copy (1.30 ms) sit between `k_norm_rope` and the attention kernel.

![main, layer 6 attention section](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kpham-sgl/sglang/assets-prefill-h2h-2026-10-16/prefill-h2h-2026-10-16/main-job3470-layer6-attention-section.jpg)

After: this branch, same layer, 3.36 ms and 15 launches.

![this PR, layer 6 attention section](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kpham-sgl/sglang/assets-prefill-h2h-2026-10-16/prefill-h2h-2026-10-16/pr44838-job3476-layer6-attention-section.jpg)

title: [Perf] deepseek_v4: run FlashInfer autotune for block-FP8 models served as MXFP8
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

Torch-profiler trace of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash DEP2 prefill on GB300 (MegaAttention, MegaMoE, DSpark, 16K-token prefill budget per rank), one 16K-token cold chunk per rank, rank 0:

| Dense MXFP8 GEMM (`flashinfer_mm_mxfp8` → CuTe-DSL `dense_blockscaled_gemm_sm100`) | |
|---|---:|
| Launches per step | 210 (130 after #44837 removes the shared-expert MLP) |
| Per launch | 221 µs |
| Total per step | 46.5 ms of a 322 ms step |
| Shapes at M=16,384 | fused wqkv_a N=1792 K=5120; wq_b N=32768 K=1280; wo_b N=5120 K=8192 |

Every one of these launches runs on FlashInfer's untuned fallback tactic: the server log has no autotune pass at all, and `Fp8LinearMethod.apply` keeps `pin_tactic=True` for block-FP8-as-MXFP8 layers until the prefill autotune hook sets `mxfp8_prefill_autotune_min_tokens`, which never happens.

## Why

`should_run_flashinfer_autotune` treats FP8 dense GEMMs as tunable only for `quantization == "mxfp8"` (and modelopt per-tensor FP8). DeepSeek-V4.1 checkpoints are block-FP8 `[32, 32]` with `ue8m0` scales, which `Fp8LinearMethod` serves through the MXFP8 view on FlashInfer CuTe-DSL, the same tunable `mm_mxfp8` op. The model already has `autotune_prefill_kernels` / `wants_prefill_autotune` (from #38798) to tune exactly those GEMMs at the prefill token ceiling, but it is only reached from the gated autotune pass, so it never ran.

## Modifications

- `should_run_flashinfer_autotune`: also return True when a resident FP8 linear serves block-FP8 as MXFP8 on a FlashInfer CuTe-DSL/CUTLASS backend (`_model_serves_block_fp8_as_mxfp8_on_flashinfer`). The existing decode-shaped pass and the DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill hook then run and persist tactics under `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR/flashinfer/autotune/...` exactly as for `mxfp8` models, so restarts stay fast.
- Drops the stale "SGLang temporarily skips mxfp8_gemm by default due to an IMA" help text on `--flashinfer-autotune-skip-ops`; `FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_WORKAROUND_SKIPS` has been empty since #33962.
- Numerics: tuned tactics change only the GEMM tile/cluster schedule. Batch-invariant and deterministic modes keep the pinned tactic as before (`pin_tactic` override in `Fp8LinearMethod.apply` is unchanged).

## Measured

GB300, DEP2 (TP2 + DP attention, EP2), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MegaMoE, Mega-mHC, decoder bounded replay, eager prefill, 16K-token prefill budget per rank, rank 0. Main (job 3470, `2d3dd3168d`) against this branch (job 3471). Startup log on the branch, both ranks: `Running FlashInfer autotune with cache: .../flashinfer/autotune/0.7.1/sm103/.../rank_tp0_pp0_dp0.json`.

| Unprofiled, median of 3 | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| One 16K-token cold chunk per rank (ms) | 247 | 235 |
| 128K-token prompt in eight 16K chunks (ms) | 1,906 | 1,773 |
| 8 x 2K fresh tokens on 90K cached tokens per rank (ms) | 672 | 669 |

| Profiled 16K step | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Dense MXFP8 GEMM launches per step | 212 | 212 |
| Dense MXFP8 GEMM time per step (ms) | 46.5 | 29.9 |
| Mean per launch (µs) | 220 | 141 |
| Layer 6, fused wqkv_a / wq_b / wo_b GEMM (µs) | 160 / 563 / 721 | 88 / 449 / 369 |
| Attention section, layer 6 (ms) | 5.00 | 4.48 |

The step is dispatch-bound, so most of the 16.6 ms of removed GEMM time hides behind launch gaps on a single chunk; it shows fully on the 128K prompt.

title: [Fix] megamoe: Support EPLB rebalance on SM100
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Register the SM100 MegaMoE per-expert tensors that are copies of the expert parameters as parameters of the experts module: the UTCCP-transposed L1/L2 scales in `build_mega_moe_experts_weights`, and the NVFP4 `mega_l1_alphas`, `mega_l2_alphas` and `mega_l2_act_scales` in `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod._build_mega_moe_weights`. EPLB moves each expert's slice of every routed-expert parameter (`get_moe_weights`), so a rebalance now moves these copies with the weights they come from; before, moved experts kept the previous experts' scales
- SM90 and ROCm MegaMoE already read the parameters EPLB rewrites; unchanged

No behavior change without `--enable-eplb`, except that these tensors now appear in `named_parameters()`.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP2 on 2 x GB300 (`--tp 2 --dp 2 --ep-size 2 --enable-dp-attention --moe-a2a-backend megamoe`, `--eplb-rebalance-num-iterations 32` when EPLB is on), GSM8K with sgl-eval, 200 examples, greedy, thinking off:

|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| main | on | 142 | 72.50 | 465.4 |
| this PR | on | 35 | 97.00 | 127.2 |
| this PR | off | 0 | 97.50 | 127.6 |

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4.1: Serve prompt-logprob requests under decoder SWA bounded replay
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `late_layer_whole_extend` picks the requests that read prompt rows: prompt logprobs, or every hidden state outside DSpark. Their late-layer tail is their whole extend, so these requests are served instead of raising in the forward and taking every scheduler down.
- `late_layer_tail_layout(whole_extend=...)` gives every row of a whole extend its plain sliding window, so no row of these requests is truncated; other requests keep the window tail and its floor. Both the CUDA and the HIP backend use it.
- A step whose tail outgrows the prefill CUDA graph's tail block runs eagerly. The backend answers the same question from the schedule batch (`vote_prefill_cuda_graph`), which the DP prefill-graph vote calls, so no DP rank replays the graph while another runs the step eagerly.
- DSpark's exemption comes from the server's speculative algorithm, since prefill-graph capture batches carry DSpark's `FULL` capture mode without it.
- `_check_late_layer_tail_readers` now raises only when the tail misses rows a reader needs; the DSpark logits path moves prompt-logprob starts into the tail.
- `--enable-return-hidden-states` makes every tail a whole extend, so decoder SWA bounded replay now resolves off with it; passing both flags still runs correctly.
- The DeepSeek-V4.1 cookbook and the flag's help now say that prompt-logprob requests are served, and that RL rollouts whose logprobs must match the trainer should pass `--no-enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay`.
- Unit tests in `test/registered/unit/layers/test_dsv41_late_layer_tail_readers.py`.

Supersedes #41448 and #42719.

No behavior change for requests that read no prompt rows: their tail layout, prefill-graph decision, and logits path are unchanged.

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] modelopt-nvfp4: Read w13 global scales in the TRT-LLM [up, gate] order
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

On the FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE backend, ModelOpt NVFP4 experts whose gate (w1) and up (w3) global scales (`weight_scale_2`) differ are dequantized with the two scales swapped. Under this layout the loader stores w13 rows, and their per-tensor scales, as `[up, gate]`, but `_compute_gemm1_alphas` (#27588) reads column 0 as gate.

Standard ModelOpt exports tie gate/up scales (NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer#1033), so most checkpoints are unaffected. Before Model-Optimizer 0.45 (NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer#1560), experts never reached during calibration could stay untied, e.g. 6 of 3,840 in `nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4`. It was reported on an in-house checkpoint with untied scales. Online NVFP4 (`nvfp4_online.py`) quantizes gate/up together with one shared scale, so it is unaffected.

## Modifications

- `_compute_gemm1_alphas` takes `up_first` and reads the columns in w13 row order; `process_weights_after_loading` passes `up_first=self.use_flashinfer_trtllm_weight_layout`. Other backends are unchanged.
- The TRT-LLM SwiGLU params move into `_compute_trtllm_gated_act_params`. Beta is added to the raw up half, so it now uses `g1_alphas_up`. The kernel applies one clamp limit to both raw halves, which can't be exact for both when their scales differ; it stays in gate-half units and logs a warning.
- Unit tests: the beta/clamp units and the SiTU branch of the moved helper.
- E2E (weekly, 4x B200): serve [`mmangkad/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4-untied-gate-up`](https://huggingface.co/mmangkad/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4-untied-gate-up) on `flashinfer_trtllm` and require GSM8K >= 0.90 (sgl-eval). Locally: 0.960 with this PR, 0.305 on the base commit.

## Accuracy Tests

`mmangkad/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4-untied-gate-up` is `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4` with `up_proj.weight_scale_2 *= 4` and `up_proj.weight_scale /= 4` in every expert: gate/up differ, dequantized weights are bit-identical.

sgl-eval 0.1.3 GSM8K, 200 examples, `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm`, TP1, 1x B300 (Qwen3 cookbook recipe, but with an NVFP4 checkpoint and a forced MoE backend):

| Checkpoint | Thinking, before | Thinking, after | Non-thinking, before | Non-thinking, after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Original (tied) | 98.0% | 97.5% | 95.0% | 95.0% |
| Untied | **51.0%** | **97.0%** | **29.0%** | **95.0%** |

Thinking: temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, max_tokens 32768. Non-thinking: temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8, max_tokens 2048.

Kernel checks for the SwiGLU params: one expert with gate/up scale ratio 0.30, run through `prepare_static_weights_for_trtllm_fp4_moe` and `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` against a dequantized reference (alpha 1.702). Relative error; FP4 noise floor 0.09.

Beta: `1/up_alpha` gives 0.089, `1/gate_alpha` gives 0.508.

Clamp, real limit L, kernel given P. Each row is a hypothesis for the real thresholds the kernel applies:

| Real thresholds | P = L/gate_alpha | P = L/up_alpha |
|---|---|---|
| gate <= P * gate_alpha, abs(up) <= P * up_alpha (both raw) | **0.072** | **0.133** |
| both at P * up_alpha | 0.608 | 0.742 |
| gate only, up unclamped | 0.611 | 0.873 |
| both at P * gate_alpha | 1.989 | 2.155 |

The kernel clamps both raw halves at P, so with untied scales no single P gives both halves the real limit L.

title: [Feat] ComfyUI: Add online INT8 quantization for BF16 Qwen-Image-2.1 single files
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
## Motivation

Users on 24 to 32 GB GPUs often already have the BF16 ComfyUI file for Qwen-Image-2.1 but cannot use online quantization with it. Today they have to find and download a separate pre-quantized file.

Two things blocked this:

1. The plugin preflight rejected `quantization` for any ComfyUI single file.
2. The worker's single-file loader (`comfyui_checkpoints/spec.py`) only built a quant config from per-layer markers in the file. A BF16 file has none, so `--quantization` was silently ignored and the DiT stayed in BF16.

## Modifications

- `runtime/loader/comfyui_checkpoints/spec.py`: when a single file has no quant markers and `quantization` is set, resolve it through the existing `resolve_transformer_quant_load_spec` (same path native directories use), build the matching `WeightLoadPlan`, and run the quant post-load hooks. Methods that need serialized weights (e.g. `mxfp8`) raise a clear error instead of being ignored.
- Plugin `core/preflight.py`: allow `convrot_int8` on BF16 Qwen-Image-2.1 single files. Other models and other methods stay rejected with a clear message.
- Options tooltip and README updated.
- Tests: worker regression test (quant config, param dtype, load device and hooks reach the loader) and preflight accept/reject cases.

Scope is Qwen-Image-2.1 + INT8 ConvRot only. FP8 was tested and left out (results below). Other single-file models can be added once validated.

## Accuracy and speed (Modal, L40S)

ComfyUI v0.41.0, headless API graph through `SGLDUNETLoader` + `SGLDOptions`. `Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1` turbo file, 1024x1024, 8 steps, euler/simple, cfg 1, seed 42. Time is the second (warm) run. Peak GPU is whole-process `nvidia-smi` (includes ComfyUI's text encoder and VAE). PSNR/SSIM are against SGLD BF16 on the same seed.

| Run | Sampling time | Peak GPU | PSNR / SSIM vs SGLD BF16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Native ComfyUI BF16 | 3.43 s | 22.9 GB | 28.19 dB / 0.969 |
| SGLD BF16 | 3.29 s | 26.9 GB | reference |
| **SGLD online INT8 (this PR)** | **2.35 s** | 23.5 GB | **28.55 dB / 0.966** |
| SGLD online FP8 (not enabled) | 4.49 s | 23.5 GB | 21.74 dB / 0.855 |

Worker log for the INT8 run:

```
convrot_int8: quantized 224 linear layers (13.00 GiB of BF16 weights -> 6.50 GiB INT8; jit 0, comfy_kitchen 224), left 0 in BF16
```

INT8 is about 1.4x faster than BF16 and halves DiT weight memory, and its distance from BF16 is in line with native ComfyUI vs SGLD BF16. On L40S (CC 8.9) the JIT INT8 kernels are unavailable, so this ran on the comfy_kitchen backend.

### Why FP8 is not enabled

Online FP8 quantizes the same 224 layers but drifts from BF16 and is slower than BF16 on L40S. Keeping some layers in BF16 (`--quantization-ignored-layers`) did not fix it consistently (2 seeds each):

| FP8 variant | Time | SSIM (seed 42 / 1234) | PSNR dB (seed 42 / 1234) |
|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 reference | 3.17 s | | |
| FP8, all layers | 4.36 s | 0.855 / 0.854 | 21.7 / 20.8 |
| keep `img_mlp.out` in BF16 | 3.75 s | 0.814 / 0.866 | 20.6 / 21.7 |
| keep `attn.to_out` in BF16 | 4.18 s | 0.915 / 0.876 | 24.0 / 21.4 |
| keep both | 3.55 s | 0.879 / 0.884 | 22.6 / 21.8 |
| keep blocks 0 and 31 in BF16 | 4.23 s | 0.955 / 0.881 | 27.2 / 22.0 |

So the plugin rejects `fp8` for single files for now.

### Pre-quantized file note

Loading Comfy-Org's own `qwen_image_2.1_turbo_int8_convrot.safetensors` through `SGLDUNETLoader` fails on current main with `Parameter transformer_blocks.1.attn.comfy_attention.config not found in custom model state dict`. That is the serialized-marker path, which this PR does not touch; I can open a separate issue.

## Testing

- Unit tests on Modal (`test_comfyui_checkpoint_spec.py`, `test_comfyui_options.py`, `test_comfyui_generator.py`, `test_comfyui_qwen_image21.py`): 64 passed, 3 skipped.
- Same new tests against unmodified main: 5 failed (the 3 worker regression tests and 2 preflight cases), confirming they guard the change.
- End-to-end ComfyUI runs on L40S as above.

## Limitations

- Only Qwen-Image-2.1 single files are allowed in the plugin; Flux, Qwen-Image, Z-Image and MiniMax-H3 keep the existing rejection until validated.
- FSDP inference with online ConvRot INT8 on single files was not tested.

title: [Fix] kda: Align graph tracking branch dtype with the recurrent state pool
author: Jzz1943
body:
## Motivation

KDA graph tracking can read an FP32 chunk-boundary snapshot or a recurrent-state pool entry. With a BF16 state pool, these branches produce different Triton types, causing compilation to fail before the final store cast.

Observed during GLM-5.3-Flash prefill BCG initialization with BF16 recurrent state:

```text
triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError: at 19:4:
    stride_h_row,
    numel,
    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
):
    r = tl.program_id(0)
    mode = tl.load(track_mode + r)
    if mode == 0:
        return
    dst = tl.load(track_dst + r).to(tl.int64)
    offs = tl.program_id(1) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
    mask = offs < numel
    if mode == 1:
    ^
AssertionError("Mismatched type for val between then block (<['1024'], bf16>) and else block (<['1024'], fp32>)")
```

A cast after the `if/else` cannot resolve this error: Triton requires matching types for `val` when merging the branches, before compiling the subsequent cast.

## Modifications

Cast the snapshot to the state-pool element type before the branches merge. The stored dtype is unchanged, and FP32 state pools retain their existing behavior.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated in GLM-5.3-Flash PD serving on 8 × H200 with BF16 recurrent state and MTP516: GSM8K, 1,314 examples × 2 rounds, scored **95.4% / 95.9%**. These results are from the existing integration configuration containing this fix and the separate Decode RadixCache changes, not a new full-model run on this rebased PR branch.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

This is a correctness fix; no inference speed improvement is claimed.

## Checklist

title: [Fix] moe: Renormalize per-rank shared-slot routing over routed experts only
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #44913
* #44912
* __->__ #44904
* #44901

## Motivation

With fused shared experts in per-rank slots (`--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` with a DeepEP-class or `megamoe` a2a backend), every MoE layer renormalized its routed weights over one routed expert too many on CUDA, so the routed experts it kept summed to about 0.85-0.97 instead of 1.0.

How it happened:

1. On the per-rank slot path `select_experts` gives the router no shared slot (`num_fused_shared_experts=0`), because `_post_process_topk_ids` appends the shared column afterwards. On aiter it also gives the router the routed count, `top_k - num_fused_shared_experts`. Off aiter every router call kept `top_k` (`num_routed_topk if _use_aiter else top_k`), which counts the shared slot.
2. So the router selected `top_k` routed experts, one more than the model's `num_experts_per_tok`, and renormalized their weights to sum to 1.
3. `remap_topk_for_per_rank_shared_slots` then overwrote the last column with the home-rank shared expert.
4. The routed experts kept sum to `sum(top K) / sum(top K+1)`, per token, in every layer. The CUDA routers return their top-k sorted by score, so the kept experts are the right ones; only their weights shrink.

#36515 (non-grouped routers) and #40943 (grouped routers) gave the router 0 shared slots on this path. That fixed aiter, where the router already gets the routed count, and left CUDA in the state above. Before them, CUDA gave the router `top_k` with the shared slot, which selects the routed count and renormalizes over it.

Kept routed weight sum per token, one H200, 64 tokens of random logits, EP8, rank 3, one shared expert:

| Router path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| grouped sigmoid + bias, 256 experts, top-8 (DeepSeek-V3 shape; FlashInfer router after the fix, Triton fallback before) | 0.873-0.913 | 1.0000 |
| grouped sigmoid + bias, 384 experts in 8 groups, top-8 | 0.873-0.914 | 1.0000 |
| grouped, one group, sigmoid + bias, 384 experts, top-8 (Kimi-K2 shape) | 0.873-0.919 | 1.0000 |
| grouped softmax, no bias, 64 experts, top-6 | 0.886-0.967 | 1.0000 |
| ungrouped sqrtsoftplus + bias, 256 experts, top-6 (DeepSeek-V4) | 0.850-0.885 | 1.0000 |
| ungrouped sigmoid + bias, 256 experts, top-8 | 0.877-0.912 | 1.0000 |
| ungrouped softmax, 128 experts, top-8 | 0.909-0.949 | 1.0000 |
| `HashTopK` (DeepSeek-V4 hash layers), torch and fused kernel | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 vision routing on MegaMoE | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |

In every row the routed experts equal routing without fusion (64/64 rows) before and after; the shared column is the home-rank slot with weight `1/routed_scaling_factor`.

Affected: CUDA, and other platforms without aiter, with shared-experts fusion on a per-rank backend (`deepep`, `mooncake`, `mori`, `pplx`, `megamoe`); for the DeepSeek family that takes `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`. The original per-rank normalization bug does not affect aiter, Waterfill, the global fused slot (no a2a backend), runs without fusion, `HashTopK` and the DeepSeek-V4.1 vision routing, whose routers already select the routed experts alone.

Two related problems on the same path are fixed here too:

- **FlashInfer's DeepSeek router ignores `renormalize`.** `fused_topk_deepseek` always normalizes the selected weights, and its ninth parameter is `launch_with_pdl`, which sglang's wrapper called `renormalize`. With routed-only sizing the per-rank top-8 path now fits that router (top-9 did not), so a `renormalize=False` configuration would have been normalized. Configurations without fusion or with the global slot already were, within that router's shapes. Grouped sigmoid routing with a bias, 256 experts in 8 groups, top-8, `renormalize=False`, zero logits (each raw weight is sigmoid(0) = 0.5): before this PR 0.125 per expert without fusion and 0.5 with a per-rank slot; with this PR's first version 0.125 for both; now 0.5 for both.
- **Padded rows on the per-rank path.** The append shifted a padded row's `-1` to `-1 - num_fused_shared_experts` and gave it a live home-rank shared slot, so padded rows did not leave top-k as `-1`. `HashTopK` and the vision routing already mask after their append.

The `renormalize=False` guard also exposes the Triton global shared-slot path. That path previously wrote `sum(selected routed scores) / rsf` before normalization, so disabling normalization made the shared output depend on the routed-score sum (4x for eight zero-logit sigmoid selections). It now writes a shared weight of 1 when rsf is folded, otherwise 1/rsf, after processing the routed weights. The dynamic-bias torch route receives the corresponding repair from #44901.

## Modifications

- `select_experts` decides once, for every router, what the router is asked for: where `_post_process_topk_ids` appends the shared columns (aiter, per-rank slots), the routed count with no shared slot; otherwise `top_k` with the shared slots, as before. The values are unchanged on aiter, on the global slot and without fusion.
- `remap_topk_for_per_rank_shared_slots` takes the routed columns and appends the shared ones, the contract `fused_append_remap_shared_experts_deepep` already has on aiter. Routers that still write shared placeholders (the per-token-bias router, the DeepSeek-V4.1 vision routing, `HashTopK`) have them dropped before the append. On CUDA the EPLB remap splits off shared columns only when the router wrote them, and padded rows are masked again after the append.
- `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` takes the FlashInfer branch only when renormalizing; otherwise the Triton router, which honors `renormalize`, serves the call. The wrapper's last parameter is renamed `launch_with_pdl`, and the global shared columns that branch appends take `fused_shared_expert_weight(...)`.
- `RoutedExpertsCapturer.capture` pads routed-only ids (the device width minus the fused shared experts) to its device width and raises on any other width; the host side already keeps only `num_experts_per_tok` columns. The per-rank path now captures routed-only ids, and without the pad `--enable-return-routed-experts` would fail with a shape mismatch.
- The fused aiter kernel's docstrings name its eager twin.

## Tests

On one H200 (driver 595.71.05, torch 2.14.1+cu130, flashinfer 0.7.2, triton 3.8.0), for this branch (`03d13ebf8b`), its base #44901 (`bd4de12cfa`) and this PR's previous head merged with that base:

- `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_fused_shared_expert_scaling.py::test_per_rank_slot_routes_like_no_fusion` (CPU): `select_experts` with a per-rank slot keeps the routed experts and weights of routing without fusion, summing to 1. Fails on the base, passes here.
- `test/registered/moe/test_fused_append_remap_per_rank_shared_slots.py` (CUDA):
  - `TestSelectExpertsPerRankSharedSlots::test_routes_like_no_fusion`: the same property through five CUDA routers (the DeepSeek-V3 grouped router, the Triton grouped fallback, torch grouped routing, the DeepSeek-V4 sqrtsoftplus router, softmax). Fails on the base for all five, passes here.

title: [Perf] mhc: Parallelize small-batch post across hidden tiles
author: leonardHONG
body:
## Motivation

`mhc_post_tilelang` currently launches one CTA per token and iterates over hidden-dimension tiles inside that CTA. For the GLM-5.3-Flash verification shape `M=24, H=4096, hc=4`, this launches only 24 CTAs.

This change distributes hidden tiles across CTAs for small batches. The same shape now launches 96 CTAs, improving parallelism while preserving the per-element accumulation order and BF16 writeback.

## Modifications

- Add `num_h_blocks=1` to `mhc_post_tilelang`.
- Launch a two-dimensional grid over tokens and hidden blocks.
- Map each iteration to `i_h_iter * num_h_blocks + i_h_block`.
- For `M <= 256`, split the hidden dimension using the existing 1024-element tile size and GCD adjustment.
- For larger batches, retain one hidden block per token.
- Keep scheduling, sampling, and the existing mHC fusion threshold unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

- Eager and CUDA Graph kernel checks cover multiple batch sizes, hidden sizes, and hc configurations, with bitwise-equal outputs.
- Integrated core checks cover real M24 input, synthetic M6/M24/M48/M256/M512/M8192, and H3072.
- Graph checks update inputs before replay.
- Ruff lint, Ruff formatting, and repository-configured isort passed.
- The final formatting-only revision is AST-equivalent to the GPU-tested source.
- Three service A/B responses still differ in their initial text prefix; the cause has not been established.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Measured on **4 x B300 / SM103, TP4**, using:

- GLM-5.3-Flash, checkpoint revision prefix `46a050bec130`
- SGLang base `f7ad4345b86d147a1c3095a3cebabca9a33ebaa1`
- Torch 2.14.1, FlashInfer 0.7.1, Transformers 5.19

One baseline/candidate pair was measured without profiling. Each arm ran C1/C4/C8 with 30/40/80 measured requests, respectively, after 64 warmup requests per concurrency. Warmup output length was 32 tokens; measured output length was 1024 tokens. Inputs used the same seeded random ShareGPT workload with nominal 8K input length and chat templating.

title: [Refactor] moe: Split the two meanings of num_fused_shared_experts
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #44913
* __->__ #44912
* #44904
* #44901

## Motivation

`num_fused_shared_experts` carries two meanings: shared experts executed by the fused MoE layer, and shared id/weight slots emitted by ordinary TopK. Waterfill needs fused computation while appending the shared slots after ordinary routing. Conflating these quantities makes TopK and HashTopK rewrite their constructor arguments for Waterfill.

## Modifications

- Keep `num_fused_shared_experts` for the experts-layer layout and use `num_shared_topk_slots` for shared output positions emitted by ordinary routing, before Waterfill expansion.
- Derive ordinary routing slots once in `shared_topk_slots`: the fused count normally, zero when Waterfill writes the slots later. Construct TopK/HashTopK from these meanings directly.
- Update router consumers and layout helpers; retain existing kernel interfaces.
- Guard the single-writer invariant: the router or Waterfill emits the shared slots exactly once, including unfused and empty-output cases.

#44913 places both quantities in one immutable model-owned configuration and exposes it through `get_model().shared_experts`.

- Latest naming change (`456745b5ee` → `6a5c963f49`): inverse-renaming yields identical Python ASTs in all 15 changed files. Applicable pre-commit hooks pass.

Coverage limits: no full-model Waterfill, fused-draft, distributed DeepEP/MegaMoE, AMD, NPU or XPU run in this validation. The GLM smoke is a limited equivalence check, not an accuracy benchmark.

title: [Perf] DSv4.1: Reduce BCG metadata memory
author: Oasis-Git
body:
[codex/claude generated]

## Motivation

With encoder bounded replay disabled, DSv4.1 breakable prefill graphs retain oversized page tables and duplicate index buffers across capture buckets and compression ratios.

## Modifications

- Bound low-ratio BCG page-table width by the existing prefill graph context limit in both capture and metadata refresh. Eager context support and graph admission limits stay unchanged.
- Reuse full-metadata index storage across serial capture buckets, keeping c1/c2, raw/page, and full/tail buffers independent and retaining old allocations when capacity grows.
- Share fully overwritten per-layer combined-index scratch between c1/c2 within a prefill chunk. Keep cached c0/c128 outputs separate.

## Accuracy Tests

On main `4eb606b2a`, validation passed 56 existing CPU tests and 60 subtests, plus two local buffer-ownership probes that are not included in this PR. GB300 probes passed byte-exact ragged combined mappings, ratio switches, separate c0/c128 storage, cross-bucket aliases, old-address stability on growth, full/tail isolation, and graph replay with refreshed inputs. Selected Ruff lint checks passed.

On the measured base `4fc86f73c`, two independent GB300 runs passed byte-exact metadata/replay probes and model/cache smoke tests, including 16,384/16,640-token contexts followed by short requests. Each capture-size run recorded 52 responses plus 8 cache-prime requests. Output token IDs and usage/cache statistics matched across repeats. Logprobs showed small run-to-run differences; this is not a full model-accuracy evaluation or a bitwise floating-point equivalence claim.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Local memory measurements on `4fc86f73c`, 4×GB300, DEP4, decoder bounded replay, FlashMLA mega attention, native DSPARK block size 5, static memory fraction 0.7 and chunk size 8192. Encoder bounded replay is OFF.

| Maximum prefill capture tokens | Baseline | This patch | Repeated result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192 | 16.18 GiB/GPU | 12.24 GiB/GPU | 12.24 GiB/GPU |
| 2048 | 6.77 GiB/GPU | 5.10 GiB/GPU | 5.10 GiB/GPU |

These are prefill capture-end memory increments, not whole-server memory. Startup reserved-memory peaks decreased only slightly. The combined-index change improves the 8K result but adds 0.07 GiB at 2K compared with the first two changes alone (5.03 GiB). No throughput claim; memory measurements have not been repeated on the rebased main revision. No allocator-policy toggles are included.

## Checklist

- [x] Validate existing regression suites and local GPU probes.
- [x] Preserve model context and capture sizes.
- [ ] Run upstream CI.

title: [Perf] [AMD] deepseek-v4: Skip top-k refinement for proven positive-zero ties
author: Duyi-Wang
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 top-k can collect more than 2048 bitwise positive-zero scores in its threshold bucket. The overflow refinement added in #37941 then rescans the input even though all candidates are equal. This case occurs in score tensors captured from an InferenceX AgentX serving run on MI355X.

## Modifications

Prove that every threshold-bucket candidate is bitwise +0, including candidates beyond the staging buffer, and skip refinement only when that proof succeeds. Negative zero, subnormals, and nonzero candidates retain exact refinement.

The shortcut covers register, streaming, and split paths and is gated by `USE_ROCM`; non-ROCm builds retain the original refinement path. Existing shared-memory storage and the split limit are preserved.

## Accuracy Tests

- The eight added graph-replay cases pass on MI355X for both baseline `3b34d9f8` and patch commit `e04efd0a`, with fresh JIT caches. They cover K=1024/2048, all three dispatch paths, and transitions between +0 ties, late tiny positives, subnormals, and negative zero.
- On the serving-image stack, the patch also passes 224 adversarial cases per variant and 96 existing strict prefill tests. Captured-score checks verify exact selected values and valid, unique indices.

**GSM8K with the top-k patch: 1246/1319 (94.47%).**

DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 with FP4 experts, TP8 on eight MI355X GPUs, using SGLang `34c4ba14` / AITER `2bb54910` with this PR's top-k headers. The evaluation ran directly through Slurm.

All 1319 test questions were evaluated with eight examples from the training split, temperature 0, seed 42, a 512-token generation limit, and request concurrency 32. Graphs and speculation were disabled. Zero request errors, invalid answers, or truncations.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Serving benchmark: [InferenceX](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX) AgentX agentic-coding workload**, using DeepSeek-V4 FP4 on 16 MI355X GPUs: one 8-GPU prefill node and one 8-GPU decode node. Concurrency means the AgentX client's `--concurrency` setting (replay lanes).

The controlled A/B uses the same node pair, Python TreeCore, and `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261016` base image; the candidate changes only the two top-k headers. At concurrency **192**, with a **1200-second measurement** and **one extra warmup request per lane**:

| Metric (higher is better) | Original | Patched | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| P90 interactivity (tokens/s; 1/P90 ITL) | 75.52613 | 81.74591 | +8.24% |
| Total tokens/s/GPU | 40418.21406 | 41878.94256 | +3.61% |

The patched run completed 6740 profiling requests with zero errors. Additional full-length InferenceX AgentX runs at concurrency **192, 256, 384, and 512** used **3600 seconds and ten extra warmup requests per lane**; all completed with zero profiling request errors. Raw results and collected metrics were reconciled.

For operator timing on baseline/patched main, five of six captured input tensors improve by **28.1%–44.5%**, while one is effectively unchanged, using an original → patched → original-repeat sequence on one MI355X. Separate large-batch synthetic controls on the serving-image stack measured **0.59%–5.92% latency overhead** on non-overflow/nonzero cases, so the benefit depends on the input distribution.

## Checklist

- [x] Added and ran ROCm operator regression tests.
- [x] Provided operator timings and InferenceX AgentX serving results.
- [x] Ran pre-commit checks on the unchanged code revision.

title: [Perf] deepseek-v4.1: Run encoder SWA bounded replay in the breakable prefill graph
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay` now accepts `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`; other prefill graph backends stay rejected, and so does any prefill graph on ROCm, which replays hits in a forward of their own
- The static batch carries the fold's `encoder_swa_replay`, `encoder_swa_row_floor` and `encoder_swa_compress_rows`, so capture and replay build the same window floors and compressor slots as an eager prefill
- Under the graph the request-window layout covers the live rows and pads to the bucket: padding rows get no window, write past the live rows and commit nowhere (`window_layout(padded_rows=...)`, `WindowLayout.leading_rows`); the window groups are fixed at one per request slot, at most one per row
- `refresh_for_breakable_cuda_graph_replay_` copies the request-window layout in place, and capture and replay activate it
- Graph metadata keeps its compressor slots in its own buffer (`_compressor_out_loc(own_buffer=True)`), so the in-place refresh before a replay leaves the static `out_cache_loc` as the runner filled it
- With DP attention, the prefill graph vote counts the folded replay rows, which an extend replay runs, so the vote agrees with the runner's own check
- The request-window workspace also covers the largest breakable prefill graph bucket, which can exceed a DP rank's share of the chunk
- Add tests for the padded layout, the slot buffer, the startup check and the workspace size; all five fail on main
- Checked on GB300, TP4/EP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, encoder and decoder replay on:
  - The replay rows' cached c1/c2 bytes, compared before and after each prefix-hit prefill: 0 rows changed over 8 graph and 8 eager hits
  - GSM8K, all 1,319 questions behind a shared 8-shot prefix (903 replay prefills, 909 of 910 prefills in the graph): 97.04%; with the same settings on the previous day's main, eager prefill with replay scored 97.50% and the graph without replay 97.27%
  - TTFT of 417 new tokens after a 13,312-token cached prefix: 81.2 ms; eager prefill with replay took 231.6 ms on the previous day's main; contexts above 16K still run eager
- Checked on GB300 with DP attention 2 / EP 2 and MegaMoE, encoder and decoder replay on: GSM8K, all 1,319 questions behind the same prefix at 64 concurrent requests, 97.27% with the graph and 97.35% eager
- Known issue on main, not changed here: with DP attention and MegaMoE, the breakable prefill graph hangs when one DP rank prefills while another is idle, because decoder replay's late-layer row-count gather runs only in the idle rank's eager forward

Supersedes #43010.

No behavior change unless encoder replay runs with the breakable prefill graph, which used to be rejected at startup; in every breakable prefill graph the captured compressor slots are now a copy refreshed before each replay instead of the static `out_cache_loc` itself.

title: [Perf] DSv4.1: Bound encoder BCG metadata memory
author: Oasis-Git
body:

## Motivation

Encoder SWA bounded replay now supports breakable prefill graphs, but the BCG metadata context bound and cross-bucket low-ratio index sharing still exclude request-window pools. This retains page-table columns outside the graph's existing context limit and separate index outputs for each bucket.

## Modifications

Apply the existing low-ratio BCG metadata bound and full-metadata index-buffer sharing with encoder replay enabled as well. Capture and replay use the same bound. Reuse the existing storage-lifetime handling; full/tail and ratio/page/raw storage remain distinct. Model context length, graph admission, long-context eager fallback, and feature defaults are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Local GB300 validation against main `3671503e44fa0acbf4f1bba4057e517282a7ccdb`:
- 42 existing encoder-replay, compressed-pool, and late-tail regression tests passed.
- Standalone GPU probes passed: byte-exact bounded page entries and graph input refresh; index-storage sharing, capacity growth, alternating bucket replay, and tail isolation.
- Model requests cover short/ragged inputs, 16,384/16,640-token contexts, and prefix-cache hits on all four DP ranks. For each bucket size, all 52 recorded requests matched main in complete output token sequences and usage/cache/rank/finish metadata, in both candidate runs. KV capacity remained 39,928,064 tokens.

title: [Fix] moe: Avoid stale prefix reads in ep_scatter
author: Degeneracy-Evil
body:
We hit an illegal memory access while running GLM-5.3-Flash + DFlash2 with TP8 on H20. We traced it to `_fwd_kernel_ep_scatter_1`.

In this kernel, every program writes the full expert offset table, then reads its own offset back from global memory. The writes and reads are not properly synchronized, so the read can return a stale value.

This PR follows the approach in #31930: compute the current offset directly from the expert token counts, and have each program write only its own entry. This avoids the stale read and removes the repeated full-table writes.

## Testing

- All 4 regression tests passed on H20, covering empty experts, tile boundaries, CUDA Graph replay, and BF16/FP8 scatter.
- Compute Sanitizer reported no memory errors.
- With the fix and CUDA Graphs enabled, the serving setup that originally failed completed the 32-request benchmark at concurrency 1 and 32.

To run the tests:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_ep_scatter.py -v
```

The kernel was faster in isolated tests than the approach in #31930. We did not see a noticeable end-to-end speedup over our earlier correctness-only patch. Full model accuracy evaluation has not been run.

Related: #31929, #31930.
