title: [Refactor] moe: Derive layer contracts from the selected quant method
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR was part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #44994 (merged)
* __->__ #44993 (merged)
* #44991 (merged)
* #44480 (merged)

## Motivation

A MoE quantization method can execute on Triton while the requested backend remains FlashInfer or AITER. Dispatch, weight preparation and routing must follow the layer that actually executes. Backend identity also does not prove that a native router implements the model's routing policy: AUTO-resolved NVFP4 must preserve custom routing and renormalization.

## Modifications

- Quantization methods expose their effective execution backend, including wrapped methods, secondary runners and direct kernels. FusedMoE binds dispatch, expert-ID layout, transport payloads, post-load transforms and each model router to that contract.
- TRT-LLM in-kernel routing requires a declared policy matching the model's scoring, grouping, bias, renormalization, custom-router and shared-slot behavior. Other routers retain materialized STANDARD output. Explicit `Default` enum value 0 remains a real policy, distinct from an unspecified selector.
- TRT-LLM routed adapters consume materialized weights without renormalizing them again. Unsupported materialized per-tensor FP8 input fails before the kernel; an undeclared per-tensor router retains the Triton fallback and its compatible weight layout.
- Materialized TRT-LLM routes include the routed factor for every effective quantization method, including compressed-tensors FP8/NVFP4 schemes. Grouped/biased fallback producers apply the factor independently of renormalization while preserving shared contributions. Native routers still apply their own factor once. Ordinary loaders zero untouched padded weight tails, including repeated loads.
- Preserve model-wide DP layout for fallback payloads, gate AITER-specific transforms on the effective backend, and keep weight-only helpers with no runner valid. Binding is idempotent for the same contract and rejects conflicting reuse. The gfx1250 W4A8 internal router rejects unsupported expert sharding.

Equivalent native policies are declared for normalized MiMoV2 grouped sigmoid/bias, BailingMoE grouped sigmoid/bias or plain softmax, and Cohere2 sigmoid. Other configurations remain materialized. DeepSeek's logits-only dual-stream graph requires a BYPASSED router even when this PR is used independently.

Llama4 FP8 explicitly selects the model's top-1 sigmoid native policy. Gemma4 NVFP4 materializes its model router so selected-expert softmax weights retain the learned per-expert multiplier. These change behavior relative to the earlier native defaults; CPU contract tests cover the boundaries, but no full-model accuracy A/B is claimed for either model.

BailingLinear resolves its optional AWQ provider only when AWQ weights are loaded, so ordinary model construction does not require `vllm`. The Kimi constructor fixture declares the routing selector explicitly.

Requested-backend reads remain where they select a method, allocate compatible shapes or establish model-wide policy.

title: [Refactor] moe: Derive routing inputs from the layer and active forward
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR was part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* __->__ #44994 (merged)
* #44993 (merged)
* #44991 (merged)
* #44480 (merged)

## Motivation

Model forwards can omit expert placement or the live token count, routing logical IDs against physical expert weights or processing padding as real tokens. Move those decisions into TopK and the active forward. Automatic padding also makes inactive routes reachable at EP1, so every affected consumer must skip their data, weights and expert addresses safely.

## Modifications

- Resolve placement per call and capture draft identity during construction. Align draft weight loading with identity routing, including in-range draft layer IDs; retain target placement-aware loading.
- Bind the prepared ForwardBatch across eager execution, graph capture/replay, CPU graphs and TBO children. Bind copied row/tail batches too. Decline DeepSeek row-tail capture when its MoE count is a separate GLOBAL buffer, using the existing eager path.
- Preserve lazy routing metadata until materialization. Keep the producing layer ID in TopKConfig, including piecewise reconstruction, so lazy LP conversion defaults to the correct solver while explicit overrides (including 0) still win. Keep the existing five-field tuple ABI. Reject logits-only consumers that cannot apply required remapping. Route DeepSeek graph admission through the same layer contract. Keep shared expert columns outside LP solving and routed-only remapping.
- Make Triton, Marlin, GGUF, W4AFP8 and Humming consumers honor inactive routes independently of EP, including NaN inputs/weights and poisoned intermediate buffers. Generic Marlin reuses its projection allocation, clearing the down view after activation consumes the up view; LoRA retains separate zeroed buffers.
- Support the published `sglang-kernel==0.4.10` GGUF provider with Python block-size selection, safe vector indices, masked inactive intermediates/contributions, and initialized MMQ slack metadata. Retain the AOT source fixes for future wheel builds.
- Initialize CUTLASS FP8 gather maps and use a masked Triton reduction that skips inactive data and weights. Pass token count and supported weight strides at runtime without value specialization so new lengths reuse compiled kernels. This fixes both block-FP8 and MXFP8 without requiring a newly released AOT wheel.
- Reject LongCat zero-expert placement configurations at startup, since routed-only placement tables cannot represent its identity experts safely. Plain identity placement remains available.
- Assert the Marlin allocation property rather than an incidental `.zero_()` call; set its CI runtime estimate to 720 seconds to cover cold compilation.

## CI repairs and validation

Current head: `2447ebc8cd21ba19ceb5f94c67826d30ff4aeaa0`; base #44993 is `4275a5026050615139c3658a72b6a7d05d65b17f`. Updated by normal fast-forward pushes.

Two latest repairs:

- Shared-expert routing fixture: publishing TP=1 and then overriding EP=8 failed topology validation before routing. Supply a consistent virtual TP=EP=8 topology at rank 3, without process groups or collectives. Registration and numerical assertions are unchanged. On one NVIDIA H200, the original complete file produced seven topology subtest errors; the repaired file passed all four tests at both stack production revisions, including five CUDA router variants, shared contribution and fullgraph compile behavior.
- AMD AITER prefill: eager draft extend selected a new query-offset table in `ForwardMetadata`, while CK still received the backend's stale prompt table. Measured Q had 80 rows but the passed offsets reached 4,648, immediately followed by the GPU memory fault. Publish ordinary prefill offsets into the same metadata owner and consume that owner's view in CK, ASM and 5D prefill. Kernel selection, KV padding and speculative helpers are unchanged. [#40872](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40872) describes the same defect with a producer-side repair; this patch keeps the existing per-forward owner authoritative at consumers.

AMD before/after: the unchanged EAGLE canary failed with a memory fault on both this stack and its original main base. After repair, all 20 requests and original assertions passed (50.6s process). A second serialized observation run passed too: CK received `[0,4,...,80]`, all 588 eager CK calls returned, and no malformed query CSR or HSA fault was observed. Decode graphs and all test assertions remained enabled as configured. Hardware: one AMD MI350X; original CI used MI300. Torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0, Triton 3.8.0, AITER 2bb549102, CK 96afae1d5. NHD/BF16 is exercised; the corresponding 5D/FP8/ASM corrections have source review coverage. Final source differs from the tested repair only by removing a stale comment. Independent source review and configured pre-commit checks passed.

H200 fixture runtime: Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, sglang-kernel 0.4.7, FlashInfer 0.6.18. This is single-GPU routing validation, not eight-GPU collective or full-model validation.

Other failures in the latest CI run:

- JIT B200 failed before tests: its local wheel was truncated to 94 MiB and lacked a ZIP central directory. A sibling verified the same artifact and installed its full 356 MiB wheel successfully (4,821 tests passed). A clean artifact download/retry is needed; no retry was triggered here.
- Qwen3-Next FP8 HiCache multi-turn KL exceeded its unchanged threshold. The same production code passed this method in the preceding run. The local numerical A/B ran zero comparisons: its Rust cache extension could not build against Torch 2.14.1. No version-check bypass was applied. This failure remains unattributed; no numerical fix or passing baseline is claimed.
- AMD disaggregation failed at startup with HIP OOM, also seen in an earlier main run. The AITER query-offset fix addresses the separately reproduced EAGLE memory fault, and does not claim to fix this startup failure.
- NPU QwenImage has identical failing metrics in three unrelated PR runs with the same expected image. A scoped source audit found no changed numerical path from this MoE stack, but no bare-base NPU A/B was run and its root cause remains unresolved.

Earlier CI-only repairs at `0a3e1cfa68` remain included: inherited DeepSeek dual-stream fixture correction from #44993, current activation import, Bailing NextN/V3 parity ownership, and Python 3.11 wheel selection in the simulator job. Their recorded validation was 54 quantization tests, 85 kernel namespace tests, the complete DeepSeek opcheck/compile/graph-replay test at both production revisions, two parity tests, 49 fusion-gate tests plus 11 subtests, and artifact-name matching. Those checks were not rerun for these bounded changes. Full CI and full-model acceptance remain pending; earlier validation below stays tied to its named revisions.

## Earlier validation after rebase

Head: `5a0a941ff3013d5c98cff1a5854d03bebff7324c`. Rebased onto main `553836c1647b3bfbeb266b49d76ec2c9df012425`; base `cheng/refactor/moe-layer-backend-semantics` is `fc2dd3d90bf86fe1b61741c1bb8d28a4e121dc8a`.

- At this exact integrated head, 12 focused CPU modules passed: 119 tests plus 200 reported subtests. Coverage includes lazy LP ownership, routing metadata/graph bounds, dispatcher contracts, shared/routed scale, native model policy admission, ModelOpt/FP8 ownership, runner extensions and placement. The lower PR was also checked independently. New regressions fail against their pre-fix production sources for the intended conditions.
- All 3 CUTLASS FP8 CUDA test methods passed on one NVIDIA B300, including real native block-FP8/MXFP8 GEMMs and mixed/all-inactive graph replay. The reduction test spans 12 token counts, contiguous/transposed weights, FP16/BF16 and poisoned NaN routes. The old real Triton cache grew to 23 entries per dtype; the fixed kernel retains 1. Tested kernel/test bytes are unchanged by the final merge.

The new focused CPU and 3-method CUTLASS runs above replace the corresponding coverage for this revision; the Marlin/GGUF kernels are unchanged this round.

title: [Fix] kda: Keep FlashInfer prefill off its grouped kernel's bf16/flat-dt_bias contract
author: rainj-me
body:
## Motivation

Serving Kimi-K3 with `--linear-attn-prefill-backend flashinfer` (the default on SM100/SM103) and the radix cache enabled crashes the scheduler in two ways, both coming from the same place: FlashInfer's `recurrent_kda` picks its **grouped recurrent kernel** instead of the flash prefill kernel whenever no sequence in the packed batch extends more than one token. That kernel has a stricter tensor contract than the flash prefill kernel, and SGLang's wrapper did not honor it.

1. **`dt_bias` layout.** The grouped kernel binds `dt_bias` as a flat `[H*K]` tensor with a unit leading stride (`mark_layout_dynamic(leading_dim=0)`). The wrapper passed a `[H, 128]` view, so the first extend that reused a cached prefix failed at compile time:
   ```
   RuntimeError: Expected strides[leading_dim] == 1, but got 128.
   ```
2. **State pool dtype.** The grouped kernel loads the recurrent state pool into bf16 registers. The KDA pool is fp32, so a packed batch where every sequence extends exactly one token (retracted requests re-entering with a fully cached prefix, as happens under memory pressure with long inputs) fails at compile time:
   ```
   NotImplementedError: autovec_copy only supports equal source and destination element type bit widths, got Float32 and BFloat16
   ```
   Multi-token extends take the flash prefill kernel, which accepts the fp32 pool, so short-prompt workloads never see this. The existing reroute to Triton only covered a single one-token sequence (`T == 1`).

Neither issue is addressed by the flashinfer-python 0.7.2 bump: its grouped kernel keeps both the flat `dt_bias` binding and the bf16 state load.

## Modifications

- `kda_flashinfer_prefill.py`: pass `dt_bias.reshape(-1)` (flat `[H*K]`) to `recurrent_kda`. Same values, same order; only the view changes.
- `kda_backend.py`: `KDAKernelDispatcher.effective_extend_kernel` takes the packed sequence count and routes any batch with `num_tokens <= num_seqs` to the Triton KDA kernel (generalizing the previous `num_tokens <= 1` rule). Both call sites (`extend` and the track-snapshot capability check in `KDAAttnBackend.forward_extend`) pass `query_start_loc.numel() - 1`.
- `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/linear/kernels/test_kda_flashinfer_prefill.py` (new, `base-a-test-cpu`): three CPU cases.
  - `dt_bias` reaches the kernel flat, unit-stride, float32, values in the layer's order. The `recurrent_kda` stand-in enforces the grouped kernel's leading-stride contract, so the pre-fix `[H, 128]` view fails with the production error.
  - A packed batch of four one-token sequences dispatches to Triton; FlashInfer is not called.
  - A batch where one sequence extends two tokens stays on FlashInfer (guards against the reroute widening into a blanket Triton fallback).

  Verified red on the pre-fix code (dt_bias case: `Expected strides[leading_dim] == 1, but got 128`; one-token case: FlashInfer called instead of Triton) and green on the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

Both bugs are hard crashes, so the fix is accuracy-neutral by construction: the flat `dt_bias` is a view of the same parameter, and one-token-per-sequence batches now run on the same Triton kernel that already served the `T == 1` case. 

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No impact on ordinary prefill: the FlashInfer flash prefill kernel is still selected whenever any sequence extends more than one token. The reroute only affects batches consisting solely of one-token extends, which previously crashed.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (not applicable)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4.1: Start the PD decode draft SWA window at the prefill draft valid-from
author: hnyls2002
body:
- With encoder SWA bounded replay on a PD prefill worker, the DSpark draft ring restarts at the cached prefix, but PD sends the draft's last SWA window from its start. After a prefix hit whose extend is shorter than the 128-token window, decode's paged draft SWA held rows the prefill never wrote for that request, and the draft attended over them. Lossless, but it lowers acceptance.
- The draft pool keeps that mark per request slot (`swa_valid_from`), and PD sends it as a new `REQUEST_ROW` state component: one item per request slot, sent slot to slot by Mooncake and NIXL, registered after the draft's SWA. Decode receives the prefill ring's mark in its own draft pool. Every DSpark draft on CUDA keeps the mark, ring or paged, in the custom mem pool like the pool's other transferred buffers, so both PD roles register it; it stays 0 unless the ring restarts or PD writes it.
- `ComputeDsparkWindowGather` takes an optional `valid_from` (torch and triton), so the paged window stops there, as `BuildDsparkSwaRingIndices` does for the ring.
- The ring's `swa_req_ring_valid_from` / `reset_swa_req_ring` become `swa_valid_from` / `set_swa_valid_from`: one per-slot mark for both storages.
- Tests: paged indices with a valid-from match the ring's; a DSpark draft keeps the mark for either storage and registers it as a `REQUEST_ROW` component after its SWA, while other drafts keep none; triton matches torch with a valid-from.

Checked on GB300 with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: one DEP2 prefill worker (encoder replay on) and one DEP2 decode worker on one node, DSpark block 5, MegaAttention, MegaMoE, Mooncake, greedy.

| Workload | main: accept length (tokens) | This PR: accept length (tokens) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2048-token cached prefix + 43-token question, 64 new tokens, round 1 (128 requests) | 3.16 | 3.85 |
| same, round 2 | 2.87 | 3.80 |

This workload leaves an 85-row gap on every hit. GSM8K (sgl-eval, 1,319 questions, thinking off) behind a shared 8-shot prefix, whose prompts hit at a page boundary that leaves no gap: 97.12% and 96.89% on main over two passes, 96.74% with this PR. Zero KV transfer failures. These runs predate moving the mark's allocation to one place; that move does not change the DSpark PD path. Not run with a Mooncake custom mem pool (`SGLANG_MOONCAKE_CUSTOM_MEM_POOL`).

Known limit: with a decode-side prefix cache that holds more of the window than the prefill, the mark also hides those decode-local rows (acceptance only).

Behavior change: PD workers with a DSpark draft on CUDA register one more state component, and decode's draft window stops at the prefill's mark. A DSpark draft without PD keeps the mark at 0, so its window gather adds one clamp that leaves the values unchanged; nothing else changes.

title: [Perf] deepseek-v4.1: Run decoder replay tail layers from CUDA graphs on eager prefill steps
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Under decoder SWA bounded replay, the layers from `late_layer_start` on run over each request's last 128 extend rows. On an eager prefill step those few rows still pay one host launch per kernel. This PR replays these tail layers from breakable CUDA graphs keyed by the padded tail row count: multiples of 128, up to `SGLANG_DSV4_DECODER_TAIL_GRAPH_MAX_ROWS` (default 2048).
- New model-agnostic `RowBucketGraphRunner` (`model_executor/runner/row_bucket_graph_runner.py`): breakable CUDA graphs of a layer range keyed by padded row count.
  - static input buffers sized once for the largest bucket and shared by every bucket;
  - each bucket captured on first use, largest first, into the global graph pool on the global capture stream;
  - graphs start only after a forward of a full prefill chunk, so lazily sized workspaces have reached their final size.
- New `models/deepseek_v4_replay_tail.py` with `DecoderReplayTail`, the DeepSeek-V4.1 side: when to use the graphs, the tail layer stack the runner records, the mHC state flattening, and the eager SWA KV store break. `deepseek_v4.py` keeps only the hooks.
- Inside a tail graph, the SWA KV store, the attention and the low-ratio sources run as eager breaks that read the step's live tail metadata and real row count.
- Scope: eager prefill steps with attention DP size 1. Prefill-graph steps, DP attention, context parallel, unified-KV Triton and expert-distribution recording keep the current path. Prefill-graph steps and DP attention follow in a stacked PR.
- Behavior change: on by default on CUDA whenever decoder replay is on. Captured graphs add GPU memory that KV sizing does not count: 16 buckets took 2.2 GiB per GPU on GB300 TP4. `SGLANG_DSV4_DECODER_TAIL_GRAPH_MAX_ROWS=0` keeps the current eager path. The graphs are also off with `SGLANG_ENABLE_GRAPH_POOL_BORROW`.
- Verification: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GB300, TP4, eager prefill, DSpark; main (`cff88d6eac`) vs this change on two nodes (A, B), each pair run on one node in opposite orders.
  - Cold-prompt TTFT (`max_new_tokens=1`, median of 5): 128 tokens 150.4 / 154.5 -> 103.6 / 105.3 ms (node A / node B); 8K tokens 162.4 / 169.0 -> 111.7 / 112.2 ms.
  - 64K cached prefix plus 2048 new tokens, TTFT: 172.4 / 179.2 -> 124.2 / 124.4 ms.
  - Saturated prefill (`bench_serving`, random 8K input, 1 output token, concurrency 64): 94.6K / 93.1K -> 125.0K / 125.2K input tok/s (+33%).
  - GSM8K (sgl-eval, 1319 examples, no thinking): 96.66 / 96.89% -> 96.89 / 96.59%.

title: [Perf] deepseek-v4.1: Stage late-layer DP row counts through pinned memory
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

With decoder SWA bounded replay and DP attention, `enter_late_layer_dp` installs every DP rank's late-layer row counts on the device in the middle of the model forward. When the counts differ across ranks it did so with `gpu.new_tensor(counts)`, a pageable host-to-device copy. That copy synchronizes the stream: the host waits until all early layers have finished on the GPU, and only then launches the late layers, so the GPU idles while they are launched.

Torch-profiler trace of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash DEP2 prefill (DP attention 2, EP 2, MegaMoE, DSpark, 32K tokens per rank per step) on GB300, rank 0, 15 steps:

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| `enter_late_layer_dp` host time per step | 241 ms | 0.16 ms |
| Kernel time / step span | ~75% | ~97% |
| Step span | 500-680 ms | 425-500 ms |

## Modifications

- Non-uniform counts go through `async_h2d` (pinned staging, copy enqueued on the current stream), the helper the DSv4 backend already uses for host lists. Rank-uniform counts keep `full_like`, the only branch a graph capture takes.

## Accuracy Tests

Not affected: the device receives the same values on the same stream; only the host no longer blocks on the copy. Checked on GB300 under `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")`: entering the late layers with uneven counts raises on main and runs clean with this change, with identical int32 counts installed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GB300, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, PD disaggregation with 6 DEP2 prefill workers and one DEP16 decode worker, agentic multi-turn workload at concurrency 2884 (prefill-bound), 60-minute measurement window:

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Prefill GPU utilization (nvidia-smi, 3 nodes) | 75-79% | 91-93% |
| Input throughput per GPU (incl. prefix-cache hits) | 475.2k tok/s | 535.8k tok/s (+12.7%) |
| Output throughput per GPU | 3.55k tok/s | 3.94k tok/s (+11.0%) |
| Requests / s | 96.2 | 106.8 (+11.0%) |
| TTFT p50 / p90 | 9.5 / 20.3 s | 5.5 / 13.3 s |

At concurrency 1228 (decode-bound, 4 prefill workers) TTFT p90 drops from 3.4 s to 2.3 s and input throughput moves +1.8%.

- [x] Format your code according to pre-commit.

title: [Perf] deepseek-v4.1: Default PD to MegaAttention, with the KV layout in the PD handshake
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `_default_dsv4_attention_backend` no longer falls back to FlashMLA under PD, so both roles pick MegaAttention (`flashmla_mega`) on SM100/SM103, as a single server does.
- MegaAttention and FlashMLA store KV in different layouts (packed V4.1 vs V4 by default), and the PD handshake compared only `kv_cache_dtype`, so a mismatched pair would transfer KV that the decode misreads. The prefill now registers its KV layout (`DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool.pd_kv_layout`: the main layout plus each compression ratio's), the Python and Rust bootstrap servers relay it, and the decode raises `KV layout mismatch` next to the dtype check. Other pools report no layout and skip the check.
- The trtllm PD rejection no longer says the handshake lacks a layout; trtllm under PD stays rejected as untested (#37838).
- The DeepSeek-V4.1 cookbook's PD section states the default and that both roles must match.

Verified on two GB300 nodes (DEP2 prefill + DEP2 decode, DSpark, Mooncake) with no `--dsv4-attn-backend`: both roles resolve `flashmla_mega`, and GSM8K (1,319, greedy) scores 96.66%, the same as with `flashmla` on both roles. With only the decode on `flashmla`, its first request fails with `KV layout mismatch: prefill server has kv_layout=v41,c1:v41_fp4,c2:v41_fp4, but decode server has kv_layout=v4,c1:v4,c2:v4`.

Behavior change: DeepSeek-V4.1 PD on SM100/SM103 runs MegaAttention on both roles by default. A prefill on SM100/SM103 paired with a decode on another GPU now needs `--dsv4-attn-backend flashmla` on the prefill. An older decode cannot parse the new `kv_layout` field, so upgrade both roles together.

title: [Fix] hicache: Count the EAGLE bigram boundary token in PD decode restores
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

#40857 lets EAGLE / EAGLE3 run with `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache`, so the decode tree of a non-Mamba model uses bigram keys: N cached positions are keyed by N + 1 token ids. Decode HiCache counts its prefix lengths (`l1`, `l2`, `l3`, `decode_prefix_len`) in bigrams, but passes them back as token counts in two places:

- `_try_hicache_queue_load_back` rematches with `max_prefix_len=decode_prefix_len`. That becomes `RadixKey.limit` (a token cap), so the bigram key has `decode_prefix_len - 1` entries and the page-aligned rematch stops one page short. `device_prefix_len + loaded_len < decode_prefix_len` then always holds, the restore is marked FAILED, and every request that hits L2 or L3 is aborted ("HiCache restore failed").
- `_start_hicache_prefetch` slices `l3` token ids for the prefetch, which `prefetch_from_storage` turns into `l3 - 1` bigrams, so the prefetch also lands one page short.

Mamba trees disable bigram keys and are not affected. The non-PD path passes every remaining token and is not affected either.

## Modifications

- Both call sites add the bigram boundary token (`int(tree_core.is_eagle)`) when they turn a prefix length into a token count.

## Tests

- `test_decode_restore_rematch_covers_bigram_prefix` (CUDA): a real EAGLE `UnifiedRadixCache` with a host-only 16-position prefix, the real `match_kv_cache`, and the real `_try_hicache_queue_load_back`. It runs on both the Rust and the Python tree core.
- `test_storage_probe_and_prefetch_use_node_handles` now also checks the EAGLE prefetch span.
- Negative control: with the fix reverted, both tests fail. The real-cache test logs `HiCache load_back failed ... new_indices=12, expected decode_prefix_len=16`.
- `test_decode_hicache_tree_core.py`, `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py`, `test_decode_radix_lock_ref.py` and `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` all pass on 1x H200: 1386 passed, 1585 skipped, 89 subtests passed. The new class also passes with `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=python`.

### Service-level check (8x B300, 1P1D over Mooncake)

Qwen3-8B, plus `Tengyunw/qwen3_8b_eagle3` in the EAGLE3 arms. The decode server runs `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-write-policy write_through --max-total-tokens 6144`. Each run sends a 1600-token prompt twice, then 8 distinct 1600-token prompts so the first prompt's prefix is evicted to host, then the first prompt again with 4 more tokens.

| tree | spec | last request | `load_back_tokens_total` delta | "HiCache load_back failed" log lines |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | none | 200 | 1600 | 0 |
| main | EAGLE3 | **500** (decode_internal_error) | **0** | **5** (`new_indices=1472, expected decode_prefix_len=1536`) |
| this PR | EAGLE3 | 200 | 1536 | 0 |
| this PR | none | 200 | 1600 | 0 |

author: Jiminator
body:

Follow-up fixes to #44518, now rebased onto `main`. Handle unsupported NVFP4 weight exports safely and correct the BF16/FP8 GEMV dispatch paths without losing the measured fast cases.

- Return failed control responses for blocked weight exports and reject phase layout before remote weight storage is published.
- Keep unsupported strides/alignment on the existing cuBLAS path. On SM90, use cuBLAS for the measured `K=5120, N<=512` regime. Restore two rows per warp for SM120 FP8 GEMV at `N=8192`.
- Complete lazy kernel registrations using the current `KernelSpec` schema, move layout-cycle ownership into SRT, and remove unused state/arguments.
- Rename the four PR-only toggles to `SGLANG_OPT_SM120_NVFP4_PHASE_LAYOUT`, `SGLANG_OPT_SM120_MTP_ROUTER_TOP22`, `SGLANG_OPT_FLASHINFER_DRAFT_HOST_INDPTR`, and `SGLANG_OPT_FLASHINFER_VERIFY_HOST_PLAN`, without old-name aliases.

No test files or cases are added, deleted or moved. The only test edits are eight required flag-name substitutions in two existing files; assertions, subcases and CI registration remain unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

- Rebase validation: **372 passed, 2 expected skips on RTX PRO 6000 (SM120)**; **7 tests and 7 subtests passed on H200 (SM90)**. This covers MoE routing, FlashInfer host planning/masks, FP8 linear, BF16 GEMV/addend, kernel namespace, environment and MoE placement checks.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] fused_moe: Add H20 configs for GLM-5.3-Flash TP8/TP4
author: QNan0513
body:
## Motivation

With plain tensor parallelism (`--tp 8` or `--tp 4`, no `--ep`), GLM-5.3-Flash runs its routed experts through the Triton fused MoE. The serving lookups are:

- `E=289` for the target layers, because the shared expert is fused into the routed experts by default.
- `E=288` for the NextN/MTP draft layer, and for any run with `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`.

No config exists for these shapes on any GPU, so on H20 every MoE layer logs `Using default MoE kernel config` and runs with `BLOCK_SIZE_M=64`. #38913 added H20 configs for the EP4/EP8 shapes (`E=72`/`E=36`, `N=2048`). This PR adds the TP shapes.

## Modifications

Four Triton 3.8.0 configs (main pins torch 2.14.1, which ships Triton 3.8.0):

| File | Used by |
| --- | --- |
| `E=289,N=256,device_name=NVIDIA_H20,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128, 128].json` | TP8, target layers |
| `E=288,N=256,device_name=NVIDIA_H20,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128, 128].json` | TP8, MTP draft layer / shared-expert fusion disabled |
| `E=289,N=512,device_name=NVIDIA_H20,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128, 128].json` | TP4, target layers |
| `E=288,N=512,device_name=NVIDIA_H20,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128, 128].json` | TP4, MTP draft layer / shared-expert fusion disabled |

The files were generated with the stock `benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton/tuning_fused_moe_triton.py`, using the default search space (1,280 configs after the `BLOCK_SIZE_K` filter) and the default 18 batch sizes. Each batch size was tuned in its own process on one GPU.

To get `E=289`, I applied #43647's one-line `common_utils.py` change locally. That change adds `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` to the fused-shared-expert list; without it, the tuner writes only `E=288`. This PR leaves the tuner alone so it does not overlap #43647.

Small batches now use `BLOCK_SIZE_M=16` (M ≤ 512), M=1024 uses 32, and M ≥ 1536 mostly uses 64. The separate down-projection (`_down`, TMA) configs from `tuning_fused_moe_triton_sep.py` are not included. Serving keeps reusing the up config for the down GEMM, as it does today.

## Setup

All numbers below are from a re-run on 2026-11-01 with this branch rebased onto main `b801787`. The four files are the ones tuned on 2026-10-19; they were not re-tuned.

- Image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261031-a2cafa56` (torch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0, sglang-kernel 0.4.10, flashinfer 0.7.2, the versions main pins), with `PYTHONPATH` set to a source tree. The default arm uses main `b801787`. The tuned arm uses this branch rebased onto `b801787`, so it reads the four files from their in-tree location. The two trees differ only in these files.
- Tuning ran with image `nightly-dev-20261015-a6a8c560`, whose fused-MoE kernel, config loader and tuner files matched main `58ad074`. Since then main has changed the Triton fused-MoE kernel (`sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py`) and `fused_moe.py`. The config loader and the tuner script are unchanged.
- Two 8× H20 96 GB nodes. On node A, one GPU overheats under sustained load (0.7–1.2 GHz, 87–90 °C). During tuning, the 10 batch sizes first tuned on it were re-tuned on the other GPUs, and 7 of those picks changed. The kernel benchmark (GPUs 0, 1, 2, 4) and TP4 serving (GPUs 4–7) run on node A without that GPU. TP8 serving runs on node B, where all eight GPUs stayed at 1980 MHz and at most 52 °C in every case (`nvidia-smi` sampled every 2 s).

## Kernel benchmark

Stock tuner in benchmark mode (no `--tune`; the #43647 line is applied so that `E=289` is benchmarked): 100 iterations of 10 CUDA-graph replays per M. For each shape, the default arm and the tuned arm alternate on the same GPU for 3 rounds; the table shows the median. Speedup = default / tuned.

Like the tuner, the benchmark routes each token to 8 random experts out of E. The `E=289` columns therefore treat the fused shared expert as one of 289 candidates, while serving sends every token to it (top-k 9). This is why the `E=289` and `E=288` columns are nearly identical. The serving results below use the real routing.

title: [Perf] [AMD] deterministic: Faster extend attention launch on gfx950
author: aarnetalman
body:
## Motivation

Deterministic inference (`--enable-deterministic-inference`) runs prefill with the unified extend-attention kernel (`extend_attention_fwd_unified`), whose reduction order does not depend on the batch. On gfx950 it launches every head_dim <= 128 with a 64-row query tile and 4 warps. Each workgroup streams the whole prefix for its query rows, so with long prompts the kernel is bound by KV reads: at 64k-token inputs it takes 82% of deterministic mode's GPU time (Qwen3-8B on MI350X), and deterministic throughput falls to about 0.2x of normal mode.

A 256-row tile with 8 warps reads each KV block once for 4x as many query rows. The KV block size (`BLOCK_N`), and so the order in which each row's softmax and sums are accumulated, is unchanged, so the output is bitwise identical to today's.

## Modifications

- `extend_attention.py` (`extend_attention_fwd_unified`): on gfx950, for head_dim <= 128 with the default `BLOCK_N` of 64, launch with `BLOCK_M = 256` and 8 warps. Other GPUs, head dims, the shared block-size table and the non-deterministic extend kernels are unchanged.
- `test_triton_attention_kernels.py`: on gfx950, the unified kernel's output with the new tile equals the default tile's output bit for bit (head_dim 128 and 64, three sequences with 0-4k prefixes).

A pipelined variant (128-row tile, 2 stages) was faster in isolation but aborted in ROCm Triton's compiler (LLVM `iota_range` assertion) for the server's kernel specialisation, so it is not used.

## Accuracy Tests

The output is bitwise identical to the current launch, so accuracy cannot change. Checked three ways on MI350X (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261018`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, our open deterministic-mode fixes for MI350X applied):

- Kernel level: 500 launch configurations timed on 8k-token chunks after 0-56k-token prefixes and a 4-sequence mixed batch, head_dim 128 (Qwen3-8B: 32/8 heads) and 64 (gpt-oss: 64/8 heads, sinks). Every configuration with `BLOCK_N = 64` gives output equal to the current launch (`torch.equal`); the new one is 2.0-2.6x faster.
- New unit test `test_extend_attention_unified_gfx950_tile_bitwise` passes on MI350X. Two existing tests in the same file fail on gfx950 with and without this change (same results on the unchanged image): `test_extend_attention_block_sizes` (expects the tile #34461 added, which #35770 narrowed) and the head_dim-80 case of `test_extend_attention_unified_vs_regular` (max diff 0.167, tolerance 0.15/0.17). Both are pre-existing; the first is fixed by #45099, which restores that tile and is independent of this PR (the two apply together cleanly and were tested together).
- End to end, deterministic mode with the change, `python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic --test-mode {single,prefix,radix_cache} --n-trials 50`, `--test-mode prefix --return-logprob`, and a bitwise batch-size check (the same prompt in batches of 1 to 50, 1,275 responses, token IDs and logprobs compared exactly): all pass for Qwen3-8B (TP1, TP2, TP8), Qwen3-30B-A3B, Phi-4, gpt-oss-20b (TP1, TP2) and gpt-oss-120b. Long prompts (16k-120k tokens alone vs with other requests in the batch, and with chunked-prefill boundaries moved by other requests) give identical token IDs and logprobs. Rechecked on the 2026-10-19 nightly (`v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261019`): Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-30B-A3B pass every check.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf`, deterministic mode, before and after alternating twice on the same GPU (every pair within 0.5%), output throughput:

| Model, attention | 1k in / 1k out (256 prompts, conc. 256) | 8k / 1k (256, conc. 128) | 15k-32k / 256 (64, conc. 16) | 64k / 256 (32, conc. 8) | 120k-126k / 256 (16, conc. 4) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-8B, Triton prefill + AITER decode | 7,070 -> 7,234 (+2.3%) | 1,211 -> 1,469 (+21%) | 47.9 -> 86.2 (+80%, 32k) | 17.8 -> 35.2 (+98%)* | 5.9 -> 13.7 (+130%)* |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B, Triton prefill + AITER decode | 6,635 -> 6,822 (+2.8%) | 1,262 -> 1,664 (+32%) | | | |
| Phi-4, Triton prefill + AITER decode | | 778 -> 924 (+19%) | 95.4 -> 139.8 (+47%, 15k) | | |
| gpt-oss-20b, Triton | | 1,644 -> 1,877 (+14%) | 90.6 -> 160.5 (+77%, 32k) | | 13.0 -> 27.5 (+112%) |
| gpt-oss-20b TP2, Triton | | 2,610 -> 2,893 (+11%) | 154.5 -> 246.3 (+59%, 32k) | | |
| gpt-oss-120b, Triton | | 1,031 -> 1,169 (+13%) | 59.6 -> 105.3 (+77%, 32k) | | |

\* Qwen3-8B with YaRN (factor 4, 128k context). Time to first token drops by the same factors (Qwen3-8B 32k: 41.4 -> 22.3 s); inter-token latency is unchanged (decode does not use this kernel). gpt-oss ran with ROCm/aiter#6583's deterministic MoE.

Profile at 64k input (Qwen3-8B, 8 prompts, 40 forward steps, deterministic mode): `_fwd_kernel_unified` 79.0 -> 30.7 s of GPU time; total GPU time 96 -> 48 s.

No change without `--enable-deterministic-inference` or off gfx950.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Perf] [AMD] attention: Restore the gfx950 extend tile for head_dim <= 128
author: aarnetalman
body:
## Motivation

On MI350X/MI355X (gfx950), the Triton prefill attention kernel used to run faster for models with head size 64 or 128, such as gpt-oss, Llama and Qwen. #34461 made that change, with identical outputs. A later PR (#35770, for Kimi-K3) appears to have undone it by accident, so these models are back on the slower setting. The test #34461 updated still expects the faster setting and fails on MI350X; it runs only on MI300 in CI, so nobody noticed. This PR restores #34461's setting.

@clintg6, was narrowing it intended for the MLA kernels? MLA head dims (576/512, 192/128) take their own branches and are not affected by this change.

## Modifications

- `extend_attention.py` (`_get_block_sizes_for_extend_attention`): restore #34461's condition and comment, `_is_gfx95 and Lq <= 256`. `BLOCK_N` is unchanged, so outputs stay bitwise identical.
- No test change: the existing `test_extend_attention_block_sizes` already expects this.

## Accuracy Tests

The reduction order (`BLOCK_N`) is unchanged, so outputs are bitwise identical; checked at kernel level on MI350X for head_dim 64 and 128 (8k-token chunks after 0-56k-token prefixes, and a mixed 4-sequence batch): output equal to the 64-row tile's with `torch.equal`.

`python3 -m pytest test/registered/attention/test_triton_attention_kernels.py -k extend` on MI350X (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261018`): before 3 failed / 5 passed, after 2 failed / 6 passed: `test_extend_attention_block_sizes` fails before and passes after. `test_extend_attention` and the head_dim-80 case of `test_extend_attention_unified_vs_regular` fail on MI350X with and without the change (tolerance checks, unrelated).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI350X, Qwen3-8B TP1, `python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf`, before and after alternating twice (pairs within 0.3%), output throughput:

No change off gfx950, for head_dim > 256, or with other attention backends.

title: [Perf] deepseek-v4.1: Run decoder replay tail graphs in prefill-graph steps and under DP attention
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Follow-up to #45059, which runs the decoder-replay tail layers from row-bucket CUDA graphs on eager prefill steps with attention DP size 1. This PR extends those graphs to prefill-graph steps and to DP attention.
- Prefill-graph steps: a captured shape of at least `SGLANG_DSV4_DECODER_TAIL_GRAPH_MIN_PREFILL_TOKENS` tokens (default 2048) no longer captures the tail over its padded block.
  - At the tail switch, one eager break of the prefill graph switches onto exact-row tail metadata of the live batch (`_enter_eager_tail_in_prefill_graph`, `_unpadded_batch` in `deepseek_v4_replay_tail.py`).
  - It replays the tail graphs, or runs the tail layers eagerly past the largest bucket, and writes the tail rows into bridge buffers that the later captured segments read.
  - Smaller shapes keep the tail in their own capture, where the break would cost more than it saves.
- DP attention: every rank captures and replays the bucket of the largest rank's tail, and an idle rank takes part with no rows of its own.
  - TP MoE: the tail runs in a rank-uniform DP layout. Row counts come from the pre-forward exchange (`ForwardBatch.global_late_layer_num_tokens_cpu`). Each rank's padded tail IDs are gathered when the MoE routes on IDs.
  - MegaMoE: each rank sees only its local bucket, and the ranks agree on it through a host gather of their counts. This path needs the prefill graph disabled, since MegaMoE ranks may pick a prefill graph or eager independently.
- `RowBucketGraphRunner` gains `batch_scope`, `bucket_from` and `out_rows`, so the DeepSeek-V4.1 side can lay out the DP batch and replay a shared bucket.
- Tail-graph capture fix: a breakable graph runs each eager break once during its capture pass, on activations its segments never computed. In a tail graph the low-ratio sources break then ran the indexer on that memory, which could select out-of-range candidate blocks and trip DeepGEMM's `logical_page_idx < block_table_stride` assert, intermittently, at capture. The break now has a capture stub that skips it during a tail graph's capture pass (`_low_ratio_sources_capture_stub` in `deepseek_v4.py`); its replay runs the body, and the prefill-graph capture is unchanged. The same capture pass exists in #45059's eager tail graphs. Seen on DP2 attention + MegaMoE under a multi-turn agentic trace; with the stub, 20+ runs had no assert.
- Behavior change, on by default whenever decoder replay is on:
  - prefill-graph shapes of 2048 tokens or more run the tail outside the captured block;
  - DP attention with a TP MoE, or MegaMoE on eager prefill, runs the tail from graphs.
  - Still off: encoder replay inside a prefill-graph step, context parallel, unified-KV Triton, and other all-to-all backends under DP. `SGLANG_DSV4_DECODER_TAIL_GRAPH_MAX_ROWS=0` turns the tail graphs off.
- Verification: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB300 with DSpark. Baseline is main before #45059 (`58ad0748a6`). Each pair ran on one node; GSM8K is sgl-eval, 1319 examples, no thinking.
  - TP4, breakable prefill graph (max 8K tokens): cold 8K TTFT 146.4 -> 100.4 ms; 64K cached prefix + 2048 TTFT 178.0 -> 121.4 ms; saturated 8K-input prefill at concurrency 64, 59.9K -> 82.1K tok/s (+37%); GSM8K 96.97% vs 96.74%. Shapes under 2048 tokens are unchanged (cold 128: 33.8 vs 32.2 ms).
  - DP4 attention + TP MoE, eager: cold 8K TTFT 368.3 -> 233.7 ms; saturated prefill 93.7K -> 140.9K tok/s (+50%); GSM8K 96.89% vs 96.97%.
  - DP4 attention + TP MoE, breakable prefill graph: cold 8K TTFT 335.7 -> 287.8 ms; 64K cached + 2048 TTFT 201.8 -> 139.8 ms; saturated prefill 100.2K -> 112.6K tok/s (+12%); GSM8K 96.82% vs 96.66%.
  - DP2 attention + MegaMoE (EP2), eager, encoder replay on: cold 8K TTFT 208.4 -> 166.2 ms; 64K cached + 1K TTFT 153.8 -> 116.0 ms; 48 sessions with a 32K cached prefix each adding 2048 / 8192 new tokens, 81.2K / 108.9K -> 97.1K / 133.4K fresh tok/s; GSM8K 96.29% vs 96.89%.
  - The same MegaMoE setup with the breakable prefill graph captures no tail graphs and serves normally (GSM8K 96.89%).

title: [Refactor] kernels: Regroup operators by computation and dissolve ops/muse_spark
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

`python/sglang/kernels/README.md` says to classify kernels by the computation they perform, not by the model that first used them, and never to add a model bundle as a top-level group. An audit of current main found that this had drifted:

- `ops/muse_spark/` (#44665) was a model-named top-level group. It contained 22 files mixing norms, routing, GEMMs, collectives and reductions, with no KernelSpecs and no kernel tests. It had been added to `_GROUPS`, which is the only thing the guard test checked, so the test did not catch it.
- `attention/dsv4/` and `attention/dsa/` had collected quantization kernels, KV-cache stores and copies, a split-K GEMV, collective attention-residual kernels, runtime controllers and config predicates, and test oracles.
- Elsewhere, ops sat in the wrong group: GEMMs in `quantization`, RMSNorms in `elementwise`, attention metadata in `kvcache`, a forwarding shim in `attention/utils.py`, and the same computation implemented in two or three groups.

This PR fixes all of it in one pass. It writes the classification rules into the README and the `kernel-organization` skill, and makes the guard test enforce the README.

## Classification rules (README + skill)

- RoPE, including standalone RoPE and position ids, stays in `attention`.
- **Producer + output quantization belongs to the producer's group:**
  - norm + quant → `layernorm`
  - activation + quant → `activation`
  - a GEMM with a quant epilogue → `gemm`
  - MoE dispatch + quant → `moe`
  - `quantization` holds only pure format conversion: quant, dequant, scale layout, repack.
- **Any kernel that performs a cross-rank collective, or reads or writes peer memory, → `communication`**, whatever compute it fuses. Workspaces, symmetric buffers and process groups stay in `srt/layers/communication/`.
- **`kvcache` owns ops that read or write KV-cache contents:** store, gather, copy, quantize-into-cache, clear rows.
- **`attention` owns the index, shape and schedule tables attention kernels consume:** page tables, cu_seqlens, kv_indices, schedule metadata.
- A fused compute+store op stays with its compute group.
- `kda_kernels/` and `cake_kernels/` are documented as the agent-generated kernel backends. They are deliberately left in place, and new agent kernels keep landing there.

**Guard test** (`test_kernels_namespace.py`):
- The README group list must equal `_GROUPS`.
- The README Layout must list exactly the packages under `sglang/kernels/`.

Both checks fail on main.

## Modifications

All relocations are `git mv` plus import updates. Every moved function, class and constant was checked to be byte-identical apart from import paths, either by AST comparison or by a normalized diff. Relocation commits are kept apart from semantic commits. No forwarding shims remain: 94 old module paths have zero references anywhere.

### `ops/muse_spark` dissolved
- **layernorm:** `muse_spark_norm_gate{,_jit,_helion}`, `muse_spark_norm_residual{,_jit}`, `muse_spark_rmsnorm_nvfp4_quant{,_helion}`, `_muse_spark_tuning`.
- **attention:** `muse_spark_qk_norm_rope_store{,_helion}`.
- **moe:** `muse_spark_routing{,_jit}`, `muse_spark_post_expert_finalize_triton`.
- **communication:**
  - `muse_spark_all_gather`, `muse_spark_all_gather_norm_residual`
  - `muse_spark_moe_finalize_all_reduce{,_cutedsl,_helion}`
  - SP `cutlass_all_gather_gemm`, `cutlass_gemm_reduce_scatter`, `sp_collective_gemm` (moved from `gemm`)
- **elementwise:** `row_sum`. **gemm:** `muse_spark_router_gemm`. It is kept but still unused; the model only reads its `MAX_TOKENS` threshold.
- **Helion runtime:** → `kernels/jit/utils/helion_runtime.py`.
- **Runtime state → `srt/layers/communication/`:** the GEMM+all-gather composition and projection workspace, `FinalizePushWorkspace`, and the SP collective-GEMM symmetric-memory workspace. The SP kernels now take the workspace as an argument.
- **The model calls the all-gather+norm op directly.** The removed `forward_with_ag` used to route it, and the norm op no longer imports srt model classes.
- **New coverage:** KernelSpecs for every entry point, plus 6 kernel test files (fused vs native). `triton_sum` → `sglang.test.kernels`, used as the `row_sum` bitwise reference.

### DeepSeek V4 / DSA
- **To `quantization`:**
  - `act_quant` (Triton and TileLang)
  - `fp8_group_major_quant_ue8m0` (was `dsv4/fp8_wo_a`)
  - `fp4_fake_quant` (was `dsv4/torch_quant`)
  - `quantize_fp4_indexer_tensor`
  - `dsa_quant_k_cache` (returns new tensors; it never writes the cache)
- **To `kvcache`:**
  - request-window row copy, c128 draft-state cleanup
  - V4 main-KV and DSA index-K accessors
  - unified-KV scatter
  - FP4 index-K store and gather (CUDA and HIP)
  - the DSA fused index-K store
- **To `gemm`:** `dsv4_indexer_head_weights_hip`, a split-K GEMV.
- **To `communication`:** `attn_res_collective` (NVLS pull reduce-scatter, multicast all-gather).
- **Runtime code → srt:** `OnlineC128MTPController`, the unified-KV config gate, `Gfx950FusedIndexer`.
- **Launchers into the kernel modules:** the sparse-prefill and CP-interleave launchers now live there, so srt no longer imports private `@triton.jit` kernels.
- **Folder fixes:**
  - DSA-only files at the attention top level → `dsa/`
  - V4-only files → `dsv4/`; `nsa_triton_decode/` → `dsv4/triton_sparse_decode/`
  - `dsv4/elementwise.py` → `dsv4/norm_rope.py`
  - the V3.2-only Q indexer → `dsa/indexer_q.py`
- **Renames:**
  - same-named dequant functions → `*_dsa` / `*_dsv4`
  - kpool metadata functions → `*_kpool`
  - `_kv_splits_for_stream` → `kv_splits_for_stream` (public)
- **Test oracles → `sglang.test.kernels`.** The dead `triton_create_paged_compress_data` is deleted.

### kvcache ↔ attention, attention subpackages
- **To `attention`:** `kv_indices`, `trtllm_mha_page_table`, `trtllm_mha_graph_metadata`, `aiter_unified_page_table`, `fused_qk_rope_reshape_and_cache`, and the MLA Q/K prep from `cache_ops` (→ `mla_qk_prep.py`).
- **`attention/utils.py` forwarding re-exports removed.** 21 importers now import from the defining modules. The shuffle-5D store and gather → `kvcache/shuffle_5d_cache.py`. Two duplicate inventory specs dropped.
- **SGLang-written files moved out of the vendored `attention/fla/`:** 7 files → `attention/linear/`, and `kda_prefill_graph_track` → `mamba/`. `BailingLinearKernel` → its srt backend.
- **FA4 MLA SM100:** test and benchmark code moved out of the production module (`flash_fwd_mla_sm100.py`) into `test/manual/`.
- **MiniMax sparse:** the Gluon prefill moved from `srt/layers/attention/minimax_sparse_ops` → `kernels/ops/attention/minimax_sparse/`. Its `tests/` folder had never been collected and had stale imports; it is now in `test/registered`, with the slow autotune test nightly. The unused `naive/` references are deleted.
- **Lazy KernelSpecs** for unregistered public entry points: Helion/CuTeDSL/PTX KDA and GDN, FP8 FA SM120, vattn asm, minimax sparse and CP indexer, and others.

### Other groups
- **GEMMs out of `quantization` → `gemm`:** `nvfp4_gemm_swiglu_nvfp4_quant`, the gfx950 MXFP8 GEMV/GEMM (with its tuning JSON), `mxfp8_flydsl`, `mxfp8_aiter`, and the MXFP8 blockscaled linears.
- **By rule 3:**
  - `rmsnorm_fake_quant_amd_gfx95` → `layernorm`
  - SwiGLU/SiLU+MXFP8 → `activation`
  - `minimax_quant_ue8m0` → `moe`
  - `upscale` (dequant) → `quantization`
  - MXFP8 epilogue helpers → `quantization`
  - `quant_store_kv_mxfp8` and the interleaved SF → `kvcache`
  - diffusion modulate+MXFP8 → `diffusion/modulate`
- **`elementwise`:** RMSNorms → `layernorm`; `gelu_and_mul_triton` and `bias_gelu` → `activation`.
- **Other moves:**
  - `hc_mix` split-K → `gemm`; `router_gate_matvec` → `gemm`
  - `silu_and_mul_clamp` / `silu_and_mul_contig_post_quant` → `activation`; these also serve dense MLPs.
  - `ngram_embedding` → `embeddings`
  - `softcap_row_argmax` → `sampling`
  - `bmm_fp8`'s implementation moved out of srt into `gemm/flashinfer_bmm_fp8.py`
  - `communication/mp.py` → `srt/distributed`
- **Duplicates:**
  - `moe/triton_sigmoid_gate_mul` merged into `elementwise.fused_sigmoid_mul`: bit-exact over 92 cases on sm_90/sm_100/sm_120.
  - Kept, each with a one-line comment saying why, because they are not bit-exact with their twin: `mla_output_gate` (rounds the gate to bf16 first), the `hc_mix` split-K vs persistent kernels, `swiglu_oai_mxfp8`, DSpark `SoftmaxTemp`, `act_quant`, the V4 Triton RoPE, the grok/gfx1250 RMSNorms, int8 group quant on ROCm, marlin SiTU.
- **Housekeeping:**
  - hipcc build helpers → `kernels/jit/utils/hipcc.py`
  - `_jit_*` module prefixes removed
  - KernelSpecs added for `kv_canary` / `lplb`
  - `mhc.hc_combine` → `mhc_combine` (it clashed with `elementwise.hc_combine`)
  - test helpers `fp8_cvt` and `scatter_req_token_ids` reference → `sglang.test.kernels`
  - the unused `mxfp4_marlin_repack` deleted
  - CODEOWNERS kept in sync for moved files

## Bugs fixed along the way
- **CuTeDSL GDN/KDA prefill was selected on SM120 and crashed.** `_is_blackwell()` returned `major >= 10`, but the kernels need tcgen05. The first extend failed with an NVVM `unsupported operation` on sm_120a. They are now gated to SM10x, and SM120 falls back to Triton; B200 still selects CuTeDSL.
- **Muse Spark RMSNorm+NVFP4 quant had no native reference.** `forward_native` raised `NotImplementedError`, which BaseFusedOp does not allow. It is now implemented and checked against the JIT kernel.
- **MiniMax sparse attention tests never ran:** they sat inside the srt package with stale imports. They are fixed and registered.
- **FlashInfer KDA comments wrongly said "SM100-only".** SM120 runs the generic CuTeDSL path, verified on an RTX PRO 6000. Comment fix only.

## Coordination
**#44667 and #44668** (Fridge003) touch `ops/muse_spark/`. New locations:

| old `ops/muse_spark/…` | new |
|---|---|
| `fused_muse_spark_routing.py` | `moe/muse_spark_routing.py` |
| `fused_norm_gate.py` | `layernorm/muse_spark_norm_gate.py` |
| `fused_norm_residual.py` | `layernorm/muse_spark_norm_residual.py` |
| `fused_op_tuning.py` | `layernorm/_muse_spark_tuning.py` (configs in `layernorm/configs/muse_spark/`) |
| `fused_qk_norm.py` / `helion_qk_norm.py` | `attention/muse_spark_qk_norm_rope_store{,_helion}.py` |
| `helion_runtime.py` | `kernels/jit/utils/helion_runtime.py` |
| `fi_trtllm_moe_finalize_with_rmsnorm_cutedsl.py` | `communication/muse_spark_moe_finalize_all_reduce_cutedsl.py` |

Notes for the rebase:
- `FusedPostNormResidualPreNorm` now takes `post_norm_is_input_scale` and `use_residual_gate`, and `forward_with_ag` is gone. Call `communication.muse_spark_all_gather_norm_residual(..., **op.jit_kernel_kwargs())`.
- `FinalizePushWorkspace` now lives in `srt/layers/communication/muse_spark_finalize_workspace.py`.
- #44668's `helion_megakernels/` and its tests need a logical group; the guard test rejects `ops/muse_spark` and `test/registered/kernels/ops/muse_spark`.

## Validation

- **Static checks:**
  - pre-commit is clean on every changed file.
  - Every relocation is byte-identical apart from import paths (AST or normalized diff, per move).
  - The 94 old module paths have 0 remaining references.
  - A static resolver over every `sglang.*` import and every KernelSpec target finds 0 new unresolved names vs main.
- **Collection and imports:**
  - `pytest --collect-only` over `test/registered`, the diffusion unit tests and the AOT tests shows no new collection errors on H200 or B200. 340 more tests are collected: the new tests plus the MiniMax tests that could not be collected before.
  - The import walk over `sglang.kernels`, `multimodal_gen` and `srt.{layers,models,speculative,mem_cache,disaggregation}` fails on exactly the same modules as main. These are only the optional helion/aiter/flydsl dependencies, now under their new paths.
- **GPU sweep on H200 (sm_90) and B200 (sm_100):** 676 test files, covering every changed test and every test that imports a changed module.
  - Each failure was re-run on main and compared by FAILED test id. **No new failures.**
  - The two files that failed only in the parallel sweep hit port collisions (`EADDRINUSE`) and pass when run alone.
  - The split MXFP8-swizzled tests reproduce main's 29 H200 failures exactly. They are registered on B200 only.
- **Multi-GPU (4×B200, through each test's torchrun launcher):** `test_collectives` (covers the moved attn_res collectives and the gemm all-gather), `test_ar_fusion`, `test_tp_qknorm`, `test_symm_mem_all_gather` and `test_deterministic_reduce_scatter` all pass on both main and this PR.
- **Moved ops vs main:** bitwise identical, old path vs new path, for 17 ops on H200 and B200, and for `indexed_scale_shift_mxfp8_` both directly and through the diffusion facade. The `sigmoid_gate_mul` merge is bit-exact over 92 cases on sm_90, sm_100 and sm_120.
- **New Muse Spark kernel tests (fused vs native)** pass on sm_90, sm_100 and sm_120.
- **Helion backends:** the four moved Helion kernel files are line-identical to main apart from imports, and they import under Helion 1.4.0. Helion is not in the CI image, and its pinned configs cover only production shapes.
- **sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000):** the GDN/KDA CuTeDSL gate fix was checked before and after; FlashInfer GDN/KDA was probed against Triton; the Muse Spark op tests pass.
- **Final head with latest main merged:** main's new tests and the namespace test (85 passed) pass on H200 and B200.
- **Not validated at runtime:**
  - ROCm/HIP, NPU and XPU paths, which got static checks plus imports of the CUDA-importable modules.
  - Muse Spark's multi-GPU paths (all-gather, fused-AR finalize, SP collective GEMMs). They have no unit tests; only `test_muse_spark_12_b300_pd.py` covers them.
  - The 8-GPU variants.

title: [Fix] diffusion: Prevent int32 overflow in Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo VAE RMSNorm
author: tristan-me
body:
## Motivation

The channel-first RMSNorm pointwise kernel in the Qwen-Image 2.1 VAE computes flattened offsets in int32. When `CHANNELS * SPATIAL` exceeds `INT32_MAX`, compilation can fail. A larger total element count across batches can also overflow the flattened index.

With SGLang's default `quality="lossless"` setting, Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo can fail when generating 4K images, reporting an error at `norm_index`:

`CompilationError: Scalar 2371092480 is out of range for type int32`.

Fixing the channel RMSNorm indexing allows generation to complete.

## Modifications

- Cast `program_id` to int64 **before** multiplying by `BLOCK` in `channel_rmsnorm_preserve_reduction.py`:
   ```python
   index = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
   ```

## Accuracy Tests

### Fix verification

`quality` uses the default `lossless` setting. The environment uses PyTorch 2.13.0 and Triton 3.7.1, with text-encoder CPU offload enabled and VAE tiling disabled. Both arms use the same model, inputs, seeds and eight-step configuration; only the indexing expression changes. All four cases below use an actual size of **3840×2144**. Before the fix, each fails to compile due to the int32 error and produces no image. After the fix, each completes one warmup and three measured requests; all four outputs within each case are byte-identical. Times are the means of the three measured requests. Raw request times and configurations are in `default-lossless-validation.json` in the bundle.

| Workload | Before | After | Fixed mean (s) |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Text-to-image | Failure | Success | 111.666 |
| One-reference edit | Failure | Success | 167.492 |
| Two-reference edit | Failure | Success | 235.382 |
| Three-reference edit | Failure | Success | 307.789 |


### Output equivalence

**Environment:** 1×H20 (SM90), Python 3.12.15, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Triton 3.8.0.

- **30 CUDA regression tests passed**, including full nonuniform BF16/FP16 tensors crossing `2**31`. All four full-tensor outputs match the Torch reference byte for byte.
- 4K text-to-image test with `quality` set to `exact`: **generation fails before the fix, with no image; after the fix, generation succeeds, and the warmup image and all three measured images exactly match the Torch norm reference images.**
- The 4K generation was confirmed to call the fixed channel RMSNorm function.

<details>
<summary>Regression coverage and reproduction</summary>

Full-tensor tests cover the large tensor used by a single 4K decode and tensors whose total element count across batches exceeds `2**31`, in BF16 and FP16. The reference is `F.normalize(x.float(), dim=1).to(dtype) * scale * weight + 0.0`. Whole-output byte checks cover channel and batch boundaries, offsets around the 32-bit index limit, and the tail.

Community-source model settings: BF16, 8 steps, seed 1042, CPU generator, guidance 1, `torch_sdpa`, TP1/SP1/CFG1; text-encoder CPU offload on. Workloads that generate successfully both before and after the fix use one warmup and three measured requests per arm. The reference images use the Torch implementation with this kernel’s optimized dispatch disabled; other settings are unchanged.

```bash
# In the SGLang checkout, with diffusion dependencies and at least 40 GiB free GPU memory:
SGLANG_REPO="$PWD"
pre-commit run --all-files
# Run standalone validation from the unpacked bundle using the tested source/environment:
cd /path/to/unpacked-validation-bundle
PYTHONPATH="$SGLANG_REPO/python" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
  SGLANG_TEST_LARGE_CHANNEL_RMSNORM=1 python -m pytest -v \
  files/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_channel_rmsnorm_preserve_reduction.py
PYTHONPATH="$SGLANG_REPO/python:$PWD/reproduce" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
  python reproduce/kernel_validation.py --repo "$SGLANG_REPO" --output "$PWD/kernel-replay"
PYTHONPATH="$SGLANG_REPO/python" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
  python reproduce/benchmark_graph.py "$SGLANG_REPO" "$PWD/graph-replay"
```

The validation bundle, [channel-rmsnorm-int64-pr-ready.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33653278/channel-rmsnorm-int64-pr-ready.zip), contains replay scripts, model configurations and raw records.

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Whole-model generation

Retested on one H20 using the community source and runtime above. For each quality setting, four fresh model instances run in this order: **before, after, after, before**. Each instance performs one warmup and three measured requests per workload. Each table value pools six measured requests from two instances.

SDK wall time includes preprocessing, IPC and PNG saving, excluding model loading and warmup. Values are **mean ± sample standard deviation**. Change = `(after / before − 1) × 100%`. **The table’s 24 measured before/after image pairs are identical in PNG bytes and RGBA pixels, with SSIM 1.**

| Quality | Workload | Size | Before (s) | After (s) | Mean time change |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| lossless | Text-to-image | 1024×1024 | 4.871 ± 0.350 | 4.757 ± 0.070 | -2.33% |
| lossless | One-reference edit | 1024×1024 | 6.305 ± 0.235 | 6.302 ± 0.296 | -0.05% |
| exact | Text-to-image | 1024×1024 | 5.035 ± 0.422 | 4.885 ± 0.139 | -2.99% |
| exact | One-reference edit | 1024×1024 | 6.252 ± 0.009 | 6.257 ± 0.026 | +0.08% |

<details>
<summary>Pointwise-kernel microbenchmark</summary>

Each CUDA graph captures 100 kernel launches; each timed event covers 10 replays. After warmup, before/after order alternates for 30 paired rounds. Values below are median GPU time per launch, not whole-model time. Shape order is batch, channels, time, height, width; four-dimensional inputs omit time.

| Dtype | Input shape | Before (µs) | After (µs) | Time change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| bfloat16 | 2,32,3,7 | 1.574 | 1.607 | +2.09% |
| bfloat16 | 1,128,1,256,256 | 16.312 | 15.138 | -7.20% |
| bfloat16 | 1,384,1,256,256 | 53.055 | 50.509 | -4.80% |
| bfloat16 | 1,288,1,512,512 | 165.648 | 157.587 | -4.87% |
| float16 | 2,32,3,7 | 1.561 | 1.579 | +1.13% |
| float16 | 1,128,1,256,256 | 15.777 | 14.681 | -6.95% |
| float16 | 1,384,1,256,256 | 53.016 | 50.831 | -4.12% |
| float16 | 1,288,1,512,512 | 166.290 | 158.444 | -4.72% |

</details>

These measurements cover the listed inputs on H20. Raw request times, image checks and graph samples are in `performance-recheck.json`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit) (`precommit-linux.json`).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (Standalone regression tests are in the validation bundle.)
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not applicable: this internal kernel fix does not require user-documentation changes.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Perf] [AMD] dsv41: run gfx950 MXFP8 dense GEMMs on aiter's preshuffled FlyDSL kernel
author: kkHuang-amd
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.

Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

On gfx950 the aiter MXFP8 dense route runs the Triton group32 GEMM on the plain weight. aiter's FlyDSL MXFP8 GEMM
(ROCm/aiter#5896, already in the pinned aiter) is faster when the weight is kept (16, 16)-preshuffled.

## Modifications

- `SGLANG_ROCM_MXFP8_AITER_PRESHUFFLE` (default off): at load time shuffle the aiter-route dense weights in place
  (one copy, no extra memory) and call `gemm_a8w8_blockscale(..., isBpreshuffled=True)`.
- Preshuffled layers skip the in-tree FlyDSL MXFP8 prefill path (`SGLANG_OPT_HIP_FLYDSL_MXFP8`), which needs the plain
  weight; the aiter kernel serves prefill as well.
- DSpark draft: the fused wkv projection passes the preshuffle flag through.
- Test: the aiter-route test also runs with preshuffle on (M 1 to 2049), within one bf16 ulp of the bf16 route.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP2): 0.898 -> 0.901 with this on (same tree otherwise).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP2 on MI355X, flag off -> on: decode step bs 16 18.03 -> 17.17 ms (-4.8%), bs 64 36.51 -> 35.67 ms
(-2.3%); idle prefill 4k / 16k new tokens over a 32k cached prefix 0.123 -> 0.110 s / 0.303 -> 0.291 s.
AgentX c64: 169,008 -> 170,633 tok/s/GPU.

- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Perf] function_call: stop rescanning unclosed GLM tool calls per chunk
author: YangChen-pro
body:
## Motivation

GLM-4.5/4.6 (`Glm4MoeDetector`) and GLM-4.7/GLM-5 (`Glm47MoeDetector`) already stream args incrementally, but on every chunk they run the streaming regex over the whole buffer again, just to get the name and the args so far. So one long arg (like `write_file` content) costs O(n²). Profiling a 16k-char arg with 4-char deltas, `re.Pattern.search` is 85-87% of the time.

## Modifications

While a call is still open, the buffer only grows at the end, so the name and where the args start can't change. `_match_tool_call` remembers them after the first match, and after that only looks for `</tool_call>` (or `$`) in the new tail. It returns exactly what the call site used to read from the match, so the rest of `parse_streaming_increment` is untouched. The cache is dropped once the closer shows up.

+27/-5 and +34/-10, plus one test per detector.

## Why the output is the same

- The cache only exists while the call is open, and during that time `_buffer` is only appended to. It only gets reassigned when the closer is found, or when there's no `<tool_call>` in it, which can't happen while a call is open.
- Appending can't move the match start or the name. The name ends at the first `\n` or literal `\\n` (GLM-4.5), or the first `<arg_key` (GLM-4.7), and those are already in the buffer.
- The args end at the first `</tool_call>` or `$`. The old buffer had no closer after the args start, so a new one has to end in the new text. Scanning from `len(old) - len("</tool_call>") + 1` is enough.

## Testing

- Fuzzed against `main`: 25k random streams per detector. Half look like real calls (multiple calls, `\n` / `\\n` / no separator, empty names, unclosed calls, tag pieces inside values), half are random tag pieces, newlines and text. Chunk sizes 1-40. I compared every chunk's result, `finish()`, and all detector state. No diffs. To check the fuzzer itself, I broke the patch three ways (no tail overlap, overlap one char short, never clearing the cache), and each one fails within the first few cases on both detectors.
- New `test_streaming_long_argument_is_not_rescanned` for both: a 4000-char arg in 3-char chunks runs the streaming regex once, and the args come out right.
- `TestGlm4MoeDetector`, `TestGlm47MoeDetector`, `TestGlm47FullAssistantGrammar`, `test_glm47_schema_types.py`: no new failures.

## Benchmark

One long string arg, 4-char deltas:

| detector | chars | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-4.5 | 32,000 | 3.93s | 0.15s |
| GLM-4.5 | 128,000 | 59.30s | 0.99s |
| GLM-4.7 | 32,000 | 5.91s | 0.15s |
| GLM-4.7 | 128,000 | 88.41s | 1.15s |

What's left per chunk is plain string copying (`_buffer += new_text`, slicing the args, `_current_value += char` in the XML-to-JSON state machine). It still grows with the arg, but at memcpy speed. I kept it out of this PR to keep it small.

author: AgainstEntropy
body:

Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

Out-of-tree (OOT) platforms cannot run EAGLE-family speculative decoding today, including NEXTN/MTP drafts:

- The built-in `EAGLEWorkerV2` keeps its bookkeeping in device tensors with data-dependent shapes. Platforms that compile a graph per shape cannot run it efficiently, so they ship their own speculative worker (for example one that keeps the bookkeeping on the host) and today have to monkeypatch `SpeculativeAlgorithm.create_worker` to install it.
- On an OOT device the built-in path is broken without saying so: `verify_tree_greedy_func` (`kernels/ops/speculative/spec_tree.py`) has no branch for it and returns its inputs unfilled, and `build_tree_kernel_efficient_func` calls a kernel that is only imported on CUDA/HIP/MUSA builds.

This PR is the first step of generic OOT speculative-decoding support. It adds the platform worker factory and makes the unsupported built-in path fail loudly. Follow-ups will add the seams the built-in worker needs on an OOT device (draft attention backend registry, draft graph runners, spec kernels on `BaseFusedOp` with native fallbacks).

## Modifications

- `SRTPlatform.get_speculative_worker_cls(algorithm)` (default `None`). On an OOT platform `create_worker` returns this class for any algorithm; `None` keeps the built-in worker. The class is constructed with the built-in worker's keyword arguments and must reject flags it cannot serve. `SpeculativeAlgorithm.get_platform_worker_cls()` is the single lookup.
- EAGLE / EAGLE3 / NEXTN / STANDALONE on an OOT platform now require `supports_speculative_algorithm(algorithm)` (NEXTN is asked as `"EAGLE"`), mirroring the existing DFLASH gate, with an actionable error.
- `adaptive_unsupported_reason()` reports a platform worker, so `--speculative-adaptive` falls back to static parameters with the existing warning instead of being silently ignored (`AdaptiveController` lives only in `EAGLEWorkerV2`).
- `build_tree_kernel_efficient_func` and `verify_tree_greedy_func` in `kernels/ops/speculative/spec_tree.py` raise `NotImplementedError` via `reject_out_of_tree_path` on an OOT device that has no tree kernel. In-tree devices and OOT platforms on a CUDA/HIP/MUSA torch build are unchanged.
- Docs: the hook is added to the plugin guide.

**Behavior change for OOT platforms:** EAGLE-family algorithms now need `supports_speculative_algorithm(...)` to return True (default False, same as DFLASH). Built-in platforms are unaffected.

## Accuracy Tests

No change on built-in platforms: every new branch is guarded by `is_out_of_tree()` or sits on a path that previously raised or computed nothing.

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/spec/test_oot_eagle_hooks.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`):

- worker selection: the platform class wins on OOT, the built-in worker when the platform declines, in-tree platforms never consult the hook;
- algorithm gate: an unsupported OOT platform is rejected, built-in platforms are not gated;
- adaptive falls back with a platform worker and stays available with the built-in one;
- tree construction and greedy verification raise on an OOT device without a tree kernel (both fail on the pre-fix code), and the in-tree fall-through is unchanged.

```

       test/registered/unit/test_split_attention_backend_decisions.py

## Motivation

An out-of-tree (OOT) platform that runs the built-in `EAGLEWorkerV2` with device graph capture cannot capture the EAGLE draft graphs:

- `EagleDraftWorker._capture_cuda_graphs` looks the draft decode and draft extend runners up in maps keyed by in-tree device names (`cuda`, `npu`, `xpu`, `musa`), which raises `KeyError` for an OOT device.
- Adaptive speculation (`--speculative-adaptive`) hardcodes `NPUGraphRunner if _is_npu else DecodeCudaGraphRunner` for its per-configuration target verify graphs, so an OOT platform gets the CUDA runner, while its startup target verify graph comes from `get_graph_runner_cls()`.

This is part of generic OOT speculative-decoding support, for platforms that use the built-in worker (the previous PR covers platforms that bring their own worker).

## Modifications

- `SRTPlatform.get_speculative_graph_runner_cls(algorithm, phase)` (default `None`) with `phase` in `"draft_decode"` / `"draft_extend"`. The class is constructed like the built-in runner for that phase. `None` runs the phase eagerly, and the hook is not consulted when `capabilities.graph_capture` is False.
- `_select_spec_graph_runner_cls` picks the runner in one place: built-in platforms keep today's device-keyed selection (including the draft extend backend conditions); on an OOT platform only the platform answers, so the device maps are never indexed.
- Adaptive target verify runners on an OOT platform come from `get_graph_runner_cls()`, the same class as the startup target verify graph, so one run never mixes runner classes across step configurations. The keyword arguments it must accept (`attn_backend`, `speculative_num_steps`, `speculative_num_draft_tokens`) are documented on the hook.
- Docs: the plugin guide lists the new hook and the adaptive requirement on `get_graph_runner_cls()`.

## Accuracy Tests

No change on built-in platforms: their runner selection is evaluated exactly as before.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

## Tests

Added to `test/registered/unit/spec/test_oot_eagle_hooks.py` (CPU):

- `_capture_cuda_graphs` on an OOT device takes the draft decode and draft extend runners from the platform and constructs them with the worker (fails with `KeyError: 'custom'` before this change);
- nothing is consulted or captured without `capabilities.graph_capture`;
- built-in platforms never consult the platform hook.

## Motivation

Add initial Cambricon MLU support, including device management, CNCL communication, RMSNorm, installation instructions, and CI tests.

## Modifications

### Initial MLU support

- Platform detection and device management, including device selection, memory queries, synchronization, cache management, and random-seed support.
- Reuse generic all-reduce and all-gather paths with CNCL and MLU custom-op registration.
- Fused RMSNorm and residual addition, with reshaping for 1D, higher-rank, and transposed inputs, and native fallback for unsupported configurations, layouts, and mixed dtypes.
- Reject deterministic mode explicitly for MLU RMSNorm; deterministic inference support is deferred to a follow-up.

### Tests and CI integration

- Add MLU test registration and suite execution through `--hw mlu`.
- Add single-device RMSNorm and two-device communication suites, covering eager and `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` collectives, with platform and operator-dispatch unit tests.
- Include MLU tests in CI coverage reporting and registration validation.
- Add MLU test recognition to `/rerun-test`.

### Installation and documentation

- Add `srt_mlu`, `all_mlu`, and `dev_mlu` installation extras. Pin `torch-mlu`, `torch-mlu-ops`, and Triton to their versions in `scripts/ci/mlu/component_versions.properties`.
- Record the reference container tag and vendor component versions.
- Document container setup, vendor package preparation, source installation, and CI suite execution.
