title: [Feat] beam: Add Beam model, runtime support and checkpoints (4/7)
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

Split #44747 into reviewable parts. This part adds the runtime support Beam relies on and the Beam model, position 4 of 7 in the merge order below. It folds in #45255, which is closed in its favor, the way Muse Spark's runtime and model landed together. It is based on #45254's branch (`beam-stack-02-kernels`), so its diff shows only this part.

## Modifications

Runtime support:
- **TRT-LLM MHA.** An extend batch whose trailing requests extend by one token runs that tail on the decode kernel. This now also covers FP8 KV and batches made only of one-token requests. It extends #43238 and runs on trtllm-gen (SM100) only; SM90 and SM120 take FMHA-v2 or the context-parallel path and never reach it.
- **FlashInfer MegaMoE.** Beam is added to the validated MegaMoE architectures. The startup autotune fix that the high-throughput recipe needs with default autotune, and the optional decode workspace, are in #46213.
- **PD decode.** A token-ID logprob row is reserved for the handoff token, so streamed rows stay aligned. That row is empty, because prefill does not send token-ID logprobs.
- **Forward-pass metrics.** DFlash is added to the spec decode pre-settlement snapshot.
- **Pool configurator.** The SWA request-cap budget now includes the DFlash draft cell.

Beam model and config:
- Hybrid sliding-window/full attention, SSMax query scaling, attention output gating, sandwich norms, depth-scaled residuals and grouped MoE routing.
- BF16, ModelOpt NVFP4 and compressed-tensors FP8 checkpoints. Compressed-tensors NVFP4 is rejected.
- **DFlash integration.** Beam uses the general CUDA attention-DP implementation from merged #46330 and draft placement from merged #46290. This PR adds the `DFlash2BeamDraftModel` alias, Beam's embedding/lm-head DP mapping, and hidden-state capture. The generic DFlash admission hook, worker, embedding helper and verify-metadata path match the parent branch.
- GB300 Triton MoE configs for `E=256,N=640`, used by the BF16 Triton MoE path.
- **Opt-in single-token MoE GEMV** (`SGLANG_OPT_BEAM_DECODE_GEMV`).
  - It uses the unquantized Triton MoE path and requires `SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_SWIGLU_INTERLEAVED=1`, BF16 experts of the Beam shape, MoE TP4/EP1 and SM103. Each invocation also needs one contiguous BF16 token.
  - Other setups, and forwards with more than one token, keep their normal MoE path. Only a failed static check logs that the switch is unused.
  - It is not bit-exact with the Triton path.

Beam's router uses the tiny FP32 GEMM up to 16 tokens for BF16 checkpoints, then the GEMV, then the cuBLAS BF16x3 GEMM. The cuTile router and `SGLANG_BEAM_ROUTER_BACKEND` are in #45361.

General fixes found while adding Beam are in their own PRs:
- #46213: MegaMoE startup autotune on FlashInfer 0.7.2, and an optional decode workspace;
- #46214: the FlashInfer ragged prefill sliding window;
- #46200: the SWA KV pool start layer under pipeline parallelism.

The only test change is DFlash in `test_forward_pass_metrics.py`'s snapshot loop. Without the metrics change, Beam with DFlash and `--enable-forward-pass-metrics` fails during startup warmup with `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable`.

The Beam E2E test is in #45257. The unchanged upstream DFlash admission, embedding and metadata tests come from #46330.

LoRA serving for Beam is not part of this split. Beam raises `NotImplementedError` for `--enable-lora` and `--lora-paths` when the model is built. LoRA serving will follow separately.

The split commits carry the `Co-authored-by` trailers of the Beam commits that touched these files.

## Validation

**Current DFlash integration cleanup (`903d45e17d`):** 58 tests passed across seven existing DFlash/draft-placement files, with one existing CUDA-only test skipped in the CPU-only run. The nine admission/embedding/metadata cases pass unchanged. No test code was added or modified. The two remaining generic DFlash overrides were removed so this branch uses #46330's implementation.

**Historical GPU/model results:** the runs below predate this cleanup and were not repeated for it.

All runs are on 4×GB300 with FlashInfer 0.7.2. The tree is this PR plus #43216, which has since merged.
- **Checkpoints:** the public `reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4`, `reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-FP8` and `reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B` checkpoints, plus the DFlash2 draft.
- **Evaluation:** GSM8K with sgl-eval 0.1.3, 1,319 questions, temperature 0.
- **Revisions:** all runs are on earlier commits of this branch.
  - Those commits also carried the FlashInfer ragged sliding-window fix (now #46214), the MegaMoE changes (now #46213) and the SWA pool start-layer change (now #46200). None of the runs uses the FlashInfer attention backend, the decode workspace or pipeline parallelism.
  - The high-throughput rows with default autotune need #46213's autotune fix.
  - Since these runs, the branch has merged newer main changes through #45254, including #46330 and #46290. The DFlash cleanup removes the earlier Beam-only admission check and the broader selector-warmup override.
- **Cold-JIT row:** this run deliberately hid the AOT top-k artifact and removed its cached build.

| Configuration | GSM8K | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Cookbook low-latency NVFP4 (TP4, DFlash, without parser flags) | 96.36% | zero request errors; the DFlash2 selector is folded into the draft CUDA graph |
| Cookbook low-latency FP8 | 96.66% | zero errors |
| Cookbook high-throughput NVFP4 (MegaMoE TP4/DP4/EP4), cold autotune cache | 96.44% | with #46213's autotune fix; MegaMoE autotune completes |
| High-throughput NVFP4 plus DFlash, default autotune | 96.44% | with #46213's autotune fix; zero errors |
| The same with autotune off | 96.44% | zero errors |
| BF16 TP4, attention DP2, DFlash | 96.44% | concurrent outputs identical to isolated in the probe |
| BF16 TP4 with the decode GEMV | 96.21% | the GEMV kernels run at batch size 1 |
| Cold FlashInfer JIT (no AOT top-k), DFlash with attention DP4 | 96.51% | the selector's top-k builds during startup; without the warm-up, the first decode builds it inside the scheduler watchdog and the server is killed |

- **Verifier.** With #45257's parser changes on top of this branch, the pinned Beam verifier `dfa85fe771b3bcf014f5af5913f2ed363d31dfdf` passes all 133 required e2e cases at temperature 0, with its source and fixture integrity check passing and no skips.
  - The run uses the cookbook low-latency recipe with parser flags and scores 96.59% on GSM8K with zero request errors.
  - Chat reasoning, streaming, a chat tool call, Responses text, a Responses function call, a Responses shell round trip and `/tokenize` all pass.
  - No optional verifier suite or third-party evaluation was run.
- **TRT-LLM mixed tail.** The mixed-tail cases from #44747 pass (16 passed, 2 skipped on SM100). They include batches of only one-token requests, split-versus-unsplit parity, long-context FP64 references and CUDA-graph replay.
- **GEMV numerics.** Both kernels were compared with an FP64 reference that rounds to BF16 where the kernels do: after the gate/up projection, after `silu(gate) * up`, and at the routing-weighted output.
  - On 8 real checkpoint experts, the GEMV's BF16 output matches the reference on nearly every element, with relative L2 below 2e-9.
  - In the tested random-input cases, the GEMV is within relative L2 3.4e-4.
  - The Triton deferred-sum path is within 4.2e-4 to 6.8e-4 of the same reference, and the GEMV versus Triton is within 6.3e-4.
  - With a fixed kernel config, the shared Triton MoE path is bitwise unchanged from the base.
- **Existing GPU tests.** Main's tests for the touched code pass unedited: TRT-LLM MHA dense, graph metadata, encoder-only and stride parity; Triton MoE padding and fused MoE; and the DFlash buffer, Domino and graph-pool tests.
- **CPU tests.** The CPU tests that import the touched modules pass, except three files that fail the same way on main in this environment. pre-commit passes.
- **Known behavior.** Under attention DP4, a request's greedy output can change with other ranks' load.
  - This was observed with MegaMoE, with the TRT-LLM MoE runner without MegaMoE, without DFlash, and on the previously published head.
  - In the probe's valid comparisons, the isolated run's top-2 logprob margin at the first differing token ranged from 0 to 0.262 nat.
  - Isolated requests were deterministic in repeat probes, and these runs showed no GSM8K accuracy regression and zero request errors.
  - This does not establish universal batch invariance or a specific kernel-level cause. BF16 with attention DP2 matched isolated outputs exactly.
- **Not validated here:**
  - NPU;
  - Hopper and SM120 (all runs are on GB300);
  - BF16 on two nodes (TP8), including the TP8 cluster path of #45254's all-reduce boundary;
  - serving with PD token-ID logprobs (that fix has CPU checks only).

## Merge order

Each part is based on the one before it, so its diff shows only its own changes. Merge bottom-up; after each part merges, the next part is retargeted to `main` and `main` is merged into it. #44747 stays open, unchanged, as the full reference. Merge in this order:

1. #45253 — Beam CUDA Docker image (merged)
2. #45291 — OpenAI SDK 2.8.0, needed by the Responses shell tools in #45257 (merged)
3. #45254 — Kernels
4. #45256 — Beam model and runtime integration (using upstream #46330 for DFlash CUDA DP) (#45255 folded in; also after #46213 for the high-throughput recipe with default autotune; #43216 is merged)
5. #45257 — Beam reasoning, tool calls, response templates and the Beam E2E test (#40478, #43941 and #40479 are merged)
6. #45290 — `nvidia-cuda-tileiras`, needed by #45361
7. #45361 — cuTile BF16x3 router GEMM (optional: without it Beam uses the cuBLAS router)

#45292 (Dynamo and `grpcio-tools` pins for the Beam image) is not in the merge order for now.

title: [Perf] deepseek-v4: DSpark draft stages take the TF32 mHC statistics path from 32 rows on SM100
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

Under DSpark decode, the three draft stages compute the mixing statistics of their six mHC boundaries with the Triton split-K kernel (`hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn`) at every batch, while the target layers run DeepGEMM's `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` from 128 rows. Two reasons: the DSpark model never calls `refresh_mhc_norm_weight_cache`, so its stages have no TF32 weight parts, and `_mix_stats_impl` keeps the DeepGEMM path off under 128 rows on SM100 (SM90 uses it from 32).

Measured on GB300 (DEP16 decode, DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash, 128K contexts, torch profiler, kernel durations):

| Draft rows (= requests per rank) | `_hc_mix_stats_partial_kernel`, 6 launches | `_hc_mix_reduce_sinkhorn_kernel`, 6 launches | Per cycle |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 | 6 x 23.8 us | 6 x 9.0 us | 0.197 ms |
| 64 | 6 x 42.2 us | 6 x 9.1 us | 0.307 ms |
| 256 | 6 x 150 us | 6 x 10.5 us | 0.963 ms |

In the same traces the target's unfused boundaries run `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm_impl` at 7.4-7.9 us per launch (160 and 320 rows) plus a 16-slice reduce of 7.8 us: about 23 us per boundary against 52 us on the Triton path at 64 rows. The 128-row floor is not a kernel requirement: DeepGEMM's SM100 kernel uses `block_m = 64` with a grid of `num_splits x ceil_div(m, 64)` and no assertion on M.

## Modifications

- `DeepseekV4ForCausalLMDSpark.post_load_weights` calls `refresh_mhc_norm_weight_cache` on each stage, which builds the TF32 parts of the 24 x 20,480 mixing weights (24 MB per GPU for three stages).
- `_mix_stats_impl`: the row floor for the TF32 parts becomes 32 on SM100 as on SM90 (`x_flat.shape[0] >= 32` replaces `>= 128 or hopper_medium`, which already meant 32 on SM90). Batch-invariant mode and rows under 32 are unchanged.

Expected: about 0.17 ms less per decode cycle at 64 requests per rank (22.6 ms cycle), 0.06 ms at 32.

## Accuracy Tests

The draft's statistics move from the Triton tf32x3 kernel to the two-part TF32 split the target already runs at 128 rows and above. Accept length from the A/B decode logs will be posted here; GSM8K at native acceptance on request.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The A/B at 64 requests per rank (same recipe, base main 49766a74f9 against this branch) is running; the six draft launches and the log cycle will be posted here.

title: [Feat] [NVIDIA] megakernels: Qwen3.5 binding and EAGLE entry wiring for NVIDIA megakernel plugins
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

The NVIDIA megakernel for Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (NVFP4) decode on GB300 lives out of tree, in sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega#20. sgl-project/sglang#44945 added `--enable-nvidia-megakernel` and the plugin layer for DeepSeek-V4.1. This PR adds what the Qwen3.5 megakernel needs on the SGLang side, in the same shape:
- **a binding for Qwen3.5**: the runtime state SGLang hands the plugin, as data;
- **EAGLE draft entries**: the draft and draft-extend graph runners capture a plugin step at the batch sizes it serves;
- **KV-length attention graph variants**: a runner captures one graph per attention variant the megakernel names, and each replay picks one by KV length.

SGLang keeps every runner, worker, schedule batch and CUDA graph, and everything after a target step (sampling, acceptance, commits). The plugin gets data: the forward's attention and GDN metadata, the KV and mamba pools, and per-entry structs with SGLang-owned outputs. Before capture, every rank must offer the same entries, batch sizes and variants, or SGLang refuses to start.

This PR is based on main and does not depend on sgl-project/sglang#45474 (the runtime changes for the same decode path). Either can merge first; merged in either order, the two give the same tree. Without `--enable-nvidia-megakernel` nothing changes.

## Modifications

One commit per change:

1. **Pick each megakernel's binding by architecture, and agree on the entries it offers** (`megakernels/runtime.py`, `spec.py`). Qwen3.5's `HybridLinearAttnBackend` keeps its metadata on its two child backends, so it needs its own binding. `spec.ENTRIES` names the optional entries (`draft_sampler`, `draft_loop`, `draft_extend`, `begin_draft_round`), and every rank must offer the same ones.
2. **The binding of Qwen3.5's megakernels** (`megakernels/eagle_binding.py`, new). `EagleBinding` returns the view a covered step reads: attention metadata, GDN slots, the KV and mamba pools. Each pool is sealed at its first read, and `assert_live` fails by name if one is reallocated. The entries' structs carry tensors and numbers only. What a plugin may call or read besides data is listed in literal tuples that the plugin's contract test pins.
3. **EAGLE draft graphs run the draft megakernel's `draft_loop` and `draft_extend`** (`speculative/eagle_megakernel.py`, new, plus the worker and the two draft graph runners).
   - Before capture, each runner calls the entry's factory once with its own outputs. At the batch sizes the factory serves, the graph captures that step in place of SGLang's draft loop, or in place of the draft model step and its top-1.
   - `begin_draft_round` runs on the host before a served draft graph replays.
   - The draft worker builds the entries at the end of its `init_attention_backends`, before any capture. It refuses setups it cannot serve: a non-chain draft, rejection sampling, DP attention, a sliding-window target KV pool, or backends other than GDN with `trtllm_mha`.
4. **Capture a megakernel's KV-length attention graph variants in the verify and EAGLE draft graphs** (`spec.py`, `runtime.py`, `forward_batch_info.py`, `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`, the draft runners).
   - A megakernel may offer `graph_variants` for `target_verify`, `draft_loop` or `draft_extend`: capture labels plus a `select` that picks one from host state. At the batch sizes that run the megakernel, the runner captures one graph per label and replays the one `select` picks.
   - `ForwardBatch.attention_kv_len_lower_bound` gives `select` a one-request batch's committed KV length without touching the device.
   - With the plugin, its split-KV kernels run from 8K (verify), 16K (draft steps) or 32K (draft extend) tokens, and SGLang's attention below.

Earlier revisions of this PR were stacked on #45474 and also offered `verify_sample` and `gdn_extend`. Both are removed: the plugin's `verify_sample` had no kernel and only turned on #45474's post-verify graphs (`SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH=1` does the same), and no plugin offered `gdn_extend`. They can come back in a follow-up once a plugin has a kernel for them.

Known limits: draft entries serve graph replays only; a variant's `select` gets a KV length only for one-request batches; SGLang's images pin a plugin commit without Qwen3.5 (`SGL_NVIDIA_MEGA_COMMIT`), so sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega#20 must be installed until that pin moves.

## Accuracy Tests

GB300, TP8, real acceptance, GSM8K on a fixed 250-question subset (sampled: temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 20).

- **Flag off**, against main on the same trays, greedy at concurrency 1 and 16: 250 / 250 texts identical (main against a second main start: 250 / 250). The same Triton kernels and JIT modules are compiled, and no megakernel line is logged. The only visible differences are the new `ForwardBatch` field and one field in the `SGLANG_LOG_DECODE_GRAPH_KEY` debug line.
- **With the plugin** (sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega#20):

| configuration | greedy | sampled | acceptance length vs reference (greedy / sampled) |
|---|---|---|---|
| reference: the development build | 0.980 | 0.984 | 1 / 1 |
| main + this PR + plugin | 0.980 | 0.988 | 1.000 / 0.991 |
| main + #45474 + this PR + plugin | 0.980 | 0.976 | 1.000 / 0.998 |

  Greedy outputs match the reference on 249 / 250 questions in both rows. Every slot, entry and variant capture is active on 8 / 8 ranks.
- **CPU**: the megakernel, speculative and graph-runner unit tests pass wherever main's pass. The plugin's Qwen3.5 tests, including its contract test, pass against this head.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GB300, TP8 across two 4-GPU trays. Static decode of one request at 128K context with forced acceptance 4.80, about 1,780 rounds per server start. TPS/User = 4.80 tokens / round time. Rows 1–3 are the mean of two pairs of trays run in opposite orders. The plugin was measured at `3509187d74`, an earlier revision of sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega#20; the PR head differs only by an opt-in for more than one request, off by default.

| configuration | TPS/User P50 | TPS/User P90 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 706.4 | 700.3 |
| main + this PR + plugin | 765.7 (+8.4%) | 729.6 (+4.2%) |
| main + #45474 + this PR + plugin | 1291.7 (+82.8%) | 1276.0 (+82.2%) |
| the development build (reference) ¹ | 1275.2 | 1249.5 |

¹ On a third pair of trays, row 3 reaches 101.0% of the reference at P50 at 128K, and 100.8% / 100.6% and 101.9% / 101.6% (P50 / P90) at 8K and 32K.

These results were measured on main `28448a86d4`; the branch has since been rebased onto main `b57b5e2286` without changes, and the GPU checks are being repeated on the new base.

Row 2 gains little because the round becomes host-bound: the verify takes 1.87 ms less, but the gaps between graph segments grow from 0.06 to 1.36 ms per round. Row 3 adds #45474, which removes that host work, and the gaps return to 0.06 ms.

title: [Perf] deepseek-v4.1: Drop host syncs from encoder-replay folding and tail metadata
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Encoder SWA replay folding and the late-layer tail metadata built small device tensors with copies that block the host until the stream drains: `torch.tensor(..., device=cuda)` (pageable), `.to(device, non_blocking=True)` on pageable host tensors, a 0-dim CUDA tensor used as an index, and `repeat_interleave` without `output_size`. They run once per prefill step with encoder SWA replay on.
- They now go through `async_h2d` or pinned copies, index replay heads with the batch's host pool indices (`req_pool_indices_cpu`), and pass `output_size`. No behavior change: same values, same rows.
- The unit test's fake batch gains `req_pool_indices_cpu`, which `ScheduleBatch` always carries.
- Verification: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB300, DP2 attention + MegaMoE (EP2), DSpark, encoder and decoder replay on, a multi-turn agentic prefill trace at concurrency 512, 900 s per run.
  - With `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("warn")` over a full run, no synchronizing call remained on the scheduler's forward path.
  - Throughput is within noise (-0.3% to +1.7% on three nodes): once the request-window reset sync was gone (#45247), the scheduler was no longer blocked on these copies. This keeps the forward path sync-free so a later sync is not hidden behind them.
  - `test_encoder_swa_replay.py` and `test_dsv4_compressed_pools.py` pass.

title: [Perf] deepseek-v4.1: Skip the request-window history check when invariant checks are off
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `RequestWindow.buffer` checks each SWA layer's history through `expect(_SWA_HISTORY_PRESENT, ...)` (#45223). The predicate `(tags[layer, src] == history_pos) | ~history_valid` was built before the call, so its three kernels ran on every SWA layer even with `SGLANG_INVARIANT_CHECK` off, the default.
- The check now runs only at WARN or above, the same gate other signal-only `expect` call sites use (`unified_hybrid_swa.py`, `dspark_planner.py`). It has no recovery action, so nothing changes at any level except the skipped launches when it is off.
- Verification:
  - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB300, DP2 attention + MegaMoE (EP2), encoder and decoder replay on, a multi-turn agentic prefill trace at concurrency 512: py-spy put 1.5-2.2% of the scheduler main thread's samples on the predicate line with the check off.
  - A GPU script on `RequestWindow`: matching history passes at STRICT; missing history passes at OFF (not checked) and raises a device-side assert at STRICT.

title: [Perf] detokenizer: Add SGLANG_BATCH_TOKENIZER_OUTPUTS to opt out of grouped return sends
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

#44288 made the detokenizer group its return IPC sends by tokenizer worker: a batch of N requests spread over W workers now costs W sends instead of N. That is the right default for throughput serving.

For latency-sensitive streaming workloads it is not free. Every scheduler step emits one small chunk per request, and each tokenizer worker only wants its own chunk as soon as it exists. With grouping, every reply sits behind a per-step packing hop, and the first reply of a step waits for the whole batch to be split before anything is sent. Deployments that care more about per-chunk latency than about IPC message count need a way back to per-request delivery without giving up anything else.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: add `SGLANG_BATCH_TOKENIZER_OUTPUTS` (`EnvBool`, default `true`).
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/multi_tokenizer_mixin.py`: `_send_output_to_tokenizer_workers` only calls `_split_batch_by_key` when the flag is on. When it is off it takes the existing per-request path, the same one already used when a batch cannot be grouped.
- `test/registered/unit/managers/test_multi_tokenizer_mixin.py`: the return-path test now runs under both settings (via `envs...override`) and asserts that grouped and per-request delivery send the same rids and strings to the same workers in the same order, and that the input batch is not mutated either way.

Nothing else changes. The GPU batch, the scheduler, and the output content are identical in both modes; only the number and shape of detokenizer -> tokenizer-worker messages differ. The default keeps today's behaviour.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. This only changes how many IPC messages carry the same outputs between processes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`python -m pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_multi_tokenizer_mixin.py`: 23 passed, 4 subtests passed. The new subtests cover both values of the flag on a batch whose owners are non-contiguous (`[worker-b, worker-a, worker-b]`), so the per-request path is checked for order as well as destination.

With the flag off, a step with N requests across W workers goes back to N sends, as before #44288; with it on (default) the W-send grouping from #44288 is unchanged.

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] modelopt-nvfp4: Keep MoE global scales in gate/up order
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE global scales identify the logical gate and up projections, while some kernels require weights in physical `[up, gate]` order. This PR replaces the merged #44858 implementation with a loader fix that keeps global scales in canonical `[gate, up]` order across backends.

The contents of #44858 (`78185f4b3f565cbe0fec20d71bb5deb372428e80`) are reverted, including its helper extraction and added weekly test. The loader implementation retains the SwiGLU beta correction (`1 / g1_alphas_up`), the shared-clamp warning, and CPU tests of the actual loading and post-load paths.

## Changes

- Reorder ModelOpt NVFP4 weights and block scales in `_load_w13`, leaving per-tensor global scales in logical order.
- Use `use_flashinfer_trtllm_weight_layout` so nominal TRT-LLM with MegaMoE retains canonical weight order.
- Remove the backend-dependent `up_first` argument from GEMM1 alpha computation.
- Cover backend layouts, TP slicing, repeated loading, non-gated experts, and SwiGLU/SiTU post-load parameters in the existing CPU suite.

## Validation

- [x] Full-package [targeted CPU CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39393382909) at `bef4f088d1`: NVFP4 scale tests **20 passed**; MegaMoE capacity tests **40 passed, 1 existing xfail**.

title: [Perf] hybrid-swa: Detect hybrid SWA models from layer_types
author: siliangchen-amd
body:
## Motivation

Gemma 2, Gemma 3, EXAONE 4 and Olmo 3 mix sliding-window and full-attention layers, but sglang serves them from a single KV pool: their model overrides turn hybrid SWA memory off unconditionally, so every sliding-window layer keeps KV for the whole context. Hybrid SWA detection is an architecture allowlist with a layer rule per architecture, so each such model needs its own change (#41143, #41013, #41012). This PR replaces them with one rule: a config that sets `sliding_window` and whose `layer_types` mixes `sliding_attention` and `full_attention` layers is hybrid SWA, split by `layer_types`.

## Modifications

- `is_hybrid_swa_model()` falls back to that rule after the allowlist and the `is_hybrid_swa` opt-in, and `get_hybrid_layer_ids()` splits by `layer_types` after the existing branches, so listed architectures keep their rules. `ModelConfig.is_layer_types_hybrid_swa` marks models that came in through the new rule.
- For those models, `ModelRunner` checks the split against the `RadixAttention` layers it built: a layer in the SWA pool must have a window and a layer in the full pool must not. A mismatch, from model code that does not read `layer_types`, fails at startup and points to `--disable-hybrid-swa-memory` instead of silently dropping context. It fails rather than falling back so that every pipeline stage keeps the same pool layout.
- Gemma 2/3, EXAONE 4 and Olmo 3 no longer opt out. The opt-outs that stay: Gemma 3n and ExaoneMoE (not supported), and Gemma 3 on fa3 (#9123) until NVIDIA/FA3 validation covers SWA page allocation, freeing and reuse under long-context memory pressure; removing it is left for a separate PR.
- On the aiter backend, models detected through `layer_types` keep the single pool. With the SWA pool aiter switches to unified attention, which loses a passkey 32K tokens back on Gemma 3 (below). Listed models are not affected.
- Speculative drafts stay on the listed rules. Their workers size draft KV pools themselves: FROZEN_KV_MTP gives `Gemma4AssistantForCausalLM` (3 sliding layers, 1 full) a single-pool dummy config, which the `layer_types` rule would leave without SWA pool sizes.

Models whose behavior changes: Gemma 2, Gemma 3 (text and VL), EXAONE 4 (EXAONE-4.0-1.2B has no window), Olmo 3, and the other models whose code already takes its windows from `layer_types`: Cohere2 (Command R7B, Command A), Cohere2-MoE, AFMoE and Granite SWA.

## Accuracy Tests

1x MI325X (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.2, main at `a90e9c5d` against this PR, TP 1, `--attention-backend triton --mem-fraction-static 0.85`. GSM8K is `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k` (8-shot, 512 new tokens, 1319 questions).

| model | window | KV tokens, main → PR | GSM8K, main / PR | passkey, main / PR | greedy probes equal to main |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gemma 3 12B it | 1024 | 529,157 → 634,988 | 0.906 / 0.908 | 15/15 / 15/15 | 12/12 |
| Gemma 2 9B it | 4096 | 623,152 → 692,391 | 0.851 / 0.845 | 5/5 / 5/5 | 12/12 |
| Olmo 3 7B Instruct | 4096 | 416,256 → 489,712 | 0.352 / 0.356 | 5/15 / 5/15 | 12/12 |
| EXAONE 4.0 32B | 4096 | 643,632 → 757,214 | 0.906 / 0.908 | 15/15 / 15/15 | 12/12 |

- Probes: 48 greedy tokens on prompts of window - 1, window, window + 1 and 2 x window tokens, and on a 2 x window prefix extended by 512 tokens, each sent cold and again with a radix-cache hit. All 12 outputs per model are token-identical to main.
- Passkey: a 5-digit key in the first sentence, plain filler, the question at the end; 5 keys at 2 x window, 4 x window and the context limit (Gemma 2: 8128 tokens only). Olmo 3 7B misses the same keys in both arms.
- `--enable-hierarchical-cache` with the hybrid pool (Gemma 3): GSM8K 0.904, passkey 15/15, probes 12/12, so it needs no opt-out.
- Command R7B (Cohere2): main fails at the first forward on the triton backend (`layer 0 is a sliding-window layer but this forward built no window_kv_indices`). With the hybrid pool it runs: GSM8K 0.798, passkey 5/5 at 8128 tokens.
- aiter: Gemma 3 with the hybrid pool forced on gets GSM8K 0.901 but passkey 10/15, missing all five keys at 32,704 tokens that triton retrieves. On main, Gemma 2/3 do not start on aiter at all (`aiter paged decode cannot honor sliding-window attention`), and this PR keeps that.
- Speculative drafts: `test_frozen_kv_mtp.py` (Gemma 4 E4B with its assistant draft), main merged, MI300X with the AMD CI environment: GSM8K 0.715 / 0.705 at topk 1 / 3 (threshold 0.65). Without the draft rule the server fails at startup.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`sglang.benchmark.serving --dataset-name random-ids`, output tok/s and running requests at the peak, same setup:

| model | 12288 in, 2048 out, 128 prompts at concurrency 128 | 16384 in, 512 out, 256 at 256 |
|---|---|---|
| Gemma 3 12B it | 670 → 766 (+14%), 36 → 43 running | 317 → 321, 30 → 36 running |
| EXAONE 4.0 32B | 521 → 519, 44 → 52 running | 157 → 158, 37 → 44 running |
| Gemma 2 9B it | | 590 → 606 (7168 in, 512 at 512), 77 → 86 running |
| Olmo 3 7B Instruct | | 270 → 286, 23 → 27 running |

The default `--swa-full-tokens-ratio` (0.8) gives the full-attention layers 11-20% more tokens, and concurrency grows by the same factor. A smaller ratio gives more: at 0.2, Gemma 3 runs 108 requests at 870 tok/s (+30%) in the decode-heavy run. The window pool must still hold window x running requests: EXAONE 4 at 0.2 (322K window tokens for 69 x 4096) retracts requests and loses 17%. EXAONE 4 32B on one GPU is compute-bound at 44-52 running requests, so its extra capacity does not raise throughput there.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Unit tests: the `layer_types` rule and its non-cases in `test_model_config.py`, the split check in `test_layer_setup.py` (real `RadixAttention` layers, both mismatch directions, one pipeline stage), and the overrides (including the Gemma 3 fa3 opt-out) and the aiter pass in `test_model_overrides.py`.

Supersedes #41143, #41013 and #41012.

Hyperloom found this gap while optimizing `allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct`; Gemma 2, Gemma 3 and EXAONE 4 have the same gap.

title: [Fix] [AMD] diffusion: Enable `--quantization fp8` on gfx1250 (torch.compile lowering + per-channel weight scales)
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

`--quantization fp8` does not work on gfx1250. With `--enable-torch-compile` it dies in Inductor lowering on the first warmup request, before a single image:

```
LoweringException: AssertionError: target: aten._scaled_mm.default
  args[3]: ... FixedLayout('cuda:0', torch.float32, size=[], stride=[])
```

`args[3]` is the weight scale, and it is a **rank-0 scalar**. Inductor's `_scaled_mm` template loads it with two index symbols against a zero-length stride, so the `len(index) == len(stride)` assert at `ir.py:2034` fires.

The scalar comes from the missing-CUTLASS fallback: `cutlass_fp8_supported()` is `False` for every ROCm device (`fp8_utils.py:398` is `if not _is_cuda: return False`, before it looks at compute capability), so `process_weights_after_loading` falls to `input_to_float8`, whose single `aminmax()` yields a 0-dim `weight_scale` instead of a per-channel `[N]` vector. **The crash and the quality loss are therefore one bug**: a per-tensor scale that Inductor cannot lower *and* that throws away the range a BF16 checkpoint needs to survive FP8. NVIDIA takes the per-channel CUTLASS branch and sees neither symptom, which is why this is gfx1250/ROCm-only.

Avoiding the lowering is not enough on its own: hipBLASLt ships no tuned gfx1250 kernels, so at the FLUX.2-dev 720p shapes `torch._scaled_mm` FP8 reaches 471-506 TFLOPS while the BF16 torch.compile templates it replaces already reach 645-710.

**The scheme here is A8W8** -- a fully FP8 GEMM. Both operands are `e4m3`: per-token dynamic scales on the activations, per-channel scales on the weights, FP32 accumulate. It is explicitly *not* weight-only (A16W8); the activations are quantized too, so the matrix cores actually issue FP8 MFMA, which is where the speedup comes from.

**The fix** is two changes for two different reasons, either of which alone stops the crash:

* `process_weights_after_loading` takes the per-channel branch (`per_token_group_quant_fp8`), giving a real `[N]` scale. This is the *accuracy* fix; the ranks line up as a side effect.
* `apply` quantizes the activations per token and routes both operands to an A8W8 Triton tile, so `aten._scaled_mm` is never reached. This is the *performance* fix: 1150-1255 TFLOPS instead of 471-506.

This affects any gfx1250 run passing `--quantization fp8` with a BF16 checkpoint. Nothing in the fix is model-specific -- it is the shared `Fp8LinearMethod` in the diffusion stack -- though the reproduction here is FLUX.2-dev at 720p, where linears are 83% of GPU kernel time. MI300X, MI355X and NVIDIA are unaffected: `is_gfx1250_supported()` is false there, and `cutlass_fp8_supported` already routes NVIDIA to a per-channel CUTLASS GEMM.

## Modifications

* New `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/fp8_gfx1250.py`: an A8W8 (per-token activation / per-channel weight) FP8 `[M, K] @ [K, N]` Triton tile plus the per-token activation quantizer that feeds it. The tile indexes its operands modulo M and N rather than masking the loads (masked loads cost ~10% on this target and the tail is at most one tile), and masks only the store. `_select_config` carries the tile sizes an offline sweep picked for the served shapes.
* `multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/quantization/fp8.py`: `Fp8LinearMethod.__init__` computes `use_gfx1250_triton_fp8` once; when set, `process_weights_after_loading` takes the **per-channel** branch for a non-FP8-serialized checkpoint -- replacing the rank-0 `input_to_float8` scale that both breaks the lowering and drops the checkpoint's range -- and `apply` tries `_apply_gfx1250_triton_fp8` first, returning `None` to the existing path for any shape the tile does not cover.
* `srt/environ.py`: `SGLANG_DISABLE_GFX1250_FP8_GEMM`, a diagnostic kill switch.
* The quantized weight is stored **row-major** `[K, N]` rather than as the transposed view of `[N, K]` that this method has always produced. A BLOCK_N slice of one k-row otherwise reads N single bytes strided by K instead of BLOCK_N contiguous ones; making it contiguous once at load is worth 1.05-1.33x per GEMM and 1.06x end to end. The tile's config table is tuned for that layout, and a unit test pins it, since a refactor that drops the transpose would be a silent regression.
* `test/registered/amd/test_fp8_gemm_gfx1250.py`: tile correctness against a dequantized reference, and the dispatch seam itself.

**BLOCK_SIZE_K is capped at 64 on purpose.** On gfx1250 with triton 3.8.0, an FP8 `tl.dot` miscompiles for `BLOCK_SIZE_K >= 128`: it silently returns NaN for every `num_warps` x `num_stages` combination tested (16 of 16), and the broken kernel *times about 40% faster than a correct one*. An autotune sweep without a correctness gate will therefore select it and report a phantom ~1730 TFLOPS. This also means 1150-1255 TFLOPS is the ceiling for correct Triton FP8 on this target today, not the hardware's ceiling. Note that `triton_scaled_mm`'s own heuristic picks `(128, 128, 128)` for M 128, so callers must not route gfx1250 FP8 there until the compiler is fixed.

## Accuracy Tests

No accuracy harness applies -- this is a diffusion image model, so there is no gsm8k-style score. The gate is instead split into the two questions that can actually be answered separately: is the kernel numerically correct, and did the image get worse.

Measured on one gfx1250 (DPX half-package), FLUX.2-dev 720p, 50 steps, seed 42, `--enable-torch-compile true`, aiter attention, all offload off. The "before" arm is BF16 at this PR's merge base. There is no "FP8 without this PR" arm, because that configuration does not run at all -- it is the lowering crash described in Motivation.

### 1. Trajectory divergence -- is the kernel correct

Comparing the per-step denoise latents of the two arms (`[1, 50, 3600, 128]`) separates the error the GEMM introduces from the amplification the sampler applies to it afterwards. One seed is sufficient here: this measures numerics, not a sample distribution.

| step | relative L2 | cosine | mean bias | growth vs prev |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.00149 | 0.999956 | +5.75e-05 | -- |
| 2 | 0.00224 | 0.999954 | +1.71e-04 | x1.51 |
| 3 | 0.00288 | 0.999952 | +2.47e-04 | x1.28 |
| 5 | 0.00407 | 0.999949 | +2.01e-04 | x1.18 |
| 10 | 0.00778 | 0.999926 | -7.04e-05 | x1.14 |
| 20 | 0.03700 | 0.999273 | +1.41e-03 | x1.13 |
| 30 | 0.11282 | 0.993576 | -6.01e-04 | x1.10 |
| 50 | 0.31035 | 0.951731 | +3.72e-04 | x1.00 |

**Mean bias stays within +-1e-3 at every step and changes sign.**

### 2. Image quality -- did it get worse

| Prompt | CLIP BF16 | CLIP FP8 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cat and dog baking in a kitchen (many small props) | 36.31 | 35.96 | -0.35 |
| Watchmaker's hands close-up (skin and metal micro-detail) | 24.66 | 24.91 | +0.25 |
| **mean** | **30.49** | **30.44** | **-0.05** |

All deltas are within +-0.5 CLIP points and go both ways (mean -0.05), i.e. no quality change. n=2 at a single seed.

### 3. Pixel similarity to BF16 -- reported, not the gate

| Prompt | PSNR (not a gate) | SSIM (fine: > 0.8) | LPIPS (fine: < 0.1) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cat and dog baking | 18.30 | 0.8413 | 0.0959 |
| Watchmaker's hands | 18.79 | 0.8530 | 0.0843 |
| **mean** | **18.55** | **0.8472** | **0.0901** |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

### End to end, on the tracked MI450 dashboard configuration

Both rows are from the same dashboard harness, same image (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi45x-20261020`), same day, same arm (**MI450-MC Hammer: DPX TP1 (A0), `--enable-torch-compile true`**). The baseline row is the arm as it ships today -- BF16, because `--quantization fp8` cannot be passed on this target without the crash above. The second row is this PR *plus* the flag it enables:

| Arm | Text encode (s) | **Denoise (s)** | VAE decode (s) | **Total (s)** |
|-----|-----------------|-----------------|----------------|---------------|
| DPX TP1 (A0) + torch-compile (BF16, today) | 0.0034 | 48.7215 | 3.0623 | 51.787 |
| + PR 45304 + `--quantization fp8` | 0.0031 | 36.0457 | 2.9947 | **39.044** |
| **Delta** | -- | **-26.0% (1.35x)** | -2.2% | **-24.6% (1.33x)** |

The entire win is in denoise, which is what the change touches; text encode and VAE decode are unchanged, and they are what keeps the e2e ratio (1.33x) below the denoise ratio (1.35x).

> Note for anyone reproducing: the `+ PR45304` row **must** carry `--quantization fp8`. Every line of this PR sits behind `Fp8LinearMethod.use_gfx1250_triton_fp8`, and that class is only constructed when the flag is passed -- so a "+PR45304" arm without it measures plain BF16 and shows no change. Also discard the first run after a cold start; cold Inductor/aiter JIT costs roughly 8 s of denoise.

### Isolated A/B on one gfx1250

FLUX.2-dev, 720p, 100 denoise steps, seed 42, one gfx1250, `--enable-torch-compile true --attention-backend aiter`, all offload off. Runs serialized on an otherwise idle box, two repetitions each, no profiler attached.

| Metric | BF16 s/step | FP8 s/step | BF16 e2e | FP8 e2e |
|--------|-------------|-----------|----------|---------|
| rep 1 | 0.7553 | 0.5553 | 87.77 s | 64.13 s |
| rep 2 | 0.7569 | 0.5592 | 87.93 s | 64.45 s |
| mean | **0.7561** | **0.5573** | **87.85 s** | **64.29 s** |

**-26.3% per denoise step (1.357x), -26.8% end to end (1.367x).** Spread across repetitions is under 0.5%.

The row-major weight layout is a further **-5.3%** on top of that, measured the same way (3 reps each, same GPU, serialized, warm compile cache):

| s/step | rep 1 | rep 2 | rep 3 | mean |
|--------|-------|-------|-------|------|
| column-major weights | 0.5522 | 0.5523 | 0.5565 | **0.5537** |
| row-major weights | 0.5234 | 0.5288 | 0.5211 | **0.5244** |

A matched pair of profiles (same step count, same GPU) attributes -174 ms of GPU time over three steps to the GEMMs, against a total of -108 ms; GPU-busy time falls 1791.5 -> 1683.6 ms, which tracks the wall-clock change. Cumulative against BF16: **0.7561 -> 0.5244 s/step, 1.44x.**

These per-step figures are the host loop average (`[DenoisingStage] average time per step`), while the dashboard's Denoise column is `[DenoisingStage] finished in`, which includes the GPU tail drain and runs ~20% higher on the same run. Compare within a table, not across the two.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Feat] openai: Render DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 chat prompts with deepseek-recipe
author: zhendonghua
body:
DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1 chat prompts are rendered and tokenized by [deepseek-recipe](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-recipe) 0.2.0, DeepSeek's official encoder library, through the `dsv4` / `dsv41` chat encoding adapter. SGLang's copies of the checkpoint encoders (`encoding_dsv4.py`, `encoding_dsv41.py`) are removed.

## Changes

- `parser/deepseek_recipe_renderer.py`: translates the request for recipe (`developer` -> `system`, object tool-call arguments -> JSON, `continue_final_message` -> `prefix`, `required` and named `tool_choice` -> `auto` because SGLang's grammar enforces the choice, `structural_tag` left to the grammar), then renders and tokenizes with the served checkpoint's fast tokenizer. It adds the two SGLang extensions recipe does not model: quick instruction `task`s and V4.1 numeric effort budgets.
- `serving_deepseek_recipe.py`: the adapter. Only the prompt goes through recipe; thinking, `reasoning_effort`, sampling (`n`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `max_tokens`) and the trailing-assistant rule of `_handle_last_assistant_message` follow SGLang's request handling. An unset effort falls back to `SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT` / `SGLANG_DSV41_REASONING_EFFORT`, then to recipe's default. A bad default effort fails at startup.
- Adapter protocol: `encode_messages` takes the handler's `thinking` decision, and adapters declare `strict_tool_call_arguments`.
- Output parsing is unchanged: the DeepSeek reasoning and tool-call parsers still parse model output.
- `encode_simple_chat` (offline tools) renders DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 through recipe as well.
- `deepseek-recipe==0.2.0` is a dependency in every `pyproject*.toml` (wheels for Linux x86_64 / aarch64 and macOS).

## Behavior changes

DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 prompts follow deepseek-recipe wherever the removed encoders differed:

- Reasoning effort
  - V4 follows DeepSeek's official effort profile. The preview profile and its `dsv4_reasoning_effort_profile` override are gone, so `high` and `max` render the official prompts on every checkpoint.
  - V4 `medium`, `xhigh` and `ultra` map to recipe's tiers instead of being ignored.
  - With thinking on, an unset or `none` effort renders recipe's default effort prompt on V4, where nothing was rendered before.
  - A numeric `reasoning_effort` (integer or float) on V4 returns 400 instead of being ignored.
  - V4.1 `minimal` maps to `low` (budget 50) instead of falling back to the default budget 75.
- Tools
  - V4 tool schemas render in OpenAI field order, without the `strict` default.
  - A tool without a description renders `"description": ""` (V4 rendered `null`, V4.1 omitted the field).
  - A named `tool_choice` renders only the chosen tool, as SGLang does for other models.
  - History tool calls with non-object `arguments` are accepted instead of returning 400.
  - A `tool` message that answers no preceding tool call returns 400.
- Messages
  - `developer` messages render as system messages instead of user turns.
  - A mid-conversation system message on V4 moves to the start of the prompt instead of rendering in place.
  - A trailing `latest_reminder` renders before the generation header.
  - V4 joins multiple text parts with a blank line instead of a space, and renders an image part as `[Unsupported Image]` instead of dropping it.
  - Special-token strings in message text are encoded as plain text. V4 used to turn them into special tokens; V4.1 rejected the image token.
  - `continue_final_message` in thinking mode continues the answer after `<think></think>` instead of inside the reasoning block.
- Response format: `json_object` and `json_schema` requests get the official response-format instruction in the prompt.

Other models:

- `reasoning_effort` accepts `ultra` for every model. Models whose encoders do not map it keep their own handling: gpt-oss falls back to its default effort, and Inkling and Hunyuan reject it.
- Assistant messages accept `prefix`, which used to be dropped. Chat templates that read it (such as the DeepSeek-V3.1 / V3.2 tool templates under `examples/chat_template/`) now see it.

The Rust processor (`rust/sglang-processor`) still renders DeepSeek with its own encoder, and its parity fixtures are unchanged.

## Tests

- `test/registered/unit/parser/test_deepseek_recipe_renderer.py`: request translation, numeric effort budgets, every task with thinking on and off (token ids), and the effort-line rewrite.
- `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_deepseek_recipe.py`: adapter construction and startup checks; through the chat handler, the thinking default, request effort over the server default, `temperature` and `max_tokens` left to SGLang, numeric effort and `task` reaching the prompt, and the trailing-assistant rules.
- `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_deepseekv41_detector.py` renders its fixtures with deepseek-recipe.

title: [Perf] pd: Publish decode KV destinations without host syncs under overlap
author: nvjullin
body: ## Motivation TL;DR decode needs to send memory addresses reserved for a request (this is called publishing) to prefill in order for prefill to initiate kv-transfer. Publishing happens on the host, but memory allocation happens on device. Consequently decode needs a D2H, waiting on the device memory allocation, to get the memory addresses (in the form of page indices). To avoid syncing on the D2H and stalling the scheduler, we defer publishing by 1 decode iteration. `k` refers to which iteration it happens in. Allocation `k` is used in the far future, it is not used in forward `k` or `k+1`. Under the overlap scheduler, PD (prefill/decode disaggregation) decode still makes the host wait on the in-flight forward about once per new request. Each wait idles the GPU, and with attention DP (data parallelism) it idles every DP rank. After launching a forward, the scheduler fences `schedule_stream` behind it (`_apply_war_barrier`, a write-after-read barrier). A host-blocking call on `schedule_stream` while the next batch is being scheduled therefore waits for that forward. The next forward can't launch until the host returns, so the GPU idles in between. With attention DP, the per-batch DP sync spreads one rank's stall to every rank. Two such calls remain on main's PD decode path: 1. **Destination publish.** `DecodePreallocQueue.pop_preallocated` allocates a request's KV pages on `schedule_stream`. It then immediately reads the page indices back to the host, through `kv_to_page_indices(...).cpu()` and the state-index payloads, to send them to prefill. The readback waits for the allocation, which is queued behind the forward. 2. **EAGLE draft input.** `build_eagle_disagg_draft_input` calls `torch.any(...).item()` on the remapped device tensor to check whether any DSA (DeepSeek Sparse Attention) seed row is empty. It runs after `schedule_stream` has waited on the forward stream, so it waits for the whole forward. #38955 and #44598 made the nearby H2D (host-to-device) copies non-blocking. Within an iteration, the first blocking call pays the whole stall. The decode step stops stalling only once these two calls are gone too. ## Modifications **1. Deferred destination publish** (`disaggregation/decode.py`). This is on when overlap and the WAR barrier are on (CUDA, or `SGLANG_ENABLE_WAR_BARRIER`), `pp_size == 1`, HiSparse is off and the staging buffer is off. Otherwise the publish runs inline as before. - `pop_preallocated` no longer reads anything back. It does five things: - reserves the request's metadata buffer slot, since free slots cap admission in the same pass; - sets `DecodeRequest.awaiting_publish`; - counts the request as a published destination until the transfer queue takes it. That keeps the unified-memory move gate closed, as the inline publish did, so a later allocation in the same pass can't compact the request's pages before the publish reads them back; - records a CUDA event after the allocation; - moves the request to the transfer queue at once. In the transfer queue the request polls `WaitingForInput` until its KV arrives, as before. - `publish_pending_destinations()` runs at the start of the next `process_decode_queue`. For each pending request, a side stream waits only on that request's event. It then reads the indices back and sends them to prefill through `_publish_destination`, which is the previous inline body, moved; its two defensive `getattr` calls are now `isinstance` checks. The side stream comes from PyTorch's priority -1 pool. The schedule, forward and result-copy streams all wait on the forward and come from the default pool, so the side stream can't alias them. Afterwards `schedule_stream` waits on the side stream, so later forwards see the publish's GPU writes (DSV4 request-state clears). - Ordering: - The event is recorded after the allocation, which was fenced behind the previous forward's reads. So the side stream reads a finished allocation and writes only after that forward. - The forward in flight at publish time can't read the request's rows, because the request joins no batch until its KV arrives. - Prefill learns the destination only after the side stream's host readback returns, as before. - Cost: prefill learns the destination one decode iteration later. - Why it's off with PP, with staging, or without the WAR barrier: - With PP, `pop_preallocated` is called from the PP mixin rather than from `process_decode_queue`, so nothing would publish. - With the staging buffer, a room is registered with the staging handler only at publish, but staging polls every queued request. - Without the WAR barrier (the ROCm default), `schedule_stream` isn't fenced behind the in-flight forward, so the inline readback doesn't stall and deferral would only add latency. The barrier's predicate moved to `managers.utils.is_war_barrier_enabled()`, which the scheduler uses too. **2. Failures inside the deferral window.** - The publish all-reduces one poll per pending request over the attn-TP (attention tensor-parallel) group and skips failed requests. A request the transfer queue has already released has no receiver. `_ReleasedReceiver` stands in for it and polls as `Failed`, so every rank still passes the same list to the collective. These polls skip test failure injection (`inject_failure=False`): an injected failure leaves the receiver live, so the transfer queue would never release the skipped request. - `pop_transferred` releases a failed request that is still `awaiting_publish` at once, instead of through deferred KV release. No prefill rank received its destination, so none can write into its pages. Deferred release would wait for drain acknowledgements that are never armed for such a request. It would hold the KV for the full `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DEFERRED_DECODE_KV_RELEASE_TIMEOUT` (30 s). The immediate release also clears any abort-ACK tracking that the abort, or the receiver's `clear()`, armed under the `prefill_complete` allocation policy. No drain would ever resolve it. `awaiting_publish` is the same on every attn-TP rank, so the ranks still agree on whether to hold its KV. - `release_memory_occupation` also clears the pending publishes. **3. DSA seed check on the host** (`speculative/eagle_disaggregation.py`). Whether any row ends up without a seed is now decided on the host copy of the seed. It uses the same per-row conditions the device remap applies: - all entries are < 0; - or, when remapping, any entry is < −1, ≥ `seq_len`, or ≥ the `req_to_token` width. The remap's one device-only condition is a valid position that maps to an unallocated slot (≤ 0). It cannot hold here. Before a request reaches the prebuilt path, every slot of its `req_to_token` row below `seq_len` has been written: by prealloc, and for a cached prefix by the decode prefix cache and the HiCache restore. **Tests** (`test/registered/unit/disaggregation/`): - `test_deferred_destination_keeps_its_metadata_slot_until_published`: - nothing is sent at prealloc; - the publish waits on the request's event and sends with the slot reserved at prealloc; - the published-destination counter nets to zero. - `test_deferred_destination_closes_the_move_gate_until_queued`: a deferred request keeps the unified-memory move gate closed until the transfer queue takes it. - `test_released_receiver_keeps_the_publish_reduction_aligned`: a released pending request still contributes one poll and is not published. - `test_publish_ignores_injected_poll_failures`: an injected poll failure doesn't skip a live receiver's publish. - `test_failure_before_deferred_publish_releases_immediately`: a failure before publish is released in the same pop, not deferred, and the abort-ACK tracking its receiver's `clear()` armed is cleared. - `test_pd_decode_fused_topk_drops_seed_past_request_length`: the host check drops the seed when a row has a position past the request length. ## Accuracy Tests Validation ran on this PR's base (d0a7565) in `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261021-c1c287a4`, on one 4-GPU GB300 node, with and without this change. **Unit tests**, one pytest process per file: | | files | without | with | |---|---|---|---| | CPU: `test/registered/unit/{disaggregation,spec,speculative}` plus decode-related `managers`, `mem_cache`, `model_executor`, `observability`, `server_args` files | 105 | 1293 passed, 18 failed | 1298 passed, 19 failed | | GB300: the CUDA-registered subset | 51 | 444 passed, 12 failed | 458 passed, 2 failed | - The one failure only with this change, on both platforms, was `test_two_rank_release_consensus`: its request stub lacked the new `awaiting_publish` field. The stub is fixed in this PR, and the three changed test files then pass (96 tests). The full suites were not rerun after that fix. - 11 of the 12 GB300 failures without this change are `test_hisparse_unit` tests that failed to bind a port because both arms ran at once. They pass with this change. The remaining failure is in both arms. **Abort storm, PD end to end** on one 4-GPU GB300 node. The setup is that of `test_disaggregation_aarch64.py`: Qwen3-8B, prefill TP2 → decode TP2, Mooncake transfer, overlap on. The test targets the window this change adds between prealloc and publish. - Three rounds of 600 `/generate` requests go through the PD load balancer, 96 at a time. Prompts are about 160 to 3,200 tokens, with 64 output tokens. - Every other request is aborted on both servers after a random 0 to 0.6 s delay, so aborts land throughout a request's lifetime. - Pass criteria: every request that isn't aborted returns 200, and both servers pass `/health` afterwards. It passed with this change, and without it on a base 107 commits older (6cac4dc). - With debug logging on both decode ranks, 4 requests failed while awaiting publish. Each was skipped at publish on both ranks and its KV released at once, with no deferred-release timeout, KV leak or traceback. - GSM8K, 200 examples, on the same servers afterwards, scored with the test's built-in `sglang.test.run_eval`: | | score | |---|---| | this change | 0.950 | | without (6cac4dc) | 0.950 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling The measurements below predate #38955 and #44598, so this change also made those H2D copies non-blocking. They therefore measure all the blocking sites together. If only the H2D copies are fixed, the stall moves to the two calls this PR removes. The measurements also predate this revision's review fixes (WAR-barrier gate, priority -1 side stream, move-gate count, failure-path fixes), none of which adds work to an iteration that publishes. **Decode-only A/B (n = 1 per arm).** Setup: - GLM-5.2 NVFP4 decode, DEP4 (attention DP + expert parallelism over 4 GPUs), with MTP (multi-token prediction) on one node. - `--disaggregation-transfer-backend fake`, so prealloc, transfer and prebuilt run without a prefill server. - 36 closed-loop clients, 60k to 180k-token prompts, 500 to 1,500 output tokens. - 420 s window after a 120 s warm-up. | | without | with | |---|---|---| | iterations with `process_decode_queue` or batch selection > 10 ms | 8.9% | 0.1% | | decode step mean / p50 / p99 (ms) | 30.06 / 28.60 / 62.3 | 29.17 / 28.57 / 37.3 | | blocking syncs per request in those two stages | 11 | 0 | | output throughput (tok/s) | 2,946 | 3,005 (+2.0%) | Both arms ran with CUDA sync tracing, which adds host cost to every sync. The matching p50 indicates matched load. **Full-scale PD.** Setup: GLM-5.2 NVFP4, 4 prefill workers (PP4 each) → 1 decode worker (DEP8) with MTP, Mooncake transfer, 24 GB300 GPUs, an agentic multi-turn trace at concurrency 227. Nsight Systems captured 80 decode iterations on all 8 decode ranks: | | without | with (3 captures) | |---|---|---| | iterations where a rank blocks > 10 ms in `process_decode_queue` or batch selection | 18 of 79 | 0 of 78 in each | | GPU idle per decode step | 1.60 ms | 0.47 ms | - Without this change, each stall was one 21 to 26 ms `cudaStreamSynchronize` on one or more ranks while the others waited at the DP sync, costing about 6 ms of GPU idle per stalled step. - The captures with this change also switched the MoE all-to-all backend. That changes transfer time but not host stalls. **Stability.** This change, ported to an older base and combined with unrelated prefix-cache and decode-allocation changes, ran six 1-hour runs of the full-scale deployment. Together they served about 124k measured requests plus warm-ups, with 0 errors, and every run completed. End-to-end throughput was not measured for this change alone. **Known limitations:** - **Early ABORT.** Once the handshake is done, decode sends ABORT to every prefill rank, whether or not the destination was published. A prefill rank that hasn't registered the room yet drops the ABORT and waits out `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT` (300 s). It holds no KV, but the client waits. - This already happens for aborts during the handshake; deferral widens the window by one iteration. - In the abort storm: 1 such timeout with this change (from a request that failed while awaiting publish), 1 without (6cac4dc). - The fix belongs on prefill: keep an early ABORT until the room registers. - **GPU metadata buffers.** `SGLANG_MOONCAKE_CUSTOM_MEM_POOL=INTRA_NODE_NVLINK` puts the metadata buffers on the GPU. There the seed's `.cpu()` is a real device read, as are the existing per-request `.item()` reads in `_commit_transfer_to_req`. The default, with host buffers, is covered. - **Stream ordering.** The unit tests mock CUDA streams, so the GPU ordering is validated only by the end-to-end runs. - **ROCm side stream.** PyTorch gives ROCm two stream priorities, so the priority -1 pool is shared with high-priority NCCL streams (`TORCH_NCCL_HIGH_PRIORITY`). With that and `SGLANG_ENABLE_WAR_BARRIER` both set, a pool slot repeats after 32 draws. An aliased publish readback would then wait for that NCCL work. This affects latency only, not correctness. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. title: [Perf] [AMD] dsv41: Skip unneeded layer 20 computation under decoder-bounded-replay
author: 1am9trash
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

With `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay`, DeepSeek-V4.1's decoder layers only process the last 128 prompt tokens of each request during prefill. Layer 20 (the first decoder layer) still has to write the KV cache for every token, but it does not need to run the indexer, attention, and MoE on all of them. Currently, The amd code path still runs all of layer 20 on every token.

Nv enabled the skip in #42901. Amd was left out because its fused layer path runs the whole layer 20 in one call, so the KV write could not be split from the rest of the layer.

This PR enables it on amd. Layer 20 writes the KV cache for every token first, then runs the rest of the layer on the last 128 tokens only.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

No change on nv. All changes are in `deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py` or under `_is_hip`.

- **`deepseek_v4.py`**
  - Set `tail_writes_source_kv` to `True` on amd, so the tail starts at layer 20 instead of layer 21.
  - Get layer 20's input for the KV write from `fused_boundary_attn_input`.
- **`deepseek_v4_platform_stage.py`**
  - The fused boundary delays each layer's mHC post to the start of the next layer, so it has not run yet when layer 20 starts.
  - Add `fused_boundary_attn_input`, which runs that pending mHC post and builds layer 20's attention input for every token.
- **`deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py`**
  - Reuse `DeepseekV4AttnBackend.write_tail_source_kv` to write layer 20's KV cache for every token.
  - Layer 20 now runs its indexer on the last 128 tokens only, and writes data straight into the tail buffers.
  - Remove the code that copied these results out of the full-token buffers, since it is no longer needed.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

Server cmd:
```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_OPT_HIP_OPUS_SPARSE_PREFILL=true SGLANG_OPT_HIP_FLYDSL_MXFP8=1 \
SGLANG_HIP_FP4_INDEXER_ROWGROUP=1 SGLANG_HIP_DSV41_INDEX_K_PAGE8=1 \
SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1 SGLANG_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE_LAYOUT=per_rank \
ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT8 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 2 --enforce-shared-experts-fusion --fp8-gemm-backend aiter --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \
  --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --prefill-decode-interval 32 \
  --swa-prefix-tails 2048 --max-running-requests 64
# DSpark rows add: --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5
# The radix-cache-off row adds: --disable-radix-cache
python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 1319 --parallel 32
```

| GSM8K, 1319 questions | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No speculative decoding | 0.905 / 0.900 | 0.906 / 0.900 |
| DSpark, block size 5 | 0.902 / 0.898 | 0.917 / 0.901 |
| No speculative decoding, radix cache off | 0.903 / 0.906 | 0.904 / 0.898 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

Follow SA MI355 tp2 setting:
- DSpark block size: 5
- Simulated accept length: 3.51.

Time spent in layer 20 for one 16K-token prefill chunk:
| Prefill chunk | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First chunk of the prompt | 13.4 ms | 3.0 ms |
| Last full chunk of a 200K-token prompt | 34.4 ms | 3.0 ms |

title: [Fix] glm-5.2: Record side-stream work right before its join to keep CUDA-graph replay on one stream
author: wenscarl
body: ## Motivation On GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), a CUDA-graph decode replay spreads across many CUDA streams, so a profiler trace is hard to read: each layer's indexer chain lands on a different stream row. This is the same issue as DeepSeek-V4.1 in #39420. That PR found that at graph replay a join node continues on the stream of its first-recorded parent. A side-stream block captured before the concurrent main-stream kernels therefore pulls the main chain onto a side lane at the join. Its fix keeps the fork where it is and captures the side-stream work right before the join. Inspired by and following the approach of #39420 ("[DSV4.1] Record side-stream work right before its join"). ## Modifications Two side-stream blocks on the GLM-5.2 decode path were captured before the main-stream kernels they run alongside. In both, the fork (`alt_stream.wait_stream(current_stream)`) stays where it was, and only the capture order of the side block changes. 1. `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer.py`, `_fused_q_prepare_and_store`, stage 1: the `wq_b` GEMM on `alt_stream` is now captured after the main-stream `wk_weights_proj`, right before the join. 2. `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py` (decode graphs, DSA path): the `q_b_proj` block on `alt_stream` is now captured after the indexer, right before `current_stream.wait_stream(self.alt_stream)`. `k_nope.unsqueeze(1)`, a view with no kernel, now runs on the main stream. I checked the rest of the GLM-5.2 path and found no other active violation under TP4 / NVFP4 / `flashmla_kv`. In particular, `DeepseekV2MoE.forward_normal_dual_stream` already issues the routed experts before the shared-expert side block, and stage 2 of the fused indexer is already ordered correctly. Test: `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_dsa_indexer_stream_order.py` pins the issue order of the stage-1 block (fork, main GEMM, alt `wq_b`, join). It fails without the change and passes with it. ## Results GLM-5.2-NVFP4, aggregated serving, TP=4, CUDA graphs on, dummy weights, GB200 x4. One run per arm, rank TP1, same load for both. Distinct CUDA streams seen in the profiler trace: | | baseline | this PR | |---|---|---| | 10-step decode window | 123 | 81 | | 30 ms slice of the window | 45 | 3 | In the baseline, 99 of the 123 streams are tiny, each carrying a few kernels of the indexer chain (`fused_q_indexer_rope_hadamard_quant`, `sm100_paged_mqa_logits`, `topk_small_batch_cluster_kernel` and a TgvGemm kernel). With this PR those streams disappear: two main lanes carry about 13.3k and 9.8k kernels. The kernel count is identical (23,324 vs 23,319), so the same work runs. Median TPOT (`sglang.bench_serving`, random 512 in / 256 out): | concurrency | baseline | this PR | |---|---|---| | 1 | 10.51 ms | 10.43 ms | | 8 | 11.88 ms | 11.78 ms | | 16 | 13.33 ms | 13.28 ms | No regression. The 0.4% to 0.8% gain is within single-run noise and is not claimed as a speedup. ## Reproduce Model files only, no weights (config and tokenizer from `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`; weights are random via `--load-format dummy`): ```bash mkdir -p /path/to/glm52_cfg && cd /path/to/glm52_cfg for f in config.json generation_config.json hf_quant_config.json tokenizer.json tokenizer_config.json chat_template.jinja model.safetensors.index.json; do curl -sfL -O https://huggingface.co/nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4/resolve/main/$f done ``` Server (run once on `main` and once on this branch): ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code \ --model-path /path/to/glm52_cfg --load-format dummy \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --quantization modelopt_fp4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_kv \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --max-running-requests 16 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16 \ --context-length 32768 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` TPOT at concurrency 1, 8 and 16: ```bash for C in 1 8 16; do python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --model /path/to/glm52_cfg \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \ --num-prompts $((C*4)) --max-concurrency $C --warmup-requests 2 --seed 1 done ``` Trace of a steady-state decode window (start profiling about 6 s into the run, while it is decoding): ```bash python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --model /path/to/glm52_cfg \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 256 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \ --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 16 --seed 2 & sleep 6 curl -s -X POST localhost:30000/start_profile -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"num_steps":10,"activities":["CPU","GPU"],"output_dir":"/path/to/trace","profile_prefix":"run"}' wait ``` Count distinct streams per rank: read the trace JSON, take events with `ph == "X"` and `cat == "kernel"`, and count the distinct `args.stream` values. The full traces are 330 to 460 MB each. For Perfetto, cut a 30 ms window from one rank so it loads. ## Notes and limits - Dummy weights: this checks stream layout and latency only. It says nothing about accuracy. I compared TPOT, not generated outputs. - Single run per arm, one rank analyzed. The TPOT difference is within noise. - Stream assignment at replay is driver behavior. The result is from one driver and torch version here (torch 2.14.1+cu130, driver 580.x). - The `forward_mla.py` edit moves `q_b_proj` after the indexer. A reviewer raised a theoretical allocator-reuse hazard: tensors the indexer allocates on `alt_stream` are freed at return, and the trailing `q_b_proj` could reuse a block while a main-stream kernel still reads it. I did not reproduce a failure, and the A/B shows no change in throughput. I have not proven it safe either, so please look at this one closely. - The patched trace still has 78 streams that each hold one kernel, a FlashInfer RMSNorm, one per layer. They come from a separate stream hop that this PR does not touch. - This covers the CUDA-graph decode path (`is_decode_or_idle`). The target-verify and draft-extend graphs do not take the `forward_mla.py` overlap branch. ## Checklist - [x] Unit test added - [ ] Accuracy test (not run; dummy weights) The diff is still uncommitted on glm52-graph-stream-fork, and nothing is pushed. Two things to decide before you post it: - Allocator-race note. I disclosed the unresolved allocator-race concern about the forward_mla.py edit in "Notes and limits". I'd leave it in; the alternative is dropping that edit or adding a keep-alive fix. - Repeat runs. Repeating each arm a few times would let you replace "within noise" with a number. title: [Fix] modelopt: Correct NVFP4 TRT-LLM clamps for untied gate/up scales
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

TRT-LLM applies one GEMM1 clamp to both raw gate/up projections. With unequal NVFP4 global scales, converting the limit using the gate alpha gives the up projection the wrong effective limit: the up limit becomes `L × up_alpha / gate_alpha`, so a configured limit of 7 becomes 28 at a 4× ratio, or becomes stricter when the ratio is below one.

## Modifications

Normalize the effective gate/up alphas to their maximum during the existing TRT-LLM clamp preparation, folding the scale ratio into the smaller-alpha half’s E4M3 block scales. Derive the clamp, beta and output scale from the shared alpha. The fold uses the resolved gate/up alphas and leaves the raw global scales as loaded. Block-scale rows in this backend are `[up, gate]`. The work happens at load time, with no added forward operations.

Extend the existing CPU post-load regression for both halves' effective clamp limits, weight preservation and SiTU behavior, with GPU packing mocked. The GPU regression used in the accuracy tests below was a development-only fixture and is not part of this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

On rebased `main` commit `c1c287a42928495166e14dbcef31b9e1f1dac199` (including #45289), the CPU scale suite passes 20/20 and dispatch suite passes 5/5, with GPU devices hidden. The CPU clamp regression fails on this base with an effective up-half clamp of 28 instead of 7 and passes with the fix.

The GPU and numerical results below were collected before this rebase, against `main` commit `afe3e1df3107b0487258cd4a3d8e625248a8f881` on GB300 with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2 and sglang-kernel 0.4.10. GPU runs were not repeated for conflict resolution:

- A development copy of the GPU backend test with a temporary unequal-scale clamp regression passed 5/5 with this fix; the regression fails on the base at cosine 0.9034 against the unchanged 0.99 threshold. That temporary regression is not committed.
- Exact power-of-two controls match tied outputs bitwise, including real GLM expert weights with synthetic activations, routed/non-routed execution, per-token activation, reload and CUDA graph replay. Tied, unclamped, SiTU and sibling-backend controls are preserved.
- All 14 non-binary cases match the unmodified backend loaded with the same normalized weights bitwise, on both execution paths.
- Public prompt check on `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` at revision `da920bb0b9f4a06727223a349e55468e38352348`: the untouched checkpoint gives identical responses before/after. Re-expressing gate globals as ×4 and gate block scales as ÷4 is exact for this checkpoint; the fix’s ÷4 rescaling of the up block scales is exact too. The base then changes its response from 373 to 95 tokens; this fix restores the original content, token strings and logprobs exactly. Each configuration was repeated twice, with separate logprob diagnostics and cache flushes.

All public prompt runs copied the final table correctly and contained no replacement characters; their raw content included reasoning. This checks representation invariance, not reproduction of the reported Unicode failure. The reported finetuned checkpoint was unavailable.

**Rounding tradeoff:** non-binary normalization re-rounds one half's FP8 block scales. In the synthetic sweep, that changed the half's weights by 2.7–3.2% relative L2 and the reference output by 4.7–8.5% with both activation quantization steps included (0.7–3.4% when both were omitted). Every tested case improved over the incorrect clamp. No underflow occurred in these fixtures, but sufficiently small scales can become subnormal or flush to zero, including with power-of-two ratios. This is not a general model-quality evaluation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Before this rebase, sequential A/B/A/B CUDA graph measurements covered 52 points: 1–4096 tokens, routed/non-routed, tied/untied scales, 288 experts, hidden size 4096, intermediate size 512 and top-8, with L2 flushed before timing. All output controls passed. Candidate/base latency ratios were 0.9936–1.0031, within the pre-set `max(2%, 2 × baseline run spread)` criterion. The untied post-load step took 97–115 ms versus 90–105 ms on the base, once per 288-expert MoE layer at load time. Profiles confirm the TRT-LLM E2M1 GEMM/SwiGLU kernels.

## Checklist

- [x] Full `pre-commit run --all-files` passed without modifications on the validated tree, which also contained the temporary GPU fixture.
- [x] Added and ran the CPU post-load regression; isort, Ruff lint and formatting checks pass.
- [x] Ran GPU validation with a temporary regression fixture.
- [x] Provided numerical and operator-latency evidence.
- [x] Followed existing code style and backend preparation structure.
- Documentation: no public API or configuration change.
