title: [Refactor] kernels: Add the plugin kernel backend and split plugin contracts from their srt integration
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Some kernels are specialized for one model, configuration and platform, and replace a model's whole step. They come from external libraries that load as SGLang plugins:

- the NVIDIA megakernel, from [sgl-nvidia-mega](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega)
- the AMD monokernels, from [sgl-amd-mono](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono)

Today these plugins serve small-batch decode and verify steps. Nothing ties them to low latency or to "mega" fusion; prefill or high-throughput specializations would plug in the same way.

SGLang's side of each integration lived in `srt/megakernels` and `srt/monokernels`. This PR splits that code at the kernel/runtime boundary:

- what a plugin implements and registers moves to `kernels/plugin_kernels/<hardware>/`, recorded by a new `KernelBackend.PLUGIN` (as with `kda_kernels/` and `cake_kernels/`)
- SGLang's serving integration stays in `srt/`, as `srt/kernel_plugins/<hardware>/`

The kernels themselves stay in their libraries.

## Modifications

```
python/sglang/kernels/plugin_kernels/   # the contract a plugin implements; imports nothing from srt
  nvidia/spec.py                        #   registration, API version, requirements, capabilities,
  amd/spec.py                           #   widths, build/forward contract
                                        #   (<hardware>/<model>/ for thin kernel wrappers later)
python/sglang/srt/kernel_plugins/       # SGLang's integration, one binding.py per hardware
  nvidia/binding.py                     #   startup checks on the resolved config, build, TP agreement,
  amd/binding.py                        #   CUDA graph coverage, forward dispatch with fallback,
                                        #   weight observation (AMD), the runtime state handed to a plugin
```

- **Move.** The code moves unchanged; only imports are combined.
  - `srt/{megakernels,monokernels}/spec.py` → `kernels/plugin_kernels/{nvidia,amd}/spec.py`.
  - Each hardware's `guards.py` + `runtime.py` (and, on NVIDIA, `binding.py`) → `srt/kernel_plugins/<hardware>/binding.py`.
  - Unit tests → `test/registered/unit/kernel_plugins/{nvidia,amd}/`. They now patch the one `binding` module.
- **No aliases.** `sglang.srt.megakernels` and `sglang.srt.monokernels` are removed.
  - The plugins import the new locations first and fall back to the old ones for earlier SGLang: sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega#21 and sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono#25, both merged.
  - The pins move to those merge commits:
    - `SGL_NVIDIA_MEGA_COMMIT` becomes `6fd7ac3` in both CUDA Dockerfiles. Main pins `3333e4c` (#46030), an ancestor of `6fd7ac3`.
    - The `sgl-amd-mono` pin in `pyproject_other.toml` becomes `05e0bb0`.
- **`KernelBackend.PLUGIN`.** Adds the enum value and a `forward_plugin` hook on `BaseFusedOp`, placed after KDA/CAKE in `DEFAULT_PRIORITY`. The namespace test pairs `plugin_kernels/` with this backend.
- **`--monokernel-backend amd` → `--enable-amd-monokernel`.** The flag becomes a boolean next to `--enable-nvidia-megakernel`.
  - `--monokernel-backend amd` stays as a deprecated spelling: it warns and sets the new flag. Any other value is rejected.
  - The field keeps its slot in `POSITIONAL_FIELD_ORDER`.
  - Both spellings also work in `--config` YAML files. Previously the merger accepted only `store`/`store_true` actions, which rejected the deprecated alias and, through the shared dest, the new key too.
    - The merger now passes single-value actions as `--flag value`.
    - A key stays usable when a supported flag also reads it.
    - A regression test covers `monokernel-backend: amd`, `enable-amd-monokernel: true` / `false`, and both CLI spellings. Before the fix, the three YAML cases raise `ValueError`.
  - The resolution hook is renamed `handle_amd_monokernel`.
  - Error messages, the server-args doc, the DeepSeek-V4.1 cookbook and the ROCm Dockerfile comment are updated.
- **Docs.** `kernels/README.md`, `plugin_kernels/README.md` and the kernel-organization skill describe the split.

No runtime behavior changes: the default path is untouched, and the megakernel and monokernel code is the same code at new paths.

**Not covered: the MSA plugin.** The MiniMax-M3.1 cookbook (#45924) serves the MSA plugin with `--monokernel-backend msa`. On this PR that value is rejected, and the plugin's `sglang.srt.monokernels` imports fail. That plugin is moving off the monokernel name separately.

## Accuracy Tests

All runs: 4x GB300 (sm_103), `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13`, plugins at the pinned commits (sgl-nvidia-mega `6fd7ac3`, sgl-amd-mono `05e0bb0`).

The PR content was tested at `7311b92f02`, which has main `6e667c4310` merged. The head has main `3ea7e210d2` merged instead; that merge changed nothing in this PR except resolving the NVIDIA pin conflict.

### Tests and plugin loading

- **43 CPU-relevant test files**, each run in its own process: `unit/kernels/**`, `unit/server_args/**`, `unit/model_loader/**`, the moved tests, `test_dspark_draft_block`, `test_runtime_context` and others.
  - Main `6e667c4310` and this PR fail the same single case.
  - The 5 moved test files pass.
- **Plugins through their real entry points.**
  - On this PR, `sglang.srt.megakernels` is gone, and both plugins register from the new locations.
  - On main, they register from the old ones.
  - Either way, the NVIDIA DeepSeek-V4.1 target and draft specs resolve to `MegakernelSpec`, and all six AMD specs resolve on `gfx950`.
- **The plugins' own `test/unit`.**
  - sgl-amd-mono `05e0bb0`: 5 failed, 124 passed on both main and this PR, the same five. They are GLM-5.3 spec cases.
  - sgl-nvidia-mega `6fd7ac3`: the Kimi K3 tests fail on both.
    - On main they fail because the hybrid views from #45406 are missing. With `--continue-on-collection-errors`, that is 22 failed, 162 passed, 1 error, all Kimi K3.
    - On this PR they also fail because `kimi_k3` imports `sglang.srt.megakernels` with no fallback. #45406 has to move those views to `srt/kernel_plugins/nvidia/binding.py` anyway, and `kimi_k3` should then import them new-path-first, as DeepSeek-V4.1 does.

### The real megakernel, end to end

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, served with the plugin README's command (TP4, DSpark block 5, `--enable-nvidia-megakernel` and the three required env vars):

| | main `b453996b7d` | this PR on `b453996b7d` (`48b0063ff6`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NVIDIA megakernel: active` (target and DSpark draft specs, 4 ranks) | 8 lines | 8 lines |
| `draft proposal engaged` during graph capture | 108 | 108 |
| GSM8K, sgl-eval 0.1.3, 200 examples, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, no thinking, seed 0 | 0.985 | 0.990 |

On main `6e667c4310`, the same command fails with or without this PR, identically:
- Both activate (8 lines).
- Both then fail during the first verify-graph capture, also with `--max-running-requests 8 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 8`. SGLang's DeepSeek-V4 indexer, reached through `view.low_ratio_sources`, hits `assert A.shape[:-1] == As.shape[:-1]` in the fp8 `wq_b` GEMM.

A partial bisect puts that regression between `bb9e9d5632` (good) and `b588aa39e9` (bad, #45921). The head after the latest main merge was not run on GPU.

title: [Perf] cosmos3: optimize v2v preprocess performance
author: xupinjie
body:
## Motivation

Cosmos3 V2V currently decodes the full source video and repeats CPU preprocessing for temporally padded frames. Reduce this overhead while preserving the original preprocessing and generated outputs bit for bit.

## Modifications

- Use PyAV to load the required first/last conditioning frames without materializing the full video.
- Add batched Triton Lanczos resize with optional crop and normalization, preserving input layout and matching Pillow rounding.
- Preprocess each source frame once, in batches of up to 8. Convert to the VAE dtype before temporal padding, and release pixel tensors after VAE encoding.
- Enable GPU video preprocessing by default; reuse `SGLANG_FORCE_CPU_IMAGE_PREPROCESSING=1` for CPU preprocessing.

## Accuracy Tests

Compared against the original ImageIO + CPU/PIL baseline across **8 configurations**: 480p, 720p, 1080p and 4K inputs, with either fixed 480p output or output resolution following input.

All configurations are **bit-identical** for the FP32 source preprocessing results, the complete 45-frame BF16 VAE input, the final MP4 file, and all decoded RGB frames.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Environment:** 1× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (96 GB); Docker image: `lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:b1259f3ea3275f66237c498ea388919729018bc9f01c3d638391e06e2cf3f469`.

**Workload:** Cosmos3-Edge, official `robot_pouring.mp4`, resized to each input resolution; first 5 conditioning frames, 45 output frames, 24 FPS, 35 steps, CFG 5, seed 42. All offload, torch.compile and guardrails are disabled.

Each configuration uses a separate process with **1 complete warmup + 1 measured request**, using different videos and positive/negative prompts. Every measured request misses the conditioning cache and executes VAE encoding and both text branches. Baseline is the original ImageIO full-video decode + CPU/PIL implementation. Speedup = baseline / optimized.

### Fixed 480p output

| Input W×H | Output W×H | Baseline preprocess (ms) | Optimized preprocess (ms) | Preprocess speedup | Baseline E2E (s) | Optimized E2E (s) | E2E speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 854×480 | 832×480 | 311.751 | 24.025 | 12.98× | 6.422 | 6.128 | 1.048× |
| 1280×720 | 832×480 | 954.077 | 40.117 | 23.78× | 7.122 | 6.175 | 1.154× |
| 1920×1080 | 832×480 | 1636.807 | 80.402 | 20.36× | 7.812 | 6.241 | 1.252× |
| 3840×2160 | 832×480 | 5607.374 | 284.450 | 19.71× | 11.781 | 6.443 | 1.829× |

### Output resolution follows input

Output dimensions are aligned to the model's 16-pixel requirement.

| Input W×H | Output W×H | Baseline preprocess (ms) | Optimized preprocess (ms) | Preprocess speedup | Baseline E2E (s) | Optimized E2E (s) | E2E speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 854×480 | 848×480 | 311.950 | 23.854 | 13.08× | 6.544 | 6.303 | 1.038× |
| 1280×720 | 1280×720 | 575.703 | 39.960 | 14.41× | 17.972 | 17.464 | 1.029× |

| 3840×2160 | 3840×2160 | 6790.350 | 321.065 | 21.15× | 555.197 | 548.448 | 1.012× |

Preprocess time includes video decoding, resize/crop/normalization, stacking and GPU completion. The optimized version performs BF16 conversion and temporal padding in latent preparation; these are included in E2E rather than the preprocess column. E2E includes MP4 saving and excludes model loading. Each row is a single measurement.

### Peak GPU memory: output resolution follows input

title: [Perf] glm-5.3: Encode GLM-5.3 Python chat template prompts segment by segment
author: Dovis01
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #45154. The GLM-5.3 Python chat template still renders the prompt to one string, which `parallel_prompt_encode` then has to take apart again. It scans the text for added tokens to find cut points, only engages at `SGLANG_PARALLEL_PROMPT_ENCODE_MIN_CHARS` (32,768 characters) and above, and probes once whether `encode_batch` really runs in parallel. Shorter prompts are encoded with a single tokenizer call, and every request re-encodes its whole prompt, even though in function-calling and agent workloads most of it (system prompt, tool list, earlier turns) repeats from request to request.

The renderer already knows where each turn's special tokens go. This PR hands those positions to the encoder: the text between them is encoded in one `encode_batch` call at any prompt length without scanning the prompt, and its token ids are cached, so the parts that recur are encoded once.

## Modifications

- **`parser/glm53_chat_template.py`**: `render_glm53_segments` / `render_glm53_flash_segments` return the prompt as the list of strings it concatenates, with `[gMASK]`, `<sop>`, `<|system|>`, `<|user|>`, `<|assistant|>`, `<|observation|>` and the generation prompt's `<think>` as items of their own. `render_glm53` / `render_glm53_flash` join them, so the rendered prompt is unchanged byte for byte.
- **`parser/python_chat_template.py`**: `PythonChatTemplate.render_segments`. The installed `apply_chat_template` and the new `render_chat_segments` share one render path. `render_chat_segments` returns `None` when `chat_template_kwargs` holds an argument of `apply_chat_template` itself (`chat_template`, `continue_final_message`, `documents`, ...), so those requests keep the original path, errors included.
- **`entrypoints/openai/parallel_prompt_encode.py`**: `encode_prompt_segments(tokenizer, segments, encode_kwargs)`, a drop-in for `parallel_prompt_encode(tokenizer, "".join(segments), encode_kwargs)`.
  - A segment that is a whole added token is a cut point if no added token can match across it (`_cuts_at`, checked once per token). The text between cut points goes through one `encode_batch` call, whatever the prompt length, and the prompt itself is not scanned.
  - The ids of that text are kept in a per-tokenizer LRU (up to 1M tokens, entries up to 128K tokens), so a recurring system prompt, tool list or earlier turn is encoded once.
  - Uncached text of at least `SGLANG_PARALLEL_PROMPT_ENCODE_MIN_CHARS` is still split with `split_prompt`, so a long document stays parallel on its first request.
  - It uses the same one-time tokenizer validation (the per-tokenizer plan) and per-call checks as `parallel_prompt_encode`, and falls back to it for everything else: no plan, post-processor specials, truncation / padding / `encode_special_tokens` left on the backend, `SGLANG_PARALLEL_PROMPT_ENCODE=0`, other encode kwargs.
- **`entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py`**: `_render_and_encode_chat_template` takes the segment path when a Python chat template is active. Jinja templates, and every model without a Python template, keep `apply_chat_template` + `parallel_prompt_encode` unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

- **Token-id identity on the real tokenizers** (GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash): 6,608 comparisons, 0 mismatches. Segment-path ids equal `tokenizer.encode(rendered_prompt)` for randomized conversations whose content contains special-token spellings, partial spellings next to the cut points, and unicode, plus a 150K-character document and the 128-tool prompt below, each encoded a second time from the cache. 600 of them are also compared with Jinja `apply_chat_template` ids.
- **Online A/B** (this PR vs. `main`, GLM-5.3-Flash, greedy decoding): identical `prompt_token_ids`, status and outputs for 24 cases. They cover chat, `reasoning_effort`, multi-turn reasoning, `clear_thinking`, tools (`auto` / `required` / named / `none`), out-of-order tool results, inline system messages, `continue_final_message`, images, streaming, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/messages`, and the 400 error cases.
- **Unit tests**:
  - `test_parallel_prompt_encode.py::TestPromptSegments`: id identity on fuzzed segment lists, text encoded once with no length threshold, long text split, tokens another added token can overlap are not cut points, fallbacks, cache budget.
  - `test_glm53_chat_template.py`: segments join to what `apply_chat_template` renders, turn tokens are segments of their own, routing back to `apply_chat_template`. With `SGLANG_TEST_GLM53_CHECKPOINT` / `SGLANG_TEST_GLM53_FLASH_CHECKPOINT` set, segment-encoded ids are also compared with the checkpoints' tokenizers.
  - `test_serving_chat.py`: the serving wiring.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Render + encode per request** (what `_render_and_encode_chat_template` does), median ms with the GLM-5.3-Flash tokenizer. The last message differs on every request. *Cold* has nothing cached: the first request with a given tool list and history. *Warm* has the tool list and earlier turns cached: the next request of a conversation, or another request with the same tools.

| Scenario | Prompt chars / tokens | `main` | This PR, cold | This PR, warm |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| chat, 1 turn | 103 / 23 | 0.050 | 0.065 | 0.038 (1.3x) |
| 8 tools, 1 turn | 2,312 / 596 | 0.730 | 0.601 (1.2x) | 0.083 (8.8x) |
| 128 tools, 1 turn | 82,925 / 20,238 | 2.835 | 2.918 | 1.003 (2.8x) |
| agent: 8 tools, 18 tool-call rounds | 38,262 / 7,997 | 1.559 | 1.447 (1.1x) | 0.357 (4.4x) |
| agent: 8 tools, 8 rounds × 3 parallel calls | 25,053 / 5,276 | 7.596 | 1.160 (6.5x) | 0.233 (32.6x) |

- The 8 × 3 agent prompt is below 32,768 characters, so `main` encodes it with a single tokenizer call. The segment path batches it at any length, so it is 6.5x faster even with nothing cached.
- The 128-tool prompt is above the threshold, so `main` already encodes it in parallel, and cold the two paths are on par. Warm, the remaining ~1 ms is the Python render.
- A cold request whose new text is two or more tiny segments pays rayon's dispatch (+15 µs in the first row), once per conversation.

**End to end**, client-side TTFT p50 in ms. Setup: GLM-5.3-Flash FP8, TP4 / EP4 on 4×B200, EAGLE MTP (5 / 1 / 6, adaptive), `--reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47`. `main` and this PR ran side by side with the same checkpoint and flags. Requests are streamed with `max_tokens` 512 and temperature 1.0, with no cache flush and a unique nonce in the last message of every request: the radix prefix cache is warm, and the whole-request render cache misses. 20 requests at concurrency 1, 64 at concurrency 16.

| Scenario | Prompt tokens | c=1: `main` → this PR | c=16: `main` → this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128 tools, 1 turn | 20,247 | 185.3 → 159.1 (−14.1%) | 550.3 → 422.9 (−23.1%) |
| agent: 8 tools, 18 tool-call rounds | 8,006 | 77.6 → 65.7 (−15.3%) | 142.4 → 122.0 (−14.3%) |
| agent: 8 tools, 8 rounds × 3 parallel calls | 5,285 | 73.6 → 66.1 (−10.2%) | 103.0 → 108.4 (mean 136.3 → 123.6) |
| 8 tools, 1 turn | 606 | 54.5 → 55.0 | 129.4 → 127.5 |

- With this PR, the 128-tool request comes within 3 ms of the ~156 ms measured when the render cache returns the whole prompt for a repeated request.
- The 8-tool prompt has under 1 ms of preprocessing to save, so its TTFT is unchanged.
- Environment: Intel Xeon 6960P (144 threads), Python 3.12.15, transformers 5.19.0, tokenizers 0.23.2.

title: [Feat] [NVIDIA] megakernels: Expose hybrid runtime and DSpark verification views
author: leejnau
body:
## Motivation

Hybrid MLA/KDA megakernel plugins need typed access to SGLang-owned cache and step state after model resources are prepared and before CUDA graph capture. This includes ordinary decode and fixed-width Kimi K3 DSpark target verification. The companion implementation is [sgl-nvidia-mega #25](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega/pull/25).

## Modifications

- [`9b00e04f`](https://github.com/leejnau/sglang/commit/9b00e04f555a2ed9b583d2e3baf3e302cfd0ba21): explicit post-resource preparation, typed per-step views, graph-static ownership checks, and existing non-hybrid behavior, rebased onto the current NVIDIA kernel-plugin layout and API v2.
- [`ca36ffa8`](https://github.com/leejnau/sglang/commit/ca36ffa89a687505b7d0705d0b02945a2b425aed): request-local KDA verification state, MLA query-width metadata, auxiliary hidden-state buffers, and capture-lifetime checks. SGLang retains ownership of acceptance, recurrent-state commit, and stock draft-model execution.
- [`27687018`](https://github.com/leejnau/sglang/commit/27687018a1e33252bc42cdcd0c337116c8f6c91f): preserve architecture-specific EagleBinding dispatch/capture behavior, with a real-binding regression.
- [`5f31ea56`](https://github.com/leejnau/sglang/commit/5f31ea5649618cf0d81fbb359411e403a2ebdf0f): avoid per-view legacy accessor closures while retaining lazy access and typed-only hybrid views.
- [`3e41ef87`](https://github.com/leejnau/sglang/commit/3e41ef8764018321d612d15f69da8a9f4c35796a): align runtime test fixtures with the API-v2 installed-object and optional-entry contracts.

The foundation and DSpark commits formerly proposed in [#46479](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46479) remain separate reviewable commits. No kernel arithmetic or default execution path is changed. The focused DSpark configuration is GB300, TP8, five draft proposals plus one anchor (q6), and DCP off. Uniform q4–q8 metadata support retains fail-closed layout and ownership checks. The original full-model evidence uses an 8,192-token context; bounded long-context qualification is described separately in the companion plugin PR.

The [isolated Kimi plugin compatibility commit](https://github.com/leejnau/sgl-nvidia-mega/commit/32262d4f5b4eecc725a5b89584f33bbcf3c85273) in the companion PR supports ordinary decode independently of DSpark. It prefers the new interfaces and falls back only when the new namespace is absent.

## Accuracy Tests

Current rebased pair: SGLang `3e41ef8764018321d612d15f69da8a9f4c35796a` and plugin `90e1b1b48a79d556dbddc093a3358b1d9b7912e2`. CPU-only Python checks passed **55 tests and 150 subtests**, covering the actual binding, registry, runtime/preparation functions and plugin contracts, including real EagleBinding target/draft dispatch and capture-tail checks. Server/GPU dependencies unavailable on the host were isolated with test stubs; this is not a full native-framework import or GPU requalification. Focused repository lint, import ordering and formatting checks pass. The GPU measurements below remain attributed to their original revisions.

The native old/new-layout matrix passed on GB300 for ordinary-decode and DSpark bindings: all 34 isolated test-file runs completed without failures or skips. Checks covered actual module/type/registration/preparation identities and audited installed wheel payloads, identical across layouts within each pair. The ordinary-decode pair is SGLang `d8543baa` / plugin `32262d4`; the native-tested DSpark pair is `0e9e2aa` / `e64e4d0`. The subsequent `d3d6d8c` changes only one test import's formatting, with identical AST and no production changes. This is focused compatibility validation, not a new full-model accuracy run.

Historical full-model measurements apply specifically to **SGLang `02406d4ef05680cbf3d77287354d887b039141d9` + sgl-nvidia-mega `194d693d15a51f74a727889531fd6d9cd01bf355`**, not the rebased pair. GSM8K was 1,283/1,314 specialized versus 1,284/1,314 stock; accepted draft tokens per verification were 3.7966 versus 3.8264, excluding the bonus token. The known numerical canary remains **FAIL**, separately from quality and timing; these results do not establish general numerical equivalence.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

On that same historical DSpark pair, matched end-to-end output throughput was 1.43–2.09x stock for B1/B4 and 128/6,144-token inputs; see the [measurements and limitations](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega/pull/25#issuecomment-6408017781). These are bounded end-to-end results, not isolated kernel speedups or new measurements on the consolidated head. Earlier ordinary-decode measurements are recorded in merged [sgl-nvidia-mega #17](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega/pull/17).

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] deepseek-v4.1: Fix the breakable prefill CUDA graph in the late-layer tail on SM90
author: JohnZhao01
body:
## Motivation

On H200 (SM90), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with decoder SWA bounded replay (on by default; the [cookbook](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/76560713092795ac051d0411574c3a8d73145c2f/docs/cookbook/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V4_1.mdx#L108) lists breakable prefill as supported with it) cannot serve with `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`. The late-layer tail fails in two places, both on paths that SM100 does not take: SM90 has no in-graph low-ratio path (`low_ratio_prefill_graph` is false), so the ratio-1/2 sources run as eager breaks or, in one place, get captured.

1. **Warmup before capture.** The first faulting kernel is the device-side assert in `torch.repeat_interleave` (`Repeat.cu:20: result_size == cumsum_ptr[size - 1]`); the CUDA 719 and DeepGEMM errors that follow are knock-on errors. Call chain: `bcg_deepseek_v4_low_ratio_sources` → `forward_low_ratio_sources` → `token_req_indices` → `repeat_interleave(req, extend_seq_lens, output_size=positions.shape[0])`. Inside the tail, the eager break sees only the tail's live rows, while `forward_batch.extend_seq_lens` still spans the whole extend. The hoisted `low_ratio_req_indices` / `low_ratio_pos_i64` already hold the tail's rows (live rows first, bucket-sized), but they are only used when their length equals the break's row count, which it does not inside an eager break.
2. **Replay of the first real request.** With (1) fixed, capture and startup succeed, and the first real prefill asserts in a replayed graph: `the output_size argument (8) must be the same as the sum of the elements in the repeats tensor (6)`. The source-layer KV write at the start of the tail (`write_tail_source_kv`) is called directly from the model, not through an eager break, so on SM90 its `token_req_indices` and the host-side compressor are captured with the capture-time row count.

This still reproduces on `main` @ `c1c287a4`: without this change, the breakable launch below crashes while capturing the prefill graph with the same `Repeat.cu:20` assert.

#45381 fixes a different capture failure of the same low-ratio prefill-graph path on SM12x.

## Modifications

- `deepseek_v4_backend.py` (`forward_low_ratio_sources`): when the hoisted rows are longer than the break's rows in an extend, take their live prefix instead of rebuilding the rows from `extend_seq_lens`. Bucket-sized calls (the in-graph path) and calls without hoisted rows are unchanged.
  - The hoisted rows are longer only under the prefill graph, where both the prefill-graph metadata and the tail metadata store the live rows first and the padding after them. Outside the tail the live prefix therefore equals what `token_req_indices` computes; inside the tail it is the only correct value. The prefill-graph full top-k break (`_prefill_graph_full_topk_break`) already takes `low_ratio_req_indices[:real]` the same way. If a narrower condition is preferred, it can check the tail metadata explicitly; happy to switch.
- `deepseek_v4.py`: a new eager break, `bcg_deepseek_v4_write_tail_source_kv`, slices the source-layer input to the live rows like `deepseek_v4_low_ratio_sources`, with the same capture-stub contract as `_low_ratio_sources_capture_stub`. The tail's source-KV write uses it inside a breakable prefill graph when the backend has no in-graph low-ratio path; every other configuration keeps the direct call. The condition reads `low_ratio_prefill_graph` the same way as the existing low-ratio call site in `_forward_prepare`. With no live rows it skips the write but still sets `tail_source_kv_layer_id`, as `write_tail_source_kv` does, so the source layer's own pass inside the tail keeps skipping its compressor. Rebased onto `main` @ `c1c287a4`, where #45339 computes `source_x` at the same call site with a HIP branch; that computation is kept and only the call after it is dispatched.
- Tests (run on H200 against `main` @ `c1c287a4`):
  - `TestDSV4LateLayerTailLowRatioRows` checks that a tail-sized eager break gets the live prefix of the hoisted rows for both the compressor and the indexer. It fails before this change (`RuntimeError: allocated size does not match required size` from `repeat_interleave`, the rows rebuilt from `extend_seq_lens` not matching the break's row count) and passes after.
  - `TestDSV4WriteTailSourceKvBreak` checks that the source-KV break passes only the first `global_num_token_non_padded_cpu` rows of `x` and `positions` to `write_tail_source_kv`, and that with zero live rows it does not call it but still marks the source layer. It covers a function this PR adds, so it has no before/after comparison; it passes.

## Accuracy Tests

Setup: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8×H200, image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261021-c1c287a4` (`main` @ `c1c287a4`), with this PR's commits applied to the image's source tree for the "this change" column.

Launch flags: `--tp 8 --attention-backend dsv4 --moe-runner-backend marlin --mem-fraction-static 0.70 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --prefill-decode-interval 16 --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay --swa-prefix-tails 1024 --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 --speculative-num-steps 1 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 2 --language-model-only`, plus `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 4096` for the graph runs. "Eager" is the same launch without the two prefill-graph flags.

| | eager (no prefill graph) | breakable, before this change | breakable, this change |
|---|---|---|---|
| startup | ready | crashes while capturing the prefill graph (`Repeat.cu:20` assert, item 1) | ready |
| GSM8K, sgl-eval 0.1.3, 1,319 questions, model preset (thinking on, reasoning effort high, T=1.0, top_p 0.95) | 0.9704 | — | 0.9697 |
| GSM8K, lm-eval with the InferenceX setup, 5-shot, flexible / strict | 0.9735 / 0.9742 | — | 0.9727 / 0.9735 |
| long-context retrieval, 6 prompts | 6/6 | — | 6/6 |
| `max_total_num_tokens` | 23,892,736 | — | 23,892,736 |
| smoke: 15 real prefills, 1 to 30,000 words (9 single, 6 concurrent, covering the padded bucket sizes) | 15/15 | — | 15/15 |

- Server logs of all runs of both columns have no assert and no CUDA error.
- Which requests exercise the changed path: under decoder SWA bounded replay every prefill extend runs the late layers over each request's last min(extend length, 128) rows, 128 being the model's sliding window (`SWA_WINDOW`), unless it asks for prompt logprobs or every hidden state; speculative verify extends do not run the tail. (`--swa-prefix-tails 1024` is unrelated: it sizes how many radix-cached prefix tails the SWA KV pool keeps room for.) In a separate run of this change with a counting log added (not part of this PR), sgl-eval GSM8K (200 questions) and the smoke ran 40 prefill forwards through the tail after startup: 31 were graph replays (up to 3,447 tail rows), which run the two eager breaks changed here, and 9 ran eager (batches over the 4,096-token capture cap, or chunks whose context exceeds the 16K replay limit).
- Earlier measurements on `nightly-dev-cu13-20261018-b234b5c3`, before the rebase: GSM8K (InferenceX setup) 0.9727 / 0.9735 with this change and eager, a second pair with `--max-running-requests 64` at 0.9742 / 0.9742, long-context retrieval 6/6, smoke 15/15.
- Prompt logprobs (on b234b5c3; 21 fixed prompts, 40 to 12,000 words, 76,144 prompt tokens, `/generate` with `return_logprob` and `logprob_start_len 0`, T=0): the graph-vs-eager difference (mean |Δlogprob| 0.158 / 0.160) is the same as the run-to-run difference of each configuration (0.159 eager, 0.157 graph). Requests for prompt logprobs run the late layers over the whole prompt rather than the bounded tail, so this check covers the graph's numerics but not the tail path changed here; the tail path is covered by the accuracy rows and the smoke above.

`--cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 4096`: with the default capture sizes the graph pool takes about 29.6 GB at `--mem-fraction-static 0.70`, and the first eager chunk of a 128K cold prefill (chunks past the 16K replay limit run eager) ran out of memory in the eager torch indexer scoring (measured on b234b5c3). Capping the capture at 4,096 tokens keeps the pool at 8.75 GB with the same KV pool size. That is a memory-headroom setting for this configuration, not part of the fix: with the default capture sizes the fix also captures, starts and serves the same smoke prefills without errors, with the same KV pool size, long-context retrieval 6/6 and GSM8K 0.9697 (within the ±0.0047 standard error); only the 128K cold prefill ran out of memory.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

On `main` @ `c1c287a4` (single requests, same server as the accuracy rows):

| | eager | this change (breakable, bs 4096) |
|---|---|---|
| 128K cold prefill (131,071 tokens) TTFT | 6.30 s | 6.05 s |
| decode TPOT p50, B = 1 / 8 / 16 | 2.15 / 4.80 / 6.39 ms | 2.18 / 4.69 / 6.60 ms |
| 262K-token request with 4 short requests behind it: long TTFT | 19.68 s | 19.69 s |

Measured earlier on b234b5c3:

Cold-prefill TTFT (random-word prompts, no cache hit, `max_tokens` 1, median of 3; the nominal sizes are estimated at 2.3 words per token, so actual token counts are somewhat larger):

| nominal prompt | eager | this change (breakable, bs 4096) |
|---|---|---|
| 512 | 0.202 s | 0.079 s |
| 2K | 0.201 s | 0.150 s |
| 8K | 0.384 s | 0.368 s |
| 16K | 0.776 s | 0.784 s |
| 32K | 1.587 s | 1.605 s |
| 128K | 9.310 s | 9.380 s |

Short prefills lose a fixed ~0.2 s of eager launch overhead. Prefill chunks whose context exceeds 16K still run eager on SM90 (#43733 lifts that limit only on SM100), so long prefills are unchanged.

Load test, 900 s per point after a 600 s warmup, InferenceX agentic traces (SLO lines TTFT p90 ≤ 5,750 ms, TPOT p90 ≤ 34.5 ms), same flags as above with `--max-running-requests 64`:

| | max concurrency within SLO | total throughput at that point |
|---|---|---|
| eager | 10 | 56,550 tok/s (TTFT p90 1,902 ms, TPOT p90 19.7 ms) |
| this change | 16 | 83,542 tok/s (TTFT p90 3,220 ms, TPOT p90 33.4 ms) |

title: [Refactor] sgl-router: Move experimental/sgl-router to top-level sgl-router
author: sherlockwu
body:
Move sgl-router out of `experimental/` to a top-level `sgl-router/` directory.

## Modifications

1. **Pure rename**: `git mv experimental/sgl-router sgl-router`. All 290 files are 100% renames, so history and blame carry over (`git diff --name-status -M100% HEAD~3 HEAD~2` shows only `R100` entries).
2. **Path fixups**:
   - Relative paths that depended on directory depth:
     - `sgl-router/Cargo.toml`: `../../rust/sglang-{processor,api-types}` → `../rust/...`
     - `tests/e2e/k8s_integration/setup.sh`: `REPO_ROOT` now goes up one level fewer
     - The `PYTHONPATH` hint in `generate_array_content_fixture.py`
   - Repo-root path strings `experimental/sgl-router` → `sgl-router`:
     - `pr-test-sgl-router.yml`: the paths filter, rust-cache workspaces, `working-directory`, and the k8s build/pytest paths
     - `docker/sgl-router.Dockerfile` and `tests/e2e/k8s_integration/Dockerfile.router`
     - `.pre-commit-config.yaml`: the `rustfmt-sgl-router` hook
     - `.gitignore`: the `Cargo.lock` un-ignore. This matters for git only; Docker patterns are root-anchored, so the bare `Cargo.lock` line never excluded the router's lockfile from the Docker context.
     - READMEs, docstrings, and comments
   - Renamed `nightly-experimental-sgl-router-docker.yml` → `nightly-sgl-router-docker.yml` and its display name. Nothing references the filename, and the schedule/dispatch triggers move with it.

**Unchanged on purpose:** the published image tag `lmsysorg/sglang-staging:experimental-router-dev` and the dashboard `uid`, so existing pullers and imports keep working.

## Verification

- `cargo metadata --locked` resolves the new path deps; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes
- `cargo test --locked --release --workspace -- --skip parity_matrix` (the CI tier-2 command): 1596 passed, 0 failed
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes, including the renamed `rustfmt sgl-router` hook
- `setup.sh` resolves `REPO_ROOT`/`SGL_ROUTER_DIR` to the repo root and `sgl-router/`
- `router_binary_path()` resolves correctly with no env, with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, and with `SGL_ROUTER_BINARY`; an explicit `Gateway(binary=...)` still wins; `pytest --collect-only` in `tests/e2e` collects all 60 tests
- `git grep experimental/sgl-router` is empty
- `docker/sgl-router.Dockerfile`: all COPY sources exist. Reproducing its final builder-stage layout (only the files it copies, at `/work/sgl-router` + `/work/rust`) builds with `cargo build --locked --release --bin sgl-router`, and the binary runs
- **Not covered:** an actual `docker build` (no Docker here). PR CI doesn't build this image either, because `sgl-router-docker-build-test` is a placeholder; the nightly is the first real build. The k8s integration job does build `Dockerfile.router` once `run-ci` is set.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] DSpark: Enable the simulated-acceptance fast paths on CUDA
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` set (simulated acceptance for benchmarking), DSpark already has three fast paths, but they are gated to HIP:

- the verify skips the draft / target accept sampling (softmax + rejection), whose result the simulated length overwrites;
- the accept and the sampled bonus fold into the verify CUDA graph (`SGLANG_DSPARK_SIMULATE_FOLD`);
- temperature-only rows are treated as greedy (`SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_GREEDY`).

On CUDA the same simulated runs still pay for the discarded sampling and the unfolded accept. This PR lets CUDA take the same paths.

## Modifications

- `dspark_verify.py`: skip the accept sampling under simulated acceptance on every platform (was `simulate and _is_hip`).
- `dspark_worker_v2.py`: `simulate_fold` and `_simulate_acc_greedy` no longer require HIP; both keep their existing env switches (default on), so either can still be turned off.
- Remove the now-unused `_is_hip` / `is_hip` imports in both files.

No effect when `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` is unset, so real serving is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Only the simulated-acceptance path changes. Accuracy runs use real acceptance (`SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` unset) and take the same code as before.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4 GB300, DSpark, `--enable-nvidia-megakernel`, AgentX agentic-coding, concurrency 1, `--max-running-requests 1`, `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.51` (match-expected, real-draft-token), 3,600 s. Measured on main `8e7601ae4a4` + #44945; the two arms differ only by this change (one boot each, different nodes):

| | requests | tok/s/user p50 | p90 | TTFT p50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| without this change | 404 | 760.0 | 719.3 | 102 ms |
| with this change | 474 | 949.7 | 926.0 | 96 ms |

The two runs reached different context mixes (ISL p50 294K vs 153K), so here is the steady decode step from the server's decode-batch log, binned by context and matched on (conversation, turn):

| context | ≤ 64K | 64–256K | > 256K |
|---|---|---|---|
| without this change | 4.581 ms | 4.595 ms | 4.522 ms |
| with this change | 3.654 ms | 3.669 ms | 3.723 ms |

A rerun on current main will be added.

title: [Perf] [KDA] cookbook: enable custom all-reduce for GB300 BF16 Muse Spark
author: Waterpine
body:
## Motivation

This PR is powered by [KDA](https://github.com/NVlabs/kda) team. On GB300, the BF16 Muse Spark checkpoint runs TP8 across two nodes of one NVL72 rack. Custom all-reduce v2 supports a multi-node group when all ranks share one NVLink clique, but only if PyTorch's caching allocator is VMM-backed (`custom_all_reduce_v2.py`). The cookbook recipe does not enable that, so the server logs "CustomAllreduce is disabled because this process group spans across nodes" and every decode all-reduce goes through NCCL. At batch size 1 that is 4.4 ms of a 10.0 ms decode step.

Depends on [#45422](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45422): the GB300 BF16 recipe needs that flag to start.

## Modifications

The gb300 bf16 cell of `docs/src/snippets/configs/meta-models/muse-spark.jsx` sets `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`, with a two-line comment that explains why. Custom all-reduce v2 then handles the TP8 group, and the fused MoE finalize + all-reduce turns on as well. There are no code changes. The other cells are unchanged, because single-node groups (B300, B200, NVFP4) already use custom all-reduce

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K via sgl-eval (1319 questions, temperature 0, reasoning effort xhigh, max tokens 8192, 8 runs per side): 93.65% before and 93.55% after. The paired difference is -0.10 pt, with a 95% CI of [-0.86, +0.65]. Greedy one-token replay matches exactly

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Setup: 2x GB300 nodes, BF16, TP8/EP8, layer-norm SP + MegaMoE, 64 requests per point, two independent jobs per side. "Before" is the recipe with #45422's flag; the two unchanged-recipe jobs agree within 0.6%

| Workload | ITL before | ITL after | Speedup | Output throughput |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1K in / 1K out, C1 | 10.5 ms | 6.3 ms | 1.65x | +65% |
| 1K in / 1K out, C8 | 16.8 ms | 12.6 ms | 1.33x | +32% |
| 8K in / 1K out, C1 | 10.5 ms | 6.4 ms | 1.65x | +64% |
| 8K in / 1K out, C8 | 16.3 ms | 12.1 ms | 1.33x | +31% |

TTFT is unchanged

Tested on GB300 only, which is the only cell this PR changes. Measurements used the recipe's High Throughput form (speculative decoding off) without HiCache. The default Low Latency form uses the same all-reduce path, but this change was not measured there separately.

Compatibility:

- On GB300 nodes that do not share one NVLink domain, the fabric-clique check in `can_use_custom_all_reduce_v2` fails. Custom all-reduce then stays disabled exactly as before, and the server keeps using NCCL; the setting only changes PyTorch's allocator mode
- Two known incompatibilities with expandable segments do not apply to this recipe:
  - Mooncake with `MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL=efa`: the cookbook's GB300 PD mode transfers over NVLink
  - The weight-cache daemon process
- The combination with PD disaggregation was not tested

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`

title: [Fix] [AMD] imports: Skip import-time device probes when no GPU is visible
author: Arist12
body:
## Motivation

On a ROCm build of torch, `torch.version.hip` is set whether or not the process can see a GPU. Several sglang modules query the device at import time on the HIP path, so a ROCm process without a visible GPU (a CPU-only worker, a router, CPU unit tests) dies while importing `sglang.srt`:

```bash
$ docker run --rm -e HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES= -e SGLANG_USE_AITER=0 <rocm image> python -c "import sglang.srt.layers.quantization"
  File ".../sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/fp8_kernel.py", line 102, in <module>
    if is_fp8_fnuz():
  File ".../sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/fp8_kernel.py", line 98, in is_fp8_fnuz
    return "gfx94" in torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).gcnArchName
RuntimeError: No CUDA GPUs are available
```

The CUDA path does not have this problem: `is_cuda()` already requires `torch.cuda.is_available()`, so the CUDA arch checks return False on a machine with no visible device.

## Modifications

- `srt/utils/common.py`: `is_hip()` also requires `torch.cuda.is_available()`, like `is_cuda()` and the platform layer's `_is_rocm_available()`. `is_gfx95_supported`, `is_gfx942_supported` and `is_gfx1250_supported` check `is_hip()` instead of `torch.version.hip`. In a process with no visible GPU, the `_is_hip`-guarded device queries and aiter imports that run at import time (`is_fp8_fnuz`, `ON_GFX950`, `CUDA_CAPABILITY`, ...) are then skipped, as the `_is_cuda`-guarded ones are on CUDA.
- `kernels/ops/attention/rocm_mla_decode_rope.py`: drop the local `is_hip()`, which asked Triton's active driver at import ("0 active drivers" without a GPU), and use `sglang.srt.utils.is_hip` like the rest of the kernels.

With a GPU visible, `is_hip()` is True as before, so every caller gets the same value; CUDA and CPU builds stop at `torch.version.hip is not None`. `torch.cuda.is_available()` does not run torch's CUDA lazy init, and `import sglang` already calls it (in the platform checks), so HIP is not touched earlier than before. Without a GPU, a ROCm process takes the paths a CUDA process without a GPU takes: `is_hip()`, `is_cuda_alike()` and the gfx probes are False, and `fp8_dtype` / `FP8_E4M3_MAX` are the `float8_e4m3fn` values.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: with a GPU visible, `is_hip()` and every value derived from it are unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Add unit tests: `TestHipProbes` in `test/registered/unit/utils/test_common.py` (CPU).

## Testing

`python -m pytest test/registered/unit/utils/test_common.py`, CPU torch 2.11.0:

- main + the new test: `test_returns_false_without_querying_the_device` fails for all four probes (`is_hip()` returns True, each gfx probe raises `RuntimeError: No CUDA GPUs are available`).
- this PR: 13 passed, 2 skipped, 8 subtests passed.

GPU-less import check: 22 `sglang.srt` / `sglang.kernels` modules, each imported in a fresh interpreter, in `rocm/sgl-dev:miles-rocm10-mi35x-20261019` with no GPU device (`HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=`), aiter main (includes ROCm/aiter#6738). The list includes `layers.quantization`, `model_executor.model_runner`, `managers.scheduler`, `entrypoints.http_server`, `entrypoints.engine` and `models.qwen3_5`. 7/22 import on main (the rest stop at `is_fp8_fnuz`, `is_gfx95_supported` or `is_gfx1250_supported`), 22/22 with this PR, for `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` and `=0`.

I also imported every module under `srt/models`, `srt/layers`, `srt/managers`, `srt/entrypoints` and `kernels/ops` (1646 modules) the same way, with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`. On main, 681 fail at a device query. With this PR, no module that imports on main fails, and 2 still query the device at import: `kernels/ops/diffusion/norm/norm_triton.py` (fails the same way with CPU-only torch) and `kernels/ops/attention/unified_attention_3d_mtp.py` (imports `e4m3_dtype` from aiter, which derives it from the GPU arch; no module imports it at import time). The other failures are missing optional packages, NPU/XPU-only modules, import paths that current aiter does not have, and models that fail the same way with CPU-only torch (Mamba, DBRX, XVERSE MoE).

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dspark: Move the host work between DSv4.1 decode graphs into the graphs for the megakernel path
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash low-latency decode on GB300 (TP4, DSpark speculative decoding). With the NVIDIA megakernel plugin enabled (`--enable-nvidia-megakernel`), the GPU part of each decode step gets short enough that SGLang's host-side work between graphs (input preparation, verify metadata, accept bookkeeping, KV commits) becomes a large share of the step. This PR moves that work into the existing CUDA graphs, into fewer launches, or off the critical path.

Most changes are behind environment flags that default to off. Two DSpark-only changes are on by default: the draft sampling-param restaging (1) and the draft runner's metadata prep through the glue graph where it applies (2). The two changes that reach beyond DSpark are opt-in: the MoE output-shape fix (3, `SGLANG_OPT_MXFP4_DEFERRED_FINALIZED_SHAPE`) and the CUDA graph fill fast paths (7, `SGLANG_OPT_CUDA_GRAPH_FILL_FAST_PATH`).

## Modifications

One commit per change:

1. **DSpark draft:** restage the draft graph's sampling params only when they change.
2. **DSpark draft runner:** prepare its attention metadata through the glue graph.
3. **MXFP4 trtllm-gen MoE** (`SGLANG_OPT_MXFP4_DEFERRED_FINALIZED_SHAPE`): pass the finalized output shape on deferred-finalize calls above 32 rows, so decode batches hit the tuned tactic instead of the default tile. Off keeps main's 97-384-row window.
4. **Fused static accept tail** (`SGLANG_DSPARK_FUSED_ACCEPT_TAIL`): the static greedy accept and its bookkeeping in one kernel.
5. **One-launch step inputs** (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_PREPARE_INPUTS_ONCE`, `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_MID_FOLD`): the step inputs in one launch; the verify ids come from the draft graph's tail.
6. **Deferred draft context-KV commit** (`SGLANG_DSPARK_DEFER_CONTEXT_KV`): the static verify's draft context-KV commit moves to the next draft graph.
7. **CUDA graph replay fill fast paths** (`SGLANG_OPT_CUDA_GRAPH_FILL_FAST_PATH`): skip the padding reset of an unpadded fill; copy one dense integer dtype pair with one foreach launch.
8. **Target verify metadata through the glue graph** (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_TARGET_VERIFY_METADATA_GLUE`).
9. **Engram history commit and block accept lengths inside the verify graph** (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_POST_FORWARD_CUDA_GRAPH`).
10. **Draft graph metadata on a side stream** (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_DRAFT_PREP_FORK`).
11. **Seq lens and bonus relayed from the verify graph** (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_POST_FOLD`).
12. **The deferred context KV projected inside the verify graph**, so that only its stores are deferred.
13. **Simulated bonus:** reads the shared accept length as a stride-0 view. Simulated acceptance only.
14. **The deferred commit's staging in one launch** (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_ONE_LAUNCH_COMMIT_STAGE`).
15. **Target verify metadata built beside the draft graph** (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_TARGET_METADATA_EARLY`; enabled only when the runner's conditions hold, including the metadata glue graph).
16. **A pre-planned verify replay skips its input re-copies** (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_SKIP_PREFILLED_INPUTS`).
17. **Skip the replay ForwardBatch view** once the metadata glue graph is captured (`SGLANG_OPT_SKIP_GLUED_REPLAY_VIEW`).
18. **Draw the simulated acceptance before the draft launch** (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_SIM_DRAW_AHEAD`). Simulated acceptance only.
19. **Block-wise rejection sampling for the sampled verify accept** (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_BLOCKWISE_REJECTION`).
20. **A CUDA graph for the static verify's temperature-sampling accept** (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_SAMPLING_ACCEPT_GRAPH`): the sampling accept, its TP broadcast and the KV / engram commits replay as one graph launch.

## Accuracy Tests

GB300, TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, megakernel plugin on, all flags above on, real acceptance (commands under Reproduce below):

| check | all 20 commits on (incl. 19-20) | commits 19-20 off |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K-200 c8, greedy | 196 / 200, accept length 4.26 | 198 / 200, accept length 4.29 |
| GSM8K-200 c8, temperature 1.0 | 198 / 200, accept length 4.17 | 196 / 200, accept length 4.07 |
| needle at ~155K tokens | 26 / 27 | 24 / 27 |

Both commits were confirmed active in the first run (block-wise rejection on sampled verifies, the sampling-accept region captured, 4 / 4 ranks). The needle test varies between 22 and 27 / 27 from run to run on identical code.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GB300, TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. AgentX (InferenceX agentic traces), concurrency 1, 3,600 s, synthetic acceptance 3.51 with the stock accept sampling (the simulated-acceptance shortcut is reverted in every arm). All arms run on SGLang main `f0b65907227` with the same image and settings, and are compared on the same 220 requests. TPS/User = 1 / ITL.

| configuration | TPS/User P50 | TPS/User P90 | decode step p50 (> 256K) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 694.0 | 676.1 | 5.06 ms |
| main + this PR (commits 1-18) | 709.7 (+2.3%) | 694.1 (+2.7%) | 4.95 ms |
| main + megakernel plugin (sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega#18, default slots) | 762.2 (+9.8%) | 717.4 (+6.1%) | 4.57 ms |
| main + this PR (commits 1-18) + plugin (#18, 42 slots) | 952.0 (+37.2%) | 902.2 (+33.4%) | 3.66 ms |
| main + this PR (all 20 commits) + plugin (#18, 42 slots) | 995.7 (+43.5%) | 972.8 (+43.9%) | 3.54 ms |

Rows with this PR were measured with the changes listed above enabled, including `SGLANG_OPT_MXFP4_DEFERRED_FINALIZED_SHAPE=1` and `SGLANG_OPT_CUDA_GRAPH_FILL_FAST_PATH=1` (on by default at measurement time). With the plugin held fixed, this PR adds +30.6% P50 / +35.6% P90 (rows 3 and 5). Rows 4 and 5 also enable three opt-in plugin slots. Without the plugin, the host work this PR removes is hidden behind the longer GPU step, so the PR alone moves little. Rows 1-3 repeat on a second cluster within 0.3% at P50.

Known interaction: with `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` and `NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1` set in the environment, the deferred context-KV commit (`SGLANG_DSPARK_DEFER_CONTEXT_KV`) adds a 45-105 ms stall before the last streamed token of requests above 256K tokens (87 / 209 such requests in one AgentX run). The stall grows with context length. With both NCCL variables at 0, no request stalls (0 / 209) and P90 rises 4.5%. The table above was measured without these variables.

### Reproduce

**Code and setup.** One GB300 node (4 GPUs), image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261020-ab580b2e`, model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (revision `df42c109f1d`). Every tree is on `main` at `f0b65907227` with #45421 reverted (`git revert 7d9bc104932`): under `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` that commit skips the accept sampling on CUDA.

| tree | rows |
|---|---|
| `f0b65907227` + the revert | Speed 1 and 3 |
| commits 1-18 on the same base (YAMY1234/sglang `98891329ced`) | Speed 2 and 4 |
| all 20 commits on the same base (YAMY1234/sglang `227d2a4934e`) | Speed 5, Accuracy |

The current head carries the same commits on a newer main plus review fixes. On it, also set `SGLANG_OPT_MXFP4_DEFERRED_FINALIZED_SHAPE=1` and `SGLANG_OPT_CUDA_GRAPH_FILL_FAST_PATH=1` (commits 3 and 7 had no switch when measured). Plugin for Speed 3-5 and Accuracy: sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega `547bf4486e9`, installed over the image's copy with `pip install --no-deps -e .`; it stays inactive without `--enable-nvidia-megakernel`.

**Server (Speed Tests).**

```bash
# all rows
export SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC=rng,-dspark-accept-sample
export SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1 SGLANG_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE_LAYOUT=per_rank
export SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MEGA_MHC_PREFILL=1
export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.51 SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token
export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 SGLANG_DSV41_REASONING_EFFORT=high SGLANG_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=900
# rows 2, 4 and 5: this PR's switches
export SGLANG_DSPARK_FUSED_ACCEPT_TAIL=1 SGLANG_DSPARK_DEFER_CONTEXT_KV=1 \
  SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_PREPARE_INPUTS_ONCE=1 SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_MID_FOLD=1 \
  SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_POST_FOLD=1 SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_DRAFT_PREP_FORK=1 \
  SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_ONE_LAUNCH_COMMIT_STAGE=1 SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_SKIP_PREFILLED_INPUTS=1 \
  SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_SIM_DRAW_AHEAD=1 SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_TARGET_VERIFY_METADATA_GLUE=1 \
  SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_TARGET_METADATA_EARLY=1 SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_POST_FORWARD_CUDA_GRAPH=1 \
  SGLANG_OPT_SKIP_GLUED_REPLAY_VIEW=1
# row 5 also
export SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_BLOCKWISE_REJECTION=1 SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_SAMPLING_ACCEPT_GRAPH=1
# rows 4 and 5: the plugin's 39 default slots + target_lm_head, hop_b_quad_trigger, lm_head_pinned_tactic
export SGLANG_NVIDIA_MEGAKERNEL_SLOTS=hop_a,moe,gate,attn,embed,two_shot,markov,draft_lm_head,aux_mean_stats,gate_wide,shared_ll,hop_a_batch2,engram,attn_qkv_a,attn_qkv_a_bf16,index_q_mxfp8_in,attn_indexer,hc_prenorm,hop_b,hop_b_wide,early_trigger,hop_b_start_trigger,draft,draft_moe,draft_gate,draft_tail,draft_post,draft_seam,draft_attn,draft_qfront,draft_wo_a,draft_swapab,draft_qkv_a,draft_prenorm,draft_qkv_a_ll,draft_wo_b_ll,sched_ahead,req_pos_once,kv_before_wait,target_lm_head,hop_b_quad_trigger,lm_head_pinned_tactic

python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash path> \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --trust-remote-code --tp 4 --ep-size 1 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --context-length 1048576 --max-running-requests 1 \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay \
  --dsv4-attn-backend flashmla --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable \
  --cuda-graph-bs-prefill 128 256 512 1024 2048 3072 4096 6144 8192 --prefill-decode-interval 0 \

# rows 3-5 add --enable-nvidia-megakernel
```

**AgentX client** (SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX `ea0db0384`, `benchmarks/srt_agentic.sh`, run with `CONC=1 DURATION=3600`):

TPS/User P50 / P90 = 1 / p50 and 1 / p90 of the per-request ITL in `profile_export.jsonl` (profiling phase, failed requests dropped). Every row is read on the same 220 requests, matched by conversation and turn; over each whole run (391-492 requests) the values are within 0.8% of the table. Decode step p50 (> 256K) comes from TP0's `Decode batch` lines with one running request: accept length / gen throughput, lines above 262,144 tokens.

**Accuracy Tests.** Tree `227d2a4934e`, the plugin with the 42 slots above, real acceptance (no `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_*`), the server args above with `--max-running-requests 256`. The two columns differ only in `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_BLOCKWISE_REJECTION` and `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_SAMPLING_ACCEPT_GRAPH` (1 vs 0). These runs used image `nightly-dev-cu13-20261012-e6072935` with FlashInfer 0.7.2 and sglang-kernel 0.4.10, the versions in the image above.
- GSM8K-200: the first 200 `openai/gsm8k` (main) test questions, 5-shot from the first five train examples, DeepSeek-V4.1 chat format with thinking off, sent to `/generate` with `max_new_tokens` 512 and 8 requests in flight, temperature 0.0 or 1.0. title: [Perf] moe: Preserve Marlin workspace and route-count budgets
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #45681
* #45917
* __->__ #45462
* #45916
* #45915

## Motivation

An expert ID of `-1` represents valid padding, including without expert parallelism. Reusing Marlin projection storage can expose stale values for those routes; clearing the entire allocation adds work to valid routing. Muse also needs its gate/up and down projections to share the original workspace budget.

## Changes

- Reuse one Muse projection workspace sized for `M * topk * max(2I, H)`. Finalization predicates inactive routes before reading payloads or scores, including poisoned inactive values, and preserves the existing product-rounding boundary.
- Add opt-in `zero_inactive_output` to native Marlin. Down projections complete inactive destinations within the existing kernel, including public `no_combine` output. The default preserves caller-owned inactive rows; active GEMM math, atomics and reduction choices stay unchanged.
- Let owned alignment producers optionally publish `[padded_token_count, inactive_prefix_blocks]` in one count allocation. An explicit consumer flag selects the packed read and existing compressed sorted scheduling. Scalar/external producers keep the checked fallback; EP keeps its generic path. Empty inputs, dirty allocation tails and graph replay retain defined count semantics.
- Preserve the upstream scratch callback ABI and accept scalar or one-element packed-router counts through a storage-sharing view. Ordinary Marlin and Muse opt into the count fact only with producers that actually publish it.

Review the alignment/count contract first, then native output completion, Muse workspace/finalization and the registered regressions. LoRA projection changes belong to #45681.

- Keep paired inactive-prefix counts independent of optional expert-map capacity completion, including combined-option graph replay coverage.

## CI cadence

The complete Marlin GEMM, inactive-route, LoRA and Muse matrix now runs in opt-in `extra-a-test-1-gpu-large`. Base CI retains the routing, alignment and packed-top-k checks.

Across the stack, six existing CUDA file registrations move from base CI to extra/nightly, removing 854 estimated GPU-seconds from the default gate (registration estimates, not a measured wall-time saving). All test bodies, cases, inputs, assertions and tolerances are unchanged. Full before/after discovery validates 2,535 files and 3,077 registrations, with every moved file selected in its enabled destination suite. Configured hooks pass; native tests were not rerun for this registration-only update.

## Validation

- At integrated `e6670af1ad`, the focused native Marlin/LoRA route suite passes 14 tests on 1× B300 with the pinned providers, including changing padded routes and output completion.

- Two additional direct Marlin output-ownership configurations did not complete within a 600-second cold-compilation budget on B300. No result is claimed for that extended run; it is separate from the completed route replay and producer-contract checks.

- At integrated `e6670af1ad`, the alignment suite passes 89 tests on 1× H200 and 1× B300, covering count publication, signed IDs, complete expert-map capacity and combined options during graph replay. The GGUF native-entry suite passes 7 tests on B300 with sglang-kernel 0.4.10. H200 uses PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 for the source-local JIT producer; this is not full native H200 GGUF admission.

- Configured pre-commit hooks pass. 1× NVIDIA H200 native ownership, count, packed-router and Muse tests passed on the pre-rebase implementation; these are operator checks, not full-model serving results.
- On the rebased composed tree `f3a1165`, 1× NVIDIA B300 passed 39 selected alignment-count cases and the scratch/count-pair CUDA graph replay probe. The selected Marlin/Muse run exceeded its 480-second cap before completion; it is **not** reported as passed, and no B300 Marlin/Muse latency result is claimed.
- Earlier H200 Muse measurements retained the projection peak budget. Its strict M512 cross-run comparison also failed on unchanged-baseline repeats; a diagnostic using identical routing metadata produced bitwise matching projections/final output. This does not establish unrestricted numerical equivalence.

CUDA validation used PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0 and sgl-kernel 0.4.10. Broader shapes, distributed communication and native MUSA execution remain outside this evidence.

## Rebase validation (before the CI registration fix)

This five-PR stack was rebased without conflicts onto main `8b9f72417f`. All five patches retain their stable patch IDs relative to the preceding published stack; the newer main commits do not touch the stack's changed files. The existing removal of the unused `materialized_routing` parameter and its three call-site arguments in #45917 is preserved.

Each rebased PR commit passed its configured pre-commit checks independently. The final stack passes `git diff --check`, and all 72 changed Python files parse successfully. CPU test suites, native GPU tests and performance measurements were not rerun for this rebase. Previously reported results, including those at integrated `e6670af1ad`, remain evidence for those earlier revisions with their stated limits.

## Prior CI registration fix

The GGUF weighting test now uses the existing `nightly-musa-1-gpu` suite with `nightly=True`; at that revision, its CUDA kernel-unit registration was unchanged. The previous nonexistent MUSA suite caused global registry validation to fail before CPU, CUDA and AMD tests could run.

The original collection failure was reproduced. Full registration collection and suite validation now pass on the GGUF component (2,533 files / 3,075 registrations) and the integrated stack (2,535 files / 3,077 registrations), including enabled MUSA nightly and CUDA selection. Configured pre-commit checks pass for the corrected test. This update changes one registration line and is propagated through the existing stack.

## CPU CI follow-up

Run [39935811691](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39935811691) exposed an upstream Flux2 import test registered in the CPU suite, whose environment lacks the diffusion dependencies. The import chain also queries the active GPU. #45915 moves that check to the existing CUDA diffusion unit suite, which installs those dependencies, while retaining its XPU registration and the real subprocess check that blocks Intel Triton imports. This registration fix is propagated through the stack.

The Flux2 import check passes on 1× NVIDIA B300 with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0 and Diffusers 0.37.0; its five Intel-XPU numerical cases are skipped on CUDA and were not rerun on XPU. Full integrated registry collection validates 2,535 files / 3,077 registrations, including the enabled diffusion/XPU selections and the preceding GGUF MUSA fix. Configured checks pass for the changed files. Only three test files change across this follow-up; production code is unchanged. A fresh full CI result is not claimed.

## Merge preparation

Rebased this component onto main `e6451c1a95` for squash merge. The preceding stack components are already merged into main; only this component is replayed here. No test suites or performance measurements were rerun for this merge. Earlier validation sections describe their named revisions.

title: [Fix] attention: Restore block pointers on Triton 3.9 for FLA kernels
author: akhilg-nv
body:
[by Claude Code]

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Fixes #45426.

The `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-cu134-*` images from 2026-10-20 ship torch `2.15.0.dev20261005+cu134`, which pins **Triton `3.9.0+gitaad2a60d`**. That Triton includes triton-lang/triton#10833, which removed block pointers: `tl.make_block_ptr` and `tl.advance` now raise `NotImplementedError` at compile time. The vendored FLA kernels (GDN / KDA: Qwen3.5, Qwen3-Next, Kimi linear attention) use block pointers about 200 times, so these models fail at their first kernel compile. Qwen3.5 dies at prefill CUDA-graph capture in `l2norm_fwd_kernel`.

The MiniMax sparse attention kernels had the same problem, plus a Triton 3.9 autotune-key error. #46135 has since ported them off block pointers and fixed the key on main, so this PR now covers only FLA.

The Triton 3.8.0 release still has block pointers (lowered in its Python frontend to plain pointer loads), so the regular images (torch 2.14.1 + Triton 3.8.0) and Triton 3.7.1 are unaffected.

As in #40805, this is a guarded compatibility shim with a TODO, not a port.

## Modifications

- New `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/triton_block_ptr_compat.py`. It does something only when `triton.language` has no `advance` (the Triton build removed block pointers). It then defines `tl.make_block_ptr` / `tl.advance` on top of a small Triton aggregate, and wraps `tl.load` / `tl.store` so they accept `boundary_check` and `padding_option` for it. The lowering follows Triton 3.8.0's own frontend implementation: int64 shape / strides / offsets, per-dimension coordinates broadcast to the block, a bounds mask only on the checked dimensions, and `padding_option` mapped to `other`. On Triton builds that still have block pointers the module does nothing, so behaviour there is unchanged.
- The shim is imported from `fla/utils.py` and `fla/fused_norm_gate.py`. Every module that uses block pointers (the FLA kernels, including the XPU copies) imports one of them.
- TODO: drop the shim once the kernels are ported off block pointers, as upstream FLA did in fla-org/flash-linear-attention#1062.

Alternatives considered:
- Port every call site to plain pointers. Upstream FLA did this in fla-org/flash-linear-attention#1062, a diff of +6088/-5512 lines over 88 files.
- Use tensor descriptors. They can't express the transposed and strided 1-D blocks these kernels load, and they need 16-byte alignment.

## Accuracy Tests

These runs predate the merge of #46135. The MiniMax sparse tests below exercised the shim on MiniMax's old block-pointer kernels, which main no longer has.

**Unit tests**: FLA and MiniMax sparse kernel tests on one B300, run in the `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` image's tree (ab580b2e) with this patch applied. Each Triton version used a fresh Triton cache. The 3.7.1 and 3.9 builds were put on `PYTHONPATH`, ahead of the image's own Triton 3.8.0.

| Triton | Shim | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 3.7.1 (PyPI) | inactive | 143 passed, 2 skipped |
| 3.8.0 (image) | inactive | 142 passed, 2 failed\*, 2 skipped |
| 3.9.0+gitaad2a60d (torch nightly pin) | active | 142 passed, 2 failed\*, 2 skipped |

\* The same two `TestKDAVerifyDecodeParity` bit-exactness checks fail on Triton 3.8.0 **without** this patch and pass on 3.7.1. The failure is pre-existing and not related to this change.

Files: `test_chunk_gated_delta_rule.py`, `test_kda_kernels.py`, `test_gdn_prefill_layout.py`, `test_fused_norm_gate_strided.py`, `test_kda_gate_beta_cumsum.py`, `test_kda_track_state.py`, `test_minimax_sparse_decode_paged_tile.py`, `test_minimax_decode_topk_page_table.py`.

MiniMax sparse tests that sit at their pre-#45112 path in that tree (`test_flash_with_topk_idx.py`, `test_sparse_gqa.py`; these cover the decode kernels, including the ones that use `tl.advance`): 74 passed on Triton 3.9 + shim and on Triton 3.8.0. `test_minimax_sparse_fp8_attn_gemm.py`, taken from main: 10 passed on Triton 3.9 + shim and on Triton 3.8.0.

The same test list also ran natively in the `nightly-cu134-20261020-306ccf6` image (torch 2.15 + Triton 3.9) on GB200. That run found that zero-padded fp8 loads failed to compile (`cannot cast int32 to fp8e4nv`); the second commit fixes it and is what the `test_minimax_sparse_fp8_attn_gemm.py` result above covers. Everything else passed: 220 tests.

**Generated code**: I compiled test kernels to TTIR on a CPU-only machine with fresh caches. They cover 1-D, 2-D and 3-D blocks, transposed `order`, strided 1-D blocks, `padding_option="zero"`, partial `boundary_check`, and `tl.advance` inside a loop. Triton 3.9 + this shim emits the same TTIR as Triton 3.8.0's own block-pointer lowering. The one difference is the lowering of an fp16-to-bf16 `.to()` cast that isn't on a block-pointer path.

**End to end**: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (hybrid GDN) on one GB200, TP1, `--reasoning-parser qwen3`. sgl-eval GSM8K, n=200, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, max_tokens 16384, top_k 20 from the model's generation config.

| Image | Triton | This PR | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nightly-cu134-20261020-306ccf6` | 3.9.0+gitaad2a60d | no | server dies at the first prefill: `NotImplementedError: Block pointers have been removed` (#45426) |
| `nightly-cu134-20261020-306ccf6` | 3.9.0+gitaad2a60d | yes | 80.5% |
| `dev-cu13` | 3.8.0 | no | 82.0% |

The 1.5-point gap is within sampling noise; the standard error at n=200 is about 2.8 points.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

With Triton 3.8.0 or older the shim is inactive and no kernel changes. With Triton 3.9 the shim produces the same IR as Triton 3.8.0's lowering of these block pointers, so I don't expect a speed change against 3.8.0. Not benchmarked.

title: [Perf] scheduler: Plan hybrid Mamba extend batches without host-device syncs
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

With the overlap scheduler, every implicit host-device sync in extend planning waits for the forward that is already running, so the scheduler cannot get ahead of the GPU. On hybrid Mamba models with `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer` or `extra_buffer_lazy`, planning one extend batch synced several times per batch and once more per request. Counted with `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode` on the extend scheduling path:

- `HybridReqToTokenPool.alloc` indexed two device mappings with a Python list (a pageable copy each).
- `_mamba_radix_cache_v2_req_prepare_for_extend` read each request's ping-pong slot id with `.item()`, and `prepare_for_extend` then copied the ids, mask and seqlens back to the device from pageable memory.
- The lazy strategy's "is the other ping-pong entry free" checks, the ping-pong frees (`free_mamba_cache`, streaming-session release) and `kv_mamba_slots` all read `-1` flags off the device buffer.
- Clearing a ping-pong entry assigned the Python int `-1` into a CUDA tensor, a pageable copy that blocks the host until the stream drains.
- `MambaPool.clear_slots` and the ReplaySSM fresh-row reset wrote zeros through list or expanded-tensor indexing.
- `_get_multimodal_mask` used `torch.isin`, which switches to a `unique()`-based path (and syncs on its count) once there are enough placeholders.

#43637 removes two of these sites (the list index in `alloc` and the device-side track indices in `prepare_for_extend`) by keeping per-request device views; this PR covers the same two sites with a single gather from the pool mapping, plus the remaining ones above, so the two overlap on those hunks.

## Modifications

- `ReqKvInfo.mamba_ping_pong_empty` mirrors on the host which entries of the ping-pong buffer hold no slot. `_alloc_ping_pong_buffer` sets it with the buffer, `set_mamba_ping_pong_slot` flips it on every write, and every reader of `buf != -1` (lazy prepare in `schedule_batch.py`, the batch result processor, `free_mamba_cache`, `StreamingSession` release, `kv_mamba_slots`) reads the flags instead. `free_mamba_cache` frees every surviving entry by position, with no device mask. The MLX auxiliary-state pool and model runner set and clear the flags with the buffer like the CUDA pool.
- `prepare_for_extend` records each request's track *position* (`_MambaRadixCacheV2TrackEntry.track_position`) and gathers the slot ids on the device from `req_index_to_mamba_ping_pong_track_buffer_mapping` with one advanced index (`_gather_mamba_track_indices`); `set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs` uses the same gather. Track positions, mask and seqlens are staged pinned and copied `non_blocking`.
- `HybridReqToTokenPool.alloc` writes its two mappings through a device row index (`async_h2d`); ReplaySSM fresh rows reset through `index_fill_`; `MambaPool.clear_slots` zeroes with `index_fill_` on every branch, the fused conv kernel staying the fast path; `set_mamba_ping_pong_slot` clears an entry with `fill_(-1)`.
- `UnifiedMambaPool` sets `replayssm_spec_write_pos` like `MambaPool`, so `alloc()` reads it as a plain attribute instead of `getattr`.
- `embed_mm_inputs` sorts the placeholder ids once on the host and `_get_multimodal_mask` looks them up with `searchsorted`; an empty placeholder tensor is an assertion.

Behaviour is unchanged: the same slots are tracked, freed and cleared; only where the bookkeeping is read and how the writes reach the device change.

## Tests

New and updated unit tests (all CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`):

- `test_mm_chunked_embedding_unit.py`: the `searchsorted` mask equals the broadcast compare and `torch.isin` on host-sorted placeholders, including a repeated placeholder and int32 ids, at sizes on both sides of `torch.isin`'s sort threshold.
- `test_unified_tri_pool.py`: over a CPU unified pool, the mapping rows equal the request buffers after `alloc()`, donate and set, and the device gather equals the per-request `.item()` reads it replaces; the hand-built kv fixture sets the flags with the buffer.
- `test_mamba_checkpoint_depth.py`: the track position is taken before the ping-pong swap, for both starting positions.
- `test_batch_result_processor_mamba_boundary.py`: calls the production `set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs` with no pinning shim; the boundary fixture sets the flags.

Run locally on CPU: the four files above plus `test_mamba_capacity.py`, `test_batch_result_processor_spec_grammar.py`, `test_mamba_unittest.py` and `test_unified_radix_cache_core.py` (the other callers that build ping-pong fixtures) pass.

title: [Perf] cuda-graph: Capture FlashInfer KDA prefill with context parallelism
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

FlashInfer KDA breaks out of each prefill graph, leaving every KDA layer eager, including with context parallelism enabled.

## Modifications

- Capture FlashInfer KDA using per-bucket, per-layer `RecurrentKDAPrefillWrapper` plans. Refresh sequence lengths, state indices and radix-cache checkpoint mappings before replay; guard empty padded sequences and handle small buckets whose sequence-slot count would otherwise select decode.
- Size KDA graph metadata from global `extend_num_tokens`, since CP positions can describe only the local shard. Keep the selected FlashInfer backend; installations without the experimental wrapper retain the eager graph break.
- Extend the GPU regression to FlashInfer, multi-request replay, CP global token capacity, radix checkpoints, unused state slots and small buckets. Run it on Blackwell CI.

## Validation

The GPU results below were collected at `8f7d7cc9c7`, before restoring the original `memory_hook.py`. This PR no longer changes the MLA/DSA capture default (2048); reproducing the earlier 16384-token run requires an explicit capture-maximum override. GPU tests were not rerun for this exact restoration; pre-commit and base-file equality checks passed.

On `glm53-dev` (4× GB300):

- GPU KDA graph tests: **9 passed, 20 subtests passed**. The new small-bucket regression reproduced the original capture failure before the fix.
- Linear-attention configuration, FlashInfer adapter and Mamba checkpoint metadata tests: **23 passed, 113 subtests passed**.
- GLM-5.3-Flash + DFlash2, using `test_glm53_flash_cp.py` settings: **GSM8K 473/500 (94.6%)**, average speculative acceptance **4.862**, both image-input checks passed. Batched four-request outputs match individual requests exactly.
- Capture maximum in that validation run: **16384**, 74 prefill buckets captured successfully, approximately **31.98 GiB / 66.62 s** on TP0, with `mem_fraction_static=0.75`.
- Pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.

**Integration scope:** GLM CP serving still depends on open #43182. The end-to-end run used this PR's `43aebae1e0` base plus this change and a temporary three-way integration of #43182 at `2aa855c0e8`. Those dependency changes are not included in this PR. The devbox has FlashInfer 0.7.1 with the experimental wrapper, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 and Triton 3.8.0; the wrapper is capability-gated because it is not present in every FlashInfer installation.

## Profiling

`bench_serving`: concurrency 4, ISL 1024, OSL 10, 160 requests, 20 target steps. **160/160 requests succeeded**, all requested lengths verified. The profile contains 7 prefill steps (actual scheduler batch sizes 1–3) and 13 verify steps, plus draft work.

All four rank traces confirm **34 FlashInfer KDA prefill kernels per prefill are associated with `cudaGraphLaunch` and nonzero graph IDs; zero KDA prefill kernels run eagerly**. Each prefill has **23 graph launches**, versus 57 in the earlier trace with 34 KDA breaks. FlashInfer's planned path uses one core kernel per layer; the earlier eager path used a prep/chain pair. This is graph-replay evidence, not a controlled throughput comparison. All four traces and logs were downloaded and their SHA-256 hashes verified.
