title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] speculative: Move the host work between Qwen3.5 MTP decode graphs into the graphs (1/2)
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (NVFP4) low-latency decode on GB300, TP8, MTP (top-k 1, 7 draft tokens). With the NVIDIA megakernel plugin, the GPU part of a decode round gets short enough that SGLang's host work becomes the bottleneck: input staging between graphs, the verify's eager sampling and commits, and the scheduler's per-pass TP syncs. This PR moves that work into CUDA graphs, into fewer launches, or off the critical path. It is the Qwen3.5 counterpart of sgl-project/sglang#45450.

This PR contains no megakernel code. It is independent of the wiring PR, sgl-project/sglang#45266: both are based on main, and either can merge first. The plugin is sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega#20.

Every new code path is behind an environment switch that defaults to off. With all switches off, the same GPU operations run in the same order as on main; the accuracy tests below check this. Note that main's Qwen3.5 AgentX recipes (`docs/src/snippets/agentx/Qwen/qwen3.5.jsx`) already set six of these switches to `1`.

## Modifications

One commit per change. The TPS/User figures are what removing that change alone would cost on the full stack (this PR + #45266 + plugin, TP8, one request, 128K) ¹.

1. **Post-verify CUDA graphs** (`SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH`, ≈ 78 TPS/User): the EAGLE verify's sampling, acceptance and commit outputs replay as CUDA graphs, and the mamba state commit runs on a side stream. Batches a graph cannot reproduce (grammar, penalties, per-request seeds, ...) keep the eager path.
2. **Test:** the post-verify graphs match eager sampling bitwise at batch sizes up to 64.
3. **GDN extend kernels and tables for captured prefill buckets** (no switch; used by 4).
4. **GDN extend in breakable prefill graphs** (`SGLANG_ENABLE_GDN_PREFILL_GRAPH_EXTEND`): prefill no longer leaves the graph at every GDN layer. It does not affect decode; TTFT drops from 82.9 to 40.6 ms for 256-token prompts at TP4.
5. **`small_field_copy`** (`SGLANG_Q35MF_BK_VEC_COPY`, < 1 TPS/User): a JIT kernel that copies up to 16 small fields in one launch, with a 16-byte vectorized path. Item 6 uses it.
6. **Verify-round input staging** (`SGLANG_Q35MF_MKH_N3B`, `_N3C`, ≈ 19 TPS/User):
   - reuse the previous round's mamba track indices;
   - skip input copies that a pre-planned replay already made;
   - load the post-verify graphs' inputs in one launch.
7. **Chain-tree verify build and compact top-k sampling** (`SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_CHAIN_TREE`, `_SPARSE_VERIFY_SAMPLING`, ≈ 70 TPS/User):
   - a top-k 1 draft builds its verify chain without the tree mask, which TRT-LLM MHA does not read;
   - a verify whose requests all use a top-k of 2–128 samples on that support instead of the full vocabulary.
8. **Packed verify broadcast** (`SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_PACKED_VERIFY_BCAST`, ≈ 3 TPS/User): a sampled verify result reaches the TP group in one broadcast instead of three.
9. **Scheduler TP syncs through shared memory** (`SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SHM_SYNC`, `_SHM_SYNC_MULTIHOST`, `_MULTIHOST_TCP`, ≈ 121 TPS/User): the request broadcast and the HiCache ready counts go through a shared-memory table instead of gloo. Across hosts, the counts use one exchange between the host leaders.
10. **Doc:** the `environ.py` section comment names SGLang branch `nvidia/qwen35-agentx-gb300`, which reads the same switch names.

¹ Measured on an earlier head of the full stack (1,267 TPS/User at P50). Items 1, 7 and 9 are derived from host-time and Kineto measurements rather than separate runs, so the rows do not add up. Four host-side items of earlier heads were dropped: together they gave ~1.3% for 1,204 production lines.

## Accuracy Tests

GB300, real acceptance, GSM8K on a fixed 250-question subset.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| Every switch off vs main, Qwen3.5 TP8, greedy at concurrency 1 and 16 | 250 / 250 texts identical (main vs main: 250 / 250). Same 46 Triton kernels and 8 JIT modules compiled; same KV cache and memory. |
| Every switch off vs main, gpt-oss-120b + EAGLE3, TP2, HiCache on | texts differing from main: 39 / 39 (main vs main: 64 / 69); this model's greedy output varies across restarts |
| Full stack (this PR + #45266 + plugin) vs the development build | greedy 0.980 vs 0.980 (249 / 250 identical); sampled 0.976 vs 0.984; acceptance length ratio 1.000 / 0.998 |
| Full stack vs #45266 + plugin without this PR | greedy 0.980 vs 0.980 (250 / 250 identical); sampled 0.976 vs 0.988; acceptance length ratio 1.000 / 1.006 |

On CPU, the changed test files and the speculative and megakernel unit tests fail only where main fails on the same machine.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GB300, TP8 across two 4-GPU trays. Static decode of one request at 128K context with forced acceptance 4.80 (`SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=4.80`), about 1,780 rounds per server start. TPS/User = 4.80 tokens / round time. Rows 1–4 are the mean of two pairs of trays run in opposite orders. The plugin was measured at `3509187d74`, an earlier revision of sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega#20; the PR head differs only by an opt-in for more than one request, off by default.

| configuration | TPS/User P50 | TPS/User P90 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 706.4 | 700.3 |
| main + this PR | 752.8 (+6.6%) | 742.5 (+6.0%) |
| main + #45266 + plugin | 765.7 (+8.4%) | 729.6 (+4.2%) |
| main + this PR + #45266 + plugin | 1291.7 (+82.8%) | 1276.0 (+82.2%) |
| the development build (reference) ² | 1275.2 | 1249.5 |

² On a third pair of trays, row 4 reaches 101.0% of the reference at P50 at 128K, and 100.8% / 100.6% and 101.9% / 101.6% (P50 / P90) at 8K and 32K.

With the plugin fixed (rows 3 and 4), this PR adds +68.7% at P50 and +74.9% at P90.

These results were measured on main `28448a86d4`. The branch has since been rebased onto main `b57b5e2286`, where two commits differ only by an import path that sgl-project/sglang#45112 moved; the GPU checks are being repeated on the new base. Without the plugin it adds less, because main's longer GPU step hides much of the host work it removes.

On InferenceX AgentX (TP8, concurrency 11, 3,600 s, one request per server at a time), the full stack scores X 1234.57 against the development build's 1219.51 on the same trays. TPS/User is 1314.35 / 1236.99 against 1302.52 / 1230.18 (P50 / P90).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

title: [Fix] [AMD] MoE: Preserve CT FP8 Triton layout and reduction dimensions
author: lunarwhite
body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` and an explicit Triton MoE runner, compressed-tensors CHANNEL FP8 layers receive AITER-shuffled weights and lose 128 reduction elements in the non-block FP8 kernel (1024 → 896 in the regression). Both cause incorrect outputs.

## Modifications

- Shuffle CT CHANNEL FP8 weights only for an actual AITER runner.
- Match the non-block FP8 kernel's padding calculation to its existing caller when AITER is enabled.
- Add an AMD CI-registered runtime quantization test under `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/`, covering checkpoint loading, postprocessing, and numerical Triton/AITER MoE comparisons with 1- and 33-token inputs.

Related: [#41636](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41636) addresses the shuffle mechanism in `Fp8MoEMethod` block-FP8; this PR fixes the separate compressed-tensors CHANNEL path and the non-block kernel dimension calculation.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested on MI355X (gfx950), Python 3.10.12, PyTorch `2.9.1+rocm7.2.0.git7e1940d4`, HIP `7.2.26015-fc0010cf6a`, using the official image:

```
lmsysorg/sglang-rocm@sha256:8cb29fc407c2e46bdb1866c5edb91f109ac1acbbcb6905089beaa6c79b0813a2
```

Base: `9db58ab547516435b544ae050dd6c2f91b52bcf3`  
Head: `7d7d8b79eec61eda1884c54311b2580bd6159cff`

Layer controls use identical seeded weights, routing and test source, `SGLANG_MOE_PADDING=0`, isolated processes/caches, and verified import paths/hashes.

| Variant | Explicit Triton, 1 / 33 tokens | AITER, 1 / 33 tokens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base, AITER disabled | pass / pass | not run |
| Base, AITER enabled | fail / fail | pass / pass |
| Only shuffle guard | fail / fail (cosine 0.7757 / 0.8207) | pass / pass |
| Only kernel padding fix | fail / fail | pass / pass |
| Both fixes | pass / pass | pass / pass |

Both final test methods pass without errors/skips. The independent reference uses dequantized checkpoint weights and identical routing; fixed thresholds are cosine > 0.99 and relative L2 < 0.1. Controls fail numerically, establishing that both fixes are required.

title: [Perf] srt: Record on the host whether an extend batch completes a prompt
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

Model code that does extra work only on the forward that finishes a request's prompt (a head that reads the last prompt token, an output published once per request) has no host-side way to tell whether the current extend batch contains such a row. The available check is on the device: compare `extend_prefix_lens + extend_seq_lens` with `orig_seq_lens`, then `.any().item()` to decide whether to run or publish anything. That is one blocking device sync per extend forward, paid even when every row is a non-final prefill chunk.

## Modifications

- `ForwardBatch.contains_last_prefill_chunk`: a plain `bool` that `init_new` snapshots from request bookkeeping. For a non-speculative extend batch it is `True` when any request that is not a running decode row ends this chunk at `len(full_untruncated_fill_ids)`, i.e. this forward produces that request's next token. Speculative verify batches and the decode rows mixed into a chunked prefill do not count. The dataclass default stays `True`, so synthetic capture and replay batches built directly by the graph runners keep every gate open.
- `TboForwardBatchPreparer.filter_batch` copies the field to both child batches, like the other forward-level flags.
- `init_new` reads two more `Req` fields, so the stand-in request in the mamba metadata test gains `extend_end` and `full_untruncated_fill_ids`.

Why not reuse `ScheduleBatch.contains_last_prefill_chunk`: that flag is set by the scheduler for pipeline parallelism and is false only for a lone non-final chunk. The new field is derived per request when the forward batch is built, so every builder of an extend batch gets the same answer, including mixed batches and zero-token requests whose prompt-final step is their only output.

`init_new` does not mutate the `ScheduleBatch` for this; it only reads `reqs`, `decoding_reqs` and `forward_mode`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no numerics change. The field is a new host-side bool with no reader inside this repository yet; existing behaviour is unchanged.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not run: the change adds one Python loop over `batch.reqs` per extend forward and no device work.

## Checklist

- `test/registered/unit/managers/test_schedule_batch_out_of_place.py::TestForwardBatchPrefillCompletion` checks the snapshot across `NONE`/`EAGLE`/`EAGLE3`, mixed and zero-token requests, against the result processor's first-output commits, and that a later change to `req.extend_end` does not move the snapshot. Red on current main (`AttributeError: 'ForwardBatch' object has no attribute 'contains_last_prefill_chunk'`), green on this branch.
- `test/registered/unit/batch_overlap/test_tbo_filter_batch_marker.py::test_filter_batch_inherits_prefill_completion` checks both values survive `filter_batch`. Red on main, green here.
- The three touched test files pass locally on CPU: 25 tests, 130 subtests.
- `pre-commit run --files` on the five changed files passes.

title: [Perf] pd: Send prefill KV chunks without a host sync on the scheduler thread
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

On a PD prefill worker under the overlap scheduler, every KV send to the decode computed its page indices with `kv_to_page_indices`, a `.cpu()` on the schedule stream. `_apply_war_barrier` fences that stream behind the in-flight forward, so the copy returns only when that forward's reads are done: the scheduler thread waits for the previous forward on every send (twice per request: the early cached-prefix send in `run_batch` and the final send in `process_batch_result`), and the next forward launches late. With attention DP the per-batch DP sync spreads each rank's stall to its peers. This is the prefill-side counterpart of #45328.

Measured on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GB300, 10 x DEP2 prefill + 1 x DEP16 decode, Mooncake transfer, AgentX traffic at 6,400 conversations: sampling the prefill schedulers' main thread once per second over a 900 s window put 30% of its samples in that `.cpu()` and 26% launching forwards.

## Modifications

- `_send_kv_chunk` computes the page indices on the device as before, copies them into pinned host memory with `non_blocking=True`, records a CUDA event on the current (schedule) stream, and passes the host tensor plus the event to the sender. The sender needs only the length on the scheduler thread. Context-parallel transfers, which filter the indices on the host, keep the synchronous path; so do backends that do not declare `supports_host_tensor_indices`.
- `TransferKVChunk.indices_event`: the Mooncake transfer worker, which already waits on the early-send event before reading KV, waits on this event too and converts the host tensor to NumPy before any use.
- `MooncakeKVSender.send` and `MooncakeKVManager.add_transfer_request` take `indices_event`.

## Benchmarking

Same shape and client, 900 s windows, sglang main `472f0d540b` + #44623:

| | Total tok/s/GPU | p90 interactivity | p90 TTFT | Requests | Errors |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| before | 521,838 | 120.90 | 36.0 s | 151,612 | 1 |
| after | 543,328 | 122.36 | 29.3 s | 157,027 | 0 |

The scheduler thread's share in the send path went from 30% to 0% and its forward-launch share from 26% to 52%; the prefill queue fell from 27 to 8 requests per rank, and the decode's slot count became the bound.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerics change: the same page indices reach the transfer, later. 70,910 warmup and 157,027 window requests completed with 0 errors through the asynchronous path. The last chunk's state payloads (SWA window, DSA state) still read the device synchronously; they are once per request and left for a follow-up.

title: [Perf] [KDA] muse_spark: Run the one-token router GEMV on CuTe DSL
author: Waterpine
body:
## Motivation

This PR is powered by [KDA](https://github.com/NVlabs/kda) team. `MuseSpark1xRouter` computes FP32 router logits on a side stream in every MoE layer, and the MoE waits for it. At one decode token cuBLAS runs this as a split-K GEMV plus a separate reduce kernel. In NVFP4 batch-1 decode on GB300 the main stream waits 146-152 us per step (of about 5.4 ms) for the router.

## Modifications

- `kernels/ops/gemm/muse_spark_router_gemv_cutedsl.py` (new): a CuTe DSL FP32 GEMV with one launch, no split-K workspace and a fixed reduction order, so results are deterministic and differ from cuBLAS only by FP32 summation order
- `router_gemv_cute_eligible` admits FP32 inputs on SM10x GPUs with aligned rows. Muse Spark enables TF32, under which cuBLAS already runs multi-row logits as a TF32 GEMM, so only the one-token decode call moves
- `srt/models/muse_spark.py`: `MuseSpark1xRouter.forward` calls the kernel when eligible and keeps `F.linear` otherwise
- `kernels/ops/gemm/__init__.py`, `test_kernels_namespace.py`: register `gemm.muse_spark_router_gemv` in the kernel inventory
- `test_muse_spark_router_gemv_cutedsl.py` (new): FP64 reference with an FP32 error bound, 1-16 tokens, misaligned rows, other shapes, bitwise repeatability, side-stream CUDA-graph replay and the TF32 dispatch rule. Registered on H100 (fallback path) and B200 (CuTe path)

## Accuracy Tests

- 16,600 cases over 200 configurations stay within the FP32 error bound (largest error 0.5% of it); Compute Sanitizer is clean
- GSM8K (sgl-eval, 1319 questions, 8 runs per side): NVFP4 +0.27 pt (95% CI [-0.13, +0.69]), BF16 -0.08 pt ([-0.50, +0.34])

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel vs cuBLAS on GB300 at one token (hidden 8192, 256 experts), two jobs:

| Weight | cuBLAS | CuTe DSL | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cold (HBM) | 6.24 us | 4.19 us | 1.49x / 1.50x |
| warm | 4.35 us | 2.14 us | 2.03x / 2.03x |

Model, cookbook GB300 High Throughput recipe, decode-C1 mean ITL, two pairs per format:

| Format | Pair 1 | Pair 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NVFP4 (1x GB300, TP4/EP4) | 1.017x | 1.007x |
| BF16 (2x GB300, TP8/EP8) | 1.030x | 1.031x |

- No repeatable regression above 2% at any serving point in either format
- The Low Latency (DFlash) recipe never calls the kernel: its verify steps route several tokens per request (0 launches in the rank-0 profiles)
- Measured before [#45112](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45112) moved the kernel to `ops/gemm/`; on current main the tests pass on GB300, and GSM8K with the other Muse Spark changes applied shows no loss (NVFP4 over five pairs +0.00 pt, BF16 +0.19 pt)

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Perf] [AMD] vattn-asm: Split small-batch MTP verify attention over all CUs on gfx950
author: chuyeh
body:
## Motivation

At mid concurrency, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4 on MI355X decodes 1 to 4 requests at a time, and the full-attention layers run the MTP verify pass through `vattn_asm`. The kernel uses about 148 KB of LDS, so one workgroup fits on a CU, and it splits each sequence into at most 64 segments. At batch size 1 with one KV head per rank, that is 64 workgroups on 256 CUs: three quarters of the GPU is idle during long-context attention.

Also, the seg-plan cache is keyed on the `seqused_k` tensor, but `aiter_backend` builds `seq_lens + max_q_len` again in every layer. The plan is rebuilt in each full-attention layer instead of once per forward.

This PR extends the length-aware seg plan from [#39172](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39172). It lets small batches use up to one segment per CU and builds `seqused_k` once per forward. On AgentX, against a same-image control that already has #43861 and AR fusion, interactivity improves by 9% (median) and 4% (P90) at TP4 c8, and the gain fades to no measurable change at TP2 c16.

## Modifications

- `vattn_asm_gfx950/__init__.py`:
  - The segment cap goes from 64 to `num_cus` (256 on MI355X), and the seg plan also runs at batch size 1, so the segment count follows the context length.
  - Each segment has at least 16 KV tiles (256 tokens). Shorter segments cost more in fp32 partials than they save.
  - `vred.s` reduces at most 64 segments (one per lane). Above 64, a new Triton kernel `_reduce_triton` reduces with the same contract. For 64 or fewer, `vred.s` still runs.
- `aiter_backend.py`: `ForwardMetadata.verify_seqused_k` caches `seq_lens + max_q_len` per forward, so the seg-plan cache hits after the first layer. In a TP4 profile, plan launches drop from 18 to 4 per decode step.
- Tests: `test_vattn_asm_segment_plan.py` (CPU) bounds the cap by `num_cus` and adds a 2-sequence case. `test_vattn_segplan_mi35x.py` applies the 16-tile floor in the reference, also checks batch size 1, and checks that `_reduce_triton` matches `vred.s` on identical partials.


## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, InferenceX protocol (lm-eval `local-chat-completions`, 5-shot, temperature 0, `max_tokens` 16384, thinking off), strict-match. Image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261020`, `amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2` with MTP. Control is `0025f93944` + #43861; both arms use `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion --disable-aiter-allreduce-fusion-in-prefill`.

| Setup | Control | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| TP4 | 0.9773 ± 0.0041 | 0.9765 ± 0.0042 |
| TP2 | 0.9735 ± 0.0044 | 0.9757 ± 0.0042 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Kernel microbenchmarks

- MI355X, one GPU, CUDA graph replay.
- `mtp_verify_attn_fwd_asm` with 4 query tokens per sequence, 1 KV head, head_dim 256, fp8 page-16 KV cache.
- TP4 has 8 query heads per rank and TP2 has 16.
- The plan cost is spread over the layers of a forward.
- Times are in µs, baseline → this PR.

| Context per sequence | TP4 (8 q heads) | TP2 (16 q heads) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 16k | 14.3 → 13.1 (−9%) | 17.6 → 16.4 (−7%) |
| 64k | 26.7 → 18.6 (−31%) | 31.3 → 25.4 (−19%) |
| 224k | 62.7 → 30.5 (−51%) | 71.1 → 38.2 (−46%) |
| 224k x 2 | 64.1 → 47.7 (−26%) | 73.4 → 54.5 (−26%) |
| 224k + 16k | 63.3 → 33.2 (−48%) | 71.6 → 39.9 (−44%) |
| 128k + 64k + 16k + 4k | 43.5 → 30.7 (−29%) | 49.8 → 39.5 (−21%) |
| 32k x 4 | 24.3 → 23.7 (−3%) | 29.6 → 32.0 (+8%) |

Max absolute difference to the baseline output is 4.4e-4 over all points. The one slower case, four uniform short sequences at TP2 (about +2 µs), picks 128 segments and so runs the Triton reduce instead of `vred.s`.

On the decode path (q_len 1) at batch size 1, this PR is +20% at 16k context, −2% at 32k and −23% to −49% from 64k, with the plan rebuilt on every call.

### AgentX benchmark

- MI355X, one point at a time with nothing else on the node, one run per arm.
- InferenceX recipe `qwen3.5-fp4-mi355x-sglang-agentic` (MTP), image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261020`, same model as above. No KV offload, except the TP2 c16 point, which uses HiCache DRAM offload (`--hicache-size 253`, write-through).
- Client: the CI AgentX command, `aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp` on `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126_256k`, 3600 s per run, 0 failed requests in every run.
- Control: `0025f93944` + [#43861](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43861), with the recipe flags and `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion --disable-aiter-allreduce-fusion-in-prefill`. This PR: the control plus this PR's head. Only this PR differs.

TP4, concurrency 8:

TP4, concurrency 16:

The gain is largest at TP4 c8, which has the smallest decode batches and so the most idle CUs in the control, and shrinks as concurrency grows. At TP2 c16 there is no measurable change. Each arm is a single run, so differences of 1 to 2% are within noise.

The TP4 c8 pair on image `...rocm724-mi35x-20261019` gave interactivity 353 / 259 → 383 / 271 (+8% / +5%).

title: [Perf] cuda-graph: Raise MLA prefill capture default to chunked size capped at 8192
author: Fridge003
body:
MLA currently defaults prefill CUDA graph capture to 2048 tokens even when chunked prefill is larger. Default MLA capture to `min(8192, cfg.chunked_prefill_size)` to expand coverage while limiting capture memory growth.

Non-MLA models retain the existing default of `cfg.chunked_prefill_size`. In particular, Muse MegaMoE + LayerNorm SP with a 16384-token chunk keeps a 16384-token capture ceiling, satisfying its requirement that captured workspaces cover the largest prefill chunk.

For MLA, chunked prefill sizes of 4096 and 16384 default to capture maxima of 4096 and 8192, respectively. This applies when prefill `max_bs` is unset; explicit settings and existing downstream caps retain their behavior.

Validation:
- Executed the actual default-selection blocks and bucket generator in a standalone CPU harness: 16 cases passed across MLA/non-MLA, chunk sizes 4096/8192/16384/32768, explicit max_bs, and existing PP/max-total-tokens/Llama-2 caps. The non-MLA 16384 case failed on the previous revision and passes after this change. This is a focused configuration check, not a full server startup test.
- Python AST parsing, `git diff --check`, and all applicable pre-commit hooks passed.
- A prior GLM-5.3-Flash TP4/DFlash2/no-CP sweep on 4 x GB300 completed explicit 8192-token capture on all four ranks (12.16 GiB graph pool reserved per GPU). That experiment used fixed chunked prefill 16384, mem_fraction_static 0.60, and FlashInfer 0.7.1; it did not test this latest default-selection change or reproduce the B200 CI environment.
- GPU runtime tests were not rerun for this default-selection update.

title: [Perf] dsv4: Restore sparse prefill for request-window rows
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `_use_sparse_prefill` no longer rejects a batch whose KV pool has a request window, so encoder SWA bounded replay rows above the sparse threshold take sparse prefill again instead of the paged decode kernel. #42273 admitted them; #38603 brought the old clause back while reworking the call-site condition, and #37958 moved it into `_use_sparse_prefill`. The decoder tail (`late_layer_tail`) still stays dense.
- The chunk cache already builds from the request-window layout (`_build_sparse_prefill_chunk_cache`), and a request-window batch still publishes no prefill read-done (`_snapshot_prefill_shared_reads` returns `UNKNOWN`), so the cache is built in the first layer behind the whole-forward barrier.
- DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on GB300, DEP4, encoder replay on, 131,072-token context with 4,096 new tokens per request, one run per arm: 79,375 -> 86,987 tok/s/GPU at 32K tokens per rank (+9.6%; attention kernels 83.2 -> 46.7 ms per step) and +5.3% at 64K. GSM8K (sgl-eval, 200 examples, with `SGLANG_OPT_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PREFILL=1` so smaller extends take the sparse path too): 98.99% over the 198 answered before an unrelated crash, vs 98.50% on main.

Changes behavior only when encoder SWA bounded replay is on.

title: [Perf] dsv4: Gather V4.1 index-K slots once per forward and cache the prefill index plan
author: hnyls2002
body:
- DeepSeek V4.1's low-ratio indexer no longer gathers its index-K pool slots from `req_to_token` in every layer: `_snapshot_low_ratio_k_slots` gathers them once per ratio at metadata init (`scoring.prefill_k_slots`), shares them with the late-layer tail metadata, and passes them as `PrefillInputs.k_slots`. The indexer backends stop taking `req_to_token` for prefill.
- The batch-only part of the prefill data (request starts, per-request lengths, compressed lengths) is built by the first layer of each ratio and cached per metadata (`PrefillIndexPlan`, `low_ratio_index_plans`), instead of rebuilt by every layer.
- The eager extend also fills `low_ratio_req_indices` and `low_ratio_pos_i64` once at metadata init, as the tail and the prefill graph already do.
- Captured prefill graphs carry no snapshot and keep the per-layer gather.
- DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on GB300, DEP4, 131,072-token context with 4,096 new tokens per request, one run per arm: at 4K tokens per rank the step goes from 106-110 to 98.3 ms, measured together with a request-window change that is not in this PR (the slot snapshot alone was not measured); 8K and 32K move under 1%.

No behavior change; host work moves from every indexer layer to metadata init.

title: [Perf] dsv4: Compute request-window history rows once per batch
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `window_layout` now computes each history slot's source row (`history_src`: `row_loc` of the slot's request and position, or the zero row when invalid) once per batch and stores it in `WindowLayout`, instead of `RequestWindow.buffer` recomputing it in every layer through `_history_src`. It takes the window's `zero_row` to do so.
- `WindowLayout.copy_` copies the new field, so a captured layout refreshed in place for graph replay carries the current batch's rows.
- The two `window_layout` callers (the CUDA and HIP DeepSeek V4 backends) and the tests that build a layout pass `zero_row`.
- DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on GB300, DEP4: `row_loc` and `_history_src` take 4.1-4.8% and up to 2.9% of the scheduler thread at 4K tokens per rank, and 3.2% and 1.7% in a multi-turn prefill workload at 640 concurrent sessions, all per layer under `get_swa_raw_buffer`. With this change and the V4.1 index-K slot snapshot (#45577) together, the 4K step goes from 106-110 to 98.7 ms (one run per arm); this change alone was not measured.

No behavior change; only applies with encoder SWA bounded replay.

title: [Perf] dsv4: Let the decoder tail leave the prefill graph under DP attention with MegaMoE
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `breaks_out_of_prefill_graph` no longer requires `attn_dp_size == 1` or a non-all-to-all MoE, so under DP attention with MegaMoE the decoder replay tail leaves the prefill graph for its row-bucket graphs, as it already does without DP (#45107), instead of computing every row of the captured bucket in the late layers.
- The clause assumed ranks pick graph or eager independently and agree on tail rows through the eager tail's host gather. Inside the graph neither holds: the DP prefill-graph vote is min-reduced, so all ranks replay or none do, and the in-graph tail break reads every rank's tail rows from `global_late_layer_num_tokens_cpu`, exchanged before the forward since #44948. The module docstring now says so.
- DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on GB300, DEP4, MegaMoE, breakable prefill graph (buckets 4096 and 8192) with #44627's changes applied, encoder replay off, 131,072-token context with 4,096 new tokens per request, one run per point: 4K tokens per rank 78.6 -> 58.7 ms per step (52,127 -> 69,746 tok/s/GPU), 8K 140.3 -> 97.5 ms (58,408 -> 84,027), against 96.2 ms eager. GSM8K (sgl-eval, 200 examples) on that configuration: 98.00%, vs 98.50% on main.

Changes behavior only for prefill graphs under DP attention with an all-to-all MoE; the request-window, CP, and unified-KV Triton exclusions stay.

title: [Fix] [SM100] quantization: Honor `deep_gemm` for 32x32 block-FP8 linears
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `--fp8-gemm-backend=deep_gemm` now runs `[32, 32]` block-FP8 linears with UE8M0 scales (DeepSeek-V4.1) on DeepGEMM on SM100, instead of falling back to Triton. DeepGEMM serves this recipe there with `sm100_fp8_fp4_gemm_1d1d`.
- SM100 DeepGEMM casts the fp32 block scales to UE8M0 itself, which is exact only for powers of two. Weight loading checks that every block32 weight scale is a power of two (as the Hopper BF16 path already does) and the linear keeps any other layer on Triton, so a checkpoint labeled `ue8m0` with other scales keeps working. Pre-quantized `(q, scale)` input stays on Triton on SM100, since nothing checks its scales.
- Block32 weights without `scale_fmt: ue8m0` stay on Triton on SM100. An explicit `deep_gemm` that still lands on Triton for a non-128 block layout now logs a warning.
- `test_warmup_memory` now also covers the block32 kernel type on Blackwell.
- Verified on B300 through the real linear layer: UE8M0 weights run on DeepGEMM and match the Triton path within BF16 rounding over 5 shapes; scales scaled off powers of two fall back to Triton with output identical to Triton; pre-quantized input runs on Triton. Layer latency (N=4096, K=7168) drops from 135 us to 23 us at M=1, and from 1011 us to 56 us at M=2048.

Behavior changes only for `--fp8-gemm-backend=deep_gemm` on SM100; `auto`, the other backends, and SM90 are unchanged.

<!-- pr-states:start -->

title: [Perf] [AMD] deterministic: Allow AITER prefill attention on gfx950
author: aarnetalman
body:
## Motivation

In deterministic mode, prefill attention on ROCm runs on SGLang's Triton extend-attention kernel. At long inputs that kernel is most of the remaining cost of deterministic mode: on MI350X, Qwen3-8B at 32k input spends 9.3 s in Triton prefill attention vs 4.1 s in AITER's batch prefill per profiled window, two thirds of the gap to normal mode. #44489 lets deterministic mode use AITER for decode attention; this PR does the same for prefill.

AITER's batch prefill (`mha_batch_prefill_func`) is run-to-run deterministic, and a row's result does not depend on its batchmates, with two conditions found on MI350X (gfx950):
1. **`max_seqlen_q` must be the same in every call.** It sizes the launch, and the output depends on it; with `max_seqlen_q == 1` the wrapper also switches to a non-causal mask. SGLang passes the batch's longest extend, so a request's bits changed with its batchmates.
2. **Prompt splits must fall on multiples of 128 tokens**, the kernel's query tile. The same tokens computed as one extend, or as a cached prefix plus an extend, give the same bits only when the split point is a multiple of 128. Splits come from chunked prefill and from radix-cache hits.

This PR, in deterministic mode on gfx950, accepts `--prefill-attention-backend aiter` and meets both conditions: a fixed `max_seqlen_q`, and page size 128 so that radix-cache prefixes and chunk ends fall on the tile. With either condition missing, the checks below fail (see the control runs).

**Impact**
- Who: `--enable-deterministic-inference` with `--prefill-attention-backend aiter` on gfx950 (MI350X/MI355X), non-MLA models, bf16 KV cache, no speculative decoding.
- Effect: deterministic-mode throughput +9% at 8k input and +48% at 32k on Qwen3-8B; up to +73% at 32k on Qwen3-30B-A3B (tables below). Bitwise batch invariance, cached-prefix and chunk-boundary consistency hold.
- Page size: becomes 128 in this configuration unless already a multiple of 128 (with a warning); a `--chunked-prefill-size` that is not a multiple of 128 is refused.
- Exact chunk fill (gfx95, `SGLANG_EXACT_CHUNK_FILL`) is off in deterministic mode: it ends a chunk wherever the token budget runs out, off the page grid. With page size 1 this makes no difference to where chunks end.
- Refused, with an error naming the reason: other GPUs, MLA models, speculative decoding, an fp8 KV cache (not deterministic end to end in our tests yet; also when `--kv-cache-dtype auto` resolves to fp8 from the checkpoint's KV cache quantization), sliding-window models and the unified-attention / 5D-cache AITER paths (as for AITER decode in #44489).
- Unchanged: deterministic mode with Triton prefill (the default), and everything without `--enable-deterministic-inference`.

## Modifications

- `arg_groups/overrides.py`:
  - `_deterministic_attention_backend`: `--prefill-attention-backend aiter` is accepted in deterministic mode on gfx950 for non-MLA models without speculative decoding and with a bf16 KV cache; otherwise the error says why.
  - `_deterministic_aiter_prefill_page_size` (new pass, run in `handle_attention_backend_compatibility` next to the other page-size constraints): page size 128 unless already a multiple of it; a chunked-prefill size that is not a multiple of 128 raises.
- `layers/attention/aiter_backend.py`: in deterministic mode the batch prefill gets a fixed `max_seqlen_q` (the chunked-prefill size, or the context length without chunked prefill; never below the batch's longest extend), and aiter prefill on a resolved fp8 KV cache raises at startup. The existing deterministic guard now names aiter attention in general.
- `managers/schedule_policy.py`: no exact chunk fill in deterministic mode.
- `test/registered/unit/test_model_overrides.py`: the backend acceptance cases (gfx950, MLA, speculative decoding, KV-cache dtype) and the page-size pass.

## Accuracy Tests

MI350X, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261020` (ROCm 7.2.4) with this branch's `python/sglang` (and #43788). Server:

```
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <model> --tp <N> \
  --attention-backend triton --prefill-attention-backend aiter --decode-attention-backend aiter \
  --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --enable-deterministic-inference
```

(The log shows page size set to 128 and the radix cache on.) Checks: `python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic --test-mode {single,prefix,radix_cache} --n-trials 50` (prefix also with `--return-logprob`); a bitwise comparison of 1,275 responses (the same prompt in batches of 1-50, token IDs and log-probabilities) against batch size 1; a 30k-token document followed by different questions, sent repeatedly so later requests hit the cached document (12 comparisons); with YaRN x4, a 64k and a 120k prompt alone vs next to other requests (8), and a 100k prompt split at different chunk boundaries by other requests (12).

| Model | single | prefix (logprobs) | radix_cache | bitwise | cached 30k prefix | 64k/120k | chunk boundaries |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-8B | 1 unique | identical | pass | 1,275/1,275 | 12/12 | 8/8 | 12/12 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | 1 unique | identical | pass | 1,275/1,275 | 12/12 | | |

The same settings applied through a launcher patch (instead of this branch's code) on `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261018` also pass every check above for Qwen3-8B at TP2, Phi-4 and Qwen3.8-27B.

**Control (page size 1, i.e. without this PR's page-size rule, everything else equal):** cached prefixes reach the kernel off the 128-token tile, and the prefix check with log-probabilities fails and the cached 30k prefix matches in only 4 of 12 cases, on Qwen3-8B. Without the fixed `max_seqlen_q`, results depend on batchmates already at kernel level.

Rechecked as pushed on the 2026-10-21 nightly (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261021`, with #43788): Qwen3-8B every check above incl. cached prefix, 64k/120k and chunk boundaries; Phi-4 every check and a 12k cached prefix.

Unit tests on MI350X: `test_model_overrides.py` 115 passed, 6 failed (the same 6 CUDA-specific failures as on main without this branch).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Deterministic mode, TP1, same node and image; before: Triton prefill (`--prefill-attention-backend triton`), after: AITER prefill (this PR); `python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf --random-input-len <in> --random-output-len <out> --num-prompts <n> --max-concurrency <c>`. Output throughput (tok/s), Qwen3-8B, this branch, 2 rounds:

| in/out, prompts, concurrency | Before | After | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1024/1024, 256, 256 | 6,660 / 6,663 | 6,714 / 6,723 | +0.8% |
| 8192/1024, 256, 128 | 1,481 / 1,485 | 1,613 / 1,616 | +8.8% |
| 32768/256, 64, 16 | 92 / 92 | 135 / 137 | +48% |

Same settings through the launcher patch (those runs used `--attention-backend aiter`, which turns the radix cache off; these random prompts share no prefixes, so that does not affect throughput), one or two rounds:

| Model | 1k/1k | 8k/1k | 32k/256 | 64k/256 | 120k/128 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-8B (YaRN x4 for 64k/120k) | 0% | +8% | +49% | +39% | +37% |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | +1% | +14% | +73% | | |
| Qwen3.8-27B | +44% | +9% | +13% | | |
| Phi-4 (16k context) | 0% | +7% | | | |

No change without `--enable-deterministic-inference` or with Triton prefill.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

In DeepSeek-V4.1 Mega attention decode, wqkv_a and wo_b quantize their bf16 input in a separate kernel before the MXFP8 GEMM. The producers of those inputs (Mega-mHC and the wo_a `fp8_einsum`) can write the MXFP8 input directly.

## Modifications

- `LinearBase.deepgemm_mxfp8_input`: `MQALayer` sets it on wqkv_a and wo_b before load; `Fp8LinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading` packs a DeepGEMM weight scale beside the FlashInfer one and keeps the flag only when it did. A DeepGEMM-packed activation pair is a plain `(fp8, int32 scale)` tuple, which `apply` routes to the existing `deepgemm_w8a8_mxfp8_linear_with_fallback`.
- `mhc_mega_boundary` takes `y_fp8` / `y_gemm_sf` out-buffers; the Mega-mHC post fills them for the next layer's wqkv_a.
- The Mega wo_a `fp8_einsum` writes its FP8 output pair for wo_b.
- On whenever the layer can be prepared (Blackwell, DeepGEMM UE8M0, FlashInfer dense backend, aligned shapes); decode/verify only (no extend, no SP), at most 2048 rows. Every other linear is unchanged.

title: [Perf] dsv41: Fuse the q_norm MXFP8 quantize for wq_b at every row count
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

The fused `rmsnorm_mxfp8` that feeds wq_b only ran up to 8 rows because its scale swizzle addressed a single 128-row tile; larger batches ran RMSNorm plus a separate `mxfp8_quantize`.

## Modifications

- `mxfp8_epilogue` addresses any number of 128-row scale tiles (unchanged below 128 rows).
- `rmsnorm_mxfp8` accepts any row count; FP8 values and swizzled scales are bit-identical to `mxfp8_quantize(..., is_sf_swizzled_layout=True)` from 1 to 1280 rows.
- Drop the 8-row cap at the q_norm call site.

title: [Perf] [KDA] muse_spark: use BLOCK_M 240 for BF16 MegaMoE prefill shards
author: Waterpine
body:
## Motivation

This PR is powered by [KDA](https://github.com/NVlabs/kda) team. MegaMoE is the largest prefill cost in the BF16 TP8/EP8 deployment: about 68 ms of a 131 ms 8K-token TTFT on rank 0. For BF16 prefill shards DeepGEMM's heuristic picks BLOCK_M 192 (`2,192,48,128,2`), sized for uniformly spread routing. Muse Spark routing is skewed, and on GB300 `2,240,40,128,2` is faster for these shards. DeepGEMM reads `DG_MEGA_MOE_TILES` on every MegaMoE launch; an empty value keeps its heuristic.

## Modifications

- `srt/layers/muse_spark/muse_spark_megamoe.py`: `_tile_override` asks DeepGEMM's `get_block_m_for_mega_moe` for the launch's tile (LRU-cached); only when it returns 192 for `bf16xbf16` does `_megamoe_tiles` set `DG_MEGA_MOE_TILES=2,240,40,128,2` around that one launch and reset it afterwards, including on exceptions
- NVFP4, decode and small prefill shards (smaller heuristic tiles) and a user-set `DG_MEGA_MOE_TILES` are left alone
- `test_muse_spark_megamoe_tiles.py` (new): the override rules and env scoping on any GPU; on SM100 it pins the installed heuristic, checks that DeepGEMM honours the override and that BF16 output is bitwise identical with either tile. Registered on H100 and B200

## Accuracy Tests

- BLOCK_M only changes how rows are split into tiles, not the K-loop order, epilogue or combine; the registered test checks bitwise-identical output with 192 and 240
- GSM8K (sgl-eval, 1319 questions, BF16 TP8/EP8, 8 runs per side): 93.71% vs 93.55% (-0.16 pt, 95% CI [-0.41, +0.08]); Low Latency recipe -0.08 pt (4 runs per side); greedy replay identical to main

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel on GB300, EP4, 256 experts, top-k 8, expert popularity lognormal (sigma = skew), rank-max time, two jobs:

| Tokens per rank | Skew | BLOCK_M 192 | BLOCK_M 240 | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2048 | 1.2 | 1933 us | 1788 us | 1.081x / 1.083x |
| 2048 | 0.7 | 1772 us | 1664 us | 1.065x / 1.066x |
| 2048 | uniform | 1763 us | 1769 us | 0.996x / 0.998x |
| 1024 | 0.7 | 1177 us | 1124 us | 1.048x / 1.048x |

BF16 model vs main (2x GB300, TP8/EP8, cookbook GB300 High Throughput recipe, 64 requests per point, two pairs):

| Point | Pair 1 | Pair 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8K C1 TTFT | 1.035x (131.3 -> 126.9 ms) | 1.024x (130.4 -> 127.4 ms) |
| 8K C8 TTFT | 1.043x | 1.021x |
| mixed C1 / C8 TTFT | 1.037x / 1.041x | 1.025x / 1.022x |

- Rank-0 MegaMoE time per 8K request: 68.1 -> 63.7 ms and 67.3 -> 64.5 ms
- Decode ITL within 0.3% of main; no serving point regresses
- Low Latency recipe (DFlash, one pair): 8K C1 TTFT 1.034x [1.032, 1.037] (145.6 -> 140.8 ms), verify-step time 1.002x-1.032x, accept lengths unchanged
- NVFP4 is unchanged (the override only applies to `bf16xbf16`)
- Measured on GB300 only. The override also applies to B200 and B300 BF16 (same EP8 shards); B200 speed is untested, and the gain depends on skewed routing (uniform routing is 0.2-0.4% slower in the kernel table above)
- Happy to limit it to SM103 (B300/GB300) if reviewers prefer, or keep it on B200 if someone can measure there

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not applicable.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: [Test] cpu: prune mirror and tautology cases from the per-commit CPU suite
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary

The per-commit CPU suite (`base-a-test-cpu`) grew to 860+ registered files. A full audit of every file against the unit-test admission rule (`.claude/rules/unit-test-admission.md`: each case must name a future diff that turns it red) found a large share of cases whose assertions restate the implementation: wire-format round trips asserted against the decoder's own output, one-predicate-per-case rejection truth tables, mock call-count blocks, and happy-path tautologies.

This PR removes them in three commits: 177 files changed, ~14.2k lines deleted, no production code touched.

## Changes

- **Whole-file deletions (21+5):** files whose every case is a mirror or is fully subsumed by a sibling suite — e.g. `test_uno_token_accounting.py` (re-computes the one-line `get_num_generated_tokens`), `test_radix_cache_slru_accuracy.py` (no external oracle; `test_evict_policy.py` pins the SLRU priority tuple directly), ROCm-only leaf-predicate tables, and `test_http_server_auth.py` (subset of `test_auth.py`).
- **Disaggregation case pruning (~200 cases):** wire round trips on `from_zmq` / pack / transfer-indices helpers, `test_pd_role_switch.py`'s 14-case `test_rejected_*` truth table, `test_encode_server.py`'s 50-case `TestEncoderDelivery` mock-permutation class. Kept: protocol ordering, failure injection, negative branches, cross-process contracts.
- **Case pruning across managers / spec / mem_cache / observability (~120 cases):** accessor mirrors, dict-semantics tautologies, constructor read-backs, and one 540-subtest sweep whose oracle re-implemented the rule it tested. Two cases that were unconditional CUDA skips in the CPU suite (dead coverage) are also removed.

## Verification

- `py_compile` on all touched files; `pytest --collect-only` clean on touched directories.
- Executed the pruned suites locally: disaggregation 672 -> 309 collected cases, all passing; managers 334 passed; spec/layers 203 passed; mem_cache 253 passed; observability/misc 229 passed. The remaining failures reproduce identically on main (missing native extensions in the local env).
- Every deletion was checked against the current file contents, not just the audit snapshot; a handful of audit-flagged cases that had since become load-bearing were kept (listed per-commit).

title: [Fix] [AMD] kernels: Import the HIP launch helpers from jit.utils.hipcc in smallm_fp8_blockscale_gfx950
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## What
`smallm_fp8_blockscale_gfx950` imports its HIP build/launch helpers from `sglang.kernels.jit.utils.hipcc` (`check_hip`, `hip_lib`, `hipcc_path`, `HipKernel`) instead of the private names that no longer exist in `smallm_moe_gfx950`.

## Why
#45112 moved `_check`, `_hip_lib`, `_hipcc` and `_Kernel` out of `smallm_moe_gfx950` into `jit/utils/hipcc.py` under the new names. #42229 added this module against the old location and merged a day later, so importing it fails:

```
File ".../kernels/ops/gemm/smallm_fp8_blockscale_gfx950/__init__.py", line 10, in <module>
ImportError: cannot import name '_check' from 'sglang.kernels.ops.moe.smallm_moe_gfx950'
```

`aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` imports it on gfx950, so FP8 block-scale dense linears fail there. Three tests in `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` have failed with this since: `test_smallm_fp8_blockscale_gfx950.py`, `test_dsv4_dense_mxscale_gfx95.py` and `test_fp8_bpreshuffle_dense_linear_mi35x.py`. Example: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39599109770/job/119218874753

The helpers are the same code under the new names; this is the change #45112 made to the sibling `smallm_fp8_gfx950`.

## Test plan
- [x] `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` partition 0 on rocm10 and rocm720: `test_dsv4_dense_mxscale_gfx95.py` and `test_fp8_bpreshuffle_dense_linear_mi35x.py` pass, all 32 files green: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39687298904

title: [Fix] lora: Preserve MoE projection identity and routing lifetimes
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* __->__ #45681
* #45917
* #45462
* #45916
* #45915

## Motivation

Independent gate/up A factors require matching rank halves during expansion. The stock virtual-expert hook reused the gate half for the up output: with `x=1`, `A_gate=2`, `A_up=3`, `B_gate=5`, `B_up=7`, it produced `[10,14]` instead of `[10,21]`. Inactive routes and absent/disabled adapters also need complete private outputs without consuming stale or NaN payloads.

## Changes

- Keep one full-`2R` shrink and select the matching A half inside the existing expansion. Internal rank/half-width constants and half-local masks support ragged widths without another projection launch or tensor. The default expansion keeps its original formulas.
- Bound raw virtual IDs and adapter slots before histogram, address or payload formation. Preserve borrowed inputs, valid adapter 0 and original-width int64 validity; shared routing retains negative routes. Missing, disabled and out-of-range adapters cannot read private deltas or contribute NaN scores.
- Complete owned LoRA outputs in their existing kernels and guard capacity-grid programs before grouped division/modulo. Empty helpers preserve their return/output contracts. Activation and shared-outer rank reductions retain active arithmetic and rounding.
- Prepare paired per-expert gate-B/down-A routing once on the main stream, aligning at each stage's actual block size. Release the shared raw owner before projection buffers and the side-stream fork. Existing cache contracts and staged fallbacks remain for unsupported pairings, including global-ID EP.

- Remove unused expert-ID sanitizers and the unused metadata-bearing activation branch. Keep the production three-tensor activation and existing producer/reduction contracts.

## CI cadence

The CUDA virtual-expert and experimental shared-outer LoRA suites now run in opt-in `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small`. CPU runtime checks and the core routing-kernel tests remain in base CI; the existing XPU registration is preserved.

Across the stack, six existing CUDA file registrations move from base CI to extra/nightly, removing 854 estimated GPU-seconds from the default gate (registration estimates, not a measured wall-time saving). All test bodies, cases, inputs, assertions and tolerances are unchanged. Full before/after discovery validates 2,535 files and 3,077 registrations, with every moved file selected in its enabled destination suite. Configured hooks pass; native tests were not rerun for this registration-only update.

## Validation

- At integrated `e6670af1ad`, the focused native Marlin/LoRA route suite passes 14 tests on 1× B300 with the pinned providers, including changing padded routes and output completion.

- Two additional direct Marlin output-ownership configurations did not complete within a 600-second cold-compilation budget on B300. No result is claimed for that extended run; it is separate from the completed route replay and producer-contract checks.

- The focused production activation/reduction suite passes 10 tests on 1× B300 after cleanup. The deleted helpers had no production callers; retained production Triton kernel bodies are unchanged.

Performance comparisons use main `b008ec3de6` before #44480, #44991, #44993 and #44994 merged. The integrated candidate also includes intervening main changes; the measured improvement is not attributed solely to this PR.

- Configured hooks and runtime/policy CPU tests pass. 1× NVIDIA H200 nonzero-LoRA tests cover real stock, factored and three-adapter temporary paths, poisoned inactive data, mapping/enabled changes and valid → inactive → recovery CUDA graphs. Runner unit doubles are separate from native/full-entry evidence.
- The final pre-rebase H200 comparison (`3c486bd6` versus `b008ec3d`) completed 60 workers and 384 fixed `rtol=0.01, atol=0.001` checks at M32/512, H256/I128/E8/topk2/rank8. Factored and multi-adapter outputs agree bitwise across revisions. Paired graph medians improve 1.82%/1.41% for factored and 4.72%/6.62% for multi-adapter paths; measured peaks do not increase. The nongated stock compatibility fixture retains bit instability on both revisions despite passing fixed-close checks; it does not prove a fully gated checkpoint.
- Four H200 factored memory workers retain 2 MiB/4 MiB graph-pool reservations, lower capture allocated peaks by 512 bytes and preserve replay allocated peaks. These are allocator/current-pool observations, not historical per-pool peaks or non-PyTorch memory coverage.
- B300 virtual-expert tests passed 19 cases/102 subtests, with five abstract-base skips. The final full-width route-factory suite passed six tests/12 subtests. Its new regression fails six builder combinations on the original helper and passes all 18 builder/state checks after repair. Three representative int32 shapes retain identical non-debug PTX tokens and queried resources for both standalone and inlined producers.

H200/B300 tests used PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0, sgl-kernel 0.4.10 and FlashInfer 0.7.2. The H200 performance/memory results precede the main rebase; no B300 full-runner LoRA performance, native MUSA or distributed-serving result is claimed.

## Rebase validation (before the CI registration fix)

This five-PR stack was rebased without conflicts onto main `8b9f72417f`. All five patches retain their stable patch IDs relative to the preceding published stack; the newer main commits do not touch the stack's changed files. The existing removal of the unused `materialized_routing` parameter and its three call-site arguments in #45917 is preserved.

Each rebased PR commit passed its configured pre-commit checks independently. The final stack passes `git diff --check`, and all 72 changed Python files parse successfully. CPU test suites, native GPU tests and performance measurements were not rerun for this rebase. Previously reported results, including those at integrated `e6670af1ad`, remain evidence for those earlier revisions with their stated limits.

## Prior CI registration fix

The GGUF weighting test now uses the existing `nightly-musa-1-gpu` suite with `nightly=True`; at that revision, its CUDA kernel-unit registration was unchanged. The previous nonexistent MUSA suite caused global registry validation to fail before CPU, CUDA and AMD tests could run.

The original collection failure was reproduced. Full registration collection and suite validation now pass on the GGUF component (2,533 files / 3,075 registrations) and the integrated stack (2,535 files / 3,077 registrations), including enabled MUSA nightly and CUDA selection. Configured pre-commit checks pass for the corrected test. This update changes one registration line and is propagated through the existing stack.

## CPU CI follow-up

Run [39935811691](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39935811691) exposed an upstream Flux2 import test registered in the CPU suite, whose environment lacks the diffusion dependencies. The import chain also queries the active GPU. #45915 moves that check to the existing CUDA diffusion unit suite, which installs those dependencies, while retaining its XPU registration and the real subprocess check that blocks Intel Triton imports. This registration fix is propagated through the stack.

#45917 also updates the MoE CPU fixtures to use the production CompressedTensors/Quark method wrappers and to resolve the FP8 routing policy through the initialization hook. Existing backend, EP mapping and zero-valued/default routing assertions remain intact. The three original fixture failures were reproduced before the fix; both complete files now pass on CPU (26 tests, 55 subtests).

The Flux2 import check passes on 1× NVIDIA B300 with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0 and Diffusers 0.37.0; its five Intel-XPU numerical cases are skipped on CUDA and were not rerun on XPU. Full integrated registry collection validates 2,535 files / 3,077 registrations, including the enabled diffusion/XPU selections and the preceding GGUF MUSA fix. Configured checks pass for the changed files. Only three test files change across this follow-up; production code is unchanged. A fresh full CI result is not claimed.

## Merge preparation

Rebased this component onto main `ac3db731b3` for squash merge. The preceding stack components are already merged into main; only this component is replayed here. No test suites or performance measurements were rerun for this merge. Earlier validation sections describe their named revisions.

title: [Perf] spec: Let DSPARK prefill publish read-done by placing its draft KV inject before the target forward
author: hnyls2002
body:
- DSPARK prefill can now publish prefill read-done: `supports_prefill_shared_read_done` returns True for DSPARK as well as DFLASH. Its one later shared reader, the draft KV inject after the target prefill, no longer reads scheduler-shared tables after the target forward.
- `TargetHiddenKvInjector.place_prefill` computes where a prefill's target hidden lands in the draft pool (`PrefillPlacement`: the draft write ids from the batch's own plan, positions, the SWA ring's slot and final position, and the SWA rows). `DSparkWorkerV2._forward_prefill` calls it before the target forward, whose read-done event is recorded before replay, and after the forward calls `inject_prefill`, which only selects the kept tokens and writes. The position and ring code moves from the worker unchanged; the SWA rows come from `_mla_swa_loc`, moved out of `_inject_mla` unchanged, for both the per-request ring and the paged full-to-SWA mapping. `inject_target_hidden`, used by verify, is unchanged.
- The pinned allowlist test now includes DSPARK.

Behavior change: DSPARK target prefill publishes read-done when the attention backend declares a pre-replay read end, so the next batch's scheduler-stream work waits only for the target's metadata reads instead of the whole forward. Validation on GB300, DEP4 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with DSPARK, GSM8K (sgl-eval, 200 examples), with a debug build that also computed the placement after the forward and compared: with encoder SWA bounded replay (SWA ring) 98.00% and 134/134 prefill injects identical; without it (paged SWA mapping) 97.50% and 137/137 identical; read-done active on every DP rank in both. Rerun the same way on the placement-into-injector commit: 97.00% with 137/137 identical (ring) and 98.50% with 144/144 identical (paged mapping), read-done active on every DP rank.

title: [Feat] HiCache: Support fused DFLASH KV in unified hybrid SWA pools
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

Muse Spark fell back to a private DFLASH KV pool when unified memory and HiCache were enabled together. This change lets target and draft share the same GPU backing pool per TP rank.

## Modifications

Keep the FA4 draft's BF16 rows inside the target's FULL page envelopes alongside its FP8 KV rows, and reuse the existing HiCache page translation to transfer both together. Wait for envelope restoration before DFLASH prefill, including CUDA graph replay, and skip the separate draft host sidecar.

This enables L2 HiCache for a full-attention DFLASH draft on a unified hybrid-SWA target. Other host-pool paths, including L3 storage, retain their existing private draft fallback. No CUDA kernel is added.

## Accuracy Tests

- All pre-commit checks passed.
- Actual CUDA direct and kernel HiCache roundtrips preserved complete mixed-dtype envelopes and neighboring pages at different physical page locations.
- 1,464 fixed-input FA4/TRT-LLM output and LSE comparisons were bit-exact.
- A bounded real-model cache test restored 2,304 tokens from host with zero device-cache hits and correctly recalled a reference number stored in that prefix. Full-model logprob equality is not claimed; resident controls were also non-repeatable under this serving configuration.
- Startup validation on all four TP ranks confirmed target and draft share the same underlying unified buffer, without a draft host sidecar.

Complete evaluations on 4 x B300, TP4/EP4, target `trtllm_mha`, draft `RadixArk/Muse-Spark-Open-DFlash2` with `fa4`, unified memory, and HiCache size 200:

| Dataset | Correct / total | Score |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AIME26, 8 repeats | 228 / 240 | 95.00% |
| GPQA Diamond | 177 / 198 | 89.39% |
| Video-MME short, 96 frames | 798 / 900 | 88.67% |
| GSM8K | 1284 / 1319 | 97.35% |

All evaluations had zero request errors. AIME26 and GPQA each had one output-length truncation; Video-MME and GSM8K had none. The prior accepted run used B200 and scored 94.17% / 89.90% / 87.44% on the first three datasets. Against the original GPQA reference of 179/198, this run is lower by 1.0101 percentage points.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No controlled throughput comparison was performed. The existing synchronous host-arena compaction caused pauses during the continuous evaluation sequence. This change does not modify that allocator.

title: [Refactor] radix-tree: Move insert overlap handling into a resumable OVERLAP phase
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

The resumable insert walk in `UnifiedTreeCore` handles an overlapping node inline inside `_insert_walk_step`: the component overlap hooks (`update_component_on_insert_overlap`), the duplicate-slot frees and the hit-count backup check all run in the same step that matched the node. The walk can suspend at a barrier only between steps, and the only phase a suspended walk can resume into is `WALK`.

That leaves no place for a tree core that has to wait on a resource barrier before it may take ownership of the overlapping slots. Such a core would have to return from the walk step before the overlap hooks run, and the resume would then match the same node again and repeat the pre-barrier work (touch, split, priority), with the overlap still unclaimed.

## Modifications

- `_InsertPhase` gains `OVERLAP` between `WALK` and `COMMIT`; `_InsertWalkState` gains `overlap_node` and `overlap_prefix_len`, and `_advance_insert` dispatches `OVERLAP` to the new `_insert_overlap_step`.
- `_insert_walk_step` keeps the matching, split, priority and unevict handling. For a live node it now records the node and prefix length in the state, switches to `OVERLAP` and calls `_insert_overlap_step` immediately, so an ordinary overlap still completes within one step and emits the same actions as before.
- `_insert_overlap_step` holds the moved overlap body: the component overlap hooks and the duplicate-slot frees (including the split below the SWA eviction floor). A subclass that overrides it can append a non-deferrable action and return while the state stays in `OVERLAP`; `_advance_insert` suspends as usual and the next `resume_insert` lands back in the overlap step for the same node.
- `_finish_insert_walk_node` holds the bookkeeping both the unevict path and the overlap path share: the hit-count backup check, advancing `key` / `value` / `total_prefix_length`, clearing the overlap fields and resetting the phase to `WALK`.
- `components/README.md`: the hook table and the algorithm note name `_insert_overlap_step` as the caller of `update_component_on_insert_overlap`.

No behaviour change for the built-in Full / SWA / Mamba components: the actions emitted per step, and the points at which the walk suspends, are the same as before. The test inspector's `advance_insert_walk_once` precondition (phase is `WALK` between steps) still holds, since an inline overlap returns to `WALK` before the step ends.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A: no model numerics change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A: one extra enum assignment and two state fields per walked node.

Tests run on this branch (CPU, Python core):

- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_insert_walk.py` and `test_unified_radix_cache_core.py` together: 574 passed, 59 skipped (45 subtests passed), including the barrier tests (`test_insert_aborts_continuation_when_action_apply_fails`, `test_insert_abort_drains_pending_deferred_frees`, `test_deferrable_actions_ride_final_step_without_suspension`).
- `ruff format --check` / `ruff check --select=F401,F821,F823,UP037` (0.15.1), `isort --check-only` (7.0.0) and `codespell` (2.4.1) on the changed files: clean.
- Not run here: the Rust-backend re-run (`test_unified_radix_cache_rust.py`) and GPU suites; this change touches only the Python core.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (Existing barrier and overlap tests cover the moved code; no new behaviour for the built-in components.)

title: [Perf] [AMD] kda: Use a HIP chunked-prefill kernel for KDA on gfx950
author: Monstertail
body:
## Motivation Kimi-K3 has 69 KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) layers. On MI350X / MI355X (gfx950), KDA prefill runs the multi-kernel Triton `chunk_kda` pipeline. This PR adds a HIP chunked-prefill kernel for gfx950 and tries it first inside `TritonKDAKernel.extend`, so the default prefill backend gets faster on gfx950 without a new flag. Other GPUs, and inputs the kernel does not cover, keep `chunk_kda`. **Note: This kernel is generated by [KDAgent](https://nvlabs.github.io/kda/blog/2026-09-27-kda-for-kda/) in AMD ecosystems. Cost around 5k dollars in humanize2 flow to get this.** ## Modifications The kernel follows the `sglang.kernels` layout of RFC #29630: it was produced with the Kernel Design Agents workflow, so the implementation lives in `kernels/kda_kernels`, it is registered with `KernelBackend.KDA`, and runtime code reaches it only through the `sglang.kernels.ops` facade. - `kernels/kda_kernels/csrc/attention/kda_prefill_gfx950.cu` and its loader `kernels/kda_kernels/kda_prefill_gfx950.py`, JIT-compiled on first use with `load_extension_with_recovery`. The kernel needs the bf16 16x16x32 MFMA and up to 157 KiB of LDS, so it is gfx950-only. - `kda_intra_kernel` runs over (64-token chunk, head). It computes the gate `-5 * sigmoid(exp(A_log) * (g + dt_bias))` and its chunk cumsum, the beta sigmoid, the q/k L2 norms, and the chunk's UT transform and intra-chunk attention, and stores them as one workspace block per chunk. - A recurrence kernel walks each sequence's chunks and writes the outputs, the final states (in place, like `chunk_kda`) and the optional `track_state` snapshot. `kda_recur_path` picks one of six layouts from the batch shape, the longest sequence and the CU count: a pipelined single kernel for balanced batches with about one (sequence, head) pair per CU, sequence groups joined by an fp32 scan for one long sequence, warp-specialized value-split kernels for few pairs or a dominant long sequence, and one workgroup per pair otherwise. - `kernels/kda_kernels/README.md`: provenance entry. - `kernels/ops/attention/__init__.py`: registers `attention.kda_prefill_gfx950` (`KernelBackend.KDA`, HIP). - `kernels/ops/attention/linear/kda_gfx950_prefill.py` (facade): `extend()` calls the kernel through `get_kernel` and returns `None` for anything it does not cover: other GPUs, `SGLANG_ROCM_KDA_HIP_PREFILL=0`, spec-decode extends, prefill CUDA graph chunk tables, a gate lower bound other than -5, non-raw beta, per-chunk states `h` requested without a track buffer, non-bf16 inputs, head dim other than 128, and a non-contiguous state pool. It passes `max(extend_seq_lens_cpu)` to the kernel, so choosing the layout needs no GPU sync. - `srt/layers/attention/linear/kernels/kda_triton.py`: on ROCm, `TritonKDAKernel.extend` calls the facade first and keeps `chunk_kda` when it returns `None`. This guarded call is the only runtime change; CUDA builds never import the facade. - `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_gfx950_prefill.py` (MI35x suite): the Triton extend routes to the HIP kernel; uncovered inputs fall back; eight layouts covering all six recurrence paths, the chunk-aligned track extend and five track-snapshot cases match `chunk_kda`; untouched state slots stay bit-identical. ## Accuracy Tests MI355X, `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi35x-20261020`. - Against `chunk_kda` over 210 shapes (1-128 sequences of 64-64K tokens, 12 and 24 heads, with and without `track_state`): output, final-state and track-snapshot relative L2 difference at most 0.59% (both kernels round to bf16). Unselected state slots stay bit-identical. - Pass: the new test, `unit/kernels/test_kernels_namespace.py` (includes the KDA directory/backend pairing check), `attention/unittests/kda/test_triton.py`, `attention/test_kda_kernels.py`, `kernels/ops/attention/test_fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py`, `kernels/ops/attention/kda_flydsl/test_kimi_k3_kda_decode.py` and `amd/test_kimi_k3_kda_inproj_fusion.py`. - Kimi-K3 TP8 GSM8K (8-shot, 1319 questions): 0.960 with both HIP kernels off, 0.961 with this PR and the companion fused-decode PR on. ## Speed Tests and Profiling **Kernel.** Median of 20 calls after 3 warmups, `chunk_kda` through `TritonKDAKernel.extend` versus the HIP kernel, MI355X: | Sequences (tokens) | Heads | track_state | Path | Triton | HIP | Speedup | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 x 64 | 12 | no | fused | 0.189 ms | 0.018 ms | 10.71x | | 1 x 1024 | 12 | no | ws4 | 0.205 ms | 0.047 ms | 4.34x | | 1 x 4096 | 12 | no | grp | 0.364 ms | 0.093 ms | 3.90x | | 1 x 16384 | 12 | no | grp | 0.957 ms | 0.262 ms | 3.66x | | 1 x 65536 | 12 | no | grp | 3.928 ms | 0.907 ms | 4.33x | | 8 x 1024 | 12 | no | ws2 | 0.321 ms | 0.093 ms | 3.46x | | 16 x 1024 | 12 | no | fused | 0.501 ms | 0.157 ms | 3.19x | | 64 x 256 | 12 | no | fused | 0.507 ms | 0.152 ms | 3.33x | | 128 x 128 | 12 | no | fused | 0.528 ms | 0.167 ms | 3.17x | | 8192 + 16 x 128 | 12 | no | ws4 | 0.571 ms | 0.273 ms | 2.09x | | 17 + 4096 + 333 + 8000 | 12 | no | ws4 | 0.600 ms | 0.280 ms | 2.14x | | 1 x 8192 | 12 | yes | grp | 0.545 ms | 0.146 ms | 3.72x | | 1 x 16384 | 12 | yes | grp | 0.974 ms | 0.263 ms | 3.71x | | 8 x 1024 | 12 | yes | vs2 | 0.331 ms | 0.095 ms | 3.49x | | 64 x 256 | 12 | yes | vs1 | 0.522 ms | 0.228 ms | 2.29x | Over all 210 shapes: 2.06x-11.11x, geomean 4.08x (one sequence 4.56x, equal-length batches 4.27x, mixed-length batches 2.98x, with `track_state` 2.91x; 12 heads 4.21x, 24 heads 3.94x). The chosen layout is within 0.3% (geomean) of the fastest of the six layouts forced one at a time. **The model runs the kernel.** Kimi-K3 TP8, rank-0 GPU profile (`/start_profile`) of one 10,244-token request with 8 output tokens: | Kernels (calls) | Baseline | This PR + fused decode PR | |---|---|---| | KDA prefill | `chunk_kda`: `l2norm_fwd` (138), `kda_gate_chunk_cumsum` (69), `chunk_kda_fwd_kernel_intra_sub_chunk`, `chunk_kda_fwd_kernel_inter_solve_fused` and `recompute_w_u_fwd` (thousands of calls, because the first request at this length triggers Triton autotuning), `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h` (69), `chunk_gla_fwd_kernel_o` (69) | `kda_intra_kernel` (69), `kda_recur_grp_vs1` (138, two passes), `kda_recur_grp_scan` (69); no Triton `chunk_kda` kernel | **Kimi-K3 TP8 E2E.** Measured with this PR and the companion fused-decode PR applied; the baseline sets `SGLANG_ROCM_KDA_HIP_PREFILL=0 SGLANG_ROCM_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND=none`, which is the current `main` behavior. Baseline and candidate servers were launched alternately, two rounds each; the tables show the mean of the two rounds. The default extra-buffer radix cache passes `track_state` on every extend. ```bash SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT=1 AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE=1 AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --tp-size 8 \ --attention-backend triton --dtype bfloat16 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 --max-running-requests 64 \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --trust-remote-code python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids \ --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 1 \ --num-prompts 80 --max-concurrency 16 --warmup-requests 16 --flush-cache --seed 42 # also: --num-prompts 320 --max-concurrency 64; and --random-input-len 8192 # --random-output-len 64 --num-prompts 40 --max-concurrency 8 --warmup-requests 8 ``` Single-request TTFT isolates prefill: streamed `/v1/completions` with `max_tokens=1`, each prompt unique from its first token so the radix cache cannot reuse it, median of 5 after 2 warmups per round. | Prompt tokens | Baseline | This PR | Change | |---|---|---|---| | 1,006 | 156.5 ms | 137.9 ms | -11.9% | | 4,006 | 218.1 ms | 209.9 ms | -3.8% | | 10,246 | 421.7 ms | 406.3 ms | -3.6% | | 32,006 | 1718.3 ms | 1658.1 ms | -3.5% | Online serving (`bench_serving`). TTFT under load also includes time spent behind other requests' decode steps, so these rows reflect both PRs: | Workload | Metric | Baseline | Both PRs | Change | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1024 in / 512 out, concurrency 16 | median TTFT | 1028.7 ms | 987.1 ms | -4.0% | | | median TPOT | 23.7 ms | 22.9 ms | -3.6% | | | output throughput | 617.7 tok/s | 642.7 tok/s | +4.1% | | 1024 in / 512 out, concurrency 64 | median TTFT | 3841.7 ms | 3695.7 ms | -3.8% | | | median TPOT | 33.5 ms | 32.4 ms | -3.2% | | | output throughput | 1536.7 tok/s | 1590.1 tok/s | +3.5% | | 8192 in / 64 out, concurrency 8 | median TTFT | 3866.4 ms | 3771.8 ms | -2.4% | | | median TPOT | 20.2 ms | 19.5 ms | -3.8% | | | output throughput | 99.5 tok/s | 102.4 tok/s | +3.0% | The two rounds of each server differed by at most 0.6% in output throughput.
Batch prefill TTFT with bench_one_batch_server `last_ttft` of `python3 -m sglang.bench_one_batch_server --model None --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 --batch-size 1 8 32 64 --input-len 1024 --output-len 512 --dataset-name random-ids` (and `--batch-size 4 16 --input-len 4096 --output-len 16`), median of 2 runs: | Requests x tokens | Baseline | This PR | Change | |---|---|---|---| | 1 x 1024 | 168.9 ms | 145.5 ms | -13.9% | | 8 x 1024 | 451.0 ms | 440.1 ms | -2.4% | | 32 x 1024 | 1698.5 ms | 1647.4 ms | -3.0% | | 64 x 1024 | 3409.6 ms | 3306.8 ms | -3.0% | | 4 x 4096 | 859.6 ms | 845.5 ms | -1.6% | | 16 x 4096 | 3432.3 ms | 3335.4 ms | -2.8% |
