title: [Fix] moe: Preserve CUTLASS routing metadata and execution budgets
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #45681
* __->__ #45917
* #45462
* #45916
* #45915

## Motivation

CUTLASS routing must define every permutation entry when routes are negative or nonlocal. Clearing maps, preparing activation-sized copies and materializing rounded scores separately adds work even when all routes are valid. The effective FP8 backend also needs to reach TopK and dispatch before they choose route layout and token-count ownership.

## Changes

- Publish the effective FP8 routing policy before TopK/dispatch, preserving raw signed IDs and the correct local token bound for native FP8/W4A8 consumers.
- Share one complete CUDA route producer between FP8 and W4A8. It writes invalid output-map entries as `-1`, unused input-map capacity as token zero, and the appropriate grouped-GEMM M/N layout. One CTA owns each expert cursor; no separate expert cursor allocation or clear is needed. Non-CUDA and DeepEP paths retain their existing producers.
- Reuse W4A8's existing maps, normalize exceptional ID layouts once, and mask dynamic scale loads before reading inactive rows. Valid inputs avoid the previous activation/ID copies.
- Use a native checked weighted reduction that excludes inactive payloads and NaN scores before access. The FP8 caller opts into the original score-to-output-dtype rounding before FP32 slot-order accumulation. Cached backend/type admission, strided-score support, the Triton fallback, current-stream execution and compile/fake behavior are retained.

- Complete the routing-policy interface for all four plain MXFP4 adapters without changing their inheritance or loading lifecycle. Derive native block-FP8 cardinality from materialized routes, including deferred finalize; widen FP16 scores to FP32 in one copy and preserve supported score storage. Keep Llama4's native per-tensor scaling convention after materialization.

## CI cadence

The mapped shuffle/reduction microbenchmark now runs in `nightly-test-1-gpu-large`. FP8 and W4A8 correctness, map-completion and graph replay tests remain in base CI.

Performance comparisons use main `b008ec3de6` before #44480, #44991, #44993 and #44994 merged. The integrated candidate also includes intervening main changes; the measured improvement is not attributed solely to this PR.

- Configured hooks and focused policy/dispatch unit tests pass. On 1× NVIDIA B300, the registered FP8/W4A8 routing/reduction files passed 16 tests and 143 subtests; this is not blanket native W4A8 admission.
- 1× NVIDIA H200 full native W4A8 comparisons at `d1990d57` cover M32/512 with E2 and M512 with E128, static/dynamic scales, strict `rtol=0.01, atol=0.001` checks, output bits and graph replay. The later LoRA int64 repair does not change this CUTLASS implementation.

B300 validation used PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0, sgl-kernel 0.4.10, FlashInfer 0.7.2, CUDA 13.0 and NVCC 13.0.88. The B300 W4A8 full-entry experiment stopped on an architecture error and numerical/graph failure in the **unchanged baseline**, before candidate admission; H200 W4A8 results are not transferred to Blackwell. This five-PR stack was rebased without conflicts onto main `8b9f72417f`. All five patches retain their stable patch IDs relative to the preceding published stack; the newer main commits do not touch the stack's changed files. The existing removal of the unused `materialized_routing` parameter and its three call-site arguments in #45917 is preserved.

Each rebased PR commit passed its configured pre-commit checks independently. The final stack passes `git diff --check`, and all 72 changed Python files parse successfully. Previously reported results, including those at integrated `e6670af1ad`, remain evidence for those earlier revisions with their stated limits.

## Prior CI registration fix

The GGUF weighting test now uses the existing `nightly-musa-1-gpu` suite with `nightly=True`; at that revision, its CUDA kernel-unit registration was unchanged. The previous nonexistent MUSA suite caused global registry validation to fail before CPU, CUDA and AMD tests could run.

Configured pre-commit checks pass for the corrected test. This update changes one registration line and is propagated through the existing stack.

## CPU CI follow-up

Run [39935811691](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39935811691) exposed an upstream Flux2 import test registered in the CPU suite, whose environment lacks the diffusion dependencies. The import chain also queries the active GPU. #45915 moves that check to the existing CUDA diffusion unit suite, which installs those dependencies, while retaining its XPU registration and the real subprocess check that blocks Intel Triton imports. This registration fix is propagated through the stack.

title: [Perf] dsv4: Optionally stage V4.1 engram rows from the shared host table on the scheduler
author: hnyls2002
body:
On GPUs without ATS, the GPU maps the shared Engram host table in its own page tables. A gather of random rows from a table far larger than its translation reach then runs at a fraction of PCIe bandwidth, and it sits on the forward stream. Sorted reads soften this but do not remove it.

This adds an opt-in path, `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_STAGING=1` (default off), that moves the gather off the forward:

- The scheduler knows every token of an extend batch before its forward. `EngramRowStager` builds each token's look-back window from the requests' fill ids and hashes it on the CPU through `EngramHasher.hash_windows`, the same code the hasher's torch path runs, on host copies of the hasher's buffers.
- It gathers each Engram layer's fp8 rows and e8m0 scales from the shared table into pinned memory with a small thread pool, and copies them to the GPU on a side stream while the previous forward runs.
- The layer waits on the copy's event and only dequantizes contiguous rows (`EngramEmbedding.dequant_staged`); padded rows of a prefill graph are zero.
- Under the breakable prefill graph, the Engram lookup becomes an eager break when the path is on, and it reads the replay batch's staged rows from the forward context.

When the switch is on, the path still turns on only where it applies: every Engram table in the shared host layout (the only layout that maps every row in each process), a GPU without ATS (the same device attribute the sorted reads check), and no prefill context parallelism. Everywhere else, and always with the switch off, the stager is never built and the forward runs the table lookup exactly as before.

A batch falls back to the forward's lookup when it is not a plain extend (decode, target verify), or when a request's newest token is still on the device (a decode row in a converted or mixed batch under overlap scheduling). With encoder SWA bounded replay, the staged rows follow the folded extend, so a replayed request starts at its replay start. The unfolded replay path asserts that nothing was staged.

It is meant for large prefill batches, such as a dedicated prefill node, where the host work hides behind the previous forward. Online serving with small, variable batches may be slower with it on and is still being tuned.

Verification:

- Staged rows match the table lookup bit for bit in every layer: in eager mode and in prefill-graph replay, with encoder replay on (folded replay rows included) and off.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash DEP4 offline prefill on a GPU without ATS is faster with the switch on.
- The hasher's torch path is unchanged by the extracted `hash_windows`, and the stager's CPU hash ids match it on random batches with image tokens and chunked prefixes.

The shared layout under the breakable prefill graph needs #45881 (merged), independently of this change: the hang it fixed occurs without staging.

author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #43262. sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.3.post2 carries sgl-project/DeepGEMM#116 (the `release/v0.2.3` port of #112), which skips the finite-score check on masked rows, so `bf16_mega_gate` no longer needs its input zeroed on padded rows before every MoE layer. - `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_mega_gate.py` already replays graphs with NaN and inf in padded rows, so it is the regression guard for the kernel change.

title: [Perf] dsv4: Write V4.1 K rows with one warp per token in the fused k-norm-rope store
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `fused_k_norm_rope_flashmla` normalizes, ropes and stores every token's 512-wide KV row into the paged FlashMLA cache. It ran one 256-thread block per token with 4-byte loads, a shared-memory reduction and a block barrier, far below the copy rate of the row on large prefill batches.
- For the V4.1 layouts (fp8, fp4, uniform fp8) and batches of at least 2048 tokens, a new kernel gives each token one warp: each lane loads 16 consecutive values with 16-byte loads, the sum of squares stays in registers, and the existing `store_row` writes the lane's 16 values.
- The sum of squares is added in the same order as the block-per-token kernel, and the RoPE and sum-of-squares fma are pinned in both kernels, so the written rows are bitwise equal to before. Smaller batches (decode, short prefill) and the V4 layout keep the block-per-token kernel.

Output is bitwise identical to before.

Verification:
- The cache bytes written by the new kernel match the block-per-token kernel bit for bit for fp8 and fp4 layouts, int32 and int64 positions, strided inputs and skipped rows, from 1 to 65536 tokens, on B300 and GB300.
- A micro benchmark on V4.1-Flash shapes shows the new kernel well ahead from 2048 tokens up, on B300 and GB300.

title: [Perf] dsv4: Combine the final mHC streams from bf16 without an fp32 copy
author: hnyls2002
body:

title: [Perf] dsv4: Replay the V4.1 prefill graph past 16K contexts on SM90
author: hnyls2002
body:
- On CUDA, the DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill CUDA graph builds its replay metadata at the live context width whenever no c4/c128 compress metadata is captured, so SM90 replays contexts past 16K as SM100 already does. Nothing captured on that path depends on the width: the width-sized metadata is swapped in per replay, and without two-level candidates the ratio-1/2 sources run as one eager break.
- The 16K default moves to the HIP backend, whose prefill graph metadata is captured at a fixed width; HIP keeps its behavior.
- `TestPrefillGraphReplayContext` checks the live width for V4.1 and the fixed width with c4/c128 metadata.

Behavior change only for V4.1 with `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable` on CUDA without two-level candidates (SM90): contexts past 16K replay the graph instead of running eager. Under attention context parallelism, which had no default limit, replay metadata is built at the live width instead of the table width. Follows #45407.

title: [Fix] diffusion: Keep dynamic LoRA deltas on fused linear-GELU sites
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

`FUSED_LINEAR_GELU` is in the `"lossless"` tier, and `quality` has defaulted to `"lossless"` since #42370, so the fused linear+GELU epilogue mounts by default. With a dynamic (unmerged) LoRA, the site's linear is a `BaseLayerWithLoRA`. Its `.weight` and `.bias` forward to the base layer, and it passed every duck-typed guard. So `fused_linear_gelu_tanh(x, proj_in.weight, proj_in.bias)` multiplied the base weight only and silently dropped the adapter's delta.

This affects every GELU site that serves a dynamic LoRA:
- LTX-2 two-stage, stage 2, always: the distilled LoRA is applied dynamically on 1370 layers;
- LTX-2.3 in `original` device mode, which is the default on H100/A100;
- dynamic LoRA serving on Wan, FLUX, HunyuanVideo, GLM-Image, Qwen-Image and LongCat.

CI did not catch it:
- #42370 pinned every consistency-checked case to `quality="exact"`;
- the site unit tests used plain `nn.Linear`;
- nightly does run LTX-2.3 TI2V at the default tier with a dynamic LoRA on H100, but it measures latency only;
- the Wan2.2-A14B LoRA case uses layerwise offload, so the fusion never mounted.

## Modifications

`fused_linear_gelu_site.py`:
- `can_use_linear_gelu` takes the module forward while a LoRA wrapper adds output (`lora_active`). A disabled adapter, or a merged one without an output offset, keeps the fused path, because the base weight the epilogue reads already holds the update.
- The mount-time guard judges a LoRA wrapper by the layer it wraps. Before, the wrapper hid that layer's quantization, `skip_bias_add` and multi-rank `gather_output`.
- The module docstring still said the path mounts only for `quality="high"`. It now describes the lossless tier.

Tests:
- `test/unit/test_quality_fusion_lora.py`: every fusion in `_QUALITY_FUSION_HANDLERS` either runs on a site whose linears carry a dynamic adapter, or is listed with the reason it cannot drop an adapter's output. So a new fusion has to pick a side. On a site, the mounted output must equal the unfused forward and differ from the base weight alone. The file also pins the per-call guard to the adapter state and the static guard to the wrapped layer.
- New 1-GPU server case `wan2_1_t2v_1_3b_dynamic_lora_default_quality_1gpu`: Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B serves the Arcane-Jinx adapter unmerged, at 480x272, 9 frames, 8 steps. The adapter carries `ffn.0` (= `ffn.fc_in`) LoRA weights on all 30 blocks. The case needs no golden: the default-quality output must match a `quality="exact"` request to the same server, and differ from a request with the adapter off. Two `DiffusionTestCase` fields express these checks for any case: `reference_quality` and `run_lora_effect_check`.
- The case runs in the NVIDIA 1-GPU PR suite. It is skipped on AMD, whose PR lane parametrizes the same case list, because its thresholds are calibrated on NVIDIA only.
- The case's baseline is intentionally absent from `perf_baselines/h100.json`. Its first CI run fails and prints the block to add (the usual two-step seeding).

This PR and "[Fix] diffusion: Keep the linear-GELU verdict cache out of torch.compile traces" both edit `can_use_linear_gelu`. They merge cleanly in either order. The adapter check sits above that PR's compile branch, so it also applies while tracing; keep that order if either one is rebased.

## Accuracy Tests

**LTX-2 two-stage** on 2xH200, against a stage-2-only exact reference: stage 1 runs at `lossless` and stage 2 is forced to `exact`. Stage-1 latents are bitwise identical across arms.

| | PSNR vs reference | high-frequency energy vs reference |
|---|---|---|
| main | 23.4–24.0 dB | 13–15% lower (blurrier) |
| this PR | 31.3–34.1 dB | within 1% |

`quality="exact"` output is bitwise unchanged.

**New server case** on H200, per key frame. The case passes at mean_abs_diff ≤ 3.0 and PSNR ≥ 30 dB against `quality="exact"`, and mean_abs_diff ≥ 12.0 against LoRA off.

| | vs `quality="exact"` | vs LoRA off | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| this PR | mean_abs_diff 0.73 / 1.41 / 1.55, PSNR 45.9 / 42.1 / 41.3 dB | mean_abs_diff 15.0–16.2 | pass |
| this PR with only the guard reverted to main | mean_abs_diff 8.35–8.75, PSNR 25.7–26.6 dB | mean_abs_diff 9.1–12.6 | fail |

The case takes 79–88 s on H200 (also re-run on this branch merged with the compile-guard PR: same numbers, pass).

**Unit tests**: `test_quality_fusion_lora.py` 5/5 pass on GPU. On main, `test_linear_gelu_static_guard_reads_the_wrapped_layer` fails: the wrapper hides `gather_output` on a TP2 layer.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Only requests with an active dynamic LoRA change path: their GELU sites run unfused. LTX-2 two-stage e2e on 2xH200 went from 7.34 s to 7.51 s. Requests without a LoRA, or with a merged one, keep the fused epilogue.

title: [Fix] diffusion: Keep the linear-GELU verdict cache out of torch.compile traces
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

#44643 caches the fused linear-GELU verdict per linear in a module-level `WeakKeyDictionary`, `_VERDICTS`. Under `torch.compile`, dynamo guards on that dict's size. DiT blocks share one compiled forward, so every new linear a block brings changes the size and recompiles the frame. On 4xB300, an LTX-2 compile run logged this on both ranks:

```
torch._dynamo hit config.recompile_limit (64) ... ltx_2.py:1263 ... last reason: len(...fused_linear_gelu_site._VERDICTS.data) != 28
```

After that, the blocks ran eager behind failing guards on every call.

This fixes a regression introduced by #44643 (same author).

## Modifications

In `fused_linear_gelu_site.py`, `can_use_linear_gelu` computes the input-independent verdict directly while tracing (`torch.compiler.is_compiling()`), as it did before #44643. Eager calls keep the cache. The verdict is the same either way, so outputs are unchanged.

New CUDA test `test_mounted_gelu_sites_compile_one_frame_across_linears` in `test_sites.py`: 12 blocks with two mounted sites each must compile to one frame. On H200 it fails on main and passes here (`test_sites.py` 27/27; with the dynamic-LoRA PR merged in, `test_sites.py` + `test_quality_fusion_lora.py` 32/32).

This PR and "[Fix] diffusion: Keep dynamic LoRA deltas on fused linear-GELU sites" both edit `can_use_linear_gelu`. They merge cleanly in either order. The LoRA PR's adapter check sits above this PR's compile branch, so it also applies while tracing; keep that order if either one is rebased.

## Accuracy Tests

The same verdict is computed, so the same path runs and outputs are unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

LTX-2 two-stage, compile profile, 2xH200, two interleaved rounds (e2e):

| | round 1 | round 2 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 10.754 s | 10.487 s |
| this PR | 10.152 s | 9.915 s |

That is −5.5% in both rounds:
- stage-1 step time: 0.198–0.206 s → 0.185–0.190 s;
- server ready: 128 s → 104 s;
- the `recompile_limit` line is gone from the log.

LTX-2 under compile is still slower than eager on H200, because of graph breaks after attention. That is out of scope here.

title: [Feat] sail: support sail fa3 and flashmla [3/N]
author: Vinsmoke86
body:
## Motivation

Refs #37519 

T-HEAD SAIL exposes a CUDA-compatible torch backend (`SailSRTPlatform` already exists in `platforms/sail.py`), but its attention kernels are not the ones `sgl_kernel` ships:

- `sgl_kernel` imports its compiled `flash_ops` (FA3) at import time, so the import fails on SAIL.
- SAIL provides its own FA3 interface (`flash_attn_interface`) and FlashMLA library, with different metadata semantics: a lazily-initialized scheduler-metadata object, a 320 `sm_parts` cap, and no `qv` / `only_qv` support.
- The FA3 backend's capability assert rejects MLA on SM 8.x, which is the capability SAIL reports.
- Channel-wise FP8 `kv_b_proj` weights go through `channel_quant_to_tensor_quant` + FP8 BMM, which SAIL does not support.

This PR lets MLA models (DeepSeek / GLM family) run on SAIL with `--attention-backend fa3` and `flashmla`, including MTP / EAGLE speculative decoding and CUDA graph. It keeps the existing backends unchanged: SAIL-specific behavior is injected via `@plugin_hook` and only loaded when SAIL hardware is detected.

## Modifications

### New: `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/sail/attention/`

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `flash_attention.py` | Wraps SAIL's `flash_attn_interface`: `flash_attn_with_kvcache`, `flash_attn_varlen_func`, `get_scheduler_metadata`, with the same signatures as `sgl_kernel.flash_attn`. FA4 (`ver=4`) and `only_qv=True` raise `NotImplementedError` with a clear message. |
| `flash_mla.py` | Wraps SAIL's FlashMLA library: `get_mla_metadata`, `flash_mla_with_kvcache`, `flash_mla_sparse_fwd`. |
| `sail_fa3_hooks.py` | Hooks `flashattention_backend.flash_attn_varlen_func` / `flash_attn_with_kvcache` (REPLACE) and `FlashAttentionBackend.__init__` (AROUND), so the FA3 backend calls the SAIL ops. |
| `sail_flashmla_hooks.py` | Hooks for `sgl_kernel.flash_mla.*` (REPLACE) and `FlashMLABackend`: caps the CUDA graph metadata buffer at 320 `sm_parts`, and replaces `_apply_decode_target_verify_metadata` (SAIL metadata object, DRAFT_EXTEND_V2 seq_lens) and `init_forward_metadata_in_graph`, so lazy metadata init runs inside graph capture. |
| `sail_dsa_hooks.py` | Hooks for `DSAFlashMLAMetadata.copy_` / `.slice` and `DeepseekSparseAttnBackend` graph-metadata init/replay, so the cached SAIL metadata is never overwritten during replay. |

### Platform detection and hook loading

- `platforms/sail.py`: adds `is_sail_available()` (cached; true when the CUDA device name contains `ZW`). When it returns true, imports the three hook modules to register them. They are applied by the existing `load_plugins()` → `HookRegistry.apply_hooks()` path.
- `runtime_context.py`: adds `"is_sail"` to `_PLATFORM_PROBES`, so `get_platform().is_sail` is available.
- `sgl_kernel/utils.py`: adds `is_sail()`. `sgl_kernel/flash_attn.py`: skips the `flash_ops` import on SAIL, so `import sgl_kernel.flash_attn` no longer fails there.

### Attention backend / model changes

- `attention_registry.py`: the FA3 capability assert also accepts `major == 8` with MLA when `_is_sail`.
- `flashmla_backend.py`: `forward_decode` / `forward_extend` accept optional `q_rope` / `k_rope`.
  - When `k_rope` is given, the KV cache is written with `set_mla_kv_buffer`.
  - When `q_rope` is given, the backend builds the 576-dim query with `concat_mla_absorb_q_general`.
  - The `ForwardMode.EXTEND` branch forwards them to `FlashInferMLAAttnBackend.forward_extend`.
- `deepseek_common/utils.py`: adds `"flashmla"` to `FORWARD_ABSORB_CORE_ATTENTION_BACKENDS`, so the model passes `q_rope` / `k_rope` separately and does not pre-concatenate. Adds `_is_sail`.
- `forward_mla.py`:
  - Uses `concat_mla_absorb_q_general` in place of `torch.cat` for the non-absorb-core `q` / `k` concat.
  - On SAIL, skips the FP8 `w_kc` / `w_vc` BMM branches; the weights are BF16 there (see below).
- `deepseek_weight_loader.py`: on SAIL, dequantizes channel-wise FP8 `kv_b_proj` to BF16 (`w * weight_scale`) instead of `channel_quant_to_tensor_quant`.

- `python/pyproject_other.toml`: adds `flash-attention-for-sail`, `flashinfer-for-sail` and `flashmla-for-sail` to `srt_sail` (no version pins).

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`: requires `get_device_sm() >= 89` before selecting the FlashInfer biased grouped topk kernel.

### Server-arg resolution

- `model_override_base.py`: on SAIL, MHA models default to `fa3`, under the same `is_no_spec_infer_or_topk_one` condition as Hopper.
- `model_hook.py`: on SAIL with an MLA backend, sets the prefill phase of `cuda_graph_config` to `DISABLED`. A captured prefill graph pins MLA to the absorbed path, which passes `qv` to FA3, and the SAIL FA3 interface rejects `qv`.

### Impact on non-SAIL platforms

- All `_is_sail` / `is_sail()` / `get_platform().is_sail` branches are false on non-SAIL devices, and no hook module is imported.
- **One shared behavior change:** with `"flashmla"` in `FORWARD_ABSORB_CORE_ATTENTION_BACKENDS`, CUDA FlashMLA now receives `q_rope` / `k_rope` and does the concat and `set_mla_kv_buffer` inside the backend. This replaces the concat in the model plus `set_kv_buffer`. It needs CUDA (Hopper) validation before going upstream.

### Known limitations

- SAIL FA3 does not support `qv` / `only_qv`. DSA + `fa3` (`DeepseekSparseAttnBackend._forward_fa3` always passes `qv`) is therefore not usable on SAIL; use `flashmla_kv` for DSA decode.
- Prefill CUDA graph is disabled for MLA on SAIL (see above).

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- TODO: fill in before merge -->

- [ ] SAIL: DeepSeek-V3 / GLM-5.x, `--attention-backend fa3` and `flashmla`, GSM8K
- [ ] SAIL: MTP / EAGLE (`speculative_attention_mode` prefill & decode), GSM8K + accept length
- [ ] CUDA (H100/H200): `--attention-backend flashmla`, DeepSeek-V3, GSM8K (regression check for the `FORWARD_ABSORB_CORE_ATTENTION_BACKENDS` change)

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- TODO: fill in before merge -->

- [ ] SAIL: `bench_serving` / `bench_one_batch` for fa3 and flashmla
- [ ] CUDA: `--attention-backend flashmla` decode throughput, no regression vs. base

title: [Perf] [NPU] AscendAttnBackend: D2H-free block-table gather for mirrorless DSA graph replay
author: wutaosang
body:
## Motivation

Enable mirrorless speculative decoding for GLM-5.x/DSA on Ascend with `SGLANG_NPU_ATTN_BACKEND_NEEDS_CPU_SEQ_LENS=0`, building on #38461.

Graph metadata preparation currently relies on the CPU sequence-length mirror or gathers the full captured block-table width. Carrying a host-side upper bound derived from KV allocation lengths allows replay to limit the gather range without reading sequence lengths back from the device.

## Modifications

- Publish `max_seq_len_host` from the maximum page-aligned KV allocation length when the CPU sequence-length mirror is absent.
- Propagate this bound through `ForwardBatch`, decode graph replay, draft-extend replay, and multi-step draft views.
- Use the host bound to size block-table gathers, including speculative offsets, and clear unused table columns. Preserve the full-width fallback when neither a CPU mirror nor a host bound is available.
- Guard eager CPU length updates against an absent mirror and pass device lengths to `_npu_paged_attention` for mirrorless eager decode.
- Keep the CPU mirror enabled with a warning for hybrid SWA and `ASCEND_USE_FIA`, whose attention paths require host-side lengths.

title: [Perf] LoRA: improve throughput and GPU memory usage for multi-LoRA serving under PP
author: glenliu21
body:
## Motivation

Pipeline-parallelism is a foundational paradigm for serving large models efficiently. However, currently, multi-LoRA serving does not handle PP in the most efficient way possible, both in terms of throughput and GPU memory usage.

#### Example

Consider PP=2, with 4 slots on each GPU. Microbatch A uses 2 adapters, and the scheduler is building microbatch B from requests for 3 other adapters. Both microbatches pass through both GPUs, but each GPU only considers the adapters of its own microbatch. Since B's 3 adapters fit in 4 slots on their own, the scheduler admits all of B's requests, even though A and B together need 5. Every GPU then evicts and loads adapters on every step as A and B take turns. With this PR, each GPU keeps the adapters of all in-flight micro-batches loaded, and the scheduler only admits a request if its adapter fits alongside them. B gets 2 of its 3 adapters, and the request for the third waits until a slot frees up.

```
main
  Stage 0 │▒ load ▒▒█ run A █│▒ load ▒▒█ run B █│▒ load ▒▒█ run A █│▒ load ▒▒█ run B █│
  Stage 1 │                  │▒ load ▒▒█ run A █│▒ load ▒▒█ run B █│▒ load ▒▒█ run A █│▒ load ▒▒█ run B █│

branch
  Stage 0 │▒ load ▒▒█ run A █│▒ load ▒▒█ run B █│█ run A █│█ run B █│
  Stage 1 │                  │▒ load ▒▒█ run A █│█ run B █│█ run A █│█ run B █│

█ compute   ▒ load adapters
```

## Modifications

There are two main modifications that I made:
- `LoRAManager`s on a given PP stage should prioritize keeping adapters that are needed in other stages in the memory pool. Previously, `LoRAManager`s were only aware of the adapters needed for their own next microbatch.
- Each stage's LoRA memory pool only allocates adapter weights for the layers that stage uses, which reduces the GPU memory per adapter slot by a factor of the PP size.

## Accuracy Tests

- Added a new unit test for PP LoRA
- All LoRA tests pass

## Speed Tests and Profiling

I benchmarked on 2xH200s on a single node. To benchmark throughput and memory improvements for `main` and my branch:

1. Start the server:

```
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct \
    --pp-size 2 \
    --enable-lora \
    --max-loaded-loras 16 \
    --max-loras-per-batch 8 \
    --lora-paths \
        adapter0=advy/llama71b-mentalchat16k \
        adapter1=advy/llama71b-career-guidance \
        adapter2=clembench-playpen/llama-3.1-70B-Instruct_playpen_SFT_DFINAL_0.6K-steps \
        adapter3=reissbaker/r1-llama-70b-distill-lora \
        adapter4=kushwanth7/llama-70b-manim-lora \
        adapter5=kmtao/llama3.1-70B-HIVDB-adapter \
        adapter6=cosmicishan/llama-70b-mcq-dlgenai \
        adapter7=impactIA/chimere \
        adapter8=dv347/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-honly \
        adapter9=cyborgwittgenstein/cassie-70b-v7-lora \
        adapter10=eac123/MarcusChenHolloway-70B-LoRA \
        adapter11=hf-100/Llama-3.1-Spellbound-StoryWriter-70b-instruct-0.2-lora \
        adapter12=Strike0010/hs-classifier-70b-dpo-iter2-arm1 \
        adapter13=ReflexxIA/reflexx-70b-v1 \
        adapter14=Boffl/BullingerLM-llama3.1-70B-instruct-qa \
        adapter15=gane5hvarma/joe-adapter
```

2. Run a benchmark where there are more adapters being served than slots in the memory pool:

```
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \
    --backend sglang \
    --base-url http://localhost:30000 \
    --dataset-name random \
    --num-prompts 400 \
    --max-concurrency 32 \
    --random-input-len 512 \
    --random-output-len 512 \
    --lora-request-distribution uniform \
    --lora-name \
        adapter0 \
        adapter1 \
        adapter2 \
        adapter3 \
        adapter4 \
        adapter5 \
        adapter6 \
        adapter7 \
        adapter8 \
        adapter9 \
        adapter10 \
        adapter11 \
        adapter12 \
        adapter13 \
        adapter14 \
        adapter15
```

#### Throughput Results

| Metric | `main` | PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Benchmark duration (s) | 2,370.2 | 420.1 | **−82.3%** |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 44.3 | 250.2 | **5.6×** |
| Mean E2E latency (ms) | 187,553 | 31,353 | **−83.3%** |
| Median E2E latency (ms) | 189,043 | 30,307 | **−84.0%** |
| P99 E2E latency (ms) | 404,723 | 79,866 | **−80.3%** |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 709.4 | 77.0 | **−89.1%** |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 722.3 | 77.0 | **−89.3%** |
| P99 TPOT (ms) | 928.4 | 87.8 | **−90.5%** |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 2,601 | 11,196 | +330% |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 854 | 2,341 | +174% |
| P99 TTFT (ms) | 33,987 | 47,861 | +41% |

The scheduler now admits a request only when its adapter fits alongside those of in-flight micro-batches, instead of evicting adapters that are still in use. Thus, new requests may wait longer for a slot (resulting in higher TTFT), but no longer cause reloads on every decode step, resulting in a much lower TPOT.

title: [Perf] dspark: Combine the draft's mHC streams from bf16 without an fp32 copy
author: hnyls2002
body:
- The DSpark draft head combined its mHC streams with `mhc_combine(x.flatten(1).float(), ...)`. The `.float()` copied the whole `[tokens, hc_mult * hidden]` input to fp32 before the kernel read it.
- `_mhc_combine_kernel` widens every element to fp32 as it loads it, so the bf16 rows now go to the kernel directly, as the target model's final combine already does. bf16 to fp32 is exact, and the kernel computes the same fp32 products in the same order.

Output is bitwise identical to before.

Verification: the combine on the bf16 rows matches the fp32-copy path bit for bit from 1 to 65536 rows on GB300, and the copy no longer runs.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Shard LTX-2 stage 2 over the CFG ranks as Ulysses
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

LTX-2/2.3 two-stage runs stage 2, the distilled refiner, without CFG. Under `--enable-cfg-parallel`, `LTX2RefinementStage` was `MAIN_RANK_ONLY`, or `MAIN_RANK_ONLY_AND_SEND_TO_OTHERS` with parallel VAE decode. So on 2 GPUs one GPU sat idle for all of stage 2. At 768x512x121 on 2xH200 that is 3 steps at 0.394 s each.

TensorRT-LLM runs stage 2 as Ulysses 2 on the same ranks. In a 4xB300 benchmark round, sglang's stage 2 took 0.143 s/step x3 under breakable CUDA graphs, while TensorRT-LLM took 0.30 s for the whole of stage 2.

Sharding only pays off once stage 2 is long enough. At CI's 768x512x25 (1536 stage-2 tokens), it made `LTX2RefinementStage` slower, so the new path is gated on the stage-2 sequence length.

## Modifications

At stage-2 entry, every CFG rank already holds the same inputs:
- stage 1 combines the guided prediction with an all-reduce, so all CFG ranks hold the same latents after every step;
- the latent upsampler is replicated;
- stage 2 draws its re-noise from a generator re-seeded from the request seed. LTX-2 resets the batch generators and LTX-2.3 builds a fresh one, so every rank draws the same noise.

So a stage without CFG can be sequence-sharded over the CFG ranks instead of leaving them idle:

- `parallel_state.py`: when `cfg > 1` and `sp == 1`, the CFG ranks also form one pure-Ulysses group (`get_cfg_sequence_parallel_group()`). `SequenceParallelGroupCoordinator.over_group` builds it as a view over the CFG group's communicators. It adds no process group or NCCL communicator, and destroying the CFG group releases it.
- `use_sequence_parallel_group()` points the SP accessors at that group for one scope. Everything that reads `get_sp_group()` follows it: latent shard and gather, RoPE offsets, the Ulysses all-to-alls. The exchanges use the usual SP transports: the 2-rank CUDA-IPC all-to-all by default, otherwise NCCL.
- `stages/base.py`: new `StageParallelismType.SEQUENCE_PARALLEL_OVER_CFG_RANKS`. `parallel_executor.py` runs such a stage on every CFG rank inside that scope.
- The executor reads each stage's parallelism per batch through the new `PipelineStage.parallelism_type_for(batch)`, which defaults to `parallelism_type`.
- `LTX2RefinementStage.parallelism_type_for` returns the new type only when the group exists and stage 2 has at least `CFG_SP_MIN_TOKENS_PER_RANK` (2304) video tokens per rank. It reads the sequence length of the packed stage-2 latents, which every rank holds with the same shape, so all ranks pick the same path. Shorter requests keep the previous main-rank path, and so do CFG ranks that have SP of their own (`sp > 1`). A warmup takes the same path as serving at the same shape, so breakable CUDA graphs capture what serving replays.
- On the new path, stage 2 ends with the SP gather, so every rank holds the full latents for decode. With parallel decode, the post-stage batch broadcast no longer runs.

Tests: `test/unit/test_sequence_parallel_over_cfg_ranks.py` runs 2 gloo ranks on CPU with cfg=2, sp=1. It checks:
- the group is a view over the CFG communicators (same device group, Ulysses 2, ring 1), and the global SP size stays 1;
- the executor runs an `LTX2RefinementStage` batch one token per rank short of the threshold on the main rank only, and the other rank keeps its batch;
- a batch at the threshold runs on both ranks with SP world 2, and SP 1 is restored afterwards;
- inside the scope, LTX-2's video and audio latents round-trip exactly through shard and gather, the shard's start frame follows the rank, and Ulysses attention matches single-rank SDPA for both sharded and replicated inputs.

No files are shared with #45942, #45943, #45944 or #45948, and this PR merges cleanly with all four. With parallel VAE decode, stage 2 now leaves the full latents on both ranks instead of broadcasting the batch. #45942 changes the decode itself, so the two PRs are independent. Stage 2's exchange runs on the 2-rank IPC transport, which #45948 (N-rank transport) does not touch.

## Accuracy Tests

2xH200, LTX-2 two-stage 768x512x121, `--enable-cfg-parallel`, against main:

- PSNR 33.4–35.7 dB, high-frequency energy unchanged. The output is not bitwise equal: stage-2 attention now runs on two head shards, which reorders the sums.
- Breakable CUDA graphs: no hang, and the output is bitwise equal to eager in every arm. Main captures 3 graphs, with stage 2 on rank 0 only. This PR captures 4, with stage 2 on both ranks at (1, 3072, 128).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

2xH200, LTX-2 two-stage 768x512x121, `--enable-cfg-parallel`. Server benchmark with a fresh server per run, arms interleaved.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| stage-2 step, eager | 0.394 s | 0.280 s (−29%) |
| stage-2 step, breakable CUDA graphs | 0.365 s | 0.2345 s (−36%) |
| e2e, default profile (eager) | 7.336 s | 6.877 s (−6.3%) |
| e2e, breakable CUDA graphs | 5.966 s | 5.386 s (−9.7%) |
| peak memory GPU0 / GPU1, breakable CUDA graphs | 85.2 / 78.1 GB | 80.8 / 80.6 GB |

- The compile profile went from 10.508 s to 9.757 s, but that was measured with this change stacked on other pending changes.
- Eager peak memory is 0.8–1.8 GB higher.
- VAE decode is slightly slower on this branch under breakable CUDA graphs: 0.665 s to 0.715 s. The e2e numbers above include it.
- 121 frames is above the threshold below, so the gate keeps these numbers. LTX-2.3 is measured in the next section.

### Sequence-length gate

2xH200, two-stage 768x512, `--enable-cfg-parallel --dit-layerwise-offload false --performance-mode speed`, eager. Server benchmark, one warm request per shape, then medians of the measured requests. LTX-2 25/57/89/121 frames ran in 2 interleaved rounds (n≥4); the other shapes ran on one server per arm (n=2–4). The server rounds the frame count so the latent frames split evenly over 2 GPUs, so the table lists the served frames. "Step" is `[LTX2RefinementStage] average time per step`, and "e2e" is the server's request time.

LTX-2:

| frames (served) | stage-2 tokens | per rank | main step | ungated step | gated step | main e2e | ungated e2e | gated path |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 25 | 1536 | 768 | 203 ms | 277 ms | 200 ms | 6.21 s | 6.40 s | main rank |
| 57 | 3072 | 1536 | 210 ms | 280 ms | 209 ms | 6.48 s | 6.68 s | main rank |
| 73 | 3840 | 1920 | 254 ms | 280 ms | 254 ms | 6.74 s | 6.65 s | main rank |
| 89 | 4608 | 2304 | 304 ms | 282 ms | 274 ms | 6.93 s | 6.75 s | SP over CFG |
| 105 | 5376 | 2688 | 363 ms | 282 ms | – | 7.04 s | 6.80 s | SP over CFG |
| 121 | 6144 | 3072 | 397 ms | 280 ms | 277 ms | 7.38 s | 6.91 s | SP over CFG |

- The ungated step stays at about 280 ms at every length. Eager stage 2 is host-bound at these sizes, and Ulysses adds about 75 ms of host work per step. So the new path wins only once the main rank's step passes that floor, between 1920 and 2304 tokens per rank (about 2.1k by interpolation). The threshold is 2304, the first measured win (−7% per step).
- End to end, the crossover is lower, at about 1.6–1.9k tokens per rank. Between stage 2 and decode, the main-rank path also spends 80–160 ms broadcasting the batch, which the new path skips. At 1920 tokens per rank, the gate gives up about 30 ms e2e to keep the faster stage 2.
- Stage 1 varies by about ±100 ms between server launches. That is why the e2e columns are noisier than the step columns.
- CI's `ltx_2_two_stage_t2v` settings (default serve args, 768x512x25): `LTX2RefinementStage` takes 590 ms on main, 841 ms ungated, and 609 ms gated.

LTX-2.3 (`Lightricks/LTX-2.3`, same flags):

| frames (served) | per rank | main step | ungated step | gated step | main e2e | ungated e2e | gated path |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 25 | 768 | 147 ms | 221 ms | 145 ms | 5.61 s | 5.76 s | main rank |
| 73 | 1920 | 226 ms | 224 ms | – | 6.16 s | 6.18 s | main rank |
| 89 | 2304 | 265 ms | 282 ms | 287 ms | 6.57 s | 6.49 s | SP over CFG |
| 105 | 2688 | 320 ms | 307 ms | – | 7.67 s | 7.50 s | SP over CFG |
| 121 | 3072 | 352 ms | 229 ms | 226 ms | 8.16 s | 7.66 s | SP over CFG |

- On LTX-2.3, the ungated step does not grow monotonically with length: 224, 282, 307 and 229 ms at 1920 to 3072 tokens per rank. At 2304 tokens per rank, the new path makes its stage 2 6% slower. The request is still about 74 ms faster, because the batch broadcast is skipped.

Breakable CUDA graphs, with warmup at the serving shape (LTX-2, n=2):

| frames | main step / graphs | ungated step / graphs | gated step / graphs | main e2e | ungated e2e | gated e2e |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 25 | 87.1 ms / 3 | 91.5 ms / 4 | 87.4 ms / 3 | 2.53 s | 2.39 s | 2.52 s |
| 121 | 367.4 ms / 3 | 236.6 ms / 4 | 237.2 ms / 4 | 6.02 s | 5.44 s | 5.43 s |

- The gated server captures the graphs of the path it serves: 3 graphs at 25 frames (stage 2 on rank 0 only), 4 at 121 frames.
- Graphs remove the host floor, so at 25 frames the new path is only 5% slower per step. The request is 141 ms faster because the batch broadcast is skipped. The eager-measured threshold gives up that win for short requests under graphs.

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Perf] diffusion: Cut LTX-2 denoising-step host overhead
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Every LTX-2 denoising step pays two host-side costs.

1. **Sigma reads sync the host.** Each step moved `scheduler.sigmas[i]` and `[i+1]` to the device and called `.item()` on both. The stage-1 guider path called `.item()` on sigma again after the forward. Each read blocks the host until the stream drains, so the host cannot enqueue the next step while the GPU runs the current one. Stage 2 also paid a pageable H2D copy per sigma, because its distilled schedule lives on the CPU. Once the forward is graph-replayed (breakable CUDA graphs), this sync is the bubble that remains. Removing it lets the host run ahead.
2. **The prompt mask is rebuilt in every block.** The 0/1 prompt key mask goes to every block. Each block's two prompt cross-attentions (`LocalAttention`) turned it into the additive SDPA mask again: a cast, a subtract and a multiply per call. That is 288 small launches per forward over 48 blocks.

## Modifications

- `ltx_2/denoising.py`: `_prepare_denoising_loop` takes fp32 host and device copies of the sigma schedule once per loop (`LTX2DenoisingContext.sigmas_host` / `sigmas_device`). Steps index the device copy for tensor math and the host copy for Python scalars. The guider's x0 conversion takes the device sigma instead of its Python float. `_ltx2_velocity_to_x0` scales in fp32 either way.
- `layers/attention/layer.py`: `_prepare_sdpa_mask` is renamed `prepare_sdpa_mask`. `LocalAttention` now calls it instead of keeping its own inline copy of the same conversion. The values are the same for float and 0/1 masks.
- `models/dits/ltx_2.py`: the model forward converts the video and audio prompt masks once with `prepare_sdpa_mask`, and the blocks pass the float mask through. `LocalAttention` only casts and reshapes a float mask. Prompt cross-attention is always `LocalAttention`, and the prompt mask never goes through the SP K/V gather.

Tests:
- `test_ltx2_bcg_coords.py`, `test_steps_never_read_device_sigmas_on_host`: runs one denoising step in each guidance mode (official CFG, batched guider, TI2V, HQ, legacy, legacy batched). The sigma schedule's `item()` / `__float__` / `__bool__` raise, and the outputs must equal a run with a plain tensor. It fails on main in every mode.
- `test_ltx2_bcg_coords.py`, `test_tensor_sigma_x0_matches_python_float`: the fp32 x0 conversion gives bitwise the same result for a tensor sigma and a float sigma.
- `test_ltx2_prompt_mask.py`: `LocalAttention` gives bitwise the same output for a prebuilt additive mask and for the raw 0/1 mask. A 2-block LTX-2 model converts the masks exactly twice per forward (video and audio), and its output matches the per-block conversion bitwise.

No files are shared with #45942, #45943, #45944 or #45948, or with "Shard LTX-2 stage 2 over the CFG ranks as Ulysses". This PR merges cleanly with all of them.

## Accuracy Tests

2xH200, LTX-2 two-stage, `default` profile. Decoded frames and audio are bitwise identical across base, the sigma commit and the prompt-mask commit, in every round.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

2xH200, LTX-2 two-stage, `default` (eager) profile. Three interleaved rounds, e2e median per run:

| round | base | + sigma reads without sync | + prompt mask once per forward |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 7.571 s | 7.392 s | 7.161 s |
| 2 | 7.507 s | 7.487 s | 7.248 s |
| 3 | 7.395 s | 7.422 s | 7.260 s |

- Prompt-mask commit vs sigma commit: −0.231 / −0.239 / −0.162 s (−2.9%), consistent in every round. The stage-1 step went from 0.130 s to 0.123 s.
- The sigma commit alone cannot be separated from noise in eager mode: its sign differs between rounds. It pays off under graph replay, where the per-step sync is what stops the host from running ahead.
- The base for these numbers was main plus the fixes in #45944 and #45943 (the latter in an earlier revision). This PR does not depend on either.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Remove per-step and per-request host syncs in Cosmos3 and Qwen-Image-2.1
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Two blocking device reads sit on the host's critical path:

1. **Cosmos3, every step.** The denoising loop checked the CFG window, and the Transfer control-CFG window, with `t.item()` on the device timestep. So the host waited for each step's kernels to finish before it launched the next step.
2. **Qwen-Image-2.1 edit, every request.** The edit path built the VAE latent mean/std with `new_tensor` right after launching the condition-image VAE encode. That pageable upload made the host wait for the encode before it could start the prompt's image preprocessing.

## Modifications

- `cosmos3.py`: the loop takes one host copy of the timestep schedule (`timesteps.tolist()`), and `_cfg_active_at` reads the window from those floats. The per-step decisions and kernels are unchanged.
- `qwen_image21.py`: `QwenImage21EncodingStage` uploads the latent mean/std once per `(dtype, device)` and reuses them, so the preprocessing overlaps the encode. The normalization is bit-identical.

Tests:
- `test_cosmos3_rollout.py::test_cfg_window_check_reads_host_timesteps`: runs the denoising loop with a `[400, 1000]` CFG window over timesteps whose `item()` / `float()` / `bool()` raise. The window must still choose batched CFG at 999, 700 and 400, and the cond branch alone at 399 and 100. It fails on main.
- `test_qwen_image21.py::test_condition_latents_reuse_uploaded_latent_stats`: two edit requests must produce the reference-normalized condition latents bitwise, and the second request must reuse the first one's mean/std tensors (checked by identity).

No files are shared with #45942, #45943, #45944 or #45948.

## Accuracy Tests

The output pixels are identical across arms for both models.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Server benchmark, 2 interleaved rounds x 5 repeats, e2e. Each commit was measured on its own against the same base.

| case | GPUs | base (round 1 / 2) | this PR (round 1 / 2) |

title: [Perf] diffusion: Turn on breakable CUDA graphs by default for LTX-2/LTX-2.3 two-stage serving
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

LTX-2 two-stage stage 1 runs at half resolution (~1.5k video tokens), so its step is launch-bound: on 4xB300, TRT-LLM's CUDA-graph configuration runs a stage-1 step in 0.044 s against 0.192 s for sglang eager. Breakable CUDA graphs (BCG) close most of that gap, and the graphs replay the same kernels, so the output is bitwise equal to eager. Today BCG is opt-in, so every flagless LTX deployment leaves this on the table.

BCG stays opt-in everywhere else. The validated-model list records correctness, not speed: FLUX.3 won 1 of 10 cells, Qwen-Image-2.1 on 1 GPU is 0.5% slower, and MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA showed no speedup.

| HW (2 GPUs, CFG parallel) | Model | Eager (s) | BCG (s) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B300 | LTX-2 T2V 768x512x121, 40 steps | 6.693 / 6.882 | 3.797 / 3.785 | −44% |
| B300 | LTX-2.3 T2V 768x512x121, 30 steps | 6.294 / 6.202 | 4.735 / 4.726 | −24% |
| H200 | LTX-2 T2V 768x512x121, 40 steps | 7.398 / 7.593 | 5.969 / 5.970 | −20% |

B300 rows: two interleaved rounds, fresh server per arm. H200 rows: see Speed Tests.

## Modifications

- `ModelDeploymentConfig.bcg_default_pipeline_class_names`: the pipeline classes measured faster with BCG. `LTX2PipelineConfig` lists `LTX2TwoStagePipeline`; LTX-2.3 inherits it. The field names the pipeline class because one config serves the one-stage, two-stage and HQ pipelines, and only two-stage was measured.
- `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph` defaults to unset. `_adjust_breakable_cuda_graph_support` resolves an unset flag to on only when all of these hold, and to off otherwise:
  - the pipeline class is opted in and the checkpoint is on the validated BCG list;
  - `--performance-mode` is `auto` or `speed`;
  - the platform is CUDA (`current_platform.is_cuda()`, so ROCm, NPU and MPS stay off) with separate host and device memory (GB10 stays off);
  - the server warms up at startup (`sglang serve`); `sglang generate` and request warmup would pay a full extra generation;
  - monolithic role, ComfyUI mode off;
  - no torch.compile, Cache-DiT, dynamic batching or `--lora-path`;
  - both stage DiTs stay resident: no DiT component, snapshot or layerwise offload, no FSDP, a GPU with at least 130 GiB (the threshold LTX already uses to pick `resident` mode), and LTX-2.3 in `resident` mode.
  An explicit `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph true|false` always wins. When the default turns BCG on, the server logs `[Diffusion BCG] enabled by default for LTX2TwoStagePipeline; pass --enable-breakable-cuda-graph false to run eager.`
- Video BCG warmup now captures the model's full default resolution. It used the server-warmup resolution, which caps video at 832x480: LTX's 768x512 fits under the cap, but Wan (1280x720), MiniMax-H3 (1344x768) or LTX-2.5 (1920x1088) would capture a shape no request uses. Frame counts already used the full default under BCG.
- Graphs replay the weights and LoRA branches they were captured with, and serving never re-captures. So an external LoRA change (`/v1/set_lora`, merge, unmerge) or `resume_memory_occupation` now drops the captured graphs, and later requests run eager with a warning. The two-stage pipeline's own per-request distilled-LoRA switch is part of the capture and is unaffected.
- Docs: CLI reference and the LTX cookbook describe the default, its gates and the captured shape.

Behavior to know about (one-shot `MISSED` warning, then eager; no regression against today's eager path):
- Only the captured shape replays: 768x512, 121 frames, the warmup's quality level, text-to-video. The OpenAI video API defaults to 4 seconds, which LTX rounds to 89 frames, so those requests run eager unless the server passes `--warmup-num-frames 89`. Image-conditioned requests run eager.
- A request at another quality level (for example `quality="exact"`) runs eager; the runners are already keyed per level.
- Per-request attention-backend overrides are rejected under BCG, as before.

Tests:
- `test_server_args.py::TestBreakableCudaGraphDefault`: flagless LTX-2 two-stage serving on a mocked 141 GiB CUDA GPU resolves BCG on and captures 768x512; LTX-2.3 needs `resident`; explicit off, offline runs, request warmup, memory/manual modes, compile, batching, `--lora-path`, ComfyUI, one-stage and HQ pipelines, unvalidated checkpoints, every DiT offload form, low free memory and an 80 GB card resolve it off; ROCm (`is_cuda()` false) and shared-memory devices stay off; explicit on elsewhere is unchanged.
- `test_cfg_parallel_warmup.py::test_bcg_capture_keeps_the_full_default_video_resolution`.
- `test_diffusion_bcg_padding.py::TestBCGWeightChangeAfterCapture`: `set_lora`, merge, unmerge and `resume_memory_occupation` drop the graphs, and the runner then runs eager.

On main the default-on, platform-gate, capture-shape and graph-drop tests fail; the gate-off cases pass there by construction and guard the gates from here on.

## Accuracy Tests

LTX-2 two-stage on 2xH200, CFG parallel, the benchmark-default command (`--performance-mode speed`), seed 42, 768x512x121. Same MP4 bytes and same decoded-frame md5 for every arm:

| Server | Request | Path | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| this PR, no BCG flag | default quality | BCG replay | `742a1862…` |
| this PR, `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph false` | default quality | eager | `742a1862…` |
| main | default quality | eager | `742a1862…` |
| this PR, no BCG flag | `quality="exact"` | eager (no graph at that level) | same as eager server |
| this PR, no BCG flag | API default, 89 frames | eager (`MISSED`) | same as eager server |
| this PR, no BCG flag | after `/v1/set_lora` | eager (graphs dropped) | same as eager server after the same call |

With the CI-shaped request (1 second = 25 frames, `quality="exact"`, `--warmup-num-frames 25 --warmup-sampling-params '{"quality": "exact"}'`), BCG, eager and main also produce identical outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

LTX-2 two-stage, 2xH200, CFG parallel, the benchmark-default command (`--performance-mode speed --dit-layerwise-offload false --enable-torch-compile false`, no BCG flag), 768x512x121, 40 steps. [diffusion-bench-framework](https://github.com/mickqian/diffusion-bench-framework) `single_e2e` (median of 2 measured requests after warmup), fresh server per run, rounds interleaved main / PR / main / PR:

| | round 1 | round 2 |
|---|---|---|
| main (eager) | 7.398 s | 7.593 s |
| this PR (BCG by default) | 5.969 s | 5.970 s |

Stage breakdown (round 2): `LTX2AVDenoisingStage` 5.368 → 3.702 s, `LTX2RefinementStage` 1.187 → 1.096 s, decode unchanged (0.67 s). On Hopper the FA attention calls stay eager, so each forward captures 289 segments; on B300 LTX attention is captured as well (1 segment per forward), which is why the gain there is about twice as large.

Cost on 2xH200, this PR with and without `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph false`, two alternating rounds:

| | BCG default | `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph false` |
|---|---|---|
| Startup to healthy (round 1 / round 2) | 104.1 / 84.1 s | 86.1 / 78.0 s |
| Server warmup | 121 frames, 40 steps: 52.1 / 32.2 s | 25 frames, 2 steps: 31.6 / 26.5 s |
| Peak memory per request (rank 0) | 82,654 MB | 75,690–75,704 MB |

Startup grows by about 6 s once caches are warm (about 20 s on a cold first start), and peak memory by 6.9 GB. On B300 the same comparison was +2 s and +0.95 GB (LTX-2) / +1.1 GB (LTX-2.3).

## CI and baselines

No perf or memory baseline should move:
- The H100 suite's LTX cases run on 80 GB cards, below the 130 GiB gate, so they stay eager. The B200, 5090 and XPU suites have no LTX two-stage case, and AMD is not CUDA.
- The explicit-BCG CI tests (`test_diffusion_bcg_*zimage_turbo.py`) are image models; the warmup-resolution change only affects video.
- If an H200/B200-class LTX two-stage case is added later, its runtime peak will include the capture (+~7 GB on Hopper), and its warmup runs one full generation; seed its baseline with the usual two-step flow.

## Risks

- Startup grows by one full-shape generation plus capture: +6 s on 2xH200 with warm caches, about +20 s on a cold first start, +2 s on B300.
- Peak memory grows by ~7 GB on Hopper, where attention stays eager (289 segments per signature), against ~1 GB on Blackwell, where LTX attention is captured too (1 segment). The 130 GiB gate keeps 80 GB cards, whose speed-mode headroom is smaller than that, on eager.
- LTX-2.3 is validated on B300 only (above). The H200 runs here cover LTX-2.
- #45943 changes the dynamic-LoRA linear path that stage 2 runs; BCG captures whatever eager runs, so outputs stay equal to eager, but its speed should be re-checked once both land.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Perf] diffusion: Keep every component resident in auto mode when memory allows
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

`--performance-mode auto` places components from a static per-model allowlist. Above `keep_resident_min_available_gb` (the model's value, else 45 GB for image and 120 GB for video models) only `keep_resident_components` stay resident: the VAE by default, plus the DiT for image models. Everything else streams layer by layer at any memory size:
- Z-Image, Ideogram-4, FLUX, Qwen-Image and LTX-2 stream their text encoder even on a 288 GB GPU. A B300 server log reads `267.1 GiB of free device memory selects layerwise offload for text_encoder` and then `resident=0/36`; Z-Image-Turbo spends 0.066 s of a 0.354 s request moving 3.4 GB over PCIe.
- Wan2.2-T2V/I2V-A14B list `auto` in `dit_layerwise_offload_modes` and set no threshold, so both 14B experts stream layer by layer on every GPU, including H200/B200/B300. That also pins ~54 GB of host memory per rank.

On H100, Z-Image-Turbo with every component resident was 12% faster than auto (0.701/0.699 vs 0.793/0.799 s). The memory-aware fix was meant to come from the warmup-calibrated planner (#37917/#37918), which is not merged. This PR adds a conservative interim rule.

## Modifications

- Memory-rich tier in auto mode (`ServerArgsAutoTuner._fits_all_components_resident`): when the least-free selected GPU has at least twice the per-GPU weight bytes free, every component without an explicit placement stays resident. That means no default layerwise list, no DiT layerwise and component offload cleared, which is the placement `speed` mode gives. Explicit placement flags still win per component.
  - Weights are sized before load from the cached checkpoint's safetensors headers (`checkpoint_component_sizes` in `loader/utils.py`): every `model_index.json` component, counted in its serving precision (`resolve_component_precision`, else as stored), with DiT folders divided by `tp_size`. Text encoders count as full copies even when TP-folded, which is conservative.
  - The tier does not apply, and the per-model policy runs as before, when the checkpoint is not fully cached yet, holds non-safetensors or quantized weights, or is overridden (`--quantization`, `--transformer-weights-path`, SVDQuant, component paths, weights or quantizations, model overlays). It also does not apply with dynamic batching (the factor of two assumes one request's activations), on shared host/device memory (GB10) or on MPS.
  - The rule is platform-agnostic. On ROCm, where auto has no layerwise defaults and offloads the text encoder whole, a GPU that fits the rule now keeps it resident too.
- Wan2.2-T2V/I2V-A14B set `keep_resident_min_available_gb=120` with the DiT and VAE resident. Both experts stay on the GPU on H200-class cards and above; 80 GB cards keep streaming (the two bf16 experts alone are 53 GiB). This holds even when the tier cannot size the checkpoint.

What changes on common GPUs (single GPU unless noted; per-GPU weights at serving precision):

| Model | Weights per GPU | Tier at 2x | H100 80 GB (~79 GiB free) | H200 (~139 GiB free) | 32 GB RTX 5090 (~31 GiB free) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Z-Image-Turbo | 19.1 GiB | 38 GiB | all resident (text encoder was layerwise) | all resident | unchanged |
| FLUX.1-dev | 31.4 GiB | 63 GiB | all resident (T5 was layerwise) | all resident | unchanged |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 | 30.2 GiB | 60 GiB | all resident | all resident | unchanged |
| Qwen-Image | 53.7 GiB (TP2: 34.7) | 107 GiB (TP2: 69) | unchanged (TP2: all resident) | all resident | unchanged |
| Cosmos3-Nano | 32.5 GiB | 65 GiB | all resident | all resident | unchanged |
| Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B | 24.3 GiB (fp32 T5) | 49 GiB | all resident | all resident | unchanged |
| LTX-2 | 65.7 GiB | 131 GiB | unchanged | all resident | unchanged |
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B | 74.9 GiB (fp32 T5) | 150 GiB | unchanged | both experts and VAE resident (threshold), T5 layerwise | unchanged |
| Ideogram-4 FP8, ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4 | not sized (quantized or `--transformer-path`) | | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged |

B200 (178 GiB free) and B300 (288 GiB) fit every bf16 row, Wan2.2-A14B included. Rows other than Z-Image-Turbo and Wan2.2-A14B follow from the sizing rule; they were not run.

Tests:
- `test_server_args.py`: Z-Image-Turbo keeps every component resident at 139 GiB free and at 45 GiB free (the bf16 serving size fits twice there, the fp32-stored bytes would not). 31 and 23 GiB free resolve exactly as an unsized checkpoint does. Batching, shared host/device memory and an unsized checkpoint keep the text encoder layerwise. Off CUDA, the tier replaces the whole-component text-encoder offload. Wan2.2-A14B keeps both experts and the VAE resident at 139 GiB free while T5 streams, and keeps everything resident at 280 GiB free with sizes.
- `test_weight_utils.py::TestCheckpointComponentSizes`: per-component sizes from a local layout and from a cached hub snapshot without network access; a partially downloaded snapshot (only `model_index.json`, as before the worker downloads), a missing shard, `.bin` weights or FP8 weights stay unsized.
- `conftest.mock_cuda_platform` and the server-args helper stub the sizing, so tests that construct `ServerArgs` for a real repo id never read the runner's HF cache.
- Docs: the `auto` row of the performance-mode table in the deployment cookbook describes the tier.

The new tests fail on main: the sizing helper does not exist there, and the all-resident, serving-precision, off-CUDA and Wan2.2 assertions fail on their own.

## Accuracy Tests

Placement only: the same modules run on the same device, so outputs do not change. On 1xH200, Z-Image-Turbo outputs for five distinct prompts have the same md5s on main and this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Z-Image-Turbo on 1xH200, flagless `sglang serve` (auto mode), 1024x1024, 9 steps. Each run: fresh server, 2 warmup requests, then 5 measured requests, each with a distinct prompt so the conditioning cache never answers the text encoder's work. Rounds interleaved main / PR / main / PR:

| | e2e median (round 1 / round 2) | `TextEncodingStage` | Peak memory per request |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (text encoder layerwise) | 0.952 / 0.954 s | 0.130 s | 15,456 MB |
| this PR (all resident) | 0.867 / 0.863 s | 0.031 s | 22,170 MB |

That is −9% end to end. Every PR sample is below every main sample (0.860–0.872 vs 0.950–1.008 s). The server logs `Auto memory policy for ZImagePipelineConfig: 139.3 GiB free on the least-free selected GPU holds the 19.1 GiB of weights per GPU at least 2x, so every component without an explicit placement stays resident.`

The same PR with all but 30 GiB of the GPU held by another process (the inputs of a 32 GB card) keeps main's placement: text encoder and VAE layerwise, DiT component-offloaded, `TextEncodingStage` 0.130 s.

Earlier evidence for the same gap: H100 Z-Image-Turbo, all resident 0.701/0.699 s vs auto 0.793/0.799 s (−12%).

Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, flagless on 1xH200 (startup only; no timed request): main streams both experts (`transformer` and `transformer_2`: 1.74 GB on the GPU, 26.18 GB pinned on the host each) and the text encoder. This PR loads both experts on the GPU (26.62 GB each) and keeps the VAE resident and the fp32 T5 layerwise, so 52 GB less pinned host memory per rank; the tier itself does not apply (150 GiB needed, 139 free). The end-to-end gain was not measured here.

## CI and baselines

The tier changes placement on the 80 GB H100 lanes wherever the checkpoint is cached and fits twice, so these scenarios will report higher `load_peak_vram_mb` / `runtime_peak_vram_mb` and fail the up-only 1%/2% memory checks by design. Their latency baselines may become stale-high (not a failure). Re-seed them with the usual two-step flow (first run prints the blocks to add to `perf_baselines/h100.json`):
- 1 GPU: `flux_image_t2i`, `zimage_image_t2i`, `zimage_image_t2i_multi_lora`, `cosmos3_nano_t2i`, `cosmos3_nano_t2v` (transformer already pinned resident; the small components join it), `sana_video_2b_t2v`, `longlive2_t2v`, `longlive2_i2v`, `fast_hunyuan_video` (38.5 GiB, 77 of ~79 GiB: closest to the line), `wan2_2_ti2v_5b`, `fastwan2_2_ti2v_5b`, `turbo_wan2_1_t2v_1.3b`, and the Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B family (`wan2_1_t2v_1.3b`, `_teacache_enabled`, `_frame_interp_2x`, `_upscaling_4x`, `_frame_interp_2x_upscaling_4x`, `wan2_1_t2v_1_3b_lora_1gpu`).
- 2 GPUs: `flux_image_t2i_2_gpus`, `zimage_image_t2i_2_gpus`, `zimage_image_t2i_2_gpus_non_square`, `qwen_image21_t2i_tp2`, `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b_cfg_parallel`, `wan2_1_t2v_1_3b_cache_dit_sp_only_2gpu`, `fsdp-inference`.
- `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b_encoder_permanent_residents` exists to test a permanent layerwise resident set on the text encoder, so it now pins the encoder layerwise with `--component-residency text_encoder=layerwise-offload`.
- Unchanged: the 5090 lane (nothing fits twice in ~31 GiB), every quantized or `--transformer-path` case, cases with explicit placement of the components that would move, Wan2.2-A14B, Qwen-Image 1-GPU, LTX and MiniMax-H3 on H100. The B200 lane runs only ModelOpt cases with `--transformer-path`/quantized weights.

The list comes from sizing each case's checkpoint at its serving precision against ~79 GiB free; a runner whose HF cache misses a model keeps main's placement for it.

## Risks

- Steady VRAM grows by the components that used to stream (Z-Image-Turbo +6.7 GB peak, the LTX-2 text encoder on H200, ~53 GiB of Wan2.2-A14B experts on H200). The factor of two leaves at least the weights' size free for activations, assuming one request at a time.
- A checkpoint that is not cached at startup is not sized, so a first start can place components differently from later ones. That is the same placement as main, never more resident.
- `ServerArgs` now reads safetensors headers of a cached checkpoint at startup (local files only, no network).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Perf] diffusion: Skip the residency calibration probe in auto mode until a planner consumes it
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

#37916 (1/4 of the auto-residency stack) added warmup-calibrated residency measurement: in `--performance-mode auto` with server warmup, the warmup builder raises the step count to 4 (`AUTO_RESIDENCY_TIMING_STEPS`) and, when the bounded warmup shape is smaller than the default request, appends a full-shape probe plus a re-warm of the bounded shape. After the probe the worker drops the IPC and Ulysses all-to-all staging buffers.

Nothing consumes the result. The planner and the apply/rollback path are still open (#37917, #37918, #35335): `_auto_residency_warmup_records` are read only to size the probe itself, and `server_warmup.auto_residency_skip_reason` has no caller. Auto mode therefore pays for calibration on every startup:
- a full-shape probe for video models (1024x1024x81 for Cosmos3-Nano), plus a second bounded warmup;
- four warmup steps instead of two;
- a staging-buffer drop that the next request has to undo. On 4xGB300 Cosmos3 (CFG 2 x Ulysses 2) this raised `std::get: wrong index for variant` on some ranks after the probe and hung the next all-to-all until the NCCL watchdog fired.

The debug residency hint also told users that auto "applies safe adjustments automatically", which is not true yet.

## Modifications

- `auto_residency_args_skip_reason` ends with `"residency planner not available"` after every other gate passes. The warmup builder already keys the probe, the 4-step floor and the stage-timing retention on this gate, so auto mode is back to the bounded warmup that every other mode runs. The planner PR replaces this one line with `return None` when it lands, which re-enables the probe in the same PR that consumes it.
- Warmup memory measurement (#37916) is unchanged; it is cheap and the planner builds on it.
- The debug hint in `do_mem_analysis` keeps only the explicit `--component-residency <name>=resident` advice.

Tests (`test_auto_residency.py`):
- New `test_eligible_server_warmup_runs_no_probe_or_step_floor`: an auto, server-warmup, CUDA video config whose bounded warmup is smaller than its 1280x720x81 default builds one warmup request at the bounded step count. On main it builds three (bounded, probe, re-warm) at 4 steps.
- The three tests that asserted "every other gate passes" (`test_fixed_loading_paths_still_calibrate_other_components`, `test_parallel_paths_reach_planner_gate`, `test_eligible_path_reaches_planner_gate`) now pin the platform to CUDA and expect the planner reason, instead of accepting either `None` or `"requires CUDA"` depending on the runner. All four tests fail on main.
- The probe-shape and probe-sizing tests still patch the gate open, so the machinery stays covered for the planner PRs.

## Accuracy Tests

No numeric path changes: only warmup requests differ, and serving requests run the same code.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Cosmos3-Nano T2V on 2xH200, flagless `sglang serve --num-gpus 2` (auto mode, CFG parallel), fresh server per run, rounds interleaved main / PR / main / PR:

| | Startup to healthy (round 1 / round 2) | Server warmup |
|---|---|---|
| main | 62.1 / 46.0 s | 832x480x17 at 4 steps, then the probe at 1024x1024x81 (4 steps, 6.1 s), then 832x480x17 again: ~9 s |
| this PR | 50.0 / 40.0 s | 832x480x17 at 2 steps: 2.7 s |

The PR's server logs contain no `auto residency probe` line.

Serving requests run the same code, so their latency and memory do not change.

## CI and baselines

No perf or memory baseline should move. Warmup peaks are reported apart from `runtime_peak_vram_mb` since #37916, and the probe's allocator pool and staging buffers were dropped before serving anyway. Auto-mode warmup is back to what it was before #37916: the bounded shape once, at 2 steps. Video cases in the auto-mode suites start faster; their `estimated_full_test_time_s` entries are now slightly high, which only affects shard balancing.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Perf] dsv4: Let the fused MXFP8 producers run inside the breakable prefill graph
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `fused_mxfp8_rows` decides when the fused producers write the next DeepGEMM consumer's MXFP8 input directly. Extend batches took the fused path in eager prefill, but not inside a breakable prefill graph, so graph prefill (the low-concurrency shapes) still wrote bf16 and quantized it in a separate pass before `wqkv_a`.
- The prefill graph captures with the extend flag cleared, so the check also counts the prefill graph scope (`is_in_prefill_graph_scope()`): extend batches now take the fused path inside the graph as well.
- The mHC boundary producer runs in a captured segment and its consumer reads the pair as ordinary graph tensors, so it needs no special handling there. The attention output producer is unchanged in the graph: the mega attention runs inside an eager break that writes a captured bf16 buffer.

With this, graph prefill and eager prefill run the same producers and the same `wqkv_a` GEMM, so a prefill batch computes the same values whether or not it replays a graph. Against the previous graph path, `wqkv_a` moves from FlashInfer's quantize-and-GEMM to the DeepGEMM MXFP8 GEMM that eager prefill already uses, so graph prefill outputs are not bitwise equal to before; they now match eager prefill's path.

Verification:
- Inside graph replay and in eager prefill, the fused boundary's MXFP8 pair matches a standalone per-token-group quantize of the same normalized rows: the fp8 bytes match exactly, and the scale bytes match on every group that holds data (they differ only on all-zero groups, which decode to zeros either way).
- A GPU profile of graph prefill shows the standalone quantize before `wqkv_a` gone; the remaining standalone quantize calls feed `wo_b`, whose producer stays bf16 inside the attention break.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill with the breakable graph captures and replays every batch with the fused producers, with no OOM at the recipe memory fraction, and GSM8K is unchanged. `test_deepseek_v4_pipeline.py` and `test_deepseek_v4_boundary.py` pass.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Serve image responses from in-memory encoded bytes
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

`/v1/images/generations` and `/v1/images/edits` spend avoidable time after the image is decoded:

1. **A disk round trip per image.** The output rank encodes the image into a file under the output directory, and the HTTP server then reads that file back to base64 it. With `--output-path ""` nothing is persisted, so the file goes to a per-request temp dir purely as a transport.
2. **A slow PNG encode.** PNG is deflated at zlib level 1 on the output rank, single-threaded. For a 1024x1024 image that is tens of milliseconds on the request's critical path, while level 0 produces the same pixels several times faster.

## Modifications

- `entrypoints/utils.py`: an image is encoded once, in memory (`_encode_image_frame`). `save_materialized_output` writes those bytes when saving and, with `return_image_bytes`, returns them even when nothing is written. `save_outputs` / `post_process_sample` collect them through `image_bytes_out`.
- PNG defaults to zlib level 0: same pixels, about 3x the bytes of level 1 on typical generations, several times faster to encode. An `output_compression` other than 75 still selects a level. JPEG and WebP go through the same imageio call into memory instead of into a file, and their bytes are unchanged.
- New sampling field `return_image_bytes` (default off, set by `/v1/images`). The output rank also encodes when `save_output` is off but the bytes are requested, and returns them in `OutputBatch.output_image_bytes`. The scheduler slices them per request when it splits a dynamic batch, and the API-side save path fills the same field.
- `image_api.py`: b64_json responses are built from `output_image_bytes`; no file is read back. A file is written only when the server persists outputs (`--output-path`, default `outputs/`) or uploads them to cloud storage, and the persisted file holds exactly the returned bytes. `file_path`, `/v1/images/{id}/content` and url responses are unchanged. GLM-Image's actual output size is read from the bytes.
- Docs: the `--async-output-save` scope now includes `return_image_bytes` requests, and the output-quality notes describe the PNG level.

Tradeoff: PNG responses and persisted PNG files are larger (1024x1024: Z-Image-Turbo RGB 1.60 → 3.15 MB, Qwen-Image-2.1 RGBA 1.83 → 4.20 MB; the b64_json body grows by 4/3 of that). Pass `output_compression` to trade encode time for size.

Tests (`test_image_response_bytes.py`):
- the returned PNG decodes to the source pixels exactly for 2-D grayscale, single-channel, RGB and RGBA frames, at the default and at explicit levels, and no file is written when `save_output` is off;
- a saved file holds exactly the returned bytes (PNG, JPEG, WebP), and JPEG/WebP bytes equal what the previous file writer produced;
- the worker returns one encoded image per output and writes the file only when saving; it encodes when either saving or returning bytes;
- a split dynamic batch keeps each request's bytes;
- both image endpoints answer b64_json from the returned bytes without a file, and request a file only when the server persists outputs.

## Accuracy Tests

Same request (seed 42, `output_format=png`, b64_json) against both arms:

- The returned PNGs decode to identical pixels for Z-Image-Turbo (RGB) and Qwen-Image-2.1 (RGBA).
- With the default `--output-path`, the persisted file is byte-identical to the response.
- With `--output-path ""`, no output file is written, `file_path` is null, and the pixels are still identical.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Server benchmark, 2 interleaved rounds x 5 repeats, client e2e latency (median; min-max spread ≤ 6 ms in every run). Requests ask for PNG.

| case | GPUs | base (round 1 / 2) | this PR (round 1 / 2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Z-Image-Turbo T2I 1024, TP2 | 2xH200 | 0.679 / 0.678 s | 0.640 / 0.641 s (−38 ms, −5.6%) |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I 1024 | 1xH200 | 4.374 / 4.370 s | 4.331 / 4.333 s (−40 ms, −0.9%) |

The server-side stage sum is unchanged (Z-Image 0.50 s, Qwen-Image-2.1 4.22-4.23 s); the time comes out of the post-generation tail: 0.183 → 0.146 s and 0.154 → 0.115 s.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
