title: [Perf] diffusion: Wait on the socket when the scheduler is idle
author: rwang5203
body:
## Motivation

With nothing to run, the diffusion scheduler's event loop received from its socket with `zmq.NOBLOCK` and looped again at once, so an idle server kept one CPU core fully busy, between requests as well as during long idle periods. The loop already waits on its poller while a dynamic batch fills and while outputs are being saved, but not when it is simply idle.

## Modifications

- Add `--sleep-on-idle`, disabled by default to match SRT and preserve the existing busy-polling latency policy.
- When enabled, an idle single-rank monolithic replica waits on its existing socket poller. Messages wake it immediately; each wait is bounded by one second or the pending allocator-cache release deadline, whichever is sooner.
- `release_cache_if_idle` returns how long that release still has to wait, so the release happens when it did before.
- A replica that relays requests to other ranks keeps the old loop, because those ranks time their own cache release by its cadence.

## Accuracy Tests

```bash
pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_idle_cache_release.py
```

`test_idle_scheduler_wait_policy` covers default busy polling, opt-in bounded waits, multi-rank fallback, and timely allocator-cache release. The scheduler, metrics, output save, pi05 segment, warmup, port and client unit tests pass as on main.

`nvidia/Cosmos3-Nano` served with its defaults through every Cosmos3 modality (text, image and video to video, with and without sound, and the action modes), 636 requests per arm in fresh servers. Every output is byte for byte the output before the change.

In one run each of a native server on this branch and on main, the scheduler process used 20.2 CPU seconds in a 20 second idle window on main and 0.08 here, both requests returned the same bytes, the allocator cache still went back to the driver about one second after each request, and SIGINT stopped the server in the same time.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The measurements below were collected before the opt-in follow-up, with idle waiting enabled. They are not new measurements of the current head; the default now retains busy polling. Blocking waits can add idle-to-active wake-up latency, so latency-sensitive deployments should benchmark their low-QPS tail latency before enabling the flag.

One GPU per server, a fresh server per run, the same workload in each, eight paired runs and four more on fresh prompts, seeds and source media.

| Measure | Before | After | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Server CPU while idle, CPU seconds per minute | 65.5 | 0.25 | -99.6% |
| Server CPU per request, text to video | 7.58 s | 7.07 s | -6.7% |
| Server CPU per request, video to video | 8.08 s | 7.56 s | -6.4% |
| Server CPU per request, image to video with sound | 8.11 s | 7.54 s | -6.9% |
| Server CPU per request, forward dynamics | 2.90 s | 2.37 s | -18.1% |
| Server CPU per request, policy | 1.97 s | 1.58 s | -19.7% |
| Server CPU per request, two text to video requests at once | 7.54 s | 7.23 s | -4.1% |

The busy loop also ran between back to back requests, which is where the per request savings come from. Latency, throughput, GPU time and energy per request, device and host memory, startup, first requests and shutdown show no measurable difference in either set of runs. A request waiting in an idle loop reaches it within about 10 us of when a spinning loop would see it.

title: [Fix] humming: adapt integration to kernels 0.1.18
author: huangzhilin-hzl
body:
## Motivation

Bump `humming-kernels` from 0.1.12 to 0.1.18 and adapt the integration to the newer quantization APIs

## Modifications

- Use schema-based weight quantization and preserve static, secondary, and per-shard scales.
- Handle Hadamard quantization when loading CPU checkpoint weights.
- Preserve both input scale levels and allocate buffers using each MoE sublayer's input dtype.
- Align indexed MoE routes separately when `w13` and `w2` use different M tiles; validate DeepEP and masked quantization compatibility.
- Place Humming cache and temporary files under `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR`, preserving explicit overrides.
- Add unit and GPU regression coverage.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, all 1319 questions, [sgl-eval](https://pypi.org/project/sgl-eval/) 0.1.3 (zero-shot chat, `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=4096`, thinking off, 32 concurrent requests). 1 × 8-GPU H20-3e node.
A = baseline SGLang (container image) + humming-kernels 0.1.12, B = this PR + humming-kernels 0.1.18. Launch commands are under [Benchmark](#launch).

| Model | A | B |
|---|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (TP4, DSPARK) | 96.66% | 97.12% |
| GLM-5.3-W4AFP8-AWQ (TP8, EAGLE) | 96.51% | 97.19% |
| Kimi-K2.6 (TP8, EAGLE3) | 97.42% | 97.50% |

No request errors on any arm; one run per arm.

## Benchmark

1 × 8-GPU H20-3e node, A and B back-to-back on the same GPUs, `bench_serving` with `temperature=0`, one warmup pass per point.

### Launch

All arms set `SGLANG_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"float8e4m3"}'`. A and B use identical flags.

```bash
# DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (GPUs 0-3)
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --tp 4 --trust-remote-code \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --mem-fraction-static 0.88 \
  --moe-runner-backend humming --quantization humming \
  --disable-radix-cache --context-length 270336 --stream-interval 1 --random-seed 1

# GLM-5.3-W4AFP8-AWQ
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path GLM-5.3-W4AFP8-AWQ --tp 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
  --moe-runner-backend humming --quantization humming \
  --disable-radix-cache --context-length 270336 --stream-interval 1 --random-seed 1

# Kimi-K2.6 (also SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1)
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Kimi-K2.6 --tp 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE3 --speculative-draft-model-path Kimi-K2.6-Eagle3-Long-Context \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --reasoning-parser kimi_k2 --tool-call-parser kimi_k2 --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
  --moe-runner-backend humming --quantization humming \
  --disable-radix-cache --context-length 270336 --stream-interval 1 --random-seed 1
```

### DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731

`random` dataset; 3 rounds per arm in the order A1 B1 B2 A2 A3 B3; values are 3-round means. Requests per point = concurrency.

| TTFT, output 256, C=1 | A ms | B ms | Δ |

title: [Perf] mhc: Split hc_combine_norm_mxfp8 rows by batch size and zero padding scales in the kernel
author: akhilg-nv
body:
[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

`hc_combine_norm_mxfp8` is the DeepSeek-V4.1 mHC kernel that builds the attention input on Blackwell: it combines the
four residual streams weighted by `pre` (the per-row weights of the four streams), applies RMSNorm, and writes the
result in BF16 and in MXFP8 for `wqkv_a`. It runs when the batch has at most 128 rows, and only where the previous
mHC post has not already built that input (the fused MoE all-reduce epilogue at TP2/TP4 and Mega-mHC do), so with DP
attention and Mega-mHC off, as in every published DEP recipe, it runs before 39 of the 40 attention layers of each
decode step of up to 128 tokens per rank. It had two fixed costs. It always ran 4 CTAs per row, and each of them
recomputed the whole row (the combine and the RMS statistic) to store a quarter of it; that split was chosen when the
kernel took at most 8 rows, and #42245 raised the limit to 128 rows without revisiting it. And its MXFP8 scale buffer
came from `torch.zeros`, a separate fill kernel before every call (the scales of the rows past the batch are padding
of a 128-row scale tile and must be zero). This PR picks the split by row count, as `hc_combine_norm` in the same
file already does, and zeroes the padding scales inside the kernel. The outputs are bitwise identical: every CTA still
computes the whole row in the same order, and the split only decides which CTA stores which columns.

- **Accuracy:** bitwise identical to the previous kernel on B200, B300 and VR200 (3,082-3,850 cases per GPU, 0
  mismatches). GSM8K under AgentX load on B200: 97.67% without this PR, 96.33% with it (exact McNemar p = 0.29).
- **Kernel:** 41-46% faster on average at 49-128 rows (B200 6.24 → 3.40 us, B300 5.63 → 3.20 us, VR200 4.56 →
  2.68 us) and 20-26% faster at 1-32 rows, measured alone; the fill kernel before every call is gone.
- **End to end: no measurable change.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4x B200, the published InferenceX AgentX DEP4 c192
  cell (where this kernel runs on the most decode steps at the most rows), real speculative acceptance, 2 ABBA pairs on
  one node: per-request decode time per token −0.32% (95% interval −0.56% to +0.02%), inside the run-to-run noise of
  the same configuration (0.6-1.1%); output throughput per GPU −0.01% and −0.12%.
- **Why the kernel saving does not reach the step on B200:** in decode the combine runs at the same time as the mHC
  statistics of the same residual on a side stream (on SM100, two DeepGEMM TF32 GEMMs from 32 rows up, a Triton kernel
  below). Next to them the new kernel is not faster: with the DeepGEMM statistics beside it, a combine + GEMM
  iteration takes 19.82 us before and 21.89 us after this PR (mean over 48-120 rows, microbenchmark), and in the
  serving profile the next GEMM did not start earlier.
- **End to end (estimate, not measured):** counting the per-call saving as if the combine were on the critical path,
  a B200 DEP4 c64 profile (decode at 24-30 rows) gives 39 calls x 2.45 us = 96 us per 11.5 ms decode step, about
  0.8%. The measurement above and the side-stream overlap show that this upper bound is not reached.

## Modifications

**+41 / −25 runtime code (1 file), +74 / −1 tests (1 file).** A Triton kernel change; no new flags, no default
changes.

In `python/sglang/kernels/ops/layernorm/hc_combine_norm.py`:

- `_parts_for(m, k)` uses the same split as `hc_combine_norm`: 4 CTAs per row up to 8 rows, 2 up to 48 rows, and 1
  above that. Up to 8 rows the split is unchanged.
- The scale buffer is allocated with `torch.empty`. Extra programs after the last row zero the padding, as
  `rmsnorm_mxfp8` already does: each takes one 512-byte block of the scale buffer and zeroes the bytes of the rows
  past the batch. At hidden 5120 that is 40 extra programs; at 128 rows there is no padding and none run.
- The kernel takes the row count `M` as an argument. The per-row body is unchanged, now under `if row < M`.

**Related:** draft #41628 by @harmya contains the same row split inside a larger change (it raises the fusion batch
limits and keeps `torch.zeros`). This PR carries the split on its own, plus the in-kernel zeroing.

Tests, in `test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_mxfp8_epilogue.py`:

- The existing bitwise test against `hc_combine_norm` followed by FlashInfer `mxfp8_quantize` (cuda and cute-dsl
  backends) adds rows 48 and 49 (either side of a split threshold), 84 and 120.
- New `test_combine_norm_mxfp8_split_invariant`: with the split forced to 1, 2 and 4, the outputs equal the default
  split byte for byte, both eagerly and on a CUDA-graph replay whose outputs were first filled with `0xFF`.
- New `test_combine_norm_mxfp8_padding_disjoint_from_live_rows`: on the GPU, a padding program that also overwrote a
  live row's scales would go unnoticed, because the live row stores its scales last (on B200 even the largest grid,
  520 CTAs, runs in one wave). The test runs the kernel in Triton's interpreter (`TRITON_INTERPRET=1`, in a
  subprocess, on CPU), which runs the programs one at a time in grid order, over a scale buffer filled with `0xFF`,
  for 1, 49 and 127 rows and splits 1, 2 and 4. It checks that every byte gets written and that exactly 160 bytes per
  live row are non-zero. It takes about 20 s.

## Accuracy Tests

**The kernel's outputs are bitwise identical to the previous kernel's:**

| Check | B200 | B300 | VR200 (SM107) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_mxfp8_epilogue.py` | 107 passed, 0 skipped (this branch) | 106 passed, 0 skipped (before the interpreter test) | 106 passed, 0 skipped (before the interpreter test) |
| Byte-for-byte against the previous kernel (BF16 output, FP8 values, scales) | 3,850 cases, 0 mismatches (re-run: 3,082 / 0) | 3,082 cases, 0 mismatches | 3,850 cases, 0 mismatches |

- The byte-for-byte check covers every row count from 1 to 128, input scales 1e-3 / 1 / 1e3, BF16 and FP32 `pre`,
  the split forced to 1 / 2 / 4, and 10 CUDA-graph replays over `0xFF`-filled outputs. The 3,850-case runs add 768
  cases for a benchmark-only variant that is not part of this PR.
- CI runs this file on B200 (`base-b-kernel-unit`). Hopper and ROCm never reach this kernel: the caller takes it only
  on Blackwell with MXFP8 output and hidden size 5120.

**Do the tests catch a broken padding program?** Each row is this PR's kernel with one deliberate change, on one B200:

| Kernel change | GPU tests (before the interpreter test) | Interpreter test |
|---|---|---|
| Drop the padding branch, keep `torch.empty` | 76 of 106 fail | fails: "scale bytes unwritten" |
| Padding mask `pad_row >= M - 1` (also zeroes the last live row) | **all 106 pass**; 0 bad calls in 480 poisoned-buffer GPU calls | fails: "160 live bytes zeroed" |
| Padding block index without `* tl.num_programs(1)` | 49 of 106 fail | fails: "scale bytes unwritten" |
| The previous kernel (scales zeroed by `torch.zeros`), default split | - | fails: "scale bytes unwritten" |

**GSM8K under load**, on the end-to-end setup below (runs B2 and A2): 60 s into a second AgentX run on the same
server (concurrency 192, 300 s window), `sgl-eval run gsm8k` (sgl-eval 0.1.3, 300 questions, 16 threads, temperature
1.0, top_p 0.95, max tokens 16384, seed 0; thinking on through the server's `SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1`):

| | GSM8K-300 | Errors | AgentX load during the eval |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Without this PR | 97.67% (293/300) | 0 | 1,300 requests, 0 errors |
| With this PR | 96.33% (289/300) | 0 | 1,301 requests, 0 errors |

- The arms answered 8 questions differently: 6 right only without this PR, 2 only with it (exact McNemar p = 0.29).
  The kernel's outputs are bitwise identical, so the difference is sampling at temperature 1.0 in batches whose
  composition differs between runs.
- One answer with this PR hit the 16,384-token limit: a coherent, long deliberation over an ambiguous question that
  the run without this PR also answered wrongly, after 7,441 tokens.
- Speculative accept length (real acceptance, rank 0, profiling window): 3.464 and 3.355 without this PR, 3.386 and
  3.396 with it.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Microbenchmark**, one GPU, CUDA graphs. Inputs: BF16 `x` of shape [m, 4 x 5120] and FP32 `pre`. Times are per call
in us: the median of 7 repetitions, each 100 replays of a graph of 20 calls (hot L2 on purpose: the inputs are at most
5.2 MB, and in serving the kernel reads residual streams that the previous sublayer wrote just before).

| rows | B200 | B300 | VR200 (SM107) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3.89 -> 2.87 | 3.38 -> 2.67 | 3.20 -> 2.46 |
| 32 | 4.01 -> 3.08 | 3.59 -> 2.87 | 3.45 -> 2.59 |
| 64 | 5.12 -> 3.28 | 4.51 -> 3.17 | 4.28 -> 2.65 |
| 96 | 6.18 -> 3.38 | 5.63 -> 3.18 | 4.32 -> 2.68 |
| 128 | 7.08 -> 3.48 | 6.46 -> 3.28 | 5.21 -> 2.71 |
| mean of 49, 64, 84, 96, 100, 112, 120, 128 rows | 6.24 -> 3.40 (-46%) | 5.63 -> 3.20 (-43%) | 4.56 -> 2.68 (-41%) |

- Every timed row count got faster: 17 row counts from 1 to 128 (14 on B300). At 1-32 rows each is 20-26% faster.
- Above 48 rows, the two parts of the change save, per call (means over 49-128 rows): the new split alone (the old
  kernel with only the split changed) 1.90 / 1.74 / 1.13 us on B200 / B300 / VR200, and removing the fill alone (the
  new kernel forced to 4 CTAs per row) 1.02 / 0.65 / 0.53 us. Up to 8 rows the split is unchanged; the 0.7-1.0 us
  saved there is the fill.

**Next to the side stream (B200).** In decode, `deepseek_v4_mhc` forks the mHC statistics of the same residual onto
a side stream right before the combine. On SM100 with at least 32 rows they are `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn_deepgemm` (two
DeepGEMM `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` calls and a Sinkhorn kernel); below 32 rows, and where DeepGEMM's prenorm is off, the
Triton `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn`. Per iteration: fork; side stream the statistics; main stream the combine, then a
stand-in for `wqkv_a` (BF16 GEMM [m, 5120] x [5120, 2048]); join. Mean us per iteration over 48, 60, 72, 84, 96, 108
and 120 rows (each the median of 7 repetitions), outputs checked byte for byte:

| Layout | Before | This PR | This PR, split forced to 4 | This PR, split forced to 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Combine alone | 5.48 | 3.24 | 5.03 | 3.73 |
| Combine + GEMM, no side stream | 13.90 | 11.67 | 13.48 | 12.19 |
| + DeepGEMM statistics on the side stream (the SM100 serving path) | 19.82 | 21.89 | 21.20 | 22.09 |
| + Triton statistics on the side stream | 27.04 | 22.66 | 25.84 | 23.80 |

- With the DeepGEMM statistics beside it, this PR is about equal at 48 and 60 rows (18.86 → 18.42, 19.14 → 18.79 us)
  and slower from 72 rows, by 1.3 to 4.0 us per iteration. Without the fill kernel, the combine starts as soon as the
  statistics do and competes with them for SMs; the variant that keeps 4 CTAs per row and drops only the fill is
  slower than before as well.

**In the server (B200 DEP4 c192, GPU profile of 80 steps on all ranks, one run per arm, profiler on):**

- Every target-verify decode graph holds 39 calls of this kernel in both arms. Before this PR every call (12,168 of
  12,168) directly follows the fill kernel; with it, none do.
- At 60 rows, at 37 of the 39 layers both kernels run entirely beside the side-stream DeepGEMM GEMMs. The old path
  takes 1.31 us (fill) + 0.48 us (gap) + 4.38 us (kernel), medians over all calls and ranks; the new kernel takes
  7.0 us (median; 3.2 us alone in the microbenchmark, and 4.1 us at the other two layers, where the GEMMs overlap it
  for only about 2 us). At 18-30 rows (Triton statistics) the new kernel takes 3.8 us, and the old path 6.2 us from
  the start of the fill to the end of the kernel (4.6 us of it the kernel): 2.45 us more per call, the figure the
  estimate above uses.
- The time from the end of the mHC post to the start of the `wqkv_a` GEMM was not shorter with this PR: 6.85 → 7.68
  us at 60 rows, 6.9-7.4 → 8.6-10.7 us at 18-30 rows. In both cases the GEMM waits for SMs held by the side-stream
  statistics, which start later relative to the combine once the fill is gone.

**End to end on B200.**

- Setup: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 4x B200 on one node, the published InferenceX AgentX DEP4 c192 cell (command below),
  image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261021-c1c287a4`, whose `hc_combine_norm.py` is byte-identical to this
  PR's base and to current main. "With this PR" is the same image with this PR's `hc_combine_norm.py` mounted over it;
  each run checks the md5 of the file Python imports before any traffic. One change from the published cell: real
  speculative acceptance (the published runs set a simulated acceptance length).
- Why c192: the kernel runs only when a rank's decode batch is at most 120 rows (a CUDA-graph batch of at most 20
  requests x 6 verify tokens with DSpark block size 5; the next graph size, 22, is 132 rows). In the published B200
  DEP4 runs (InferenceX run 39606211010, server logs) the busiest rank decodes a median of 5 requests at c64, 10 at
  c128, 16 at c192 and 26 at c256. In our c192 windows 62% of the decode log samples ran the kernel, 41% at 49-120
  rows.
- Runs: without, with, with, without this PR, fresh server per run; AgentX (agentx-harness 1.0.12, the published
  trace set, concurrency 192, 900 s profiling window after its warm-up).
- Rule, fixed before the runs: a change counts only if the 95% interval of the pooled per-request ratio excludes 0,
  both pairs agree in sign, and the pooled change is larger than both same-arm repeat differences.

| | Without (A1) | With (B1) | With (B2) | Without (A2) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Output tok/s/GPU (InferenceX scorer) | 1,808.7 | 1,808.6 | 1,806.0 | 1,808.1 |
| p90 interactivity (1000 / p90 ITL) | 104.19 | 103.04 | 103.60 | 102.35 |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (s) | 1.10 / 2.31 | 1.10 / 2.39 | 1.09 / 2.31 | 1.10 / 2.39 |
| Requests / errors | 6,936 / 0 | 6,912 / 0 | 6,924 / 0 | 6,902 / 0 |
| Accept length (rank 0) | 3.464 | 3.386 | 3.396 | 3.355 |

Per-request decode time per token ((latency − TTFT) / (output tokens − 1)), median of the per-request ratio over the
6,648 requests present in all four runs (AgentX replays the trace set in a fixed order; output lengths are equal):

| | B1 / A1 | B2 / A2 | Pooled with / without | A2 / A1 (same arm) | B2 / B1 (same arm) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Change (95% bootstrap interval) | +0.26% (−0.07, +0.66) | −0.89% (−1.29, −0.51) | −0.32% (−0.56, +0.02) | +0.59% | −1.10% |

**Result: no measurable change.** The pooled interval includes 0, the two pairs disagree in sign, and the pooled
change is smaller than the same-arm differences. Output tok/s/GPU changes by −0.01% and −0.12% (same-arm: −0.04%,
−0.14%), p90 interactivity by −1.11% and +1.22% (same-arm: −1.76%, +0.55%).

title: [Perf] cosmos3: Accelerate conditioning hashing with GPU BLAKE3
author: xupinjie
body:
## Motivation

Profiling shows substantial device-to-host (D2H) transfer and CPU SHA-256 computation in Cosmos3's conditioning fingerprint path before VAE encoding. Fingerprinting takes **115–614 ms** across the measured 480p–1080p workloads.

SHA-256 benefits from optimized CPU implementations, but sequential block chaining limits GPU parallelism for a single large tensor. Our single-message Triton SHA-256 prototype was **23–28× slower** than CPU SHA-256 including D2H. The existing GPU alternative, `python/sglang/kernels/ops/memory/gpu_tensor_hash.py`, uses a custom **64-bit non-cryptographic hash** with no cryptographic collision-resistance guarantee; a collision could cause incorrect VAE cache reuse.

[BLAKE3](https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3) is a cryptographic tree hash whose independent chunks and tree reductions suit GPU parallelism. BLAKE3-256 targets **128-bit collision resistance** ([specification](https://c2sp.org/BLAKE3)), matching SHA-256's collision-resistance strength ([NIST](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/hash-functions)). Computing the fingerprint on the GPU avoids transferring the input back to the CPU and returns only a **32-byte digest**.

## Modifications

- Add a Triton implementation of standard unkeyed BLAKE3-256. It hashes the complete tensor contents on the GPU and returns only the 32-byte digest to the CPU.
- Use a Cosmos3-specific VAE conditioning cache key containing the digest, tensor metadata and encoder settings. Reuse the existing cache storage and invalidation mechanisms, preserving CPU and distributed fallbacks.
- Add BLAKE3 correctness tests and a focused Cosmos3 cache-key test.

### Generality and follow-up work

The BLAKE3 kernel hashes raw CUDA tensor bytes independently of Cosmos3's video format. Concrete reuse candidates in the existing conditioning cache paths include:

| Model | Potential integration |
| --- | --- |
| Wan2.1/2.2 I2V, Wan2.2 TI2V-5B | Image-conditioning tensors in the Wan VAE encoding cache |
| FLUX.2 / Klein | Reference-image tensors in the VAE encoding cache |
| Qwen-Image-Edit | Input-image tensors in the VAE encoding cache |
| LTX-2 I2V | Image-conditioning tensors in the video VAE encoding cache |
| MiniMax-H3 | Image/video tensors in the VAE encoding cache, including tiled encoder inputs |

Follow-up work is to discuss shared GPU fingerprinting with the community and evaluate these integrations, retaining each model's tensor metadata and encoder settings in cache keys. Output consistency and E2E benefits require validation for each model.

## Accuracy Tests

- GPU digests match official BLAKE3 vectors and the CPU `blake3` implementation bit for bit, including block/chunk/tree boundaries, storage views and raw dtype bit patterns.
- The Cosmos3 integration test verifies cache hits for identical videos and recomputation with correct outputs after changing the last frame or encoder settings.
- Complete Cosmos3 V2V outputs are **bit-identical MP4 files** against the CPU fingerprint baseline at all three resolutions below.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Environment:** 1× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (96 GB). Docker: `lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:b1259f3ea3275f66237c498ea388919729018bc9f01c3d638391e06e2cf3f469`.

**Workload:** Cosmos3-Edge V2V, official `robot_pouring.mp4` resized per row; first 5 conditioning frames, 45 output frames, 24 FPS, 35 steps, CFG 5, seed 42. Output resolution follows input, aligned to 16 pixels. All offload, torch.compile and guardrails are disabled. Both variants use identical GPU preprocessing; baseline uses the existing CPU fingerprint path.

Each variant runs in a separate process with **1 complete warmup + 1 measured request**, using different videos and positive/negative prompts. Every measured request has **0 cache hits / 3 misses**. E2E includes GPU completion and MP4 saving, excluding model loading.

| Output resolution | CPU fingerprint (ms) | GPU BLAKE3 (ms) | Fingerprint speedup | Baseline E2E (s) | GPU BLAKE3 E2E (s) | E2E speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 848×480 | 115.303 | 0.2850 | 404.5× | 6.273 | 6.119 | 1.025× |
| 1280×720 | 268.067 | 0.6625 | 404.6× | 17.042 | 16.845 | 1.012× |
| 1920×1088 | 613.860 | 1.3247 | 463.4× | 56.217 | 55.892 | 1.006× |

Fingerprint timings include synchronization and digest retrieval. These are single-request measurements; 1080p experienced some thermal throttling, so E2E ratios also include runtime variation.

### Peak GPU memory

Per-request PyTorch peaks, measured after output saving. Values are rounded to 0.001 GiB.

| Output resolution | Baseline peak allocated (GiB) | GPU BLAKE3 peak allocated (GiB) | Peak reserved, both variants (GiB) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 848×480 | 10.591 | 10.591 | 11.551 |
| 1280×720 | 14.898 | 14.898 | 17.781 |
| 1920×1088 | 24.674 | 24.674 | 29.832 |

Hash temporary tensors are released before VAE encoding: all three configurations retain **0 additional allocated bytes** after fingerprinting. A separate 480p check also confirmed a **27 KiB temporary peak** and no retained allocations across 10 consecutive calls.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Some models use the same architecture name in SGLang but need different mono kernel specs. For example, dsv4-pro and dsv41 both run as `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`. The mono kernel registry looks up a spec by architecture only, so it cannot tell these two models apart.

This PR lets the registry also use the model type (`model_type` in the model's config) to choose the spec.

Needed by sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono#48. Merge this PR before it.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Registering (plugin side): `register()` in `kernels/plugin_kernels/amd/spec.py` takes an optional `model_type`. A plugin can register a spec for one model type, or leave `model_type` out (`None`).
- Looking up (sglang side): Sglang's startup check and runtime in `srt/kernel_plugins/amd/binding.py` pass the served model's `hf_config.model_type` to `find_spec()` and `spec_registered()`. A lookup first tries a spec registered for that model type, then a spec registered without one.

With the current sgl-amd-mono repo, every model gets the same spec with and without this PR.

title: [CI] diffusion: Run the FLUX.2 XPU norm-fusion test on the XPU suite only
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

#41942 registered `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_flux2_xpu_norm_fusions.py` on the CPU suite (`base-a-test-cpu`) as well as the XPU suite. Both of its CPU-runnable paths import `sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.models.dits.flux_2`, which imports `diffusers`, and the CPU suite installs only `python[dev]`, without the `diffusion` extra. Every `base-a-test-cpu` partition that picks up the file fails with:

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'diffusers'
```

This now fails CPU CI on unrelated PRs, for example [#40479](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39938364150/job/120363719922) and [#45785](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39937459719).

## Modifications

- Drop the file's `register_cpu_ci` registration; it stays on `stage-b-test-1-gpu-xpu`.
- The Intel-Triton import regression still runs there: its subprocess blocks `triton.language.extra.intel`, so it simulates a host without Intel Triton on the XPU runner.
- The docstring now says why the file is XPU-only.

Skipping the CPU case when `diffusers` is missing would make it skip on every CPU run, and adding `diffusers` to the CPU suite's install would grow every CPU partition for one import check.

title: [Perf] diffusion/registry: Reduce model discovery work at startup
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

Model discovery parses every component file and walks every expression in each model's forward implementation, although registration only needs class and assignment statements.

- Skip parsing helper files without `EntryClass`.
- Skip expression subtrees while preserving breadth-first declaration and alias ordering, including nested statements.
- Flatten the registration branches without changing the supported entry formats.

No new runtime flag, persistent cache, production file, or model import. Pipeline discovery and external-package registration keep their existing behavior. This is separate from the CLI backend-detection work in #43317.

## Validation

Compared main `4b273537dec5` with `41558c352e38` on a dedicated two-H200 environment: Xeon Platinum 8558P, approximately 2 TiB host RAM, Python 3.12.15, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Diffusers 0.37.0, Transformers 5.19.0.

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Registry discovery, 20 interleaved samples, median | 664 ms | 377 ms |
| Single-GPU process start to HTTP readiness, 3 paired samples, median | 30.26 s | 29.39 s |
| Ulysses2 process start to HTTP readiness, 3 paired samples, median | 30.02 s | 29.61 s |

The complete mapping of **110 models and 18 aliases** is unchanged. Discovery is faster by about 43%; that is not a 43% server-startup improvement.

The 12 real server launches use `Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers`, cached checkpoint revision `0fad780a534b6463e45facd96134c9f345acfa5b`, offline Hub access, `--warmup-mode off`, and otherwise unchanged defaults. Each launch completes 4-step and 24-step requests at 512x320, 17 frames, seed 42; all 24 outputs were downloaded and decoded. Decoded-frame hashes match before/after within each GPU configuration. No live child processes remain after shutdown.

Startup measurements exclude model download and warmup. They are bounded measurements of this configuration, not a general speedup guarantee; first-request JIT time is not included or claimed as an improvement.

24 tests passed across `test_registry.py`, `test_external_model_package.py`, and `test_plain_component_loader.py`. Added coverage preserves nested declarations, aliases, and single/list/tuple entry formats without importing optional model dependencies. Pre-commit passed.

Production diff: one existing file, +50/-52; tests: +27 lines. No user-facing API or command changes, so no documentation update is needed.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Keep shared denoising paths off the host and add host-sync test guards
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

A denoising step that reads a device value on the host (`item()`, `float(t)`, `if t:`, `nonzero`, boolean-mask indexing) or uploads a constant with a pageable copy blocks the host until the stream drains. The host then cannot queue the next step while the GPU runs this one. These regressions pass every numeric test, so they come back. This PR adds unit-test guards for them and removes the ones in shared code: RoPE position setup, two schedulers, the DMD stage and the ring-attention hop.

The model-specific fixes are in two follow-ups that use these guards: image models (#<B>) and video models (#<C>).

## Modifications

Guards (`test/unit/host_sync_guard.py`):
- `no_cuda_sync(allow=...)` / `assert_no_cuda_sync(fn, ...)` run the code under `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("warn")` plus explicit `synchronize()` calls, and fail with the call site of every sync whose issuing function is not allow-listed. They skip without CUDA and restore the debug mode.
- `SyncOnRead` is a CPU stand-in for device tensors (timesteps, sigmas, masks): host reads of its values raise, and `.cpu()` is the explicit copy that is allowed.
- `forbid_host_syncs()` is a `TorchDispatchMode` that fails on the ops that sync on CUDA whatever tensor they read: scalar reads, `nonzero`, boolean-mask indexing, data-dependent output shapes.
- The contributing guide documents the three.

Shared hot paths:
- `rotary_embedding/mrope.py`: `OneDRotaryEmbedding` keyed an LRU cache on `tuple(pos.tolist())`, a device read per axis plus a hash over thousands of floats, and a pageable upload on a miss. FLUX.1/Kontext/FLUX.2, JoyImage, LingBot and the Wan sequence-shard path paid it per image, text and condition axis on every request. It now computes from the device positions directly (same ops, same values).
- `rotary_embedding/{utils,base}.py`, `layernorm.py`: `apply_qk_norm_rope`, `apply_flashinfer_rope_qk_inplace` and both `RotaryEmbedding` paths rebuilt `[offset, offset + seq)` with an `arange` (and a `repeat` for batch > 1) in every block when the caller passes no positions: 64-120 launches per step in eager mode for FLUX.2, Z-Image, Qwen-Image, Wan and others. `rope_positions()` shares one read-only tensor per shape. Compile and graph capture still build their own, so a capture never fills the cache with an arange it did not execute.
- `schedulers/kandinsky6_piflow.py`: the policy rollout looped `range(substeps.max().item())`, a device read right after the DiT forward on every step (video and audio scheduler). The substep counts now come from a host copy of the same fp32 math.
- `schedulers/scheduling_helios.py`: UniPC built `torch.tensor()` over lists of 0-dim device tensors and uploaded `0.5` constants, about a dozen syncs per step; they are stacked and filled on the device, and `linalg.solve` becomes `linalg.solve_ex` (same kernels, no host-side singularity check). The DMD path read the timestep twice per step through `torch.full(..., tensor)`; it is now cast and expanded on the device.
- `stages/denoising_dmd.py` (Wan DMD / FastWan): `int(t.item())` per step now comes from a host copy of the same schedule, and the per-step NaN assert is OR-ed on the device and checked once after the loop (same message; a NaN request still fails).
- `attention/backends/flash_attn.py`, `attention/layer.py`: the ring hop built `cu_seqlens_q/k` with `torch.tensor(..., device=...)` on every hop of every block, twice per hop for the tail-pad path. The hop now uses the cached `cu_seqlens_on_device`, moved next to the FA backend so the varlen and ring paths share it.

Tests (the fix tests fail on main):
- `test_host_sync_guard.py`: the three guards catch scalar reads, explicit synchronizes, boolean-mask indexing and data-dependent shapes, let device-side selects through, honor the allow list and restore the debug mode.
- `test_denoising_host_sync.py`: one CFG request through the shared `DenoisingStage` loop with `SyncOnRead` timesteps matches a plain run, and runs under `no_cuda_sync` on CUDA; one DMD request with `SyncOnRead` timesteps matches a plain run bitwise, and NaN latents still raise.
- `test_rope_host_sync.py`: `FluxPosEmbed` with `SyncOnRead` positions matches bitwise; positions are built once per shape, rebuilt under compile and capture.
- `test_scheduler_host_sync.py`: PiFlow and Helios UniPC/DMD steps with `SyncOnRead` schedules match plain runs bitwise, NaN bits included.
- `test_attention_host_sync.py`: two ring hops get `[0, n]` int32 bounds from the same device tensors.

No hunk overlaps #45942, #45943, #45944, #45948, #45965, #45966, #45967, #45977, #45978, #45979 or #45987; each of them still applies on top of this branch.

## Accuracy Tests

2xH200, eager. Decoded outputs are bitwise identical to main for every model below, two requests each with different inputs (pixels for images, decoded frames and audio for video), with this PR and both follow-ups applied:

| model (request) | GPUs | outputs compared | main vs PRs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I 1024x1024, 40 steps | 1 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 edit 1024x1024, 40 steps | 1 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Z-Image-Turbo 1024x1024, 9 steps, TP2 | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| FLUX.3 Klein Base 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Ideogram-4 FP8 1024x1024, 20 steps, TP2 | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2I 1280x720, 35 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2V 1280x720x61, 35 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| HunyuanVideo 848x480x61, 30 steps, Ulysses 2 | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| LTX-2 two-stage 768x512x121, 40 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B 1280x720x33, 40 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| MiniMax-H3 T2VA 1344x768 4 s, 12 steps, Ulysses 2 | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |
| MOVA-360p I2VA 640x352x97, 20 steps, TP2 | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Host syncs inside the denoising stage, counted with `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("warn")` around the stage's forward on a real server request (rank 0, second request, per denoising step):

None of the twelve models above runs the code this PR changes in a way that syncs per step: their counts move only through the follow-ups (#<B>, #<C>). The paths changed here are FLUX.1/FLUX.2/JoyImage/LingBot RoPE setup, Kandinsky-6 PiFlow, Helios, Wan DMD / FastWan and ring attention on the FA backend. A GPU sync count and A/B for those (FastWan2.2-TI2V DMD, Wan2.1 with ring degree 2, FLUX.2 klein) is still to be run.

The CUDA guard tests (`no_cuda_sync`) ran on an H200 and pass.

Keep this PR in draft until the A/B above exists; the RoPE-position change removes 64-120 small launches per eager step, which should show on launch-bound models (FLUX.2, Z-Image), but it has not been measured in isolation.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Remove per-step host syncs and uploads in image models
author: mickqian
body:
Depends on #46045 (host-sync guards in `test/unit/host_sync_guard.py`); this branch is stacked on it.

## Motivation

Several image pipelines read device values on the host or upload constants with pageable copies inside the denoising loop, or redo request-constant work in every forward. Each such read blocks the host until the stream drains, so it cannot queue the next step while the GPU runs this one. This PR removes them model by model. All values are unchanged.

## Modifications

- **Qwen-Image** (`dits/qwen_image.py`, `pipeline_configs/qwen_image.py`, `qwen_image21.py`, `vaes/base.py`, `qwen_image_layered.py`):
  - Layered built `additional_t_cond` with a pageable `torch.tensor([0])` per CFG branch. The branches got different objects, so the DiT's modulation cache never hit on the negative branch and every step recomputed 60 blocks x 2 modulation GEMMs. Both branches now share one device tensor.
  - Batched prompts of different lengths rebuilt their varlen metadata every forward, uploading the lengths from pageable memory (a sync per step and branch). The metadata is cached by its lengths; each forward gets a fresh dict, since attention may memoize into it.
  - Layered's condition-image encode, the channel-wise VAE stats helper (Qwen-Image edit encode/decode, Krea-2, JoyImage) and Qwen-Image-2.1 decode uploaded latent mean/std per request; they are uploaded once per (device, dtype).
- **FLUX.3 Action** (`flux3_action.py`): `cosmos_unipc` called `float(tick)` on each device tick, a sync per step. The ticks are copied to the host once per request; each step still gets the same device tick.
- **Ideogram-4** (`dits/ideogram.py`, `model_specific_stages/ideogram.py`, `progressive_resolution/ideogram.py`): every forward cast the (B, T+I, 53248) fp32 LLM features to bf16, masked them and ran the RMSNorm and the 53248 -> 4608 projection (plus its TP all-gather) on inputs that never change within a request. The stage projects each branch's conditioning on its first step, inside that step's forward context, and passes it to later steps as `llm_cond`. BCG replays still pass the raw features, which their prompt padder pads; the progressive stage drops the projection when the sequence grows. Decode uploads its latent scale/shift once per (device, dtype).
- **GLM-Image** (`dits/glm_image.py`, `pipeline_configs/glm_image.py`): the eager forward dropped the unconditional branch's prior tokens with `prior_embedding[prior_token_drop] *= 0.0`, two nonzero syncs per forward. It now selects `prior_embedding * 0.0` with `torch.where` (same values, signed zeros included). Decode stats are uploaded once.
- **Krea-2** (`pipeline_configs/krea2.py`): without SP the DiT always got a key mask and ran `bool(mask.all())` every forward. The config decides once per request and passes `mask=None` for unpadded prompts, the maskless path the DiT took before.
- **HunyuanImage-3** (`hunyuan_image3_utils.py`, `hunyuan_image3/ar_stage.py`): per step, a pageable timestep upload, host-built `timestep_embedding` frequencies uploaded on every call (five calls per CFG step), `masked_select` on the request-constant image mask for the scatter and the gather, and per-step condition-timestep uploads on the edit path. Positions, device timesteps and condition timesteps are taken once per request, predictions are gathered by position, and the frequencies are uploaded once per device.
- **SenseNova-U1** (`modeling_neo_chat.py`, `modeling_fm_modules.py`): the CFG-window check compared the device timestep in Python (two syncs per step); the window is computed for the whole schedule with the same fp32 comparisons and read once. The timestep embedder's frequencies are uploaded once per device.
- **SANA** (`dits/sana.py`): every block cast the int64 prompt mask to bool; the forward casts it once.

Tests:
- `test_qwen_image_rope.py`: batched prompts of different lengths build their varlen metadata once, and the second forward matches the first bitwise.
- `test_qwen_image_layered.py`: both CFG branches share `additional_t_cond`; VAE and condition-latent stats are uploaded once.
- `test_qwen_image21.py`, `test_glm_image_dit.py`, `test_ideogram4.py`: decode stats/constants are uploaded once and reused bitwise.
- `test_flux3_action.py`: `cosmos_unipc` with `SyncOnRead` ticks matches the plain run bitwise.
- `test_ideogram4.py`: the LLM projection runs once per branch and every step matches the unprojected forward bitwise; BCG replays get the raw features. `progressive_resolution/test_progressive.py`: a resolution change drops the projection.
- `test_glm_image_dit.py`: the prior-token drop runs under `forbid_host_syncs` and equals the graph path's `masked_fill`.
- `test_krea2_pipeline_config.py`: only ragged prompts carry a key mask.
- `test_hunyuan_image3_denoise_step.py`: timestep frequencies are built once; the image-token scatter/gather runs under `forbid_host_syncs` through the precomputed positions.
- `test_sensenova_u1.py`: timestep frequencies are built once per device.
- `test_sana_dit.py`: the prompt mask is cast once per forward, output unchanged.

The model tests run their tiny DiTs on CUDA when the runner has one (the diffusion unit suite runs on an H100).

No hunk overlaps #45942, #45943, #45944, #45948, #45965, #45966, #45967, #45977, #45978, #45979 or #45987; each of them still applies on top of this branch. #45967 also uploads Qwen-Image-2.1 latent stats once, in the encoding stage; this PR covers decode, a different function.

## Accuracy Tests

2xH200 (1 GPU for Qwen-Image-2.1), eager profiles, two requests per model with different inputs. Decoded pixels are bitwise identical to main:

| model (request) | GPUs | outputs compared | main vs PRs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I 1024x1024, 40 steps | 1 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 edit 1024x1024, 40 steps | 1 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Z-Image-Turbo 1024x1024, 9 steps, TP2 | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| FLUX.3 Klein Base 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Ideogram-4 FP8 1024x1024, 20 steps, TP2 | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2I 1280x720, 35 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2V 1280x720x61, 35 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| HunyuanVideo 848x480x61, 30 steps, Ulysses 2 | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| LTX-2 two-stage 768x512x121, 40 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B 1280x720x33, 40 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| MiniMax-H3 T2VA 1344x768 4 s, 12 steps, Ulysses 2 | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |
| MOVA-360p I2VA 640x352x97, 20 steps, TP2 | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Host syncs inside the denoising stage per step (rank 0, `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("warn")` around the stage, real server requests):

| model (request) | main: per step in the loop / per request | this PR: per step in the loop / per request |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I / edit 1024x1024, 40 steps, 1 GPU | 0 / 1 | 0 / 1 |

title: [Perf] diffusion: Remove per-step host syncs and uploads in video models
author: mickqian
body:
Depends on #46045 (host-sync guards in `test/unit/host_sync_guard.py`); this branch is stacked on it.

## Motivation

Video pipelines run long denoising loops where every blocking host read or pageable upload stalls the host on the previous step's kernels, and several of them rebuilt request-constant RoPE tables or masks on every forward. This PR removes those per-step costs model by model. Outputs are bitwise unchanged.

## Modifications

- **MOVA** (`model_specific_stages/mova.py`, `bridges/mova_dual_tower.py`): the loop uploaded both timesteps every step and `step_from_to` read them back with `float()`, four syncs per step. The paired schedule is uploaded once and the scheduler steps on the host values. Every forward re-uploaded both towers' CPU complex128 RoPE tables (six blocking copies, ~17 MB for audio) and redid the full-sequence concats, and every bridge layer rebuilt its fp32 cos/sin caches (30 layers x 2 directions); tables and bridge caches are built once per request and freed when the loop ends.
- **MiniMax-H3 / FastH3** (`dits/minimax_h3.py`, `minimax_h3_adaln_cache.py`): FastH3 PDD heads copied that step's weight and bias from the host stacks, four blocking copies per step; the stacks are uploaded once per (device, dtype) and indexed by step. The AdaLN online cache indexed its slabs with a 0-dim device slot (a host read, two per step); it now gathers with `index_select` and keeps the old strides.
- **HunyuanVideo** (`dits/hunyuanvideo.py`): the forward built the RoPE cos/sin on the host and copied both to the device every forward (~59 MB per step at 720p x 125 frames). The uploaded tables are kept per request in an underscore `Req.extra` key, which the disaggregation transport skips.
- **Helios** (`helios_denoising.py`, `dits/helios.py`): frame indices were built on the host and uploaded by each of four RoPE embeddings per forward (eight syncs per CFG step); they are built on the latent device. Every block cast the full-sequence [B, L, 6, D] modulation to fp32 (~1.4 GB per block at 384x640); the compact rows are cast once before the expand/concat.
- **Wan family** (`dits/causal_wanvideo.py`, `dits/wanvideo.py`): causal Wan (LongLive2) copied its host RoPE tables to the device every forward; they are uploaded once per request and chunk position. Wan and causal Wan blocks each cast the batch-wide modulation to fp32; the forward casts it once (the per-token TI2V table keeps its fused bf16 path).
- **LTX-2** (`dits/ltx_2.py`, `ltx_2/denoising.py`; paths not touched by #45966): `prepare_video_coords` uploaded two constant tensors per call (every forward on the LTX-2.3 one-stage path, every step for JoyEcho memory coords); they are uploaded once per device. HQ res2s: the SDE coefficient NaN replacement went through a 0-dim boolean index (nonzero on get and set, four calls per step) and is now a `torch.where`; the 100-iteration bongmath refinement hoists its fp64 casts and `h * a21`; the stage-1 step size starts from the step's host sigmas instead of `.cpu()` reads.
- **JoyEcho** (`joy_echo/denoising.py`): every DMD step read sigma and sigma_next with `.item()`; the loop takes fp32 host and device copies of the schedule once. With the memory bank (shot >= 2) the shot-constant cross masks, audio block mask and memory RoPE coords are built once per loop instead of every step.
- **SANA-WM / SANA-Video2** (`sana_wm*.py`, `sana_wm/streaming*.py`, `sana_video2.py`): the cache-type flag was uploaded in every block's clean pass and read back by the next chunk (20 uploads + 20 reads per chunk) and is now a host tensor; self-forcing steps read their timestep once per chunk; `forward_long` windows camera/Plucker inputs once per chunk so the UCPE and Plucker caches hit; the UCPE invalid-ray fix is a `torch.where`; the chunked refiner reads its sigmas from a host copy and builds each block's RoPE once on the device. SANA-Video2 builds its RoPE tables once per latent shape instead of uploading complex128 tables twice per forward.
- **Cosmos3 world models** (`dits/cosmos_dreams.py`, `dits/cosmos3_sim_auto.py`, `cosmos3_simulation/sim_auto.py`): Dreams zeroed null-action V slots by indexing with a Python list in each of 36 layers (a blocking upload each); the slots are per-frame slices. Sim-Auto's scatter/gather indexes, mRoPE frame ids and generated-frame masks are built once per chunk on the device. The default Cosmos3 T2V/I2V loop is untouched (#45967 covers its CFG window).

Tests:
- `test_mova_denoising.py`: steps never upload or read device timesteps (`SyncOnRead` schedule, one upload); RoPE tables built once per request; outputs bitwise equal.
- `test_minimax_h3_pdd_offline.py`, `test_minimax_h3_adaln_cache.py`: heads uploaded once; slab gathers run under `forbid_host_syncs` with the old values and strides.
- `test_hunyuanvideo_rope_upload.py`, `test_wan_step_host_overhead.py`: RoPE tables uploaded once per request (per chunk position for causal Wan), identical tables; blocks receive fp32 modulation.
- `test_helios_step_host_overhead.py`: frame indices live on the latent device; blocks receive fp32 modulation.
- `test_ltx2_step_host_overhead.py`: video-coord constants uploaded once; SDE coefficients under `forbid_host_syncs`; the refinement casts once.
- `test_joy_echo_denoising_host_overhead.py`: host/device sigma copies, steps never read device sigmas, the memory prefix is built once.
- `sana_wm/test_host_overhead.py`, `test_sana_video2.py`, `test_cosmos3_simulation_host_overhead.py`, `test_cosmos_dreams.py`, `test_cosmos3_sim_auto.py`: the SANA-WM, SANA-Video2 and Cosmos3 world-model paths above.

No hunk overlaps #45942, #45943, #45944, #45948, #45965, #45966, #45967, #45977, #45978, #45979 or #45987; each of them still applies on top of this branch.

## Accuracy Tests

2xH200, eager profiles, two requests per model with different inputs. Decoded frames (and audio where the model produces it) are bitwise identical to main:

| model (request) | GPUs | outputs compared | main vs PRs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I 1024x1024, 40 steps | 1 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 edit 1024x1024, 40 steps | 1 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Z-Image-Turbo 1024x1024, 9 steps, TP2 | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| FLUX.3 Klein Base 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Ideogram-4 FP8 1024x1024, 20 steps, TP2 | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2I 1280x720, 35 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2V 1280x720x61, 35 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| HunyuanVideo 848x480x61, 30 steps, Ulysses 2 | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| LTX-2 two-stage 768x512x121, 40 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B 1280x720x33, 40 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| MiniMax-H3 T2VA 1344x768 4 s, 12 steps, Ulysses 2 | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |
| MOVA-360p I2VA 640x352x97, 20 steps, TP2 | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Host syncs inside the denoising stage per step (rank 0, `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("warn")` around the stage, real server requests):

| model (request) | main: per step in the loop / per request | this PR: per step in the loop / per request |
|---|---|---|
| HunyuanVideo 848x480x61, 30 steps, Ulysses 2 | 4 / 121 | 0 / 3 |
| MOVA-360p I2VA 640x352x97, 20 steps, TP2 | 16 / 320 | 0 / 13 |
| LTX-2 two-stage, stage 1, 768x512x121, 40 steps, CFG parallel | 4 / 161 | 2 / 81 (the sigma reads #45966 removes) |
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B 1280x720x33, 40 steps, CFG parallel | 0 / 2 | 0 / 2 |
| MiniMax-H3 T2VA (fl2va) 1344x768 4 s, 12 steps, Ulysses 2 | 0 / 38 | 0 / 38 (setup; the FastH3 PDD and AdaLN-cache paths are not in this command) |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2V 1280x720x61, 35 steps, CFG parallel | 0 / 7 | 0 / 7 |

Client latency, interleaved A/B (main, PR, PR, main), fresh server per run, median of 2 measured requests per run:

| cell | round | main | this PR (with #46045) |
|---|---|---|---|
| MOVA-360p I2VA 640x352x97, 20 steps, TP2 | 1 | 46.696 s | 46.458 s |
| | 2 | 46.706 s | 46.524 s |
| | median | 46.701 s | 46.491 s (-0.45%) |
| HunyuanVideo 848x480x61, 30 steps, Ulysses 2 | 1 | 46.120 s | 46.122 s |
| | 2 | 46.158 s | 46.096 s |
| | median | 46.139 s | 46.109 s (-0.07%, noise) |

- MOVA: the denoising stage went from 44.67 s to 44.22 s (-1.0%) in both rounds, from the 16 per-step syncs and the per-forward RoPE rebuilds going away.
- HunyuanVideo at this shape is GPU-bound (about 1.4 s per step), so the four removed syncs per step do not show in the latency; the saving is the per-step 2 x RoPE upload, which grows with resolution and frame count.
- Wan2.2-T2V-A14B and MiniMax-H3 T2VA have no per-step syncs on main in these commands (table above), so no latency change is expected there; their A/B did not complete (the benchmark machine was released mid-run, after one MiniMax-H3 main run at 138.38 s). This needs a rerun before the speed claim covers them.

title: [Perf] dsv41: Build the MegaGate row masks once per forward
author: yhyang201
body:
## Motivation
With MegaGate on (`SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_GATE=1`), `run_mega_gate` rebuilds the valid-row mask (`arange < num_token_non_padded`) and the image-token mask (`input_ids == image_token_id`) in every MoE layer, though both depend only on the batch. In DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode this is three small kernels per gate call, serialized ahead of the gate on the MoE stream, in every layer of every step.

## Modifications
- `mega_gate.py`: `mega_gate_forward_scope(forward_batch)` installs a per-forward dict on `forward_batch`; `_gate_row_masks` builds the two masks on the first MoE layer and returns them to the rest (keyed by row count and the identity of the inputs). Under CUDA graphs the capture records one build.
- `mega_moe.py`: pass `forward_batch` to `run_mega_gate`.
- `deepseek_v4.py`, `deepseek_v4_dspark.py`: wrap `forward` in the scope.

No behavior change when MegaGate is off.

## Accuracy Tests
GSM8K (`sglang.test.run_eval`, 5-shot, 1,314 examples, temperature 0, thinking off), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DP attention + EP 8, MegaGate + `SGLANG_DSV4_KV_LAYOUT=v41_new`: same score before and after.

## Speed Tests and Profiling
Decode, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DP attention + EP 8 on GB300, MegaGate + `v41_new`, 8 to 256 running requests per rank: 0.25-0.35 ms less per step at every batch size (1.1-2.3%), from the server's `Decode batch` lines. In a GPU trace, the arange / int compare / int64 compare launches ahead of the gate go from one set per MoE layer to one per forward.

title: [Perf] trtllm_mha: Split full-attention decode KV across CTAs at large batch (opt-in)
author: nbommi19
body:
## Motivation

TRTLLM-GEN decode gives each (request, KV head) `max(1, SMs // (batch * kv_heads))` CTAs. Once `batch * kv_heads` exceeds half the SMs, every request-head streams its whole KV on a single CTA. In long-context batches the longest request then sets the time of every full-attention layer.

This PR splits the KV of full-attention layers across a fixed number of CTAs at large batch, in fixed-q-len decode and verify. Sliding-window layers, ragged verify and the XQA path (SM90/SM120) are unchanged.

FlashInfer has no per-call split count yet. The split is applied by scoping the SM count that `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` reads for that one call. The number of split CTAs is capped by the workspace and the multi-CTA counter buffer.

Related: #37208 regroups mixed-length decode batches; this PR instead splits each request's KV on full-attention layers. The two compose; not yet measured together.

## How to enable

```bash
SGLANG_TRTLLM_MHA_FULL_ATTN_KV_SPLITS=8          # default 0 (off)
SGLANG_TRTLLM_MHA_FULL_ATTN_KV_SPLITS_MIN_BS=12  # default 12
```

Requires `--attention-backend trtllm_mha` on SM100.

## Performance

Muse-Spark-Open NVFP4, 4x GB300, TP4/EP4, FP8 KV cache, DFLASH with 8 draft tokens, HiCache (write-back), at most 32 running requests. Multi-turn long-context requests at concurrency 48. Each row toggles only the decode split on the same build.

| Baseline | Concurrency | Throughput per GPU (tok/s), baseline | Throughput per GPU (tok/s), this PR | Per-user decode speed, P90 (tok/s/user), baseline | Per-user decode speed, P90 (tok/s/user), this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No KV split (default) | 48 | 46,373 | 64,231 (+38.5%) | 41.87 | 72.05 (+72.1%) |
| Existing all-layer seq-len split, `SGLANG_TRTLLM_MHA_DECODE_SEQ_LEN_SPLITS=4` | 48 | 57,728 | 64,231 (+11.3%) | 58.91 | 72.05 (+22.3%) |

Throughput per GPU counts input and output tokens. Per-user decode speed excludes time to first token; P90 is the speed 90% of requests reach.

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_trtllm_mha_paged_kv.py`, 4 new CPU cases:
- the split engages only on full-attention layers, at batch >= MIN_BS, where FlashInfer would split less;
- a fixed-q-len verify launches inside the scope, sized by requests (query rows // `q_len_per_req`);
- the split CTAs stay within the workspace and counter capacity;
- the scoped SM count is restored after an error.

Accuracy, GSM8K strict match with the split: 0.9765. The split changes the attention reduction order, at rounding level only.

title: [Perf] dsv41: Fuse decode mHC post, combine and RMSNorm into one kernel
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

In DeepSeek-V4.1 decode and target-verify, each layer boundary runs these small kernels back to back on the critical path:
- the mHC post (`mhc_post_split_h`);
- the next sub-layer's four-stream combine and RMSNorm (`hc_combine_norm` / `hc_combine_norm_mxfp8`);
- above 128 rows, a separate MXFP8 quantize of the normed row.

Each is a few microseconds, and at decode batch sizes most of that is launch and dependency latency, not bandwidth.

## Modifications

- New JIT kernel `mhc_post_combine_norm_decode`. One CTA per row computes, in one launch:
  - the mHC post (updated residual streams);
  - the next combine weighted by `pre`;
  - RMSNorm;
  - optionally the MXFP8 output in the swizzled layout the next GEMM takes.
- `_post_fusion` in `deepseek_v4_mhc.py` uses it on Blackwell for up to 1024 rows. The threads per row are the count that needs the fewest waves, using the occupancy CUDA reports for the kernel. The DSv4.1 shape is required (mult 4, hidden 5120, bf16, fp32 coefficients). It is skipped in batch-invariant mode.
- Mega-mHC (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MEGA_MHC_PREFILL`, opt-in) now serves only this rank's own extend batches (target verify excluded), read from the local forward mode. On decode/verify it computed the next sub-layer's mix statistics on the critical path instead of on the side stream beside attention/MoE, and it was slower than the unfused path at every batch size measured.
- The post output is bitwise identical to `mhc_post_split_h`. The RMS statistic is summed in a different order than the Triton kernel, so the normed row can differ in the last bf16 bit.
- Registered in the layernorm kernel inventory.
- `test_mhc_post_combine_norm_decode.py` checks every thread-count transition and the 1024-row cap against the unfused kernels, with and without MXFP8, plus the gate.

## Accuracy and speed

Validated with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 decode at 128K context, ABBA arms in one job per node:
- CC 10.7: steady-state decode throughput is at or above the unfused path at every batch size from 16 to 224. GSM8K is unchanged.
- CC 10.3: at or above the unfused path at batch sizes 16 to 64.
- B200 (SM100), kernel only, CUDA graph of 32 launches over rotating inputs: up to 128 rows the fused kernel takes 3.9–4.5 µs, against 3.9–5.5 µs for the unfused kernels without MXFP8 and 5.2–9.5 µs with it. It is at or below the unfused path at every size up to 1024 rows.
- A profiler probe on each arm confirms the fused kernel replaces `mhc_post_split_h` + `hc_combine_norm(_mxfp8)` on decode, and that Mega-mHC still serves extend batches when enabled.

## Checklist

- [x] Validate on SM103 and on current main (kernel tests pass on SM103).
- [x] Validate on SM100 (kernel tests pass on B200).

title: [Perf] moe: Fold the routed scaling factor into the mega MoE pre-dispatch
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

When `routed_scaling_factor != 1`, `run_mega_routed_experts` scales the top-k weights with a separate elementwise kernel. Right after that, the JIT `mega_moe_pre_dispatch` copies those same weights into the Mega MoE symmetric buffer. That is one extra small launch on the decode critical path for every MoE layer.

## Modifications

- `mega_moe_pre_dispatch` takes `topk_weight_scale`, and the kernel applies it with `__fmul_rn` while copying the weights. It is the same single fp32 multiply, so the result is bitwise identical to the standalone multiply.
- `run_mega_routed_experts` passes `routed_scaling_factor` for the JIT pre-dispatch path. It keeps the explicit multiply for the nvfp4xnvfp4 and mxf4xmxf4 paths, which use DeepGEMM's own pre-dispatch.
- The `routing_in_buffer` path still asserts `routed_scaling_factor == 1.0`, so it is unchanged.
- A new `test_mega_moe_pre_dispatch.py` case checks the scaled copy against the separate multiply bit for bit.

## Validation

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4, Mega MoE, on a CC 10.7 node: weights bitwise identical, and GSM8K unchanged.
- Small decode throughput gain, measured together with a sibling mHC change, so it is not isolated.

title: [Perf] moe: Always pass the global token count to the Mega MoE tile heuristic
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

DeepGEMM's Mega MoE picks its tile (`block_m`) from the calling rank's own token count. With DP attention and EP, an eager prefill forward can be very uneven across ranks. For example, one 128K request is chunked on one rank while the other ranks run idle forwards. The idle ranks then size their tiles for one token, small `block_m`, but they compute experts for the busy rank's tokens. The whole fused dispatch-GEMM-combine kernel runs at the pace of the badly tiled ranks.

DeepGEMM already accepts `global_num_tokens` for this, in both `get_block_m_for_mega_moe` and `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`. SGLang doesn't pass it.

## Modifications

- Eager Mega MoE forwards pass the DP-global token count, capped at `ep_size * num_max_tokens_per_rank`, to the kernel and to both shared-expert `block_m` queries: the one in `run_mega_routed_experts` and the one in `mega_moe_input_target`, which sizes the shared-expert scale factors when Mega-mHC writes the MegaMoE input under MegaGate. Both queries then match the kernel's tile.
- CUDA-graph capture is unaffected (the hint is skipped during capture, so decode graphs are unchanged), and so is prefill context parallelism.

## Accuracy and speed

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4, 128K prompts, on a CC 10.7 node. Arms ran ABBA in one job:
- Single-request TTFT drops noticeably, because the idle ranks no longer pick the smallest tile.
- Multi-request prefill improves slightly.
- GSM8K is unchanged.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Write uncompressed PNG responses without Pillow's row filters
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Image responses are encoded as PNG with zlib level 0 by default since #45987. Pillow still runs its adaptive row filter at that level: for every row it tries the PNG filters and keeps the one with the smallest sum (the encoded files use filters 1 and 2). At level 0 the deflate stream is stored, not compressed, so the filter cannot make the file smaller. It only costs time, and the time is on the output rank between the end of the forward and the reply:

| frame | Pillow, `compress_level=0` | unfiltered rows in stored blocks |
|---|---|---|
| 1024x1024 RGBA (Qwen-Image-2.1) | 74.9 ms | 4.3 ms |
| 1280x720 RGB (Cosmos3 T2I) | 60.9 ms | 2.8 ms |

(One core of a Xeon Platinum 8558P, `Pillow` 13.0.0, zlib 1.3.2. OpenCV's level-0 encoder takes 37.0 / 26.5 ms.)

## Modifications

`entrypoints/utils.py`: `_encode_image_frame` writes a uint8 frame with `compress_level == 0` itself: unfiltered rows (filter byte 0) in one `zlib.compress(rows, 0)` IDAT, behind the same IHDR Pillow writes. Any other level, and non-uint8 frames, still go through Pillow.

The PNG is the same image:
- The IHDR is byte-identical. Pillow writes no other chunks on this path (no gAMA, sRGB, pHYs or text), so the only difference is how the IDAT data is filtered and split: one IDAT chunk instead of Pillow's 64 KiB chunks.
- Decoded pixels, mode and `info` are equal for gray, gray + alpha, RGB and RGBA frames.
- The file is slightly smaller (1024x1024 RGBA: 4,195,716 bytes instead of 4,196,804).

Tests:
- `test_output_saving.py`: levels None, 0 and 75 no longer call Pillow's save, level 100 still saves through Pillow at `compress_level=9`, and every saved file decodes to the source frame. On main the uncompressed cases call Pillow and fail.
- `test_image_response_bytes.py`: the returned-bytes test also covers two-channel (gray + alpha) frames.

## Accuracy Tests

The decoded pixels are identical to the frame the pipeline produced, so the served image does not change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Client latency (median of 5 after warmup), main vs this PR, a fresh server per arm, distinct inputs per request; the Qwen arms ran in pairs on two GPUs and swapped GPUs between rounds.

1xH200 (Qwen-Image-2.1, `--performance-mode speed`) and 2xH200 (Cosmos3-Nano T2I, CFG parallel):

| case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I 1024, GPU 0 / GPU 1 | 4.412 / 4.422 s | 4.376 / 4.385 s |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 edit 1024, GPU 0 / GPU 1 | 5.313 / 5.321 s | 5.257 / 5.284 s |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I throughput (4 requests, concurrency 2) | 0.2267 / 0.2264 req/s | 0.2288 / 0.2282 req/s |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2I 720p, round 1 / round 2 | 0.909 / 0.911 s | 0.893 / 0.895 s |

Every PR sample is below every main sample on the same GPU. On the output rank, the time from the end of the forward to the encoded bytes went from 47 ms to 9.7 ms for a 1024x1024 RGBA image (the rest is the uint8 conversion and the device-to-host copy).

B300 (same harness and protocol, B300 commands; the arms ran next to other arms on the same host, so absolute numbers sit ~10-20 ms above an idle host). The tree under test also carried other changes that do nothing for these requests (they act on reference images and the vision tower):

| case | main | this PR |

| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I 1024, GPU 0 / GPU 1 | 2.231 / 2.250 s | 2.193 / 2.204 s |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I throughput, GPU 0 / GPU 1 | 0.4514 / 0.4513 req/s | 0.4610 / 0.4588 req/s |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2I 720p (2 GPUs), round 1 / round 2 | 0.566 / 0.546 s | 0.511 / 0.512 s |

title: [Perf] diffusion/qwen-image-2.1: Keep an image prefix's K/V in the packed buffer across steps
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Qwen-Image-2.1 computes the prompt prefix (text, and for edits the reference image tokens) once per request and caches its per-layer K/V. Every cached denoising step still rebuilds the attention input from scratch: the packed projection allocates a fresh `[P+S, 3C]` QKV buffer per layer, and the fused Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE + pack kernel copies the cached prefix K/V into its first `P` rows before attention.

For text-to-image the prefix is a few dozen rows and the copy is free. For an edit the reference image makes the prefix about as long as the target (1248x864 reference: 4212 image rows plus text, against 4096 target rows), so the copy doubles the kernel's memory traffic in every layer of every step. On 1xH200 the kernel takes 164 us per call in an edit request against 95 us in a text-to-image request (grid capped at 65535 instead of 32984 blocks): about 88 ms per 40-step request across 32 layers.

## Modifications

`models/dits/qwen_image21.py`, `QwenImage21Attention`:
- After an image-conditioned prefill on the packed path, the request's per-layer cache keeps the packed buffer (`cache["qkv"]`), and its `key`/`value` become views of that buffer's prefix rows, so the separate prefix tensors are freed.
- Cached steps project into the kept buffer (the GEMM writes rows `[P:]` exactly as before) and call the same CUDA kernel with an empty prefix on the target rows, so it normalizes and rotates Q and the target K in place and copies nothing. Attention reads the full buffer.
- Text-only prefixes keep today's compact copy. The kept path needs the packed projection and a verified CUDA pack kernel, single sample, no SP, and no BCG prefix padding; anything else runs as before.

The attention inputs are the same values in the same layout, so outputs are bitwise unchanged. Memory: an edit request holds `[P+S, 3C]` bf16 per layer instead of the `[P, 2C]` prefix plus one transient buffer, about 3.1 GB more at the 1024x1024 edit shape.

Tests (`test_qwen_image21_cuda.py`, CUDA):
- `test_cached_steps_copy_the_prefix_only_for_text`: records every pack-kernel call over a prefill and two cached steps. For an image prefix the cached steps pass an empty prefix and write into the buffer kept by the prefill; for a text prefix they copy the prefix as before.
- `test_cuda_qk_rope_pack_matches_eager_prefill_and_cached_steps`: still bitwise against the eager chain on prefill and cached steps and under BCG replay; its storage check now expects an image prefix to live in the kept buffer and a text prefix to stay compact.

## Accuracy Tests

1xH200, the harness's Qwen-Image-2.1 edit and text-to-image requests: decoded output pixels are bitwise identical to main (md5 of 3 edit and 2 text-to-image outputs, stacked with the other changes listed below).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

1xH200, Qwen-Image-2.1 edit 1024, fresh servers, two GPUs alternated, client medians of 5 (base = main + stored PNG + parallel digest; this column also has the threaded condition resize, see the per-change split below):

| GPU | base | + this PR + threaded resize |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 5.246 / 5.237 s | 5.157 s |
| 1 | 5.262 s | 5.176 / 5.174 s |

Per-change split, measured inside one server that switches this change off request by request (interleaved rounds, harness edit request; an A/A pair in the same rotation stays within 5 ms):

| | without this PR | with this PR | difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1xH200, 8 rounds | 5.222 s | 5.155 s | −68 ms |
| 1xB300 (`--attention-backend fa`), 6 rounds | 2.657 s | 2.603 s | −50 ms |
