title: [Perf] mamba: write the deduplicated conv verify window as one tile
author: jianc99
body:
This is component 1 of the DFlash adaptive-verification series. Original implementation and component-only review: https://github.com/jianc99/sglang/pull/1. Integration and full-system results: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46182.

Updated onto upstream `main` (6a319e7b). All applicable pre-commit checks passed on this branch. The GPU tests and benchmark results below were run previously on the original source branch; they have not been rerun after this upstream update. Submission preparation used AI assistance.

---

## Motivation

On hybrid models, linear-chain speculative verify (EAGLE chain, MTP, DFLASH, DSPARK, standalone) calls `causal_conv1d_update` with an intermediate conv window. The window lets the conv state of the accepted prefix be restored after verify.

On CUDA and ROCm, `MambaPool` stores this window deduplicated. Each slot holds one `[dim, T + K - 2]` row, exposed as an overlapping `[T, dim, K - 1]` view whose step stride equals its window stride.

The kernel still writes the window per token, with three lane-strided element stores per draft token. Each column is therefore written up to three times by narrow scattered stores. On GB300 (dim 10240, bf16, T = 8, bs 128), the verify conv takes 106 us with the deduplicated window, against 39 us with a dense window.

## Modifications

- **`_causal_conv1d_update_kernel`**: adds a `DEDUP_CONV_WINDOW` path.
  - Step t's window is columns t..t+2 of the row `[state[1], state[2], x_0, ..., x_{T-1}]`.
  - The kernel writes that row once, as a `[BLOCK_N, next_pow2(T + 2)]` tile before the token loop, and skips the per-token window stores.
  - The tile mask covers exactly the T + 2 columns the per-token path writes.
  - Padded rows still exit before any store.
  - Two `tl.static_assert`s keep the branch from being compiled for a conv width other than 4 or together with a tree mask, so the kernel is safe without relying on its caller.
- **`causal_conv1d_update`**: takes the tile path only when all three hold:
  - the window view's step stride equals its window stride;
  - the verify is a chain (no tree mask);
  - the conv width is 4.

  With step stride == window stride == s, the per-token stores write column t + w of the row at (t + w) * s, and the tile writes column c at c * s: the same addresses and the same values, for any layout with those strides. MambaPool's deduplicated view is one such layout. There are no new arguments, and callers are unchanged. Kernels that do not take the tile get `NP2_WINDOW_COLS=1`, so no extra variants are compiled.
- **Test**: `test_causal_conv1d_update_dedup_window_matches_per_token`.
  - It runs the kernel on a dense window (per-token path) and on the deduplicated view (tile path).
  - It checks bitwise that the shared rows, the windows read through the view and the conv state match a reference row built in torch.
  - It checks that slots of padded rows are untouched.
  - It compares the conv output with the file's update tolerances.
  - Coverage: T in {2, 3, 8, 16} (T + 2 pads to tiles of 4, 8, 16 and 32), a `num_accept_tokens` state offset, MambaPool's axis-0 window layout seen transposed, fp32 and bf16, a dim that leaves a partial channel block, with and without padded rows.
- A comment in `MambaPool` is updated to describe the new write.

## Scope

This path is used by every chain verify (topk <= 1) whose conv window uses `MambaPool`'s deduplicated layout. Examples are GDN models (Qwen3.5/3.8) and Mamba2, on CUDA and ROCm.

These are unchanged and keep the per-token stores:
- dense windows: `UnifiedMambaPool`, KDA / Kimi-Linear, tree verify;
- deduplicated windows of a conv width other than 4 (for example LFM2, width 3).

## Accuracy Tests

- The new test passes, and so does the full test file (270 tests at 8eb01f2c9, which adds the tree-mask assert and the accept-offset, axis-0 and odd-T cases).
- The test is sensitive: a tile that ignores `num_accept_tokens` fails exactly the accept-offset cases, and forcing the tile together with a tree mask fails at compile time on the new assert.
- compute-sanitizer memcheck, racecheck and initcheck are clean on the tile test as of 8177311a1 (T in {2, 4, 8, 16}); besides comments and tests, 8eb01f2c9 adds only a compile-time assert and `NP2_WINDOW_COLS=1` for launches without the tile. The extra 72-case check below, which covers accepted-token offsets, transposed views and odd T, is also memcheck-clean.
- An extra 72-case check also passes, comparing the tile path bitwise with the per-token path. It covers T in {1, 3, 9}, mixed input and state dtypes, transposed views and accepted-token offsets.
- End to end, greedy, c1: acceptance length and output tokens are identical to main.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Kernel time per call in microseconds (GB300, dim 10240, K 4, bf16, CUDA graph):

| bs | T | before | after | dense window |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8 | 5.35 | 2.49 | 3.71 |
| 64 | 8 | 57.39 | 9.96 | 21.08 |
| 128 | 8 | 106.45 | 17.55 | 38.58 |
| 128 | 16 | 322.63 | 39.10 | 74.12 |

End-to-end setup:
- Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2 (block 8), TP1, one GB300;
- chain verify, bf16 mamba state, overlap scheduling on, `--max-running-requests 128`;
- SPEED-Bench first turns, T = 1, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, up to 4096 output tokens;
- mean of 3 interleaved runs.

Decode tok/s = per-request decode rate (output tokens after the first / time after the first token), times concurrency; c1 is the single-request decode rate.

| concurrency | main | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 6048 | 6361 | +5.2% |
| 128 | 6992 | 7329 | +4.8% |

Acceptance length is 3.59-3.63 in all six runs.

At c128 the running cap equals the concurrency, so about one request waits in the queue. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46182 shows that this setup reads 7-15% higher at that level than a larger cap, on both sides, so compare c128 only within this table.

Single runs at lower concurrency: c8 2031 -> 2104 (+3.6%), c32 4723 -> 4973 (+5.3%). At c1 the change is within noise: 332 -> 321, with acceptance length 3.70 vs 3.60 from sampling; per accepted token the rate differs by under 0.5%. Greedy (single runs): c1 357.0 -> 357.1 with identical acceptance length and output tokens, c64 6746 -> 7145 (+5.9%).

The end-to-end runs used the first commit; the two later commits add compile-time asserts, comments and tests, and pass `NP2_WINDOW_COLS=1` to kernels that skip the tile, with no runtime change on the tile path.

## Related upstream work

- sgl-project/sglang#38897 adds a separate packed variable-length kernel, `causal_conv1d_update_varlen`, to the same file. It writes the intermediate window per token with three stores per step, the pattern this PR replaces. There is no textual conflict (it is a new function), but if both land, packed verify through that kernel does not get the tile store. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46189 takes the other route: it adds packed rows to this kernel, so the tile store covers them too.
- This PR does not depend on any open PR.

## Notes

- The tile store is SubSir's work from the dynamic-verify branch. This PR ports it to the current kernel, gates it on the view's strides and adds the tests.
- Only GB300 was tested; ROCm takes the same path but has not been run.
- Commits: 7526326d8 (tile store and stride gate), 8177311a1 (width assert, test trim, `MambaPool` comment), 8eb01f2c9 (tree-mask assert, stride-based wrapper comment, `NP2_WINDOW_COLS=1` when the tile is off, more test layouts). Squash them when merging upstream.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] custom-all-reduce: Enable 2shot_push in SM107 TP4/TP8/TP16 heuristic
author: wookjeHan
body:
## Motivation The SM107 custom all-reduce table (#36397) was tuned before `2shot_push` existed. #42811 added `2shot_push` later but retuned only the SM100 rows, so SM107 never enables it. Above the 1shot_push ceiling, SM107 sizes fall through to `2shot_pull` (TP4 graph) or multicast `2shot_pull` (TP4 eager, TP8, TP16). On SM107, a per-algorithm sweep shows `2shot_push` is the fastest custom algorithm from about 1 MB (TP4), 384 KB (TP8) and 256 KB (TP16) up to 16 MB. Every other threshold in the #36397 table lines up with the sweep to within one size step. ## Modifications `_sm107_configs` (`configs/custom_all_reduce_v2.py`) only: - `config()` takes an optional `two_shot_push=` threshold, the same keyword the SM100 table uses. It defaults to 0 (disabled), so worlds that don't set it are unchanged. - **TP4**: 1shot ceiling 6.938 MB (graph) / 9.812 MB (eager) becomes 1 MB, then `2shot_push` up to 16 MB. The eager multicast range is untouched; it is only reached above 16 MB. - **TP8**: 1shot ceiling 2.438 MB becomes 384 KB, then `2shot_push` up to 16 MB. - **TP16**: 1shot ceiling 832 KB becomes 256 KB, then `2shot_push` up to 16 MB. - **TP2** is unchanged: `2shot_push` never wins there. TP3/5/6/7 are not tuned and keep their #36397 rows. `test_custom_all_reduce.py::test_custom_all_reduce_eager_plan_follows_config` zeroes every threshold to force the NCCL path. It now also zeroes `two_shot_push_threshold`; otherwise the size still routes to `2shot_push` on any arch whose table enables it. ## Accuracy Tests `test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_custom_all_reduce.py` (bit-exact against NCCL, graph and eager) on SM107: | world | result | |---|---| | 2 | 310 passed | | 4 | 310 passed | | 8 (2 nodes, MNNVL) | 310 passed (every rank) | | 16 (4 nodes, MNNVL) | 310 passed (every rank) | ## Speed Tests and Profiling The method follows #42811: - bf16 input. - One CUDA graph of 100 back-to-back all-reduces; median of 9 replays; max over ranks. - Eager mode is the eager dispatch path captured without `comm.capture()`, so staging copies are included and Python launch overhead is not. - Ranks are aligned on the GPU (a tiny NCCL all-reduce) right before each timed replay. - Per-algorithm columns are forced through `override_algo`; multicast `2shot_pull` is forced with a temporary heuristic. - "today" and "this PR" are the tuned tables run end to end (`auto`). title: [Feat] openai: Parse DeepSeek text for the native endpoints through deepseek-recipe
author: hnyls2002
body:
With #45907, chat and Responses output of DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 is parsed by deepseek-recipe. The native `/separate_reasoning` and `/parse_function_call` endpoints still parsed it with SGLang's text detectors. This moves them onto recipe as well and removes the text parsing that no serving path uses any more.

## Changes

- `/separate_reasoning` with `deepseek-v4` / `deepseek-v41` and `/parse_function_call` with `deepseekv4` / `deepseekv41` parse through the served model's recipe adapter: the text is tokenized, so the markers it spells count as tokens, and recipe parses it as a whole output.
- The endpoints pick the parser through the chat encoding registry (`native_text_parser`, with the adapter-owned parser names in `ADAPTER_OUTPUT_PARSERS`), so `http_server.py` does not depend on a model's module.
- `/parse_function_call` returns every call recipe parses, as chat does and as the official API does: `tool_index` is the tool's position in `tools`, or -1 for a tool outside it. Without `tools` the text comes back unparsed, as before.
- The DeepSeek detectors keep what the grammar, the scheduler and the serving decisions read (think tokens, excluded tokens, structural tag names, reasoning defaults). Removed:
  - the reasoning detector's DSML tool-start settings and the V4.1 reasoning subclass, which only overrode them;
  - the V4.1 tool detector's `strip_string_param_value`, and two attributes nothing read.

## Behavior changes

- `/separate_reasoning` splits text that closes a thinking block (`a</think>b` -> reasoning `a`, text `b`). The text parser split only text that opened with `<think>`, which V4 output never does, since `<think>` ends the prompt. A leading `<think>` is still accepted.
- A DeepSeek parser name on a server that is not serving that DeepSeek model returns 400: recipe parses with the served checkpoint's tokenizer.
- `/separate_reasoning` treats text that opens with `<think>` as reasoning even when it is cut before `</think>`, as before; a `<think>` in the middle of the text stays text, where the text parser opened reasoning there.
- A second `</think>` is dropped, and newlines that open the reasoning or the answer are trimmed, as recipe does for chat.
- `/parse_function_call` returns calls to tools outside `tools` (with `tool_index` -1); the text parser dropped them unless `SGLANG_FORWARD_UNKNOWN_TOOLS` was set. It also drops a stray `</think>` from `normal_text`.

## Tests

- Added `test_native_endpoints_parse_through_recipe`: the reasoning split, a tool call, and the 400 case.
- Removed the V4 / V4.1 text-parsing tests: the round trip in `test_deepseekv41_detector.py`, DSML routing and chunk invariance in `test_reasoning_parser.py`, and parsing in `test_function_call_parser.py`. The grammar and structural-tag tests stay.

title: [Perf] pd: Apply the prefill WAR barrier after the previous result is processed
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

In the PD prefill overlap loop, `_apply_war_barrier()` runs right after `run_batch(k)`, so all schedule-stream work in the previous batch's result processing is queued behind forward k.

The barrier waits for the whole forward whenever the forward does not publish a pre-replay read-done event. On main that is any HiCache, storage-backend or LMCache deployment, plus any backend or speculative algorithm without `PRE_REPLAY`. In that case:

- The first host-blocking device-to-host copy in `process_batch_result_disagg_prefill(k-1)` waits until forward k finishes. In our traces that copy is the KV-send state page translation (`_swa_payload` -> `kv_to_page_indices`).
- The rest of the per-request bookkeeping then runs serially with the GPU idle: radix checkpoint, SWA and paged frees, KV-send translation, and the next schedule. This bookkeeping holds hundreds of small syncs per step.
- With DP attention, the other DP rank waits for this rank in the per-step metadata all-gather. So one rank's bookkeeping stalls both ranks.

On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill (DEP2), on a build where this model still fell back to the whole-forward barrier (before #45582 and #45682), Nsight showed 70-100 ms of GPU idle between consecutive prefill forwards. That is 15-20% of a ~500 ms step. On current main the same deployment publishes read-done and does not hit this; HiCache, storage-backend and LMCache prefill still do.

## Modifications

`event_loop_overlap_disagg_prefill` now applies the barrier later: after `process_batch_result(k-1)` and `process_disagg_prefill_inflight_queue()`, and before the next schedule. On the continuous-polling path, when the oldest result is not ready yet, the barrier is applied before `continue`, so later intake keeps the current ordering. The normal and decode loops are unchanged.

This is safe only in the PD prefill loop. Its result processing mutates no request that is in forward k:

- Finished, aborted and released requests are not in forward k. Their radix checkpoint, deduplicated-page frees, SWA mapping updates and KV sends only touch their own rows and slots. Freed slots are reallocated only by the next schedule, which still runs after the barrier.
- A request whose next chunk is in forward k is only read during result processing (the non-last-chunk KV send). Its chunk stash (`process_prefill_chunk` -> checkpoint) runs in the next schedule, after the barrier.
- KV transfers and cache offloads issued here read pages written by forward k-1. Forward k-1 has completed, because the schedule stream is behind the k-1 barrier and the result copy has been synchronized.

- One write can reach memory that forward k's requests hold: inserting a finished request can recover a tombstoned SWA component on a node whose Full KV is locked by a request in forward k, and rewrite that node's `full_to_swa` entries. Those positions are outside the locking request's sliding window (its in-window nodes are SWA-locked and cannot be tombstoned), so forward k never uses them.

The decode and normal loops keep the barrier right after launch. There, result processing can rewrite rows of requests still running in the next forward; that hazard is the reason the barrier was placed after launch.

The safety depends on an invariant that the code does not check: nothing between `run_batch(k)` and the barrier may allocate or evict device memory that gets reused, stash or release the continuing chunked request, or send a partial page. The inline comment states the rule.

Limits:

- With continuous input polling, when the oldest result is not ready, the barrier is still applied before `continue`, so the gain is smaller there.
- With eager unified-memory compaction, the eager free waits for the forward stream itself, which cancels the gain.
- The PP prefill loop and the non-overlap PD loop do not call the WAR barrier and are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K through the full PD path (2x DEP2 prefill + DEP4 decode, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash FP4, DSPARK). Settings: sgl-eval 0.1.3 with `--load-preset-from-model-id deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, all 1319 examples, 128 threads:

| prefill cache | score | error rate | stop rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| HiCache (write_back, direct) | 0.968 | 0 | 1.0 |
| Mooncake external linker | 0.967 | 0 | 1.0 |

Unit tests: `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/` plus the prefill polling, idle-step, shared-read-done and decode shared-read fence tests pass on CPU (406 passed, 14 CUDA-only skipped).

## Benchmark & Profiling

Setup: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash FP4 on GB300, 6x DEP2 prefill + 1x DEP32 decode (44 engine GPUs), DSPARK, chunked prefill 65536. Workload: agentic coding traces at concurrency 3018, with a 30-minute cold measurement (no client warmup). Each arm is one run.

HiCache prefill (local host tier, ratio 1.1, write_back, direct IO). HiCache always uses the whole-forward barrier, on main as well:

| | base | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| total tok/s per GPU | 224,394 | 240,356 | +7.1% |
| output tok/s | 75,262 | 80,014 | +6.3% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 | 9.66 s / 32.1 s | 7.36 s / 27.6 s | -24% / -14% |
| TPOT p90 | 4.27 ms | 4.32 ms | +1.2% |
| successful / failed requests | 133,168 / 0 | 142,075 / 0 | |
| prefill step, mean over 12 prefill ranks | 444 ms | 414 ms | -6.8% |

Mooncake external linker on a build where this model had no read-done event and used the whole-forward barrier (before #45582 and #45682):

| | base | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| total tok/s per GPU | 253,684 | 276,154 | +8.9% |
| output tok/s | 83,002 | 89,126 | +7.4% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 | 4.40 s / 37.7 s | 1.76 s / 26.2 s | -60% / -31% |
| TPOT p90 | 4.24 ms | 4.32 ms | +1.9% |
| successful / failed requests | 148,855 / 0 | 160,474 / 0 | |
| prefill step, mean over 12 prefill ranks | 461 ms | 379 ms | -17.8% |

The same linker deployment with #45582, #45682 and #45559 applied, so the read-done barrier is active (~96% of barriers in both arms):

| | base | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| total tok/s per GPU | 285,548 | 282,860 | -0.9% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 | 1.34 s / 24.7 s | 1.35 s / 28.0 s | +0.5% / +13% |
| TPOT p90 | 4.34 ms | 4.30 ms | -0.9% |
| successful / failed requests | 165,490 / 0 | 163,963 / 0 | |
| prefill step, mean over 12 prefill ranks | 341.7 ms | 342.7 ms | +0.3% |

With read-done, the barrier already releases before the forward ends, so deferring it is neutral within single-run noise. The gain applies to every deployment that still uses the whole-forward barrier. GSM8K with read-done active and this PR: 0.969.

Nsight, linker build with the whole-forward barrier, one DEP2 prefill worker (both DP ranks), 15 consecutive steps:

| | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| GPU idle between prefill forwards (mean per step, DP0 / DP1) | 77 / 69 ms | 0.5 / 3.2 ms |
| GPU busy / step wall time | 0.82 | 0.93 |

With this PR, the remaining long host waits in the prefill loop fall inside `run_batch`, while the GPU is busy, instead of between forwards.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Stop the idle loop from starving async-save replies
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

With `--async-output-save`, single requests got slower and noisier instead of
staying flat. On 1xH200, Z-Image-Turbo went from 0.92 s to 1.00 s median (max
1.27 s) and Qwen-Image-2.1 from 4.45 s to 4.49–4.60 s (max 4.84 s), with almost
no throughput gain on Qwen-Image-2.1.

The finalize thread sends its reply on the ROUTER socket under `_socket_lock`.
While that finalize ran, the idle event loop waited with
`with self._socket_lock: self._poller.poll(timeout=1)` and took the lock straight
back in `recv_reqs()`. The loop held the lock almost all the time, and
`threading.Lock` is not fair (a semaphore on Linux / CPython 3.12): each release
wakes the finalize thread, but the loop re-acquires the lock a few microseconds
later, before the woken thread runs. The reply sat behind that loop for tens to
hundreds of milliseconds.

## Modifications

`Scheduler._wait_idle()` replaces both idle waits (in-flight finalize and the
dynamic-batching delay). With a finalize in flight it waits on the finalize
futures without the socket lock, for at most 1 ms, so new requests are still
picked up as before; with none in flight it polls the socket as before.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerical change: only the scheduler's idle wait changes.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

1xH200, `--model-type diffusion --warmup-mode server --performance-mode speed`,
1024x1024 PNG returned as b64_json. Each arm runs on a fresh server: two 3-step
warmups, then 10 sequential requests with distinct prompts, then 8 requests at
concurrency 2. Arms are interleaved and repeated twice; main is 49a2fbf817.

| case | arm | single median (s) | single max (s) | throughput (req/s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Z-Image-Turbo, 9 steps | main | 0.920 / 0.922 | 0.925 / 0.927 | 1.094 / 1.094 |
| | main + `--async-output-save` | 1.006 / 1.000 | 1.246 / 1.269 | 1.117 / 1.129 |
| | **this PR** + `--async-output-save` | **0.921 / 0.920** | **0.924 / 0.924** | **1.128 / 1.128** |
| Qwen-Image-2.1, 40 steps | main | 4.450 / 4.446 | 4.459 / 4.464 | 0.2261 / 0.2261 |
| | main + `--async-output-save` | 4.490 / 4.604 | 4.569 / 4.838 | 0.2268 / 0.2271 |
| | **this PR** + `--async-output-save` | **4.446 / 4.446** | **4.459 / 4.461** | **0.2279 / 0.2280** |

With this PR, single-request latency under `--async-output-save` matches the
synchronous path, and the flag now gives the throughput it was meant to: +3.1%
on Z-Image and +0.8% on Qwen-Image-2.1 at concurrency 2.

Instrumented run (Qwen-Image-2.1, temporary timestamps around the reply's
`send_multipart`; 10 single requests per arm): the time the finalize thread
waited for `_socket_lock` after finishing the save was 14–51 ms median and up
to 262 ms on main, and 0.00 ms for every request with this PR. The save itself
took ~92 ms on either path. At concurrency 2 the wait was already ~0 on main:
the loop is inside the next forward instead of idling on the lock.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit tests: `test_idle_wait_leaves_the_socket_lock_to_a_pending_reply`,
  `test_idle_wait_without_pending_finalize_polls_the_socket`
  (`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_async_output_save.py`).
- [x] Existing scheduler unit tests pass on 1xH200 (144 passed, 1 skipped).
- [x] The first new test fails 5/5 against the previous idle wait and passes with this PR.

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

During padded CUDA Graph replay, the variable-length KDA/GDN recurrent kernel leaves padded output rows uninitialized. Stale NaNs in these rows can propagate through downstream operations and corrupt valid-token outputs.

For example, replaying a batch-8 graph with seven active requests writes only seven output rows, leaving the last row unwritten. This fix makes the unused output tail deterministically zero.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Zero the output tail beyond `cu_seqlens[-1]` in the existing kernel, preserving valid-token outputs and recurrent state updates without an additional kernel launch.
- Extend the existing ragged kernel tests to replay the same CUDA Graph with different active-token counts for both KDA and GDN, checking zero padding, valid outputs, and recurrent state preservation.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Walk several row chunks per warp in the CuTe-DSL norm kernels
author: mickqian
body:
Branch: mick/diffusion-cutedsl-norm-chunked-warps (on main 1e894eb92d), commit 60d5f1e9ee

## Motivation

`fused_norm_scale_shift` and `fused_scale_residual_norm_scale_shift` (CuTe-DSL) launch one CTA of `D // 256` warps per row, each warp owning one 256-column chunk. At Wan's `D = 5120` that is a 640-thread CTA per row, so an SM holds only two or three rows at a time and every row waits out its loads, two block reductions and its scale/shift loads back to back. On Wan2.2 A14B 720p (`[1, 37800, 5120]` per rank on 4xB300) the three calls per block (norm1, the self-attention residual norm, the cross-attention residual norm) moved 0.77-1.55 GB each at 2.4-4.2 TB/s and took 1.16 ms of every 55 ms block inside the denoising loop, where the GPUs run at their power cap (~1300 MHz).

## Modifications

- `norm/cutedsl_common/norm_fusion.py`, `norm/cutedsl_common/reduce.py`: `tensor_slice_for_bsfd` slices one 256-column chunk of a row; `apply_norm_cta` becomes `row_norm_stats` (mean and 1/std of a row held as per-warp chunk lists) + `normalize_chunk`; `cta_reduce_sum` takes one partial sum per chunk.
- `norm/scale_residual_norm_cutedsl.py`: a warp walks `chunks_per_warp` consecutive chunks with the same lane mapping (8 consecutive elements per lane), keeps one partial sum per chunk and runs the same shuffle-down tree on each; the cross-chunk sum reads `acc[chunk]` in chunk order. The reduction order therefore depends on `D` only, so every output is bit-identical to one chunk per warp (the old kernel), whatever `chunks_per_warp` is. `_chunks_per_warp` picks about five warps per row, ten when the row also streams a gate and an affine weight (their registers cap occupancy); measured on B300 at `D = 5120`.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_norm.py::test_cutedsl_norm_chunks_per_warp_keep_bits`: 1, 2, 4 and 5 chunks per warp give the same bits (layer/RMS, with and without residual).
- Old vs new kernel, 36 cases (`D` 1536-5120, B 1-2, norm1 / RMS + affine / gated affine residual / gate 1 / 4-D frame gate / per-token scale): every output bitwise equal.
- Wan2.2 T2V A14B 720p, 4xB300, 3-step requests, lossless (crf 0) mp4: md5 identical to the base for 3 prompts.
- `test_norm.py -k cutedsl`: 150 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B300, `[1, 37800, 5120]` bf16, fp32 modulation; "capped" = each call between two 5120x5120 GEMMs at the power cap, median kernel time (matches the in-loop numbers):

| call | old isolated | new isolated | old capped | new capped |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| norm1 (LayerNorm, scale/shift) | 0.219 ms | 0.159 ms | 0.318 ms | 0.218 ms |
| self-attn residual (gate, fp32 affine) | 0.336 ms | 0.241 ms | 0.476 ms | 0.326 ms |
| cross-attn residual (scale/shift) | 0.267 ms | 0.235 ms | 0.370 ms | 0.278 ms |

Other shapes, GPU kernel time from the profiler (host issue time per call is unchanged, 36-46 us either way):

| B x S x D | call | old | new |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 x 4608 x 3072 | norm1 | 15.1 us | 13.6 us |
| 1 x 4608 x 3072 | gated affine residual | 27.7 us | 24.8 us |
| 2 x 1000 x 3072 | norm1 | 7.9 us | 7.7 us |
| 2 x 1000 x 3072 | gated affine residual | 11.1 us | 10.1 us |
| 1 x 4096 x 3840 | norm1 | 17.0 us | 13.2 us |
| 1 x 4096 x 3840 | gated affine residual | 36.1 us | 29.3 us |

E2E, Wan2.2 T2V A14B 720p (81 frames, 40 steps), 4xB300, harness single_e2e (fresh server per run, runs interleaved with the base): this PR together with #46228 ("Fuse Wan's q/k RMSNorm with its interleaved RoPE") took the request from 90.656 s (90.642 / 90.671) to 90.187 s (90.160 / 90.214), -0.47 s. The two changes were checked bitwise separately but timed together.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Fuse Wan's q/k RMSNorm with its interleaved RoPE
author: mickqian
body:
Branch: mick/wan-fused-qk-norm-rope (on main 1e894eb92d), commit 75cc4e726b

## Motivation

Wan normalizes q and k across all heads (`qk_norm="rms_norm_across_heads"`) with FlashInfer's RMSNorm and then rotates them with FlashInfer's interleaved cos/sin-cache RoPE: three full passes over q and k in every block. On Wan2.2 A14B 720p (4xB300, 37800 x 5120 tokens per rank) they take 0.54 ms of each 55 ms block inside the denoising loop (RMSNorm 0.144 ms x 2, RoPE 0.255 ms, at the power-capped clock).

## Modifications

- `kernels/ops/diffusion/rope/rmsnorm_interleaved_rope_cutedsl.py`: `fused_rmsnorm_interleaved_rope_(x, weight, cos_sin_cache, eps, head_dim)`, in place on `x [M, H]` (row stride free). The norm part is FlashInfer's CuTe-DSL `RMSNormKernel` (single-CTA rows, same tiling, `row_reduce_sum_multirow`, fastmath rsqrt), so its bf16 output matches `flashinfer.norm.rmsnorm`; the store then rotates each (even, odd) pair of that bf16 output in fp32 with the RoPE kernel's expression (`a*c + (-b)*s`, `b*c + a*s`, row `m` at position `m % len(cache)`). Each thread's 8-column runs sit one head-multiple apart, so one 4-pair cos/sin slice (two 16-byte loads) serves all of them. `can_use_fused_rmsnorm_interleaved_rope` states the supported inputs; the kernel runs on torch's current stream.
- `models/dits/wanvideo.py`: `WanTransformerBlock._qkv_rope` projects q/k/v and, when the q/k norm runs FlashInfer's kernel (`forward_cuda`, no TP across heads) and the transformer supplies its cos/sin cache, applies the fused pass to q and k and tells `forward` to skip the RoPE. `_qkv` (used by Wan-Animate) keeps its behaviour.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_rmsnorm_interleaved_rope.py`:
  - bitwise equal to `flashinfer.norm.rmsnorm` + `apply_flashinfer_rope_qk_inplace` (5120 / 3072 hidden, batch 1-2, rows padded apart as in a fused projection);
  - inputs produced on a side stream right before the call (it must run on torch's current stream);
  - a full Wan block (5120, 40 heads) gives the same bits with the fusion on and off;
  - unsupported inputs are rejected.
- Wan2.2 T2V A14B 720p, 4xB300, 3-step requests, lossless (crf 0) mp4: md5 identical to the base for 3 prompts.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B300, q and k `[37800, 5120]` bf16, each call between 5120x5120 GEMMs at the power cap (median):

| | RMSNorm q | RMSNorm k | RoPE q+k | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 0.144 ms | 0.144 ms | 0.255 ms | 0.542 ms |
| fused | 0.171 ms | 0.171 ms | - | 0.342 ms |

E2E, Wan2.2 T2V A14B 720p (81 frames, 40 steps), 4xB300, harness single_e2e (fresh server per run, runs interleaved with the base): this PR together with #46227 ("Walk several row chunks per warp in the CuTe-DSL norm kernels") took the request from 90.656 s (90.642 / 90.671) to 90.187 s (90.160 / 90.214), -0.47 s. The two changes were checked bitwise separately but timed together.

title: [Perf] dsv41: Translate SWA locations once per prefill graph step
author: hnyls2002
body:
Two per-step costs in the DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill CUDA graph, removed without changing any output bit.

- **SWA locations**: with no request window or SWA ring, every full-attention layer's KV store translated `out_cache_loc` to SWA locations again (an index gather and an int32 cast per layer). The prefill graph's metadata prep now translates it once into `core_attn_metadata.swa_out_cache_loc`, and replay refreshes that captured buffer in place, so every layer store reads the cached locations.
- **Tail bridge**: `DecoderReplayTail._bridge_outputs` no longer zero-fills the bridge rows past the tail. The graph's row-wise readers carry those rows only into rows that `_scatter_tail_rows` and the `real_rows_count` cut drop.

## Verification

- The breakable-CUDA-graph metadata contract test now checks that replay refreshes the captured SWA location buffer by address with the replayed batch's translated locations.
- Existing DSv4 backend and late-layer tail reader unit tests pass.

title: [Perf] dsv41: Use the fused ratio-2 compressor in the prefill graph
author: hnyls2002
body:
Inside the DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill CUDA graph, the ratio-2 compressor ran its torch path (dozens of small launches per source layer, plus a separate index-K store), because the fused compressor reads per-request extend offsets that were not graph-static. Eager extend already uses the fused kernel.

- The prefill graph's metadata carries `low_ratio_extend_offsets`, an int32 `[2, request slots]` tensor of each request's first row and row count, refreshed in place at replay. Slots past the batch hold no rows, and DP padding rows belong to no request.
- When the compressor uses the fused gate, the captured source projection writes `| kv | score |` rows into one buffer, and `_low_ratio_compress_fused` takes that projection (`projected=`) with the static offsets.
- Compressors without the fused gate keep the torch path and its separate `kv` and `score` buffers, unchanged.

## Verification

- Existing DSv4 backend unit tests pass.

title: [Perf] dsv41: Feed wo_b the fused MXFP8 attention output in the prefill graph
author: hnyls2002
body:
Inside the DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill CUDA graph, the mega attention wrote a bf16 output through its eager break and `wo_b` quantized it to MXFP8 in a separate kernel. Outside the graph (eager prefill, decode), the attention already hands `wo_b` its fused MXFP8 output.

- `bcg_deepseek_v4_mega_attention_with_mxfp8_output`: the eager break writes the fp8 data and DeepGEMM-packed UE8M0 scales into buffers allocated in the graph; rows past the live tokens are zeroed. When the TMA-aligned scale stride of the live rows differs from the padded rows', the scales are written to a live-size buffer and copied back.
- `_mega_core` accepts an `(fp8, scale)` pair as `out`; `MQALayer._mega_mxfp8_output` is the one condition for both paths.
- `deepseek_v4_mhc.empty_deepgemm_mxfp8_scales` is split out of `empty_deepgemm_mxfp8_pair`.

The prefill graph now quantizes from the attention's fp32 accumulator, as the eager path does, instead of from its bf16 output, so its numerics follow eager prefill.

title: [Fix] [AMD] dsv4.1: Fix the V4.1 k-norm-rope store build on ROCm 10
author: kevin-mii
body:
## Motivation

sgl-project/sglang#45934 added a warp-per-token V4.1 kernel to `main_norm_rope.cuh` whose two reductions shuffle with `__shfl_xor_sync(0xffffffffu, ...)`. ROCm 10's HIP headers `static_assert` a 64-bit mask (wave64), so the V4.1 fused k-norm-rope store (`fused_k_norm_rope_flashmla`, V41 layout) no longer builds on gfx950.

Every PR's `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` shard 1 has failed on `test_v41_kv_store.py` since then, for example [on sgl-project/sglang#46151](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40030122510/job/120684541903). #45934's own AMD run was cancelled before that stage ran.

```
main_norm_rope.cuh:513:18: note: in instantiation of function template specialization '__shfl_xor_sync<unsigned int, float>' requested here
amd_warp_sync_functions.h:307:62: error: static assertion failed due to requirement 'sizeof(unsigned int) == 8': The mask must be a 64-bit integer.
RuntimeError: Failed to build JIT module sgl_kernel_jit_dpsk_v4_main_k_norm_rope_flashmla_bf16_t_512_64_256_V41_false
```

A 64-bit full mask builds but is wrong:
- HIP's `__shfl_xor_sync` traps unless every lane its mask names is active.
- This kernel returns per 32-lane warp, so an odd token count leaves half of the last wave64 idle.
- With that mask, 2049, 4097 and 4099 tokens crash with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION`.

## Modifications

- The two reductions call `shfl_xor_in_warp`, a forced-inline helper.
  - On CUDA it is main's `__shfl_xor_sync(0xffffffffu, v, mask)`, so CUDA compiles the same code as main.
  - On HIP it is the mask-free `__shfl_xor`, as `warp::reduce` already uses on HIP.
  - The loops and the reduction tree are unchanged. `kWarpThreads` is 32 on HIP too, so each 32-lane half of a wave64 holds one token, and every xor mask (2, 1, 16, 8, 4) stays inside it.
- `test_v41_kv_store.py`'s warp-per-token case takes 4097 tokens instead of 4096, so the last wave64 runs half idle.

## Accuracy Tests

MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 10.0.0, this branch on main 3c6a6c80:

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/test_v41_kv_store.py`: 8 passed.
  - On main it fails to build with the error above.
  - With a 64-bit full mask instead, its 4097-token case traps.
- The fused k-norm-rope store check at 2049, 4097, 4099 and 4100 tokens: bitwise equal to the unfused kernel chain.
- The other AMD-registered tests that build `main_norm_rope.cuh`:
  - `test_hip_flash_mla_aiter_sparse.py`: 7 passed;
  - `test_swapab_attention.py`: 5 passed, 2 skipped;
  - `test_dsv4_q_rope_store.py`: 4 passed;
  - `test_minimax_m3_qk_norm_rope.py`: 24 passed.

Not executed:
- CUDA: no CUDA toolchain here. Instead, expanding the helper's CUDA branch at its two call sites and dropping the helper reproduces main's `main_norm_rope.cuh` byte for byte.
- pre-commit: its hooks are not cached on this box. Every changed line is under the 120-column clang-format limit.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed change intended: CUDA compiles main's code, and HIP runs the same shuffles without the per-shuffle mask check. Not measured.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Perf] diffusion: Split LTX tiled VAE decode across the decode-parallel ranks
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

On a multi-GPU LTX server every decode-parallel rank runs the VAE decode, so that the spatial-parallel convolutions can exchange halo rows. `_decode_spatial` only takes that height split when each rank's rows fit in one tile. Otherwise it falls back to `tiled_decode` with the split disabled, and every rank then decodes every tile of the whole frame. On two GPUs both ranks do the same work, and the second GPU adds nothing.

Tiling is on by default (`vae_tiling`), with 512 x 512 tiles, so the fallback is taken whenever one rank's share of the frame is larger than one tile. LTX-2.5's two-stage recipe decodes 1920x1088 (a 34 x 60 latent, 15 tiles): each of two ranks would get 17 x 60 latent rows against a 16 x 16 tile, and both decoded all 15 tiles. LTX-2 and LTX-2.3 hit the same fallback at 1024x1536.

## Modifications

- `models/vaes/ltx_2_vae.py`: `tiled_decode` decodes tiles `r, r + W, ...` on decode-parallel rank `r` of `W`. `_gather_tiles` pads each rank's tiles to the largest tile, all-gathers them over the decode-parallel group in one call, and puts them back in tile order before the blend. Each tile is decoded on its own, so the gathered set is the set a single rank decodes. The split applies when spatial-parallel decode is installed (every decode-parallel rank then runs the decode) and there are at least as many tiles as ranks. Otherwise the decode is unchanged.

Tests:
- `test_vae_spatial_parallel_decode.py`, `test_ltx_tile_shards_gather_back_in_tile_order`: 3 x 5 tiles with a partial last row and column, round-robin over two ranks. The gather returns every tile in order, with its own shape and values.
- `test_ltx_vae_parallel_decode.py` (two ranks over gloo): the `tiled_shard` case now runs the split and still matches the single-rank tiled decode.

## Accuracy Tests

4xB300, LTX-2.5 two-stage (`Lightricks/LTX-2.5-Diffusers`, 1920x1088, 121 frames), `--num-gpus 2 --ulysses-degree 2`, same prompts and seeds. The output MP4s are byte-identical to main for all four requests (md5 `47eb2a29...`, `cfa61144...`, `8f0094d4...`, `3cbba017...`).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same setup, synchronized stage timers (`SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1`):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `LTX2AVDecodingStage` | 2.88 s | 2.10-2.13 s |
| request (client, 3 requests after warmup) | 7.07-8.05 s | 6.31-6.37 s |

Per rank, the decode stage's GPU kernel time went from 1732 ms to 933 ms (torch.profiler, rank 0).

title: [Perf] diffusion: Validate breakable CUDA graphs for LTX-2.5 two-stage serving
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

LTX-2.5's default (distilled) path is unguided, so its stage-1 forward over 8,160 video tokens per step is short and launch-bound. On 4xB300 at 1920x1088 with Ulysses 2, a stage-1 step took 0.244 s of wall time against ~0.15 s of GPU kernel time (torch.profiler, ~8,000 kernels per step). Breakable CUDA graphs remove that host time. `LTX2TwoStagePipeline` already turns them on by default for LTX-2 and LTX-2.3 (#45977), but LTX-2.5 was not on the validated list, so it ran eager unless `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph true` was passed, and then with a "not validated" warning.

## Modifications

- `server_args.py`: `Lightricks/LTX-2.5-Diffusers` joins `BREAKABLE_CUDA_GRAPH_SUPPORTED_MODEL_IDS`. The existing default gates are unchanged: `LTX2TwoStagePipeline`, server warmup, >= 130 GiB cards, resident DiTs, no compile, LoRA, batching or offload.

- `docs/cookbook/diffusion/LTX/LTX2.5.mdx`: the default and the warmup flags for the served shape.

Tests:
- `test_server_args.py`, `test_ltx25_distilled_two_stage_serving_turns_bcg_on` (with the existing `TestBreakableCudaGraphDefault` cases: 6 passed).

## Accuracy Tests

4xB300, LTX-2.5 two-stage at 1920x1088, 121 frames, `--num-gpus 2 --ulysses-degree 2 --warmup-resolutions 1920x1088 --warmup-num-frames 121`. Warmup captures 289 segments per stage shape, and the four requests' MP4s are byte-identical to eager (same md5 for every prompt and seed).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same setup, synchronized stage timers:

| | eager | BCG |
|---|---|---|
| stage 1 (8 steps) | 1.95 s (0.244 s/step) | 1.26 s (0.151 s/step) |
| stage 2 step | 0.674 s | 0.630 s |
| request (client) | 7.07-8.05 s | 6.39-6.51 s |

As for LTX-2/2.3, graphs are captured per shape at warmup, so serving another shape needs `--warmup-resolutions` / `--warmup-num-frames` for it; the LTX-2.5 cookbook now says so.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Blend VAE tile seams in one pass
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

`ParallelTiledVAE.blend_v` / `blend_h` / `blend_t` cross-fade two tiles one row (or column, or frame) at a time in a Python loop. With 512-pixel tiles on a 448 stride, each seam is 64 iterations of a slice multiply, a second multiply, an add and a copy. LTX-2.5's 1920x1088 decode has 22 seams, so the blend alone is ~5,600 small launches per rank, all host time (the GPU work is ~10 ms).

## Modifications

- `models/vaes/common.py`: the three blends call one `_blend(a, b, extent, dim)` that writes the whole seam at once. It reproduces the loop bit for bit: the loop multiplied by the Python floats `1 - i / extent` and `i / extent`, which run in the op-math dtype, so the weights are the same doubles (computed in float64 on the device) rounded to fp32 (fp64 for fp64 tensors). Each product is rounded to the tile's dtype before the add, as the loop's tensor-times-scalar ops were.

Tests:
- `test_vae_tiled_decode_groups.py::test_blend_matches_per_slice_loop`: bf16, fp16 and fp32, the three blend dims, extents 1, 7, 64 and 100 (clipped to the tile): `torch.equal` against the per-slice loop on CUDA (36 cases).

## Accuracy Tests

The output is bitwise unchanged (unit test above; on 4xB300 the LTX-2.5 MP4s keep their md5).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

4xB300, LTX-2.5 two-stage 1920x1088 x 121 frames, 2 GPUs, on top of "Split LTX tiled VAE decode across the decode-parallel ranks" and breakable CUDA graphs, synchronized stage timers, five requests after warmup each:

| | without | with |
|---|---|---|
| `LTX2AVDecodingStage` | 1.753 s | 1.705 s |
| request (client) | 5.261-5.308 s | 5.219-5.281 s |

The five MP4s are byte-identical between the two builds.

title: [Perf] diffusion/loader: Avoid temporary GPU tensors when loading encoders
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Native text encoders allocate their final parameters before loading the checkpoint. For GPU-resident encoders, the checkpoint reader currently materializes each source tensor on the GPU as well, then the weight loader copies it into the existing parameter. This adds an unnecessary GPU allocation/copy and can transfer the full source-dtype tensor before casting or TP slicing.

## Modifications

- Read native encoder checkpoint tensors on the CPU and let the existing per-parameter loaders copy/cast/shard them into their final destinations. Safetensors stays memory-mapped instead of building a second GPU weight tensor.
- Keep the destination device, offload policy, quantization postprocessing, and customized `_get_all_weights(..., to_cpu)` interface unchanged. GGUF and Transformers fallback loading are unchanged.
- Add a small real T5 safetensors loading regression to the existing loader test file, checking both CPU/offloaded and GPU/resident parameters, exact FP32-to-BF16 values, and fused QKV weights.

Production diff: **+2/-1 lines** in one existing file. Tests: **+46 lines** in one existing file. No new configuration, helper, or production module.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on an isolated 2x H200 development machine, baseline `3c6a6c806865` versus final head `6a1e42bd117b`:

- New regression fails on the baseline GPU-resident path and passes with this change.
- Relevant loader, parallel linear, Qwen3, H3, Ming, image encoder, folding, Ideogram and reader suites: **224 passed, 3 skipped**, plus 18 passing subtests. The three NVFP4 hardware tests require Blackwell and were skipped on Hopper.
- Real two-GPU SRT CLIP folding test: **passed**, including forward-output parity against single-rank loading.
- Real HTTP generation: Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B, single GPU and Ulysses2; Z-Image-Turbo, single GPU. Within each configuration, baseline and modified decoded pixels are **bit-identical**. This is not a claim of single-GPU versus multi-GPU equivalence.
- Pre-commit passes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

H200, driver 595.71.05, Python 3.12.15, Torch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0, Diffusers 0.37.0, safetensors 0.8.0. Cached checkpoints, offline HF access, fresh server processes, `--warmup-mode off`, otherwise default deployment policy. Time is process launch to successful `/health`, polled every 50 ms. First downloads and JIT priming are excluded.

Three alternating baseline/modified pairs per single-GPU model, all on the final code:

| Model | Baseline startup median | PR startup median | Reduction | Loading peak allocated, MiB | Loading peak reserved, MiB |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B | 31.573 s | 29.845 s | 5.5% | 25740.95 -> 24983.28 | 26126 -> 25132 |
| Z-Image-Turbo | 30.853 s | 30.213 s | 2.1% | 20217.47 -> 19644.10 | 20546 -> 19812 |

Raw startup seconds, baseline / PR:

- Wan: `[31.573, 31.717, 31.372]` / `[29.845, 30.007, 29.749]`.
- Z-Image: `[32.377, 30.853, 30.646]` / `[30.213, 30.549, 30.131]`.

The Ulysses2 validation also reduces loading peak allocated from 14906.86 to 13865.42 MiB, and reserved from 15292 to 14010 MiB. These are PyTorch allocator peaks, max across replica ranks, not total device memory or steady-state inference gains. Z-Image startup peak host anonymous memory was effectively unchanged (~18250 MiB), sampled across the process tree every 100 ms. No general host-memory claim is made for legacy `.pt` checkpoints or other models.

After every launch, validate a real request with prompt `A small sailboat on a calm blue lake in daylight.`, seed 42, quality `exact`, 4 steps: Wan 512x320 / 17 frames / 8 fps; Z-Image 512x512. Download/decode the output and compare pixel SHA256. Each server is stopped and checked for surviving children before the next launch.

This is a small loading optimization, not a new direct-storage backend. The Z-Image gain is modest; these measurements do not establish a universal startup speedup across hardware or checkpoints. No public API or command changes, so no documentation update is needed.

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit / formatting
- [x] Focused regression and real GPU validation
- [x] Accuracy and startup-memory measurements
- [x] Documentation considered; no user-facing interface change

title: [Perf] diffusion: Write Wan's normed q/k straight into the Ulysses exchange
author: mickqian
body:
Stacked on #46246 (text K/V once per loop), which sits on #46245, #46244 and #46228 (the fused q/k norm-RoPE this PR extends). Also depends on #46145 (pipelined Ulysses same-device copies), carried here as cherry-picks of its two commits; review the commits after #46246 other than those.

## Motivation

Under pipelined Ulysses (Wan2.2 A14B 720p, 4xB300, CFG 2 x Ulysses 2) every block normed and rotated q and k in place, and the exchange then copied this rank's own rows of every head group into its receive slots: one same-device copy per tensor (`_copy_head_groups_kernel`, ~0.073 ms each, 0.27 ms per block for q, k, v and the output gather), on the critical path before the first head group attends. The existing `fill` hook lets a per-head QK-norm write each block itself, but Wan normalizes across all heads, so a block-at-a-time fill would reread whole rows once per block.

## Modifications

- `distributed/device_communicators/ipc_a2a_multi.py`: `pipelined_attention(..., fill_all=None)`: `fill` given every destination block at once, `[(head_start, head_count, q_dst, k_dst)]` over this rank's own slot rows and each peer's send block; the rest of the fill path (v's own rows copied, the peers' q/k blocks sent from the send buffers) is shared with `fill`.
- `layers/attention/layer.py`: `USPAttention.forward_qk_filled(q, k, v, fill_all)` runs the dense pipelined path with that hook (no first-sight reference: the pipelined backends attend a head group exactly as inside the full call) and returns None, having written nothing, whenever the call would not pipeline.
- `kernels/ops/diffusion/rope/rmsnorm_interleaved_rope_cutedsl.py`: `fused_rmsnorm_interleaved_rope_into_blocks(x, ..., dst_table)`: the same kernel, but each thread's 512-column run goes to row m of the contiguous block at `dst_table[run]` instead of back into `x`.
- `models/dits/wanvideo.py`: the block projects q/k/v, then `_attend_qk_filled` writes q and k into the exchange blocks through the address table (built once per set of exchange buffers) and attends; when that returns None (no Ulysses pipeline, capture, compile, offline q/k rotation, another attention op) the block runs its previous path on the untouched projections.

Same kernels on the same values, so outputs are bit-identical.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_rmsnorm_interleaved_rope.py::test_into_blocks_matches_in_place`: every run lands in its block with the in-place result's bits, from a strided (fused-qkv) input, which stays untouched.
- `test_usp_pipelined_attention_multi_gpu.py` (2 and 4 ranks) passes on the branch.
- Wan2.2 T2V A14B 720p, 4xB300, 3-step lossless (crf 0) mp4: md5 identical to the base for 3 prompts; a profile shows one copy (v) instead of three before the first head group.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Wan2.2 T2V A14B 720p, 4xB300, harness single_e2e, fresh server per run, interleaved in one round with TRT-LLM: base (#46246) 89.616 / 89.691 s -> 89.454 / 89.482 / 89.488 s (mean 89.475), -0.19%. After the memory-lifetime fixes in #46244 and #46246, the full stack measured 89.517 / 89.540 s against 89.556 s for this commit's stack in the same session: no regression.

title: [Perf] sgl-router: Encode tiktoken models with fastokens under --tokenizer-backend fast
author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Motivation

`--tokenizer-backend fast` only applied to a `tokenizer.json`. A `tiktoken.model` (Kimi-K3) silently stayed on tiktoken-rs, which runs at about the speed of Python tiktoken: 8 to 9 MB/s per core, so a 128k-char K3 prompt costs about 15 ms of router CPU on the TTFT path. dynamo-tokenizers 3.1.0 already ships `FastTikTokenTokenizer`, which loads the same ranks, BPE pattern and special tokens from the same `tiktoken.model`, `config.json` and `tokenizer_config.json`.

fastokens encodes exactly one input differently from the engine: U+017F (long s) directly after an apostrophe. tiktoken's `(?i:'s)` case-folds `'ſ` into the contraction and keeps ` I'ſ` as one pretoken; the fastokens scanner ends the word before the apostrophe. A sweep of every BMP codepoint through nine apostrophe and contraction contexts (571,104 inputs) against tiktoken-rs and Moonshot's `tokenization_kimi.py` found no other divergence, and the 135-case corpus below (chat, code, tool JSON, Chinese, 32k to 512k-char prompts, 60k-char base64 runs crossing the 25k split, markers typed by users) matched id for id.

## Modifications

- `adapter.rs`: for a non-json tokenizer path under `fast`, build `FastTikTokenTokenizer` and keep the tiktoken-rs tokenizer. A small wrapper routes any input whose bytes contain `C5 BF` (U+017F) to tiktoken-rs and everything else to fastokens, for both plain and segmented encodes. Load failure falls back to tiktoken-rs with a warning, as the json path does with HF.
- `stats.rs`: new `fast_tiktoken` encode backend label for the startup log.
- `REFERENCE.md`: document the tiktoken case for `--tokenizer-backend fast` and mention it in the Kimi-K3 section.
- `tests/component/tokenizer/kimi.rs`: the Kimi parity fixtures now run under both `hf` and `fast`. A second test builds a vocabulary with a merge across an apostrophe and checks that the `fast` backend matches tiktoken-rs on `'ſ` while bare fastokens does not, so the fallback can be dropped once fastokens folds the contraction.

The L1 prefix cache is unaffected: it is never built for a `.model` path (no boundary tokens are read from it), and Kimi-K3 encodes per segment anyway.

## Accuracy Tests

`cargo test -p sgl-router kimi` and `cargo test -p sgl-router --lib tokenizer::` pass; clippy with `-D warnings` is clean. On the real `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` vocabulary (revision f831ab66), the guarded fast backend produced 0 id mismatches against tiktoken-rs and the Python reference on the 135-case corpus and on the 571,104-input codepoint sweep.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Measured on an m7i.8xlarge (Xeon 8488C), Kimi-K3 vocabulary, each stack in its own process. Per-request latency pinned to one core, first encode of each input (cold caches):

| input | tiktoken-rs (before) | fast (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| short chat, ~190 chars | 35 us | ~4 us |
| medium chat, ~2k chars | 315 us | ~26 us |
| Python file, ~20k chars | 2.42 ms | ~150 us |
| 128k-char prompt | 15.4 ms | ~0.9 ms |
| 512k-char prompt | 61 ms | ~2.6 ms |

Aggregate encode throughput, all cores busy: 134 Mchars/s before, 2742 Mchars/s after (32 threads); 7.9 vs 185 Mchars/s on one core. Steady-state RSS after traffic: 69 MB before, about 340 MB after, of which the retained tiktoken-rs fallback is about 30 MB. Load time 60 ms before, about 0.8 s after.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] deepseek-v4.1: Default aggregated servers to MegaAttention only when each rank holds 64 query heads
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

Since #43922, `--dsv4-attn-backend auto` resolves to `flashmla_mega` for DeepSeek-V4.1 on SM100/SM103 with an `fp8_e4m3` KV cache, whatever the attention TP width. MegaAttention always runs a 64-head tile (`kernel_num_heads = 64 if n_local_heads <= 64 else 128`), and `pack_query` zero-fills the missing heads. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has 64 query heads, so TP2 (32 heads per rank) runs 2x and TP4 (16 heads per rank) runs 4x the attention work it needs. The `flashmla` path has a small-batch SM100 kernel specialized for 16 and 32 heads (`can_use_swapab_attention`), so it wins at these widths.

At TP4 the target-verify graph of one decode step gains the MegaAttention kernel (~1.45 ms over 40 layers) and the fp8 `wo_a` GEMM it feeds (~0.29 ms). It drops the FlashMLA partial/combine, fused `wo_a`, Q-norm-RoPE and quant kernels (~0.85 ms), so each step is ~1.1 ms slower.

## Modifications

- For an aggregated server (`--disaggregation-mode null`), `_default_dsv4_attention_backend` returns `flashmla` when attention is tensor-parallel across ranks (`attn_tp_size > 1`). This mirrors `_kernel_num_heads`, which pads to the 64-head tile exactly when `attn_tp_size > 1`.
  - TP1, DP attention at attention TP 1 and prefill CP are not sharded, so they still resolve to `flashmla_mega`.
  - Prefill CP counts as attention TP 1 directly, because `validate_deepseek_v4_cp` sets `attn_cp_size` only after this default runs.
  - An explicit `--dsv4-attn-backend` is unchanged.
- PD roles keep today's default (#45075): `flashmla_mega` on both prefill and decode, whatever their attention TP size.
  - The two backends do not store the same KV layout. `SGLANG_DSV4_KV_LAYOUT` defaults to `v4`, so `flashmla` stores V4, while `flashmla_mega` forces V4.1.
  - Gating PD roles by head count would let a TP prefill and a DP-attention decode resolve differently. They would then fail the KV-layout handshake: on GB300 such a pair failed its first request with `KV layout mismatch: prefill server has kv_layout=v4,c1:v4,c2:v4, but decode server has kv_layout=v41,c1:v41_fp4,c2:v41_fp4`.
- The `--dsv4-attn-backend` help text describes the new default. The cookbook PD note now says both roles run MegaAttention whatever their attention TP size; it previously said "as a single server does".

## Accuracy Tests

The change selects an existing backend; no kernel or model code changes. Paired runs:
- Aggregated TP4 EP1 server, same image as below, DSpark with real acceptance.
- `sgl-eval` 0.1.3, GSM8K, all 1319 examples, `--load-preset-from-model-id deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, thinking, reasoning effort high), 128 threads.
- The two servers differ only in the attention backend.

| backend | GSM8K 1319 | errors / truncated | mean output tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auto` with this PR (resolves to `flashmla`) | **96.82%** | 0 / 0 | 266.7 |
| explicit `flashmla_mega` (main's `auto` here) | 96.59% | 0 / 0 | 270.5 |

The 0.23-point gap is 3 of 1319 questions, inside one standard error (about 0.5 points at this score).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash FP4 on GB300, `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261021-c1c287a4`. Aggregated serving behind the Dynamo frontend, DSpark (MTP), agentic multi-turn coding trace replay, full warmup, then a 60-minute measurement window. One server per row, with the same recipe except `--dsv4-attn-backend`. `auto` resolved to `flashmla_mega` on this image.

| Point | Backend | Requests / errors | Total tok/s/GPU | Interactivity P50 / P90 (tok/s/user) | TTFT P90 | Clean decode step, 1 / 4 running |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP4, conc 4 | `auto` (mega) | 751 / 0 | 9,881 | 537.6 / 465.8 | 0.288 s | 6.41 ms / - |
| TP4, conc 4 | `flashmla` | 741 / 0 | 9,736 | **683.7 / 590.8** | 0.254 s | **5.05 / 6.72 ms** |
| TP4, conc 16 | `auto` (mega) | 2671 / 0 | 29,051 | 473.8 / 403.7 | 1.888 s | 6.40 / 7.85 ms |
| TP4, conc 16 | `flashmla` | 2714 / 0 | 29,371 | **593.2 / 468.6** | 1.401 s | **5.06 / 6.84 ms** |
| TP2 EP2, conc 16 | `auto` (mega) | 2662 / 0 | 57,766 | 376.2 / 309.0 | 1.310 s | 7.19 / 9.67 ms |
| TP2 EP2, conc 16 | `flashmla` | 2675 / 0 | 57,999 | **414.8 / 315.4** | 1.176 s | **6.07 / 9.22 ms** |

The decode step is taken from scheduler log intervals with no prefill batch: `running x accept length / generation throughput`. P90 interactivity rises 27% (TP4 c4), 16% (TP4 c16) and 2% (TP2 c16, P50 +10%), at matching throughput.

Resolution checked with `ServerArgs.resolve_once` on a GB300 node, the image above with this change's two files in place:

| Arguments | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `--tp 4` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla` |
| `--tp 2 --ep 2` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla` |
| `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 2` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla` |
| `--tp 1` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla_mega` |
| `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla_mega` |
| `--tp 4 --dp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla_mega` |
| `--tp 4 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla_mega` |
| `--tp 4 --dsv4-attn-backend flashmla_mega` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla_mega` |
| PD prefill: `--tp 4`, `--tp 2`, `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4 --ep 4`, `--tp 2 --attn-dp-size 2 --ep 2` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla_mega` |
| PD decode: `--tp 4`, `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4 --ep 4`, legacy `--dp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention --ep 4` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla_mega` |

Larger batches, same setup. TP2 c32 uses `--max-running-requests 64`. TP4 c64 uses `--max-running-requests 256` and `--prefill-decode-interval 24`. With DSpark block size 5, every bucket of 9 or more running requests is above the swap-AB row cap, so `flashmla` pads to 64 heads there too:

| Point | Backend | Requests / errors | Total tok/s/GPU | Interactivity P50 / P90 | TTFT P90 | Clean decode step by running requests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP2 EP2, conc 32 | `auto` (mega) | 4792 / 0 | 120,870 | 282.4 / 220.5 | 1.978 s | 1-8: 9.06 ms, 9-16: 12.82 ms |
| TP2 EP2, conc 32 | `flashmla` | 4817 / 0 | 122,250 | **291.5 / 227.4** | 1.780 s | 1-8: **8.31** ms, 9-16: **12.46** ms |
| TP4, conc 64 | `auto` (mega) | 11501 / 0 | 116,866 | 210.9 / 176.0 | 2.000 s | 1-16: 9.38 ms, 17-32: 12.13 ms |
| TP4, conc 64 | `flashmla` | 11604 / 0 | 118,577 | **220.9 / 184.8** | 1.754 s | 1-16: **8.40** ms, 17-32: **11.57** ms |

The TP4 margin narrows as the batch grows: -10% at 1-16 running, -5% at 17-32, and -4% at 33-48 (steps with prefill, 23.44 vs 22.58 ms).

Fixed batches at TP4 EP1, to cover the high-throughput regime the trace does not reach:
- `bench_serving --dataset-name random-ids`, 4096 input / 1024 output tokens, C requests sent at once, two rounds per C.
- DSpark, simulated acceptance 3.51, `--max-running-requests 256`, `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 256`.
- Clean decode step from scheduler log intervals at that running count:

| running requests | `flashmla` | `flashmla_mega` | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 57-64 | **17.50 ms** | 18.25 ms | -4.1% |
| 121-128 | **26.48 ms** | 26.98 ms | -1.9% |
| 241-256 | **42.64 ms** | 43.58 ms | -2.2% |

`flashmla` decodes faster at every batch size up to 256. MegaAttention prefills slightly faster (median TTFT at C=128: 4.54 s vs 5.22 s), which leaves end-to-end bench throughput within 1.7% at C=128/256.

Side effects on aggregated TP2/TP4 servers:
- **KV layout:** they now store the V4 KV layout instead of V4.1. The swap-AB kernel reads V4. The KV pool at `--mem-fraction-static 0.8` was 66.86M vs 67.19M tokens (-0.5%) in the fixed-batch runs.
- **Shared HiCache stores:** a HiCache storage backend shared with a V4.1-layout server (a DEP server or a PD role on `auto`) would see a different layout. The store key does not include the layout.

Not measured:
- `--enable-cp-decode-attn-tp` (opt-in), which splits heads across CP ranks at decode. It still resolves to `flashmla_mega`, as on main.

The GB300 TP2 CI suites with `--attn-dp-size 1` now run `flashmla` instead of padded `flashmla_mega`.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Wan-Animate-2 decode clamp, LTX-2 Bongmath closed form, rollout log-prob/CPU-copy, validators NaN gate, in-place decode normalize
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
Six independent, small fixes found while reviewing the diffusion denoising/rollout/decode path. Each is its own commit; no commit depends on another.

## 1. `[Fix]` Wan-Animate-2: clamp decoded frames before uint8 cast
`WanAnimate2DenoisingStage`'s per-clip decode calls `clip_decoder.decode_raw(...)`, which does not clamp its fp32 output to `[-1, 1]`. The frame-to-uint8 conversion then did `((decoded_frames + 1) * 127.5).to(torch.uint8)` with no clamp: a value a little outside `[-1, 1]` (e.g. `-1.02`) pushes the scaled value outside `[0, 255]`, and the cast wraps around instead of saturating, producing a bright/dark speckle instead of a clean pixel. Fix: extract the conversion into a named helper and add `.clamp(-1, 1)` before scaling, matching the existing pattern in `decoding.py`'s `_to_unit_range`.

Test: `test_clip_decoded_frames_past_unit_range_saturate_instead_of_wrapping` — values straddling the boundary, asserts saturation instead of wraparound. Fails on the pre-fix formula, passes post-fix.

## 2. `[Perf]` LTX-2: replace Bongmath's 100-iteration fp64 loop with a closed form
The Bongmath anchor-refinement loop (`anchor = x_mid - h*a21*eps1; eps1 = denoised - anchor`, run 100 times, both video and audio, at two call sites) is an affine contraction in `eps1` with ratio `c = h*a21` (`|c| <= 0.22` in practice), so it converges to a fixed point `eps1* = (denoised - x_mid) / (1 - c)`. Solving directly replaces ~800 full-size fp64 kernel launches per step with a handful of elementwise ops.

Verified: closed form matches the 100-iteration loop to ~1e-16 relative error across the full valid `h` range, independent of the loop's starting point (tested numerically with real torch/einops, not just by inspection).

## 3. `[Perf]` rollout_hooks: skip the CPU copy init discards
`init_rollout_env_if_enabled` copied `pos_cond_kwargs`/`neg_cond_kwargs` to CPU (a host sync) on every rollout request that returns the denoising environment, but `finalize_rollout_if_enabled` always overwrites both with its own SP-gathered CPU copy before anything reads them. The initial copy was pure waste.

Test: `test_pos_neg_cond_kwargs_are_kept_as_is_not_copied_to_cpu` asserts the stored values are the exact same (GPU) tensor objects, not a copy.

## 4. `[Perf]` validators: gate the NaN scan behind an env flag (opt-in)
`StageValidators.is_tensor`/`tensor_with_dims`/`list_of_tensors`/etc. each run a `torch.isnan(x).any().item()` scan (full-size kernel + host sync) on every field they check, on every request — roughly 6+ of these fire per request on the standard path (text-encoding output, latent-prep input, timestep-prep output, denoising input). Shape/type checks stay on regardless; `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_DISABLE_STAGE_NAN_CHECK=1` skips only the NaN scan, for callers on few-step/distilled models who want to cut per-request sync overhead and already trust their pipeline.

Test: `test_stage_validators_nan_gate.py` — default still rejects NaN, the flag accepts it while keeping shape checks, clean tensors pass either way.

## 5. `[Perf]` flow_rollout_controller: simplify SDE/CPS log-prob to one reduction
`-((full_variance_noise*noise_std_dev)**2) / (2*noise_std_dev**2)` is exactly `-0.5*full_variance_noise**2` (`noise_std_dev`, a scalar here, cancels algebraically), and `-log(noise_std_dev) - C` is the same scalar at every spatial position, so summed over the reduce dims it is just `local_elem_count * that scalar`. Moving both out of the per-element sum turns a full-size divide plus two full-size broadcast-subtracts into a single reduction plus a cheap per-batch-row correction. Also stopped allocating and summing a full-size zero tensor on ODE steps (`p_ode` is always exactly zero), and stopped allocating the ODE debug noise tensor when debug mode is off.

Verified against the existing `test_scheduler_rollout_unit.py` FlowGRPO bit-for-bit reference check (`atol=1e-6`, covering both the full log-prob and no-const branches) and a 200-trial numeric comparison against the original formula (max abs error 3.6e-7 on `log_prob_mean`).

## 6. `[Perf]` decoding: normalize decoded frames to `[0,1]` in place (memory, not speed)
`decode()`'s final `_to_unit_range(image)` call created a second full-size copy of the decode output (900MB+ for a typical video decode) just to rescale and clamp it. `image` is `decode_raw`'s fresh output with no other live reference to its pre-normalization values (`decode`/`decode_raw` both run under `@torch.no_grad()`), so it's safe to rescale/clamp in place. The streaming `on_frames` callback path keeps the out-of-place default, since those frames come from the VAE's own per-tile buffer.

Test: `_to_unit_range(..., in_place=True)` matches the out-of-place formula and mutates its input; the default stays out-of-place.

## GPU benchmark (base vs head)
Microbenchmarks on an NVIDIA A10: each changed code path, base (`main`) vs head, on synthetic tensors at realistic shapes, median of 20 runs. Not a full end-to-end model run.

| Change | Shape | Base | Head | Gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LTX-2 Bongmath (video + audio) | `[1,128,16,32,48]` | 43.5 ms | 0.55 ms | 79x, rel err ~2e-16 |
| LTX-2 Bongmath (video + audio) | `[1,128,16,16,24]` | 11.0 ms | 0.14 ms | 81x |
| Rollout init CPU copy | pos + neg `[1,512,4096]` bf16 | 0.80 ms | 0.008 ms | one host sync removed |
| Validator NaN scan (flag on) | per field | 0.062 ms | 0.008 ms | ~0.05 ms per field, 6+ fields per request |
| Log-prob, SDE | `[4,16,21,60,104]` | 0.95 ms | 0.25 ms | 3.9x, rel err 1.4e-7 |
| Log-prob, ODE | `[4,16,21,60,104]` | 0.15 ms | 0.02 ms | 7.8x |
| Decode normalize in place | `[1,3,121,720,1280]` | 16.9 ms | 16.7 ms | same speed, 2.5 GiB less peak memory (740 MiB less at 480p) |

Notes:
- The decode change saves memory, not time.
- The validator change only applies with `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_DISABLE_STAGE_NAN_CHECK=1`; default behavior is unchanged.
- The Bongmath saving is per refinement call; a full LTX-2 generation was not measured.

## Test plan
- Each fix has a focused regression test (see above), reusing existing fixtures/test files where one fit.
- All 6 fixes were run against the real package (not just unit-test logic) in a GPU-image CPU container on Modal, head vs base where base has a meaningful comparison:
  - Wan-Animate-2 clamp: head 129 passed / base 128 passed
  - LTX-2 Bongmath: 2 passed (head only; closed form verified separately against the loop)
  - rollout_hooks: 3 passed (head only)
  - validators NaN gate: 3 passed (head only)
  - flow_rollout log-prob: head 10 passed/1 skipped, base 10 passed/1 skipped — **identical pass count on both branches**, confirming no regression against the FlowGRPO reference
  - decoding in-place: head 12 passed / base 9 passed

## Known limitations / deferred (not in this PR)
- CFG batching (combining cond/uncond into one forward pass) is not included — it needs per-model measurement, not just a correctness check, and the models that don't already do it (most besides Cosmos3/LTX-2) would need individual handling of text lengths, masks, and RoPE.
- Minor per-step CPU overhead (`_build_attn_metadata` re-deriving the builder class every step, NVTX label string formatting) is not included — caching the builder class at construction looked tempting but I couldn't confirm `self.attn_backend` never changes mid-run across all models without a deeper audit, and the review that flagged it called this the lowest-priority item ("only matters with CUDA graphs or very small models").

title: [Feat] [NPU] dspark: Integrate native sampling and verification kernels
author: AndyLi429
body:
## Motivation DSpark draft generation and verification on Ascend can benefit from dedicated NPU implementations of projection/add/argmax, temperature softmax, and draft acceptance. This PR connects SGLang to the corresponding `sgl-kernel-npu` APIs and selects NPU implementations using actual tensor placement, including environments where `transfer_to_npu` aliases CUDA device checks. Companion kernel PR: https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/899. ## Modifications - Route `MarkovGreedyStep` to the NPU implementation with native projection and dtype-correct addition before token selection. - Route FP32 row argmax and DSpark greedy verification through the NPU argmax implementation. - Dispatch temperature softmax and the shared DFlash/DSpark accepted-prefix and bonus-token calculation to dedicated NPU kernels. - Add NPU dispatch tests covering device selection, numerical behavior, and integration boundaries. `MarkovSampleStep` dispatch changes are excluded from the current diff.

End-to-end accuracy: reference integration

The companion PR reports the following matched GPQA Diamond results:

Metric | Baseline | Integration -- | -- | -- Correct answers | 180/198 | 178/198 Accuracy | 91.37% | 90.36% API errors in the matched cohort | 0 | 0

The counts follow the reported overlap: 175 correct in both variants, five correct only in the baseline, and three correct only in the integration.

Speed Tests and Profiling

Single-operator performance

A3 graph-replay amortized latency reported by the companion PR; compilation and warmup excluded. Logit vocabulary size: 129280.

Operator / workload | Torch native (µs) | NPU implementation (µs) | Speedup -- | -- | -- | -- Markov greedy: B=64, R=64, FP32 base + BF16 projection | 89.98 | 79.43 | 1.13× Row argmax: 576 FP32 rows | 296.87 | 243.16 | 1.22× Temperature softmax: B=64, 9 rows/request, FP32 | 1338.39 | 1153.50 | 1.16× Accepted-prefix length + bonus: B=64, block length 9 | 94.28 | 12.80 | 7.37×

End-to-end serving: reference integration

Both variants ran in the same container on the same A3 host using:

  • DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8, ModelSlim W8A8, BF16 KV cache.
  • Non-quantized draft model; DSpark draft block size 6, verify length 7.
  • NPU graphs enabled; Radix cache disabled.
  • use_index_cache=true, index_topk_freq=4.
  • 128 input tokens, 1024 output tokens, concurrency 128; fixed corpus and seed 1, ignore_eos enabled.

Second-round warmed results:

Temperature | Metric | Baseline | Integration | Change -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 0 | Output throughput (tokens/s) | 4671.52 | 4929.38 | +5.52% 0 | Mean TPOT (ms) | 18.60 | 18.94 | +1.86% 1 | Output throughput (tokens/s) | 3610.44 | 4286.05 | +18.71% 1 | Mean TPOT (ms) | 25.86 | 21.94 | −15.16% 1 | P99 TPOT (ms) | 33.20 | 28.23 | −14.97%

The baseline required a precision-fixed NPU Philox sampler because unmodified main failed graph capture on the tested stack. The measured integration additionally included Markov sampling dispatch and precomputed noise.

These measurements describe that reference integration; they do not isolate the four operator integrations retained in this PR.

title: [Feat] [NPU] moe: Add Ascend Ops backend for MoE prefill and decode
author: chenxu214
body: ## Motivation Ascend MoE currently lacks a unified communication backend for expert-parallel prefill and decode. The existing routing paths make it difficult to support different communication domains, quantized dispatch formats, and model-specific expert layouts consistently. This PR introduces the `ascend_ops` backend for Ascend NPU MoE execution. It provides TP-group AllGather and AllToAllV paths for prefill, EP-group MC2 dispatch/combine for decode, and shared routing interfaces for expert permutation and unpermutation. The backend also adds explicit configuration and validation for supported layouts and dispatch quantization modes. title: [Perf] diffusion: Hide the pipelined Ulysses own-row copies behind the exchange
author: mickqian
body:
Stacked on #46247 (Wan's normed q/k written straight into the Ulysses exchange, which adds `fill_all`); also needs #46145 (`attend_into`, carried in that stack). The end-of-block part only engages where `attend_into` runs, which on B300 also needs #46146 (FA4 for long self-attention). Review the last commit.

## Motivation

On Wan2.2 T2V A14B 720p (4xB300, CFG 2 x Ulysses 2), the four GPUs differ by ~2% in speed at the 1100 W cap. Every block syncs a Ulysses pair twice and every step syncs all four ranks, so the slowest GPU sets the pace. A 2-step profile of every rank shows:
- the fastest rank idles ~1.5 ms per block, waiting for its peer;
- the slowest rank is busy except for two pipeline waits per block: ~117 us before the first head group attends (the peer's group-0 q/k in flight) and ~82 us before the output gather (the last group's output blocks in flight).

Two same-device copies (~60 us each) ran right next to those waits, on the slowest rank's critical path:
- v's own rows, copied into this rank's slots before the q/k fill;
- the gather of the peers' output blocks, after every group had arrived.

## Modifications

`distributed/device_communicators/ipc_a2a_multi.py`, `pipelined_attention`:
- `fill_all(blocks, part)` fills q (part 0), then k (part 1). q's blocks go out on the copy engine while the SMs fill k.
- v's own rows are copied after the fill, while k's blocks are in flight.
- With `attend_into`, the peers' blocks of every group before the last are gathered as soon as the last group has attended, while that group's blocks are still on the copy engines. The last group's blocks are gathered once they land.

`models/dits/wanvideo.py`: Wan's `fill_all` takes the part (one fused norm-RoPE pass for q, one for k, as before).

The same kernels copy the same bytes, so outputs are bit-identical.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_usp_pipelined_attention_multi_gpu.py` (2 and 4 ranks):
  - the q/k-filled exchange (`forward_qk_filled` with a copying `fill_all`) matches the sequential exchange bitwise;
  - with FA4 in place of cuDNN in the dynamic SDPA backend, the zero-copy output path (`attend_into`) matches the sequential exchange for dense and filled calls;
  - a wrong gather offset fails it.
- Wan2.2 T2V A14B 720p, 4xB300, 3-step lossless (crf 0, x264 medium) mp4: md5 identical to the base for 3 prompts.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Wan2.2 T2V A14B 720p, 4xB300, 2-step profile of every rank, median per DiT block:

| rank | before: SM idle | before: block | after: SM idle | after: block |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 (slowest) | 0.205 ms | 54.565 ms | 0.046 ms | 54.472 ms |
| 0 (fastest) | 1.48 ms | 54.644 ms | 0.75 ms | 54.143 ms |

Rank 3's two waits (117 us + 82 us) and both copies leave its critical path: -93 us per block, ~0.15 s over the 1600 block calls of a 40-step request.

Ten head groups instead of the automatic five were slower: 55.1 ms per block.

E2E, harness single_e2e (fresh server per run, MP4 x264 medium / CRF 23), one 4xB300 box, runs interleaved: base (#46247 stack) 88.441 / 88.465 s (mean 88.453) -> this PR 88.394 / 88.346 / 88.444 s (mean 88.395), -0.06 s; TRT-LLM 1.4.0rc1 in the same rotation 93.118 / 93.173 s.

title: [Perf] deepep_v2: Reduce masked GEMM buffer memory during CUDA Graph capture
author: Jzz1943
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
