Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

DeepEP V2 sizes per-expert masked GEMM buffers using the configured maximum dispatch capacity across all source ranks, even for small CUDA Graph batches. These buffers are retained by captured graphs and can cause out-of-memory failures during capture.

## Modifications

- Bound masked GEMM buffers by the current source-token upper bound, accounting for worst-case routing, uneven TP shards, Graph padding, and GEMM alignment.
- Apply the tighter bound when EP spans the full TP group with attention DP/CP disabled; retain the existing capacity for other topologies.
- Keep communication buffers unchanged, with no additional collectives, device-to-host synchronization, or model-specific conditions.
- Add focused capacity and topology-fallback coverage to the existing CPU lifecycle tests.

## Accuracy Tests

- All **11 CPU lifecycle tests** passed. Four-rank GPU checks cover worst-case routing, uneven shards, and CUDA Graph replay.
- GLM-5.3-Flash, **4 × H200, TP4/EP4**, ordinary prefill/decode: GSM8K, **1,314 examples × 2 runs: 96.0%, 95.9%**. Model validation includes #46225 and #46424 for independent KDA/GDN padding and DSA output-layout fixes; neither is a code dependency of this allocation change.

```bash
python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_deepep_v2_buffer_lifecycle.py
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Capture comparison with an **8,192-token prefill chunk**, default model context length and attention TP gather, `mem_fraction_static=0.85`, and a decode Graph limit of 64:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Decode CUDA Graph capture | OOM while capturing bs56, after bs64 completed | All 10 capture sizes completed |
| Complete Graph memory per GPU | Unavailable: capture failed | **2.90–2.91 GiB** |
| Available memory per GPU after capture | Unavailable | **17.28 GiB** |

The baseline failed when allocating a **4.50 GiB** masked GEMM workspace with approximately **3.11 GiB** free. This PR completed capture at the same settings. Memory values above use framework capture logs; no complete baseline Graph-memory total or percentage reduction is reported because its capture failed.

Reproduction command (model path and serving address replaced):

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
EP_DISABLE_GIN=1 \
SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=2048 \
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --served-model-name llm \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --ep-size 4 \
  --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \
  --moe-a2a-backend deepep_v2 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang \
  --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --max-mamba-cache-size 320 \
  --max-running-requests 64 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \
  --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 20 24 32 40 48 56 64 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --tokenizer-worker-num 4 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8000 \
  --random-seed 42
```

The per-rank dispatch capacity is 2,048 for this TP4/chunk8192 configuration. `EP_DISABLE_GIN=1` selects the non-GIN communication path used for validation. After TP alignment, the actual captured sizes are `[4, 8, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64]`. The command uses default context length and attention TP gather and does not override `max_prefill_tokens`.

title: [Perf] [AMD] deterministic: Use a fixed-order two-stage all-reduce for large inputs
author: aarnetalman
body:
## Motivation

In deterministic mode on ROCm every custom all-reduce runs the 1-stage kernel: each GPU reads every peer's whole input and sums the ranks in the order 0..n-1. That order is what makes the result independent of the input size, but each GPU reads n times the data, so at TP4/TP8 the all-reduce takes a large share of the step: on MI350X, Qwen3-8B deterministic decode/prefill spends 48% of GPU time in it at TP4 and 63% at TP8 (8k-token inputs), and deterministic throughput at TP8 was about half of normal mode. The 2-stage kernel (reduce-scatter + all-gather) reads far less, but it cannot be used as is: each owner starts its sum at its own rank, so an element's result depends on which rank owns it, which changes with the input size. This PR adds a fixed-order option to the 2-stage kernel that sums the ranks in the same order as the 1-stage kernel, so the two give the same bits for every element at every size, and uses it for large inputs at 4 and 8 ranks. Results do not change; on MI350X deterministic throughput rises 16-24% at TP4 and 29-57% at TP8 on Qwen3-8B, and 28-54% at TP8 on Qwen3.8-27B, with every determinism check passing.

## Modifications

- `custom_all_reduce_hip.cuh`: `cross_device_reduce_2stage` gets a template parameter `kFixedOrder` (default `false`, so normal mode is unchanged). With it, stage 1 reads the ranks in the order 0..n-1 instead of starting at its own rank; stage 2 (the gather) is unchanged.
- `deterministic_all_reduce.hip`: one templated launcher instead of three copies per dtype. Inputs copied into the registered buffer (`deterministic_all_reduce_unreg`, which every deterministic call of `CustomAllreduce` uses for inputs that fit the buffer, including in CUDA graphs and the pieces of larger inputs) take the fixed-order 2-stage kernel with 32 blocks at or above 512 KiB at 4 ranks and 256 KiB at 8 ranks (the thresholds `CustomAllreduce::allreduce` uses); everything else keeps the 1-stage kernel with 16 blocks: smaller inputs, 2 and 6 ranks, and `deterministic_all_reduce_reg` (its inputs can be larger than the IPC buffer that the 2-stage kernel stages 1/n of the input in).
- New test `test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_amd_deterministic_allreduce_fixed_order.py` (`stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-mi35x`): at 4 and 8 ranks, bf16 and fp16, sizes on both sides of the thresholds, eager and CUDA graphs, the all-reduce output must equal, bit for bit, the sum of the ranks' inputs computed in torch in the order 0..n-1 (float32 accumulation). The data is chosen so its float32 sum depends on the order of the ranks.

## Accuracy Tests

MI350X, ROCm 7.2.4, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261021`.

Kernel level (bf16, hidden 4096 and 7168, 1-2,040 rows eager and 1-512 rows in CUDA graphs, order-sensitive data, 2/4/8 ranks): the fixed-order 2-stage kernel's output equals the current 1-stage kernel's output bit for bit at every size, is identical on every rank, and a row's result does not depend on the number of rows. Control: the current (unordered) 2-stage kernel differs from the 1-stage kernel at 42-44 of 42-44 sizes at 4 and 8 ranks.

End to end, deterministic mode (`--enable-deterministic-inference`, Triton prefill and AITER decode attention, together with the other open MI350X deterministic-mode PRs), `python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic` (`single`, `prefix`, `prefix --return-logprob`, `radix_cache`, 50 trials) plus a bitwise batch-size check (the same prompt in batches of 1 to 50, 1,275 responses, token IDs and logprobs compared exactly with the batch-size-1 response): every check passes (`single` 1 output, `prefix` 1/1/1/1, prefix logprobs identical, radix cache consistent, bitwise 1,275 / 1,275). With this branch's build (sgl-kernel rebuilt for gfx950):

- the new test passes at 4 and 8 ranks, and the existing 2-rank deterministic all-reduce test passes;
- every check above passes on Qwen3-8B TP2, TP4 and TP8, Qwen3-30B-A3B TP4, Qwen3.8-27B TP4 and Qwen3.8-27B TP8, and again on fresh servers: Qwen3-8B TP8 4 / 4, Qwen3-30B-A3B TP4 3 / 3, Qwen3.8-27B TP4 2 / 2;
- GSM8K (sgl-eval 0.1.2, temperature 0, 1,319 questions) is unchanged: Qwen3-8B 93.40% / 93.25% / 93.48% at TP2 / TP4 / TP8 (93.48% at TP8 before), Qwen3.8-27B 96.21% at TP4 and 96.13% at TP8.

Through the experiment-only switch (same kernel and selection) the checks also passed on Qwen3-30B-A3B TP4 with GSM8K 95.15% (95.15% before).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel time per all-reduce (bf16, hidden 4096, CUDA graph of 50 calls, median of 7), current 1-stage kernel vs this PR:

| input | 8 ranks: current | 8 ranks: this PR | 4 ranks: current | 4 ranks: this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 MiB (128 rows) | 23.9 us | 15.4 us (1.55x) | 22.2 us | 16.2 us (1.37x) |
| 4 MiB (512 rows) | 77.8 us | 31.4 us (2.47x) | 74.8 us | 43.1 us (1.74x) |
| 8 MiB (1,024 rows) | 149.2 us | 50.7 us (2.94x) | 144.5 us | 77.8 us (1.86x) |
| 16 MiB (2,040 rows) | 291.5 us | 88.1 us (3.31x) | 283.1 us | 146.0 us (1.94x) |

Below the thresholds (decode-size inputs) the 1-stage kernel is faster and is kept; at 2 ranks the two kernels are equally fast and the 1-stage kernel is kept.

End to end, deterministic mode, `python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf`, output throughput, current vs this branch's build (same server arguments, interleaved):

| model, TP | 1k in / 1k out | 8k in / 1k out | 32k in / 256 out | long context |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-8B, 2 | 10,135 -> 10,145 (+0.1%) | 2,623 -> 2,624 (0.0%) | 207.2 -> 207.3 (0.0%) | |
| Qwen3-8B, 4 | 15,543 -> 18,129 (+16.6%) | 3,946 -> 4,755 (+20.5%) | 303.4 -> 377.5 (+24.4%) | 64k / 120k: 125.2 -> 149.3 (+19.2%) / 30.8 -> 36.2 (+17.5%) |
| Qwen3-8B, 8 | 20,147 -> 26,751 (+32.8%) | 5,044 -> 7,409 (+46.9%) | 383.3 -> 600.6 (+56.7%) | 64k / 120k: 160.1 -> 233.9 (+46.1%) / 41.7 -> 60.0 (+43.9%) |
| Qwen3.8-27B, 8 | 7,635 -> 9,803 (+28.4%) | 2,191 -> 3,196 (+45.9%) | 165.2 -> 254.9 (+54.3%) | |

(tok/s; 256 / 256 / 64 prompts; long context 64k in / 256 out and 120k in / 128 out, Qwen3-8B with YaRN.) Qwen3-8B TP8 is the mean of two rounds: the current kernel gave the same throughput in both (20,136 / 20,158 at 1k in / 1k out), this PR 27,503 and 25,999 (+36.6% and +29.0%); at 8k and 32k the two rounds agree within 0.3%. TP2 is unchanged because the 1-stage kernel is kept at 2 ranks. Time to first token falls 19-47% at TP4 and TP8 (Qwen3.8-27B TP8: 5.6 -> 3.3 s, 22.9 -> 13.3 s, 13.5 -> 8.2 s). Normal mode is unchanged.

Through the experiment-only switch running the same kernel and selection, before the build: Qwen3-30B-A3B TP4 15,024 -> 16,431 (+9.4%) / 4,435 -> 5,089 (+14.7%) / 334.6 -> 393.1 (+17.5%); Qwen3.8-27B TP4 5,517 -> 6,245 (+13.2%) / 1,776 -> 2,160 (+21.6%) / 131.8 -> 164.2 (+24.6%), 64k / 128k +21.8% / +22.8%.

Related: #34543 (merged) reduces deterministic inputs larger than the buffer piece by piece through `deterministic_all_reduce_unreg`, so those pieces also take the faster kernel. The measurements above include it in both columns, and this branch merges cleanly on current main.

title: [Perf] [AMD] unquant: Pad gfx115x linear and lm_head weight rows to avoid cache aliasing
author: twoask
body:
## Motivation

Decode on gfx1151 (Strix Halo, LPDDR5X-8000, 256-bit bus, 256 GB/s theoretical) is memory-bound: over 98% of decode GPU time is in GEMMs. On HIP without AITER, unquantized linears run through `F.linear` (hipBLASLt). At M=1, hipBLASLt reaches only 132-193 GB/s on Llama-3.1-8B's shapes, 51-75% of the theoretical peak.

## Root cause

On gfx1151 (and on gfx1100, see Results), a weight whose row stride is a multiple of 2 KiB puts the rows a skinny GEMM reads together onto the same L2/MALL channel. Most dense-model K dims qualify (bf16 K = 2048, 3072, 4096, 14336, ...).

If each row is offset by one 128 B cache line, they spread out again. The logical shape and values stay the same; only the stride changes.

M=1 bf16, cold cache, best of 3, GB/s, plain row stride vs padded row stride, hipBLASLt default solutions, no TunableOp:

| Llama-3.1-8B shape (K -> N) | plain | padded | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| QKV 4096 -> 6144 | 151.5 | 214.4 | +42% |
| O 4096 -> 4096 | 131.6 | 213.3 | +62% |
| gate/up 4096 -> 28672 | 182.6 | 223.0 | +22% |
| down 14336 -> 4096 | 159.4 | 225.5 | +41% |
| lm_head 4096 -> 128256 | 192.5 | 226.5 | +18% |
| GEMM time per token | 89.0 ms | 67.6 ms | -24% |

All shapes reach 83-89% of peak after padding, and the output matches the unpadded output (relative error against fp32 is unchanged, 1.9-3.1e-3).

## Fix

When a qualifying unquantized weight finishes loading on gfx115x (RDNA3.5), give its rows a padded stride. This happens once per weight, at load time.

- **Rule:** `(K * element_size) % 2048 == 0`. If it holds, the row stride grows by 128 B; it's the same rule as vLLM's `cache_aliasing_pad_elems`. Only bf16 and fp16 weights are padded, since those are what was measured. fp32 linears, such as the router gates in kimi_k3, longcat_flash and hunyuan_v3/v4, are left alone; vLLM pads them too, but that was never measured here. `K` is the weight tensor's own dim 1, so a tensor-parallel row shard is judged by its own K, not the full checkpoint K.
- **Linear weights:** `UnquantizedLinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading` does the padding.
- **lm_head:** `DefaultModelLoader.postprocess_weights` calls `finalize_gfx115_weight_padding(model)`, which pads every unquantized LM head:
  - `ParallelLMHead`, untied.
  - A tied head that is the input embedding module itself (`lm_head = model.embed_tokens`). 54 model files tie this way, and the embedding's quant method cannot tell it apart from an untied input embedding, so the model's module names decide.
  - A tied head that shares a `Parameter` (`ParallelLMHead.tie_weights`). This is padded once.

  An untied input embedding is never padded: it reads one row per token, so padding gains nothing.
- **Gate:** `is_gfx115_supported()` is new in `srt/utils/common.py`: true on RDNA3.5 (`gcnArchName` starting with `gfx115`), with a `torch.cuda.is_available()` check. It's the gfx115x form of #47695's `is_gfx1151_supported()`.
- **Opt-out:** setting `SGLANG_DISABLE_GFX115_WEIGHT_PADDING=1` turns the padding off. It's on by default on gfx115x.
- **Log:** the first load logs one INFO line listing the padded and skipped shapes. Later weight updates (for example, each RL weight sync) log the same line at DEBUG. That includes a speculative-decoding draft model, which is the second model loaded in the process, so its line is at DEBUG too. Example:
  `gfx115x weight padding: padded {(6144, 4096): 32, (4096, 4096): 32, (28672, 4096): 32, (4096, 14336): 32, (128256, 4096): 1}; skipped {}`
- **Memory:** the padded weights grow by 128 B per row, about 1.5% for K = 4096. Llama-3.1-8B: +0.24 GB on 16 GB. While one weight is being padded, `F.pad` briefly holds both copies, so peak extra memory during load is at most one LM head (about 1 GB for Llama-3.1-8B). That happens before KV-cache sizing, so it doesn't reduce the cache.

## Results

Each configuration was measured with padding on (default) and with `SGLANG_DISABLE_GFX115_WEIGHT_PADDING=1`, on gfx1151.

Settings:
- Server: `--attention-backend triton --disable-overlap-schedule --mem-fraction-static 0.5 --context-length 8192`, plus `SGLANG_DISABLE_LEAN_ATTENTION=1`. Lean attention needs 66560 B of LDS, and RDNA has 65536.
- Decode benchmark: `bench_serving` random, 1024 in / 256 out.
- Prefill benchmark: 4000 in / 4 out.
- Accuracy: sgl-eval 0.1.3 GSM8K, 200 questions, temperature 0, max-tokens 1024, 32 threads.

These numbers were measured without #45540 (RMSNorm via torch `rms_norm` on HIP), so both arms run the slower `forward_native` RMSNorm. The two PRs touch different files and don't depend on each other. With both merged, absolute tok/s will be higher; I haven't measured them together.

**This branch, on main (638374c389):**

| Model | 1-stream tok/s (TPOT) | 8-way tok/s | Prefill TTFT, 4000 tokens | 4-way prefill tok/s | GSM8K |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, off (2 runs) | 9.98 (98.4 ms) | 65.8 | 1786 ms | 3582 | 83.5, 81.5 |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, **on** (2 runs) | **12.68 (76.9 ms), +27%** | **81.1, +23%** | 1785 ms | 3673 | 85.0, 84.5 |
| Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, off (3 runs) | 20.46 (48.1 ms) | 140.5 | 699 ms | 8818 | 85.0, 84.5, 85.5 |
| Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, **on** (4 runs) | **26.68 (36.8 ms), +30%** | **187.2, +33%** | 700 ms | 9110 | 84.0, 86.5, 85.0, 0.0 (see Known issues) |

Qwen2.5-3B covers the QKV bias, tied embeddings (`lm_head = model.embed_tokens`), and a skipped Down (K = 11008).

**Same padding on an earlier experimental branch** (sglang at `pr31137`, padding behind a flag; that experiment also padded the untied input embedding):

| Model | 1-stream tok/s | 8-way tok/s | Prefill TTFT | GSM8K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Phi-4-mini-instruct | 20.1 -> 23.4 (+16%) | 125.1 -> 140.0 (+12%) | 755 -> 756 ms | 91.0 -> 90.5% |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (MoE) | 14.6 -> 16.4 (+12%) | 45.3 -> 47.7 (+5%) | 2783 -> 2820 ms | not usable (see Known issues) |

**gfx1100 (Radeon PRO W7900D, 48 GB), measured independently by @LZ-QWQ** ([#30599 comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/30599#issuecomment-6465927305)) at this PR's head `656e95c345`. Qwen3-8B bf16, TP1, decode CUDA graphs on, 3 runs per arm, without #45540:

| Qwen3-8B on gfx1100 | Off | On |
|---|---|---|
| 1-stream tok/s (TPOT) | 19.40 (50.6 ms) | **22.79 (42.9 ms), +17.5%** |
| 8-way tok/s (TPOT) | 135.6 (54.0 ms) | **156.5 (46.0 ms), +15.4%** |
| Prefill TTFT, 4000 tokens | 1076 ms | 1095 ms (+1.7%) |
| 4-way prefill tok/s | 3545 | 3515 (-0.8%) |
| GSM8K (sgl-eval, 200 questions, 2 runs) | 95.5, 95.5 | 95.0, 95.5 |

The kernel-level table below gives +8% to +61% per shape on that card. All 12 tests in the new test file pass there, including the two device tests (run before the gate was narrowed to gfx115x; they're skipped on gfx1100 now). Their tree also carried the gfx1100 build and packaging enablement that `main` doesn't have yet (see #30599, #46900); both arms used that same tree.

**Hidden size 5120: a small loss (Qwen3-14B, gfx1151).** K = 5120 rows are 10 KiB, 5 x 2 KiB, so the rule pads every linear here, but they alias much less than K = 4096. Qwen3-14B bf16 at `656e95c345` (this PR's commit, before the main merge), `--attention-backend triton --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --context-length 8192`, decode CUDA graphs on, same `bench_serving` settings as above, one server per arm, run off/on/off/on:

| Qwen3-14B | Off (2 runs) | On (2 runs) |
|---|---|---|
| 1-stream tok/s (median TPOT) | 7.32 / 7.26 (133.4 / 134.0 ms) | 7.18 / 7.18 (135.7 / 135.7 ms), -1.5% |
| 8-way tok/s (median TPOT) | 56.25 / 56.05 (141.5 / 142.0 ms) | 55.26 / 55.26 (144.0 / 144.0 ms), -1.6% |
| GSM8K (200 questions, 5-shot, first pair) | 89.5 | 90.5 |

Per shape at M=1 (`F.linear`, plain -> padded, GB/s), padding helps the small layers and slightly hurts the large ones: QKV 7168 x 5120 216 -> 224 (+4%), O 5120 x 5120 206 -> 220 (+7%), gate/up 34816 x 5120 235 -> 229 (-3%), down 5120 x 17408 225 -> 224 (-0.5%), lm_head 151936 x 5120 241 -> 231 (-4%). Weighted by bytes, that's about -0.8% of GEMM time, in line with the end-to-end result. Outputs are bitwise identical padded and unpadded.

## What's not affected

- **Prefill:** long-prompt GEMMs are compute-bound. TTFT and 4-way prefill throughput are within noise on every model (-3% to +4%).
- **MoE experts:** fused-MoE expert weights are 3D and go through `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`, so they are not padded; vLLM doesn't pad them either. On DeepSeek-V2-Lite, the attention projections, shared experts and dense layer are padded, and `kv_b_proj` (K = 512) is skipped.
- **Quantized layers:** only `UnquantizedLinearMethod` and unquantized LM heads are touched.
- **fp32 weights**, for example MoE router gates, are left alone; only bf16/fp16 was measured.
- **Outside gfx115x:** a no-op. `_is_gfx115` is computed once at import and is false on CUDA, CDNA, RDNA3 and CPU.
- **Kernels reading raw weight pointers:** the CUDA-only bf16 GEMV/CuTe paths check `weight.is_contiguous()`. `apply_into` (`torch.mm(out=)`), `F.embedding` and the lm_head `torch.matmul` all honor strides. Model code that fuses weights after loading (`torch.cat(...).contiguous()` in qwen3_5, minimax_m3) simply produces a contiguous weight.

## Related work

- vLLM #55090 (`maybe_pad_weight_avoid_cache_aliasing`, `vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py:230`): the same rule, measured on gfx1151 (its gate covers all of gfx11). It reports only -3% TPOT because vLLM decodes through `wvSplitK`, which is less sensitive to the aliasing. sglang's hipBLASLt path is hit much harder.
- ROCm/hip-ep #1274: same cause (int4, gfx1151).
- sglang's own XPU MoE padding (`xpu_moe_ld_padding_elems`): the same idea for Xe L3 set aliasing.

## Kernel-level verification

`F.linear` on Llama-3.1-8B's weight shapes, plain vs padded. Weights rotate through more than 512 MB so the cache can't help.

**Gain per shape, BF16, M=1.** gfx1151 numbers are medians of 5 fresh processes; gfx1100 numbers are @LZ-QWQ's, from the same script:

| Shape (K -> N) | gfx1151 plain -> padded (GB/s) | gfx1151 gain | gfx1100 plain -> padded (GB/s) | gfx1100 gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QKV 4096 -> 6144 | 151.1 -> 212.2 | +40.4% | 351.6 -> 434.2 | +23.5% |
| O 4096 -> 4096 | 131.5 -> 211.9 | +61.1% | 322.7 -> 397.4 | +23.1% |
| gate/up 4096 -> 28672 | 182.4 -> 222.3 | +21.9% | 364.2 -> 587.1 | +61.2% |
| down 14336 -> 4096 | 159.7 -> 224.7 | +40.7% | 424.3 -> 458.9 | +8.2% |
| lm_head 4096 -> 128256 | 192.2 -> 225.8 | +17.5% | 649.9 -> 755.5 | +16.2% |

**Order effects (gfx1151):** both layouts are allocated and warmed. Six rounds alternate plain-first and padded-first, 20 iterations each; each cell is the median of the per-round gains. Every round was positive.

| Shape | bf16 M=1 | bf16 M=8 | fp16 M=1 | fp16 M=8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QKV | +40.9% | +46.0% | +40.8% | +40.5% |
| O | +61.5% | +57.0% | +57.3% | +56.6% |
| gate/up | +22.1% | +27.9% | +20.6% | +21.7% |
| down | +41.5% | +26.4% | +27.3% | +26.5% |
| lm_head | +17.8% | +24.2% | +16.3% | +17.2% |

**Numerics (gfx1151):** 30 cases (5 shapes x bf16/fp16 x M = 1, 8, 300, normalized random weights, with bias).
- Padding keeps every logical weight exactly.
- Padded and unpadded outputs are bitwise identical in all 30 cases.
- Both match an fp32 reference: bf16 `rtol=1.6e-2, atol=1e-2`, fp16 `rtol=2e-3, atol=2e-3`.

These are standalone GEMM tests; the unit tests and end-to-end runs cover SGLang's load and reload hooks.

## Testing

`test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_unquant_gfx115_weight_padding.py`:

- **CPU, registered in `base-a-test-cpu`:**
  - The pad rule counts row bytes, not elements.
  - The pad keeps shape and values and gives the same `F.linear` output, with bias.
  - The gate leaves the weight untouched off gfx115x, when opted out, when already padded, when non-contiguous, and for fp32.
  - An untied input embedding is not padded.
  - Tied heads, both forms, are padded once and still embed correctly, including across a second postprocess pass (a reload).
  - A quantized head is not padded.
  - A reload writes into the padded storage, keeping the stride and the pointer. This holds for `ColumnParallelLinear`, and at TP=4 through the checkpoint loaders models actually use: `QKVParallelLinear` and `MergedColumnParallelLinear` (which slice rows) and `RowParallelLinear` (which slices K). After the reload, values match an unpadded layer loaded the same way.
  - The log line is INFO on the first load and DEBUG on later passes.
  - A TP=4 `RowParallelLinear` is judged by its 768-element shard, not K = 3072.
- **gfx115x GPU** (skipped elsewhere, since most CI is NVIDIA or MI300). Run locally on gfx1151, and by @LZ-QWQ on gfx1100:
  - hipBLASLt output matches unpadded on Llama shapes at M = 1, 8 and 300, with bias.
  - A tied head embeds and projects correctly on device.
- **Mutation checks:** 13 of 13 mutations caught (element-based rule, padding every embedding, dropping the tied-module case, dropping the loader call, no contiguity check, opt-out ignored, gate ignored, quantized head padded, linear hook removed, full-K instead of shard-K, wrong view slice, no dtype limit, logging at INFO on every pass).

Repro:

```bash
python test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_unquant_gfx115_weight_padding.py -v

SGLANG_DISABLE_LEAN_ATTENTION=1 [SGLANG_DISABLE_GFX115_WEIGHT_PADDING=1] \
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --attention-backend triton --disable-overlap-schedule --mem-fraction-static 0.5 --context-length 8192
python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 \
  --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1 --num-prompts 8 --max-concurrency 1
sgl-eval run gsm8k --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 --num-examples 200 --temperature 0 \
  --max-tokens 1024 --num-threads 32
```

## Scope and limits

- **Hardware:** per review, the gate covers gfx115x (RDNA3.5: gfx1150 Strix Point, gfx1151 Strix Halo, gfx1152 Krackan Point), the same scope #47695 is moving to. Only gfx1151 was measured end to end (here and in vLLM #55090). gfx1150 and gfx1152 have a narrower memory system and are untested; owners, please report on #30599, and the opt-out exists for exactly that. RDNA3 (gfx110x) is outside the gate because `main` doesn't officially support it yet, even though @LZ-QWQ measured a gain on gfx1100; the gate can widen once it does.
- **Hidden size 5120:** on Qwen3-14B (all linears K = 5120 or 17408) padding is 1.5% slower end to end; see Results. Other hidden-5120 models (for example Qwen2.5-14B, Phi-4) have the same K = 5120 rows but weren't measured. The rule is kept as is, the same as vLLM's. `SGLANG_DISABLE_GFX115_WEIGHT_PADDING=1` turns it off for such models.
- **Weight reload:**
  - Reloads through `update_weights_*` keep the padding: the loaders copy into the padded storage (`narrow().copy_()`), and `postprocess_weights` re-runs. The second pass skips weights that are already padded, so storage pointers stay stable for CUDA graphs.
  - If a loader rebinds a weight to a fresh contiguous tensor, the re-run pads it again.
  - Loaders that bypass `DefaultModelLoader.postprocess_weights` (dummy, sharded-state, remote-instance) still pad linear weights but not the LM head. That affects only speed.
- **Head detection:** an LM head is found by type (`ParallelLMHead`) or by the attribute name `lm_head`. A tied head stored under another name (for example `embed_out`) isn't padded, which costs only speed.

## Known issues, unrelated or unresolved

- **One collapsed Qwen2.5-3B GSM8K run with padding on (0.0%).** From the first token of every answer, the output was the same garbage regardless of the question, with speed normal. It didn't reproduce:
  - 3 further padded runs, with the same script and server sequence, scored 84.0-86.5%.
  - Single-prompt checks after each benchmark stage were correct.
  - Concurrent 32-thread probes, with and without CUDA graphs, were correct.
  - A launch-loop test then started 50 fresh Qwen2.5-3B servers, alternating 25 padded and 25 opted out. Each server got 5 fixed prompts and then a burst of 32 concurrent requests, all checked against the expected answers. All 50 launches answered every prompt correctly.
  - Every launch was instrumented:
    - A SHA-256 over every parameter after loading, computed on the logical values. All 50 launches had the same hash, padded or not.
    - The tie (`lm_head` and `embed_tokens`): same module, same `Parameter`, same `data_ptr()` in every launch. The row stride was 2112 padded and 2048 opted out.
    - No NaN or Inf in any weight, in the first 50 eager-mode logits, or in any returned logprob.

  So I report it as a one-off that couldn't be reproduced. Before this test, padded runs had 1 collapse in 6 and opted-out runs 0 in 5. The launch loop doesn't replay the full benchmark sequence that came before the collapse, and the logits check doesn't cover decode steps replayed from CUDA graphs. @LZ-QWQ's two padded GSM8K runs on gfx1100 also showed no collapse. A similar intermittent breakdown happens with padding off on this stack: DeepSeek-V2-Lite's GSM8K answers degenerate into `!!!!` in 130 of 200 answers unpadded and 115 of 200 padded.
- **DeepSeek-V2-Lite `!!!!` breakdown:** happens without this PR. Please don't attribute it to this change.

title: [Perf] diffusion: opt-in Wan UMT5 padding trim (SGLANG_DIFFUSION_WAN_TEXT_PADDING)
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
Draft: the output is not bit-identical (see Results), and MOVA is only covered by the existing tests so far.

## Summary

Wan padded every prompt to 512 tokens, ran UMT5 over all 512, then sliced the padding off in `t5_postprocess_text` and zero-padded back to 512. This tokenizes with `padding="longest"` on `WanT2V480PConfig`, so UMT5 only runs over the real tokens. Typical prompts are 10 to 150 tokens.

The DiT still gets 512 long, zero-padded embeddings. `t5_postprocess_text` now returns a `TextConditioningOutput` with a 512 long mask and the real lengths, because the pipeline checks the mask length against the embedding length and `padding="longest"` alone fails that check.

## Results

A100-80GB, real `TextEncoderLoader.load` of the UMT5 encoder from `Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers`, median of 20 runs, ABBA order:

| Prompt | Real tokens | Encode ms before | Encode ms after | Max abs diff | Cosine |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| short | 11 | 324 | 31 to 33 | 2.0e-5 | 0.99999994 |
| long | 75 | 328 | 70 | 2.2e-5 | 1.0 |
| negative prompt | 62 | 330 | 48 | 5.4e-6 | 1.0 |
| batch of 2 | 11 and 75 | 617 | 117 | 1.8e-5 | 1.0 |

Each request encodes a positive and a negative prompt, so the saving is about 0.3 to 0.6 s per request. That is small next to a full generation.

End to end (Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B, one prompt, seed 42, 480x832, 33 frames, 20 steps, through `sglang generate`):

| Comparison | PSNR |
|---|---|
| base vs base | identical |
| this branch vs this branch | identical |
| base vs this code with padding kept at 512 | identical |
| base vs this branch | 30.3 dB mean, 28.5 dB min |

So the mask and output type change is faithful, and the difference comes only from the shorter padding. The embeddings differ by about 1e-5, but the different matrix shapes change the bf16 rounding and 20 denoising steps amplify it. The video is a different but valid sample. I did not judge which one is better.

## Tests

CPU, one case in the existing `test_wan_pipeline_config.py`: the config trims padding, and the postprocess keeps 512 long embeddings, a matching mask and the real lengths. I also ran `test_text_encoding_cache.py` and `test_wan_pipeline_config.py` on base and on this branch: 50 passed on base, 51 on this branch (the new case). `test_wan_streamed_encode.py` fails at collection on both.

## Not done

- MOVA reuses `t5_postprocess_text` and now gets the same `TextConditioningOutput`. It keeps its 512 padding. I have not run MOVA end to end.
- Only one prompt was generated end to end, and memory was not measured.
- Other Wan configs inherit the change through `WanT2V480PConfig`. Only the 1.3B T2V model was run.

title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: Route large BF16 linears to the FlyDSL a16w16 GEMM on gfx1250
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

**What**
On gfx1250 (MI450), FLUX.2-dev 720p image generation takes 38.96 s end to end, and this PR brings it to 30.55 s by running the large BF16 diffusion linears on aiter's FlyDSL `gemm_a16w16_gfx1250` kernel instead of the GEMMs torch.compile generates.

**Why**
gfx1250 has no tuned hipBLASLt BF16 kernels, so under torch.compile the DiT linears fall to Inductor's `max-autotune` Triton templates, which reach 610-700 TFLOPS on the large FLUX.2 shapes. GEMMs are 84% of the transformer's kernel time on this model (327 of 388 ms per forward), so the GEMM rate sets the end-to-end time. The FlyDSL a16w16 kernel runs those shapes at 890-960 TFLOPS (1.3-1.5x on every FLUX.2 GEMM, including the small text-stream ones) with one fixed config (`256x256x64` tile, 2x4 warps, 4 LDS buffers, `compute_bound`), and a 128-row tile when 256x256 tiles would not fill the CUs. It is wrapped in a non-mutating custom op so torch.compile treats it as an opaque, side-effect-free call.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/linear.py`: under `USE_AITER_GFX1250` (gfx1250 with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`), register `sglang::flydsl_gfx1250_linear`, a custom op with `mutates_args=()` and a shape-only fake impl that calls `aiter.ops.flydsl.gemm_a16w16_gfx1250.gemm_a16w16`.
- `apply_unquantized_linear` routes to it when `_use_flydsl_linear` holds: bf16/fp16 input and weight with matching dtypes, M >= 256, K >= 256 (the 4-stage pipeline needs at least 3 K tiles), and a unit stride on the last dim of both input and weight. Everything else keeps the existing path. The M >= 256 bound is where this was measured; below it torch.compile fuses the small GEMMs into neighbouring ops (for example the modulation mm with its SiLU), and routing them through an opaque custom op would break that fusion. FlyDSL is also faster than eager hipBLASLt at small M (100 vs 145 us at 1 x 36864 x 6144), so extending the route to small M is a follow-up that needs its own measurement under compile.
- Other platforms: `_use_flydsl_linear` short-circuits on `USE_AITER_GFX1250 = False`, so NVIDIA and non-gfx1250 AMD keep their original kernels and results; the only new work is that one boolean check.
- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_gfx1250_flydsl_linear.py`: a large-M linear goes through the FlyDSL kernel and matches an fp32 reference; a small-M linear does not call it. Skipped unless running on gfx1250 with AITER.

## Accuracy Tests

FLUX.2-dev is an image model, so accuracy is image PSNR against an eager reference (eager mode, `F.linear` on hipBLASLt, same prompt and seed). Same command as the benchmark below.

| Run | PSNR vs eager reference |
|---|---|
| baseline, default flags | 25.2 dB |
| baseline, `--offload-during-compile false` | 29.2 dB |
| this PR, default flags | 23.7 dB |
| this PR, `--offload-during-compile false` (run 1 / run 2) | 22.3 / 23.5 dB |
| noise floor: this PR, same config run twice | 28.0 dB |
| noise floor: baseline, the two flag settings against each other | 26.3 dB |

The compiled pipeline is not bitwise reproducible run to run, and 50 denoising steps amplify last-bit GEMM differences, so two identical runs already differ by 28 dB. This PR lands 2-6 dB lower than the baseline against the eager reference; the composition and subjects are identical and only small background details move. At the kernel level, the max abs error against an fp32 reference is 0.016 for both Inductor and FlyDSL on every FLUX.2 shape, checked on rows at both ends of M.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

One gfx1250 device (DPX partition, 96 CUs), FLUX.2-dev, 720p, 50 steps, seed 42, `--enable-torch-compile true --warmup-mode request`, `HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=0`. Baseline and this PR ran back to back on the same GPU; times are the "warmed-up request processed (with warmup excluded)" line.

**End to end**

| Flags | Baseline | This PR | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| default | 47.87 s | 39.50 s | 1.21x |
| `--offload-during-compile false` | 38.96 s | 30.55 s / 30.54 s | 1.28x |

With default flags the real request recompiles the DiT after the warmup (about 6 s on the first step and 3 s in decode), which is unrelated to this PR and shrinks its share of the total.

**Kernel time per transformer forward** (torch profiler, 2 steps x CFG, `--offload-during-compile false`)

| | Baseline | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| GEMM | 327.1 ms | 242.5 ms |
| Attention | 35.9 ms | 36.1 ms |
| Other | 25.0 ms | 25.0 ms |
| Total | 388.0 ms | 303.6 ms |

**GEMM kernels** (standalone, bf16, `triton.testing.do_bench`; Inductor is `torch.compile(F.linear, mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs")`)

| FLUX.2 GEMM | M x N x K | Inductor us (TFLOPS) | FlyDSL us (TFLOPS) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| single-block in-proj | 4112 x 55296 x 6144 | 4114 (679) | 2915 (958) | 1.41x |
| single-block out-proj | 4112 x 6144 x 24576 | 2029 (612) | 1331 (933) | 1.52x |
| double-block FF in (image) | 3600 x 36864 x 6144 | 2515 (648) | 1716 (950) | 1.47x |
| double-block FF out (image) | 3600 x 6144 x 18432 | 1222 (667) | 855 (953) | 1.43x |
| double-block Q/K/V/O (image) | 3600 x 6144 x 6144 | 406 (670) | 305 (892) | 1.33x |
| double-block FF in (text) | 512 x 36864 x 6144 | 334 (695) | 246 (941) | 1.36x |
| double-block Q/K/V/O (text) | 512 x 6144 x 6144 | 86 (447) | 65 (598) | 1.32x |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the PR flow. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`, `/tag-and-rerun-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls to merge.

title: [Fix] dspark: Draw the simulated-acceptance bonus at the simulated row
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` set, DSpark replaces the accepted length with the simulated value `c`. The bonus token, however, stays the one the real accept computed for its own length: the target argmax at the real first-mismatch row, or the rejection-sampled token at the real reject row. That token is committed after `drafts[:c]`, at a position the target never predicted it for. It is also the anchor of the next draft block. The committed text degenerates as a result, and verify batches route to fewer experts than at the same acceptance length under real verification. Simulated-acceptance throughput is therefore overstated.

The only configuration that was correct is `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_GREEDY=1` with temperature-only requests, which has been opt-in since #45433. EAGLE/MTP and DFlash already take the bonus from the target at the forced row.

## Modifications

Under simulation, the bonus is the target's token at verify row `c`, drawn with the request's sampling law.

- `dspark_worker_v2.py`: every sampled batch now passes its sampling info as `simulate_bonus_sampling_info`. Before, only `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_GREEDY=1` with temperature-only batches did. The flag now only selects the greedy draft/accept, under the same eligibility checks as before.
- Sampling-accept region graph (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_SAMPLING_ACCEPT_GRAPH`): it stays eligible under simulation for the same batches as in real serving (all-sampled, temperature-only, no logit adjustments or grammar), so a simulated run keeps the graph that real serving uses.
  - Before the region runs, the worker stages the step's temperatures and seed with `begin_sim_bonus`.
  - Inside the region, the bonus is drawn at row `c` with the epilogue's graph-safe sampler (`sim_bonus`, renamed from `_sim_bonus`), the same kernel `SGLANG_DSPARK_SIMULATE_FOLD` uses.
  - The region's rejection accept still runs, as it does in real serving; under simulation only its length and bonus are replaced.
- `build_accept_outs`: when no sampled bonus is supplied, the bonus is the argmax of row `c`. This covers greedy batches on the eager accept and on the folded greedy accept (`DsparkVerifyEpilogue._accept` without `SGLANG_DSPARK_SIMULATE_FOLD`).
- `sample_simulated_bonus`: top-k/top-p batches sample row `c` from `build_speculative_verify_target_probs`, the target distribution the sampling accept uses. Greedy requests in a mixed batch have top_k=1, so they stay argmax. Temperature-only batches keep the existing Gumbel kernel.
- `static_accept_tail` (Triton kernel and torch reference): the argmax-id bonus is read at the committed length rather than the matched length.
- A sampled simulated bonus is broadcast on the `DSPARK_ACCEPT_SAMPLE` TP sync site, so the `rng` preset keeps ranks consistent.
- `test_dspark_simulated_bonus.py`: the sampling-info stand-in gains `need_top_k_sampling` / `need_top_p_sampling`.

Scope of the sampling law under simulation:
- Temperature and top-k/top-p are applied by the bonus sampler.
- Logit adjustments (penalties, logit bias) and grammar masks are honoured only because they are already in the verify logits when the bonus is drawn: `run_non_compact` / `run_compact` apply the adjustments and the worker applies the grammar mask. The sampler itself does neither.
- Batches with adjustments or grammar never use the region graph.
- min-p is not applied. The non-simulated sampling accept does not apply it either.

Simulated acceptance is a benchmark-only mode.

TP: a sampled bonus is broadcast from rank 0 when the `DSPARK_ACCEPT_SAMPLE` site is enabled. Without it, ranks draw from identical seeds, the same assumption the simulated-length draw and the non-simulated rejection sampler already make.

Non-simulated paths are unchanged. Every new branch is behind `simulated_correct_len is not None`, and the tail kernel's non-simulated length is still `num_correct`.

## Accuracy / correctness

Unit-level checks on GB300 run the real kernels, with drafts rejected at row 0 and simulated `c = 3`:

| path | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| eager accept, greedy batch | bonus = row-0 argmax | row-3 argmax |
| folded greedy accept, eager call and inside a CUDA graph | row-0 argmax | row-3 argmax |
| fused static accept tail (Triton) | row-0 argmax | row-3 argmax |
| top-p bonus distribution (T=0.8, p=0.7), max abs diff vs. the renormalized target, 200k draws | 0.21 | 0.0016 |
| non-simulated fused tail | unchanged | unchanged |
| sampling-accept region under simulation, bs 1/1, 3/3, 3/4 (padded); eager warm-up, capture, replays at fixed seeds | rejection bonus at the real row | equals the eager row-`c` draw; drafts at `[:c]`, bonus at `[c]` |
| region bonus distribution, 6,000 replays (T=0.8), max abs diff vs. softmax(row `c` / T) | 0.65 | 0.0099 |

Existing tests, before and after: `test_dspark_accept_tail.py`, `test_dspark_sampling_accept_graph.py` and `test_dspark_sim_draw_ahead.py` pass. `test_dspark_simulated_bonus.py::test_bf16_full_vocab_low_temperature` fails identically with and without this change on NVIDIA. It is registered for AMD CI only.

End to end: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash FP4, DSpark block 5, TP2 EP2, GB300, AgentX-style agentic traces at 32 concurrent, temperature 1, `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.51` (match-expected). The committed text is re-tokenized; about 1,500 turns are shared across runs.

| | real acceptance | simulated, before | simulated, after |
|---|---|---|---|
| token equal to one of the previous 6 | 0.070 | 0.375 | 0.145 |
| 4-gram already seen in the response | 0.282 | 0.387 | 0.197 |
| share of the most frequent token | 0.042 | 0.170 | 0.083 |
| distinct experts per MoE layer, B=4 / 5 / 8 / 10 | 75.0 / 84.9 / 116.2 / 123.9 | 53.9 / 62.7 / 85.0 / 94.9 | 71.8 / 85.3 / 108.3 / 121.9 |

After the fix, the remaining difference from real acceptance is in the drafted tokens. Simulation accepts them unconditionally, so repeats 2-3 tokens apart rise from 0.027 to 0.096 of tokens. Immediate repeats (0.0008 vs 0.0024) and repeats 4-6 tokens apart match real acceptance. An independent simulated-acceptance implementation that commits the target's token at the forced position measures the same statistics on this workload (0.148 / 0.182 / 0.087).

## Benchmarking and Profiling

The size of the change depends on the point: it is largest where MoE is a big share of the step and the degenerate text cut the distinct experts the most.

**TP2 EP2, 32 concurrent** (the end-to-end setup above), 3600 s:

| | total tok/s/GPU | output tok/s/GPU | ITL p50 / p90 (ms) | interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s, 1000/ITL) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| simulated, before | 122.2K | 697 | 3.43 / 4.40 | 291.5 / 227.3 |
| simulated, after | 118.9K | 683 | 3.85 / 4.92 | 259.7 / 203.3 |

Both runs measure AL 3.51. The "after" run is 2.7% lower in total throughput and 11% lower in p90 interactivity (11% higher p90 ITL). This is expected: the "before" run's degenerate text made MoE about 1 ms/step cheaper at B=4-10. Each number is a single run, on different nodes. These two runs applied the same change to an earlier nightly and use the eager accept (no sampling-accept graph).

**TP4 EP1, 1 concurrent, NVIDIA megakernel**, `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_SAMPLING_ACCEPT_GRAPH=1`, `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.51`, same traces, 1800 s, AL 3.51 in every run. At batch 1 with the experts sharded across four GPUs, MoE is a small share of the step, so the change costs about 1%. This table also shows why the sampling-accept region change is needed:

| | region graph replays | interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s, 1000/ITL) |
|---|---|---|
| this PR | ~110k per rank | 976 / 949 |
| this PR without the region change (sampled simulated steps fall back to the eager accept) | 0 | 939 / 863 |
| before this PR (region graph with the misplaced bonus), 3600 s | captured | 987 / 954 |

Keeping the region in the graph is worth 4% / 10% at p50 / p90. The remaining ~1% to "before" is within what the text change and the shorter run can explain.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Existing unit tests updated; no new test file (verified on GPU as above).

title: [Perf] diffusion: HunyuanImage-3 prefix K/V cache, opt-in FA3 attention and think-prompt support
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
## Motivation

Depends on #46600 (the CUDA MoE noise fix, which fixes #46461). This PR will be rebased on it once it lands, so the fix commit below will drop out of the diff.

Changes for HunyuanImage-3 (the prefix K/V cache is the main one; the opt-in FA3 attention and the `cot_text` fix are described under Modifications):

1. **Fix: generation on CUDA produced a noise texture** (on main too). The MoE block ran the routed experts before the shared MLP. On CUDA the Triton `FusedMoE` path runs in place (`inplace=True` by default) and overwrites `hidden_states` with the expert output, so the shared MLP read the expert output instead of the layer input and every MoE layer was wrong. The NPU path (AscendTPDispatcher) is not in place, which is likely why the original NPU validation in #36311 did not see it; the cookbook also marks the CUDA recipe as unverified. srt's own Hunyuan model already runs the shared MLP first.
2. **Perf: cache the text prefix K/V across denoising steps.** HunyuanImage-3 recomputes the whole text prefix through every layer (attention and MoE) on every step, even though that prefix never changes. The proposal this implements:

> **P1. Prefix KV cache** (`hunyuan_image3.py`: `ImageKVCacheManager`, `forward_block`)
> The text prefix is causal and step-invariant. At `first_step`, keep the per-layer prefix K/V; on later steps feed only the image tokens as queries and attend to [cached prefix K/V, image K/V]. Replace the dense 4-D bool-mask SDPA with FA varlen (prefix causal + image full) or flex.
> Removes L_text/(L_text+L_img) of the MoE compute per step. Large for long or "think" prompts; also recovers FlashAttention.

This PR does the prefix K/V cache with the dense SDPA as the default, plus the FA varlen part as an opt-in (`--attention-backend fa3`), since FA3 is not bitwise equal to SDPA. The official model does the same caching at inference (later steps feed only the timestep and image tokens against a static KV cache).

## Modifications

**Fix (commit 2)**
- `hunyuan_image3.py`: `HunYuanSparseMoeBlock.forward` runs the shared MLP before the in-place experts.
- `pipelines/hunyuan_image3.py`: match the official `FlowMatchDiscreteScheduler` schedule, `shift(linspace(1, 0, N + 1))[:-1]` (`use_uniform_sigmas=True`). The old setup shifted the training-sigma range a second time; for 10 steps the last timestep was 8.93 instead of 250.

**Prefix K/V cache (commit 1)**
- `hunyuan_image3_utils.py`: `ImageKVCacheManager` stores each layer's prefix K/V on step 0, keyed by a cache slot, and on later steps prepends it to the suffix K/V. Adds `split_suffix_inputs` and `pad_prefix_rows`.
- `hunyuan_image3.py`: `forward_block` takes `prefix_len` and `cache_slot`. Step 0 runs the full sequence; later steps run only the suffix rows and pad the output back to full length, so callers see the same shape.
- `ar_stage.py`: computes the prefix once as the rows before the first noisy-image or timestep token, and returns no prefix (full compute) when a clean image block straddles that boundary. `first_step` is now `step_idx == 0` (it was always `True`, and nothing read it). CFG cond and uncond use separate cache slots, since they run as two backbone calls on the same modules.
- Falls back to the current path when CLA is on, when the cache-dit adapter drives the blocks, or when no safe prefix exists.

Why the cache is exact: the mask is causal, so every row before the first varying token only sees prompt and clean conditioning tokens. Clean conditioning images before the noisy block are cached too, so the saving is a bit larger than L_text/(L_text+L_img).

Memory cost of the cache: `bs x P x kv_heads x head_dim x 4 bytes` per layer per CFG slot. Measured 156 MB per GPU for a 1,248-token prefix with both CFG slots (exactly the formula); the reported peak is unchanged.

**Opt-in FA3 segment attention (`--attention-backend fa3`)**
- `hunyuan_image3_utils.py`: `build_attention_segments` splits the mask (causal text, bidirectional image blocks) into `(start, end, causal)` segments; `segmented_attention` runs one FA3 varlen call per segment with bottom-right causal alignment, for both full and cached-suffix steps. GQA is native, so no `repeat_kv`. Hopper only; elsewhere the masked SDPA path is kept.
- `ar_stage.py` / `pipelines/hunyuan_image3.py`: segments are built only when `attention_backend == "fa"` (what `fa3`/`fa4` resolve to). The default path is unchanged and still bitwise identical to main + fix.
- 2x H200: 22.6 s vs 26.8 s for the default path (1.55x vs main + fix). Not bitwise: PSNR 21-24 dB vs SDPA, same composition. On GPU the segments reproduce the attention mask exactly over 384 calls and FA3 vs SDPA differs by at most one bf16 ulp per call, so the drift is kernel rounding compounding over layers and steps. Details and images: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46454#issuecomment-6422227024

**Fix: `cot_text` from the image API**
- `configs/sample/hunyuan_image3.py`: declare `bot_task`, `system_prompt` and `cot_text` in `image_request_extra_fields`. The image endpoint only forwards declared fields, so think/recaption text was silently dropped. With it, think prompts are 1.32x to 1.50x faster than main + fix (the reasoning text lands in the cached prefix), outputs identical: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46454#issuecomment-6422648092

## How the noise bug was found

On 2x H200 TP2 with debug-only instrumentation (not in this PR):
- Checked the port line by line against the official `modeling_hunyuan_image_3.py` and `hunyuan_image_3_pipeline.py` shipped with the checkpoint. 2D RoPE, QKV split, QK norm order, SwiGLU half order, residual flow, UNetDown/UNetUp, timestep embedders, CFG, Euler step and VAE decode all match.
- Compared real decoder layers at step 0 against an fp32 reference transcribed from the official layer, with weights read straight from the checkpoint shards:

| layer | attention cos / rel err | MoE cos / rel err |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.99999 / 0.004 | 0.738 / 0.94 |
| 1 | 0.99999 / 0.005 | 0.608 / 0.80 |
| 31 | 0.99999 / 0.003 | 0.166 / 1.02 |

- Inside the MoE everything feeding the kernel was correct: router logits matched exactly, top-k ids agreed 100%, and every expert `w13`/`w2` shard and the shared MLP weights matched the checkpoint slices. That left execution order, and `FusedMoE` turned out to be in place.

## Accuracy Tests

CPU unit tests in `test_hunyuan_image3_tp_broadcast.py`, all 11 in the file pass:
- Fix regressions: the shared MLP sees the layer input when the experts run in place; timesteps follow the official schedule. With only the two fixed source files reverted, exactly these two fail.
- Prefix cache: a cached suffix-only step matches full recompute; CFG slots do not overwrite each other; the prefix ends at the first varying token and is `None` when a clean image block straddles it.
- FA3 segments: segment attention equals masked SDPA for full and suffix-only steps; overlapping blocks fall back.
- Image API: `cot_text` and `bot_task` reach the sampling params.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

main + the fix vs this PR (prefix cache + fix), 2x H200 TP2 per the cookbook recipe, 1024x1024, 50 steps, guidance 2.5, seed 42. One warmup then one timed request per prompt.

| | main + fix | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| short prompt, request | 34.97 s | 27.42 s | -21.6% (1.28x) |
| short prompt, AR/denoise stage | 34.19 s | 26.68 s | -22.0% |
| long prompt, request | 35.84 s | 27.49 s | -23.3% (1.30x) |
| long prompt, AR/denoise stage | 35.04 s | 26.75 s | -23.7% |
| peak memory (server log) | 106,318 MB | 106,318 MB | no change |
| output vs main + fix | | byte-identical on both prompts | PSNR inf |

Images and notes are in the results comment. Earlier numbers and the noise-texture images in older comments were taken before the fix and should be ignored.

## Checklist

- [x] Format with pre-commit hooks (ruff F401/F821/F823/UP037, ruff-format)
- [x] Unit tests added (fix regressions + prefix cache)
- [x] GPU time / memory / parity on the fixed code
- [ ] Docs / cookbook update (the CUDA recipe could move from unverified once the numbers are in)

title: [Perf] paged-experts: exact size pinning
author: N3mezis
body:
# [Perf] paged-experts: exact size pinning

## Motivation

This PR aims to decrease memory footprint.

Currently, the Paged Experts Feature (#42557) keeps every expert of the model in page-locked host memory. torch's pinned allocator rounds each allocation up to a power of two, so **a 402 MB `w13` tensor pins 512 MiB**. Across a model this pins about a third more than the experts need on Qwen3-30B-A3B, and 85% more on gpt-oss-20b. Pinned memory cannot be swapped, and it is often what decides whether a model fits: WSL2, for example, caps it at about half of RAM.

## Modifications

`store.py`:
- The pinned host store allocates through HiCache's host allocator (`alloc_with_host_register` with `HostTensorAllocator`). That maps exactly the tensor's size (huge pages with `SGLANG_HUGEPAGE_SIZE`), pre-faults it and registers it with CUDA.
- The gather kernel reads it through `cudaHostGetDevicePointer` as before.
- A store only staged for a repack stays pageable, as before.

## Accuracy Tests

The experts' bytes are unchanged; only their allocation differs.

**Kernel test.** The store pins exactly its size, and the gather kernel reads it.

**Paged vs unpaged, 4-layer test models** (E=32, top-4, K=8; prompt and greedy decode logprobs; RTX 5070 Ti; main 2d3de82633 and this PR in one run):

| model | runner | this PR | main |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-MoE bf16 | triton | identical | identical |
| AWQ int4 | Marlin | decode max 0.014 | decode max 0.014 |
| compressed-tensors NVFP4 | Marlin | median max 0.078, unpaged floor 0.059 | median max 0.059, unpaged floor 0.063 |

Marlin is not run-to-run reproducible, so the Marlin formats are judged against the spread of two unpaged servers (the floor); bf16 on triton is bit-identical. Each check has a negative control that must fail (a perturbed RMSNorm eps on bf16 and AWQ, unnormalized top-k weights on NVFP4), and all three do.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same machine as #42557: RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB (PCIe 5.0 x16, 62 GB RAM), Qwen3-30B-A3B, 10,240 KV tokens and 4 slots, prefix caching off, 16 ShareGPT warm-up requests discarded. Decode tok/s is `1000 / median TPOT` over 8 ShareGPT prompts sent one at a time (256 output tokens each); TTFT and ITL are from the same requests. 4 requests: 16 ShareGPT prompts from 4 clients at once (output tok/s). 2k TTFT: 4 natural ~2,048-token prompts. main (upstream 2d3de82633) is measured first and last in the same run as this PR; both values are shown, and a difference inside their spread is no difference. Pinned host memory is `Shmem` in `/proc/meminfo` once serving (the new allocator maps the store shared; torch's pinned allocator counted there too).

| config | pinned host memory | weight load | decode tok/s | TTFT p50 / p99 | 4 requests: out tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| int4, K=92: main | 18.6 GiB | 37.1 / 45.2 s | 211.8 / 212.8 | 51 / 88, 50 / 82 ms | 400 / 401 |
| int4, K=92: this PR | **13.9 GiB** (−25%) | 37.7 s | 212.0 | 50 / 87 ms | 398 |
| FP8, K=40: main | 36.0 GiB | 48.7 / 48.3 s | 90.3 / 90.3 | 213 / 301, 218 / 301 ms | 100 / 99 |
| FP8, K=40: this PR | **27.0 GiB** (−25%) | 54.7 s | 90.3 | 213 / 301 ms | 100 |
| NVFP4 (Marlin), K=85: main | 20.3 GiB | 45.2 / 44.9 s | 189.8 / 192.9 | 72 / 119, 73 / 116 ms | 352 / 349 |
| NVFP4 (Marlin), K=85: this PR | **15.2 GiB** (−25%) | 45.4 s | 190.3 | 72 / 121 ms | 351 |

Decode, TTFT and throughput are unchanged; the store pins a quarter less on all three formats (power-of-two rounding cost a third more than the experts need). Pre-faulting the exact-size mapping adds about 6 s to FP8's weight load (27 GiB of store); the 45.2 s is one slow boot of main.


## CI

The kernel test checks that the store pins exactly its size and that the gather reads it.

title: [Perf] paged-experts: fuse slot lookup into decide
author: N3mezis
body:
# [Perf] paged-experts: fuse slot lookup into decide

## Motivation

This PR aims to increase decode tok/s.

Currently, Paged Experts (#42557) runs 21 graph nodes per paged MoE layer in captured decode. 11 of them are small torch ops that turn the decide kernel's result into the runner's inputs: index the slot of each routed entry, mask padding, mask its weight. On Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 at batch size 1 they take 0.44 ms per step, about 9% of decode.

The decide kernel already knows each routed expert's slot when its eviction loop ends. This PR has it write the runner's inputs directly: the slot and router weight of each routed entry, with slot 0 and weight 0 for padding. The layer's paged part of the graph is then decide plus gather, **10 nodes instead of 21**, and the runner reads its inputs straight from the decide kernel's output.

## Modifications

`paged_experts.cuh`, `paged_experts.py`, `executor.py`:
- After its eviction loop, the decide kernel also writes each routed entry's slot and router weight. Padding entries, and ids outside `[0, E)`, get slot 0 and weight 0.
- The device executor passes these straight to the base method. A paged layer's part of the captured step is now decide plus gather: 10 nodes instead of 21.
- Router weights are passed to the kernel as float32. If they come in another dtype, they are converted back, which is exact.
- `paged_experts_decide` gains `topk_weights`, `run_ids` and `run_w`; it has no other callers. The host-planned (eager) path is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

**Kernel test.** Over 200 random routing steps with padding, the decide kernel's runner inputs equal the reference: each entry's slot from the LRU reference, and its weight, with 0 for padding. Ids outside `[0, E)` count as padding.

**Paged vs unpaged, 4-layer test models** (E=32, top-4, K=8; prompt and greedy decode logprobs; RTX 5070 Ti; main 2d3de82633 and this PR in one run):

| model | runner | this PR | main |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-MoE bf16 | triton | identical | identical |
| AWQ int4 | Marlin | decode max 0.014 | decode max 0.014 |
| compressed-tensors NVFP4 | Marlin | median max 0.076, unpaged floor 0.055 | median max 0.059, unpaged floor 0.063 |

Marlin is not run-to-run reproducible, so the Marlin formats are judged against the spread of two unpaged servers (the floor); bf16 on triton is bit-identical. Each check has a negative control that must fail (a perturbed RMSNorm eps on bf16 and AWQ, unnormalized top-k weights on NVFP4), and all three do.

**GSM8K (200 questions), Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4, K=92:** main 0.950 / 0.935, this PR 0.945.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same machine as #42557: RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB (PCIe 5.0 x16, 62 GB RAM), Qwen3-30B-A3B, 10,240 KV tokens and 4 slots, prefix caching off, 16 ShareGPT warm-up requests discarded. Decode tok/s is `1000 / median TPOT` over 8 ShareGPT prompts sent one at a time (256 output tokens each); TTFT and ITL are from the same requests. 4 requests: 16 ShareGPT prompts from 4 clients at once (output tok/s). 2k TTFT: 4 natural ~2,048-token prompts. main (upstream 2d3de82633) is measured first and last in the same run as this PR; both values are shown, and a difference inside their spread is no difference.

| config | decode tok/s | TTFT p50 / p99 | ITL p50 / p99 | 4 requests: out tok/s | 2k TTFT p50 | peak VRAM |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| int4, K=92: main | 211.8 / 212.8 | 51 / 88, 50 / 82 ms | 4.70 / 5.35, 4.70 / 5.30 ms | 400 / 401 | 247 / 239 ms | 14.7 GiB |
| int4, K=92: this PR | **234.1** (+10.3%) | 50 / 82 ms | **4.27 / 4.90 ms** | **418** (+4.2%) | 248 ms | 14.7 GiB |
| FP8, K=40: main | 90.3 / 90.3 | 213 / 301, 218 / 301 ms | 10.51 / 20.74, 10.51 / 20.76 ms | 100 / 99 | 427 / 424 ms | 13.4 GiB |
| FP8, K=40: this PR | **94.2** (+4.3%) | 219 / 300 ms | **10.04 / 20.26 ms** | 101 | 425 ms | 13.4 GiB |
| NVFP4 (Marlin), K=85: main | 189.8 / 192.9 | 72 / 119, 73 / 116 ms | 5.20 / 6.44, 5.11 / 6.32 ms | 352 / 349 | 248 / 244 ms | 14.5 GiB |
| NVFP4 (Marlin), K=85: this PR | **208.0** (+8.7%) | 76 / 117 ms | **4.76 / 6.12 ms** | **370** (+5.5%) | 248 ms | 14.5 GiB |

Percentages against the mean of the two main runs. The saving is a fixed ~0.42–0.46 ms per captured step (int4 4.71 → 4.27 ms, FP8 11.08 → 10.62 ms, NVFP4 5.23 → 4.81 ms), so it shows most where steps are short. Prefill runs host-planned and is unchanged.


## CI

The kernel test checks the decide kernel's runner inputs against the reference, and treats ids outside the experts as padding. `test_paged_experts.py` already runs captured paged decode end to end on GPTQ, FP8 and gpt-oss MXFP4.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] kimi-k3: FP32 warp split-K GEMM for the MoE front projection on SM107
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

Kimi-K3's merged MoE front projection (`(N, K) = (6016, 7168)`, FP32 output so the router logits keep their precision) runs through TGV at the spec-verify batch sizes. On SM107 a warp split-K design with cp.async ring loads is faster at `M = 8, 16, 32`.

## Modifications

- `dense_bf16_gemm_warp_splitk.py` (new, **temporary copy**): FlashInfer already ships this kernel as `flashinfer/gemm/kernels/dense_bf16_gemm_warp_splitk.py` (`run_warp_splitk_dense`, also behind `flashinfer.gemm.bf16_gemm_sm100` with the cute-dsl runners), but its input validation only accepts a bf16 `out`, in 0.7.2.post1 and on main. K3's merged front projection needs FP32 output to keep router-logit precision, so this copy differs from FlashInfer's file by 71 lines, essentially `out.dtype in (bf16, fp32)` and keying the compile cache on the output dtype. Plan: land FP32 output in FlashInfer, then delete this module and call FlashInfer's kernel from the dispatch below (the file header and the dispatch carry that note).
- `cutedsl_bf16_gemm.py`: dispatch it (with pinned tactics for M = 8, 16, 32) only on SM107 for the exact `(6016, 7168)` shape at `M in {8, 16, 32}` with FP32 output and no bias; every other case keeps the existing dispatch.
- `test_cutedsl_bf16_gemm.py`: SM107-only test comparing against `torch.mm` in FP32 and checking the router top-16 selection is unchanged (skipped elsewhere).

## Accuracy Tests

Max abs error against PyTorch FP32 output 0.001221 (tolerance 0.005); router top-16 sets match on every row. `test_cutedsl_bf16_gemm.py` on SM107 with this branch: 462 passed (including the three new M cases).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

One SM107 GPU, BF16 inputs, FP32 output, eight rotated weights, 41 interleaved CUDA-graph samples, median us per GEMM:

| M | TGV (current) | warp split-K | reduction |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | 9.400 | 7.604 | 19.1% |
| 16 | 10.704 | 7.944 | 25.8% |
| 32 | 10.820 | 9.212 | 14.9% |

92 front GEMMs per verify step; the M=8 delta projects to about 0.165 ms per step.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] kda: Narrower V tiles for the KDA spec-verify recurrence on SM107
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

`fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_kernel` is the KDA recurrence in every Kimi-K3 KDA layer and sits on the spec-verify critical path. Its launch is `grid = (V / 32, 1, heads)` with one warp per CTA: at TP8 (12 heads per rank) that is 48 single-warp CTAs, each walking the draft tokens serially over a 128x32 state slice, on a 212-SM part. Most of the GPU is idle.

## Modifications

`fused_sigmoid_gating_recurrent.py`: in `_select_recurrent_launch_config`, the KDA verify call on SM107 picks BV=4 with one warp (384 CTAs at TP8). Every other case keeps its current launch: other architectures, KDA decode, GDN.

## Accuracy Tests

Each V column of the state updates independently, so a narrower tile computes the same recurrence. Output matches the BV=32 launch exactly; the ReplaySSM ring and state match within bf16 rounding (max abs diff 1.2e-4). KDA tests on SM107 with the new tile active: `test_kda_replayssm_ring_fused.py`, `test_fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py`, `test_kda_kernels.py`. title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] kimi-k3: Route draft/dense bf16 GEMMs to TGV and narrow the MLA output gate vector
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

A per-kernel comparison of Kimi-K3 NVFP4 target verify (bs=1, 8 tokens, TP8 per-rank shapes) found three small-M bf16 GEMMs still on cuBLAS where TGV is faster, and an MLA output gate launch with too few CTAs for its `[8, 12, 128]` tile.

## Modifications

- `cutedsl_bf16_gemm.py`: add `(7168, 1792)` DSpark draft down, `(7168, 512)` draft o_proj and `(8448, 7168)` dense gate_up to `_K3_TGV_WIN_SHAPES`. The table only applies at M <= 8, so this affects decode and verify.
- `mla_output_gate.cuh`: 4 bf16 per thread instead of 8, doubling the CTA count. Output is bit-exact.

## Accuracy Tests

- `mla_output_gate`: bit-exact against the torch reference for T in {1, 2, 5, 8, 16, 128, 1024}.
- TGV vs cuBLAS on the three shapes: identical output (max abs diff 0.0).
- On this branch: `test_mla_output_gate.py` OK and `test_cutedsl_bf16_gemm.py` 462 passed on both SM107 and GB300 (SM103).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

CUDA-graph us per call with cold weights (rotated past L2). M=7 for the draft shapes, M=8 otherwise.

| op | SM100 before | SM100 after | SM107 before | SM107 after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| draft down_proj 7168x1792 | 5.64 | 4.77 | 6.23 | 3.90 |
| draft o_proj 7168x512 | 3.07 | 2.53 | 3.00 | 1.92 |
| dense gate_up 8448x7168 | 19.47 | 18.95 | 14.07 | 13.70 |
| mla_output_gate | 1.29 | 1.07 | 1.28 | 1.02 |

About 25 us per decode step in total; end to end it is within run-to-run noise (SM107 TP8, bs=1, 8k in / 1k out: 645.6 vs 647.7 / 651.7 tok/s single runs), with the trace confirming the new kernel selection.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to pre-commit.
- [ ] Add unit tests (existing `test_mla_output_gate.py` and `test_cutedsl_bf16_gemm.py` cover both changes).
- [ ] Update documentation.

title: [Perf] diffusion/worker: Move cyclic GC out of request execution
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

FLUX.2 Klein's first-request regression surfaced in #45919 but reproduces without its progress-reporting changes. A GC-instrumented H100 run captured a **449.5 ms generation-2 collection inside denoising**. The CI bisection identified #46047 as the conditional trigger, not a Klein kernel regression.

This PR collects at initialization/warmup boundaries and prevents automatic cyclic GC from interrupting protected worker execution. With server warmup the extra cleanup is paid before readiness; with request-based warmup the first caller pays it. It does not modify #45919, performance thresholds, or GT.

## Changes

- Collect after worker initialization and the final warmup, including compile prewarms. Handle request-based warmup, sequential outputs, and recoverable warmup failures.
- Share a thread-safe GC guard across model forward, deferred finalization, and output replies. Nested/overlapping execution restores the original GC state only after the last owner exits, including exceptions and forked children.
- With async output saving, drain continuous overlapping finalizers at an admission boundary after 30 seconds without a GC opportunity. Preserve ordinary overlap otherwise.
- Document the behavior and tradeoffs; extend existing worker, async-output, and OOM tests.

Reference counting and explicit `gc.collect()` still work. There is no `gc.freeze()`, threshold change, new CLI flag, or GPU allocator flush. GC can still run outside protected regions. Cyclic garbage may survive until a request finishes; the 30-second rule bounds continuous overlap, not a single long request. The drain can reduce overlap at that boundary.

## Validation

- Merged `main` (`fd5c52588ff`) at `3f4a75b2809`, retaining #45919's progress reporter alongside the GC guard. The only conflict was the import block.
- Merged head: **195 passed, 14 subtests passed, 1 skipped** on an isolated H200 devbox, including video-progress/health tests. The skipped test requires two CUDA devices.
- [H100 validation before the main merge](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40264698646): **143 passed**, including single-GPU Klein and two-GPU Z-Image E2E with existing performance, memory and consistency checks. [Merged-head validation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40265366878) is dispatched.
- Pre-commit and `git diff --check` pass.
- Same H200, Python 3.12.15, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, FLUX.2-klein-4B, 1024x1024, four steps, seed 42, `quality=exact`, server warmup, no torch.compile. Both arms use identical GC callback instrumentation and the same editable environment.

The comparison below isolates the new request guard from the **already-present startup collection** (`a8b84ce6`). The fixed measurement uses `264d0863`; the subsequent commit only fixes sequential warmup handling and its tests.

| 80 HTTP requests per concurrency | Startup-only | Request protection |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Concurrency 1 throughput, req/s | 3.110 | 3.118 |
| Concurrency 1 P99, ms | 324.95 | 323.18 |
| Concurrency 4 throughput, req/s | 3.139 | 3.144 |
| Concurrency 4 P99, ms | 1280.86 | 1277.39 |
| GC collections inside forward, including warmup | 45 | 0 |

Outputs are byte-identical. The throughput differences are below 0.3% and are **not evidence of a meaningful steady-state speedup**. The direct result is removal of GC from the protected path, not faster GPU kernels.

With async output saving, a further **600 requests per arm** at concurrency 4 give 3.158 vs 3.165 req/s. Forward GC, including warmup, drops from 38 to 0. Peak reported GPU memory is 12,996 MiB in both arms; sampled whole-device usage is 14,789 MiB in both. Between the first and sixth 100-request batches, aggregate worker RSS grows by only 0.24/0.27 MiB. These are several-minute tests, not a production-duration leak proof.

Request-based and disabled warmup also pass real HTTP generation with unchanged output hashes and zero observed forward GC.

Z-Image-Turbo, 1024x1024, nine steps, 20 prompts at each concurrency, explicitly `--component-residency all=resident`: current main `fd5c52588ff` vs merged head `3f4a75b2809` gives **1.087/1.087 req/s** at concurrency 1 and **1.112/1.112 req/s** at concurrency 4. P99 is 923.70/926.37 ms and 3613.48/3607.57 ms, respectively. Per-request hashes match, and both report 23,714 MiB peak GPU memory (25,493 MiB sampled whole-device usage). Forward GC including warmup drops from 34 to 0; the main trace includes a full collection. This is neutral steady-state performance, not a speedup.

The initial Z-Image auto-placement comparison is excluded from performance claims: downloading its metadata changed TE offload to resident. Explicit placement removes that confound.

## Original Regression Evidence

- [Regressed H100 + GC tracing](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40255099684/job/121355196163): denoise 545.7 ms, including a 449.5 ms full GC.
- [Startup fix + GC tracing](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40255589952/job/121356680453): denoise 228.1 ms, no full GC during the request.
- [Startup-only final validation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40256202833/job/121358559241): three fresh-server requests passed unchanged performance, VRAM, and consistency checks, E2E 374.72 / 377.02 / 445.03 ms. GPU reserved/allocated peaks remained 13,620/10,791 MiB, with byte-identical JPEGs.

The historical H100 tracing runs used separate runners with six ancillary package-version differences. They identify the GC stall, but are not a perfectly controlled same-host throughput comparison. The newer H200 comparison above uses one isolated device and unchanged packages.
