title: [Refactor] attention: Route every FlashAttention call through the selected kernel
author: AgainstEntropy
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

`FlashAttentionBackend.__init__` selects a FlashAttention build (FA3, generic FA4, or the SM12x FA4 entry points added in #32991) and binds it to `self.flash_attn_varlen_func` / `self.flash_attn_with_kvcache`. Only one call site uses that binding: the `fa_skip_kv_cache` varlen call (#33007). The other 14 call sites go through the module-level wrapper `sglang.kernels.ops.attention.flash_attention`, passing `ver=self.fa_impl_ver`. That wrapper has no SM12x branch, which causes two problems:

- On SM12x with FA4, the entry points `__init__` selects run on one path, and the generic FA4 entry points run everywhere else. One consequence: the static `max_seqlen_k` that the SM12x runtime policy sets for CUDA-graph decode is dropped before it reaches the paged-decode fast path.
- A subclass that needs a different FA build, such as a vendor backend, has to replace both the `__init__` binding and every module-level call. There is no single seam.

What a single dispatch buys:

- **What `__init__` selects is what runs.** The kernel choice lives in one assignment, so a build-specific feature (the SM12x entry points, their runtime policy, any future build) reaches every call site, not only the one that happens to read `self.*`.
- **One override point for other FA builds.** #45946 (SAIL FA3 / FlashMLA) is a live example. To swap the FA build today, it extracts the binding into `_init_flash_attention_functions` and overrides it, and it also adds `_call_flash_attn_with_kvcache` / `_call_flash_attn_varlen_func` methods and rewrites every call site to go through them, because those call sites ignore the binding. On top of this PR, overriding the binding is enough: the `_call_*` methods and the call-site rewrites can go, along with the function-local import they run on every CUDA call. The FA part of that PR's base-class diff shrinks to the method extraction.
- **No `ver=` to thread through each call**, and the new guard test keeps the backend from drifting back to two paths, which is how it got here (see below).

### History

The backend used to have a single dispatch. #22028 bound `self.flash_attn_*` in `__init__` and aliased them at the top of each forward. Four days later, #20796 replaced those aliases with the module-level wrapper plus `ver=`, so it could route FA3 through the kernels-community loader. That left the `__init__` binding unused. #32991 added the SM12x choice to that binding, and #33007 reconnected one call site. #33426 unified the dispatch again, but it was reverted in #39405 for process reasons (merged before review and CI completed) and never resubmitted.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Every FA call in `flashattention_backend.py` goes through `self.flash_attn_*`. The per-call `ver=` and the module-level wrapper import are removed.
- For FA3, `__init__` now binds `sglang.kernels.ops.attention.flash_attention_v3`, which is the build the wrapper already dispatched to for `ver=3`. `fa_skip_kv_cache` on FA3 used to call `sgl_kernel.flash_attn` directly; it now follows `SGLANG_USE_SGL_FA3_KERNEL` like every other path. The default (`1`) still loads the `sgl_kernel` build. `get_scheduler_metadata` still comes from `sgl_kernel`.
- `flash_attention_v4_sm120.flash_attn_varlen_func` / `flash_attn_with_kvcache` accept and forward `mask_mod`. Previously their `**_` swallowed it, which would drop FA4 image masks on SM12x now that those paths route there. A call with `mask_mod` skips the cached paged-decode fast path.
- New `test_flashattention_kernel_dispatch.py`, a CPU test: it fails if any FA call in the backend uses a name other than `self.flash_attn_*`. Verified to fail on `main` and pass here.

Behavior by configuration:

| Configuration | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| FA3 | wrapper(`ver=3`) -> `flash_attention_v3`; `fa_skip` -> `sgl_kernel.flash_attn` | `flash_attention_v3` everywhere (same kernel by default) |
| FA4, not SM12x | wrapper(`ver=4`) -> `flash_attention_v4`; `fa_skip` -> `flash_attention_v4` | `flash_attention_v4` everywhere; kwargs the wrapper filtered out land in its `**_` |
| FA4, SM12x | 14 sites -> generic `flash_attention_v4`; `fa_skip` -> `flash_attention_v4_sm120` | `flash_attention_v4_sm120` everywhere, with `max_seqlen_k` and `mask_mod` reaching it |

Out of scope: `dots_hybrid_backend.py` and `minicpm/attention_adapter.py` still call the module-level wrapper with their FA backend's `fa_impl_ver`.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

A/B tests ran this branch and its merge base (`d4939cc267`) side by side on two GPUs of the same host, with identical server flags. GSM8K used sgl-eval 0.1.3, 200 examples, temperature 0, max_tokens 1024. For Qwen2.5 the prompt was Qwen's own math prompt ("Please reason step by step, and put your final answer within \boxed{}"), because the default GSM8K prompt makes it answer with a bare `\boxed{}`. DeepSeek-V2-Lite used the default prompt.

**H200 (SM90)**

| Model / path | Flags | branch | main |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, GSM8K | `--attention-backend fa3` | 91.5 | 92.0 |
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, GSM8K | `--attention-backend fa4` | 90.5 | 91.0 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (MLA), GSM8K | `--attention-backend fa3 --trust-remote-code` | 60.5 | 58.0 |
| gte-Qwen2-1.5B-instruct, `fa_skip_kv_cache` | `--is-embedding --attention-backend fa3 --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size -1` | cosine(branch, main) min 0.9999998 | |
| gte-Qwen2-1.5B-instruct, `fa_skip_kv_cache` | same, `--attention-backend fa4` | cosine(branch, main) min 1.0000000 | |

Unit tests:
dense `test_fa3.py` and `test_fa4.py`, `test_flashattention_return_lse.py`, `test_flashattention_paged_mha.py`, `test_flashattention_graph_metadata.py`, `test_flashattention_pa_swa_prefill_lens_size.py`, `test_verify_widening_is_wired.py`, dense `test_tbo.py`. Result: 38 passed, 0 skipped.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

No kernel changes.

title: [CI] [AMD] install: Cache the AOT kernel wheel and stop wiping venv bytecode
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## What

Two cuts to the setup that every AMD CI job runs in `amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` before its first test:

| Change | Per job | Expected per week |
|---|---|---|
| Cache the AOT kernel (`sglang-kernel`) wheel on the runner's persistent `/sgl-data` volume | ~30 s build → wheel install on a cache hit | ~350 runner-h (~830 GPU-h) |
| Stop deleting every `.pyc` under `/opt/venv` | ~6 s | ~70 runner-h |

"Per week" assumes the ~41,900 AMD GPU jobs measured in the week of Oct 19–26 and a high hit rate. The real hit rate depends on how often `kernels/aot` and the CI image change. It will be measured after merge.

## Why

The install step takes ~2.3 of the ~2.5 min of per-job setup:
- 30 s of it compiles `python/sglang/kernels/aot` from source with `setup_rocm.py install`, in every job, although that tree rarely changes.
- Another ~6 s is `find /opt/venv -name "*.pyc" -delete` and the `__pycache__` cleanup. The `pip uninstall` calls just before it already remove the old sglang files, so the walk only throws away torch's bytecode, which every job then recompiles on first import.

## Notes for the reviewer

- **Cache key:** the git tree hash of `python/sglang/kernels/aot`, the container's image ID, and the image's GPU arch. Those are the only inputs to the build: `setup_rocm.py` reads nothing outside that directory, and the image fixes torch, HIP and Python.
  - A dirty tree, as in local runs, or a missing key builds without caching.
  - A host without the `/sgl-data` mount gets a container-local cache, so it just misses every time, same as today.
- **Build method:** the build switches from `setup_rocm.py install` (an egg plus `easy-install.pth`) to `setup_rocm.py bdist_wheel` and `pip install --no-deps --force-reinstall`, so a cached build and a fresh one install the same way. Nothing else in the AMD scripts reads the egg or `kernels/aot/dist`.
- **Concurrency and cleanup:** jobs on one host can build the same key at once, so each builds into a temp dir and publishes with `mv -T`; the loser drops its copy. Entries not used for 7 days are pruned, and a hit refreshes the entry's mtime.
- **Bytecode:** clearing `__pycache__` in the checkout is kept.

## Test plan

- [x] `pr-test-amd.yml` dispatch on rocm10 ([run 40430315918](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40430315918)):
  - The install step took 128–133 s on a cache miss, against ~136 s before this change; that difference is the bytecode wipe. On a cache hit it took **97–99 s**. 4 of the 8 MI300 small shards hit; the 5 first-wave jobs started together, so each built its own copy.
  - `sgl-kernel-unit-test-amd` passes against the wheel install.
  - The gfx950 build works: `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x (0)` passes.
  - One small shard failed in `test_openai_server.py` (`cannot import name 'ResponseFunctionShellToolCall'`). That's the OpenAI SDK bump from #45291, fixed on main by #46774, not this change.

title: [Perf] diffusion/ming: Reuse ordered RMSNorm in the DiT
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Ming's DiT computes RMSNorm statistics in FP32 and rounds normalized values to BF16 before multiplying by the learned weight. Its native implementation launches separate square, mean, reciprocal-square-root, cast, and multiply operations throughout the denoising loop. This reuses the existing ordered RMSNorm implementation to reduce those launches while preserving the native result.

## Modifications

- Add `eps=1e-5` to the shared cast-before-weight operator, keeping its existing `1e-6` default and epilogues unchanged.
- Extend its ordered reduction to width 3840. Widths 128/3840 use the ordered path for eligible row counts; other shapes, including width 2560, retain ATen mean with fused pointwise operations.
- Dispatch `MingRMSNorm.forward_native` through the existing per-signature bit-exact gate. Residual, compile, unsupported dtype/epsilon, and noncontiguous input/weight cases retain native behavior.
- Add focused reduction-boundary, mixed-magnitude, model-dispatch, CUDA graph replay, and native compile fallback coverage. No new flags or model weights are introduced.

## Accuracy Tests

Baseline: `af21e2b989e482cfdce39689126562f2209d53ac`  
Final head: `c77f23077712f4f6e43654e6492079f649894284`  
Checkpoint: `inclusionAI/Ming-Image-0.1-Design@c57c49689d12ef7d4e24a170014f1dc43d3ce258`.

On B300, 59 norm/kernel tests and 37 Ming tests passed. Full native quality runs cover short/long T2I prompts, seeds 42/43/44, image editing, and repeated requests. Final and pre-cleanup outputs are byte-identical to the matching main topology, including all 216 warmup/formal benchmark PNGs. Both SP2 ranks execute the norm operator and verify its signatures; no gate was disabled.

High quality, CFG=2, native sequential two-output generation, and the lossless revisit all pass against the corresponding main outputs. All 44 compatibility PNGs retain the expected identities; all eight high-mode comparisons are also byte-identical to lossless (RGBA/RGB/alpha/black and white composites: SSIM=1, zero maximum error, infinite PSNR). The two-output case is sequential multioutput, not dynamic batch2.

**BCG limitation:** both main and final capture one graph per worker and replay it only during warmup (12 replays per worker). All six serving cases miss the warmed signature: 84 misses for single-GPU T2I and 168 across the two edit ranks, zero serving replays and zero serving captures. The final norm operator executes 205 times during each capture, so capture includes the new path, but these requests subsequently use eager fallback. T2I capture wall time is 0.586s main / 2.338s final; edit captures take 2.130–2.143s main / 2.960–2.961s final per rank. These instrumented first-capture costs include preparation and are not amortized performance claims. Full capture memory and request-state records are retained. No new BCG serving support or BCG speedup is claimed.

Actual main/final generated images are shown below; previews use identical resizing. The original RGBA PNGs, exact requests, and hashes are retained in the evidence archives.

![Ming native text-to-image: main and final](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-ming-norm-evidence-20261027/text-to-image.jpg)

![Ming native image editing: main and final](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-ming-norm-evidence-20261027/image-edit.jpg)

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Fixed physical B300 GPU pool 0/1; T2I uses GPU0, editing uses Ulysses2 on both. Native BF16 DiT/text/VAE with FP32 latents and CPU RNG, 1024×1024, 12 steps, guidance 1, seed 42, PNG compression 0, all components resident. These are repeated saved requests with the existing native conditioning cache warmed. They are not cold-prompt latency measurements.

Each scenario runs `[main, pre-cleanup, final, final, pre-cleanup, main]` twice: 12 fresh servers, 3 warmups and 6 measured requests per server, 24 formal samples per arm. The timer covers HTTP submission through receipt of all response bytes, including native image generation/saving/encoding; client decoding and evidence copies are excluded. Profiler and synchronized stage diagnostics run separately. Tested GPUs are checked for foreign processes at every boundary; unrelated work on GPUs 4–7 is recorded in the raw telemetry.

| Scenario | Main E2E p50 / p95 (s) | Final E2E p50 / p95 (s) | p50 reduction | Sequential req/s main → final | Denoise main → final (s) | Peak allocated GiB per GPU main → final |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| T2I · 1 GPU | 1.7494 / 1.7559 | 1.3861 / 1.3935 | 20.77% | 0.572 → 0.721 | 1.6845 → 1.3209 | 49.430 → 49.430 |
| Edit · SP2 | 1.4558 / 1.4687 | 1.1166 / 1.1290 | 23.30% | 0.687 → 0.895 | 1.2459 → 0.9077 | 32.934 → 32.934 |

Denoise values are medians from separate synchronized diagnostics, using the slower rank for SP2. The empirical p95 uses 24 formal requests per arm. The workload has concurrency 1. Startup, warmup requests, reserved memory, and every individual sample remain in the raw results.

The full native T2I profile drops from 31,783 CUDA kernels on main to 14,587 at the final head. The identical profile output PNG is verified. This profile establishes the launch reduction; its instrumented duration is not used as an E2E benchmark.

**Baseline selection.** Both native TP2 and SP2 T2I alternatives fail the predeclared image-quality thresholds and remain recorded as failed cells. For editing, both pass; two main A/A medians are 1.7801/1.7824s for TP2 and 1.4499/1.4564s for SP2, versus 2.3420/2.3396s for single GPU. The final edit comparison therefore uses SP2.

**Cleanup retest.** Pre-cleanup `e94a5034a8d3b4ff1f607911aca1d8342ff79c95` is measured alongside the final head in the same symmetric runs. Cleanup removes redundant optional-argument guards and simplifies tests. All changed files were reviewed and pinned pre-commit checks pass.

| Scenario | Final vs main reduction, rounds 1 / 2 | Final vs pre-cleanup latency change, rounds 1 / 2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| T2I | 20.64% / 20.89% | +0.134% / -0.004% |
| Edit · SP2 | 23.06% / 23.49% | -0.500% / -0.418% |

Initial single-GPU T2I A/A median drift is 0.099% for main and 0.376% for pre-cleanup; selected main SP2 edit A/A drift is 0.447%. Adjacent final pairs in the formal run drift by 0.237%/0.289% for T2I and 0.199%/0.153% for editing. The largest positive round cleanup change is +0.134% (T2I), below the measured noise; both edit rounds improve. Pooled mean/p95 cleanup changes are +0.093%/−0.036% for T2I and −0.459%/−0.708% for edit. The retest detects no performance regression from cleanup; these small differences are not claimed as a separate optimization or a population-tail guarantee.

**vLLM-Omni comparison.** Frozen native Omni `817d4c17feb702289a2d2b2cbacfd594c262b7a7` uses the same checkpoint, prompts, inputs, seeds, shape, steps, guidance, and two-GPU budget through its complete VLM→connector→DiT→RGBA pipeline. Its default FlashInfer MoE path fails same-input repeatability. Native Triton MoE restores repeatability, and native regional dynamic compilation with precision-cast emulation is confirmed to execute. Both still fail the quality gate for all 7 T2I samples and 2 of 4 edit samples against the selected SGLang references; edit seeds 43/44 have RGB SSIM around 0.936–0.939, below 0.95. No Omni speedup is claimed, and these cells are not counted as quality-qualified cross-framework performance results. All attempts and images are retained.

**Scope.** This validates Ming-Image-0.1-Design on B300, with the documented native configurations. The separately trained Layer checkpoint and other GPU architectures are not benchmarked here. Existing BCG compatibility findings are reported above; this PR does not claim new BCG coverage. The default kernel epsilon remains compatible with existing MOSS call sites.

**Reproduction and raw evidence:** [release assets](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/tag/b300-ming-norm-evidence-20261027). The package contains fixed source SHAs and patches, commands/environments, request fixtures, every timing/quality result, traces, failed alternatives, archive manifests/checksums, and actual media provenance. Reproduce the commands in the archive on idle GPUs; do not run the profiler during the HTTP benchmark.

## Checklist

- [x] Scoped pre-commit formatting and style checks.
- [x] Focused unit/kernel tests and real native model validation.
- [x] Accuracy, saved-request speed, cleanup retest, and profile evidence.
- [x] No new user-facing flags; behavior and limitations documented here.
- [ ] Upstream GPU CI/reviewer approval (Draft).

title: [Fix] cuda-graph: Keep attention metadata and SP workspaces alive across graph variants of a batch size
author: jybsuper
body:
## Motivation

Enabling the LoRA dual graph (a base-only `nolora` decode graph captured next to the `lora` graph for every batch size) made the graph runners capture two graphs per batch size. Attention backends that rebuilt their per-capture metadata keyed only by batch size then freed buffers the first graph still read, and replay refreshed only the table entry. The symptom depended on allocator recycling: zeroed attention rows on GB300 (full prefill backend), a wrong token at a later decode position on H200/H100 (breakable backend), nothing visible elsewhere. The LoRA CI graph tests caught it as an intermittent decode fault. The bug itself is in the attention backends and the sequence-parallel workspace and applies to any second graph per batch size (attention variants, verify tiers), not only to LoRA.

## Modifications

- `flashinfer`: share the CUDA-graph attention wrappers across the graph variants of a batch size (MHA and MLA decode with a one-time bootstrap plan, MLA verify reuse); replay refreshes buffer contents, never table entries.
- `attention` (TRTLLM MHA/MLA): keep per-batch-size capture metadata alive across graph variants, with regression tests.
- `sp_collective_gemm`: retain workspace generations that captured graphs still use when the workspace grows.
- `lora`: the dual decode graph becomes opt-in through `SGLANG_ENABLE_LORA_DUAL_GRAPH` (default off). The fixes cover the backends that exist today, but nothing guarantees that a new backend or runner keeps its per-batch-size metadata alive under a second graph, so the optimization stays off by default; the stacked PR (#46721) adds the tool and skill with which a deployment that wants it can check its own serving command before turning it on.
- test kit: the attention unit-test kit captures two real graphs per decode case, so a backend that drops the first graph's buffers fails in CI.

No tolerance, default graph backend or router precision changes.

## Accuracy Tests

- CPU regression tests (`base-a-test-cpu`): `test_attention_graph_metadata_reuse.py`, `test_trtllm_mha_paged_kv.py`, `test_layernorm_sp.py`, `test_lora_inactive_batch_skip.py`: 12 of 30 cases fail on the base commit, all pass here.
- Attention kit real captures (six backend files) pass on GB300 and H200.
- The standalone lifetime tracer of the stacked PR, run on Qwen1.5-MoE with a LoRA adapter, flashinfer attention and the dual decode graphs (TP1 and TP2): on the base commit three decode graphs read flashinfer wrappers freed while alive and the worker dies; here no dangling operand across 106 captured graphs per worker.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel or scheduling change; the fixes keep already-allocated metadata alive across captures.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Test] cuda-graph: Add a standalone CUDA-graph lifetime validation tool and its skill
author: jybsuper
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #46720 (merged). The bug fixed there was found because the LoRA dual graph made the runners capture two graphs per batch size, and nothing short of a corrupted output could reveal that the second capture had freed the first graph's buffers. This adds a tool that inspects captured graphs directly, and a thin project skill that drives it. It is also why the dual graph is opt-in in #46720: the fixes cover today's backends, but a new component can reintroduce the same class of bug, so a deployment that wants the optimization first runs this check on its own serving command (model, backends, parallelism, graph settings) and turns the knob on only when lifetime and coverage pass for that configuration; the skill is the operator's interface to that check.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/test/cuda_graph_lifetime/`: a tracer injected through a `sitecustomize` on `PYTHONPATH` (no production hooks) wraps `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` and the SGLang graph backends and runners, reads each captured graph's kernel operands and classifies every device-memory operand against the PyTorch allocator history, and fails the serving process on an operand freed while its graph lives. The harness (`python -m sglang.test.cuda_graph_lifetime --serving-cmd ...`) launches a serving command three times (eager reference, as given, instrumented), drives identical traffic, and writes one ledger with three verdicts kept apart: lifetime, numerical (token-aligned logprobs against eager within 1.0 nat, fail-closed), coverage (the promised graph paths replayed on every worker). `--recompute` re-judges an archived run from digest-verified outputs.
- Tests: one CPU test in `base-a-test-cpu` with twelve independent subtests of the fail-closed contracts (complete evidence passes; drift, truncated responses, a missing worker, a stale flush, a missing graph variant, a crash with saved outputs, a digest mismatch, an unusable or mismatched control never do; the archived ledger is never modified), and one model-free GPU known-good/known-bad control in the label-gated `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small` lane (an optional diagnostic over private allocator and CUDA inspection APIs; edge-case coverage intentionally kept to these core contracts).
- `.agents/skills/sglang-multi-graph-check/`: a thin operator skill for the CLI (new execution versus archive inspection or recomputation, an execution-path preflight, the boundaries every report states).

## Accuracy Tests

- GB300 and H200: the CPU contract test and the GPU control pass (the fuller 35-test and 13-test suites they replace passed there too); on Qwen1.5-MoE with a LoRA adapter and the dual decode graphs (TP1 and TP2) the tool reports lifetime PASS with verified worker identity on the fixed tree and FAIL with three dangling flashinfer wrappers on the base commit; negative controls on saved evidence fail as designed.
- The `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small` lane (RTX 5090) has not run this suite yet; all GPU evidence is GB300 and H200.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: test-only code, nothing on the serving path.

title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: Optimize the Wan VAE decode for gfx1250
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

**What**
Cut the Wan VAE decode on gfx1250 (MI450) from 22.5 s to 8.5 s for Wan2.2-T2V-A14B 720p / 193 frames. The changes: run the ROCm batched-Conv2D replacement in NHWC, install the existing Wan VAE fast path (fused RMSNorm+SiLU, DupUp3D+add) on gfx1250, and drop the slow `where` from the gfx1250 math-SDPA VAE attention.

It also keeps that fast path under multi-GPU: with `--num-gpus 2 --enable-cfg-parallel`, Wan's `auto` VAE parallel-decode mode no longer picks spatial-shard decode on gfx1250, and only the main rank decodes. TP2 VAE decode goes from 28.5 s to 9.0 s.

**Why**
A torch profile of the decode showed only ~9 s of the ~20 s of GPU time was convolution. The rest was unfused fp32 elementwise work plus one attention fixup:

- `RocmPlatform.optimize_vae` never installed `wan_vae_cuda_opt`, so every `WanRMS_norm -> SiLU` ran as `linalg_vector_norm` + `div` + `mul` + `silu` (div 4.8 s, mul 3.0 s, silu 2.7 s per decode).
- The fused norm needs a channels_last_3d input, but the ROCm batched-Conv2D replacement produced `[N, T, C, H, W]` memory. Simply making the conv2d channels_last does not help: PyTorch runs MIOpen convs in NHWC only when `PYTORCH_MIOPEN_SUGGEST_NHWC=1` (read on every call). Without it, a channels_last conv2d is transposed to NCHW and back. With it, the VAE convs run 1.4-2.9x faster (34.97 -> 11.89 ms at 96 ch, 720x1280). The conv output then folds back to channels_last_3d without a copy, so the fused norm applies.
- gfx1250 pins VAE attention to the math SDPA backend (AOTriton fails above head_dim 256). 121 of its 131 ms per call is the `where` in `_safe_softmax` that zeroes fully masked rows. There is no mask here, so computing the same ops explicitly (`q*s @ (k*s)^T`, softmax, `@ v`) is bit-identical and skips it.
- Multi-GPU: `WanVAEConfig.auto_parallel_decode_prefers_spatial_shard()` returns True, so with more than one rank the decoder is built for spatial-shard decode, and `_maybe_optimize_wan_family_vae` then skips the fast path (`Wan VAE: spatial-parallel decode; skipping fast path.`). The sharded decode on the slow path takes 28.5 s on 2 ranks, slower than one rank on the fast path. Once `auto` stops sharding there, `AutoencoderKLWan.use_parallel_decode` was still the raw config flag (always True), so `DecodingStage` stayed `REPLICATED` under cfg-parallel and both ranks decoded the same full video (10.0 s).

## Modifications

- `platforms/rocm.py`:
  - On gfx1250, `optimize_vae` installs `maybe_optimize_wan_vae` / `maybe_optimize_qwen_image_vae`.
  - `_replace_conv3d_with_conv2d` keeps a channels_last BF16 2-D weight when the 3-D weight is channels_last_3d, and sets `PYTORCH_MIOPEN_SUGGEST_NHWC=1` with `setdefault` (an explicit user value wins).
  - `_conv3d_as_batched_conv2d` gets an NHWC branch: one copy gathers the Kt frames and casts to BF16 into `[N*T_out, H, W, Kt*C_in]`, and the output reshapes back to channels_last_3d.
- `models/vaes/wanvae.py`:
  - Import the Triton VAE helpers on gfx1250 too.
  - Keep the fused cat+pad away from convs patched by the Conv2D replacement (it would call the unpatched epilogue).
  - Use explicit math attention when `_sgl_math_sdpa` is set and inputs are fp32.
  - `AutoencoderKLWan.use_parallel_decode` is the config flag, except in `auto` mode where it is True only when spatial-shard decode is chosen, so a single-rank decode runs on the main rank alone under cfg-parallel. Explicit modes keep the config flag.
- `configs/models/vaes/wanvae.py`: `WanVAEConfig.auto_parallel_decode_prefers_spatial_shard()` returns `not is_gfx1250_supported()`. An explicit `parallel_decode_mode=spatial_shard` still shards.
- `models/vaes/wan_vae_cuda_opt.py`: allow the exact-tier post-op fusion on HIP. It keeps its first-use `torch.equal` verification and falls back to aten on any mismatch. On ROCm it is only reachable through the gfx1250 install above.
- Scope: all new behavior is gated on `is_gfx1250_supported()`. NVIDIA, MI300, and MI355 paths are unchanged (one extra `hasattr`/`getattr` that evaluates false).
- Tests (`test_rocm_conv3d_patch.py`):
  - The NHWC conv matches the original `WanCausalConv3d` (with `residual=` / `skip_bias=`) and returns channels_last_3d.
  - Explicit math attention is `torch.equal` to the math SDPA backend.
- Tests (`test_vae_spatial_parallel_decode.py`): `auto` does not shard on gfx1250 while explicit `spatial_shard` does; `use_parallel_decode` is False only for `auto` on gfx1250 (`spatial_shard`, `patch`, and non-gfx1250 `auto` are unchanged). The existing Wan assertion runs with gfx1250 patched off.

## Accuracy Tests

Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, 720x1280, 193 frames, 8 steps, seed 42, fp32 VAE decode, single MI450 (gfx1250) partition. The video is compared against main with the same flags, per frame:

| comparison | PSNR mean | PSNR min | last frame |
|---|---|---|---|
| this PR vs main, full 8-step video | 38.45 dB | 35.64 dB | 38.34 dB |
| VAE attention change only vs main | bit-identical | bit-identical | bit-identical |

The difference comes from the NHWC conv algorithm (the BF16 compute was already there) and the fused norm's rounding order (`quality="lossless"`, the default request tier). Against an fp32 `conv3d` reference, the NHWC and NCHW batched-conv2d paths have the same relative error (3.20e-3 / 3.05e-3 / 3.00e-3 at the three decoder resolutions). Frames were checked visually, including the last frame.

Multi-GPU (TP2, `--num-gpus 2 --enable-cfg-parallel`), same prompt and seed, decoded video compared over all frames:

| comparison | PSNR |
|---|---|
| single-rank fast-path decode vs spatial-shard decode (before) | 38.7 dB |
| main-rank-only decode vs both ranks decoding | inf (identical) |

Spatial-shard and single-rank decode were never bit-identical; per-frame PSNR is flat (37.7-38.9 dB), with no shard seams.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

`sglang generate` with the flags of the Wan2.2 cookbook debug script: `--num-gpus 1 --vae-decode-precision fp32 --attention-backend aiter --enable-torch-compile false`, `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_VAE_CONV2D_BF16=1`, `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_VAE_CHANNELS_LAST_3D=1`, `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_FLYDSL=1`, `HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=0`. One gfx1250 partition (DPX), single request:

| | denoise (s) | VAE decode (s) | e2e (s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main `3dce594de3` | 199.3 | 22.5 | 223.3 |
| this PR | 198.9 | **8.5** | **208.9** |

VAE decode kernels (torch profiler, one decode):

| op | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `aten::div` (F.normalize) | 4.83 s | fused |
| `aten::mul` | 3.03 s | fused |
| unary (SiLU) | 2.75 s | fused |
| math SDPA (25 calls) | 3.28 s | ~0.2 s |
| convolution | ~5.3 s + transposes | NHWC, 1.4-2.9x faster per conv |

Multi-GPU. TP2 is `--num-gpus 2 --enable-cfg-parallel` on the two halves of one gfx1250 package, same flags otherwise. These runs were on a later branch that also has #46723, with the dashboard shape (90000 DiT tokens), so absolute times are not comparable with the TP1 table above:

| run | text encode (s) | denoise (s) | VAE decode (s) | e2e (s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP1 (reference) | 1.05 | 161.3 | 8.7 | 171.4 |
| TP2 before the multi-GPU change | 1.97 | 93.8 | 28.5 | 124.7 |
| TP2 with this PR | 1.96 | 93.6 | **9.0** | **105.0** |

TP2 e2e is 1.19x faster, and TP2 vs TP1 goes from 1.37x to 1.63x. The remaining denoise gap to 2x is the package power limit (both halves pin the 1600 W socket cap, gfx clock ~1840 -> ~1360 MHz), not this code path.

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the PR flow. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).

title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: Replace the gfx1250 bf16 scale-shift torch fallback with a bit-exact Triton kernel
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

**What**
On gfx1250, replace the torch fallback behind `fuse_scale_shift_kernel` for bf16 `x` with an fp32 scale by a dedicated Triton kernel. The kernel is bit-identical to that fallback and 6.4x faster, and covers Wan's `MulAdd` residual gate (`x * (k + scale) + shift`).

**Why**
#42859 routes every bf16 `fuse_scale_shift_kernel` call on gfx1250 to `fuse_scale_shift_kernel_native`, because the existing Triton kernels miscompile there (the identity term is dropped). With an fp32 scale, that fallback promotes to fp32 and returns fp32, so Wan's `mlp_residual(...).to(orig_dtype)` costs three passes over a [90000, 5120] tensor: an fp32 broadcast mul, an fp32 add, and a bf16 cast. That is 2.18 ms per block, 40 blocks per forward.

When the scale is fp32, every intermediate in the fallback is fp32. A kernel that does the same fp32 ops, with FMA contraction disabled (`enable_fp_fusion=False`) and a single rounding to `x.dtype`, therefore produces exactly the fallback's result cast to bf16. That cast is the next thing every caller does, and it matches the `empty_like(x)` contract of the CUDA kernel. Any other case (bf16 scale, per-frame 4-D scale, non-3-D `x`) still takes the fallback.

## Modifications

- `kernels/ops/diffusion/modulate/scale_shift_triton.py`: add `_scale_shift_fp32_rows_kernel` (16x256 row tiles, int64 row offsets, shift that is per-token or broadcast) and `_fuse_scale_shift_fp32_gfx1250`. The guard checks shapes, dtypes, and unit stride on C, and returns `None` for anything else. The kernel is tried first inside the existing `is_gfx1250_supported() and x.dtype is torch.bfloat16` branch.
- `test_modulate.py`: add a gfx1250-only test asserting `torch.equal` with `fuse_scale_shift_kernel_native(...).to(bf16)` for k in {0, 1}, full and broadcast shift, bf16 and fp32 shift.
- Scope: gfx1250 with bf16 inputs only. Other platforms never enter the branch.

Note: `test_scale_shift_3d_tiling_is_bit_exact` (added by #46147) already fails 8/8 on gfx1250 on main, because its reference is the Triton `blc_opt` kernel that #42859 routes around. With this PR, 3/8 pass. The remaining cases compare against that miscompiled reference.

## Accuracy Tests

Bit-exact by construction and by test: `torch.equal` against the fallback in 8 parametrized cases, plus 24 shape/dtype cases at L = 777 / 90000 / 176400, C = 5120.

End to end, Wan2.2-T2V-A14B 720p, 193 frames, 8 steps, seed 42 on gfx1250: the output video is **bit-identical** to main (per-frame PSNR = inf, max abs diff 0).

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Kernel, gfx1250, [1, 90000, 5120] bf16 `x`, fp32 scale, bf16 shift:

| path | time |
|---|---|
| torch fallback + `.to(bf16)` (main) | 2.176 ms |
| this PR | **0.341 ms** (6.4x) |

End to end, `sglang generate` Wan2.2-T2V-A14B 720x1280, 193 frames, 8 steps, CFG, `--num-gpus 1 --attention-backend aiter`, `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_FLYDSL=1`, `HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=0`, one gfx1250 partition, single request:

| | denoise (s) | e2e (s) |
|---|---|---|
| main `3dce594de3` | 199.3 | 223.3 |
| this PR | **197.3** | **221.5** |

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] muse-spark-open: Fuse MoE finalize with the 2shot_push all-reduce
author: wookjeHan
body:
## Motivation Muse Spark fuses its MoE finalize with the custom all-reduce. Today the fused kernel only implements `1shot_push`, and it runs only where the standalone all-reduce would pick `1shot_push`. Above that size the MoE output falls back to a separate finalize kernel plus a standalone all-reduce launch. This PR adds a `2shot_push` exchange to the fused kernel. The fused path now follows the standalone all-reduce's choice: fused 1-shot where it picks `1shot_push`, and fused 2-shot where it picks `2shot_push`. Independent of #46197; the fused 2-shot path runs wherever the all-reduce table picks `2shot_push` (main's table on GB300; on SM107 from #46197). SM107 numbers below are measured on top of #46197, GB300 numbers on main. ## Modifications **Kernel** (`muse_spark_moe_finalize_all_reduce_cutedsl.py`) - The 2-shot exchange follows the `2shot_push` protocol of `custom_all_reduce.cuh`. - The output is bitwise equal to the fused 1-shot path. - It reuses the communicator's push slots and epoch controllers, so there are no new allocations. - When M exceeds the controller count, a block finalizes two tokens, one row of threads each, with per-row named barriers. This applies to 2-shot and unicast 1-shot; multicast 1-shot measured slower. - One-row fused blocks reduce four experts per barrier pair (`group_width` 4, as the cluster path already does). - Refactor: the 1-shot `push_token` / `reduce_token` and the new 2-shot functions share small helpers: copy atoms, `_vec_at`, `_epoch_base`, `_remap_sentinel`, `_poll_arrived` and `_sum_ranks`. **Dispatch** (`muse_spark_finalize_workspace.py`, `muse_spark_moe_finalize_all_reduce.py`) - `two_shot_max_tokens = slot_bytes * world / (4H)` (2048 tokens at TP4 with the default 8 MB slot). It is 0 unless `H % (8 * world) == 0`, so every rank owns whole 8-column vectors. - `uses_two_shot_push(M)` is true exactly where the standalone all-reduce picks `2shot_push`, including under `override_algo`. - `can_fuse` takes the fused 1-shot or the fused 2-shot path. The separate `override_algo` check is gone, because both predicates already go through the communicator's own override handling. - No standalone all-reduce thresholds or buffer allocations change. ## Accuracy Tests **E2E** Muse Spark Open, DFlash (8 draft tokens, real acceptance), sgl-eval with T=1.0, top_p=1.0, top_k=64 and xhigh reasoning. On SM107 fused 2-shot serves every decode batch above 128 tokens (c ≥ 17). | GPU, config | GSM8K | AIME26 pass@1 (x16) | AIME26 pass@16 | |---|---|---|---| | SM107 TP4/EP4, #46197 + this PR | 97.35% | 96.46% ± 2.57 (SEM 0.64) | 100% | | SM107 TP8/EP8 (2 nodes), #46197 + this PR | 97.35% | 97.08% ± 2.06 (SEM 0.52) | 100% | | GB300 TP4/EP4, main + this PR | 97.57% | 95.83% ± 3.10 (SEM 0.78) | 100% | | GB300 TP8/EP8 (2 trays), main + this PR | 97.65% | 95.62% ± 3.15 (SEM 0.79) | 100% | On SM107 the acceptance length was 4.84 / 3.85 (GSM8K / AIME26) on main (earlier run) and 4.94 / 3.85 with #46197 + this PR.

title: [Perf] [AMD] moe: Add tuned Triton fused MoE config for gemma-4-26B-A4B on MI355X
author: lishuoshuo-amd
body:
## Motivation

On MI355X, gemma-4-26B-A4B's Triton fused MoE (`--moe-runner-backend triton`) has no tuned config, so every batch falls back to the heuristic:

```
Using default MoE kernel config. Performance might be sub-optimal! Config file not found at .../moe_runner/triton_utils/configs/triton_3_8_0/E=128,N=704,device_name=AMD_Instinct_MI355X.json
```

The heuristic uses `BLOCK_SIZE_M 64, BLOCK_SIZE_K 32` from batch 256 up. At batch 4096 the fused MoE takes 1303 us; with a tuned config it takes 722 us. `main` has no MI355X fused-MoE config at all.

## Modifications

One new file, no code change: `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/configs/triton_3_8_0/E=128,N=704,device_name=AMD_Instinct_MI355X.json`, 14 batch buckets (1 to 8192).

- `E=128` is `num_experts` and `N=704` is `moe_intermediate_size` at TP1. Other TP sizes give another `N` and do not use this file.
- `triton_3_8_0` matches the ROCm 10 image (`triton.__version__ == "3.8.0"`). Images with another Triton version reach this file through the newest-first fallback, with a warning. I measured only Triton 3.8.0.
- There is no `_down` file. The down projection then reuses this table (`get_moe_configs` falls back to the up config), and the kernel numbers below time both GEMMs.

### Tuning

`benchmark_config` from `benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton/tuning_fused_moe_triton.py` over the default ROCm search space (1600 candidates per bucket, bf16, TP1), one bucket per process. Two candidate groups are excluded:

- `num_warps=1`. On gfx950 with Triton 3.8.x, single-wave kernels race on LDS between a `ds_read` and the direct-to-LDS loads, and write rows that the store mask should drop (llvm/llvm-project#187673, reverted upstream in llvm/llvm-project#208280 but still in Triton 3.8.x's LLVM). This also makes the stock tuner crash with a memory fault at M = 512, 1024, ... .
- `num_warps=2` with `BLOCK_SIZE_N=16` and `BLOCK_SIZE_M>=128`. These intermittently produced wrong elements in the down GEMM in our checks.

Every selected entry uses `num_warps` 2, 4 or 8. The tuning driver is not part of this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

`fused_moe` output with each tuned entry vs the heuristic config, same inputs: max abs diff 0 for all 14 buckets, three reruns identical. A `num_warps=1, BLOCK_SIZE_M=128` control at M=640 shows a mismatch, so the check detects bad configs.

GSM8K, chat API (`python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 1319 --max-tokens 2048 --temperature 0`), server flags as below:

| SGLang commit | base | tuned | base repeat |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3ea7e210 | 0.9581 | 0.9604 | 0.9566 |
| bea6a21 | 0.9589 | 0.9566 | 0.9581 |
| 52a6f70 | 0.9581 | 0.9574 | 0.9574 |

The tuned scores are in the base-repeat range.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X, ROCm 10.0.0, torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0, Triton 3.8.0+git4cff872c.

**Kernel** (`tuning_fused_moe_triton.py` without `--tune`; the tuned arm sets `SGLANG_MOE_CONFIG_DIR`; SGLang 52a6f70; mean of two alternating rounds, round-to-round spread <= 0.3%):

| batch | default (BM/BN/BK/G/warps) | default us | tuned (BM/BN/BK/G/warps) | tuned us | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 16/32/64/1/- | 41.5 | 32/16/256/8/4 | 33.2 | 1.25x |
| 2 | 16/32/64/1/- | 49.7 | 32/64/128/4/2 | 45.7 | 1.09x |
| 4 | 16/32/64/1/- | 77.4 | 32/64/128/4/2 | 74.5 | 1.04x |
| 8 | 16/32/64/1/- | 140.6 | 32/64/64/1/4 | 121.8 | 1.15x |
| 16 | 16/32/64/1/- | 183.8 | 64/64/64/4/4 | 182.2 | 1.01x |
| 32 | 16/32/64/1/- | 252.7 | 32/64/64/4/4 | 240.1 | 1.05x |
| 64 | 16/32/64/1/- | 273.8 | 64/128/64/8/2 | 269.3 | 1.02x |
| 128 | 16/32/64/1/- | 283.4 | 64/128/64/4/2 | 276.6 | 1.02x |
| 256 | 64/64/32/8/- | 348.5 | 64/128/64/8/2 | 286.4 | 1.22x |
| 512 | 64/64/32/8/- | 389.5 | 64/128/64/4/2 | 308.8 | 1.26x |
| 1024 | 64/64/32/8/- | 514.3 | 128/128/64/4/8 | 349.1 | 1.47x |
| 2048 | 64/64/32/8/- | 764.8 | 256/256/64/1/4 | 473.8 | 1.61x |
| 4096 | 64/64/32/8/- | 1302.8 | 256/128/32/4/4 | 721.8 | 1.81x |
| 8192 | 64/64/32/8/- | 2392.4 | 256/128/32/8/4 | 1189.8 | 2.01x |

No bucket is slower than the default.

**End to end** (SGLang 52a6f70; the tuned arm only adds `SGLANG_MOE_CONFIG_DIR` pointing at this file):

```
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /path/to/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it --tp-size 1 --dp-size 2 \
  --moe-runner-backend triton --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mem-fraction-static 0.88 \
  --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --context-length 11264 --disable-radix-cache
python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids --random-range-ratio 1 \
  --random-input-len <ISL> --random-output-len <OSL> --max-concurrency <C> --num-prompts <N> --warmup-requests 8
```

Each arm: 4 consecutive runs, a fresh server for each run, run 1 discarded, median of runs 2-4. The tuned server logs `Using MoE kernel config from .../triton_3_8_0/E=128,N=704,device_name=AMD_Instinct_MI355X.json`.

| ISL / OSL, concurrency | total tok/s base | total tok/s tuned | change | mean TTFT | mean TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8192 / 1024, 64 | 32655 | 34773 | **+6.5%** | -15.9% | -5.1% |
| 1024 / 1024, 64 | 10506 | 10831 | +3.1% | -15.6% | -2.6% |
| 8192 / 1024, 1 | 1745 | 1904 | +9.1% | -15.0% | -8.1% |
| 8192 / 1024, 16 | 16452 | 16839 | +2.4% | -14.2% | -1.7% |
| 8192 / 1024, 256 | 48964 | 53378 | +9.0% | -15.9% | -7.1% |

Throughput ranges do not overlap between the arms; within-arm spread is 0.1-1.2%. Per-run total tok/s, in run order:

| ISL / OSL, concurrency | base r1 (dropped) | base r2 / r3 / r4 | tuned r1 (dropped) | tuned r2 / r3 / r4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8192 / 1024, 64 | 32213 | 32655 / 32546 / 32698 | 34728 | 34773 / 34569 / 34809 |
| 1024 / 1024, 64 | 10350 | 10548 / 10426 / 10506 | 10685 | 10841 / 10783 / 10831 |
| 8192 / 1024, 1 | 1737 | 1750 / 1741 / 1745 | 1893 | 1898 / 1904 / 1905 |
| 8192 / 1024, 16 | 16419 | 16452 / 16500 / 16425 | 16578 | 16842 / 16839 / 16829 |
| 8192 / 1024, 256 | 48936 | 48996 / 48943 / 48964 | 53472 | 53378 / 53458 / 53371 |

The same design on SGLang bea6a21 gave +7.5%, +3.2%, +8.5%, +2.1% and +9.0%, and on 3ea7e210 +7.2%, +3.7%, +9.3%, +2.4% and +9.1%.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (JSON written by `save_configs`.)
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). N/A: config only.
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). N/A.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Fix] cuda_graph: Release base storage held by empty break inputs
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

A zero-element accelerator view can still own a large nonempty base allocation. Breakable CUDA graph capture currently keeps these views unchanged in eager-break argument closures. For NoPE attention, empty Q/K RoPE views can therefore pin the projection outputs once per layer and captured bucket.

## Modifications

Replace empty accelerator arguments with zero-storage tensors preserving shape, strides, dtype and device. CPU arguments keep their identity, and nonempty arguments keep the existing weak-reference behavior. Add a regression for nested views and multiple graph buckets with changed-input replay after temporary-storage reuse.

This is independent of KDA, ReplaySSM and MoE optimizations. It does not address the separate nonempty-input lifetime issue in #37448 or change the eager-output ownership fixed in #30584.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested directly on main `def8f93212bd997ec19b1395e0d892b442374552` plus this patch, on one B300 (PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2, Triton 3.8.0):

- New regression against unmodified main: **2 failed, 1 passed**, exposing retained base storage.
- New regression plus existing BCG capture/replay/copy unit classes: **18 passed**.
- Changed-input replay assertions are bit-exact. CPU empty-argument identity is unchanged.
- Pre-commit and `git diff --check` pass.

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/cuda_graph/breakable/test_empty_view_capture.py \
  test/registered/cuda_graph/breakable/test_breakable_cuda_graph.py::TestBreakableCUDAGraphBasic \
  test/registered/cuda_graph/breakable/test_breakable_cuda_graph.py::TestCopyOutput \
  test/registered/cuda_graph/breakable/test_breakable_cuda_graph.py::TestBreakGraphHelper
```

**Validation limitation:** isolated model-level validation remains pending. An earlier GLM-5.3-Flash experiment on `d1bbcbdc`, combining this fix with a separate convolution-layout change, scored 1281/1319 on GSM8K versus baseline 1286/1319; both had four truncations, and both passed 12/12 long-context retrieval probes. Long-input teacher-forcing also varied in repeated unchanged-baseline runs. Those results do not establish the cause or a model-quality pass for this individual patch. ROCm/NPU hardware has not been tested.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The model-free regression uses a shared graph pool with 512/384/256/128-row buckets. The old implementation retains 15 MiB of active projection storage; the patched test requires less than 1 MiB of additional active allocation and verifies replay after input changes.

An earlier isolated memory A/B on 4×B300 used GLM-5.3-Flash, a fixed 1627-slot Mamba pool and the same integration source/configuration in both arms; this empty-view patch was the only difference. Cumulative additional active graph allocation per GPU was:

| Last captured bucket | Before (MiB) | After (MiB) | Released (MiB) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16384 | 2481.26 | 369.26 | 2112 |
| 15872 | 4528.95 | 370.95 | 4158 |
| 15360 | 6509.62 | 371.62 | 6138 |

These are graph-allocation measurements on the earlier integration base, not whole-server VRAM or new-main serving-throughput results. No request-level speedup is claimed.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add registered regression tests.
- [x] Document memory measurements and their scope.
- [ ] Complete isolated model-level validation.

## Cleanup validation (2026-10-29)

Cleanup at `669fc03b`: simplified the storage-ownership explanation and checked shape, stride, dtype, and zero-storage metadata for both nested empty views. Production execution is unchanged. On RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, the regression and existing BCG capture/replay/copy classes passed **18 tests**. Changed-file pre-commit checks pass. The earlier B300 memory measurements above were not rerun.

title: [Perf] kda: Write convolution output directly into contiguous QKV planes
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

KDA already computes packed Q/K/V convolution in one call. Its token-major output leaves the three channel slices non-contiguous, so the FlashInfer prefill path materializes three copies before consuming them. At the GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 16K-token shape, those copies cost more than the convolution itself.

## Modifications

Add an optional split-output layout to the existing Triton convolution. The convolution stores directly into contiguous Q/K/V planes in one allocation, using the runtime total-token count as the plane pitch. Arithmetic and convolution-state updates are unchanged.

Both eager KDA prefill and captured KDA prefill enable it only for FlashInfer with equal Q/K/V widths. Other backends and unequal widths retain the original layout. There are no server-argument, graph-size, precision, MoE or memory-budget changes, and no dependency on the separate empty-view fix #46737 or community PRs #45369/#45583.

Related work: #32474 packs convolution with a separate output-layout kernel; #34299 integrates a native checkpoint backend; #45992 handles copies in the Triton KDA normalization path. This patch changes the existing convolution producer's store for the existing FlashInfer path, including graph execution.

## Accuracy Tests

Rebased and tested independently on main `def8f93212bd997ec19b1395e0d892b442374552`, B300, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2, Triton 3.8.0:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/mamba/test_causal_conv1d_split_output.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_prefill_graph.py::TestFlashInferKDAPrefillGraph
```

**5 tests and 12 subtests passed.** The new operator regression checks bit-exact output and state, unequal request lengths, strided input, padded block-table rows and changed-input graph replay. Existing KDA graph tests use their existing numerical tolerances; they are not described as bit-exact. A separate five-case microbench also passes bit-exact output/state/replay checks, including FP32 convolution weights at model dimensions. Pre-commit and `git diff --check` pass.

**Validation limitation:** isolated model-level accuracy remains pending. An earlier `d1bbcbdc` GLM-5.3-Flash experiment combining this change with the separate empty-view fix scored 1281/1319 on GSM8K versus baseline 1286/1319; both had four truncations and passed 12/12 long-context retrieval probes. Thirty-two fixed short-input teacher-forcing probes matched exactly, while long-input probes also varied between unchanged-baseline repeats. This does not establish the cause or an accuracy pass for this individual patch.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Single B300, BF16 input, FP32 width-4 weights, no bias, local Q/K/V width 2048 each, input row stride 6416. CUDA-event medians of nine samples, alternating baseline/candidate order; each sample includes 100 invocations through CUDA-graph replay. Both arms use the same patched operator: the original output mode plus three contiguous copies versus the new split-output mode.

| Total tokens | Original convolution + Q/K/V copies | Split-output convolution | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1024 | 24.945 us | 10.272 us | 2.43x |
| 8192 | 180.952 us | 68.585 us | 2.64x |
| 16384 | 347.838 us | 130.748 us | 2.66x |

These new-main measurements cover this local path, not full-model latency or request throughput. The convolution-only kernel is not claimed to be 2.66x faster; eliminating the three layout copies supplies the improvement. No combined serving-throughput result is attributed to this PR.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the 16K local timing</summary>

Run from this PR checkout with SGLang installed and one idle GPU:

```python
import statistics
import torch
from sglang.kernels.ops.mamba.causal_conv1d_triton import causal_conv1d_fn

torch.manual_seed(44)
lengths, h = [8192, 8192], 2048
m, dim = sum(lengths), 3 * h
x = torch.randn(m, dim + 272, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)[:, :dim]
w = torch.randn(dim, 4, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) * 0.1
seed = torch.randn(4, 3, dim, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
states = [seed.clone().transpose(-1, -2) for _ in range(2)]
cu = torch.tensor([0, 8192, 16384], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64)
slots = torch.tensor([2, 1], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
initial = torch.tensor([False, True], device="cuda")

def run(split):
    out = causal_conv1d_fn(
        x.T, w, None, states[int(split)], cu, lengths, slots, initial,
        output_split_size=h if split else 0,
    )
    return tuple(out.unbind(0)) if split else tuple(
        t.contiguous() for t in out.T.chunk(3, dim=-1)
    )

before, after = run(False), run(True)
for a, b in zip(before, after):
    torch.testing.assert_close(a, b, rtol=0, atol=0)
torch.testing.assert_close(states[0], states[1], rtol=0, atol=0)
graphs = []
for split in (False, True):
    for _ in range(5):
        run(split)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
        for _ in range(10):
            run(split)
    graphs.append(graph)
samples = [[], []]
for repeat in range(9):
    for index in ([0, 1] if repeat % 2 == 0 else [1, 0]):
        start, end = (torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(2))
        start.record()
        for _ in range(10):
            graphs[index].replay()
        end.record()
        end.synchronize()
        samples[index].append(start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / 100)
print("baseline_us, split_us:", *map(statistics.median, samples))
```

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add registered operator correctness tests.
- [x] Run existing FlashInfer KDA graph tests.
- [x] Provide scoped microbenchmarks and reproduction.
- [ ] Complete isolated model-level validation.

## Cleanup validation (2026-10-29)

Cleanup at `f5495a66`: clarified convolution-output naming and fixed the CPU hook fixture to initialize the KDA dispatcher and check the Q/K/V tuple contract. The fixture covers GDN, Triton KDA, equal-width FlashInfer planes, and unequal-width fallback. The old fixture reproduced `AttributeError: kernel_dispatcher`; the updated CPU file passed **5 tests and 11 subtests**. On RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), split-output convolution and Triton graph tests passed **4 tests and 8 subtests**; the existing **4 FlashInfer graph tests were skipped because they require SM100/SM103**, not counted as passes. Production dispatch, convolution arithmetic, and kernel source are unchanged; changed-file pre-commit checks pass. Earlier B300 results above were not rerun.

title: [Perf] LoRA: bound csgmv CUDA-graph segment grids by token count
author: glenliu21
body:
## Motivation

CSGMV LoRA kernels launch one program per segment and column tile. Inside a CUDA graph the launch grid is fixed at capture, so the current code sizes the segment axis to the whole static metadata buffer. That buffer is sized for the largest captured batch, and every captured graph launches a program for each of its entries, which is unnecessary.

## Modifications

-  Add `csgmv_segment_grid_size` as a helper:
   - Eager launches are unchanged and use the batch's exact segment count

title: [Fix] [AMD] quark: Keep MXFP8 shared experts out of the MXFP4 fused slot on dense-first models
author: ZhengGong-amd
body:
## Motivation

`amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` crashes at load because its MXFP8 shared experts are fused into the packed MXFP4 routed-expert slot, so this PR makes the Quark fusion gate probe every named MoE layer and has the MiniMax-M3 hooks ask that gate.

```text
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (384) must match the size of tensor b (768) at non-singleton dimension 1
```

`QuarkConfig.can_fuse_shared_expert()` compares routed and shared specs only at layer 0 and the NextN block. When layer 0 is a dense MLP (MiniMax-M3, DeepSeek-V3, GLM-5.x, Kimi-K2.x), both lookups fall back to the global spec and agree, whatever the MoE layers hold. The MiniMax-M3 hooks never ask the gate anyway: they refuse only `modelopt_mixed` and `minimax_m3_nvfp4`.

## Modifications

- `quark`: `can_fuse_shared_expert()` also probes every target decoder layer whose routed or shared experts are named in `layer_quant_config`, so one mismatched layer refuses fusion in any entry order. Draft entries (`mtp.*`, NextN layers past `num_hidden_layers`, non-`layers.<N>` bases such as `model.mtp.0`) are skipped, so an FP8 MTP block still vetoes fusion only for the draft.
- `minimax`: both MiniMax-M3 hooks call `quant_blocks_shared_experts_fusion(quant_config)`, as DeepSeek-V2/V3/V4 do. The name list stays because `MiniMaxM3Nvfp4Config` does not implement the gate.

The checkpoint now loads unfused and logs why, the path `--disable-shared-experts-fusion` selects today. Across 13 local Quark checkpoints only this one changes (fused → unfused); MiniMax-M3, GLM-5.x, DeepSeek-R1-0528, Kimi-K2.6, Muse-Spark and Qwen3.5 MXFP4 exports keep their decision.

Correct output also needs the MXFP8 scale handling from #46693, #46587 and #44080 (on `main` 2160 `weight_scale not found in params_dict`). #46587 instead requantizes the shared expert to MXFP4 to keep fusion; Quark leaves lossy conversion opt-in via `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`.

## Accuracy Tests

4×MI355X, TP4, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, `main@6393e66b86` plus the same scale handling in every arm. GSM8K via `sglang.test.run_eval`, 5-shot chat, temperature 0, 1314 items.

| Arm | Load | GSM8K |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | crash (fusion enabled) | — |
| `--disable-shared-experts-fusion` | ok | 0.9665, 0.9673 |
| this PR, default | ok, fusion disabled | 0.9627, 0.9665 |

Both loading arms run the same unfused path; differences are within noise (stderr ±0.005).

New tests in `test_quark_config.py` and `test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py` cover dense leading layers, both entry orders, named routed experts, NextN drafts and a real `QuarkConfig` in M3.1's layout; 106 pass.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not a speed change: the fused path does not load on `main`.

title: [Perf] [NPU] dsv4: drop host-syncing ops from the decode scheduler chain (aclnnNonzeroV2 + D2H)
author: iridiumine
body:
# Motivation

DSV4-NPU decode schedules everything on a single host thread. Three ops on that chain synchronized with the device mid-chain, pinning the scheduler thread until the in-flight forward drained and leaving the NPU idle:

1. The verify bundle built the ratio-4 compressed loc table with a boolean index (`x[mask]` → aclnnNonzeroV2; output shape depends on device data, so the count must be read back to host) — ~3.9 ms/round on the spec path.
2. The same boolean index in `_derive_c4_loc_from_full` on the alloc path — 32.5 ms/round on the non-spec path (it inherited the whole queue-drain wait once the mirror D2H was disabled).
3. `maybe_write_dsv4_decode` read `batch.req_pool_indices` back to host (31.4 ms/round, same inheritance).

## Modifications

- New `_compact_c4_loc` helper (dsv4_common_hooks.py): compacts the group-closing slots fully on device via `cumsum → masked_fill → scatter` (a trash slot absorbs invalid rows, sliced away after). All shapes are host-known, so nothing syncs. Output is zero-padded to a fixed upper bound — byte-identical to what the consumers already build from the compact tensor (eager `zeros(bs)` prefix copy / graph-replay zero-tail), so no consumer changed.
- Call sites pass a constructively-safe bound only where it holds: the verify bundle uses `min(t, t//4 + bs)` (the padding width the backend already applies); plain decode passes `t` (one new slot per request bounds the count unconditionally). Multi-slot (spec reserve) and extend shapes keep the original boolean index.
- `maybe_write_dsv4_decode` takes the batch's `req_pool_indices_cpu` host mirror (the extend hook's existing contract) instead of D2H-syncing the device tensor.

All changes are behind NPU/DSV4 gates; CUDA paths are untouched.

## Accuracy Tests

title: [Perf] scheduler: Refresh PD prefill bootstrap-queue prefixes in the waiting-prefix LRU pass
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

#41593 keeps waiting requests' device prefixes warm by touching them in the radix LRU on each refresh pass. On a PD prefill worker it walks only `waiting_queue`. Requests still in `disagg_prefill_bootstrap_queue`, which are waiting for decode to pre-allocate their slots, are never touched. When decode is full, the bootstrap queue is the deep one, and those prefixes age out while the requests wait. Each evicted prefix is then reloaded from the external (L3) tier or recomputed when the request is admitted. That slows prefill, lengthens the wait for everyone behind it, and evicts more prefixes, so the loop feeds itself.

We hit this serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB300 with 9 DEP2 prefill workers and one DEP16 decode worker, using an agentic multi-turn trace at 7480 concurrent sessions and a Mooncake L3 tier. After the client's turn burst, the bootstrap queue held about 300 requests per prefill rank, each waiting about 100 s. Device-radix hits fell from about 65 % to 22 % of prompt tokens and L3 loads rose to 73 %. Prefill throughput collapsed and did not recover within the run. The router kept 95-98 % of turns on their session's previous worker throughout, so the prefixes were evicted while the requests waited, not routed away.

**Impact**
- The gain below is not a speedup of healthy serving. It comes from preventing this throughput collapse: with the fix, prefill recovers from the turn burst instead of staying stuck in the evict-and-reload loop.
- Only PD prefill workers whose bootstrap queue holds requests long enough for their prefixes to age out are affected. That needs decode to be the limit (slots full) and a live prefix working set at or above the device radix pool.
- Unaffected:
  - Non-PD servers and PD decode workers: the bootstrap queue is `None`, so the pass is the same as before.
  - Configurations #41593's gate already skips: cache-aware policies while they still match every waiting request (for example `lpm` with at most 128 waiting), non-LRU eviction policies, and `--disable-radix-cache`.
  - PD prefill whose bootstrap queue stays short, or whose working set fits the device pool: there is nothing left to evict, so eviction order does not change outcomes. The healthy-shape check is below.

## Modifications

- `SchedulePolicy.calc_priority` takes the PD prefill bootstrap queue. The scheduler passes `disagg_prefill_bootstrap_queue.queue`, or `None` when not running PD prefill.
- On the same refresh pass, `_touch_waiting_prefixes` touches up to `WAITING_PREFIX_REFRESH_BOOTSTRAP_MAX` bootstrap entries (512, a module constant next to the existing `WAITING_QUEUE_PREFIX_MATCH_MAX` and `WAITING_PREFIX_REFRESH_INTERVAL`) before the waiting queue, both in reverse order. The waiting-queue head therefore still carries the newest timestamp. No new environment variable: `SGLANG_ENABLE_WAITING_PREFIX_REFRESH=0` still turns the whole refresh off.
- The existing gate from #41593 is unchanged: cache-agnostic policy, LRU eviction, not decode, no fast match path, prefix sharing supported, and `SGLANG_ENABLE_WAITING_PREFIX_REFRESH` on. Non-PD and decode workers behave exactly as before.
- `test_scheduler_held_row_admission`'s `Scheduler` stub gains `disagg_prefill_bootstrap_queue = None` for the new argument.

Limits:
- Bootstrap entries are refreshed only on passes that reach `calc_priority`. The caller returns earlier when the waiting queue is empty or no request rows are free, so the bootstrap queue is not refreshed on its own.
- With more than 128 waiting entries, waiting entries past the first 128 are still not touched and can end up older than the refreshed bootstrap entries.
- The touch path is the one #41593 uses (`refresh_device_prefix` / `touch_prefix`). It never allocates or issues an external-tier lookup, including with the unified radix cache and the Mooncake external linker.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the change only reorders radix-cache eviction and does not affect model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GB300, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash FP4, one DEP16 decode worker, agentic multi-turn trace, 1200 s window, Mooncake L3 tier, simulated acceptance length 3.51. Dynamo frontend with its backend admission limits raised (`DYN_BACKEND_ADMISSION_*`), so waiting turns reach the prefill server as with Dynamo 1.6 and earlier.

**Collapse case, isolated on current main** (SGLang main at 5884e4fe, this PR only): 9 DEP2 prefill workers (max 64 running per rank), 7480 concurrent sessions.

| | main | with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| total throughput (tok/s/GPU) | 347,197 | **551,223** (+59 %) |
| p90 interactivity (tok/s/user) | 134.2 | 144.0 |
| p90 / p50 TTFT | 147 s / 60 s | 59.8 s / 31.5 s |
| throughput in minutes 10-20 | ~300k | ~620k |
| bootstrap queue p50 / p90 per prefill rank | 320 / 402 | 178 / 254 |
| prompt tokens from L3 / device radix | 74 % / 20.5 % | 22 % / 73 % |
| decode running per rank | 19 | 52 |
| errors | 0 | 0 |

An earlier pair on main at 656331295, with four other open PRs (#46497, #46593, #46592, #46404) on both arms, showed the same: 361,815 → 560,412 tok/s/GPU, L3 share 73 % → 21 %. Each arm is a single run at an operating point that can settle in a healthy or a collapsed state; the effect repeated on both bases and is far larger than the 3-4 % run-to-run spread we see on this setup.

**Healthy shape** (10 DEP2 prefill workers, 6400 sessions, default Dynamo admission, main at 5884e4fe): throughput −2.5 %, p90 interactivity +1.8 %, steady state identical, i.e. neutral within noise. The bootstrap queue stays at p90 4 per rank there, so the new part barely engages.

**Refresh cost** (scheduler-thread time per refresh pass, timed in the runs above):

| | per refresh p50 / p90 / p99 / max | of which bootstrap part p50 / p99 | refreshes per rank | share of wall time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| collapse case (bootstrap 92 p50, 327 p99 entries) | 40.6 / 74 / 100 / 272 ms | 17 / 72 ms | every ~16 s | 0.24 % |
| healthy shape | 7.9 / 25 / 35 / 44 ms | 0 / 1.7 ms | every ~12 s | 0.09 % |

Most of the healthy-shape cost is the existing #41593 waiting-queue touch (about 0.2-0.25 ms per touched request at these prompt lengths). A cap of 128 bootstrap entries would bound the new part near 25 ms, but it would leave queue positions 128-320 unprotected, which is where the collapse happened, so the cap stays at 512.

title: [Perf] [AMD] qwen3: Use the fused QK-norm + RoPE + KV write in decode with an fp8 KV cache
author: chaojhou
body:
## Motivation

#44267 fused dense Qwen3's decode QK-norm, RoPE and KV-cache write into one aiter kernel on ROCm, but only for a KV cache in the activation dtype. With `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` every decode layer still runs two `add_rmsnorm_quant` launches, two contiguous copies of the strided q/k views, `rotary_embedding` and the Triton `reshape_and_cache_flash` fp8 write. The aiter kernels that path calls already quantize the cache write with a per-tensor scale.

## Modifications

- `Qwen3Attention.forward` also takes the fused decode path when the NHD cache is `aiter.dtypes.fp8`, the only fp8 dtype aiter's binding accepts (e4m3fn on gfx950, e4m3fnuz on gfx942).
- The kernel gets the layer's own k/v scales: `k_scale_float` / `v_scale_float` from `BaseKVCacheMethod`, a plain float from `load_kv_cache_scales`, or 1.0 when the layer has none. They are cached as CPU tensors on first use, because the kernel reads them on the host and a device tensor would sync inside graph capture; a scale without a host copy raises.
- The mRoPE (Qwen3-VL) kernel shares the gate and gets the same support; it is covered by the unit test, not benchmarked. bf16 caches are unchanged.
- Reached by dense Qwen3 and the models that use its decoder as their language model (Qwen3-VL dense, the Qwen3 variants of InternVL and Intern-S1, MiniCPM-V 4.5, LightOnOCR, Step3-VL-10B, Qwen3-ASR). Qwen3-MoE and Qwen3.5 have their own attention and are not affected.
- `test_qwen3_aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope.py` adds fp8-cache cases for both kernels with k/v scales (1, 1), (0.5, 2) and (2, 0.5), checking q, the dequantized K, V against `(v / scale).to(fp8)`, and that no other slot is written. Passing inverted, swapped or unit scales to the kernel fails every case whose scales are not 1.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X (gfx950), torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0, sglang-kernel 0.4.10, aiter `285579b62`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` (attention backend resolves to `aiter`, decode CUDA graphs on). Every server runs `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` with otherwise default args. Baseline is main `132b0f0ae7`.

**Unit test.** `test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope.py`: 6 passed, 64 subtests passed.

**GSM8K**, `python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 1319 --max-tokens 4096` (chat API, greedy; 1314 questions after the 5 few-shot examples):

| Model | Baseline | This PR | Runs per arm |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | 0.9495 (0.9444 to 0.9543) | 0.9475 (0.9437 to 0.9566) | 8 |
| Qwen3-14B-FP8 | 0.9559 | 0.9559 | 1 |

One run has a standard error of 0.006. On Qwen3-8B the baseline's own runs span 1 pt, so a single pair says little and both arms ran 8 times: the difference of the means is -0.20 pt, 95% CI [-0.61, +0.21]. lm_eval's 5-shot GSM8K over 13 few-shot seeds gives +0.06 pt, 95% CI [-0.23, +0.36], and teacher-forced decode NLL on the same questions changes by less than 0.12%.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GPU kernel time in one Qwen3-8B decode step at batch 64 (36 layers), torch profiler, CUDA graphs on:

| Kernel | Baseline | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `aiter::add_rmsnorm_quant_kernel` (q_norm, k_norm) | 72 launches, 288.1 µs | |
| contiguous copies of the strided q/k views | 72 launches, 301.1 µs | |
| `rotary_embedding_kernel` | 36 launches, 155.9 µs | |
| `reshape_and_cache_flash` (fp8 KV write) | 36 launches, 155.1 µs | |
| `fused_mrope_rms_kv_kernel<…, fp8e4m3fn>` | | 36 launches, 165.7 µs |

The decode step goes from 6.39 to 5.94 ms. Qwen3-14B-FP8 at batch 8 shows the same swap: 240 launches taking 1039 µs become 40 launches taking 181 µs. With a bf16 cache both trees run the same fused kernel.

`python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 1.0`, `--num-prompts = max(16, 4 × concurrency)`, prefix cache flushed before each run, one benchmark at a time. Median TPOT, two rounds with the GPU assignment swapped, mean of the two.

**Qwen3-8B** (per-round deltas: −1.8 / −4.1 / −7.5 / −7.6 / −3.1% and −2.3 / −5.3 / −8.0 / −7.5 / −4.5%):

| Concurrency | Baseline (ms) | This PR (ms) | Delta | Output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8.941 | 8.758 | −2.0% | +2.2% |
| 8 | 9.443 | 8.999 | −4.7% | +3.2% |
| 32 | 6.473 | 5.973 | −7.7% | +6.1% |
| 64 | 6.870 | 6.351 | −7.6% | +6.3% |
| 128 | 10.210 | 9.819 | −3.8% | +3.5% |

**Qwen3-14B-FP8** (per-round deltas: −3.8 / −6.9 / −8.2 / −6.3 / −3.2% and −3.7 / −7.4 / −7.3 / −5.9 / −6.1%):

| Concurrency | Baseline (ms) | This PR (ms) | Delta | Output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 7.038 | 6.775 | −3.7% | +3.8% |
| 8 | 7.667 | 7.119 | −7.2% | +7.3% |
| 32 | 8.509 | 7.848 | −7.8% | +6.8% |
| 64 | 10.312 | 9.685 | −6.1% | +5.4% |
| 128 | 14.166 | 13.506 | −4.7% | +3.9% |

Mean TTFT is within ±3% of the baseline in every cell; prefill does not take the fused path. At concurrency 1 and 8 Qwen3-8B decodes slower than at 32 in both arms on this stack: at batch 8 one bf16 GEMM per layer runs as aiter's Triton `_gemm_a16_w16_kernel` and takes 6.0 ms of the 9.8 ms step, so the relative gain there understates the 0.18 / 0.44 ms saved per step. gfx942 is not measured.
