title: [Perf] hicache: Wait once per write_back eviction walk, not once per victim
author: pengwu22
body:
## Motivation With `--hicache-write-policy write_back`, the device-eviction walk in `UnifiedRadixCache` copies each victim to host and blocks on that copy before taking the next victim. Each wait sits behind the write fence, so once the host pool is full the scheduler stalls once per victim while the GPU idles. This PR queues the walk's copies, submits them together, waits once, then demotes the victims in walk order. Eviction decisions are unchanged: same victims, same order, in both tree cores. ## Speed Tests and Profiling One GB300, `--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-write-policy write_back --hicache-size 100`, `benchmark/hicache/bench_multiturn.py`. The device pool holds ~1/4 of the history and the host pool all of it, so admissions evict but nothing is dropped. Mean (min-max), arms alternated, fresh server per run. | | main | this PR | | |---|---|---|---| | `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, eviction-bound: req/s (5 runs) | 113.0 (109.0-115.6) | 120.5 (117.8-122.4) | +6.6% | | TTFT p50 / p99 (ms) | 366 / 813 | 308 / 559 | -16% / -31% | | blocking D->H waits per eviction pass | 3.78 | 0.91 | -76% | | cache hit rate | 0.874 | 0.874 | same | | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` (full attention), eviction-bound: req/s (3 runs) | 83.7 | 86.2 | +3.1%, within noise | | `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, no eviction: req/s (3 runs) | 150.6 | 149.5 | neutral | The gain grows with victims per eviction pass (3.8 for gpt-oss-20b, 2.5 for Qwen3-8B). The first copy of each pass still waits for the in-flight forward; batching cannot remove that.
Reproduce on one GPU (run each checkout twice, compare the second runs) ```bash #!/bin/bash # One arm of the HiCache write_back eviction A/B on one GPU. Run it from an sglang checkout of # main, then from the PR checkout (same GPU, nothing else on it), and compare the printed lines. # A checkout's first server JIT-compiles kernels and runs slower: run each arm twice, compare second runs. # bash run_ab.sh main; bash run_ab.sh main; git checkout ; bash run_ab.sh pr; bash run_ab.sh pr # Defaults reproduce config G (gpt-oss-20b, device pool ~1/4 of the sessions' history, host pool holds # all of it). Env overrides: MODEL, PORT, DEVICE_TOKENS, HOST_GB, BENCH_ARGS. set -euo pipefail LABEL=${1:?usage: run_ab.sh
## Accuracy Tests Same KV and same eviction decisions, so no accuracy change. New tests, red on main and green here: - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_write_back_eviction_parity.py`: the batched and per-victim walks on a seeded multi-session workload (Full and Full+SWA, both cores) give the same residency and evicted/backed-up/loaded-back counters, with fewer waits. - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_write_back_eviction_batching.py`: one fenced submission and one wait per batch, and nothing a queued copy reads is freed before that wait. - 2 cases in `test_unified_radix_cache_hicache.py`, and `sglang-radix-tree` tests (942 -> 958). Overlaps https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43808 (same loop); whichever lands second rebases. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #41616183761](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41616183761) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #41616183399](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41616183399) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #41616183672](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41616183672) > [!TIP] > Base CI only covers the core cases, and its workload may not exercise your change. title: [Perf] dsv41: Use the Engram all-to-all lookup for decode and CUDA graphs
author: hnyls2002
body:
Follow-up to #46917 and #46925.

- `auto` now uses the Engram `all_to_all` lookup for decode batches and inside CUDA graphs too, not only for eager prefill. Only a prefill batch of uneven per-rank counts captured in a CUDA graph keeps the earlier collective.
- Equal per-rank counts (MAX_LEN batches, CUDA graphs) take the fixed-size collectives, which a graph can capture: `all_gatherv` already reduces to an all-gather for them, and the exchange uses `reduce_scatter_tensor` or `all_to_all_single`; uneven counts keep the variable-size ones.
- `auto` is resolved in one place, `resolve_engram_config` in `engram.py`: once per process at model construction, when the parallel layout is final, and recorded in `engram_config` (log: `Engram lookup auto -> ...`). The layers run the resolved lookup, and the per-step `_dp_exchange` choice is gone; server-argument resolution only validates explicit values.
- The DP lookup is one method per exchange: `_dp_reduce_scatter_lookup` and `_dp_all_to_all_lookup` beside `_dp_global_buffer_lookup`.
- An explicit `reduce_scatter` or `all_to_all` now applies to decode as well; `all_reduce` keeps the collectives used before `auto`.
- Docs: `auto` and its decode measurements.

Behavior change: DP-attention decode on CUDA with columns that divide over the TP group moves from the reduce-scatter to the all-to-all; the output is bitwise the same.

## Measurements

GB300, one host-table Engram layer, rank 1, us per layer:

| DP | Tokens per rank | `all_reduce` (us) | `reduce_scatter` (us) | `all_to_all` (us) | `auto` (us) |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | prefill 32K | 3,479.0 | 2,645.6 | 2,478.2 | 2,475.1 |
| 2 | decode 16 | 31.4 | 28.2 | 37.3 | 35.2 |
| 2 | decode 400 | 72.3 | 68.5 | 65.3 | 65.2 |
| 2 | decode 1,280 | 135.0 | 130.7 | 123.7 | 124.3 |
| 4 | prefill 32K | 5,861.4 | 3,819.1 | 2,463.2 | 2,460.4 |
| 4 | decode 16 | 49.6 | 33.7 | 42.1 | 41.6 |
| 4 | decode 400 | 105.5 | 101.2 | 69.2 | 70.1 |
| 4 | decode 1,280 | 193.3 | 187.1 | 130.5 | 131.2 |

Before this PR, decode used the reduce-scatter. In a decode microbenchmark under CUDA graphs on GB300, B300 and H200 (DP 2-8, 16 to 1,280 tokens per rank), `all_to_all` was faster in 35 of 48 shapes: from DP 4 it was up to 48% faster and at most 12 us behind at 64 tokens per rank or fewer; at DP 2 it was at most 20 us behind and up to 53 us ahead.

## Verification

- Bitwise check of the `EngramEmbedding` DP lookup on GB300 at DP 2 and 4, every `lookup` choice against `all_reduce`: prefill (uniform, skewed, one empty rank) and decode captured in a CUDA graph and replayed with new ids. All equal.
- `test_deepseek_v41_flash_gb300_dp2ep2.py` on GB300: passed, GSM8K 0.98, MMMU-Pro 0.79.
- The same recipe at attention DP 4 / EP 4, GSM8K: 0.985.

title: [Perf] Hunyuan3D: Skip redundant OBJ exports when generating GLB
author: charliechenye
body:
## Summary

Avoid two intermediate OBJ exports in the Hunyuan3D-2 **Shape + Paint → GLB** path:

- **Shape Save:** skip exporting the untextured Shape OBJ when Paint and GLB output are both enabled. Paint consumes the in-memory `shape_meshes`, not the saved OBJ.
- **Paint Postprocess:** export the final textured GLB directly, without first writing a textured OBJ and its auxiliary files.

Shape-only OBJ and Paint+OBJ output behavior remain unchanged. This is a two-file change with no new flags, dependencies, or helpers.

## H200 performance

One NVIDIA H200, eager (`torch.compile` off), lossless quality, 50 Shape / 50 Delight / 30 Paint steps, 32k geometry chunks, fixed input image and seed. Each comparison used an eight-visit ABBA sequence with fresh processes and native SGLang stage timings.

| Experiment | Comparison | E2E median | Stage-local improvement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P2: skip textured OBJ | Native → P2 | **25,038.80 → 23,733.69 ms (+5.21%)** | Paint Postprocess: **4,184.28 → 2,892.93 ms (−30.86%)** |
| P3: skip Shape OBJ | P2 → P2+P3 | **23,780.26 → 22,794.05 ms (+4.15%)** | Shape Save: **~958.81 → ~0.07 ms** |

These are **separate, sequential A/B comparisons**. The percentages should not be added, and no single combined Native → P2+P3 speedup is claimed.

## Correctness

- **P2, same live textured mesh:** direct GLB, OBJ-first-then-GLB, and repeated direct GLB exports from deep copies had matching GLB bytes and matching geometry, normals, UVs, texture pixels, bounds, and material properties for the tested mesh.
- **P3, live Shape mesh:** the original Shape OBJ export did not change the vertices or faces consumed by the pinned Paint remesh/UV path (bitwise equality for the tested mesh).
- **Output contracts:** H200 smoke tests passed for Shape-only OBJ, Paint+OBJ/MTL/PNG, and Paint+GLB. The candidate's GLB remained loadable with geometry and UVs.

GLB hashes across **independent model runs** varied even in the native baseline, so cross-run byte equality is not used as a correctness gate. Same-mesh parity and output-contract checks are the relevant evidence here.

## Scope and compatibility

- `hunyuan3d/shape.py`: make the Shape OBJ export conditional on whether Paint+GLB needs it.
- `hunyuan3d/paint.py`: export either the final GLB **or** textured OBJ, rather than both.
- Preserve existing output path metadata and artifact cleanup.

**Tradeoff:** Paint+GLB no longer leaves an intermediate Shape OBJ when Paint subsequently fails. The pinned pipeline has no supported resume-from-that-OBJ flow; this is an intentional change to intermediate artifacts, not the requested final output.

Experiments: [P2 direct-GLB ABBA](https://github.com/charliechenye/sglang-scripts/tree/exp/hunyuan3d-paint-obj-export-p2/experiments/hunyuan3d_paint_obj_export_p2) · [P3 ABBA, smoke, and live-mesh parity](https://github.com/charliechenye/sglang-scripts/tree/exp/hunyuan3d-shape-obj-skip-p3/experiments/hunyuan3d_shape_obj_skip_p3)

title: [Feat] diffusion: Support Hy-Nomas INT8 DiT and FP8 VAE checkpoints
author: trebladev
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

Add support for the official [Hy-Nomas](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy-Nomas) distilled INT8 DiT and PixelUMM FP8 VAE checkpoints to the existing Nomas pipeline introduced in #46124.

The INT8 DiT stores quantized weights and retains BF16 linear computation. The FP8 VAE uses block-scaled Triton FP8 GEMM.

## Modifications

- Validate official checkpoint metadata, layer manifests, tensor shapes and dtypes before loading.
- Load groupwise INT8 DiT weights through the parallel linear loaders, dequantize in FP32 for BF16 computation, and preserve FP32 scales across component moves.
- Load the FP8 VAE on meta, replace its 180 selected decoder projections, and stream weights through the existing VAE loader.
- Match the official SM89 activation quantization using 128×128 blocks and reuse the existing Triton block FP8 GEMM.
- Let the VAE model declare quantized projections and unused encoder weights while retaining strict decoder validation.
- Extend Nomas tests to cover checkpoint validation, serialization, parallel loading, quantized computation and dtype preservation


## Accuracy Tests

### Demo video

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8d2c514c-c3d8-4c0a-b999-b294f70bdd75



### Real-weight generation and reference comparison

Generated a video through the public DiffGenerator API on one RTX 4090 D with the official INT8 DiT, FP8 VAE and Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct text encoder.

Configuration: 352×640, 40 frames, 24 fps, 8 Euler steps, guidance scale 1, seed 42, structured JSON caption, and CPU offload for all three components.

| Comparison | Result |
|---|---|
| SGLang DiT replay vs. captured pipeline | All 8 predictions bitwise identical; all 775 scales remain FP32 |
| Official DiT vs. SGLang with shared text and main attention implementations | All 8 predictions and final latent bitwise identical |
| Video pixels using each implementation's attention and FP8 GEMM paths | PSNR 26.37 dB; mean SSIM 0.8277 |
| Video pixels with shared DiT attention, Triton vs. official CUTLASS VAE | PSNR 42.64 dB; mean SSIM 0.9920 |
| Video pixels with shared DiT attention and test-only official CUTLASS VAE linears | Bitwise identical |
| Standalone SGLang VAE replay vs. captured pipeline | Bitwise identical |

Pixel metrics are computed before MP4 encoding. PSNR uses raw outputs with data range 2; SSIM uses outputs normalized and clipped to [0, 1]. Shared-backend substitutions are for validation only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Test with 1 single 4090D, output 40 frames at 24 fps.

Smoke measurement with the configuration above:

| Metric | Result |
|---|---|
| Generation time | 69.52 s |
| Peak allocated GPU memory | 15,317 MiB |
| Peak reserved GPU memory | 16,158 MiB |

This measurement includes component transfers and cold execution. It is not a comparative performance benchmark.

title: [Fix] custom-all-reduce: Keep integer all-reduces off the custom all-reduce kernels
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Custom all-reduce v1 and v2 now return False from `should_custom_ar` for dtypes other than bf16, fp16 and fp32, the only ones their kernels reduce. v2 reads the list from `SUPPORTED_DTYPES` next to its JIT loader (`FloatTrait` in `communicator.cuh`); v1 keeps it beside `_SUPPORTED_WORLD_SIZES`. Other dtypes fall back to NCCL.
- `_dp_gather_via_all_reduce` sends integer rows to the in-place NCCL all-reduce at every TP size. It did so only up to TP 8, a stand-in for "the group fits on one node" that no longer holds on multi-node NVLink.

Since #46853, a multi-node NVLink group of 2-16 GPUs uses custom all-reduce v2 without a VMM-backed allocator. With DP attention and a TP size above 8, `_dp_gather_via_all_reduce` sends integer tensors to `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce`, which picked v2; v2 then failed to JIT-compile its kernel for the integer dtype:

```
RuntimeError: Failed to build JIT module sgl_kernel_jit_custom_all_reduce_int64_t_16_true ...
communicator.cuh(128): error: class "sglang::device::distributed::FloatTrait<int64_t>" has no member "kNegZero"
```

One case: DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram lookups at DEP16 across four GB300 nodes gather int64 hash ids this way on prefill batches.

No behavior change for floating-point all-reduces. Integer DP gathers above TP 8 take the in-place NCCL path instead of `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce`; before #46853 both ended in NCCL.

## Verification

- With the v2 dtype check alone (`107bbf81bc`), on four GB300 nodes (TP 16, DP attention 16, one NVLink domain), an Engram DP lookup benchmark that failed with the error above on main now runs to completion with custom all-reduce enabled, prefill and CUDA-graph decode, outputs bitwise equal across `all_reduce`, `reduce_scatter` and `auto`.
- Unit tests in `test/registered/unit/distributed/`, `test/registered/unit/layers/test_dp_attention.py` and `test_dp_attention_cp_replicas.py`: all pass.

title: [Perf] pd: Poll finished KV transfers while the prefill loop waits for a forward result
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

In the PD prefill overlap loop, a request whose KV transfer completes during a long forward step is noticed only after that step ends. While a forward result is pending, the loop blocks in the oldest result copy's `synchronize()` and calls `process_disagg_prefill_inflight_queue()` once per pass, so a transfer that finishes early in a step is retired only when the step is over:

```text
                 step N                       step N+1
GPU:   |========================|==================================|
                                ^ request's prefill done
                                post KV send, poll: Transferring
                                |-- transfer --|                    ^ poll: Success
                                               (done, unobserved)     KV released, output streamed
                                |<------ handoff = length of step N+1 ------>|
```

A short request that finishes behind a long prompt therefore waits for the whole following step before its KV cache is released and its output is streamed, even though the transfer itself took a small fraction of that time. On the decode side the first token is already out; this delay reaches the client only where the client waits for the prefill response (for example when it asks for prefill-side logprobs), but it always delays the prefill engine's KV release and metadata-slot reuse.

## Modifications

Add `SGLANG_DISAGG_PREFILL_POLL_TRANSFERS_WHILE_WAITING` (default off). When it is on and a transfer is in flight, the loop waits for the oldest result through the existing non-blocking readiness poll (the one continuous input polling uses) and calls `process_disagg_prefill_inflight_queue()` on every waiting pass, so finished transfers retire as soon as they complete:

```text
                 step N                       step N+1
GPU:   |========================|==================================|
                                ^ post KV send
                                poll  poll  poll: Success -> KV released, output streamed
                                |<- transfer ->|
```

- **Intake during the wait.** New requests and batches are taken while waiting only with `SGLANG_ENABLE_DISAGG_PREFILL_CONTINUOUS_INPUT_POLLING`. With only this flag, the loop takes no input until the result is ready, exactly as the blocking wait did; pause and shutdown requests land on the next pass.
- **Shared support check.** Both flags use one `_supports_result_wait_polling()` check: attention DP=CP=1, non-speculative, autoregressive generation, no dLLM. Under it the oldest result's copy is always submitted and the inflight queue is identical on all TP ranks; readiness is MIN-reduced, so every rank issues the same collectives in the same order and leaves the wait on the same pass. With attention DP or CP > 1, shards keep different inflight queues, so one shard could leave the wait while another enters the TP-wide readiness all-reduce; there the flag logs a warning once and the blocking wait stays.
- **Barrier order.** When the WAR barrier is deferred, finished transfers retire before the pending barrier is applied, matching the ordering of the regular result path.
- **Default path.** With the flag off, the loop is unchanged: the only new work is the flag read at loop entry.

Retiring a transfer while a forward runs (releasing its KV cache and metadata slot, streaming its output) already happens at the end of every step today; this change only moves the poll earlier.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model forward or sampling. The flag is off by default.

Unit tests in `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_result_polling.py` cover the new behaviour on CPU:

- transfers are polled during a result wait only when the flag is on, with and without continuous input polling;
- a blocking wait becomes a polling wait only when a transfer is in flight, and the result is processed exactly once;
- pause and shutdown ordering is preserved in both loops;
- the flag needs a supported loop (attention DP, CP, speculative, embedding and dLLM configurations warn and keep the blocking wait);
- under TP=2 (gloo), ranks whose copies finish on different passes still leave the wait on the same pass, with a collective asserted on every poll;
- a transfer that finishes while a result is pending is retired exactly once, its metadata slot is reused by the next admission, and a failed admission still retries only after the result;
- the deferred WAR barrier is applied after the transfer poll.

```
pytest test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_result_polling.py
16 passed, 57 subtests passed
pytest test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_abort_result_cleanup.py test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_complete_integration.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_disagg_idle_step_counters.py
46 passed, 76 subtests passed
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

With the flag on, the time from a request's KV transfer completing to its KV release and output stream drops from "the rest of the current forward step" to roughly one polling pass, which matters for short requests that finish behind a long prompt. No end-to-end numbers are included in this PR; the flag is opt-in and the default path is unchanged.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Perf] joy-image: Fuse image MLP GELU on SM120 in high quality
author: BBuf
body:
<!-- joy-current-head-cleanup-failure-20261030 -->
**Validation update (2026-10-30): official head `b08c24e9630c63790c9f86b48d6c7fc10a0c4301` failed the frozen square cleanup revalidation. The original model report below remains evidence for tested head `4c135ea92d6b4cbb0ead69bb39976f7dbe995455`; the later cleanup note already identifies that distinction. See “Current-head square revalidation: cleanup gate failed” at the end for new measurements and actual current-head images. The separate input-lifetime repair `03368cf1c325e526184b8fb223443e1ae931b13c` has now passed fresh square/wide model and cleanup gates plus native quality/profile checks; the final supplement contains those separate measurements and actual images. The merged head remains unchanged and its failed result is retained.**
<!-- /joy-current-head-cleanup-failure-20261030 -->

Joy Image Edit's BF16 image MLP runs a 4096-to-16384 projection followed by a separate tanh-GELU. On RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, the existing fused GEMM/GELU operator is faster for the model's large image-token dimension, while the smaller text projection regresses. The generic operator policy disables SM120 based on other model shapes.

This change opts only Joy's image MLP into the existing epilogue at `quality="high"`. It leaves the generic policy and text MLP unchanged. Eligibility requires SM120, BF16, contiguous batch-1 inputs with at least 7168 image tokens and the expected projection dimensions. The native single-reference buckets contain 7168–8192 image tokens. Active dynamic LoRA on the input projection, quantized/ineligible projections, unmatched devices, other shapes and `torch.compile` retain the original MLP. The quality decision is passed from the current request without persistent mutable model state; `exact` and `lossless` retain the original computation.

Validated source:

- Main: `af21e2b989e482cfdce39689126562f2209d53ac`.
- Candidate: `4c135ea92d6b4cbb0ead69bb39976f7dbe995455`.
- vLLM-Omni: `817d4c17feb702289a2d2b2cbacfd594c262b7a7`.
- Checkpoint: `jdopensource/JoyAI-Image-Edit-Diffusers@4b41fb25d961f37668750178ccbb380da326201c`. All36 runtime files are checked against the frozen HF content hashes.

On 2026-10-28, the Joy model, fused-linear helper, regression-test file and documentation at latest main `990ee89877f668304761d7551d803ed6b93d1673` were verified byte-identical to this frozen baseline. The benchmark source SHAs remain unchanged.

The two-file diff reuses the existing fused operator and static linear predicate, and adds one actual-MLP regression test. Full-diff cleanup review found no remaining experimental code, extra configuration or unrelated changes. The final commit contains the exact v4 patch used for the 48-output model quality run; fresh final-head servers requalify their images before every primary block.

## Performance

Final committed-source square and wide results are fully audited: all twelve planned comparison blocks and 120 outputs are present. The four final SGLang traces and both separate Omni native-profiler diagnostics are also audited.

| Workload | Source | Denoise p50 (s) | HTTP E2E p50 / p95 (s) | Sequential req/s | Max sampled NVML (MiB) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1024×1024 | SGLang main | 35.6274 | 36.0095 / 36.0168 | 0.027770 | 60223.4 |
| 1024×1024 | SGLang PR | 34.9200 | 35.2994 / 35.3233 | 0.028328 | 59805.4 |
| 1024×1024 | vLLM-Omni native compile | 37.1286* | 37.7202 / 37.7281 | 0.026512 | 66735.4 |
| 1792×512 | SGLang main | 30.1285 | 30.4694 / 30.4866 | 0.032820 | 58747.4 |
| 1792×512 | SGLang PR | 29.5247 | 29.8698 / 29.8798 | 0.033479 | 58711.4 |
| 1792×512 | vLLM-Omni native compile | 31.2797* | 31.8228 / 31.8328 | 0.031424 | 65525.4 |

For square, temporal-pair main/PR ratios are **1.020039916× / 1.020039914×**, geometric mean **1.020039915×** (1.9646% less latency). Omni/PR ratios are **1.068459208× / 1.068408881×**, geometric mean **1.068434044×** (6.4051% less latency). Every pair improves. Peak sampled NVML is 418 MiB lower than main for this square case. For wide, main/PR pair ratios are **1.020118214× / 1.020061684×**, geometric mean **1.020089949×** (1.9694% less latency). Omni/PR ratios are **1.065245650× / 1.065301669×**, geometric mean **1.065273659×** (6.1274% less latency). Every wide pair improves; the candidate's wide peak sampled NVML is 36 MiB below main.

Hardware: one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, 97887 MiB, driver 595.84); the second card is idle. SGLang uses Torch 2.14.1+cu130/Triton 3.8/cuDNN 9.24/diffusers 0.37; Omni uses Torch 2.13+cu130/Triton 3.7.1/cuDNN 9.20/diffusers 0.40. Both use transformers 5.19; exact package pins are archived.

Same physical GPU0, batch 1, concurrency 1, 30 steps, CFG 4, CPU seed 1101, empty negative prompt and frozen reference image. DiT, encoder and VAE are BF16 with native mixed-precision internals; the final runtime audit is included in the evidence. SGLang main and PR have identical traced CFG/solver tails: BF16 projection and CFG arithmetic, followed by FP32 norm normalization and solver updates. Omni’s scheduler input/output is BF16 with autocast off; its scheduler upcasts the sample internally to FP32 and casts the result back to BF16. This is the same BF16 component/no-quantization policy with native mixed precision, not identical intermediate arithmetic. The PR changes only the high-mode MLP epilogue. SGLang uses its native resident eager pipeline with cuDNN transformer attention and synchronized stage timing. Omni uses its native default regional compilation and CUDNN_ATTN. The primary prompt changes the red teapot to blue; long English and Chinese prompts check quality. The 512×1792 case is quality-only.

Protocol: main A/A, original-v1/final-head cleanup ABBA, then main/PR/Omni/Omni/PR/main per shape. Each final arm has two fresh processes and eight measured requests; every process performs four quality requests and two explicit warmups first. Existing disk/compiler caches are retained, so startup is not a cold-cache result. Every raw source/input/request/PNG hash and archived GPU ownership sample is audited; GPU1 remains idle. Profiling is separate. NVML sampling is every 250 ms during requests and can miss transient peaks. Sequential req/s is the reciprocal mean latency at concurrency 1; p95 is descriptive over eight samples.

Square main A/A process medians differ by 0.01527%, with maximum within-process CV 0.01925%. In final pairing, first/last main medians differ by 0.02328%, within the predeclared 0.5% limit; maximum within-process CV is 0.05645%. These are descriptive noise checks, not confidence intervals. Wide main A/A medians differ by 0.04261%, with maximum CV 0.02844%. Wide final first/last main medians differ by 0.01966%; maximum within-process CV is 0.05459%. All four wide pair improvements exceed the observed A/A envelope and the main endpoint check passes.

Cleanup retest: precleanup/final ratios **1.000489641× / 0.999740908×**, geometric mean **1.000115204×**. Final latency changes are −0.04894% / +0.02592%; both satisfy the prospectively fixed 0.1% screen. The mixed directions show no systematic aggregate regression, and do not establish a cleanup speedup. Final main/PR results above use the cleaned, committed implementation.

title: [Test] [NPU] deepseek_v4_flash: Switch FP8 4P GPQA test from EAGLE to DSPARK and add acceptance-rate test
author: YZY00Raiser
body: ## Motivation Migrate the Ascend NPU DeepSeek-V4-Flash FP8 4P GPQA test from EAGLE to DSPARK speculative decoding, add a DSPARK acceptance-rate throughput test for the 950 (A5) environment, and load the extra custom ops that DSPARK requires on A5 from the shared NPU e2e launcher. ## Modifications ### 1. Enable DSPARK runtime environment (`python/sglang/test/ascend/e2e/run_npu_testcase.sh`) Add three environment variables required to enable DSPARK for DeepSeek-V4 in the 950 environment: - `SGLANG_DSPARK_A5_EXTRA_OPS_SO` — path to the custom ops shared library (`/usr/local/Ascend/extra-ops/vllm_ascend_C.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so`). - `ASCEND_CUSTOM_OPP_PATH` — prepend the custom_transformer vendor path (`/usr/local/Ascend/extra-ops/vendors/custom_transformer/`). - `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` — prepend the custom_transformer `op_api/lib` path. ### 2. Model path and acceptance-rate assertion (`python/sglang/test/ascend/e2e/test_npu_performance_utils.py`) - Change `DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_DEFAULT_MODEL_PATH` from `.../DeepSeek-V4-Flash` to `.../DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`. - In `assert_metrics`, change the speculative acceptance-rate assertion from `assertGreaterEqual` to `assertGreater`, so `accept_length / --speculative-num-draft-tokens` must be strictly greater than the configured baseline. Both test cases that set `accept_rate` (the new `TestNPUDeepSeekV4FlashDSPARK` below and the existing `test_npu_deepseek_v4_flash_w8a8_8p_in8k_out1k_50ms.py`) now require `> 0.5` instead of `>= 0.5`. ### 3. title: [Fix] attention: Compute extend attention KV offsets in int64
author: xiaofei-zheng
body:
## Motivation

`_fwd_kernel` and `_fwd_kernel_unified` in `extend_attention.py` load a KV slot from `kv_indices` and multiply it by the KV buffer stride in the index dtype. With int32 `kv_indices` the product wraps once `slot >= 2^31 / stride`, which is 2,097,152 tokens for 8 KV heads x 128 head dim. The kernel then faults or, when the wrapped address is mapped, silently reads the wrong KV.

The aiter backend's CUDA-graph `cuda_graph_kv_indices` is int32 and is used as-is by the legacy target-verify path (NGRAM, EAGLE with topk > 1), so a long-running aiter server whose KV pool exceeds that size eventually crashes in `_fwd_kernel`. Spec-decode `kv_indices` built in `eagle_info.py` / `ngram_info.py` are also int32. The triton backend's own buffers are int64 and are not affected.

## Modifications

- `extend_attention.py`: cast the loaded slot to int64 before the address math in `_fwd_kernel` and `_fwd_kernel_unified`. This covers the `PAGE_SIZE == 1` and paged branches and any caller dtype.
- `test_triton_attention_kernels.py`: add `test_extend_attention_int32_kv_indices_above_2g`, which runs both kernels with int32 slots above `2^31 / stride` against the same data at low slots. The slots sit just below `2^32 / stride` so a wrapped offset reads zero rows in front of the buffer rather than faulting (~8.6 GB). On main both subtests fail (max abs diff 1.09 / 1.04); with this PR they pass.

## Accuracy Tests

Only addressing changes: for slots below 2^31 / stride the int64 cast leaves every offset unchanged, so outputs are unchanged.

MI355X (gfx950), torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0, triton 3.8.0, aiter `285579b62`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, CUDA graphs on, `amd/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV` with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --speculative-algorithm NGRAM`; the KV pool is 3,503,271 tokens. Every fault below is a `Memory Fault` in `_fwd_kernel` with grid `[24576, 32, 1]`:

- main `7fe5b127e4`, GSM8K (1319 questions, `--max-tokens 4096`): faults between questions 430 and 485 in three runs, when cumulative allocated slots reach about 2.1M.
- With the KV-scale fix (#47030) applied, `bench_serving` random 512 in / 4096 out, 600 prompts, concurrency 48: faults after 265 s. The same run on the triton backend completes.
- This PR, the same `bench_serving` run on aiter: all 600 requests complete (2.46M output tokens, 1792 s) without a fault.

Unit tests: `test_triton_attention_kernels.py` and `test_gemma4_unified_swa_virtual_ids.py` pass (18 tests, with `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI_AMD=1`).

MI325X (gfx942), torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0, aiter `285579b62`, main `cb55d77d37` with this patch: the new test fails on main and passes here (the two gfx950-only tests skip). NVIDIA is not tested.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`extend_attention_fwd`, 32 Q heads, 8 KV heads, head dim 128, bf16 KV, MI355X, median of 7 x 50 calls:

| Shape | int32 indices, main | int32 indices, this PR |
|---|---|---|
| verify bs 48, prefix 1024, extend 12, custom mask | 333.4 us | 332.2 us |
| verify bs 8, prefix 4096, extend 8, custom mask | 207.2 us | 206.2 us |
| prefill bs 4, prefix 2048, extend 512 | 231.9 us | 232.9 us |
| prefill bs 1, prefix 8192, extend 2048 | 873.2 us | 873.0 us |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Perf] dsv41: Read Engram rows in place by default for GPU tables over NVLink
author: hnyls2002
body:
Follow-up to #46955.

- With `--engram-config` `lookup` `auto` (the default) and the tables in GPU memory (the default), each rank now reads its tokens' Engram rows in place from the owning GPU, as `peer_read` does, when the TP group is one NVLink domain: one node with full NVLink, or one multi-node NVLink fabric such as GB300 NVL72. Otherwise `auto` keeps picking a collective. The choice is one more branch of `resolve_engram_config`, the single place `auto` is resolved since #46955, and the log says `Engram lookup auto -> peer_read`.
- `custom_all_reduce_utils.in_one_nvlink_domain`: the topology check, built from the existing NVLink helpers; the physical-GPU-id gather moves out of `can_use_custom_all_reduce_with_nvlink` into `gather_physical_device_ids` so both use it.
- Docs: `auto` and its measurements.

Behavior change: default DeepSeek-V4.1 deployments with TP > 1 over NVLink allocate the Engram shards through CUDA VMM and map their peers' shards at load, instead of running a collective per Engram layer per step. The shard per GPU is the same size. Host tables and explicit `lookup` values are unchanged.

## Measurements

One Engram layer, GPU tables, slowest rank, us per layer. Decode is replayed from a CUDA graph.

DP attention 8, `all_to_all` (what `auto` ran before) against `peer_read`:

| Case | GB300 a2a (us) | GB300 peer (us) | B300 a2a (us) | B300 peer (us) | H200 a2a (us) | H200 peer (us) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| prefill 1K tokens per rank | 770 | 124 | 414 | 56 | 305 | 65 |
| prefill 8K | 731 | 200 | 476 | 158 | 619 | 204 |
| prefill 32K | 1,541 | 554 | 1,421 | 504 | 2,050 | 684 |
| decode 1 token per rank (B300) | | | 38.8 | 9.7 | | |
| decode 16 | 47.7 | 9.8 | 48.9 | 11.5 | 33.5 | 5.7 |
| decode 1,024 | 92.4 | 23.1 | 98.5 | 25.5 | 105.7 | 27.2 |

GB300 DP 8 runs on two 4-GPU nodes of one NVL72 rack.

DP attention 16 and 32 on GB300 (the hash columns do not divide, so the collectives are the all-reduce and reduce-scatter):

| Case | DP16 reduce-scatter (us) | DP16 peer (us) | DP32 reduce-scatter (us) | DP32 peer (us) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| prefill 1K | 811 | 128 | 1,333 | 119 |
| prefill 32K | 15,552 | 559 | 31,216 | 567 |
| decode 16 | 76 | 10.3 | 118 | 10.0 |
| decode 1,024 | 569 | 24.1 | 1,119 | 24.3 |

Plain TP (no DP attention), all-reduce against `peer_read`:

| Case | B300 TP2 AR (us) | B300 TP2 peer (us) | B300 TP8 AR (us) | B300 TP8 peer (us) | GB300 TP8 AR (us) | GB300 TP8 peer (us) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

Every collective and `peer_read` returned the same rows (bitwise across lookups in one process under DP attention; equal output checksums across processes under plain TP).

title: [Perf] [AMD] aiter: Bucket decode paged-attention partitions by sequence length
author: xiaofei-zheng
body:
## Motivation

aiter decode on the non-MLA path calls `paged_attention_ragged` with `max_num_partitions = ceil(context_len / 256)`: 512 for Llama-3.1-8B, 160 for Qwen3-8B. The main kernel's grid is `(num_seqs, max_num_partitions, num_kv_heads)` and the value is baked into every decode CUDA graph. Blocks past a sequence's length exit early, but launching and scheduling them still costs time, and at high batch the cost is no longer hidden behind real work. In the microbench below, at batch 64 / 1536 tokens P=512 costs 19.8 µs more per call than P=16 (0.63 ms per 32-layer step); at batch 256 it costs 274 µs more (+93%).

## Modifications

- `graph_variants.py`: new `SeqLenBucketGraphVariants` picks the first bucket whose limit covers `max(seq_lens_cpu)`, else the fallback. It reads only the host copy; a missing, empty or device tensor selects the fallback.
- `base_attn_backend.py`, `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`: `AttentionBackend.get_decode_graph_variants` returns None by default; the decode runner asks the backend after the DSA / DSV4.1 factories and reuses the existing variant capture and replay code.
- `aiter_backend.py`: buckets `p16` (up to 4096 tokens) and `p128` (up to 32768), each kept only when 4x its partition count is at most `max_num_partitions`, plus `pmax` for any length. Llama gets p16 / p128 / p512, Qwen3 gets p16 / p160, models with fewer than 128 partitions get no buckets. Only plain decode with one token per request on the `paged_attention_ragged` path gets variants. Eager decode uses the same table when `spec_info` is None and `seq_lens_cpu` is present, so aiter never JIT-builds a new reduce kernel while serving. Spec decode, graphs captured without a variant, and the sync-free path without `seq_lens_cpu` keep `max_num_partitions`; an unknown capture label raises. The chosen count goes into the new `ForwardMetadata.decode_num_partitions`. Every choice keeps `partitions * 256 >= max seq_len`, since fewer partitions drop KV silently. The workspace stays sized for `max_num_partitions`.
- `environ.py`, `environment_variables.mdx`: `SGLANG_AITER_DECODE_PARTITION_BUCKETS` (default true); false disables bucketing.
- Tests: new `test_aiter_decode_partition_buckets.py` (AMD CI); `test_aiter_fp8_kv_scales_paths.py` and `test_aiter_fp8_q_unified_attention.py` add `decode_num_partitions` to the `ForwardMetadata` they build.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X (gfx950), torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0, sglang-kernel 0.4.10, aiter `285579b62`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, `--attention-backend aiter`, bf16, otherwise default server args. Base is main `cb55d77d37`. GSM8K with `python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 1319 --temperature 0 --max-tokens 4096` (1314 questions after the 5 few-shot examples):

| Model | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | 0.8067 / 0.8075 / 0.8097 (mean 0.8080) | 0.8082 / 0.8067 / 0.8044 (mean 0.8064) |
| Qwen3-8B | 0.9482 / 0.9444 / 0.9490 (mean 0.9472) | 0.9444 / 0.9475 / 0.9460 (mean 0.9460) |

Greedy outputs already differ between base runs. With a fourth base run, the share of questions scored the same is 96.75% base vs base and 96.27% base vs PR for Llama, 98.22% and 98.22% for Qwen3.

Unit tests: `test_aiter_decode_partition_buckets.py` fails 6/6 on main and passes 6/6 here. It covers the bucket table, selection boundaries (4096 / 4097 / 32768 / 32769), eager and capture partition counts, spec decode, and bit-exact output against `max_num_partitions` for bf16 and fp8 KV; a negative case checks that 16 partitions with a 4097-token request give a different result. The two touched aiter tests pass.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Microbench of `paged_attention_ragged` (32 q / 8 kv heads, head_dim 128, bf16 KV, page size 1), 32 calls captured in one CUDA graph, median of 100 replays, µs per call. `-` means fewer partitions than the sequence needs. Output is bit-identical to the smallest valid P in every case except batch 256 / 32768 tokens at P=512.

| Batch | Max seq | P=16 | P=32 | P=128 | P=160 | P=512 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 1536 | 16.8 | 17.3 | 17.6 | 17.7 | 25.0 |
| 64 | 1536 | 76.8 | 77.1 | 78.5 | 75.0 | 96.6 |
| 256 | 1536 | 294.7 | 298.8 | 319.7 | 340.7 | 568.4 |
| 64 | 8192 | - | 368.0 | 371.9 | 370.3 | 409.1 |
| 64 | 16384 | - | - | 710.2 | 704.9 | 760.3 |
| 64 | 32768 | - | - | 1449.7 | 1446.6 | 1480.8 |

`python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 1.0`, server `--attention-backend aiter --disable-radix-cache`; the mixed row uses `--dataset-name custom` with 304 prompts of 1024 tokens and 16 of 40000 tokens. Blocks of 4 runs in the order base, PR, PR, base; the first run of each block is dropped and each block reports the median of runs 2-4. Base and PR are the means of their two blocks; noise is the second base block vs the first.

| Workload (input / output, concurrency) | Output throughput, base → PR (tok/s) | Median TPOT, base → PR (ms) | Noise, throughput / TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|
| Llama 1024 / 1024, c64 | 7076 → 7657 (+8.2%) | 7.55 → 6.86 (−9.1%) | +0.3% / +0.3% |
| Llama 1024 / 1024, c256 | 8731 → 12740 (+45.9%) | 26.47 → 17.19 (−35.1%) | −0.5% / +0.5% |
| Qwen3 1024 / 1024, c64 | 7144 → 7254 (+1.5%) | 7.40 → 7.26 (−1.9%) | +0.4% / −0.4% |
| Qwen3 1024 / 1024, c256 | 10670 → 11810 (+10.7%) | 21.05 → 18.74 (−11.0%) | +0.2% / −0.2% |

| Qwen3 30000 / 256, c8 | 218.5 → 218.4 (−0.06%) | 23.71 → 23.65 (−0.3%) | −0.5% / +0.3% |
| Llama 8192 / 512, c32 | 1729 → 1758 (+1.7%) | 14.69 → 14.37 (−2.2%) | −0.6% / +0.5% |
| Llama 1024 / 1024 with 5% of prompts at 40000, c64 | 2253 → 2255 (+0.08%) | 23.74 → 23.80 (+0.3%) | +0.1% / −0.3% |

The TPOT drops match the microbench: P=512 vs 16 at batch 64 and 256 accounts for 0.63 and 8.8 ms per Llama step (measured 0.69 and 9.3 ms); P=160 vs 16 at batch 256 accounts for 1.7 ms per Qwen3 step (measured 2.3 ms). TTFT changes by at most 1.0%.

Startup, median over all server logs of the runs above (decode graphs for batch sizes up to 512): Llama capture 8.0 s → 13.1 s, graph memory 1.61 → 1.81 GB; Qwen3 8.3 s → 11.2 s, 1.43 → 1.54 GB. `max_total_num_tokens` is unchanged (1698595 and 1508113).

MI325X (gfx942), torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0, aiter `285579b62`, main `cb55d77d37` with this patch, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, same method: 1024 / 1024 c64 5086 → 5335 tok/s (+4.9%, noise 0.0%), TPOT 11.71 → 11.12 ms; c256 6137 → 8181 tok/s (+33.3%, noise +0.1%), TPOT 38.79 → 28.33 ms. <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
AITER varlen routed every varlen call on gfx942 to AITER's Triton kernel, working around a hang on MiniMax-H3's packed sequences reported in #33275. The condition was architecture alone, with no shape, length or head-count qualifier, so MI300X/MI325X never reached the FAv3 kernel for any model or any shape.

The hang does not reproduce. 
Across every varlen shape H3 submits, all four Ulysses degrees, 28K to 104K rows, including the zero-length second segment that occurs whenever the used length is a multiple of 64, the FAv3 kernel completes and is 6.6-27% faster (median 15.1%), matching the Triton output to bf16 accumulation noise.

title: [Perf] [AMD] kda: Narrow the Kimi-K3 TP8 KDA recurrent tile for small batches on gfx950
author: yuychang
body:
## Motivation

Kimi-K3 at TP8 has 12 KDA heads per GPU. The recurrent KDA update (`fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update`) uses a value tile of 32 with one warp, which gives only 48 workgroups for a small batch, too few to fill an MI355X. With speculative decoding and ReplaySSM, this kernel runs on every verify step, and plain decode uses it when the fused KDA decode kernel is not armed.

## Modifications

- On gfx950, for KDA with 12 heads, head dim 128 and at most 4 requests, use a value tile of 8 with one warp. Everything else keeps the current launch.
- One warp keeps the same reduction order, so outputs, the recurrent state and the ReplaySSM rings are bit-identical to the default launch.
- New test `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_recurrent_launch_gfx950.py` (MI35x suite): checks which batches take the narrow tile, and that verify (with ReplaySSM rings) and decode (with state update) are bitwise equal to the default launch. 7 passed.

## Accuracy Tests

Outputs are bit-identical to the default launch (checked by the new test for verify and decode, n = 1 and 4), so model accuracy cannot change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel, one MI355X, bf16 state, cold L2 (a 1 GiB buffer is written before each call), median of 200 calls, two alternating passes per config, measured on two GPUs (they agree within 4 points):

| Mode | Requests | Tokens per request | Default (us) | Narrow tile (us) | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| verify | 1 | 4 | 12.7 | 10.2 | -20% |
| verify | 1 | 8 | 19.9 | 15.2 | -24% |
| verify | 4 | 4 | 13.0 | 11.1 | -15% |
| verify | 4 | 8 | 20.4 | 17.2 | -16% |
| decode | 1 | 1 | 7.9 | 6.4 | -19% |
| decode | 4 | 1 | 8.0 | 6.9 | -10% to -14% |

End to end: 8x MI355X, `Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`, TP8, DSpark block 3 with ReplaySSM, real acceptance, Kimi-K3 integration build (A/B toggles only this change). Random 8192 in / 1024 out, 16 prompts per concurrency level with warm-up, 3 servers per side, alternating. Median TPOT:

| Concurrency | Default | Narrow tile | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4.37 ms | 4.30 ms | -1.6% |
| 4 | 6.90 ms | 6.86 ms | -0.6% |

title: [Fix] kernels: Hash tensors over 8 GiB in gpu_tensor_hash
author: g0djan
body:
## Motivation

`gpu_tensor_hash` computes each tile's offset as `pid * TILE` in int32. For a tensor over 8 GiB (2**31 words), the offset wraps negative and the kernel reads before the buffer: `CUDA error: an illegal memory access`.

`/weights_checker` with `action=checksum` hashes every weight with this kernel, so it crashes the engine on any model with a tensor over 8 GiB per rank. We hit it on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP 8, where each rank's engram table slice is 12.3 GB.

## Modifications

- Compute the offset in int64. Tensors under 8 GiB hash to the same values as before.
- Add a test that hashes a tensor just over 8 GiB (it fails without the fix), and one that pins the hash of a small tensor.

## Accuracy Tests

The change affects hashing only, not model outputs. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (8×B300, TP 8, EP 8), the `/weights_checker` checksum failed before the fix. With the fix, it succeeds in 6.9 s and the engine stays healthy.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hashing a 4 GiB tensor on a B300 takes 2.94 ms before and 2.99 ms after (about 1.7% slower). The kernel isn't on the forward path.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] moe: Add H20 block-FP8 Triton configs for Qwen3-30B-A3B
author: vincentbryan
body:
## Motivation

With plain tensor parallelism (no `--ep`), Qwen3-30B-A3B runs its routed experts through the Triton fused MoE kernel. On H20, at `moe_tp_size = 1` (TP1 serving, or one replica per GPU), the serving lookup is `E=128,N=768` with `fp8_w8a8` and `block_shape=[128, 128]`.

The lookup key is derived from the kernel's per-rank shape, not from the model: `N = moe_intermediate_size / moe_tp_size`, and `E` grows by the fused shared expert. So the same model served with `--tp-size 8` looks up `E=128,N=96` and keeps the heuristic — these configs cover the `moe_tp_size = 1` geometry only. Conversely, any model whose expert geometry is `E=128, N=768, fp8_w8a8, block=[128,128]` picks these files up regardless of its name; `top_k` and `hidden_size` are not part of the key.

`triton_3_8_0` has no config for that shape (main pins torch 2.14.1, which ships Triton 3.8.0), so the runner falls back to the `triton_3_3_1` entry — five Triton versions stale — and logs:

```
Config file not found at .../triton_3_8_0/E=128,N=768,device_name=NVIDIA_H20,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128, 128].json.
Fallback to triton version 3.3.1 ... Performance might be sub-optimal!
```

## Modifications

Adds one file, `triton_3_8_0/E=128,N=768,device_name=NVIDIA_H20,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128, 128].json`, covering the 18 default batch sizes.

Tuned with the stock `benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton/tuning_fused_moe_triton.py` on 8x H20 96 GB, default 1280-config search space, `--tp-size 1 --dtype fp8_w8a8`, i.e. the `moe_tp_size = 1` geometry described above.

Because the tuner measures each candidate once, its pick was re-verified per batch size against four other candidates — the `triton_3_3_1` fallback, the heuristic default, and three hand-picked shapes — three repetitions each, median kept. That pass changed the winner for several batch sizes, notably M=64/96/128 (BM=16/BN=128 instead of BM=16/BN=64) and M=4096 (the 3.3.1 shape instead of BM=128/BN=64). Each number below is a re-measured median, not a single-shot tuner sample.

The separate down-projection (`_down`, TMA) configs from `tuning_fused_moe_triton_sep.py` are not included; serving keeps reusing the up config for the down GEMM, as it does today.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — kernel tile parameters only, no change to numerics or model code.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Single MoE layer kernel time, 8x H20 96 GB, Triton 3.8.0 / CUDA 13.0 / driver 580.126.20:

| M | 3.3.1 fallback (us) | this config (us) | delta | vs heuristic (us) |

title: [Feat] [NVIDIA] runtime: Add a master switch for megakernel runtime optimizations
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

Enable the runtime optimizations accompanying NVIDIA megakernels with one opt-in switch across model paths, instead of carrying a long list of per-optimization environment variables in launch recipes.

## Modifications

- Add `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION=0` (default). The `SGLANG_ENABLE_` name follows the env-var conventions.
- Reuse `EnvField`'s generic lazy callable-default mechanism: each included `EnvBool` has `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION.get` as its default. Resolution stays in `environ.py`; call sites and existing capability checks are unchanged.
- **Explicit child values take precedence**, including `0`/`false` with the master on and `1` with the master off. **Unset children follow the master**. The **master defaults off**, preserving current defaults. `.set(None)` retains the existing explicit-None behavior. This switch does not enable the megakernel backend itself.
- Upcoming megakernel follow-up PRs will use this switch instead of adding their own master switch.

Included switches (verified with `git show`, `git log`, and `git blame` against main `4517a5ff1bbd1f944d6bde1819300ed14af7b698`; DSv4.1 source commit `c82f7141ad`, Qwen3.5 source commit `b74fd392e1`):

| Child environment variable | Introduced by | Runtime behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SGLANG_DSPARK_FUSED_ACCEPT_TAIL` | [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450) | Fuse the static greedy accept tail |
| `SGLANG_DSPARK_DEFER_CONTEXT_KV` | [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450) | Defer draft context-KV commits with existing eligibility checks |
| `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_DRAFT_PREP_FORK` | [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450) | Overlap draft metadata preparation with embedding |
| `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_POST_FOLD` | [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450) | Fold verify sequence-length and bonus scatters into the graph |
| `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_SKIP_PREFILLED_INPUTS` | [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450) | Avoid re-copying already staged verify inputs |
| `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_BLOCKWISE_REJECTION` | [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450) | Use distribution-preserving blockwise rejection sampling |
| `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_ONE_LAUNCH_COMMIT_STAGE` | [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450) | Stage the deferred commit in one launch |
| `SGLANG_OPT_MXFP4_DEFERRED_FINALIZED_SHAPE` | [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450) | Use finalized output shapes for deferred MXFP4 tactic-cache lookup |
| `SGLANG_OPT_CUDA_GRAPH_FILL_FAST_PATH` | [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450) | Skip no-op padding resets and group dense integer copies |
| `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_PREPARE_INPUTS_ONCE` | [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450) | Prepare the DSpark verify window and draft anchor once |
| `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_MID_FOLD` | [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450) | Write folded draft tokens directly into the sampler buffer |
| `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_TARGET_VERIFY_METADATA_GLUE` | [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450) | Capture backend-declared host-free target verify metadata preparation |
| `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_TARGET_METADATA_EARLY` | [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450) | Overlap eligible target metadata preparation with the draft graph |
| `SGLANG_OPT_SKIP_GLUED_REPLAY_VIEW` | [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450) | Avoid rebuilding replay views after metadata glue is captured |
| `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_POST_FORWARD_CUDA_GRAPH` | [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450) | Commit Engram history in the static verify epilogue |
| `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_SAMPLING_ACCEPT_GRAPH` | [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450) | Capture eligible sampled DSpark acceptance and commits |
| `SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH` | [#45474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45474) | Capture eligible EAGLE post-verify sampling and commits |
| `SGLANG_Q35MF_BK_VEC_COPY` | [#45474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45474) | Vectorize small-field copies |
| `SGLANG_Q35MF_MKH_N3B` | [#45474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45474) | Reuse unchanged Mamba tracking indices and already staged verify inputs |
| `SGLANG_Q35MF_MKH_N3C` | [#45474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45474) | Stage post-verify inputs in one launch (does not enable simulated acceptance) |
| `SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_CHAIN_TREE` | [#45474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45474) | Build a chain tree for topk-1 TRT-LLM MHA verify |
| `SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SPARSE_VERIFY_SAMPLING` | [#45474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45474) | Sample on eligible finite top-k support |
| `SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_PACKED_VERIFY_BCAST` | [#45474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45474) | Broadcast packed verify results once |
| `SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SHM_SYNC` | [#45474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45474) | Use same-host shared-memory scheduler synchronization |
| `SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SHM_SYNC_MULTIHOST` | [#45474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45474) | Use hierarchical synchronization for eligible whole-world multi-host groups |
| `SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_MULTIHOST_TCP` | [#45474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45474) | Use a TCP leader exchange for eligible two-host groups |
| `SGLANG_ENABLE_GDN_PREFILL_GRAPH_EXTEND` | [#45474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45474) | Capture supported target Triton GDN prefill extends |

Excluded / independent:

| Switch or group | Source / reason |
| --- | --- |
| `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_SIM_DRAW_AHEAD` | [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450); `sim_draw_ahead_enabled` only acts when simulated acceptance lengths exist. |
| `SGLANG_SIMULATE_*`, `SGLANG_DSPARK_SIMULATE_FOLD`, fake/forced/test controls | Preserve explicit configuration and benchmark semantics. `SGLANG_ENABLE_DSPARK_SIMULATE_SKIP_SAMPLING` is not registered on this main baseline; this PR does not add it. |
| `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MEGA_MHC_PREFILL` | [#42808](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42808); selects a model kernel, outside the accompanying runtime switch group. |
| `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_BF16_INDEX_LOGITS` | [#45880](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45880); independent kernel precision override with an auto (`None`) default. |
| `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_STAGING` | [#45921](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45921); separate host-table prefill optimization whose tradeoff depends on batch size and ATS support. |
| `SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE`, `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_ENGRAM_PEER_SHARDS`, layout and sizing controls | Placement/backend/capacity configuration, outside the runtime group. Peer-shard lookup originates in [#46180](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46180). |
| `SGLANG_ENABLE_METADATA_GLUE_GRAPH` | Predates these follow-ups ([#33561](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33561)); the DSpark-specific metadata switches above remain backend guarded. |

### Mapping to the existing model recipes

- **DSv4.1 / DSpark ([#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450)):** the runtime recipe contains the 16 included DSv4.1 switches plus `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_SIM_DRAW_AHEAD`. The latter remains explicit when simulated acceptance is used. The master additionally enables the Qwen3.5 group; most of that group is inactive on this path, but the shared scheduler synchronization and replay input-staging paths below can apply.
- **Qwen3.5 / EAGLE MTP ([#45474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45474)):** the runtime group contains the 11 included Qwen3.5 switches. The master additionally enables the DSv4.1 group; most of that group is inactive on this path, but the shared graph-fill and captured-metadata replay paths below can apply.
- Settings outside these groups remain explicit in the recipes, including `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MEGA_MHC_PREFILL`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_METADATA_GLUE_GRAPH` and `SGLANG_EAGER_INPUT_NO_COPY`, where used. Simulation, placement, backend and numeric tuning settings are not replaced by the master.

For the **dedicated DSpark target-verify glue/early path**, the generic `SGLANG_ENABLE_METADATA_GLUE_GRAPH` is not a prerequisite: with the master on and all three child/generic settings unset, both DSv4.1 child switches resolve to true and the eligible runner creates its own metadata glue graph. Explicitly enabling generic metadata glue instead creates `_metadata_glue` first, bypassing `_target_metadata_glue` selection and its early-metadata path. Keep generic-glue recipe settings specific to the path they were measured with.

These four shared switches extend beyond the model-specific recipe in which they were measured:

| Model receiving an additional optimization | Switch | Why it is intended to preserve outputs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DSv4.1 / DSpark | `SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SHM_SYNC` | Single-host TP4 scheduler TP syncs exchange the same values through a shared-memory table. Its multi-host companion switches apply only to eligible group/topology configurations. |
| DSv4.1 / DSpark | `SGLANG_Q35MF_MKH_N3B` | The generic decode/verify replay `_restage_skip` path checks tensor identity, `_version` and stream before skipping duplicate input copies; unchanged Mamba tracking indices are reused only where that state exists. |
| Qwen3.5 / EAGLE MTP | `SGLANG_OPT_CUDA_GRAPH_FILL_FAST_PATH` | Without padding, `reset_padding` is already a no-op; the dense integer copy fast path writes the same fields. |
| Qwen3.5 / EAGLE MTP | `SGLANG_OPT_SKIP_GLUED_REPLAY_VIEW` | Applies when metadata glue is enabled, including the `SGLANG_ENABLE_METADATA_GLUE_GRAPH=1` setting used for #45474's measurements. For an already captured key, `MetadataGlueGraph.run` does not read `fb_view`; calling `replay()` reinstalls and replays the same metadata. |

**GPU A/B on both models (below) measured these paths on the receiving model:** no measurable effect on throughput, prefill latency or accuracy. Explicit child `0` remains available to disable each path.

The remaining model/backend-specific switches are inactive on the other cited recipe: DSpark paths check the DSpark algorithm and their worker/backend/static-graph conditions; EAGLE post-verify and GDN capture have their own worker/backend gates; chain-tree construction applies only to TRT-LLM MHA; the vectorized small-field copy is consumed by EAGLE post-verify graphs; and the Qwen3.5 recipe uses NVFP4 rather than the MXFP4 path. Deferred context-KV retains its cache, disaggregation and attention-DP eligibility checks. EAGLE graphs require CUDA, topk-1 and no attention-DP, with eager fallback for unsupported batches; GDN capture checks the target worker, Triton kernel, layouts and buckets. No additional model-name restrictions are introduced.

### Broader backend applicability

`SGLANG_OPT_MXFP4_DEFERRED_FINALIZED_SHAPE` affects **any model using deferred-finalize MXFP4 trtllm-gen MoE**, including the `deepseek_v2` / DeepSeek-V3, `deepseek_v4`, `minimax_m3`, `mimo_v2` and `kimi_k3` model paths. It changes the FlashInfer tactic-cache key for 33–96 rows and more than 384 rows by supplying the finalized output shape. This setting was tuned only on DSv4.1; its performance on those other model paths has not been validated here.

## Accuracy Tests

- CPU `test/registered/unit/test_environ.py`: **14 tests passed**, including master off/on/off, all 27 children, explicit `0`/`false`/`1` precedence, unset restoration, explicit `None`, and unchanged defaults throughout the rest of the registry (including simulation controls).
- Compared all **785 existing env defaults** against main: identical with the master off; with it on, exactly the 27 listed switches change to true.
- **GPU (GB300), GSM8K via `sgl-eval`, 200 questions, real acceptance.** A = each model's recipe with its child switches set explicitly; B = the same recipe with those children removed and only `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION=1`. No errors, empty or garbled outputs in any run.

| Model | Mode | A accuracy | B accuracy | A accept length | B accept length |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B NVFP4 (TP8, MTP) | greedy | 95.0% | 95.0% | 5.446 | 5.446 |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B NVFP4 (TP8, MTP) | T 0.6 / top-k 20 / top-p 0.95 | 97.0% | 95.5% | 4.817 | 4.717 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP4, DSpark) | T 0 | 98.0% | 98.0% | 3.747 | 3.710 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP4, DSpark) | T 1.0 | 95.5% | 97.5% | 3.567 | 3.660 |

Qwen3.5 greedy outputs are identical for all 200 questions. The sampled differences are within the ±1.3-point standard error of a 200-question run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GB300, `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261028-586355a8`, this PR's code (`3f7fa97971`; later commits only touch the test file) with the NVIDIA megakernel plugin enabled. Both arms use the same source, image, plugin, slots and frozen autotune results; their resolved environments differ only in the child switches versus the master. TPS/User = 1 / per-request ITL.

- **Qwen3.5-397B-A17B NVFP4**, TP8 across two trays, MTP (top-k 1, 7 draft tokens), recipe of #45474 with its 11 switches, plugin `sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega@3bd8c0ba45` (slots `route,mkm,gdn_verify,gdn_pdl,hop,draft_loop,draft_extend`), synthetic acceptance 4.8.
- **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** (rev `df42c109f1d`), TP4, DSpark, recipe of #45450 with its 16 switches, plugin `sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega@9a21cb037a` with #45450's slots minus `engram`, synthetic acceptance 3.51. Both arms add #46864 so that simulated acceptance keeps the stock accept sampling, as in #45450's measurements. The `engram` slot was dropped from both arms because that plugin commit still read `_HostTable.layout`, which #46893 renamed (fixed since in sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega#29).

**Static decode** (one untimed warm-up sweep per arm. Qwen3.5: about 590 decode rounds × 3 repeats per point, A→B on one node pair and B→A on another, mean of the two pairs. DSv4.1: 30 timed requests at c1 and 40 at c8, A then B on the same node):

| Model | Point | A TPS/User | B TPS/User | (B−A)/A |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3.5 | c1, 8K context | 987.4 | 985.9 | −0.15% |
| Qwen3.5 | c1, 128K context | 881.9 | 880.5 | −0.16% |
| DSv4.1 | c1, ISL 8K / OSL 1K, T 0 | 1044.2 | 1044.0 | −0.02% |
| DSv4.1 | c1, ISL 8K / OSL 1K, T 1.0 | 1011.4 | 1016.4 | +0.50% |
| DSv4.1 | c8, ISL 8K / OSL 1K, T 0 | 494.3 | 495.6 | +0.26% |

**InferenceX AgentX, 3600 s** (one run per arm, both arms in parallel on different nodes):

| Model | Metric | A | B | (B−A)/A |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3.5, c7 | TPS/User P50 / P90 | 904.7 / 865.5 | 910.8 / 868.3 | +0.68% / +0.33% |
| Qwen3.5, c7 | tok/s/GPU | 5,364.6 | 5,348.4 | −0.30% |
| DSv4.1, c1 | TPS/User P50 / P90 | 965.6 / 942.2 | 967.3 / 943.5 | +0.19% / +0.14% |
| DSv4.1, c1 | tok/s/GPU | 8,114.6 | 8,114.1 | −0.01% |
| DSv4.1, c1 | TTFT P50 / E2EL P90 | 0.468 / 5.562 s | 0.445 / 5.564 s | −4.8% / +0.0% |

**Prefill latency on Qwen3.5.** In the AgentX pair above, B's TTFT was 24 ms higher at the**Prefill latency on Qwen3.5.** In the AgentX pair above, B's TTFT was 24 ms higher at the median of 1,545 matched requests. A same-node A→B rerun at c1 then showed cold 8K-token prompts 4.1% slower to first token in B (other prompt lengths and cached-prefix prompts moved less than 3%). To isolate the only B-only switch that can touch prefill here, `SGLANG_OPT_CUDA_GRAPH_FILL_FAST_PATH` was toggled inside one running server (it is read on every call) over 8 interleaved blocks on each of two boots: the difference was +0.30 ms, 95% CI [−1.7, +2.3] ms, and traces of both settings are identical (the fast path does not engage on this prefill registry, whose slots mix dtypes). Within a single process, cold 8K TTFT drifts by about 2 ms between blocks, so the 4% and the AgentX TTFT gap are run-to-run variation, not a cost of the master; the DSv4.1 pair shows a similar-sized TTFT difference in the other direction.

e DSv4.1 AgentX runs inherited `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` and `NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1` from the default environment (confirmed in every rank's NCCL log). With the deferred commit on (A and B), none of the 209 measurable requests above 256K tokens showed a 45–105 ms gap before the last streamed token (largest 37.7 ms). A third run, B plus `SGLANG_DSPARK_DEFER_CONTEXT_KV=0`, was 1.5% / 1.6% slower at TPS/User P50 / P90 than B, so the deferred commit stays in the master group.

title: [Perf] rust-server: Flatten egress logprob columns only for rows that carry them
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

In Rust frontend mode, `RustServer.push_generation` runs on the scheduler thread every step, with the GIL held, and flattens the batch's logprob columns into the frame the embedded Rust server decodes. Its per-family filter tested whether a column had any entries. But the output streamer gives every request in a batch with any logprob request a cell in all twelve logprob columns, most of them empty, so the filter never skipped a family: every pair family visited every row of the batch, one bound-method call per row, and filled its value buffer with a per-element `array.extend`. A batch of a few hundred requests in which one asks for logprobs paid that cost for all of them, on the scheduler's critical path.

## Modifications

Each `*Columns` family in `utils/flatten.py` gets `fill(batch_size)` in place of the per-row `accept(i)`, and `push_generation` calls it once per family:

- `fill` finds the rows whose cell carries data (`any`, then `itertools.compress`, both in C), flattens only those rows, and scatters their lengths into place, 0 for every other row.
- A family no row carries stays empty. The Rust decoder already reads an empty column as absent (`per_req_ok` admits it, `lens_i` reads 0 for every request), and the `header_cols`/`data_cols` loops still walk every family, so column order and arity are unchanged.
- Buffers are filled with `array.fromlist` over one flattened list instead of per-element `extend`. A single carried row, such as a prefill's input logprobs over a long prompt, is appended without the flattening copy.
- The idx/val parity asserts are kept, per row and, for the ragged families, per position. The now-unused `flatten_ragged` helper is removed; nothing else referenced it.

No Rust change. The data buffer is byte-identical to before. The header differs only in that a family no row carries is sent as `[]` rather than one 0 per request, which the decoder treats identically.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model numerics change. The logprob values that reach the client are the same floats in the same order as before; only the Python code that lays them out in the frame changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No benchmark numbers in this PR. The Python work per step is now proportional to the rows that carry logprob data rather than to the batch size times the number of families: `fill` flattens only the rows with data and bulk-fills the value buffers, and a batch without any logprob request takes the existing path unchanged.

## Testing

- New unit test `test_mixed_logprob_batch_frame` in `test/registered/unit/multimodal/rust/shared/test_rust_server_extension.py` (CPU CI). It builds a four-row batch in which each family is carried by a different subset of rows (input logprobs with the leading `None`, a null top-k position, token-id logprobs, hidden states, and one family no row carries), decodes the frame in `for_each_chunk`'s column order, and checks that every row reads back its own cells and that the uncarried family's header columns are empty. Against the previous `server.py`/`flatten.py`, every value check passes and the empty-family check fails with `([0, 0, 0, 0], []) != ([], [])`.
- `pytest test/registered/unit/multimodal/rust/shared/test_rust_server_extension.py`: 5 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files` on the three changed files: passed.

title: [Perf] moe: Fill padded rows of large narrow buffers with a strided grid
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

`_fill_padded_rows` (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fill_padded_rows.py`) sets every padded row of a 2D buffer (rows `>= num_token_non_padded`) to a fill value with one Triton launch. The grid is one program per row, and a program whose row is live exits immediately. For a large buffer of narrow rows whose padding is a short suffix, the launch is therefore dominated by programs that do nothing, and its cost scales with the buffer rather than with the tail.

## Modifications

- For buffers with at least `2 * 1024` rows whose rows are at most 2 KB, the kernel launches 1024 programs (`STRIDED=True`). Program `p` owns rows `p, p + 1024, ...`; it starts at its last owned row and walks down while the row is padding. Padding is a suffix, so stopping at the first live row is exact. The pad count is still read from device memory inside the kernel, so the launch remains safe to capture in a CUDA/HIP graph.
- Every other shape keeps the one-program-per-row launch, as a separate compile-time branch (`STRIDED=False`): wider rows already stream at full bandwidth with one program per row.
- Both branches compute the row offset in int64. The previous int32 `row * stride_row` overflows for buffers with more than 2^31 elements.
- The result is bitwise identical to the eager `arange + (>=) + index_put_` reference on every shape; only the launch geometry changes. No new flags.

## Testing

- `test/registered/moe/test_topk_padded_region.py` gains `TestFillPaddedRowsStrided`: it patches the program cap down to 3 so that every residue class and every pad count (0 through rows + 2, including all-live and all-padding) is checked against the eager reference on 1 to 13 rows, then checks a large narrow-row buffer with the real cap. The existing tests in the file cover the per-row branch and CUDA-graph replay.
- On this branch, on one Blackwell GPU: `pytest test/registered/moe/test_topk_padded_region.py` gives 9 passed, 3 skipped (the HIP-only cases), 39 subtests passed; `pre-commit run --files` on both files passes.
