title: [Fix] multimodal: Preserve strong identities across VLM caches
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Multimodal cache equality must depend on actual model-facing content, not a short scalar or a caller-provided hint. The old GPU reduction admits structured collisions, composite keys lose information through `hash(tuple(...))`, and matching only part of a media placeholder can still reuse unrelated KV state.

This is a correctness-first fix across the shared VLM paths, not a model-specific opt-in or a universal speedup claim.

## Modifications

- Add shared CPU/GPU BLAKE3-256 with typed shape/dtype/container/metadata identities. GPU tensors transfer only their digests to the host.
- Preserve full identities through embedding caching, batch deduplication, sessions, EPD and native Rust sidecars. Rust output digests use full SHA-256 and bind the serving configuration at ingress.
- Namespace KV requests using ordered full media identities and `cache_salt`. Short or partial placeholder matches cannot substitute for complete identity equality.
- Stop allowing caller `mm_hashes` to override content identity, including precomputed embeddings. Keep the separate explicit `--trust-mm-content-hashes` boundary documented.
- Preserve Kimi source/config/grid protections; cover composite processors and finalized OCR metadata. Reuse full Qwen/Muse artifact fingerprints on cache hits instead of rehashing their feature tensors.
- Add common-contract, kernel, native/transport and real Qwen input regressions, plus documentation of compatibility and prefix-sharing tradeoffs.

The GPU BLAKE3 kernel is adapted from @xupinjie's #46028; author credit is preserved. Related narrower work: #44653, #46552, #46815 and #47066. This PR does not modify diffusion conditioning caches or include #37537.

## Accuracy Tests

Current conflict-resolution head `16b61eade952` normally merges pinned main `133f712a498e`. It preserves main's move of multimodal wire types into `managers/req_types.py` and relocates the complete strong-identity implementation there, without duplicate classes or an eager scheduler/identity import. Full BLAKE3 and typed-identity hashing remain unchanged from the preceding PR head.

Exact-head validation on an isolated B300 (driver 590.48.01, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0) passed:

- CPU-hidden identity/padding/cache and native Rust contracts: **114 tests + 81 subtests**, with one CUDA-only test skipped.
- GPU hash/IPC/request/abort contracts: **97 tests + 187 subtests**, no skips.
- GPU-visible identity tests plus the previously skipped cache case: **18 tests + 26 subtests**, no skips; 17 cases repeat CPU-covered tests in the GPU-visible environment.

All final phase exits were 0; changed-file pre-commit and scoped relocation checks passed. The first CPU-hidden attempt failed collection because an existing test helper indexes an empty `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`; rerunning the same source with an out-of-range GPU ordinal and an explicit zero-device assertion passed. IPC teardown emitted a producer-lifetime warning; ending GPU memory/utilization were 0 MiB/0%. This is conflict-integration validation, not a new full-model, performance, multi-node or leak-free-soak claim. Current-head targeted CI is requested separately.

Previous delivery head `48150838db03` normally merges the pinned main commit containing #47835, fixing the two unrelated diffusion fixtures from the old CI snapshot. It preserves @g0djan's #47066 diagnostic-checksum fix and leaves full BLAKE3/typed VLM identity unchanged. Isolated B200 validation on this exact head passed **244 tests + 241 subtests**, exit 0: hash/identity (28 + 197 subtests), request/abort/Rust interface contracts (103 + 44 subtests), and four diffusion fixture/cache files (113). Runtime imports and freshly built extensions used this checkout; driver 580.126.09, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. This is merge-integration validation, not a new full-model serving or performance result.

Remote H200 validation, implementation `15884434708` (the following commit changes documentation only):

- **976 passed**, 23 skipped, 149 passing subtests: common CPU/processor/cache/session/encoder tests, including actual Python and Rust radix trees.
- **51 passed**, 133 passing subtests: GPU hash/IPC/VMM/encoder tests. One FABRIC test fails because this container returns `CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED`; POSIX fallback passes. The test is unchanged and normally runs on GB300.
- **2 passed**: native Rust encoded-sidecar tests. Native Python/Rust suite: 49 passed plus four PIL resize parity subtest failures reproduced on the pristine base; no tolerances or assertions changed.
- Real Qwen2.5-VL-3B: CPU and CUDA IPC, videos with caches enabled/disabled, raw/processor/precomputed inputs, A-B-A and concurrent isolation. Final existing input fixture: **4 passed**.
- Final native Rust HTTP and two-GPU Mooncake EPD: **23 requests passed each**, including ordered multi-image requests and identical caller hints. Earlier ZMQ EPD and global embedding store runs also passed 23 each.
- Real InternVL3.5-1B: **22 requests passed**. This is representative E2E coverage, not a claim that every VLM checkpoint was tested.
- CPU/GPU BLAKE3 reference agreement includes 15 crafted legacy collision pairs, length padding, noncontiguous inputs, streams, and a manual 8 GiB + 17 byte boundary check.

Qwen revision: `66285546d2b821cf421d4f5eb2576359d3770cd3`; InternVL revision: `2f71cf52542334823e48a46ffba0e2bc9add3446`. Environment: H200, driver 595.71.05, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8, Python 3.12.16, blake3 1.0.11, Rust 1.92. Multi-GPU EPD was same-host; cross-node and non-NVIDIA E2E remain untested. Zero observed collisions is not proof that collisions are impossible.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Matched Qwen serving: CUDA IPC, 64 MiB preprocess cache, context 8192, memory fraction 0.45, CUDA graphs off, max running 8, seed 37, one greedy output token. After three warmups: 33 changing images and 20 same-image requests. Baseline was repeated twice. Median milliseconds:

| Workload | Baseline changing | Candidate changing | Baseline same image | Candidate same image |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 224 image | 40.62-40.70 | 41.47 | 21.83-21.85 | 22.18 |
| 1024 image | 68.26-68.82 | 72.67 | 29.55-29.81 | 29.63 |
| Shared 2048-token text + 224 image | 41.07-41.14 | 42.66 | 22.44-22.74 | 22.74 |

Generated token IDs matched in these benchmark cases. Full identity checking adds work on changing-media requests. Different media deliberately no longer share their common text KV prefix; same ordered media still shares it. Long shared-prefix workloads can incur a larger prefill penalty.

Interleaved 100-sample GPU microbench, including host synchronization: 12 MiB raw BLAKE3 **0.099 ms**, typed identity **0.128 ms**, versus old GPU64 **0.100 ms** and D2H+CPU BLAKE3 **3.068 ms**. At 153 MiB, raw BLAKE3 is **0.301 ms** versus old GPU64 **0.237 ms**. This avoids feature-sized D2H, but is not uniformly faster than the old weak GPU hash. Dense hashing needs small scratch buffers; noncontiguous inputs require a contiguous copy. No saturated-throughput claim.

## Checklist

- [x] Changed-file pre-commit checks, including Rust format/clippy
- [x] Regression tests and representative real-model validation
- [x] Documentation, caller trust boundaries and performance tradeoffs
- [ ] Upstream CI

title: [Perf] diffusion: Wan-Animate-2 1.7x faster denoising via exact FA3 in-context attention, opt-in FP8 reference K/V
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
## Motivation

Wan-Animate-2's in-context self-attention is about 71% of GPU time per denoising step on H100 (torch profiler). It runs compiled flex_attention over a padded [generation | reference video] layout that is always sized for a full-length clip, so short clips also pay for the padded frames.

## Modifications

1. **Exact FA3 path for the in-context attention (Hopper).** `_in_context_attention` computes the same masked attention as FA3 calls merged by log-sum-exp with the existing `merge_state` kernel:
   - dense FA3 over the generation keys;
   - varlen FA3 per frame over the reference keys (generation frame j attends reference frame j-1);
   - for `log_scale != 0` (distilled checkpoint), generation frame 1's keys get their own call with `lse + log_scale`, which equals the score bias;
   - a short clip's missing frames are zero keys under the full-clip mask, so they are added back exactly as `out * sigmoid(lse - log(num_zero_keys))`.

   `_split_attention_is_exact` gates it. Grids that differ by a row, batch > 1 and non-Hopper GPUs keep the flex path unchanged.
2. **Opt-in FP8 reference K/V cache.** `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_WAN_ANIMATE_2_FP8_REFERENCE_KV=1` (default off) stores the per-clip reference K/V as `float8_e4m3fn` with one fp32 scale per (token, head). Each block dequantizes into its attention input. It errors on non-CUDA, below sm89, and ROCm.
3. The reference cache is stored once per clip in the padded slot layout, sized to that clip.

## Benchmark

H100 80GB, official Wan2.2 demo inputs (`examples/wan_animate/animate`), 944x528, seed 42, layerwise DiT offload and text encoder CPU offload as in CI, FP8 off unless noted. Single runs; the PR ran first on a cold compile cache. Denoise step = steady-state s/it.

| setting | main step | PR step | step speedup | end to end (main to PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base, 1 GPU, 1 short clip, 40 steps | 9.75 s | 5.52 s | **1.77x** | 441.4 to 265.5 s (1.66x) |
| base, 1 GPU, 3 clips (2 full + short), 40 steps | 11.26 s (full clip) | 8.08 s | 1.39x (full), 3.17x (short) | 1299.6 to 809.5 s (**1.61x**) |
| distilled, 1 GPU, 10 steps, guidance 1.0 | 5.62 s | 2.94 s | **1.91x** | 109.7 to 73.4 s (1.49x) |
| base, 2 GPU CFG-parallel | 5.06 s | 2.84 s | 1.78x | 263.5 to 173.1 s (1.52x) |
| base, 2 GPU Ulysses SP=2 | 5.23 s | 3.08 s | 1.70x | 255.7 to 158.6 s (1.61x) |

Peak memory (base, 1 GPU, 1 clip), reserved / allocated: main 58.5 / 32.2 GB, PR 56.6 / 30.8 GB, PR with FP8 **27.2** / 23.7 GB. FP8 costs about 1-3% per step. Multi-clip and multi-GPU peak memory is about the same as main.

The FA3 path ran in every PR run: 0 flex autotune lines on a cold cache, while main logs them.

## Accuracy

- Unit tests (`test_wan_animate_2_parallelism.py`): 47 passed on H100, 167 passed / 8 skipped (H100-only) on CPU. New tests cover:
  - split vs flex on H100: full and short clip, `log_scale` 0 and -1.3, FP8 on and off;
  - split vs dense masked attention on CPU, with a torch stand-in for FA3;
  - when the gate allows the split;
  - FP8 quantization: zero rows, outliers, saturation.
- Single attention call at the real shape, split vs flex: rel L2 3.6e-3, max abs 2.4e-4 (bf16 rounding).
- End to end, per-frame PSNR of the decoded video vs main. Main is bitwise deterministic across runs, so this measures the change:

  | setting | PSNR mean / worst frame |
  |---|---|
  | base, FP8 off | 39.0 / 36.0 dB |
  | base, FP8 on | 40.4 / 36.0 dB |
  | distilled | 40.2 / 37.8 dB |
  | 3 clips | 39.3, 36.8, 35.0 dB per clip / 30.5 dB |
  | 2 GPU CFG-parallel, SP=2 | 37.8 / 32.7 dB, 40.5 / 38.3 dB |

  FP8 adds no measurable error on top of the kernel change. The difference is bf16 rounding in a different attention kernel, compounded over steps and blocks. It grows across clips because each clip is conditioned on the previous one. Main itself moves 38-40 dB between 1 and 2 GPUs.

main vs this PR (FP8 on), same inputs and seed:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/db0bfe1f-fbf7-4858-8930-e9827a79eb70

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0c2e540-aef3-4e9e-9232-396e73d01fe1

![main vs this PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OnePunchMonk/sglang/wan-animate2-refkv-assets/fa3/side_by_side.gif)

Multi-clip and multi-GPU videos, raw numbers, logs, profiler traces and harness scripts are in the comments below and in [the run archive](https://github.com/OnePunchMonk/sglang/tree/wan-animate2-refkv-assets) ([INDEX.md](https://github.com/OnePunchMonk/sglang/blob/wan-animate2-refkv-assets/INDEX.md)).

## Not covered

- TP > 1.
- Repeated runs for variance (all numbers are single runs).

title: [Perf] dsv4: Fix amax8_varlen and mega MoE pre-dispatch grids for 1024-thread SMs
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

Two DeepSeek-V4.1 decode kernels lose time to grid shape on GPUs whose SMs hold 1024 resident threads (CC 10.7 / sm_107), not to memory bandwidth:

- `amax8_varlen` (two-level indexer block keys) sizes `grid.y` from the logits buffer width (`max_compressed_seq_len`), but rows only hold `compressed_seq_lens` keys. At 128K context about 85% of the 512-thread CTAs exit after reading `seq_len`; at 2 CTAs/SM that is dozens of waves of empty CTAs.
- `mega_moe_pre_dispatch` launches 640-thread CTAs for hidden 5120. Two do not fit a 1024-thread SM, so the quant CTAs plus the pad CTAs run in two waves.

## Modifications

- `block_amax.cuh`: cap `grid.y` at two waves of resident CTAs (occupancy API, cached per device) and grid-stride over key chunks.
- `mega_moe_pre_dispatch.cuh`: when two one-chunk-per-thread CTAs do not fit an SM (`cudaDevAttrMaxThreadsPerMultiProcessor`), launch half the threads with two 16B chunks each (both loads issued before the quant-group reductions) and two pad slots per thread. On 2048-thread SMs the launch is unchanged.
- Both per-device host queries are cached with `init_once`. The two-chunk launch is used only when `top_k <= num_chunks / 2`, so no previously valid `top_k` is rejected.

Both kernels produce bitwise-identical outputs (all outputs compared, including pad slots and the scale swizzle).

## Accuracy Tests

On sm_107 (CC 10.7), at this PR's head (merged with main, including #46090):

title: [Perf] rust-server: Pin frontend threads to one shared CPU set, not one core each
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

The Rust server used to split the cores it was given into disjoint per-group sets (API runtime, tokenizer pool, detokenizer pool, the two router threads) and pin each thread to exactly one core. A thread pinned to a single core cannot migrate: when anything else runs on that core (an MM worker's decoder thread floating over the same set, or another process) it waits in that core's run queue while the rest of the set idles, and every stream it serves stalls with it.

Separately, the Python launch path narrowed the scheduler's own thread to the few reserved launch cores after the server started. A busy neighbour on one of those cores then holds the scheduler thread, and every TP rank waiting on it at the next collective, in that core's queue.

## Modifications

- `rust/sglang-server/src/utils/threads.rs`: replace the per-group core plan with one shared `CpuSet` built from `cores` (`frontend_cpu_set`), and pin each thread to that set with `rustix::thread::sched_setaffinity` (`pin_current`). Core ids outside the set's range are ignored with a warning.
- `rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs`: every spawned stage, the tokio API runtime's worker threads and the thread running its `block_on` pin to the shared set. The router-scaling note moves next to the `to-scheduler` spawn.
- `rust/sglang-server/Cargo.toml`, `rust/Cargo.lock`: drop `core_affinity`; `rustix` (already a dependency) gains the `thread` feature. `num_cpus` and `hermit-abi` leave the lockfile with it.
- `python/sglang/srt/rust_server/server.py`, `config.py`: the launch thread narrows its affinity only while the MM threads are created (so they inherit the server cores) and then restores its full mask; the scheduler thread is no longer pinned to the reserved launch cores. The reserved cores are still kept out of the frontend set. Docstring and log wording updated to match.
- `rust/sglang-mm/src/common/par.rs`, `message/config.rs`: comment updates for the new pinning model.
- `test/registered/unit/multimodal/rust/shared/test_rust_server_extension.py`: `launch_context` takes a core partition; a new test launches on a thread of its own with a two-way partition and checks that MM threads are created on the server cores while the launching thread ends with its full mask.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: thread placement only, no numerics change.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not run here. Locally: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p sglang-server --all-targets` and `cargo test -p sglang-server` (413 passed) are clean, and `test_rust_server_extension.py` passes (7 tests, including the new one).

title: [Perf] observability: Send scheduler timing to the tokenizer as typed reports
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Send scheduler time stats to the tokenizer as `time_stats`, a per-row list of `SchedulerOutputTimeStats` msgspec structs, instead of a pickled list of `SchedulerReqTimeStats` objects in `BatchTokenIDOutput` and `BatchStrOutput`. A struct holds only the five values the tokenizer puts in `meta_info` (storage prefetch and staging waits, forward entry, prefill finished, queue time), named and ordered as the `meta_info` keys, with timestamps converted to wall-clock on the scheduler.
- With metrics off, the scheduler builds none and `time_stats` is `None`. Before, every emitted row's stats object went through pickle on every step even though its state was empty.
- `BatchEmbeddingOutput` no longer carries time stats: embedding requests never have a metrics collector, so every row was empty. The tokenizer reads a missing row as empty time stats.
- The detokenizer and the multi-tokenizer split pass the structs through as typed values instead of unwrapping and re-pickling them.
- Remove what only served the old path: `SchedulerReqTimeStats.__getstate__`, `has_timing_data`, `SchedulerReqTimeStats.convert_to_output_meta_info`, and the clock rebasing in `ReqTimeStatsBase.__setstate__`, which no sender uses any more.
- Drop the unused `scheduler_time_stats` argument of `APIServerReqTimeStats.convert_to_output_meta_info`.

No behavior change: `meta_info` and the non-streaming first-token time are the same as before.

## Micro benchmark

One decode step of output on the CPU only: 512 requests, one new token each, built by the real `_GenerationStreamAccumulator`, then pickled and unpickled as the default IPC does. Base and this PR ran interleaved, 6 rounds of 200 steps each; each value is the minimum over rounds (laptop CPU, so absolute numbers are indicative).

| metrics | build (us/step) | pickle (us/step) | unpickle (us/step) | scheduler build + pickle (us/step) | message (KB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| off, base | 491 | 278 | 250 | 769 | 35.3 |
| off, this PR | 478 | 112 | 133 | 590 (-23%) | 29.6 |
| on, base | 509 | 401 | 585 | 909 | 81.5 |
| on, this PR | 655 | 294 | 267 | 949 (+4%) | 65.0 |

- With metrics off (the default), the scheduler spends 178 us less per step and each receiving process 117 us less.
- With metrics on, receivers spend 54% less on unpickling. The scheduler spends slightly more, because building each row's `SchedulerOutputTimeStats` now happens in the step instead of inside pickle.

title: [Perf] pd: Copy the last chunk's state page indices to the host without a scheduler sync
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

On a PD prefill worker under the overlap scheduler, `_send_kv_chunk` already hands a sender that declares `supports_host_tensor_indices` its KV page indices as a pinned host tensor plus a CUDA event, so the scheduler thread does not wait on the in-flight forward to send a chunk (#45492). The last chunk's state payloads were left out of that path: the sliding-window and full-KV state page indices still went through `kv_to_page_indices`, a `.cpu()` on the schedule stream. `_apply_war_barrier` fences that stream behind the running forward, so the copy returns only when that forward's reads are done, and the scheduler thread still blocked once per request, in `process_batch_result`, right before the hand-off to the transfer.

## Modifications

- `_send_kv_chunk` decides the host-tensor path once per call: a sender with `supports_host_tensor_indices`, outside the context-parallel transfers that filter indices on the host. The per-segment KV page indices use it as before.
- The last chunk's SWA-window and full-KV state page indices now take the same copy (`async_d2h` into pinned memory), returned as a NumPy view of the host tensor so the sender's consumers keep their types. The state rides the last segment's send, whose `indices_event` is recorded after these copies on the same stream; the Mooncake transfer worker already synchronizes that event before it reads the chunk, and on the scheduler thread the sender only takes their length.
- Senders without host-tensor support keep the synchronous read. The Mamba and DSA state payloads are unchanged; they do not go through `kv_to_page_indices`.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerics change: the same page indices reach the transfer, later. Ran the unit tests that drive `_send_kv_chunk` and the Mooncake chunk queue against this branch:

```
pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_minimax_m31_cache_transfer.py \
       test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_mooncake_transfer_batching.py \
       test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_fake_kv_sender.py
61 passed, 33 subtests passed
```

title: [Perf] scheduler: Send the per-request output stats only when they may have changed
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Per-request output values that change only at a few points in a request's life (`prompt_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `cached_tokens_details`, the retraction count, the image/audio/video token counts, and the scheduler time stats) now travel together as one `RequestOutputStats` in `request_stats`. A request sends it on its first output, on its first output after each retraction, and on its finished row; other rows carry `None`, and the field is `None` when no row carries one.
- `Req.take_request_stats_due()` decides: it compares `retraction_count` with the retraction count of the last stats sent (`Req.request_stats_retraction_count`) and records the send. No other code marks anything, so a new output path cannot skip a send. A value that changes between outputs other than across a retraction shows only on the finished output; the cases today are listed below.
- The tokenizer manager keeps the latest `RequestOutputStats` in `ReqState.request_stats` (`ReqState.update_request_stats`) and builds `meta_info`, metrics and span attributes from it. A row that arrives before its request's stats, which only a late row of an aborted request whose rid was reused can do, is dropped with a warning, as a row for a missing state already is.
- `retraction_counts`, `cached_tokens_details`, `time_stats` and the media token counts are removed as per-row lists from `BatchTokenIDOutput`, `BatchStrOutput` and `BatchEmbeddingOutput`. Rust server mode still fills `prompt_tokens`, `cached_tokens` and the media counts per step, which `push_generation` reads.

The finished output's `meta_info`, all metrics and the finished-request span attributes are the same as before, and so is every output of a request that is never retracted, is not dLLM, and sees no HiCache storage attach or detach. For those three cases, outputs before the finished one keep the stats values sent last:
- dLLM requests: `cached_tokens` and `cached_tokens_details`, which change with each block.
- Retracted requests: `num_retractions` is current from the first output after the retraction, but `queue_time`, the storage waits, and after a PD-decode re-bootstrap the cached tokens, change again later and show only on the finished output.
- HiCache storage attached or detached mid-request: the `storage` keys of `cached_tokens_details`.

## Verification

A differential test drove 20000 random request lifecycles (prefill, chunked prefill, decode with stream intervals 1-3, retraction and re-prefill, PD-decode prebuilt, dLLM blocks, embeddings, metrics on and off, Rust mode) through the real scheduler output path, detokenizer and tokenizer manager on main and on this PR. Finished outputs, metrics calls, span attributes and Rust payload columns matched exactly, and so did every earlier output except the stats values listed above for retracted and dLLM requests.

## Micro benchmark

A steady decode step on the CPU only: 512 requests that have all emitted before, one new token each, built by the real `_GenerationStreamAccumulator`, then pickled and unpickled as the default IPC does. Main and this PR ran interleaved, 3 rounds of 200 steps each; each value is the minimum over rounds.

title: [Perf] [AMD] dsa: Replicate the DCP query projection on the owned route
author: EricKing626
body:
## Motivation

On the owned DSA DCP route from [#44322](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44322), every MLA layer all-gathers the full-head query (`[T, H, 576]`) before attention, in decode and in every DSA extend, and the a2a merge ships each head's partial at `kv_lora_rank` (512) wide. This PR removes the query all-gather and halves the a2a payload, without changing what attention computes:

- **Q replication**: every rank holds the whole DCP group's `q_b_proj` and `w_kc`, so it projects all query heads locally. `--dcp-replicate-q-proj` (already on by default for DeepSeek-family models on the a2a backend) now also covers DSA extend on HIP, not just decode.
- **Project before merge**: the LSE merge is linear in the partial output, so every partial is V-projected first and the a2a carries `v_head_dim` (256) instead of `kv_lora_rank` (512) per head.

## Correctness

MI355X, `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`, TP4/EP4 + DCP4, FP8 KV, MTP (EAGLE, 5 steps, 6 draft tokens), real draft acceptance. Both columns were measured on the same day with the same scripts.

| 40 | this PR | **19.70** | **26,583** | 95.0% | — | 97.0% |
| 48 | #44322 | 2.56 | 10,774 | 82.6% | — | 96.1% |
| 48 | this PR | **3.18** | **12,819** | 81.9% | — | 96.4% |

- P90 interactivity is 1.15–1.25x of #44322 at every point, and throughput per GPU 1.05–1.07x at c16–c40.
- The gain comes mostly from prefill (extend 13–21% faster above), which shortens the decode stalls behind each prefill batch. Decode itself is about 3% faster.
- At c48 the DCP pool is still full (chip hit rate 82%), so P90 stays low; throughput per GPU is 1.19x because each recomputed prefix costs less.

## Modifications

- **Replicate `q_b_proj` / `w_kc` across the DCP group** (`model_runner.py`, `forward_mla.py`)
    - The model runner all-gathers `q_b_proj` and `w_kc` once before graph capture. The local `q_b_proj` weight then aliases its own slice of the replica, so replication adds `(W-1)/W` of the weight instead of doubling it.
    - GLM keeps `w_kc` / `w_vc` as per-tensor FP8 on gfx95; they are dequantized to bf16 before the gather instead of skipping the layer.
    - `is_dcp_q_replicate_phase` also returns true for DSA extend on HIP, so prefill skips the Q all-gather too.
- **Project before merge** (`forward_mla_rocm.py`, `deepseek_v2.py`)
    - With the a2a backend and an unquantized `o_proj`, each rank V-projects the partials of every group head with the replicated `w_vc` before the a2a, and the merged result goes straight to `o_proj`.
- **Token-major absorb** (`forward_mla_rocm.py`, `dcp_kernels.py`)
    - The absorb bmm writes `[T, H, kv_lora_rank]` directly instead of transposing a head-major result. A small Triton per-head bmm (`head_bmm`) serves batches up to 288 tokens; larger ones use `torch.bmm` on transposed views.

Scope: Without `--dcp-size > 1` nothing changes. The new extend path is gated on `is_hip()` and DSA; CUDA keeps the decode-only behavior. `--no-dcp-replicate-q-proj` restores the old route. No new environment variables.

## Checklist

- [x] `pre-commit`
- [x] Kernel tests (`test_dcp_qrep_hip.py`), and the existing DCP kernel/unit tests
- [x] GLM-5.2 DCP4 end-to-end sanity (passkey up to 96K, NLL)
- [x] GSM8K, this PR vs. #44322
- [x] Agentic replay at c16 / c24 / c40 / c48

title: [Fix] diffusion: Preserve FP32 product rounding in Anima RoPE
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation and change

On RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, the existing Anima FP32 split-half RoPE kernel fails its first-use exactness check and falls back to eager. Triton 3.8.0 emits contracted arithmetic in the FP16/BF16-output specialization even with `enable_fp_fusion=False`: the inspected original cubin contains eight `FFMA` instructions, and the captured Q/K case has 90 differing values. The guard prevents incorrect model outputs, but leaves the intended fusion unused.

Use the existing `mul_rn_f32` helper for both products before their FP32 addition and output cast. The inspected replacement cubin has no `FFMA`; the existing exactness gate passes and real Anima serving uses the fused kernel. The gate, supported shapes/dtypes, quality policy, fallback and compile behavior are unchanged. The only other change documents the operator in its existing README table.

Frozen SGLang main: `af21e2b989e482cfdce39689126562f2209d53ac`.
Final tested PR head: `883ad602418f51dc406378e1a5aa0ba8438f6b27`.
vLLM-Omni: `817d4c17feb702289a2d2b2cbacfd594c262b7a7`.

[Evidence index](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/README.md), [numerical/codegen audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/evidence/preflight/anima-rope-numerics2.json), [existing tests](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/evidence/block-runs/anima-rope-final-tests1/final.log).

## Final-head model measurements

One RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, SM120, 97,887 MiB, 600 W, driver 595.84. The same physical GPU0 serves every arm; GPU1 remains idle. SGLang uses PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 / Triton 3.8.0; Omni uses PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. Dependency pins and NVML samples are archived.

Anima Base v1.0, 1024×1024, 50 steps, CFG 4, CPU seed 42, empty negative prompt, maximum 512 text tokens, batch/concurrency 1. Components run BF16; initial noise and solver arithmetic retain the native FP32 contract. SGLang uses its native pipeline and cuDNN attention, lossless quality. Omni uses native single-file loading plus components, cuDNN attention, and its default **28 regionally compiled transformer blocks**, retained throughout.

Primary measurements have no profiler and no added stage synchronization. A symmetric 12-process sequence contains two processes per configuration; each prompt has one warmup plus four measured requests per process (**n=8/config/prompt**). HTTP time includes the complete PNG/base64 response transfer and excludes client PNG decoding/disk writes. Throughput is serial requests divided by their summed HTTP time. Denoise below is from separate synchronized SGLang diagnostics, n=4/config/prompt, and is not subtracted from primary HTTP latency. Omni's API generation-stage metric also includes other stages; a comparable isolated denoise value was not collected.

| Configuration | Prompt | E2E p50 / p95 (s) | req/s | Peak GiB | Synchronized denoise (s) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| omni | short | 5.7682 / 5.7721 | 0.17342 | 11.494 | not collected |
| omni | long | 5.7998 / 5.8044 | 0.17248 | 11.494 | not collected |
| main_eager | short | 7.0910 / 7.1061 | 0.14097 | 7.576 | 6.8552 |
| main_eager | long | 7.0905 / 7.0949 | 0.14108 | 7.576 | 6.8496 |
| final_eager | short | 6.1622 / 6.1710 | 0.16225 | 7.531 | 5.9337 |
| final_eager | long | 6.1618 / 6.1659 | 0.16230 | 7.531 | 5.9304 |
| main_bcg | short | 7.0884 / 7.1109 | 0.14100 | 8.812 | 6.8205 |
| main_bcg | long | 7.0907 / 7.1012 | 0.14105 | 8.812 | 6.8154 |
| final_bcg | short | 6.1884 / 6.1985 | 0.16156 | 8.718 | 5.9190 |
| final_bcg | long | 6.1908 / 6.1973 | 0.16152 | 8.718 | 5.9198 |

Paired process-median comparisons, short / long prompt:

- **Main → PR eager:** latency **−13.10% / −13.08%**; all process pairs improve.
- **Main → PR BCG:** latency **−12.73% / −12.70%**; all process pairs improve.
- **Omni remains faster:** PR eager is **6.88% / 6.27% slower**. This PR does not establish a cross-framework win.
- **BCG has no net benefit here:** final BCG is **0.40% / 0.47% slower** than final eager and uses about **1.188 GiB** more peak memory. This is existing BCG compatibility, not new beneficial BCG coverage.

Before comparisons, native-main A/A had CV 0.037–0.058% and maximum half-run median drift 0.098%. The first V1 ABBA independently showed 13.15% / 13.09% lower latency. All samples, backend screens, negative comparisons and quality failures are retained in the [raw audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/evidence/preflight/anima-rope-final-compare1-audit.json); [summary](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/evidence/preflight/anima-rope-final-summary.json).

Cached launch-to-ready times were 44.03–48.04 s for PR eager, 44.03–46.04 s for PR BCG, about 46.03–46.04 s for main, and 38.02–38.03 s for Omni. These reuse existing disk/compiler caches and are **not cold-start measurements**. In a separate final-head observer run, native graph construction took 0.617 s on main and 0.587 s on PR; the complete warmup denoising call took 7.310 s / 6.402 s. These are single observed warmups, not repeated cold-start estimates.

## Profile and BCG execution

Separate synchronized profiles, representative GPU step 3:

| Configuration | GPU kernels | Sum of GPU kernel times (ms) | Fused paired RoPE calls |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| main eager | 3326 | 135.694 | 0 |
| PR eager | 2486 | 117.836 | 56 |
| main BCG | 3330 | 134.300 | 0 |
| PR BCG | 2490 | 116.026 | 56 |

These diagnostic sums are not primary serving latency. [Final profile audit and trace paths](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/evidence/profiles/anima-rope-final-profile-audit.json).

Final-head BCG checks switch short → long → Chinese → repeated short, then lossless → exact → high → lossless at the same shape. Each arm has one actual warmup capture with 57 segments, **17 serving requests, 900 model-level replays, and zero serving capture calls**. Exact/high use the native uncaptured path; returning to lossless reuses the existing graph. All 17 images per arm match the corresponding native-main PNG exactly. The lossless profile contains 456 `cudaGraphLaunch` events across its four captured GPU-step annotations; the fused RoPE is present inside PR execution. The counter observer adds no tensor reads or CUDA synchronizations and is excluded from primary timing. [Lifecycle audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/evidence/preflight/anima-final-bcg-audit2-audit.json).

## Correctness and actual generated images

The original single-file DiT is pinned to `circlestone-labs/Anima@f973fc41ec7545364ac9776c2440285f43ff2a30`; components are `circlestone-labs/Anima-Base-v1.0-Diffusers@073c3a9db359c31ad0e8aa268d15775473c2176c`. All downloaded files have verified hashes; the native converter establishes exact equality for all **685 DiT/conditioner tensors**. Both frameworks receive equal Qwen/T5 token IDs and masks, initial noise, timesteps and sigmas. Their native BF16 text-encoder/conditioner results have small numerical differences; these are audited rather than silently replaced.

Main versus final PR: byte-identical PNGs for short, long, Chinese and repeated short in eager/BCG and the tested quality transitions. Cross-framework admission was fixed at SSIM ≥0.95 and PSNR ≥28 dB:

| Prompt | cuDNN SGLang / Omni SSIM | PSNR (dB) | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| short | 0.983579 | 37.1984 | pass |
| long | 0.974539 | 30.4278 | pass |
| Chinese | 0.936743 | 26.5305 | **fail; excluded from performance admission** |

The Chinese prompt asks for a teapot scene and “慢慢喝茶”; both frameworks instead generate anime café figures, with differences in hands/text. This failure is shown below and remains in the matrix. English images preserve the same composition with small reflection/cloth differences. Native torch-SDPA screens also retain their Chinese quality failure. An explicit `fa` screen resolved to torch SDPA under the existing SM120 policy; it is not evidence of a FlashAttention run.

Real main / final images, 1024×1024, seed 42, 50 steps, CFG 4, BF16, identical prompts. Rows are short, long and Chinese; labels identify the commits and the failed cross-framework row. Original image pixels are unchanged in these panels.

![Anima eager: actual main and final PR outputs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/media/eager-main-vs-pr.png?v=883ad602)

![Anima BCG: actual main and final PR outputs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/media/bcg-main-vs-pr.png?v=883ad602)

![Anima final PR and native Omni; Chinese failure retained](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/media/pr-vs-omni.png?v=883ad602)

[Image manifest and visual review](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/media/manifest.json); [effective-input audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/evidence/preflight/anima-runtime-input-audit1.json).

## Cleanup, tests and reproduction

Reused the existing numerical helper and existing tests; no new wrapper, flag, test copy or gate bypass. Scoped review removed experimental code from the production diff. Final executable kernel bytes equal the pre-cleanup V1 bytes; the final commit adds the necessary operator documentation.

The original cleanup comparison gave final latency +0.1365% / +0.0884%. One fixed supplementary ABBA, two warmups and eight measurements per prompt/process, gave +0.0187% / +0.0108%. Keeping all four process pairs gives **+0.0776% / +0.0496%**, n=24 per arm/prompt. All four point estimates are slightly negative for the final version; we do not call the difference zero. Descriptive 95% process-paired log-ratio t intervals are [0.99813, 1.00032] and [0.99863, 1.00038] for V1/final, including no change and satisfying the predeclared 1% noninferiority margin. Only four process pairs limits precision. Final-head gains over main remain above 12%; no further favorable-result retries were run. [Complete cleanup audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/evidence/preflight/anima-rope-final-cleanup-admission.json).

- Existing Anima tests (`test_rope.py`, `test_model_fast_paths.py`, `-k anima`): baseline **3 failed / 5 passed**, final **8 passed** on SM120. Seven captured/synthetic FP16/BF16 numerical cases also pass exactly.
- Scoped pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` pass. Initial harness permission/root assertions and their corrections are retained; they did not alter model code.
- [Frozen workload](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/inputs/anima-t2i-workloads.json), [launch/request/benchmark commands per process](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/evidence/block-runs/anima-rope-final-compare1-03-final_eager/metadata.json), [reproduction instructions](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/README.md).

```bash
# In the pinned SGLang environment, with the verified component checkpoint:
SGL_REPO=/task/candidates/anima-rope-rounding-final \
SGL_EXPECTED_HEAD=883ad602418f51dc406378e1a5aa0ba8438f6b27 \
  sh /task/launch_sgl_anima_cudnn_primary1.sh
# The archived launcher supplies the complete native server arguments.
python3 bench_anima_serving.py sgl --help
# Reproduce the fixed sequence with the archived plan and runner:
python3 run_anima_blocks2.py anima-rope-final-compare1.json
```

Scope: the measured native single-GPU Anima workload and conservative existing RoPE contract. Other resolutions, batches/concurrency and GPU generations are unrun. Omni rejects the tested model's TP/SP/parallel-CFG/quantization/offload combinations; no unsupported two-GPU comparison is claimed. No full-matrix or new BCG win is claimed. Weights, traces and media are kept outside the code PR.


## CI status

The scoped local pre-commit checks and eight SM120 Anima tests pass. Repository `lint` also passed. The initial PR title-format failure was corrected by changing metadata to `[Fix] diffusion: ...`; the tested code head is unchanged. GPU CI is not claimed passing: the [PR gate log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40811240990/job/123241921417) explicitly says `PR is draft. Blocking CI.`, and dependent test jobs were skipped. This remains a Draft PR as requested.

title: [Feat] unlimited-ocr-v2: Add Unlimited-OCR v2 model support
author: DonggeYang
body:
## Motivation

Unlimited-OCR v1 (#29186) serves single images and short documents with a prefill-aware sliding window. [Unlimited-OCR-2](https://huggingface.co/baidu/Unlimited-OCR-2) (`UnlimitedOCRV2ForCausalLM`) targets long multi-page documents (hundreds of pages in one request). It replaces the sliding window with DASH sparse attention (a learned per-page router plus a per-page 2D position frame), so serving it needs a new attention backend, model, and processor, plus serving-side support for splitting a long document into page windows that reuse each other's KV cache.

## Modifications

**Model and attention**
- `models/unlimited_ocr_v2.py`, `multimodal/processors/unlimited_ocr_v2.py`; v2-only processor options in `configs/unlimited_ocr.py` (`v2_layout=True`; v1 keeps its upstream tile cap and crop layout).
- `layers/attention/unlimited_ocr_v2_backend.py`: DASH sparse attention (learned per-page entmax router, sparse prefill/decode attend, page-local 2D RoPE). Full prefill and decode CUDA graphs supported; eager decode also supported.
- Triton kernels in `kernels/ops/attention/unlimited_ocr_dash/` with `KernelSpec` registrations; runtime state (page/coord state, router math) stays in `srt/layers/attention/unlimited_dash_ops/`.
- `arg_groups/model_overrides/unlimited_ocr_v2.py`: selects the `unlimited_ocr_v2` backend, sets `page_size` to the sparse block size, disables the radix cache, and rejects unsupported modes (see below).
- `UnlimitedOCRV2KVPool` (K + router-index K) in `mem_cache/memory_pool.py`, sized in `kv_cache_configurator.py` / `pool_configurator.py`.

**SAM vision encoder (shared with DeepSeek-OCR / Unlimited-OCR v1)**
- Two JIT kernels, `elementwise.sam_rel_pos_bias` and `elementwise.window_unpartition_add`, used only when their contract holds (CUDA non-ROCm, bf16, shape/stride/alignment); otherwise the eager path runs. Query-chunked relative-position bias capped at 64 MiB.

**Long-document serving (v2 only)**

Serving, retained-window KV state, prefetch, scheduler hooks, and decode/crop helpers are owned by Unlimited-OCR v2 under `models/unlimited_ocr_v2_support/`. The serving loop owns window progress and a single prefetched successor; plans are validated once in `document_split.py`. The retained KV-row holder is `RetainedWindow`.
- `models/unlimited_ocr_v2_support/chat.py` + `models/unlimited_ocr_v2_support/document_split.py`: with `--uocr-doc-split`, a multi-page chat request is split into page windows (with lookahead pages) and answered as one response / one stream. Windowing with KV splicing is approximate and opt-in; the default serves the whole document. `serving_chat.py` only gets a `None`-checked hook. If a window is rejected for exceeding context while other windows succeed, the non-streaming response preserves their text and usage, reports an incomplete document with `finish_reason="length"`, and includes the rejected window in its diagnostic metadata. The cookbook client checks `doc_split_complete` before using the text as a complete document.
- `models/unlimited_ocr_v2_support/document_reuse.py` (`DocReuse`), `models/unlimited_ocr_v2_support/retained_window.py`: a finished window's KV tail is retained and copied into the next window instead of re-encoding and re-prefilling the overlap page.
- `models/unlimited_ocr_v2_support/document_prefetch.py` (`DocPrefetch`, `EarlyEmbeddings`): the next window is sent while the current one decodes and its pages are vision-encoded early on a side stream.
- Per-page output cap (`--uocr-max-page-tokens`) through the built-in page guard, without enabling external custom logit processors. External serialized processors still require `--enable-custom-logit-processor`. The processor collects its per-row bans / forced tokens and applies them with one non-blocking index upload, so it never blocks the host on the forward.
- With doc split, the request pool has `2 * max_running_requests` rows: each in-flight document may hold a retained window row next to its running row (the running cap is unchanged). Without this, retained windows were evicted near the running cap and the follow-up window lost its predecessor's context.

**Scheduler / runtime (created only for Unlimited-OCR v2; `None` otherwise)**
- `models/unlimited_ocr_v2_support/scheduler_hooks.py` owns all per-scheduler document state (no module globals) and is reset by `flush_cache`.
- `models/unlimited_ocr_v2_support/async_shm.py`, `models/unlimited_ocr_v2_support/overlap_release.py`, `models/unlimited_ocr_v2_support/crop_transfer.py`: SHM materialization off the scheduler thread, deferred overlap release, pinned crop prefetch.
- `models/unlimited_ocr_v2_support/greedy_graph.py`, `models/unlimited_ocr_v2_support/decode_graph_io.py`: greedy argmax recorded in the decode graph and decode inputs relayed through it.
- `Scheduler` / `ModelRunner` only construct, wire and delegate; request-side state is declared on `Req` (`uocr_doc`, `page_guard_state`).

**Unsupported with Unlimited-OCR v2 (rejected at launch with a clear error)**
- speculative decoding, `--pp-size > 1`, PD disaggregation;
- `--dp-size > 1` / DP attention while doc split is on (omit `--uocr-doc-split`).

**New server arguments**

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--uocr-doc-split` | off | Opt into approximate page-window processing with KV reuse |
| `--uocr-doc-page-window` | 1 | Maximum transcribed pages per window, across all image modes |
| `--uocr-max-page-tokens` | 0 | Per-page output token cap (0 = off); enforced by the built-in page guard |

The model-owned `UocrDocumentConfig` declares and validates these CLI arguments. Advanced request settings use typed `doc_split_options`: `max_batch_pages` (may tighten the server window), `overlap_pages` (default 0), `lookahead_pages` (default 1), and `max_page_tokens` (may tighten the server cap). A larger lookahead can require an explicit `--context-length`. Window settings require `--uocr-doc-split`; per-page limits can also be used with whole-document serving.

**Internal environment overrides** (expert kill-switches / resource thresholds; not semantic model settings): `SGLANG_ENABLE_UOCR_DOC_PREFETCH`, `SGLANG_UOCR_DOC_PREFETCH_MAX_MB`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_UOCR_CROP_PREFETCH`, `SGLANG_UOCR_CROP_PREFETCH_MAX_MB`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_UOCR_ASYNC_SHM_MATERIALIZATION`, `SGLANG_UOCR_ASYNC_SHM_MAX_MB`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_UOCR_SHM_WRAP_MODEL_DATA`.

**Changes visible to other models**
- Custom logit processors: when every row of the batch uses the same processor, it is applied to the full logits in place (bit-exact; saves two full-logits copies per step).
- SAM encoder JIT kernels (above) for DeepSeek-OCR / OCR2 / Unlimited-OCR v1 on bf16 CUDA; a kernel bug for strided `rel_w` inputs is rejected instead of producing a wrong bias.
- `DeepseekOCRNoRepeatNGramLogitProcessor`: new opt-in params; with default params output is identical (3000 random cases). Out-of-vocab banned ids are ignored instead of raising.
- Fastokens: unchanged for every tokenizer that loaded before. A tokenizer whose `tokenizer.json` pre-tokenizer disagrees with its declared class (v2 declares `LlamaTokenizerFast` with a ByteLevel pre-tokenizer) used to fail under `--tokenizer-backend fastokens`; it now loads through Hugging Face with the v5 component fix and wraps the repaired backend.
- Unlimited-OCR v1 prompt building, processor and serving behave exactly as before.

**Tests and docs**
- Document planning and split-response tests: `test/registered/unit/models/unlimited_ocr_v2/test_document_split.py`.
- Unit tests under `test/registered/unit/{session,managers,mem_cache,sampling,entrypoints,server_args,models,layers/attention}`; kernel tests and benchmarks under `test/registered/kernels/{ops,benchmark}/{attention,elementwise}`; e2e server test `test/registered/vlm/test_unlimited_ocr_v2_server.py` (single page + multi-page with splitting and KV reuse).
- Cookbook page `Baidu/Unlimited-OCR-2.mdx` with its config; new flags in `server_arguments.mdx`.

## How to reproduce

Server (1x NVIDIA L20 48 GB). The command below uses the current CLI names. The benchmark results below are carried over from the original PR description at `f15f2d1aa007e7df0e79495285eb2f50f8389a90`, before the configuration cleanup. The original recipe used equivalent one-page windows; these results have not been remeasured on the current head. Only `--uocr-max-page-tokens` differs per benchmark:

```bash
SGLANG_VLM_CACHE_SIZE_MB=0 PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path baidu/Unlimited-OCR-2 \
  --served-model-name Unlimited-OCR-v2 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \
  --tokenizer-worker-num 8 \
  --tokenizer-backend fastokens \
  --chat-template unlimited-ocr \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.7 \
  --max-running-requests 64 \
  --max-prefill-tokens 2048 \
  --random-seed 20260918 \
  --uocr-doc-split \
  --uocr-max-page-tokens 20000 \
  --enable-custom-logit-processor \
  --enable-streaming-session \
  --allow-auto-truncate \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --mm-preprocess-cache-size-mb 0 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-decode full \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-prefill full \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 16384 \
  --cuda-graph-bs-prefill 1024 2048 \
  --cuda-graph-config '{"prefill": {"backend": "full", "full_prefill_max_req": 64}}'
```

`--uocr-max-page-tokens` is 8000 for MPDocBench and 20000 for MarathonDocBench. MPDocBench sends multi-page documents with `images_config.image_mode="base"` and single pages in the default `gundam` mode; MarathonDocBench uses `gundam`.

Request: one chat request per document, all pages in one message; the server splits it into page windows and returns one answer.

```python
from openai import OpenAI
from sglang.srt.sampling.custom_logit_processor import DeepseekOCRNoRepeatNGramLogitProcessor

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")
pages = [...]  # data URLs or http(s) URLs, in page order
content = [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": u}} for u in pages]
content.append({"type": "text", "text": "<PAGE><image>" * len(pages) + "Multi page parsing."})
resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="Unlimited-OCR-v2",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": content}],
    temperature=0,
    max_tokens=20000 * len(pages),
    extra_body={
        "skip_special_tokens": False,
        "images_config": {"image_mode": "gundam"},
        "custom_logit_processor": DeepseekOCRNoRepeatNGramLogitProcessor.to_str(),
        "custom_params": {"ngram_size": 35, "window_size": 1024 if len(pages) > 1 else 128},
    },
)
```

## Accuracy Tests

sgl-eval has no OCR suite, so we report document-parsing benchmarks from the benchmark revision noted above; client temperature 0.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MarathonDocBench throughput on 1x NVIDIA L20 48 GB, using the benchmark revision and configuration noted above (`--uocr-max-page-tokens 20000`): 64 long documents, 11,748 pages in total, every document sent as one request at a fixed client concurrency.

author: YAMY1234
body:
## Update (2026-11-02): slimmed to nine optimizations, one per commit

This revision is rebased onto `main` `57bfde9f2c` and keeps nine optimizations, one per commit. Four earlier changes whose isolated throughput effects were within run-to-run noise were removed (see "Removed"). The previous seven-commit description is kept below for reference.

### Per-commit changes and measured effect

Measured on Qwen3.5 (GB300) with the NVIDIA plugin enabled. "Disable" = throughput change when only this commit is turned off in the full stack (one 1200 s AgentX trace-replay run per arm, TPS/user P50 / P90; run-to-run noise ≈2% at TP8 c16 and ≈1.4% at TEP8). "Static" = cumulative per-batch decode TPS/user change when the commit is added on top of the previous ones (identical requests, warmed rounds). Effects are not additive across commits.

| # | Commit | Change | Production / tests | Measured effect |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| 1 | `d0385b181d` | Verify on vocabulary shards (no full-vocabulary logits gather) | +1299/−47 · +331/−8 | Disable: TP8 PD c16 −3.6% / −1.8%; TEP8 PD c272 −8.1% / −5.9%. Static gain appears together with #2 (switch is wired there) |
| 2 | `8bbfc2c3ab` | Capture the post-verify tail (sampling, acceptance, output prep in one graph) | +671/−116 · +168/−54 | Static (with #1): TP8 B1/8/16/32/64 +4.2/+2.1/+4.8/+6.3/+10.0%; TEP8 B8/16/32/64/128 +3.7/+6.1/+7.0/+11.0/+14.1% |
| 3 | `b19e38a511` | Keep unchanged top-1 / hidden-state relay rows in private graph buffers (includes alias fix) | +208/−34 · +127/−4 | Disable: TP8 PD c16 −4.0% / −3.7%; TEP8 c272 −1.1% / −0.4% (within noise) |
| 4 | `15aa4dfede` | Share draft attention metadata and fused-path policies | +201/−19 · +363/−9 | Disable: TEP8 PD c272 −6.6% / −4.2%; TP8 c16 −0.6% / −1.6% (within noise). Static TEP8 B8–B128 +7.5% to +12.5% |
| 5 | `018b707117` | Defer staging KV scatters to between decode forwards | +327/−71 · +69/−1 | Add: TEP8 PD c130 +4.1% / +3.4% |
| 6 | `b50357ff68` | Read staging metadata asynchronously (pinned, fenced) | +44/−13 · +79/−0 | Add: TEP8 PD c130 +3.8% / +9.1%; TEP8 PD c272 +11.9% / +19.2% |
| 7 | `35039280b3` | Overlap PD decode admission with the in-flight forward | +63/−10 · +114/−0 | Leave-one-out gain at DEP8 PD c704: +4.5% / +20.3% (TP8 / TEP8 points not measured separately) |
| 8 | `ef001f9d5f` | Reuse attention length-group plans within a forward | +140/−0 · +167/−0 | Leave-one-out gain at DEP8 PD c704: +5.2% / +14.5% |
| 9 | `49c9a41235` | Record draft-extend read completion in the graph and guard KV-page reuse | +102/−7 · +82/−2 | Leave-one-out gain at DEP8 PD c704: +4.3% / +15.0% |
| 10 | `0e7516f9b4` | Reserve decode staging only for the chunks covered by the current prefill batch, instead of a long request's whole length at its first chunk (the staging FIFO no longer waits on chunks that have not been computed) | +17/−3 · +53/−0 | Add, TEP8 PD concurrency 272 (same-time control, one 1200 s run each): **TTFT P90 −53.3% (1.87 → 0.88 s)**, E2E latency P90 −4.4%, TPS/user P50 +0.4% / P90 −1.1%. Prefill KV-transfer stage mean 380 → 159 ms. Follows the runtime master switch; with it off, or for dummy / unsupported managers, the whole-request reservation is kept. CPU per commit: no new failures; TEP8 GSM8K 10/10 |

Total (ten commits): production +3067 / −288, tests +1712 / −73 (the previous revision was production +5148 / −358, tests +4386).

### Removed

| Removed change | Production lines | Measured effect when disabled alone |
|---|---:|---|
| Single-launch ReplaySSM state commit | +953 | TP8 c16 −0.0% / −1.2%; TEP8 c272 −0.6% / −1.1% |
| Decode scratch / host-copy pooling | +347 | TP8 c16 −1.2% / −1.3%; not active under EP |
| Per-shape fill / copy-plan reuse | +412 | TP8 c16 −0.2% / +1.6%; not active under EP |
| Preparing the next draft round early | +1409 | TP8 c16 −0.4% / −2.8%; not active under EP |

Each is within run-to-run noise on its own. Disabling all four together, measured three times per arm at TP8 PD concurrency 16 (one prefill + two TP8 decode workers, 1200 s each, all valid):

| Arm | TPS/user P50 (min–max) | TPS/user P90 (min–max) |
|---|---:|---:|
| All four enabled | 1380.3 (1377.3–1384.2) | 894.5 (859.6–913.6) |
| All four disabled | 1335.0 (1332.8–1338.1) | 902.9 (883.9–925.5) |
| Difference of means | −3.3% | +0.9% |

The P50 ranges do not overlap, so removing the four together costs about 3% at P50 at this point; P90 is within its spread. The two groups ran about 1.5 h apart. Fused EAGLE index preparation is left for a follow-up.

### Default behavior (runtime master switch off)

`SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION` defaults to off, and its child switches follow it. With it off, execution matches `main`:
- EAGLE / multi-layer / UNO / NGRAM eager verify calls `eagle_sample` with the same arguments as `main` (no provider hooks or post-verify views are built).
- The asynchronous staging-metadata readback is not used; the original synchronous path runs.
- FlashMLA stays in the draft-extend graph-supported backend list, as on `main`.

Remaining differences on the default path are structural only and do not change execution: new dataclass fields with defaults, attribute initialization, imports, the decode admission `wait_stream` placement (same position relative to `prepare_for_prebuilt` and the KV checksum, with no GPU work between), and one `.to(bonus.dtype)` cast in the existing verify-commit Triton kernel that is a no-op for the default `int32` bonus buffer. Paths that remove clones, take the FP8 pre-quantized input, add the staging chunk-arrival lock, or pass an LM-head `out=` buffer are reached only through the optimized (switch-on or plugin) callers.

Validation of this head: per-commit CPU tests on `main` plus all ten prefixes (no new failures); GSM8K 10/10 with the switch off and the plugin off (TP8). GSM8K 10/10 with the switch on (TEP8, with #47201 and the plugin).

### Integration order

Merge #47201 first, then this PR, then enable the plugin. This PR keeps optional contract discovery and stock fallbacks; the plugin uses the provider contracts from #47201.

This PR is the in-tree caller of the post-verify hook added in #47201: `eagle_worker_common.py` calls `bind_speculative_runtime_hooks` with the stock hooks from `speculative_runtime.py`, `eagle_utils.py` sets `LOCAL_KEYS_SUPPORTED`, and `sharded_verify.py` runs the verify path behind it.

### Validation

- CPU: `main` and each of the nine commit prefixes run the same relevant unit tests; 0 failed relative to `main` (`main` has two pre-existing failures, unchanged).
- GSM8K (10 questions, real acceptance) with #47201 and the plugin: TP8 10/10 and TEP8 (EP4) 10/10, strict and flexible, no empty responses.
- End-to-end AgentX for this exact revision (with #47201 and the plugin; one 1200 s run per point, all valid, zero errored requests). "Full stack" is the same deployment with the four removed commits still included:

| Point | This revision TPS/user P50 / P90 | vs full stack |
|---|---:|---:|
| TP8 PD, concurrency 16 | 1051.6 / 792.3 | −1.2% / −0.8% |
| TP8 PD, concurrency 128 | 665.3 / 544.3 | +0.2% / −2.7% |
| TEP8 PD, concurrency 130 | 484.5 / 348.0 | −0.5% / −3.0% |
| TEP8 PD, concurrency 272 | 301.2 / 206.1 | −2.3% / −3.6% |

  P50 is within run-to-run noise (≈2% TP8, ≈1.4% TEP8) at three of four points; P90 is 2.7–3.6% lower at three points (single runs). Against `main` (`efdcb420c7` with the released plugin installed unmodified, megakernel off), TEP8 PD at concurrency 272, same recipe and window, one 1200 s run each:

  | Metric | `main` | `main` + #47201 + this PR + plugin | change |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | TPS/user P50 / P90 | 87.5 / 83.1 | 301.2 / 206.1 | +244% / +148% |
  | TTFT P90 (s) | 8.02 | 1.99 | −75% |
  | E2E latency P90 (s) | 24.25 | 8.37 | −65% |
  | Total tok/s/GPU | 64569 | 89732 | +39% |

  This is the full stack (binding, runtime and plugin together) and is not attributed to this PR alone.

<details>
<summary>Previous revision description (seven commits)</summary>

## Motivation

Speculative decoding performs many small index-building launches, copies, allocations, graph metadata updates, and recurrent-state operations between draft rounds. This PR adds model-independent, capability-checked fast paths while retaining the existing SGLang implementation as the fallback.

This PR contains runtime optimizations only: no provider ABI, provider factory, model-name check, or Qwen-specific kernel policy. It is based directly on `main` and does not depend on the companion binding PR.

**Switch inventory:** this standalone runtime tree has **28** Boolean child switches that follow `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION` when unset. The base `main` supplies 27; R7 adds exactly one, `SGLANG_TRTL3_EP_DEFER_FINALIZE`, as the 28th. This PR declares no other master-following child switch.

| ID | Purpose | Switch |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Verify directly on vocabulary shards | `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION` |
| R2 | Fuse EAGLE index preparation | Master switch |
| R3 | Prepare the next EAGLE draft round | `SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH` inherits master when unset |
| R4 | Capture the EAGLE post-verify tail | Master + post-verify graph switch |
| R5 | Commit ReplaySSM state in one CUDA launch | Master switch |
| R6 | Capture generic GDN prefill state updates | `SGLANG_ENABLE_GDN_PREFILL_GRAPH_EXTEND` inherits master when unset |
| R7 | Reuse graph resources and speculative relays | Master; explicit child values take precedence |

## Modifications

### R1 — Verify directly on vocabulary shards

- **What:** Produce native or provider-supplied token keys from rank-local vocabulary logits and reduce the compact keys across tensor-parallel ranks. SGLang owns the reducer and every collective.
- **Why:** Greedy verification needs only the winning token, so this avoids a full-logit all-gather, temporary full-vocabulary tensor, and following argmax.
- **Switch:** `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION`.
- **Fallback:** Sampling, penalties, watermarking, logprob requests, provider decline, or a consumer without shard support returns to the original full-logit gather and verifier before provider RNG is consumed.

### R2 — Fuse EAGLE index preparation

- **What:** Fuse chain-tree construction, draft-extend layout, draft/cache locations, positions, and mRoPE indices in generic CUDA kernels.
- **Why:** Remove repeated small launches and intermediate tensors from model-neutral EAGLE index production.
- **Switch:** The master runtime switch.
- **Fallback:** Dtype, layout, shape, or device rejection occurs before JIT loading and uses the existing Triton/stock producers.

### R3 — Prepare the next EAGLE draft round

- **What:** During post-verify, stage request rows, accepted sequence lengths, positions, and KV write-window locations directly into the next draft graph's static buffers. A fresh host key and one-shot lease guard request-pool reuse; scheduler and runner tensors remain distinct.
- **Why:** Avoid returning through a scheduler gather and runner copy when the next graph-compatible destination is already known.
- **Switch:** `SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH`; when unset it follows the master switch, while an explicit value takes precedence.
- **Fallback:** Unsupported algorithm, top-k, EP/layout, graph miss, stale key, invalid lease, or insufficient reservation executes the original scheduler gather and runner copy.

### R4 — Capture the EAGLE post-verify tail

- **What:** Fuse chain acceptance and, for compatible cases, capture sampling, acceptance, commit-output preparation, and next-draft layout. Eager, graph, EAGLE, MultiLayerEAGLE, NGRAM, and UNO paths call one always-present strategy; runtime-only builds resolve a structural stock strategy.
- **Why:** Remove the multi-launch eager tail while keeping the stock verifier authoritative outside the graph contract.
- **Switch:** Fused chain acceptance uses the master switch. Capture/replay uses `SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH`, which follows the master only when unset.
- **Fallback:** Missing binding capability, unsupported device/tree/sampling/watermark/graph key, or provider decline invokes `eagle_sample` and the original eager path.

### R5 — Commit ReplaySSM state in one CUDA launch

- **What:** Fold accepted rows and update circular cache, tracking rows, cursor, and stable state in one generic CUDA launch before unchanged circular-fold bookkeeping.
- **Why:** Replace a multi-operation Triton state update and its intermediate launches/traffic.
- **Switch:** The master runtime switch only.
- **Fallback:** BF16, contiguous layout, supported shape/index, SM90+, CUDA binding availability, and successful NVRTC prebuild are all required; any miss uses the stock Triton commit. The CUDA path changes FP32 accumulation order and is tolerance-equivalent at `rtol=2^-7, atol=1e-6`, not bitwise-equivalent.

### R6 — Capture generic GDN prefill state updates

- **What:** Capture compatible GDN prefill/extend state tracking and FlashInfer calls in reusable CUDA graphs with caller-owned dynamic-input bridges.
- **Why:** Remove repeated host dispatch and allocation at graph-stable shapes.
- **Switch:** `SGLANG_ENABLE_GDN_PREFILL_GRAPH_EXTEND`; when unset it follows the master, while an explicit value takes precedence.
- **Fallback:** Unsupported mode, shape, graph size, backend, or capture error uses the existing eager implementation.

### R7 — Reuse graph resources and speculative relays

- **What:** Pool speculative tensors/events, reuse graph buffers and TRT graph metadata, batch small field copies, retain unchanged top-k-1 relay rows, and skip allocation work when prepared-next already owns the destination. It also adds capability-checked FP8 prequantized-input reuse, MNNVL shape/EP tuning, EP deferred finalization, and an optional lazy FlashMLA graph import.
- **Why:** Remove repeated allocation, copy, metadata construction, synchronization, and backend setup at draft/verify boundaries.
- **Switch:** The master runtime switch. R7 declares `SGLANG_TRTL3_EP_DEFER_FINALIZE` as the 28th master-following child; it and the 27 inherited child controls honor explicit `0` or `1` values before inheriting the master.
- **Fallback:** Shape, EP, backend, layout, graph-lifetime, or optional-import rejection performs the original copy, allocation, metadata construction, finalize, or backend path.

### Independence and composition with #47201

This PR and #47201 are independently based on `main`; neither is a merge prerequisite for the other. When the second PR is rebased after the first lands, or when both are composed before merge, their EAGLE changes overlap in exactly five files:

- `eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py`
- `eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py`
- `eagle_megakernel.py`
- `eagle_worker_v2.py`
- `test_eagle_binding.py`

The later PR should retain this PR's relay/static-buffer behavior and #47201's always-present facade while resolving those overlaps. The combined focused suite covers that composition.

The composed branches have five ordering adapters (`speculative_runtime.py`, `eagle_post_verify_graphs.py`, `eagle_utils.py`, `eagle_worker_common.py`, and `sharded_verify.py`) and six test ownership/fixture changes (`test_speculative_runtime_contract.py`, `test_speculative_runtime_hooks.py`, `test_speculative_runtime_hook_execution.py`, `test_sharded_verify.py`, `test_megakernel_guards.py`, and `test_dspark_step_inputs_once.py`). The adapters cache optional capability lookup and provide standalone stock fallbacks. With both PRs present they resolve to the same canonical views, provider callback, reducer, collectives, and optimized dispatch; they change no kernel, graph launch, shape eligibility, plugin selector, or autotune snapshot.

## Accuracy Tests

- Every R1–R7 commit independently completes changed-file `compileall`; the complete runtime tree also completes import smoke and full relevant-directory compilation.
- Runtime-only focused CPU result: **276 passed, 21 skipped, 2,684 subtests passed**.
- Combined runtime-plus-binding focused CPU result: **302 passed, 18 skipped, 2,726 subtests passed**.
- Master-off tests cover stock identity and bypass for sharded verification, prepared-next, ReplaySSM commit, GDN prefill graphs, resource reuse, and explicit child-switch overrides. Unsupported consumers preserve the full-vocabulary stock path.
- A no-simulation serving run completed GSM10 with **10/10** answers. An integrated serving run also completed a 53-request long-context replay.
- Layer-by-layer localization found no numerical difference before the ReplaySSM committed state. At that first difference, 233 of 5,898,240 BF16 elements differed, all within `atol=1e-6, rtol=2^-7`; this state is tolerance-equivalent, not bitwise-equivalent.
- In a real two-request TEP8 verify batch, all eight ranks compared 434,560 provider-slot logits and 57,344 hidden-state values with the stock computation and found zero bitwise differences.
- DEP8 with only the master switch enabled (runtime only, without Qwen3.5 plugin enablement) completed no-simulation greedy GSM10 with **10/10** answers.
- Greedy default verification, including requests carrying seeds, is bitwise identical to direct stock behavior.

GSM8K on the current head, no draft-acceptance simulation, seed 1234 (strict / flexible accuracy):

| Topology | 1319 questions, greedy | 250 questions, greedy | 250 questions, sampled T=1.0 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TP8 | `0.978 / 0.977` | `0.988 / 0.988` | `0.972 / 0.972` |
| TEP8 | `0.980 / 0.979` | `0.980 / 0.980` | `0.968 / 0.968` |

No empty responses in any run. TP8 also passed a 53-request long-context replay (three attempts, all 53/53, no CUDA errors).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Static decode uses identical requests and warmed, unprofiled rounds; P50/P90 TPS/user is derived from round latency. Autotune selections were frozen for all measurements in both columns; TP8 B1 was measured before the latest plugin commit, which does not affect the single-request path; all other rows were measured on the current head.

| Topology | Batch | main P50/P90 TPS/user | this PR P50/P90 TPS/user | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP8 | 1 | `773.39 / 753.59` | `1561.443 / 1553.168` | `+101.9% / +106.1%` |
| TP8 | 8 | `492.46 / 488.33` | `657.33 / 650.93` | `+33.5% / +33.3%` |
| TP8 | 16 | `410.25 / 406.68` | `553.19 / 546.35` | `+34.8% / +34.3%` |
| TP8 | 64 | `260.23 / 258.97` | `324.28 / 323.57` | `+24.6% / +24.9%` |
| TEP8 | 32 | `359.99 / 357.98` | `431.472 / 428.328` | `+19.9% / +19.7%` |
| TEP8 | 64 | `283.69 / 282.05` | `351.007 / 348.592` | `+23.7% / +23.6%` |
| TEP8 | 128 | `201.43 / 200.51` | `258.757 / 257.732` | `+28.5% / +28.5%` |

Here, `main` means upstream SGLang with the master switch disabled and no optional megakernel plugin installed. 

AgentX trace replay, 3600 s window, TEP8 prefill/decode disaggregation at concurrency 272, same request set and the same fixed draft acceptance length in both columns:

| Metric | main | this PR | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TPS/user P50 / P90 | `85.48 / 81.31` | `129.37 / 112.92` | `+51.3% / +38.9%` |

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] speculative-decoding: Bind generic provider strategies
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

Optional speculative-decoding providers need one narrow, model-neutral boundary. Provider discovery should happen once, graph-facing call sites should invoke an always-present strategy, and provider absence or decline must preserve SGLang's stock RNG, collective, verification, and state-lifetime behavior.

This PR contains only provider contracts, binding, and stock-or-provider facades. It is based directly on `main` and does not depend on the companion runtime-optimization PR. The two PRs can build, test, and land independently.

**Switch inventory:** this standalone binding tree retains the **27** master-following Boolean child switches already in its `main` base and declares no new child switch. It adds only `SGLANG_NVIDIA_MEGAKERNEL_SLOTS`, an independent tuple selector rather than a child of `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION`. When composed with #47200, `SGLANG_TRTL3_EP_DEFER_FINALIZE` from R7 is the 28th master-following child, so the combined stack has **28**.

| ID | Commit | Purpose | Switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1a | `b376bc4bf9` | Define speculative provider contracts | None; declarations only |
| B1b | `538c3101ef` | Bind provider factories to stock defaults | `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION` |
| B1c | `d62abccc85` | Bind an always-present DSpark draft strategy | Existing `--enable-nvidia-megakernel` provider construction |
| B1d | `b7c65f65e5` | Route EAGLE draft entries through a stock facade | Existing `--enable-nvidia-megakernel` provider construction |

## Modifications

### B1a — Define speculative provider contracts

- **What:** Add frozen, structured `VocabShardView`, `ShardedLogitsView`, verification/sampling/watermark views, `PostVerifyIO`, `PostVerifyOutput`, `PostVerifyStrategy`, `SpeculativeRuntimeHooks`, and `HooksFactory` contracts. The optional factory is published by `BuiltMegakernel`. Contract tests freeze field names, exact types, key encoding, shapes, splits, logits write-back semantics, and strategy forwarding.
- **Why:** Give providers a stable ABI while keeping the replaceable seam limited to rank-local `local_keys` production. SGLang continues to own reduction, collectives, gather/write-back, acceptance, forced acceptance, sampling policy, and state updates.
- **Switch:** None. This commit declares types and an optional protocol member only.
- **Fallback:** It changes no call site or runtime behavior. Older providers remain valid because the factory is optional and discovered with `getattr`.

### B1b — Bind speculative provider factories

- **What:** Add `bind_speculative_runtime_hooks`, `default_local_keys`, `default_post_verify`, environment registration, and focused binder/default tests. The provider factory receives SGLang's complete stock defaults and may replace only local-key construction; it cannot replace the verifier runner.
- **Why:** Resolve optional capability once at the NVIDIA binding boundary instead of branching on provider presence in every round or captured path.
- **Switch:** `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION`. An explicit off value takes precedence and returns the caller's stock bundle by identity without inspecting a provider. `SGLANG_NVIDIA_MEGAKERNEL_SLOTS` selects plugin entries independently and is not a master-following Boolean child.
- **Fallback:** A missing built provider or factory returns stock defaults. Unsupported local-key requests return `None` before provider RNG is consumed and use the gathered stock verifier. The default local-key implementation remains deterministic for greedy requests, including requests that carry seeds, and declines non-greedy temperature sampling. Provider availability must agree across ranks.

### B1c — Bind an always-present DSpark draft strategy

- **What:** Resolve a stock or specialized DSpark proposal strategy once and call the same facade for every batch. Cross-rank agreement determines the batch sizes served by a provider.
- **Why:** Remove provider-presence branches from the sampler while keeping graph-facing dispatch stable.
- **Switch:** No new switch. Existing `--enable-nvidia-megakernel` construction determines whether a provider can be offered.
- **Fallback:** No provider, no factory, or an unsupported batch size invokes the unchanged stock Markov block. The greedy stock path avoids unnecessary step-logit allocation.

### B1d — Route EAGLE draft entries through a stock facade

- **What:** Add `EagleDraftRuntime` and route draft-loop, draft-extend, round-start, token-extension, and proposal selection through an unconditional facade in workers and graph runners.
- **Why:** Centralize optional entry selection before graph capture and remove repeated provider-presence checks from EAGLE call sites.
- **Switch:** No new switch. Existing `--enable-nvidia-megakernel` construction controls whether specialized entries are available.
- **Fallback:** With the flag off, no offered entry, or an unserved captured batch, the facade calls the original SGLang callbacks and preserves `main` clone semantics. An offered-but-incompatible setup is rejected during binding, and rank disagreement raises on every rank instead of permitting divergent execution.

### Independence and composition with #47200

#47200 and this PR are independently based on `main`; neither is a merge prerequisite for the other. When the second PR is rebased after the first lands, or when both are composed before merge, their EAGLE changes overlap in exactly five files:

- `eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py`
- `eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py`
- `eagle_megakernel.py`
- `eagle_worker_v2.py`
- `test_eagle_binding.py`

The later PR should retain #47200's relay/static-buffer behavior and this PR's always-present facade. The combined focused suite covers that composition.

The composition uses five small ordering adapters in `speculative_runtime.py`, `eagle_post_verify_graphs.py`, `eagle_utils.py`, `eagle_worker_common.py`, and `sharded_verify.py`, plus six test ownership/fixture changes in `test_speculative_runtime_contract.py`, `test_speculative_runtime_hooks.py`, `test_speculative_runtime_hook_execution.py`, `test_sharded_verify.py`, `test_megakernel_guards.py`, and `test_dspark_step_inputs_once.py`. The adapters cache optional capability lookup and provide runtime-only or binding-only stock fallbacks. With both PRs present, they resolve to the same canonical views, provider callback, reducer, collectives, and optimized dispatch; they change no kernel, graph launch, supported shape, plugin selector, or autotune selection.

## Accuracy Tests

- Every B1a–B1d commit independently passes changed-file `compileall`; the complete binding tree also passes import smoke and full relevant-directory compilation.
- Binding-only focused CPU result: **36 passed, 1 skipped, 39 subtests passed**. The combined runtime-plus-binding focused CPU result is **302 passed, 18 skipped, 2,726 subtests passed**.
- Contract coverage includes exact structured fields and types, master-off stock identity with no provider inspection, missing-provider and provider-decline fallback, greedy-with-seed bitwise stock behavior, decline-before-RNG, rank agreement, and DSpark/EAGLE stock facades.
- On the current combined tree, both the optimized empty-slot service and the stock service answered all 10 GSM questions correctly. An integrated TP8 configuration with the sharded-sampling and draft-finalize providers active also answered all 10 questions correctly.
- With only `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION` enabled and no optional provider slots, a no-simulation DEP8 serving run answered all 10 GSM questions correctly. This is runtime/binding-only evidence, not plugin support for DP attention.
- Layer-by-layer localization found no numerical difference before the ReplaySSM committed state. At that first difference, 233 of 5,898,240 BF16 elements differed, all within `atol=1e-6, rtol=2^-7`; this state is tolerance-equivalent, not bitwise-equivalent.
- In a real two-request TEP8 verify batch, all eight ranks compared 434,560 provider-slot logits with the stock computation and found zero bitwise differences.

GSM8K on the current head, no draft-acceptance simulation, seed 1234 (strict / flexible accuracy):

| Topology | 1319 questions, greedy | 250 questions, greedy | 250 questions, sampled T=1.0 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|

No empty responses in any run. TP8 also passed a 53-request long-context replay (three attempts, all 53/53, no CUDA errors).

## Update (2026-11-02, later): rebased on `main` `efdcb420c7`; per-commit performance
