title: [Perf] diffusion: Hold a Qwen-Image-2.1 Q/K norm + RoPE row with a half-warp
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

On B300 the fused Q/K RMSNorm + complex RoPE + K/V packing kernel of Qwen-Image-2.1 took 89 us per launch inside a 1024x1024 request (1280 launches, ~114 ms of GPU time per request): one warp per 128-wide row, 8-byte accesses and 64-bit work indices kept it near 1.5 TB/s.

## Modifications

- A half-warp holds a row: each lane owns 8 elements (16-byte loads/stores), i.e. two of the reference's 4-element groups. The aten mean order is kept exactly: four squares left to right per group, then the same tree (reference lane offsets 16, 8, 4, 2 become lane offsets 8, 4, 2, 1, offset 1 becomes the in-thread add of the two groups).
- 32-bit work indices (host check that the row count fits), 128-thread blocks.
- Tests: odd head counts (6 heads, a partial last warp) added to the existing bit-exactness tests.

## Accuracy

Bit-identical. `torch.equal` against main's kernel on the production pack shape ([1, 4096, 32, 128], 27-token prefix), the kept-buffer edit shape, copy-V, odd heads and the single-tensor entry point; the existing eager-reference tests pass (`test_complex_rope.py` + `test_qwen_image21_cuda.py`: 70 passed on B300). End to end, the decoded PNG pixels of every request match main (md5 of the RGBA array, T2I and edit, 6+ requests each).

## Benchmark (B300 SXM6, 1100 W, 1 GPU, `b200-1gpu-resident-fa` profile)

Kernel alone, [1, 4096, 32, 128] + 27-token prefix (CUDA events, 200 launches):

| variant | us/launch |
|---|---|
| main (warp per row, 8 B, int64 indices) | 65.5 |
| 4 rows per warp | 68.8 |
| 32-bit indices only | 54.0 |
| half-warp per row, 16 B, 256 threads | 38.6 |
| **this PR (half-warp per row, 16 B, 128 threads)** | **37.1** |

In a serving request (nsys): 89.4 -> 52.1 us per launch.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Skip the cross-request cache for Qwen3-VL vision features
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

For a Qwen-Image-2.1 edit request, the cross-request conditioning cache on `Qwen3VLModel._get_flat_visual_features` cost more than the vision tower it skips (B300, 1024x1024 reference, nsys):

- the lookup hashes `pixel_values` on the host: a 25.9 MB device-to-host copy plus SHA-256 (~22 ms, GPU idle);
- every miss pins fresh host pages for the four 8.6 MB outputs (`cudaHostAlloc` 4 x 6.7 ms) until the 512 MB cache fills;
- the vision tower itself is ~11 ms of GPU work.

With distinct references every request pays both; with the same reference and a new prompt, a hit is no faster than recomputing.

## Modifications

Drop `@cached_conditioning` from `_get_flat_visual_features`. The stage-level entry keyed on the prompt and the reference image and the VAE posterior cache still serve repeated requests.

## Accuracy

Unchanged: the same features are computed instead of restored. Decoded PNG pixels of every request are identical to main (md5 of the RGBA array).

## Benchmark (B300, Qwen-Image-2.1 edit 1024, one GPU, harness-shaped requests, 6 measured)

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| distinct reference per request (s, median) | 2.604 | 2.562 |
| same reference, new prompt each request (s) | 2.557 (vision cache hit) | 2.555 (recomputed) |

MiniMax-H3 uses the same encoder with 2048-pixel references, where the hashed `pixel_values` are several times larger.

Qwen2.5-VL (`get_image_features`, Qwen-Image-Edit) keeps its cache: that pipeline conditions the VLM on a ~384x384 image, so its `pixel_values` hash is a few ms.

## Combined with #47465, #47466 and #47467 (B300 harness, two rounds in reversed order)

title: [Perf] diffusion: Replay Qwen-Image-2.1's text-only encoder from CUDA graphs
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I encodes the prompt with the Qwen3-VL text model: ~2600 small kernels and 40 ms of host time for ~10 ms of GPU work on B300, all of it before the first denoising step. Under `--async-output-save` the next request could not even start encoding early: the processor outputs were uploaded with a pageable copy, which first waits for the previous request's queued denoise and decode.

## Modifications

- `TextEncoderGraphs` (Qwen-Image-2.1 encoding stage): the text-only encoder forward is captured per prompt length on its second request and replayed afterwards. A replay runs the same kernels, so the output is bit-identical. Image-conditioned prompts, tensor parallel encoders and non-resident weights stay eager; a change of any parameter or buffer address (offload, reload, replacement) drops the graphs; at most 8 lengths are kept; a capture failure falls back to eager for good.
- `upload_without_sync`: processor and tokenizer outputs go to the GPU from pinned memory (the Qwen-Image-2.1 stage and the generic `TextEncodingStage`, which already asked for `non_blocking=True` on pageable memory).
- Test: replay matches eager bit for bit, image inputs stay eager, replaced weights drop the graph.

title: [Perf] dspark: Refresh Mamba tracking once per verification step
author: sshleifer
body:
## Codex notes

### Motivation

Every non-idle DSpark decode step calls `prepare_mamba_track_for_verify` in the worker and again in `DFlashVerifyInput.prepare_for_verify`. With Mamba prefix-cache tracking enabled, this prepares the same tracking indices twice before the target forward.

### Modifications

Remove the worker's earlier call and its unused import (two production-line deletions). Ordinary and compact verification both reach `prepare_for_verify`, which refreshes tracking before `ForwardBatch.init_new` and before graph loading or eager metadata initialization. No intervening consumer needs the earlier refresh.

This benefits DSpark targets using radix caching with `extra_buffer` or `extra_buffer_lazy`. Eligible architectures include Kimi Linear/K3, Qwen3-Next/3.5, Nemotron-H, Falcon-H1, Granite hybrid and Inkling, when used with a compatible DSpark draft. With tracking disabled, the removed call only performed an early return.

### Accuracy tests

Fresh [B200 CI on `c617e09210`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41483413993) passed the registered Nemotron 3.5 NVFP4 DSpark test: **192/200 GSM8K answers correct (96%)**, zero request errors, and two responses truncated at the 16,384-token limit. This uses the published target and matching DSpark draft.

Removed the mocked verification-preparation harness. The full-model smoke and GSM8K results below were collected before this test-only cleanup; the two-line production change is unchanged.

A full-model GB300 smoke completed on head `6d6fa068e3` and main `5008726431` using NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4 and its matching DSpark draft, `extra_buffer` tracking, TRTLLM MHA draft attention, and full verify CUDA graphs. Both completed 19 requests at batch sizes 1, 2, 4, 8, 3, 1 with 32 output tokens each. However, two outputs differed at batch 8. A repeat of the unchanged baseline also changed two outputs at batch 3, so this run does not establish output parity or identify the cause of the differences.

Local runtime: PyTorch 2.11.0/CUDA 13.2, FlashInfer 0.7.2, CuTe DSL 4.8.0, and installed sgl-kernel 0.4.6.post1 with `SGLANG_SKIP_SGL_KERNEL_VERSION_CHECK=1` (upstream expects 0.4.9). Target MoE used CuTeDSL W4A16 and draft MoE used Marlin. This was a smoke test, not an accuracy evaluation or throughput benchmark.

A subsequent 64-question GSM8K comparison with sgl-eval 0.1.3 completed on candidate `6d6fa068e3` and original base `5008726431`: **64/64 correct on candidate, 63/64 on base**. The base had one response truncated at the 8,192-token limit; candidate had none. Both had zero request errors. Each server ran on one GB300 GPU with the same Nemotron 3.5 NVFP4 target and DSpark draft, `extra_buffer` tracking, full verify graphs (maximum batch 8), disabled overlap scheduling, Triton target attention, TRTLLM MHA draft attention, CuTeDSL W4A16 target MoE, and Marlin draft MoE. Context length was 16,384. The evaluator used temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, seed 42, and concurrency 8; reasoning was enabled by the model template. This is a small accuracy comparison, not proof of output parity, a statistically established improvement, or a throughput benchmark. The local runtime/version limitation above still applies.

### Speed tests and profiling

A GB300 microbenchmark on head `6d6fa068e3` measures the real tracking helper with CUDA mappings at batch sizes 1, 8, 32, and 128. Two calls take 112–160 µs versus 55–80 µs for one call with ordinary tracking; lazy tracking takes 89–129 µs versus 46–64 µs. These are medians of three 200-iteration measurements per variant in an alternating order, with CUDA synchronization around each measurement block. The runtime mode accessor is supplied by the harness and the optional index-reuse cache is disabled. This measures tracking preparation only, not model throughput.

-Robot

title: [Perf] rmsnorm: One SM100-tuned JIT template for plain, fused residual-add and fp8 per-tensor quant
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> (auto generated by Claude)
> (auto generated by MyGO (Make your GPU-kernel Optimal) agent)

## Motivation

On CUDA the JIT rmsnorm kernels were only used on the HF-semantics path; `RMSNorm.forward_cuda` ran flashinfer for the plain, fused-add and per-tensor FP8 variants. The flashinfer CuTe-DSL kernels pay two CTA barriers, three shared-memory passes and a weight re-read per row, and issue nothing before `griddepcontrol.wait`; at decode sizes they leave 0.3-0.8 us per launch on the table on B200, and at hidden sizes below 4096 they stream at 3.8-4.6 TB/s.

## Modifications

- `elementwise/rmsnorm.cuh`: one template kernel with an `RMSNormMode` (`PLAIN`, `FUSED_ADD`, `QUANT`, `FUSED_ADD_QUANT`) and an HF-rounding flag. One row per `threads_per_row` threads, `rows_per_cta` rows per CTA, 32 B vectors on Blackwell (16 B elsewhere); the row stays in registers, the weight slice is loaded before `griddepcontrol.wait`, rows spanning several warps reduce with one barrier, short rows (32-496) take a power-of-two slice of a warp. Sum of squares and epilogue use `fma.rn.f32.bf16` on Blackwell (`out = T(fma(x, w, -0) * r)`, one rounding, no converts); the fused residual sum is one packed `add.rn.bf16x2` and the normalized value is the rounded residual; fp8 outputs are `cvt.rn.satfinite.e4m3x2.f32` pairs packed into 16 B stores. Replaces `fused_add_rmsnorm.cuh` and `rmsnorm_hf.cuh`.
- `ops/layernorm/norm.py`: the schedule `(vec_bytes, threads_per_row, rows_per_cta)` is chosen in Python from measurements (4-8 warps per row, 2 vectors per thread for the plain op and 1 at decode for the fused op, packed rows for short rows at large token counts), both schedules of a signature are built at once with `parallel_compile`, and the token count picks one at call time. Public entry points `rmsnorm`, `fused_add_rmsnorm`, `rmsnorm_quant`, `fused_add_rmsnorm_quant`; `cast_x_before_out_mul=True` replaces `rmsnorm_hf`. Supported hidden sizes: multiples of 16 in [32, 16384].
- `srt/layers/layernorm.py`: `RMSNorm.forward_cuda` and `forward_with_per_tensor_quant_fusion` use the JIT family on SM100 for bf16 / fp16 (static gate per layer); other archs keep flashinfer. The HF path uses it on every CUDA arch, as before.
- Registry entries, `bench_norm.py` quant benchmarks, `test_rmsnorm.py` rewritten (plain, fused, HF, quant, strided, empty) with a parallel prebuild fixture; `test_fused_add_rmsnorm.py` and `test_rmsnorm_hf.py` folded in.

## Accuracy

Plain output within 1 bf16 ulp of flashinfer on < 2e-4 of the elements (accumulation order); fused residual bit-exact to `(x.float() + res.float()).to(bf16)`; HF output bit-exact to the fp32 reference; fp8 bits equal to flashinfer except <= 2e-6 of the elements for `rmsnorm_quant`. `test_rmsnorm.py`: 2777 passed (full sweep) on B200.

## Benchmark (B200, bf16, CUDA graphs, median us per launch, cold L2; flashinfer CuTe-DSL in parentheses)

| rmsnorm | 7168 | 1.29 (1.65) | 2.20 (2.60) | 3.01 (3.37) | 11.4 (12.5) | 36.4 (37.6) |
| rmsnorm | 3072 | 1.14 (1.61) | 1.99 (2.50) | 2.32 (3.02) | 5.69 (8.46) | 17.7 (24.6) |
| rmsnorm | 16384 | 1.82 (2.62) | 2.64 (3.57) | 5.30 (6.19) | 22.7 (26.3) | 79.9 (83.6) |
| fused_add | 4096 | 1.20 (1.70) | 2.22 (2.63) | 3.15 (3.62) | 13.1 (14.3) | 42.6 (43.2) |
| fused_add | 8192 | 1.57 (2.13) | 2.52 (3.01) | 4.43 (5.20) | 22.8 (24.1) | 81.7 (81.8) |

## What this PR does

- Adds a JIT row softmax (`kernels/ops/sampling/softmax_jit.py`, `jit/csrc/sampling/softmax.cuh`): fp32 / bf16 / fp16 logits in, fp32 probs out, per-request temperature fused, in place for fp32. - Adds a JIT row argmax (`kernels/ops/sampling/argmax_jit.py`, `jit/csrc/sampling/argmax.cuh`): int64 output, a tie takes the lowest index.

title: [Perf] Kimi-K3: Enable the fused KDA decode at 6 and 3 heads per rank
author: ByronHsu
body:
## Why?

- `KimiK3DeltaAttention._prepare_fused_decode` accepts only 12 local KDA heads (TP8).
- The fused KDA decode kernel supports 12, 6 and 3 heads (TP8, TP16, TP32), and its kernel test covers all three.
- So at TP16 or TP32 every KDA layer logs "K3 fused KDA decode disabled". Decode then runs three kernels (`causal_conv1d_update`, the delta-rule recurrence, gated RMSNorm) instead of one fused kernel.

## What?

- Check the local head count against the kernel's supported set, now public as `kda_fused_decode.SUPPORTED_HEADS`, instead of a hard-coded 12. The `A_log` and `dt_bias` shape checks use the same count.
- The "disabled" log names the local head count and the supported set.
- The ROCm path is unchanged.

## Verification?

```text
Kimi-K3 at TP16 → 6 local KDA heads

Before: _prepare_fused_decode → A_log.numel() = 6 != 12 → "K3 fused KDA decode disabled"
        → decode: 3 kernels per KDA layer
After:  6 in SUPPORTED_HEADS → _kda_fused_decode_ready = True
        → decode: 1 fused kernel per KDA layer                       (expected)
```

- Reproduce: launch Kimi-K3 with `--tp 16` and search the server log for `fused KDA decode disabled`.

## Test?

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_fused_decode.py` already covers the kernel at 12, 6 and 3 heads: **pending CI**.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: **observed** passing.
- Kimi-K3 at TP16 on GPUs: **pending**.

title: [Perf] unified-memory: Bind the SWA tail's new pages without a host sync in alloc_extend_swa_tail
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

`ChainAllocator.alloc_extend_swa_tail` is the decode-side preallocation path for hybrid full/SWA models under unified memory: the owner band takes virtual pages for the whole sequence, and the window band binds only the pages of the live window tail. The pages to bind were picked on the device, with `torch.unique` over the tail of the extend kernel's output followed by `torch.isin` against the new virtual pages. Both are data-dependent and synchronize the host with the device, so admission in the scheduler stalled behind the in-flight forward.

## Modifications

This change is expressed on the allocator structure introduced in #46976, where `alloc_extend_swa_tail` hands `_allocate` a `tail_pages` closure that selects the window pages to bind.

Pick the tail's new pages on the host instead. The extend kernel hands the j-th new virtual page to sequence page `first_new_page + j`, and `num_swa_pages`, the number of tail pages that are new, is already computed on the host for admission pricing. The tail's new pages are therefore the last `num_swa_pages` entries of the new virtual pages, so `tail_pages` returns that slice (and an empty slice when no new page lies in the tail) with no device round trip. The pages bound, the prefix pages left alone, and the admission price are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerics change: the window binds the same pages as before. Ran the unit tests that drive `alloc_extend_swa_tail` against this branch on one GPU; the swa-tail test also passes unchanged on main, as expected for a sync-free rewrite that binds the same pages:

```
pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_swa_tail_allocation.py
1 passed, 16 subtests passed
pytest test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_decode_prealloc_no_host_sync.py \
       test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_tri_pool.py \
       test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hisparse_allocator.py
63 passed, 105 subtests passed
```

title: [Perf] model_executor: Write small forward metadata with fill kernels behind SGLANG_ENABLE_MLP_SYNC_METADATA_FILL
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

The forward's small per-batch metadata (the DP-attention token counts and their logprob counterpart, the extend sequence and prefix lengths, and the non-padded token count) reaches the device as pinned host-to-device copies. Those copies share the copy engine with bulk host-to-device DMA, so when a large transfer is queued ahead of them, for example a HiCache load-back with the `direct` io backend, the forward waits behind that transfer before it can start, even though the metadata itself is a handful of integers.

## Modifications

Behind `SGLANG_ENABLE_MLP_SYNC_METADATA_FILL` (default off, CUDA only), write that metadata with a Triton kernel that takes the values as kernel arguments instead of copying them, so the write is an ordinary kernel launch on the compute stream and never waits on the copy engine.

- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/memory/small_copy.py`: `write_host_ints(dsts, values)` fills several small contiguous 1-D int32/int64 CUDA tensors in one launch and validates its inputs. The values are encoded as `16 * v + 3` before the launch so Triton's integer specialization (equal to 1, divisible by 16) never splits the kernel cache by value; the kernel decodes with a shift.
- `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py`: `_host_ints_to_device(values, dtype, device)` builds a tensor from a varying-length list by padding to a power of two up to 256 elements, and to whole launches of 256 past that, so the set of compiled kernels stays bounded; the caller receives the leading `len(values)` elements. `init_mlp_sync_metadata`, `init_new` (extend lengths), `_init_num_token_non_padded` and `prepare_mlp_sync_batch` take the kernel path when the flag is on and the device is CUDA, and keep the existing pinned-copy path otherwise.
- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: the new `EnvBool`, default off.
- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/l2_transfer.py`: `L2TransferEngine` warns once when it is created with the `direct` io backend on CUDA while the flag is off, since that backend moves KV with copy-engine DMA that the metadata copies would queue behind.

With the flag off (the default) nothing changes.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerics are touched: the kernel writes the same integers the pinned copy would have written.

## Checklist

- [x] Upstream pre-commit hooks (isort, ruff, ruff-format, codespell, ast) pass on the four changed files.
- [x] On a single NVIDIA GPU: `write_host_ints` writes the expected int32 and int64 values (including 0, 1, 16 and `2**31 - 1`) into several destinations in one launch; 20 further launches with random values of the same shapes compile no additional kernel; `_host_ints_to_device` round-trips lists of every length from 1 to 69 and 127/128/129/255/256/257/300/600 in both dtypes, returns an empty tensor for an empty list, and the 0-dim `squeeze(0)` form reads back correctly; the validation errors fire on mismatched counts, a float tensor, a CPU tensor and a wrong length.
- [ ] Serving with `SGLANG_ENABLE_MLP_SYNC_METADATA_FILL=1` under DP attention is covered by the CI suites on this PR.

title: [Perf] R3: Keep the routed-expert host cache only on the output rank (1/3)
author: ByronHsu
body:
## Why?

With `--enable-return-routed-experts`, every rank keeps a pinned host copy of the routed experts, but only one rank per DP group, the one that talks to the detokenizer, ever sends them out. This is bad for CPU RAM constrained case like GB300.

```text
Before (TP8, no DP attention)                      After (TP8, no DP attention)
rank 0: capture → D2H → host cache → output        rank 0: capture → D2H → host cache → output
rank 1: capture → D2H → host cache   (never sent)  rank 1: capture
  ...                                                ...
rank 7: capture → D2H → host cache   (never sent)  rank 7: capture

Nemotron 3 Ultra, 11.4M-token KV pool, pinned host memory:
        8 × 101 GiB = 808 GiB                      1 × 101 GiB = 101 GiB
```

With DP attention, each DP group has its own output rank, so one cache per group stays:

```text
TP8, --attn-dp-size 2 (attention TP 4 per group), DeepEP

               Before                                         After
group 0  r0:   capture → AG → D2H → host cache → output       capture → AG → D2H → host cache → output
         r1-3: capture → AG → D2H → host cache (never sent)   capture → AG
group 1  r4:   capture → AG → D2H → host cache → output       capture → AG → D2H → host cache → output
         r5-7: capture → AG → D2H → host cache (never sent)   capture → AG

AG = attention-TP all-gather of DeepEP's scattered tokens; r1-3 and r5-7 still join it.
Pinned host caches: 8 → 2, one per DP group.
```
## What?

- Only the output rank of each DP group (`pp_rank == attn_tp_rank == attn_cp_rank == 0`, the scheduler's `is_rank_zero`) allocates the host cache.
- Other ranks still capture on the device (the all-gather needs them) but skip the copy and the readback.

## Verification?

8×H200, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, base `main` at `7146002be8`. ITL = median inter-token latency from `bench_serving`, 1024 in / 256 out, median of 3 runs. Each setup ran main and this PR on one node with no profiler; a repeat of main at the end matched to 0.004 ms (**observed**):

```text
                                         main                   this PR
A  --tp 8                   host cache   8 × 6.88 = 55.0 GB     1 × 6.88 =  6.9 GB   (−48 GB)
                            ITL c1       3.620 ms               3.621 ms
                            ITL c128     8.210 ms               8.227 ms
B  --tp 8 --dp 2            host cache   8 × 7.08 = 56.6 GB     2 × 7.08 = 14.2 GB   (−42 GB)
   DP attention + DeepEP    ITL c1       5.429 ms               5.421 ms
                            ITL c128     7.458 ms               7.462 ms
                            TTFT c1      60.9 ms                60.9 ms
routed experts, 4 greedy prompts                                bitwise identical to main
```

Repro:

```bash
# A
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 --tp 8 \
  --enable-return-routed-experts --mem-fraction-static 0.85
# B (FP8: on main, BF16 DeepEP low-latency mode asserts)
SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=1024 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8 --tp 8 --dp 2 --enable-dp-attention \
  --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto --enable-return-routed-experts --mem-fraction-static 0.85
# client, concurrency 1 / 8 / 32 / 128
python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1 \
  --num-prompts 8 --max-concurrency 1 --extra-request-body '{"return_routed_experts": true}'
```

- Speed is unchanged: the output rank does the same work as before.
- The 101 GiB per rank for Nemotron 3 Ultra was **observed** on our internal sglang fork.

## Test?

- `test_routed_experts_scattered_a2a.py`: 7 passed with this PR, and `TestOutputRankHostCache` fails on main's code (**observed** on the same H200 node).
- `pre-commit`: **observed** passing.

title: [Perf] R3: Skip routed-expert capture on ranks that send no rows (2/3)
author: ByronHsu
body:
Stacked on #47552.

## Why?

Without DeepEP, every TP rank computes the same top-k ids, but only the output rank (pp0 · attn-tp0 · attn-cp0) sends them. The other ranks still copied every MoE layer's ids into a device buffer that nothing reads.

```text
Before (TP8, no DeepEP)                            After
rank 0:   capture → device buffer → host → out     rank 0:   capture → device buffer → host → out
rank 1-7: capture → device buffer  (never read)    rank 1-7: skip
```

## What?

- Only the output rank allocates the routed-experts device buffer.
- Without DeepEP the other ranks skip capture. With DeepEP they still join each layer's all-gather, so the output rank doesn't hang, but they keep nothing. #47554 removes that per-layer all-gather.

## Verification?

Same 8×H200 benchmark as #47552 (Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507; A = `--tp 8`, B = `--tp 8 --dp 2 --enable-dp-attention --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto`), median of 3 runs, each setup on one node with no profiler (**observed**):

```text
                                         #47552                 this PR
A  --tp 8                   device buf   8 × 12 MB              1 × 12 MB
                            ITL c1       3.621 ms               3.571 ms   (−1.4%)
                            ITL c32      5.357 ms               5.289 ms   (−1.3%)
                            ITL c128     8.227 ms               8.178 ms   (−0.6%)
B  DP attention + DeepEP    device buf   8 × 12 MB              2 × 12 MB
                            GPU memory   -                      −32 MiB on each of 6 other ranks
                            ITL c1       5.421 ms               5.393 ms   (−0.5%)
                            ITL c8       5.668 ms               5.632 ms   (−0.6%)
                            ITL c128     7.462 ms               7.391 ms   (−1.0%)
TTFT c1                                  unchanged (A 24.4 → 24.2 ms, B 60.9 → 61.0 ms)
routed experts, 4 greedy prompts                                bitwise identical to main
```

- A gains more: its 7 other ranks now skip capture entirely. In B they still join each layer's all-gather, which #47554 removes.
- Also DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat TP2: device buffers 2 → 1, routing bitwise identical (**observed**).

## Test?

- `test_routed_experts_scattered_a2a.py::TestOutputRankHostCache`: `test_only_output_rank_keeps_rows` and `test_scattered_other_rank_only_joins_the_all_gather`. Both **observed** passing on H200 (`lmsysorg/sglang:dev`), and both fail on #47552.
- `pre-commit`: **observed** passing.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Pipeline Ulysses attention over head groups down to three waves
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

The auto group count keeps only groups whose attention call fills four waves of 128-row tiles. The groups attend on their own streams, so a call's tail overlaps the next group's start, and the four-wave floor is higher than needed. MiniMax-H3 at Ulysses 4 (14 heads per rank) gets 2 groups at 1280x704 and 1344x768 because 7 two-head groups fill 3.5 and 3.9 waves, yet 7 groups are faster.

## Modifications

- Lower the floor from 4 to 3 waves. H3 now auto-selects 7 groups at both shapes; the case behind the old floor (Wan 1.3B, one-head groups, 1.7 waves) still stays sequential.
- Test assertions for the group counts at known shapes added to `test_ipc_a2a_multi_gpu.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

Head grouping does not change bits on the pipelined backends: MP4 md5 identical to main in every arm (6/6 on FA4, 4/4 forced-cuDNN).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

4x B300 (stand-in for B200), MiniMax-H3 T2VA, 49 forwards, fresh server per arm, ABBA, 1 warmup + 3 timed, server-side `inference_time_s`:

| | 1280x704 | 1344x768 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 26.72 s | 31.94 s |
| this PR | 26.55 s (-0.17) | 31.78 s (-0.16) |

B200 runs this attention through cuDNN rather than FA4, so I also forced cuDNN on the B300: main -> this PR + the alignment-row PR is -0.14 s at 704 and -0.23 s at 768, md5 identical.

title: [Perf] minimax-h3: Skip attention for the packing's alignment rows in the Ulysses pipeline
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

H3 pads its packed sequence to a multiple of 64 per Ulysses rank, so a 1280x704 request attends `cu_seqlens [0, 33002, 33024]`. cuDNN SDPA's varlen runs each segment as its own call, so every pipelined head group ran the real rows, a copy into the output, a cuDNN call for the 22 alignment rows and a second copy. With 7 groups per layer that is 28 extra launches and their host work per block.

## Modifications

- The alignment rows only ever reach their own rows (attention keeps them in their own segment, everything else is row-wise), so group attention now attends the real rows only, writes them straight into the output when the backend can (FA4), and zeroes the alignment rows. The real rows run the same call as before.
- Test added to `test_minimax_h3_dit_contract.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

Bit-identical output: MP4 md5 identical to main in every arm (4/4 on FA4, 4/4 forced-cuDNN).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

4x B300 (stand-in for B200), same protocol as the three-waves PR; measured on top of it:

| | 1280x704 | 1344x768 |
|---|---|---|
| three-waves | 26.55 s | 31.78 s |
| + this PR | 26.46 s (-0.10) | 31.63 s (-0.14) |

Together with three-waves, the 20-prompt 720p median goes 26.793 -> 26.517 s (-1.03%).

Note: this touches the same H3 pipelined-Ulysses block in `minimax_h3.py` as the ROCm Ulysses-pipeline PR; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

title: [Perf] [ROCM] diffusion: Pipeline MiniMax-H3's Ulysses exchange over head groups on RCCL
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Without the copy-engine transport (ROCm), each H3 layer packs q/k/v, waits on the input all-to-all, attends, then waits on the output all-to-all: ~2.5 ms of exposed RCCL per layer at 1280x704 on 4xMI355X (14.5% of a denoise step).

## Modifications

- Split the local heads into two groups: queue both input exchanges up front on the collective stream, and send group g's output while group g+1 attends. aiter attends a head group with the same bytes as inside the full call (verified), so the output is bit-identical.
- Two groups was the best choice: 7 groups, 14 groups and unequal splits ([4,10], [2,10,2]) are all slower because attention gets a partial extra wave per call.
- Test added to `test_usp_pipelined_attention_multi_gpu.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

Bit-identical output: 22/22 MP4 md5s equal to main in the final run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

720p median -3.24 s (the largest single item). Per step, ~63 ms of RCCL is now hidden behind attention; 849.5 -> 738 ms/step together with the QK norm change.

Note: this touches the same H3 pipelined-Ulysses block in `minimax_h3.py` as the CUDA-side PR that skips the packing's alignment rows; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

title: [Perf] [ROCM] diffusion: Bit-exact fast QK RMSNorm and fused RoPE for MiniMax-H3
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

On ROCm, H3 keeps the per-head QK RMSNorm on aten `rms_norm`. Its `vectorized_layer_norm_kernel` runs one 256-thread block per 128-wide row (~0.6 TB/s) after a `.contiguous()` copy of each strided q/k view of the fused QKV: QK norm plus that copy is 5.1% of a denoise step (43.7 ms/step) at 1280x704 on 4xMI355X.

## Modifications

- New Triton kernel `aten_head_rmsnorm_triton.py` that replays aten's arithmetic (4 contiguous squares per lane, shfl-down fold 16/8/4/2/1, rsqrtf, `w * (rstd * x)`) and reads the strided q/k views directly. It is used only after a first-sight `BitExactFusionGate` check against the eager path passes.
- Second commit: the bf16 NeoX RoPE (each product and the sum rounded to bf16, dims past rot_dim passed through) is applied in the same pass, behind its own first-sight gate.
- Tests added to `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_norm.py` (fail on main, pass here).

## Accuracy Tests

Bitwise: MP4 md5 identical to main for every prompt checked (22/22 in the final 20-prompt run, which includes the other ROCm branches), plus the kernel unit test comparing against aten bit for bit.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Setup for all numbers below: 4x MI355X, MiniMax-H3 T2VA, 1280x704 (SemiAnalysis "720p"), 124 frames, 49 forwards, Ulysses 4 + aiter, single stream. Each arm is a fresh server (1 warmup + 3 timed requests), ABAB across two rounds, base = main `75a5da7f`.

title: [Perf] [ROCM] diffusion: Skip dead math-SDPA work in the MiniMax-H3 VAE decoder on gfx950
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

gfx950 forces the H3 VAE decoder attention onto aten's math SDPA. That path also masks all-`-inf` rows (`_safe_softmax`: isneginf + all + where) and downcasts the fp32 attention weights it returns; the decoder discards both. On rank 0 this was ~58% of the 2.85 s decode, about 0.5 s of it dead work.

## Modifications

- Replay the math op chain (fp32 upcast, sqrt-scale on q and k, matmul, softmax, matmul) without the dead mask and downcast. Only the gfx950 math-SDPA path is touched.
- Test added to `test_minimax_h3_vae_output.py` (fails on main, passes here).
- The MIOpen workspace warnings in the VAE convolutions are left alone: giving MIOpen more workspace selects different conv algorithms and changes the output bits.

## Accuracy Tests

Output is bit-identical (per-op replay of the same chain): MP4 md5 identical to main on every prompt checked.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: [Perf] diffusion: keep GQA and MOSS-Image attention on cuDNN SDPA on Blackwell
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

On B200 (sm_100), #33655 made dense diffusion attention default to `DYNAMIC_CUDNN_SDPA`, which uses cuDNN SDPA and falls back to FA4. Two models still did not get cuDNN.

**Cosmos3 (grouped-query attention, 32 query / 8 KV heads).** `DynamicCudnnSDPAImpl._use_cudnn_sdpa` returns False whenever query and key head counts differ, so every Cosmos3 DiT layer ran FA4. `CudnnSDPAImpl` already handles GQA: `SDPAImpl.forward` passes `enable_gqa=True`. Forcing `--attention-backend torch_cudnn_sdpa` was 14% faster in denoise.

**MOSS-Image.** The main DiT blocks pin `default_attention_backend=FA`, so the Blackwell default never applies to them.

This was found while benchmarking the cookbook commands on B200: forcing `--attention-backend torch_cudnn_sdpa` made Cosmos3-Nano T2V 720p 13% faster end to end than the default.

## Modifications

- **`DynamicCudnnSDPAImpl._use_cudnn_sdpa`.** On sm_10x, grouped-query attention stays on cuDNN when the query heads are a multiple of the KV heads. The existing tile-size rule for short sides still applies. Pre-Blackwell GPUs and uneven head groupings keep the FA path.
- **MOSS-Image `_Block`.** The `default_attention_backend=FA` pin is removed, so the platform default applies:
  - Hopper: FA, as before.
  - sm_10x: `DYNAMIC_CUDNN_SDPA`.

  The two text-refinement blocks keep FA. The supported-backend set is unchanged, since `DYNAMIC_CUDNN_SDPA` is accepted wherever FA and Torch SDPA are.
- **`test_dynamic_cudnn_sdpa_routing.py`.**
  - GQA, both self- and cross-attention shapes, stays on cuDNN on sm_100.
  - Uneven head grouping, and GQA before Blackwell, stay on FA.

## Accuracy Tests

The kernels are the ones Blackwell already uses for multi-head attention: cuDNN SDPA through `CudnnSDPAImpl`, with FA4 as the fallback. Only the routing changes, for the two cases above. As with #33655, cuDNN and FA4 round differently, so outputs are not bit-identical to the FA4 path.

`test_dynamic_cudnn_sdpa_routing.py` and `test_dynamic_cudnn_sdpa_selection.py`: 8 passed on B200.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Setup:
- 1x B200, main at d2cf2371b0 vs this branch, run back to back on the same GPU, with the cookbook commands and no attention flag.
- End-to-end client latency through the HTTP server: the median of 2 requests for video, 5 for images, after the harness warmup.
- Denoise time is from the server's stage log.

| Workload | main | this PR | Change | Denoise main → PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2V 1280x720, 189 frames | 112.32 s | **97.55 s** | -13.1% | 102.37 → 87.67 s |
| MOSS-Image-Base 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG 3 + uncond skip [22] | 4.772 s | **4.540 s** | -4.9% | 4.362 → 4.157 s |
| MOSS-Image-Base 1024x1024, 50 steps, ordinary CFG 3 | 4.621 s | **4.412 s** | -4.5% | 4.422 → 4.206 s |
| MiniMax-H3 T2VA 960x544, 124 frames (MHA, control) | 27.714 s | 27.707 s | 0.0% | 25.15 → 25.18 s |

The same routing at 4 GPUs, measured as `--attention-backend fa` vs `torch_cudnn_sdpa` with CFG 2 x Ulysses 2:

| Workload | FA | cuDNN | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cosmos3 T2V | 29.40 s | 26.39 s | -10% |
| Cosmos3 I2V | 29.42 s | 26.65 s | -9% |

title: [MiniMax-M3] Keep the fused q/k/v + index GEMM writable by online weight updates
author: Zhichenzzz
body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-M3's sparse-attention layers fuse `qkv_proj` and `index_qkv_proj` into one GEMM after loading and free the originals. `update_weights_from_tensor` then writes into the emptied `qkv_proj`, so the first RL weight sync fails:

```
IndexError: start out of range ([0, 0], got 128)
```

## Modifications

In `maybe_build_fused_qkv_index`, for bf16 the original `qkv_proj` / `index_qkv_proj` weights become views into the fused weight instead of being freed. An online weight update through the regular loader then writes the fused weight in place (same storage, so captured CUDA graphs keep reading the same buffer), with no extra memory. MXFP8 scales are re-laid out when fused, so MXFP8 originals are still freed as before; online updates into an MXFP8 checkpoint stay unsupported.

## Validation

Colocated RL in miles (Megatron trainer + this engine, BF16 rollout, GB300):

- Without this change, the first weight sync fails with the `IndexError` above.
- With it, MiniMax-M3 4-layer cut (2 dense-attention + 2 sparse layers), TP4/EP4, 3 steps: `--check-weight-update-equal` passes after every update, train/rollout log-prob abs diff 0.0050 / 0.0050 / 0.0050.

Run on the `radixark/miles:dev` image's sglang (before the v0.5.23 rebase of `sglang-miles`) with this function patched in; `maybe_build_fused_qkv_index` is unchanged between that base and the current one.

On the current `sglang-miles` (v0.5.23) with this PR, miles CI on 4 × H200 passes both MiniMax 4-layer e2e tests (colocated RL, weight check after every update): MiniMax-M3 https://github.com/radixark/miles/actions/runs/41275852481, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash https://github.com/radixark/miles/actions/runs/41275851020.

miles side: radixark/miles#4581 (MiniMax-M3 support) and its stack.

title: [CI] ci: Re-tier CUDA tests across base, extra, nightly, and weekly by importance
author: hnyls2002
body:
Re-tier the CUDA test registrations by what each test guards, so the per-PR gate keeps the core paths and the rest runs on the cadence its signal needs. - Tiers after this change: `base` (every PR) keeps the core default paths (scheduler, radix cache, default attention backends, chunked prefill, default speculative decoding, OpenAI API, basic PD/TP/DP-attention/PP) and cheap unit tests; `extra` (labeled PRs, and `main` every few hours) holds current flagship-model end-to-end tests and features people use that are off the default path (PD variants, HiCache storage backends, non-default speculative decoding, LoRA variants); `nightly` holds niche paths and tests whose only assertion is an accuracy or performance gate; `weekly` holds tests of old, unpopular, or superseded models. - 130 registrations in 128 files change stage; every test keeps its `runner_config`. - Estimated from recent measured per-file times (time x GPUs): `base` drops by about 63,600 GPU-seconds per run (about 70%), `extra` by about 39,000 net (about 17%). - `extra` gains `2-gpu-gb300` and `4-gpu-gb300` matrix rows. These rows pass no Rust-extension artifact, since that artifact is built for x86_64, so they restore the aarch64 cache that `pr-test.yml` seeds. A PR that changes sgl-kernel has no aarch64 wheel in this workflow, so those rows cannot run for it. - `nightly-test-nvidia.yml` folds its per-runner jobs into one matrix job, as `weekly-test-nvidia.yml` already does; the timeouts are unchanged and `runner_filter` becomes a free-text field matched in `_pr-test-stage.yml`. On top of that, `nightly` gains `1-gpu-small` and `8-gpu-b300` rows, so tests on those machines move to nightly on the same hardware. - Drop the `base-c` `8-gpu-h20` and `8-gpu-h200` matrix rows and suite names: no test registers there any more, and an empty suite would fail its stage job. - A PR that touches a demoted path can still run those tests with `/rerun-test`, which resolves extra, nightly and weekly registrations the same way as per-commit ones. - Add a `rerun-test` skill (`.agents/skills/rerun-test/SKILL.md`) on picking and running the tests a change touches; `ci-workflow-guide` and `write-sglang-test` point to it. title: [Perf] [AMD] attention: Forward decode graph variants through wrapper backends
author: xiaofei-zheng
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #47042, which added `AttentionBackend.get_decode_graph_variants` (default None) and the aiter decode partition buckets. Two non-blocking follow-ups from its review:

- Wrapper backends inherit the default None, so aiter partition buckets silently turn off under `HybridAttnBackend` (e.g. `--decode-attention-backend aiter`), `TboAttnBackend` and `HybridLinearAttnBackend`. Output stays correct; only the speedup is lost.
- The bucket tests checked capture metadata and eager output but did not capture and replay real decode graphs.

## Modifications

- `HybridAttnBackend.get_decode_graph_variants`: ask the backend that `_select_backend(capture_forward_mode)` routes to, the same routing its metadata and graph-state calls use. `SailHybridAttnBackend` inherits it.
- `HybridLinearAttnBackend`: ask `full_attn_backend`; linear-attention metadata does not depend on the variant label, so the same linear graph state is captured under each label. `ShortConvHybridAttnBackend` and the other subclasses inherit it.
- `TboAttnBackend`: ask `primary`. During capture the children read the same global variant label, and the label is chosen from the whole batch's longest request, which bounds every child's.
- Not forwarded: the Dots wrappers (MLA / FlashAttention / DSA children, one decode graph) and `MiniMaxHybridAttnBackend` (dense side not verified with buckets on ROCm).
- Tests:
  - `test_kv_translate_ownership.py` (CPU): every wrapper found by `_derive_wrapper_names()` must be listed, and each must return its decode child's variants, or None when that child returns None while another child returns variants. Fails for Hybrid, HybridLinear, ShortConv and TBO without this change.
  - `test_aiter_decode_partition_buckets.py` (AMD): `test_bucket_graphs_replay_like_eager` captures one real decode CUDA graph per bucket (p16 / p128 / p512) through `init_forward_metadata_out_graph(in_capture=True)` and `forward_decode`, checks the captured partition counts, then replays at max lengths 4096 / 4097 / 32768 / 32769 and requires bit-identical output to eager decode at `max_num_partitions`; a 4097-token batch replayed in the p16 graph must differ.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X (gfx950): `test_aiter_decode_partition_buckets.py`, `test_kv_translate_ownership.py` and `test_aiter_fp8_kv_scales_paths.py` pass (15 tests). The wrapper changes only decide which graphs are captured; each graph's output is covered by the replay test above.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured. Under the three wrappers decode now gets the same buckets #47042 measured for a plain aiter backend.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] moe: One-warp-per-token CUDA MoE router for sigmoid, sqrtsoftplus and softmax routing
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> (auto generated by Claude)
> (auto generated by MyGO (Make your GPU-kernel Optimal) agent)

## What

A JIT CUDA MoE router, `moe_route_warp`: one warp per token, each lane holds E/32 experts as order-preserving u32 keys, sorts them once (compile-time Batcher network in the new `sgl_kernel/algorithm.cuh`), and every top-k round reduces only the 32 lane heads (`redux` max, then min lane for the lowest-id tie-break). The launcher picks 1 warp per CTA while all tokens fit in one wave and 4 warps per CTA beyond that.

Covered (static config, 128..512 experts, multiple of 32): sigmoid / sqrtsoftplus with correction bias (grouped `noaux_tc` or ungrouped) and softmax, fp32 / bf16 logits, fused shared-expert slots, renorm epsilon, `num_token_non_padded`, packed FlashInfer ids. `moe_fused_gate` and `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` dispatch to it whenever the config is covered; everything else (fewer than 128 experts, Kimi-K3's 896, softcap, fp16 logits) keeps the Triton router.

Also:
- DeepSeek-V4.1 VL per-token bias (`input_ids` / `bias_alt`) as a compile-time mode; the token id is loaded before the PDL wait.
- MuseSpark routing moves to the same kernel (compile-time mode); `muse_spark/routing.cuh` is removed.
- Removed kernels whose paths now go through `moe_fused_gate`: the JIT `topk_softmax` (unused on CUDA), the LoRA `kimi_k2_moe_fused_gate` and `topk_softmax_pack` (and the two LoRA env flags of the former).
- NaN logits rank last (as DeepGEMM's mega-gate).

## Performance

B200, CUDA graph, median; main path = flashinfer `fused_topk_deepseek` (DeepSeek-V3) or the Triton router (others). Router alone, us:

| config | T=1 | T=1024 | T=16384 |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V3 (256, 8 groups / 4, top-8) | 1.88 -> 1.43 | 3.07 -> 1.97 | 24.6 -> 12.3 |
| Kimi-K2 (384, top-8) | 2.42 -> 1.60 | 4.22 -> 2.33 | 39.7 -> 13.1 |
| GLM-4.5 (160, top-8) | 1.80 -> 1.43 | 2.91 -> 1.80 | 23.4 -> 9.4 |
| Qwen3-MoE (128, top-8, softmax) | 2.38 -> 1.23 | 2.99 -> 1.60 | 13.9 -> 8.2 |
| Qwen3.5 (512, top-10, softmax) | 3.40 -> 1.68 | 5.82 -> 2.33 | 63.1 -> 15.6 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 (384, top-6, sqrtsoftplus) | 2.50 -> 1.64 | 3.93 -> 2.91 | 35.2 -> 17.2 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 VL (per-token bias) | 2.58 -> 1.99 | 4.10 -> 2.85 | 35.6 -> 17.6 |
| MuseSpark (256, top-8; old JIT kernel) | 1.64 -> 1.27 | 2.70 -> 1.97 | 16.8 -> 10.7 |

Behind the gate GEMM with PDL (decode), the router costs 0.5-2 us less per MoE layer. H200 gains are larger (e.g. Kimi-K2 T=16384 45.6 -> 15.8 us).

## Validation

- Router vs an fp64 reference (sigmoid / softmax / sqrtsoftplus, grouped and ungrouped, renorm, scaling, fused shared slots, padding, packed ids, per-token bias): same expert set up to near ties, descending ranking order, weights within fp32 rounding; exact ties go to the lowest expert id. NaN / inf handling is implementation-defined and not pinned by tests.
- `test_moe_route_warp`, `test_muse_spark_routing`, `test_moe_fused_gate`, `test_jit_grouped_topk`, `test_fused_topk_deepseek`, `test_marlin_packed_topk_unpack` and the MoE dispatch / routing unit tests pass on B200 and H200.
- End-to-end on 1x H200, this PR vs its parent on main (sgl-eval gsm8k, full 1319, seeds 1 / 2; decode ITL from `one_batch_server`, input 512 / output 256):

| model | gsm8k main | gsm8k PR | ITL bs1 / bs8 / bs32 (ms), main -> PR |

| Ling-mini-2.0 (256 experts, grouped sigmoid) | 89.92 / 90.67 | 90.22 / 91.21 | 1.85 / 2.65 / 3.75 -> 1.80 / 2.38 / 3.66 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B (`--moe-runner-backend triton`, softmax) | 94.92 / 94.92 | 94.92 / 94.69 | 3.68 / 7.55 / 11.50 -> 3.65 / 7.15 / 11.08 |

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] mega_moe: Count EPLB load in-kernel
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

With EPLB recording on, each MegaMoE layer launches a separate histogram kernel over the gate's physical top-k ids to feed the expert distribution recorder. On a DeepSeek-V4.1 DEP16 decode step this is one extra launch per MoE layer, about 0.16 ms per step at 40 requests per rank.

DeepGEMM's `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` already counts, per local expert, the rows each expert receives (`cumulative_local_expert_recv_stats`, int32, one entry per local expert, accumulated). The pinned `sgl-deep-gemm==0.2.3.post2` exposes it. The histogram therefore repeats work the kernel already does.

## Modifications

The change applies when all of these hold:
- the layer runs SM100 `fp8xfp4` MegaMoE with no fused shared experts (`num_fused_shared_experts == 0`);
- the new `ExpertDistributionRecorder.get_current_pass_local_count_buffer(num_experts, ep_rank, ep_size)` returns this rank's slice of the current layer's physical count row. It returns `None` without a current layer, without the select-experts gatherer, when neither recording nor a CUDA graph capture is on (the same gate as the histogram it replaces), or when the row width differs from the layer's expert count. The no-op recorder always returns `None`.

In that case `forward_mega_moe` passes that slice as `cumulative_local_expert_recv_stats`, and runs the routing inside `disable_this_region()`. Neither the MegaGate in-buffer path nor the regular top-k fallback can then count the picks a second time. Ranks with no local tokens also pass the row: they still receive, and count, other ranks' rows.

Counts are now kept per destination rank instead of per source rank. Physical expert ids are rank-major, so the cross-rank sum gives the same physical loads.
- **`per_pass` dumps change:** each rank's row now holds the rows its experts received, not the picks it sent.
- **Padding:** padded rows (top-k id -1) are never dispatched, so they are not counted.

Where the change does not apply, the router histogram is kept and behaviour is unchanged. The only addition is one recorder lookup per layer on the host.
- **No current layer:** the recorder has no row to hand out. This happens in the DeepSeek-V4 NextN draft, and in prefill under piecewise CUDA graphs.
- **Fused shared experts:** these use the 256+EP per-rank shared-expert slot layout. Those slots are not EPLB experts, so mapping the kernel's per-slot counts would need a separate translation, which this PR does not attempt.
- **Other cases:** recording off, SM90, and other MMA types.

Routed-experts capture does not need a fallback: the kernel row is passed on every routing path, and the experts capturer is not gated by `disable_this_region()`.

The DeepSeek-V4.1 MegaMoE deployment keeps the shared expert in the kernel's own shared weights (`num_fused_shared_experts == 0`), so it takes the new path.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerical change to model outputs: only where the EPLB statistics are counted changes.

- **EP4 equality on 4 GB300 GPUs, through `forward_mega_moe` and the recorder's slice method at this PR's head.** A stand-in recorder adds a real histogram (`record_physical_counts`) into the same count row whenever it is asked to, unless a `disable_this_region()` is active, as the real recorder does. The check is: received counts summed over ranks == histogram of every rank's own top-k ids, summed over ranks.

  | per-rank routing | rows / padded | counted vs histogram | histogram calls |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | all MegaGate in-buffer | 240 / 17 | 10,704 = 10,704 | 0 |
  | one rank with zero local tokens, rest MegaGate | 384 / 5 | 13,644 = 13,644 | 0 |
  | mixed: zero tokens / top-k fallback / MegaGate / MegaGate | 960 / 40 | 33,120 = 33,120 | 0 |
  | all top-k fallback | 1152 / 0 | 55,296 = 55,296 | 0 |
  | no current layer (recorder returns the whole table) | 384 / 5 | 13,644 = 13,644 | 6 (histogram fallback) |
  | recording off | 240 / 0 | nothing counted | 0 |

  - **Routed-experts capture on:** the same six cases, with the gate returning the out-of-buffer routing it produces under capture (`mega_gate.py:206`), give the same counts as above in every case, with no histogram calls in the four counted cases.
  - **Negative control:** with `disable_this_region()` made a no-op (capture on), the four counted cases double count (for example 21,408 vs 10,704). The no-layer and recording-off cases are unchanged.
  - **Idle ranks:** an earlier variant passed the stats only on the MegaGate in-buffer path. It failed the zero-token case (5,690 vs 13,644) and the mixed case (15,346 vs 33,120). A rank without local tokens still receives other ranks' rows, so it must count them.
- **EPLB still converges:** in a DEP16 decode run with the earlier in-buffer-only form, every rebalance (every 15000 steps) reaches window balancedness 0.89-0.90. Balancedness is mean over max of the per-rank loads summed over the window, per layer.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

The workload is DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, PD-disaggregated, with DEP16 decode. Decode runs at most 40 requests per rank (35.5 mean), with simulated acceptance length 3.51 and agentic traces. The comparison is against the same image without the change. The "this PR" row is this PR's code applied to that image.

| | decode step p50, 32-47 running | decode step p50, 16-31 running | client throughput / GPU (steady window) |
|---|---|---|---|
| base | 14.1 ms | 13.5 ms | 1.000x |
| this PR | 13.9 ms | 13.4 ms | 1.006x (within run-to-run noise) |

- The step saving matches the removed histogram launches (~0.16 ms per step in a profile at this shape).
- In this configuration, client throughput is flat within noise.
- An earlier in-buffer-only form gave the same step and throughput.
- No errors in the run.
- Both runs used the deployment above (`num_fused_shared_experts == 0`, layer index always set in the target model), where this PR's final form takes the same path as the measured form.

## Checklist

- [x] Format with `pre-commit run`.
- [x] Unit tests, 28 passed on GB300:
  - `test/registered/unit/eplb/test_megamoe_prefill_recorder.py`: `get_current_pass_local_count_buffer` returns this rank's slice of the current layer's row, and `None` with no current layer, a width mismatch or recording off;
  - `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_mega_moe_deepgemm_api.py`: MegaMoE asks the recorder with its expert count and EP rank and size, falls back on fused shared experts, SM90 and other MMA types, and passes the kernel argument through (absent by default).

title: [Perf] kda: Batch strided FlashInfer prefill input copies
author: Codoge
body:
## Motivation

Kimi-K3's token-major prefill convolution leaves strided Q/K/V views, and its merged gate projection leaves a strided beta view. FlashInfer's KDA wrapper materializes these inputs with separate copies. Batch those required copies into one Triton launch without changing KDA arithmetic, gates, state precision, or checkpoint handling.

This integrates the measured PP8 prototype into upstream `main`. Full-model serving validation now passes for these production changes on the common upstream `main` base `592754fc5e`, with FlashInfer 0.7.2; the standalone and repeated combined results are reported below. Real GPU operator tests pass on both FlashInfer 0.7.1 and the pinned 0.7.2.

### Relationship to sgl-project/sglang#47451

The optimizations overlap on the Q/K/V materialization cost, but use different approaches:

- #47451 changes the convolution producer to write contiguous Q/K/V groups, eliminating those three copies. It also covers the FlashInfer prefill-graph producer path.
- This PR leaves the producer layout alone and combines outstanding consumer-side copies, including beta. It covers both `FlashInferKDAPrefillKernel.extend` and `FlashInferKDAPrefillGraph.run` through the same helper.
- Contiguous inputs are returned unchanged. When fewer than two inputs require copying (e.g. grouped Q/K/V plus only strided beta), the ordinary contiguous path is retained. There is no redundant Q/K/V copy or extra fused-copy launch in that case.
- Their standalone speedups must **not** be added. Prefer the producer-layout solution where applicable; this is a separately reviewable alternative for remaining token-major inputs, not a second claimed gain on top of #47451.

## Modifications

- Add a bit-preserving multi-input copy kernel under `kernels/ops/attention` and use it at the FlashInfer KDA input boundary.
- Keep contiguous tensors aliased, validate device/dtype/indexing bounds, and fall back to PyTorch for unsupported inputs or autograd.
- Preserve input slicing and all existing KDA computation arguments. No new environment variable or CLI option.
- Add registered GPU coverage for the real 16K/96-head K3 layout, short/tail/empty shapes, BF16/FP32 bit patterns, already-grouped QKV, CUDA Graph replay, and real FlashInfer outputs/state.

## Accuracy Tests

On an idle B300/B30Z (SM103), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, separately using FlashInfer 0.7.1 and 0.7.2:

- **5 GPU tests passed on each version**, including actual Triton execution at `[1, 16384, 96, 128]` and CUDA Graph replay with changed inputs.
- Raw-bit comparisons cover NaN payloads, infinities, subnormals, and signed zero.
- Real FlashInfer KDA calls on strided inputs match contiguous-reference outputs and recurrent state exactly, in eager mode and through the production graph adapter replayed with updated inputs. Warmup and capture use the same stream, as required by the FlashInfer workspace.
- The candidate kernel and wrapper were loaded from this branch into the existing GPU environment; no installed source was modified. FlashInfer 0.7.2 was tested in an isolated wheel overlay without bypassing its version checks.
- Ruff, isort, AST parsing, registered-test lint, and `git diff --check` passed.

The current six full-service runs each pass 12 fixed greedy output checks covering input lengths 1,024 / 16,383 / 16,384 / 16,385 / 32,768 / 65,536, each repeated twice. All 60 comparisons against A1 match output token IDs and input SHA256 hashes. An additional eight C4 concurrent fixed-input checks match between A2 and B2. These are finite output-regression checks, not logits-level equality or a full task-accuracy benchmark.

### Blackwell review follow-up (2026-11-01)

## Motivation

For the measured Kimi-K3 TP1/PP8 prefill workload, FlashInfer 0.7.1's 16K-token MoE candidate enumeration exposed token tiles 192 and 256. A supported tile128/config0 tactic, discovered through smaller-shape candidate enumeration and then executed at the real 16K shape, performed better on captured early/late-layer routing.

This ports the tile128 approach to the repository's pinned **FlashInfer 0.7.2**, using its existing cache-loading API. Re-enumeration on B30Z identified **tile128/config4**, and real captured-input replay verified that tactic and the new record. The older 0.7.1/config0 record is not installed or accepted. Tactic IDs are version-specific; no dependency downgrade or version-check bypass is included.

## Modifications

- Seed one serving-derived 16K MoE tuning bucket during startup, before the user's persistent cache is loaded. Explicit user-cache entries retain precedence; disabling cache reuse keeps fresh tuning behavior.
- Restrict loading to Kimi-K3, TP1/PP8/EP1, chunk16K, BF16 model dtype, SM103 and FlashInfer 0.7.2. FlashInfer's full environment metadata check further restricts the bundled record to the measured B30Z/CUDA/library combination.
- The cache key includes both activation/weight formats, local/global expert counts, top-k, hidden/intermediate dimensions, activation and weight layout, plus the unpacked routing representation.
- Fix the existing target/draft CUDA cache-phase fixture to supply the runner field read by the startup guard.
- Use the existing `load_configs` mechanism; do not replace `AutoTuner.choose_one`, add a process-wide monkey patch, or add a new configuration switch.

The record follows FlashInfer's tuning-bucket semantics. It is not a universal tile128 policy for arbitrary sequence lengths, models, hardware, EP or decode workloads. Existing explicit cache choices can override it.

- **2 unit tests passed**, with subcases rejecting other model types, parallelism, chunk sizes, dtypes, hardware and unvalidated FlashInfer 0.7.1/0.7.3.

The 0.7.2 Python wheel and its matching NVIDIA kernels were tested in an isolated overlay, retaining version checks; the installed 0.7.1 package was not modified. These verify the policy, public cache adapter and actual MoE operation.

Full-model serving validation now passes for these production changes on the common upstream `main` base `592754fc5e`, with FlashInfer 0.7.2; the standalone and repeated combined results are reported below. title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dsv4: Route padded decode replays through the metadata glue graph
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

`DecodeCudaGraphRunner._init_replay_attn_metadata` only routes the attention-metadata prep through the metadata glue graph when `raw_bs == bs`. Every other replay runs the eager `init_forward_metadata_out_graph` path, which is dozens of small host-dispatched ops. Two common cases hit that path:
- The DSpark draft runner is dp-local, so it replays at the capture bucket of its own batch size. Any rank whose batch is not exactly a capture size takes the eager path.
- Target verify replays padded to the DP max take it as well.

On DSV4.1-Flash GB300 disagg DEP16 (c2884, 40 running per rank), the draft `G.attn_meta` costs 0.56-0.62 ms on padded ranks vs 0.06 ms glued. That cost sits on the host path between the DP agreement and the draft graph launch.

## Related PRs

One of four DSV4.1 attn-DP decode host-path changes that cut the host work between the DP agreement and the draft graph launch. They are independent in code and were measured together: #47676 (padded metadata glue), #47677 (persistent DP-MoE counts), #47678 (bulk decode-prep fill) and #47685 (KV page top-up, measured on top of the other three).

## Modifications

The glue route now also takes padded replays (`0 < raw_bs < bs`). There is no separate switch: it engages wherever the backend declared the DSV4 draft or target-verify glue (the audited host-free prep) and the runner is not in ragged verify mode, and falls back to the eager prep otherwise. Non-DSV4 backends, the generic `SGLANG_ENABLE_METADATA_GLUE_GRAPH` glue, TBO and LoRA keep the padding-free route.

Behavior change: the DSpark draft glue is on by default (static ragged verify mode), so padded draft replays now take the glue graph without any flag. The target-verify glue still follows `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_TARGET_VERIFY_METADATA_GLUE`. The DEP16 / DEP32 validation below ran without `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION` on decode, i.e. in exactly this default configuration; the TP4 c1 runs had it on.

Why the padded prep is the same as the eager padded prep: both read the same `req_pool_indices` / `seq_lens` slots, whose tails `fill_from` resets to the registry pad values (0 and `seq_len_fill_value`). The glue view reads the padded `out_cache_loc` slot (`num_tokens` is passed for every glued replay). `fill_from` zeroed that slot's tail, and the eager prep zero-pads the raw tensor to the same length. The declared prep reads nothing else that depends on `raw_bs`, so the captured prep for key `bs` serves padded and unpadded replays alike. IDLE replays stay eager. The contract comment in `metadata_glue_graph.py` is updated to cover the padded route.

All runs: GB300, DSV4.1-Flash, on a 2026-10-30 nightly.

## Accuracy Tests

- In-server bitwise check (diagnostic overlay, not part of this PR): for the first 40 captured padded draft replays per rank, the check snapshots the glued metadata, runs the eager padded prep on the same inputs, and compares every metadata tensor (page_table, raw_out_loc, seq_lens_casual, positions_casual, swa_page_indices, swa_topk_lengths). Result on DEP16: 640 checks (16 ranks, raw_bs 2-13 on bs=14), 0 mismatches.
- The padded target-verify route is covered by the same argument, but none of the runs below exercised it: it needs `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_TARGET_VERIFY_METADATA_GLUE`, which was off in the DEP runs, and TP4 c1 never pads.
- GSM8K, 1P1D DEP16 with real DSpark acceptance, together with the two sibling host changes (#47677, #47678): 96.82% (1319 examples, 0% truncated or errors) vs 96.89% without them. Accept length 3.50 vs 3.49-3.51.
- TP4 c1 agg (mega flag on, all three host changes): T=1 GSM8K 97.33% vs 97.33%, long-context needle retrieval at 20K-160K tokens 48/48 vs 48/48 (greedy) and 24/24 vs 24/24 (T=1), accept length 3.591 vs 3.598.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

| | DEP16 nsys, before | DEP16 nsys, after |
|---|---|---|
| draft `G.attn_meta`, median over ranks | 170 us | 58 us |
| draft `G.attn_meta`, worst rank | 620 us | 64 us |

The following numbers are **combined** with the two sibling host changes (#47677 DSpark persistent DP-MoE counts, #47678 DFlash bulk decode prep). Same cluster and recipe, but the two arms ran on different days:
- DEP32 c5768 (10P1D): decode step p50 13.9 ms vs 15.2 ms. This is the robust number.
- Same runs: steady-window per-GPU throughput (prompt + completion tokens, mean of minutes 8-20 of the aiperf run, same x0.96 normalisation for both arms) 660.6k vs 664.4k tok/s/GPU at p90 interactivity 219.8 vs 200.8 tok/s/user (+9.5%). Same-day controls of this recipe drift by about 3% on interactivity, so read the interactivity gain as indicative, not exact.
- DEP16 c2884: 720.1k vs 719.0k tok/s/GPU (same steady-window metric and normalisation), step 13.73 vs 13.80 ms (no regression).
- TP4 c1 agg: step p50 3.514 vs 3.501 ms, p90 interactivity 968.1 vs 963.2 tok/s/user (neutral).

A MegaMoE NVLink barrier timeout after the benchmark abort also happens without these changes, so it is not caused by them. Serving-phase results are unaffected.

## Checklist
- [x] Format with pre-commit
- [x] GPU validation on cluster (above)
- [x] Unit tests: test_dsv41_draft_metadata_glue.py, test_dsv41_target_verify_metadata_glue.py and test_decode_cuda_graph_runner.py (existing tests updated for the `num_tokens` argument, a padded-slot case, and the padded / IDLE routing cases)

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dflash: Fill decode-prep length buffers in bulk
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

`DFlashDraftInputV2.prepare_for_decode` writes the committed, current and next KV lengths with one CPU-tensor `__setitem__` per request and field, i.e. 3 x bs element writes every decode step. On DSV4.1-Flash GB300 disagg DEP16 (40 running per rank), `prepare_for_decode` takes 1.0-1.4 ms per step, and these element writes are about 0.4 ms of it. That time sits on the pre-agreement host path of the last DP rank to arrive.

## Related PRs

One of four DSV4.1 attn-DP decode host-path changes that cut the host work between the DP agreement and the draft graph launch. They are independent in code and were measured together: #47676 (padded metadata glue), #47677 (persistent DP-MoE counts), #47678 (bulk decode-prep fill) and #47685 (KV page top-up, measured on top of the other three).

## Modifications

The per-element loop is replaced by an exact rewrite, so there is no switch:
- The committed lengths and top-k values are gathered into lists.
- Each length buffer is written once through its numpy view. The buffers, their dtypes and the point at which they are written, before the non-blocking H2D copies, are unchanged.
- The sums, max top-k and uniform top-k value are computed from the lists.

All runs: GB300, DSV4.1-Flash, on a 2026-10-30 nightly.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] gemm: Tiny GEMM as SIMT + mma.sync templates with batch-size dispatch
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> (auto generated by Claude)
> (auto generated by MyGO (Make your GPU-kernel Optimal) agent)

## What

The tiny GEMM (`x[m, k] @ w[n, k].T` for MoE router gates and other skinny projections) becomes one kernel family with two templates under `kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/tiny_gemm/`, replacing `tiny_gemm.cuh` and `small_gemm_bf16.cuh`:

- SIMT (`simt.cuh`, CUDA and ROCm, bf16 or fp32 weights): K / 16 lanes cover a row of w and reduce it with shuffles (and shared memory past one warp); a CTA owns a few rows of w, loaded before the PDL wait. Larger batches copy each weight tile into the fewest CTAs along `blockIdx.y`, rows spread evenly.
- MMA (`mma.cuh`, sm90+, bf16 weights): `mma.sync m16n8k16`, K split over a thread-block cluster and its warps (any cluster size from 1 to 8 with an even split), partial sums reduced over the warps in shared memory and reduce-scattered over the cluster with `st.async`. Batches are tiled over CTA rows sized by the driver's cluster occupancy.

`tiny_gemm_bf16` picks the template per batch size: m = 1 always takes SIMT, larger m takes MMA from `M* = max(2, round(1 + 300 / (K * (4 + N_TILE) / 128)))`, a B200 cost model (SIMT pays an L2 re-read of x plus `N_TILE * K` FMAs per extra row, MMA a fixed ~300-cycle DSMEM reduction), with measured exceptions for K <= 512. FP32 weights always take SIMT (exact fp32 products); ROCm and other archs only have SIMT. Any m is served; callers keep their own cuBLAS cutover.

Also:
- `small_gemm_bf16` is removed: the DeepSeek-V4.1 indexer (`wk` 128x512, `weights_proj` 32x5120) calls `tiny_gemm_bf16` directly, under the same gate.
- `max_m` / `n_split` are removed from `tiny_gemm_bf16` / `can_use_tiny_gemm` (no longer used by the kernels); callers are updated.
- The cluster occupancy probe (`csrc/occupancy/cluster_probe.cuh`) sets its function attributes once per device instead of on every query, so concurrent queries (e.g. from `parallel_compile` threads) no longer race.
- The test and benchmark cover more router shapes (DeepSeek-V3/V4/V4.1, Kimi-K2/K3, GLM-5, Qwen3/3.5, dots3, gpt-oss, Kimi-K3 KDA, DeepSeek-V4.1 indexer) and build every module in parallel before running.

## Performance

21 shapes (above) x m = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, bf16 output, CUDA graph, median. PDL: behind a producer that releases its dependents early (weights prefetched before the wait); cold: L2 flushed, no PDL. Geomean of time ratio (this PR / baseline, lower is better):

| GPU | vs main (PDL / cold) | vs FlashInfer tinygemm_bf16 | vs FlashInfer router GEMM (5 shapes) | vs cuBLAS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B200 | 0.73 / 0.88 | 0.52 / 0.69 | 0.35 / 0.69 | 0.28 / 0.58 |
| H200 | 0.72 / 0.89 | 0.52 / 0.71 | 0.38 / 0.81 | 0.20 / 0.53 |

Examples, us, PDL (main -> this PR; cuBLAS in brackets):

| shape | GPU | m = 1 | m = 16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V3 router 256x7168 | B200 | 1.28 -> 1.28 (4.83) | 4.38 -> 1.79 (5.50) |
| Kimi-K3 router 896x7168 | B200 | 1.73 -> 1.76 (7.74) | 9.41 -> 2.27 (7.33) |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash router 384x5120 | B200 | 1.41 -> 1.38 (5.34) | 4.54 -> 1.57 (5.60) |
| DeepSeek-V3 router 256x7168 | H200 | 1.28 -> 1.25 (7.33) | 4.83 -> 1.92 (7.58) |
| Kimi-K3 router 896x7168 | H200 | 1.95 -> 1.95 (9.02) | 13.57 -> 2.94 (9.09) |

m = 1 matches main (both SIMT); the gain grows with m.

## Validation

- `test_tiny_gemm`: both templates against an fp64 reference over all shapes and m up to 64 (bf16 and fp32 output, fp32 weights), per-template batch invariance (a row's result does not depend on its batch), and the dispatching entry point; passes on B200 and H200.
- ROCm runs the SIMT template only; it is exercised by the AMD Kimi-K3 KDA test (`test_kimi_k3_kda_inproj_fusion`), which calls the tiny GEMM.

title: [Perf] attention: Round the DeepSeek-V4.1 dense indexer logits tiles to whole SM waves
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> (auto generated by Claude)

## Motivation

The DeepSeek-V4.1 dense prefill indexer (`dense_prefill_topk`) tiles the `[rows, keys]` logits of a chunk by query rows under a memory budget, and DeepGEMM strides each tile's row blocks (`128 // heads` rows) over one CTA per SM. At long context the budget gives tiles that end in a mostly empty wave, e.g. 1308-row tiles at 400K compressed keys are 2.2 waves on 148 SMs, so every tile pays for 3.

## Changes

`flat_index_logits_rows_per_tile`: on CUDA, a tile of more than one wave is rounded down to a whole number of waves (`128 // heads * num_SMs` rows). Tiles only shrink, so the logits stay within the budget; tiling is by rows, so the results are unchanged.

## Validation (B300, `dense_prefill_topk` as V4.1 calls it: 32 heads, top-k 512, DeepGEMM 0.2.3.post2 + DeepSelect)

Median of 9, cold L2, CUDA graph (eager agrees within 1-2 %). Top-k identical in every cell (up to DeepSelect's existing bf16 tie nondeterminism, also present between two runs of main).

| chunk rows x max compressed keys | tiles main -> this PR | main (ms) | this PR (ms) | ratio | peak logits MiB |

| 16384 x 128K | 4 -> 5 | 6.068 | 6.095 | 1.004 | 1029 -> 893 |

title: [Perf] diffusion: Nomas camera attention reads each frame's value directly when camera_chunk_size is 1
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
## Summary

When `camera_chunk_size == 1` (the value in the released Hy-Nomas `transformer/config.json`), each camera chunk is one latent frame, so the softmax in `NomasCameraAttention` runs over a single key and equals 1.0. The output for every token is just the value vector of its frame, independent of q and k.

This PR takes that path directly: it skips the `img_attn_q` GEMM, the q/k RMSNorm + RoPE and the per-frame SDPA launches, and gathers `v` by frame index (with `token_offset` for sequence-parallel slices). Other chunk sizes use the old code unchanged. The change is 7 lines in `nomas.py` (`git diff -w`); the rest of the diff is re-indentation of the old path into the `else`.

Scope: this only runs for requests that carry camera poses (`norm_extrinsics`). Requests without a camera never reach this module.

## Evidence

Real Hy-Nomas DiT weights loaded from the assembled checkpoint (0 missing / 0 unexpected keys), H100, 352x640, one 10-latent segment of 8 steps, DiT only, random text embeddings, median of several runs:

| | original | this PR | bitwise equal |
|---|---|---|---|
| hist 0 | 1341 ms | 1237 ms (-8%) | yes |
| hist 3 | 1460 ms | 1271 ms (-13%) | yes |
| hist 8 | 1543 ms | 1322 ms (-14%) | yes |

A second container (slower host CPU) showed larger gains for the same comparison: 1858 -> 1370 ms (-26%) at hist 0, 1920 -> 1438 ms (-25%) at hist 3, 2299 -> 1814 ms (-21%) at hist 3 with action windows. The forward issues about 8k kernel launches and the GPU is idle roughly half the time, so the gain scales with how launch-bound the host is. Absolute numbers differ between containers; only compare within a table.

## Tests

`test_camera_chunk_of_one_reads_each_frames_value_without_attention` in `test_nomas.py`: builds the expected output with real SDPA over random q/k (one key per frame), checks the module matches it, checks a slice that starts mid-frame, and fails if `img_attn_q` is called.

- main: fails (`a one-key softmax needs no query`), Modal CPU.
- This PR: **not run on the final tree** (CPU or CUDA unit tests). Bitwise equality was checked on real weights in the benchmark above.

## Review

An independent review pass found no correctness issue. Optional follow-ups it suggested: a `has_camera` tensor case in the test, and a comment that the shortcut relies on `chunk_size == 1`.

## Not checked

- No end-to-end camera request, only the DiT.
- Fixed-tree CPU and CUDA unit tests not run (see above).
- TP/SP multi-rank run not done; the slice test covers the `token_offset` path on one rank.
