title: [Feat] [AMD] quark: Quark int4 W4A16 on ROCm, and gfx1151 kernels for Strix Halo decode and prefill
author: hubertlu-tw
body:
Co-author: @clintg6  @peizhang56

## Motivation

On `main`, `amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-INT4-W4A16` does not load. It is a Quark AWQ export (dense, int4 weight-only, group 128), and Quark has no int4 weight-only scheme, so loading raises `NotImplementedError: No quark compatible scheme was found`. #41389 and #47408 added W4A16 execution for Quark MXFP4 MoE checkpoints only.

On a Strix Halo APU (gfx1151, Radeon 8060S, RDNA3.5, 256 GB/s LPDDR5X), single-stream decode with the DFlash2 drafter is memory-bound, and the generic kernels run well below the memory roof:

- At M <= 8, W4A16 GEMMs read weights at 40-70 GB/s.
- Target-verify attention walks the cached prefix once per query block; the split-KV verify kernels are gfx95-only.
- Without aiter or vllm, `GemmaRMSNorm` falls back to an 11-op eager chain: about 1,400 of the about 2,600 kernel launches in one 8-token verify step (counted from the forward code).

This PR adds the Quark int4 W4A16 scheme for ROCm, gfx1151 kernels for those paths, and two exact one-kernel replacements on HIP fallback paths.

## Modifications

### Design

- One gate: every gfx115x path checks `use_gfx115_kernels()` (`srt/utils/common.py`): `is_gfx115_supported()` (RDNA3.5, the same check #46327 uses) and the kill switch `SGLANG_DISABLE_GFX115_KERNELS` not set, read once. The kernels were tuned and measured on gfx1151 (Strix Halo); the other gfx115x parts share the ISA. Each kernel module also has a `covered()` predicate that admits only measured shapes; anything else falls back to the existing code.
- Decisions are made at init where possible: the Quark scheme decides at weight load (including whether the Gluon kernel is usable, see below), and the Triton backend's verify path decides in `__init__`.
- Generic layers are untouched: unquantized linears, the LM head and DFlash's candidate ranking keep their `main` code paths. Only the Quark int4 scheme reaches the gfx1151 GEMMs, and one early return in the Triton backend sends verify attention to its kernel.
- The kernels live in arch-named files under `kernels/ops`, like the existing `*_gfx950` and `*_sm100` files, and no generic function signature gains an arch parameter.

### Quark int4 W4A16 scheme (ROCm)

- `QuarkConfig._is_int4_w4a16` selects `QuarkW4A16Int4` (`srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a16_int4.py`) on HIP for int4, symmetric, per group of 32/64/128, static, weight-only quantization. On CUDA it returns False, so CUDA behaves as on `main`. The scheme rejects asymmetric checkpoints. Their zero points would need repacking and a wrapped loader in the fused GDN projection, and there is no checkpoint to test them.
- Quark stores signed codes in AWQ packing. At load the weights are repacked once to `[N, K / 8]` with unsigned codes and zero point 8 (`repack_awq_w4_to_skinny(..., signed=True)`), which is lossless.
- The GEMM is a Triton skinny GEMM (`kernels/ops/quantization/w4a16_skinny_triton.py`) with generic block sizes by shape and a gfx1151 config table. On gfx1151 with symmetric group-128 weights, the small-M and prefill kernels below take the shapes they cover.
- `qwen3_5.py`: the fused GDN projection loader splits packed int4 tensors in packed units.
- Credit: the Quark int4 scheme, `_is_int4_w4a16`, the skinny GEMM with its AWQ repack kernels and gfx1151 config table, and the `qwen3_5.py` loader fix start from Clint Greene's Strix Halo branch ([clintg6/sglang@3c8a486](https://github.com/clintg6/sglang/commit/3c8a486f63b91733df8091758cc75cc53ff49345)), whose Triton GEMM is adapted from vLLM's (vllm-project/vllm#37352). This PR drops the GPTQ parts and the HIP `wvSplitK` kernels of that branch, restricts the scheme to ROCm, and adds the gfx1151 kernels and the row pad.

### gfx1151 kernels

- W4A16 small-M GEMM (`kernels/ops/quantization/w4a16_small_m_gfx1151.py`): a Gluon WMMA kernel for at most 16 rows (decode, a DFlash verify block). The int4 codes become bf16 WMMA operands with one `and_or` per register: `(w >> 4i) & 0x000F000F | 0x43004300` is bf16 `128 + q`. Weights and scales are prefetched into loop-carried registers and no load is masked. Configs per shape come from graph-timed sweeps: the Qwen3.8 target projections run split-K 1 (no zero-fill and cast launches around fp32 atomics, about 3.5-4 ms per verify step over split-K 2); split-K, where kept, is at most 2, so the fp32 atomic sum is order-independent. It reads at 165-210 GB/s on the Qwen3.8 projections at M = 8. It needs Triton >= 3.7 (`AMDWMMALayout` with register and warp bases); the Quark scheme checks this once at load and otherwise logs a warning and leaves small-M calls to the skinny GEMM. The public gfx1151 images ship Triton 3.7.
- W4A16 prefill GEMM (`kernels/ops/quantization/w4a16_prefill_gfx1151.py`): the same operand trick in `tl.dot`, from 256 rows, bf16 activations.
- int4 row pad (`pad_rows` in `w4a16_skinny_triton.py`, applied when Quark W4A16 weights load on gfx1151): rows read together alias onto the same L2/MALL channels. A 128 B pad per row makes the prefill GEMM 1.10x and an 8-row verify step's small-M GEMMs 1.06x faster, summed over the Qwen3.8 projections (up to 1.2x on `down` and `o_proj`); results are bitwise equal with and without it. This is the int4 counterpart of #46327 for bf16. The three W4A16 kernels take the row stride from the tensor.
- Verify attention (`kernels/ops/attention/verify_attention_gfx1151.py`, called from the Triton backend's `forward_extend` in TARGET_VERIFY): one program per (request, kv head, split) reads its share of the prefix once for all draft tokens and q heads. q is re-read in 32-wide chunks per KV tile instead of being held as a whole WMMA operand, which keeps the kernel at 12 register spills instead of 139 (a test guards the count). Numerics follow `extend_attention_fwd`: fp32 online softmax, with `p` rounded to bf16 for PV. It runs only for page size 1, full-attention layers, no KV id translation, causal attention, dense q and o, contiguous bf16 KV caches, and none of soft cap, sinks, custom mask, sliding window or KV descale.
- GDN prefill: a grouped three-head `chunk_fwd_o` kernel for the Qwen3.5/3.8 head ratio (`fla/chunk_o.py`) that computes the chunk's `q·kᵀ` once for the three value heads sharing a q/k head, and head-major launch order for `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kkt_solve_kernel` and `recompute_w_u_fwd_kernel` (`fla/chunk_fwd.py`, `fla/wy_fast.py`), so concurrently running programs read the same token rows.

### HIP without aiter or vllm (exact one-kernel replacements of eager fallbacks)

- `GemmaRMSNorm.forward_hip` calls the Triton `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm` / `gemma_rmsnorm` instead of `forward_native`. Those kernels were added for MiniMax-M3 in #28715 (moved to `kernels/ops` in #32045), and `main` uses them only when aiter is on. The new `round_sum=True` normalizes the residual sum rounded to the activation dtype, as `forward_native` does. It is bitwise equal on the tested shapes, and goes from 24.5 to 3.2 us per call in a CUDA graph on gfx1151. This complements #45540, which replaces the same fallback for `RMSNorm` with `torch.nn.functional.rms_norm`; Qwen3.5/3.8 use `GemmaRMSNorm`, whose eager path rounds the residual sum and applies `1 + w` in fp32, so reusing the existing Triton kernel keeps it bitwise equal.
- `_GDN_FUSED_QKVZBA_RATIOS` includes head ratio 3 on HIP without aiter. The fused split kernel is from #34421; ratio 3 was enabled for CUDA in #34859 and for AMD with aiter in #44302. It is bitwise equal to the unfused split.

### Effect on other hardware

| Change | CUDA | CDNA (gfx942/gfx950) | other RDNA | CPU/NPU/XPU |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Quark int4 W4A16 scheme | unchanged (`NotImplementedError` as on `main`) | new: these checkpoints raised `NotImplementedError` on `main` and now load and run on the skinny Triton GEMM; no existing model changes kernel | same as CDNA | unchanged |
| gfx1151 kernels, row pad, GDN prefill changes | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged |
| Triton `GemmaRMSNorm` | unchanged | only without aiter and vllm | only without aiter and vllm | unchanged |
| GDN ratio-3 fused split | already on | already on with aiter; now also without | yes | unchanged |

The gfx1151 modules, including the Gluon import, load only after the gate passes. The numbers below are from gfx1151. During review we also ran the new Quark scheme (generic skinny GEMM path) and the two HIP fallback changes on gfx1100 (RDNA3) and gfx1201 (RDNA4). We did not run CDNA beyond the registered unit tests in AMD CI (MI300).

## Accuracy Tests

Setup: Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), Windows 11 with WSL2, ROCm 7.2.4, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.19-rocm724-gfx1151-20260914`.

Server (CUDA graphs on):

```bash
SGLANG_MAMBA_SSM_DTYPE=bfloat16 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-INT4-W4A16 \
    --served-model-name qwen38-awq \
    --attention-backend triton \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
    --max-running-requests 4 \
    --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
    --max-total-tokens 131072 \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
    --speculative-algorithm DFLASH \
    --speculative-draft-model-path incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 \
    --speculative-draft-attention-backend triton \
    --speculative-num-draft-tokens 8
```

GSM8K:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 \
    --num-questions 200 --num-shots 5 --parallel 4 \
    --max-new-tokens 512 --temperature 0
```

| | `main`, bf16 `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` | int4, `SGLANG_DISABLE_GFX115_KERNELS=1` | int4, this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GSM8K, 5-shot, 200 questions | 0.980 | 0.965 | 0.965 |

`main` cannot load the int4 checkpoint, so its column serves the bf16 model the checkpoint was quantized from, using the same command. The drop from 0.980 to 0.965 is the accuracy cost of the Quark int4 export. On the same int4 checkpoint, the gfx1151 kernels do not change accuracy. After the review changes, both int4 arms again gave 0.965 on `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.23-rocm724-gfx1151-20261102`.

Unit tests, 94 passed on gfx1151 (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.23-rocm724-gfx1151-20261102`):

- Registered for AMD CI (they cover code that runs on any ROCm GPU):
  - `test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_w4a16_skinny_triton.py`: the AWQ -> skinny repack against a torch reference (signed and unsigned codes), and the skinny GEMM, with and without the row pad, against a dequantized matmul at M = 1 / 8 / 33 / 300;
  - `test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_gemma_rmsnorm_round_sum.py`: the Gemma norm against eager;
  - `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_gdn_fused_split_ratio3.py`: the ratio-3 split against the unfused split.
- `test/manual/test_gfx1151_small_m_kernels.py`, which skips on anything but gfx1151:
  - the small-M GEMM over shapes and M in {1, 5, 8, 16}, padded and unpadded (bitwise equal), and its fallback to the skinny GEMM when Triton is older than 3.7;
  - the int4 quantizer round trip, the prefill GEMM and the skinny GEMM on padded rows;
  - verify attention against a torch reference with scattered KV slots, batch 1 and 2, for (q heads, KV heads, head dim, draft tokens) = (24, 4, 256, 8), (32, 4, 128, 8), (12, 2, 128, 4), (8, 8, 64, 8), and its rejection of a q sliced from a fused qkv buffer;
  - the GDN chunk forward at Qwen3.8 shapes with the head-major grids and the grouped `chunk_fwd_o` against the default kernels.

Verify attention against the generic kernel (Qwen3.8-27B attention shapes: 24 q heads, 4 KV heads, head dim 256, 8 draft tokens, scattered KV slots). Both kernels get the same cache and inputs and are compared with an fp32 reference; they are equally close to it:

| Cached prefix (tokens) | max \|gfx1151 − generic\| | max \|generic − fp32 ref\| | max \|gfx1151 − fp32 ref\| |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1,000 | 9.8e-4 | 8.1e-4 | 8.1e-4 |
| 8,000 | 4.9e-4 | 2.7e-4 | 2.4e-4 |
| 39,000 | 2.4e-4 | 1.2e-4 | 1.2e-4 |
| batch of 3: 1,000 / 8,000 / 300 | 2.0e-3 | 1.2e-3 | 1.1e-3 |

GDN prefill: head-major output and final state are bitwise identical to the default order. With the grouped `chunk_fwd_o` kernel the final state is bitwise identical and the output differs by at most 6e-5 (bf16 rounding from a different accumulation order).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

End to end, same server and GSM8K setup as above, single request:

| Metric | `main`, bf16 `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` | int4, `SGLANG_DISABLE_GFX115_KERNELS=1` | int4, this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Decode tok/s, short prompt | 5.64 | 18.32 | 29.82 |
| Decode tok/s, 8.7k-token context | 5.22 | 15.13 | 30.91 |
| Decode tok/s, 39k-token context | 3.75 | 6.82 | 21.49 |
| HumanEval+ greedy, tasks 114/0/15, thinking on (weighted tok/s) | 7.12 | 21.12 | 32.95 |
| Prefill tok/s, 1k / 4k / 16k | 175 / 138 / 127 | 240 / 119 / 112 | 410 / 367 / 337 |
| TTFT, 8.7k-token prompt | 62.3 s | 71.8 s | 24.0 s |

- `SGLANG_DISABLE_GFX115_KERNELS=1` runs this PR's Quark scheme with the generic skinny GEMM configs and the two HIP fallbacks, and none of the gfx115x kernels.

- The server processes were pinned to a few CPU cores with `taskset` after startup, which keeps the HIP runtime's busy-waiting threads from taking power from the GPU on this APU. title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] fused-a-gemm: Check the selected backend's K alignment before taking the fused path
author: lingxling
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #47710.

On SM120 the fused-A GEMM dispatcher auto-selects the CuTe DSL kernel, which requires `K % 1024 == 0`, but `fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible()` only checks the JIT kernel's `K % 256 == 0`. A DeepSeek-style MLA model with `hidden_size=3584` (or 2560) therefore passes the check and then crashes in `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` on the first <= 16-token batch:

```
AssertionError: K must be a multiple of 1024, got 3584
```

The same shape works on Hopper, where `auto` resolves to the JIT kernel.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/fused_a_gemm.py`
  - Add a per-backend K alignment table (`JIT: 256`, `CUTEDSL: 1024`) mirroring each kernel's assert.
  - Factor the `auto` resolution into `_resolve_backend()` and use it in both `dsv3_fused_a_gemm` and `fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible`.
  - `fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible` takes a keyword-only `backend` (default `auto`) and checks K against the resolved backend. The dtype, `N % 16`, CUDA and SM >= 90 checks are unchanged.
- `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py`: pass `backend=self.fused_a_gemm_backend` to both eligibility checks, so the check matches the backend the subsequent `linear_with_fused_a_gemm` call uses. `nemotron_h.py` uses the default (`auto`) for both calls already, so it needs no change.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/gemm/test_fused_a_gemm.py` (new, registered on `base-b-kernel-unit` / `1-gpu-small`, i.e. the RTX 5090 runner, skipped elsewhere): on SM120, a K=3584 weight must be ineligible and the guarded path must match `F.linear`; a K=7168 weight must stay on the fused CuTe DSL path and match `F.linear`. This is a separate file because it needs the 5090 runner; adding that registration to `test_cutedsl_dsv3_fused_a_gemm.py` would also move its full kernel matrix onto the 5090.

Behavior:

| GPU | backend | K % 256 == 0, K % 1024 != 0 (e.g. 3584) | K % 1024 == 0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| non-SM120 | auto (-> JIT) | fused (unchanged) | fused (unchanged) |
| SM120 | auto (-> CuTe DSL) | **unfused fallback** (was: AssertionError) | fused (unchanged) |
| any | explicit `cutedsl` | unfused fallback (was: AssertionError) | fused |
| any | explicit `jit` | fused (unchanged) | fused (unchanged) |

Why gate in the eligibility check rather than fall back inside `dsv3_fused_a_gemm`:

- The kernel entry points keep their shape asserts as their contract. A silent fallback in the kernel wrapper would hide a caller that passes a shape the kernel can't run.
- On SM120 there is no fused fallback to switch to: the JIT kernel sizes its pipeline for Hopper's shared memory (see #29897), so the only fallback would be a plain torch matmul inside a kernel op.
- Callers already treat `fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible` as the gate (cached once per layer) with the regular linear layer as the fallback, so fixing the predicate fixes all of them.

## Accuracy Tests

Not a numerics change: shapes that run the fused kernel are the same as before, except the SM120 shapes that used to crash, which now use the regular linear layer.

RTX 5090 (SM120), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, run before and after the fix (repro scripts are attached to the issue).

New test. It fails on unpatched code and passes with the fix:

```
# before
FAILED test_fused_a_gemm.py::test_eligibility_follows_cutedsl_k_alignment[1-3584-False]   (assert True == False)
FAILED test_fused_a_gemm.py::test_eligibility_follows_cutedsl_k_alignment[16-3584-False]  (assert True == False)
2 failed, 2 passed

# after
test_fused_a_gemm.py::test_eligibility_follows_cutedsl_k_alignment[1-3584-False] PASSED
test_fused_a_gemm.py::test_eligibility_follows_cutedsl_k_alignment[1-7168-True] PASSED
test_fused_a_gemm.py::test_eligibility_follows_cutedsl_k_alignment[16-3584-False] PASSED
test_fused_a_gemm.py::test_eligibility_follows_cutedsl_k_alignment[16-7168-True] PASSED
4 passed
```

Kernel-level repro (guarded fused-A linear vs `F.linear`, N=2112):

```
# before: K=3584 and K=2560 -> AssertionError: K must be a multiple of 1024 (6 cases), FAIL
# after
  K=3584  N=2112 M=1  -> path=unfused max|diff|=0 ok=True
  K=3584  N=2112 M=4  -> path=unfused max|diff|=0 ok=True
  K=3584  N=2112 M=16 -> path=unfused max|diff|=0 ok=True
  K=2560  N=2112 M=1  -> path=unfused max|diff|=0 ok=True
  K=2560  N=2112 M=4  -> path=unfused max|diff|=0 ok=True
  K=2560  N=2112 M=16 -> path=unfused max|diff|=0 ok=True
  K=7168  N=2112 M=1  -> path=fused   max|diff|=0.007812 ok=True
  K=7168  N=2112 M=4  -> path=fused   max|diff|=0.003906 ok=True
  K=7168  N=2112 M=16 -> path=fused   max|diff|=0.007812 ok=True
PASS
```

End to end: a config-only `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM` (DeepSeek-V3 MLA dims, hidden_size=3584, 4 layers, 16 experts), `--load-format dummy --skip-tokenizer-init`, one `/generate` request with `input_ids`:

```
# before
FAIL: bug reproduced (died during startup); server log contains 'K must be a multiple of 1024'
# after
server ready; sending /generate with input_ids
HTTP 200; output_ids (16): [...]
PASS: decoded 16 tokens with hidden_size=3584
```

Not run on Hopper. Eligibility there is unchanged (`auto` resolves to JIT, which keeps the 256 check), and the existing `test_dsv3_fused_a_gemm.py` / `test_cutedsl_dsv3_fused_a_gemm.py` run in CI on H100.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change on non-SM120 GPUs: same predicate result, same kernel. On SM120, K values that are 1024-aligned keep the fused CuTe DSL path. K values that are only 256-aligned, which used to crash, now run the regular linear layer.

Possible follow-up, not in this PR: the CuTe DSL kernel's K indexing (`TILE_K=256`, split-K inside each tile) does not obviously need `K % 1024`. With the assert bypassed on the 5090 it matched `F.linear` at K=3584 and K=2560 (N=2112, M in {1, 4, 16}; max |diff| <= 0.016, same order as K=7168). Relaxing the assert to 256 would need a wider shape sweep and a perf comparison against the unfused path, so it is left for a separate PR.

title: [Perf] diffusion: qknorm_complex_rope keeps two Q/K rows in flight per half-warp
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

`qknorm_complex_rope` (the bit-exact RMSNorm + complex RoPE of Qwen-Image-2.1 attention prep) reaches about 3.2 TB/s on B200, half of what a plain copy of the same bytes does. Each half-warp loads one row, then waits on a reduction and the rotation before its store, so few bytes are in flight.

## Modifications

The kernel now takes the Q/K rows two at a time per half-warp: both rows' loads are issued before either row is normalized and rotated. `norm_rope_row` is split into `load_row` and `norm_rope_store`; the arithmetic is the same code, so the output stays bit-identical. Prefix copies, V copies and an odd tail row keep the existing one-row loop. The launch uses half as many blocks.

Wider variants were measured and are not used: 256/512 threads per block (no gain, slower at 512), and 4 or 8 rows per half-warp through arrays (slower).

## Accuracy Tests

Outputs of the single-tensor and the pack entry points are `torch.equal` to the previous kernel at 4352 and 9216 tokens (24 heads x 128).

- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_qwen_image21_cuda.py`: 28 passed (B200).
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_complex_rope.py`: 43 passed (B200).
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_model_fast_paths.py -k "qknorm or qwen"`: 33 passed; `test_ernie_qknorm_rope_is_bit_exact` fails the same way on unmodified main and does not use this kernel.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B200, Q+K through the pack entry point, 24 heads x 128, three alternating runs each:

| tokens | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4352 | 33.0 / 33.0 / 32.9 us | 31.0 / 31.0 / 30.9 us (-6%) |
| 9216 | 71.8 / 71.8 / 71.8 us | 65.3 / 65.4 / 65.2 us (-9%) |

End to end this is small: Qwen-Image-2.1 1024px, 40 steps, one B200, two alternating runs each, 2.20 / 2.20 s before and 2.19 / 2.18 s after (about -0.4%).

title: [Fix] dspark: Stage each request's own SWA ring slot at batch size 1
author: weireweire
body:
## Root cause

When the DSpark draft keeps its SWA KV in a per-request ring (for example with `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay`), the static verify epilogue (`DsparkVerifyEpilogue.run_static`) builds the per-row state slots like this:

```python
io.req_pool_indices.view(-1, 1).expand(bs, self.stride).reshape(-1)
```

At `bs == 1` this reshape returns a stride-0 view instead of a copy. The one-launch staging kernel (`stage_commit`, used when `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_ONE_LAUNCH_COMMIT_STAGE` is on, which is the default under `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION`) reads `state_slot` as a flat contiguous tensor. So rows `1..stride-1` pick up `req_pool_indices[1..stride-1]` from the graph's static buffer (stale or padding values) instead of request 0's slot. The deferred commit then writes those tokens' draft KV into other requests' rings, and the draft loses that context.

At `bs >= 2` the reshape has to copy, so only single-request steps are affected. Configs without a draft SWA ring pass `state_slot=None` and are unaffected.

## Fix

- `run_static` makes the state slots contiguous before staging.
- `stage_commit` asserts that `state_slot` is contiguous, as it already does for `cache_loc` and `positions`.

## Validation

- Extended `test/registered/unit/spec/test_dspark_deferred_commit.py`: the static epilogue now runs with a ring and the one-launch stage at bs 1 and bs 2, and the test checks that every staged row carries its own request's slot.
- On GB300 (CUDA) the file passes 6/6. Without the fix, the bs 1 subtest fails and bs 2 passes.
- End to end on GB300: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4, one concurrent request, real DSpark acceptance, `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay` with deferred commit and the one-launch stage, GSM8K via sgl-eval 0.1.3 (300 examples, temperature 1). Both arms ran on the same node. Mean accept length went from 2.13 to 3.56 with the fix. Accuracy was 98.33% without the fix and 98.00% with it, the same within noise because the target verifies every token.

title: [Perf] imports: Keep light modules off HF patches, model configs, and the scheduler
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `sglang/__init__.py` no longer applies the transformers compatibility patches (`apply_all`, renamed `apply_all_hf_patches`). They are applied by the HF loading layer (`sglang.srt.utils.hf_transformers`) on import, and by the code that loads HF objects straight from transformers: `sglang.benchmark.utils`, `sglang.test.test_utils`, `one_batch_server`, and the comparator.
- The `LlamaFlashAttention2` re-export now lands when `transformers.models.llama.modeling_llama` is imported (a `sys.meta_path` hook), instead of importing that module and its modeling/quantizer chain up front. That import was 2.6s of the 3.3s the patches cost.
- Drop `_patch_flash_attn_availability`: transformers 5.19 already excludes the `flash-attn-4` distribution in `is_flash_attn_2_available`, so the patch is a no-op. Also drop the stale `PilImageProcessingMixin` name, the redundant mistral-patch flag, and a duplicate `ForwardMode.is_dllm_extend`.
- `sglang/srt/configs/__init__.py` is empty. Its aggregate import moved to `sglang.srt.configs.all_configs`, which the HF loading layer uses for `_CONFIG_REGISTRY` and the AutoConfig/AutoProcessor registrations. The move is byte for byte except that `Cohere2MoeConfig` joins `__all__`: it is imported only to register itself with transformers, and outside a package `__init__` the linter would drop the import as unused. Other importers take each config from its submodule.
- `ModelConfig._verify_quantization` imports the quantization registry when it runs, so importing `model_config` no longer loads every quantization method's kernels.
- Light types split out of heavy modules, moved byte for byte; every importer now imports them from the new module:
  - `ForwardMode`, `CaptureHiddenMode` -> `sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_mode` (from `forward_batch_info`)
  - `DisaggregationMode`, `FAKE_BOOTSTRAP_HOST` -> `sglang.srt.disaggregation.mode` (from `disaggregation.utils`)
  - `MultimodalDataItem`, `MultimodalProcessorOutput`, `ReturnHiddenStatesMode`, `SamplingLogprobsMode`, `get_return_hidden_states_mode`, `MM_PAD_SHIFT_VALUE` -> `sglang.srt.managers.req_types` (from `schedule_batch`)
- `schedule_batch` imports `DllmConfig` only under `TYPE_CHECKING`.
- `logging.Logger.warning_once` / `info_once`, which many modules call, came from transformers patching `logging.Logger` on import. `sglang` now installs them itself (`sglang/_logging_once.py`, same once-per-message behavior), keeping transformers' versions if it was imported first.

No behavior change, except: `import sglang` alone no longer patches transformers; `from sglang.srt.configs import XConfig` must import from the submodule (or `all_configs`); and `schedule_batch` no longer re-exports `MultimodalInputFormat`, `CudaIpcTensorTransportProxy`, or `flatten_nested_list`.


Test and CI changes, needed because importing `sglang` or `test_utils` no longer loads transformers, torch inductor, and the quantization registry up front:

- The CPU stage's fork worker preloads `transformers.models.llama.modeling_llama` and `sglang.srt.layers.quantization`, which `test_utils` no longer pulls in, so each child does not import them again. On a host with a CUDA driver, the worker skips extra preloads and checks CUDA availability through NVML: a child forked after the parent called `cuInit` or loaded flashinfer or sgl_kernel crashes on its first driver call.
- Three tests imported real modules inside a module-level `patch.dict(sys.modules)` stub (`test_w4afp8_deepep_post_reorder.py`, `test_encoder_decoder_varlen_gather.py`, `test_mem_pool_ep_unit.py`). The stub unloads every module first imported inside it while torch keeps their registrations, so a later import failed once `import sglang` stopped loading that stack up front. Each now loads its real dependency before the stub.

Import time at 51a3f5f7f4 against its merge base on main (e152f531d9), CPU only, warm `.pyc`, median of 3:

| module | main (s) | this PR (s) |
|---|---|---|
| `sglang`, `sglang.srt.environ` | 4.8 | 0.25 |

title: [Fix] kimi-k3: Honor initial expert placement in fused routing
author: Codoge
body:
## Motivation

Kimi-K3 does not expose the model metadata required by `--init-expert-location`. Its merged gate / latent-projection front also wraps logical top-k IDs without the ordinary placement remap or active-batch padding mask. A configured placement must agree with both checkpoint weight loading and runtime dispatch.

## Modifications

- Expose expert-location metadata for both the text model and multimodal wrapper, allowing the existing loader to place checkpoint experts according to an initial permutation.
- Pass the current routing inputs to the existing top-k post-processing helper after the merged front. Keep the existing capture / recorder behavior, including avoiding duplicate counts when mapping and recording are fused.
- Keep fake dispatch on the ordinary routing path because it transforms logits before top-k selection.
- Reject online EPLB and redundant experts, whose weight layout is not implemented by Kimi-K3. Reuse the existing `--init-expert-location` / `--ep-dispatch-algorithm static` options; do not introduce a placement heuristic, a benchmark-specific map, or a new flag.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested against upstream `b146a8576de930cf3adc104e601feb2790cdf3f6` with this PR applied independently:

- `test_topk_routing_inputs.py` and `test_kimi_k3_expert_placement.py`: **28 passed, 73 subtests passed**. Covers target/draft isolation, changes to the active padding mask, metadata for both model entry points, and rejection of unsupported relocation modes.
- `test_moe_front.py` and `test_expert_location_weight_loading.py`: **10 passed, 42 subtests passed**. The GPU case runs the actual merged front and model method with a non-identity permutation and padded tokens; mapped IDs, routing weights and latent output match the reference exactly. It also checks that fake dispatch declines the fused routing contract.
- `test_moe_front.py` and `test_eplb_map_record.py`: **4 passed** before adding the fake-dispatch eligibility assertion. Mapping/counting kernels filter padding correctly.

GPU tests used NVIDIA B30Z (B300), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 and Triton 3.8.0. Full-model output validation has not been rerun on this integration; the results above are operator and unit validation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This change enables a valid initial placement and preserves the fused routing path where its contract is supported. No end-to-end speed claim is made for this branch. Earlier Kimi-K3 tuning motivated the change, but those results also depended on a workload-derived expert permutation and other patches; they are not attributed to this integration.

title: [Perf] mla: Use masked K concatenation for padded head counts
author: Codoge
body:
## Motivation

Kimi-K3 has 12 local MLA heads at TP8. `_concat_and_cast_mha_k` currently requires a power-of-two head count before calling the Triton helper, even though that helper already handles padded head counts. These shapes fall back to two separate tensor copies.

## Modifications

Remove the redundant head-count restriction at the shared model dispatch point. Reuse the existing masked concat kernel and keep the feature-dimension guards and the 128-head specialized path.

For FA3 with FP8 KV storage, these head counts now follow the same output-dtype rule as the existing power-of-two Triton path. Other covered backends retain the input dtype.

## Accuracy Tests

Upstream `b146a8576de930cf3adc104e601feb2790cdf3f6` plus this PR only, NVIDIA B30Z (B300), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 and Triton 3.8.0:

```bash
python -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_concat_mla.py -k model_mha_k_concat -q
# 14 passed, 94 deselected
```

The tests call the actual model helper and Triton implementation. Coverage includes BF16 / FP16, empty and 64K-token inputs, 12 / 24 heads, an 8-head control, strided inputs, and repeated CUDA Graph replay with changed inputs. Outputs match the reference exactly. The FA3 dtype case compares raw FP8 bytes for finite random inputs against the reference cast.

Full-model accuracy and serving throughput have not been rerun on this branch; the results below are isolated operator timings.

### Upstream CUDA validation

The complete registered `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_concat_mla.py` passed on the upstream H100 CI runner for head `81955274f6363c91979dd12d05e2662621bc4346`: **108 passed, 0 skipped**, including all 14 new model-helper cases and the existing JIT/AOT regressions. title: [Refactor] kernels: Centralize GPU architecture queries in sglang.kernels.arch
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> (auto generated by Claude)

## Motivation

Kernels query GPU architecture in many ad-hoc ways: `torch.cuda.get_device_capability(...)`, `get_device_properties(...).multi_processor_count`, `gcnArchName` string checks, `sglang.srt.utils` helpers, and the JIT compile target `get_jit_cuda_arch()`, which several kernels also used for runtime decisions. These are duplicated, sometimes hard-code device 0, and make `sglang.kernels` depend on `sglang.srt`.

This PR adds one self-contained entry point, `sglang.kernels.arch.current_arch()`, and moves kernel arch queries onto it.

## Modifications

- New `sglang.kernels.arch` (torch only, no srt dependency):
  - `current_arch()` returns a process-wide cached object chosen from `PlatformInfo.detect()`: `CudaArch` on NVIDIA, `HipArch` on AMD, a plain `DeviceArch` elsewhere. All GPUs in a node are assumed to be the same model, so there is no device argument. Attributes are `cached_property`, read lazily on first use.
  - Shared: `num_sms`, `warp_size`, `l2_cache_bytes`, `smem_per_block_optin`, `smem_per_sm`, `regs_per_sm`, `max_threads_per_sm`, `name`, `props`, `supports_pdl`.
  - `is_sm(major, minor=None)` / `is_sm_at_least(major, minor=0)`: False off NVIDIA, so call sites need no platform guard.
  - `.cuda` / `.hip` narrow to the platform object (None elsewhere). `CudaArch` adds `major`, `minor`, `capability`, `sm_version`, `max_vec_bytes`, `supports_cluster`; `HipArch` adds `gcn_arch`.
- `PlatformInfo.detect()` is now cached (`_probe()` is the uncached probe) and gains `is_hip` / `is_musa`; the selector drops its own `lru_cache`.
- JIT compile target: `ArchInfo` is renamed to `CompileArch` (a frozen `msgspec.Struct`). `get_jit_cuda_arch()` becomes the internal `get_compile_arch()` used only by the build pipeline, and `make_jit_cuda_arch()` becomes `CompileArch.for_capability()`. `override_jit_cuda_arch()` is removed (its only user compiled for the local GPU anyway). `is_arch_support_pdl()` reads `current_arch().supports_pdl`, and `is_hip_runtime()` / `is_musa_runtime()` read `PlatformInfo`.
- About 80 call sites in `sglang.kernels` (plus a few kernel tests and benchmarks) now use `current_arch()` instead of direct torch/srt queries. Several one-line local helpers (`_num_sms`, `_get_num_sm`, `_mla_core_count`, ...) are removed.

Left unchanged on purpose: vendored code (`flash_attn/cute`, `fla`, code ported from vLLM/aiter/FlashInfer/CUTLASS), import-time queries, srt predicates that also gate on the CUDA toolkit version (`is_sm100_supported`, ...), AMD family predicates (`is_gfx95_supported`, ...), and sites that rely on ROCm reporting gfx-derived capabilities. These can follow once the matching interfaces exist.

Behavior notes:
- Kernel helpers that took a `device` argument for an arch query now ignore it (same-model assumption). The parameters are kept to avoid touching callers.
- CUDA-only paths that used to compare ROCm's gfx-derived capability now treat ROCm as "not NVIDIA".

## Accuracy Tests

No numerical change: the patch only changes how architecture facts are read.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] moe: Rewrite moe_finalize_fuse_shared as a JIT kernel with all top-k gathers in flight
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> (auto generated by Claude)
> (auto generated by MyGO (Make your GPU-kernel Optimal) agent)

## What

Rewrites `moe_finalize_fuse_shared` (the deferred-finalize combine of the trtllm-gen MoE path: `out[t] = sum_k w[t, k] * gemm2_out[permuted_idx[t * K + k]] (+ shared[t])`) as a header-only JIT kernel and removes the old cutlass-based `.cu`.

- Each thread owns 8 bf16 of one token and issues all K row gathers at once, so a token costs the index load plus one gather round trip; tokens map to `blockIdx.y`, so even one token spreads over `H / 1024` CTAs.
- The token's route (K row indices and weights) is spread over the warp (lane k holds slot k, read by shuffle), which keeps top-k 16 within one wave.
- Skipped rows (index -1) use a predicated load into zeroed registers with weight -0.0, so the sum stays bitwise unchanged without a branch per slot.
- bf16 weights use the mixed-precision `fma.rn.f32.bf16` (`math::fma_f32_bf16`), fp32 weights the packed `fma.rn.f32x2` (`math::fma_f32x2`, added to `math.cuh`); both give the fp32 FMA's bits.
- One token per CTA row while the grid fits one resident wave; past it, a persistent variant walks tokens and prefetches the next token's route.
- New optional arguments: `out=` writes into a caller buffer with a row stride (e.g. a symmetric-memory buffer); `routing_ready` (default on, with PDL) reads the route and the shared row before the PDL wait, which is valid because the trtllm-gen gemm2 triggers its dependents only after its own wait and the routing runs in an earlier kernel.

Results are bitwise equal to the old kernel (fp32 accumulation in k order, shared row added last).

## Performance

B300, us per call, warm (inputs in L2 as right after the gemm2), measured inside a CUDA graph behind a producer kernel that writes `gemm2_out` and triggers PDL right after its wait (like the trtllm-gen gemm2); old = current main.

| hidden / top-k (shared) | weights | T=1 | T=64 | T=192 | T=384 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7168 / 8 (yes) | fp32 | 1.30 -> 0.60 | 4.88 -> 1.34 | 5.38 -> 2.42 | |
| 7168 / 6 (yes) | fp32 | 1.39 -> 0.57 | 5.63 -> 1.14 | 5.92 -> 2.13 | 8.82 -> 3.46 |
| 7168 / 6 (yes) | bf16 | 1.55 -> 0.70 | 5.84 -> 1.22 | 6.13 -> 2.11 | 8.96 -> 3.38 |

| 3584 / 16 (no) | fp32 | 2.58 -> 0.96 | | | |
| 3584 / 16 (no) | bf16 | 2.50 -> 0.75 | | | |

3584 / 16 at T = 32 / 96 / 186 / 256: fp32 2.94 -> 1.06, 4.05 -> 1.60, 4.27 -> 2.26, 4.35 -> 2.97; bf16 2.99 -> 0.98, 3.95 -> 1.49, 4.27 -> 2.26, 4.32 -> 2.69.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] qwen3: Fuse prefill QK norm and RoPE with contiguous Q
author: mani1106
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Dense Qwen3 prefill launches QK normalization and cached RoPE separately, then FA3 or FlashInfer materializes contiguous Q. This change combines normalization, the same cached RoPE, and contiguous Q output in one CUDA launch. K is normalized and rotated in its original packed QKV storage; Q input and V remain unchanged.

It uses the existing `--enable-fused-qk-norm-rope` opt-in and remains disabled by default on CUDA. Attention kernels and KV-cache handling are unchanged.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- **Kernel:** Add lazily registered `attention.qk_norm_rope` with FP16/BF16 support, tensor/device/dtype/stride/alignment checks, and explicit K/output mutation metadata. D128 processes two rows per warp; D64/D256 use one. Share the existing standalone half-warp normalization arithmetic, round normalized values before FP32-table rotation, and preserve shuffle participation for an unmatched final row.
- **Dense dispatch:** Fuse only ordinary dense-Qwen3 `EXTEND` on Hopper, head dimension 128, TP1, unquantized weights, FA3/FlashInfer, full-head unscaled NeoX RoPE, and matching activation/weight dtypes. Keep speculative, mixed, verification, inherited/non-Qwen3, deterministic, compiled, and other unvalidated configurations on the separate path. Preserve existing BF16 table decode guards.
- **Coverage/documentation:** Extend existing kernel and model fixtures for native byte parity, Q/K/V ownership, padding, empty input, fallback dispatch, and changing-input CUDA graphs. Add a cold-L2 preparation benchmark including the baseline consumer's Q conversion, and document the opt-in in the Qwen3 cookbook.

Disabling the existing flag or reverting this contribution rolls the change back; there is no checkpoint, schema, or persisted-data migration. On upstream base-versus-PR comparisons, keep the existing flag enabled in both trees so BF16 decode treatment is identical.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

|---|---|

| `python -m pytest test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_qk_norm_rope.py -q` | 21 passed; decode preservation, exclusions, BF16/FP16 changing-input graphs |
| `python -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_qknorm.py -k two_rows -xq` | 3 existing standalone half-warp equivalence regressions passed |
| `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --error-exitcode 99 python -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_table_qk_norm_rope.py -k hybrid -xq` | 7 passed; 0 errors |

**Fresh compatible-serving validation:** one H200, TP1, SGLang v0.5.20 serving paths, Torch `2.13.0.2+cu130`, Triton `3.8.0`, FlashInfer `0.6.18`, and kernel `0.4.7.0+cu130`. The QKV producer, cached NeoX RoPE and attention consumer paths used by these cases were checked; the exact PR CUDA/shared-normalization files from `01b927b` were loaded through a compatibility adapter. The CUDA header SHA256 is `eb5c6486fdfd265bf8aa9a54ea52be72ce126516f50802b747ea951e4bf430e0`. The comparison uses optimized #45214 standalone normalization in the baseline and preserves identical original decode treatment in both arms.

Paired real-model smoke outputs are exact at **128, 4096 and 8192 input tokens** for Qwen3-4B BF16/FA3 and Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B FP16/FlashInfer. A direct compatible-runtime FP16/BF16 contract check also matches Q/K exactly, with Q input/V unchanged, K updated and contiguous Q.

| PR CUDA hybrid | 188/200 (94%) | 0 | 0 |

The same 200 questions, expected answers, generation texts and per-question grades match exactly. The existing verified canonical corpus was reused; no prompts, grading or tolerances were changed.

Checkpoints:

- `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` revision `1cfa9a7208912126459214e8b04321603b3df60c`

  --out-dir "$OUTPUT_DIR"
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

**Fresh compatible-serving comparison:** baseline A1 → candidate B → baseline A2, with fresh servers, identical checkpoint/runtime/seed/cache/chunking/graph settings, and **200 measured requests per window at concurrency 4** after warmup. This is six server phases and nine serving windows, not a repeat of the broader candidate matrix. All **1800 measured requests completed without errors**.

For each metric, the baseline below is the arithmetic mean of A1 and A2's window metric. Change is `100 * (B / mean(A1, A2) - 1)`; these are descriptive bracketed comparisons, not confidence intervals or pooled percentiles.

| Workload | p50 change | p95 change | p99 change | Completed requests/s change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-4B BF16/FA3, 4096 input / 1 output | -2.39% | -2.75% | -2.93% | +2.27% |
| Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B FP16/FlashInfer, 4096 input | -3.70% | -1.47% | -2.89% | +3.65% |
| Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B FP16/FlashInfer, 8192 input control | -1.69% | -1.59% | -1.76% | +1.86% |

Absolute per-window latency:

| Workload | A1 p50 ms | B p50 ms | A2 p50 ms | A1 p95 ms | B p95 ms | A2 p95 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-4B 4096→1 | 251.470 | 245.000 | 250.533 | 256.680 | 249.602 | 256.639 |
| Embedding 4096 | 55.062 | 52.898 | 54.794 | 56.167 | 55.252 | 55.986 |
| Embedding 8192 | 160.953 | 157.954 | 160.397 | 163.223 | 160.947 | 163.859 |

Generation latency is the **complete non-streaming HTTP request through response-body read/JSON parse with one generated token**: a one-token request-latency/TTFT proxy, not first-streamed-token TTFT. Embedding latency is complete embedding response latency. Throughput is completed requests per second over each measured window.

<details>
<summary>Serving reproduction protocol</summary>

For an independent source-pair reproduction, compare base `b50d4394945d3dcacea05ee4afd334a9b225cbdc` with PR `01b927b0ba6992c18b6dd185f0490ff528eeb0fe` on one Hopper GPU. Enable the existing flag in both source trees; use the pinned model revisions above. The recorded compatible-v0.5.20 measurements use the adapter described above, so these source-pair instructions specify the workload rather than package that adapter.

Common launch settings in every arm:

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path "$MODEL" --dtype "$DTYPE" --attention-backend "$BACKEND" \
  --enable-fused-qk-norm-rope \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31122 --tp-size 1 --random-seed 42 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \
  --max-total-tokens 196608 --max-running-requests 64 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.7 --log-level warning \
  --cuda-graph-config '{"prefill":{"backend":"breakable","bs":[1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192,16384,32768],"max_bs":32768},"decode":{"backend":"full","bs":[1,2,4,8,16,32],"max_bs":32}}'
```

For Qwen3-4B use `DTYPE=bfloat16`, `BACKEND=fa3`, and append `--return-hidden-states-mode last`. For Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B use `DTYPE=float16`, `BACKEND=flashinfer`, and append `--is-embedding`. Use local model snapshots with offline Hugging Face/Transformers access and only one visible GPU.

The HTTP client uses explicit token IDs, not tokenizer-generated random text:

```python
def ids(length, seed):
    return [1000 + (i * 13 + seed * 79) % 3000 for i in range(length)]
```

- **Generation:** `POST /generate` with `input_ids=ids(4096, seed)`, `sampling_params={"temperature": 0, "max_new_tokens": 1, "ignore_eos": True}`, `return_logprob=True`, and `return_hidden_states="last"`. Hidden-state/logprob response serialization is included in the measured latency.
- **Embedding:** `POST /v1/embeddings` with one token-ID array in `input=ids(length, seed)` and `encoding_format="float"`; measure lengths 4096 and 8192 separately.
- **Order/cache:** fresh servers in A1 -> B -> A2 order for each model/configuration. Before each window issue eight concurrent warmups with seeds `700 + i` (`i=0..7`), wait for all eight, then `POST /flush_cache?timeout=60` once. Read that response as text, not JSON. Submit 200 measured requests with seeds `1000 + i` (`i=0..199`) through a semaphore of four, with no flush between requests.
- **Timing:** after acquiring the semaphore, start the request timer immediately before the HTTP POST; validate status, read the complete response body as text and JSON-decode it before stopping. Client semaphore queue time is excluded. Compute percentiles over the 200 successful request times. A separate wall timer surrounds submission/completion of all 200 requests; throughput is `200 / wall_seconds`.

`bench_serving --disable-stream` reproduces the non-streaming timing class, but ordinary `random-ids` mode does not guarantee the same IDs, diagnostic fields or JSON-read boundary. Use the explicit HTTP protocol above when matching this workload.

</details>


**Untimed actual-server profiles** confirm `qk_norm_rope_kernel` engagement in the candidate:

| Profiled workload | Baseline GPU kernels | Candidate GPU kernels | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-4B | 2081 | 2009 | 72 |
| Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B | 364 | 308 | 56 |

The activation-dtype Q-copy kernel family disappears; other copy kernels remain. Native decode normalization remains in the generation candidate trace. Separate current-source preparation profiles show **three preparation kernels → one**, with no `aten::contiguous` in the hybrid path. D128 BF16/FP16 int32/int64 specializations compile with **56 registers and zero spills** on SM90a. Profiles are untimed engagement/copy-removal evidence and are not mixed into serving measurements.

**Current-source cold-L2 preparation microbenchmark:** `python test/registered/kernels/benchmark/attention/bench_qk_norm_rope.py` passed all six token/dtype shapes. At 4096 tokens, 32 Q heads / 8 KV heads / D128, split norm + cached RoPE + Q conversion measured **79.456 → 33.455 us (BF16)** and **79.331 → 31.787 us (FP16)**. The marker framework rotates inputs to defeat L2 reuse.

title: [Refactor] environ: Rename the SGLANG_Q35MF_* runtime switches to SGLANG_OPT_* names
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

Nine runtime switches that came in with #45474 still carry an internal code name (`SGLANG_Q35MF_*`, with `EDGE`, `MKH_N3B` and similar fragments). The names do not say what the switch controls and do not follow the `SGLANG_OPT_*` convention used by the other children of `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION`. This PR gives them descriptive names.

## Modifications

| Old name (deprecated alias) | New name | What it controls |
|---|---|---|
| `SGLANG_Q35MF_BK_VEC_COPY` | `SGLANG_OPT_SMALL_FIELD_COPY_VECTORIZED` | Vectorized small-field copy kernel |
| `SGLANG_Q35MF_MKH_N3B` | `SGLANG_OPT_SPEC_VERIFY_REUSE_STAGED_INPUTS` | Verify reuses inputs already staged on device |
| `SGLANG_Q35MF_MKH_N3C` | `SGLANG_OPT_SPEC_POST_VERIFY_ONE_LAUNCH_LOAD` | Post-verify loads its inputs in one launch |
| `SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_CHAIN_TREE` | `SGLANG_OPT_TRTLLM_MHA_CHAIN_VERIFY` | TRT-LLM MHA chain-shaped verify path |
| `SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SPARSE_VERIFY_SAMPLING` | `SGLANG_OPT_SPEC_COMPACT_VERIFY_SAMPLING` | Compact verify sampling |
| `SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_PACKED_VERIFY_BCAST` | `SGLANG_OPT_SPEC_PACKED_VERIFY_BCAST` | Packed verify broadcast |
| `SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SHM_SYNC` | `SGLANG_OPT_SCHEDULER_SHM_SYNC` | Scheduler shared-memory sync |
| `SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SHM_SYNC_MULTIHOST` | `SGLANG_OPT_SCHEDULER_SHM_SYNC_MULTIHOST` | Scheduler shared-memory sync across hosts |
| `SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_MULTIHOST_TCP` | `SGLANG_OPT_SCHEDULER_SHM_SYNC_LEADER_TCP` | Leader TCP exchange for the multi-host sync |

- `environ.py`: each switch is now declared under its new name with `EnvBoolWithAlias`, keeping the old name as `deprecated_name`. Setting the old name still works and logs a `DeprecationWarning`. Defaults are unchanged and still follow `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION`.
- Call sites read the new names. The shared-memory exchange log and error messages drop the internal `EDGE` prefix.
- `docs/src/snippets/agentx/Qwen/*.jsx` still use the old names. They are generated from the SemiAnalysis InferenceX launch commands and are marked "do not edit by hand". They keep working through the aliases and will pick up the new names on the next sync.
- No behavior change.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model outputs. Only the environment-variable names change; the old names map to the same switches.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: no change to any code path.

- `test_environ.py`: for each of the nine switches, the old name still applies and emits a `DeprecationWarning`, and the new name wins when both are set.
- The unit tests that set these switches were updated to the new names.
- Local runs, compared with the same tests on `main`: the touched unit tests show no new failures, and pre-commit passes.

title: [Feat] halops: Add HALOps as an opt-in MXFP8 GEMM backend for Blackwell and support mxfp8 megamoe
author: Wanglongzhi2001
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation
[HALOps](https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/HALOps) is the PaddlePaddle team's high-performance kernel library for NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100). This PR integrates its W8A8 MXFP8 dense GEMM and fused `group_wise_quant` activation quantizer. It also integrates the MXFP8 MegaMoE path used in the benchmark below: MXFP8 experts are served by the existing DeepGEMM MegaMoE W8A8 (`fp8xfp8`) kernel, and the MoE scale layout stays canonical so MegaMoE can derive its own layout from it.

SGLang already serves MXFP8 dense linears through DeepGEMM and FlashInfer. HALOps is added as a third backend, selected explicitly with `--fp8-gemm-backend halops`. Defaults are unchanged: `auto` never resolves to HALOps, and the package is not imported unless the flag is set.

The `halops` wheel is published on PaddlePaddle's CUDA 13.2 package page rather than PyPI and ships cp312/Linux wheels only (x86_64 and aarch64). The official Docker image installs it in a parallel build stage, skipping the package when no wheel matches the build platform; outside Docker, install it with:

```bash
pip install halops==0.1.0 \
  -f https://www.paddlepaddle.org.cn/packages/stable/cu132/halops/
```
<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Usage

Use the following example to serve DeepSeek-V4-Flash with online MXFP8 quantization and HALOps dense GEMM:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Attention HALOps MXFP8 + MoE MegaMoE MXFP8
set -e

export SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=0
export SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=0
export SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE=1
export SGLANG_OPT_USE_ONLINE_COMPRESS=1
export SGLANG_EXPERIMENTAL_ONLINE_C128_MTP=1

export SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=4096

MODEL_PATH=/path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-bf16
PORT="${PORT:-30000}"

sglang serve \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --tp 4 \
  --dp 4 \
  --ep 4 \
  --enable-dp-attention \
  --moe-a2a-backend megamoe \
  --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \
  --quantization mxfp8 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port "$PORT" \
  --nccl-port 18201 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 2 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 3 \
  --context-length 131072 \
  --allow-auto-truncate \
  --enable-cache-report \
  --enable-metrics \
  --fp8-gemm-backend halops
```

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
- `layers/quantization/halops_mxfp8.py`: lazy `halops` loader with an install hint, SfAtom scale swizzle, and the load-time weight quantizer.
- `layers/quantization/halops_mxfp8_linear.py`: W8A8 MXFP8 dense linear runner. Shapes HALOps has no tile for, K not 128-aligned, non-bf16/fp16 activations, and non-SM100 devices fall back to FlashInfer CUTLASS using the canonical scale kept on the layer.
- `layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`: `HALOPS` entries in the FP8/MXFP8 backend enums, resolution, and dispatch. Selecting `halops` for a block-FP8 checkpoint raises instead of silently running a different kernel.
- `layers/quantization/fp8.py`: `weight_scale_inv_halops` prepared at load, apply-path wiring, and canonical MXFP8 MoE quantization for MegaMoE.
- `layers/moe/mega_moe.py`: pick the `fp8xfp8` MMA type from E4M3 expert weights, turn UE8M0 scale bytes into fp32, and read K as un-packed (one element per byte) for that type.
- `arg_groups/choices.py`, a `halops` wheel download stage in `docker/Dockerfile` and `docker/Dockerfile.cu134`, and a documentation entry for the new backend.
- `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_halops_mxfp8.py` (CPU): SfAtom layout, arguments passed to HALOps, dtype handling, and the FlashInfer fallback.
## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->
DeepSeek-V4-Flash on GSM8K, full 1314 samples, 5-shot, greedy, `--max-tokens 4096`. The three arms differ only in `--fp8-gemm-backend`; MoE is MXFP8 MegaMoE in all of them.

| arm | `--fp8-gemm-backend` | gsm8k |
|---|---|---:|
| HALOps | `halops` | 0.895 |
| DeepGEMM | `deep_gemm` | 0.897 |
| FlashInfer | `flashinfer_cutlass` | 0.879 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->
On 4*SM100 GPU. DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4 / attention-DP4 / EP4, EAGLE, `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm`, `--quantization mxfp8`. Attention dense MXFP8 GEMM is the only variable: MoE is MegaMoE in all three arms and the arms differ only in `--fp8-gemm-backend`.

Dataset level (`bench_serving`, 512 random prompts, mean input 1024 / mean output 128, concurrency 128):

| backend | req/s | out tok/s | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **HALOps** | **23.94** | **1576** | **592 ms** | **74.2 ms** |
| DeepGEMM | 20.23 | 1332 | 1212 ms | 81.2 ms |
| FlashInfer | 19.51 | 1285 | 865 ms | 89.2 ms |

> NOTE: The difference is on the host side, not in the kernels. On the same prefill traces all three backends execute the same 8296 kernels:

| prefill, 16384 in | HALOps | DeepGEMM | FlashInfer |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GPU kernel total | 421.1 ms | 417.3 ms | 424.3 ms |
| of which MXFP8 dense GEMM | 58.5 ms | 56.9 ms | 61.5 ms |
| CPU-op busy | 1528.8 ms | 1812.6 ms | 2956.7 ms |
| CUDA runtime calls | 22,955 | 17,127 | 51,213 |

GPU time is flat within ±2%, so this PR does not claim a GPU-level speedup over the other two backends. HALOps has the lowest CPU-op busy time (breakable CUDA graph not enabled); FlashInfer's host path is the heaviest.

### CPU dispatch overhead

Host dispatch cost vs kernel time at N=8192 / K=4096 on a single GPU, with the benchmark script: [HALOps vs DeepGEMM host-overhead benchmark](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LsvPMVH1KmNcxfKUECui-42uOKnVay9ourd9_BZTxWw/edit).

title: [Fix] KDA: Compile the CuTe DSL decode kernel for the caller's dt_bias dtype
author: SunskyXH
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

`_get_compiled_kernel` in `cutedsl_kda.py` compiles the CuTe DSL KDA decode kernels against a bf16 `dt_bias` placeholder, and the dtype is not part of the compile-cache key. CuTe launches do not check tensor dtypes, so when a caller passes an fp32 `dt_bias`, the kernel reads the fp32 bytes as bf16. Kimi-Linear keeps `dt_bias` in fp32 (`kimi_linear.py`), and `kda_cutedsl.py` forwards it without a cast. So with `--linear-attn-decode-backend cutedsl` the forget gates are wrong, and NaN shows up in the decode output and in every state slot the batch touches.

## Modifications

- `cutedsl_kda.py`: compile with the caller's `dt_bias` dtype, and add the dtype to the compile-cache key. The kernel bodies are unchanged; they already convert `dt_bias` to fp32 on load.
- New `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_cutedsl_kda.py`, modeled on `test_cutedsl_gdn.py`. For batch sizes 16 and 128, with dense and varlen inputs, it runs bf16 and then fp32 `dt_bias` at the same shape. Over 3 decode steps it compares the outputs and the whole state pool against Triton `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update(is_kda=True)`, with one padded `-1` slot. Running both dtypes at one shape means a kernel compiled for one dtype cannot quietly serve the other.

## Accuracy Tests

The new test on one H200 (H = HV = 32, K = V = 128):

| | bf16 `dt_bias` | fp32 `dt_bias` (as in Kimi-Linear) | test |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | matches Triton | NaN, 97% of outputs mismatched | 4/4 fail |
| placeholder dtype fixed, cache key unchanged | matches Triton | NaN (reuses the bf16 kernel) | 4/4 fail |
| this PR | matches Triton | matches Triton | 4/4 pass |

`test_cutedsl_gdn.py` still passes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The kernels are unchanged. A model compiles one variant for its `dt_bias` dtype, and nothing is added per call.

title: [Fix] quantization: Store --quantization-param-path KV scales the way checkpoint KV scales are stored
author: zengleixin-amd
body:
## Motivation

`--quantization-param-path` loads per-layer KV cache scales from a JSON file through the models' `load_kv_cache_scales` (13 model files, including Llama, Qwen2 and Qwen3). They assign a Python float to `attn.k_scale` / `attn.v_scale` and leave `k_scale_float` / `v_scale_float` as None. The attention backends expect what `BaseKVCacheMethod` stores for checkpoint scales: `k_scale` as a device tensor and `k_scale_float` as its host value. So on main, a server with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --quantization-param-path <json>` fails during startup. The aiter backend fails in `reshape_and_cache_flash`:

```
ValueError: Unsupported ptr type triton.language.float32 in `tl.load`
```

and `--attention-backend triton` fails in `decode_attention_fwd`:

```
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'float' and 'NoneType'
```

#37446 converts the scales for Qwen3.5 only and keeps the tensors on CPU, where the aiter and FA3 kernels cannot read them.

## Modifications

- `load_model_utils.load_kv_cache_scales`, the only caller of the models' loaders, now runs `_kv_cache_scales_to_tensors` after them: every `RadixAttention` whose scale is a float gets a 0-dim float32 tensor on the runner's device, and the float is kept in `k_scale_float` / `v_scale_float`. The model loaders are unchanged.
- `ModelRunner` passes `device=self.device`.
- New CPU test `test/registered/unit/model_executor/model_runner_components/test_load_kv_cache_scales.py` (`base-a-test-cpu`) checks the tensor, its host copy, and that a layer without a loaded scale is left as None. On main, after `load_kv_cache_scales` the layer still holds `k_scale = 0.25` as a float and `k_scale_float = None`.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X (gfx950), image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi35x-20261025` (torch 2.11.0+rocm10, aiter `285579b6`), CUDA graphs on, KV cache `fp8_e4m3`. Llama runs use `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` with the repo's `test/manual/quant/kv_cache_scales_llama3_8b.json` (per-layer scales 0.04 to 0.18) and `python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 1319 --max-tokens 4096` (chat API, greedy). "x0.01" is the same JSON with every scale multiplied by 0.01: K/V then overflow the e4m3 range unless the loaded scale is actually applied, so it shows whether the kernels read the JSON scales.

**main `b960aa903a`, TP1.** On main both servers with the JSON fail to start with the errors above (aiter reports the `ValueError` inside a `CompilationError`).

| Attention backend | `--quantization-param-path` | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| aiter | none | 0.8166 | 0.8067 |
| aiter | `kv_cache_scales_llama3_8b.json` | fails to start | 0.8090 |
| aiter | same JSON x0.01 | — | 0.0046 |
| triton | none | — | 0.8067 |
| triton | `kv_cache_scales_llama3_8b.json` | fails to start | 0.8067 |
| triton | same JSON x0.01 | — | 0.0076 |

**More paths, this PR on main `b85d6a8893`.**

| Model, backend, TP | Calibrated JSON | All-1.0 JSON | No JSON | JSON x0.01 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B, aiter (default decode), TP1 | 0.8105 / 0.8105 / 0.8044 | 0.8097 | 0.8029 | 0.0068 |
| Llama-3.1-8B, aiter unified-attention decode (`SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1`, `--page-size 16`), TP1 | 0.8128 | — | — | 0.0068 |
| Llama-3.1-8B, triton, TP1 | 0.8037 | — | 0.7968 | 0.0053 |
| Llama-3.1-8B, aiter, TP2 | 0.7877 / 0.8044 / 0.8044 | 0.8006 | 0.7983 | 0.0068 |
| Llama-3.1-8B, triton, TP2 | 0.8067 | — | — | 0.0053 |
| Qwen3-8B (qwen3 loader), aiter, TP1 | 0.892 / 0.889 / 0.886 / 0.886 | 0.901 / 0.898 / 0.897 | 0.906 / 0.897 / 0.901 / 0.898 | 0.005 |

Qwen3-8B uses 5-shot completion GSM8K (`python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 1319`), because the chat API makes Qwen3 think at length. Its JSON sets 0.05 for every layer (not calibrated), which caps K/V at 0.05 x 448 = 22.4; that file costs about 1.3 points, while the all-1.0 JSON matches the run without one, so the loading path itself does not change accuracy.

With calibrated scales every path scores within the run-to-run spread of the fp8 cache without scales, and scaling them by 0.01 breaks every path, so the loaded scales reach the kernels on aiter (both decode paths), triton, TP1 and TP2.

At TP>1 the JSON must give scales for every TP rank. The repo's `kv_cache_scales_llama3_8b.json` only has rank 0, so at TP2 the schema validation fails and `kv_cache_scales_loader` logs an error and falls back to 1.0 while the server starts normally (behavior on main, unchanged by this PR). The TP2 rows above use the same scales copied to ranks 0 and 1.

The JSON schema defines e4m3fn scales, while gfx942 stores the fp8 KV cache as e4m3fnuz (max 240); `BaseKVCacheMethod` doubles checkpoint scales there. On MI325X (gfx942), torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0, aiter `285579b62`, main `cb55d77d37` with this patch, doubling the JSON scales makes no measurable difference, so this PR loads them as given:

| Attention backend | JSON as given | JSON scales x2 |
|---|---|---|
| aiter | 0.8113 / 0.8158 | 0.8151 / 0.8196 |
| triton | 0.8166 | 0.8158 |

For reference on the same machine: aiter fp8 KV without JSON 0.8227, bf16 KV 0.8326.

Not tested: NVIDIA backends (FA3, FlashInfer). They already read checkpoint KV scales stored as a device tensor plus host float, which is the form this PR now gives JSON scales too.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The conversion runs once at model load; nothing changes in the forward pass. Measured on MI355X, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, aiter, TP1, this PR, `python -m sglang.bench_serving --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 32`, two runs each:

| KV cache scales | Output throughput (tok/s) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| `kv_cache_scales_llama3_8b.json` | 4512 / 4971 | 6.08 / 6.08 |
| none | 4513 / 5020 | 6.09 / 6.09 |

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] fused-a-gemm: Relax the CuTe DSL kernel's K alignment from 1024 to 256
author: lingxling
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #47712. On SM120 the fused-A GEMM `auto` backend is the CuTe DSL kernel, which asserts `K % 1024 == 0`. Since #47712 the eligibility check honours that, so DeepSeek-style MLA models with `hidden_size` 3584 or 2560 no longer crash, but they run `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` through the regular linear layer, which is 1.6-2x slower at decode batch sizes of 2-16 on an RTX 5090.

The kernel's K indexing does not need 1024. `_global_k_col` splits K into `SPLITK=4` contiguous chunks of `K/4` and walks each chunk in `TILE_K=256` steps (64 bf16 per warp per tile), so `K % 256 == 0` keeps every tile in bounds and every `cp.async` 16-byte aligned. That is the same requirement as the JIT kernel, and the existing kernel test already says `hd_in must be a multiple of 256`. The 1024 assert appears to come from the shapes the kernel was written for (6144, 7168).

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/cutedsl_dsv3_fused_a_gemm.py`: assert `K % TILE_K == 0` (256) instead of `K % 1024 == 0`, and update the two docstrings.
- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/fused_a_gemm.py`: `_K_ALIGNMENT[CUTEDSL]` 1024 -> 256, so eligibility follows the kernel.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/gemm/test_cutedsl_dsv3_fused_a_gemm.py`: add K=2560 and K=3584 (256- but not 1024-aligned). This test runs on the H100 runner, so it also covers the kernel on Hopper.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/gemm/test_fused_a_gemm.py` (SM120 runner): K=3584 must now be eligible and the fused path must match `F.linear`; K=3200 (not 256-aligned) must still fall back. Drops the K=7168 case, which no longer guards anything the K=3584 case does not.
- `fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible` also requires `layer.bias is None`: the kernels compute `x @ weight.T` only, so a biased layer (e.g. a Nemotron-H `fc1_latent_proj` with `mlp_bias=True`) now keeps its own linear path instead of dropping its bias. `test_fused_a_gemm.py` covers a biased K=3584 layer.

Behavior:

| GPU | backend | K % 256 == 0, K % 1024 != 0 (e.g. 3584) | K % 1024 == 0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| non-SM120 | auto (-> JIT) | fused (unchanged) | fused (unchanged) |
| SM120 | auto (-> CuTe DSL) | **fused** (was: unfused fallback) | fused (unchanged) |
| any | explicit `cutedsl` | **fused** (was: unfused fallback) | fused (unchanged) |

Models whose `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` (deepseek_v2) or `fc1_latent_proj` (nemotron_h) has such a K are affected. The `q_b_proj` path is gated to K=2048 and is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Not a numerics change for shapes that were already fused. For newly fused shapes the kernel matches `F.linear`'s error.

RTX 5090 (SM120), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0. Kernel sweep with the assert bypassed: K = 256..4096 in steps of 256, plus 5120, 6144, 7168, 8192; N in {2112, 2624}; M = 1..16. The weight and activation sit at the start of NaN-padded buffers, so any out-of-bounds read would show up as NaN. Every shape passed, with no NaN, and the kernel's max |err| against an fp32 reference was equal to or lower than `F.linear`'s on the same inputs. Excerpt (max over M = 1..16):

```
  K=  256 N= 2112  max|kernel-ref|=0.1749  max|F.linear-ref|=0.1749  ok
  K= 2560 N= 2112  max|kernel-ref|=0.4988  max|F.linear-ref|=0.4988  ok
  K= 3328 N= 2112  max|kernel-ref|=0.4994  max|F.linear-ref|=0.5006  ok
  K= 3584 N= 2112  max|kernel-ref|=0.4991  max|F.linear-ref|=0.4991  ok
  K= 3584 N= 2624  max|kernel-ref|=0.9303  max|F.linear-ref|=0.9303  ok
  K= 7168 N= 2112  max|kernel-ref|=0.9935  max|F.linear-ref|=1.1640  ok  (already allowed)
correctness: PASS
```

Unit tests on the 5090 (`test_fused_a_gemm.py` + `test_cutedsl_dsv3_fused_a_gemm.py`, full M = 1..16 locally):

```
# before (main)
66 failed, 66 passed     # every K=2560/3584 kernel case: "K must be a multiple of 1024"; K=3584 eligibility: assert False == True
# after
132 passed
```

End to end: a config-only `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM` (DeepSeek-V3 MLA dims, hidden_size=3584, 4 layers, 16 experts), `--load-format dummy --skip-tokenizer-init`, default server args (CUDA graph on), one `/generate` request with `input_ids`. The server starts, CUDA graph capture runs the fused kernel, and the request decodes 16 tokens:

```
server ready; sending /generate with input_ids
HTTP 200; output_ids (16): [...]
PASS: decoded 16 tokens with hidden_size=3584
```

Not run on Hopper. There `auto` resolves to the JIT kernel, whose eligibility is unchanged. The CuTe DSL kernel with the new K values is covered on H100 by `test_cutedsl_dsv3_fused_a_gemm.py`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

RTX 5090, fused CuTe DSL kernel vs `F.linear` (which SM120 runs today for these K). Each provider is timed inside a CUDA graph, rotating over enough weight copies (>= 512 MB) that the weight is read from HBM, as in a decode step. Times are in us per call.

| K | N | M=1 | M=2 | M=8 | M=16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2560 | 2112 | 7.66 vs 9.39 (1.23x) | 7.72 vs 14.99 (1.94x) | 7.84 vs 15.10 (1.93x) | 8.03 vs 15.29 (1.90x) |
| 3584 | 2112 | 10.29 vs 12.41 (1.21x) | 10.36 vs 20.44 (1.97x) | 10.45 vs 20.51 (1.96x) | 10.72 vs 20.78 (1.94x) |
| 2560 | 2624 | 9.21 vs 10.79 (1.17x) | 9.32 vs 15.22 (1.63x) | 9.44 vs 15.33 (1.62x) | 9.67 vs 15.68 (1.62x) |
| 3584 | 2624 | 12.49 vs 14.32 (1.15x) | 12.50 vs 20.74 (1.66x) | 12.64 vs 20.82 (1.65x) | 12.90 vs 21.09 (1.63x) |
| 7168 (already fused) | 2112 | 19.31 vs 21.35 (1.11x) | 19.32 vs 39.19 (2.03x) | 19.50 vs 39.34 (2.02x) | 19.84 vs 39.56 (1.99x) |

The speedups for the newly allowed K match those for K=7168 and 6144, which already take this path. At K=3584, N=2112 the fused kernel reads the 15 MB weight at about 1.5 TB/s, close to the 5090's HBM bandwidth.

No change on non-SM120 GPUs with the default backend.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Avoid upscaling native H3 references by default
author: yz-wqf
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

<!-- Suggested PR title: [Perf] diffusion: Avoid upscaling native MiniMax-H3 references by default -->

## Motivation

A motivating MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA workload was substantially slower in SGLang than vLLM-Omni. Investigation found that SGLang defaults to `reference_resize_mode="diffusers"`, which upscales small reference images to a 2048-pixel short edge and increases reference-token work throughout denoising.

Switching to the existing `max` policy reduced median latency by **37.7%** and achieved **5.3% lower latency than vLLM-Omni** in that comparison. Informal visual review found no clear quality regression; the broader proxy-score results are below.

## Modifications

- Default native H3 Ref2VA image references to `max`: only downscale when the short edge exceeds 2048 pixels, with dimensions rounded to multiples of 32.
- Share the default across sampling parameters, prequeue planning, and reference encoding.
- Preserve explicit `diffusers`/`match` overrides and FastH3 Omni's existing `diffusers` default.
- Update documentation and resize/admission regression tests.

Reference conditioning can change generated content. Requested output resolution, frame count, denoising steps, and precision are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Evaluated **26 public VBench small-reference cases**, producing **148 videos** across both policies: 24 cases at seeds 42/43/44, plus reused seed-42 outputs for cases 16 and 64. Settings: native H3 Ref2VA, BF16, 50 steps, 1344×768, 124 frames at 24 fps, concurrency 1, conditioning cache disabled.

| Metric | SGLang `max` | SGLang `diffusers` | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Imaging quality (MUSIQ) ↑ | 71.74 | 72.05 | −0.43% |
| Subject consistency ↑ | 92.16 | 92.41 | −0.28% |
| Background consistency ↑ | 94.82 | 94.97 | −0.16% |
| Aesthetic quality ↑ | 61.88 | 62.06 | −0.29% |
| Motion smoothness ↑ | 99.07 | 99.08 | −0.01% |
| Dynamic degree | 79.49 | 85.90 | −7.46% |
| Reference-subject similarity ↑ — 15 cases | 91.02 | 91.16 | −0.15% |
| Reference-background similarity ↑ — 11 cases | 89.61 | 89.57 | +0.04% |

Scores average seeds within each case, then weight applicable cases equally; quality values use a 0–100 scale and relative changes use unrounded values. Dynamic degree's apparent quality regression reflects a binary motion-threshold pass rate, which does not establish worse perceptual quality.

These are H3-adapted VBench diagnostics, not official leaderboard scores or a formal quality-equivalence study. The expanded quality evaluation predates the latest rebase.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Public VBench performance:** the 26-case affected-input subset averaged **192.91 s with `max` versus 223.44 s with `diffusers`**, a **13.67% reduction**. Timings use the same seed-then-case weighting as above; the two reused cases retain their earlier-device timings.

An earlier five-input public VBench run used the unmodified official vLLM-Omni serving benchmark client, one B200, the same output shape, 50 steps, and one timed request per input:

| Configuration | Mean latency | Median latency |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| SGLang `max` | **187.18 s** | **200.41 s** |
| SGLang `diffusers` | 210.83 s | 212.37 s |
| vLLM-Omni | 279.32 s | 308.58 s |

The five-input aggregate includes different reference sizes because SGLang caps large references while vLLM-Omni retains native geometry. On the two cases with matching resolved reference sizes, SGLang averaged **161.29 s versus 169.28 s**, or **4.73% lower latency**; encoder defaults and runtime versions still differ.
