title: [Fix] [AMD] qwen3: Guard dtype alignment when fused decode omits KV
author: XinyuJiangCMU
body:
## Problem

Since the October 31 rebase of `sglang-miles`, dense Qwen3 decode on ROCm crashes while the server captures its decode CUDA graphs:

```text
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3.py", line 364, in forward
    if should_force_bfloat16_dense_tensor_math() or q.dtype != v.dtype:
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'dtype'
```

The AITER fused decode path from #44267 writes K/V straight into the KV cache and returns `v=None`. The true-on-policy commit on this branch ([1/76], 41d9f48) also compares `q.dtype != v.dtype` when true on-policy is off, so ordinary decode now reads `v.dtype`. `main` casts only under true on-policy and is not affected.

The server exits during startup, so each affected test waits about 30 minutes for its timeout instead of failing fast. In the [November 1 ROCm 10 nightly](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41355785159), ten tests that passed in the [October 31 nightly](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41246952254) crashed this way. The timeouts also pushed four of the five jobs past their 180-minute limit, so 45 more tests that passed on October 31 never started (three of those jobs also had unrelated DeepSeek-V4 failures).

| Test | Job | November 1 | Crash log |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/e2e/ckpt/test_qwen3_0.6B_ckpt.py` | 2-GPU | timeout (1875 s) | [log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41355785159/job/124995387638#step:8:3377) |
| `tests/e2e/fsdp/test_qwen3_0.6B_megatron_fsdp_align.py` | 2-GPU | timeout (1800 s) | [log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41355785159/job/124995387638#step:8:48533) |
| `tests/e2e/megatron/model_scripts/test_qwen3_0_6b_lora_native_ci.py` | 2-GPU | timeout (1800 s) | [log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41355785159/job/124995387638#step:8:311484) |
| `tests/e2e/sglang/test_chat_input_ids_equivalence.py` | 2-GPU | failed (35 s) | [log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41355785159/job/124995387638#step:8:547860) |
| `tests/e2e/megatron/test_qwen3_4B_ppo.py` | 4-GPU part 1 | timeout (1800 s) | [log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41355785159/job/124995387840#step:8:28360) |
| `tests/e2e/megatron/test_qwen3_4B_muon_offload_disk.py` | 4-GPU part 1 | crashed, then cut by the job limit | [log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41355785159/job/124995387840#step:8:257807) |
| `tests/e2e/short/test_multi_policy_solver_verifier_gsm8k.py` | 4-GPU part 2 | timeout (2125 s) | [log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41355785159/job/124995387743#step:8:74495) |
| `tests/e2e/megatron/test_qwen3_4b_fully_async_eval.py` | 8-GPU part 2 | timeout (1875 s) | [log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41355785159/job/124995387745#step:8:614663) |
| `tests/e2e/ckpt/test_fully_async_ckpt.py` | 8-GPU part 2 | timeout (1800 s) | [log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41355785159/job/124995387745#step:8:623319) |
| `tests/e2e/ckpt/test_fully_async_ckpt_missing_step.py` | 8-GPU part 2 | timeout (1800 s) | [log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41355785159/job/124995387745#step:8:657275) |

## Change

Only align Q/K to V when V exists. The fused path has already written K/V to the cache and passes `save_kv_cache=False`, so there is nothing to align, the same as on `main`. Non-fused decode keeps the existing condition, and so does true on-policy, whose contract disables the fused path.

## Validation

On MI350X with the November 1 ROCm 10 nightly image and only this file changed:

- `test_chat_input_ids_equivalence.py` passed (42 s); it failed in 35 s in the nightly.
- `test_qwen3_0_6b_lora_native_ci.py` passed (284 s): TP2 with sequence parallelism, two rollout/train/adapter-sync rounds with the existing checkers, and all 52 decode graphs captured.
- `test_qwen3_aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope.py` passed (3 tests, 16 subtests) once the runtime context is initialized. Run bare, it fails before reaching this code, identically with and without this change.

A CPU run of the original `forward` over 16 mode, TP and RoPE combinations reproduced the four fused-decode crashes. With the fix all 16 pass, and the other 12 keep the same calls and outputs.

title: [Feat] [NVIDIA] megakernel: Support prefill and extend steps
author: wenscarl
body:
## Motivation

Extends the NVIDIA megakernel plugin contract to cover prefill and extend steps, in addition to decode. Today the plugin interface handles `target_verify` and `draft_extend` (inside CUDA graphs) but not regular target prefill/extend. This PR adds the framework-side contract so a plugin spec in `sgl-nvidia-mega` can implement a prefill megakernel through the same interface.

Discussed with the SGL team — see linked thread. Yangmin Li confirmed the current interface does not cover regular prefill/extend and a new mode is needed. This PR provides that mode; the in-tree consumer is a separate PR in `sgl-nvidia-mega`.

## Modifications

- **`Requirements.prefill_graph_backends`** (empty by default): a decode-only spec is unaffected on every path. When non-empty, SGLang checks the prefill graph backend at startup and installs a prefill capture-check hook.
- **`BuildContext.prefill_widths`**: the captured prefill graph token buckets, passed to the spec's `build`. Empty for decode-only specs or when prefill graphs are off.
- **`Step.mode`** may now be `"extend"` (a prefill/extend step), in addition to `"decode"` and `"target_verify"`.
- **`_Dispatch.captured_tokens`**: tracks which prefill token buckets ran the megakernel during capture (decode still uses `captured` keyed by batch size).
- **`_CaptureCheck`** now accepts a `phase` argument (`"decode"` or `"prefill"`). A prefill instance is installed only for a spec that declares `prefill_graph_backends`, so decode-only specs are refused on their decode graphs alone and never asked to run a prefill graph they never claimed.
- **`ModelRunner.prefill_capture_tail_hooks`**: separate list for the prefill graph runner, so decode capture hooks are never handed a prefill capture.
- **`PrefillCudaGraphRunner`**: calls `prefill_capture_tail_hooks` after each graph capture, with the same contract as the decode runner's `capture_tail_hooks`.

## Tests

- `test_megakernel_guards.py`: new test verifying that only a spec declaring `prefill_graph_backends` is checked on the prefill graph backend, and that a decode-only spec is unaffected.
- `test_megakernel_runtime.py`: new test verifying that a prefill-covering spec receives `prefill_widths`, gets a prefill `_CaptureCheck`, the check is keyed by token bucket (not batch size), and the check refuses when no prefill graph runs the megakernel.
- Both tests run on CPU.

title: [Perf] dsv41: Keep MXFP4 Engram tables packed and decode E2M1 in the gather
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

[nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-NVFP4) stores the two Engram tables as packed MXFP4 (`uint8 [rows, 128]`, two E2M1 values per byte, even column in the low nibble, unchanged per-32 ue8m0 scales). `EngramEmbedding` allocates an e4m3 `[rows, 256]` table, so loading fails on the shape mismatch. Widening the rows to e4m3 at load would keep the FP8 checkpoint's size: about 25 GB per table per TP4 rank, about 190 GiB of host RAM per node with `placement: cpu`. Keeping the tables packed and decoding in the gather (as vllm-project/vllm#61530 does) halves that.

## Modifications

- When `quantization_config.engram_embed_quant` is `"mxfp4"`, `EngramEmbedding` allocates the table as `uint8 [rows, dim // 2]` in every layout (device table, per-rank and shared host table, peer shards), and `_load_rows` copies the packed rows as stored. Absent means `"fp8"`; any other value raises.
- `_engram_gather_kernel` and `_engram_gather_peer_kernel` take a `PACKED_FP4` constexpr that loads the byte, picks the nibble and builds the fp32 value from its bits before the unchanged e8m0 multiply. Every E2M1 value is exact in e4m3, so the output is bit-identical to the gather of the widened table, -0 included. The sign bit is set directly in the fp32 bits rather than through unary minus, which Triton before 3.8 lowers to `0 - x` (turning -0 into +0).
- The forward, staged-dequant, peer and torch-fallback lookups pass the mode. The scheduler stager moves bytes per row and needs no change.
- FP8 checkpoints allocate and gather exactly as before. A packed table in a checkpoint that does not declare `engram_embed_quant` fails at load with a message naming the key, instead of loading at twice the memory.
- New `test/registered/kernels/ops/embeddings/test_engram_gather.py`: all 256 byte values with random scales through `engram_gather` and `engram_gather_peer`, packed and widened, compared with an E2M1 spec decode as int16 bits, so signed zero is checked too.

## Accuracy Tests

GB300, TP4, one node, SGLang nightly 2026-10-30 plus this change, DSpark (block size 5), `--engram-config '{"placement": "cpu", "replication": "none", "lookup": "auto"}'`. GSM8K via sgl-eval 0.1.3: 1319 questions, concurrency 64, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, thinking on.

| Engram table | GSM8K | accept length |
|---|---:|---:|
| packed (this PR) | 96.82% | 3.38 |
| widened to e4m3 | 96.82% | 3.41 |

Gather checks on GB300: every packed lookup equals the same lookup on the widened table bit for bit. One GPU: all 256 byte values, random rows and scales, device, pinned-host, sharded and sorted gathers, `EngramEmbedding` with a per-rank host table, staged dequant and the torch fallback. Four GPUs: the peer kernel through real `_PeerShards` export/import. `test_engram_gather.py` passes on GB300 (Triton 3.8.0).

The GSM8K and timing runs predate setting the sign bit directly. On Triton 3.8, which lowers unary minus to `fneg`, both versions produce the same bits.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Memory, per TP4 rank per table:

| | widened | packed |
|---|---:|---:|
| host table | 24,170 MiB | 12,451 MiB |
| host RAM per node (two tables, four ranks) | ~189 GiB | ~97 GiB |

GPU memory after load is unchanged (77.3 GB), since this deployment keeps the tables on the host.

Gather kernel time, one GB300 GPU, 24M-row table (one TP4 rank shard), random ids, in us:

| table | ids | fp8 | packed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| device | 256 | 9.4 | 6.7 |
| device | 2,048 | 6.9 | 6.8 |
| device | 16,384 | 14.6 | 14.7 |
| device | 131,072 | 75.6 | 75.6 |
| pinned host, sorted ids | 256 | 69.6 | 73.9 |
| pinned host, sorted ids | 2,048 | 73.6 | 82.8 |
| pinned host, sorted ids | 16,384 | 141.6 | 131.6 |
| pinned host, sorted ids | 131,072 | 326.5 | 252.5 |

The device gather is unchanged. The host gather is a few us slower at small batches and up to 23% faster at large ones, where it reads half the bytes over C2C.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Fix] attention: Migrate FLA Triton kernels off tl.make_block_ptr
author: njriasan
body:
Upstream Triton removed `tl.make_block_ptr`/`tl.advance` (triton-lang/triton#10833), breaking the FLA/KDA kernels on Triton builds without block pointers.

Following vllm-project/vllm#60502 (and upstream flash-linear-attention#1062), this replaces every block-pointer use with explicit pointer arithmetic plus masked `tl.load`/`tl.store`:

- 19 kernels / 226 call sites across the CUDA FLA kernels (`cumsum`, `chunk_o`, `l2norm` incl. GDN strided prepare, `wy_fast`, `fused_norm_gate`, `chunk_intra_token_parallel`, `chunk_delta_h`, `chunk_fwd`, `kda`, `chunk_intra`) and the XPU copies.
- Masks reproduce `boundary_check` semantics; offsets are widened to int64 like block-pointer offsets were.
- Deletes the `triton_block_ptr_compat` shim and its imports — no shim is needed once no kernel uses block pointers.

Block pointers lowered to plain vectorized loads (not TMA), so this is behavior-equivalent by construction.

Test: per-kernel A/B against pre-port baselines on H100 (Torch 2.11 + Triton 3.9) — bit-exact for all kernels, both normally and with `tl.make_block_ptr` deleted, incl. partial-chunk, strided, gated, fused/non-fused/safe-gate paths, plus an end-to-end `chunk_kda` smoke test. One exception: `kda` Aqk differs by at most 1 fp16 ulp because the autotuner picks a different `num_warps` for the ported sub-intra kernel (reduction reassociation). XPU kernels are compile-checked only (no XPU in the test env). `ruff check --select=F401,F821,F823,UP037` and `ruff format` pass.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dsv41: Split small-batch decode mHC post-combine-norm rows over a CTA cluster
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #46088. The fused decode mHC post + combine + RMSNorm kernel runs one CTA per row, so each row's ~50 KB of stores (4×5120 bf16 residual + normed output) drains through a single SM at ~32 B/cycle — ≥0.8 µs on its own — and the norm weight is only loaded after the RMS barrier. At decode batch sizes that are a fraction of the SM count this leaves most of the GPU idle.

## Modifications

- **Cluster split.** The kernel is now templated on `Split`. With `Split > 1` the grid is `(Split, rows)` with cluster dims `(Split, 1, 1)`, and each CTA handles `640/Split` vectors of the row. Each warp `st.async`s its partial sum of squares into every peer's 20-float shared pool, tracked by the peer's mbarrier (`expect_tx`), same idiom as `softmax.cuh`. Every warp reduces the pool in the same order, so `inv_rms` is bit-identical across the cluster.
- **Unsplit rows** keep the 1-D `(rows)` grid and use one `__syncthreads` instead of two.
- **Weight prefetch** before the RMS barrier, only where `Split > 1 || kVPT == 1` — doing it everywhere raised 160-thread registers 48 → 64 (8 → 6 CTAs/SM) and slowed large m by 16–82%.
- **Config pick** (`_pick_config`):
  - m ≤ 128: 4 × 160 threads, or 5 × 128 with MXFP8 output
  - #SMs < m ≤ 640: 2 × 160 threads
  - otherwise: the existing fewest-waves pick, unsplit

  Splits stop there because cluster launch cost grows with the grid (an empty 4-CTA-cluster grid at m=1024 costs 3.1 µs vs 1.0 µs unclustered), and past 640 rows the 2-CTA split no longer wins reliably.
- SM count comes from the existing `get_device_core_count`, cached.
- `CHECK_HOST(rows <= 65535)` for split configs, since rows go in `grid.y` there.
- Test: added the new config boundaries (128/129, #SMs/#SMs+1, 640/641) to the transition rows.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_mhc_post_combine_norm_decode.py`: 4/4 pass on B300.
- Standalone check over m ∈ {1..1024 sweep, 3, 127, 129, 1023}, every config: updated residual bitwise-equal to `mhc_post_split_h`; normed row within 1e-2 of `hc_combine_norm`; MXFP8 values and scales bitwise-equal to flashinfer's quantize of the normed row; repeated runs bit-identical.
- SASS: no generic `LD.E`, no stack, all global access `LDG`/`STG`.
- No end-to-end model accuracy run yet (see below).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

1× B300 (sm_103a, 148 SMs). CUDA graph, one launch per buffer set; cold rotates sets past 3× L2, warm replays one set. Old and new kernels interleaved in the same process, median of 11 rounds. µs per launch, before → after:

| m | cold | warm | MXFP8 cold | MXFP8 warm |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4.23 → 3.08 | 3.73 → 2.26 | 5.44 → 3.89 | 4.94 → 2.77 |
| 16 | 4.10 → 3.19 | 3.73 → 2.32 | 4.50 → 3.40 | 4.18 → 2.39 |
| 64 | 4.44 → 3.85 | 3.86 → 2.94 | 4.83 → 4.10 | 4.24 → 3.09 |
| 128 | 5.00 → 4.89 | 3.90 → 3.47 | 5.40 → 5.20 | 4.24 → 3.79 |
| 160 | 6.41 → 5.88 | 4.87 → 4.15 | 7.06 → 6.72 | 5.62 → 4.82 |
| 256 | 7.36 → 7.10 | 5.03 → 4.88 | 8.04 → 8.09 | 5.76 → 5.64 |
| 384 | 9.08 → 8.95 | 6.61 → 6.59 | 10.25 → 10.03 | 7.46 → 7.69 |
| 512 | 10.81 → 10.67 | 7.83 → 7.31 | 12.29 → 11.64 | 9.07 → 8.53 |
| 640 | 13.46 → 13.36 | 9.30 → 8.78 | 15.27 → 14.63 | 10.94 → 10.46 |
| 768 | 15.23 → 15.23 | 10.80 → 10.75 | 17.58 → 17.59 | 13.12 → 13.14 |
| 1024 | 19.14 → 19.23 | 14.48 → 14.49 | 21.55 → 21.39 | 19.78 → 19.74 |

Worst point: MXFP8 warm m=384, +3%. Above 640 rows within ±0.5%.

**Still draft because:**
- Not yet timed on B200 (sm_100a); thresholds are B300-tuned.
- No end-to-end DSv4.1 decode A/B yet. A cluster needs its 2–5 CTAs co-scheduled in one GPC, which concurrent side-stream kernels could delay — the e2e run needs to confirm this holds in situ.

title: [Perf] srt: Record per request whether an extend row completes its prompt
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

#45487 gave `ForwardBatch` a host-side `contains_last_prefill_chunk`: one `bool` saying whether *any* request in a non-speculative extend batch finishes its prompt on this forward. That is enough to gate batch-wide work, but model code that acts per request on the forward that finishes that request's prompt (a head that reads the prompt's last token for some rows and not others, an output row published once per request) still has no host-side way to tell *which* rows those are. The device-side alternative is the same one the batch-level flag removed: compare `extend_prefix_lens + extend_seq_lens` with `orig_seq_lens` and sync, once per extend forward.

## Modifications

- `ForwardBatch.extend_is_final_cpu: Optional[List[bool]]`, snapshotted by `init_new` for non-speculative extend batches, one entry per `batch.reqs` row in order. A row is final when its extend ends at `len(full_untruncated_fill_ids)` (so resumed and retracted prompts are handled the same way as fresh ones), or when it is a running decode request mixed into the extend batch, since that row also produces a token on this forward. Decode batches and synthetic capture or replay batches leave it `None`.
- `contains_last_prefill_chunk` is now derived from the same list, ignoring the mixed-in decode rows as before, so the two fields cannot disagree.
- `TboForwardBatchPreparer.filter_batch` slices the new list per child batch, alongside the other per-request CPU lists (`extend_seq_lens_cpu`, `extend_logprob_start_lens_cpu`, ...), instead of inheriting the parent's whole list.

No reader inside this repository consumes the list yet; the batch-level flag keeps its meaning and its readers.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no numerics change. The field is a new host-side list derived from request bookkeeping that `init_new` already reads.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not run: the change replaces one Python generator over `batch.reqs` per extend forward with a list of the same length plus one `zip` over it; no device work is added.

## Checklist

- `test/registered/unit/managers/test_schedule_batch_out_of_place.py::TestForwardBatchPrefillCompletion` now also checks `extend_is_final_cpu` across `NONE`/`EAGLE`/`EAGLE3`, mixed and zero-token requests: the mixed-in decode row is final, the incoming request follows its chunk, a later change to `req.extend_end` does not move the snapshot, and `dataclasses.replace` preserves it.
- `test/registered/unit/batch_overlap/test_tbo_filter_batch_marker.py::test_filter_batch_slices_extend_completion_per_request` checks that `filter_batch` hands each child its own slice and leaves the parent untouched.
- Both test files on CPU: red on current `main` (`AttributeError: 'ForwardBatch' object has no attribute 'extend_is_final_cpu'`, 31 failed), green on this branch (17 passed, 40 subtests passed).
- `pre-commit run --files` on the four changed files passes.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dsv4/topk_v2: Exactness modes (fast / exact / deterministic) and an exact cluster path
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> (auto generated by Claude)
> (auto generated by MyGO (Make your GPU-kernel Optimal) agent)

## What

The DeepSeek-V4 top-k v2 kernel gets a process-wide exactness mode, `SGLANG_TOPK_V2_MODE`, compiled in as `-DSGL_TOPK_MODE`:

| mode | contract | default |
|---|---|---|
| 0 fast | legal output; an overflowing threshold bin keeps an arbitrary subset | opt-in |
| 1 exact | selected values equal `torch.topk`'s; tie choice unspecified | CUDA, ROCm |
| 2 deterministic | exact, and the same selected set on every run (ties by smallest index, -0 == +0) | |

On main, only the cluster path is inexact: it truncates an overflowing threshold bin to 2048 entries in arrival order. This happens on real GLM-5 indexer scores, where layer 1 overflows on most rows. NaN input stays implementation-defined in every mode, with legal output only.

Changes, mostly in `topk_impl.cuh`:
- Cluster path (C16 / C8 small batch, C8 persistent pool):
  - 11-bit coarse bins;
  - the histogram is exchanged by `st.async` all-gather, so every rank finds the threshold and its own output bases (no rank-0 merge, fewer cluster barriers);
  - above-threshold elements are emitted directly;
  - a one-warp rank of the k-th digit replaces most of rank 0's tie stage;
  - rows whose threshold bin overflows are resolved inside the cluster (fine histogram + second pass), off the normal-row codegen path;
  - +-0 / inf / NaN bins are made consistent with the bin bounds instead of taking a slow path.
- One-block paths (Register, Streaming): `refine_ties` uses digits relative to the bin's lower edge (2 rounds instead of 3); Streaming folds overflow detection into the collect pass; score loads compile to `LDG`.
- Mode 0 compiles out every exactness fallback, including the ROCm split path; mode 2 adds index-ordered tie resolution only where an equal group straddles the k-th place.
- Blackwell plan table for the persistent pool re-tuned (the old one sent large batches of long rows to the pool where one-block Streaming is faster).
- `SGL_TYPE_CHECKING` (set only by the clangd config from `python -m sglang.kernels.jit`) defaults JIT-passed macros for IDE indexing.

## Performance

Mode 1 is the default on every platform. B300, nvcc 13.4, median % vs main (negative = faster), 108 shapes: real indexer score rows of GLM-5.2 (k 2048), DeepSeek-V4-Pro (k 1024) and V4.1-Flash (k 512), 8K-1M, bs 1-256, plus mixed batches. CUDA graph behind a producer that triggers PDL after its stores.

| path | mode 1 (default) | mode 0 | mode 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Register (<= 16K) | -2.7 | -1.7 | +1.4 |
| Streaming | +0.8 | +1.4 | +3.7 |
| cluster, small batch (C16) | -13.8 | -14.4 | -12.6 |
| cluster, small batch (C8) | -6.1 | -4.2 | -4.8 |
| cluster, persistent pool | -4.3 | -4.2 | -0.5 |
| mixed batches | -4.1 | -3.7 | -0.9 |
| all | -3.5 | -3.0 | -0.8 |

By context, mode 1: 8K -2.4, 16K -2.9, 32K -8.3, 64K -4.3, 128K -7.8, 256K -5.5, ~1M -8.8.

| shape | main | mode 1 (default) | mode 0 | mode 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.2 64 x 128K (main's bin overflows) | 50.1 | 33.0 | 27.1 | 34.7 |
| GLM-5.2 64 x 256K | 40.2 | 38.0 | 37.2 | 38.5 |
| GLM-5.2 1 x 960K | 15.6 | 13.5 | 13.5 | 13.9 |
| V4.1-Flash 64 x 256K | 34.1 | 32.7 | 32.8 | 33.9 |
| V4-Pro 64 x 128K | 24.1 | 24.3 | 24.3 | 25.2 |

(us per call)

Known regressions:
- Streaming at bs >= 64, 32K-128K: mode 0 up to +2.3 % (0.1-0.4 us); mode 2 up to +6.7 %.
- Batches where every row overflows (GLM-5 layer 1) on the cluster paths: mode 1 up to +9.6 %, mode 2 up to +18 % vs main, which returns a wrong top-k on those rows.
- H200: works and is exact; mode 1 is +2.4 % overall vs main, more on batches with overflowing rows.

## Correctness

288 adversarial cases per arch: bin overflow, narrow bins, ties straddling the k-th place, all-equal, two values, signed zero, inf, NaN, at k 512 / 1024 / 2048 on every paged path.

| | main | mode 0 | mode 1 | mode 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| inexact cases (B300 / H200) | 75 / 60 | 113 / 113 (allowed) | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| run-to-run different sets | 199 / 198 | allowed | allowed | 0 / 0 |

On the real score rows, main is inexact on 13 GLM shapes (all cluster paths); modes 1 and 2 on none. No illegal output in any mode.

## Tests

`test_topk_v2.py`: in-process tests run in the default mode 1; `test_topk_v2_modes` checks mode 0 (legal output) and mode 2 (exact, deterministic) in a subprocess each (one mode per process), started at module setup so their JIT builds overlap the in-process tests (cold run on B300: 89 s). 314 passed / 26 skipped on B300 in modes 0, 1, 2 and on H200.

title: [Feat] [AMD] custom-all-reduce: Run the JIT custom all-reduce v2 on ROCm
author: wenkaidu
body:
[Feat] [AMD] custom-all-reduce: Run the JIT custom all-reduce v2 on ROCm

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

`CustomAllReduceV2` (the JIT custom all-reduce, "carv2") only runs on NVIDIA today. On AMD the custom all-reduce is AITER's (or the legacy AOT one), so ROCm gets neither carv2's Lamport push algorithms nor the push/pull communicator planes the fused collectives are built on.

The push algorithms matter most for decode-sized all-reduces: on 8x MI350X, carv2 `1shot_push` is 20-37% faster than AITER at 4-64 KB, and carv2 matches or beats AITER up to 4 MB (table below).

This PR makes carv2 build and run correctly on ROCm (gfx950) and tunes its launch geometry for MI350X. It does **not** change ROCm dispatch: `dispatch_custom_allreduce` still selects AITER on AMD, so serving behavior is unchanged until a follow-up enables v2 there with tuned thresholds. CUDA behavior is unchanged.

## Modifications

Two commits: the ROCm port, then the MI350X block/thread tuning.

**Symmetric workspace over HIP VMM + POSIX fds** (`srt/utils/hip_vmm_utils.py`, new)
- `HipSymmetricBuffer`: one `hipMemCreate` allocation per rank (`hipMemAllocationTypeUncached`, POSIX-fd handle type), exported as an fd, exchanged with the existing `exchange_posix_fds` (`SCM_RIGHTS`), imported and mapped into every peer, and exposed as per-rank uint8 tensors on the local device. It replaces torch symmetric memory on ROCm and needs no FABRIC handle and no multicast.
- Chunked fallback: some amdgpu/KFD drivers reject a VA-less VRAM allocation whose `[0, size)` overlaps an SVM range, which RCCL init can leave in Python's low brk heap (dmesg: `Address: 0x0 already allocated by SVM`); every later large allocation then fails as out of memory with the GPU nearly empty. On that failure the buffer is built from smaller handles mapped back to back, and the handled error is cleared from `hipGetLastError` so torch does not report it later.
- All ranks agree on allocation success before the fd exchange, so a failure raises everywhere instead of hanging peers.

**JIT kernels under hipcc** (`ptx.cuh`, `custom_all_reduce.cuh`, `utils.cuh`)
- HIP implementations of the `ptx::` vocabulary behind `#ifdef USE_ROCM` (the CUDA PTX is untouched): system-scope `__builtin_amdgcn_global_{load,store}_b128` for peer-visible 16B accesses, `__hip_atomic_*` for flag traffic, `__builtin_amdgcn_fence` for fences, and traps for multimem (no multicast on ROCm).
- The local Lamport poll uses agent scope (`sc1`). The uncached workspace is still L2-cached by its owner, with peer writes over XGMI invalidating the line by probe. A single-thread signal fence keeps the poll in the loop: without it LLVM treats the b128 builtin as a pure read and deletes the spin loop.
- `2shot_pull`: every wave issues a system-scope release before the block barrier. On gfx950 `s_barrier` does not drain a wave's outstanding stores and the signalling thread's release only covers its own wave; without this, graph replays rarely read stale reduced shards (1 bad replay in 200 at TP6).
- `utils.cuh`: add the missing `cudaMemcpyDeviceToDevice` / `cudaGetDevice` HIP aliases.

**`CustomAllReduceV2` on ROCm** (`custom_all_reduce_v2.py`, `configs/custom_all_reduce_v2.py`)
- `_allocate_symmetric_memory` returns `(owner, per-rank views, multicast VA)` and uses `HipSymmetricBuffer` on ROCm; `has_multicast` is False there.
- No graph zero-copy input registration on ROCm (the 2-shot graph path would store into peers' cached input buffers, which XGMI does not keep coherent); captured all-reduces stage through the workspace. `IPCManager` is only built when graph registration can happen.
- ROCm gets its own tuning table instead of falling into the SM90 table because gfx950 reports capability 9.5.
- Gate: on ROCm, `can_use_custom_all_reduce_v2` disables v2 with a warning when the loaded HIP runtime (`hipRuntimeGetVersion` on the `libamdhip64` torch loaded) is older than `MIN_HIP_VERSION = (7, 2)`, the oldest validated. ROCm 10.x ships HIP 7.16+.

**MI350X launch geometry** (second commit). Swept grid size x threads per block x message size at TP2/4/6/8, two runs per point (median run-to-run spread 1.3%):
- `num_pull_blocks = 32` in the ROCm table instead of one block per CU. Each pull block runs its own cross-GPU barrier, so 256 blocks spend most of a pull all-reduce on flag traffic; 32 blocks make `2shot_pull` 39-65% and `1shot_pull` 35-51% (from 1 MB) faster at TP8, and are within a few % of the best grid at TP2/4/6. The existing thread rule stays within ~3% of the best block size at this grid.
- `1shot_push` launches 1024 threads per block from 128 KB on ROCm (TP8 -7 to -11% at 128-256 KB, -8% at 1 MB; TP4/6 -4 to -8%; neutral below 128 KB).
- The push grid stays at one block per CU: `2shot_push`, which covers the mid range, is best or within ~2% there at every world size, and the push grid is bound to the counter array.
- Size thresholds are unchanged (follow-up).

**Tests**
- `test_custom_all_reduce_v2_capability.py`: the HIP runtime gate (7.0/7.1 rejected before topology checks, 7.2/7.17 admitted).
- `test_custom_all_reduce.py`: graph capture uses `capture_error_mode="thread_local"`; the reference NCCL group's watchdog thread queries events during capture, which fails under global capture mode on ROCm.

## Accuracy Tests

Kernel-level, bit-exact against RCCL (`atol=0, rtol=0`) on 8x MI350X, ROCm 7.2 (HIP 7.2.26015), image `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x`, on the final branch:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_custom_all_reduce.py --num-gpu 2,4,6,8` with `SGLANG_JIT_KERNEL_RUN_FULL_TESTS=1` (4 algos x eager/graph x fp16/bf16/fp32 x 16 B-8 MB) | 310 passed per world size |
| `test_custom_all_reduce_v2_capability.py` | 13 passed |
| Back-to-back stress, no host sync, random algo/size interleaving (eager), and CUDA-graph replay, each also with RCCL initialized before carv2 (exercises the chunked VMM path) | 0 mismatches at TP8 (also TP2/4/6 before the tuning commit) |

No model-level accuracy run: ROCm dispatch does not select v2 in this PR, so model outputs are unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8x MI350X, TP8, bf16, CUDA-graph mode (16 all-reduces per graph), us per all-reduce (max over ranks), median of 3 runs; every column from the same runs. Bold is the fastest custom all-reduce (AITER or carv2).

| Size | RCCL | AITER | carv2 1shot_push | carv2 2shot_push | carv2 1shot_pull | carv2 2shot_pull | best carv2 vs AITER |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 KB | 14.5 | 5.3 | **4.2** | 6.7 | 6.9 | 10.0 | -20% |
| 16 KB | 14.4 | 5.6 | **4.4** | 7.0 | 7.2 | 11.0 | -23% |
| 64 KB | 14.3 | 8.7 | **5.5** | 7.3 | 7.9 | 11.2 | -37% |
| 128 KB | 14.1 | 7.3 | **7.1** | 7.5 | 9.4 | 11.4 | -3% |
| 256 KB | 16.7 | **7.6** | 10.6 | 7.8 | 11.9 | 12.1 | +3% |
| 512 KB | 21.7 | **8.7** | 16.4 | 8.7 | 16.8 | 13.1 | +0% |
| 1 MB | 25.0 | 11.3 | 28.0 | **10.3** | 26.0 | 16.4 | -9% |
| 2 MB | 31.2 | 16.7 | 49.2 | **16.4** | 44.0 | 23.2 | -2% |
| 4 MB | 48.5 | 25.8 | 90.6 | **25.3** | 83.8 | 36.6 | -2% |
| 8 MB | 73.1 | **44.5** | 172.3 | 49.0 | 158.7 | 64.5 | +10% |
| 16 MB | 112.0 | **82.6** | 333.5 | 90.8 | 306.8 | 122.1 | +10% |

carv2 is faster than RCCL at every size. Against AITER, `1shot_push` wins up to 128 KB (20-37% up to 64 KB), `2shot_push` ties at 256-512 KB, leads at 1 MB (-9%) and ties at 2-4 MB, and carv2 trails by ~10% at 8 MB and up.

Effect of the MI350X tuning commit (same setup; before = first commit, push medians of 3 runs, pull 1 run):

| Size | 1shot_push | 2shot_push | 1shot_pull | 2shot_pull |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 KB | 4.1 -> 4.2 (+2%) | 6.9 -> 6.7 (-3%) | 6.8 -> 6.9 (+1%) | 19.8 -> 10.0 (-50%) |
| 64 KB | 5.6 -> 5.5 (-2%) | 7.3 -> 7.3 (-0%) | 8.2 -> 7.9 (-3%) | 21.7 -> 11.2 (-48%) |
| 128 KB | 7.7 -> 7.1 (-7%) | 7.6 -> 7.5 (-1%) | 9.8 -> 9.4 (-4%) | 22.0 -> 11.4 (-48%) |
| 256 KB | 12.0 -> 10.6 (-11%) | 7.8 -> 7.8 (+0%) | 12.6 -> 11.9 (-5%) | 28.9 -> 12.1 (-58%) |
| 1 MB | 30.5 -> 28.0 (-8%) | 10.4 -> 10.3 (-1%) | 40.1 -> 26.0 (-35%) | 46.1 -> 16.4 (-65%) |
| 4 MB | 92.4 -> 90.6 (-2%) | 25.3 -> 25.3 (-0%) | 170.0 -> 83.8 (-51%) | 60.2 -> 36.6 (-39%) |
| 16 MB | 337.2 -> 333.5 (-1%) | 90.8 -> 90.8 (+0%) | 568.7 -> 306.8 (-46%) | 212.2 -> 122.1 (-42%) |

Even tuned, the pull algorithms trail `2shot_push` (1 MB: 16.4 vs 10.3 us), so the ROCm thresholds should route 1-16 MB to `2shot_push` rather than `2shot_pull`. Retuning the thresholds and enabling v2 in ROCm dispatch are follow-ups.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (no user-facing docs change: ROCm dispatch is unchanged)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] moe: Localize DeepGEMM Mega MoE weights across locality domains
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

On GPUs with two locality domains, DeepGEMM's Mega MoE gives rows `[d * N / 2, (d + 1) * N / 2)` of every expert to domain `d`'s SMs. With `deep_gemm.localize`, those rows also live in domain `d`'s memory, so weight reads stay local. DeepGEMM takes localized weights since sgl-project/DeepGEMM#119 (native CUDA 13.4 locality domains); this PR wires it into SGLang behind an opt-in env var.

`deep_gemm.localize` returns `(domains, experts, N / domains, K)` tensors, but the expert parameters are also read in two places outside Mega MoE:
- The deep-ep path above `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK` (`DeepseekV2MoE.forward` falls through when `should_use_mega_moe` is false).
- EPLB, which slices every routed-expert parameter by expert. A domain-major tensor fails `filter_moe_weight_param_global_expert`'s `shape[0] == num_local_experts`, so EPLB would silently move the scales but not the weights.

This PR keeps EPLB working and makes the token cap explicit.

## Modifications

- `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_LOCALIZE` (default off), applied on compute capability 10.7 only.
- `build_mega_moe_experts_weights`: localizes the interleaved L1 and the L2 weights. The kernel gets the domain-major tensors (`mega_l1_weights` / `mega_l2_weights`); `w13_weight` / `w2_weight` hold the expert-major `(experts, domains, N / domains, K)` view of the same memory, so every `get_moe_weights` keeps slicing by expert. No second copy of the weights.
- `build_mega_moe_shared_weights`: localizes the fused shared expert's L1 / L2 (DeepGEMM requires shared and routed weights to agree).
- `update_expert_weights_single_layer`: P2P needs each expert's slice dense, and a localized expert's halves live in different domains. Such a tensor is sent from a contiguous staging copy (one message per expert, like every other tensor) and received into a contiguous temp buffer; its weight, temp buffer and staging copy are viewed as int64 once when all three allow it. Every other tensor is moved exactly as before.
- `should_use_mega_moe`: with localized weights there is no non-mega fallback, so tokens above the cap assert with the same message pattern as Kimi K3.
- `test/manual/test_expert_location_updater.py`: the exchanged weights include an expert-major view of padded domain-major storage, so staged sends go through P2P. Passes with gloo (8 and 32 ranks) and NCCL (4 GPUs); with the previous updater NCCL rejects it (`Tensors for P2P must be non-overlapping and dense`).

Setting the env var requires sgl-deep-gemm >= 0.2.4 built with CUDA >= 13.4 (the cu134 image builds it from source).

## Accuracy and speed

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, one node, DP-attention 4 / EP 4, `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`, DSPARK, main e152f531d9 + this PR, sgl-deep-gemm v0.2.5.post3 built with CUDA 13.4, `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=16384`.

GSM8K (200 questions):

| Localize | EPLB | First commit | Head |
|---|---|---|---|
| off | off | 0.990 | 0.990 |
| on | off | 0.995 | 0.990 |
| off | on, 32 redundant experts, rebalance every 100 iterations | 0.995 | 0.980 |
| on | on, same; 5 rebalances during the eval, `SGLANG_EXPERT_LOCATION_UPDATER_CANARY=1` | 0.995 | 0.995 |

Decode, 128K-token context, output throughput (sum of per-DP medians), interleaved off / on / on / off:

| Batch | On vs off |
|---|---|
| 128 | +2.6% |
| 224 | +0.9% |

Both "on" runs beat both "off" runs at each batch size.

EPLB weight update, one layer on 4 GPUs (104 physical experts per rank, shuffled placement, `update_expert_weights_single_layer`, median of 36): localized weights take +3.5% vs plain weights, and plain weights are unchanged from main. Moving each domain's slice as its own message instead cost +22%: the update is dominated by per-message overhead, not bytes. In the server, a rebalance took 13.5% longer localized than plain (mean of 5 each, same run). Transient memory during a rebalance grows by the staging copy of the localized tensors (about 2% of weight memory at 104 experts per rank).

Memory: the routed experts keep one copy (the localized one). Weight memory reads 1.7% higher and KV capacity 1.47% lower: the original routed weights are freed from PyTorch segments shared with other weights, and those holes cannot be returned to the driver. The fused shared expert's L2 is held twice, as the original stays for the shared-expert linear.

`test_waterfill_eplb.py` passes.

## Not covered

- Prefill throughput (Mega MoE prefill showed no gain in earlier kernel measurements; not re-measured).
- Elastic EP's reload of missing experts from disk and `update_weights_from_disk` into localized parameters.
- Multi-node EPLB (only single-node P2P was exercised).

title: [CI] test: Relax bs=1 perf limits for CI hosts with slower CPUs
author: em-dreyer
body:
## Motivation

The 1-GPU H100 CI lane (`1-gpu-large`) now runs on hosts with slower host CPUs. Two batch-size-1 perf tests fail there on every run with no code change, which blocks PRs on that stage:

| Test | Limit | Previous hosts | Current hosts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dllm/test_dllm_batching_fdfo.py::test_bs_1_speed` | > 250 tok/s | 257–263 | 214–252 (31 samples; medians 232 and 248 on the two host types) |
| `moe/test_torch_compile_moe.py::test_throughput` | ≥ 285 tok/s | passes | 272–276 on the slower host type |

Both tests time a single request end to end. At batch size 1 that is bound by the host CPU as much as by the GPU. dLLM decoding runs with overlap scheduling disabled (`_dllm_overlap_disable`) and syncs with the host after every denoising step (`LowConfidence.step` → `done.tolist()`). In the scheduler logs the number of denoising steps is identical across hosts (365 for the 654-token answer), and the whole per-step time distribution shifts up by 3–13% (p50 7.05 → 7.25 / 7.94 ms). That points to the host CPU, not the GPU kernels.

## Modifications

- `test_dllm_batching_fdfo`: `speed > 250` → `speed > 200`
- `test_torch_compile_moe` (CUDA): `throughput >= 285` → `throughput >= 260`

Both new limits stay well above what a real regression would produce, with ~5% margin under the slowest measured host. Accuracy assertions are unchanged.

## Follow-up

A host-independent version of these checks would assert on GPU time per step and track CPU overhead separately, so host speed stops being baked into the limits. Happy to discuss that separately.

title: [Refactor] imports: Import names from where they are defined; remove re-export shims
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Code imports each name from the module that defines it, or from the nearest module that exports it (`__all__`, a package `__init__`), instead of through a module that only imports it itself. 322 imports move, e.g. `GenerationBatchResult` from `sglang.srt.managers.utils` instead of `sglang.srt.managers.scheduler`, `ModelTaskType` from `configs.task_type` instead of `pipeline_configs.base`. A name a module binds per platform or as a fallback (inside a runtime `if` / `try`, such as `causal_conv1d_fn` in `mamba.py`) keeps going through that module.
- Imports a module kept only so others could import the name through it are removed, including the kernel forwards in `spec_utils` and `mem_cache.utils`, which the kernel layout already asks not to leave behind. The test that guarded the `spec_utils` forwards goes with them.
- Callers of the compatibility re-exports in `arg_groups.overrides`, `server_args` (`NS`, `A`, `Arg`, `LoRAPathAction`, and the unused `LoRARef`, `CudaGraphConfig`, LoRA constants and arg helpers), `model_runner`, `unified_radix_cache`, `sana_wm`, and the comparator's `output_types` import from the source, and the re-exports are removed. The choice lists and plugin helpers that `server_args` documents as public stay.
- Deprecated shims are removed, with every in-tree reference (code, tests, patch targets, docs, cookbook, scripts, workflows) moved to the real path:
  - `sglang.bench_serving` -> `sglang.benchmark.serving`
  - `sglang.bench_one_batch_server` -> `sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server`
  - `sglang.srt.utils.hf_transformers_utils` -> `sglang.srt.utils.hf_transformers`
  - `sglang.srt.layers.attention.nsa` -> `sglang.srt.layers.attention.dsa`
- `deepseek_janus_pro.py` imports the five names it uses from `configs.janus_pro` instead of `import *`.

No behavior change, except: the four module paths above no longer exist, and names this PR stops re-exporting can no longer be imported through the modules that used to forward them. Every moved import resolves to the same object as before.

Names no longer importable through the module that forwarded them, and where to import them from:

- `sglang.srt.arg_groups.overrides`: `MODEL_OVERRIDES`, `register_model_override`, `mamba_extra_buffer_of`, `_MODEL_OVERRIDE_FNS`, `_PREDICATE_OVERRIDE_FNS` -> `sglang.srt.arg_groups.model_override_base`
- `sglang.srt.server_args`:
  - `NS`, `A`, `Arg` -> `sglang.srt.arg_groups.arg_utils`
  - `LoRAPathAction` -> `sglang.srt.arg_groups.argparse_actions`
  - `LoRARef` -> `sglang.srt.lora.lora_registry`
  - `CudaGraphConfig`, `parse_cuda_graph_config_arg` -> `sglang.srt.model_executor.cuda_graph_config`
  - `LORA_TARGET_ALL_MODULES`, `SUPPORTED_LORA_TARGET_MODULES`, `human_readable_int`, `json_list_type`, `nullable_str` -> `sglang.srt.utils.common`

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] qwen3: Reuse the table QK-norm/RoPE kernel for MRoPE decode
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

#46908 fuses QK RMSNorm and RoPE into one Triton kernel (`table_qk_norm_rope_`) for dense text Qwen3 decode, behind `--enable-fused-qk-norm-rope`. Qwen3-VL uses the same `Qwen3Attention`, but its `MRotaryEmbedding` keeps it on the split path: JIT QK-norm, then `triton_mrope_fused`. This PR extends the table kernel to MRoPE. It supersedes #43425, which added a separate CUDA kernel for the same case.

## Modifications

- **`table_qk_norm_rope_`**
  - Takes `[3, T]` MRoPE positions (row-strided, as the decode graph runner passes them) plus `MRotaryEmbedding.axis_map`, and gathers each rotary lane's position from its own axis. Any positions are handled correctly, including precomputed spatial decode positions.
  - Accepts a BF16 rotary table. With one, it rotates in BF16 using `triton_mrope_fused`'s expression, so its output is bit-identical to the split MRoPE path.
  - Above 1024 (token, head) rows, each program handles eight heads over four warps, instead of one (token, head) per one-warp program. A `[heads, 32]` partial-sum tile keeps each head's reduction order, so the output stays bit-exact. With one head per program, the kernel's cost grew with tokens x heads and it lost to the split path at decode batches of 256-512; it now wins at every measured size (table below).
  - The rotation arithmetic is flattened into one shared multiply/add branch. The non-`match_cuda` path keeps one head per program and four warps, and its output is bit-identical to before (checked at head_dim 64/128/256).
- **`Qwen3Attention`**
  - The gate now also admits `MRotaryEmbedding` with an `mrope_section`, at head_dim 64 or 128. At head_dim 256, the table kernel's BF16 rotation isn't bit-exact with `triton_mrope_fused` (about 14% of elements differ by up to 1 ULP), so MRoPE at 256 keeps the split path. Plain RoPE still covers 64, 128 and 256.
  - With 2D positions, the layer first casts the rotary table to the activation dtype (`_match_cos_sin_cache_dtype`, the same cast the split path makes). The cast happens during graph warmup, not after capture.
  - MRoPE with 1D positions, extend, and speculative verify keep the split path.
- **Tests**
  - Kernel: BF16 table with distinct per-axis positions vs JIT QK-norm + `triton_mrope_fused`, bit for bit, at head_dim 64 and 128, for the section, interleaved, and GLM-interleaved layouts.
  - Kernel: new cases with head counts that aren't a multiple of 8, so the eight-heads-per-program path also runs partial head blocks.
  - Model: MRoPE layers in the dispatch and changing-input graph-replay tests, with distinct, row-strided axes. Graph replay includes batch 128 (1280 rows), which runs the eight-heads-per-program path inside a captured graph.
  - Model: MRoPE at head_dim 256 stays on the split path.
  - Model: 1D positions on an MRoPE layer stay on the split path.

The flag stays opt-in on CUDA.

## Accuracy

The fused path is bit-identical to the split path, so no accuracy eval was run.

- **Unit tests:** 78/78 pass on one B300 (SM 10.3): `test_table_qk_norm_rope.py` and `test_qwen3_qk_norm_rope.py`.
- **End-to-end:** `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct`, TP1, default backends, decode CUDA graphs on, one B300. 6 concurrent greedy chat requests (2 with an image, 4 text-only), 256 tokens each. All 6 outputs are identical with the flag off and on. A call-recording hook on the flag-on server confirmed fused calls during capture of the bs=512 decode graph, with row-strided `[3, 512]` positions and a BF16 table.

## Benchmark

Kernel only, on one idle B300. Each value is the median per-call time in µs over 30 replays of a CUDA graph holding 100 calls. Setup: bf16, head_dim 128.
- **MRoPE:** BF16 table; split is JIT QK-norm + `triton_mrope_fused`.
- **Plain RoPE:** FP32 table; split is JIT QK-norm + `apply_rope_with_cos_sin_cache_inplace`.

Every row is bit-exact with the split path.

| RoPE | Q/KV heads | Tokens | Split | This PR | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MRoPE | 8/1 | 1 | 2.66 | 1.54 | 1.72x |
| MRoPE | 8/1 | 512 | 4.23 | 2.44 | 1.73x |
| MRoPE | 32/8 | 1 | 4.17 | 1.58 | 2.64x |
| MRoPE | 32/8 | 32 | 4.75 | 1.74 | 2.72x |
| MRoPE | 32/8 | 128 | 5.00 | 2.12 | 2.37x |
| MRoPE | 32/8 | 256 | 5.78 | 2.73 | 2.12x |
| MRoPE | 32/8 | 512 | 7.39 | 4.15 | 1.78x |
| MRoPE | 64/8 | 1 | 4.77 | 1.62 | 2.94x |
| MRoPE | 64/8 | 512 | 8.79 | 6.12 | 1.44x |
| Plain | 16/8 | 128 | 2.96 | 2.00 | 1.48x |
| Plain | 32/8 | 1 | 2.30 | 1.40 | 1.65x |
| Plain | 32/8 | 256 | 4.98 | 2.60 | 1.91x |
| Plain | 64/8 | 256 | 6.69 | 3.56 | 1.88x |
| Plain | 64/8 | 512 | 8.00 | 5.91 | 1.35x |

The full sweep (T = 1, 8, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512 with heads 8/1, 16/8, 32/8, 64/8) ranges from 1.35x to 3.09x. Below 1024 rows the kernel keeps the one-head layout; interleaved old-vs-new runs at T <= 24 match within noise.

No end-to-end latency was measured.

## Checklist

- [x] Repository pre-commit checks pass.
- [x] Unit tests for the kernel and the model dispatch.
- [x] GPU correctness on the PR commit (B300).
- [ ] End-to-end decode latency for Qwen3-VL.

title: [Fix] moe: Revert the JIT rewrite of `moe_finalize_fuse_shared` (#47784)
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Revert #47784 (`ca819c11cd`), the JIT rewrite of `moe_finalize_fuse_shared`: restore `moe_finalize_fuse_shared.cu` and its Python wrapper byte for byte, and drop the new `.cuh` kernel with its unit test and benchmark.
- Keep the `fma_f32x2` / `mul_f32x2` / `add_f32x2` helpers #47784 added to `sgl_kernel/math.cuh`; `kimi_k3/attn_res/fused_tma.cuh` uses them now.
- #47784 drops GSM8K of `test_dsa_glm52_hisparse.py` (GLM-5.2-NVFP4, 1P1D, HiSparse + MTP) on 8-gpu-b200 from ~0.95 to ~0.90, below its 0.935 threshold. The test is nightly-only, so the PR's CI did not run it.
- The failure reproduces on 8-gpu-b200 only; on 8x B300 the same commits pass (0.942-0.950).

No behavior change other than going back to the pre-#47784 finalize kernel.

## Suspected cause

cc @DarkSharpness @BBuf. This is our reading of the code, not yet confirmed by a targeted run.

- With `routing_ready=True`, the default and what `finalize_flashinfer_trtllm_deferred_output` passes, the new kernel loads the routing tensors **and the `shared_output` row** before `PDLWaitPrimary` (`moe_finalize_fuse_shared.cuh`, `Token::load` and `finalize_kernel`).
- The old kernel also staged the routing tensors before `cudaGridDependencySynchronize()`, but read `shared_output` only after it. The early `shared_output` load is the one ordering change #47784 makes.
- In `DeepseekV2MoE`, `shared_output` is produced by the shared expert on `alt_stream`, and the main stream joins it with `wait_stream` right before the finalize launch. The `routing_ready` docstring requires the inputs to be complete when the kernel launches. We suspect that under CUDA graph capture with PDL, the dependency on the shared expert's last kernel is relaxed too, so finalize can read rows that are not written yet. The routing tensors come from an earlier kernel on the same stream, which is why reading them early was safe before.
- That fits the symptom: no crash, a few points of accuracy lost, and only on one GPU type, where the timing exposes the race.

## Relanding

- Keep the routing prefetch, and move the `shared_output` row load after `PDLWaitPrimary`, as the old kernel did. Or pass `routing_ready=False` whenever `shared_output` is given, at some cost in latency.
- Add a test that produces `shared_output` on a side stream inside a CUDA graph with PDL on. The current unit test builds every input before the launch, so the early read is always safe there.
- Run `test_dsa_glm52_hisparse.py` on 8-gpu-b200 before merging; it is nightly-only, so PR CI does not cover it.

## Bisect

`test_dsa_glm52_hisparse.py` on 8-gpu-b200, threshold 0.935; two scores are the first try and the automatic retry. In commit order:

| commit | what | GSM8K | result | run |

| `e8bf40b8ee` | window midpoint | 0.960 | pass | [41541080899](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41541080899) |
| `2b38f4a6ed` | parent of #47784 | 0.934 / 0.952 | pass | [41541056397](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41541056397) |
| `ca819c11cd` | #47784 | 0.904 / 0.916 | fail | [41541068672](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41541068672) |
| `cec4554871` | later main | 0.910 / 0.918 | fail | [41534879970](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41534879970) |
| `fbb847bed6` | later main | 0.914 / 0.916 | fail | [41534893338](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41534893338) |

title: [Refactor] mem_cache: Own state and fixed payloads in the KV storage plan and size from them
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #48026
* #48025
* #48024
* #48023
* #48022
* #48021
* #48020
* #48019
* #48018

* #48007
* #48006
* #48005
* __->__ #48004
* #48003
* #48002
* #48001

## Motivation

The unified memory pool sized its arena from token counts and handled state (Mamba/GDN/KDA recurrent state), request-indexed and fixed payloads in separate, per-model code. This PR makes the KV storage plan declare every payload — state entries, request rows, scratch and derived pages — before allocation, and sizes all of it from one total byte budget, so capacity, resizing and admission read one source.

## Modifications

- Declarations: `mem_cache/kv/decl.py`, `kv/plan.py`, `kv/layout/parts.py`, `kv/memory/fixed.py`, `kv/memory/request_window.py`, `kv/memory/snapshot.py`: state, request, scratch and derived storage are declared parts of the plan; checkpoint and request-reset behavior is preserved through layout views; resume boundaries and tracking effects are carried by the storage.
- Sizing: `mem_cache/kv/sizing.py`, `kv_cache_configurator.py`, `model_executor/pool_configurator.py`: one solve over the total budget sizes FULL, windows and state; every arena band can be resized after capture without changing captured addresses; physical and widened DCP units are accounted separately; request payloads are fitted within the usable budget; runtime sizing includes peak state demand.
- Admission and retraction: `mem_cache/prefill_budget.py`, `managers/schedule_policy.py`, `managers/scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py`: request state-slot demand is shared between sizing and admission; retraction keeps complete entries.
- Linear-attention state staging: `layers/attention/linear/kernels/state_pool_io.py`, `gdn_backend.py`, `gdn_flashinfer.py`, `kda_backend.py`, `hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py`: with a strided state pool, prefill stages requests' states at rows 1..n and keeps row 0 as the padding row the FlashInfer GDN prefill expects.
- Replay geometry is read only for enabled modes (`fused_recurrent_linear_replayssm.py`, `spec_utils.py`).
- Tests: new declaration, sizing, request-window, state-alignment and staging tests under `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/kv/`, `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/`, plus updates to the existing unified allocator, admission and golden-layout tests.

**Behavior change:** under `--enable-unified-memory`, `--max-total-tokens` sizes the arena (as it sizes separate pools): the arena is the smallest budget whose solve gives that many FULL tokens, with windows and state sized by the same rules. FULL may still grow into the whole arena; the flag is not an allocation cap. Only a pipeline stage's synchronized share caps FULL.

**Known limitation:** with a strided state pool, the GDN prefill path rebuilds its staging indices in every layer. On short-request workloads this costs about 4% (Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B TP2 unified, 2x B200, GSM8K 1000 questions, warm server: 36.0 s vs 33.8–35.4 s on `main`). Computing the indices once per forward removes it; the longer-term fix is kernels that take the state slot stride directly.

## Accuracy Tests

Serving validation was run at the **top of this 26-PR stack** (the cumulative change), not at this PR's head. Software: torch 2.14.1+cu130, flashinfer 0.7.2, sglang-kernel 0.4.10. GSM8K is few-shot, 500 or 1319 questions as noted; `main` is the same commit the stack is based on, same flags.

| Hardware | Model | Configuration | Stack top | main |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, `--enable-unified-memory` (rebased stack) | 0.954 (1319 q) | 0.950–0.954 |
| 1x H200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b | TP1, `--enable-unified-memory --max-total-tokens 120000` (rebased stack) | 0.842 (1319 q) | 0.839 |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, unified, MTP (EAGLE, 3 steps, topk 1, 4 draft tokens) | 0.951, accept length 3.56 | 0.953, 3.56 |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, unified, DFlash draft | 0.951, accept length 5.42 | 0.952, 5.44 |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | PD (prefill TP1 + decode TP1, mooncake), unified, repeated runs | 0.952–0.960, no hang | 0.954–0.958 |
| 2x H200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b | PD (TP1 + TP1, mooncake), unified | 0.810 | 0.808 |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, unified, HiCache | 0.954 | — |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | PP2, unified | 0.953 | 0.955 (static pools) |
| 2x B200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, unified (500 q) | 0.958 | 0.960 |
| 2x B200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b | TP2, unified, `trtllm_mha` (1319 q) | 0.849 | 0.863 |
| 2x B300 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B / openai/gpt-oss-120b | TP2, unified | 0.950 / 0.849 | 0.954 / 0.849 |

On B200 and B300, 40 greedy GSM8K generations were compared with `main`: 35–40 of 40 are identical, and the rest first differ after at least 27 characters (near ties). The H200 runs above other than the two marked "rebased stack" were run at the stack top before it was rebased onto the current base; the code they cover is unchanged by the rebase except for conflict resolutions.

The Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B rows exercise the GDN state staging and state sizing here; the gpt-oss `--max-total-tokens 120000` row exercises the token-limit sizing.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Measured at the stack top, same flags as `main` (bench_serving, random 4096-in / 512-out unless noted):

| Hardware | Model / configuration | Stack top | main |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1x H200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b, unified, `--max-total-tokens 120000` | 3.93–3.95 req/s | 3.95 req/s |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B PD (TP1 + TP1), 2048-in / 256-out | 5.65–6.28 req/s | 6.21–6.29 req/s |
| 2x H200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b PD (TP1 + TP1) | 9.39–9.45 req/s | 9.21 req/s |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B MTP TP2 / DFlash TP2 | 4.26 / 4.36 req/s | 4.29 / 4.35 req/s |
| 2x B200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B TP2 / openai/gpt-oss-120b TP2 | 6.35 / 19.31 req/s | 6.34 / 19.28 req/s |

See the known limitation above for the GDN staging cost on short requests.

body:

* __->__ #48005
* #48004
* #48003
* #48002
* #48001

## Motivation

A speculative draft fused into the unified pool used to be placed by its layer kind; draft layers whose retention differed from the target's either got a private draft pool or were forced into a band that does not match their lifetime. This PR places draft KV by retention lifetime: a draft layer shares the target sub-pool with the same lifetime, and gets its own band otherwise. It also makes window reclamation independent per window and derives the draft's KV coordinates from its attention execution (DCP width, backend).

## Modifications

- Placement: `mem_cache/layout/fused_draft.py`, `kv_cache_configurator.py`, `kv/plan.py`, `kv/alloc/runner_ids.py`, `kv/alloc/id_space.py`, `unified_draft_pool.py`: draft bands are planned by retention lifetime; fused draft views share the target's storage arena.
- Allocation: `kv/alloc/{chain,band,pricing,interim}.py`, `kv/storage.py`, `prefill_budget.py`: independent windows are reclaimed for cleanup and admission; physical reservation scopes and takes cover every chain band.
- Execution: `configs/attention_execution.py`, `layers/attention/{flashinfer_mla_backend,triton_backend}.py`, `kv/layout/{mha,mla,page}.py`, `layout/token_major.py`, `models/dflash.py`, `speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py`: draft KV coordinates come from the attention execution (replicated vs DCP-sharded).
- HiCache: `managers/cache_controller.py`, `hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py`, `kv/memory/host_backing.py`, `hicache_storage.py`, `storage/umbp/umbp_store.py`: storage rank replication is decided per view; the `"file"` storage backend uses the page-envelope host pool (it reads and writes whole pages); a single-pool envelope host is sized from that pool's capacity under `--hicache-ratio` rather than from the whole region.
- Tests: draft placement, DCP capacity, HiCache DCP/identity, multiwindow placement, tri-pool and radix-cache tests under `test/registered/unit/`.

**Behavior changes:**

title: [Perf] disaggregation: Cache host-staged decode admission accounting across a transfer pass
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

`DecodeTransferQueue.pop_transferred` admits completed host-staged requests to device memory through `DecodePreallocQueue.allocate_host_staged`. #46898 made a pass stop device admission at the first refusal, because trying every later request recomputed the request-independent accounting (running-batch token sums, maximum per-request growth, transfer-queue device-destination count, retracted-token requirements) on every attempt: O(W × (R + Q + T)) per pass for W attempts, R running requests, Q transfer entries and T retracted requests.

Stopping at the first refusal trades utilization for that bound. A later, smaller request that would fit waits for the next pass even when device capacity is free, and near a full pool that is exactly when the capacity matters. This change lets every completed request in the pass try, and keeps the pass linear by computing the shared accounting once.

## Modifications

- `_HostStagedAdmissionStats` holds the pass-invariant accounting: retractable full/SWA token sums over the running batch, the maximum per-request growth (full and SWA), the number of transfer entries holding a device destination, and the retracted queue's full/SWA token requirements. Each field is filled lazily on first use and reused by later admission calls in the same pass.
- `DecodePreallocQueue._use_host_staged_admission_stats` scopes the cache with a context manager around each `allocate_host_staged` call in `pop_transferred`. Outside that scope (every other caller, the next pass, and after an exception) `_host_staged_admission_stats` is `None` and all helpers read the live queues as before.
- A successful admission increments the cached device-destination count so later checks in the same pass see it; the pass-local "first refusal" flag from #46898 is removed, so a refused request is skipped with `continue` and later ones still try, in queue order.
- `_need_space_for_single_req` returns early for an empty running batch or a `None` retractable count, then computes the maximum per-request requirement once and subtracts the retractable tokens; the result is unchanged.
- New `_retracted_token_counts` returns the retracted queue's `(full, swa)` requirements in one walk and replaces the two separate loops in the full and SWA allocatable-budget helpers.
- New `has_device_destinations` property on `DecodePreallocQueue`; `disagg_transfers_in_flight` in `disaggregation/utils.py` reads it instead of scanning the transfer queue itself, so the unified-memory pin predicate also benefits from the cached count during admission.
- `test_unified_memory_move_gate.py`: `_FakePreallocQueue` now subclasses `DecodePreallocQueue` and holds the fake transfer queue, so the move-gate test exercises the real `has_device_destinations` property.

Rebased onto main after #43908: the two new iterations over the decode transfer queue (`has_device_destinations` and `_active_req_count`) read `self.transfer_queue.queue.items()`, matching the request-list container that refactor introduced; the `pop_transferred` loop keeps its `queue = list(self.queue.items())` form.

Allocator availability, eviction credit and SWA capacity are not cached; allocation, reclamation and failed-transfer cleanup inside a pass affect the next decision. The cache holds Python integers only; the admission path adds no device readback or GPU-to-CPU synchronization.

## Testing

- `pre-commit run --files` on the three changed files passes.
- `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_unified_memory_move_gate.py`: 10 tests, 22 subtests pass on this branch.
- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_decode_radix_lock_ref.py`, `test_decode_retraction_backup.py`, `test_hisparse_allocator.py` and `test_unified_dynamic_gate_capacity.py` (the registered unit files that exercise the changed admission helpers): 35 tests, 23 subtests pass on this branch.

Co-authored-by: ZYHowell <ZYHowell@users.noreply.github.com>

title: [CI] runners: Move H100 tests with no H100-specific dependency to 1-gpu-small
author: em-dreyer
body:
## Summary

The H100 pool (`1-gpu-h100`) is saturated:
- **Before Nov 2:** in the 24h to 2026-11-02 it ran 993 runner-hours on 40 runners, and per-commit base-b H100 jobs waited 33 min at the median and 394 min at p90.
- **Now:** on Nov 2 the pool lost 24 of those runners and is down to 16. Its queue peaked at 412 jobs on the evening of Nov 2. At about 3pm PST on Nov 3, 286 jobs were queued, with a 5.2h median wait and the oldest waiting 16.9h.

The 5090 pool (`1-gpu-5090`) ran 525 runner-hours on 48 online runners in the 24h to Nov 2.

This PR moves 386 test files from 1-gpu-large (H100) to 1-gpu-small (RTX 5090). The only change in each test file is the `runner_config` value of its `register_cuda_ci` calls. Whole files move: a file moves only if every one of its 1-gpu-large registrations qualifies, and no file is split.

A file stays on H100 if its code (comments and docstrings excluded) shows any of:
- **Hopper-only code:** FA3, FlashMLA, DeepGEMM, HPC-Ops, exact SM90 or SM90/SM100 gates, `int8_scaled_mm`
- **A model over 26 GB,** sized from the checkpoint's weight files on the Hub
- **`lmms_eval`,** which is not installed on the Blackwell runners

This first pass also holds back anything that needs a judgment call:
- throughput or latency floors
- more than one server launch
- "SM90+" gates
- models whose size could not be determined
- combined model sizes over 26 GB

| Suite (est_time) | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| base-b 1-gpu-large | 118 files / 118.3 min | 62 / 93.5 min |
| base-b-kernel-unit 1-gpu-large | 289 / 199.2 min | 59 / 71.5 min |
| base-b-kernel-benchmark 1-gpu-large | 78 / 31.4 min | 16 / 12.6 min |
| extra-a 1-gpu-large | 28 / 137.6 min | 15 / 97.7 min |
| nightly 1-gpu-large | 67 / 160.9 min | 28 / 92.5 min |

Counts are from main as of 2026-11-03. Files added to main since the selection was made are left on H100 for now.

Weekly H100 tests are left alone: the weekly workflow has no 1-gpu-small job, and they add almost no H100 load.

## Workflow change

base-b, extra-a and nightly partitions are sized from est_time by `compute_partitions.py`. The JIT-kernel lanes have hard-coded shards, so `pr-test-jit-kernel.yml` changes:
- kernel-unit on 1-gpu-large goes from 2 shards to 1.
- kernel-unit on 1-gpu-small goes from 1 shard to 3.
- A new `benchmark-test-1-gpu-small` job runs the kernel benchmarks that move.

## Validation

- [ ] `/rerun-test -c` on the 5090 runners. Files that fail, or skip cases that run on H100, are reverted to 1-gpu-large.
  - Nightly moves ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41741354758)): three files are reverted to H100.
    - `test_qsa_determinism.py`: needs a native top-k op the 5090 build lacks.
    - `test_moe_lora_down_b_into_base_matrix.py`: CuTe DSL error.
    - `test_score_api.py`: 35 ms against its 32 ms latency limit.
- [ ] Compare skip counts against main's scheduled H100 run.
- [ ] Raise `est_time` where the 5090 duration is more than 1.5x the estimate.
- [ ] Full PR CI (`run-ci`) to exercise the jit-kernel workflow change.

## Prior work

#41231 by @mmangkad surveyed the same move and found most of these files pass on the 5090. This PR redoes the selection from scratch on current main.

title: [Perf] Hunyuan3D: Reduce redundant QEM quadric accumulation
author: charliechenye
body:
## Summary

Hunyuan3D's Paint remeshing computes a symmetric 4×4 quadric-error metric (QEM) matrix for each vertex. The existing implementation independently accumulates all 16 matrix entries using `np.bincount`, although only 10 entries are unique.

This PR:

- Computes the **10 unique upper triangular entries** and mirrors them into the lower triangle, eliminating six redundant `np.bincount` calls.
- Preserves the original vertex/face indexing, weight accumulation order, `float64` dtype, and downstream mesh simplification behavior.
- Adds one focused regression test comparing the optimized implementation against an independent 16 entry reference on closed and open boundary meshes.

The change is limited to QEM quadric accumulation. It does not modify edge collapse logic, UV unwrapping, texture generation, or model inference.

Note: shape only requests do not execute this Paint remeshing path.

## Correctness

Validation was performed at three levels:

1. **Frozen OBJ and synthetic CPU inputs:** bitwise parity passed against the original implementation.
2. **Captured live Paint mesh (P4D):** raw NumPy vertices and faces were captured immediately before `mesh_simplify()` on a 568,580 face mesh. Replaying the identical input through the original and optimized implementations produced bitwise identical initial quadrics and matched the recorded live QEM output fingerprint.
3. **Paint+GLB inference:** generated GLBs were successfully loaded and checked for geometry and UVs.

The regression test uses an independent 16 entry reference and compares quadric arrays through `view(np.uint64)` to enforce exact bit pattern equality.

Cross request GLB SHA256 values were not used as parity evidence, since independently generated outputs can differ even with the same seed.

## Performance

We evaluated the optimization on one H200 using an eight-visit
A-B-B-A-A-B-B-A comparison (four measured visits per arm).

- Control: pristine Core `bde43d6c132ecd726ffdd68702bdb66900cae303`
- Candidate: only the symmetric-QEM accumulation change
- Same input image, seed, inference settings, and request warmup
- Paint enabled with `paint_use_remesh=true`
- Native SGLang performance measurements

| Metric | Control | Candidate | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Paint Preprocess | 9,197.01 ms | 8,694.76 ms | **5.46%** |
| Native E2E | 22,642.59 ms | 22,079.16 ms | **2.49%** |

All four adjacent A/B pairs showed positive Paint Preprocess and native E2E improvements.

An earlier exploratory cohort showed substantial timing instability and was excluded from the primary performance summary. Both cohorts are documented in the investigation log.

Paint Preprocess includes QEM, UV unwrapping, and rendering, so its improvement is not attributable exclusively to QEM.

### Same-live-input CPU QEM replay (P4D)

To isolate QEM more directly, captured live Paint mesh arrays were replayed through both implementations using identical input bytes.

| Captured input | Original QEM | Optimized QEM | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| v00-control | 7,033.75 ms | 6,692.41 ms | **4.85%** |
| v01-candidate | 7,300.26 ms | 6,732.47 ms | **7.78%** |

Both inputs passed exact QEM output parity.

These measurements characterize CPU QEM replay performance and should not be interpreted as native Paint E2E improvements. The instrumented live capture timings are diagnostic only.

## Tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python" python -m pytest \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_hunyuan3d_native_texture_models.py \
  -k TestHunyuan3DPaintRemesh \
  -v
```

Result:

- **5 passed**
- **2 subtests passed**
- 8 deselected
- 19 warnings

The new regression coverage is intentionally limited to one test method with closed/open mesh subtests. Existing remeshing tests remain unchanged.

## Scope and limitations

- Only two files are changed: the QEM implementation and its existing unit test file.
- Performance was measured on one H200 with a fixed request configuration.
- Correctness was verified on synthetic, frozen, and captured live Paint inputs; this does not establish parity for every possible mesh.
- Native SGLang E2E stage timing does not represent user-perceived network latency.
- The optimization does not affect Shape only inference.

Detailed experiment reports and investigation history are recorded in charliechenye/sglang#2.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).

title: [Perf] paged-experts: load experts without a staging copy
author: N3mezis
body:
# [Perf] paged-experts: load experts without a staging copy

## Motivation

This PR aims to reduce memory footprint while loading checkpoints.

Paged Experts (#42557) keeps every expert in a pinned host store. Today a start first loads every expert into a pageable staging copy in the checkpoint layout, then fills the store from it K experts at a time (on the Marlin runner — GPTQ, AWQ, MXFP4, NVFP4, compressed-tensors W4A16 — through the repack). The staging copy is as large as the store, and while loading, both are in RAM at once, next to the checkpoint's page cache.

So a start needs host memory for every expert twice. Paged Experts exists to serve models whose experts don't fit in VRAM from host RAM, and the staging copy halves which models that is: a model whose experts fit in RAM once but not twice cannot start without swapping heavily, and is killed on a host without enough swap. For example, Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-NVFP4 on an RTX 5070 Ti with 62 GB of RAM:
- the staging copy takes 44 GB,
- 19-26 GB go to swap during the start,
- `load_model` takes 177-352 s, depending on how much it swaps,
- after the start, 3.4-3.5 GB of the server process stay in swap, which raises TTFT.

This PR removes the staging copy: the expert loads replay K experts at a time from the mapped checkpoint, straight into the store (or the repack). On the same machine, Qwen3-Next loads in 125-128 s without swapping, and TTFT p50 drops from 220-231 ms to 192 ms. Models whose experts fit in RAM twice don't gain from it; their start is 1-2 s slower.

## Modifications

- **Loads wait** (`store.py`: `ExpertLoads`). With mapped safetensors (`--load-format auto`, `safetensors`, `mistral`, without `--weight-loader-disable-mmap`), an expert load of a paged layer does not run; it waits as a write on its view of the mapped checkpoint. A load that cannot wait (a stacked checkpoint tensor as in gpt-oss, a tensor torch allocated) and every load of the other loaders go to a table of every expert, as before.
- **The post-load step K experts at a time** (`formats.py`: `PostLoad`, `build_store`). After loading, the waiting loads replay one chunk of K experts into K rows, the base method's post-load step runs on them (a repack on the Marlin runner, from the layer's state before the first chunk), and the result is copied into the pinned store. Each chunk's checkpoint pages are read ahead while the previous chunk runs (`MADV_WILLNEED`) and given back after it (`MADV_PAGEOUT`, on a thread of its own, since the kernel reclaims synchronously; skipped where the kernel lacks it, never `MADV_DONTNEED`). Experts 1..K, which the existing mixing check repacks once more, keep their pages until it ran, so every expert is read from the checkpoint once.
- **Behaviour change: `--load-format`.** #47476 refused only `dummy`. The store fills from `model.load_weights` followed by the post-load step, so the loaders that do that are accepted (`auto`, `safetensors`, `pt`, `npcache`, `mistral`, `fastsafetensors`, `instanttensor`, `runai_streamer`) and every other format is refused at startup with its reason: `dummy` has no real weights, `gguf` holds GGUF-quantized experts (no expert format pages them), the rest load the weights without Paged Experts' loader and post-load step.

Outside Paged Experts nothing changes. Docs: `paged_experts.mdx` ("Load formats", "Startup", "The K-slot table and the host store").

## Accuracy Tests

The pinned store holds the same bytes as before: the same native per-expert loader and post-load step run on the same experts, only in another order. GSM8K (200 questions), Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-NVFP4, base / this PR, two starts each: 0.965, 0.975 / 0.970, 0.960 (standard error about 1.6 points). Unit tests on CPU:

- `TestLoads`: a view of a mapped file waits and a tensor torch allocated does not (a real safetensors file as control); only the mapped safetensors loaders let loads wait; a load that cannot wait moves the waiting ones into the table (negative control: a waiting load left out keeps its created value); replayed views keep their bytes after `madvise`, refused advice leaves anonymous memory alone (negative control: `MADV_DONTNEED` zeroes it); pages are given back on a thread of their own and `drop` waits for it (control: read-ahead stays on the caller); without Linux no libc is loaded and advice is skipped; a build replays each expert once and gives each expert's pages back once, after its last read, also experts 1..K after the mixing check (negative control: giving pages back at every replay re-reads 1..K).
- `TestLoading`: the host loader follows the base method and the parameter's tags; a stacked tensor reaches the native loader after the waiting loads; the repack runs per chunk from the layer's state before the first; a short last chunk pads with real experts (NVFP4A16's scale check passes); a step that mixes experts is refused; a loader that reads the layer's state sees it as loaded at every replay (negative control: without restoring it, the mixing check refuses the result).
- `TestCompat`: every `LoadFormat` member is accepted or refused with its reason.
- GPU (`test_paged_experts_kernels.py`): the store's constructor change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same machine as #42557: RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB, 62 GB RAM, PCIe 5.0 NVMe, `--paged-experts-num-resident auto --max-total-tokens 10240`, page caches dropped before every start, base and this PR alternating twice. `load_model` is the model loader's wall time, swap the most swap in use during the start, decode `1000 / median TPOT` over 8 ShareGPT prompts (256 output tokens, after 2 discarded warm-up requests).

| model | `load_model` base / this PR | swap at start, base / this PR | decode tok/s, base / this PR | TTFT p50, base / this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-NVFP4 | 352.1, 176.6 / 128.3, 125.5 s | 25.6, 19.1 / 0.2, 0.2 GB | 101.6, 100.7 / 102.6, 100.3 | 231, 220 / 192, 192 ms |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 | 33.5, 33.0 / 45.4\*, 34.1 s | 0.2 / 0.2 GB | 233.6, 233.2 / 233.7, 233.4 | 41, 40 / 40, 40 ms |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 | 52.1, 51.3 / 53.1, 53.1 s | 0.2 / 0.2 GB | 105.0, 105.0 / 105.1, 105.1 | 183, 182 / 182, 183 ms |

On Qwen3-Next the base's start time varies 2x with how much it swaps; this PR does not swap. On the 30B models nothing swaps, and this PR's start is 1-2 s slower than the base: replaying every expert's load into the K rows costs about that much more than the base's direct loads (the page-out of the replayed pages runs on a thread of its own and is off the critical path). \*3 of 7 GPTQ starts of this PR in three runs (none of 7 base starts) spent ~10 s more in the safetensors weights iterator, the part of the load this PR does not change; the other four took 34.1-34.6 s.

Decode is unchanged (the slots and the store hold the same bytes); on Qwen3-Next the base's TTFT is higher because it serves with part of its process in swap.

## CI

The unit tests run on CPU (`base-a-test-cpu`, estimate raised from 5 to 20 s: 18.7 s measured, most of it imports). The end-to-end test (`test/registered/e2e/moe/test_paged_experts.py`) is unchanged; its classes now load through the waiting loads.
