title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] moe: Release localized Mega MoE originals so KV capacity matches non-localized
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_LOCALIZE=1` (#47976), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash loads 1.5 GB more weight memory (89.18 vs 87.65 GB) and gets 1.47% fewer KV tokens, although the routed experts keep a single copy.

A memory snapshot at the end of loading shows where it goes:
- `build_mega_moe_experts_weights` interleaves the L1 weight (a 1.05 GiB temporary) before it interleaves the L1 scale and builds both UTCCP scales. Those scale tensors are carved out of the freed temporary's segment and keep it reserved: one 1080 MiB segment is left with 877.5 MiB free, held by four scale tensors. The non-localized path has the same hole, but the fused shared expert's interleaved L1 copies (40 × 22.5 MiB, built later) fill it. With localization those copies move into locality-domain memory, so the hole stays.
- The fused shared expert's L2 is held twice: `deep_gemm.localize` copies it and `down_proj.weight` keeps the original.

## Modifications

- `build_mega_moe_experts_weights`: builds the scales before the L1 weight interleave. When localized, frees the replaced weights and calls `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` per layer, so the next layer's scales do not land in them.
- `build_mega_moe_shared_weights`: when localized, frees the shared expert's `gate_up_proj` / `down_proj` weights (localized weights have no non-mega fallback) and calls `torch.cuda.empty_cache()`.
- `autotune_prefill_kernels`: skips linears whose weight was freed.

## Memory and accuracy

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, one node, DP-attention 4 / EP 4, `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`, DSPARK, `--mem-fraction-static 0.76`, sgl-deep-gemm v0.2.5.post3 built with CUDA 13.4, `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=16384`. Rank 0. Measured on the #47976 branch plus this commit (the code this PR touches is unchanged on main).

| | Localize | Weights (GB) | Draft weights (GB) | Available before KV pool (GB) | KV tokens | GSM8K (200) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | off | 87.65 | 2.66 | 179.58 | 98,056,960 | 0.995 |
| main | on | 89.18 | 2.85 | 178.36 | 96,620,032 | 0.990 |
| this PR | off | 87.45 | 2.67 | 179.77 | 98,282,240 | 0.995 |
| this PR | on | 88.06 | 2.14 | 179.69 | 98,187,776 | 0.995 |
| this PR | on, EPLB (32 redundant experts, rebalance every 100 iterations, `SGLANG_EXPERT_LOCATION_UPDATER_CANARY=1`) | 101.68 | 1.65 | 165.26 | 81,701,888 (main: 80,294,912) | 1.000, 12 rebalances |

Localized KV capacity goes from -1.47% to -0.10% of non-localized. The reordering also helps the non-localized path (+0.23% KV tokens).

What remains: the freed shared-expert originals sit in loader segments shared with live weights, so only part of them returns to the driver (the draft model reuses some of it). Allocating them in their own segments would need a loader change.

## Not covered

- Decode / prefill speed (the kernels and their inputs are unchanged).

title: [Perf] spec: Default `SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC` to `init`
author: nvpohanh
body:
## Motivation

`SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC` defaults to `all`: on every speculative step, rank 0 broadcasts its draft, plan, accept, and target decisions to the TP group (#33614), `gamma + 3` small broadcasts per DSpark decode step. They guard against TP ranks committing different tokens and then deadlocking in a collective.

The divergence they guard against has a root cause, fixed in #38565: the top-p / top-k renorm kernels summed with float atomics, so ranks renormalizing identical logits could differ in the last bits, and a sampling coin landing in that gap committed different tokens. With every broadcast off, the old kernels hung in every run of #38565's repro and the deterministic ones never diverged. Since #38565, renorm is bit-identical across ranks at `tp_size > 1`, so every per-step decision is computed alike on every rank (identical logits, counter-based draft / rejection noise keyed by the server seed, and the torch RNG seeded alike on every rank). The per-step broadcasts now only cost time, and deployments turn them off by hand (`SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC=rng,-dspark-accept-sample`).

## Modifications

- `SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC` defaults to `init`. Only the two startup memory probes stay synced (`dspark-mem`, `dflash-mem`): free memory differs per rank and decides which draft CUDA graphs are captured, so it stays reduced to the group minimum. Every per-step site is off. The mechanism, presets, and sites are unchanged; `all` restores the previous behavior and is the first thing to try if TP ranks still diverge.
- The broadcast sites are logged at startup only when `SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC` is set, so a default launch no longer warns.
- `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` stays safe under the new default: since #48298 its draws come from a server-seeded generator, so ranks agree without the accept broadcast.
- Model overrides that set the variable themselves (MiniMax-M3.1 DSpark: `rng`) are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

No change in what is computed: a broadcast that is now skipped copied values every rank already held.

- DSpark smoke at TP=2 with the variable unset, overlap scheduling on (`Qwen/Qwen3-14B` + `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_14b_block7`, flags of `test_basic_sanity_dspark.py`, conc 32, 512 in / 512 out):

| sampling | requests (reqs) | succeeded (reqs) | accept length |
|---|---|---|---|
| greedy | 128 | 128 | 4.46 |
| temperature 1.0 | 256 | 256 | 4.15 |
| temperature 0.7, top_p 0.95, top_k 20 | 256 | 256 | 4.22 |
| temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 | 1024 | 1024 | 4.18 |

`/health_generate` answered after every run; no watchdog, NCCL timeout, or traceback in the server logs. Simulated acceptance with the per-step sites off is covered in #48298.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured separately: the default drops the per-step speculative broadcasts (`gamma + 3` per DSpark decode step).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Only the `SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC` comment in `environ.py` changes.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Test] [NPU] deepseek_v4: Replace 8K perf case with 128K 1P1D case and add L2 host hit-rate checks
author: YZY00Raiser
body:
## Motivation

Replace 8K perf case with 128K 1P1D case, and adds an L2 host hit-rate assertion to the DSV4-Flash and DSV4-Pro accuracy tests.

## Modifications

- Added `test/registered/npu/performance/deepseek_v4_flash/test_npu_deepseek_v4_flash_w8a8_1p1d_16p_in128k_out1k_prefix90_20ms.py`
  - New nightly perf case `TestNPUDeepSeekV4FlashW8A81P1D16PIn128kOut1k20ms`, registered via `register_npu_ci(est_time=3600, suite="", nightly=True)`.
  - 1P1D PD-separation with 16 NPUs per node: prefill `--tp-size 16 --dp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy zigzag`; decode `--tp-size 16 --dp-size 16 --enable-dp-attention`. DeepEP (`normal` on prefill, `low_latency` on decode), `modelslim` W8A8 quantization, `dsv4` attention backend, bf16 KV cache, `--enable-metrics --enable-cache-report` on both nodes.
  - Prefill serving config: `--page-size 128`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.62`, `--max-prefill-tokens 70000`, `--chunked-prefill-size 32768`, `--disable-cuda-graph`, `--optimistic-prefill-attempts 1`, `--load-balance-method round_robin`.
  - Decode serving config: `--page-size 128`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.71`, `--swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.05`, `--cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 3 4 6 7 8 10`, `--load-balance-method round_robin`.
  - Both nodes pass `--json-model-override-args '{"use_index_cache":true,"index_topk_freq":2}'` and `--tokenizer-worker-num 16`; prefill additionally sets `--expert-distribution-recorder-mode stat --expert-distribution-recorder-buffer-size 512`; the router uses `--policy cache_aware`.
  - Decode enables DSPARK speculative decoding: `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK`, 6 draft tokens, `--speculative-dspark-block-size 5`; the draft model is the same DSV4-Flash-0731 W8A8 checkpoint (`modelslim` quantization, `ascend` attention backend).
  - Prefill uses `--init-expert-location expert-layout-ais-replicas16.json` together with `--ep-num-redundant-experts 16` and `--ep-dispatch-algorithm dynamic`.
  - Prefill and decode use separate env sets (DeepEP buffer sizes, WAR barrier, multi-stream, etc.).
  - Workload: `generated-shared-prefix`, 90 prompts, `input_len` 131072, `output_len` 1024, `repeat_rate` 0.9, `max_concurrency` 55, `request_rate` 3, `seed` 1, `random_range_ratio` 1, `warmup_requests` 16, `benchmark_tool = BENCHMARK_TOOL_DEFAULT`.
- Added `test/registered/npu/performance/deepseek_v4_flash/expert-layout-ais-replicas16.json`: `physical_to_logical_map` with 43 rows x 272 columns, consumed by `--init-expert-location` and used with 16 redundant expert replicas.
- Updated `.github/workflows/nightly-test-npu.yml`: the DSV4-Flash W8A8 1P1D 16P perf entry is renamed from `deepseek_v4_flash_w8a8_1p1d_16p_in8k_out1k_50ms` to `deepseek_v4_flash_w8a8_1p1d_16p_in128k_out1k_20ms`, and its `test_case` now points to the new `..._in128k_out1k_prefix90_20ms.py`.
- Removed `test/registered/npu/performance/deepseek_v4_flash/test_npu_deepseek_v4_flash_w8a8_1p1d_16p_in8k_out1k_50ms.py`, which is superseded by the long-context case.
- Extended the GPQA PD-separation accuracy jobs with an L2 host cache hit-rate check:
  - `test/registered/npu/accuracy/deepseek_v4_flash/test_npu_deepseek_v4_flash_0731_w8a8_1p1d_16p_gpqa.py` (`test_npu_deepseek_v4_flash_0731_w8a8_1p1d_16p_l2_host_hit_rate`)
  - `test/registered/npu/accuracy/deepseek_v4_pro/test_npu_deepseek_v4_pro_0813_w4a8_1p1d_32p_gpqa.py` (`test_npu_deepseek_v4_pro_0813_w4a8_1p1d_32p_l2_host_hit_rate`)
  - Both reuse the deployment already launched by the accuracy case (`self.host` / `self.port`, model path from `model_config`), so no extra server launch is needed.
  - Each runs a 32K `generated-shared-prefix` bench via `run_bench_serving`: 3 groups x 32 prompts, `input_len` 32000, `output_len` 1024, `max_concurrency` 32, `seed` 100, `warmup_requests` 16, `cache_report=True`.
  - `min_hit_rate_pcts = {"host": 0}` is checked by `assert_metrics`, which asserts strictly greater than 0% and fails if the host tier line is missing (e.g. cache report not enabled).
  - The workload shares a 28800-token system prompt (32K x 0.9) plus a 3200-token question, which exceeds L1 so evictions land in L2.

## Accuracy Tests

The existing GPQA accuracy assertions are unchanged. Both GPQA PD-separation cases now additionally require a non-zero L2 host cache hit rate on the 32K GSP workload described above, so a regression in host-side prefix caching fails the nightly accuracy job.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The new perf case runs the 128K/1K shared-prefix workload described above. Baselines and the effective assertion bounds applied by `assert_metrics` are:

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] moe: Add L4 Triton fused MoE configs for Qwen3-30B-A3B
author: shijie-lyu
body:
## Motivation

There are no fused MoE Triton configs for the NVIDIA L4 (AWS g6) yet, so MoE models on L4 run with the default kernel heuristic (`Using default MoE kernel config. Performance might be sub-optimal!`). This adds tuned configs for Qwen3-30B-A3B, which fits on 2x L4 in FP8 and 4x L4 in bf16.

## Modifications

Two new files in `configs/triton_3_8_0/`:

- `E=128,N=384,device_name=NVIDIA_L4,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128, 128].json`: Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 at TP2
- `E=128,N=192,device_name=NVIDIA_L4.json`: Qwen3-30B-A3B (bf16) at TP4

`N` is `768 / tp`. Other models with the same expert shape (e.g. Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B, Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B) use the same files, but I only measured Qwen3-30B-A3B. FP8 at TP4 isn't valid for this model (192 isn't a multiple of the 128 block), and bf16 TP8 (`N=96`) isn't covered here. There's no `_down` file, so the down projection reuses the up config (the server logs `reusing the tuned up-projection config without TMA`), as #47070 and #46731 do.

Generated with the default search space and batch sizes:

```
python benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton/tuning_fused_moe_triton.py --model Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 --tp-size 2 --dtype fp8_w8a8 --tune
python benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton/tuning_fused_moe_triton.py --model Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --tp-size 4 --tune
```

Setup: 4x NVIDIA L4 (g6.12xlarge), torch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0, sglang at 23c6442cde. Tuning and the kernel numbers below ran on driver kernel module 595.91.07; the end-to-end and accuracy runs ran on 595.112.07. Both arms of each comparison ran on the same driver. There is no `NVIDIA_L4` file in any `triton_*` folder today, so the default arm is what L4 users get now.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K with sgl-eval 0.1.3, one run per arm:

```
sgl-eval run gsm8k --num-examples 1319 --temperature 0.7 --top-p 0.8 --max-tokens 2048 --seed 42 --chat-template-kwarg enable_thinking=false
```

| | default | tuned |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8, TP2 | 95.22% | 95.30% |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B, TP4 | 94.77% | 94.62% |

That is +1 and -2 questions out of 1319, within the noise of a single sampled run (one standard error is about ±0.6 points).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**End to end.** Fresh server per run, 3 runs per arm, alternating default and tuned. The default arm points `SGLANG_MOE_CONFIG_DIR` at an empty config tree and the tuned arm at the new files; every server log was checked for the expected config line.

```
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 --tp 2 --mem-fraction-static 0.85
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --tp 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.85
python -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 \
  --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 200 --max-concurrency 32 --seed 42
```

Concurrency 32 (medians of 3):

| | output tok/s | median TPOT | median TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|
| FP8 TP2, default | 381.7 | 69.2 ms | 2.77 s |
| FP8 TP2, tuned | **393.7 (+3.2%)** | **66.6 ms** | 2.78 s |
| bf16 TP4, default | 408.0 | 64.0 ms | 2.83 s |
| bf16 TP4, tuned | **420.1 (+3.0%)** | **62.0 ms** | 2.81 s |

At concurrency 32, every tuned run beat every default run on output throughput and TPOT, for both models.

Concurrency 1 (16 prompts, same lengths), median TPOT: FP8 TP2 11.17 → 10.77 ms (-3.6%), bf16 TP4 9.65 → 9.62 ms (no change).

**Kernel.** The tuning script without `--tune`, median of 3 runs per arm, in microseconds. For M=1 and 2 the weights the kernel reads (about 19 and 38 MB) fit in the L4's 48 MB L2, and the script replays the same inputs, so the FP8 1.50x/1.48x at M=1 and 2 overstates the gain (at M=4 the working set leaves L2 and the time jumps to about 290 us in both arms). The concurrency-1 numbers above are the better guide for small batches.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] moe: Re-land the JIT moe_finalize_fuse_shared with the shared row read after the PDL wait
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> (auto generated by Claude)
> (auto generated by MyGO (Make your GPU-kernel Optimal) agent)

## What

Re-lands #47784 (the JIT `moe_finalize_fuse_shared`, reverted by #47994) with one fix: the shared-expert row is now read after `PDLWaitPrimary`. The routing tensors still load before the wait when `routing_ready=True`. It also drops the device guard #47784 added around the launch.

cc @hnyls2002 @BBuf

## Why the revert happened

#47994 suspected the early `shared_output` load, and that is the cause. `shared_output` is written by the shared expert on `alt_stream` and joined with `wait_stream` before the finalize. In a CUDA graph, that cross-stream join into a PDL launch is a programmatic edge as well, so a shared expert that triggers its dependents early lets the finalize start before the row is written. Only the PDL wait orders it.

Reproduced on B300 with a shared-expert stand-in on a side stream that triggers at entry and spins 300 us before writing, joined with `wait_stream`, followed by the PDL finalize:

| kernel | eager | CUDA graph | eager, PDL writer | CUDA graph, PDL writer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #47784 | 0/20 wrong | 0/20 | 0/20 | 20/20 wrong |
| this PR | 0/20 | 0/20 | 0/20 | 0/20 |

The reproduction needs a purpose-built early-triggering writer kernel, so it is not added as a registered test.

## Performance

B300, hidden 7168, top-k 8, bf16 with fp32 weights, CUDA graph behind a real PDL producer that triggers before its final stores. Finalize cost = pair time minus producer-only time, medians of 2 x 15 replays.

| | this PR vs #47784 | this PR vs the pre-#47784 kernel on main |
|---|---|---|
| warm (the shared row was just written, in L2) | within +-0.04 us at 1-8192 tokens | 1 token -0.65 us, 32-128 tokens -1.5 to -2.9 us, 4096-8192 tokens equal |
| cold (rotated buffers) | +0.12 / +0.23 us at 64 / 128 tokens, about 0 elsewhere | 32-128 tokens -2.6 to -6.5 us |
| without PDL | about 0 | |

Issuing the shared load right after the wait is as fast as or faster than issuing it in use order (after the gathers): for one-wave grids ptxas places it after the gathers either way, and the persistent kernel is up to 0.6 us faster with the early issue.

## Tests

`test_moe_finalize_fuse_shared.py` on B300: 132 passed, 6 skipped (unchanged from #47784). SASS: the shared `LDG.E.128` is after the grid-dependency wait; no stack or spills in any instance.

Needs before merge: `/rerun-test` of the nightly `test_dsa_glm52_hisparse.py` on 8-gpu-b200, which caught the regression and is not part of the per-PR runs.

title: [Perf] dsv4: Expand the low-ratio indexer page table in one Triton kernel
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

In a DSv4.1 DEP16 decode trace with DSpark verify (bs 256 per rank), building the indexer metadata for the ratio-1 and ratio-2 layers ran a chain of torch ops for each ratio: int64 cast, multiply, broadcast add of an arange, and a cast back to int32. All of them ran at the full expanded width, `[1024, 2049 * blocks_per_page]`. Together they took about 67 µs per step.

## Modifications

- `expand_index_page_table` (`dsv4/metadata.py`) sends GPU tables with unit column stride and a power-of-two `blocks_per_page` to the existing Triton kernel in `attn_glue_hip.py`. That kernel writes the int32 table in one launch and matches the torch expression bit for bit. Other inputs keep the torch path.
- `test_dsv41_decode_glue_hip.py::test_expand_index_page_table` used `expand_index_page_table` as its reference. After this change it would compare the Triton kernel with itself, so its reference now runs the torch expression on CPU.
- `test_fp4_indexer.py::test_expand_index_page_table_matches_cpu` (CUDA) covers the CUDA dispatch, which the gfx95-gated HIP file does not. It compares the GPU result with the CPU torch path, on a contiguous and a row-strided table.

## Accuracy Tests

Output is bitwise identical. A standalone check on one GPU compared the Triton kernel with the previous torch expression using `torch.equal` on these inputs:
- `[1024, 2049]` with `blocks_per_page` 4 and 2
- `[256, 2049]`, `[3, 17]`, `[1, 300]` and an empty table
- a row-strided table
- `-1` entries and int32 edge values (`2^31 - 1`, `-2^31`, `2^30`)

All matched. `test_expand_index_page_table_matches_cpu` passes on a B300 (5/5).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Each call was captured in a CUDA graph and replayed 200 times, in A/B/A/B order. Times include the graph-replay overhead.

| shape | blocks_per_page | before (µs) | after (µs) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[1024, 2049]` | 4 (ratio 1) | 40.9 / 41.1 | 7.1 / 7.2 |
| `[1024, 2049]` | 2 (ratio 2) | 25.0 / 26.7 | 7.3 / 7.1 |

That is about 67 → 14 µs per decode step at bs 256. Prefill and the sparse-candidate table use the same function, so they benefit too. These numbers come from running the operation alone; end-to-end step time was not measured.

title: [Perf] dsv4: dequantize several KV tokens per program in the V4.1 paged dequant
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

`dequantize_k_cache_paged_v41` (the DeepSeek-V4.1 paged KV dequant used before sparse prefill) launches one 128-thread program per token. On SMs that hold 16 resident blocks and 1024 threads (CC 10.7 / sm_107), the programs are too small to keep enough loads in flight, and the kernel reaches a small fraction of HBM bandwidth. The fp4 kernel also writes each token's 512 bf16 values with two stride-2 stores.

## Modifications

- `_dequantize_k_cache_paged_v41_fp8_kernel` and `_dequantize_k_cache_paged_v41_fp4_kernel` take `num_tokens` and a `TOKENS_PER_PROGRAM` constexpr. Each program dequantizes that many tokens as a `[TOKENS_PER_PROGRAM, 512]` tile and masks the tail.
- The fp4 kernel interleaves the low and high nibbles with `tl.interleave` and writes each token with one contiguous store.
- Every backend launches 8 tokens per program with 2 warps. Only CUDA was measured; on gfx950 the same launch is untested (the dequant test is CUDA-only).

The math per element is unchanged, so outputs are bitwise identical.

## Accuracy Tests

On sm_107 (CC 10.7), at this PR's head:

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsv4_dequant_k_cache.py`: 3 passed (5 subtests).
- This PR's kernels against main's, bitwise, on random caches with finite scales: V41, V41_NEW, V41_FP4 and V41_FP4_NEW, page size 64 and 256, 1 / 7 / 9 / 16,896 / 262,144 tokens (the small counts exercise the masked tail). All identical.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

sm_107 (CC 10.7), one GPU, kineto median of 20 calls, time relative to main:

| layout | tokens | this PR vs main |
|---|---|---|
| V41 (fp8) | 16,896 | -62% |
| V41 (fp8) | 262,144 | -80% |
| V41_FP4 | 16,896 | -37% |
| V41_FP4 | 262,144 | -69% |

In a DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill step at 16K new tokens per rank, these kernels are about 0.9% of the summed kernel time. The saving depends on how many tokens each call dequantizes. No end-to-end run is claimed.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the pre-commit hooks.

title: [Perf] dsv4: four chunks per thread in mega MoE pre-dispatch for prefill-sized batches
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

#47149 made `mega_moe_pre_dispatch` launch 320-thread CTAs with two 16B chunks per thread on SMs that hold 1024 resident threads (CC 10.7 / sm_107), since two 640-thread CTAs do not fit. That PR measured decode-sized batches. At prefill-sized batches (thousands of rows) the kernel is still launch-bound: one CTA per token, three resident per SM.

## Modifications

- `mega_moe_pre_dispatch.cuh`: add a four-chunks-per-thread instantiation (160-thread CTAs for hidden 5120). It is used when the two-chunk launch already applies (1024-thread SMs), `num_chunks` is a multiple of 128, `top_k <= num_chunks / 4`, and `num_tokens >= 6 x SM count`.
- Below that row count, and on 2048-thread SMs, the launch is unchanged. The cutoff comes from the sweep below: four chunks lose 3-16% at 424-1024 rows and win from about 1.3K rows up.

Outputs are bitwise identical (FP8 bytes, scales, shared-SF layout, top-k copies and padding).

## Accuracy Tests

On sm_107 (CC 10.7), at this PR's head:

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_mega_moe_pre_dispatch.py`: 6 passed.
- This PR against its parent at 198, 342, 1024, 1272, 4096 and 16384 rows: all outputs bitwise identical.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

sm_107 (CC 10.7), one GPU, hidden 5120, top_k 6, 4 calls per CUDA graph, ABBA-interleaved replays, median time per call relative to the parent (hot = one buffer set, cold = rotated):

| rows | this PR vs parent, hot | cold |
|---|---|---|
| 198 | -2.9% | +5.5% |
| 342 | -4.3% | +4.4% |
| 1024 | +2.3% | 0.0% |
| 1272 | -3.9% | -14.3% |
| 4096 | -11.4% | -18.6% |
| 16384 | -23.9% | -24.1% |

Rows at or below 1024 take the same kernel as the parent, so their differences are run-to-run spread. DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill at 16K tokens per rank calls this kernel once per MoE layer at 16384 rows. No end-to-end number is claimed.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the pre-commit hooks.
- [ ] Add unit tests (the four-chunk path only runs on 1024-thread SMs; covered by the bitwise comparison above).
- [ ] Update documentation as needed.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (kernel level).

title: [Perf] deep_select: use the 3-CTA tier for non-paged bf16 top-512 too
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

#47328 added a 3-CTA-per-SM config for bf16 top-512 and switches to it when it needs fewer rounds than the 2-CTA config. It is built only for the page-transform path. The non-paged ragged calls, such as the DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill indexer top-k (thousands of rows, 64K-131K columns, per-row ends and offsets), never get it.

## Modifications

- `deep_select.py`: build the 3-CTA config for every bf16 top-512 module except `sorted_index`, instead of only for `page_transform`. The C++ rounds-based switch from #47328 then picks it whenever it needs fewer rounds.
- `test_deep_select.py`: `test_denser_tier_with_end_and_offset` runs the 3-CTA config without a page table, with ragged ends and per-row output offsets.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_deep_select.py` on sm_107 (CC 10.7) with the module-level skip forced off (`is_deep_select_supported()` does not list CC 10.7): 17 passed, including the new test.
- Benchmark inputs below: the selected index sets are identical to the parent's.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

sm_107 (CC 10.7), one GPU, bf16 logits, k = 512, ragged ends, 2 calls per CUDA graph, kineto median, time relative to the parent:

title: [Fix] test: Import sgl_kernel in the Xeon thread-binding test
author: leejnau
body:
## Motivation

On main, PR Test (Xeon) fails `test/registered/cpu/test_binding.py` in `build-test (xeon-gnr, gnr, stage-a-tp-test-cpu-intel, gnr)`. Every PR whose run reaches that job fails too:

```
AttributeError: '_OpNamespace' 'sgl_kernel' object has no attribute 'init_cpu_threads_env'
✗ FAILED: /sglang-checkout/test/registered/cpu/test_binding.py returned exit code 1
```

The test calls `torch.ops.sgl_kernel` but never imports `sgl_kernel`. It relied on the `sglang` import chain loading the op library as a side effect, and #47731 removed that. The Arm64 MoE test broke the same way (#48221, fixed by #48223).

Evidence:
- **Main fails it.** [Run 41738971626](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41738971626/job/126276036425) (`a4bef204c5`, 11-03 23:25) failed. Only `test_binding.py` failed: the TP server tests in the same suite, and both SPR jobs, passed.
- **It started with #47731.** The last GNR runs on main that completed passed on 11-01, from `0f93be7b65` to `240f2a0a64`. #47731 merged on 11-02 at 21:51, and every GNR run in between was cancelled. Later "green" Xeon runs on main skipped `build-test` entirely, via `check-changes`.
- **It's the only file left.** Across `test/registered/`, the only tests that use `torch.ops.sgl_kernel` without importing `sgl_kernel` are this one and the Arm64 `test_moe.py`, which #48223 covers.

## Modifications

Add `import sgl_kernel  # noqa: F401` to `test/registered/cpu/test_binding.py`. This is how `test/registered/cpu/test_moe.py` and the other CPU tests do it.

Production code isn't affected. `srt/distributed/bootstrap.py` calls the same op, but server launches load `sgl_kernel` some other way, as the passing server tests in the same jobs show.

## Testing

pre-commit passes. I have no Xeon machine, so this needs PR Test (Xeon) to actually run the GNR `build-test` job, via `run-ci` or a CPU-mode `/rerun-test test/registered/cpu/test_binding.py`.

title: [Fix] spec: Draw `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` once per step from the server seed
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Under `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`, DSpark draws each step's forced correct length and bonus seed once, in `TargetVerifyExecutor.begin_simulated_step`, from a generator seeded by the server seed. The graph path's seed buffer is filled there, `begin_sim_bonus` no longer draws, and the eager path takes the same seed. Every TP rank draws the same values whatever else reads the process RNG.
- The `simulated_bonus_sample` op, whose only job was drawing that seed from the process RNG, is removed; its one caller passes the step's seed to `simulated_bonus_sample_graph`. The top-k / top-p simulated bonus stays a `torch.multinomial` draw, on the CUDA RNG that every rank's sampled accept already shares.
- DFlash draws its forced length from the same kind of generator. It overwrites `accept_len` after the accept broadcast, so the forced length was never synced across TP ranks, even with `SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC=all`.
- `simulated_acc_len_generator` moves unchanged from `eagle_post_verify_graphs.py` to `spec_utils.py`, shared by EAGLE, DFlash, and DSpark.
- Test: two ranks that consume the process RNG a different number of times stage the same draws, at both draw points (DSpark, DFlash).
- DSpark TP=2 (`Qwen/Qwen3-14B` + `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_14b_block7`) with `SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC=init` and `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3`: 512 sampled requests, accept length 3.00, no hang.

No behavior change outside `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`; with it set, the simulated lengths and temperature-only bonus seeds keep their distribution but follow a different sequence.

title: [Refactor] kernels/diffusion/tests: Prune new dead code and make silently skipped tests run
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation This is the second pass of #44690. Three weeks after that PR, `python/sglang/kernels` had gained another 66K lines, `python/sglang/multimodal_gen` 43K and `test/registered` 162K. This PR removes what in that code is dead or redundant. More importantly, it fixes the places where CI is green without testing anything, and the runtime bugs found along the way. **433 files, +5,551 / −13,052.** - About 1.4K of the additions are tests moved to `test/manual/`, because no CI runner has the hardware or package they need. - About 0.8K are shared test helpers that replace copies. ## Bugs fixed (please review these first) | Area | Problem | Fix | |---|---|---| | Kernel CI | `base-b-kernel-unit-test-8-gpu-h200` has no registered test. On every kernel PR and three times a day it books an 8×H200 runner, installs everything, and logs `No tests found`. | Matrix row and suite removed. | | Kernel CI | Tests registered on lanes whose hardware never satisfies their skip gate. The production kernels behind them had no CI at all. | Registered on hardware that runs them, and each was run there:
• SM120 FlashMLA fallback (`Ran 15; skipped=15` on H100)
• Blackwell FP4 indexer quant (36 of 39 cases skipped)
• Q8KV8 sparse prefill (25 cases)
• FlashInfer KDA prefill graph and input pack
• SM100 Mamba stochastic rounding
• the FA3 extend-init regression
• KDA MTP slot stride
• Gemma4 Blackwell sampling split
• gfx950-only kernels on the MI300 lane
• diffusion FA4 `forward_into`
• SubBlock sm100/sm120 kernels (one case skipped on sm_100, see below)
• 4-rank and 2-rank diffusion cases on 1-GPU lanes | | Q8KV8 sparse prefill | Once the Blackwell cases ran, 15 of them failed on main. #45909 packed each request's compressed history contiguously and updated the H100 cases, but nobody ran the Blackwell cases, so their expected offsets stayed stale. Their output-vs-paged-attention assertion passes. | Registration and expectation fix land together; 37 passed on sm_103. | | Kernel tests | `test_kpool_topk_transform_fused.py` runs under `unittest.main()`, which drops the module-level pytest functions. 4 of its cases (ties, overfull bins, page-table mapping under graph replay) never ran. | `pytest.main` entry; scanned the kernel tests for the same pattern. | | Kernel tests | Assertions that cannot fail:
• a tensor compared with itself (`test_rmsnorm`);
• an AMD all-reduce "determinism" test with no assert, which only prints ✓/✗ and tests RCCL rather than SGLang;
• `*_jit_vs_aot` comparisons against AOT ops that do not exist (always skipped);
• a MoE wna16 GEMM test that always skipped (it now checks against a dequant reference and runs its 24 cases). | Fixed, or deleted where nothing SGLang-owned was tested. | | Unit tests | Triton kernels tested only from CPU-registered files, so their CUDA cases never ran: `row_logsumexp[_topk]`, `free_unbind_inplace`, `gather_page64_kv_latent`, the token-id translation Triton path. | GPU registrations added (5090). | | Unit tests | Tests of copies of the code instead of the code:
• the decode CUDA-graph profile options (a test-local copy);
• four MoE shared-expert fusion gates asserting only `assertTrue(reason)`, which the CPU early-return satisfies;
• `test_h3_request.py`, which failed 8 of 12 cases when run alone because its ComfyUI stubs had rotted. It passed only if another test happened to import the real module first. | The tests now call the real method and assert each branch's message. The stubs are fixed. | | CI registration | `test_gated_launch.py` used `nightly=True` on a CUDA registration, so no job ever ran it. | Flag removed; it now runs in nightly. `check_registered_tests.py` rejects `nightly=True` on CUDA/CPU. | | CI tooling | `update_est_time.py` matched registrations with a single-line regex. It missed 150 of the 2,459 CUDA/CPU registrations (wrapped, positional, float), so their `est_time` never refreshed. | The literal is found through the AST: 0 missed. | | Diffusion | `--srt-encoder-connection-timeout` was stored under a name that is not a field, so the documented flag (and the one GLM-Image's timeout error recommends) was silently dropped. `type=int` also rejected the documented default 3.05. | `dest=` the field, `type=float`. | | Diffusion VMoBA | The runtime imported `kernel.attn.vmoba_attn.vmoba`, which exists nowhere. The chunk-selection fix in #44286 went into the in-tree copy that nothing imported, and its tests sat outside CI discovery. | The runtime and resolver import the in-tree module. Its tests moved into `multimodal_gen/test/unit`. | | Diffusion `exact` tier | Wan and LingBot fuse Q/K/V into one GEMM unconditionally. At the model shapes it is bit-identical on H200 and GB300. At M ≤ 256, cuBLAS picks split-K and the result differs, so `exact` requests were not bit-identical. Wan's fused RMSNorm+RoPE had no check either. | The QKV fusion is gated at `lossless` (same math, rounding moves), the default tier, so default behavior is unchanged. The norm+RoPE fusion goes through `BitExactFusionGate.run`. | | MiniMax-H3 | The pipelined Ulysses attention never ran its first-call equality check. Enabling the check exposed that the sequential reference left non-zero pad rows that #47566 zeroes, which would have turned the pipeline off. | The reference zeroes the alignment rows (never read downstream); the check runs and passes (`same=1`). | | Registry | `gemm.dsv3_fused_a_gemm` pointed at `sgl_kernel:dsv3_fused_a_gemm`, which does not exist. The namespace test only checked that the module existed. | Spec removed. `test_inventory_targets_resolve` now resolves every target's attribute statically (incl. the AOT package) on the CPU lane. | | CuTe DSL GDN/KDA decode | The wrappers accepted `scale`, `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel`, `softplus_beta` and `softplus_threshold`, then compiled with fixed values. Today's callers pass exactly those values. | Non-matching values raise `ValueError` (+ test). | | ROCm block-FP8 | `use_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_unrolledx4` evaluated its condition without `return`, so production never selected the unrolledx4 kernel. Only the tuner ran it. | Kernel, selector and tuner branch removed. Runtime behavior is unchanged. | | Unlimited-OCR / QK-norm gate | Their PDL probes checked `capability >= 9`, which is true on gfx942/950, so they emitted PDL on ROCm. | `current_arch().supports_pdl`. | ## Modifications ### Kernels (`python/sglang/kernels`, 108 files, −3.1K net) - **Dead code** (each re-checked by whole-repo grep, incl. string targets): - 865 lines of `jit/csrc/moe/expert_specialization/*.cuh` that nothing loads; - ngram decode fast paths that were never wired in, and their benchmarks; - the MuseSpark `router_gemm` JIT kernel (the model only uses its token limit); - the test-only TextSeal standalone selector; - two unused LoRA MoE custom ops; - LPLB shmem helpers, `row_argmax` and `create_argmax_workspace`; - the f32x2 helpers left by a reverted PR; - `finish_flat_indexer_topk`; - the `small_field_copy` descriptor path; - an unloadable LoRA plans table; - losing `mla_qk_prep` variants (the default path is byte-identical on H200 and GB300 over 64 cases); - unused `use_tma`/`topk`/`config` parameters; - the MuseSpark softmax routing branches; - aliases, constants and re-exports nothing uses. - **Classification** (#45112 rules): - `engram_gather_peer` (peer-memory read) → `communication`. - MSA-v1 `compact_dequant` (KV-cache gather + dequant) → `kvcache`. - The two diffusion op ids that targeted quantization/activation modules are renamed to their real groups; their facade re-exports are gone. - `qwen_moe_topk_output` moves to its only caller in `qwen2_moe.py`. - The gfx1250 per-token FP8 quant → `quantization`. - **Arch queries:** about 15 sites that still probed the device by hand now use `sglang.kernels.arch` (#47782) with the same semantics. `argmax`/`softmax` JIT adopt `max_vec_bytes`. Import-time device-0 probes moved to call time. - **Dedups:** - the gfx950 gluon MoE helpers (identical AMDGCN for all 68 cases); - the hipcc compile-and-load block; - the SM90 FP8 CuTeDSL LoRA class, now a subclass of its BF16 sibling (bit-exact on H200); - the gfx950 vattn HIP binding. - **Env:** raw `os.environ` reads in kernels/models are declared in `environ.py` with the same names and defaults. Two settings are removed: - `SGLANG_HIP_MHC_BOUNDARY_WIDE_TILE`, a kill switch for a bitwise-identical tile; - `SGLANG_XPU_LN_MOD_NUM_WARPS`, a layout-only setting. - **HiCache:** the page-unified layout is admitted only if both the write-back and the load-back JIT probes pass; until now the load-back probe was never called. - **Docs:** cookbook lines that told users to set env vars nothing reads are removed. ### Diffusion (`python/sglang/multimodal_gen`, 118 files, −1.5K net) - **Dead code:** - 7 disaggregation flags nothing read; - `--mask-strategy-file-path` (sliding-tile attention reads `--attention-backend-config mask_strategy_file_path=...`, and the error now says so); - the `/stats` timeout counter that was always 0; - vestigial `PortArgs` fields that leaked three temp files per construction; - about 25 unused helpers, constants and config fields; - test oracles moved out of runtime modules into the tests. - **Shared helpers:** - four more hand-written verify-once gates use `BitExactFusionGate.run` / `can_attempt` (flux3 video VAE, FLUX.2 XPU, KL-VAE, Qwen-Image-2.1); - Wan and LingBot share one row-packing helper; - the duplicated Nomas helpers, OpenAI image/video/mesh API helpers and flux3's copy of the launcher conditions are merged; - the two disagreeing "unrecoverable device error" classifiers are now one. - **Docs:** - `--enable-attention-backend-autotune` was documented but not a CLI flag; it is now one. - `ring_sp_performance.mdx` documented a flag that does not exist; it now uses the real `--kv-gather-degree`. ### Tests and CI - **Deleted:** - tautologies (argparse pass-through, default and constant echoes, `inspect.getsource`/AST source tests, mock-the-SUT, torch-math); - duplicate cases and files; - benchmarks of test-local copies; - always-skipped tests; - `#47603` leftovers (dead model lists, a test that `return`s in CI); - tests with a hard-coded developer path. - **Merged** copy-pasted fakes, fixtures and oracles into `python/sglang/test/` helpers. Two test classes were collected twice through imports (45 extra runs per CPU job). - **Trimmed grids** with no coverage gain: page-unified dtype sweep (252 → 168 cases), MiniMax decode top-k (144 → 48). - **Faster CPU gate:** - `test_runtime_context.py`: 132 s → 13 s; - `test_flashinfer_autotune_sync.py`: 30 s → 10 s; - three one-purpose files merged. - **Moved to `test/manual/`:** tests that need NCCL ≥ 2.31.2, a private checkpoint, an unset env var, or 4 GPUs of a manual-only class; plus a benchmark CLI that lived in a registered test. - **CI:** - the empty 8-GPU XPU nightly job is removed; - stale suite names, globs and `rerun_test_groups` entries are removed; - the Muse Spark HF token follows the runner, not the stage; - `comfy-kitchen` (no deps) is installed for the diffusion unit/B200 jobs, so its three tests stop skipping. ## Behavior changes - Diffusion CLI: - the 7 unused disaggregation flags and `--mask-strategy-file-path` are now rejected; - `--srt-encoder-connection-timeout` takes effect and accepts floats. - Diffusion `exact` requests no longer use the fused QKV GEMM (Wan, LingBot). `lossless` and `high` outputs are byte-identical to main. - HiDream-O1 rejects `--flow-shift`/`--scheduler-class-override`, as it already does for its other fixed settings. HunyuanImage-3 honors a user `--flow-shift` instead of overwriting it. - `/v1/images/edits` returns 400 when `mask` is given; it was silently ignored. - The diffusion client treats `CUDA error:`, `HIP error:` and `torch.AcceleratorError` as unrecoverable, like the worker does. - ROCm: no PDL in the Unlimited-OCR DASH / QK-norm gate kernels. The gfx1250 kpool indexer uses Triton `act_quant`, like the other two DSA paths. - CuTe DSL LoRA prepare: SM120 now gets a clear `NotImplementedError` instead of compiling the SM100 class and failing. - Removed env vars: `SGLANG_HIP_MHC_BOUNDARY_WIDE_TILE`, `SGLANG_XPU_LN_MOD_NUM_WARPS`. Newly declared boolean envs (`SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_FP8_BS`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_LFM_FUSED_CONV`) parse like every other `EnvBool`. ## Left alone (owner decisions, not in this PR) - **AMD/NPU suites no workflow runs:** 55 AMD files (~8.9K lines) and 8 NPU files (~1.5K lines) register suites that no workflow invokes. `run_suite.py` does not validate AMD/NPU suite names. The list is in a comment below. - **Cake softmax on SM100:** since the JIT branch went first (#47512), the Cake softmax can no longer be selected; its input domain is inside the JIT one. - **MiniMax-H3 4-GPU H100 smoke suite:** `FILE_SUITES["4-gpu-h100"]` has no bridge file and no workflow, so its three cases never run. - **Code waiting on #46693:** the gfx950 kernels from #46690–#46692 that #46693 wires. - **Auto-residency probe:** unreachable since #45979 ("until a planner consumes it"). - **SubBlock ragged tail on sm_100:** `TestSubBlockNumerics::test_ragged_tail_reproduces_dense` returns NaN on the B200 lane and passes on sm_103 and sm_120. The kernel is not changed here, so the case is skipped on sm_100 until the tail path is fixed. - **`topk_sigmoid` on ROCm:** every case of `test_moe_topk_sigmoid.py` failed on the MI300 jit-kernel lane, so the test stays CUDA-only. - **`pr-test-sgl-kernel.yml` benchmark loop:** `|| echo` means the job cannot fail. ## Accuracy Tests **Full regression sweep, base (`4c7c775c`) vs this branch, same box.** Each test file runs in its own pytest process. Failing test ids are compared: | Box | Files | Test ids failing only on this branch | |---|---|---| | H200 (sm_90) | `test/registered/kernels/ops` (448), `test/registered/unit` (1153), `multimodal_gen/test/unit` (395) | **0** | | GB300 (sm_103) | `test/registered/kernels/ops` (448) | **0** (15 fewer: the Q8KV8 Blackwell cases) | | RTX 5090 (sm_120) | `test/registered/kernels/ops` (448) | **0** (the same 833 pre-existing ids) | The remaining failures are identical on both trees: multi-GPU tests on a 1-GPU box, optional packages missing from the image, and kernels that need hardware the box lacks. **End to end, fixed seed, base vs this branch.** An instrumented run confirmed the fused paths were active on both sides. | Model | Box | Result | |---|---|---| | Wan2.1-1.3B | H200 | `lossless`, `exact` and `high` mp4 byte-identical; fused QKV GEMM active (M=14040); norm+RoPE gate verified | | Wan2.1-14B | GB300 | `lossless` and `exact` byte-identical | | Qwen-Image-2.1 | H200 | byte-identical; 10 DiT gates verified (incl. the converted ones) | | LingBot-World realtime (CI case) | H200 | `exact` and `lossless` raw frames identical; fused GEMM active under `lossless` | | MiniMax-H3 T2VA, Ulysses 2 | GB300 | `lossless` and `exact` byte-identical; pipelined attention first-call check `same=1` | **Kernel dedups, bit-for-bit (`torch.equal` on dumped outputs, base vs branch):** - the CuTeDSL FP8 LoRA class merge, `gelu_and_mul_triton`, MuseSpark routing, argmax and the SM10x JIT softmax: 88 tensors on H200 and 112 on GB300; - `mla_qk_prep`: 64 cases on H200 and GB300; - the gfx950 gluon helper hoist: identical AMDGCN for all 68 cases (372 compiles via Triton's AMD backend). **Lane changes** were run on the hardware of their new lane: - SM120 cases on an RTX 5090; - SM100/SM103 cases on GB300; - H100-lane cases on H200; - the new 4-GPU diffusion cases on 4×GB300. **CI tooling:** - `pre-commit run --from-ref 4c7c775c` passes over the whole range, including the workflow checks. - `check_registered_tests.py` passes; on main it fails, naming the `nightly=True` file. - Suite selection was simulated with `run_suite.filter_tests`, and `compute_partitions.py` gives the same shard counts for pr-test, pr-test-extra, nightly and weekly. - `update_est_time.py` dry run: 1402 updates, up from 1372; the old 1372 keep their values. - The diffusion partition planner reports 0 missing estimates, and both newly scheduled 2-GPU files ran on 2×GB300. - An import walk over `sglang.{kernels,multimodal_gen,srt,test}` finds no new import failures. - After merging main `851642ad`, the 18 test files touched by the newly merged upstream commits pass on main and on this branch. **Not validated:** - true SM100 / B200 (no B200 machine was available; sm_103 stood in for every `major == 10` gate); - ROCm, NPU, XPU and MUSA (those changes are mechanical and import-checked); - the VMoBA CUDA path (FlashAttention 2 is not in the image); - FLUX.3 e2e (gated weights); - HiDream-O1, HunyuanImage-3 and Nomas e2e (unit tests only). ## Speed Tests and Profiling No perf-path changes intended: - Default-tier fused paths are unchanged. - The removed kernels and branches were not selected in production. - The `mla_qk_prep` default variant is byte-identical. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #42123536075](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42123536075) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #42123536315](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42123536315) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #42123536434](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42123536434) > [!TIP] > Base CI only covers the core cases, and its workload may not exercise your change. title: [Refactor] env: Dispatch on the GPU architecture instead of env vars that restate it
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

SGLang declares about 910 environment variables (819 in `srt/environ.py`, 91 in `multimodal_gen/envs.py`) and reads about 115 more raw. Many of them only restate the hardware: a path that is valid on one GPU and must be switched on by hand there, or a kill switch for a path that is already gated by architecture. This PR deletes those and decides at the read site from the GPU itself (`sglang.kernels.arch.current_arch()` / the platform helpers).

Rules used for every variable:

- **Selector that restates the hardware**: deleted; the read site checks the architecture.
- **Kill switch of a default-on, architecture-gated path**: deleted; the path keeps its existing gate. Kept when a doc tells users to set it, or a CI test uses it as the A/B control (listed below).
- **Default-off fast path for one architecture**: only the five with the strongest evidence are turned on: the cookbook already sets them on exactly that hardware, and GSM8K was checked wherever a checkpoint was available. The rest stay opt-in.

Wrong architecture gates and env bugs found during the audit are fixed here too.

**41 variables deleted** (33 declared, 8 read raw); 4 are now declared or read under their documented name.

## Behavior changes (please review these first)

| Area | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4 on gfx950 | `SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM`, `SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_FUSED_INVROPE`, `SGLANG_HIP_DSV4_C4_INDEXER_ROWGROUP` (and `SGLANG_OPT_HIP_FLYDSL_MXFP8` for V4.1) had to be set; every MI355X cookbook cell set them | On by default on gfx95 / gfx950 when the kernel is available. `FUSED_INVROPE` stays an opt-in on CUDA |
| DSA `flashmla_sparse_q8` (SM90) | Per-row top-k length behind `SGLANG_ENABLE_DSA_Q8KV8_TOPK_LENGTH` | Always on (bit-exact by construction: skipped blocks hold only `-1` pads) |
| MiniMax-H3 VAE | The fused residual-add + RMSNorm ran at every quality level, including `exact`, though it is not bit-exact | Runs only at `lossless` / `high`; `exact` output now equals the unfused path byte for byte |
| `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_USE_TENSOR_CORE` | Compared to `"true"`, so `=1` turned tensor cores **off** | Parsed as a boolean; unset keeps the heuristic |
| `SGLANG_FORCE_SHUTDOWN`, `SGLANG_SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP` | Documented under these names, read as `SGL_FORCE_SHUTDOWN` / `SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP`, so the documented name did nothing | Read through `envs`; the old names still work as deprecated aliases |
| `SGLANG_USE_DEEPGEMM_BMM` | `not DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL` let SM120/121 into DeepGEMM's SM90 masked/einsum kernels; dots3 had no gate | Requires SM90 (MUSA keeps its path) |
| MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 native stack | `is_blackwell` (majors 10-12) selected MSA-v1 kernels that build for SM10x only | SM10x only |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 indexer | `major >= 10` sent SM120 into the DeepGEMM `fp8_fp4` path, which raised at build time | SM100 family only; SM120 gets the torch / Triton paths |
| DSA backend | TRT-LLM workspace allocated on SM120, where the kernel raises "Unsupported architecture" | Allocated on SM10x only |
| DeepSeek-V4 model hooks | The ROCm block overwrote 9 variables unconditionally; `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2` on SM120 and `SGLANG_OPT_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PREFILL` on ROCm overwrote user values | Values the user set are kept; sets equal to the default, or for variables nothing reads on that platform, are removed |
| MegaMoE on ROCm | `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe` without `SGLANG_AMD_USE_FLYDSL_MEGA_MOE=1` ran DeepGEMM, which has no ROCm kernels | megamoe on ROCm is aiter MegaMoEv2 |
| DSpark on NPU | Needed `SGLANG_DSPARK_FAST_KERNEL=0` | Chosen by platform |
| smallm router, smallm FP8 block-scale GEMM | Admitted any `gfx95*` | `gfx950` exactly, like the other smallm kernels |
| gfx1250 MXFP4 MoE | Every recipe and test had to set `AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1` | SGLang's own decisions key on gfx1250, and startup sets the variable for aiter on gfx1250 when unset |
| DGX Spark DeepSeek-V4 recipe | Selected the `b12x` FlashMLA backend, which main does not have | Removed from the recipe |

## Deleted variables

**Restate the hardware (decided at the read site)**

| Variable | Now |
|---|---|
| `SGLANG_DEEPGEMM_ON_H20` | SM90 with 78 SMs (H20 / H20-3e) |
| `SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_INDEXER` | `is_hip()` |
| `SGLANG_AMD_USE_FLYDSL_MEGA_MOE` | ROCm + `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe` |
| `SGLANG_DSPARK_FAST_KERNEL` | `not is_npu()` |
| `SGLANG_DSPARK_SHARDED_ACCEPT` | `is_hip()` |
| `SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM`, `SGLANG_OPT_HIP_FLYDSL_MXFP8`, `SGLANG_HIP_DSV4_C4_INDEXER_ROWGROUP`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_DSA_Q8KV8_TOPK_LENGTH` | On for their architecture (table above) |

**Kill switches of default-on, architecture-gated paths (path and gate kept)**

- NVIDIA: `SGLANG_FA4_TMEM_LOAD_RED_MAX`, `SGLANG_HICACHE_TMA_TRANSFER`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_BF16_SPLITK_GEMM`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_MUSE_SPARK_FINALIZE_AR`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_MSA_V1_Q8KV4`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_FP8_GEMM_CONFIG_TUNE`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_MINIMAX_FP8_Q_EPILOGUE`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_LFM_FUSED_CONV`, `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_FAST_DECODE_INDEXER`, `SGLANG_DSV41_FUSED_WO_A`, `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS`, `SGLANG_EXPERIMENTAL_DSA_KPOOL_METADATA_FUSION`
- ROCm: `SGLANG_DISABLE_GFX115_WEIGHT_PADDING`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_SPLITKV_VERIFY`, `SGLANG_TRITON_DENSE_PREFILL_ATTN`, `SGLANG_EXACT_CHUNK_FILL`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_QUARK_MXFP4_MOE_W4A16`, `SGLANG_GFX1250_W4A8_MOE`, `SGLANG_MOE_SHUFFLE_GFX1250`, `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_FP8_PROJ`, `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_ROUTER`, `SGLANG_ROCM_KDA_HIP_PREFILL`, `SGLANG_ASM_VERIFY_ATTN`, `SGLANG_DP_MASK_PAD_ROWS`, `SGLANG_HIP_SHARED_ACT_MXFP8`, `SGLANG_HIP_WO_A_MXFP8`, `SGLANG_HIP_FFN_NORM_MXFP8`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE`

Tests that flipped one of these now patch the gate instead (for example the FA4 sm_103 test builds the FMNMX kernel with `tmem_load_red_max=False`), so no comparison was lost.

**Nothing read them:** `SGLANG_NGRAM_FORCE_GREEDY_VERIFY`, `SGLANG_DATA_PARALLEL_BUDGET_INTERVAL`, `SGLANG_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDA_GRAPH` (written by `--debug-cuda-graph`, never read; the BCG doc now points at `--cuda-graph-backend-decode breakable`).

**Diffusion:** `MINIMAX_H3_VAE_DECODER_FUSED_NORM` (now the quality gate).

## Kept on purpose

- Documented escape hatches / CI A/B controls: `SGLANG_DISABLE_MSA`, `SGLANG_K3_SP_COLLECTIVE`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_FUSED_AR_QUANT`, `SGLANG_AITER_GFX942_BLOCKSCALE_USE_CK`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_GFX1250_FP8_GEMM`, `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_MOE`, `SGLANG_ROCM_DISABLE_AITER_TOPK_GATING`, `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_FP8_BS` (now also gated on gfx950).
- `SGLANG_AITER_CAPTURE_COPY_IN` stays off. #43077 moved it from on to off on purpose and scoped it to the DeepSeek-V4.1 MI355X DP-attention recipe. It is now declared, and its comment no longer says the opposite of the default. On Qwen3-30B-A3B TP4 / DP4 DP-attention on MI350X, turning it on costs about 2.7% output throughput with the same GSM8K.
- The other default-off candidates stay opt-in. The closest to ready are `SGLANG_OPT_SM120_MTP_ROUTER_TOP22` (bit-exact, needs a re-benchmark) and `SGLANG_ENABLE_FP8_BLOCK_GEMV` (needs an H200 accuracy run).

## For the owners (not changed here)

- The DGX Spark DeepSeek-V4 cells are still `verified: true`, but they use the preview image and `--moe-runner-backend b12x`, which main does not have.
- MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 still keys on `is_blackwell` in `model_overrides/minimax_m3.py` and `quantization/minimax_m3_nvfp4.py`, so SM12x end to end is unsupported. This PR only stops SM12x from selecting MSA-v1.
- `single_batch_overlap.py` uses `not is_blackwell()` for the Hopper paths; switching to `is_sm(9)` would change HIP / MUSA with SBO, so it is left alone.
- The gfx950 V4.1 multi-stream branch from #41308 has never run in a server: the ROCm hook already turned `SGLANG_OPT_USE_MULTI_STREAM_OVERLAP` off. It stays off by default, and setting it to 1 now works.
- DeepGEMM `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` also runs on SM120; the V4.1 prefill indexer could re-admit SM120 there.
- With `SGLANG_FA4_TMEM_LOAD_RED_MAX` gone there is no runtime switch back to FMNMX. Two benchmark rounds on GB300 showed `ld.red` about 5-7% slower on d64 ViT shapes and 3-10% faster on d72 / d80.

## Validation

Every changed read site was tested on base (`27aedf7f93`) and on this branch, on the hardware it runs on.

**Full sweep.** All 1,561 files under `test/registered/unit` and `multimodal_gen/test/unit`, plus the kernel tests this PR touches. Each file ran in its own process on both trees, and every failure seen only on the branch was rerun serially on both.

| Hardware | Failing only on the branch | Import / collect |
|---|---|---|
| H200 (sm_90) | 0 | identical |
| GB300 (sm_103) | 0 (3 port-in-use failures in the parallel run pass serially) | identical (+2 tests) |
| RTX 5090 (sm_120) | 0 | identical |
| MI350X (gfx950, ROCm 7.2) | 0 (13 port-in-use failures in the parallel run pass serially) | identical |

**Accuracy** (sgl-eval 0.1.3, GSM8K). DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4, 200 questions, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, max tokens 8192. Base runs the recipe with the deleted variables set; the branch runs it without them:

| Setup | Base | Branch | New default path seen |
|---|---|---|---|
| GB300, cookbook FP4 low-latency | 98.0% | 97.5% | same command |
| MI350X, MI355X FP4 low-latency | 97.5% | 97.0% | `aiter::inverse_rope_group_quant_kernel` in the trace |
| MI350X, plus `--enable-deepseek-v4-fp4-indexer` | 97.0% | 98.0% | row-group FP4 MQA logits kernel logged on every rank |
| MI350X, `SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=false` (the CI setting) | 98.0% | 98.5% | `_batched_gemm_bf16_kernel` in the trace |

Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 on MI350X (TP4, DP4 DP-attention, TP MoE; all 1,319 questions, temperature 0.7): 0.9598 / 0.9545 with `SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=0` and 0.9591 / 0.9598 with the image default (base / branch). Output throughput is within 1%.

**Targeted checks**
- MiniMax-H3 VAE on H200 with real weights: `exact` is now byte-identical to the unfused path (base differed by up to 1.36e-2), and `lossless` / `high` are byte-identical to base.
- FA4 on sm_103: `test_flash_attention_4_sm103.py` still checks FMNMX against `ld.red` bit-exactly (62 passed).
- FlyDSL MXFP8 GEMM on gfx950, now the default on the V4.1 route: matches an fp32 reference within bf16 rounding for M = 2048-8192. No V4.1 checkpoint was available for an end-to-end run.
- Probes: `SGLANG_FORCE_SHUTDOWN=1`, `SGLANG_SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP=true` and `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_USE_TENSOR_CORE=1` take effect only on the branch, and the old names still work. The changed arch gates were probed on H200, GB300, 5090 and MI350X, and mocked as gfx942 / gfx1151 / gfx1250 / gfx115x.
- `cargo clippy -p sglang-server -- -D warnings` passes on Linux; the Rust changes are doc comments only.

After merging main (`77c3bcbe`), the DSA metadata tests and main's new `test_dsa_kernel_metadata_hook.py` were rerun on H200 and pass.

**Not run on hardware:** H20 (the 78-SM rule), gfx1250 / gfx1151 / gfx115x (arch-mocked unit tests only), MegaMoE EP8 on ROCm, DGX Spark, MuseSpark finalize-AR, and MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 end to end.

title: [Perf] deepseek_v4: bump sgl-deep-gemm to 0.2.6, FlashInfer-layout scales from DeepGEMM producers, current MQA logits API
author: zcnrex
body:
## Summary

Bumps `sgl-deep-gemm` to 0.2.6 and adopts the two 0.2.6 changes that need a caller-side change. The other 0.2.6 changes are DeepGEMM-internal and on by default: Mega MoE block_m 64 for decode loads, the mega_mhc split-barrier fix under CUDA graph replay, the K=64 MXF8F6F4 dense MMA on CC 10.7, and the SIMT dispatch pull for FP4 activations.

### DeepGEMM producers write FlashInfer's 128x4 scale layout (sgl-project/DeepGEMM#136)

On CC 10.7, two DSv4 linears take their input as an MXFP8 pair written by a DeepGEMM kernel. `wo_b` gets it from the `wo_a` `fp8_einsum` epilogue, and `wqkv_a` from Mega mHC. 0.2.6 lets both producers write the scales directly in FlashInfer's 128x4 layout: pass a 4-D int32 scale `[ceil(rows/128), K/128, 32, 4]`, and its flat uint8 view is FlashInfer's `a_descale`. The pair then runs on the FlashInfer MXFP8 GEMM with no conversion step.

- A producer writes the FlashInfer layout whenever its consumer is a FlashInfer layer (the only case in which a pair is produced), outside batch-invariant and deterministic modes. There is no per-shape or per-row threshold: FlashInfer beats or ties DeepGEMM at every measured row count (table below). The scale converter added earlier in this PR is removed.
- `mxfp8_input.py`
  - `deepgemm_pair_takes_flashinfer` is the route check. `batch_invariant_or_deterministic` moves here from `fp8.py` (with top-level imports), and `Fp8LinearMethod.apply` uses it for `pin_tactic`.
  - `deepgemm_mxfp8_linear_input` hands a filled 4-D pair on as `Mxfp8SwizzledInput`. `Fp8LinearMethod.apply` already sends that type to FlashInfer.
  - `zero_deepgemm_mxfp8_scale_rows` zeroes padded rows in either layout.
- `deepseek_v4.py` / `deepseek_v4_mhc.py`: the producers allocate the 4-D scale (`flashinfer=` on the allocation) when the route applies.
  - In the breakable-CUDA-graph path, the live rows' 4-D scales are a prefix of the padded ones, so they need no restride.
- A DeepGEMM-packed int32 pair (batch-invariant or deterministic mode) still runs on DeepGEMM, as on main.

### Current MQA logits API for bf16 index weights (sgl-project/DeepGEMM#134)

The 0.2.3-style call (positional `clean_logits` plus `logits_dtype`) is routed by sgl-deep-gemm to `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits_legacy`. With bf16 weights, `flat_index_logits_tiles` now calls the current API, which reaches the kernel #134 sped up. fp32 weights keep the legacy call. The logits are bitwise identical.

### Decode

- The `wo_a` einsum producer also runs for decode and verify batches up to 2048 rows. So `wo_b` takes the FlashInfer route there too, and the kernel table below covers decode-sized row counts.
- `wqkv_a`'s Mega mHC producer is prefill-only, and the paged MQA logits call is unchanged, so neither route affects decode.
- Accuracy in decode is covered by the GSM8K runs below. Decode throughput is in the decode table below.

## Performance

**Kernel level, CC 10.7.** Producer + FlashInfer GEMM on 4-D scales, divided by producer + DeepGEMM GEMM on packed scales, both on 0.2.6. Each cell is one run or two runs (`run1 / run2`) on swapped GPUs. Lower is better.

| rows | wo_b | wqkv_a |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.92 / 0.87 | 0.93 / 0.93 |
| 8 | 0.91 / 0.90 | 0.94 / 1.03 |
| 16 | 0.88 / 0.87 | 0.96 / 0.96 |
| 32 | 0.87 | 0.89 |
| 64 | 0.85 / 0.86 | 0.96 / 0.95 |
| 128 | 0.93 / 0.92 | 0.90 / 0.91 |
| 256 | 0.88 / 0.88 | 0.95 / 0.93 |
| 512 | 0.92 / 0.93 | 0.91 / 0.91 |
| 1024 | 0.92 / 0.96 | 0.97 / 0.97 |
| 2048 | 0.94 / 0.98 | 0.98 / 0.96 |
| 4096 | 0.94 / 0.92 | 0.96 / 0.97 |
| 8192 | 0.96 / 0.93 | 0.99 / 1.00 |
| 16384 | 0.91 / 0.94 | 0.99 / 1.00 |

- At 1, 129, 1000, 4100 and 16384 rows, the 4-D scales and fp8 data are bitwise equal to the packed-scale path followed by a conversion. So is the FlashInfer output, including with NaN-filled pad scales.
- DeepGEMM's best case is a tie: `wqkv_a` at 8K–16K rows (0.99–1.00). On CC 10.3, an earlier measurement of the same producer + GEMM pair puts FlashInfer at 0.89–0.99, and DeepGEMM ahead by at most 1% (`wqkv_a` at 8K–16K). So no shape keeps a DeepGEMM route.

**#134 (CC 10.3, index logits per prefill chunk, H32, 131K context, 4×4096 new tokens):** −4.3% with the new call. The old call is unchanged. Logits are bitwise identical.

**Server, CC 10.7, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4** (`--dsv4-attn-backend flashmla_mega`, `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MEGA_MHC_PREFILL=1`, DSPARK). Each arm ran once on each of two nodes.

| arm | GSM8K-200 | prefill TTFT, 16 × 16K prompts (s) |
|---|---|---|
| main + 0.2.5.post3 | 0.990 / 0.995 | 0.384 / 0.386 |
| main + 0.2.6 | 0.985 / 0.995 | 0.380 / 0.381 |
| this PR + 0.2.6 | 0.995 / 0.985 | 0.377 / 0.390 |
| this PR + 0.2.6, no routing table (head) | 0.985 / 0.995 | 0.376 / 0.378 |

Accuracy is unchanged. At 16K-token prompts, prefill time is within run-to-run noise: these GEMMs are a small share of the step.

**Decode, same server setup.** Steady-state generation throughput summed over the 4 DP ranks, in tok/s. 128K-token context, simulated acceptance length 3.51, decode CUDA graphs up to 128. One server per cell; each arm ran once on each of two nodes.

| arm | 32 requests | 128 requests |
|---|---|---|
| main + 0.2.5.post3 | 14000 / 14340 | 40941 / 40551 |
| main + 0.2.6 | 14641 / 14549 | 43417 / 43455 |
| this PR + 0.2.6 | 15073 / 14357 | 44068 / 44249 |

- At 128 requests, 0.2.6 alone is +6.6%. The `wo_b` route adds +1.7% on top (+1.5% and +1.8% on the two nodes).
- At 32 requests, 0.2.6 is +3.0%. The `wo_b` route adds +0.8%, within noise: +3.0% on one node and −1.3% on the other.

A profiled prefill step on this PR (rank 0) shows both routes taken:
- `wo_b` and `wqkv_a` run on FlashInfer's block-scaled dense GEMM.
- The only DeepGEMM dense GEMM left is the `wo_a` einsum that produces `wo_b`'s input.
- Index logits run `sm100_mqa_logits`, not the legacy kernel.

## Tests

- `test_fp8_blockwise_linear_backends.py::test_deepgemm_producer_flashinfer_layout`:
  - the 4-D scale's flat view equals `flashinfer.block_scale_interleave` at 200 and 256 rows;
  - the FlashInfer route matches the DeepGEMM route and the fp32 reference;
  - a spy checks which route runs;
  - the pad-row zeroing matches 2-D zeroing followed by a relayout.

  CC 10.3 with sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.6: the file gives 17 passed and 7 skipped.
- Indexer tests (`test_fp4_indexer`, `test_dense_prefill_indexer`, `test_dsv41_prefill_sparse_indexer`, `test_dsv41_indexer_tp_shard`) on CC 10.3 with 0.2.6: 117 passed, 2 skipped.

title: [Perf] [AMD] dsa: Split-K HIP sparse MLA for decode/verify
author: RolaoDenthu
body:
Generated by SkyOpt (Berkeley SkyDiscover)

## Motivation

On MI355X (gfx950), when Kimi-K3.1 runs TP8 speculative decoding, the target-verify batches go through the Triton split-K kernel in `triton_sparse_mla_fwd`. Each request contributes bs × 6 rows (DFLASH MLA5 draft, 5 draft tokens), so a batch is 16–512 query rows. In a TP8 bs48 decode step, sparse MLA takes about 18% of the step time. The gfx950 HIP sparse MLA prefill kernel is already in the tree, but it runs one CTA per row, which can't fill the GPU at these row counts.

## Modifications

- **`sparse_mla_prefill_gfx950.cuh` / `.py`**: add a split-K mode (`run_split` / `sparse_mla_split_gfx950`). Each row's top-k is split across `splits` CTAs, and the partial results are merged with an fp32 log-sum-exp combine, so the merge adds no extra rounding. `sparse_mla_decode_splits(rows)` picks the split count from the row count (16 / 8 / 4 / 2, from per-shape microbenchmarks; numbers in the docstring).
- **`triton_sparse_mla.py`**: in `triton_sparse_mla_fwd`, batches of 16–512 rows (H ≤ 16, shapes supported by `supports_sparse_mla_prefill_gfx950`) go to the HIP split-K kernel. Smaller batches (6 / 12 rows) stay on the Triton split-K path, which is faster there. Batches above 512 rows keep the existing single-CTA HIP path. Non-DCP only.
- **`environ.py`**: new switch `SGLANG_ROCM_SPARSE_MLA_DECODE_HIP`, on by default; set it to `0` to fall back to Triton.

Kernel time (MI355X, 12 heads, top-2048):

| Rows | Triton split-K (µs) | HIP split-K (µs) |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 24 | 28.6 | 20.5 |
| 96 | 89.5 | 31.2 |
| 192 | 239 | 46.3 |
| 288 | 103 (single-CTA HIP) | 70.8 |

## Accuracy Tests

Kimi-K3.1 on MI355X, compared against the same tree with this change off:
- GSM8K (DCP8 c48, TP8 c4): unchanged
- Real accept length: unchanged

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X, Kimi-K3.1, InferenceX fixed-seq 8k/1k, simulated accept length 3.69, paired against the same tree with this change off. Throughput per GPU:

| Concurrency | Change |
|---:|---:|
| 4 | +1.3% |
| 16 | +4.0% |
| 32 | +6.9% |

The sparse MLA decode step itself runs about 6× faster.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: [Perf] [AMD] dflash: Row-shard the draft's target-hidden fc in prefill chunks
author: RolaoDenthu
body:
Generated by SkyOpt (Berkeley SkyDiscover)

## Motivation

The DFlash draft model's `fc` projects the target model's hidden states captured from 6 layers, [6 × 7168 → 7168]. Without `SGLANG_OPT_DFLASH_TP_AUX_FC`, every TP rank holds the full `fc` and projects **every row**, so the computation is repeated on all ranks. For long prefill chunks this is significant: in a 16K-token DCP8 prefill step on MI355X, the replicated `fc` takes **7.6 ms**.

## Modifications

All changes are in `python/sglang/srt/models/dflash.py`:

- When `fc` is replicated (`fc_tp_columns is None`), TP > 1, and the number of target-hidden rows is ≥ `_FC_ROW_SHARD_MIN_ROWS` (4096), each rank runs `fc` + `hidden_norm` on only its 1/TP of the rows (the last shard is zero-padded), and an `all_gather_into_tensor` assembles the full result. The all-gather costs about 0.6 ms.
- Decode and small prefill chunks (< 4096 rows) keep the replicated path. When `SGLANG_OPT_DFLASH_TP_AUX_FC` is on (column-split `fc`), the existing column all-reduce path is used and row sharding does not apply.
- The `fc` call and the quantized-output unpacking move into a `_fc()` helper so both paths can share it.

There is no new env switch; the threshold is the module constant `_FC_ROW_SHARD_MIN_ROWS`.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K 1319: 0.9735 

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X, Kimi-K3.1 + DFlash draft, DCP8, 16K-token prefill step:

| | Time |
|---|---:|
| Replicated `fc` (before) | 7.6 ms |
| Row-sharded `fc` + all-gather (after) | ≈ 7.6 / 8 + 0.6 ms |

TODO: end-to-end TTFT for 8k/1k (or longer inputs), with and without this change.

title: [Perf] [AMD] moe: Run the small-batch sort + stage-1 quant up to 1024 pairs on Kimi-K3
author: RolaoDenthu
body:
Generated by SkyOpt (Berkeley SkyDiscover)

## Motivation

In Kimi-K3's MoE (E = 896, top-16, block_m 32), small batches go through a patched sort kernel that also quantizes the stage-1 input to MXFP8. Until now it covered at most 256 (token, expert) pairs, i.e. 16 tokens at top-16; larger batches fell back to aiter's opus sort + quant.

On MI355X the patched sort is **31–46% faster** than aiter's sort + quant up to 960 pairs, and only ties from 1152 pairs, where its bitonic sort width doubles past 1024. The 256-pair limit therefore left decode/verify batches of 17–64 tokens on the slower path.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_sorting_small.py`:

- Raise the limit from 256 to 1024 (token, expert) pairs (64 tokens at top-16).
- Rename `_EMIT_MAX_PAIRS` to `_SMALL_SORT_MAX_PAIRS`, and use this one constant both for picking the patched sort and for its stage-1 quant, which previously had separate hard-coded `256` checks.

Batches above 1024 pairs still use aiter's sort + quant.

## Accuracy Tests

The patched sort's outputs (sorted ids, weights, expert ids, and the quantized stage-1 input) are **byte-identical** to aiter's at 384–1024 pairs, so model outputs do not change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X, Kimi-K3.1, InferenceX fixed-seq 8k/1k, throughput per GPU:

| Concurrency | Change |
|---:|---:|
| 4 (TP8) | +2.3% |

title: [Perf] pd: Poll the prefill result wait per attention-DP shard and pump HiCache storage events in it
author: metamergebot
body:
<!-- oss-sync ci-note:start -->
**CI status (oncall, 2026-11-06 20:40Z): every test ran on this head and passed.** In the PR Test run on this head ([42128706400](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42128706400)), `base-a` and 12 of 13 `base-b` shards are green. The remaining base-b shard(s) were cancelled while queued, and their test files ran green on this same head via `/rerun-test` ([42191548990](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42191548990), [42191563799](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42191563799)). `pr-test-finish` is red only because those shard(s) ran outside the PR Test run; nothing is untested. Ready to merge.
<!-- oss-sync ci-note:end -->

## Motivation

`SGLANG_DISAGG_PREFILL_POLL_TRANSFERS_WHILE_WAITING` (#47015) lets the PD prefill overlap loop retire finished KV transfers while the oldest forward result is still pending. It was gated on attention DP=CP=1 because the readiness check ran a MIN all-reduce over the whole TP group while each attention-DP shard keeps its own transfer queue: one shard could skip the wait and go on to the TP-wide intake broadcast while another shard was still inside the TP-wide readiness all-reduce.

Under attention DP the same wait also matters for HiCache L3 storage. The scheduler drains HiCache events once per scheduling step, so a storage prefetch that completes while a forward is running is acknowledged only after that forward finishes and the next step starts:

```text
                 step N                       step N+1
GPU:   |========================|==================================|
              ^ L3 prefetch issued
              |-- storage I/O --|                                  ^ event drained
                                (complete, unobserved)               request admitted
```

## Modifications

- **Readiness per attention-DP shard.** The MIN all-reduce that decides whether the oldest result is ready now runs on `dp_tp_cpu_group`: the attention-TP group under attention DP, the TP group otherwise. Every collective the wait issues is shard-scoped (the transfer-queue poll and the HiCache drain already use the attention-TP group), and the TP-wide collectives (intake broadcast, MLP sync) run only outside the wait, so every rank still issues them in the same order while shards may leave the wait on different passes.
- **Gate.** The transfer-wait poll now needs only attention CP=1, since CP peers sit outside the readiness group. Continuous input polling keeps its DP=1 requirement because intake and batch creation are TP-wide.
- **HiCache pump.** New opt-in `SGLANG_DISAGG_PREFILL_POLL_HICACHE_WHILE_WAITING` (default off, separate from the transfer flag so the two can be enabled independently). With a hierarchical cache, an L3 storage backend and a `UnifiedRadixCache`, each unfinished wait pass also calls `_process_hicache_events(should_retry_storage_prefetch=False)`, so prefetch completions and host write acks land while the forward runs. Storage prefetch retries still count scheduling steps, and the drain never calls `check_prefetch_progress`, so no prefetch stop policy changes. HiCache D2H and H2D copies already fence on `forward_stream`, so draining events mid-forward does not change copy ordering.
- `_yield_gil_if_needed` and the readiness all-reduce key on the readiness group's size instead of `tp_size`.
- **Default path.** With both flags off the loop is unchanged: the only new work is one flag read at loop entry.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model forward or sampling. The new flag is off by default.

Unit tests in `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_result_polling.py` cover the new behaviour on CPU:

- `test_attention_dp_shards_leave_result_waits_independently` (Gloo, two shapes: TP4 DP2 with attention-TP 2, and TP2 DP2 with attention-TP 1): first only shard 0 has a transfer to retire, so it polls while shard 1 blocks; then both shards pump HiCache and leave the wait on different passes (2 vs 5 pumps, none with a storage retry). With the readiness all-reduce put back on the TP group, the attention-TP 2 shape deadlocks: all four ranks time out and the test fails.
- `test_result_wait_pumps_hicache_events_with_its_flag_and_l3_storage`: the wait pumps HiCache only with the HiCache flag and an L3 storage backend; the transfer flag alone, or the HiCache flag without storage, keeps the blocking wait.
- `test_transfer_wait_polling_needs_the_flag_and_a_supported_loop` now expects attention DP to be a supported loop for the transfer-wait poll.

```
pytest test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_result_polling.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_disagg_idle_step_counters.py
38 passed, 113 subtests passed
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

With the HiCache flag on, an L3 prefetch that completes during a forward is acknowledged on the next polling pass instead of at the next scheduling step, so the request is admitted up to one forward earlier. No end-to-end numbers are included in this PR; both flags are opt-in and the default path is unchanged.
