title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] deepseek-v4: Pass a caller-owned multi-CTA counter buffer to the trtllm sparse MLA kernel
author: leejnau
body:
## Motivation

`--dsv4-attn-backend trtllm` needs a multi-CTA KV counter buffer sized by query rows. FlashInfer's default buffer is sized by request count, while the DSv4 VarSeq kernel indexes it by query row.

The backend worked around this by replacing the private `flashinfer.mla._core._get_trtllm_gen_multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer`. That has two problems.

1. **The patch doesn't take effect on the current FlashInfer pin.**
   - In 0.7.2 and 0.7.2.post1, `trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4` gets its buffer through `flashinfer.utils._resolve_trtllm_gen_multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer`.
   - When no buffer is passed in, that function calls `_get_trtllm_gen_multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer` from `flashinfer.utils`'s own namespace, not from `flashinfer.mla._core`.
   - So the replaced function is never called on this path. FlashInfer allocates a new buffer sized by request count on every launch.
2. **It breaks with FlashInfer 0.7.3.** `flashinfer.mla._core` no longer imports that name, so backend init raises `AttributeError`. This blocks the FlashInfer 0.7.3 bump (#46926).

The workaround's docstring says to drop it "once FlashInfer accepts a caller-owned buffer". The function has accepted one through its public `multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer` argument since at least 0.7.2. The MLA, MHA and DSA trtllm backends already pass their own buffers this way.

## Modifications

All changes are in `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_trtllm_backend.py`.

- Remove the monkeypatch and the import of `flashinfer.mla._core`.
- `_reserve_trtllm_query_rows` (renamed from `_install_persistent_trtllm_semaphores`) only records the query-row capacity, computed as before from chunked prefill, max prefill tokens and running requests × draft tokens.
- `_get_trtllm_kv_counter_buffer(num_heads, device)` returns one zeroed persistent buffer per head count.
  - It is sized with FlashInfer's public `get_trtllm_gen_multi_ctas_kv_counter_bytes(capacity_rows, num_heads, sm_count)`.
  - It is held in the runtime context's persistent buffers, like the existing trtllm workspace.
  - It is created outside graph capture; the assert is unchanged.
- Both `trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4` call sites (decode and varlen prefill) pass it as `multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer`. The existing `_check_trtllm_query_rows` guard still applies.
- The manual Blackwell prefill test also passes the buffer.

This works with FlashInfer 0.7.2, 0.7.2.post1 and 0.7.3. The public argument and helpers exist in all three.

## Tests

- New unit test `test_trtllm_kv_counter_buffer_is_sized_by_query_rows_and_shared` in `test/registered/attention/unittests/dsv4/test_deepseek_v4.py`. It checks:
  - the buffer is sized by reserved query rows, not request count;
  - it is zero-initialized;
  - it is reused across calls;
  - each head count gets its own buffer.
- On GB200 (SM100), in `lmsysorg/sglang:dev` (arm64) with torch 2.14.1+cu130 and nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0:

  | FlashInfer | Code | `test_dsv4_trtllm_prefill.py` (rows 1/16/17/8192) | New unit tests |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 0.7.2 | main | pass | n/a |
  | 0.7.2 | this PR | pass | 2 passed |
  | 0.7.3 | main | **fail**: `AttributeError: module 'flashinfer.mla._core' has no attribute '_get_trtllm_gen_multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer'` | n/a |
  | 0.7.3 | this PR | pass | 2 passed |

- End-to-end on one 4×GB200 node: DeepSeek-V4-Flash with the cookbook's verified GB200 low-latency recipe (TP=4, `flashinfer_mxfp4` MoE, EAGLE with 3 steps and 4 draft tokens) plus `--dsv4-attn-backend trtllm`, image `lmsysorg/sglang:dev` (arm64). Full GSM8K (1319 questions) through sgl-eval 0.1.3 at temperature 1.0 and top_p 1.0, the cookbook's recommended sampling:

  | Code | FlashInfer | GSM8K | Request errors |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | main | 0.7.2 | 96.66% | 0% |
  | this PR | 0.7.2 | 96.74% | 0% |
  | #48468 + this PR | 0.7.3 | 96.59% | 0% |

title: [Chore] [NVIDIA] deps: Bump FlashInfer to 0.7.3 and migrate the NVLink one-sided all-to-all to flashinfer.moe_ep
author: leejnau
body:
## Motivation

This PR bumps FlashInfer to 0.7.3. It also brings in @trevor-m's migration of the NVLink one-sided all-to-all to `flashinfer.moe_ep` from #46885, because neither change can land without the other:

- **The bump needs the migration.** FlashInfer 0.7.3 removes `flashinfer.comm.MoeAlltoAll` and `moe_a2a_get_workspace_size_per_rank`, which the current `FlashinferDispatcher` uses (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6047, #6621).
- **The migration needs the bump.** #46885 passes `runtime_max_tokens_per_rank` to `flashinfer.moe_ep`, and that argument only exists from 0.7.3. In 0.7.2 it is `max_tokens_per_rank`.

#46926 (0.7.2.post1) stays open for now as a fallback.

## Depends on

- #48467 (DeepSeek-V4 trtllm counter buffer), now merged. Main's `deepseek_v4_trtllm_backend.py` patches `flashinfer.mla._core._get_trtllm_gen_multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer`. 0.7.3 no longer has that name, so `--dsv4-attn-backend trtllm` fails at init. #48467 works on 0.7.2 and 0.7.3, so it can merge first.

## Modifications

- Commits from #46885, cherry-picked with @trevor-m as author:
  - Switch `NVLinkOneSidedAllToAll` to the `flashinfer.moe_ep` API.
  - Lint fix.
  - Pass `runtime_max_tokens_per_rank` in dispatch.
- Pass the new `last_valid_index` argument to `flashinfer::sampling::DeviceSamplingFromProb` in SGLang's JIT tree speculative-sampling kernel (`sgl_kernel/speculative/sampling.cuh`). flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5352 (in 0.7.3) added that parameter. Without this change the kernel fails to compile, and the first EAGLE verify step crashes the scheduler. The change mirrors FlashInfer's own chain speculative-sampling kernel, and it only compiles against 0.7.3 headers, so it has to land with the bump.
- Pass the new `fixed_uniform_q_len` argument in the FlashInfer backend's `fast_prefill_plan`. FlashInfer 0.7.3's FA2 paged-prefill `plan()` takes 21 arguments instead of 20. The fast plan also clears `_eagle_verify_fp8kv_sm90_state`, as FlashInfer's own `plan()` now does on every call.
- MiniMax-M3.1's fused NVFP4 KV store now zeroes the payload when a block's scale underflows to zero, to match FlashInfer 0.7.3's quantizer (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6996 changed its guard from `amax != 0` to `sf != 0`).
- **Temporary workaround for flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8831.** FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 and 0.7.3 include flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6546, which adds a small-batch MoE finalize kernel for 4 < top-k <= 64. That kernel adds the top-k expert outputs in a different order from the large-batch kernel, so a token's MoE output depends on its batch size, and prefill and decode logprobs stop matching. With `--enable-deterministic-inference`, the pre-routed NVFP4 trtllm MoE path now calls FlashInfer with `do_finalize=False` and sums the outputs with SGLang's `moe_finalize_fuse_shared`, which uses one order at every batch size. `moe_finalize_fuse_shared` gains an `out=` argument so the sum lands in the usual output buffer. Nothing changes outside deterministic mode. Remove this once #8831 is fixed in a FlashInfer release.
- Bump FlashInfer from 0.7.2 to 0.7.3 in `docker/Dockerfile`, `docker/Dockerfile.cu134`, `python/pyproject.toml` and the `engine.py` version check.

0.7.3 requires `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]>=4.8.0`, and SGLang already pins 4.8.0.

## Tests

- CI. The first run is expected to hit the cold SGLang JIT cache in the jit-kernel suite, as on earlier FlashInfer bumps.
- On GB200, #48467's DeepSeek-V4 trtllm prefill test passes on 0.7.3 with the fix, and fails without it.
- On GB200 with FlashInfer 0.7.3, `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_speculative_sampling.py` passes (11 passed).
- `TestInklingSmallNvfp4DsparkDeterministic.test_input_output_logprobs_match` (KL threshold 1e-9) on GB200, with the test's `--tp` changed from 4 to 2 (GB200 at TP=4 fails even on main with 0.7.2):

  | Code | FlashInfer | avg KL |
  |---|---|---|
  | main | 0.7.2 | 0.0 (3 runs) |
  | main | 0.7.3 | 5.6e-6 to 1.6e-3 (several runs) |
  | main | 0.7.2.post1, small-batch finalize disabled | 0.0 |
  | this PR, with the workaround | 0.7.3 + matching jit-cache | 0.0 (2 of 2 runs) |

- @trevor-m validated the `moe_ep` migration on 0.7.3 on 4×GB200 (see #46885): GSM8K 96%, and `test_flashinfer_a2a_wide_ep.py`, `test_flashinfer_dispatcher.py` and `test_muse_spark_runner_dispatch.py` passed.
- End-to-end on one 4×GB200 node: DeepSeek-V4-Flash with the cookbook's verified GB200 low-latency recipe (TP=4, `flashinfer_mxfp4` MoE, EAGLE with 3 steps and 4 draft tokens) plus `--dsv4-attn-backend trtllm`, image `lmsysorg/sglang:dev` (arm64). Full GSM8K (1319 questions) through sgl-eval 0.1.3 at temperature 1.0 and top_p 1.0, the cookbook's recommended sampling:

  | Code | FlashInfer | GSM8K | Request errors |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | main | 0.7.2 | 96.66% | 0% |
  | #48467 | 0.7.2 | 96.74% | 0% |
  | this PR + #48467 | 0.7.3 | 96.59% | 0% |

  Before the speculative-sampling fix, the 0.7.3 run scored 0%, because every request failed when the scheduler crashed on the JIT build error.

title: [Perf] [AMD] kimi-k3: Row-sharded MoE front, o_proj and stream for gfx950 prefill
author: RolaoDenthu
body:
Generated with SkyOpt (Berkeley SkyDiscover)

The code changes are hip only.

## Motivation

On gfx950, Kimi-K3/K3.1 prefill already runs the MoE tail on row shards (#48427), but the MoE front, the shared experts and o_proj still run on every row on every TP rank, and the stream is all-gathered after each layer. This PR keeps that work on row shards too.

## Modifications

Three opt-in gfx950 switches, off by default, active only on the row-sharded tail path (≥ 4096 tokens):

- `SGLANG_ENABLE_ROCM_K3_ROW_SHARDED_FRONT`: router top-k, latent down-proj and shared experts run on this rank's rows, using full shared-expert weights gathered at load (~24 GB/GPU). Only the MXFP8 routed input and the top-k are all-gathered. BF16 only.
- `SGLANG_ENABLE_ROCM_K3_ROW_SHARDED_O_PROJ`: o_proj's input is exchanged to row shards by all-to-all, and o_proj runs there with its full weight (~16 GB/GPU). Eager batches only.
- `SGLANG_ENABLE_ROCM_K3_ROW_SHARDED_STREAM`: the stream stays on row shards between layers. Enabled only with PP1 and when every later layer takes the row-sharded FFN read.

The MoE logic is in `kimi_k3_amd/moe.py`, the o_proj helpers are in a new `kimi_k3_amd/row_shard_o_proj.py`, and the FFN-read hooks are in `attn_bank_hip.py`. Each common-code branch in `attn_bank.py` and `kimi_k3.py` is gated on `_is_hip` and its switch, so CUDA and the switch-off path are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Kimi-K3.1 + DFlash2 MLA5 draft, 8× MI355X, TP8, all switches on. GSM8K (1319 questions, c48, real draft verification): **0.9697**; accept length 4.673. 300 of 305 prefill batches took the new path.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8k/1k fixed-seq, TP8, simulated accept length 3.69. Both arms use the same code and the same args (`--mem-fraction-static 0.90 --context-length 32768 --max-mamba-cache-size 24 --disable-radix-cache`); only the switches differ.

| Concurrency | Off (tok/s/GPU) | On (tok/s/GPU) | Gain | TTFT p50 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 543 | 573 | +5.5% | 481 → 380 ms |
| 16 | 1021 | 1128 | +10.5% | 523 → 422 ms |
| 32 | 1105 | 1243 | +12.5% | 7.53 → 5.98 s |

With all three switches on, the weights take ~40 GB more per GPU, which does not fit at the recommended `--mem-fraction-static 0.85`; FRONT + STREAM alone add ~24 GB.

title: [Perf] mem_cache: Order recycled unified-page writers after the forward instead of the current stream
author: metamergebot
body:
Stacked on #48450: this branch is based on `oss-sync-29377d228a`, so the diff shows that fix until it merges; the change here is the second commit.

## Motivation

#48450 orders physical-page reuse in `Band._free_lazy` after the latest forward by making the current (scheduler) stream wait on the forward-done event. That keeps an in-flight forward's prepared attention page table from reading pages a later allocation overwrote or zeroed, but the wait sits on the wrong stream: every lazy free under a running forward stalls the scheduler stream, so any later host read of device indices queued behind it (HiCache index preparation, decode host restores) blocks until that forward ends, and the GPU idles between forwards.

## Modifications

The guarantee stays: a recycled page is not rewritten before the forward that may still read it completes. Only the writers of recycled pages are ordered after the forward; the current stream never waits.

- **Held frees.** On CUDA with a forward in flight, `Band._free_lazy` holds the freed physical pages together with the latest forward-done event (`Band._unsettled_free`) instead of waiting. `_settle_freed` moves them into the free list once that event has fired, at every hand-out and flush. Capacity counts held pages as drainable: `_available_tokens`, the peer hole credits (`_peer_drainable_hole_bytes` and `FloatBand`'s side credit), the pricing snapshot and `_check_invariants`.
- **Early reuse under pressure.** When settled holes fall short, `take_physical_pages` takes the held pages before growing the watermark into the chain gap, the order the capacity checks assume; the watermark then moves the same way on every rank whichever forwards have completed locally. Instead of a stream wait, `_order_reuse` records a reuse fence, an event at the forward stream's tail, and the writers of those pages order after it:
  - hand-out zeroing (`_maybe_zero_pages`) runs on the forward stream;
  - an urgent `_flush` waits for the fence after its host read, and an opportunistic flush skips while frees are held or a fence is pending;
  - the decode-side deferred destination publish waits for the allocator's `reuse_fences()` before exposing a destination to the prefill's RDMA writer, which follows no stream. `BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator.reuse_fences()` is new, empty by default and overridden by `ChainAllocator`;
  - HiCache loads, decode host restores and storage loads already order their copies after the forward stream, and the next forward's own writes follow by stream order.
- **Forward stream.** The scheduler passes its forward stream with the forward-done event: `set_latest_forward_done_event(event, stream)`. Without a stream, the band keeps #48450's current-stream wait.
- `ChainAllocator.resize` refuses a band with held frees, as it already refuses one with pending reuse.
- Tests: the stand-in peer in `test_unified_memory_move_gate.py` gains the held-free count, and the allocator stand-in in `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py` gains `reuse_fences`.

Scope: CUDA lazy (unified) bands only. CPU bands, eager compaction and `FloatBand` behave as before. `free_physical` (rollback of a load reservation no forward read) is unchanged, as in #48450.

## Accuracy Tests

The unified-memory allocator, HiCache and disaggregation unit files (`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_*.py`, `test_multi_ended_allocator.py`, `test_kv_storage_lifecycle.py`, `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_decode_queue_cleanup.py`, `test_unified_memory_move_gate.py`, `test_dsv4_unified_fp8_pd.py`, `test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_unified_out_cache_loc_rebind.py`), one pytest process per file on a CUDA host, give the same results with and without this change. Tests that free under an unfired forward event and expect immediate holes or compaction use CPU bands, where frees are not held, so they keep testing the same behaviour.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured here; mechanism only. The per-free `wait_event` on the current stream is gone, so host reads of device indices queued after a free no longer wait for the forward in flight. In its place, the completion events order the writers of recycled pages, and a small zeroing kernel per pressured hand-out runs on the forward stream between forwards.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). The two stand-ins above are extended; the existing unified-memory free-path tests cover the changed functions.
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Feat] dsa: Kernel prerequisites for a DCP-sharded indexer
author: hnyls2002
body:
Original authors: @yhyang201, @BBuf, @nvpohanh, @kpham-sgl

## Port of #48414

The Kimi-K3.1 Day-0 branch (#48414) shards the DSA indexer's index-K cache across the DCP ranks (`dsa_dcp_sharded.py`); on main, Kimi-K3.1 still rejects `--dcp-size > 1`. This PR ports the kernels that path needs, with tests and no caller yet:

1. Store only the rank's own index-K slots.
2. Select a local top-k whose candidates merge exactly across ranks.
3. Build FlashMLA's split-KV schedule cheaply for the short per-rank lengths.

Against the raw port, tie order and the cluster path reuse #47960 instead of the branch's own versions (whose cluster path missed ties in the top coarse bin), and `schedule` / `dcp_size` / `dcp_rank` replace the branch's flags and names. Left for the sharded indexer PR: the schedule tests that need its backend code.

## Modifications

- **Top-k candidates** (`topk_v2.cuh`, `topk.py`)
  - `topk_transform_candidates_v2`: a ragged top-k that writes `(fp32 score bits, local * dcp_size + dcp_rank)` per selected position, `(0, -1)` padded, so the ranks' candidates merge into the global top-k. It shares the ragged selection (`ragged_window_topk`); rows past `cluster_floor` run the shared cluster top-k (`TopKCluster`), each rank emitting the candidates it selects. The cluster size is picked from the row count on SM90 / SM100, where the cluster path is built.
  - `deterministic=True` on the ragged, paged, packed and candidates entry points builds that call in top-k mode 2 (#47960), whatever `SGLANG_TOPK_V2_MODE` is: equal scores at the k-th place resolve to the smallest indices, which the merge relies on. The module name carries the mode, so both builds load in one process.
- **FlashMLA schedule metadata** (`flashmla_sched_meta.cuh/.py`)
  - `schedule="parallel"`: the partition walk by pointer doubling across the block, giving the same schedule as the serial walk.
  - `schedule="windowed"` (sparse only): request costs cut into equal windows; a valid schedule with the same bound on the costliest partition, computed in a few microseconds.
  - The default stays `"serial"`; either alternative falls back to it when it does not fit in shared memory.
- **Index-K store** (`fused_store_index_cache.cuh`, `dsa_fused_store_index_cache.py`)
  - `dcp_size` / `dcp_rank`: with widened slots, a rank stores only its own slots, at row `slot // dcp_size`. Defaults keep the current behavior.
  - Negative locations are skipped instead of written.

## Tests

- `test_topk_v2.py`: candidates against the ragged top-k, with and without row starts; cluster against one block, including rows whose threshold lands in the highest coarse bin; index-ordered ties on the paged, ragged and packed paths in a process whose default mode is exact.
- `test_flashmla_sched_meta.py`: the parallel walk reproduces the serial one bit for bit, and a replay whose lengths outgrow its workspace falls back; the windowed schedule covers every request's blocks exactly once, and FlashMLA gives the same attention on it as on its own schedule.
- `test_fused_store_index_cache.py`: under DCP, owned, foreign and negative slots mixed; the buffer equals a plain store of the owned tokens at `slot // dcp_size`.

On one B300 GPU at this head: `test_topk_v2.py` 400 passed, 14 skipped; `test_flashmla_sched_meta.py` 242 passed; `test_fused_store_index_cache.py` 16 passed.

## Speed

B300, each call replayed 50 times in a CUDA graph, best of 5 (us per call).

`flashmla_sched_meta`, 148 partitions, top-k 2048, block 64, overhead 5. Per-request lengths uniform in [1, 512] (a DCP8 rank) or all 2048:

| lengths | b | serial (us) | parallel (us) | windowed (us) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1..512 | 4 | 4.13 | 4.14 | 3.25 |
| 1..512 | 8 | 5.53 | 6.08 | 3.28 |
| 1..512 | 32 | 10.78 | 6.02 | 3.61 |
| 1..512 | 256 | 25.21 | 9.84 | 3.90 |
| 2048 | 8 | 16.07 | 6.93 | 3.51 |
| 2048 | 64 | 18.18 | 11.09 | 3.68 |
| 2048 | 256 | 27.57 | 27.57 | 3.93 |

Below `kMinParallelBatch = 8` the parallel schedule is the serial one; at b = 8 it is slower on short lengths and faster on full ones, and from b = 16 it is faster on both. At b = 256 with full lengths its tables do not fit, so it falls back to serial.

`topk_transform_candidates_v2`, top-k 2048, deterministic, randn scores, `cluster_floor=0`:

| rows | seq_len | one block (us) | cluster 2 (us) | cluster 4 (us) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8192 | 4.39 | 4.91 | 4.39 |
| 1 | 16384 | 6.79 | 6.49 | 5.25 |
| 1 | 131072 | 28.14 | 16.68 | 10.71 |
| 16 | 16384 | 7.20 | 6.67 | 5.39 |
| 16 | 131072 | 28.80 | 17.03 | 11.00 |
| 64 | 8192 | 4.42 | 5.71 | 6.12 |
| 64 | 131072 | 29.38 | 17.31 | 16.73 |

The cluster path loses at 8192 and wins from 16384 on, which `_CANDIDATES_CLUSTER_FLOOR = 16384` follows (rows up to it take one block).

title: [Perf] tokenizer_manager: Keep the crash-dump request history pickled so the cyclic GC never scans it
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

With `--crash-dump-folder`, `TokenizerManager.record_request_for_crash_dump` keeps the last five minutes of finished requests in memory as live Python objects so that `dump_requests_before_crash` can write them. Under load that history is a large number of GC-tracked objects (for every finished request: the request object, its dicts and lists, the output dict and its `meta_info`), and every full (gen2) collection walks all of them from the event loop thread, stalling request handling for the whole walk. #37297 converted the token lists to tuples, which removed the per-token part of that cost but leaves the rest tracked.

## Modifications

- `record_request_for_crash_dump` pickles `(obj, out_dict, created, finished)` once when a request finishes and keeps `(finish time, bytes)`. `bytes` are not tracked by the cyclic GC, so the history costs the collector nothing; the five-minute trim reads the finish time from the tuple's first slot. A record that does not pickle is left out with a one-time warning: the dump pickles the same tuple, so it could not have written it either.
- `dump_requests_before_crash` unpickles the records, with GC paused while they are rebuilt, right before writing, so the dump file holds the same tuples as before. Each output dict is now a snapshot taken at finish time, so fields the response path adds afterwards are no longer in the dump.
- `test/registered/unit/utils/test_crash_dump.py`: the fixture holds the finished record in the new `(finish time, bytes)` shape.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model execution or outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The per-request cost is one `pickle.dumps` of the record at finish time; in exchange, full collections no longer walk the crash-dump history, so the event-loop stalls that grow with request rate under `--crash-dump-folder` go away.

title: [Feat] model: Support ERNIE 5.5 Flash
author: chang-wenbin
body:
## Motivation

  Add day-0 support for Baidu's ERNIE 5.5 Flash (`Ernie5_5_MoeForCausalLM`): a 280B-total / 14B-active multi-router latent MoE with hybrid HCA + MLA-DSA attention, ECHO
  decoding and a 1M context window.

  - Released now: `baidu/ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Base` (FP8) and `baidu/ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Base-BF16`.
  - Coming soon: ERNIE-5.5-Flash (FP8 / FP4 / BF16), with reasoning, tool calling and a bundled DSpark draft.
  - Blog: https://ernie.baidu.com/release/ernie-5-5-flash-base/

  ## Modifications

  **Model** (`models/ernie55.py`, `configs/ernie55.py`, `arg_groups/model_overrides/ernie55.py`)
  - 43 layers: 1 dense FFN layer plus 42 Multi-Router latent MoE layers (512 experts, top-10, plus a shared expert in a 2048-d latent space), with SiTU experts.
  - Hybrid attention: 37 HCA layers (one compressed entry per 128 tokens plus a 128-token sliding window) and 6 MLA layers with DSA sparse attention (top-2048 plus the
  trailing window).
  - Low-rank output gate, VHA post-mix, QK-norm, mHC hyper-connections and a MultiMax head.
  - Loads FP8 (128x128 blocks, UE8M0 scales) and BF16 checkpoints.

  **Attention and KV cache** (`layers/attention/ernie55_backend.py`, `mem_cache/ernie55_memory_pool.py`)
  - `ernie55` attention backend over the compressed-KV pool for HCA, plus an MLA latent sub-pool for the DSA layers.
  - HiCache and PD disaggregation support, including a NextN draft that owns no SWA buffer.
  - Prefill work is skipped on rows the LM head never reads. MLA sparse prefill uses the 64-head FlashMLA kernel.

  **DSA indexer**
  - The fused Q/K indexer kernels gain NeoX-rope and 128-point Hadamard variants (`kNeoxStyle`, `kHadamard`) for ERNIE 5.5. DeepSeek-V3.2 and V4 instantiate the same
  kernels as before.
  - Add `--enable-fp4-indexer`: FP4 index-K cache and queries for DSA-indexer models (SM100).

  **Speculative decoding** (`models/ernie55_nextn.py`, `models/ernie55_dspark.py`)
  - ECHO: the final layer serves as a multi-step chain MTP draft (`--speculative-algorithm EAGLE`).
  - DSpark: the draft ships with ERNIE-5.5-Flash.

  **Parsers**
  - `ernie55` reasoning parser (`<ernie:think>` ... `</ernie:think>`).
  - `ernie55` tool-call parser (`<ernie:tool_call><invoke name=...><parameter name=...>`).

  **New kernels**
  - MultiMax, the multi-router top-k, appending the window to top-k, post-mix with the FP8 `wo_a` GEMM, and the sigmoid gate multiply.

  **Fix**
  - The DeepGEMM contiguous SiTU FP8 quant now writes the UE8M0 scale that the GEMM reads.
    - Before, `_situ_mul_quant_contig_kernel` quantized with `amax / 448` and stored that scale, which `_cast_to_e8m0_with_rounding_up` rounds up to a power of two before the down GEMM reads it, so the GEMM saw its input scaled up by the rounding factor (1x-2x per 128-value group).
    - It runs only for SiTU experts on the runner's contiguous path with UE8M0 scales (SM100 / SM120). For Kimi-K3 and K3.1 that means `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm` without MegaMoE; their default Blackwell paths (FlashInfer MXFP4, MegaMoE) do not use this kernel.

  **Docs**
  - New cookbook page `Baidu/ERNIE-5.5-Flash` with its command-generator config. The pages move from `Ernie/` to `Baidu/`, with a redirect.
  - Supported-models entry, `server_arguments.mdx` (`--enable-fp4-indexer`, and `ernie55` among the parser and attention-backend options), the tool-parser and
  reasoning-parser tables, and the Baidu card plus a featured-model entry on the cookbook home.



## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

**SiTU contiguous FP8 quant** (B300): the kernel output, dequantized with the scale the GEMM reads, against an fp32 SiTU reference.

| | rel. error | gain |
|---|---|---|
| main | 0.50-0.67 | 1.42-1.59 |
| this PR | 0.026 | 0.999 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: [Perf] kimi-k3.1: TP-shard the decode MoE front and latent-up tail
author: nvpohanh
body:
[by Claude Code]

Original authors: @nvpohanh, @kpham-sgl

## Port of #48414

On main, every TP rank of a Kimi-K3.1 MoE layer reads the full router (12.9 MB) and latent down-proj (51.4 MB) rows of the merged MoE front, and the full latent up_proj (51.4 MB). For DFLASH verify batches these GEMMs are bound by weight reads. This PR ports #48414's TP-sharded MoE front and latent-up tail (developed as radixark/sglang-k31#151), so each rank reads only its own row block of both. It applies to batches of 18-256 rows for the front and 13-256 rows for the tail; the window is a row count, so extends of those sizes are covered too.

Against the raw port (the first commit):
- `_fused_front`: main's inline replicated front moves into the source's `_fused_front` helper, copied byte for byte. #48504 adds the same helper.
- The two new `TensorMatcher` entry points use main's `kDLGPU` alias (#47300).
- No API change for the source's callers: every name and signature here matches the source.

Left for the port of the GB300 decode-GEMM tactics (`SGLANG_K31_DECODE_GEMM_TACTICS`, not on main): the `(896, 3584)` latent-up slice entry of that port's TGV tactic table, and the comment on it. Until then, the TGV slice GEMM uses the default tactic ladder.

Related: #45126 (open) shards only the latent rows of the same front, with fp8-quantized gathered activations, for M in {1, 8} under deferred finalize. Its window does not overlap this one (18-256 rows, fp32 router and latent). Whichever lands second needs a rebase in `_forward_fused`.

## Modifications

- **Sharded MoE front** (`models/kimi_k3.py`)
  - For 18 <= M <= 256 (`_SHARDED_FRONT_MIN_TOKENS` / `_SHARDED_FRONT_MAX_TOKENS`), the 4480 `[router | latent]` rows are split into one contiguous block per TP rank (560 rows at TP8).
  - `_merge_front_weights` puts a copy of the rank's block in front of the merged weight's buffer (`_lead_with_rows_copy`). `[block | gate_up]` is then one fp32-out GEMM, and the replicated `[gate_up | router | latent]` weight stays the same view.
  - A new fp32 multicast all-gather assembles the blocks into exactly the replicated front's `[router | latent]` columns.
  - The shared experts and their all-reduce (16 blocks, the tuned table's value, instead of 4) are queued on the side stream before the routed `gemm1`, which fills every SM.
  - Below 18 rows the gather plus the block GEMM cost more than the replicated read saves. The choice depends only on M, so each captured CUDA graph uses one front and every rank picks the same one.
- **fp32 multicast all-gather** (`kimi_k3/comm/moe_front_ag.cuh`, op `moe_front_all_gather`): pushes the row-strided `[M, n_local]` blocks through CustomAllReduceV2's push workspace. This is the Lamport protocol that the K3 push all-reduce and `gemm_ag` already use.
- **Sharded latent-up tail** (`kimi_k3/comm/gemm_ag.cuh`, `ops/communication/gemm_ag.py`, `k3_ar_fusion.py`)
  - The TP world size is a template parameter (2 / 4 / 8). The spin consumer strides over the output and widens its block, so it covers any M that fits a push slot.
  - New `gather_add3` kernel: pushes a precomputed `[M, 7168 / tp]` slice and assembles `out = slice + b (+ c)` in the same kernel.
  - `gemm_ag_up_fits` covers M up to 256 (`_SHARDED_UP_MAX_TOKENS`). Up to 12 rows, the fused GEMV producer runs unchanged; above that, the rank's row block runs through `slice_gemm` and then `gather_add3`.
  - `gemm_ag.MAX_TOKENS` becomes `GEMV_MAX_TOKENS`, plus `WORLD_SIZES`.
- **Slice GEMM dispatch** (`k3_ar_fusion.slice_gemm`, shared by the front block and the up_proj slice)
  - Under the `cutedsl` bf16 backend (what `auto` resolves to on SM10x): warp split-K for CUDA-graph-captured batches up to 32 rows, because it compiles per M, and only when N is a multiple of 16, its smallest output tile (the TP16 front block is 1048 rows); TGV otherwise.
  - Other backends use `torch.mm` / `F.linear`.
- **Switch**: `SGLANG_K3_SHARDED_MOE` (default on). Setting it to `0` restores the replicated front for every batch and limits the tail to the fused-GEMV range.
- **Online weight updates** (`update_weights_from_*`) are rejected while the block copy exists, through the `_derived_weight_cache_error` hook. An in-place weight write would not refresh the copy.

Unchanged:
- the replicated front and its schedule outside the window;
- EP a2a / MegaMoE layers;
- ROCm;
- `SGLANG_K3_AR_FUSION=0`;
- TP sizes that do not split the rows into whole 16-byte fp32 vectors (no block copy is made there).

Router logits and the latent stay fp32 end to end. Weights, shared experts and the all-reduce stay BF16.

Cost: +8 MB of weight per MoE layer at TP8. On the source this measured +0.66 GB per GPU, and the KV pool shrank by 1.4% (TP8/DCP8/EP2 agg, `--mem-fraction-static 0.88`).

## Tests

- `test_moe_front_ag.py` (new; registered where `test_collectives.py` runs, `4-gpu-b200` base-c and `8-gpu-b200` nightly): the gather is checked bit-exact against an NCCL all-gather of row-strided blocks at M 18 / 96 / 256. The checks cover CUDA-graph replay and runs interleaved with the push all-reduce. It skips below SM100 or without multicast.
- `test_collectives.py::test_gemm_all_gather`: runs at world 2 / 4 / 8 (it was TP8 only), at M 1 / 12 / 13 / 256 (both sides of the GEMV / gather boundary and the cap), with and without `c`. The `gather_add3` result is checked bit-exact against NCCL-gathered slices over three push-plane phase rounds.

Results recorded on the source (GB300), on revisions before the tests were trimmed to these cases:
- `test_moe_front_ag.py`: 12/12 at TP4 and TP2.
- `test_gemm_all_gather`: 14/14 at world 4 and world 2.
- Front equivalence against the replicated front (real `KimiK3MoE`, K3.1 dims): top-16 ids identical on every row. At M >= 96, logits, latent and MoE output are bitwise identical. At M <= 48, fp32 |diff| <= 5.5e-5, which is GEMM reduction order.
- Tail equivalence: TGV slices are bit-identical to the replicated tail. Warp split-K slices differ by at most 1 BF16 ulp on 0.035% of elements.

At this head: `pre-commit run --all-files` is clean, and every touched Python file compiles. The GPU tests have not been rerun at this head yet.

## Speed

All numbers are from the source on GB300 (Kimi-K3.1 FP4), not from this head. On main, the up_proj TGV slice uses the default tactic ladder instead of the source's tuned GB300 tactic (see "Left for" above).

Front GEMM, TP8 per GPU (CUDA graph, cold weights, µs per layer):

| M | 6 | 24 | 48 | 96 | 216 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| replicated 6016-row front | 14.4 | 14.9 | 15.6 | 18.3 | 23.0 |
| 560-row block | 4.1 | 4.9 | 6.4 | 6.9 | 7.4 |

With gate_up folded in (2096 rows at TP8), the block GEMM takes 6.9-8.0 µs with warp split-K (captured M <= 32) and 8.2-10.5 µs with TGV, against 9.7-13.1 µs for cuBLAS.

Shared-expert schedule (2 x GB300, TP8/DCP8/EP2, DFLASH 6 draft tokens):
- The exposed wait in front of the latent all-reduce dropped from 18-20 µs to 0.5 µs per MoE layer.
- Decode step: -0.97 ms at N=8, -1.09 ms at N=20 (128K context), and -0.69 / -0.84 ms at N=36 (32K / 128K).

Latent-up tail (one GB300 node, CUDA graph, latent AR + RMSNorm in front, µs per layer, slowest rank):

| M (bs) | TP4 replicated | TP4 sharded | Δ TP4 | Δ TP2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 6 (1) | 11.86 | 11.86 | 0.00 (GEMV both) | 0.00 |
| 18 (3) | 15.22 | 11.57 | -3.65 | -2.16 |
| 48 (8) | 17.05 | 14.33 | -2.72 | -1.01 |
| 144 (24) | 28.95 | 25.55 | -3.40 | -0.34 |
| 216 (36) | 32.61 | 31.32 | -1.29 | +0.47 |

At TP8, the slice GEMM takes 2.3-5.0 µs, against 9.6-14 µs for the replicated GEMM.

AgentX on GB300 NVL72 (agentic multi-turn trace, 3600 s, DFLASH with 6 draft tokens, `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=4.12`), one agg TP8/DCP8/EP2 worker, one run per arm:
- Tail alone, c8: the median decode step at bs 3 / 4 / 5 is 0.35-0.55 ms faster than a fast-mode baseline, and 1.1-1.2 ms faster than a slow-mode one. bs 1-2 is unchanged (GEMV path). tok/s/GPU is +1.3%.
- Stack including this PR, c4: 3,569 -> 3,713 tok/s/GPU (+4.0%), P90 tok/s/user 204.9 -> 227.0, GSM8K 0.9689 -> 0.9704. This is a stack A/B; the microbenchmarks above give this PR's share.
- Why the 18-row floor: a revision without it was 0.43 / 0.37 ms slower at bs 1 / 2.

title: [Perf] kimi-k3: Fuse the decode MoE routing for 1-256 rows into one kernel
author: nvpohanh
body:
[by Claude Code]

Original authors: @nvpohanh, @kpham-sgl, @zcnrex

## Port of #48414

In every Kimi-K3 / K3.1 decode MoE layer, a serial chain of small kernels runs between the router and the routed experts. It is `route_quant_fused` (top-16 of 896 plus the MXFP8 quant), then the padded-row mask, then trtllm-gen's routing kernel inside `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`, which builds the expert-sorted permutation. #48414 replaces the chain with one kernel for 1-256 rows and any local expert range. The routed MoE then runs only its GEMMs, from that kernel's metadata, through FlashInfer's prepared-routing body. This PR ports that: the kernel with its op and test, the `route_quant_handoff` / `select_experts` / `KimiK3MoE` wiring, and the MXFP4 runner's prepared-routing entry.

This PR differs from #48414 in three ways:
- **Named for Kimi-K3, not K3.1.** K3 and K3.1 share the MoE that the kernel is specialized for: 896 experts, top-16 by sigmoid plus bias with no groups, a 3584-wide latent, and MXFP4 trtllm-gen SiTU experts. Their checkpoint configs differ only in K3.1's `dsa_config`. Both models run `KimiK3MoE`, so the fused path already ran on K3. `kimi_k31_fused_routing` is now `kimi_k3_fused_routing`, and the `K31*` symbols are now `KimiK3*`.
- **No kill switch.** `SGLANG_K31_FUSED_ROUTING` is removed. Every case that the fused path cannot serve already falls back to the unfused chain.
- **SM107 with FlashInfer < 0.7.3 keeps the unfused chain.** On SM107, FlashInfer 0.7.2 builds no FP4 tile-192 kernels and turns MoE PDL off, and #48414 mirrored both rules. This PR skips SM107 on those versions instead. The prepared path then passes `trtllm_moe_enable_pdl(num_tokens)`, as the routed call does. It no longer reads FlashInfer's private `_device_support_moe_pdl`, which 0.7.3 deletes (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6271). The check can go once #48468 moves the pin to 0.7.3.

Nothing is left for a later port: every fused-routing hunk of #48414 is in this PR.

## Modifications

- **Kernel** (`kimi_k3_fused_routing.cuh`, `kernels/ops/moe/kimi_k3_fused_routing.py`). It covers the MoE that Kimi-K3 and K3.1 share: 896 experts, top-16 by sigmoid score plus correction bias with no expert groups, and a 3584-wide activation quantized to MXFP8. A `static_assert` pins these values. It builds in the `route_quant_fused.cuh` TU.
  - CTAs `[0, M)` run `route_quant_fused`'s routing body and CTAs `[M, 2M)` its MXFP8 quant body. Ids, weights and quantized activations are therefore bit-identical to the unfused chain.
  - Each routing CTA sets its row's ids to -1 when the row is padding (`num_token_non_padded`). It also writes the trtllm-gen expert weights: BF16 up to 64 rows and FP32 above, as the routed call does.
  - The last routing CTA builds the metadata that trtllm-gen's `routingPermutation` would, using one histogram over the local experts and a block scan. It handles non-local routes (-1), padded rows, the tile of the autotuned tactic, and experts that span several tiles.
  - The routing CTAs fire the PDL trigger right after the top-k select, so the routed MoE's first GEMM launches under the metadata tail. Its `griddepcontrol.wait` still waits for the whole grid.
- **Runner** (`flashinfer_trtllm.py`).
  - `select_trtllm_routed_body` looks up the tactic that FlashInfer's autotuner picks for the routed call at this M, using the same runner, inputs and tuning config. It returns that tactic as FlashInfer's `DABody`, so the GEMM kernels are unchanged. It returns None on SM107 with FlashInfer < 0.7.3.
  - `_run_trtllm_prepared_routing_moe` runs the GEMMs, and the finalize unless it is deferred, through `MoERunner.forward` with `da_routing_metadata` / `da_body_workspace`.
  - The MXFP4 trtllm-gen SiTU path takes the prepared routing when the handoff published one for its ids.
- **Wiring**.
  - `KimiK3MoE._forward_routed` / `_forward_routed_deferred` stage the routed-experts layer together with the rows.
  - `select_experts` binds the padded-row bound. It also records whether its post-processing keeps the router's ids: no expert-location dispatch, no routing override and no shared slots.
  - `route_quant_handoff.try_route_quant_fused` runs the Kimi-K3 kernel when it covers the call and a prepared body was selected. Otherwise it runs `route_quant_fused` as before.
  - `stage()` and `clear()` reset the whole handoff record, so the new per-layer fields cannot leak into the next layer. This reset and the `_publish()` helper come from #46484.
- **Fallback**. Any miss keeps the unfused chain: another runner, autotuning in progress, more than 256 rows, a different MoE shape, or SM107 with FlashInfer < 0.7.3. No dtype changes.

#46475 / #46484 (both open) fuse the same chain for M <= 8, but only on a layer that holds all 896 experts, so at EP2 (448 local experts) they fall back. This path covers any expert range and 1-256 rows.

## Tests

These ran at c10af883bc (after merging main) on one B200 with `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` (FlashInfer 0.7.2) and this branch's `python/` first on `PYTHONPATH`:
- `test_kimi_k3_prepared_routing.py`: passed in 96 s. It is registered on `base-b-kernel-unit` / `4-gpu-b200`. It compares the prepared body bitwise against the unfused routed call at EP2 rank 1, with:
  - M = 6, 65 and 192;
  - FlashInfer's default and autotuned tactics;
  - finalized output and deferred finalize;
  - 3 padded rows.

  It also asserts that the prepared body ran. Building the metadata for twice FlashInfer's default tile makes all 6 default-tactic subtests fail.
- `test_kimi_k3_fused_routing.py`: passed, 9 subtests. They cover M 1-256, padded rows, expert ranges, tiles 8-256, and rows whose experts span two tiles. Outputs are checked bitwise against `route_radix` + `per_token_group_quant`, and the metadata against the trtllm-gen contract.
- `test_route_quant_prerequisites.py`: 3 passed. These cover the unfused `route_quant_fused` path.
- Routed-MoE parity, the full manual script that the test above trims: **240/240 bitwise on the valid rows**, and every case went through the prepared body. The script compares the fused path against the unfused chain. Both run through `_fused_experts_flashinfer_mxfp4_sm100_trtllm_gen` with random MXFP4 weights. It covers:
  - EP2 rank 0 and rank 1 (448 local experts, intermediate 768) and EP1 (896 experts, intermediate 384);
  - M = 1, 6, 12, 24, 48, 64, 65, 96, 192, 256;
  - FlashInfer's default and autotuned tactics;
  - the finalized output, and deferred finalize (expert weights, plus `gemm2_out` rows matched through `expanded_idx_to_permuted_idx`);
  - all rows valid, and 3 padded rows.
- pre-commit: all hooks pass.

End-to-end results come from the Kimi-K3.1 development branch that #48414 was squashed from (GB300, Kimi-K3.1-Pro). They compare fused routing on against off, using that branch's switch. They were not re-run on this branch. Kimi-K3 was not run end to end; its MoE layers have the shapes that the parity script covers.
- TP8/DCP8: greedy outputs were identical on 4 prompts. GSM8K (sgl-eval 0.1.3, 200 examples, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95) was 98.5% on vs 99.0% off.
- TP8/DCP8/EP2 with DFLASH: greedy outputs were identical. GSM8K was 98.0% on vs 97.5% off.

## Speed

These numbers are from the development branch on GB300 and were not re-measured here. The setup is a Kimi-K3.1-Pro decode step at aggregated TP8/DCP8/EP2, with DFLASH verifying 6 tokens per request and acceptance pinned at 3.69. Each request has an 8K-token context. The two arms are fused routing off and on, with one server start each.

| Requests | MoE rows (M) | Before (ms) | After (ms) | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 6 | 13.51 | 13.32 | -0.20 (-1.4%) |
| 2 | 12 | 16.42 | 15.67 | -0.74 (-4.5%) |
| 4 | 24 | 19.97 | 19.49 | -0.48 (-2.4%) |
| 8 | 48 | 24.75 | 23.82 | -0.93 (-3.8%) |
| 16 | 96 | 31.33 | 30.78 | -0.55 (-1.8%) |
| 32 | 192 | 41.90 | 41.59 | -0.31 (-0.7%) |

A torch profiler trace on rank 0 shows the routing kernels across the 92 MoE layers of one decode step. They take 1.00 / 1.73 / 1.76 ms before and 0.87 / 0.90 / 1.16 ms after, at 1 / 4 / 16 requests. Per-start FlashInfer autotuner tactic choice moves the step time by up to about 0.6 ms, so the changes at 1 and 32 requests are within noise.

title: [Feat] dsa: Exact multicast top-k merge for DCP decode
author: hnyls2002
body:
Original authors: @yhyang201, @Oasis-Git

## Port of #48414

Under DCP, the Kimi-K3.1 Day-0 branch (#48414) shards the DSA indexer's index-K cache by token: each rank selects a local top-k and the ranks merge them into the global top-k. This PR ports the merge for decode rows: one kernel that exchanges candidates over NVLink multicast and selects the global top-k exactly. It comes with a test and has no caller yet.

Against the raw port, the context-split verify mode (`split`) is dropped; the merge is built with `DcpTopKMerge.create(group, max_rows, topk, dcp_rank)`, which returns None where it cannot run and asserts that the group rank is the rank the candidates encode (the constructor and `usable()`'s buffer check go); it takes `dcp_rank` / `out_slots` / `multicast_ptr` throughout; its keys tie -0 with +0, as #48501's deterministic local top-k does, so a DCP row selects what one GPU would; and the test calls #48501's candidate top-k with `dcp_size` / `dcp_rank` / `deterministic=True`. Left for the sharded indexer PR: `init_dcp_topk_merge` and the rest of `dsa_dcp_sharded.py`. Left for target verify under DCP: the split mode.

## Modifications

- **Merge kernel** (`dcp_topk_merge.cuh`, `dcp_topk_merge.py`): one CTA per row. Each rank pushes its best 384 candidates to every rank with multimem stores, selects the k-th key among all candidates, and checks a certificate. Where a rank may hold more of the global top-k, the kernel reads that rank's full local top-k and selects again. It writes this rank's keys at or above the k-th key as widened KV slots, -1 after them. Each entry carries an 8-bit epoch tag, so no flag is needed; two parity buffers alternate.
- **`DcpTopKMerge`** (`dsa_dcp_sharded.py`): `create` allocates the symmetric buffer and runs the rendezvous. It returns None unless there are 8 ranks (16 with the megakernel), top-k is 2048, the ranks share one NVLink domain, and multicast is available. Calls go on one stream, with the same rows in the same order on every rank.
- **PTX helpers** (`distributed/ptx.cuh`): a relaxed 64-bit system-scope load and store, and a 64-bit multimem store.

## Tests

- `test_dsa_dcp_topk_merge.py` (8 GPUs): every rank's merged slots equal its share of the global top-k on random, tied, single-rank-owns-top-k (fallback), signed-zero and short rows. A CUDA graph replays three alternating inputs until the epoch tag wraps. The signed-zero case fails without the -0 / +0 tie.
- Not covered: the test passes without `deterministic=True`, so it does not pin the local tie order the merge relies on; the 16-rank path has no test.

On 8 B300 GPUs at this head: 5 passed.

title: [Perf] deepseek_v4: call the current DeepGEMM paged MQA API for DSv4.1 decode
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

#48424 bumped sgl-deep-gemm to 0.2.6. In 0.2.6 the SM100 paged MQA API is varlen-only. The DSv4.1 low-ratio (c1/c2) indexers still called it with the 0.2.3 signature (positional `clean_logits` + `logits_dtype`) and built the schedule without `indices`, so DeepGEMM's shim routed every decode call to the frozen legacy kernel. In the DSv4.1 decode benchmark on VR that made paged MQA logits +20% per call at bs64 and +30% at bs256 against the Oct 30 stack.

## Modifications

- `PagedIndexerMetadata` builds the varlen schedule (one row per token, per-row lengths, request ids as `indices`) on SM100 with bf16 index weights and at least 96 query rows. Below that the legacy kernel stays: it is faster at bs8-16.
- `paged_logits_args` passes the per-row layout and `indices` to `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits`. The schedule is per chunk when the forward is row-chunked.
- The c4 indexer, sglang's JIT schedule and non-SM100 keep the legacy call.

The kernel this selects is exactly the one the 0.2.5 stack ran: `sm100_paged_mqa_logits<32,128,128, block_q 4, 128, 2,8,3, split 384, ...>`.

## Accuracy

Logits new vs legacy are bitwise identical (whole and row-chunked), H32. Unit tests in `test_dsv4_nonpaged_indexer.py` pass on B300 (32 passed), including a new test for the 96-row gate.

## Speed

VR, page 128, 65536 compressed columns, 4 rows/request, CUDA graph, with a big-code kernel between calls to keep the instruction cache cold as in production. Kernel time, new / legacy:

| bs | 8 | 16 | 24 | 32 | 48 | 64 | 128 | 256 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| shared 127K prefix (decode benchmark) | 1.00 | 0.99 | 0.92 | 0.91 | 0.86 | 0.86 | 0.81 | 0.79 |
| distinct contexts | 1.09 | 1.02 | 1.00 | 0.94 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.05 |

The gate selects the new kernel from bs 24 (96 rows). The benchmark shares one prefix across requests, so the paged KV stays in L2, and that is where the new kernel wins. In situ, the 0.2.5 kernel ran 0.836 (bs64) and 0.767 (bs256) of the legacy one. With distinct contexts the two kernels are within a few percent of each other.

title: [Perf] kimi-k3.1: Fuse MegaMoE padding masks, DSA indexer Q prep and CP row copies
author: Fridge003
body:
Original authors: @Fridge003

## Port of #48414

Fused kernels for Kimi-K3.1 PCP prefill (radixark/sglang-k31#51), the third PR of the split of #48504. Depends on the MegaMoE / BCG PR (base branch `k31-pcp/2-megamoe-bcg`).

Against the raw port: the head-gate kernel sits next to main's head-gate choice in the indexer split op (#46890), and is used only for Kimi's no-RoPE BF16 head gate.

**Split of #48504.** Stack: #48709 (core) → #48710 (MegaMoE / BCG / DFlash) → #48711 (fused kernels) → #48712 (PP × PCP BCG). Independent: #48713 (shared-expert TP across PCP), #48714 (trtllm DSA), #48715 (Linker PCP L3).

## Modifications

- **`mega_moe_pre_dispatch`** (JIT, `moe/dsv4.py`): an optional device count of live rows. The kernel zeroes the input of padding rows and routes them to (-1, 0), and the count is read on every replay. This replaces the Python mask before dispatch from the previous PR.
- **`attention.indexer_q_quant_head_gate`** (Triton): Kimi's indexer Q quantization plus BF16 head-gate scaling in one kernel. It matches `act_quant` and `float(bf16(gate * heads**-0.5)) * q_scale * softmax_scale` bit for bit.
- **`memory.interleave_rows`** (Triton): coalesced copies between interleave CP rank order and sequence order. Used by the KDA reorder and the aligned CP gather; uneven or non-contiguous inputs keep the existing fallbacks.

## Accuracy Tests

Measured on sglang-k31 dev with the original PR (not re-run on this branch):

- GSM8K first 500: 489/500 = 97.8%.
- AIME26 30 × 16: 441/480 = 91.875%.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8× B300, PCP8 + EP8 MegaMoE + BCG + DFlash2, `bench_one_batch_server` BS1 / ISL8192 / OSL1. Median TTFT:

- dev: 273.9 ms
- this change: 265.4 ms
- dev repeat: 275.2 ms

That is 3.1–3.6% lower.

## Tests

- `test_indexer_q_quant_head_gate.py`: bit-exact against `act_quant` plus the reference gate, including under CUDA graph replay.
- `test_mega_moe_pre_dispatch.py`: the live-row count changes across replays of one graph, with NaN padding rows.

title: [Feat] cuda-graph: Kimi-K3.1 breakable prefill graphs with PP x prefill CP
author: Fridge003
body:
Original authors: @yhyang201

## Port of #48414

Breakable prefill CUDA graphs with pipeline parallelism × interleave prefill CP for Kimi-K3.1 (radixark/sglang-k31#80), the last PR of the stack split from #48504. Depends on the fused-kernel PR (base branch `k31-pcp/3-fused-kernels`).

Against the raw port:

- The PP admission in `InterleaveCPBCGInput.supports` is added to main's version (#46890); only Kimi-K3.1 relaxes `pp_size == 1`.
- The test fixture no longer sets `_trtllm_fused_q`, which nothing on main reads.

**Split of #48504.** Stack: #48709 (core) → #48710 (MegaMoE / BCG / DFlash) → #48711 (fused kernels) → #48712 (PP × PCP BCG). Independent: #48713 (shared-expert TP across PCP), #48714 (trtllm DSA), #48715 (Linker PCP L3).

## Modifications

- **BCG under PP** (`cp/bcg/`, `prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py`, `cuda_graph_setup.py`):
  - A later stage takes the previous stage's CP-local hidden states, so only the positions are sharded.
  - Middle stages send the rows an eager stage would send, so the next stage may replay or run eagerly on the same shard.
  - The PP proxy is sized per capture bucket to its CP-local rows, and rows past the received shard are zeroed so a replay never reads stale rows.
  - Zigzag BCG keeps `pp_size == 1`.
- **FlashMLA sparse** (`dsa_backend.py`): pad this rank's logical query rows up to the physical metadata rows (zero queries, -1 indices), then trim the output.

## Accuracy Tests

Kimi-K3.1 + DFlash2, 16 GB300 (PCP2 × PP4 prefill, TP8/DCP8 decode), TRT-LLM DSA, measured on sglang-k31 dev with the original PR (not re-run on this branch):

- GSM8K full: 1281/1319 = 97.12%.
- AIME26 pass@1: 453/480 = 94.38%.

## Tests

`test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner_helpers.py`: PP proxy rows of a CP bucket, and zeroing of the rows past the received shard.

## Review notes

The FlashMLA row padding is not limited to interleave CP. #48598 fixes the same query / metadata row mismatch (DP padding under prefill graphs) from the other side, trimming the metadata to the query rows, so the two changes need one approach.

title: [Perf] mega_moe: reserve 18 SMs for MegaMoE in sm107 decode and target-verify
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

In decode and target-verify, DeepSeek-V4.1 runs the next sublayer's mHC stats (`tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` + sinkhorn) on `hc_stats_stream`, beside MegaMoE. MegaMoE takes every SM except `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_RESERVED_SMS` (default 2). That margin keeps the clustered grid barrier launchable, but it leaves the stats GEMM 2 SMs. Its CTAs need ~206 KB of shared memory, so it cannot share an SM with MegaMoE. It finishes after MegaMoE, and the consumer of the stats waits for it.

Reserving more SMs in prefill only slows MegaMoE, because there is no stats stream there. So the extra reservation is limited to decode and target-verify.

## Modifications

- On sm107, MegaMoE launches in decode and target-verify reserve 18 SMs (`max(SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_RESERVED_SMS, 18)`). Prefill and extend, and every other architecture, keep `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_RESERVED_SMS` as before. No new env var.
- Only the MegaMoE kernel launch uses the decode budget. The symmetric buffer and the mega gate keep the base budget; the decode budget can only be smaller, so the buffer's SM budget still covers the launch.
- Unit test for the gating; one existing test fixture gains `forward_mode`.
- Measured on sm107 only. Other architectures have different SM counts and side-stream grids, so they are left unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

The SM count does not change the math: MegaMoE outputs were bitwise identical at 210, 194, 178 and 162 SMs in a kernel-level replay.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

DeepSeek-V4.1, 16-rank DEP decode (attention DP 16, EP 16), 3 draft tokens, simulated acceptance 3.25, 127K-token cached prefix, balanced routing. Step time ratio = this setting / base (lower is faster). Two runs per arm, interleaved A B B A.

sm107. Reserving 18 SMs, first for every MegaMoE call (`RESERVED_SMS=18`) and then decode/target-verify only (this PR):

| requests / rank | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| reserve 18 everywhere | 1.004 | 1.000 | 0.964 | 0.977 | 0.971 | 1.000 |
| this PR (decode/verify only) | 1.004 | 1.001 | 0.961 | 0.977 | 0.969 | 0.998 |

Prefill MegaMoE (kernel level, 16K tokens/rank) gets ~7% slower on 194 SMs, which is why the global setting is not the default.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit test: `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_mega_moe_deepgemm_api.py`

title: [Fix] gemm: Keep Kimi-K3's tiny GEMM shapes on SIMT at every batch size
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

`test/registered/e2e/models/test_kimi_k3_b300_low_latency.py::TestKimiK3B300LowLatency::test_bs_1_speed` (NV Extra, `extra-b-test-8-gpu-b300`) fails deterministically on PRs tested against current main: the accept length is **3.4594594594594597** against the 4.0 threshold, on both retries and on every PR.

PR runs of this test, by the main commit CI merged each PR onto:

| main base | result | PR |
|---|---|---|
| `b147f4aa10` | pass | deps/transformers-5-21 |
| `1305b1830a` | **3.4595** | codex/pp-arrival-match-main |
| `89b2641381` | **3.4595** | fix-mamba-copy-from-temporal-oom, feat/hicache-mamba-request-end, fix/hicache-prefetch-swa-match-boundary |
| `3fa242f27c` | **3.4595** | deps/transformers-5-21, codex/pp-arrival-match-main |
| `c03b6b3df5` | **3.4595** | fix-mamba-copy-from-temporal-oom |
| `06c60f412a` | **3.4595** | #48715 |

The only PR that still passes on these bases is #48468 (FlashInfer 0.7.3), which changes the MXFP4 MoE runner Kimi-K3 uses and so changes its numerics anyway.

Of the main commits in `b147f4aa10..1305b1830a`, only #47683 reaches Kimi-K3's TP8 + DSpark decode path:

- #47866 (CuTe DSL KDA decode) only runs with `--linear-attn-decode-backend cutedsl`; this test uses triton.
- #47678 (DFlash decode prep) fills the same buffers.
- #47785 (Qwen3 QK norm) and #48588 (DSA DCP top-k) do not reach Kimi-K3.
- The rest are docs, NPU, AMD, CI and diffusion.

#47683 makes the tiny GEMM switch from the SIMT to the MMA kernel at a batch size picked per shape. Each kernel alone is batch invariant, but a row's result depends on the batch through that switch. Kimi-K3 runs its KDA gate and router projections through `kimi_k3_tiny_gemm`:

| (N, K) | MMA from m = | bs=1 decode (m = 1) | 8-token verify (m = 8) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 144 × 7168 | 2 (cost model, B300) | SIMT | MMA |
| 896 × 7168 | 2 (cost model, B300) | SIMT | MMA |
| 1536 × 128 | 8 (tuned) | SIMT | MMA |

So the same token's gates round differently in decode and in speculative verify.

## Modifications

Pin the three Kimi-K3 shapes to SIMT at every m in `_TUNED_MMA_MIN_M`, as `128x512` already is. Other tiny GEMM callers (DeepSeek routers, DeepSeek-V4.1, beam, dots3) use other shapes and are unchanged.

## Validation

**Draft until confirmed:** I had no free B300 to bisect on, so the root cause above comes from elimination plus the dispatch rule. `/rerun-test` of the failing test on this PR decides it.

- If it passes, this goes ready for review.
- If it fails, the next step is to check #47683 directly.

body:
## Motivation

`index_q_rope_pack_weights` (`index_q_kernel` in `fp4_indexer_rope.cuh`) applies RoPE and two-stage fp4 packing to the DeepSeek-V4.1 indexer query and also writes the head weights. It gives each (token, head) row of 128 bf16 to one warp, which per row means:
- 4-byte loads;
- four 16-lane max reductions and two shuffles;
- two 1-byte payload stores per lane;
- 4-warp CTAs.

That shape was chosen from decode measurements and suits decode. At prefill sizes it runs far from memory bandwidth. On VR200 a 32768-token chunk with 32 index heads (1M rows, ~340 MB of traffic, ~26 us at HBM speed) took 251 us per indexer layer.

## Modifications

- `index_q_block_kernel` gives each 32-element fp4 block to one thread: four threads per row, 256-thread CTAs of 64 rows. Warps 0-3 take the head blocks and warps 4-7 the RoPE blocks, so the RoPE branch is warp-uniform. Each thread does:
  - all of its loads before any math: the input block, plus its `freqs_cis` slice for the RoPE half, as `kMaxVecBytes` vectors (32 bytes on Blackwell);
  - the RoPE of its tail pairs;
  - both block absmaxes as trees seeded with 0;
  - the fake quant up to the e2m1 grid value, then the packer's exponent read from the grid amax's biased exponent (no division) and the e2m1 codes, with the two power-of-two scales folded into one multiply;
  - one 16-byte payload store and one byte of the row's little-endian scale word.

  The row's first thread writes the head weight. The current version of the kernel is @zcnrex's from review (about 10-23% faster than the first version, same bytes).
- **Bitwise:** every fp4 stage of `index_rope_quant_pack` works per element except the block absmax, and a max is exact in any order, so the bytes match the warp kernel's. Both kernels write the RoPE products with `__fmaf_rn` / `__fmul_rn` as `fma(x, fx, -(y * fy))` and `fma(x, fy, y * fx)`, so they match by construction. For `index_rope_quant_pack` (warp kernel and index-K) that is the contraction nvcc already chose, so its bits are unchanged. Left to nvcc, the block kernel contracted the imaginary part the other way and differed in rare last bits.
- **Dispatch:** `IndexQKernel::launch` takes the block kernel for calls of at least 8192 (token, head) rows on SM100-family GPUs (CC 10.x). The gate counts rows, so decode reaches it too: with 4-token speculative verify and 32 index heads, 64 requests per rank make 8,192 rows, and decode graphs at bs >= 64 capture the block kernel (it is also faster at that size). Smaller batches, other GPUs and ROCm keep `index_q_kernel` unchanged. The PDL wait placement is the same as in the warp kernel.
- **Alignment:** on the block-kernel path, `launch` checks 32-byte alignment of `input` and `freqs_cis` and 16-byte alignment of `payload`, so a misaligned view raises a clear error instead of a misaligned-address fault.

## Accuracy Tests

The change is bitwise, so no model-level accuracy run is needed. The new test `test_index_q_rope_pack_prefill_matches_decode_kernel` covers this. It runs 4100 tokens x 32 heads as one call (131,200 rows, block kernel) and as 128-token calls (4,096 rows each, warp kernel), and requires payload, scale words and head weights to be equal. The inputs cover seven families: normal, per-row scales of exp(6 N(0,1)), sparse with signed zeros, below both fp4 amax floors, values on e2m1 rounding ties, per-row scales of 2^U(-150, 126), and 0.3% each of inf / -inf / nan. It runs with int32 and int64 positions, and skips unless the GPU is CC 10.x (elsewhere both calls take the warp kernel). It passed 14/14 on VR200 with this branch.

The updated kernel was also compared directly with the first block kernel of this PR on VR200: payload, scale words and head weights of both Q kernels, plus the index-K slot bytes, on the seven families x 9 shapes (128 / 255 / 256 / 257 / 4100 / 32768 tokens x 32 heads, 2731 x 3, 8193 x 1) x int32 / int64 positions, are identical in all 126 cases.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

VR200 (SM107), one GPU, 32 heads x 128, bf16 head weights. CUDA graph of 20 calls, us per call:

| tokens | rows | `main` | first version | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | 4,096 | 1.9 | 1.9 | 1.9 (warp kernel, unchanged) |
| 255 | 8,160 | 2.5 | 2.5 | 2.5 (warp kernel, unchanged) |
| 256 | 8,192 | 2.5 | 2.1-2.2 | 1.6-1.7 |
| 1,024 | 32,768 | 6.4 | 3.6 | 2.7 |
| 8,192 | 262,144 | 52.2 | 16.2 | 13.7 |
| 32,768 | 1,048,576 | 251.1 | 60.3-60.4 | 55.4 (4.5x) |

The first-version and current columns are three alternating rounds each in one job; the `main` column is from an earlier job. B300 numbers for both versions are in the review thread.

End to end on 4x VR200 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 prefill with 32K-token chunks per rank), the first version of this kernel together with two DeepGEMM MQA-logits epilogue changes (sgl-project/DeepGEMM #138 and #140) gave +1.0% prefill throughput. The index-Q part alone saves about 0.6 ms per 192 ms forward: three indexer layers, ~190 us each.

## Testing

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_fp4_indexer.py::test_index_q_rope_pack_prefill_matches_decode_kernel`: 14 passed on VR200 against this branch's JIT build. It skips outside CC 10.x, where both calls take the warp kernel, so it needs a Blackwell runner (`/rerun-test`).
- Whole `test_fp4_indexer.py` on VR200: 108 passed, 2 skipped, 6 failed. The 6 failures are `test_fp4_paged_logits_replay` cases whose `topk_v2` JIT module fails to build in my VR200 environment; they fail the same way on the previous head of this PR. On B300 the file passes (110 passed, 2 skipped, per the review thread).
- The pre-commit hooks pass, including clang-format.

## Limitations

- Measured on VR200 here, and on B300 in review. The gate covers the whole SM100 family because the cost being removed (per-row shuffles and byte stores of a warp-per-row layout) does not depend on the SM variant. B200 and GB300 timings would be welcome, and the gate can be narrowed if either regresses.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Perf] mhc: halve the DeepGEMM prenorm slices when the grid overflows one wave
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

`hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn_deepgemm` always splits K into 16 slices. Its two `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` calls launch `ceil(m / 64) x 16` CTAs, and each CTA's shared-memory footprint allows one CTA per SM. During DeepSeek-V4.1 decode at 256 requests per rank with 3 draft tokens (m = 1024 rows), that is 256 CTAs: more than one wave. The grid runs on `hc_stats_stream` beside MegaMoE, and its second wave holds SMs that the main-path kernels need.

## Modifications

- `_hc_mix_deepgemm_slices(m)`: 16 slices when `ceil(m / 64) * 16` CTAs fit in one wave, otherwise 8. The reduce/sinkhorn kernel already takes `NUM_SLICES=slices`, so both stages stay consistent.
- 8 is the floor. Error against an fp64 reference grows about linearly with K per slice. 8 slices doubles the 16-slice error, 4 quadruples it, and 2 is 8x.
- The `bf16x3` path keeps `_HC_MIX_COMPENSATED_SLICES`.

## Accuracy

Max abs error vs fp64 over pre/post/comb, hidden 7168 (K = 28672), relative to the 16-slice error at the same m:

| slices | m = 32 | 1024 | 4095 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 1.9x | 1.9x | 1.9x |
| 4 | 4.8x | 3.4x | 3.9x |
| 2 | 9.0x | 6.5x | 8.0x |

hidden 4096 follows the same pattern.

## Benchmark

Standalone `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn_deepgemm` time, 8 slices / 16 slices (CUDA graph, ABBA):

| m | hidden 4096 | hidden 7168 | grid at 16 slices |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 1.16 | 1.33 | one wave |
| 576 | 1.12 | 1.26 | one wave |
| 1024 | 0.76 | 0.80 | > one wave |
| 2048 | 0.77 | 0.83 | > one wave |
| 4095 | 0.82 | 0.90 | > one wave |
| 131072 | 0.75 | 0.86 | > one wave |

16 slices wins while the grid fits one wave, and 8 wins once it does not, so the rule switches on grid size.

In-situ DeepSeek-V4.1 decode (DEP16, MTP with 3 draft tokens), step time this PR / base, one run per arm:

| requests per rank | m | slices | with `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_DECODE_RESERVED_SMS=18` (#48723) | without |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 256 | 16 (unchanged) | 0.998 | 0.998 |
| 128 | 512 | 16 (unchanged) | 0.998 | 0.998 |
| 256 | 1024 | 8 | **0.980** | 1.001 |

The 64 and 128 rows run the same code in both arms, so they are controls (noise is about ±0.2%). The bs256 gain needs the decode SM reservation from #48723. Without it, MegaMoE leaves almost no SMs for the side stream, and the smaller grid saves nothing in that configuration. An earlier pair of runs with an env-gated 8-slice override reproduced the bs256 result: 0.983 with the reservation.

## Checklist

- [x] Accuracy vs fp64 checked
- [x] In-situ step time measured

title: [Perf] eplb: Vectorize the static per-rank dispatch map
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

With `ep_dispatch_algorithm=static`, every EPLB rebalance rebuilds the per-rank dispatch map in `compute_logical_to_rank_dispatch_physical_map`. It calls `_find_nearest_expert` in Python once per (layer, logical expert, rank). For DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at DEP32 that is 40 x 384 x 32 calls, which take 250-290 ms on every rank on each rebalance while the whole DP group waits.

## Modifications

- `_compact_candidates`: move each row's valid physical ids to the front, keeping their original order.
- `_nearest_expert_dispatch`: pick the same-GPU replica, otherwise the same-node replica when it narrows the candidate set, using tensor ops over the replica slots. Rows with a single replica broadcast it. This is the same rule as `_find_nearest_expert`, which still serves the startup collapse in `_compute_logical_to_all_physical_map`.
- Only the (layer, expert, rank) entries left unresolved still go through `_fair_choices` with the seeded `random.Random`, in the same row-major order. The output is therefore bitwise identical to the previous implementation.
- Scratch tensors are created on the input map's device, and `_logical_to_all_physical_raw`, which lost its last caller, is removed.

## Accuracy

Placement is unchanged. Bitwise comparisons against the previous function, all equal:

- 96 cases: 12 layouts x 2 shapes x 4 ranks, scattered -1 padding, with and without the node topology.
- 17,430 random layouts x ranks: ep 1-16, 1-8 nodes, scattered -1 padding, duplicate ids, int32/int64.
- 12,910 random layouts x ranks at the head: ep 1-32, 1-8 nodes, shuffled candidate order (so first-match order is exercised, not just smallest id), scattered -1 padding, duplicate ids, int32/int64, node preference on and off.

## Performance

Time per call:

| shape | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| 40 layers x 384 logical / 416 physical, ep 32 | 255 ms | 39 ms |
| 3 layers x 128 logical / 160 physical | 5.6 ms | 9.1 ms |

The small shape gets a few ms slower from tensor-op overhead; the large one, where the time matters, is 6.5x faster.

End to end, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash disaggregated serving on GB300 (DEP32 decode, 8 nodes), EPLB every 15000 iterations, AgentX 3600 s at concurrency 3018, one same-day run per arm:

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| rebalance pause p50 | 0.734 s | 0.467 s |
| total token throughput per GPU | 458.7k | 466.6k (+1.7%) |
| interactivity mean (tok/s/user) | 346.2 | 354.4 (+2.4%) |
| interactivity p90 (tok/s/user) | 326.7 | 339.8 (+4.0%) |
| TTFT p95 | 9.33 s | 7.81 s |

The rebalance pause shrinks by 0.27 s, in line with the per-call saving; that is the effect of this change. At one rebalance per 15000 iterations the pause is a small share of the run's wall time, so the throughput, interactivity, and TTFT deltas, from a single run per arm, are larger than the removed pause alone accounts for and should not be read as its effect. The gain grows with rebalance frequency and EP size.

## Related

#45282 (non-blocking EPLB rebalance) moves the rebalance off the forward thread but keeps calling this function, so the two are complementary; it adds a `device` argument to the same function, which is a small conflict.

title: [Chore] sgl-kernel: Remove the vendored FlashMLA build and wrappers
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

FlashMLA on CUDA now comes from the `sgl-flash-mla` wheel (pinned in `python/pyproject.toml`) through `sglang.kernels.ops.attention.flash_mla_interface`. No runtime path calls `sgl_kernel.flash_mla` / `sgl_kernel.flash_mla_mega` anymore, yet sgl-kernel still fetches and compiles the whole FlashMLA tree into `flashmla_ops`, which only costs build time and wheel size.

## Modifications

Under `python/sglang/kernels/aot/`:
- Drop `cmake/flashmla.cmake` and its `include` in `CMakeLists.txt` (no more `flashmla_ops` target).
- Drop `csrc/flashmla_extension.cc`, `csrc/flashmla_mega_extension.cc`, and the FlashMLA op declarations at the end of `include/sgl_kernel_ops.h`.
- Drop the Python wrappers `sgl_kernel/flash_mla.py` and `sgl_kernel/flash_mla_mega.py`.
- Drop `tests/test_flashmla.py`, `tests/test_flashmla_mega.py`, and `benchmark/bench_flashmla_mega.py`, which only exercised those wrappers. FlashMLA coverage stays in `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/` against the `sgl-flash-mla` interface.

Also repoint one SAIL docstring that referenced `sgl_kernel.flash_mla.get_mla_metadata`.

Not touched: the XPU branches in `dsa_backend.py` / `deepseek_v4_backend.py` that import `flash_mla_*` from `sgl_kernel` (they come from the XPU kernel package, not this CUDA build), the `sgl-flash-mla` wheel build/release scripts, and the JIT `flashmla_sched_meta` kernel.

## Checklist

- [x] `pre-commit` passes on touched files.
- [x] `git grep` finds no remaining reference to `flashmla_ops`, `sgl_kernel.flash_mla`, or the removed tests outside this diff (one comment in `docs/src/snippets/configs/moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro.jsx` mentions `flashmla_ops` in the external K3.1 image, left as is).
- [ ] sgl-kernel wheel build in CI (not built locally).

title: [Fix] overlap: Skip deferred-relay flush when future_map is None
author: nvpohanh
body:
[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

Fixes #48808. Since #47200, every LLaDA-Image request fails with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'takes_deferred_relay'`. This breaks `llada_image_bf16_t2i` and `llada_image_bf16_edit` in `multimodal-gen-test-1-gpu (1)` on every PR based on current `main`, for example https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42128128424/job/127658012603.

The LLaDA-Image conditioning stage runs a standalone prefill and calls `resolve_forward_inputs(batch, None)`. #47200 added an unconditional `future_map.takes_deferred_relay(batch)` call at the top of `resolve_forward_inputs`, which raises on `None`.

## Modifications

- `resolve_forward_inputs` skips the deferred-relay flush when `future_map` is `None`, because a caller without a `FutureMap` has no deferred relay.
- The `future_map` parameter is annotated as `Optional[FutureMap]`.

This restores the pre-#47200 behavior for the LLaDA-Image caller. Scheduler callers always pass `self.future_map`, so their behavior is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. No change to model outputs: this only restores the code path that LLaDA-Image used before #47200.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

title: [Perf] dspark: Prepare the DSpark draft attention metadata through the glue graph under every verify mode
author: Qiaolin-Yu
body:
Stack: **this PR** → #48832 → #48833

## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1 DSpark in compact verify (`SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact`) is slower per decode step than static verify, even when compact verifies every draft. Part of the gap is host work. The DSpark draft runner prepares its attention metadata through the metadata glue graph (#45450) only under static verify. Under the other modes it falls back to the eager prep: `init_forward_metadata_dspark_draft_block` and the prefill metadata it builds, a few dozen small launches per step.

The draft runner's replay path does not depend on the verify mode. `ragged_verify_mode` is set only on the target verify runner, and the draft block always extends each request by the block size. So the mode check in `_glues_draft_metadata` only switched the glue off.

## Modifications

- `DecodeCudaGraphRunner._glues_draft_metadata` no longer refuses the non-static verify modes. The backend's own checks (`glue_draft_metadata`) still decide.

## Accuracy Tests

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 4x B300, TP 4, EP 4, DSpark block size 5, compact verify. sgl-eval gsm8k, 200 questions, temperature 0, no thinking: 0.98. The server log confirms the draft prep runs through the glue graph.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same setup. One request per concurrency slot (`bench_serving` random 1536 in, 2048 out, `ignore_eos`), so the decode runs without new prefills. Each arm ran twice, alternating with main. Accept length moves between runs (5.03 to 5.24), so the table compares decode step time = mean TPOT x accept length, averaged over the two runs:

| step time (ms) | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| c=1 | 4.87 | 4.58 |
| c=16 | 12.21 | 12.01 |
| c=64 | 24.65 | 24.66 |

At c=64 the GPU step is long enough to hide the host prep. The first main run at c=1 (5.03 ms) is above the second (4.70 ms), so the c=1 gain is likely overstated.

title: [Perf] dsv4: Run compact target verify's ratio 1 and 2 compressors through the fused kernels
author: Qiaolin-Yu
body:
Stack: #48831 → **this PR** → #48833

## Motivation

Under compact verify (`SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact`), DeepSeek-V4.1's ratio 1 and 2 compressors run the general torch path, `_low_ratio_compress_torch`. Each of these layers then launches a chain of small torch kernels: the pair-partner lookup with `roll` / `where` / `masked_fill`, the gathers from the pair-state ring, the norm and the stores. Static verify uses the fused `c1` / `c2` kernels instead. On 4x B300 at concurrency 16 and 64, the torch chain was the largest compact-only GPU cost in the verify graph.

The fused ratio-2 kernel already has an extend mode (`c2_prefill_norm_rope_store`) that takes each request's first row and row count, and it handles exactly what compact verify needs:
- rows that mix requests;
- a partner taken from the previous row when that row is the same request's previous position, and from the pair-state ring otherwise;
- CUDA graph padding (`raw_out_loc == 0`) skipped in the pooling and in the ring write-back;
- each request's last `ring_size` rows saved to the ring.

A compact verify step is exactly such an extend: each request's packed block starts at `qo_indptr[i]` and spans `verify_lens[i]` rows.

## Modifications

- `DeepseekV4AttnBackend._low_ratio_compress`: target verify with a ragged layout under compact mode calls `_low_ratio_compress_fused` with `extend_offsets=(layout.qo_indptr_device[:-1], layout.verify_lens)`. In a replayed graph these are the captured layout's buffers, which the runner restages every replay. The ratio-1 kernel does not depend on the layout.

The rows of a staged graph layout are capped at the verify window, which is narrower than the pair-state ring, so the ring write-back covers every row of a request.

## Accuracy Tests

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 4x B300, TP 4, EP 4, DSpark block size 5, compact verify, with this stack: sgl-eval gsm8k, 200 questions, temperature 0, no thinking: 0.985. Accept length matches static verify on the same workload (about 5.0 at concurrency 1 to 64).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Torch profiler on TP 0, decode steps at concurrency 16 and 64 (`bench_serving` random 1536 in, 384 out, greedy). Main against this stack, kernels inside the verify graph per decode step:

| | main | this stack |
|---|---:|---:|
| kernels per verify step, c=16 | 1564 | 1381 |
| kernels per verify step, c=64 | 1730 | 1550 |
| torch elementwise kernel time per verify step, c=16 | 171 us | 22 us |
| torch elementwise kernel time per verify step, c=64 | 320 us | 159 us |

`roll`, `gather`, `reduce`, `_rmsnorm_fp32` and `_index_k_rope_pack` disappear from the compact verify graph. `flash_c2_decode`, `index_k` and `c2_prefill_store` take their place, as in static verify. The end-to-end step times for the whole stack are in #48833.
