title: [Chore] flash-attn: Remove the kernels-hub FA3 loader and the kernels dependency
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

The HuggingFace `kernels` package is used in exactly one place in SGLang: the opt-in path in `flash_attention_v3.py` that loads FA3 from `kernels-community/sgl-flash-attn3` (via `load_kernel` with `$SGLANG_CACHE_DIR/kernels.lock`, or `get_kernel` from the Hub). That path only runs when `SGLANG_USE_SGL_FA3_KERNEL=False`; by default FA3 already comes from `sgl_kernel.flash_attn`. Carrying a hard dependency, a pyproject lock section and a multi-step Docker download for a non-default path is not worth it.

## Modifications

- `flash_attention_v3.py`: remove the kernels-hub loader and its constants; `_load_fa3_kernels()` now imports from `sgl_kernel.flash_attn` directly. Drop the now-unused `logging` / `os` / `envs` imports.

- `docker/Dockerfile`, `docker/Dockerfile.cu134`: drop `kernels lock python`, the retried `kernels download python`, and the `kernels.lock` move into `/root/.cache/sglang/`.

title: [Feat] kimi-k3.1: Sync the prefill-CP review fixes from the port PRs
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

Brings the review fixes from the prefill-CP split PRs back into #48414, so this branch matches what the port PRs now carry. Review threads: #48709, #48710, #48711, #48712, #48713, #48714.

## Modifications

One commit per port PR, cherry-picked from its branch and adapted to this branch:

- **#48709**: Kimi-K3 hands its prefill-CP boundary to `EagerRunner._execute_extend_cp` through `prepare_cp_inputs` and drops the model-local `_forward_cp`.
  - The K3.1 multimodal wrapper injects image embeddings before sharding.
  - `_execute_extend_cp` changes in two places: it runs a wrapper LM's text body, and a middle PP stage returns before the aux unpack.
  - `cp_sequence_to_interleave_order` goes back to main's copy, with the `interleave_rows` fast path on top.
- **#48710**:
  - The BCG indexer split op returns to #46890's `in_cp` path: no live-row truncation, and no aiter gate. Two generic fixes stay: the top-k-reuse store under CP, and the -1 top-k tail.
  - Kimi MegaMoE no longer requires `--max-running-requests`, and the largest prefill forward must fit `NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK x ep_size`.

title: [Perf] layernorm: rmsnorm_mxfp8 on 2 warps for 1280-wide rows; hc_combine_norm loads its weight before the reduction
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

Two latency-bound Triton norm kernels of DeepSeek-V4.1, both changed without changing a bit of their outputs.

**`rmsnorm_mxfp8`**: `rmsnorm_mxfp8` (the DeepSeek-V4.1 `q_norm` before `wq_b`, 1280-wide rows) runs one row per 8-warp program with `BLOCK=2048`. 768 of the 2048 lanes are masked off, so 3 of the 8 warps hold no data but still take SM slots. At prefill sizes the kernel is latency-bound, and it sits on the critical path once per layer.

**`hc_combine_norm` / `hc_combine_norm_mxfp8`** (four-stream combine + RMSNorm, decode-sized batches): each loads its weight only after the row reduction's CTA barrier, so every CTA waits one more memory round trip before the epilogue.

## Modifications

`rmsnorm_mxfp8.py`:

- `_sumsq_8warp_order` writes out the order in which 8 warps reduce `tl.sum(v * v, 0)` over a 2048-element row: the pair tree inside each thread's 8 elements, the lane butterfly 16..1, then warps 4/2/1. Each step is a size-2 reduction over a reshape. A sum of two numbers gives the same result in any layout, so any `num_warps` produces the same bits as 8 warps.
- `rmsnorm_mxfp8` runs `BLOCK == 2048` rows on 2 warps with that order from 1024 rows. Below 1024 rows the extra programs do not pay, and the kernel is unchanged (8 warps, `tl.sum`).

`hc_combine_norm.py`:
- A `_combine` helper issues the four stream loads before the per-stream `pre` scalars that scale them. The zero-initialized accumulator is kept, so signed zeros are unchanged.
- `_hc_combine_norm` and `_hc_combine_norm_mxfp8_kernel` load their slice of the weight before the reduction, so its latency overlaps the cross-warp sum.

## Accuracy Tests

The change is bitwise, so no model-level accuracy run is needed.
- New test `test_k1280_matches_8warp_tl_sum` compares the op against the previous kernel (`tl.sum`, 8 warps):
  - rows: 1, 37, 129, 1023, 1024, 4095, 4096, 16385
  - row strides: 1280 and 1792
  - inputs: normal, per-row exp(3 N(0,1)) scales, 1e-30, 3e38, rounding ties, signed zeros
  - checks: y, q and the full scale buffer, including padding entries
- The existing FlashInfer-reference tests (`check`, CUDA-graph replay) still pass.
- `hc_combine_norm` and `hc_combine_norm_mxfp8` against the previous module in the same process: 0 mismatching bytes over 14 row counts (1 to 4095) x 3 input scales with signed zeros.
- On CC 10.7: `test_mxfp8_epilogue.py` 135 passed and `test_mhc_post_combine_norm_decode.py` 4 passed.
- On B300: `test_mxfp8_epilogue.py` passed with the `rmsnorm_mxfp8` commit.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

One GPU, 1280-wide bf16 rows viewed from a 1792-wide buffer (as in the model), CUDA graph of 50 calls, median of interleaved rounds. Each entry is this PR's time divided by the previous kernel's time.

| rows | CC 10.7 | B300 |
|---|---|---|
| 16384 | 0.492 | 0.615 |
| 8192 | 0.593 | 0.653 |
| 4096 | 0.645 | 0.695 |
| 2048 | 0.722 | 0.764 |
| 1024 | 0.858 | 0.906 |
| 512 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| 8 | 1.003 | 0.998 |

`hc_combine_norm(_mxfp8)`, CC 10.7, ratio to the previous kernels:

| rows | `hc_combine_norm` | `hc_combine_norm_mxfp8` |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0.969 | 0.959 |
| 8 | 0.962 | 0.962 |
| 16 | 0.977 | 0.962 |
| 32 | 0.973 | 0.948 |
| 48 | 0.962 | 0.955 |
| 64 | 0.964 | 0.981 |
| 128 | 0.956 | 0.983 |
| 512 | 0.995 | - |

In a DeepSeek-V4.1 DP prefill with 16384 tokens per rank, the op runs once per full layer on the main stream, back to back with its neighbours.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Fix] [AMD] imports: [sglang-miles] Skip import-time device probes when no GPU is visible
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## Motivation

Cherry-pick of #45443 onto `sglang-miles`, which branches from `main` at 2a7987f (10-27) and so does not have it. On a ROCm image, any process that imports `sglang.srt` with no GPU visible dies at import:

```text
sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/fp8_kernel.py:102: in <module>
    if is_fp8_fnuz():
...: in is_fp8_fnuz
    return "gfx94" in torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).gcnArchName
E   RuntimeError: No CUDA GPUs are available
```

This is what currently fails Miles' `tests/e2e/long/test_qwen3_0.6B_verifiers.py` on the ROCm 10 nightly ([11-05 MI35X run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42119447202)): its SDK contract step imports SGLang with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=`. radixark/miles#4718 works around it in the test by keeping the GPUs visible on ROCm; with this change in `sglang-miles` that workaround can be removed.

## Modifications

Same diff as #45443, which applies cleanly:

- `is_hip()` also requires `torch.cuda.is_available()`, and the `is_gfx95_supported` / `is_gfx942_supported` / `is_gfx1250_supported` probes use `is_hip()`, so a ROCm process with no visible GPU skips the import-time device queries, as a CUDA one already does.
- `rocm_mla_decode_rope.py` uses `sglang.srt.utils.is_hip` instead of asking Triton's driver at import.
- Adds the CPU unit tests from #45443 (`TestHipProbes`).

With a GPU visible, `is_hip()` and everything derived from it are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Cherry-picked with no conflicts on `sglang-miles` 056f871a7.
- [ ] Not run on a ROCm image yet. The next Miles ROCm image built from this branch should let the Verifiers contract import SGLang with GPUs hidden.

title: [Perf] dsv4: route wo_b and Engram KV MXFP8 GEMMs to cuDNN on CC 10.7 above 8K rows
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

> **Workaround.** This hard-codes two shapes until flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9020 lands. That PR lets the `mm_mxfp8` autotuner rank CuTe-DSL and cuDNN after CUTLASS, so it picks cuDNN for these shapes on its own, and for `wq_b` (N=32768, K=1280) too. Once it is in, SGLang should pass `backend="auto"` on this path and this table should be deleted.

On CC 10.7, DeepSeek-V4.1 runs its dense MXFP8 linears through FlashInfer's CuTe-DSL kernel. sglang passes `backend="cute-dsl"`, and FlashInfer's `"auto"` picks a single backend by priority, so cuDNN's MXFP8 GEMM is never timed against it. For two prefill shapes cuDNN's kernel is faster, and its output is bitwise equal to CuTe-DSL's:

- `wo_b` (N=5120, K=8192)
- the Engram KV projection (N=25600, K=6144)

## Modifications

- `flashinfer_mxfp8_blockscaled_linear`: a `"cute-dsl"` call runs with `backend="cudnn"` when all of these hold:
  - the device is CC 10.7 (`get_platform().device_sm`);
  - M >= 8192;
  - (N, K) is one of the two shapes above;
  - FlashInfer's cuDNN backend supports override-shape graphs (`_is_cudnn_override_shape_available`, cuDNN >= 9.23.1). Without that support cuDNN would build a new graph for every distinct M.
- No scale handling changes: CuTe-DSL already requires 1-D swizzled scales, which is what cuDNN takes.
- Other shapes, smaller M, and other GPUs are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Bitwise. Through this function, the cuDNN output equals the CuTe-DSL output for both shapes at M = 2048, 4096, 8192 and 16384 (MXFP8-quantized random inputs). No model-level accuracy run is needed.

No unit test is added: CI has no CC 10.7 runner.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

CC 10.7, one GPU, CUDA graph of 10 calls. Ratio = cuDNN time / CuTe-DSL time (CuTe-DSL untuned pick):

| shape (N x K) | M=2048 | 4096 | 8192 | 16384 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5120 x 8192 | 0.86 | 0.90 | 0.94 | 0.80 |
| 25600 x 6144 | 0.84 | 0.82 | 0.84 | 0.82 |

At M=16384, against the best of every CuTe-DSL tactic (the set the startup autotuner chooses from), the ratios are 0.91 and 0.88.

End to end, DeepSeek-V4.1 DEP2 prefill (TP2 / DP2 / EP2, 16384 tokens per rank per step, 131K-token contexts, 4096 new tokens per request), same node, alternating base/PR jobs, 8 benchmark runs per arm: step time **0.989x** of base (-1.1%); the two arms' runs do not overlap. A profile of the PR arm shows both GEMMs running cuDNN kernels. A rerun of the final commit gave the same step time.

The M >= 8192 gate is conservative: cuDNN is already faster from 2K rows in the kernel table, but only 16K-row prefill steps were measured end to end.
